_childDocuments_.review: The game has given me the sort of sense of wonder and fun as those old PS1- and 2-era monster raising games, while having really polished gameplay and mechanics. The combat is a really fun take on the rock-paper-scissors style battles with an monster mostly controlled by AI, but you can give it commands at the cost of the games equivalent of MP.  The graphics are gorgeous yet the game runs without a hitch on my not-state-of-art PC at max settings. All that while being set in the Monster Hunter universe which I've been hooked on since the first game, what's there not to like!?The main problems I see would be the grindy gameplay loop getting boring if it isn't your sort of thing, the story being rather cliché and the multiplayer being locked until after about 8~ish hours of gameplay and being way less robust until you complete the main story.  There were also some visual artifacts which lots of people have mentioned on the wooden fences in the third area you visit, but those would be sort of nitpicking it.  And Navirou.The multiplayer is really, really fun!  On Steam the players that appear on the list of available ones are tied to Steam's download region which took a moment to figure out, but changing it lets you play with anyone across the world.  I assume that might be tied to Switch's region lock.  Another downside is that there is no crossplay between PC and Switch, so keep that in mind if you want to play with a pal.All in all, one of my new favorite games!  I've managed to get good 50-ish hours out of it despite of not having scratched the post-game content all too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Because I am a long-time monster hunter fan, I personally recommend this game. If this would be your first game in the monster hunter "universe", this game probably isn't for you.The game mechanics are very simple, and the story takes a long time to ramp up (which is odd, considering it's called Monster Hunter "Stories").  The thing that kept me playing until the end was collecting the eggs and fighting the monsters from all the monster hunter games I've played. It's a really good nostalgia hit because of that. All of my game time was exclusively on the Steam Deck. The game is marked "unsupported" due to the end credits using a video codec that isn't licensed to be used with Proton (you'll end up seeing "No Signal" bars for a majority of the end credits and small snippets of the final sequence). You can work around this by using Proton GE. Note: this game is an absolute battery hog no matter what settings. Just leave them on high and cry in approximately ~2h battery life.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even very far yet, however what a purrific game already! If you like turn-based JRPGs, the Monster Hunter franchise, or monster collector games in general then I feel like you'd love this title. Not too dissimilar an idea from Pokemon but at the same time it isn't Pokemon at all. It has checked off all the boxes and scratched all my itches so far. Loving the "anime" feel of the graphics and animations, with terrific over the top exaggeratedly explosive specials that you perform beside your Monsties that you'd never see in the mainline games. Monster riding and collecting seems to be one of the main features of the game, and it's great. Each monstie seems to have its own cool special, and there are a ton of them to collect. I'm excited to flesh out my team and get to the multiplayer aspect of the game (which I haven't yet, will have to update this when I do). Obviously the other part is the turn based combat with your chosen monsties and then your 6 different weapon types. The combat system is neat with a Rock/Paper/Scissors-ish dynamic that you have to keep in mind in order to min/max damage taken/given to monsters, a system that is easy to dive into on the surface but with intricacies that make it neat to master when things get inevitably more complicated. Then just like the mainstream games, each weapon type kind of has its own special uses and method of mastery (Horn still buffs, Gunlance/Greatsword/Bow still need to be charged for full potential, etc.). I find it all works really well, I'm having a lot of fun. Another similarity to the main games of course is the variety of weapons/armor you can utilize, with each monster having its own equipment set that you can craft with the materials of the fallen. A completionist's nightmare, but if you're someone like me who just genuinely appreciates all the variety then this game has it all: You can build your dream Armory and your dream Monster Stable. Not very deep into the story yet however it certainly has me interested. The music and voice acting are fun. Will update some more the further I go, whether it's notably good or not. My oooonly (minor) gripes so far is that the beginning can in fact feel a little slow and linear, so you have to commit some time to the game before it really starts to shine. This is mostly because on the surface everything seems pretty basic but really there are a lot of different mechanics and features that the game drip feeds you throughout the beginning questline. This is forgivable though, as the other option would be to throw all the mechanics at the player immediately and that would be too disorienting. The other gripe is the lack of all the classic Monster Hunter weapon types (maybe there are more, but all I see for now are the 6, Greatsword/Sword&Shield/Bow/Gunlance/Hammer/Horn), which could also be forgiven since the game's fun anyway. But as a Charge Blade main in the mainstream Monster Hunters I was a little sad, not gonna lie. All in all, definitely happy I got this! Was needing a good turn-based RPG, looking forward to putting more time into it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything that I wanted so far, and more. I'm not even that far in and it's great.I loved the first game for how it did everything it could within the limitations of the 3DS / mobile platform. Now that it's on PC / Switch it can do so much more and it delivers. So many QoL changes, graphics, animations, sound design, literally everything has been vastly upgraded for the better. The new co-op system is fun and makes me appreciate NPCs more. The story is interesting so far. The cutscenes are a treat to watch; the english voice acting is honestly not bad at all.I'm really glad that this game is receiving proper marketing and support and that it has been ported to the PC because it really wouldn't deserve the fate of its predecessor. If a turn-based monster fighting/collecting RPG is your thing, then you have to check this one out. Especially if you've grown tired of whatever the heck is going on with Pokemon, and want something actually good The only gripe I have so far is that your monster storage is limited. I know you can buy upgrades early on but I don't yet know if, towards endgame, you'll get unlimited space. But, either way, in the first game your storage was, iirc, much more forgiving, from the very start. And since going into dozens of dens and hatching as many monsters as I can is part of my playstyle, it's a bit annoying that I have to keep an eye on space now.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big Monster Hunter fan, I honestly couldn't get into this game. The strategy in combat really just boiled down to a rock paper scissors match where you pretty much knew which of the three they would draw after the first turn. I kept hoping for more depth or difficulty in combat but it never came and I got bored. I've heard people say this game is like a better version of Pokemon, but to me it would be like if Pokemon only had grass, fire, and water types and you couldn't even control what the Pokemon did. I never even found the need to swap out monsties even if it would technically make the combat easier. It's definitely a JRPG that feels geared towards young children or something... the palico sidekick character is horrendously annoying and unfortunately has the most voice lines in the game since the player character never speaks.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the few negative reviews dissuade you! It seems like there's been an increasing trend for people to play a game for thirty minutes (probably not exit character creation much less the tutorial) and then leave a negative review. But Stories 2 has a lot of characters and is a vast improvement on the formula of the original. Many quality of life changes have been made and the port to PC was a godsave as someone who played the original averaging 10 fps on the 3DS. People will probably relate this game to pokemon mostly, and the comparison in part is apt. You'll spend a lot of your time hunting down eggs to try and find the best monsters that you can but that is where the comparison ends. Just like any other monster hunter game you'll be hunting the creatures for create weapons and armor for yourself. They've made a big improvement when it comes to the weapons, both adding a few new types compared to the original stories and giving each of them some unique skills related to their individual gauges. You can tell a lot of love has gone into the game. The animations are top notch and completely blow other similar games out of the water. There's a huge variety of monsters to choose from, probably about 80 from what I have read of reviews (not including variants). Best of all, there's even a demo for both the PC and switch versions! If you don't want to take my word for it, at least give the demo a go. The progress from it even carries over so if you like the game you can keep on going with your adventure! For my part though I'll keep enjoying my adventure with all my monstie pals.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, a big improvement over the first one. Animations are really great and it has a pretty fun gameplay loop. Comparing it to Pokemon better looking in terms of graphics and animations. Much more fun gameplay and just some more rpg sutff added on top like crafting gear for yourself. Would easily recommend.

name: Dustoff Z
detailed_description: JOIN THE COMMUNITY ON DISCORD About the Game Get those blades spinning and load up on guns and ammo, the time has come to rebuild humanity! Dustoff Z is a game about maneuvering combat-helicopters in one of the harshest weather conditions possible – A Zombie Apocalypse. Hire gunners to ride along and engage in a variety of missions such as rescue operations, convoy defense, and high-value target destruction. Train and improve a gallery of different shooters, as well as upgrade and maintain a bunch of different helicopters – all with their own unique playstyle. Use your chopper’s winch to interact with the environment. Pick up supply drops, place base defenses, bring back the largest zombies for analysis, or why not use a shipping container as a battle ram?

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable shootemup where you man a helicopter, go on various tasks and fend off zombies. There are plenty of levels in the game where you undertake objectives such as rescuing mission and collecting cargos. The addition of having multiple star points per level where the time it takes to complete a level or completing without casualties also adds some replayability to the game as you try to perfect your game. Along with the different objectives, boss fights with larger zombies also occur from time to time as you progress through the story. Along with this, you also have a team of people with different roles that you level up and grows as you progress. Controls are smooth and also simple enough to play with. The graphics and visuals are also nice with the minimalist design of the characters, enemies and environment gives an arcadey kind of feel to the game. It's also cool to see all the bullets and explosions being fired which causes hectic and mayhem. Overall It's a pretty fun game where you can just have some chaos and zombie fighting.
_childDocuments_.name: Dustoff Z

_childDocuments_.review: If you have to choose between cool concepts and great execution, great execution will always win. Dustoff Z is a game with a great concept. A basic helicopter game where you can blast hordes of zombies, rescue people, and then continue zombie blasting. However, when it comes to delivering on that concept, the game falls short in just enough places to make it feel like a waste of time.Dustoff Z hits the mark in a few areas. The chunky aesthetic works for the silly design of zombies, makeshift helicopters, and over-the-top weaponry. It’s easy to discern everything around you while not requiring much effort to make it run smoothly. The choice in art style is one that I can appreciate and is one of the things that originally sparked my interest in the game.The idea of shooting at zombies from a helicopter is also pretty appealing. On paper, it doesn’t seem like it would be that challenging given the nature of zombies, but the various types of zombies make that more viable. These enemies can leap from the ground and grab onto your vehicle weighing it down and making it sluggish to maneuver so they can bash it up. Others will heave furniture such at you as you fly by. Some variants can fly with bat-like wings or even leap at you to detonate suicide bombs. These aren’t your grandpa’s zombies.I also found the upgrade systems to be solid for the most part. Iterating through a collection of unlocked helicopters with different roles, upgrading them, and adding gunners with different abilities created a solid system. It’s pretty easy to tangibly tell the difference as you upgrade systems and it’s a requirement for being successful as the missions become more complex and deadly.The problem I have with Dustoff Z is that it’s just so sloppy. Every aspect of the gameplay feels like it’s needlessly imprecise. I spent as much time fighting the mechanics as I did fighting the zombies within it. The focus on physics seemed like it would add some entertaining moments, but more often than not it was just a disaster you had to try and overcome in order to progress.The place where this was most obvious was in the item pickups. They are the cornerstone of succeeding in the game but at the same time one of the most common ways I’d lose. Every enemy killed has a chance to drop health, fuel, or ammo. There seemed to be no correlation in the drops relative to what you needed, so if you had only a tiny bit of ammo, you could easily see several fuel drops in a row – even after being full. Then there was the issue that these items would always fall to the ground meaning you had to swoop down and put yourself right in the middle of the zombies to grab them before they blinked out of existence. To make this even worse, they could easily fall into an area extremely close to or underneath terrain debris and you coulnd’t get to them.  Even when you could, it was difficult to even determine if or when you picked it up in many cases.Another area the game frustrated was with the limited scope of movement you could work with. I understand it’s necessary to squeeze in close to the ground to make the zombies feel like a threat, but it makes navigating the physical barriers seem ridiculous. Several times I had to strain at the top of the screen to try to get high enough to go over a barrier because the game wouldn’t allow me to fly high enough freely. This made boss fights downright stupid since you couldn’t easily fly over the top of the boss. You just had to fly into this giant creature and hope it allowed you to pass to the other side of the restricted boss fight area – or risk getting pummeled into the side.One reason this disappoints me so much is that a previous game from this developer was much more fun for me. Dustoff Heli Rescue may be simpler, but it feels cohesive and functional. The challenge comes from mastering the controls, not fighting the physics. I get that Dustoff Z is trying to be an arcade-style experience, but it doesn’t excuse the sloppy execution in the bulk of the gameplay.The sad thing is, it seems like there’s some effort there to make the game comedic and they have some fairly solid voice acting for an indie title. If the game could sit at least on par mechanically with similar games of this style, it would definitely be a gem. However, even for the bargain couple of bucks I paid for it, it doesn’t deliver. For me to recommend a game, I have to have fun with it beyond any other requirements, and I couldn’t have fun here.

_childDocuments_.review: Few zombie apocalypse games give you a helicopter, and winching objects along the map to kill zombies is satisfying.If you want to see my first impressions of gameplay as they happened, watch my video above. There's a weird glitch(?) during the tutorial that makes the game feel like it's crashing. I recommend using the keyboard controls through it and holding the relevant WASD keys to move instead of relying on the controller.Dustoff Z is what it says on the box. Helicopters are always a little awkward to control, and this plays to Dustoff Z's credit. Not only are there multiple helicopters, but upgrades will change their appearance, and you get further customization from minor paint differences (I wish there were more), gunners for each seat, and the variety of missions you'd expect: go somewhere, rescue people, kill things, escort, defend, etc.My one complaint is that it's easy to miss winchable objects. The first gif in the description shows a bladed contraption being drug out to the front of the base, but I completely missed that it was possible when playing that mission myself. Some things that you think might be winchable aren't. For me, the winch was what I was most excited about going into this game, and it was probably the part of the game I was most let down by because to how rarely it seemed to be usable.If you're looking for something casual and a little different, Dustoff Z might fit the bill. It won't be everyone's cup of tea, and it's an overall average game, but if you like the charm then you'll have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little snack-size blast-em-up to enjoy between bigger gaming jaunts.  I'm surprised this has so few reviews on steam as it's perfectly functional and cheap game to pick up and gun through on a lazy weekend afternoon.  Ignore the time played, I probably took about 4 hours to complete this fully.The basic premise is you fly a helicopter about on a 2.5D plain after a zombie apocalypse has occurred, strafing zombies down below, all the while performing convoy escorts, base defense, cargo delivery, and survivor rescues.  You upgrade the helicopter and onboard gunners with coins and parts/supplies that you collect/earn for completing missions.  There is quite a variety of zombie types arrayed against you with plenty of damage they can bring to bear on you (and even the unarmed walkers have a serious jump you need to dodge or you'll be pulled out of control into a horde).  You have to manage your fuel, health and ammo meters throughout each mission which you top up from collectibles that spring from killing zombies or landing or recharge helipads, which also double as in-mission save spots.  The game does make some mistakes - one is making the bonus level dependent on killing specific unique "lieutenant" zombies and not making that clear from the start.  And once I had done 30x missions there was no way I was going to trawl back through them to find these guys.  And either the achievements for completion are bugged or they have for some reason tied the achievement in to this bonus level.Also the threat of death is diminished, particularly later on when you're flush with cash, by a very generous 50-gold in-mission revive mechanic.Also the helicopters and onboard gunners you can unlock have a very uneven progression curve - I felt no real need to change from the helicopter and some of the gunners I picked up midway through and the entire final quarter of the game is a barren plateau for progression.Also having the higher difficulty levels available from the start makes no sense because your beginning gunners and helicopter are so undergunned I think it's literally impossible to make it beyond the first half-dozen levels on the higher levels from scratch - forcing you to play at the normal default difficulty.  It feels like the game is designed to go through each difficulty in turn, bringing your leveled up characters and helicopter through from the previous run, which given the fixed nature of each mission, is not an enticing prospect.But those wrinkles aside it is a fun blast that I enjoyed and would definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you mix in a dash of Jungle Strike, Choplifter, and a healthy sprinkle of The Walking Dead? You get Dustoff Z, an air combat, zombie shooting frag fest that will keep you glued to the edge of your seat. Despite the cartoonish visuals, the game is riddled with fun especially if you’re feeling destructive but morally uptight about any form of senseless killing. Dustoff Z will satisfy that itch to land a few blows for the good of humanity while causing a crazy amount of destruction to the undead.Right from the start, you’ll get to pilot a makeshift chopper assembled from what seems to be parts lying around a junkyard and point it left, right, or straight ahead over various terrain and scenarios. Each level has a distinct objective ranging from escort missions to rescuing citizens trapped between salvation and the undead.The post-zombie apocalypse storyline unfolds nicely as you fire at identified targets and some unexpected jumping enemies all the while trying to keep your chopper in the air without taking on too much damage. Thankfully, upgrades abound and you can even recruit an AI partner to ride shotgun to help you take down the undead. From the moment you boot up the game, you’ll find there is plenty to do and many, many zombies to take down.The beauty of Dustoff Z is its ability to combine resource management, strategy, and a sense of unfolding nerve-wracking adventure from start to finish. In regards to graphics, the game is very nice to look and the music syncs perfectly with the action going on. While enemies often look comical and cartoon-like, the various missions and endless waves of zombies really do feel like you are being overwhelmed which inspires dread and fear as you swing your gun around to stave back any unforeseen attacks.But the biggest thing Dustoff Z brings to the table is the tension that many games in this genre lack. With other games, there always seems to be plenty of time to land and pick up hostages, whereas in this game, for example, the moment the chopper touches down and when it soars back into the sky, the player is sweating bullets. Somehow, many games miss the mark on this, but Dustoff Z brings out this small human drama in such a subtle but impactful way. Well done, Invictus Games, well done indeed.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi everyone I am the bkbossman, you can find me on youTube and publishing videos here on steam. First off I'd like to thank Alf and Marie from Zordix publishing for putting me in touch with this little gem.I've played a few hours of Dustoff Z now and I'm enjoying it thoroughly, it has definitely taken the great aspects of the original Dustoff Heli rescue and enhanced them with a better tech tree, graphical enhancements and a fun and engaging story line.The original was simple involving just 4 upgrades (2 choppers and 2 guns) and focusing on great game play, something which has transferred well into this latest iteration. The tech tree has been expanded so you now have not only more helicopters to choose from but you can upgrade them individually. You can also now choose to have gunners on your chopper and the type you bring with you can affect your progression in the game.These guys can also be upgraded to make them more effective when facing down the apocalypse and your selection will help you to take down the varied supply of zombies that will run.. jump... fly and scream in your direction.The game also has movable units that you can position with your chopper, from slicing machines that chop up your zombie foes to stationary cannons that work from a distance. So far I've found a few elements of environmental interaction where you would effectively change parts of the map for your benefit, (clearing a path for example). There are many different types of missions from defending a convoy to chasing down an enormous boss (check out my video to see just how big)!The game itself runs very smoothly and has low system requirements so should run on just about any PC, the cell shaded graphics were a pleasing diversion from the harsh reality of A+ titles and 4k resolutions and the focus on game play coming first is always a benefit when you want to spend some time just having fun.In all a great little game with a low learning curve and plenty of collectables for all you achievement hunters out there!

_childDocuments_.review: If Rocky ate lightning and crapped thunder, well then Creed Champions is thunder. It's a decent enough arcade boxer at first, but there's a lot missing.The gameplay is not bad; it's pretty shallow but it's not aiming to be a boxing simulator. You have three meters to keep track of, health, guard and a super meter. Health is self- explanatory, the guard is how much you can block before your opponent penetrates your defenses, and the super meter fills when you land attacks or counter. Once you fill it, you can do a damaging punch or combo that overrides almost any enemy attack. However, it can be blocked, dodged or countered with another super, forcing the player to make smart choices about when to use the move, like when an opponent is dazed or commits to a slower attack. The AI often does a good job making these decisions, and may wait for you to use your super before trying its own. The sound is fine. There are recognizable tracks from both "Creed" and the "Rocky" series, like "Eye of the Tiger," "Gonna Fly Now" and "Into the Fire." The voice acting is decent enough, but there's not quite enough of it. Characters' stories are told mostly with text boxes, while voice is used for boxers' in-ring taunts and victory chants.It's a shame about the voice actors not being employed for the individual arcade mode stories, because some of these tales are adorably cheesy. I really don't know if the low quality of the writing is a good or bad thing because it's given me a lot of joy. For example, Drago has a fight against Clubber Lang, but he has a psychotic episode and hallucinates the Southside Slugger as Rocky Balboa. Rocky collects debts for his loan shark boss, Gazzo, while wearing full boxing gear. Apollo tries to escape a bar tab by having Rocky fight the owner in an establishment that just happens to have a boxing ring built inside it. Oh, and Rocky has a Viking as a running buddy. Spoiler Alert! The Viking dies after he and Rocky are mugged offscreen at the behest of a shady boxing promoter. My question is, who is this mugger? You never see him, but if he's capable of taking on both Rocky and a Viking and is adept enough to cause fatal wounds to the latter, then why isn't he a fighter in the game? He should've been Adonis Creed's final boss, not some skinny Don King wannabe.The graphics are a mixed bag as well. Character models look great, but the game doesn't add any bruising or damage of any kind, which is surprising considering "Creed: Rise to Glory" used the same assets and included the damage. Also, the costume variety isn't great and betray some laziness on the developers' part. For example, Apollo Creed isn't wearing his own stars and stripes gear from the "Rocky" movies, but his son's trunks with the name "Johnson" stenciled on the back. I knew Apollo was a cocky dude, but running around in front of audiences and cameras with the last name of your side piece on your backside is a whole new level of not giving a crap.The real problem I have with the game is that, whether you play online or off, there are aspects of Creed Champions that significantly decrease its appeal. There is no online, and the really baffling part is that you still need to be connected online for any of your unlocked boxers or costumes to save and load. Why, in a game with no online feature, should I have to be online to keep my earned progress? It's an extremely foolish setup for a fighting game that's just guaranteed to have no appeal to anyone.If you have a PlayStation 2 or an Xbox, just fire up "Rocky Legends." It has better gameplay, sound, story, character variety, costume variety, a functional save feature, and just surpasses Creed Champions in every single category.

_childDocuments_.review: Big Rumble Boxing: Creed Champions:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Who could forget the sensational scene of Apollo Creed dancing in front of a packed house at the Grand Hotel to the iconic song from James Brown, "Living in America", while the boxing ring rises from beneath the stage with Ivan Drago in the middle in Rocky IV? A film franchise with 8 movies and the upcoming Creed III (2022), which has sold over 1.7 billion at the box office worldwide. A musical and 9 video games, including the Big Rumble Boxing: Creed Champions. So, who would you fight with to become the next boxing champion? Rocky, Apollo, Ivan or Adonis! Can you hear the theme? Can you? It's time to get them, tiger!Big Rumble Boxing: Creed Champions is a boxing arcade game developed and self-published by Survios Inc, on the 4th of September 2021 on Steam platform. The game is also available on PS4, Xbox One and Nintendo Switch.The game features 20 boxers divided into three different boxing styles (General, Slugger, Swarmer), 13 arenas, an arcade, a versus and a training mode. In addition, there are 3 levels of difficulty: Rookie, Pro and Champion. I do recommend selecting the easiest level for your first few fights to get a feel of it before increasing the difficulty.  As you launch the game for the first time, you will have access to all the modes, but only 10 out of the 20 boxers will be available for selection.  As many people know, the genre of arcade games is extremely fun if you know how to execute most of the moves, which are combinations, by punching buttons in specific sequences and using the directional stick on your gamepad to perform moves. Some moves are straightforward, while others require a bit of practice to get down pat, so the perfect place to go is the training mode.  You can play a versus game with a mate on the same screen or play against the computer. The mode I really enjoy is, of course, the arcade mode. As you are on the character screen, you'll see two layouts. On the top, there are the 10 available characters and right beneath them are the other 10 characters you'll need to unlock. I found out that each character has a journey/mini story to complete, which involves 6 fights in total, and depending on the character, 1 or 2 training sessions in between. Each time you complete the journey of one of the boxers from the top layout, you'll unlock 2 skins (shorts) for that boxer as well as the character straight underneath him. By finishing the story of the boxers underneath the main 10 characters, you'll only unlock their additional skins (short). I couldn't avoid playing my first game as Rocky Balboa, and off I went straight into his journey, reflecting most of his movies' fights (Rocky 1 to 4). After a short introduction of both boxers (you can turn off the intro in the settings), ding…. ding…. ding, and it's time to rumble; well, box! On both sides and at the top of your screen, you have the avatar of both boxers. Two gauges are displayed next to each avatar. The top gauge represents health, and the one beneath is stamina. The Super gauges for both boxers are located at the bottom of your screen on each side.You really need to K.O. your opponent as fast as possible by knocking him on the floor at least 3 times and not being flattened yourself.  Your stamina gauge will decrease significantly when you execute a special move or block your opponent’s moves (including special moves). So you'll really have to learn how to move and evade your opponent’s punches as much as you can. This will also help to regenerate your stamina. Each punch that properly hits your adversary will increase the super gauge. When it's full, you can unleash your boxer’s unique supermove and boy, it will inflict serious damage to your opponent. Each time I was able to execute that move, I liked the short focus on your boxer and slow-motion movement that followed through. Expect plenty of super moves coming your way in this game. However, you can block it by pressing one of the right buttons on your gamepad or by moving away, but that must be done at a precise time, and if you miss it, you're the one who’ll be blessed by a supermove from your opponent. However, if you block, your stamina will drop dramatically. You can also counter it, but you must have your super gauge full as well to be able to counter it. Again, it will come down to timing. The training is just like a mini-game really, running on a treadmill, hitting a bag or a rack of beef, and that’s about it. You'll receive points and golden starts, but it won't give you any benefits towards your next fight.  All the characters look magnificent, and the animations are so well done. Sure, it is not a proper boxing simulation, but it is so much fun. The whole arena looks good and has its own feel, and on top of that, you have some of the most iconic tracks of the movie franchise while fighting.    One thing I would have loved in this game is seeing the boxers' faces with cuts and swollen cheeks after going down and progressively being worse. That would have been fun! Unfortunately, it’s not the case in this game. Apart from that, the game ran smoothly in each of my sessions.Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics and soundtrack+	20 different boxers with their own mini-stories+	13 different arenas+	Arcade, versus and training modes+	Crazy and fun moves+	Super fun and addictive +	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	No trading cards as yet-	No facial changesThink of your favourite Rocky song and rise to the top, Champion; a fabulous arcade game!8/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I am somewhat disappointed at the game. The characters relatively resemble those in the movies, and the music is great. I almost didn't want to select my character just so I could listen to the music. However, the game play itself sucks. I thought the game would feature authentic boxing with a few exaggerated special effects here and there, but I was dead wrong... No real boxing just full of unrealistic animated punches with overwhelming special effects. At the same time, most of the characters have similar or exactly the same movement and/or move sets. In other words, not enough individuality in each character. Personally, I also dislike the control and the game doesn't allow you to change buttons either... Anyways, IMO, this is a bit of a let-down. I love the Rocky franchise but this game is a bit of a disappointment. I would rather play Tekken Steve with a Rocky mod if there is one. And I am waiting for 'esports boxing club'.

_childDocuments_.review: BIG RUMBLE BOXING: Creed ChampionsAn arcade boxing game where you can play as the characters from the Rocky and Creed movies. Moste of them have a small campaign with a thin story. Your goal is to fight your way to the top with them. There is training button pressing but overall it does not matter how you do.The game is unfair / unbalanced you as the player have a delay (laag) of sorts, so if you get caught in a combo from the opponent you cant do anything about it but watch yourself get beaten to a pulp. Also while fighting a meter fills up and you can do a special powerful move, that will take alot of health away from your opponent if you press the button and start the special move your ai opponent can use his special move which will cancel your move so you get a beaten ,but you can not do the same to him no canceling the ai's special move..Its a cheap way of making the game difficult and frustrating at times.If you are a fan of the Rocky or Creed Franchises or just really hungry for a button mashing boxing game then this is for you.I enjoy the game at times.

_childDocuments_.review: The most valid criticism of the game is the lack of multiplayer and story mode.  Arcade is ok but instead of animated cut scenes it's just still frames. If this game had taken the approach of previous Rocky games I think it would've been received a lot better.  Beyond that I still recommend it.  There's a learning curve to defense which I think is a positive.  Even on the rookie setting you can't spam the same move forever.  There's also a fun mix of original characters that gives it a Ready 2 Rumble feel. I also have to recommend it based purely on the serious lack of boxing and mma games on PC.  I will admit I may not have been as receptive to this if it didn't have the Rocky license so grain of salt.

name: GUNBIRD 2
detailed_description: Let's go on the treasure hunt through the skies of the world! The ultimate 'Psikyo Shooter'! GUNBIRD 2 is a vertical-scrolling shooter game that first appeared in arcades in 1998. A comical story about the 'magical potion' from ancient times. You can see the dialogue demos that unfold during the intermission and when the boss appears, and the dialogue between the characters that changes when the 2 players mode. New systems has been added, making score attacks even more fun! You can set the difficulty level, life, number of continues, controls, screen orientation, and more. In addition, now we have online rankings! Be the world's best GUNBIRD! Characters: Little great wizard 'MARION' Flying honors student 'TAVIA' from Germany Lone vampire 'ALUCARD' from Romania Military robot 'VALPIRO' from Russia Obese body 'HEI-COB'from Arabia Naked samurai '???' Planes: Power up with 'P' items, with sub-weapons also added. Get bombs with the 'B' item to wipe out enemy bullets and evade your foes! Unleash the super shot to take down your enemies! Risky, but a high-powered, use the close range attack! Arcade mode: 7 levels of difficulty can be selected for beginners. Now players can really test out their skills with a 'HARD' and 'VERY HARD' mode. We're looking for recruits who are up for the test. Local rankings will support all difficulty levels and your own planes. Options: The vertical screen mode that allows you to play in arcade style like back in the day. Select the screen filter from the normal +2 version. You can set the number of lives from 1 to 9 and the number of continues from 0 to unlimited. Assign 'Shot', 'Auto Shot' and 'Bomb' in the key configuration. The vertical screen mode can be operated in the horizontal mode as well! Now enjoy a completely different gameplay. Score Attack: This is a new feature that has a very severe mode with a fixed difficulty level and number of lives. Compete in high scores and score attacks against players from all over the world! Online rankings can be viewed from the options menu.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm infatuated with Psikyo STG's. IMO they're the best out there as far as flow goes, and this statement takes into account all which Cave, Taoplan and Raizing have made.*There is no input lag on the PC ports*That said, some improvement could be made regarding display settings (they don't save between sessions), and other general QoL features on the PC.Keep'em coming!
_childDocuments_.name: GUNBIRD 2

_childDocuments_.review: As the title suggests, this is the sequel to Psikyo's lighthearted bullet hell shooter "Gunbird" which features a cast of mostly new characters (the main hero, Marion, is the only holdover), a new storyline (trying to find a magic cure-all potion and keeping it away from the clumsy pirate trio) and more.Like the original, this is a virtually arcade-perfect port of the game, with the only changes being a remixed soundtrack (the original is missing though) and the addition of a "2P Story Mode" that allows a single player to play with two characters alternating when lives are lost, which also mixes up the story cutscenes and offers more replay value. This one also includes the Score Attack mode with online leaderboards and multiple difficulty levels. The only tweak that needs to be made is the addition of an "Exit" option on the main menu, currently you have to press ALT+F4 on the keyboard to exit (a few other of these games have the same issue).Unless you wish the original soundtrack was present, there's really nothing to complain about here-City Connection has done another great job of porting Psikyo arcade titles to Steam and there are more to come. This is another one that is worth buying, and can also be enjoyed without having to play the original first. Also this is MUCH better than the subpar mobile version. Buy this and help the developer/publisher keep the Psikyo games coming!
_childDocuments_.name: GUNBIRD 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just love these arcade shoot'emups.Psikyo games have that unmistakable Japanese flavour and zaniness while being backed up by serious game design.Gunbird 2 is no exception and is a must have for any fan of arcade shooters, Japanese pop culture and good gameplay.City Connection are a developer that has my respect as it seems every arcade to PC conversion they handle is always good quality.A great game and an easy recommendation

_childDocuments_.review: I suppose the original coin operators complained customers weren't dumping enough quarters into Gunbird.  Hence we have Gunbird 2.  Gunbird 2 is several magnitudes more difficult than the first Gunbird.  If I didn't know any better, I imagine every bullet ever fired in every other shooter was snatched up and stuffed into Gunbird 2.  Gunbird 2 gives Raiden a run for its money with the amount of onscreen bullet madness.  Another problem given the insane amount of bullets on screen is the trouble you will encounter "seeing" the bullets because the "ground" is so detailed in many areas.  A boon for coin operators, but a tragedy for the player.  Finally, some may enjoy the goofy humor, but I find it distracting and unfunny.  If not for the ability to reduce the difficulty and adjust game options for providing a fighting chance, I would not recommend this game.  With all of that said, Gunbird 2 is good, but compared to the original Gunbird it falls short.  Stick with the original Gunbird and leave this one alone unless you are a collector and/or really love shooters.Summary Rating:  6

_childDocuments_.review: GUNBIRD 2. It's a vertical-scrolling shoot'em up game based on the fantasy steampunk worldview. Originally released in 1998, GUNBIRD 2 is the official sequel to GUNBIRD 1(1994). As with most old school arcade games, even if you have not played the previous one, there is no problem at all. Rather, GUNBIRD 2 will be one of the best Psikyo Shooter collections regarding to gameplay.The worldview and storyline is quite interesting. 6 playable characters, each with their own reasons go on an adventure to get the all-around medicine that has been passed down since ancient times. In order to obtain this legendary magic potion, you should summon the god of medicine by using 3 artifacts. What's impressive is that all characters have both individual and collaboration endings. In other words, if you properly experience the game content, there are over 20 kinds of stories and endings. The story keeps a comical vibe overall.As an old school arcade shooter, the game system is pretty solid. Basic attack shots(+ auto shots), Bomb, close range attacks and more. Each character has unique skills and performances. Unfortunately, the succubus character Morrigan (CAPCOM/Dreamcast) is not included. However, this Steam Edition is an enhanced version. Screen resolution and sound effects have been upgraded, and customization game settings for players are supported. You can adjust gameplay settings to suit your taste. Thanks to this feature, even beginners unfamiliar with this genre can easily start to play the game, and there are also modes for experienced players.GUNBIRD 2 (ガンバード2). This is definitely one of the best classic STGs. It refined the gameplay quite nicely. Of course, it is a pity that some contents such as the hidden character and voice acting are missing, but we can guess that there are some reasons for not including them. Best of all, it is welcome that we can meet Gunbird 2 on PC. If you have a nostalgia for the old school arcade, GUNBIRD 2 is for you. If you are hesitating at the fence, just dive into it, this game is definitely worth!
_childDocuments_.name: GUNBIRD 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to rightly look at the Shoot'em Up genre with a proper lens as I simply consider myself an outsider to it. That being said, Gunbird 2 has always fantasized me in a way that most other SHMUPs don't. The style of it looks charming, the game is very colorful, there are a multitude of characters to chose from, and it was one of the few arcade machines at this local Burger King joint I used to go to.Going to play Gunbird 2 for nostalgic reasons; I was really surprised how beginner friendly this game can be. Like don't get me wrong, it has challenging issues, but the initial start of the game wasn't nearly as off putting as some other shmups out there. Gunbird 2 has a tendency to shift between it's first few stages giving players a chance to become more familiar with it's levels. The way that you lose power ups is gradual as it's not all at once, and the enemy attacks do have some predictable patterns once you get use to them. All in all, Gunbird 2 is at least friendly in the beginning, which makes for the last 2 levels spike in difficulty really exasperating.Honestly, I think that's just the main problem with Gunbird 2 here. No matter how much you pay attention it can always feel like a bomb didn't go off fast enough or an attack came out way too fast. And really this is only noticeable near the end of the game, at Gunbird 2's last two levels that things feel unfair. Why there is suddenly a laser that can instantly come out, or the way certain enemies and attack patterns start attacking from the sides really feels more jarring than challenging. No enemies are introduced before hand that are like this, and the game sort requires you know when a boss is just going to fire a laser with little warning. It just makes getting to the end point, only to game over feel awful, or simply dying in these last few levels a hellish nightmare of survival that feels like there is no way out.Still, I feel Gunbird 2 offers more to it's audience than the average SHMUP. Not to knock other SHMUPS, but the fact this game has a team attack mode with it's own unique story for each pairing is just super neat. The difficulty levels range through 9 different ones that honestly feel like a proper work up to each level. Boss and enemy designs are fairly neat and stick out on the maps without distracting the player or the bullets that you have to dodge. The backgrounds are all different and unique on each stage, and the music is very poppy. Gunbird 2 is just ascetically pleasing to look at, and deceptively friendly at first that I can't help to not recommend to others simply because it's inviting.
_childDocuments_.name: GUNBIRD 2

_childDocuments_.review: Between the original Gunbird and Gunbird 2, I like the sequel a little more.  They're basically the same game mechanically with the exception that Gunbird 2 expands the charge mechanic a little more.Very few of the characters of the original return here.  Which is a shame, as I liked the previous cast more than the new characters here.  Each character has their own regular shot, charge shot, charge melee attack and bomb.  Which might seem like a lot, but I find the melee attack overly  risky for the reward.  Especially since it drains the charge meter a tad.  I found it better to fill up the meter and save it for the bosses.  Since just charging the attack can be dangerous since you momentarily stop shooting.  Which allows waves of enemies to fill the screen with bullets.  And that may take a bomb to clear them out and keep the game going... At least if you aren't particularly good at shoot 'em ups.This is one of City Connection's better ports of a Psikyo game.  I wouldn't say it's a good port, though.  For best results, the player has to fiddle with the Configuration Tool before booting up the game.  As it defaults to window mode instead of full screen.  If you play on a non-standard (read: XBox) controller, you'll also want to map the buttons are.  However, re-mapping isn't done yet.  Once in the game, you set the actions to the buttons you wish to use.  Of course, you can skip the configuration tool step, but then it's a bit of trial and error to figure out what the game thinks the button are.  Which is a hassle for someone like me that enjoys playing shooters on an 8-button USB Genesis Controller.  But at least the game allows for it, so I won't grip too much.I think Gunbird 2 is my favorite non-military aircraft (aka Strikers 1945) shooter.  It's a long ways from my favorite has overall the Psikyo touch (charge attacks, random initial stages, power ups preferring the upper portion of the play area, starting at the beginning of the later stages with a continue,  et al) are all mechanics I just don't care for.  However, I did enjoy playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: GUNBIRD 2

_childDocuments_.review: Straight from the hit arcade game, Gunbird 2  is the most intense test of coordination and skill. This action shooters features 7 characters on a quest for the magical ingredients to produce the All-Purpose Medicine. On a journey to see the wise medicine master, you are intercepted by a rowdy band of pirates. Now, maneuver through insane levels of enemy fire to pick up power-ups and other weapons and be the first to recover your stolen bounty and unlock the secret of the medicine master.

name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York
detailed_description: More World Of Darkness About the Game You’re a nobody. An outcast in your own vampiric sect. A political prisoner of no particular value. An immigrant who never found her roots in a city of immigrants. A chainsmoker whose favorite pastime is staring blankly at the streets through the windows of a fast food joint at 4AM. The sinking feeling in the pit of your stomach tells you that you’re doomed, and distorted voices from the shadows seem to agree. The curse of your clan makes interacting with everyday technology difficult. Dissociation is your natural state. But when New York’s Anarch leader meets a gruesome end, out of all the bloodsuckers in the metropolis, you’re the one picked to investigate. Make no mistake: this is obviously a trap, yet another move in the horrible game of Jyhad, the eternal struggle for power between warring vampire generations. But you’re Lasombra, and if there’s one thing you know, it’s this: if the Ventrue Prince and her followers underestimate you, they’re going to deeply regret it. Vampire: The Masquerade – Shadows of New York is a visual novel set in the rich universe of Vampire: The Masquerade. It's a continuation of our previous title, Coteries of New York. While Coteries was a general introduction to the world depicted in the 5th Edition of the hit tabletop role-playing game, Shadows presents a more personal and unique tale. A visual novel tackling themes of personal and political horror, suitable for both Vampire: The Masquerade veterans, and fans of narrative-driven games who are newcomers to the setting. A continuation of Coteries of New York. See the familiar metropolis through entirely different eyes. Expect new characters, new locations and a fresh original soundtrack. Play as a member of the Lasombra clan. Formerly vicious foes of the Camarilla, the Magisters decided to search for safety in the ranks of their former enemies. Master the shadows and communicate with the inhabitants of the Other Side, but beware – Oblivion is always lurking out there, ready to devour you whole. Explore the streets of the Big Apple. While you search for ways to satiate your bloodthirst, catch glimpses of various fascinating vignettes and forge connections with the eccentric inhabitants of the city. One playthrough won’t be enough to see it all. Shape your mind, shape your fate. You used to avoid defining yourself and tried to stay neutral, but given your situation, you can no longer afford to do so. The choices you make will alter the way you think, and your thinking will alter the paths you take. If it’s called Vampire: The Masquerade, does that mean you have something in common with World of Darkness, Bloodlines 2, Redemption, the cult tabletop RPG system, or...? Yes. Shadows of New York is set in the same shared universe, but offers independent experiences and stories. You may spot some connections with the other titles, but Shadows is not a sequel to any existing products. The World of Darkness is a media franchise and shared universe, shaped by various creators and participants, meaning: all stand-alone stories play into a greater whole. Berlin falling to the Anarchs during an official LARP, the Lasombra clan joining forces with the Camarilla in the Vampire: The Masquerade - Chicago By Night 5th Edition sourcebook, Sophie Langley’s plot to take control of New York in Coteries of New York – all of these events subtly influence and interact with each other. Do I need to play Coteries of New York to understand and enjoy the story of Shadows of New York? Not at all. Shadows of New York is a continuation of Coteries of New York, which means it shares the New York City setting and a large part of the supporting cast with our previous title, but is designed to offer a different experience. Coteries served as an introduction to the basics of Vampire: The Masquerade 5th Edition – it was focused on showcasing different vampire Clans and core concepts of the setting through the point of view of a newly-fledged vampire, a character who did have a defined backstory, but by and large meant to serve as a player avatar. Shadows of New York is a more personal story, told from the perspective of a well-defined character who’s already integrated into the Kindred society and has a developed inner monologue of her own (which means you influence her personality instead of shaping it). Those who are familiar with Coteries will already know a large part of the cast and catch some references that would otherwise go unnoticed, but those who decide to start with Shadows and get back to Coteries later should be able to enjoy both experiences just as much as they would if they played them in their release order. The two stories are essentially separate, different both tonally and thematically. Which platforms is Shadows of New York available on? Shadows of New York launched simultaneously on PC (Windows/Mac OS/Linux), PS4, Xbox One and Nintendo Switch in September 2020. Does the game support controllers? Yes. You’re able to play both with mouse and keyboard, as well as with a controller.
about_the_game: You’re a nobody. An outcast in your own vampiric sect. A political prisoner of no particular value. An immigrant who never found her roots in a city of immigrants. A chainsmoker whose favorite pastime is staring blankly at the streets through the windows of a fast food joint at 4AM. The sinking feeling in the pit of your stomach tells you that you’re doomed, and distorted voices from the shadows seem to agree. The curse of your clan makes interacting with everyday technology difficult. Dissociation is your natural state. But when New York’s Anarch leader meets a gruesome end, out of all the bloodsuckers in the metropolis, you’re the one picked to investigate. Make no mistake: this is obviously a trap, yet another move in the horrible game of Jyhad, the eternal struggle for power between warring vampire generations. But you’re Lasombra, and if there’s one thing you know, it’s this: if the Ventrue Prince and her followers underestimate you, they’re going to deeply regret it. Vampire: The Masquerade – Shadows of New York is a visual novel set in the rich universe of Vampire: The Masquerade. It's a continuation of our previous title, Coteries of New York. While Coteries was a general introduction to the world depicted in the 5th Edition of the hit tabletop role-playing game, Shadows presents a more personal and unique tale. A visual novel tackling themes of personal and political horror, suitable for both Vampire: The Masquerade veterans, and fans of narrative-driven games who are newcomers to the setting. A continuation of Coteries of New York. See the familiar metropolis through entirely different eyes. Expect new characters, new locations and a fresh original soundtrack. Play as a member of the Lasombra clan. Formerly vicious foes of the Camarilla, the Magisters decided to search for safety in the ranks of their former enemies. Master the shadows and communicate with the inhabitants of the Other Side, but beware – Oblivion is always lurking out there, ready to devour you whole. Explore the streets of the Big Apple. While you search for ways to satiate your bloodthirst, catch glimpses of various fascinating vignettes and forge connections with the eccentric inhabitants of the city. One playthrough won’t be enough to see it all. Shape your mind, shape your fate. You used to avoid defining yourself and tried to stay neutral, but given your situation, you can no longer afford to do so. The choices you make will alter the way you think, and your thinking will alter the paths you take. If it’s called Vampire: The Masquerade, does that mean you have something in common with World of Darkness, Bloodlines 2, Redemption, the cult tabletop RPG system, or...? Yes. Shadows of New York is set in the same shared universe, but offers independent experiences and stories. You may spot some connections with the other titles, but Shadows is not a sequel to any existing products. The World of Darkness is a media franchise and shared universe, shaped by various creators and participants, meaning: all stand-alone stories play into a greater whole. Berlin falling to the Anarchs during an official LARP, the Lasombra clan joining forces with the Camarilla in the Vampire: The Masquerade - Chicago By Night 5th Edition sourcebook, Sophie Langley’s plot to take control of New York in Coteries of New York – all of these events subtly influence and interact with each other. Do I need to play Coteries of New York to understand and enjoy the story of Shadows of New York? Not at all. Shadows of New York is a continuation of Coteries of New York, which means it shares the New York City setting and a large part of the supporting cast with our previous title, but is designed to offer a different experience. Coteries served as an introduction to the basics of Vampire: The Masquerade 5th Edition – it was focused on showcasing different vampire Clans and core concepts of the setting through the point of view of a newly-fledged vampire, a character who did have a defined backstory, but by and large meant to serve as a player avatar. Shadows of New York is a more personal story, told from the perspective of a well-defined character who’s already integrated into the Kindred society and has a developed inner monologue of her own (which means you influence her personality instead of shaping it). Those who are familiar with Coteries will already know a large part of the cast and catch some references that would otherwise go unnoticed, but those who decide to start with Shadows and get back to Coteries later should be able to enjoy both experiences just as much as they would if they played them in their release order. The two stories are essentially separate, different both tonally and thematically. Which platforms is Shadows of New York available on? Shadows of New York launched simultaneously on PC (Windows/Mac OS/Linux), PS4, Xbox One and Nintendo Switch in September 2020. Does the game support controllers? Yes. You’re able to play both with mouse and keyboard, as well as with a controller.
short_description: Your old life is dead and buried. You have no afterlife to look forward to, and your vampiric unlife is about to fall apart unless you solve an unsolvable crime. Welcome to New York City... and welcome to the Lasombra clan, where failure is not an option.

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest complaint with the previous game, Coteries of New York, was that none of your choices ever matter. They've doubled down on that with this game. It feels more like reading a short story one sentence at a time. The art, characters, music, and general atmosphere are all absolutely wonderful. I just wish the player was involved beyond turning the pages.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VERY tentative recommendation. There is a lot to like about this game - the artstyle, the music, being set in the World of Darkness, the gothiness if that's your thing - but some... let's call them *quirks* of the writing seemed to deliberately try and sabotage the good things it had going on.The problems of the game's writing (and being a visual novel, it's 99% writing) can all be summed up in one single word: "Julia". See, most of the characters are pretty good as these things go. They're well written, varied, occasionally inflicted with wanky dialogue, but overall, solid performance. But our main girl Julia... Oooh boy. She starts out alright, as a reporter getting to the bottom of some twisted controversy archetype, but after she inevitably gets turned into a vampire, her few appealing qualities quickly get drowned out by a neverending cascade of endless, pseudo-philosophical inner monologues, insulting characters that are much less infuriating than herself for partially really flimsy reasons, and hogging a lot of playtime that could have been spent focusing on literally anyone else.I can respect wanting the story to be focused on your main character's perspective, and on principle, I think sticking to their internal perspective like that is a good approach, since it allows the player to get to know them better and become invested in their struggles. But all of that only works when your main character isn't such an infuriatingly obnoxious drama queen that you would rather stake her than empathize with her.I'm giving Julia flak because I genuinely think that I might have liked this game quite a lot if it had gone with a different kind of protagonist. As it stands, if you think that she's someone you can relate to or vibe with, then you most likely will appreciate her constant presence and will probably have a good time with the story. And I will say that despite my annoyances, the ending I got didn't completely leave me cold. It also did not leave me with much desire to go through the game again for the other ending option, but nevertheless, overall I mostly enjoyed the game in spite of my problems with it, and you might too, or ideally you might get a lot more out of it than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished Shadows of New York in seven hours, pushing my supposedly-sleeping body because I been waiting for this game, because I am big fan of Lasombra.Graphic wise, its not much different than the first game, in fact... a lot of the backdrops are from the first game. It doesn't matter tho, they are cool and you also get to see a lot more keyplayers of Camarilla New York and even the old ones are displayed in new attires once (its quiet entertaining). Music are amazing, it sounds like great haunting cello and choirs inside a church-- without making it feels too churchy, with touch of modern instruments and edits that I am too poor in musical knowledges to understand.Story wise, it may feel having a little less options because they focus more on Julia's characteristics and her inner turmoil. Instead, they have 'trait' system that shape Julia's characteristics, that would decide some actions and which ending she will get. The blood-system is toned down too and using variety of power to solve problems feel more epic-- even thought my logic mind keep asking how a fledgling get lvl 5 power.What get me excited is how the dilemmas Julia having are dealt so much in lasombra's perspective. Telling more will spoil the story. And if you play the previous game, it did ties all lose ends from the previous, while new players can play this independently. Oh, also even if you are expert on VtM lore, check out the dictionary because it is written on Julia's perspective, it is quiet amusing.The cons is that the game may feel very railroady as no matter what you choose, the story keep going. The focus of the choices more on Julia's attitudes and her decision at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically Coteries of New York with a better-developed story arc due to less freedom of choice. You're not starting out as some newbie fledgling this time around, instead you're stepping into the established shoes of a down on her luck independent journalist turned creature of the night. As such your odds of dying are greatly diminished compared to the original title, but she does a solid job of irritating her minder and others.Very nice visuals as usual, lots of recycled scenes from the last game which isn't really a bad thing. Expect to see many of the characters from Coteries again this time around. Great soundtrack as usual. Minimal grammatical errors, no issues with lag like I had slightly on the first release.Completionists, you're looking at around 3.5 hours for an initial play-through plus another couple hours or less to 100% based on how much you abuse text skip. If you enjoy your initial romp I'd suggest reading rather than skipping as some things do change dramatically.Easy recommend if you're into out of the ordinary visual novels with super dark moods.

_childDocuments_.review: If Coteries of New York is good, then Shadows of New York is fantastic. Shadows features all of the machiavellian mind-games, and cunning intrigue that you’d want from a VTM game, as well as a thoroughly-likeable protagonist. _childDocuments_.review: I will join the throng of people who say "I wish I could leave a neutral review."tl;dr? If you know what "Lasombra" means, the game will make sense, and you might like it. If you have no idea what that is, the game will make much less sense, and you'll be confused by the ending(s).If you know enough about Vampire: The Masquerade (VtM), or World of Darkness (WoD), then this game might be a good choice. However, if you've never experienced these games before, the progression of the narrative, and especially what ending you get, and why, will seem confusing. You aren't judged on whether or not you solved the case, but rather your ability to play a Lasombra.Unlike the prequel (Coteries of New York), your choices DO determine the ending you get. That's a positive. Now, however, there are much fewer choices to make. I felt that this wound up making it even less of a game, in some ways, than the previous title; it feels like you're (still) on rails. The hunger/feeding mechanic of the previous game is gone. That could have also been a good keep, but they removed it.Concerning the writing, there's a lot to like, in the sense that, taken by itself, the writing is good. However, if you've played the previous game, the quartet of coterie characters seem less well-written than before (and in one case, not written at all). The new character that shows up (that isn't you or your girlfriend) that originally seems (very?) important has virtually nothing to do with most of the game's narrative, and only really shows up in one of the endings. I don't understand how she was relevant. The main character and her narrative, is good, overall. Once again, however, I'm wishing there was more.As with the previous game, the music and art are fantastic. It was nice to see multiple images of the main character (i.e. moods), which was a positive improvement from the previous installment. Many "snapshots" of pivotal moments in the game, especially the endings, are very good. The music absolutely nails the mood of the game, and the universe.To someone who's new to the genre, I think this game would be considered difficult to understand, if not, a little strange. I would argue that a newbie playing the previous game before this one would be even MORE confused, since many of the core concepts that are claimed (repeatedly) to be important are now basically ignored (hunger/beast/Masquerade). I'm experienced with Vampire, and even I was wondering about my Humanity, when I could feed (and why I wasn't being bothered for not doing it), and so forth.To VtM vets: if you've always wanted to roleplay a Lasombra, this is your game. It took me about 7 hours to get all the achievements, so it's a quick playthrough. If that sounds like you, then you'll like the game. If you were hoping for any improvements from the previous title beyond "multiple endings, dictated by choices you make in the game," you may still be disappointed (there aren't any).

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand why this is a game. Coteries of New York was bad enough, but this game doesn't even have the illusion of choice. You can easily spend half an hour not making a single choice and just clicking through endless dialogue. The music and the art are really the only things worthwhile about this title, but if you're looking for an interactive novel or Vampire: The Masquerade game, do yourself a favor and check out Night Road instead. That game might be mostly text with a few character portraits here and there and no music, but at least the story is engaging and feels like playing Vampire: The Masquerade. I've played Night Road five times and yet just finishing Shadows of New York once felt like a massive chore. If like me you're still holding out for Bloodlines 2 and this is something to tide you over, move along. You're not missing anything by skipping this one. At best, just buy the soundtrack and listen to it while reading V:tM books or playing Night Road.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.4h (based on Steam, 100% achievement) No. Yes (11 achievements). No. is a sequel of  (), telling the story of what happened one year after the first game. It's still a visual novel in the  universe, with a new main character and improved features from the previous game. However, despite the improvements, some features in the first game are neglected in the second one. More on the review.- 2+1 endings that tell different story- A lot of filler monologues- Side quests act as fillers- Newcomers might have a problem understanding the gameThe game reuses a lot of assets from the first game with the addition of some new ones. Backgrounds still have the realistic look with slight animation on some people or objects to make it more alive while portraits are retaining the painting-like style with a more polished look. Some recurring characters from the first game also have their portrait redone, giving a different vibe from how they used to be.Some improvements are also noticeable if you played the first game. Detailed scenes are added at certain points of the game, allowing you to see what was told in the narration instead of imagining it with the usual backgrounds and portraits. Some characters also have more than one portrait compared to the static, single portrait in the first game. While it's not needed most of the time, sometimes they prove to be useful, especially when you see someone opening his/her mask. A certain degree of understanding the  universe is needed to understand the story, unless if you want to refer to the dictionary section often. A lot of vampire-exclusive terms will be introduced as you play the game without explaining what they mean, forcing you to visit the dictionary section to learn about it - there was even a point where the game mentioned a new name out of nowhere without context. People who have played the first game will recognize the person, but those who aren't will be left in the dark until the game introduced the person, vaguely. Some characters and events from the first game will also be connected to this game that you won't be able to enjoy the game to its fullest if you didn't play the first one beforehand.For a story-driven game, filler monologues fill 80% of the story. Julia, the main character, seems to talk a lot in her head, to the point that she kept on bringing topics that have nothing to do with the story. Not only that it unnecessarily makes the game longer, but they also tend to be hard to understand, especially with the heavy use of exquisite words. Most dialogues also tend to be long that I had to re-read the full paragraph just to understand the context. Side stories act as a filler to make the game last longer, nothing else. There are no chain side stories, meaning that everything will become of no value once you finished them. There is also nothing interesting unless if you want to know more about Julia's friends and what's happening to the world, which doesn't do much in the first place.There are 2 endings excluding one where the game ends its story abruptly if you choose the wrong choice. The game seems to note the lack of decision making in the first game and introduces two different endings based on your previous decision.  is introduced as a component that will affect Julia's inner monologues, and with it, changing her decision that will lead to two different endings. Both endings are completely different from each other, with one revealing a twist.Despite the unique endings, the conclusion feels like a joke. The game starts with a murder in place, making murder mystery to be the theme of the game. You'll gather some clues from the crime scene and interrogate every suspect at first although everything doesn't seem to matter in the end since all clues that you gathered won't be used for solving the case. The main character will state some facts that were never mentioned throughout the game out of nowhere, making it impossible to deduce the perpetrator. There is some kind of twist in it, but the ridiculous conclusion to the murder mystery gave a bitter taste to my experience.Different dialogue choices are available throughout the game, although not necessary. The game allows you to answer from a series of options sometimes, which don't seem to affect anything. Most choices only affect the next few dialogues in the game and unlike the first game, you won't get any extra info out of it - all choices will lead you to a slightly different answer from each other. There are only several dialogue choices that matters, which are related to the  mechanic that I had mentioned previously. I finished the game in 6.2h and spent the rest of my playtime obtaining the other endings. The game can be finished faster if not for the useless monologue and side quests, which doesn't affect the main story. It's still worth playing the game for a second time though to unlock the other ending, or maybe a third time if you want to unlock all endings.Intel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The lack of relationships in this game makes the story feels empty. I enjoyed the relationships between all characters in the first game, despite what happened in the ending. However, most conversations in this game come from your inner monologue with a lot of fillers in it. There's another person that the main character interacted with, and although I enjoyed their private time together, it feels too short, especially with their conversations being redundant at first.This game doesn't interest me as much as the first game, somehow. Sometimes, the wording feels alien to me, especially with the use of exquisite words and references that I didn't get. Additionally, some people are talking too much that it took a lot of dialogue boxes just to explain something - I had to reread the whole paragraph after losing focus most of the time due to the wording. It makes me feel that the story was written by someone else because of it.

_childDocuments_.review: “You should never ask anyone for anything. Never- and especially from those who are more powerful than yourself.”--The Master and MargaritaIt's not surprising to quote this important Russian novel when it perfectly suits the theme of this story throughout the whole affair.Shadows of New York is a sequel to this studio's previous game, Coteries of New York, and it's a much better work.  The writing is far stronger, the main character leaves an actual impression as opposed to the humdrum protagonists of the previous title, and even the returning cast is far more interesting this time around.This is a visual novel where a former journalist turned vampire has to investigate a murder within her community, yet she knows it's a all sham, we know it's all a sham, and the entertainment comes not from unraveling the mystery on why she was setup like this (which is interesting on its own) but on how her decisions during the narrative affect the outcome, leading to two possible endings.Vampire: The Masquerade enthusiasts will rejoice not only on playing as a Lasombra kindred, but also on guiding the leading character to either embrace her clan's self-serving ruthlessness or reject her Blood to embrace her dwindling humanity.  Neither is a "good" or a "bad" ending, simply the logical destination that the protagonist chose little by little.It's just a shame that it's such a short story.  While it has a beginning, middle, and an end, it does feel like the middle portion is missing some content, which would have helped expand the choices possible and also showcase more of the happenings in New York.  Most likely, production was affected due to the early days of COVID (it's a 2020 game).But, true or not, it doesn't invalidate that this is ultimately a good experience with great writing, gorgeous art, and a fine musical score.  Stake it out.
