There are four binary choices which determine which of two endings you get, and though they're presented as determining her personality, it's really just how committed to playing the Camarilla game she is. You can still pick where you go at night, but the choices don't seem to matter or build on each other. You meet people from the first game sometimes, and that's about it. Having such a strongly defined protagonist and story arc wouldn't rankle as much if Julia wasn't so difficult to like right out of the gate, but she is and it does.Shadows has the skip function Coteries needed, and the glitchy visual of Julia on a camera feed is neat, but overall this game has very little to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: *****************This game is critically different to it's previous installment, "Coteries of New York", and if you go into it expecting a straight up sequel (gameplay wise), you'll be sorely disappointed. I personally enjoyed both games, but for very different reasons.Shadows of New York is mostly reading. If I were a harsher reviewer I would probably say it's only reading. That is, apart from the gorgeous (sometimes recycled) visuals and fitting atmospheric audio, there is little else on offer other than reading. I didn't mind this and actually found myself a fan of the narrative voices present in this work - it's clear that a lot of effort has gone into the tone and variation of the writing - but it  sometimes be too much. I'm thinking specifically of moments where it seemed as if the authors simply wanted to show how cultured, intelligent and sophisticated they are. Nonsensical references to both history and pop-culture that really interrupted the flow and immersion (I know, I know, stupid to say, I know). Long winding philosophical, biblical conversations that got concluded with jabs at Kanye. Choice word usage that wasn't technically jargonistic as our main protagonist is/was a fancy journalist, but occasionally just felt complex to create a faux depth. You get the idea.As a whole I really enjoyed this. Quite a fresh and modern voice - many ideas all lost in the chaos of inserting the developers' personally beloved aspects of our world. A frenzy of thoughts mimicking the scattered homely but foreign New York you witness. And a cool underground vampire society that constantly feels on the brink of surfacing. I only mention all this because I think that for a game of mostly reading you ought to know what you're getting yourself into. It's this very absurdity and inconsistency of voice that I found most intriguing and enjoyable of what the game offers.Regarding narrative, I don't really have any strong thoughts. I enjoyed it, but this is probably due in most part to the writing. Not the craziest story, and heavily reliant on the player having fully experienced Coteries first, but yeah, enjoyable.When it comes to the 'gameplay', Shadows really suffers. I've spoiler tagged this next section because I think that if you're going to play the game, you absolutely do not want to go into it knowing this, but  [Summary: the game is very... linear]. On a second playthrough you really notice this, and other than some slight further exploration (events you couldn't witness due to limited choices), the game is practically unchanged. In turn, replayability is really lacking. Which I personally think is not ideal for a 19AUD product, but I understand that people consume entertainment and media differently, so perhaps this is not such a turn-off for you.I enjoyed the experience of Shadows of New York, that's clear to me, but I'm slightly hesitant to recommend it to other people because I'm so aware of it's shortcomings. And as unfair as it may be, I cannot help but critique it over elements of Coteries that I loved that are absent here (like... forming your coterie... and progressing multi-day sub stories... and gameplay....). I do recommend trying the game if you can get it on sale, you've played Coteries of New York, and you don't mind a different experience that continues the ideas and themes of the fascinating Masquerade.*****************Lymao, how do I end reviews?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a better "novel" than the prequel, not as abrupt and suddenly ending but still  very short. Very modern in how people think and do things, but that fits VtM V5. I would say they hit the mood even more this time around and manages to pull off a decent feel of the World of Darkness setting. It is no Bloodlines, it is not an RPG, it is not long or even that deep but it is a short experience for people who look for a very one simple but moody "novel-like" game. It manages to pull off interesting characters decently, some returning cast is what I think is the most interesting. Qadir, the  Toreador Sheriff is a favourite of mine along with some others with interesting twists. Sadly the game is extremely short and feels like it could been extended and had more deepended mechanics to make it a bit more open ended. The game have two endings and from what I understand your choices changes the outcome. You get traits from your actions but considering how short the game is, it feels like almost playing a demo. This was a similar issue the first game had but either from me knowing how that game just abruptly ended or this one being a more well designed story, it didn't feel as out of the blue when the ending drops by. I would recommend it if one like Vampires, World of Darkness, Visual novels or a short story driven game and  got 10-11 euros laying around one boring weekend. I would say its a middle of the road game but Steam only have a thumb up or down.

_childDocuments_.review: Finishing this game and seing all of it makes me think I might've expected something different, and it sort of spoiled an impression a little. First - the protagonist annoyed me to no end. She's constantly pissed off, gloomy, bored, "I'm all special and you all are mere boring mortals" - your typical teen who recently realised they know f-words and use them uncontrollably. And she gets away with it. What is your problem, woman? Even when being called out by a friend she lashes out. I mean I love that the protagonist was given a personality - the ones in "Coteries" kind of lacked it - but this is too much, imo. Second - I found the story to be...loosely knit? I mean it seemed more than once that the whole story is just to support the artworks, which are undeniably stunning, but the plot leaves quite some questions. What actually happened? Why bringing the 4 characters from "Coteries" here if they barely serve any purpose (except for showing the new outfits)? What's everyone motivation? Why not adding a little bit of story to the side quests and make them brighter (again, you can't even check all of them nor you can skip them)? The choices don't matter that much, again. I don't even want to play this again because of all the above. Again, the art is beautiful, I love that there are different images now per caracter, and all the effects like gleaming eyes and smoke, but to see the artworks you can just buy an art book. And, although I'd love to see what the developers come up with next (and I very much hope they will), I can't recommend this game. Get the art book, the soundtrack, - you will get the idea.

However,...Unlike Coteries of NY (Which had a little of the writers' political ideology wrote in, and was easily ignored in favor of the gameplay. Sticking mainly to topical political jokes and the like, pretty funny) This game shoves it's ideology straight down your throat. Some things I agree with, some I don't, that's not the point.... I don't play games to have my ideology confirmed or denied!! I play them to not have to think about that BS for just 1 ******* HOUR!!!! I don't CARE if you agree with me, politically! I want to be a vampire for an hour or two!!! Before I have to go back out and face imbeciles..... Shame on you for taking advantage of people in such a vulnerable state. If I wanted to have my politics reinforced/questioned I'd watch the BL***Y NEWS!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is bad. Firstly, the game fails to deliver a captivating and engaging story. The plot is predictable and lacks any significant twists or turns. The characters are one-dimensional, and their motivations are uninteresting, making it hard to connect with them or care about their fates. The dialogue is also dry and uninspired, making it feel like a chore to read through.Additionally, the lack of voice acting in the game is a significant issue. While some players might not mind reading through the dialogue, others might find it tedious and frustrating. Voice acting would have helped to bring the characters to life and create a more immersive experience.Overall, "Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York" is a boring and unremarkable game that fails to deliver an engaging story or an immersive experience. If you're looking for a game with compelling characters, a captivating plot, and excellent voice acting, this game is not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a rather sad miss for me, as the game does have a few things I reallly liked a lot, such as- constant cynicism and sarcasm throughout the game (although: if Vampires and the Masquerade were real, our heroine probably would't survive one month in this game, but that aside - it was just so fun to read)- a few cute drawings (particularly of Dakota and Julia)- revisiting some of the characters from the main game (albeit I didn't quite like what they did to most of them :/ - SPOILERS: just take Hope as a corporate, yikes)neutral (to me):- just as the main game [Coteries of New York], the game doesn't really employ the skill system of Vampires: The Masquerade (at least not that I could tell it played a role in any outcome in the game, and it sure didn'T show in your stats-  and other than its otherwise more simplicistic predecessors, which came sort of a surprise). It doesn't really bother me, but some real Vampires The Masquerade fans might find it disturbing- I guess this is because, this game is really more of a visual novel, only that the visuals are mostly limited to a few background pics [as the writin gis mostly fun, I can live with that]however leading down to the downside:- the choices in this game are not only super scarce, they are also super arbitrary, as in: you get a dreamy sort of sequence in which you can "steer" the dream which a command phrase [I rember sth like "who?", "where?" or "why?" - but you have no freaking idea what the next scene of this "dream" even is, so in reality, you don't really "steer" the dream but just stumble around between arbitrary choices, which could sometimes just as well be named "A", "B" or "C" for all the game let's you know. Seriously, I don't mind taking tough choices and I can take that you cannot always foresee an outcome of a potential line of action, but at the very least I would like to know WHAT ACTION THE HELL I AM TAKING!!!- this comes on top of that for main parts of the game, you can't really steer your character at all, because the writers have decided to simply rollercoaster you along.In short, a combination of no choice and unintelligible choices. Gee, thanks, but no thanks, dear developers.What makes me wonder more is that, in the main game, they somehow did it. it wasn'T like you could steer your character all through, but the choices were way more numerous and they made sense.If this game was in devlopment stage, I'd say:nice story guys, but you definitely need to redevelop the way the user interacts with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate the use of Unity for visual novels. It makes them slow, clunky and lacks key features. _childDocuments_.review: On paper, this game suffers the same problems as Coteries of New York.The UI is annoying. The narrative is badly managed and constantly reminds you that the writers can't think even one scene ahead (which for an investigative mystery is REALLY bad and makes the finale laughable. There is no set-up and payoff, there's just things that happen with two minor details actually foreshadowed). The choices are shallow, the consequences are none, the plot is thin and more linear than an average dime-pile paperback.What elevates Shadows of New York above its predecessor is twofold: It's no longer trying to pull off more than it can chew. It still doesn't chew enough, but it doesn't get stuck in your throat when you try to swallow it. The story is more personal, so the characters get to have their little moments and feel like that actually matters. The narration and story is more tailored to the protagonist, who is entertaining to focus on in all her conflicted moody glory. The plot is introduced fast and focused on directly and constantly, so you can easier ignore it (because it's still garbage) and focus on the little things that make the experience meaningful. The scope is deliberately small, so at no point does it seem like the lack of choice is a technical failure. It just is more humble and so nothing gets in the way by the end. The writer might not have the ability to write a good story, but the writing is entertaining, so what does that matter? Which brings me to the second point... It doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥. Or maybe, I don't give a ♥♥♥♥. It just feels so more self-indulgently unhinged from the get-go that it begs to be engaged with on the line-by-line vibe, and on that front it delivers in spades. It's crass, it lives in the realms of references, it's unabashed in what it wants, and it does everything it wants without rhyme or reason. Sometimes, you could swear this is a Malkavian narrative. The prose lacks so much professionalism that its pageant for the low-brow becomes that much more delicious. It's fun. And that's the focus. The story just gets in the way sometimes.It does have a novel problem which it predecessor didn't have. The characters all sound the same. Nobody sounds distinct, which is especially apparent for the character who previously had actual personality to them. Instead everyone talks the same, says the same things, does everything in the same way, and only ever talks. They also seem to spout the exposition at you way more often than it makes sense. They are transparent vehicles of narration rather than characters who happen to illuminate it.In the end, I wouldn't say I wasn't awfully disappointed. This is very close to a "don't play this" kind of review. But since it's a mostly direct sequel to something that was already garbage, I can only recommend it to the person who managed to stomach the previous VN.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as modern visual novels go - this one is a keeper. There are some rough edges here and there; the world could have been bigger, the story longer and the characters brought to life in a more complex, vivid manner. However the author/developer(s) were clearly working with limited resources on a project that's meant to be a shorter form demonstration of what the VTM world could be (something I myself only have a very light understanding of).I guess my only criticism of the game is that I would have loved to see the devs working with more resources over an expanded development time period, like how some of the more iconic Japanese visual novels are made. There's much hint of greatness here that sadly remains limited in scope. Was this game worth my eight hours or so of playtime? I would say yes. And if you are specifically looking for a good visual novel experience, this is worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: A visual novel set in the World of Darkness universe. Depicts the power dynamics within the Camarilla and to some extent the Anarchs in New York. This is a standalone expansion to Vampire: The Masquerade - Coteries of New York, by the same developer, with yet another on the way. Not as distinctive / unique as that of Werewolf: The Apocalypse – Heart of the Forest, but still more than serviceable. Although some animated sequences are a bit odd, most panels contain minute animated details that improve the experience. These create an expectation that most animated elements will be diminutive, expectation that is at times subverted (e.g., by a large shadow striding down a corridor, behind frosted glass) that keep you immersed. Most of the time works great as background ambiance for the panels, but the main theme (Julia) is worth listening to on its own. The game does a good job interweaving multiple narrative threads, ranging from the main plot line (a murder mystery), evolution of interpersonal relations, and one-off encounters that don't have any impact on the overarching story but help reinforce the backdrop of the city. After finishing the game, you get a sense that you've been introduced to too many characters but spent too little time with any of them, considering your impact on their society and them, personally. Two playthroughs of the game are sufficient for completionists. You only have a good ending and a bad ending, determined by traits you acquire during the run. The decision tree is fairly simplistic, online guides stating that for one ending all you need to do is pick the top dialogue choice every time and for the other, the bottom choice. Regarding the one-off encounters, you are usually presented with a choice between 2-3 of them at a time, with the possibility of choosing 2 in a row when 3 are presented. The excluded choice will be locked for the remainder of the playthrough, so two runs are sufficient to experience everything. Your character is a rather angsty pseudo-intellectual reporter that is overall unlikeable, with precious few redeeming qualities. Playing her can become tiring after some time. I can only hope that the next game's protagonist will have a better personality; not less edgier, but less annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: For the mere cost of around 4 dollars, I got to play both "Coteries of New York" and "Shadows of New York". And what is it that there is to say about those games ?First of all, the narrative is enticing, endearing, and most characters are definitely well written. Something that one might expect from canon characters (like Kaiser or Prince Panhard), but even original characters created for the game are still very good and enjoyable.The graphic designs are very good too, the immersion is great, and the fact that very few pictures are completely still (even the CG are animated) makes it even more enjoyable. The darker colors and tones truly make a great job at representing the darker vibes of the World of Darkness. Music makes a very good job at this too.One thing I regret, however, is the fact that both stories are far too short. (Coteries' storyline can be completed in like 2 hours if it's not your first playthrough, and Shadow's could benefit from a longer storyline too).The major problem is that many problems and questions that were raised in Coteries are not resolved in Shadows, even though Shadows is a direct sequel.THIS BEING SAID : still very good games, and EXCELLENT introdution if you are truly a stranger to the World of Darkness in general and Vampire : the Masquerade in particular.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite good read, only qualm is that these stories seem to be like mini-series or mini-episodes, a mere glimpse into the world of darkness. After cotories and shadows of new york, it just leaves you with a... lingering hunger of sorts for more of these stories. The story is nothing short of thrilling with the right amount of intrigue in its flow to keep you on the toes of what's about to happen next? The usual movie/TV tropes don't apply as obviously as they do in Shadows of new york and the WoD Universe lends the game with even more intrigue as it is a widely underrated lore that most don't know about either. The plot twists or reveals are definitely witty and surprising in some turns which keeps you wondering who's what and what's when, even if you are highly accustomed to most of the mainstream tropes already.If you've already tried Cotories of New York, there is a good mention and tie in to the events and a few cameos that appear which breathes some soothing relief if you remembered what happened then...Also plus point!! Character story progression!! Not many games feature it well enough or pace it well but in shadows of new york you truly feel like going from nothing to a fledgling up to some semi-experience know it all randomly batting at the air with educated guesses that somehow luckily made it in the world.The only real negative point that doesn't line up is probably lesser and lesser controlled dialogues that appear in the sequels. Being part of the Lasombra clan only gives its aesthetics to the storytelling rather than allow you to dictate which powers you want to use at key points of the events. This problem exists in both visual novels and definitely is a weak point in the 'game' or linear story as compared to its more solid game comrades like Bloodlines/Swansong.TL;DR if you love a good "woah I didn't expect that" story, it is worth it especially at sale, understandably at $13 (in my region) it may be a bit pricey for something that can be done in 4 hours. It may not seem like a game to most gamers even as a visual novel as there are alot less gameplay mechanics or options present.Non-american friends may find it slightly "lame" or hard to relate to due to many american film references but nothing a short google doesn't help or if you've managed to watch these references before. _childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this unhesitatingly.Having read many of the reviews, I was expecting disappointment. I bought it anyway, when a sale popped up.I was *not* disappointed at all. I'd played the first game (Coteries of New York) and found it excellent - and this one is a perfectly fitting successor.It's absolutely at the least every bit as atmospheric. The art*, and the extraordinary custom soundtrack, are very carefully produced and used to enhance the story at every turn. Short animation sequences, subtle animated details in the static scenes, everything is deliberate and everything really really works.*(except the cars. The artist(s) absolutely cannot draw cars properly, for some reason)The big thing is the writing. A lot of the reviews I read shared a common thread - a strong dislike of the protagonist's character and attitude. There were a lot of people saying that the character was a sneering "woke" sort almost to the point of parody. Many reviewers condemned the writing as being heavily politically charged.I think this view is superficial and does the game and the writing a great injustice.Yes, the protagonist is a young, modern, woman. Ostensibly left-leaning, part of the zeitgeist, using a lot of the terminology and poses of the stereotype.But the writing isn't that shallow - with further exposure to the character we are shown that she's like anyone else, just trying to make sense of the worlds she's found herself in using the the understanding of the time she's in. To a reasonable extent, the persona is just that - a mask - like many of us wear when we're starting out in life, before we have the full confidence of our own experiences. A starting point, a framework to build from. A bit of a shield, a bit of a guess. A front. Arrogance masking vulnerability, a bit of a trope, but not heavy-handedly done. If you don't immediately bristle and take everything at face value, it's very easy to empathise with the poor protagonist, who - after all - is really just going from one highly unenviable situation to another throught our time with her.The character of our protagonist is not this one-dimensional "woke" caricature described by many other viewers. There's a lot more to it than that, and through the story we see a great deal of self-doubt, self-reflection, internal conflict, potential leaps, and personal growth.The characterisation which was done so well in the last game has absolutely been extended into this one, for so many of the characters. The writers have done an excellent job in conveying a very great deal of depth within the constraints of comparatively few words.There is no shortage of thought that has been put into this story - it's a story far more about the people than it is about the events, and that personal touch allows the art and the music to be used to incredible effect.Play this in a dark room, at night, take your time. It's one to savour. It's far more about the atmosphere than the plot, and if you really just sit and breathe it in, let the animations loop, let the music play, you'll get a very great enjoyment and value from it.I would have been perfectly happy even if I'd bought this at full price. It's actually a very memorable, thought-provoking, and sometimes moving semi-interactive experience, with a lot of heart despite the fairly flimsy plot.10/10 from me. I'm so glad I gave it a chance and didn't miss out.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10, though I kind of wonder if this VN would make sense to someone who has skipped the first game in the series. It's a direct sequel, though a weird one - it both introduces significant changes to its structure and gameplay, and feeds on the previously established characters and areas.Design-wise, Shadows of NY is not as interesting as Coteries, but that also means it avoids many of its predecessor’s pitfalls. It's a classic VN, though with only two possible endings (and that's OK) and a single romantic interest (which suits the story). Gone is the awkward character’s Clan selection with no real impact on the story - you get a pre-written character, whose class is tightly connected to the game’s plot. The protagonist has a strong personality, instead of being a vague avatar for the player. There’s hardly any gameplay, no Hunger / Feeding systems, no tutorials. The story is much more linear, but the few times you’re presented with a scene selection moment, the scenes feel somewhat unique and weird.Also, Shadows of NY spends much less time introducing you to Vampire the Masquerade world, and has a much broader glossary that you may, or may not, read. It hits the good balance between being accessible, and taking its most recognizable features as a given.Therefore, your enjoyment with the game will mainly depend on your personal taste as a reader. If you enjoy role-playing as a sexy, edgy young adult who wears a big cross on their chest and oftentimes entertains conversations about the meaning of life, faith, and depression, you may enjoy it. It’s also interesting to read a game that references pieces of art that came not that long before its release so directly, or even has its story somewhat tied to the 2020 start of the pandemic. Here, the line between pretentiousness and highbrow metafun is narrow, and you may land on any side, though if you enjoy World of Darkness in general, you’ll more likely to have fun. A few scenes connected with me emotionally, while some others made me only skim through the text. It’s not a masterpiece, and it abandoned its adventure game side for good, but if you’re OK with the Visual Novel format, this one does its job well.

They look down on you, don't understand your complex background and cultural references. You can swear all you want, just don't overuse the well-known k-swear. You get the worst jobs possible without a proper contract, meaning you may or may not be paid depending on the mood of your boss. Forget about OSH. Prepare for the constant nagging of the local catholic priest and his ultra-consersative followers (don't tell them you are in a same-sex relationship).Oh you also get Embraced into the Lasombra clan and are left alone in a Camarilla city. The conditions don't change much but you are now immortal. I enjoyed this one more than CONY but the story of SONY relies heavily on the main game so I recommend playing them in a sequence to get the "oh hey I remember who you are!".

_childDocuments_.review: Shadows of New York is a sequel to 'Coteries of New York',Shadows of New York has more satisfying conclusions, at the expense of fewer player choices and more restrictive roleplaying. The prose feels down to earth and human (as ironic as that may seem), with genuine and believable interactions. The scale of the narrative is quite small -- the player interacts with a small part of a large world. As with Coteries of New York, the game has a focus on Camarilla/Anarch power dynamics (vampire politics), placing the protagonist in an impassionately crushing world. What Shadows of New York gains in a more consistent and... satisfying(?) story and dialogue, it loses with fewer oddballs and personalities.You can see the art for yourself, the gorgeous style and theming features subtle animations that play an unspoken role in making dialogue just a bit more dynamic.I stopped playing halfway through to just listen to the soundtrack, which itself is full of melodramatic pianos, drones, and gritty patches. A perfect accompaniment to an urban fantasy theme and the protagonist's bleak future optics throughout the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly really enjoyed this game, as well as Coteries of New York.  These were my first real exposure to any Vampire: The Masquerade stuff, and I gotta say, they managed to get me very interested in the world with these games!  They're really well written visual novels, particularly Shadows.This game's a lot more linear than Coteries, but honestly I think that's fine since the choices in Coteries had limited impact on the story.  This allows the narrative in Shadows to be stronger I think.  You've still got some choices, though for the most part they only impact the immediate scene for a few lines, with only a handful giving you a trait that helps determine which ending you get.  Also a big fan of the soundtrack of this, very ominous and foreboding.I'd recommend this for fans of visual novels that want to see about the world of V:tM, or people who are already fans and want to see a short visual novel in the world set up by New York by Night. Well, I was very disappointed.This time, the player can't choose one of three playable characters. The main character is Julia, a very rude person thinking she's the most important person in the world. Disrespectful, egocentric, uninteresting. I couldn't really care about the story, sorry. Whatever. This game feels like some taken out story from the other game, made into a separate game not worth your and my time. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: First, this is the sequel to Coteries of New York. So play that first, otherwise this game won't be as fun. Coteries is a well told story, and Shadows is even better, but not without playing Coteries first.Second, the game takes less than 10 hours to see all endings. It's good, but if you're working on a budget then you'll want to buy this game on sale (which happens a lot).Third, this game's story impacts the larger WoD meta-narrative. So if you're a fan of L.A. By Night, Vampire: Swansong, or are eagerly awaiting the (yet to be release) Bloodlines 2, you'll want to give this game a try.All that out of the way, this game (like most of the WoD titles out nowadays) is a visual novel of sorts. It sits somewhere between the very very good writing of Night Roads, but with visuals to keep things a little more engaging than black text on white backgrounds. You don't use disciplines as much as in Coteries, and this title is much less "gamey" than the others, but it's unique in its own way that's enjoyable. Think of Shadows as a much needed sequel and ending to the stuff that happened in Coteries.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: A great continuation of Coteries of New York. Like the previous game the art/sound design and overall story is also great too. Player agency is a bit higher but still at a bare minimum with 2 endings instead of 1 ending that Coteries of New York has offered. The endings are more satisfying too. But of course there is a room for improvement for example: there are only a few CGs. The ones that are present are great but more CGs(arts) would make the future games better in a visual sense or having more endings and most importantly more forks(major decision dwellings ) in the story that mattered, this game really lacks those. But overall if you liked more or less linear visual novels then this is your choice, it doesn't have much important decisions and variety but linearly story is great. Have a nice day!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a darkly immersive, very aesthetic vampire story, that is where this one shines. It is well-made in this respect, and plays similarly to Werewolf The Apocalypse: Heart of the Forest, which I loved. I think this one is better, though!Overall it was awesome. It's like they put Jessica Jones into the world of darkness, which should tell you something about where most mixed opinions are coming from:I think some people who review this come into it with the wrong expectations. I haven't played "Coteries" yet, but it's important to understand that these games likely have very different visions behind them, and so you're not supposed to expect the same things from them. This is not in the same vein as an old-school pen & paper RPG, it's more of a classical visual novel.What makes this one great is a very interesting, character-driven underdog story in an eerie and compelling setting, with a rough first few minutes (my main complaint.) It will necessarily be hit or miss, because like any story you won't necessarily like the main character. But I encourage everyone to be open-minded to experience it on its own terms.It's unfair to not recommend this title based on expecting something that it's not supposed to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

I would have really appreciated if I could search the beautifully painted scenes looking for clues and had a third (or, I guess fourth) possible ending where I successfully piece all the clues and motives together to actually solve the crime.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr: I would recommend this game even if you haven't played Coteries of New York, and even if you aren’t familiar with the Vampire the Masquerade setting. It is one of the best visual novels I’ve ever played, and might have the best writing I’ve come across so far.Whereas Coteries of New York was a dark, always threatening, out of control experience, Shadows (SoNY) isn’t as horrific, but instead has more warmth and even humor – as much as a noir and Vampire the Masquerade setting will allow for, at least. Ironically, it was only in the so called "Good Ending" that things got really dark for me. Recurring characters that filled me with cold fear in Coteries and made me afraid to make any mistakes at all, are here bantering with me, and telling jokes – the tone is just very different. In theory some of it could be said to come down to the differing roles the protagonists of the two games have, but it's just not enough of an explanation – the two games have very different tones to them, which also changes how the recurring characters are interpreted, and I'm fine with that, since I enjoy this interpretation more, making it one of the best visual novels I’ve ever played. The protagonist in SoNY has much more of their own voice, and personality, which infuses everything in the world with their perspective, and I believe it could be primarily the same writer(s) that were behind Hopes awesome storyline in the predecessor that have here been given free reign to become very personal in their style, a style that has the same rawness as for example Chuck Palahniuks prose (the guy who wrote Fight Club). It is a voice that I hope returns in future visual novels - like for real, I even read the dictionary entries in this game explaining things I already learned in Coteries of New York just because the voice/writing was so strong in this game that it was just a pleasure to read.I also thought this game had more engaging and beautiful music than Coteries, whereas the artwork was just as impeccable, which makes the artwork in these two games my absolute favorite ones in the domain of visual novels (although I have a soft spot for Moacubes Solstice, as well). This game had less dialogue choices than Coteries, but a much more engaging story, and well thought-out and satisfying endings. In this game ”traits” were also introduced, which are awarded to our protagonist upon making certain choices, which further dictates how she approaches things, automatically, which I think is a very cool thing, even if I would enjoy knowing when said traits kick in and change around dialogue, though.All in all – superb. And if you want another recommendation for an awesome visual novel with vampires in it, I would recommend trying out the lesser known ”Tell a Demon”, which is quite a bit shorter than SoNY, but has much more divergence/reactivity, making i natural to replay a bunch of times to get a better picture of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I can understand the points made in the negative reviews. The story is fairly linear with only 2 possible, but very satisfying, endings. Overall, I recommend Shadows of New York if you're a fan of Visual Novels, World of Darkness or if you loved Coteries of New York.

_childDocuments_.review: A more cohesive narrative than the predecessor 'Coteries of New York' with a protagonist, actually deserving of the description character. Compared to the protagonist from 'Coteries', Julia has traits to her character, which determine her general approach and behavior in a situation and a central tension around her relationship to the concept of hope. What makes one hope? How do different characters in the story define hope? Her own jaded view on the world straining against her tendency to empathize and her wanting to help others. Yes, these descriptions are a little vague, but it is the biggest strength of the game and its story, how Julia is developed and interacts with the world around her. A strength one should experience through play.By way of receiving characterization, Julia easily beats the vague, non-descript protagonist from 'Coteries'. Where Julia has a place in the fictional world, has believes and an established moral foundation for her behavior, this other (slightly customizable) protagonist was simply a tool to interact with the game world. A rather limited avatar for the player, who could never live up to the TTRPG source material and its wealth of possible approaches to a situation, while suffering as a character by lacking a defined ... well, character.With the protagonist as the strongest element, the story cleverly connects her to the fictional world and Kindred society in New York City. Her journey from life as an investigative journalist, over the process of the Embrace to the current events pushing her back in the role of an investigator is concise and avoids clutter. It is an intensely personal experience with moments of horror mixed in, all of which have nothing to do with literal monsters, but the things we do to people and the things we should have done. Regret, rejection and ignorance play a major role. Anyone wanting to have a brush with the World of Darkness and doesn't need a whole lot of visually exciting action, can buy this game, play it and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd definitely recommend it, and while it IS a direct sequel to Coteries, I wouldn't necessarily recommend playing that one first. The story and characters of the first do play a role here, but it's not particularly necessary to know them ahead of time. Frankly, Coteries is worse in every way, though Shadows is not without its faults too.Pros:- Absolutely fantastic music reminiscent of Disco Elysium's top-tier dramatically moody tracks- Beautiful art- The story is a very engaging whodunnit of political intrigue. It really exemplifies what Vampire the Masquerade is all about- Writing and characters are interesting, especially the main protagonist- Everything is appropriately moody and filled with self hate, but with a wonderful lack of edgelord cringe- Choices matter more than in Coteries, *sorta*. Basically there are 5 choices that will determine which of the two endings you get, everything else is just flavour. I'm giving it enough of a pass to call it a positive, but don't expect wild branching paths here. As long as you know this going in, it's an enjoyable ride.Cons: - Speaking of, unlike in Coteries, where you'd decide what characters to see and when, this one is much more railroady. ALL of the main story content is fixed. What you choose to do with the in-between time is entirely flavour. None of the side activities seem to have any relevance to the plot or characters, thus making them feel incredibly pointless- The player is not given the final choice of what to do at the very end. Instead, the protagonist decides for herself based on 5 key choices the player made throughout the game. This can (and did for me) lead to the character acting in a way that the player didn't want in the final confrontation. However, after my initial disappointment, I actually liked the outcome that it led to, UNTIL I GOT THE ACHIEVEMENT:Basically my biggest gripe, as petty as it seems, is the fact that they named the endings "Good Ending" and "Bad Ending". After getting both of them, they're both well written and satisfying in their own ways. It's exactly what you want from a"choice-driven" visual novel, yet to qualify either as good or bad severely devalues or overvalues the result. Really took me out of the moment. They should've called it "Lasombra Ending" and "Kine Ending" or something similar. But as I said, it's a bit of a petty complaint, so if THAT'S the biggest bother, than obviously the game overall is quite good.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth playing for the art alone; it's moody, atmospheric and gorgeous. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool interactive novel. Not quite as involved as the first one, but still makes me really excited to continue my journey through the VTM universe!I like that this is a stand-alone game in the sense that you don't *have* to have played the previous game in order to play this one, but it makes the story more interesting if you have. There are overlaps here and there, but I don't fell stuck in that same story line.I also like the addition of the "traits" system. It reminds me of a bare-bones version of the personality traits system in The Dark Pictures Anthology games (Man of Medan, Until Dawn, Little Hope). Choices your character make define who they are as a character and effect the outcome of later decisions. Makes for a more immersive, unique experience and also makes replays enjoyable and desirable.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it only to the point that you know what to expect ...I had very average expectations before I tried it ; other than I like the Vampire The Masquerade (VtM) setting.  The writing in the introduction was to my liking!  It starts slow, but for good reason.  Without much fanfare, through the eyes and thoughts of the character, it highlights some good existential questions about our choices in life, how we live. I won't say more, not to spoil anything.  I will only say I like the writing, which is valuable as I have seen a lot of bad writing in video games.  It flows well. Respect. The setting, how you slowly discover the characters, your vampire clan... A nice experience. You can guess it is an interactive novel, but really easy to read, in short dialogues and thoughts.  Before you buy, you must be told that impactful decisions are FEW and far between.  Most dialogue choices are not actual decisions, but later a few rare decisions determine Traits that in turn *determine* the ending ...  Many of the decisions are written in very vague and confusing ways, so you do not really know what you are deciding, which makes them not real decisions.  I was able to guess the meaning of the cryptic choices during the story and had a "good" ending.   The short vague options are not a design choice I am fond of.  It looks purposefully designed so that you feel you should play a second time and try different choices (and you cannot backtrack to a past save, except by forcibly closing the game the wrong way). I recommend it, at a low price, as long as you know what to expect (eg. the graphics are a few paintings, the gameplay is not original and is vague, though it has a nice style).  It is a cool story and very good in terms of describing how psychology could change from Human to Vampire. The polls online (about 70 players) show an average of 6-7 hours to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: A good sequel to the original, and deliciously fun if you're a fan of Vampire the Masquerade. There is more choice and agency in endings this time through, though both the games in this series are more similar to interactive novels than open ended video games. I really enjoyed this as it tied up the plot threads from the original, and also featured a cameo (Katherine Weiss) from Vampire lore - the "good", and "bad" ending are both fun and bittersweet, and neither is a "preferrable" outcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: A very good take on the Lasombra Clan, managing to create an original character without those artificial clan ties to the church, sea, and other nonsense old Masquerade lore. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully written game with compelling characters, atmospheric sound design and gorgeous art. A clearer story and a wholesale improvement on the already solid first game. Only minor complaint is that it can be tough figuring out exactly whether you're doing the right thing or not - but the characters and world kept me engrossed regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: So so so much better than Coteries. If you are here after playing the first one and contemplating whether you should get this, the answer is yes.First of all, it's longer. Not that "longer" necessarily means better, but in this case it certainly does. You get more time to explore your character and soak up the atmosphere, and I didn't get the feeling that everything ended before the cogs even started to turn.Secondly, it's infinitely more satisfying. Instead of choosing 3 noname characters which were supposed to be "our protagonists" but ended up being useless puppets, here we are presented with an already shaped character (and well-written at that). The choices actually matter, and neither of the two main avenues feels forced onto the protagonist (as she has seeds of both in her and it just depends on which ones you water and nourish). Julia indeed feels like an independent actor rather than a silent observer with no say in whatever the game tosses at you. FInally, it's gorgeous. the artwork, the music, the writing - a great experience.I hope whatever comes next will be even better.

_childDocuments_.review: This would be another game I would put a "Meh" or "Either/Or" review, the thumbs up/down system can be too restrictive. I received this game from a friend picking apart a bundle. After going back and forth, I'd give a Cautious Recommend to get on sale.Positives:-It drips with atmosphere, even in the club and coney island there's a moody sense of isolation, grime, and the feeling of being adrift without a paddle, combining art, music, and word choice to get into Julia's head.-Art: Character art is good, even many one-off characters have a model, and you can get a sense of who they are at a first glance. -Writing: I'm going to separate this from story, but it's extremely evocative, from the description of the kiss, a character's lament on the loss of 90s-era internet, it's writing that elicits emotions. It also doesn't fall into the trap of having characters explain things that Lisa should known, instead highlighting the terms for you to look up, so dialogue sounds more organic, if a touch 2edgy4you. The choice of giving you a defined character with a background and clan is a smart one - it means that they can tighten the focus and not write around all possibilities, or fall back on extremely generic dialogue choices that does little to give you insight on who you play. Julia is not a nice person, she's bitter and resentful as anyone would be in her circumstances, with a couch full of unresolved issues and trauma from her mortal life that doesn't get better - but the deft writing spins them all into a whole human being, a little broken but someone you probably passed by without knowing.Neutral:-Story: You're never meant to solve the mystery, and the game hammers in that Julia is really a nobody and a pawn in a wider game, it can leave a sour taste in people's mouths. It does however work as a story of someone trying to find new meaning in a life they never asked for. It's not a particularly deep plot either with hints that you're basically on the ancillary of a much more intriguing plot. This kind of story is not for everyone.Negative:-It's very short, a slow reader would finish it in about seven hours, and skipping to get the other ending if you didn't save at a good spot would give you another half hour at most. I am not expecting Umineko-level of read time for the price, but seven and a half hours is very short for a VN.-No native option to adjust screen size, or windowed it. or for text to appear instantly. -Yes there is a skip button, but you have to figure it out yourself - it's CTRL for the record, and when you save and quit there's no option to save in the other slots, making it slightly inconvenient to go back and see alternative scenes.The What:The endings being labelled "Good" and "Bad" doesn't make much sense to me, I feel like other names would more accurately fit their overall themes, Does Lisa embrace her life as a Lasombra, or does she stubbornly insist on keeping some of her humanity regardless of the cost?

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr A tentative recommendation. if this game is on sale, if you like visual novels, if you think you'll be able to put up with the game lacking save and skip functions, get it. Story and art are great, but the lack of certain QoL features and it's short length make it not worht it for the cost outside of a sale.This is a visual novel game set in the world of Vampire: The Masquerade. Like other visual novels, the gameplay consists of reading scrolling text and watching scenes play out, while occasionally being given multiple choice options to dictate what actions the protagonist will take, with your choices leading to different endings. The art, the music, the setting, the story, I find all of these to be top notch. I have two main concerns though: the game is missing certain QoL features that most other visual novels have, and the length of the game. First off, a visual novel, because it allows different choices and thus different endings, demands multiple playthroughs. Thus most visual novels will have features that make this convenient, such as allowing saving before difficult choices, or skipping scenes the player has already seen. This game does not have that. So if you want to play through the game again to see a different ending, instead of being able to hold down the ctrl key or just select a skip option, you have to painstakingly go through every bit of dialogue via the enter key or left-clicking your mouse. Even the enter key isn't safe, as I have several times ruined a run this way by selecting an option I did not want this way, since hitting the enter key when a choice is presented appears to select the topmost option. It makes one wonder if it is even worth it to try to achieve other endings? I recommend you get this game like I did: wait for a sale, such as the Paradox publisher sale for PDXCon.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Lazy art work with reused backgrounds from the previous game, why do we not have a choice of characters like in the previous one? _childDocuments_.review: Although I can't give this game a lauding review, let's at least start with some positives:The ambience of the game is properly World of Darkness / Vampire the Masquerade. From how utterly depressing the main character (the player) is from the very start of the game to the over the top pseudo-philosophical 'revelations'. I like that the ending is decided by your decisions throughout the game and not something you can just decide on at the last moment, but . The story telling has some unique moments and it's nice to see a bit more from clan La Sombra, but overall it's all quite predictable and your average fan fiction will have more depth.The game itself however is very short and I don't feel the price tag is justified. In part, this is because the lack of content, but there are other factors at play too. A lot of the graphics, both in terms of locations and character models, are directly re-used from Coteries of New York. The vast majority of the dialog options (of which there are far too few) have absolutely no impact on the story progression and tend to give you 1 or 2 sentences of alternative dialogue (if even that.) As for decisions that do impact the ending, there are about 5 of them, some feel fairly forced and some are just misleading .To conclude: Sit in this chair, Sit in this chair, Sit in this chair.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: A vast improvment on the first game Coteries of New York. The music,art,characters, and story are 10/10. If you love the world of Darkness and/or you live visual novels where your choices matter, this game is perfect for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I know nothing about this franchise, I just picked Shadows of New York up in a Humble Choice and thought it looked interesting, but I enjoyed it quite a bit anyway. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: This "episode" of the Vampire series (Coteries of New York being the first) is better than the original. The artwork is better and more varied, animations in the background are more numerous, and the overall story is an improvement.That said, it is the same 'ol situation as the original - you are completely railroaded through the story and choices basically do not matter. This is by far more of a visual novel than a game.The terrible part is that you are essentially a passive observer to the story and never become a PART of the story.Many of the original cast make their return and they did a good job referencing events from the first story into this one making one feel as though there is continuity.Overall I give this a solid 5 of 10. The main reason being that you just spend 2-3 hrs hitting enter and reading far faster than the text appears. After that, it's game over. Not a game, just a visual novel.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but with qualifications -- this is not a game for everyone.If you're familiar with the World of Darkness and you're familiar, in particular, with Vampire: The Masquerade, AND if you're interested in a narrative, essentially text-based novella where your choices are by necessity limited, you will find this an entertaining way to spend a few hours. The English version of the game is pretty well written, with some typos and grammatical errors, but these are in the main minor and don't really distract from the story, in my opinion.I've played both Shadows of New York and Coteries of New York, and while Shadows is essentially a "sequel" (in truth it isn't, but rather a follow-up story set in the same "universe" and building on the events of Coteries) and is shorter, I actually preferred this one to its predecessor. The writing is more accomplished, and more mature, and the commitment to a single protagonist voice -- you play Julia, recently Embraced into the Lasombra -- give the narrative genuine strength.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice story line that reminds me of the choose your own adventure. You'll get different responses from your answers but in the end there are very few (ie. 1) time which will change your ending options. The game is worth a single solid play through. To unlock all the achievements I also did a speed playthrough just for fun and to explore the locations I did not get to. The game takes place over around 8 nights. It is a good throw back to the days of narrative story telling and the art style is on point for the grunge of the Masquerade. The game is true to it's source material and it is nice to see the in game dictionary provide information to those who do not know it.I would highly recommend getting the game. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stylistically very interesting and tells an equally interesting story.However, your choices seem even more limited than those of most average visual novels which can hamper the fun with it if you don't find as much enjoyment in the story itself. There are still multiple endings and on my first playthrough the ending fit the gameplay I chose, I will need a few playthroughs more to find out if that holds true for other playstiles as well.Lore Wise it also breaks with how final death is portrayed for the sake of making it work as a murder-mystery story, which in my opinion is completely fine, but I could guess that absolute lore-buffs in Vampire the Masquerade might dislike this slightly, since it changes the lore in telling their story instead of trying to find a way to tell their compelling story around the lore.The Story is ultimatively a murder mystery story that worked, at least for me. The writing is interesting to say the least and it's reference heavy and very much a product of it's time, with the game not only acknowledging the current pandemic but referencing it in the story. The game has a chance to age quite badly because of the movie references inside of it.I can't shake the feeling that the game was rushed into a release.So in the end all I can say is that there are some caveats that might hamper your enjoyment of the game, but if none of these are a deal-breaker for you and you are able to treat it like a choose your own adventure book instead of as a game, then I can recommend it for some light and interesting reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sequel to Coteries of New York, though in my opinion is aided by you not having any meaningless choices that parade as character customization, like picking clans. If you liked Coteries of New York, you'll like this one. If you like VtM/World of Darkness, and don't mind visual novels, then you'll probably like this one. Playing Coteries of New York will help you understand some of the characters better, but I don't believe it's necessary to play it before playing Shadows.Personally, I love the VtM universe, and while I don't particularly like visual novels, I found Shadows of New York was still enjoyable. There isn't a ton of choices in this game, but many of those choices will effect how the character acts throughout the game in their more automatic decision making, and change the "monologues" (often how your character is internalizing the information she receives) that go with them.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Forget about Bloodlines, Vampire the Masquerade: Coteries and Shadows of New York are the real pinnacle of World of Darkness storytelling. Both games are equally as fantastic, but this review is about Shadows, which is a sequel to Coteries. In a thrilling finale to the series, we follow the story of a recently fired investigative journalist, Julia Sowinski in her climb to the top of the vampire society. Will she be able to overcome her struggles and the traps set by the New York's night elite?I just couldn't put this game down. It felt shorter than the first one, and it had some minor differences, but overall it was a great experience. Would definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, a great art style and soundtrack, interesting characters, but few endings (2 and a fail state ending) and a sort of muddled set of secondary quests mar an otherwise excellent short visual novelIt almost feels like the first handful  chapters of a larger work and I would love to see more from Draw Distance in the WoD setting in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is quite good. If you like the VTM theme and lots of reading then this will appeal.  If that appeals then its definitely worth picking up at a decent price e.g. when on sale. StoryThe story content is quite solid and self contained. Its well written and sets out a compelling VTM themed world. They also include lots of details that aren't really part of the main story. These exist to build up the main character and her relationships and background. This is a nice touch since ultimately the role playing aspect is a significant part of the appeal.GameplayThe game is multiple choice but follows a very tight story. Quite often these choices are actually just for role playing flavour and don't really impact what comes next. However, some decisions will alter the outcome in small ways. The main choices are ones which decide your "personality." The ending you get will then be based on the overall personality rather than other choices.Replay valueGiven how text heavy the game is you'll probably only play it through for the different endings. My own play time includes two run throughs and a fair bit of time with the game open in the background. I'd suggest the main game can be played at a reasonable pace and completed in one long sitting if you really wanted to.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire The Masquarade - Shadows of New York is loosely connected to Coteries of New York and I recommend getting that game first. Both titles are an introduction to World of Darkness,  both are visual novels. Still, “Shadows...”  takes place after “Coteries...” and involves plenty of recurring characters.  It could be enjoyed as a stand-alone experience nevertheless. This time, as a member of a clan recently accepted into the Camarilla, the player is tasked with explaining a mysterious death of a vampire baron. Is it a serious investigation or... a set up? Who is pulling the strings? As always, diving into politics is inevitable... can You handle the situation properly? “Shadows..” presents a bit more fleshed out narrative than Coteries. Fixing the issue of it’s predecessor story being completely “on rails”, this time the player has two distinct ways of developing the protagonist. It’s not much, still more than before. Welcomed change, two possible endings are always better than one :) Shadows of New York plays it’s cards right, presenting an interesting story and building on the fundaments of the first game. It’s again, very atmospheric, engaging experience with really great soundtrack. If you liked Coteries of New York - you’ll like Shadows of New York. As simple as that.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the first game a lot, and this is a great followup so far. Way more of a straightforward visual novel than the first, but the lore of the world allows for a good deal of storytelling. Only a few hours in though, so I am excited to see what clans and pieces of the storytelling they decide to bring in. But, if you've played the first game, you are familiar with its' tragic failing - forgetting how to end a game appropriately. For all I know, I'm 2 minutes from rolling credits? TIME WILL TELL, but I still absolutely recommend.

Julia's story feels like the table-top game, with the usual scheming elder's political job I neither want, nor am qualified for. Which of course is the point. Oh such sweet politicking. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: This builds on the previous more open Coteries of of New York by only having one well constructed character you are role playing, they also take out the feeding mechanism which I think helped the pacing a lot. Although, playing this right after Coteries left me anxious to look for feeding opportunities since that was a bigger mechanic in the previous game. Maybe I was starting to feel like an actual vampire? Anyways, this one was excellently made and had me really feeling like I was experiencing the unlife of Julia as she entered the Masquerade. Once again, more than a visual novel with animations, music and sounds. I did not realize how much more impactful my choices would be this time around until I got a game over at the very first choice I received in game!I did get the good ending, and I am not sure quite if I want to go back to get the alternate ending yet (I feel like I would still make the same choices). I feel that this will be like a good book where eventually, some time down the line, I can pick it pack up again and once more immerse myself in this small corner of the world and be surrounded by my Kindred once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement over Coteries of New York, with a more focused story and a wonderfully written main character. Might be hard to get into if you aren't familiar with VtM (despite the team's efforts to explain every term through the in-game dictionary), and I would definitely recommend playing Coteries of New York first to get a full grasp of the characters.Also I love Julia, but as with the first game, I need Qadir to kiss me pronto thanks
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I can't deny, it's my favourite vampire game. It's short, it's sweet, I just wish there was more of it. The characters are intriguing, Julia's way of entering the world is a lot of fun, and the illustrations are quite pretty; but a lot of the exposition feels inelegant and somewhat hurried - particularly around the beginning - due I presume to the brevity of the experience. Still, what it lacks in grace, more than makes up for in character. It's a fun, thoughtful dive into the world of the masquerade, and I can recommend it wholeheartedly. Just remember rule no1: Don't talk about bite club.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: This completely surprised me as I don't usually like the idea of railroad visual story's with emotional undertones, but this is by far the best game I have ever played. The Soundtrack is amazing and the best to any game I've ever listened to, the artwork is great.Perhaps the conclusion could have been easier for the player to follow, but if you pick up the little things it all makes sense in the end.I thoroughly recommend trying this game even if it traditionally the kind of Genre you don't like, this is coming from someone who tends to prefer open world survival/shooter games which is the opposite of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, I got the VTM New York games (Coteries and Shadows) from a bundle, and on complete whim without regard for plot continuity decided to play Shadows first. I played Coteries afterwards.The result of this sequence of play meant that I actually knew nothing about a lot of what was going on in the story behind the scenes and of the past events that might have made sense to someone who played it in chronological order. Amusingly, I think it might have helped with the immersion, being that I wound up being just as lost as the main character was, just fumbling my way around from area to area. One thing I appreciate about this over Coteries (I'm writing this review after having played both) is that this at least gives you two endings. What I don't appreciate, however is for the game to label them "GOOD" and "BAD". Literally they're achievements you get for each one. It's like, you want to make an improvement from Coteries, giving the players a sense of choice in getting the ending that they might have wanted, only for them to be snubbed by an achievement that might slap them in the face with an achievement going "BAD ENDING". Which was the case for me, and I quite liked the so-called "BAD" ending too, so colour me biased. Nevertheless, like with Coteries, I think the art is decent (really, a lot of it is just straight up reused so this isn't saying much). Like I mentioned above, I think the characters were great, more likable even, and the music struck me as nicer compared to Coteries. All in all, it's a game I think I can recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Massive downgrade from Coteries of New York. We go from the ability to choose our protagonist and customise their personality to having one protagonist with a defined personality. A personality that is very grating at times. At least in the prior entry there was a minor degree of interactivity, there's options here and there but we have almost no control over Julia Sowinski. A sequel should provide more options not remove them.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: So it is a good story that is interesting to experience. The images are fitting, the sound builds on the sense and the story is current. However, the interactive choices in this story are fairly limited. A very small number of them impact the story in any significant way. So don't expect this to be to much content.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game from the beginning to the end. Unlike the Coteries of New York, where the beginning seemed to me to be a cliché and I really started enjoying it only in the second half, the Shadows of New York had a great atmosphere and immersion right from the start. Personally I think that not giving the player a choice of a character and having a single character with a great back-story is much better for the visual novel genre.  I really hope more games are coming in the series!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game, but conditionally. This was the first "interactive novel" I've ever played, and the results were a mixed bag. The protagonist's internal thoughts are poorly written and come across as those of a whiny and annoying college student. However, the actual dialogue and interactions between characters are gripping, and the central mystery is intriguing to both those new and familiar with the World of Darkness. Still, a game that bases itself around story and writing needs consistent quality, and this ain't it. Maybe get it on sale if you're a fan of the lore like I am.Also for a game set during the COVID pandemic, it's pretty freaking weird that none of the Kine were wearing masks. Artistic oversight or ham-fisted politics? You decide!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Superbly written, illustrated and scored, love the characters, there are some nice twists and satisfying endings, criticisms of not enough branches in story may be valid, but as a visual novel it is gripping and drenched in atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: A darker and more satisfying story. ProsGreat Protagonist - Interesting and flawed but has great qualities that add depth to the story.Great Dark Atmosphere - the soundtrack, color scheme, and art style really immerse you into a darker side of the city. Adds an unease and tension to your decisions. The painterly chaotic imagery enhances the narrative and the illustrations are top notch.Interesting Characters - like Coteries of New York most of the characters you come across are interesting and rarely dull. The art style helps with this as well. Everything has a purpose and meshes well with past characters.Improved Lore - and feels true to the World of Darkness lore over the previous installment.Multiple Endings - though only a few it's better than the previous installments illusion of having your choices not effect the end. ConsLack of Chapters/ Save areas - This installment only follows one character but if I want to replay sections you'll have to start from scratch. Not a huge issue. _childDocuments_.review: This is part 2 of a visual novel series (part 1 is "Coteries of New York"). You do not have to have played part 1 to experience the full story, it just helps to understand some of the characters better.In this visual novel, you play as a recently turned vampire who was created to--essentially--be a low-level vampire bureaucrat. Obviously the story picks up intensity and before you know it, you're tasked with solving a whodunit.Unlike "Coteries of New York", in this visual novel you can actually change the ending. Huzzah!The characters and prose are overall much better than part 1. The writers are definitely hitting their stride.The art and music are excellent and definitely set the tone.Price. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed it. Is it worth full price? Maybe, if you're already a fan of the VtM universe. As an independent game, maybe not. Shadows of New York is a direct sequel to Coteries of New York, meaning many of the main characters and locations from Coteries show up (as well as some new faces and places), and the major plot points from Coteries influence the story in Shadows. In terms of similarities, Shadows of New York has the same beautiful art, soundtrack, and atmosphere that draw you into its prequel. In terms of differences, well...Improvements:- Story. I'm a sucker for a good murder mystery. Although it takes a while to pick up, the suspense is well-maintained, and the vampire politics tie into the story much better this time around.- Character Development. Already loved all the characters from Coteries. Now I love them more.- Dialogue(?) This one might be more a matter of personal taste, since there are a lot more references to modern politics and pop culture. But aside from a slightly clunky beginning, conversations between characters come across a lot more genuine and entertaining.The Negatives:- Gameplay. (Can you call it gameplay if you spend 99.9% of your time clicking "continue"?).- Very text-heavy. Lots of exposition, especially at the start. Conversations can go on for a while without any input from the player's end.- Choices? What choices? It took a third of the game before I reached my first "Big Decision". Coteries at least offers you some agency in choosing your sideplots. You get some of that here, but it never really feels as impactful. Some dialogue options seem to range between "Shut up!" and "Shut the hell up!"The Neutral:- Did not like what they did with Kaiser's character, loved what they did with Benoit's character.-  The story ties in with the main character's Eastern European heritage and relationship with religion/spirituality, which was a huge plus for me.- They tied COVID into this too??
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! What a ride!Every single criticism I had of Vampire: The Masquerade - Coteries of New York has been addressed by Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York. It's called a "standalone expansion", and maybe it is, but it is so much better than the original game in every single way. But I guess, like "Mask of the Betrayer" needed the slog of NWN2, "Shadows" needed "Coteries" to set the stage for a fantastic story.You play Julia Sowinski, a freelance journalist who is embraced by the Losambra Clan as part of their rehabilitation into the Camarilla. You're no longer a central pawn in the games of the court, but a nobody who's suddenly thrust into the limelight. The game is set several months after "Coteries", and you get to meet with many of the same characters, and a few surprise characters from the oWoD mythology. It is so awesome, I squee'd when I saw them."Shadows" has amazing music. It's bass-y and dark and gothic and moody, and just fits the theme of the game so well. The art is incredible. They've added some amazing vignettes, like the one for Julia looking down onto Times Square, like a vampire Batman. This time around, the characters also have more than one pose and expression. Julia, especially, is so amazingly emotive. I, like, totally <3 her, and I want to play a Losambra in more games.Hunger plays less of a factor this time around. Certain decision points lead to Julia earning traits, which may lead to one of two endings. They're labelled as "good" and "bad", but honestly, they both looked like wins to me. They really do fit in with how you've been playing Julia.Along the way, there are "optional" side missions. Beyond the main missions, you have "time" to play two out of three that you get every night, so you get a bit of replayability there as well.I loved this game, and even if I only got 4 hours of play out of it, it's been totally worth it. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York

_childDocuments_.review: This is a damn good game. Strong writing with very satisfying endings. Both the overall plot and the prose in this game is wonderful, and I enjoyed it the whole way through. Intrigue piles upon intrigue in ways that *hint* at the truth, but don't quite get you there. There is a mystery, but not the kind of mystery where it can be wrapped up with everything explained. No, things go much deeper than that. It was a refreshing change of pace to be in a mystery where "whodunit?" was one of the lesser concerns.If you've played Vampire: Bloodlines, don't be confused. This is a visual novel. When you get one ending, just use the guide on this site to get the other. You have to start over, but it really takes like 5 minutes to get back to the end because using CTRL for fast forward is SO fast. They are both great endings in different ways and you will want to see both. They call them "good" and "bad", and that's true in a very specific way, but not in the way you might  be thinking.

Think The Matrix's Architect and his arrogant explanation of "how the world really is".All that said, the work that went into carefully crafting New York by night is great, and still worth experiencing.
