_childDocuments_.review: Stuck on an infinite loop of death at level 4. Not sure if it was level 4 or 5 but it was right after you fight the Twin boss. Cut scene plays. My character grapples to the top and just falls to his death. I mashed buttons, mashed jump, held the directional keys, and even just let it play out thinking the creator is pulling a Metal Gear Solid 3 with the Sorrow but no. Just stuck in a perma death loop.I'm sorry. I know this was a one-man show but I requested a refund until this is addressed. There's also some conveyance issues that I didn't like: the mid boss in level 2, I try grappling over him and nope, not supposed to do that. Try jumping over him when he does that bull rush attack and just couldn't do it. I ended up beating him (on Normal) by just taking the hit. Get to the boss of level 2 and it's clear how the creator wants you to dodge the flame attack where fire is on the platform. So, I hold down and jump and no, you slide instead of dropping down like in almost every action platformer ever created up to and including Contra: Hard Corps where the idea of the invincible slide is taken from. Okay, I walk off the platform and use the grappling hook but I aim at an angle and it doesn't work and I die. Do it again thinking that I aimed at the wrong part of the thing to grapple to. Nope. Try something else thinking that I'm not supposed to do that, nope. Try again, this time I walk off the platform, I double jump towards the center and do the neutral grappling thing and then it works. There's just some bad conveyance as to where you're allowed to use the grappling hook and where you are not. Another reason why I give this an 8 is the difficulty. Normal difficulty is kind of insultingly easy and makes the game too short whereas Expert is (you guessed it) way too hard. On Expert you take more damage and there's no checkpoints so when you die once you restart the entire level all over again. I feel like a happy middle could have been achieved by offering checkpoints or a life system or something. That all said, I give it an 8 out of 10. It sucked refunding it but I got stuck at a loop that I already mentioned that didn't allow me to proceed further. Furthermore, as a huge fan of Shatterhand on the NES I would have LOVED to play the original 8 bit version of this that played more like Shatterhand. So I more than understand Kickstarter backers that feel ripped off that they didn't get a Shatterhand spiritual sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be entirely honest, I want to like this game, I do.The aesthetics are top notch; art's amazing, music is killer,  hell, the ideas put into it are all quite cool.Unfortunately the gameplay itself is complete and utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Stages and bosses want you to make split-second responses to attacks when your movement is manageable at best? Invuln frames on a slide that won't get you through most things unless timed exactly or near-exactly perfect, a double jump that's only just worth using, and a wire mechanic that will likely go in the wrong direction if you happen to be attacking at all when you use it since both it and your attacks follow input direction. This, coupled with very poor tells for attacks makes each boss fight feel more like a damage race then any real honest challenge.The game as a whole feels like it's trying a little too hard to hit that 'retro-classic' difficulty - and it nearly does, then veers right into the 'GOTCHA!' type difficulty where you feel more like you were cheated on an error than that you made any real mistakes.Absolutely not worth your money in any situation, barring maybe at a 90% discount to appreciate the artwork and music in motion.

_childDocuments_.review: Off the bat and right away, this game is SHORT. As of this review, my playtime is at 62 minutes, and I already beat the game (normal mode). That's not a flex either, this game is just way too short. Take away a few minutes for the few bathroom breaks I had in between, and the unskipable credit crawl, and I'd say this can definitely be beaten in under an hour. I died quite a bit also, so I would even dare to say that some of you gamepad masters out there might only get about 45 minutes out of this ride. This is the biggest negative I have about the game by the way, so if the length doesn't bother you for it's price, then go for it. There's a great deal of fun to be had here for as short as it is. It's packed with exaggerated amounts of enemies and explosions, and the bosses are all really awesome. Unfortunately though, the game itself lacks a meaningful amount of content and gameplay mechanics, leaving this feeling half baked.Taro (your character) has an electric whip and a zipline that he can easily attach to any wall within reasonable range. It's a great gameplay mechanic, and it was a very interesting to see how the devs incorporated the zipline into the some of the bossfights. Unfortunately, out of the 5 bosses here, a lot of them can be half beaten by tanking their damage while spamming the whip right in their faces. You can't get away with doing this for the entire fight on any of these bosses, but I found myself able to do it quite a bit, especially when the tide shifted in my favor. I would have liked to have seen a more pressure based approach to some of these bosses to discourage that kind of gameplay. Panzer Paladin, for example, breaks its boss fights into sections based on the bosses health. The boss will start behaving differently based on the amount of health that it has, and it leaves things unpredictable. In this game, however, once you have the boss on the ropes, you can confidently go right up and spam since the pattern never changes.The electric whip is a cool idea and a great concept for a hero in this kind of an action game. Unlike Contra, which this game seems to take a heavy inspiration from, Taro never picks up a gun. However, his whip does get a power up that allows him to fling electricity at enemies to catch them at a distance. This was a great way to keep the entire idea of playing as an unarmed man (well, unarmed as far as firearms go) intact, however, this is the only power up in the game. As cool as I just described it to be, it's actually pretty underwhelming after you realize that this is all that Taro gets. The only other thing in his arsenal of tricks is that he gets a short baseball slide, that if timed correctly, he can pass through enemy projectiles.The way this game plays is fantastic for what it is. It's just unfortunate that there isn't enough content to make this feel like a full experience. I'd say content wise, this game would need to be at least double of what it currently is to make it worth its asking price. What's on offer here inside of 5 stages is great, but unfortunately, there just isn't enough greatness here for me to recommend this to anyone. And don't get me wrong, I've played short games before and still recommended them. Summer of '58 was a game that I was able to beat in under 2 hours, and I would still recommend it. But the difference between this and a game like Summer of 58 is that Summer of 58 goes out of its way to leave an impression you. It had a story to it that sucks you into its atmosphere and provokes thought. For something so short to stay with someone even after the credits role makes it worth it. A game like Steel Assault, however, is basically just "check your brain at the door and kill some stuff". It's just the nature of the beast with these kinds of games, so the value falls on content and gameplay here. As cool as some of these stages and bosses are, none of them have enough to them to stick in your mind, so when you get to the end of this game, all you're really going to notice is.... "Man, this was short!" Followed by, "I WISH THERE WAS MORE!" You can think of it like going to a restaurant, and getting a tiny amount of food, but it tastes fantastic. It's going to leave you wanting more, and not in the good kind of way. That's basically this game.I'm going to refund this game just for now. I do want to own it in my library some day, but not at this price point. There just isn't enough on offer here. I know that some people are saying that the value will come from the extra modes, but I disagree. The main mode IS the game. Extra modes are just...extra. For instance, the arcade mode is just the main story again with a harder difficulty. At that point, you've seen it all already. If challenging yourself with extra modes is worth it to you, I'm not knocking anyone, but I don't feel like extra modes should make up for more than half of this games asking price, and honestly, that's how I would value this game. At half. It feels like half a game, and would be more appropriate at half the price, so when it hits a sale, I'll own this again, but for now, I can wait on it.P.S. If you think it's wrong to refund a game that you beat, you aren't considering your own money for value here. Simply reaching the end of something doesn't mean you got your moneys worth out of it, and it certainly doesn't warrant keeping something. The average length of a movie is about 1 hour and 45 minutes. If you went into a movie theater and watched something that only lasted 45-50 minutes, would you automatically consider that to be fair? Or would you have some things to consider at that point? Was that short ride packed with memorability for the price tag? Or did the curtain close just as the movie felt like it was hitting its stride? Getting to the end of something doesn't automatically make it worth your money, and it doesn't automatically warrant having to hold onto a purchase. If the value just isn't there, the length of the game is irrelevant.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen others lament how everything visually and aesthetically is spot on, yet the gameplay is far too unforgiving.  And I agree with them.  But the gameplay is far too unforgiving in a lot of sections, especially when it comes to covering the distance with your double-jump or hooking onto something just in the nick of time. The room for error when it comes to dodging projectiles is SO small too, even if you've died over and over and can (mostly) tell what's coming.  (Also one mini-boss lets you shoot a turret, but the fact that it gives you so little time to use it before you're hit by something makes it almost..deceptive?)  The pixel art and soundtrack are *astounding*!  BUT, I think the visual splendor also hurts clarity.  So much is going on at once, and it's hard to tell what your rope can and can't latch onto.  If they just balanced the art and the gameplay more equally, this could've been a hard but fun hit.  As it is now, it's a gorgeous but nigh-unfair romp.

_childDocuments_.review: It has problems to be sure, specifically at this price point. It lacks enough length to matter and relies on harder difficulties to pad out more time. _childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steal Assault is totally worth your time despite it's length, it is a well polished product. Reminds me of the Gameboy Advance in a good way, though it's very clear that it takes some inspiration from the SEGA Genesis and some more modern faux-retro titles.I beat the game on normal in about an hour.The hard difficulty took me about 4 hours to beat, but now I'm very good at the game and find it very fun to blast through.If you would like to watch gameplay, I have recorded a full playthrough here:This game is a fast paced action game reminiscent of Contra, Castlevania, Mega Man, and a boatload of Treasure games, especially Gunstar Heroes. You take your electric whip, whip enemies with it, and the enemies explode in some really nice looking pixel art. Get to the end of the stage and defeat a pretty crazy boss. Do this 6 times and you win the game. Also rock out to the soundtrack.You always feel in control, and the grappling hook mechanic gives you a lot of freedom in the air, once you get the hang of it. Protip: Don't hold "up" when you jump.The difficulty is also very reasonable on normal, the only times I died was when I misunderstood a exactly what I was supposed to do. So only a few times really. I would not call this game a frustrating experience.You can grapple onto almost any surface, and using your grapple gives you a bit of extra air time, which is more novel than you think.Despite the fact that this game starts with an extremely ugly bilinear filter, you can turn it off in the options. Other than that, the sprite work is amazing, detailed, and has quite a bit of animation. The final boss is a little choppy, but other than that, it's a treat for the eyes.You also have your scanline/CRT filters built into the game, but I don't typically touch those. I know the sharpened pixel look bothers a bunch of people with no taste, but the "raw" pixel look is very nice as it is. If I want to, I can (and do) play games on a CRT to get the CRT feel, and since this game is in 4:3, you should have no problems viewing it on a CRT if you have one. I think this game will look really nice on my CRT.Despite the pixel aesthetic and "retro 16bit" inspiration, the soundtrack would be at the level of CD quality audio. So like PS1+.Since there are few levels, there is only a few tracks, but all of the music is good.You can also choose an FM only version of the songs that are good in their own right, though I prefer the "CD" quality audio.There is no way around this. I beat the game on the normal difficulty in ~49 min. This is not a problem for me, and I tend to replay games once I get the hang of them to see how far I can push my skills. I don't know if I'm one of those people who "master" games, but a second playthrough at least on shorter titles usually makes me appreciate it more once I know what I'm doing. However, if you are one of those strange people that only play a game once, and only because they are new, then you will feel disappointed due to the game's length. That's more of a you problem than a knock against the games quality.I do understand that for ~$15 you have your choice of games that are many times longer and just as enjoyable, and I think it is reasonable to consider the length of this game.I think the best way to put it is, if you are looking for this kind of game, and what you saw in the trailer looks good, you should purchase this game.I do not regret my purchase, and would easily recommend this to anyone looking for that Treasure/Contra vibe. Now if they would only put Mischief Makers on steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.It has an interesting use of the grappling hook. Fast, fun, and beautiful. Execution is very tight. You don't have much margin for error and timings are very strict. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to the Sega Genesis and SNES era with plenty of references to some games from those consoles. _childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation is top notch, but the rest of it is not. It's got great music and a good look, but games need more than that.It's extremely short. I beat it on normal mode in 60 minutes. I got stuck in 2 places due to their bad design. The abysmal level 2 and the final boss. I really wanted to like this game and I was excited for it. When I finally got to play it, I discovered it was very shallow and disappointingly short with problems in it's mechanics.I deeply love old Castlevania, Megaman, Contra and similar games and I'm quite good at them. The opening video is kick-ass. The aesthetics are great with sweet unique music per stage and art that just feels right (except when Taro's face is inconsistently drawn). It's mostly similar to Ninja Gaiden and Contra but not as precise as those games generally are. When you have a game this short, your gameplay needs to be razor tight and this wasn't.The game is shallow in many ways. The gameplay is too simple to be very engaging. You jump, attack, slide(dodge), and use ziplines. Keeping with the Contra and Ninja Gaiden similarities, it's better for you to go fast and skip most things that aren't directly in your way. This helps avoid infinitely respawning enemies and prevent others from getting into position where they would be annoying. There is no exploration to speak of. It's almost a game on rails. You can take your time, but it will probably be worse for yourself and there aren't even little secrets for a powerup or something. Powerups are laid in front of you and you honestly have to avoid them intentionally to not get them. There's a "story" but there really shouldn't be in a game like this. An opening and ending video like Hard Corps Uprising is all you need. This game has two side-kick characters who only say a few lines here (no voice acting) and there if you even notice. Sometimes they even talk to you when you're in battle so obviously you won't be paying attention to them at all. They are really pointless; both in what they say and how/when they say it. While the environments can look nice and there was an effort to create a sense of world-building, it's sometimes nonsense. I think it's supposed to be a kind of post-apocalypse. One level features a derelict city overgrown with plants. But it also has working TVs, lights, and capitalistic advertisements. So which is it? An old abandoned derelict city or a technologically alive modern dystopian nightmare?This game's gimmick is a zipline that you hardly use outside of roughly one attack per main boss and maybe one elevator section in a level or two. And you can't even use it for a direction that would help you the most (down-right, despite the tutorial saying you can use it for 8 directions). The game says there are subweapons but there is only one, electric (which simply extends your whips range via three projecticles). It's a good one to be sure, but there are problems. The others are health and a two-hit shield. They are also in pre-placed areas so you won't encounter them randomly or via enemy drops. And shield and electric overwrite each other, so you can't even get both at once if you're good enough to keep one. And there are hardly any little detours so there is no exploration to find them either. And there is no health item past level 3. On normal mode, this doesn't matter as checkpoints are decent enough. But on hard and arcade where the intent is to beat it in one life, that's when it becomes awful. The punch-to-regain energy is pointless because there is only one "subweapon" to recharge. It appears about once a level. That subweapon basically just extends your whip. But that means the mechanic and the only powerup it serves to help are in conflict with each other. If you use all your energy, even if you regain it through this mechanic, doesn't matter, the powerup is gone. You also lose it on death, so you're out of luck by the next checkpoint. So the only powerup in the game never lasts long unless you go out of your way to conserve it which generally isn't a good or feasible idea.The gameplay is not great. It's simultaneously too easy and also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at too many parts. It's too simple and almost never requires you to improve. It's shallow, it's inconsistent, and also bounces radically between unfairly hard and sleep-inducingly easy. I've had too many dropped inputs on a brand new controller, and invincibility frames after taking damage aren't consistent either so you can get unfairly double-dipped. The hitboxes are also not consistent. Too often things that hit, shouldn't; things that shouldn't, do. The whip itself is a mess to look at. The sprite is not defined enough and even has weird triangles at the end of it. This is your only attack, there should be no confusion with it and it should be awesome every time. Sometimes the bad hitboxes are in your favor (not fun) and sometimes they aren't (super not fun). Same with contact damage. Sometimes I overlap with an exploding enemy or phase through bullets for no reason and nothing hits me, other times I'm obviously not touching anything and I get hit and wonder why.The dodge-slide is a few frames too short from being useful. For example the final boss has a flamethrower attack that can hit you even though you slide through it. It's the only way to dodge it and yet it's inconsistent. Come on now.Again, if your game is this short, the physical gameplay has to be consistently good.Some bosses die before you can even see what they can do like the miniboss robot-mastodon with a chainsaw-nose.The faster you play, the easier it is. You can kill some minibosses before they even turn around. You can defeat main bosses before they even get off three or more attacks. You can do this even on accident. But if you don't know how, or naturally play slower, it becomes unfair without trial and error. Bosses are pattern based but also not challenging enough to let you see what they can do, so you feel shortchanged. And if you do let them do more attacks, it usually starts to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The mark of good level/boss design is near-death situations that demand "perfection" from the player, but perfection derived from practice, not memorization or exploiting. The key test for "real" or "fake" difficulty is: could a person theoretically make it through a stage on their first try assuming their reaction time and skill is good enough. That's not this game. It's entirely trial and error for the rare parts where it's actually hard. Most of the time, enemies are mainly placed where you'd naturally jump and whip or something similar. Some enemies are already shooting before you see them on screen so you'll end up jumping directly into their attacks. Also everything does two damage so it's pointless to have all the extra pips on your life bar when every attack does the same anyway. Might as well have half the pips and everything do one damage. It's the same either way. It's an unnecessary illusion.I feel no desire to 1cc this because of those factors unlike Hard Corps Uprising which was much harder.It also wouldn't have been hard to include a boss rush mode or level select. To play arcade mode without mastering boss patterns is a death sentence of frustration and not worth it on top of all the inconsistency in gameplay. Arcade mode is even worse actually. Only some item boxes can actually change between shield and electric powerups. And pits are deaths instead of just damage, which kick you back to the start. Extra fun when an enemy shoots you from off screen while you jump to the only platform available which then knocks you into death. So yeah, very poorly designed.Level 2 is probably the worst stage I have ever played. All the worst attributes of the game come out. Random enemies that randomly explode, off screen shooting, all the above. Stupid power up placement (shield first and then health in the very first section WHERE YOU DON'T NEED THEM). Unbelievable.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I played this sooner! Because then I could have refunded it as it would have been in the 14 day grace period.First off, credit where credit is due: The graphics and music are very good! However, It may be very pretty, but it plays like ****, the mechanics are poorly thought out, or seem like there are mechanics missing: -you have 10 health but every single attack does at least 2 damage.-when you get close you do a short range melee attack that's worse than your normal attack - it restores subweapon energy but there's only one and it's a drop from chests so you'll almost never have a subweapon. -The dodge is bound to down+jump even though there are a ton of free buttons. _childDocuments_.review: Do you remember every c*ck sucking and bullsh*t stuff from old NES and SNES games. For example, knockback when you get hit, instakill death pits, enemies appearing out of nowhere and hitting you, 2 phase boss fight that doesn't refill your health bar and doesn't have a checkpoint between phases. Put all these ♥♥♥♥ into one game and you get Steel Assault. A game that only took the worst parts of the retro games and forget the fun and enjoyment. As soon as you start level 1, the game starts sending enemies from left and right. This is just first level, let me get used to controls. Nope, this game has no mercy, You have to master the controls and play without making a mistake from level 1. You don't time to make mistakes because if you do, you will die. Some of the bosses cover the floor with electric and flame and you have to fight them while on a zipline or wait for floor to return to normal. Another c*ck bending and unnecessary game mechanic. The game only has 5 levels. It is too short. You can literally finish it under 1 hour and refund it. I finished the game both on easy and normal mode in 2 hours. In order to compensate for the short length of the game, they made it criminally hard. Steel Assault is exactly that. Also this sh*t released in 2021 and it doesn't have widescreen, 2k or 4k support. It forces 4:3 ratio. Don't say it adds retro aesthetic, it's complete bullsh*t!

_childDocuments_.review: It's just too short to recommend. The game should have additional content, but instead feels rushed with the bare minimum seemingly to appease the kick-starters (I assume).However with that said, the game does have a high quality polish to it. _childDocuments_.review: this game is 15 bucks which is about 14 too many in quarters that I'd be willing to spend on it. very cheap kills and you die extremely fast. The presentation and music and design is topnotch but the actual moment to moment gameplay absolutely sucks ass and most deaths do not feel like it's your fault and instead feel like the game is kicking you while you're down. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, even though the sprites are on the small side. Sound and music is great. The game-play is unique with the grapple mechanic and is tight, even though some of the platforming can get quite frustrating. This game would have been a perfect fit on the SNES and Genesis back in the day. The only real knock I can give it is that it is short and can be beaten in under an hour on its easiest setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the Mega Man X series on the SNES and PS1 and Steel Assault brought back the nostalgia of the fast paced action of my youth.  In addition to the speedy combat, the style is fresh.  I don't consider this a Mega Man clone but there is certainly inspiration reflected in the design.Instead of a gun type weapon as the primary, this game utilizes a whip so you are fairly close during enemy engagements.  The encounters are more frantic during this style of close range combat and quick enemies.The game is short and the story and characters are lightly written in retro style.  Still if you enjoy fast platformers, I think you will have fun.  The soundtrack is also rockin' which was a great plus for me!*I did encounter one recurring bug and as far as I can tell it is rare among users.  I could almost never get the upper right zip line to deploy when using the keyboard.  I was able to beat the game even with the bug.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a fast paced 2D Action Platformer that will test your skills, the game has a unique mechanism which is called the wall hook, where you need to hook 2 walls or 2 platforms and hold on to the rope while platforming which makes it even more fun and interesting.The combat is fast paced you will need lots of dodging / sliding to overcome multiple sections and then faced a major boss at the end of each stage.The Boss fights designs were very nice and the music is really top notch, It took me back to those childhood days where I used to go to the arcade and insert the coins to play those games.Very recommended action platformer with an overall rating 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique gameplay with the zip n' whip mechanics, despite being short (It took me about 1 hour to beat), everything in it is very well polished. The artwork is great, the gameplay mechanics, enemies, bosses, it is all great. 100% worth to do the 1 live to beat mode since it is very short.Also, play with the CRT and Billinear filter on, the game looks amazing with them.I'm craving for a Steel Assault 2. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, the pixel art is immaculate, soundtrack is great and it has an interesting mechanic with the wires you can deploy and climb on. The main issue is that the game is extremely short, it doesn't feel like it has the time to properly flesh out its own mechanics or really push them so that the player has to get good with them and the developers could do more with it. Outside of the bosses and a few key sections during the levels it doesn't really get much use. I would have much preferred the game had a few more levels making use of the same settings/visual design across more levels, rather than having 2 or more different locations for every single level if it meant the game was longer.This is still a great game, but unless it looks like your dream game I'd say wishlist it and wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Very good gameFinishing the game on arcade mode was pretty funCool OST👌Only problem i had with the game was some bugs, like when switching scenarios, if you go outside the screen the game just freezes. _childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. Like others have said, it's a short game but I thought it was worth picking up. The description of the game says that this is a 16-bit retro style action game but truth be told this reminds me so much of the Gameboy Advance, which is technically 32-bit. But you would never get sound out of the GBA like this game. I really dig the soundtrack. And props to the devs for giving the option for a nice CRT filter. Not everybody likes them but I enjoy them when done right, and this game does it correctly.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a short and sweet platformer with honestly some of the best sprite work and music I've experience in an indie title.Instead of a sword or a gun Taro wields a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ electric whip and its just the one button and that's it.Really had me feeling like the games i grew up with, super simple but extremely hard to master.You can't really hold right and attack and run you gotta learn enemy patterns and spawns tons of trial and error ESPECIALLY the bosses. Other than tight controls and a double jump what sets this apart is the inclusion of a zip line you can deploy whenever you want in any direction as long as the two ends latch on to a surface. Felt like Bionic Commando + Contra in all the good ways possible. Lots of death pits and stage hazards that force you to start thinking how to approach situations while using the zip line, its a ton of fun really makes the platforming challenging.If there's any issues i have with it, other than feeling a little -too- short, the second level is a painful difficulty spike. Feels like something that should have been saved for stage 4 or 5.What makes it all the more painful is the two hardest achievements involve beating each stage with no checkpoints - and the whole game on a single life. If the second stage wasn't such a massive pain in the ass id try for these more but the memorization on the little enemies on this stage really don't compare to anything else. Maybe if i feel like hurting ill try them some more but for now ill be happy with having everything but those lmao.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing!Pure arcade goodness! Nonstop action, with very precise controls and tight gameplay backed by a frantic soundtrack!The graphics are gorgeous pixelated.The game consists of 5 stages with very platforming/action sections and various bosses. Each boss plays completely different from the previous ones.The last stage is a banger all around.Great game! Hghly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Only 2 hours in and ive had so many "WOW" moments. this game feels like the final boss of side scrollers. Everything i've learned from metroidvanias and side scrollers like megaman zero used flawlessly. Crazy enough while this game feels like home it adds a new grapple mechanic that makes movement feel amazing. The graphics are jaw dropping. Reminding me of some older ds games but modernized. I always loved that aesthetic. Only draw back could be the controls could take some people awhile to understand. Its a shame this game is not talked about. Must buy 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, short arcade-style game. Feels mostly like a mix of Castlevania and a side-scrolling shmup. Kinda like if a shmup was designed with mid-ranged combat in mind instead of their usual long-ranged player projectile fire.The music goes crazy, and the visuals are really nice, impressive bits of polish and personality were all over the presentation. There were some things I'd have designed differently maybe, but ultimately they didn't hurt the game that much for me. Things like the slide maneuver used for i-frames being really short, I feel like that could've been longer. Or the kinda awkward system of using melees to keep your whip powerup for longer, otherwise it just gets spent up and goes away.Regardless of some minor gripes, Steel Assault was a pretty enjoyable game and worth beating at least once. Lots of care clearly went into this and it shows!Oh and a tip: definitely recommend rebinding the grapple move to R1 or something besides circle/right face button. Makes it a lot easier to use at a moment's notice, and the game frequently asks you to platform off (i.e. jump) or attack while on your grapple rope. The R1 mapping makes it a lot easier to deal with those scenarios imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Over all I liked this game. If I had any real complaints, it's that it's sometimes a bit hard to see some bullets, and the default controls are kinda clunky. I rebound the grapple hook to R, jump to A, and attack to X. As well as, in Steam Controller options, bound Down+Jump to the L button. Because I am so annoyed by games not just giving slide its own button.It's much easier to get used to the grapple hook when you don't have to take your thumb off the very critical jump button do use it.As for the rest of the game, the level design is solid, the visuals are drop dead gorgeous, and both versions of the soundtrack are killer. I especially loved the FM versions.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic fast paced action platformer with a banger soundtrack! I first watched General Andrews run this game on stream and was a lucky recipient of a free copy from that stream. I absolutely fell in love with the action and music, and this is one of the very few games that I wanted to speedrun just from watching it with no prep work. There's some unexplained tech - Punch attacks don't use your energy bar if you have the electric power-up and on a successful punch kill, you'll get an orb to recharge 2 of the electric energy bar. The only major downside for the game isn't one that most people will be concerned with, or know about. It has to do with the difficulty levels. From somewhere between now and launch, there was a change in the amount of damage taken during normal mode, so now 5 hits, restart the screen. This is not really a big issue aside from 4 screens, primarily the waterjet section in stage 2.  Once you get into Expert difficulty, take that same 5 hits, and now it's through the whole level, making the heart pickups actually valid, but if you die, back to the beginning of the level you go. Arcade... same scenario without the pickups. Extremely unforgiving, and practically impossible to speedrun in a <20 minute run.On the flipside, Very Easy is literally that, very easy and if you die, you fell off the screen most likely. Easy is almost of the same caliber, but you might die if you don't dodge some of the attacks.Outside of the lackluster difficulty approach, the game feels and plays crazy well and I'll still be playing this gem for quite some time in the future.And for those who are curious, I did hold the VE and E speedrun records at the time of this comment (15:12 and 15:10 respectively) and a Normal mode run (17:49) on
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Although it is only 5 stages long, the game is amazing. Beautiful, tight controls and challenging AF! Playing on Normal was hard enough, final boss was great. My only complaint is the lack of a dedicated button for the "dash/slide" command, would make so much sense to me.I know the game is already cheap, but you can find it 50% off in any sale, so heads up.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on Normal difficulty (warning: it is tough.)This is a good game after you get used to honing in your twitch reflexes (you will need it to make any progress in the game). My main complaint against this game is that the screen just gets too busy to know what is coming at you and what to avoid (and where to shoot your grappling hook). Progress is made through dying a lot in tough spots (and often without sufficient warning for you to react in time on first encounters). The unlimited continues help as well as the checkpoints. I also found the later level bosses a lot easier than the first 2 level bosses. I remember I stopped playing not knowing what to do with the first boss. I came back to the game many months later to take another crack at it before I started making good progress.If you are looking for a challenge and enjoy gorgeous retro style pixel art then definitely play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault's heart is in the right place but there's just too many flaws for me to recommend buying it. Enemies frequently spawn on top of you, enemies have confusing hitboxes such as a giant chainsaw on a charging enemy not being able to hit you but the very edge of their buttcheek can, bullets are hard to see with incredibly busy environments which is made worse by the game defaulting to an optional blur filter turned on in video settings, the grappling mechanic is awkward and a bit of a throwaway, and boss health bars legitimately block your view of the playable area in 2 of the 5 boss fights in this game with the last boss fight blocking your view of the one safe place to stand in the very last phase. I was in such disbelief of the last boss health bar issue that I went to youtube and found a clip of someone else standing there safely to make sure that wasn't a glitch. _childDocuments_.review: I have a few negative things to say, but ultimately I do recommend this game if you like demanding run-and-gun type games.  The art is great and the controls are tight, and each level and boss feels unique.  The controller support was great for this game (Switch, PS4, XBOX prompts).Touching on the theme this is like Contra, Metal Slug, and Castlevania adopted a baby, and is well executed for the most part.  It's linear level progression interspersed with boss battles at a very demanding pace.On the note of pacing, on Normal difficulty I find it almost too hard.  I would put Normal at arcade quarter-crunching Metal Slug levels of difficulty, in that you will find yourself dying a lot to barrages of unpredictable enemies.  I felt demanded to execute mechanics in a timing-perfect manor before I was able to even learn how to use those mechanics.  I found myself dying a lot while trying to even figure out how I was supposed to beat a challenge in front of me, which I found frustrating, and I'm not stranger to these types of games.Luckily, the game never sets you that far back from where you died, so I rarely felt like like I was loosing too much progress.  Despite my frustrations, I found myself progressing through the game, which all said and done is relatively short (less than 2 hours for my Normal play-through).And while there are so many intentional designs decisions for this game (like CRT modes, low-resolution settings, intentionally hard gameplay), one thing that really bugged me (probably because I spent the longest on this section), was why you would leave the boss health meter for the last boss cover up part of the area you are fighting him in.  With so much attention to detail paid, that seems like an odd thing to overlook, especially when there is so much empty real estate at the top of the screen.Despite all that, I still enjoyed the game.  It's not one I would want to come back to unfortunately because of how frustrated I got, but for the very hardcore of this genre I think you'll have a good time.

The zipline is a fun mechanic to play with. Being forced to watch intros every time you respawn gets annoying quickly, especially if you suck at this game. Attempting to jump over certain enemies without making contact and receiving damage is more difficult than it should be.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a brutal and beautiful game.  I highly recommend it for those who like games like old-school Ninja Gaiden, Bionic Commando, Contra and Metal Slug.For a little background, my first console was an Atari 2600, but my first true love was the NES.  I was drawn to the more difficult games like Ninja Gaiden, Castlevania, Contra and Street Fighter 2010 and Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link.This game is a little misunderstood, because it's the opposite of what many games are today.  Instead of holding your hand, it has a brief, optional tutorial mode.  It's not just "sort of" old-school hard.  It's old-school hard on steroids.  Steel Assault throws you right into the fire, and pummels you over the head the whole way through.  There are two types of players at this point - Those who say "forget this" and play something else, and those who also get their butts kicked but say "give me more, we'll see who wins".It's not for everyone.  In fact, I found my whole play-through on normal difficulty to be incredibly difficult.  I have seen some of the superhuman speed-runs on youtube, and I'm not one of those people.  I still like my games tough, and to be honest, this game is tough - but it's also fair the whole way through.  If I die, it's my fault.  If I fail to memorize an enemy pattern, or take advantage of an opening, it's still my fault - especially on the second or third try.Every little nook and cranny, every enemy and ability at your disposal is perfectly posed where there is a way to victory.  It's up to you to figure it out - whether to play offense, or defense, or find a new strategy altogether.  Upon my first try at the game, I felt winded by the time I made it to the second stage.After a few hours, I was speed-running my way to the final boss, and still finding new and more efficient ways to dispose of enemies who I never thought I could take out in the first place (sometimes just avoiding them will work).With all that said, there are four difficulty modes, including easy, and very easy, which are better-geared for gamers who just want to have a good time without sweating bullets and clenching their teeth.As far as the graphics and music, this game slams.  The music is some kind of melodic techno-metal with an 80's montage feel. The graphics are like some GBA game on overdrive.  Thematically, the game is awesome.   Short, animated cut-scenes are really cool, and made me root for Taro, whom I think is one of the coolest-looking game protagonists I've seen in a long time.  I also really liked the enemy characters, and I wanted to know more about them, even though the game mentions very little in detail.The controls are also very tight.  That said, the zipline system takes a lot of getting used to.  My first playthrough was very awkward....but this is the type of game that will reward you as you spend more time with it.  In fact, using the zipline to traverse through corridors and tops of buildings is an absolute joy, and the platforming parts are usually my favorite.The whip is downright nasty and fun to use.  One you learn the boss patterns, it's a lot of fun to spam the attack button and take out that op boss way earlier than expected.So, most importantly, the game-play is great.  It is awkward at first, but so is riding a bike or playing guitar.  You have to have a little patience and be wiling to take criticism from the game and improve.I give this game a solid 9/10.  The only reason I don't give it a 10/10, is that like some have argued, it is a little too short.  Some extra challenge stages, or maybe some later dlc, could fix that shortcoming.  Other than that, this game is perfect for what it is.  It has razor-sharp game-play that rewards commitment, and is overflowing with style and inspiration that I find lacking in many of the old-school throwback games out there today.Highly recommended to anyone who likes a little pain in their game, and want to feel a true sense of victory upon completion.

_childDocuments_.review: An gorgeous game with a rockin soundtrack, fully created with love of the unforgiving S/NES era. _childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool albeit short retro action-platformer (emphasis on short) with visuals straight out of a GBA and a banger soundtrack, which blends gameplay elements from classics like Castlevania, Bionic commando and even a touch of Contra.One remark though: difficulty settings are all over the place. You can go from a cakewalk on Normal, with health refills at the end of each screen and very generous checkpoints, to a true hard-as-nails retro arcade experience on Expert, with all the aforementionned advantages being-stripped out and ennemies hitting twice as hard. Something in between would probably have been much better for the overall longevity of the game.Fun game all things considered, I'd just wish it would go for a little longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Steel Assault is a tad short, but it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool.The framerate runs at 60, but the doesn't have widescreen. It's a stylistic choice to emulate arcade cabinets. What is nice, though, is that the game supports all controllers, with button prompts for Dualshock, Nintendo, and Xbox controllers. You can jump, attack in any direction, use a pulley to attach to fill gaps in any direction, and slide with i frames. But the environment around those mechanics make full use of them. The art style is top tier, and the pixel art is SNK/Darkstalkers level. I literally utter "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" and "woah" at certain points just from the pixel fidelity.I guess I wish the characters would get more backstory/interactions, as well as a longer campaign. But that's how good it is. I wanted more. I wanted to hang out more in this game. And you will spend a lot of time, since on normal, this is hard. But you have endless continues, and four difficulties means four ways to play.Steel Assault is a steal (HEHE). Please consider buying it.

So thanks to him I got the chance to know and give it a try. :DIt feels like an original Mega Drive. The pixel art and cutscenes are stunning. It's special. Good level design and challending. Well balanced as well. Something that I miss really much in modern games from big companies. But I think just the indie developers like you guys can bring it to us. Pity the game is short. _childDocuments_.review: well... this is more of "i'd recommend, but..." steel assault has amazing pixel art, good music, proper old-school arcade gameplay... but it is incredibly short. it is so short that even the sentence you've just read is longer than the game. granted, there's some replay value, but i really hope there will be some dlc's later on. for now i wouldn't really recommend it for the full price. it is a beautiful and fun game, but it lacks content.
_childDocuments_.name: Steel Assault

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that the developers listened so much to our feedback from the demo already deserves praise. I'm not going to go into details, but basically, they improved on basically every aspect of the game by a lot and made the more frustrating parts less frustrating, or non-existent.While it's a joy to see all the differences and improvements in the game compared to the demo, the game itself is fantastic. It's a high adrenaline action platformer, where split second decisions will always demand your focus pretty much all the time. It really wears down your fingers, but this is exactly what we came for. Don't get me wrong, this isn't just for oldschool platformer veterans, since now they added difficulty levels which is a welcome addition. Don't EVER feel bad for playing it on Easy or Very Easy. Get familiar with the feel of the game, the different type of enemies, stages, etc. Then if you feel like you've mastered that difficulty level, you can always challenge yourself by playing it one difficulty level above. But it also pleases the more hardcore crowd. The Normal difficulty I feel like is just right, it offers a good challenge.The music and visuals are both great, I don't have any issues whatsoever.The only real con to this game is how short it is. You're going to die a lot, but even then, it's really really short, even shorter than some oldschool NES/SNES/Genesis action platformers. Even so, I do recommend this game due to its high replay value and how generally fun it is.

name: Astral Ascent
detailed_description: Updates Roadmap Join our community (link in the right column) About the Game Astral Ascent is a 2D platformer roguelite game set in a modern fantasy world. As one of 4 Heroes with very different personalities, you must escape from The Garden , an astral prison guarded by 12 powerful and vicious bosses, the Zodiacs. CREATE YOUR OWN PLAYSTYLE Unlock dozens of unique spells for each or your characters. Optimize your own build or try out new ones to face all the challenges you'll find on your journey for freedom. Get progressively stronger with time to match up with your foes. Each run will test your skills and your reactivity. TWELVE ALMIGHTY BOSSES TO FACE The Zodiacs are 12 experienced guardians dispatched over 4 gorgeous worlds. Each with their own unique attacks and combat styles, backstories to uncover and reasons to be fighting you, they'll pose as a big threat to anyone seeking a way out of the Garden . Get yourself warned! 4 PLAYABLE CHARACTERS Unique characters. Unique weapons. Unique ways to play. Ayla: A skilled assassin sent on a mission by her guild to prove her worth, she uses her sharp blades to eliminate targets before they can react. Her speed and proficiency are unmatched. Kiran: An orphan that has learned life the hard way. He uses his raw strength to deliver attacks powerful enough to create shockwaves. Brutal. Calie: This talented sculptor became a warrior to recover the freedom her people have lost. She will use her magical gemstones to pierce enemy defenses and shred them to bits. She is unforgiving. Octave: Trained by a powerful witch, this young fighter summons ethereal weapons to attack his foes. Big or small, short or long range, he has the right one for every occasion. Lethal in all cases. A STORY THAT OPENS UP, ONE PIECE AT A TIME Astral Ascent is a roguelite infused with narration. Replayability is part of a story that will be unraveled piece by piece. As you get stronger, you will discover more about the characters, their motivations and the secrets of the world they’re trapped in. LOCAL CO-OP The weight of destiny is too heavy to carry by yourself? Don’t worry and bring a friend to play with the two-player co-op mode. Fight and crush your enemies together in local co-op or online using the Steam's Remote Play Together feature. A VAST, COLORFUL FANTASY WORLD WAITING TO BE EXPLORED Dash across gigantic landscapes. Explore original and hand-crafted areas. Discover a fantastic universe loaded with gorgeous art and fluid frame-by-frame animation.

CREATE YOUR OWN PLAYSTYLE Unlock dozens of unique spells for each or your characters. Optimize your own build or try out new ones to face all the challenges you'll find on your journey for freedom. Get progressively stronger with time to match up with your foes. Each run will test your skills and your reactivity. TWELVE ALMIGHTY BOSSES TO FACE The Zodiacs are 12 experienced guardians dispatched over 4 gorgeous worlds. Each with their own unique attacks and combat styles, backstories to uncover and reasons to be fighting you, they'll pose as a big threat to anyone seeking a way out of the Garden . Get yourself warned! 4 PLAYABLE CHARACTERS Unique characters. Unique weapons. Unique ways to play. Ayla: A skilled assassin sent on a mission by her guild to prove her worth, she uses her sharp blades to eliminate targets before they can react. Her speed and proficiency are unmatched. Kiran: An orphan that has learned life the hard way. He uses his raw strength to deliver attacks powerful enough to create shockwaves. Brutal. Calie: This talented sculptor became a warrior to recover the freedom her people have lost. She will use her magical gemstones to pierce enemy defenses and shred them to bits. She is unforgiving. Octave: Trained by a powerful witch, this young fighter summons ethereal weapons to attack his foes. Big or small, short or long range, he has the right one for every occasion. Lethal in all cases. A STORY THAT OPENS UP, ONE PIECE AT A TIME Astral Ascent is a roguelite infused with narration. Replayability is part of a story that will be unraveled piece by piece. As you get stronger, you will discover more about the characters, their motivations and the secrets of the world they’re trapped in. LOCAL CO-OP The weight of destiny is too heavy to carry by yourself? Don’t worry and bring a friend to play with the two-player co-op mode. Fight and crush your enemies together in local co-op or online using the Steam's Remote Play Together feature. A VAST, COLORFUL FANTASY WORLD WAITING TO BE EXPLORED Dash across gigantic landscapes. Explore original and hand-crafted areas. Discover a fantastic universe loaded with gorgeous art and fluid frame-by-frame animation.
short_description: Choose one of four heroes and explore the Garden, an astral prison guarded by 12 powerful mystical bosses: the Zodiacs. Challenge them with dozens of unique spells and faithful friends by your side to unfold the story of this platform roguelite with lightning fast combat.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute visual spectacle and incredibly robust rogue-like. Great to play in both single-player and coop. Regular updates are keeping things fresh even in EA. I can't wait to see how this game progresses in the future. One thing I will mention is that the spell/ skill system has taken a while to get used to. Either having to remember what order your skills are, or glancing in the bottom left corner to see what's next can lead to taking unnecessary damage because you're not focused on dodging. Likewise, the default PC keybinds overlap equipping spells/skills and using the healing feature, which has lead to me using my fully charged healing (one use) ability while attempting to browse the shop directly before a boss fight, often prematurely ending my run because I am entering the boss fight with half the effective HP pool. Other than these small gripes, I 100% recommend the game to anyone who has played and enjoyed games such as Wizard of Legend, Dead Cells, Rogue Legacy, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: While I didn't receive this game for free, I did get it at a discount through a Humble Choice monthly bundle. Overall, I enjoy this game. The fast-paced combat becomes easy to flow in once you understand how attacks, spells, and signature skills work together, figure out enemies, and learn to weigh the types of boons you go for in each room. The dialogue helps flesh out the setting, and is a treat because all dialogue is voiced. It's there for players who want to explore lore more, but not too in the way for players looking for the action. And when you can get the right auras to synergize, it's very satisfying.I will vent some nitpicks, however. For context, I have beaten the game a few times, gotten to level 7, and have begun to tinker with other characters past Ayla. Some of the controls/movement and hitboxes can feel off. I've had problems with hitboxes once or twice that reach further than they appear, and the invulnerability on dashing has felt off at times (has lasted extra long when I didn't act afterward, or getting hit when dashing through a laser). Pertaining to the bosses, while it's part of the challenge to "get good", I wish there was a means to practice against individual bosses. When you unlock harder levels and the bosses have bigger movesets, it can be frustrating to get 30 min into a run only to lose your step when you need to figure out the new attacks from one of the three later bosses. When the screen flashes red with the incoming hitbox, it can be hard to tell when to use your movement to avoid.Getting to the end of the story is a decent, enjoyable challenge, with multitudes of harder difficulties for those who want more. You get to better your skills how you wish and choose your path to get stronger for the bosses. At a discount, I can comfortably recommend this title.

_childDocuments_.review: So that you don't have to read the rest, the conclusion is that buying it is definitely a good game.Now, the game is curious to say the least, especially because unlike other games of its genre, which work in a way of scaling is quite simple, I have a skill and I improve it in two ways, passively related to that skill or improve the skill itself. This game works the same way, it has not invented the wheel, it has curious elements, first of all the difference of the characters. In the game we are presented with 4 characters with their own skills, and the game does in a very subtle way by touching 4 parameters that the gampley and the feeling of playing is totally different between them, and even the stats that you raise in the character are different and you prioritize one or another before the regular ones.Having said that about the characters, the game is "confusing" and ironically I would say that the game teaches you but the truth is that it is not the game that teaches you. Each character has 4 skills associated with a mana cost, each skill can be exchanged for others that you get in your run, but the funny thing about this is that the important thing is the passives that you equip and if they relate to your gameplay. It is complicated because the game does not make you a tutorial explaining it, but you as a player you are overwhelmed in some ways and you need to know what each thing does out of curiosity, but if you are one of those players who like to rush and run forward without looking back, this will happen to you.Now talking about the gameplay, it is certainly easy, the moment you understand how the passives go the game becomes easy and even if every time you pass the game it adds one more difficulty, it is true that as it is now at the level of balanca, if you read a little the passives and have a half decent combo you pass it pretty easy and from there it becomes boring "in my opinion".

_childDocuments_.review: Even at it's current state and with what little it has in it's early access content, this game is a blast to play, and I had no hesitation in playing it past the 2 hour refund mark. The pixel art graphics, which is what brought me to this game in the first place, looks very nice and I enjoy it a lot (especially the boss intro cutscenes. I never get tired of those). This game has a unique kind of style in it's presentation that I rarely see in other games. It being early access, there are still a few rough edges. The game could use some optimizations to let it frame lag less, as I've had to set my graphics to very low to make it run smoothly, which is strange considering that this is a 2D game and I've had less stylized 3D games run smoother with higher settings.  and also I've had some issues with crashing (which seem to only happen in windowed mode). 10/10 would recommend. _childDocuments_.review: TL; DR: It's an extremely beautiful, fluid, original and beautiful rogue like game.You are also invited to my steam installer page95/100ENGThe game is really well designed. We play with a main character named Ayla and our overall goal in the game is to defeat the zodiac signs and reach the last boss named Master. To do this, we go through the worlds of earth, fire, water and air to reach the final boss. I played and finished the game with Ayla until I unlocked Octave and with Octave after I unlocked Octave. First of all, the game is very fast. Generally, wall climbing and double jumping are not given at the beginning of the game, but these features really brought speed and mobility to the game. There are many events in the game. As we go from one room to another in the worlds, we enter another room by seeing a few things. First of all, there are two rooms, the exploration room and the battle room, and these rooms provide access to boxes that can be opened for 3 or 5 keys, give us new abilities, give us Aura, which is a passive ability, or provide power-ups called Gambits to improve these abilities, give Quartz -the main substance used in the dungeon- and also provide stars according to their difficulty. The game is really incredibly detailed about this. Both abilities, Gambits, and Auras have their own rarity, and abilities also have elements, and as long as a Gambit is given according to these elements, the elemental damage increases in addition to its own damage. Apart from that, abilities also have their own levels and we have the chance to upgrade these levels as we progress through the rooms. We have four abilities in the game and while these abilities are the abilities of the character we choose at first, we can improve these abilities and add Gambits as we progress. Apart from these rooms, there are also special rooms. In these rooms, we can rest, gain Aura, choose Gambits or elemental Gambits, take on challenges given to us by the Zodiac Signs and gain their powers. The dialogs and monologues in the game are extremely beautiful. Each character's short dialogues with the characters in the garden, learning a little bit about their past, their goals, their little laments when they sit in the rest rooms, their dialogues with the zodiac signs are extremely well done. Every word is voiced and very well done. There are four things I don't like about the game. The first one is that the game gets incredibly slow when fighting the final boss, the second one is the lack of improvements in the garden, and the third one is that we have to finish the game too many times to reach the real end. You have to replay each main character and each sign of the zodiac to see the true ending. The last one is that the bosses are randomized when you finish each world. Unfortunately, I finished the game without ever meeting Pisces in the water group. It was either Scorpio or Cancer.TROyun gerçekten çok iyi tasarlanmış. Ayla adlı bir ana karakter ile oynuyoruz ve oyundaki genel amacımız burçları yenip Master adlı son bossa ulaşabilmek. Bunun için de sırasıyla toprak, ateş, su ve hava dünyalarından geçerek son bossa ulaşıyoruz. Oyunu Octave’ı açana kadar Ayla ile, Octave’ı açtıktan sonra da Octave ile oynayıp bitirdim. Öncelikle oyun çok hızlı. Genel olarak duvara tırmanma ve çift zıplama oyunun en başında verilmez ama bu özellikler oyuna gerçekten hız ve hareketlilik getirmiş. Oyunun içerisinde birçok olay var. Dünyalar içerisinde bir odadan diğer odaya giderken birkaç şeyi görerek başka bir odaya giriyoruz. Öncelikle keşif odası ve savaş odası olarak iki oda var ve bu odalar 3 veya 5 anahtar karşılığında açılabilen kutulara erişim sağlıyor, bize yeni yetenekler veriyor, pasif yetenek olarak geçen Aura veriyor veya bu yetenekleri geliştirmek için Gambit adı verilen güçlendirmeler sağlıyor, zindan içi kullanılan asıl madde olan Quartz verip ayrıca zorluklarına göre yıldız sağlıyor. Oyun gerçekten bu konu hakkında inanılmaz derecede ayrıntılı hazırlanmış. Hem yeteneklerin hem Gambitlerin hem de Auraların kendi arasında da bir nadirlik derecesi var. bunun dışında ayrıca yeteneklerin de elementleri var ve bu elementlere göre Gambit verildiği sürece kendi hasarı dışında element hasarı da yükseliyor. Bunun dışında yeteneklerin de kendi seviyeleri var ve bu seviyeleri de odalardan ilerledikçe yükseltme şansımız var. Oyunda dört tane yeteneğimiz var ve bu yetenekler ilk başta kendi seçtiğimiz karakterin yetenekleri iken ilerledikçe bu yetenekleri de geliştirebiliyor ve Gambitler ekleyebiliyoruz. Bu odalar dışında bir de özel odalar var. Bu odalarda dinlenebiliyor, Aura kazanabiliyor, Gambit veya elemental Gambit seçebiliyor, Burçların bize vereceği meydan okumaları yapıp onların güçlerini edinebiliyoruz. Oyundaki diyaloglar ve monologlar aşırı güzel. Her bir karakterin bahçedeki karakterler olan kısa diyalogları, bu vesileyle biraz geçmişini öğrenmemiz, amaçları, dinlenme odalarında oturduklarında küçük küçük hayıflanmaları, burçlarla olan diyalogları aşırı güzel yapılmış. Her kelimede de seslendirme yapılmış ve çok güzel yapılmış. Oyunda sevmediğim dört şey var. Birincisi son boss ile savaşırken oyunun inanılmaz derecede kasması, ikincisi bahçedeki geliştirmelerin yetersizliği, üçüncüsü oyunda gerçek sona ulaşmak içi oyunu çok fazla sayıda bitirmemiz gerektiği. Her bir ana karakter ve her bir burcun gerçek sonunu görmek için tekrardan oynamak gerekiyor. Sonuncusu ise her bir dünyayı bitirdiğimizde gelen bossların rastgele olarak gelmesi. Su grubunda Pisces ile hiç karşılaşmadan oyunu bitirdim maalesef. Ya Scorpio ya da Cancer geldi.Bunlara rağmen muazzam bir iş çıkartılmış. Steam Dolara geçtiği için aşırı pahalı fakat ucuz bulunca bütçeniz yetiyorsa mutlaka alıp oynamanızı tavsiye ederim <3

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, got the true ending so I think a review is in order. The first thing to note is that this game is incredibly impressive from a development standpoint. There is a lot of passion and thought and skill put into it from such a small team, so I'll try to make my review at least a little effortful by rambling about whatever comes to mind.There is a huge focus on meta-progression and scaling difficulty. You have to choose your attacks, your spells for the attacks, your passive benefits, your stat boosts, your secondary passive benefits, and more as you flesh out your build for each run. You make choices about what kind of rooms to clear (with varying difficulties and varying resources) until you eventually reach a boss. You can buy permanent buffs between runs to make this process go by easier and faster over time. There are four characters to rotate freely between, but I only played the brawler because punching makes me feel good.The core progression for me was learning the game until I could beat it in my sleep, then making the game increasingly harder with debuffs until I was eligible for the true ending. I never looked anything up and discovered how to beat it consistently through trial and error and paying attention to all the little numbers and symbols on my screen. The very early game is quite scary if you do it like me, but having a little bit of diligence will go a long way and I think this is the most fun way to play the game.The difficulty was in this learning process rather than the actual fights themselves; once I knew the attack patterns of a boss I could pretty easily brute force through them. I played every fight by spamming my attack and spells as much as I could and occasionally dashing/countering/jumping when prompted to. The gameplay is very floaty, but I like air combos and jumping around so it was fine for me :)The mechanics of the game are very tightly designed. Advantage X might be good, but you could also sacrifice it for Resource Y, which could lead to you getting Advantage Z, and so on. This kind of system means that your micro-choices in each run add up and you have to always think about what is the best possible build out of the options offered to you. This and the floaty gameplay are what kept me invested the most.The story feels like I'm playing a video game adaptation of a series that would have been popular on Tumblr in the early 2010s. The game fully leans into this vibe, so I can't be a hater since it feels sincere the whole way through. I wasn't really playing for the story, but the execution of it was very clever. There are a ton of characters in this story, most of them being moody humans in flashy armour. Character introductions were done in flashy animated (skippable) scenes to draw the eye and the dialogue between characters is short and snappy. You are invited to think and care about these characters but your time is not wasted if you don't want to. The gameplay loop and mechanics are made to be a part of the story itself, which is always nice to see in games. Though I'm a bit sad that the true ending .TL;DR Game is good if you want a floaty Dead Cells where the combat is more forgiving but making the correct micro-choices in your runs requires more learning and adaptive thinking.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, but pretty easy for the most part.This game is fun, it's extremely polished and plays great.  The build variety is fantastic, the amount of spells that differentiate each character and play through is fantastic and the aura's make you feel so intelligent when you get a few that chain together.  Also the unique ideas for summons as well as how the spells can combine are amazing.  All that said this game is really easy.  It reminds me a lot of hades in difficulty.  like the first 4-8 hours will be a bit of a struggle and then everything after that you'll be more confused if your health ever gets low.  I'm currently at destiny 5 and I don't think I've lost a run since getting past destiny 1 around hour 5.  The only hold ups on progression are the destiny fragments which seem to be sort of time gated on runs as you can just go to destiny 6 and get the 4 from the lower level ones you killed before you'll just get 1 each time you fight that boss (odd decision which doesn't really respect your time).  That being said it does give you more time to work on builds, however, it makes the difficulty of a normal run even lower.  Again if you like Hades this is going to be your jam as it's around the same difficulty and will only get "hard" when you start to throw an absurd amount of additives that almost feel unfair like the 400% heat level modifiers.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelikes I've played. Normally, when I 100% a roguelike I drop it for another one, but I keep coming back to this one. The combat in Astral Ascent feels so snappy; you never feel the game screws you over with any of the mechanics, knowing you can always improve. The voice acting is incredible with 99% of characters fully voiced.The Story isn't very complex, but it is there, with mostly characters interacting with each other. There are also collectible stories you can pick up in a run. The spell/aura/weapon systems bring in a very welcome complexity, that gives you a diverse build every run. The only negative thing I can really say about this game is the length of runs. If you aren't a speedrunner, I've found the average time of a run is just under an hour, which also depends on which difficulty you're on. I'd like to end this review to just plead with whomever may be reading this: This game is worth every penny and is a complete steal with a sale. The devs are excellent and update the game to this day regularly. Do yourself a favor and grab a copy (and even play some couch co-op or remote play co-op with some friends)

_childDocuments_.review: Sorely missing a two-handed weapon warrior-type character. Not a big fan of cycling abilities. Not a big fan of such small upgrades in the potion. 5% dmg is boring. 2% crit is laughably bad and boring. Auto-attacking feels awful in this game. They feel like mild slaps, not punches. You never know when a mob is going to be stunned by your punches or not so you end up taking damage and it's EXTREMELY frustrating, and the sounds are really puny which just feels ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Trying to drop down a ledge also feels terrible. Sometimes one press of down is enough, sometimes you need three. I really don't understand itIt sucks that for every new room you go into you have to wait for the animation of the door to finish before you can interact with it. Can't re-bind interact so my dash is also on R1/RB and I keep dashing when I want to interact, and in the city I keep interacting when I don't want to interactIt's extremely hard sometimes to tell if the element of abilities match with the element of the rune you want to slot into it.Upgrading abilities with the flat 20% dmg thing is boring, you have so many other trash abilities you have to cycle through before you get to use the one you want or find interesting so it just feels sourMost of the upgrades you get after you beat a boss are boring or lameI just don't find the gameplay loop particularly satisfying. This game has huge potential, but I simply doubt that they will go the direction I want it to goI would refund if I didn't accidentally go over 2 hours playtimeI find the gameplay not very satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: I HIGHLY recommend for everyone who even remotely likes roguelikes to play it. The developers love the game and community, having listened constantly during early access and included community inspired changes each patch.Story is great as you piece things together, really fun in that aspect. Combat system is a 11/10 for me. The hundreds of spell modifying gambits, over 100 total spells and hundreds of build-defining auras intertwine with each other into a beautiful song of chaos and pure fun. Then there is Andromedas bar, the stone altars, spell level increases via pavo's feathers, the sun and moon, zodiac summons, echoes, eclipsed rooms, Andromedas challenges, fight room challenges, 4 unique areas each with three bosses before the event horizon, the element system with, of course, elemental and non-elemental status effects. The choice of one of 3 random daily buffs via the telluric telescope, near infinite replayability via the destiny level system and destiny fragments to buff yourself up as you keep exponentially increasing the games difficulty to get stronger yourself, if you so choose. Oh, did I mention the game has coop?! Granted it's either local or steam remote play together, but it's there!The roadmap for 2024 looks insane as well! We already have new spells and pvp in beta. There is another character named Yamat in the works. Currently there are 13 zodiacs and 4 characters (Ayla, Calie, Octave, Kiran), who each have an ending dedicated to them. The playable characters are going to get one or more other weapons to play with, which will of course change the playstyle and the ability system is going to get reworked as well! Last but not least, there is another world planned after which a new gamemode will follow.And there is a good chance there will be more to come after.Again, I urge you to play Astral Ascent! The game, developers, and especially you, deserve it!

_childDocuments_.review: A faster-paced dead cells with the story/plot/lore delivery being a Hades-lite. For the latter, part of the issue with trying to utilize the Hades style of story-telling is that the you need to use a pantheon of gods/characters that have personalities and backstories that the audience already has a notion of. That way you can allude and subvert what the audience expects the characters to do. Otherwise you need to take the time to build up and introduce the characters, which Astral Ascent does not do.Instead it forgoes much of the world-building at the beginning for putting you into the gameplay loop. There is a lot of variety in terms of spells and passives, but it does (somewhat) devolve into the mash buttons to fill the screen with flashy effects. The bosses do force you into a loop of dodging and openings, which is nice. There were few times where I was baffled by how I got hit/died, so the enemy's moves and hitboxes are well-done.Overall, pretty addicting. Would even buy outside of a sale.My main wish for a patch is being able to remove spells from the move pool. I have yet to see some of the cooler spells you get at the end of the game because the player is incentivized to choose spells with the matching element to the auras (passives) you choose. The room you get for changing the element of 1 spell shows up infrequently (which I understand is for balancing). I would hope they patch in a method to either purchase another gambit in that room or to remove spells from the pool (possibly via the endgame crescent-thingies).

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh and fun entry to the genre, Astral Ascent delivers on beautiful stylized visuals and fast free-flowing combat. The progression system is incredibly rewarding, and unlocking new spells gives a very enjoyable variety from run to run. The particles and enemy attacks/patterns are very polished and readable, as well as the intense boss fights that present themselves in visually flashy and viscerally satisfying ways. Movement in this game is an absolute treat and it feels amazing to hop from wall to wall in parkour segments and among enemies in combat scenarios. The cut scenes and soundtrack, not to undersell it, are fantastic. The themes for The Sun and The Moon inspire such a feeling of awe just to name an example. I have been keeping up with this game since the beginning of its early access run, and I believe here we have a truly fantastic game that is a hidden gem of its kind. Highly recommended, especially to play locally with a friend. My one and only gripe is the voice acting can be awkward, unfitting and limply delivered at times, but it is easily overlooked among all its other shining qualities.
