_childDocuments_.review: + different characters with unique skills and play styles - it is quite fun and provides a lot of diversity. i've found two playable characters so far in my early access run, but the developers addressed there will be more.+ fast paced movement and combat. it's a pleasure how the combat is playing out so well already. it's pacing is fast, with layers of vertical combat and many different spells. improving the skills with gambits and building some synergies is quite interesting and enjoyable. the magnificent combat is already one of the major selling points.+ the boss design is excellent. there is a lot of variety in design and skill set, making each boss a unique and memorable experience. i really liked their decision making a pool of different bosses for each encounter.+ liked the room progression system. it's all about meaningful decisions and how you progress in your character development.+ eye-catching pixel art in-game graphics and exceptionally well-drawn character art. astral ascent is a pleasure to look at!+ fully dubbed dialogues, and the dub is actually decent as well. i'm usually quite critical about dubs and prefer no dub over a bad one. at least, the audio quality. the quality of some of the dialogue texts is something they have to dastically improve on.+ combat controls are quite decent, ui controls and managing your stuff is a tad bit clunky at times, but nothing you won't get used to after a couple of hours.+ wholesome sound design, calm and relaxing audio is soothing your ears on a high level quality.~ melee combat feels weak no matter what upgrade you're obtaining. there is quite some balancing to do. at least most of the spells seem fine tho.~ charming characters, although they don't have enough interesting lines of dialogue.~ it's awkward how the game shows you a dialogue symbol on npcs, but they don't even have anything new to say. instead, they'll repeat the same line over and over. please don't bait me with pop ups, if nothing is going to happen.~ some character names are pretty nonsense. a dragon called "barbecue", are you serious? it's not funny.~ meta progression needs to be worked on. ~ some of the enemies and their skills kinda aim tracking you, which feels awkward to play against.~ would've loved to see different outfits instead of different colors for the same skin.~ the combat controls are quite good, but piloting the UI and managing your items can be a little clunky at times. this is nothing you won't get used to after a couple of hours tho.~ pricing of the early access isn't accurate in my opinion. 20 bucks on sale for an early access title is a lot to ask.- unnecessary detailed AND unskippable tutorial. it was indeed well built into the game, but i generally dislike forced tutorials. even more so if they're showing me plain and basic game mechanics like: how to attack on the ground, attack in the air, jump, dodge and so on. it's simply boring for seasoned players and will be delaying the game for no reason in the beginning.- it's not possible to skip anything meaningful to speed up runs. like boss intro, end of run resource count (at least not fast enough), respawning and so on. those things will take up an unnecessary amount of time while doing a run and in between runs.- game performance is kinda bad in this early state. frame drops, micro stutters and lags. the good and odd thing is that the combat performance is actually flawless, but starting a dialogue or loading something hurts the games performance for a couple of seconds.- didn't like the traps at all. please make them destroyable or think about other kind of traps, like basic spikes or something. undestroyable thingies which spawn a constant flood of enemies are not fun  (plants already got fixed)that's my conclusion after a couple of hours and more or less finishing the early access content. i'll update this review after more hours played and of course content updates, which will happen since the developer is motivated and reacting to critique from the player base. overall i think this game has a bright future, so i'll rate astral ascent with an 8/10 despite having some early access problems. the premise is definitely there, and only time will tell if the devs manage to make a real gem out of this already pretty solid base of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was actually about to refund this game after thirty minutes or so, because there was just *so much* stuff that I didn't understand and the combat wasn't really clicking with me. But I stuck with it because I saw so many positive reviews - and I'm glad I did, because after a few hours more I'm now having a blast! The key to me was realizing that, even though this game looks and feels a lot like Hollow Knight or other Metroidvanias, it's really not. If you expect to engage with each enemy individually by using your main attack, the combat is going to feel too stiff and restrictive. But once you start thinking of it almost like an ARPG (Diablo, Path of Exile, etc) then it really opens up. Your goal is to create "combat loops" of spells and abilities that you use against entire groups, while your main attack is more just about generating mana. The game doesn't do a great job of communicating this, but if you can get into that mindset, then it's really fun and rewarding. The boss fights are really great too and stand out as especially well-designed. I don't care much for the story or aesthetic - fantasy stuff like this doesn't really appeal to me - but the art is great and the environments are varied. Overall, I would really recommend it for anyone who wants a dense, deep roguelite that's structured like Hades but plays more like Diablo.

_childDocuments_.review: This new roguelike promises to be a new and interesting experience for those that like this gendra. Heavilly makes me feel about Dead Cells. The game loop feels in a good place and the choices you make through each run feel meaningfulll towards building a different character. The way you use spells and upgrade them is interesting and original, and makes for different runs everytime. Right now, two things are in a rough state : game feel and balance.For balance, I would worry too much, but i'll just hope that the devs will focus more on working on the existing spells/auras rather rather than add new ones. The amount of spells/auras is huge, and while this is a good thing it shouldn't make the balancing work get out of hand. I also feel that a lot of builds good at clearing the main game are horrible against bosses (like electric stacks). In general, bosses mostly fall to raw damage rather than specific stack build ups. Some stacks like pacify and vulnerable dont seem to do much and I would much rather go for elemental stack. In general, stack building should maybe be a bit quicker, as it seems you need to heavily invest in one set of stacks to get some mild effect out of them. The stage two boss seem to have overtuned health. As for game feel, I think it will be the most important thing towards making this a great game or a decI would ent game. Right now, air movement in particular feels pretty bad. The Taurus challenge room is a good example of this, it feels clunky to do and difficult for the wrong reasons. Some battle situations can get a bit confusing when they are multiple ennemies. The wind up and tells for their attacks are somewhat hard to see in the visual noise. I think the game devs need to work on visual feedback in general, making the game clearer. Although I criticize the game in lenght I had a fun time playing it and plan to continue playing it for a while, and it is in a very good place full of content for an early access game.

_childDocuments_.review: -------------------------------------Video Review Here:--------------------------------------Transcript:Dead Cells and Hades just had a baby:  And its name is Astral Ascent, and it’s gooooood.	That’s the TLDR anyway, but also doesn’t do the game enough justice as it’s completely hooked me in a way that a new release hasn’t in awhile.  The artwork is beautiful, the animation is seamlessly fluid, the music is enchanting, the story is…OK I guess, we’ll circle back to that later, but, most importantly, the gameplay is an electric, screen clearing display of organized chaos that invokes a sense of wizard-power-fantasy that few other games have achieved for me.  With how stacked this year has been with incredible releases from AAA studios and indies alike, I almost feel obligated to help it out by showing this game some love, and if you’re a fan of the rogue-genre, I think you should too.	Astral Ascent is a sidescrolling action roguetype where you play as one of four different characters and attempt to break out of an eternal prison-realm by an ominous unknown entity named “The Master.”  At first, the format and gameplay is pretty familiar and seemingly simple. Each character shares a simple dodge, double jump, and falling attack that may remind you of another certain game…  They also have their own basic attacks, signature abilities, and exclusive spells to each.   The secret sauce for this game, however, is in its spell-based combat.  Most rogue games tend to focus on either your basic attacks or weapon pickups being your primary source of damage, with active abilities just being a secondary option that, while offering some useful utility, are only available to use sparingly or, if you’re like me, completely forget to use them at all.  Astral Ascent flips this dynamic around where the active abilities, or in this case, spells, are the stars of the show.  Throughout a run you’ll find several new spells to add to your arsenal, with up to four equipped at a time.  Spells, naturally, use mana as a resource that is refreshed upon landing basic attacks, making a simple but satisfying loop of interspersing spells and attacks in order to keep your mana up.  Unlike other games, though, where you’d normally be able to freely use whatever spells you want, Astral Ascent requires you to use all four spells in your “queue” in order for them to refresh.  This sounds weird at first, but it’s actually a small mechanic that makes a world of difference in terms of making the moment-to-moment gameplay feel fresh.  With this system, the player has to keep in mind what spells are coming next as to position themselves accordingly in order to get the most out of each.  Some spells are more forgiving and will attack most of what’s on screen or auto-target enemies, while others require a bit more precision and, in some cases, actually grant invincibility during the cast animation as a means to dodge attacks.  There are a metric ___-ton of spells to choose from and the animations and effects from the ones that I’ve seen are spectacular.  Some are more useful than others, but like any rogue game of this type, that’s to be expected.  Spells can also be augmented with “Gambits” that offer varying effects from launching meteors on cast or summoning poison-dealing saplings.  Furthermore, passive abilities called “Auras” offer significant bonuses and have huge potential synergies with your spell-queue and even other Auras.  All of this together creates an absolutely WILD array of possibilities, and some of the late-game results from these intertwined systems can get ABSURD.  It’s a very, very satisfying system.	But what are all these spells good for without things to fight them with?  Astral Ascent has a solid bestiary of grunt, elite, and ESPECIALLY boss enemies to fight.  The opening half of the first area is a bit of a pushover, but that quickly changes.  All enemies have a variety of attacks and patterns to keep you on your toes.  Some packs of elite enemies and challenge rooms are honestly tougher than some boss fights.  And speaking of bosses, this game’s bosses, kick.. ASS…  A lot of times in these games, I get to a boss and think “____, a boss” but here I think “_____ YES, A BOSS!!”  If it wasn’t obvious by now, the bosses in Astral Ascent are representations of the twelve Zodiac signs, each with their own personalities, unique dialogue, and fighting styles and they are all extremely satisfying to fight.  Some of the attacks genuinely made me think “how did they think of that?”  Unfortunately due to RNG I haven’t fought all of them, but so far I think it’s safe to say these devs know how to make a good boss fight.  The best part is the enemies and bosses only get more interesting as you rack up successful runs.  After your first completed run, you gain access to Destiny Levels.  Think Heat Level in Hades or Boss Cells in Dead Cells.  Even the first Destiny level expanded the moveset of regular enemies and elites making regular encounters much more interesting.  It’s a solid addition of variety so far, and given that people in early access have previously cleared Destiny levels 30 and higher, it seems like the challenge won’t prove to be insurmountable.  It’s a great take on adding difficulty to runs that’s more than on par with similar systems in other games.	There’s also some little details and quality of life features that I really appreciate that I think are worth mentioning.  Being able to preview what a spell does before picking it up, being able to save and quit mid-run at the start of ANY room, the icon for your next spell appearing above your character, and, most important to me, the option to outline your character and enemies for better visual clarity that the game points you to right at the start.  These are always the qualities I feel that make a good game great, and are my favorite things to point out because I feel they’re a noteworthy indicator of how much effort the devs have put into their game.	I feel at this point it goes without saying that the presentation is gorgeous.  The character artwork, cutscene animations, spell effects, and overall scenery are nothing short of eye-candy (Also shoutout to godrays, I’m a sucker for godrays).  I also appreciate the main menu with its Kingdom Hearts vibes.   I’d wager some people may have a bit of pixel-art-fatigue in the indie sphere, but I personally think there’s a certain charm to pixel art that goes beyond feelings of nostalgia for games-of-yore.  I dunno, I never get tired of it.  Audio-wise the soundtrack is insanely good.  The hub world music alone is incredible.  And the rest of the tracks deliver equally well if-not better.  Audio during combat has just the right amount of ‘oomph’ to it, with spells, enemy attacks, and important prompts like being out of mana all being audible enough without being too overstimulating.  The voice acting is… alright.  Most of the cast gives a solid performance, with the Zodiacs being the highlights (though I might be biased because they’re all hot, not as hot as Papa Yalee, but hot nonetheless).  Some characters are… kinda annoying though.  Kiran, for example, is probably my favorite character to play, but least favorite to listen to.  I’m kind of over the “over-confident-frat-boy-who-punches-things” trope.  Kiran: “I’ll forgive you… if you can do THREE HUNDRED PUSHUPS FASTER THAN ME!”  Overall, though, Astral Ascent is a great audio-visual package that is quite the achievement for such a small dev team, let alone a game at its price-point.	As for the story… it’s… OK I guess.  I’m still fairly early in, but so far the story hasn’t particularly gripped me.  The stakes aren’t exactly interesting from first impressions, big bad guy destroys planets and we gotta stop him and all that.  And while many of the characters are charming, especially this Capybara guy called “Sire Bapy” who I just wanna give a big ol’ hu

_childDocuments_.review: Only 3 hours played, 4-5 runs attempted, and already a lot of fun had. The progression is satisfyingly quick and hits the perfect beats a roguelite should hit to keep players engaged without overwhelming them. The fundamental gameplay is also fantastic, for me some of the best in the Metroidvania genre (which I'm normally not a huge fan of). In particular, the ability to reset your jumps and dashes while still in air by simply landing an attack is something that makes the fights feel fair, frenetic, and overall something that makes you still feel powerful despite the relatively simplistic graphics. The different heroes all feel like their own characters, which is something that gives the game immense replay value due to the different ways you can build each characters throughout your runs. My favorite so far is honestly the starter (think Wraith from Apex Legends). I'm definitely a fan, and I'll definitely be picking up any DLC characters as they get released (on sale, because I am cheap).

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game it is a Roguelite in a similar style to Dead Cells with gorgeous pixel art and a fun collection of characters with varying abilities and personality which makes for an entertaining time seeing the different ways everyone interacts. The gameplay loop is solid and hits the craving for one more run with the different builds holding my interest and the way that skills interact, I am fond of the voice work in the game as well the whole experience has just been checking my boxes to make me love the game and I can't recommend it enough.Bonus points: Calie's hands are the right shade for the palms and when that care is taken with art direction it is a bonus point for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun, but I can't say I love it. It plays pretty well, and the idea of pitting the player against overpowered but sympathetic anime villains with insane attacks that cover the entire screen is appealing. But where it falls apart for me is the story, or the attempt at that. I almost wish there was no writing in this game at all. As far as I could tell, the game tries to emulate Hades with its fully voice acted, large roster of characters, but nothing that anyone had to say during my time with it was even remotely interesting and a lot of it was totally and painfully cringe inducing. It feels a bit weird to downvote a game for something that was clearly not the focus and could be easily ignored, but I feel like the game tried to present itself as having characters I could be even somewhat invested in and that just wasn't the case. If you're the type of player that only cares about gameplay you will find plenty to like here, but for me it didn't click.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun action rogue like. Gameplay is solid, characters are fun, and builds are interesting to put together. My main negatives with this game is that it feels way to easy once the game's basic strategy clicks with you and there is so much visual noise it feels impossible to keep track of your tiny character in the late game of a run. I've already beaten the game after what feels like a handful of runs, which feels really early for a rogue like. Art style and music is pretty good. Overall worth buying if you are into these types of games.Update: I got the "true" ending of the game after beating it several times. Still recommend the game, but I really do wish it were harder. Getting the true ending after only about 15 hours feels rather quick for a rogue like game personally. If you are a fan of higher difficulty rogue likes, and don't want something more casual I would avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, although i wish there was more content. I feel like i exhausted all of the content much more quickly than i had anticipated (my hours played aren't accurate, as i have a bad habit of forgetting to close games). It didn't take me very long to unlock all of the spells and  purchase all of the upgrades, and then you're just kind of going through the same exact worlds and beating the same exact final boss over and over again with increasingly higher difficulty levels, which isn't actually very difficult at all once you get the hang of everything and learn which spells and auras you prefer.  It ultimately took me a fraction as long to do everything and unlock everything in this game than it did in, for example, Hades.I got excited for the new character/DLC, thinking i had a reason to pick it back up and had more content to explore... but then i beat it on my very first run with her without any problem, at which point i was back to pretty much being out of things to do again. Hopefully there is more content coming down the road; like i said, the gameplay itself is pretty fantastic. Just wish i had a reason to continue playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the price.  Art, music are definitely AAA level.  There is a lot of love put into this game.Regarding mechanics, people might find that combat can feel clunky or not very engaging -- this is not the case.  All movement is able to be cancelled with a dash.  You get one dash, but it resets upon impacting an enemy with a basic attack, leading to a fluid combat system, albeit detracting from the beautiful art present within the attacks themselves.  Dashes can also be reset with a ground slam, which does require an enemy to hit.Difficulty.  This game will absolutely maul you at the higher difficulties if you don't prepare properly.  It's also very very approachable on the easier difficulties, a very good balance.  You can choose modifiers to make the game harder/easier and are rewarded with permanent bonuses for completing these difficulties.  There are many choices, which leads to a strong choose your own adventure system.My one complaint is that many (or even all) of the spells have pre-swing animations.  They don't leverage the art of the game mostly and serve to dissuade me from using spells altogether.  The spell system is an attempt to do something unique regarding spells in games, rather than just FIREBALL over and over.  It uses a rotating 4 slot system and you MUST spend each spell to re-use another one.  Duplicates are allowed.  I really hope they change dash cancelling auto attacks proceed through the later animations of characters, so I can see the rest of the animations more often.  The spell cast delay I'd hope they change to be associated with huge high level nuke spells or something equivalent so they FEEL strong.  Standing still to throw 3 shurikens feels awful.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I am not too much a fan of Rogue-like/lite games. I grabbed this without knowing what it was because I liked the visuals of the game and it also reminded me of one of my favorite games. Boss battles aren't weirdly unfair like some rogue-lites and they are actually fun. They seem more akin to a Mega Man Zero boss than a typical boss from this genre, which is a nice breath of fresh air.

_childDocuments_.review: Just 100% the game, and I have to say that this has a pretty well-designed gameplay:- The movement is  super smooth, very comparable to Dead Cells in this regard.- There are a lot of spells, spell modifiers (gambit), and passives (aura/echo/weapon passive) that creates a ton of builds and optimizations you can make during a run. The spell recycle mechanic is also a brilliant idea that forces you to use a number of spells instead of just spamming one spell again and again. I much prefer this to having a spell cooldown.- There are 4 characters (with one to come with the DLC), each has 3 weapons, and each weapon comes with 3 passive, which creates even more gameplay diversity.- The spells and auto-attack animation all looks very good and feels good to play.- There are a lot of bosses (13 bosses and 6 mini-bosses in total).- Run progression feels right. You start out slow but always feel broken toward the end of the run.Overall, this is a must buy for action rogue-lite fan.

_childDocuments_.review: extremely fun, extremely replayable game. If you're looking for a game with incredible artstyle, nice music, excellent voice-acting, action-packed & fun gameplay with some elements of classic rogue-like RNG progression, this is the game for you.  It was a serendipitous experience playing this game for the first time and watching it just exceed all expectations, highly recommend that more people give it a chance and try it, because I guarantee that it can get you hooked if you let it.The game also includes the ability to do steam remote play with a friend, or just local co-op if you have a controller on hand. I play it with some of my online friends and it's a very fun experience going through the levels together, and I am looking forward to the future of this game. Hopefully we will see a greater degree of player agency and customization in terms of each playable character. My suggestion is adding appearance variables for each character so that players can feel more engaged with their character.But that just about wraps it up, it's a great game and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a good replayable 2D indie experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly easy to recommend. This is one of the best roguelikes out there. Probably the best co-op roguelike.+ Extremely satisfying, snappy controls+ Very good enemy design+ Steam remote play works like playing locally. Slightly finicky+ Never feels unfair, i just feel bad+ Does a great job of balancing flashy attacks and visual clarity. You can mostly see vital attack information over screen clutter+ Great progression inside as well as outside of a run+ Lots of fun build options+ Every Character is very unique+ I like the Art style+- Nitpick 1: The Skill system with 4 different skills in a chain is... strange. Its not the best system i have ever seen, but it is novel and works. I dont think there is anyone actually making a combo out of this. Everyone will just try to get the same skill 4 times. But it is an additional hurdle and thus still works fine as a roguelike system.+- Nitpick 2: I don't like shared rewards. The game gives out enough for both players, but you just get additional loot you can distribute among both players. It is really not much of a problem here, but i just prefer everyone having his own loot pool. Having a shared loot pool just means that it is sometimes better to give everything to one player which i disfavour.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. So many things are seemingly impossible to dodge. There are no move speed or dash upgrades, so how do you expect me to get to the other side of the screen?2. The verticality of almost every enemy attack is not properly shown (other than beams). Hell - I'd almost rather you DIDN'T show me how they're going to attack, if it doesn't properly describe how to dodge it. Moreover, the red markers/beams/etc aren't always precise. I think I'm out of it, but oops - there goes a quarter of my health!3. Combat can be extremely floaty (attacks/spells keep you in the air) making positioning for these hard-to-dodge enemy attacks even harder.4. Everything attacks EXTREMELY quickly with very little animated telegraphing.The concept of this game is excellent. But... the movement is seriously not for me. I like precise, methodical movement. It CAN be quick, but not floaty or chaotic. I wish the dodging system relied on jumping/dashing instead of floating in the right spot through actions that are NOT jumping/dashing. Making the game about 30% slower would help with this, but the rest of this probably can't be helped. Hell, I'm not looking for an easy game. Make enemies hit harder. But don't make me feel like there was absolutely no way to win. Side note: For those reading who enjoyed the fluidity of Dead Cells, ignore everyone who is comparing the two. This is *not* the same kind of game, other than it being a side-scrolling, 2D action roguelike. Judge this game on its own merits. And, believe me, it IS a good game. But it's not Dead Cells 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute insane amount of RNG.Your basic attack may as well not do any damage at all and exists only to charge your spells, which you cannot choose when to perform since they follow an ordered sequence. So in the heat of combat, you need a ranged attack and instead do a melee spell.You'll spend more time dodging than fighting since every enemy has a ranged attack and can shoot you from the next town over and you'll be facing at least 5 foes at a time.Normal fights are a slog and take forever because, since there's so few health drops, you cannot risk being aggressive and have to rely on hit and run tactics.Lots of little power ups, but because there's so many, they end up having barely any effect.  Just lots of reading and weighing options that ultimately have no meaning.  You'll be dead soon anyway and have to do it all again.Typical rogue-like: Grind, die, grind some more.

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetically beautiful game. Action is somewhat average though. I didn't really like the 4 rotating skills gimmick. The limited mana pool and spell rotation felt restrictive and limiting. You either spam those 4 skills untill all of them are on cooldown or try to micro-manage them in some way, but overall it didn't add to the enjoyment of this game. Game world is chopped up into small arena pieces. Every area is like a few screens in length. Too much teleporting and stuff, No seamless transition between the areas.Music is okay'ish, but it felt out of place. Had to turn it off. Didn't mesh with the things you see and do in this game. Voice acting is also hit and miss. Some characters sound great, others - mediocre. The writing is a bit too cringy though. You can easily tell this game is from this time period.Kinda fun to mow down small enemies, but the bosses are "unnavoidable damage" dealers pretty much all the time. Unless you overpower them faster and save your a$$. Game is very hard at first, but the more stuff you unlock, the easier it gets, (only bosses are still a very big pain in the cheeks) and then this game suddenly becomes like a big chore. If you don't want to play a good roguelite platformer and want to invest your time into something mediocre - this game is the right choice for you.

_childDocuments_.review: **v1.0 updateForgot about this game and haven't played for almost a year, went back when I heard v1.0 is out. Played from the start, and gahdawm they made improvements alright. Everything's smoother, no more frame drops. I love the new aura system and the changes they made for the skills of each hero. Time to sink more hours into this until hades 2 comes out.My previous review below are still valid. This game's awesome.***************Verdict: Must buy! The only thing that might discourage you to buy it (for now) is that the game is incomplete and some random fps drop issues which is a tiny inconvenience at best. - The story of the game has huge potential, I love that it's like Hades where there's a progression in terms of the NPC dialogs. Makes you wanna do another run just to know what the NPC is gonna say next.- Phenomenal music and narration, the music goes really well with the fast-paced game (or slow paced areas) and the voices for each NPC is really good. It makes you feel that each NPC have their own unique identity.- Art is hella great, period.- The action part of the game is AWESOME. Just with the initial release of two characters there are already a lot of build that you can create. The execution of skills and attacks of your character is so smooth that you can chain your AAs in between skills fluidly.- Replayability for sure isn't going to be a problem, even with an incomplete game it's already really fun to play since there's already a lot elements that you can play around to build your character for each run. I'm looking forward to the release knowing that there will be a lot of bosses and 5 different characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I also own this game on Switch, where it runs great! I decided to come purchase this on Steam as well, so that I could receive beta updates, and leave a glowing review here on Steam.Astral Ascent perfectly scratches my itch for Sega Genesis era 2-player co-op side-scrolling beat em up action; I haven't been this happy with a cooperative multiplayer experience since Castle Crashers, which should say a lot!Astral Ascent also scratches a very particular itch for me, both the progression and the environment's themeing make me feel like I get to experience endgame raid/bossing party content in a classic lite MMO like Maplestory or Runescape, without the hundreds of days of grinding (and paying for microtransactions or subscriptions) first. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun and strategic roguelite, it's pretty good in couch coop (which is something severely lacking in other roguelites - couch coop mode). Nice sinergies, and the combat is fun. In regards to the combat, the mobs are easy and more of a HP risk than something difficulty to deal: you need to preserve HP for the bosses, the true challenge. All mobs and bosses telegraph their attacks, so a good player can deal with them even with a sub-optimal build (not my and my GF case lol). Took me 60h to win the game with one character (by win I mean winning DL6) only playing couch coop with a total newbie (my GF, don't tell her). 60h is a looooot of gaming hours for me, so this game was worth every cent.Hoping for patches/DLCs to play more time - my GF don't understand the concept of grind by the grind and would want to play DL7-DL100 right now, though it looks that it should be fun (as you upgrade your metagame by winning DLs).

_childDocuments_.review: I've put in three and a half hours. Unless something changes drastically I will state the following:I like this game.Snappy invincibility frames, fluid pixel animation, and that summer day kindness that Anime influence transmits so well. There is a whimsical vibe to the entire experience.You start as an assassin. You know, people that lurk in the shadows and kill for a living? Yeah, she's a people person who respects and cares for life. This entire game is de-fanged in a way that leaves the emotions high and gracious. The opening sequence clearly states all common enemies are soulless immaterial matter. The bosses (Zodiacs) are characters with backgrounds and stories that you never kill, just defeat in battle.This is the nobility of fighting for a just cause with the trappings of magic and blades. No moral quandaries here, and no silly twists thus far. There may be some by the end, but for now there be likable unrealistic characters and a fluid, fun combat that bears mastering. The attitude wins me over. A lightness not generally associated with rogue-like games. It feels like a labor of love.I got this in the Humble Bundle for August of '24. It is a surprise gem. I'll update this review if this game ends up turning sour, but nice job, Hibernian.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally got a true ending , and 71% of completion , will probably go for 100% thoughtPros:- Visually incredible game : stop and look at the detailed pixel art on backgrounds is surprising , its a nice contrast with the flashy , and sharp (Some of them) skills , one of the most beatifull roguelikes out there- Really flashy combat and animations : Not only your skills , the boss fights are awesome too- Fast paced and good movement : Very enjoyable if you are looking for a game to pump some adrenaline while dodging some screen covering attacks that leave some small pixels-Nice progression : Levels are quite balanced overall- Daily modifiers : You can choose one of three daily modifiers every day , gets some nice variation Cons : - Very fast paced if you are not familiar with these type of games- Cutscenes are unskippable (I think?) : By the third time libra was gonna beat me into minced meat , got really traumatizingCritique:- Challenge spike on certain bosses or levels : Libra is harder than Master , prove me wrong - Lack of rooms : 1.0 just released , so its undestandable , but by run 30 or so you will probably see most of the rooms- Some builds depend heavily on you finding a very specific aura : If i see another ice fragment astral on my pure slime run , i WILL cry - This game goes for a common way of story in roguelikes , you do something -> you get a conversation in your hub area about it , its simple , but thing is this gets really jumbled up really easily because when 2 things happen that trigget a conversation , one gets pushed back until next time you enter the hub  This stacks up overtime , by my 44th run , the hub learned that i defeated Libra- I would like more interaction between PC and Zodiacs : Banter beetwen PC really makes them feel fun , and if they are friends , but there is a very limited amount of itAnd zodiacs are the second most developed chracters after the PC´s , but there is just so little opportunity to chat with them , and most of it is general I would like to be able to talk to them in the bar , get a friendly one in the hub even to speak to them  Overall : Excellent game , my favorite roguelike of the last years , and my favorite fast paced one overall , worth the buy

_childDocuments_.review: Worse version of deal cells with a less than stellar UI/UX. The descriptions of the actual impacts of abilities is incredibly unclear. If I put a 50% chance of poison on my three knife throw default spell, I personally expect the ability to have a 50% chance of poison. That said it could be for my whole character, the spell, each knife in the spell, spells as a whole, my attacks while the spell is queued, my attacks while the spell is in progress, my attacks in general, etc. It seemed to impact my basic attacks and not the spell itself though. This is one example, but that is then repeated across all modifiers in the game. I'm picking things up that are only vaguely explained, then they work completely different to how I would expect them to since I am applying to a slot attached to a spell/spell slot. The combat feels alright, but overall is just a worse/less fluid version of dead cells. Hopefully they make some level of adjustment to the UI/UX and how descriptive things are so I can understand better what is going on and the benefits of picking one ability over another. Until then I'm going to refund the game and keep an eye out on future updates since I think there is some level of promise.

_childDocuments_.review: I think people that enjoy Hades and enjoy roguelikes would probably like this, but this game is absolutely NOT for me.The graphics are so overly stylized that I can't tell what in the heck is going on in combat, even with outlines turned on.Hard to tell enemy from projectile from environment.Why do you have four rotating abilities? I just feel like I have zero control over what skill I will be using next, and just mash my abilities hoping it will be useful. Am I meant to memorize what four skills I have, in what order, and keep track in my head of the rotation as it changes? Just feels... Needlessly unintuitive. And it is very hard to tell each skill apart at a glance, like in combat. The icons are so focused on being pixel-art that they completely missed the mark on being quickly identifiable.Also, the cutscenes were very cool, but for the love of all that is holy LET ME SKIP THEM IF I WANT.Why are we still seeing games with unskippable cutscenes?I totally respect the work and effort you put into those amazing cutscenes, but damn, let me skip them if I want.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only recently gotten into rogue-likes and rogue-lites, having for most of my life thought they were beyond my ability, or difficult to truly find myself invested in them. I was never able to get into Rogue Legacy, for example, and wrote the genre off, until I recently played Hades, Risk of Rain 2, Backpack Hero, Slay the Spire, and now Astral Ascent. I love these latter titles for multiple reasons, but the common denominator is a complex, in-depth system of mechanics that is yet somehow incredibly intuitive and rewarding. Astral Ascent does this in spades, and as such is well on its way to becoming my favorite rogue-lite. One more thing that Astral Ascent does better than all these games (except maybe Hades)? A wonderful story, memorable NPCs, bosses, and allies, lovable characters to play, and incredible dialogue/voice acting. The art is also pure joy to experience, and that's something considering I never really enjoyed pixel art before this game.If there's anything to improve on, for me, would be the randomizing of skill drops. I've unlocked a lot, character-specific and general, but I feel that after a few dozen runs, I still largely get the same 6-8 skill drops. I presume later skills get unlocked on maps with more stars or later areas, but even with that I haven't experienced even 20% of everything I've unlocked. Maybe I'm just unlucky though!Edit: Progressed far enough, drop rate makes more sense now!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Great action platformer roguelite that goes heavy on build customization during a run. Plenty of spells to try out to build your own skill rotation, linear room to room map system where you choose from 3 different rooms to enter with different rewards. Plenty of animation cancelling and movement related stuff to make the gameplay fast feeling. You attack until you fill up your mana meter and start spellcasting relentlessly.Bosses are fun fights and have fun patterns on their normal and true forms, designed well around your cooldown-based iframe dodge and positioning.Nice metaprogression elements, first time clear happens pretty early and opens up more meta progression and story related elements. Best part about this is the amount of voice acting, so many lines said between characters and even deciding on what you get or what happened in the current room is nice to hear from the characters and shows their personality really well.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10. Astral Ascent was probably the most fun I've had with an action roguelike since Hades, the latter of which has - for me - become the golden standard of what a roguelike should be. First, the positives. This game very clearly mixes the easily recognisable level structure of Dead Cells with the narrative structure Hades so amazingly perfected. It is a 2D platformer that rewards exploration while also not punishing you for dying so often, because every run you do - be they short or long - advances the story even further. Combat and spell customisation is great but certainly takes some getting used to. I also personally feel like it could be a bit more intuitive, but that's just me. Sometimes it's just difficult to pull off combos or dash away in time even though I'm very clearly pressing the right buttons. The art in Astral Ascent, in one word, is just gorgeous. The landscapes in the background, as well as the character designs and even the soundtracks are well made and possibly one of the game's biggest selling points for some people. Co-op mode is a great bonus, though I haven't made use of it yet myself. So what are the cons? Well, for me the biggest thing that is keeping me from giving it an 8 or above is the story and the dialogue. It is, for a lack of better words, cringe and incredibly cliché. The characters, despite their cool looks, unfortunately fall flat as soon as they open their mouth. They sound so one-dimensional. They have one signature trait and that's their whole personality. The story also just isn't very interesting in my opinion. You're trying to escape from a prison but to do that, you have to beat some overpowered celestial beings. That's basically it. No real side stories, or any interesting ones at least. You want backstories on any of the characters? Do some runs, collect some memory fragments and maybe you'll get to read about how little Aries came to be who she is now. Granted, I've only done about 15 runs and the furthest I've gotten was the 5th zone I think, so maybe I've just not seen enough yet. All in all, Astral Ascent definitely could use some improvements but it's worth picking it up if you're a massive roguelike fan or if you're just looking for a bit of a challenge.

Fluent control, carefully designed rouge system, outstanding bgm, great artworks with an easily-accepted constellation background and continuous devotion of devs make this game excellent. Imo this game is as good as Hades to a great extent.But here are some feedback of game experience which drives to write this from the perspective of expecting a better Astral Ascent.1. Bugs do appear in a rare pattern during my cooperation playtime, like i can't pick up the spell that i bought.3. Maybe we need indicators that show where i am, coz the scene is just too full to recognize myself especially there are two players in late game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just absolutely amazing. The devs care for it, and you can definitely tell. I will say it's not a game for everyone, but if it catches your eye initially, I doubt that you'll regret picking it up.The gameplay is smooth and enables a high skill ceiling, the fights are pretty engaging and you have to think and react to thinks quickly later on in your progression.There's 4 characters each with their own unique playstyle, and each have 3 unlockable weapons that change the way they play as well, and each of the weapons have 3 unlockable upgrades that even change how the weapons feel to an extent.The game does a really great job at holding your hand so you're not super lost early on, and it doesn't feel intrusive or annoying. There's a lot that isn't explained that is just left for the player to experience too. The lore is rich, and it's incredible, I love the characters and the world building and just everything is so charming and grand. There's a lot of secrets to discover, and at the moment I'm nowhere near uncovering everything, but the things that I have found pull me in and make me ask questions, and make me want to find answers. My biggest issue with this game is that the runs feel a bit same-sy, because you always start in the same area and progress linearly. But the bosses in each area can change, and as you beat the "Destiny" tiers (difficulty increase ranks after clearing runs), the enemies and bosses also gain more abilities and ways to throw you off your balance.There's something a bit confusing at first, and this will be spoilers so read at your own riskThe final boss is INCREDIBLE. Maybe I'm doped up on adrenaline because I just barely managed to defeat him, but it was a really exciting fight. The music was incredible, the visual effects were stunning and flashy, the sound effects were awesome. The fight is just very well done but pretty difficult.Overall I absolutely recommend this game. I will definitely play more, especially in the future because I know for the fact the devs are cooking some good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Barring Dead Cells, which has a different sort of appeal, this is the best 2d action platformer roguelite I've played so far. Very Hades inspired, but with more interesting builds, more variety and a longer lasting meta progression. The moment to moment gameplay feels excellent, it's clear that a lot of testing, effort and care has gone into making the movement as smooth as possible. No enemies feel truly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ either, except for maybe a few moves from a few bosses. This is mostly fine though, as the focus is split 50/50 between executing the moment to moment, and creating a solid build that can either deal disgusting amount of damage or outtank the final boss eternally.My main gripe is the lack of endgame/postgame goals. Feels like the only thing to do once you've beaten the final boss for real is play a bunch more to unlock more stuff while upping the difficulty for yourself, very little bespoke content beyond that point. Nevertheless, it's fun to try new aura combinations and to see how OP you can make a run. It's also fun to push yourself to beat higher and higher difficulties in this game's version of Hades' "pact of punishment". The story is somewhere between servicable and good, characters range from annoying to endearing. Doesn't matter much, clearly not the main focus of the game.Game also looks disgustingly beautiful and controls like delicious butter.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not the most addictive game I've played since I bought a Steam Deck. It's fast, it's fun, it's challenging and it keeps me coming back for more. The fighting mechanics are easy to understand and you'll get used to them rather fast, but it never made me feel like it compromised in depth. I'm really in to Couch Co-ops, but this game is easily as fun on your own. If you're into fast paced roguelites then this is definitely worth a try. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: So far now they have 4 Characters totaling Ayla (dagger) Kiran (Fist) Octave (Dual Pistol) and Calie (Gems) and the 4 World is out which is definitely a lot more challenging. They reworked some of the rooms only appearing in certain conditions. And Auras! they wasn't kidding about adding 250 Auras. The synergies that each Aura have now. It isn't just plain old If you heal you get a shield for 3 seconds. It'll be something like that with an added of 2 armor and anything else revolving around that field. Fall attacks trigger combustion and ember. Burning enemies that are crit heal. Its a new fun system that will make finding a nice build you like really fun. They've definitely come a long way with listening to us the players and community to making an amazing game. So if you're gonna hate the game hate us honestly haha but we're all doing our part communicating with the dev team to make a really fun and unique game.I gotta say this is one of the best rouge-lites out there. It's so damn fun and rewarding even when you die. You always have new things to look forward to once you finally die or complete the run. You use spells to do big damage to enemies and can also be slotted with up to 4 gambits that give that spell special effects like, % damage/heal chance of crit or status and even summons. Your goal is to escape but each stage will be a fixed list of 3 Zodiacs that will be random. So 4 stages and with each being 3 zodiacs that are random and after either encountering them or beating them once. There is a chance you can find them in the next run or at A bar and they'll join you if you can clear their challenge. There's only too much to explain in a review to cover everything but I'll do the most I can.Spells/Gambit/Auras - To use spells you need Mana which can be gain by Basic Att or picking it up from trees. 4 spells can be slotted. Cost 1-3 mana. Can be rearranged. Have to use all spells to refresh, no cooldowns. Where to find? Peddler shop (refreshable using currency) Void Boss. Any exploration room (small chance) Celestial Spirit. Zodiac boss. Zodiac Challenge. Salvagable for Currency. Cannot regain gambits when salvaged in case you want to add a Gambit onto a different spell unfortunately :( Spells can be upgraded to do overall more damage using Pavo's Feather or you can simply find higher level spells with a chance of a gambit slotted.Auras - Auras are passive effects like 15% attspeed/dmg or permanent wisp. 4 can be slotted and replace. Can be found by going into a Yalee Kingdom Room. The more Yalee you rescue (kill elites that have yalee captives)The more Auras can be found in The Yalee Rooms but you can only pick one Aura.Sun Pieces - Used for unlocking passive power-ups for your runs. Buying new spells/auras you've unlocked. Can be gained by finding memories during exploration rooms. Completing challenges. Defeating enemies and Zodiacs once run is completed.Stars - The higher the difficulty the higher the Stars. Used to buy upgrades (Hp/Att/Attspeed) at andromeda's Bar. A chance for fixed amount of Keys, 1 Slot unlock, and Quarts From the Chameleon. Every room that involves combat will give Stars.Keys - Used for the Astral Chests (found in exploration room) 1 Key for Quarts and heal/mana or 3 for chance of Upgrade Shrine/Aura/Spell/Gambit. Used for a room (forgot the name) after beating a Zodiac. The first room will have a few rooms and one special room that requires 9/12 keys (2nd stage/3rd stage) and 3 of the random npcs back at Base will give you a special effect like bringing you back to life or one free purchase at each Peddler shop.Quarts - Healing Shards. Spells/Gambit at the Pedler shop or the special Sun Room.Amazing and buttery. Very charming and easy on the eyes with all the spells and attacks going off when fighting loads of enemies.I'm sorry I can't get it all noted down. But it's very well worth it. Especially if you enjoy the Rouge-lite Genre and the whole Zodiac thing. There isn't a Video out there that explains Every use of Currency. What each Room has. List of Character spells and general Spells but it's worth playing for yourself and seeing it or simply watch a video on youtube. Runs are usually about 20 to 40 if you make it to that farthest stage which is 3 for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Previous time I wrote review on this game, it was the very first early access version (or I believe so), there were only 2 locations as of the moment. Now I write it after beating it numerous times on different ascensions on full release. I liked this game from the very first time I played it, but there was only one issue I had with it – it was too easy. And I do mean it. It was easy. If you can beat a rogue-like from like a second run, something is wrong. And it what I did on early access. Now game is released fully, with 2 new locations, new bosses and mechanics. Is this problem fixed now?No. Apparently, it became even more apparent. Yes, I am saying it after numerous playthroughs, so I have a lot of things unlocked, but... well, in first location, it is literally hard to take damage at all. Second and third locations... are perfectly balanced. Bosses are still just "minor inconvinience", but overall, second and third locations are neither too hard, nor too easy... but then, you just get overfed. At 4th location, I oneshotted most enemis (minus bosses), and even Zodiacs died in like 10 seconds or less. At this point, having all Spells at level VII or higher is pretty easy, and if they are at this level... go, queen, slay. Nothing can really live through a Spell or two.Final boss... is disappointing. To this point, every single zodiac had its unique mechanic, at least on 1 or 2 attacks... final boss does not. He is... just a guy who hits very hard and very wide. Is he hard? Depends on whether do you have 20+ attack increases or no. Just joking, he is usually easy. As I said, attack patterns are pretty simple and even damage is not cracked. He is... just boring.So, is the game bad? Absolutely not, it is a fantastical rogue-like, one of the best I've ever played. Is it too easy? Yes. But it is not a reason to overlook this masterpiece. Just make sure to not expect a hardcore challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for game that is equally rewarding as it is challenging, look no further! Please note that my Review may contain some spoilers on some surprises you will run into in this game, including what kind of content you unlock and discover as you play, feel free to skip my review if you care about this kind of thing, but at least know that I've never been as happy about purchasing a video game in my life as I am with this one!What captured my eye at first is the 2D Pixel Art style of the game, and boy did I have 0 idea the amount of fun i was going to have when I made this purchase!Ever played a game where, upon beating it for the first time (after many attempts full of trial and error) it indirectly told you that what you just beat was actually just the tutorial, sent you back to the hub world, and introduced you to the real game? Look no further, this game did this exact thing to me and I immediately fell in love with it! Welcome to the Path of Destinies!Quite a lot to say and review about this masterpiece so i'll try to keep it as short as possible, but first i must praise the theme, setting and overall vibe that the game gives off, as well as the stunning pixel artwork, animation and the voice acting (Available in both English and Japanese for Anime-enjoyers)! - 4 different characters with completely unique playstyles to play and experiment with + 1 DLC- vast and expansive list of spells to unlock and use throughout your runs to experiment with and discover new tactics and ways to go about clearing the game- the thing that shocked me the most: every character has 3 different weapons and 3 different passives for each weapon to choose from to further customize and discover your favorite playstyle- 12 different bosses each with their own unique challenge and type of difficulty, coupled with more (i believe 8?) optional minibosses that you can come across in the middle of your runs. keeps things fresh and challenging every time- absolutely stunning graphics, worlds, chracter designs, and a lovely hub world to mess around in and talk to NPCs, check challenges and acheivements, unlockables and more...- color customization with a decently large selection of colors and variants to really express your personal style onto the characters you choose to play- a 5-element system of buffs (called gambits and auras) to discover throughout the run and find synergies with your playstyle and your chosen weapons and spells, there's a lot, and i mean A LOT of those- interesting and intuitive 4-spell system that keeps things limited but also interesting. Alongside a unique signature spell for each character that functions separately from the 4 spells that you equip- RPG-like level up system throughout the run that rewards you with "Prowesses" that buff your basic and signature attacks, combine the right ones with the gambits and auras you pick up throughout the runs and the synergies you discover will make you feel overpowered and ease your worries about beating the current run even when you're only halfway through it!- tons of different bonuses and unique rooms to explore throughout the run, each with its own gimmick or challenge and reward- Bosses you've beaten before can be befriended and called to deliver devastatingly good assist attacks, the same things you're usually dodging for your life. However, first you must beat them in their challenge minigames - what I mentioned in the preamble of this review: the Path of Destinies difficulty modifier: beat the game once and you'll be presented with new and more challenging difficulty levels, the first 6 are nonnegotiable, and once you've beaten level 6 you will unlock the various character endings as well as 48 more levels of difficulty that you can personally customize to your liking. I have not personally gotten to nor beaten level 54 just yet to comment on the difficulty of the extra-challenging difficulty levels beyond them (levels 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100, which you unlock by beating lv54) but I will gladly update this review to discuss them once I have.- Even though you might lose against the higher difficulties, you still acquire "Destiny Fragments" which you can use to equip yourself with bonus perks that help you get through each run easier, reward for trying and bigger reward for success.- 2 Player local co-op for double the fun with a friend, relative, or partner!!- If the difficulty of the game is too high for you, Resilience Mode in the settings can be turned on to make things easier and avoid the challenging becoming too frustrating.- Andromeda's bar,... enough said- Controlling your characters takes a bit of time to get accustomed to despite being intuitive and well-designed and programmed, understanding the jump recharge system and how dodging works took me a bit, but once you do there should be no complaints- There are A LOT of terms, effects, buffs, debuffs...etc. to learn and memorize. again takes a while to do so, but it's part of the fun of trial-and-error and learning the game; the glossary is also useful when in doubt. it will take some time before everything clicks, but when it does the enjoyment you derive out of this game will multiply exponentially- some of the weapon passives are challenging and difficult to unlock, you might need to play a few runs on lower difficulty just dedicated to unlocking them, only to find that they were not worth your time due to incompatibility with your playstyle.- While the story is lovely, interesting and well written, the way you go about unlocking the Memory Fragments is too dependent on RNG and thus you will find that some dialogues make zero sense to you because you didn't happen to unlock the right portion of the story text to read and be informed about the characters and their motivations. also the fact that it's text to read may not be everyone's cup of tea.- the difficulty can feel DAUNTING at times, starting off i had no idea how i'm going to get good enough at the game to even challenge Level 6, let alone the remaining difficulty levels, but the simple and effective roguelite improvements system quickly allowed me to fix some cracks in my strategies and worry about less as i played.- a full run from start to finish takes on average 55-70 minutes to complete assuming you don't lose halfway through, so you might need to take a break here and there or save and quit to come back to it later.- perhaps the biggest problem with this game is that at some points A LOT can be happening on screen at the same time and leave you cross-eyed trying to figure out where your character is, maybe costing you a good bit of life points or the whole run. "git gud" can't cut it if your screen is covered in enemies and effects that obscure your character from sight and gives you little indication on if you're safe or getting bombarded with damaging attacks, this is most egregious in the higher difficulties and can get frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Devs are quietly cooking and adding great updates consistently. Gameplay feels balanced and rewarding. I've never felt like RNG held me back from making a strong enough build to end a run. Unlockable skills and weapons for each character keep the loop from going stale on-top of discovering general skills each character can use. Quality animations, gorgeous artwork, and voiced characters keep me invested in the world. With an enjoyable soundtrack looping in the background of your home base, and battles. Eventually you unlock a difficulty modifier equivalent to heat/fear in Hades. Keeps you on your toes and makes it fun to see each Zodiac again so you can farm the special currency. The only downside is not having a demo with limited scope to show people what you've built here for newcomers. Apparently there used to be one from their kickstarter but it fell out of date and was disabled. I'd personally pay more than 25 dollars for this game knowing what I do now. Thank you devs for your hard work. Great game.

I took my sweet time enjoying this game to the fullest.Each character is unique in its own way and their own dialogues, the controls and attacks are super solid, I haven't faced a single bug in the game during my 62 hours that I put into this magnificent Gem. And boy, did Astral Ascent developers  (Hibernian) pay attention!With a This game has the nervous & frantic combat from Dead Cells, the iterative storytelling from Hades, 4 different characters with distinctive personalities and gameplay, and, most outstandingly, a   as it's the best in the genre since Isaac and the Gungeon.A colorful, fast and furious game best enjoyed with a friend. If Hades and Dead Cells are the 9/10 of the genre, this is a solid 8.5+.(+) Excellent moveset,   rife with double jumps, dashes, wall climbs and plunging attacks(+) Surprisingly  . Hats off to the devs for pulling this out successfully(+) Coming back to the garden and the bar, with its relaxing music in the background, is a welcome change of pace between 2 bouts of frenetic dashing.  (-) The  , which makes the Memory Fragment unlocking underwhelming. A lot of effort went into crafting backstories for the Zodiacs, but not much of it is compelling. Little character development in the dialogues with your characters and the zodiacs between first encounters and final runs. You'll quickly learn to click "redeem all" and ignore the text. _childDocuments_.review: This game plays like a more free flowing Dead Cells, with aerial combat and fast movement at its core. The other large inspiration seems to be Hades, as the game is heavy on story elements in and outside of its hub with an absolute ton of voice acted dialogue that evolves as the game progresses. There was a large amount of work and love put into this game, and it definitely is a "hidden gem" if I have ever seen one. I do have some complaints about the game so far, to name a few:- no real secrets during your run- music is nice but often too relaxed- King Counter feels wonky to use - seems like its the same map progression every time- also seems like you cant disable subtitles if you wishAnd the character writing doesn't always thrill me, with "cringey" dialogue from certain characters like Kiran, and an overly sappy/wholesome home base where everyone seems sweet like a puppy (maybe a positive to some), but as far as the actual gameplay goes its a blast. Lots of spells to equip and possible builds to make with some fun bosses to fight them with. I definitely recommend this game to most all roguelike fans and fans of combat platformers as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best roguelike out there at the moment, it has pretty much everything I am looking for in a game like this. Amazing art design, unique classes with different playstyles (especially after the new 1.4 patch), a fun combat system that is fast-paced and rewards players for learning all the mechanics, a very good and rewarding meta progression that carries over smoothly to the late/post-game. My only negative feedback is that it was kind of hard to get a build with systems going, but they recently fixed that in an update, making it much easier and more exciting. Speaking of updates, these devs just keep pumping out content patch after content patch. Almost every update feels like it could easily be a paid dlc. I can't recommend this game enough, and I'm suprised not more people are talking about it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really solid roguelite. Good mechanics, combat feels snappy, the characters and world is interesting and well made, and the amount of unique ways you can get through a run is massive. The different systems they have put in all work really well together, and they've continued to build on it since release in really fun ways. It's also couch co-op which is amazing and a blast to play through/All that said, I found one of my favorite parts being the story. It isn't a linear story telling, so you aren't working your way through it in the way an RPG would typically present it. Similar to hades, the story develops as you work your way through the world each run, and then has some sort of capstone moments when you get back to home base. There's also memory fragments and other bits of non-linear story telling. It seems like this leads to some people thinking its a bit on the shallow side, or hard to parse, but I really liked it since it gave the game a sort of investigation vibe where as you go through you are looking for the next little bit of a given characters backstory, or learning more about who the big bad is, etc. It all gets tied together with each playable character, and each of the 12 bosses having their own ending sequence you can look at, which often ties in the other characters as well.10/10 game, and 10/10 devs. Been no lifing this thing with my wife for a long while now and it seems like every time things get a bit stale, a patch comes out a couple weeks after to freshen things up

_childDocuments_.review: Like some mentioned; after about ten hours the cracks start to show.Primarily its the fact that almost everything is some sort of passive improvement that does not change your playstyle between runs. You got an aura focused on Meteors? ok, add meteor gambits to all your spells and watch them  oblitorate the screen. Ok, today its Spark. Tomorrow its Fire Shield. The spells themselves, 4 spell rotation, do not change anything about the way you approach the game. Its hit, hit, hit, spell, hit, hit, spell, etc. It does not matter if its pillars, knives or lightning balls flopping from the sky. They are just a damage dealer with a different animation.The low variety is one thing, but the hitboxes and telegraphing are inconsistent and hurt the overall flow of the game. One enemy show its red hitbox and you need to dodge instantly, another has a windup and now you got hit. Another does not have any telegraphing hitboxes at all for some reason. Some windups show it by increasing the red colored gradient, others do not. There is no rhyme or reason to it and this inconsistency I do not understand, and makes dodges kind of confusing. Was this a windup or an instant? And sir, why don't you have any red hitbox and just throw your massive sword out of out nowhere?Speaking of dodges and hitboxes, that is assuming you can see them, There are enough explosions and Meteors and stuff flying about that often it's barely clear what is happening. Coupled that with the fact you do not have invincibility frames, You might just lose 50% hp in a single barrage of attacks in an eclipse room, where a lot of  glowing elite enemies and explosions do not make it easier to see what is going on.Having said all of that; the game is easier than you think. Life, regeneration, and echoes (more passives) with life bonuses fly around so often that all the random damage and unclear hitboxes are quickly healed back. It just takes a run or two to figure out you need auras focusing on a single mechanic; fire shield, poison, slime, spark or whatever and align all your gambits and passives to that same mechanic and everything dies within seconds. Also at DL5, where I called it a good day, sir.

_childDocuments_.review: I was mainly looking for co-op games to play with a friend, and here are my thoughts on Astral Ascent, a well-crafted title.It’s been a while since I’ve enjoyed this type of game. The visuals are stunning, absolutely gorgeous. However, the art style tends to blend enemies and the player character due to a similar color palette. I highly recommend using line contours to make things more visible, especially in crowded areas. Later in the game, you can change the color palette to suit your preferences or to create better contrast with the background, which helps a lot with visibility.The background design is vibrant and alive, a rarity for pixel art games like this. The sun effect, in particular, is one of my favorites. Each biome looks better than the last; it’s truly eye candy. Boss animations, especially during their introductions, feel sluggish with only a few frames, but overall the game’s movement is fluid.Now, let’s talk about the controls. They added a neat feature that lets you switch between Xbox and PS4 controller interfaces on the fly—something I haven’t seen in other games. Kudos to the devs for this. However, the game feels overly complicated. There are so many mechanics that it feels like you need four hands to play. It’s like a chocolate cake with chocolate topping and chocolate filling—too much. Over time, you’ll get the hang of it, but the complexity is unnecessary and could be simplified.Co-op is fun, but there’s a major issue: when two players try to interact with upgrades or anything that brings up a description on screen, only one player can see it at a time. This slows progress considerably. Each player should have their own instance, rather than having to wait for the other. If one player gets an upgrade, it only applies to them, while the second player gets nothing.Another issue is the lack of in-game explanations. Spells have elemental affinities, but the wiki is incomplete, so it took me around 20 runs to figure things out. A small in-game encyclopedia would help a lot. Spells have small symbols indicating their element, but it’s not immediately clear. There seem to be five elements: neutral, fire, poison, ice, and electric. Making the perfect combos feels random, and upgrading spells is confusing. You often end up dropping spells just to pick them up again later, which is an awkward design choice.The enemies are challenging, and regular monsters can easily defeat you if you’re not careful. Some achievements, like completing a biome without taking damage, feel absurdly difficult. The bosses are hard, but you gradually learn their patterns. Some, however, feel overpowered—Virgo, the first boss, feels stronger than Leo, the second. This imbalance didn’t sit well with me.Another gripe: if you unlock too much in one run, such as new characters, they won’t appear until after you die. The game only shows one new addition to the base per run, which feels anticlimactic.There’s a lot of potential for quality-of-life improvements, but overall, the game is well-executed. The soundtrack is cinematic and pleasant, though it can get repetitive. Stunning art, great OST, but poor controls and co-op mechanics. Still, I’ll be playing more.After beating the game once, you haven’t truly beaten it. Not after the second, third, fourth, fifth, or even sixth time. Only after the seventh run (Destiny +6) do you unlock the "true" ending.About these "Destinies": replaying the game so many times becomes tedious. After many hours, I gave up. The final boss in Destiny +6 is chaos. There are so many projectiles flying around that it’s impossible to see your own character. With everything in a purplish palette, and red boss attacks, it’s hard to predict anything. The only build that worked for me was a combination of attack speed, healing on crits, healing on base attack, and healing on echoes. Every other build felt unreliable and too RNG-dependent.I understand the game is designed around RNG, but there should be a way to start building your character with at least an aura or spell of your choice.Finally, the most discouraging part: farming Moon Shards. You get one shard per boss, but you need around 50 shards for a single max upgrade. This means defeating 50 bosses, with each stage taking 10-15 minutes. That’s an absurd amount of time for just one upgrade. The grind is excessive and poorly designed.
