_childDocuments_.review: A very good game if you enjoyed dead cells or just die already (both also amazing games), what keeps this game interesting is that even after defeating the final boss you don't actually win. It sounds maybe crazy but I like that because Hades did the same style where you have to complete the game multiple times to get the actual ending and not to mention after clearing the game the first time the enemy attack patterns and boss patterns change, not to mention other positives and negatives and of course this can be switched of at anytime if you wanna play vanilla. I highly recommend this game. animations 10/10 (stunning)Music is an absolute 9/10 (Mystical kinda like hollow knight)story 8/10 (the fact that other constellations has backstory and lore with each other is interesting)combat 10/10 (combat is a nostalgic feeling to a mix of dead cells and Hades)
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to like this game, and love several of its contemporaries in the genre, but it falls very flat.Compared to Dead Cells or Skul, this has few things going for it. Wonderful art being the main one. Voiceacting is solid, character design is delightful.Gameplay is really, really lacking though. Balance is atrocious and severely limits any meaningful choices. A central tenet of this game seems to be giving you worthless filler upgrades, while simultaneously creating 'locks' that you need to spend points to upgrade just to keep your  path open to future upgrades. What this means is that I'm weighing either optimizing my build -- to get stat upgrades, to go for keys only and 1 cost mana spells -- versus the *opportunity* to get cool flashy stuff. And usually the cool flashy stuff is lackluster or actually worse than the starter spells. So what that means is that if I go for the risk of hoping for a flashier build, that build usually is destined to die. It reinforces playing just at the core loop of 'choose the key room, dodge a bunch, hit square and triangle a bunch to cycle through your starter spells and use whatever crap upgrades the game throws at you til you win based on dodging and DPS'. Besides that, the world and terrains are very empty and uninspired compared to contemporaries. Possible when this comes out of early access it'll be better but so far the design choices feel pretty baked into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: roughly 80-100 hours, both co-op and solo (mostly co-op)This game is wonderful and super fun so I'm leaving a review to try and bump their visibility before full release early next month. AA is an action roguelike with beautiful pixel art and music, fun characters and really unique bosses. All based around the zodiac signs. Runs are nice and diverse with daily timer mixed power-ups, tons of buffs, spells, ect. to unlock.They are super active in their discord and the community is real sweet. If you're looking for a fun arcadey, high fantasy style action rogue-like with super solid co-op, this one deserves your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is what I look for in a good roguelite, love it.- Multiple character with different skills and upgrade paths- Each character in interacted with differently, each boss will introduce themselves to each new character in a nice touch- The town you go back to is fun, alive, and easy to navigate- There's variety: Multiple skills, each skill can be modded up to 4 times during that run, utility skills, and 2 passive charms- Has nice next level selection, you see difficulty, rewards, and type of room.- Fun little extra rooms with everything from free stuff to extra mini bosses- Feels smooth and fun to play- Art is great and on point
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Beautiful visuals.Almost all dialogue is voice acted, usually pretty well done (perhaps even all of it, havent finished the game yet).Combat feels good. scratches my itch for a good 2D Action Platfromer, and the animations make everything look cool.Tons of different things to do in the hub world, ways to customize your runs and more.Quality of life stuff.Great soundtrack done by Dale North, who also did the soundtrack for "wizard of legend".Big variety of bosses which all have unique attack patterns and such. As i said before, i havent reached the final boss yet let alone beat him, but I am sure difficultly is going to be interesting as there is a decent skill ceiling.Game is quite cheap, i got in on sale for 15 dollars, after all it is an indie game.Cons:Roguelite elements, as in run custimization and build variety. the permanent upgrade system is fine, giving you basic stat boosts as well as bonus resources, aura slots and more. what i found to be a bit underwhelming is the build variety and potential. The game has different elemental types, and there are quite a bit of things you can synergize with the element you chose, like your spells, auras, prowesses, gambits and more, so it is already on par with something like dead cells, but if you are looking for a complex, or at least very exciting and interesting build potential you may found it a bit underwheming. I have to say, although I like and enjoy build complexity and variety, the absence of it in this game was not very present, as they nailed pretty much everything else i was looking for in this game.All and all, if you have seen the gameplay and it intrerests you, i recommend giving this game a try.If there is any aspect i forgot to mention and you would like to know about please mention it in the comments (As i progress in the game i will be able to talk about the story as well, so far there is not much.)
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Played like 20hrs on a pirated version of the game. Made  me want to buy it. And I dont buy games often, much less in early access.SFX, art, music, gameplay. enemy difficulty, replayability. Its all outstanding.Hope they get to really flesh out the lore of the game because its so interesting and unique.Grateful for the devs for making a great game and improving it so much and so quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying this game a lot.  It's a platform beat 'em up with bosses and roguelite progression.  Unlike Dead Cells it's fun and full of character, and the movement feels fluid.  Characters are boisterous and the game encourages you to keep trying in many good-natured ways.  The best things about the game are the graphics and the characters you come across.  Playing with controller very much recommended.  Big thumbs up over here!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game has become my go to for short gaming sessions. It is easy to pick up and do a run (or three) when I am looking for a way to pass the time. The amount of effort put into creating spells and builds has really paid off. The developers have made the game extremely replayable and rewarding for doing so. The meta-progression is parallel to a run modifier system that makes sure your overpowered builds are still challenged by cool variations including the basics like increased enemy health and damaged, but also more complex things like unique enemy movesets and rare enemy types! I have almost 100 hours as of this writing, and I fully intend on doubling that after full release. Easily a top recommendation to lovers of the rogue genre.Oh, the visuals and the score are amazing. While not at the forefront, the overarching story and character interactions are more than set-dressing for the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I debated whether to wait 3 weeks for the Winter Steam Sale or not to buy it. Eventually I caved in and bought it full price. I don't regret it at all. If you enjoyed games like Hades and Dead Cells, this has a very similar vibe to it. The bosses are also really fun to fight, it doesn't feel as if you're just mashing through a hp sponge since you actively have to respond to their attacks.I can say much more but I think it'd be best to play it for yourself and see how great it is!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super pretty game with amazing movement and simple but impactful power system. It has may different ways to build your character. The boss fights are also challenging and rewarding, you can really tell when your getting better at the game and i just found myself really loving the game as i played it. One of my favourite features about the game is the remote play, i love playing this game with my friends. : )
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: A platformer fighter roguelike with smooth gameplay and flashy animations. The game is gorgeous and you can scale your build to explosive heights with a very fiddly build crafting system. It reminds me quite a bit of Hades in its pacing, storytelling, and roguelike mechanics. There seems to be no end to the meta progression systems, which can be a plus or a minus depending on your perspective. Co op is only local, which is a bummer. All-in-all I really like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelites currently on the market, especially for co-op. No two runs are quite the same, since there are many different vectors of power to make your character stronger. Room choices feel meaningful, while still maintaining good moment to moment gameplay.There are many different kinds of power fantasies offered, and it's incredibly satisfying seeing your build scale to screen-filled madness in 100 different ways, from barraging your enemy with hundreds of missiles per second to burning them to death through fire explosions. The RNG to get enough synergies to bring your unique build to life is also fairly forgiving, allowing you numerous re-rolls to get what you want but not making it too easy.I've only really mastered two characters (one of them being DLC) in my 230 hours played so far, so this shows you the depth that this game has to offer. This game only really opens up once you unlock all the roguelite unlocks (and beat the game at least once, unlocking the postgame progression), so most of the rewarding gameplay comes from both knowledge and skill. Highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Bright, beautiful pixel-art fantasy roguelite with elemental, magical, and (very light) astrology references. Playing this game co-op and it's a LOT of fun! Just got to unlocking the Destiny runs after about 11 hours of gameplay (maybe 6 or so runs).Highlights+ Art - Beautiful character designs; very cool, fluid animations; distinct backgrounds and NPCs; cute summons (YALEES!!!) + Music - Whether it's epic combat or a place of calm, the music fits the vibe well+ Straightforward gameplay - It's a lot of button mashing since the screen gets to be kind of a mess after all the abilities you pick up,  but as long as you can move, jump, dash, and spam your attacks/spells you're good. Glad there aren't a lot of hyperspecific combos to memorize. Just keep moving and attacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Unique combat style with spells and elements. Amazing visuals for a pixelated game and an even more amazing soundtrack. Been playing since before the Telluric Telescope update but after the 1.0 release, decided to leave a review because I needed to say that the final boss fight gave me such an enjoyable thrill. Even the other zodiacs are interesting and unique to fight. Great game and probably my rouge-lite of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Game is excellent, the artwork and animations are beautiful. The zodiacs are HAWT and enjoyable to fight. I love the difficulty increase system and the perk unlocking system, it makes the game very rewarding to play. The character voice acting is awesome and the story of each character is interesting. Most of the music slaps to the highest degree. Build diversity is sort of low but I've never had a similar run yet, the controls are a bit of a learning curve but once mastered they flow perfectly. Best played with a controllerEdit: After a few updates the build diversity has gotten MUCH better and I LOVE all the new weapons (each character has 3 weapons and each weapon has 3 passives you unlock as you play). This game has given me a hyper focus and feels EXTREMELY rewarding to play. This game has so much replay-ability... You can also make the game super difficult after beating Destiny 6 and I enjoy the challenge. 10/10 recommend if you like build focused rogue-likes I've been playing since EA and this game has come a long way, the Devs put so much love and care into this game it has evolved into a beautiful narrative that has an addictive gameplay loop. Looking at the upcoming updates (with the telescope) it looks like they are adding yet ANOTHER mechanic that will make the game fun to play all over again (adds some risk/reward aspects like chaos in hades 1 and 2). This is one of those games where it isnt hard to 100%. All you have to do is play and the achievements will naturally unlock, no minmaxing needed to fully complete, just play and find some fun builds (my personal favorite is ice fragment -- just covering the screen in dmg is so insane)This game is worth to buy even at full price -- plenty of content and the devs update/hotfix very often. If you are on the fence, please... just get this game <3
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: It's the most beautiful pixel art game I've ever seen and it is my favorite rouge-like game ever. Honestly, I would give the Dev's 25 dollars without getting the game, I've been on their discord and I've seen how much they care about the game and the people that play it. Give it a go, I think you'll like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game when It was on Early Access, waaaaay back in time and oh boy, we came a long way didn't we? With every update Astral Ascent became more and more fun, the devs actually took their time to listen to their community and implement suggestions. We got solid updates that changed the game for the better, every single time! This game have a lot of challenges, content and lore to explore, It truly can be played infinitely.After 70h (- afk time), 94 escape attempts between early access/full release and a lot of sweat I think I got my money's worth out of it. Here's a  if you want to take a look, also here's the  that helped me conquer last floor.Unfortunately, this game have a lot of patronizing dialogs, pretentious and out of place backstories etc. They gone too deep with progressivism with this game, it came to a point where I stopped reading the dialogue altogether and just mindlessly tried to beat the game. Astral Ascent has a lot of unnecessary gender ambiguity/female empowerment dialogue, none of which is handled with moderation or feels organic. Telling the player a character did this or that is not enough to make a good backstory, even less if looks forced or unrealistic. The sense of grandiosity the Npcs try to convey about each other and the main characters is so bleak, you just can't picture none of it happening, even so when they start yapping about it trying to steal an awe out of you.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Worth buying only if you can ignore the dialogues and just go with the flow in the runs, the gameplay is not bad. The ending is what kills the mood to play again and see others characters ending ( ). The NPCs in the garden doesn't even acknowledge that you "killed" the bad guy, it's so lackluster man >:(
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: super solid game, really enjoyable combat with varied builds between characters/runs, the writing is enjoyable and interesting, the setting seems to be taking a lot of cues from Hades (bosses are not strictly antagonistic and some of them can even be recruited as summons in your runs, overarching story that explains both what you're trying to achieve and also how you keep repeating runs) but puts its own spin on it, and the updates have been very solid and have added some great QoL and lots of avenues for run variance and build variety.Incredibly worth your time even in early access, and full release comes next month so if it looks up your alley now is a perfect time to grab it before a full release price increase
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Undoubtedly, one of the best 2D roguelites I've played. As of writing this, I have about 50% of the achievements from the in-game npc. The amount of build potential is insane, and the game just keeps getting better as the difficulty increases with more features and options opening up. The lore is there for people who enjoy it, and the character design is fantastic. Each character has unique playstyles, and as I keep playing I find myself more and more engrossed in how to make the options I was given take me to the end. The combat is fluid and fast-paced, and by the end stages of a run, genuinely looks and feels like an insane fight you would see in anime. I haven't tried it, but there is also (couch) coop, which is a plus. You can even duel each other at the end of every map. I don't usually leave reviews, but honestly, this game deserves it. Great job, devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of magical wonder and fantasy to it, from the art to the beautiful music and the map. I love it. I really wish my clicks would do more in the UI when it comes to selecting things like empty slots to equip spells and so on. Overall the combat makes sense for a rogue like and the dialogue evolves as you go. Overall a solid game so far can't wait to see whats coming.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: If Hades contended for game of the year, this should contend for game of the decade. Simply put, just a better roguelite in every sense. Far more interesting combos, an insane amount of skills that can create chains you've barely dreamed of, incredible art style with a soundtrack that rivals even the biggest titles. If you're into roguelites, you owe it to yourself to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent is amazing. Its raw 2D rogue-like gamestyle is phenomenal. Here is the problem for a few of us: To get 100% of the steam achievements in the game, its not based on skill really (only a few are), its based on time. Time of grinding and grinding. Sometimes you can play for entire day but only make 1% progress towards an achievement unless you go out of your way to farm it. I'm gonna give it a thumbs down, but if they change the steam achievements to be more balanced instead of "unlock 100% of _____" then i will change my review to an upvote instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Editing after being 90 hours in, having got all the achievements. I absolutely adore this game. It's easily S tier, right alongside Hades. This game rulesThis game kicks ass. An excellent roguelike, in the same vein as Dead Cells. Tons of polish, lots of systems, charming characters and an interesting story. Special shoutout to the art style and the intro cinematics, they're gorgeous. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Watch out, looks like someone dropped their Hades all over my dead cells.. they also bumped into a Yale while awkwardly rushing out and spilled unique lore out the wazoo. This is a beautiful mess that I look forward to cleaning up for the coming weeks and a definite labor of love. the rnd, visuals, mechanics and flow are all a major chef's kiss. Worth every penny
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy games like Hades, you'll probably enjoy this one! It is a bit simpler, though. Regardless, I know I'm having fun with it. I LOOOOVE all the astrology/constellation themes of this game. All the characters are cool, and there are so many ways to play/things to unlock on your runs. You'll get a lot of hours out of this game, and it seems like they are still updating things too! Definitely a recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of substantial content for an early access. Good variety of spells and add ons for build variety. Each character has good personality. The pixel art is just incredible. One of the best looking indie games in my opinion. Developer stays dialled into the community and takes their suggestions for balancing. Great roguelike.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic mashup of a Hades hub world and character interactions with Dead Cells-ish combat.  I played Early Access up to the update prior to Telluric Telescope, and had to force myself to put it down so I could save some content for the official release.The Zodiacs are akin to the gods in Hades in that each run has some character or lore flavor to add between them and your player character.  I thought all the voice acting was decent and really gave the characters and world some depth.Combat has tight controls and the focus on the 4 rotating skills allow for a lot of variety to runs if you're looking for that.  I wish the sound mixing had some more impact on normal attacks but skills are popping off so often you don't notice after a while.Music is top notch and by the same person that did Dreamscaper (I think).  Each track really blends in with its stage and helps pull everything together to give the world and exploring it a great feel.I've put all my hours in on the Steam Deck and it runs like a dream.  Art style and animations are on point, and I never had a performance drop even in late game with all that chaos on screen.Can't recommend this one enough if you enjoy the world building of Hades with platform combat.  Underrated/overlooked as far as I'm concerned and really looking forward to the full release.  I hope it gets some more visibility and traction then because this game is a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best and one of the more underrated rougelite games out there. I found this one a while ago, but from other people gameplays I saw, I thought it'd be way too chaotic to play. And now I know I was too quick to judge.At first, I thought that having to use spells and the room-based areas where you choose where to go, would get boring pretty fast. Heck, I was wrong.Every area feels nice and is actually very rewarding when you perform well. Gaining spell stones, leveling up spells and gambit affixes can heavily affect your run, as well as your auras (passive skills) and Echos.The option to ramp up the difficulty is super fun to keep you on your toes, plus you can tweak the difficulty yourself.I really enjoy the game, so far I completed D10 and plan to continue ramping it up.Each of the 4 (base game) playable characters feels nice to play, too.WHAT I LIKE:+ Nice use of every game mechanic, it's connected very well, including the meta progression.+ Bosses - Love every one of their design and attack patterns, the individuality of each one of the bosses is nice, too.+ The dialogues are fine, not too long, which I really like, there's some jokes here and there, too.+ Graphics and animated cutscenes?? HOLY! - I wasn't a fan of pixelized artstyle until 4 months ago and now I see a specific charm in it (Thanks, Dead Cells!), I also feels like that kind of art style goes well with this genre of games.WHAT MAKES ME A BIT DISAPPOINTED:- Lack of worlds, there's only 4 of them so far (not counting Event Horizon), so after some playthroughs, it might feel repetitive- Exploration areas feel too easy, a few more obstacles wouldn't hurt.I'll give this one 9 / 10. It's a must-play, in my opinion. Especially if you're diving into roguelites and better if you like a bit of platforming, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Wow just wow. This game is such a breather from the recent drought of games. The visuals in this game are just breathtaking and the animations are exquisite. The game play is easy to understand and get the hang of for all the new players. There is so much diversity in all of the abilities and skills you can acquire and unlock throughout your journey in this game. The amount of mixing and matching you can do with the gambits and spells makes the game feel new every single attempt to escape. I love that each character and NPC have there own little story and dialogue, it gives each character there own significance and personality. Though the only negative I have to say, at the time of writing this review, is that the damage scaling for the basic attacks is a bit low. It almost makes you feel as though that skills are the only source of damage, making the basic attack just a mana replenisher. Other than that, to wrap it all up, the game is amazing and the full version isn't even out yet. I highly recommend this game to people who like rogue-like games. I'm very excited to see the future of this game
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: No cap, this is an easy top 5 roguelites in the past year. Considering the saturation in the market, thats  impressive. Especially since I have a Steam Deck, I see myself having Astral Ascent in rotation for the rest of the time with the other big boys like hades, enter the gungeon, etc. The 25 dollar price tag was the only thing holding me back from that first purchase, but after seeing what it was like even in Early Access, I would have dropped a full $50 on this puppy without blinking.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: In gameplay Astral Ascent is a roguelite blend of the best parts of Hades and Dead Cells. Taken in a vacuum that should be enough to justify the asking price but there's so much more to enjoy here. I can't say enough about the music and pixel art. The vistas and strings juxtaposed against the idea that the game setting takes place entirely in a prison is a masterclass in storytelling by showing rather than exposition. If are a fan of video games as an art form do check out Astral Ascent when you have the time. Without rushing, the runs only take about 1.5hrs once you get the hang of the game flow. There's lots of lore to read which is drip fed and can be ignored if reading isn't your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of the best Action Roguelikes i've played in a long time, my hours don't show it but me and my buddy would co op this game on his ♥♥♥♥♥♥ pc at 15fps (on his account) for hours on end, had so much fun, I ended up buying it myself I can't recommend this game enough! Every time I feel like it's getting stale they add some insane cool stuff that makes me wanna go at it again. straight up good buy you won't be dissapointed.I keep hoping for games like this to scratch the same itch but so far i've been unsuccessful. so fun with a friend 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Got this from humble choice.There is almost no aspect of this game that does not annoy the hell out of me.There is a difference between Complex and Complicated. Hades and Dead Cells, which this is compared to, are complex games but not complicated. Seconds to learn, hours to master. Astral Ascent is not complex. It's complicated. After 40 minutes play I'm still pausing at every point to read the tool tips to check which button I am supposed to press. In Hades or Dead Cells, correct buttons are muscle memory within seconds. I haven't played either game in a year but I could pick either of them up right now and instinctively know the control layout without checking. Astral Ascent feels like it would take me a year to learn the control layout.As mentioned in other reviews, the floatiness removes any kind of rhythm or flow to combat. You hit something in the air, expecting to fall to earth to carry on your combo against ground enemies. Then you're just stuck in mid air, throwing useless attacks against nothing, while the ground enemy attacks up and kills you. The graphics are pretty but crowded and counterproductive. As soon as you get more than a few enemies on screen, everything starts to blend into the background meaning you start getting hit by attacks you should have seen coming, but didn't. Compare again with Hades and Dead Cells where beautiful backgrounds are created with muted colours allowing the enemies and attack patterns to show up in bright, high contrast colours. Still tough, but never unfair like it feels here.As a consequence, the times I died, I didn't feel that I was dying because of my mistakes that I could learn from and correct or overcome through getting stronger in the metaprogression. I died because I was wrestling with the game graphics, mechanics and controls and no amount of anything was going to correct those.Having completed both Hades and Dead Cells, this should have been a game I loved. I wish it was but I don't see myself touching it ever again.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like the build combos run progression of hades mixed with combat more like crisp bullet hell dead cells. The pixel art is gorgeous and crisp, the sound design is incredible, and while the game gets in my opinion pretty damn hard at the higher difficulties, it never feels unfair. The individual characters also play very differently from each other with their own spell lists, and (I think almost) every spell can spawn with any sort of element on it, so the types of builds you can make are changing every single game. This last update changed the aura system to actually cater to builds, seeing as there's 250 options, most with 3 levels of power and some that are "astral"with much more powerful effects. It also adds more feeling of progression to every individual run. This is just the tip of the game, as it also has voice acting, full lore unlocked through memories you find in runs, challenge+parkour rooms, and much more. Now this isn't to say the game is perfect yet by any means, but as they still have this full year ahead of them with more updates, I think this game will become a staple in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this compared to Hades. Just no. The core combat is not great and enemies are not fun to fight. It's not snappy or punchy, and there is very little feedback to the player when attacking enemies. The jumping is also floaty which you do a lot of. If you're looking for snappy and responsive combat just stop here because you'll be disappointed. Another downside is that the four spells you have rotate/cycle. If you find a cool spell during your run, you'll have to slot it in and wait for it to come up in rotation. All this does is make combat needlessly cumbersome. This is such a bizarre design decision for an action focused game. I was baffled while playing trying to figure out why this mechanic even exists. To top it off, the UI is annoying.If you're looking for tight, rewarding gameplay and combat then this probably will not satisfy you.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Roguelikes on Steam. Deep Spell-Customization System, with Auras, one signature spell for each Hero which can all be customized and leveled up. Lots of Meta-Progression upgrades. Also Risk & Reward Decisions are to make during every run.  Gameplay is very fluent with nice animated pixel-graphics. Everything is voiced, every Boss has it's own intro and something to say. All the spells/gambits/auras can be overwhelming at start, but after 2-3h in, it gets better and better. If you like Roguelikes, this is definately worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Wide variety of builds with lots of beautifully animated spells, dynamic boss fights and an accessible learning curve, although the game becomes challenging at a certain point, it also offers the necessary buffs to keep it fun.While the story is interesting, I don't think many players really paid attention to the dialogue, it's more of a mind-numbing hack and slash. Waiting for the update...I liked it so much I got it platinum!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Look, the game is good but it doesn't feel unique, the pixel art is great and it does have some unique elements but it just was not meant for me. It also does this thing where they take liberties with the races of the real world deities used in the game, I'm more of a true to source material kind of guy so there's that, but i don't want to get knit-picky.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: That's a really good game with an amazing fluidity in gameplay and amazing art style/animation. You're a really talented developer with a lot of passion, that's for sure.--I have 2 main issues with the game that separates a good title from a possibly great one:-The amount of visual effects during the fight and the current HUD makes it impossible to read any information, while in action. Some combat depth will not be possible to achieve with this issue.-There are plenty of spells and upgrades that looks awesome, but during these 11 hours that I had, I felt like I've experienced only 1 common playstyle on all of the characters with all these different builds. In the end the spells and the gambits didn't really matter that much, because I never felt like I'm allowed to approach the game from a different angle. In all these runs I was just smashing buttons like a madman, while being focused mostly on dodging.These issues (especially the 2nd one as its essential) are the main reason why the game can become boring quite fast, even if there's plenty of content that can still be unlocked. Randomly pressing buttons feels fun at first, but if the game is not difficult, and lack of depth in combat makes the loop identical, it falls short and can't use even half of the potential that it has.Btw I've also recognized that everything feels so similar not only in gameplay, but also in numbers. All of my successful runs had almost identical damage done and that is also concerning. Without a possibility to make broken builds its not as fun as it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: sports a gorgeous pixelated look, but to me the real specialty this game has is in its mechanics.Between a large pool of Spells, four playable characters with their own specialties, and attachable Gambits for those spells alongside Auras that synergize with them, there is a frankly incredible amount of build variety that makes each run feel fresh and engaging.Helping matters, of course, is the fact that every boss is manageable with practice. No run feels truly impossible to clear with in this game, and I have enjoyed that the entirety of Early Access.If you enjoyed Hades's story structure, this game's going to ring a few bells in how it handles lore and downtime between runs. But beneath the storytelling is a  different mechanic set that lends a rather different feel to it--enough to stand on its own merits, I'd say.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun 2d action roguelike.  It is similar to Hades in terms of progression, where you get a lot of upgrades and unlocks that open up as you progress through the game, as well as unlocking new characters as you reach higher levels.  Each character has their own set of unique moves, and spells that you can equip them with have upgrade slots that you can load with different effects (for example having a status effect trigger whenever the spell hits an enemy or when it is cast).  Spells have lots of different animations and the effects you can attach to them are really varied, everything from summons to firing missiles or flying swords.  The art, music and voice acting are all good, there is a story although it's mostly told through short cut scenes when encounter a boss in game as well as through lore you can pick up as collectibles.  I'm usually not into 2d action/platforming games but this one really sucked me in and I've completed the main story portion in 34 hours, but there is a ton more customized difficulty levels above that if you want to keep playing.  Definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - A fast, frenetic action rougelike in the mold of Hades that’s almost immediately broken. With heart, wit and explosively creative build potential, even if the art and writing doesn’t charm you, the gameplay will floor you.Long read - If you’re a rouge lite/like fiend Astral Ascent needs your attention. Through precise, interlocking mechanics and punchy combat that regularly moves between bounding chaos and focused duels, I’ve found myself enchanted by Astral Ascent. While the gameplay is the inarguable draw, the writing is sharp. Honing in on themes of duty, guilt and community built on mutual or like-goals, the breath of depth of the characters caught me off guard. Hades is still the high water mark for story in these sorts of action rouglikes but Astral Ascent is not far behind. The voice acting and direction carry most of the weight in bringing this sense to life. Along with a poppy, dreamlike color palette and beautifully loose animation on pixel art that can only be described as painstaking, Astral Ascent continues to surprise me at every turn. Like the transcendent beings you fight as part of the game’s name sake, Astral Ascent deserves a place on many a pedestal.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, would have bought again even if it wasn't on sale. I've played tons of roguelikes/lites: Skul the hero slayer, Hades, Hades II, 20 minutes till dawn, against great darkness, boneraiser minions, downwell, death must die, and the list goes on. Despite the high expectations I'd rank this game a solid -A tier game, just below "Dead cells".The visuals might seem weird at first but from what iv seen they keep the visuals to a minimalist style while making the combat and mechanics as interesting and engaging as possible. In fact I remember seeing a tutorial on how to make character visuals similar to the style in this game. I don't want to compare this game to dead cells too much, but it makes it a lot easier to judge this game. Dead cells is a very ground-based game. You don't want to go in the air too often, and you learn patterns of enemies and take them on one by one, trying to clear rooms as fast as possible before they get chaotic or (spoilers!)  Astral ascent is the opposite, the rooms are BY DEFAULT very chaotic, and you are challenged with your knowledge of enemy attack patterns when multitudes of different enemies are on your screen attacking you at the same time. More importantly. Astral ascent HEAVILY prioritizes aerial combat, and being able to orient yourself while in the air. Its like "scourge bringer" if scourge bringer was a good game (half joking).I couldn't tell you how many times I lost trying to beat my first dead cells run. Somewhere from 15-20. I beat my first run of astral ascent in 3 runs. There is a difference between "challenging" and "punishing", where challenging is the task you are given (dodging attacks), and punishing is your penalty for failing the challenges (taking damage or dying). And while the game hasn't been very punishing in the first 6 hours, I can certainly say that I can feel that the game is challenging, and I hope that as I progress the game will be more punishing and I will be expected to have a higher level of skill to win.On a side note, if you're reading this odds are you're a part of the roguelike/lite community too! I wasn't expecting to find myself here, but after laughing at the references to other roguelikes in games like this, I realized I was definitly a part of this community whether I liked it or not. If you want to classics as good or better than this game i'd highly recommend hades or dead cells too.

_childDocuments_.review: You know, the cynic in me is forced to wonder if the naming of Astral Ascent had anything to do with aiming for the top of alphabetised listings. I know that isn’t a particularly interesting observation, but to be fair, it isn’t a particularly interesting game.The visuals are nice, colourful, bright, all those good words. Problem is that everything is a bit flat. Nothing really pops out and it wasn’t uncommon for me to lose my character on screen which is always a sign that someone f*cked up.Not gonna lie, the writing is also super forgettable. I know it isn’t exactly fair for me to complain about writing when my default is to skip it anyway, but I do feel like maybe some people care? Citation needed. Mind you, I was a lot less sh*tty about the writing after I turned the voices off in the menu and was spared from the constant “I’m out of mana” and other random lines the characters throw in.Now I know that in theory, those voice lines wouldn’t have annoyed me so much if I wasn’t constantly mashing the spell button even when I was out of mana, but that does ever so nicely bring me to my other complaints:This game expects you to keep track of up to 5 different spells, each with an average of three distinct upgrades and different mana costs. These spells cycle through with use rather than when you want to switch them out. You also have multiple character upgrades as well as a signature spell, up to four upgrades on your signature spell and four on your basic attack. This is on top of two types of currency, and character stat upgrades and individual spell level ups.Think that’s a bit much to keep track of? How about this: instead of just ice, poison, electric, and fire effects, Astral Ascent needs to be special by subdividing each of those elemental damages into their own set of effects leading to situations where a stack of one kind of electric makes an enemy take bonus damage from certain weapon upgrades and another stacks up to ten before adding one of a different kind of electric stack.This. Is. Too. Complicated.There is no f*cking reason for this bullsh*t, if you’ll forgive the dense academic jargon.So why have I sunk so many hours into it? Why is this review positive? Because they’re doing something that is surprisingly hard to find which is decent co-op gameplay, and I like to play games with my partner. Don’t get me wrong, half the time we play this game, we’re b*tching about the mechanics, but there is just enough fun here to recommend playing with someone.I will say that the fact only one spell description can be on screen at a time makes the co-op experience frustrating as hell sometimes, but overall, I’ve had about as much fun with Astral Ascent as I think it’s possible to have. For real tho, if you’re looking for a solo experience, play literally anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up, despite my many criticisms. I mean, many. Because when you start looking this game as it actually is and not what it *INTENDED* to be, this quite a solid and fun game, actually. And here my review starts:The biggest flaw with Astral Ascent is that it tries so hard to be Hades, so hard, but it fails so miserably because Hades is better at everything. Period.As with Hades, you're trying to escape somewhere, you have a hub world with many characters, dozens if not hundreds of upgrades to unlock, story that unlocks itself little by little, you have to beat the game multiple times to see the real ending, full voice acting, fast paced, action packed game and so on.The issues are:- The writing is bad. Not horrible, but bad. Cringe, most of the time. Very cringe.Characters are one dimensional (both main characters and NPCs);- The shallow writing reflects directly on the voice acting. While the actors aren't bad, the voice directing hasn't been very good, to say the least.For example, you have the fiery, hot headed, expansive hero (there are four heroes); all of his lines are spoken like he has to be excited and extrovert every single line. There's no nuance whatsoever.All the characters' lines stay stuck to their "personality" which makes for a very bland voice acting.- Gameplay wise, this game does play a bit different than Hades. For starters, it's a platformer, so you can jump.Each character has a basic attack and a unique special (called "signature move"). Then you can equip up to four spells and each spell has four slots for extra power/effects. Also each spell can be upgraded for higher damage.The gimmick part is that the spells rotate each time you use one.Most Negative Reviewers dislike this mechanic, but I don't mind it at all. It's gimmicky, but not game breaking by any means.Oh yeah, you also have "auras" that give you passive effects for the run.And you can get upgrades for your basic attack and signature move. Then here's a double edged knife: while some people may enjoy the amount of customization, others can find it unnecessary over the top. I wouldn't call it overwhelming, but Hades has proved that you can keep it faster, cleaner and better. - The boss battles are... OK. Depending on your RNG, they can be easy or almost impossible. (not impossible, but they'll take so damn long that you will give it up). The issue is: your main attack does very little damage. It's purpose is to fill the mana bar so you can deal real damage with your spells. However, some spells are slower/have shorter range and on later difficulties the window to hit the boss is really small. Some bosses are notoriously harder than others, because they keep moving way more frequently making them harder to hit. Well, I could go on and on with this list. Again, especially if you compare it to Hades. But once you stop seeing the game for what it is, stop reading the atrocious dialogs, turn off the sound (so you don't have to hear the bad voice acting) and truly getting into the game's gimmicky mechanics, it IS a fun game. Controls ARE good and responsive, which is a must with this kind of game. You can feel that you start "gitting gud" also. Of course, unlocking perma upgrades help, but it's a game that you, the gamer, improves as well. I probably won't 100% this game, unlock all the endings and such, but it's still a nice one. Just wish that with the amount of effort and money that it's been put on it, it would be more it's own thing and not a Hades (derpy) clone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game nails the formula for what makes build varieties fun in an action roguelike: DISTINCT. BIG. BROKEN.I love the aura system where you can get these chain reactions of slimes creating poison chains or lightning orbs creating spirit swords. I also like that there are Astral auras that add visual changes in addition to effects such as lava slime turning slimes orange. It keeps me invested because I want to see every combination.Besides that I think this game is not brutally hard so anyone who is new-ish to the roguelike genre should be able to manage well. The only downside for me is the spells system. For example, if I wanted a build where I am rapidly applying burn stacks per spell hit, I am just looking for the spell with the most hits. Or, if I have a crit build I want a spell with a single hit. There are a lot of spells that force your character into movements that could hurt you and I found myself avoiding those because the spells go in a fixed order. Now I know there is a button to skip the spell but I never found a need to be strategic about it and I played until DL 20.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game with gorgeous spritework, buttery-smooth combat and progression, and overall excellent, addictive gameplay! The customizability of the characters and builds is immense, and the way fighting enemies and platforming feels is wonderful. I love the concept of the Zodiacs and how varied each of the bosses are- it's exciting to get to meet each one and learn their patterns and moves. The sense of decisionmaking is strong and you have a lot of control over how your runs unfold even with the randomness.  The character designs, from the main cast to the 12 Zodiac bosses, are excellent and all super cool and full of personality. There's a surprising variation of rooms, items, enemies, and secret encounters to discover, and the devs plan on adding more which is beautiful. I love seeing developers who care about their game.My only issue, which I would unfortunately say is a relatively big one, is the writing. It's less the actual  of the writing; it's fundamentally not bad at all! I love how much there is to learn about both the main cast and the various NPCs, and you get some occasionally fun interactions and learn some pretty cool lore. I think a lot of my issue comes down more to the translation or localization. Much of the dialogue has a somewhat stilted, awkward feel to it, and coupled with the various typos and grammatical errors in the game's text, I'm lead to believe that English isn't the developers' first language. There's a lot of parts where the on-screen text doesn't match the actual voiceovers either, which I'm assuming is where the voice actors clean up the sloppier wording of the script through their deliver. I understand how errors are likely with this in mind, but it is nonetheless worth mentioning. The core ideas of the script are perfectly fine, but it just feels like much dialogue and text needed a second pass or a proofread from someone to touch it up and make it feel more natural. The game has just as much of an emphasis on dialogue as Hades, which is why this is so noticeable; characters just as often have (fully-voiced!) things to say, so it's a shame the actual writing doesn't reach the same level of organicness and polish. I find otherwise great ideas for lore and interactions are hampered greatly by the text feeling sort of... clunky, for lack of a better word, which bleeds into the (otherwise stellar!) voice cast at times being made to saying things that don't totally sound like a person would ever say them.Another thing I notice is conversations sometimes feel like they end too early; your character may say something, then an NPC will say something in response, then you'd think your character would have something else to say to that (sort of like, again, Hades having Zagreus have a final comment just as you walk away from the person he's conversing with), but it just.. ends. I feel bad to tear up this part of the package because it's clear there's a lot of genuine love in it, and I myself even find it really charming and loved learning about the various Zodiacs and the circumstances behind the cast of four, from the hard-working Ayla to the showboating Kiran, but considering how unbelievably solid the rest of the package is, I'm left to single out basically the only thing I think is worth calling attention to in a negative way.Otherwise do check it out if you love solid beat em ups with great customization and flashy battles, and the elements found in games like Hades appeal to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent is yet another of literally thousands of 2D retro platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  It's a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's also been put on Steam as a bit of an afterthought, as it's very much designed for the handheld/console gaming audience.  And there's so many problems with this, it was hard to decide where to begin. First I guess this is just a terrible idea for a game, but I can't really comment much on what Nintendo Switch gamers like and what they don't... the Switch is a handheld console designed for children, and we're here on Steam for PC games.  But so many things that game developers should never do have been done here on this sloppy Nintendo Switch port, so let's get into it.  It's a basic 2D retro pixel platformer, one of thousands, only worse.  It's contentless, as all you do is continue to grind through procedurally generated, soulless levels, with clunky Nintendo Switch "combat", wonky controls... this is just a train wreck.  I suspect the only reason people liked this was it had an anime type animation at the start, or something.  It's a mystery. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.To make matters worse, while lazy, low quality pixel "art" has been used, making the game look bad, many elements of the game aren't done with pixelcrap... which accomplishes a couple of things.  First, it shows the developers perhaps could have done better and they knew it, so that's a major screwup.Secondly, it destroys any hopes the developer had of creating a "retro aesthetic" as their excuse for the lazy pixelart compromise... It looks completely inauthentic from a retro gaming perspective.  Visually, this is a hamfisted mess, a dogs breakfast of bad visuals, and this kind of laziness and poor quality should never be foisted on gamers.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.PC gamers will be insulted by the demand from the developer that a console peasant children's toy controller should be used, despite this being on PC.  Developers should try to be aware which platform they're developing for, and must never, under any circumstances dictate to gamers how their games are to be experienced.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only  players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Astral Ascent, a "D minus" Nintendo Switch port, has the almost unethical AAA pricing of $25 USD, for which you could easily get any number of actual AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $25 asking price for this game could get you games like "Assassin's Creed: Odyssey", "Bioshock Infinite" or "Disco Elysium".  No pixelcrap is worth $25. If developers want to get paid the same kind of money as real game developers who know how to do graphics properly, they need to learn how to do graphics properly.  Seriously.  These guys want AAA PRICING when they don't even know how to do video game graphics properly.  What a joke.  I'd laugh if I wasn't so insulted.  Let's keep Nintendo Switch pixelcrap where it belongs.

_childDocuments_.review: The game-play is very fun, the characters feel very different from one another and both the art-style and music perfectly fit the aesthetic the game is going for. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how this flew under my radar for so long. It's one of the best roguelikes I've ever played, and i've played a lot. The movement and combat is just so fluid, it keeps surprising me with how much build diversity and content there is, the art is gorgeous and such a nice style, the boss cinematics are sick, the characters have so much personality I honestly just can't recommend this enough. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, Charming and full of heart I think those words sum up what i like most about the game. The world is beautiful , i absolutely love the how everything looks. Im a sucker for pixel graphics, the characters are all loveable in their own way and you can tell the devs are putting a lot of care into this game. Honestly i have played my share of early access games, most show potential, few live up to it. If they never improve this game and left it as is i would be very satisfied. Now luckily there is still more to be added. Now let me get into a few specifics:The combat - Smooth and addictive, the combos are great and the spell mechanic adds another layer making every run feel unique and fun. I love customisation and figuring out on the fly what spell, gambit etc will fit in any given run is great. The music - Ah this is where the charm lives, the soundtrack is lovely, for an action game it feels like it wouldn't fit but honestly it is just so relaxing there has been times mid run where you can stop at benches and sit and i have my characters do so for a while just to listen to the track and marvel at the art.The Lore - I haven't gotten to the end of the game yet but from what they have put forward in the first couple hours it just makes me want to keep going to find out more about everyone. The premise is super interesting and the rate at which you learn more and more is good. Overall: I'd give this a solid 8/10 simply because it isnt finished yet but if they keep up with the how good things have been so far it would be a solid 9 maybe evem 10/10. Longest review i have ever written so that gotta count for something as well! If your on the fence like i was, go for it , you wont be dissapointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: For $25 and still early access I am happy to say that this game is very much worth it. If the early access part scares you then I am here to put your fears to rest, even if you do see yourself going through the worlds fast the bosses (Zodiacs) will firmly put you in your place. My favorite realization was when i went from hoping for a specific zodiacs that I felt good against to being confident against any of the 3 potential ones.... and then I got to feel it again in the next world and so on.

_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelites I've ever played. Fairly ingenious scaling that keeps things interesting after many runs without just saying, "here, it's harder now, can you beat that?"Has an attention to detail that is reminiscent of Japanese game design (and has a lot of nods to that, including full Japanese VO available, despite being a French dev studio). It's clear that they've played their own game a lot and really focused on eliminating any annoyances that plague some indie games, whether that's in UI, balance, bugs, etc.Also, the Hades-like expanding story keeps you interested without being overbearing, and can be ignored freely if you just want gameplay.Exceptional, 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as Hades or Dead Cells, but quite close. _childDocuments_.review: Difficulty of this game is just insane. The first boss has the most absurd movement and skills it's annoying as hell to play the first stage over and over. Souls-like x1000 and it's a pixel graphics platformer. The concept of moving in super close to do attacks that do almost no damage to just use a spell here and there is extremely unenjoyable in this execution. Timing is also completely unforgiving for this game. The boss has so many differently timed pauses between all of the moves which makes it just a game of learning the boss moves and timing of them over and over while the rest of the game is a boring breeze. It's also another one of those games that amazingly takes just over 2 hours to realize all of this and therefore cannot be refunded.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite 2D roguelite of all time. _childDocuments_.review: Update: The dev has since updated the game but I'll leave my original review below. Performance is great now and all of my other points still stand. This is a great little 2p coop roguelite. Lots of fairly unique new mechanics and the art is awesome. Definitely worth a shot these days.-----Honestly, I want to love this game so badly. The art is great, the animations seem pretty good, the combat is interesting and the mechanics are slightly different from everything else I've played.Unfortunately, the game runs like complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and stutters so hard it makes almost any of the more precise timings impossible. Any more than 3-4 enemies on screen at the same time and you're basically running the game at half speed. I'll probably update my review in a year or so when this game is out of early access, but getting a hard thumbs down from me until some serious performance improvements are made. I've got a GTX3080 12GB and an intel i9 11th gen... the only reason a pixel art game should be stuttering at all is just poor, poor optimization or the underlying game engine. Lack of graphics options is another huge underlying issue--there are only two settings or so to change. No framerate options period, no vsync options, period. tl;dr: this ones still a bit too early

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent finally left early access and it's great.The first thing that you notice about the game is its beautiful pixel art and great soundtrack. But, there is a lot more to it underneath the surface. In this roguelite you take the role of one of the 4 playable characters and try to escape the garden (prison) fighting common enemies and bosses on your way to final boss. Combat comes down to casting your spells, which are actually special attacks that consume your mana and in order to refill your mana you have to use basic attacks in between the spells. Each character has their own unique set of spells with some spells being universal and shared between characters and there is a lot of spells which really affect the way you play the game. Of course, the game gets more complex with various upgrades later on but I don't want to spoil anything. It may sound intimidating at first, but, trust me, it's not. Once you get the hang of it, it all clicks in the place and you start having a lot of fun. What's really important is the fact that gameplay is fluid with responsive and customizable controls which is great for a fast paced game. The game also has a story with fully voiced characters. It also has a coop mode which I haven't tried and can't tell you anything about its quality (sorry).When it comes to difficulty, it's challenging, but not too difficult and offers the option of modifying the difficulty.One thing that's a big plus of Astral Ascent are the developers. They are constantly fine tuning the game and are very active in the community, talking to players and listening to them. If you are a fan of roguelites that have story like Hades, or you like the 2D side scrolling pixel art ones like Dead Cells, give Astral Ascent a try. You won't regret it and you'll be supporting a great team of developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: This gaym is fantastic! An absolute must play for Roguelite platformer fans. Excellent!This might be the most polished gaym I have every played. Everything, from the voice acting, to the transitions between zones and the amazing timeline it shows you, to combat and spells, to character movement, to the visual and background environments, to the boss fights - it is all amazing.I literally only bought it because I loved Dark Devotion, the studio's previous gaym. Wasn't even planning on playing it - just opened it to see what its about. Got caught in a 2 hour enthrallment session.You know a roguelite is great when you die and you don't even care too much. So excited to see what happens next. Excited to see all the enemies you killed lined up at the end for a final presentation. Can't wait to speak to the NPCs again. My god. This is so polished.It really doesn't do a whole lot new. Its basically a bit like Skul in level design, but combat feels more like a Hollow Knight, Dead Cells and Gaucamelee blended mix. The key here is the execution being so damn good.The only negative thing I have experienced so far is the key mapping. I don't understand why you use one key (E) to interact the first time with an object, another (R) to place the object and another (F) to interact with NPCs and some other objects. Like, was (E) not sufficient? Does this make more sense on a controller?Also, some enemy actions are barely visible and not well telegraphed in the chaos of actions. This could be improved with better visual cues.Still. Brilliant. Now go give Dark Devotion another chance!

_childDocuments_.review: Ahhhhhhhhhhhh... if you are looking for a good action game, avoid this game. It's a good roguelike, very well cherished by the devs, but the action part is all over the place. You are not doing combos, you are not facing fair enemies (aside from the main bosses) and skill it's easily replaced with rpg elements and infinite meta-progression grind. After you beat the game the first time, mobs gets their attacks updated at the limit of unfairness: everything tracks you, everything attacks you at the same time, all the projectiles are multiplied by 3 and they can explode and shoots other unpredictable projectiles, all while trying to dodge insta-lasers/moves and other uncomprehensible patterns. The enimies got super armor always, so don't think that chaining your attacks is useful in some kind of way, aside from regaining mana. It felt like the game tryes constantly to make everyhting unfun, I don't want to melt  enemies with 1 hit to make me say "oh it's a good action game because I'm winning!", I want my actions to be meaningful and fun to pull off, accumulating buffs and gatling all my spells randomly on the enemies it's not what and action game is, in my book.Overall I'm happy to have bought this, the quality of the game is well worth the price, but I'm haveing half of the fun that I expected, that is all.

_childDocuments_.review: 2D side-scrolling Hades + Dead cells is an addictive, fun, difficult yet not overly-hard rogue-lite with a decent story and a lot of lore. There's a lot of interactions between the characters, many of them non-linear, but for 12 bosses, and over 10 npcs each to have multiple unique interactions with the 4 + 1 DLC characters, the game is very ambitious in that regard and sometimes it falls short at providing a meaningful through line for each possible character combination, but the game has an addictive "one more run" feel to it that will see you moving lightning-fast through the hours. Its rough and still needs features like an improved "quit mid run" feature and sometimes it crashes in multiplayer but overall a great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a blend of some of my favorite roguelites into 1 ball. You got the voice over quality and same sort of 'escape' story whilst having to go through bosses that are meant to prevent your escape from happening as Hades. The pixel art of and and color pallet of Skul, the platforming and combat of Deadcells, and the music gives me the same vibe that Dreamscaper did. Put that together and you have whats Astral Ascent, and what is there so far is great. Characters have personality and are voiced, the move set is varied and the progression between runs is something you can feel unlike some other games where the upgrades barely do anything to your character.The dev team is very helpful via the discord to boot, I had an issue on the steam deck and they spent about 2 hours helping me with a save file issue, I totally would recommend this title!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend it purely for the combat alone, that's also the only thing I want to talk about here.Apparently there are some people that don't think it's fast paced... I don't understand how they got to this conclusion.There's a basic attack, 4 equipped spells, a double jump, a ground slam, a dash with i-frames and then your signature spell.The signature spell is a unique move that is different for each character, for example: Ayla teleports behind an enemy and cuts them, Kiran has a counter attack parry. Basic attacks are very fast(even without attack speed upgrades) and you can cancel the recovery animation by jumping, attacking an enemy in mid-air also gives you back your 2nd jump, so you can always jump straight after attacking.You can do the ground slam when you're in the air, the slam does damage around you when you hit the ground but it also damages the enemies you hit while on your way down... you don't even have to hit the ground as you can cancel a slam by attacking in mid-air.Attack on the ground-> Jump to cancel recovery-> Attack in mid air-> 2nd Jump to cancel recovery of the mid-air attack-> Slam to hit the same enemy again-> Attack to cancel the slam so you hit the enemy AGAIN and get back your 2nd jump... You can do this pretty much endlessly and this takes care of enemies really fast.All of this is without even taking into account the fact that there are dozens of spells you can weave into your combos, though you can only ever have a total of 4 equipped throughout a run.If you do fail to cancel your ground slam it should be noted that actually landing with a ground slam always gives you back your dodge... instantly.You can: Dodge-> Jump-> Slam-> Dodge in quick succession to be pretty much be unhittable and to move around the levels a bit faster.My only real complaint? There's really not much that'll change the way you play DURING a run, only things that augment you and make you more powerful.I would've personally loved more upgrades that could change how a signature spell would work for example, instead of just giving it a neutral/ice/fire/lightning effect, adding explosions or reducing cooldown etc.From having played Ayla, Kiran and recently Octave... I have to say:Kiran is the best character hands down, though I should say up since he uses fisticuffs.Mostly because landing his parry gives you a strong counterattack AND causes you to be a invincible for some time.There's an upgrade for his signature spell(the parry) which reduces the total uptime for his parry(from holding it for 1 to 2 seconds it changes to be 0.2 or something) but also reduces the cooldown by 99 seconds when you land it.You can see how insanely strong this makes the character, it's by far the best upgrade that I've seen for any character so far.

Countless possible builds with enough tools to get what you need or close to.
