_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot so far and would recommend it. Adding some edits to my initial review:Things I like: - Graphics are great- Combat is pretty satisfying- Movement gives a lot of flexibility on how you approach enemies and adds a nice vertical dimension to fights- Meaningful choices about routes through the different zones, giving you a ton of options for how you want to scale your character- To add to that, HOW you upgrade seems to matter. It feels like you can make a better or worse choice along the way and that can make the run notably tougher or easier for you. I think as I'm starting to make better choices, the runs feel more streamlined- The healing system is interesting, utility spells are a nice departure from your "active" spells, and the auras give nice permanent boosts that feel like they matter from within a run- It feels like there's a LOT of replayability here, and the NG+ system is fun so far and looks like it's shaping up to add some nice difficulty and give the player a lot of control over how to apply that difficulty from run to runThings I'm less fond of:- Even with damage scaling, it never really feels (to me) like your character hits very hard if it's not a spell. Honestly, I don't want to melee regular enemies 10-20 times to kill them, and IMO, melee damage could be scaled up. Right now, the meta-progression feels like I have more options per run as I go, but it doesn't feel like I'm getting much stronger at all from run to run. This can be particularly egregious during boss fights, which ARE fun, but which can tend to drag on for a LONG time because you have to hit them through SO many attack cycles.Edit: I still think the damage could be scaled up BUT it feels like less of a problem with some of the stronger auras, and I'm seeing those more frequently now. The boss fights still sometimes feel like hitting an angry sandbag with a spatula.- There are situations where a reward like an astral chest will be placed between two traps. It's a minor thing, but it doesn't feel great. I don't want 2 tree stumps to chuck 6 explosive dudes at me repeatedly while I decide which stat I want to scale.Edit: I still think this is true. I've had a few instances now where I've gotten smacked by a static trap while standing in front of an altar or at an end-of-level reward. It's never ruined a run, but it's made me grind my teeth a little. - Some parts of the "return to town" experience feel weird. For example, a bunch of the unlocks from the poet and the dragon (who wears his name well, despite what my character may think) were already auto-unlocked prior to my completing my second run. It makes the meta-progression aspect of it feel less fun, because I didn't have to work to unlock them.Edit: I think I was wrong to suggest that a bunch of the selectable spells and auras were "fluff", so I deleted that from my first comment. After some more play time with them, they do feel better to use than I expected. I do think that synergies seem harder to build than I'd like, but maybe that's because they're not meant to really lock in until late game, which isn't out yet. Might be nice to see an added bonus if you have like 2 of the same type of gambit apply to a spell or something, particularly since there are a limited number of Pavo feathers and you can only upgrade so many times. - My own personal thing, but 4 spells feels like maybe 1 too many. I'd rather see more ways to upgrade the spells I do get. Combat is frantic enough that I'm not really actively choosing individual spells during fights most of the time, and the icons are small enough that I'd have to memorize the rotation during each run or stare at the lower left corner to pick them in real time anyway. The pace of the combat just makes it seem like there isn't really time to do that. It's a little different with boss fights, but given that you HAVE to cycle through spells, it feels like they're on a conveyor belt most of the time anyway, and 1 fewer might make for a better rotation, and synergies would be a little easier to build up. Edit: I'm torn on this. I still feel like the spell rotation is a little clunky. Maybe it's because I'm usually still toting around one "beginner spell" even by the end of the second zone. It's probably because I'm prioritizing keys and spell upgrades and Andromeda's bar when it shows up, but it seems like you SHOULD be prioritizing those things. It just always feels like there's one weak link in the rotation that doesn't really need to be there, especially because the "gambit slot" upgrades are so rare. Weaker/neglected spells are just going to continue to stay weak/neglected, because you're not going to spend the resources to level it or add a slot, when you already have 2 or 3 other things that are better and aren't maxed out. - A new one: I've had a few runs now where, even though I've taken keys whenever I'm low on them, I'll still hit a spot where I won't get any keys for several rooms in a row. It doesn't happen often, but it really sucks when you have to pass up 4-5 astral chests in a row. It seems hard to make up missing that many upgrades or auras, and so the run is kind of scuttled just because of bad room RNG. Maybe a mechanic where if you have 0 keys, the likelihood of a key room choice appearing at the end of a room increases by a small amount every time one doesn't appear. That way, if you're ever out of keys for more than a few rooms, it's because of a choice you've made and not because of bad luck. I like this game a lot. It's a ton of fun, and I'm eager to see where the devs go with it. I think it's more than worth the asking price, even at this point in its development.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically and visually amazing, with a great soundtrack to boot. The combat feels snappy, responsive and intense and the movement is crisp and precise. Like many of my favorite roguelites before it, I found and got it in early access and so far I don't regret it.That being said, for what is on offer it is a little pricy in my opinion. There are better, fully released titles with active development that have a similar price. I think it doesn't add up - maybe the (unnecessary) anime trailer was too expensive in production
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This one's a winner. Action hack-and-slash rogue-lite with a magic mechanic that makes combat pretty interesting and not too repetitive between runs, plus good pacing on meta-progression in the over world so you always feel like you're moving forward even when you fail. The main story's not going to knock anyone's socks off, but some of the characters and their dynamics are pretty good (at least enough to keep you interested for 1 play through anyways). The art style is vibrant, bright and colorful, which very much fits with the tone of "MAGIC! PEW PEW!" that the game is going for.Haven't tried co-op so I can't comment on that (local only = :( but I understand the decision for a small team to prioritize other things), but for the single player game alone I'd say it's definitely worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind I also have another 20-ish hours between the game's previous demos and playtests.This roguelite combines some of the best pixel art and animation on the market with fluid gameplay and an interesting mysterious world to explore, creating a special treat for almost any type of player. This game can provide a challenge for experienced roguelite/like players while also being accessible to those who have not yet tried any games in the genre. It takes inspiration from many other great games before it and so far executes every aspect flawlessly.I'm starting with the cons only because there are so few. Everything after this is positive. The devs have a very high standard of quality and are very critical of their work. This means that at the time of writing this review, there may not be enough content to satisfy everyone - even though the game is quite addicting. That said, there is more content than first meets the eye. The game also needs a little more difficulty balancing work done to it, but it is adequate enough as everything would need to be balanced all over again once the next two worlds are finished.It's damn good pixel art. From the characters to the world art to the spells, it just doesn't get better than this. It's worth following their Twitter account for this alone.Also top tier, Dale North's work on the game's soundtrack continues to impress me. The sound design of the world around you truly brings the game to life - especially at The Garden (your hub world). Attacks and spells for both yourself and enemies have distinct effects and satisfying feedback.I'm sounding like a broken record, but the character design is just as impressive as the rest of the game. There is a very diverse cast that is also FULLY voice acted with talented actors behind it. They are all memorable, and I definitely want to cosplay Taurus one of these days. There is not much story at the time of writing this outside some mystery and lore, but I am sure this will be expanded upon later.The gameplay loop is addicting - which is undoubtedly the most important part of making a good roguelite. One of my favorite parts about the gameplay is how many other activities there is to do outside of just fighting during your runs. There are already dozens of unique spells to use and countless upgrades, both temporary and permanent. The two existing characters play quite differently despite both being melee characters, and the remaining three characters will only make the gameplay more insanely varied. There is also already a NG+ system up to +12 with customizable challenges.The developers are very friendly and also active on their Discord server. That is also the best place to report any bugs or make your own suggestions on how to make the game better. The devs are on top of any and all issues impacting the experience and even pushed out a week-1 patch to increase performance after several complaints with more fixes on the horizon.Give this game a try! I can almost guarantee you won't be disappointed. Even now it is worth full price imo, and yet the amount of content in the game is going to basically double by the time it launches outside of early access!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooooo good I want to cry. Need more devs like this in the gaming industry :')The gameplay is soo fluid and fast paced at the same time, it's so amazing to fight a boss for the first time even if you're getting your ass whooped. To me at least, this game actually rivals Hades and Dead Cells (but I didn't play Dead Cells too much, so not sure about this) in terms of gameplay, only thing Hades has over it is the levels of voice acting and story behind it. However, that's not to say this game doesn't have good story elements, it certainly does. I can't wait to see if they have any additional content to add. All hail Hibernian Workshop.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Side-scrolling Hades, the bosses are based on the traditional twelve zodiac signs instead of mythological gods. The in-game and cutscene art is gorgeous, the scenery is gorgeous, the music is nice and the voice acting hits.Obviously it's early access, so the game isn't finished, the last area isn't yet included but I haven't encountered any bugs yet. My only real gripe is that I wish it had true online co-op, remote play together is nice but it's way too susceptible to lag.UPDATE: This game still slaps and people are sleeping on it, it's only improved with the 1.0 release and I wish I could convince more of my friends to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Release is upon us! and god is it glorious, everything in here is triple A quality, gorgeous animations, beautiful designs, amazing gameplay and a great soundtrack to boot, Astral Ascent is probably one of the best if not the best roguelike out there right now, there is so much variety between the characters and the builds, it ain't no isaac, but it sure succeeds at keeping every run fresh, my biggest gripes are that there currently is no wiki to speak of (but to be fair most unlocks are pretty easy to figure out, as the game is pretty linear with them) and the movement while great, is left for you to figure out (ground slams reset your dash, take advantage of this by jumping, dashing, ground slamming then dashing again!)All in all, Astral Ascent is a must play in my honest opinion.Edit: it's even better now!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent has potential to be a very respectable game in the genre. Great art style, mechanics, pace and flow! One my current issues is that many times during the run, the music does not match the pace of the gameplay. For example, sometimes when I'm massacring a wave of mobs the song is still in a chill and slow mood, which sets me off. The runs are still short but absolutely fun even with the current early access gameplay. I recommend fans of the genre give it a try and help the devs with feedback. Looking forward to the future of this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a first impressions sort of review:As someone who hasn't played many other games like this (pretty much Hades), I've got to say. I HIGHLY recommend this game! Been following their project for the past few years & I'm so glad to finally be playing version 1.0!The art is beautiful, the OST is phenomenal & the game just feels buttery smooth and responsive whether you're playing on KBM or controller. It's difficult to explain at the moment, but I'll probably come back later & make a full review. I'm very impressed by Astral Ascent & my score at the time of reviewing is an easy 8/10 at LEAST. And I know I've barely scratched the surface.For those who don't want a score: Just buy the game. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; great fast paced roguelitePros:Cons:Astral Ascent probably isn't the best choice for your first roguelite game, but outside of that it's amazing. Heroes are distinct enough that it takes me a while when switching to a different one. No prolonged grind-for-the-sake-of-grinding, just about everyting progresses you somehow. Builds are diverse, withing the combinations offered, and your will often change them during a run. Generally not constricted by rng drops, you can get anything you want if you really want it; either through shops or special rooms. It has tons of progression and you are free to invest into whatever you think you need. Even reset/redistribute in some cases.This game, at least at first look, looks super complex. All the info you need to intake and then make use off, looks daunting. But it's well structured and it connects together nicely. Once you're over the hump, it's insane fun. Maybe I'm getting old, but the village map was a tad annoying to navigate. Once I learned about the teleport stones it got better :). Controls for navigating, connecting and slotting of items was rough on me, too. There is nothing explicitly wrong with it, I enjoy it now, it just took a while to commit to muscle memory.I'm definetly happy I purchased this one. IMO worth full price if you're into this kind of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Can't begin to say how good this game is and how much the devs deserve a huge success. This is one of the best and most fun action roguelikes I've ever played. The spells, story, characters and world building feels unique, the artstyle and music are both fantastic, and you have hours upon hours of content to unlock and explore. I was genuinely excited for the 1.0 and after playing with a friend yesterday for two runs (YES, the game has one of the best COOP experiences for an action roguelike I've ever played) I can safely say this launch version is totally worth it. Please get this game because you will probably never regret it, totally worth its price! <33
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun platform roguelite in the vein of Dead Cells and Skul, with some really fresh mechanics that provide a huge amount of build diversity.AA is also visually and aurally stunning, with the art and soundtrack putting most other titles to shame, and the difficulty is incredibly well tuned. Boss fights so far (I've encountered 4 unique bosses) are challenging but never frustrating.As good as Dead Cells, and it's not even feature complete yet. 11/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of my favorite solo player games. it reaches everything that a roguelite/roguelike could for me. there's character archetypes/classes, a lot of personality, intimidating yet cool bosses, beautiful art, deep lore, and even furry characters. i love this game for the main reason that it's not too taxing on your computer to run yet is even more beautiful than most medium and lower budget games. there are parts that make you sad in lore, parts that are funny, parts that make you go "wtf???" and more to come as it's not even fully finished yet. the only thing i would say i don't like is how ayla and (mostly early game) kiran are kind of lacking in style compared to octave and callie. and it seems like that'll become even more prominent with yamat. but this is hopefully something that'll be touched up on as i do like both the characters; i just feel their fighting is getting a little lacking but that's a personal opinion of my own and you might love their more simple yet effective fighting styles. i'm a person who usually only plays games online with my friends but this is one of very few games i enjoy playing alone, i've played this game more that what my time on here would say as i've played a lot with my friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lot of fun, and the lore is surprisingly interesting.Edit: After beating the Master/Ophiuchus for the first time, the game introduces this new currency you get by grinding out the Zodiacs on higher difficulty runs and that prospect made me lose all interest in continuing to play. I think it's an okay game on a sale, but not at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game since before it was on Steam, and this is without a doubt the best Roguelike I've ever played. The art and character designs are phenomenal, the combat feels incredibly satisfying and has a rewarding skill ceiling, and there is an incredible amount of content. The devs show so much love and care for this game and the community, it only keeps getting better as time goes on (especially as of The Arsenal update!)Not to mention the variety in runs is insane. The sheer amount of spells between all of the characters, gambits, auras, Zodiac assists, and now WEAPONS each with multiple different passives give so many options for builds, it never gets old.The co-op is also a fantastic feature, and I wish more 2D roguelike games would do it. That's absolutely one of my main draws to this game, being able to play it with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This is like Hades but as a 2d platformer, although I think its even better with the rotating 4 spells system making each run fresh and unique. I got to the end boss twice, never beat him but I was satisfied with the gameplay loop and didnt want to start another run. I think the runs are a bit too long as you get further but thats just a me problem. Highly Recommend for those who like challenging games.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely wonderful, full of vibrant colours and a wonderful voice acted array of characters. The intricacies of the spells and the modifiers make every run something cool and unique, and I cannot wait to see the other characters be released. It's my first time being buying an early access game as I am always a little hesitant but I can safely say this is well worth the price!I'm hoping the full release will have co-op online rather than just the steamplay so my friends and I can progress our save files together.The only issue I saw that arose came with the boss fights, I'm not a game designer nor do I know a lot about the ins and outs of programming - but the AI in boss fights still sees the dead co-op player as a living player and will priority target them still, it made the boss fight funny, but probably not intended on what the developers wanted!
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't do this before stopping to play the game, but this one is so perfect it deserves it. The game is much closer to Hades than Dead Cells, as the I-frames are plentiful, and sometimes the screen looks more like a bullet hell than anything. Still, the game is a lot of fun, has a nice and steady learning and difficulty curve and the progression in any run is truly sublime. Highly, highly recommended.An update: With the addition of more content and even more coming, this game is getting ridiculously good. Buy it, especially at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Despite how it looks initially, I would definitely say that this is one of the more unique ways of going about a rogue-lite. The characters feel balanced, yet challenging when learning each of their unique abilities. The ability to choose which style of level comes next makes it a bit more strategic to think about in the long run, especially if you're going for a specific build. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Blending action-packed combat with rogue-lite elements, it delivers a visually stunning and fast-paced experience. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game is good. Even better than I expected. Beautiful visuals, super crisp combat, and a rewarding upgrade system both in meta progression and per-run progression. The only negative I’d bring up is the difficulty landing good synergies. You may start a run with a passive that helps your missiles, but then have a hard time getting a way to even generate missiles for instance. I’d prefer that passives always have at lease SOME utility. Some are totally worthless unless you pair them up with others. All in all though, fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent is a wonderful game.It is even hard to find something bad to say about it.From excellent exploration gameplay to tight combat mechanics. Awesome boss design to great progression system. Very nice cutscenes, endings, crisp sound design, beautiful original soundtrack (special mention to the final theme of the final boss), endearing characters with very nice voice acting... pretty much everything is well executed.And as usual with the current state of the industry, it's important to note that there is little to no bug.Unlocks and meta progression are well balanced and does not feel forced at all (the only thing requiring a bit of farming are the colors... so it's not mandatory and only cosmetic). Spells are diverse enough to satisfy everyone.If you liked Dead Cells, Rogue Legacy or Hades, you will most likely enjoy Astral Ascent.Thank you for this great game Hibernian Workshop <3

_childDocuments_.review: Astral Ascent is an action 2D-roguelite that has a satisfying gameplay loop, nails the feeling of progression and offers a lot of variety over the course of the many runs one can have.Only some small nitpicks add up that hold this game back from being an alltime classic. Okay, let's start at the very basics of what makes an action roguelite good:Engaging gameplay loop (you don’t want to zone out, it needs to be mechanically and theoretically engaging)Runs have to feel different (roguelites are supposed to be replayed, they have to differ)Steady feeling of progression (unlocking new stuff, options or possible opponents)Consistency (a good player should be able to win every run consistently)These I think are some of the main points, they are not exhaustive. Astral Ascent basically nails all of them.It is a skill based 2D action roguelike which has almost fully preventable damage, especially as Astral Ascent always shows danger zones of enemy attacks. The player can rely on mechanical skill, but does not need to. Absurd and strong combos are not only encouraged but also rewarded. I want to stress that despite some combinations being forceable, flexibility is very important as brute forcing is rarely as optimal as going with the flow.I don’t want to spoil the surprises, but there is a lot of variance, starting with the multiple playable characters even. My favorite part of the game is the progression:Astral Ascent offers permanent upgrades which are not necessarily just stat increases but often consistency boosters and new “gimmicks” that allow varied play.Sometimes I don’t want just more damage, but to abuse a new technique to then earn myself high damage. Just one spoiler for the challenge seekers: the game offers content even after unlocking most upgrade, as a system akin to the heat system in Hades exists (as in you pick disadvantages to spice runs up and get more rewards). And it is VERY hard. This is some sweet pixel art. Everything in Astral Ascent oozes lively energy. The sprites are very simple, but convey enough. While the playable characters are animated well, the bosses steal the show.They are energetic, fast-paced, but still very comprehensible. It is hard to create good and varied patterns for bosses that still feel intuitive and fitting for the character. An often used test is that a character should be recognizable by their silhouette. Astral Ascent passed that test with flying colors.Using this transition:Especially, I want to stress how well the game uses colors. Different elements use different key colors, but the game manages to make me understand what I am seeing despite dropping like 10 different colored projectiles because of my build. The color coding helps a lot, even in menus. Memorizing that poison symbol? Nah, I just memorize purple, easy. Through the use of a smart keyword system, everything gets explains fast and well, without having the player bored by superfluous tutorials. Long gone are the times I am ready to invest an hour or two for something that I could learn within 10 minutes. Astral Ascent actually keeps it at 10 minutes and technically makes most of the information completely optional. It is absolutely possible to win runs and finish the story without ever really understanding most of the keywords and basic interactions. The music of Astral Ascent is very competent, yet it lacks that certain oomph.Especially the relaxing pieces are very well done and can be listened to endlessly.The battle themes on the other hand are too short and loop a little too soon as a result.Everything that is in the game is good. The problem is that the tracks needed to be a little longer to fit in the mood, and listening to the same battle track three times in 10 minutes does get tiring. I do not dislike the music, far from it. This is one of the few times I did not only want, but actually needed more music. The lore of Astral Ascent is more than serviceable, despite being told in relatively short text segments. Especially, characters explicitly talking about what happened in the past and discussing their relations is very much interesting as relationships evolve over the course of the runs.The problem I am having is that the actual story is too simplistic, even for its own sake. I think that the developers wanted to reduce overhead and create something very coherent (at which they succeeded), but could not formulate a more ambitious goal for the story as a result. If you care about genuinely good stories and want to invest in something like that, Astral Ascent is the wrong game for you. I really liked my time playing Astral Ascent and I do see myself going for some more runs, despite being a person who hates having no concrete goals. The runs were fun, the gameplay is engaging, and the consistency is good enough. If the story and music were on par with the rest, I would call this a masterpiece. At this point, I will still wait, but if Astral Ascent gets even more updates and gets even better, this game becomes a no-brainer to pick up.If you are a gameplay first kinda guy, though, you can do nothing wrong with Astral Ascent.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches that Hades itch while also being totally different. The combat is satisfying, the characters' personalities are all very different from each other, the writing is good, and the aesthetic is exactly what I like.  So while I can't say it'll be a great game for someone else (like it is for me), I definitely think it's worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot like Hades, which I like, both story-wise and gameplay-wise! You unlock bits of dialogue and story with each run/death, and there's always something to upgrade when you go back to the hub area, and new mechanics are introduced at a steady pace.The boss fights are really neat, each having their own mechanics to dodge, and they're all really fun. The spell-system is neat and I like how they're upgraded, and there's a lot of passive bonuses you can stack via different mechanics available to you.I can see the game has a lot of updates coming in the future as well. With all of this said, I highly recommend the game!

_childDocuments_.review: I spent 42 hours completing Destiny 7 and found the game mechanics outstanding. The interaction between spells and gambits makes each playthrough unique, with each run taking about an hour to reach the final boss. The diversity in characters and their play styles enhances the game's depth. The storyline is engaging, and the audio and voice acting are particularly noteworthy. _childDocuments_.name: Astral Ascent

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a visual delight and extremely fun with enticing characters and a very good combat system. The spells rotating is a brilliant way to make sure you value every ability instead of feeling forced into using one that is obviously best. _childDocuments_.review:
Astral Ascent is a 2D platformer rogue-lite game set in a modern fantasy world. As one of 4 Heroes with very different personalities, you must escape from the Garden, an astral prison guarded by 12 powerful and vicious bosses, the Zodiacs.

Unlock dozens of unique spells for your 4 distinct characters. Optimize your own build or try out new ones to take down 12 powerful bosses. Get stronger with time to match up with your foes. Each run will test your skills and your reactivity.

name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes
detailed_description: The Dark Pictures Anthology is a series of standalone, cinematic branching horror games where the decisions you make in the game determine the story and the outcome you receive. House of Ashes is the third game in the series. In House of Ashes, at the close of the Iraq War, Special Forces hunting for weapons of mass destruction unearth something far deadlier – a buried Sumerian temple containing a nest of unearthly creatures. To survive the night below, they must forge a brotherhood with their enemies from the world above. - Navigate the underworld and escape a terrifying threat Fight your way out of a buried sumerian temple against hordes of deadly monsters that have claimed you as prey. - The enemy of your enemy is your friend This time, your crew is composed of 2 opposing factions that rarely see eye to eye. Can you put aside your character's rivalries to fight together as one ? - Don't play alone The two critically acclaimed multiplayer modes are back. Share your story online with a friend or aim for safety in numbers through the offline 5-player pass-the-pad mode. The Curator's Cut The Curator's cut features new scenes playable from the other characters' perspective with brand new choices and decisions to make. The Curator's cut is only available once you have completed the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: is a series of horror games, developed by the studio responsible for making Until Dawn - a very well received horror game, most known for having both cliché as well as unexpected twists, tough choices with genuine consequences, and mysterious monsters, which we know nothing about at the start. Since then, people have been waiting with set up expectations for a similiar game, but for the first two games, . felt like it was the closest one to Until Dawn . I wouldn't necessarily call it Until Dawn 2, but it might be a worthy successor. Personally, the first two games of the series were easily forgettable, with characters that I couldn't feel sympathetic towards, and a twist that I found annoying. When I heard this game would tell a story of soldiers fighting in Iraq, I was convinced I'm not gonna be attached to these characters either.To my surprise, some of the House of Ashes characters were the ones I liked the most out of  of their previous games. It seemed phenomenal how much a person, with their mind and principles shaped by war, can change - .However, I won't go into details, as I will be keeping this review spoiler-free.I think this comes as a good storytelling game with horror elements attached to it. Not many jumpscares are in the game, and the monsters don't feel that unnerving. Or perhaps they do, but knowing that you play as trained soldiers, you just keep your cool over time, sort of getting used to their presence. What's important is , as it kept me alarmed through the game. You go into the unknown, exploring ancient ruins, not knowing what you're heading into, while the place could seemingly collapse. And the space momentarily was , that it suddenly made me feel claustrophobic. A very intentional design, as later on a total opposite was done - you are thrown into a  area, feeling the same level of discomfort, but this time from the room being too big. Clever, and I really enjoyed this aspect of the game, as the atmosphere really kept me immersed.The most disturbing scene to me was talking with the Curator, actually. The moment our conversation ended, I noticed something really shady, which made me rewatch the scene, frame by frame, to confirm what I saw. An easily missable, subconscious detail, which most people won't even notice, but it left me frightened enough.The twists. Not gonna hint at what it is, but just to say, every game had a twist so far, and so to guess, every future game will have one as well. I don't think they are needed, I think the games are good enough without them, and they seemingly could discourage some players from enjoying the story. _childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes is an action-packed roller coaster ride where you try to survive a night in a cursed temple hunted by supernatural horrors. The game is less horror and more action, but the suspense and atmosphere will have you carefully weighing your choices. The graphics are photo-realistic and you will quickly feel you are watching a movie. I have a background in archaeology and spent some time in the military, and both these areas of the game are done extremely well. The temple looks realistic and the period pieces and lighting adding to feeling that danger lurks around every corner. The military aspect has your survivors communicating, fighting, and moving as a real team would. While playing this game, you will feel as if you are a soldier trying to escape a forgotten temple -- and it is terrifying. The story is fairly original . Your team is hunting for a weapons cache and quickly learns there is something much more dangerous lurking and survival is the new objective. The latter stages of the game takes an odd turn, that may or may not, add to an already good story. The characters have backstories that matter, their choices can lead to possible fatal or life-saving possibilities -- all dependent on how you play them. If you want what you decide to matter than this game is a good choice.House of Ashes is by far the most action-oriented entry in the series. If you want more horror and less shooting, this may not be for you, but if you want a thrilling ride through a cursed temple chased by monsters -- than I can only recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes sees a group of people trapped in underground ruins in Iraq during the 2003 US invasion attempting to escape vampire like demons that have been down there for thousands of years. The main characters include a CIA operative with a hideous character model that is for some reason in charge of a small group of the most incompetent Marines I've ever seen who have apparently been existing in a combat zone in an unready state while hoarding some war crime white phosphorus grenades, until her husband that she has been away from for a year shows up to take over. Her husband being an Air Force Lieutenant Colonel whose satellite project is being used to try to find hidden weapons of mass destruction and is what finds the old ruins. There are two marines main characters with one being the guy the CIA agent has started a relationship with while away from her husband, and another one who is a racist with a 9/11 hat. The last character is a member of the Iraq Republican Guard who is there to be the only competent, badass, friendlier person, who might just be able to make the racist marine not as racist anymore and if the entire game was just about him fighting the Americans and the demons it would have made for a better time. Unfortunately, he can't save the game all by himself.The previous entry in the series, Little Hope, wasn't good but it at least had some ideas and moments that could have lead to it being good if not for the terrible overarching premise, this looks like it might take the series into something the developer can do a better job with by making a more action packed faster paced ridiculous ride but it manages to mess even that up. While Little Hope had some very strong acting in a mostly mediocre script, Ashes doesn't even have that with the best actors giving just passable performances with the exception of Ashley Tisdale as the CIA operative who is always terrible. The constant finding of items and collectibles to slowly examine take you away from the immediate story as much as before, but even more so here in what should be a more dangerous fast paced situation.The action scenes end up being laughable incompetent with every shot seemingly being a tracer round that frequently show the bullets going nowhere near what anyone should be aiming at. The scenes where US and Iraq forces fight make Steven Seagal movies look well shot and better able to follow a logical event chain. The monsters don't even seem to react to being shot in the face multiple times in certain scenes but can apparently be stabbed and killed with old slightly pointy objects not designed to be used as weapons. The camera is completely unable to handle some of the confined or narrow areas you find yourself in. Characters mouths don't always move when they are speaking and there are frequent fast jump cuts in multiple scenes either like frames missing from action scenes or like it was possibly looking for a scene or line that might have happened if different choices were made then cut somewhere else when it couldn't find it. The characters apparently all have an infinite supply of ammunition (until near the end of the game when they finally start running out), though that doesn't end up being very useful to them. They find out UV light will set them on fire so when they start breaking through one of the doors they are defending they decide to shoot at the door instead of just shining the light on their hands or through the open cracks of the door (or shooting larger hold in the door that could then have the UV light shine through it). The dialogue is ridiculous, any soldier in the game tends to be written in the most stereotypes ridiculous way imaginable. A side character dies after seemingly being shot in the legs, making you think that the plot might understand that getting shot is actually bad, only for multiple characters to be shot later on only to have them completely ignore it and to go on with it never mentioned or considered a problem for them. Like all bad monster media the creatures are as fast or slow, strong or weak, and smart or stupid as the couple minutes needs them to be before deciding to do the opposite in the next scene.Being that it stars characters that are CIA and marines invading a country outside of WWII I assumed I'd want them to die but these characters were nearly David Cage levels of unlikable and incompetent to the extent that I'd want them to die no matter who they are or what they were doing. It also makes it difficult to want to go back and see what changes different choices can lead to as it doesn't allow you to skip any of the scenes that you have already seen before.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes, the sequel to Little Hope and Man of Medan in the Dark Pictures Anthology series has some explicitly major improvements from its predecessors, and overall is an excellent QTE horror game in every essence. Although, from my personal opinion, little hope contained a certain concept and mechanic that i thought should've been incorporated into this sequel, but was absent after completing my first play-through. This specific concept i am referring to is the traits certain characters have at the beginning that is true to their personality having an impact on the characters lives and outcome at the end, depending on the players decisions. Even though you could shape the character however you please, this had no effect on their death. This minor concept that i thought would've only made the game even more excellent, nonetheless was a missed opportunity. I'm sure plenty might disagree with this addition, but personally i thought it would be a great addition.Now, to discuss the majority positive aspects and mechanics of this sequel. First off, the QTE action sequences were well executed and exciting, and definitely were polished and improved from the previous titles in the anthology series. Second, i also enjoyed the fact that succeeding certain quick time actions actually resulted in negative consequences, depending on the scenario and what you were succeeding at doing. In hindsight, failing to do something when you have the option otherwise can also punish the player and take an innocent main characters life as well consequently. It can potentially go either way, and the game expects you to correctly read the situation as you would in real life to make the appropriate course of action. Asides from the QTE and decision improvements, i also loved the setting, the monsters (trying not to spoil), the story and lore that you discover through playing, finding secrets and journals, and i also got attached to many of the characters, even some of the minor support ones as well. The character development is relatively even for most of the characters, but my favorite is definitely Salim and Jason which seems to be a popular notion. To avoid spoilers, i was kinda bummed that my one chain of decisions out of kindness and compassion ended up in a main characters death, but at the same time it was realistic and the possibility was still there. Last but not least, the port and it's optimization and performance. In terms of consistent frames, it was relatively stable and didn't impact my gameplay, which is pretty imperative for a quick time event game where reaction times and decisions need to be made in seconds. The hardware requirements are definitely at least mid-range in terms of hardware quality and performance, and if you want way over 60fps and ultra quality, a high-end CPU and graphics card is likely necessary. Even so, most players can run this game and have no issues. In terms of glitches and bugs, i think i encountered one maybe, but it was just a visual bug and didn't affect gameplay and was only during a cut-scene transition. To give an overall rating, House of Ashes is easily a 8/10 in my book. I somehow managed to save 4/5 main characters, and as i mentioned before, i lost one due to prior decisions instead of quick time events. I definitely recommend this title to anyone that enjoyed the previous games in the anthology series, and also loves horror games where choices definitely matter and quick time events are your thing. Even if you're new to QTE games, this one is a good start.Please, feel free to leave any comments you have about the game and my critique.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Decent voice acting.Story was so-so.Characters were ok, especially Salim and Jason.EDIT: forgot to mention the optimization was nicely done. I maxed the settings on a 21:9 1440p screen without any FPS drops or micro-stuttering.Cons:In my opinion, the ending didn't feel like it gave me enough closure. Some may not not mind it, especially after the last game...but I wanted more from this one.Some of the decisions were very vague. I knew from the character dialogue what I wanted to choose but it wasn't obvious what I would be choosing so I had to guess and often went against my wishes. Really upsetting in a game where choices matter and since you can't go backwards, once you've made the choice the game is ruined permanently unless you start over.Some plot holes, nothing major, but small stuff that lacks consistency. "I need help, I'm injured" then 45 secs later he's sprinting without issue. Come on man...They removed the fast walk. Also the FOV changes at random and isn't adjustable. More often than not the FOV is claustrophobically narrow.Sound effects were terrible and the dialogue wasn't that great so overall it lacked any feeling of seriousness or drama. Not at all a horror game to me.Overall:Disappointed. The first game was great and the second one was creepy and fun right up until the lame ending...this one didn't deliver which makes me question if I should get the 4th one.Additional note, not sure if con against the game or Steam:EDIT: to get some options like ray tracing to work, you have to enable DX12 mode. Steam was kind enough to add an option to choose from within the game's properties so you set which version runs by default...problem is you must always run the game from within Steam for that to work. If you run from a desktop icon, it always defaults to DX11 no matter what.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first game in the series, and I must say, I will definitely be checking the other ones out.Pros:My absolute biggest love for any game is to be able to make decisions and have those decisions actually affect the outcome in very different ways. This delivers on that. I had so many choices and it felt amazing to get instant feedback on how people around me interpreted them, how I came off, and what traits people started to associate with me. This in turn affected every character I played, which meant that while playing through every character in the group, the ones I'm not currently controlling are making decisions based on my previous reasonings and traits! Super thrilled about that! I actually geeked out quite a bit since it's been awhile since I've had a game actually deliver on their decision game mechanics. Bravo.I enjoyed the style of the gameplay as well. While some may not enjoy the simple "timed click to avoid this", I felt it was an appropriate mechanic, and it became rather fun anticipating the next one. Where I felt it fell short:SO many questions to their choices, and at times, lack of questions they asked! As someone who loves science and has a curious mind, I was distraught at the lack of specimen retrievals, samples, and collections. How can you pass by XYZ and NOT want to analyze this?!?! I want to see what it's compromised of!! UGH. You have an entire ... and you choose to NOT preserve it?! UGHHH.Cons:There is absolutely no skip for the cutscenes. They are quite lengthy and there are a lot of them. This game feels more like an interactive movie at times. I would love to play through this game again for additional choices but until they implement a SKIP feature, or create a mod that allows this, sadly, I will not. This took around 7+ hours of playtime, and I would much rather just spend an hour to look up all the endings instead of the huge amount of hours watching cutscenes. That's saying something considering the choices were my favorite aspect.Overall I would recommend this game as a fun playthrough with a pretty interesting story.

_childDocuments_.review: The third episode has you play a team in Iraq searching for WMDs. Instead they find an evil from the beginning of history.This is a straight up "creature feature." It is fun but this installment leaves you feeling like it could have been better. Everyone is a character cliche. For me, the personal problems the characters are dealing with has been done and redone to death. A marriage split with one of them still in love and the other is fighting with inner feelings- and happens to be in a relationship with someone else. Soldiers dealing with the trauma of a horrible mistake in war. The nicest people get killed to show the senselessness of war. FOR NO OTHER REASON- they don't even bother to develop the character beyond "They are great people, why did they die?"I don't know if it was how I played the cast but I swear 3 of them would not die. When I chose wrong or missed a quick time even the character would get bitten, pounced on by monsters and even fall over the side of cliff, only to be introduce a few scenes later having survived something where you swore they were dead.Now to say for the record: this was a harder game to keep your characters safe. The other two games were tense but your people never seemed in real danger. Some were killed, sure but till that point you felt they were safe. This story had you thinking they all could be killed any second and their was no rime or reason.Maybe that was the developers goal. Maybe it was me, I am not sure.The controls were switched up a bit. You now can turn on and off your flashlight or lighter and direct where the illumination shines with the mouse and keyboard controls and it feels better that just being on and shining in front of you like the others. Moving and looking around is better and work independently but is still hampered by the camera now and then. A few times I would turn around in a hall and the camera pointed the direction I was going and the character and light pointed in the new direction.The monsters are cool looking being crossed with giant vampire bats, the "quiet place" monsters and drug through some "stranger things" before trying to eat your face. They start as demons then become vampires then change to cosmic horrors, it could seem the creators didn't want to miss a genre. They creatures do not morph or change they explain them within the story as being all of these.The sets were good also. Most everything happens in long forgotten tombs and catacombs but open up to giant scales when you get into the caverns and other places.Again it was fun to play and follow the story but was a bit off for me. I still recommend this for fans of the style but get it on sale. $20 bucks is a very good price- $30 for full price is a bit much in my opinion. -MrGrAnD

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best so far:-great ambiance, great use of sound to set the mood, dynamic and interactive gameplay (kept us glued to the game for hours on end without noticing)-looks phenomenal, detailed models (a few reused though), nutty level design, sick game design with differing POVs and scenes, and a few QOL improvements over the last two (except some forced syncing delay sometimes to inspect things)-some genuinely good spooks thanks to the previous points-story was far grander than what I had expected (versus previous two games), you can even cultivate some decent character development-and some serious replayability, at least imo thanks to how unique the scenarios experienced are for player 1 versus player 2 (felt the most compelled to replay this game versus any other to date), not to mention the branching outcomes (which again this game did the best at making us care for)

_childDocuments_.review: 🎀Going beyond the usual clichés that reduce the credibility of the various characters, it is precisely the meticulous search for a cinematic experience that betrays the premises and the promises of the work.House of Ashes develops exactly like the previous chapters, offering a third person view, but modifying itself in accordance with the most excited moments. There are no more fixed shots and the protagonists, who alternate in the unfolding of the story, control themselves rather easily, despite the fact that they have the habit of planting themselves in certain points of the scenario. The usual QTEs and moral choices rattle off at a much more dilated pace than the previous exponents of the saga, unraveling the homogeneity of the campaign and drastically decreasing the level of immersion. Fortunately, the level of inclusiveness takes a big step forward, allowing you to customize your actions to make them less anxious and pressing.🎀Each title is a case in itself and chasing the labeling of a genre is a practice that I have always considered superfluous. As a mature and established entertainment work, the video game no longer has to worry about justifying its existence; a development team that tries to instill a message to the detriment of gameplay cannot be penalized, just as those who do exactly the opposite cannot be penalized, relying on overwhelming gameplay, at the expense of everything else. There are no "real" video games or "fake" video games, but only more or less successful titles. Unfortunately, House of Ashes belongs to the second category, and despite being formally the best exponent of the mini saga to which it belongs, it is only so if analyzed in its individual parts.🎀More than once it happens to lead one or more characters through dark corridors barely lit by torches, and it is not uncommon for these animated sequences to follow each other without any intervention from the player. Precisely because there are moments in which you have to escape, shoot or hide, it is anomalous that entire chapters see the protagonists perform these activities without our intervention, remaining only to watch. After yet another abyss jumped, door pushed and monster sent on the run without touching the controller, then it is clear that the mechanism behind the project has jammed.🎀The result is a game that is certainly more relevant to the narrative register that the developers have aimed at, giving, however, to its users only an acceptable film, supported by a mild interactivity that barely expands its use. All this, not wanting to be too strict, could also represent a conscious choice by the developers, were it not that the entire script continually winks at replayability. "If only I had done this or that", the protagonists often recite; yet repeating the game sequences, even not necessarily from the beginning, is exhausting, redundant and above all, simply boring. This did not happen with the previous chapters of the anthology and it is clear that Supermassive Games has let itself be carried away by the search for spectacularization at all costs, which however only happens through the excellent graphics and the extraordinary sound.🎀The stylistic coherence, the refinement of the scenarios and the careful use of filters in post production, give life to remarkable, almost photorealistic settings. The same care is taken in the creation of the protagonists, who through the performance capturing return a more than honorable actor's proof. Clearly, much of this is lost by opting for dubbing other than the original one; it is a physiological element typical of similar experiences, rather than a real defect.There are therefore no sound swings, voices that are too low compared to the audio effects and the assembly of the scenes that clumsily agree, rather obvious shortcomings already recognized in the previous Man of Medan and Little Hope. In this sense, this chapter reaches a technical maturity of a certain importance, which, however, clashes awkwardly with the game system that is not very cohesive and inserted almost by force in the flow of events. As with a blanket that is too short, Supermassive Games has failed to create a sufficiently homogeneous experience, despite the obvious efforts to better combine the two media it draws on. The result, unfortunately, is monotonous and obvious as a Movie and scarcely interactive and stimulating as a video game.🎀Replaying certain chapters to see new developments is a grueling exercise due to the very little interactive rhythm of the game.A coherent script, albeit weakened by character stereotypes and narrative banalities. The level of customization of the experience has been implemented properly and the game is usable even without having extraordinary reflections. If, however, the pleasure of replayability is taken away from the "game book" formula, opposed by infinite sequences that cannot be skipped, then the balance between the two genres of reference is lacking, ending up disappointing both the admirers of the Movie's and those of the video games, not for nothing the greater time of gameplay is occupied more by interactive sequences where we will remain only to observe rather than play.The worst title in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, this was a very fun game with a really good story.However, it is extremely hard to recommend this game, even on sale price of $20 for a few reasons. First, the game is too short to warrant a $30 and even a $20 price tag. The game has 6 hours of playtime in it and it is hard to milk more time out of it. The only way I can justify the price and gameplay time is if you take into account that there are not many games out there that are like this.The next reason on why this game is hard to recommend is because there are so many bugs. The first bug I had was that I could not get the game to fullscreen on the right monitor for the life of me. When I did manage to get it on the right monitor, I either had to have an upscaled resolution(no way to change it) or it would just force itself back to the other. The next bug were a variety of gameplay issues itself. My coop partner had issues where they could not see the game and could only hear it. This was resolved after restarting the chapter which is not ideal when you're at the end of the chapter. The next gameplay bug was random frame drops, especially during quick time events and heartbeats. The worst parts to have lag spikes in. Lastly, if you're buying this  game and intending to use the friends pass, good luck. It was a headache to figure out how to use because the instructions have been very bare. Becuase of the headache I had to buy another copy of the game for my coop partner because spending money was worth saving making my already bad headache worse.I can not recommend this game because there are way too many bugs and it was more than a nightmare to play through.

_childDocuments_.review: I felt that Little Hope improved on the mistakes made in Man of Medan, and House of Ashes did the same to Little Hope. This is objectively the best in the series so far. While the writing still lacks at times, the majority of the dialogue is phenomenal. With an exceptional cast, backstory, and environment, this blows the previous two titles out of the water. The third act had such an impressive climax that keeps you on the edge of your seat, and an ending that brings the story to a satisfying conclusion. I would definitely recommend this game; it is best played with friends but works alone too. I will likely replay this game a couple times to try out the different endings, something I didn't really bother to do in either Man of Medan or Little Hope.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Pictures: House of Ashes so far is the best of the series for me. Man of medan had a simple (but effective) story, the dialogues where to the point and not much else, but it was tons of fun. Little hope had much more ambition in the story and the setting but ultimately it got blown up in the end (not in a good way). This one in the beginning i had to admit i was afraid of not liking the characters because of being your typical manly north americans marines which i don't care at all but, i was proven very wrong about this.The marines were indeed what you expect them to be (sorry, stereotypes were confirmed!) but that was all as intended... in fact this was all a setup to incorporate something new to the series (and many other games out there): character arch!!! Yes!! This latest chapter in The Dark Pictures Anthology has really good dialogues (specially on the later half of the game) and also it has a great story this time. It is still a relatively simple , relatively short horror story but it does get somewhere and it does have a good ending (or not, depending on your actions and choices). The game first takes its time to present the main characters (both playable and non playabe) All while playing  of course, its not a cutscene! in fact you are already making some important choices at the beginning that will influence what happens later, much later in the game. I love that they took the time to do this, since its in direct contrast to what they did with the main characters in the previous games. In little hope you were already making choices for characters you barely knew, but this time when the main event begins you are already in knowledge of who is who, you may even know their names! *ahh!*  and you actually CARE about whats going to happen  to them... well, most of them anyway (i'm looking at you  , you piece of poop! you don't deserve to live after what you did with you know who on one of the endings.... *disgusted!*)The main characters have all previous stories going on with them, which during the course of the game you can see surface through their actions and your choices. This establishes a sharp contrast to how they "may" end up evolving. Yes, indeed,  character evolution is not free! you have to make it happen! Best character archs are . They start up in completely opposite places, they almost kill themselves at one point (if you allow it) but by the end of the game they are best friends. I loved seeing them go at the  fighting them, but even more so, taking care of each other. It was also interesting, some of the dialogue they have before the later part of the game, when they are still knowing each other, there are some interesting commentaries on different subjects related to the context of the story which are somehow unexpected but really cool to have them. It adds flavor to the story, it is cool to have some quiet moments with interesting dialogues. Then of course the game is just plain fun, besides the story and the characters and the dialogues, i think Supermassive is getting better with each game.It's not a Spoiler to say this, but, this review is

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly dissapointing. Perhaps an unpopular opinion, but I felt this was the weakest one in the series so far. Man of Medan had a good premise with poor execution, while Little Hope had a bad premise with great execution. House of Ashes falls into the pit of mediocrity: it's a safe premise with OK execution. Very predictable and felt very unoriginal overall. Definitely a ripoff of classic Sci-Fi films (won't mention them as it's a very obvious spoiler for the plot twist if I do).Not only was the story bland and unpredictable, the game wasn't great in the polish department either. Somehow, this was the buggiest mess yet of the series so far. Man of Medan went off without a hitch, Little Hope had a small 'Ready' bug, and House of Ashes has that same Ready bug, while also introducing plenty of crashes and it just felt like an alpha build instead of being ready to ship.Mechanics: Somehow the movement got worse. So much worseInteracting with items softlocks your character for 5-10 seconds if the character is not EXACTLY where the developer wants you to be (and interacting with items is also really difficult even if you're standing in a totally normal position). The finger-music puzzle near the end of the game was also wildly confusing in CO-OP and we got it pretty much by trial and error. Definitely needed a mini-tutorial to explain you needed to line up the fingers on both sides in the same place to progress.Overall, this was still a fun experience (highlight being the relationship between Salim and Jason) but I'm still left dissapointed going from the previous entries into this one. It's definitely longer which some people might see as a positive, but I'm an advocate for "Quality over quantity", and the game just felt like a worse story, stretched for way too long to the point where every chapter was utterly predictable. If you've already played the prior entries and liked them, then this isn't a bad play, but I wouldn't play this as your first Dark Pictures game. Hoping The Devil in Me is a return to form. Getting real tired of all the supernatural stuff so a game about "true" crime is quite appealing at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is gonna be a long one so TL:DR - if you liked Until Dawn and thought Man of Medan/Little Hope were a let down this is a step in the right direction. I honestly say give it a go. You'll start with some characters rough around the edges but the story knows that and if you move towards the "positive outcome" ending - most of them ditch their baggage and become pretty great (including one of the better bromances - certainly in recent memory).If you haven't played the game and are thinking about it, turn back now because here thar be spoilers.Hoo boy, that was quite a ride. I'll open up saying something positive. As I mentioned, vast improvement over the previous DPA games. I will confess I bought this going in ready to absolutely slaughter this game in to the ground for a stupid story that didn't matter and dumb characters that I hated - and then you hit me with G-d. D-mn. Dracula. At that point honestly stop drilling because you folks had hit gold so great job there! Also as is usual affair for these games the actors/mocappers really nailed it. I think the only line that I laughed at (that I wasn't supposed to laugh at) was Nick flatly asking "is that all you've got?" after he gets clocked by Eric and that's clearly not the VAs issue because elsewhere he gives fantastic performances. I dunno if it was a rush job from a rewrite, if the director was sick that day or if it was just recorded 5 PM on a Friday. The fact that it stood out to me though speaks pretty highly of the game.As final positive even if you don't like the characters, there are some pretty good opportunities to get people you don't enjoy maimed/killed in a pretty satisfying ways - so honestly the whole thing comes together in a package that's not bad, and dare I say it's actually a pretty decent experience.On to the bad... well it's most of the regular DPA stuff. What you do in the prologue doesn't really matter, and we already know our opening characters are both doomed. I put this in the bad because it's kind of predictable - but as an homage to the old 80's slashers that had to open with a "first kill" I appreciate it. I just respect that I'm in a minority here and it might be wearing thin on some people.Speaking of predictable - while this game certainly doesn't remove any sense of threat by making "the spooky stuff isn't real" it does still make sure it rationally explains how we got Dracula. I get it. The horror is scarier if it's more "real", and again this is honestly just personal preference - but when I said stop drilling in the positive section, I meant it. Leave some mystery to the monster or better yet, just let it be supernatural. I'll expand on this a bit more later.Finally the game goes on a bit long. Not too bad but I was kinda doing the "okay wrap it up" gesture in the final walking section with Jason + Salim. The section itself is fine but allow the characters to move at a brisk jog now because there's so much walking.Now I'm going to get in to the story - I don't think this will be a really relevant section of the review for a player and is more for the devs. If you want to read my insane ramblings by all means but you were warned, the things I'm talking about are more dev feedback than anything else.Eric and Rachel... why are they two characters? Like obviously they have to be to stop the interesting story every now and then to talk about their marital issues but like if you remove the strained marriage/love triangle subplot (which has no parallels or connection to the overall story) why are they two characters? Given that Eric designed the satellite I will assume he is the "primary King" and combine Rachel with him, however as I said the actors gave stellar performances and to be fair to Ashley Tisdale she could also absorb Eric in to her character.Eric drives the plot forward by inventing the satellite mcguffin and initiating the mission. Rachel just kind of babysits the team and gets usurped by Eric - really quickly too so they could just as easily have been a team Eric just met, or one that Eric had been prepping. Throughout the game there is nothing Rachel does that could not be done by another. I guess she serves as a hazard by bringing Clarice back? But you don't need that - Joey does fine as the "marine antagonist" and for extra scares could just keep coming back death after death after death to haunt the team - who perhaps are having trouble letting him go and dealing that final blow. Rachel does serve as a "lore check" towards the end in that she touches the big computer, explains "aliens" as if we hadn't figured that out already and then makes sure you got all of the hints about UV light by being infected and then immediately cured of the infection - a role that could again, go to literally anybody on the team. Imagine if instead Eric was infected and he had to convince a team he'd just met that sort of resented him for dragging them down to hell to use the UV light?Suppose for a moment though you give them both distinct roles - suppose rather than being "satellite nerd" Eric has, through some happenstance encountered a person or situation that convinces him the Vampires are real? That he is looking for the vampires actually - and must sign on with the US military as a means of getting access to this new site. Then suddenly his usurping of power from Rachel is a bigger plot point. He took her team and dragged them in to what amounts to a suicide mission on purpose, but because it was his only option - and the team have to reconcile being placed in mortal danger (a thing they were already in fighting in Iraq) with doing the right thing (a thing they're supposedly trying to do, fighting in Iraq).This can then be the central point of friction between Eric and Rachel, and how well it is resolved can even alter if their marriage is repaired or slaughtered like so many marines in a cave of Draculas, y'know make Erics and Rachels actions be the determining factor (like how it's actions that determine if Salim and Jason cooperate, rather than just dialogue). This also can give Rachel some active role in the story as the intermediary between Eric and the team of marines - that Eric needs her to help get the team on board with his pie in the sky mission to slay Dracula.Speaking of Dracula, ditch the alien angle. Just let it be Dracula. I know you're probably sick of hearing about it but Until Dawn - one of the studios greatest successes. There was no scientific reason for the transformation. "The mountain is cursed, evil spirits, possession" was good enough. Leave a bit of mystery!Finally, this also makes the "it was all a government cover up" a much more relevant twist - and perhaps the endings with Eric alive should have the team stay quiet about what they saw. "What? No nothing in there. Just rocks and dust." because Eric knows admitting the team knows places them in danger. It explains why he needed to use Rachels team specifically, because they were the only ones he could trust.I could go on, but I think you get the point and hey, if you want someone to punch up the next story let me know. The ground work you put down was solid, and overall an enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I had an absolutely great time with this game, and am so thankful that we have these developers pumping out this kind of entertainment. Not only was this a lot different than their other games, but it also really seamlessly incorporated what they labeled as their inspirations (which I didn't read about until after finishing the game). I wouldn't have cared if it was, but if any of you are concerned: yes, they are military people in this game, but that aspect doesn't overpower the story at all -- so if that was a concern, don't worry. I will agree with others that, no...the characters aren't as likable as in some of their other games, but the reasons are valid & they aren't one-dimensional -- you might not agree with what they do / have done, but they have reasons on display! Some people were saying the graphical fidelity varies & sometimes doesn't look good. If I'm honest, I didn't notice that at all -- I thought it was an amazing looking experience. There are a few "well lit" areas above-ground at spots, and that's all I can think of that they might be referencing (harsher light = harsher to pull off), but I thought they looked fine. Anyway, this is another great release by Supermassive. Of all of their releases, I think this ranks at either #2 or #3. For its time period / setting Little Hope is my favorite (which I know is not a popular opinion), followed by either this or Until Dawn. I recall Until Dawn being excellent, but it has been a very long time since I played that & I do recall the dialogue being a bit tinny, whereas the production values are high here -- so they're kind of equal in my mind. Hope some of you enjoy this as much as I did!
