_childDocuments_.review: I've been chasing that Until Dawn high throughout the Dark Picture Anthology. Between PS4 and pc, I've played them all. If you're looking for a short answer, this game is about on par with Man of Medan and Little Hope; a little better in some regards, worse in a number of others. The short answer is no, in my opinion, I do not recommend this game.Honestly, I would wish all three installments of the Dark Picture Anthology out of existence if it just got me Until Dawn 2. House of Ashes suffers from the same issues as its predecessors along with a few new glaring problems.First off, this is not a horror game; it's a short walk, clunky walk between cutscenes/QTEs with some light third person shooter elements. The only time it gives up control and lets you move around is when it wants you to search a small area for a few collectibles that add literally no context because the entire story is spoon fed to you. Even just moving around or getting your flashlight to point where you want it to is a chore sometimes.The story was meh. It's not a good sign when it feels like a short game is dragging on too long. The characters all felt shallow mostly because the game was so anxious to get us back into the action that it didn't spend any time fleshing out the sacrificial meat bags beyond singular qualities meant to stir up some small drama later on.These yearly installments, they're just not working out. It's like they stripped everything that made Until Dawn great out of them and then jammed in multiplayer to fill the void. Seriously, if you can't play a horror game alone, then maybe the genre isn't right for you. I feel like, same with everything, that this franchise has just gone the way of easy profits, selling cheap thrills and an underwhelming experience so that they can appeal to the widest demographic.Edit: I'm terrible about replying to comments so I figured I'd just add one or two additional points to try and clear up some things in the original review. I'm not looking for an actual Until Dawn 'sequel'. I understand that story is cut and dry, leaving no room for any natural continuation. Rather, what I would like is an installment that was as well thought out, planned and executed as Until Dawn, not something squeezed out annually. In my opinion, I thought Until Dawn was great because it was campy, the characters were fairly shallow but they filled out their tropes well, and there were plenty of memorable scenes that I enjoyed enough to remember. The story branched just enough so that it didn't get wildly out of control. It was, indeed, campy, but its writing was cohesive in such a way that the Dark Picture Anthology has not yet seemed capable of replicating. I suppose this could be one of the drawbacks of trying to adapt multiplayer into a broad, branching storyline which is already challenging enough to do well. In my opinion, the Dark Picture Anthology has been a classic case of quantity over quality.

_childDocuments_.review: its great overall but has plotholes that leave you wondering. You just accept it's a game but it seems with every iteration they take less account for realism.. which isn't too bad but helps keep it a little grounded, which is little to begin with. Choices are what bring the game to life and they do it well. You are rewarded for successes, and penalties on failures. QTE's are genius and their slow-mo scenes are the best ones I relish greatly. Camera angles are wonderful as always. Moving around is better than clicking so that's nice (as 2nd one was click only). If you're missing a character it seems some scenes lose a bit of their flow, again isn't really too bad but helps keep the realism in check. I was missing one person (spoiler free) and the two characters just hung their on a camera angle for 10 seconds or so.. clearly the game was checking to see who was alive, what choice was made, the game logic I assume. I must have broken the chain so poorly haha. But to have them sit in silence with no expression really detaches a moment and all feeling, you're reminded it's a video game. I liked it and it's great, Dark Pictures is a great successor to TellTale (not related to each other but they made similar style games).  The one thing I hated though, it's clear that some or certain characters (no spoilers) had plot armor just because they were absolutely needed later on (maybe if I had someone alive, not sure). Along with the guns, I understand it's not a first person shooter, but the sound of the guns were really off to me.  I know I probably am the only person to notice and pay attention, but they almost never reload. It shows them reloading very rarely but they fire off so many mags and it does lose realism here as they seemingly have infinite mags (until the end). Yes, vidya gayme, but it wouldn't hurt to try. It's why i still vote this yes / positive. Despite having plot holes, small game engine logic hiccups (rarely), and a bit of realism being detached, it still is a very enjoyable game. It looks great with Unreal, runs smoothly, and you can tell they put their passion into their work.

_childDocuments_.review: A very brutal experience filled with tough decisions.Quite frankly, this game was a lot more character driven than the previous Dark Pictures entries. If anything, it's the closest the series has come to mimicking Until Dawn (which I consider the pinnacle for SMGames).Characters actually grow and develop personal relationships with each other (or a lack thereof) depending on your choices. This makes you give a damn about them and their story. THIS IS WHAT DARK PICTURES NEEDS TO CONTINUE DOING!If I had any negatives, it's that Dark Picture games are such pale imitations of Until Dawn in their pacing. These games are very simply boiled down to Intro Flashback, Introduce Characters, Get Chased for 4 Straight Hours, Finale.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes, sadly, fails to meet the expectations, serving as a disappointing entry that Supermassive Games desperately needed to be a redeeming one. While the game does offer some accessibility options to make it more inclusive, it counteracts these efforts with controversial political themes, cumbersome camera handling, an uninspiring cast, and numerous bugs. What should have been a thrilling and politically intriguing experience turns out to be a lackluster affair that leaves players feeling uninspired. Supermassive fans and the horror genre as a whole deserve a better offering, and, regrettably, this dark plunge falls short of recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: I write this review as an Iraqi/Mesopotamian myself.. and as a gamerPROS:- this has been the most anticipated game for me this whole year, and I was in tears of joy when I first saw its announcement simply because it's the first and only piece of modern media that has FINALLY adopted our mythology and civilizations, it's the most ancient and most influential in human history yet it's completely overlooked, call me biased but I give it thumbs up simply because of this one reason- the story overall is amazing, really engaging and tense with a lot of twists and variety for your decisions- graphics and performance are really good and very well optimized- acting is top-notch (ONLY for the American cast)MIX: - the characters overall are ok, I didn't really feel as much emotional connection to them as other interactive narrative games, but maybe that's just meCONS:- even though I love that it revolves around our myths, I HATE the fact that the baseline of the story is the war AGAIN, with typical American soldiers protagonists... couldn't have they made the protagonists the actual locals of this land!!!! or at least if American they'd be tourists, humanitarians, researchers, or whatever other than soldiers- WTF is up with Arabic voice actors!!!! all of them were Egyptians NOT Iraqis... it was easier for me to understand their dialogue through English subtitles... Arabic is NOT the same everywhere, it's like they brought a Spanish actor saying his lines in Spanish for a Portuguese character- following the previous point, the cultural adaptation of Iraqis and Iraq is kinda lazy and stereotypical, it feels like there was not a single Iraqi in the studio team... which is really disappointing for a game about Iraq, they could've at least made a limited contract for an Iraqi during the development- controls are a bit janky, and sometimes the camera gets stuck and I have to pause and resume to fix it... but I assume it'll be patched quickly- SPOILER WARNING: OVERALL:it's a good game, and I highly recommend it, with both my biased and unbiased opinion... there were a lot of things that could've been better, but I give my sincerest thanks to the studio for at least adopting our mythos and civilizations

_childDocuments_.review: "Long ago I met a blind poet who impressed upon me these wise words: 'Long is the way and hard, that out of Hell leads up to Light."Set at the end of the Iraq war, a team of four special forces operatives, an Air Force Colonel, and a CIA field officer venture underground searching for weapons of mass destruction but uncover an ancient Sumerian temple that houses a giant hive of bloodthirsty monstrous creatures;  The six of them must work together to make it out alive.A significant improvement from the last game in virtually every aspect.  House of Ashes is so much more engaging and captivating than Little Hope and you actually have the motivation to keep playing this time around.  The game is packed full of visually striking environments and locations and more compelling character dynamics and I love how they attempt to tie together a present-day military conflict with an ancient civilization along with the science fiction-type origin of the creatures.  It’s a great blend of edge-of-your-seat horror and action-packed shooting sequences.  Also, there’s so much more chemistry with all the main characters and they give you the choice to play out all their interpersonal struggles exactly how you want;  The relationship between Jason and Salim is easily the best and it works so well not only for your satisfaction but for the outcome of the story.  Obviously, the core mechanics of the game are pretty much identical to all the other games but this time around they put a subtle twist on it with all the action scenes and there are way more aim-to-shoot quick-time events which I loved.  Another thing I really liked was the whole Predator movie vibe they tried to do and they succeeded perfectly, but some people may find it to be derivative but again it’s a great homage.  The only bad thing I can say is this game probably has the most bugs I’ve seen in the series;  There’s so many scenes where the textures never fully render and sometimes when you inspect an object and pull away, the camera just stays focused on it which is pretty annoying.  Overall though, this game was excellent and easily makes up for how boring and disappointing Little Hope was.House of Ashes is definitely the best game in the series and gives the player such a unique blend of action packed shooting and creepy horror sequences, along with a compelling mixed historical narrative and a really intriguing sci-fi twist.  If you like the Dark Pictures even a little bit, you’ll love this game.  By far my favourite in the series.         7/10

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5/5Probably my favorite game out of the Dark Pictures Anthology. It's definitely not as scary as others and the jump scares are much less frequent. However, the game is significantly better compared to others when it comes to the characters and the writing overall, with a pretty interesting plot. It's still pretty bland, but at least the second half escalates a bit and is actually exciting to play. The time and place setting is good, and even though the characters are very dislikeable at first, their stories improve amusingly and they do end up as some of the most memorable characters out of the series. The same quality is put in setting up and explaining the story of the evil enemies. Their reveal is very "classic horror"-esque, showing only glimpses of the creature and building the suspense and tension. QTE's are pretty classic and there are some harder sequences but nothing worth bashing your head over it, even though later towards the end a death could come with each failed QTE.The graphics are very good and the mocap animations are solid, with some visual bugs that happen unoften.Camera movement is still kinda wonky on keyboard/mouse but it works.It takes about 5 hours to fully complete the game so I really recommend it if you're in for an interesting horror experience.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first - the only real impact you have in this game are relationships in between main characters and some QTEs. Otherwise... I would say it's a movie in which your word has a certain weight. If you expect something similar to Detroit: Become Human or Life is Strange games... you'll be disappointed. But I think, that at this point, everyone knows what to except from Dark Pictures Anthology.And let's move on to the game itself - it was HELLA A RIDE, not gonna lie! I haven't had a chance to play Man of Medan yet (I only saw gameplay couple years back), but I have played Little Hope. I had expectations about the story, about the characters... and I was left with open mouth and totally differently paced game than I expected. Was it scary? No, not really. Was it surprising? Definitely! I had a chance to play with a really dear friend of mine and I enjoyed every single second. Especially because both of us can get stressed over little things and then panic (I'll be honest - I was the panicking one usually and he came over to save my poor ass multiple times - thank you for that!). I really enjoyed playing this game and I think it's a great way how to spend an evening with your friend(s), when you're bored of watching TV series and movies all the time or playing the same multiplayer game over and over again. House of Ashes can make your evening different and magical and that's what counts. So I definitely recommend. I hope you'll enjoy the outcome as much as me and my dear friend did!

Of course the developers once again never fails on good storytelling, though the two things I oppose about House of Ashes is the game - at least in my own opinion - has very minimal jumpscares. Sure the game itself has some scary moments and the creatures were creepy, but unlike Until Dawn, the atmosphere just doesn't feel like how a horror game should be. Mostly the game was really bright, despite my brightness being low, it lost sense of some parts in the game to be scary, but nonetheless, still a fun game to play. _childDocuments_.review: The best out of the first 3. Still not Until Dawn levels of quality but much closer this time.In terms of characters, Jason in particular is very well written, and Salim is also really good. The other 3 main characters are serviceable, but nothing special. I did manage to kill one of them off pretty early, so I'm under the impression that I missed out on some content there.The plot is significantly more coherent than the previous two entries and has good pacing throughout. Dialogue is a bit hit or miss, I didn't care for the unnecessary love triangle thrown into the plot, and there's the odd bit of daft dialogue about the Iraq war (the game is set in 2003, but the dialogue is written with the knowledge we have now) but it's not enough to detract from the experience.Overall it's a good horror film in the format of a game. Just don't play on the top difficulty, unless you want all the characters to die because you can't do a QTE in 4 milliseconds.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Pictures Anthology as a whole, is everything I want in a series. Reasonable play lengths to travel through immersive stories filled with difficult choices that matter. Sometimes these moments 'hit' more than others across the series and with House of Ashes it hits almost the entire time. Compared to the other entries, Man of Medan may still take the #1 spot for being the original and for 'spook' as well as twist. The issue is that once that twist is told, it loses some of the magic. It's given a very close run for it's money by House of Ashes and the benefit is that it will retain much of it's magic forever because it didn't rely on any gimmicks. The characters are interesting enough. The plot is actually pretty damn good even when it starts to swing for the fences. The quick time events could have been more plentiful and difficult (but I'm a sucker for a QTE when I know others aren't fans). I think my only issue is that there are objects and notes that don't seem to really pay off and you spend a bit of time wandering from piece to piece reading or inspecting for no reason. That being said, this is the first episode in the series which reaches back to try and pull together the 'world' as a whole. Overall a solid way to spend your time and money, high recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far the best addition to the Dark Pictures Anthology. The main story is compelling, the characters are rich and in-depth, and the dynamics between the characters are complex and interesting; I really felt driven to helping the characters to survive the game.My only complaint, as with every Dark Pictures game is that the decisions don't impact the overall story. You still get the same handful of scenes every play-through, just with different dialogue options depending on what you've done throughout the game. I'd love for one of these games to add additional scenes that showed up depending on what decisions you made throughout the game.Overall though, I love this game and it's my favourite in the series so far! I give this a solid 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have never seen such an atmosphere anywhere else, it frightens and makes you shiver without screamers, it makes you want and be afraid to play this story, the game frightens you with its atmosphere of helplessness and the true, ancient evil that lurks somewhere in the depths!Paranoia and a feeling of hopelessness will haunt you, and monsters will expect you to make a mistake, which you will make sooner or later under the influence of difficult choices and they will not forgive it! The darkness of the underground Sumerian temple puts pressure on you and forces you to constantly turn around in the hope of seeing the source of the constant rustling and crackling, but you will see nothing and will not see anything else... ever...The entire line of The Dark Pictures stories with their own unique aftertaste! Everyone should read this story!

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes is an entry in The Dark Pictures Anthology.. my adventure in this kind of games continues after playing The Quarry i needed something similar and this was the obvious choice because i already had it on my library for a really long time. House of Ashes follows a squad of marine soldiers who find themselves trapped in an ancient temple, the story revolves around their struggle to survive and find a way out. The narrative is great and i don't want to unveil too much of it but expect horror and a lot of tough choices. Simple decisions can lead to branching paths and different endings for our story. The gameplay is simplistic ,with quick-time events where you need to press your mouse or aim your cursor to an enemy. The exploration and navigation part feels immersive, the caves and the sounds makes you feel vulnerable.I really liked the graphics..the cinematic experience is great. With a dark lovecraftian motif..the temple and the network of caves where the shadows are at home creates a tense envinronment and perfect world design for our adventure. Not everything is perfect, the similarities with The Quarry unfortunately are dominant in this genre..i wished for more control in combat scenarios. I was so annoyed when a single missed key lead to a character death but maybe they will fix that in future titles.However there are some positives that really stand out and thats character development and background stories,i feel they did a good job covering those. Another thing i enjoyed is finding journal pages and the cutscenes from the past really helped to understand the origins of this story.In conclusion this is a great narrative game that i enjoyed a lot , after playing this i'm interested in the entire anthology because even if the gameplay is not great the story alone makes it worth!My ScoresStory 10Graphics 10Gameplay 5Sound 9Overall 8.5

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played any of the previous games in the Dark Pictures Anthology you've got a pretty good idea of what to expect when you play this.  The environments and story are easily the best Supermassive Games has put out so far.  For anyone that's been to Iraq during 2003 or after, keep in mind that this touches on some of the aspects of the conflict there at the time.  There's a lot that's frustratingly difficult to process, due to the portrayal of the characters.  There are some moments and actions that could trigger some bad memories.  The characters are the most irritating bunch I've spent a Thursday night with.  They have the personality of a wet sock and are just irritatingly annoying for much of the game.  That's problematic as the end goal is to keep as many of of them alive as possible.  Thankfully, Salim is a down-to earth guy and overall a pretty decent person.  Most everyone else feels designed to not be liked, and it probably isn't so bad if you let them all die.Voice acting is good, and is only thrown off by the valley of the dolls expressions of the characters.  Everyone looks so stiff and it was really off putting.  Aside from that, graphically the game looks fantastic.  Maybe it's because I'm a big fan of anything mythological and ancient civilizations blow my mind - but this game blew it out of the park on the environment.  Music is good but largely forgettable.I went in blind for this game but treated it a bit like the last 2.  Don't do that.  At least, don't treat it anything like the last 2.  Take everything you see as legit, and act accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: It makes me very sad, but its not a game i will recommend and just to be clear I love the series, I even pre-order the game, I even borrow from a friend a ps4 to manage to play until dawn. Played first Man of Medan and after that I had to play everything from Supermassive Games. I suggest to get it on Sales when its like below 10 euro or something, just for the collection. If you haven't play the rest games, just go get the others they are amazing!Why I don't recommend this game? For start I really really tried to find good things about this game (comparison to previous games, Man of Medan, Until Dawn and Little Hope). Pro:Graphics was great...From the main protagonists... Salim was ok...New mechanics? They added a new camera navigation. Was ok for me, my gf had problems with it, so its 50-50 on that one.And I guess we are done. Negatives:The major issue for me... Its a Horror game and me and my gf we had like 2-3 jump scares and that's all. No tension in most of the game and mainly not a Horror game. Not even once i got chills, nothing. So big big fail on that part.Characters? OMG... Except Salim... I wasn't really care for anyone if they survive or not. No character develop. One guy that was whining all the time, one woman with authority issues and a bf with issues again... and lastly a marine guy with no history, just a normal security person, more or less. I was more interest for the support characters that the main ones. The main story? ffs... no logic at all. I never understand why, even they had the climbing gear they just don't go up and they keep going down... no logic at all. As for the ending I wont spoil it, by far the worst from all the games and by end I mean the way they manage to get out... anyway...And last thing... I really don't get the logic on level difficulty. You have forgiving, challenging and lethal... so mainly easy, normal and hard... why normal has only 1 button to play with? all actions was on X... in forgiving you don't have actions? wtf? Anyway... that was pretty bad in our gameplay because we figure it out around half or more of the game and wasn't a turning back. Just start on lethal and if you stuck with 1 guy then switch it to "normal".ClosureMy main feeling for this specific game is that Covid did the job done, at least I wont to hope. Probably company couldn't do all the testing they wanted, especially on the horror reactions part, and it was something like... just do that because we need to publish it or something. I would prefer if they just push it back for 2,3 or even 6 months back and have a result we expect.Really hope the next game is better and even I was really disappointed by this game I still looking forward to play the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good story, although not scary at all, some tense moments in your first playthrough though. The playable characters are a bit flat, but not terrible. You'll probably only care about two characters, be neutral to another two, and dislike the last.The achievements take a lot of time and playthroughs/chapter selects to get if you want all 30, as many are mutually exclusive and/or require a lot of setup, so you have sit through all the unskippable cutscenes until you get your payoff. Make sure to find a good guide and plan the whole thing out if you want to do this. Also there isn't much actual gameplay, it's mostly watching cutscenes and making a couple of dialogue choices, and then some quicktimes (there were lots of points where I thought there could have been a quicktime, just for some interaction, and there wasn't), and walking about a little bit. That's kind of standard for all the Dark Pictures games I believe though. Definitely interesting, and has good replayability of course, there's actually a good amount of variation in how things can play out in ways that aren't obvious. All in all I'd give it a 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure i'm going to get obliterated by some fans of this series since this game was my first experience with it so please take that into consideration whilst reading. This game absolutely fails everywhere where it should have been great. The gameplay presents itself in a similar way to the tearjerking, timeless, and incredible masterwork that was Detroit Become Human. It's a realtime choices matter game interspersed with some open world and quicktime events centered around a story. A game of this format has no business being set in the Iraq war. That being said, I like the way they portrayed and designed the NPCs as they look exactly like American troops and Iraqi soldiers respectively and I could tell the devs did their research on the Iraq war to portray it as realistic and inoffensive as possible.  So that is a major pro in my eyes. However, the bold step they took in putting a mythology centered horror game in the modern world just falls flat on it's face. They would have been better off setting this full in Ancient Iraq or even Ancient Egypt. An ancient mythology game set in an ancient setting is obviously formulaic but it would have worked better instead of forcing it on a modern setting. Also in Detroit Become Human, the main characters were all likable and easy to sympathize with while the villains had zero redeeming qualities, they at least had a personality and believable motivation. Here none of the characters are remotely likable and are just plain offensive. The setting and designs are great but the characters are just bad and completely forgetable. All and all, I respect the devs going for accuracy in how the world looked and felt but they failed to bring any magic regarding the characters and story to the table. It could have been a good game in a rarely explored setting but the lack of good characters and story completely not right for the setting is what kills it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: - Strong points : - Salim's character- An effective French version- Rhythm better controlled than its predecessors- Catchy atmosphere- An interesting plot- Visually successful- Weak points :- Decors less varied than before- Persistent moody tones (at the same time, underground...)- Some sound bugs- Uneven handwriting- Some annoying charactersSummary : House of Ashes does not distort the philosophy of Supermassive Games. While retaining the cinematic staging of The Dark Pictures saga, this third episode now offers a 360° camera and better integrated QTEs. Thanks to its controlled pace, its claustrophobic atmosphere and its interesting plot, it surpasses its predecessors despite its flaws (uneven writing, caricatural characters, frozen shooting phases, etc.). For anyone who enjoys interactive experiences of the genre, this latest iteration of the anthology is worth a look.15/20

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with games like these is that you really can't say much in a review without spoiling it, so I'll try my best. I've only played Until Dawn and this game so far, so I'm hoping Medan and Little Hope will be a lot more enjoyable like Until Dawn. In this game, all the characters besides maybe Salim are just extremely cringy, and half of the dialogue doesn't even seem like real human interaction. I swear some of the options you can say to people would make 0 sense at all, and be the last thing on your mind to say. I honestly let some of them die because I was annoyed with their presence, which shouldn't be a factor in something like this. 90% of this game is a movie, which is good to some people, and bad to some people. Also, most of the collectibles are just along the main path now, leaving the player with no desire to look around. The endings in this are so dumb, leaving you not getting any of the achievements in 50% of playthroughs if you literally make 1 mistake at the beginning of the game. The only reason I was still playing was to get the achievements, and I didn't even get them because of a briefing choice. Until Dawn just had better characters, and a better story, with better gameplay. I don't even know how, because you'd think a scenario like the one they've painted in this game, would surmount some 20 year olds dying in the woods. The ideal player for this game would probably be a veteran, (thank you for your service) because all of these characters are so damn boring with only chatter for the army or for Rachel. Only one I liked and tried to keep the longest was Merwin. That guy to me was the only interesting character in the game, and they shafted the hell out of his character arc. I got gifted all of the Dark Picture games from a friend, but I'd say this game is maybe worth $10-$15 to be honest.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start of with saying that I absolutly loved the two previous games in this series. Man of Medan was really nice and kept you on your toes, while trying to figure out what's going on. Little hope was a really well blended mix of horror and story, although crashing alot. So expectations launching House of Ashes were high.Story wise, House of Ashes is Okay. There is a story, but it's a bit hard following along with, especially compared to the previous games. They also trew a couple of curve balls at you, making you have to change how to think a bit compared to the previous games and I love it! Unlike Little Hope there are no crashes or problems like that here.However, House of Ashes feels rushed. One character picks up a pipe and uses as his weapon. The animation however is that he just equip and unequip it by moving it over his shoulder. The weapon does not connect to anything at his back and more so just floats in the air there. The same character also has a lighter instead of a flashlight. A lighter, which shoots it light forward like a flashlight, instead of lighting up the general area around you.When you click to inspect something, it's not uncommon for your character to walk a circle around before stopping by the item again and slowly inspecting it.Finally, the camera angles in this games feels quite weird from time to time, with the camera looking one way, you moving another and the light shining in a 3rd directions.The game is okay, but it's not on level with the games before and it does feel rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotta say, I didn't expect something of this caliber from Supermassive Games. I've played Until Dawn some years ago, and, while pretty looking and entertaining enough for an interactive movie, it was just a bit short from being a truly great game in my eyes. The characters just weren't that well written for you to truly root for them. And then Man of Medan came out and it was a step down in every direction, and I thought they've completely lost their touch. Boy, was I wrong.I gotta tell you, back in the first third of the game I wasn't really feeling the cookie cutter characters (even if they had the least amount of bullsh!t dialogue), and couldn't possibly imagine I'd be rooting this hard for them to survive. The chemistry between some of them really comes together towards the end of the game. A gameplay of simple QTE prompts became amplified by tension of real stakes - my homies making out of it alive. The plot, despite cliched beginnings, weaved and unfolded in new, truly unexpected ways, and had me way more engaged than previous escapades of teens at mountain resort and ghost ship.And visuals, man, that's gotta be one of the most good looking games out there right now. Supermassive Games perfected the faces, volumetric lighting and depth of field effect. The artistic direction is also worth commending - I couldn't keep my finger from screenshot button for five minutes, the environments and clever use of special effects is really something to behold. And for how great it all looks it also runs surprisingly well. I think I've had more framerate issues with rather drab looking ship of Man of Medan than I did with this game's spectacular looking caverns and tombs.A solid interactive movie that I'm not ashamed to recommend to any horror enthusiast. I'm looking forward for this studio's next and final Dark Pictures chapter now, and am also gonna check the Little Hope chapter soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying that I genuinely don't mind whether these games are  good or bad. I absolutely love this genre, and I'll always buy and support them because I feel like there's something unique about Supermassive's games that other franchises fail to capture. With that out of the way, I think this game is pretty decent.Set in Iraq following the US invasion, it effectively portrays the impact of 9/11 on Americans. It's interesting to see the character arc development throughout the story; some characters change their views, while others don't. The story conveys commendable values and keeps you thoroughly engaged.The gameplay primarily consists of your standard QTEs and decision-making. I do wish they'd allow us to skip cutscenes, so I can 100% this game. There is also potential for a 2nd playthrough in the Curator's Cut, where you get to play the story from other perspectives and make different decisions. The performance is consistently solid, never dipping below 70 FPS. In terms of graphics, it's on par with previous Dark Pictures games.In my honest opinion, this game deserves a spot at the top of Supermassive's games. The jump scares are superior to those in previous installments and don't come across as cheap. With that and the tense QTEs, the game is sure to keep you on your toes.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous graphics with high quality models and textures. Ambient lighting and visual effects like particles, flairs and fogs give a push to the dark atmosphere.- Impressive world design with some massive blockbuster sceneries.- Nice direction and photography. Overall it's very cinematic with high quality cut scenes.- Good animations overall. Pretty convincing facial animations that reveal the emotional states of each character.- Nice sound design with convincing ambient, environmental and especially battles' sounds.- Cool music that seems to fit any given moment. Great heavy metal music during some parts.- It has some replayability value. You can try many playthroughs to watch some alternative endings and see what's gonna happen to the characters if you make different decisions.- It's a nice, smooth co-op experience. You can play it with friends either online or locally.- At last there are no annoying bugs of corrupted save files or infinite loading screens like the previous episodes of the series.The bad- It's awfully similar to its predecessors. Same pace, same gameplay mechanics, same well worn, boring QTEs, No innovations at all. I get it, it's the same series but you have to try to offer a new challenge.- There is almost no story. Its predecessors had flaws but at least they had a lot of mystery and you were wondering what's going on till the end. Here it reveals to you the monsters right from the beginning and you just run and fight in order to survive. it's a shallow action experience with weak atmosphere and no mystery at all.- Except of the last part, it is much less interactive than the previous games of the series. Cut scenes and just passively watching is way to much. Also, there is only a few of free exploration and most of the interactions happen via predefined animations during cut scenes. It's more of a big movie than an actual game and it becomes boring after a while.- Dull characters with flat personalities and shallow backstories. Dialogues and texts seem simplistic with a lot of cliché parts. It doesn't help you to love the protagonists so you end up not really caring who dies or lives.- There are some control mechanics issues. It's very slow and not responsive when picking up objects, characters tends to block the way of one another, while pathfinding and collisions aren't the best.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a game like this before, so I wasn't sure exactly what to expect. It's mostly a cinematic-style adventure, in which you decide how characters respond to each other to shape the story. Interspersed with that are sections where you explore areas looking for clues and figuring out how to proceed, as well as action sections fill with Quick-Time Events and similar fast response mini-games.The strengths of this game are the way it builds the characters and their relationships over time, and the control you have in shaping both. By the end of the game, I really cared about these people. The story, which starts out as a simple war tale, also gets surprisingly big as you go, until the end had a few surprising reveals.My playtime is a little inflated, but I probably completed the entire thing in about ten hours. There were so many branching moments in the narrative that I can definitely see myself coming back to this game at some point and replaying it with different choices to see how that affects the story. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: At five hours and close to the finish mark on my first playthrough, I have to say that I'm really enjoying the game.This is definitely an 'interactive movie' more than some other games but it is well-acted, well-told, and constantly engaging.  There are moments of excitement and tension that really hit home and the pace is kept up well enough that I never grow bored.The only drawback is that, as an interactive movie, some of the characterization can be inconsistent when your decisions don't mesh up with what the writers wanted.  The worst example of this being the continued tension between two characters near the end, after they've saved one another's lives, and seemed to make a connection, over and over again.  That, and some of the 'choices' don't really mean anything as the outcome is the same either way.  Those things aside, the story is worth participating in and doing so has gone a long way to draw me into the experience. The short length (about 6-7 hours seems to be the norm on here) means that the usual price might feel a bit high, but definitely get this when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A Gripping Thriller with Unforgettable Choices - House of Ashes House of Ashes is a masterpiece of interactive storytelling that seamlessly blends horror, suspense, and decision-making to deliver an unforgettable gaming experience. From the moment you step into the depths of the ancient Sumerian temple, you are gripped by a sense of impending dread that never lets up until the very end.The game's graphics are stunning, with detailed environments that draw you into the eerie world beneath the desert sands. The sound design is top-notch, creating a tense atmosphere that keeps you on edge as you navigate the dark corridors and underground chambers.One of the standout features of House of Ashes is its branching narrative, where your choices have real consequences on the fates of the characters. Every decision you make feels weighty and impactful, leading to multiple endings that encourage replayability.The characters are well-written and fleshed out, each with their own motivations and secrets that are slowly revealed as the story unfolds. The voice acting is superb, adding depth and emotion to the already engaging storyline.The gameplay is a perfect mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and intense action sequences that keep you engaged from start to finish. The tension is palpable during the game's heart-pounding moments, and you'll find yourself holding your breath as you make split-second decisions that can mean life or death for your characters.In conclusion, House of Ashes is a must-play for fans of horror games and interactive storytelling. With its gripping narrative, stunning visuals, and meaningful choices, it sets a new standard for the genre. Prepare yourself for a journey into darkness unlike any other – you won't be able to put this game down until you've uncovered all of its chilling secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Until Dawn, this is definitely their strongest game since.The story is fine, doesn't quite hold up to UD but given this is around half as long that's probably to be expected - it's similarly as campy, but with a more serious overtone given the nature of the game (vs a bunch of teens in the mountains).On the whole, this definitely shows that Supermassive can take the Dark PIctures series and any future titles (The Quarry, hopefully) in an improved direction from Until Dawn. This game, despite being shorter, already features more 'branching' paths based on your decisions than UD did - you can end up with considerably different outcomes resulting from your previous decisions/indecisions to a level I never saw in UD, which definitely makes your choices feel much more weighty.If you blitz through, probably 5 hours, I explored a fair bit and likely ended up with some longer cinematic sequences on account of keeping everyone alive, which probably added a couple of hours on to the playtime total.Either way, I would definitely recommend it if you're a fan of UD, and if you liked the earlier Dark Pictures instalments then this is 100% the strongest of the 3 by a large margin.At full price I would only recommend it if you plan on using the Curator's mode or getting friends to play it as well, else wait til it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think that any review I write will be enough to describe just how amazing the game is. After I finished it I thought to myself; "this is everything a game should be". I'm a big fan of interactive choices genre games & this kind of immersive experience just can't be found anywhere else. Each choice ACTUALLY mattered and the relationships of the characters played a huge role as well. These games intrigue me so much because of the variant of pathing. Two endings or twenty endings are both fine, but it's seeing the way events can occur with different characters, the way conversations and decision points can unfold differently, that really intrigues me. I played many games from that same genre- but this is by far the best one.As I am also a huge history nerd, the lore of the game itself was so fascinating to me. I love that the dark pictures anthology actually do their research- keeping the player on edge with every 'secret' being found. Every note and entry were so interesting to read, and if you are a fan of such themes, you will be tempted to go back and re-read all of it even after the game is done like me.As for a multiplayer experience (movie night)- this game has the coolest features I have ever seen. The way it switches angles mid combat to the other player, the way you can actually assign characters to each player before the game begins- it was all so good. The action in the game only added to the overall experience, and me and my girlfriend had a blast playing this. We loved all the characters and actually wanted to do everything in our power to save them. There wasn't a single bad character, and as the story progressed; so did the characters. The realistic aspect of a group being stuck in such difficult situation is what got me. Each character handled the situation in their own way; and I found it very appealing to see.The graphics and character designs were incredible, there were absolutely no bugs or crashes (PC), the soundtrack was epic, the story is amazing and captivating in every aspect. I will definitely replay it and try to get all the different possibilities; something that didn't happen with the previous games in the anthology as I simply uninstalled them after I was done playing. But this game draws you in and leaving you with a taste for more. (Also, )As I mentioned at the start of the review, nothing I say will do this game justice or explain just how great it is. I will say, however, if you get all the four games in season 1 of the anthology- play them by order. That way, you will definitely appreciate House Of Ashes a lot more and understand why this game is by far the best one yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game a 4/5. The story was interesting enough to keep the player interested in the roughly 5 hours of play time. Note that this game is meant to be played through many times, especially for those wanting to earn all of the achievements or see all of the endings. The voice acting was pretty well done, but there were moments where the tone of the voice did not match the action happening on the screen (e.g. exasperated breath from climbing/running, Sadness/sobbing in times of fear/sorrow, etc.). Graphically, the character renders are beautiful with detail really showing through on the characters' clothing and facial expressions. However, the amount of detail in the characters made the quality of the foreground environments lacking; running up a playdough set of stairs often broke my immersion at times when I was meant to feel fear or tension.  The animation overall was decent, though I noticed moments where the characters moved and contorted like they had a stick up their...you know, and the movements of the mouth and eyes, while very rare, seemed buggy and unnatural. With all of that said, I think the game is very well worth the price, especially if you are a fan on the anthology and enjoy playing these short-play through games multiple times.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 85/100- Action is a fun change of pace compared to the others in the anthology. For reference, I prefer the more slow paced creepy style but this game was just as fun. I played 3/4 of the games back to back (HOA -> LH -> TDIM) and it was nice to have two slow burn creepy games and one be an action packed shooter. I found this ratio perfect, once I get through MOM maybe this opinion will change. - The relationship dynamic of this group is really interesting, there's some good heartfelt moments. I really enjoyed how the backstory was slowly built up for all the characters, this created a good emotional climax.- The decisions felt weak in this game. To me, felt like I had 5+ attempts to right a wrong. Oops messed up a quick time event, don't worry there's probably going to be a few more to save that character  they will just magically survive. Said something stupid and pissed someone off, well, they'll probably still save you. Maybe I walked some golden path and my decisions overall made this seem more outspoken than it is. There really is a lot of decisions to be made and I can't really pinpoint if it's my doing or the devs so I'm classifying this as meh rather than bad.- There's definitely some cringe voice lines and awkward delivery at a few parts. - N/AA little minor backstory, I have a pretty mentally taxing job and recently I've been a little burnt out on playing games where I actually have to do things but I still wanted to play games. I'm weird yes I know but I was in the mood for something that played like an interactive movie so I could sit back and enjoy the show but still participate. This game, and the whole anthology, is that to a tee. If you're like me and in those same shoes, I would highly recommend not only House of Ashes but the whole Dark Pictures Anthology.In my opinion, this wasn't my favorite of the anthology but it was a great addition. If you're looking for something that plays like an interactive action movie, this is probably the game for you. I felt like the action was done well and the relationships in this game contributed to a great overall story line that kept me invested. I had a few moments where I had to shake my head and grit my teeth at some questionable writing but because I was so invested in the underlying story of these characters, it didn't pull me out too far. If action isn't what you're looking for then I'd recommend checking out some of the other games in the anthology.I wasn't a huge fan of how the decision making mechanic felt in this game compared to some of the others but honestly, it really didn't phase me too much. I think somewhere between the action nature of this game and me being so invested in the characters, I was honestly happy the game coddled me in some situations. Overall I had a lot of fun playing this game. I played solo while my wife and a friend watched me play it over a discord stream and that was a fun dynamic being able to talk about the game and discuss it in real time. I would wager based on my experience that a co-op play through would also be a great way to enjoy the game. If you're just planning on playing completely solo, then you're also in for a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: Arguably the scariest of the Dark Pictures games thus far.   Not that these games are really "about" scares first and foremost - they're far more concerned with narrative and character than your usual horror fare - but it's a fact worth noting just the same. The often claustrophobically shallow field of view is partly responsible for this; at first, it felt like the "camera" was zoomed  too far in on the character's backs, but once I hit the caves/ancient ruins that are the setting for the majority of this game's action, I understood. It certainly helped ramp up the tension at times, making it feel like danger could be lurking around every fresh corner (something I hadn't really felt in the series prior to now).   Something this game unfortunately  a little, in comparison to earlier entries: the fruits of exploration. There's a bit less stuff to "examine" this time around, especially early on in the game; "secrets" being particularly scarce in the first few hours. This gradually picks up as the story progresses, but anyone who's a firm fan of Supermassive Games' tendency towards a very modern approach to "adventure" gaming may be slightly disappointed by this game's initial tendency toward plot momentum over meticulous exploration. Other players may, of course, warmly welcome this slight change of pace.   It's certainly the most action-packed of the Dark Pictures games to date, and should thereby delight fans of Until Dawn or Resident Evil-style games who've been feeling like this franchise hasn't been fast-paced or gun-happy enough for their liking. Clearly, the odds of this being your most or least favourite game in the series to date will depend somewhat on your own tastes. I'm personally going to proclaim this my fave so far, mostly due to the more sophisticated/profound choices you're forced to make (this one isn't just about "save as many characters as possible at all costs"), and the uniformly excellent acting throughout (even performers who were a bit so-so in earlier entries are perfectly effective here). It still falls a bit shy of the overall brilliance of Until Dawn...but at this rate, we might get there yet!   I'm still loving this series, any-which-way, and hope it remains an annual event for years to come. (The next one looks like more of a serial killer thriller, so you can't accuse Supermassive of skimping on the variety!)   Oh, and as a final bonus to those using keyboard and mouse: the default Quick-Time controls are just two buttons this time, rather than four, meaning you'll hopefully suffer fewer cheap deaths due to your shoddy reflexes! (Emphasis on "hopefully"!)   Verdict: 9.5/10.(PS If you enjoyed this review, feel free to check out my two Curator pages: Cheers!)

_childDocuments_.review: War is not the only horror you'll face.Story: Set during the Iraq war, you play as multiple characters. A task force is formed to attack a possible secret chemical weapons lab belonging to Saddam, but once you wide up there a massive sinkhole opens up which claims everyone into an underground ruin where enemies must become ally's to survive a new evil.The story of House of Ashes is incredibly awesome to say the least. Everything from the choices you make, character interactions and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane plot twist are just incredible. The game has a slightly slower pace than the other two, but once it picks up it just keeps getting more insane and I was just having a blast. Everything about the plot improves on the structure the first two games had. The characters are a lot more likable across the board from the start. The way you build friendships provide for some great moments of comedic relief after a tense moment or when things seem dire, actually drove me to try me to save everyone before I reached the ending and I felt devastated after I failed, something I can only say only happened in Man of Medan too.Graphics:House of Ashes graphics are just as good as the previous game in the series, however there are slight improvements. The cave is massive and some of the environments are massive in scale and look incredible. I actually really wanted to check out everything the environments had hidden and just seeing some of these places made my jaw hit the floor.Audio: The audio design is again rather on the weak side. Voice acting is again top notch, everyone across the board does amazing job with their roles, especially Ashely Tisdale as Rachel, who I was very surprised by, but everyone nails their parts super well.The music is again slightly on the weaker side, however I felt a little more positive about this one, the score is just okay. There's some great tracks when the game goes action mode, but there's still quite a lot of droning loud music that every horror game uses once in a while.Gameplay:House of Ashes has the same type of gameplay as the previous two titles in the Dark Picture series. It's a movie on rails, you walk around interact with stuff, do some QTE's and then make a choice which will impact what happens in the story. However unlike the other two games, it actually feels a lot more interactive.There's a lot more ways you impact the outcomes like items you can pick up (required or not) and they play into the story in different ways which was incredibly cool. Also there's a bit of a combat system, even though it's basically QTE"s you have to hit at the correct time, but it's still cool that it at least wasn't fully an on rails experience.Verdict:House of Ashes is the best game in The Dark Pictures series. After the huge disappointment of Little Hope I lost all hope in the series, but House of Ashes spun that ♥♥♥♥ right around and if the other entries are just as good then we're in for some good horror games. Can't wait to see how the first Season wraps up, so bring on The Devil in Me.Final Rating:8.5/10Pros:+ Story is great and incredibly off the walls+ Some truly jaw dropping environments + A lot more gameplay Cons:- Soundtrack is disappointing - Pacing of the story is pretty slow If you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: Played from – to: (2022-12-06 – 2022-12-23) – PC controller.‣ 8/10 – “Do you believe in God?”‣ Thoughts: House of Ashes surprised me, because I found it to be not only interesting but enjoyable on top. From the three games in the Dark Pictures anthology that we have played I finally felt like I played a game. Sure, there were still plenty of cutscenes, but the contextual combat gave us more control. Also, the choices we made lead to character fates that made sense and did not force us to question certain deaths, which is a step-up form Little Hope. Overall, I found this games story to be the most interesting out of the three we played and most involving. All this to say, I crown House of Ashes to be the best game in this franchise so far. The characters were distinct enough and enjoyable to make me care. The story sure had its lowlights but kept me engaged and overall gave us a conclusive ending. Of course, there were definite miss steps in story telling here and there and some conversations made little to no sense, but again this was the most enjoyable game out of the bunch. _childDocuments_.review: You get to make decisions from two (or three) either stupid, similar, or obvious options. The obvious ones gives you the expected result. Now I've told you, and you are most welcome.So basically, you have no idea what you are doing (except when you get the obvious choices), but have to gamble. That kind of gameplay is completely pointless if you ask me. It's like watching a movie, getting asked to make some random decision, only for the movie to play out exactly like the director intended anyway. I wouldn't be able to tell the difference. The only way it has any value, is if you intend to replay it several times, trying different options. I have no plan to do so whatsoever.So think of the game as a movie, trying to keep you engaged by making "choices", while actual movies do so by being good instead. It's all about a bunch of soldiers falling down into a monster infested temple, where you are supposed to ♥♥♥♥ your pants. But you don't, because it isn't scary.

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes is an absolute triumph in the Dark Pictures Anthology series, and it's not an exaggeration to say that it's the best installment yet. This game offers a gripping narrative, top-notch performances by the cast, and an unforgettable duo in Salim and Jason that's among the finest in gaming history.From the very start, House of Ashes pulls you in with its thrilling story and doesn't let go until the very end. The game's premise, set against the backdrop of the Iraqi war, is both unique and haunting. As you navigate the eerie, underground ruins of an ancient Sumerian temple, you'll be immersed in an atmosphere of constant tension, suspense, and spine-tingling horror.The standout feature of House of Ashes is undoubtedly its stellar cast. The characters are brought to life by phenomenal actors who deliver exceptional performances, making you genuinely care about their fates. The chemistry between Salim Othman and Jason Kolchek is nothing short of extraordinary. Their dynamic and evolving relationship, filled with tension, trust, and camaraderie, adds a layer of depth to the story that few games can match. The emotional journey these two characters go through is, in my opinion, one of the most compelling aspects of House of Ashes.The choices you make throughout the game significantly impact the outcome, and the consequences are as dire as they are rewarding. Each decision keeps you on your toes, second-guessing yourself, and questioning your moral compass. It's this interactive storytelling that sets the Dark Pictures series apart from other horror games, and House of Ashes perfects this formula.The visuals are stunning, the sound design is impeccable, and the game's attention to detail is remarkable. The oppressive darkness of the underground, the unsettling noises, and the lurking horrors create an immersive experience that will have you at the edge of your seat throughout.In summary, House of Ashes is a masterpiece that exemplifies what interactive horror storytelling should be. It's a gripping narrative with great actors and unforgettable characters, particularly Salim and Jason, who stand out as one of the best duos in the gaming world. If you're a fan of the Dark Pictures series or just appreciate a well-crafted horror experience, don't miss this game. House of Ashes is a shining gem in the world of interactive horror gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I wanted to reminiscence about the war crimes my country committed in this part of the world, instead what I got was a great freaking game.I adored House of Ashes because of its amalgamation of unique sub-genres and themes. An ancient temple based creature feature starring a military-based cast with a sci-fi twist is such an ambitious merging of ideas but it’s pulled off so well. Its themes of war bringing the downfall of everyone involved are pretty powerful in the context of the time period, and the characters are a reflection of that. A strained relationship becomes even more strained when a couple is torn apart by work, another’s trauma of killing an innocent woman is reminiscent of many true war horror stories, a soldier’s aimlessness pushes them into becoming a marine and having their racism nurtured into hate by conflict, and a man’s unfortunate fate of being dragged into a war he doesn’t want to fight in so he can support his son to have a life better than his.The game completely engrossed and drew me in from the first few minutes. This game has an amazing storyline, real feelings and mostly likable characters who you actually start to care about and desperately want to keep alive, just a super immersive gaming experience like no other. I’ve replayed it twice already getting different outcomes and always trying to keep everyone alive to the end.Other than the themes, the nature of the game having a real enemy is something that was new in this series when this came out, as we’d yet to see a real creature or otherworldly presence. The characters are probably the most solid in any Supermassive Game.  Each one is interesting and complex.  Not as scary as some of the other games, but very character driven and it works. Yes some of the characters are mean or irritating, and yes some scenes are pretty repetitive, but it’s a game that has a strong message that ties together its genre combinations brilliantly, on top of just being a fun journey.I’d say it’s the most worthy game that supermassive has made. For the relative cheap price of about $30 you get an exciting game with a good story, mostly good characters and acting, some cool kills if you’re into that, good graphics and an all around fun experience. It has flaws for sure, but not more than any other game. Fair warning that it’s not really horror, more like an action-thriller. Honest to god if you haven’t experienced this masterpiece I envy you because I wish I could go in blind again. Just please put aside a full night for this game.Did I also mention that there’s also a naked Eric mod available? I’m sure if you’re even remotely interested you’d never regret buying it. What the hell are you waiting for?10/10

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes is a profound disappointment. The third installment to The Dark Pictures Anthology is so badly written and paced that the game feels like a chore that both insults and mocks multiple nations as well as the person playing the game. This game is the result of lazy development that did zero research before endeavoring the subject for their environment and attempt of immersion. The story is horrifically bad, and mocks the entire behavior or Iraqis and Americans. The story is only made worse by the abysmal dialogue, which seems to have been written by people who have never had a healthy conversation or person to person interaction in their life. The side plots that go along with this show further this problem. For example, the developers seem to think including a love triangle, that is more unbelievable than the story, is the way to keep things interesting. People being shot, blown up, sliced in badly graphical displays of gore and more around them dead as they are fighting to stay alive, but they have time to play this drama out. Two men are pawning for a chance of a sexual relationship with a woman in the middle of a war zone, during a life and death situation. This woman who is an expert in many field, needs no man, cheats on her husband, is the most athletic and capable of the bunch, speaks multiple languages, can throw heavy rocks further than Brett Farve and more. The graphics are a step down from the previous two. There is a clear display of filler and repeated textures, which is something that was not a problem with the previous games. I even complimented that they avoided that in the prior. In House of Ashes, the repetition is painfully obvious. Even the blood patterns on the uniform, which is applied to all of the character model, so it looks like the gear is bleeding, not the person. Very lazy and poorly done.The controls remain awkward as prior, but become more of a task in this game than the prior two iterations of the so far trilogy. There is a blur effect that seems to be with some desire to make things a focus or layered view. It causes issues, being that now many of the walls have break points, where at angles they do not show correctly. These are common graphical issues with independent games, but the first time it has been an issue with this series. The graphics overall are the same besides that.In all, this game is a hard pass for me. The developers did no research and took a very lazy approach to this game. It is by far a disappointment and a complete failure on the part of the developers. I do recommend the first two of The Dark Pictures Anthology.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer:  Do you need to play Man of Medan or Little Hope to understand what is going on?  No.  Each of these stories are individually contained.  You can ignore the first two and play this one just fine. The story is about 5 military personnel on differing factions who fall into an underground temple.  Something lurks in the depths, stalking the group.  The group must try to put their personal beliefs and struggles aside and find a way out of their predicament and survive the horror beneath the desert.This review is based off of one play through, solo.  I don't personally enjoy the military theme at the beginning of this game.  I've just never been into that type of story line, especially in horror movies or stories.  It is too easy for military group to come in guns blazing and blast up what ever is in their way and for me, that is why it lost the horror element at the start.While the developer and story writers stated that they wanted the war element to not over shadow the developing plot line, it still stuck in the back of my mind.  I felt I was just playing Call of Duty: Side quest during act 1 and through the majority of act 2.  These characters were still just army people running around with guns and explosives.  There were a few similar scenes where they would some how drop the gun they were holding and have it slide just out of reach.  They would plain open fire on what ever they were mad at or fearful of.  I wish they would have taken the amount of guns / ammo / bombs out of the equation and focused on a minimalist survival story.  Might have been better as an archaeologist team, with differing views of the temple site. That would have probably increased the horror element for me.  Giving characters too many weapons and ammo at their disposal decreases any sense of survival horror and brings it into the realm of action horror.Similar movies it may remind you off:  Aliens, The Descent, Predator.I disliked most of the characters aside from Salim and Nick, the others were quite obnoxious.  It was ham-fisted military acting at best.  They might as well all yelled "You maggots" every second line.  Didn't really care much for the love interest story line, or the "I don't trust you cuz yur different than me and we're not on the same side" problems they faced or the "i'm a higher rank than you, so you need to do what I say" lines, or the "stay away from my man" "I'm not interested in him ThAnKz!" girl rivalry trope.  Salim and Nick seemed to be the only two reasonable characters in this story, at least for my play through.Without going into too much spoiler, the plot began to flesh out end of act 2 beginning of act 3 and turned into a decent ending.  Little Hope had me hooked in Act 1.   I believe I was startled twice or three times during house of ashes so beware, they still have them.  Not as much as Man of Medan though.  The horror is still present without them.The setting / atmosphere was good along with lighting effects. The soundscape has been top notch.  I do give credit to The Dark Pictures, they have nailed the sounds quite well in each story.They reuse the same character models through the stories.  Similar to how American Horror Story uses the same actors to play different roles each season.  Ashley Tisdales' model looked funny and she was just covered in blood the whole time. The game offers different difficulties, depending on how challenging you wish your QTE's to be.  You can also turn prompt prior to QTE's off or on depending if you need a warning before the game requires you to input something.  I did choose to use prompts as I tend to lose focus on these games in favour of watching the story line play out.  The aiming QTE's are slightly different, where there is no target circle to aim for.  You aim for what ever is coming at you and your cross hair turns red to know when to pull trigger.  You will face rhythm QTE's in stay calm events.  Aim and target QTE's.  Button mash QTE's and quick reaction QTE's.I fumbled a lot of  QTE's and still managed to save 3 out of the 5 characters.They added a flashlight system which you can toggle on and off.  It was interesting.  I did find that this game was quite dark given the suggested configuration when you first start the game.I had played this game in 3 sittings.  There are 3 acts and roughly full play through took me about 6.8 hours.  This play through was longer than what I put in for Man of Medan at about 4.5 to 5.5 hours and Little Hope which was about 4.5 - 5.5 hours.  So far, how do I rank each story.1.  Little Hope - The characters were great, I cared about each one. It had me hooked at the beginning with the story line and the creatures were disgusting.  The ending while still sad / personal horror and psychological damage, paranoia and trust, almost mirror'd Man of Medan's "twist".  It left the community divided on if this ending was actually good or not. 2.  House of Ashes - The characters were annoying, the story didn't start to get good until mid to end of the 2nd Act and I am just not a fan of characters in horror stories having access to an arsenal of weapons at their disposal.  With that said, it branched out to be something bigger towards the end and did end up with some interesting ideas.3. Man of Medan - While the story was cool, it got spoiled way too early.  It lost it's horror element and focused on jump scares to get a rise out of you.  The story seemed a bit disjointed and the acting seemed a bit misplaced at times.I still will say this is a decent addition to the Dark Pictures and am looking forward to The Devil in Me.  The Season 1 Finale.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Supermassive game quality game!No spoilers here.Graphics: The graphics of their games are always top notch and one solid game to play visually.Audio: Atmosphere, sounds, music is all spot on with this game, like all Supermassive games.Controls: Easy keymap, harder to do quick times and get right.Gameplay and everything else after: So if you've played a Supermassive game or any of The Dark Pictures games, you know what to expect.There are twists, turns, jump scares, atmosphere setting, brain thinking, killing off people, choices to make that effect the game. Your actions can kill off someone and affect the way it will end, the way the story is told, the different dialogue options and overal effect the general telling of what happens.You play a multiple amount of characters in the game, a lot goes on and it's up to you to solve and find out. You can "accidentally" kill of some people or make the wrong choice and someone dies off, can you keep them alive? Do you want to keep them alive? It's up to you what you want to do, but each choice decides actions with happy or bad choices, that's good fun!It has multiple play through's for different options to keep alive, kill etcWould I recommend? _childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed this interactive movie. Not sure about the quality of the previous titles of The Dark Pictures Anthology, since I didn´t have the pleasure, but I can wholeheartedly recommend to anyone looking for a good story, good thriller(not really horror), or just a good action movie. I mentioned this is an interactive movie. But until now, I have never seen it so well executed - throughout the movie, you have hundreds(not exaggerating) of choices, that shape the course of the story. What characters will survive, what friendships and betrayals will happen, which ways the characters go...All of this and more is decided by you. By dialog choices, by succeeded(or failed) prompts, or just by foolish choices you make.Your freedom of choice is close to absolute. I was really surprised, when my two favorite characters died after several failed prompts, that the game continued with this outcome. There is no "Game Over" screen, the game counts with all eventualities and carries on. So to sum it up:+ your choices actually matter+ great acting, memorable characters+ interesting story+ good sound and graphical design of "bad guys"(no spoilers)+/- Game length. I finished it in 6 hours, but that was just one of myriads possible outcomes. Every playthrough is different, so the replayability is virtually infinite.Well, that´s that. Thank you for reading and give it try - this gem deserves it.
