_childDocuments_.review: This third entry into the Dark Pictures Anthology is without a doubt, the best entry in the anthology thus far. To the point that if you're new to the Dark Pictures Anthology series, this is the one I would recommend first; having played the other two chapters myself, I have to say, Man of Medan was 'okay' while Little Hope is a game I seem to dislike in further increments every time I think about the plot. I very much enjoyed a lot more fully in this one, and there were very few 'Oh, come ON' moments in this one, as compared to the previous two games, with Man of Medan being the most guilty on that front. One of the pluses of this being an anthology series, is that you can start on any of the three available games without needing to play the others, and if you want to spend money on the series, start on this one. It's a bit difficult to go into WHY this game is better than the other two in my opinion, without going into heavy spoilers for the other two, and it also depends on your taste in horror, and the different genres in horror. The other two entries in the series lean more into the psychological horror, and mystery, with Man of Medan being more realistic, and Little Hope (poorly attempting) to be more 'deep' about it (Little Hope's plot is like a back alley off brand attempt to do Silent Hill, and it fails hard).  This game, however, plays more into the action-horror genre, and I frequently found myself thinking of it as sort like a hybrid mix of Pitch Black, the Descent, and a light pinch of The Thing, and Ghosts of Mars. Whereas in the previous games in the series, you are playing as civilians, in this story, every character is a member of the military, quite tough, and very much armed. While you feel 'safer' in a sense because of this, the threat you face is more than enough to avoid making you feel overpowered. You will feel a lot more tense in this entry, at least in my opinion, compared to the previous two games. I found the characters in this one to be a step up from the others as well, with one in particular standing out as having a really nice character arc, where he starts the story as a standoffish, borderline douchebag, and can become one of the most heroic characters, who will do things for others that you wouldn't have imagined him doing at the start of the story, and you genuinely feel as if he's grown as a person. Plot-wise, I very much liked this one better than the other two; it's very much more straightforward with both, it's threat, and the situation they're stuck in, while still making it creepy and the tension fairly high. The story starts out far in the past, showing glimpses of an event that occurs, and then jumps far ahead to 2003, where that same threat is now encountered, buried far beneath the sands of Iraq, by a group of more modern soldiers. They are confused, disoriented, and have to try to escape said threat, while also dealing with an enemy general who doesn't seem to grasp the threat in the buried caves of the old civilization, and attempts to kill them several times. You also play as a reluctant soldier in the enemy army, who holds no ill will towards the other characters, and only wants to get out of the situation. There IS an underlying mystery, of what exactly the threat is, and a sub plot of an older archaeology team who found the ruins in the WW2 era, that's also decently handled, a fitting backdrop to paint the situation further, without feeling like it takes too much out of the tension. I will say, there ARE still a few of the almost trademarked 'Why can't I just do this' or 'Really?' sort of moments, where your characters, have the means to stop a threat in that moment, and just decide to NOT use it, for the sake of plot; without trying to give too much away, there is a part where two of your characters, both armed, are fleeing from a threat, and hide. It's the perfect opportunity to ambush this threat, as there are two of you, and only one of them, but it forces you to hide, and if you fail the 'heartbeat QTE' you will highly likely get one of the two characters you play as killed. It was one of the very few parts that actually had me irritated, but the game HAD warned me that there was a threat here, and I merely misinterpreted that warning. The QTEs are for the most part, fair, though I hate the 'heartbeat QTE' which is the one that you must play whenever your characters need to be quiet and stealthy. I feel like the game doesn't exactly explain the way it works very well, in ALL three of these games, and seeing as if you fail THESE particular QTEs, more often than not it will result in death or injury, I feel like they should be more clear on it. You have to time your button presses to a series of prompts that slide along a bar, and I assumed you had to hit the button RIGHT as the prompt touches your cursor, like a rhythm game, but that is incorrect, and got me hurt or killed or put into a worse situation each time. It wasn't until my partner I was playing with informed me you had to hit the button when your cursor is right in the MIDDLE of the prompt, that I started to be able to pass those QTEs. If not for that, I would have failed EVERY heartbeat QTE that I encountered, and lost more characters, which, I feel would have made the death unfair, as I misunderstood how that mechanic worked. Perhaps a safe 'practice' mode for the QTEs outside the story would help?Another thing regarding the QTEs; in this developer's early game, Until Dawn, the mechanic where you can decide to shoot/strike/throw an object or harm another person, it lets you know right away that sometimes NOT going through with the action, is a better choice. I don't know if I missed it here because I was already used to that mechanic and skimmed by the instructions, but I don't recall the game telling the player that they don't HAVE to shoot/stab/throw something when the prompt comes up in this one, so I could see someone accidentally killing or harming a character because they felt the game was forcing them to, when that isn't the case. Also, I feel as if they should change the icon they use for the 'button mash' QTE, where you must mash one button as fast as you can to fill up a meter to succeed a strength check. It looks a little similar to the regular one-tap button prompts, so sometimes it'll come up and you tap the button, and waste a second or two before you realize it's a mash prompt instead, and then have to scramble to start mashing. Even a game like RE4 handled it's mash prompts obviously, compared to it's one-taps, so I feel they could easily handle that in this game. Beyond the minor elements of plot railroad with the 'why didn't we just shoot that guy when we could' mentioned above, and honestly, that was one of the only points that happened, there are a lot less of the flaws of the previous two games here, and it feels a lot more polished and smooth compared to them. I played through (one time thus far) playing co-op online with a friend of mine all in one sitting, and I will say, I feel as though that's the premiere way to play the game, not to say the single player isn't good, it is, but going through with a buddy, who you can speak to and hear what's happening on their end (or not telling, if you want lol) can be a boon. I will also say that out of all the ending sequences in Supermassive Games series, this one has the best one, similar-ish to Until Dawn, which goes through all the surviving characters being interviewed by the police, this one runs through what happens after whoever is left (which could be NONE of them depending on how you play) manages to escape, and it's really cool. All in all, this is the best game in the Anthology so far, and I can only hope that they keep this up for the next chapter, which is previewed in the ending to this game, as looking like a serial killer story, sort of like SAW? I'll be replaying this one to see the variations of endings, and really enjoyed it!

_childDocuments_.review: House of Ashes succeeds at many things. With fantastic visuals, interesting characters and a claustrophobic atmosphere, it makes for a very fun game. I was really engaged with the story for the most part, but the ending started to lose me. While it's at least satisfying (unlike its predecessors), it felt too colossal and I think it needed to be more grounded in reality. Overall, I really enjoyed this and can't wait to replay it with the knowledge of how to save my characters. I think it is easily the best in the series, and I can't wait to see what the next game has in store. After a rough beginning to The Dark Pictures Anthology, I am confident that the developers are on the right track.

_childDocuments_.review: I love QTE games. I'm lazy and have a giant TV at the end of my bed, that's bigger than the bed itself. Problem is I can't aim very well with my mouse on the bed, nor can I aim particularly well on a controller. So games like this which have minimal aiming (and assist options for it too) are great fun for me. Plus with a giant a$$ 4K gaming TV, it helps me immerse better in a game that's designed to be super immersive.For the above reason, I own every game these guys make, twice in fact for a few of them (on PS4 too). and I have a blast every time. I still can't quite get my head around whatever the hell happened last year in Little Hope, so I'll have to go back to that one for a replay soon.But House of Ashes, I feel was truly the best in the series. It starts a little slow, a bit weak sauce, but once you get deeper into the chapters it starts to really get exciting. And the deeper you go, the crazier it gets. So whilst I definitely recommended buying the full Dark Pictures series, I'd say even if its your first one, this is the right one to pick. There are some Little Hope references in it so that might make you pick that one up too, just to see how it all connects.With this game series, one of the rewards for beating the game is it shows you the NEXT upcoming game. So next October, fans will get another game added to the series, and thats already looking pretty sick too. As I said earlier, I played this on the highest settings on my 4K TV, there was absolutely no lag or input issues, the game was smooth as a whistle with no issues stopping and starting. it played as you would expect it to on a console with perfect fluidity. My GPU is the 980ti, so it's getting on a bit in age now, but still performed perfect on this game.So if you want an immersive experience where you can distract yourself from the real world and engage in the plight of others - I say pay full price and go for it. I'll pre-order the next line up in the series as soon as it's available.
_childDocuments_.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes

_childDocuments_.review: Just played Man of Medan, and this is much, much better, they have come a long way forward.  It is about (at least) 3x the length, there is no bs "you must finish the game first" so chapters can be immediately replayed if someone is drunk or tired and they screw up a QTE.  Story is much better, though this is subjective, the setting and characters were more interesting people.  It is a great game, well worth playing, and a good relaxing game because of the story-driven nature.  Only one problem is the quick transition between just relaxing through the story and some action happening that needs fast QTE.  Some warning would be good so can put hands on controller/mouse and concentrate first.  I think something like this was in a patch(?) though probably after I played.If anyone has trouble beating the heartbeat thing, if you can increase to 120fps, it is SIGNIFICANTLY easier than on the 60fps, I flubbed up my nvidia settings and played this locked to 60fps and only discovered my mistake when playing Man of Medan.  Just some advice if this kind of thing is annoying or inordinately difficult.  Graphics are mostly fantastic, animations are good, no complaints any way around it is a nice game that meets 2021 visual standards.Like all of these games, they are a 1-2 time playthrough experience.  There is a "curator's mode" where one can play as a different character in the scenes giving some replayability, which I have not tried yet, as it hadn't unlocked when I played, but at max game is 2 playthroughs.  Dont take it on a desert island if it is the only game you bring.So I do recommend it, nice game, no political correct woke bs being rammed down my throat which I really appreciate( a HUGE turn-off for me and I would not have played/finished the game if it was there).  Game deserves to be played if nothing else on the radar, it is just south of a "must play" but not by far.  Polish is very good also, bugs very minimal, annoying things very minimal.  Definitely put on wishlist and pick it up for a rainy day when on discount if not going to play today would be my advice.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best Dark Pictures Anthology game.It starts as Black Hawk Down, turns into The Descent by the end of the first act, and then it turns into Alien, and if that doesn't sell you on the game, I don't know what will.Like I said before, this game is much better than the previous entries in the Anthology, and in my opinion, the game achieves this because the devs actually tried to do something interesting with the story and characters.In this game, the characterization is much better than before We get an american soldier with PTSD, a dude that starts as a cartoony racist soldier but then you realize there's more to him than that, an Iraki soldier who's drifting apart from his son, and even a love triangle. Now make no mistake, this is a Supermassive Games horror game, so in terms of gameplay it's almost the exact same formula they used on Until Dawn and the other DPA games, so if that is not your cup of tea, you're not gonna enjoy this game. The story is amazing, good graphics, characters are all intriguing and the game play is decent. Although the story has a semi-linear path, choices still can have detrimental impacts. It was always fun to replay and find different clues that led to new choices and outcomes. The only thing I would change is more chances for exploration, a more open world type of feel. If you love choice games, I highly recommend buying this one. My overall rating of this game is a 9/10. _childDocuments_.review: A true spiritual successor to one of my favorite games of my childhood, Battle for Bikini Bottom, to say I was excited for this game is an understatement. After sinking 8 and a half hours and finishing the game, this game has exceeded every single one of my expectations. I'll start with the art. The character animation is expressive and fits the characters well (I did notice though that almost all of Spongebob's idle animations were reused from Battle for Bikini Bottom: Rehydrated, not saying this is a bad thing though), and each world is packed with detail and vibrancy, some more than others but still beautiful nonetheless. All of the character costumes are true to the show and serve as nostalgic fanservice for fans (Costumes have no gameplay effect other than cosmetic appearance).  Now onto Gameplay. One of the biggest changes I noticed from Battle for Bikini Bottom is a more open type of level design, which was a very welcome change personally considering the very linear nature of BFBB's level design. Combat feels responsive, with the new array of attacks at Spongebob's disposal being very fun to use. However i did notice a rather annoying inconsistency with hitboxes. Some attacks will not hit occasionally despite being right next to an enemy and some attacks will hit me despite being well outside of the hitbox. Platforming elements have a varied level of difficulty attached to them, with some areas being harder than others in every level. One of my favorite new platforming mechanics is when you have to jump on a boulder and roll down a hill while avoiding obstacles. Mechanics such as sliding also made a return in the game, however I did notice a weird issue when hitting tikis while sliding. There are certain times where I would jump to hit a tiki but the game would not break it, but instead bounce off of them, more often than not knocking me off the track and forcing me to restart from a checkpoint. Now onto writing and voice acting. The game follows Spongebob and Patrick (who gets turned into a balloon) as they try to bring their friends back to Bikini Bottom after meeting a fortune teller mermaid called Madame Kassandra, getting a magical bubble soap from her called Mermaid's Tears, which tears up the fabric of the universe, opening up Wishworlds that are takes on locations from the series with a theme behind them. The voice acting saw the return of the main cast from the show, including a well-awaited return of Clancy Brown as Mr. Krabs after being absent from Battle for Bikini Bottom. Other returning members include Tom Kenny as Spongebob and Gary, Bill Fagerbakke as Patrick, Rodger Bumpass as Squidward, Carolyn Lawrence as Sandy, Mr. Lawrence as Plankton, and many others. My biggest complaint with the voice acting is the delivery, it feels... weak, especially from Tom Kenny at certain times as Spongebob. Onto PC Performance. The game is powered by Unreal Engine 4 and was played on my Desktop Gaming PC, powered by a Ryzen 9 5900x, RTX 2080, and 32 GB of RAM, and installed on a SSD. Playing at 1440p wielded pretty satisfying results, with no changes to default settings (which is an issue, as the video options is pretty barebones, only offering window type and resolution options, and requires going into the game files to make setting adjustments). On default settings my game ran at a wide framerate range, anywhere from 90 FPS to 165 FPS (my monitor refresh). There was some stuttering here and there caused by what i can assume to be shader compilation, however it was much less frequent than other Unreal Engine games i've played on PC, and did not impact my experience much.   Overall the game is a fantastic sequel and successor to one of the best licensed 3D platformers available in the last 25 years, with faithful art direction, good voice acting, and fantastic level design. I highly recommend picking this game up, especially if you really liked Battle for Bikini Bottom. 9/10(My review will be updated after i finish the game with any additional thoughts or changes)

_childDocuments_.review: A very acceptable, honest successor to Battle for Bikini Bottom. Here are a list of my initial pros and cons. Will edit as I continue playing. Basically, this game is great and IGN is horrible.- Most aesthetic and gameplay elements return from BFBB, but many new ones are added to make the game feel more like an inspired love letter to BFBB rather than a soulless ripoff.- With that said, it plays almost exactly like BFBB. Relive your childhood.- Lots of unique objectives and minigames that revitalize the gameplay experience.- The graphics are very vibrant and cute.- The areas/zones/levels are very well designed and detailed and are incredibly creative.- The cutscenes are beautifully animated- The music is as great as BFBB's was.- The story is good for what it is.- The sound mixing is pretty bad at times. Voice lines with inconsistent volume, music clipping in and out harshly, etc.- The voice acting is below average in my opinion. The delivery of a lot of lines seem weak to me, and a lot of characters are either a little off or straight up sound like a bad impression of themselves.- The cutscenes can be very wonky/glitchy a lot of the time, even though they're usually animated very well.- Little nuanced, jarring details, like NPC's spawning right infront of your face, some voice lines glitching and playing twice, cutscenes being very awkwardly paced, and tikis floating in the air (not the ones that are supposed to).- The humor is definitely centered around the modern era of Spongebob, with lots of throwback references thrown in, which can be seen as a pro or a con depending on how you feel about modern Spongebob.I think I can honestly say that this game exceeded most people's expectations, and If you grew up playing Battle for Bikini Bottom, then you will most definitely enjoy playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely a super fun, enjoyable experience for me. Personally, I liked it a little more than Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated. It seems like they took Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated and expanded upon it further. Although, instead of playing as different characters, you play as only Spongebob who gradually learns every single mechanic, new or old, as you progress further into the game. Several new enemy types get introduced throughout the story. You unlock more silly costumes over time. It sounds like they got most of the original voice actors to reprise their roles. There's a lot more charm and personality added into the animations too. But best of all, if you're like me who is a big fan of Spongebob and grew up watching the original seasons, you will definitely appreciate all the different memes and references they make throughout the game because they don't hold back on those. Overall, it's a very chill, basic 3D platformer. It isn't a difficult game by any means, so you can just casually play about, have some fun exploring the worlds, enjoying the dialogue, and everything! Very good game! A great addition into the franchise, and an improvement over Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated. Hope the dev team remaster more of the original Spongebob games later in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: When SpongeBob and Patrick get their hands on wish-granting Mermaid Tears, the fabric of the entire universe starts to unravel. Now, our favorite sponge has to work with a balloon Patrick and travel across different worlds to put everything back in its place. Donning over 30 iconic costumes, The Cosmic Shake will send you on a 3D platforming adventure across 7 different lands. Traverse and defend yourself using classic skills, with many new ones you can unlock as you progress. Will SpongeBob be able to save the day?Even though I am older now, SpongeBob has always delighted me, and it's wonderful that this game captures that same delight. The art style is incredible, vibrant and simple, and the gameplay was very enjoyable. I had a blast going from world to world, seeking out the Bikini Bottom residents we have come to know and love, all voiced by their original cast! If you're a fan of SpongeBob, or looking for a great game to play after Battle for Bikini Bottom, this is going to be it. With that said, let me tell you a bit about how this will run on the Steam Deck.While The Cosmic Shake starts off on a great foot and decently well out of the box with 60 FPS, it does start to dip in certain areas. This is much less stable later on, with drops to the 40s, and battery drain rising to 24W+. Luckily, there are a couple things we can do to make this game significantly more enjoyable on the Steam Deck!The first thing I did when trying to optimize this one was see if upscaling would look alright. To my surprise, I actually noticed almost no change from native resolution! I even believed that it initially didn't work because it looked so close to native, yet it helped significantly with stability in most areas.From there, it was a matter of finding the right balance of framerate cap and TDP limit. For The Cosmic Shake, it seemed to dip to around 41-42 at the worst of times, so a 40 FPS cap worked out the best. This, along with the upscaling resolution, allowed a TDP limit of 9 that held up in all playable areas and still felt fantastic. I also put on a GPU Clock Speed Frequency of 1200 as this chilled out the framerate instability that occurred from time to time.I wanted to also find a 45 FPS build that I could be happy with, since 45 FPS felt fantastic. While there are still some areas that will dip to 41-42, even with TDP caps on at all, it held up beautifully with a TDP limit of 10. The times performance dipped the most were actually the cutscenes. These scenes tended to sometimes drop below 40 FPS and could be really hard on the system, but it ended up going right back up to normal as soon as the cutscene ended. They are more than likely real-time cutscenes that use extra filters to make it look much better and those could be taking a toll on the system. It's nowhere near a deal-breaker though!I also had no issue with any controls and didn't encounter any visual bugs, but I did find that the costume menu dropped performance by a significant amount. Going and selecting costumes went down to 27 FPS with a maxed out battery drain. I didn't mind it since I was just selecting my costume and it went right back to normal getting out of it, but it was still noteworthy.SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is just a joy to play. It has all the charm and beauty that SpongeBob is known for, but integrates some wonderful gameplay elements into it. Pair it up with the unique worlds it showcases and you've got yourself a good time! On top of that, this is fully enjoyable on the Steam Deck and those little tweaks really make a difference to stability and saving battery. The battery drain is a little high for my tastes, but overall, this will have no problem on your Deck!

_childDocuments_.review: It's not as good as the best Spongebob games (BFBB, Movie Game, Creature from the Krusty Krab, etc) but still, a step above the generic ones that came out in the 2010's. There definitely was a very genuine attempt to create something fun for Spongebob fans and not just a corporate cash grab, and I appreciate that. For positives, it is a very nice looking game for the most part, and a step above BFBB Rehydrated. The humor is great and captures the vibe of classic Spongebob better than the TV show does currently. The hub world is fun and cool to see an expanded version of what we've seen before. I love that the game attempts to take some of the game design language of the previous Spongebob games and create something new with it. At the same time however, this is a bit of a double edge sword as it leads me to my biggest issues with the game. I think this attempt was largely unsuccessful and it's very frustrating.My biggest problems with the game are the level design and the combat, which makes up a bulk of the experience so it's hard to ignore. To start with the combat, the expanded arsenal of moves is a very welcome addition, but falters for me because of how deliberately limiting it is implemented. I don't like that a lot of the moves can only be used in certain times and only on certain enemies. Specifically the kick move would be way more fun to use if you could do it all the time and level design would encourage that. This is something that was very prominent in BFBB that I think this game missed out on. The platforming and combat abilities were one in the same, and the level design reflected this and was designed around it. Same goes for the bubble move which feels like a downgrade from the Bubble Bowl from BFBB. The closed in combat areas make this issue the most apparent with how operatic and empty they feel. In a better game, I don't think we'd need them at all.More on the level design now. One thing that made BFBB great is how the level design made the world feel much bigger and expansive than it actually was. Sure there is an obvious direction and flow to the levels, but you could make a mental map in your head of the environment and every nook and cranny was memorable. This maze like design is largely absent with the level design in this game is being mostly straight forward. The few times the levels opened up a bit was welcome. I just wish they went further in that direction. Best examples being the later levels such as Halloween Rock Bottom, Pirate Goo Lagoon and Medieval Sulfur Fields. The latter is probably the best level in the game in my opinion.A few other issues with game include it's shorter length, less engaging collectible system, and mediocre boss fights. These don't bother me as much but feel worth mentioning none the less as obvious downgrades. Now I've been very critical in this review, but I do still recommend the game. All these issues aside, there's a lot of glimpses of brilliance and capturing the magic of what made BFBB so great (at least to people like me who grew up with it). I did still enjoy it, and think if Purple Lamp where to make a sequel that addressed the issues with this game, it could be something really special. I don't know how well this game is selling, so it may be unlikely. If I had to give this game a score it would be a 6/10. Thank you for reading this way too long review. This may resonate with a very niche group of weird cartoon-game nerds like myself, who are getting to old to care about this sort of thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I begin, this review will inevitably feature several comparisons to Battle For Bikini Bottom (BFBB) and The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie game (TSSM) as the overall gameplay is pretty similar to those titles and I am pretty familiar with them. With that said, let's get into what I liked about the game.-The presentation is beautifulFrom the animations, to the lighting, to the various character and environmental models, this game looks fantastic. The more cinematic cutscenes are a treat to see and remind me very much of watching an episode of the show. In-game graphics are no slouch either and there were several times where I spent time looking around just to observe my surroundings-Gameplay overall is solidThe way that SpongeBob controls feels pretty good and he has a variety of moves that can be used for combat and platforming. To provide an example, SpongeBob gets access to a karate kick move early on in the game that homes in on enemies and certain obstacles and bounces you up into the air after you hit them to give you a second to decide what to do next and keep your momentum going. Occasionally, you will have sections in the levels where you're doing other stuff such as riding on a seahorse through a large stretch of land or (returning from BFBB) sliding down a slide that help keep the gameplay loop fresh.-Level design is goodIf I had to compare the levels to something, I would say that they're most similar to the levels in TSSM. What I mean by this is that levels are linear for the most part with some small side areas to explore or challenges to complete to obtain collectibles. Also similar to BFBB and TSSM, when you first go through each level, you won't have the necessary abilities or meet certain requirements to obtain everything. To add onto this, after completing the level for the first time, you will usually encounter a character in the HUB world with a quest that has you returning to past levels to collect stuff for them to obtain collectibles needed for 100% completion.As for the levels themselves, I found all of them to be pretty good. They're interesting to travel through and you're introduced to at least one new ability or mechanic that you'll use through out each level. The game is very good at telling you where you should go to complete the main objective and levels are designed in a way that it's difficult to get lost. You won't be seeing any BFBB Kelp Forest here.-Classic Spongebob songs and voice actors are usedNothing much to really say here, the voice actors that have been with the show since the beginning are here and sound exactly like you expect. If you like the music that's heard in the show, then I'm happy to say that they've likely used a familiar track in at least one part of the game somewhere. The game also features several original tracks (I think?) that fit with each level that they are in.-Only one playable characterThe only character you play as through the entire game is SpongeBob. It's a shame that previously playable characters like Patrick and Sandy aren't playable, but it makes sense when you consider that Spongebob has an expanded moveset that features moves very similar to the ones they had in BFBB, which would make them redundant.-Story is not all that interesting but serviceableThe story is mostly just here to give SpongeBob an excuse to go to each level. You can tell right away who the main antagonist is going to be within the first several minutes of the game and there's no kind of twist or anything to make it interesting. The story of each level can basically be summed up as: Find character or important building you want to save, figure out the conflict(s) of that level, solve the conflict(s), take character or building back with you at the end. The story isn't offensively stupid and there are some funny moments in the story and levels, which is why this is more neutral than outright negative.-Costumes aren't as important as they're made out to beIn the game and in promotional material, costumes were hyped up to be this thing that would allow you to complete levels using their powers. In reality, they are purely cosmetic and offer no gameplay changes. This is somewhat disappointing, but also understandable considering how many moves SpongeBob already has available to him. On a more positive note, you're able to change your costume at any time during the game through the pause menu and there are quite a lot of them to unlock, with the vast majority of them being references to stuff in the show.-Collectibles don't feel rewarding enoughThis might sound strange in a game like this, but the rewards you get for collecting stuff feel... underwhelming. When you're not collecting stuff to complete one of the quests, the main collectible is doubloons. As you collect doubloons, you'll fill a bar and eventually level up. What does leveling up do? It gives you access to more costumes you can purchase and then wear... and that's all it does. Unless you're going out of your way to get 100% completion or there's a costume you really like at a specific level, there's not much incentive to collect doubloons. The same thing applies to the jelly that you see everywhere in each level. Jelly is only used to purchase the costumes that you unlock through leveling up and nothing else. In this game, golden spatulas return from BFBB and there's 1 in each level. What do they do? They give you an achievement after you collect all of them and that's it. You don't even get to hear SpongeBob say any unique lines or do any kind of animation when you collect them, which makes them even more pointless than the previous collectibles if you're not going for 100% completion. Finally, in a few of the levels you can find the golden underwear from BFBB and it does increase your health like in that game, which makes them one of the only optional collectibles that affects gameplay in any way (still no unique lines or animations though rip).Finally, my last gripe with the collectibles has to do with 100% completion. After you finally get all the collectibles and complete all the in-game awards (achievements basically), what do you get for putting in the effort? Nothing but achievements and the satisfaction of completing the game entirely. I find this disappointing as in both BFBB and TSSM, you got an extra ending scene, got to view concept art, and other cool rewards to make collecting everything worthwhile. It just seems strange that the most notable rewards you get are costumes and a few health upgrades and it feels like something is missing.-The Final Boss is not very goodI won't say too much to avoid spoilers, but the final boss seems like they combined a few of the bosses you previously encountered and called it a day. The whole battle follows the pattern of: Dodge multiple shockwave attacks, pick up the power up you were introduced to in the final level, charge it up on basic enemies the boss summons, hit boss with charged up shot, repeat this cycle two more times and the boss is done. It sounds like I'm simplifying it, but it really is that easy, and for an enemy you encounter at the very end of the game, it shouldn't be.SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake was very fun for me to play through. I enjoyed all the silly references and memes from the show and previous games, and the entire game was captivating enough for me to want to 100% complete it, despite how underwhelming the process was. If you're a fan of both older and modern SpongeBob, have played BFBB or TSSM and enjoyed them, or just want an casual platformer and don't care about getting 100%, I can highly recommend this game. If you do not fall into any of those categories, I would wait for a sale if you still want to try it at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm going to give my honest review of this game starting sort of from the beginning, and giving comparisons to past SpongeBob games I played.As a kid, I grew up on BFBB (Battle for Bikini Bottom) and The SpongeBob Movie Game (both on the PS2). I also played a plug-and-play SpongeBob game, as well as PRR (Plankton's Robotic Revenge) on the Wii. I also purchased BFBB Rehydrated when it was released (PC and got it free on PS4).So OBVIOUSLY, I was STOKED to play The Cosmic Shake, as I had been waiting for its release since it was shown off at Sony's "State of Play" a while back. This is where my comparisons are gonna come in.BFBB/BFBB Rehydrated: To me these games remain the best SpongeBob games TO DATE, the original is timeless, and the remaster (although I had a few gripes) was spectacular as well. The Cosmic Shake definitely seems to take a pretty decent bit of inspiration from them, but In my opinion just isn't quite as good.PRR: Wasn't my favorite of the SpongeBob games, and although fun with a second player, felt dull in comparison to the other games I had played. The Cosmic Shake definitely tops PRR by a mile.The SpongeBob Movie Game: Really good game, but super long, and VERY grindy. Never beat it as a kid because the grindiness of the game couldn't keep my attention. I'd say personally that The Cosmic Shake, is a bit better than TSBMG.So now I'm going to go over the Pros and Cons of buying the game, what it did well, and what it didn't.PROS:1) The graphics are really good, maybe even slightly better than BFBBR.2) In comparison to TSBMG, it is a lot less grindy. I like that you can actually progress through the game and story without having to go get a bunch of bloody doubloons, unlike TSBMG and the Goober Tokens...3) THE FIGHTING OMG, I love love love the fighting mechanics in this game. I'd say it may have my favorite fighting mechanics out of all the games I have played. The Karate Kick is especially fun to use and made me feel super cool and like a total parkour master. The only thing I missed having, is the Bubble Bowl from BFBB. 4) THE VOICE ACTING!  It's pretty much all the original voice actors which makes it just that much better. Unlike BFBB where Mr. Krabs...well...sounds not quite right. The only thing I would complain about would actually be SpongeBob's voice, as it is a bit off. However, I know Tom Kenny is getting older, and SpongeBob isn't exactly the easiest voice to pull off, so I'll give it a pass.5) COSTUMES! I believe TSBMG did have them as well, but I really do like that they brought them back in this game.6) The callbacks and references made me smile.7) Smacking Anchovies, I rest my case.8) I do like that Patrick gives you Health/Underpants, I think that's a really nice addition, as it makes it a little bit less hectic when you're trying to fight a lot of enemies. Speaking of enemies...9) The new enemies are really neat, and I like how many different variants there are. Makes you have to actually have some form of strategy to how you play and fight.10) Level Designs: I think they did really well here, although I will say there are 2 that after a few times of running through, I started to not like as much. But, I didn't hate any of them, unlike another particular level from a particular game...(I'm looking at you Kelp Forest...)11) I will say it did pretty well on the achievements, the majority of them are fun and not super hard to get, but still fun and challenging enough to keep my attention and not make me wanna tear my head off in absolute frustration and rage.12) I like that you can use the Seahorses to get around Bikini Bottom, although I personally am quite partial to the legendary Sponge-Ball, they do indeed suffice for their intended purpose.Cons:1) The story...It's not bad, and it's a fun idea, but I personally just didn't feel like it was super engaging. A lot of the humor and dialogue fell flat for me. Sure, it had a few good jokes in there, but it just was all kinda bland/dry humor in my opinion. Also, the main plot line and villain were basically obvious from the beginning of the game. Although most of the SpongeBob games do follow that sort of rule of thumb to have it shown from the beginning, it just felt  Like perhaps it's just a bit too cliche for me, others may disagree though.2) As of now, there are bugs. I will give it the fact that the bugs I experienced were minimal, and I'm sure they'll fix them soon; but as of right now, the game does have some minor bugs (ie: Characters disappearing or becoming transparent in cut-scenes.).3) The length of the game: I managed to 100% the entire game in just shy of 22 hours. This means unless you play the game slowly, you'll be able to beat the entire story in 10 hours or less, and 100% it in under 24 hours.4) The price: I pre-ordered the game the day before release; and although I would say I did have a lot of fun with it, I feel like the game should have been only $20 and not $40 or more (for special editions). 5) The amount of content is lacking in my opinion. For as long as it took them to make the game, I would think that it would have a lot more content. And although I did enjoy the uniqueness of the levels and the new abilities/powers, after a while you get too used to everything and it starts to get a bit boring.6) The lack of levels: I actually wish there were more levels to play; the majority of them were really fun to play, and with all the new mechanics, I feel like they could have done so much more, especially with the expansive world that is Bikini Bottom.7) I know I said I like the Seahorses, but the controls do feel a bit wonky, and I don't like the fact that once you hop on it, you have no way of stopping them other than just dismounting them. 8) The boss's achievements in particular bothered me a LOT. Now it's not the achievements themselves that I have an issue with; overall, they weren't that bad and I actually had decent fun with them and found them challenging. The problem lies in having to restart, which normally I wouldn't fuss about...HOWEVER! In the case of these, any time you enter a boss fight, if you wanted to just commit die in order to restart the level, or you wanted to simply restart it by re-entering the level, that's not gonna work buckaroo. Every time you have to restart a boss level, you have to literally quit to the main menu, and then load up your game file...EVERY. SINGLE. BLOODY. TIME. And not gonna lie...it gets reallllly old quickly.9) The overall challenge of the game...wellllll it's just not exactly there. Sure it has a few moments where it could be a bit hard, but the majority of the game is really really easy, which in comparison to BFBB and TSBMG, makes this game like child's play. Even the bosses are so cut and dry and super easy, really only one of them did I have a minor struggle with. But the attack patterns were so easy to learn that it just felt almost a bit saddening. I was very disappointed by how easy the literal FINAL BOSS was.EDIT: I have two more things to add to this list.10) The repetitive voice lines get bothersome after a few times, I'm officially sick of The Krusty Krab Pizza song...11) Patrick pointing towards people and things that you just spoke to, or if you sit still for a moment he turns into an arrow and tries to point you somewhere, or even just wandering off to look for things he will do it then as well, which can get annoying. As well as audio cues telling you there's a secret nearby; it's not much of a secret, or gratifying when you find it if they literally tell you one's there.FINAL THOUGHTS:Overall, I'd say this is a good game. Although in my opinion, it is a bit lacking in content, I did still have fun with it. My advice is to wait for the game to go half-price, and then purchase it. But regardless of what you chose to do, full price or not, I do still recommend it, as it had a lot of charm to it.

_childDocuments_.review: To start this review off, let me just state that I  receive a key for this game from THQ Nordic, and while I am incredibly grateful, this will not influence my opinion in any way, shape, or form. I will always be honest, as I do not want to falsely sway anyone's opinion.Cosmic Shake felt so amazing to play, and I had so much fun with this game—even more fun than in . The atmosphere and voice acting just felt extremely polished in comparison to BFBB. For some reason, I feel like the BFBB voice acting was cheesy. But this was very well done. It features lighthearted humor for all ages, even if you haven't watched the TV show! I really enjoyed all the dialogue and found my adult self laughing. Playing through this game was like reliving my childhood with all the references to the show, and I loved every minute of it. In terms of graphics and soundtrack, visually and audio-wise, this game is so beautiful, and Purple Lamp/THQ Nordic did an excellent job.A lot of the worlds/levels are similar to BFBB: Rehydrated  they're more of an enhanced and better version of them, in my opinion. My favorite world was Halloween Rock Bottom! A lot of new enemies are introduced, some that I found super cool and others that I found so annoying (I'm talking to you, Baby Booms). Most enemies you can kill with a basic attack and have 1 HP but other enemies have 2-3 HP, and they can get a little irritating, like one of the enemies, Big Jelly. You can only hit him once he finishes his attack, and you can only hit him once. If you get hit during his attack, it won't allow you to hit him at all; even if you physically melee him, nothing will register. This annoyed me sometimes, but I just learned to get used to it. The boss fights are very easy and have very simple mechanics, but that's okay! Some of us don't like overly difficult games :P The only boss fight I kind of struggled with was the final boss, and it was more of the ADDs that were making the boss fight difficult for me. All in all, combat is extremely fun and mindless, which I adore in games like these. I don't want to get frustrated and angry. I just want to have fun, fight, and collect s**t.One of my favorite things about this was the amount of side quests available alongside your main objective to progress through the game. You can still work on these side quests after you finish the game, and I plan on finishing them in order to 100% the game. The side quests aren't too difficult to complete but give you a reason to go back and revisit the worlds, while also collecting any other collectibles you missed during the first run through. The collectibles are SO fun to collect without feeling too annoying. They don't require much thinking or puzzle-solving, but some will be "locked" in a way until you get a certain ability through progression of the game. The collectibles include: doubloons, golden spatulas, golden underwear, Spot locations, sticky notes, and so much more. If you love collectibles in games, this is a great one for you! Especially if you like 100%'ing games.In brief, do I recommend this game? Yes. Do I recommend it for the full retail price? It depends on the circumstances. I finished BFBB in 20~ hours. I finished Cosmic Shake in 11~ hours, but again, I do plan on going back and grabbing all the achievements. So, if you're a one-and-done kind of player, wait for a sale. If you love achievement hunting, the full retail price is worth it, in my opinion! I will easily get 20+ hours in this game through achievement hunting. Happy gaming!Thanks for reading my review and have a fantastic day!Rating: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this under two conditions. You're either a child or a big spongebob fan, otherwise this game is not worth it.I played the first one, both original and remake and that game was a blast, absolute fun level design, gameplay, etc. This game however.. it's not bad, if anything it's pretty fun. But it is kind of braindead. The game is incredibly easy, you're never once challenged, the levels feel smaller than they did in BFBB and this time you're playing just as spongebob. The collecting part here also feels a bit off. You don't really have a reason to do any sidestuff or collect things other than for completion, so it feels tedious to go back for things to levels you have completed already.The story is alright, again a little predictable but it works. The game also has lovely cutscenes and you're once again able to just run through different places from the show, which is always cool. The only issues I've had where that sometimes the hitboxes seem a bit bigger than they are which has let me to get hit when it looked like I should be fine, but that is a really minor issue, cause even if you do get hit or die, the game doesn't really punish you for it. You also fight the same 6-7 enemies all game over and over, and while every single one has their unique thing, most of them you can very easily kill, while there are two, that kind of require you to just wait around a bunch.That being said, the game really does feel like it was made for a much younger audience in mind. But if you can see past that, it would say it's still fun to run around Bikini Bottom and other familiar places with Spongebob and everyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know who the target audience is. The game has REALLY good reviews, while I couldn't get into it at all, and I adore SpongeBob. I also loved BFBB a lot and completed it several times as a kid and recently.The biggest (and almost the only plus) is that it looks visually good. I love the graphics and art style; it's super nice to look at. But that's kinda where it ends for me.The level design is kinda eh at best; it's just confusing, copy-n-pasted, and random in many areas. I absolutely hate the backtracking mechanic that makes you come back to levels hours after completing them just to get some collectible with a mechanic that you learned way later on. (That might be subjective; I know there are people who like it, but I find it severely unsatisfying.)And then the combat—it's absolutely horrendous and repetitive. (Except the jump-attack-thingy; that one is very satisfying.) You have to fight to progress, so you can't just skip it; you HAVE to engage with it. The bathtub mf is the worst offender; it's painfully boring to wait for him to attack you and lose his stamina/get his bathtub stuck three times in a row.I don't know, man. There are so many people that love it that I almost feel bad and weird for writing this, but I just really don't get the appeal. Except for nostalgia and graphics, the game doesn't offer much, especially for that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for September 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before October 1st, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A classic Collectathon SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is impressive. You can just tell someone to put in the extra effort in everything on this title. The cut scenes are well-animated with a style that is way above what I was expecting. I didn’t, it just wasn’t smooth. Also, sometimes players will be confused about what is expected of them, but not too often. The controls are smooth. It’s more of a question of what is possible. One thing I will bring up is the voice cast. The entire cast is back to my knowledge, and it brings me back to the original cartoon. I do want to call out Bill Fagerbakke. His line delivery as Patrick made me laugh so many times in the first hour. Pick this up if you’re a fan of Spongebob, or just like a good collectathon. The level design here is great. _childDocuments_.review: look. i am probably the biggest 'casual fan' of the classic spongebob duo for the ps2/xbox/gamecube. BFBB and The Movie Game were my favorite games as a kid. Which makes me extremely sad to say how *agonizingly mediocre* this is. Which is sad! Because it was announced after favorable reviews of BFBB:Rehydrated, and it was by the same studio that brought us that (still good! but less good than the original in my eyes) game. So this is clearly intended to be a companion piece, a 'sequel' to battle for bikini bottom that wasn't associated with a (by now) classic movie.Unfortunately.. it's.. not great? They missed a lot of what made BFBB *good.* There were no 'quests,' no menu to track them, just the characters of bikini bottom telling you what needed to get done, and on occasion, meters to track collectibles. It was a true collect-a-thon. But this.. this is the World of Warcraft method of collecting. It's incessant backtracking and disappointing, unmemorable hiding places. The humor, also, leaves a lot to be desired. The few jokes that aren't "Hey, Remember the Show?" usually fall flat-- not to say there aren't a few ones that ushered a chuckle out of me, but most of them were mediocre. The enemies from Battle for Bikini Bottom all had a 'joke' associated with them (the Ham-Mer wielded a giant piece of ham, Slick was a bubble blowing baby, and the Tubelets were a bunch of rude little kids that you got a kick out of hitting.) but the classic environmental humor of The Cosmic Shake just seems to either be generic point-and-laugh "haha, look, it's a CUBE" style humor, or.. again.. "remember the show" vis a vis the Enemy Spawner (everybody run, it's the Appetizer!).This may all sound like it's failing to live up to the expectations set by the company's previous title, a remaster of a beloved cult-classic Nickelodeon title. But it's important to say, sadly, the game fails on it's own merit.The moveset, devoid of comparison to the original title, leaves a lot to be desired. It attempts greatly to be smooth, with moves leading into each other (or at least, that's what I take away from it). Unfortunately, the game seems to announce it's best moves (a flying kick that locks onto enemies, like Sonic's Homing Dash, and Grappling-- a stiff, clunky move that Sandy had in Rehydrated. They're so similar I'd wager the code was lifted straight from their previous project.) way too soon, leaving the rest of the game feeling uneventful amd gimmicky.The story, if you came to it for story, also leaves something to be desired. To summarize, Spongebob gets a magic bubble wand, and makes an inordinate amount of wishes, causing a multiversal-level catastrophe. In order to fix it, Spongebob teams up with the (clearly telegraphed villain) mysterious Madame Kassandra. We will get to her in a moment. Despite the ambitious more in-depth planned plot, it detracts from the gameplay of the moment, making every level seem dedicated to running through as fast as possible, beating the boss (which is usually the character you came here for. i don't know why they're fighting you, even after beating the game.) and then going back in to do a side quest or two (which is always 'collect 5 objects.') So mediocre.Now, back to the antagonist, Madame Kassandra. She appears to be one of the devs' Donut Steele level ocs, a disappointing villain on all fronts, and nowhere near as satisfying a villain as any of Heavy Iron's ps2/gamecube titles. Now.. this is where it gets disappointing, vis a vis the characterization. She appears to be heavily inspired by the stereotypes surrounding Romani people, or 'G*psy.' I am not at liberty to speak on issues on behalf of the Romani people-- because I do not know nearly enough about their culture. However! I can tell that "Caravan-Riding G*psy Mermaid who never displays anything but wanton lust for power and a propensity for stealing" is.. not a great look! But, again, I'm not at liberty to say.But, all in all, for every good thing this game does, there's at least two bad things sandwiching it. Really disappointing on all fronts, especially considering how ready I was to let Purple Lamp show off their game-development chops on a brand new, original title. Unfortunately, it seems Purple Lamp has very little originality to show for it, and what they do have I'd rather they'd keep.4/10. A passable experience.. in the sense of 'No thanks. I'll pass.'

_childDocuments_.review: I love the smell of bubbles in the morning. Smells like... victory.Pros:* Well crafted worlds, stories, and situations to play in. I was never bored!* The move-set and game progression was greatly improved from the predecessor. * Most importantly, it pays honest tribute to SpongeBob! Cons: (Spoiler Free)* The final boss and ending was a letdown. It was too easy and short when compared to other battles. * Audio transition problems with music. This happened for most early game events. Sometimes music would even stop playing for boss battles, although I am sure this will be patched in the near future!* (Some) Empty promises. For example, one level constantly remarks about a certain character being a threat, and they build it up as you get closer, but we never see said character. It makes the game feel dishonest and cut short. As someone with a lifelong love for the franchise and videogame series, I wholeheartedly adored this experience. Adoration aside, this is a joyful experience that anyone can have nautical nonsense with under the sea.

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me feel so nostalgic. I remember playing SpongeBob on my old Xbox as a kid while visiting family in Bosnia. I would sit inside and play while it rained, or while the 40+ degree weather was hitting its peak around noon until I could go back outside with friends. To put it more simply, playing this game for me is kind of what the dish in Ratatouille is for the critic when he takes his first bite. I am instantly transported to simpler times, and my heart is happy.Everything runs extremely well and the game is graphically beautiful. The colours all pop and the new worlds you can explore are unique. Even the writing is great. I have found myself giggling quite a bit under my breath the past couple of hours while playing. The dialogue suits each character very well, and the voice acting is good, too, despite what some other reviews seem to think.While the game is "linear" in the sense that you have a primary quest to follow, I have been exploring around quite a bit to find gold items and the like. There is definitely a sense of freedom here that many platformers fail to have. Jumping is smooth and I have no complaints about any of the controls! I am currently playing with my keyboard and mouse but I will almost definitely play later on my Steam Deck with its controller. I have no doubts that it will run well there since I played the first game on Switch.This game is a fun, funny experience and it instantly has become one of my comfort go-tos. The world(s), characters, narrative design, music, everything... it works so well!  It was worth every penny in my opinion. Nostalgia, nostalgia, nostalgia! Now, if only I could get my hands on SpongeBob-shaped mac and cheese once again...

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a neutral option for reviews, if so I'd use it. Gonna go for Positive so the game doesn't get buried, I guess. _childDocuments_.review: The creative team at Purple Lamp have done it again with SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake! The game has players follow the yellow and lovable square sponge that we all know and love, in a quest to save his friends and his beloved underwater town of Bikini Bottom.In typical SpongeBob fashion, after acquiring a magic bubble blower from a mermaid named Kassandra, both SpongeBob and Patrick have some fun, causing the ensuing chaos that leads to the games story.The story is amusing; foremost, it is both interesting and humorous, leaving nods to the show all over its fantastically built levels. Dialogue is amazing, and on point. The story never made me feel bored, keeping me engaged the entire time. It felt as SpongeBob as SpongeBob could ever feel. Hats off to Purple Lamp for the creative and fun original story!Just as the remake to Battle for Bikini Bottom was stunning, Cosmic Shake takes it even more beyond that. The visuals are taken straight from the show and plastered all over the game. Each level is filled with details as well as gags that should not be missed. This has to be the most visually pleasing and stunning SpongeBob video game to date.The game is not super mechanical, however, there is a nice list of moves that you can do and mess around with, making it a very enjoyable experience! With newly added dodging, players can move out of the way of danger as well as use it for a slight boost in movement. You can double jump and now glide, allowing players to fall with style. There are others, but I won't spoil it. Attacking is just about the same as it was in the remake of Battle for Bikini Bottom, except with the added bonus of costumes (more on that below).THERE ARE COSTUMES, AND GOOD ONES TOO! Yes, that is right, costumes. I can now dress as a clown and defend my underwater home! The costume selection is great, with many costumes fans can enjoy playing in, most notably, a hard-hatted war hero. Seven costumes are locked behind a "DLC" paywall, which is quite sad, but there are 35 other costumes to enjoy if you so wish not to spend money on it.Costumes have another added feature that most might miss, while some costumes have changes and other don't, keen eyed players will notice that when attacking regularly, SpongeBob's weapon of choice changes just as well!Even though they don't serve much purpose other than being really, really cool. Players can have fun dressing up a sponge in this great addition to the game.They're fun, however, they aren't as challenging as I would have liked, and no, I don't want a Soulslike SpongeBob game (although that sounds kinda funny and I would probably play it). I just hoped that they wouldn't be as simple as dodging an attack, and within two minutes the battle would be over. I will say that some are different from others, but overall, are very easy to beat, making it feel as if there is little to no challenge in these fights.I felt that I should add this as I've seen reviews about people disliking them. They aren't all that bad. I mean, yes, they're kinda just there. Regardless, they are still enjoyable.Cosmic Shake has seven unique levels for the player to enjoy. They're each amazing and beautifully well made, leaving the player to want to explore as much as they possibly can.As aforementioned, the dialogue is amazing in this game; however, the lack of no auto-dialogue options/button is very much missing. Many times SpongeBob speaks and as he's cut off, the game requires the player to make an input causing a sort of weird stoppage to the pleasing dialogue that is expected to continue. The developers should take note of this and (hopefully) add it to their next game to come.The lack of extra/more phrases is very much apparent. I must have heard three phrases over and over throughout the seven levels the game possesses. One particular phrase, "sticky sweet", not only had me and my friend laughing, but had me just as annoyed for the 100th time.This may sound deranged, but, I wish there were more loading screens. This is the only game where I've wanted to see as many loading screens as possible. They are perfect nods to the show, directly ripped from those infamous time cards that appear in it.Finally, those pictures. If you know, you know.This is a great start to what is hopefully the beginning of new SpongeBob video games. I hope (more like pray) that Purple Lamp continues to create fun experiences for fans of the show and games alike!Gameplay mechanics are great and work well.Visually pleasing to look at, my eyes never hurt once, having me glued to my screen just as I did watching the show.Roughly 9 hours for main story.Roughly 12 hours for 100% completion.Personally, I would recommend purchasing at full price, but as always I have to say, wait for discount/sale.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Given the chance, I would do unholy things to SpongeBob if I could get into one of his holes… This is a game for kids, just like Dark Souls. Got this for my 8 year old autistic nephew and he has never been so quiet. I'm 35 years old, so naturally I loved this game too.One of the best adventure games ever made. Played it multiple times, and it never fails to get me all immersed. The lines, the visuals, the music, the costumes, they're all filled with SpongeBob nostalgia; I loved it! What an honorable love letter of a game.This game wasn't designed to be the next groundbreaking gaming experience. It was designed to be a SpongeBob experience for fans of the franchise. The average person isn't going in expecting it to change the industry, they're buying it to see the wacky sponge man cause mischief with the bloated pink balloon for a few hours.It's great, the levels are long but well designed and don't overstay their welcome, the story and humor are based on the early years of the series rather than the modern episodes, classic characters like King Neptune (who was retcon'd in Sponge On The Run) make a return and are all voiced by the original voice actors, the new characters like Kassandra are great and feel right at home in the SquarePants universe and my favorite part, THE SLAPPING SOUNDTRACK, every SpongeBob fan should play this!There’s many throwbacks to older episodes. Such as voiceline references, some pictures and level settings. The developers definitely have love for SpongeBob and it’s shown throughout the game. Also I loved using different costumes for SpongeBob. Despite you only playing as SpongeBob in this game, I didn’t mind it. I loved the constant SpongeBob and Patrick chemistry as he always follows you around in the game and it did make me laugh a good amount of times. Don’t go into this expecting it to play like Bikini bottom though, BFBB is a collectathon where you walk around and do tasks for golden spatulas, while this game is a lot more linear and you just go point A to point B with a lot less exploration. Games graphics are really nice looking and the gameplay is fun overall. If you’re a SpongeBob fan and have played previous games 100% pick it up
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: This review is coming from someone who really liked Battle for Bikini Bottom. As a BFBB lover, this game is only okay to me. It nails story, the platforming feels good and reminds you of the previous game and the characters and dialogue are all great, but to me it's a total miss in one very important category and that is the level design, which in my opinion is one of the most important aspects of a 3D platformer. They basically took BFBB and put it "on-rails" which I personally don't really like. The game points you to your next objective, you go to the objective and push a button - then you go to the next objective and push a button, and so on. It would be a stretch to call BFBB an "open-world" game, but it was certainly not on rails to this degree, and Cosmic Shake really doesn't encourage exploration or going off the path it is point you through at all. To me, it comes down to level design. B4BB took elements from open-world games and made them work on relatively small levels because the game was not forcing you to only go in one direction to get to the objective, and perhaps also because it was not telling you with arrows and objective markers exactly where to go and how to get there. It seems like Cosmic Shake has you run through the level once with no reason to return to any parts of the level you've already been to, whereas BFBB made full use of the levels by having your return to same areas to accomplish different goals or objectives and interacting with the same part of the level in different ways. It is still a decent game, so pick it up if you love SpongeBob and I'll give it the recommended thumbs up, but I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a bit disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake offers a nostalgic journey through the beloved cartoon's universe.The game features straightforward platforming mechanics reminiscent of early 2000s 3D platformers. While these abilities provide a solid foundation, some players may find the gameplay lacking in innovation. While the main campaign lasts around 10 hours, The Cosmic Shake offers some additional content for completionists, these extras provide some incentive for replay, though their appeal may vary depending on the player's interest in full completion.The Cosmic Shake takes players through seven distinct "Wishworlds," each themed after different SpongeBob episodes or concepts. These colorful and vibrant environments offer a visually appealing backdrop for the adventure. However, the platforming challenges are relatively simple during the game.One of the game's standout features is its soundtrack. The Cosmic Shake combines recognizable SpongeBob tracks with original video game tunes, creating a delightful audio experience that captures the essence of the show.  In addition, the voice acting is another highlight, featuring performances from the original SpongeBob cast. This attention to detail helps bring the characters to life and adds authenticity to the experience.In conclusion, SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake delivers a solid, if somewhat dated, platforming experience wrapped in the charm and humor of the SpongeBob universe. You should try the game if you love 3D platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty worthy followup to Battle for Bikini Bottom and is definitely in Top 3 SpongeBob games for me. It starts off a little too simple and easy for my liking, but picks up when there's more enemy variety and when there are more abilities available to the player.The costumes all look great and are fun to collect, but if you don't care about cosmetics then there may not be a lot here to hook you. The levels are pretty straightforward and short if you're not going out of your way for the optional collectibles, and there aren't any other unlockable bonuses besides the costumes (and achievements, I suppose).As someone who hasn't really been following new episodes of the show that closely for about 10 years, I was pleasantly surprised by the charm and wit in the game's writing. Not every joke lands, and the cutscenes in particular are paced very strangely, but there's tons of references to the show's first 3 seasons and I got a laugh out of some of the game's original jokes as well.Cosmic Shake is just good, solid, simple fun, and kept me busy for a good week combing through every world to get all the costumes. Fans of SpongeBob, particularly chad Battle for Bikini Bottom enjoyers, should get a kick out of this game, and I'd recommend it to them. If you're not personally attached to BFBB, but still enjoy 3D platformers, I say check that game out instead, or wait for this one to go on sale first.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed as of writing this review: 100%As one of the people who have completed Heavy Iron’s trilogy (BfBB, Movie and Tr.or Sq.), I think this is a great comeback of the old SpongeBob. Yes, I’ll admit that the charm of BfBB is still yet to be repeated, but it’s really close to it, with many cool references and how a cast of characters is being treated. The levels were very well constructed, even if they’re just a one road now (well like in a movie game basically), they’re still fun to play. The music is fine enough, though nothing special like in BfBB and Movie (the licensed songs comeback is amazing tho). The bosses were really well-designed (for the most part), except for the final boss, which was a huge letdown, most likely rushed for release. The gimmicks are also fun and SpongeBob’s moves are also satisfying to use. My only gripe with this game, is the replayability though. I’m not having any trouble with being told to collect things everywhere and replay the levels again and again. The problem was with guidance - there is none! My guidance was my friend, who googled everything to tell me the exact location, because I was tired of replaying the same level over and over. One of the doubloons in the first stage was a sick joke, because that’s the only time you use a mechanic (if you know, you know). Yes, I like the style of side-quests and how much they reference, but the quests themselves were so dull and tedious, because they were well hidden, but the game never tells in which part of the level you need to explore, which kinda defeats a whole point of exploration, because you’re empty-handed without any hints. Unfortunately there is no case of giving you a reward for 100% like was in BfBB and Movie game, instead you just get an achievement, like in many other generic games. I’m disappointed with 100% aspect of the game and it counts, because I was satisfied with all this in BfBB and the Movie game, which Cosmic Shake was trying to be a successor to. The other minor nitpick is the difficulty, but that’s a given for games for kids nowadays.Other than all that, I’m happy that SpongeBob is not in hands of that other publisher anymore, who didn’t care about SpongeBob for a whole decade. Now we got a real deal after like, what? 20 years almost? (Movie game came out in 2004) So yeah, it’s good to be a SpongeBob fan with this coming out and I can say that SpongeBob’s game series are in good hands once more!

_childDocuments_.review: Consider this a neutral review. If you were (or are) a kid who enjoyed Spongebob growing up, you'll probably enjoy this game. It is not as good as Battle for Bikini Bottom though. Its far more linear, has less interesting mechanics, poor sound design, weird bugs, poor attention to detail, and lacks polish. I 100% completed BfBB but after the credits rolled on this one, I think I'm probably done.One major gripe I have: It is a PC game with virtually no video options. The only video option is for screen resolution. That's unacceptable in 2023.  On the positive side, the writing is funny and it seems like they got the vast majority of the show's voice cast for the game. And the gameplay, while limited and linear, is solid and not frustrating (Unless you play with inverted camera controls. Those don't work while riding a seahorse or rolling around on a rock).

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ∞/10Review:SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake catapults players into an intergalactic escapade that transcends the boundaries of traditional gaming. As a fervent follower of SpongeBob's ventures, diving into this cosmic journey was an experience unlike any other. Brace yourself for an odyssey that defies gravity, logic, and perhaps even Bikini Bottom itself.Visually stunning and bursting with creativity, The Cosmic Shake delivers a visual feast that rivals the most vibrant galaxies. From the neon-lit streets of New Kelp City to the surreal landscapes of Neptune's Moon, every location is a testament to the boundless imagination of the developers.But it's not just the visuals that dazzle; the gameplay is equally impressive. Seamlessly blending platforming, puzzles, and cosmic shenanigans, each level is a kaleidoscope of challenges and surprises waiting to be uncovered. Whether you're bouncing through zero-gravity environments or dodging asteroids in space, the gameplay mechanics are as diverse as they are delightful.What truly sets The Cosmic Shake apart, however, is its narrative depth and emotional resonance. Beneath the zany humor and whimsical charm lies a heartfelt story of friendship, courage, and the power of imagination. As SpongeBob and friends embark on their cosmic quest, they confront their fears, overcome obstacles, and discover the true meaning of teamwork.Moreover, the game's replay value is astronomical, with a plethora of collectibles, side quests, and hidden secrets scattered throughout the cosmos. With multiple endings and branching paths, every playthrough offers a fresh and exhilarating experience that begs to be explored time and time again.In conclusion, SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake isn't just a game; it's a celestial odyssey that transcends the boundaries of imagination. Whether you're a seasoned SpongeBob enthusiast or a curious newcomer, this cosmic adventure is a must-play masterpiece that will leave you starry-eyed and grinning from ear to ear.Also one of the greatest games ever created.
