_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I'm a HUGE Spongebob fan - I've played and own most of the existing Spongebob games and I was able to notice almost every reference to the show in this game, which was very exciting! I appreciate how THQ Nordic took a lot of the existing elements from BFBB - Rehydrated, such as combat and art style, and went even further with it. The scenery in this game is beautiful, and every location is memorable! However, there are a few issues that hold this game back from being at the same level as BFBB - Rehydrated.As I mentioned earlier, this game is stunning. It's colorful, almost TOO colorful. Every location is a mix of older Spongebob references such as Prehistoric Bikini Bottom and Glove World with different overall concepts. I've seen others complain about this, but I LOVE the boss fights in this game. Each one is unique and well thought out. They're not overly difficult and vary from one another. The music is very fitting for each area and will likely be stuck in your head for a few days (I'm looking at you Wild West Jellyfish Fields). The new combat mechnics are pretty smooth, especially the new kick ability. I'm a bit sad that you can no longer use the Bubble Bash like in BFBB, but the new varitey of abilities more than makes up for it. I did encounter a few combat glitches, specifically the hitbox for certain enemies are a little wonky. There's a relatively long cooldown between Spongebob's primary attack that the game may not always recognize the next one.I'm so glad Clancy Brown reprised his role as Mr. Krabs. Clancy is notorious for being one of the only main cast members to not make an appeareance in many Spongebob games, so having him in this one was a treat.Enemy variety is pretty decent. I enjoyed almost all of the enemy types except for the Jelly Maker, that one was just downright annoying. They fall in line with the story pretty well, but honestly, I'm just glad we're not fighting robots anymore.THE COSTUMES are you kidding me??? There are SO many wonderful designs in this game that are well worth a 100% playthrough. I did pre-order the game to get the DLC skins, which were totally worth it, in my opinion. Coupled with the overall beauty of this game, the costumes make Spongebob stand out so well and serve as such cool callbacks to the show.I'm no audio expert, but this game seems to have weird sound mixing in most areas. Whenever the game transitions to a cutscene, an entirely different track plays for roughly 4-5 seconds, then cuts back to the theme of the world you're in. This happens A LOT and I don't really understand it. I'm also not a fan with how the cast memebers  in this game. I realize the voice actors for the cartoon have changed the way their characters sound in the last few years for the new, younger audience, coupled with the fact that the actors are getting older, but Spongebob's voice sounds much more... forced? He doesn't *sound* like Spongebob to me. Same goes for Sandy and Mrs. Puff. It's almost like the VA's are doing impressions of their own characters? As for the gameplay, The Cosmic Shake hides a lot of collectibles behind upgraded abilities for Spongebob that you'll have to go back and obtain later in the game. That's great and all, I really enjoy backtracking, but the menu doesn't really help you find the general area of where that collectible would be, unlike BFBB - Rehydrated. You're never sure what you're actually looking for in these levels once you eventually go back, which I'm really not a fan of. It's not a huge deal since the levels aren't that big, but since they're so linear it's not ideal to run through each level from start to finish all over again.Finally, the story, in my opinion, is not very strong. Which is fine... it's not a huge deal to me considering it's just a Spongebob game, and I wasn't expecting anything elaborate. Kassandra is... okay I guess? Her design is very cool, but I don't really understand why she's a villain, if that makes sense. The intro arc to this game () does not fall in line with how the story plays out at all, which I found very weird.As a fan of the original cartoon, I'm very impressed with all the references to the early (and some newer) seasons of the show. The costumes were a huge plus for me and made up for the fact that we can no longer swap characters like we could in BFBB. Level and boss variety is great but I wish there was an incentive to replay the game. The story took about 7-8 hours to complete and a little over 20 to 100%. I would say wait until it goes on sale, if you're interested, but don't sell this game too short! I hope to see more titles like this from THQ Nordic in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The Cosmic Shake is a fun and worthy successor to the Battle for Bikini Bottom remaster. You can tell right away that the game is basically a sequel - the control scheme is the same, SpongeBob has most of the moves that were spread across him, Patrick, and Sandy in BfBB, and even with the change in general aesthetic, the graphics are just like BfBB. The big change is that SpongeBob is the only playable character, and that the stages are all linear in design with a clearly defined starting and ending point, though there are plenty of branching paths for side missions and hidden content, evoking the feeling of BfBB's wide open stages at times. I think this is a good change, given the scope of the game - it keeps it focused and rolling forward from start to finish, shifting your attention away from the extremely simple story and centering the pitch-perfect tone of the jokes and gags instead.I will say that for all the ways in which marketing focused on the costumes, I found the feature completely inessential, and it didn't feel satisfying to try and find the collectibles that would allow me to unlock the higher costume tiers. I also found myself drifting away from the game after a few hours, with a couple of bosses that were disproportionately difficult, especially compared to the overly-easy final boss. Though I was fine with the bare-bones story, it does leave you feeling like you're not especially sure why you're doing anything, aside from being told by the main villain to romp through the levels. on the whole, though, the critiques I have are no big deal - it's a well-made, fun platformer, so it's worth it if you like the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr A mediocre platformer wrapped in Spongebob assets.  This is not a proper successor to the previous BfBB Spongebob game. Spongebob's voice lines are also pretty repetitive.  I hope I pick it back up later and find a reason to delete this review.EDIT: Nope..  EDIT 2: After returning this game, I went back and replayed the entire previous title BfBB and loved it.  Here's why it's better: Multiple collectibles placed in fun places that reward exploration, multiple characters with unique playstyles, myriad references to the show from the collectibles to the levels to the dialog, proper level design that rewards returning to it later, more levels, better boss battles, better map fast travel system, I could go on..  Ultimately these developers ignored the entirety of what made BfBB such a great title, which is a shame because they had an excellent template for a successor.  Cosmic Shake is a lazy cash grab by comparison, and they have the audacity to charge for DLC like costume packs.  Brave new world..:(

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game on a sale if you can get it. Took me roughly 8.4 hours to complete the main game and I do plan on going back to 100%ing it, however.. I know it's not going to be that good going back to 100%.Overall, Spongebob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is a 6.6 / 10. It's not a fantastic game, but it's not like it's a bad game either. It's a serviceable game that does its job of being a fun platformer with some challenges. Some of the pros of this game in terms of gameplay is pretty much the combat & fluidity of moves into each other. I think the combat can be a *little* stiff at times, but it's not terribly stiff and all the moves can flow well into each other. Landing combos from Karate Kick to Ground Pound followed by a dodge to bubble blow are very satisfying and I love the amount of variety to them. The story itself is also fine, leans more to classic Spongebob naivety mixed with his own emotions of discomfort and disdain at times. It's clear the writing is moreso modern Spognebob, but I do commend the team for working with the newer stuff. The worlds are also pretty cool and varied around with the amount of costumes that Spongebob can dawn on be plentiful. It's also cool to see citizens and other characters being portrayed in their said worlds differently too, just wish the enemies were like that akin to how you had the possessed Bikini Bottomites in Spongebob Squarepants The Movie: The Game.Now onto what makes the game very.. lackluster. The game tends to get pretty repetitive pretty quickly and while most Spongebob games tend to do this, I just wish there was some variety within the worlds. It's also clear that some things for doubloons or side objectives get little treatment since you're repeating the same abilities over and over again, which is a shame as I liked the areas where I had to chain together different techniques to get to different platforms. Like in the medieval world I remember having to chain together a Bubble Blow to open up a platform, use the Pizza Glide to get to said platform, and then jump towards and do a Lasso Swing. That was fun, that was cool. I wish this was in a good amount of the platforming. Also movement can be pretty stiff, but it's not terribly stiff. Going forward or backward wasn't terribly bad, felt a bit weird at times, but comparing it to Rehydrated Spongebob's turning was just god awful to perform and he seems to slow down when doing so? It's not a major turn off, but it definitely needed more tweaking and refinement. Also the final boss Overall just underwhelming fights & movement with some actual decent writing and great combat makes The Cosmic Shake get the grade of 6.6 / 10. For me personally, it means it's worth player so long as you're willing to get through some parts of slog.Edit: 12:43 EST @ 2/3/2023 - Just completed the 100%. No guides whatsoever, meaning if you want to go and find everything in the worlds, it's pretty simple to do so. There's a couple extra side things that go off, but that's about it. I'd say the hardest of the Achievements / Awards to get is the "No Get Hit" during the Royal Ballroom Boss. It's just making sure you don't bombrush each cake. Won't say much else.

Fortunately, I found a guide online, so it wasn't the end of the world.I spent around seven hours completing the main missions, but I still have side quests to tackle. It’s fun revisiting the maps to take on challenges again and hunt for hidden gems.If you’re on the fence about getting this game, I wholeheartedly recommend you go for it—you won’t regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, where do I even begin with this one? SpongeBob Schwammkopf: The Cosmic Shake is a game that will leave you scratching your head in confusion, laughing out loud at its bizarre humor, and wondering what the developers were smoking when they came up with some of the levels.First things first, let's talk about the story. SpongeBob and his pals are on a mission to save the universe from destruction by collecting cosmic energy in the form of golden spatulas. Along the way, they encounter strange creatures and visit even stranger worlds, all while trying to avoid the clutches of the evil Plankton. The story is pretty standard for a SpongeBob game, but the levels are where things get really weird.In one level, you play as Patrick as he tries to avoid getting crushed by giant hamburgers falling from the sky. In another, you play as Sandy as she navigates a maze of cheese in outer space. And in perhaps the strangest level of all, you play as Squidward as he tries to escape a nightmare version of his own mind. The levels are all wildly different and keep the gameplay fresh and interesting.The controls are fairly simple and easy to pick up, but some of the levels can be quite challenging. The difficulty level ranges from easy to frustratingly difficult, so be prepared to die a lot if you're not careful. However, the game is forgiving enough that you won't get too frustrated, and the checkpoints are well-placed so you don't have to repeat too much if you mess up.The graphics are colorful and vibrant, just like the TV show. The character models are spot-on and the environments are imaginative and strange. The music is also great, with catchy tunes that will get stuck in your head long after you've turned off the game.But the real star of the show here is the humor. SpongeBob has always been a show that appeals to both kids and adults, and the game is no different. The jokes are clever and silly, and there are plenty of pop culture references to keep the adults entertained. One level even has a boss fight against a giant robot version of David Hasselhoff, which is just as ridiculous as it sounds.Overall, SpongeBob Schwammkopf: The Cosmic Shake is a fun and entertaining game that is sure to delight fans of the TV show. It's weird, it's strange, it's bizarre, and it's funny as hell. If you're looking for a game that's a little bit different and a lot of fun, give this one a try. Just be prepared for some weirdness along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I've been pondering something. When people say "This plays like a PS2 game", I don't think of it as a pejorative, I think of it as back when video games had soul and didn't exist solely for profiting while pretending to be about artistic merit. Guess we can add this game (alongside Hi-Fi Rush) to the list of games this year that either hit the right buttons (nostalgia speaking, being familiar in the right ways while still being fresh), are mostly exempt from the modern AAA or Japanese fashion of shipping broken/busted (and never getting patched) or with a load of contemporary hot-button subtext that weighs down the focus, or that are truly like the PS2 era in terms of experimenting around with gameplay.The gameplay mechanics in this are refined compared to BFBB (both the original and Rehydrated) and the Movie Game (A point where a bunch of people say the TV-show flatlined after, which is nearly 20 years ago). There's a ton of new abilities in SpongeBob's arsenal, such as dodging, gliding, karate kicks, and so-on. The best way I can explain this game is like SpongeBob: Truth or Dare, if it wasn't the result of executive meddling. None of the Camp Corral or Sponge on the Run crap here, this game mostly references older episodes ad-nauseum and doesn't constantly contradict itself (and even references some of the stuff from Season 4, such as the Karate Island episode), and I say this in a good way. If I were to play a drinking game of spot the SpongeBob reference, I'd actually die of alcohol poisoning (and this is while taking the fact that I dropped off the show after Season 4, when the show mostly became obnoxious and full of gross-out humor for the sake of it). This actually feels like a love letter to the series (without the shackles of a remake like BFBB Rehydrated), while not defecating/urinating or spilling a bucket of semen mixed with cow blood (Metallica style) on Stephen Hillenburg's grave (Like Sponge on the Run and Camp Corral are).The worlds are rather linear (I finished the game), and I say it in a good way. None of the worlds overstay their welcome (In contrast to the Kelp Forest in BFBB which dragged on for way too long), and the game still leaves areas to explore when you get new abilities, so you can revisit and collect things when you are interested. The ending falls a bit flat. The bosses and worlds put a new spin on familiar environments, and even has areas like Glove World in the hub area, or references to stuff like Fred (the chocolate guy), Plankton's pet Spot, or the Hash Slinging Slasher. It's not a collectathon in the traditional sense (or like the original BFBB was), but there's enough substance here to have replay value while not being a slog for people that just want to play w/o the fat. The lighting in a bunch of areas looks great.There are a few things to keep in mind if you have sensory or photosensitivity issues however (I.E: autism spectrum disorder, where sensory issues are a thing, or in the case of epilepsy, seizures/blackouts from flashing lights). The game's generic photosensitive seizure warning isn't specific enough about what causes problems in the game, and this is a worrying pattern with game releases that offer accessibility options but don't do basic things or give players some discretion regarding whether or not the game is going to go out of it's way to be as safe to play as possible (Remember, seizures and blackouts can cause injuries). When you walk close to the explosive Tikis, they will rapidly flash red and yellow (Similar to it's behavior in BFBB Rehydrated, the shouting text in Gal*Gun Returns before it got patched, or something like the KO text in Sonic the Fighters, to list three examples), I've managed to somewhat work around this by using the bubbles to hit the tikis from a distance. There is also a portion in the second world where you have to do a QTE that involves camera flashing (Which flashes a white overlay on screen), and that involves rapidly pressing the left mouse button. While I'm aware that the QTE probably cannot be changed, it's really questionable why the explosive tiki effects have not been modified in either BFBB Rehydrated or this game. The game's accessibility options mostly consist of just subtitle options and a simple colorblind filter (that isn't the same as modifying UI elements to look correct or distinct with different types of colorblindness).The most that I can really say about the PC release in particular is the lack of graphics options (Something of which has became a bit of a problem with Unreal Engine games, which is funny considering how scalable the engine is), the Vert- FOV scaling (which zooms in on the game FOV with anything wider than 16:9, despite the game's HUD not having any noticeable problems), or the keyboard/mouse support needing work (the lack of rebinding and forced mouse acceleration are here sadly). The fact that you can't disable depth of field, camera vignette, or chromatic aberration is a bit sad, and the developers seemingly have removed the option for the engine to read values from a config file (Resulting in there being no flexibility if you want to tweak things to run or look fine on your setup). For the time being, you need to use Universal Unreal Unlocker to set the FOV to about 100 (at 21:9) or 110 (at 32:9) if using an ultrawide monitor, or use it to adjust graphics options that the game doesn't expose normally. Judging by the Steam Deck, I'd recommend playing with Unreal's Temporal Upscaling (and Gen2 TAA) and ~75% resolution scaling (Reason being to keep the game UI sharp and artifact free, which the system's FSR support doesn't do) to get close to locking to 60FPS (rather than being stuck with a 40FPS cap due to the game's lack of graphics options).I've played a majority of my playthrough on KB/M, as Bluetooth was acting up on my system (and preventing my controllers from working), and I can say that the controls are a bit confusingly laid out. Having the option to rebind my controls to something that I find comfortable would be great. There are some UI elements (Like when you get freezed by certain enemies) that don't display KB/M prompts as well. The game also lacks any sort of PlayStation controller support (Outside of SteamInput controller emulation), a reversed A/B menu layout (for Nintendo controllers), or button prompts for different types of controllers, for the people that aim to dismiss the criticisms about keyboard/mouse support with "JuSt UsE a CoNtRoLlEr", so unless you have an Xbox controller, it's going to be a subpar experience.Outside of those port issues, the game runs without any noticeable framerate cap, outside of VSync (Which honestly is a better approach than attempting a framerate cap using hardcoded 30/60/90/120 options, as that gives the user more flexibility if they have refresh rates that don't line up with 60Hz (or don't have FreeSync) and that don't want to bother with Exclusive Fullscreen or changing the refresh rate on every game startup), if you need a limit, you will have to use an external limiter like RTSS or Special K, this is probably for the better. Runs like butter on my 6700XT+Ryzen 5 5600X (at a mostly locked 175FPS and at 3440x1440), so they clearly optimized the game with last-gen consoles in mind (Which is a good thing, nowadays you'll see cases like Halo Infinite where it runs with weird performance issues that straight-up didn't exist on even the Xbox One). No shader compilation stutter (like other Unreal Engine games) here, as it uses DirectX 11 instead of 12.This is very similar to Sonic Frontiers in terms of actually interesting me (a long-time fan that has grown tired of the semantics) after many years of mediocrity and uninterest/apathy. I'm glad I wishlisted this game and kept tabs on it before release. It has met my expectations so far. Fix the port issues, and do something about the red/yellow strobing Tikis, and I won't have any big complaints about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I went in with high expectations since I enjoyed the last game a lot, and sadly felt a bit let down after all.________________________________________________________________________________Likes:Design: The visuals are great and the details how the world is built as well. Even though there were a few assets noticeable reused I was through ought the whole time playing impressed by the designers work and the ideas converted.Gameplay: The slide system definitely improved from the last game. Overall I enjoyed the pace the game allowed me to have while playing through it. Skip-able cut scenes, dash mechanics, roll spam aso.  I also liked that it felt new and refreshing from the previous title.  I loved to karate kick enemies. Playing with different outfits also added some fun to the table. The only improvement I can see here is to change voice-lines according to outfit since sheriff SpongeBob most likely wont say 'Oogaa'. (I am not referring to cutscence since the outfit always changed into the story mission original during them)Level design: I wish I would be able to state more positives here but for me the only thing that I found good about the level design, is the fact that there were slopes to walk to everywhere. This let me explore more of the world and gave me the opportunity to actually seek items and loot since there was the chance to find something behind any corner.______________________________________________________________________________Dislikes:Length: I played through the game with 100% achievements in 11 hours active game play. Level design: Very linear, the player feels a lot of the times hold at his hand while walking through. Also jumping puzzles were usually just rewarded with currency and not even a lot. Therefore doing some side jumps for 5 jelly felt very underwhelming and lame. Finding treasures was also quite easy which ended in an underwhelming feeling of achievement.Difficulty: It was very much too easy. Overall enemies were either tedious while being easy to fight due to multiple health bars, or just one shot by any source of dmg. This created overall a rather boring combat experience.Similar goes for the platforming aspect. The platforming was partially so boring that i turned the camera in circles while platforming. The last game had better and more interesting platforming. Sometimes I also thought the devs did not relay think before designing the jumps and just randomly placed objects to parkour. I say so, because there were plenty of quite obvious ways of cheesing through complete parts by either jumping on boxes or by pulling up ledges. Probably missed therefore a ton of puns but yeah it didn't at all caught my attention. (without skipping the story you maybe get an hour overall of extra content I would assume)Gameplay: Minigames were ridiculous, most of them were quick time events, or fighting waves of enemies. I bet the next game will be a banger and maybe then it would be the perfect time to buy this game on a decent sale. -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------TLDR:Overall too short of a game (10h-20h). _childDocuments_.review: It was just two years ago that we got Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated, a faithful remake of the original SpongeBob game that ended up being my personal game of the year... so you could say I was just a bit excited for this one.For those that have played Rehydrated, you can expect a lot of that same style of gameplay here. The game world is divided into areas where you need to jump, dash, and swing your way to victory and you’re given an assortment of tools to do so. Among these are some returning ones, like the ground pound, but also some really cool new ones, like the karate kick which is effectively identical to the homing attack from Sonic the Hedgehog.This mechanic in particular gives the game a nice sense of speed to it that the previous did not have and was easily my favorite of the new moves. That said, not all of them stick. Cosmic Shake introduces a seahorse riding mechanic, for example, that felt too “on-rails” for my liking. Like, you literally get the invisible walls and everything during these sequences and it is nowhere near as exciting as the tongue sliding segments of the previous game - which are still present in this game, just not to the same scale.The experience as a whole is a lot more linear, with some levels being these straightforward things and others having a bit of exploration, but not quite on the level where it felt like I was free from a set path. This might not even be a problem for some, but it made the game feel far less rewarding and challenging. I mean, yeah, it is a kid’s game at the end of the day, but I feel like Rehydrated struck a nice balance there that Cosmic Shake is now lacking.You also lose the ability to play as other characters, which sounds bad at first, but I think the devs actually did a good job giving SpongeBob all these other abilities to make up for it. Rope swinging, bubble surfing, karate kicking across the screen - it’s nice to be able to do all of this without having to worry about swapping characters at a predetermined location.The combat itself is practically identical to the last. Most enemies can be taken down with a simple swing of your basic attack, but there are a few that require a ground pound or karate kick to set up for that basic attack to finish them off. Nothing too complex and if anything, the enemy variety could have used just a bit more to reduce some of the monotony.As a whole, the game is relatively well-paced. Most levels last just long enough that you don’t get tired of the setting and the story moves quickly to match. The experience is slightly shorter than the last game, taking me just five hours to clear, which may be disappointing for some, but honestly, if they wanted to make this one any longer they would definitely need to up the enemy variety, boss fights, and exploration to make it worthwhile.The story is a plus. It has that same energy you’d get from a traditional episode of SpongeBob with all the one-liners and character cameos and the like, but with the added bonus of the devs really feeding into the culture surrounding this show with plenty of references to famous scenes from the series’ glory days. The hash-slinging slasher, the chocolate guy, SpongeBob’s famous mocking pose - it’s all there and although cheesy, it is done in good fun.The references continue when you get to the whole unlockable costume thing. In order to enter new areas, you’re given a new costume to match the theme - like pirate, prehistoric, etc. However, you’re also able to purchase new costumes using the collectibles you find and there are over 30 of these to choose from - a nice incentive to collect shinies as you play.Although I did not have issues like crashes or freezing, I did have numerous occasions where enemies would glitch into the ground, I would get stuck in-between some random objects, and all sorts of different audio issues. Whether that be audio clipping before finishing, audio starting abruptly, or just outright stuttering.On a grander scale, I feel like the game’s sound design could use some work. There are several scenes where it feels like there should be sound effects, but there just aren’t and it leads to such scenes coming off as empty.Otherwise, the game does at least run well. I played at 4k and hovered around 120 or so fps for the entire experience. It never really dipped below 100, but I should note that the game was also using my entire 3080 Ti, so it does run pretty hot.Settings-wise you get resolution, screen mode, Vsync, and gamma correction. That’s it. The controls also do not appear to be rebindable. I played through on a controller - which felt fine - but tested keyboard and mouse for this review and although those controls were also fine, the ability to rebind them is a must and is unfortunately lacking here. Overall, it’s a fairly straightforward PC port with just the bare minimum of options.The Cosmic Shake, while not quite as good as its predecessor, still manages to carve its own identity through its fun platforming and storyline. The new mechanics like karate kicking are genuinely fun to use and the experience is well-paced on top of that. That said, the game was a bit too linear for my tastes and not all of the new mechanics landed. Still a fun game and a worthwhile play if you enjoyed Rehydrated.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: *Are ya ready, kids?* Aye aye, captain! Because SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake—in my biased, life-long SpongeBob fan opinion—is the first great game of the year. The Cosmic Shake follows in the squeaky footsteps of SpongeBob and his lovably dumb best buddy Patrick Star as the immortal duo is induced by the mysterious and most-likely malevolent mermaid fortune teller, Kassandra, to rip apart the boundaries of space time by blowing some wish-granting bubbles made out of mermaid tears... because why not? What follows is a frequently funny Psychonauts 2 sorta journey into the innermost desires of Bikini Bottom’s long list of side characters: you’ll help squirrel sheriff Sandy hunt down a cactus-juice hoarding outlaw version of Mr. Krabs; you’ll cut off the sugar-rush of SpongeBob’s pet snail, Gary; you’ll star as the “Kar-Ah-Tay" Kid in Squidward’s high-budget action flick; and that’s only three of the seven insane journeys you’ll go on. Consider me impressed by The Cosmic Shake’s story in general, as it features a light-hearted and enjoyable if surprisingly well-paced plot, some of the most memorable characters in cartoon history, and the entire original voice cast (including Mr. Krabs, who sadly wasn’t voiced by the amazing Clancy Brown in developer Purple Lamp’s remake of The Battle for Bikini Bottom).  Before moving on from dialogue, do note that Tom Kenny’s delivery has dropped what feels like a full octave since my childhood, which was a little jarring at first, but hey... the dude is 60.  Whereas The Battle for Bikini Bottom featured multiplayer and multiple playable characters, The Cosmic Shake is all single-player SpongeBob all the time, unless you count your Patrick turned balloon/Mario Odyssey-esque Cappy companion who will occasionally save you from drowning or drop you an extra pair of health-restoring briefs when things get bleak. Which they actually will! After face rolling the game’s first world, I was feeling fairly underwhelmed with both the combat sequences and non-combat platforming sections. However, as the game introduces more and more “jellenemies” (that’s jelly enemies) and crazy movement mechanics from tongue-surfing to rock rolling, well, I ended up pretty impressed by the game’s fun and engaging mechanics.  Meanwhile, I don’t have much to say about the game’s simple UI, but the playability here is as solid as Patrick’s house. In addition to being largely bug-free and sporting snappy loadtimes, The Cosmic Shake controls well and the game’s difficulty deftly balances challenge with fun, thanks in large part to a forgiving checkpoint system. Really, even my platform-challenged wife was able to will her way through a whole world. Good job, wife. Speaking of world, the level and environmental designs in The Cosmic Shake are just awesome—super varied across all seven realms (eight if you count Bikini Bottom), and each features fun and unique objectives that rarely overstay their welcome. As the trailers suggest, at the end of each level, you’ll face a boss... “sequence,” we’ll call it, because fighting isn’t really SpongeBob’s style. Instead, you’ll dodge old witches and serve cakes to slumber party guests, suck up jellenemies with a reef blower before turning the gelatinous contents on an evil glove... yeah, it’s just a crazy time, and you can relieve each boss sequence after beating the game by using The Cosmic Shake’s friendly fast-travel system. Said system should aid the completionists out there, as The Cosmic Shake has quite a bit to discover. In addition to those golden spatulas from the first game and all of the cosmic jelly blobs scattered about the land, there are gold coins you need to unlock outfits that span the show’s millions of episodes. Thus, I do think there’s legitimate value here beyond The Cosmic Shake’s eight-to-ten-hour campaign, provided you like collecting things, and the level of love and polish crammed into every corner of the game does enough to justify that $40 price tag in my opinion.  Finally, a few words on style. As far as I can tell, The Cosmic Shake uses the graphics engine that did The Battle for Bikini Bottom, and it still looks pretty spiffy. That said, some textures are a little lacking and some in-game cutscenes drop frames, but wow do the animated cinematics look stellar. I also love the occasional cutaways to hand-drawn images a la the actual cartoon—great touch. The music and sound design, meanwhile, both benefit from the truly iconic and unmistakable magic of the show itself, but each go beyond what’s expected here to deliver an experience unique to the game. That said, a few sound effects are still missing, but a “Known Issues” email I received from the publisher suggests the devs are aware of most of these auditory issues.  In the end, The Cosmic Shake stands out as special in ways that few if any other games have managed to do in 2023. I’m giving it an aggregate MEGA score of 3.93/5 and consider the game a sweet, sweet victory. Thank you for reading! Curator:

_childDocuments_.review: "SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is a great time for anyone who is a big fan of the series and 3D platformers. The game serves as a worthy successor to Battle for Bikini Bottom while also expanding on SpongeBob's moveset and abilities, and stays true to the whimsical and nautical nonsense of the show with plenty of costumes and outfits. There are plenty of references and callbacks to the series for longtime fans. The story is pretty short and simple; the twist will probably not come as a big surprise to you if you pay attention and can be completed in about 6-8 hours. While BFBB was a homage to the golden era of the show, Cosmic Shake is geared more towards the more modern seasons and references. If you loved BFBB, you will definitely enjoy Cosmic Shake. I would highly recommend it."

_childDocuments_.review: There are better Spongebob games out there (Battle for Bikini Bottom stares disapprovingly from afar), however I have to say The Cosmic Shake has excelled more than any other Spongebob game as a love letter to the entire series. Music from the show is used regularly in and out of cutscenes and each level is peppered with references to multiple episodes - both old and new. I was genuinely suprised to hear and see some of these callbacks. The devs are very clearly lifelong fans of the show and I have to respect that as despite some personal issues with pop-in and feeling like the game is a bit too hand-holdy (but I am glad the hints are there for kids), I have probably enjoyed this game as a Spongebob fan more than any other Spongebob game I've ever played.Finally I think I have to appreciate that the team didn't just make a reskinned BFBB and instead did something different. They could have gone the easy route and instead decided to make something new - That's awesome. If you're a lifelong Spongebob fan I think as long as you can look past the fact this title was made with a younger audience in mind, it's probably the most straight-up enjoyable, fanservice-ey licensed game we've gotten in ages. I'd happily play another title from this studio if they put as much love into it as this ended up getting.

_childDocuments_.review: There are times this games was fun, but I don't think it stands well as a sequel to Battle for Bikini Bottom, or as a 3D platformer. With several of the voice cast being noticeably different and the awkward writing, I don't even think it stands great as a Spongebob experience. There's pretty much no reason to play this over Battle For Bikini Bottom unless you've gotten all you can out of that and this is on a steep sale. I would've had regret over purchasing this if I hadn't gotten it in a bundle. The level design is canned, the abilities are uninteresting, the combat is awkward and never feels properly challenging, the optional content just feels like time-fodder, and worst of all the level of polish on this is very poor in contrast to the other game. The only positive mark I can give this as a platformer is how the audio design is often referential to the previous game but remixed in a way that puts on a cool thematic twist and is otherwise really good. There's also some funny Spongebob references, but those are accompanied by a lot of overplayed ones that feel a bit like kicking a dead horse or looking at fan-art.I played the heck out of Battle For Bikini Bottom as a kid and then as an adult, and it's a top-tier 3D platformer. I knew this wouldn't quite compare, but I expected at least something a little more cohesive. I'm not sure if it was over-ambition and under-funding or what, but this game is a bit of a let-down to the genre as a whole. I'd give it a 7/10 and only recommend this if you really liked the original and feel like you gotta have more Spongebob platforming even if the quality is lower.

_childDocuments_.review: Spongebob Harlem Shake does exactly what it says from the getgo: a spiritual successor to 2005's Battle for Bikini Bottom. I'll begin with the speculatory side, the name and some of the ideas presented lead me to believe this game was in development for a fair bit. That out of the way the game utilizes the shows voice cast, the art direction is really true to the source material and overall feels like you're playing a modern version of a Spongebob 3d Platformer. Another positive this has over its predecessor is it feels a lot more finished towards the end, where the older game has levels getting shorter and more straightforward as it gets toward the end, the levels keep a consistent level of quality.Regarding the world, the game's levels are a lot longer than the other games, but much more linear in nature. The game itself is in its entirety Spongebob Theme Episodes, you know the ones where its like "this is medieval, this is prehistoric, this is spooky, this ones a kafkaesque commentary on the lines at theme parks" they stick to this format for better and for worse, and I was never offended by them, but I can see if someone thinks this is hot Dog Water.A sidebar, I've never been to Disney World, or Disney Land, I've been to the local fair and i was already vibrating in the 2 minute line how do you think i'd last in a 45 minute line to be angry on the splash mountain ride. I think you have to grow up exposed to that environment of slowly dying to be able to enjoy it for what it is.Overall decent game, its modern and it doesn't cost 90 dollars so it kind of screams "take me home tonight"

_childDocuments_.review: Had a blast playing the main campaign and I can solidly say that Cosmic Shake is a worthy successor to BFBB, though not without its problems.The game primarily shines, as it was the case with Rehydrated, through its visual art style and sound design, as well as the game's premise, storyline and character writing. The voice actors also did a phenomenal job bringing these characters to life, especially with lines that are reminiscent of early SpongeBob episodes.The levels felt engaging for the most part, though quality ranged widely from wishworld to wishworld. Stages like Prehistoric Kelp Forest felt a bit empty and uninspired compared to areas like Karate Downtown or Halloween Rock Bottom. I'm also not sure if the levels has become easier compared to BFBB or not, but I know is that level length and complexity did not increase progressively and ended up being sort of randomly dispersed throughout the main campaign.The platforming kept me hooked. Karate-kicking the balloons and gliding using the pizza box were engaging new additions and I'm glad to see Purple Lamp expand the formula. Patrick also serves as a lovely sidekick, providing you with health when running low and giving directions. Non-platforming features like the seahorse riding, the slingshot and other small features thrown in between segments kinda fell short unfortunately and I wish they would've been utilized more or given more attention to. The boss fights have also been a little clunky and inconsistent at times.These issues have been similarly prevalent in Rehydrated and it's a shame to see that those areas have not seen much of an improvement. I enjoyed the studios attempt to reintegrate cut content from BFBB by including Glove World and a Squidward boss fight, but it's unfortunate that these things, especially being the climax of the game, fell short too. It's a bummer, because you can feel the admiration the studio has for the SpongeBob IP, and I wish to see more time and resources given to perfecting all aforementioned areas for any future titles.That being said, if you enjoyed the Rehydrated treatment of BFBB from PurpleLamp, you'll likely have fun with this game too, despite its flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun and decent original new Spongebob game by Purple Lamp Studios The visuals were just as stunning, if not a little better than BFBB remake too. While I enjoyed a lot of the levels, especially the later ones, others did feel a bit lackluster.Sometimes I felt like there was a few pacing issues with a lot of stuff, including weird cutoffs in cutscenes.There was also a lot of minor bugs here and there, including weird tiki physics, general wonky physics and hit detection, and one major part where I softlocked the game.The new moveset for Spongebob felt great and way more fluid than before, especially the new dodge mechanic, though I do miss the old air and bubble ball attack.There are a lot of new enemies, and come with a lot of variety which is nice, though some are kind of "reskins" of old games (Tartar launcher enemy, etc), though I don't mind. Finally, there is a lot of emphasis on costumes this time around, though all of them are cosmetic only, they are pretty fun to use and wear, and there are a LOT of them, each referencing older episodes of the show, and each looks great. Overall good and fun game, but personally felt slightly off sometimes?If you loved the BFBB remake and just like Spongebob games in general, definitely get it, otherwise consider it on sale maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: I know there are many nostalgic folks out there who like me, played BFBB when they were kids and want to revive them glory days.This review is mostly directed to them.the game is worth it, it has everything you could ask for a modern platformer including collectibles and big worlds to explore(although most of them feel way too linear in comparison with bfbb). the game is pretty reminiscent of bfbb in terms of gameplay but it also expands spongebob's forms of attack and movement so it doesn't feel like a copy of it's predecessor. patrick and sandy are no longer playable and that makes the game stand way behind what bfbb had to offer in terms of variety of characters, but it isn't that big of a deal since playing as spongebob only is still very fun due to the many tricks and moves he learns through the game.One thing you need to consider tho, is that the game is marketed to the new generation of spongebob fans(kids aged 5-10), I'm not going to pretend like bfbb's dialogues and humor wasn't rather cringy and outdated for today's standards, but this game is on a whole new level, so if you play this prepare for some of the most forced kind of humor you can ever think of and jokes that would only make a 5 year old laugh. _childDocuments_.review: This game was one of my most anticipated releases ever, and I am happy to say it did not disappoint. However, even though this game is a spiritual successor to BFBB, you have to take it for what it is, it's own creation. It's not as open world as BFBB, it is much more linear, and the collectibles are largely for achievements, not progression, so don't expect the game to play like BFBBThe game is its own thing, and thats a good thing. The art style is great. The soundtrack is solid. The gameplay is fun, and includes some fun moments of variety within the levels themselves. The platforming feels good. The boss fights are interesting and unique, while not being overall too hard.That's not to say the game is perfect, I wish the combat sections weren't forced onto the player, and I also wish the abilities were able to be used more free form. The audio could use some work, as there were times the dialogue overlapped itself. And I do prefer a game where the progress feels more tangible than just get to the end of the levelOverall, this is a very worthy spiritual successor to BFBB, while being its own thing. 8/10 would recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a new Spongebob game to match the fun of Battle for Bikini Bottom and this one really does it. Even if you're new to Spongebob in general or prefer the newer episodes' humor, then this is still a magnificent 3D platformer. Definitely gets a thumbs up from me.

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable 3D platformer and a real treat for any Spongebob fan. Almost made me feel like a kid again at some points. :')Is it better than Battle for Bikini Bottom? In some ways, yes; the changes made to Spongebob's moveset are all great (the karate kick being my personal favorite), the visuals are a step up from Rehydrated (which already looked really nice), and the various references to the show (both the golden era and even post movie eras) never failed to put a smile on my face.I do wish some of the collectibles served a bigger purpose though. Jelly is only ever used to buy more costumes and nothing else, and the golden spatulas are just kinda there... they aren't required to progress the story, they don't even have an in game counter, they just... exist??? The final boss also left a lot to be desired, despite being pretty cool in concept.It's not perfect by any means, but it's still a fun time and a true love letter for Spongebob fans of all ages.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best official SpongeBob game to exist yet, there's so much love and attention to detail. This game actually had a decent sized budget which is crazy (stares at Nick All Star Brawl). The voice acting sounds good too, they managed to fix SpongeBob's weird sounding voice from the trailers (like some type of re-record).Purple Lamp did such a good job with everything from gameplay, to graphics (this is a SpongeBob game why the hell is the lighting impressive???). The gameplay is smooth and super responsive with fun mechanics from BfBB along with new stuff made for Cosmic Shake. Future SpongeBob games should use this game as an example of how to make a good SpongeBob title. Positives:- This game downright looks beautiful. No questions needed. Impressive.- Gameplay is great, and SpongeBob's abilities can combo into each other so well once mastered.- The level gimmicks and stage designs are super imaginative and even play into some SpongeBob tropes quite well.- The levels also does back tracking in a much better and more streamlined way to where certain major level events are permanently triggered once you revisit them, making the side stuff much easier to go back to without it being annoying.- The references are spot on in a way that doesn't feel forced onto you and instead respect you for knowing what they are (once again, stares at Nick All Star Brawl). The costume amount is just crazy as it references the old stuff along with the new stuff.- SpongeBob has a great moveset once you unlock all of his abilities. Ironically enough, his homing ability is better than Sonic's recent homing ability.The only downsides for this game is that:- This game is oddly resource intensive at times, causing subtle lag spikes.- It's super short (clocking at around 5/6 to hours while mostly going for everything). I wish it was longer :(- The collision can get buggy where SpongeBob can get stuck (and even cause a few softlocks).- Hitboxes on certain attacks and environmental hazards are poorly represented (looks at Sandy's fight).- SpongeBob's glide move has a broken animation (the Pizza Delivery reference is poorly represented as the Pizza doesn't popout and turn into a cheese parachute, instead it's a flying closed pizza box).TL;DRGo play this gameIt has flaws but it's an actually good game if you can look past them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really awesome game, it can be a bit wonky at times, but it's fun, charming, and beautiful, and I can't wait to see where Purple Lamp goes with SpongeBob games in the future!However, it should be noted that this is not exactly Battle for Bikini Bottom 2. BfBB is a 3D platformer with some combat and a collect-a-thon focus. Cosmic Shake is a 3D platformer with some collectibles and a focus on combat. The combat feels great in this game, but there's much less importance on the collecting aspect, nothing collectible in the game is required to beat it or progress, only the tasks put in front of you in each main questline through each world. Doubloons unlock the ability to purchase costumes, and Jellies are then used to purchase them. You don't need either of them to actually beat the game, making it feel much more linear and encouraging you to just play through each world once and only go back later to collect everything for 100% once you've unlocked all the abilities. It's strange too as Kasandra continues to tell you to bring her more Jelly, but there are never any times she actually charges you for Jellies you've collected. It's a bit of a shame, but I enjoyed this game a lot more once I realized how the game was structured differently from BfBB.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, this game is a love letter to Spongebob and I'm sure long-time fans will at least appreciate all the references put in, but I just do not like it. 35 hours because I left the game open, I haven't beat it entirely. I have made it through over halfway, though. So this isn't a premature review.It just feels like everything I liked from the old platformers are taken away. The collectathon aspect of them, to start. I don't mind it being linear, but even the Movie game was very fun because of the collectables. Here, there's still some present, but they're so much more boring to collect. They're just there in the world, no challenges or special missions to collect them most of the time. I also found collecting Golden Spatulas/GG tokens in the old games very satisfying because of the animation and sounds that play when Spongebob collects one. Collecting the more "important" collectables in this game is the same as collecting a normal one, which is lame. Even the normal collectables aren't as cool, since the old game, they had variation, different colors, different points given. Here, it's the same generic "blob".Some of the platforming moves also feel bad, but that may just be a personal problem. I really don't like how the glide move feels.The combat IS better than the previous games and the enemies are okay, though it's kinda sad because all the enemies feel very generic, too. Enemy variations like in the Movie game would be neat. The Movie game also introduced a cool upgrade system I liked, but any type of upgrades is absent here, which is fine, it's just sad.It feels like the little improvements Movie made over BFBB are just completely absent in general and it doesn't even feel like it does a good job at replicating what BFBB had in the first place.There's some other nitpicks and issues I have, which I won't get too much into. It's sad because I can't even recommend this as mindless fun, since it's a drag for me to even complete the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, laid-back game to play. Cut-scenes made the game feel like a long episode. The game is a joy to experience, mostly. The audio is not as memorable. Soundtrack from bfbb is far more memorable. Even the enemies from bfbb had their own pre-attack audio that let you know what type of enemy on around was about to hit you. Here in cosmic shake that hardly exists for any enemies.Gameplay is similar to BFBB- double jump, swing jellyfish net, ground pound attack. etc. This time only spongebob is a playable character. Just like BFBB, backtracking to previous worlds is necessary when you unlock more moves and want to unlock more collectables/costumes. Levels feel more linear than bfbb.Only a few bugs, stuck in a wall here, some stuttering there.At some points I do feel like the game was rushed. I beat the whole game, got all collectibles, did not get every trophy, in about 15 hours.Overall this is a fun game to to run down memory lane from all the references to different spongebob episodes. I do hope they add additional content in the future. Or even remaster other spongebob games like the movie game.If you want something laid back that doesnt require a lot of attention to detail and thinking, this is your game. Maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of BFBB, you'll like this game.Short review, this is a good game, with a lot of references to the show and solid gameplay. If you played BFBB or the movie game, you are going to notice that a lot of the mechanics are the same, although the game introduces new ones.I really liked playing the game, also it's not full AAA price.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr If you liked Battle For Bikini Bottom, you will like this game. The graphics are beautiful, the level designs and themes are really imaginative, SpongeBob is great to control, it's all I'd want from a BFBB Sequel. It can be a little rough around the edges.- The music is ok but gets repetitive hearing one song for like an hour on loop during a stage.- The Camera can go wonky in tight areas.- Patrick sometimes 'rescues' you and will drop you in the wrong place.- A lot of cutscenes are a bit unpolished, with abrupt BGM changes and characters poping around.- Not done with the game yet, but I wish you could explore inside of the Bikini Bottom buildings like you could in BFBB. The hub world feels a bit empty, and a step back from BFBB.- You will hear the same 5 lines over and over as SB jumps around.Overall none of that gets in the way of my enjoyment of it. This is a solid game so far. The game is a bit simple, but has enough flare to keep your attention.UPDATE: The game has mostly been without bugs, but loosing all your health and respawning in the Pirate level has consistently just stopped the BGM music from playing, the loops get a bit repetitive but it's better than pure silence lol.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine. I can overlook the ease and glitches. _childDocuments_.review: So I love Spongebob, and I loved Battle for Bikini Bottom Rehydrated. Cosmic Shake was bound to be good, right? And it is. _childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: This game just feels bad to play. Movement in a 3D platformer is the most important aspect of the gameplay IMO. The movement in The Cosmic Shake is beyond bad. Your basic speed is abysmal, and your jump height isnt variable at all. The glide feels so anemic, but every other unlocked ability feels like the animation speed was cranked way faster than necessary. The combat is my other big gripe. Beyond being incredibly simple, the "special" enemies are all seemingly designed to be as annoying as possible. Big impervious guy that has to play out slow stupid aoe animations before you can hit him once and has 3 health? Check. Mob spawning enemy that stuns you after every hit regardless of your positioning or being on or off the ground? Check. Enemy that is faster than you, runs away from you, blocks your bubbles and cant be kicked? Check. The spongebob stuff in this spongebob game are why you play this thing. And that stuff is all fine. The unlockable costumes are mostly bangers and being in bikini bottom is always nice nostalgia. I just wish the actual game was better.
_childDocuments_.name: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake

_childDocuments_.review: For all the chances I gave this game, it is not good. All of the comedy in this game relies wholly on poorly done references taken straight out of the show. Any of the times where it shows a close up still image of a character in high rez, it felt more awkward than funny. The story also felt really lazy. There doesnt really seem to be a reason the specific characters are in their respective worlds, it just seems random and is never explained in the story.As for the gameplay, while it was nice to have a wider variety of abilities, many of them weren't really needed past the world you got them in. The kick is the only one that felt any fun and had a variety of uses that actually felt applicable.My biggest gripe while at the end of the game was how difficult the devs made it to get the awards. I'm not talking about difficulty of the challenges, I'm referring to the fact that during the boss related awards, if you mess up, you would either have to complete the entire boss encounter, or exit the game entirely. You cannot load a save cuz you're in a boss battle, and there are checkpoints in the boss battles, making them feel not nearly as challenging as they could be, but they completely mess you up if you are trying to get awards.My next gripe is the autosave system which, at times, felt non-existent. I would be able to go through multiple levels or bosses, and not a single autosave would be made. It would happen at random times and severely screwed me over during some of the challenges.Overall, I cannot recommend enough to NOT get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Significantly more well-made than Rehydrated, though that's not saying much. I have a lot of issues, especially with the about the first half of the game. Stuff like the levels not being fun, the enemies being annoying (though tbh thats more second half), the audio not working right especially during cutscenes, etc. I could go on and on and on about various small nitpicks: The seahorse should have a take damage sfx, the pizza glide is flaccid and janky and you should be able to pull it out more than once, the hitbox for underwear is too small, the hitbox for the basic attack should be bigger vertically, etc. etc.That being said, this game DOES fix a lot (well, maybe like half) of my issues with rehydrated, and the writing for this game is genuinely ON POINT. The jokes land, and it feels like a Spongebob episode, both of which are something even the current seasons of the  are lacking. During the later levels, the constant minor annoyances went away, mostly, and I was actually enjoying the game quite a bit. After beating it, however, going back to the earlier levels brought me back into the dark side of the game and it became a real pain.I really can't help myself from complaining about small issues, if I thought MAYBE the devs would update the game and fix some of them then I might take the time to actually list them somewhere, but I doubt it so oh well.If you're a big Spongebob fan, and especially if you're one of the few people who enjoyed Rehydrated, then I would recommend this game. If you can get through the first couple sections, or if you're just less of a Squidward than me, then I think you will enjoy this game.Gameplay 3.5/10Story 5/10Writing 8.5/10Overall 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Just to be clear, while this is a negative review i found it to be an decent game that has a few serious letdowns.  It's not awful, but not worth full price and game wise feels closest to Creature from the Krusty Krab although it seems to pull a little from each game, it's ok just not great.The first and most glaring issue the game's length.  There are around 7 fairly short levels that in order to 100 percent complete you have to play twice, once for the main story and again to collect various collectibles to finish side missions which feel like more of a chore than a worthwhile experience.  In defense of the game however a lot of negative reviews complain about the game being more linear than Battle for Bikini Bottom, however i found the game to feel closer to a condensed version of that game instead. The game has several costumes both as DLC and in the base game.  These do nothing other than change character skin which isn't worth the DLC cost at what it is and feels like a missed opportunity to have costumes provide special abilities or other gameplay features.The game's controls are at that frustrating point of almost being good but not quite where the difference between making a jump or landing an attack feels random, the kind of game play where it feels like moves that should land don't and those that shouldn't do.Lastly, the game feels like a blend of all of the Spongebob games we've all played and enjoyed but without any of the charm.  It's clear a lot of the assets and vague level design are from B.F.B.B. Re-hydrated which makes sense.  However, the game also has a fanciful story line resembling Creature from the K.K., a few enemies and sound effects that immediately remind me of the S.B. movie game, and even a few quick time mini games with that Lights Camera Pants feel.  Instead of making me like this game it made me say "Wow, this makes me wish for them to remaster X or go replay Re-hydrated."

_childDocuments_.review: It's an extremely average game and I frankly regret paying as much for it as I did.It's not bad, but everything about is so mid; the level design is as linear and unispired as it comes, there's nothing experimental in it, challenging, nor that fun. There's costumes to be unlocked but most of these are locked by tiers that you unlock by collecting coins through the levels, problem is, most of these coins are locked behind pathways that require abilities to access them, which means, a lot of the costumes won't be unlocked until much later into the game.The combat and items are about the same they were in "Battle for Bikini Bottom", but while in that game they fit, here the tiki torches and blocks feel a bit strange, lazy, and out of place; I really wish they would've themed the levels a bit more in this regard given that in just about everything else, they're quite well made. Each area is distinctive and has its own personality, although I will say, after a while most of them end up feeling a bit samey; like they are part of a same trope of jumping from movie set to movie set; heck, there's even a level built around a film set.Again, I know I'm sounding really negative, but these are about the things that got the most highlighted for me while playing, everything works, and the story is fine -I guess-, but the remainder of the game just doesn't stand out in any way; It's not bad, it's a just a very bland game...I'll give you another example; in "Battle of Bikini Bottom" you get a number of cool boss fights that help pace the platforming of the game; here there's a moment early on where you go inside a large area that serves as the Alaskan Bullworm's Burrow, now anyone that's a fan of the show knows that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ worm, but I'll tell you, if you're like me, and you were expecting a boss fight, you'll be left dissappointed... they just have a large encounter with the same enemies you'll be fighting for the remainder of the game.It's just a shame, I was expecting something of at least decent quality, but generally, all I got was a bland game that's fun at times... whoever thought to add the costumes, had the right idea, but they mess this system with how they unlock; there's Patrick who follows you around for story reasons, which I thought was pretty cool, but he doesn't really serve any purpose mechanically; they could've done so much with this.The whole game just feels like it is playing it too safe, a bit too much for my tastes, and after a while, it doesn't really feel like a Spongebob game, nor an episode of the show that anyone can enjoy; but instead, it starts to feel like a game that has a Spongebob skin on top, but with a pandering game made for children in mind. Spongebob was a great show because it could appeal to anyone, adults could find it creative beyond it being silly, the same way kids could understand the humour and ironisms the episodes had in its characters and dillemas. This is just a game that's silly for the sake of being silly.

_childDocuments_.review: The levels are extremely repetitive and has extremely poor level design. Honestly feels like a cash grab. They don't give you any special buff or power up from any of the costumes, they're just there for looks. _childDocuments_.review: The game is OK but for sure a huge downgrade from Bikini Bottom in every aspect. ACTUAL Price value ~ 12 to 20$ max-ALL collectibles in the game are for show. You cannot use them for ANYTHING.And No. Buying a costume is not "something". It is an accessory for show. It offers NOTHING to gameplay.So there are no upgrades. No weapons or tools or upgrades for your tools. The ONLY external weapon in the game is a vacuum sucker you use on Monsters that you have NO choice when you want to use it. The game will spawn it for you.-The story is very lacking. It is meant as a children's game but that is no excuse to put up random stuff together, or even worse (like in this game), copy-paste a theme that is so overused nowadays it is boring.Crash Bandicoot already explored this same exact story. So did Ratchet and Clank. So did countless games before in a much better story adventure.- in Bikini Bottom during the slides and Time Trials, you could actually skip in shortcuts. Jump from the slide down to another part of the slide to save time (if you were doing TT). The level was designed properly and had no invisible walls or death-walls. This game has a LOT of those. If you are buying this hoping it is an exploration game, do not be fooled. Even the rarest items like spatulas or w.e are useless and are only there to give you a game trophy. No significance whatsoever. + the invisible walls not allowing you to go anywhere.- Linearity: When i read comments saying this game was too linear i kind of expected it since Bikini Bottom was linear too.But this takes it to a whole new level. This is literally made for toddlers. I do not need you to put ONE and ONLY ONE missions at a time lol. I do not need adhd pills i can focus on multiple things at once thanks. If you will make this game for Toddlers at least advertise it as such. Don't waste our money.Also there is not a single side missions that contributes to the story. ALL side missions ask you to find X item for X character and then they fk off and don't do anything. The story doesn't change. The gameplay doesn't change in any significant way-The artstyle is ok. Enjoyable. Game performs alright on my RIG. You can expect 120+ fps with a 3090 in 4K at max settings.-When you ride the seahorse the Camera Settings get reset to their default option again. This is obviously an unintended bug.-Some enemies are very clunky in their animations but this is not very important.---- Overall:5/10. Would Not buy for more than 20$.

The pacing is very weird especially. You constantly get the control and camera ripped out of your hands to show you something on the other side of the map without explanations. Many cut scenes also just start and end randomly without any indication of them doing so. Sadly I cannot recommend this and would rather urge you to play BfBB.

_childDocuments_.review: A comparison of Cosmic Shake & BfBBBfBB had a charm that is hard to match. Especially being from my childhood, it made it really easy for me to love BfBB Rehydrated. Purple Lamp did a good job making this game but it's not what I was expecting/ looking for. First of all, in Cosmic Shake, collecting doubloons (kind of like the golden spatula) is not needed to move forward in the story. In fact, nothing you collect in this game is necessary for progressing in the story line. They're only needed for the many costumes you can put on Spongebob. However, they made the costumes feel like a main feature with the way it's presented in the game. Almost like I would need to unlock a costume by collecting so many doubloons to be able to move forward. Unfortunately, they are only cosmetic. Part of the reason I liked BfBB, is the reward that you felt collecting the golden spatulas and how important they were to moving forward in the game. In BfBB the world felt more open to me. Yes, the areas were locked and you didn't go seamlessly between areas, but the game could be adapted to do that. With cosmic shake, The way you go from area to area would be more at home with a Rick and Morty Platformer. It would have been better if instead of having to go through a portal to get to the locations, the locations in bikini bottom were replaced by these new skinned areas they represent. The big problem with the locations is they feel very linear. BfBB felt like it had more freedom to move around the areas, in cosmic shake, you just go through the motions.The boss fights were a joke. The first “boss fight” in the Wild West Jellyfish Fields was the normal enemies you see throughout the game. That's not a boss, that's a mild inconvenience. On top of that if you read the warning signs leading to the caverns, all of them point towards their being a bullworm. A BULLWORM BOSS WOULD HAVE BEEN AWESOME! The other boss fights, weren't challenging enough. In the games defense however, the boss fights in BfBB were also easy but it was at least a little challenging having to switch between characters in some. On a side note, I found it kind of odd how the main characters of Spongebob were in these new worlds and instead of wanting to come back to bikini bottom, they all wanted to fight you to stay. Don't you think that they would have wanted to come back?Using only Spongebob in all the worlds was boring. It would have been nice to use different characters with different abilities. That was, in my opinion, why BfBB was so good. I had to learn to use multiple different characters to their advantage for different tasks. It was also getting old listening to the same character dialogue over and over. “The krusty krab pizza is the pizza for you and me” will be stuck in my head for a while. Same with “Yoink!”.Final thoughts/ my two centsThis game made me realize that BfBB worked so well because it capitalized on existing ideas. Staying true to the plot of the series, but adding it's own flare. Personally, I think a Spongebob game based around the already existing parodies of superheros in the series would have worked better. Having boss fights against Mermaid Man and Barnacle boy's enemies while you play as Spongebob, Patrick, Sandy, and Squidward dressed up in their superhero costumes would have been a hit.   I don't recommend this game for someone looking for the next Spongebob cult classic hit.

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat this game as of 4AM september 14th 2024these are my rough and mostly unorganized thoughts after beating the game. Allow me to start by saying this isn't a hard no. The game isn't bad. Its just not particularly good in any notable way either and there's way more impressive platformers you could be playing first.In short this game is so incredibly okay.its like a sequel to battle for bakini bottom that came out the same year but somehow has graphics from the future.which is to say that it still feels like an average (but nice) PS2 tie in platformer from 2003 that hasn't really learned anything from the better games around it.Like I guess the point is to be a sequel to battle 2 bikini bottom but it feels arguably a little too faithful in that regard. I've been wowed like less. I'd tell someone to buy Super Lucky's Tale Before this. Which is a baby easy platformer but still felt more fun to just control the character in. its not like Spongebob controls bad there's just nothing remotely interesting about controlling him. The level design platforming wise is equally fine but uninterestingVisually the level design is pretty nice. Cut-scenes well animated and fun.soundtrack perfectly serviceable but forgettable. Only the lava level had a song I particualrly liked.dialouge pretty alrightOne of the main draws for collection (besides the urge of completion in people like me) is to be able to collect the costumes. Since its not a collectathon anymore and you don't need spatulas to advance. So you collect these coins and whenever you collect enough you level up and can buy a new row of costumes.but the costumes really aren't that interesting. Maybe more interesting to a Spongebomb mega-fan, I haven't watched in a long time. It'd be more interesting if they had cute little effects like changing an animation or two, but I haven't noticed any besides one costume with a peg leg changing the walking sound effect. Which was good.The combat is functional. It has good enemy variety, but the enemies almost never used as an obstical to platforming. Sometimes they're just like in the path and  that's whatever.very often you have to clear out enemies before you can move forward or clear an objective. and every now and again it felt like they were layered in a clever way but most of the time I just didn't care.  You have a basic spin attack, a homing attack, and bubble that can freeze up to 1 enemy at a time. They are decent tools but its not interesting enough for how often they want you to fight. They make you fight as often as if its Psychonauts 2, but its no Pyshonauts 2.also the "boss fights", I can hardly even give them the praise of being considered such. All kinda suck. I don't really even know how to get into that one right now.tl;drGame is good but incredibly average.I only recommend if you've already played a lot of the great platformers since A Hat In Time, and simply want a anther platformer to play. or if you really really liked battle for bikini bottom

_childDocuments_.review: SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake - A Fun, Nostalgic Adventure for FansRating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)“SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake” is a vibrant and nostalgic adventure that perfectly captures the spirit of the beloved animated series. Developed by Purple Lamp Studios, this 3D platformer sends SpongeBob and his best friend Patrick on a wacky, dimension-hopping journey to save their friends and Bikini Bottom from chaos. With colorful visuals, entertaining gameplay, and plenty of fan service, *The Cosmic Shake* is an engaging romp through the absurd yet charming world of SpongeBob.The premise is simple but effective: SpongeBob and Patrick come into possession of magical wish-granting bubbles, only to accidentally tear open the fabric of reality. The result is a multiverse of different “Wishworlds,” each filled with iconic SpongeBob characters, reimagined settings, and zany scenarios. Fans of the show will appreciate the many references to classic episodes, with each Wishworld capturing a unique vibe—from a wild west setting to a prehistoric land—all offering fun twists on familiar locations.Gameplay-wise, The Cosmic Shake features traditional platforming mechanics that are easy to pick up and play. SpongeBob’s moveset includes a range of fun abilities like bubble-blowing attacks, jellyfish-catching, and karate kicks, all while collecting shiny objects and solving light puzzles. The levels are packed with collectibles and secrets, which adds replayability for those who enjoy exploration. The controls are smooth, and the platforming feels solid, though the game sticks to a relatively simple formula, making it more accessible to younger or casual players.Visually, the game bursts with color and charm. Each level is filled with vibrant and faithful recreations of SpongeBob’s world, with cartoony textures and lively animations that bring Bikini Bottom to life. The voice acting, with the original cast reprising their roles, adds an authentic touch, and hearing Tom Kenny’s SpongeBob and Bill Fagerbakke’s Patrick deliver their trademark humor keeps the tone light and fun. The humor is in line with the show’s silly, whimsical style, and longtime fans will enjoy the quirky interactions between characters.While The Cosmic Shake is undeniably fun, it does have a few shortcomings. The level design, while visually diverse, can sometimes feel repetitive, and the platforming challenges may lack depth for players seeking more complexity. Additionally, some of the combat encounters can be a bit simplistic, with basic enemy patterns that don’t offer much variety as the game progresses. However, these minor drawbacks don’t detract too much from the overall experience, especially for younger audiences or those simply looking for a SpongeBob-themed adventure.In conclusion, SpongeBob SquarePants: The Cosmic Shake is a fun and nostalgic platformer that will especially resonate with fans of the show. It’s a lighthearted, colorful journey packed with references, humor, and classic SpongeBob moments. While it may not reinvent the platformer genre, it excels at delivering a fun, accessible experience that captures the magic of SpongeBob’s universe. If you’re looking for a breezy, feel-good adventure, The Cosmic Shake is worth diving into.
