_childDocuments_.review: Gonna be honest, the game is just quite boring. The name speaks for itself, you basically just re-run the same course endlessly. You are supposed to unlock new stuff and exciting new combos of tiles at some point, but that... simply doesn't happen. No idea how many hours I'm supposed to put into this before something is going to happen. And frankly, it's just no worth my time to find out.  It's too grindy, with most runs being completely useless and not unlocking anything new at all. Sure, after the tenth identical run I might have enough ressources to upgrade something at the base camp... but doing the same thing ten times in a row is just so bland. The game doesn't require any user input apart from placing random tiles and equipping random items - that just gets old really quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Grinding is fun when you're still discovering a game and working towards a goal within reach, but once that stops, it just becomes a chore.  Loop Hero has some really cool ideas and a nice soundtrack, but it also has some balance issues that necessitate taking certain cards and hoping that RNG doesn't screw you over.  That's not to mention all the different resources that you have to grind for, which sometimes require subpar decks to acquire, doing run after run until you have enough orbs to finally be able to place river tiles.  The late game grind is even worse, where you're hoping for RNG drops of specific items to add to your supply so you actually have a chance against the final boss.I managed to make it pretty far, but the final chapter broke my interest.  I could just see the extra 10 hours of grinding ahead of me to finish the game (after already putting in 20) and realized that I would get no joy out of it, especially when I had already optimized my runs as much as possible.  There was nothing new except watching my little guy do his laps, unable to look away from my constantly shifting cards and items, hoping RNG would be kind.  If your tolerance for RNG and grind is higher than mine right now, then by all means, check this game out.  There are some really cool ideas here; they just need some more polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Read my full review on SuperJump at Loop Hero, developed by Four Quarters Games and published by Devolver Digital, is a compelling new tile-placement RPG packed to the brim with tile placement and deckbuilding, RPG mechanics, roguelike progression that persists between sessions, and a hint of luck/cycle optimization. It’s a strange mix of content and game mechanics that feels like a mash-up of a pen-and-paper RPG and Carcassone, a popular tile placement board game with a very different theme. It’s as fun as it is difficult to describe.For $12 and some change with the promo price, Loop Hero is a bargain. I expect to get many, many hours of enjoyment out of this title and am excited for the full release and additional updates that extend beyond the already content-rich game. Don’t be surprised if I’m not the only one raving about this new game — I’m sure you’ll hear plenty about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: What is the purpose of this game? Why was it made? What experience did the developers hope to create for the players?I struggle to answer these questions. For the first two, I guess maybe it was created to make money for the developers? Or as like some creative endeavor, because why not? But I definitely don't understand what its developers hoped players would get out of the game.As best I can tell, it's a game that's meant to spend your time in a neutral, chill mood. It doesn't deliver any narrative that explores any aspect of humanity. It doesn't provide complex mechanical puzzles to hone your problem solving skills and provide intellectual satisfaction. Its music, sound, and artistic design are proficient but will not provide any real aesthetic joy. Definitely no visceral fast-paced gameplay to get the heart racing. Its sole purpose seems to provide a low-stakes gameplay loop that requires minimal making of choices and the minor dopamine hits of itemization and base-building progress to give it an addictive edge, so that you can pass the time in a fugue state, until it's time to return life's larger responsibilities.Which, yeah, you can decide whether that's something you want or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets repetitive very quickly, however different tile combinations and progressing little by little reveals different parts of the story that keeps me hooked. Once I'm stacked, I can do something else while my hero does the work, though that doesn't always mean I won't die at some point. The art style is beautiful, and I'm a big fan of the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what happens when a developer takes the term "gameplay loop" ultra literally.It's another one of those games like Valheim that you just have to play to appreciate (it's hard to describe what makes it enjoyable without actually experiencing because there's so many different interconnected systems and elements). There's tons of elements from all types of genres which blend masterfully into a beautiful game. It feels very passive at first but there's many more things that you can do to affect your trajectory than you might initially perceive, it's a true min-maxer's delight. As with Valheim, the hype behind this game is well deserved. And the music is just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, I find myself nodding my head to some of the beats. Actually, just about everything in this game is good, I am struggling to find a complaint off of the top of my head.As with Valheim, I completely recommend going into this game blind unless you have very little time to play and just want to experience it. But there are a ton of mysterious gameplay elements and mechanics which are begging to be discovered, it hearkens back to my childhood with Mortal Kombat, where it always felt like there was another secret or undiscovered mechanic around the next corner.One other thing that I find enjoyable about this game is the gambling or risk:reward element. You always feel compelled to take that next loop. You can play either extremely conservatively or always take the next risk. At first I always took too much risk, it all comes down to building your deck along with your class and strategy and knowing when to pull out.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest games made in the last decade. I grew up as a kid during the MSDOS era, and this game nails that vibe. The soundtrack is a masterpiece too. It's the perfect game if you work at your computer, and you want to take a quick coffee break to play a loop, it's super easy to get back to work after a run. Worth every cent. Have not seen anything this innovative or unique in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It's more like a city builder than a traditional RPG. Battles are automatic so you have to carefully pick which stats to focus on upgrading with equipment and which tiles you want to use. A lot of tiles spawn enemies, some are much more difficult than others, but other ones boost your stats or provide other benefits. Certain tiles also interact with each other and alter how they behave; providing new buffs, debuffs or enemies. It's pretty fun unlocking new classes and finding new tile combinations. I hope they make an expansion at some point in the future to add something new to change it up.Some problems are that your upgrades in a run are random and some of the upgrades or equipment you get is just straight up worse than others. There's also like 12 different resources and it can be really tedious to farm some of the rarer ones. You also have to spend resources to unlock the encyclopedia, which tells you how to farm certain resources which is annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love it for the way you can manage and match your deck and build the surroundings.Great OST.Unique bosses with nice mechanics.I quite liked the story, worldbuilding and lore tidbits.Definitely recommend it, even without a sale ongoing. (Tip: Do speed up the speed of battles and walking, it will save you a lot of time. Just be ready to pause if you need it via space, and counters the boredom a lot of people seem to encounter.)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: SO ADDICTIVE. It took me 30hrs to beat the first boss. There are 4 of them.Deckbuilder : Populate your loop with cards. Most cards have some effect when placed close to each other card (Combos).RPG : Get load of LOOTS ( Common, Uncommon, Rare, Ultra rare ). Attack, Defense, Attack Speed, HP drain, Counter, Evasion, Crit, and many more (Depend on your class : Warrior, Rogue, Necromancer). Get load of material to unlock stuff (More class, More cards). Get load of artifacts (Like Slay the Spire but focus more on HP restore, Spike damage).Get to choose traits after level up.Auto-Battler : Infinite loops. However, It has a cap on how much material you could take back per run.Tactical : Gears matters - Plan a lot about whether you are going to replace old gears with new gears you got. Bad gears = Run endingCards matters - Plan a lot about what cards you should use on the loop. Bad cards = Run ending.Create a loop with cards you get from defeats monsters in the loop. Placement matters as cards have different bonuses/benefits/conditions to adjacent tiles.Get Loots from defeating monsters. New weapons. New Armors, New Accessories. Build HP, Defense, Regen, Vampire, Counter, Evade, etc.The excess items will get recycle automatically into materials that you can use to upgrade your campfire at the end of the run. This is where rogue like comes into the play. Your upgrades can help you in the future runs.The difficulty is cards can create a path that spawn monsters on that block or adjacent blocks.Many monsters block = You might die but you need to balance it. That's the fun part. You must be strong enough to beat the boss given that your loop and your build is efficient enough (Not die before and after the boss encounter).The boss will spawn after the boss gauge is full (Fill boss gauge when place any tiles).At the end of each loop, you could stop at the campfire and decide to retreat (End the run). If you retreat at the campfire, you get all materials in the run. Otherwise, It's only 30% (You die, Retreat anywhere else on the loop)If you like to create a system or have some sort of obsession with min-maxing/efficiency like me, this is A MUST PLAY.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, fun, adictive:  I always keep myself saying "just one more expedition".It is really a fresh air in the beaten fantasy RPG genre, and while the combat is automatic, it is also very tense: "should I quit now and retain all my loot, or should I try my chances on the next loop and lost 60% of my things if I die".Two thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a gameplay-review, look at the other positive reviews.I just wanted to say how much I was surprised by the story in an indie-game.The story itself was interesting, the hero and the antagonists had well thought-out dialog without much "filler"-lines, and actually gives something to philosophise, without getting  pretentious.A fresh and nice tasting cherry on the top.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: So. It took me 37 hours to complete the game. For such a price and the enjoyment I had, I think I have to greatly recommend this product. It was just a fun blast, a bit gridndy at times, but fun nontheles. I still could upgrade more of the city and continue to build more things but overall I think I am done with the game. I would be glad to play for 10 hours, almost 40 is just way beyond my expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Another deck building roguelike? yes... however! this one has the biggest twist, it is a map building deck builder tactical autoplay roguelike!Does that make sense? not if you just read it, but once you play it, it all comes together, as you populate the world and with it you make your character and his foes and allies stronger, this means that despite you the player not being in direct control of your character's actions, you are always in control of the game, for you are the one that dictates how much the world itself advances, in what manner, and at what times.A game that uses mechanics which have been done ad nauseam, and yet remains and excels at being a game that is one of a kind, unique on its concept and execution, an prime example of taking something old and making it fresh and novel. But it is not just great game-play, it comes with beautiful pixel graphics and a soundtrack that slaps super hard too!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is a great cooling down, take at your own pace game. With the ability to pause the time and select everything, you have no pressure to go fast or learn fast. I personally like playing it while queuing for other games as it has minimal system requirements and can just be open in the back.        The visual and audio design is a great upgrade to the classic 32-bit style and I can't get enough of it. I've put in 18hrs and feel like I've barely scratched the surface of the content, with promised updates to come. So if you want time for your money, it has it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want to create a world from nothing? Do you like fighting monsters? Multitasking? Feeling like your game is from 1998 only better because it's not glitchy? Then this is what you want. I literally only stopped play because I have to work... it's so soothing yet full of chaos. 10/10 everyone needs this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a testament to the quality that can be achieved even with a small team of developers. The concentrated passion of design Loop Hero exudes is the most impressive I've seen in years. This is the game you didn't know you wanted and the game you'll keep coming back to. Just one more time around the Loop...
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with enough strategy and uniqueness to keep me occupied for way too long. I would say: it gets GRINDY. 10-15 hours of grinding out orbs of expansion and time shards to get enough to upgrade some of the mid-late game buildings. But luckily the game is beautiful, so watching your little dude fight is entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I recently played this game again a bit over the holiday and this is just so perfect and polished. it is so self consistent and well done that it almost hurts. it's special and everyone who likes retro feel in games with a modern level of polish needs (NEEDS) to play this. it's been my comfy game for years and it never ceases to impress me.A Really Unique Blend of Retro Style mechanics and modern rogue-lites that lends itself to a deceptively deep and fun experience. the art is also fantastic and takes you back to the days of playing Oregon Trail in elementary school but with a modern level of fidelity that is still honest to the retro style. all in all it has the aesthetics, the mechanics, and the low energy involvement to be a great game to plug away at when you need something low energy that still has some real engagement.a general breakdown might look like this for me.Mechanics: 9/10Art: 9.5/10Music: 9/10Story/Lore: 8/10it's really quite solid and I've put in a lot of time into this game when I needed something low energy but still engages me. highly recommend.so for those who have not gotten it yet get it; game has a lot of hours of laid back fun that is truly unique like Knights in The Nightmare.. which I highly recommend if you have a PSP or NDS.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Very original and interesting concept, and a reasonable price. The game is interesting, but has a slowness that gets to you. It is sorely missing a faster speed up functionality to avoid the boring parts.PROS- Original. You create your own enemies spawn points, by doing that you get more loot but also more difficulty. Balancing the risk and reward is a fun mechanic.- Kind of atmospheric- Some like the art (I don't)- kind of addictive, one more loop!CONS- First few hours are fun, then it gets repetitive and you wish you could speed up through the slow parts. The 2x speed is very insufficient and I wish to see something similar to monster train. We need at least 4 to 8x. There are ways to speed up like editing the ink files but they create some bugs snd issues.- The graphics are not important, but the art style doesn't cut it for me, personally. It's just too grey and bland for something I’d be looking 100+ hours at. It needs some colors and better style. That said, the portraits in the dialogues that well done.- The mechanics and how things work are not explained or shown at all... stamina, counter attack, defense, most of the traits you unlock are not clear at all in how they work exactly. It's the kind of game you'd have to check the wiki to understand, and i absolutely hate that. For instance, what stops the game from telling what monster and what tiles drop what? You learn over time that spiders drop cards and vampires drop gear for you, but the whole process is again, a bit too slow and obscured for my taste.- it can be super Grindy? In most rogue likes you are trying to go deeper and you do that by becoming smarter and more experienced, while having some meta progression.. In this one yes you are, but 70+% of your time is spent grinding materials to upgrade your base. To beat the final boss you need more power and that comes from these upgrades, necessary to unlock important cards, healing upgrades, gear, and other functionality. And it can be a bit boring to do hours long expedition just to collect wood, metal, stone, or some of the rarer ressources that drop very rarely. WORTH IT?I think it can be a big winner with some adjustments, but for now it feels a little bland and slow. I feel burned out a little after getting to the final boss and realizing I’ll need to farm to upgrade my base more to beat it. I’ll be taking a break and definitely  revisit it after a few patches, especially if they add more speed functionality. I am hoping I can turn this no into a yes after a few patches.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: For the first bit of gameplay and honestly even before buying (watching videos and stuff) I was not immediately grabbed and I did not really understand how the progression of the game would be fun and I also didn't really understand how it would try to keep me coming back for more. I was quickly given the answers through its fun, intense, but also somehow laid back gameplay that always made me want to just start again after losing. I still haven't played it too much so I don't have all that much more to say other than it is a cheap and relatively fun game that can surely provide many many hours of enjoyment. Why not pick it up?
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is a mesmerizing blend of strategy and roguelike gameplay that offers a unique and addictive experience. With its innovative loop-based mechanics and charming pixel art style, the game draws players into a captivating journey of exploration and discovery. The strategic placement of cards and the constant evolution of your hero's journey create a dynamic and engaging gameplay loop that keeps players hooked for hours on end. Whether you're battling formidable foes or uncovering secrets in the ever-changing world, Loop Hero offers a delightful and satisfying adventure that is as challenging as it is rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the trailer for Loop Hero, I was very impressed. It seemed to tick all the right boxes for me. A very specific retro visual style and sound effects, which Loop Hero really nails right on the head. It is often referred to as a roguelike, but to me it is more of a tile placement board game. I really enjoyed my first several hours, with its innovative and addicting gameplay.The problem, however, is that its length was artificially prolonged by locking progression behind grind. For the first several hours, that didn’t really bother me as I was enjoying my time with the grind. But Loop Hero is actually a much more simplistic game than it first appears to be. There are not many synergies among the tiles and it doesn’t take long to figure out the optimal way to play. A few hours after Act 3, I’ve just got really bored with the grind and decided to grind through the rest of the game was not worth my time.I still applaud Loop Hero for the visuals and innovative gameplay. I have the feeling that a sequel would be great, if it preserves what is good about Loop Hero but improves upon things that don’t work well (meaningless grind, lack of clever synergies…).
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game if you like retro.+Soundtrack (also retro)+Gameplay (easy to learn, maybe hard to master)+Lore (nice characters and plot)+Dyslexia-friendly font-May change later, but wording on some items and traits are confusing. _childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game for the priceFairly good storyGameplay loop swaps between addictive and boring due to its idle natureA little RNG reliant for the later chapters but upgrades and buildings even most of it outMusic is very nice and never got grating despite the repetitive tracksOverall an enjoyable game with difficulty spikes where you either get lucky or have to do multiple runs just for resources
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Personally one of my favorite games Devolver Digital has published, Loop Hero has a very distinct style to it. The art and music are superb, and the gameplay is very unique compared to the usual roguelike. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone that doesn't like to wait around and watch their character fight for themselves, or anyone that doesn't like minmaxing their character's stats to gain an advantage.I'd say give it a shot if you're interested, especially considering the low price- I could have sworn it was more than $15.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: What an interesting game. I sunk alot of time into it, and I must say, it's one of the most addictive games on the market at the moment. That being said, it's weird.The difficulty requires experimentation to play around with, and at a certain point, one begins to figure out the builds they like. The obtaining of resources is time consuming, and serves as a grind, but the main game is fun enough where I never really had an issue with it. Easily the most interesting mechanic is deciding whether or not to loop again, and the general risk management, as resources to improve long term are on the line. The real customization comes in the deckbuilding, and figuring out the sort of setup the character is looking for. The pacing's interesting. Early on the game's quite fun, but after the first 13 hours it slows down. That being said, the lull is regrettable, as I think the second half of the game is quite strong. The game becomes far more fun once the warehouse is available, as it provides permanent buffs, allowing for an entertaining power snowballing. Four Quarters put a lot of effort in and it shows. The games brimming with polish, and the spriting/worldbuilding is fantastic. I love seeing unknown teams strike it big, and they're doing quite well via word of mouth.That being said, the gameplay's odd. Micromanaging the game is often boring, as the fighting is done for you, but you can rarely leave the hero looping and idle. It's in a weird crossroads between an idle game, and a standard game, and even after 60 hours, I couldn't tell which it wanted to be. I definitely recommend Loop Hero, unless you despise grinding in games. For me, it scratched an itch I love scratching, but I can understand why someone might be annoyed with the time it takes up.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I love the approach this game takes with difficulty and meta progression. Placing tiles creates a risk vs reward game and there is a fair amount of fun deck building and planning out builds.Each class is given a good amount of tools and ways to approach the game, and most tiles are fun to play with.I can only say I wish there was more combinations and tiles, but only because I loved everything the game offered.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game that ticked all my checkboxes for roguelikes\roguelites. + Addictive, the feel of progress, constant loot utilization, GRIND. + A lot of game synergies and mechanics, extra dopamine every time you discover another combo and proceed to shredding the loops.+ Games got some lore as well and beautifully detailed characters be it enemy mobs\bosses or friends in your camp. Yota a bae!+ Sick OSTs as well, did not regret buying fullpack.+ A C H I E V E M E N T S - Once you are past the middle of the game and start piling mobs (4-5 on every tile) x2 speed is really not enough, One of my runs took me 4 hours because I wanted to max out my resources. Please implement x4 speed so I don't have to edit the files botching achievements.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------As a person who did 99.9% achievements in The Binding Of Isaac, I fully approve of this game. Thank you very much, Four Quarters.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I normally wait to review a game until I put in a bit more time, but holy crap! This game is an excellent take on the rouge-lite & card game genre mashed together. The vintage pixel art, chiptune music and sound FX also draw me in with its nostalgic aesthetics. With each enemy you beat you gain gear and cards. You place cards down for resources and enemies. Each loop is one enemy level. So 5 loops means enemies are level 5 and gear drops can be higher or lower than level 5. When you retreat to your camp you keep all you found and the loop changes and all the cards you placed disappear. If you die you keep 30% of you loot and the loop resets. No one loop is the same and every loop will present different challenges based on the RNG of cards and gear gained from enemies. Its also an auto battler. You character moves continually and your character also fights their own battles. How you outfit your character dictates how proficient they are in battle. Health regen, vampirism, evasion, damage all enemies and other perks are on the gear.Just two hours in and Im already writing a review for this game. If you like Slay the Spire, Pixel art and games that have a truly unique play style, then this game will make two hours melt away in 5 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A neat and addictive little game that, despite playing itself for the most part, illicits a "one more run" feel in me. Though I can't seem to play it for longer than an hour at a time, for some reason. Although the concept here is well worked out, it feels as if it could have used a couple more months in development, getting polished up and becoming more nicely balanced. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It is a slow burner. It took me a while to get the hang of the mechanics and story, but after you know how it works, it's really addictive.The retro-pixelated aesthetic breaths life into the board you build, and the sprites for enemies and even resources are so high-quality that some people take it for granted. It looks gorgeous. And the sound design it's on par with the art style.The gameplay is all about experimentation and synergy with builds, with a little RNG for the flavor. I truly love how you need to see what works with every class and what deck you need to make for your advantage, though I highly recommend looking for guides if you don't have the patience to learn all the ropes.Overall, it's a satisfying game to perfect. If you love retro-style games with a cool learning curve (and something to put idle on your second monitor), this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A fun blend of collecting loot upgrades, deck building, and strategy, all while at the mercy of RNG (random number generator, and in this case, randomly generated drops).  Games can be played at your pace, whether that is step-by-step slow or recklessly fast, with the ability to speed up both battles and trips around the loop.  As you equip your character and silently hope RNG is kind and gives you the stats you need to optimize your build, it's very satisfying to discover what all the cards are for, and how to best utilize them on the expedition loop.I found myself thinking, "One more loop," more than a few times while playing, and the achievements have been fun to work toward.A caution, this game does have a fair amount of grinding to unlock upgrades in your town, so that you can unlock all the cards, and other special upgrade perks, so be prepared for that if you want to maximize your chances of beating the game and completing the achievements.Overall a fun, slightly addictive game at the mercy of RNG and your own strategic thinking.  Looking forward to seeing if any updates are in the works!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Art style is sexyGameplay is pretty good especially once you get the not garbage land cardsStory is interesting, dialogue runs a lil long sometimes but theres a skip it button.The alt classes you unlock are dope.Once you've got the gist you can safely chill with a video in the backgroundvery nice 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun deck building strategy game. You have to set up the tiles as your main character follows a loop slaying monsters and looting for items until they get to beat the loop boss.Pretty basic concept but deep and well executed.There is a base building minigame that adds more cards, powerups and classes to start with.Also, a lot of the cards put in certain formations create new tiles that spawn new monsters or give different stats or mechanics.Overall, it is a fun semi-idler to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: No doubt one of the best indie games of the year for me   Pros- Super good pixel art, with a decent enemy variety.- The soundtrack is so good, catchy, and the bosses soundtrack is just superb (blinch created such an amazing ost)- The mechanics are simple but it has a such a good complexity (or a learning curve), especially from mid to late game, a new different game, the best way to discover is by playing it.- Had no crashes, bugs or glitches during my playthrough- The price is good for the amount of hours you are going to enjoy this game- You can get addicted  Cons- You can get addicted... Keep looping!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game has a major issue - the gameplay revolves around you making the optimal choices to complete the level and gather the correct resources (which are the major componant of progression) but should you fail the level or accidentally miss the exit tile and die on the following loop you will lose 70% of the resources you just spent and hour+ focusing on getting. i feel there is nothing worse in a game than the feeling you just wasted your time and need to do everything all over again and might not even be able to do it next time. unlike games like monster hunter where you do 30 minutes hunts to try and farm an items you might not get - at least the gameplay itself is challenging and fun. here there is little gameplay, its just about making choises and sitting back with an addictive-style auto battler. the art is cool, a lot of care went into this, but i think there is a fundamental issue with how the game is designed. I had more fun with it before I understood the mechanics, once I did I realized how much time I was wasting and expected to waste
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't say that I enjoy it. While the presentation, visuals and overall idea of Loop Hero, the game-play...Or, rather, the lack of it, didn't appeal to me. I can understand the appreciation people have for a sort of "Auto-fighting" game, but I came into Loop Hero expecting a puzzle-RPG game and what I found was, essentially, an idler game. Which I can't say I have anything against, I have one or two in my library gifted to me, but I still don't really enjoy it. Perhaps if I could have controlled the fights instead of watching them play out I'd have been more interested. It seems good, but its not for me.The strategy felt simple and simply a numbers game, while the core "Loop" was...extremely similar. I got up to the point of unlocking, and trying, a new class and when it really didn't change anything I figured it wasn't the game for me. The extremely positive reviews made me pretty excited, but I guess I must have weird taste compared to the normalcy.Can't say I personally recommend it unless you like an idler sort of game, where you increase numbers and watch the game play itself mostly. The tiles didn't seem to do much besides unlock more resources to get bigger numbers to unlock more cards for more resources...Also, this is a stupid and childish take on my half, but the game is absolutely nothing like Rogue and I'm finding myself hating the bastardized term "Rogue-like" more and more. It'd be nice if it was changed. DC:SS, ADOM, e.t.c are rogue-likes. They're like...Well, Rogue! Oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero its a deckbuilding roguelike where you "put the quests" in front of you and its a mechanic I loved since the really underrated Runescape's online TCG.You are merely an spectator watching some of your decisions unfold on the board and waiting for the next event to come. Cultist simulator players will find a home here. Put a forest on the road and wolves will spawn for you to kill and loot but maybe in the distant future you will regret this move, specially when you have all this different terrains and spawn-points stacking mobs, effects and hazards.Its not the kind of roguelike where you fightfightfight uncontrollably for the best loot and one-shot a boss.  You REALLY need to learn to stop, gather your rewards and start over or your greed will get you.The only thing I think this game needs its 4x speed, but I'm impatient so that's only me.For the roguelike players and card-lovers, this is a must buy, you wont regret it.PD: FourQuarters, maybe make somekind of competitive multiplayer? just like "Chronicle:Runescape legends"? _childDocuments_.review: This game exemplifies the design principal of "easy to play, hard to master."Auto battle, card draft, tile placement, multi-vector combinations, RPG skill and tech-tree, town-building, roguelike - mechanics that so ridiculously disparate and incongruous come together so well in this joy of a game. It is satisfying and delightful to discover hidden tile combinations, place tiles at the right time to adjust the difficulty curve and beat the Lich (with a personality straight out of Adventure Time! I love it).I'm still surprised at the lack of cheap clones for this game.  As a game designer, the best thing I can say about this game is that I wish I had made it first. It's just that good.

_childDocuments_.review: I first want to say that this game is one of the game types that's great if you don't really want to put too much effort into playing something. All you need to do is think and use your mouse, so if you feel too lazy to play a game that takes more concentration, this is the game for you. Don't take that as a negative, either, I often have the feeling of "I don't feel like touching my keyboard for a bit, I just want to lean back and click." For that, this game is good, as it's something you can focus on while also doing something else, like watching a video or just listening to music.  Though the in-game music itself is good enough for that part.So why can't I recommend this game? Well... It's a grind. A constantly inconsistent yet always there grind that ends up being just as empty as the world you remember. The entire theme of the game being empty except for what you "Remember" is accurate to the gameplay as well; as you can easily play the demo of this game and get mostly the full experience, which is what drew me in at the beginning. You can tell from the hours I've spent on it that I still enjoyed the game at first, but as time went on, it became more... expected and dull. What drew me in from the Demo was the ability to combine world tiles together to create new things; to discover secrets the world had "forgotten", and engage in new things or new buffs or abilities. But... That's the issue. There's just nothing really there after the first few you find. The biggest thing you can do is discover new enemies to engage with; which you actively have to do in order to gain some resources. Which is fine, but that's about where the customization really ends. The game eventually feels as empty as it wants you to "remember" it is and you find yourself stuck in this loop, heh, of just... grinding resources. Because you can't really progress to the final chapter without building your home town up quite a bit, so your character is strong enough to get through everything. And after that... there's nothing.So again, why can't I recommend this game? Because there's just not enough to it. Yes, it's fun for what it is and it does that well at first, but once you hit the grinding wall, it becomes more and more obvious that you won't really get anywhere else. It's also missing some things, such as pieces of equipment being shown, but no one can actually get them. Which does hint at future updates, but it feels like an empty promise when they're already there. Isn't the theme supposed to be things don't exist unless I remember them? So why are they there? I clearly don't remember them.That aside, this game's core mechanic relies on the Hero to just go around in a circle and you don't control what they do, just what they engage with. It's dull after awhile because there's just not much to do except place down more tiles, which you can't even replace with better ones if you decide to use the smaller tiles given to you with the Forest or Desert choices. It's best to just ignore the small ones for the most part and move on to bigger and better things, yet at the same time, there are tiles that you can take with you and not see for the entire game. Some of which are required to get specific resources to upgrade your town.The town itself is dull in its own way; like giving you number stats you can't really feel, as one of them is literally just "The hero gets 4% stronger!" when you upgrade it, which doesn't translate well into gameplay where you don't actually pay attention to damage numbers that much. Additionally, the things you /can/ get are pretty empty feeling, with the most impact being from getting new classes or unlocking a new feature you barely have to use. But once you unlock those, there's... nothing. Just numbers increasing, unlocking new slots for town equipment which just increases your numbers in specific ways, and numbers, numbers, numbers. It just kinda goes to a point where you don't feel like you're progressing until you get that /one run/ where everything lines up perfectly.So for now, the reason I can't recommend this game is simply because it doesn't feel like it's actually done. There are features that need added, things that need fixed, and overall it just needs more content. Is it worth its price? Absolutely; honestly there are way worse games out there that are like $20 dollars more. But if you're looking for a satisfying experience from start to finish, this isn't the game for you. It's a grindy game that only grinds your gears into more grinding habits with not much reward for grinding. Once its given a few updates, I think it'll be fine, but I'd avoid it for now.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: fantastically tight and focused design, Loop Hero executes on its modest goals with remarkable grace and style, never overreaching or under-delivering. my only complaint is that it can be a little obtuse at times, making the optimization a bit haphazard. overall, this is  my favorite take on the rogue-lite since Slay the Spire!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been into the idea of 'idle' games, but Loop Hero - which arguably classifies as one - is thoroughly enjoyable. The gameplay needs no explanation here, there are Let's Plays for that, but what's not immediately obvious - and is something I quite enjoyed - is how neatly the lore is woven with the game mechanisms. I came to Loop Hero expecting a rather abstract but nonetheless enjoyable game, its workings largely unexplained in any world-building. Instead, I was delighted to find that the story that emerges through the game's dialogue actually explains just about every major feature of the game in a way that doesn't even feel contrived, from placing tiles on the map to surviving death and replaying the same bosses.A really impressive little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Was fun for a few hours, then I got REAAALLLLLY bored in chapter 2. It feels like I have to hunt for certain resources but -- unless I'm missing something -- the game forces you to pursue a bunch of pointless gameplay just to try to figure out how to mine one particular resource in order to unlock more buildings in your camp.
