_childDocuments_.review: listen. the pixel art in this? transcendent. the limited palette absolutely shines in ways you wouldn't expect it to be able to, creating texture and character out of seemingly nothing. the character portraits are all gorgeous and evocative of their subject, the ui is full of simple charm without taking away from its clarity, and each tile is clear and distinct, merging seamlessly into each other to build a varied little world as you go.  it's truly fabulous, and the whole thing is worth it for that alone.also the game is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Nope. Loop Hero takes a great idea, has some great music and art and then falls flat on the gameplay. The loop (heh) that indie games have is exceptionally boring here. Buildings take too long to unlock, and apart the card unlocks they don't feel impactful, either.I didn't feel my choices had that much impact, or I was forced to obvious choices. No matter my build, if I get a weapon that's level 12, and I have a level 8 weapon - obviously I'm going for the better one. So I'm left there equipping items that are just a higher number a lot of the time. I found this tedious, along with all the land cards, I wish there was an auto place feature.At this point I'd say it's an idle clicker game. I expected strategy, and this game is not that.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Novel gameplay idea. Good-looking NES-style pixel art, good music, somewhat interesting story. First few hours are fun. However, gameplay grows stale quickly: You are, in fact, optimizing HP loss and damage through small, grindy upgrades until you beat the game. Tactics or strategy are neither necessary nor possible, because the few options you have for interacting with the game do not have all that much effect.You can build a deck of cards, place cards in a run, choose hero equipment, and manage your camp.Choosing cards has little actual consequences: Cards primarily determine monsters, but despite different monster abilities (e. g. life steal, item steal), all encounters play out the same. Even if you pick slightly more dangerous foes, there isn't any particular reward for doing so. Utility cards, on the other hand, balance their advantages with similar downsides (e. g. fasten flow of time causes faster healing but also faster enemy respawn). Apart from a few hard-coded combinations (e. g. place card X next to Y), there is hardly any emergent interaction between card effects. In the end, even a very basic deck is more than sufficient to complete the game.Placing cards in the core game loop quickly becomes cumbersome. There are a few, very obvious placing patterns that work well on every run and there is little incentive to use any other than these default patterns. Since monster spawns take a few in-game days to have their effect, there is hardly any chance for reacting to the current state of affairs (e. g. by placing more or less monster spawns). Choosing equipment is an exercise in futility: On the one hand, the heavy RNG kills any intentional builds - on the other hand, just picking items with higher level once available works just fine in most cases. Equipment seems somewhat self-balancing (e. g. if a sword has additional magic damage, it has less normal damage), which just makes equipment management even more futile.Camp management is a grindfest for most of the game. You need to farm resources over many runs just to collect a myriad of miniscule, stacking bonus effects. In contrast, certain upgrades (i. e. attack speed card, archers, magic HP shield for rogue, alchemy) are drastically overpowered and break the entire game. Finally, a usability glitch: some buildings need to be placed next to specific other buildings - which the game does not tell you beforehand, so with a little bad luck you need to raze half your camp for upgrades. Suggestions for improvement:- Add interacting monsters (e. g. goblins combining with ratwolves to goblin rider)- Add minimum and maximum levels for monsters (i. e. make card choice matter)- Have loot differ by monster strength (e. g. skeletons drop better loot than ratwolves)- Have loot differ by monster type (e. g. vampires drop items with life steal, allows targeted builds)- Add opportunities to interact with the game (e. g. cards that damage monsters with specific attributes)- Add mechanics apart from optimizing HP loss vs. damage (e. g. status effects on enemies)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is a game that on the surface seems really simple and boring when in reality it is a more nuanced game that is incredibly addicting.  You can cater it to what you want to achieve in each expedition and I think that is a key to the game that is easily overlooked.  Do you want to just loop a bunch, collect resources and build up your encampment?  You can do that!  Do you want to see how hard you can push yourself before you face the boss or have to retreat?  You can do that too!  The ability to dynamically change the focus and difficulty of the game by how you stack your deck in the beginning is really the backbone I think of the game design.Is it a game that will require twitch reactions and have incredibly hard content right from the start to make you grind a ton before you even reach the first real boss?  Not exactly; but if that is the sort of game you are looking for than Loop Hero is not for you.  If you want a nice mix between Idle and Rougelite that lets you customize your experience based on what sort of gaming mood you are in than buy Loop Hero.  I promise you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: After twenty five hours of play, I'm in the midst of trying out strategies with the Necromancer class. I place a river tile and blink at my screen as something flashes and transforms. I hold my cursor over what was once a battle-field tile and see "Shipwreck"??? This game is phenomenally fun, with tonnes of synergies hidden out of sight that you need to explore to figure out or stumble upon by pure chance. I highly recommend this game under one caviat. Do not look up strategy guides that tell you the tile synergies. I haven't, and I cannot imagine this game being half as fun if you shortcut the main elements of exploration and learning through repetition. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is terrible, unfunny drivel, I almost wish there was no plot like in other roguelikes because it just makes me mad. Game is one note and some classes seem to not be fully developed like necromancer stats don't seem to upgrade very quickly, which is perhaps because the class is already insanely OP, meanwhile the warrior feels really bad to play. I wouldn't advise people to buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly interesting and fun! I thought I'd be doing a run now and then, for a tranquil moment far from more intense games. Then I found myself playing over and over again. The number of interesting interactions between placeable parts of the world in every run make for regular surprises and small puzzle times. There are many different ways to play and the best way to find out about them is to test things in different ways. It may take a bit of time to unlock some game changing tiles though. For example the rogue class seems very weak when you first unlock it but quite a few hours and new foundings later it can actually be very refreshing. I like this game a lot and am already awaiting an eventual expansion!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: If  you want a Relaxing game, ie not Twitch gaming ,  simplistic to play ,  hard to master/beat , Loop Hero is a game for you.  It's not complicated almost could be developed on a C64.  You can exit the game at anytime and start right back where you left off.  I like to just lean back , play some music of my liking and get the looping going to gather materials to build out the home base.The Game is controlled by Mouse for selecting inventory items (This isn't a inventory homework game , use it or lose it during Gameplay), drag drop enchantments to the land/loop and space bar to continue to next battle or start next loop.  Something between Simplistic MTG card game meets Roll Dice game of RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine an RPG which all you can do is to prepare the adventure passively and not actually engage in it. You set the scene and simply wait for things to happen. Nothing exciting happens and You grind for hours until the game progresses only to be rewarded by less than 5mins of dialogue. The only variety in the game is passive variety. Different enemies have different passive effect. Different tiles have different passive effects. Different hero class have different passive effects. Different equipment have different passive effects. Nothing in this game is exciting or rewarding. One of the most boring game I’ve ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful little indie game and it can be pretty addictive, too. The basic game principle is quite simple: Your hero walks along a path in a loop. You place obstacles and resource spots there. These will have benefits regarding health and health recovery. Some will spawn mobs that your hero has to fight, giving you better equipment and resources. These resources can be used to upgrade your camp. I have to admit - even with the tutorial, I at first thought, "why should I even put mobs in there to make it harder? What is the benefit?" Well, aside from the loot that you can use to improve your camp, you will get better equipment. The enemies get more challenging after each loop that is finished - therefore, your hero needs better gear to fight them. I was hooked quickly, and I enjoy this quite a bit. It's a casual game with relatively slow in-game-progress and some grinding involved. I spent a few hours with this already, watching TV while sending my hero through loop after loop. Quite addictive and a whole lot of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Although it takes some getting used to and requires some understanding about how its card combinations and camp upgrades function, Loop Hero provides a really interesting game loop (hehe) that scales properly depending on the difficulty. The deck choices also provide some really interesting benefits depending on which of the 3 character builds you decide to play as, with each having their own benefits and weaknesses. Overall a very polished and enjoyable experience that I hope they add more to in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: a deceptively "casual" game that has a lot of interesting layers and much to learn. despite it "advancing automatically", it's actually closer to a real-time with pause game and you'll find yourself pausing often to optimize the tiles and equipment. in addition the art and music style is fantastic, simultaneously retro and innovative.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: There are very specific ways to defeat the encounter in every chapter.If RNG doesn't agree with you and allow you to stack to ONLY correct stat for that boss, then too bad for you, start again. Keep doing it over and over again until you get the right RNG for the right stat.I would never design a game like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very unbalanced. I like the game and a lot of the mechanics but the fact that you could be dropping enemies left and right and the next battle the enemy starts hitting you for 160 damage per hit just makes every loop feel like gambling. If I wanna gamble I'll go to a casino. Also, the grind is unreal. You unlock some new classes on the way but after 2-3 loops it feels repetitive again.After over 10 hours I feel like I accomplished less than other games in 2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Excellent in theory, sort of lackluster in execution after around 20 hrs or Act II.The ideas contained within Loop Hero are creative and solid. Combine a deck builder, roguelite w/ classes, map design, synergistic builds, INCREDIBLE art style + music, and an original story and you have a fantastic game in the making. Unfortunately as things progress, a lot of the pretty sheen starts to fall off and the gameplay loop (get it) becomes a little monotonous, repetitive, and without much new challenges besides "enemies get harder". There isn't much of a way to theory craft or discover new synergies, and man it does get grindy as time goes on to upgrade your settlement and match the power spike that happens in between Acts.If this were to receive a sequel that was more fleshed out it really feels like it could take off and be an AMAZING game, while right now its more of a good way to pass the time. All in all, 6.5/10, still a nice little game. Get one sale for sure and maybe you would love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The gauntlet beckons, much like growing the factory, if the factory were for monsters with the intent to kill your hero of course. Similarly, it will not grow itself, so instead you will facilitate its prospering and win by not killing The Lich but instead destroying your hero as many times as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game kind of reminds me of the good ol' tower defense games, except it's also somehow the opposite in every way.Also, as someone with no eye-hand-coordination whatsoever I appreciate a game that mostly plays itself and yet is addictive enough I forget about unimportant things like sleep or food.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on a whim and while this isn't necessarily my favorite type of came, I thoroughly enjoyed it for the most part. If you want a cheap throwaway game that will blow some time, this is it. I especially recommend it to people who like to micromanage and test out different strategies,etc..Things I like-Simple gameplay loop with lots of room for strategy and synergy-Amazing aesthetic that feels with excellent visuals and music-Pretty interesting premise and decently written dialogue.Things I didn't love-Even with all the different strategies and elements, it started to feel grindy after several hours and the lack of progression slow compared to many other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game based on the huge popularity it had when it was released. unfortunately, I failed to see what was so special about it, don't get me wrong, I like roguelike when executed correctly in a way that keeps every run unique and fresh(For me, the best example would be Hades). but this game tends to feel really repetitive in each run. I barely had the determination to go beyond the first chapter. In short, it was really boring for me that I barely played 6 hours before deciding to uninstall it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: very fun game to have running on the side while you are doing other task. I use it when i'm watching youtube videos or streams as a way to still be interactive without actually having to start up a whole 200 hour long game to load in and do nothing for like 30 mins until i decide to watch tv. This little boy just sits there a runs for u which is great. The higher loops do require some attention from you to swap out your gear or place the correct tiles where u would perfer but besides that the game is preety chill 8 outta 10 for me :) !
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel style is really pretty, I don't think I will ever get tired of seeing the characters and creatures in this game. Which is good because you're going to be seeing them a lot. In typical roguelike fashion, you're going to be looping over and over again in order to find out who is destroying the universe and put an end to it. This is definitely the game for you if you like to play something while doing something else - it's not particularly "active", it holds itself more as an idle RPG kind of thing. You can alter the world around the Hero with cards gained from battle, and equip better stuff over time to get ready for the boss(es)... but that's about it. I have found this game perfect for playing while working from home as it doesn't require my full attention and can be paused at any moment if required. A lot of the time spent in this game is just going around and around, hoping RNG gods smile upon you and give you what you need. But then again, that's the beauty of this genre. Just one more run, one last loop...
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Just about 3hrs in and Loop Hero has won me over in so many ways. Without diving much into the details of the actual gameplay mechanics Loop Hero delivers in a big way when it comes to it's narrative, it's music and it's art direction. The entire thing is just a joy to play, it tingles through your senses and as far as "End of the World" narratives go, I cant think of another story that feels as original and fresh as Loop Hero does. Each and every creature, person and thing you interact with from a narrative perspective brings something powerful and fantastic to Loop Hero's story. Do yourself a favor and consider picking this one up. A friend gifted me my copy and by the time I was done with my first session I was turning around and gifting a copy forward to another friend. What a wonderful game you've made Four Quarters, BRAVO!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly creative and the gameplay is both simple to learn and incredibly complex. I have a deep love for games that let you play in real time or pause to think things through, and Loop Hero handles this mechanic flawlessly. The art style is unique and visually amazing, and it's super easy to put down and pick back up without forgetting what you were up to. Cheers to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is an AFK Battle Game which has interaction only when picking building placement, cards, and items for the camp. You start off with a generated map that has a road which loops, and you go around and around until you either die, retreat, or beat the boss then you can still keep going or retreat. Each loop increases the power of the enemies as well. Equiping items during a loop is more about RNG and picking the best out of the batch that you get. You'll be able to play as a Warrior, Rogue, and Necromancer, each with their own builds. Cards are used to shape the world during the loop, and items will help you but you'll need to find a synergy and get enough of them. Over all this game was worth the few dollars I payed for the 33 Hours. I'm still on the final chapter but not willing to grind more for my camp to keep going on.I wouldn't suggest playing the game if you're looking for anything with real substance. This game is indeed a grind feast with a lot of RNG on top so be prepared.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game a lot because of the retro fantasy aesthetic. The idea of building the world around you and having these realistic interactions that affect stats/gameplay is fascinating and definitely got me hyped in my early hours. There is some pretty great world building to go along with this too, and I love the dialogues because they help set all that up.Where the game falls apart for me is in the actual rouge-like elements. Specifically in how repetitive it gets so quickly. I found myself doing the same things over and over again, getting bored of using the same cards and builds because it was what worked without much feeling of forward progress. For example, the only class that I've been able to complete runs with any degree of regularity is the warrior. Despite unlocking two other classes, it just seems way more powerful, reliable, and easy to use. Maybe there are cards I would have been able to get later on that work better with the rogue and necromancer, but I don't really know that for sure because you can't view specific details about the tech tree unlocks later down the line. Perhaps I might be able to see that one of the next buildings I can build unlocks the "forest" card. Great, what does it do? Does it synergize with one of the other classes somehow? Don't know. I don't even know how to unlock that building, because the game shows me little symbols without names or tooltips for the resources needed to unlock it. I've never seen those symbols before though and they don't seem to correspond to any of the types of resources I've been picking up. None of my cards are capable of making a resource with that symbol and I don't even know what that symbol means because I can't scroll over it to view a tooltip of some kind telling me how I can get it. Even when I spend a lot of hours grinding to unlock a building that supposedly allows me to trade books to unlock codex entries, all it does is unlock flavor text for already discovered things, not new information. The opaqueness of these mechanics really kills my motivation to make forward progress because I'm bored of doing the same thing for 10 hours and I have no idea when its going to get better. It also sucks loosing a run, and therefore a bunch of resources, because you suddenly died. Without being able to control the battles directly, the only control you have is in what cards you place, what gear you equip, and what talents you take. But all of that is subject to both RNG (in terms of what you get) and also varies wildly in balance. Some cards/stats/talents are total garbage while others are auto-takes. There just isn't enough variety, and a lot of these systems are pretty shallow. Like you're just getting +7% more attack speed or something most of the time. It doesn't make decisions interesting and tactical. Like obviously I'm going to take +7% attack speed over +5% attack speed every time. Its very Diablo-esque in that its about scaling your numbers to get bigger without really making very interesting moment-to-moment decisions. For example, maybe I could get an item that adds possibility of lightning damage to my weapon, and also a talent that says whenever I deal lightning damage, it stuns the enemy for 1 second. An environmental card effect could then say stunned enemies take extra damage or something. This is how you do synergy in an interesting way, but its more complex to implement, and it feels like the developers kinda just didn't want to do all that. I think what they wanted to make was an idle mobile game where you really don't do much and don't have much control over anything, because that's what this game is. Its repetitive and the RPG systems are very shallow, even for an RPG lite. It has painfully slow progression and a major lack of variety. If you like an endless grind of collecting random resources because I said so and making numbers bigger then this game might be interesting for you, but I like something with more depth. And sure, maybe it gets better later, but I've already played 10 hours. I beat a boss and I'm just bored now because the prospect of doing it all over again with the same setup but harder just isn't appealing to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I have such incredibly mixed feelings about this game, and what I've settled on in the end is this: I like this game, and I'm having fun (mostly), but I don't think it's a very good game. The fun I'm having comes also with a *lot* of oddities, too. The game feels almost hostile to the player in a way that isn't fun, denying the player any explanation of a ton of the basic mechanics. I think they wanted to make some sort of challenge of discovery part of the game, but some of the things you have to figure out are ridiculously obtuse and un-intuitive. It feels like the developers don't want me to play their game. Sure, you can solve that by reading guides and finding the wiki page, but I don't think that is at all a point in the game's favor.Every cool moment or interesting idea presented is immediately followed up by something confusing or frustrating. I don't feel like this game challenges me in any way that is interesting. It's just rolling the dice with RNG but dressed up a little bit to seem exciting. I don't feel like I'm making good decisions or doing anything smart when I win a run, and victory is rather hollow for it.I got this game on a sale, and I've been having a much better time with it since I read some guides and started playing it in the background while watching a movie or chatting with friends. I do just a quick run and then put it back down, and it's fine. I wouldn't buy this game at full price, and I overall don't feel like it's the kind of game I can recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Came into this game, expecting it to be weird, boring, and not my cup of tea. But because of the high praise and positive reviews, I gave this game a chance. And I am extremely happy that I did. This has been one of my most favorite recent releases and I obviously highly recommend. Recently, I made quite a bit of money and decided to buy A LOT of games. So far this game appears to be the best out of a lot of very good games.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazingIt may start a bit slow on the first hours, but you quickly start to understand its mechanics even though they are no explicitly explained.It feels amazing to make a build that is really effective and slash through the loop with flying colors, the lore is really really interesting even with the little bits you get if you don't read the in-game's encyclopedia.Nearly 50 hours in this game, and i think i'm gonna play it a little bit more to complete it.It's such a blast of a game, and i love every pixel of it
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is a video game in which the player travels through time and builds a world to defeat a mysterious force known as the "void." The game involves building a loop of cards representing the hero's journey and collecting resources and allies to progress. The game is known for its procedurally generated content, which means that the game generates new content each time it is played, making for a different experience each time. Loop Hero has innovative gameplay, beautiful art style, and interesting story. 7.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Literally exactly what I've been looking for. I'm obsessed with tower defense games, cookie clicker like games, and card game rogue likes. This is the first time I have seen a combo of these three done in one game, and in such a synergistic and fun way. I love it and I don't see myself stopping any time soon. Brilliant work!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from a great visual style and sound design, this game also has gratifying progression and intuitive game mechanics. When you boot this game up, you don't even need to ask what the gameplay loop is like. Easy to pick up, hard to master. Great dev team that tackles balance issues and bugs quickly, and offers public betas to test out new features. Definitely one for the basebuilder/roguelight fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: THEME: You're saving the world, which has been destroyed and thrown into a formless void -- or maybe you actually have dementia and severe hallucinations/delusions while walking in circles around the block.GRAPHICS/SOUND: The graphics are terrible 80s pixel art and there is no voice acting. That may be merciful because the English is at times tortured. There is music, I suppose. Also, I know they're inspired by old JRPGs, but for the love of a MANATEE, will you please stop making text appear letter by letter while beeping? Not cool, old-school games. Not cool.GAMEPLAY: it's a roguelite, so collect stuff, die, come back stronger. Mostly you sit there watching your dude slaughter ratwolves and worm-things. Your player role is to place tiles on the map (which determines the monsters & building materials you get) and equip items on your paper doll. You can't be a woman; I don't know why. SO WHY ARE YOU THUMBS-UPPING THIS? The truth? Well... I can't explain it. The first few hours I was like, "This game stinks." Then I couldn't stop playing it. I am mesmerized by my new forest unlock and golden tiles that change how a class plays. I want to beat the JRPG-ish bosses and save the world. It's strangely mesmerizing.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Great rogue-like with a unique and comprehensive progression system with a fantastic original sound track that, combined with the retro-style graphics, really immerses you into the world the developer has crafted for us to explore. Before playing, word-of-mouth reviews had me believing that the game's writing, and English translation, was somehow messy or incoherent but I have not seen any such display as of Chapter 3 (where I'm currently grinding through) and I do not expect to see any such grammatical errors and messy dialogue.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Loop Hero after multiple PC Gamer issues sung its praises... but I don't understand why anyone likes it. The progression system is super grindy and poorly explained. The town building segments allow you to make mistakes which can cost you hours of resources when you realize you have to tear down several tiles and rebuild. After a couple of hours it feels like you've seen all of the tile combos and there's nothing more to see. While the general concept is novel, there are far better roguelikes out there that are actually fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is a roguelite card-driven game that is  a Slay the Spire clone!  Can you believe it?  It should be commended on that alone!  Of course, that probably leaves you asking just what the heck it is in the first place.At a very high level, your hero travels around a looped path that, at first, only has a campfire on it that will heal you as you pass through it.  The path will spawn basic monsters that will drop gear that you can equip to boost your stats and HP, but more importantly, they will start dropping cards from a deck that you build over time.  These cards aren't played, per se, in the traditional sense, but rather they create features on the map on-demand.  Not all of these features are positives, but the negative ones tend to give you access to tougher mobs that drop better loot.The lite side of things, then, is whenever you decide to stop at camp (or you're forced to it because you risked too much), you can spend resources that you've gathered by bashing mobs and placing tiles to build structures that give you benefits on the field.  Whether you stop voluntarily or not, the world outside resets and you start back at loop level 1, ready to go around again.  However, as you build structures, you will also unlock different cards that you can add to your deck for various benefits, making it easier to farm resources for your next pit stop.Narratively, your hero is trying to remember what the world looked like and therefore is rebuilding it piece by piece, but the trick of the game is that every time you stop at camp to beef up your long-term progression, you reset the world again.  As such, resetting is a strategic decision like in most idle games rather than one caused by error as in most roguelikes/lites.  In fact, you really have no agency over how combat or travel works.  You make no decisions on who the hero fights or how they fight at all.Player agency on the field is entirely about equipping gear (mob drops) and placing tiles by playing cards (also mob drops).  As such, while you could compare Loop Hero to a clicker/idler, it requires a lot of attention because you will need to constantly drop tiles onto the map and swap gear if you are to survive long enough to even see the first boss.  Of course this means that the grind is as real as they come, but at least you can survive for quite a long time each run, even on your very first play, so it doesn't feel like the game is stacked against you in that regard.Oh, and that tile-laying thing?  That's not just for show.  Yes, each of the cards/tiles tells you what they do and how to place them, but what you don't know up front is that laying stuff out in a certain way will actually spawn stuff that isn't found on a card.  Experimentation and discovery are key to this aspect of the game, as is your deckbuilding which you can do when you stop at camp.  It might be tempting to remove the annoying mob nests from your deck, but doing so could severely hinder your progress in more ways than one.  However, playing around with the cards is as fun as any other deckbuilder without bogging you down with combos or memorizing keywords.  You don't even have to count copies or figure out frequency or anything like that - you may have only one meadow listed in your deck, but you can bet you're going to get 10 copies of it in no time.Four Quarters have done a terrific job here making Loop Hero an engaging and fun experience, even if you never see it to its end.  There's something compelling in the way that they brought together elements of roguelites and idlers together and I'm sure that this will be the start of the new clone season to come.  At this point, I'd buy ten more copies of Loop Hero rather than spend a dime on yet another Spire clone.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It's an 8-bit auto-Monopoly Solitaire World Builder RPG with elements of Magic TCG, Settler of Catan and Tower Defense. What's not to get and love? It always amazes me when there is a new, must-play 8-bit game like this. It's like it could have existed 40 years ago, but uses all that time of game ideas and design to make something truly fresh and unique. Additional specific comment: I LOVE how this game handles looting. There are only 12 inventory slots, but they rotate out like a stack, first in, first out. Anything that falls out of the bag due to having too many items is converted into a more permanent and less restricted resource. It's such a wonderful feeling to loot your ass off and not have to worry about the space limit.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop hero for me was an incredible experience.Going in, I wasn't so sure, the cards you have at the start are pretty basic and generic. The first sign to me that loop hero was special, was when I put 9 mountains next to each other and discovered the mountain range. The map building aspect is so cool, and discovering new combos is really satisfying. Aside from the map building, the actual gameplay put me off at first. The gear seemed boring, and I thought that the looping and trying to beat the boss would get old quickly. I was dead wrong. The number of game-changing things you unlock while building out the camp was astounding, I feel like I'm playing an entirely different game than when I started (in a good way). The last big surprise was the different classes. I expected the rogue to be somewhat similar while employing perhaps the use of daggers and a crit mechanic of some sort, however, many core mechanics change and it was so refreshing. The blending of my favorite genres works spectacularly here from combining deckbuilding, roguelike, turn-based RPG's and base management. Last but certainly not least- the art style and music. The retro style and music is done very tastefully and doesn't come off as gimmicky as it does in many other games these days cashing in on nostalgia.Overall, couldn't recommend more! 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: If you're perusing the reviews, then you, too, have probably been duped by the vast marketing machine that has pushed this game into the forefront of gaming conversation. The music, the retro graphics, the streamers who seem to be enjoying it.I regret to inform you that this game is not worth it. I've lost respect for many people who seem to have sold out promoting this game. I hope the payout was worth the reputation hit for them.The basic premise is solid, but the execution is painfully tedious. In order to progress, you need to farm resources, some of which are only going to drop every couple of attempts. The River, in particular, requires 15 Orbs of Expansion. Even if you edit the config file to artificially go 4x speed, this will take hours of looping the same thing over and over with no other benefit.After you farm some of these things for hours, you may find that you can't actually place them anywhere because there are hidden restrictions. This means tearing down other tiles, losing those farmed resources, and then trial-and-error repeating the process, praying to not get into a bind beyond your control again.I find it baffling that people actually enjoy any of this. It's tedious, repetitive, and uninteresting. What's sad is how close to a great game it could have been. If strategy/skill could have overcome the time sink for farming resources, I'd have a different opinion. As it stands, do not fall for it. Tons of money has been put into making you think this is the next hot thing. I'm here to tell you the truth that it's not.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: At first it was cool because I'd never played a game in this format before.  It was a unique experience of game play with some good text dialogue and interesting progression.However once i hit the next chapter I sort of realized that game progression wasn't going to be that hard and it was going to be a slog of grinding / dying to upgrade the camp.  Not long after that this new game play style kind of lost its charm and i realized I wasn't having fun actually playing the game, so I've dropped it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this without any prior knowledge of the game, and thusfar it's been one of the best gaming experiences of my life. The 80s RPG pixel art is incredibly beautiful, and the game combines a lot of styles and mechanics but somehow it does a great job in letting you discover how everything works. I've seen it described as a roguelite/deckbuilder/auto-battler, but none of those terms really do it justice. Loop Hero is a unique blend, a thing of its own. Loop Hero is an expertly crafted work of art, please don't skip this one! Got to go and play one more loop now... or maybe two. Probably five.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, it's really hard to describe this game. I can only say that it surprised me, how good it is. The game plays by itself, your character moves in a loop. After defeating monsters the player is rewarded with cards (chosen randomly from a preset pool of cards aka player's DECK)The game revolves around the player using these cards to modify the map. And collecting materials. After a set amount of modifications has been made the boss spawns and the player is given the choice to either fight the boss or run away. Running away or dying to the boss (loss of a percentage of materials) gets the player to the camp, the materials are used in the camp to unlock cards, passives, a different class (maybe there are more but I only unlocked 1) and more.After defeating the boss a higher difficulty loop unlocks with a new boss, player can then choose which one they want to play. The story is alright, at least it's not cringe.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Good game overall.Also note that after hours of grind (collectiong/crafting supply items, upgrading buildings which gives you hp potions and revive options) game becomes so easy.You collect/craft supply items through your gameplay which I had 83 of them after almost 60 hours. Those items can synergise with other items. So for example, there is an item called "kitchen knife" which gives you +1% base hp for each food item in your camp. You can also use hp potions (there is a grind part for that too of course)In the end I had 7 kitchen knives and 57 food items so that makes ~+400% base hp. I also had 10 hp potions, each healing 10% hero hp on use. With this setup, I tried killing end game boss using all three heroes and had no problem.As a result, you have three options to beat the game1) Spend hours on grinding perks, items etc. then beat the boss using no brain at all.2) Play smart3) Get crazy RNG (which is very unlikely)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The game is simple, but addicting. There's a lot of hidden strategy that isn't obvious the first few dozen runs, and things stay fresh as long as you're creative with your approach. There can be some hard let downs, but the permanence of your progress is inevitable as long as you keep rolling. Highly recommended as the game on your second monitor, please enjoy it between rounds when you're dead.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is another gem on Steam.I started at 2 pm and couple of minutes later was 1 am already.Everything is spot on, pixel art, animations, music (damn, this music!).I don't know how many classes are there, I'm on rouge. I've been surprised there are different classes.At first everything looks so simple, but quickly rides the tempo.This game begs for 1:1 ios (tablet) port. Please consider it in a future.For me it's 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the most addictive game of the year. It looks great, it sounds great, it plays great. It's every enjoyable element of deckbuilders, idle games, and roguelites smashed together into a one-of-a-kind soup that tastes great. Almost every aspect of the game that seems weak eventually gets supported by later developments and unlocks, making it feel perfectly balanced. The amount of strategy involved in character builds, tile placement, and deck composition is enormous. Even with exactly the same deck, no two expeditions are the same. And despite the metaprogression giving you progressively greater advantages, you will never make an inch of progress without a combination of long-term planning, good luck, and meticulous equipment tweaking. Oh, and the plot, which it doesn't need at all, is fantastic. This game could've gotten by with an opening cutscene and nary a word after the fact, and instead there's a unique and surprisingly philosophical narrative that unfolds throughout the experience. It's not as character-rich as Hades, but, then again, what is? In a related pleasant surprise, there's also lore entries for everything in the game. I've only got a couple complaints. It'd be really nice to be able to pull up the encyclopedia during an expedition and learn about the world during downtime, although this might not be entirely coherent with the narrative, so I can forgive it. The difficulty spikes between chapters are unbelievably sharp -- if you're not at Light Yagami levels of strategy, you're gonna be grinding earlier chapters a lot to give you an edge. Overall, a strong early contender for game of the year, and one of the best curiosity purchases I've made on Steam since Hotline Miami released. 10/10, would painstakingly reconstruct a broken reality from my memories again
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop hero is a masterclass in UX design and how to streamline gameplay. Its a great rogue-lite that does things differently than other games. Instead of the hero, its more like you're more a DM.  Setting up the events, enemies, chests, and landscape for your character to adventure through. As you play, you'll optimize your heroes gear and stats using a quick and simple interface that never slows you down. Already addicted. Pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the most unique games I've ever seen. You are a hero lost in a void and are slowly trying to remember. Remember what? Basically everything. The entire game is focused around memories, from the resources to the NPCs. You set out on expeditions to remember what came before, and while doing so you gather resources that you need to build a village.While on these excursions, you travel around a randomly generated path. 100% of the gameplay consists of placing tiles and equipping your character.Even though the combat and travelling happen fully automated, it doesn't feel like you're not doing anything. This game really doesn't have a lot of set pieces, but it does an amazing amount with the little that it has. It really shines when you find out that combining various tiles result in unique combinations.Absolutely worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Update: My review below was based on 3 hours gameplay. I've now hit 34 hours gameplay. I've completed all the chapters with each character, unlocked all the cards, seen just about every combination there is, and if I dont quit now I'll probably put another 30 hours into this game. Super addictive, easy to fall into the "just one more loop" rhythm, and im thankful this is not on my phone because I'd have put a lot more hours into it.Original ReviewLoop Hero is what happens when you take a clicker / idle / progression game, add some sim/management elements, add some style, add some story, and get rid of microtransactions. The end product is something that gets its addictive claws into you, especially if you are someone who is susceptible to progression games and min-maxing you builds.Three and half hours in my first session, and I definitely want to see what happens next.Also, I hate to say it, but this game would be a much better fit as a mobile game. I would love to be playing this on my phone during my commute to work.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: SHORT REVIEW: Loop Hero its "addictive"... but shallow and boring, like cheap nicotine. Brand new  ANTI-game concept, based on NON-interactivity, and the worst playibility I ever seen. 99% of the time you just sit back and do NOTHING.- Even if you are Gari Kasparov, or Stephen Hawkin`s smartest brother, you just CANT WIN.Cause, in loop hero, your decisions are 95% IRRELEVANT-  the "stuff" its 100% RANDOM and 95% USELESS. Your decissions are 100% neccesary, but 99% IRRELEVANT - the ONLY WAY to progress is spending DOZENS, HUNDREDS, OR THOUSANDS of HOURS of your life... FULL REVIEW:- Sid Meier once said ""A game design is a collection of interesting decisions, and the “stuff” in the game is there not just to fill space but to let you execute decisions.”".  In Lopp Hero, the "stuff" are 100% RANDOM, and 95% USELESS. -  Your decissions are 100% neccesary, but 99% IRRELEVANT  Your hero make turns in a empty circuit. As you progress, you kill things, and recive random objects and "random" cards, that you can place all around  the track.  If you place a spider nest card int the circuit. The next turn, you hero have to kill the spiders. If you place a forest, your hero have to kill wolves.  Any time your hero kill things on the road, you recieve RANDOM cards and RANDOM items. (most of the items are only garbage). You can pick this equipment to "dress" you hero with swords, armour, etc. but you DONT do the fight. You dont command the hero in battle. You dont jump, dont use the "sword", or the "shield" You cant use any potions, or spells: you ONLY DRESS YOUR HERO, SIT BACK and WATCH  your life depend on LUCK.- Later in the game, you may unlock and pick other cards, to kill other things. But there is no real deck (this is not like Magic: the Gatherin, or Gwent).  Loop its a lot more random, and a lot less strategic- It will be easy to make the game deeper. (more interactive and more intresting) imagine that you gather resources to build your own weapons lets say you place forest cause you need wood...- But NO. in Loop, almost everything is RANDOM. There is no clue on what item you will recieve next Each of your decissions are useless  As player, YOUR ONLY TASK is to check what LUCK has for you search in the garbage pile, and pick the rare usefoul items before they are discarded- Most of the time, only LUCK will tell when you will die.   Yes, you can die a litlle bit faster... but -sooner or later- you will die because you just cant survive-  At first, you have ZERO chance of survive- Each time you die, you keep a few resources After a number of deaths (or retreats), you may have enough resources to raise a BUILDING-  You MUST construct buildings if you plan to win one day. But, most of the time, You only die (or run), just to recive a bunch of (mostly, useless) materialsAfter some hundreds or thousands of turns (literally), you will have the materials to make the needed buildings... and, ONLY then, you will be strong enough to kill a boss - Even if you are Gari Kasparov, or Stephen Hawkin`s smartest brother, you just CANT WIN. Cause, in loop hero, your decisions are 99% IRRELEVANT- the ONLY WAY to progress is spending DOZENS, HUNDREDS, OR THOUSANDS of HOURS of your life... - Graphics are "nice"...  but gameplay is so shallow.... so empty... so random... so repetitive and SO BORING.  This "Dressing princess" game its noy my cup of tea  yes, after some hours of gameplay, you may be able to trade some resources... most BORING thing i ever seen  Buy The Last Spell instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: This game almost lost me when I first tried it, it seemed so complicated and odd. 80 hours in, I can say that it's more than worth the money. I like relaxing games, and Loop Hero fits the bill. It's an auto-battler, so you just sit back, choose your gear as it comes in, and choose where to put your tiles. Like many roguelites, the skill is in figuring out how much difficulty to add to your run so that you get strong from fighting lots of stuff but don't crush yourself. Nice to play this while watching a video or listening to some music. The difficulty level is quite high—you'll be doing a lot of dying—which suits me just fine. It's fun to discover unexpected combinations of the landscape tiles, and each of the 3 classes has a distinct feel that improves the game's replayability. It took me at least 50 hours of play to beat the entire thing with one class (the rogue).This game is old school in every sense—not just the graphics, but the lack of explanation. It can be incredibly opaque and counterintuitive, and there were many things I didn't bother trying to understand too deeply (like enemy stats). I'd recommend checking out the Loop Hero wiki to improve your strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting casual game that is gonna be an excellent time sink. Pretty methodical but also very casual in it's game play. It plays like a management game, where you focus on gearing a hero who automatically goes through the area defeating creatures while you use the loot to build the environment around them.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop hero is a strategic game where you have to use your brain in order to progress, you learn from your mistakes and improve. You can also build buildings in your village to make your journey easier. I'd give this game a valid 8/10 for its creativity. Everything might be a little confusing in the beginning but if you just read what the items do you should be fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Greed is good, you say? Not for me - not for this game.It always gets me every single time I would die from being too greedy, thinking another loop won't hurt but I end up losing majority of those hard-earned resources...... I have to remind myself every single death and loss that greed is not. good. at. all. Anyway, I digress. I've been enjoying the gameplay so far; lore-wise, I've barely scratched the surface but the bits and pieces I've seen seem interesting so hopefully it would be just as enjoyable. It sort of gives me that "building a civilisation" vibe.Good game. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A nice game to play, quite addictive as just one more expedition, just one more loop.By placing the tiles on the map one increases loot drop possibilities on the loop run, but also the amount of adversaries one encounters. This feels like one can make the game as hard or easy as one might want. It is a rogue light and by leveling up the base camp map one unlocks boons and extra classes for future runs which is great for replayability.Was sceptical at first seeing it, but it works delightfully and is a charming little game to play on and off.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very addictive! My only problem is how grindy the late-game gets - expecting you to grind 20-30 loops for an hour each before progression is even plausible. A bit frustrating, but there is so much experimentation you can do while you do that to keep you engaged you'll end up doing it anyway. It's got that 'one more expedition' feel to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: My not-especially-indepth review:  this game is good.  If you like roguelite strategy games, you will probably enjoy this game, as that essentially is what it is:  a strategy game.  A strategy game that begs for just one more turn. . . when there are no turns.  Highly addictive, and with enough complexity so far that things don't get repetitive.  Every 1-2 loops, you typically will unlock *something* new:  a building, a class, or an entire new mechanic.  The art and music are also quite good; minimalist, but with an appealing style that I've not really seen much elsewhere.No game is perfect, mind.  I would say its biggest flaw is that the interactions between structures on the map are almost entirely mysterious.  To see what happens when one building mixes with another, you have to experiment, and in ways that are not especially intuitive.   Maybe there are improvements later on which give some hints, but if so, I haven't unlocked them yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Do you feel lazy at doing something productive but you also too lazy to play a game, do you just want to stare at your computer screen?. Or do you like me?, a person who is actually busy with something but you just want to procrastinate and play something light so that you're not guilty enough to abandon your responsibility, while also not too committed to your game. then this game is for you!This game really forces you to explore basically everything that exist in the game, every tile combination, item, enemy types, i even still confused sometimes which enemy drop which resource, so basically encyclopedia is your best friend. lore wise, the main character really didn't know basically anything and everything that is ever exist in like... ever, so i can understand how the game forces us to be creative with our own world that we created. and help the hero pave the path.there's also some achievement that i am having fun trying to complete it, such as "Broken Geography" and "Crunchy Company". trying to get the achievement has always been a motivation for me to be better at this game, to find the best class that are suitable to achieve the optimum result. and speaking of best class, Necromancer is one of the best class you can get in this game if you want to go far. not fighting alone is already one of the best advantage a hero can get. Because your trusty skelly will make sure that you're going far on your journey, and you better make use of that.in my 50+ hours, this game really teach me something. because this game heavily relied on trial and error, RNG, luck, and sufficient knowledge on the class and tile composition. don't be afraid to experiment, losing is normal, sometimes you feel like the luck isn't really on your side, but that's okay, life is suck, you can't get everything in this world. Sometimes you really hate to start over when everything is good, your gear is good, you have looped for the longest of times, you're on your top of the game, and then you realize you're on chapter 1 and there's limit to how much resource you can get on there, but you didn't wanna move on, you're afraid to start over. that's fine, i played my first 30 expeditions in chapter 1 precisely because of that, and i kinda making it harder for myself because there's some resource that can only be obtained on chapter 2 and so on, but at least you can familiarize yourself with the game first.thank you to the developer for creating this funsized game that accompany me on my daily life in a past few weeks. and also for anyone who played or planned to buy the game, i hope you have fun just as much as i am:)
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It's cool, enjoyed it on the steam deck so far. not my fave rogue like but really cool concept and great execution. Imo, the gameplay is good, but gets grindy fast without introducing too much to the loop to keep it fresh. Definitely worth checking out, idk if i'll play this to the end. Banger soundtrack too.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: It was a bit addictive and quite interesting. Basically an idle game. Nice concept, sometimes RNG-heavy, and some village management in between the rounds.If you like the old school sounds and looks, and niche games, this could be great for you.I had fun, but I'm moving on even though I've not completed the story yet. So there's still something that didn't quite hook me.7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is absolutely one of those games you start playing and time around you just melts away like the time forgotten described in this games story. You will absolutely be saying to yourself "just 1 more loop then I will go back to base" until you've risked too much and only get to keep 30% of your resources. Progression, like many rogue-likes, is tied to your greed.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: The game definitely has some interesting ideas, and you can clearly see the effort and polish that was put in. However, the core loop is you doing mostly nothing, as all combat is done automatically. Furthermore, your choices in items and tile placement seem to vary from trivial to meaningless. The different characters that I've tried so far don't change the experience all that much either.I'd recommend this if you have an interesting podcast or audiobook running in the background and need something mindless to do while listening. Otherwise, you can probably skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A mix between idle games and tower defence. Two genres I really don't like put together to make something brilliant. This is the perfect game to 'waste' time on. You'll be going round and round and lose track of time very easily. Before you know it an hour has gone by, where does the time go? Well, apparently some ass hat is making it disappear. Good thing your trusty hero plans to put a stop to that.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Addicting for a looping rougelike autochess card game. It mixes the elements very well. Although it does feel very grindy and punishes failure with reduced progress rather than just the reset. I wish there was the ability to back out whenever without the loss of items, although there's probably a future perk for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: A simple but fun mix of rogue-like, idle, and management game. The core is easy to understand, but as new elements and mechanics are introduced, your ability to improve and make your runs more efficient rises along with your understanding. Multiple playable characters with their own playstyle, meta-game item management to unlock new items and abilities in-game, and tile-combination bonuses you'll only learn about by experimenting. Give the game a try, and I'm sure you'll fall in love with its slow-pace action and deep systems begging to be explored.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Great - old school good looks with a winning combination of roguelike dungeon, base building, deck construction, and idle style movement - into a single gameplay loop. And loop you will...But for the more prosaic, a non-permadeath roguelike game of character progression with gradual permanent unlockable bonuses, three classes, three chapters with a different boss (and probably a final 4th boss), lots of different terrain, monster types, monster skills, equipment etc.For the price, a solid title to soak up the pandemic hours quite happily. Excellent. I recommend it if you like this kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I love rogue likes, imo goode rogue like > AAA games. But as for this game.....This game starts off really good. It is a game that you need to take hours on hours to learn. The nyace and synergy in placing different tiles next to eachother suprices me still after 27 hours, but there is a few problems. After you used hours learn the tweaks and kinks about how to boost your chance to get progress, you will find out, it does not matter. No matter how much you tweak your gameplay, you will fail or succeed depending on RNG loot and "lvl up skills". The problem is that a round takes too long to play when you loos so much. One round will last yhou 30 min - 45 min, and if you do not get the right RNG gear and skills you will lose no matter what. When I say 30-45 min it is at 2x game speed and that is the fastes the game will run.. And when you die you will lose almost all of your so called loot to improve your "starte area".  The problem with this game is two fold.1.) A round take way too long. There should be a 3x and a 4x, and the player should them self deside how comfortable they are at this speeds.2.) The RNG balance is way out of wack. The game if fun for a few hours, but when the RNG kicks you down 9 out of 10 times, then there game is no longer fun. Can't recomand this game as it is today.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely what I didn't know I needed. If you've ever played a Castlevania game on the Game Boy then you'll be right at home with the vibes of this game, and the dialogue/lore is top notch. Really challenges me to experiment and play things outside of my comfort zone, and fittingly punishes me for greedy, risky plays. Never lets me feel too comfortable, either--I really, really enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this game. it has a bit of everything and done well; story, dialog, game play variety, music. The story is simple but effective; save the disappearing world. The dialog is snarky and fun; "hes GOD for Gods sake."Gameplay variety is so smooth and fun. you can create simple decks that make barren lands look like some sort of DND map. deserts, forests, villages, burning trees, and much more to find on your own with synergies that buff you or hurt enemies or even hurt everyone. you collect supplies and create your own camp that also buffs you up. a camp filled with fun characters like Asmongold, a Grounds keeper, and his cat, Cat Danny. The difficulty does ramp up a bit but nothing you shouldnt be able to handle after playing a few rounds. and learning. and maybe dying. The music is top notch. Great tracks to get you motivated to clobber some Ghouls.Overall great game. I played 31 hours of the demo and hit 13 on here and ive barely beaten chapter 2. Dont want the gravy train to end too soon. 9.5/10        -.5 for strange bug that cuts all sound if pc is put to sleep. i love that music, man.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Go play. Die. Die again. And again. And then realize you got so strong nothing is actually a big dealThe visuals and music is wonderful (for indie game, at least). Some balance issues here and there. but still the game is wonderful. Do play it, but don't set your expectation too high. That's a neat indie, not a "game of the year 10/10"
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game! Very easy to pick up, extremely casual, and  great if you don't have a ton of time to play in one sitting. Replay factor is off the charts in that you start with simple strategies and tiles. Before you know it though, you are creating more complex builds in order to accomplish a specific goal. Love the way the game rewards you and builds over time as well. You start weak, but soon get much stronger.Outstanding job Devs, probably my favorite game out there right now!
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and interesting game, definitely worth a shot for its price. The progression is well implemented (although a bit grindy at times).I really disliked the fact that there's no Borderless Window mode, this is a game that really favours you having two monitors and watching youtube or something while you play, however on fullscreen it minimizes everyitme you click outside the window...
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive, and Extremely fun to play. Fantastic retro style (and the CRT filter is one of the best I've ever seen)  You will have to do a bit of grinding but you'll enjoy it so much it will hardly feel like it. The unique thing about the game is,  while still semi-rougelike, your adventure is only as hard as YOU make it. Last loop or two a bit to easy? Place a few more enemy tiles down and get those extra few items from them, a bit too tough? Lay down a few buff tiles, but watch out! Some buff tiles, can have some consequences! I was very on the fence watching the initial gameplay, but after getting into myself, I've found myself hooked. Get it now! 100% worth it's price.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game! Super original, which is hard to do in the rogue genre nowadays. It maybe feels a bit grindy to work on your base and improve your runs - this is alleviated by the alchemist, but the alchemist takes a long while to get to and there's nothing really suggesting how useful the alchemist is for improving your camp until you unlock it. Otherwise, it's pretty good. It's relaxed, has tile combos that are fun to explore, classes that feel fairly different and fresh from one another, interesting base building and upgrading - all that you can really need in a rogue, with a new and unique coat of paint.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: If you buy this game thinking you will stop playing it before the 2 hour refund timer expires, you are most likely wrong. This game is addictive sure, but so are Methamphetamines. Both feel rewarding in their own way but really, you just need to get your ♥♥♥♥ together. But as your ass gets fatter and your existential dread intensifies, you'll realize that the hours you've invested "playing" this game could have gone into literally ANYTHING ELSE and you would be better off for it. I was pulled in by the art style and graphics and the idea of an idle deck building game loop seemed appealing. But after the amount of time I've spent I just don't feel excited to come back to it. The equipment and loot system desensitizes you to any reward you feel getting an epic or legendary as an upgrade. It just replaces another piece of gear that is stuffed into your inventory and after several hours I was barely paying attention to stats or weapon types. I simply stopped caring. Lost interest. If it had the highest level and had the 'yellowest' background it got equipped. I'm sure I could have min-maxxed the stats if I spent more time making decisions to, but I didn't want to. After a while I didn't even understand why I purchased it in the first place. If this was a game I played on my phone then I would play it while I was taking a ♥♥♥♥ but outside of that I would forget about it. I place rocks to create mountains and meadows to create...meadows. It gives you resources you use to upgrade your camp and unlock more cards. The grind comes from having to run the same loop multiple times until you are finally able to overcome the boss. The boss gives you some story and dialogue and then you die, lose all your gear and 60% of your gathered resources for that loop. Grats. Start over. Repeat that over and over until you have enough resources to build a potion maker or a blacksmith or a farm. Cool, you finally upgraded your camp! Some upgrades seem interesting, like unlocking the rogue or having healing potions but ultimately they don't feel like they were worth the wait. I demolished the building that unlocked the rogue class because having a second class felt useless and uninteresting. With those resources I built a farm or something equally unfulfilling. Your little hero is already off to the races, killing every enemy that spawns on the map in a very hands-off, uninteresting way. You can swap out his weapons  but really that's it. Everything else is automated. Some times I would get distracted by something on TV and entirely forget this game was running. I dunno guys, I'm sure this works for some people but I can't help but be bored as ♥♥♥♥ playing it. _childDocuments_.review: I don't normally like to do reviews with only 12 hours of play time, this will be the exception. This game is super addictive. The slight nuances between all the different tiles you obtain via deck building elements is a blast to figure out. The overall progression of your main base camp keeps you wanting to dive back into the loop. Once you start getting a stockpile of worthless gear, have no fear, it will turn into additional resources for upgrading the main base. If you are a fan of rouge-lites, this one is an absolute must.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero

_childDocuments_.review: "Just... One... More... Loop..."The second thing that you'll notice about Loop Hero is how the wonderful graphics (which you'll notice first) are slightly curved to recreate the experience of gaming on a CRT TV. You might think that this will be distracting, but soon you won't notice it anymore, which is a great example of how much thought went into this game: The creators recreated a CRT TV's curved display—probably because they grew up gaming on CRT TVs—and then they made sure you wouldn't really notice their design decision; after all, if you grew up gaming on CRT TVs, you remember the games, not the curved displays. And a similar intentionality flows through the entire game, from the story (which is fantastic) to the gameplay (which is ranges from deceptively simple to rewardingly complex). I don't want to spoil anything about the game, but I'll say this: The third thing you'll notice about Loop Hero is the way the game just drops you into a pile of gameplay mechanics and concepts that you won't understand after your first or tenth loop. There really isn't a tutorial, and that's by design: The creators trust players to figure out how things work, and the game rewards players not only at the end of that process but throughout that process, which is why it doesn't feel like a process; you just feel like you're playing a great game—and you are. However, it's hard to categorize Loop Hero. I've heard people compare it to Slay the Spire (one of my favorite games) because it's a roguelike with deck-building elements, but you're going to be disappointed if you're expecting Slay the Spire. There are also TRPG elements, but it's not a TRPG simulator. Loop Hero is its own game, and it's one of the best games I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Loop Hero
