_childDocuments_.review: So, I've not played this 50 hours yet, but it's been left running for a while, probably half that.  I've beat the game.  This game is very addictive, but work, like you're managing a spreadsheet. You have to pay close attention to everything if you want to actually win act 3 or 4 and your runs may take 5 or 6 hours a piece.  All you are mostly doing is check stats on each item, for hours, because if you play like you need to for acts 3 or 4 you'll be getting a steady stream of orange items ever battle, sometimes 5+, where your only job is to choose it and equip it.  This is not fun, its tedious.  I'd say first 2 acts are fun.  To move on from there, you have to use only certain cards, usually a deck of 11 or less, and do the same thing, and hope for right items or traits to finish a run in act 3 or 4. This game has taken time from me, I've beaten it, but it doesn't leave me feeling accomplished or  like that time was worth the investment, like on game like Total Warhammer 2 (on higher difficulty) or dark souls, hard but the pay off is there.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally beat the game, omega, act iv or whatever, and then carefully kept my loop going to about 25 loops, actually fairly confident I could even leave it on all night. But while I'm still watching it the thing crashes. it's gotten my progress, so I guess the story impetus is mostly over.. but I lost the insane amounts of loot I had carefully spent literally 6 or 7 hours building. opening the game again, all of it is gone. I had items saved up, playing necromancer - I had a resurrection and then still a "take all" option left. There was no way I was gonna lose that loot, I was going to let it play out to the limit. But no, all gone. I got the end cutscene and achievements (a good 10 loops before the crash) but I lost all the FEELING of victory. After 44 hours playing, my triumphant final day (which I basically took off to play, which is a testament to the game really) ended up being a feeling of frustration and loss, and "eh", I guess I'm never going to play this again.You see, I was going to use that to upgrade my camp, then try out a few different styles, see about trying to beat it as each class, etc... but I couldn't upgrade anything and my relatively narrow path out the gate with how I tried before meant I basically have to redo the whole day without the excitementWhy? Because this game apparently doesn't have a basic autosave feature or any way to continue after a crash.For a game with levels that are also bosses as unforgiving as a soulslike, but as complex as sim city.. the lack of this basic feature seems like a huge oversight. I'm lucky that this crash hit me after the boss and not right before it, though I admit if it had I would have just tried again and treated it like every other countless time I tried and lost everything on some dumb movebut this time I did everything right, I had all the luck, it was a thing of beauty I had just set up and was ready to kick back and watchi - and I lost anyway through no fault of my own. I've heard there will be an update to allow saving and continuing during an expedition. that's good. I hope that also means they will fix this bug, At that time, this will become a firm "yes" and I'd even maybe call it a 5 star game. I loved most of my time with it. Unfortunately, this ending means I'm unlikely to pick it up again.Edit: Seems they have added a save feature. I haven't checked it out myself, but that's enough for me to revise this review. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a fun, addicting game that provided a more than adequate experience for the price. However it falls short in some key ways that keep it from being great/ a game I'd come back to. Pros:- While it's hard to describe, it has the right "feel" that you want out of a progression-based game. It's satisfying to find new items, build out the map, and get upgrades to give you an edge later. - The central mechanic, that you fill up the map with a landscape to provide both bonuses and enemies to fight, is a novel idea that's promise helps draw you into the game as you wonder what strategies and combinations are yet unexplored. - The aesthetics are mostly really enjoyable. The music, while repetitive, is great chiptune background for your hours of grinding. The 16-bit retro art looks good, and the story, or at least it's premise, is interesting. Cons: - The game's biggest shortcoming is that there isn't more to it. While at first the tile combinations would seem to promise a lot of depth as you discover new ones, in reality there just aren't that many of them, and the balance is such that some choices are so much generically better than others that you won't get a lot of replayability out of trying out different builds. In addition, the game is pretty short in terms of content. There are only 4 Acts that don't take that long to complete once you get a few base upgrades and figure out the mechanics. After that there's nothing more to challenge you. You can wring a little more fun/time out of the game by trying to make your character so OP that you can leave the game to run on it's own for hours to farm resources, but by the time you can do this it serves little to no purpose to the game's progression system and you'll never really find a meaningful challenge after that. In fact I'd say the game never really challenges you more than your first run before unlocking anything. The game only gets easier from there. The game could really use some kind of post-game challenges. A NG+, an ascension mode like StS, etc. - The game is incredibly vague about how various mechanics work. For some things like tile combos, that's half the fun, but it's frustrating to not even know what the stats on your gear do so that you can make meaningful decisions between items. In addition, while the game tells you a few stats about the monsters you fight, it leaves out important info such as the monster's armor and evasion chances which are useful pieces of info if you want to decide how to prepare your build to fight them.In some cases you have inconsistent wording that makes it hard to know what something does. For example "HP" is used interchangeably to describe either healing or max hp increases. - The UI isn't particularly good. While the 16-bit art looks nice, the more atari-style graphical depictions of the characters on the loop are hard to distinguish and once there are enough of them the screen gets so cluttered it's easy to lose track of where your character even is. The positioning of certain elements of the UI splits the eye focus such that you can sometimes not notice important pieces of information if you're not paying careful attention. There's an entire mechanic, the stamina bar, which I just straight up wasn't aware existed until significantly later in the game when increased attack speed made it relevant because the bar representing it is so tiny that it's barely visible until you manage to run out of stamina.

_childDocuments_.review: Or Loop Hero is a new concept game.  You continually roam a loop that you modify with cards won from monster battles.  Easy to play, difficult to master.You are trying to recover the world.  The world is now a dark place and you are confined to a looping path.  You are trying to bring back the world.There are three classes, warrior, rogue, and necromancer.  You start off with the warrior and once you beat the boss of the first loop you unlock the rogue and then you unlock the necromancer.  Each class has different play styles.  All three start off with a shield, armor and a weapon.  However, only the warrior can use all three.  The rogue can use only the weapon and armor.  The necromancer can't use any of them.The warrior is a straight forward hack and slash.  The warrior will gain gear and cards from battles.  The gear can replace what they are currently using.  The cards are used to change the loop terrain.The rogue can dual wield weapons and collects trophies from each kill that are turned in at the camp at the "end" of each loop for gear.  They also gain cards.The necromancer raises skeletons to fight for them.  They cannot use any of the warrior starting gear.The cards you gain when you defeat monsters are used to modify the loop.  Many cards modify other cards if they are close to each other.  Like forests and thickets in the productivity of meadows (which give you health at the start of each day).  Some cards will modify your path, like the Village that will heal you when you pass, but give you a quest (increase the stats of a monster) that you will receive a reward for after you defeat the on your next pass.  Part of the game is figuring out what cards to play and where it is best to play them.Each pass along the loop increases the monster's stats and the rewards you will gain by defeating them.  You can choose to exit the loop when you die or when you are at the camp.  If you exit when you die you will lose some of the resources you have collected.  If you exit at the camp you will not lose resources.The resources are used to improve your camp.  You will gain better starting gear and additional gear slots with different buildings.I recommend this game. This game is easy to play, difficult to master, and addictive.Intel i7-8086K Coffee Lake 6-Core 4.00GHz CPUCrucial Ballistix Sport AT 2666 MHz DDR4 RAM (16GB x 2)ASUS GeForce RTX 2080 Overclocked 8G GDDR6Or

_childDocuments_.review: A simple game with a lot of depth. Your job is to place obstacles on the path of your AI adventurer. As he fights monsters, he gets new gear, until eventually he is ready to fight the boss. The challenge is to not place so many obstacles that the adventurer gets overwhelmed and dies, but not so few that he doesn't kill enough monsters.The depth comes from the combination of obstacles that you can make. Most map tiles can be combined into new effects or harder challenges, and some of them help or hinder the adventurer.The game's story comes from interacting with the NPCs at camp or by chatting with some enemies and the bosses. Further lore can be extracted from item descriptions.This is one of the most fun and satisfying indie games I've played in a long time. Highly recommended.

The rest: Really formulaic and requires guides if you want to retain your sanity, i.e. every change in your built would require hours upon hours on fruitless expeditions, just to see if x is viable against y boss, which becomes the only deciding factor, after you know what enemy tiles to place/avoid. Very little built variety, samey weapons, armours, items, perks—there's always something that dwarfs the competition/is objectively superior to all the other options, you would be stupid not to gun for that.This game would be great if the path you can walk wasn’t so narrow, if there was more than a handful of ways you can become powerful enough to achieve anything. _childDocuments_.review: In Loop Hero, you observe as a small dude traverses a perilous path. It’s a game that plays itself, almost. Only delegating some very specific tasks to you, architect of adventure; tailor of heroes.First of all, you get to equip the hero as he works his way through his adventure. It’s the only reason Loop Hero needs your input to begin with. Because as time flies, his environment develops and grows more fierce. He, however, does not, unless you nudge him in the right direction and don the wonderful trinkets he gathers along the way. It’s where all the juicy RPG-stats and terms come into play. Like strength, evasion, and critical chance. And where you have to juggle equipment with disparate types of benefits. Do you want a warrior with a penchant for damage dealing, or a more defensive one that regenerates lost health? Secondly, as an architect, you’re tasked with developing the world. This is where you specify the different locations the hero has to pass through in order to progress, and the surrounding landscape. Oftentimes, placing these have pros and cons -- giving him specific resources or equipment in exchange for an area that now generates monsters he has to defeat first.You might have guessed it already, but the path he’s on is on a constant loop. Meaning that once he finally reaches camp, his travel starts anew -- same road, same conditions. Therefore, all the things you place for him, the environments you form, serve as immortal landmarks until he retires. Whether that’s because of death or otherwise. It’s also where you’re most likely to overindulge in Loop Hero; where hubris can take over and really make for an impossible mission. Overengineering is actually a classic pitfall. More often than not, you want to be smart. Play environmental tiles and effects that have synergies and added bonuses. Sure, a scary forest is a must-have in any fantasy adventure. But place it next to a magical grove, and suddenly mother nature chips in with killer vines and an occasional golem for you to fight.Most of what’s going on under the hood here is outside of your realm as a player. In fact, the flow of information almost necessitates a lot of guesswork and goodwill on your part, deciphering how it all works. It’s a slow churn, for sure. But if there’s one thing you should remember playing Loop Hero, is that it’s all about the process. Thinking you can force your way to the end credits is a sure-fire way to frustration. So remember to enjoy watching the ebb and flow of his adventures. Advancement will come automatically -- more or less.Recommended if you have a tinkering nature and enjoy engine-building in 8-bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. Not bad but generally feels incomplete (like having inventory slots that are never unlocked and generally balance doesn't feel right), grindy and repetitive. Visuals and soundtrack are quite charming though. Has a little bit of dialogues and story which are okay so far.First you need to learn what cards (tiles) you can place and what are their interactions with other cards and what kind of enemies they may spawn. Once you got that, you create some strategy. Gameplay becomes just placing cards (tiles) according to the strategy (there isn't that much to think about placement) and filtering the items you obtain. That's it. Filtering items becomes pretty tedious very quickly because you just get flooded with items and need to figure out if it's better to have 0.25 X stat or 0.3 Y stat while there isn't any kind of in-game preview calculator and unequipped items are trashed. Oh, and about 2-4 times per run you choose a skill from random selection. I suppose that's the worst part of RNG because these skills really define your run. Then you repeat that while trying to stop yourself from placing too many enemies on the map.Basically the game has wedged itself in the dangerous gap between idle games and interactive games where it isn't idle because you can't just leave the hero alone but the gameplay isn't really engaging and becomes tedious.

It is an absolute grindfest that takes ages to unlock anything, has few actual different strategies, and refuses to explain many of its mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: I don't remember the last time I played a game that I simultaneously loved and loathed at the same time,The game has so much going for it at the start with different tile combinations and seemingly expanding strategies the further you go. Unfortunately that is only up until the end of the 2nd act, where the immense grind sets in. Grind for hours for resources to unlock a building to get one specific card or miniscule % increases per upgrade to your hero that becomes absolutely vital for completing the game.The game also relies heavily on RNG from item drops, ''card'' drops and level up perks. The perks go from completely useless to required to win. But only if you get them early enough, otherwise they fall into the useless pile with the rest.The art is gorgeous, the story, even if limited, was interesting enough for me to grind through the endgame. I would say of the 47 hours I put into Loop Hero, 25 - 30 of those were pure grinding.This game has the potential to be amazing. If the developers fix the grind, rebalance the perks and add some more tile combinations it probably will be. But until then, this is a grindy timesink that is hard to justify to most people.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't remember the last time something /some game made me feel this way. The nostalgic vibes take me back to simpler times. Same satisfaction I felt after going to Blockbuster to pick up a movie to watch while grinding the night away on RPG's Recommending this game is ''No brainer''. Hell, I actually bought 4 copies to share. That should be enough to convince you. If not...Imagine a dungeon-empty dungeon. Start by traversing the path on a loop to get stronger and acquire better loot as the Loop levels increases. On top of that, the creature spawning elements surrounding the dungeon are set by the player as you gain cards that you use to fill the dungeon area while adventuring and grinding the loop. Don't let the graphics or (Castlevania) look get you unmotivated. This game is a ''Love letter'' to Old-school players as it welcomes them to a new but somewhat familiar setting. Price? believe me, the game is too good and addictive. You will wonder why it's so cheap after playing.  no need to mention the soundtrack---------it's too good! -Graphics: Wouldn't want them any other way-Sound: Already said is going to take you back...way back:) It's goooooood!-Game-play: Simple but engaging. not an easy game. GRINDING NEEDED!IMPORTANT: The combat is ''AUTOMATIC''. You take care of the adventurer, their weapons and armor.Ok, I'm done........................................JUST ONE MORE LOOP. (You will remember this)

_childDocuments_.review: Loop Hero is an inverted tower defence: you place enemies and your hero moves around the map to defeat them. On each loop the enemies that you've placed get harder to defeat, but to balance that the more difficult the map becomes the better the loot gets and the stronger your hero becomes. To progress you must tread the fine line between life and death to stay ahead of the difficultly curve.The game has many interesting and complex card synergies along with just the right amount of RNG to prevent it from becoming formulaic. Without doubt this is the best strategy game that I've played in the past 20 years. For me it was very reminiscent of the classic Zeus + Poseidon from Impressions Games  which I played when it originally came out.Despite how brilliantly crafted the game is, it's very far from perfect. There are three things that let it down for me:- The meta progression of the hero outside of the core game is a confusing mess. It adds artificial difficultly through a hodgepodge of various mechanisms that are required to boost your starting stats, which even after completing the game I don't really grok.- The game reached a plateau about halfway through where I felt like I was just grinding for resources that I wasn't really sure how to properly allocate. I get that the idea is for the player to work out the best strategy, but needing to grind for an hour to just try something out takes the fun out of it.- A huge amount of time has been spent developing a story that I personally couldn't be less interested in. What I am interested in is how the game actually works and this is presented a very cryptic manner. I get that this is probably a trend in game-making, but personally I would prefer a clearly written set of instructions rather than a codex of clues.Anyway gripes aside, it's an awesome achievement and a game you must play if you're a strategy fan. It will stay with me the way that Knights of the Old Republic has (again I played that when it first came out).

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice change of pace and an interesting game play LOOP. It is a lot of fun upgrading your base and figuring out what works with what and how you like to play. Slight build spoilers  The difficulty curve is pretty minor. once you unlock all the cards and so on, the game becomes quite easy. After which point unless you intentionally make things hard on yourself you wont have any trouble completing the game. If you like to 100% games the achievements are nice and fair and you could probably get them faster than i did. As a roguelike game it feels a bit limited in its replayability, you yourself might employ some sort of third party randomiser to keep things interesting.  Overall is a very nice game and i had fun playing it. I am intrigued to see what these guys make next.

_childDocuments_.review: The world is gone, rendered to dust. The entire universe was wiped from existence by an unknown force. Nothing is left,... nothing but a man. A single man clings to his reality by will alone. With the little remaining memory he has left, he can bring fragments of his world back to life, little by little rebuilding it. Will he gain the resources he needs to grow his whole universe from the seeds of his own mind? Will he find and defeat the shadowy creature that stole all of reality from him? Or, is he destined to fight in an endless loop for the rest of eternity in the small whisp of the world he left behind?Loop Hero, a deck building roguelike with idle elements, is about a man fighting to regain the world he lost by rebuilding it piece by piece and surviving by the tip of his sword. Place tiles to make his journey more fruitful, but beware the consequences. Every boon has a bane, and the greatest resources can end his quest in death.Your quest is to build a thriving town out of the void with the resources you find fighting in the loop. Placing tiles on that loop might gain you health, better gear, or a valued resource, but it could also unleash ancient monsters.You can choose the tile you are able to place before starting out on your adventure, and you get them at random when you defeat monsters. There is a limit to the amount of tiles, or cards, you can choose from before each adventure, and you get a wider selection as you progress through the game.Stopping by a village will gain you some health back, and a new quest to defeat a boss. A boss is essentially a very beefy monster, far stronger than others of its kind. Returning to that village gains you a nice piece of gear. Adding fields to that village boosts the amount of health you will receive from it, but also risks spawning scarecrows. Too many villages and they'll spawn rogues who try and steal your best gear.Most of the game is centered around a track. Your character travels this track, and fights anything that gets in his way. The player has no control of his fighting but can equip him with the best gear, which is Diablo-ish randomized loot. You can find anything from a sword that hits every enemy at once, to a vampiric shield that sucks the life out of your victims. Progression unlocks character types like a thief or a skeleton-raising necromancer as well. Experience will also gain you traits like having a wolf companion, or the ability to stash half your loot every time you pass camp so you don't lose as much if you die.Never think you're safe. The stronger you get the closer you are to death. As you gain power, so does the hoard. A couple of wolves or spiders sound easy enough, but make one of them a quest-boss, and add a flesh golem, and you could be in your last battle.The graphics are in true Devolver fashion, an old-school pixelated piece of art that when coupled with the music that sounds like something out of an old RPG like Ultima feels very nostalgic for a retro gamer like myself.I've found this game quite enjoyable, and certainly able to spend countless hours in. For those of us with less than stellar patience, you can speed up time. Different types of warrior are unlocked as you progress, as well as new tiles you can place. The price of $14.99 is well worth it, as it's a game you may never tire of. I highly recommend it, as I've played it over and over. It never seems to get old because your strategy is constantly changing.

_childDocuments_.review: Great and rather unique game (at least for me).  This game is aboutmechanics: learning by experiencing and adopting.  There is an archingstory, partially with cut-scenes. It's fine -- but of course no onecares at some point.The game is about meta progression and fuses some genres likeauto-battler, deck-, and base-builder.  The graphics and soundare great and aim for some 8-16bit style (visuals remind me of thethings, that can be done on a C64 nowadays (long past its prime); soundis bleeps and banging chip-tunes).  For play style, it reminds me most of Darkest Dungeon: you makestrategic decisions before a run by picking a character (once unlocked),a chapter (ditto), an (ever growing) deck, and what to put in yoursupplies.  Then the loops start and your goal basically is to stall asmuch as possible, see as much of your good cards to chooseyour fights.  Or in short: hedge against bad luck -- and yet theresometimes just is.Things to complain about are definitely things the game hides from you.You don't know by picking your cards, how your deck is set up.  Somemechanics are just not explained (what is magic damage).  Also there isno "battle log", that would allow for some insight.  The fun thereclearly is to learn this by experimenting and doing -- but if you areused to tool tips like in Crusader Kings 3 or Slay The Spire, this isquite some barren land.Overall this a very fun and addictive game... while you are learning it.Once you know your way around, you will snowball into invincibility.Nonetheless a clear recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is really cool and for the first few hours it's fun. But progress is too slow and after the first boss, it gets repetitive (well, it's called 'loop hero', wadda ya expect?). It lacks a good progress system because the things you progress in don't really seem to matter except to get other heroes. And I don't know what this game has to do with a roguelike, it's more like a browser/idle game in which you have to be more active (which is not a bad thing. It reminded me of 'Dark room' which is a great browsergame in my opinion).But at the current state, it sadly lacks something.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay  : 7/10You're a "hero" stuck in a loop, you'll let the autobattler do the thing, sometimes the AI can be very stupid by focusing tank or adds but It works, I'd like to have the speed on battle too. The item management is ok, I think there's some balances to do : some items are too strong for their level and others can be weaker than underlevel equipment. The build mechanic before boss is great and be able to continue after it to push a little more your run is a good idea. The story will follow your game experience after each "first discovery", pleasant maybe a little too "simple" but It's a rogue-like not a RPG Price and Lifespan : 7/10The price is fair, I'd say the game can be finished in 40h but I didn't finish it yet. I enjoyed most of my gametime, there is no wiki so you've to learn a lot from your mistakes. A lot of content for a game of that genre.Audio/Graphism : 9/10 As a old gamer, playing this game remember me the old arcade times, that retro feels pretty good. The pixel art is super neat. Soundtracks are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing.Keep continue guys, hope you'll release more content or even DLC !

_childDocuments_.review: A rather grindy tower defense-ish game where YOU are the mob and the towers don't shoot you. I'm conflicted on this one, it makes a very good first impression but then gets quite repetitive as you are expected to grind for resources. Great sprite art (when it's not minimalistic), nice music and doesn't demand any real agility, reflexes or quick thinking (fights are always resolved automatically), so you can run a loop or two after work easily.I'd recommend to watch a bit of the gameplay first and then take into account that unlocking new features goes at a very mediocre pace.

_childDocuments_.review: The writing, the art style, and even the basic idea of the game is cool. The actual gameplay part is horrible, terrible, no good, boring garbage.The gameplay loop (haha) involves you watching your little adventurer walk in a circle. Sometimes he runs into bad guys, you get to watch them fight. Sometimes the bad guys drop loot or land cards. If the loot is better than your gear you can upgrade your little dude, land cards are placed on the map to alter the game. If your dude dies, or if you retreat to camp, you bank a few supplies, then start over again from nothing.Much of the game is about experimenting with terrain or equipment, seeing what works and what doesn't. But it's also really random. I had two runs end because I didn't get any useful cards in the first loop. There is a progression mechanic of a base that you build up. But it takes a very long time. This game has a weird vibe of hurry up and wait. Sometimes the game will give you several choices to make at once, and then other times you'll have nothing to do for minutes at a time.This is so boring I just can't deal with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting to like this game. It bills itself as a deck building rogue like game and it was recommended because I really enjoy single player card games (Tainted Grail, Slay the Spire etc.). Do not sleep on this game. The mechanics are difficult in general, and a lot of the game is trial and error. I highly recommend this game for it's pixel art aesthetics, banger of a soundtrack, and solid repeatability.

If you have a hard time reading the game text because of the font just change it in the settings.It takes a lot of mechanics from other games & create a unique experience.Resource gathering, base building, tile building, deck building, (reverse) tower defence, light rpg elements & Slay the Spire re-playability gameplay are some genres I can think of on top of my head.It's slow passed but time runs by. _childDocuments_.review: Loop hero is an excellent example of modern day Roguelikes that are fantastically designed but outstay their welcome extremely easily. The presentation is fantastic, the game mechanics are solid (although a bit barebones), the story is extremely gripping at first, and the game puts a ton of effort into giving its world some character. And I can't overstate just how well made those parts of the game are, when you meet a new enemy they get their own dialogue box sprite and they will talk to you about how they perceive the broken world that you the hero are trying to repair. The deck building aspect can be a ton of fun and you can mix and match cards that you maybe would never have thought of. It can be very addicting to do a run and reset. Those are just some of the many examples of the great potential this game has.So what makes this game drag on if so many things are so good? Currently I have 10,2 hours into the game according to steam. In about 2 hours you will see most of the important and interesting mechanics the game has to offer, after that it uses the same horrible system that a lot of modern roguelikes employ where you have a base that you upgrade, and upgrading that base makes you more powerful. However in loop heroes case this becomes even more important because you barely have any control over the game. If you want to avoid RNG your options are to grind a ton or to abuse certain builds to make it through the harder levels.So how difficult is this game? Up until what I assume is the final level, I haven't had much trouble at all. But the final level is what made me give up on this game. Its exactly everything I hated about the game combined. This is technically also a deck builder, but your freedom in creating a deck feels like it doesn't exist. The final level is so hard that its hard to win even with using really strong strategies, if you haven't been grinding a bunch like me then your base also isn't strong enough to make use of a lot of these strategies. So not only am I not playing the game the way I want to play it, I also have to pray that it all ends up working out. It completely drains any and all fun that I had with this game and feels overly punishing as a result.It sucks because I wanted to experience the ending of the story myself. It starts off pretty strong and while it does start getting pretty monotonous, it still is pretty unique and fun. I wanted my time in this game to matter more. But I am not willing to put in another 10 + hours just to see that ending, this game does not have enough depth for that to be the case.I give Loop hero a very disappointed negative review. I think there is a lot to love here, but to me it absolutely wasn't enough to keep me going until the end. I would rather have spent my time playing something else.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, that would be an amazing game with a bit more polish. I also think that rivers should be changed, since optimal river placement is un-intuitive and very jank looking.Still, I very much enjoyed this game and excitedly look forward to any updates or other games from these creators.

name: Autopsy Simulator
detailed_description: In Autopsy Simulator: Dead Memories, you play a middle-aged pathologist whose life has taken a turn for the worse. After a career downfall and the loss of your beloved wife, you live each day shattered and exhausted. One day during a routine post-mortem, you find a relic of your past hidden inside a body. Now, it feels like something just won’t let go… FEATURES Examine the bodies and study the files to get all the answers Every case has its own story and each victim has their secrets. Uncover them to solve the puzzles and learn the truth about your subjects... and yourself. Cases prepared and analyzed by specialists Each case is designed with the help of real life pathomorphologists and forensic doctors, ensuring the feel of being involved in an authentic autopsy process. Down to even the most gruesome details. Detailed depiction of organs and autopsy cases In-game bodies, organs and injuries are crafted with unprecedented attention to detail. While this makes it easy to create immersion, it's also not for the faint hearted. A unique mix of simulation and horror A combination of engrossing gameplay mechanics and spine-chilling moments will keep you on your toes throughout all of the story's chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest issue is the name of the game. I expected an actual simulator where by observation and deduction I have to determine the cause of death. After playing almost 2h, it is more like clicking on stuff that the game wants you to click on until you got all clues and then reach a hand-held conclusion. It doesn't feel like I am doing anything, except pressing buttons to advance the narrative for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Autopsy Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: In the process of refunding this now. For anyone looking for a simulator in which you are a coroner or mortician and dissecting bodies, this isn't it. This is just an even more hand holdy version of mortuary assistant with a worse story, worse voice acting and no components of a simulator at all. As someone who absolutely enjoys immersive life/job sims, this is false advertisement and honestly it truly upsets me because this game was on my wishlist for years and to see what it is on release is a massive disappointment. My gripe isn't with price, or even the content. I'm sure if it was labeled as a horror game visual novel, SOMEONE would have enjoyed it. But labeling this as a simulator is just false advertisement and misrepresenting itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Autopsy Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say - I've been excited for this game for months and followed a majority of the updates and releases. That being said, I have to give this game a pass. I beat it in one sitting, and I was let down. I'll start with the positives, first.-Medical Accuracy I love forensic science, it's been a special interest of mine since I was a teen and it was very cool to see an accurate medical autopsy. Obviously it's a game so not everything is super accurate, but the devil is in the details and I enjoyed that. -AtmosphereThe game does a pretty good job of making itself creepy - though with the subject matter, I feel that 's a given. However, there are parts that just...don't make sense and are there for the sake of being creepy. Like the bathroom, what's up with that? Why is it so dingy and broken, why is there a shack outside? Why did we put a saw in the basement after "cleaning" it when that would be a massive hazard? We gotta move the story along, I know, but it breaks some of the immersion. Dunno, maybe I'm too picky. That's where the positives end. -GameplayMaybe it's on me, but I didn't like how hand-holdy this game was. I assumed we would learn everything we needed in the tutorial (which I did like how it was structured) and then we would perform autopsies on our own to uncover the story based on how thorough and accurate we were (with help tips, if necessary). Instead, this is a hand-hold simulator for each autopsy and you cannot do anything that deviates from what the game wants. This was a massive let down. I understand that not everyone has in depth medical knowledge, but allowing players to make mistakes or give guidance when asked would be better. I've seen what other people say, and it feels like it falls just shy of being a true simulation game. -StoryI can't say much because I don't want to give spoilers, but I'll say this.I hated the story. I completely understand that this is narrative driven, but the story is so weak that the gameplay can't back it up. It's cliche, uninvolved and I honestly could not care less about our protagonist, if you could even call him that. If more time had been put into how we engage with our surroundings, I'm sure it could be really cool. There's also an entire plot point that seems to be missing (or I didn't find it) that involves two bodies we autopsy involving a bite mark, but I guess Jack is too busy trying to not go insane, or I'm connecting dots that aren't anywhere related. -UnfinishedThis game was delayed several times and honestly, I wish it was delayed further. The end of the game, it's very clear where corners were cut to avoid animating certain things and the final conflict resolves and does nothing for the story, which also gets largely revealed in the same instances as the conclusion. There's a secret ending that I'm not entirely sure how to get, but the other thing is, I kind of don't care about getting it.I'm not sure if there was a bug, but I sat there for about 3 minutes straight just downing pills and nothing happened. Not sure if that's intentional but I feel like something should happen if I just horf down the entire bottle.  Overall, I'm pretty disappointed in the game. If you enjoy medical stuff, you'll like it for that. Maybe they can update it in the future and clean up some loose ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Autopsy Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Summary: A very intelligent, but buggy and boring slog through a 4-hour long tutorial with what could have been an interesting story and concept.Pros:* Game looks great. A few graphical bugs here and there when I was speeding through a 2nd time (more on that later)* Impressive in terms of research, topical knowledge, and information. I'll be honest, I learned stuff from this experience....but that's about itCons:* Let's get the big one out of the way first: this is barely a game. When "simulator" is tagged on a title, you expect a lot of freedom in playing that role, but you will not get that here. Even though it's labeled as "horror", the scares are cheap and minimal. This is a "psychological trauma interactive narrative". Don't expect much more than that.* Confused scares. While few in number, the scares in here feel like they don't really know what they want to be. They come with the cliche stinger sound and blurry vision, but aren't jump scares? Imagine someone yelling "Boo!" while slowly walking around a corner. I don't know how else to explain it, but they just didn't work for me.* Far too "hand-holdy". I felt like I never left the tutorial phase. You are always presented with a single action you can perform, and that's about it. It would have been nice to have 1 or 2 "tutorial" bodies, then given the player a chance to figure out what to do next. It even teaches you some cool mechanics and scientific studies, just to never see it happen again. The only choice I got was taking pills too early and it soft-locked me. * Buggy (NOT broken). There were more than a few instances where I was soft-locked: got stuck, couldn't perform the "next step", etc. There are also some features that don't appear to be working consistently, one example being the "secret ending" being broken for a lot of people (me included).* Weak story. Pretty cliche, "person deals with trauma of a lost loved one with drugs and alcohol" trope. There's a buildup to the mystery of what happened, but the conclusion falls extremely flat.* Wasted potential. Look, some of the "cases" presented are genuinely interesting. There was a single moment were I had a revelation of cases being linked and it felt genuinely great. But there was no way to even acknowledge that in game. Like most things, it fell to the wayside and was gone in an instant. I know you're the pathologist, not the police...but it felt like nothing existed outside those four walls.* Annoying main character. Talks WAY too much. _childDocuments_.review: Autopsy Only Mode is now in an alpha stage and it is a bigger joke than I thought, it is literally just tutorials with no freedom to choose. A total scam.Woodland Games has abandoned the game, not surprising as they have a record of doing that. The new developers taking over have announced there will only be 3 bodies in Autopsy Only Mode, with 8 causes of death each. Bringing in new developers and they are not even going to perform less than what we were expecting for AOM, don't even bother making it. Not only was criticism not listened to, they literally don't care. Avoid this game at all costs, don't buy, don't view, don't pirate, let it die.Original reviewI'm going to post probably the longest, most in depth review I have ever posted. Autopsy Simulator contains neither simulation and barely any autopsies. In development for nearly 5 years with a 2 year delay I am still scratching the epidermis off my scalpel wondering how anyone on the development team managed to not realize how far off the rails this went. It's barely a game, contains a recycled story to every morgue related setting ever, and dialog. Oh my Lord does it have dialog. The character has so much dialog that the game actually will overlap itself while examining something making you miss up to 10% of the lines spoken. Let's break this down, let's actually tell the development team where to go and then let's see if anything is done. Autopsy Simulator is composed two things. Doing an autopsy, and maintaining your character's mental state with fetch quests. The best parts of the game are when you're examining an organ and finding clues. The worst parts, is literally everything else. Listening to your character groan and sigh constantly to having to fetch everything with boring horror elements while uncovering a back story about your character's trauma. Unlike real life, the best time is in the morgue. Look morgues and horror go hand in hand an it never gets old, but this is the first time where it has been so far off the mark that it makes you wonder why this thing was even made. Morgues and funeral homes are generally where people experience some of the most negative memories they will ever have in their life, so that is naturally scary. What's not scary is making it boring. With almost no interaction at all and the entire game is a tutorial giving you no freedom at all, it just makes you beg to hurry up. There are only 6 bodies, broken down from Prologue to Chapter 5. It's not until chapter 3 that we actually get our first interesting case, and I will now quote John Carpenter. "Death by natural causes, I hate natural causes! Give me a big old stab wound to poke around in, then I'm happy. Ahhh, here we are, body bags! See if it's murder suicide or a nasty accident, they put 'em in these bags." Yes folks chapter 3 gets interesting fast. Each body after 3 heavily progresses in the decay and mutilation that it's in creating a sense of deep investigation and wonder of what happened. It's actually the last 3 corpses that are the most interesting, and they are sadly dampened down by the non stop droning of the character and trauma elements. It's not until we get to the last body that I was full blown horrified. The condition of the last body is so grotesque and the horror only increases the more you find out about it. This is easily the best body of the game, and you don't even get to begin to start it before the game just abruptly ends. I don't mind anti-climax endings, but everyone hates endings with no explanation. To make it worse, there is supposedly a second secret ending with no way to unlock it and the people who have figured it out, the ending doesn't unlock for most making it a bugged ending. Making the player get to sign their own name on paper was a nice touch but a lot is missing. A corpse is not carelessly thrown in the same drawer. It's prepped, tagged, re-bagged or covered before the drawer. There's plenty of drawers here, and only one is used. What is this the public bathroom? Need to knock to see if it's occupied? However, this is a tool that the devs can expand upon. The devs now have two directions they can go:1: Listen to all criticism, update the game to be more interactive in the story mode and put in new details 2: Ignore everyone and fail I think I'm the only one staying around for autopsy mode to be released but you need to do work. A lot of work. The main story needs to have some more details put in. Such as actually hanging your apron up and throwing your gloves away. The characters mental state could be influenced by actions and not guessing at taking pills. For example, Jack doesn't sign in. How about letting us sign in the time sheet, this can be an influence to a positive mental state. Getting rest, getting coffee instead of alcohol, small things like this could have been done for a more classic ending A or ending B set up. Autopsy only mode needs to have way more corpse models than the six, and it needs to have nothing scripted. Make this thing completely random, make some cases sad, some normal, some utterly nightmare fuel (hence body 6, and actually let us finish that) Let us actually properly store a body. In fact, make an interactive style of us opening a drawer of the several so we don't know what to expect, or a mode where we have to unpack and do everything. There's so much you can do with this mode that it's insane. As the game sits now it is not even worth a glance, but the autopsy only mode, some additions and patches to the story and all done properly could save this game. Overall rating 2 (ironically the same amount we actually get to interact with) body bags out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for  after my friend recommended it a few years ago, claiming it would be a great game. Unfortunately, it turned out to be a massive letdown.The gameplay itself is riddled with issues. During the very first dissection, I encountered problems with taking a camera shot. The game demands you find a pixel-perfect point to take a photo, which is incredibly frustrating and tedious. is another nightmare. The models spin wildly with the slightest mouse movement, making it nearly impossible to examine anything properly. Don't get me started. They magically disappear with no explanation, while other operations involve small, often buggy minigames. This inconsistency is jarring and breaks immersion. The censor filter sometimes doesn't work, such as when you take a photo of the dissection. This oversight is unsettling and detracts from the experience. It's also worth mentioning that compile information from the CI/CD pipeline is included inside the game directory. Directories like  and lines in the debug log such as  should not be present in a final release. Additionally, it appears the publisher uses alternate accounts that don't look like employee accounts to respond to comments. This behavior seems suspicious and raises concerns about the authenticity of their interactions with reviews. An example of this can be found in the comments, and the evidence of that was retrieved from a public portal with Steam data, if you search their main username it will display their social media accounts such as LinkedIn or X.To top it all off, I got softlocked after picking up another lung to view it. _childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to give this game a thumbs up, but after much reflection, I can’t.*minor spoilers ahead*The game was slow to progress, but overall it operated pretty smoothly with the exception of some minor mechanical flaws, like interaction indicators appearing through objects or walls, and one section in Chapter 4 where Ripley tells us there’s a letter on the desk... what letter? Nothing to be found. Prior to this, Ripley was at his desk when he apparently wasn’t supposed to be, and then later when he was “sleeping” he was sitting there with his eyes wide-open.It was also very amusing that the camera angles and props were conveniently placed to hide the character’s faces during dialogue so they didn’t have to be animated.The autopsy sections hold your hand a tremendous amount. I thought after the prologue that this would ease up a bit and we would be left to our own devices with our notes to refer to, but it continued to be the same throughout. There is a LOT of monologue and analysis from the protagonist which can drone on, but at least the option to skip is there. I do hope that the upcoming Autopsy Only Mode pulls back on these aspects.It was also unusually irritating that there was no “clean-up” after an autopsy and Jack would walk around doing other things with his gloves still on.As far as being a “horror-hybrid”, the game simply wasn’t scary. There was no tension at parts where a jump-scare was attempted, and it was lacking in comparison to the effort poured into making an accurate autopsy experience (at least for those unfamiliar with the process). The monologue and constant need for Jack to talk was a large factor in removing any tension build-up and uneasiness when the protagonist had a psychological break. The sound design overall was disappointing. Lots of squishy noises while you’re playing around with organs, but not much ambient noise (or lack of) to increase the immersion and spook factor. There were also parts where Foley was noticeably missing as well, like the whisky glass not making a sound when thrown on the desk.Contrary to other reviews I feel like having ‘simulator’ in the name is suitable, as it didn’t feel much like a gaming experience, but more like a semi-educational virtual task list.The lacklustre story definitely made it feel like the budget and time was dedicated to making the autopsies accurate, so corners had to be cut in other areas to try and finish it. With that said, the ending was VERY disappointing. Its rare that a game can render me confused and speechless by the end of it, but man, what the actual hell was that? I was left wondering how the devs decided it would be a fitting conclusion.I also went back in to get the second “secret” ending in hopes that it would be worth the extra effort and give me a more satisfying conclusion, but it was somehow even more disappointing than the primary ending.While I’m aware that there is more to come for in-game content, in its current state I would not recommend purchasing this game, especially considering its given price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Disappointing Journey Through Autopsy Simulator: A Nurse's ReviewAs a nurse with firsthand experience in the medical field, including shadowing a pathology PA, I was eager to delve into the world of Autopsy Simulator. However, what awaited me was a journey more akin to a frustrating labyrinth of disappointment rather than an immersive exploration of forensic medicine.The game play of Autopsy Simulator felt more like a convoluted attempt at weaving a lackluster story rather than delivering the promised thrill of a truly terrifying experience. As someone familiar with the intricacies of the medical profession, I found the portrayal of pathology and autopsies to be grossly exaggerated and lacking in authenticity.While the graphics were undoubtedly a standout feature, with meticulous attention to detail, they failed to salvage the overall experience. The voice acting, rather than adding depth to the narrative, felt like an overly dramatic distraction, pulling me further away from any semblance of immersion.One would hope that amidst the chaos of the game, the medical information provided would serve as a beacon of accuracy. However, this was not the case. While some aspects were commendably precise, others were egregiously inaccurate, leaving me questioning the integrity of the entire experience.What truly disappointed me was the game's failure to capitalize on its potential. As someone anticipating a hands-on approach to diagnosing cases through autopsies, I was left sorely disappointed. Instead of being challenged to apply medical knowledge and critical thinking skills, I was subjected to a series of disjointed tasks that bore little resemblance to the reality of forensic medicine.It's evident that considerable time and effort were invested in the creation of Autopsy Simulator, yet the end result falls short of its intended mark. The mixed reviews it has garnered are a testament to the widespread sentiment of disappointment among players, and I wholeheartedly share in their dissatisfaction.In conclusion, Autopsy Simulator is a regrettable waste of both time and money. Its failure to deliver on its promises leaves players with a bitter taste of unfulfilled potential. As someone with a genuine interest in the field of pathology, I can only hope that future endeavors in this genre will strive for authenticity and substance rather than opting for cheap thrills and superficial storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: There are many negative reviews about this simulator slash game and unfortunately for good reason the criticism is deserved.I waited the three to four years for this simulator being a trainee mortician myself (In real life) and knowing I would enjoy it.First there is only five levels, and replay-ability is boring for many reasons, they way is made makes you not wan to sit through the endless stream of ummss and moans and groans from the main character. The  main characters voice narration is highly annoying full of over the top swearing coughing sighing and very irritating vocal tones. You get to the stage were you say to the character 'Just shut up I am fed up with hearing you'.Then there is the problem of the fact that you cannot manually save instead having to rely on automatic save which is so infrequent that if you stop halfway through..... when you return you have to play the entire scene again.The interactions are very very narrative driven and there is far too much talking from the main character when all you want to do is get on with the "simulator".The story is boring and the ending is such a cliff hanger that is is annoying, not very well planned feels rather rushed.The constant highlighting of "the next step" or item/object to pick-up is over the top, there is no ability to pick up equipment at free will you HAVE to pick up what you are told to at a certain time.Had the developers stated that there would never be an autopsy only mode them I am afraid I would be asking for my money back at this point, indeed the only thing stopping from requesting my money back and deleting this is the fact that there is supposed to be an autopsy only mode in development..... though I suspect that just like everything else the developers have done it will be a year plus before the autopsy only mode is even ready. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:- The autopsies themselves were very fun! I really enjoyed the medical accuracy and the in depth explanations for what we were seeing on the bodies.- I personally really liked the mechanics for the autopsies- The model design on the bodies was very, very well done, and the overall anatomy was excellent. - Autopsy only mode is on the way! Yippee!Everything else (minor spoilers):- I think I would best describe this game as an attempted horror. The atmosphere itself seemed to lean too much on eerie music on repeat and the protagonist coming unglued rather than subtleties that would have done it more favors- infrasound (the natural creepiness of mortuary labs and perceived silence would have done wonders for this game, I swear), strange noises, more discreet hallucinations (did you see that body just move out of the corner of your eye?)- The protagonist's descent into madness felt rushed, while everything else moved at an oddly slow pace until the very end when everything suddenly slams on the gas pedal, leading to a discordant flow of story.- Character animation for everything but the protagonist's hands felt like a lot of corners were cut. The only other character we see consistently is the office's clerk/security man, and we only ever see him sitting static in his chair holding a newspaper up to cover his face. Outside of a handful of brief hallucinations, the only time we have a character on screen for an extended period of time is the final scene, in which the character's face is conveniently out of frame as to not show him speaking to us. His movements are otherwise lackluster, feeling more like a standard conversation NPC than an aggressor in a heated conflict.- I'm not sure you could pay me to care about the protagonist's story, if I'm honest. There was a LOT of monologuing that was such an impressive mix of drivel and exposition that didn't hint to the right things and laid out a lot of stuff that could have just been left to context clues, while a lot of very interesting potential plot hooks were left to the wayside.- The fetch quests for items outside of the lab got on my nerves, I won't lie. Why is the notebook with the centrifuge information not in the lab, with the centrifuge? Why is the saw in the cellar after being cleaned? Why do you not have pump tubing in the lab?- This is just me being picky, but there were a few good lab safety things that drove me nuts; dirty tools, organs not being cleaned up, the protag taking his medicine with his dirty lab gloves (just... handling everything with his dirty lab gloves, actually), bodies being left on carts in the administrative hallway, and things like unbalanced centrifuge use.Would I recommend this game for the story? Definitely not. For the autopsies though, definitely yes!

_childDocuments_.review: I was very much looking forward to this game and purchased day one thanks to it's relatively cheap price, I can agree the game probably had £12 worth of work per copy put into it, however I do not feel I got that level of enjoyment out of this game.The game is a hand-holding 'Simon Says' where your character does not. stop. talking. Meaning if you want to enjoy the surface level story there is you must stop and wait after almost every mouse click. There is complete tonal whiplash if you don't stand completely still too, where your character will hallucinate something horrifying then remark about how messy his work space is :p Too many times I would enter a room, hear an audio stinger to suggest something scary was happening, only to click on the main objective 1 second later and my character couldn't have a care in the world.The story is also unfortunately very predictable if you have ever played a game in this rough genre before, any game where the protagonists wife has died before the game begins due to mysterious circumstances. There are two endings, the more 'secret' of which to obtain is not an ending, the game just stops halfway through the final chapter instead.The only active engagement you can have is with very brief mouse-maze mini games when cutting open organs 2-3 times a chapter. There are no punishments should you fail these mini games as well. I enjoyed chapter 1 and was looking forward to them taking the training wheels off an adding in some challenges, risks, times I may actually have to think for myself or secrets to uncover. The game contains none of these, as an example, there is one achievement for reaching the previously locked off top floor of your apartment using the elevator, there is an audio stinger but literally nothing up there, you must then walk back down.I am sad to say after collecting 100% achievements I feel as though this could have been a great comparison game to Mortuary Assistant, doing it's own things but the killer is really the hand holding nature telling me where to go, what to do, and the music and environmental queues telling me how to feel. Watch a YouTube walk through of chapter 1 and make your decision based on that, that's the game.Hopefully the developer makes some kind of sequel, this game would require a major overhaul to too much for me to recommend at the moment and I find that unrealistic.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. That's probably the only way to describe this game...not good, not bad, just, Meh. I won't spoil anything that happens for the story, however my thoughts for the game are.The game took me just over 5 hours to complete, not a vast amount of time considering the price. In essence you are a pathologist tasked with looking at bodies, performing autopsies and deciding on the cause of death. In theory this is a great idea, and a great game, however in practice the game tells you exactly what to do, at every opportunity. After your first body, you should be allowed to turn help off, but no, its "Get the scalpel, check this, cut that, drain those over there"..over and over on every body, which is a huge shame. I wouldn't mind if you were working on lots of bodies, but you aren't, just a handful then the ending.Graphics are great, with floppy internal organs that you cut and remove, jiggle in your hand a bit, slice and dice, then repeat on the next part. Luckily the naughty bits are censored so you will be able to stream and not get into trouble. The atmosphere is good, flickering lights and sound effects popping up now and then, building the games scariness levels but I found that they were too little and too ineffective.Jump scare wise, there are events happening that you miss a lot. You see something out of the corner of your eye and its gone, or the main character will make a scared sound "what was that?" and that's it. So much potential in a game like this, and failed to deliver (Check out "The Mortuary Assistant" for how Jump scares should be)The story line is fine, but gets grating after a while, going on and on about it, and how he is. The main character...man oh man does he annoy me. The voice acting of the main character is very much Keanu Reeves from Wish. I just found him really annoying.As for the ending. Without giving any spoilers away ll I can think of is the dev's had a strict timescale of when the project was be to finished and spent 99% of that time on the main story, graphics and sound, and 20 minutes before completion they realised they hadn't done the ending so rushed one quickly, because it was terrible. No thought into it at all, simply "Yea, that will do...pub now?" Disappointing.My suggestion for the devs, remove the story (or add a new game play mode) and just make this an Autopsy simulator, with random bodies and stories behind the bodies, allow people to work on them and come up with their own ideas on them.As I said, for me its just a Meh rating. I am in the middle of Yes and No rating, squarely in the maybe option that isn't there. If this drops below £10 then I would take a go at it knowing you are getting around 6 hours gameplay, but for more than that I would be hard pushed to recommend it.

And as a result, we got this Frankenstein of a game that's neither scary or fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first negative review I have ever given a game so I will just jump right into it.The name of the game is very misleading.  This is not a "simulator" game.  It is a realistic game, but not a simulation.  It is very on rails and offers the player an extremely limited range of agency.  It tells you what to do, when to do it and you have a very narrow window of deviation.  It is a story driven game.This might be a hot take but I think calling this a "game" is kind of a stretch.  It has no fail state.  You mess up any of the interactions and nothing much happens.  You can screw up the cutting mini-games all day and you will never see a game over screen.  In fact, I am confident in saying there is no game over screen.There is no reason to learn how the autopsy works because not only does the game tell you what to do the whole way, it won't allow you to do anything else other than what it says.  To say it bluntly, the game starts with the tutorial and the tutorial never ends till the credits roll.My final complaint, is the story.  It needed more time to cook.  It feels like the second, maybe third draft of the story.  Lots of red herrings, lots of spooky stuff added for no other reason than "spooky", some conflicting information, and an ending that is not an actual resolution.  There are also a lot of moments of weird stuff that I could not tell was done on purpose of if they are bugs.  My guess would be bugs but they left them in because no one else could tell the difference either.My impression is that the writer(s) did not fully know what the theme is.  Theme, in story writing, reveals itself through the interaction of character arcs and the plot.  This is why multiple drafts are important, so you can dial that in better.  Jack has no character arc, he is just "sad medical examiner" the whole time.  Mr. Ridley has no character arc and Steven, Jack's friend/wife's brother, has no character arc.  I am harping on this in detail cause the game leans heavily into it's story and this is why it fails to engage and why a lot of people are calling it a "yapping simulator".By far the most compelling part of the game is the actual autopsies.  Each one is different, with a fleshed out backstory and the process of examining bodies, as guided as it is, is cool and really feels like you are trying to solve a mystery.  It does a wonderful job of putting you into the Medical Examiner mindset and very quickly you stop seeing them as corpses and seeing them as a collection of potential clues for solving the mystery of how they died.  A lot of care and planning went into this part of the game and it shows.Over all I don't recommend this game simply because the list of negative stuff is a hair longer than the positive.  Technically it ran fine, didn't encounter any game breaking bugs, but the half cooked story and the lack of player agency really did it in.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave myself some time. I gave myself some time to actually compose myself... compile my thoughts... and bounce around in conversations with other "like-minded" gamers/content creators such as myself. The verdict however... remains the same. This game is boring. It literally has the right word in the title... "simulator". Because that's exactly what it feels like you're clicking through here. Everything... every mouse click... every movement... is preplanned by the protagonist. Like there isn't any "openness" to this game at all. The autopsy's that you perform... are all scripted... and the parts that you get to participate in feel like some upgraded digital game of "Operation" the board game. Not to mention you can't even take a liking to the main character here... because all he does is complain the entire time. He literally talks down about every single cadaver that arrives before him. His addictions... are on the lowest part of the totem pole as far as "reasons you won't like him" go. Then the end... or what they "called" an ending. It just cuts off. No finality whatsoever. I won't go into any details about how it ends... because I'd never want to ruin a game for someone else. However... the way it ends is likely going to garner the same reaction for you as it did for me... pure anger. I was so pissed when it just ended... with nothing. It was like "revelations... then retreat" is how they played it. Like maybe they lost ideas... felt crunched for time since the game had been delayed time and time again... and just said "that'll do". This is far from the game that was shown so many years ago... the "horror" aspect is missing entirely from this game. The only thing "in game" that scared me was a coffin falling in the basement... and that only scared me because the game had almost basically lulled me to sleep and the sudden loud noise startled me back. I would've swallowed another "year" delay... rather than have to swallow the $25 I spent on this lackluster unfinished game. We now refer to this game as "Autopsy S**tulator"... which to me and my community is a much more fitting title. Had this game never listed itself as a "horror" game... it wouldn't have garnered so much hate and negativity. Because as it stands as a "thriller" game... the only thing it's missing is an absolute ending. But as a horror game... it's missing SO MUCH more. So three of the games I've been patiently waiting on... "Stray Souls", "Pine Harbor", and "Autopsy Simulator" have been absolute busts in the horror genre. Much cheaper games from other devs have done much much more for the horror genre than all three of these games combined. You want a good suggestion that'll cost you $15 less?? Go pick up "Baisu"... I had an absolute blast with that game... and it did something in a game that I'd never experienced before (and it truly startled me). As for this game it was the worst experience out of the three that I had been waiting for. I am almost to the point now where I'm going in with not so optimistic expectations with the other games that I've had on my wishlist for a while now. Honest take... if I were you I'd save the money on this game and buy so many other games that you'll actually enjoy (because it's Steam and $25 can get you a couple different games). But if you insist on playing it... DO NOT expect anything even close to the caliber of "Mortuary Assistant" here. MA STILL reigns as king of the cadaver horror business.

It's like you perform autopsy with 5 bodies and you get to ending. It's supposed to be way longer, make the story for rich and add more details to the story.The endings are, I'd say, half-baked. Not show us any answer, aside of those that we could've guess ourselves. At the end, we got only a fraction of the revelation which are unfulfilled and disappointingThe horror jumpscares are more annoying than adding the flavor or relevance to the story, as if it's there because of it's horror game, with less to no connection with the story and being there just to scare you.Voice lines, however, is awesome. I tell you how MC feels and enhance psychological aspect of the game.-------------------------------------Autopsy:+ I'd say that it's not bad, but I expect more detailed action, more degree of freedom of dissection, and of course, the autopsy only mode -- which the latter is now under development.------------------------------My wish,I hope that the game could add the court system where our autopsy report could be used in the case, or anything that actually solve the mystery. _childDocuments_.review: So i went through the story (havent unlocked all endings or achievements yet)I would like to preface: PLEASE DO YOUR RESEARCH BEFORE BUYING A GAME!The tremendous amount of people complaining this is not a simulator per se, even tho apart from the name it never claimed to be is hilarious and terrifying at the same time.That being out of the way. its a nice little game that puts you in the role of a mentally unstable person working on autopsies. You play through pre-scripted Autopsies and the story of the protagonist unravels more and more with every chapter.- Nice Graphics- Detailed Bodies and Organs- Thorough Explanation of alot of medical stuff- This is maybe personal: I didnt encounter any Bugs in my Playthrough. Not even a visual glitch or anything small of that sort. - The Game is very linear without giving you much options to think outside the box. This obviously isnt for everyone.- There is no way to do something inherently wrong. You get walked through everything. Again this is not everyones cup of tea so be aware that you get hold by the hand through basically the entire game.- its a very short game. Depending on how you play, you will get through the story in about 4-6 hours probably.- There is ONLY the Story Mode right now. A Sandbox Mode is being worked on.- The Jumpscares and Scary Moments are... okay at best. Im happy i didnt get my Ears Blown out by what we normally get for Jumpscares in other Games, i just wish there was more creative and well placed scare moments.- While i do like the Voice Acting itself (the voice of the protagonist), im sorry devs but the script is really bad. Its overexaggerating for what it is supposed to portrait which gets to a point where its either hilarious or just plain annoying to listen to. (The tremendous amounts of sighing could potentially be a Meme at this point)- The story had a strong start but it kinda fell flat and uninteresting the more you progress. With a Story driven game like this i expected a bit more polish. It gave me the feeling of someone having a really good idea about a story, and then just tried to exaggerate it more and more over the course of progress.- Even though the Game holds your hand throughout the whole game, there have been 2 parts where i was just plain stuck for 30 minutes because i just couldnt figure out how to do these 2 things. I only finished them by randomly doing stuff till it somehow worked. And yeah i listened to what im supposed to do, but that didnt really help ^^All in all i enjoyed the experience still to an degree where i think a thumbs up is agreeable because i knew what i was buying into as i informed myself. There is definitly stuff that could have been better. Im kind of excited what the Sandbox Mode will bring to the table and will update the Review accordingly.

Also some of the notes have minor mistakes, like confusing left and right.Aside from the autopsies, you follow the story of the Pathologist, who has psychological issues, and who's wife passed away recently.The whole game is voice acted, and the pc is commenting on everything relating to both the autopsies and the story.The sighs can get a bit much at times, and even if he's hallucinating and having a panic attack, he's back to normal 2 seconds later.Overall I enjoy the game, though I feel the horror aspect and side story is unnecessary. _childDocuments_.review: Some spoilers if you haven't played already. Or if you don't wanna you can just go ahead and read this <3I knew going into this that it was going to be story driven despite others not doing so. Granted, the name of the game is misleading.. I've only gotten one ending so if I missed something vital that I complained about here, lemme know. There's a few things I want to go over and i'm going to be brutally honest.I played this game with a friend watching. We were very invested in Jack's story (although I know it's not for everyone). We felt bad for him MOST of the time. Other times we were very confused by his behaviour. Sometimes he'd just do the most absurd things in reaction to events going on around him, leaving us awkward and confused. We also found him to be really empty minded most of the time, him taking forever to deduce things we found clear as day.There were a lot of times I was really confused by the atmosphere because there were a lot of plot holes in the actual environments themselves. Tables fixed, windows fixed, things that should have been missing were back where they were before. It threw me off. Jack having to go home during an autopsy and says he'd come back later, only to never come back and the body being gone the next day?? Not to mention some other autopsies that didn't feel complete at all. The burn victim?? Like despite all the clear evidence that the victim couldn't have bound himself like that, it was still deemed an accident?? like how? There was also a letter that was mentioned by Ridley that I never managed to find on Jack's desk. Where it went? Got no clue but apparently it wasn't important. There was also a lot of things I did that I thought would change the outcome of the end: Closing windows and doors constantly, not taking the pills unless I absolutely had to, checking every intractable. I don't think that changed the outcome.There was a lot of audio and visual bugs, things floating, locker noises repeating when nothing was there, doors randomly closing in front of me. I'm sure that all can be patched up, just mentioning it anyways.Last thing was the ending. It was hella abrupt and confusing. Whether Jack actually killed his wife or not- I had no idea. Ridley got shot and it stopped at that, leaving me super unimpressed. No explanation, nothing more. Me and my friend were super bummed out.All in all, not all that impressed with the game. Between the voice acting, the confusing story and the lack of freedom with the autopsies. It wasn't really worth the 40 bucks canadian I had to pay for it. Maybe a 20 dollar game at best.
