_childDocuments_.review: How to beat this game:1. Get as much Power and Endurance as you can.2. Use the Fire Chain as your main weapon until you come across the Claw that gives you Blade Storm skill.3. When you get THAT claw, get as much armor as you can in your Modules and clothes.4. Blade Storm your way to ending.Honestly, I thought this game would be like Elden Ring where you need to kinda read the enemy's moveset in order to land a hit. _childDocuments_.review: No, no, no. Do not buy this game in it's current state.I played through the game once right after release (30 hours), actually wanted to give a negative review, but waited for the first patch to be fair. Unfortunately, the first patch does not change the main problems of the game.Gameplay:The player should be given a sense of freedom through jumping, climbing, air dashing and the grapling hook. However, this feeling is very much affected by limitations of the level design. There are fences for example, over which you can actually jump, but this is prevented by invisible walls.Towards the end of the game you realize that there was no time left for development. This is also made clear by the "subsequently added" New Game + mode, which at least appeared on the announced date.Performance:Without understating, I have never played a game with such poor performance. The game is simply unoptimized. With DLLS disabled and all graphics settings set to "low", the game runs at under 40 FPS (5k ulrawide monitor, resolution set to 3440x1440@60hz).The only way to get stable 60 FPS, with DLLS enabled on automatic. The first patch unfortunately doesn't fix any performance problems, but at least there is a justification on the part of the developers, in the form of a FAQ. Even when the game runs stable 60 FPS, it feels not fluent and the character movement feels melancholic.Price:The price is way too high for an "AA" game (is it an AA game?). However, if the performance was bearable, the price would be OK.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a soul-like game with great art and concept.I personally like this concept of "french renaissance meets androids" concept. I only find it sad that it's not an actual open world and there is a lack of local map.Gameplay wise, the character movements feel a bit too wide and stiff, but it plays pretty ok most of the time. The variety of weapons and associated attack patterns lets you find a game style that suits you, though I find Elden Ring to be more varied in that regard.The story is ok, though not overly complex and is worth collecting the lore elements and side-quests.The difficulty is high as expected of a souls-type game, but is not as crazy as some other titles of this category.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this game a 4/10. gameplay is very chunky and there is like 5-6 different enemies in the game. So combat gets extreme repetitive. Also the game was very easy, so for me it was just dull button mashing. Didnt die to any of the main bosses. So claws with buff, or claws with shield or claws with counter etc etc. Also there are some brights ideas with elemental dmg, but it doesnt get utilized in the game. The story is decent, but again the gameplay kinda ruins it for you, so much running back and fourth and re-re-re-exploring areas after the questgiver has said "ok, now you can get the item for me". takes 5 mins to run there and 30 secs to solve and 5 mins of running back. Ok ideas for a soulslike but imo poorly executed for 50 moneys. At the current state the game feels like an indie and should only be worth about 25 moneys.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with a really interesting setting and a wonderful art design---{ Graphics }---Graphics are beautiful. Sometimes they could have used a little bit more variety, but all in all I really loved the atmosphere.---{ Gameplay }---It is a souls-like (kinda on the easier side). It is not perfect by all means (some difficulty spikes, especially if you go straight for the main quest, and some mechanics feel a little bit overpowered), but it is not at all disappointing. There is a good variety of weapons and armours available and you can build your character with the combat style you prefer.---{ Audio }---Nothing to complain about. Good voice acting, good sound effects and beautiful atmospheric soundtrack.---{ Audience }---It is for everyone, except kids and really sensitive persons. Keep in mind that there is a lot of violence depicted.---{ PC Requirements }---You need to have a decent computer to run it properly. I played it on a laptop with i7 11th gen processor and RTX 3070 and it was smooth sailing with very high settings.---{ Difficulty }---As I said it is a souls-like, even though a little bit easier. I am not really good at them so I found some difficulty spikes here and there but if you do all the side quests and level up properly it is manageable and enjoyable.---{ Grind }---You do not need to grind, but I would really recommend to complete all the side quests because they make your life easier, by discovering more powerful weapons and items.---{ Story }---I am biased because I love the French Revolution period, but I found the story to be enjoyable. Aegis, the main character, is a surprisingly lovely heroine, and she will be accompanied by some real historical figures like Robespierre and Queen Marie Antoinette. The ending is influenced to a degree by some choices you make during the main and the side quests, so again I strongly recommend doing them all. Besides, some of them are quite good and make you know better the different characters.---{ Game Time }---I think it is not too long and not too short. About 20 hours only for the main story line, 30 to 40 hours if you want to explore everything.---{ Price }---I have taken it with a 50% discount (€ 24.99) and I could not recommend enough for that price. For the full price maybe if you are really a fan of this kind of game.---{ Bugs }---I have encountered only a few really forgettable bugs.---{ 8 / 10 }---In conclusion I really enjoyed Steelrising and I would give a solid 8/10: good story, really good atmosphere/graphics/sound design, nice gameplay, very few bugs. Do keep in mind that if you do not like souls-like games you could subtract at least 1 point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a neutral review. There is an enjoyable game underneath the jank, but there's so much jank. SR is one of the worse optimised games I've ever played and definitely has the worse texture pop. It fundamentally fails as a soulslike because it's too janky to be precise with.The best way to play the game is to turn off the souslike aspects in the options and play it as an action game. The mechanics don't add anything to the game except artificially inflate its runtime. Spiders would have done better to spend more time playtesting it instead.That said, the design of aegis and the weapons have a gorgeous aesthetic, and hitting things with the flame chain is a fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: The girl-next-door of souls-likes.Pros:1. the game is fun! The enemies are fun, the levels are fun to explore and the loot is also really good.2. the art is awesome, as usual for Spiders. The costumes, the environments, the enemies. I especially liked how they created jerky movements for clockwork automatons. I thought it was a neat little detail.3. music is also nice. Especially the main theme.4. I liked the weapon design and variety5. the bosses were not too difficult and not too easy. Ok, a little easy maybe, but very fun nonetheless! :)Cons:1. some minor bugs with textures. 2. reaching some places required trick jumps and this game is not made for trick jumps :)Overall, I enjoyed the game very much. I had fun, which is important, and the game did not overstay its welcome. The combat is easy to understand and I enjoyed it. There`s also a story, but since I am not overly familiar with the French revolution, I did not understand much. Last time I had anything to do with the history of France was at school about 20 years ago, so some names are familiar, but not enough to evaluate what the difference between the game and reality is. I did ALL the side quests and a lot of the stories were delivered via text notes (come on, this design element is way overused and needs to go), which I did not read. Anyway, I liked the enemy design, I thought it had artistic flair to it with the musical automatons among your standard knights, infantry, and dogs. I did not use alchemy much because you need bottles and of course if there`s a finite resource - I will hoard ALL of it. But I was ok with the physical weapons.EDIT: I noticed a lot of reviewers mention that it required advanced HW. That is true - I usually play on my MSI GP Leopard laptop (GF RTX 3060 laptop GPU) and I had to use the LOW quality settings. I moved to the desktop I have, which has GF RTX 3080Ti. So yeah, the game is not well optimised.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you meet the following requirements:-You have already bought and played all the mainline FromSoft Souls games. If not buy those.-You have already played, soulslike B titles like The Surge, Lords of the Fallen, Remnant and the upcoming Lies of P-You enjoyed those games and were not too bothered by the B quality-You have jank tolerance and can handle lack of polish and a smaller scale gameplay depth than real souls games-You have spare cash and want to play a new soulslike game-You can handle last gen graphics unless you have a top tier pc with 15+ GB of VRAM to put the textures above mediumIf all those requirements are met, you can get a pretty enjoyable 10-20 hours out of the game.On one hand I want to recommend the game even at it's full pricepoint because the foundation is solid and the gameplay is great. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, where do I begin. Let's start with the cons. Platforming and traversal around debris strewn on the maps can be hit or miss at times. A little more polish and this could have been fixed but overall, it does not take away from the rest of the game. The difficulty is definitely on the easier side for a Souls-like which is more subjective than a major con. Tutorial pop ups occur at the most inconvenient times. This could have been implemented a bit better. Some of the stats aren't explained very well.Now, onto the good. Literally everything else is amazing. The graphics, the maps, the art, the combat and the music, but MOST OF ALL the storytelling and voice acting! This has to be one of the most well written stories I've come across in any game I've ever played, PERIOD! This makes it stand out 10 times more in the Souls-like genre. The reuse of the maps to complete various side stories is top notch and well executed. Very interesting lore! I love that this story was told via in game events, cutscenes, conversations and text. This is how it should be! Also the weapon variety is amazing. I enjoyed every minute of Steelrising and I HIGHLY recommend it! This game is nothing short of a masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played 45 extra hours, until I've finished the game and the DLC. First the good things: the robots designs, the Paris recreation is really really awesome, for me the best feature of all. There are some "copy and paste" stuff (same designs used over and over through the game) but is ok.  The fighting is also great, Aegis is easy to maneuver, every enemy has its unique power and weak point, and you'll have to learn to fight each one. Aegis' arsenal is massive, lots of impressive weapons. The history is also very good, several characters and I really like the dystopian France idea with robots in 1789.  The music of the entire game is fascinating, so well composed for the era and location.Regarding the things I did not like: during the fights there are moments when the camera falls behind trees, bushes, leaves, walls, and block your vision. This should be corrected: the objects should go invisible during these times, to avoid vision block.The mission "selection" could be better. Another annoying thing: is incredible the amount of tiny places where Aegis gets jammed. Just a small step or ledge and the character gets trapped there and cannot move forward. Regarding the graphics, they are good, but the requirements are too high. The system optimization is bad and the high loading times for textures should be corrected. The graphics are not that impressive in these days, even the faces of characters in the dialogues are graphically really poor. I think that the game is amusing, almost 2 months playing it but  it was launched too soon. There were still things and details to solve before launch. Still too green.There are tons of bad reviews claiming for an update for this game, and the developers just launched a FAQ.  Sorry, but until you don't came out with a patch, I cannot recommend. I can recommend it only to the one that want to play a Dark Soul's type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Having just now finished it, I can say it's an incredible game that excites with wicked combat, absorbs you in its dark atmosphere and carries you through an amazing story that builds up to one emotional climax. Bon travail Spiders! Definitely a game well done!To go into more details: Staring with the game as a whole. It really is done well. It has certain Greedfall qualities - so many of the same voice actors, it was lovely to hear! They did an outstanding performance again. The story is basically the French Revolution - I know, surprise, surprise. They tossed in decent variety of automates. So the range of enemies is not bad. It did have moments were it began to feel very grindy, I won't lie. I had times where I was left sighing over the countless assaults. (And getting lost, a LOT, I can't remember quite where... Louxembourg? Or La Cite? But uff.. a few streets just look a tad too much alike) BUT, it certainly keeps you engaged, albeit a bit monotonous at times. That said, I did play with Assist Mode, perhaps I could have tried turning that off at some point. However, I'll always be a firm believer that games should be challenging AND fun, not just the former. So, they certainly gave you a good option to gauge how you like to play. Back to automates, Aegis is the outstanding one, of course. While I wondered at some point in the story, what really sets her apart, her character develops nicely and naturally. I don't wanna spoil anything here but I promise, if you feel a bit stuck, perhaps even a bit tired of it - hang in there. It gets better. The story picks up and the ending was phenomenal! I also did all the side-quests which I found to be quite well fleshed out. They played into the main plot and even affect the ending. So, whoever finishes this game in supposedly 15 hours.. I have no clue how, nor why anyone would want to rush through a game in the first place. Do all the side-quests, engross yourself in the experience and Steelrising will definitely leave you satisfied at the end of it. As for bugs - I had no framerate problems whatsoever. Not in the Beta and not now. A few hiccups. Like the E button prompt would sometimes disappear. Along with the enemy health bars. I had one instance where the voices cut out during a cutscene, too. Luckily I had the subtitles on.Other than that, nothing major.From atmosphere to the soundtrack, the combat and the story I would give it a strong 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice soulslike that wears its inspiration like bow for all to see.The movement takes a bit to get used to, but it fits seeing as it's a robot you controlReally well designed levels with shortcuts and details, and the Bloodborne inspiration easy to see, especially how you interact with the NPCs through the windows and such.An interesting plot that keeps you engaged.Lots of interesting weapons. However, those weapons also becomes the focal point of one of the weirdest design decisions I have experienced in a long time. So many weapons to try, but no respeccs. So I ended up equipping weapons, trying them out, thinking: this seems cool, too bad there's no point since my stats won't work with it. Then putting it away again.I cannot fathom how they landed on giving us no respecs with that array of weapons available, just mindbogling.But I do hope the team takes their experience and creates a sequel, or something in the same genre. There's a lot of brilliant ideas here, but a lot of polish would be needed and experience to make this a stellar experience to play.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s obvious what  was going for, and while it succeeds in some aspects it ultimately is a Neoclassic-style victim of its own ambition.You take the role of a clockwork girl in service of the queen of France as she’s set to stop the madness of the king who seeks to raise a metal army to crush all who oppose him.You’ll meet various historical figures who will help you to achieve this plot to overthrow the monarchy in this alternate history setting.Equip your weapons, attacking and dodging your way to victory, it’s a very simple formula but one that works well thanks in no small part to the smooth controls, making dodges feel snappy and precise while other upgrades let you personalize your experience further.Levels themselves are a simple go from point A to point B while having some little side paths you can take to explore a bit and looping on themselves so you can open shortcuts near savespots.Another thing it features is traversal upgrades to make warded off areas explorable, so you’ll run in the various locales multiple times with different paths depending how far you’re into the story.Relatively to the game it tries to mimic it lacks depth, polish, aesthetics, and a characteristic sense of style many smash hits seem to have.Here’s some major complaints:Now this wouldn’t be a problem unless we consider what this game is priced at 50$, landing it in the same ballpark as the best of the best in its genre while being not only inferior but clearly a copy to them.I still had my fun and the game still does something interesting with its mechanics, hence why I recommend it, however is absolutely not worth the admission price, wait for a VERY generous discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is incredibly clunky.- If you don't mash the attack button your combo starts over, so everything feels choppy.- You need to hit the dodge button at least three times before you'll actually dodge, and even then the enemy attacks track you and hit you during the dodge.- Every enemy has high poise, so every fight becomes "attack, attack, dodge, wait for your incredibly slow stamina to come back, attack, get hit, attack."It feels like an incredibly cheap knockoff with a cool setting. Play Lies of P instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising was at first a positive surprise to me, despite me disliking Souls likes and combat centric games. It's because it's pretty easy in every way. At least the first parts. But since combat is everything in this game, it gets repetitive and boring in the long run. In fact, there's too much of the boring and annoying stuff. The genre is apparently not for me.Combat... Yeah, it's the same over and over and you have to either spend lots of time to avoid taking damage, or play it like I tried to do - agressively, with lots of power to finish the enemies off as fast as possible. But my build was obviously not good enough from the boss in the mines and onwards. At that point I had no patience left and was fed up with the same challenge in repeat. So I started up WeMod. God bless one hit kills. Because grinding isn't fun. Neither is "gitting gud".Then there are close to impossible jumps... Trying to reach that ledge that you have to reach to get to your objective? Well, try and try again, only to fall down and take damage or die, because it's too far. Finally succeed by glitching onto an invisible ledge just below the one you wanted to reach, and jump up. Annoying.It was one jump in particular that I just couldn't make that made me turn to Youtube. It turns out I was expected to use one of the special attacks to make the jump - one of those attacks to you believed only works when you have a lock on an enemy. Jeez.Navigating the city... OMG. There are walls, blockades and fences everywhere. Going from one side of a building to the other can require a detour around the whole city. You can spend a good amount of time only to figure out how to reach the objective marker. Annoying.However, I enjoy the story and love the atmosphere and the music. It's an amazing game in that regard. But the gameplay... No thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the gameplay and aesthetic, enough to recommend to anyone who enjoys action RPGs, however if you're here for the story, characters, or history you'll likely be disappointed. The story is fine as a premise, but the way it is told is incredibly stilted and shoddy. I couldn't play the developer's other game Greedfall due to the poor lip sync, and while this game is just good enough the animations overall are quite lacking, both in cutscenes and combat. The main twist of the game is incredibly obvious, the main characters are largely unlikable people you are meant to care about helping as well as all looking very similar. As for the history it is less an exploration of the period and events and more like wax dolls of historical figures quoting textbooks about the French Revolution at each other. The combat is generally fun though it is hampered by a lack of clean animations on some enemies, most enemies taking a bit too long to kill, and performance issues that crop up every once in awhile. TL;DR Gameplay is pretty good but the story and historical elements are poorly done.

_childDocuments_.review: It has an interesting take on the soulslike genre. The combat is a bit slower paced, but has a rhythm to it that fits very well with the aesthetic and theme of being clockwork machines. It does some things I don't like (no i-frames on dodge) but does a number of things I DO like (don't mind the haters, heavy weapons are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SATISFYING to land, I've not seen many soulslikes that actually give heavy weapons the feeling of ACTUALLY slapping someone in the face with a fat penis. If you can't get HRT, just play Steelrising with a halberd on max strength. It's the same feeling. If your erection lasts for longer than 4 hours, call a doctor).There is a surprising viable build diversity as well. My personal build was a str-based heavy weapons build that was very fun, while the 'meta' is a medium weapon agility build based on stance breaking and ripostes. Status ailments aren't broken, but are effective enough that an elemental build is just as (if not more, in some cases) viable. Though, a part of this is also a function of the game's difficulty - it's a bit on the easy side. So easy that there is an achievement for not using heal flasks, and it's surprisingly attainable even for mid-range players.The story is actually pretty solid as well.  There is something to be said about how the sidequests softlock you out of one of the endings if you do them, which I found a bit annoying. Without spoilering too much, I really enjoyed how Aegis starts off as a blank-slate droid and develops into a distinct personality complete with her own political opinions by the end, and I at least think it had a very satisfying payoff.At casual pacing, expect a good 30-40 hours, depending on how much side content you do, with an easy 10ish hours extra if you go completionist with it. The worst string of collectibles to find runs about 18 pieces, and they aren't just random ticks on a counter, they are all actual intractable pieces of the game with little pieces of worldbuilding that can actually make them somewhat worthwhile if you really get into the setting.The art design is amazing all throughout, though the level design doesn't quite touch the level where you can avoid getting lost without a map. It's not bad-bad, but there are a couple of points in the game where you'll feel it (especially if you're going completionist with it).There are a couple of minor threads that are a bit annoyingly lose (like too small to be an actual plot hole, but big enough to ask 'what happened with that'), but the narrative wraps up nicely with a definitive conclusion that would make a narrative sequel a bit hard to pull off. There is a sense that there is more meat to this game than it's story allows you to really chew on. I hope to see the devs do more with this framework in the future.Overall, the price point is solid for what you're getting (I'd say it's worth it without waiting for a sale - but the DLC, definitely wait on, it is nowhere near enough content for full price there).

_childDocuments_.review: i'm on a 5800X3d and 6950XT 16gb with 32gb Ripjaw pc4000 and have the game installed on my SK Hynix P41 m2 ssd. In 1440p max settings, I get 55-60fps. That's absolutely terrible, considering this game doesn't look any better than Thymesia. The character models certainly don't, they're reminiscent of Xbox 360 or PS3 character models. If you notice the screenshots they chose for their Steam store page, you'll notice most of them are filled with bricks/gravel/rocky surfaces or surfaces with baroque looking artwork. That's because they can pump up the tesselation and ambient occlusion which give these specific types of polygons softshadows and other fidelity enhancements, and at a low resolution it does an excellent job of tricking your eye into thinking everything on screen is of equivalent quality. They just slapped a lot of bloom all over everything like they did in Greedfall.I don't mean to sound like a complete hater, but the negative reviews are absolutely correct. Spiders really screwed the pooch and jumped the shark with optimization here, it's absolutely ridiculous. My machine should only be getting framerates like this @ 2160p with Ultra quality and extensive raytracing enabled, ie. Cyberpunk 2077.It's too bad the framerates and 1% averages are so awful. After you've gotten acclimated to 120fps/240fps+ gaming for an extended period of time, anything below ~85fps starts to look really choppy and can even feel unplayable if it dips further. It's amazing how much a good machine spoils you.As is usual with Spiders titles, however, the setting is immersive and absolutely fantastic. I love Greedfall on my Series S, the Rennaisance-era/Early Spanish fusion for the aesthetic is unique and gorgeous despite the mediocre player models. Steelrising is the same exact way, this French Revolutionary era aesthetic is uniquely beautiful as well and despite some (once again) mediocre player models, still manages to create a distinctly original setpiece for the game's environment and backdrop. Spiders really does know how to create realistically immersive locales and ingame worlds, it's easily their strong suit next to combat mechanics.After playing Thymesia, Combat in Steelrising just feels kinda -meh-, like an average Soulslike game if you will. The atrocious stamina limitation is the main culprit here, you can barely string together a combo and a dodge before your character starts to overheat. If you can spam alchemical effect resistance potions to prevent getting frozen from instantly recharging your stamina bar (pressing E during overheating), than it doesn't feel that bad. But that of course isn't really feasible, especially early game, since they're rare. This jilted level of early game stamina leads to some really boring encounters, like the unstable automaton in the early garden level. Talk about a snore fest.I can't recommend Steelrising until they fix the game's performance. The quality of the game does not warrant the 9 gigabytes of used VRAM when you consider how poorly it performs. RDR2 on Ultra everything uses 2-3 less gigabytes of VRAM and looks much better than Steelrising. And I average 120+ fps in 1440p in RDR2 with everything maxed out and raytraced.PS. In fact you can tell for sure optimization is broken, because using 1080p->1440p FSR/enhanced scaling gives identical performance as just playing in 1440p direct scale regardless of the profile you've selected (ie. ultra/quality,balanced,performance,etc). Spiders needs to address and fix this issue immediately.. the longevity of this game is going to be a literal blink of an eye if they don't, I almost gauarantee you.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10If you're looking for a game that is a Souls-like, and takes a chance, Steel Rising works. There are pros and cons, but overall, I enjoyed it. Taking place during the French Revolution, you play Aegis, an Automaton loyal to the Queen, Marie-Antoinette. You embark on a mission to uncover the truth behind the automaton invasion, and how to stop it. At one point in the story I felt the pace ground to a halt, with the Black Frenchman, Julien. I personally didn't care if there was a black man in Paris, during the Revolution, who hailed from the Colonies abroad, but the lecture about slavery being bad wasn't necessary. We all know it's bad. It kinda tainted the story for a bit, and bothered me way more than it should, as I felt the writers were trying to justify Julien being there. The lecture about slavery came off as a virtue signal to me, and left me rolling my eyes, wondering if I were going to see a BLM Banner somewhere in the game. It's a Steampunk fantasy about the French Revolution, so anything goes. As for the rest of the story, it needed A LOT of focus. While I get wanting to write a complex story within this setting, sometimes just focusing on one or two elements is all that is needed. Too many different names to remember and what they were doing bogged the story down.I went with a very powerful Alchemy/Engineering/Power Build, with the Fire Bayonet and the Fire and Ice weapon, and with that combo the damage was insane, as are many other builds. But add in the Ordinary vials that dropped like crazy and you really didn't need to use the Burette. Modules made the combat and boss fights too easy. Level 3 Fortifying Counter essentially healed you for quite a bit when you successfully used a Counter. I LOVED the visuals of this game. The city of Paris was burning, smoldering, destroyed. It was fun to find different areas and explore them. I can't remember the name of the coat I had for Aegis, but I stopped and took a look at the embroidery on it and was really impressed by the level of detail there. Automats were really lovely as well. However there were some performance issues, and I have a pretty good rig(i7 10th gen, 2070 RTX Super), and the FPS sometimes dropped significantly for no reason. As I said above, if you're looking to scratch that Souls-like itch, STEELRISING is a decent game. I'd love to give it higher marks, but the cons and the story and game pace got in the way. I got my money's worth out of it(I saw that some folks beat it in 8 hours. Guess they just needed to speed run it), and even purchased a copy for a friend to enjoy. Pros:*Visually gorgeous.*Combat can be fun(but there are some caveats to that)*Character models are really interesting*Movement is nice, most of the time.*Spiders and Nacon are taking big chances with their games, offering something new and unique.*Aegis, and the Automats were beautifully designed.*If you like Sekiro you'll like this and how Aegis moves*Interesting fantastical take on the French Revolution, and those involved.*Weapons were fun to play with, but once you get into a rhythm with what you liked, the others weren't necessary.*Really awesome outfits for Aegis. Spiders and Nacon knew that Fashion is a priority with alot of folks.Cons:*Unstable performance issues*Combat can be easy(get enough "Echoes" and you can buy grenades, and just throw them at your enemies from a distance. Boss fights are too easy).*Assist Mode. Wasn't necessary. *Too many tools for you to use for survivability(the grenades and immobilizations should have been EXTREMELY RARE, not easily purchasable at the Boutique)

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is one of the most difficult games to review. On a scale from super frustrating to maximum fun, this game hits every single note.My initial impression was not great. I jumped into the game expecting another Spiders RPG and seemingly only got a linear combat simulator. Not being experienced in Souls-like games it took me an hour to familiarize myself with the controls and concept. Also the first map is probably the weakest graphically. After I finished the map and wanted to travel to Paris, the game crashed and reloading didn't help. After an hour of research and fix I was finally able to continue the story. This kind of crash still happened randomly later in the game, which unfortunately still has a lot of bugs.The first half of the game is pretty much just combat after combat. The gameplay is very simple: you try to reach the next save point and open all the shortcuts, so in case of death you can avoid excess combat. Apart from the enemies, there are no other NPCs on the streets at all, it feels empty and you also don't have a companion this time. Understandable from a story perspective, I just don't like running around in empty spaces with the sole main character. The combat itself is one of the highlights of the game, at least until you've seen and tried everything. There are no ordinary weapons and enemies, everything feels pretty unique and crazy. The design and animation of the automatons are awesome. Huge kudos to the designers, artists and programmers here.Once you start meeting human characters, another aspect of the game opens up. It turns out that there's a decent underlying story. If you skipped history class, and names like Robespierre don't mean anything to you, it might not be such a relevation. I had a lot of fun meeting these historical characters in a wildly fictional setting. The cutscenes (especially the echoes) are a joy to watch. I have to commend the melancholic, orchestral soundtrack that boosts the mood in these scenes. Still, it's not a proper role-playing game, all your skills are for combat, and the story doesn't really branch out (although there are several endings, but only with subtle differences).Unfortunately, after a while the core gameplay becomes tedious, there's a lot of backtracking, even with the shortcuts and fast travel coins. By the end, I wished there was a movie or series based on this alternate setting instead of the game. So is it a bad game then? Not at all. But don't expect it to be a masterpiece either. The story kept me going, but I totally understand those, who dumped it after a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Steel rising is pretty good souls-like game.Right now it has some optimization issuses as it doesn't run great, but luckily I was able to brute force past that with my pc.And first off this is AA game not a AAA game so it has some jank but nothing too awful, think the worst I had was a boss push me though the map at some point so I died.Music is pretty good but a bit quite.The level design is really great with having a lot of shortcuts back to old check points and unlocked upgrades that allow you to open paths you couldn't before.I really enjoyed the story, since the french revolution is a pretty cool point in time, and it can be ignored if you don't care since you get a compass the points to the place you are supposed to go.The npcs was okay, I had the problem that they just kind of blend together most of the time, since they kind of look and dress the same and the French names is not helping me.I wish they would add more explanation on some things, like they never explain what your stats do, so how good is 20+ armour? _childDocuments_.review: A slightly overpriced game with nice gameplay.+/- graphics are ok, certainly not bad, FPS-drops have been amended, textures sometimes pop in after loading and the animations for faces during cutscenes is sometimes non-existant. Also loading times are looong and iam not even talking about loading into the gameplay... the mainmenu has its own loading screen.One funny bug that happened to me was that I fell into the Boss arena by accident and triggered it, luckily you can return afterwards and finish the rest of the level.+ sounddesign is nice and has a fair amount of "clank" for these automats.+ enemy design is varied, with elemental variations and unique behaviours to them, the cherry on top are the titan-bosses! While other bosses exist they are mostly powered up regular enemies which spice things up and stop you from accessing rest-points.+ the best point is the combat but sadly there are barely any weapon varieties, most of them are just reskins with barely any weapons that feels unique which mostly comes from the weapon special ability.But who needs weapons when you can beat the game with grenades... those are very powerful and there are many types (explosive, elemental and ones that open enemies up to crits) and to make it worse there are better versions as well, balance be damned.Frost seems to be a little to powerful as well, freezing enemies solid is just not balanced. They have amended this by making every grenade and ammo harder to get...Grenade damage and effects should be nerved, but scaling should be added. Also carrylimits should be introduced. Perhaps have a grenadebandolier or something as equipment to raise the amount, with drawbacks like worse defense. That way the grenades are not to precious to use and you cant just have all types on you for spamming.Best way to fix the frost in my opinion would be to freeze small enemies and slow bigger ones. The devs could also consider only freezing certain parts of bigger enemies which would cause them to chnge the way they fight! If an enemy hast small limbs > they get frozen, now it will try to crush you with its bodyweight or kick you. People would need to adapt to the new movements!+ nice interconnected, open levels with secrets galore. Some of the areas are little bit repetive but it isnt that bad. Reused assets are barely noticable as the devs have taken care of how they implemented it.- The price is too high for what you are getting. 35 $/€ is fair for this (Bastille Edition). Would pay for DLC if there is new weapons and fresh enviroments!+ the story is set in revolutionary france but with out of control automats going on to slaughter the people of paris. The atmosphere is just right with burning barricades and defensive positions set up, but overrun by automats, corpsepiles everywhere and frightened citizens hiding in their homes. Good work!Minor spoilers for three characters:My only complaints are that I feel King Louis in this portrayal was not fully done justice and some minor things about Julien Raimond, a black plantation owner who is trying to free slaves, the thing is you never see any slaves just find hints about them. _childDocuments_.review: A few opening thoughts before I get to the review :- I've not experienced any performance problems noted in other reviews. However, im running the game on medium with a beefy system (RTX 3070, 64gb ram, and a nice beefy ryzen CPU). I've not bothered putting the game on higher graphics because it doesnt look like it's super worth it.- I have a pretty high tolerance for jank in my games- I have a pretty low tolerance for bad design decisionsOn to the review :Spiders makes a souls-like, and it's .. pretty much on par with what you'd expect from a souls-like made by spiders. If you aren't familiar, spiders is a "double A" development studio that's made some very hit-or-miss games. Its most recent entry was Greedfall which (surprisingly maybe ?) seems placed in a very similar era and style. Where Greedfall promised a "mass-effect"-like experience, this one is hopping on to the "git gud" soulslike train, and just like Greedfall it .. sorta works. Your mileage may vary.The atmosphere, music and visual presentation is honestly on point, it's original and bold enough to actually be compelling. The narrative is alright, servicable if anything, but so far it's nothing to write home about.  Where I think things start to get "spiders"-y is the combat -- it's stiff, really stiff. This is "by design" (depending on whether you believe the studio's explanation to be completely true, half true, or a lie is up to you) and meant to emulate fighting as a big ol' clunky set of gears of and whirring bits and bobs. Some weapons do feel noticably more fluid -- namely the fans and claws -- while some others feel almost unusable because of the animation commitment every single move requires from you -- namely any heavy weapon. Where things get a little out of my comfort zone however is the difficulty in understanding how enemies will react to certain attacks, and how you'll react to theirs. Much like souls-like games you've got some "poise" score that will determine if getting slapped will knock you straight on your robot arse, or if you're just going to trade blows and watch a chunk of your health get nipped out. For the player, this is super consistent and easy to figure out -- for enemies however, that stagger seems to be on an invisible bar (similar to the "posture" bar that medium weapons excel at breaking for a finisher, but not to be confused with it) that rises and falls based on the "impact" score of your weapon. This inconsistency is a little irksome as you need to do some mental math in order to know if its worth pressing the attack or if you need to back away for a second to avoid trading health. It isn't a dealbreaker, but these are the little details that may be dealbreakers for some.The last bit I want to touch on is the element mechanic; You get fire for damage over time, lightning for added damage per hit, or frost for (and wait for it) a complete stun for a few seconds on any enemy (including bosses!). This.. is pretty insanely unbalanced -- stacking frost on any build trivializes a big portion of the game until you find some frost resistant enemies, but then fire will be just as devastating. Your ability to abuse these boils down to whether you want to spend a few extra minutes farming for resources to just stock up on grenades, or little alchemial solutions to use your special abilities. I have a hard time justifying this completely skewed balance. But it's part of the "spiders" charm -- just like guns in Greedfall being absolutely overpowered, its just how it is.Overall, Steelrising is FINE, its competent, it does what it says on the tin -- here's a souls-like game with some cool twists made by a studio that's tiny. If that's your thing, great -- its not a bad romp. But for a double-A game with a triple-A pricetag, you may want to wait for a slight discount if you're on the fence.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising falls into the second category of bad soulslikes. The one that nails the fundamentals, but fails at pretty much everything else. The levels are too large with too much empty room between and around encounters, so there's little reason to engage in them. There seems to be only a single biome in the game, that being the palace and the park combo. So it ends up all looking the same from start to finish. Enemy placement is mindless and random.I'm glad that Spiders finally nailed the combat... after making the same game for over a decade. It really does feel good in Steelrising as do the weapons. But everything else is sadly lacking. Also, why is it called "Steelrising" when the "automats" you fight all seem to be made out of brass? I guess "Brassrising" wouldn't sound as cool.The game also suffers from horrible performance issues being very obviously so poorly optimized. Mind you, on the same machine that I played Plague Tale Requiem on maximum settings in 1440p at noticeably very high frame rates, Steel Rising stutters and lags on even high settings, sometimes dropping to single digit FPS. If you compare the two games, Plague Tale Requiem is just gorgeous, and Steelrising kinda looks like s**t, except for Aegis herself who clearly stands out. If that weren't enough, it also eats VRAM like crazy. On maximum settings it almost entirely took all of it on my machine, which is insane, as it's 16Gb. It also crashes randomly overtaking all of it if you don't leave it enough headroom, which is a problem in and of itself, as the game tells you in the settings that it should be enough, but isn't.Steelrising is not a complete waste of time. Like I said, the gameplay is good in its basics. It feels great to move and to fight. The story is intriguing enough. Sadly, Lies of P it is not. I've played a lot of soulslikes in my day and the only great ones were the already mentioned Lies of P and Salt & Sanctuary. Everything else is just mediocre at best. As is, again unfortunately the case here.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: it's poorly optimized but if you wanna get a taste of soulsgames while being stylish as hell, check this out. _childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game and want to leave some positive feedback though I don't think it'll be for everyone for a couple reasons I'll get to in cons.pros:-setting-the art style-controls. This is being called clunky. I simply do not agree. I think the controls are super tight and it's really easy to translate desire into action.-animation. somehow the animation looks robotic despite tight controls which really helps contribute to the atmosphere. Aegis's animation in particular is really beautiful.-side quests: the side quests actually have a lot of meat and interesting storylines. make sure to keep subtitles on though due to all the french vernacular thrown in.-level design: I do agree with some criticism of it feeling "samey" which can make it hard to navigate. however, I think the labyrinthian genre it resides in doesn't mean that spells doom. Some of the locations that have bigger landmarks to center yourself put it on a level that I think is on par with a certain other series in the same genre.-stamina system. I think the cooldown system that builds frost status is a neat idea that encourages aggression. I especially like having it as a way to add difficulty by having the later game have more enemies that deal frost damage which increases the risk of using the mechanic in a cool way. Bonus points for the animation and sound queues that make it usable without keeping your eyes glued to the stamina bar.-the bosses declared with "titan" are all unique and interesting. Some of them have cool mechanics as well.cons:-Optimization is really rough. I have a gtx 3080 and i7-10700 and am playing on medium 1080p (I will always take smooth 60 over looking impeccable). Honestly though the higher settings don't look that much better. A note on the optmization. the worst area is the second area in the game. It doesn't seem to matter the settings, it just tanks. The second half of the game was far superior. Hopefully that bodes well for a patch to resolve the issues.-this game is really buggy. They are usually small bugs of little consequence but they are annoying. Sometimes alchemy doesn't apply the effect to weapons properly. Easily resolved by changing weapons back and forth. More annoyingly though. Items will randomly be impossible to pick up. You get the item but the "item here" visual effect won't go away which triggers my OCD in uncomfortable ways.-if you want this game to have a good difficulty balance... you will need to artificially handicap yourself. Elemental damage is so insanely overpowered and you are showered with way more grenades, healing, and bullets than you could possibly use. I truly hope they patch the effectiveness of alchemy as well as add a mode that severely dampens the amount of loot you find.-"unstable" bosses don't deserve to be "bosses" and don't deserve a named healthbar. Most souls-likes are guilty of this. I'm kind of okay with finding a boss that is a regular enemy later in the game. but finding a boss that is a clone of enemies I've already felled 100 times is really disappointing. I'd prefer the boss count to simply be lower than to make it seem like there are more bosses.-story is actually fairly entertaining. but it really struggles to find it's footing early on with long cutscenes and conversations that I had a hard time following or having any attachment too. As I sidequested later on and the story hit stride. I did find myself invested and enjoying all the worldbuilding.The game really evokes similar gameplay feel of Bloodborne and it's the first game to do so not hampered by 30 fps with bad frame pacing (even at it's worst, this game is better than bloodborne's performance... though admittedly it probably won't me on most machines). I kind of thought I'd get my bloodborne fix from thymesia but it was much more sekiro (which I was fine with :D ). If you like the art style and setting, have an overpowered rig, and like bloodborne and are looking for a fix... I think it's worth a shot. If you don't hit all 3 of those, wait for some patches and updated impressions over time (or take advantage of Steam's great refund policy)If this isn't it for you... hopefully we all find that 60 fps bloodborne experience when Lies of P comes out sometime :)

_childDocuments_.review: Played on a laptop with a 3070.Overall, this game was fantastic.  The combat is fun, the environments are gorgeous, the clockwork-feel of the enemies is great.  The weapons are varied and the attack animations are unique.  There's an actual narrative story (not just item descriptions like soulsborne games), along with some meaningful choices that do affect the ending.  Sprawling levels of city streets and gardens that weave back and forth like a maze to get to your next objective.  Picking up several tools to allow quicker traversal is great, though I wish there were more grapple points and more ways to get around a lot of the blockades in the city streets.Equip the compass.  Use the compass.  Appreciate the compass.  Because otherwise you will get lost.  The game does suffer from a few hiccups in 'where do I go next?' sort of moments, but can get a little confusing when you're having trouble accessing an area because you need a tool from another area.  It all 'clicked' once those tools were acquired.Invisible walls are sooooooo frustrating.  Particularly when you can clear the actual wall by several feet, but just *bonk* into nothing and fall to your death.  They are omnipresent in the game, but only marginally frustrating in a few places (DLC included).There was some framerate drops in a couple of spots.  The big offenders that I ran into were around the Louvre, and in two of the longer cutscenes (one of which was the ending) the frames dropped to single digits.  I'm assuming there was some sort of front-loading going on, but it was really jarring.The game as a whole is easier than your typical Dark Souls/Nioh sort of difficulty.  Some enemy attacks easily hit just as hard as those games, though, and some enemies are frustratingly effective in that regard.Spiders did a fantastic job capturing the look and feel of revolution-era France and injecting some clockwork-style sci-fi/fantasy into a well-established history with notable figures.  I'm really looking forward to seeing what they work on next!Small Addition:  After starting a new game as a Guardian and going for Power weapons (the 'strength' equivalent) that are slow, I can say that the slow weapon combat isn't as good.  You can block with some of the slower weapons, and it does prevent 100% of damage in exchange for some stamina loss.  You can parry/counter with some weapons as well, but the window is really small.  Both of those are fine.  But enemies can recover from a bounce faster than you can get your block down and attack in some cases, making the ability to counter (and block) kinda pointless.  Charge attacks are so slow it's nearly impossible to build a full-charge before getting hit.  Blocking is directional, which is fine, but doesn't track what you're blocking very well.  As a result, enemies that have attacks that move or turn can result in you blocking the first attack but failing to block the second, or preparing a block that the enemy clips through due to movement and hits you from the side anyway.  I built up stagger WAY more on my claws, and I have yet to actually stagger an enemy, let alone a boss, with a massive hammer, chain, or the big clock of vengeance.  Seriously, not one.  My claws would need anywhere from 6-12 hits to stagger an enemy and leave it open for a critical hit, but nothing on the power weapons. This really soured on me.  I was looking forward to bringing the beat down, particularly when the clock weapon was one of the ones featured in the trailers.After 10-15 attempts of the Unstable Blacksmith boss in the Forge (reference the above issues with blocking and countering and slow weapon combat), I called it good and decided I'm about done with the game.

I can say this is a perfectly fine game.Spiders' games have always struggled with combat and writing, and while the writing here is still not top notch, the combat is much better.I'm hoping Greedfall 2 is the inverse (focusing on writing first) so that these devs can finally start reaching some of their true potential.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not the worst Soulslike I've played, but it doesn't come close to the best. My biggest gripes are how the majority of the cutscenes felt off, the boss fights that weren't difficult at all and desperately needed a second phase, and the combat and animations, which were not as fluid as I would have liked. To be more specific, the facial expressions in the cutscenes were terrible; the eyes appeared hollow and lifeless and the facial expressions were not there, which clashed with the passionate voice acting. The combat felt stiff most of the time—while this could be justified by the fact that we’re playing as a robot, it just made everything feel off. I did find the cooldown system interesting, as it allowed for long strings of offensive attacks. The environments were well done, but they started to feel repetitive around the middle of the game. The number of invisible walls was truly infuriating, leading to numerous deaths and frequent glitches. I encountered about 5-6 bugs, ranging from interesting to annoying, though none were game-breaking.So, do I think the game is bad? No, but I also wouldn't recommend it to my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it feels like a grind you've played before. It's not open world in any way, it's totally linear but feels like it should be open world enough to annoy you. I was hopeful that it would be great because it had so many great particulars to it. Historical Paris, automaton, action heavy. Then there's the boss fights, they're just dumb. They aren't fights, they're methods you strictly follow or you die. Want to jump in and give a few hits while the boss ain't looking? Not a chance you have to wait until they are ready for you to hit them. Only then can you do damage, stupid. In fact, the whole game is like that if you play it on the higher difficulties, you couldn't possibly play it without strict health monitoring, absolute precision timing and exit. I wish I just had the fantasy that it was a cool game but not actually buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: 12 hours in so far and just been to a few districts with 7 (maybe 8?) bosses fought and I'm loving this game, with me being a long-traditional FromSoft gamer since the OG Demon's Souls back in '09-'10 down to Elden Ring...glad I took the dive into my first so-called souls-like game (not counting Darksiders 3), although Steelrising is more akin to Bloodborne than the Souls-Ring games. With all the similarities it shares with the mega FromSoft titles, it does its own thing well in a way that it manages to not feel like a cheap knock-off. Exploration is a bit lacking at first BUT game-world opens up after a couple Titan Bosses...and I've only been to like 3-4 districts/areas. For being a souls-like, this game is a half-step more forgiving and involves rhythmic tactical weapon use and movements in order to one-up the lowest of low enemies to the big boiiis and all the way to the mini and main bosses. Can't wait to finish this game in its entirety and it's worth the money I pad for this. Will update this review as needed.On my equipment with Ryzen 7, 32gigs, 1660Ti/6gigs, the game so far runs at a consistent user-limited 60 fps with occasional drops to 55-56 in transitional world-load areas with one catch: everything graphics-related on lowest slider positions but with 100% resolution scale and POV pulled back at max 1.5. CPU temp averages 75-80degrees during high intensity graphical areas and interactions so meaning it won't turn your rig into a furnace. But hey, even at 1080p with lowest graphics setting used, game still looks gorgeous. Maybe a future update can optimize this game further for lower-spec'd equipment like mine? One can only hope...PS devs: this game didn't need an Assist Mode. Just a bit of farming (with the help of even just the level 1 module to help with farming) and diligent treasure hunting pretty much turns Aegis into a ruthless sexy automaton.

_childDocuments_.review: I am supposed to immediately give this game a negative review right after joining as such a game claims to be "soul-like" but they include difficulty adjustments. This undermines the core appeal of a soul-like experience. Additionally, the game suffers from numerous issues. The enemies are too easy, parrying and dodging their attacks overly simple. The bosses are uninteresting and less challenging than normal mobs. The NPC design is poor, with characters looking almost identical. Furthermore, the game features many weapons. Although those weapons are technically usable, some of them are very difficult to use. For example, some weapon skills have animations that take 2-3 seconds to perform, during which a player could be defeated multiple times. Overall, these flaws detract significantly from the game's quality.However, the only reason I gave a positive review is that the game provides you with a compass. _childDocuments_.review: Yes indeed.. yet another soulslike. You know the drill, enemies that respawn and are harder than the bosses, you loose your souls when dying, healing bottle, shiny's to pick up, barrels to break, savepoints (bonfires) etc.. SO is it any good? oh yeeesss!This is a rather slow-paced soulslike, where you will benefit from taking down one enemy at a time, not rush things and explore everything to the full. (You have no map, but you have a compass that guides you in the direction of your quests.)Its a classic hit and dodge -watch your stamina- souls, but you can go the "parry way" also if thats what you prefere, both works perfectly fine. The game itself feels rather stiff/clunky at first, but you will get used to that fast (If you are familiar with games like lords of the fallen, back to ashes, mortal shell etc you will have no problem) Also I can see its been punished in reviews for having alot of bugs, but personally i didnt encounter a single bug, and i went through the games 3 times to get all endings, and did one of them as a speedrun. The game has a nice variaty of weapons and modules, each weapon has its own special move, and elements attached to them (like lightning, flame, frost etc), the mechanics feels cool, and the various modules makes it possible to create many fun builds. Replay value is good and rewarding. In ng+ you will be able to Ng+ is much like in DS though where you will fly through the enemies, get alot of souls etc..8.5 /10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to leave a thumbs up on this because I think the devs did the best they could being smaller than their competitors (they made Greedfall). This is far from a perfect game, but is unique enough to be enjoyable for souls-like gamers. Story: The story so far has been rather cut and dry, but being a living robot working for the queen against the murderous king Louie is pretty cool. As with all souls-like games, there are areas to explore with bits of dialogue and short movie clips from time to time.  Controls: The controls are a mixed bag. I haven't tried to change the settings since I chose to use a PS5 controller so I'm not sure if you can or not. I'm not sure if it's because I'm used to playing games like Sekiro and Elden Ring that they just don't flow right for me sometimes. I find myself on several occasions pushing the wrong buttons, just to find out I used a "health potion" (not what they're called in game). Sound: The music and atmosphere are pretty well put together. I have thoroughly the few tracks they have to offer. The voice actors are all top notch except for one thing: they don't sound French (you're located in France so this kind of bugs me). Just try not to think about it and you'll be fine!Graphics: For a small studio, I expected the graphics to be...fine. Strangely enough though, the devs decided to make a game that has some pretty high standards for play-ability. I have a 3060 6GB and barely meet the low spec recommendations. They definitely didn't optimize this game very well.Overall Thoughts: Look...I know I busted this games balls on each category, but I think most players who like souls-like games will enjoy this. It's not perfect, but the devs did a decent enough job that it's still worth a play-through. I would recommend getting this game on sale for around 20 to 30 bucks. Thank you for reading my review! I have played for a total of 15 hours and have enjoyed it. It's not perfect, but it'll keep me busy until I can get my hands on Lies of P :).

_childDocuments_.review: Few words from me: as a supporter of soulslike genre and Spiders - studio that has brought us such a underrated games as 'Technomancer' and 'GreedFall' (which I like a lot, obviously) I couldn't resist to get 'SteelRising' day one edition. And I am not dissapointed. 'SteelRising' is a love letter to 'BloodBorne' and I'm ok with that! Maybe mechanics are not so superb as in mentioned game however 'SteelRising' has it own clunky (in good way, at last it's all about automatas) yet rewarding battle system. I dig the atmosphere of filthy streets, damaged chapels, filthy tombs of XVIII-Paris etc Plot is rather engaging with some clever historical references to mentioned period; love the protagonist though! SPIDERS, good job! I'm waiting for DLC! PROS: Great art direction; exceptional 'XVIII-France' setting. Cool, versatile fight mechanics. Great weapon designs. Nice locations. Good OST. CONS: Not-so-good face animations. Re-used (?)assets from previous games. Maybe too easy when you'll get some experience in mechanics. No fast-travel between vestals. Few bugs.PS: Worth of mentioning is great UI design/art style - bravo to graphic designer!

_childDocuments_.review: Let's put it this way. Type "Transmorphers" into Google. That's what this is. It's Transmorphers. It's Snakes on a Train. It's Atlantic Rim. Spiders took Dark Souls - probably Dark Souls 2 - put it in the same rusty blender that they put Mass Effect into to produce Greedfall, and out came alternate history robo-France.I got about 20 minutes in (actual gameplay, because Greedfall taught me to skip cutscenes aggressively) and I just can't. Steelrising is aptly named in that the sound steel makes also perfectly describes how it feels - clunk. Someone seems to have worked really hard to capture the movement of clunky, old timey robots and even doing it on purpose it's still so poor that it seems to have spread like a virus into the gameplay. Combat was stiff and lacked any semblance of smoothness, including and especially how few moves it takes to drain your stamina and get completely locked out of action for an insufferable length of time.Seventy metal thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of aesthetic going for it, but unfortunately gameplay doesn't hold up. First off, the game is poorly optimized; loading screens are like 2 mins long, and you need to go through one to reach the main menu, and another to get into your game, and then you're STILL getting lag as the level buffers in around you. Combat is very awkward and clunky. Combos are not smooth, dodging isn't always consistent, and the character model is constantly getting stuck on terrain and textures. The character menu is also similarly clunky; there's too many options, and not enough explanation  of what most of it does. This game only came out a few months ago, but there's already DLC for it. They should have released some patches for better functionality. If the developers make new patches and upgrades to the game, maybe I'll come back and try it again. As it stands, there's many other games that are better at what Steelrising is trying to do

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun and clearly a work of great passion. The aesthetic is great, as are the weapon designs and movesets, and most of the enemies as well. Level design is a little uninspired in the opening area but gets more intricate as it goes on, and the bosses are pretty fun, although the process of using an enemy as a miniboss and then immediately seeing more of them as normal foes afterwards is a little annoying. I will say the game is a bit rough around the edges. I've only had one crash, but the graphics leave something to be desired, as does some of the animation and tracking feeling more jank than like intentional robotic movements. Also all the the voices are just inaudible for me in cut scenes, which is a shame because the game actually puts effort into telling a story (including having a voiced protagonist) which I think is admirable. Overall, 7.5/10, fun game, but definitely buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 4hrs, refund denied. Here's a summary of what you'll avoid if you don't purchase this game;- 67GB download. absolutely terrible.- Terrible optimisation. My PC is pretty strong, but had to really chug the fans on any graphical setting over low.- Boring enemies. No enemy does anything other than swing, or shoot. - - Enemies never enter hitstun on normal. Thy chew through anything you throw at them - -  All attacks hitboxes tied directly to object animating, meaning the enemies get a 240degreee swing which even your invincible dodge will not let you step out from. - - Stamina does not start recovering until the used portion fully depletes.  You will be constantly waiting to get 1 attack in every 10 seconds or so.- - - Further consequence of this is any buildup (stun, fire, frost, electricity) is inconsequential. you will never get these to trigger unless you chew through your healtth bar- Health refills are few and far between. _childDocuments_.review: Clunky and slow.TL; DR Combat is polarizing, clunky and slow. First boss turned me off the game for being a lazy attempt at a skill check. Wish there was a middle ground for recommending games. This fits that category perfectly. The story is okay, unique but just didn't grab me. From what I could understand with the info dump that was that opening cutscene, was that Paris was under attack. The machines were made to protect(?) the people. They went bad and now we - also a machine - have to stop them because we were told too.The combat is nothing like I expected from the trailers. Extremely slow or extremely fast, those are your options, neither of them work well. The fast combat is fun, a lot of fun, but you get hit. A lot. I used the pre-order fan blades, they were pretty fun to use, and the combos were pretty solid. The one downside to this is lack of healing, along with the sheer amount of stamina it takes to get in close to an enemy leaves you hanging. Another one of the weapons I tried was the pre-order Discus Chain, it's a pretty safe bet. The one massive downside? It's just not fun to use, it's incredibly slow and has some boring combos. The starting weapon I tried was the Halberd, do not pick this one. It's ranged attack is worthless and the nature of the attacks leaves you high and dry just ready to get hit.The boss design is rough. The first boss is supposed to be the test of what the player has learned. This thing was exactly that, and at the same time, a waste of time. What the game had taught me was "go behind the enemy and wack it". So I did just that, and it was a cake walk. I think the other dudes were supposed to be an addition, but they just kind of bumbled around looking lost. The one major thing I dislike about that first boss is all the garbage on the floor. I get the game has a jump button, but you get so much hang time that its practically just saying "I'm open! Now's a good time to kill me!". I should not die to a boss that easy because I got stuck on a giant rock in the center of the arena, or a stack of bodies. After killing this dude and progressing a little further, I called it quits there. The game has one thing going for it, the setting and the main protag's design.

_childDocuments_.review: I have experienced none of the optimization issues others are posting about. Tooled around with the advanced settings, enabled DLSS Balanced, jacked up the settings a bit and turned on raytracing. Framerate is stable, no crashes, and very few if any bugs.The game looks great, and I appreciate the minor innovations on top of the traditional Souls-like formula. The need to balance stamina, the need to be more mindful in smashing R1 to chain combos together, all that jazz. It is NOT just a wrote re-hash of FromSoft's masterpieces, and it least makes a very genuine attempt to distinguish itself.There is some minor jank in camera movement that is typical of the genre, but nothing about this game several hours in warrants a negative review. It's great to look at, the combat is fun, I like Aegis as a character and the weapon options and enemy variety is engaging so far. I like Steelrising. It's a very comfortable 7/10, and deserves to be played. The ONLY real detriment is its price. It FEELS like a game that should have cost $29.99 instead of $49.99. I'm unsure if it warrants its own price tag yet, but it certainly has potential to. C'est la vie.

_childDocuments_.review: It's still early but I really like this one.  It's no elden ring, it's clunky and slow, but the amount of love poured into the animation and sound design really shines through, resulting in it feeling really good to play, and its theme is really like nothing else - not just in soulslikes, but in general.  My biggest criticism at the moment is that it runs extremely poorly, so be prepared to drop settings.Edit: Updating my review because I have now finished the game!The game's animation, visual design, and sound design remains top-notch throughout, and the gameplay stays fun, though it's comparatively easy to completely break the game with a good build.  I don't really mind, I don't think games should be entirely balanced around players who analyse systems and then minmax, and there's nothing wrong in the existence of an easier soulslike, but it is worth mentioning that it's not too hard to make the late game pretty trivial, by soulslike standards at least.  It is still reasonably tough compared to a run of the mill action game, but it's substantially easier than Dark Souls, Nioh, or Elden Ring.However, it comes with its fair share of problems.The gameplay is mostly great, things feel and look amazing, landing hits is satisfying and impactful, the 'immobilisation' system ripped out of Sekiro is still fun here - but there are some serious issues that particularly manifest with enemies whose attacks come out fast.  Enemies don't stagger on hit as far as I can tell - a system is present to inflict stagger that's separate from the immobilization thing, but even light enemies will just eat an entire combo before being interrupted.  What this means is that you can start a swing, a fast enemy can start to attack, you can land your hit on the fast enemy, and the fast enemy will still hit you, which forces you to wait for more serious threats to attack before you can make a move, and can generates a lot of dead space in combat where you're waiting for something to happen, because just attacking might get you hit.  This is worsened by some readability issues, particularly on the small enemies, as most of the game is quite dark, and enemies like the arachnids and felines are small enough that they can be partially obscured by the player character's body.The hit trading problem with smaller enemies isn't a huge issue, Aegis can take a lot of hits and fast attacks usually don't hit too hard, but what *is* a serious issue is how the camera behaves when you lock on to one of these small enemies.  The arachnid class of enemy in particular are priority targets that should be killed first, as they can buff other enemies or heal them, but when you lock on, the camera cranks down so far that it becomes very difficult to read the attacks on other enemies in a group, making group combat involving arachnids incredibly annoying.Lastly, the writing is really pretty bad, and to be honest this bothered me a lot more than the issues with gameplay.  I'm not going to go into a lot of detail for spoiler reasons, but there was a predictable twist in the latter half of the game that resulted in an equally predictable conclusion, one that left a lingering negative feeling.  There was a reasonably compelling mystery leading up to that point, but in the end it felt like Aegis, and me as the player by extension, were being deprived of agency and told that we didn't matter, despite Aegis having apparently carried the french revolution on her back.  The characterisation of the various historical figures you bump shoulders with was very weak as well, the voice actors did their best but they all kinda felt like slight variants on the same vaguely-determined-and-heroic-good-guy character archetype, with a few less scrupulous characters who were still flat and dull in their own ways.  The only real exception was maybe Robespierre, who was still flat, but was at least fun whenever he was on screen.In conclusion: it's a 7/10 action game, and I love these.  I'd rather play something flawed and weird than ambitious but safe any day, and this falls squarely in that category, even if its story did leave me with a bad taste in my mouth.  If you like soulslikes, want something unique, and are willing to put up with bad writing and a bit of jank, this is a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a great game that is definitely doesn't get enough credit. You play as the robot bodyguard of Marie Antoinette, Aegis. You are tasked with saving Paris during the French Revolution from the King's robot army.The common Soulslike staples are here. Dropping souls on death, opening short cuts throughout the areas to save time after death, rewards for exploring, etc. What sets it apart is it's metroidvania approach in that, after defeating some of the major bosses (called Titans), you are rewarded with an ability to traverse previously inaccessible areas. The game is overall mush easier that most souls games. A majority of the bosses I beat on my first attempt, and those I lost to were beaten on the 2nd or 3rd attempt, tops. If the game is still daunting to you, there are accessibility options to help you customize a more user friendly experience. Combat is where the gameplay differs a bit. Weapons work the same in that there are different types of weapons and equipment. However, instead of swords and shields, you get weapons like fans and muskets. The difference is in weapon abilities, you can't block or parry unless you have an ability that allows it on the weapon. Every weapon comes with one ability that defines the weapons kit. A baton that can be imbued with ice can't block or parry, but a set of claws may let you parry but not block or imbue. This is where the combat feels more limited. A weapon in Dark Souls for example can deal poison damage, block, and leave a spot open to use another weapon or parry. Here you need to choose what from two weapon slots what skills are important to your build.  The story is mush easier to follow, but isn't honestly isn't all that interesting. It mostly revolves around helping a bunch of guys in powdered wigs wax poetic before giving you a side quest or telling you where to go next. Side quests are okay, and it'd be fine skipping them as it's typically about side tracking back to an area to find an item then going back to the quest giver a few times. I enjoyed my time and beat the game and completed all side quests in 20 hours. There is a NG+ mode that apparently offers more challenge and equipment but I've yet to try that. If thats to little for the asking price, I'd try to snag it if its on sale.My biggest complaints would be the lack of enemy variety and bugs. There are maybe 8 enemy types in the game and they are recycled and given a different element with different stats. This makes enemies feel repetitive rather than challenging. Which is a shame as the robots (Automats) have such awesome designs. The bugs aren't too bad but I'd jumped into spots that softlocked me a few times.If you can get this on sale, I highly recommend it. Despite its flaws its one of my favorite non-souls, soulslike.
