_childDocuments_.review: So, at the time of writing I've been on a bit of a Soulsborne and Soulslike binge and bought Steelrising despite the mixed reviews. As I'm nearing the end and dipping into the dlc I think I can give a bit more of a nuanced review.Steelrising is in essense a game that explores an alternative history based on the question: What if Louis XVI had an army of overpowered mechanical soldiers to stave off the revolution. Add in that the king is homicidally insane, estranged from his wife and egged on by a madman sans scrupules and you'll be glad that the squishy humans have at least one Automat able to step up to the plate to challenge the gruesome twosome and their machines.The game is a Soulslike/lite with (much like the Dark Souls series) no open world, but does allow one to unlock more exploration through the tools you'll acquire after the first few bosses. A fun bonus is that these can also be used in combat (at a cost) to deal elemental damages to freeze, shock and set afire any unlucky Automat standing in your way. Aegis can be configured to have somewhat different looks and has some starting classes to choose from, though these at most are for the initial stat allocations and weapons.Par for the course maybe, but no matter the starting class, you can build your Aegis as you wish. You can also pick up a variety of weapons throughout the game and dlc to fit your playstyle. Pet peeve here: the best weapon imo, the Discus Chain, is sold as DLC. And that is a bad move imo. You can upgrade each weapon to level five with enough sou... erh.. anima essence and materials. Kinda like Bloodborne, almost all weapons have a secondary attack form that consumes an alchemical capsule or more. Some weapons are worth using, but others... Unlike what other reviewers gripe about... I'll have to say the enemy variety is actually not that bad. Yes, you get enemies with similar body types... but they wield different weapons/elements and some varieties gain armor as you progress. The grunts are okay, though the bosses are where the game's at. I do not like the  since its final phase is so cheap it might as well be an arcade quartermuncher. Aegis is (comparatively) fragile and most of her outfits don't really add to armor so you'll want to invest in her stats. Health, stamina and armor are more key to surviving the game than the attack stats. Especially since Aegis will overheat if she runs out of stamina.Steelrising does a lot of things right. Combat is fun, bosses are good, there's a lot to like about the environments, lore and more... but its also hampered by small on their own issues which do add up. The grappling hook is finnicky, you burn through alchemical capsules like nobody's business, the cutscenes (especially for dialogue) are rough, the door npc's for fetchquests are frankly damn awful to get back to... and the voiceacting is bad. This one thing though, I place squarely on the conto of the voice actors. The devs might not have had budget for native speaker level French voice actors, but this lot try to out-British the British despite knowing full well it's a game set in France. Even I could put in more effort to emulate a French accent rather than a British pub-hanger one they apparently default to.Personally, I do think the devs need to fix a persistent issue: items are sometimes damn hard to pick up. The button press is registered, but the flame effect and items remain on the ground until you try dozens of times at times... And finding your way through areas is just a tad confusing.I do recommend Steelrising. It's flawed (much like Dark Souls), but I do think it's worth experiencing this game. Not sure if its worth a replay though, but as is? Certainly. Just be aware you'll want the dlc content, but that it may be better to pick this one up during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Effortpost ahead. tl;dr good. some irks. For most of you, you're considering buying this because it's a soulslike, which it is. So most of my review is going to focus on the soulslike aspects of this game, for the other stuff I'm gonna rapid fire it off with just a Good - Yes, or bad - No.-Graphics, looks fantastic and the aesthetic is really charming and sort of fresh. - Yes! -Performance, runs pretty good on my rig, can't max it out though but I don't really need to - Yes! (Looks like it is rough on certain midspec systems though)-Voice Acting, I get budgets are a thing but the game is set in France and everyone has English accents. I don't want English people in my game. - No! (VA's are competent though)-Story, haven't finished it yet and I like Aegis. - Yes!-General control and game feel, general movement feels slightly janky, even for a soulslike but it's nothing major and the rest id fine. - Yes! (I would like a HUD indicator for when I'm walking though)With that out of the way, it's onto the soulsy stuff. The bonfire system is pretty fine, however the fast travel is a lot more restrictive than in say DS3. Each "area" has a single point you can travel to/from, with the rest of the area being 'bonfires' that you can't fast travel to. That being said the shortcuts are pretty genius, especially in the Louvre area, there's still a couple doors I'm missing in there but I'll get them eventually. A few people have commented on the lack of exploration but I feel what they really mean is the lack of items rewarding you for exploration, anything you see on the ground is a consumable which honestly I don't care about too much that begin said the level design itself does promote exploration as you'll be unlocking generally either shortcuts, or alternate routes which is more than enough for me, and the gameplay is fun so I have no problems with playing more in a different area. Characters/ build customisation is maybe 1/4 of what it in DS for example you can only have one active weapon slot but it's still pretty decent, armor is very obviously tiered to some extent which I'm not a fan of, because with this setting fashionsoulsing would be great. The combat itself is certainly easier than the average soulslike but that's not a terrible, and it's still a soulslike so it's not like it immediately becomes babbys first action rpg. The attacks both feel and look good and i suppose that's the silver lining of having a reduced weapon set. Enemy movesets are pretty limited though and the telegraphs are insanely visible, most enemies can parry though which is a fun surprise that being said it does slow the combat down a little once you realise that they all have a "parry stance" so you have to stand there and wait for it to finish before resuming your fight, another gripe is that enemies aren't really that aggressive, especially the most basic mobs, who can still parry, which again slows the game down. I'm probably in the last 30% of the game and there's been a couple of times where I've dropped myself into a boss fight totally unprepared and got it first go, or almost gotten it first go. That being said I'm running weapons with a parry special which does trivialise them a bit with their insane tells. The largest complaint I have with this game is that you can't respec, or at least not from what I've seen. All in all this is a fantastic soulslike, and perfect for someone who wants to take the plunge into the genre, there is also an accessibility mode to make it easier should you wish, I haven't tried it yet but reading the options makes it look like it's pretty customisable. If you're a souls vet, this is still a great game however you if you WANT to clench and sweat the entire game maybe look somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: And that's Steelrising beaten. What a strong start leading to kind of a weak finish. It's cool to see Spiders experimenting with other genres, even if I'm not the biggest Soulsborne fan, but I'm not sure one so dependent on enemy variety and exploration is the best pick for a side project while they develop other games. Game took me about 13 hours, not counting the 10 hours I accidentally left it on overnight, lol.+The world, art direction, etc, are all fantastic. Creative designs, cool architecture, fun twist on the French Revolution.+Boss designs were creative and interesting as well, and each major boss had pretty unique mechanics.+Weapon variety isn't bad at all, with some fun special abilities like alchemical power-ups, meteor hammers, etc.+Aegis is a neat character for how basic her concept is; I liked her in a kind of dignified way. Also highly customizable.+Honestly NOT an ugly game. It's not cutting-edge, but for a small studio like Spiders, it's impressive how consistently good-looking much of the world and enemies were.+AWESOME accessibility options, some of the best I've seen. Total invincibility, damage discounts, stamina consumption, etc. Tailoring to your preferences is very possible.+Consistently solid PC port. No crashes, performance was solid. Some framedrops in fire-heavy areas but nothing that felt too painful.+Some surprisingly decent platforming bits.-For a Soulsborne, availability of healing is a big deal. This game makes potions cheap and plentiful and I had 90 of them by game's end. This kind of meant I could windsprint between bosses and ignore the back half of the game. Infinite stamina potions only made this worse. Singlehandedly the biggest problem.-The story is just...weak. Some cool ideas are buried under a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of cutscenes about french dudes arguing, and it feels very disjointed and weird.-Combat, while feeling good, never meaningfully evolves, due largely to lack of variety in enemy types. 'Fat robot, spear robot, snake robot, soldier robot, and flail robot' literally make up 80% of foes, with only occasional deviations. Prooobably 15-20 actually distinct enemies in the entire game? It became noticeable by the end.-Many side missions require a Metroid-vania style backtracking once you have boss equipment, but it's more tiring than fun because nothing changed in that area while you were gone. -Side quests in general all amount to 'go here, pick up object, watch french dude talk for awhile', fight reskinned miniboss'. Felt them eminently skippable.All in all, the game opened as a potential 8/10, but by the end, it felt like more of a 6/10 for the reasons above. It's a worthy Souslborne take for the world design and weapon options, but you definitely feel the seams of the Eurojank budget by halfway through. Still recommended because it does some interesting things.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this by saying I have beat this game and have spent over 13 hours playing it. I don't know why steam says I only have 7 hours.Anyway... I overall enjoyed this game, it's really well polished for being an indie souls-like game, even though it bites more than it can chew in my opinion, so let me detail my thoughts below.First, I'll start with the positives, like I said, this game is really well polished, the graphics are really good, and the animations are fantastic. The art design is pretty cool, you get to play in paris during the french revolution, but it's alternate history where there are robots everywhere.Regarding the combat, it's pretty fluid, it's the typical souls-like combat, with attacks that force you to commit to them, and it's limited by a stamina bar, there is a surprisingly large number of weapons available to you, and there is some RPG elements such as stats and armor perks. My only criticism with it is the unique abilities weapons get, some of them get a block, some get a parry ability, and some get a cool extra attack, these are fine but they limited my option in weapon choice since I really like to parry in these type of games. The parrying in this game feels nice, but it is way too easy to pull off, you get a large window to parry, and you always automatically riposte afterwards, you're only limited by being stuck in other animations, which is really easy to avoid if you're just patient.This game is surprisingly large, there are like 7 areas, and they're all pretty large and decently designed, with the typical souls design of it being interconnected with multiple shortcuts and stuff, but tit is not as tight as fromsoft games obviously. Also, some of the shortcuts are nonsensical and useless, I remember a particular one in one of the early levels where there's a locked door, and a hole in the wall next to it, you enter that hole and land behind the door and then you can open it, not to mention there's a bonfire right behind this gate as well making it double useless.Even though the areas are pretty big and decently designed, there's unfortunately very little enemy variety, you're going to be pretty much fighting the same 10 enemies the entire game, which just felt boring to me halfway through the game so I just decided to run past everything, since it's so easy, you have good movement options and the enemies rarely pose a threat even if you fight them, they just waste your time. Also, their AI is really bad, I have yet to find an enemy in this game that I couldn't cheese just by circling around them, and that includes most bosses.Speaking of bosses, there are a lot, and they're all uniquely designed, but they're really easy, I have only died 3 times to bosses the entire game, and two of those was because I entered boss fights with low healing items. Also, this game has a really broken item that gives you infinite stamina for 30 seconds, which makes every boss a cake walk, not that you'd ever need them, because there's also a mechanic of freezing enemies, that lasts an eternity so you can destroy half the boss's health with only a single freeze. Regarding the story, from what I could tell it seems like there was a robot uprising, and you play the single robot who decided to be a class traitor and a pickme and side with the humans, so you go around killing your fellow robots for the sake of the french nobles. But don't take my word for it, I literally skipped every cutscene and dialogue option lmao.Despite all of this, I had fun playing this one, I would recommend it to people who like souls games, and only on a sale, it's definitely not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't beat this, but I'm not really pushing myself to any time frame.If you are familiar with the Souls-Like combat, then this is going to feel very clunky at first.  Given how a lot of the enemies are also moving with a lot of staccato then I would say that the clunky disjointed feeling is intentional.  Once I got more weapon options I found a few that I like and each can have a different level of flow.  I like the idea of the story, but I'm not taking particular or significant interest.  The French Revolutionary setting feels great and I am not familiar enough with the history to know if any liberties they took are particularly egregious.  There is a compass in the game to give guidance on your objective, I would encourage you to use it if you get stuck.  Around the 3rd boss or so I was in the right area and looking at the right stuff, but came to the point where I needed another item to pass through the blocks I had found.  When I used the compass I had to follow it to each check point about 50 meters before it pointed out a hole between a fence and a window that I didn't notice and that was the only way forward to a boss fight and get the item the other paths were blocking me on.  I felt silly, but It is good they had the compass guidance built into the game.  There are bugs in the game, I haven't seen anything break a quest line or progress, but one field kept telling me I was in some guy's garden then the city catacombs every few steps, so certainly some polish that didn't get into the product.  The Load Times have been irritating, I mean full 60 to 150 seconds from start game in steam to being able to load the save file, some similar times in transition between areas.  I have read that this can be improved by using a solid state drive, but I haven't spent time moving the files.Over I think this is a game worth my time, but I would certainly encourage people interested in game design to play this and question any details they find.  Have fun with it!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A good game with a unique world, brand new for under $60 US.  Buy it if you have a system that can run it.Although I think most of the performance complaints will be ironed out pretty quickly, I just want to state that the game is playing smoothly for me.  It has some pretty stiff requirements that I'm not sure it earns in visuals, but I haven't dropped a single frame so far.  I have a good rig but not a beast or anything.  late gen I-7 with a 1660's ti (overclocked a bit).  It suggested low graphics settings, but I fiddled with them and was able to upgrade a few things without running out of vram.  No raytracing of course without the rtx label.$50 on a brand new game is respectable.  It isn't some indie rogue-lite deckbuilder.  Some people say it's only worth $30, but I can't get two meals at a restaurant these days for under $30.  The economy sucks and milk costs more for developers too.  Hell, I bought two coffees today and spend $15 bucks.  This game has already given me more enjoyment and will assuredly last longer than four cups of coffee.I've been enjoying killing clockwork monsters.  So far, nothing particularly inspiring on a design level.  Most have been humanoid with weapons.  The first boss was pretty easy, but not impossible.  It's definitely easier than a souls game with an interesting upgrade system.  It's still points in stats but it looks prettier.The game looks nice, the first few areas were just square and sparsely decorated.  I was worried that the whole game was going to be that way, but once I got into the woods, the areas (at least from an aesthetic view) have become more organic.  Lots of small animations inside the character models bring a lot of life and detail that a texture map just wouldn't do.  It's not Elden Ring graphics, but not a lot of games can claim that they are.The combat is loose, more than souls games but once you get the hang of it, it becomes second nature.  Either way, I love the animations.  The automatons look clumsy but move with surprising elegance just when you let your guard down.  The textures are beautiful but definitely require too much to run. I didn't exceed my ram limit to see what the ultra textures look like here.  I wanted to test the game for the first two hours so I could know if my rig could handle it.  So far it is performing way better than I am lol.  I'll push it now that I know it will play for me and see how broken the higher settings are with my under-powered card.Not necessarily related to this game, here's a few optimization tips (I've always had mediocre pcs).  First of all, kill all the background stuff that you don't need running.  chrome, firefox, brave, spotify, battlenet, Origin, ubisoft connect, gog, discord, epic games store, the bloatware that came on your rig (if you bought a prebuilt) and any other software that has found its way onto your start-up/automatic services/task scheduler.  Turn off automatic updates.  I even killed my fan speed controls (windows handles that just fine). As for the games themselves, one of the biggest performance killers that people don't think about is vsync.  Kill it and let the game find its own frame rate.  Shadows are another killer, especially on nvidia cards and the higher settings usually aren't worth the performance hit.  Don't be afraid to use the upscaling features dlss (I think is what it's called).  I generally kill motion blur (I don't know if it causes slowdowns, but I don't like the look).  HDR isn't worth the hit or the burned out oled.  Some of the light filtering and AA stuff is definitely worth the hit if you can afford it (but they do take resources).  Particles are worth it and generally don't need much.  And I'll usually push the textures as high as the game lets me. and the view distance as far as the game lets me.I'm really not a fan of nacon's business practices, but an upcoming lawsuit might change my mind when I am able to hear both sides of the argument.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 7/10Level Design: 9/10A->B: 9/10Bosses: 5/10Combat Mechanics: 8/10Character Customization: 7.5/10Early Game: 6/10Mid Game: 7/10End Game: 8.5/10Full Game Score: 8/10Good:- The A->B is really good, the level design is top notch. I *wanted* to explore more, to look around for hidden things, to look for enemy ambushes, to check out other paths. It was interesting walking around. Probably the best A->B of a non-fromsoft game I've played. It's also beautiful.- Because you unlock new movement powers as you play, you open up more of previous areas - which side quests take advantage of. Giving you reason to explore again.- Side quests give a homeward bone equivalent, to reduce walk-back, which is just a real nice QoL.- The combat feels good. Getting a counterattack, or a block in time, or freezing a foe and smacking them, timing a charged attack properly, or a perfectly timed dodge - it all feels good.- The run backs to bosses are nice and short, and there are plenty of shortcuts to open to help with the huge levels. These help when you later go back for sidequests too.- The Rapid Cooling/stamina management is very clever and enjoyable to use.- The titans were enjoyable fights, especially the last boss.Bad:- Occasional lag spikes, but only once or twice a session.- Very long load times.- Side quests that involve bouncing around the city a lot, so more load times.- Infusions just feel bad. While it's cool that you can make your weapon hit with fire, lightning or ice, unless you're playing an alchemist it isn't going to help much. If you are playing an alchemist than you *need* that damage, which means you're expending vials to keep it up. A lot of the infusion moves can easily be interrupted too, so you can't really make use of the aoe damage very easily. Additionally if you swap to your other weapon you lose your infusion, which is just frustrating if you want to use more than one weapon in a fight.- Like many soulslikes, the game is esoteric in what different stats/items actually do. Modules especially "Gives a significant increase to physical damage when you full charge an attack" doesn't really tell me how much that damage boost is. Also sometimes they're inaccurate, like the module for counter attacks saying physical damage, but also increasing elemental damage. Mediocre:- Like bloodborne, this uses a bullet like system to control the 'magic'. These bullets are consumables you pick up as you kill things. Playing an alchemist build becomes very costly (though some things help offset that, like your pants and two of the modules), as to make your weapons do elemental damage you have to spend bullets for 40 seconds of powerup. Muskets cost bullets per shot, your movement skills cost bullets to use on enemies - it's all very expensive and you can run out fighting bosses.- Boss design is kind of lazy. 12/21 of the bosses are just super versions of normal mobs (called "Unstable X"). At the start of the game this is okay, because it's the first time you fight the various enemies. You don't know what they do, so you have some patterns to learn. But once you've fought an enemy 50 times, facing it as a boss 10 hours later isn't exciting or interesting. Especially since often times they are stronger than the titans because they've been super upgraded. - The unique bosses are far more interesting. However, some of them seem to glitch out. I fought one boss that did this belly flop attack, which had a huge opening for me to smack him while he was on the ground, and was easy to avoid - for half his HP he just kept doing this over and over. The designs are interesting overall. However across the board, the bosses are very easy for any soulslike vet. Only one titan (the one in La Cite) gave me any trouble, every other boss died on my first try without even using up my estus flasks. The La Cite boss was the first time my alchemist build ran into an enemy that was very resistant to frost/fire, my main two elements at the time - once I grinded up a lightning weapon I was able to beat it.- Leveling weapons sucks, especially early. The materials are very expensive, and you need a lot. To get a weapon to level 2 is two copper bars, to get it to level 3 is three copper bars and one or two cast iron ingots, it's very easy to run out of copper early if you don't farm for it, but since it's 2000 anima per bar that means to get a level 1 weapon to level 3 you need 16000 in raw resources, plus another 7500 for the leveling up. For comparison, at the end of the game when I was in my mid 30s, it cost 24000 to level. Just to get a single weapon to level 3 (around level 10) cost me as much as 2-3 levels, or a full late game level.The Strange:- You can't teleport from the 'bonfires', the Vestals, meaning you have a lot of walking around the city to do. On the flip side, the level design is very good, and thus as you unlock more movement abilities it's not much of a chore.- You get very few 'estus flasks', getting 2->4 of them, but you get consumable heal over times. I actually like this, as it means you're really focused on maintaining life with slow heals, and avoiding damage. But I can see if you have a lot of HP this being hard to deal with (unless they heal a percentage, the game doesn't tell you). Late game you have so much money/consumables that you could spam them for an entire boss fight to make them pretty easy.- Modules and items are pretty nebulous on what they actually do. Many modules specify they 'slightly increase', 'moderately increase' or 'significantly increase' a stat, but unless it's an attribute you can see (like hp or armour), that doesn't really mean anything. Some items specify they increase physical damage, but some of them affect elemental too. - Outfits are mostly aesthetic, but also have stats and some of them have somewhat hidden bonuses; like two pairs of pants 'randomly give alchemical capsules', which doesn't really mean anything but sounds useful. Some of the shoes also boost your movement skills but it doesn't say how they're boosted or show any real change.- No dedicated healing item button is weird, especially with two healing items. Only 6 slots to equip items means you only really get to equip 4 if you want both healing items.- Some items are quite strong, like the ability to be immune to all elements (or a specific one) for 30/60 seconds, or a potion that gives 30 seconds of unlimited endurance. Using these can make boss fights trivial as it removes all their damage or lets you attack/dodge as much as you want.The Awkward:- Build/Weapon variety. Since everyone gets the same three movement skills, and two weapons, there isn't much build variety. There are three main builds which do play differently from each other, but within a build there isn't much variance.Power - hit things hard, knocking them over; you attack so low that you need high vigor to survive being hit back and not be knocked over mid swing.Agility - hit things a lot and 'immobilize' them, to get crits. You need high endurance to attack lots, and it also buffs your crit damage.Alchemy - hit with elemental afflictions, you want to raise the elemental damage and multiplier to freeze/fire/lightning things often, using infusions/muskets/movement skills, and focus on engineering/alchemy.However, there are 9 weapon types in the game, four are for power, three are for agility, two are for alchemy - though most other weapons have an elemental infusable version or two, they generally scale really lowly. Unfortunately this means that weapons tend to feel identical to each other other than the special ability being different - this is even worse on alchemists who are mostly forced to use one weapon type, the baton (the musket does rather low damage mid->late game, a fully charged heavy attack was doing less than a single light attack with a baton).

_childDocuments_.review: The bosses in this game are actually less dangerous than normal enemies.Even a boss of the third level, which got its own intro cutscene and a death splash screen, was absolutely trivial compared to regular enemies before it (Yes, I'm talking about you, ball boy). For a soulslike game, this is not acceptable. You should NOT be able to right-click your way through literally E V E R Y boss that the game throws at you. The reason for that is that the bosses were just not built with quick cooling mechanic in mind, and they get absolutely BODIED by constant heavy attacks that you unleash while they are unable to retaliate because they're too slow and too clunky.The normal enemies are somewhat dangerous though, so that's something, right?The optimisation is probably the worst I've seen in a long while.I know it says RTX 2060 in its minimal requirements, but the game's got nothing – NOTHING – that would justify that. The game is stuttering, FPS is inconsistent, and it absolutely devours my computer's resources just to run that poorly.Cutscenes are cringe.Facial animations in cutscenes are dogwater. It's 2022, you require RTX 2060 for your game, yet your facial animations are worse than that of a 2009's (I think?) Assassin's Creed II.It wouldn't be such a big deal if rhe game didn't shove the camera right UP INTO their face. I am not talking about robots here, these are human beings, and I swear Aegis's face is animated better than theirs.Movement is jankJumping kills all momentum you have,  parkour sections feel really unbalanced in that you're never quite sure if you're gonna make it or not. To be fair, most of those times you DO make it.Ledge grabbing works fine, and it's probably why the parkour sections end up working. Because jumping sure is out to get you every time you do it.Bonfires are really usefulIntroduction of a shop and a blacksmith into this game's bonfires is much appreciated. It's convenient and easy to use. Quick cooling is neatWhile playing the beta, I thought quick cooling was way too punishing. I still think the punishment for sinking heat tol early is very harsh – locking you at 0 Endurance for like two seconds – but you definitely get used to the mechanic and mess up less and less as you go. It's a really nice way to promote aggressive gameplay, but sadly, that is the entire readon you can right-click any boss to death with absolutely no regsrd for your own safety. Because bosses were not built to punish you if you're constantly in their face.Overall, it's about a 4/10. The game is too easy to be a true soulslike, many things it does, it does poorly, the optimisation is absolute garbage. It gets some points for some QoL and quick cooling, and I guess the weapon designs are cool, but as a soulslike, it's a definite failure.

_childDocuments_.review: Extraordinarily fun. Aegis is one of the best protagonists of the year, and with her I had some of the most fast-paced and engaging combat I've experienced out of a souls-like game since Bloodborne. Graphics are also extremely impressive considering the size of the studio. So often while playing this game I would just stop what I'm doing to explore a room, check out the detail on a statue, or just gaze out across the city. Aegis also has some great customization, and this game is sorely lacking a photo mode to really capture her and the many outfits you can give her.The game does have its flaws - while fun, the combat is easy to cheese. Consumables seriously need to be limited to prevent spam and bosses all around need to attack more often and have higher alchemical resistances. You can get essentially infinite healing in this game which is just absurd. Other than that, I just have a lot of smaller gripes about facial animations, occasional difficulty in telling which doors are usable and which ones aren't, and a little annoyance about the end, which I won't get into here.But even while this game isn't perfect, I had a really good time with it, and considering this comes from a smaller studio this is just an incredible piece of art and I cannot wait to see where Spider goes from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasantly suprissed by how much i enjoyed this souls like, very likley SPIDERS best game to date.Solid combat, exploration, weapons and build options in a very unique and well relisted alternate history. Great design work through out, decent graphics and a story that does enough (i kept getting lost on who and why because a bunch of white wigged men kept refering to french places and each other, was hard to keep track but just might be me) still had some compelling moments and the game is good enough at base level that the not particularily engaging story wasn't a big detriment.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommendation: Only on a sale, otherwise, there are better games out there.Pros: Great aesthetics, interesting concept, relatively solid voice actingMid: Combat is fine, grapple is kinda cool, gear/upgrades get the job doneCons: The most uninspired boss fights ever, too much back tracking, WAY too much dialogue for how mid the story is, too long (even though it's only 20ish hours)Over all Steel Rising is alright. Not terrible. Not great. It's just... fine. I get that it's retelling the French revolution in an alt history setting, and that's a cool idea, but my god were the stories they told boring af. They really want to tug at your heart strings, but it's done in such a way, that it just makes you roll your eyes. There are a ton of Soulslikes on the market, I'd only recommend this one if you're out of better ones to play. There are absolutely worse games in the genre, without a doubt, but aside from a cool art style and a cool story idea, this ones just... alright. So, if you're a history nut with a penchant for French history, or you just really like the idea of alt history/steam punk robots, then wait for a sale. Actually, even if you do fit into one of those categories, I couldn't recommend this at 50 bucks, no way. $30 tops. I stuck with it and beat it, but after about 12 or so hours, I was rapidly growing bored. The final boss is a complete joke, not only in terms of difficulty, but the design was just... mini boss design at absolute best.Still, I can't give it a thumbs down because relative to other games out there, it's... fine.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit Bloodborne, a bit Assassin's Creed; Steel Rising is a fun little souls-like from Spiders that certainly doesn't hide its parentage. Combat feels very Bloodborne, with dashes and measured sequences of attacks being the name of the game, but a unique stamina management system keeps things fresh. Elemental debuffs also switch things up - a favoured tactic of my playthrough being to freeze enemies from a distance with my firearm, before closing in for a couple of charged attacks while they're locked down.There's a good variety of weapons to be had, with your standard mix of light, heavy and medium options. I chose the Falchion and Sabre early on and happily stuck with them through the rest of the game. Fashion Souls fans will also no doubt be pleased by the many lovely period-inspired hats, coats and shoes to choose from.Combat initially felt a little easy thanks to the embarrassment of grenades, oil vials, and alchemical capsules (ammunition) enemies dropped, but that has been tuned in the recent patch that also added NG+, so hopefully things will feel a bit more challenging.There is a fair bit of backtracking involved if you're a completionist like me who wants to do all of the sidequests; and I did start to really feel the lack of a teleport system between the Vestal lamps (bonfires/lanterns), but I understand the choice to not include one. The level design can also be a little confusing at times, so don't be afraid to use the Compass item if you're stuck trying to work out where a sidequest wants you to go next. All in all, a very worthy addition to the SoulsBorne canon with some period-piece flare and a surprisingly poignant conclusion. Bravo, Spiders; and dare I ask, encore?

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for a couple of hours now, I can safely say that I haven't needed to tweak graphics settings and it runs just fine, even on my venerable GTX 1050 Ti.Fun game, even if it is a souls-like.  I haven't had to swear at the game yet, but I'm not exactly too far into it.  Its quite pretty, combat is generally fun (although the hitboxes on the Unstable Lancer boss were a bit wonky).It feels a little more polished than previous Spiders games, but continues their fine tradition of each game being a bit better than the last.  They're definitely a studio I'm following with interest.  They don't quite hit the highs of the studios they're inspired by, but their games are interesting and tell decent stories, and the love for their work is apparent.  Steelrising is no exception (so far at least)EDIT: Played for a few more hours and my poor graphics card is struggling to load textures on occasion, but I've still only experienced one stutter (during the first Titan fight).  I'd still recommend the game, but with the caveat that it will suit those who like the idea of souls-likes but don't want to deal with the difficulty.  Steelrising is definitely easier than a FromSoft game.  But that suits me just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: I think 6/10 is a fair rate for this one.I love the setting and design. Enemies are astonishingly beautiful, but they stop to impress you the moment you reach the 3rd location and you see the same exact 10 dudes, just a little upgraded. Those are too repetitive, in the final arena I had no strenght to deal with them anymore.The locations look good and are interesting to walk across, but they don't have this unique fresh feeling when you move from one to another, so it's entirely possible to get bored in the halfway. Worldbuilding is well done, but it feels a bit less apocalyptic and more hopeful than in the soulslikes I've played before. Not saying it's a bad thing.The plot... exists, and I believe the writers did everything to include every side plot they found important, however I didn't bother to complete all side quests because I had no will to come back to already explored locations because of how unintutive they are to explore without a compass. But this may be on me and my lack of sense of orientation in the field.I loved the dancer class, the combat for me was friendly, not too demanding, just the right amount of agressive (which appeals to me quite well after getting addicted to Bloodborne), but the stamina consumption is a pain in the ass. Nice healing system, few renewable hp potions + loosely limited amount of potions that refill hp in a slower matter, but using them with brain makes surviving in fights much easier.Actually I found this game pretty easy, as for someone who doesn't put much care in combat in games other than soulslikes, I had no trouble with casual enemies, and there was only one boss I found pretty hard (the first titan I guess?), all the others were down in the first attempt.Big minus for the optimalization, the graphic requirements are ridiculously high even for low settings, which can make the game a bit stuttering, the animations look floppy and the details load with a delay, maybe even unplayable for many.In conclusion, I find Steelrising a very promising game and I can feel the heart that was put into it, just the financial possibilites of the company were limited or the production was a bit rushed. It has a lot of field to improve, but it's not a complete flop. I adore the Spiders ideas and I sincerely hope one day they will have all the possibilites to make a game that won't have any underdeveloped aftertaste.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would give this a 7.5/10Pros: Amazing story, I was entirely invested in the world, its characters, and cried at the true ending. To get the full story side quests are imperative, but they weren't a slog. Really loved it, it was my favorite part.Atmosphere was really great, the burning city, the massacres, the feeling of despair in almost every map. It was really nice and felt authentic. It really got you into the mood for the game and really set the tone while doing the quests.Combat was relatively easy, but wasn't baby-mode. I'm not the best at souls games so I liked that, even without assist-mode, normal difficulty was exactly as described. Major bosses took one to two tries, had mechanics and patterns. Normal enemies annoyed the hell out of me but what is a souls game without dogs.Voice acting was extremely solid. A lot of them are from previous Spider Games, or were VA's who i could easily identify and did a great job as always. The voice of Aegis was amazing and made it super easy to connect and get invested in her.CONS:Not like other Spider games. For me the companions, the romances, and the friendships you build along the way are imperative to a good game and narrative. While I still enjoyed the characters, and connected with a lot of them, I'm sad they abandoned their normal design. I do accept this is what normally gets left out in souls games, but I think it would have added a special feel to the game.Bugs made the game a bit jank. I've played almost all Spider games and without fail they are always jank. For me it wasn't much of an issue, I could run everything fine, but now and then I got drops in frames as well as audio issues. A single cutscene wasn't voiced or animated as well. But Spiders isn't AAA so it really wasn't much of a problem/surprise, but I put it under cons as some people are mad about it. Other Comments: I really loved this game. I liked it a lot. I think, if they blended their usual stuff with this souls-like it could have been closer to a 9/10 but the lack of companions and romances really bothered me, even though I was still invested. The True Ending made me cry, and I really liked Aegis. Even though I missed these, however, I think the narrative is one of the better ones I have played through in a while. I also appreciate that it was straightforward. The sidequests were fun, it easily expanded the lore without being super long, and I think the game has a good length as well as decently fun combat. I think for most people searching for a chill game that is a good time, has good characters, a cool story, and decent gameplay will be pleased with this game. There are some bugs, but most games that come out these days have them, and for me they weren't much of an issue.I see a lot of people harping on the fact there are black people, or that its non historically accurate, among other things. Don't listen to them, they are idiots. It's a steampunk game about Robots fighting other Robots. It's fantasy, and if you can't get over a black person in it or they fact they added some random person or event for drama sake, don't play it. That is just my opinion, but I felt the need to put it here. It's a fun fantasy world and bigots need to go cry a river elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: For the first few hours of playing this game, I was battling the feeling of what a mistake I was making. The awful performance (more on that later) was so atrocious that I was barely able to run the game at a playable framerate. Jankiness is there, getting stuck on the terrain while running is there, bugs, getting soft-locked, characters freezing in dialogues, or completely bugging out are all there. The bosses are laughable, if you are competent or semi-competent even, they cannot kill you. Design-wise, yes, some bosses are intriguing but gameplay and challenge-wise? shamefully, not a single boss is memorable from this entire game. And regular mobs and enemies, once you understand how the game works you will rarely die even when outnumbered, it's just disappointingly easy.However, underneath that pile of issues, there's a game about friendship, heroism, serving God and Nation, about a political struggle on a national scale that will either sink or explode France. For those reasons, the game is worth playing. Assuming you really, really like soul-like games and are addicted to them (like me), then you can play and enjoy Steelrising. Here is where this game suffers the most:Steelrising has a Metroidvania-like aspect; you start out missing some abilities that you need to progress to other parts of the map and for combat, like every other MD except here: 1) This game isn't optimized whatsoever. I don't understand what their intention was here, the game needs so much VRAM on your GPU, and to do what? the game doesn't look revolutionary at all or special. Since the performance is so bad, almost everyone will have to lower the settings so much that the game will look like a mess so their work on the graphical part was in vain...2) The early levels are so uninspired and bland that it might just kill off your interest before you even get to the fun parts. 3) You have no special abilities at the start, you cannot interact with things you see in the world. Your combat options are limited and you care not about anyone in the story because you know nobody just yet.Now, if you can suffer through the first few hours and accept the bad performance, you will discover how this game grows on you. I believe, or at least that what happened to me is the game slowly got better or I understood it better. I still had to restart the game because I got stuck in the terrain or a quest got bugged out, but despite all that, those political characters that you meet, Ageis herself, slow and bulky elemental combat, and exploration make it all worth it. Especially more so when you finally unlock abilities that allow you to fight in more fun ways and more importantly, progress further in each region so you can start doing the interesting and fun side quests that help you understand the world and its people, foes, and allies, those who lived in the past and the future generations. The way people spoke in France back then, according to this game, and their traditions and clothes, haircuts, and culture, the artistic nature of life back then, it was a special thing to witness too.Maybe Aegis' heroism and dedication to her task aren't really things to admire about her because she isn't a self-conscious being, she cannot make an active decision against fulfilling her duty or looking the other way. If one cannot refuse to do something, then doing it isn't worth the praise. I wouldn't blame you for thinking that way, but at the end of the game, you will realize that even a rising steel can be conscious, and can make active decisions.Aegis says: "I cannot escape my obligations. It is in my very nature to honor them." But what about the player? Who made an active decision to play and suffer through this game's shortcomings as Aegis suffered through the game's events?Just you and her both, aiming to reach the same end goal: Pour La Nation...  Pour La Nation.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game completely blind not knowing what to expect. I was pleasantly surprised at how much I've actually enjoyed this one. I've enjoyed all of Spiders works thus far, so I suppose I shouldn't be. I probably wouldn't have picked it up had I known it was a souls-like, cause they usually aren't as fun in the long run and are much easier than what they're often compared too. The game isn't much different when it comes to the challenge not being all there, at least for me personally, for most of the game. After a certain point once you invest points into your base stats and weapons, the game is pretty breezy. The combat is responsive and feels really good. The weapons and their secondary abilities aren't that varied, but for me personally that wasn't too big of a deal as I used 3-4 of the same weapons and abilities for most of the game. The story is a solid 6 and a half, maybe 7. Combat is a high 8. Difficulty is maybe a 6/10 and once you get the combat down and some upgrades it's about a 4 or 5, maybe a 6 depending on the area. It's a decently lengthy game with a good amount of content and area's to explore. There were a few annoying action glitches, like when you go to pick up an item the animation for the item is still active in the spot that you retrieved it from. I fell through the floor in a boss area once about 24 hours into the game, and some times enemies wouldn't pop up in an area, but when I reloaded it there would be another enemy there and it would catch me off guard. Almost convinced me it was programmed that way to make it harder with the few times that it happened. In one area you have to jump over a broken set of doors to leave, and I was stuck there for a bit because the air time you'd have to get is so precise. That was a common theme with other gaps/jumps throughout the game, which was a bit tedious, but manageable. Outside of those things I didn't encounter many issues, and none of which were game breaking. I think for 20-30+ hours the game is a decent price. Certainly not as long as some of their other titles, but this is a bit different than the norm from Spider. I don't think many can capture the atmosphere of a Souls game or the intricacies and detail, but this is pretty good and at times came close, but all the same I thoroughly have enjoyed my time playing this game and I recommend it. I want to give it an 8, but a 7 might be better for the overall rating. Fix some of the bugs and maybe add a board to make a few gaps closer or remove some railing and maybe add an item and/or some enemies to the empty rooms in the game and it has the potential of a solid 8.

_childDocuments_.review: It is probably one of the worst optimized games of all time, its performance is absolute trash.Running on 12900k, 32 GB Ram, 3080 Ti at 1440p, and regardless of the visual settings, there are constant fps drops, stuttering and bad frame pacing. Disabling E-cores makes it run better, but there are still constant fps drops. It seems that the game utilizes only a few cores, and hence the stutters when the main thread is locked.And it actually looks like a 5-10 year old game, especially the janky animations, horrible particle effects and human characters right from the uncanny valley.Gameplay wise, it's also nothing special, just another Soulsborne clone with really bad level design (the locations are mostly linear and have no memorable areas), the only interesting thing about it is its setting. But this only plus is utterly destroyed by all the cons: horrible performance, janky animations and clunky controls. Avoid at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of Greedfall, and when this was announced, the setting interested me, so sign me up! After finishing my first playthrough, I can say this game probably won't stick with me quite as long, but I still definitely enjoyed it. I only wonder what could have been if they had a larger team or budget.The character-focused story/sidestory is a solidly entertaining experience, and the main draw of the game for me. The facial animations leave a lot to be desired, but the voice acting is solid. Most of the stories are interesting and unique, and seem to have multiple endings that I believe have an impact on how the game ends, though I could be wrong as I've only completed it once at the moment. On top of that, I appreciate that it's easy to follow the side stories in this game. Some people may like the cryptic, almost definitely missed on first playthrough experience of a Souls-game, but personally, I'm thankful that wasn't the case here as it makes it easier to appreciate the story of the game.The level design and world building is very well made, with a labyrinth-like map with plentiful exploration and shortcuts to reduce the amount of mindless backtracking to get where you need to go. For the vast majority of the game, I was fully immersed in running around this downtrodden city. Chests are always exciting as they are nearly exclusively filled with stuff that I wouldn't consider 'filler' items. I do wish there was a slight bit more variance in the way the world looked, 2-3 of the areas had a very 'samey' look. It led to a bit of confusion as to which map I was on. On top of that, a frustrating feature of this game is some paths being locked behind quests, without being obvious in that feature. It does slightly disincentivize exploration to a small extent as it can be frustrating reaching an interesting looking area to run into a gate that you cannot open and have no idea why you cannot open it.Combat and general gameplay feels super good in my opinion. There's a good variety of weapons and they all feel fun to use; despite having less weapon types than a game like Dark Souls, I ended up using more weapons overall as more of them just felt interesting and fun to use. On top of that, it's much harder to 'mess up' your build and gives you more freedom to explore all your items. On the flipside, this simplification of the character progression does mean it's not as exciting, as there are less choices to be made and stuff like stat-locked weapons are not a thing. Also, some of the unique features of combat are quite fun. Fast-cooldown took some time to get used to, but once I did, it was very fun to use and significantly impacted the way I playedAlong with combat, enemies are solid but leave a bit to be wanted. There were no enemies that left me frustrated, they all had a solid place in the game. That being said, variety does lack compared to the more mainstream games of this genre. My main criticism in this regard is the bosses, or lack of. There's a relatively small amount of bosses, and an even smaller amount of bosses that actually stood out to me as interesting fights. It left me wondering if this game being in the 'Soulslike' genre was the right option, or if it should have been in the same realm as Greedfall.I probably have a lot more to say but this review is kind of dragging on, so to TL;DR some of my views of this gameThe good-Very interesting story/world, side-stories in particular-Voice acting is solid-Very satisfying minute-to-minute gameplay-An accessibility mode for those that need it (sorely lacking in this genre)-Pretty environments, enemies, outfits, basically everything has great artstyle/aesthetics-It stands out as a unique experience in gaming-Level design is solidNot so good-System requirements are way too high for the technical quality of the game-Enemy variety leaves a bit to be desired-Boss fights are a weaker aspect of the game, which is disappointing considering the genre-Facial animations can be jarring-No french dub? :(-Story-locked areas can leave you confused-It leaves you wanting more from itAll in all, if you want to get the best bang for your buck, this might not hold up to something like Elden Ring. That being said, it's still a solidly fun ~20 hour experience and I enjoyed it the entire way through; it's one of those games that I just lost track of time playing it. At the end of the day, that's what I tend to desire from games, so I would say this game is worth playing to me.(as a sidenote, Spiders seems like a cool smaller dev and I enjoy supporting groups like them, which makes this an even easier buy)

_childDocuments_.review: A game that throws a lot at you but lacks any depth. There are better Soulslikes that are much, much cheaper. It's linear, punishes exploring or any attempt to break the set path, and has no fun upgrades to look forward to. Visual design is an enticing point, but once gameplay kicks in that falls dead on the floor. Severe lack of enemy or weapon variety combined with armour and upgrades only increasing stats instead of changing the way you play means you'll be fighting the same enemies the same way for a dozen hours long. Some design choices are excessively lazy, with you being able to kick a robot to death but needing an upgrade to kick open a door or crumbling wall, every citizen dialogue being virtually the same and every locale being the exact same (Burning French city with exclusively dead people around).The story starts decent, is a slow mess for most of the rest of the game but ends strong, with multiple options to unlock. A replay is in my opinion not even remotely worth it.Combine this all with the many other complains people have such as performance issues and you got a game that doesn't even remotely hold up to the first Dark Souls, has worse systems, but a higher price tag. Get a different game.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you to the developer Spiders and Publisher Nacon for providing a new fun action game for me to escape, explore and enjoy. *This review also includes the DLC. My steam review rating: PositiveA couple of things first, this is not a souls like game. Second, performance is still weird even 6 months from launch. I tried to lower each option in the graphics setting(low or off) one at a time and nothing would ever change. My solution was to set everything to low and it fixed the problem. The strangest part of that decision, I couldn't tell the difference between max and low settings(besides FPS), none. Steelrising is a reimagining of the French revolution where King Louis and his advisor Caligistro have assembled a robot(called automats) army and declared martial law against all who oppose his rule. In the game you will play as Aegis, a automaton who has been assigned by the King to be the personal guard of his wife Maria Antoinette. Maria and her helper have been exiled by the King to a nearby city as they watch flames and smoke of Paris from afar. Maria worries the King has gone mad from the loss of their young son and is being led astray by others. She orders you to seek out those who understand the automatons' function and to help stop the King. A strong story set up and setting makes for a really great adventure, and it is, but the story is…Ok. There are two major issues that I couldn't ignore. The first is once the King and Caligistro are aware that you(Aegis) are causing all the havoc they could simply have pulled the plug, to avoid some story spoilers. The other major issue is the total lack of any amazement(there is a little) that an automaton has free will of their speech, actions, and thoughts. So much so, Aegis will be asked her opinion on certain political issues multiple times which have consequences to multiple endings the game provides. The story is not the worst ever and with good voice acting, tons of lore, and actually a story that I did find interesting, I think it was just a missed opportunity. This is also magnified by the DLC which feels like a stripped away chapter of the game and would have given some more insight into the real enemy of the game, Caligistro. After receiving your orders to go to Paris you have the ability to customize your look which is minimal and choose between 4 classes: The Alchemist, Bodyguard, Soldier and Dancer. This choice really only affects your starting equipment but keeping an eye on stats and how you distribute points as you go will determine how you want to play. I chose Dancer due to it being the class with fast mobility and agility which is how I like to play these games. Aegis would use light/medium class weapons and be able to dodge(dash) and strike quickly. You of course have a light and heavy attack and if you hold in for the heavy it will give even more damage. As I played through the game multiple times, I tried almost everything and found any class to be fun. As a third person action game, not too much is different from what we have seen the past 10+ yrs in the genre. There is a stamina bar, a very good parry window,  if you die, experience points you have gained will drop at that spot and enemies will respawn. You will be distributing points into 6 categories(I never added any into health on first playthrough) which consist of Power, Vigor, Engineering, Elemental Alchemy, Agility and Durability. There are plenty of weapons to enjoy from dual wield, two handed, guns and others which are all perfect for the steampunk like setting that has been created. Each weapon also will come with unique and different animations for each attack variation. All are very cool and the integration of Aegis' dance moves is pretty awesome. My favorite is probably using the morning star as Aegis will do a ballerina spin move and then kicking it at the enemy.   All combat will be against other automats who come in all shapes, sizes and wielding all sorts of weapons and even musical instruments. The creativity that went into the automats is definitely one of the highlights of the game. The enemy variation however is slim as they all will be used multiple times. As an example, the first enemy may only wield a ball and chain but later the same enemy and weapon will have elemental attacks like electricity, fire or ice included. Also when entering an area you will have a mini boss fight and once you have defeated that enemy they will become part of the rotation you will encounter while exploring. As the game is not the long slog like other titles in the genre, it didn't bother me but a few additional enemy types or just some different animations would have propelled the experience. I was disappointed the dlc did not include new enemies, but just more reskins with a few new tricks. One being a necromancer to raise fallen enemies and one to heal their friends during encounters, yea I'm sure to not be anyone's favorites….ever..As I stated earlier graphically the game looks gorgeous even on the lowest settings but I just have no idea how your system will react. The created world of Paris and surrounding bureaus are fantastic to explore and while a majority are just cobblestone streets, housing complexes and large gov. buildings you will also explore the sewers, a mining operation and grounds of large estates all in a very destructive state. One thing that I did not expect was the verticality and hidden pathways. Some bosses will drop equipment that will allow you to unlock doors, break walls and reach higher areas you encounter on the journey(avoiding spoilers). The DLC does offer a more countryside setting and definitely breaks up the confined city look of the main campaign.  A brief talk on bosses, unlike the common enemies you will engage with the bosses here are all well thought out, unique and fun. There are 8 major must beat bosses with an additional 10 that are tied to side missions. If you are either new or veteran of the genre nothing is really too difficult and unlike others most save locations are seconds away from retrying if you fail. I may have died only a few times until encountering the 2 last bosses(and the DLC) which definitely requires more patience compared to the others.There are actually two ways you can play SteelRising and one is sticking to the main story(no side missions) which will probably take around 15hrs max but if you go down the rabbit hole of exploring and doing all the side missions and DLC it will equate to around 30+hrs. After around 21/2 playthroughs to complete one of my favorite achievement lists, I never was bored or felt like any of my time was wasted. That my friends is what i like to call a good game. PositivesFun, cool action gameUnique story and setting Excellent enemy and weapon creativityFun RPGvaniaSolid combat DLC UI is simple and informativeOne of my favorite achievement lists to 100%Not a 100hr boring slogNegativesWeird graphical performanceSome story elements Enemy varietyNo area maps

_childDocuments_.review: Is Steelrising a good game in the Soulslike genre?No! Unfortunately it isn't. The game has some good approaches and has areas with great attention to detail. But the negative aspects simply took over! Here is a small list.Positive points from my point of view:- the game doesn't have too long of a playing time- beautiful graphics of the clothes and the design of the doll itself- the main bosses were nice- a few options for weapon selectionNegative points from my point of view:- controls are very terrible and clunky, especially at the beginning- combat controls are implemented quite poorly (when dodging you always had to press the button twice, otherwise you would always get 100% hit)- the wayfinding is a joke in this game (you're just running around and searching, unfortunately very confusing)- a Soulslike lives from its opponents, but not from the masses of enemies (there were too many enemies in one place in some places - not that great with the combat system)- the bosses were recycled and then turned into normal mobs, but they were incredible HP sponges- the story was conveyed quite poorly- the cutscenes for the story conversations were far too long and, to be honest, boring- there were NPC conversations in the city that seemed to be secondary tasks - I couldn't solve any of them because it wasn't clear where I could find something to solve them... so much for finding the waySo here is my conclusion:I played through the game - so it's not that bad. But at times I was so annoyed by the pathfinding and the associated jumping mechanics that I won't play this Soulslike game again. On the other hand, it was too “easy”. The main bosses were cool but also quick to kill. So the challenge isn't there and that's a shame.It would be presumptuous to compare this game with big titles like Dark Souls, because that's simply not fair. But I can only say this much, I enjoy playing the other Soulslikes every now and then - but not this one and that actually says it all.Of course, if you want to form your own opinion - then definitely wait for a sale!

_childDocuments_.review: The souls genre has become oversaturated. As with any fattened fandom, this has resulted in widespread subversion, due to the relatively simple concept. People want to give out hot takes and so they will get as subjectively faux-pedantic as possible.  Steel rising is a good game but, you can tell that it's affected by the shifting discourse in the genre. If I had to relate it to a game, it wouldn't be dark souls. It would be Soul Reaver, which is the ancient great grandaddy of darksouls that no one cares to give credit to.  I wouldn't have even marketed this game as a souls-like or even used the out of place 'bonfire' mechanic to pander to 'souls-like fans'. The combat isn't worth dissecting the Spiders classic combat system for. The animations were better and more unique when it launched but they weren't dark soulsy enough for a loud minority of players.  The weapon availability and styles were better when it launched but people cheesed the mechanics and then loudly blamed the game for it. I despise 'souls-like' fans. They don't actually care about gaming or games. They care about sublimating their masochism, rooted in low self esteem, into negativity in online talk spaces. They ruin games, like this one.  It's a single player game. No one cares about your steam 'achievements'.

_childDocuments_.review: The Soulslike genre has created an entry that is incredibly difficult to follow. I put hundreds of hours into Elden Ring while avoiding the rest of the Dark Souls franchise like the plague as intense amount of challenge and difficulty do not generally appeal to me. I don't like the idea of spending six hours on the same boss until I can dodge the right amount of times and kill the thing. No thanks, I have things to do.This game brings in the wondrous "assist mode", which I haven't seen in the likes of Surge or otherwise. You can customize damage reduction and stamina regeneration, both things that are incredibly useful in making the game a lot more playable for casuals like myself. I put it at the middling 50%. I still get punished for not timing dodges while not being killed in two shots, so it's a nice middle ground.So if you know anything about the Soulslike genre you know the deal, here. Challenging and difficult with enemies that pop out of boxes and corners, don't get their attack animations cancelled (while cancelling yours), and large boss setpieces that are most certainly designed with the sense that it will take more than one attempt to figure out. Block, dodge, maybe even parry if that's a thing you can do. I certainly never can, in any game really. Beyond that, there's no need to get detailed with the mechanics as it's all pretty standard fair. Limited potions, refreshes at save points (which also respawn all enemies), and so on.Generally what this genre has to do to set itself apart from others is theme and aesthetic. We're placed in Alternate History Paris where a mechanist invented automatons. You play as Aegis, a feminine Automato special for its ability to speak and think on its own. The intro scene doesn't explain why or how, just that the Queen's aide just says it is so. You're sent off to fix all the things.I don't yet know the full breadth of the story, whether they are actively on the fritz and sacking the city or if they're just doing what they're told... by sacking the city. Much like Bloodbourne (which I only know from Let's Plays), much of the civilian populace is unseen behind boarded up windows that occasionally yell things as you get near. So like most of the genre, a lot of the game feels fairly lonely. It mostly makes up for that with the general aesthetic, spades of Steam or Clockpunk are abound, and if you like the general clicking and whirring of gears you'll be plenty happy here. You can hear every step Aegis makes and patrolling Automat can be heard beyond various walls.Overall, I'm enjoying the game but there are issues.Elden Ring this is not. While you can return to previous areas to farm out experience, this is not an open world rife with activities. There are some side quests spread around for you to look into but it's really just a railroad of a game. A fancier corridor slasher in its own right (like the classic, older Souls games). So don't come in expecting a lot to "do" in general, as it's mostly a game of clearing all the hallways until you stop finding glowy bits to pick up.I have problems with this style of exploration. It's not always clear on which fences are mountable or not. Sometimes you see some messy white paint that denotes a grab-able ledge but it's not universal. Sometimes you just see a broken fence with some greenery all over it but there's nothing distinct about it to tell me that it's an explorable segment. Some ledges and fences look perfectly jumpable but there's a ton of invisible walls because they couldn't figure out any other way to say "there's nothing back there". Much of the city is in ruins so a broken fence just looks like a broken fence to me. Early on you learn about keys and gates and it just made me run into every gated door in the game only to find that there's not even a prompt on most of them so a lot of the times I spend exploring I'm just kissing the perimeter until I see a prompt for... anything.Notably, the game is badly optimized. I tried to record for my youtube but it came out as an unwatchable slideshow. The VRAM useage in-game is not representative of what the game actually uses. While the game itself runs fine on medium settings, it still bogs down my computer to the point where my podcasts on the second monitor start to hiccup and skip, and alt-tabbing makes my computer have a small seizure. At one point, I got a Crash To Desktop by changing some of the settings so even the game itself doesn't like you fiddling around with its inner workings.It's basically a task, the very first thing any player should do is lower the settings.I have this on "Yes" but honestly I would respect anyone waiting for a sale or putting it on follow to let this one cook in the oven for a few more months. There's some merit here, but a lot of calling out in the reviews saying the Devs are being inactive... for two month old game. Maybe they're not communicating as much as they should but let's cross our fingers and hope they work on the optimization. That's the biggest problem here so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This review comes from someone who has 300+ hours in Souls games, Sekiro and Elden Ring, TL;DR below.Where to begin with Steelrising? I am conflicted because I am inclined to recommend this game for all Souls players to experience what can be done better in the genre, but the lack of consistency when it comes to quality does put me on the fence. I have thought really hard on how to write this review, and maybe it is best I present some of the dualities in game quality first:On the one hand, the diegetic inclusion of cutscenes pulls me into the story and increases my involvement; on the other hand the outdated facial animations and abrupt story pacing is further exasperated by said cutscenes. (I have to note here the numerous amount of unexpected story twists that actually surprised me)On the one hand, your character is as mobile as it can be with sprints, dodges, dashes, air attacks and grappling hooks; on the other hand the abysmal enemy variety delimits any experimentation with any gameplay styles.On the one hand, the game surprises the player at every turn with how its world is interconnected and how shortcuts are everywhere; on the other hand every single area can be described as "Urban streets in Revolutionary France" and assets get old quickly.On the one hand, the weapon variety and the levelling system provides a customisable engagement; on the other hand it is both very easy to overlevel which makes the already very easy game, quite very easy (For my run I used a weapon with high attack speed and the ability to deflect, and wanted to mirror my now 4-time-finished Sekiro experience)The game starts out slow and rather boring. You quickly meet with many NPCs and start doing side quests for them, and the momentum of the intrigue and main quest escalates quickly and pulls the player in as they try to navigate the interconnected streets of Paris. During the peak times of the game you are having solid fun with combat-map design-story as the stakes are raised with every quest and new area. You've made mindmaps and can quickly navigate between environments. You try to piece together information that will allow you to deduce what will happen in the next cutscene. Afterwards it slows down to a series of quests that involves a lot, a lot of backtracking through previous areas to just talk to people. Regardless of its shortcomings, Steelrising is encouraging when it comes to experiencing Soulslike variants, and especially puts forth new methods to expand upon the gameplay, at least theoretically. I would not hesitate to buy a potential Steelrising 2, or other Soulslike releases from the same dev. The game would have been an instant buy only if, instead of an "Assisted Difficulty" option that decreases the difficulty, it had a "Hardcore" mode with bigger and better enemies. TL;DR: Buy this game if you are not a Soulslike player. Buy this game if you are a Souls player and are curious about viable advancements for the genre when it comes to story and game design and don't mind the fact that like out of 15 bosses in total only 3 of them are really unique.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm enjoying this, great visuals, decent performance and interesting story. Sometimes the camera and controls feel a bit sloppy but it's not terrible and certainly not game breaking, just requires some getting used to. Once you learn the cadence and rhythm of combat getting into a flow comes fairly naturally. It follows the souls formula well but is far less challenging, consider it a casual souls like. This is a good thing as I think more players will find it more accessible, it's a decent entry into the souls-like genre. It could use some polishing, which I'm sure will come with future patches. All settings at high or ultra except for shadows and shadow distance, ray tracing enabled. Getting 60-80fps on a 3080 10gb with DLSS set to balanced at 4k. Without DLSS I get mid 30's.Overall I'm having fun with this so far and would recommend it, but I'm only 3hrs in so you decide what thats worth.

_childDocuments_.review: My first review, yay.I just finished my second playthrough, the first being regular and the second with NG+. Some pros and cons to my experiences regarding both.Pros:I picked this game for a few reasons, being the beautiful character model of Aegis, the premise, and the fact that it looked like a less intense Soulslike game. I've been wanting to try the genre, and I felt like this would have enough going for it to keep me playing while learning the ropes, which it did.During my first playthrough, I eventually decided to turn on the Assist Mode because I felt like I wasn't having a good time learning the Soulslike mechanics without dying constantly. Roast me if you want. I really appreciated the Assist Mode because it did let me learn the mechanics of attack timing, stamina, and better resource management, which I'm frankly not as used to in most other games I've played.I unknowingly picked what's been deemed as the most difficult class to start for new Soulslike players, being Alchemist. I've had a good time with that class, and the batons that are associated with the class are right up my alley for a faster attacking play style. I'm going to use a third playthrough to try out the heavier weapons.I do feel like the game is scaled pretty well as you go through.I think the story is pretty good.Cons:I don't know the specs of my computer, and I know there are known optimization issues with the game, dropping frames, sudden closing of the game, etc. I'm pretty understanding that this is both because my computer isn't the most optimized, and that issues can occur unknowingly after publishing a game.Some of the achievements are still locked for me, notably the  and  achievements. I'm pretty sure I should've also gotten  and  achievements as well, but maybe I missed something in those achievements.While your main character is really well made (just the velvet on the armor pieces is immaculate to look at), I can't say the same for most of the human characters. There's some janky facial animation during the cutscenes that are in that uncanny valley spectrum. Monseigneur de Le Fare barely opens his mouth, even during high energy dialogue, for example.I do wish the world (well at least this context, this region including Paris), was more open world with each of the areas connected and there was a more proper mount to travel with. Imagine, an automaton horse to ride on and attack with.One more con that contains spoilersAnd with both the pros and cons, I don't think currently it's worth what I payed for it, but I do believe it could be if these aspects were tightened up.Overall, a solid 7/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10. Overall a decent Souls-inspired game. On the positive side, the graphics are amazing, the setting and locations are interesting (the first 5 hours at least), and the combat, while at times clunky, is quite fun. On the negative side, France and the French, the side quests are unnecessarily confusing to get to, the level design is extremely linear (and yet confusing), and the enemy variety is quite limited, which adds to the fact that the whole game is set in basically the same city, makes the experience repetitive after the first 5 hours or so. Having said that, the gameplay is compelling enough to finish the game without getting too fatigued. I wouldn't say this is a Souls-like game as it lacks the combat depth, the open-ended and interconnected level design, the challenging difficulty, memorable boss fights, and environmental storytelling. nevertheless, it is a fun, lighthearted experience with a pinch of Souls flavor with substance and a lot of heart.
