_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I want to preface my review with the fact that I've enjoyed every minute I've played. I'm running on a gaming laptop from 2016 and still capable of playing on custom graphics on a mixture of ultra, medium and low config settings. That being said, this games optimisation for PC is very lacklustre. The gameplay itself is quite fun and rewarding, if not just a touch shallow. The latter boss unlocks allowing for alchemical attacks provide a good way to open up for elemental damage for non alchemist starting profiles. I've enjoyed the setting, the atmosphere, the story and the characterisation of the historical figures; and I appreciate the accentuation of the Voice acting. All in all, the game itself has been quite a fun experience overall for me since my purchase; and I have been lucky enough to skip a lot of the problems a lot of other people in the reviews have had to experience. All of this being said, my experience with the title has been utterly ruined by a single glitch that has completely stalled my progress through the campaign. In MontMatre, after defeating the Centaur; there is a Lift. After doing some of the side quests and going to find the final echo for the coffin before said lift, I decided to be a derp and leave aegis under the descending Lift. This proceeded to kill Aegis. I expected this. What I did Not Expect was upon returning to the lift, it was fully recalled to the top of it's ascent path; and the lift lever that calls it down to descend is completely inoperable. This completely has forestalled my progress in the campaign. I've reloaded the save, restarted the game. tried fast travelling to other areas in the game and coming back. None of these have made the lift lever operable. For this reason alone I am giving the game a negative review, as the devs have clearly not even been bothered to think that their players might try to stand under lifts, and seeing as this specific lift is the single route to one of the final areas of the game; it completely halts all progress of a campaign. A major oversight of the design phase and truly unforgivable in my own opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing, beating, and doing some side stuff, i can say that Steelrising is a great soulslike with some bad gameplay designs and decisions.First the positives. It looks fantastic! The detail in the world, the designs, the animations, everything is great to look at. Weapon animations in particular are downright gorgeous, even if the weapon variety is a little baron. Controls are tight, allowing for great movement in fights, and with the gameplay being more attuned to Bloodborne, speed is your best friend. Weapons feel top tier, hitting enemies is satisfying regardless of the weapon you choose, and with the addition of more modern features introduced in Sekiro and Elden Ring, jump attacks, critical hits, staggering, charge attacks, are all here and all great. Lets get to the juicy part, the bad. As mentioned, Steelrising is visually a very good looking game, but this comes at the cost of system requirements and performance across the board. I own a 3080ti, and the performance is decent, but seeing videos on people playing with even the 1080ti, i can see why people are complaining about performance. The story is so damn boring, that i rush through the dialogue at every opportunity, and thank god i do since some of these conversations can go on, and on, and on. Difficulty is either easy... Or incredibly easy. This all depends on whether or not you use the most broken thing i have ever seen in a soulslike. Steelrising's frost mechanic. Its insanely overpowered from the start, and only gets better when you level up weapons and find heavy weapons to synergize its effect. Freeze an enemy, swap to a another weapon, charge attack, profit. Even when not using this broken combo, the enemies have some tracking issues when it comes to dashing around them. None of these are honestly bad, but after hitting max level with my heavy and ice weapons, the game's bosses are literal jokes.One last thing to note is the price and how people are up in arms about it. $50 is steep, yes, but this isn't a unity asset flip. Its not a retro game with a minimalism style. Its a full fledged game that took alot of time and effort from an indie company to make look and feel Triple A as they possibly could with what they had. Its not fair for people to assume $1=1 hour or some nonsense like that. Is the game Elden Ring good? Of course not! Elden Ring had 100+ people working 5+ years, its safe to say Steelrising does not. the company needs money to fuel future projects of equal or greater scale, and i think $50 is fair considering most soulslikes are honestly pretty damn bad or lesser copies of the original inspiration. I really liked Steelrising, a few issues, but i would 100% recommend this if you're looking for a Bloodborne-like.

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice and unique addition to souls-like genre by Spiders (their first). I enjoyed the game a lot: atmosphere, overall design and setting, but the best part in my opinion is a really fun gameplay. It is not hard or challenging once I understand how it works, but it is always immensely satisfying. So much so that I overlooked repetitive combat encounters and lack of enemy variety. The story is set in alternative version of Paris during French revolution, except, robots are everywhere. Historical is mixed with fantastical in interesting way and it all fit together nicely as I was uncovering what was happening bit by bit from conversations with many characters and doing some side quests. Yes, game has many well written side quests that have effect on ending of the game.The world of the game, mostly city of Paris, is separated to multiple enclosed levels. Each of them is vast and interconnected with a lot of hidden and not yet accessible areas and also visually unique (some more than others considering its mostly one city).There are a lot of small, but interesting features that enhanced my experience, like game pausing automatically after cinematic ends if I switched to second monitor in meantime or unique ways of dealing with elemental damage (except electricity for some reason). And many others I'm sure, that just don't come to mind.Overall I had a great time with the game, it is not super polished AAA experience, but that is not to be expected. The biggest issue I had was questionable optimization and really uneven performance, where I had  60+ fps in one level and barely 40 in other.

_childDocuments_.review: Just don't. This is not worth your time, money or attention.Performance is terrible and textures look so low-res that they rival the PS1 for fidelity if they even load properly at all, Gameplay feels awful and far too stiff, There's absolutely no variety whatsoever once you've finished the tutorial as almost every single weapon type and enemy type is found in the tutorial, Armour (clothing) is literally pointless as none of them actually appear to do anything of actual valueLight (agility in-game) weapons are the only ones of value due to the "immobilisation" mechanic demanding repeating hits to get "critical" hits (backstabs, basically), making the entire heavy category pointlessRanged attacks are worse than useless,Only the frost elemental damage serves a function as fire and lightning appear to do literally nothing, where frost damage locks enemies in place for big hits and the majority of enemies are vulnerable to it AND you get a reliable way to deal frost damage in the tutorial and another after the first major boss which puts you into melee range,There's only 8 bosses in the entire game. Only 8, and with each district only taking about 30 minutes to get through even while looking for pickups (most of which are useless items which give you currency), you'll fight the first three (which give you the mobility upgrades) within about three hours,The story is a mess and has absolutely ZERO catharsis since it's so unbelievably predictable that it could genuinely be a Dora the Explorer episode for how simplistic everything is. The plot thread regarding who/what Aegis is is literally resolved as soon as you achieve the second major objective of the game if you have two braincells to rub together and can do enough critical thinking to make a prediction.Every historical character you meet in the game is weirdly off-kilter. Somehow at one point, famous abolitionist Lafayette is talking about how he owns slaves and how much profit they make directly to Julien Raimond, a black slave owner who justifies his own ownership of slaves in the same conversation, and the game entirely unironically paints Robespierre as an incorruptible (a laughably bad take) figure of truth, justice and liberty. For a game made by French people, they absolutely do not appear to have any pride for French history if they're getting things THAT wrong. And yeah, yeah, it's an AU where robots exist, but beyond that they're all real people being portrayed, and yet here Spiders are portraying Marie Antoinette as a good person and fully justified in their dismissal of the peasantry rather than a flighty gambling addict so detached from reality that she was LITERALLY a traitor to France.TLDR: Don't buy this. Even on sale it's not worth your money. I finished it in just over 10 hours, and even THAT was too long for such a waste of developer time and my money. The DLC isn't worth your money either, as it's literally two reskin bosses, two reskin weapons and ONE new gimmick weapon and boss in an area that looks like every other area of the game and STILL doesn't have any catharsis as the bad guy STILL gets away.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play and visuals of this game are amazing.The story is filled with plot holes, way too much exposition, and is incredibly anticlimactic.There is also a fair amount of backtracking and what feels like filler. you get two ways to transverse the landscape but are still very limited to where you can actually go, and considering there is no map it can get kinda confusing. I really liked the combat, its souls like Victorian clockwork, but the story and the end of the game feel very rushed. The voice lines are really well done, there is just so much of it. I heavily dislike that stores have a finite amount of ammo for sale per area. I did have a surplus for most of the game, but it means if you where to stick around to grind, you could go through all of them. I also did not have to grind, other then a few times where i wanted to level up new gear I just found. otherwise most bosses where killed on first try. I really loved the automate styles and different units. in reality there are only a handful of robot types but each have sub groups with different ascetics and varied attacks. Gear is varied and has a bunch of different styles and speeds. the modals work like rings from a souls like, and clothing changes your stats and armor (but lack a weight system). There is also a New Game Plus that introduces new enemy's and gear.Get it on sale if your interested, but do not expect a good story.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting combination of Bloodborne and Vampyr formulas, making a unique take on the souls genre. Game looks good when looked upon from far away, but a lot of texture and lighting problems come to light when going through dark areas, or areas that are close to a very bright light source, making quite a lot textures and lighting look out of place.Story is very mild. Nothing interesting happens, and after a certain point of the game you get a lot of unnecessary exposition and downright uninteresting comments. The same goes with citizens around the map, where almost all of them act the same way towards you. Voice acting is not bad at all, but the animation during talking cutscenes is subpar at best. However, I did not like the way they portrayed important choices throughout the game, and sometimes picking one of them can happen by mistake in the midst of combat/progression.I did dislike the limit of weapon and armor choices. Very limited, and most of them (weapons) play the same if they are from the same class. For example, I played the bodyguard class, where heavy slow weapons are the thing, but there are only 4 of them in game, and all of them have the same moveset and attacks, just different damage values and specials. As for the armor sets, only two armor sets are made for the heavy class, one that I used for around 80% of the playthrough until I found the other one a lot later in the game, near the end. Standard enemies feel fine, but I really disliked the bosses. Game has two version of bosses, the mini and the real ones. Mini ones are just corrupted versions of the regular enemies that have increased stats and that block your next checkpoint until defeated...and to be honest, they don't deserve to be called bosses at all in my opinion. The real bosses are rare, and only a few of them exist in the game (around 7). They are interesting, but only one of them is great, the others are almost on-paar with some of the more dangerous mini-bosses.In the end, I cannot really recommend this game, but also cannot say that I did not like it. It had it's moments, good and bad, but in the end it was not really dull nor did it have amazing moments at any point. It could have used a lot more work and polish.Overall, it is a solid 7.5/10I would like to see a similar project from the devs, but I would also want to see the above mentions improved, especially the weapon/armor selection.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only this is a great souls like, it's a great game overall. The combat is good with some tweaks to the system with interesting weapons. I didn't use all of them, but the halberds had cool animations with nice combos even being medium/heavy weapons. There are no, of at least very few invincibility frames during dodges so it took a bit of time to get used to it, but not a big deal for the way enemies act. The maps are super detailed, big and intricate with several shortcuts. It's not one huge map like the souls games, more like huge areas you can travel to, but they are so big that I didn't mind.The game is absolutely gorgeous, but optimization is its achiles' heels. I managed to run it on high on my 3060 and even then it wasn't quite enough, while I can play heavier and newer games on max quality with no problems unless I turn on raytracing. One of its top points though is the story. It actually grabbed my attention and I was curious to see how they would fit it in the French Revolution context. It was a nice mix of history and fiction with known characters but with a puppet plot very similar to Lies of P. If you consider the optimization problems that got the game its mixed reviews, consider buying it on Sale. I bought it very cheap on a steam sale and I had a blast with it. I finished the game near the 22h mark, but if I try to go for the platinum I extimate easily another 10h or even more, the game has multiple endings and a new game plus so it actually incentivize you to have another run with different weapons.Overall a very solid experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not had any performance issues, there were a couple texture loading issues that I experienced but nothing bad, and the game was easily playable for me. I have a Ryzen 5800, RTX 3070, 16 gigs of ram, running the game off of an SSD.First off, I understand what the devs were trying to do with the mechanical feel in trying to make you feel like an automaton. Unfortunately, it doesn't feel GOOD. I don't think it's more important to feel like a robot than it is for the game to be fluid and fun. Something about just moving around feels kind of glitchy and stiff. When you're designing the feel/look of a heavy machine, you need to think about POWER rather than stiffness. Again, I understand the stiff feel they're going for, but in my opinion, it is not executed very well. Machines might be a bit stiffer, but they're also REALLY HEAVY and POWERFUL. I think it would be better to shift the focus away from a stiff feel and more into a powerful, weighty, feel. Longer charge ups, bigger slams.This made the game feel a bit unfun to play at a base level.The reason I'm refunding is because of the hitboxes. After upon reaching the first boss (the tall robot that summoned normal enemies as minions) I realized that, at least that boss, has really bad hitboxes. I was getting hit a lot when I wasn't anywhere near the robots attacks, and even after dodging through some of them. It could be that I was just not timing dodges properly, I was playing with muscle memory from my experience with Dark Souls and other souls-like games, and it did me no good here. I simply can't play without feeling like I'm getting hit when I'm not supposed to. Maybe Dark Souls is such a huge part of how I see video games these days that it makes me unable to appreciate other forms of combat and their small differences, but unfortunately, unless this issue is fixed, I don't see myself enjoying this game.Aside from that, atmosphere, graphics, it all seemed pretty good. Some of the animations were smooth too, I like the feeling of injecting the oil vial (estus flask) and the ledge grab/jump up animation you do when grabbing ledges is smooth. I'm sure theres a lot to appreciate in this game, but you have to be able to play enough to get there and see them, and I can't play the way it is now.

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say what Steelrising is not: it is *not* Nioh.  That anyone is making that comparison is baffling.  I realize we can only draw points of reference from what we've played, but If I had to pick a game this is most adjacent to I'd say Bloodborne.  I also think it does *just* enough to be it's own thing.  So, if you are a fan of action RPGs such as Dark Souls will you like Steelrising? I think so.  Spiders has done maybe some of their best work yet, gameplay wise, and I'll admit it's nice to get out of generic fantasy.  If you wanted Bloodborne but with a French Steampunk aesthetic, here you go.I think it's worth noting who it *won't* appeal to: if you just finished Elden Ring and want another 120 hour, poorly balanced epic with hundreds of choices to make for your character build: this ain't it.  Steelrising as a game is fine, but if your expectations are that it's going to rival the top dog in terms of content and presentation then save yourself the heartache and pass it up.  If, however, you like the genre and you could go for more?  You'll find that here.  If you are usually put off by these games for those very reasons, this also might just be the one to ease you into the genre.  I'll go ahead and say it as well: I'm fine when games don't need hundreds of hours to beat.  Sometimes you just want to play a game you like and finish it.  The content here is solid.As for what sets it apart from a basic Bloodborne clone?  Well, it's source inspiration is pretty bald faced, but you can chain attacks, jumps and dodges more easily and you have a more generous stamina bar.  There are other small tweaks but in general it just feels a lot "softer" than Souls-likes usually do.  Your movements are still very deliberate, it's *nowhere* as fast paced as Team Ninja's offerings, but they are less restrictive.  You unlock traversal abilities that also open up some options in combat.  You have equipment choices, but you aren't going to agonize over it.  That's not to say it isn't challenging, just that it lets you get away with a bit more and asks for a bit less.  Fans of the genre will feel right at home with *just* enough tweaks to help it have its own identity and, personally, it's challenge is just right.  If you let your guard down, you'll get your teeth kicked in, but rely on those old instincts and you'll find it very manageable.  Now if you'll excuse me, I have a game to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear god, I was in despair after almost 5 hours of playing. But then I remembered watching a streamer fight Malenia with a RL1, I even watch (not entirely) Kai's 100+ hour Elden Ring. They kept losing and trying again and again, and I realized I need to play with patience. So yeah, it works for me (in this game).My first play took about 12 hours, including several side quests, reading a bit of lore, and unlocking the 1st ending. 2nd play was NG+ took 11 hours, it was for unlocking some achievements, learning more about the lore, collecting all echoes, and somehow got 3rd ending. I wasn't sure how I did it, but it showed that your choices do matter. There are three endings in total.I agree that Steelrising is not too difficult (after my first 5 hours, of course), but it does have some very challenging moments. The game features Immobilisation, which the enemies get stunned when the diamond is filled, allowing you to hit a critical attack. You can use throwable bombs like flame to ignite, frost to freeze, and explosive goes explode. I chose the Dancer class and my favorite weapons are Armoured Fans and Requiem Mallet.There are Unstable bosses and main bosses. The Unstable bosses weren't very hard for me, though I died 2-4 times. However, the two main bosses, The Selenite and The Bishop gave me motion sickness. The rest were a mix, some 1st try, others took 2-5 runs. If the game is too hard, you can always turn on assist mode, but I decided not to use it to see how far I could go on my own.Overall, I enjoyed the story, the combat, the character design, and the world. The only issue was the performance. But if the game were more polished, it would be amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it! A fun, engaging experience that was not too difficult, but did require some attention and focus. I had a great time with the game, and while I probably wouldn't want a direct sequel, as the story is already self-contained, I'd absolutely check out the studio's next iteration on their ideas.What I loved: Boss designs! These bosses were extremely creative, absolutely marvelous, amazing spectacles. I really cannot properly phrase just how incredible the main bosses were. They were also all very well balanced, providing a reasonable challenge but not halting your progress for 30 hours.  Atmosphere and world design! Steampunk Paris looks truly fantastic. I often stopped to admire the detailed buildings, fountains, all sorts of decorations and miscellaneous objects. It's clear a lot of love went into the graphical presentation, and it's a great experience to go through it. The idea of combining robots with French revolution politics is a surprisingly well working combination. Not only does it add a unique style to the whole game, it also provides enough room for all sorts of stories and mini-tales weaved into the game. I really like the overall creativity that is behind every corner, every important mechanic, and every design decision. What I didn't really like: Some parts of the level design were a bit troublesome to go through. I do like to explore and find my way through a world, but some paths were really not apparent at all, and sadly, are absolutely crucial for progression, as all levels are made as little labyrinths, with only one correct way through them. I missed a certain small story-related part of the game near the start, and this snowballed beyond my imagination. Me missing this one thing maybe 1/8th into the playthrough eventually resulted in a certain NPC not appearing where he was needed for an important side-quest. I went back and finally got the NPC to move to the right spot, but by that point the side-quest broke and I couldn't progress. Note this was the only side-quest I managed to break, so it's not some huge issue, on the other hand I wanted to finish all side-quests and got blocked because of some small thing I missed out on 15 hours earlier, which is never fun. It's also true that enemies start to repeat about mid-way through the game. Although it's not a big deal, it does get somewhat repetitive at times, especially when coupled with the level design which always makes sure to drag you through every location in the longest route possible. But I totally understand the reasoning behind why that ended up being the way it is.I can't comment much on the technical state of the game. I experienced 2 crashes and 1 minor visual (repeating) bug throughout the whole game, so I can't complain. It was a fun game, and I was surprised by just how well made it was! Definitely a good experience!

_childDocuments_.review: A solid soulsborne game with some interesting ideas, but also some flaws that are hard to overlook.Things I loved:1. The concept of "fighter doll" is, let's be real guys, just awesome. Not only the design is cool, the "built-in" mechanism made the choreography weirdly satisfying. 2. For a game with a 10-15 hour-ish playthrough, the build variety in this is pretty good. Every build has its own potent choice of weapon, with moderately balanced power.3. The learning curve feels satisfying. You can feel a bit frustrated at first, but once you found the right weapon/build for your, the difficulty decreases significantly (however, this might ruin your experience for being too easy).4. The voice acting throughout the character development. Something really subtle but you do appreciate it once you hear it.Things I think needed improvements:1. The fighting mechanism is a bit "dense". With no moveset-related perks/skills/talents, no cancel-animation, and hyper-armour for nearly every enemy, the game felt very punishing for being (even just moderately) aggressive. Also, the highly emphsised riposte mechanism was surprisingly niche, since lots of enemies has (delayed) attacks with extended or multiple hit-boxes (+the hyper-armour that will just blunt force through your counter-attack).2. The scaling in new game + felt a bit off. Opening new level cap was nice, but it just turned the new playthroough into "either I one-shot you, or you one-shot me". 3. The story, except for Aegis' personal story line, lacks in engagement. Overall, a nice game to play while waiting another game from FromSoft.

_childDocuments_.review: For me Steelrising is my favourite example of a soulslike made outside of From Software and sits on a level as Sekiro for me in terms of tone and visual style, as well as accessibility into the genre. The spectacular alternative history backdrop of France around Louis XVI is a delightful way of getting people interested in the events and people of the French Revolution, and that’s backed with some of the most enjoyable and distinctive level and environment design that I have seen in a long while in this genre, and he soundtrack is one of the best of this year. I love the side quests, I love the characters you interact with, the mechanics work very well (for the most part, I prefer the tight hit boxes of Elden Ring, but hey, you can't have everything). For me, if it hadn't come out in the same year as Elden Ring, then it would have gotten my award for the best soulslike of the year -- actually, let's not mess around, Steelrising IS my soulslike GOTY!

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a pretty fun Soulslike that benefits from its historical domain characters and alternative reality/history setting against the backdrop of the impending French revolution - definitely not an overused setting - which bring the scenario to life in a way that other Soulsbornes usually don't. It is understandable considering the voiced protagonist - though a little regrettable IMHO - that there are limits to customising the player character as far as appearance is concerned, though that should not distract from your experience. As far as combat, the main gameplay, goes, I'd say right now that the weapons feel a bit imbalanced to me, with the use of fast weapons working out much better than slower, more powerful weapons. System-wise, I have had some stability issues, with intermittent crashes to desktop, but since the game constantly saves and updates progress, there hasn't really been a loss in progress. All in all, definitely worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a medium rating to this, but I will give this a thumbs up in good faith. There is a lot to love in this game fighting with a lot to dislike.FIRST OFF TO ALL THE PEOPLE WITH PERFORMANCE ISSUES:If you move the setting to ultra, Ray Tracing will be turned on which will TANK you FPS. If you are 100+FPS on 1440p on high, going to Ultra may drop you to 60FPS and less on busy battles.You can still play on ultra, but once you change the setting, go to advance graphics and turn Ray Tracing back off. If you have an RTX card, you can play with DLSS to see if you can do some balance if you, for some reason, want the Ray Tracing feature on. CP2077 does this too, but they give you a setting of Ultra + Ray Tracing to avoid the mega drop in FPS.I am playing on 4k, Ultra settings, no Ray Tracing, DLSS on balanced and I maintain a steady 60 FPS. My GPU is a 3080ti combined with Ryzen 5900x...so your mileage may vary.That part out of the way, the game is overall solid. This game shares a lot of DNA with Bloodborne (sans the hit back to heal mechanic), so if that is your jam, you make like this. I will give some quick points on what I enjoyed and what I really think can be improved in the game:POSITIVE:-Aegis mechanical model is beautiful. The way her plates are rendered is very natural, you can FEEL she is a machine made of gold, or steel, or marble depending on the character creation. A+ on this...you can tell the devs put a lot of love into her design.-Combat animations are interesting and varied, and they kick-ass making you FEEL strong. Several weapon types have moves that pierce, slash, or smash enemies, and the devs really spend time making you feel like a badass at it. Most charge attacks make Aegis do some additional animations that are just down right cool. It's like, ballet that can kill. Solid A here.-Environments are rich and well artistically developed, which makes the immersion grip you. Deep green forest and gardens, muddy streets, graveyards, and everything is designed to be natural and realistic with god rays peeking in different places. The whole design is congruous to the game's aesthetics and it really sucks you in. Another Solid A.NEGATIVE:-The cooling system is a good idea, but it doesn't add much to combat. I think the mentality here was to give the game something like "Active Time Reload" in other games like Gears of War or Guardians of the Galaxy. If Aegis runs out of stamina, she overheats and needs to cool down, and you can do a "minigame" to get the cooling down at the right time. Problem is in the heat of battle, it's hard to pay attention to it. While you are managing enemies, weapons, healing, stamina, and countless other things, the last thing the player need is "oh damn, now I gotta add ONE more mechanic." I think they wanted this mechanic to make the game have a key point to say "HEY! We do something real different than other soulslikes with combat!"I think the idea was good, but like other games that have a mechanic like this (reload/regain stamina with proper timing), I think the cool down could have an icon in the center of the screen, so when it pops, the players eyes do not deviate from the action. Games like this can kill you if you are not paying attention, so don't add a mechanic that introduces distractions the players cannot always predict. I think if it gets a bit more of a revamp, it can moved to a positive (it would have been cool to see Aegis body really heat and vent steam as the overheat approaches).-Yanky hit boxes. I HATE THIS ONE. In the first miniboss, there are piles of body's on the ground and sometimes you can walk on top of them (like you scaling a small mountain) and sometimes you get STUCK on them (like if they were a wall). I also randomly get stuck on the environmental features (like logs or tress) even when Aegis' model is clearly out of the way. This makes some encounters frustrating as I died to being stuck on nothing...and that is incredibly frustrating in these types of games since precision is key. It feels bad when you are dodging an enemy and then get randomly stuck and die. You didn't make a mistake, but you are punished for it.-The voice acting (minor issue). The voices are mostly okay, and the models are mostly okay, but put them together is awkward to watch. Just the intro scene, characters sound calm but their models are agitated like there is a sense of urgency, and sometimes it's the other way around.-Aegis' movement is awkward when traversing, and she doesn't have physical impact in the world (minor issue). When you walk slow, Aegis' model looks great, when you sprint, it looks fine, but when you just run and you turn left and right, Aegis' looks like a top moving left and right on it's axis. It makes you feel like you are turning more than you really are. Also, when Aegis moves through bushes, she doesn't move anything in the foliage. when she walks on mud, or dirt, her feet do not cause any dirt or anything to kick up. It almost make her seem like she is flying.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is undeniably janky, and I've not completed it yet, but what I've seen in the 5 or so hours I've played so far i've found enjoyable. I would call myself a souls veteran but this game has been a nice change to be honest. After the honestly frustrating slog that was the last third of elden ring, and the constant need for perfection in sekiro, a slower and more easy/forgiving soulslike has been welcome.- The game's optimization is probably poor, but with my relatively mid rig its been running quite well (ryzen 7 3700x, rtx 4060).- The dialogue sounds honestly janky, and Aegis especially feels very strange, but for her at least it kind of adds to the doll charm for me. - Some enemy attacks feel pretty unfair, with damage hitboxes appearing practically instantly to deal damage without windup, and some attacks where it really feels like i was outside the attack range but took damage.Overall i've very much enjoyed what i've seen, and i've been wishing for a game where you get to play as a doll (actual doll, instead of the completely human P from lies of P). So yeah I really hope we'll get more like this in the future, hopefully with more bloodborne style worldbuilding perhaps?

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable, especially as a Lies of P followup, though not as polished and satisfying. Gorgeous main character who looks like an actual puppet as a bonus, great weapon options and beautiful souls fashion. Difficulty level is easy if you've played other soulslikes. Many bosses including the final one can be first-tried, summons are not available, or needed, many cheese options like bombs can be ignored for the entirety of the game. It has an open world feel since you can, and must, revisit some areas because they can only be unlocked once you find a certain weapon/tool. There are some amusing glitches, like picking up loot 15x without clearing the prompt, enemies getting stuck in doors, and less amusing ones like an unholy amount of rubble for Aegis to get stuck on during combat, or the game crashing while she twitches on a fence. Also didn't enjoy having her auto-access the boss areas once she came close enough, or the autostarting of some cutscenes which prevented exploring and even finishing a certain quest during the ending.  The larger areas are rather badly and thoughtlessly interconnected with many unlockable doors and barriers, and can be lengthy to navigate, sometimes I didn't find my way back to the vestal or to the place I was looking for, and had to run in circles while fighting the same monsters over and over. Some rooms/corners feel too samey and like added fluff without contributing much to the worldbuilding. History lovers will enjoy meeting French Revolution celebrities and get to know them a little. Kudos to the La Fayette voice actor for the nice voice and flawless pronounciation in both English and French. Players who dont care about the story might skip everything, but they will miss out on a lot of cool details and getting  different endings.In summary: combat is easy, maybe too easy, map is too convoluted, the game should have been optimised more before release. But I would play a part 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a fun game despite it's flaws.You are playing as robot girl, you can customize the face, hair, and skin tone. Then you will get to choose starting class, although it doesn't really matter mid-late game because you have plenty time to change your playstyle.The combat is okay, just like dark souls game. The stamina bar runs out really quickly at the beginning of the game and you can do rapid cooling to restore it momentarily while in combat (need timing). The combat pace is slow, giving you plenty time to react. Block & counter is only available when using certain weapons. Dodge is always an option. You also have alchemy bullet to use alchemical skills. Bomb is also very good.The area is dominated in the city of France, so you are going to spend most of your time in the ruined city. The architecture is interesting enough, and the feel of each area is distinct enough, so not really a problem.You can upgrade weapon, potion, status. You also have some skills but you need to progress further in the game, it can help you traverse the map and fight. The story is slow at the beginning, you don't know anyone or where the story is going. But it picks up mid game when you finally get the sense of the situation and the people. It's interesting enough when you are invested in it.Now the negatives based on my opinion,1. The GPU load is high, even using RTX 4050 6GB, i can only play on 1920p low to get consistent 60-70 FPS with DLSS Ultra Performance :) and you don't want low frame in games like this...so that's a bummer. It doesn't make sense why the GPU load so high, the visual isn't that revolutionary...2. Bugs and lot's of them, stuck when running, the pop up menu disappearing, drop item visual cues not disappearing, freezed animation at cutscene, etc.3. Side quest, you don't know when you are supposed to do certain side quest, because certain side quest is actually locked before you progress the main quest, so good luck wasting time trying to complete it because you are not supposed to yet...4. The combat feels weird until you get used to it, i think this is also because of the GPU load, making the game feel sluggish if you don't have adequate GPU (6 GB is REALLY the minimum).I recommend trying it if it's on sale, and make sure your GPU at the very minimum have 6GB or it's unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: If the game stayed as good as it is at the start, I'd recommend it. Unfortunately the longer it goes on the worse it gets. It's a beautiful game with decent combat, although heavy weapons feel terrible here and fast weapons are king (bizarrely all weapons are classed as either heavy or medium, there's no light class for some reason), and a lot of effort went into the mechanical designs being both fun to fight and interesting to look at.Unfortunately by the time you're 1/3 through the game you will have already seen all but one or two of the standard enemies it has to offer. Even though it's only about 20 hours long it feels like an utter slog after a point because of the horrible lack of enemy variety leaving you fighting the same things over and over regardless of locale, and the player is able to quickly become so strong that enemies don't even pose a challenge, especially since there are so few movesets to familiarise yourself with.The few abilities you have to move around the environment aren't really that special; you can only use the grapple at a handful of select points in each level so it's basically a non-factor, while the wall break is even less useful, but I do appreciate that they all have uses in combat with distinct ailment effects tied to them so I was making use of all of them in combat towards the end of the game.The story is undoubtedly the worst part here, being a dull mess of cardboard characters that talk too much and say too little. Cutscenes frequently interrupt exploration and rarely offer anything interesting to make them worth sitting through. The ending of the game is laughably bad,  The game having quests that see you constantly running back and forth across environments that aren't particularly designed for speedy traversal and various locations being locked behind keys that only appear through such quests doesn't help the exploration feel rewarding, nor does the fact that 99% of items you find throughout the game are just consumables and ammo, with actual gear being relegated to only sparse chests.There was definitely a good core here and I was impressed by the visual design of the game, and the combat certainly isn't bad, particularly as far as Souls-likes go, but there just isn't enough meat here. Oh and it isn't very well optimised either; the frame pacing is awful and swapping from high settings to low made effectively no difference to performance.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after completing it:This game is like the film Tenet. A silly, but fun concept that looks pretty good until it sticks around way too long and dies huffing it's own farts. It was fun for a while, but became painfully repetitive, the mazelike levels are utterly painful to have to constantly backtrack through, what you can and can't pass through/ jump over is awfully janky, quests can bug and become impossible to complete for no reasons, and the story is embarrassing, boring, and utterly misguided. Credits rolled and I said, "thanks, I hate it" and unistalled it. I no longer recommend this game. Original Review:My feelings towards this game are powerfully ambivalent with a positive leaning simply because the gameplay is so much fun.The Good:The concept and aesthetics of steampunk regency France is undeniably brilliant and is largely pulled off. The classic Soulslike elements, Souls, bonfires, respawning enemies, enemies that hit like trucks, and bosses that are even bigger than said trucks, are all there and work well, actually integrated into the world and story in ways that surpass some others in the genre  The addition of the more fluid movement and combat from more traditional action adventure games is a fun addition.The art design, at least for Aegis, weapons, outfits, and enemies, is genuinely wonderful and works beautifully with the steampunk nightmare regency era France.The elemental mechanics are fun (though it's easy to lean into ice and paralysis and not have to really think about the rest or use any of the protective fluids). The Bad:The story is actually offensive in a number of ways. The actual writing of the narrative and dialogue is just interminably dull and longwinded without saying anything at all. The easiest thing to compare it to is all the politics and trade embargo discussion from The Phantom Menace. It also just slows everything down without actually adding anything to it because, ultimately they are just saying go here, do this, king bad, automats scary, with the occasional bit of French and waving a frilly collar at the idea of the French Revolution. I wish I wasn't so neurodivergent that it is impossible for me to watch every cutscene and choose every dialogue option (less options, rather a checklist of things to cover with no actual choice, outside of don't say all the things), but you truly do not have to. This really is an extension of the last, but it is so egregious it needs its own point. The handling of politics, discussion of slavery, plantations, capitalism, and the French Revolution itself are embarrassing and offensive. There's no other way to describe it. It's milquetoast liberal sanitised state education word vomit with no understanding of the history and motivations for the revolution, and absolutely no intention of sticking its head above the political parapet beyond easily agreed statements like slavery bad and maybe people shouldn't be starved and murdered. The mind truly boggles. If you can't stomach the politics and history, don't set your game in it. Using it as a fun aesthetic and setting is utterly morbid. It absolutely could have just been fantasy regency Europe (ignoring all the difficult colonialism) without losing anything. The hero of the revolution in this game is Marie Antoinette's bloody bodyguard!??? The NPCs look very iffy and sound OK. It's kinda repetitive (but that's the whole genre and I'm not complaining having played many other titles a ridiculous number of times). I feel like I wrote a lot more for the bad, but this is just because it's so ridiculous and got my goat. Ultimately, it's a lot of fun and something absolutely worth playing if you need a break from From Software and/ or want to imagine you are the Dancer of the Boulangerie Valley. Gameplay 4Visual Design 4Everything Else 1.5

_childDocuments_.review: Just for context before my review, I have 100%ed Bloodborne, Dark Souls 1, Dark Souls 2, Dark Souls 3, Sekiro, Elden Ring, Nioh 1, Nioh 2, Surge, Surge 2,  Thymesia, Mortal Shell, Remnant From the Ashes, Code Vein, The Lords of the Fallen, Ashen, Tails of Iron.*** Difficulty *** - Pro/Con - 1. General DifficultyEasy and relaxing compared to all other souls games. Died less than 10 total times in the game all from being lazy. 2. BossesAll but 2 bosses were 1 shots. All bosses could have easily have been 1 shots, but I was just being lazy/greedy. 3. Items/HealsThere are tons of heal/buff/damage items throughout the game that make the game even easier. I ended the game with hundreds and never even needed them.4. EnemiesEnemies move sets are simple and there are probably less than 15 total enemy types in the entire game. Most bosses are just buffed health bars of existing trash mobs with increased health pools. The game has dodge and parry mechanics and I completed the game only using dodge mechanic and it is extremely forgiving compared to other souls/souls-like games.Difficulty summary: Con. In my opinion it should have been more difficult*** Story *** - Pro/ConThe story wasn't bad. It had a few cool twists. It may just be me, but I had a hard time getting into the story or caring for the characters other than the main character you play. All names are in French and difficult to follow who its referring to and I think that makes it harder to follow to fall in love with all the side characters.Story summary: Con. I did not really enjoy the story.*** Visuals *** ProI really enjoyed the visuals. Very similar to Thymesia which I enjoyed*** Game stability/Glitches **** ConHonestly I was surprised by the amount of glitches and crashes. I have a new pc (built in last 18 months). Ran graphics on normal to make sure I was way under threshold my pc could handle and I still had 15-20 complete crashes during my playthrough. 2 times I got stuck in between trees or fell through the floor on the boss fight. Bot times I had to summon back to a bonfire and lose all souls just to fix it (shutting down game and reloading didn't work)*** Value *** Pro/ConIf you enjoy souls and souls-like games, its not a "must play". However, if you are like me and love souls games and want to play every souls/souls-like game ever created, this is one I would suggest buying for less than $20. It is not worth anywhere close to $49.99 in my opinion. I purchased for $29.99 on sale and feel like I overpaid.*** Game Length ***I completed this game and all side quests in 40 hours. If you didn't care about side quests or exploration it could be completed in 20 hours.Overall Summary - I would not pay more than $20 for this game. If you enjoy souls-like games and you're bored, then this is a fun relief from the typical punishing souls-like experienceOverall Rating - 6 out of 10passe une bonne journée

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the campaign, I would say if you have been eyeing up this game, wait until a sale or find it cheaper elsewhere.Things I liked; the setting, beautiful and detailed from the weapons. to the world, and even aegis herself all look beautiful and you can tell they have done their research.The satisfaction of taking down a titan boss; these beasts will test you and the feeling of accomplishment at taking them down was always great.The story itself; I wont lie, the ending did make me slightly teary which means they made a great story work. You feel as you progress through the game, you want to uncover the truth.The cons; OK, anyone who has seen any reviews will know this already, its a game plagued with mechanics that are not very well polished from the fact that enemies attack without little to no warning over and over again, to the locking system just going from one enemy to another, to frame rate drops that literally will mean the death of you, yet again.Oh, and there is ZERO indication of how what weapon you use, you need to make sure you level up the correct attribute. I did not realise this until a few hours in, and had to restart as you cannot reset your stats. Ever. So for example I chose the dancer class, and her weapon the fan needed two specific attributes to be upgraded so she was actually levelling up properly.Overall, I still do say YES get this game as its great to see a AA studio improve with each game, and I feel even with its flaws, this is still a gem of a game worthy of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre game that is carried singlehandedly by its strong aesthetic and gorgeous level design. - The story and writing are weak despite this being an RPG-centric studio.- the combat is awkward and you'll need some time to get used to the overly-long wind-ups on pretty much all attacks; this coupled with no dodge-cancel make it closer to monster hunter than a souls game.- the music and sound design are decent, if forgettable.- the difficulty feels all over the place at the beginning; bosses are easier than mobs. But after you find a weapon and stick with it you'll breeze through; i got through the last 3 bosses on the 1st try and PLENTY of healing flasks to spare.Tl;dr it's a decent time but definitely not worth it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Dark Souls if it was made by EA: Approachable difficulty, tons of bugs, and an ending so painfully stupid I want a refund.Actual review:If you're wanting a Souls-like game that isn't too difficult to dip your toes into the genre, SteelRising is a decent enough choice. The game is very forgiving with enemy placement, attack patterns, health items, and anima essence/souls, so even new players shouldn't find it too frustrating to advance through the game and upgrade their character. However, be aware that the game is also very buggy, has some very confusing level design in several areas, and has an ending so painfully stupid that I'm annoyed that I'm outside the refund window. Pros:Cool setting of revolutionary FranceAutomatons are awesomeInteresting boss designsLots of weapons to choose fromForgiving for those new to Souls-likesSome enemies blend into terrain making them almost impossible to counter or dodge attacks fromCons:So many bugsPainfully stupid endingThere's actually only 5 or 6 weapons, they've just been reskinned to pad-out the contentBugs I ran into in my 47 hour playthrough:-Getting stuck on terrain while trying to walk in the middle of a clear street-Item pick ups not picking up -Item pick ups allowing multiple duplicates before actually being picked up-That time I clipped through an entire apartment building to be trapped between two invisible walls-Bosses aggroing before you even enter the arena (One even insta-klilling me out of the air as I was falling into the arena)-Enemy AI not activating-Crash to desktop entering the final boss arena (only happened once in the entire playthrough though)

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game tentatively on the basis that if you want to play a competent souls-like, but don't care *too much* about good bosses or story, you could have a good time with this game. I think it's gameplay is a solid 8/10 - satisfying combat and a number high-mobility options for navigating levels quickly, interesting enemy design, sometimes interesting boss design. However the bosses do not feel particularly menacing or like an event. /minor spoilers/ The final boss was particularly lackluster and there was virtually no build up to it and no fanfare for defeating it. Environments are visually neat but sometimes blend together in ways that make it easy to get lost. That can make doing side quests quite tedious, even with the optional objective marker the game gives you in the form of a compass item.Story is meh, alternate history french revolution stuff. Interesting concept but it's delivered with such soulless character-to-character dialogue and cutscenes that I never felt particularly engaged. Things certainly could have been pulled off better. It doesn't help that all of the human character designs are quite boring and they're rendered fairly ugly. Their rough motion-capture animations paired with overly poeticized period dialogue made the whole thing feel rather goofy. The game does have its jank. I didn't experience many glitches or bugs in my play through and it ran fine, with one or two moments of stuttering throughout the whole thing. However the quest system and progression itself seems kind of precarious. I accidentally sequence broke a few events, but were able to return to them later and they triggered correctly after I fulfilled other prerequisites for the quests. But it sounds like I may have gotten lucky based on some other reviews. And one of the side quests never left my objective marker or location quest indicator, even though I had completed the criteria for it and it was added to my finished quest list in the journal. The game allows you to move freely between areas, however I'd be wary of picking up items when exploring areas you're not sure you're supposed to be in. It's very easy to get over certain obstacles that aren't obviously meant to keep you out of areas you're not meant for yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: France? Rebellion? Mechanical clockwork maids that can dance and inflict death? I've never knew I needed all of these so much and here in Steelrising they are everywhere.After roughly 32hrs I've finished my first play through with the majority spent trying to wrap up the side quests and find all the weapons I could without looking online for hints - but I still did need help for one of the side-quests. What does this game have going for it? 1. Voice Acting. I hate people, and I hate people talking even more, and the way games try to make a plot mean something can either be great or so cringeworthy it stops you playing. Thankfully, this game is in the first category; the delivery of the dialogue was very well done. The lead, Cassie Layton, appeared in Greedfall by the same studio, delivered a believable performance which I think is especially commendable given that she's a clockwork robot in revolutionary France.The in-game animations do make the game feel a bit clunky in places and there are some uncomfortable moments where NPCs would be staring into my soul without a single word coming from them - but this I was able to ignore because I cared about the story. Everyone's French was commendably interwoven to remind me that we were in France and although I cannot speak French, I should expect it to be spoken in France - even clockwork France. The council of assembled learned and clergy each delivered similarly commendable performances, although spending all of my time with Aegis makes me bias to her contribution. 2. It's Different. I mean... as I said before it's historically accurate France during the assembly of the third estate the point of revolution but catapults expectations into The Bastille’s dry moat and takes us on a totally weird and wonderful adventure. 3. The Environment. It isn't perfect, as an addict for breakable objects I have found many a suspiciously floating book or candle in the middle of nothing but once again I wanted to find every street, every villager voice segment, and be shown just how brutally the people of this world tried to fight for their freedom but never had a single hope of accomplishing it. I also tried to jump on rocks and ended up sliding into eternal falling pits of sadness more than once - with a lot of menu pausing and using the camera to nudge myself in the direction of "not this Hell" I escaped. I consider the faults to be minor and not sufficient to ruin my enjoyment of all the death, disease, and dancing.4. The Music.I enjoyed it very much and found it to be impactful when needed and pleasant when in the background – the ending credits was a really beautiful piece that I enjoyed listening to especially.The Bad: 1. Performance.It's something that is very, very noticeable and will have you sitting on loading screens for 2-3 minutes when travelling. I cannot be sure why but I think the lighting in the game is possibly too good and everything else suffers because of it - coupled with the highly detailed environment I can see that it would be a very expensive process to get it performing to a 2022 standard. However, I think it would be worth the investment even if it were just to optimise the travelling between zones - I played Bloodborne on release and I consider my debt paid to loading screens.2. Character Models. I found the mechanical robot to be more emotive and expressive than the flesh and blood comrades found throughout the game. I can't even call it poor implementation or bad artistry; I believe it is a lack of resources to match the vocal performance to the visual - a limitation I believe can be better focused going forward. 3. So many streets. I loved running around and breaking everything, but when I realised, I had missed a collectable behind some random gate or fence I was suddenly wishing the game had some kind of map. I don't even want a full top-down Google Maps, I would love a scrap of paper that Aegis can draw on to remember where we went and where we didn't just so the spirit of adventure can have a direction to visit without handing it to you. 4. Wrapping Up.The game has volumes of text, dialogue, quests, and descriptions - I found items that by the end of the game I had no use for or never found to whom they belonged. I also found a prisoner in Le Bastille begging for food with no idea where or how to help him, I checked what I could but only found books, straw, and some questionable HR policies. I think the voice talent is so well assembled that on finding the memories a full cut-scene to bring the player up to the moment they find them would engage better. 5. Cost. For the dialogue I think it's worth the price, but for the action and execution of the graphics I feel the game is reaching for a price-point it doesn't belong in. What others do with their money is their own business, but I would fully believe that this game thrive in a lower price-point and be enjoyed more for it. However, I do understand that everything costs money and it isn't easy to "just do it" - of course they developers want to release the best game they can, but they also want to eat and have a dependable income. 6. I Want to Dance WIth Athénaïs de Vaucanson.Just let me dance with her and be happy... for like... 5-minutes, okay? She's been through a lot and so have I... we need this.... Finally the music box enemies need a mute button because sometimes I was hearing it when I wasn't at my PC and that's not okay.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a bit to say about this game, after playing for a bit, beating a main boss and going through some ofthe story, here is my opinions. _childDocuments_.review: Flawed, but fun! Imagine if Skynet became aware and Judgement Day happened in the 1800s...This is a janky but enjoyable title-not so much Soulslike as Souls-esque, or say...Souls-adjacent.  It apes the mechanics in a beautifully rendered setting, but misses the heart of what makes those games compelling on their own merit.  I found the game ran fine on my own machine, fearing the worst from reviews but very pleasantly surprised.  The flavour of the game being set in an alternative steampunk French Revolution is wonderfully different, and the sumptuous background is one of the game's strengths.  I cannot count how many times I marveled at the dust within god-rays breaking into an interior environment.  There is a lot to praise in the variety of asset you encounter in an area too.  There are exceptions of course-NPC faces contort with more muscles than I suspect exist in real people during dialogue, and the jitter of inaccessible space is severe at times.  Controls-wise, this game is more DMC than DS3 - there is a slippy overstep that occurs that while undetected in combat does tend to make itself known in more careful play.  At times, I felt like my character was balancing on a unicycle at the end of a walk, but ultimately it is not a game that depends on finesse to overly matter.  The draw for me was the more action-orientated focus of the title.  There is a confusing map layout that slows it down, but this is ultimately a linear game whereby you gather the resources you need most near where you will want them.  It is hard to miss a secret, and Steelrising provides enough brief side-missions in level to merit taking your time as you explore.  The enemies are varied, but do repeat quite a bit.  The tactics of my agility-based robo-dancing-ninja-bot never really varied no matter the weapon it employed; save for when there were multiple enemies on screen and it becomes a chaotic fight and dash away strategy.But I do love it.The game has so much it does right, that in a world without Dark Souls, it shines brightly.  With so many Soulslike titles out there, I would describe this more like a far more accessible, period-based version of The Surge 2.  It has that one-more try appeal crucial to this genre and varies itself just enough to push through the jank.  I love unpolished gems, and this more than qualifies.  I also root for smaller developers to make their mark on the market, and while this is just about a niche interest; it is a promising sign from the Spiders software team.  I recommend it in a sale for now; but it certainly merits the attention of both Soulslike aficionado and newcomer alike.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Steelrising. However the game isn't without its flaws. Detailed notes below for those considering buying the game who have a few minutes to spare. Want to make the game harder?  .Worried the game will be too difficult? .  : So much care was given to the model of the player character, Aegis. From the cogs which are constantly spinning in your back to the rapid changes to your arms as you swap or use your weapons, it really added to my experience of the game.  : Clocking in around 20 hours for a run where I did a ton of exploring / completed the side-quests. This is very subjective, but I found it to be perfect. I don't feel burnt out from Steelrising's content. In fact I want to dive back in and see how I can affect the story through choices made during the game.  : I'm going to wrap these two into a single point, because I think most souls-likes often suffer from doing too little in these departments. The weapons are grouped into various "types", which are refreshingly creative. Some move sets are obviously more inspired than others, but the fact that each weapon has a "special" ability adds variety, and gives the best-designed weapons a unique identity. Armour design is gorgeous, but be warned that some suffer from poor cloth physics. I ended up finding a set of armour ("Diana") which I used throughout the majority of the campaign. The variety of weapons and armour was pleasant enough and, importantly, rewards your exploration of the game world, particularly in the first half.  : The clockwork enemies in the game are beautiful, and can be quite creative. The musicians were favourites of mine, playing their instruments like good bots until they try to kill you with them. Some enemy types which are genre tropes suffer from the same weakness fans will have grown accustomed to, such as dogs remaining the most predictable. However, Spiders did innovate on those tropes in fun ways due to the setting and themes. : This really should be mixed, but I want to give recognition to Spiders for the first three locations you visit in-game after Saint-Cloud. The levels are well-crafted, and serpentine, in a way that genre fans should enjoy. The abundance of shortcuts are complimented by a clear dedication to verticality, particularly within set-piece buildings. The last third of the game's level design does suffer from third-act-let's-wrap-this-up-boys-idis (what the medical community also refers to as Lost Izalith), which is a shame (especially because  is so beautifully recreated). To the developer's credit, the fact that this portion of the game is gated behind a point of no return indicates that they knew you'd be somewhat railroaded until the end of the game, which is appreciated and leaves you less surprised when it happens.   : This is something which has already been addressed by many reviewers, but the game is not particularly difficult. Difficulty is something I seek out in games like these, so it left me feeling ambivalent. Keep in mind that difficulty could later be affected by balancing changes and can be affected by your choices as a player (see the two spoiler tags at the top of this review). : I found the game's environments beautiful, but they can become quite repetitive, particularly in the last third of the game. Being grounded in realism, they are often too concerned with remaining true to life. This is obviously intentional on the part of the developers, but it left me a little disappointed, especially given the more supernatural elements in parts of the game. The last level you visit,  was by far my favourite from an environments-perspective. While several concessions affect the realism of the location in order to make it fun to play through, a lot of attention was given to it's recreation and it shows .  : The mileage you get out of the game's story will really depend on how seriously you take it, and how much you appreciate its subject matter. It is focused on a few key players of the french revolution, which won't be everyone's cup of tea. I thought the more engaging elements were those involving the fiction which the developers crafted themselves, and not the multiple conversations where Lafayette and Robespierre bicker. The story also suffers from some side-quest bloating as you near the first point of no return , with those same quests often asking you to retrace your steps. However, the developers were kind enough to ramp the difficulty / vary the type of enemies in the zones you revisit, which was appreciated.   : This is obviously very subjective, but I found the game's bosses really suffer from a lack of appropriate balancing, and are far too easy for more experienced players. Their vulnerability to critical hits, status elements, and bombs creates an unfortunate disconnect between their beautiful design and their actual difficulty / how long you end up fighting them. I found it a shame that an effective build could lead you to ignore some of their mechanics, especially since so much care was obviously put into their animations / design.   : Buyer beware, this game is quite demanding / taxing on a PC! My build below, for comparison:Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700K CPU @ 3.80GHz || 48.0 GB RAM || NVIDIA RTX 3070I ended up having to pay attention to what settings I put on high, and opted to turn many of them down to medium so I could run the game over 60 fps in 1440p. I recommend reading up on optimisation guides / graphical requirements and seeing if your computer can run the game comfortably before diving in, as choppiness can affect your appreciation of the game. As Nacon has been kind enough to comment however, this is something that they are currently working on improving, so if your computer isn't as high-end, you may wish to wait until they've had a chance to make some changes. Ted talk over,thanks for the great game Spiders![Edit: some typos, small changes made to the content per developer comment]. -

_childDocuments_.review: The lack of real factions and fact that enemies are only robots makes what should have been a large and interesting world feel flat and one dimensional. The cinematics are done well, but with such a superficial world its difficult for the plot to be much deeper than a generic escalator moving the character onward. Gameplay feels a bit linear; in the way that a really good game for playstation 2 might. In a way it is a nostalgic callback, but in 2022 it mostly just removes the "open world" feeling of most truly great modern RPGs. Combat, true to the "Souls" style, is difficult to the point of being tedious. There is an assist mode to tailor the challenge level to something more along each person's individual preference. Animations and weapons are done in a way that is both unique and clear quality; these are redeeming factors to an otherwise let down. Though the weapons are easy to pass by and can only be found in one specific area of each linear map. I find myself watching location videos to make sure I don't miss anything. It is not my preferred method to play games, but little alternative is offered except to wander aimlessly through a world populated only by the same generic enemies.Overall this time period offers a unique and refreshing change of weapons and scenery from most traditional fantasy rpgs, and the steampunk element is done well. The worldbuilding and linear story progression lack depth, and I hope that future DLCs remedy this with additional enemy factions and better character customization.  TLDR: Worldbuilding: 2/5. Story/Progression: 3/5. Combat: 4/5. Graphics: 5/5. Overall: 3.5/5. Hope for future: High.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a much better game than you'd think.You start to realize roughly an hour in, after you've wrestled with the jank a bit and begun familiarizing yourself with both how and why this game is *different*. Sure, there are a few systems that present themselves rather immediately as throwing a wrench in some of the established works; an impromptu way to regain stamina after you run out -- with just the right amount of risk-reward play -- stands out. Then there's a story, with, y'know, cutscenes, which flies right in the face of the established norm. These games normally obfuscate their lore, don't they? But then it really hits you: you're having fun. And that's weird because, generally, these types of games are so hard that they're frustrating at times, but for whatever reason, that never happens here. Why?Well, it's because Steelrising is an easier Souls-like. It's easier for a lot of reasons: for one, it's fair. You don't feel like whoever designed this game is constantly out to get you: enemies present themselves in reasonable combat encounters. The game gives you just the right amount of heals, items and weapon options to make it through to the next shortcut with just a *little* bit of patience and time. But also, none of these enemies are poorly designed: they all have really great tells and animations, hinting at when and how they'll attack. And when they do, it doesn't kill you in one hit. Hell, it doesn't even knock you off that edge because, in *this* game, there's a grapple. That's right. You heard it here first. And the hits keep coming because as you get stronger in this game, you actually feel yourself getting stronger. What a revelation.And you DO get stronger. Every traversal option you unlock in a metroidvania-esque fashion (an in-air dash/doge, and a grappling hook among them!) can also be used in battle, endowing you with additional contextual abilities. It's a great change of pace from just having your weapons only dictate what you can do. Factor it all in with ample build options through weapon variety, stats, and armor to wear, and you've got yourself some replay value. Then there's the level design folks, and let me tell you: Steelrising doesn't disappoint here. Levels are large, layered, with repeat visits for side-quests allowing you to travel further and further in, unlocking tons of shortcuts and new paths as you go. The way the levels weave in on themselves is great, and while the game isn't fully connected (there are discrete levels that you eventually can choose to go to in differing order), I always felt there was a great sense of exploration. Exploration that ends, as it should, in a fun boss fight. No difficult bosses, mind you -- something that may seem strange because, again, isn't this a Souls-like? It is, and don't worry, some of the bosses probably will kill you. Once, maybe even twice. But never that third time: this game is just too fair; bosses, like yourself, stagger, and not a one of them comes equipped with a one-shot or a stunlock. It just isn't that kind of thing. You'll feel like a boss when you one-and-done them, and y'know what? That's okay. It's especially okay because these bosses are really cool to look at, and really cool to fight. But there has to be something wrong, doesn't there? And there is. At the time of this writing, Steelrising's performance is rough. Certainly playable, mind you; toggle on DLSS in the menu and you'll squeeze out the performance you need to keep the game moving along with you, but it's still a bit sad to see Spiders swing and miss here. If they release a patch addressing this issue (and some visual bugs), I'll try and update my thoughts accordingly. So, who is this game for? If you've never played a Souls game, and you want to, start here. It's incredibly approachable, and that's not to even mention the accessibility menu the game has for adjusting things to your liking -- but I don't think you'll need it. As I said, this game is more fun than it is difficult, and for someone who plays almost every Souls-like game whether I like it or not, it's a breath of fresh air to play one that isn't constantly trying to waste my time with cheap deaths or unreasonable demands. I also recommend this for even seasoned players who want the equivalent of a breather; you'll sink your teeth into this game and bite right through it, but I think you'll still have a ton of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of "a diamond in the rough".I am only recommending it due to having a lot of fun and being very tolerant of the flaws.The combat, the aesthetic, the characters, the setting and the bosses are all absolutely fantastic and well worth experiencing, especially once the gem is polished.In its current state however, the performance complaints are the least of your worries I would say. I have a fairly old rig and had to play at 70% resolution to make it not overheat my poor i5-4690k CPU and RTX 2060 into force restarting my PC.The main concerns are what plagues many recent bigger games - enemy variety, lackluster exploration rewards and NPC dialogue animations. There is also the difficulty being a bit too low, especially on bosses, and the shortcuts for the sake of shortcuts, but those are minor comparatively.The Enemies - technically, there is a lot of variety, however this is achieved by simply having an enemy type have 3 different elements or wielding 3-ish different weapons, normally giving it an extra attack or different element, with the rest of the moveset remaining the same. You will witness the entire roster of enemies about half way through, at which point you'll beg for a boss, but will get a mini-boss that's just a powered up version of one of those enemies.Just having more fodder enemies can help with this, simple ones with a single attack even. I get that each enemies needs a lot of time with the model and animation production, which is why just having throwaway enemies is completely fine, simply for variety's sake.The Exploration - the levels are designed very well, good pacing, decent enemy placement, and good loot spots, however this gets tarnished by the fact that the enemies placed are ones you've killed hundreds of already and the items are consumables or extra upgrade materials which, if you already have selected your weapon of choice, won't give you much after you get your weapon to max level (which is again achieved about half way through the game).Having more miscellaneous consumables can help here, like random self buffs, apart from the resistance ones, mines or knives or something completely passive like a +1 to specific stat on use even, anything more interesting than yet another explosive or healing item.The Dialogue Animations - overall the animations are great, some can look floaty, some janky, but overall it's great. However the dialogue scenes focus heavily on the speaking character, this makes the animation a priority to deliver the emotion, importance or nuance of the lines being delivered. I could forgive it during the side quests as I simply appreciated this being a well voice acted dialogue instead of just reading a note, but when heavy story beats are being delivered it stands out a lot. This especially hits hard during a very emotional moment, which the story built up to, but fell flat when the good voice acting and dialogue is delivered by dead-eyed face models or animations not matching the tone at all.This just needs a bit of polish, easily fixed in a patch or two as the story, dialogue and voice acting itself is already there and good, just needs the animation to match.Well worth during a sale, might want to avoid the side content to make it feel less repetitive, but otherwise waiting for performance improvements is a must for most.
