_childDocuments_.review: While there is fun to be had here, I cannot recommend this game to anyone unless they are VERY into souls games and have already played everything else out there. Combat is fun despite the clunkyness, but people are not exaggerating about the performance issues, and it's glitchy/buggy as hell and it's been out for over a year now so it doesn't seem like anyone's ever going to bother fixing any of it, the story is mind-numbingly boring (man in identical powdered wig indistinguishable from the other 10 identical characters gives you exposition dump of some BS that happens off screen over and over and over and over again), and it's not very long for one of these types of games (several hours of padding backtracking sidequests dumped on you right before the end of the game to artificially lengthen). It's not as bad as say Dolmen, but the fact that they released this game in this state and actually slapped a full price price tag on there is ridiculous. If you're THAT desperate for another souls game to play and see it on a deep sale, maybe it might be worth the risk to you. It's enjoyable enough for under $10. Everyone else? Don't even bother.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising has all the ingredients of a great souls-like.  The setting of the French revolution with machines is beautifully realized.  Weapon, enemy, and level design are standout.  Combat is mechanically satisfying, albeit a bit clunky, but once you get the hang of it, it’s fun.  It’s not too difficult either, so any deficiencies with the combat don’t become frustrations. Unfortunately, boss fights are the simplest and easiest battles in the game though.  Performance could be better.  The game is regularly on sale too, well worth it at a low price.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: After a wave of underwhelming souls-bourne-like games, I finally found one that pleased me, it is Steelrising. I was skeptical about this one, the marketing was not very convincing and the gameplays shown didn't comunicate very well too.But after 20+ hours of game (finished) I can say the developers managed to deliver, a game that is structured similarly to souls-bourne, with great level design, full of secrets, well placed shortcuts and checkpoints.Enemy variety could be better and bosses could be challenging( this is on the easier souls side). The combat might not please everyone, even though they managed to make convicing automat with animations that are very realistic, if can feel clunky and rigid depending on the enemy, heavier enemies are more stiff and slow. The protogonist however is fast and slick conveying the idea of what it represents.Story is well done and very interesting, it kept my attention from beginning to end. Narrative is similar to Greedfall with slightly better animations, but well executed mostly.Now the elephant in the room.... the performance, yeah if you have seen system requirements you realize that a beafy gpu an cpu are a must. For me the biggest issue is the CPU, my ryzen 2600x clocked at 4ghz couldn't maintain a locked 60 fps all the time, there are areas of the game which brings framerate down to low 40s with sustenained mid 50s in some places.... and there is nothing you can do to alleviate this, and aparently this is not justified either, game doesn't have NPCs walking around nor there are so many enemies... the developers need to improve this that is for sure. On the GPU side things is not so bad, my rtx 3070 is able to maintain almost locked 4k60 with tweaked settings, but I used DLSS to give it more room for busier moments.I  didn't test all the weapons and builds, in fact I sticked to the one I found worked better for me right at the beginning until the end. So, I can't say much about re-playability but it seems to have potential.Some side quests feel like fetch quests, but they may have important implications on the story and ending.Finally, I recomend this game and hope it will be improved over time.

I don't have a high end gaming PC by any means (Ryzen 5 5600x, RX 6600, 16GB RAM, PCIE4 NVMe) but when the FPS drops the game slows down too so it's unplayable. It's a shame because it looks interesting. Please PC devs, GIVE US GAME DEMOS.EDIT: I appreciate the response, and I did submit the dxdiag before this review based on your response to another user's review. Best of luck to you guys.

_childDocuments_.review: In a market becoming saturated with souls-like games, this one definitely stood out to me. To keep things relatively short and simple; the gameplay was very fun and smooth albeit it wasn't exactly the hardest souls-like game I've ever played and I've played a LOT. The weapons are AWESOME and definitely warrant multiple playthroughs to try different builds and the armors are all beautifully designed with clear inspirations. The story, setting and protagonist, Aegis, were also all beautifully designed and written. As for performance, I've had a completely smooth playthrough from start to finish. I know people seem to be having trouble but I've had no framerate or graphical issues during my entire time playing the game, and in that time I think I encountered only 1 or 2 noticeable bugs. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game and I'm definitely gonna give it another playthrough to try out an alchemy build this time. Worth every penny ^_^

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game. Definitely one of the better soulslike, and I have played a bunch. - It's too easy for my taste, that makes combat a bit boring sometimes. Runs smooth with rtx3070 and ryzen3600, 70-90 fps on high/ultra. Never under 60fps. - levels are a bit flat. Exploration has it's limits but there is some.- itemization and character progression is limited bit its enough. Recommended. _childDocuments_.review: The optimization is bad, but I don't think nearly as bad as many other reviews let on. Plays 1080 low/med with ultra character models and pretty steady 60 fps on a 3060. _childDocuments_.review: Believe it. I have a 30 series and listened to one reviewer who said, "It wasn't that bad"..... Yes it is. I have a 3070, the game recommends I play on normal settings. First game to ever do that. AA at that! (SCROLL TO BOTTOM FOR UPDATE)Look.Look cool? YesCombat fun? Yes (imo)Interesting story? Got my attentionDo I want to play more? YES! But! I am more tired of people rushing out the product because quarters are about up, or holiday is around the corner. I do not know and I do not care. This game, ONE HUNDRED PERCENT, needs a patch / fixing. To give an example, the camera doesn't feel like it is transitioning up and down as you move. It feels like it is bouncing up and down. I never truly understood people when they said they felt motion sick (never had it before). I am not getting sick, but I have had to blink my eyes because it felt like they started bouncing up and down (weird feeling by the way). WAIT TO BUY. I listened to the thumbs up on a mixed game. I also listened to someone saying, "not that bad".. I am here with a spent 60. You? Not yet. So prove to devs and pubs why quality is key and NEVER trust the "not that bad" guy.. UPDATEI read another comment... and admittedly forgot DLSS is a thing. Did it fix it 100%? No. Stutters, frame drops (These two are by far the WORST offenders. Makes fighting a frustration in a SoulsBourne), rendering taking awhile to kick in. Everything detailed except a rug or wall, or even the road itself. Looking like a muddy mess. Pausing the game to continue. EVERYTHING continues, EXCEPT Aegis (your character). She stays locked in for another 2/3 seconds. Getting mauled in the process if a fight is taking place. Turn off Depth of Field, it continues to persist. Muted dialogue. Turn in a side mission item, awkward silence for a good 10/15 seconds. Then mission over. I have NO clue the resolution and no pop up from received items (if I got one). Then what lead me here to update my review, a crash. First one to be fair, but one none the less. Outside the technicalRarely, but some enemies have terrible attack animations. Where their blade WILL go through you, but does not count damage. It is not a bug, just not the hit to register damage. This is terrible design. Especially if you parry like me. Because the actual hit comes in, in the time I am stuck in the parry animation. Texture Quality at HIGH means blurry (looking at her armor). Only EPIC is clean looking. No joke. Higher the settings, more prone to the issues above. Now mix all this together. And for the ones not having these issues, congrats! However, this IS the gaming world and I know some are just dealing with it. If it was one of the these issues and not all, maybe. This is too much for it be just me / a few of us. I cannot wait to see what a patch does. I want to really like this game. IMO, they went all out. I can see what they were going for. I can see the craft. But it seems either PC was left behind due to negligence, or the engine cannot hang. Either way, we pay full price. End Game UpdateI beat the game. I am saddened because I kept playing thinking today would be the day the patch came. That turned into the day the devs would announce a patch would be coming soon.. I got to see neither. I usually rate Soulsbourne from beginner, intermediate to SoulsBourne. I would say this is a beginner level. There is NO limit to items. So once you find yourself rolling around with 187 heals and your estus (reusable heals) you have to make a decision. I decided to not allow myself to heal outside of parrying (item required) which kept the game interesting. Grenades are STRONG. Like, "I may die. Oh wait! I have grenades. I'll be fine" kind of strong. I guess the limit is 999 when factoring in how many healing I had because by the time credits rolled I acquired 40/60 per nade type. When it came to the upgraded variant, I had maybe 20/30 of those too, and I never used them. Didn't need to honestly. The normal nades where more then enough for enemies. IMO, I would do what Bloodbourne did. Have a max of 2/3 items, anything more is put away. Stored at the lanterns/carriage. Re-upping when you visit. HOWEVER! If I were the devs I would work on enemies with staff like weapons. Their reach is too far/wide. I would i-frame through as needed, but the range was so far to the left, right, center (whichever way they swung) the only real option was to run, or get far enough away, which in turn would take me out of the fight. If Aegis is within a foot of that weapon, you still get popped. So side stepping was a pain but BB is my favorite SoulsBourne to date. Side stepping/parrying is what I do. So I suggest fixing their hit boxes or shortening their weapon. Maybe both. I say this because at the end of the game, last map, you find yourself going against two staff wielding enemies at once. SO MANY GANK HITS!! This resulted in grenades. Tossing them like Aegis was trying out for the local baseball team. Fast balling like an auto turret. Worked. But it felt like I was cheating. Right then I thought of going into the final boss fight and seeing if my 30 or 40 level 2 explosive grenades could take the win (for closure, I didn't do this but I guarantee you, nades would win). Another review said this, but I have to agree. Normal enemies gave me more trouble then any boss. Shield barer, the one using a log and the one dual wielding two chains (sadly I cannot remember the names). Granted this was to do with the hitboxes more then the moves themselves but still. There isn't much to say here besides I hope they add a Added Difficulty section in the menu if some want (kind of joking). Also, between bosses and enemies, after they do some combos, or a few attacks, they would just stop. They just stand still, no movement what so ever. No joke for a quarter of the game, I thought this was a trick to reel me in like a trap. It isn't though. I moved in and hit them 2/3 times before they moved again. Not sure if this is a bug or not. My suggestion. Get rid of this and speed up some enemies. I love when my heart rate goes up in these games.  All in all, I like the game. I think it is gorgeous, fun, and I appreciate actually giving us a story. IMO, you HAVE to do the side content. It is half the game and fills in half the lore. However, to save you time, you will get side mission pretty early on, but it is not until you have the special abilities (obtained through the titan, main boss, fights). There are three abilities. Once you have those, most side content is good to go. However! Some will still be locked until certain story beats (need a key for example). As long as you keep talking to the NPCs, you'll get them all. Still. until the patch addressing the technical side drops and cleans up that side of things, I have to stay with a thumbs down. This has to stop. It is crazy to me something as SteelRising, which you can SEE the craft, releases in this state. UPDATE 9/28/22Patch came and what a massive difference it made. I played until the workshop (beating the first two areas). Running with Aegis never felt better. Only stutter I noticed was moving while the game was loading a new area, or auto save. There where a few muddy objects. However, we're talking a box, instead of the actual roads. Again, much better!  UPDATE 11/12/22Sadly this latest "DLC" deleted my saves. I had a end game save to load to instantly play the "DLC" at release. However, that is now gone. All that is left is my NG+ save. Which only has the first boss on it. I am HOURS away from the "DLC". Not in the mood to play that much again. I put parenthesis around DLC because apparently it has been in the game the whole time. Wow. Sorry to give a roller coaster of a review. I hope this proves I tried giving Nacon the benefit of the doubt. At this point, months after release, still having constant issues and the introduction of even more, a thumbs down is deserved in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this was my first soulslike, So I lack genre context. but I can provide some basic notesSetting: marvelous, the plot and atmosphere is refreshing and interesting. characters feel lifelike and plausible.Gameplay: Tough but rewarding. No doubt a veteran souls player will find it easy, but there are a number of difficulty settings to elevate the challengeLength: Just right, the game neither dragged on nor felt rushed at any point, the pacing was smooth and the challenge level rose consistently.Combat: Very good, combos and dodges were satisfying to use,  enemies telegraphed well, without feeling stilted, aided by the whole mechanical theme. Enemy variety was good, and sensibly typed out without being too redundant.Weapons and builds: Good, while i didnt experiment with too many builds I found a nice mix of weapons for various playstyles and experimented with  a few even though I wasnt ideally statted for them.Aegis recieves a number of interesting armor sets that suit her very well and many therein have differing focuses.

On my 2060 with quality DLSS on all high settings except textures (because of 6 GB ram) runs most of the times at 60 fps. Oh and disable Indirect Illumination, it kills perfomance for some reason.And Spiders if you read this...get a proper marketing team for once.You are one of the few studios in the world that still have that old Bioware's touch in character and world building. It is a CRIME that your games do not get the recognition that they deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: My first soulslike, which I mainly bought and played in anticipation of Lies of P to see if I could even enjoy this sort of game and the answer is: yes, absolutely. I mean, I ate dirt for the first hour or so but once I got used to the mechanics, it was smooth sailing. There's a large variety of weapons throughout the game so you can really customize your playstyle. I believe the main story is 15 hours but doing the side quests will extend it to 20, maybe 25 and I highly recommend that you do because I personally found them much more interesting than the main quest. Your enjoyment will partially depend on how much you care about the French revolution with automatons setting, so don't be surprised when you start encountering major historical figures from that time period. If you're a history nerd like me, that might even be a big draw for you and I think in that aspect, the game does deliver. In fact, I had so much fun with it that I ended up double dipping with new game+ to get some more achievements I missed the first time around, which I hardly ever do. Got the game when it was on sale for $20 or so and I think it's well worth that price.

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising is a soulslike that has a few key QOL and design features that make it a good game for me personally. 1. It has pretty good voice acting and the story is actually comprehensible and good. 2. Quest design actually tells you where to go while not being too obvious or intrusive. 3. Combat is fast and there is a large variety of builds to try out. 4. The checkpoints (bonfires) are well placed and you will never lose a ton of progress from dying, or have to do a ridiculously long run to a boss room. If you are a fan of soulslike games and the above appeals to you, you will enjoy this. There are some bugs and I had to lower shadows for performance but they weren't a big deal. The movement animations look stiff in videos because you are an atuomaton in the revolutionary france era, the actual combat feels smooth and responsive.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's do good/bad  reviewer, shall we?+ Gorgeous character models and architecture, excellent animations.- But very copy-pastey, sometimes disorienting, overuse of invisible walls.+ A soulsborne game with quests, decent story and extensive cutscenes. Awesome voice acting.- At times nonsensical scenes, overall more on the predictable side.+ Although  a bit clanky combat, way more responsive than The Surge for example. Creative weapons fitting in for the setting.- Very 'flat' progression system. (Attributes have almost no effect) Not much sense in experimentation.+ Unique Bosses. Base mobs that gain 'twists' the farther you go.- No real encounter variation because of not enough meat on the base mechanics.+ I like the decision of including metroidvania elements, but not overuse it.- Mind-boggling rule-changing of aspects regarding navigation for no apparent reason.+ Fresh and interesting setting. Doesn't shy to show violence.- Wouldn't mind if they included a spark of humor. (in addition to the hilarious music automatons)I can recommend the main game and story DLC. Could have finished it ~3h early if I used the damn compass earlier and not running around aimlessly for side-quests.As others said, not the best on the technical side. Around 15 crashes on Linux with Proton/GE.

_childDocuments_.review: I ran the game with a stable 80 FPS and had no problems in this aspect. The combat is severely lacking in this game. Often times I can visually see the AI breaking down. They would just stand there while taking hits. The enemy variety is not there and there's a lot of re-skins. They're trying to be innovative and create unique combat systems that work okay. They still need to do a lot of number tuning as stats make too much of an impact on your play style. I started as an alchemist and played with lack luster damage until I just decided to go full strength starting at level 25 or so. I went from doing no damage to practically one combo everything to death. There's a huge disparity of damage between the different weapons. Elemental abilities are extremely lack luster, however, frost is probably too overpowered as freezing an enemy allows you to do a full charged attack. There's no diminishing returns, so most BOSS fights can be won by freezing and spamming charge attacks. The story is okay. The rewards for side quests are atrocious. They reward you with story and achievements and one mobs worth of souls. They don't give you anything else such as cosmetics or equipment or even modules. I cleared the game while freeing everyone and doing all the side quests in my play through.They really messed up by having no free roam after beating the final boss. My file is now bricked and unplayable. There also doesn't appear to be a respec option for the characters, So my character was utterly trash for the first twenty five levels. The terrain is also super buggy and can bug out a lot. The levels are not as platformable as they might appear. Overall, I'd give this a 5/10 for being mostly bug free and innovative combat systems that need numbers tuning.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat starts great, unfortunately you never get new weapons after the first couple hours, so it gets a little bit samey by the end.They do give you alternate versions of the weapons with one of the elements attached, but since I wasn't spect for Alchemy I wasn't interested in those.Sound is great, all the Enemies sound great, the hit sounds in combat are good and the songs, when they do come in, are good too. Nice overall package soundwise.Setting and Story are interessting, optional Quests for the most part are worth doing, no complaints here.Looks great, ruined Paris gets a bit old after a while. But the other areas do make up for it.Performance isn't great, but I could still run it at 60fps most of the time (on medium), and my pc is over 6 years old at this point. Overall Good Soulslike, not exactly Nioh2 but better than average.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game, if you want some French infusion in your blood.[+]1) FRENCHSet in France, characters are French, there is even some French in English. Perfect.2) UNIQUE WEAPONSEach type is unique and with a different special ability.3) PRETTY GRAPHICSIt is not Elden Ring, but some Paris scenery is really beautiful.4) GOOD VOICE ACTINGVoice acting was pretty good, but bad facial expressions ruined the immersion.5) GOOD STORYSurprisingly, the game has a good story, with some mystery and a predictable, but still sad conclusion.[-]1) CLUNKY MOVEMENTMovement is clunky and annoying, especially rotational movement.If that was done intentionally to show the character's Automat nature, then it was a bad idea, which somewhat ruined the experience.2) UNBALANCEDAction RPG - yes, Souls-like - no.By the third of the game, you become overpowered, and the gameplay just collapses.3) BAD FACIAL ANIMATIONAnimation is so bad, it ruins a good voice acting.4) STUCKINGCharacter gets stuck on a small brick, or sometimes even on nothing at all.5) BOSSES ARE A JOKEThis game bosses are a joke. They are easier than ordinary mobs, not aggressive at all,and when 2), you kill them with 2-4 hits.6) COPY-PASTE MOBSAll mobs are just a copy-paste of bosses or other way around.7) SCARCE WEAPONS AND ARMORLow variety of available weapons and armor.8) EITHER GAMEPLAY OR STORYYou either play for an hour, or listen to storytelling for an hour.If only he storytelling was integrated into the gameplay, the game would be more engaging and captivating.Conclusion: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Spiders did the same mistake again. As previous projects, game have good choice of setting, art design, plot. And these are all the positive aspects of the game.Game having lack of level design, battle system, balance, boss and enemies design, but that is forgiven for first souls-like game for the studio.What is really terrible is optimization and performance of the game and how developers addressed these issues. _childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: You'll enjoy it, if you you know what to expect. This game is definitely not a AAA title and worth 50€ but I got it for less than 30€ and that is alright.How difficult is it?I completely spikes in the first few hours and in a few boss fights. But once you get grenades/potions and learn how to use them, most enemies are easy going. IMO this is completely imbalanced because you can carry an infinite amount of grenades and potions and they are not very expensive.   Where it shines:- Combat and upgrades: Huge variety of different weapons that have completely different attack styles. Very Bloodborne-like, and you can combine two different weapons and several types of throwing weapons to develop your own approach to combat. -Art style and environment: Very unique and atmospheric. Next best thing until Lies of P. get released. Where it sucks:Cutscenes and overall story: In typical Spiders-fashion, this is early 2000s story telling. Looks like these guys don't have one single decent writer on their payrole or someone who knows the basics of camera work for dialogue scenes. Absolutely dreadful facial animations, no dramatic development and very little suspense whatsoever. This is a major problem in basically all of their games. Some boss entrances are souls-like but still sub-par. Performance: It doesn't run well and you need to lower most setting even on high end machines to get a stable framerate. Considering the resulting visuals, this is technically pretty weak. Watch a few gameplay videos first and decide for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: After going through the game to the end and completing all the achievements and DLC, I can give it a strong 6Pros for me- setting of French Revolution and automatons- a wide variety of weapons and costumes- cool mechanics with cooling- the plot is intriguing at the beginning- interesting final bossCons for me- many similar mobs- a small amount of loot (this is especially evident in addition to the game)- pulling camera to the enemy- there are flaws in the plot- bad optimization on startDo I recommend buying this game?Yes, if you like the setting as much as I do

_childDocuments_.review: For me it was a surprisingly good game. For sure no AAA-souls like. But if you lower your expectations, you can have quite a good time for your money. (If you buy it in a sale)I would recommend it especially for people who are new to the genre, as it is quite easy, when you are progressing to the endgame. Positive:- Setting (French revolution with robots?)- Combat System and Upgrade SystemMeh:- Story could be better. But if you are trying to complete all the sidequests, it can be okay to say the least- Performance- Graphics. For me the graphics are okay. But with time the assets are getting quite repetetive.Bad:- Balancing. I think that this is definitely the weak point of the game. I ignored the whole alchemist-aspect, because i never needet it. And after like 10 hours or so, i killed all major bosses with my first try. - Enemy AI. There are always situations, where you can cheese the fights. And the enemies tend to be very passive, which can result in you benefiting from heavy weapons and heavy attacks very much.So if you think that the cons and mehs are no problem for you, and you are looking for a more "relaxing" souls-like experience -> Give it a try

_childDocuments_.review: This is Ubisoft 2.0.I played the closer BETA, two weeks ago.The game runs like ass on a 3090 and an 11900k.I thought, well they will optimise the crap out of it in the next two weeks and have a great release.Talk about shoot yourself in the foot.Nothing, nothing at all was done.I only needed to play two minutes and monitor things using afterburner to see that it’s the same crap as the BETA.People do like this game, but like I said they have shot them selfies in the foot by being flat out lazy on the PC version.Like they had two setup in the studio with slightly different hardware and that was it.Maybe they just don’t know how to code for DX12 being that it’s on the dev now to optimise for it, and the heavy lifting isn’t done at the driver level. anymore. _childDocuments_.review: 7/10 from me.Music is really good when there is music, mostly it is just ambience.The Story is rather deep I think but I skipped a lot of it, bc. I play it for the gameplay not the story.The Game is really, really easy compared to DarkSouls, did the final boss first try without even needing 3 healing items.The worlds are beautiful BUT, and this is a giant BUT, it is basically impossible to not get lost in all the mazes there are, the levels are very linear yet there are many, many places to get lost, everything kind of looks the same, there is few landmarks to get a feeling of where you are, after a while it felt tedious to just search for where it continues to the point where I watched walkthroughs to find out where I needed to go. I would absolutely play the game again on New Game Plus but the simple fact that the maps are so confusing to navigate, I think I will not replay it any time soon.I did hop into NG+ though and it seems to get a bit better difficulty-wise but they also allow you to level up even higher than in the normal game.Almost everywhere is loot yet basically none of it really is interesting or fun, every now and then you find grenades but I didn't find a need to use them because the bosses were so easy. The best loot and the most interesting loot to find is upgrade materials, modules and weapons.With a heavy weapon you can stunlock almost everything from normal enemies to main bosses.The side missions are basically go there and there and so on, not really interesting nor was it interesting enough for me to do them all.Finding keys is a good feeling until you remember that you saw at least 3 doors, let me give an example. I was in the Bastille and I saw a bunch of locked doors, every time I found a key it seemed the door is less than a minute away, the fun thing was that I always was unsure if this was finally the key for the locked door I was at a while ago, the answer was always no, might be because of me skipping a bunch of the story cutscenes but yeah.I didn't feel as rewarding to beat bosses as it does in other games, probably because, just as said, none of the bosses really pose any challenge, the most I've died to a boss was likely 7-8 times, not more.You start just running past all enemies if you die just searching for the right way.Many parts of the game are unbalanced and there are some bugs, like items still being there after picking them up (makes it fun to guess if you've been to somewhere or not) or getting stuck and using the return to the last checkpoint item until you notice that the game just said, no and you lost all cash you had.I got it on preorder with the DLC included with a discount, the DLC took me about 2 hours or so at most, it was a beautiful level and actually one of the better ones.If you want to play it, buy it on sale, I don't think I'd buy it at full price after having played it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of my favorite games I have played in a while. I am really into historic games. While yes, it is clearly not meant to be an accurate retelling of the french revolution, it still pulled into that time era. I love the design of Aegis, the clothes were also a lot of fun to see. I do have some complaints about the game. One, sometimes its hard to find the certain tools that will help you unlock doors. For example, it was very hard for me to open the last door in the game. I also wish there was no auto lock switching because when I was fighting the enemies, it kept switching which enemy that I was locked on. Now that could be the weapon I used or the setup I had, but it was a real big issue for me. I still feel like this is a fantastic game for anyone that likes historic games and a fun kinda dark soulish game.

_childDocuments_.review: For those who aren't veteran souls players, this is a great introduction to the genre. The trainer option gives you ways to make the experience of learning the combat more pleasant and less punishing while still keeping the game a challenge. No, it's not the most original game, and as usual with Spiders, it's just a little off, but there's a lot to like about what they've done here and the French steampunk aesthetic is appealingly different than most of these games.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: I was on the fence about purchasing this game, I've been in a souls-like binge and I've loved a lot of the games I've played but this one... It reminded me of Lies of P, to find out it came out BEFORE LoP, I really truly wanted to like this but a combination of the buggy textures / physics, the abundance of french words spoken by people who predominantly speak English (that's on my part I am aware, but I can't help but struggle to follow with what's going on or care if I can't understand half the words used) ALSO there are so many cutscenes and so much talking its practically a visual novel with some fighting.This game is so poorly optimised that it takes my 3070 to 99% usage on MEDIUM settings, not to mention the 80gb game size, it's NOT that big I promise you, three locations use pretty much the exact same assets, enemies are either piss easy or tanky as all hell. Bosses have like 4 moves and that's it, The story was just really not interesting and I've managed to softlock myself in multiple places quite easily...However! This game does quite well with the movement, in the beginning it was clunky making it really awful to move around with but after a few hours of playing I started to understand the movement and got into the flow with it. The game does an awful job at a sense of direction, you're given a compass quite early on but it doesn't tell you that you can use it to make way marks to guide you where to go. This would be good IF the game showed you a clear path, a lot of the time the ares you are told to go just take you to clearly locked gates.In conclusion, I would highly recommend against this game, full price, UNLESS you know for a fact you can either speak french or are able to understand the words with ease (again that part is on me entirely) or can accept that it's less of a souls like and just an easy Sekiro??? Just get this game with a key or on sale, if you want to play a good souls-like game with this as a base, I'd definitely recommend Lies of P.Not the worst game I've played but sadly one of the worst Souls-like I've played, I really wanted to like it but they just needed to keep this in the oven for a few more months.EDIT : My first review was after 19 hours which was to beat the game, not including the DLC, I didn't discover you can easily be locked out of the DLC if you're not careful until my NG+I'm now over 50 hours and 6 times playing through to get these final achievements and I want to just again say how INSANELY BAD THIS GAME IS. I cannot stress how annoyed I am by the bugged game, bugged areas and more importantly bugged achievements. I've followed countless guides to assure I don't miss any of the side quests or citizen stories. I've sucessfully spoken and interacted with all the NPCs for the citizen stories and the game just decides to not give me the achievement. This game is beyond atrocious. The voices are too quiet even at 100%, whenever the game wants it'll flip my camera 180 degrees which have led to me dying countless times. The enemies are harder than the bosses 9 times out of 10, the DLC is underwhelming and useless, the game crashes whenever it deems fit and I cannot tell you how much I hate this game. I'm still playing this long because I'm craving this last achievement and I'm expecting to have to replay it three more times before this piece of ♥♥♥♥ decides to give it to me. Look at the r/PlaySteelrising subreddit and a lot of the posts there talk about how bad this game is and how buggy it is on console and on PC. I have absolutely found the worst game I have ever played in my entire life. This couldn't have even been close to a passion project or anything that the devs loved, it felt like they tried to cash in on a Souls-Like experience without trying to make it enjoyable. 2/10(Don't even attempt to 100% it, you'll bald in minutes)

_childDocuments_.review: So it is definitely a Souls-lite. The character customization is very bare-bones but I understand. The combat is solid but slow and calculated focusing more on elemental damage. The enemies and unstable versions are quite slow and easy to dodge around. The leveling system is quite good and clear on what you are leveling. The weapon upgrading however very expensive but makes little difference (stat ups boost damage more early on). The item descriptions are a bit too detailed  (IE sometimes having a few paragraphs to just say its an elemental bomb). Story is OK but the cut scenes are very frequent and I have a hard time getting over that you are in 1800's France yet all the voice actors have almost 0 accent and when they do speak french, its only 1 or 2 words similar to broken french.All in all 7/10 decent game
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: A steampunk souls-like with excellent art direction and story. Don't be misguided by the average score, it is a good game that offers its own view on the souls-like combat system, and for that has found some disappointed detractors. It is hard to say whether the game is easier simply because, unlike dark souls, you're not fighting the controls, or because the difficulty is actually lower. One thing that is true is that I enjoyed the gameplay much more than I did the one dark souls game i played (dark souls 1) and that is simply because it is much more refined, mouse+keyboard friendly (you absolutely do not need a controller to play this), and the platforming side is actually intuitive and rewarding.The game itself is somewhat on the shorter side, even if you take your time I doubt you'll be sinking more than 30 hours into your first playthrough, with subsequent ones being much faster.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Mon Dieu!Steelrising is a "Soulslike" from developer Spiders and initially offers pretty much exactly what you expect: lots of action-heavy fights, loss of your currency when you die, leveling up at rest points. If you're looking for a Soulslike with a very cool, crazy setting , which is comparatively easy and can be child's play if desired thanks to its freely configurable level of difficulty, the game is definitely worth a look. And the French have not only copied the powerful and varied combat system, but also added a few interesting ideas of their own. The different and numerous weapons in particular invite you to experiment with their various extra abilities. Very good for getting a taste of the genre.Easy 100%!

_childDocuments_.review: Steelrising has a lot of potential, set in an alternate Paris where automatons dominate. The concept is intriguing, and the world design is impressive. However, it has its issues. The combat system and animations feel clunky, there are performance problems and bugs. Nonetheless, it's still worth checking out./!\ Steelrising runs well on Steam Deck, around 45-50FPS using low settings, frametiming is a bit all over the place, texts are difficult to read. "SILVER" on ProtonDB.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not intending to shield Spiders, but I believe this game got bad rep for free.The game is not perfect (I am yet to find a Zelda levels of polish in another game, so I would argue that actually no game is perfect) but I don't find it to be particularly bad.I'll start with the problems:Inconsistency:Do You think Aegis (the character) will climb that ledge? Well, think twice, because it might not work... Or does it?Do You think a command will stay consistent along the menu? Well, not alwaysDo You think "she" can traverse that area... Well, it depends...And so on and so forth.The game is easy: The combat is DS1 levels of simple, which I don't find to be wrong, in fact, I am enjoying the experience so far, amend the inconsistencies... Yet, the AI is far from smartThe systems are highly exploitable... But We should be familiar with that at this point. Are We going to ignore That in every Fromsoftware title enemies can attack through the walls? Or the infinite amount of healing in DS2 (don't make me talk about the bosses in that game, please... What a joke)?The good parts: This is going to be my GF's first souls, since is like a light version of one. I'd call this a souls-light. So, if You only came for the dificulty, this one is not for You.The ambient, world design and narrative are pretty good. They do the same as Assassin's Creed regarding the storytelling (fantastic history) and it works wellThe combat is simple, but clean. I have something to say regarding terrible animations, high tracking and terrible bad telegraphed move sets... But it is not regarding this game but Lies of P. I believe that this game is better polished (combat wise) than LoP.The systems are easy to understand, which also plays well with my GF's play through this game planAre You lost? Do You have no Idea of What You are doing? Ok, They can add some markers for You if You decide to equip and use the compassAre You lacking skills? No worries, They offer guns (similar to magic builds in ER) that can and will Your life easier... And don't worry about resources, they support Your play style by providing enough and more of what You need All and all, I haven't experience weird deaths like in the DS games or ER? (I died of infinite falling from a meter and a half ledge in DS1, DS3 and ER. Annoying).I haven't experience any game breaking bug yet... Damn! SOTE (ER DLC) has (d?) a missing collision in a wall inside a catacomb and nobody is talking about that.So, it is my believe, that people is throwing ♥♥♥♥ to this game for free.I bought this game like 2 years ago and I am playing it now, because I was expecting Lords of the Fallen levels of bad, but it is not the case. In fact, I bought the first cosmetic pack of my whole life, just to support this guys.Keep up the good work and get better at what You are missing.7/10 It is not a game to throw a party for (even if people is celebrating another crab's treasure, notwithstanding the buggy mess it gets to be, only because the game is cute) but it is an acceptable game with a bad reputation, coming from people expecting to play DS4.

_childDocuments_.review: It is enjoyable and could infact be an excellent entry point to someone new to soulsborne likes.  The gameplay is a little too easy for a Dark Souls veteran however.  Some negatives:-There are still occasional crashes-The stat scaling is not great; you either feel weak or way way too over powered-The graphics are not great either; the water on the street cobblestones looks MUCH better than most people's faces and those eyelashes of Laclos... dear god why do they go INSIDE his eyelids?!-Side missions have a bad habit of displaying waypoints you are not able to reach without progressing the story further-Be warned that points of no return ARE advertised in-game as such, the only one you can come back from is the DLC point of no return which takes you to the Bastille area (that one you can come back from and revisit later)If you can look past the flaws, there is a fun game here tho.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this one. It has excellent weighty combat - I went for a parry based build and found it incredibly satisfying to turn the machines' attacks back against them. The visuals are great and I had experienced no problems with performance; the game ran fine with highest setting and ray tracing on my 3080 with no stutter and not a single crash. The only things I'd change is the side missions which drag you back through familiar setting with extremely sketchy navigation (the compass often fails to chart the correct path). These are optional but I felt compelled to complete them even though they were not as rewarding as the main story bits. The difficulty could do with some balancing as well. I chose the dancer class and started out quite weak which meant each encounter was exciting as I could be killed in one or two hits. By the end the enemies has not scaled with me and I found I could charge in and absorb a lot more damage. Perhaps I was getting better at the game but even the bosses posed little challenge and the sense of achievement for killing than was slightly diminished.All that said it's still really fun to play and worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Steelrising

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I usually have a very hard time with "soulslike" games but I try to persevere and do get some enjoyment out of them.  I LOVE Steel Rising!  The story is cool, the characters are interesting and relevant, and the way they weave history into the narrative is a lot of fun!  I think that most of the negative reviews are just nitpicking and once you figure out Aegis' rhythm you will find that the fights are satisfying and fair.  I think the only thing that makes this a souls like is because there's an endurance meter.  It's not as hard as Dark Souls or Nioh or anything, it's good for people that want to enjoy souls like but, like me, are terrible at video games!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been enjoying this game quite a lot. I was expecting one thing, and was honestly surprised to find another. The game setting is wonderful, the history is nothing to write home about, but its very enjoyable and concise. Graphics wise, there is indeed a few FPS drops, but I am playing on Steam Deck, only, so its understandable.Now, to my biggest praise to the game: this is is a Soulslike game. Its meant to be punishable, and hard. But, Spiders, in what I will consider one of the best decisions I ever seen a game developer make, decided to add an assist mode: were, if anything becomes too difficult, you'll be able to use it, and at least, be able to experience the game you paid for.The addiction of this caused a lot of backlash, and a lot of anger, unfortunately...The addiction of this mode caused so much backlash that, upon seeing it, I genuinely started to question my taste for video games, (a media that brought me so much happiness until now). I, for myself. will, once again, praise Spiders for this. Many players, like me, love Soulslike games, but, cannot, for varied reasons, either skill or time, spend 10 hours in one single boss, and this mode will help and not alienate anyone. Enjoy the game. It is an awesome game, and an awesome developer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 4th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Dark Souls with Marie AntionetteSteelrising has some interesting thoughts. Marie Antoinette is decrying the French Revolution. Though in this universe King Louie has created automats, basically clockwork robots. Marie has her own loyal version, Aeris, controlled by the player. Steelrising starts with this interesting concept, however, once you choose your archetype and start the game there are French influences, but so far it’s another Dark Souls Game. There are great choices for the Art Design and the combat feels fluid. Well mostly, the dodge is more of a side step that never feels as good as a full tumble. Overall this is a game trying to not be like other Souls-Likes so you have stuff like a massive jump but lack the weight and feeling of a Souls-like Combat, it’s being different but different isn’t exactly better in this case. Pick this up if you’re a fan of Souls-like and want a B-Tier entry. You can also look at the other games Spiders, the studio behind this, has made. That includes games like Greedfall and Of Orcs and Men. They’re interesting concepts but overall I don’t think they are the top-tier games people will be raving about. Still, it’s a Souls-like. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre attempt at a pared down Bloodborne clone. It does nothing unique or interesting in terms of gameplay, and the story does not make up for it in any way. You play as a living machine, yet they completely fail to take advantage of this. It is a cookie-cutter game with some style and little substance, and the style wears very thin once you get used to the recycled assets and backtracking. I think that there were a lot of very easy ways they could have taken advantage of the admittedly interesting world they created to make a better game. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the more accessible Souls-like games. Arguably the best one to recommend people who wish to get started with the Souls-like experience thanks to the assist mode. There is such a unique style to the character designs and animations and steampunk setting, I just wish performance was better.On an RTX 3090 I barely manage 60fps at 1080p (upscaled to 4K via DLSS) with Raytracing on and all other settings maxed out. I can't recommend using Raytracing at this time as it offers little visual improvement at the expense of a lot of performance. I can tolerate the 60fps if the frame times were better, I was getting a projected 60fps most of the time with 1% lows of sub 30fps at times which made for a really jarring experience. Otherwise turn off Raytracing to stabilize performance.Otherwise, based on the first hour and a half, performance could be better and enemy designs could be more varied, but that could change the more I play. It's still a mostly solid and unique experience despite how much it borrows from other Souls games. So far I give it a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably worth it on a sale, I'd really like to give a neutral review but steam does not and likely will never allow that.Let's talk about the elephant in the room. Technical issues. This game runs *really badly*, the recommended specs are a joke relative to how the game looks. On top of that it does not allow inverted camera, or rather it only allows it on the Y (up/down) axis, want inverted X? No you don't, not according to the devs at least.The devs clearly lack confidence in their level design abilities since they decided to spam invisible walls around quite literally every corner, the game feels extremely constrained and railroaded because of this.The combat is nothing to write home about either, the weapons are pretty haphazardly balanced with some being orders of magnitude better than others, not that it matters overmuch. The general design philosophy seems to be relatively sparsely populated (read: empty) levels with the occasional mook ambush, these are not a threat. Then there's the inevitable "mini-boss" room which is one or more (usually more) very strong enemies that hit like a firetruck and have enough poise to just ignore your attacks. If you randomly get shot by an enemy far off in the distance you've likely stumbled upon such a room, oh and the ranged type enemies have absurd aggro range (realistic, perhaps, but it's not very engaging to just get slammed with a shot from an enemy you didn't even get a chance to see).The stamina management feels, for lack of a better word, 'bad'. There's nothing obviously wrong with it at a technical level but it feels weirdly punishing, this might just be because your bars are in the bottom left corner so it's harder to see them when playing, but it's harder to get a feel for your stamina use than in... let's say dark souls 3. Additionally the stamina recharge delay is extremely punishing, likely to incentivise using the self-harm effect to recharge faster.Speaking of stamina, the dodge does not feel very good to use due to a combination of having practically no i-frames combined with some rather intense tracking on some attacks (that probably shouldn't have anywhere near as much) as well as some pretty suspect attack timings from certain enemies. That, and some rather strange hitbox choices frequently leads to getting hit by attacks you should have cleared. The best strategy for dodging seems to be dodging away, which is counter to wanting to actually hit the enemy with your attacks, this further reduces your practical attack window. You could, of course, also just use the block feature if your weapon has it but this trivialises combat if you play slow and methodical.Now we've already discussed weapon balancing, but armour balancing stands to mention as well. Armour balancing is practically nonexistent. Every new armour set you get is, more or less, a strict upgrade from what you had before. Do you like what your current armour looks like? Sucks to be you, it doesn't help that the game tends to dump armour with resistances suitable to the level you're in as well. If you're in a level with a lot of fire damage it's going to give you fire resist armour and fire resist consumables.For what its worth I do like the modules system, it's a compromise between power and progress gating in a way that traditional ring slots cannot realistically achieve.I don't... hate this game. I also can't recommend it outside of a very steep sale either. It has too many problems and doesn't run well on current hardware, let alone hardware from when the game was released. Future hardware may alleviate this but that's beside the point (and my machine is more than overkill sporting an Rx 7900 XTX and a Ryzen 7 5800X3D).

_childDocuments_.review: I initially had a negative review due to performance issues and a lack of universal block/parry. I still think those are issues but I think the game is HALF decent. I am returning the game, though, because it's not for me. Performance issues: Running 2k screen with medium graphics on a 2080 super and watercooled 10 series and constantly fluctuating down to 50 fps with really basic surroundings. I can usually run max graphics at 2k on any game with a crisp 60fps.Why I don't like the game: There is no universal block or parry move. Instead those moves are individually tied to specific weapons. Meaning some weapons can block, some can parry, and many can't do either. What's more is that dodging doesn't seem to have i-frames (maybe it does but didn't really feel like it when I played). So it seems that you're left with - pick a thin selection of weapons with defensive abilities or stay far away from attacks and get in little pot shots where you can. You can block attacks for 5% of your stamina and cause enemies to recoil, or get hit for 30% of your health bar. Sort of a weird balance.After about an hour with a defensive setup, I realized that the block and parry moves aren't even relevant because the enemy movesets are very limited. Just let them do an attack sequence, then punish them. It's just way too easy. They don't close the gap on you, they don't attack in groups, they don't surprise you, they just solo patrol. It's like a Steven Seagal movie.The art and animations and atmosphere all look great. Marionette automatons in the French revolution. Very cool character and concepts. But after playing so many good/unique souls-like games, I just can't get into an easy/slow one. Beyond the art, there is nothing uniquely alluring here.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried pretty hard to like this game but a few elements just sucked the fun out of it for me.Pros-Visually looks nice, some pretty unique looking enemies.- Special attacks are cool, felt different needing certain weapons to have access to parries or shielding but I think that cancels out the positive in a sense.- Customisation of the character is okay, since you are a robot after all.- The later plot related skills are pretty amusing to use, great utility and I won't spoil how they can also be used in combat (they are really strong). Cons- Felt a bit too easy? With the access to health regen relatively regularly and less aggressive enemy types I never felt like I had to go all out to clear an area or defeat a boss, with the other part of it being that the attacks are a little too telegraphed and having enemies parry your attack and still not hit you is very funny. I was expecting to be dying constantly  but the challenge simply wasn't there aside from one boss in particular.- Armour types don't seem to matter outside of stats. I just picked the heaviest armour and left it at that. Sure some of the resistances might be nice but better armour overall just felt more consistent.- Attack patterns per weapon are very uninteresting or rather it's just a difference in stats and your basic spear has the same moveset as the later ones, could have been nice to have something special per weapon even if it's something small.- Mild visual jank from time to time, for example enemies getting stuck on boxes or being too dumb to walk around- Level Design is pretty weak. Even with the extra help thanks to the compass there was several times I got stuck because it wasn't clear where I was supposed to go next. Part of this problem is that at times some chests or ledge look like they are accessible when they actually are not.tl;dr A French made and themed "souls-like" with a pretty unique plot that falls short despite trying some new things. Pick it up on sale, I've heard it's short to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some limitations, but I found myself continuing to come back to it. I completed the entire story, explored every level, and did every side quest I could find, so I would recommend it!The difficulty curve of this game is actually the hardest in the very beginning. However, once I found a weapon that I really liked and started to optimize my character around using it, I found the game getting easier and easier until by the final level I don't think I died once. You can also see where the designers had to deal with a limited budget. Most of the levels are either sewers, various types of palaces, or wartorn city streets, and the decorative objects used to make the levels are repeated again and again. The developers also did essentially no action animations on the human characters, so all parts of the story that involve dynamic movement of humans are told in flashbacks with large amounts of cutaways and darkness, or recounted in conversations while the human characters stand still. I get it - this game isn't made by a major studio, so they have to stick to a realistic budget. That said, even with the limited storytelling tools, I found the story pretty interesting. I liked both the high concept and the twists as you discover who you are and how the automatons work. And once again, the true test of whether a game is good or not is whether or not you keep playing it and enjoying it, and I found that I kept playing and enjoying this game for quite a few hours. I would recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: I will be reviewing Steelrising as a souls-like, comparing it to other similar games that I have played.I enjoyed the game, and I think the devs executed a lot of elements very well:- to my surprise, I really enjoyed the idea of 'What if French revolution but robots?'- Ludia and Automats look really cool, model designs are amazing- side characters and quests are well written, but are lacking in terms of actual game design (it is 90% just running around betweeen compass marks). That said, I was so invested in the story that I completed all of them- combat system is good but not great. I enjoyed itThere are some things which I would expect in a souls-like but they were not there:- The level design is almost entirely linear. You almost never have to choose which way to go and you never get lost. This is something that I missed a lot compared to Souls games- Build variety is lacking. First of all, I don't think there is a perk reset system. Second of all, weapon upgrades are quite rare (so there is little incentive to switch your old upgraded weapon for a new, unupgraded one). Third, some weapons are so OP that they make the others obsolete. I almost ran through the entire game with the weapon I found in the first location, and I enjoyed it.- Bosses are ridiculously easy, I killed all of them, including the optional ones, in 3 attempts or less (and I am not THAT good). But they make up for it with their looks, at least for me- Enemy variety is also not really there. Near the end of the game I just got bored and ran past everyone, skipping entire huge areas. Something which again would not be possible in Souls games because you would get lost, trapped, jumped on, staggered to death, etc.Still, I wanna say that I drop games immediately if I see that they are boring or generic. This one I completed, and I really think it deserves attention of other souls-like enjoyers, despite its shortcomings.P.S. OBVIOUSLY with a huge discount

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you're a huge Souls fanboy like me, Steelrising is well worth your time. If you're new to the genre, or you only played FROM Software games, I recommend you play Lies of P, Nioh 2, Salt & Sanctuary, The Surge 2, Mortal Shell, and Grime before you spend money on this. PROS:- art design is awesome, the enemy and weapon designs are very cool and thematic, especially bosses- gameplay is great- music, sound design, and graphics are okay- level design is superb, with LOTS of hidden paths, shortcuts, and areas you can find and explore- lots of main and side quests, so plenty of stuff to do. I could've easily played for another few hours if I wanted- story is okay. the villain's speech in the final cinematic actually tugged at my heartstrings- I guess the difficulty settings can be a good thing if you're new to the genre and scared to play FROM's games? Still, I'd say Dark Souls 1 with a knight build is easier than this and a better entry point into the genre.CONS:- needs a lot more enemy variety- loot is extremely underwhelming and mostly limited to consumables, so the awesome level design is somewhat wasted as you will rarely find anything useful- game is too easy even without assist mode, you basically get infinite healing potions, and you fight the same enemies so much you fully learn their patterns, so the game gets even easier as you progress- despite looking cool, bosses are way too easy, which completely kills the epicness of the fights- minibosses are just regular enemies with a big healthbar- you can easily enter areas you're not supposed to enter yet and get softlocked as a result, forcing you to commit suicide and lose your souls in order to get back to the game proper- optimization could be better, but the game was comfortably playable on Asus Rog Ally, and stayed in 60+ fps on a GTX 1070 on 1080p, so most people should be able to run it without issues- you can't respec, so if you wanted to try out different builds and weapon types on your first playthrough, tough luck. Conclusion:Longtime Soulslike fans should definitely check this out. It's probably not worth the full price, though. Get it on a huge sale. The DLC is pretty short, but it's worth it on a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Any Souls player will be familiar with 90% of the mechanics here, but it also has some neat little features I've not seen in other similar games. The combat is quite a bit easier than all Souls games, and that's even without using OP items like grenades. But the setting, environment, and story are great, as usual with Spiders' games. I'm getting consistent 105 fps on custom medium/high settings on a laptop (16 GB RAM, Radeon 6700M GPU, 5800H CPU).In 15+ hours of playing, the game has crashed on me once when the game tried to fast travel me after beating a boss. I do wish it was a bit more challenging (even without grenades), and the other small nitpicky complaint I have is that when you land from a jump the audio is way out of sync with the animation. It's jarring to me. Otherwise, very thrilled with the purchase.

name: Tails of Iron
detailed_description: Bright Fir Forest - Free Expansion Tails of Iron now includes ‘ Bright Fir Forest ’, a second free expansion that continues Redgi’s regal journey. Featuring 13 new quests (four story quests and nine side quests) this end-game expansion takes the young Rat King to the Squirrels’ renowned Festival of Leaf Fall, adds three new challengers in the Mole Arena, further broadens character customisation with new weapons and armour, includes eight cosmetic upgrades for the Crimson Keep, and more. King of Frogkind, the maniacal Greenwart has been vanquished, but despite the joyous celebrations in the forest, a new amphibious menace may be about to bubble through the pond scum… can Redgi overcome the emerging threat and be back in time to enjoy an acorn cup of Bright Sap under the luscious green canopies of Bright Fir? Your tail continues… Bloody Whiskers - Free Expansion Tails of Iron now includes ‘ Bloody Whiskers ’: a free expansion which introduces a new post-game questline, two additional difficulty modes, five new bosses, a selection of special armours and weapons, and a secret that was perhaps better left forgotten… With the tyrannical Greenwart now defeated, King Redgi’s vast lands chime with celebration. But the recently crowned saviour isn’t free to rest easy on his throne just yet. As decreed by an ancient Rat tradition, the new King must prove his worth… in a deadly trial of combat. Defeat the most lethal warriors from across the land to claim the key to the old King’s room. But what heinous secret lurks within? Your tail continues… About the Game Set in a grim land plagued by war, Tails of Iron is a hand-drawn RPG Adventure with punishingly brutal combat. As Redgi, heir to the Rat Throne, you must restore your broken Kingdom by banishing the merciless Frog Clan and their ferocious leader, Greenwart. As you explore the deceivingly charming world, you’ll encounter a cast of unique companions, ready to aid you in your adventure. And you’ll need all the help you can get, whether that’s new meal recipes, blueprints to forge deadly weapons and armour, or even a land-chugging, armour-plated mole mobile! Overcome your fears. Rescue your brothers. Restore Your Kingdom. Your tail has begun… Explore a Treacherous Kingdom Fully accompanied by the deep, raspy narrations of the legendary Doug Cockle (celebrated within the world of RPGs), prepare to embark on an epic adventure across the mediaeval-fantasy Rat Kingdom. Complete side quests and faction hunts for some additional gold-on-the-side, or join forces with a sharp-eyed companion to help even the playing field. Master Brutal Combat From frog zombies to gargantuan grubs - and everything in-between - the Kingdom is awash with danger. To overcome each perilous encounter, you’ll need to study your opponent’s attacks and react accordingly! Thankfully, there’s a range of deadly abilities at your disposal, including parry bashes and fatal executions, not to mention ranged attacks with your nifty bow and arrow. Customise your Attack Adapt Redgi’s combat style to the task at hand. Heavy armour may provide better protection but can you really afford to slow down your dodge-roll? And then there’s the question of weapon; axes pack a punch, while spears are quick and nimble. Perhaps you’d prefer the all-round performance of a trusty broadsword? Overcome Savage Boss Fights While danger lurks around every toadstool, you’ll need to keep your wits sharp and your blade sharper when it comes to the devastating boss fights. Cold-blooded in every sense of the word, these oversized amphibians each present their own unique combat challenge, and you’ll need more than a good set of armour to come out on top. Brew Recipes, Craft Weapons, Forge Armour Redgi’s keep is also home to his brothers, Rem-Rem, Bam-Bam and Dug. Rem can cook up a health-boosting feast with ingredients found throughout the world, while Bam can craft new weapons and armors from special blueprints you’ll uncover… if you look hard enough. And then there’s Dug, who’ll update you about new quests available throughout the Kingdom. Features: Master brutal combat, inspired by the souls-like genre, featuring dodge-rolls, parry bashes, and fatal executions! Explore a vast and treacherous Kingdom, comprising six distinct biomes, each with its own hidden paths and secrets Immerse yourself in a compelling story, narrated by the deep, raspy vocals of the legendary Doug Cockle Customise your attack style with a vast array of distinct weapons and armour Assemble a band of brave companions, ready to aid you on select missions Complete side quests to earn additional gold-on-the-side Unearth special blueprints to forge new and powerful weapons Collect rare ingredients to cook up health-boosting feasts Overcome savage boss fights against the Frog Clan’s deadly, oversized generals Lose yourself in the gorgeous and lovingly-crafted 2D hand-drawn art style.

_childDocuments_.review: To what extent do the developers of a videogame recognize and learn from the shortcomings of their gaming inspirations? Do these developers apply critical thinking as a way of carefully and thoughtfully separating what is good and bad in each of the gaming titles that inspired them? Or do they just simply stare at these gaming titles with slaw-jacked reverence, as if everything these games do is inherently and unquestionably good? Tails of Iron, a game that wears its Dark Souls and Hollow Knight inspirations on its sleeve, sadly does far more of the latter, which is why I have to give this game a negative review.Case in point, let's take a look at what happens every time you die in this game. Here are two important questions to ask on this matter for any "Souls-like" genre games such as this:: Dying is something that happens a lot by design in this genre, so surely the developers have made sure that there is minimum downtime and frustration after each death, right? : Considering that the developers have designed a game that has first-time players dying frequently to bosses, surely they have incorporated options like quick boss restarts upon a player death so that they can immediately get back in the action and work towards overcoming this boss hurdle, right?The answer to both questions is a depressing no. When you die, you get sent back to the nearest checkpoint that you just activated. Dying to a boss means getting sent to the checkpoint you last activated outside the boss room, since there are no checkpoints you can activate inside boss arenas. This is already an issue, considering that dying to a boss means you always have to deal with runbacks to the boss arena. To the credit of the developers, the game always provides checkpoints generally close to the boss arena. So in this game, you thankfully won't have to deal with treks back to the boss as cancerous as (say) the Flamelurker runback in Demon's Souls, which takes close to 2 minutes to perform from the nearest checkpoint all the way at the start of the area.However, since deaths don't happen only once or twice in this game (or in other Souls-like games), the amount of time a player wastes in death screens, post-death loading screens, respawning and running back to the boss and actually landing the first hit on a boss -- . Let's say you die a minimum of 10 times per boss in this game. Let's say it takes you 20 seconds from the exact moment you die to going through the post-death loading screen, to waking up at the bench, to getting off the bench, to running back to the boss room, and to the exact moment you are able to start a boss fight. This game has roughly 20 bosses. (At least I think it has that many. I didn't bother doing a proper count and I didn't do any of the post-game DLC bosses.) So let's do the math:All of this is just wasted time that does not enrich the gameplay experience in any way. For me, it raises the question: Why not give players the option to instantly restart a boss as soon as you die? So many action games have this option. Why? Because sensible developers know that players who die to a boss want to instantly get back in the action and try that boss again. Nobody actually likes runbacks of any kind (the people who posture and pretend that long runbacks are good only say it to make themselves come off as super hardcore gamers, and they don't count as serious individuals). Now let me add one more major complaint about the death system in this game before I move onto my other complaints: the post-death "wake up" animation. Nobody likes having to wait like 2 seconds after dying and exiting a black screen in order to regain control of your character. We get it. The developers played Hollow Knight. Redgi sitting at a bench to save progress and activate a checkpoint is just like Hollow Knight! The player dying and then reviving in a sitting position at the bench is like Hollow Knight! The player spending 2 seconds sitting down before you can even regain control of your character and move back to the room where you died to the boss is like Hollow Knight! Just because Hollow Knight did it doesn't mean you should do it. Hollow Knight doing it was dumb. You copying this stupid mechanic and putting it in this game was even dumber, since there was no way you actually enjoyed having to sit down for 2 seconds after dying a hundred times in Hollow Knight. Yet you put it in this game anyway. Why do Souls-like games do everything they can to make failure feel miserable? Traditionally, in videogames, failing to defeat the boss was already a punishment, since you have to redo the fight from scratch and having your progress halted. Yet, with Souls-like developers, it always seems like a contest to outdo each other in punishing players for dying.
