_childDocuments_.review: While this game does have positives to it the lack of polish is unbearable. While I did try to enjoy this game it quickly became clear that near the end of development the developers found they were running out of time and just threw some things together. About a third of the game is spent running back and fourth doing side quests through the same rooms killing the same grubs and mozis. Additionally many of the attacks seem to not be prepared for anyone dodging or blocking any other way than the intended way resulting in weird hitboxes sitting around attacks that they decided you should block (even ones without the block indicator). Hitboxes in general needed a lot of work. Enemies were spammed even in boss fights. Many attacks seemed untested. And then there is bloody whisker mode, it is the hard mode of the game required for 1 achievement of beating the final boss (yes you have to replay the entire game for 1 achievement) and to make it harder they just made you take more damage and made hitboxes worse. this is the first and I hope the last time I see a game try to make itself harder by making the hitboxes more obtuse, they also just spammed more enemies in bloody whisker mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: If you love the gameplay of Blasphemous with Batman style "rock paper scissors" combat you'll have a good time.It's a combat platformer with very little room for experimenting with different playstyles but it does have a wonderful aesthetic.Unfortunately it's been slapped with the "Souls-like" tag when all it really has in common is punishing combat and a refillable healing flask, so personally I didn't get the expected experience and will have to revisit when I'm in the mood for this kind of game.That said, this is clearly a well made game so if this is your wheelhouse I can recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: It has a great combat core mechanic, nice atmposhpere and art.The regular: The music and the story.The Bad: It has repetitive "side" quest that are not optional at all. This makes you travel the same map again and again to fight the same enemies. This is not fun, specifically in this game because the way the character moves. I'm going to explain what I mean:This game is mixing two things that should not be mixed. 1. The combat mechanic needs you to be precise and thougtfull (Soul like). So the character movement is slow and non acrobatic. Ok, that's good design.2. The map backtracking is non optional and excesive. Something that require a fast and smoothless character platformer control to be fun. See were the problem is? You can't have both, unless the character move set drastically change from combat to exploration, or you make it more linear, allways moving forward.I know I'm way to late to the party, and this game has been reviewed by everyone at this point. But if someone reads this I just wanted to say: Understand what are the strenghts and weakness of the game/genre you are making. Understand the reason behind the mechanics, before just adding them because they exist in other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Beautiful art style and assets moving in the backround.- Enjoyable and catching story.- When combat is done right, it is a plesant experience.- The Narrator has done an amazing job.- The Souls-like + Metroidvainia combitnation is pretty neat.Cons:- Medium Mode is too easy and there is too much of a difficulty spike in the frog invasion stage of the Hard Mode.- Doges should genrally make you untouchable for a split of a second but in this game that is not a case. That leads too to many unpleaseant situation in which you are being ragdolled across the room.- Red attacks are often undogable due to the lacluster telegraphing of the Enemies,- Multiple minor visual bugs (like floating or missing assets).- There is a chance you can block yourself out of obtaining the "Complete Redgi's Armory" achievement. At the beginging of the Frog attack sequence, you can miss a Light Helmet #10 under the broken bridge, behind a breakable barrel. Later this bridge is repaired, thus preventing you from getting all achievements.- Game constantly reuses the same boss movsets, bosses, and does this irritating thing, when there are x quests in the same location, but you can pick only one quest from each quest board which leads to consatnly running back and froth through the same areas.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, I first tried the game just to see if my boi Geralt(I know that's not his name, but who cares, it's ya boi Jerry of Raviolli) was actually a narrator, turns out he is, all the way through the game. The thing I didn't expect was for the game to be SO much fun. It's a very simple game, both in mechanics and story, but it does all of it VERY well, it's super polished and aside from that, the artstyle is phenomenal. If you're one of those people who go for the "1$= 1 hour of content" BS approach on games, then wait for a sale, the game only has about 10 hours of content if you do everything. But if you enjoy brutal and meaty melee combat and you like buying indie games to help out companies that deserve money far more then the "triple A" garbage, the by all means, this is something you won't regret buying (or just get it on greenman for a better price).A few more details:Combat- is a beautiful dance of blocking/parrying/dodging at the right time depending on enemies attacks and the attacks have a lot of weight behind them. Just be aware this game is melee focused...there are no ranged/magic etc builds or anything like that, it's not an RPG.Story- is simple fantasy stuff, but it's very charming...just don't expect any mindblowing twists.Music- very little of it and it only plays when rats with instruments (bards) are on screen, which I found funny.Artstyle- fantastic, you can see it in the screenshots.Hope to see more content and more variety from the next one. Cheers to the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly as a game its not great, its clunky, bad hitboxes and repetitive in alot of ways, also progress way too fast i feel like i only just started and already have my stats maxed out which i presume means the end of the game is near so ya just too short. The artstyle 100% saves it and the overall notion of going through and rebuilding the kingdom is really sweet plus the world is pretty cool. Get it on steep sale for sure
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conscience recommend this game.The story is basic, which may across as oddly charming, but something is just unsettling about the tutorial, which aims to paint the MC as an underdog maybe too much (something non-descript and ordinary would have come across better). The sounds they use in dialogs are horribly ear piercing and maybe squeaking would have been better since these are rats? No idea here to be honest.Gameplay... It tries to paint itself as Dark Souls in 2d, but it fails horribly in every aspect. Why you ask? Well, every enemy has three types of attacks and you have three types of defense, however you have to use the exact defense on that exact type of attack, more like QTE in some games than Dark Souls. To expand on this point, were it more Dark Souls you would have those three types of defenses, but you could have used those on every type of attack, but the harder style defense (like parry) would have some incentive for you to use it. For example stunning the enemy for a short period of time. It shows the basic misundertanding the develoeprs had when designing this game and does not paint a very good picture about core design philosophies this game has.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review just so I can warn any like-minded people about a simple mechanic which completely ruins this for me from the very start. It is the fact that the controls are not tight. Simple character movement has an acceleration to it. It is not this game's fault that I recently played Hollow Knight blind, but going from that to this was very difficult. So, its not so much that I don't recommend this game. Its more like I want people to be warned going into it. I will probably replay this properly at a later date and revise this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: as someone who doesn't usually enjoy combat oriented games, this one surprisingly reeled me in! honestly i find timing the parries and dodges so fun, kind of like a rhythm game without the beat! combat Can be clunky at times but nothing that gets in the way that much. i will note; the original keyboard mapping really takes a strain on your left hand while your right hand barely does anything (the mouse is just for attacks), if you don't use a controller id either skip this one, or rebind everything to the keyboard completely so you can use both hands (personally i did arrows to move, WASD for the other stuff). maybe that's just me though, but definitely improved my gaming experience and my hand doesn't hurt anymore trying to move, parry, dodge, shoot and everything else with one hand haha
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Playing on bloody whiskers mode. Cool game although frustrating at times. You can fight a boss, reach the next one, play other games for a week and come back without feeling lost. The story is simple yet it can surprise you every now and then.I have no idea where reviews complaining about this not being a metroidvania are coming from since there is nothing in promo materials saying the game attempts to have a non-linear gameplay. You should also take the souls-like tag as "hard game" because weapon differences are minimal so you are in reality locked into one fight style and exploration is limited to a handful of side bosses and areas.There are almost no i frames and there are no recovery frames. I.e. if you don't get up immediately after getting hit you are going to get hit again.There are some problems i don't know if are intentional or just lack of polish:Bosses will input read/have instant reaction to your movementsSome bosses will chain an unavoidable combo if you get hit once and delete your entire life bar even with almost max armor and racial resistanceHitboxes can be a lot larger than the animation makes you believe they areThere is some degree of randomness in some attacks. I.e. an aerial attack consistently lands right in front of you if you don't move but every now and then you get hitSome attacks are not dodgeable unless you have a millisecond reaction time or is lucky to be in the correct position before it startsAgainst multiple enemies you will sometimes be in a position where getting hit is unavoidable because two enemies are attacking at the same timeThe only thing i've found straight up unfun were battles against more than one boss at once.I wouldn't say there is replayability once you finish it aside from doing harder modes or speedrunning.If you get frustrated easily, don't recommend buying because you will die and there will be nothing you could have done differently to avoid it. If you like the art style and like difficult action rpgs this game is aight. Wait for a sale if unsure.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I like this a lot! Very cool art, great music, narrated by a Geralt sounding fellow. Other than the narration, all story telling and conversation is through graphic thought bubbles. It's neat! Even your inventory has very few words- it's all communicated through pictures (with not many exceptions)I'm still early on, but the combat feels very weighty, and the splashing bug guts are satisfying. It's a well developed system, and it does feel unique, not just another side-scrolling knock off. You feel like you're really delivering crushing hits against shields, and repelling your enemies attacks in a way that just feels good.The world-building is excellent so far. Definitely play with a controller. It recommends it right in the intro screen, but if you don't have one/don't like them, I think this would be weird to play M+KB. That's my one caveat.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Look, it's probably my own damn fault for buying a Soulslike when I generally hate Soulslikes. But I  did not enjoy this one, as much as I wanted to. I loved reading Redwall while growing up. It has an interesting art style and so on.Also, I'm a furry, so there's that.These were not enough to salvage a game with truly bewildering hitboxes--a concept utterly crucial to have locked down airtight for Soulslikes. Instead, it was just depressing and sadistic, with interspersed moments that felt actually unfair to the player instead of merely to the protagonist (another cardinal sin, even for the genre).Like any game, there will be people who adore this game, surely. I, however, cannot be one of them. I have put up with Gitting Gud for a number of games better than this at feeling worthwhile (the Monster Hunter series, for instance, which I've expended far too many hours of my life upon), so it is not merely that I am not up to the challenge; indeed, I finished Tales of Iron's campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: For the fans of Redwall - 100% matchAmazing piece of art. I've finished it in about 15 hours.Good story, wonderful narration, great sound design, I really enjoyed the graphic style and animations.Also I love rats, they are truly loving and joyful creatures with a very short live.Shout out to Dennis, Robin, Dug, Rem Rem, Regi, Rexy and Pinky <3

_childDocuments_.review: How to make graphics that won't age? Produce a work of art. Despite the simple plot, the game has a unique atmosphere thanks to the visual and sound layers. Without unnecessary complexity, it allows the player to smoothly enter a unique world. On top of that, the developers implemented an excellent combat system. I don't even know what to call the genre itself. The gameplay draws from many sources and does it very well. I look forward to seeing more.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Game in  1 sentence : Rat became King and finally killing Frogs Don't know who to root for because I don't know which critter is more troublesome IRL...Overall the narration is on point and you get a tremendous satisfaction  after killing the bosses because the devs actually added some praising to the players who beat the bosses kudos to the developersPro Tip : Remember to Block with shield , because dodging always doesn't workIf you are new to the souls like 2d Platformer games , I highly recommend this game as it's a good jumping base for new players
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. Lovely graphics, good music, amazing atmosphere and fun gameplay that is good amount of fair challenge on normal. Sometimes walking back and forth was approaching annoying and some of the content added after the release felt repetitive, but these minor downsides didn't diminish my enjoyment of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The game Tails of Iron has been a kind of salvation for me. When you've been sitting for a long time not knowing what to play, this game suddenly appears and captivates with its visuals. The artwork in the game is beautifully drawn and meticulously detailed. The eyes rejoice at the incredible play of colors. The game tells a rather amusing and engaging story. I really liked the references to various characters (such as Thor). The bosses are not easy at all, and the combat is excellent. I played this game on PC with a keyboard and mouse, but I didn't like the controls very much. I recommend playing with a gamepad. It took me 20 hours to complete the game, and those 20 hours brought me immense pleasure. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:  Recommendation as long as you play the game on Easy or Normal.  Hard shows glaring design flaws that are best left unseen.I recommend this game PURELY for those who will play it only on easy or maybe normal difficulty.  The amount of absolutely frustrating and un-fun fights in this game on hard mode almost made me not recommend this game.  A good balanced game will make me go "ok, i messed up and that was on me, i need to get better".  Not this game.  The longer the game went on, the less and less fun I had. The more I thought to myself "That was horse crap!"Bosses which combo you into oblivion with no counter once you are caught in it.  Enemies doing so much damage there is basically no point in putting your weight limit into the "heavies" zone; you'll just be 2 shot anyway.  Also, bosses and enemies which sometime launch attacks offscreen... so you have NO idea if the attack they are doing requires you to dodge, block, parry, or counter attack!  And the WORST offender:  going into an execute animation with other enemies on screen, so you are locked into it without your consent.... then the moment it ends, another enemy hits you, with zero frames to react.   Its not a very in depth game, but I bought this game knowing this.  There is a lot of charm and the art and scenery is so fun to look at as I run from place to place.  The game crashed on me only once and i lost no progress.  So pretty much no bugs which was a major factor in why i did recommend it.  A lot of love was put into this game I can tell.I completed this game on Hard purely out of SPITE.  I stopped having fun half way through the game.... and that's not a good sign.  The worst feeling out of all of it was how close all this was to a overall solid game.  With just some fine tuning and some rebalancing it could have been so much better...So again, I recommend this for those who play on easy or normal.  Hard is doable, but don't except to enjoy the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron's beautiful and unique art style takes my breath away with each new scene. I am continually in awe of the scenery and the creative thought and effort that has been put into each detail. Being a fairly new gamer, the combat in this game is quite challenging and it took some time to learn the mechanics, but once I got the hang of it, it became very satisfying to defeat the more difficult battles. I also love the calming narration of Doug Cockle (Geralt of Rivia), who's tone of voice fits in perfectly with the grim yet lighthearted story. I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I truly enjoyed most parts of the game, however there are certain number of "buts". Let's start with the good parts of the game. Visual style, art, music and voiceover are great. Art style and professional voiceover really got me sold on this game. It really is that good, however combat and difficulty scaling are somewhat weak parts of the game. This game centers around combat so it not being enjoyable personally for me is really a punch to the gut. Hitboxes, both yours and your enemies are broken, you get hit when you clearly dodged the attack and you will sometimes miss the enemy that you are standing right in front of. Difficulty scaling is kind of iffy too, first you start off against weak enemies but very soon you will be facing giant bug queen with crappy equipment and weapons that barely scrape her. If you are willing to power through broken parts of the game, I.E combat then I would recommend the product.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is a wonderful little game. From start to finish it has a gripping story, filled with charming characters and beautiful visuals. The gameplay is fun and is often rewarding. I highly recommend it to anyone who is a fan of games like Hollow Knight. Now it's time for the longer review. Spoilers as always. I’ll have them marked. (Inspirations)Tails of Iron wears its inspirations on its sleeves. A lot of the little references it has are recognizable yet natural. Adapted wonderfully into the game without issue. Things like the quest board have been seen in many games, though this one seems to be inspired by The Witcher. Other things like the benches are very remnant of Hollow Knight. This one felt a bit more out of place, but quickly became alright with me as the game went on. Not every reference was adapted well. There were a few lines of dialogue that were more or less just direct references changed into rat puns. These were still nice but felt a little less earned than other ones. (Gameplay)The gameplay of Tails of Iron is a tricky fish to review. While I really like it, there are some glaring issues that crop up here and there. The primary gameplay lies in the game’s combat. Almost every enemy encounter was very fun. A challenge to overcome but not one that was poorly put together. These encounters felt rewarding as with bugs, you not only got currencies from looting them, but you regain healing juice as well. It helped me feel like I didn’t need to backtrack to a barrel in order to heal. There were a few encounters however that didn’t feel so pleasant or rewarding. The way the enemy AI is programmed can result in some pretty messy fights where your actions aren’t related to you being hit. Sometimes a gank fight can result in one or two enemies lining something up that is completely unavoidable given the situation. These are more at the end of the game but are still a downer when you encounter them. (Weapons/Gear)There is a plethora of gear that you use throughout the game. I love the options the game gives you for taking on your challenges. You get swords, axes, spears, bows and more. Along with that, you have your shield and armor to help keep you defended. These pieces of gear all have their uses, the armor being the most useful with their specified defenses against certain enemy types. These defense values are imperative to the combat as they do block A LOT of damage. Your armor is also split up by weight. Heavier armor being slower to move in but allows you to take more hits. Honestly, when it came down to weight, I barely noticed much of a difference between light and heavy loads. Some actions like dodging particular attacks were more noticeable in difference, but really weren’t huge. So you can use whatever you like if it suits you. The enemy specific defenses will matter more than your base defense. Weapons are a tricky fish. These things feel just fine as they are, but also feel lackluster with what they provide. It isn’t clear whether or not the different weapon types have different effects on different enemies. The game never tells you anything about it, so I just assumed it was all the same. Really it does feel the same. The weapons have great design, and all feel good to use. There wasn’t a single one which I felt personally offended to wield. Though there is one huge issue with them. I never felt overpowered or underpowered. I only ever felt adequate during my playthrough. I feel like a lot of this has to do with the weapons. No matter how high your one handed or two-handed attack is, you will always spend a fair amount of time with each enemy or boss. Not as much time as with lower attack weapons, but you won’t be breezing through them.  I don’t want to feel like I’m absolutely destroying an enemy, but I’d at least like to feel like I’m strong. Even with this though, the combat is fun enough to excuse this issue. (Story)The story of Tails of Iron is brief but bold. It’s a classic tale of a scorned hero on a journey for revenge. It’s something we’ve seen before, but it’s rat themed now. I may be biased, but that’s a pretty cool take on the formula. Even though the story theme is something we’ve seen before, how it’s told is what makes it stand out. Each character is lively and has a good sense of individuality. Some rats feel samey, but not so much that they fall out of being unique. Each one comes together to build up a kingdom that is exhilarating to explore. Seeing all the small details etched into each scene. These things all come together to provide an excellent setting for our story. Throughout the game, we are made to feel bad for poor Redgi as he battles the frogs. Tring to rebuild his fallen kingdom. We get to see the effects of Redgi’s efforts as we go along. Slowly watching life return to the war-torn streets of the kingdom. The losses Redgi faces aren’t small, and each goes a long way in making the player feel for Redgi. It’s a great motivator for seeing the journey through to completion. And what a journey it is. Taking us all throughout this kingdom of rats. From the forests surrounding the Long Tail Village to the depths of the rotten swamp the frogs call home. Each having it’s own challenges that must be overcome so that Redgi can fulfill his duty of rebuilding his kingdom and avenging his family. It’s a tale told in few parts, but with lots of significance in each part. The whole thing is pleasantly narrated by Doug Cockle as well which is just a treat. (Conclusion)Tails of Iron is a short but sweet title featuring plenty of action and entertainment. It’s flawed in places like all games are, but these flaws aren’t too bad that they ruin the experience. I recommend this to anyone who is a fan of games like Hollow Knight or The Witcher. I’ll throw in some bonuses for people who love rat or frog related puns. Well, animal puns in general. And good ones too.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this Tails of Iron, but ultimately I cannot recommend it as a 2D souls-like. It's very cute and I was genuinely enjoying it until , but then the pacing really hits the breaks.You're tasked with performing underwhelming side quests that the game even lampshades with a line from the narrator, observing how normally kings send their subjects to run these errands. Questing is made all the worse by the baffling limitation of only being allowed to accept 1 at a time. You'll be running in circles between the same bounty board and dungeon until you have enough currency to progress the story. Shortcuts, a beloved feature of better souls-like games, are absent from Tails of Iron.The above wouldn't necessarily be bad if the gameplay loop was fun, but I grew to dislike combat after the admittedly strong beginning. You're frequently trapped in arenas, forced to clear an entire horde of damage sponge enemies (usually only 2 at a time) with your single-target attacks as they enter from both sides of the screen. This sometimes happens in places you've previously explored. Enemies are invincible until they've finished walking into the arena and some of their attacks have no telegraph. Even telegraphs can be so short that you might not have time to respond if you've already committed your own attack and have to wait to recover. Also, dodging doesn't have i frames that I could notice; instead, its purpose is to preemptively flee incoming damage zones.I'm not thrilled about leaving this negative review, but I can't help but think how much better Tails of Iron would be if it were a 2.5D hack-n-slash/beat-em-up, fully embracing linear levels, fast pacing, and interesting set-pieces to stop and fight in. Instead, we're left with a fundamentally flawed 2D metroidvania that feels almost ashamed of being a souls-like. I truly wish Odd Bug Studio luck going forward, but this game has soured me, so I'm taking my leave from this series.

It doesn't appear to be anything new or groundbreaking, and yet its better than every other game of its type i have played.- Fighting is simple, yet combat is challenging if you are not careful, and prepared. - The story telling is well done, and with "The Witcher" narrating the adventure you cant go wrong. - The art style is great, and the environments have obviously gotten some love and attention with plenty of      depth and detail.- Music and sound are on par as well, the music is dynamic, coming in during combat, or in certain locations, and the sound effects are solid and convincing. _childDocuments_.review: I'll try to keep this short.  I didn't find the combat to be "brutally punishing" so much as just not impossible to lose at. I suppose if you aren't somewhat used to games that require timing, patience and a bit of grit to overcome, this game will seem quite hard, but for everyone who's played games that let you fail, this should feel comfortable enough. It isn't incredibly deep, though, and both lenient in some ways (while you are shown how to redirect your shield while it's up, for instance, you will automatically block and parry attacks from any direction if the button input is there, and parrying isn't very tight for a soulslike), and unfair in others (regis sometimes seemingly doesn't grab ledges, and iframes, while there, aren't generous).  It's also rather short. I spent about 10 hours playing, and have completed everything except for the last hidden boss and the final arena round, both of which are post-game activities (and are a fair bit harder than everything that precedes it). What's there, though, is wonderfully executed. Pacing, showing the player the ropes, the world-building, sound, music and voice acting (mainly being that of geralt of rivia's VA), art direction and story all culminate in an engaging and simply GOOD game. It's a bit linear, in that sidequests aren't usually optional and there isn't much to discover once you've cleared an area, but I finished the game feeling very satisfied. The setup of quite cute woodland critters brutally slaying each other is very emotive, and reminds me a lot of watership down, albeit with much lighter themes.I dearly would've liked to have explored more of the world, but that's my only real qualm here; the game's short lifespan.I hear many people lauding it as GOTY contender, but as much as I'd grant the makers their accolades, it is simply too short to qualify imho.  Still, this is a game and studio worthy of your time, attention, and, insofar as this kind of game appeals to you, your money. Yes, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: An adorably gruesome tale! Following Redgi's tail as he battles great odds, to reclaim his home and claim his throne, was so much fun. The combat is was really enjoyable; 9/10 times I died because I knew I hit the wrong button. For my adventure, I chose Bloody Whiskers mode - dunno why - but every time I died I wanted to get back in there.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game on bloody whiskers mode (highest difficulty), so I cant judge how the game feels in lower difficulties.I had alot of fun playing this game. Even the normal enemies can kill you if you dont watch out. Bossfights felt somewhat like a dance. On bloody whiskers mode every hit hurts. I dont know if its how it works, but it felt like you cant get oneshoted. One hit did put me on 1HP. So it seems like you cant get oneshoted(?). Also it didnt feel like there is something like I-Frames. This game works more like: are you in front or behind an enemy. So you have to pay alot of attention to your positioning. That beeing said, I have to admit, I did beat the game only through a little trick to gain more movement:Your "escape" consinst out of two parts. First comes the dash and then a roll (so you have to press dodge 2x to get to the roll). The dash feels agile but the roll doesnt. At least I ALWAYS got hit when I used the roll. That beeing said, the bossfights were quite fun. As I already mentioned, they felt like a dance. If you know every step, its alot of fun - if you forget one step you might feel a foot on yours...and with foot I mean you get hit in the face with a truck. So you feel if you mess up (I'm looking at you stomp attacks....). Also I mentioned that it feels like you cant get oneshoted. This remains true but most likely if you get hit once, the bosses can start combos of death so you will die anyway. But if you get it all right it just feel so amazing. Normal enemies were hard too but the more I got the hang of the game, the easier they got.The story is entertaining and the artstyle is just gorgeous.But it is not perfect! Spontaneously I had soundbugs which were deadly in bossfights. But those were easy to fix with a restart. And my biggest negative point might sound silly, but it is what it is:If you saved on a bench and die, you have to watch Redgi (you) first taking a seat before you can stand up again. This might not sound like a big deal - and for most people this might just be irrelevant - but if I die in two hits from a boss, I dont want to watch Rechie taking seat 50 times before I can stand up again. It just feels like wasted time. So feel free to give this game a try. It was fun to play and if you want to explore the story without a big husstle, just dont pick bloody whiskers.All in all: If you are interested in this game, feel free to give it a try. The game sucked me in pretty fast. Worth the money!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Over all, I do have to say, this game is great. Does LOTS of things right. Especially the visuals and the music, and for a 2D action adventure, combat is done quite well too.However, there are several complaints I think the devs should hear:- early game spoiler. Any player that is mildly paying attention when they play this game, will likely notice very quickly that 4 species of opponents are labelled immediately. Perhaps, like with weapon types and ammo, question mark cover them, until the player first encounters an armour for it? I noticed pretty much immediately, and the existence of moles was therefore not a surprise.- "Get off the bench" I'm not sure what the problem is, but whenever I save, or have just died, it takes a lot of effort to get off the bench, and I find myself saying this line near constantly. Suggestion: spawn Regie off the bench, when you respawn? It would help flow a lot.- I can't remember quite how far spread a problem this was, but at least in "The Village Sewers", there were at least 2 barricade fortifications you need a 2 handed weapon to demolish. And several vines. If they weren't constantly self resurrecting, it would be far less annoying and flow breaking.- Side quests, are not side quests, if they are mandatory. Most, if not all the missions labelled as "Side Quest" are non-negotiable to complete. Therefore the game looks like it should be slightly open, but really is quite linear. Maybe just label them all as "Board missions" and "Arena bounties" or something.- There's not much that can really be done about it, but in the middle-ish section of the game, there's a LARGE potion of you just fast travelling back and forth, "Hi I've finally returned home... you want me to go where? Okay, off I go. Hi I'm back, did that thing! ... You've got another one? Okay fine, catch you later. Woo finally got that one... you're kidding me, another one? And you can't do this yourself because. . ? I am the king, you know? I have slightly more important things to do"- Poison. Um, does it do anything? Or is it just a placebo? It definitely doesn't do any significant DOT to enemies, that I've noticed (many tests occurred, but not rigorous ones, just visual). Does it just boost the actual damage you deal? If so, why bother colouring the health bar of bosses?- Oh... and Jey should have their music box playing a lot more often.But yeah, as said before, good game, lots of content, lots of fairly well made mechanics, the constant mini arenas through some areas were a little tiring, but fairly fun, certain battles were really well crafted, music in certain places is stella, art style superb, continuity of what you select to wear: EVERYTHING is visually shown, and I love that, quality of life is very little, story all lines up, so no immersion breaking points. Thumbs up, well done.

_childDocuments_.review: i've never left a negative review before, but here goes.  i wanted to like this game, but right away the game was messed up for me because you cannot change the controller options.  this makes no sense, i've never heard of a game that actually didn't let you change your controller layout.  it even suggests playing with a controller, but why suggest a controller if you can't set it the way you want?  anyway after some fiddling around, i managed to change the button inputs in the "controller setup" option through steam, and it worked ... for about five minutes.  literally while i was in the middle of playing (trying to get the food from the basement, i hadn't even started combat yet) the controls randomly switched back to their defaults.  the controls changed in mid-game and even though they were still changed on steam, the game had returned to their defaults and nothing i did could fix it.  it is the most baffling and incomprehensible thing i've ever experienced in a video game.  i've read some other reviews and comments from people have problems with their controllers, so i'm not the only person who had trouble with this.  sadly i'm not wasting anymore time on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I've been playing for 30 minutes and all I can say is the combat is atrocious.  The rest of the game seems charming enough.  But even thier "indicator" system for when an enemy attacks is more of an indication of "when they'll attack once they've done the laundry and gotten around to it".  The window for those indicators is either cartoonishly wide or embarassingly short.  I only fought the first 2 available enemies and there was no semblance of timing.  Way too much fake-out and posturing for reflex fighting to be viable.The whole thing feels insanely clunky like one giant QTE game instead of some action adventure.I'm returning it.  I'm sure the story is nice once you get past the terrible battle system.

_childDocuments_.review: Adventure-focused souls-lite game in forest-critter setting.✔ dedication to the setting - lots of background details, especially with the rat-folk and how some locations change as time progresses✔ rough, bloody style✔ extra post-game boss encounters❔ lots of bosses with small number of other encounters (compared to other souls-like games), but at the same time it feels like you fight minibosses instead of having big, meaningful encounters✘ I wished for some interesting boss encounters with (relatively) huge animals, but it's all based on humanoids and some insects✘ unnecessary padding in the early-mid game when you have to do a series of quests, each forcing you to go to the underground and then back for another quest, instead of letting you do them all in one visit✘ on top of that annoying respawning blockades and vines, so that each time you have to cut them to go through...✘ disincentivises exploration (do not go anywhere you are not lead by a quest - there won't be anything there and another quest will make you go there later)Overall it's good, but not great. Doesn't excel in any of it's component parts like combat or worldbuilding, but it was a positive experience overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Semi-linear metroidvania with some soulslike combat. Send ups to Redwall and Mouseguard and a sparse yet meaningful story. Folks might not like the lack of iframes on your dodge but really it's a game of simon says. With that being said, I'm impressed with how the devs were able to shake up combat situations with that concept. I don't usually go out of my way to finish everything in games, but I just about did it all and then some in a matter of two days.

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy game, from getting stuck on benches, ladders and other interactable objects, taking full damage upon entering an arena from an invisible boss object and needing to quit out to the menu to fix it, all the way to the most infuriating of all which is bosses bugging out and breaking their patterns leading to undodgeable attacks on top of your ranged shots sometimes just straight up not registering despite seeing the enemy have the damaged animation which makes the broken ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bosses a lot harder than they actually are, this has the effect of making bosses feel extremely tedious by having "I've done my long winded attack cycle now, it's safe to hit me or you risk me bugging out if you go in for 1 more hit" which is gambling literally 99% of your health. This game needs A LOT of polish, not only in cleaning up the game bugs but also """side quests"" being mandatory making everything linear instead of open world. If you're looking for something like Hollowknight, don't be swayed by the art style, that's the only thing these games have in common, which I do admit is charming. Work on some of these issues and I'll come around to it but this is the game where I've asked myself "why would you design something like this?" more times than I can count and I'd recommend a pass till some of these issues are addressed unless you're only interested in playing the "narrative" and default difficulty, which is a shame, it could become a great game like Hollowknight if it has proper effort put into it.Other bugs I forgot to mention:-Your parries will not register sometimes .-Unique drops like armor and weapons will disappear from their pick up zone if you die without visiting a checkpoint, you have to quit out to the main menu to be able see them again to pick them up sometimes.-Not sure if it's a bug but right now the amount of fall damage you take is almost static, you can drop from the highest ladder at heavy encumbrance and take nearly or the same amount of damage you do as falling from a mid height at no encumbrance. If this is an intended mechanic to skip slow descents then maybe consider adding a prompt to slide down ladders.

But finally their works are just something pure unbalanced and torturing. _childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: So before the negatives I will say I 100%'d the game at first for usual gaming reasons, but bloody whiskers was easily the worst contender, so from that perspective I'd say not a fun time.Graphically this game's pretty cute, I like the many small details strewn across the game in many areas.As for the negative, a few points:- Voice of Geralt was at first amusing but not a selling point. After awhile it gets really irritating to have to repeatedly hear his same lines, mostly in cases like certain boss fights. Also, it's obviously Geralt of Rivia, it's going to get in the way.- Heard a criticism once of this game mentioning needless backtracking and I agree. A lot of the game time is basically back and forth between same areas when the story needs to because suddenly you can't go any further until you can basically afford to unlock the story, aka do the "side missions", which to my next point:- Side missions are nearly non-existent. Other than a few exceptions, pretty much all of them feel mandatory to the game to get gold for essential items that it's both unenjoyable and unnecessary. It feels like a confusing design choice overall when it feels like you're mostly going to have to do essentially most of them.- Also, lots of other confusing mechanics that really get blundered. The resource system is a joke for starters, as the resources become extremely abundant later, and in some cases their usage makes even less sense, (i.e give x20 items to a rat for a poison refill, when soon enough you can just use the checkpoints for free), or worse, become obsolete.- Playstyle also feels cheated in a way. There's honestly little to no actual place to change much besides weapons of choice, but even then the game ends up in favor of more dodgy builds as the challenge ramps up, not to mention the fact that the shield is either not going to reduce damage even when used or the fact that even with good resistance choice you'd still be better off dodging.- Speaking of cheated. Bloody Whiskers difficulty is kinda frustrating. Sure, on one hand you can defeat every boss by learning the pattern, but it doesn't make each encounter in the world fun when basically everything can nearly kill you in a handful of hits. Thankfully there are some merciful systems to exploit, but otherwise the difficulty feels like fighting enemies made of sponge, that spew nuclear fire.So all in all, definitely not worth initial price, not sure if even worth recommending really either. Other than the graphics, which are pretty nice to look at, this game just has some really odd choices of design that take away from my experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation's great, with a good narrator (Geralt of Rivia's voice actor), but from early gameplay (so take this review with a grain of salt), it doesn't seem like the combat will go anywhere special. The gear you can get doesn't seem to have any interesting properties, it's just weight and damage values. The ranged weapon autoaims.The combat's solid, though a bit confusing at first, because the dodge roll doesn't have any invulnerability that I could find, which you'd expect in a Souls-like. Enemies, at first, seemed like they had too much health for how uninteresting it was to attack them, but I started appreciating their higher health. It provides you more opportunities to make mistakes, or to over-commit, and lose health. The difficulty is nice, and it's interesting to figure out when attacking is safe. The only problem I have with the combat is that it has no flair. No Hollow Knight charm system, seemingly no difference between different melee weapons, no special properties that encourage you to attack or play a certain way to do more damage or debuff enemies.Pretty early on you start unlocking sidequests (the game even calls them sidequests). This strikes me as a problem, because exploration isn't interesting at all with such limited mobility and a lack of tools for exploration. Any amount of exploration or backtracking seems guaranteed to be boring.

_childDocuments_.review: A compact rat becomes the one that makes all of the rules?Ladies and gentlemen, they did it. They created Jerma's perfect game.Jokes aside, the actual game's pretty damned good (six hours in at the time I posted this and I think I'm wrapping things up before the endgame right now), at least in my opinion. Combat's tight, story's decent even if it doesn't do anything particularly new and the art speaks for itself. If you came here expecting a Hollow Rat/Dark Frogs jaunt that'll probably keep you going for about eight hours or so, you won't be disappointed. Plus Geralt of Rivia's narrating the whole shebang. 'Nuff said, really.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron: A Rat-astrophe of Fun!I'm not sure what's more surprising, the fact that rats can wield swords or that I actually enjoyed getting my furry little butt kicked repeatedly. Tails of Iron is like a medieval cartoon crossed with a hardcore roguelike, and it's absolutely bonkers.You play as a rat prince who's trying to save his kingdom from a bunch of froggy invaders. It's like Bambi meets Game of Thrones, but with more fur and less Bambi. The combat is tough but fair (mostly), and the art style is so charming it's almost criminal.I've died more times than I can count, but every respawn is just another excuse to dive back into this rodent rampage. It's like a never-ending cheese-fueled adrenaline rush. If you're looking for a game that will make you laugh, cry, and scream all at once, Tails of Iron is your oyster. Or should I say, your cheese?10/10, would get eaten by a giant frog again
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Grabbed this up after reading a few reviews and watching the trailer and glad I did!I went into the game with a curiosity for how they would handle RPG elements and combat in a traditional side scroller. It reminded me of old school Wonder Boy meets that classic book series RedWall. It was a nostalgic hit for me.The mechanics were simple but well executed. Combat was just challenging enough to keep you on your toes but not so intense to need breaks (Ahem.. Dark Souls) I found the art style both endearing, charming, and savage as they didn't pull any punches on cartoon gore -- which I respected. The audio and atmosphere of the game really shines as they choose a fantastic score and really delved into their world building. Well! for what you saw of the world it was fantastic -- as you progress areas change and new NPC appear in the background and foreground. My only gripe here is that you do revisit areas a lot but I can appreciate that this is a new IP and they had to make cuts somewhere -- again, I will say, that their pivot in trying to evolve the areas, after your progression through them, does freshen them up each time and make the game feel alive and dynamic.RPG elements! Not heavy handed by any means, more of an action RPG light. You don't pick stats or anything but there is a vast array of different loot that you can adjust your stats with. In this way, customisation feels natural and earned through the iron price. No crafting or cooking, A quick assortment of side quests that are mostly necessary to complete the main quest. Nothing overly inspired here but very fitting to the story. To keep the game paced out I believe they chose that you could only have one active quest at a time. This was a bit annoying but if they hadn't done this I could see the game being considerably shorter. You do feel weird going from the same 2 sections of map repeatedly when you could have struck out to tackle all obstacles at once. Hopefully they can make an adjustment with the next game with an assume-ably bigger budget to indulge more content. Again, new IP so I only warn this so others can shrug it off as well and see the potential of what was created.The story was straight forward in the fallen prince revenge and rebuid plotline. There are some nice quirks though that got me excited for the possibilities. I wish they could have explored more and spent more time in certain areas. Very good showing for what I hope is a first game of a continued series.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I've often heard that the better a work of media is, the harder it is to write a detailed review. I absolutely get that now. Tails of Iron is one of the best games I've played in the last decade. The combat is fluid, the art is wonderful, and the world-building has an incredible attention to detail which rivals many of the big name western rpgs. The only reason I'm not playing this thing from start to finish in one sitting is because I am forcing myself not to.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Visually it's nice, the controls are bad and slow to respond. You can rebind controls but the game really wants you to play with R1 as the attack because the other actions mostly make sense where they are. You can't fall off edges, you need to jump down. Unfortunately I know some fat kid is playing this thinking he can live out his fantasy of being a furry warrior and that bugs me a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply pure art, I have gone through some moments of stress and problems that exhausted me mentally and caused me discomfort, but playing this game was so beautiful and not only was I able to ignore my problems for a moment to breathe and be serene and even happy. , but that each victory at its maximum difficulty (yes, I have a problem that causes that if I do not play any solo game at its most extreme and insane difficulty allowed, I do not have enough fun) allowed me such ecstasy and feeling of victory similar to that my favorite games (Souls-Like) cause in my mind, making me able to analyze my problems with that same calmness and be able to move forward, I love this game and I look forward to 2......Long live the Rat Empire and to the Mole Republic
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is an alright game, but it's incredibly short and there isn't a lot of boss variety. There's a few archetypes that the bosses fall into and once you've "figured out" (very generous way to say it because the patterns are as telegraphed and easy to follow as something from a Zelda game) their moves, there's not many surprises left. I beat the five bosses they added in about half an hour because I already knew their attack patterns from the rest of the game. I didn't use anything heavier than medium armor because the way they increase difficulty is to make enemies move faster, so it's pointless to have any delay in your dodging. Weapons also didn't really matter and there are just straight upgrades throughout the game (a sword that is lighter and has better attack power, for example, than a similar one you have earlier in the game rather than alternative weapons that matter and have different pros/cons). The only wholly unique boss fight is one of the "secrets" within the Catacombs and his health/attack rotation is so small that it's over way too quickly.Ultimately, the reason to play this game is the charming atmosphere because it was very easy (I played on Normal, so I can't vouch for Bloody Whiskers, but the shallow combat and the side quests that you're forced to do to progress don't make me want to play again) and there's not a whole lot of depth. I really liked looking at a lot of the locations. I wouldn't recommend picking it up for more than 10 dollars if you care about bang for your buck.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Really wonderful game made with a lot of love. I really enjoyed my playthrough and can recommend this game. I got two criticisms: the backtracking from sidequests is really annoying and hurts the flow of the story and the missing Iframes make it sometimes tedious to fight bosses and multiple enemies. But overall, BUY.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A well put together Side-Scrolling Souls-Like, with a nice story, enjoyable combat that's not too challenging and lovely looking design.Combat could have been a bit more in depth, but for just under 5 hours to 100% the whole game it doesn't get dull.The games length itself is a bit short, but it doesn't overstay its welcome and drag it out for 40+ hours like some other games but rather; leaves you wanting more.Would recommend, mostly for when it's discounted more heavily in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks great and plays very well. It is challenging but not pointlessly difficult. The world is fascinating and the enemies are engaging. I really get a sense of development and looking forward to each coming upgrade. I am about half way through and so far I have not felt that I am grinding or anything would be a chore.It is an absolute must if you are a fan of Redwall, Mouseguard or Mausritter!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Cool art, nice atmosphere, neat music, good narrator. The combat though is atrocious, especially playing it on bloody whiskers (hard) mode. Hitboxes are inconsistent, bosses give you barely any time when telegraphing their move and of course they can shot themselves across the arenas. Total lack of i-frames also means getting hit can stun lock you to death and will which just feels miserable due to aforementioned hitboxes. The game also features a ton of weapons and armor, though half way in you get the best weapon in the game and while there is different weights of armor, you don't actually want to engage in it and instead keep yourself super light so you have a  better chance of dodging attacks that as mentioned are poorly telegraphed and reach across the stage. So that whole system just felt pointless with just using the same weapon and the same armor for majority of the game.I really wanted to like this game, but the combat is just so bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A great stylized indie game! Progression is very linear but nicely paced. Combat feels good and enemies give visible indications of the type of attack they are going to execute. It's a relatively short game, ~11 hours for me to collect all the medals, roughly 3 hours of which were post-credit content added to the game after release. I can recommend the game to anyone that likes metriodvania style games like hollow knight but doesn't mind a shorter more linear experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: As others have pointed out, this games art work is truly amazing.  But what sets it apart from most games (at least for me) is its simple story and gameplay.  Unlike most other games where the minions you fight are basically cannon fodder and easily dispatched, the frog enemies in Tails of Iron are/ can be formidable.  But as long as you keep your wits about you and properly attack, block and parry at the right moments, you will be victorious.  Like I said, the game is fairly simple."Simplicity's sometimes toughest to master." - T Bug.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended with a few caveats. Controls are not as responsive as I would have liked, some tells for attacks are unreadable (at least for me) and basically it was a guessing game in some fights. Story is charming and the art I thought it was great.The big con was the excessive backtracking (probably due to lack of budget), and the obligatory side quests (don't disguise them as side quests when they are not it).But overall, it was an enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I'm biased, I own rats and I do Were's Wally genre illustrations with rat themes, so this one speaks to me.Doug Cockle (VA of Geralt) really sets the tone of the game with his narration, making the game about cute storybook characters feel extremely grim dark.I can't comment about the gameplay as I don't really play souls like games or side scrollers but I've had fun with Tails of iron.If you want a game that's well illustrated well voiced acted with a nice revenge story you'll enjoy this title ( extra points added if you like rats)
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: In comparison to the games from the same genre I would say that there is too much unnecessary backtracking especially in DLCs. Art is nice, gameplay is meh, terrible hitboxes. There are too many items in this game with bad stats. I was on the verge of quitting and not finishing this game when I had to backtrack for the gas mask.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Fun until the late game where you're forced to fight arena bosses to continue the storyline. I'm sure plenty of people enjoy fights like that, but the indicators of what to do don't match up with the actually necessary actions, and there's always one exact way you're allowed to beat the fight. If you don't do that one exact thing over and over and over until the boss dies, you lose. I still recommend because aside from the extremely restrictive boss design at the later stages, the rest of the game is great fun and very well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I normally did not like arcade-ish side scroll/platformer, so something like dead cells or castlevania-like is not on my wishlist,but this one is good, maybe because it's a souls-like combat. it has good art and atmosphere, also nice animation,combat is also of course great, especially the execution on final blow. I kind of curious though, is Geralt the narrator? lol and here's the cons :main quest is too short,side quest is too few,map and dungeon is also not many.kind of wonder too, what use is town for? only one shop with limited things to trade.I got maximum stones? or ingot? and don't even know what to use them for? such a waste.kind of thought they will be needed later on for maybe rebuilding or something, but it never happen.equipment lack uniqueness, the difference is just in weight, or attack/defense power, and resistance in armors, so it's kind of redundant to have many kind of equipment/weapon since it's better to just use the strongest. it would be better if shield or helmet also have a bit resistance to it, and maybe the weapon to have other effects or prefixes. well, at least that's how I prefer it to be :)all that combined resulting in just this much playtime, around 8 hours for me to finish. too bad, because I'm not satisfied at all.the only way out is probably just to play it again from the beginning...  in any case, I'd still recommend it,and I hope there will be sequel later in the future :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyable adventure. Ignore the kids tagging it as a souls-like. there is no similarity, aside from occasionally challenging combat.Some fights are infuriating but none take more than 5 attempts if you are able to handle games beyond button mashing.The worst fights are some of the later waves of enemies. Fighting a single enemy is fun - but it feels like the game was never intended for waves of groups. But that's only a mild nuisance.The visuals are great but make little allowance for being a game - its a battle of the grey-green-brown vs the grey-green-brown on grey-green-brown backdrop. The palette overstays its welcomeI am not a fan of the ragdoll animation system (prefer frame by frame) but thats the price you pay for a large armory and the ability to play fashion-rat

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty great souls-adjacent game. The presentation is incredible right out of the gate, the hand drawn art-style evokes a storybook feel and looks amazing in motion. The sound design is great as well, all sounds, and music are high quality and battles erupt in a suitably visceral and punchy exchange. The narration is also top notch, the voice of Doug Cockle (Geralt of Rivia in the Witcher series) is a welcome addition and brings a healthy dose of gravitas to the story beats.Combat largely consists of a dance between yourself and the enemy, as you learn from their choreographed attacks, knowing when you have a gap to strike and when to retract and defend are key. The game gives you three methods of both attack and defense; one handed weapon, two handed weapon, and ranged and dodge, block, and parry respectively. The enemy variety does a good job of making you utilize each of these tools and pulling off the perfect combos to win a boss fight is suitably enjoyable.While the game is on the shorter side; a completionist run is easily obtainable in 10-15 hours, it is time well spent. As I find myself with less and less free time, I have come to appreciate these polished and concise experiences and find that they are among the most rewarding and enjoyable times I have with games. Tails of Iron is a well-crafted game, and I would highly recommend it, especially if you enjoy your side scrollers with a little touch of souls.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A great side scrolling fighter / search action experience, with satisfyingly crafted combat, that doesn't overstay its welcome.It's adorable, and violent, and somewhat tragic and bittersweet. The environments are beautiful and dense, the animations are diverse and well done.Really nails the look of a storybook come to life.Only complaint is its quite linear at times. Only 3 weapon types for each slot (one handed, heavy weapon, and ranged), the "side quests" are usually required to progress the main story.Not much of a "side" quest if you have to do it, hehe.Must have for Rat Appreciators, they honk. THEY HONK! ; w ;Hoping for a sequel, i love these kinds of forest critter settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game immensely. It's fun, memorable, beautiful but a tad bit short.  Buy at full price to support the devs or now during the winter sale.  Tails of Iron strong points are:-gorgeous 2D graphics-a simple but engaging story-combat is simplistic but allows for some good skill expression. -many different kinds of armor and weapons-decent enemy variety -it's narrated by Geralt from Rivia Weak points are-for most of us the game will be too short. After around 10 hours I finished the game and got 99% of the achievements. -besides the Bloody Whiskers difficulty mode there is little replayability-the side quests force you to do a decent amount of backtracking. Overall despite it's flaws Tails of Iron is a great indie game and I sincerely hope that the devs will release a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Literally one of the worst games I have ever played.Cute theme and art, but the game is 80% combat and the combat is atrocious. Hitboxes are off, controls are poorly mapped and muddy, the enemies telegraph some moves but not others (and some telegraphs are simply false), and one-shot deaths are common. Plus, the game literally never explains how any of it works so I guess, google it if you want to play?The non-combat portion of the game consists of endless fetch quests as the main plot, and in addition side quest grinding is required to advance that storyline. It all leads to a lot of pointless retreading the same areas of the map in order to extend the gameplay length.Level design is absurd and very poor. Most rooms have lots of platforms, but your character is ♥♥♥♥ at jumping. Ladders abound, but if you drop off of one even a millimeter above the ground, you take falling damage. This serves no purpose except to make you waste time climbing all the way down a ladder rather than jumping off it from a safe distance LIKE EVERY OTHER PLATFORM GAME IN EXISTENCE.Just a total waste of time, the art style and theme made me want to like it but it's truly not worth your time even if free.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: For describing it like a "soulslike" game, combat wasn't  responsive enough for the level of difficulty. They limit your fight arena to extremely small 2d area's that allow 0 margin of error given that some attacks quite literally will hit half of the battlefield. Plus the addition to multiple enemies during bossfights make fighting very chaotic & frustrating. The off key whistling noises that the mice make while speaking gets annoying real quick. Visuals are great. Voice over is very Bastion like. But overall, the game is too clunky to be worth the visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall, it has rats in armour killing bugs and frogs, what more do you want??The art, world and characters are amazing and I believe is its biggest selling points. On the downside there were some pacing issues as some parts of the game felt slow and others pretty fast. Also at some point there were a lot of fetch quest that made you go back again and again to the same places to kill X enemies or a boss. I think it was the worst part of the game, but even that was enjoyable. Highly recommended game although I would wait for a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay mechanics are just plain annoying: only specific attacks can be parried and you gotta wait for 'em, same for attacks that can only be dodged. This means that any other attack it's there just to annoy you, you can either block it or dodge it but there's no reward for timing a parry against it (btw parries are really easy to do). Enemies have a ton of health and fights are long and tedious. Animations are awful. Gotta say that both story and narrator sound pretty good but I won't give anymore of my time to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: ------------------------------------------Tails Of Iron is a diamond in the rough. There a number of good things here but it is hampered by more than a few issues that prevent it from being a truly great game. The art and graphics of this game is it’s standout. The story is good but has bad pacing. The music is good but sparse. The combat is interesting but is mired with control issues. And the controls here is frankly speaking, not good – not bad, but not good either. If you can live with control and movement issues, there is certainly much enjoyment to find here. Tails Of Iron has a potential to be a cult classic – not good enough to be mainstream, but good enough to have gain key core fans over time. I look forward to seeing a sequel from Odd Bug Studio and improving from a certainly good foundation they’ve established here. Partial Recommendation. ------------------------------------------ The setting and the style reminds me of the brother’s Grimm fairy tales, and not the Disney kind, I mean the old-school 18th century German kind that has horror, blood and gore. The background is busy with parallax scrolling and  animation which adds to the atmosphere of the game.------------------------------------------ You play as Redgi, the newly crown king of the rats who has to save his ratfolk from an invading frog army. As cute as this sounds (and it does sound cute) the story gets dark very quick. War after all is pretty ugly and death comes often in this game but each character's death feel significant despite them having no dialogue or in-depth backstory.  The middle part is quite removed from the main plot, effectively being a collection of side-quests that do not add very much to Redgi’s arc. They're not bad, just not very good. It would’ve been better if side-quests somehow tie-in with the 3rd and final act and in any case, this is something that Odd Bug Studio could improve on in the future.  There are parts of the game where there’s only ambient environmental sounds rather than an actual background music. Some times this is warranted for atmosphere, but too often I find myself thinking that certain stages could’ve use more music. Shoutout to the sick Hard Bass track in Mole kingdom. ------------------------------------------In any side-scrolling action game, the most important aspects to nail down without exception are the movement and control, and  There is a drag and floatiness to Redgi’s movement. It is more noticeable during combat, where even if you equip Redgi with the lightest of gear, his attacks and movement are still sluggish compared to the enemies specifically bosses.  You can only jump, run/walk and dodge. And you can’t even do a jump attack.  seems wasted to me. Combat even though interesting, isn’t executed quite as well as I’d hoped.  While the combat move-set is slightly more robust than his regular movement, there’s only a limited number of things that you can accomplished with them, leaving no room for player creativity. The sluggishness in controls also compound an already stifling combat. For example, dodge doesn’t actually dodge, let me explain. Any dodge should have invincibility frames included throughout the entirety of the animation so that you can effectively escape from taking a hit. Dodge in Tails Of Iron works differently, where the invincibility frame is not applied through the entire dodge animation.  You can and you still have to use dodge (because it’s an integral part of combat) but timing your dodge now becomes even more difficult since the timing window to dodge is effectively cut by half.  Once you press an attack, you have to wait until the attack animation is finish before you’re able to input the next move, and yes, even when equipping light gear with little weight. This gets really frustrating especially when  While your enemies and bosses attacks and movement are quick and instantaneous, as if they operate on different physics engine. Even with color-coded icons telegraphing enemies’ attacks, there is barely enough time for you react to them given the unresponsive controls and sluggish animation, making the combat feels crippling and unrewarding.  Attack isn’t on X or Y (on Xbox Controller), rather they are bound to RB and RT. Why? And why can’t I have the option to rebind the keys? Having attack bound to RB and RT is just weird and simply shouldn’t exist on a 2D side-scrolling action game. ------------------------------------------Despite the issues, the game skirts by well enough for it to be mostly enjoyable. I am optimistic for an improved sequel from Odd Bug Studio. Partial recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun to play, has a beautiful artstyle, a rewarding combat system and neat, charming storytelling. It can get a little repetitive from time to time, as some of the quests and bosses in the game are used slightly altered multiple times, especially in the (post-) late game. I like the idea of the weight system, which lets you choose between mobilitiy/attack speed and the best defensive stats/the highest damage output depending on your playstyle, but as the game progresses, a large portion of the equipment you can find will be obsolete, because you got better rewards beforehand. Apart from these minor flaws it is a great game that i can fully recommend.

Not to say some fights aren't challenging, it just gets stale pretty quickly. but it's a cute side scrolling game to pass the time, and if that's what you're looking for, then this is a good choice.

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm entirely sold on the setting and concept, the gameplay is far too slow and tedious. This feels like a much larger project that wanted to do many things, but ended up doing a lot of things incompletely. The traveling system is designed for a large world, but character movement is too slow or stilted to cover the distances without getting bored by the lack of interaction with enemies or much else.I adore the idea of mice fighting for their kingdom, and I think that this game idea could be tweaked into something that's still challenging without feeling like its playtime has been artificially extended. _childDocuments_.review: is a 2D action-adventure with very light Metroidvania elements (1 item allowing to traverse a new area, and 3 health upgrades to find). The setting is low fantasy with anthropomorphic animals. The story follows a young vaguely-European rat king whose kingdom was invaded and father killed by vaguely-Afrikan frog raiders. The game is not an RPG by any measure - the story and the character development (health upgrades) are completely linear. There are no choices and no roleplay. The other critical issues are the narration - while the protagonist is as genocidal as an average action game main character, the narration brings attention to it (“he [the MC] would not be satisfied until every frog in his kingdom had croaked their last”), but not any reflection. The other “dialogues” are communicated via symbols above the speakers’ heads (e.g. an arrow, a thumbs-up), so the only spoken lines are from the narrator. It is possible to disable in the settings, but it is on by default.The pacing is slow - at every other main story point, it is necessary to complete 3 mandatory side quests to earn gold and purchase the next quest item, be it the materials for castle repairs or a piece of cake. Only one side quest (per board) can be active at the same time, which leads to 3 delves in the nearest dungeon and back to the board. Fast travel is possible, but limited to a few specific points. There are only 2 large areas, 1 final area, and 1 additional post-game area. In general, the post-game offers several actually optional side quests in different locations, with the Bright Forest ones having significantly less backtracking and all uncollected equipment becomes visible on the map. Finally, the combat encounters. On the Normal difficulty, everything is a hard-hitting damage sponge, with the game regularly locking the arena to one screen and the enemies walking in for about 20% from the border while being invulnerable. The combat itself sounds good enough in theory, but the quirks make it unsatisfying - there are blockable (indicated by white lines), parryable (yellow lightning), and dodgeable (red lines) attacks. Then there are no-dodgeable attacks (pink circles), with the enemy’s hitbox being far from their weapons or even bodies and the rolling i-frames being ignored. Some attacks, which are possible to block, do not have any indicators. Additionally, the enemies can stand on the same spot and visually block each other, so it becomes harder to tell when to act. On a positive note, the protagonist also can stand in enemies without contact damage, looting the insect type enemies refills the healing flask, which lore-wise is filled with bug bodily fluids, and the bosses’ movesets and appearances change as the battle progresses. The equipment is reasonably diverse - there are 1- and 2-handed melee weapons, several types of ranged weapons, and light, medium, and heavy armour, consisting of helmets and body armour. The issue is that within a type, the moveset is the same and the lightest item with the highest damage/protection is the best one. For the armour sets, the later light ones outperform the medium and heavy armour in terms of protection and weight. This is the only way to customise one’s build, with the ranged builds being less convenient due to the ammunition refilling mostly from the barrels next to some checkpoints. The NPC companions join and leave as the story dictates and it is not possible to choose them. They deal some damage and cannot die or be targeted. Some of them also provide soundtrack. The controls are as comfortable as they can be and rebindable, with 5-button mice supported. The game uses generously-placed checkpoints to save progress into one overwriting save slot (3 slots total), so if one wants multiple save states, using Windows Explorer is necessary. There are difficulty options and the difficulty cannot be changed after starting the game. The only bugs I have encountered are the odd hitboxes and one of the bosses had attack indictors covered by the arena architecture. Lastly, the visual design. It is delightful and reminds of old illustrated books. The locations change as the story progresses, most notably, the castle. The map is detailed and helpful, and matches the locations. Overall, while the game is visually appealing and does not outstay its welcome (I was able to finish it below 6 hours, including the post-game), with the lower difficulty and disabling the narration removing the more irritating issues, nothing can fix the poor pacing, the amount of filler content, and the complete linearity of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and satisfying. Combat is fun: there's a parry, a fast attack, and a heavy attack, and a real feeling of progression as I improved. I would try the same boss, again and again, and see the noticeable improvement. I'm not pro, by any means, but seeing myself get better was a great feeling, so compliments to the devs for making that possible. There are regular in-game location save points, so low penalty for dying. Just remember to save whenever you can.100% achievement is a HUGE pain, there is no map marker that indicates what items you have missed. If you're a trophy hunter, this might not be for you.I recommend the game for 8+ hours of fun.
