_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Beautiful Environmental Visual- Combat (2D Souls done properly.)- Linear Game Progression (No headache in figuring out where to go. I'm tired of open world games with a million hidden collectibles or quests that require specific guides.)Cons: - Character & Equipment Design: God awful. Almost as if the designer went out of their way to make the equipment ugly and undesirable.- Story & Dialogue: Almost as good as a middle schooler's mid-term project.- System: Basic. There's no weapon arts or any special attributes to the equipment or even the weapon types that separates them apart in a meaningful way.- Backtracking: Lack of better fast travel system and save point makes me feel that my time is not appreciated as the player. Even if you kill a boss, if you didn't save and died due to falling from a 1cm drop, you will have to fight it again.There's definitely more cons than pros in this game but the few pros make me recommend this game and anticipate that they improve/fix all the cons in the sequel. Please, no player wants to wear an ugly piece of armor made of toad skin or have a toothpick or a chipped toothpick as weapon options throughout the ENTIRE GAME. I would not hire the same artist that designed the equipment.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful rat game. The hand-drawn style of everything is one of the most beautiful I’ve ever seen, the music is awesome, you can literally run this on background and just relax, the gameplay is ok, not the peak of difficulty but it has its moments. Combat is brutal with a good dose of gore and feels authentic, bosses are not sponges and they have enough mechanics to be a challenge.The overall story is a classic fable tale with some creepish points, nothing more on this, but the characters are interesting, and that’s a lot considering they communicate only trough drawings. The narrator does his job perfectly narrating the story just like you could read it in a book.The game is unfortunately very short, it took me 10 hours with a calm pacing to 100% (at normal difficulty). This isn't exactly a flaw, this game lacks a lot of awful mechanics like farming or lose resources on death so it's 10 hours but 10 good hours.Overall a very good game from an unknown studio, a soulful work.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Redwall, Mousegard, Secret of NIMH, love all that stuff. There's an inherent whimsy and wonder these little mouse worlds that charms me every time. But I don't really like this game. Mostly because it's 90% combat and that combat isn't very good. See, the character animation in this game is really stiff and lifeless. This is a side effect of the of the motion-tweened, paper doll looking character sprites. Better character sprites and animations would have gone a long way to improving the feel of the player's attacks and the readability of enemy attacks. As it stands, our attacks feel weak and enemies awkwardly jerk all over the place, doing whatever they want whenever they want to. A few of them can even animation cancel, which the player can't do. And many have randomly placed invincibility frames where your attacks can pass harmlessly though them.This game is also not structured like dark souls. There is almost no exploration or adventure to be had. It's structured more like Painkiller or Serious Sam. Hallways followed by combat arenas followed by hallways, often the same hallway you just came through. The backtracking is made a lot more bearable by this games absolutely drop-dead gorgeous environments. Many have 4-5 layers and the detail barely drops as distance increases. There aren't many places to visit, but the ones you can visit are rich with detail and change over time as you complete quests. I wish there was a way to hide the UI so I could take some clean screenshots. Another nice detail I want to point out is that the music is all diegetic! Anytime you hear music, you can see a little minstrel in the background playing his heart out. It's adorable. Especially during boss fights.My last complaint is about the story. It's not much deeper than Quake 2. Make the bastards pay for what they've done. And while the narration is pleasant, I would have been more invested in the world if I could of had a regular conversation with some of the NPCs instead of getting some pictographs and narration. I understand the storybook aesthetic their going for, but I would prefer having some people I could actually talk to.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot less depth than it first seems. There's no character customization or stats, no experience or levels, no real skills to unlock. Combat is simplistic and repetitive. You don't really get information on what the stats do, you make some bars go up and down and presumably more is better, but it isn't clear why you would want to use a spear versus an axe, and whether it matters what kind of shield you have if you're fighting with a two-handed weapon. There are no numbers in this game, so you don't even know how much damage you do. It is pretty nice looking, but there's just too much backtracking and combat is too clunky and information about gear is basically useless. Not worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game. Gameplay is a combination of Redwall and Hollow Knight, art is Redwall and Darkest Dungeon, music slaps (though I wish there was more in the boss battles, as they can get weirdly silent compared to just walking through the village), sound design and the way of doing narration vs dialogue is clever and cute, all in all I have loved this game. I wish it was longer (with my first playthrough on the normal difficulty taking around 15 hours, though I know I've missed some things and there's apparently some DLC bosses I haven't found), with enough variability in play styles that I know I'll do another play through at some point. If Hollow Knight was a bit too vague about where to go and what to do, you're not great at keeping track of places to go back to later in traditional Metroidvania style games, then this is a good spot for you. There's enough exploration to be fun and interesting, with rewards that make it feel worth your time, but you're not going to get madly lost and have no clue where to go. Overall, rate it 8.5/10, thoroughly enjoyed my time, with very minor gripes that are really more wishlist items rather than negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definately has some strong points but there's too many annoying things that drag the experience down for me, mainly the objectives. Almost every 'quest' in this game is go there and kill/retrieve something arbitrary. To make this worse though your character will often stop at a supposed clue or hint, kneel down into a lenghty animation that adds nothing to the experience only to get back up without contextualizing/saying anything. These long and drawn out animations, which are also used for EVERY item you pick up, feel like a waste of time. Had they been used sparingly perhaps they would've made sense but as it stands they got really annoying after a few hours. The objectives also felt like busywork without contributing to a cohesive narrative, these adventures feel tagged on to lenghten gametime rather than deliver a good narrative. This is also because most side missions needed to be completed to earn coins so you can continue the main story. The game failed to make me interested or care about the world and it's characters even though they were masterfully voiced by Doug Cockle (Gerald of Rivia VA).Other than running around the place to complete tasks there's also a lot of fighting to be done. Here i once again felt the game came short, with unresponsive controls, sluggish dodging/blocking and boring enemies. Even the bosses failed to make me engaged which is a cardinal sin for 'soulslikes' as far as i'm concerned. There's a large variety of gear and weapons to be found but these are too similar to one another to keep you engaged. At least the level design and visuals were fun to traverse, as well as being accompanied by a fitting soundtrack. Nothing too memorable but enough to atleast somewhat make up for the lackluster gameplay/narrative. I did not encounter any bugs and performance was great so atleast the product is finished, however at this pricepoint it's hard to recommend this game (especially for it's lenght). I'd give it a mid rating if steam would allow it but it's not quite there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to an unwelcome synergy between a back pain and a sinusitis, I decided to empty the list of my un-played Steam games, at list a bit. I forgot I bought this indie gem back in the day, some Black Friday ago, and I totally recommend it. Tails of Iron is an interesting story-driven souls-like metroidvania, featuring the story of a war between a realm of rats against tribes of ferocious frogs. Story is largely inspired by Homer’s Batrachomyomachia, a parodistic epic poem telling the story of a war between rats and frogs in a way that mocks Iliad and similar poems. The story starts with frogs raiding a Middle Ages-esque Realm of Rats and the newly appointed King of Rats is player’s alter ego. The story is pretty linear, with true horrific moments and more humorous ones, there are genius intuitions like Samurai-resembling kamikaze frogs or forging an alliance with a fully industrialized Communist Republic of moles. Gameplaywise, it kind of resembles 2-D soulsbornes like Salt and Sanctuary or Hollow Knight, but in a less punishing way, more generous parrying time and an easy mode, so that those who find From Soft games ‘inaccessible’ will be happy to hear this (and will ignore this game anyway). There is some backtracking but nothing too deep or difficult. Even at an harder difficulty, challenge is pretty balanced and overall doable.It's a short game, I almost managed to plat it in less than 15 hrs (but I need a second run to plat it and no, I won’t do it). Ignoring all the collectibles and achievements it won’t take more than 8-9 rs. Another surprise is the narrator voice (mice, frogs and moles won’t speak), played by the same voice actor playing Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher series. I totally recommend this indie gem, because small studios like these are the ones who keep videogames still decent, since big companies seem only able to milk people with addiction-inducing microtransaction traps, forced diversity BS and grindy-grifting boring stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game with great art-work and a nice atmosphere! I don't like souls-like games, because I don't enjoy learning patterns and repeating fights ten times, but all in all the combat seem tight.Here's what I didn't like, just to add some constructive criticism:The storyline seems like they abandoned some reveal half-way through, or maybe you get there after the credits. There were a few light plattforming parts, that I absolutely hated, because it feels like they randomly changed the distances on a few plattforms, in order to check the plattforming-box, but not adding anything to the game, except tedium.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Whoever worked on the art-style of this game deserves double whatever they are being paid currently. The backgrounds and locations, although few, are absolutely gorgeously designed and teeming with detail. It is clear that the principle of quality over quantity was applied here, and the overall package is better for it. Same applies to gameplay. Little fodder and a lot of bosses and mini-bosses. Sure, it may make the game seem shorter as a result, but it's absolutely worth it, especially because...yeah, I can definitely see the combat becoming stale after a while. It works as intended ( despite what some that don't want to learn to how time dodges, parries or interrupts may claim. not everything has to play exactly like dark souls. git gud ), however design-wise I can definitely see it going stale if the game kept going after the most recent DLC. I might revisit it someday just for the artstyle alone, but even if I don't, i'm satisfied with the experience I got.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This review is from the perspective of a person who loves a fair challenge and isn't interested in an easy game. As a result, this is a critique of the hardest mode only and does not reflect on the game as a whole.With that said, this game feels pretty great. The controls are tight yet punishing when you over commit, the combat is visceral yet satisfying, and there is a reasonable amount of variety in what I've seen so far. In particular all the bosses have been a very enjoyable challenge, learning their movesets was a lot of fun despite the many deaths. Where the difficulty seems to fall apart is the smaller enemies, in particular their health bars. They take a couple hits more than feels reasonable, but even then I don't entirely mind it except for one enemy in particular: the archer. Not only does the archer have ranged attacks that take out your entire health bar in one hit, they also seem to have just as much health as melee grunts and a very long-range dodge roll to boot. It makes killing them a complete pain in the butt and ignoring them isn't really an option given their frankly absurd damage output. If they either had smaller health bars, as one would expect from a lightly armoured archer, or didn't have a dodge roll, they would be entirely manageable. Those two things combined with their mobility and health pool make them just plain awful to deal with however. I was able to get to the point of getting no hit by Lans Alut only to be consistently killed by the archer he summons because there's no reasonable way to deal with it, and it just felt awful. I really want to love this game, it seems genuinely incredible in a number of ways from beautiful artwork to very enjoyable combat, but this one minor enemy takes all the fun out of playing all on its own.If you want to play this game for the story and not the challenge, I highly recommend it. It has so much personality and the gameplay is genuinely well designed. If, however, you're looking for a challenge like me? I'd still recommend you give it a go, but I'd also caution you that the hardest difficulty suffers on the account of one very frustrating minor enemy.In the end I'm choosing to not recommend this game because I personally couldn't enjoy it, but I also recognize my preferences are rather niche so I do recommend most others give this wonderful game a try.One more minor complaint: hearing the narration for Lans Alut every. single. time. was sort of infuriating. If you're going to skip the little cutscenes on subsequent fights, which was a very good call, you should also be skipping the narration.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: As beautiful as it is brutal- I'm only 4 hours in, and I was actually dreading that a) the combat would feel too simple and b) that the story and lore would slow down the action. Boy, was I wrong!! The combat is fiendishly hard, but with the save points being so frequent, it's forgiveable and so rewarding when you finally get to spray some frog blood! But I'm most surprised at how the lore and story works so well hand-in-hand with the combat. Graphics and audio are absolutely top notch, and having a respite walking through the villages before another onslaught is a lovely balance.That being said, I think I'm gonna restart the game and play on easy -something I never do- just because some of the later bosses are too much of a grind. But again in compliment to the game, I don't feel any beef about starting over because the worldbuilding is so rich.You can run the game on integrated intel graphics btw, you will just need to lower the resolution to something very low.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really frustrating to me. On one hand, the artstyle, the soundtrack, the narration, and the atmosphere are all really amazing, and to be honest, among the best of the genre. Most of the time the combat is really enjoyable, the new areas are exciting to see, the late game bosses have really fun movesets, etc. Except, the game is an unpolished mess. I was met with constant bugs. Over 16 hours, I had to forcefully quit and reload the game around 10 times from getting softlocked, and had to completely restart the game once to fix an audio issue. You can get stuck on the terrain, sometimes enemy attacks randomly don't show an indicator, multiple gameplay systems are never explained (the main offender being weight, with poison to a lesser degree), sitting at a bench doesn't heal you, the game kind of wants you to buy arrows and poison charges but you can just waste 3 minutes backtracking and get them for free at any point in the game, the only real collectables tend to be new gear but 95% of the time it's just objectively garbage compared to your current gear. And the backtracking is horrendous. Probably only about 50% of the content in the game is story relevant or unique, almost half of it in the direct middle of the game is backtracking doing tedious extermination missions for no real reward.I played on the hardest difficulty, and it was clearly not a focus making sure all the encounters are still fun and balanced on it. Especially with multiple enemies, you constantly get truly stunlocked from 100 to 0, stuck against a wall, etc. The vast majority of the solo boss fights have a satisfying amount of challenge, but many of the most difficult encounters are just a bunch of random enemies at once, and I doubt that was intentional. The game is good, really. There's just so much to complain about. All of the issues really nickel and dime the game down from being one of the best in the genre, to merely good with a bunch of caveats.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Burned through this game in a couple days. If you've ever wanted to hack and slash your way through a grimdark Redwall revenge fantasy, this is the game for you. Setting and tone are straightforward and uncompromising, combat is very engaging. There's a lot of cool visual detail that brings the setting - and the transition of the rat kingdom from ruin to glory - into beautiful focus.Other things (narration, game economy) are a lot less polished. And there were parts of the plot that I'd say are... weirdly misleading, and not on purpose. Small things, not a big deal.Fundamentally, it's pretty short and totally good! Get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: "Tails of Iron" is a great game that's both fun and challenging without being too tough. You play as Redgi, a rat prince on a mission to save his kingdom. The story is engaging, with cool characters and a detailed world that pulls you in.The combat is intense and makes you think, but it's always fair. The graphics are well detailed and the soundtrack is very fitting, adding to the overall experience.If you're into Soulslike games or just looking for a new adventure, "Tails of Iron" is definitely worth checking out. It's fun to play and has a simple yet interesting story.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Polished, perfect length, satisfying combat and sufficiently difficult. Voice acting was awesome. My only complaint is I wish there was more effort put into the characters. The writing was good and the world building was great but there weren't really any 'characters'. I hope if there's a sequel there's a focus on that side of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever wanna play as a rat while beating up frogs to declare dominance on them while Geralt of Rivia voices over your adventure? If the answer to this question is yes, you'd like this. Only downside (that i hope they'll fix) is not being able to re-bind keybindings. Other then that it's pretty solid. I give it a 10 rats outta 10 rats.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The game was great save for the combat system, the terrible combat system. I didnt mind that you increase your dmg and your armor by finding equipment. Its just that the main issue is the dodging system. There are no invincibility frames when you dodge so its technically only used for mobility. However the "mobility" is what you use in order to dodge under enemy attacks. This wouldn't be so bad except for the fact that enemy's hit boxes are so wonky to the point where you would need to be in a very certain spot to dodge their attacks. There are also enemy AoE attacks that were a pain to deal with also because of the dodge system. I thought it was just me until I kept playing and playing to see if it would get better. It did not. Halfway through the game I decided to finish it since i put enough time in, however I wasn't happy about it. Felt terrible playing the game the whole time because of it. Its one thing to die due to your mistakes, but when you see an obvious attack coming and try to dodge it only for it to register and ruin your experience playing the game. Felt like I was getting a migraine every time it happened. They're probably not going to change it since they are making the sequel so I hope its at least better there. This is my first negative review on a game which is unfortunate because i really tried liking it. I didnt even bother playing the post story stuff. Feels bad/10. Do not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to begin, I talked myself into waiting to post a review only after completing the game 100%. And so I did and holy crap it was a nice ride! From the narrator ( lovely voice of Metrosexual Fruitcake Gary, or Geralt of Rivia as he is better known ) to the combat mechanics, to the cleverly designed boss battles, art style and music, everything felt awesome! It's a game I wholeheartedly recommend, so go ahead and help Redgi fulfill his destiny!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I heavily enjoyed this, reminding me far more of a book I used to read by the name of "A taste for Rabbit." It somewhats takes that fantasy woodland creature ascetic, and then just slowly twists it into something of a different genre of fantasy, the overall change with the background over the course of the game's progress is a nice touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals and music in this game is fantastic!Narrative is well made.Combat is lacking some depth, but it's still feels ok.Have a little bit of backtracking, but the game istelf is short, so that's almost not a problem.Overall Tails of Iron is a good game, It's almost great, but it has  some roughness here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game with a nice story and challeging boss fights, so I do recommend it!What I do not recommend is to play it directly on bloody whiskers mode as I did since I wanted to directly 100% it in one playthrough.The game becomes MUCH harder and some bosses take hours to beat. Since you have no i-frames on the dodge you REALLY need to find exact timing to dodge some attacks or you will get hit!All in all it took me 18 hours to complete the game, all side quests and the DLC content (the extra hours on steam come from just having the game open in the background) and it was fun, but boy oh boy did some bosses make me want to pull my hair out.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Only complaint is that its not longer D: The style is gorgeous, I love the sounds they used for the voices, I loved the narrator ;) and I really appreciated that they added a difficulty option since I'm not particularly good at souls-like games. I also liked all the armor and weapon options. Great job. I really hope for another game like this in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This was really a delight. The game seems extremely difficult initially but the patterns for some enemies are just a little strange at times. A couple bosses have a non-stop technique where you'll get only a few hits in but luckily they usually have a lower health pool.The story itself is delightfully shown and told to us by the VA that does Geralt if I'm not mistaken. The combat is satisfying and the game is paced really well. While it's really a narrative piece it's always fun to rebuild or build something back up in a game like this. It's not the main focus and you see benefit from it which makes it a lot fun as an extra thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: side quests in first half of the game are really mandatory and frustrating. after that, game goes on smoothly as if it was an unplugged sink. combat manuvers are pretty simple. hit boxes and reading enemy frames are really THE main problem of this game. but overall, i really enjoyed it. it was a nice ride. just hop in and out. a pretty high standart for todays game industry if you ask me.keep in mind that i'm a huge dark souls 2 fan too :D
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it a neutral rating if possible. It's good and cheap on sale, but simplistic and outstays it's welcome if you try to do everything, mostly because of time wasting mechanics.Pro's: -Art is dope.-Combat is alright.-Surprising amount of special and normal enemies. -Lots of weapons and armor that looks great.Cons:-Many forced standstill moments that just last a good few seconds too long.-Quest board system is so annoying, having to walk into the same dungeon, kill basic enemies, kill boss, then you have to walk out all the way, repeat 3 or more times, repeat for each quest board. Painfully time wasting.-Gameplay, while decent, doesn't feel as smooth and responsive as I'd like.-I have completed the game, and besides some different swing animations, I have no idea what the difference is of weapon classes, shields, armor and weight. Conclusion, definitely a play it once game with all the timewasters. I got every achievement except one that requires a new playthrough on the hardest difficulty, i'd run through that if it wouldn't take so long with so much filler.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I really can't say enough good things about Tails of Iron. I've enjoyed it immensely. The world building and art direction absolutely steal the show. The story is solid, I liked that there was voiceover narration and the way dialogue/exposition is delivered fits very well within the aesthetic of the game world and it was an interesting and welcome change of pace from reading walls of texts in most RPGs. The gameplay was engaging and tight. At no point did I die and wonder how the hell it happened as sometimes occurs in other titles, the gameplay and controls and fights are so well done that I always knew exactly where and how I messed up. This game is worth every penny and I'm crossing my fingers for DLC or a sequel. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Main Q finished in 8hrs. Solid story and really pretty. Sidescrolling RPG with tough fights later on in the game. Nice weapon upgrades and nice variation where you can pick and choose to suit the type of enemy you'll be fighting. Bosses and boss level mobs are everywhere. Fighting is basically Block, Dodge, or Hit based on little advance warnings the boss gives you - so not exactly complex - but it's pretty hard on anything bar Fairy Tail mode. But to be honest it's a fun little story - so if you like playing a story you can play Fairy Tail, have easier fights and still enjoy it. Worth £10-15. Really nice looking and a labour of love to rats loved and lost.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to keep it simple: it's a Hollow Knight bite with irresponsive controls, mechanically incompetent, unnecessary and annoying visuals and a Mike Tyson hook-like learning curve with artificial, clunk-based difficulty, but I got it on sales and only paid 4 bucks for it and it's pretty cute, overall, and original, so I will play it. Additionally, I'm too proud to ever skip a a Souls-like or Souls-lite, so I will 100% it hands down, but overall I didn't have good impressions the first 2-3 hours. I have only played 2 hours and I'm dying due to the inability of the game to stay clean and concise, to telegraph when or when not to attack or due to random fps drops over some lighting source. Do you want crisp controls and precise movement?, this ain't it, but it's artistically beautiful and a pretty engaging revenge story with a children's book feel to it, narration of events included.Now, if you excuse me, I gotta avenge my rat homies and become the king.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat this game. Nice story. Kinda wish it had more detail but not bad at all.Interesting locations and super well designed art. By far one of the best visuals and continuing to show off why indie games are making the gaming industry shake. I like the game generally but only one thing sucks… you backtrack a lot. There’s no fast travel so you’re going to walk a lot. Tiny rat legs… still worth playing if you want to relax
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Shameless plug for video essay here: Valiant Hearts meets Redwall. I really love this game. There's not many games featuring anthro characters where you can play it without feeling like you have to alt tab whenever someone walks past your room and even fewer good ones inside that category. Tails of Iron plays simple but its extremely gratifying to get good at and is presented in such a loving and charming manner that the few flaws the gameplay and pacing have shrink in severity. It's not perfect but this game, to me, is brilliant and Odd Bug Studios really knocked it out of the park with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, but filled with small minor disappointments. Just little bits here & there where it could have been amazing but isn't.Pros:* amazing character. The story isn't anything to write home about but it's well told & has a great sense of atmosphere* interesting core combat system* haven't encountered too many bugsNeutral:* the game features somewhat slow & methodical combat, where you need to respond precisely to enemy signals to parry, dodge, block, etc. That is not everyone's cup of tea.Cons (or rather disappointments) - in order from least to most aggravating:* combat is good, nicely hits that souls-like vibe of you know you screwed up & you know how you screwed up so you keep trying again... but some of the hit boxes feel a little whack. One thing might be is the dodge doesn't actually give you invincibility frames, which can feel a little off. Alternatively, I just need to git gud :D.* economy is a bit busted, it's too easy to get grub-shells & iron, & not enough to spend it on. May have been advisable to go MUCH lighter on the various refill stations, forcing players to have to think more about how to spend their resources.* put the game down for about a week because of IRL... came back & couldn't remember what the enemy signalling meant. An easily accessible tutorial from the menu would be appreciated just as a reminder.* world feels small. I'm just about to do the mine quest... and have spent most of my time bouncing between the sewers, ranger headquarters & their damned tower, & the castle which serves as a hub. Looking thru steam guides, it seems there is maybe about another 2, maybe 3 locations to explore? It's starting to feel a bit repetitive* Weapon & armor variety - this is where the game is at it's worst... while it gives you a whole slew of weapons most of them feel the same, & even worse there just isn't a good reason to use most of them. The only stats are weight & attack; and the difference between spears, swords, & axes is rather negligible. An affix system would help a ton... but even better would be for the weapons to FEEL different, ala dark souls or bloodstained. In those games you might use a less statsy weapon just because it's something ridiculous like a floppy gargoyle tail... here not so much. Armor is a *bit* better with resistances but ultimately has the same problem... most of the equipment I find is at best a side-grade from what I'm already using.Best advice to the devs - take the same formula, give it a bigger world,  don't be as generous with consumables & for gods-sakes make the weapons & armor have bigger tradeoffs in terms of feel & playstyle. Those 3 factors take this from a great game to just very good, which is a damn shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A fun action game that I don't know how to classify. It has a combat system that reminds me of a slower Salt and Sanctuary with a greater emphasis on 1 on 1 or 2 on 1 arenas. The world feels a bit small to start with but after so many hours with it it actually feels very well used. You will go back and forth through the same areas doing side jobs and for the most part it doesn't get boring but will be a bit tedious if done back to back. The many boss fights are all fun to fight against and mostly have unique move sets that will get you killed if your not paying attention. The story is pretty good and has the benefit of being told by The Witcher's Doug Cockle. Hearing "Geralt" narrate your journey made everything you do sound like an epic in a book. I would say the game would have been worth $15 without him but with him it's worth $20. A bit shy of the actual price but not by much.EDIT 12/13/21: The new update has added several end game arena fights and a new final boss. IN addition to that it also added a new difficulty mode that made jumping in again a blast. You get 2-3 hits before death and the enemies are a lot faster with their attacks. You really have to get the timing down to a seconds worth of time. Would say that $20 point I said before holds stronger now.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Hollow knight-ish with much slower combat set in a grittier Redwall universe.The pacing falls a bit early on, but quickly picks up after you complete a bunch of mandatory 'side' quests. Some fights are frustrating, but overall mostly fair, IMO. The visuals and atmosphere are both amazing and the audio is well done. A bit too short and lacks a bit in the progression department, but I had a very good time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This Game brings a whole new experience to the Indie/RPG Genre and it's a very fun game to play around with, with all the different challenges and bosses you encounter I hope that "Odd Bug Studios" will release DLC's in the future. It has a very souls like boss fights feel to it and it's also interesting how such a intriguing story line went from young prince who's the heir to the throne tooooo, former new "Rat King" rising from the ashes and blood of his fallen family members and Kingdom. All in all the game is simply a beautiful experience and i hope the developers keep up the good work. -Lyon Allison
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, unique, and immersive aRPG. It takes the best from some of the genre's classics and delivers a riveting adventure, with both challenging combat and witty writing.. The creator's sincere and passionate love for their game is palpable and drips across detail of every screen. There is level of quality reminiscent of Stardew Valley and Hollow Knight in that regard.In all fairness I'm still early on in the game, but I'm hopeful it will continue to deliver this experience as I continue this charming adventure,EDIT: Having completed the game (13 hours IGT) I can highly recommend it to any 2D souls-like arpg player. My only really complaint is I wish that there was just more content, as it's simply that good. but also a bit short. I hope this game's success begets more content, be it DLC or new game +.Constructive feedback to devs:You have a great base combat system, it deserves to be expanded on. -Perhaps create a 4th melee weapon type (duel daggers).-Range weapons could be balanced (too strong or ammo is too easy to get), perhaps make crossbow/bullets only purchasable by shop-Expand the number of utility items vis a vis dark souls, bombs, resins, maybe/pets or summons,Per the previous points, the currency system feel unfinished, give us more items to spend currency on (potions, maps, teleport stones, etc)-Expand the social aspect of the game - give a away to increase/develop/progress our relationships with certain characters, this could be one method of better utilizing currency.Fantastic game, potentially on the same level as Hollow Knight and if continued to be developed it stands to be truly an all time classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished up this game 100%. Absolute joy to play. Such a unique setting and really great storytelling. Finished it in 2 sessions because I really couldn't put it down. I have pet rats and seeing them as the MC's in a game was boldly wonderful.Combat was crisp, narration was great. Some of the backtracking got a bit stale but there wasn't too much. Also weapons didn't really have that much variety in terms of movesets but the general flow of combat was so good that I didn't really care.The game has some faults but they are buried deep below a fantastic setting and Tails of Iron is an absolute joy to get lost in.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Literally unplayable. I've had so many problems, whether it be getting this game to load textures properly, or even load the game up at all. The gameplay itself is super fun if and when I can get it to work, but now it's just crashing on startup or crashing within 2 minutes of loading in. I have no problems playing other games that should be much more intensive than this, so I'm incredibly disappointed with my utter inability to enjoy what should be a very fun game. Buyer beware, your PC might not even be able to play this.

_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: If you took a gritty medieval setting reminiscent of The Witcher or Game of Thrones and decided to tell a story about a brutal barbarian invasion of a kingdom whose ruler has gotten old as has not yet settled his succession, so his youngest son must step up and fight the invaders away, only instead of people from different countries the story was about rats vs frogs, this is what you'd get. It's a very good looking game with a great atmosphere and clever visual design and overall presentation, for sure, and I enjoyed the bit of humor and references, such as the names of the characters or the part where, in a nod to the game's narrator, it mentions that the king's chamber smells of lilac and gooseberries. The gameplay is solid enough, though it's not really that much of an RPG and it's more of a metroidvania, and the campaign itself is not too long. It took me about seven hours to finsh the whole game, including sidequests and the expansion. And it gets extra points because the game is dedicated to the creators' pet rats and they share the name and fur coloring of the game's main cast. I just found out a sequel is coming out starring a side character you briefly meet at the end of the game, and I'll be sure to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun! I played on normal difficulty. It was just hard enough that it was satisfying to beat but not too frustrating. A few moves felt like BS but it's all very beatable.Other reviews saying it's a slog to get through side quests, not sure what they mean. There are only like 10 side quests in the game and most of them are required to progress the story so I wouldn't even call them side quests. The game is super linear, there's just a bit of back tracking.This game goes on sale. I got it for $10. If you're light on money but full on time it's hard to recommend since it is pretty short. If you have money but not time it becomes a lot easier to recommend since it doesn't overstay its welcome. For reference I beat every side quest I could find, collected everything I could, and explored every area fully in under 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrible, don't be misled by the reviews, I don't know why people like this game, maybe because is an indie game but that does not give you immunity to be criticized for your product. The worst part of this game is the combat, which is 80% of the game, the controls feel clunky and the hitbox is terrible. The maps are few and there is a little grind, unnecessary in my opinion, to extend the game artificially, the game longs 8 hours but could be 4. In counterpart the narrator is great (I don't know if is the same voice as the witcher but sounds like him).Anyway, I suggest saving time and money and not touching this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A game that will require to you less than 2 GB: I'm enjoying it far more (and better) than playing Elden Ring.I think the developers perfectly understood what a soulslike with RPG and open world elements must be.This' what I do liked so far:-Soulslike elements like hard bosses with different attack patterns that keeps you entertained; a dark world that, however, is still vibrant and colorful in some areas (there are villages and safe areas, a thing that I missed much in many other soulslike).-RPG elements like a main quest that is both thrilling and funny; quest boards with the right amount of side quests that makes you feel in a loosely open world environement, without losing yourself around forgotting the main mission; NO levels or stats to manage, you'll acquire equipments that will modify your attack, defense, etc. stats and that is sufficient: you'll still wanna choose between an armour that will protect you from evil froggies rather than another one that will shield you from devilish mosquitos (or else you'll easily die: yes, it's a soulslike).-Fu*king BEAUTIFUL art: every detail seems hand drawn, still it doesn't lack fluidity. I'm just like "WOW" at every corner. I mean: WOW. Uppercase in my mind, you know?-Weapons chians attacks and combos, and the flexibility of the weapons themselves: sometimes you'll have to figure it out which is the best suited (or the only choice) to overcome a foe.I'm absolute loving this title. I hope someday they will try to make a sequel with 3D graphic, with the same kind of art but someway similar to "Ghost of a Tail" for the 3D environment: that would be glorious! All hail King Rattus.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The Skaven and Lizardmen gang war now voiced by Geralt of Rivia. Is there more to be said?In all honesty, Tails of Iron was a complete surprise for me. I was drawn in by it's beautiful art style (which by itself could of kept me going through the games 10~ hour story, side quests involved), but found myself returning to play due to it's incredibly atmospheric world building and challenging; though fair; combat. Would highly recommend, especially for those who are low on time! It's easy to crank out the whole, well polish package within a few nights of play after a day of college classes or work. (Speaking from experience)TL;DR Gameplay and story are on point, pick it up if you can!

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare to say I enjoyed every single second of a game, but this time I did. :D - Not a true Souls-like: while the decisions here benefit the game, it does not have a stamina bar and you lose no resources upon death, nor do you level up in the classic way (you find better gear during the game and you get permenant health upgrades by sampling dishes made by the court's Chef), but it does have strategic combat based on pattern memorization and a juice canteen to let you heal). Figured I'd point this out, so people see what they get might not quite fit the label. + Otherwise the game's fantastic: I love the very distinct and clear signals for what to use: a parry (yellow sign) or a dodge (red sign). I'm usually terrible with 2D platforming and my true forte is 3D combat in Souls-likes, so this was very helpful. E.g. I can never, ever in any game get a parry right, but here there were very few I didn't pull off and I didn't lose for it either. + The mouse and keyboard are excellently implamented and very intuative. Many Souls-likes treat M&K controls as a mere afterthught, no such neglect here. I never felt I'd do better or enjoy the game more with a controller. (I also can't rate any controller controls since I played without one.) + The story has the appeal of a small underdog rising and it feels close to the Redwall series in tone since it's a heroic adventure, but not without a touch of gory details (e.g. you will see blood on enemies and some may have their guts exposed), though a certain underground town is more steampunk than pure medival fantasy that is there for the rest of the game.  + As someone with insect phobia I feel this deserves a special mention: none of the insect enemies were triggering for me, some cattle bugs were wacky in design and all of them very heavily stylized and rather cartoonish and didn't make any harrowing bugs sounds that would stop me form playing. The only thing that did make me somewhat uncomfortable was the "Odd Bug" logo as it did have buzzing sounds, but thankfully it was brief. + There's fairly little music and there's a lot of ambinet sound, but it fits the game and its enviroments very well. + The artstyle is unique and very cute and nearly fairytale like and comic-like in style while also not shying away form a bit of grittiness and blood when the story calls for it. I'd say teen and up for an age rating. + There few enemy races in the game, but they various enemy types are numerous and very diverse - I was amazed at just how many different kinds toads I fought to mention one such race. + The huge variety of gear enables any playstlye and you can be a light warrior, a walking fortress or a mix of both. + There are easy. normal and hard modes (not with such mundane names), so there's something for everyone. I finished all the story and extra content on easy mode - 2D isn't my strong suit, so I figured I'd take it easy - aside from maybe one dish and piece of gear I've likely missed somewhere in 9 hours. + While the game is short it doesn't feel dragged out and it's length is just right: it tells its story without cutting corners or overstaying its welcome. + Platforming was there, but it was not difficult. The reason why i can't properly enjoy most 2D Souls-likes is because there's a lot of platforming and while I can nail the combat, there's always some platforming section that bars my way forward (looking at you, Salt and Sanctury), not such dissapointments here. + Looking back at it, easy mode might nearly be enough even for people that have lost most of their reflexes either due to old age or some other reason. Being 25 and in good health, I can't really judge this directly, but it felt relaxed enough that one could get very far in the game even with far less reflexes. But as I'm not in position to directly test this point, take it with a grain of salt. - Edit: the game IS now sold on GOG and will be discounted for 55% until the 11the of June 2024. I'll play with my GOG copy shortly. A huge "Thank you!" to the developers. :D IN SHORT: it's an absolutely amazing game, go play it. :)

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm inclined to say I do recommend the game, I've also got a lot of mixed feelings about it. From the Souls-likes I played, it's one of the worst, though I haven't played many of them. Let's start with the good parts: Visually, it looks great. The art style is charming and the environments contain quite the amount of detail. The finishers animations are also superb. In terms of sound, it's clearly an AA game: there isn't much variety and AAA titles, such as Bloodborne, of course, blow it out of the water when it comes to OST. That being said, the few soundtracks which are present are quite nice. It would be remiss of me not to mention the narration, provided by Doug Cockle (Witcher 3). Cockle's wonderful performance significantly enhances the overall experience and does a lot of heavy lifting.Other thing I particularly enjoyed is the changes in the world. As you complete side quests and the main quest, the world around you changes: ruined castle gets rebuilt, destroyed villages are repaired, regular citizens appear on the streets and go about their business, etc. This small feature really made it feel as if the game progressed and the main character actually made a change in the world. Now, to the less pleasant parts of the game. I played it on the hardest difficulty and some of the encounters didn't feel fun at all. I don't mind learning patterns or getting used to a moveset, but I do mind having to dash around and dodge for 10 seconds just to make a single attack. It's not hard to do, really, the majority of bosses have about 3-5 moves, but it's just so tedious. On the other end of the spectrum, there are bosses who posed zero challenge and were killed in 2-3 tries even though technically they were late-game ones. Moreover, the animations are often very stiff and the attacks are not well telegraphed, which means you mostly rely on visual cues the game presents above enemies' heads. It's pretty common for a fight to be similar to a rhythm game, which I personally did not enjoy that much.Next issue is the general game design one: the game absolutely loves to waste your time with weird unnecessary padding. I will list just a couple of examples:1. Your healing flask charges are not restored on rest, but should be refilled separately instead. Is there ever a point in not restoring them? No, so each time you rest you should also spend ~5-10 seconds to restore healing charges. 2. There are consumables in the game, such as arrows. They, again, are not restored on rest. However, there are barrels with arrows inside of them all throughout the map, with an endless supply of arrows. What it means is your "get ready" routine isn't just "go and rest", but rather "fill your flask, then go to the next corner of the screen to grab the arrows, then run to another screen to grab the poison". It would be fine if there was an element of skill involved, e.g. getting arrows is risky, but there isn't. The only thing you have to do, as a player, to get your arrows is simply run. Sometimes I even closed my eyes and held the movement key because there were quite literally no enemies. The list is not exhaustive, there are other examples as well, but I hope I got the point across. This doesn't make the game terrible, it's just extremely baffling to see such questionable design decisions with seemingly no thought put into them. To summarise, as I've already mentioned, it's a mixed bag. Ultimately, I did not regret my time with the game and neither did I regret choosing the highest difficulty. I'm looking forward to seeing the next instalment and I genuinely hope the devs make overall experience smoother. There is clearly a lot of effort put into the game. It's not the best in the genre, but it's still decent enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I had pet rats of my own, however, they passed away recently. They were my whole world, I loved those rats so much, they made me so happy. I was completely destroyed when they passed. But, this game. I fell in love with this game. the soundtrack is fantastic, the gameplay is fun and compelling, the story is simple and sweet, and everything about this game made it such an enjoyable experience. Seeing all the love and effort put into this game by such a small studio is honestly awe-inspiring. all of the thought and love put into the characters, how the little buddies of the developers are forever immortalized in this game, honestly brought tears to my eyes, and it helped me get through my grief, the awful grief of losing a beloved pet. It keeps me optimistic. Just like how the ratdom overcame hardship and rebuilt what was lost, I too will get better and rebuild, and the legacy of my little buddies will live on forever and their tails will be told for ages to come. I strongly support this game and the studio, I urge all of my friends to play this game, and I urge you too. Thank you for reading if you got this far, and I hope you consider giving this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron surely looks interesting at first sight with its beautiful visuals and cute rats and frogs. Behind those are nice-looking cities, which are all hand drawn by the way. However, the game can not keep the same quality in the visuals in every area. While the kingdom looks worked on and detailed, the sewers look very undetailed and unimaginative. (Not because the sewers are a filthy place, it just looks boring. Take sewers in Dark Souls as a counter reference.) Geralt as the narrator is cool, but what's the point when you have no story to tell, other than marketing the game? To be honest, that's all Tails of Iron has in its core. Other than those, we have a janky and clunky combat with troublesome hitboxes. Sometimes, enemies won't telegraph their attacks and mess you up. There is weapon and armor variety, but using them never feels different. So its more like a visual variety. Nevertheless, you get the most powerful weapon mid game and never have to change weapons anywhere later. Game design is very problematic. Tails of Iron asks you to do the same side quests over and over again. The game almost has no main quests. In some side quests, you are expected to take the same route again and again to kill the same enemies, talking about enemies, Tails of Iron has no enemy variety. Most enemies are reskins of each other. Their hitboxes are problematic, making combat feel janky. The game tries to show itself as a metroidvania, but I hope the devs aren't defining it as one. Because metroidvanias aren't supposed to be extremely linear and scripted. The story itself is extremely predictable and routine. And the presentation is extremely ordinary. It's not the main focus of the game, but it takes too much of our time even when that's the case.  Sound effects are very repetitive and lacking, adding to the unsatisfactory gameplay. Exploration is not nonexistent, the same with music. There is no atmospheric music or any music at all.To conclude, Tails of Iron is a game with extremely unsatisfying gameplay, repetitive level and encounter design, and a poor game design. Extremely poor game overall. Not recommended even on a sale.Follow My

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun little game. Not the longest of stories, but the story itself is very good. I had a great time tracking down items, defeating foes (some very difficult) and meeting the characters along the way. Plus, Geralt of Rivia narrating the whole thing made it feel even more epic. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. The story is fun and mildly dark with some political intrigue that's really neat, the characterization and sounds for the characters is cute, and the art style is great. Lots of fun being in the world. The only thing that could be annoying for some people is that you often are backtracking and being sent to the same location over and over to progress the story or get some materials to progress the story. For people not already desensitized by MMO fetch quests, I can see how that can be super annoying, particularly because it slows the pace of the game and storytelling to a crawl. Aside from that, the boss fights are awesome and difficult. Once you get the two-handed weapon, you cannot just mindlessly wind up to break a shield, as you will get counterhit, so be sure to pick a good time to charge up... However, once you get the gun, the game becomes rather easy. All in all, great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write reviews but this game absolutely stole my heart the moment I started playing it. It had been on my radar when it was first announced but I completely forgot about it until it showed up in the 2024 Summer Sale.As soon I started the game up I fell in love with the absolutely gorgeous art style and design. The game-play at standard difficulty was challenging in a few places but felt consistently fair and balanced across the entire experience, which is no small feat with game design.The story has this underlying sensation to it... something of a colourful simplicity that I think I've been missing with a lot of games I've played these days. I say simple with no degrading intent; the story has twists, emotional weight, and depth, but doesn't try hard to be some complex narrative that to be honest, I just get tired of. It tells a story straight, lets you enjoy the moments, and immerses you in an experience that feels like you're playing through a picture book brought to life. Quality is NOT anti-theoretical to simplicity, far from it. The story and experience of Tails of Iron thoroughly proves as much, and the past couple days have been made better for it.Thank you, Odd Bug Studio.I eagerly look forward to Tails of Iron II :)

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, short, casual adventure game that delivers a short story about a rat prince restoring his kingdom by personally exterminating all of its enemies all by himself.The art and enviroments look great, sound design is pretty alright.The game is incredibly short however and there are surprisingly few areas to explore, they try to extend the gameplay by adding "side quests" (in a million quotation marks) which are actually mandatory that require you to backtrack to certain areas several times, you are also encouraged to revisit every area after every progression in the main quest (sometimes this is as insiduous as one of the traders suddenly having one extra blueprint for sale, I have no idea why this is).There is tons of weapons and armors to collect, but there is no reason to use 90% of them? A lot that you come across minutes later is objectively better than the previous thing you were using, you also collect bug shells and iron as currency? But you don't really spend it on anything so you cap out at 99/99 really quickly. Not sure if they meant for the game to be longer or if they added this stuff because other similar games have it. Pretty strange.While the game isn't hard per se, the combat is absolute dogshyte garbage with certain enemy prompts either blatantly lying to you or being weirdly deceptive, especially for the larger bosses. The hitbox for some of the enemy attacks, again, especially for large bosses, is incredibly hit and miss sometimes resulting in these sometimes incredibly frustrating and cheap hits and deaths. A big chunk of attacks are also badly telegraphed, not in the sense that you don't see that the boss is about to do an attack, but rather where the attack will land. So you get these situations where you are given say, a red circle signal (signifying an area of effect attack that cannot be dodged or blocked), making you stay clear of the boss, only for the boss to then do some steroid and cocaine induced olympic quadruple summersault launch across the entire room - but only sometimes - sometimes the same attack doesn't do this at all. I wish I could name one boss or enemy that I enjoyed but if I'm gonna be completely honest here all the trash mob enemies along the way were a chore and the bosses were all varying degrees of violently brutally unfun and annoying.The hardest boss in the entire game (for me) was actually just the tag team in the arena, one guy with a spear and one big guy with a shield, the spear guy is all over the place and the shield guy has a heavy hitting shield bash that you have ½ seconds to react to and dodge, also they both frequently attack at the same time or just slightly out of synch, leading to you getting wombo combo'd to death. Bosses that dodge attacks or that jump from one end of the arena to the other are also just terrible. I get that its a 2d game so there is really only so much you can do while trying to vary bosses, but damn is it ♥♥♥♥♥.Bunch of people say the combat n such is good or okay though, so I don't know, maybe it's just not for me.Anyway this being said I liked it, mostly, but wish it was longer.25 bucks for what amounts to a 7-12 hour one time experience (there isn't really replayability here) that you can finish in one or two sittings seems kinda steep to me, so maybe get it on sale

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game for which I wish there was a neutral ratingThe world in which the game takes place is really well crafted, the narration is amazing, you can see that a lot of work was put into it.However, I was expecting a lot more depth from it after seeing the trailer and playing other 2d action rpgs with similar presentation. There is only one playstyle in this game, for instance, you don't get to weigh the pros and cons of equipping a 2 handed weapon, it is always equipped. You can combo 1h and 2h attacks without any delays, so the 2h weapon is really just the same as a heavy attack that you would see in other games, having an equipment screen gives the illusion of rpgs elements.As for the bow, I don't see any reason to limit the amount of ammo you can carry aside from denying players the possibility to play ranged. Not that it would matter since arenas have very little to no places to jump and distance yourself from your enemies. This is another area where the game falls short, it is a 2d game where you only really play in 1D. You move left and right, time your parries and dodges but there is no verticality in the gameplay. Some enemies fly but you can't jump attack, and don't even need to aim at them thanks to the bow's autoaim, they might as well be at ground level.Aside from that, the game has a lot of redeeming elements, exploration is fun, death animations are very cool, the enemies are varied. I was really on the fence with this review, but since I don't think I will stay motivated to play it through the end, I will make it negative for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you know those games, that try to be more sours like than souls, ending up being unplayable? _childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is different from others in the genre but that's a welcome change.  It is very much a linear adventure compared to the Metroidvania style found in Hollow Knight or the Ori series. The gameplay is also unique in that it's very chunky as opposed to being quick and nimble - even with a light build.  Combine all this with the adorable story and you get a really fun game experience.  It's best to remember that this is an indie title so it can feel lacking in some areas but that's expected from a smaller studio.My only real complaint is forced side missions which is unfortunately something we're seeing in more and more games these days.  This is when the main story abruptly stops to quite literally force you to go do redundant and inconsequential side missions before you can progress. It's done as a way to stretch the main story playtime and it's a trend that really needs to die.  Beyond that, this is definitely worth a playthrough.  Fun story with challenging gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game is full of charm from top to bottom, fantastic art style, beautiful narration and general narrative of the story, funny and just a good time all around. Combat is simple but works well within the game style and has a decent learning curve from beginning to end. Boss battles are fairly straight forward, you'll probably perish a few times until you learn the basic pattern and claim your victory. Fashion Rat, a tonne of weapons and armours to use each with their own benefits and perks, but once you've nailed down the battle mechanics the stats are fairly negligible so you can wear whatever take your fancy really.Overall great game, cannot recommend it enough, short but sweet (around 10 hours to completion).9/10 would have gotten full marks if it had a little more content, Tails of Iron 2?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. It can be supremely frustrating trying to learn boss patterns and time all the buttons you need to hit just right, but when success comes, it feels incredible. _childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is a fun little 2D souls like RPG adventure game. You are Redgi, prince and heir to the throne of the Rat Kingdom. Your kingdom is invaded by the evil Frog Clans and your father, The King is killed. Embark on a quest to reclaim your Kingdom, defeat the champions of the Frog Clan and banish them from your lands.Pros- Charming colourful 2D art and good music.- Difficult but rewarding combat with lots of weapons to suit your playstyle.- Decent length campaign (10-12 hours at least if you don't get stuck on any particular boss).- Narrated by Doug Cockle (the voice of Geralt of Rivia from the Witcher games).Cons- Honestly nothing I can think of.A very enjoyable little game that I streamed all the way through over a weekend soon after the game's release. It has a very fun feel to it and made by a small team of passionate devs who even dropped by during my streams.Lots of little easter eggs thrown in as well. If you like fun indie games with challenging but fair combat give this a try when you see it on sale next time.Here is a video I compiled of all the named bosses in the game (in case you get stuck on any particular one) :

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really well achieved. The graphics are charming, the soundtrack fits great (it's even sort of surprising in some parts). The fact that the narrator is the actor that voices Geralt in the Witcher games is an absolute gem! I really like how the characters don't speak, but communicate through pictures and flute sounds (they are rats after all).Truth be told, I'm not a huge fan of side scrollers, but on this game, everything comes together and makes sense just the way it is. It's part of its "rustic" charm.Mind you, no matter how charming this game sounds and looks, it is still a souls like, so be prepared to die, over, and over, and over again (make sure to save as often as possible). The map traversal is a bit tedious and there are some annoying fetch quests. The combat feels very clunky and weird. The game pretty much decides for you if an attack should blocked or dodged. _childDocuments_.review: i really enjoy the game and many things about it. the art is beautiful, the soundtrack is perfect for the game, the combat system is fun, and the exploration is great. my only gripes with the game are that fall damage gets really annoying when you take damage from like a 6 foot drop, and in combat against more than two or three enemies, if you get hit by one in the next second you could get hit by every other enemy with a red attack. i also think that basic attacks should be more emphasized. they shouldn't have a flashing color, but it should be more telegraphed. i love the game and can't wait to see what else this studio has planned in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: DNF the free DLC(s), and I can see that the achievements from those are also lacking in percentage of completion, which really doesn't surprise me.I had my eyes on Tails of Iron for a while. The art and atmosphere looks amazing, and that someone would combine that with a souls-like? Seemed amazing to me.The biggest problem with this game is that the combat is simply too wonky, too underdeveloped.- Bosses can corner you in areas with attacks that make it so that there is literally no way out of taking the damage. This could have been fixed with dodging having some i-frames, but it doesn't, since that defeats the purpose of other combat mechanics (it's basically a kind of "Simon says").- Hitboxes are simply not fair and the enemies have i-frames, while you don't.Other than that... Bugs needs to be fixed and there needs to be done some QoL things done. - There's a quest you can get softlocked in never completing even though you have fulfilled everything. - The game is quite linear and some of the paths you have to take to move on provides you with unavoidable fall-damage. - A lot of the encounters on the way between points of interest seem like boring resource drain. Especially since completing something like a "mini-boss" doesn't save the game.- You have to save manually ALL THE TIME. Like, you can be on your way to complete a quest by returning to the questgiver, thinking "I'm safe to go there, I've been there before" and BOOM new encounter. Oh? The task you completed before that encounter? You have to complete it again. Same thing with "cinematic" intros to characters or storyline cinematic stuff. I literally had to go somewhere, have the cinematic play, then go back to save, and then go face the boss that is after the cinematic, just because the cinematic was placed right before the boss but never skippable after watching it the first time.It was an annoying game to finish, even though I wanted to. For this reason, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the positive things I have to say about the game, the presentation of the game is really good. I really ejoy this whole world of animal kingdoms. The graphics and the whole art direction is really good, the characters look very cute and the environnements are beautiful too.Now this is why this review isn't positive. The whole game basically only rely on it's combat system, it tries to be a "2d Soulslike" with a dodgeroll/guard/parry mechanics. But in my opinion it does a pretty  mediocre job. The combat doesn't feel good at all, you basically have attacks being color coded to know what action you have to do to evade that attack, wether it's a small dodge, a big dodge or a parry. I also felt like the dodge mechanic basically worked half of the time. I know it tries to be dark-soulsish but in dark souls as soon as you press the button your character rolles and is invincible for a small time. Here either the invulnerabilty frames are very wierd or the dodge has basically none. The movement feels very weird to, you character takes a little while before getting his running speed wich feels so weird and there are a lot of other small stuff that really doesn't feel good (like picking up items playing a slow animation every single item you pickup).You basically have to comlpete little missions to gather resources to rebuild your castle, wich basically mean the whole game is very tedious and has a lot of meaningless backtracking with no real upgrade or fast travel (at least for the 2hrs i've played).I can tell a lot of love has been put into this game, but I can't recommand it for all it's shortcomings. The devs are working on a sequel Tails of Iron 2: Whiskers of Winter, and i really hope they revamp the structure of the game and improve the combat system because I really love everything about the game's presentation and visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I wouldn't recommend this game. The game is pretty good looking and is somewhat immersive despite having no music. I could get past VERY linear gameplay and generic story. The things which kills it for  are:Reusing game content over and over. There are 3 main biomes which you'll visit dozen of times to clear a Boss who suddenly spawned right on the edge of the map. You can only pick up one quest at the time so you spent about 1/3 game backtracking to pick up the another one and go right back where you been few minutes ago. In the post-game content there is even situation where shorter route to a Boss is conveniently blocked off by NPCs so you have to take the longer one and run longer for sake of running. Why?You spent most of the game figting Bosses and the combat system is VERY bad. Enemies have 3 indicators for upcoming attacks - Block, Dodge, Parry,  Even though you are playing a rat, the character is about as sluggish as it can be. The animations feel slow and always have to be finished and you can't buffer anything. About 70% of my damage taken was from being in attack/dogge animation and being UNABLE to do anything about upcoming indicator which popped up right after me doing a command. As a result the main gameplay is just you waiting for indicator -> Block/Dodge -> hit once -> stand still and repeat. You can also Roll with extra action during Dodge, while it covers more distance it takes about twice as long as Dodge and it's just inferior with how fast the bosses get.I don't think I played any other platformer/2D game which wants you to press less keys. It's just extremely frustrating to see what enemy is about to do, be able to react to it, but the action won't go off because you had the audacity to try to get extra attack (half second stun lock) or you tried to Dodge left | -> | Attack (and now you are Rolling).The end game bosses are completely not compatible with the move set you are offered. You can't be creative ever and every fight plays out the same. I think a lot of things would be so much smoother if only you could block/dodge during animations, but oh well.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I loved the art direction and attention to detail in this game. They captured the feel of an age-old fantasy tale perfectly and the icing on the cake is that Doug Cockl (Geralt of Rivia) narrates the story and his voice fits the tone of the story well.The story is entertaining enough to keep the player interested even though it is simple. There are some relatively grim passages that balance out the cute graphics. It's even funny at times, especially with Geralt's raspy voice.The evolution of the rat kingdom throughout the game is very enjoyable. As you progress through the story, the castle, the village and their surroundings are rebuilt, which is nice because you pass through the same areas quite often. There are also a few secrets to uncover which add a bit to the main story and encourage a bit of exploration.Before I talk about the gameplay, I'd like to add that even though this game is labeled "souls-like", it's still pretty accessible.Combat is the main element of gameplay and the concept is pretty simple on paper: enemies have 4 different "emotes" they can do that indicate what attack they will do next. In short, some attacks can be blocked or parried, others require you to dash or roll.In theory, this sounds easy, but in practice, it doesn't really work. For example, if you are too close to a boss, you can be hit even if you rolled or dashed an attack that was supposed to be avoidable as the game taught you, which is a small flaw at first. Another small flaw is that some bosses will combo you to (almost) death, but I guess that's part of the genre.Overall, the combat is satisfying and I felt rewarded for learning the enemies' moves. I didn't feel like the game was too punishing, it was just right, as we have plenty of healing and tools to fight the bosses.  My advice to anyone who is struggling is to keep a good distance, learn each enemy's moves and use your ranged weapon if you get into trouble, as it can really carry you.There is a lot of different equipment which is a nice touch, but I feel like it becomes less important as you progress through the game.In conclusion, I think the storytelling and attention to detail were top-notch while the gameplay was respectable. I also finished it at 100% on normal difficulty in just under 9 hours, so it's not as demanding as other souls-like games. However, I wouldn't recommend it to people who just want to relax as it requires a bit of patience and training for the tougher parts.

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle a little giving this a thumbs-down, and maybe I'll eventually come back to the game and change it.  But so far, the game is cute but outside of the first couple hours just not well executed.Just to preface, I play a lot of souls-likes.  I prefer games with hard difficulties, and usually don’t have any trouble finishing them (Elden Ring being an exception due to sheer size, need to go back and finish it some day).First, the combat.  I know this aspires to the "souls like" title, but I think it falls pretty far short of that.  The combat doesn't feel very fluid.  I'm not sure if there are no i-frames, or if the execution of them on a 2d space isn't very good, but I frequently find myself getting hit by attacks that just don't feel like they should be hitting as I dodge.    Attacks, dodging, blocking all feel sluggish.  You can do it, and I'm sure if I just sat here and beat my head against it I would fly through the game, but it sure isn't as fun as most "souls like" games I've played.  If you were looking for something in that genre that's a sidescroller, Hollow Knight is just worlds better than this.The feeling of progression is virtually nonexistent.  There's no xp or leveling system, it's entirely equipment based.  That could be ok if the equipment was really unique and exciting, but it isn’t.  There’s basically 2 stats on every piece, damage/damage mitigation coupled with weight.  That’s it.  The 3 different weapon types dictate general swing speed and reach.  That’s it.  So you don’t progress a character, and the equipment you attain is all extremely same-y.I think the thing disappointing me the most is the repetitiveness of the game.  There’s just a massive lack of content here.  The first couple hours will be fun, you’re seeing new areas and enemies.  But then… you mostly stop getting new areas.  You might spend 2 hours grinding literally the same room, which you have to keep running back to over and over (because you can only have one quest at a time), to get enough currency to progress the story.  And that recipe seems to be through pretty much the whole game.  I got into the third iteration of this loop when I decided it just wasn’t worth it anymore.  I’d rather have had 5 hours of actual content than what appears to be 5 hours of actual content with 20 hours of filler slapped on.  And forget the kinds of neat exploration you do in a normal souls-like, at least in the first half of the game.  It’s effectively entirely on rails… the “exploring” you do is highly obvious and scripted.One additional thing to mention: the game is basically unplayable without a controller.  Seriously.  I play most souls-likes with a mouse and keyboard even though it’s more difficult, but for this particular game it just isn’t doable.  If you don’t have a controller don’t bother frankly.All in all, the game has a cool atmosphere and art style, and the narration by the guy that narrated Geralt in the Witcher games is a lot of fun.  But fundamentally the game just doesn’t feel very good to me.  It isn’t utter trash, I’d say if we were doing a 1-10 rating system it’s somewhere around a 4 or 5.  But ultimately I didn’t feel it was enjoyable enough to stick more than 7 hours into so I can’t honestly recommend it.
