_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is an action RPG that borrows elements from the Souls genre. The gear system might feel familiar to you if you've played Souls games before. There are a few different weapon and armor types. Depending on what you equip, your damage output will change, but weight is also something you need to consider, as the bigger the load you carry, the slower your dodges will be.In this game, you've got light weapons on your primary attack button. These are usually a bit more swift, and can be charged up if you hold the button down.On your secondary attack button, you carry your two-handed weapons. Usually a bit heavier. Throughout combat, you can alternate attacks seamlessly between the two. On top of that, you have a ranged weapon that can be fired at enemies.As for defence, you've got a shield, that can additionally parry if you time it right, as well as a short evade, and a dodge roll for further distance coverage.I found the combat to be exhilarating. You are very often caught in between two enemies. You'll have to shield arrows flying at you from one side, while you fend off enemies on the other.Enemies also all have special attacks, that are either undodgeable or unblockable. Depending on the warning above them, you will have to use the corresponding defensive manouver. I loved the combat system, as I always felt like I had to be alert, and aggressive. It is quite unforgiving, and you can die quite quickly, but I never found the game to be that daunting.Similarly to Dark Souls, you can heal combat damage by drinking from your flask. However, in this case, it heals gradually as you hold the button. I think this is a lot more of an interesting and tense way to do it.To save at a checkpoint, you sit down to rest at certain benches. These do not replenish your flask. You will have to look for specific tankards for that. As for the story, the frogs have invaded your rat kingdom. You must take it back. Although simple, the story is quite compelling. You actually do end up caring for NPCs that you meet briefly throughout the game, despite the fact that there's no voice acting. Instead, they squeek and grunt with speech bubbles to get the point across. It's effective, and keeps the appropriate tone of the game. The game's overarching story is narrated. By Geralt of Rivia, in fact. It startled me at first, but I felt his voice was perfect for it. Every now and again, he will comment on what your character's next goal might be, or what they are thinking. It isn't constant commentary.I really enjoy the world the game is set in, and it manages to always feel alive. Characters come and sweep rubbel from areas you've already cleared, and you can see enemies patrolling in the background. There's so much nice attention to detail.The aesthetic speaks for itself, and I personally love the art style. It reminds me of Darkest Dungeon, but not as terrifying. More along the lines of a dark fairytale book. This accompanied with the beautiful lighting effects and parallax, it's just a joy to look at.To conclude, I am in love with the game. It feels so great and everything about it feels thought out and polished. The only real complaint I have, is that at a certain point, the game has you run back and forth between the same areas doing similar quests. It gets a bit tedious, but overcomes that after a while. Most of the game is refreshing. Overall, I highly recommend it! I think it's my favourite game I've played this year!

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank A- (85-88%)Great game - play this if you can!!See my profile for more details about my reviews.What a great little game! Tails of Iron really took me by surprise, and like a slow burn. I had not much expectation for it, although the trailers and images made me probably think that it would be more of an adventure RPG than anything. Not at all! This is a huge tribute to Dark Souls (tough fighting gameplay, basic enemies can kill you quickly, painful bosses, light/medium/heavy weight gear with rolling and parrying, drinking potions etc etc...). The game is also mixed with a bit of metroidvania ala Hollow Knight but with barely any platforming, a bit of Witcher for its medieval fantasy atmosphere (and Geralt as a voiceover!), and a bit of references here and there like Metro 2033 etc.The first couple of hours, I was really underwhelmed, not only by the heavy gameplay (it FEELS clunky at first), but also by the odd choice of making the characters do annoying little sounds, and by the repetitiveness of it (you will backtrack DOZENS of times, and the overall map is not really big, this is NOT a metroidvania for that). The only thing that captivated me... was the visuals. MY GOD this game is BEAUTIFUL. The art is FANTASTIC. So I kept on because of that... well, served me well, because that little game is GREAT. The gameplay ends up being very pleasant to handle, the story, atmosphere and writing are all quite good, and the game just oozes of love in its craft. I really believe the guys who did this game did it with their HEART and SWEAT. Congratulations for that. So many references in it, such a good gameplay, so many tough fights, please if you try this game do not give up, it rewards you for staying (isn't it the case for any FromSoftware after all?).I came for the art (hats off to the artist, my god this is sumptuous), but I stayed for the game itself. If you loved Blasphemous like I did, you ought to try this one too. I hope now Odd Bug will make a HUGE next game, they deserve to be famous. is  on ,  on ,  on

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say, I friggin hate that this game keeps getting called a souls-like. Difficult side-scrolling exploration games with minimal health and challenging bosses existed before Dark Souls dangit. Just because it's grimdark with a melee combat system more complex than the OG Castlevania doesn't mean it's Souls-like. If anything, this reminds me more of Castlevania than Dark Souls, or Megaman, or any of the other hundred or so games that came out before dark souls that played like this. Speaking of which, Don't come into this game expecting Dark Souls. You will have to unlearn some of the habits those games have drilled into you, like depending on I-frames to dodge attacks instead of using dodge to get out of the way, or thinking you can push the offensive while a boss is mid attack combo. Like I said, this game plays more like a classic Action side-scroller. In fact, they also incorporated some mechanics that I would love to see in an actual souls game, such as a healing system where instead of a fixed health gain per item use, it's based on a health gain to resource drain mechanic as you steadily drink to restore health. Much better for not wasting healing uses like in souls games, and I haven't seen it in too many other games. Pitfall Harry the lost expedition being the only other one I remember it from.As for the game itself, haven't played it long, but I love almost everything about it so far. Combat is visceral, Story is straightforward and easy to get behind, and the world and art is just beautiful. Makes me feel like I'm watching an old fable cartoon. On top of that I just love brutal cutsy stuff. That kind of too kawaii to live, too sugoi to die with forest critters murdering the hell out of one another. Love it.I can agree on some of the attacks the bosses do being BS, particularly the AoEs, but so far, I haven't been felled by them to such an extent where they become impassible. Maybe I'll change my tune after I progress farther, but as is, I love this game. I watched one review on it that labeled it as mediocre, and I'm glad I didn't listen to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted 2D-soulslike with lots of charm and an intriguing world, which kept me hooked till the very end. As i am still very alien and new to games which offer similar combat styles, i cannot account to other reviews by fellow gamers complaining about flaws in the fighting mechanics. Well... the game is not easy and as i have played the whole thing in Bloody Whiskers mode i cannot deny saying that i experienced points where i chewed on the armrests of my chair xD more experienced players and Souls veterans may find a hidden gem in this game for themselves.A few points that i noticed (or were too stupid to understand xD), that could maybe be improved: - i totally get some people complaining about backtracking and having to run back and forth just to accept a new quest from a questboard. Personally, i had no problem with this as i always enjoyed the artistic backgrounds and lovely music while traversing through the different game sections. Maybe this could be solved by adding more fast-travel boards, items or companions that allow faster travelling (a mole that could dig you and himself to another level would be awesome, for example in the crypt - the moles also had pretty impressive vehicles which would be awesome to use for yourself at some point ;D ) or allowing players to jump to different areas in one section (if i remember correctly, there are two fast-travel boards in the mines but you cannot travel between them)- the currency system (iron and monster parts) and the option to exchange became obsolete for me towards the end of the game as i gained everything by defeating enemies. Its a nice idea but could maybe be elaborated upon in the second game :D- several times i encountered a bug were i was stuck in the flask-drinking animation when re-spawning at a save point. A quick reload fixed the problem but maybe a small bug fix can remove it :D- the depth of the armor system could maybe be extended upon as well as the idea of having certain armor with perks and attributes against certain monster types is nice but fell short for me at the end of the main game and the Fir-forest DLC as new monsters appeared and stats of new acquired armor parts cannot be changed. (being able to upgrade your favourite amor/weapon and changing its attributes would be neat)I really enjoyed my journey with ToI and would always recommend everyone to check it out for themselves. Really looking forward for the second part (hopefully Geralt of Rivia is still narrating the story!!!? :D)Cheers, OLF

I've never played dark souls or bloodborne games before so this was my first ever Souls-Like game. When I jumped in, I was met with beautiful scenery,the ambiance of the different environments, a well written story, amazing narration, and out of this world fights and boss battles that had my learning curve wanting more at every defeat. The tail of Redgi and his kingdom is forever in my heart and if there is a sequel coming sometime soon you can believe I will be right there getting my copy! I am highly satisfied that I chose this game as my first Souls-like experience. @OodBugStudio Thank You for allowing me to take this amazing journey!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit mixed on this one. On one hand, I love the artstyle, the story, the naration. It's just very.. redwall. I don't mind the repeating quests and the backtracking. The main problem here is the combat system. I've played a lot of souls games. When you get killed, it's usually "fair". Here that's not quite the case:* The knockback attacks can be very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. No windup, they knock you back, and then hit you multiple times when you're down. You need to know when a boss can do knockback, and avoid those situations entirely. The final bosses second phase is especially ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in phase 2.* The hitboxes can be quite inconsistent* Some attacks are just very hard/impossible to block if you're badly positioned* The lack of i-framing does hurt hereTo beat some bosses, you have to "play" their AI. Invite certain attacks, position yourself so other attack types are rarer. This is just.. tedious. This might be coloured by me playing on the highest difficulty. Everything is beatable, sometimes it just takes a long time. I suspect higher difficulty levels just magnify the issues the combat system has.The game is fun. The expansion bosses feel fairer. I hope they fix the issues in part 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game overall. Artwork was awesome. I enjoyed all the backgrounds and the cool boss designs. The combat was well executed, crisp, and responsive. Very beginner friendly with the visual cue system to let you know what type of attack the enemy is executing. If you are on the fence about this game because you don't like how hard souls-like games can be, this game is very noob friendly. What could have been better?The metroidvania aspects of the game (backtracking/gaining new abilities) could have been better executed and more interesting. It felt uninspired.No custom keybinds/controller mapping is a big drawback. I feel like that is inexcusable, to be honest, but I will still rate the game positive because overall I enjoyed my experience very much. The flute noise the rats make when they talk was cute at first, but became irritating by the end of the game. Finally, I'm super triggered cuz I'm missing 1 piece of light armor to 100% the game. I have no good way to figure out where that armor is. I guess I'll mindlessly traverse the world looking for it, but I wish there was a better way :'(Edit: Alright, I found the stupid armor. 100% in 7 hours of play-time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Awful attack animations leave you wondering what exactly each enemy will do next. You have to hard learn what each of their code will do based on your position to them and their position in the room. Many enemies have the same symbol for a number of their attacks, and each of them will hit you at different areas if you're not positioning correctly. The story is charming and the narrator is great, along with the art direction.The gameplay unfortunately is the meat of the game though, and that, became quickly more irritating than fun, worsening as the "difficulty" of the areas went up.Don't play this game for the challenge, as the design of it is simply a memory test of learning every single enemy. I'd recommend playing it on easy, not sure how much of a difference that makes as I played on normal.But, the story is decent enough if you can stomach the irritations of combat and mandatory side quests that have you walking back and forth between long treks, some of which will make you go back that very same area you just came from, and you can't grab all of the quests in one go.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game by a quite small studio. Tails of Iron definetly shines in environment and character design. The characters are surprisingly endearing despite never uttering anything other than squieks and the combat is pretty good too. Other people have explained why better than I could.My main issues are, as others have pointed out, that there is waaaay too much backtracking. Like, early ps3 levels of backtracking. It absolutely kills the pacing and makes you not want to play the game in certain sections.Another issue I have is coming in towards the end. The frogs have been established as "vicious tribals" which is quite problematic in of itself but towards the end you see frog farmers just going about their business and even Regi (The MC) says that the frog field seem just like home. You expect there to be a "we misunderstood them" or an "they were misled by their power hungry leader" moment but that just never comes.  Like, please pick a lane devs. I'm not gonna hold that against them too much, not even AAA games get that right (looking at you Jedi: Fallen Order)But all in all, can recommend at a discount. I think 20€ is a fair price for the game, 25€ is a little much.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A finely crafted and satisfying game that has equal parts grit and charm. Much like Hollow Knight the beautifully drawn setting makes the world of Tails of Iron a joy to explore. There is far less difficult platforming in this game, however. The meat of the game feels much more like Salt and Sanctuary, whereby you try different loadouts and are met with enemies who have set attack patterns. If you are a fan of Hollow Knight or Salt and Sanctuary you will love this game. The only criticism I would give Tails of Iron is that, for a 'souls-like', it is quite easy. Perhaps this reflects the fact that it was also released on the Nintendo Switch. Very few of the bosses really challenged me for a long period of time. Nevertheless, there were some tense moments that were satisfying to overcome.Without spoiling any plot elements, there is a fantastic setting twist that has to do with the Mole People of this game. Not only was it very clever it also sets up what is surely going to be a sequel to Tails of Iron. More evidence that playing smaller indie games is just the way to go.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is a "Geralt of Rivia ASMR" RPG. Honestly the narrator makes this game at least twice as good as it would be without. Gameplay wise Tails of Iron is rather simple, but polished enough that the combat is engaging so simple button mashing won't work. Some attacks cannot be dodged while some attacks cannot be parried which is indicated by red/yellow symbols. Graphics are amazing and music fits the game perfectly. Tails of Iron is pretty much a nearly perfect short game. The only annoying thing is that some hitboxes are quite questionable and attacks that definitely should not hit still did hit.One important thing, this game is not a souls-like. Sure it features parry based combat system and equipment load mechanic, but that's about it. There are no bonfires, no souls lost on death and no stamina.As for the difficulty, unless you play on Bloody Whiskers the game will be rather easy and all of the bosses will be easily doable within a handful of tries. If you do play on Bloody Whiskers the game sadly won't be challenging and will just be bs. Hitboxes feel even worse and rolls still don't give i-frames.Tails of Iron works amazingly on Steam Deck with no tweaks required.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Has some good things but also the most frustrating dodge implementation I have ever played, and the last boss make combos that are guaranteed death. Played on hard with light gear. I like hard games but I don't understand this trend of making games so difficult that they stop being fun.- Why make a dodge that doesn't dodge consistently or not at all?- Why make some attacks have the same initial animation?- Why make combos that are unavoidable?This is cheap low level design decisions.If you want to save yourself out of the most frustrating experience, do not try Hard mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The platforming is clunky is hell and serves no real purpose here, but the boss-fights are fun and some really are oh-so-challaging. I really enjoyed the backgrounds, art direction and humor. 100% achievments in about 17 very satisfying hours. Not really souls-like though, not sure why the tag is added here. It's sort of like Hollow-Knight at home, with more emphasis on story.

Just Hold Guard and then Press HEAVY ATTACK not DAMN NORMAL ATTACK. If I understood this, I would have finished this within less time than what I already had. (Why wasn't the narrator explaining the training segment is Beyond me. He explained Everything except that part.)-Most powerful One hand weapon have a stupid hitbox where you won't hit smaller targets near you because it is performed in an Arc. Smaller bugs will not be hit by it, and it is annoying when you want to refill your Bug Juice aka ESTUS FLASK same golden color.-Stupid travel system where you travel on each map to ONLY one main travel location while the same map have multiple travel locations. (Damn waste of time)- Dodge doesn't have invincibility + the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow roll ("Lightweight=♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow roll", "Mid weight=technically a roll aka Fat rolling" "Heavy weight= I didn't try it because mid roll and light roll hardly work and if fast unblockable were done and you didn't predict it before attack start YOU WILL GET HIT with string attacks that takes half if not all your HP".- Multiple heavy enemies CAN stun you when they do the unblock-able attack back to back.- Your movement with Attacks is like a slow motion Matrix to the enemies and I think the weight only effect your double Roll speed.-You can't map the buttons which is fine MOSTLY except for the point below.-The Devs who thought it was a great idea to make the guard button the back Left trigger and the healing Left trigger rather than the opposite just like Darksouls. Thankfully, the saving system returned me shortly from where I Bugged.- That one Dev that makes things annoying with ONE Achievement requiring to Replay everything on hard mod. The fast jumping unblockable is favored against you and if for some reason the AI decided to jump three times, and you are at the corner after running from the first jumping unblockable, you better know you will be hit. Add more damage by the Hard mod and some enemies can chain block with that hit = instant death. I will save myself the annoyance and enjoy the game rather than start hating it for it's short coming. _childDocuments_.review: Did you read Mouse Guard when you were younger? Perhaps you've read Podkin-One-Ear as of recent or really enjoy the theme of anthropomorphic attributes to woodland creatures... in a Souls-Like setting? This game is for you.Containing a beautiful story; tasked to protect your homeland after your father recently falls victim of the fearsome Toad Leader at his own celebratory tournament. Unfortunately you're the youngest of Rats within a large family and you're the only one who is charged with hunting down the Toad leader and taking back your land.This game is distracting enough to make you fawn over the adorable nature of being a rat with whimsical sound effects for their narration, to completely overwhelm you in combat if you're not prepared with the queues of enemy attacks. The combat is challenging but each enemy has weak points and can be taken down slowly or quickly depending on your own strategy and skill set.Collecting equipment is seemingly endless and I'm not overly sure if their attributes work within combat to defend against certain enemies, I'm a coward and played more for the story line however I'd imagine with higher difficulties they would become very situational.The artwork is astounding and coherent throughout the levels, It's very inspiring to see the level of detail and parallax effect within a 2d environment, every town and area has a distinct atmosphere complimented beautifully with the music, I could listen to the MoleTown rave all day.I can't see much return value after completing some of the secret areas after the storyline other than to achieve higher difficulty trophies but this has been the best 4-5 hours I've spent in any side scroll adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game. Anyone thinking of purchasing it I recommend you skip it. It's very short and can be beat in a couple hours on normal difficulty or around 10 on hard mode. The combat is all around bad and has many issues making it very frustrating. Enemies have attack indicators that tell you how you're supposed to deal with their attacks, but they become basically pointless on 90% of the bosses who have hyper attack speeds, huge attack hit boxes and cheap shots that can hit you when they really shouldn't. This causes the boss fights to devolve into a memorization game. You can't react to anything they do without prior knowledge and if you mess up the pattern you will be chain attacked till you die or the AI derps out and maybe gives you a second to stabilize. Bosses attack patterns can also be very random at times.All weapons have basically the same attack animations. Armor comes in all shapes and sizes, but 80% of the ones you find don't serve a purpose as you already have better ones when you find them. Nothing felt well designed when it came to weapon and armor selection. Your defense and attack stats are mostly just for show and very little changes if they are high or low. Your health bar is basically a LIE and most things do 75% of your life on the first hit then the next hit magically only does 24% of your health. I exploited this to the max to beat hard mode and healed for only 10% of my health each time to extend the amount of times I could get hit. The only time you can really die is when your under 10% health.The game play is repetitive. There is no searching for upgrades or power ups to find. The game puts you on rails from the very beginning and there is no deviation from it. Everything you do is in the same order and nothing you can do changes it. For some reason the developers give you the best weapon in the game at the halfway point as well. There aren't a lot of areas to explore either.On the other hand the one thing I thought was decent was the rebuilding of your town/castle, but it doesn't really change anything in the game other than the scenery. It would be nice if you had to make decisions on what to upgrade or hell just have something to spend your resources as I was capped out most of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is challenging and fun game with gorgeous graphics, a diverse selection of enemies and equipment and a decent story narrated by the voice actor of no other than Gerat of Rivia from our beloved Witcher games.However, among the games downsides is that it has no bestiary with information about the various enemies, and the fighting mechanics, while challenging and satisfying, are not particularly deep.If you enjoyed Salt and Sanctuary and looking for something of similar genre to scratch your itch, your certainly should give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Salt & Sanctuary or Hollow Knight, but now with rats. It is nowhere as open-ended or long as the two, but still offers high quality gameplay from start to finish. I completed the base game and free dlc on the normal difficulty just under 12 hours.Highlights:- Awesome art style, character and world design.- Great attention to detail, for example whenever there is a soundtrack playing, usually you can find a bard or musician somewhere in the map who is playing an instrument.- Levels are all visually distinct and immersive, if only there was more to explore.- Plenty armor and weapons to find, some designs of which clearly inspired by The Witcher.- Engaging combat for a 2D Soulslike, but has one pretty big flaw (explained below).Criticism- Mostly linear progression, yes there is some side content off the beaten which is VERY worth to tackle, but the general storyline is quite strict in terms of where you can go.- Lack of i-frames on dodge. I understand this was to make positioning important, but enemies' pink / area of effect attacks often cover too wide of an area and happen to fast to reliably dodge AND can be spammed. Many of such attacks are outright undodgeable if you are too near the borders of the combat area.- Finnicky flying enemies. Sometimes, hitting a flying enemy (especially the mozis) does not register despite them clearly being in the hitbox.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, however it feels like it is missing something. As the game is, it is good. The graphics are clearly the place where a lot of love and care has been put into. The narrator is great, overall presentation is frickin' awesome but, the game desperately needs two things. A sense of progression and music.Like, sure you get weapons and armor quite regularly but, aside from that the game-play stays the same. Learn patters and hope you don't mess up. Even though at the time of writing this I haven't finished the game yet, but I do feel like it needs something more. The map opens up but, I know there may be a armor piece or weapon to discover when I go there. But, I just can't shake the feeling that there should be more to this. Finding a boss to kill it and getting really nothing interesting in return just isn't really a reward of its own.What I mean by lack of music that there isn't really music. Just ambient sounds, and creature sounds. There are few places where there is music, but that is about it. It needs music. Exploring feels a little bit hollow when there is no track to go alongside it.But with all that said, the rat is fun to control. Moving around and slashing foes is fun, but I do wish there was bit more to it. What is great about this style of game is that I can pretty confidently say that this is quite safe to buy. You will be doing the same thing from hour 1 to hour 5, but it is harder. So, if you buy this and read this review, and decide to give it a go. If the first hour isn't fun for you, refund this. Personally, I am gonna keep playing this to finish. But, the game is on the harder side and I play on medium. In my opinion I do think it is hard to squeeze more hours out of you, to cover for lack of content. But that is my opinion.Edit: I have played through the game. I had to start a new save file with easier difficulty, as the default or "recommended" difficulty is bit too much for me and one boss had me stumped. I wish there was some way of customizing it as the middle difficulty was way is too hard for me, and I don't have time to bash my head against the wall and try something over and over again. But, the easy difficulty was too easy.However, with that said it was worth experiencing. And I can say that I have no interest in playing in harder difficulty, seeing what was the last boss move set. I do wish there was more to this game, but as it is. It is fine.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this "not very hard" game has an interesting game mode that's available even for a first playthrough called "Bloody Whiskers". While playing this mode is definitely not recommended for most players, I consider it a suitable challenge for Souls veterans. With this single mode, the combat system of the game is transformed into one of the most punishing and intricate puzzle I've come across.Despite my extensive experience with Souls titles, I must say that the "Bloody Whiskers" mode is one of the most challenging gaming experiences I ever come across. While the regular base game may be finished in 10 hours or so, this mode took me over 20 hours to beat - it definitely earned its price.It's essential to unlearn some of the Souls habits (e.g. i-frames). The boss fights are more akin to fighting games, where spacing, positioning and planning are everything. There are attacks that cannot be avoided if you are in the wrong place at the wrong time, but with enough attention and practice, you can practically avoid getting hit even on the toughest of bosses. The game has a fair number of bosses, and they typically have some interesting designs and multiple phases.While the base game may be a chill story with passable combat, "Bloody Whiskers" is when the game is transformed into a SL1 Wretch challenge. If this difficulty mode had not been available from the start, I doubt that I would have enjoyed the game as much, nor discovered nearly as much tricks and nuances in the combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I gotta admit, I didn't think I'd enjoy this game as much as I did. It has its flaws, yes, but the overall package is very endearing. I LOVE when games try unique art styles and presentations, to which this game shines in that the department. The combat mechanics were easy to grasp, and collecting and experimenting with different armor pieces was fun. The narrative complemented the "souls-like" gameplay it was going for. However, I found some encounters to be unfairly tuned, especially on normal difficulty, and frustratingly difficult on "Bloody Whiskers" (Hard mode) due to hit box issues. Nevertheless, I still enjoyed my time with the game and still felt that dopamine hit after successfully clearing a hard boss fight.  If you appreciate a challenge and are drawn to games with cool art styles, this one is definitely worth checking out!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is dark, brutal and heavy. Its combat is so much fun, with parries and some awesome excution animations that feel savage and have a amazing "die ♥♥♥♥♥ die" energy to them. The art and backround are beautiful, dark atmospheric scenes made only better by amazing uses of paralax scrolling.. I will say the music is a bit lacking. You only hear it when something or someone in the world is playing it (bard, speakers, whatever) but this means alot of the time you're fighting to ambiance and it feels a little lacking... But really the combat alone makes up for it, just wait until you get your two handed weapon and you'll have a blast. Oh and story is a little lacking, and it has some padding which can drag things down a bit. Its not much more then "pause the story and go fight mini bosses" but its all good fun~Edit: the new content is so SWEET! <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game on the hardest difficulty is not for the faint of heart - achievement hunters beware!This game has charm and a nice aesthetic but it will piss you off. Hitboxes are bad and there's no invincibility frames on dodges. Most boss arena claustrophobic, oftentimes making getting hit by attacks inevitable, especially when bosses or groups of common enemies start mixing up between unblockable attacks (red flash sign) where you can just dodge to escape and the slam attacks (red circles) where you have to double roll away from in order to not get hit.There's also unparriable attacks (yellow flash sign) often executed by enemies capable of thrust attacks, similar to Sekiro's Mikiri Counter mechanic. Not to mention the fact that whenever your health gets low enough, your screen starts to grey out to indicate that you're near death. You cannot turn this option off and it sucks because it interferes with your ability to read enemy attacks as the type of attacks the enemy throw are indicated by different colored icons. In theory the contrast between grey and solid colors would help, but the grey screen effect also makes it harder to read ordinary enemy attacks that have no special characteristics as it darkens the game screen.The flaws of the core combat mechanics shows itself when you play this game on Bloody Whiskers mode as enemy attacks are sped up and damage is increased even more to the point where you get stuck positive feedback loops in which the enemies or bosses combo you back to back until you die.Regardless of its flaws, I beat the game on mouse and keyboard on Bloody Whiskers my first playthrough and am about to finish up the new update's content thus beating the game 100% and getting all achievements. I enjoyed the aesthetic and the narration done by Geralt of Rivia and even the puns. There's charm to the game but that charm might not be enough to win you over if you find the combat mechanics overwhelmingly frustrating/unfair/janky. I was debating between recommending this game or not, I'd say it's worth playing on the lower difficulty. Here's hoping the sequel has better fleshed out combat mechanics and hitboxes and i-frames on dodges/rolls.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: An utterly gorgeous and viscerally satisfying game held back by the lack of variety and re-use of old areas. The games art style is absolutely beautiful, drawing you into the environment and characters like few other 2D games manage. Every item you can equip has a unique model which is visible when displayed on your character, making collecting them all very satisfying, by far not a standard for 2D games of this nature.Something that I would have loved to see more are themed/silly items (cheese shields, tail swords, etc) and objects to signify that this is indeed a rat kingdom. As it stands it's just a wonderfully realized medieval world that happens to be inhabited by rats. Very few items/areas have enough of a distinctive tone and style to remind you that it is indeed a rat society. I understand this is a personal preference and the art direction team shouldn't be swayed from their vision for the game.The story is very basic and doesn't need to be more complex for what it is. It manages a good balance of dire and dark atmosphere with occasional lighthearted moments. (Also having Geralt of Rivia narrate the story doesn't hurt.)The music is good across the board, so far I haven't encountered a track that really burned itself into my mind but everything fits the atmosphere and environments.The combat system is good for the most part. Attacks, parries and dodges all feel incredibly satisfying and the auto-aiming ranged weapons are a great implementation as an aid in combat that doesn't interrupt the flow. However some of the attacks are poorly/incorrectly telegraphed and can feel misleading. Certain bosses will flash the icon to perform a double evasion roll only to then jump to a completely random point in the arena and proceed to do an attack you would have evaded just by standing still, or dogding normally. If you want to have sekiro-style markers for attacks, they have to be perfectly consistent and predictable.The item system seems a bit unbalanced as there rarely a reason to equip heavier weapons/armour since their bonus defense/attack is neglible and not worth the weight penalty. You can always wait a few minutes to find a weapon which is both lighter and stronger. Also the point of having different weapon classes escapes me if they all work basically the same, the slight differences in attack patterns don't matter for 99% of the enemies and otherwise they all perform the same functions.The game is linear by design but presents itself as an open-ish world where you discover new areas and go back to them later in order to find new quests/items. This seems counterintuitive and can throw people off. Either have a tightly designed linear experience or allow for player exploration and experimentation. Here's it's a weird amalgam that doesn't really work either way.I'm still greatly enjoying my time with the game and will most likely finish it. It's a great first project and I can't wait to see what the developers make next.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron - Where I Set Out to Be a Heroic Rat King but Ended Up as the King of Fleeing (After 11 Hours of Furry Frustration)Rating: ★★★☆☆Tails of Iron, the game where I embarked on a noble quest to save the rodent kingdom but mostly just ran away from colossal frogs (after 11 hours of whisker-twisting excitement).Pros:- I've mastered the art of swift retreat. When you're up against foes like sword-wielding frogs twice your size, the tactical retreat becomes your best friend.- The game's world is like a medieval mouse fairy tale. Roaming through tiny villages, battling enormous foes, and doing quests for fellow rodents is as charming as it is chaotic.- I've learned that sometimes you just need a bigger hammer. Upgrading my mouse hero's weaponry and armor is like that satisfying moment when you finally get your dream gadget.Cons:- My mouse hero should probably consider a career change to professional sprinting. I've run away from more foes than I've slain, and the frogs' croaking taunts me in my sleep.- I've developed an irrational fear of tongues. Frog tongues are like elastic death traps, and their unpredictable strikes have made me jump in real life more times than I'd like to admit.- The game's humor is like a cheesy but lovable animated film. The banter between characters often had me chuckling, even while fleeing for my life.Tails of Iron is a game that invites you to be the hero of a rodent kingdom but doesn't mind if you sprint away from danger. It's the kind of game where you'll start with dreams of epic battles and end up laughing at the sight of a mouse with an oversized hammer outrunning massive frogs.To those contemplating a whiskered adventure: Embrace the retreat, face your frog fears, and remember that in Tails of Iron, it's not about the battles you win; it's about the entertaining run you have while trying.In conclusion, Tails of Iron is where I've learned that when life gives you frogs, rodents, and a really big hammer, you run, you explore, and you laugh at the petite pandemonium.Overall rating: ★★★☆☆

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is above all a labor of love. It is clear in every moving part of this game that this was someone's passion project, and you can tell while playing. Where Tails of Iron shines though is the presentation. The character models, animations, environments, and music really bring the game to life and is the heart of the experience. Paired with the combat, It all comes together to make a very charming world that is a joy to play through.This little game made by a little team driven by passion really does deserve to be enjoyed by more players. Give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great example of laziness. Yes, the the visuals are good, and suddenly hearing the VA of Geralt from the witcher series was nice, but that's it. Once you get past the looks and into the gameplay, you start noticing all the corner-cutting and lack of thought in the design (I will give my examples for this at the end of this review).Boss fights - Lazy. Bosses and their attacks have ridiculous hitboxes. Many times you'd be sure you dodged but still get hit. This is made worse through the 'Bloody Whiskers' mode, since almost every boss chains their attacks and their attacks knock you down. This means that if get caught once, you can't escape and will probably die, even if you had max health. Gameplay itself - Lazy. The are no combos and there isn't any real difference between different weapon types(different attack speeds at best). You can try to use both 1st and 2nd weapon and maybe that allows for faster attacks, but that's it.Most of the time you're running back and forth between quests. Also you get a bow, then a crossbow and then a pistol, but they all feel the same. It's just another button to push when you need to wear down a boss. Regarding the lore and writing - There isn't much of it and the little there is doesn't make any sense. Frogs are your biggest enemy but you'll spend most of the game fighting bugs and walking back and forth through the sewers. The developers tried to add some humor by giving the moles faction a soviet vibe, but it just feels too random and uninspired. Exploration - There is none. The game is linear and the map is small. Most areas are only unlocked through the main quest and 'side-quests' are just running back and forth to kill something in the same general area. Finally, my examples for laziness- Lets say you saved at a bench and you died. Once you are revived, you can't hop off the bench instantly because the game was design in a way that technically your character 'teleports' back to the bench, sits, on it, and that's when the game fades back in. This makes it so it's better to save at an inventory box(Which are almost always next to a bench) and so what's even the point of the bench then.Obstacles re-appear when you re-enter a map, which is the dumbest thing I've encountered in a game. Why do I have to not only run back and forth for some side-quest, but to also have to destroy the same weeds 5 times just to get through the map.All ranged weapons are the same, and their only purpose is to be spammed at bosses.All fall damage is the same, no matter the height. This isn't the big deal but rather the reason for finding this- you have to go through so many ladders in this game, at some point you just start hopping down rather than climbing down endlessly. TL;DR:Game is semi-decent. If you get it at 5-10$ and just play it casually on a low difficulty, it could be worth its time. I'm going to assume it's priced at 25$ since most of the budgest went on Geralt's VA.

_childDocuments_.review: A frustrating mess that goes against all the established rules of the souls-like genre.Pros:+ Nice graphics, I guess+ Keyboard customization is an optionCons:- Combat is completely unsatisfactory, rigid, with no fluidity and no rhythm- Combat can be described as a series of QTE actions. To evade one  roll through red attacks and  block yellow / white attacks. Attempting to block red attacks or roll through yellow / white attacks will lead to an immediate interruption and significant health loss- No I-frames during roll, not even when appropriately used against red enemy attacks- There are dead zones right next to your character where enemies and destroyable scenery cannot be touched. In other words you must be a character length away in order for your strike to connect- No energy bar and/or energy management (unlike every souls-like out there)- Extremely short times for enemy attack telegraphing - Generic story in a by-the-numbers, cookie-cutter fantasy world- Completely linear game. No alternate routes, no unlockable shortcuts, no secrets- No fast-travel system (so far). Annoying levels of needless back-tracking- Unskippable dialogue (i.e. floating pictograms). The flute sounds that accompany said 'dialogue' are annoying after the 100th time. You then have to listen to the (again, unskippable) narrator translating the pictograms into English- Annoying running animation- Garbage inventory system. Weapons & armor aren't named and have no stats, only vague bars to distinguish between their quality levels- Loadout customization only possible at 'bonfires'. Ridiculous- No text description or mouseover tooltips for any inventory gear, items or resources- Keyboard cannot be used for menu / inventory navigation
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is fun, very fun. I can't articulate much past that. The beginning was compelling, even making my wife who loves frogs, hate the antagonists. The gameplay is clean, very few times have I been hit with a wombo combo that kills me before i have the chance to dodge. it's a simple gameplay loop that becomes very satisfying later on as you memorize enemy attack patterns. the art is masterful, very castle crashers-esque, but done in a medieval tone that pulls of a fantastical and yet gritty environment. If you like gritty dark souls like games with unforgiving yet satisfying combat, Tails of Iron is for you. Plus it's a ton of cute knight rats, what could be better!The only issue I've run into is the Doom style executions in the middle of combat. While awesome, often times an enemy winds up for an unblockable attack and turns me into a wall crayon right when i finish the animation. In conclusion, I would whole-heartedly recommend this cutesy, gritty, rat-tastic little sword and board sidescroller that I enjoy so much.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about half way into the gamePros:Lovely artstyleokay gameplayConsSometimes the character just won't climb if you stand too close to the ladder, you have to jump on itProgression system is all over the place, meaning you find 1 weapon then the next 20 will be useless because they are weak.Poorly explained/ indicated mechanics. At first you learn that there are 3 different attacks. Yellow which you can parry, red which you dodge and red circle which you must double dodge most of the time. Now it's all good when indicated but later in many boss fights the indicator is missing and you are left with you've seen the attack once and now you must know how to handle it. While yes this would be nice but not on the 1st encounters because this isn't making the game challenging it just makes it annoying and poorly made.I got no explanation of what toxin does or why should I use it. So I'm guessing it's just extra damage. While it is nice it would be nice if someone explained it that it does nothing but bonus dmg so you are not there waiting for it to do any extra effect. In 6 hours I've found 2 pages of med and light armor and only found 4 heavy armors, which again is a poor progression since every med armor is better than any light and at this point any heavy armor. There is again no explanation of why should I use Sword over axe or spear since they are pretty much the same with very very little variety in moveset. (Some maces are categorized as axes and some hammer as axes for some reason.) The game gave me an explanation about the axe being able to tear down wood baricades, but then again so can the spear or sword so there is nothing special about them.Barricades respawning for no reason except to annoy you and to make it take longer to get from A to B even after you destroyed those. Sidequests, are not sidequests but mandatory quests. They are needed to progress the main story.Currency, it seems like I'm capped at 99 and can't earn more but I can't spend them as there is nothing to spend them on. Lastly while it was fun first, the annoying random instument sounds for rats. It makes no sense. At the very first scene it was funny when we joked about someone probably made the bard eat his whole set of instruments because of how he wakes us up, it got annoying as we progressed. From random balloon or whatever sounds to a whole washing machine effects. It just progressively got worse.I like the game but there are so many problems that I haven't seen anyone mention is strange. But even with this I recommend because it's a nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. Art is great, characters are neat, mechanics are simple. BUT:Battles are just bad and give no joy. Hitboxes of enemies attacks are unpredictable. Fights with more then one opponent and helping NPC are a mess. Everybody moves in the same 2D plane and CPU always attacks player. Often you'll be attacked from outside your field of view. Player attacks never do stagger (except when parrying) or even won't break enemy attacks. Reggie moves slow as turtle, and because of this often there is no way to run/roll away from unblockable enemy attacks.  Enemies are flying and jumping all over the scene and you cant even attack them! Range weapons are weak and don't stagger enemies too. Poison seems to be a placebo rather then doing anything. And worst thing for me - you cannot redefine gamepad controls. WHY? Generally game worthy of buying and playing, but becuse of its length, fights are done in very frustrating way.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing!Reminds me so much of Mouseguard or the Chronicles of Redwall... I simply love the concept!The art-style is gorgeous (hand-drawn but the animations flow very naturally and not at all "stick-figure-y", if you get what I mean?) and everything looks like it jumped right out of a fable book.The gameplay is very solid too! Movement feels fluid already 5 minutes in and combat can be hectic and... well, sometimes pretty hard too, to be honest, but never really unfair. One time you're rolling and jumping all over the battlefield like a one-man-army and the other you decided on tanking with higher defense and clever shield-play and just steamrolling everything that stand before you, calmly and methodically. 100%-ed normal mode and just restarted in hard mode, might say that combat is even better (feels like the stakes are higher). Difficult? At times, sure. Never exasperating or discouraging though.Weaponry is not very varied outside of the 3 weapon types for every category, but it never feels too little. There are indeed lots of different weapons per se, but other than a couple outliers (one very, VERY powerful as well... you'll see :D ) it's mostly reskins of the same weapon types with the same animations but different stats - still pretty cool, nothing missing there.There's also a plethora of references to history, other franchises and general nerd-culture: found myself chuckling quite a bunch of times after seeing names of enemies or locations - or even recognizing parallels in certain situations.The "instrumental" voices and the comic-like speech bubbles are adorable, of course, but what about the narrator? None other than DOUG COCKLE... THAT'S GERALT OF RIVIA, YA'LL! Dayum, stellar casting! Makes the whole story that much more epic and enjoyable - at times witty, but still always heroic and grand.Not much more to add, other than: play it.Odd Bug Studio, chapeau to you. You made an amazing game and a folk tale for the ages.Can't wait for other chronicles from the Tails of Iron world.......... I guess I'm a fan now.

_childDocuments_.review: Man do I love this game! Only  a couple of things though. 1st thing is that dodge & roll don't actually make you invincible like in Dark Souls, which make the game quite unfair at times. You have to guess the hit boxes through trial & error in order to dodge successfully which makes the game a bit more frustrating than it needs to. 2nd thing is about defense vs. weight tradeoff. I find heavy build/ high defense so useless since you can't roll/ dodge effectively and that's 50% of how you survive in this game. And high defense build only gives you marginal difference in taken damage though. So it's more like an illusion of choice and in order to enjoy the game the 1st time you'd have to pick the most optimal build: either go full light gear or balanced & invest weight points in decent weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game so much, but the gameplay is just not fun. Not difficult, it's more like Simon Says rather than actual combat at times, just incredibly slow, clunky and repetitive. You just wait until the enemy telegraphs what kind of attack he is going to do (which is very easy to tell thanks to the colored symbols over their heads) and then you either block, dodge or parry followed by an attack. Rinse and repeat until the enemy goes down. The "difficulty" comes from the lack of invincibilty frames and the slow movement from your character, which can lead to you getting bounced around like a pinball if you have to deal with more than one enemy at a time. And considering the high amount of save points, they knew how annoying that would be. I guess they just didn't know how to fix the problem.Overall: very nice Style over sleep inducing substance.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I enjoyed this game. While being souls like, it didn't feel like a terrible grind. Interesting story points, art and sounds.Some gameplay issues did exist. Early game equipment management was interesting, but at certain points overpowered gear is on the table for people willing to fight a harder boss. While it is rewarding to get  good gear, you lose any point in managing gear if 95% of new items are worse than your nice shiny hammer of death. Resources were managed in odd way. At all points you had a abundance of all the resources. You can use resources to buy poison and arrows, but the later is almost pointless since its more of hassle to buy them than just finding a restock point and poison is overpriced in the store, but bit harder find. Maybe a couple times during the game can you really have a reason to shop.If this game would've dragged on for much longer I think the weakpoints of the game would've started becoming more obvious, but for a 12ish hour game it wasn't glaring
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I was really expecting more from Tails of Iron.  The narrative is pretty generic at best being a simple revenge plot and seeing your empire being rebuilt as you do so.  Nothing deeper than that.  It's fine but I wouldn't call it great.  Combat is a bit janky with some of the mechanical tells feeling a bit misleading (I guess this is where the souls-like aspect comes in where you die and learn.)  A friend had called it  because of how jumpy it looks.  Enemies will jump halfway across the field to throw an attack.The background and environments are  beautiful!  I love looking at them as I'm running through the scenery.  It cant hold up the whole game though.  I really wish the story was more than just defeating the bad guys because they're the baddies.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The experience was like reading a short-novel. I enjoyed the adventure and I am satisfied with the purchase.I liked how the game used text sparingly and, instead, apply pictures and sound together to converse messages to the player. It was an excellent execution of graphics to communicate that was simple, yet, easy to understand.Another thing I liked from the game was the beautiful music. Fantastic soundtrack in the game that help reveal the atmosphere and emotions in the fantasy world.As for the general combat interactions in the game, it felt like a good mix of action, rhythm, and puzzle. Fairly easy to understand right after the combat tutorial. You might fumble with controls in your early encounters, but you will soon become more familiar with how to duel enemies as your adventure progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: Finished the game on normal difficulty. Its challenging enough with really nice pacing. The game has a nice story. CONS: If you care of steam achievements. It has one that requires to beat the final boss on hardest difficulty, but because the difficulty cannot be changed it means you need to play the whole game all over again, not a fan of that. Also, the hardest difficulty is extremely hard.. 2 hits of most mob and you're gone, 1 on bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is PERFECT! ...If you ignore the combat.TL;DR: Buy on sale, play easy mode. Otherwise it's not worth it unless you're a masochist. Just finished the main story on the normal difficulty, I cannot recommend easy mode enough. The visuals, music, sound design, story, character design, and exploration are all brilliantly handled. The issue is that the combat feels horrible. The enemy hitboxes had me exclaiming in frustration at least once each combat, to the point upon defeating a boss I wouldn't feel accomplished as much as I was just thankful that it was finally over. So when you're at the final boss gauntlet of the game it's a slog. Repeating the same janky-feeling fight over and over until by what feels like luck you're able to guess what the game wanted you to do and survive with next to zero health left. I really wish there were invincibility frames on the dash or dodge-roll, most of the times where I'd die and felt frustrated would have been avoided. Now what I'm absolutely astounded wasn't included were invincibility frames upon taking DAMAGE. Holy god how the hell is it fair to take a hit from an enemy, get staggered, take damage from a second, stagger again, then take damage from the first again and die?  I really really want to like this game but I wish I just watched someone else play through it instead of playing it myself! Last note: The attack indicators were also a joke, especially when they show up for half a second before the enemy smacks you with an attack that covers 70% of the battlefield. If the sequel adds I-frames after taking damage that's good enough reason to play the sequel. If it adds I-frames to the roll & dash, they have the perfect game in their little rat paws.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a blast. The visuals are pretty, and the combat is pretty well done for a souls like. The game is pretty straight forward with a lot of liner levels, but it gets to the point. The devs on this game really taught you about this world, and made you feel for it. I highly recommended this game !
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn to Tails of Iron because of its immersive atmosphere and cool setting. Tails of Iron treats you with lovely characters, grotesque enemies, immersive landscapes and living, changing world. Watching trailers I was afraid that the game would be clunky, but it feels much better than it looks. Combat is juicy and gives you feel of a struggle rewarding to overcome. Especially parries and finishers bring seamless, cinematic feel. Character development and customization are far simpler than expected, but serve core gameplay loop well - even tough every weapon in category works the same and there are no skillpoints to dispose, player is encouraged to change weapons and armours according to enemy types, and for balancing weight vs power.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A solid beat 'em up with souls inspired combat. It's not a full/traditional soulslike though - there's no XP to lose, enemies don't respawn after you use a checkpoint, no stamina system, no metroidvania-esque exploration. The game's not interested in punishing or stressing the player out at all.The combat never gets too big for its boots, so you'll usually be fighting one or two enemies at once, 3 or 4 in rare cases. The encounters always fit the combat systems.The animation work has character, but isn't very detailed, so the game relies a lot on visual indicators for the type of attack the enemy will do. It's not as boring as it might sound - one enemy can have several attacks of one type, and to properly react to them you'll need to anticipate them even before the indicator appears.The problem with the game is in the time wasting - you'll be sitting through hundreds of slow, pointless animations and running around the map following quest markers, back and forth between two places at times.If you do decide to play it, don't explore areas that don't have any quests set in them. The game is extremely linear despite being set in an open map, so just wait until a quest takes you somewhere before you waste time running around a new area prior to all the events meant to take place there being set up by the game.You also can't change the difficulty partway through the game, and it takes a long time before the intro gets out of the way and lets you see whether the option you chose actually fits you. Even if you're confident in this style of game, I'd stick with normal difficulty, because the combat just isn't tight enough to dive right into the instadeath mode that is the alternative.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: its aight. Combat is ok, the walking is mostly annoying, the art is nice the premise two. I recommend it for the price i bought it at during sale which is about 5 bucks. Any more and id rather play hollowknight or ninesols which are objectively better, but for the low pice of 5-6 bucks this game delivers enough. It art is pretty sweat, the premise is simple but catchy and rather serious. the fights are challenging, although i am not a big fan of long cooldowns. for example if you do an action you cant do a different action until the animations is finished. Which means you cant just hack and slash otherwise you will be stuck in a movement and cant block for example. This is not a con, just a personal preference. i get it. it makes sense, but at the end of the day playing games is not always about what makes sense but what is more fun. Personally id like to parry whenever i want and attack until the very last millisecound before i have to parry
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wish Steam gave me the option to post mixed reviews, unfortunately I can't so I have to give this a thumbs downEven though it tries to be, it's no Hollow KnightPremise: I haven't finished the game, I think it's not all that bad but the flaws are so blatant and frustrating that I cannot reccomend it in this state for its full price, I got it on the summer sales for like -70%, this might be the right price for it. Also the fact that the background for its Steam page is a collage of positive reviews made by """journalists""" is quite eloquent by itself-All weapons within each subclass have the exact same moveset, boring-The weight system is never explained, I never bothered going above the first tier but from other people's experience it seems like it doesn't matter at all-The additional defense for each enemy type that armor provides feels completely worthless, even the regular defense stats does-Combat in general is lazily designed and frustrating, enemy attacks are often not telegraphed or straight up instantaneous and impossible to dodge if you don't play painfully safe, the timings are inconsistent, some attacks even change between attempts for seemingly no reason, I had this happen in a bossfight, the finisher animations lock you in and if you are fighting multiple enemies at once there's a chance you might get hit instantly once it's done with no way to prevent it-Fall damage is janky and I'm not 100% sure about this but there might be a couple spots where you drop from a high platform and are forced to take it-Half the game is backtracking/running and walking in general which is made even worse by the next two things:-Looting dead enemies and items off the ground is REALLY slow, the animations are (seemingly) randomized but the slowest one takes something like two entire seconds, some save points have a couple grubs to kill to replenish your healing flasks instead of the usual keg that fills it entirely, so you are forced to take out your weapon, oneshot the harmless thing and then harvest the juice which as I said is unnecessarily slow-For some reason, you have to put away your weapons by pressing a button to run faster, which would be fine if it didn't use a half a second long animation and you could move while performing it, can't I just move fast outside of combat automatically?-The sidequests and menu in general are handled horribly, you have to accept sidequests at the quest board, go into the area and complete the quest and then backtrack to the board to accept another quest that takes you basically in the same place of the previous one, forcing you to backtrack for no good reason, just let me accept quests from the menu-Exploring on your own is 99% of the time just a waste of said time, every area I have found was completely empty and its only purpose was to home a story or secondary event, so getting there without the respective mission active doesn't serve any purpose, this is made exponentially worse by the fact that, as I said, it's only true 99% of the time, so if you don't want to miss that 1% of hidden things you are forced to either play it safe and explore constantly, wasting your time in the process, or just look up a guide so you know exactly when and where you should be exploring-When equipping armor and weapons from the designated "chest" that hold all your equipment you can see the weight icon change color when you are picking up something that changes your weight tier, so you can easily see what tier you are in on the fly, really good! But when looting equipment you have the option to either equip it right away or send it to the chest for later, you can see how it changes your current weight but there is no colored icon to indicate the eventual change in weight tier, only the notched bar which is not clear at all, why is this QoL feature missing?-No adjustable video/performance settings other than changing resolution and disabling vsync, I don't care about the fancy bloom (which is way more laggy than it's worth) and parallax, I want a stable framerate-No remap options for controllers-Some minor graphical glitches including one that made the entire ground texture disappear, changing area did not fix it, I assume restarting the game would but I have yet to open it again, so I'm not sure-I'm probably forgetting some thingsThe story and aesthetics are cool, I guess? I personally couldn't care less tho, I play games for the gameplay, if I prioritized these things I would have watched a movieOverall I get the feeling that the devs might have focused way to much on aesthethics and atmosphere and forgot to polish the game and make it fun to play, I haven't gotten to the point of dropping it completely but the more I go on the more I feel that moment getting closer
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing I'd like to say is Souls-like games require two things. Extreme combat difficulty and character progression. This game lacks the later. Because souls refers to a re-collectable currency/exp system lacking that feature makes me feel like I was lied to. The game isn't terrible, although I wouldn't recommend it to my friends. I do feel bad for leaving a negative review but I feel like I have to be honest since I did pay for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Here you play as a youg skaven, defending your lands from frog attacks. Game is cute, narration is on point, and the game is practically a boss run with metroidvania elements (very little) and more arcade-ish combat - challenging, but not as reliant on I-Frames like games such as DS,I would say that the replay value is low, as there is one story, it is being told, your hand is being held - that's it. No complaints really, if Soulslike combat and metroidvanias are your thing, this is a another awesome entry in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Art is fantastic, the combat quickly gets boring. There's not enough variety and combat becomes dodge/parry + button mash attack, repeat. It just seems too simplistic. _childDocuments_.review: 10 hours might not seem like a lot, but for this little indie game it's finishing everything there is to do minus the hardest achievement (beat game on hardest difficulty). I played on the easiest for one reason only, the combat.Combat/Gameplay - this is not this games strongest point. It does the job, but it does become very tedious even on easy difficulty. If you like the challenge it gives on normal or hard (Bloody Whiskers is hard) then you may enjoy it. Essentially it boils down to 3-4 types of attacks your enemy can do. Blockable (let's call them white attacks as sometimes they are colored with white markings), Parry-able which are marked with yellow markings, normal dodging which are red claw marks, and full dodging which you do a roll of and the enemy marks are red circles. You are very punished for adding in any attacks inside the latter 3. If those markings come up, you basically can only do the respective ability to negate damage. Otherwise you are trampled and punished. There are a lot more intricacies like weapon weights, armor weights, resistances to certain types of enemies, etc but from what I've noticed you don't even need to pay attention to those if you become a master of what the game wants you to do during combat.Story - reminds me a lot of when I read the old Brian Jacques series Redwall. You're a rat. Living in a world of other animals. Some are mean, some are allies, some are just regular bugs with no real cognitive thinking abilities other than survival. I enjoyed it but there are some who may say it's rather....generic. Obviously no spoilers but if you've read the old Redwall series, enjoy a good "revenge" story, and like the art style of 2D hand drawn, this is for you.Art style and performance - speaking of art style, this game is gorgeous to me. Doesn't take much to run it either(I completed the game entirely on the Steam Deck with zero issues). A LOT of detail was put into this game and it shows. Absolutely no glitches I ran into, no stutters, no crashes, etc. It played flawlessly to the end. Again, I ran it on the Steam Deck so YMMV.Price point - I got this game on sale for $12.50. For 10 hours of gameplay plus the amount of enjoyment I got out of it I'd say was worth every penny. If you do not play on easy, you may die more and therefore have more playtime but during my easy-mode playthrough I never died once, and just kept making progress so if you buy this game at MSRP, depending on your idea of price point versus hours played versus enjoyment it may be worth considering a sale. However, what is here in that 10 hours is quite enjoyable as mentioned before in the Story section.Overall - I recommend this game to anyone who likes and loves the 2D metroidvania souls-like genre looking to also enjoy a fun story with rats, frogs, bunnies, bugs, etc. There is a ton I did not get into for fear of making this review way too long and frankly, it's cheap enough that if you read this and still want to play it, just do it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: If you like hollow knight and want to play a linear side to side combat game definitely give this a go. Combat is pretty fun. The middle part of the game doing a bunch of back and forth fetch quests does drag on a bit too much but some are optional. Worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty sure this game is under the indie category. This game is so good the art style, game play, game mechanics, everything about this game is phenomenal in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: Received the game via Lurkit Streamed every minute of it 9 near 10 hours. Really cool art style and narrative game :) The names of bosses made me chuckle a good few timesCombat is smooth, bosses and mobs can be challenging. i found my self hitting my head against some of the bosses for a good 30 minutes while others get killed in 1 try.Found myself wanting to play more and i have all but 1 achievement which i will go back and get (need to kill frog king on hard difficulty.100% recommend
