_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Game took me about 11 hours to 100% on hard difficulty (excluding the achievement for beating the game on the highest difficulty)Overall, the story and combat are very good in this game. The story is fairly short, you could probably complete it in like 7-8 hours if you did absolutely none of the side content. Sadly, there are no permanent companions which I thought would be the case when I first bought the game, there are only 3 temporary companions that accompany you during certain missions.The combat in this game is very simplistic in design yet works perfectly. Combat revolves around your arsenal of weapons, of which you have the following: one handed and shield, 2 handed, and ranged. All three of these weapons can be swapped around and combo'd together. For example you can charge an attack with your 2-handed weapon and then immediately follow up with a flurry with your sword and board and then shoot an enemy on the other side of them. As for defensive abilities, the player can block, parry, dodge, and roll. Which one you use depends on the scenario and each has their uses. Now the main draw of the game are the bosses. The difficulty of he bosses varies wildly but there are some bosses where you should definitely prepare for some torture. I never really found myself getting bored in boss fights because each of them have multiple different attacks and most have multiple phases. Most bosses would take me 2-3 attempts to beat on hard difficulty but a certain marvel wannabe took me about 10-15 attempts to be able to beat.Overall, the game is very good, there weren't very many issues that I noticed during play. The only problem I had was that it seemed as if attack canceling didn't work in combat as I would try to dodge an unblockable attack but my character would continue their shield bash anyway. I didn't encounter any bugs whatsoever during my playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off really great.Nice little action game with weighty combat.After a few hours the game turns into pure padding.It's honestly quite a slog, returning to places you've been many times, killing the same enemies over and over.The game calls these "side-quests", but they are not. They are required to progress the story.If these were removed entirely and the game length cut down, it would be amazing.But it is just terrible pacing and I can not find it in myself to finish the game
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a very charming surprise. the art direction went exactly where it needed to go. combat is tight and responsive tho i will say that a few bosses have attacks that can randomly trigger before you have a chance to proactively reposition and they will ruin your day but besides that combat is simple yet quite engaging. i was hoping the story would expand a bit more on what clearly seems to be a more complex story than meets the eye. theres also a bunch of characters that are oddly useless. the turtle and the bunny for example. you meet them once and both are just, there. turtle is an old friend of your dad and he rows the boat for one single sequence. no chat no nada, he just is. same with the bunny on the cover of the game. you fight him at the end of the game as extra content, thats it. is this a good purchase? yes. is this going to be the big next sleeper hit? no
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The general tone youll get from comments is that its fun and a lot of love but some of the criticism is there. I enjoyed the game and loved the narrator and the late Kings behind the scenes story. Sad part is thats the ONLY story. The rest is a normal hero's tale. Get beat down get up and get revenge. Game is easy even on normal and the story isnt really there, most of its doing the side quests for gold for story progression.The fun times were definitely there, the game is fun and the story has its comic relief. All in all, 7/10 i enjoyed the game, just wish there was more, Outside of the late Kings story.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A cool game that I had a ton of fun playing and completing to 100% after coming back for it's update.If you like to get beat up over and over again, you'll enjoy this.The art is nice and I very much liked looking in the backgrounds a lot, Combat is great in my opinion, and the story is being a rat exterminating a whole frog race.Weapons and equipment have a scale to them, as well as weight, armor can defend better against certain enemies better then others do but you'll mostly be fighting against frogs so you don't have to switch it up a ton.Weird quirk about weapons, only stat shown is their damage scale. However some can attack faster or slower then normal, not obvious for all of them but it's there.You will die, a lot, even on it's normal difficulty. And I first played it on it's hardest, which sure was challenging, but learning the combat took some time. Then I was smooth sailing with some bumps along the way.Only issues I ever had were attacks from certain bosses being cheap and almost unavoidable, but if you got a iron will, you'll end up making it.The gameplay itself is good but the way some enemies attack can be hard to predict since they are telegraphed in a weird way.There is some repetitiveness to the game such as some quests going over the same path 3 times over and overall backtracking quite a bit. I have an aggressive play style so perhaps a more passive one will suit others better. the game is a solid 6/10 If you can overlook it's flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: i never wrote a review about anything in my life but the HITBOXES of 80% of the enemies you encounter were utter BS. i went with the hardest difficulty looking for a challenge but i was quickly humbled by it, and the fact you can't lower the difficulty after changing your mind was brutal because now you have to restart things all over from the start. the backtracking was repetitive and tedious but the story, atmosphere and art design were beautiful. 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever played Hollow Knight, you will very likely enjoy this game as well. It's got the same amount of charm, good narrative, great art and battle mechanics that are very satisfying, though they take some getting used to. I love roaming around this rat kingdom looking for fights to win and treasures to discover. Can't wait to finish the whole thing!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: An ideal game for who love this genre but don't have too much time.The fighting system is pretty cool and easy to learn. However this is also a cons of this game, the move set of bosses is repeated. The final boss is the most boring fighting screen you ever see. Once you defeat the mosquito boss, you master the game.Otherwise, this game is good for a short game and for entry level of rogue-like genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. The gameplay feels smooth on controller, and the the enemies go through a variety of attacks that you have to actually combat in order to not die. It feels pretty organic and smooth, even though it can be infuriatingly difficult. But with the number of save points the game gives you, it actually isn't too bad going back and re-fighting something. The plot is also really easy to invest in, especially if you grew up on Redwall (and you'll be spared pages upon pages of reading about food). It's easy to root for the hero, and the fact that your story is told both by the visual language of the animals AND the voice actor for Geralt from the Witcher games, doesn't hurt either.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Stop what you're doing and just play this game. Cool premise and amazing narration. Combat isn't too difficult compare to other souls-like video games, but it can still be challenging at times. Fit with amazing story telling and hilarious quips by the narrator here and there, this game had me asking for more throughout my entire play through of the game. Personally I believe this is a hidden gem in the rough and would give this game a 9/10 (highly recommend).
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really polished and good.It isnt a Metroidvania, and youre only character progress is stat bonuses associated with new and shiny gear.I like that your kingdom basically gets destroyed at the beginning, and the more story progress you make, the more the kingdom starts repairing itself. Visual progress like that is satisfying.Combat is amazing and the story is really well made and narrated.My only complaint is there are some points which require you to drop down and take fall damage for some reason. Also no re-mapping of controls.A solid 8.5/10 from me
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A neat little game oozing with style and visual aesthetic.  The sound design excels (think  meets ).Having seen a number of reviews criticizing the game for backtracking tedium and rather simple combat, I played the game on the easiest difficulty.  I enjoyed it, and while I probably would've wrung more hours out of this game had I chosen a harder difficulty, I doubt I would've adored those hours.  Combat was challenging enough at some points even on the easy mode.  If I'd really yearned for more challenge, I could've picked worse equipment options.Music's pretty good.  The story hits the same sort of beats as any fairy tale.  The rats speak to you in pictures and whistles.  The only human voice is apparently the voice actor for Geralt from ; however, having not played that game yet, this was not much of a selling point for me, although the in-game references to  series did not escape my notice.  The guy's narration isn't bad, but I wouldn't write home about it; he did seem to put more feeling into it as the story went on, though.A fairly recent review points out that this game is, indeed, not an RPG aside from the dress-up you can play with the equipment.  It does retain a fantasy setting one would expect.I appreciate the game's length.  For me, it did not overstay its welcome and told enough story to satisfy.  Still, if you valuate games based on entertainment hours, perhaps consider picking this up on sale like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is definitely a 7/10, or an 8/10 if you like the "Swords and Whiskers" style. The art and sound design work incredibly well together, none if it feels fake or out of place. The combat is challenging but fun, although with the way shields and dodging work, heavy builds don't feel like they have much of a place. The gear is also strangely distributed you'll often pick up items that are not at all worthwhile. I wish the game was a little bit longer, and that there was less backtracking . I look forward to further updates, dlc, and/or sequels.All in all, it's a worthwhile purchase at full price, but definitely pick it up if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game with great narration and a beautiful artstyle. Could use some more music here and there and at one point I was very frustrated with the sidequests and all the backtracking they involved (but kept on playing and I am happy that I did). The game is completely linear and does not really encourage random exploration (besides maybe a few "secrets"). The game always tells you where to go next and, when you don't but visit some area too early, that is without the appropriate quest, you may get a few items and monsters a little earlier but have to come back later, resulting in backtracking a lot. I think here the game could have used more of those metroidvania mechanics to tell you it's not time yet.. Also, speaking of which, there are barriers that you can only break once you get a certain item but the thing is that these respawn on every load of the map and take about 10 seconds to take down. Just why? Also the game never really takes off before maybe the 2 or 3 hour mark?However the world is charming (and small) enough so I was able to overlook the little issues and keep on playing and after finishing the game I can assure you: no regrets. For some people the game may feel too short (after 12 hours I have seen everything that the game has to offer (so far)) but I liked it. It was a neat little story with interesting fights, in a way like a smaller Hollow Knight with more color.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok, but it feels small and the combat feels lacking. The bosses don't move fluidly, they simply fly across the screen at their whim to get in place to perform moves (or simply avoid you). Sometimes, this vague approximation of a leap does damage. Sometimes, it does not. It isn't always clear, and the hitboxes of things isn't always matched by the body size (nor represented by any appropriately large effect), leaving me feeling like I was hit by something unfairly far away.Speaking of hits- armor feels irrelevant. It's always two hits from anything before I'm a hit from death. Thankfully, you can't be one-shot. If you're at risk of death, colors fade. If you heal just enough to see color again, you'll be safe from dying to the next attack. There's little reason (beyond taking a hit that will confirm a second) to heal your whole healthbar as a result, you get more mileage out of your potion with little sips, which are also safer.As for moves from the bosses: Some things are clear, like when an AoE is coming, or something you must dodge, or must parry. They teach you the warning color and symbols that show up before powerful attacks.But the AoE alert doesn't always tell you where the AoE is going to be, or if the boss will move to deliver it (as opposed to simply stomp the floor around them, as the tutorial and starting enemies teach you AoE's do), nor quite how big it is. You only learn after you get hit (or not, if you guessed right). It's similar with charges. In fact, it's confusing as to the difference sometimes. If a stomp involves leaping forward at my exact location, and a charge does too, and neither can be blocked (and I must simply not be there when they happen), why flash different symbols? Parrying, at least, is stupidly easy and satisfying. But most bosses involve dodging. This isn't dark souls, you don't have i-frames for your dodges. Simply don't be where the attack is when it happens.Another thing that isn't clear is when an enemy is in combat or not. Especially when you begin to fight undead, who are some of the most sluggish of enemies when it comes to entering combat. There is no visible difference between someone immortal and unable to be hurt, and when someone is finally done entering the scene and can be hit. It's annoying to wind up a heavy strike and whiff air through an enemy, and get hit as a result. On a similar note, it's not clear when you can or can't damage a boss in phase changes- you only notice when you see the attacks don't hurt the healthbar. Movement is pretty clunky when you explore the world, your character has a lot of weight. I've had plenty of moments where I am just shy of grabbing an easy ledge, or a roof-ladder, and my character either hops in place or strangely leaps forward off a cliff unless I slowly creep-walk with my shield up for the precise spot I need to stand for the grabbing of ledges and ladders to work.Speed is weird. I don't understand why holding different weapons out slows me down, yet there is no draw time for them if you make an attack. I can have a shield and spear out, and instantly swing my greatsword when I press the button for a heavy strike. Yet, now I walk slower because I've been swapped to the heavy weapon. Pressing light attack for my light weapon lets me run faster once again, because it swaps me right back. Sheathing my weapons, understandably, makes me run the fastest. Though I've never done that in combat. In or out of combat, I've never seen reason to waltz around with my greatsword out beyond the style of having a weapon larger than yourself. It's not like I'll be caught wanting for it's power-strike if I have my other weapons out instead, I can draw it and start winding up in an instant. It's strange to make me move slower if I forget to swap back, it seems like I'm meant to use my whole arsenal in any fight.You can't aim your ranged weapon- it fires instantly at a random target when you shoot it. That's not always nice. You have precious few shots, which is more annoying when you miss because the enemy across the room technically hasn't finished walking into combat and become someone you can kill yet.The questing isn't very good from what I've seen. At the start it's nice and varied, but quickly became "Go to the sewer and kill bugs for money. Return to the surface, get new quest (to go to the sewer. to fight bugs). Go to the sewer and kill bugs for money (again)." over and over. That's pretty boring.Thankfully, I only paid $5 for this.

_childDocuments_.review: In general I enjoyed it.  Loved the concept, art, music, theme, story, characters, etc.  It really was great in that regard and better than its price tag.  Loved the narration by Doug Cockles (Geralt of Rivia).  Side-quests are ok - going to be re-traversing the same areas a lot to kill x-monster or do fetch-quests.  This is a common element of rpgs and was ok here.  It had a story element to it, and it was fun to rebuild the keep.  It didn't feel tedious or too overdone to me.  Having the background world adjust over time was a nice touch.From a value standpoint - You can 100% the game in 15-20 hours depending on how good you are at the games mechanics.  That's a pretty good value for price.This is not a perfect game, though.  As much as I loved many aspects of it, the combat system was a bit frustrating to me, especially with boss fights.  The bosses and some tougher enemies will often have insane hitboxes on you and be able to seamlessly hit you multiple times after you're already down while you have very little you can do.  They will often be able to move and attack more fluidly and quickly the way you wish you were able to fight.  There are a lot of unblockable hits that are hard or near impossible to dodge at times.  Movement, attacks, defense felt clunky for me the whole game for the most part.  When you do have NPC assistance, they are pretty bad, and the enemies only focus on you. You are pigeon-holed into the "mechanics" or "puzzle" of figuring out each boss fight.  So, expect to die a few times on several bosses before figuring it out and then managing to survive long enough to finish them off before you die from their mysterious hitboxes.  I'm not against boss fights with boss mechanics, the frustration was more around the player character mechanics feeling inadequate even when you felt like you knew what to do.  The damage can be punishing in some fights.  I like a challenge, and was enjoying myself for the most part, but I was frustrated often toward the end, and was not looking forward to later bosses and definitely not looking forward to replaying on hard mode.  The boxer rat fight is just a bunch of BS.I love all the weapons and equipment to be found and the encouragement to change out gear depending on enemies.  This was a great idea.  I didn't love the gear discovery system here.  You'll spend more than half of the time finding gear that is worse than the gear you got a long time ago.  It takes the fun out a bit when the majority of stuff goes straight into the chest never to be used again.  I think I only ever wore one of the crowns for just a little bit, and I'm a King!  Would have loved a different system here.  Maybe different benefits to different types of gear that allows for different play styles.  Or, let us use resources to improve equipment we like so we can trade gear out without losing benefits (for fashion reasons).  Or, make the weight differences between light, medium and heavy feel more significant.Anyway, other reviews are pretty thorough here.  So, I'll just end saying it is definitely a thumbs up from me even with the issues I didn't love.  I love the heart the devs put into the design/art/music/story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a captivating experience that blends humor, engaging gameplay and a well crafted storyline. What truly sets this game apart is the storytelling. The narrative is outstandingly developed (and narrated <3), and as you progress through the game, you will fnd yourself deeply invested in the fate of the main character and his kingdom. Also a good point goes to the unique art style.Overall I highly reccommend this gem!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good 2D soulslike game. A bit on the easier side, but it actually have a block mechanic that work ( and must be use ) so that's a big plus. And it's not just an abuse of invulnerability frame galore.It is on the very short side. Ended up 100% the achievement in 9.7 hours. I didn't die much, maybe 10 times for the whole game and I kinda explore a lot and did some unnecessary back tracking, so for 25 USD ( without special ), you don't get much. But it's good. Also learn to sheath your weapon, you move way faster.The story is compelling for the style. You actually have one, which is rare for a soulslike. Like you must already know, the narrator is Geralt from the Witcher video games, so that's great.You kinda lack customisation for your character. Yes you have a lot of piece of equipment, but it really doesn't change much. 3 style of weapon pretty much + light/heavy/ranged. I still have no idea what the weight threshold do. Seems to roll the same and move the same, maybe attack speed is a bit slower, still have no idea.It is very story driven, not like a standard soulslike, you have bar instead of numbers, so you don't really have any real of the change you get when you upgrade to a better weapon, except at one point you start killing enemies quite faster.All in all, a very good game if you have like me a Salt and Sanctuary itch.I would probably wait for a big discount to get more for your money, but you will enjoy the time you play with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extraordinary game with great detail put into every aspect of it. The first thing that strikes is, of course, the visuals, which are very unique. The playable environment is 2-dimensional but visually, there is incredible scope to how these places are rendered. The various buildings, vegetation, and NPCs going about their business remind me of flat set pieces like you would see in a stage play, except these go on forever in the distance and create the sense of being immersed in an actual place. This is totally fitting because a lot of what this game is doing is telling a story. The story itself is pretty simple: the evil frog tribes come, mess things up, and the heir-apparent of the victimized rat kingdom must take up his father's sword and rebuild. It's a universal sort of "hero's quest" story, but what makes this instance of it particularly engaging is the pacing of it, which is realized through a very consistent balance of combat, exploration, and narrative exposition. There is arguably a sparseness to the combat compared to what one might expect in other 2-D games. But every encounter is a very deliberate one which the player character is not allowed to avoid. The fights are also not easy. Imagine playing a heavyweight character in a fighting game; you cannot simply slash through everything, moves have to be well-timed and thoughtful. But this isn't to say that the combat is slow. And there's quite a bit of variety to it in terms of dodging, blocking, counter-attacks, secondary vs primary weapons, and projectiles. Additionally, there's all kind of different items you can equip in terms of armor and weapons, that can be bought, found, or forged. In this way, you can give your character different balances of speed versus power, and of course, make him look super cool. The shear amount of gear really surprised me, and I found myself getting excited and backtracking to various places just in case I missed some hidden spear or shield.  But back to the pacing of how and when combat is encountered: because there are not waves of low-tier enemies to scatter on every screen, each fight feels significant. And each fight usually coincides with some revelation by the player character. Such as "I see there is a band of frogs hiding here, I should find and defeat the leader", or "This new skill I just learned will certainly prove useful moving forward". Those are obviously not literal things the character says, but you get the idea. Each fight is meaningful and serves to move the story along. No jumping on goombas three at a time here. The narrative is not simply a dressing which we are reminded of after a boss fight, it is interwoven with the game play throughout the whole thing. To me, this is the shining aspect of the game. You are not simply pressing buttons, you are enacting a story, a story that has stakes, as silly as that might feel considering you're an anthropomorphic rat with a sword.All in all, this game is such a well-balanced experience and an interesting example of what games have the potential to do. I really hope these people make more of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of iron is an awesome game, the combat is punishing and definitely requires strategy but you have enough save points to learn from your mistakes without being too frustrating. And the story is very good, really immersing you in the world and wanting to play more. Not the longest game, but definitely worth the money. Hope they make a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game! But I have one question: who tags this as souls-like? It's just a cool boss rush. I totally disagree with those players who recommend playing on easy difficulty just to find out the story. There is nothing special about it. A plot in this game is just a bonus that adds to the atmosphere. In the second part of Tails of Iron, devs should get rid of the easy mod at all, because it ruins the game!Yes, I also think there are a lot of problems with the combat: it feels like you can't dodge some attacks because of randomness, even if you've got the timing right. If you play on the Bloody Whiskers mod with heavy equipment, it's almost impossible to beat most of the bosses. There is no difference in damage between a simple heavy attack and a heavy attack with hold, and so on.Anyway, I believe that the next game will be better and will include all the best things from the first game. If so, Tails of Iron might become one of my favourites!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming game I just came across! For sure, one of the best I've played this year. For starters, the art is gorgeous, giving you a lush and vibrant world that can look beautiful or bleak at times - you know it's good when you decide to walk slower. Combat is tight and tense, with a good rythm most of the times and the story is really the best part for me: a strong presentation that takes you into a narrative that is great in its simplicity and wonderfully narrated by the White Wolf himself, Doug Cockle, who's up there with the narrator for Darkest Dungeon, Bastion and Disco Elysium. Lastly, the only issues I had with this game, that did not spoil the experience at all, were in a very small number of boss encounters that felt like they had a hitbox that was slightly off and some of the postboard side quests that pop up after you're finished with the storyline - they felt rushed or lazy in comparison. The amount of available weapons and armor also feel a bit scattered and unecessary for my taste, especially if you do pay attention to your surroundings but, again, ultimately do not hinder the game.If you enjoy a charming fable filled with challenging and varied creatures to combat, please do give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Hollow Knight, but with chaos potatoes! Art and style is beautiful, and the combat is better than expected.Side quests are paced well, and they add to the game instead of being too tedious. And I'm in love with the naroator, rat Gerrald, who guides you through like its a grim story book. The first game I've compleded in many years. The structure of the maps are so that you wont miss anything along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start by saying that due to the small map and a lot of backtracking it can get a little repetitive, and once you get the hang of it it isn't to challenging, but... damn if it didn't hook me right away! Most fun I've had in a while. It is short though (100%, 9+ hours), i would wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: i really wanted this to be a good game, because it looks soo good! every screen has wallpaper quality and with the different layers you get a feel of depth wich i really liked!but thats were the pros end for me. the first hour was fun but the further you explore the map, the more you realize that the combat mechanics just dont work! combat on paper is super simple:normal attacks: dodge or blockcharge attacks: dodgestomp attack: double dodgeheavy attack: parryso far so easy. but stomp attacks will hit you almost always even though you double dodge, charge attacks have sometimes such a low window that if you pressed attack before the attack of your foe was telegraphed, it is impossible to dodge. sometimes enemies will chain attack after attack that can kill you instantly especially if there are more than one big enemy. if you are unlucky, they play ping pong with you because there are no invincibility frames. that was so rage inducing for me that i often alt f4 the game. its not just challanging but sometimes just unfair. i finished dark souls 3 and sekiro more than once so i like challanging combat, but this is just bad.some QOL improvements should have been made. if your flask is empty and you are low hp, you have to fill your flask, heal and then fill up you flask again. why not fill health and flask at the same time? but thats just a small detail. dealbreaker for me was the bad combat, no progression and backtracking straight out of hell. you can tell that the developer put a lot of love in this game and thats why it hurts me to not recommend it but it was just no fun in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best "compact" metroidvania-esque experiences, maybe not groundbreaking but definitely one of the best titles in the genre of 2D soulslikes or whatever you want to call it. Up there with Blasphemous, albeit shorter and in my opinion on the easier side of difficulty. Interesting world, Geralt as a narrator and a lot of light-hearted corny humor. Combat feels reactive, requiring good timing, but isn't extremely demanding, although personally i would prefer a little bit of iframes on roll and less focus on positioning, since some of the boss fights feel a little bit of clunky with those small arenas, but that is only a subjective opinion. Finished in about 13-14 hours with all quests/exploration done. Definitely worth it full price, and a no-brainer while discounted.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an awesome metroidvania type game about heroic rats fighting off invading frogs. It's more combat oriented than something like Hollow Knight, and so the combat is proportionally more involved and challenging. It plays really well though and manages a fine balance of being challenging without being super annoying and unfair feeling. What's really great is the attention to detail and the world building. Every backdrop of every stage has multiple layers of stuff going on in it, relevant to the specific quest you're on and how far through the story you are. It's great to see how the kingdom is being restored by your actions little by little, and hints to what enemies and challenges will be coming up. There's just a huge amount of detail and care put into every screen in the game and the rats themselves are extremely cute and charming. I've not finished it yet but I think I'm entering the third (and possibly final?) act of the main story, but I know a big update just happened to add more post-game stuff. There's also some secret side stuff i've found but not yet completed. My one and only complaint so far, apart from wishing there was infinite story, is that the jumping controls have some quirks it takes a while to get used to, but again it's pretty minor and easy to get the hang of, and there is less jumping than in something like hollow knight. 10/10 would help rats defeat frogs and harvest bug juice again
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: A great little indie ARPG! So I heard about this game when it came out and it’s been in the backlog for a while until recently I picked it up. These last few weeks have been very hard for me on a personal level, with my mom being in hospital and her recently passing away. This game, though simple, provided a nice distraction from all the bad and for that I will always be grateful for it. But what is the game all about?The story is pretty simple with you being a prince whose father is killed by some evil Frogs and now you need to rebuild the kingdom and get your revenge. The story was nothing to write home about, but it was enough to keep me going and I felt it had some good moments throughout. While the characters aren’t voiced the game is narrated by actor Doug Cockle, who of course voices Geralt in the Witcher games, and as someone who is a big fan of that series it was a real treat to get his VO here! The man could read the phone book to me and I would be captivated the whole way through!Combat has that souls-like feel of dodging, blocking and parrying but thankfully there are difficulty settings which is great for me since I’m not that into challenging games. The easy difficulty felt good for me in that it was more forgiving but not brain dead easy and I did die a few times to bosses. The combat does feel very good though, with the hits feeling weighty and satisfying to perform and your character will even perform executions on bigger enemies which are fun to see. Alongside that you get a pretty nice variety of weapons and armours to find which always makes completing quests or defeating bosses satisfying since you get that great reward at the end of it.The game can be a bit on the shorter side, but it's a satisfying campaign and you do unlock new side quests after the main story, so it's got a bit of an endgame to get through as well. Overall though, I loved this game and I look forward to the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ trash... hitboxes don't make sense, controls are clunky, there are no iframes for the player but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ENEMIES AND BOSSES get iframes. The audio bugs out constantly forcing you to restart the game to fix it. Damage is inconsistent, half the game mechanics aren't explained anywhere, nearly every boss has a 4-5 hit true combos that will 100 to 0 you no matter what, and worst of all, 100% completion is locked behind the hardest difficulty where these problems are increased ten-fold. This game does not deserve any of the praise it gets. Dark Souls 2 is a better game than this mess.Overall this game gets a 3.5/10. The game is ass, but the graphics are unique and it has an interesting soundtrack. The story is fairly neat so if you must play it, don't bother playing on anything other than the easy mode since the game isn't challenging, it's unfair. If you are a completionist, don't play this game, it is not fun to get 100% in and I'm debating if I even want to finish off the last few achievements I need since I did not enjoy this game enough to care.I said it once and I'll say it again: This game is not Hard, Challenging, or Difficult. This game is Cheap, Unfair, and Frustrating. Your skill means nothing to the game and your success is not determined by your abilities.Update: I decided to grind out the 100% and my opinion still stands. The game sucks ass for most of it. The post game content is a little bit better than the base game but some of the bosses still have the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hitboxes with inconsistent hit detection. With the Bright Fir Forest expansion this game is a 4/10 (0.5 points up from before) which is still bad. This game does not respect your time, it does not respect you as a player and it is not designed to challenge you. This game is designed to kill you and frustrate you. There is nothing fun or enjoyable about that. Ya sure, it only took me 16 hours to get 100%, but that's due to the extremely limited amount of content available. It's also due to the fact that the game is, once again, not hard or challenging. I played the entire thing on Bloody Whiskers and every single fight was either pathetically easy or cheap and unfair. There was no challenge to the game just rolling the dice and hopping for a favourable outcome. Against enemies where 5 out of 6 of their attacks have no openings for counter attacks, you could be waiting for upwards of 2-3 minutes to get a SINGLE attack before going back to waiting around again. And it's not just mindless waiting, you have to be playing near perfectly dodging everything you can just in case the boss decides to chain together a set of moves that is guaranteed to deal some damage to you with nothing you can do about it. And trust me, that will happen in almost every attempt.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game.  Great art, the narrator is fantastic.  Enemies hit very hard and you can die in a few hits, but they have tells and the parry window is generous.  There are frequent checkpoints, so its easy to keep trying the boss until it falls.  If you are used to dark souls like games, the 2-D combat takes some getting used to but it is a very charming and fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron is a great game! I thoroughly enjoyed it from start to end, the story was good, the combat was great and the artstyle was adorable. A great metroidvania game but I have to say it is linear and not focused on exploration, which isn't an issue but I would have loved some exploration to be there so I can come back to this world and play some more. Overall I would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, but a bit short. Was able to play through the whole game and finish everything (minus ) in under 9 hours. Combat was fun to learn, though initially clunky, especially the parry mechanic which I frankly didn't fully pick up until I was on the last area. There are a three types of light/heavy/ranged weapons that all have their inherent pros/cons, i.e. rate of attack, damage output, ect...The art design was amazing/unique, and the world design was interesting in that .The story started off fast and you get caught up initially but there are a few areas where there is no full explanation like . At the end the game left me wondering if this was all it had to give me, with the ending not really all that fulfilling. Catch this one on a sale if you like games like Hollow Knight/Dark Souls.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much that makes me  to like this game. The art is great, the world and story so far are intriguing, and the item system has potential.But the  of this game is just kind of awful. It feels like you're trudging through molasses, everything feels the opposite of fluid, even when prioritizing lightweight gear. This game also suffers from the intense frustration of a lot of...just....walking...back and forth. Side quests that take as long or longer to  than to actually complete once you arrive have been the norm in my playthrough so far. The combat is also quite weak, both from the aforementioned lack of fluidity (which is so paramount for good platformer combat!) and the damage-sponge nature of many, even pretty basic enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: "Tails of Iron" stands out as an engaging action RPG that impresses with its smoothly executed combat system. Unlike many games where frantic button mashing leads to victory, "Tails of Iron" demands a more strategic approach, especially on harder difficulty levels. Each battle is a calculated affair, requiring thoughtful engagement and quick reflexes. This is complemented by a straightforward inventory management system, allowing players to focus on enjoying the game rather than micromanaging items. Keeping gear light enhances agility in combat. Additionally, the game’s narration by Doug Cockle, famous for his role as Geralt in "The Witcher" series, adds an unmistakably charming layer, enriching the experience, especially for fans of the series.However, the game isn't without its quirks. Side quests tend to encourage extensive map exploration, which initially seems rewarding but can lead to time-consuming backtracking as players often need to revisit previously explored areas. Furthermore, while enemies do not constantly respawn, their occasional reappearance requires either re-engagement or strategic avoidance. The game’s duration might also be a drawback for some, as it can be completed within 5-6 hours; despite this, the side quests are well-integrated, offering valuable rewards that justify the required back and forth.Overall, "Tails of Iron" is a delightfully crafted game that combines simple yet deep combat mechanics with an immersive narrative experience. The arena battles introduce a humorous element, with clever nods to various video game icons and sports celebrities, each bringing unique combat styles into the fray. With its balanced mix of action, strategy, and storytelling, "Tails of Iron" is recommended for both seasoned gamers and newcomers alike. Fans should be excited for the upcoming sequel, which promises to build on this solid foundation.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with Redwall you'd have a sudden moment of excitement at the idea that these guys could easily pull off a game that is fitting to the narrative of the book series.  Of course, this game has nothing to do with any of the Redwall books.  And that's fine.At it's core, it's a revenge story.  The bad guys, which are some Frogs, decimate your kingdom.  There's been an ongoing war between the two of your kingdoms so it almost feels like it's the turn of the Rats to be taken down a notch.  But, of course that's a silly notion.  You're the newfound king due to both your father's demise and winning a trial by combat against your brother.  Your job now is to restore your kingdom, and it's a blast.Combat is probably one of the biggest highlights in the game.  There are some questionable hit boxes, and some incredibly frustrating moments in the game where things just don't seem to go your way.  One wrong roll and you're pinned in a corner and subsequently dead.  Sometimes the block/parry combo doesn't work like it's supposed to and that might leave you a bit on the hurt side.  However those moments were all few and far between, minus the last boss battle where I often seemed to be fighting a boss who liked to attack from off-screen.  It's a lot of rolling, blocking, heavy attack and light attack, and some occasional ranged fighting.  Combat is like you'd expect from most games really.  Figure out how  your enemies attack, and then get into the motion of things to combat that.  Enemies are not particularly varied, but the pacing is good enough to where it feels like you're seeing a nice range of them.  Travel is what you'd expect from a game that's Metroidvania like.  You've got a large overall map and you move to different areas with the occasional fast travel.  I wish there'd of been more fast travel to some locations simply because the Side Quests(basically mandatory for gold) would often have me going through areas I'd already visited just to do a quest that was very similar to one I just finished.The environment is great, every area you visit is full of detail and keeps enough variety that each room feels just a bit different from the last.  Enemies look great as well.  If you're a fan of seeing your armor and weapons change based on what you actually have equipped you'll likely be happy with seeing that aspect here.  There are multiple weapons, sword, axe, spear, shields, ranged, and two handed weapons as well.  You also have light, medium, and heavy armors that will all change on your character depending on what you're wearing.Overall you've got a great experience with very satisfying combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice and simple 2D souls-like with gorgeous graphic style, these rats are adorable! Game has a lot of different bosses, some of them gave me a good challenge. To fully complete the game you have to backtrack a little but consider that game is not very long it was ok.Definitely waiting for sequel that was already announced!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Took roughly 17 hours to beat the game but man what a fun ride! Beautiful art direction, beautiful sound design and music, I absolutely adored this world! Very well done, very fun, very entertaining. Whiles some of the fights felt very cheap at times, giving very little room for reaction even when you memorize what each boss ability does, it was still a good kind of challenging. Oh, and oh my gosh the audio and art style in this game are so amazing! I was not a big fan of the whistling noises to represent characters speaking, that was slightly grating, but everything else was truly amazing! The music was great and I still love Jay's little radio and the music it would play when running around with them. The world and theme were great, and it's the kind of world where I just wanted to explore and see more and more and more! Every setting was vibrant and beautiful, thematic music and sound design, interesting storytelling. Fantastic stuff!Would absolutely recommend if you are looking for a good Souls Like Side-Scrolling Platformer and can not way for Tails of Iron 2!Below this contain's spoilers so read more at your own discretion.I think the hardest fight I experienced was either Croakhis Khan or Double Trouble in the Mole Arena for me. They may not have been the most mechanically difficult fights but I think I had the most deaths to them and were some of the more annoying. Double Trouble would have been easier probably had I remembered to switch back to the Mole Arena armor instead of wearing my Frog defense armor still. Croakhis Khan on the other hand, until you get him off his mount, just was not fun in my opinion and even then this game really comes down to "Memorize the Fights and Patterns" and "Play Defensively". Once you learn the patterns and play on the defense you can easily take down most the bosses with only a few having just plain rough to counter moves.Game also has some really strange bugs that didn't ruin it per say but were unfortunate. Often times you would have to switch from 1h to 2h because something would bug out and you wouldn't be able to swing the currently drawn weapon. Graphical bugs like weapons being invisible or the poor Turtle when you get to the frog swamp only existing as a disembodied hand holding a pipe were minor (Probably should patch that one?) Had one bug where I was drinking when I died but revived stuck on a bench in the drinking animation and unable to get off so I had to quit and re-load the save. Just strange stuff.All in all though it's honestly a really charming and great game.I think the only major things I didn't like was the way equipment was handled. Often times I got a piece of armor that is like "Man, that would have been useful to have earlier and now I don't have a chance to make use of it..." like the extra mole armors I got well after fully finishing the Arenas in parts of the post game. I had no idea I would be getting other Mole Defense armors otherwise I would have held off on doing the Arena's until the other content was completed.Lots of stats had no real obvious information. For example, I still have no idea what weight does. Does it affect your dodge roll? I always went for a large amount of armor and enemy resist based on the scenario due to just how nasty some of the mechanics could be so I felt the only way to counter some of them was bulk up. Even then, it's not clear what defense and what resistances even do as there is no visible values like "Reduces Damage by X%" or anything to give an idea of the benefits of focusing general armor or focusing resistance values. A bit more transparency there would have been nice. Same with Weapons given the lack of damage numbers. I usually went for the spears because of their speed but there was no real way to tell if there was that much of a benefit to slower weapons like Axes/Maces over Spears.Some of the attacks also could have been telegraphed better. The training dummy at the start of the game does an AMAZING job at explaining the different attack prompts and what they mean, honestly really well done there! Block White, Parry Yellow, Roll away for red, double roll away for pink... until the line between pink and red becomes so skewed in the actual game that what was taught for those doesn't really matter and Pink and Red basically become "Well, you need to dodge but good luck figuring out what kind of dodge, which direction, etc. to do until after you have seen the animations and learned the fight a bit!" Some times its a simple straight forward attack, some times they rocket half way across the map, some times they home in on you, it's never clear until you have actually seen the moves. So the tutorial's explanation's of Red and Pink quickly become pointless and Red and Pink basically become the same thing, the boss is going to do something unblockable somewhere some way some how.Mind you all of this is super minor nitpicking on my part. Tails of Iron 2 looks even more crazy and fast paced from the trailer, curious to see what has changed in terms of the game feel based on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: A tough yet extremely enjoyable and rewarding metroidvania. Mechanically the game plays similar to Hollow Knight but it's theme, gorgeous artwork and fantastic sound design set it apart from all others in the genre. While Tails of Iron is a tough game, it does a really good job of never making obstacles and enemies feel impossible to overcome - not once did it feel like the game had become a grinding slog. The game get's a high recommendation from me and has left me wanting more 😀
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing that sucked me in to buying this game was the art style. It's so beautiful to see from example gameplay and from small Let's Plays that a few youtubers have done. So I figured I'd get this game for myself if this would stay true from end to finish, which I was pleasantly to find that it was and the world changed as the story progressed so you can tell the devs put a lot of love in to this game.Difficulty? I played on easiest to get through the story and not really the challenge, though there were the odd moments where even I had to drink from my health potion when one of the big bosses really has a strange attack pattern the first time around. Only died once during that playthrough and that's only because of the no-go-zone you'll find in a select area of the map. (Essentially a "you're not meant to be here yet so you better go back before you die. Don't do it! Don't do it! We warned ya. Now you're dead")The voice actor who narrated the game as you progressed was o-kay to listen to, if a bit too gritty on the story telling but when the story really needed that growly nature to it it was 100% deserving. A lot of the happier sequences weren't all too great to listen to with this voice. Keeping in mind, if you're not a fan of the narrator's voice you can turn it off in the options menu.That said, for four hours? It's a decent enough game and I'm glad I only spent £10 on it. A lot of that added time could've been spent getting all the achievements but by this stage I was ready to call it quits. I've completed the game, did a few additional quests but by that point I wasn't really up for going through all of that again. There were a few questions left unaswered but I'm hoping the hint we received means the creators are already making a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I've grown tired of "difficult" games (Hi, Cave Story+!) and occasionally just want to enjoy a good story with quality game play. After restarting the game on easy, I played through it slowly over about a week and really enjoyed quite a few surprises in the story. Nothing in the game is boring or repetitive. Cheers to the developer for making a solid, tight and well done experience.

Also not really worth the 20$ because you only get about 6-8 hours of sadness. The noises the rats make are cute tho.

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly just an OK game.  Simply put, it's a 2D souls-like but not really good or bad.The story is pretty much linear despite having a map that looks like it encourages going off the rails and exploring, and be prepared for a lot of backtracking as every main quest will force you to return to the throne before telling you where to go next without an option to instantly return, so you end up having to run back and forth usually for no reason and with no new quests showing up so it seems the game is artificially being prolonged.  One quirk I didn't like was having a board full of sidequests, but you are only allowed to accept and work on them one at a time, meaning you have to backtrack to the board each time to accept another available sidequest (again, backtracking for the sake of prolonging the game).As for the combat...  I had a lot of issues with it.  I found some enemies having some hidden quick move (with no tells) that knocks you down attached to the end of their combos which inconsistently shows up, so after successfully evading their combo and moving in for a damage phase you'll find the enemy just randomly knocking you down when you're not even in the hitbox and losing your damage phase altogether.  So that just results in you having to wait a second more to prevent these random knockdowns which decreases the number of hits you can get in per damage phase, needlessly prolonging fights.Another thing is that enemies can and will chain stun lock you into a corner with knockdowns, so it gets super frustrating unless you try to stay relatively in the center of the screen.Overall, I still think the game is worth trying out, but more of a game you place in your backlog for a rainy day.

_childDocuments_.review: Tails of Iron has it's moments for those who enjoy challenging combat, indie art and dark settings. It's a bit like Salt and Sanctuary meets Red Wall. While enjoyed the combat mechanics and over arching story, the game falls a bit short with the questing mechanics. Rather than playing directly into the plot the quest delivery format feels more like fetch quests that have you retreading the same few zones over and over. If you could pick up a few quests at once this could be greatly improved, even better would be integrating the quests in as part of the story and not a bulletin board quest grab. That said there is a lot more good than bad here, particularly the weapon and armor variety. I'm a sucker for equipment changes reflected on your avatar. For people who like a mix of  soulslike and metroidvania this will do. But I'd recommend grabbing it after you finish Ender Lillies and Vigil.  Overall its a unique take on the genre and solid way to keel 15 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game is great. It has a lovely artstyle and the game design is basically entertaining. I'd really want to like it.BUTIt is hardly fun. _childDocuments_.review: I loved this game.  Art style is amazing, I felt it was oozing with charm, and it was obviously made with love.  Took me about 12 hours, but i played on the hardest difficulty.  Be warned, the enemies are definitely more aggressive and also move quicker than lower difficulties, which made some later fights feel unfair.  Combat is fairly simple relying on color-coded attacks, and there are no i-frames when dodging, so positioning is extremely important.  Overall I enjoyed it, I'd probably pick it up on sale since I think $25 is a bit steep for how short it'll be for most people.  Plus Geralt narrates so what more do you need?
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is extremely compelling. It's challenging enough to be satisfying when you finish a fight but not so difficult as to be frustrating. Most of the tougher bosses only took me 2 or 3 tries to beat on Normal difficulty. The only criticisms of the combat I have are that each sub-class within each class of weapon (one-handed, two-handed and ranged) all feel the same. Swords vs axes vs spears, bows vs crossbows etc, you just pick whichever has the best stats because there's very little difference between them otherwise. Two-handed weapons also seemed almost completely useless outside of breaking the guard of shielded enemies, and even then most of those don't keep their shields up all the time anyway and by the time you've very slowly charged your shield break attack, the enemy has probably already hit you. Those are minor quibbles though. The combat is fun, the art is a great mix of cute and grim, the story is a standard revenge tale but those are almost always compelling and that's certainly true here. I finished the 10-hour main story within a day of purchase. Definite thumbs up from me.One last caveat: there are some slight tones of racism in there - certainly understandable that the protagonist would hate the frogs that did all that stuff, but the script definitely has him hating all of frog-kind, particularly repeating about how they smell. It didn't bother me too much but I did find it a bit on the nose (no pun intended).
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 20+ hours to fully clear standard difficulty and beating the last story boss in bloody whiskers mode you should definitely play this game and here is why...Combat is brutal, skill based, and extremely satisfying. Seamlessly alternate between your one hand, two hand, and ranged weapons. Gear and enemy scaling is on point in the early to middle game. You can feel the impact of new weapons and armor and the enemies scale up in difficulty as you get stronger. Their new mechanics punish mistakes like improper positioning or blocking instead of dodging. First of all the narration is on point, it sounds like the Witcher is performing some of the dialogue. Add in the great art, music, and just enough story to make it feel like you are on an adventure. I won't lie some of the songs in the game made me just stand still so I could enjoy an entire song from start to finish!A solid variety of weapons and armor where you can feel the differences in armor resistance, weight management, and weapon types. And not only can you feel the differences, but you can SEE them! I felt like a boss when my character resembled a rat samurai with a bone mask and katana!A very good variety of major and minor bosses, with unique skills and mechanics that reward you for proper positioning, and fully utilizing the appropriate attack windows without getting too greedy. Most of the bosses on standard difficulty don't pose much of a challenge but allow you to enjoy and explore the game. If you want that souls like genre boss battle experience that might take 10, 20, 30 or more tries to fully learn each phase then bloody whisker mode is for you. Certain bosses which I won't name took me 30 minutes to an hour to best.The only minor negative comment I have relates to the end game. Once the story is over, gear really stops having any major impact and turns into just a cosmetic. Also, some of those boss mechanics are reused and it feels repetitive running to areas you have already been to multiple times over just to fight another boss clone.All in all this was an extremely well made and enjoyable game I would recommend to anyone full price or on sale. Tales of Iron 2 is definitely on my wishlist, and should be on yours too!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: played this and tried to like it ... but the game made it impossible.It really looks gorgeous and Doug's the voice acting (Geralt of Rivia) is really good...so what are the problems?Combat & movement!There are so many issues here, so let's start simple:- When you jump, you lose all your momentum, so jumping is incredibly undesired as a movement option since it stops the flow of movement.- When you start to move in any direction, there is a ~0,1-second delay before your character starts moving... why?- In combat, you have three options to deal with an attack, which is indicated with a colored icon above the enemies head: block, dodge or parry (shield charge). Every enemy has red (dodge), yellow (parry) or white (block) attacks. The first issue I encountered was that some enemies do not show any indicators when they attack. They just do a white attack but do not indicate so. So you have to know what it looks like when an enemy prepares an attack and block it. Bosses also have multiple red attacks, and since you have no iframes (dodging only makes you move faster), you have to know which attack it is. As an example, the first boss you fight is a giant toad that can either do a lead in the direction it is looking or jump up and land on the same spot. One requires you do doge through the boss before the attack, and the other requires you dodge away from the boss. If you get this wrong, you take a big chunk of damage. Which attack it is, is often not telegraphed well as its movements look very similar.- Building on the previous point, the problem with the game is also that it feels extremely repetitive since it uses its colored (especially red) attacks constantly! You are more focused on the icon popping up than on the actual movements of the enemy. Games like SEKIRO have the same mechanic, but it's sparingly used in comparison, since the intention is for you to look at the enemy, not the symbol. Here I felt like doing a paint by number game, as in some fights I had enemies spam their colored attacks in a row.- Enemies are reused and spammed at you. When a fight starts, the area you can move in is limited and enemies usually come in from the sides. Once you kill one, another comes in. Usually you will fight 2 maybe 3 at the same time. It's extreme annoying when you have to kill wave after wave of enemies. This is especially the case when you have enemies that can block or dodge roll around and evade your attacks... fights then drag on even more so since you cannot just spam attacks as enemies can then start a counter attack, which of course is not indicated. So you do X attacks and see how many you can land before the enemy strikes back and have to learn the timings.- (intended difficulty) Difficulty is all over the place .... some bosses are so easy that you can defeat them on the first try while starting with half health, others might need a few tries. None of that seems balanced, every fight is like a dice role. There is no progression of complexity or mechanics. - Hitboxes are wonky: Some of the attacks land when you are standing far away from the enemy when it lands. A good example is the vertical leap of bosses. They jump up and land on the same spot. The hitbox for that is larger than it visually indicates.- My worst gripe: EVERYTHING is a proverbial bullet sponge! Even if you spam heavy attacks, you need 10 hits to kill a regular mob?! Bosses are even worse, it feels like the only reason anything is this game is remotely difficult is because you need to hit it so often, that you get annoyed. And the worst part is that you cannot do anything about it. You cannot upgrade your weapon or find weapons that are especially effective against certain types. You cannot buff your weapon (except for applying poison, which feels barely noticeable). - Gear is also a pain. You have a quick melee weapon and a string melee weapon and a ranged weapon. The weapons only distinguish themselves by weight and damage. The more the weight, the slower you move and dodge. While the game offers a solid amount of weapons, those are meaningless since none of them have defining characteristics. You probably can find over 20 spears, but they all are just variations of damage and weight. There is nothing special about them, no lore to read, nothing. They are visually different, though. For me, that is meaningless, and I would argue that fewer weapons with more defining characteristics would have been a) more rewarding to find them and b) allow for more significant choices when it comes to selecting a weapon. The same goes for armor, though here you can have special resist stats (e.g. against Frogs -the main enemy of the story), so here at least you have a little to consider and can use different armors to adapt to enemies you will fight. The world, quests & travel!- There are side quests ... 99% seem none optional except for the ones that can be repeated.- The quests send you to the same spots AGAIN and AGAIN! "Kill insects in the sewers", "Kill mosquitos in the sewers", "kill another insect infestation in the sewers". You cannot accept all quests at once, you HAVE to do all of them in sequence... This feels like doing dailies in an MMO!Dialogues!- They are not skippable and are really slow. _childDocuments_.review: Edit:So they added a bit of content; 5 new bosses and some skins. Took me ½ hour, tops, to beat them all and then that was it. Granted, it was free extra content, so I can't complain too much....But! Why not make the new skins lootable? The whole point of this game is progression; once you have everything, nothing has value anymore 'cause there's no reason to put it to use. Why not reward me for beating each new trial with some new loot? Then I could choose what to bring to the 5'th boss, that would've felt alot better..What an adorable cute title this is!So when you see the promo material, you can actually expect the game to match this. It's a Souls-like, as they say, it's comparable to Hollow Knight in some ways but instead of the platforming focus, it's more about the Dark Souls-ish combat; dodge/parry/block at the right times. The universe is very cute, the sound design is great, yada-yada, but what I want to emphasize is how this game also mechanically, really comes off as a kids game, and here's why:- Combat: I've seen reviews here mention how there's no handholding and the combat is very (too?) difficult and then someone mentioning how the color symbols, relating to dodge/parry/blocking really pulls the difficulty down. I agree with the latter. I don't consider myself gud or pro, but this game is sooo accessible combat-wise. Not that you can't make mistakes or get too cocky and die for it, but you get delivered all the dance moves right away and it's just up to you to utilize them. Using a controller, there's nothing complicated to it.- Death penalty: There are no "souls" to collect and loose upon death. You have one flask to heal from and half the monsters provide refill when looted AND there's kegs of juice, ad libitum, scattered all over the map. When you respawn from death, it's full and all you loose is progress, which is very little due to the abundance of "rest benches" on top. No long boss runs either.- Resources and loot: roughly said, you get what you need, just as you need it, both in terms of upgrades and new types of gear, as well as quest items and general resources. There's two types of currencies and you can trade between them, 5 for 2, and I've never had to farm any of them. In fact, the only managing I'm doing is trying to spend it on blueprints (which you can exhaust from the trader) and the odd purchased quest item from the store, so I don't sit at the 99 cap, when going on the next side quest. And there's just so much convenience baked into when you need this type of food or that construction material to progress the stage you're at, so you don't have to figure out where to find it - you stumble right into it, when you follow the natural order of quests. Regarding gear, you keep getting so much stuff all the time, that you don't really have to think about how/when to upgrade yourself, beyond the choice of how heavy you wanna be and managing the defense types before going against a particular category of enemy. I mean, unless you really care about the skins, that's it. So far, the blueprint slot-machine is just a resource-dump, with a 1/8 chance of a minor upgrade - if only I could buy unlimited BP's! - Map and exploring: Compared to Hollow Knight, the map is very, very small. There's like 4 locations to fast travel between and the quests keep using the same buildings or sewer spots, just with new bosses. The only lost I'm getting is trying to find the cowscrub for more milk xD There's no complex wandering around, hoping to locate some key-fragment to unlock the next are or finding the thing for the guy to trade for the other thing for the other guy, Zelda-style. There's a few locations where, if you're the minimum of curious, you check them out to find something, you don't even need yet and thus the game kinda feels super linear to progress through. My point with all of this is; I can't figure out if the game is almost too easy, or if I'm just used to being thrown all around the game world and having to farm and manage everything, though it's often actually such a hassle - and in reality, an artificial extension of content! This game is a relief to me, usually getting exhausted clearing ?-marks off the map in Witcher3, locating quest-relevant NPC's and wondering if I even need to loot everything, when I never craft in DOS2 and other examples.. Sometimes those games are just too big, you know? (Am I getting old?) ....but I feel like this game is so manageable, there's maybe something missing? Or should I have been 8 years old to match the complexity level better? In either case, I really enjoy it and I keep imagining Geralt is reading a bedtime story for the kid, he'll never have, or he's looking at some toads and rats while meditating and this is what goes though his head^^....might be a tad overpriced, depending on what Doug Cockle would cost for a narrator-job. But bear in mid, I haven't completed it yet, so it could still explode on me with another map to progress through and more complex items - who knows!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. There is a nice charm to Tails of Iron. From the art style, to the characters, the music and the wonderful narration; you can tell a lot of love went into this game. The premise is straight forward. Your kingdom is being overrun by nasty Frog-folk and as the newly crowned King, you must defend it. This means setting off on a grand adventure that takes through farm lands, underground tunnels, mines, and a few other surprising places I'd rather not spoil. There's a few adventure game tropes here in terms of locations and a few that break the mole to deliver a nice change of pace. The great art style does a lot to bring these places and characters to life too. As simple as it is, my main draw to keep playing was the story and seeing where our Hero ends up next. Your adventure is wonderfully narrated by none other than the voice of Geralt of Rivia, Doug Cockle and the whole game feels like you're unraveling a storybook. A violent story book, because combat can get very bloody, with over the top kill animations and the plot alludes to a lot of sinister things. If you had to compare, Tails of Iron is less Hollow Knight and more Salt and sanctuary in terms of gameplay, but with a focus on narrative.Combat is challenging, but never frustrating. The bad guys telegraph their attacks with visual ques, letting you know when to block, dodge or roll out of the way and failure to do the right move is very punishing. Once you get the hang of it though, there's a ice flow to the combat that I loved till the end. Boss fights crank this up to 11 and again, some fights can be difficult or tricky, but I never felt that any of them were unfair. Weapons come in a few flavors, such as axes, swords and hammers, offering different swing speeds and animations, but I often just went with whatever had the better damage stats. They don't really change much in play style. Armor sets give better defense the better quality armor you pick up and some offer resistance to specific baddy types, so you'll end up switching these out for certain fights a lot. I am also a huge fan of things like Mouse Guard and Redwall, so that added another layer of enjoyment to Tails of Iron for me.All in all, I think Tails of Iron is a great game that I highly recommend to anyone who's up to a fun, but challenging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: a really nice game, It is a salt and santiary / deamon souls / exploration 2d game, the difficulty is not super  hard but hard enought to be enjoyable.I dont enjoy the deamond souls like games, i think they are not well designed in terms of difficulty, there is a moment when those games becomes a chore more than a game, but this game gets the difficulty in the right amount. the exploration is little/medium but very enjoyable, the setting is very nice and while you advance in the game you can notice how the world around you evolve which is a very nice touch. the voice of the  narrator is excelent, animations are great, the style of the enemies and characters is good, well, long history short, it is a good game. even if you dont like deamonds souls game, give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, Tails of Iron just isn't fun. Gameplay revolves entirely around combat and combat is clunky and irrational. Parries only work if you press the button nearly half a second before the attack. Some attacks are telegraphed with the colored red/yellow indicators (indicating that you should dodge/parry), and others aren't, with no discernable rhyme or reason as to why. Dodging doesn't appear to have invincibility frames, so it's not actually about timing them, it's purely about avoiding the attack, and totally possible to dodge through/into the attacks area of effect, taking the full hit. It all feels very unsatisfying and arbitrary. And that's it. That's combat. Attacking, dodging, blocking (arrows exclusively), and parrying. It's extremely basic. Three of your actions are defensive, and poorly implemented. Attacking is a simple combo string followed by a delay. That's it. Skill and choices don't exist here. It's just all so mindless.Progression is standard gear collection, but without any meaningful depth. Every decision is just damage/defence vs weight, and honestly there's nothing interesting to it and never ever a reason to not always choose the higher damage/defence item. Worse, the "upgrades" all feel incredibly incidental and nothing feels satisfying. I quickly stopped caring about new gear, and after that, nothing else matters. It's just stuff that you pick up because it's there. Refunded

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all-time, period.  Bloody Whisker difficulty was perfectly balanced and fair, which is very important for a soulslike.  The parry system is brilliant.  I usually don't like parrying in soulslikes, but it's satisfying and rewarding here.  I like how there's a short window to hold the parry, yet it's not OP feeling.  Excellent variety of armor, weapons, grunt enemies, and bosses.  Not one boss fight was too easy nor too hard on the max difficulty, which I applaud the devs for.  It's hard to fine tune a game's difficulty that precisely and meticulously.  Your character's movement is very well designed and never a hindrance.  I like how you gain a slight speed boost when sheathing your weapon.  Once you master the movement you'll feel like a little ninja.  Excellent sound design, art design, PC performance (no stutter or frame pacing issues), etc. Will buy the sequel on day one.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails of Iron

_childDocuments_.review: Such a nice game. The gameplay borrows the best aspects from other Souls-/Metroidlikes that have been sprouting everywhere during the last years. The atmosphere is phantastic and the gloomy-catoony world design is top notch. Combat is fluid and progression paths are quite well-telegraphed.BUT, the game also has some noticeable downsides: In my opionion, there was too much backtracking, which made the world feel smaller than it should've felt. Going back to places you have already visited for bounty hunting, which rewards you with currency that unlocks new paths is just a lazy concept that stretches playtime unnecessarily. Also, the difficulty curve (apart from the endgame arena and some good bossfights) is quite weird. The game becomes very easy in the second half when you will have mastered and found new gear. Furthermore, there are currently 6 new achievements in the game for content that can't be played yet. This is misleading, don't bother trying to 100% this game but save your time for a hard mode run when the free expansion is released or get the game at some later date.All in all, I still had a blast playing this and would rate this a very solid 7/10.
