_childDocuments_.review: Great game with big potential but needs A LOT of "polishing"It is very similar to Subnautica but in space enviroment without enemies. Open world survival craft fans will love itPros:- The terraforming mechanic is a great addition to the genre and makes this game unique. You start at a martian desert and you end up in a green planet with lakes and trees.- Great pace with little grinding- The unlock tree is well made with many upgrades and quick unlocks to keep it interesting- Not really challenging which is great for me (full-time job and kids). Some might find it bad though.Cons:- The graphics need a lot of work. The lighting is terrible, the terrain feels poorly made and the textures are too simple. You get the feeling that the game was released 10 years ago- There are no transport means expect a jet pack which just hovers above ground and gives you a speed boost. There is no way to transport cargo long distance so you have to build many small outposts with crafting stations to make up for it.- The resources could be harvested a different way other than laying down on the ground one by one. There could be bigger rocks you could harvest that give you multiple amounts of a resouce and be scattered more far apart.- Small map but with no way of navigating other than a compass. You are able to send a really expensive gps rocket to space but all it does is give you a small map of the area around a screen you have to build and place on the ground. No way open a portable map.

_childDocuments_.review: An early access indie game which is surprisingly polished.  It is a first person game that doesn't have aliens or zombies to kill which may disappoint some people.  The game is about you landing on a planet with very little and having a mission to terraform it.   Its all about crafting, exploration, researching, gathering, base building and watching you planet develop. There is also some resource management involved (food, water. oxygen).  No gruesome deaths, but should you run out oxygen you will respawn at your original drop pod having dropped a few items. I don't know how much replay value it will have once you have finished it (until it is updated) but I have 10 hours on the game already so definitely worth the money. There is something satisfying watching your barren planet turning into a green oasis.  I recommend you try the free demo as it gives a generous amount of gameplay to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this ONLY on Hardcore, and having "beat" the game, I can for sure tell you that the level of challenge, the "grind" and the amount of things to do are extremely well balanced. I'm excited to see where they head with this. In it's current state, there is ample to give you your money's worth and there will definitely be good replayability once there are more aspects to the game.A few things I would like to see features wise:1) Bigger map2) More lore (flesh out the back story etc)3) Fishing (every great game has fishing)4) More base functionality (water production inside the base, usable furniture etc)5) A carryable map that starts blank and reveals as you travel.6) Instead of "Super Alloy" consisting of all the commons, make it harder to manufacture by introducing more rare elements that need to be mined for that purpose only. That would eliminate the mining of an "alloy"I thoroughly thoroughly enjoyed playing through this. Of course being on Hardcore only meant I had to restart several times. If I had to guess, it was nearly 10 or 15 times before I found what worked. This was never a deal breaker however because I never had a death that wasn't my own damn fault (dying to some ridiculous mechanic or getting "stuck" would have been enraging) Please devs, for the love of all that's holy! Do NOT make hardcore mode easier. Make a care bear setting for those who wish to experience the game devoid of challenge, but for those of us who love to "beat a game" this is just about perfect in terms of challenge/reward ratio.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like numbers going up? Do you like stockpiling dozens of chests of a single resource? Do you like the idea of hardcore drugs but think they're too expensive? Then Planet Crafter is the game for you!At first you will want just a little more food, water, and oxygen to refill the constantly depleting survival meters but very soon you will solve that problem only to realize you are just a few hours into your shiny new scifi addiction. You will dash around snatching up every ore you can find lying around literally everywhere, sometimes coming across dopamine in a box aka chests. These chests will dangle goodies in front of you like seeds for your garden or flowers for your oxygen producers. Did I forget to mention you are an interstellar convict whose sentence will be commuted once you completely terraform a planet and watch it's ecosystem come to life before your very eyes? The Terraformation Index, helpfully abbreviated to TI in the UI so your brain can focus on finding just one more uranium to build another nuclear reactor which will seemlessly power your ever expanding terraformation operation.Anyway, back to the flowers. So you use flowers to produce more oxygen while using food seeds to make snacks to keep you alive while exploring this gloriously desolate yet nubile wasteland. All the while your drills will increase pressure and your heaters will, get this, increase heat. I know, an amazing concept. As the TI goes up so does the cost for the next level which means you need T2 then T3 and then T4 of everything to keep advancing. Discover brand new resource types and blueprints scattered around the world before you launch rockets into space to help you map out this now gargantuan play area. Seed life in the freshly melted lakes then mutate that life to serve your own needs. Drive a truck to add additional storage capacity to your inventory as you frantically trek from outpost to outpost looking for more and more stuff. And partake in every homosapiens' favorite past time, exploding natural rock formations to lay claim to the resources the soil dared to hide from you. TLDR: It's Satisfactory without the math getting in the way. HOOK. IT. TO. MY. VEINS!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. It's a bit of a struggle at first, but once you get going and problems like food, water, oxygen and energy are less of / no longer a problem exploration gets real fun and the further the planet terraforms the more beautiful it gets.The exploration of procedural wrecks can be a bit of a pain sometimes since there is no map to help you navigate. Since my sense of direction is pretty bad, I sometimes died of hunger / thirst because I got lost and couldn't find the exit in time. :)There are some minor bugs, like sometimes the rain falls through the roof of my base and I don't always like the way building elements connect to each other. Also rockets for gps and other uses.I am having a really good time Planet Crafter. Kudos to the developers
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I'm taking crazy pills after how good the reviews are for this game. I felt like I was fighting the inventory and short oxygen timer more than enjoying the game. I'm sent on a mission to terraform a planet, but my oxygen tank doesn't even last a minute out of the gate?- You're going to need to bring extra oxygen tanks to top yourself off for the first few hours when you want to go outside for more than a minute or two.- Items/materials do not stack. Everything from a plant seed to large crafted items take 1 inventory slot. This makes having to carry multiple oxygen tanks even more punishing.- When you build something (say, a part for a base), it exits crafting mode so you cannot make multiple without reopening the crafting menu and selected the part again.Maybe it gets way better later on, but I ran into so many annoyances in the first hour that seemed like systemic design issues, I lost interest.Overall, the game design didn't feel like it learned from the quality-of-life improvements that have been standardized by other modern survival games.

_childDocuments_.review: 0. Disclaimer:Most modern titles are vast as an ocean and deep as a puddle. This one is vice versa and definitely deserves your money and attention. Do not hesitate to buy it. Some day it will stand among the giants of interactive worlds like 7D2D and TLD, probably.Not today. Today this game has met a sophisticated player.1. At first you criticize this technical demo of a game for:— Pushing out a DLC before polishing out the initial product.Features-first Google approach has always been an epitome to the commercialization of entertainment. Meanwhile video games are art (sic!) above anything else, and imperfections which break the Player’s immersion are nearly unacceptable, now and forever.Low budget, humble team size or Early Access badge are not an excuse for the lack of quality, thorough game mechanics design, sanity checks, or extensive usability testing.— Poor clipping.There are plenty of places on the Prime map where your character floats above ground with no actual feeling of traversing the terrain, while camera clips through it. And although the invisible walls can be justified at map borders; having those in the middle of the map, especially in a game where you can literally build a stairway to heaven with zero regards to physics or common sense, — are mildly irritating, even though you do get the dungeon master’s incentive to limit your shortcuts.— W-syndrome.Long time ago Hinterland gave up to the community demands of introducing a toggled auto-walk button. Constant middle-finger spasm on the W-key is pretty common among first-person action gamers, and the Planet Crafter is no exception. In fact here it pushes the problem to a new level: you prefer NOT having a mining speed upgrade chip installed because it invokes minimal gameplay relevance, but secures a much needed rest for your left hand. Tool distance upgrade would have been a much more relevant option indeed, reducing the excessive movement of the Player. How come this hasn’t been resolved yet with built-in game feedback feature, eludes me.Same goes for shift-running. Auto-run outside and auto-switch to walking indoors would do the trick, but toggled shift would have worked even better.— Partial SFX.Game has only three types of footsteps: over metal, wood, and common. There are entirely no walking sounds in some areas (and no flying too for no apparent reason), and limited variability of existing ones eventually end up quite stale, especially the common ones. Doesn’t matter if you traverse snow, sand or stone, they are one and the same. Footprints are also above this game menu.— Lack of effects.Be it a sandstorm, rain or whatever, there are no environmental visor effects, and therefore you can’t help but feel you’re not actually a character in a dire situation, but simply a controllable movie camera. On top of this — such impression is also enforced by barely animated hands. I bet everyone smiles sadly when they see how protagonist lovingly dusts his multi-tool every once in a while.Moreover weather impact on your activities is utter zero, except for the meteor shower which brings in free resources. You don’t even need the compass not to get lost in a fog with all the beacons. And there’s no point in weathering the storm in a shelter, since it is of no danger; just go around your business like an iron man.— Physics.Or the lack of it to be precise. Believe it or not you actually fall faster on slopes and in water!Unless you intentionally go full-in on aesthetics as a rule — your builds end up cluttered with all parts overlapping each other at no sanity or repercussion. Solar panels will work just fine underground, interlaced wind turbines will perform perfectly, everything’s cool under any angle, and both weather and object placement has zero effect whatsoever. You can literally build anyhow anywhere, it just works, and is connected by ether. Power lines? Never heard of’em.In fact, the more you think of it, the more ludicrous it becomes. A couple of indoor heat generators and a few gas drills break the camel’s back on a planet that has open lava pools? Snow plains near the desert? Everything goes.— PEGI rating. It’s 18 in case you had no idea.The pretext of a male convict doing his sentence of terraforming a planet for an unspeakable transgression, doing weird dances each time he puts on a new space suit, is quite telling. He can die of hunger, thirst, suffocation and fall fractures. Some really ♥♥♥♥♥♥-up psychological ♥♥♥♥ can be found in the logs of hidden bunkers and spaceship debris. There’s even a cemetery of almost a full crew in one of the caves. And I can’t help but wonder why oh why this severe foundation was not built upon. Instead of dismembered corpses, frozen in ice, littering the trap-planet, and telling a story, you get a Disneyland vacation music and a cartoon palette. Yay!How about we progress from the existential dread to a loony toon instead of mixing it together from the very beginning?2. Then you start to kinda like it:— Once you dig a bit into the game, settle-in and understand what it is and is not by all measure, you decide to give it a chance.After all it respects your time by not making you hold your left mouse button or die of old age while you gather the resources like in No Man Sky, right? I mean you still doubt the game design decision to allow building structures without foundations, and can’t understand why containers need them, while living compartments absolutely do not. But you start getting somewhere.— Custom settings are always a fine choice.On my first run I’ve set both my vitals drain, weather and terraformation speed to 0.3 to compensate for difficulty, and began to actually enjoy the exploration. Without an impression I have to hold my breath in a jerrycan every time I go outside — the underground mushroom river, the crater, the moonlit veins field, the innards of space ships became a reflective sightseeing experience.Letting players do their thing is always awesome, but more settings are definitely on demand.— Although some stuff still made no sense.Why running does not double your vitals drain? Why dehydration causes your sight go blank and die outright instead of gradually draining health? Who needs a bed? That kind of stuff, insomnia induced no doubt.3. Then you begin to enjoy it:— Immediately when you build yourself a basic jetpack.I mean your left hand still hurts from no auto-walk key, but holding space instead of shift helps. Using it first time — really felt like reality. You jump, and then you thrust. Huh, this will never get old! Now the terrain turned out to be passable, walking sounds no longer get on your nerves, and going down a cliff no longer a cringe. Now that’s how it’s actually supposed to be played, huh?!Cool stuff.4. Finally you are astonished by it:— First Biodome and then Biolab finally show you what’s in store.Woah, this game is huge! Unlike the map it’s played upon. The environment starts to change, and if you keep the terraformation speed low enough, every aspects unfolds like a charm: puddles, lakes, rivers, waterfalls... Melting ice opens hidden caverns making re-exploration viable. Satellites turn out to be a disappointment, but you start building bases in breathtaking places to watch it all evolve...5. And then you make a rover...Wait, wat?Blueprint progression, darling.Clunky, bulky, slow, constantly stucking 3rd-person viewed vehicle with inventory that brings minimal advantage in comparison to the blazing exosuit capable of crossing the map in 5 minutes?No thanks.Air is not a problem anywhere, since you can build micro-bases, like, every ten paces. It’s not Subnautica for it to be ever feasible.I’ve bought Planet Humble, to support the devs if nothing else, and tried it too.But I will hold on for a year or so before getting back to this game.Let’s hope it terraforms.

_childDocuments_.review: As you might be able to tell with over 200 hours,  this game had me hooked.  First thing to remember is this is early access and not complete yet, but still playable for what has been developed so far.    Some of the cons is it is not procedurally generated and A LOT of the things in it (wrecks, chests etc) are in the exact same place every start up. I really hope that changes.  Although the random start areas does help with that a little.   That said there is a lot of pros to the game.   I was reading a negative review in the game and it is obvious the reviewer didn't play very long.  Yes  there are materials scattered all over the place, and yet there will still be times when your scrambling for a certain type of material later in the game.  Yes the start up gear is very limited, but expands as you either find blue prints or get further into the terraforming of the planet.  Some of the background of the story starts to come out in messages left on various view screens found in the wrecks you come across.  Although I do agree a cut screen or something explaining, why you are sent there would be nice. There are also hidden challenges that are hinted at through messages that you receive that if you don't figure out, you will find yourself in scramble mode to prevent a disaster to your base.    I've found it quite enjoyable seeing the changes in the planet it's self occurring, based solely on the actions I've taken.   I've played MANY survival games and this is the first I've played where my actions actually affect the world it's self.   It is enjoyable,  relaxing and  involved.  Be warned time does seem to run away while you do just one more thing.   I'm looking forward to seeing the next step in the terraforming take place.   In short if you like building something, don't mind a grind (there are times where it seems nothing but), enjoy exploration and figuring out how you can get just a little further, then you will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing resource and building game. There are a few very minor bugs, like picking up a water bottle if it was dropped on the ground seems to be really picky about how you're pointing at it. But wow... I love this game!First of all, there have been reviews mentioning that this is a lot like Subnautica. I agree. However, your goals and everything you need to do to get there is completely different. Different story, different items, different everything. But, if you played Subnautica, you'll no doubt have that same feeling we all did. It reminds you of that game. The music is very similar and a lot of the mechanics are similar as well.This game is very relaxing to play. You can leave it running and walk away to do something else and come back to it. While you were away, things will have happened, furthering your progress. Yes, it takes a bit of patience unless you use cheats. But I love that. There is something about the accomplishments after you worked and waited for enough oxygen, heat, or pressure in the atmosphere so you can unlock that next piece of technology that will speed everything up. The further you get into it... the more new tech you can build and the faster you turn the planet around into something able to sustain life. As it stands right now, there is a TON of content already. So don't let the early-access fool you. It will keep you busy for quite a while. I honestly can't wait to see what else they add to this game, but the possibilities are endless here.Things I'd like to see added:  1 - I would love it when you're building something like grass spreaders to make it so you don't have to keep opening the build menu. If I want to build 5, I'd rather go select it, then build all 5 where I want them. Maybe a toggle to turn on/off the build function. 2 - Upgradeable flashlight - make the beam wider at next levels. That initial light is so small you literally have to turn 90 degrees at every corridor to make sure you're not passing up an opening (this is in regard to exploring crashed ships). 3 - A crashed ship that actually powers up when you load in the fusion cell. I saw that once I was able to fuel a reactor, a few doors opened in the ship. That was cool! But maybe add another ship or 2 that actually powers up - lights, functioning doors, etc... opening up endless possibilities for more story and maybe even other rare items or technology you can use. 4 - Water-tight buildings you can place under water! 5 - Some kind of flying transportation you can build. 6 - Life - fish, small animals, etc... Would be cool to see fish evolving. Would prefer not to have raging animals that kill... or the option to turn them off because part of the magic in this game is the peacefulness. 7 - More weather patterns, perhaps even seasons if that is possible. Maybe an added survival point for cold. 8 - Better foundations (and more of them). The metal frame thing is neat for the beginning... but would love to see more. 9 - More building options like wooden houses or more technical housing as well, concrete, etc... 10 - More inventory space upgrades. This sucker should get to T10 or even more, with the inventory list scrollable. 11 - Better map of the area... the current map is just a still and you can't really move around on it. Also, after adding the T2 satellite, I didn't really notice a big difference. Not sure the purpose of the map at this point other than to get a general idea of your trees, grass, and water coverage. Would be nice to be able to move the map around, zoom in or out, etc.I'm sure I'll think of other things, but keep up the good work on this wonderful gem. Definitely worth the money. *****

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. If you like Subnautica, this is like a more laid back version. Being that this is in early access, naturally there are some flaws that might be obnoxious to you. Building needs some work, currently you can just place things literally in the sky, as well as there being no collision with the ground but there is collision with the boulders that are jumbled everywhere, which is very weird. There is also no way to get rid of these rocks and it's kind of crap to have to build around them, especially if you like having a neat/organized base layout. Plus the game does give you explosive powder, but nothing to actually explode with it. I'm assuming this will be fixed or remedied somehow in the future!Another thing with building, you'll see that you have an invalid placement, but there will be no additional feedback on why that is happening. Ground not flat enough? Rock in the way? Other building in the way? Who knows! That is also a bit obnoxious, and also weird since individual building parts have no collision with the ground when placed (unattached to existing buildings) but when you want to attach them suddenly there is an issue. Overall it's good, but quirky at this time. There are other collision issues, mainly when it come to you yourself and clipping in the world. Definitely needs polish there, but not really thaaaaat game breaking. Lastly be prepared for storage issues, it will feel like you need a warehouse to hold all your materials. There feels like there's some balancing issues to be dialed in here imo, especially late game. The good news is that this is very playable and entertaining for an early access game and I'm excited for what's in store for us as the game continues to develop!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a "meh" review. There are some really neat ideas in this game, and I generally enjoyed the early game exploring, but holy crap, does this ever become a "watch the numbers go up" grindfest to get to the end of it. I got an ending - I suspect there are multiple - after 67 hours, and I would say I enjoyed about half to 2/3 of those hours. I could have done some things more efficiently throughout to speed up progress, but whatever. This is a game that's trying to dip its toes in the Satisfactory/Factorio water, but it's absolutely not one of those, and it doesn't run nearly as well as either of them. I suppose it's a difficult thing to balance, but I wish they had increased the amount of exploring to do and reduced the amount of grinding to do. If I'm not mistaken, that's 0/3 for me on games rated overwhelmingly positive in the last year or so. I'm beginning to not trust you guys.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game, and there is a lot to explore and find.  As someone who loves exploration and environmental survival games, this was right up my alley.  There ARE bugs, however, likely due to this being early access.  Terrains will disappear at random, clipping through walls happens a lot, and for some reason all the food in my inventory disappears whenever I close the game then log back in later.  On the other hand, there is another bug that basically gives you unlimited food, water, and oxygen, as long as you never actually use them but just move them to a chest and then back to your inventory.  Overall it is a fun game, and watching the barren planet slowly terraform into a lush world is rewarding and addicting, but the bugs need to be fixed to make the gameplay more worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Mix of survival, exploration, and mad science :)Was very very very satisfying to see the planet change over time. I caught myself smiling as I came back to an area and seeing how it changed, or how my species spread across the map.As you teched up, and the planet changed which allowed you to explore new areas easier. While the story is limited, it is there and was cool uncovering the mysteries.My only real, and minor, complaint was at some point I was nearly "done" but I had to just wait for things to tick over for 100% terraforming. I could have spent that time crafting more terraforming gear, but it was same time to just wait it out. Perhaps it's dumb, but would have been cool as a final tech tree item to be able to "pass time" while I let the last few % tick over in a timelapse.I played at 1.0 at launch and dumped 55 hours straight away and "finished the game". So my review is before any further QoL changes they have made. I am very much looking forward to the new map! I just wish I could play it again for the first time :)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to write a review since I see I still haven't. But I don't know where to start. I made some mistakes along the way. Took me forever to figure out some things. Had to move my base because I started at the bottom of a hill. (In other words the bottom of a lake) The different environments on the planet are neat. The different resources are neat. The way blueprints unlock is a bit tedious but I can understand why it's that way too. Fist in the air when I finally got the one blueprint I was waiting for. I think it was one of the last. I've enjoyed this game so very much. I would load it up and start over tonight except the new update is supposed to be "soon" and I'd rather start over then. It's fun to see the planet come to life. It's fun to build things. It's fun to see the numbers go up as you influence the planet.I'm hoping they work on the graphics and performance sometime soon. There are parts of the game that feel completely incomplete. But it's in early access. And it doesn't crash. Doesn't seem to have many? bugs? Or at least nothing major or memorable.  Resource management and crafting, let's call it workflow, does get tedious depending on how well you laid out your base. But at least for now, there's no loss for destroying something you built so you can rebuild it. Check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: $17.99 on Sale is the price I paid.... For an E.A. Game with that price tag, I kinda expected more but also for an E.A game it has a lot more polish than I expected.EDIT: If I could go back in time and choose to buy this game again or not I would still buy it. With a dev team of just 2 people I'd back that any day for what this game is and who I am supporting it is well worth it.... just wanted to be clear.Overall rating for an E.A. in its current state: 7/10Pros:Decent GraphicsSmall nooks and crannies to ExploreDifferent Crafting MenuTwist on a game similar to AstoneerCons:Object of the game isn't reachable without more contentSeems that there is things missing (*obvious with an E.A. game)Best mobility items aren't very fastSmallish Map that after a few hours you have a good grip on where to go and how to get there and where everything is.Suggestions:More areas to explore (caves, caverns, wash outs etc....)Vehicles that move a lot faster than walking or other modes currently in game.Zeolite should have some way to grow/harvest after searching the entire map/after end game... you run out pretty fast.Automating some of the smaller tasks, like food, water, oxygen, mining machines...AUTOMATE SORTING! Ugh, I will say I like I can sort my inventory with a click of the mouse but I would love to be able to put items into something that sorts them into respective bins.Bigger storage containers (your containers should be able to hold more than your inventory IMO)Some Kind of AI companion or NPCsActual Wild Life?... Maybe something like a Gene generator where you create bugs/animals? I could see an entire splice and dice DNA/GENE machine being a wild hit with the players.**Spoiler ALERT** After 80+ Hours in game and launching 100+ rockets with 1000x multiplier I'm still no where near what the original goal is.**END SPOILER ALERT**The game could use more content. There isn't really much to do other than explore a world with invisible boarders collecting resources and building the next items you unlock...After 80 hours of game play, I would say a lot of that time was spent waiting for resources and then collecting them and then waiting again often times afking with an empty inventory. I often would let this game run in the background while I did other things to pass the time in game or while I was at work.Even after everything is unlocked, and built 10+ times... You are no where near the end game, which means there is plenty of room for new tech and what not.

_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of the survival genre I can't recommend this game.  The concept is good, but it needs serious work.  And I don't just mean the code, I mean the core gameplay concept needs to be tweaked because what is here atm is a game where you build machines to make a number go up.  The more machines you build, the faster the number goes up.  When the number reaches a certain limit you win the game.  That's IT.  No environmental threats except occasional meteors you can largely ignore or exploit for extra resources.  The environment is bland, and I get that it's supposed to get better as the game goes on and be bland to start, but not *this* bland.  And when it does get more colorful it's still pretty basic.  There's just no real game here.  Wish I'd bought Satisfactory instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Within the first few minutes I felt the hooks sink in. This game is special. It actually feels like you are terraforming the planet. This game focuses on base building, exploration, and moderate survival. There are no enemies other than the lack of air, water, and food.I recommend going in blind if you can. You can easily spoil the discovery aspects which pull you into the setting and makes it not just a game where you are increasing some numbers.I would compare this to Subnautica. However It is in no way the same game in practice. Although I would guess that if you like Subnautica, you'll like Planet Crafter. Finally, while this game does have some bugs, none of them are major. Some machine UI is confusing. You can clip into terrain or go out of bounds fairly easily if you try. It is extremely stable though. I experienced zero crashes or freezes. That is almost unheard of today. For $20 this is a must buy if you like the concept. You won't be disappointed.  Oh, you also can rebind the keybinds. Something EVERY game should have but enough games don't allow that it must be mentioned.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent exploration and crafting game! Just like Subnautica, minus the enemies.The game is really intuitive to play (quite the opposite to No Man's Sky, actually). It features nice colors and lighting, visuals are clean and easy to understand.The game progress is quite well balanced. Not 100% but still well balanced. Sometimes there are many unlocks in a few seconds or a couple of minutes, and sometimes you don't unlock anything for hours.There are still a few bugs that need to be addressed (clicking issues, unclickable resources, building placement issues, invisible ceiling, animals are a real pain to feed, etc.), but to be honest they are seldom and not too bothering.Also, some improvements could be made, e.g. slightly modifying the world (i.e. destroying rocks that prevent buildings placement, for example), better made endings (not just 3 lines of text... we are not in 1990 anymore), ceiling lights for the shelters, moving a container (or anything else) without having to empty it first, improving the usability of the item deconstructor, increasing the duration of day/night cycles, allowing to stack chests (and/or put them on top of other furnitures), more things to discover (related to the different intrigues that arise), procedural worlds, and so many other things!!!Still, this game was very pleasant to play, and I fully recommend it to people who enjoy these kind of games.Also please build an antenna (and an email-computer) asap if this is your first run and you start at the default location.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, teraforming sandbox style game! The addition of dna and random biomes were a significant improvement along with drones!! Highly recommend checking out. _childDocuments_.review: For me it was totally worth the price.The game is not finished yet. If you rush the game, you can easily beat it around 30h. I was exploring everything and used the rocket very late, which slowed progression down.Apropos slowing down. When you develop your base and build more structures, it's possible that the fps will go down. I have a PC from 2016 and I have no problem playing something in FUll HD. When the stages with trees began it really dropped and began to stutter. My solution was that I used the teleporter from the endgame and moved all my industrial objects far away that it won't render when I'm in my base. The same with flower and treespreader.To clarify this is a game with terraforming aspects, a little bit of survival elements and base building aspects. At this point ( Ver 0.4.015) there is no automation like in other games. That means you have to get the ressources all by yourself. It will get easier later on, but in the beginning and midgame that means a lot of travelling by foot or jetpack.I hope that there will be some kind of optimization. Otherwise I'm afraid the performance with upcoming updates and later stages will become more and more poor.Do not forget to use the rockets as early as possible. It will boost your Terraforming index a lot. I was nearly ready to quit, cause there was no progression, before I used it.

_childDocuments_.review: The content provided by this delightfully deceptive cozy survival game cannot be overstated. Upon landing on your barren rock for the first time, you may not realize it, but this place will soon become your home. I would offer to demonstrate what this means, but the game will do it for you. The addictive positive feedback grind loops, the wild adrenaline pumping exploration when your oxygen begins to run low, the mystery of the logs you find on the surface as a new story piece is around each corner (for multiple stories that tie into one to boot), this game has it all.I would challenge someone to find an issue with a Survival Crafter that managed to remove combat, and still keep you on the edge of your seat. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love and recommend this game to anyone who loves survival or crafting simulations. its unique in my experience as the planet and environment actually change as you reach new terraforming milestones. The collectionist in me spent a lot of time trying to get every tree, insect, frog and fish so with the new animals update, I am thrilled at the possibilities of so many configurations. And I love that once you place a type of flora or fauna in the area around your base or bases, they start appearing in other places on the planet.  I also really like that you don't need to have power and other items right next to your main base, because you can have bases all over, any power item you put down anywhere powers everywhere. I think the only thing you need to have in a specific radius is a communications tower and the communications screen.While there are only a few base building pieces this still gives you the freedom to imagine a ton of different configurations, even building in the sky! I hope in the future they allow for underwater and underground builds and additional or more types of building pieces for those who want true building customization. _childDocuments_.review: It's early access, but really GOOD early access. Definitely a neat game, exploration, base building and something of a story line. Basically, you are tasked with terraforming a planet. No small task. The game has the usual functions of a survival game and a few different modes to choose from, Easy, Standard or Hard. Stay hydrated, stay fed, all the while doing what you can solo to get the resources needed to make the planet a bit friendlier towards life as we know it.I am very interested to see where the dev's go with this. It's already a fun game, if survival games are your thing. There's no enemies, at least none I have encountered so far. Co-op would definitely make things better, hopefully there are plans for that.First couple hours impressions? Decent, I like it. I like the sort of desolate feel of being basically marooned solo on this barren planet and given a nearly impossible task in order to leave. It has a very Subnautica feel to it. hopefully the developers will be able to add that level of depth over time.All in all, the price point is fine, and the game is very playable thus far and does not feel broken. To fans of survival genre games, I'd say download the demo first, which I did, and see if it suits. I decided to buy.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Planet Crafter is a great beginning. All the most of the basic gameplay is here.  It is a terrific little casual survival builder, and I hope the developer fleshes it out, and makes it more scientifically realistic :) My ThoughtsBut it is challenging to see where it evolves to. With the game itself being humans terraforming a planet the stage progression is more of a race than a real change to the conditions of the planet. I hope to see the developers make the terraforming stage progression less abstract and somewhat more realistic. I dont mean making it take millenia to change the planet but basic things like your planet doesnt start off at 0K (for those who dont know -273C (-459F) and then have rain and liquid water at a temperature around 1mK (-272C).Having the start conditions being something closer to say Mars ( NASA among others has lots of great info that could be used to set this up ). Then tieing the progression to actually meeting somewhat realistic requirements for the stages the developer has defined, such as liquid water at 273K (1C) and lets say 50,000Pa (about half Earths atmospheric pressure at seal level). The building gameplay is good for the development stage it is at, and from my experience surprisingly few bugs, The story attached to the planet and the players being there are basic but a solid platform to expand on. Definitely a game worth supporting.

_childDocuments_.review: Ive been playing this game with my friend for DAYS. When i get home from work, PLANET CRAFTER. After the gym, PLANTER CRAFTER. When i wake up, PLANET CRAFTER. I know it only says 17.6 hrs on record, but that time is over 2 1/2 days. The DEVS are STILL ADDING CONTENT to this game, and seem to be taking care of it. The gameplay is simple, but involved and the concept of the terraformation is simple enough to understand, multiple sub-progress trees effect the total progress. Its easy to get lost in building something, then realize you neglected some other project, or need more materials, meaning there is always something you COULD be doing, and there is also a sort of "puzzle adventure" type thing you can do (it was an incredible way to break up some of the monotony of craft/gather). Its been a long time since i got hooked on a game this hard. will probably buy for a friend or two as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet crafter is a game I would certinaly recommend for survival craft enthusiasts, or people wanting to give survival craft a go. It's very well paced majority of the way through constantly giving you things to do whether through new tech to build or areas to explore. The map is well thought out with lots of nooks and cranies and little tunnels you keep finding, even though you have been through there plenty of times. It's a really great game. Until the ending, I found the ending, either of the two easily attainable endings, shallow and left me feeling a bit empty. Certainly, for the length of time it takes to work your way through the game, finally get to the end and are left with that, it's a bit of a let down. But aside from that the game was great.

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow.I didn't complete the game yet (but hey, I have lakes already), but I can tell you: I absolutely love it.It's not your typical "build a base on Mars". I cannot put into words how much I appreciate devs' choices.1. Changing world. You're not just doing bigger numbers, you can visually see how it affects the world around you, slowly. Not "congrats you achieved 100 points, now there's water everywhere". It gives so much satisfaction, and because map is huge, you can visit far-away points once in a while and be suprised how much they changed.2. No fighting, no fear. If you're a pro gamer like me, you will appreciate there's no jump-scare, no "oh god it's dark, something will attack me", you're going into wrecks without fear.3. Easy mode and keep equipment. Again, as a pro gamer I very much appreciate when I can just chill my beans and wander around without fearing for my life. _childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is a great game for those that like Satisfactory and Space Engineers - if they had a love child, this is what that would be. As for other aspects of the game:- Exploration is always interesting - 8/10- Strategic base making is something to be aware of (I like a challenge) - 9/10- Storyline is basically non-existent but you're also not on this planet wondering why the heck you're there - 8/10- Bugs, next to none - 10/10- Graphics aren't amazing but good enough to thoroughly enjoy - 9/10- No Multiplayer but the game is very enjoyable regardless. For a lot of games that's difficult to do so - 9/10All in all, I very much recommend this game if you're questioning whether or not it's worth it. 9/10 overall i'd say!Thank you devs for making a game such as this, with only a small team of 2. _childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter : A Richly Detailed, and Addictive Sandbox ExperiencePlanet Crafter invites players into a richly detailed sandbox where creativity knows no bounds, offering a mesmerizing journey into the depths of creation and exploration. Visually, Planet Crafter is gorgeous, not top of the line graphics gorgeous, but gorgeous nonetheless. What it might lack in shortcomings in flashy effects, it makes up for in almost every other category of the game. This game pulls you in, and pulls you in hard. What truly sets Planet Crafter apart is its addictive gameplay and flawless execution. From the moment you dive into the game, you're greeted with a sense of endless possibilities. Whether you're terraforming lush landscapes, building up your base, or crafting a multitude of different items, every action feels meaningful and rewarding.The fun factor of Planet Crafter is undeniable. There's an inherent thrill in experimenting with different building techniques, exploring new biomes, and pushing the limits of your creativity. Much like Subnautica, Planet Crafter instills a sense of discovery and wonder as you delve deeper into its world, uncovering hidden secrets and unlocking new possibilities. This game also gives you the apprehension that Subnautica created. You all know what I am talking about, we were afraid to move 10 feet away from our pod in that game, and the world seemed so huge and dangerous. It is exactly the same thing here, the player will feel that apprehension, and slowly build confidence as they progress throughout the game. Moreover, Planet Crafter offers a staggering amount of replay value. With a vast array of tools and options at your disposal, no two creations are ever alike. Whether you're a seasoned builder or a newcomer to the genre, there's always something new to discover and create.In conclusion, Planet Crafter is a masterclass in sandbox game design that offers a rich and immersive experience, addictive gameplay, and endless creativity combinations that create a truly unforgettable adventure. If you're a fan of sandbox games, building games, or survival games, well, you've got it all with this one, and on a scale not seen since the likes of Subnautica. Planet Crafter is an absolute must-play. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much like Breathedge in both game play and early access.  Breathedge early access I felt very disappointed with but could see potential. But when the full game was released they fixed many of the issues I had and put a large amount of time into it and was very satisfied. Already 20 hours into this game and I can see great potential.  The way the environment changes as you teraform is great... Except when you have setup your starting area at the bottom of an ocean and have to rebuild everything.  So the biggest issue is the tutorial / journal system.   There is nothing explaining how to play the game, or what to do.  There is a communication system that sends you info that would be a really cool early on feature, but I didn't unlock this until 15ish hours into the game.  You start off not knowing what you're doing, how to unlock new tech, or how progress is advanced. which is kinda important and I can see why people wouldn't play after an hour or two. But I keep on being surprised by how much has been done in the game.  You make a large progression and some new features are unlocked and you realize the depth they unlock.   Oh, rockets?  Whatever.  Then you realize they unlock mapping and ability to pull down astroids to the planet.  Oh, once you start to get water forming new tech is unlocked.  Plant life is new tech, etc.  Things seem so minimalized because you get very little information on progression.Very few bugs so far in early access.  You can clip into some areas and I'm still not sure if blueprints are screwed up or if I'ved unlocked them all and I get no type of notification but overall, worth the money, and I'll enjoy it again at full release I'm sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun yet a little frustrating at times. Depending on your setup there is 6 hrs of game play with no unlocks near the end of the main goal.Please don't mistake the number of cons vs pros as this game is trash. Also, look on the bright side: If this was a AAA studio's game, would have better visuals indeed, however, it would be unoptimized, unfinished, unpolished, ultra-buggy, no issues ever fixed, and 29 pay DLCs already out, if not microtransactions, as we learned from Dragon's Dogma 2, even a SP game might have such BS (/spit Capcom).This game instead didn't try to be more than what was fundable & achievable for the creators, so it actually IS finished(!), in a good quality, again, can't emphasize engouh, fun to play, very well coded & optimized so it doesn't try to kill the PC (against the odds as it's running on Unity Cr@pgine), so it's just good, absolutely worths the price - I can only recommend it!Can't wait to see Planet Crafter II, hopefully without all the negatives (I'm not listing here, as for this game, it doesn't matter).

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Subnautica survival on the surface of Mars, except without combat. There's fully-functional optional multiplayer here as well. My wife and I have put about 23 hours into it so far, terraforming the red deserts into lush environments, while slowly uncovering some background story.I can't speak for having more than two players, or how well chat works, but we've been pleasantly surprised with how well the game and multiplayer runs. No perfomance issues or really any major bugs. Good for casual exploration and building (once you get past the early struggle to unlock food growers ASAP). I imagine that some quality of life improvements will be coming to take care of a few minor annoyances.+Tons to do+New schematics unlock or are discovered at regular intervals+Considerable customization of difficulty/duration+Decent graphics and music+Multiplayer works very well+Save anywhere+Saves and loads rapidly+No splash screens~Menus could use some touching up~A few items aren't explained well~You need to progress to food growers ASAP (should have been an early goal)~No combat or any real threats other than running out of food early on~No autosaves?~Needs some quality of life updates~Some environments lack variety or detail~Lacking/late on story compared to even first Subnautica game-Really needs an item to display your location to other players-Map is difficult to traverse and could use coordinate compass-Beacons can't be selectively turned off w/o a mod, causing clutter-Compass could use a marker for exact location you're looking at-Inviting Steam friend sometimes takes multiple attempts-Some objects can be difficult to place or snap-Meteors create temporary debris that clips into rooms/gets you stuck-Not always obvious when you've taken damage-A number of terrain features you can clip into-Frequent bug where you can't do much besides jump straight up when you load the game. Have to close entirely and restart to fix.Played on:Win11, i7-14700, RTX4060 Ti 8GB, 32GB DDR5-6000 @ 1920x1080using KB&M on a slightly modified Standard difficulty
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty nice and relaxing game from what I believe is a two person team.Be warned though, the game struggles late game when you've got a lot of flora growing and/or build a big base. It gets severely CPU limited at this point.If you don't mind low framerates then this is not an issue.There seem to be a CPU scheduler issue for Ryzen 5000 series at least, where the load is so spread out over available cores that the core clock speed never goes up much, and this reduces overall performance.Disabling one or more cores for the exe (CPU affinity) seem to help force the clockspeeds up and also help overall performance.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, it's... fine.I appreciate that sounds like I'm damning it with faint praise, but it really is a fine little game. You start on a drop pod, and your first struggle is just getting a base set up and not dying of dehydration. Then when water starts forming, you probably have to start worrying about moving your rapidly flooding base...That's essentially the game play loop; you have problem X, you fix it until Y comes along and you have to fix that.There's a few problems which are 'gameplay feel'; the game feels like it's 'unity asset' syndrome, and it can be very boring sometimes where your options are 'build X producer repeatedly to try and get past this lull in the tech tree' or just zone out and enjoy the pleasant-but limited-music. As you advance the stages terrain goes from lifeless brown sand to... green. I know there's buildings to generate flora, but it would be nice for things like grass to start spontaneously appearing.There's also the problem where multiple buildings that generate noise generates a 'chorus' sound effect. Randomising the pitch by a semitone or so per sound instance and hard capping the total simultaneous playing of the audio would fix things if you're listening, devs.Despite the nitpicks though, I still recommend; nothing is a real deal breaker, it's very relaxing to play and de-stress with, and it's also less than a third of mainstream games these days so I'm far more forgiving. There is a nice little touch with savegame files too; the preview of the planet gets steadily greener with more water on the surface as you progress.

Seeing the planet change as you hit milestones is really rewarding.Yes, there are a few minor bugs, I have not yet encountered a game breaking bug, more bugs that cause annoyance than anything else, the definitely don't ruin the game.Thumbs up to the team creating this game!I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone wanting a game that is relaxing with the survival base building elements that has made this genre so successful.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neutral review.The very beginning is very well done - you're thrown onto unlivable rock and need to survive and to survive you need things that this planet doesn't even have. Like food. So you feel pressure, hurry to build and expand, and in the process watch the planet change.However, after some point your progress slows to crawl, pressure disappears, and it turns into a chore that involves running back and forth between faraway locations.The first problem is that you have very limited inventory, and the items  One item - one inventory cell.  So if you need a lot of resource X, you'll have to run back and forth between the point where you can get the "resource X" and your base. This quickly becomes tedious.The other problem that you frequently end up starved for a resource you need to advance. For example, metals are collected from nodes on the ground, and at some point I started to run out of alluminium. This is not factorio/conan exiles, and if you mined out all alluminium in the nearby area, you won't be having fun, as you'll have to either search for a needle in a haystack, or WAIT for an event that has a chance to bring you more allumunium.There are several mineable resources like that, where you can get stuck in the game for long period of time, until you unlock AND build mechanics that would make your life easier.Later on in order to expand you'll be dependent on several resources that respawn, but slowly. So if you want more, you'll have to wait, and if you want to accelerate the gathering process, you'd need to build more sources, and then you'll probably need something else, and you'll have to wait for that too, or will need to run into another end of the map to get the required stuff....This gets very boring. The other thing is Terraforming Index, which pretty much determines how "Terraformed" the planet is. To advance you'd need to push this to ridiculously high values, and while t here are mechanics to accelerate the process, eventually reaching the next milestone become way too slow.--------All things considered, I'd say this is an interesting experience, but it makes sense to wait for sale, or wait for updates. That's because after very well done beginning, slowing down of progress, and frequent resource starvation greatly affects the game, and not in a g ood way.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for 44 hours at this point - probably should have done things like sleeping during that time, but, well, just one more blueprint unlock... I love this game so much - it feels like when I first discovered Subnautica (admittedly, more of a bleak and desolate hellscape when you arrive, rather then a stunning tropical reef, but hey, that's what you're there to fix).Firstly, it runs smoothly, the controls are intuitive and I haven't discovered any major bugs or glitches. There are occasional bits of scenery which are a bit clunky, but then it's a small, early access game with a two-person dev team, the quality is amazing considering that.It irons out all the gripes I've had with other space survival/crafing games - awkward UI. impossible survival, boring maps, ugly buildings, stressful conditions, lack of heart etc.It is an incredibly feel-good game. For once, you come to a planet, not to strip-mine it for resources and slaughter all the indiginous species, but peacefully, to bring it to life and make it thrive and be beautiful. There is no combat, a decision I applaud, and it's so refreshing to play a game where you can really do some good and see the difference you're making. (The only other game I've played with this 'Johnny Appleseed' theme is Green Project, a little pixel graphics indie game which I also recommend - it has heart!). After playing games like Satisfactory where it's beautiful but you're forced to commit ecological vandalism, this is a breath of fresh air. (Well, not actual fresh air, maybe you can create a breathable atmosphere eventually?).It's also a really good message - there's nothing like carefully nurturing a barren world until you start seeing plants trying to take hold, to make you appreciate living, growing things. I hope it goes far!There is also an intriguing story lurking here - I understand it's still in progress, but I'm excited to see where it leads!Back to practicalities - in terms of balance and progression, the game works well, but it pays to give attention to all the aspects of terraforming to avoid reaching milestones with, say, O2 levels, and then having to wait ages for your heat or pressure to catch up because the blueprints you just unlocked requires a component you can't make yet. In my case, I didn't send up any rockets for ages, and they make a huge difference!It also pays to explore the map thoroughly, and pay attention to detail. It's an amazingly rich and interesting map, full of secrets and hidden corners, and you can find some precious resources tucked away if you look carefully. There are also a lot of beautiful sites to place your base, some of which only become accessible later. All in all, it's still in early access and the devs are working on more content, but I'm already hooked, and excited to see where it leads.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 20-or-so hours of this game are fantastic. It gave me distinct Subnautica vibes, with the same dopamine-hit feeling of satisfaction when you collect items and craft increasingly complex recipes. Seeing the planet change around you was so cool, and I loved the narrative touches (getting messages when you reach certain checkpoints).The only negative, for me, is that you plateau after a while. The number of new blueprints you can unlock become more and more spaced out, and it can start to feel like an absolute grind, spending hours and hours and hours crafting the same kinds of machines. The story dwindles, too. You don't get any more messages from the company or "Riley," your long-distance terraforming friend. At around the 40-hour mark, I started to get bored, because I felt I'd discovered all of the main world, and I'm not as interested in exploring procedurally-generated wrecks you eventually are able to access via a portal (like a stargate). I found those wrecks very annoying to navigate, because they all looked the same, with so many identical rooms that I think the intent was for you to waste time wandering around endlessly. The only goal of going to those places was gathering of resources--there's no story in the other areas. As a narrative gamer, I think my interest waned when the story dried up. Only the most die-hard players will get to the endings, I think. After planet crafting for 45 hours, I only terraformed about 1/5 of what is needed to win the game. I honestly think the developers are trying to stretch things out so they can add content later, which totally makes sense if an endless game is your thing. But I like a more cohesive game that has an ending you can achieve in a reasonable time frame (see: Subnautica). I'm not going to spend 100 hours of my life endlessly collecting the same things and building the same machines (that totally clutter up the planet and make everything look super messy, by the way), only so I can "escape" the game. I can do that now, by not playing any more, if you see what I'm getting at.These minor complaints aside, I enjoyed this game immensely!  These kinds of games are so relaxing to play, and the "blooooop" of sucking up resources is so satisfying. It was visually engaging, well thought out, and with an ingenious way of adding in new levels of difficulty/new mechanics as you went along. Good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: I have put 75 hours into this game so far. It has been a very relaxed but fun experience, from the first arrival on a barren desolate world, to the hours of exploration and discovery leading to water and vegetation appearing. Don't get me wrong, it can get a little tedious at times, some might say boring, but personally I sometimes like to immerse myself into something that feels casual and relaxing, but with a point to aim for. You start with pretty much nothing, small bags, small oxygen tank etc and it has basic survival elements, food, water and of course oxygen. But as you progress you can unlock items and expand your capabilities. The base building is fun and easy - not over complicated. Currently no enemies or fighting - I don't think there are plans for that in any case and that is fine, because the purpose of this game is simply to terraform the planet. I've had an enjoyable time so far. I've reached a point, where my planet has water, trees, insects (although haven't seen them) and is now heading towards fish. I might be wrong or it could be because it's early access but I 'think' that's as far as I can go....for now at least. All in all, enjoyable, relaxing and easy going survival/terrraform/base builder game.

_childDocuments_.review: After 121 hrs of play I have finished the game with 100% achievements. I didn't rush and loved every minute. It's a chill game with no pressure (apart from managing food/water) and it was fun to watch your planet go from a barren landscape into a thriving ecosystem. The lore was a nice touch and added further interest along the way. This is one of the few games I have completed (and possibly the only one where I got all achievements) as I tend to get bored after spending too long in a game. Although I have a lot more hours in other games, they are generally sandbox and don't have an ending and I also tend to take breaks with them. Overall if you are looking for a relaxing game to fill your time I can certainly recommend this one. Oh and I'm 65yrs old in case anyone of a similar age (or older) is unsure whether it would be a game for them.Note: I just read a comment about a player not wanting to lose their build and avoided playing any ending. You don't lose your build, that's how I managed to get 100%. You can load up the game after you chose an ending and it puts you back on the evacuation platform just prior to leaving so you are able to choose another option - if you have the correct materials etc.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 47 hours, I found it hard to decide whether to recommend or not.Overall, I will reward the creative concept and the sheer potential, but I will advise against fully purchasing it just yet.Not much to spoil but I will describe the current end game. There isn't one. You play for a satisfying 10 - 13 hours, exploring the map, shipwrecks and outposts, eventually accessing blocked caves, unlocking and implementing better technologies, building up your base. It was great at first. But head my warning. Once you unlock trees, there's not much point in pushing through to insects and the final unlocks just yet. That is unless you just love grinding. Basically nothing happens. And according to the developers updates, the game apparently doesn't have much further to expand, other than some map additions, spawning in some basic animals, maybe some new tech and a tiny bit more story. They have fully admitted that their development capabilities are limited and they intend for this to be a pretty basic experience even by the end. So with that info, I will declare that the price point is frankly a stretch, and will likely remain so. This seems like maybe a 12 dollar game at most. So my final thoughts. Great concept. Check out the demo. Keep an eye out for updates on final game progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Building in a game is one of my favorite aspects of it.  I played Subnautica Below Zero when it was first released. _childDocuments_.review: This game slaps so hard it's not even funny. Wake up on a desolate rock as a convict sent to terraform the planet so that the mega corporations can build factories (or something like that). You have no idea what's going on but you do the little small tasks the game sets out for you and by hour 4 you have a fully built base with a jetpack and nuclear reactor. The terraform index is probably the most unique thing about the game, indicating the percentage of the planet that the player has made hospitable to life. This, combined with the surface of the planet itself and it's atmosphere and ecology all changing and evolving due to your actions is something that very few games can ever pull off well (i.e. the amygdala reveal in Yahar'gul from Bloodborne). the constant trickle of rewards and progression are so smooth and well-paced, which makes playing through the game from start to finish a highly enjoyable experience, even on a second playthrough, which offers a good amount yet not nearly as much replayability as i think the devs are wanting to have in the game. Of course, this is still ONLY early access and the fact that it's ~$20 makes it well worth the time and more than worth the money

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delight.  I started playing in Early Access, they provided several significant updates, and I was excited to see it leave Early Access.They did not disappoint!  This is a labor of love through and through.  They stuck to what they promised and the result is one of the most relaxing and rewarding exploration/crafting/base building games I've ever played.Just to set expectations, here are some details new players should know before buying:- There are no enemies nor weapons -- even more peaceful that Subnautica.- Well, except for the occasional meteor swarm.  :)  A direct meteorite strike can hurt you, but won't damage anything you build.- You can die from any of the standard survival means - lack of oxygen, water or food.  There are several modes where you can adjust this, however.  All of this naturally gets much easier as the game progresses.- The graphics are somewhat behind the times, and the geometry of some of the maps are pretty basic.  This is intentional, and they stated it would be the case from the outset.  They decided to focus on a pleasant gameplay loop over graphics.  Nevertheless, It's a ton of fun to explore, there's a great deal of beauty as the game progresses, and I found my jaw dropping a few times, just from unexpected beauty or grandeur.- The mining animation is unrealistically silly and the Level-of-Detail transitions for plants are jarring and exaggerated, but I found it kind of endearing after a while.  :D- The terraforming has an effect on almost every part of the world, some of them in surprising ways.  It's really gradual and pleasant.- The built-in game modes range from Creative, Relaxed, Standard, Intense, and Hardcore.  But you can also customize any of these 'til your heart's content.  Mix and match the qualities of whatever modes you like!- Hardcore mode out-of-the-box is a brutal, punishing, blatantly unfair experience.  I wonder if they did this to give you the option of experiencing what it might have been like for others to have landed there with a horrible start.  I think it may be survivable IF you know the map very well, plan very carefully, move quickly, and do everything efficiently.- At a certain point your gear is so good and the terraforming so far along that it will become much easier to survive.  It's a very satisfying curve. _childDocuments_.review: This game is already pretty awesome.  It checks a lot of boxes for me:-- Base-building-- Resource gathering-- No enemies-- An extensive and well integrated tech tree.-- A decent number of resources that can be used to make other resources.-- And just when I began to feel the grind, the game threw me a little something new.  I felt as if I'd gotten my second wind.  I was ready to push on.The Cons:-- Once movement speed becomes less of a problem, the world begins to feel too small.-- The existing biomes are interesting.  One, in particular, is confusing but breathtaking.  Yet, I would love to see more.  Once again, the world needs to be bigger.-- The crafting system suffers from the same problem as most crafting games.  The player still needs to run from locker to locker to collect crafting items.  In some games, it makes sense.  However, that kind of busy work doesn't make sense in this one.  The technology in Planet Crafter is so advanced that a single person can terraform an entire planet.  However, there is no system to automatically feed resources to the crafting stations?   -- The best storage option is more obtrusive than it needs to be.  There's a big bump out on the back that serves no purpose.  If that was where the transport mechanism was located or something,  I wouldn't mind as much.-- The premise for the game is intriguing.  I found a location that is absolutely chilling, as well as  heartbreaking.  It brought to the fore the loneliness, desperation, and urgency  that the game play did not.  As a result, I got the impression that the developers have the skill to tell a story that can immerse and move me.  If it is  in the works, I can't wait!  If this is all there is, I'll be a bit let down.-- The lighting still needs work.  Transitions are jarring.  I especially don't like the lighting in the Bio Lab.-- I love base-building.  Planet Crafter makes it easy.  Perhaps, a bit too easy.  I wish that there were more building blocks to toy with.   Also, more decorations, collectibles, and functional furnishings could assist with role-play.  Otherwise, the biodomes are beautiful respites from the institutional sameness of the main modules.--Finally, unless additional handmade worlds are in the works, or the team is working on procedural generation, once the game is done, it's done.  There's not much reason to play again.Yet, despite the cons, The Planet Crafter deserves its current rating.  I'm having a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game pre-release for years, on and off, and finally again now that it hit 1.0 release, for hundreds of hours, I felt I owed it to the developers to post a review.  It's the least I can do, I certainly got my money's worth.  Obviously, I like the game.  I like the vibe, it's both relaxing and (occasionally) nerve wracking at the same time.  At first, survival is difficult, takes planning, and a bit of luck.  But after you've established a minimal base, it's easier to survive a moment and start working on the goals.To keep this review spoiler free, I won't discuss storyline, or even specific play mechanics, because those grow over time in the game, and that's half the fun.  But rest assured, there is far more to this game than it seems like, at first.  So here's my rundown:Gameplay: 9 of 10Graphics: 7 of 10Music: 10 of 10 (it's really fantastic, a highlight of the game)Sound FX: 8 of 10Controls: 6 of 10 (there is a bit of input jank to overcome but it's not bad)Mechanics: 8 of 10 (base building and crafting are great.  Not perfect, but great)Story: 5 of 10 (whatever, the story doesn't factor into the gameplay much at all)The low marks for the story are only because it's barely there, and barely matters.  What's there is good though, and has plenty of atmosphere and keeps you interested.  It's just so minimal I'm almost tempted to say 'there is no story', but that's not quite true. For the size of the development team behind this, this game punches so far above it's weight it's like a Smurf knocking out Mike Tyson.  I mean it's just amazing what a small team has done here, AAA studios should take a page - focus more on gameplay, less on "message".  On that note, this game does not have any embedded political or social messaging that I could detect.One last note, about the graphics.  I gave it a fairly middling score, which isn't entirely fair because the developers produced fantastic art with great design and if it was made with Unreal it'd probably be 10 of 10 or at least a 9.  However, the game engine they used is getting a bit dated, so hopefully for sequels or remasters, they'll consider a more modern option.  Don't let that deter you though, this game is great.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not impressed with this game. I had high hopes because of all the good reviews but im also confused by all the good reviews. Maybe I quit too soon before it got good but I should not have to play more than 14 hours for a game to start being good. To start its extremely grindy which is fine to a certain extent but it felt like I never got any resources to help automate some of this or it takes way too long to get to that point. I dont like how you can build wherever you want and magically have power from your reactors or solar panels that are half way across the map. There should be actual pockets of these minerals that you have to mine not just random bits scattered across the entire map.It would of been nice to have more danger in this game other than just oxygen which you can cheese the hell out of by just building a living compartment wherever you want. _childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is truly an amazing game! From the moment I first entered the world of Planet Crafter, I was fascinated by its immense variety and endless possibilities. The graphics are breathtaking, and the environments of the planets feel so realistic that I felt like a real space explorer.One of the best aspects of this game is the freedom it gives players to create their own worlds. From crafting ecosystems to building cities and exploring different planetary landscapes, the possibilities are truly limitless. Every detail can be customized according to one's imagination, providing a sense of absolute creative expression.The gameplay is also great. The controls are intuitive and easy to learn, allowing players to quickly immerse themselves in adventures and explore new worlds without unnecessary delays. Exploration is rewarding, and every corner of the planet holds something new and exciting.The community around the game is fantastic as well. Forums and social media are full of inspirational stories and ideas from other players, adding another dimension to the game and encouraging collaboration and sharing among fans.Overall, Planet Crafter is a great choice for anyone who loves exploration, creation, and imagination. It's a unique experience that's worth trying out and exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a unique and cool concept to me, one I would have never thought of. But I want to be clear about this game up front: It is like a cross between a Survival/Gather game and a Walking Sim. There is No Combat in it, aside from Time and dodging meteors. It's not stuffed full of annoying minigames, it's not really hard, and it takes a lot of patience.It's also one of the most... Isolated games I've ever played (in solo mode, but there is multiplayer which appears to work quite fine). You are going to be by yourself, rarely getting messages from others, but it is just you and the loneliness of space. Some people will love this idea like I did, others will find it incredibly boring or uncomfortable. But I did want to mention it.However, watching your assigned planet terraform in real time is so... Surreal. It happens slowly, very slowly. But you will start noticing a lot of changes around if you keep your eyes open. There's always something to explore, something to do while you're waiting for your machines to do their stuff. You just need to pack your supplies; food, water, oxygen, and embark on foot.What the devs made here was unique when I played it back in E.A. Coming back to it now, I'm glad they stuck with it. Not much has actually changed, but sooooo much has been added! I'm still in the process of seeing all of it again.
