_childDocuments_.review: A really wonderful game, I've had such a good time with it. Every time I open it I can't seem to put it down for hours and hours. I'm sure i'll plug many more into it as time goes on. Great for tuning out the world and letting your brain focus on something productive after a hard day. I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Really love how this game works and plays with the potential for a lot more to come! Only downside I see so far is the lack of strong boundaries(collision detection) of our airtight habs as the random growth of trees and flora that seem to grow through the hab walls and prevents access to our machines or lockers as well as the water that gets into our prebuilt bases even if we have sweet airlock systems set up! I would like to build into the ground like so many of the people who have been to the planet have done yet failed the mission before us!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: At first you might find the progress as slow but the idea of changing an entire planet to an atmosphere that is clean is quite fun, you dont need enemies in this style of game. I went from a cold dark planet to blue skies and normal clean rain from the clouds that formed. This game is more about finished project, as in when you change the world, you can see it and that it shows you put work into it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Still early access and unfinished, so bear that in mind before buying; however, I have enjoyed it and am looking forward to the next updates. If you liked subnautica, you'll probably enjoy this one. In my opinion it is more satisfying as you can see the changes taking place as you progress through the stages of planet development. There is also some interesting story/lore that is enjoyable, but you can also completely ignore it if you just want to planet build.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Super relaxing game and adorable critters. There are no enemies so really the only thing you worry about is staying fed, hydrated and not without air. There are secrets to find and multiple "endings." There are quite a few bugs to fix still like phasing through the map, hollowed geometry you can see under or just walk under. However no matter how stuck into geometry you can sometimes get into, you will find a way out its not completely game breaking. Hopefully there will be more planets and stories in the future, it is a bit expensive for a single planet run through however, since it is always the same layout, it is not like minecraft/valheim with large world random layouts. Overall if you are just wanting to chill out with some good tunes, this game is great and also fun with friends!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo first and was like 'Yea, I can see this going places' so bought the game to support the company and I'm having a blast even if its not finished. I haven't experienced any game breaking bugs but I would advise is make sure you save. I don't believe there's an autosave but I have went hours without saving and have to remind myself to.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: There's something odd with this game. Like a good book you start playing then don't want to put it down. I do hope the Devs stay the course and add to the game as there is so much that could be done. It's nice to be able to play something that you don't necessarily die in. If there had to be a criticism it would be maybe a number of planets could be added to give some more replay and diversity value.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: An early access game, currently with only about 20 hours or so of content, but what is there is a lot of fun. There's something exciting about the idea of converting a barren, lifeless world into a pristine Eden that draws you into the game for hours and hours. There are still some technical bugs in the game, particularly at the edges of the map where clipping is an issue and with resource balancing, but development is regular and relatively fast. I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Really well made game. There are some flaws, but overall very enjoyable. It goes from simple survival, to base building and automation.I'm surprised at how much there is to explore and things constantly changing.Coop also works really well, with some minor bugs here and there, with some already patched.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed the current content and am impressed.  Every time I said this aspect is becoming repetitive the developers had a solution at the right time.  Looking for more content; eta Feb 2023.   Was fun at current stage but the game has a bit to go to be considered complete.  My hope is that the developers include new stuff for early stages so it is fresh for early access players.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, I've completed the Prologue and continued playing the game until it was released on the 24th. To my surprise, I was able to continue my saved game from the Prologue. Now, around 68 TTi and 6.7 % of the Insects Stage complete and the possibility that the Insects stage might not be in the game yet, I still love to play. I focus on increasing Oxygen, Heat, Pressure, and Biomass. Currently: O2 @ 63778.14 ppm, Heat @ 1288.52 mK, Pressure @ 1279.83 Pa, and Biomass @ 1.4 mt. You probably can see how many hours I played before writing this review. What can I say, I love this game.Developers - Thank you far an AMAZING game and can't wait for more updates. Merci
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun crafting survival game, exactly what I wanted. I'd prefer a bit more guidance on how to achieve your teraforming goals, and more of a quest tracker (as the game only gives you a tracker for your first couple of things, then disappears). It'd also be nice to have a glossary of terms or something, as I have no idea what all the different measurements mean or how to affect any specific one. But all of this is just personal preference, because I've continued to progress the milestones just by doing my own thing, exploring and basebuilding and building new technologies as I can.I definitely recommend starting on the easiest mode though, as you can barely explore before running out of oxygen for a good chunk of time in the early game, and I personally hate losing items upon death - especially when some of your early-game resources like food, until you can grow your own, are finite finds.I do hate how limited your inventory and storage options are though - especially later in the game, even with upgrades, some crafts take many different items so you have to go back and forth a lot. I also soon gave up on building chests and just left piles of ores around my base for a while in early game, because it just got ridiculous. Also, I wish I could scan for the rarer materials or something - without looking it up, seems to be  based on pure luck of where your exploring takes you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Very much a labor of love initially, an hour or so of patience in the first steps after leaving your pod and you'll see why the reviews are so hype. This is the most I have played a game in a good while and I'm anxious to continue playing and supporting this game in it's early stages.Most of what felt "grindy" was out of the way once I realized how the tech unlocks worked and started building properly. Buy the game, and give youtube a search for one of a surprising number of beginner tips/guides, and get terraforming. It also runs just swell at high settings on a Dell G3 3590.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a joy to watch this game grow and develop over EA.  Whilst not sporting the most UHD graphics that is quickly forgotten exploring the world and watching it subtly change as terraformation gathers pace.  Starting with a world at home in the Martian you transform it into a vibrant green and blue one. Resource gathering can be a bit clunky at times and less refined than factory focused similar games but later on this is somewhat streamlined.  Terraformation is slow at certain points but this is largely as I forge to massively spam certain buildings before I go off exploring more of the world.During EA most of the rough edges have been smoothed but a few kinks remain however having played it though a good chunk of development these are despite a lot of love and attention from the devs rather than due to a lack of the same. The devs have a good track record of listening o the community and acting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: i watched a youtuber play this @jacksepticeye's video and i had also seen this game on steam but didn't think much about it until seeing the gameplay and like others have said this has some similarities to subnautica a game i really loved so i said screw it why not and bought it and i was so amazingly surprised.  it's very fun and its clear there is a lot of love and passion put into it the gameplay starts of slightly confusing but once you get it which doesn't take long it becomes very simple.  the progression is very satisfying and cool to watch and exploring the world is really cool as you find odd biomes and areas and see the changes that happen as you progress through the Terraforming.  the lore while not fully developed has a lot of potential and is already taking advantage of that potential with the small pieces there.overall its a very fun survival game with a lot to give and i would absolutely recommend purchasing it and supporting the devs who are a smaller group and have somehow managed to make a more enjoyable game than so many other mainstream publishers if your into the survival game genre
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: great example of early access game with great potential at the moment tho still needs polishing.At the moment the game feels like its in an Early Alpha Stage.Its playable, enjoyable even but there is obviously since its early access a lack of content still and a lot of balancing and refining that needs to be done.I did grind myself through to the current end of the game but i wouldnt suggest to do that in its current state as due to the lack of vehicles (as of now, they are in developement) it basically becomes a walking simulator where you just pick up ressources to bring them back to ur base in order to expand a little.Things that need fixing atm (in my opinion)Jetpack: Getting out of bounds and reaching areas that you are not meant to progress to yet is easy because the collision models of many things arent yet very refined so you can just fly up to the peak of mountains or glitch through rocks and get to areas barred by ice that is supposed to melt after a certain ammount of terraforming.Tedious running and ressource collection:Game needs some sort of inventory upgrade beyond just adding rows (stacking ?) or some sort of vehicle.This should only be implemented after expanding the world by the developers or in the late mid to end game stage since otherwise the game would be cut too short atm.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a strange mixture of idle game mechanics and survival. You are essentially tasked with turning a mars-like planet into another earth. In order to get there, you gradually gain access to advanced technology that (over time) can actually make that happen.Your character needs food, water, and oxygen, which become more easy to obtain as the game progresses. Progression is based on several independent scores that increase with a certain velocity, depending on what you have built. As you reach milestones on these scores, new technology unlocks, from simple farms to automated production and logistics. All resources (maybe except those laying on the surface) are infinite so it all scales with the kind of structures (mining or otherwise) placed across the landscape. Some things come quickly, others require a lot of buildings, energy production, and patience.Overall I really like this game. Most changes (since its initial version) are solid, it is on a good trajectory. The things missing are on the far end of the progression ladder. You won't notice anything missing for many hours. The far end is work in progress. We are at the time of writing at mammal level currently missing, with the frog (amphibian) stage mostly complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, with an in-depth tech tree, interesting landscape (though still needs some work done on it!), many secrets to find.Very relaxing gameplay, quick to start up, keeps you on your toes for the necessities of life.Overall a good game and is likely to get much better as it gets out of early access.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun. Not finished yet, but definitely will get many hours of fun out of it as it is atm.The idea of the game is very cool. A survival/crafting game where you must terraform a planet.As you progress through each stage of the process, it feels very rewarding.It's quite a zen-like experience for a survival type game. It shares some of the same qualities from Subnautica too. The gameplay loop is similar in many ways.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall. Can be a bit grindy a times, as it takes a lot of resources to evolve and terraform the planet (you see the environment change when progressing in the game).Story is rather simple but interesting.The graphics are rather simple but fit the environment and the game well.Very nice soundtrack, very relaxing ambience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: A remarkably well-balanced 1st person sim! Up until the very end I pretty much always had something interesting to be doing, with tech development pretty well spaced out. There are little storylines hidden in the game, optional but fun. I probably missed a few things, but that's all right. I finished and have no real desire to go back for more: I got my money's worth, and I'm ready to move on to another game.  Which is no bad thing! I have other games to play, and it's good to draw a line under this one. I really enjoyed seeing the well-crafted game world progress from lifeless to full of plants, insects, and frogs. The scenery is frankly gorgeous in places. And the portal feature adds some much-needed variety late in the game. The wrecks are interesting (some downright haunting), and I enjoyed being able to return to them and get more out. I wish there were more story tied to them, and I would love to see another level of disassembler to get further benefit from them. Base-building is fun, and there's forgiveness later for being silly enough to build multiple bases, though in the mid-game that got really painful. A rover with extra storage and maybe oxygen would have been a huge help in the middle of the game, even if it had limited mobility.I like how streamlined the survival mechanisms are; just enough to give a challenge and force some tough decisions, but not so much as to be a constant annoyance after the early game.That said, I think once the game got to the mammal stage, the pacing pretty much fell apart and I spent a lot more time letting the game sit while I went to do other things just so I could finally be done. The animal building could be cool, and seemed at first to have infinite variation, but there are only three base species, and I only rarely got new variants. I was deeply disappointed to not find the world populated with the animals I did create, too: they just hung around my base, one of each.Anyway, on balance I really enjoyed the game and have already recommended it to a bunch of people. With just a few improvements it could be better, but it's fun as it is.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this game! It has great visuals, a nice progression and much fun to be had designing your base. The environmental and exploration aspects are interesting and as others have said its very subnaughtica like, but without the scary bits. I'm looking forward to more back story perhaps and  more decorative elements, posters shelves etc being introduced maybe? Would be nice to introduce fish and birds in the later game. A lot to do and has kept me obsessed with it since I got it. My tip for newbies is don't build on the low ground!

_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice and simple relaxing game to play and just lose yourself in it, the progression feels it has a good pace so it doesn't feel too fast or slow and there is a lot to do in this game in general from exploring, gathering resources, building, etc. However, one feature which I personally would like to see be implemented is some sorts of storage item organise so that when you have a lot of resources they can be quickly organised in storage lockers some kind of way.Otherwise, in my personal opinion this is a very good game I would recommend to others and I can't wait to see what the dev team has for us in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's get the obvious out of the way first.  Clearly they have created something special here, a "good game" some might even say.For all of it's curiosities, however, I could not have been more enthusiastic about it being over.Planet Crafter accomplishes something that games with enormous budgets commonly fumble in that it is a game that actually evolves as you play it in a satisfying manner.  The plot hook in and of itself is less the creation of things, but the impact these creations are having on the environment around you. It feels good to have your actions directly and visibly terraform the planet.The map is static, and that's fine. We don't need a procedural crapshoot - the hand crafted map appears to have had a good amount of thought put into it.  It is also well catered to players who want to look at a map online to find out where to mine certain materials, or find certain items. Let it be known that towards the late game, this is remarkably handy.It took me 54 hours to complete the game, but this is because I spent my first 10 - 15 hours creating a monolith of a home base on the ridge overlooking the starting valley that I then never returned to beyond the 20 hour mark.  I'm a natural born artist and my bases must be perfect, and as you uncover more and more technologies, the game does this mildly annoying thing thing where it takes the layout you've spent hours and hours putting together and says, "no actually, this wont do at all" - that may be fine for some, but for me, I literally lost sleep.The way you craft and collect isn't novel, but it works well.  I will say though that the inability to move an item that you've built without actually having to deconstruct it first is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ obnoxious, especially when trying to move lockers full of items. Towards the end of the game you will have dozens of lockers full of literally hundreds of items. The brain ♥♥♥♥ that is moving your production and crafting and storage is in need of some serious review. Just let me pick up a locker full of ♥♥♥♥, and put it somewhere else... Pretty please.The mystery surrounding the world is shallow, but mildly intriguing.  There are things to discover, a story of sorts to unravel, trite as it may be. The wrecks you find around the planet at first create an eerie and tense feeling, but that quickly fades to utter frustration.This needs to be said... Artist I may be, maze runner I am not. Running mazes is like putting my brain into a garlic press and these late game wrecks that do appear to have been PROCEDURALLY GENERATED are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ couriers of confusion, stress, and regret. If they were, in fact, designed by hand, then they were done so by a genuinely evil individual.  I have little to no idea how the developers married such a grand vision of discovery with such a bankrupt interpretation of "difficulty" - and yes, late game wrecks are given "difficulty" ratings.Let it be known that death in this game is a weightless and unobtrusive occurrence, but being lost in the depths of a spaceship, in what seems like an endless collision of right-angle and identical tile-sets, is not an experience I wish upon anyone.  The size, and related labyrinth, of these crashes appear to be what they are attempting to describe in their difficulty ratings.My planet had trees and lakes and waterfalls and butterflies and... it was beautiful.  The experience of creating and evolving that this game creates is unlike any other, but the experience of discovery is like being naked in a spa with a dog that won't stop farting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a gem of a survival game. The 1.0 addition of base game multiplayer (was possible before modded, but janky) is a MASSIVE improvement. I always felt like this game, despite being solid solo, was really meant for multiplayer. Like the other reviewer said, it really feels like I'm playing minecraft for the first time again. Excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter was a game I was given by a friend though I didn't touch it much at first. This was well-well-well before release date. It wasn't until I was on a depression spiral and feeling the worst about everything that I needed a big distraction from my own brain so I tried it out. I am so happy I did. While the world of a game isn't reality, being able to see the effects of my efforts change an entire planet landscape made me feel so many positives. For the times it felt like a grind, I could go exploring. For the moments I was waiting for a next tier of development, I could fiddle with optimization of my methods. The graphics are kind of midway between surreal and real, which I can dig (and some of the biomes are such a beautiful mix of effects and colours).I've suggested this game to multiple friends and I still play it when I'm just wanting to see positive growth. I'm so glad the devs managed to slip multiplayer in and I hope they continue to take pride in what they made. The only thing that could possibly make this game even more of a lovely time is added lore! I've still got so many questions!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: So. This is it. Just finished 100% of the game. All 55 steam achievements acquired, everything explored and seen, all endings done. There's no more to do. I could say a lot about this game. Honestly I regret all these 70+ hours put in this game. Why I did it then ? Because I'm a ''completionist gamer'' and when I start a game I must finish it and do everything. I saw the overwhelming good reviews on steam and tell myself a lot of time ''this game must be good at some point'' and then I continue to play again and again waiting for this fun and rewarding moments to show up. But it never did and I feel bored during my playthrought all along. Now I even regret buying the game. What to say about this game then ? There's a lot to say. Well, I guess it is some kind of functional, reasonable and okay game. It work. And most of all I put 70 hours in this game to do everything possible and more. Which for me is a bare minimum. 1$ = 1 hour of gameplay for me. So this game is cost efficient at least. I must give it that. But the question is : does it really was worth it to put 70 hours in this game ? My answer is no. These are some of the reasons I could list, but there could be more : - Most of all, be prepare for a lot, I mean A LOT, of boring grinding. Especially if you want all the three endings. There is a possibility mid and late game to automate the ressource gathering and be more efficient but it is still a lot of managing and the automation system just feel boring and not rewarding at all. - The game is visually, aesthetically and graphicaly unpleasant. This game want to be some kind of Subnautica, maybe with some mixed elements of No Man's Sky and Satisfactory. But this game just can't get the beauty and wonder in the face of Nature that these games have. In Planet Crafter, the world look boring, it look cheap, it look unreal, it look just lame and sad. There's no life in it. When you reach the insect/animals terraformation you do not see animals roaming the land, they are just silent and still in some spot. Butterfly are the only living being that really add somethings. And mammals, there's only 3 species and they must be crafted and put into farm­. The world also feel weirdly terrestrial and not alien at all. I mean there's butterfly, frogs and fish that look like our real animals. The trees do not move, even when you ear some kind of wind or when there's a storm. And again a lot of trees just look like the one we have on earth. I was just unable to recreate the ''wow'' effect that the world of Subnautica and Satisfactory create on me. These worlds really feel alive compare to Planet Crafter.  - The lighting and weather physics are horrible, cheap and so disappointing. When you're inside building or wreck the outside lighting affect the one inside which make no sens. You can hear the rain and wind when far inside Wreck. Lamps and lights feel odd and weird, unatural. There's no shadows, darkness is only in wreck. The sky is standing still with three ugly planets that will never move. There's no stars, no sun and the clouds are horrible. When you change spot, the lighting drastically change, which is so unrealistic. Imagine walking in dunes under full lighting, then because you enter some kind of crystal biome out of nowhere the sky become black and the lighting become cold and grey. But you are outside. This make no sens. - Sound design is inadequate and unsatisfying. Machines only emit sounds when you are very - I mean very - close to them. Animals do not emit a lot of sound if not none at all and again you must be almost directly on them to hear them. Fauna and flora feels silent and uncanny. Even water feel silent and emit no sounds. The soundtrack is very repetitive and become annoying fast. - The meteors storm system is so annoying. The camera shake during the storm, the sound is destroying your ear. Some meteor move so slowly in the sky and take so much time before ground impact it is so strange, and when it hit the ground it does only spawn a lot of rocks that will block you from harvesting the precious ressources the meteors bring so you will have to wait that the rocks magically disappear. - The base building is way too insufficient and poor, there's not much to do and you quickly discover everything to do. This do not encourage you to make good and well looking base. I dont understand why I can make such simple thing like tree pot only in the end game when base building do not interest me anymore. - The story is cliche, boring and the ending is soooo disappointing. Ending the game leave no feeling alike the one after finishing Subnautica. - The game is not well optimize. Mid to late game in my base I was dropping to 40-50 FPS while I was 100-120 in the wilderness. There was some bugs everywhere, props floating in the air, floor that overlap, hit boxes that make no sens, invisible walls, places where you can go threw walls of grounds, etc. I will stop there. But I could say a lot more. Please consider that this is an opinion review. It is personal, it is subjective. You could enjoy this game while I did not. After all, this game still as overwhelming review on steam. But me I was disappointed. I know that graphics and story do not make goods games and that gameplay is more important. But I do not feel that gameplay was really rewarding here. I did not see anything special about gameplay. I mean, after all it is just some king of clones of Subnautica. If you want my opinion, just grab Subnautica 1 and 2. Play No Man's Sky. Play Satisfactory. These are way more pleasant and immersive games in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: If you like survival base-building and exploring, you're going to enjoy this game. Been with it for a while and I enjoy myself immensely every time I open it! It's made by a small team that's still under 10 people as of 1.0 (congrats to the devs for the 1.0 release!) and I'm perpetually amazed at all they've achieved. Super stoked for all the new music and creatures and still delighted by watching the planet change around me. You can definitely lose track of time playing so take care!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the playstyle of Subnautica then youll like this. However this game doesn't have those OH SH!@# moments like Subnautica as the only thing you fight is the environment. They did a great job on having the game change over time as you terraform the planet, I wont give examples because you know spoilers. All in all this is a solid game well worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I can't believe this game has been created by a team of two people! Even in early access it looks very solid, the planet looks incredibly alive and full of character and there's so much stuff to do. I've always loved the mechanics of terraforming but I don't think there's a game that does it quite like The Planet Crafter. You get to experience the process in first person and it's happening at the right speed. If it were too fast, you'd get bored with the game too fast and if it were too slow, you wouldn't even reach any progress because you'd get annoyed by the grind. Watching the planet slowly turn green and fill with life is the most satisfying feeling ever.And don't even get me started on the base building, which is my natural habitat in any game. Some aspects of the building are a little rough, especially placing stuff and the need to have the resources in your inventory but it's still a lot of fun to play with. And the fact that you can build almost anywhere on the huge map is mindblowing.Yes, the map is huge and there's so much to explore. A lot of the places unlock only later on and you need to really plan your exploration but I really love that because it doses it at just the right amount without ovewhelming you or letting you discover everything too early and leave you without any purpose. 45 hours into the game and I still have a lot I want to do. I'm half-way to breathable atmosphere and I'm an avid tree spreader, so that's my current goal number one. And I can't wait to see animals! I'm really looking forward to whatever future updates bring as I'm sure I'm going to love anything this duo does!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Likes: This game had me coming back to see what opens up next. I like the base building and crafting. I like the hard to find hidden treasures and secrets. It does have a subnautica feel to it.  Dislikes:   I am now near what I believe is end game, and the forward process is so terribly slow at this point. Am I doing something wrong or was it designed this way?
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. Helping the planet come to life, watching the cascade of life you set in motion slowly start to work its way across the planet provided a sense of peace and awe that I haven't felt from a game in a long time. What a beautiful world in the end, and you get to watch your work trigger it all. It's a fun, accessible grind and the game does a good job of introducing you to mechanics and elements as you dive deeper in an organic fashion that leads you deeper on without feeling rushed or forced. There are some bugs, and a few issues with textures and boundaries but without going out of the way to find problems I had a mostly bug free experience. The world is still growing and updates are still coming. I look forward to seeing where the game goes from here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: The game is only in early access and already breath-taking. The way the planet transforms is beautiful and i am in awe every time i see a new part of nature arise on the planet, especially when the first butterflies start appearing in flocks and when nature burst open mountains to effectively unlock a new part of the map to explore.The only tiny thing the creators could work on is the way to find ores. it is a bit weird to just see small chunks of all basic ores lying around everywhere. And the rain looks like slime falling from the sky xDOther than that really beautiful and highly recommended! Worth every cent spent!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful survival and exploration simulator with a fair amount of mystery. The developers found a great balance, for me at least, between No Man's Sky and Subnautica. Planet Crafter is complex enough to keep things interesting and allow for replay, but simple enough to prevent frustration over learning how things work. Mechanics aside, this game made me gasp in awe *many* times. Give the demo a try!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Great game already (v0.4.7) currently in alpha. Already put 13 hours in this game + 4 in the demo. The game has a great atmosphere, understandable gameplay and is calming to play. I don't review that many games but in the game really deserves a good review. If you are not sure yet, try the demo to see if this game works for you. Keep it up!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 30 hours of play and still learning stuff - how the world changes as you terraform is pretty amazing. Crazy well developed for an EA game. Graphics are surprisingly good, movement and general game play is great, not too taxing (I imagine you could play this even if you don't have a nuclear-powered gaming rig). Lightning fast saves and loads, decent community support / guides available. Awesome fun, relaxing game with ridiculous potential - even if they never added anything else, it's fantastic as-is - everything beyond this will be bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: An early access title to look out for, which is Planet Crafter.So what is this game about?You are stranded on a hostile planet with one task. To make this planet habitable. But you are alone in a planet with no sign of life. There is no water, no breathable air, no food, no contact with anyone, there are sandstorms, there are meteor showers which makes you think “can one person do this?”But from picking up the first ore, everything in the game moves you in a path to shape this planet. To create a blue sky, to create cloud, to form rain, to create lake, to make an ecosystem.As you are better equipped, you slowly try to expand and explore this barren planet, to find what secrets it holds all the while finding more and more things, unlocking more and more base building, biomass, machine to produce oxygen, food, heat, pressure; everything you require to bring a change to this planet.This might make you think how this is stress free, this seems complex. But as I said, the motto is do it simple. The game takes inspiration from science but it doesn’t want to make it too complex that you won’t enjoy it. This has been said by the devs in their official roadmap.Everything the game does or provides is good, and it gets better and better the more you play it. You simply run to every location at first. Well, now you get t1 gear, which makes you faster. Then you get t2 gear, which makes you faster. Then t3. But what now? Now you get a different gear which makes you better at traversing. The game teaches so well and you rapidly become efficient at doing what needs to be done and you can see a visible change in the environment because of your action.But you may wish to play it with a friend. And good news for those wishing that because the devs have announced co-op mode for 2024. The game is also getting 1.0 release in 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I have kept my eye on this project for sometime and I am glad to say the game does not disappoint. Think Subnautica in space. The biomes, tools etc are approachable. While it is a bit bare-bones right now I am SO excited for what this game is going to become. Definitely a project I am behind with my money and well worth it IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's fun, but there aren't any enemies or other dangers around so you pretty much just run around collecting materials and wait for the next world tier. It feels like playing subnautica without any creatures. It's also really short. I believe I have done pretty much everything there is and its only been around 50 hours. I would say keep this in your wishlist for another a year or so.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

Now that 1.0 is out, it's gets even better.  So much more to explore and create and now you can do all that with your friends (And a bunch of them at that). Get it while it's good and never look back!  (Poor Xiaodan)
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

Love seeing the barren rock turning into a lush world all thanks to you hard work. Some glitches when trying to climb unclimable mountains with the jetpack. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

I like meteors hitting my face. or hitting those high mountains and drops clipping thru ground <.< . But other than that. There is lot of things to do. Building system is great, but sometimes its really annoying when it autolocks items. (mostly because I am trying to build my base top of some rock and autolock prevents me to place item lil bit higher than item next to it.) Hmm. What else.. There is good amount of exploration, lots of things to build, items and crafting recipes are simple to understand. This is really good game to be at Early Access. Can´t wait for more things to this. And animals. Even after you have done "everything" there is still even more things to do. Tho. It being just building whole map full of trees and stuff. And somehow still stumbling upon some lootable crates. Best thing in building stuff is that you can destroy them and get all materials back. And there is recycle device to reverse things even more. Except when trying to fly between gaps. Jetpack falls faster than just jumping without it. Sometimes it does glide. Sometimes its like rocketing to ground and hovers there. Lastly? _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: [EDIT: Expanded]Zen. Fun. Streamlined. No real story, no distractions, just nice progression and crafting. It doesn't look amazing, ground textures are low-res and repeat, but the gameplay is immensely satisfying, and that's what counts. The devs are communicative and consistent with updates which is another big plus for this project. A few things can be wonky, but based on their update history, I am assuming they will be fixed by 1.0. First, collision detection can be hit or miss. I spent time building a series of stairs to reach the top of a spire only to fall through. Fortunately, this has never gotten me stuck or soft-locked the game, but currently there is always a chance that where I'm about to go doesn't have collision. Second, there is only one type of platform you can build, it can't be turned to patch the terrain, and to build you must be a few awkward feet from where you want the platform to go because snapping is weird. Not to mention some terrain seems to be 'special' and can't be built on at all, such as surfaces that transition from sandy to rocky. There are some clear EA signs, but none of them got in the way of the game. Let me re-emphasize this: the game itself is relaxing and fun as hell. There are no enemies. There is no time limit (save your own oxygen supply). In fact, you could, theoretically, construct the bare minimum of basic terraforming devices and sit back and wait for the game to unlock progression. It would take forever, but you could do it. In other words, there isn't a 'right' or 'wrong' way to play the game. You don't have to guess what the developers were thinking about when they created it. You can just play. Go terraform.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Exploration & building game.Rather well done, addictive, though.   And the progression is slightly too fast early on, and slows down a lot.  There are small, but sometimes quite deadly bugs, I'm sure these will be fixed, though.  I just wish it had more than one save slot, I'm a bit scared.Overall, it's good fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: The full version is much bigger than the prologue in terms of unlockable features and map size. Overall if you enjoyed the prologue, the full version is still a lot more content on top of that. There is also a story that plays out in the messages found throughout the map. This game is kinda like subnautica but on a lonely dry planet which slowly becomes earth like. If you go through the different terraforming stages, the map automatically turns green with life, trees, plants, insects and lakes all come to life naturally. The sky also goes from red to blue. The transformations you create are amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: First I was hesitant... I tried the demo twice... the second time I got hooked,  bought the game and 3 hours past like 3 minutes! It's calm and relaxing. I love the fact that there is no rush, you got time (almost) to level up your base of operation. Nothing is gonna attack you. You're just here to teraform that planet!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend the game for its price of around 25$.. You start on a barren wasteland and step by step terraform it to a greener planet. This is its key selling point and quite impressive seeing this change. But the game feels a bit too like a late Early Access game at the moment. This game needs a progress improvement. And better graphics.Other aspects are lacking - the exploration seems interesting like in Subnautica - but in the end there is not really something. New resource, maybe a snippet of message, but the world feels empty. The graphics are ... okay at best and the quality fluctuates. Some textures are very low res and in general it is not a beautiful game. My problem is: The progression system is not really balanced. You don't have a steady progress and its get grindy after 10 hours (the time I stopped, I've just created moss) - even sometimes downtimes. The feeling to always expand the base is not there - I need way to many machines. More rockets? I've fired ca. 10-20 rockets but I've not unlocked the screen for it. I can build a tree spreader - without a tree seed? I get a message that rockets are important and mines are biome dependend - after I've build 10 rockets and multiple mines. Why? Also there is a way better movement system missing - vehicles or a better jet suite. Teleportation can be unlocked, but way toooooo late. The map is a bit buggy and there are many clipping and missing collisions. I could get under the map, avoid mountains. I hope the devs improve the game because the base idea is interesting and something else and it is cool to see the water rising and the world gets greener. I would like to reexperience this in a year or so with a better game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: long terraforming concept, one of the better ones ive seen, lots to do, lots to upgrade, its an actual pleasure to see the changes as you progress, like finding a new copse of trees, or herd of animals or school of fish in areas that you hadnt been to before. Very detailed. love the ability to use drones later on to manage your storage areas, takes out a lot of the tedium, you can literally create a box in the open and set the drones to collect everything and store it an suitable receptcle. The animal dna creation is great and highly recommend this and the DLC. quite a few bugs here and there, lots of clipping errors but that doesnt detract too much.  Would be more challenging with damage to structures from the constant meteors strikes, maybe have auto repair drone abilities but all good very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

There are secrets to find if you've the interest.  Looking forward to seeing more polish, or perhaps different world types (if there aren't already).  World is big enough to share with others. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

I just throw my favorite music on in the background and build my world!I would recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game is addictive.  It's easily the best game released this year.  Still in early access so it slows down a bit toward end play, but I'm excited to see what they produce.UPDATE:  So Planet Crafter is coming out of Early Access soon, and I for one can't wait.  There has been so much added since my last review, that I wish I had kept this review updated.Definitely an amazing game.  Every time I go back after an update, I'm amazed at how fun this game is. _childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games you always wanted, but no-one ever created. Looks like this little 2 person studio finally went and did it, thanks Miju Games. I love this game! Kind of like Subnautica with a beginning and end and a great story, but with The Planet Crafter, we see the changes going on all around. Just amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. This is one of the only games I've ever played that really captures the essence of being stranded on a barren planet. Returning to your pod/base moments before suffocation/starvation/terminal dehydration creates real tense scenes. The survival elements could use a tweak (I don't think I should need to eat and drink every 30 seconds to stay alive), but the experience is tense and challenging. That's good. Surviving and terraforming an otherwise inhospitable landscape doesn't sound easy! My favourite part though, is watching the world change, dynamically, around you as you play. You can sit there and watch sea levels rise, the sky turn blue or life return to the water. Sure, you'll die of thirst long before then, but one can dream! Fantastic game. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun survival/crafting game.  The game play loop is very satisfying, being able to explore and find different parts of the planet to terraform and upgrading your tech based on your terraform level.  Building/rebuilding/upgrading your base or even just moving it to a new spot altogether.  Have been completely obsessed with this game, putting over 70 hours into one save.  Don't want to say too much and spoil anything for new players, but if you enjoy exploration, crafting, and surviving the elements in games then this is definitely one I would recommend.  There might not be any monsters or animals to fight off, but there is so much else to keep you occupied and more is coming out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I have played to a certain point thus far.I have entered the water terraforming phase and now very slowly heading towards lakes.So, the basic gist thus far seems like you are a convict from some interstellar civilization. Your character, seems to have made a bargain that if you help terraform a planet that a specific corporation has deemed to be altered to become earth like, your sentence will be commuted and I suppose you will walk away as a free man (either to live on the new planet you terraformed) or who go back to earth I don't know.So, there isn't one specific way to go about terraforming the planet. They sky that was red was first changed to blue and then I was finally able to change the planet enough to form clouds.After that, rains began (periodically).And now moving towards lakes.Thing is, as you survive, (and at the start you really have to watch your oxygen in-take. You really need to make like ten oxygen canisters at the start of the game. As your tech improves, oxygen doesn't become as big as an issue (but it's always there).If you die on standard, you lose a bit of your stuff and you have to back and get it.You also have to watch your water and hunger but those aren't so bad on standard.I highly suggest you make that starter flashlight when you find wrecks (so far nothing dangerous inside); however it is very dark and the flashlight helps.Certain items you will want (like certain types of flowers) to grow to increase the oxygen on the planet. Certain flowers produce more oxygen than others.Eventually I think this is becoming a balancing act, as I don't think you want one parameter to go lightning fast past another. So far, the amount of oxygen being expelled on the planet is at a much faster rate than the amount of heat and pressure I'm increasing as well.Heat and pressure though at this point in my game is pretty close to one another, though it's funny that heat was very low for awhile next to my pressure and now the heat I am producing is at a slightly faster rate than the pressure I am generating as well.The music goes well with this game. It feels like you are all alone and just the mood is alien.Eventually, after a certain heat parameter has been met, certain ice in caves begins to melt. You can't do anything while the ice is blocking your way still but you should periodically check it out to see how it's melting. You also do not have to wait for a block of ice to completely melt before bypassing it and seeing what the ice was blocking. You will really want those materials later on.I have a fear though that I did not make my base high enough. You can't build on the rocks. My base still has a foundation but I have a growing fear that once I reach lake stage of this process, part or a good chunk of my base might end up underwater.Time will tell.This is where I am right now with it.In general it's okay.One con. It's not so much of a con, but just wanting this game to be better, exo planet real life science has come very far in twenty five plus years I think.There are a number of real life exoplanets that scientists are debating who habitable they are. Of course, we don't have the technology to get to these real life worlds, it's still fun to see what they think.So some of the real life exo planets under consideration that might be able to support some sort of life (are based on distance from sun, rocky world, etc.However, this measurement isn't completely accurate. So, for example. There is a real life planet that is orbiting a red dwarf star. Considering that red dwarf's are not as hot as our sun, a planet could be closer to this type of star and still be not too hot and not too cold to live on.However, that measurement doesn't also consider the fact, that though a red dwarf is not as hot as our sun, red dwarf's are also unstable. Meaning, that solar flares that are erratic are much more common on a red dwarf and when they do occur they can be much more powerful than the one's coming off our sun.That alone might make possible living on this planet orbiting such a star never really feasible.Lastly, another real life planet orbiting another system in our milky way galaxy (sorry forgot the name but it starts with a T) might be a super earth. An issue with a super earth is that because it's mass is so much bigger, that the gravity on this planet is basically double that of earth. It would mean that if one day humans actually lived on this planet orbiting this star system that starts with a T, everything would weigh twice as much as on earth.Furthermore landing on the planet would be fine but ever getting off the planet would probably be impossible as any rocket would require double the amount of energy that our present rockets that leave earth require.So what does this real life science space stuff have to do with this game?Well, the alien game world is suppose to be at least at the start) much more alien than earth.So maybe specific minerals (that are alien or certain other parameters that make this planet seem very alien) should be added at least at the start, before you really begin altering it to be more earth like.Like, maybe if this game world is bigger than earth, gravity should be an issue more so than earth and you need extra tech in addition to what you already have to move faster.Possibly specific alien minerals should be part of the landscape as well. Lastly, going back to real life exo-planet science for a moment. There have been thousands of exo planets that have now been confirmed to exist in our milky way galaxy alone. That doesn't even include the first planet they think they found in another real life galaxy that is not the milky way.Many of these worlds are very different from Earth and even the ones that are similar are somewhat different than earth as I explained already. Even worlds that are similar to other planets in our own solar system, like the many exo-planets similar to Jupiter (being a gas giant); means that planets can be created in many ways.Perhaps the title of this game then (since the goal is to create a new earth-like planet); should be changed to Earth Crafter (instead of Planet Crafter).

_childDocuments_.review: Some background: I was desperately looking for a game, I was let down by a considered-soaring classic and a crash-and-burn newcomer. I was suddenly caught in a desolate wasteland. Then I accidentally landed on this game. Approaching cautiously, I ventured forth into the unknown.This game hits every mark. It sends you into a sprawling dead landscape without hope of ever living to see beauty. You work, you learn, you discover. The game rewards you in the most subtle way. You slowly transform horror into bountiful wonder. You get to terraform a freakin’ planet! How could that not be fun?  Approach the elements with a balanced-eye and you will be rewarded.I eagerly await what updates come next. I celebrate (hopefully) the ability to eventually remove the helmet and bask in the hard work of achieving the unachievable. Can’t recommend this game enough.Some critique, at least as of September 2022. While the game is well balanced, once you understand the mechanics and the moderately sized landscape, the game can become much easier to approach. When you get into Hardcore mode, and the looming threat of a deleted save upon death, it reinstills the danger (I had a few very close calls). Some variety in maps or ideally procedurally generated maps can solve this. But, I have faith in what’s to come.Disclaimer: I’m a nasty, little, annoying Steam community member that never writes reviews. Just, all of the sudden, I got the urge to go on a reviewing binge. So, I am very, very, VERY late to the party on this game and many others, but I’m finding catharsis in getting my 2¢ out there. If you like it, thank you! If you don’t like it, I don’t really care. Love you just the same.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Soooo Planet Crafter....I was attracted to the game as I like this genre in general, but with the add familiarity of Subnautica on land.Game play so far as I'm just over 50% into the one of the higher end goals is pretty good. Various machinery  still need some work balancing and tweeks. It holds promise so far even though it is very unfinished and the end game doesn't seem to exist a tall currently. I  do love how you do see the impact of your progression as each milestone is reached.Personally I would like to see:• intro sequence that explains your predicament like a montage of being caught, sentenced, commuting sentence, training and finally bundled into a ship and launched.• More game lore which would make this sparkle even more.• Overall chart of total terraforming goals.• Voice logs and vocal alerts.• Gathering Drones and drone stations.• Ability to harness ship reactors.• Cutting through doors and bulkheads would be a great addition to exploring and salvaging wrecks.• Polar regions.• 2-4 person Co-op mode (done similarly like Icarus for hosting).• ship/satellite crashing instance.• Motivational device/monitor spouting positive cheesy and some what sarcastic phrases.• Turning plants into cloth.• A mini rover with cargo space and/or trailer (although the jetpack is fun).
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying crafter, make-number-go-up, automation style game. Clearly takes a lot of inspiration from Subnautica, but manages to be much more relaxed in vibe. The story is not as well executed as Subnautica though. It feels a bit more like an after thought, there if you want to engage with it, but easily ignored if you don't.It is a bit rough around the edges still, often literally. It's really easy to find yourself falling through the map, or behind/inside rock walls, especially after obtaining the jet pack. I'm not sure it functions as intended. Exploration feels relatively trivial fairly early. So long as you bring enough 02 with you, there is very little preventing you from travelling almost anywhere.The base building is lacking some polish and can be a bit frustrating if you have any sort of perfectionist/OCD streak in you. Nothing fits in a base rooms evenly, and many things cannot be centered. If you are a fan of the genre, it's definitely a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Showing just how good indie developers are and that you get much more bang for your buck than you do with AAA studios.This game has only gotten better since I bought it on day one and with the new DLC (Haven) it has reignited my interest and obsession in it.  The developers are very open to feedback and have consistently improved the game with every patch and the patches, unlike many other games, do not tend to introduce problems of their own.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing and satisfying after getting accustomed- the first bit can be rough.  But watching each attribute tick up as the world changes around you is mega cool and satisfying.  You can play this fast or slow.Music is on key- need more!The sparklies and shimmeriness of the environment is lovely.Simple (not bad) lore is fed to the player slowly as they explore.Inventory management is key for traveling far away from base, but you can grab a few resources and build a new base anywhere- beacons and all.Has tons of potential, so I'm looking forward to the game's growth and improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: PSA: DO NOT JUST BUILD YOUR BASE RIGHT NEXT TO THE STARTING POD. IT'S GOING TO BECOME A LAKE. YOU WILL BE FORCED TO MOVE EVERYTHING. This is a great game. Had a ton of fun with my friend doing co-op and we were able to focus on the things we both enjoyed the most in the game which complimented our progress very well. The base building is really fun, the exploration is fun, and seeing the planet slowly turn into a habitable place was very satisfying. Some things could have been done a little better, but I think that was more on us than the game itself. We pushed a little too hard on oxygen/heat/pressure so we had moments like unlocking tier 2 animal food before we had tier 1. It was really fun making a little paradise around our base full of bees/butterflies/animals/ecosystems. Be wary of the tier 3 tree spreader because placing 8 of them to take advantage of the tier 2 machine optimizers is going to turn that area into a rather dense forest. It's highly recommended you spread out your machines and biomass growers. At the end of the day you have full freedom to do almost anything you want, but again don't build all your stuff next to the starting pod or you will have to move it eventually. The portal generator was really cool. The environments the game generates were often beautiful. The ships themselves though made me feel claustrophobic. The latest patch notes said they made the ships less maze like so I can't even imagine what they were like beforehand when they were still extremely convoluted at times. The end game of being able to create your own animals was really cool, but you reach limitations with it pretty quick. There's not a ton of variation of species, just the colors/size you can make them. Overall it was a super chill and fun experience and I fully intend to play through it again at some point in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played for about 8 hours, but I can genuinely say this is one of the greatest survival/ base builder style games I have ever played. There is always more to do and upgrade, and it feels endlessly fun watching your planet slowly evolve and grow as you explore, upgrade your capabilities, and build bases and equipment. Definitely one of the best! I was even more blown away when I discovered this game only came out a few weeks ago at the time of writing this review. It feels fully refined - no glitches or any problems whatsoever as of right now. Highly Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game that has such a cozy survival mechanic. I've played for over 17 hours so far and feel like I've barely made a dent. I have so much of the planet still to explore and content to unlock. This is easily a game I'll probably sink close to 100 hours into if not more. The concept is pretty cool and it's so nice watching the planet go though the beautification process as it's terraformed. The minute I hit blue sky I knew I was going to be hooked! Beautiful game, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: So, simply said - I like it very much. It's absolutely worth the price and I can only say that the “demo” version has already got me hooked. I was able to get a good impression of the game, it has a great fun factor and you can really let off steam. The technology is no longer the “latest hot ♥♥♥♥” in terms of visuals BUT who really needs that? I'd rather have good gameplay with solid technology that doesn't stink x times than a great polished surface. Therefore, I don't regret the purchase, I would buy it again at any time - the only drawback is spending a few hours in the game and suddenly it's already “tomorrow” ;-) It has an addictive factor! :-)
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: It is super addicting, it progresses just so nicely. Having to bounce back and forth in the progression trees. It does get lonely, but there is the fun little drone buddies you unlock towards the endgame. Autocrafting and logistics is super fun. Exploration is a must. The world changes all the time. For example, the ice melting unlocking new caves, and the crater's middle which was piping red hot, turns into an oasis. Nice goodies to find in golden chests hidden around the map. No bad guys to worry about either, other than starvation, suffocation, and dehydration.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time ever that i comment on a game but i feel like this game is worth it. Even for someone like me who mostly plays FPS this game is lots of fun and even changed my opinion about a sandbox.  I have been playing it for a year but i have left the game for a while due to the fact that a year ago there was not that much to do, which is expected from an EA. However after the last update there is so much to do. In the past they have also always listened to the feedback from the community, improving the game even more.There used to be some Cons back in the day, however these are mostly fixed.* The first  one was balancing (mostly collecting resources) but I feel like with all the feedback, they got balancing right.* Some big rocks that where not meant to be climbed also had no hitboxes which meant u could fall through them and end    up being stuck, the issue is mostly fixed and since this is such a small part of the gameplay/ map its not really an issue.* I feel like the game is missing some more furniture to brighten up your home (honestly the only bad thing i can say about    the game).The Pro's: * The graphics look decent, they are a little cartoonish but i think this is great.* I have never seen the world around me change so much, this makes it even more fun to start terraforming.* U have a decent amount of building blocks to make a house to your liking.* The adventuring and searching for other (crash)landend survival pods and uncovering what has happened to the    planet are also fun and a great way to keep yourself entertained.* The difference between endgame loot and early game loot is big which makes you want to advance even more. However    I don't think the endgame loot is not balanced, i think it's right where it has to be (ofcourse after some time you will automate    everything but even that will give you something to do).* I have not encountered a lot of bugs in my 75 hour play time even tho this game is in EA, it feels like a complete and    polished game. If you are not sure if u want to buy it in EA, just go for it.So what is my overall opinion, This is one of the best games I've played in a while, ofcourse there are games that I have played more since playing PVP games gives you more variety since every game, even played on the same map is a different  experience (but ofcourse this is the opinion of a guy who likes to play PVP games and barely plays any single player games). I have read that some discord moderators are not nice to people but honestly there is an ingame button to give feedback about a bug and there is plenty of information on the internet if u have a question so don't let that scare you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game. Started on hardcore. Ran around collecting all the iron and built a nice big house. Followed the starting checklist and built some TVs. Ran around and found some seeds in a chest. Pretty neat. Checked my TV to find out how to build the plant grower. Ran out of food and starved to death because I spent to much time building a big house.Next game, small house, find things fast, gotta live. Build heaters, find golden chest w/ golden dildo inside. Noice. Position golden dildo so it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the heater. Ez. Build plant growers. Don't have seeds. Contemplate building flashlight. Nah, waste of resources. Find wreck. Go back and build flashlight. Find seeds in wreck! Sky turns blue on my walk back from the wreck with my seeds. Yay atmosphere! Got almost enough food to survive now and another wreck to scavenge. Fun game.Edit: And 30 some odd hours later I have 100% completed the game. Late game does get a bit boring, as you eventually build a breatheable atmosphere and then it just becomes rinse and repeat of optimizing your process for building the same ♥♥♥♥. So, rather sandboxy endgame as of now. Could use a bit more balancing in some areas. Could really use a better jetpack sound too cuz that ♥♥♥♥ is annoying after hours of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: Planet Crafter is a 9/10 gaming experience for me. It's probably the first game in a decade that I've bought immediately after finishing the demo, I was hooked and needed to see more. In roughly 30 hours I completed what is currently available in the game and plan to return as more becomes available.The only 'complaint' I had personally is that the information (or lack thereof) about progressing your terraforming can get confusing towards the later (current) stages. Finding a good balance (and learning that rockets stack) took some online research, but once I knew what to do I could quickly farm up the correct resources and set myself up to unlock the final items.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very enjoyable game even in Early Access. Fun building systems, good survival gameplay, and even an interesting story.Maybe my favorite thing about this game that sets Planet Crafter apart from a lot of space survival games is that the planet changes as you play. Usually games of this type just concentrate on surviving the hostile environment and its entirely about resource management.I've been looking for a space game that made me feel like a real terraformer for a while now and PC really scratched that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: You are a Prisoner, sent to a alomst dead Planet and your Job is to habitable the Planet for the human race. How do you do that? You have several key tasks you have to improve, like oxygen, air pressure and heat. You Gather resources, built equipment and maschines, find new recipes and more and more you play, your almost dead planet, starts to regroth and empty deserts change to lakes and forests.There are several ship wrecks, caves and secreat bunkers to explore. Right now, there are not any living creatures, friendly or enemys, in the game. Might be changed in the future. Right now, you have 0 Weapons. That means you can built peaceful your base, gather resources and make progress to heal you Planet. The map is really big, but because its just in early access, there are a lot of empty space right now. But, the game is still in development, so they can add more and more stuff in the future.Before i bought the game, i played the Beta for 4 HOURS. But i bought the game right after it. So far i had not really any Bugs, besides that you can fly through some rocks because the killosion is still missing in some places.Overall, the game is really fun and i hope to see more updates in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches an itch. You discover this to discover that to discover the other thing. The resources are not too hard to find and if you pay attention to the clues given you can easily accomplish the required items and stats to keep advancing.Not too many bugs, I only got stuck once and there is an unstuck in the main menu. Once you advance a bit it is possible to go through the map in certain areas, but the game is early access.All in all it is a fun game and I did enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I really enjoyed that one, the progression of the terraforming was really enjoyable, it takes time at first then like a snowball effect it become faster and faster, allowing you to not get bored about it, each stage of the progression having it's own unique content, and even if the game seems empty at first there is really alot of it to discover the further the go.For the bad sides there is a few but not that impactful, the biggest in my opinion is the lack of replayability, I really enjoyed playing once, but it's the kind of game which doesn't even bring the least desire to play a second time, not because it's bad or anything, but just that after playing it once you probably won't feel like there is anything more to see, there is a lack of variability in the game playthrough, you could say the end game portal with random crashsite try to change that, but you'll get bored of it sooner of later, another point if the limited impact you have on the ecosystem you build, after building the few machine you need to raise parameters you can totally just wait for it to progress (although that would be pretty dumb and boring xD) and get the same result as if playing like you're supposed to, making it a bit unrewarding on that point (and as a total opposite I remember in the last stages there was even a time everything progressed so quickly I didn't even manage to fully enjoy that stage and I was already at the next ) also the fact that you can rise indefinitely the parameters is weird, it would be better to have objectives to maintain, with a way to get them down too, not only rising, that way you could totally have a few different results of terraforming (like a fail, success, and perfect success for example, add a disaster level fail for even more fun xD)In conclusion, it's quite a good game to play once, but I still feel this game could be a lot more better, to be honest it's quite rare for me to think that a game have such potential not exploited but still enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's relaxing and just plain fun to play. I also love the progression of the world changing around you. I never really could get into No Man's Sky, but this game's terraforming gameplay is lots of fun. Another thing, the developers are making constant updates. _childDocuments_.review: I think I'm going to drop this game, because it's just addictive in a vapid sort of way, and I don't feel like there's more to discover beneath the surface.  Terraforming is a neat idea, but you mostly just run around to get parts to build stuff to make the numbers go up.  Once the numbers go up enough, you get different stuff that makes the numbers go up even faster.  Rinse and repeat.Sure, the numbers represent terraforming, but really you're just playing a first person IDLE GAME.  That requires more attention.I dunno, maybe it gets better later but I'm doubting it's worth the time investment.  Wish I'd realized earlier and refunded.  If I'm gonna get addicted to a game it should be something like Factorio or Satisfactory with more on offer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically like these survival/building games, but this is a good one. I'm 28 hours in and just about to unlock the bug stage of terraformation, which means I have a bunch of gameplay still ahead of me and I am having a blast.For anyone even looking at this game, at least download the demo. I played like 4 and a half hours just on the demo before it cut me off when I hit a milestone and asked me if I wanted to buy the game. In my experience, most demos are like 15 minutes long; this was 4 hours of pure, free, fun game play. And once you hit that milestone in the demo, you can either say "nope" and uninstall, or decide to buy the game. And this is what's cool is if you buy the game, you get to keep your save file and just continue. No need to make a new game. Just keep going. I haven't tried multiplayer but I imagine that can be fun if that's up your alley as well.But yeah, it's a fun mining, building, survival, terraforming game that I just like to play casually to have fun while I relax. Definitely recommending it for anyone on the fence.
_childDocuments_.name: The Planet Crafter

_childDocuments_.review: This probably was the best invested money in an EA title in quite a while. I thoroughly enjoyed this game so far and still do come back with every major update. Particularly for an EA title I like the fact, that I don't have to start the game from scratch, world updates are integrated into the current game. I don't understand why others can't do that as well. The game is quite enjoyable, it's one of these... "oooooh, what's there"-games where you want to find all little corners and see what's behind the next rock. It can get quite tough sometimes, but not frustratingly tough.There are quite a few graphical glitches, here and there rocks that are see-through or resources mid-air, but little things, no major fun killer. Particularly as you get a jet pack at some point, you will be able to reach places, which you are probably not meant to reach and therefore you'll come across graphical glitches a bit more often - obviously, since you're not meant to be there. :DGenerally I highly recommend this game. I wished it had a bit more lore, the currently implemented lore is curious and interesting, but not sure it's quite there. Technically it doesn't need lore, it's a nice bonus to have. Also... I think the "ancient" buildings and the "sci-fi" lore are not quite... compatible. But again... it's a nice bonus to have.I wished there'd be more inventory space. There is so much to discover and yet I have to run there 20x because there are so many items to find and take back. But that's just my high-level moaning.Learning curve (read: survival curve) is quite steep (and difficult) and it gets quite easy once you have established the basics (water and air) and it feels a bit too easy then (I don't want to say boring, though that might be more applicable). So maybe a bit more end-game stuff would be good. Otherwise it's a really nice "watch the fruition of your efforts" game. I thoroughly enjoy(ed) this. Thank you.
