_childDocuments_.review: First off i have 4,000-4,500 hours of in game time; all my screenshots on steam are from gw2 (barring like the first 5 or so) so you can check the date i took those are proof if you want.Guild Wars 2 is a mmo i always find myself coming back to, but lets address the elephant in the room..is gw2 pay2win?No, there is nothing in the in game store that will increase your dps, healing or sturdiness over other players in pvp or pve. What gw2 does have is pay for convenience though in my opinion its minor and can easily be played without. Now what do i mean by convenience? There's unbreakable gathering tools, otherwise you will have to buy new ones, not really an issue as they are cheap. And there's unbreakable salvage kits, same as above but these do in fact cost in game currency to use. Barring those that's the only "pay2win" that you can say the shop has and even that is reaching. You can REALLY reach and say the expansions allow you to access subclasses for each class and they tend to be better than the core classes but what game does not have some kinda class tied to an expansion? Being this is a f2p game it does have a lootbox system, though in my opinion its not really worth doing for a handful of materials and the tiny chance of a resource node for your house. You can exchange the premium currency for in-game gold and in-game gold for premium currency, so that's good.The classes are very different from one another, no two classes are alike and on top of that with each expansion introduced a subclass you can equip for each class, so that is 3 for each class that will drastically change how your class plays.The combat feels good BUT its not for everyone i suppose, it feels juicy and heavy, it is not tab targetting so do with that info what you will.Mounts, what can i say? they are the best out of any mmo, each one is unique and has its own use; it's not just a mere speed boost each mount has it's own unique ability..be it swimming or jumping really high.Next i will talk about pvp and i will not lie to you its not easy to get into, you will get your butt handed to you, but if you keep trying i'm sure you will be the one doing the butt kicking; my experience in pvp is shallow so that's all i can really say.pve is good, no other mmo that i have played be it eso or ff14 have i seen where an entire map is required to coordinate to beat that map's specific map meta event and then work together to kill a map boss.Story is a mixed bag. Core story is good..ignoring one part, the vets will know what part i mean, season 1 is pretty good for what it is, season 2 is alright, a little stale but its not bad, heart of thorns is pretty good but you can see some cut content if you look hard enough, season 3 is good, path of fire is good, season 4 is my personal favorite, icebrodd saga had the potential to be great but they REALLY messed up towards the end, they obviously diverted resources to the next expansion, and finally end of dragons it was alright. As you can see its a mixed bag, nothing special but not that bad either.My main complaint lies that new fractals(dungeons) and raids do not come out nearly as often, i mean its been over a year or so since the last new one; they are releasing strikes (semi raids) i suppose but that's not enough. My other complaint is the team is at times, ever since gw2 was released the prey of mismanagement and just questionable choices be that the mass lay offs or the pathetic marketing this game has. Oh and no options to tune down other players visual effects. Icebrood saga really makes me mad too, such potential.Last one might not make sense to new people but wheres my new super adventure box world? we want it, just do it.That is all, thank you for reading and have a nice day.

_childDocuments_.review: To note, I have played this game since it's beta and release back in 2012. I've put in over 8,000 hours and played relatively consistently. I played Guild Wars 1 since 2006 or so--not sure how much I put into that, but likely A Lot. To state that I love this game is...putting it mildly. This game, the art, the community, and more have pulled me through some rough times. I wouldn't be the artist and creator if it weren't for Guild Wars, if I may be incredibly cheesy.That being said, I know I'm clearly biased. I'm not a hardcore gamer or meta by any means. I am also aware of many flaws, letdowns, and changes. So you might have to take this review with a grain of salt compared to others. Personally, yes, I recommend this game! I've been able to tempt friends to join us, and so far, they all have enjoyed it. Of course, I recommend finding some friends to play with, but it's also doable if you are often a hermit in MMOs like me.The game is not what we all thought it would turn out to be ten years later, but it is not wholly a bad thing after they did layoffs a few years ago (which sucks). Better quality of life updates, more interactions with the player base, roadmaps, and more. That has been incredibly helpful and a boon. They are adding in Season 1 finally, and as I said--the quality of life updates! Those are sometimes more important than new content, IMO.End of Dragons has been a fantastic expansion and worth the decade's wait. Still, I can be pretty picky about the story (I'm so bummed about Icebrood Saga! It had so much potential!). Still, the official characters are unique and memorable. Customization for our characters is a bit dated now to other MMOs. BUT I still argue you can't get better than glowing plants and fluffy military cats. I even enjoy the human race in this game, thanks to GW1, they have a  good fleshed out story! The game still has a fantastical and stylistic style that has aged reasonably well.Personally, I would love to see an update toward that, improving graphics, better textures, etc.  The engine itself is a heavily modified one from GW1, and it demands to step on your poor CPU.If you have played this before and now have moved on, that's valid. A lot has gone down and changed, and I won't argue on that point. But still, give the game a solid try. The art direction, races, ambiance, and much more are very satisfying. I can't comment much on factors such as professions and specific gameplay. I don't raid, and I often choose to enjoy experimenting and messing with builds than following meta. I honestly have low standards, bluntly. Life is short, if the game is fun, then that's enough for me, otherwise I do my best to be proactive if it's important enough. But I've been in the game developer industry, making and maintaining games are HARD. Try to have some patience as they work on improving it as best they can with what they have (ngl NCSoft probably breathes down their neck a lot)I'm more of a person who wants to roleplay, devour lore, explore characters, get distracted by shiny things, and exploring. It's inviting to get into if you're an artsy-fartsy, roleplayer, LGBTQ+, or even just absolute trash casual like me. No subscription service, but buying the game+expansions is worth it. It's a good MMO to pick up and drop off any time and doesn't feel pressured to keep up.I'm not sure if this review was helpful for anyone. Again, I'm inclined to tell you to try out the game. But I also have been incredibly involved with the community, have worked on fan projects, and the like. The love of the game is based on a lot of deeper factors. If you're similar to me, then you'll likely love it! But again, I do feel why some have mixed or negative feelings.But at the end of the day, my brain thinks, "sylvari glow brain go brrrr!!!", "I would die for Gorrik", and "FASHION WARS IS END GAME."Cheers! Feel free to reach out and bug me if you need help, advice, or simply just a buddy to enjoy the game with.(dangit i wanted to post the review at 69 hours, RIP)EDIT: I completely forgot to mention! It runs well on my steamdeck! A bit lower graphic settings than my PC rig, but it's such a good feeling to lazily play in bed (super great for those who are chronically ill/disabled, don't have a gaming PC). It's maybe crashed...once or twice? But frames are smooth. If you're playing directly with the actual steamdeck controls, then it may take awhile for you to find an ideal keymap. Look to FFXIV for inspiration or there are some great options done by the community. Might be worth setting up a small bluetooth keyboard for easier communication. But thumbs up here!

_childDocuments_.review: I have 3,380 hours in this game. I have many things to say, but the crux of it is: Try the game for yourself and see if you like it. There's a mountain of good content without buying expansions. You don't need them to have fun, but they add endless hours of content. Whether you enjoy playing alone or with friends, if you prefer the levelling experience or the endgame, if you like challenging content or just taking it easy, if you enjoy fashion or just want to grind our raids, this game has a little something for everyone.Guild Wars 2 isn't exaggerating when it advertises itself as the MMORPG that literally changed the MMORPG industry. You can draw a sharp line between "old"-style and "new"-style MMOs, and Guild Wars 2 is that line. SWTOR started to tiptoe away from the classic way that games like WoW and LotRO were designed, but Guild Wars 2 completely did its own thing as though no other MMORPG had ever existed. Since then, every MMORPG has in some way been inspired by GW2 (and even a certain older MMORPG that's trying to hold its sub base).My only major gripes are with the way it was integrated into Steam. I can't link my existing account to Steam, and that launching through Steam brings up the game's launcher, but doesn't let me log into my own account.With over 3k hours played, I have plenty of nitpicks and some major issues, but ultimately, the game is fun and I strongly recommend it. It's not the greatest game ever made, but I would say it's one of the best MMORPGs ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably one of the most hardcore players on this game. I have been playing for 10 years and I have around 25k hours count on my account so this is not a new player review.With this being said I'm not going to lie and sell you the game as a perfect game.I'm realistic it have a lot of issues, but most of these (if not all of them) are only relevant for a really long time veteran player, because we somehow demand more stuff and faster than the developers can deliver, so don't take that too seriously,it's just a very passionate group of people that just want more and more. Arenanet management has been a huge problem for years mostly by choosing the wrong priorities. But things seems better now and the release here on Steam is proof of that.For you if you are starting now, damn I envy you. You are blessed, you have YEARS of content ahead, there is legit so much stuff to do, FUN stuff and actually always relevant because veterans like me are everywhere around still enjoying the same stuff because its FUN.I make guides and content to help people because me and many other people in the community actually love to help each other. The community is nice but you still can find some bad apples, like everywhere, it's not perfect so don't believe that.The game offers a lot of things to do but sadly it fails on communicating these to the player and due to how immense the variety of stuff to do is, most players get lost or don't even have the chance to experiment the different options, so make sure to not underestimate the game by your very first experience.This is mainly because the game have horizontal progression, you can do stuff when you want and how you want, so you have to set your own goals.The game values your time and your freedom, you aren't being told or forced to do something. _childDocuments_.review: I've played countless MMOs, but GW2 is the only one that I keep coming back to. It is one of the few MMOs with a horizontal progression system. This means that the level cap has stayed at 80 and ascended/legendary gear is still the best after 10+ years. I played heavily when GW2 launched in 2012 and then took a 6 year break. When I returned, my level 80 characters were still geared for most content in the game. GW2 is the only MMO where taking an extended break doesn't punish you and invalidate your progress.So what is the point of playing? First of all, fully gearing a character still takes time, especially when playing multiple builds and classes. Secondly, there is no shortage of goals to grind for (it is an MMORPG after all). The goals simply aren't all tied to character power like vertical progression games. Lastly, the answer depends on the player because GW2 caters to so many different audiences. Some of my favorites are listed below.With 5 playable races, 5 Living World seasons, 4 expansions, and more to come, GW2 truly has a decade of content. Almost all of it is fully voice acted including minor NPCs. The quality of the story varies but is good overall. The Personal Story (base game) and Icebrood Saga (LW season 5) are lackluster in my opinion. Everything else ranges from good to amazing. LW season 4 in particular was an absolute joy to experience for the first time.Each race has a wealth of history to discover. The Sylvari (plant people) are my favorite. Their aesthetics are very creative, and they have the curious perspective of only existing for ~35 years in the game's timeline. Every race has a dedicated male and female voice actor which keeps things fresh when playing through the story as a different race or gender. There are also plenty of non-playable races with their own lore and culture such as the Tengu (bird people), Kodan (polar bear people), Choya (cactus rascals), Skritt (rat-like hivemind), etc.GW2 makes exploration feel natural. It is very fun to explore a zone for the first time. Every zone is filled with discoverable points of interest and dynamic events. Many zones also have jumping puzzles and meta events that can span the entire map. Transitioning between these activities is seamless and usually lead to undiscovered portions of the map. Level scaling, achievements, and meta events mean that zones stay populated beyond leveling.The dynamic/meta events are top notch game design. If there are players doing an event, you can simply follow them. You don't have to worry about picking up a quest, backtracking to turn it in, or forming parties (though you can if you want). All you have to do is participate to receive credit. This makes it incredibly easy to aid other players you come across, and has helped foster GW2's notoriously friendly community. One example of this is world bosses. These are massive bosses that spawn in specific zones on a timer. There are usually a few Commanders ready and waiting to lead 50+ people to kill the boss, and anyone in the area can join in. Stumbling across a swarm of players attacking a world boss while leveling really captures the "massively multiplayer" in MMO.How will you show off to your friends without an endless supply of equipment with bigger numbers? By styling on them with superior fashion sense of course! GW2 has an insane amount of skins to collect. Once unlocked, skins are available in the account-wide wardrobe forever. The only cost to reskin an item is a Transmutation Charge which can be obtained in game or bought with real money. I've never bought a single one and have more than I can use. If you're up for the grind, one of the perks of legendary items is that they can be reskinned for free. Unfortunately, many cosmetics are gem store exclusive (real money), but that is a trade off of a non-subscription MMO. However, you can farm gold and exchange it for gems in-game, and many skins are tradable on the auction house. Additionally, there are lots of cool skins that can only be acquired through gameplay.But wait, there's more! There are also account-wide unlockable dyes. Changing dyes is unlimited and completely free, so swap colors as much as you like. There are currently 636 dyes in the game that range from basic colors to dyes with special effects such as a vibrant glow or metallic finish. With the exception of weapons, most skins are dyeable including mounts. Many skins have multiple dye channels which greatly expands customization. To my knowledge, every dye is purchasable on the auction house, even ones bought from the gem store (although those can get pricey). Dyes can also be obtained through gameplay, crafting, and birthday gifts.The community has created some excellent "cosplays". Whether you want to be a cute, pink princess, a battle-hardened war veteran, or a gloomy goth, it's all possible. I've even seen a shockingly accurate Optimus Prime out in the wild.The main format of "Structured PvP" is Conquest, a 5v5 capture point mode. Shorter 2v2 and 3v3 deathmatch leagues are run between Conquest leagues. All equipment is standardized and skills are balanced separately to PvE and WvW. Characters are set to level 80 which means a new character can jump straight into PvP! The only exception is elite specializations which are locked behind expansions.The combat in GW2 is so satisfying. It is action combat oriented with dodging and a little tab targeting thrown in. What makes it work so well is that there aren't any global cooldowns and most skills can be used while moving. Every class has its own identity and multiple playstyles. All of this results in fast paced, fluid combat that is engaging and fun to learn.Unfortunately, PvP has been neglected and only receives balance patches every few months. It desperately needs new content or refreshed rewards. I and many others continue to play PvP because we genuinely find it fun. The combat is just that good.WvW combines the best parts of GW2. It is a 24/7 territorial siege between three "worlds" (3 gigantic teams) with PvE and PvP objectives across multiple maps. There can be hundreds of players battling over control of a keep, roaming groups looking for skirmishes, and even solo players sneaking around flipping camps. Playing WvW with a good Commander is some of the most fun I've ever had in any game. There are plenty of Commanders who lead public groups as well as dedicated WvW guilds. It's also great to play casually with friends. Even getting steamrolled by a massive enemy zerg can be fun. To top it off, WvW has good rewards and loot drops like candy in battles. The only downside is that maps fill up quickly during peak hours and can feel dead other times since WvW never ends. GW2 has the BEST mounts of any game. They aren't just designed to get from point A to B. Each mount feels like a living animal and behaves differently. There's nothing quite like sky diving on a Griffon or drifting on a Roller Beetle. ArenaNet lumps anything from small easter eggs to epic quest lines in the achievements. Many of GW2's best goals and rewards are buried here. If you're unsure of what to do next, make sure to dig through the achievements. A guild hall is a huge time and gold sink, but it has many benefits and can be decorated. It is even possible to make Roller Beetle racing tracks. Gradually upgrading a guild is perfect for a group of friends. There are 6 annual festivals for various occasions. They have special rewards and are an easy way to farm gold. These instanced encounters are the hardest PvE content in GW2. The tiered progression of fractals is simple to get started with.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 10k hours of play in 9 years, I can say that GW2 is one of the best MMO's. Of course, every MMO has its own charm. GW is a great game for free to play for free-to-play players and also for players who have bought at least one expansion. It offers an incredible amount of content, but you are not forced to invest money, because there is no pay-to-win.First of all, I would like to address some of the criticisms of other players:- GW2 offers hundreds of hours of play for free. All ingame purchases are pay-for-convinience or cosmetics.- With the Steam offer (99,97€ for all expansions+Living Story) you save a lot, even if it is a big investment at first sight (but remember: the game offers more than enough content for free).- Hundreds of hours of gameplay, in different content (story, open world, instanced content, pvp, large scale pvp and much more).- Story: extensive and full of achievements that could be done- Massive open-world: dynamically appearing events (comparable to FF:XIV Fates), huge world bosses, group events, jumping puzzles, other puzzles...- Character: races don't matter... just play what you like. The level cap is at level 80 and there is no item spiral. Also, endgame items are account-wide usable and can be dragged to other chars. Every class has 3 specializations which are available with the expansions. These specializations can change the playstyle of the class completely.- Mounts via Path of Fire: GW has a unique mount system where each mount has its own way of moving around with different advantages. With the EoD expansion, ships (skiffs) are now also available.- Community: So far I have not found a nicer community in any game. The players are incredibly helpful... and if you want to become a part of it, there are also many guilds you can join. Of course there are players who are not friendly, but you can find them in every game :D- Balancing and developers: Currently ArenaNet communicates a lot with the community and responds to feedback on changes early on. In the past, there were wrong decisions, like in every other game, but these were quickly reconsidered and changed. - At first glance, the game may not be very beginner-friendly. If you have questions, you can simply ask other players. - Free-to-play players have a few restrictions, e.g. regarding trading, whisper chat, etc.Check out the game free to play and if you like it you can at least buy HoT and PoF expansions to have access to more endgame content. It also removes restrictions on chat and trading.Enjoy the game <3

_childDocuments_.review: I can't speak to PVP or general group stuff since it isn't in my immediate interest to do those so at the moment I'll rate it as an RPG. MMOs aren't generally my bag but I will keep in mind MMO standards and base my rating off of that. I'm playing as a mesmer and I'm not very good with this class but sunk cost fallacy etc.I think this is a fun game, the visual design is nice, the story so far is pretty nicely done, and there is /some/ amount of quest variety (which in an mmo is to be commended). Mobs all look pretty different, and actually have attack patterns where you have to pay attention (this is partially due to the dynamic scaling, which I'll get to) and bosses actually feel like more than damage sponges and have proper gimmicks and phases. There is crafting and, I have barely done it, I gained some levels to fulfill some achievements, but I haven't delved in to check what it does. I don't think the systems themselves are complex but they are kind of all introduced all at once with little explanation and require you to go out and do content for materials anyways so I plan on grinding that out after another couple hours of material collection. Now I'll talk about the monetization which is generally why I avoid the genre. The monetization is there, you can buy progress, there are a ton of convenience items, but I think the game feels good to play without that. Progress isn't meaningfully difficult, I'm already level 50 at 15 hours (although this is with a +50 percent boon from an event, so multiply the time by 1.5) and you can do a lot of content regardless of level. I have already fought a level 80 rift boss and won (it had mechanics, and I had to collaborate with people who just happened to be nearby, which ruled.) In a single player game, I would find this kind of monetization unforgivable, but I'm going to have to put aside my bias since this is bog standard mmo monetization. The short of it is, so far, to me, I haven't been overly compelled to buy cash shop items. I was compelled and did buy the expansions, they were 7.50 usd at time of purchase and gave me a mount, which is a major convenience item. You may also be compelled to buy more item or bank space but I would bite the bullet and sell or break down all the stuff you don't need on your first playthrough since you unlock a whole new tier of equipment at level 80 anyways. In addition to all that there are additional benefits to becoming a paying owner such as access to sales on the black lion trading post which you basically need if you want to get enough money to earn gems as far as I can tell. I consider the double expansion bundle more or less required for that alone, not even to speak to the new content or specializations, which fundamentally change the classes. The game has a neat system where you will always be making progress, because you will scale down to enemies in your zone. You will still generally always outclass a lower level player with your additional attacks and benefits, but it at least makes it so you can't sweep the whole map to ruin their grind, and allows enemies to actually consistently be threatening if you aren't paying attention. Overall, recommended to pass time. It's been a decent action game to play solo to the point I may actually be interested in the group content, and most people seem friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of my favorite games, hands down. I have over a thousand hours in it in the non-steam client. I'm on free to play for steamdeck right now, and I love it. The combination of a dodge button with big combat that's well telegraphed, in addition to tab targetting, means you can play it as an action rpg or a traditional tab targetted MMO. The free to play portion, "vanilla" if you're coming from WoW, has a pretty decent story, and by the current expansion the story is amazing. I really cared about all the characters as we progressed through the new maps together. If you're a mostly friends player, there's both tiny dungeons that get harder, ala tower of judgement, and raids, and mini raids, depending on how serious you want to be. There's also quite a lot of group-with-strangers content in the open world, and they've done a great job of making it challenging without feeling unfair.As far as class difficulty goes, there's a big range of skill floors and ceilings. There's "piano classes" (that I love) where you're throwing down fire fields and exploding earth spheres inside them while you guarentee crits, there's simple builds where you just use a couple of skills off cooldown, and there's everything in between. My personal favorite is the Elementalist, so I can feel like Aang as I ride the wind and chill enemies witih water. Mesmer is also really intersting, summoning illusions that mostly only last until they get hit a couple times, but look the same as you.If your goal is Fashion Wars this game gives you a huge toolbox of dyes and skins that you use to outfit your character as you see fit.  I think the steam client is superior to the main client, just because it gives you the same ability to get into your locked account.

_childDocuments_.review: -Less of a superfan review, with a couple months of playtime-Neither pro, nor con: Not a new game.This is a 10 year old game. You shouldn't expect anything groundbreaking or revolutionary. But with that said, it still holds up. It is stable, most of the bugs have been ironed out throughout the years, so on that front you should be safe.PRO: CommunityI played a few online games and I have to say that GW2 has some of the best players that I have met. You can always expect to find helpful people around you, no matter your struggle.I do think that the devs are to thank for this, because the game seems to be designed in a way that rewards helping each other and if you play greedy you will not get any advantage, you will just be rude.CON: Storage/lootThe game showers you in loot, sometimes in very obnoxious ways. You can get lootbags that look identical but will not stack. This combined with the very limited storage at your disposal causes annoyance. This is one of the places where the game really feels like it pushes you towards microtransactions, to buy more bag and/or bank spaces.PRO: Material storageIt must be said, though, that it is very handy that crafting materials have separate storage, into which you can easily deposit your freshly gathered stuff, with a simple button click. But here again it won't be long until you feel how limited it is. (You get one stackful of space for every mat, which you can expand with gems, seven times.)CON: Story, writingThe story in the basegame is so simplistic and black and white that it is almost unbearable for people who are sensitive to this. It gets somewhat better in the expansions, but don't expect big twists or GoT levels of political intrigue. Every character is either a hero or a villain, and that doesn't really change. Character development is minimal. At least as far as I noticed, and I've almost reached the last expansionPRO: Horizontal progressionIt is very nice not to worry about gear as much. It is not very difficult to gear up a character in ascended gear, no matter how you choose to play. With that you are ready to anything the game can offer, and you are free to do whatever you want.CON: Low downtimeI know most reviewers put this as a Pro, but for me it isn't one. The fact that there's always something going on and everything is on a timeline (even if it is repeating) introduces a bit of stress. A feeling that if I do 'A', I will miss out on 'B', 'C', 'D'..... especially if you only have like an hour or two every day. And this gets worse as you go through the game because with every expansion there is more to do. For some people this might not be a problem, but for me it definitely is, no matter how hard I try to let go of the playaholic in my brain.CON: Living WorldLiving World are the name for the stories between the expansions and they are not included in either the game or the expansions, so if you want to know how our heroes got from A to B between the stories you will have to pay some real world money or quite a bit of gold.Though I have to say that these, plus the storage expansions are the only stuff you will really want to buy and are only available with gems, which are the microtransaction currency. And maybe the unbreakable gathering tools, which is more of a convenience upgrade but it is really annoying for your tool to break in the middle of a zone (or even worse, to have to carry multiple tools, when you already have so limited space.)With all that said, I'd recommend it, especially to try the basegame. Why not? It's free. If it's not your cup of tea, the most you'll lose is a couple of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing a little at the original launch in 2012 and being disappointed with the PvE endgame, I stopped playing. Back then the game was fine if you enjoyed PvP (and WvWvW) but for me, farming dungeons and events was a little dull, coming from raiding in WoW.Fast forward 9.5 years and I was in the mood for a decent RPG. The ship had sailed for WoW, I was tired of the constant grind when coming back to the game every year or two after leaving with amazing gear, and once friends stop playing, it's either find others to play with or farm old content that nobody is playing. I log back in to GW2 and what do you know, my character is still reasonably relevant! Sure, new gear stats had been added, we now have Ascended items to go for, and loads of legendaries but I could pick up from where I left off and continue the story without a single thing to grind. No new levels to grind out, no rep grind, no grinding dungeons for hours for new gear, just log in and go. As of now it's been six months since I started again, just over 1000 hours played in that time before Steam release and I'm still not tired of playing. Every area in the game has people doing their own thing every evening, world events constantly happening and packed with players, Fractals, Strikes, Raids... even World vs World (vs World) is popular and really fun in a group. I can't see myself playing anything much else for the next couple thousand hours of gaming time. In comparison to other MMOs on the market it's an incredible value for money.

_childDocuments_.review: I have far more hours on this than is showing on steam. Guild wars 2 for me is THE MMORPG over other big names like WoW, i'll only briefly give a couple reasons but feel free to comment and ask for more info should you want it.Graphics: While being quite and old game at this point its still gorgeous as long as you have the computer to handle being on high gfxMusic: Its just phenomenalWvW: World vs World is incredibly fun in my opinion. while you choose a server upon first logging in the only major thing it chooses is the Team you pick in world vs world which pits 3 servers (sometimes 6 in a 2v2v2 scenario) against eachother to seige castles settlements and open world zerg vs zerg. Its fun as hell imo.Combat style: It has an action element to the combat, while you can apply a buff that will make targets miss you resulting in "evaded" pop up on you, you do actually have a dodge mechanic which you have to actively press with 2 charges that have a cooldown. It makes you feel a bit more like you are actually playing instead of just allowing boons and conditions to play the game for you.Questing: I hate quests that do this: Vendor>collect 10 fur from dead wolves>vendor>new collection quest>vendorIn gw2 this made far easier and almost just a part of exploration, once you come into a zone where a quest can be completed the heart will appear in your sidebar with the objective and you can choose to complete it if you want to. Its easy, hassle free and even when you complete it, it again comes up on the side bar with the reward, not a return to vendor situation.World events and bosses:Events happen throughout Tyria (the core world of guild wars 2) regularly. Just by being around a zone or near an event, it will pop up on the side bar with the objective and again you can earn additional rewards and xp from completing these. In the expansion maps each map has a meta-event which is a string of events that can last somewhere between an hour to 3 hours (i think 3 is the max i might be wrong) in which you get a lot of resources, xp etc which are useful for end game things, you also have the chance for rare drops in these circumstances.DLCs: The expansions go on sale quite often and are well worth the money. Normally introducing a great expansion/continuation to the story, ~4 maps zones, loads of events and with each one new mastery skills (more on Mastery points later) Each one so far has added something to the arsenal. Heart of thorns added gliding, Path of fire added mounts (5 of them to be precise, Each with unique abilities) and End of dragons added a few things but i am yet to unlock them as of writing this so i wont mention them here as i dont know what they are like.Mastery points: Level 80 is the max level for characters in Gw2 core, once you unlock expansions you start to unlock something called mastery points, this is continuous levelling that you could consider 80+1, 80+2 etc. with each mastery you unlock, you gain an additional buff or skill or function within the game.This is just the tip of the iceberg of what Gw2 has to offer, there's also, PvP, guilds and guild halls, World bosses (which are awesome imo), playing the market, Crafting (which is actually super simple when you know how), Seasonal events, Story content, Living world (the continuation of the story between DLC's free if you log in when they are active), Achievement hunting, Legendary crafting/questing, Rare farming, Edge of the mists (smaller scale WvW), interesting classes and races, world building, Personal story, exploration and infinitely more to love about this game.And i didn't even mention fashion wars which is a whole subsection of the game that will eat your gold and you will do hate yourself but love your character for spending your gold on dyes.Its free, give it a try....

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I've played since release, on and off. I have thousands of hours in this game. Could I have spent my time elsewhere? Absolutely. Do I regret it?  If you haven't played an MMO before, or you have and didn't like it, GW2 might be the one to change your mind. It's an MMO but it does some things differently. At first it will be overwhelming, there's not a lot of hand holding or direction in this game, but when the pieces start to click it will reward you with hours and hours of varied game play.It's an odd beast in the world of MMOs because it is sandbox enough to let you approach things in the way you want. Classes aren't locked with races and it abandons being locked into the traditional roles of tank/heals/dps, so there's a lot to learn. At the same time, it still has that MMO grind. But wait! Not in the way most MMOs approach grind, no, the grind is all from self directed goals. Very little content will be blocked from you if you don't grind one thing out and there's often various methods of getting to where you want to be, goal or otherwise. Endgame isn't the same few quests or raids until a new expansion, oh no, endgame is where the tutorial ends. The amount of content in this game is  There's crafting, trading, large and small scale PvP, open world (which allows you access to world bosses very early), personal story, various types of dungeons, strikes, raids (all of which have puzzle elements and are never just rotate skills till thing dies), jumping puzzles, mini-games, fishing and collectables. There's even a base-building esque feature, with plenty of freedom to make your homestead as you want with a separate crafting system and placement mechanic. Combat is super fun, with huge amount of abilities and ways to play each class. The combat is also more action based than a lot of MMOs, with dodges and a tonne of movement based skills. This game has some of the most unique classes I've seen, even when playing standard classes such as warrior or ranger. There is a cash shop, but it sells mostly fashion items (true end game, btw) and some items that give you convenience but it's never hard pay to win. Think things like unbreakable mining tools or salvage kits. The 'free to play' tag should really be marketed as a trial version, because the F2P accounts are restricted. But the way they've approached the F2P is just to market this to new players, it's healthy for the game because it means the game hasn't changed to balance out the fact its 'free', which has killed other MMOs. There's no subscription, you just buy the game and the expansions and can play for as long as you like. Which is also another great point of this game, you don't feel locked into playing every day. Heck, you can take a year (or two, or 4 in my case) out and it's perfectly fine to just pick up where you left.It's a good MMO to play solo too, because there's so much to do. So you don't have to wait for bro to get on. You can play with a small group of friends, or join a guild to do group content. The community is pretty chill and usually happy to help out with stuff, possibly because there's no sub fee so people don't feel like they are on the clock. They have time to goof about and help people out. Honestly, try the game out and commit to levelling a character. There's so much to this game, there's something in here for everyone. It's a real gem!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1) Mounts- Best mounts in the industry by far to the point where WoW is trying to copy one of them. Mounts in gw2 are not just a system where you use them to get from one place to another; in this game, you use mounts to get to new areas, damage break bars, events, mini-games, etc. 2) Combat- The combat in this game is so buttery smooth when I compare it with other MMORPGs. There is no global cooldown and you have 2 dodges in this game. Whenever you switch weapons for a class you immediately get 3-5 different skills so it feels so refreshing in combat. 3) The game is essentially mostly free- The only thing you technically have to spend money on in this game is the expansion. I think this is pretty fair and the company has to make money somehow. Everything else in the game you can pretty much buy with gold to gem conversion. 4) It actually feels like an MMORPG- In my opinion, this is one of the few MMORPGs that actually feel like it in this day and age. There are world bosses being done every hour where you have 50+ people battling them all the time in different instances. Also, in those world bosses, you see max-level players fighting alongside low-level players which is absolutely amazing. 5) Never on maintenance- Have you ever been annoyed when you get home and the game you are looking forward to playing all day is on maintenance/patching? Guild wars 2 is never on maintenance or patching. Everything new that is being patched or on maintenance is done on the backside. 6) Horizontal Progression/no holy trinity/ no set gear path - I hate coming back to a game where you come into a game and you have to spend an endless amount of hours just trying to catch up and just to get to the current content. Luckily, in gw2 there is no vertical progression(aside from Fractals) so if you reach the best gear since launch you can jump right into the end game immediately. There is no set holy trinity like in other games in gw2. There are healers and tanks in this game but you have a lot of freedom with it here. For example, if you see a ranger or druid in other games they are usually squishy and may die really quickly. In gw2, that may not always be the case because they can be quick, tanky, healer, etc. 7) PvP and WvW - PvP in this game is split up into 2 main different modes. First is the standard PvP where it is 5v5 trying to hold 3 points. For Worlds versus Worlds, you have servers against another server fighting against each other. It can get to the point where you have a ton of people trying to capture keeps, castles, etc (50vs50vs50) Very hectic but there is literally no other game that does this kind of mode. Cons:1) End game is not clear all the time- This games offer a lot and is not always clear because it offers so much. For a long time, ArenaNet(developer) was not sure where they wanted to lead this game. For example, in the end, game, you can do fractals, raids, strikes, WvW, PVP, world bosses, dragon response missions, dungeons, etc. I love a lot of this end-game content but it can be a lot and clutter for new players. 2) Achievements UI is horrible to navigate- GW2 uses the achievement log/sections as similar to a quest log from other games. I really enjoy it but it is too messy. If I was a new player looking at it, it is a huge mess and unclear. 3) LFG/queue system-  Probably one of the worse systems in this game. They need to rehaul this because it is not really a queue system. It is a panel where you open it and then you try to join. Since, the system does not check for your role, gear, etc. players have to go out of their way to call out their roles. This may not sound too bad but it gets really hectic and frustrating in raids, strikes,  and fractals. 4)User interface for buffs/boons needs to be improved-Unfortunately, you cannot change the UI for your buff and boons in this game. They are too small and in an awkward area, especially when you do end game. Overall:I absolutely love this game and have been playing it since 2014. Personally, I have a little over 3000 hours and I do not see myself stopping anytime soon. Every time I play other MMORPGs I always appreciate how much gw2 offers and in some cases is better. This is a long review but I have not even gotten to talk about other stuff like the amazing community, art style, music, jump puzzles. They have already announced a 4th expansion and Arenanet said the Steam launch has had even more players comes in than the recent expansion. This game is not perfect but it is one of my favorites for what it offers. Hopefully to see you in-game and feel free to message me any time for any questions. (kev.4537)

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is the most MMO like MMO, kinda reminds me of EverQuest and early WoW. The entire focus is on horizontal progression. Max level is 80 and it has been since release. Gear isn't that important except for high end stuff which only appeals to the most hardcore players.Story is amazing ngl, I love it although the presentation of the first arc (1-80) is slow. Because the story takes a pause every 10 levels, which makes it feel disconnected and the reason I dropped this game in the beginning and probably the reason many didn't like the story. I recommend using the free level boost to get the full story experience and also level your mastery earlier, also before you commit to the boos, you get to play that class at max level in a certain zone to get used to it.The world is the best. I LOVE EXPLORING. Feels similar to games like Legend of Zelda BOTW. The heart quests I love and the rewards stay relevant, in fact all the zones stay relevant all the time, so the game feels alive even now more than a decade later.I love the mastery system that appears after hitting level 80, where you continue to gain xp and levelling. This system allows you to get amazing passive and some active skills. Ranging from things like small xp boost, new merchants, new abilities for your mounts etc. They also appear for alts. Honestly this is the most alt friendly MMO.Mounts are amazing, they feel like mounts and they have their own abilities too, like the raptor is good at jumping long distances, the griffon is like a airplane that needs wind to ascend and gets faster when it descends, the skyscale is like a helicopter albeit slower than the griffon, the jackal is like the raptor but good for short distance jumps for certain puzzlers and I belive generally faster? etc.Combat is also very nice, its a mix of action and tab targetting where you can switch it around. _childDocuments_.review: 19 hours on steam, closer to a couple of hundred on the ANet launcher.Im a long time veteran of Guild Wars 1. bought this game day one. Played for a month, quit because it had an identity crisis of trying to be a sequel to Guild Wars while at the same time trying to be something entirely different. It just was not a cohesive or engaging experience. At all.I said I would wait a year until they had better fleshed out their overall design philosophy in terms of what exactly Guild Wars 2 was trying to be and who it was trying to appeal to.Instead, I waited an entire decade and came back to find out this game has aged better than any fine wine ever could. It feels like its own game, every facet has been polished to a shine and the game feels like it has come into its own, both creatively and mechanically, while still staying grounded in the source material it spiritually succeeds. It has gone from a 4/10 smashed up 1000-piece jigsaw puzzle of an MMO to one of the most gratifying, fair and engaging online gaming experiences you can currently have.9/10. Don't let anything stop you from giving this a shot. Even if it takes 10 years.

_childDocuments_.review: In Guild Wars 2, the gearing process involves an extensive and repetitive grind of acquiring countless stacks of "useless material x" to craft component A. This is followed by farming overwhelming quantities of stacks of y to create component C, then progressing to amass stacks of z for component D. Again and again.All of this effort is ultimately geared towards obtaining an item, but the journey is marred by unengaging and monotonous content.The quality of the content lacks excitement, never presents a challenge, and ultimately feels like a considerable waste of time.When faced with such a grinding experience, it's tempting to opt for a quicker escape by purchasing an attractive outfit from the gem store, allowing for a brief 10-minute appreciation before logging off.The desire for more meaningful and entertaining content becomes evident, especially when the current gameplay feels like a repetitive cycle with minimal satisfaction.The drop rates for prestige items are disappointingly low, to the point where obtaining these items feels almost impossible. It's as if the items practically do not exist, making the pursuit of prestige rewards an excessively challenging and frustrating endeavor.Ultimately, players engage with content in pursuit of rewards rather than for the content itself.When both the rewards and the content prove to be elusive, unattainable, and lacking in entertainment value, players understandably become impatient.The disconnect between effort invested and the satisfaction gained can lead to frustration and a diminished sense of motivation.A more balanced and rewarding system that aligns player efforts with meaningful and attainable rewards would contribute significantly to enhancing the overall gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the difficulties of development during the 2020 pandemic lockdowns and beyond, Guild Wars 2 still remains as a contender for best MMO, in almost every metric - by far the best aspect of it is how it balances the content available to you, while also allowing you to play as little or as much as you want, due to a horizontal-progression based system. _childDocuments_.review: Guild Wars 2 does various things right but there's a few things I want to shout them out for: - Monetization: I love that I can purchase the expansions once and that's ALL I need to do. Everything else to be purchased in game is for convenience or aesthetic purposes. Not only that but purchasing the expansions provides you with a lvl 80 boost so that means if you want to hop into a new after you level your main or if you've had a few characters maxed already this gives you the option to boost one you haven't tried yet.  Very cool and something that other companies would charge you more for or sell separately. - Fashion: I mentioned the aesthetic nature of the offerings in the cash shop. As a fan of Warframe as well, I love that part of the end game to GW2 can actually be fashion. HOWEVER not only are we talking about purchasable fashion, we're talking about gear you can far via achievements, events, drops, or missions within the different expansion. Add to that all the various dyes and effects and it really is a compelling part of the game and something that makes me WANT to seek out the pretty pieces of gear to customize my character. - Leveling: Before Guild Wars 2 launched, it had been maybe a decade since I had played a game where I felt like Leveling was done right. At no a single point during the progression of my character did I care that much about my level. What I was doing at Lvl 1-10 was fun, what I was doing at lvl 50-80 was fun and what I was doing at cap level was extremely fun. But never did I feel like rushing through and leveling which I think a lot of the current popular games fail at. WoW for example makes you feel like you need to get to cap ASAP or loose out on key events that unfold during the launch of that expansion. In GW2 there's SO MUCH TO DO and so much of it is enjoyable that there's really no reason to rush and half the time that I make a character in this game I will get to 80 before I know it, seemlessly, without worrying about gear....- Gear: This leads me to gearing. If you've done any research you've probably heard about Ascended of Legendary gear. Both of these kinds of gear are part convenience (the ability to share the gear with alts and change its stats) and partly allow you to play certain game modes (but those game modes are also a path to get ascended so that solves itself). For 90% of the game (maybe 80 but feels like 90%) you don't need ascended and definitely don't need legendary gear. This gear gives you about a 10-15% extra stat boost, but exotics already get the job done and can be purchased off the player marketplace for cheap. So technically you could even purchase multiple sets of exotics for different builds and have the same experience as legendary gear. So what's so cool then about the ascended and legendary gear sets? Well they look cool as hell, there are some beautiful looking pieces of gear and this makes me and other want to unlock those. They're also still stronger, so if you're min-maxing this is your end game in a way, and I mentioned they allow you to play certain game modes. When you get to that point, those gamemodes will provide a path toward ascended gear and might become part of what you play regularly so you don't even have to worry about it in a way, you'll get there just by doing what you like to do....- Game modes: That leads me to all the different game modes in GW2, there's so much. We're talking: PvP, WvW (which is the most fun I've ever had in MMO in years), and then everything that PvE offers with meta events which is basically a string of events that lead up to a boss run at the end,it's so cool and map-wide, it's amazing. You can just hunt boss monsters for the day, there's tons of exploration, which you're rewarded well for and is possibly the chillest way to get a character to lvl 80, there's jumping puzzles, and there's achievement hunting which BY THE WAY. Hunting for achievements in this game is actually a core part of it, it's the way that you unlock: Mounts, Skins, Ascended and a path toward legendary gear, and various other cool loot and items that let you access even cooler loot and items, it's insane. That's not even everything you can do in the game, I just spoke about what I've really dived into myself. There's fractal mists which are extremely rewarding, short, replayable dungeons you can do with a group. This is one of the quickest paths toward ascended gear I believe (disclaimer I've barely played this), theres 10 player Raids and Strike missions which are also hugely reward and scratch the itch for those people used to WoW and Final Fantasy end game dungeons/raids....I think that's most of the official stuff that you can do but there's still so many ways to play this game and all of it is rewarding and I love how GW2 has been able to figure that out. Rewards: Whch helps me end on this note. This game, knows how to reward you for your time. I started a new character recently and am focusing on exploration which means before I move on with the story I'll fully explore every map that I'm on. This itself got me to lvl 80 (while I was supposed to be maybe 60 in the story). It got me great gear that will carry me through the rest of my story until I get to 80 and then i can purchase exotics. In the meantime of exploring I took part in world events which randomly gave me great loot to either use or sell for gold (I definitely already made enough gold to buy a full set of exotics and be set for most of the game). I unlocked achievements which gave me mastery points OH....OH >>>MASTERY POINTSMastery System: This is an account-wide system which means you can farm it on all your alts and somtimes you can make alts that will effectively focus on getting certain masteries. For example I made an alt where I was going to focus on getting all the story achievements to unlock the mastery points from those. This system has unlockable mastery skills so for example for Path of Fire this is the system that helps you unlock mount skills and passives. For Central Tyria this is how you unlock certain special crafting and farming systems. Its amazing, it's so cool, I love it, it's account-wide so one and done and so nice to be able to work on it with various characters. This itself is something you can focus on and do for end game and it's again, so rewarding!I don't know if there's a character limit on steam but I feel like I could hit it going on and on with how amazing this game is. I really hope that a Guild Wars 3 is announced and is a direct successor to this with updated graphics but this game is chefs kiss** already and just needs some official quality of life  enhancements if anything BUT Arena Net allows third party plug ins to use API keys and essentially solve for those quality of life features. And the community for Guild Wars 2 is one of the nicest I've ever encountered probably even nicer than the Monster Hunter community. Love this game, I hope it succeeds above all else.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, engaging, brings people together and respects players' time. Shines the most in open world content. Instanced content is difficult enough but not to the point it drives player off like other mmos. Graphics are awesome. There's a variety of armor and mount skins to obtain, all of them without paying real money. Nearly all of them can be dyed. And there are A LOT of colors to choose from. The combat system is dynamic and fun and as are the mounts. All of them are useful and have their own abilities. The only issue I find in Guild Wars 2 is the lack of freedom when it comes to key-binds. You cannot drag your skills across the screen like in World of Warcraft. Every weapon type in the game has their own skills and they all share the same keybinds. The same goes for mounts. You can't key-bind your mounts' abilities individually. They all share the same key-binds. ( At least you can change those, just like the weapons' skills ). Some mount abilities are tied to the same key-binds as your weapons, thus making it very frustrating when you get a new mount and have to change the key-binds you're used to in order to be able play properly. Other than that the UI is very clean and well-designed. No clusters of text, meters and icons like other popular mmos. There is an  option play with action camera instead of holding right mouse button as well and it is perfectly viable. The game has horizontal progression and there is no irrelevant content. Each expansion is bought individually and and there is no subscription. You're definitely getting your money's worth and more. Exploration is a very big part of the game and the leveling process is long and fun. There is always something to do even after hitting max level and getting max gear. The game is actively bringing players to more populated maps, thus making it so you always have someone to play with. Despite its major key-binds issue, Guild Wars 2 is by far the best mmo I have ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 5000 hours in this game outside steam over years and while I did not play all main MMO games on the market, I think this is one of the best possible picks, taking into account active population, no real "pay to win", amount of content (though amount of hardcore content is a bit lackluster compared to casual one, still can deliver a lot of fun), there is also optional grind for convenience or cosmetic stuff (getting rich / crafting legendary items which allow you to change stats and do not provide strength advantage over non-grindable version, I personally went for that) that are not deal breaker for people who do not want grind stuff. Without grinding you can enjoy all sorts of content without being weaker than others, you just need ascended quality gear which is not a big deal to get. Some semi-proof that I know what I am talking about - one of my characters: IMPORTANT: Note that the game in reality is "buy to play" which is still very fair way of monetization compared to monthly fee that grows into huge costs over months/years.Also take in mind that all MMO's take some design choices, some cater to some people, while choices in other MMO's can cater to other people. There is no open world player killing in PvE, there is no constant gear grind (max level doesn't get increased over time by design), in competitive pvp matches gear strength is temporarily buffed/nerfed so all players have same strength etc. There is no "holy trinity" split of character classes (heal, tank, dps). Leveling is easy and serves as sort of tutorial, vast majority of activities are designed for max player level.I bet over time there was/will be minority of negative comments about "elite specialization that requires expansion is stronger than base game ones" or "raids / selling items / map-wide chat are hidden behind expansion purchase paywalls" - I would ignore these, anyway amount of content to try before buying expansions and living world is fair enough.PS. purchasing pretty much everything except expansions can be done via grinding gold if you are stubborn and do not want to spend money for living world episodes etc. Still, I think the amount of content in this game is huge and worth the moneyEDIT: if I got to nitpick about something then this game is sorta "chaotic" and "confusing" as it doesn't exactly tell / hold your hand and explain what you should do or not, so new players tend to do stuff thet they may not enjoy because they do not know if "it's better to do it" or not. I answer this right now: you can safely skip, stuff will not get locked out as you level up etc. Pretty much everything is optional, including "heart missions" and "story missions" with green markers, though story tends to give fair amount of non-grindy experience for first time players, and sometimes decent rewards. And the game doesn't exactly tell you what do you need and what are your options, so you browse various gamemodes, events, crafts and achievements to see ways to get ascended gear and other useful items. The upside is that community is very friendly and you may be able to get your question answered by other players when you ask in steam wforums /gw2 reddit, some decent ingame guild, or maybe make LFG advertisement in mentoring tab (or however it was named) that you need some sort of help.There may be other beginner player "confuse points" like LFG for dungeons being fairly empty p tl;dr answer is that they are oldest and now unupdated content, their rewards are poor and there is no big interest from veteran players to regularly do them + many beginners have social awkwardness for starting groups etc. If all you see is "speedrun" group then create own "beginners, no rush" group etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so... Guild Wars 2, arguably one of the best and most innovative MMORPG currently available on the market today, the game is literally a decade old now but despite its age, it still manages to feel fresh and up to modern MMORPG standards.But don't get it twisted though, GW2 ain't your typical Themepark MMORPG like FF14 or ESO (all 3 of which I love with a damn passion). In fact, the best way to kinda describe GW2's philosophy is by labelling it the "Anti-Themepark", because y'see, the game had for main goal two things:1. Proving that an MMORPG can indeed exist and thrive without a subscription model shoved up its ass2. Breaking away from most, if not, all the typical MMORPG tropes established by WoW and try to come up with brand new systems that went against the old WoW philosophyAnd that leaded to systems like: Renown Hearts, dynamic events, most things being account-wide, no gear treadmill, heavy focus on open world rather than instances, skills based on weapon types, and so on and so forth.The game is also F2P and B2P, with NO subscription model whatsoever, not even an optional one, and Cash Shop currencies are easily obtainable by converting Gold (Main in-game currency) into Gems (Premium Paid currency)Now, one thing you also probably noticed is that... GW2 doesn't really get talked about much, we could even argue that the game is under-represented by the general public, many people are under the impression that the game is """Dead""" just because they don't get bombarded with memes, obnoxious ad campaigns or mainstream articles, but this couldn't be farther from the truth. The game is just PACKED with people playing, at almost every levels, from the Newbie zones to the late-game zones, there are plenty of people running around and doing stuff.So yeah, definitely give this game a go if you're interested in it, you can start with the F2P version and later upgrade to the expacs if you're enjoying the game enough, the game gets updated frequently and unlike many other online games these days, GW2 very RARELY uses FOMO tactics, so don't be afraid to take breaks, the game isn't going to make you play catch up the next time you log in, especially since there is no proper gear treadmill in this gameEdit: Nominated this game for the Labor of Love Award because it deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: GW2 is a great game. It's got something for everyone. Like personal story quests that take you across several continents? Check. Like the idea of massive World vs. World vs. World pvp seige battles? Check. Like instant, accessible pvp with different modes and play styles? Check. Like building networks and socializing with access to up to five different guilds? Check. Like action platforming and puzzle solving? Check. Like special events with unique content and rewards? Check. Like exploring and games that promote exploration? Check. Like being able to personalize your look with a deep transmog system and massive dye selection? Check. Like account wide progression with no penalties for playing alts? Check. Like Dungeons? Check. Like progressing through increasing difficulty with increasing rewards through an independent dungeon system called Fractals? Check. Like Raids with immersive stories and amazing challenges? Check. Like in-depth crafting systems with real benefits? Check. Like massive in game markets with the potential to make actual profits? Check. Like the idea of a hybrid system with the structure of tab targeting and the fluidity of action combat? Check. Like massive world events and accessible dynamic boss fights? Check. Like mini "raids" for quick rewards and challenge modes? Check. Like an exhaustive achievement panel that provides new and exciting ways to interact with your environment and progression? Check. Like Minis? Like playing music? Like fishing? Like having access to the best mount system and mount skins in any MMO? Check. Like an MMO that actually respects your time and likes you back? Check.Basically, this is only a few of the things GW2 does well. I have another account with roughly 4.5k hours. Pretty sure thats a lot of ROI on fun vs. money spent. _childDocuments_.review: ARENANET WILL SCREW YOU:If you are a player with an existing arenanet account, do NOT buy expansions on steam, these idiots cant even figure out how to the two accounts "shake hands" and they will not help you if you fail to see this. While talking with support, I learned that, because I used steam to buy it (so I didnt have to enter card info on the arenanet website) I was now SOL because they only recognize products purchased directly through them. Customer support literally told me to "just buy it again"There is no reason to have an "inability" to share this information between accounts in the current year, screw these people.Original review:Really lame that when I come back to this game its gone f2p and because I paid full price for the core game I get less benefits than someone who buys an expansion for 15 bucks on sale.That said, Its not the worst.Combat does this irritating thing where it pretends its action but pretend is all it does...I understand netcode is going to cause trouble with anything else but at that point I think its time to just rethink your approach, Just don't fall for anyone trying to sell you on it as an "Action" game. Another weird feature is that weapons are your skills, and weapon switching allows you to have two "builds" at your disposal on command. There are a few additional skills that you have regardless, but your playstyle is mostly defined by each weapon. It works, but the variety in combat for individual weapons is limited and shallow - if you like four of the five skills for a weapon, you're just going to have to get used to using the fifth one, or ignore it. It also sucks that you cant work to improve individual skills, instead you can upgrade the weapon to add stats you like - but because you are going to use an optimal strategy, instead of wasting a slot to upgrade the skills you don't like, you'll just bolster the ones you do. This isn't terribly different than a game with set skills for a character, except that progression doesn't unlock opportunity and some weapons have skills that seem redundant to certain classes, making the freedom to choose a weapon seem more like an afterthought or a "wouldn't it be cool?" instead of a well designed mechanic.Of course, its simplicity is what makes it so easy to access and experiment with, you can level by doing anything, from killing monsters to filling out the map to pelting kids with snowballs, or all of the above. The game drip feeds you so you're never overwhelmed and because you can level up by passing out beer to thirsty soldiers in the desert, you'll never feel like you're wasting your time dong something. Its a great way to emphasize the best parts of an mmo while stomping out the worst....its just a shame that the levelcap throws all that out the window.Overall, If you like the idea of mmos but hate the grinding, loot mechanics, and 6 hotbars worth of skills that you may have built wrong and totally ruined your character - This may be the right game. Grind doesnt exist, the game seems to always find a way to give you something from a big fight, and simplicity is at its core, Its major flaws are just a lack of customization and a sometimes frustrating combat, especially against world bosses that are incredibly confusing if you dont read guides or ask.Really, The biggest thing holding it back is the very thing that makes it easy to get into, meaning the complaints exist mostly as a consequence of the praises. Give it a try, aim to fully explore one region before you decide to buy or uninstall.

_childDocuments_.review: Given how many positive reviews have been left by the game's established veteran playerbase, I will offer the reader a more critical outlook. Guild Wars 2 has 3 gamemodes, player vs environment (PvE), player vs player (PvP) and World vs World (WvW). PvE is the gamemode that receives the most updates. The other 2 are nearly non-existent. While I am primarily a WvW player, I have dabbled in PvE (I have over 20 legendaries unlocked) and will explain why I lost interest with PvE over time.The game relies heavily on horizontal progression, (you play for cosmetics not for increases in stats) not vertical progression. The endgame gear is easily obtainable within a few weeks of playing (ascended), however infusions which offer extremely minute stats (~1%) might take a bit longer. This means the reason you keep on playing i.e. the gameplay loop, outside of community related factors will be cosmetics, primarily unlocking legendaries.However, most of the high quality non-legendary cosmetic unlocks are not earned in-game but through the cash shop. All the mount skins, save for 1 are unlocked through the gem store, not through raids or difficult milestone achievements, like getting 250k kills in WvW. Sometimes the cash shop weapons overshadow the legendaries (compare the Vermilion Tail Feather with the legendary torches). Even the legendary back pieces cannot be dyed yet the majority of the gemstore ones can. The greatest scourge however, would be cosmetics that can only be unlocked through Guild Wars 2's very own lootbox system: the black lion chest. Moreover, the loot changes periodically within the black lion chest and you can only unlock these cosmetics later down the line with copious amounts of black lion statuettes (60). In the worse case, you will need to open 60 chests since you get one guaranteed statuette for each chest. Opening a single chest requires 125 gems. The smallest denomination of gems is 800 gems for $10 USD. This is classic artificial scarcity.Speaking of artificial scarcity, the cash shop contents regularly rotate even though they have no reason to. There are items that are "on sale" even though they are not at all discounted. Want a particular weapon skin your friend is wearing? Too bad, it's not on the gemstore currently. Be sure to buy it immediately the next time you see it on the gemstore!Cosmetics are not the only things found on the gemstore, there are other 'convenience items'. The game will throw you all sorts of junk and loot containers. Reward tracks are the worse offenders with many different reward containers (~40 for the triumphant armor track) and these containers in turn contain junk items that will occupy even more inventory slots. There are even items that share the same name and icon but do not stack in your inventory and take up 2 slots instead of 1 (experience scrolls) not to mention the numerous quest items you will receive. The default bag slots are simply not enough. Then there are the infinite salvage kits that are even more mandatory unless you want to be carrying multiple copies of salvage kits in your inventory. Instead of paying for convenience, the player is actually paying to be done with the hassle of cleaning their inventory every hour. Then there are equipment and build template slots. The game is lauded for being alt friendly and yet bag slots, build template and equipment template slots are character bound. Every expansion releases with 1 new specialisation for each of the 9 professions yet you are only given 2 equipment slots. You will eventually run out of slots if you wish to experiment with the newer specialisations. Furthermore, these equipment slots offer a distinctive combat advantage, especially in WvW where you can instantly swap builds to fit the occasion so these 'convenience items' are no longer strictly for convenience only. If this happened in monster hunter, the playerbase would be irate but because other MMOs are more egregious, so the fanboys can always lean on whataboutism. There are of course true convenience items like lounge passes but the bag, equipment and build slots are cleverly disguised as 'convenience items'. These "convenience items" are not cheap either. $USD 5, 6.25, 3.75 for a single bag slot,   equipment template slot and build slots respectively. Create the problem and sell the solution. After buying slots for your 9th character, suddenly monthly subscriptions fees don't seem so bad after all. We once had player-made build templates but that was removed for obvious reasons.The dynamic event system is awesome and is one of guild wars 2's strongest points; some even have event chains culminating in some final epic event. However the rewards for completing small events are minsicule. This coupled with the limiting factor for most of the legendaries being gold, being able to exchange gold for gems to buy things on the cashshop means your endgame consists of farming on the same set of profitable maps ad nauseam. After some time, the lines between playing and working will blur. There are achievements for completing events in the open world i.e. the armor and weapon sets that released with each expansion which is where Guild Wars 2 actually shines but these are the exception not the rule. You would therefore be better off 'farming' in real life through McDonalds than playing gw2 if you really want the best gold per hour unless you like Excel sheets. In which case you can play the trading post rather than the actual game. Welcome to your second job! This brings me to the transmog system which is great, allowing you to match any different armour piece of the same weight class together and dye it however you want. However, this is not true with outfits which make up the majority of new releases on the cash shop. There is no customisation for outfits apart from dyes which are also present with regular non outfit armor. If outfits are so limiting why does the developer still make them? It turns out outfits are easier to make and because the game has a healthy population of whales, it is more profitable to make them. WvW has the worse gold/hr and the least amount of unique skins. The WvW legendary armor  literally looks the same as the ascended version. Minipets in WvW give your location away if you are in stealth, meaning every player should hide their mini pets in WvW by default but nothing has changed in the 10 years of the game's release. In WvW, you win matchups by having the most points which is largely determined by having more towers and keeps in the server's possession. However this aspect of WvW is the most shallow. There are only so many ways that one can place a ram or catapult down in the same usual spots or spam 1 on the ram. The siege mechanics in WvW are also rather bland and actually subtract from the game imo due to the low effort to high impact ratio. You could watch Netflix and spam 1 on your arrow cart without any thought and have DPS output that is greater than any player. It is extremely cheap, both in supplies and gold, to place an arrow cart or other siege down resulting in little tactical depth. Therefore, winning a matchup usually comes down to the server that has more night cappers i.e. players that flip your structures while you are asleep. Hence, winning the matchup is not an expression of greater mastery over the game. Indeed, much of the veteran player base, especially on the EU servers no longer play WvW to flip objectives but to fight other players. The word "content" in WvW literally means the availability of enemy players to fight. Unfortunately, because of the way the game incentivises playing WvW, we get too many groups that dodge every fight i.e. point per tick (PPT) groups which does not accentuate the excellent combat system the game has to offer. The rewards for playing support are really poor in WvW. Your DPS friends get all the bags while you get no credit for the kills making supports even scarcer than in PvE.

_childDocuments_.review: Great MMO whether you're searching for something casual or a new main game.I've played around a thousand hours before the launch on Steam and mostly play solo when I have some spare time or a new main story bit as part of a Living World season or Expansion comes out.The way the gear and leveling system works you're never at a disadvantage if your can't play for a while or don't have much time to invest in the game since there are pretty much never any new item tiers coming out and invalidating your current gear.
