_childDocuments_.review: Please let me tell you about my favorite rat in Tyria.In the Zephyrite village of Symphony's Haven, there's a storage room with nothing in it. There is no mechanical reason to go in there--no quests, no conversations, no treasure, nothing to kill, not even any named NPCs. Pact workers sort supplies, chop firewood, and speak quietly among themselves. A Zephyrite woman sits alone against one wall with a rat tucked under her arm. There's ambient rats all over the map, but this one is the  one that can't be attacked; it's been set to a player-friendly faction.This is such a tiny detail, but to me it illustrates the passion, joy, and attention to detail that makes GW2 special. The Zephyrites are a pacifist faction, is this woman protecting the rat to upkeep her vows? Is it her pet? She doesn't even have a unique name or a conversation, but she feels like a person, someone who inhabits this fictional world and theoretically has a whole life going on outside of whatever the player is up to.I've heard the word "Sonder": "the realization that each random passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own." GW2 uses the phrasing "Living World." Whatever you would prefer to call it, GW2 captures the feeling well. Roleplayers, narrativists, story-focused players, writers, explorers... you will find a wonderful experience here.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the only MMO that doesn't piss me off.They solved some really basic problems of the genre. For one, other people being around is generally always a positive. Remember old MMOs having "kill stealing"? Doesn't do that here. Everyone gets credit.They never raise the level cap. Once you get to max level you don't have to keep chasing new gear. My characters I've made years ago are still valid. There's new options and the meta shifts, but you don't have to get on a gear treadmill. You can chase legendary equipment if you like, but that's for prestige and some qol perks. One really basic thing that's so nice: you can deposit materials from your inventory to your bank from anywhere. You can sell stuff from anywhere. You can access your bank and more from anywhere (via the pvp lobby, so you suffer a loading screen). It's nice. The basic gameplay feels like a real video game. You can dodge attacks.You don't have to do inane quest chains. There are "hearts" in the world where you get credit for doing stuff in the area. Some of them are silly. Some are great. Most of them include "go kill some stuff" as an option. The main draw are the dynamic events. That's where stuff just happens in the world and anyone nearby can participate. Portals open and demons come out. The volcano erupts. Allied npc soldiers attempt to take new territory. You just hop in and play.There's also instanced content for organized (or disorganized) groups of 5 or 10 or more. The latest expansion added a big 50 person event where you have to fight a bunch of demon bosses in a big map without letting the NPC die. It's fun. There's world PVP for when you want to go knock down a keep's walls with catapults and kill everyone inside. Or just go seize supply camps on your lonesome. There's a long story. Lots of solo content there. There's mounts. They're great. Make it fun to move around the world. I could go on. I'm just rambling. I have like 3500 hours in the game on my main account.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing off and on since launch. This is probably one of, if not. my favorite MMO. It's a buy once, play forever kind; meaning you buy the expansions or whatever is out and there is no other cost such as a sub (WoW, FF14). The classes are all different and all viable for play. There is no holy trinity of gameplay here (no dedicated tank, dps, or healer). Of course though there are going to be metas for content but that is usually unavoidable for multiplayer games trying to balance across PvP, Open World, and instanced content. One unique thing about this game is that the max level is 80. When new expansions came out there was no level increase, just new zones, new story, and new cosmetics to unlock. You can get the best gear from the BASE game and never have to worry about wasting time getting the best. Can be bad but can be good depending on how you like to play. And when visiting old content, your level down scales to the zone! So if you have a friend making a new character, you don't have to make a new one with them you can just play with them and get credit for map completion with them.The real end-game here is doing raids, fractals, and crafting. The best gear in the game are the legendary weapons and armor. They could be bought from other players for a few thousand golds, but due to the economy in this game it takes awhile to get gold (or buy gems for real money and convert to gold). Legendary crafting is a grind, but the items are unlocked by account. So you can have your items on ANY character you make once you craft it and bind it. Probably the best thing about this game is almost everything is ACCOUNT WIDE! Gold? Bank? Unique Currencies? Mounts? Achievements?  Shared across all characters. You can unlock the mounts and then make a new level 1 character and use them right away (well after completing the little prologue). The gameplay is very character oriented and fun. Classes get their combat abilities from the weapons they are using and each expansion unlocks a new weapon for classes to use. You have to dodge out of damages, heal yourself when you need to, have various traits (talents) to unlock and make a build with, along with a few custom skills that are tied to class rather than weapon. Perhaps my favorite feature of this game are the mounts. Unlike WoW or FF14, the mounts have purpose and abilities beyond just getting you from A to B on autorun. The raptor is fast and can horizontally leap far. The bunny is slower but has a high vertical jump. The skimmer is slow on land but fast over water and can be upgraded for use underwater. The jackal is fast and has short teleports. The griffin isn't the fast on land but get enough momentum in the air and it becomes the fastest mount in game. The roller beetle is slow but it probably the fastest land mount with its roll ability though it becomes hard to turn and make sharp corners. The skyscale is not the fastest or slowest but it can stay in the air unlike the griffin; it has a roll for a small burst of speed. And finally the turtle. Its a two person combat mount.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to say, honestly, I have played for 9 years now.. got 5K something hours across all characters, 18k something achievement points, and there is just something about GW2 that keeps pulling me back (if that doesn't convince you to try the game, I don't know what will... I'm not the kind of person to stick around a game I don't enjoy - Jk Jk, keep reading... there is more I've got to say).But seriously, I may stop playing sporadically for weeks or even months, but eventually, I return and find something new to do, or changed about the game. I always find a new goal to play towards, a new armor or weapon piece to get, a new build to make, rediscover an area I haven't visited in a while, chill in one of the player hubs, sit down and listen to GW2s amazing soundtracks, have a conversation with random people in say-chat or guild chat, or make music with my NOT so amazing in-game drumming skills (My skills are Amazinggg hmph! hahaha - Said me never).I don't have all the in-game shiny legendaries and I am certainly not one of the richest or shiniest players in the game (honestly so much shiny also sometimes makes it look like vomit, like WHY... WHY - on a side note, Skritts may revere you as their God... just not me haha)... heck I barely know how to make 100 gold without wanting to immediately spend it in things I DON'T need to hoard, but even so.. slowly and at my own pace, I have managed to get stuff done, stuff is not impossible in this game, playing mostly solo as well as accompanied is achievable, and having fun is EASY.Some people have asked me if this is better than This Game or That Game. My answer to that question is: GW2 has its own thing going on... some people will enjoy it, some others might not... but if you are up for it, give it a fair chance, don't go into the game with the mindset of playing yet another one of those MMOs out there, just think about it as a WHOLE new experience, and trust me... at the end of your journey, you may end up loving this game as much as I have if not more; and if not at least you gave it a fair chance. ;)Also, super duper important, take your time to read through stuff, immerse in the experience, and don't let us veteran players ruin your fun by making you skip past all the important bits and pieces of the game. Take YOUR time, and do it at your OWN Pace, not someone else's, even if that someone is a friend of yours ;) and once you are ready, have them play the game with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Ive played tons of different MMOs so far and if there is one I can definetely recommend for other MMO veterans or even beginners then it's Guild Wars 2. However it has some flaws which make the game hard to play (especially for beginners) which i will talk about in the different topics.LevelingThe leveling in this game is by far the best of all MMOs I've seen so far. You are directly immersed into the maps where you have to do tasks in specific areas (marked with a heart-symbol). However you can usually chose between different tasks you can do. For example you can either kill spiders at an apple farm, or collect apples that fell from the tree and give them to the farmer, which makes the "questing" in this game less repetivive than in other games like WoW. While leveling everywhere on the map events may appear which make this area a bit more different where you can help out the people in need which will fill the heart and you will get extra XP by participating in the event (for example - bandits try to steal the crops from the apple farm which you need to kill/stop). By having this kind of leveling experience you usually complete a while map by doing all these hearts, exploring Points of Interest, visiting Vistas (seeing a different Part of the Map) and helping out at hero points to get new skills/passives for your current class. It's also easy and quite fast to finish. StoryThe story of the game is amazing, you can repeat story parts for special achievements which you can only unlock within the story parts to collect achievement points for a few new Skins or slice of life stuff. I definetely recommend playing it at least once with one of your characters! Classes/CombatThe classes/combat system has its pros and cons. By far the best is that in comparison to other MMOs you dont have thousands of different spells to press (except for Elementalist which is also called the "piano class"). Each class has also 3 different Elite Specializations which can be selected at max level (80) to recieve new spells to use. However you can only chose between one Elite Spec. The biggest con for this is, that these elite specs are waaaaaaay better at max level in comparison to the default class, so you are obligated to play either of those, but the gameplay of these elite specs can be way different in comparison to the base-class which may lose your interest to play. Unfortunately you cant test these elite specs so you have to level to 80, collect enough hero points to unlock it with all its new spells and then get live-experience whether you like it or not and if you are a new player it might be harsh to invest so much time into a class and then ditch it again just because the gameplay doesnt feel the same like before.The combat is thanks to the less spells more about combining spells together to make a bigger impact or dodging spells of enemies/players to avoid these combos which can knock you out quite fast if you dont play attention. Thanks to that it is easy to learn but hard to master, so the learning curve for combat is insanely high but also quite addicting if you are interested in getting better with your class in any kind of way.GearingThe gearing of the game is by far the best ive seen in all MMOs so far. Since the release of the base game the level never has been increased and mostly only skins or other gear stats have been added into the game to play different styles to play (healer/support/dps). This is a huuuuge plus since whenever a new addon is released all the old content is still played by players. Even in the leveling areas you will always see players (although it might be less in comparison to endgame maps or new content maps). But since there are legendary weapons and armors for the game which are more a slice of live than a insane stat increase you have to do specific tasks to get them if you want to farm all of it by yourself. This forces you to go into "old" areas (even from the base game) to collect certain items, kill certain enemies or finish certain events. So even with the newest patch all your gear from before is still viable and you dont need to throw it awayContentIf you are a new player or even if you are "midgame" i personally think its the most fun to play. You have so much things to do or things you can do - collect gear, farm mats, get your professions up, level up different characters/classes, farm legendaries, play story, play all content/events, play raids or strike missions (which are literally the new raids), play pvp, play WvW, collect achievement points, collect new Skins whatever. However if you reach some of the goals you think are very important (like gearing up, playing some raids, maybe get some legendary gear) it gets quite horizontal to play. Its up to you what you want to do since there arent any obligated things to do. You can either farm more legendary weapons/armor-types, collect more open accessible skins, collect achievements or play PvP/WvW and that is literally it. So if you dont have a certain group or guild to play with you will lose your motivation to play quite easily. Its all about the MoneyIm gonna be honest - this game is a gold-sucking machine. For literally everything you need gold, mostly not even a little bit. Especially as a beginner you will realize that you will never reach 100g easily because you either spend it on some gear, or crafting, or whatever... BUT it is NOT pay to win. Yes, you can buy diamons (Currency from real money), yes, you can exchange diamonds to gold or vise versa, but it will not accellerate your gameplay in any kind of way, except you have tons of money left to spend to buy legendaries for roughly 100€+. But literally 75% of all the skins/cosmetics in the game are in the diamond shop and hard to get with just ingame currency/farming. You can exchange gold into diamonds and then buy them but the exchange rates change almost every second depending on the demand, so be careful if you do that (even in diamonds to gold exchange). I could continue to talk about this game even in more topics but in general ill do  a TLDR now for everyone who maybe wants to look into it and i'd recommend you to play it and experience it by yourself. :) Pros+ Diverse leveling system+ Great story+ Great combat system+ New content doesnt mean old content is dead+ It's up to you what you want to do + super friendly and supportive community (some trolls included)Cons- You might lose your interest to play your class after reaching max level thanks to elite specs- All you mainly do is farm gold- Hard to get into raiding/strike missions without any experience via LFG (with guildies it might not be a problem)- It's up to you what you want to do

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of MMOs over the years. Mostly WoW and ESO, but also Terra, Bless, Scarlet Blade and probably others that I don't remember anymore. I've grown to dislike them. I've heard a lot of good things about this one, so I decided to give it a shot. It may be ok for an MMO, but it's far from some shining example that many make it out to be.Story (minor spoilers)It starts promising. At character creation you make some choices that will influence your story. Unfortunately that story is level gated resulting in grinding irrelevant events for the privilege of continuing it. Sure, there's some dialogue to every location, but I didn't run into anything memorable. It tends to just boil down to "enemy bad, we good, kill". The main story (or "My Story" as it's called) is shallow. I picked Asura. Essentially immediately you're pitted against a group (krewe) called Inquest. They are said to be by far the biggest krewe in Asura society. And they act as cartoon villains. At least from player perspective. Is the race inherently evil and players are one of the few good guys? Doubtful, since the council is also depicted as some waste-of-space institution. To me the whole thing felt like a civil war where all the krewes ganged up on one that gained too much support/power while the central government stayed out of it. Though, most likely it's just bad writing and I'm overthinking it while I should be killing Inquest. If I murder enough, they won't be the largest anymore after all! The rest of the story I experienced was just your standard of: "Betrayal! Beat em up! Another betrayal, this time by a trusted friend! Beat em up!" Everybody seems to be joining this cartoonishly evil Inquest for some reason. Tbh, I wanted to join as well. They must be doing *something* right. Later on there's some generic bandits that join up with Inquest and another faction that just seems to want to see the world burn. It felt like they were the "bad guys" of Humans and Sylvari respectively. Even further on there seem to be dragons, which are the *really* bad guys, I guess. Does the writing get better? I don't know and I don't care anymore.CombatProbably what most care about. I think it's hit or miss. I definitely see why people would like it. Depth is hinted at, but never really explained to the player. Changing a weapon gives you a new set of abilities. Going under water does too. That said, I got to lvl 40 by mashing buttons until things died and never worried about what I'm actually doing.ExplorationThere's a lot of explore. You get rewards for doing so. Completing a zone gives you some special goodies. You will need a mount, though. And for that you need to buy the game, after your mount trial expires. I think it's pretty cool how mounts have abilities; the trial mount allows you to jump into combat and swipe before dismounting. I've also seen a lot of dragons that allow limited flight.Gameplay loopMain story is a tiny part of the game. You can't level just by doing that. The meat seem to be random events that keep popping up all over the map. There's always something to kill, but there's usually no clear reason as to why you're killing this or that group. Other than them having red nameplates. I do recall some NPCs discussing how "red" enemies are dangerous and "yellow" are not.CurrenciesIn standard MMO fashion there's too many currencies. There's two main ones: money and karma. Why there need to be two? I don't know. I also encountered vendors selling stuff for at least 5 more different currencies  that probably become relevant later. Of course there's also gems which are primarily bought with real money. You *can* buy gems with basic ingame currency, but as a new player I wouldn't count on it.GearYou get showered in gear. In MMO tradition there's no reason to care about buying it from vendors early on, since you'll get something better immediately after. The only exception seem to be accessories, which I found only at karma vendors.TalentsThere's a bunch of categories to choose from, which give you up to 5 extra abilities. As a necromancer, I put all the points into summoning and empowering minions and not really worry about them otherwise.LevelingYou get a bunch of rewards for every level and a timeline of what is to come. For me that was way too many popups and inventory slots, so I stopped caring about them quite early on. As long as you don't choose a reward it doesn't take up space, so I started only claiming them when at a vendor.InventoryFor most of my play I found the inventory space adequate. Until I didn't. There's not a lot of space. You get the main inventory, which is 20 slots and then you have 2 bag slots (which added another 18 slots for me). This is somewhat offset by gathering materials going into a separate storage. But you have to move them manually, which becomes really annoying when your bags are full and you're trying to loot something. You can buy more slots with gems (and I believe you get two more bag slots by buying the game).GatheringYou can gather whatever you run across, assuming you have the correct tool of the correct quality. Tools are consumables and extras take up bag space. But don't worry, you can resolve that problem by buying permanent versions for gems.Free vs PaidDon't expect to get far without buying at least the base game. For me the major obstacle was the mount. Initially you get a trial mount for 10 hours of gameplay. After that expires you're encouraged to buy the game, but allowed to continue without. Frankly, I don't think this game is playable without a mount. An obvious downside is that you're slower. An even worse one is that you're basically forced to fight a bunch of mobs you'd just zoom past with a mount. In a game where most of gameplay revolves around limited time events this is an obvious handicap. Other than that, I felt the store was constantly being showed in my face. Want to learn more trade skills? We have a solution! Want more bag space? Only X gems per slot!In summary, if you *really* must play an MMO, you could do worse, I suppose. It seems all the fees are one time, but I have no idea how much I'd have to spend to have all the "necessities". Personally, I'd rather go back to WoW where the sub ensures I have access to the whole game rather than calculate whether this trap is worth it. I think this game is a great example of games that create problems only to sell you solutions to them.Edit: After playing some more with friends and getting larger bags, I haven't changed my mind on anything substantial. Sure, the game is much more fun when played with others, but that's the whole point of MMOs. One thing I did observe is that there's many more currencies than I anticipated. There's also several things that should be currencies but instead waste inventory space. And not all events drop level appropriate gear (some give you stuff that requires max level).

_childDocuments_.review: At well over 3000 hours, I can still say one thing: Arenanet's advertising skills are terrible but the game is the polar opposite.Why should you play Guild Wars 2 over any of the newer MMORPGs out there right now?I won't go over the regular staples - they are all here, gear, quests, dungeons, raids... all the trimmings. There are things here that I have never seen in any other mmo, and they impress me greatly to this day:1. This is an mmo that respects your time and money.This is a game that you can play for a month or two get some exotics (baseline 80 gear), leave for 3 years and come back exactly where you were - able to play all the content available then, and after those years pass. There is no gear treadmill, no reason to feel like you are missing out by not playing constantly. If you choose to play casually, you are not at a disadvantage to raiders or even streamers playing 24/7 - an even playing field in all content. There are rewards for high end content but they are conveniences and cosmetics, bragging rights and the actual fun of raids done right but nothing to say: You are playing the game wrong such as with World of Warcraft or other major players in the space.As for money, Arenanet does not charge a subscription in any way, but counter their other free-to-play competition, there is NOTHING in the store that could in the wildest stretch be considered player power. By picking up and playing the game free, you can play all the content in Tyria, dungeons, fractals (short duration dungeons - more time respect) and even baseline raids. Should you CHOOSE (if you enjoy something why wouldn't you want more of it) to pick up the expansions/living story you get a fair price for incredible amounts of content. I have since purchased all the living story/expansions and consider it a steal without a single regret.2. Gameplay design is skewed to create the least toxic community I have ever seen. While you can't attribute the community as a whole to a developer, at every junction possible ANET has encouraged cooperative play - passive buff sharing, personal loot (no tagging), rewards for assisting and helping fallen allies - skills to assist players with travel/puzzles, I can't even go over each instance but it all contributes over time to creating a positive community that wants to help and be nice to each other. They essentially are dog training players, that they will get experience/loot for helping in any way they can.In my experience this does not carry over to the structured pvp (wvw is still great however)... given the naturally competitive nature of those people - you have been warned.3. Story - This has the biggest caveat. As a whole, Guildwars 2's story is brilliant, fully voice acted, filled with clever twists, has memorable moments and truly gives a feel of being a part of an incredible world. At least it is, after personal story which is the story that follows character creation and culminates at 80 - and as far as I am concerned is the weakest foot forward for GW2. New players will find the style (character cutouts with voice acting) and be middling at best. It is something I am glad to have finished, but ALL of the following living story and expansion story (it happens in-engine, during gameplay) is worlds ahead of it and really where GW2's story shines. I highly recommend playing it in order as it is one continuous storyline with characters and side arcs that last the duration. This requires buying the living story packs (I recommend a sale) - These packs contain not just story instances, but whole massive maps/areas that you can get rewards from and explore/do events in.Guild Wars 2 Personal Story (FREE, just press play above)Living story Season 1 - FREE (depending on how soon you are reading this, it may still be in progress of re-release the last few chapters)Living story Season 2 - Lead-up to Expansion 1, Heart of thorns - helps make the heart of thorns make sense)Heart of thorns (Expansion) - Brilliant, but MUCH harder than base game -  not exactly dark souls but things expect you to dodge once in a while)Living story Season 3 - Separate story that leads to the motivation behind path of fire, just stunningly brilliant storytelling and a must playPath of Fire (Expansion) - I can't even start on this one, too many good memories, Praise Joko!Living story Season 4 - MAJOR plot points, great moments, finishes the path of fire storyline imoIcebrood saga - Mixed reviews regarding its ending, but I loved it - civil war, unique maps, fun mechanics.Cantha (Expansion) - If you make it here in the story, you are are already here to stay as you would have experienced the above - You will buy it and love it3. The gameplay is deeper than it looks.Watching from afar, GW2 combat seems to be standard mmo fare, tab targeting and action bar buttons, however it is somewhere closer to Black Desert than Warcraft, your skills need to connect physically, walls, reflects and dodges (i-frames) turn the combat into a very active real-time game - there will be abilities you need to jump over, hide behind objects and dodge to survive your “HP” is not the whole story.There is almost never a moment that you say: “I couldn’t have done anything to survive that!” buffs such as stability will counter a single stun/cc, but don’t last very long. spells and abilities are tuned to hurt, but not 2 shot you - and always, you decide how much health/damage/mitigation you want to play with - allowing for brick bunker elementalists(mages) and glass cannon warriors or anything between.There’s far more I could say, but really - it's a brilliant game, costs you NOTHING to join a welcoming community and anet is one of the few game companies that hasn’t gone evil yet (ignore NCSOFT as a publisher, they suck but have no say in the game)

_childDocuments_.review: I downloaded 65GB of a second copy of GW2 just for the sake of posting a positive comment on steam. That's how good the game really is. For what it's worth, my main account without steam has 1000+ hours played.10 years of playing the game in big or smaller bites (3 to 12 months in, burnout and break, rinse and repeat), it is always a great pleasure to log back in, and to play new content, or to rediscover old content with a new class. GW2 combat mechanics aged really well, exceedingly better than tab-games such as WoW and copycats. Graphics are still very good and outstanding in many places (even with my old PC).Exploration, lore and stories, farming, PvP, open world events, original mounts and jumping puzzle games, there is always something you will like to do in GW2. Best of all: the devs respect your time. Like REALLY respect your time. To illustrate, no gear / level treadmill: once your character is complete, your level and gear will always be top-of-the-line : the progression is horizontal (try new specs, new classes, new playstyles), not vertical like in most MMORPGs (borrowed powers, gear becoming obsolete, max level increase). Even if you take a long break, your characters will alway be there and ready to pick up dungeons, fractals or raids. That's a monumental change from WoW and most MMORPGs in general.Try it for free, no subscription, no P2W, no hidden costs, there's a massive amount of free content to do in the game. You can farm gold ingame and convert it to gems if you want to purchase cosmetics or optional convenience items. You don't need to spend any money if you can't afford to. Once you're done with all the free content, then buying all the expansions is really worth your money. Great expansion stories, awesome class/specialisations, exceptional maps and regions, outstanding mounts that are now copied by Blizzard. The devs respect your money, like they respect your time.The strongest point of GW2 ? The community: ask for help or firepower for a difficult boss or event and you'll see many players converge to help you. Lost in a quest, map, or event? Just ask in the chat and players will answer or even go out of their way to show and tell. GW2 has, and by far, the nicest and most helpful community in all the MMORPGs have I played over 10 years (i.e. pretty much all of them).The biggest weakness of Guild Wars 2? The non-existent marketing budget and team... I still cannot understand why the game never had the exposure it deserved over the past 10 years. Hence, this comment as a tiny contribution from a long-standing GW2 fan: try the game for free, you can thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that certainly has its charm but in 2024 I wouldn't find acceptable any longer. The graphics are bad, that itself didn't discourage me much, I won't even talk about that from here on. As I had feared, this game feels mostly singleplayer until supposedly you hit max level 80 (which is now what some people say is "easy to hit now" but then proceed to say that they could hit it in 3-4 days if they wanted to, which doesn't sound like much, until you understand that it takes 3-4 days IF you treat it like a full-time job. With 31 hours of this game, I tried to enjoy it and while not completely joyless, I find is out of date for its time. Maybe I got unlucky, but thief was SO boring of a class INCLUDING its "variety in weapons" that change abilities. (Very little by the way) and honestly is lame. You know how you level up in games and get stronger and get cooler abilities? In GW2, at least as far as I can discern, you get "perks" where something like "Whenever you go stealth you get more strength" or maybe something a little more. It doesn't add to the gameplay whatsoever and I found myself from lvl 5 all the way to lvl 50+ that my abilities were the EXACT SAME and my 30 hour progression grind was the same mechanics, and this includes me switching weapons often to TRY to introduce some variety and keep myself entertained. Random rant aside, numbers don't lie, GW 2 has a bustling community- but in the same way that sports technically all have large communities in that there's a lot of sports clubs, teams, whatever you call it, but it doesn't mean you can casually find a group unless you specifically look for a beginners group. I tried my damn hardest to like this game, but I'm sick of spending all of this time in order to get to "the actual game with other people". "It's not that long" is what people say but I would argue to even need grind for more than just an hour of singleplayer just to get to the good stuff is unacceptable. I'm over 30 hours and if I had to estimate, I'd say I would've probably hit lvl 80 in about.... at earliest 50 hours total? Investing 50 hours in order to see if you actually will enjoy the game that you came for is not okay. I am a huge fan of the idea of MMOs, fantasy, all that ♥♥♥♥, but even when I'm trying to like this game it just won't let me. So while this game has found a niche of people who do enjoy it (which is totally valid), in my opinion it's like OSRS where it has its audience but when you think of "Massive multiplayer online role playing game" and "Fantasy" it just doesn't stack up. Maybe that's the standard for MMORPGs is that they're simply like this, and in that case, I'm disappointed. The idea of an MMORPG is all I ever wanted, and so when I can't even force myself to like a game with that idea, suffice to say, it's clearly doing something else other than what it advertises to be. Don't call me a hater, I played 400+ hours of New World even though that game ALSO felt similarly singleplayer. My point is, at least I saw the appeal in New World enough to sink 400+ hours in with a game that most people don't consider as good (at least that's what popularity suggests), while for GW2 I was just hoping something would click for over 30 hours and nothing did. If somebody could prove me wrong in that GW2 is 1. actually significantly more fun in terms of gameplay mechanics than I had given it credit for and 2. facilitates the idea of what in my opinion an MMORPG should be (a game that encourages and facilitates multiplayer and the idea of interacting with people) and that 3. The fun part starts at the beginning (or at least doesn't take hours+ to unlock) and I'm wrong about the lvl 80 idea, then PLEASE. If you can convince me, I would be so happy because I am desperate for that type of game, and as much as I really wanted GW2 to be it, I could not even convince myself to think "this is fine".

_childDocuments_.review: No gear treadmill after every patch, gear 10 years ago is still good today. No stupid fetch quests: gather 69 boar spleens, kill 420 goblins, deliver this 'do you like me? No? Yes?' note to someone next door. Alt friendly, and I mean really, share gear between alts, Masteries unlock account-wide. A typical raid night might have me switching between  a healer, a dps, a tank, or something made specifically for a boss.Guild Wars 2 Mounts are the best, ask anyone. You can't over-hype them. You can make separate games from these mounts and they will be fun. The Mastery system replaces level cap increases in other MMOs. It serves as levelling over 80, and it unlocks abilities that are useful in the world like gliding, access to shortcuts, and etc.Fractals of the Mists are GW2's end-game 5-man content. Fractals are what mythic+ wishes it could be. Easy to access, hard to master, requires relatively more gear grind to max out.Legendaries in gw2 aren't just the strongest gear, they're the best QoL, able to switch stats at a whim making build craft easy. Shareable between alts, my warrior, revenant and guardian all wear the same pieces of legendary armor without needing to go to the bank to deposit/withdraw, thanks to the legendary armory system. And all my max-level characters can use the same legendary accessories. No hassle. Getting a legendary isn't just grind, either, and each legendary has its own story. My favorite is Shooshadoo, a legendary shield that's just a fish tank with a baby quaggan (orca person) in it, Shooshadoo is the quaggan's chosen one, invincible like Achilles, he's just a baby now, though, but he wants to help. So naturally, you put him in a fish tank and use him as a shield.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing off and on for a decade now. I love that I can jump back into this game every few months and my max level characters and their gear are still relevant and able to participate in all content. I'm a huge fan of the horizontal progression philosophy, where I can just pick something to go after (mounts, equipment, mastery points, zone completion, etc.) and focus on achieving it for a few hours or days without much in the way of prerequisites or any ilvl requirements. The non-traditional approach to questing is great, as you can just organically explore zones and participate in world events as they pop up as opposed to filling a quest log, finishing quests, then having to run them back to a quest giver.

_childDocuments_.review: Played so much before Steam release. Guild Wars 2 is nothing short of a masterpiece in the world of MMORPGs. From the moment I stepped into the vibrant and expansive world of Tyria, I was hooked by its beauty, depth, and the endless possibilities it offered.The first thing that struck me was the stunning visuals. The attention to detail in the landscapes, character designs, and dynamic events is simply breathtaking. Tyria feels alive, and every corner of the map tells a story, encouraging exploration and discovery.What sets Guild Wars 2 apart is its commitment to breaking away from the traditional MMO formula. The dynamic event system injects life into the game, ensuring that every moment is filled with action and surprises. No more mindless grinding – instead, you find yourself immersed in a living, breathing world where your actions truly matter.The character customization is unparalleled. The variety of races, professions, and the ability to mix and match skills allow for endless personalization. Whether you're a seasoned veteran or a newcomer, the game caters to all playstyles, making it accessible and engaging for everyone.The PvE content is vast and diverse, with a plethora of dungeons, world bosses, and challenging group activities. The Living World updates bring regular injections of new content, keeping the game fresh and exciting. The narrative is captivating, weaving a tale that tugs at your emotions and keeps you invested in the fate of Tyria.One of the standout features is the emphasis on cooperative play. Guild Wars 2 encourages teamwork, and events seamlessly scale to accommodate players of all levels, fostering a sense of camaraderie among the community.On top of all this, the PvP and WvW modes add a competitive edge to the game. Whether you enjoy battling other players in structured PvP or engaging in massive, server-wide conflicts, Guild Wars 2 has something for every PvP enthusiast.The cherry on top is the lack of a subscription fee. Once you own the game, the entire world of Tyria is yours to explore without any additional cost.In conclusion, Guild Wars 2 has set the bar high for MMORPGs. Its stunning visuals, dynamic gameplay, and commitment to player agency make it a must-play for any gaming enthusiast. So, grab your weapon, rally your friends, and embark on an epic journey through Tyria – you won't be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: From someone who isn't the biggest fan of MMORPGs (and I've tried a lot of them), Guild Wars 2 is the distinct exception. The world-building, combat system, and general atmosphere is as good as it gets, but these aren't the reasons why I'm impressed. The game is simply fun, and sometimes, especially now a days when games of this genre vie for you attention by pitching themselves as time-sink side-jobs, fun is hard to find. Nearly every five minutes in this game I discover something that surprises me, either through exploration, story, or mechanics, and for this reason I'm comfortable giving the gaming time I have to this one. Guild Wars 2 doesn't hold you ransom with completionist checklists, shinning new items, or new updates to keep playing. The reason to play is far more simple: it's fun. _childDocuments_.review: Before playing this game, i used to mainly play games just to have something to do with my friends, to be part of the group and have some fun together.I've now gathered around 9k hours on my main account, and rounding up around 10k across all of my accounts. I've played all aspects of the game consistently to an extent. Before i start listing small portion of why i will not recommend this game, i would like to say that Gw2 has the potential to be best MMORPG out there in my opinion, the game on its core is -stunning- once you open up and put your mind to it. , content and monetization decisions seem to aim towards Short term investment. Arenanet seeks to please people temporarily by fixing initial problems, and by shoving in expensive Gemstore content without improving rewards and quality of the game any further, bugs and issues lay around for up to years. especially for Roaming / Small Scale fights, Celestial, Deadeyes, Immobilize spam and more are massive problem to people who just wanna have reasonably skill based fight.I personally always have the ''Thrill of Hunt'' going on,  but current state of things favors ''Build vs Build'' combat more than ''Player vs Player''Celestial, aoe spam, conditions, cheap tactics of all kind, mobility resetting, 1shot scrappers pressing 1 button from stealth to one hit you, and more mixed together really destroyed the Game mode for me. I also do not like Warclaw ( WvW Mount ) they added during Path of Fire, it really ruined the immersion and distancing in roaming and teamfights, and i bet many will agreeTeamfights or ''zergs'' are our large scale fights, where these issues do not apply that much, i can enjoy this aspect of the game even with worse builds, be effective if i do my part well, although there is a lot room to improve here as well. but build diversity has gotten really bad, coming up with your own thing rarely works anymore as you will get driven over by the flavor of the Month really hard. 3v3 and 2v2 are AoE spam fest, where usually person spamming better comp will be more likely to win. 5v5 Conquest is still enjoyable to an extent, though i feel the road is rocky when it comes down to the balance this game mode has, feels very neglected and always tilts you to look for the better builds, or get completely screwedThere is -a lot- to say about the subjects regarding PvP / WvW Game play in the game, but i would not be able to fit it all in here, so let's forward to talk about the General game itself Overall very fun experience, Open world is wide and good exploration experience you will love if you like taking your time with a game, to learn your class(es) and do Map Completion, or Jumping Puzzles, hunt for Achievements, collect currencies, Masteries, Hero Points, World Bosses and so on. It is truly an experience as a new player in the game, and i would never deny thatHowever! The quality of changes during recent past years has been astronomically low, infact, many people were scared, Arenanet was silent and barely informed us what is going on, and this Affected all of the game a lot in dramatic way, We are no longer getting unique Legendaries regularly, and we resort to the cheap way of mass creating aurene Themed Legendaries as of End of DragonsMonetization keeps getting heavier and heavier, and all the visual effort goes into Gemstore while the in game rewards are nearly same as nothing, Questionable Balance changes have not only been issue in WvW and PvP, but also in PvE, only till recently the balance has been all over the placePvE is however going consistently in right direction, whether people like it or not, Arenanet is now newly doing small changes ( removing unique buffs ) to make less mandatory builds be part of the Meta.Mounts have ruined the Open World immersion on a greater scale. Overall i might return here to rewrite my review more later, but i have a lot of Passion for this game, a lot of broken hopes, and way too much Optimism through the yearsIt is not a bad game, but my addiction for this game died 5 years ago, and from the looks of things it will never come back, which is a good thing if you look at it certain way. _childDocuments_.review: Ignore steam hours, I have four max level characters on my main account. This review might be a bit long, but GW2 does things differently from most others.Though it's not as populated as other MMO's, the community is still going strong. People will happily help new comers (myself included) and toxicity is pretty rare. You can find it occasionally in PvP, but that can be safely ignored if that's not your thing. Guilds are here of course and most of them are pretty tight knit. So if you go looking for a guild, your best bet is the GW2 forums. The story is quite good! Story quests play out as an instanced quest chain. The first two quest chains are determined by the background you choose when you make your character. The next two chains by choices you make in the story itself than goes to a set path. It can be skipped pretty easily if you want, but I suggest giving it a try for your first time around!GW2 does quests a bit differently than most others in this genre. Instead of picking up a quest from a quest giver and killing x number of enemies, you have hearts which activate when you enter it's area. These hearts can fill from a variety of activities. One heart has you clear pests, play with puppies, help lost dogs, and knock down weeds for example. GW2 also places a focus on exploration. discovering points of interest on the map gives you xp and contributes to map completion. There's also vistas to be discovered that give you panning shots of the games more beautiful locals. Reaching 100 map completion for an area grants you a random reward, and is necessary if you want to craft certain legendary weapons.There are nine classes. Three each of heavy armor, medium armor, and light armor. Each class can equip a range of weapons that change the abilities they can use. For example, Mesmer can equip daggers, scepters, wands, focus's and great sword. Each weapon has unique abilities that can drastically change how you play your character! Most classes can also equip a second set of weapons that you can switch to on the fly, granting you even more flexibility. Aside from weapons, you have also skills. Skills are different. They can be freely switched out and are available no matter what weapon you're using. There are a ton of different skills for each class and even some racial skills! Though these tend to be weaker than class skills.Crafting also works a bit differently, but can still be grindy like others. You can learn two crafting skills. the usual weapon and armor crafting, as well as cooking. Crafting materials are find out in the wild and can be stored in a completely separate crafting storage so it's not flooding your inventory. Crafting is focused on discovery. You combine different components to discover a recipe, which adds it to your crafting list and gives a burst of xp and crafting skill. Higher crafting skill unlocks more recipes. Crafting is the only way to make legendary weapons, but legendary weapons are mostly cosmetic, adding cosmetic visual affects to class abilities and is more of a way to reward players that do a ton of different things more than a necessary thing.Aside from the purchaseable expansions, you have an in game shop with mostly cosmetic options. There are a few utility type things like unlimited harvesting tools, additional character slots, more bank space, the ability to learn more crafting skills and keys for loot boxes. The in game shop isn't the most egregious i've seen in an mmo, but nothing there screams have to have. if you wanted to spend some money on this game, I suggest getting all the expansions first and foremost.You've probably noticed this already, but the game has a gorgeous watercolor aesthetic for none 3d assets. The graphics on the models are fine. pretty in line for an MMO really. The music in this game is above average with some real stand out tracks. Weapon hits are skills are appropriately weighty sounding and give good feedback. Example of a standout trackArena Net crafted a wonderful game here that most people overlook for more popular fair. GW2 respects your time more than most others, offers fresh takes on classes and customization, and offers a great and emotionally touching story. If you're reading this far, I implore you to give this game a try. The most it'll cost you is a bit of your time. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is different from about any MMO I have played prior because the classes have unique skills based on what weapons you use. Part of that uniqueness is this game does not follow the holy trinity of tank, healer, dps. Instead, everyone has built in heals and buffs (some classes are better at tanking and healing than others). Like most MMO’s you get overwhelmed with what to do so I stuck to the story quests after I hit 80. As for the pros and cons:Pros:Unique classes: they feel different than other games which is a pleasant change of pace. World: Large world with lots to do, open public events go on everywhere and there seems to be a lot of activity.Subscription: You only need to buy the DLC’s and you can play the game with no sub. The base game is free so I would recommend you try this game if you have an itch for a new MMO.Community: People are friendly, active, and helpful. Feel free to ask your questions Weapon skills: Diverse options of weapons for classes. An example is the hunter can use a one-handed axe but most of those abilities are ranged attacks on main hand but on offhand those abilities change to meleeCons:Weapon options: Every class is mostly melee, with ranged thrown in. I played a hunter as I like ranged classes and found that you mostly would use melee weapons in the later game (especially raids). I can force being ranged by using a long bow and a short bow as a backbar, but this is not ideal in higher end play. Class progression: I went from feeling strong to feeling very weak as I leveled, gear was hard to come by. Felt like I was getting a lot of gear that was not for my class and I out leveled the story quests so the rewards I received from that as mostly junk to me.Monetization: As I said in the pros that there is no subscription for this game but the one problem, I see with it is for quality-of-life things like more inventory requires buying things from the shop using gems. Now its possible to get gems by converting gold to gems, but gold is extremely hard to get. Just leveling from 1 to 80 without selling my mats on the auction house I had around six gold. (my understanding is higher end players can make 5g to 25g an hour but this is based on your knowledge of the game and how invested you gotten with upgrades like mounts already) Either way your spending money to have a better experience or your spending a lot of your time grinding for gold so you can have a better experience in the future.The only game I played that had a similar shop to me was Lost Ark. When I did calculations, you would need to spend $100s to get some basic quality of life stuff to make the game feel better and that is not counting cosmetics. There should be a subscription option that gives you’re a large storage (or unlimited), gems, and some other perks. (Elder Scrolls Online uses this model)Weapon skills: Yes, I listed this one as a pro, but it is also a con because you are forced to use whatever skills are on those assigned slots. You cannot customize what skills go on what button and you get no other options, so this causes issues if you do not like certain abilities. Gold sink: Everything cost gold in this game. Scrapping kits to turn items into mats, fast traveling, and gathering tools. There is gathering tools on the shop that do not break but it is over 2000 gems which is $25 or around 500 gold depending how you get those gems. Even at level 80 “junk” items you vendor you were lucky if you received one silver for it.Overall, I recommend trying this game only because it is free to play the core game. I personally liked the classes uniqueness, but I hate the current monetization model as it reminds me too much of Lost Ark’s approach (minus the pay to win). I personally would rather play Elder Scrolls Online and Final Fantasy Online as they felt like better games overall with better Monetization models.

_childDocuments_.review: Just shy of 5000 hours played so far, i haven't quit yet because i'm addicted and you will be too.It's an MMO, you will waste your life in here and love it ( until you play for a few thousand hours then you will start complaining about random ♥♥♥♥ like all the rest of the addicts do but keep playing anyway ).Some notable things about the game:tl;dr : Amazing combat system, fair monetization ( no pay 2 win, ignore anyone whining and saying otherwise ) PvE is great, PvP is great, WvW ( world vs world ) is great. Hop in and embrace the addiction, you will be a salty veteran a few years from now but it will be worth the 100$ ( i do recommend buying the entire thing eventually ).1. Amazing combat system - probably most fluid combat you will ever find in any MMO. Fast paced, looks and feels awesome ( not the biggest weight behind hits but it is what it is ), promotes movement and paying attention to your surroundings. You have to try it to see what i mean, there is a reason you will rarely hear active players complain about the combat system, it is just that good.2. No vertical gear progression - you will not be left behind if you take a break or don't have the time to grind 5 hours a day to keep your character relevant, put 10-20 hours worth of effort into a build and you will likely not need to invest into it again for months ( maybe years ) and still be able to do virtually all PvE content in the game. There is open world meta events ( probably the best of any MMO ), instanced 5 and 10-man content, tons of achievements to hunt - there is something for every type of player.Because there is no gear power creep most PvE content will always remain relevant / reasonably difficult ( unless class balance power creep kicks in ) and you will never be able to out gear content over time and trivialize it - either get good enough to finish the encounter or wipe forever.Also if you commit to it you can get a set of gear ( called legendary gear ) that basically means you will never have to grind gear for that character or any other character that uses said gear ever again.... sounds kind of neat doesn't it?3. Fair monetization - while you can technically * pay 2 win * by swiping hard and buying every single piece of end game gear you will need day 1 this will only skip the gold grind needed to obtain such gear, you will not be any more powerful than the average player that plays for a month or less and farms the same level of gear without spending any money.100$ for all expansions and DLC's might sound like a lot but you are getting 10 years worth of content ( a lot of it 7-8 years old and still relevant and actively being farmed to this day ) that rarely becomes pointless to return to. Start by spending 30$ on the newest expansion ( End of Dragons ), buy the other 2 expansions for another 30$ ASAP to unlock your character's full potential and work on acquiring Living World seasons ( the *DLC's* ) at whatever pace you see fit.There is an annoying amount of QoL that you can only find in the Gem Store ( the cash shop ) but this is ultimately a F2P micro-transaction based game, you will spend a lot more than the 100$ cost of unlocking all content over the span of your play time. Unlike other games however this one is more than worth the investment and support.4. PvP in an MMO that is actually balanced and skill based, WOW - PvP takes full advantage of the combat system, has normalized gear ( you cannot out gear or get out geared by your opponents ), is accessible from level 3, has automated tournaments every few hours and a big tournament with unique rewards every month.You will see tons of people calling PvP unplayable and unbalanced , super toxic, saying the match maker is useless and broken and that you should avoid the game mode. Most of those players are trash at the game and while some of the complaints are true most of the issues with PvP stem from the fact that not enough players engage with it - mainly because of the stigma surrounding it and not the state of the game mode itself.5. World vs World exists - gather people from your server ( or guild, coming soon* tm with Alliances ), run around taking castles, towers and keeps while slaughtering 2 other servers in a 3 way ( hmmm ) blood bath with 50v50v50 skirmishes, ballistas, trebuchets, catapults, flame rams, arrow carts and mass casualties. Yea, it's great.Too much typing, i'm going back to slaughtering stuff in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you value a ton of top-quality content, a fully voiced story-line built inside an immersive universe and the friendliest community you have ever seen in an MMORPG, Guild Wars 2 is probably the game for you. Guild Wars 2 takes place in the world of Tyria, the surface of which is home to numerous humanoid races and civilizations engaging with each other, but also where beneath all that, primordial beings known as the Elder Dragons are hibernating. Due to events taking place in the previous games of the series, five Elder Dragons have awaken from their slumber and are causing widespread destruction to Tyria and corrupting its inhabitants. The story is enormous, with many twists and external threats, but I guess this is the main take you should know before beginning your adventure. Everything else will be known in due time. GW2 differs from the usual MMORPG formula, there are no simple straightforward quests such "Kill 20 monsters" or "Gather 10 wood" to proceed. Instead of the traditional questing system, each area has its own unique dynamic events that bring each and every map to life, presenting you with its history by having players explore & interact with it. Each action has multiple outcomes that also result in new events, creating a cascade effect. In addition to that, you don't have to be in a party to participate and you can jump into the action at any moment, even if the event is at its peak. You can also join your friends anywhere, as levels don't really matter in this game. Your level and equipment are scaled to the map and the EXP reward is percentage based. If you have a friend who's ahead, or if your buddies are only beginning, you can play content together with no real restriction whatsoever. One of it's biggest selling points is that GW2 is NOT Pay to Win. However, it is not Free to Play either. While it advertises itself as such, it's more like a trial of the main game. Let me explain:GW2 has 3 major expansions, which I'll refer as HoT (Heart of Thorns), PoT (Path of Fire) and EoD (End of Dragons). The core game is essentially available to everyone, but some key game-play elements such as Gliding, Mounts, a bunch of different class specializations etc. are locked behind said expansions. Purchase them separately or as a bundle, once you do, you will not have to spend another dime in game, at least until a new expansion comes along. You can still top-up and buy cosmetics or quality of life stuff for your account, but everything in the shop is also purchasable with in-game currency. That includes Living World Seasons, which are lore based episodes of content that act as the ongoing story-line between expansions, giving access to numerous maps and features. You can think of them as mini-expansions.You want to experience PvP in this game? No fear. Structured instances of PvP in the forms of a few individuals or even worlds against each other are easily accessible with just the click of a button. Most of the stuff (including class specializations) in casual or competitive PvP is available to everyone, meaning trying out builds or different classes is quite easy, or even encouraged in some cases.Fashion; Hate it or love it, cosmetics are a huge part of Guild Wars 2. You’ll be frequently unlocking skins throughout your adventures, either by looting them, crafting them or by purchasing them from the trading post/cash shop (which you can do using in-game currency, as mentioned earlier). Once a skin is unlocked, it is usable account-wide. Now here's the big reveal; dyes. You are able to dye your equipment with hundreds of different obtainable colors, making fashion a complete headache. You want wings? Sure. You feel like being a walking fire hazard? Go ahead. There are so many different combinations that you will spend many hours creating your own outfit, or you can just copy someone else's if you don't feel like going through this process.End Game; There is no real end-game in Guild Wars 2. The game is enormous and it's always evolving. You can have thousands of hours put in game and still have stuff to do. You can craft Legendary equipment (which is a very long process), work towards account progression, dungeons, strikes, raids, fractals, you name it. You can even hunt for collections or aim to reach the top rankings in competitive. For a game that launched back in 2012, Guild Wars 2 has been very well maintained considering that most games of this genre die out after the initial hype is over. The constant release of new content over the years makes GW2 a game with hundred of hours of unique game-play, innovative ways to explore the MMORPG genre and a compelling story that starts out slow but ends becoming breath-taking. My recommendation is that you should simply play the game for the first dozens of hours without getting any expansion, test the waters (something like a trial period), and then if you feel like exploring what this game has to offer, which you probably will, go ahead and enrich your experience. I'll only say this: enjoy the ride.Edit: some minor spelling mistakes

While mounts are different here, sure, none of their skins can be obtained by playing the game, everything from the cash shop.Gold can be directly converted from cash, which then can be used to go from lvl 1 to 80 in an hour, or more importantly you buy crafting materials to level up your crafting skill, which can then be used to craft BiS gear, that will forever be BiS because more powerful gear hasn’t been added in almost 10 years.To be fair, it is also possible to convert gold into cash shop currency, so technically everything can be obtained by playing, but you will need absolute insane amounts of gold or getting lucky by some other means like infusion drop or my preferred method, gambling.No matter how you look at it, cash provides significant gameplay advantages not just cosmetic skins, by that definition it is p2w. Gameplay is trash.Great swords and hammers often attack just as fast as dual daggers or pistols making the combat feel floaty and weapons weightless. Absurd visual clutter due to stack meta in group content, combine that with ancient engine, dx9, 20+ people, and you get an absolute vomit of colour sounds and low fps even on high end machines.Extreme class imbalance in both PvE and PvP. You can play a class that requires you to memorize 60 step rotation and deal less damage than some brainlet that autoattacks with a mechapet.PvP hacking goes unpunished for months, soft-botting is pretty much allowed. Parking your character with 5 autoattacking pets or AoE autocasting and leaving him there for days is allowed. Server vs Server open world PvP mode has been completely abandoned for years.Rewards for doing content are pathetic.Nothing is rewarding. Developers put in obvious effort when making the interface and loot systems to shoehorn you into buying bag space. Adding no less than 30 different grey vendor trash items, hundreds of crafting materials and other junk. Every new map they release adds new currency and junk into the loot table, bit by bit they continue worsen an already bad and convoluted loot system.New, more powerful gear hasn’t been added since Nov 2012, so content rewards are usually just crafting mats and vendor trash. You killed the map boss? Trash items and matsYou finished a dungeon? Trash items and matsYou left your character afk farming? Trash items and matsIt is almost as the devs want you to do braindead afk farming instead of actually playing the game. I would argue it is more profitable to just set up an afk farm and go to bed than go raiding. Exploration rewards also, without fail, disappoint every single time. You found and completed a jumping puzzle and opened a giant golden chest at the end? Enjoy lvl 20 gem, two silvers, grey trash item, and an unsellable medallion that you have to manually destroy. It’s like that every single time.Because it doesn't matter what class you play, what gear you have, what content you're doing, I would only recommend the game to those that want to pretend like they're playing an MMORPG instead of playing one.Guild Wars 2 is a perfect example of a bad sequel and failed potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this back when it first launched in 2012. I had a ton of fun back then. This game just feels better than most other MMOs I've played.  I love the feel of movement and combat in the game. You can't use as many abilities at once as you can in other MMOs, but the abilities that you can use at any given time are powerful, useful, and tend to look cool as hell. Movement is great and they really leaned into it with jumping puzzles. If you are walking around and you see something that looks jumpable it probably is and could very well lead to a secret treasure. Many of the secrets are not marked on the map, so it honestly feels like you stumbled into an area you aren't supposed to be in. I love it every time.The free to play version is the entire original version of the game and you can get to max level. The DLCs and Living World charged expansions add a stupid amount of content on top of that. If you want a game you can sink your teeth into and explore this is certainly a good one to look at.If you get this version it ties your Steam account to the launch. If you haven't played before no big deal ignore this paragraph. If you are a returning player look up some guides on how to tie the Steam launcher to your existing account. Otherwise it will launch into a completely new account and you won't have any of your existing stuff.This game has a great community. Pretty often I can be getting into trouble and a random person or two will drop out of no where to help. Or I drop out of no where to help them. Even if you mostly play solo it's easy to still feel like you're part of a community and find ways to help out. In the open world the game is a bit casual. There can definitely be challenges like world bosses and things, but for the most part the open world is where you go when you just want to chill. If you want a challenge join a guild and start hitting up things like structured PVP, world PVP, fractals, and raids. Guild Wars 2 does a great job of just letting you play how you want to play. You want to mostly level up by making stuff. It'll take a bit, but you can do that. You want to just explore everything. Knock yourself out. You want to find challenges that push your skill. Go for it. I love this game and I think most people can find genuine reasons to love it too.

_childDocuments_.review: The best action MMO is finally here on Steam! If you're looking for a new MMO to play, don't look for a New World to explore, look for one with a strong track record!Combat - 9/10The Guild Wars franchise is known for it's build craft, & GW2 features many choices to your gameplay. Your weapon & profession defines your skills. 9 professions with 3 specializations in total.As an action game, you have to actually dodge to avoid damage. Combat has tab targeting, but most target skills can be freely activated. Combat is highly co-operative. Skills can bounce off another & create combos using combo fields paired with the combo finisher, giving heals & buffs.Skill animations are grounded in reality. You don't cast ultimate meteor showers of demonic proportions to obliterate the enemy. The ultimate abilities don't feel ultimate, just strong skills on high cooldown. If you like flashy skills, you will be disappointed.Questing - 9/10One thing I miss in new MMOs is the leveling grind where exp comes from to quests, leaving grinding monsters moot. That is not the case with GW2. When combat is good, it’s something you want to do over & over. You play until you find a Dynamic Event, which takes you on a fully voiced action packed journey. Exp is given for participation in these events but feel natural as if it were from combat. Some Dynamic Events are fetch quests, but most involve combat.Meta Dynamic Events are bigger events where background story takes place. They are essential to the open world map progress to unlock gates or world bosses. Without the M in MMO, you will not progress; this design philosophy encourages high levels of co-operation. Unfortunately, some maps feel rather dead as everyone moves to play the newer content.Mounts - 11/10Each mount is unique, like playing Zelda with Epona but more. Each mount improves your ability to navigate through older & newer maps, making something that used to take forever a breeze.The Raptor, Springer, Skimmer & Jackal help you traverse the areas in Path of Fire. These maps have been built to utilize each mount's unique capabilities & incorporate mini puzzles to reach certain areas. The other 4 mounts are only obtainable after completing scavenger hunt/fetch quests.The Griffon plays like Aladdin on the magic carpet. (Cue "A whole new world~"). Revisiting the world from the skies is truly breathtaking, there are no words other than to experience it. The Roller Beetle is a slick motorcycle mount. The Skyscale is a different take on flight, being easier to control but less distance. The Siege Turtle, a returning favorite from GW1, obliterates everything with their cannons.No mount has disappointed except the Warclaw, discussed later.Story - 7/10The game starts you off on a "personal story" which is your origin story. It starts weak & disjointed due to being tied to leveling & dungeons, leaving you with a sense of dissatisfaction when you finish each mission. Elder dragons are a weak point of tension; “big evil” is hollow. If an elder dragon is involved, expect disappointment.The fifth chapter marks a major turning point, taking you on a real epic where the elder dragons become a backdrop to something greater. The latest chapter, "End of Dragons" signals the end of the elder dragon story arc. GW1 has rich lore that are yet to be tapped into. Expect better stories to come.The banter with the cast are very good, like banter from Uncharted 4. There's lots of technobabble used to disguise deus ex machina though. The addition of the communicator earpiece plot device helped drive better pacing & flow compared to previously with characters needing to pop in & out of missions.Economy - 2/10The gathering economy is strong & can be a main source of income for players, but you will be inconvenienced by limited use tools, pushing you to purchase the unlimited tools from the cash shop. One of the better things is the official gold seller service, letting you farm cash shop items with gold. Investing in unlimited tools do eventually help your sanity although it will take many years for that investment to actually pay off.Because of the cash shop, you are never rewarded. When you beat an epic boss, you will not obtain a nice skin for your weapons or armor. You will need to farm the same boss several times to obtain a currency that buy items to craft the skin. This pushes you to the highest gold/hour game loop. If you're looking for great skins you will only find them in the cash shop or after endless grind. When you do finish, the rush of dopamine does not feel satisfying because you worked for it.PvP - 6/10GW2 only takes Conquest mode seriously. There's a DotA-ish mode, we don't talk about that. Who you get matched up with usually matters in whether you will win that round or not. Unfortunately, this leads to player toxicity, as blaming others is made easy & inconsequential.GW2 often receives frequent balance changes, but the game will always have some level of imbalance so you'll have a certain meta to play with if you’re looking to compete. Some professions will not be competitive no matter how good you play. The competitive scene is non-existent, so it’s difficult to gauge if a build is top tier because it is popular or effective.There are only a few maps you will play on repeat. The lack of other modes hurt re-playability of PvP. After every season there is a mini season of TDM that lasts 2 weeks, which is a nice breather.WvW - 4/10WvW is like a game of Risk, defending your territory while invading & taking others, a war simulator complete with siege weaponry for knocking down gates & walls. The mode is addictive, until you play enough to see the flaws.The game mode is designed so that a win is based on points from capture & holding the structure to keep points rolling, so enrolling into the largest World gives you the best results. Many players avoid defense & look for fights when the population supports it. A good fight is a good day, even if you lose every tower & keep along the way. This leads to this game mode being simply a playground for big fights & the game mode itself just a backdrop.Since Heart of Thorns, WvW has no major changes. The last update was the Warclaw mount, which is inconsequential to the game mode.The dedicated WvW player base is the only thing that keeps it all together. Disturbingly, this player base is highly sensitive to content changes, where inclusion of the new Siege Turtle mount needs to be "heavily considered with the community" by the developers before including it into the mode. That's a lot of backward-ism going on.WvW needs the other mounts, period. Change the keeps & towers for better defense, & enable new attack vectors by flight, carpet bombing, etc. New incentives are needed for defense, e.g. economic incentives like gold or items. The mode needs players aligned to the objective.Conclusion - 8/10Ten years ago, this was my 10/10 dream MMO. It had everything; great combat, great PvP & a massive world to call home. The stories get bolder as it moves away from elder dragon lore. The mounts are incredible; all I do for fun is login, fly around a bit, then log out.Unfortunately, the lack of any updates to WvW, one of my favorite game modes, shows the game hasn't evolved all that much either. It's a great MMO that misses a lot of points to continue to become the dream MMO in 2022 standards. Treat it like a single player RPG that happens to have a lot of people playing. It’s best played together with a group of 5 friends, but you can play solo.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a player with years of playtime and it's a daily bread and butter for me.PRO: over the years they accumulated content that can provide entertainment for hours - assuming you won't steamroll thru itCON: convoluted content delivery - first 3 expansions come with additional content that either had to be unlocked while playing for free or purchased separaterly; steam offers Living World in the biggest and pricest bundle. Last two 2 expasnsions follow different release format - these are sort of standalone products, without any additional content.PRO: game pushes players into a cooperative gameplay - in the open world you play together to reach the common goal; loot, experience, gathering nodes are shared.CON: players coming from other mmo's may felt thrown into a deep water without a clear "what to do now" direction - there's no babysitting with detailed breadcrumb guidance. You need to set goals for yourself.PRO: game has very little downtime - it's all due to homebrewed solution of microservices for the server software. When you're forced turn off GW2 is either because of new patch being released (you still have time to finish what you do) or because something serious happen (they had 3 small rollbacks over 12 years). There's nearly transparent to the player equivalent of channels feature known from other games.CON: GW2 is heavily instanced - from open world, to story instances, to separated PvP mode; open worls isn't seamless and each map exists as a sliced out location which affects preceiving of the in-game world. There are two main servers: EU and NA and players from either cannot play together, so you need to pick server that's closer to you geographically and with time zone. There's no SEA nor OCE servers.PRO: quite appealing customization options for character model itself - you can pick between 5 playable races, 2 genders, 9 professions (9th comes with HoT expansion); then you have skins to unlock and dyes for armor pieces, weapons and backpack items. There are also one-piece costumes (outfits), and variety of skins for gliders, mounts, boatsCON: it takes time to unlock all that stuff; some argue that company abandon the unique visual coherence to satisfy tastes of particular playersPRO: you can convert in-game currency (gold) to cash shop currency (gems) and purchase anything you like without opening own wallet.CON: cash shop sells solutions for the problems they invented; upgrades purchased for characters can't be transferred, so you get inventory bags and then you delete a character (still a thing that is NOT recommended) these bag slots are gone.PRO: people playing this game are quite helpful and friendly - excluding the cesspool that sPvP is (but that's a standard for all games innit)CON: community outside the game in particular places gets easily manipulated; official forums are sanitized to the ridiculous levelsThe biggest PRO: base game is F2P (with set of limitations - annoying but these keep e.g. map chat clear out of gold spammers pretty well) - it's a very generous trial where you can see if it clicks for you. You can play it on Linux via Steam's Proton or other means like LutrisThe biggest CON: overall it didn't aged well when it comes to visuals or performance. It may looks pretty but custom engine is quite demanding and in some situations you need to compromise visuals for performance. Some people report  issues with stability even on best hardware. Hell, I managed to crash a remote streaming service setting up graphics to the max...This game could be a great world-wide success and indeed a "WoW killer" as it sometimes being amusingly called but because  decided to wear pink glasses and pretend to be a AAA studio, GW2 is a largerly ommitted title that surprises people who think it's being already shut down.
