_childDocuments_.review: This is my second go around with Guild Wars 2, I came back after I saw it on Steam. Guild Wars 2 is still the best MMO, but even the best MMO is flawed at best. First the good points:The graphics are even by today's standard terrific, everything is bright and smooth and looking at other MMO's of the same age you wonder how GW2's graphics are so much better. Nothing is blocky or chunky, actions are smooth and attacks 'hit' and aren't just you doing an animation at the enemy. Character customization and color, build and height options are all within a wide enough framework that it's easy to be unique even when you are the 'same' as someone else.The combat system is easy to pick up, hits and spells all feel solid and despite being easy to pick up it takes skill as the enemies evolve and use more attacks that you have to do the same. The tutorial as it is is simply part of the beginning story and the skills, spells and proficencies all flow together in an easy manner to understand even if it is all hard to master,The profession and skill trees give even the most rudimentary classes large amount of customization and it's easy to break out of the 'holy trinity' and play whatever style or combination of styles you want to mix. Several of the professions even have enough variety to swap focus on the fly or for a specific group or enemy.The in game community is mostly friendly and almost always helpful it's easy to join parties or just tag along even if you aren't in a guild and asking questions in global is almost never met with grief or elitism and there is very little spam or racist, sexist behavior it is a great environment.The map, it's huge but there are some caveats. The enemies are easy and mindless at first but as you progress and enter higher level territory you get enemies that are smarter and use many of the same skills, weapons and buffs that you and your party do. Group battles are almost never one-sided and many of them even at lower levels are often down to skill and teamwork to clear. Now the bad:That big map? Yeah, lots of it is locked behind quests and there is no way to directly travel to them until you have been there, exploration is hindered unnecessarily after the main map mainly to serve the story and that takes us to the second worst part of GW2The story lines, they are hot garbage. This is a game where you and thousands of other players are all 'The Chosen One' you are treated by the story lines as if you are the main character and that isn't bad except it is completely watered down once you see that is the same for everyone, and add that to the zero choices in the story and it is just garbage. For instance in the main quest you get choices of which order to join (No, you can't choose to not join an order, what are you stupid??) and you can choose some branches of the quest but if you do any alts and choose different options you quickly realize that the options are meaningless you end up in the same place doing the same things no matter what. What makes this worse is that several quests are still broken (they were broken in 2013-14 when I last played) and you will end up having to restart them multiple times to get the correct npc's, items and enemies to spawn. This is further compounded by the fact that no mater what you HAVE to be the hero, you HAVE to help and you have NO dialog choices or real choices that matter. You can ignore the story lines but in doing so you miss unlocking new maps, new gear, new dungeons and it sucks. The fact that there is not even the illusion of choice is just insulting for anyone that wants to actually RP and build their own story. Finally the worst worst part, Immersion. Nope, move along it's not here. No one is ever IC there are plush raptor and other mounts annoying 'minis' and plenty of hentai costumes so you can dress up your warrior as a big busted school girl or maid ffs. Most of the beautiful environment is just there to be looked at and maybe jumped on, there are so few chairs to sit in it's an achievement to find and sit in all of them. If a person doesn't have a quest marker on them they are a nothingface with throw away lines, what you see is what you get the immersion is only skin deep and even that dark gritty world at war skin is pock marked with balloons and harry potter broom mounts.To sum up if you want a solid MMO with lots of combat and spell customization, a wide range of professions and detailed and tough enemies and enjoyable groups and guilds and more ad-hoc co-op battles than you can ever want this is an A+ game. BUT like all MMO's the larger game caters to cosmetics and bling and the story lines were written to insult you if you take any time to do them.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Guild Wars 2 for 7k hours and I think it is still worth getting in 202X. It's a laid back casual friendly MMO with story based PvE where you don't have to worry about climbing the gear ladder or any other ladder. I stopped playing in 2016 and returned in 2020, picking up where I left, with my gear still being relevant. GW2 is a very player friendly game. You see someone struggling with a tough enemy? Help them, you'll get the same loot and experience, no need to fight for mobs and loot. You wanna play with a friend? Add them to your party, so they can join your personal story with you. Your friend created a character of a different race? Every starting zone has a waypoint unlocked by default, feel free to join them. Your friend's character is much higher level than yours? Their level and gear will be scaled down to the level of the location to keep it more challenging. Experience is calculated depending on the percentage of your EXP bar, so you (level 15) and your friend (level 65) will both get 15% of your EXP bars for completing an event on a level 10 starting map. There're always events, heart quests, world bosses and hidden locations for you to explore. And after getting your health to zero, you can still continue fighting in downed state and rally from killing an enemy.In my experience GW2 has very helpful community. You can't even jump from a height and die without someone running to revive you. If you need any help you can always ask in chat and most likely you'll find someone to help. There's also a lot of guilds that help new players. The game has great wiki, you can Shift + Click any item or ability and type /wiki before it to quickly find it on the wiki. ( /wiki [5 Iron Ore] )After getting to level 80, you should have enough gold and karma to get yourself full Exotic gear that has only 5% less stats than Ascended/Legendary gear, the best gear in the game. Now you're good to go anywhere and do pretty much anything. That's it, you're geared up. The next step is to get ascended trinkets with LW2 currencies or Laurels and when you save up some gold, craft yourself set of ascended armor, it will take you couple of weeks if you play a lot.For free you'll be able to play (with small limitations) only core GW2 content. But considering that people were paying for it $60 in 2012, it's a good deal, if you ask me. If you want to get any content released after 2015, you'll need to buy expansions and Living World seasons. Living World seasons were released episodically between the expansions, each episode usually having a new location and continuing the main story. Those episodes were given away for free if you logged in the game when they were released. If you missed them, they cost gems to get. My overall recommendation is to try F2P, finish personal story and Living World Season 1 (it's free) and if you like the game, get the complete bundle with Living World seasons, it will be cheaper this way.

_childDocuments_.review: I recognize that this game is beloved by nearly everyone that plays it, and for good reasons too; I can definitely see how Guild Wars as a franchise has made its way to the highest tiers of MMORPGs. However, this game put me to sleep twice, once at 8:40pm and again the next day at 5:00pm and in both instances I had only been grinding away levels for roughly two hours. The reason why is because the core gameplay, like many mmorpgs, is intensely boring. My gaming background includes adventure games like Zelda, Witcher, & Bethesda titles, along with various shooters and mobas, so when I trot around Guild Wars mindlessly slaying enemies to level up and the quests themselves are uninteresting, I'm inclined to pass out.I definitely did not play long enough to give this thing a fair and full review, and I definitely did not reach the end game content Guild Wars is famous for, but I simply cant turn my brain off to get there. _childDocuments_.review: I normally only review games on Steam that I actually play. Unfortunately I haven't yet played this game on Steam - because I have already racked up 6500+ hours on my main account through the official Gw2 launcher.Gw2 is the greatest MMO in terms of respecting your time. The gear treadmill from other MMO's may appeal to some, but for me, I like the fact that I can jump in and out of Gw2 every few months, and be no less powerful than when I left off. As mentioned, I have a LOT of hours in this game - you'd think I'd be out of things to do, right? Nope. If you're an avid achievement hunter, you'll be playing this game until you die. If you're a casual/social player, you'll find lots of wonderful people who enjoy the exact same sort of game-play.If you're a fan of MMO end games (or just more difficult content like me), Gw2 is a little on the sparce side of content drops. But what it does offer right now will still give you quite a few hundreds of hours of enjoyment. The game has raids, non-traditional dungeons called Fractals, scaling up to 100 (think mythic+), Strikes (basically smaller, self contained raid instances) and more.If you're a fan of massive open world PvP zergs, we've got that too!The game is free to play with some decent restrictions, but the expansions are buy once own forever. Dip your toes in to see if the gameplay looks cool enough to invest in (it is), and then prepare to dive head first, into the world of Tyria! I'll see you there.

name: Witcheye
detailed_description: Set off on an adventure as a mild-mannered witch who transforms into a flying eyeball of vengeance after a smarmy knight and wizard steal her spell ingredients. You'll guide her through 50+ levels, each containing something completely unique: tricky new enemies, mysterious new environments, and puzzling new secrets. These elements are brought to life with colorful, clean pixel art and a lively, head-bobbing original soundtrack. Witcheye is a new approach to platforming with a free movement dash through the air. Players are able to stop on a spot, reverse direction, or alter their course at will. Bounce into devilish little beasts, snag collectables and make it to the goal of each level however possible. Designer Peter Malamud Smith was the co-creator (with Charlie Hoey) of the viral hit The Great Gatsby For NES, and creator of the well-received mobile action puzzlers Satellina and Satellina Zero.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple but brilliant little game that really deserves more love and recognition, one of a few titles out there that has genuinely made me smile for more than a minute during gameplay. I loved everything from the bare but addictive core gameplay gimmick to the soundtrack which perfectly compliments the individual tone and feel of each short but sweet level, though the strongest front of WitchEye is hands down the beautiful pixel art and the effort that went into making levels that are essentially made of block tiles feel like living breathing worlds. It takes me back to when I used to make jank arse games using  and people had to draw their own tiles by hand. The art style and the range of palettes used for each tileset seriously made me tear up once from the memories they brought back, so I might be a bit biased due to my experience with pixel art but I can definitely say the visuals are top notch. Really good job on the presentation in general :thumbsup:Very minor nitpick but I felt a few noticeable spikes in difficulty within certain segments of levels (World 4's Colosseum miniboss would be a good example of this) though in general the difficulty never got too ridiculous and feels suitable for people of most skill brackets.Overall I'd say this one's a steal, considering the price tag (4 quid!), amount of content on show, the replay value that comes from the surprisingly deep secret hunting (considering the only inputs you make in game are mouse clicks and swipes) and the quality of what's on show. Pick this one up and give it a spin if you haven't already, it's bloody smooth!
_childDocuments_.name: Witcheye

_childDocuments_.review: Witcheye is a simple, well-made 2D platformer with unique controls, that's executed very well with nice pixel art and a really good OST that reminds me of Sonic games. The gameplay itself reminds me of the Kirby series, and I liked the short length of the main mode, definitely recommend the game and it deserves to be more well-known than it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Witcheye

_childDocuments_.review: Witcheye offers two control schemes: mouse and controller, and unfortunately, neither work for me. Finishing the game requires choosing between two tedious options. If using a mouse, you have to constantly drag and release in the direction you want to go. This is annoying, tiring, does not allow for precise movement as advertised, and prevents the player from moving quickly enough to avoid hazards. This could be fixed by having the player click anywhere on the screen, and moving the character in that direction until another point is selected.The other option, a controller, is slightly better and is what I used for the majority of my playthrough up until completion. The "dragging" principle is still the same here, since each change of direction requires a distinct swipe of the joystick. If you're heading diagonally downward to the right and you want to change your direction to diagonally upward to the right, you can't move the joystick in one motion. Instead, you have to bring the joystick back to the center and then move it in the new direction. See how this can be annoying?It's disappointing that the game's controls could've easily been fluid, and my experience would've been enhanced tenfold. I can only imagine how much more fun it would be if you could just move by holding in the direction you want to go, rather than constantly, repetitively swiping in a new direction.It's a short game, only took me about 1h30m to complete each level on normal difficulty, but it would've taken less time if I had more control over the character. The length of the game isn't an issue for me since the levels offer replay value with their collectibles, as well as increased difficulty with a hard mode, speedrun mode, and severe mode. Due to the controls, there is no way I'm going to attempt these anytime soon, and it sucks, because I definitely would otherwise.Some minor nitpicks: - The wall bouncing mechanic served no purpose in my playthrough. The game would feel more responsive to my inputs if it were removed. Bouncing off of enemies felt fair.- The cutscenes are long enough that they should be skippable. Some players just want to get into the action, so keeping these optional is nice.- A good portion of the enemies can be entirely avoided, though, I doubt this would even be a complaint at higher difficulties.If Witcheye was updated with improved controls, I would recommend this game in a heartbeat. Despite its shortcomings, I enjoyed myself. The game is high quality: the art is charming, all the character designs are excellent, there are a wide variety of enemies and bosses with clever attacks, the soundtrack is nice, sound design is well-done, environments are immersive. It's a solid experience and is clearly the product of mindful developers who have a proficient understanding of design. Sadly, the controls can make or break a game for me, and because of that, I can't recommend it solely for that reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Witcheye

_childDocuments_.review: A green-skinned young witch named Mabel Syrup turns into a big, bouncy eyeball (why not a boob, liver, or buttock?) to recover her stolen magical ingredients in this incredibly novel take on the breakout subgenre.  While smashable blocks  there in plenty, the majority of the challenge comes from the huge roster of foes and their extremely well-animated attacks, which increase in number and swiftness with the jump to hard mode.  Normal is pretty dang easy on the whole -- almost  in spots -- so I would encourage veteran 2D gamers seeking a bigger bang for their buck to immediately go for hard after beating the base game; all bosses are noticeably beefed up, not with more life or attack power, but with trickier patterns and maneuvers, and this is objectively the  way to do such things.  Bravo! Since we're getting to a spot where the average Steam user has about 1000+ games in his library, the amount of attention the typical indie gets is plummeting like a cartoon anvil, with experiences that "open up" later frequently being discarded before they get a chance to shine.  On that note, I'd like to reassure anybody on the fence with this one that the depth and wildness of  invention  after the first world, which is merely a fun, but admittedly staid training gauntlet -- so stick with it if you want to get into all the super-fun (and legitimately funny) stuff.  Short, clever, highly replayable, pretty as heck, bug-free, and with a crazy diversity of jazzy tunes,  is worth it at full price, and an absolute steal on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and fun. A pinball arcade game with easy control- drag mouse to alter directions and click to stop are all you need to do. The highlight is the pinball rebounds after hitting the border, which could be a challenge/strategy to attack or avoid bullets.Each level is a few minutes long, it's a 2D horizon scroll game where the player enters room after a room. Occasionally it is locked and requires to clean all enemies, but most of the time you can play at your style and pace: either defeat enemies to earn crystals and test the skill, or dash to the exit to see what's in the next level. Maps and enemies are various and satisfying with good pixel art, most boss fights are creative and can be a bit intense, some requires hit precisely like the serpent boss with bulbs, some requires good timing like the cloud boss blows wind every a few seconds, some test your reaction like that crazy pumpkin try to crush everything in the way.Witcheye is not hard, and friendly by offering heart drops often. Worth the time and price, I would like to play more interesting games like this. Great job!

_childDocuments_.review: A neat little game that you can easily play through in one sitting. You play as a witch trying to get her treasures back, so she transforms into a floating eyeball that bumps off of surfaces and follows the thief. The game gets kudos from me for the amazing enemy design; not only does the game incorporate a ton of enemies into a 90-120 minute game that all behave differently, but they are also all intuitive. One look and you know exactly how they behave, what you have to do to kill them and where you can hit them. The intelligent and creative enemy design is definitely the star of the show here, which is why it's weird to see how incredibly boring the only three human characters are. The worst is our protagonist, the witch; I don't think I have ever seen a more bland character design, both in human and eyeball form. It stands in huge contrast to all the enemies. The two human antagonists, generic wizard and generic knight, are similarly bad, but not quite as bland. It's a bit sad that the extra mile was not gone in regards to our protagonists design.That small faux-pas aside, the game is good, short fun. If you liked playing through it, there are harder modes unlocked afterwards, but I was satisfied with one playthrough. Definitely worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.name: Witcheye

_childDocuments_.review: Witcheye feels like a faithful remake of a long-lost PC Engine game. The gameplay is as simple as it comes. You control the titular witch's eye as it floats through completely linear levels, doing your best to bonk enemies before they do the same to you. That simple gameplay is accompanied by simple pleasures; The spritework is very cartoony and the soundtrack has lots of upbeat synthesizer ditties. There are dozens of ways this game could be expanded upon to create a more substantial experience, but that's not what the developers did and I respect that decision. Witcheye operates on a level of pure simplicity, and that makes it a tad more authentically retro than many other throwback attempts.

_childDocuments_.review: wow do i have some thoughts. the soundtrack in this game is amazing. i absolutely loved it, and definitely plan to listen to it on my own time outside of the game if possible. the sound effects were also great, and the art is very appealing. as for the gameplay, i was not a fan. flicking the joystick to shoot in one direction is the main gameplay mechanic, and i was open to it in the beginning. however, the mechanic itself was not satisfying at all. some of the enemies were insufferable, and i found myself trying to avoid the enemies entirely a lot of the time, even though it's kind of the whole point of the game. some of the enemies just required so much precision from a non-precise gameplay mechanic that it was entirely too tedious. the game is also just too short. i beat it in just over an hour and a half, and it ramps up in difficulty too quickly before the player can get used to the controls and get better with it in time. in the beginning i was flying through the levels, and 30 minutes later i found myself replaying every level 5 times because i just kept dying. in a lot of games, trial and error can be incredibly difficult but rewarding and satisfying. in this game, it was just irritating. i like challenge in my games, but not without satisfaction. however, despite my complaints, a lot of people seem to like this game and at only $5 i can't really super strongly recommend against it.

_childDocuments_.review: Short, simple little arcade-styled game, probably best-suited for mobile, if it wasn't for all the secrets you have to keep an eye out for. Witcheye is a game that doesn't really expand on its ideas after the first chapter,  choosing not to introduce new power-ups or make the player feel strong or skillful, but by introducing tons of new enemies very frequently and just asking you to figure out how to approach them. In that respect, I can admire the design sensibilities on display here, even if I didn't think the level design was all that great. It looks and plays well, and it's cheap, so I think it's worth your time, but not for everyone. 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: There something here, it just needs a little more work...Pros:- Good pixel graphics- Interesting gameplay mechanic that I haven't seen before- Good variety of enemiesCons:- Becomes repetitive VERY quickly (I stopped about halfway through this game and it really doesn't get much deeper than "hit eyeball into thing" mostly)- Crystals are extremely unintuitive to find and not fun (some levels it's up to luck when fighting monsters and sometimes you're literally just hitting every random area of the screen to try to trigger a hidden crystal drop)- Not much combat variation (I did pick up a sword at one point and thought "neat, there should be mechanics like this all over the place, kinda like Kirby. Sadly, twas not so.)- Not much level variation (Different shapes of rock to bounce off mostly. Could have done a pinball level, a level with gravity and the eyeball could jump instead of float, top down bullet hell level like ikaruga, etc.)- Story isn't compelling or interesting (Wizard tells knight to get witch's stuff. Gets stuff. Drops it along a path. Witch gets stuff.)TL:DR - I think the developer is on to something here and I hope they keep making games and building on their ideas, but I think this needed more time at the drawing board to become a real hit. Buy it on sale if your curious, otherwise go play Shovel Knight to get a better variety of experience in this kind of genre.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game!I haven't been this enthusiastic about a video game in a very long time. It takes a lot more to stimulate my adult brain than it did fifteen years ago, and Witcheye's one of very few games that manage to successfully capture what it felt like to play video games as a kid.Graphics are absolutely gorgeous, and the soundtrack is surprisingly rich. There's a ton of different themes (one for every single stage ?), and they're all really inspired and catchy. It was a groovy ride, and the entire artistic direction brings back a lot of childhood memories.Enemies and bosses are numerous and amazingly creative, and the level design is impeccable. Absolutely nothing feels out of place.There are also a lot of different ways to play this game. Do you want to take your time and breeze through ? Are you in it for the challenge ? Either way, the game's got you covered. There are 3 very well-designed difficulty settings (Enemies and bosses have entirely new patterns in Hard mode!), a boss rush, a miniboss rush, and a speedrun mode (pretty basic, it's not like it has built-in splits or anything, but it's there, and that's something I'd like to see in every game).It's great. A tad short, unfortunately (just completing it once without bothering with secrets takes a couple of hours), but it has a lot of replay value, and it's just so clever and rich (and cheap!) it's definitely worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but fun platformer with a refreshingly unique core mechanic, movement can be frustrating at first but feels great once you get the hang of it. The boss fights are well designed with plenty of surprisingly fun minibosses along the way, sometimes preparing you for future levels and other times giving you a chance to show off what you've learnt. The soundtrack is good and varied enough that it doesn't feel repetitive, and the visuals have a nostalgic Kirby-like feel to them. Definitely worth it for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly phenomenal and unique take on exploring the platforming adventure games that we already know and love. Others mentioned the clear Kirby inspiration, along with Mario and some of your other classics. The splash art, the short levels with collectibles, it's all thought out very carefully to deliver a very special message:Just have fun with the game.It's just a fun platformer. It's not super hard, it's not super complex with the story of Five Nights and some kind of special attack/cancel tech to beat the game even faster. It's about being a f'ing bouncy ball playing these levels. It's amazing.As someone that just beat Super Meat Boy for the exciting platformer that makes you bleed from how difficult it is? I loved that this game went the other direction, reminding me that some games aren't about getting good, it's about playing the game created and just having fun.Highly recommend, I would instabuy a sequel

_childDocuments_.review: little game--big thoughts, though! i really like witcheye, this reworking of kirby's skeleton to create something more challenging and addictive (in short bursts). instead of both copying abilities and floating around, you're the latter except weaponized, and obstacles lie in navigating stage hazards detrimental to floaters like you and enemies who vary in ways to defeat. all of this is wrapped up in a package of absolutely gorgeous pixel art and a heaping of sickeningly sweet 16 bit groove (so much midi bass). it's pretty fun to figure out how to defeat new enemies as they appear, soon mastering the ability to just wipe 'em out the moment they appear on screen, your forward momentum undeterred. sometimes it can feel very sloppy and you'll somehow effortlessly glide through a level despite not really knowing what's happening, but you learn. a particular highlight is the kirby styled locked miniboss fights, many really inventive. there's also this whole deal about collecting gems, but it's honestly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥: many, many times a gem will clip through the ground and disappear, and i'm having fun, sure, but i'm really not that interested to replay a level just to grab more bing bing jewels.you know, probably the worst and weirdest thing about this game is the design of the main character and her alter eye ego. exceptionally bland: why? all of the enemies are charming even if many are reskinned waddle dees and gordos. the bosses are pretty cool, too... so why does the main character look so nothing? her name's mabel syrup but how could you even know that when all she sports is a dumb purple frock and matching hairbun? and the eye is just... an eye. i'd really like to draw some fanart for witcheye, but good lord it won't be the main character.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's only $5, but even with that it's worth well more than that.  Gameplay is simple and easy to pick up, levels are short so death doesn't mean you lost 10 or more minutes, and the secrets are hidden enough to be tricky but rarely so hard as to be infuriating.  A single playthrough is 3-ish hours for a 100% completion, but then that unlocks the harder difficulty with remixed enemy placements, tweaked behavior, and changed placement of the secrets and collectibles.  There's a second even harder difficulty which I imagine changes things in a similar way, but I can't say for sure.  And that's not even mentioning the other modes like boss rushes and speedruns (which this game seems intended for).

_childDocuments_.review: Set off on an adventure as a mild-mannered witch who transforms into a flying eyeball of vengeance after a smarmy knight and wizard steal her spell ingredients. You’ll guide her through 50+ levels, each containing something completely unique: tricky new enemies, mysterious new environments, and puzzling new secrets. short_description: Post Void is a hypnotic scramble of early first-person shooter design that values speed above all else. Keep your head full and reach the end; Kill what you can to see it mend; Get the high score or try again.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it when a game is new. Post Void isn't just a shooter, it's a rogue-like score-attack shooter with a time limit. That's new. And it all works, too.	You can finish this in under an hour, but a death sets you back to the beginning. There are no permanent upgrades for subsequent runs, so you just have to git gud. 	Finish the levels before your mug runs out of juice. This juice slowly dripping away also doubles as your life bar. Get hit; get that much more depleted on juice. Kill something and your cup fills up slightly. 	So just keep shooting and killing, move fast, and don't get hit. It's disgustingly exhilirating playing this.	What I like more than something being new is it being so in style. And Post Void has style. Trippy art direction, with the levels slanting and moving as you move. The colors accentuate this. The only way to describe it is a deep-fried look/feel, after being dipped into acid. 	I have this little rating system in my head. Most games are average, so a 5. Few games are an 8 (that's usually GOTY level stuff). If I had to rate Post Void I think it's at least an 8, if not a 9. It's such a simple game but it's incredibly made. It's so easy for rogue-likes to devolve into slow affairs, with procedural generation being an excuse for actual level-design. But Post Void doesn't falter in this department.

_childDocuments_.review: "CHANGE YOUR WEAPON INTO A SHOTGUN"Post Void is a clear example of something that works for a lot of players out there, in those moments where you don't want to invest your time into a full and longer experience and playing this simple yet addictive game just works.Kind of the same feeling as "Cruelty Squad". When you get in, the only thing you can say is "what the hell is going on" but you get hooked really fast.One of features that makes it so addicting is its focus on speed.Speed in boomer shooters has always been a part of the game, the original "DOOM" even displaying the time you spent on the level when you reach the exit, but here, it has been made into the focus of the game.If you don't kill any enemies, you will die in about 12 seconds, this makes the player be constantly on the run and on the look-out for enemies to shoot so they can maintain their life, although enemies can really bring you down if your bullets hit you.With an awesome track that never gets old playing in the background as you speed through the several gauntlets, each different with their challenge, Post Void is one of those experiences where you hit "Play" whenever you want and have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to what a lot of the negative reviews are saying: This game is not "maze-like", the path to go is extremely easy to follow. Despite the health system being punishing, I think it really makes this game unique and gives you a sense of urgency, which I love. The game is similar to a rogue-like where you start from level 1 every time you die, but because of the perk system and semi-randomly generated levels, the game doesn't get frustrating, old, or boring.My only criticism with this game is how short it is. This game took me only 4 attempts to beat, and if you can see my hours at the time of this review that about sums up how short this game is. However, I'm sure the developers will add new levels in the future as this game is only in beta.9/10 I love it, and for the price it's definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A devious little FPS based around a single concept: you're constantly losing health and the only way to get more health is to kill enemies. Every single second is a mad dash to kill something and from that one core concept a mad scramble of desperation and excitement takes form. I don't generally find myself interested by "rouguelike" or "procedurally generated" levels because they don't really feel "curated" the way a level in say Doom would, but the base mechanics are simple enough that you really just need the level design to give you some blocks to weave in and out of to let the manic combat shine. From the very first level, you're on a power trip. While you might only have a pistol at first, that pistol is a one-hit kill if you score a headshot and I was quite pleased to find myself getting more precise at that the more I played. Each level you beat gives you some new option like an uzi or exploding enemies, and the feeling of becoming more and more powerful with each passing level is great. But just because you have more skills doesn't mean the game gets easier, I've only surivved to the fourth round so far and the levels get a bit more complex to navigate and you start to see some tougher enemies like Half-Life 2 style Manhacks that are harder to hit. I'm looking forward to seeing what comes later and I can't imagine how insane the final level must be. While you start from zero every time, I never mind going back to that basic pistol level because even that basic starting point is just fantastic. Each of the weapons feels fantastic and all of the powerups really switch things up while still keeping the core game loop the same. Any game that you can play for 5 minutes or an hour and still have as good a time is great and this will probably be one of my go-to timekillers for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gem of an action roguelite, like a much faster-paced first person version of Nuclear Throne. Your HP depletes rapidly (something like ten to fifteen seconds from full health if you don't get shot) and you restore it by getting kills. There's enemy progression as you advance through the various levels and you get kicked back to the start when you die. The aesthetic reminds me of Cactus' games a bit, particularly Hotline Miami but also the interactive music video he made called Keyboard Drumset ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Werewolf. The headshot sounds are the crunchiest I've heard in a 2.5d shooter and the weapons are cool, though I think the starting pistol might actually be the best option. The procedural generation is good enough for the purpose - repeating elements are obvious but all that matters is you don't know exactly where the next enemy is.

I bought the game, showed it to one of my friends, he ended up buying the game and actually beat it before me. When I was playing, I was using the pistol for the most part. The Uzi had too much recoil and made it hard to track targets. The knife was neat, but I couldn't get the hang of it. My friend then recommended I use the shotgun. I was confused at first because the shotgun has this LONG reload cycle. Well, it's not that long. But it was long for the way I was playing the game. When I played I would just try to get to the end as fast as possible. If I missed a guy, I would just leave him behind. However, when I started using this double-barrel, something clicked. My play-style completely changed. Instead of rushing through, I slowed down a bit to make sure I was clearing my path of every obstacle (slowed down relatively speaking. The game is still plenty fast-paced). This is what ultimately led me to finishing the game.I loved my time with this game. I've showed it to plenty of my friends and will continue to dabble with it in the meantime. Content wise I don't have anything left, however I am going to try to beat the game using the various other weapons just for fun. Sure I'd like there to be more content, but the amount of value that is presented at this pricepoint is hard to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void is like a never-ending fever dream. A mindless, hyper-charged sequence of gore and violence that often feels like it’s over before it starts -- if you can even identify the seams between your runs. You sprint and you kill. Rinse and repeat. Anything else will end you in seconds, as the giant, bold count-down reminds you of whenever you find a lull in the action.After a while it even hits that Hotline Miami edge, where you’re completely desensitized to the visual spectacle of the action. And that’s saying something, considering how uniquely expressive the game is with all its trippy and grotesque imagery.Everything turns into snap calculations and muscle reflex, with a relentless pacing that constantly has you on-edge; constantly within death's grasp. In any other game, in any other setting, the loop of never-ending restarts and retries would be a frustrating grind. Here it’s just par for the course, and so elegantly designed it’s hard to put down.It’s an exciting experience if you can stomach it. And definitely an effective and dizzying escape from reality. Even if it’s only for ten or fifteen minutes at a time. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: [Post Void] is a fever dream. It's a squigglevision, Kafkaesqe colorful nightmare. But what exactly  [Post Void]? On its surface, [Post Void] might look all flash and no substance. Even if that were true, the flash is enough to make it worth the low price of admission. But the game offers more than a feverish art style.One part rogue-lite, one part corridor shooter, and a simple dash of time attack make up the soul of [Post Void]'s gameplay. You start the first level equipped with only a pistol. Your objective is to shoot your way through a maze of narrow corridors to the glowing portal at the end of the level. You then get to choose one of three random upgrades and jump right into the next map.What makes [Post Void]'s gameplay loop challenging, rewarding, and above all , is each level is both procedurally generated and progressively more difficult than the last. Adding to this is a constantly draining health bar, represented by the idol your character holds in their left hand. Killing enemies is the only way to fill the idol. This creates a tense, pressing need to quickly gun down enemies and always move forward. Failure to do so leads to death, sending you back to the very first level. Points are awarded based on your accuracy, enemies killed, headshots, and the level you reached. Rinse. Lather. And repeat as desired. Fortunately, this frantic action is complemented by simple yet satisfying shooting. Guns handle tight, their recoil feels weighty, and crisp pixelart animations offer juicy impacts - heads pop and spray pinkish gore across walls and ceilings. Tight corridors and some nice vertical touches make gunning down enemies, and avoiding their attacks, surprisingly difficult at times. The ability to perform a stylized slide can assist you in outmaneuvering enemies or quickly closing the distance for a speedy takedown. Otherwise, speed and reaction time are your only friends here. Maybe the only downside is a limited selection of weapons: the starting pistol, a sawn-off shotgun, an uzi, and a knife. Switching to these weapons is only available in-between levels, and are part of your three random options. This adds some RNG flavor to the mix, but can be frustrating if you have a preferred playstyle. [Post Void] is proof that simple yet well-executed gameplay and an inspired art direction can create a masterpiece. At only $2.99, this game is an absolute steal. I've paid over three times the price for games that were less original, less entertaining, and left less of an impression than [Post Void]. If you're considering picking this game up, do it. It's one hell of a ride.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sucks ass, but it's so cheap that it's worth recommending. It comes close to being great, but it ends up falling flat on it's face and just being ok.It has a pretty solid and fun gameplay loop, but the visual presentation takes a ♥♥♥♥ all over it.Let me ask you a question. Have you ever wanted to play Doom, but every time you pull the trigger, someone covers your screen with piss and ♥♥♥? Because that's how this plays. It's very fast, and puts heavy emphasis on constantly moving and hitting as many headshots as possible, since that's the fastest way to kill enemies, and, as previously mentioned, you want to keep moving. Sounds pretty straightforward, right? Yeah, that's because it is. None of the perks really change this core concept, so that's what you're coming for, and that's what you're getting.On the topic of the perks, they're actually terrible. Two thirds of them don't really do much, some of them are actually terrible (see: Shotgun). Honestly, you want faster reload, bigger clip and the uzi. You can get the other ones if you want, but they're not exactly optimal. As for the weapons other than the uzi, the knife is alright, but doesn't scale well into the later acts, and the shotgun is god-awful. In a game where you want to be constantly shooting, it has two shots and the longest reload time out of every weapon. To make up for it, it has higher damage, enough to one-shot every enemy. The problem is, even with that increased damage, it still loses to the starter pistol in raw dps, because hitting headshots also kills things instantly.The story was pretty vague, to the point that I'm convinced it's actually intentionally meaningless. I have nothing to say about it, because if it has anything to say, I didn't get it. The post-void is as empty and meaningless as the old void, it seems.To conclude, I'll put my main argument nice and short:It has pretty fun gameplay for the price tag, I wish I could have seen it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool.It's totally unlike any of the FPS games I've played recently - closest one I can think of is DUSK - because of it being psychedelic (flashes, visual and audio affects, etc.), and having an art style that's a mix of PS1-era, pixel, grunge, and horror, while keeping the game play to-the-point with a thirty second to one minute long tutorial.I have finished the game and the bulk of the story seems to be told via the intro and rest via the player interpreting what's happening (since the intro is so vague - its also really cool). It works for this kind of game given the tags (FPS, action rogue-like, psychedelic, etc.). Its subjective, but I really liked the message of the story. It seems like the message is more universal - appealing to a wide variety of people - than one might initially think. If you're worried about not being something you could play for more than 5 hours in like a week and not get sick of it and you're skill with FPS titles ranges from horrible to above average, I think you're fine; it will be hard enough (under certain terms - well talk about that). Unless you get a particular pair of upgrades (that I'll get to). The upgrades, the lengths of the levels, the enemy design (and even how bullets work in this game), all of these seem to well facilitate typical fast-paced FPS necessities like checking corners, proper time to kill - given how fast you have to be -, fast enough movement, and (while I don't think this is not a necessity in rouge-likes/lites - is giving the player a reason to go through the level quickly (in this game, it may be the high school or just for having fun). As for the rogue-like aspect of the game, it seems pretty solid. I don't have any gripes aside from one upgrade that I think is a bit too overpowered.  All I had to do was sidestep like a maniac and have decent aim and it was immensely easier than how it was before where I run directly at the enemy and either slide to avoid bullets or hope I nailed a head shot. I think it's overpowered, really - at least that combo is. Maybe, to fix this, there could be a trade off where you get slower movement but the bullets are just as slow as they are in the current patch. [/spoiler] It's a short and simple rogue-like FPS with a grungy, pixely, edgy, horrific, art style that facilitates the player to keep up consistent movement and aim while also playing around the upgrades they choose between levels. If I were to give it serious criticism it would be to adjust the movement and bullet speed so the player isn't pressing keys a and d like a madman to dodge bullets, and, maybe, it could be where they have to react to it instead of spamming keys a and d. Still, I found this game to be very fun - even towards the end I wanted to play a little more. I say that this is something special. It's cheap, unique, I found it to be super fun and seems to be well designed as a fast-paced rogue like FPS.

The underlying story in the game, and world is also quite unique and intriguing for what it is, however it's clear that gameplay is the main focus.Schizo weapons:The pistol has next to no recoil, reloads fast, and shoots fast. One/two shot hand cannon.The uzi has a fast rate of fire, and high recoil. A bit lower damage than the pistol (i think), but spits lead. Low damage, fast kills.The Knife is the only melee weapon in the game and forces you to get up close and personal. The knife has an alternate slash mode that lets you "charge" your next slash for more damage. Fast slashes and good damage, but forces you to take more damage as well Schizo tips:The bouncing bullets and explosive bullets are some of the best upgrades in the game, and are extremely overpowered, especially when combined.More Liquid in the Idol is also quite good upgrade, especially if you use the knife or pistol.Turn the audio off if you feel like you're about to get a headache, works surprisingly well. No, you don't just put a hole through an enemy's head, your bullets make it EXPLODE against the walls and ceiling. Eventually the soundtrack, the enemy noises, your guns... everything blends together as you dodge, shoot reload and... die. Again and again.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void is like a drug from a cyberpunk film. It spins, distorts, flashes, and screams with color. This is the kind of art that would absolutely wreck my dehydrated, anxious, caffeine-riddled middle school brain. Just ten seconds of it is enough to give you motion sickness, then a migraine, then you start to get it and fall into the loop. You turn it on and immediately it tastes like stale gas station coffee, alcohol, getting a headache between vinyl school bus seats and trying to tamp it down with lemon tea. Whichever way it bends, it's over just as quickly as it starts, and turning it off feels like being hit with a truck made of silence, like you just now realized how many layers of noise were happening to you and you had to quit cold-turkey.

_childDocuments_.review: + Exhilarating. To a point where if the game were any longer it'd bring on a headache. I'm not much of a shooter but little beats the quick draw corner shots, the satisfaction of clearing through more than you expected, passing over the high walls that separate the Acts, the suspense of the countdown...+ Gorgeous delirious retro vomit visuals. I can't really pin down what you call a mish mosh grainy style like this so I have to settle for adjectives, but I love it. Simply a mess!+ As short as the price. So few short-form games with this much tact, style, or vision seem to be made in the popular light.~ Not much too say of a story, though that's not so necessary for a quick one like this, and it's a fun potential of a concept anyway.- The visuals that aim to hinder vision work for their goal, but sometimes don't seem so intentional, like how vertical sections obscure the flat enemies from above. Feels like accidental difficulty, or at the very least not so satisfying.- Murder and speed are here in equal parts, but it can feel like the latter is incentivized at times, and some upgrades feel strangely picked.Ignore my negatives, they're more like rambling. This game is too short and spends its time too well to matter as to whether it's worth some spare change of time. If I was more of a leaderboard climber or a self-bester I probably would've spent a good few more hours with it, but I loved the short time I spent anyways. I would only really avoid it if you're sensitive to migraines or don't get off too much on adrenaline.( full review at  )

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void is probably the most unique new fps I've played this year.Pros-The cool unique art style might be a turn off to some but personally i love any game that breaks the norm of hyper realistic shooty game-The music in this game is a single track overarching track that plays throughout the whole game only having slight remixes between level transitions and the pause menu. This gives the game a feeling of non stop action, a feeling that there is no breaks, some people may not notice this at first, but this is one of the small things that makes this game great-The length of the game is in my book perfect, the game doesn't over stay it's welcome nor does it end to quick it's really great to see a game know when to end-The weapons are really fun to use, the generic pistol is a great beginning weapon and isn't all that bad for the first couple levels, but by around level 3 you should have access to one of the extra weapons which can all lead to different play styles, like when using the uzi you can pretty easily kill off enemies without needing to get a headshot, or with the knife you can play more on the edge in a constant state between nearly dying and getting just enough fluid for the idol, or with my personal favorite the shotgun you can basically play as chaotic as you want since it's basically a one hit kill, but you really wanna make sure you're full with ammo before running head first.-Another fun thing about this game is the slow progression of getting better and better at headshotting enemies it's absolutely integral to hone this skill to the best of your abilities as it's the easiest and fastest way to kill enemies, it's really fun to start off sucking a$$, but as you keep on playing being able to chain headshotting an enemies from half a mile away-And last but not least the gameplay!!!! The gameplay is such a unique concept I can't even wrap my head around it, I've never quite seen a fps game that focuses so much on speed and trying to finish a level as quick as you can. Throughout the game you need to carry your own head which is filled with fluids, but as you go on the head slowly drains away and once its empty you die, but for every enemy you kill the idol refuels more and more, to play well you really wanna hone your headshot kills since it's happened quite often to me I spend too much time hitting an enemy in the chest I run out of time with the idol. This one of the most unique fps gameplay mechanics and is a really great breath of fresh air from a lot of fps games blending together being the same old same old every year so it's really refreshing to see a change of pace for once in a while.It's not all good, just mostly. So anyways it's time to see what isn't so great about Post Void.Cons-The difficulty really is something here, personally I never unironically got upset at the game, but I could definitely see someone getting a little peeved off while playing, but this is really all subjective so I guess I couldn't call this a con really -Sometimes you can get really bad choice of perks, this isn't too bad of a thing to me since it's kind of fun to need to decide which of the worst you're gonna pick, but it definitely be obnoxious-Since all the levels are randomly generated you can so easily lose a really good run because you might not be able to find any enemies in time before the idol runs dry, you can also easily get stuck at dead ends especially if you're trying to dash through the level and have a horde of enemies chasing after you-Now even for how much I love the art style in this game it can really get straining on the eyes if you're playing for long periods at a time-And I don't know if this is a common occurrence, but whenever I start-up the game it runs really smoothly at the beginning but slowly starts lagging and slowing down more and more which kind of messes up the flow of the game. Now this could fully be caused by me often alt tabbing out the game to check texts and such, but it is quite a downer for a super fast pace game to kind of be ruined when it's slow as molasses, at times I could perfectly dodge enemy bullets cause it was going so slowBut all in all Post Voids a really amazing game and for such a low price its absolutely a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: You're a guy holding your own decapitated head in your hand, filled with liquid able to sprout a flower that will put you back to rest from the madness. In your way stand 11 levels full of horrific creatures trying to prevent that from happening. Every second, your idol leaks more of your life essence away. Every bullet, bite and slash will speed up that process even more. Drain it all and your life is over.This is most likely the most fast-paced game you'll ever play. You have absolutely no time to dawdle or gawk around. You have to push forward and obliterate everything standing between you and your goal. Time is extremely scarce and precious and taking more than a split-second to think about a direction or target priority will be the end of you. The further you progress, the more enemy types will spawn and vertical the levels will become, putting your ability to make fast decisions to the test.Enemies come in all sizes and flavors. It all boils down to killing them as quickly as possible - if moving on does not have a higher priority - but they all have their own quirks and need to be dealt with accordingly.You start with a pistol but you get to pick upgrades along the way. Some of these upgrades include a knife, shotgun and smg. They are all quite viable in their own way, even if it may not immediately appear to be the case.There is only a single song playing throughout the levels, other than in the introduction and main menu, but somehow it doesn't get boring or annoying. It fits the theme of the game quite well.The visuals are without a doubt extremely vibrant and flashy, as well as some of the sound effects being high pitched and obnoxious. While these things are woven into the crazy nature of the game, it brought some negative side effects with it. There is a good chance you'll get motion sickness or headaches if you're susceptible to such while playing this game, and especially if you're suffering from epilepsia it should be a no-brainer to stay away from this game.Furthermore, until you get anything else than your starting pistol, you are forced to spam mouse 1 a lot, which is also contributing to carpal tunnel, RSI or other related issues.An unfortunate thing is that the game actually tends to freeze in the later stages. So far this happened to me three times in 2 hours.If you actually manage to beat the game, it's basically a free 100% achievements game. A nice touch. It also comes with trading cards.An extremely fast-paced, flashy action roguelite. If lots of quick and eventful rounds are up in your alley, then definitely grab this game. The low price is definitely worth it for the amount of content within. Due to health related things however, it's best not to play this game for long intervals.

_childDocuments_.review: Post Void is a gleefully violent and eccentric roguelike first-person shooter which brilliantly calls upon a unique and wild energy in the player. Its clever gameplay hook forces you to play at top speed at all times, as you health is constantly draining, with only progressing and slaying foes to restore vitality. The gameplay is magnificently fine-tuned. Gunplay is responsive and thrilling, especially the delightfully crunchy headshots. Control is tight, with the slide providing an excellent way to hasten your charge. You'll always find yourself operating on split-second twitch reactions. Every time an enemy appears on screen, you have a sliver of a moment to make a crucial decision. You'll either need to scramble to down the foe for its health drop, or zip by it and hope you won't pay the price. I found myself wildly firing off shots any time anything so much as entered my field of view; it's crazy, chaotic, cathartic, and just plain fun.The power-ups you accrue are a mixed bag. Some can turn the tides in your favor tremendously, while others seem simply outclassed by other options. The shotgun seemed by far the best weapon in the game. It disposes of enemies ruthlessly, and synergizes best with the other upgrades. The uzi is powerful, but its recoil makes it less reliable. The knife is more useful than one might expect, but its range leaves it woefully ill-equipped to handle scenarios which will inevitably arise within the eleven floors. The reload speed upgrade feels negligible in effect, and I feel the greater immediacy - a crucial commodity in this game - of the ammo clip upgrade was wholly superior. Powering up your backwards run speed can be useful, but most of the game encourages moving ever forward, so it's quite situational, especially since you can outspeed most incoming threats by default if you're skilled. The compass is also situational, and often, when you most need it, you've already killed the run. If you need to reorient yourself toward the exit, you may have already turned yourself around, leaving your health sapping away with little to slay for recovery. Explosions on kills can be very powerful, especially in later, more cluttered areas. I avoided Ghost entirely, because the in-game description didn't convey its effect well, so I didn't understand the benefit. Slowing down bullets seemed like a downgrade, as it stalls progression in some cases, forced to wait longer for bullets to pass. The health upgrade is straightforward, but consistently beneficial. Finally, the bouncing bullets are probably the most powerful upgrade in the game, especially with the shotgun, as you can damage foes with less regard for precision, or you can even snipe enemies from safety with a well-placed ricochet.The enemies are suitably eclectic, and make for excellent challenges. Crucially, none of them are too threatening on their own as to consistently threaten to end your run out of bad luck. Each is manageable by itself, with the danger coming from their placement in the environment and the combinations of monsters in a given area.Visually, the game is striking, with psychedelic colors, bizarre monsters, and more. I especially enjoyed the constantly warping environment giving a sense of motion and urgency even in the off-chance you stop to breathe. I do feel the film grain is perhaps a bit too much when coupled with the constant motion of the scene, but it can be disabled. I also wish there was more than one song, perhaps one for each act, as the single track is solid, but it does get repetitive after several runs.Post Void is simple, yet it achieves its goal remarkably. It's heart-pumping, frenetic gunplay bliss, and I can't think of any FPS that delivers the same rush.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. There are some neat concepts here that could make the game fun, but so many design elements are conflicting with each other. It both wants to be a Hotline Miami FPS that wants you to beat levels quickly and die often, but then smashes that together with the rougelike genre by forcing you to beat all 11 levels in one go while also randomizing everything so you can't memorize layouts. These ideas go together about as well as orange juice and toothpaste.It's not even just how easy it is to be killed by enemies. The time health mechanic turns getting lost into a game over in a map layout that is very easy to get lost in. I made it to Level 4 twice and lost both times because I got lost. By that point I realized whatever was in the next 7 levels wasn't worth the frustration of playing the same levels over and over again with what seemed like very limited and uninteresting upgrades between them.If they just put checkpoints between levels this game I would probably be able to see past some of its annoyances, but having to start back at the beginning highlights its issues so much more. I just wasn't having fun while playing this. Thankfully it is only $3, but even then I've seen similar games at similar price points feel so much more fun to play (Vampire Survivor, 20 Minutes Till Dawn).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good as it gets so many things right.I like how it requires you to kill enemies to stay alive, It makes you keep up with the pace.And I like how killing enemies gives you enough health so you can still make good hit trades without perpetually getting upset about your constantly diminishing health. Dodging things are necessary but not punished too harshly if you're good enough at killing. I mean you never die instantly just because you're on low health.I like how it is literally a corridor shooter yet it is very confusing to look at when you first start playing.I like popping off crunchy headshots with the starting luger, it cuts a lot of time.I like how effective the uzi and the shotgun is against a crowd of enemies as i try to quickly line them up in front of the barrel.I also like nitpicking good games:The endgame of this short video game is not as good as the rest. Because at the beginning of the game you have your headshots to think about, it stimulates the player to think about killing a single enemy fast enough to get to shoot the next one. Then you grab your shotgun or uzi and now you don't have to think about killing one, but killing multiple enemies without wasting too much time before the next batch.But as soon as you get enemy death explosion and bullets bouncing off the walls, you're left without that kind of train of thought. You're now shooting in the general direction of bodies, and dodging things become less of an issue and more of a suggestion because you're regenerating a lot of health from your kills. The massive decimation and gore is still fun, but I wish those explosions were a grenade on a cooldown or something so it would still include me making decisions.It is also too short. Not because it does not deserve its money, but it left too good of an aftertaste, i want more of it.I hope you guys decide to make more shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Well...it certainly is a strong contender for a "WTF did I just play????"-award. As you can clearly see from the vids, the gameplay is fast, franctic to the point of nauseating and a gore-fest. So the feint of heart or easily suffering from motion sickness should stay clear. And if you're a sucker for violence, you probably have already bought it.But to the remaining readers (who want a review that isn't written by someone on acid), there's the question: is it actually any good? And I've got to say: yes. It honestly is. Not 50 bucks good, but easily 5 or even 10, so for 2.5 it's a steal.The "why" is harder to explain. The easy comparisons are hotline miami and super hexagon, as they're great in that same type: there's a certain flow you get into each of these games once you commit to getting better. A death is brutal and puts you back a lot, but up until that moment it can feel like you're poetry in motion.Post void is a first person shooter, sure. But more so than any other (and believe me: I've played 'em by the dozens) it rewards recklessness. More so: it's the only way to really get anywhere. Your life is constantly running out, killing enemies restores health, you've got infinite ammo and the level design is roughly a corridor with a few small dead ends to make it feel less so. Oh, and there's a reward at the end of each level.Result: if you're not sprinting toward the exit headshotting everything that moves in your way, you're simply doing it wrong.In that sense, the aesthetics and the gore make sense. You, the player, are suffering from some sort of bad acid trip. And the only way out is through. With the weird monsters (note: the explicit nature loses its shock effect if you see it fly by at mach 17). And the Z-axis that gets steeper with every level. And the...erm...well, that's mostly it.The biggest flaw is that it really aims to get people over the initial step. Unlockables? Story content? Roguelite elements? If there are, I haven't found 'em. And because I ran into some error once (whoo, linux proton :P ) I once played through the whole sitting in one go without even a warning because it was running at half speed. I barely got the credits. Enemy variety? I think I've counted four in total, perhaps five. Level design? Different wallpaper, some more z-axis and that's roughly it. Almost as if the game's more a proof of concept than something actually released.But ey...to remind you: 2.5 bucks. At that price I can't flaw it for these details when the overall package is a wild rollercoaster. Because make no mistake: full speed is about twice as fast as other shooters, and that's WITHOUT the ultra-fast sliding move taking in account.

_childDocuments_.review: An auditory & graphical assault on the senses. While this game didn't last too long, I enjoyed it as a twitch shooter. I would like more music tracks as there's really only one you'll be hearing. This game is extremely intense and if you are sensitive to auditory/light sensory issues, you should really not play this. I enjoy the art style as it takes the Doom/pixel sprites and runs with it. The level design is solid for a roguelike and can't wait to see more from it. I find most of the reviews for this game to be boring repetitive meme quality content and felt like I should put a serious review on it rather than "LOL DRUG TRIP". The game is a solid use of your time if you enjoyed Doom and twitch shooters. I sincerely hope that the developers create more with this game, as it's barebones content wise with limited enemy variety but has a solid foundation. At 3$, it's a great experience if you're into this style of game. It's def not for all and has a particular niche player base but if you like the art style in the store page video, give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: So... I know there are a lot of meme reviews here, but here's a somewhat half-hearted attempt at a real one.As a longtime fan of games like ULTRAKILL, REAVER, Katana Zero, and Hotline Miami, I decided to give this one a shot. $2.99 is cheap, and I wanted something new to play.Holy ♥♥♥♥. This did not disappoint.This game is a very strong contender for my favorite indie FPS of all time, and I say this as someone with over 200 hours in ULTRAKILL. PV is precise, adrenaline-pumping, and violent as ♥♥♥♥. Enemies explode into gore when you shoot their heads off, they can explode via upgrades, the health system keeps you moving and attacking, and the limited movement you're given only helps grow your gameplay. After a while, you learn how to slide under bullets, and you begin to experiment with new combos of perks and tools.I'm usually not a huge fan of roguelike games, but something about this is really tickling my fancy. The best way I can describe it is everything that Get to the Orange Door wants to be. It's fun, not rehashing old levels that are just "stand here for 20 minutes!" and it's nowhere near as complex as REAVER. It doesn't have a compelling story like ULTRAKILL or Hotline Miami nor the gritty, cyberpunk aesthetic of Katana Zero, but what it does have is a grimy, dreamcore-like aetshetic reminding me of Baphomet Kun (who is already one of my favorite YouTube channels).Play this game if you like fast-paced violence and don't have epilepsy.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for exactly thirty minutes.I am one hundred percent confident in saying that this is the best game within this price range on the entire friggin’ store.As someone who’s only seen clips of this other game, Post Void plays just like Ultrakill, but is a lot friendlier on your wallet and can probably run on my five year old broken down Android phone.Don’t be mistaken, though, Post Void is NOT Ultrakill. Though they’re both games where you run fast and feed off the blood of your enemies, Ultrakill is all about the long haul and how your enemies move really, really fast: the game allows you to upgrade the many weapons you find, and, as a testament to the game’s speed, the pistol has an upgrade that allows you to throw and shoot coins, because some enemies are so fast, shooting a predictable target the size of an actual coin is easier than shooting some hit box careening towards you at Mach four.Post Void flips the Ultrakill model on its head. Instead of the enemies being really fast, YOU are really fast. This opens up an opportunity for vastly different gameplay. Mainly, you have an incentive and, hell, the ability to shoot at the enemies directly. Post Void also is a much shorter experience. With its roguelike mechanics and the mechanic of your life force melting away with every second you spend not killing, it’s the perfect game to boot up when you’re, say, waiting for your friends to join your Discord call so you can play a different game. With how short even a full playthrough can be, this game dodges the vice of needing to dig in to get the full experience. If you need to go out or get something to eat but want to keep playing until you win or lose, you’ll be off the hook in a matter of seconds.It’s very rewarding to improve at this game. You can, in one sitting, witness yourself go from struggling to stay alive beyond the starting area to sliding under bullets and hitting instant-kill headshots left and right.And don’t even get me started on the different weapons you can get, the knife especially!Overall, this game is a hidden gem. There’s not many other experiences like this on Steam, let alone for three bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: A very stylized rogue-lite shooter about a man holding his own head killing strange beings in a psychedelic world.Shooting? Very satisfying, I don't generally like game comparisons but it has a hotline miami style of shooting satisfaction where enemies are dispatched quickly and in high number. Weak point hits are chunky and do what you'd expect. Every weapon is usable but not all of them are made equally.No real story to be told, not really important. Interesting mechanics? You're basically sprinting like a madman against the clock to reach the end, except you gain more time by getting kills. This is an excellent way to make sure the player feels like they need to interact with your game and not just run to the end. The whole game only takes a few minutes to clear after you get a handle on it, but you can go through it so quickly that death never truly feels bad. Since this is a rogue game, you get upgrades at the end of every segment and some are useful and others aren't. You pretty quickly feel out the best ones and since the game doesn't change, just what upgrades are presented. It's not going to hold you for very long nor is it trying to.For the asking price of Post Void I can say this is a thorough recommend. 3$ gives you 2-6 hours of high speed shooting goodness that doesn't wear out its welcome. Solid 8/10 with 7/10 shooting. A very tight, sometimes hard to look at experience.

_childDocuments_.review: [Intro]Post Void is a short, speed focused challenging shooter game. The game will make you want to come back time to time in your little spare time to play again if you love to aim for a higher score or just simply like the genre. Game is budget friendly and simple. You will clear each level before your time runs out and will be offered 3 upgrade options each time. Each time you die you must restart from the beginning. There are 11 levels in this game. And each restart will always the same but slightly different level structures due to procedural generation.The game has awesome art style which somehow reminds me of pre-21st psycho-horror genre. Visual could be a headache for some people. It is pretty rough.[Where is the fun?]Despite it's simplicity, it is very addictive and exhilarating to shoot through horde of enemies to reach your goal. The game is quite challenging (It is not the most easy game), and it gets difficult as you progress in each level. The game supports global score board so your best score will be automatically shared. If you could just imagine doom but each level filled with only weak enemies and time is your life bar... the game is like that.[Downs?]Only 4 weapons in this game. Which are pistol by default, shotgun and SMG and knfie by upgrade. And you will usually end up getting same upgrades as you progress because there aren't much varieties.[Conclusions]Only get this if you like challenging game and if you're OK with repetition. Because each restart will always going to be the same. Don't expect anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to complain at this price, but I will.The level generation is great, it does a good job of letting you constantly move in a general "forward" direction without stopping. But the game is (intentionally) "psychedelic" enough that, early on (before you tune out the flashing effects), it can be easy to get turned around and be disoriented enough that you don't know which way is forward. Since this is a game with a strict timer, that's usually the end of that run.If you like using the same mouse sensitivity in every FPS, using a web app to translate your sensitivity from one game to another, that won't work in this game. The sensitivity setting is a slider without a number, so you'd have to find your ideal cm/360 sensitivity the old fashioned way.If you use two monitors, this game doesn't lock your mouse cursor to the game. You'd need third party software to do this manually. I lost a lot of runs to clicking outside the game window and having it minimize. It's tough to interpret the skull chalice that represents your remaining HP and time. After clearing a level, it resets to full, but it always looked mostly empty to me. Sometimes you'll drop to low enough HP that the timer shows up, and you think you'll get caught in a loop you can't break out of, where you kill an enemy or two and the timer immediately shows back up, because you aren't killing enough. And yet, sometimes that doesn't happen—you get a few kills and the chalice looks healthy again. Other times you  fine, but you jump up or down a floor, get hit while you're getting your bearings, and you're down to the timer.And that's the next issue: getting ambushed. You have to go fast because of your shared HP+time resource, but go too fast and you'll get ambushed by enemies around the corner or on a different floor, and they (especially the melee enemies) can kill you really fast. It makes it feel like there's a major luck element to winning. If enemies appear mostly in your line of sight, you're golden. If you go to another elevation and get hit twice from behind by the melee enemy, and something else shoots you while you deal with the melee enemy, you can die abruptly. It's too easy to get blasted as you're getting your bearings on a new floor, and going up/down while shooting preemptively can be counterproductive, because the screen flashes when you shoot and you can't see what's going on. If you get blinded by the flashing enemy in the later stages, it's either harmless, or it makes you die from walking into a melee enemy. The game has a lot of situations that can kill you abruptly.The powerups are good overall, but the starting weapon is one of the best weapons, and the uzi feels like a worse pistol. The compass is dumb and unnecessary and sucks and might as well be a baseline UI element. "Walk backwards faster" is a lame upgrade too, even for dodging. It's not bad to have bad items in a pool of random items, but there are few enough options in this game that the bad ones showing up can make you prefer to take nothing at all (you don't have the option to skip).It's good for the price, but the mouse cursor leaving the game window is annoying enough for me to refund it. The game crashed once in 2 hours, which isn't bad, considering it's a pretty new small-scale game.
