_childDocuments_.review: Key things to mention about the game,- There is PVE AND PVP or you can queue into random. Idk why people say there is no PVE only mode. You literally have to beat the tutorial to unlock both options, which leads me to believe folks are not even beating the tutorial and leaving a review. Also, they're mentioning the PVP was the bad part, that means they lost PVP matches to BOTS in the tutorial. - PROGRESSION IS GOOD, feels good, you unlock both class specific and universal mods that make your characters play differently and make each run unique.- CAPCOM - It's a CAPCOM game so the style and characters are fun and could possibly use more variation, but this is a new launch so more characters to come. - PROBLEMS: Microtransaction hell. This is an industry first, and by that I mean a $60 USD game, with a $10 battlepass, YIKES. The SaaS business model has really put a chokehold on game publishers and developers. It's understandable why the game is a day one XBOX Gamepass game, they probably saw the low player count during BETA and realized that unless they sold battlepasses and skins, they would not cover the $60 box price of the game. It's an odd LIVE SERVICES model mixed with full payed experience. I do not see this as a solid business model moving froward, so confused why they tried to re-invent an already greasy wheel. - CAN NOT PLAY WITH FRIENDS ON OTHER HARDWARE THAN THE ONE YOU ARE PLAYING ON - This is an overal weird launch choice, the game is cross-platform, however, you can not party queue with your friends on other consoles/platforms. XBOX is limited to inviting only XBOX players, PC to PC, XBOX to XBOX. Again this is very strange, no real empathy or understanding around why they made this decision. Could be CAPCOM tech debt, limiting their ability to queue servers (SQL issue who the hell knows), or, an XBOX situation where Microsoft does not want their DAY one exclusives on other devices. There's no net positive to not letting gamers play with their friends on other hardware, so this seems for better lack of words "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid".IN THE END - the game is fun, give it a few weeks in the oven, HOWEVER, at $60 dollars with at least $10 in microtransactions needed to get cosmetics. The worst part of this game is the business model, very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad, but gameplay is very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good.

_childDocuments_.review: So been trying exoprimal for a couple hours. Its not what I thought it was going to be, but it occupies a unique place due to how its designed.At its core its a PvE game, but you do race the other team to complete the objectives first. So the games REALLY easy, like I honestly don't think you could fail if you tried to levels of easy. You're just a bunch of bad ass warframes basically, but while this might be a negative if the game wasn't a racing game (lol), since it is at its core a race, even if you technically aren't being challenged by the PVE element, you feel compelled to try your best because you can lose simply by doing it slower.This creates very weird situations that don't normally exist in a PvE or a PVP game. So someone like a genji/tracer can occupy a weird space of, we need you to race to the other objective as fast as possible so we can start the next PvE phase slightly faster the the other team. Than everyone gets there and you feel like badasses because of how fast you killed everything, but than you find out the other team is a bunch of badasses, so they're hot on your heels, so you're like damn, gotta do faster, better, stronger.Ultimately I think it gives the game the advantages of both and the disadvantages of both, its strong PvE because you feel awesome doing everything, but you don't feel like you are getting dominated like in a PvP game. While the PvE is easy and technically you can't lose, you still feel like you want to win against the other team, so you still try, even though its easy, but you lose, and it doesn't feel bad because you don't actually get dominated by them ever? Its something I think you ultimately need to experience to know how it feels exactly, but it occupys a pleasant place of being easy and fun, but still challenging and you lose due to the other team being faster at times, but it doesn't feel bad because you felt like a badass throughout? Its hard to explain.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite what I was expecting or what was advertised...BUT....TLDRIf you're into horde shooters and coop, this game spins it in it's own way. While I've yet to see anything ground breaking or epic in terms of gameplay, it is a solid "s'hmup" and weirdly implemented pve or pvevp that has some interesting mechanics that are tried and true.Essentially, you are one member of a 5 man team of exosuit wearing characters sent into combat with each other at the benefit of an AI that seems to dump dinosaurs on you. It definitely has given me some Metal Gear Kojima type vibes with the weird story but I'm not playing it for the story, I'm here for the drip and the teamplay.PVP is "optional" and pits you against a team of similarly equipped players that are racing against you to make it to the end of a mission zone. Once you get there, the pvp is thrown in for a short period of time. I've really not experienced anything quite like it, but there is a handicap thrown into the mix wherein one of the opposing team members will be given an opportunity to wreck havoc against your team if you're outperforming them by transforming into a dinosaur. That part is legitimately fun and if you know what you're doing, you can easily stall the enemy team and watch your team progress past them. Past this, the aesthetics are nice, I do think it's intentionally over the top in terms of glitz and cosmetics, but that's part of what makes coop games interesting; giving a player a timesink that grants them the ability to make their in-game avatar customized to their liking. The reward system seems fair.Onto the bit that leaves a bad taste in my mouth. Microtransactions and season passes. I hate that ♥♥♥♥. It's thrown in your face right out of the gate. Full price for the game is enough and with the current world we live in as gamers, there are plenty of other options out there that don't make you feel unworthy of the same rewards as another player that handed over another chunk of change. In the end, it's your hard earned money, you get to decide. Anyways, this is long enough. What you see is not quite what you get and it's lacking polish and content imo. It's new though and perhaps that's just the beginning of their concept. I'm not thumbing it down for now, because I prefer games like these and have a soft spot for intense wave combat, which it does do well, even if it makes absolutely no damned sense the entire time. Best of luck and see you in game.

_childDocuments_.review: Went into Exoprimal with zero expectations, and boy, was I pleasantly surprised. After 23 hours spent immersing myself in all roles, I finally finished the story - and it was an experience to remember.Let's address the elephant in the room: yes, it's a repetitive third-person hero shooter. But, does that detract from the experience? Absolutely not. The story was actually pretty damn good, the whole time it had me looking forward to any and all cinematic or story progression read outs. The characters are charming, likeable, and overall just unique plus the boss battles or 10 man fights were like fine wine. Now let's talk about combat. Though it may seem fundamentally repetitive, the variety provided by each exo and their respective roles makes it thrilling to play. Whether you're a hovering skywave support or a front-running zephyr, you'll enjoy blasting and slashing your way through swarms of dinos. The potential this game has for growth is impressive - perhaps even enough to evolve into a franchiseAll I'm saying is that this game is a real gem that had some real heart put into its design even if at its surface it seems pretty straight forward. I have high hopes for future content and more pve focused experiences, but it does really well with its PVPVE approach. I can't wait to see what the future holds for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I read a few reviews regarding Exoprimal having "rampant" or "excessive" monetization and wanted to comment because I was initially skeptical about that and what the nature of this game was as well. We've all found new titles or even old reboots that wind up being blatant cash grabs/soulless live services a plenty, theres no doubt. I find it disheartening every time.    One of the things I appreciate most about Exoprimal is the fact that you are rewarded for just playing the game. All the Exosuits and their variants are obtained by earning currency as a reward from finishing matches, leveling up your account/Exosuits. Everything is unlocked through in-game currency except the few, just IMO, mediocre season pass skins, stamps, and such. The many and arguably cooler skins otherwise aren't purchased with IRL money from an MTX store. There isn't even an MTX store in the game, nor is there a premium currency or subscription rewarding XP boosters or exclusive items. Just a season pass with silly emotes, dances, and skins, currently Security Guard Zephyr, Barrage in surf shorts and others...    Instead, all skins including legendary ones are thrown at you for playing via chests and credits when your account levels up every few matches. Leveling your Exosuit up earns you mods, credits to upgrade your suits and mods, and unlocks Exosuit variants which change that suits weapon. You don't pay a dollar for chests either, they are simply earned behind level ups. Thats it.    Rampant monetization is when a game launches a list of ads you spam close after every single match. Excessive monetization is releasing Exosuits and Mods that you have to pay IRL money for, or making the grind or power differential so steep that you can't reasonably afford the time to keep up with other players power without thinking about paying for catch ups or upgrades/xp, even to the point where they release arguably identical versions of characters or weapons with an extra arbitrary star or rank locked behind premium/paywall. To the point where you might be PvPing against or PvEing with people with gear you can't touch without paying $29 upfront or it being part of some payed pass. Or even instances where you can't even try a new character before paying for them. Games that hide behind EA with barely functioning systems, abundance of bugs save for the fully functioning MTX store from day 1. Its pricing your in game items for 1150 points when you can only buy  1100 points at a time without buying more than you want/need. BS gouging strategies straight out of a textbook.Exoprimal doesn't have any of that.     That was an unexpected surprise to me. Advertisement wise, Exoprimal has a small rectangular window on the bottom right of the home page that flicks through 4-5 ads about news, updates, season pass contents, new suits, emotes, etc, no MTX store, anything purchasable just links to the steam store. The UI is silent and unflagrant relative to other games that treat whatever your eyes can see like FOMO real estate.    To me, skins and emotes are totally besides the point, but I wanted to address that specifically. I tried the Exoprimal demo earlier this year, and was less interested while having my own reservations towards the quality of the game since then especially upon releasing as a full price title ($79.99 CAD). In the little I had heard and seen of this game recently, I was still genuinely suspicious of its prospect in seeming like it could just be another half-baked momentary live service.    So my expectations were not high to begin with, but they were definitely surpassed considering how much I enjoy the game play, team play, progression, and specifically how little incentive there is to pay for anything more when all of that is tied neatly together. At level 86 I'm still unlocking mods and variants through progression rewards every game and still seeing 10-30 second queue times every day and night on PC since the matches are cross platform. 10 new suits were released to unlock since the update went live this morning, unlocking them and slowly but surely upgrading them, learning their play styles and potentials with other suits is a big part of what I like about Exoprimal.    My experience has been this funny incidence of waivering a lot of my initial expectations in satisfaction of what was being presented. Some of the main things that I didn't initially realize or expect but enjoyed while progressing and trying out Exoprimal after playing it to this point were the following:    You unlock new maps and differing scenarios as you progress through the story. Your story progression is dependent on the amount of matches you have played, not apparent right away.After a certain point early on, you can choose to queue up for PvE only, Guaranteed PVP encounter, or Random Queue in the main game mode called Dino Survival which gives a slight bonus to match rewards.Sometimes the match will throw you and the enemy team together for a 10vZ raid encounter.Seeing players go way beyond the level 20 reward track with their favorite exosuits up to level 100, accounts level 350+ playing the Savage Gauntlet mode competitively for placement on the leader boards or just for fun.And switching suits mid match to accommodate more dangerous encounters you become familiar with over time (ie: PvP/Large Dinos)Relatively small but very active player base.    If you enjoy those aspects in other shooters like this, any and all of those activities are how you upgrade your Exosuits and mods over time, including earning the overwhelming majority of all that secondary stuff like skins and emotes like I keep reiterating. Its nothing fancy or incredible, and it does get repetitive (kinda like this review) due to a lack of game mode variety currently, but its certainly not egregiously trying to sell you skin upon skin. I don't understand why or how some of the reviews are complaining about how that ISN'T the case. I found the story to be totally generic and skippable, but thats OK with me, I wasn't under the impression that Exoprimal was the second coming of Regina and Gail. That all being said, even with today's content update, I would say Exoprimal is still now slightly overpriced without more than the two game modes currently offered. Over all though, the unexpected amount of fun and interest relative to my initial impression is in itself why I wanted to drop by and say this is far from what I would label soulless cash grab or anything like that at the very least. Time will tell if the next content update justifies the asking price for this game and whether or not it can earn more players. Adding 10 variants for 20 suits total now was sick. They call them Alpha Variants, and they plan to release 10 more Beta Variants in the future. Cool. Before then, I think Exoprimal still needs different game types and lacks features in terms of long term replay value. Its not currently lacking more new skins and juiced up season pass rewards. Maybe Capcom will indeed lean in that more monetized direction in the future, it would be classic of them, but so far it has been surprisingly the opposite with no expectation of it lasting nor changing.

But you get these awarded for leveling up your pilot and they CAN NOT be bought for real money. I'd also like to add that they are very generous on the rewards you get out of em. My buddy got 5 legendary skins out of em after the first day of playing. I got 2 myself. Anecdotal sure. But still.There is a pack you can buy to get access to a couple exosuits early instead of having to wait to reach the corresponding pilot level to unlock them. _childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal is a title that promises an immersive and engaging experience, but unfortunately, it fails to deliver on its lofty expectations. With a hefty price tag of $60, one would expect a game packed with content and replayability. However, after spending just five hours with the game, it becomes evident that it falls far short of its value proposition.Lack of Content and Value:One of the most glaring issues with Exoprimal is its lack of content. With a price point that suggests a robust and expansive experience, players are left feeling shortchanged. The game's content feels more suited for a 15$ price range, as there simply isn't enough to justify the higher cost. Within a mere five hours of gameplay, the game becomes monotonous and fails to hold the player's interest.Absence of Character Customization:Another disappointing aspect of Exoprimal is the absence of character customization. In a time where personalization and individuality are highly valued in gaming, the lack of options to tailor one's character to their liking is a significant oversight. This omission further contributes to the game's overall lack of depth and replayability.Repetitive Game Modes:The game modes in Exoprimal suffer from a lack of variety and innovation. Each match feels strikingly similar, with only minor changes to differentiate them. This repetition quickly becomes tiresome, leaving players craving more diverse and engaging experiences. The lack of fresh and exciting game modes greatly diminishes the game's longevity and replay value.Underwhelming Story Mode:The story mode in Exoprimal is a major letdown. It fails to captivate players and lacks the depth and narrative complexity that one would expect from a game of this caliber. The story mode feels rushed and poorly executed, leaving players feeling disconnected and uninvested in the game's overarching narrative.Unbalanced PvP Experience:One of the most frustrating aspects of Exoprimal is the unbalanced PvP experience. After spending a significant amount of time engaging in PvE activities, the PvP portion of the game lasts for a disappointingly short duration of 3-4 minutes. Additionally, the impact of completing objectives faster is rendered meaningless, as players can easily be steamrolled in PvP events. This lack of balance undermines the competitive aspect of the game and leaves players feeling frustrated and unfulfilled.Conclusion:In conclusion, Exoprimal is a title that falls far short of its price tag. With a lack of content, absence of character customization, repetitive game modes, underwhelming story mode, and unbalanced PvP experience, it fails to provide the immersive and engaging experience that players expect. It is advised to steer clear of this game, as there are far better options available that offer greater value for your money.﻿

_childDocuments_.review: BLUF: Story is interesting, but not terribly compelling. Gameplay loop is mid - weapons have mediocre feedback at best, teammates are often poor quality, and the PvPvE modes don't feel great. If you're looking for PvE against dinosaurs, majority of the game is that but always ends in competition against an opposing team in some manner. If you want a solely PvE experience, you'll have to wait and see if they add such a mode. On the one hand; It's not a terrible game. On the other hand; I can't recommend it at it's current price. Wait for a sale, and then it might be worth it.Long version:PVP mode ends with you and the enemy team fighting one another at the end of the match as part of a data-cube escort mission. It's not very good. Suits are not balanced to be fighting one another, so once one team wins a fight it's pretty much game over. The PvE mode has you compete in objectives against the enemy team for the final segment, avoiding suit-on-suit warfare and has the possibility to end in a double victory (If one team finishes the final objective the other team has 20 seconds or so to finish their final objective. If they do, they also win - or so I've experienced.) Each suit unlocks upgrades that can affect each of it's abilities, but those abilities have to be unlocked and upgraded via bikcoin (yes, really) which you get through suit-progression or player account level and battle pass progression. There are also generic upgrades that apply to every suit in place of skill-specific upgrades, and they also need to be unlocked and upgraded with bikcoin. The "Survival Pass" and heavy monetization leaves a sour taste in my mouth, and I understand why any would not purchase this game because of it. I don't hate this game, and it has potential, but the current state of it is middling at best and not really worth the $60/70 USD, imo. We'll see what other game modes they add to help enhance the current experience, and what tweaks they make to suits/abilities/game modes down the line and see if it's really worth the current cost of the title.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll go over what I thought Exoprimal was, the monetization system, the gameplay structure, and my current rating.I'll be upfront that I had purchased Exoprimal hoping more for a pure PvE experience with PvP being available for those who wanted it. I'm a big fan of both Monster Hunter and Lost Planet and was hoping that this new Capcom IP would help satisfy that itch, however because of the confusion regarding the games launch and play structure that I was a little disappointed. I don't mind playing competitive games, but I was hoping that Exoprimal could have just been more similar to EDF or DRG style of game but with mutant dinosaurs fighting robots.There are currently two modes of play, Dino Survival and Savage Gauntlet (Savage Gauntlet is  accessible after completing the "story" which takes about 55 games of Dino Survival, which in my case took about 20 hours)Dino Survival: Players can queue PvP and PvE modes where they race to complete a number of missions against another team in two rounds. As other reviews have mentioned, when you first start out in the game, the missions are pretty simple, kill "x" raptors, kill a triceratops, etc. As you progress through the story, more variants of missions are thrown into the possible missions, now you have "Defend Checkpoint A", or "Escort the cube". Whether or not you win or lose Dino Survival will progress you through the story, so you'll always be introduced to these new variants, even on a losing streak. So long as you play more you increase the variety of missions you can experience. It is important to note that  in a race, and the difference is either indirectly (PvE) or directly (PvP). I'll try to describe the flow:Round 1:Complete missions racing against the other team, with the in-game narrator letting you know if you are matching or falling behind the enemy team's pace, teams do not directly interact.Round 2 (If you chose PvP):Towards the end of Round 2, you will compete directly against other teams in PvP combat while trying to complete the mission, This is hectic, this can be fun, this can be frustrating. Dominators are given to both teams in this mode, allowing a player to "play as" a dinosaur and fight the other team. Some gameplay missions will only be available in this mode.Round 2 (if you chose PvE):This mirrors round 1 where you continue to race against the other team, but the team that is slower is given a Dominator, in an attempt for the slower team to catch up. A little later the opposing team will get their own Dominator to use at their own discretion. Whichever team completes the final mission first is declared the "winner", and the other team then has 20 seconds to complete the final mission. I've played a fair number of games where we're on the "losing" team, but still manage to complete the final objective before the time runs out, and the narrator calls us winners as well, even netting the victory exp bonus as well, so it's actually possible for both teams to actually win here. Some of my favorite matches were where both teams had the dominator, but neither team ends up using it, either out of fear of a revenge invasion or want for both teams to do well.Dominators are present in both modes, so if you are looking at Dino Survival (or Exoprimal in general) know that you will always be competing, and if you were looking for something purely cooperative, that this game may not be for you.Savage Gauntlet: PvE only mode that has teams of 5 playing a set sequence of missions that records time scores. Replaying this mode during the same period allows for teams to polish their strategies and compete for better times. This mode was released today, and from my impressions of it, it seems underwhelming. Savage gauntlet was advertised as a cooperative mode that would build off of that level of skill level and engagement deserving of a mode that is only available post-game, but instead it's a short romp of a few missions. Savage Gauntlet is supposed to rotate weekly with new variations and mission challenges, and only time will tell in this regard how well this will be handled, but my first impression was not great.I think 60 USD is  too steep of a price tag for the game at the moment, given the content we've received so far. You may take my continued negative review with a grain of salt, since I've established that Exoprimal's structure is (disappointingly) not for me, but I think there is still not enough content to justify a 60 USD price tag, .What kept me playing until now was a combination of sunken cost fallacy, wanting to beat the story so I could try out the savage gauntlet mode, and surprisingly, I found myself playing to continue learning about the story. For a horde-type game, you would not typically advertise story as being one of the stronger parts of the experience, so I was very pleasantly surprised and entertained in this regard., but the game modes available are structured in a way that a player like myself (who was looking for a traditional PvE game) am not really satisfied and could not recommend to other players looking for that kind of experience.I want this game to do well and I think Capcom has had a good streak with its releases lately, so I hope that one day I can come back to this review and make appropriate changes. Again.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game, for addressing some of the bad reviews by the 1.5  hour review gang:-At the start (like the first 10 to 15 missions) the game give you only basic dinos and the usual 2 maps and modes, after that the maps increase and the new dino varieties start stomping your team and making casualties in the pve part (fighting a carnotaurus, 3 pachy and a whole horde of the tanky raptors is a little difficult to manage), for the modes other than the push the cart from the start there's energy collection, hammer thing, control point and some other i'm forgetting.-The price is 60 and you are the one who decide if it's okay for you or not (for me it's ok, 40 would've been better maybe but i don't really have an issue), all the "dlc" on the store is just the battle pass and a bunch of skins that you can easily obtain in game with the currency you collect, there's no premium currency or other type of microtransaction, there's loot boxes but you just win them and can't buy them so mechanically really it's just like live service stuff like dead by daylighht or overwatch but they forgot to monetize it, wich is all fine and dandy; For the battle pass you can just not buy it if it bothers you, you're not really losing anything of importance and for the one who buy it a season change is every 3 months-the game requires that you make a capcom id, now,i think that you can lament of this only for 2 reasons: you either are a tiny bit tech illiterate and this is a roadblock for you or the more probable things is that you are a cheater and don't want to have your account banned like a stupd monkeyNow, for why you should buy this game: you're a mechsuit killing tons of dinos with your team and then some other mechsuit in the last phase (more pve in case you want a gluten free anti-pvp option), the story so far (46% as of this review) is interesting and the characters are surprisily likeable, for me at least, you do you; i like quite a lot the atmosphere in general with the maps with vegetation and ruined buildings, the exosuit are really cool, varied and fun in general and there's some customization with the modulesI don't know how to end the review,we already have a roadmap of update for the next 9 months, if you're still on the fence there's gamepass i guess

_childDocuments_.review: Horde shooter, Hero shooter, exosuits, dinosaurs. This game has everything I could ask for in a 5 v 5 multiplayer game. It takes a few games to get the hang of it, but just when you do, the game starts throwing spicier twists at you. New dinos, new game modes, new mechanics. It doesn't stop, all the way to the end of the story.Oh yeah, they added *Story* to my Dino Punching game. It's really good, too. You always get a new piece of dialogue or a cutscene after a mission, and I'm glad you can binge all the cutscenes you've unlocked after you're done playing with your mates - no cutscene walls slowing down the evening of pub stomping (or being stomped). Yeah the characters feel like one-note caricatures or stereotypes, but they get fleshed out to a point where they feel more like the people those stereotypes were based on.The ability to switch suits mid game (hells, mid *fight* if you're daring enough) is huge as you can swap off a tank to a DPS if the situation calls for it, or swap to the counter class to an opponent's shopwrecker. Or even have one suit for PvE and another for the PvP section.Overall, i thoroughly recommend this game when it's on sale - $30-$40 for this game is a very reasonable price.

_childDocuments_.review: The one thing I can say about this game is that it was not what I was expecting at all. It just kept giving. I read a lot about people getting bored from this game but so much changes as you play more that I really don't see how. I just finished the game and have done two savage gauntlet runs when writing this. + Differing Game modes that occur at random+ PvPvE and can decide if you would rather have pvp or pve endings+ Dope Exosuits w/ way diff styles of playing (like MH weapons)+ Fun Dinos Appear Later ;)+ An Interesting Story+ Dope Skins+ Sick Emotes- Another Time Loop story o_o- When playing solo it is pretty tough to get into full games- No crossplay invites but is Crossplay?- Too many audio logs, even though I love listening it can be annoyingIt's another asymmetrical, team coordinated shooter, akin to Overwatch. But they throw in obstacles. PvE mixed in with your PvP. I love that. I need more of that. I am so tired of the trope of just being sent straight in me against people who are able to put in more time than me in a competitive game. Having the dinos kind of adds that complexity that can give anyone the edge in a moment. I saw a lot of people saying they got tired of Dino Survival after like 5 games, but those people must have very short attention spans and these types of games may not be for them. That's fine. Heavy riffing guitar with digitized beats behind it. Very fun. Nothing that you get chills over but definitely entertaining to listen to. There were a few good tracks in moments of the story that made me go wow, but thinking back on them, nothing really stuck. But when you hear them, they're great.The story is another time loop head scratcher. I really liked the story. I REALLY liked it. It was funny when it needed to be. I would definitely like to see more story from it.The world is our world, but in 2040- after an apocalyptic event where vortexes opened everywhere and destroyed everyone. It's a fine trope. I hate that.It also has issues trying to find rooms when playing solo. There should also be a ranked added! Would be super fun for pvp'ers. _childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game design ruined by monetization. Diagnosis: This is a free-to-play game with a $60 price tag.Exosuits must be leveled-up in game, then you spend currency to buy upgrade modules, then you spend more currency to upgrade those modules (up to 5 times each, getting more expensive with each upgrade). All of this requires you to play in matchmaking, against other players who already have everything unlocked, so you'll be at a significant disadvantage and drag your teammates down until you grind out several dozen matches. Unless, of course, you're willing to pay even more money on top of the $60 you already spent for the game. Also, there's a battle pass (of course there is), with a premium track, and loads of cosmetics, so expect to see exosuits running around in swimwear and giant teddy bear costumes.I love the design ideas behind this game. Competitive team-based PvE culminating in a final PvP showdown, or sometimes teaming up with the enemy against a massive PvE onslaught feels extremely novel. The way they deliver plot and meta progression in a competitive team game like this feels like an evolution, although an imperfect one.My understanding is that you unlock more mission types and objectives as you progress the plot. Once in matchmaking, the game decides on objectives depending on the least-progressed person in the lobby. So you might get stuck in simple dinosaur-culling missions over and over if the game decides to match you with noobs.The competitive PvE aspect doesn't feel very impactful. Maybe this changes at higher levels, but at the start it's just a race. Go here, kill the things, do it faster than the other team, that's it. Once one team gets a lead, it feels very unlikely that you'll make up the time difference, so the rest of the match becomes a formality. There's not much you can do to slow down the enemy team that they can't just throw back at you. There's very little decision-making besides spamming your abilities as often as possible.I know that all of these things can be improved and the game concepts are solid. But I don't feel comfortable paying retail price for a game that's going to ask for money again and again and then maybe get shut down in two years.

The new game modes will add more life to the game and the seasons will add more modules (hopefully) and new skins, ect. _childDocuments_.review: This is not a "Play for 2 hours and you've played it all" game like I've seen some reviews seem to read or have playtime below 2 hours. There are 10-man activities, the objectives get harder, the dinosaurs get replaced with Neo-Saurs, or harder dinos, and MASSIVE 1000+ swarms. The story is done well so far, the characters are likeable. Now, monetization is a valid complaint, but I counter that with the premium pass being only cosmetic. The only DLC that provides tangible in-game benefit is the Headstart pack, and the Overdrive kit, which will unlock all of the Alpha suit variants, because you insta unlock suits. And the Alpha suits don't release for 3 months. I really like this game. Its alot of fun. Now, there is not pure PvE experience where there are no enemy players. The closest you have is PvE with one enemy player showing up as a high tier Dino one time to wreck your day. There is no pure PvP experience, there will always be dinos butting into your fights. Ignore anyone with a playtime under 3 hours. Understand that there are no loot boxes, and there are goofy skins you earn from the pass, or that you get from playing the game. This is a new IP from Capcom, give it some time, they are learning as they go.

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this game. The gameplay loop is super fun, you bash dinosaurs, then either fight players or bosses or race other players for an objective or everything at once. This is a really creative competitive shooter. Optimization is actually insane. I can run the game maxed out with a 2080 super without a hitch on PC as well as a steady 60 fps with some dips to 45 during the worst of it on my steam deck.Decent optimization is rare these days and I do want to commend Capcom for it as all their releases recently have been very well optimized.The way the content is delivered is unique as well, like any competitive game you keep running the same mode repeatedly, yet as you progress new enemy types, new maps, new types of objectives all emerge along with a decent story.There are plenty of cosmetics to unlock just by playing the game which is great.I'm not a big fan of battle passes or early game monetization, but there's lots to unlock with the in game currency.The gameplay mechanics are clean they work well, each exo feels unique and suits a variety of different play styles. It's very reminiscent of overwatch and being able to swap characters on the fly.For consI think my biggest issue is one that's been addressed, it's the cross platform grouping, although you can play cross platform, you can't make a party with your friends if you are not on the same system. They did say they are working on it.Now for these reviews...I almost never write reviews, but in this case I had to because I see people reviewing after drinking bleach from a bottle labeled "bleach" and expecting Pepsi.The steam store says "online pvp" , the game was marketed and showcases as pvevp. It was never ever marketed as PvE exclusively. It was always meant to be a competitive game. Giving a negative review to a game for not being a PvE game when it never even pretended to be one is like going to a ramen restaurant and asking why they don't have any pizza and then literally flipping a table...Anyway, it's a great game, I'm looking forward to more content from it, hopefully monetization is controlled.

_childDocuments_.review: Some stats for the 100% achievements: 88 hours, 249 Dino Survival games played, 169 player level. It's maybe not a pure PvE game like some people had hoped, but I actually found the PvP to be pretty tolerable in this game.The main mode Dino Survival consists of two parts, a PvE section where you go from place to place eliminating dinos, and then the final mission which can be PvE but is usually PvP. There is however an option in the menu to select whether you would prefer a PvE or PvP final mission so you do have some choice. I always left it on Random so I can't say if it will take longer to find games that way.The other thing of note is that on occasion when you play Dino Survival you will, instead of the normal game, be given a 10-man raid which is completely co-op PvE. This is somewhat related to the story as progressing through the story will unlock more content you can play in Dino Survival, including new maps and those PvE raids which are tied to big events in the story. There's a few of these but after you play them for the story it's random if you get them again, and story progression is tied to the least progressed player in the lobby, which means you can't just choose to play them and you probably won't be seeing the final fight very often. At least I didn't, I only got it one other time and I got booted from the game because Steam Maintenance had to happen at that exact moment. So yeah I only got to do the final fight once for the story.All you need to do to progress the story is play Dino Survival and every few games you'll be given a cutscene to watch. The story itself was good but not amazing, I don't regret not skipping anything and listening to all the extra files though. The game features you as a silent protagonist, similar to Red Dead Redemption 2 Online. Personally I wasn't a fan of this, but I can understand why it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to start by saying: DON'T LISTEN TO MANY OF THE NEGATIVE REVIEWS!! Most of them aren't making very valid points.I just finished the main story of this game and can wholeheartedly say that this is a great game and i love itFirst I'll address the negative reviews, or at least the main points they've been making:- "There is no content." No, there is content, it's just that you dont start to unlock more until after a few hours. The first few hours are to get you accustomed to the basics before throwing more challenging things at you.- "The monetisation makes this game unplayable." No, far from it. Granted it's a payed game with a battle pass system, but the pass is completely optional and you can earn MANY cosmetics without it. If you aren't willing to pay the big price tag to play it, then wait for a sale, thats totally valid.- "The crossplay is trash." This is the only take i somewhat agree with, but then again, it doesnt make it unplayable, it just prevents partying up with people from other platforms. If youre friends all have the same platform for it then youre golden. Granted im a little biased since all my friends play on PC, but regardless.- "Theres only one gamemode." NO, THERES NOT. YOU UNLOCK MORE. You just need to play a bit to get them. Dino survival is a catch all term, once youre in, there are 11 game modes that can switch into one another. Area defence, Dinosaur cull, Omegacharge, Energy Collector, the list goes on. Plus they added the savage gauntlet mode for people who complete the main story, and from what i understand, its a lot like deep dives from DRG.Now that im through the negative stuff, i'll get the the praise.- The game is very well balanced. Aside from one suit i think that could use a buff (Vigilant), i think all of the exosuits are totally viable and i think so long as you dont flood your comp with one class then youll be fine with anything.- This game is a shining example of how to optimise a game. It runs like a dream, even when you have literally hundreds of individual dinos rushing at you at once, and up to 10 players doing their own things all on screen at once, it still runs amazingly. And before you say it, my PC isnt the strongest in the world, and it still runs fine.- The gameplay. In short it can be described as "Amazing dumb fun." I rarely had moments where i found it lacking. At the end of each match, i would always find myself raring for another. I even find myself having fun when i lose. The PvE is satisfying and you always feel like youre being helpful, even when playing tanks and supports. The PvP is far more fun (in my opinion) to PvP in games like Overwatch and CoD. It doesnt feel sweaty at all because unlike those games you dont get popped in less than a second if youre not the biggest tryhard alive.- The story is far better than i expected from a game about exosuits fighting dinosaurs. The characters are endearing, and there were multiple times where the plot developed in a way beyond what i was expecting.If youre wondering if it's worth it because of the somewhat mixed reviews, then listen to me when I tell you: YES. If youre short on cash, maybe wait for a sale, but just know that you will get your money's worth. Please get this game and show it the love it deserves,

_childDocuments_.review: I seriously love this game and everything it has to offer.  The characters, gameplay, story, visuals, and everything else is just fun.  Doesn't take itself to seriously and is a joy to experience.  All the exosuits are a blast to use and customize with some great looking cosmetics.  Unfortunately it seems a ton of the negativity surrounding this game seems to stem from misinformation, wishing that the game is something else entirely, issues from an abundance of micro transactions and some weird decisions how cross-play is represented in this game.  I agree with the latter two but almost all of the game was crystal clear from the developer streams and trailers.I love the way the game mixes PVP and PVE.  It's not the most balanced but this game isn't meant to be competitive past just playing the game like MP games of the olden days used to do.  There's no ranking system here, which makes it way more fun to just hop in and play both alone and with friends.Speaking of with friends, the one biggest flaw that this game has is a lack of cross-platform friends list features (and cross-save to some extent).  While the game does have cross-platform play, it does not allow you to form parties with your friends on other platforms (ex. Xbox App w/ Game Pass and Steam).  This sucks for me personally as that meant I did have to refund the game on steam just to play it on the Xbox App so I could play with the majority of my friends and will probably hamper the game in the future.  Even though I'm not the biggest fan of the micro transactions (Battle Pass, DLC Cosmetics packs and DLC Skip packs), they're at least priced much more fairly than a typical F2P title.  However this is not a F2P title but at least you can earn skins through gameplay without paying any extra pretty regularly.I highly recommend you try this game out for longer than a couple of matches (either via Game Pass or Steam).  Content is unlocked at a very steady rate and from what I've played in the betas and seen in the trailers, there's a ton more out there that early reviewers have not experienced yet.  Just be aware of the caveats that this game has, and don't be surprised if it isn't for you.  It's definitely gonna have a smaller than average player base but I hope this one can live on.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is a lot of fun. The game play loop is fairly simple and the missions overall are a little repetitive. However they do have an ok variety of events during the missions. The game runs smooth on my computer rig of almost 8 years old on high settings and there are very few visual hiccups. Most of them happen on loading into the initial loading area and mission area. During game play is quite smooth. The game isn't pay to win, the few things you do buy with in game currency are things you can get enough of to buy in 2-3 missions. Especially in the beginning when you are constantly leveling up your player level, Exosuit level, and this version of a season pass. Overall the game is a lot of fun, you go around shooting and exploding dinosaurs for the first 4 parts of the mission, and then you get a final mission that may or may not be PVP depending on if you chose to include those missions or not. The only time the enemy team can mess with you other than the PVP specific last missions is when each team gets to summon a large dinosaur and control it while it gets teleported near the enemy team or sometimes you can complete an event that increases the difficulty on the enemy side.One of my favorite final missions I've seen so far would be the cooperative missions where both teams come together and essentially fight a Raid Boss ala MMORPG style. Complete with hiding behind large pillars during aoe party wipe attacks, and jumping or maneuvering away from targeted or sweeping attacks.The game is great, however the only thing that really holds it back is the gameplay loop. As I said it is pretty simple, and honestly not worth 60 bucks. Maybe they will add a bunch more free into the game that will make it worth that price, but right now, either wait for a sale, or until they add a content update or two.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very obvious from reading a lot of the user reviews that most of them did not get far enough into the game, although I will admit this is likely due to the game's massive design flaws. It does at first seem like there is only one game mode; however, the more you play the game, the more modes you unlock, from takes on classics like escorting payloads and capturing control points, to more interesting fare, such as MMO-inspired raid battles where both teams set aside their differences and work together to take down one big, bad dinosaur using The Power of Friendship™ (my personal favorite missions). The issue is that the game does not make it immediately apparent that there IS more than one game mode, and while this appears to be done for very deliberate, story-related reasons that I will not spoil here but that are easily found online, I have to say, it really does the game a disservice. Personally, I enjoyed slowly unraveling the story and discovering why new game modes were being unlocked, but I can totally see why this would be a huge turnoff to some people, especially the casual crowd that is just wanting to jump in and out for some quick matches and/or those who are not interested in the story. And honestly, the story is a way bigger part of this game than it really advertises and I was pleasantly surprised to see a multiplayer game with such an interesting, albeit insanely cheesy, campaign - but it's completely understandable that some people don't even make it to this point since, on the surface, Exoprimal appears to be just another standard hero-based team shooter and those are typically very straightforward. The graphics are technically very impressive, although some of the environments are a little bland for my taste, and the sound design is great. Weapons feel good to use and a lot of the characters are insanely fun, but another huge ding against the game is that there just aren't enough characters. In combat, your customizable player character pilots giant mecha called "exosuits" to fight off the hoards of dinosaurs and/or the enemy team, and while each exosuit has their own unique play style, voice lines, cosmetics, etc., and the roster initially looks pretty large, in reality, there is a very small base roster of only 10 exosuits, with 4 DPS options and 3 each for tank and support. The remaining playable exosuits are α and β variants of each character, but there is great variability between how different the variants are from the base suit, so while some may feel almost like a different character entirely, others feel almost the same as the default exosuit, with only minor changes. This can feel disappointing and frustrating at times, and is made worse by the fact that you have to either buy the variants with real money, or grind for several hours to reach level 20 on what is essentially each character's "battle pass" that you level up by playing matches with that suit (battle passes that are free I might add, but don't you worry, there's paid seasonal passes too). So, depending on the number of variants you're interested in obtaining, you're looking at potentially hundreds of dollars spent buying each of them outright, or hours spent grinding to get each exosuit to rank 20.The rest of the game is largely fine. The story is extremely cheesy and tongue-in-cheek, often in a "so bad it's good" manner, reminiscent of straight-to-DVD B-movies playing on basic cable at 3 PM on a Saturday type of way. It's nothing groundbreaking, but I found it enjoyably dumb and interesting enough. The voice acting falls into the same category, being a hodgepodge of either perfectly adequate or laughably bad, as characters shriek at your sweet, dumb, doofy-looking silent protagonist in exaggerated Russian, Jamaican, and British accents. The progression system is unusual in that you unlock new cutscenes and story sequences by playing a certain number of matches; sometimes you may end up waiting in matchmaking for several minutes if you are being unknowingly queued into the next campaign mission, which can often lead to getting matched with bots or players who have already completed these missions. This can lead to some confusion, as you may occasionally get matched with a group doing a campaign mission you have already completed, and for some reason, every time you complete a campaign scenario, the same story-related cutscene plays when you exit the match. It took me a while to realize why I was occasionally finishing a match and seeing cutscenes I'd already seen before, and on more than one occasion I actually got matched with groups doing story missions I hadn't even unlocked in my own campaign, which led to me exiting a match and loading into a very confusing cutscene where the story had apparently jumped ahead with no explanation.Overall, I think Exoprimal is a great game, just one held back by some rather head-scratching decisions on CAPCOM's part. While I would say I definitely got more than my money's worth from Exoprimal, and I would argue the high production value warrants the $60 price tag, it is a paid entry in an over-saturated genre that has almost entirely pivoted to a F2P model, which is understandably off-putting to a number of players. Add to that the presence of paid DLC - and yes, the majority of it is obtainable with in-game currency, but there is some content locked behind four paid seasonal battle passes, as well as crossover content from other CAPCOM games - and the first impressions are, sadly, really not great. Even if one gets past these hurdles, the convoluted manner in which the story is told and locking alternative game modes and characters behind dozens of hours of playtime does little to help an already struggling game's reputation (to say nothing of the complete and utterly baffling lack of marketing). I have enjoyed my time with Exoprimal greatly, but I completely understand why it has the negative/mediocre word-of-mouth that it does, and as much as I would love to play with my friends, I can't fault them for not jumping into an exosuit to shoot up some dinos with me, especially now that it's been announced the game is "complete" and will not be receiving further content. Why it is obvious to thousands of average gamers the many reasons that Exoprimal failed to become the next big thing, but not to the million-dollar development company responsible for it floundering, is absolutely beyond me, but I sincerely hope that CAPCOM realizes how hard they dropped the ball on this game, how much potential it has, and revisit it in the future instead of letting it fade away into obscurity like so many other live service games these days. TL;DR - Great game held back by questionable choices, I'd get it on sale. Alternate game modes locked behind hours of progress. Small roster, 10 characters + 2 variants each & some variants are too similar to default. Paid DLC, including $40 worth of battle passes. Story is dumb fun, but told in a confusing way. Lack of fresh content going forward due to game being "complete."

_childDocuments_.review: Up front, the concept of destroying large hordes of dinos with exo-suits sounds fun. I wish they just focused on that. This game feels like it's having an identity crisis. It wants to tell a story while having no actual campaign aside from a few events that feel like RNG things that just happen when the game starts. They give you these somewhat open areas but force you along a path. You only get 2 maps, City day/night and jungle cavern. Then they want it to be PVP but not PVP? Only in a few circumstances do you actually fight another team. The rest of the time you're just speed running along side them. Just separate the modes if you really want PVP. I came to detonate dinos with the boys in our fancy power armor. Why do we have to compete against another team when there is no real reason for it? The story reason is dumb and I'm going to completely ignore it. On top of that they throw in a battle pass, free and paid, and you don't even get all the suits. Well not without some grinding or paying for them outright. Something I could look past if they game itself was free but it's $60. I hope they can change it up. I like the game play and it looks good. I just wish they focused on the PVE, dinos vs power armor, over this weird MOBA but not a MOBA thing they're trying to do. Get it on a HEAVY sale if you really want it. Please don't pay full price for this, thing. You'll thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into the game's earlier beta--as well as its full release--very concerned about their PvEvP approach to the game flow. In practice, though, it's been incredibly fun, and I think it will help the game's longevity going forward to have that competition between the teams. There's a lot of depth to be found in both your character choices as well as your loadout and traits. I would like there to be more variety in which objectives are spawned on your way to the final mission, but I've found myself always enjoying that last fight--whether it's joining forces with the other team, racing to complete our objective first, or fighting them head-to-head in teamfights.I do want to say, however, that I think releasing the game at full-price with a battle pass and whatnot for this sort of experience may not be the right call. A PvP game like this that relies on a healthy population would benefit immensely from the base experience being f2p. While I don't regret my purchase, I know the price tag is going to be a hard pill to swallow.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game where you have to hunt dinos with and against other exosuit pilots.Story progression is necessary to unlock more dinos and more stages. This design is good because if you had to fight stealth dinos, sniper dinos and ability blocking dinos from the start; this game would have the Dark Souls of "X" meme all over it. Which I still wouldn't mind cause I like the game play loop. Pick a suit and start blasting some dinos.The story is entertaining and mainly serves a purpose as to why the game opens up slowly. The AI Leviathan is slowly collecting Exosuit data to further enhance development on it's pet project so, It overtime increases the variety of dinos you fight. As you play through the missions you'll get data packets that'll expand on the story, Just go to the database tab to view more. You'll still get cutscenes that progress the story; no need to to look at the database if you do not want to. You do get some really good battles where instead of competing for bonus existence you can fight together against whatever Leviathan has cooked up.

_childDocuments_.review: So... I started Exoprimal this afternoon... and I can see the Like for it, but... the blatant sales practice of CAPCOM here is "you buy game" and then "you buy everything else too", from what I can see... I'll add more to this later, once the free-weekend is over. But... so far... it's really "meh"...Sunday Night: So... after playing a bit more, and learning to understand the game... it turns out it's really just PvE but time and point competitive PvP, with moderate amounts of actual PvP. All's fine, but it's really missing something... because it's just repeat missions one after the other, feeling like an older Mech game with some newer graphics. After each match(usually) you get a Story Update, and you learn a little, or a lot, more of what-all is going on. You get Mini cinematics, where sometimes the Team is animated, and usually just shown Metal Gear Solid style, two portraits on each side of an image and given dialogue.I'm not sure if anybody would find this truly-fun after so-long of all the same missions, over and over again, collecting dialogues and mini-cinematics... Maybe if it were Dino-Crisis'd or Monster Hunter'd up a little more? And given more freedom-of-play? With the probably 10 missions I put in, I got pretty bored during this FREE WEEKEND event. Wouldn't pay the current price unless it's down by 90% on sale, for everything including all the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal is a 5v5 coop multiplayer shooter that tries to finish missions before the other players and it succeeds at what it does.Pros: 1. combat, movement, skills all feel amazing        2. really neat graphics and design        3. everything feels really smooth         4. game modes are pretty new and refreshing         5. A huge blast to play with friends        6. pretty fun for casual players         7. game has crossplay so if you have friends on console you can play         8. game offers build variety which is nice cons: 1. theres not a huge difference between pvp and pve modes as well its pretty much the same thing. but in pve mode you dont have to deal with raw pvp and only dino invasions controlled by a player.          2. The game does have battle passes for 9.99 (i know some people are against this)         3. story cutscenes are tied behind matches played.         4. some people could find it repetitive if they want a solely pve experience  all in all, i feel like this game is a solid 7/10 if you buy it knowing what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played two of the previous open beta tests and lemme tell ya, I'm still enjoying this game.This game drips with style and over-the-top action, and all the exosuits+dinosaurs are full of personality in their movements, attacks, and even death animations. The game does have a PvP aspect, which was unexpected when I played the first beta, but it's a fun change of pace. In matches like those you're balancing pushing your point while considering attacking the enemy to slow them down.The PvE mode (not Savage Gauntlet, as it's not out yet) still involves minor PvP elements; just like the regular PvP mode you can get invaded once or twice, but that's it. These invasions are simple to melt down if you're smart and focus!Defo recommend, even with the price point to be honest. I'd have been happy for it to be cheaper, but I've enjoyed hopping in my mech suit and blastin' dinosaurs and other people.

_childDocuments_.review: To all the devs, writers, and creative minds that went into making this game I offer my sincere thanks. The gameplay is very fun and rewarding, the characters are believable and memorable, and the passion and detail that went into your work does not go unnoticed. Thank you again for the amazing experience. I look forward to playing for many more hours. To all potential buyers I heartily recommend this game if you have interest in campy sci-fi action and/or horde shooters. If you already like the genre, this is an easy "It's fun because it knows what it's doing" type of game. It does not break or set new heights of design, but it does meet and exceed the average of most competitors in the genre. Please be aware its major flaws rest in its business decisions, not its gameplay or story ones, even if they are atypical. To all the business people who had a hand in this game, please reconsider whatever it is you do with your next titles. Imagine where all the effort for battlepass skins, crossover events, and lootboxes could have gone. This game might not stand the test of time because of what appears to be your greed or over zealousness. I hope I'm wrong, and that you're just trying to make ends meet.

_childDocuments_.review: I will give this game an OK rating. The game itself, the idea and the gameplay is really fun. It really is cool to be killing like 100 raptors at the same time all falling down from a portal. And I really love the mechanic of this game where you have to complete task fast with your teamates to go faster than the opposing team (PVE, there is also PVP I did not try).Overall, fun game. But my complain start with the fact that the game itself is fast, but everything else, like loading and cutscenes, are slow and that is a bit annoying. You even have to watch the same cutscene each time you get in a game that you cannot skip and takes like 1 minutes and is not even loading the game. Also, the fact that the PC playerbase is DEAD. When I tried this game, there were only 60 other peoples on all Steam playing it. There is a Cross-platform feature and apparently, the console community is doing ok for the game.But, I am a weird guy. I like trying to play games singleplayer/alone even if it was not meant to. And honestly, it was fun! The allied bots are really good. The enemy bots are not so, but still, trying to do objectives with bot as fast as possible was fun. The downside is that you have to turn Cross-platform off and wait 5 minutes for the Matchmaking to try to find someone even if nobody is there.Also, and this is stupid, you can make custom games now (YAY) But you cannot lauch a custom game alone, like with bots only. You need someone else to join you, which is stupid, because we already can do bots only games.So, I would not recommend this game UNLESS you want to play with friends, online OR you are ok waiting 5 minutes, than 1 minutes of Cutscene EACH GAME, to be pair with bots for a 20 minutes game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence about buying this game, read this review.All the people complaining about the DLC/Battlepass etc. Haven't taken the time to intelligently think about what these things are actually providing. All but one DLC are purely for cosmetics, and the premium battlepass is also purely cosmetics. The one DLC that is not cosmetic, simply helps you unlock 3 of the 10 Exosuits instantly. Those three suits can also be obtained from playing the game and getting to levels 20,30, and 40 respectively.Yes, there are lootboxes, no you don't pay for any of them. You earn lootboxes from level ups, and can even view your player level status to see when you will get a lootbox. Inside these lootboxes are, guess what? Cosmetics. Most cosmetics you can also buy with the in-game currency, which guess what? You earn that simply from playing the game and leveling up either your Exosuit or Player Level. There isn't any premium currency or premium account time either. All paid content is purely cosmetic.There is a story to the game, and the primary game mode(Dino Survival) relies on you playing it in order to progress the story, which also progresses the amount of content you get access to, that content being new dinosaurs to fight, new objectives to do, it doesn't toss everything it can at you from the beginning, it sets you down slowly.How Dino Survival works, is there are two missions with a set of 3 objectives. You compete with the enemy team to complete them the fastest. After those two missions are finished, you go into the final mission, which if you choose Random like I do, it's a coin-toss on whether that final Mission will be a PvP style mission where you will be able to directly fight the enemy team, or a PvE style mission that so far seems to be a third mission set of 3 objectives. Whoever beats all the missions first, wins.I highly suggest giving the game a try, it is quite fun and reminds me a little bit of Lost Planet 2 and Orion: Prelude having a baby.

_childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal has an identity crisis. A Dino Crisis if you like. Exoprimal is a PvE/PvP competitive co-op/multi-player 3rd person hero shooter I guess.The PvE is pretty shallow. Shoot dinos faster then the enemy team. This matters I think. As in it gets you to the final mission faster. Which is when you can fight the enemy team. But why even PVE then? It seems like odd busy work before the real fight at the end. And the busy work seems to have little to no bearing on the final decision, or it means quite a bit. I honestly can't tell and I've played like every beta. Sometimes you get awarded the ability to invade the other teams world with a triceratops or a T-Rex. They give it out to winning and loosing teams at weird times. Again I have no idea why. The cube escort missions for example. Stay with your cube for faster progress. Or don't I guess. Because you can make a b line for the enemy team and just kill them as there all standing around a cube unaware. I just don't know how they want me to play this game. The PvP seems cool to me. I know a ton of people are really only interested in the PvE aspects of the game. Which is bizarre to me. It's got all the makings of an decent hero shooter with all this really simple and repetitive PvE stuff that seems to just get in the way.That being said I'm sure people think the exact opposite of this. Only really caring about the PvE. My point being, who was this game made for? Requardless of all this is not a bad free to play game to play for a few hours with some friends for a goof....But it's 60 bucks. With a battle pass and premium cosmetics day one. Even if that doesn't really bother you. After a few games you realize it's the same boring gameplay loop over and over again and you start to feel like your wasting your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Played a bit over a free weekend - my initial impressions are that the mission variety is fairly dull: you follow a path through a city environment, killing waves of dinosaurs. The faster your team kills the waves, the sooner you can start the "final mission" ahead of the opposite team. The final missions appear to have a pool of 2-3 different objectives, two which involve PvP with the opposite team. That's essentially the gameplay loop and it doesn't get anymore complex than that.Overall, I can't see myself purchasing the game unless its on an extremely heavy discount, and even then, the lack of gameplay variety isn't too appealing. As for positives, the controls and combat feels smooth and the appearances are great. You have decent customizability for your suit's abilities as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best sleeper of 2023. A team based wave-clear shooter with mechas fighting dinosaurs while a maniacal AI pulls you and dinos through time to turn dead exo pilots into zombies with dino brains. If the premise doesn't sell you on this game the actual gameplay should, the classes (healer, tank, dps) are mostly suggestions. The tanks and healers can definitely put out some damage if built right and healing items and upgrades will give all dps teams the survivability you need to win. _childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal is weird. It's a new live-service game from Capcom, acting as a child from the marriage of Dino Crisis and Lost Planet's corpses. It is hard to define because Exoprimal feels like a blender of many different ideas and that is reflected in the main game mode currently available: PvPvE.Getting down to the basics, most of your games will involve shooting dinosaurs with class-based exosuits (that have their own personality separate from your mute character) until the last round where you either race against the enemy team more or get into an objective-based PvP shootout with them. There are dynamic obstacles in play that help the losing team and hurt the winning team, but this assistance has to used carefully so that it's not used at an ineffective time. There is more to the main game mode Dino Survival's premise, but to say more I'd likely be spoiling some nicer aspects of the game.Talking about the gameplay leads me to reflect briefly in what I've seen in many early reviews that typically only have 2-5 hours of gametime. There is a misconception in these early reviews that once you've played this long, you've seen it all. YOU HAVE NOT. There is a lot more varied game content within, however the game chooses to gate this content in two ways: general matchmaking and story progression. Whenever you matchmake for a game, it will pool all currently unlocked (or the newest unlocked, as the priority mission for you) missions for you to play - there is no individual mission selection. In addition, you do NOT unlock story content unless you go through the Data Analysis section of the menu and listen to the conversations/presentations, which are completely skippable if you don't care, but you still need to actually do it.After about 20 hours, I've played to the credits and found out there's also going to be an extreme co-op mode in two weeks time, so it will satiate more co-op minded players. What is currently here is scratching my itch but a live-service game could always use more.What I don't agree with on this game is that it costs 60 dollars and they put a battle pass on top of it. I think they were betting massively on this being a Game Pass game, but they should have at least priced this instead at more like 40 bucks, or paired the battle pass with the game at 50-60 bucks. What IS present here sounds good, feels good and is fun. I personally believe people are already busy with their own live-service addiction and they need to defend it by crapping on a brand new IP one. A point in their favor though is that those games are usually free.

_childDocuments_.review: i'm going to go through the misinformation because it has been insanely high for this game for some reason in particular.i doubt anyone will see this since the negative reviews with less than an hour played Took the top spot, people didn't research it at all and decided it was bad or not what they decided they wanted or thought it should be when they saw a handful of screenshots, it isn't. it runs beautifully the matchmaking works really well and it continues to be a blast here are some key things with now around 13 hours played.-Loot boxes- exist but you cannot buy them, you get them when you level your account and after lvl 50 you get one every single level.This is ACCOUNT LVL not battlepass level those are different. everyone gets these. These items can be got from earned coins in game and or you can wait and hope to get them out of the box. IT IS ALL COSMETIC. is Free and is included with every version of the game. They ARE NOT BOUGHT WITH REAL MONEY. its just a nice little free bit of stuff as you progress. i cant stress enough there is no paid Loot boxes. -Lack of Content- No this is not the case Its a slow burn for some but as you continue on and progress the story by just, you know playing the game, more and more maps open, more dinosaurs, more variations, more Combat scenarios, More 10 player raids, more variations on 10 people raids. Some of these 10 player sections are sick. They are some of the coolest parts of the game for sure and some of those scenarios created show so much potential for both pvp and pve its fantastic. the Idea is you are forced to compete by a rogue AI and he increasingly throws harder and weirder variants at you. i believe the game slowly introduces you to them because when these things come up you need to adapt. which brings me to my next point. -hero shooter. Yes there are classes and heroes in the game but the beauty of this game is the variation to each of them and the reason for the slow progression is teaching you not to stick with one and just only play that, the Adaptability of this game is the Strongest point of it. deciding to switch, when to switch, what rig to switch you can do all this practically on the fly and is necessary to win the games. Sticking to just one character is not a good idea and it really limits you for what is being offered. learning to play to the teams needs is important and incredibly fun if you can set yourself aside and do whats best for the group.-Pay to win/ Weak upgrades No again this is not how it works, you unlock upgrades as you level your account some of which are suite wide so you can put them on any suite as you play specific ones more often you get upgrades to different abilities of that suites abilities and those ones are super powerful if used properly but again YOU CANNOT Spend real money to buy these and are crucial to the late game but still with a good player are not extreme kill shots anything of that nature they allow you to spec each suite more varied to the abilities you prefer and variations to them, honestly think of the suite wide ones to something like monster hunter where if you Slot in high tier earplugs you can reduce or nullify the effects of roars here its similar to lower gems in that game like less knockback, faster recovery time quicker reloads. -PvP yes this is a pvp centered game at its core at the moment but it really isn't, from narrative you are being forced into it and it unfolds in some interesting ways. that said as you play the pvp becomes more and more fun the more you mess around with each class and again see what is needed in each situation. again adaptability. you can turn the tides of a match in this section or fumble it completely. but that is the nature of the game to start and i believe its done this way from the narrative In two weeks we are getting the PVE mode but i think all this helps to get acclimated with the game types and the suites to be prepared for it because i dot think it will be easy this is not a relaxed en-devour it gets really really intense and i imagine it only goes up from here which for people sticking with it i think were in for a real treat. -Paid Dlc on the store. This is the last thing ill touch on because it seems like people are super upset that there is dlc day one on the store, all the items you can pay for are in the battle pass just color swapped, if you want them and don't want to get the battle pass you can just buy the one you want albeit a different color but obviously none of this is needed. The Headstart is exactly what it says it is you can pay for the option to play suits earlier if you want to but all those suites are available in the game and you can get them as you play and level your account. to put it into perspective you get all these before level 50 and i'm at lvl 54 with right around 13 hours played which to be honest feels completely reasonable time frame. again making you try new suites as you get them because you should be swapping. none of them are over powered compared to another its really just situation dependent and the farther you get along you will see that. Another key note to mention is this was free on gamepass and even though there are deals set there for that they still need some way to gather revenue from people who did not buy the game outright and it makes sense to do it this way AGAIN none of this stuff is necessary you can get all of it in the game by playing a very reasonable amount of time. I like this game a lot, I liked the betas I enjoy what it’s offering and it could use improvement for sure but one thing I think people are missing when they say it lacks the content is that the matches get progressively harder the more you play it, you start to see more and different variations of dinosaurs and it gets more involved. The pvp aspect is not a huge setback the way it seems and I think the idea of racing to get to a completion with good teamwork is a good idea at its core. And if nothing else is something new and pretty different in this space. Is it perfect? No but they’ve listened already and done some quick turn around on some aspects which isn’t easy to do and I think as time goes on they’ll continue to make interesting changes. Honestly to me the biggest misstep they made is not having cross platform parties at launch, I also think that this isn’t entirely on capcom and more on the platform holders. I paid $55 for the deluxe edition through humble and I’m enjoying it quite a bit. But if nothing else try it on gamepass and see if you like what’s here.
