_childDocuments_.review: Early review, I will update this over time!Overall thoughts after 4 straight hours.Pros:1. Extremely satisfying. Handling and effects, just feels great to tear through Dino’s.2. PvP and PvE both feel great!3. Mechs are sweet and they feel pretty balanced & fun4. The Dino tech is crazy5. Story and cutscene direction, particularly characters, is very good. Just the right balance between serious and non-serious so far.6. Prog feels fine! Unlocking new stuff for specific mechsuits by playing as them, alongside generic perks over time7. Playing AS a Dino is sweet and fighting it is terrifying. But when you play well, you can demolish another player as a Dino and vice-versa. A very important strategic tool in PvP AND PvE, and is just well done!Cons:1. Early on they give you the same mission back to back so you can learn easily, but that’s a bit repetitive. Not awful you get through it soon enough, but keep that in mind.2. We KNOW that there’s a ton of Dino variety (including bosses) but you’ll be facing roughly the same 5 for a hot minute. I still am! However that’s still really fun, hahaha. Basically the con is, progression is real; you won’t be fighting T-rexes right away, so you've gotta get used to that. It's also a "pro" at the same time in that there's at *least* 10 types of dinos I've yet to fight alongside like 9 major bosses, which is a solid solid amount of content. Mapwise I've played on 4 so far within my first 15 games.3. Battlepass system exists. Is fine otherwise, but the system exists. That's a con for me inherently but it doesn't kill anything for me. Same for paid cosmetics, it's not a big deal to me personally - but I totally understand it being one for others!4. Cosmetics are restrained and fun but some may want more visual variety? I dunno, I can see it being an issue. 5. Can be hard to grasps breadth of strats in PvP cus PvP. PvE is just a fun tense race, but in PvP you can raid and bother people etc. That’s not a negative necessarily but if you forget enemies can and will kill you, it can be an obstacle to fun for peeps. Luckily PvE is hype!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface by saying I love ME3 multiplayer and that was what I was partially hoping for here.  TLDR, this game doesn't really scratch that itch for me, and feel like ME3 MP is just a superior product in comparison, by a decent margin.I also got excited, since most games like the premise of this one usually are FPS and I really am not a fan of FP perspective.  That isn't to say I don't or can't enjoy them, but given the option, I'll always prefer 3rd person to 1st 10 times out of 10.Having said that, the enemy types don't feel varied enough, there are too many fodder enemies not enough "hard" targets,  the pvp is just odd, not particularly interesting when I find myself in those portions.  Using ME3 mp as a comparison, there felt like  alot of opportunities for cool plays in ME3 and the gameplay by the different classes felt fresh and fun to explore from the infiltrator, to the biotic, to the geth to the turian variants etc....there just isn't that variation to Exoprimal comparatively imo and I've tried the support/tank/assault types and while they are different in how they play, to me it doesn't feel that exciting/different while playing any of the class types.This game is just not worth $60 and unfortunately by the time it hits a sale in two months the game will probably be close to dead.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun concept that was horribly mismanaged.60 Euro baseprice is not worth it at all. This should be priced 30 at most on release.most of the characters are locked if you only buy the base game and unlocks are horrificly slow. After 10 hours ive unlocked 3 new characters out of a roster of 12+ unlockable ones. Most of these barely change gameplaywise but some later ones do quite drastically.The PvP is awful. Enemies teleport frequently. Its super laggy and theres nothing you can do about it.The big dinosaurs have terrible hitboxes. If a T-Rex swings his head then everything in a huge CUBE in front of it dies. Most matches also feature PvP as a Dinosaur so now you got teleporting t-rexes with broken hitboxes.The characters themselves are poorly balanced. Some of them are borderline mandatory in certain situations like the taunt + shield. The game encourages an overwatch like character swap system in the middle of the match where youre supposed to change to optimize the time to kill. Nobody ever charnges. Even if you got a good comp you actually need people to do the thing theyre supposed to do. Most of the time they dont. Without a dedicated group youre kinda just screwed.The game does a terrible job at giving the player feedback in general. The only metric you get at the end of a round is "score". This "score" is completely arbitrary and for example blocking with the shield gives obscene amounts. But it doesnt matter if youre actually blocking relevant damage. You can legit press block in front of a horde of weak mobs and go afk and get top scores despite being completely worthless.No ingame text chat function. But voice chat exists (not sure why youd ever turn that on, guess if you dont like your ears you can).MehYou do get to beat up huge waves of dinosaurs with mechs. So yea.. amazing concept but just bad everything else.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it.  It's a hero shooter but faster paced, has a pve element and with dinos to slaughter.  It has an overarching story with cutscenes and data to read.  It's actually pretty cool.  You kinda rush against another team to progress as fast as you can and then some missions devolve into pure pvp as you attack the other team to slow them down.  It also has a pve mode but you still race against the other team, only you don't fight them in the exosuit, you only fight them via the dominator(dino control and summon)  It starts super basic and it seems like there is no content but as you play, you unlock more and more game modes and stages and they just keep unlocking until you play a wide variety of missions.  There is actually a mode where you fight together with the other team that just unlocked for me which is pretty cool.  The dino waves get super crazy like world war z levels crazy which I just love cause it runs well as you ragdoll them around. For the most part, there is a competitive high score feeling to the game so if you don't like that you may be disappointed.  Personally, I don't usually like hero shooters but the blend of PVE and PVP does make me like it.  Plus slaughtering dinos in a robotic exosuit tickles that childish place in my mind that loves such things.  Having now beat the game, the story is fairly enjoyable.  I enjoyed reading the various data you acquire as you play.  I was pleased with it overall.  It has that format that Japanese games where the enemies and scenarios get harder and more insane the longer you go until you are fighting some God-Like thing.  I really enjoyed the 10 player pve scenarios with boss mechanics and everything, or just the 10 player pve scenarios with thousands of dinos running around going insane.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so conflicting.On one hand, the way the game rolls out content is objectively bad. Playing pretty similar games back to back to back for a while until the story progresses seems like a bad idea. But the gameplay was a lot of dumb fun (in the PvE only queue anyways) of just killing large hordes of dinosaurs, and the RE Engine makes sure the game runs well the whole time. I also found the story pretty interesting, although having to stop every match or two to listen to audio might make it harder to binge with your friends. Most of the suits were fun to play too, although I do think Vigilant (the sniper) was one of the weaker ones in my opinion, as well as the flying mech. Nimbus was loads of fun though, and has lots of good tools.SO I DON'T KNOW. Objectively Exoprimal does a lot wrong and most of the players you'll find are crossplaying via GamePass and might not be worth $60. But I had a lot of fun with this game. ♥♥♥♥ the 100k dinosaur kill achievement though.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I would have been SO mad if I'd paid $60 for this. SKIP IT.On paper, this should be a game I'd die for. It's got dinosaurs, it's got mechs, you could theoretically play it PvE... However none of that coalesces into a whole I'm willing to spend time playing. Not for free, and CERTAINLY not for "AAA" game price. The best XP rates are locked behind playing "random" matchmaking between PvE and PvP modes, the customization is non-existent unless you engage with the Overwatch/Fortnite/[insert Live Service Game here]-style shop mechanics, and the gameplay itself is... fine. It feels less like a game carried on the intrinsic fun of gameplay and more like a Minimum Viable Product shipped as a vehicle for the store. But then, the store is so bare-bones and M.V.P. itself that it feels tacked-on and careless. Am I "grinding" the game for terrible cosmetics dealt out via loot boxes, or am I playing dolly-dress up in the hangar so that I can show off in the trite 3rd person shooter? Capcom doesn't know the answer to that design question, and definitely doesn't care. They're the ones with -at the very least- hundreds of thousands of dollars invested in this project. If they don't care, why should I?I could barely finish the tutorial sequence, there was just no flow and so little driving me forward. Setting up my player avatar was both slow and lacking in options. Then getting introduced to the controls had like 3 cutscenes of my silent protagonist pantomiming at the camera followed by a very on-rails explanation of how to click on things. I got told once how to activate abilities, but not what they do or why I'd use them over simply holding down the 'fire' button. The ability selected for demonstration, and the enemies chosen as targets didn't seem like a sensible pairing, either. I know it's a weird complaint, but it's indicative of the lack of attention paid to the assembly of the game. For reference: you get this big railgun on your back, and that's the swappable ability they chose to demonstrate. The enemies selected are flying Pteranodons. They're very clearly chaff-style high-volume targets, easily killable with most suits' primary fire. Thus, using your huge railgun ability on them raises a number of issues: For one, it feels like using a battleship cannon to scare away seagulls. They'd have died anyway, so the ability use feels like "Overkill". The ability is a straight-line piercing projectile and the enemies are a cluster of highly mobile targets. It's not a good tactical use of your chosen weapon against this situation. If they split up, or hover around in clusters, your railgun won't hit everyone and you'll be waiting on a cooldown to try again. You don't want to use a precision weapon here, you want something like an airburst AOE attack or a shotgun/flak-style projectile weapon. You *could* make the case that precision weapons allow you to pick them off one-at-a-time from a distance, but you'd want to use a weapon or ability with lots of follow-up shots or fast recharge. Finally, I'm also at a loss as to how much damage the railgun actually deals. Chaff enemies can be killed by theoretically anything, so the fact that this weapon instant-kills them doesn't tell me much. I tried it out later on a larger target, and dealt X% damage to it. That can be very hard to quantify and especially so when this is a chaotic team-based horde shooter. Is it worth bringing the big cool railgun? I don't know. You can kill a big procession of bunched-up raptors (a situation the tutorial assembles for you elsewhere but DOES NOT combine with the Railgun explanation), but I can't tell you if its utility overall or its damage-dealing potential makes it any better or worse than the mobility tool or "health pack" items you could swap it for. They aren't teaching me a sensible use for this ability, so why demonstrate it at all? It checks the box in the Game Dev checklist that says "you must show a player how to do a thing", so they gave me something to use my ability on and told me which button to press. The only problem is that I'm not learning WHY I'd want to use this in a real combat situation, so the only useful information passed along is the button mapping.This kind of mindlessness is present EVERYWHERE in this title. The UI is functional, but conforms to every convention that comes to mind when I say "sci-fi HUD". The characters you meet are stock stereotypes, which again is fine in a vacuum (and even preferable/beloved in some instances, such as in the context of Street Fighter/Monster Hunter). The objectives of  every mission are THE oldest and most established shooter tropes: Push the Thing, Stand in the Area, Shoot All the Bad Guys Until They Stop Spawning. The spaces you explore are... I guess *technically* varied, but they don't really make a lot of sense. You're not defending hastily-evacuated city streets, it's all simulated recreations (or you're sent back in time to specific battles that all seem to take place on a single island at various points during an emergency, it can be hard to tell because you're likely not meant to think about it too much). So you might be "On The Docks" in one mission, shooting through warehouses and piers, and in another you might be in a "city block" map. Maybe if you sink more time in, you'll play the missions that play in the "digital dimension" or deep in the jungle or whatever, but it's all just set dressing for the "lanes" and "arenas" you'll be fighting through. It all just rolls off of your mind, you might as well be playing the 'Grey Box' renderings of these spaces.What I mean to point out is that it's hard to know or care about the stakes of the action, because these aren't the streets of anywhere in particular. You're not saving New York or Tokyo or Hong Kong or Amsterdam. I *genuinely* can't tell if you're even in The Real World *at all* during gameplay. You might be simulated entirely, or you might be time-traveled to a real place at a previous time. It's impossible to know, and that *would* be fun as a narrative bit, if it weren't for the fact that all the action I saw revolved around a completely isolated and made-up island. Everyone on it, every building there, it was all built FAR from regular human civilization with the express purpose of building, researching, and sustaining their own version of SkyNet. So we might be fighting before, during or after the moment that the AI 'went rogue'. We might be caught in its endless Wargames for some kind of test, for no reason, or for some legitimate purpose that the AI has simply "gameified" as a way to push human subjects to work their hardest averting some end-of-the-world scenario that the AI is genuinely trying to prevent. Who knows? The devs probably don't, and I'd be lying if I said they presented any of this well enough to care. You're never *really* going to find out; this is a live-service game that's going to sit in limbo for as long as Capcom deems them profitable and then the servers are going to shut down. The likelihood that any of the narrative questions matter beyond set dressing is slim already, and even slimmer that they can, will, or already have worked on any wrap-up content that ties up the game's story with a neat bow at the end. You'll play the intro to get acquainted, everyone sits in the static status-quo of "keep killing dinosaurs until something happens, I guess", and then the servers will go down. All we'd have to show for it is thousands upon thousands of hours wasted "grinding" matches, thousands of dollars spent on cosmetics that vanished into the ether and a mediocre story told badly.I'll waste my time elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: For now I am rating this a YES, simply because I am enjoying time played with friends, but here is a more realistic breakdown if it is to help anyone:***THE BAD***The game should be free to play or only cost $20, as day one the developers have shown they are gonna flood with micro transactions. A $10 season pass at release, a $15 head start bundle to instantly get characters locked by progression, & $5 cosmetics that are reskins of the battle pass skins.Early game play is EXTREMELY repetitive, but opens up as you level up and the more you play by providing new levels, new enemy types, new modes, etc. No sole PVE mode, no matter what you do, you are against an enemy team, even in the so called PVE game type.Main story seems...random at best. There are story cutscenes that are triggered by playing certain missions, but the missions seem to spawn randomly and can be repeated at any time.Loot boxes.***THE GOOD***Class type versatility is great and definitely provides needs for appropriate team comps to allow for a competitive drive against the enemy team.Each suit adapts to different play styles so it seems there is a fit for everyone's style of play.Loot boxes are free to open fortunately and don't need a key or grinding to access components to unlock.High octane action.The lore and story can be experienced on anyone's schedule as it is largely told through a database that is accessed in the main menu.Allows for 5 player teams so it is easy to grab friends and vibe in a squad while slaying dinosaurs.For now these are my biggest gripes and highlights, but we all seek something different in gaming. I will say, if you buy this and look to test it before the 2 hour mark for a refund, you won't even experience 1/4 of the overall game. It feels intentionally designed this way to reduce refund costs. If you manage to catch a sale on this game, I do highly recommend it as it is a great way to kill time and just have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Whoa, what a ride that was. Just finished the story and I will say I enjoyed every second playing this game. It brought me back to a feeling of nostalgia of playing Lost Planet 2 with friends on the Xbox 360. (BTW capcom please fix LP2 on steam). It truly feels like an Xbox 360 Capcom game, but in a good way. I didn't know it was a feeling I missed. I may be biased because I am a pvp gamer, but I do recommend this game. I enjoy the gameplay loop of racing the enemy team by  killing your hordes and completing your tasks faster than them. If you are not a fan of pvp, the pure PvE boss battles that you can eventually do are some of the best experiences I have had in a long time. Unfortunately you have to grind the PvP till you can reach them, and then you can queue for those battles specifically till a few weeks from now I believe. I know this game won't be for everyone, but I do suggest you try it. A few things to note:- The game drip feeds you content. The beginning might feel repetitive, but the new missions that come as you level up are what truly make the game shine. Once you get that first big boss battle, you crave more. It may suck, but keep going. It is WORTH IT.- The story is tied to your matches, you progress it by playing matches. There is no single player.- The story is given mostly given through dialogue with portraits of the characters that are speaking. The story itself isn't bad and is the main reason that I kept playing, because I NEEDED to know what happened next. I think the big battles that they plan to release are what will keep me playing, plus the game play itself is fun.- I have heard people say the game is heavily monetized, but I don't see it in its current state. Yes there is a battle pass with cosmetics, and most of the skins you can buy on steam are just recolored skins that are in the battle pass that you can earn. Plus so far the game has a generous loot system that has allowed me to unlock many skins for exos by just playing and leveling up. It doesn't stop, once you hit player level 50, every level afterwards is 1000 coins; then a loot box and 1000 coins the next level, repeat. The coins can buy most skins besides the current premium ones. All in all I do recommend this game. It isn't perfect, but damn is it fun.

_childDocuments_.review: THE GAME ADDS SIGNIFICANTLY MORE CONTENT AS YOU PROGRESS THE STORY.I DONT KNOW WHY CAPCOM DID IT LIKE THIS BUT ITS HOW IT IS.I've got ten hours in the game, so i think i'm entitled to review it.Exoprimal is a PvPvE hero shooter, where PvE takes form in objective-based, competition gameplay agaisnt the other team in two phases. The final mission being (at your choice, or at random) either a PvP-possible objective, or further, difficult PvE objectives.Catch on this wargame mode, is that during the final phase, you will be granted (or the enemy, depending on who's leading), a dominator. Using this lets you invade the enemy team's play area with a miniboss dinosaur likea t-rex  carnosaurus, etc, in order to hinder their progress. Think Destiny 2's gambit invasion if you need a direct reference, except you are a dinosaur.This will be the bread and butter most of the time. I do not yet know how the matchmaking choice on mission bases, but i suspect two factors may be involved: Average story progression% and the players' level average in the match. I've had times where i've had back to back, same type missions that you encounter at low playtime/progression, with a story-variant  mission or a 10-person pve megaboss event here and there.YES: the 10-person PVE mode exists. It's purely just progression and RNG whenever you get to play it or not. I find the way the missions are done somewhat confusing, if needlessly complicated, and capcom could have certainly done a better job with emGraphics are 'modern' to say. Nothing eye-gasmingly amazing, but nothing too horrible either. Enough to at least render two thousand raptors onto your screen with no problems.Game play, whilst repetitive, feels satisfying to myself at least. Certain Exoframes are more appealing to me, but there are many styles. My basic brain favors simple ones like Barrage, Deadeye or Funny Samurai man. When i played during the beta, Vigilant used to be my go-to due to sheer PvP damage it can dish out, but the frame has been turned into a pure glass cannon after the fact, everything kills her quite easily.As with all online games now days, or free-to-plays, the game has a battle pass system. Presumably 10$ being the standard price (i got the deluxe edition because of my beta impressions), i can say that if you plan to play the game, you will definitively get your money's worth, as it has been one of the most /generous/ battlepasses i've seen as of yet. The only way to progress it is..to play the game. No silly quests, no tracking 'bounties' to do specific games, you just play it, and the game dumps almost identical quantities of XP to both your Player level and the pass.As for the generosity remark: Far as i notice, you get an exoframe skin every three levels, with littered decals, emotes and weapon skins in between, and every ten levels or so, you get one of the many legendary skins available on the pass. Would i recommend it? Yes, BUT: If you got other games to play, or the patience to wait for a while, i recommend you do so definitively. If you got nothing else on your list, and are looking for a new game, not minding the light grindiness, then definitively give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Do Not Buy This Game. First off, it is lacking content and the "content" that it has is gated behind hours of playtime. This usually isn't an issue unless the actual gameplay loop is not fun nor has any depth which is the case for Exoprimal. Gameplay consists of shooting hordes of dinosaurs which sounds like it could be fun, but this game feels like you have zero agency. When you're succeeding there is almost no reward and when you're failing you hardly get punished. Gameplay is just blah so you have no incentive to try or not try. Literally the kind of game that will rot your brain.The storyline is pretty bland and repetitive. It's clear there's some mystery going on, but they don't tell you anything interesting until you play for 5 or 10 hours. The story consists of bland cutscenes and reading data logs. You don't really get transported to different areas or unique maps. Think of a game like Titan Fall 2, The story is its own thing and the multiplayer is separate. This game combines the two, but completely fails to deliver any semblance of story. It would literally be like if TF2 removed the entire campaign and added a lore tab in the settings menu where you could read a few data logs that's the story.The icing on the cake is Exoprimal being a $40 game on sale and having a microtransaction, loot box, and battle pass system integrated. It's very clear this game is intended to push the limits to see what people are willing to buy. This borders on being a scam.Long story short your $40 will be much more valuable by Not buying this game. Go spend money on literally anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a total surprise how much I'm enjoying this. Fast, fun combat. Interesting progression with the module/rig system, well-designed Exo suits that feel and play different with enough depth to make you want to level them all to max. The flow of each match has been awesome, horde mechanics interspersed with a sort-of dungeon boss with it's own Monster Hunter-like patterns. Do a few of these as fast as possible for a head start in an Overwatch PvP scenario. If you're bad at PvP you can absolutely make up for it by coordinating with your team to get ahead in PvE, and if you're a PvP demon you can catch up/extend any lead in the PvP section.Also a game that's well-optimized on PC is a welcome change. Solid 120fps on Ultra preset on a 3080, even with what seems like 1000 well-animated units on my screen.Seriously, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. I was expecting EDF with dinosaurs, but got something more akin to a Warframe and Monster Hunter hybrid that's entirely multiplayer. It is a bit of a shame that there's no way to be completely singleplayer, and there's a good chance that after this free weekend it'll be too easy to find lobbies full of bots... but hopefully Capcom will advertise this game more and really push for attention. It's got tons of potential in many different places.Progression feels pretty good with the system to unlock new exosuits (and modules for them) as you play them more. Standard and straightforward, something that's all too rare these days. Especially compared to something as complicated as Monster Hunter, another Capcom game nonetheless. Both exosuits and modules change gameplay by a very wide margin, even within the same classes, and the modules allow for the more personal loadout customization in each individual suit. Just a few more additions to each suit would make for some wonderful variety overall.My biggest complaint that doesn't have to do with the smaller playerbase size has to do with the matchmaking. I've seen lobbies with 3 bots on my team and none on the enemy's, level 500 players on mine and only up to level 30s on the other, etc. There doesn't seem to be much correlation to how the teams are balanced, which I understand is tough to implement in a game that isn't exactly thriving with players, but I still need to bring it up. I'm sure it kind of annoys many players in general.Otherwise, not too much else to talk about. Cosmetics look pretty nice all around, and I do not have many QoL changes that I'm really itching for. The game runs pretty well and I haven't had any weird bugs or optimization issues crop up. This is a pretty well polished experience that just needs some more well-rounded content selection and touch-ups with the multiplayer integration. Capcom has it hidden away for some reason and is allergic to advertising it more. Big shame. Tl;dr: Fun to play, feels good to level up and unlock stuff. Multiplayer internals could use some tweaking. Would benefit greatly from more players/Capcom doing better at letting people know the game exists. Get it on sale if you're interested.

_childDocuments_.review: Update Title update 3: Since the latest update I feel like the game has become a lot better content variety wise. I don't get beginner maps as often, and I feel like the modes I get in general are different most of the time. There is also a bigger variety of weapon selection for exosuits. I wish they had more ability variety as well but oh well. It still isn't perfect but its a major step up. I still wish there was a bit more control over the modes/maps you play on, for example I played like 30 matches in the last 2 days but still haven't seen the new super raid fight. I wish I could skip cutscenes I have already seen. There is a lot more I wish was just better, but at this point id be comfortable to put this in the recommend range rather then just neutral. There is still a lot of work to be done but its absolutely going in the right direction.This is exactly the type of game I wish I could give a neutral review. Exoprimal is a great game with so much going for it. Yet the game is riddled with annoyances and things holding it back. Lets get into it.First what makes this game great. The core aspects of this game are fantastic. It looks fantastic and runs great. The game is fun to play and has a good amount of varied and fun content. The story is surprisingly strong with fun characters and an engaging plot, its nothing award winning but it adds a lot to the game. The game has high difficulty pve content and the chaos you feel as thousands of dinos swarm your team is something fresh, exciting and fun. There is also a challenge mode/speedrun mode that switches every week after you beat the story. The goal of that mode is to clear it or to get as fast as a time as possible beating it to compare yourself to others. The joy I had when I got a top 10 % time was insane, its incredibly fun to try and improve your time even by seconds, the game feels so rewarding in those moments. I seriously can't praise all of these parts of the game enough.So what is holding me back from just saying this is a recommend 100 %? Its that getting to actually play the game is an insane drag. To begin with the story is integrated in your early progression, every match you get a bunch of lore explaining what is going on, if you collect enough lore you can progress the story. Once you have progressed the story enough you start seeing the different modes the game has to offer, it took me about 10 hours to feel like the game was genuinely offering something more to me then the basic mode of slaying basic dinos, those 10 hours are a drag and don't feel fun. The difficulty at those 10 hours is so incredibly low and boring that you can almost do everything alone. During matches you race against opponents to see who can finish the PVE content first, but with the difficulty being so low I felt like both teams were always next to each other in terms of progress to finish the missions. It took me another 15 hours to finish the story and the game kept getting better during those 15 hours.So that makes about 25 hours to finish the ''turtorial''/story mode. If that was all the game asked it would be fine, but the problem is that the game gives you practically 0 control over what you are going to play, that cool boss you just faced, want to do it again? Well that sucks you can't. You can only hope the game offers it up on a limited time speedrun contest every week or for you to randomly get it when you queue for a match.Not only that but because other new players also need to play through those first 10 hours we now also have to deal with playing those low level easy missions even after completing the story. Imagine having to play the first level in a game over and over again without being able to decide if you want to play it, there isn't enough diversifying to make that first level feel interesting. To add salt to injury if you do get an interesting mission you usually have to watch a cutscene, those cutscenes are really fantastic the first time, around, but after seeing them for the 5th time you start to REALLY wish there was a skip button.The last topic I want to cover is the live service model. In general you can get everything in the game through gameplay relatively simply, it can be a bit time consuming but it is honestly quite nice to see a game offer nice cosmetics and progression that is very accessible. My only complaint is that the game recently added more exosuits variety that you can play as, the unlock requirement for these suits however is quite time consuming, being able to experiment more with those suits would help a lot with enjoying the grind through those first 10 hours.All in all Exoprimal is still something I would recommend. I see a massive amount of potential here, it has that capcom magic all over it and the roadmap already showed some exciting updates like a collab with Street fighter 6 as well as Monster hunter. That being said right now that potential isn't realized properly and there is a lot holding it back, are you willing to shelf over 60 bucks for a live service game when there are now a ridiclious amount of free to play games that offer even more content then this game? That is up to you to decide. What I will say is that when Exoprimal is at its best its a REALLY good game, something that will keep getting improved. If capcom doesn't decide to pull the plug on this game due to playercount then I think this game has a very bright future.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It is a very fun game, but the amount of content is not worth the 60 euro (basically 70 euro...) price tag.The main gameplay loop consists of running through a map completing objectives, such as defeating a certain amount of dinosaurs or defending an area. When you're doing these objectives survival is rarely a major concern, the main focus is instead to complete them faster than the enemy team. The game features an interesting story and an expanding amount of gameplay content the further you go, on the flipside this means the game feels fairly barebone at the beginning. Overall the game is quite fun with a fairly interesting story and an okay amount of replayability, but it does only have the one speedrun gamemode with a limited amount of variability, which would make it a great 40 euro game, but in my opinion lacking content for a 60-70 euro game.Update: Now they added an new variation of each exosuit, but to play them you either need to grind each and every character or... pay money of course. The game was already lacking content for the price tag, and now they're just adding more paid content instead of making the game worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review: Its mechs vs dinosaurs, of course its a super fun game! Long review: Exoprimal has a  with multiple things levelling up, be it the player level, battle pass, or individual suits' levels, which constantly makes you feel like you are progressing. Even after a less-than-ideal round, you feel like you've at least achieved something. The  is impressively good. Dominators (big dinos you possess) and Dino Upgrades (makes the dinos fighting the enemy team harder), evening the playing field, leading to almost every match feeling like a close call. Every mech has a unique playstyle that compliments a large set of other exosuits and setups. Swapping between mechs at any time allows for a fun and un-punishing flow between different objectives for example switching from the close-ranged Roadblock for clearing out hordes of dinosaurs to a Krieger for more long-ranged payload defense. The same goes for Rigs which is basically bonus-abilities that any mech can equip. This leads to a large variety of gameplay variants which helps spice up the replay-ability. The  is surprisingly fun to follow with entertaining characters and good story beats. The characters are fun, quirky, and likeable. There interesting world building and lore as well as some cute character moments that help draw you into the story. The cutscenes are fun as well as some of the reveals. The beginning of the game is a bit slow, with . Since I beat the Season 1 story two days after the game's release (the story took me about 24 hours to complete) (I am unwell) a lot of late-game missions are still locked behind the newest member of whatever party I join. I still haven't encountered two of the Neosaurs listed on the exoprimal website. This will probably get fixed up once more people have played and beat the story proper.  On top of the $60+ ($70 for the deluxe version) there's also a battle pass ($9.99), head start kit ($14.99), and cosmetics dlc ($4.99 each). Personally if this is the direction this game wants to go, I think it should be a "free" to play game. It could help entice bring in new players to enjoy a new ip that they may be hesitant towards supporting/investing time into. There's  despite being able to match with them. I have friends who I want to play it with who are playing through xbox's gamepass. I really enjoyed playing in a 5 stack team during the free beta and I haven't been able to recreate that feeling because of this. I've had a lot of fun so far! think this game has a ton of potential and I'm excited to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: I maintained a powerful level of hype for this game, participating in both beta tests over the past year or so. The betas were both enjoyable and incredibly promising. Surprisingly enough, with the launch of the full game, the amount of content not in the beta was subtle. An explanation: when you start the game, for the first......10(?) war-games you play, your combat content is actually limited to dinosaur culling almost exclusively. It's still *very* fun mind you, but not even seeing area defense, or any other alternate mission objective was weird, and can easily bore most players, especially with the PVP only using data escort as well. I mean, its the same content, on the same 3 maps. perfectly reasonable. But after those, ~10 or so, war-games, and you've progressed the story, you get put into a story forced round, where nothing but new ♥♥♥♥ is thrown at you. After that, the game starts throwing new objectives, and new pvp modes at you consistently: area defense, point capture, omega hammer, NPC escort. Along with this, the dinosaur variety explodes from about 4 dinos on repeat to like 10 or more.It weirdly locks the game content, in a very thematic way mind you as its leviathan seeing your progress and wanting to challenge you, behind story progress. thematic yes. problematic, kinda yes. It doesn't take long, but that's still 10 approximately thirty minute matches. This could easily turn off players. SO firstly, stick with it, it gets sooooooo much better after that story hurdle. Not even including the crazy new boss fights.Gameplay-wise, the suits all handle uniquely and all satisfyingly perform their roles, with the ability to switch suits mid match still helping you adjust to tough fights. PVP is also very fun, never feels unreasonably stompy, and the variety of suits lets you really dish out punishment to the enemy team. Not to mention the unlock-able passive chips that you can equip to your suit to then further customize their playstyle, albeit slightly.Now the few complaints I have:1. taking 3 suits randomly and making people unlock them when they were playable in the beta. Like seriously, is dumb2. Same thing with the swappable rigs(6 unique use items, only 3 available at start), why.3. The price. Is the game worth $60 with only multiplayer content? yes but no. Will you get that much enjoyment out of it? probably, I know I am. But its a hefty tag when there's no solo content.If you want to show capcom that this game is worth it, and hopefully give them reason to make more like it(maybe even with a campaign mode) I recommend buying it. Waiting for a sale works too. But honestly getting a full recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: The real game is not like the beta. It's a bit more varied. And you pretty much unlock everything in this game simply by playing.Its PvE mode is integrated with the competitive nature of the story.There is still PvP. But you can turn off direct PvP. You will still be competing and it is relevant to the story, so you -have- to do it. Honestly, it isn't bad. Although it will feel a bit repetitive, you are always rewarded with more story. _childDocuments_.review: Updated on Jul 5th:  So basically:- After season 4, comes season 1 again, and so it'll be until the servers are shut down ( "Time loop rebellion" revealed itself as a great title for the most recent game mode in many ways now)- No new battlepasses, game modes, thicc robot skins or collabs with Capcom IPs (They seriously gave us Megaman Collab before a DMC collab and I'll never forgive the Japanese for that)- Expect the same dumb Capcom dongle as reward for login bonus on every Capcom Anniversary until the end of time. That's it folks, pack it up, Kunitsu-Gami is right around the corner and I can't wait to be made a fool again.Original review:First and foremost:  . The game is great, actually one of the best multiplayer experiences I ever had in my miserable life, but the steam price is outrageous and it's really holding this game down. Capcom is out of their mind by not dropping this ridiculous price tag in order to open doors to new players on steam. 1- Comparisions to Helldivers 2 are constant and not only dumb, but criminal and should be a capital offense punished by making the offender take a shower. The only thing both games share is the "coop" tag. Exoprimal is about putting Iron Man in the Dino Crisis universe to see how many chicken-ancestors he can take before a rogue Chat-GPT says it's time to go to bed. It's an arcade experience not intended in any way to have you tactically moving to complete objectives. You pick your exosuit, and smash hordes of dinos while learning among dozens of hours on how to best make use of upgrades and skills, to do it better, faster, sexier (hope this is a word). Matches are short, and your class matter, as typical hero shooter. So, as I said: Nothing like Helldivers 2.2- The game is not dead, far from it. Matches start after 2 or 4 minutes in queue. And as long as Game Pass players keep being able to join with their mics permanently turned-on while they eat dorittos and scream at their moms, the game will be alive and well. Also, updates are slow, collabs are probably going to be mixmashes of Capcom franchises ultil these servers are unplugged, since let's be real, this game didn't take off at all. And in-house Capcom IPs are probably indeed the smartest option to keep things interesting here.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, it's really that simple. A premise so straightforwardly dumb that I can't help but ask, "Why didn't this happen sooner." :DWith 3 classes for each role of Attacker, Defender, or Healer there are 9 unique playstyles to choose from. Each of them also has an Alpha variant that changes one thing about the class (e.g. Deadshot's weapon goes from an automatic rifle to a tri-burst/shotgun). At any point in a match, you can change your class and equipment so experimentation is encouraged.Matchmaking has always been fast. Even now with the hype of the launch died down I still find matches within 5 -10 sec.I could not care about the story in the slightest. I came to kill dinosaurs and the game doesn't get in the way of that since the story is played through multiplayer (there is no single-player mode). However, when an antagonist is introduced and established I did notice I was getting a little bit hyped with the dynamic it was creating. The more you go through the story the more maps are unlocked, more alterations of dinosaurs fought, and a couple of more game types are introduced. Even though I wasn't paying attention, I did enjoy how the story was delivered because when the end of the game came I actually understood what was going on. With that being said, the game types are no different than the ones you'd find in Team Fortress or Overwatch. I really wished there was a greater variety of dinosaurs in the game. I read a lot of dinosaur books as a kid and would love to fight Therizinosaurus or an Elasmosaurus that's able to be on land. They do have unique dinosaurs but it feels like such a small sample is currently available. As a second option for multiplayer, every weekend there is a Gauntlet Mode where your team has to take on a more difficult threat under tighter constraints than the main multiplayer. While I enjoy the challenge, it does feel creatively uninteresting.There are updates coming along. We have a collab with Street Fighter and Monster Hunter for the next two seasons. This is the most I've enjoyed an online shooter since Black Ops 2 and Overwatch so if those updates can bring more maps, more game modes, and (most importantly) MORE DINOSAURS, I think I'll be really happy because it's already a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've honestly been looking forward to this game, not because I had any big expectations, simply because I knew it would be something to semi-mindlessly enjoy. This game has actually surprised me with the way the combat and progression systems are set up. Each Exo-suit is fun to use and the modules (upgrades) allow you to change your play-style and priorities according to what you think/feel is most beneficial to either yourself or (preferably) the team.The leveling is actually insanely fast and the 'story' progression is done in a unique way, It ties to the scaling difficulty of newer missions and game modes unlocked as player level increases. The game did feel repetitive for the first couple of hours, mainly because it felt easy, but as new modes and enemies are unlocked it definitely becomes more challenging and forced players to switch up the way they approach some tasks.As for the those that want a more PvE experience.. remember what the base concept of the game/lore is about.. creating the perfect.. using combat data. No matter what mode you play you will be going up against other Exo-fighters. The only difference with PvE is that you don't directly fight other humanoid players. As far as them using the dominator.. just think of it as an intelligent AI control dino.. Kite it, Kill it. (I personally don't get the complaints on that one sorry)I think this game is incredibly fun, but I get that not everyone can make that full commitment without the assurance of a refund, so I'd recommend checking out higher level game-play videos in order to make a more informed decision.Best of luck, and happy hunting.. "You are completing objectives faster than the enemy team" :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'd rate it a solid 7.2/10 for its current state. It feels like the game was rushed-- and I don't mean that in the standard fashion. It feels more like the developers had more planned, but decided to keep the original release date vs holding off on it and releasing it with additional content.Don't get me wrong, the current game-play loop is incredibly satisfying. I haven't experienced any graphical, audio or any other glitches whatsoever, which is surprisingly rare on most games first launch week theses days. However, it does feel odd that additional enemy dinos, modes, and maps appear to be somewhat locked behind a progress log that has something to do with the total amount of matches you have played thus far, and the amount of Archive based content you have unlocked/watch/read.While that in and of itself might be fine, its very odd that I have yet to experience the purple-goo dinos shown in the trailers, or that lava lake like fight, but I assume it has something to do with the locked content behind a progression-like wall.I do think a sandbox like mode with a sea of dinos being thrown at you in a large map with two objectives; survive and kill some behemoth of a creature at the end, would go a long way in additional content for this game. Additionally, while the story is very interesting, its unfortunate that there isn't any single player mode to enjoy the story in. And while its an odd choice, it isn't necessarily a bad one.Regardless, more content such  additional modes-- particularly a true PvE mode where no 'invasions of player dinos' can happen and a single-player based mode would go a long way in retaining interested of all players alike. Even though I greatly enjoy the game and want it to do well and expend on whats currently here, I can't recommend it for its current price tag. Its got a value of around 25-30$ USD, not 60$. Definitely would tell any curious users to hold off until the game goes on sale. Or at the very least, for the next 3 months or so when the devs are more likely to release additional content.Still, that said, out of this years pre-ordered games, I don't regret this purchase one bit, despite its shortcomings, its still a very enjoyable game with fluid combat and relatively smart horde-like AI.

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this game. But making this game a PVP-focused multiplayer game is possibly one of the worst decisions ever. The game should've played like Left 4 Dead, Deep Rock Galactic mission-based Co-op horde shooter.The game's main marketing point was all about fighting a massive horde of dinosaurs but the game barely provide those. It's really unfortunate. It feels like Capcom has this bad habit of putting a lot of money and effort into these weird ass multiplayer games that are kinda destined to fail. If this continues, people's respect that Capcom has been built might crack as well.If you wanna play a better Capcom multiplayer game, just buy any Monster Hunter or Street Fighter 6, and if you wanna shoot down massive hordes of enemies, buy RE4 Remake and play mercenaries. Capcom has been doing amazing with their main IPs seriously, now it's time to get their ♥♥♥♥ together with all these weird multiplayer titles like RE Verse and Exoprimal.UPDATE:I played this game for a total of 19 hrs and just saw the ending. And as you might read in other reviews of this game, the game unlocks more dinos and events and adds more challenges as you progress through the story. I actually quite enjoy the final boss fight, it was fun and needed some co-operations and it had a ♥♥♥♥ ton of dinosaurs.But I still don't think I can fully recommend this game. Mainly the game is $60 and has shallow content (at least for now) and the main mode is still kinda annoying sometimes, even after the endgame. The game being more co-op focused would be much better.If Capcom makes some good calls, I think the game can be much better at a later date. But it's sad to see that Capcom out of all the video game companies is also doing this "Game will be better at a later date" Live-service tactic. Their recent Street Fighter 6 and especially Monster Hunter World/Rise was packed with content when it was released.I would say that if you want to buy the game, I would say that personally, Battlepass is quite worth it, it gives you a lot of cosmetics that's actually quite worth it. But that's just my opinion so I recommend doing your own research.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too good. Monster Hunter feel andd quality, but third person shooter horde mode with objectives. The game's downfall is the menu just showing off one gamemode at the beginning (you get more later on) as I've completed the story, almost all suits at level 20 and player level 100+, but I'm still meeting new dinos and missions and maps. A new player might believe there's only like 5-10 missions if they only play a few hours or group up with a friend that's lower level as them since new missions get unlocked as you level up (no indication of this in-game either, you just have to experience it) and the lowest leveled player controls the pool of missions available (which makes sense as they do get harder). The season pass you can gladly skip unlike most games and it's cheaper aswell (no Blizzard greed). 90% of cosmetics are outside paywalls and progression doesn't feel grindy at all. It's a strange take on story presentation, but it's actually very well thought out for a multiplayer game you didn't expect to have such a great story. There's only worldbuilding intro and basic tutorial before you play multiplayer for the rest of the game, even story missions. However you cannot manually choose missions, so story progression can get very on/off depending on the friends you play with or even solo (less so solo) as you need to get enough progression before the next story mission is available, then you need to matchmake with people at the same place. This hasn't been a problem, just a note, but this is how friends can "halt" your progression somewhat, but there's no real downside to this as you won't powerlevel and just destroy the next mission. Solid 9/10 we need more of these highlights to this year. There's also more of this coming for free already this month.

_childDocuments_.review: After 45 hours, I can say that I recommend this game for those who like horde shooters. As quite a few other reviews have stated, many complain about the lack of content, but the content is locked behind the story's progression system. So the more you play the game, the more maps, dinosaurs, and game modes will unlock. This can be a good or bad thing, depending on what you're into. For me, it's good, as the more I play, the more I unlock things and the game feels less repetitive. The downside is that it will take time for those to unlock content, and it can be a huge con for those who are looking to jump in to play a quick game, expecting all content to be available to them. There are some few janky things here and there, but the devs seem to be listening and have been very open with communication so far. Other than that, $60 can feel a tad expensive for what the game is, so I definitely recommend either trying out the game on game pass or wait for a sale. I'd say this is a good game for those that like horde shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll redo the review after 30 hours in the game.The response to commands is fantastic, I have never noticed a slowdown or input lag.For the first 3-4 hours of the game I would have gladly returned it, but after getting the hang of it for a moment, understanding the various exosuits, understanding the types of dinosaurs, in the end this game is wonderful.after 30 hours can you already hear the repetition? Unfortunately yes, but it's not excessive, each mission can be different especially due to the PVP element in which at a certain point you have a carnotaur at your disposal with which to attack the opposing team. At the beginning this can be disturbing and for those who love PVE it can even be hateful, but in reality with that touch of randomness that never hurts, it's as if there was a more intelligent extra boss to fight, so it's not bad. (+10,000 points are always welcome)There are few Steam users, but cross-play and multiplatform is enabled so matches can be found rather quickly.Do you like exosuits and do you like killing dinosaurs? then this is the game for you.The thing I love most is blocking a triceratops' charge with the shield, really, you can feel the power of the triceratops impacting the shield and the exosuit using all its strength to contain it.Skins can be bought or unlocked with supply crates that you earn as you level up, from level 51 onwards, you get a supply crate for each level.Great community.No toxicity.Widely recommended.The dinosaurs are waiting for you.

_childDocuments_.review: $30 game, not $60. And suits take way too much grinding to level up to actually be able to use your unlocked attachments on them. _childDocuments_.review: A fun, unique title with its share of pros and cons.Pros:- A variety of objectives (through play time) that can be done casually or somewhat competitively.- A smaller, but distinctive roster for many different play-styles (with more Variants to come).- Generous amount of customization, both cosmetic and stat-wise.- Fits well with people who are fans of PvPvE, but has a sole PvE mode coming soon (at time of posting).- Crossplay... to an extent, so matchmaking times aren't bad, especially solo-queuing.Cons:- Many people see it's price of $60 as well as having a Premium Battle Pass for an additional $10 as a bit off-putting.(And I agree, I do think if the game was a bit cheaper, or the same price but with the Battle Pass content all being free it would be more appealing, as I've seen the price point being the deal breaker for quite a few people.)- Only 5 Maps at launch. ( It seems that games are getting more and more cheap when it comes to giving us maps; I remember when games like Call of Duty would launch base games with 12-15 maps, then around Cold War down to as little as 8. There needs to be enough different environments to keep things interesting. I know there are examples of games having fewer maps and working, but this isn't one of them, it needs more variety.)- Launch Roster of 10. (As I mentioned earlier, the roster is diverse and fun enough to hold people over, but not for long. They made all the characters available in the Beta, which usually you don't do that, so I'm sure like myself, others were disappointed to see no new characters at full release. Again, they said they will be releasing new Variants of the current roster in title Update 1, meaning new movesets and slightly altered design, but not entirely new suits. I'm okay with this, but I still think a new suit should be planned every now and again, because a roster of 4 DPS, 3 Tank and 3 Support doesn't sit well.- No Cross-platform Parties. (They did address this in a tweet that it was a difficult process and that they would make an effort to implement it in the future, but don't count that as a guarantee.)I've personally been having a blast, and it seems a good 74% (at the time of posting this) of the playerbase is as well. It's a very fun game, especially with friends (although that's almost any game) and I hope it gets and sustains a decent playerbase. Hopefully when the PvE only mode drops it will bring back the people who have already written it off, as well as persuade newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start...There's not much in terms of gamemode or map variety. There's an insulting amount of skins/battle pass/DLC greed on display. The story feels tacked on and it unconvincingly attempts to contextualize the game's obtuse premise. Story dialogue is almost always awful and the exosuits’ limited number of quips range from annoying to uninspired. The silent protagonist situation is super awkward and player character customization is surprisingly weak for an engine/company that brought us the character creator in SF6 and MHR.Queue times are long, matchmaking seems mostly random, and the gameplay is no replacement for many of the other co-op shooters. Close/back-and-forth games seem rare with momentum being hard to stop and no obvious tug-of-war system to keep the leading team on their toes. Team compositions aren't usually well-coordinated either. The number of synergies between exosuits that might've enhanced gameplay are slim to none. Abilities are usually single-purpose self/AoE buffs or defense stuff with the rest being individualistic attacks.Enemy variety is rough. Of all the games that could’ve taken fun creative liberties with dinosaurs, Exoprimal keeps the lizard diversity dry with basically two categories: small ones that are trivial and medium/large ones that charge at you.While Exoprimal comes across as largely derivative and has elements that bear a striking resemblance to various ongoing live service games, what's here isn't not fun to play. All the weapons/abilities have satisfying animations/sounds which makes the moment-to-moment dino-hunting haptically entertaining. The whole absurd  premise has my inner child pretty hyped. Plus, I've kind of been looking for a team-based shooter that's not exclusively PvP that also includes classes/support characters. So, against my better judgment, I've been mostly enjoying the core of Exoprimal.So, the game fills a random, temporary niche for me, but I can't bring myself to recommend it based on that. It also feels wrong to promote a game with such toxic monetization. But if you are interested in the game, don't buy it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with lots of content on the horizon. They already have a new hardcore mode coming in about a week and numerous new exosuits, areas, and skins planned out for at least a year. Many people are complaining that you are forced to PvP and this just isn't true, in fact the PvE elements are WAY more enjoyable than fighting players, but the PvP feels fairly balanced with the ability to outplay anyone with anything as long as you know what you're doing. PvE-wise, not only is there a PvE-only queue, but some missions end in a 10-player coop showdown against a huge wave of enemies or a big baddie boss, which is TONS of fun, challenging, and completely cooperative. The gameplay itself is great at what it is: shooting/slashing dinos feels very sastisfying in both the visual and auditory feedback. A rogue AI constantly screams at you to do better. This does make you want to do better. However, Capcom are asking you to shell out a LOT of money just for the game (which is effectively Overwatch if it had a PvE mode before you did PvP with anyone), let alone the battlepass which is an additional $10. I don't have an issue with this because I love this game, but if you don't feel like paying $60 upfront for Dinosaur Overwatch, definitely get it on GamePass.It's not as microtransaction-heavy as other reviews want you to believe. I guess people put in like 30 minutes to get through the tutorial, see a few classes are level locked with an option to buy them, and want to cry about paywalls. Many things can be bought with ingame currency that the game loves to shove down your throat, including EVERY class and I would say 80% of the cosmetics.If you enjoy the repetitive grind of the average hero shooter, this game is worth the money and definitely does not lack for content in that regard. I'm not entirely sure that people who don't think this game has the content to at least be charging SOME money have ever played a hero shooter or any lobby-based cooperative game, because if they had, they would know MANY games charge this amount of money for what is ultimately a repetitive, grindy loop carried by playing it with your friends or competing against randoms. Sure, Overwatch is free, but Overwatch is also pvp-only and makes its money off the tons of skins sold by its immense reputation and history in the industry which obviously a new game trying to innovate on the formula doesn't have.Sixty bucks? Maybe not. Good thing it's on GamePass. Personally I don't mind if a game like this costs money. One, I KNOW this game will give me my money's worth and two, spending money generally deters cheaters (lets be honest, EAC doesn't do anything).The story gets completed in give or take 10 hours of running missions and spamming your way through the lore, probably significantly longer if you watch everything but honestly it's just barely good enough and is carried by the decently-written and well-acted characters. The best part of the story is honestly unlocking the big cooperative endings where you fight bosses because THAT is real good stuff.Very fun, sometimes frustrating, and a little overly expensive, but ultimately a quality, polished product that, while not likely to ever be as popular as its competition, definitely has staying power and potential to grow into an even better game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the story for Exoprimal. This game has a lot of potential story and gameplay wise! The new missions, maps, and dinosaurs you will encounter are a absolute blast to experience! You unlock new modes, maps, and dinosaurs to fight as the game progresses. Every 5 matches you will get a new cinematic that will involve a boss fight with all ten players, a new map, or gamemode! I really enjoyed how the progression in this game works and I encourage others to stick with it! The only micro transaction in the store is to buy the battlepass and cosmetics for suits for the suits. Loot boxes are in this game for cosmetics, however they are not obtainable by purchasing them. You can only earn them by leveling up.The gameplay is highly addictive with every new match being just as great as the last! I personally really enjoy the suit, "Kriegor." You can swap suits mid game while on the battlefield allowing you to switch your play style whenever you would like. The suit transferring animations and amazing to watch and I really enjoy being able to swap suits while in game. The beginning of the PVP matches goes as each team of five race in parallel universes to get their missions done the quickest. Once a team as completed all of their missions, they get transported to the same universe with the other team and it is now a race to complete what the objective might be. Such as, payload, zone control, energy pick up, etc. The team who gets their missions done the quickest will be at the shared universe before the other team giving them a slight advantage in whatever the gamemode is. Customizing your suits are fun. There are a lot more skins that are not shown available for purchase (only obtainable in loot boxes). You can give your suits augments they give them bonuses, such as faster reloading, faster movement, more health, less damage from dinosaurs, etc. They each have their own unique augments specific for that suit. None of them are game breaking to the point where you blame the enemy player for winning because they had said augment. They provide a unique change of playstyle that is not too impact full to be game breaking or a balance issue for PVP.Small rant to negative reviews, steam shows to not have a not-so active player base of under 5k. However this game is cross platform and a majority of players are on consoles. I get in matches in under seconds never having to wait long to play! I recommend this game for anyone who likes shooting a endless amount of dinosaurs with a fun pvpve gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom tried something new with this game and I really enjoy it. The first few hours are pretty repetitive and that's due to the fact that the story is tied to the "matchmaking" and unfolds as you queue up for matches. The missions are pretty straight forward with you and your team racing against the enemy team to follow a set path and eliminate all the dinos in a specific area as fast as possible and towards the end of the mission you will either be (depending on the mode type) fighting against the enemy team and/or their team controlled dinosaur and vice versa. Near the end of the matches depending on who is in the lead, the game will reward the losing team a controllable dinosaur first to attempt to gain an advantage. Matchmaking is also determined by whoever has the least story progression in the lobby which will have you playing the same story missions until the current player base is progressed enough through the story.Gameplay feels great in exoprimal as you are always on the move and the characters are very fluid and feel fun to play. The characters are separated into 3 classes being Damage, Tank, and Support. each character has a unique playstyle that can be modified with unlockable perks, and a secondary equipment weapon. There are also plenty of cosmetics and unlockables that don't require any real purchases and can be earned by playing and spending in game currency.The real MEAT of the game comes in a few hours into the story which is a shame because the missions become raid boss levels of insane at times and some missions just have both teams join together to fight a single large threat. There are more enemy types that begin to appear and they each have their own mutated variant that have their own unique abilities that can be very challenging at times as you can be swarmed with hundreds of dinos while you try to fight off the larger ones that are barrel rolling your team into the dirt.Coming into this with low expectations I have to say I am having a great time with Exoprimal, it definitely isn't your standard multiplayer experience but it offers something new and exciting that few other games have today.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like mechs and want to blast a bunch of dinos in different ways I highly reccomend this game, with a caveat of getting a key or game-pass as it's absolutely not worth the £50 price tag thats still listed nearly 12 months later.Exoprimal offers somewhat decent progression in the form of (character) mech-unlocks, which are the original mechs but with a twist. Your 3 mainstays of tank, damage dealer and support are on offer and each has their own way to keep things fun and getting you to try out ways to speedrun your way to the end of each level - outpacing other teams. The story is fine, what really shone for me were the combat/ raid style encounters that follow. They feel special, unique and really make you feel like there's a big bad AI to kill. However it's a shame you can't jump into these great moments easily, together with friends like you could in other Capcom greats like Monster Hunter.After racing to complete the first lot of objectives (commonly hordes of raptors, but different maps) you'll be thrown into another dimension to complete a different style of race either PVE or PVP.The gameplay loop is good, somewhat let-down by having you bash your head against the same 2 maps and Objective completing missions. PVP follows well-known modes, lending itself to either a payload push or king of the hill style brawl which I found to be a bit more adrenaline inducing. There may have been stellar marketing for this game on arrival however it doesn't seem to do much to keep you wanting more 12 months on. Right now there's a mega man raid and I've seen theres also a monster hunter raid, alongside the fact that upon completing the story you unlock 2 harder missions to jump into which I like the sound of. Considering it's a full priced game, the battle pass system is ridiculous and the fact you can pay real money to unlock free content is bizarre. I wish they kept that out of the game and introduced a novel progression track that enticed players to stick around instead of opening their wallet (again, this is a FULL PRICED GAME nearly 12 months on).All in all, give it a shot if it's on a big sale, give it 10-15 hours and work through the story content to really enjoy that raid-like content and fingers crossed you'll have as much fun as I did!

_childDocuments_.review: After about 20 hours of gameplay, I managed to beat the story. The story is comprised of a series of audio-logs and cutscenes (most are skip-able) that you obtain randomly throughout playing the missions. The further you progress into this story, the more difficult missions become.I played a total of 56 matches to get to this point, and overall, I would recommend this game.As an aside, the game features [at time of review] 10 unique exosuits (basically heroes/characters/what have you) that you can choose from during a match, all fitting in 3 categories: Damage, Tank, and Support. 3 of them you have to level up in order to unlock, but all the suits I tried are fun.As you progress through the story, you will start to encounter boss fights, which feel a lot like raid bosses from your favorite RPG game. Instead of team V team, the entire lobby works together to defeat them. I think there are about 3 or 4 of these bosses in total, and every single one of them are both challenging and engaging. Overall, the bosses are fun.Mentioned previously, the farther you get into the story, the harder enemies appear during matches. I couldn't count the unique enemies, but there are plenty in my opinion. As far as the battlepass goes, I know its a hot topic of discussion. I had reached level 30 in the battlepass at time of review, which is a bit less than half. To purchase the battlepass, it is $10. KEEP IN MIND, the battlepass is purely optional. The only things you get from it are cosmetics. They dont lock new characters to play behind it (like some other hero PvP games that shall not be mentioned.) Do NOT let the fact that it has a battlepass deter you if you are interested in the game. Not having it wont affect your experience at all.There is [at time of review] only 1 queue-able game mode; however, after completing the story, the game reveals there is one gamemode being developed. In the current gamemode, there are a variety of (randomly selected) objectives to complete, everything from just murdering a bunch of dinos, to escorts, to strong PvP encouraged point systems. Not all objectives are PvP, but it does play a big part in the ones that are. Overall, this game in essence is pure, mindless fun where you can turn your brain off and just mass murder a bunch of dinos, and I do not regret my purchase. I would definitely recommend this game.

The 10 player co-op missions are some of the most fun I've had in a while, but some people might not/will not experience it. How many more times can i put experience in this. _childDocuments_.review: So let's get the negative out of the way.It's a full priced game.It released with a cosmetic bundle DLC.It has a battle pass.The "pve" mode you can queue up for is still basically a time-attack against another team.Now for the positives:The games free cosmetic options are frankly really good. There's the traditional recolors and then some off the wall stuff like dressing the samurai up as capcom's interpretation of robo-Benkei, a robo burger-kin. Stuff like that.The gameplay is pretty fun. It's pvevp and it scratches an itch and feels the void that was left when they axed Gambit Prime in Destiny 2 (and then soft abandoned gambit altogether afterwards).The story which I had initially written off is rather fun and well realized which is the biggest surprise to me. The presentation could use a bit of work at times but the mystery the game introduces and then slowly works the characters through is intriguing and unpredictable.The mission type is rather varied but I'm mostly looking forward to the 'end-game challenge content' they have prepared for later this month. Altogether the game is rather fun.The performance is pretty good. As is naturally what's expected from a game out of capcom, a toaster could run this game and get good fps.Now for the nitty gritty. The monetization is rather lean. You can't pay for the warchests, you can't pay for battle pass progress, you can't pay for any type of in game currency. The warchests the game gives you for leveling up your player rank seem to pull from all items at a relatively fair rate to the point that I'm more surprised if I don't get a 'legendary' skin.The only thing you can pay for are the few (rather mid) skins and the paid version of the battle pass. All in all. A pretty fun product.

_childDocuments_.review: Exoprimal is a game that is a ton of fun.  It is a PvEvP game where two teams race against each other to the end.  The race has various checkpoints where you have to kill dinosaurs.  For the final round, it can either be PvP or PvE round.  In PvP, there are various different game modes.  PvE final round is a race to the end, and both teams have a possibility of winning these rounds.  There are 10 Exosuits in the game, and they are divided into Assault, Tank, and Support roles.  They are all pretty fun to play and easy to get the basic gist of, but leave room for mastery.  All Exosuits can be modified with Modules, which can alter the way their abilities behave.  Three of them can be equipped at a time.  The game has cross play, where you can play against players from other platforms, however, it does not let you team up with players who are on different platforms.  This means that if you play the Steam version, you can only invite your Steam friends to party up with you.  The game also does not feature cross saves, so you will have to redo all progress if you decide to pick up the game on a different platform.This game has a story, and progressing that story is how the game introduces new dinos for you to fight, as well as new game modes and maps.  This can mean that the game can feel repetitive in the beginning, since the game likes to pair you with people who have made similar progress in the story.  I am sure as the game matures more, this progression can smooth out a bit, so if you are late to the party, you might have a better experience, as more and more people make it farther into the campaign.  As for the campaign, it took me about 26 hours to complete it.  The story was pretty fun, and there are some cool boss fights to look forward to.  (These boss fights take both teams, and have them work together to kill the boss.)Once you beat the campaign, you unlock the ability to play a new game mode, called the Savage Gauntlet, but this game mode is locked, since it won't be available until July 28th.  I will update this review once this content becomes available.Edit:  The game has a season pass, but I am already level 32 out of 50, so it seems to be something that progress pretty quickly.
