_childDocuments_.review: A very rare find indeed. This game has a very intuitive design at it's core, and it's a lot of fun to play. A blend of Rhythm and FPS in a rogue-like game. Akin to the idea of "Crypt of the Necrodancer" This game is fun to play and it's well worth the $20 pricetag to at least give it a shot. There is room for improvement, and we will go over that now. To generalize the game in a quick summary; You fight your way through a handful of levels clearing rooms out. Combat is like a typical fps except you have to do everything to the beat of the music. (Shooting, reloading, dodging) you are free to run around and move at whatever pace you want, but those core things have to be in time with a quarter note of the song. You can get new weapons, new gear (Head/Hand/Arm/Leg) and new abilities throughout your run. It's a good thing that just playing the game is fun because it helps cover up the downfalls... + Tight movement mechanics+ Intuitive design of genre blending action + Soundtrack is awesome (At least at first...)+ Difficulty level is very well done~ More songs... I don't know exactly how many different songs there are, at least 4 although some of them seem very similar.. It was kinda odd when I got to the 4th stage and heard the same song starting from the 1st stage, I think for a game so very based on the music, at least a unique track per level should be a thing..~ Graphics are pretty good at best, I really enjoyed the style at first, but ended up turning all saturation options down to 50% after about 2 hours.~ There's actually a decent amount of content and the levels are varied and unique, but there's always room for more content. I have "beat" the game one time on; easy and it took me about 5 hours. I still feel very intrigued by the gameplay. There's like 5 characters to choose from, and they're not too much different except their starting health/weapon, but they vary enough that I have a favorite. ~ Performance dips very rarely but it does happen. The game has never crashed for me, but playing on ultra some boss attacks cause my fps to dip a noticeable amount ( from 160 down to almost 100 for a couple seconds)  - A lot of critic reviews I've read/watched complain about the use of pre-made assets from their engine's asset store, and a lot of the enemy's are just insects. This didn't particularly bother me when I first starting playing, I still don't really care, but do with this information as you will. Personally, I fan-boy over indie dev teams and give them a lot of slack in this area.- Some of the "Challenge" modes just suck... some of them are great! Others just suck... (I'm looking at you "retro" mode where it just lowers the resolution) Anyways, if the concept even vaguely interests you I bet you'll like the game. Just understand the design is Mechanics first. If you want a super deep roguelike game, or something for mindless gory violence like a doom style, maybe pass because it's neither of those. It's a fun, indie, fps Rhythm game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing!BPM is extremely simple: just kill everyone in the room and go to the next, whatever you do you do on the beat. You have a level and you have a gun. And you have a gorgeous music to follow the beat. That's it. And to my surprise I didn't even need more to enjoy it.Every run randomizes rooms and gear so it always feels different. I tried different Valkyries and different guns so I never felt bored. A few tips for you:1. Every run takes for me 30-40 min (if I manage to finish it that said), so the game is suitable for people who have limited time to play. But even if you didn't manage to finish your run, you can continue from the level you left the game last time. The level will be restarted and regenerated though.2. Don't be afraid to spend coins in shops and banks (unless you are Herfjötur ;) ) as it unlocks some characters and shops will offer more items to you.3. Some rooms can have chests and temples hidden high on the balconies. So especially if you obtained ability to fly you can spend some time exploring each room.4. If you have problems hitting the beat, then you can turn an option that will align your actions to the beat automatically. It can make a game a bit easier, but it'll remove score multiplier.

_childDocuments_.review: Having almost 100% completed this game I feel I can give a review.The GoodRepetitive but fun game play loop. I find myself enjoying the randomness seen through the different rooms, enemies, stats, items and powers I may come across each run. Some runs I breeze through the first few levels to get destroyed down the line and other runs the first boss gains a modifier that makes him stronger or even cloned and I lose immediately or at least struggle through an intense fight. This keeps me constantly on my toes every run. The random rooms is also a key component, I can find the best items for my build and misjudge one room and find myself dead to a swarm of flies. The music beat mechanic never over stays its welcome, I am always reminded of the pure fun that is reloading, shooting and dashing to the games music. It's a fun gimmick albeit one that does feel could have been expanded upon even further such as harder levels having new music that increases or decreases in tempo and as such you must adapt to the increased or decreased amount of bullets you are able to fire and how fast enemies can move/shoot. This feels like a missed opportunity.Different characters are basically the only thing that got me to play this game for as long as I have, the uniqueness is a great extra gimmick to handle such as one character having his health based on coins essentially changing the game into a sonic mode of sorts where managing money is key, instead of buying a great gun I may have to hold off to ensure I have enough health to take a hit or two. Other characters such can come come with hard mode gimmicks such as a constantly draining health that is refilled by doing damage, the game now becomes a speed run in which I cannot take time in shops and in some cases one trip into the wrong room has led to me not having time to get back to the boss room before dying. It's great extra fun, on top of this you have their all unique abilities and super abilities that you unlock by finishing the game in easy and then hard. (One downside was however I started attempting characters on hard straight away as I found the difference between the two not very noticeable so I would finish a character, unlock both their abilities but have no reason to play them anymore other than to attempt a hellish run which offers no achievement for completion so once again, not much reason for it).The BadVisuals are a bit of a mess for me, I could really imagine enjoying this game with a more fleshed out map/enemy design. If you ask me to tell you what the games rooms, enemies and bosses look like I would tell you that off the top of head I can just see orange blurs. The game is bathed in an odd orange mess of highly saturated colours. So bad to the point I really cannot visualise anything other than this mess. The different levels do become apparent with Asgard being orange and the following levels moving through greens to reds and finally a deep dark black and red hell for the final two levels. The last levels are the only ones that I feel match the colour.Bosses are boring. Sad but it is true the bosses for me are easier to kill than the flies in half the rooms. I die more to a random projectile from a fly/bat than I ever have to bosses which all come with very predictable and obvious attacks. The best boss is the first boss and arguably the final one. Why is this? Because usually the first boss you are not that strong yet so you quickly come to respect the mechanics such as dodging to the left and right to avoid a massive attack on one side of the room. Being weak here means I have to take my time and actually dodge and weave through the boss fight. Often by the second/third/fourth boss I end up finding some sort of decent gun/gear that makes the boss a literal bullet sponge that I can clear within 10 seconds. It is so rare that I ever spend longer on these bosses to actually realise what attacks they even have. The last boss is a mix of the same, sometimes it can take me a few minutes and other times 10 seconds all based on how lucky my run has been with guns/gear combinations. On top of that when you do spend any time on these bosses you realise how boring their attacks are, the final boss for example shooting fireballs and an expanding sphere of damage you must pass through when the sphere takes brief pauses in movement. Get that down and the boss is once again just a bullet sponge with little changes even if you pick the hellish difficulty.Ah my least favourite thing. How luck based the game is... So like any other rogue like, you may come across random loot in the form of different armour pieces. A head, Shield, Hand and Boots piece can be worn at the same time. The head pieces can range from gaining explosive shots, damage vamp to the worst such as slight damage when close to enemies (You never want to be close so this is just never worth having). The shield is basically always a search for either the shield that gives double damage or the shield that gives infinite ammo, these two are so essential for an easy win that upon finding one you can almost confirm a run as guaranteed. This is mostly further confirmed by having the right weapon such as the mini gun which makes the game a snooze fest of holding down left click as every enemy in front of you drops dead (the gun is only balanced by its 30 ammo limit and charge up time both of which with infinite ammo you can get rid of). My first ever successful run was with the infinite ammo, mini gun combo and ever since I sometimes force myself not to pair the two just to ensure my run doesn't into a boring mess. Realistically the luck in this game doesn't feel well earned, the use of these amazing items should be to potentially save a dying run, in other words to not give up just because of a bad start when the next room may offer me a double damage shield or new power that gives me healing over time. The issue is that items are so unbalanced that in many instances you can just repeatedly restart the first level until you find the best starting items and secure an easy finish.Finally, my last issue is the game feels way too short. Once I got the game under control I was finishing some runs in 15 minutes. The game boils down to: 2 levels in the first zone, 2 in the next zone, 2 in the zone after and then 1 in the final zone and the last level is just the final boss. If you have ever played a game like Hades or Ultrakill the final boss in this game should realistically be the first major boss of maybe 3-5 more. Or maybe the final boss after being killed should lead to a few more zones. The game feels almost like a play test of sorts when I really begin to think about how basic its rogue like systems are compared to others. I also should mention each level can be cleared in either 1 - 15 minutes. Purely depends how slow you decide to be and how soon you find the boss room as you can fight the boss and move on at any time once found.Ultimately though, I like Bullets Per Minute, it has held my attention for many hours and I have had lots of fun and some moments of major frustration. Completing the game on hard as the character that can only take one hit felt like a major achievement and I cannot really knock this game for what it does. I have plenty of bad points but in comparison to the good the bad feels minor in the long run.I will however suggest to get this game on sale like I did. BPM cost me £3 and to me that's money well spent. For full price I think these minor issues would have felt way more problematic to me.70% out of 100% Orange Juice

_childDocuments_.review: The high notes of BPM are an amazing soundtrack and premise. The art style works to convey an ethereal style, animations are smooth and everything when everything clicks it's terrific. Unfortunately the game is marred by excessive RNG. You basically either learn to take on things with the starter pistol, or you find another game.For folks that enjoy 'getting gud' this is a must have, even at full price. For casuals like myself... wait for a sale, or pass it by.

_childDocuments_.review: : Those who enjoy rhythm games, shooters, and rogue-like elements.: Those who are turned off by rogue-like elements, dislike rock music, or find rhythm-based game play unenjoyable.Bullets Per Minute is truly unique in the way it simultaneously blends a first person shooter and a rhythm game together into one cohesive experience. At it's heart, BPM is a rogue-like, meaning that each new run will have randomized level layouts, upgrades, and rewards. As such, you are at the mercy of the RNG, meaning some runs will be met with a quick demise, while others will leave you exceptionally overpowered. There is a balance issue at times, but the fast paced game play propels you from bad to good run quickly enough to make it forgivable. Obviously, the real banger on display here is the game play highlight of BPM: Shooting in tune with the beat. All guns fire and are reloaded to the beat, which as you can imagine, has a very steep learning curve. When the screen is filled with a chaotic orgy of enemies and projectiles, keeping track of when to precisely pull the trigger can be maddening. When it clicks, it feels incredible, but until that moment, it feels punishingly unfair. Graphically, BPM is quite an ugly game to look at. The screen is over saturated with a dismal yellowish filter that causes enemies (and projectiles) to be difficult to spot. Fortunately, each level has an adjustable saturation slider which can be tweaked to your personal liking. Enemies themselves, with the exception of bosses, are also painfully generic, consisting of a small variety of bats, spiders, worms, and soldiers.It's clear that BPM was designed with it's rhythmic component first and world building a distant second. If you can look past the obnoxious screen filters and generic enemy types, there is an extremely addicting, rewarding, and head-banging hell of a time to be had.

The screenshots will give you enough to go off of in that regard.Like other roguelites, it's a lot of fun going through (dying repeatedly) and unlocking shop upgrades and new characters. Lemme tell you the first time you get The Best Defense (infinite ammo+no reload) while you've got the minigun will change your life.There's not a tremendous amount of enemy variety, but that's because most - if not all - the enemy and shopkeep designs are from Paragon (a defunct MOBA), since Epic released all its assets free to use. My friends who were lovers of that game enjoyed watching me play this game and identifying all the characters and jungle monsters from it lolIn short, game is good and game is fun. It's nothing extraordinary but it's something I can see myself sinking a good 30+ hours into. Watch a video or two and you'll probably have a good idea of whether or not you'll enjoy the game

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: BPM has some of the most exhilarating gunplay and cool style in the entire roguelike genre, but I think that it could've used some more time in the oven. 8.5/10First off, I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ adore this game. The Norse Mythology backdrop, the metal soundtrack, the incredibly fun guns, it tickles the roguelike bone in a way very few other games have in a long time. However, once you beat the game on hard with a few different characters, you've basically got the full experience.Think of it this way. BPM is a gourmet chef who makes the best ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steak you've ever had. So you go there, and you eat it - 10/10. You have 176 BPM, 4/4 time, and just enough auto-aim to make the process of aiming and timing to the beat at the same time bearable, but not difficult. You go there again. 10/10. It's even better the second time, now that you're good at it. You go a third time, maybe with a different character, 10/10 again. But eventually you want something else. All the music in the game has the same BPM and same time signature, maybe it's time to try something else?But that's all BPM has to offer. It's an 11/10 game. It's 20 hours that is by far worth your time and money. But if you're coming by expecting the traditional roguelike feel of "I want to do this over and over and over again for hundreds - maybe thousands of hours" then you should look elsewhere.I feel like the game was designed to use different BPM and time signatures, but time and budget constraints forced it into all being the same. There are weapons that subdivide oddly, fun proof of concept items that mess with the way the beat counter works etc. but the full picture isn't there.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a lot, and I do recommend it. However, it's a little saddening to talk about this game at length because I know that my favorite game of all time is somewhere buried within BPM, but what's actually here is just an ok experience. The game occasionally feels completely incredible, with the music and gameplay and having-just-learned-a-gun's-bar-defying-shot-pattern all coming together, but it's weighed down by most of the rest of what's going on.I'm a lot more of a rhythm game guy than a shooter guy, so I'm coming from the opposite angle as I imagine most people are, but for either camp there seems to be a decently sized initial wall to get over to really get into the game. After that, though, it gets a lot more enjoyable.I think roguelikes are generally overdone, and if you're going to be one you ought to bring something new to the table. BPM does nort As far as greater dungeon organization, this game doesn't really do anything a BoI player doesn't already understand. It adds some things, like shrines to improve base stats (that are miserable to find), and adds limited slots for weapons/items, but there's a shop and item room on every floor (the latter requiring a key), a square grid of independent rooms that drop items on completion, key beggars, etc. (Room rewards are actually based on how well you performed in a room [i.e. not breaking the beat or getting hit]. This is cool but not very well telegraphed to the player.)The item system is theoretically interesting but pretty underwhelming overall. You have four slots for items, head/sheild/arm/boots, and each item can only exist in one of these slots. Many items are not terribly interesting (speed up, damage up, etc.), and they're not balanced at all. It makes total sense for a roguelike to have unbalanced items, but how well a run is going depends near-entirely on getting some of the literal or effective damage doubler items. I've have runs where I 4-shot the final boss, and runs where the fight just drags on. There are occasional interesting trade-offs to make but non-specific item descriptions make the decision more of a guess or whim than an actual thought-out choice. (There's also abilities that I literally forgot about until right now because they're hardly ever given the chance to be interesting.)The guns are cool but having to save up for an armory to maybe buy a better one is really not terribly fun. I feel this is another issue with the roguelike system, learning new guns' shot and reload patterns is one of the game's strong points, but you start new runs with the same weapons every time, and once you find a decent gun there's not a ton of incentive to change it.One thing I'd like to mention because it either isn't brought up in game or I just missed it, is that there's a lot of attacks that seem completely unfair until you realize that they're telegraphed on the beat indicator in the middle of the screen. I found myself tuning the GUI out completely because you don't really ever use it, except for for one specific enemy and parts of some boss fights, so I had to relearn to pay attention to it whenever there might be a led projectile or wall of damage incoming.There's also just some final polish missing in a lot of places. Hit-register on shield enemies is funny with some weapons. Items aren't always well explained, so it's definitely a tab-to-wiki-to-figure-out-what-this-thing-even-does type game at times, and sometimes it doesn't seem like the wiki even knows either.Art style is contentious. I like it overall, but there are definitely times where incoming projectiles are impossible to make out from windows or other enemies or your own projectiles. Shrines are essential, appear nearly every room, and are really annoying to find because everything is the same color and brightness.Progression is really weird, it mostly happens to line up so that you'll have unlocked most of the game once you've gotten a hang of the mechanics, but I've beaten the game on hard with most characters and I still don't have all of the armory or the bank unlocked, and either way it feels pretty cheap to only sell you a couple items a floor at the beginning and make you unlock a shop that actually sells a reasonable amount of items over time.This review ended up being more negative than I meant it it, I promise there's a incredible core gameplay loop in there, it's just dragging a ton of small issues behind it. I probably have more thoughts--this review is already much longer than I intended because I kept thinking of new things to say--but it boils down to what could be an incredible game just ending up as a fine game. I paid full price and it was definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a roguelike I think the game loop lacks balance, it feels like if you get in the deeper levels it's because you were lucky to find OP items and it's not really rewarding you based on your decision making, but perhaps your shooting on timing skills and aiming skills will get you through the levels, I personally didn't get much enjoyment from grinding because your choices on items don't really seem to be rewarded nor structured nor balanced, the items you get are very random and totally dependent on rng.The music is nice but can get repetitive.Sound design is nice too, though one issue is that the character you're controlling will make some noises as you jump or strafe which can be mistaken as taking damage.Sometimes you'll enter the room and a small enemy will spawn to your right or left outside of your field of view and you'll take damage instantly.The enemies design isn't anything fancy, they're kinda basic in their movements and behaviour and you can avoid their attacks by strafing and running around in circles.The graphics: there's an annoying over-saturated red/orange filter, which you can tone down if you go into the settings but it just seems like a poor stylistic choice choice that reduces readability(it's hard to distinguish enemies over the scenery at times).There's an easy mode and an option to even disable having to shoot on timing, yet the easy mode still remains fairly hard, so you can't even have it easy if you just want to have fun.Other than that it's good, I am sure many people will enjoy the game if they don't mind the grinding and what in my opinion is too random and not very rewarding design.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this a "mixed" review I would. This game is fun, but I don't feel its worth the price. To start with the positives, the shooting feels fantastic. Shooting, reloading, dashing and dodging to the beat feels so satisfying. All the weapons and varied and fun to use, and the randomized level design works great. The issues start to creep up after your'e a few runs in and you realize that there is a very limited amount of content here. For a rouguelike there is a very small item pool, and I started to get repeats after only one run through the game. The item pool is so small that you will often have very similar if not an identical build run to run. And not only are the items limited, they are all very strong. That doesn't sound so bad on the surface but once a build gets going on the second stage or so the rest of the run becomes a total breeze. You start one shotting almost every enemy in the game and killing the bosses before they even get a chance to hit you. It completely trivializes the combat once you get this powerful. The last thing I have to touch on are the visuals. On first look they are serviceable, but the more you play you realize that there is this awful filter over everything and it honestly is just downright ugly. I understand that this is a small team with limited resources but that doesn't change the fact that looking at the game is unpleasant. The filter is actually a detriment sometimes. Because it makes everything the same color, its easy to miss important items in the world because it all blends together.All in all this game is a good time, but its too shallow to keep me interested for longer than a few hours. If it goes on sale in the future I might get it to play a run every now and then because the rhythm shooting is genuinely genius and very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for November 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before December 7th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Rocking out to the sounds of your bullets. Don’t adjust your speakers, I am playing music for this title. You see, BPM is an interesting concept.  Your actions need to be done on the beat.  Shooting, dashing, and jumping are all done at the rhythm of the music, and this music rocks.  I couldn’t help but jam out and man it sounds so good when you’re in the flow.  If you play this game rhythmically you’re going to have some awesome tunes. The action is hot, the game very challenging, and all I wanted to do is play another round.  There’s also a lot of difficulty levels, different characters, and assist modes including one that takes out the rhythm aspect of your actions.  While you shouldn’t use it because it’s not the real game and because of how it works it feels like it induces lag, it’s available if you need it. _childDocuments_.review: This game rocks. I'm a long-time FPS enthusiast and this might be the best that first-person shooting has ever felt.Those who aren't retired semi-professional musicians/percussionists might have a different experience than I have had. Some of them may have written reviews that boil down to complaining about how bad they are at this game. Never fear: if you have good rhythm and good aim, there are few games that can compete with this one for sheer mechanical joy.This games make *reloading* feel cool. Reloading, of all things! Weaving it in to a stylish off-the-cuff headshot dance that fells enemies as it syncopates a percussive riff produces prodigious pleasure.I recommend setting Rhythm Detection to Strict but starting each character off with a successful "Easy" run before advancing that character to Hard, as doing so unlocks the character's starting Spell which can help their playstyle come together.For example, the first and third characters both start with short-range weapons but their starting spell can be used against distant foes.Anyway, BPM is my favorite FPS. I have been playing this genre since Quake III Arena and O.G. Counter-Strike, to give you some idea of the implications of that statement.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Art style ruined a great game.And I am not talking about "Ugly", that's barely a reason to give a bad review.The issue is that the terrible design decision of making everything a single color is that there is no contrast between things. It's VERY HARD to see and identify enemies most of the time when a microsecond can decide if you take a hit or not. Not properly identifying a shield guy in a pack of enemies can easily kill any run.The saturation options are a passive aggressive deflection that does not solve the issue. The issue is not which or how strong the color is, is that there is only one. If anything, it shows that the devs do not care. There is also the irregular illumination of rooms, straining the player eyes is not good game design. I would need to constantly pause the game -> go into settings -> change gamma every new room. This is not fun.In the efforts of standing out from the crowd, this great game became barely playable. I like having fun, but not at the cost of my eye health.I would play more if I could remove ALL camera post processing and have a more normalized room lighting. Do note that this is very different from the "Dark" modifier on some levels, you get a flashlight on those. Some rooms are actually easier to see with the Dark modifier than the normal one.

_childDocuments_.review: BPM: Bullets Per Minute is a rhythm shooter. You shoot to the rhythm, dash to the rhythm, enemies also shoot to the rhythm. Sounds good in theory, and it’s fun. You can still jump without rhythm and that saves you in many situations. You can also run without rhythm. Is it a rhythm game though?There is a small catch. Enemies positioned at different distances shoot projectile weapons that do not synchronize when they reach you. Meaning, you cannot evade as in rhythm game and have to rely on jumps and speed. And oh boy they are effective. Apart from only several attacks that damage part of screen, all the projectiles can be ignored if flying around the arena in circles. Given that the only choice left is to dash, there is no downside to not shooing on every beat with reloads when enemies are not in the view. That can be automated so your hand does not hurt after some time. Partly it’s implemented with autoaim already.Maybe because I spent so much time on first levels, I remember music from there way better than the last tracks. Music is generally very good, but stays the same throughout every run, and by the end blurs into background.Something’s not quite right.. Let me start again.BPM: Building Private Modification is a roguelike game. The formula was copied over and changed so that the teacher would not notice resulting in questionable decisions.Apart from skills, there are only six slots available for items, and once you got strong items in several of them there is not much need to explore more, and I ended most my runs with more coins than I knew what to spend them on. There are tens of weapons with endless ammo, and weapons don’t repeat once you see them. But they play similarly to each other, it was mostly finding one with big range that hitscans enemies. Revolver reload animation is painful to see. I finished the game not even trying out half of them properly, returning to the previous one too often. There was just no need to fix what’s working already.Key management is a disaster. Given the random pool of items each chest contains it’s not reasonable not to use them on the first one. Each boss drops one key, otherwise they are too scarce from the start. You have to invest in you luck to start seeing them and there are way more locked chests than keys. But at some point you’ll get infinite keys item, but won’t need any more items.Worst of all, items do not synergize with each other. Some are strong, multiplying your power or removing need to reload, but it’s independent stats mostly. At least they are more than enough to get OP.Still not enough.. Let’s try again?BPM: Buying Potion Materials is a hidden object game. Every room has some sort of upgrade and each time the room is cleared, you’ll have to squint your eyes to find it. You have probably noticed from screenshots that there is too much saturation and red there. Don’t worry, it’s by design. After all, you have to feel the rhythm, not see it. It’s also hard to see why some design choices were implemented, but it’s all hidden behind the layer of red paint. It could be way cooler to see normal rooms and paint them red with enemies, but we have what we have.This will never end. How many more are there?BPM: Bounce Per Meter is a platformer game. Not only you’ll have to jump over lava and waves of enemy attacks, but rooms also contain secret areas. Most of them you cannot reach without flying, so a single upgrade is needed for most. Menu loading screen tip announces that you have to give up on some upgrades. You could also launch yourself there with a powerful weapon, but by the time you have that weapon or flight ability you don’t need any more secrets and it wastes your time. As heartbreaking as that looks there still are ledges and small platforms so skilled players can invest time to get up there. Only to find emptiness, or a chest that requires key to open while not having one.But it’s not platformer entirely. So what is it?BPM: Being Positively Murderous is dungeon crawler. The best option to have an OP character is to crawl first dungeon. And that’s it, no more dungeons after that. First levels are treated differently, have a distinct feel to them. Hits are more fatal, luck plays bigger role, each key matters.Luck aside, it is a challenging game. Two of its characters die from a single hit. Others play mostly the same, although getting more and more distinct towards the end. The time cranking the difficulty up could have been spent on making some things work together, but it was not.First enemies you see are slugs and flies. Most of my deaths were on first level due to them. I think that almost all of my deaths were on first level. If you get through, you have won. Players who hated Primal Aspids from Hollow Knight would find themselves at home. Almost every room has several of those flying around. Don’t forget to look down though, there is a slug there that will end your run. Because all the enemies inflict same amount of damage, it’s not the bosses that scare me, or regular enemies. It’s those flying abominations, hiding behind others or walls, shooting at me from any range. That’s why range is most important upgrade.Challenge room of level one is one of the hardest challenges to complete and most of the time gives no reward. First floors are generally way harder than the latter ones. Sure, there are more enemies there and their attacks are harder, but you are also stronger and in a good run it does not matter that much. Unless they are using shields that require you to dash, it all sticks to one formula – circle strafe and shoot. It does not matter what’s inside. Works on almost all bosses too.Challenges of the game are special sort of pain. Some of them not being challenging at all, just removing the beat from the equation. One is a parody of SuperHot, where the movement is also bound to rhythm. Played almost the same but made me sick after a while. How about a challenge that requires you to jump all the time and hover over every item. Flying is overpowered and you’ll win, but your hands will hurt a lot. Icing on the cake is a retro mode. It’s not just pixels though, you can’t see anything going on in the room, sometimes figuring out enemies by their shapes, other times not. Did I mention everything is already trying to hurt your eyes with monochrome colors? Doom’s colorful pickups might not fit the tone, but they fit the game. In this mode, you shoot a mass of foes in the middle hoping they will be over soon. Feeling pain is not a challenge.Boss rush was a good addition. Why, you ask, I haven’t mentioned bosses that much? Because I haven’t interacted with them much. Apart from the first one that has meaningful attacks that need to be avoided to the beat, others do not use that mechanic much. What’s worse, if you get to them you are overpowered so much that they don’t have time to attack. So seeing what they do and taking them out with base weapon and stats was a nice… challenge.BPM: Baking Partial Mess is a visual novel game. Except you remove all the dialogue and story out of it. You see, with all the genres mixed in, the story got late to the party so the others had to leave without it. There is not even the slightest mention of it, not even in item descriptions. “Free game asset factory got blown up and you are here to fix it” - Here, there is a better story in this review that in the game. That would explain all the enemies I had to kill, bats being the worst. The names of the characters are hard to read but reference Nordic myths. They seem to be wearing fur coats but walking through lava levels. First they face slugs, then rats. Except there are also mechanized robots thrown in there sometimes. And a lot of samurai warriors. With squids? Grim reaper being the first boss. Also, giant trees hate you. By the end of all this zoo I expected a dinosaur to show up as last boss cause why not. How do I say this without spoilers...

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't unlocked all the characters or properly finished the downstairs route, but I did BEAT the game a couple of times, so here's what I can really say about it so far:     The art-style hasn't really bothered me, or hindered the game-play to me in any actual way, the music that IS there SLAPS, and the actual game-play itself is so damn fun and super addicting. A doom-styled FPS with the addition of it being a Roguelike  a rhythm game? That presses so many of my buttons I can't help but be a little biased. There's been countless moments where I find myself sacrificing getting optimal game-play for satisfaction when I reload to the beat a lot, even if there's a lot of enemies left gun still full of bullets.  from said reloading, to particle effects, to shooting sound effects -- the game delves so much deeper into it's sound design by making little things like the  and that's not even mentioning the spliced noises that enemies make too. So many little touches like that add  and detail into this that really justifies the price I paid for it.     As for difficulty, again, something I need to get more into since I've really only done normal and hard, but it's definitely what you'd expect for a rogue-like - remember enemy patterns and so and such. There's also challenges you get through the game, one of them straight up being a "doom" mode with pixelated graphics and a centered gun, and another one being (i think?) a super-hot reference of sorts. It's cute. The game WILL kick your ass though, and there are some enemies I had to look up to understand like the Reaper.     For negatives, I was looking through the reviews, and I get some of the complaints, the game is  The style is very exaggerated, and the gameplay can be really hard for those that struggle with rhythm. Honestly, I do wish there was more music, or at least the option to mod custom music in. As good as the music is, I know that most people will get sick of it eventually. There are SOME solutions in the game, though, like obviously an easy mode, and I believe a setting to town down the redness or coloring in levels, but the issues are still a bit more complicated than that.     For what I think, though, the thing that really comes up most is just that it lacks  What's in the game is amazing, it's an incredible, fresh experience with a new take on FPS gameplay and I love it, but I wish there was  to it. Like I mentioned earlier, more music, more levels, more variety, there's lots of items, but it doesn't hurt to add more. This game has an unbelievably huge amount of potential to be AMAZING. I know it's a bit of an unfair comparison, because of how long it's been supported and it being 2d instead of 3d, but The Binding of Isaac is so great  it has so much variety and different ways to play. Youtubers have been playing that game from when it released to TODAY. With that being said, I'm not pitting this as an actual negative against Awe Interactive at all. I would love to see more of this game, and that's all it boils down to. I love this game to death and I'm excited to keep tabs with what they do in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I managed to finish the game once on easy difficulty I feel like commenting on it. It's really fun. I'm not any good in reflex test games when the ques are visual, but here the ques are auditive and delivered in a form of beat heavy rock/metal soundtrack. It's quite easy to stay on rythm after a bit of learning how each of the weapons and abilities work. How you do on a run is heavily influenced by RNG, not unlike all other roguelike games. On my currently sole playthrough I found the fireball launcher in the first room and it was smooth sailing since.There's one sore point currently. Even though the visual representation, while fitting the game perfectly, is from more than ten years ago it feels seriously unoptimised in the later levels. First two levels run really well and smoothly with the occassional dip when entering a new room, but later levels with a lot of caster type enemies with light effects for their attacks the game runs around 3 spf (yes, seconds per frame) for a while before stabilising. I have a AMD FX-8350 8-core, 16 gigs of RAM and a Radeon RX 580 and I run the game on Proton on Linux Mint 20. Not a super powerful gaming rig by modern standards, but runs many games with better graphics without similar framerate dips. Maybe the lighting effects in the later levels could do with some optimisation TLC?

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions:I have since finished the game multiple timesTL;DR:BPM manages to blend First Person Shooting with Rhythm game mechanics like no other game before it, at least none that I know of.Killing monsters in accordance to the beat is just so damn satisfying.There are a ton of weapons, upgrades and items that make sure every run turns out different from the previous one.In addition there are random modifiers that can occur on any given floor further varying things up.We're talking low gravity, an Icy floor that lets you slide all over the place, everything being upside down, yada, yada, yada.The gunplay feels nice and meaty, and the platforming also becomes more relevant the further in you get.So it feels great, there is a ton of replay value, it varies things up - and the icing on the cake is, that every Song in this game is a banger!The only "negativ" aspects in my opinion are, that it's graphically a little outdated and oversaturated in some parts (especially in lava levels).Also, the optional challenges are fun, but for example it would be great if boss rush could be done with anything else than the very basic weapon, or if it could at least be upgraded throughout.But overall BPM is an amazing Rougelite, mixing Rhythm-Game and FPS in a wonderful way, that can keep you engaged for hours on end.I know I'll be putting some runs in every few days, for quite a time to come!Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: The Negative first:Very lacking in items and weapons, this is very strange for a rogue-like game where there are usually hundreds if not thousands of items to discover and change the gameplay. However considering that the first patch that launched 10 minutes ago had a new weapon I hope they have more content planned for the future.Positive:Amazing soundtrack, the smoothness of playing BPM is so satisfying it's crazy. I feel they really nailed the "awesome" part of the game. I love rythm games and the mix between rythm and FPS seems to work very well. Really cool artstyle, however sometimes hard to see monsters with the same color as the background. Difficulty seems balanced, easy was easy once you understand the concept and learn the controlls.Summary: I recommend this game because it's a really fun experience, the only negative is the lack of content which I hope will come with content patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this after watching gwar gura play it on youtube and I'm glad I did.  It's a rhythm-based first-person-shooter roguelike.  The core concept of this game is innovative and new, but somehow also intuitive and easy to pick up in the first couple minutes.  It's a rhythm shooter, and you need to time all your shots and abilities to the beat of the metal soundtrack.  This mechanic is married with a roguelike game that makes for fun 30-60 minute dungeon raids.  You get four equipment slots and 2 ability slots, so there's a good amount of variety between raids - your final build can vary greatly, and part of the challenge is figuring out how to best exploit the equipment/abilities you find.  The graphics are on the simple side, but there's a consistent style throughout and it works well.  I'm looking forward to future releases from Awe Interactive. Seriously, this game is a gem.  Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Between a mix of Doom and a Rhythm Game, BPM: Bullets Per Minute is a fairly challenging and addicting experience for those looking to rip and tear with a twist. In addition to the several procedurally generated stages, there are four unlockable characters, a variety of guns to shred with, as well as challenge modes to add new gameplay.Highly addicting and I strongly recommend for fans of rhythm games and shooters alike.Edit: PLAY WITH HEADPHONES.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the game needs a tutorial, just a quick one to explain how the shooting/dodging aligns with the arrows. I spent an hour shooting at the rate of half bpm, instead of full bpm, which made the game way harder than it needed to be. This could be due to my incapability to learn, but I saw no indicator that the small arrows also counted towards your rate of fire, especially because your dashing doesn't count towards the small arrows. The game does a good job at giving you a flexible amount of options, upgrades, and guns to cater towards your playstyle. The upgrades actually change up quite a lot, and main upgrades are limited by your shield, head, foot, or arm slots. So you can only have a max of 4 main upgrades, but you can upgrade each of your stats along the way. This adds in the difficulty of learning what items are better than others, or which fit the current playthrough. Just like other rogue-likes you will find yourself dying over and over slowly learning items, bosses, enemy types etc. While it gets easier as you improve, it still remains a good challenge every run. I do find that the whole rhythm aspect of the game feels like a gimmick rather than a feature. It doesn't take long to learn the rate of fire, or the dashing intervals, or the reloading speed. The rate for each aspect of gameplay doesn't change, whether the music slows down, or you enter a different level. Maybe later on, but as of the first 3-4 levels, it is the same, despite changing the the enemy types and look of the level, aswell as the music, you will not be experiencing different gameplay. I think that the music aligning with your actions is very satisfying at the very least, and it enhances the feeling of the game compared to other FPS games. You can't spam, and that is the beauty, but I often find myself treating the game like any other FPS game after the patterns align, and without the BPM changing, once this is down, it is just the same as any other rogue-like FPS. So the question is whether the game holds up compared to other games? I think it does. I personally prefer games like Gunfire Reborn, that has much more going on with weapons, stats, upgrades etc. As well as having more interesting bosses. Despite this, compared to a game like Immortal Redneck, it definitely holds a candle. While not being focused on platforming like Immortal Redneck, I think the pacing and enjoyment I gain from this game is much higher.While I recommend this game, don't expect it to be more than 5-20 hours of fun, unlike games like Gunfire Reborn or The Binding of Isaac. I think if they added more items, and the ability to equip more than 4 main items, it would probably have the time sink that other rogue-likes have, but after you beat the game, you'll probably find that you've experienced everything this game has to offer, and found a meta build that trumps any other items you can pick up. Before I close, I want to address the artstyle. I usually find that I appreciate games trying new artstyles, and as an artist myself, I enjoy seeing what they can do with an unorthodox style. The oversaturated graphics do not work for me. At first I overlooked it, but especially in certain situations, it makes things blend it with each other. Some bosses have variants, where they gain shields, and the shield actually covers the bosses hitbox. It makes the game unnecessarily harder, and usually things that would be easily found in other games, blend in heavily with the world around you. I hope they make a sequel with a better overall look, as well as more guns, items, and the ability to equip more items, and actually change up how gun pacing works dramatically between time signatures. If they don't plan on a sequel I hope they take the time to really beef up this game. As of now, if you enjoy rogue-like FPS games, I'd give it a go, but if you were going to buy this game just for the gimmick, than I would avoid it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Unique and cool premise and solid foundation as it stands, still room for a bit of balancing and tweaking, but the enjoyment and strength of this game comes from the combination of the rhythm and FPS genres, which in itself is an amazing experience.This game is an absolute banger -- if you are a fan of Doom or retro FPS, Rogue-like, and especially rhythm games, you will have a blast playing this. It's all about staying to the beat or off-beat, and the satisfaction of completing a room along with staying flawlessly in rhythm is something to behold. They time different parts of typical gun animations as well, such as pumping a shotgun or even reloading, adding to the overall "tightness" of the game. The premise of this game makes it worth it in itself, but I've also enjoyed discovering all the different guns, items and power-ups as well. Not to mention the music is really good! The shop tune bops, glad the OST is on streaming!I do have a few critiques though, and I'll preface those with the fact that I think as it stands, this game already has such a solid foundation that I think these types of things could easily be addressed in future updates if the devs so wished.The first one is pretty subjective, but I was a bit surprised at the art style at first, the over-saturated walls and floors in the first zone were a bit much but it grew on me, plus I was so focused on the game-play that it didn't matter much. The second is also somewhat aesthetic related, but I found the placement and size of the stat powerup / chest / sacrifice / etc entities (you get one in almost every room except one of those mini-boss rooms and the starting room I believe) -- they take up like 1 or 2 units of ground space and sometimes it's a bit of a pain to find them, and because they have such a small visual presence in each room I find it hard to remember which rooms had which upgrades when going back to spend gold -- imo it would be nice to make them take up just a bit more space, or at least more-so visually. Lastly, I will say that I think this game does need a bit of balancing with the items; I'm still quite new to the game and have only completed 1 run and made it to Hellheim on another, but both times I was like *stupid* OP, snowballing hard after getting a few items,  (  ) but maybe that's how Rogue-like game tend to be -- I will say that I still felt incredibly satisfied with completing my first full run either way, and these types of things can easily be balanced out in future updates if needed.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 - Phenomenal game! Regardless of your musical capabilities, BPM is worth your time and money. It firmly delivers on its face-value expectations and experience considering this was a dev team of two people. Challenging and addictive, entertaining and rewarding, this title brings a fresh experience to both the FPS and Rhythm genres.The game is locked in a tempo of around 88bpm (beats per minute, in this case) or 176bpm counting in double time; that's roughly the tempo of "Beverly Hills" by Weezer or "Bulls On Parade" by Rage Against the Machine. There are no options to increase or decrease tempo, but there is a setting for the rhythm requirement if you are struggling to keep the beat.Small difficulty tunings are needed for bosses (general rooms are more difficult than actual bosses are throughout the entire game), as well as some minor graphical issues (screen flashing, dash animation is stuck in place and doesn't move with FOV setting changes); despite BPM's small hiccups, the game is absolutely worth picking up for the price.Personally speaking, I would be willing to participate in crowd-funding for future content of BPM. Some suggestions:- additional tracks, levels, characters, items- tempo adjustment options (preferably slightly faster options for difficulty)

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by saying that I have terrible rhythm, and as such I never was any good at rhythm games.I love this game. I don't know what it is about shooting my gun and reloading instead of jumping or tapping a certain button, but I'm oddly skilled at BPM. My friend and I got it at the same time, and I managed to beat the game several times before he managed to, when he's normally the one who's better at games than I am. The concept of a rhythm-based first person shooter is so unique, coupled by the excellent rogue-like elements and unique visuals. Some people dislike or hate the visuals, but personally, I don't mind them one bit. The enemies attacking on beat and the items being unique and supportive of different playstyles is amazing as well. Personally, I tend to avoid items that reduce damage or deal a retaliatory strike upon taking damage, as good movement is a good and fun skill to learn. Small little things, like jumping while going down stairs giving you a horizontal boost of momentum, and jumping while going up them giving you a vertical one, really help give the movement a little added flair without it being complex and based around it.All in all, this game is really good, and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Full text below, but also feel free to check out my video review:Bullets Per Minute (BPM) is a roguelike, rhythm base, first person shooter. Here your bullets, reloads, and dodges must all be within the beat of the soundtrack in order. Here you play one of a handful of angels that battles their way through the depths of the underworld killing demons and creatures along the way.The game is broken up into several levels, each with a demon boss. They are randomly generated and contain multiple special rooms containing treasure, stores, and challenges that will be beneficial along the way. Each normal room however, is filled with enemies and you are locked into each room when entering until you have defeated all the enemies. Once you do kill all enemies a treasure box will appear somewhere in the room and you will be given a key, coins, or health to aid with your journey. Some rooms also include statues that you can choose to drop a coin on as offering to receive a stat bonus. This is the primary mechanism for upgrading your damage, range, precision, etc. Here you’re able to pull a handle and fight rounds of enemies that are slightly stronger that the level you’re currently on. The rewards are unclear, but I received typical room treasure The blacksmith rooms contain one to many weapons that you can choose to purchase. You’re only able to hold one weapon at a time, but as long as you stay in the level you purchased a weapon, you can always go back to pick up the weapon you exchanged. The game features several different weapons the differ in power, reload actions necessary, clip sizes, and shot vacinities. Store rooms can be used to purchase health, health capacity upgrades, and other equipment (of which you have 4 slots head, chest, arms, and legs). All the armor pieces have different misc. abilities with some preferable to others. Like the weapons, the gear you exchange for when purchasing new gear will remain in the level until you leave to go on to the next level. Here you can pick up new abilities. These need to be charged but have varying different impacts to the game. Some are not even related to combat. You’ll need to experience each to determine what they do and how best to use them. Here you will fight the boss of the level. Once defeated, you can go back and finish any tasks left undo or to grab any gear left behind. Enter the portal when your done to proceed to the next level.Both the levels and bosses have modifiers that appear to be random. For instance I have experienceD levels that when I killed enemies they left skulls behind on the floor. Touching these skulls creates an explosion that will damage nearby enemies, but not harm you. I have also seen a level be covered in spider webs. I don’t know the depth to these modifiers, but it is clear that some of them are more significant than others.The rhythm based gunplay not only works, but it hits the whole thing out of the park. It feels smooth and empowering while being a blast take part in the sound track as you run through each level decimating enemies. Each gun feels unique and the weapons feel pretty balanced overall. Some guns can be fired down to the quarter and eight notes if timed correctly which allows lots of creativity.For a rhythm based game the music is no doubt important and here BPM once again reigns supreme. The metal ballads here fit the aesthetic of the game perfectly and not only meet the tone of the game, but serve to further empower the player. You honestly feel like the final instrument of the band saying “Bass? No sir, I’ll be playing the shotgun, thanks.” It should be noted that a number of other reviewers have contrasted my taste for the soundtrack. I do have an affinity for rock/metal so that may be helping the music along.Bosses are well designed. Each has patterns that are harsh on first encounter, but have practicing a number of times they are found to be very fair and players can no doubt over come them. The modifiers (mentioned above) keep the bosses relatively variable and spicey. It’s a nice change of pace to keep the player on their toes, though sometimes they may feel a little unfair (they’re fair though). It should be noted that later bosses in the game may feel easy due to some unbalancing in the game, more on that below.The items are also varied in a way to make each run quite different. You never know what you’ll end up with and you’ll need to get familiar with each weapon to know what suits your play style and what works best.It’s important to note that what this game gets right it gets REALLY right. The flip side however, is that there are a number of elements that remain unbalanced and need a tune up to make this a game that will be long remembered.The graphics here are all built on solid models, but the coloring is extremely bland. The default palette is over saturated and far too red/orange. While levels further down the road do vary a little, the situation does not get much better. The developers have added the ability to desaturate and decolor the game, which helps a bit, but is not an optimal solution. I found that taking the game to black and white in the options leaves a number of items like coins etc still colored and has a really cool effect overall. I was able to live with this, but I’d like to see a new coat of paint.The game overall is also fairly unbalanced. In the first level I found that almost all the enemies were almost no threat. The exception is the bats that are small targets, can move quickly, and can shoot fireballs from across the room. The player at this level doesn’t have the range to reach them and will need to approach quite close to make contact making them very dangerous. They also hit for 25% of the default health pool. This small issue is representative for the game overall.Another example was my personal experience and success in the game. My first two runs were very successful, reaching levels 3 and 4. At that point I didn’t even fully comprehend how mechanics worked. After that first half hour I didn’t get outside the second level for over 2 hours due to bad drops and poor item availability. Run after run the rooms would reward me with almost exclusively locked chests and no keys, which means I get nothing. This felt like I was getting better at the game but getting worse outcomes. The following day I decided to try again and had the luck of the Irish on my side. Levels 1 and 2 were generous with keys and coins allowing me to buy everything I saw. I shredded demons at breakneck speed and my third run culminated in me becoming so powerful that I coasted through the game killing bosses in seconds. My first experience with many of these bosses was poor because I just instantly killed them and moved on without seeing their intricate patterns that needed to be learned. This huge range of luck needs to be narrowed down to make the game a little more of a unified experience. Skill should feel like it’s more important. The game is both too hard and too easy.Finally I found a number of instances in the game where there needed to be more guidance to the player. This is definitely a game where there should be no tutorial and no handholding. However there are a number of mechanics that require further indicators on how they function. For instance there are plates in the game that reward the player after placing coins/key on them. How many? You can’t tell. You also can’t tel

_childDocuments_.review: So I don't really know what to say about BPM. It's a bit out of my wheel house. It's a roguelite/like (I dunno what the term is), I usually aren't too fond of those, though I am fond of this! It's also a rhythm game, and I suck at those. Though I've seen myself steadily improve at this. I should also point out there's accessibility options, so if you struggle to get the beat or just can't pick it up there are options to help with that and I would not hesitate to use them if it makes you enjoy them more. The elitist mindset of "hurr u make gaem easy u bad" is a nasty one, and you shouldn't stop yourself from enjoying your experience.With that out the way, it is very much your standard feeling roguelite structure. Similar to binding of isaac, somewhat. Square rooms, leading into different rooms, one chest per floor that gives an item (usually locked), occasionally other things like a shop or weapon shop, etc. Unlike binding of isaac, this game is actually pretty good, but I digress.So you start off with a fairly standard character. A lassie with 4 hits till death, a fairly run of the mill pistol which sucks but is easy to use. You unlock more as you progress, with the hardest character to play being unlocked after you beat the game on Hard. The rest are unlockedd by just getting through specific stages, I don't think you actually need to *beat* the game to unlock more.One of my favourites is the guy who can't use weapons and is dedicated to his magic attack. Fast, doesn't do great damage, but can be pushed to absurd degrees. He dies easily, but he's ironically easier to pick up than any other character in my opinion as there's no reloading, no worrying about how far your gun shoots.The guns feel 50/50. I dislike all of the starting weapons, save maybe the super shotty, but I dislike the revolver the most. It's slow, pushes you back, takes forever to reload, damage doesn't feel worth it.Ironically, the chaingun is actually one of my least favourite weapons. It's kinda weak, probably good with infinite ammo though. The uh.. Gauss cannon? Thing? Is probably my favourite. Beast of a gun, but reloads frequently and takes three button presses to reload.Oh yeah that's another thing. Different guns have different ranges and firing methods. Some can only shoot every "Beat" (Gauss from my experience can shoot at half-beat or during a beat, but not both at the same time. You have to wait a full cycle, so (bang pause bang pause). Compared to something like a pistol, which can just (bang bang bang). Some guns can shoot several times per beat/half-beat. So something like the SMG fires in bursts of two per-beat/half-beat click.And the soundtrack in BPM is just, so *♥♥♥♥♥♥♥* good. Seriously, it's real good. Like, I love all the music in this game. I think it's great. This game is decent, but the soundtrack adds another level to it. Real good.So with all that said, it is very much a short roguelite for the time being. Not that I mind that. The whole shoot/reload/dodge to the beat is very much just that, and the only punishment/reward for it is just score points. And being able to shoot, reload, etc, to the beat. Which I enjoy. I don't think it needed to be super advanced in depth game to be good? I like it how it is.One las thing, as an addendum, there's rare guns that show up from time ot time. Mostly in.. well-hidden lock boxes. I've tried 2, don't like them. But I really wanna try that quad-barrelled revolver. It looks really good.

_childDocuments_.review: While it is fun and I would absolutely recommend it, I do agree with other reviews that the balance is a bit off. I had exactly the same experience - find the first few runs really difficult (to the point of frustrating and almost quitting the game), then you find a completely broken item and just steamroll the game. For me I got a healing scroll that allows you to heal infinitely on a cooldown, so you can just max heal before every room. Combined with armour and a few max HP increases and you're basically unkillable. It is fun honestly, the shoot to the beat mechanic takes a bit of getting used to and it felt really odd to me at first, I just wanted to blast everything DOOM style initially. But eventually it becomes second nature and is pretty awesome. The guns all feel weighty and impactful and the music is good too. The loot is 'mostly' interesting, although some extra descriptions on some items would be helpful. Am I meant to know what "Marked for Death" does? Or "Cleaving"? Also I've no idea how to carry a second weapon with the "Carry Two Weapons" ring as you're never told. Sure I can start Googling these, but just providing a short description on the tab menu would be super helpful.Either way, these are mostly small things and once you get going on a good run, it's a lot of fun! If you're looking for a sick shooter, I'd probably point you towards the two recent Doom games instead, but if you've played those or want something new, BPM is your thing!

_childDocuments_.review: BPM is one of the most unique FPS games I've ever played. The rhythm aspect, despite requiring the player to get adjusted to, makes the game more engaging and challenging. You shoot, reload, dodge and jump on the beats. Getting these actions down along with the beats while fighting off swarms of enemies is very satisfying and keeps you engaged playthrough after playthrough.Due to the nature of it being a rogue-like game, this game can be fairly time-consuming. The rhythm mechanic may throw you off in the early attempts and can cost you 30+ minutes of progress. So prepare yourself if you're not used to dying a lot in videogames. I personally got stuck at the same place for dozens of attempts, until the RNG rewarded me with good items in one good playthrough, I blazed through it and finished the game.For those who seriously struggle with rhythm games or reaction speed, there's an option in the game where the game does the actions you input on the beats for you, but the combo meter and score system will be disabled. So you could play this game like a traditional FPS game, just not as fun as it's intended to be.10/10 would get killed by a random Baby Bat again

_childDocuments_.review: So, it's okay? I've beaten easy and hard on the main character, and all I can really think is that BPM is a completely fine game. I had fun. But there are two incredibly large issues. One, the rhythm aspects feel tacked on. It clearly isn't, because there has clearly been a lot of meticulous work to make sure enemy attacks, your attacks, and the music sync up beautifully. The last thing I want to do is call this game lazy, it has clearly had a lot of work put into making the rhythm work in the first place. Yet, it feels tacked on. The rhythm, no matter what level you are on, is the exact same. At no point is there any variation to the rhythm you have to keep, so it essentially becomes almost mindless. And, at that point, it's just Doom. Oh, yeah, it's a Doom game. it isn't licensed, but it takes so much inspiration from Doom 2016 that you end up just playing a Doom roguelite. Which is FINE - It's a completely good Doom roguelike, and if that's what you're looking for I'm sure you'll like it, but the rhythm of it hardly feels like it matters. Then, there's the second (and frankly much larger) problem: In this game, you are either being trampled into the dirt, or cutting through each stage like it's butter. If you get certain items (especially items related to healing), you win. Congratulations. If you don't get those items, have fun wasting your time until your inevitable death. I swear, there is no middle-ground. With some luck, you might be able to get to stage 4 with okay items, but you aren't getting any further. I'm sure you COULD go absolutely crazy and beat the game without those items, but the difficulty of that would be through the roof. One wall of text later, it DOES have good aspects. Despite the ankle-deep rhythm mechanics, they're still polished to the point where playing is incredibly satisfying. The music is pretty good too, it has to be. Enemies like Guardians are really cool to fight against, and it's fun learning how to counter them. It's a fine game.

_childDocuments_.review: A rhythm game combined with an FPS.  This sounds like a terrible genre mash.  In this instance at least, it works.  Scratch that.  It's amazing. If you've played crypt of the necro-dancer you'll understand the rhythm elements.  The rest of the game play is going to feel familiar from lots of FPS roguelikes.  Each room represents a challenge you have to complete to unlock the doors.  It's... basic, but that's the common sacrifice of procedurally generated FPS levels.  Every gun feels different.  It's surprising how integrating rhythm elements adds another layer on the feel of weapons.  Pump shotgun needs a hit on the beat to pump, then another to fire.  One of the high tier weapons fires a half beat after you hit the fire button, which makes aiming really weird.  The music is perfection.  Somehow they managed to create a rocking metal soundtrack that doesn't distract from the game.  The gun sounds are exaggerating quite a bit, so you get lots of audio feedback on reloads and when you are running out of ammo.  My qualm from the game is that the rest of it is actually quite quiet.  A lot of time I think I've gotten hit only to realize that I missed a beat.  Honestly I think it give you more feedback on missed beats than damage.Playing the game from beginning to end on a character won't take much time, but if you die you start at the beginning.  That is the glory of the roguelike elements.  You can beat the game in half an hour, but you have to be good to make it.Anyhow.  I dig the game.  I'm guessing it's about good for ten hours of gameplay for the average person, but that might be more or less depending on how deep you dig into the game.  Where I'm at it seems impossible to earn some of the higher achievements (highest difficulty without getting hit, lol).

_childDocuments_.review: Has it's flaws, but is very enjoyable, if you like the music and love occasionally just, deleting the occupants of the rooms you get into.TLDR; The game is balanced, maybe not intentionally, for getting good if you don't get good items, and then just hilarious "Haha ♥♥♥♥ you, stupid dragon"-kinds of overpowered when you do just get all the good items.It could use more items (weapons are suffecient, and most items have duplicates anyway), maybe more levels, but, there are several characters, with very different playstyles (One has constant draining health, another starts with no health, but plenty of armor), aswell as level modifiers once you beat a characters/ difficulty combo, and play it again.As for the flaws, well, you have different kinds of powerups. 4 different item slots, 2 different spell/ability slots, with a sprint ability that is different for some of the characters, as well as 6 stats you can increase (damage, move speed, luck, etc.), and then the ammo capacity.The power level of the abilities and items varies GREATLY; one pair of boots, lays temporary toxic floor where you walk, damaging opponents. Which is nice. But then you have two other pair of boots, that damage everybody, in different ways. One will just strike them, in accordance to a pattern in the beat, the other will just, slowly poison an enemy in the room. The toxic boots, seem vastly underpowered compared to the other two.There's also two different bracelets, that give you +1 in all stats, when you equip it, AND when you clear a level, and if you get it early, you have a high chance of maxing out your stats, which is just super powerful. One of them also gives you 25 max hp, but are they otherwise identical. Alternatives for the bracelet include, increased range (you can get that in otherways, including the two stat bracelets), more money from mobs(that you would use to get more stats, for one), and revealing the map while wearing some other bracers. Or, a different kind of OP item, one that turns projectiles into fireballs, that seem to be 5x as strong.Weapons, also, vary greatly. A few are weak as all get out. Some are ridicoulessly overpowered; 8 shot pistol that does 50 damage, or 1 shot energy cannon that does 2000? I'll take the cannon please. Especially since once you spend enough in the shops, you get easy access to ammo capacity upgrades, which work by upgrading the capacity of the gun; Ammo is unlimited, you just have to reload (Unless you get a shield that gives you infinite ammo. That one is fun with both the energy cannon, AND the minigun). Because you get one bullet capacity per upgrade, regardless of the weapon. Pistol? 9 shots now. Energy cannon? 2 shots now.I had 5 shots in my cannon at the end. Took three times emptying my 'clip', and the final boss was dead, on hard.Conversly, if you don't get the REALLY good items, even the normal items can change playstyle radically enough that you can get through a run, it just takes more skill.

_childDocuments_.review: A rip-tearing, head-banging good time.  Absolutely addictive primary gameplay loop with an incredible soundtrack to match.  Once you start it up and fire and reload for the first time, it's very difficult to put the game back down.However, the game isn't without its flaws.  The color palette leaves something to be desired as the monochromatic levels can lead to some details bleeding into each other, making enemies and projectiles hard to see.  The item pool is also somewhat binary making it so that some runs are a breeze without much challenge while a string of bad drops can make it so that you're woefully ill prepared.Still, that rhythmic gunplay is just pure bliss and despite everything, there's just nothing that can match it anywhere else.  Looking forward to what this developer will tackle next.🤘🤘🤘Highly recommend, despite its issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VERY good game.This game has something so many others lack: elegance.  I don't mean it's pretty.  It's not.  It's visual style is laid on with a trowel.I don't mean it's dainty.  It's not.  It has explosives, demons, and lots of fire.I don't mean it's dance-like.  It's not.  The run to not be in front of the next bullet is constant.I mean it has elegance of design.  It's simple, and yet, in that simplicity, it is beautiful.  You run.  You gun.  You do it to the beat.  There are choices to be made, and they matter for how your run will go.  And throughout it all, it never feels like you have too much to think about in too little time, or too little to think about in an abundance of time.  The game is bottled flow-state... once you get past the first several runs where you learn to feel out the rhythm.Buy it, love it, play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Get this game if you like FPS shooters with a rhythmic shooting aspect. You better be damn good at your FPS games or you won't have a good time. 6.5/10 Fun game, for sure it takes AT LEAST 4 hours to get used to shooting and reloading while moving. You can check I got pretty far. The most obnoxious part of the game is the "range" issues with guns until you get the range upgrades. So get those first. There's a reason why there are range issues however. The game is much easier if you could shoot from end to end and I get it, being as a guy who beat it on freaking Odr I get it. BUT NOT THE FLIES ANYTHING BUT THE FLIES. You will learn to HATE flies in this game no matter who you are, and you will learn to prioritize ANYTHING FLYING IMMEDIATELY. (Other than ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ guardians). People complain about the clockwork monsters but they're not much to worry about. I do like how there is a box to aim in and that auto tagets enemies in it, to reduce the amount of panic aiming at the start. You're free to turn this off if you want a hard core experience. But I promise you, you'll hate yourself and killing flies if you turn it off. Range issues along with them zig zagging in the air to the beat AND shooting will have you pulling the hairs out of your head, so don't turn off the auto aim in box feature. Regardless, fun little game easy to complete with the basic characters. You'll see some comments saying you need THE RUN to win the game and that isn't true. Just GIT GUD. However for Odr I'll kind of have to agree being someone who grinded out 100 runs on the dude to win on Hard it really feels like you need SOMETHING to make him useful and that something is either the extra life shield, or a spell that lets you survive (negate first attack, block all attacks for a set duration, become unkillable for a while), or a long range weapon. Without one of those your run on Odr will be REALLY difficult to make it far. Everyone else has life they can use so you can afford mistakes and therefore don't need the perfect run or items to win with them. But Odr you kind of do, but if you're a god of FPS and fortunate enough to not encounter too many guardians, I can see it happening without any of the things I've listed.OH, completely forgot, the one obnoxious part of the game is the color scheme. Levels being all essentially one color with enemies blending in I think is bad, but I can understand it being also done for the sake of making levels look different and unique. You get used to it, but yeah it can be annoying when you don't see a yellow fly zipping around against the reddish yellow background.
