_childDocuments_.review: Good: The main gameplay quirk is really well executed and is the main reason why this game is so fun. Everything about the gameplay is crisp and rewarding. The rhythm aspect more than makes up for the mediocre elements in the next section. Meh: The item and weapon pool is relatively small and generic. It doesn't have crazy combinations or synergies that games like Binding of Isaac or Enter the Gungeon do. Also, some items are way better than the alternatives and are basically never skipped (Double Damage and Infinite ammo). Given the small item pool, I find that I end up with pretty similar builds every game. The game could also use more content on the stages/bosses department. There is only one alternate path that you can enter from stage 1. It would be great if there was more variety. If this game didn't have the fantastic rhythm element, it would be a pretty mediocre and uninspiring roguelike.

You can easily get instakilled if you're unlucky enough to have enough bullets hit you at once, there's even a glitch with Gullveig where she does exactly that as soon as you enter the fight. This ended two of my runs.2) Flies are extremely overpowered. The final boss is nothing compared to a room full of flies, or god forbid fly spawners. Having an alternate floor theme per floor would do wonders to break the monotony. It's fast paced and challenging to a degree and can be punishing if you aren't constantly moving and shooting. The overall world design, music, and enemies fits perfectly together to create a decent visual and audio harmony, however right now replayability is limited in my humble opinion. In terms of run variety, it is rather limited. Don't come into this game expecting Binding of Isaac, where every run is different and unique, levels of diversity. A fair portion of weapons feel rather similar, just slightly different (2 or 3 beats to reload, firing every other beat, for example), and lack a lot of creativity you'd find in games like Gunfire Reborn where weapons have various firing modes, hitscan/projectile, secondary effects, etc. On the plus side, weapons feel very balanced compared to other games, where almost all weapons, maybe with the exception of some starting pistols, being strong enough to take down the final boss. Similarly items are very generic, with effects such as double damage, fire twice as fast, never reload, the game really lacks items that makes runs feel unique and different. The one thing I do like though is only being able to equip one of a shield, boots, gloves, and helmet to prevent runs just using every item under the sun until you're an unstoppable force moving through very stoppable objects. The game could certainly do with more items and especially items that come with a cost, for example speeding up music 1.5x at a cost of losing hp for example. There's a lot of potential of what could be done to make runs fun and challenging, and making the gameplay feel unique. Right now though, it is far too easy to stack damage items with a shotgun, and beat the final boss before it even has a chance of killing you. It's also worth noting that whilst the world design is good with the music, on it's own it does feel lacklustre and repetitive, and there are some issues that should be addressed by the devs. Rooms do lack flare and creativity with them being generic box shaped areas, with minimal changes from room to room and floor to floor. Chests and shrines can be very hard to see as they often match the same colour as the environment around them and only give off light from a distance. It also doesn't help that they are very miss-able, with one shrine being a literal rock with a stone coloured bowl in front of it. There is also a filter on some of the later levels that does the game a disservice by pumping the saturation too much and causing the game to be a bit of an eyesore and makes the issues with chests being hard to see, even worse. I'm torn whether to give this game a positive or negative review. There is clearly a lot of potential that could come out of this game, and the gameplay and music alone make this an enjoyable experience, at least for a few hours. Unfortunately with the lacklustre visuals and disappointing amount of weapons, items, and character diversity, it makes the game feel stale rapidly. Right now, I would recommend this game, however that would be on the basis that the devs can continue to add content to the game and make some changes to the visuals. If this game doesn't receive any content updates in the coming months, then it will be a disappointing end to an otherwise interesting game that will fall into obscurity. tldr: Music and gameplay are great, however runs will lack diversity quickly and the visuals need some polishing and changing. The game is worth buying and checking out if you think this type game is up your alley, but in it's current state, don't be expecting a game that will keep you coming back.

_childDocuments_.review: Good concept marred by terrible design decisions.1. Poor visibility. Shrines for stat upgrades blend in and can often be overlooked. Enemies that dont glow like a christmas tree can also be hard to see or track. Combined with being blinded by the visuals on screen depending on your items.2. Copying the room design from Binding of isaac was a terrible decision. As any habitual rythm player can tell you, if your flow gets interrupted you tend to mess up more. And here you have an interruption with every room transition.3. The music isnt varied enough and you will get sick of it very quickly. Which honestly is a deadly sin for a rythm game.4. The random stats/ item systems also copied from isaac go against the core appeal of the game. Because like this isnt doesnt matter how good or bad you are. Only your item drops matter. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, Im in the minority here but I'll drop my thoughts.1. Music in this game was okay for the first few minutes, quickly became bored with the low-tempo, no vocals, and extremely repetitive, obviously built for looping, track.2. This can be partially remedied through the new custom music function, however, its a little finicky, and forcefully reduces the BPM of songs that are higher BPM. This is most apparent with songs in the range of 120-130 bpm where it reduces it by half into a horrid snails pace, making it nearly impossible, or atleast unenjoyable to play along with it.3. Any changes in tempo with custom music, unless you properly know an audio editing software to modify the song slightly, cannot be compensated for. So that song simply cant be used on custom music.4. Progression of the roguelite systems of the game are rough. I come from Gungeon, Dead Cells, etc. Where the roguelite elements both make it a bit easier, and can allow for more varied/interesting playstyles outside of the normal gameplay loop. However, the characters which are unlocked are more just challenge runs, each character is harder in some way to play than the original character, but without anything that really changes the game in their kit to make the game more interesting to play. Other than IMO Skuld, which makes the game almost feel like a speedrunning game.5. Rng is a constant element in roguelites, however this game seems to make it even more evident and painful, to the point of giving modifiers that can end a run instantly and immediately such as a barren, shopless, or explosive level, on the first level.6. Normally the RNG could be excused, however the lack of any proper description for your stats, items or weapons, means that alongside ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ RNG you have to just pray you don't pick up one of the plethora of what feel like "Trap" items. Like the cursed iron, Dwarven Ring, and a few others. This is fixed with game experience, but really...its unexcusable IMO.7. Last point, more of a personal gripe...visually the game looks like hot ♥♥♥♥ fresh out the oven. Oversaturated garbage that makes my eyes hurt. This can be mitigated somewhat in the settings...but then it just becomes a gray blob where you can barely make out enemies and chests.The concept and some gameplay is pretty good, and if you get it on sale for 5 bucks like I did it can be worth a few hours of gameplay. But honestly, try one of the multitude of other rhythm games out there. And if you specifically want a rythm FPS, Metal Hellsinger while more expensive has far better default music tracks, that actually include vocals, and the modding scene has support for custom music thats far better than this game. Also, you actually get a loadout of weapons so you can play with your preferred weapon and ACTUALLY know what it does before you first use it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best rogue like and the best rhythm game I've ever played. Its far better than it looks even though it already seems awesome. If youre bad, you can sometimes get carried by RNG with the right loot. Each character has some different mechanics that will change the loot you're looking for, like health = money, constant life drain but constant lifesteal, flying and dying (Odr). Different starting weapons, like the basic pistol, or the sawed off shotgun that I try to get rid of as soon as possible (thanks Odr). And different abilities after clearing each difficulty like a shield, a fast and powerful projectile, or a useless teleport (thanks Odr). Unfortunately, although rare, the game has some bugs that can ruin your run such as an enemy getting stuck out of bounds, like behind a door or in the floor. Clearing every room as Sanngriðr but the door to the boss still won't unlock. And some item interactions that may, or may not be, bugs such as an item granting more potent healing reduces the lifesteal mechanic of Skuld, the effects of skills on your HUD are near transparent only in HelheimThe game unfortunately does not see many updates as far as I can tell. The game could absolutely use a tad more polishing here, a quality of life thing there. But overall a fantastic game that is well worth it, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.user: The Man, the Miph, the Legend
_childDocuments_.review: Bullets Per Minute is a fairly interesting game that tries to combine roguelike elements with fairly standard FPS mechanics. Whilst I personally played the game without the rhythm mechanics, I can see how this game could be rather big with the rhythm game community. My time with the game was fairly enjoyable, but I wouldn't say the game itself was anything more than your standard FPS when you get down to the core.Judging the game for what it is, I can say that I suggest it to anyone looking for a hybridized FPS which has more parts to it than just shooting; However for those coming to it looking for an FPS roguelike experience, there are other games out there which accomplish this task in a much better fashion, even though this game was fun whilst I played it.For this review and others like it, feel free to check out and follow my personal Steam Curator page if you'd like! The Good:- Great soundtrack. With the game being a hybrid FPS-Rhythm game one of the biggest hurdles to tackle is the soundtrack, and it's quite good. Everything fits well with each map, and even with the rhythm mechanics turned off I still felt like the sounds from everything fit perfectly with it.- Sound design. Weapons sound chunky, your footsteps sound heavy, and enemies make very satisfying sounds upon being hit or upon death. Everything fits well with the soundtrack as well, and only really adds to the experience.- Five characters to choose from. Each character has their own quirks and presents the player with a different challenge and weapon to learn and potentially master. There's a character with a humble starting pistol, and another with aggressive jazz hands.- A large selection of weaponry to choose from. There's everything from a starting pistol all the way to bazookas, an angry super-soaker, quad shotgun, etc. You'll have multiple options as you play through the game, allowing you to diversify your gameplay as much as you like.- Upgrades seem to be catered to your chosen character. Unlike most roguelikes your upgrades seem to be chosen and catered to your chosen character as you play through the campaign. Truly the game feels as though it's built around making you feel like a badass as you play through it.The Ok:- Fairly standard FPS mechanics. When you strip away the rhythm game mechanics the FPS combat feels bland and at times unintuitive offering almost nothing that we've not particularly seen before from other FPS-roguelike hybrids. Weapons have a maximum distance they can fire which overall takes away from the general flow of combat as there's NOTHING saying why you cannot fire your GUN more than 10 feet in front of yourself. You're allowed to carry only a singular weapon with you at a time, when having multiple guns in this instance just feels like the logical progression, as you'd be able to string together weapon switches and combos from each one to amass a higher score when done on the beat.- Very short without the rhythm mechanics. Most roguelikes are quite short, but they require more playthroughs and perseverance than BPM does. With the rhythm mechanics turned off a runthrough of the game could easily take as little as 30 or so minutes to complete, and whilst it's still enjoyable the game does feel as though the overall timesink is tied to the rhythm mechanics. I can see how the game would be much longer with them turned on. There's only 8 stages total, and whilst diverse at times they don't feel diverse enough to actually increase the games longevity.- A moderate level of diversity to the maps. With random-level generation I've typically come to expect more than what seems to be five templates for a games overworld layouts. Whilst the way the generation works is interesting, it just feels like there's some missed opportunities such as more than just a single sub-boss per level, trap rooms, etc. There's also only a singular boss per stage as well, and whilst they do have randomized effects tied to them such as having a clone of themselves, it feels as though they're overall very samey and not at all difficult after having defeated them once.- An interesting enough upgrade and item system. Whilst there are items and upgrades in this game they all feel fairly unintuitive. Upgrades and items are fairly unimpressive with some of them seeming to have absolutely no place in the game, whereas others just feel kind of overkill depending on the weapon that you're using. Upgrades come in your standard flavor of one upgrade for the stat listed upon the shrine, and this leads to there not really being anything particular such as builds, but more so just grabbing everything you can, which seems fairly counterintuitive when there's five characters with their own unique abilities.The Bad:- Tracking Projectiles. I've said this a few times in the past, but projectiles which track the player add absolutely nothing to the experience other than being a gigantic nuisance. With how you're supposed to play on the beat with the rhythm mode and can only fire at the enemies on the beat some fights turn into a gigantic mess where all you could feasibly focus on doing is dodging whilst only being able to fire back once or twice before moving once more.- Rhythm mechanics which feel too strict when it comes to the more densely packed areas. I'm not sure how most people would go about playing this with the rhythm mechanic turned on, as there are some rooms in later stages which are densely packed with both sub-bosses and previous stage bosses which devolve into a projectile spamming mess.- Difficulties feel lackluster without the rhythm mechanics. Upon trying both easy and hard I found the experience without the rhythm mechanics turned on to have no discernible difference, with the enemies doing the same amount of damage and the game seemingly having no differentiation between the two when it comes to the standard FPS part of the game. I can only assume this is tied strictly to the rhythm mechanics of the game.-Final Score: 6.5/10.Worth $17.99 ($19.99 standard)? Honestly, it's hard to say for me. If you're coming into the game looking for a roguelike FPS experience and have no interest in the rhythm mechanics I'd say the answer to this question is no. Looking at it as a standard FPS I'd say it's worth about $10 as there are other roguelike FPS's for less which accomplish the same things this game does and more from an FPS STANDPOINT.Closing Thoughts: My experience with this game is entirely based around the non-rhythm mechanics version, and whilst I definitely enjoyed my time with the game it feels like there's a lot of missed opportunities regarding both the standard FPS mechanics and rhythm mechanics. If you're looking for a fast-paced roguelike FPS this isn't the first game I'd suggest for you, but I'd say I definitely had enough fun for me to warrant recommending it overall. I suppose overall the feel I get from BPM is that it's an Early Access title which is still trying to polish itself, even though it's a fully released title.

_childDocuments_.review: If the idea of a rhythm-FPS interests you at all, the execution of the idea is done very well in this game. It feels really good to act on the beat, and the guns are satisfying to shoot and reload. This game is definitely worth it just for the originality of the concept and how well it's been realized.As a roguelike, it suffers a little bit from an underwhelming variety of item effects. Once you get the hang of it, it's usually a little too easy, as each run sees you becoming such an unstoppable powerhouse that later bosses are just not a threat. It definitely gives you that Doom feeling of running through enemies, but not the same difficulty or risk.8/10, super fun with minor quirks that only hamper replayability, otherwise a very exciting FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be real, this game is not as good as it could have been. It's a good game, but it could have been a great game.Let's start with the good things:- A lot of characters- The sync with the music is real, and you can feel it- It feels amazing to try to speedrun this game- You can get good combos (feels great)- The game was finally optimized!- There is no game alike (FPS + roguelike + rhythm + speedrun)Now to the bad stuff:- Graphics are honestly terrible, and the saturation is just a feature (not a bug) so you cannot see how terrible it actually is.- They took the models from the free unity shop, which is not bad perse, but says quite a bit about it.- The fact that you cannot kill enemies with shield if you use an explosive weapon is annoying as ♥♥♥♥.- How the ♥♥♥♥ does some bee have more HP than a human size enemy?- A lot of the weapons are completely useless- Bee levels on floor 1 to 4 are insane and have no purpose, it's way too hard for being that floor.- Same song for all floors. Like, really? I expected to at least get a different song for each boss, man. This was a huge disappointment. And the fact that there is no roadmap to add more of them for free… it just hurts.- A lot of skills and items are purely useless for characters with 0 HP. Actually, a lot of skills/abilities are useless in general.- Some rooms have enemies spawn in front of the door you enter, so if you enter sprinting, you're now dead.- When they introduce new items/mechanics, like freeze enemies, it seems like they forget about this thing called "singery", and when you freeze a boss, the boss appears frozen, but still attacks you, so now it's harder since the boss does not make any animation before attacking.- Some enemies do still kill you after you killed them. The bee, for instance, still throw it's ball, or the bosses attacks are not canceled when they die, so you can still die because of those attacks they were charging.Overall a lot of flaws to be honest, that's why IMO is not a great game, but a good one. I mean, I've played almost 50 hours as I'm writing this, so it must be good.

You get a few more unlocks as far as choices go, but it seems to be all there from the start. You, as a player, improve and learn the game mechanics over time and slowly get better. It's not the character getting better (Till you beat it) it's you. That's the hallmark of a good Roguelike to me. _childDocuments_.review: BPM has a fun idea, and I'm mostly enjoying my time with it, but it's not something I'd recommend. There's a number of design choices that are just.. poorly thought out, and the game can't be bothered to actually explain its mechanics so it's hard to break down all the issues. Don't miss a beat or you might die! Which does mean there's a chance you don't shoot or dodge, and die as a result, but there doesn't seem to really be any benefit to maintaining a streak outside of one item I've found.> Choose from 5 different characters with unique strengths and weaknesses.The thing about this is the game doesn't really explain what these strengths and weaknesses ARE, you just kinda have to play the character and try to figure it out. And also the character's secondary is locked by default. The differences mostly seem to be starting weapon, starting health, and maybe some slight stat variations. One character has infinite ammo by shooting fireballs from his hands, with the tradeoff that you can't pick up guns. You know, that other bullet point that's supposed to entice you to play the game? And stuff like range upgrades or clip capacity upgrades don't mean anything to him, but can still be found in chests anyway.> Wield a powerful arsenal of weapons, all with different behaviour for firing and reloading to the beat of the soundtrack.The weapons seem to vary from peashooters to godkillers without a whole lot in between, the starting character's gun feels especially useless.> Battle a diverse array of enemies, each with unique rhythmic behaviours.This works well with some. The first boss laughs in sync with the music, that's cool! Most of the enemies' movements have nothing to do with the music, and at most fire on beat without a tell for which beat they'll do it on. Less cool.> Equip over 40 items that buff your character in unique and interesting ways.Do you want these shoes that make you faster? Or these other shoes that make you faster? What about this glove that makes you WAY faster? What about this shield that gives you infinite ammo, which you can still get on the character that starts with infinite ammo? How about a skeleton key you keep forever, but doesn't stop keys from dropping, which is what some minibosses exclusively drop, and there's no indication that you're about to walk into a miniboss room?> Experience an epic rock opera soundtrack.I mean, yes, but my beef here is the music doesn't always stick to the beat you shoot at. The levels usually start with very solid audio indicating the pace you can fire at and soon enough abandon it. When the guitar starts shredding you'd think that it triggers when you're fighting something tough or because you've hit a high enough score multiplier and now you can shoot faster. But that's silly, that's not what happens. That part of the song just shreds.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one hellava game. This fully baked rocked out fps rouge-like is amazing with its shops and characters some of my favorites being Njord and big mama Skuld. The gameplay mixes in the characters from you losing health, but killing and harming enemies heals you, you have no health and one hit means you're out, or your health is the money on you, and then there's the money gremlin Geri. Each character is fun and difficult in their own right. I enjoyed how once I beat the game on easy playing on the same difficulty again made it way too simple and made me crave for  a challenge on hard with some interseting modifiers in areas and bosses going from a smaller version of the boss or there being two crack filled versions of the boss while the level is covered in ice in space. As any rouge-like the items are all interesting especially once you get a beast combo for a specific character or in a challenge, for example transforming Njord's orbs to explosives or with double shot with lessened cooldown and enemies fragmenting on death was an insane set of things together for a character with infinite ammo. For the entire experience it gave me I highly recommend to those who enjoy fps games and don't enjoy rougelikes as much. I didn't like rouge likes too much and still do, but this one felt like a different rhythmic journey. 9/10 nothing is perfect, but it sure does feel like it's so close.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little game but could have been better without the "shoot on the beat" mechanic. I like how the minigun rolls with the music, how you have to jump and dodge on the beat and having enemy attacks synced with the music (first boss is a great example, or the guys with the shield) and finishing bosses, creating "your own" guitar solo, is great too. However, being allowed to fire only on every beat (or dare you offbeat) is neither difficult nor fun, but just annoying. This may sound like a unique and genius idea at first but really isn't.There is an "auto" challenge, where the guns are automatic and I think that's how the game should be all the time, or at least give me the freedom to tap the pistol on 16th notes too. There is also no "rhythmic" challenge in this game. Right now this game just makes you a human metronome, hammering the same few songs into your head even harder with every *beat*.Worth the 20$ anyways.Edit: there is an option turn off rhythm which means you can spam the controls, but still the shots will happen on the beat. I have to add that "only shots on beat" is cool for some guns but feels very limiting on others. Could have been nice to have different tempos for the stages or items/skills/characters to change the tempo. More variety with the songs, a selection to choose from, different instruments/melodies/parts for different playstyle/characters? But then again it's 20 bucks and fun.P.S.: I challenge you to do the last character on hellish, it's "impossible".

_childDocuments_.review: - Shoot, reload, jump, dash n dance on the beat!- There are hidden secrets in some rooms, often up high which you only can reach with skill jumps.- Interesting movement: o Jumping off stairs uphill lets you jump higher o Jumping off stairs downhill lets you jump farther o Jumping height and length is dependant on your movement speed o You movement speed depends on different things. Basically you have a speed counter which can go from 0 up to 9 by spending coins on upgrades, if you find them, for each run. The weight of your gun influences your speed/jump height/length, but there is more to it. You can increase your current speed by bunny hopping and a smooth direction change à la Quake. With these tricks going fast and continuous you are able to reach optional secret heights unreachable from a standing position, which adds just the right amount of skill to spice it up.- High difficulty. Even easy is hard. But then again 'Hard' isn't much harder than 'Easy'. But both are definitely hard.- Different characters with different abilities and starting items can be unlocked to keep it fresh.- bosses don't require much rhythm. If you found the right items you can even kill them before any rhythm part is needed. On a regular run there is only a couple of timed dodges or jumps needed for the whole boss fight. Also those timed dodges/jumps are only once in about four 4/4 (four quarter) times. I would find it better if bosses would require much more rhythm to make it less like a usual FPS boss fight. E.g. make them invulnerable unless you do the rhythm part correct to open their guard up. And I would appreciate more rhythm combos like dodge right/jump/dodge left/shoot in rapid succesion and different combos randomized.- Sometimes enemies clip through walls and can't be hit, so you can't finish the room. The doors won't open, because that requires all enemies to be beaten, so you can not continue the level. In this case you have to quit to main menu and restart the chapter.- item descriptions are a bit vague. Most often you have to try it to understand what they do.- You can't drop an item once picked up. There is an item which enables you to shoot two projectiles with one shot. This doubles the damage, but halves the shots fired before you have to reload by inputting the gun's reload combo sequence. Now if my current weapon is already strong enough for most enemies, I prefer more shots instead of double damage. The first armour item I picked up was double shot and since it was the first one I had no other item hovering over the chest to change it back to. There should be an option to drop an item in case you don't want it.- You cannot unequip items. In some situations this would be good.- There is a character who cannot pick up certain items, but these items still spawn for him in randomized content chests for which you have to spend coins to open. So you invest into your run but are sometimes given nothing.This game is for tough FPS players who like a challenge and like some spice in their usual rogue-like FPS soup.

_childDocuments_.review: I have done 3 runs of this game and have already beaten it.My impression is that it's one of those rougelikes that once you get something, you become basically unstoppable. This something was the healing spell, which is powerful enough by its own, but I found a set of bracers that doubled its healing and let me just walk through everything. I generated an obscene amount of money too, because there's cash-for-HP shrines and the healing ability is on a short timed cooldown rather than being tied to kills or rooms cleared, which is a huge problem because it allows you to just cheese the entire game.While this isn't bad in and of itself (Rougelikes can have runs be cakewalks but compelling eg Isaac) the gameplay just isn't up to snuff. I thought I'd have fun with this game, after all I enjoyed Crypt of the Necrodancer despite being average at these kinds of rhythm games. But in trying it I've realized that there's a reason why the concept hasn't been done before: it's really not satisfying to shoot or reload on a beat. Especially when melee enemies charge at you regardless of the rhythm.What I mean is; it SHOULD feel like I'm doing really good when I keep a rhythm going in a room, but ultimately it feels like keeping perfectly in time just makes my character function as a bog-standard FPS shooty person with low firerate weapons and marginal (and strangely diagonal) autoaim.Others have said it before and yes, the filters are too much. Things blur into the background way too much, attacks included. Also I experienced some strange performance issues as well towards the end of the game, which didn't go away after tweaking my graphics settings down.So, I have to say it's a good idea but very flawed execution. It's not satisfying, you end up fighting the game more than enjoying it. There's too much to keep track of for me at least, maybe if you're a huge music game fan that wants a basic shooting game, grab it on sale. $20 is too much for this, let alone $17 what I paid for... so I'm getting a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: this is the most likely game that anyone will bring up if you ask about a rhythm-based fps game. while the penalty for being off-time is incredibly annoying and keeps you out of the rhythm for longer than it should, the timings are quite on-point. on your first launch you calibrate the timing for your monitor and audio to make sure that the timings are not unfair for you. almost all deaths i've felt i was at fault for, because i messed up somehow, whether through timings or not dodging attacks. the game itself is difficult to get accustomed to and can take an hour or so to get the hang of it; it took me about an hour myself to start making progress, and ended up fluking from asgard somehow. there are certain parts of the game that definitely need some sort of fixing, because people are able to cheese achievements through a few methods. the hardest character cannot take a single hit or they die, but with an extra life you can save-buffer and re-enter at the start of the level without any penalty. similar to the binding of isaac and its toughest character, the lost(or moreso the tainted lost), it makes it a lot more encouraging for people to cheese completion. the rng in the game is mediocre, with some issues time to time with getting the same things repeatedly. it isn't like the binding of isaac or other roguelikes where there are a lot of weapons and abilities, there's around a dozen or so per category. regardless, it still makes for some fun builds and attempts that you'll inevitable have.movement is quite odd and unusual, with bunnyhopping similar to quake or old source engine that can accumulate ridiculous amounts of speed, nullifying the practical use of dashing(holding the shift key). i think the maximum velocity based on bunnyhopping should be adjusted based on your speed stats in each run, just to encourage the use of dashing for its purpose. i'm unaware of any abilities or items that give a buff for dashing, but even if there are any, it still doesn't justify the use of it because it's incredibly inferior to bunnyhopping.all in all, the game is quite smooth and nice to play, but there are some minor issues that haven't been fixed which definitely should be considered and adjusted. by issues, i don't mean bugs, because i have experienced zero bugs so far; balance, rng, and workarounds are the most important issues i think should be addressed and resolved, hopefully sooner than later. if you like rhythm games, fps, and roguelikes, this mixes all three together with a great, enjoyable experience

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: If your next paycheck isn't dedicated to your rent, food, or gas, get this game. And even then I'd start fasting and walk to work for this game.Pros-The most amount of fun I've had in a game in a while. I didn't realize it until a week in that I'd spent so much time on it-The look of the game is unique and honestly improves the game overall-Great music, It's more methodical than just loud and I appreciate that-One of few games where you genuinely feel like a badass-Items are balanced to be strong so OP doesn't mean you are going to win a run instantly-Just the right amount of difficultCons-The item balance isn't perfect and I don't mean anything is too strong. The weak items need a real buff to feel useful. Obviously not every item needs to be a banger, but some adjusting would be well deserved. -Not many achievements in the game so the challenges you beat are ones you put on yourself-About 1 in 10 runs are dead due to bad RNG (like the level or boss modifiers) but the same thing happens in other similar games so that isn't a hardcore fault-No story at all, but tbh it doesn't need one when the core gameplay loop is so engaging and immersive-The wiki isn't nearly as detailed as I'd like it. Not enough people playing so not enough people work to get stuff on the wiki about exact item mechanicsThings to Add (for devs if they happen to read)-More levels like the Asgard Crypts, aka harder optional levels with special rooms-More special rooms in general. This would come in as a Level Modifier, like Castle, and they are always a blast-Rebalance to make items generally stronger (and probably making enemies stronger to balance)-More early - mid game floor specific enemies would be nice-More weird achievements, like specific combination of items like having 4 headgear on at once or something

_childDocuments_.review: The music is awesome, the gameplay fun and satisfying and there is a lot of content.So why the thumb down? Simple!The game has a few tiny flaws that make it basically unplayable for me.1. The RNGYes, I know. It's a Rouge-Lite. Of course there is RNG. But this game takes the cake for bad ones. Many runs are practically worthless because the RNG is so against you.I don't know what the devs were thinking here but there are so many runs where you simply can't open any chest, buy items or weapons or find any upgrades. Money and keys are so rare you basically have to rely on a Lucky Item room or for the bank to spawn, which also only happens like every fith run...The only runs that actually felt good were the ones where I wound items that give you infinite keys, money multipliers or stuff like that.I also only have beaten the game once in a run where I found an overpowered weapon, infinite keys and infinite money because I could finally actually use the shrines and shops the game gives you. After that, I never got past level 3 again.But that's not the biggest problem. The RNG is annoying and DEMANDS tweaking, but the biggest problem the game has are...2. The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flying enemiesAgain. What where they thinking? Why are the hardest enemies in the game not the giant spiders, or the big golems or even the bosses? Why are the Bats and Flies the most challenging thing the game can throw at you?!They are tiny, fast, hard to hit and they can shoot fireballs at you. They even do the same damage as every other enemy in the game. Why give me 100 base healt when everything still deals 25 damage? Why dont the flying enemies only give you 5-10 damage per hit? It would make more sense, because they are the smallest enemies and it would also be way fairer to get hit by them. Because you will. Most runs end because you get thrown in a room with like 10 of them, all swarming you from all sides and shooting at you. They can even hit you from far away, because they have unlimited range, while you have not.That's probably also why the first boss in the game is also one of the hardest ones. Because he flies around you and shoots at you.It's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frustrating not getting anything worthwhile and then dying in a room full with giant spiders because a small bat, on the other end of the room shot you.

_childDocuments_.review: i never really understood the roguelike genre, it felt really annoying when i kept dying and starting from the beginning super weak and lose all my progress.i am used to either having checkpoints and buildup my progress, or multiplayer shooter where you just get better the more you play, but you never become weaker when you start the next match.i had this game on my wishlist for a while, i know i love music, i love rhythm games and i have thousands of hours in shooter games, so this game checked all the boxes.it was fun the first few times i started the game, i was still exploring everything and having fun, but soon i started dying and having to restart from the beginning and build up my character over and over and over again, eventually i had 17 losses in a row, dying in the 2nd level every time.i finally managed to beat the 2nd level and died on the 3rd, that's when i gave up on ever making any progress in this game and closed it, i tried it a few times every day, play an hour or two and still failing.i then watched a speed runner finish the entire game in less than 20 minutes, that's when i realized i was playing the game wrong, i treated the game as a normal shooter game, .i went back to the game, kept trying, kept failing, but the game felt so much easier, i was rarely getting hit by anything, not even the bosses were touching me, i would fail because i was weak or just didn't know which enemies to focus on because they're all new enemies to me.till finally after almost 34 fails and 8 hours of gameplay, and over an hour in that last run i managed to beat the game for the first time.the only con for me is that the game is kinda short, however there are so many challenges and characters to keep you invested if you like the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has potential, and I use that term loosely.The aesthetics are great. The music is present, neither obtrusive nor grating. The core gameplay loop- actions on the beat- is mostly functional.There's several factors that drag it down, though:1. Everything blends into itself a little. Because the aesthetics are so chromakeyed, it becomes difficult sometimes to actually see enemies.2. 'Enemies attack on the beat' is a half-truth. They'll fire on the beat, but their projectiles are slow.3. There is no functional difference between health and shields unless you get a good run and get the shield regen thing early on... on a character that does have shields.4. Modifiers without rewards. Floors can have random modifiers that are almost universally punishing.5. Hardly any between-run progression. No upgrades, no new unlocks, just more challenges and no progression otherwise. You can dump coins in the bank, but after ten coins it locks out per run, and you need 100 in there to unlock a new character, with no assurance either way.6. An overreliance on RNG. Some items are OP as hell. Some are active detriments. Weapons don't do enough damage to chew through enemies as fast as they need to in order to compensate for the beat RoF, meaning you need to get lucky with items being either dropped, or purchasable with coins.Overall, I think the game has potential. The core aspects work, but everything past that is a hodgepodge that makes me feel like most of the time I'm fighting the game and hoping for drops rather than actually learning anything and improving. Other roguelikes either give progression or give variety, but in this case, I don't think they've succeeded at either.Wait on it for a while and see if it improves.

_childDocuments_.review: BPM, at its core is a very fun, rhythm based fps; however, it has some glaring issues.I really enjoy cranking up music to the max and playing video games, and many times i find myself playing video games like they're a rhythm game, so I was really excited when I found out about BPM from a friend and bought it. However, after playing for a few hours I was pretty disappointed. While the gunplay being tied to the rhythm is fun, not much else in the game actually utilizes the rhythm mechanics, and I wish i had a little more agency. The game feels kind of unfinished, like the creators had this cool idea of like a rhythm game, a shooter and a dungeon crawler roguelike, and they put them together, but then they didn't really let the concepts work together well. The rooms before the final boss which don't have mini bosses are extremely tedious to clear. It feels like the smaller mobs are just thrown in as filler, and they don't really actually add anything as kiting them boils down to "run in circle, shoot them 1 by 1" which is completely different from the feel of the bosses and minibosses. The bosses and mini bosses actually somewhat utilize the rhythm mechanics of the game and really add skill and strategy. While it is a roguelike, and every run should vary based off of RNG, it's pretty rare that you come across a blacksmith with an weapon that's better than your starting gun. There are a few other things i could nitpick which are simple ui, perfomance, and QoL things, but i don't think they are a huge issue. That being said, I have enjoyed the time I've put into the game, and plan to sink some more time into it. I love the aesthetic and I enjoy the soundtrack (though I wish I could do some music of my choice). I don't recommend buying this game full price, but if its on sale for a good deal, not a bad pickup.

_childDocuments_.review: It does a lot of things very well, and I will rate it thumbs up, because it is a very cool project that's worth the experience. I beat it in around 6 hours on "easy" (the default mode). However, there is absolutely an overuse of the extremely tiresome roguelike trope of repetitive levels followed by outrageous "gotcha" mechanics 30 minutes into a run that force a loss to artificially extend the length of the game. It's not just run-ending 'gotcha's (usually centered around bosses who bust out mechanics that are not understandable unless you've already lost to them a few times to learn their patterns), but the game is just chock full of features that screw the player until you learn not to be fooled by something twice. I'm not really sure why, considering the game is already very hard.There is some very interesting stuff going on with the rhythm mechanics, the theme is cool, and the overall flow of building your character up with increased stats and better items and abilities is what you'd expect out of a decent roguelike, but the overall hostility towards the player is a negative for me. Hard is one thing, cheap is another. If you don't mind being mocked by the devs, or you can handle raging at general cheap unfairness then you'll probably enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an instant favorite. The music is catchy. The graphics are simple but evocative. The shooting handles really well. The difficulty is punishing yet fair. There's a great sense of subtle humor and plenty of charm to go around.The learning curve is steep, but since no one run matters, you're free to learn at your pace. Extra options unlock at reasonable intervals for player investment. Even if it feels way too hard, RNG will shine on you eventually, with heal spells or regenerating armor, life steal, or a great damage spell.If you have ever enjoyed a shooter and a rhythm game this is probably for you.  If you enjoyed Crypt of the Necrodancer or Cadence of Hyrule, this is probably for you.I only wish I hadn't let it rot in my backlog for so long.PS. Extra props to the gun designs. This game suffers a little from a common problem in rogue-likes where there's just a huge number of items and no way to look up what they do or make informed decisions in a shop, but the make great use of game culture and affordances to inform the player.  For example, see a pistol with 2 barrels, it probably shoots twice per pull, increasing damage but also decreasing time between reloads, or see a revolver, it probably does more damage at the cost of longer reloads.  This one aspect was absolutely brilliant.

The issue is that with spiders and bats all the player has to do is to circlestrafe arround the room. Compared to later enemys or even minibosses who have more interesting attackpatterns that need to be dodged in a specific way.Unfortunately, since I have to restart the entire campaign instead of just the level, I will be spending most of my time with the boring enemys. Not to mention how it will be harder to practice certain enemy patterns if I always have to spend 30 minutes to go back to the enemy. Compare that to games like Ultrakill or Serious Sam who autosave 15 seconds before the encounter.I think that playing threw the entire campaign without dying should have been a challenge mode for people who have mastered the game after they had practicied properly. Otherwise you just bore players by forcing them to fight the same boring enemys in the first few levels.I would love an option where you could save between levels or a mode that allows you to select individual levels with a pre set loadout to really practice individual encounters/enemys that are almost exclusive to certain levels.

_childDocuments_.review: AGHHHHH, YES!!!  The soundtrack in general is as good as the trailer track, all of the action and a lot of subtle bits (footsteps, heartbeat, boss laughs, ..., but not item pickup sounds) are as satisfyingly rhythmic as the trailer action teases, the movement is surprisingly great (other than the jump-to-apex time not being exactly a beat long), the overall tone is great, ... Welp, at least I can still thoroughly enjoy the early stages and listen to the soundtrack on its own. When you win the lottery and have played the bosses enough to not die to them immediately, it is properly NICE again! I love this game again.  Its dedication to the beat is like nothing else I've played in FPSes (except arguably Pistol Whip), and finally not dying was the proper homemade icing on that cake.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but it honestly feels like it should be in early access. If giving it a neutral rating was an option, i would pick it. The balancing is poor to non-existent, some items are instant run-winners while others are 100% useless. Some of the characters (namely Odr and Sanngriðr) and the hellish difficulty are so unfairly brutal that it feels like the developers forgot that games are supposed to be fun, and just wanted to make it as hard as humanly possible. The learning curve is also very sharp. You're unlikely to get your first win, or even get to the second floor, until you've put in multiple hours. The game also doesn't have enough content. There's floor modifiers and boss modifiers and that's about as far as you can get from the base game. There's nothing to unlock aside achievements, once you beat the game once on hard mode you've gotten everything you can with that character. It doesn't need to be binding of isaac level with hundreds of unlocks, but I wish there was more. Something so that I could feel a sense of progress when I beat a game instead of just being returned to the main title screen. There's not even an option for custom music or alternative tracks, and theres only one song that plays on each level. It's a bop at first but after putting in over 22 hours, its started to become stale. Especially the first level, which I've had to listen to at least a hundred times with no way to change it. The color scheme is also... an interesting choice. It's not terrible, but it can make it distracting and hard to see the enemies at times. It would also be nice if the saturation was toned down at the start and an adjustment slider at the start, instead of tucking away the saturation bar in the settings.Overall, I still really like this game. It's fun, addictive, and plays well. However, the pitfalls it has are simply too big and too serious to be overlooked, and the entire game suffers as a result. I would love to see this game polished, as it obviously has huge potential, but fear that it may never reach that point.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. The concept was enough to push me through the initial slog of getting used to the gameplay, and is among my top 5 games of 2020. The best way to acclimate yourself is to think of BPM as a rhythm game first, an FPS second, and a roguelike last.PROS- Great soundtrack - and it's royalty free which will keep Twitch/YouTube off your back if you're a streamer!- Excellent well-paced integration of FPS and rhythm gameplay. Once you get into the groove, it feels almost like your weapon is itself a musical instrument.- Well-optimized, with no real game-breaking bugs. Plenty of graphic adjustment options to aid performance on slower computers.- Decent variety of weapons, all with their own distinct play styles and advantages.- Unlockable characters that offer their own distinct advantages and gameplay styles.- Good variety of enemies, each with their own distinct attack patterns, tells, and engagement strategies. The competent enemy AI is driven by the rhythm game mechanics, so don't expect complex coordinated kettling strategies or anything like that, but they are more than capable of pinning you to a wall or flanking you if you let your guard down.- There's not much downtime in the experience at all. Par time for casual runs is about 40-50 minutes and load times are quick. Quickest speed run currently on record is just over 6 minutes. Upon death, you can start a new run in seconds.- You can quit mid-run and pick up on the same floor. In the rare event of crashes (I've only had one), auto-save will continue your run at the beginning of the floor.- Interesting uses of high-saturation, limited color palettes, which sets the tone and adds to the challenge. Used effectively to "hide" upgrade shrines and secret area paths in plain sightCONS (as of this writing; there's an update coming out soon that may address some of these)- Low variety of items and rooms; runs don't feel drastically different. Floor bosses and music tracks are the same every run (sometimes the bosses and floors add modifiers but it doesn't change the same-y feel).- Still has some balance issues to work out. It's not difficult to reliably create game-breaking builds once you get familiar with the items and how they synergize.- There's a score system that doesn't integrate with the rest of the game. Score is practically pointless if you're not gonna have leaderboards (local ones at the very least).- Related: You'd think a hybrid rhythm game would integrate flawless note streaks into the gameplay, but by and large the only reason to build perfect note streaks in this game is to increase your multiplier - which only affects your score (pointless, see above) and the effects of like 1 or 2 random items.- The pause in this game is weird. It pauses enemies, but not time-based cooldowns or score decay. I found it was possible to get the "heal self" ability and just pause the game between heals to recharge it risk-free, and the only thing I lost was some points, which... y'know, who cares, no leaderboard.- There's no in-game tutorial and many of the item descriptions are obtuse/unclear even by roguelike standards.- A minor but related quibble - the fedora is the only item that uses a separate set of controls. This may explain why many streamers I watch playing this game think the fedora is useless, even though it's arguably the most OP item in the game once you know how to use it.- No story whatsoever and the artistic cohesion is flimsy. There's a "Norse lore" pastiche to the setting, but nothing to really give it context, and even that starts to fall apart once you're fighting weird robots and flying squid while wearing sneakers, astronaut gloves, and a top hat. Listed here mostly for completion's sake; it's not so much a "con" as a noticeable quirk, and actually adds to the whole arcade-y feel to the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A literal take on the 'ballad' of combat found in arena shooters and a brilliant premise that's been hidden in plain sight. The clicks and snaps of gunplay have always had a figurative rhythm to them and trailers that set weaponry to music have always caught my  ears. That said, the premise is about the only thing unique that BPM has to offer and, even then, its execution is distressing.Learning to play a ‘rhythm shooter’ is like trying to ride a bicycle backward. In BPM, a genre about patience and consistency while overseeing a set of static inputs fails to harmonize with the spontaneous decision-making and overstimulation of fast-paced gunplay. Timing is essential to flow in either case, but layering the two introduces a conflict of interest between reaction time and acting on someone else’s time. Even if forging the new habits required for BPM was simple, the game is still less than the sum of its parts. As a shooter, it’s awfully shallow and derivative. For a rhythm game, the animation often lacked impact and anticipation. The music is a highlight but is unavoidably repetitive due to its role as the metronome. It’s no help that the roguelike elements are bog-standard and share their own set of inadequacies. As an aside, It would be interesting to see how inverting the game's restriction from working  on the beat to  on the beat would change gameplay. For instance, performing actions on time could provide an essential buff to damage/I-frames/reloads. The player would grow into the tempo through incentivizing correct timing instead of demanding it. The end result would look the same. For that matter, what if a game let the player consciously compose their own ‘shotgun serenades’ as a motive for intrinsic arsenal experimentation? Digressing, red-light green-light doesn't easily suit a playstyle where unimpeded movement and split-second improvisation are the main course.Speaking of red-lights, the game's all-consuming shader is plain ugly. Red-on-orange is even less readable than the gameboy's shades of green. It’s like ten-year-old me considering that windows movie maker videos look more stylish with maximum contrast and sharpness. In terms of marketing, using the yawning valkyrie as a mascot for the steam store/nauseating menu screen if off-putting. The uncanniness of that offended grimace keeps burning into me, as if I spilled her Starbucks or something.The painful deconstructing of welded-in shooter habits while being given little opportunity to appreciate anything the game had to offer made for a generally unpleasant few hours. That said, there's certainly a market for BPM. The elevator pitch clearly got me. Those with the dedicated masochism to rip through the roughest games from BPM’s source genres may find the scrambling of their circuits delightfully exasperating. Chances are that you'll end up with another incompleted 'roguelike but with x' in your steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt of the Necro-dancer given the FPS treatment sounds like a great idea on paper, and it is, but the execution here is rough and lacking. There is a good game here screaming to be let out but it keeps getting silenced by the constant irks that are on full display. Presentation wise, I hope you like red and yellow, because the game is blurred slurry of neon-tint that often masks the annoyingly small critters deemed enemies of Norse demi-gods being thematically at odds with itself. The tint makes it hard to discern projectiles, most jarring in the later boss-fights, from micro enemy which the map layout will often mask behind the small steps, and boy does this game love small enemies which hit as hard as large ones. If going for a rhythm game then music needs to be on-point which in this game has a hit or miss, droning rock playing in the background somewhere, which has its odd moment only to fade once more... and you better learn to like that 1st track, you're gonna be hearing it A LOT; the beat indicator also doesn't feel to match the song at times, making it less of a 'feel' and more of a 'keep track of click timing' effort, and songs only acknowledge your impact after the defeat of a boss, which while a nice flair, should be something omnipresent through out the game, as an example Killer Instinct and Pistol Whip both have this down. The guns are all the shortest range I've ever experienced, forcing you to hunt down annoying zipping flies at opposite ends of the arenas, that is if you ever even get to experience the other weapons in the first place due to the RNG rouge-like mechanics at play which will often leave you with coins and nothing to spend them on, and even then, the choice of guns feels like choosing which reload mechanic you want to deal with rather than a definitive uniqueness for each; a mini-gun that is locked to a slow-beat is also a grave sin. Balancing also seems to be off, only a easy and hard mode, the only difference between them seeming to be the amount of enemies slapped into the arena per room, while damage taken remains at an all time high across the board. The game also shackles you and punishes you for the slightest misstep, while enemies seem to be free to act off-beat as they please... I can go on, but in it's current state anyways, BPM is more Butt-hurt, Pain and Masochism than it's worth, unless you're into that, I won't judge... much.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr: I personally feel this game is a good example of a 75/100. I'm having fun with it and don't regret my purchase (got it on massive discount), but I feel it's held back from being amazing by a couple of "balance" issues.Firstly the good: The guns, soundtrack, magic and item systems are great. The bad: The rhythm based gameplay works great with regards to gunplay, but doesn't feel like it hits the mark with movement and enemies. Platforming is especially a chore in later levels when I frequently miss platforms because the game didn't register my second jump input. Enemy attacks and movement also feel like they're supposed to happen according to to the rhythm, but it doesn't really matter due to the fast pace of gameplay and large number of enemies in some rooms. Also the lack of invincibility frames after being hit means your whole health bar could get nuked instantly if you're caught in an unlucky spot in the middle of a mob. The weird mid 2000's "piss filter" art style also seems interesting at first, but starts grinding my gears when enemies, projectiles and items start blending into the background. There's also barely any explanation of any of the mechanics in game so prepare to jump between the game and the Wiki frequently (turn it into a minigame and see if you can do it according to the rhythm).

_childDocuments_.review: I am very much a fan of the concept behind this game, and believe that the potential here is huge. That being said, only being  actionable on quarter and eighth notes does limit that potential to a very serious degree. At first the gameplay is quite satisfying, however you quickly become accustomed to the actionable timings and crave to be able to go faster (at least I did). Having actionable timings also on 16th and even 32nd notes would be a huge improvement to the game for relatively little effort. It would mess with balance in the games current state but tying that option to a higher difficulty and scaling damage down or giving enemies more health would solve that. This change alone would allow for much more fluid gameplay and allow for more proper expression when choosing to shoot in time to song. Another solid change would be allowing players to upload their own music to play to. I understand that this may run into copyright issues, so perhaps Awe Interactive could start by giving players a database of royalty free music that they could choose from for each of the levels. Anyway they do it however, they would have to have a way for players to dictate the BPM of the song. A rudimentary way would be for each song just allow the player to enter in the BPM specifically for that song. I'm not much of a programmer so I couldn't tell you if the enemies attacks/movements etc. are each hard coded to a specific number, or if they reference a (for lack of a better word) "code word" that they can set to be a specific BPM and that changes everything accordingly in the game. Regardless, these changes would help to make gameplay more engaging and satisfying on recurring playthroughs. As it is, it's a solid game that is mostly fun to play from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of both Doom and Rhythm Heaven, I have to say that this is the exact game I've always wanted.  The gameplay and music are both fantastic.  I love the fast based gameplay, and I love the feeling of slowly learning patterns and getting better at the game.  The oversaturated artstyle isn't my cup of tea, but thankfully it can be turned down in the options menu.  The only issue I have with the game is the map, there's no way (that I could find) to get a view of the full map.  Also, map symbols mark special rooms but nothing else.  In Binding of Isaac (for example) if you left a chest in a room, it would show up as a symbol on the map and if you opened the chest, then the symbol would disappear.  In BPM, on the other hand, locked chests only show up on the map if they are in a treasure room and don't if they show up in a different room, and opening the chest doesn't remove or change the symbol.  Basically, you can't tell from a glance how many locked chests remain, which makes it harder to decide on buying a key.One other minor issue that might get better once I play the game more, none of the weapons at the blacksmith have any sort of label or stats.  I can understand stats being hidden, due to this being a roguelike, but it's annoying because I have a hard time differentiating similar looking weapons.  Something simple, like giving every weapon a name, would both improve the gameplay and add an extra cool factor to each weapon.Other than those two QOL things, this game is INCREDIBLY fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This review hurts to write. This is, at its core, a great game. but it's mired by some really frustrating flaws and challanges.to put it as it is. it's too difficult in the early game. first of on the difficulty. The early game pistol is a waste of space. it sucks in all regards. damage is pitufull, range is downright awful and the clip isn't even that much better than most other weapons you can get. As a former Binding of Isaac player, i don't think that the early weapon is something to throw away as soon as you get something that just isn't the pistol. You typically have a revolver spawn on the first level and it's a no-brainer to get it. the reload kinda sucks but it has upwards of 4x the damage on 6 shots vs 8-10. the range is also a lot better so you don't have to be in the face of an enemy to use it. the only downside is the reload, but when you kill your enemy in the first hit, how much does a slow reload matter?the very existance of better weapons makes the early pistol simply a throwaway tool you get rid of the moment you can. No matte rhow many upgrades you get, they will do you better on any different weapon than the pistol. this becomes a real problem when you either can't afford a new weapon or a weapon room/chest doesn't spawn. Flies are way too strong in this game. all the other enemies seams balanced enough, but flies will be the bane of ones existance. Not only do they take more damage than seamingly buffier looking enemies (4-5 shots by unupgraded pistol) They are also relatively small and has a very annoying "dodge" movement pattern that makes the effort of hitting them, while timing it to the beat, really awkward and quite hard. Having one enemy type in a bad state would not be an issue if this enemy type wasn't one of the most common enemies you fight, bar bats and spiders.  Spiders you can "stunlock" until they die and bats are a 1 shot kill. They also have the one thing you don't get wiht the pistol: infinite range ranged attack. Fly TLDR: very fast, small target, high Health, long ranged attack, too used.Playing without the rythm mechanic made the game feel more responsive, but flies and a few other enemy types made the game just not feel right when you are playing on "easy" on the first few levels. And without the beat mechanic then this is not a rythm game anymore.the visuals are great, but have on a few ocations hidden enemies as they can blend in with the environment (dark orange spider in a red/orange tinted darkly lit room).overall this game felt as it took the same idea that the binding of isaac did, made it into a FPS, added a rythm mechanic and said ♥♥♥♥ it with the difficulty scaling.TLDR:Feels like it tries to make the binding of isaac into and FPS and comepltely fails at the difficulty scaling.

_childDocuments_.review: A satisfying core gameplay loop and headbanging music make this a great rogue-like.  I've tried crypt of the necrodancer, but felt it was really awkward to try and navigate the inherently stuttering design.  BPM's take of a real time game that has restricted input windows feels a lot better to me.  I've had a lot of fun rocking through a dozen runs or so unlocking all the abilities on the majority of the characters and a few runs after that.  I especially love the little fanfare you shoot out on boss kills.  The one problem I have with the game is the lack of run diversity.  There are a lot of cool weapons to chase, but I feel like I go after the same 2-3 equipment every single run.  By halfway through a run you will fill all 4 equipment slots, and by the endgame you've opened enough chests that you almost 100% will have found the items you need to win.  Only your score is penalized when you take your time and equipment don't appear twice in a run so you can open almost every chest on the map and probably see the entire equipment catalog by the end.  There also isn't much class diversity, you gain a bit more after you win a few runs and unlock the baseline skills but it's still not much.  The biggest differences are starting weapons and hp/shield values.  I think making classes too difference might force a change in the core gameplay loop, which is already fantastic, so I wouldn't push for changes from the devs here.All said, if you like metal and roguelikes this is a great pick-up.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game on hard with every Valkyrie, getting every achievement, and pretty much experiencing what most of this game has to offer, I have to say this is an extremely well crafted roguelike FPS experience. I have never seen a game like this, and it is truly unique in its premise.BPM is a rhythm based action roguelike FPS game where you are thrown into a level with one of 5 Valkyries, each with their own strengths and weaknesses. You have to shoot, dodge, jump, and reload to a rhythm. Every gun in this game has their own unique sound and reload pattern, although the beats to perform actions stay consistent across the board. A really nice touch is that all the gun sounds fit PERFECTLY to the music for every stage. All guns feel very unique in the way they function and it is a lot of fun to go in and try different guns to challenge myself, rather than defaulting to the same gun again and again.The soundtrack to this game is a nice metal track, and I love metal music and I really love the music in the game, although I do get it is not everyone's cup of tea. A small issue I have with this game is that the music is the same every time per floor. Floor 1 always has the same track, floor 2 has its own track that never changes, floor 3 as well, and so on and so on. It would be nice to have some variety in the songs, although I understand it is not entirely possible as this game is fairly new.Now, let's go over the positives and negatives in this game.- Each gun in this game has their own unique sound, reload pattern, and strengths that they play to.- Music is sick- Progression is nice in this game, it can go from a mediocre run to a very solid run in just one floor if you play your cards right and RNG is on your side. (I have seen a lot of people complain about how this game is RNG based, and to that I say "it is a roguelike, you should have known what you were getting into. Binding of Isaac has RNG to it. Lots of roguelikes do. Nothing new, this is the genre, and this is why I love it)- Upgrades are consistent, you never feel underpowered when you get past floor 3, once you are done with floor 3 and go to 4, you are pretty much in the clear for a won run.- All items serve a purpose, they are all useful in their own way.- Skill progression is nice in this game. I went from getting bodied in my first 3 hours, then I got the hang of the mechanics and now I am consistently winning runs and I rarely ever take damage. I beat the game on hard without getting hit once with Odr, and that was without the extra 1 up.- Each character does not feel too different from one another other than their starting guns, with the exception of the final character Odr, who dies in one hit and has unlimited jumps and a passive "Space" modifier, making him glide in the air.- Enemy variety is not that great in this game, from floor 3 and onward you will be facing a lot of the same enemies consistently- Bosses are extremely undertuned, you can kill them almost instantly even without any upgrades, and once you do get a solid run going, they become basic common enemies who die before the cutscene ends since you can shoot during it. Health scaling to bosses based on your damage would be nice, or some sort of damage cap. - Very little boss variety, only variety they have are modifiers that are given randomly when playing on Hard mode.- Final boss is an absolute joke, and I find the 2nd floor boss to be tougher than him in all aspects. - The color palette in this game is pretty bad, it is a lot of red and yellow. Turning down the saturation is tied with the lighting, so if you turn that down you won't see much.- Tempo stays the same for all guns and levels across the board. Would be nice if it was different per gun and level. It would require me to change my firing pattern a little bit, and adapt to the level.- Coin drops are incredibly inconsistent, I would get barely any coins one floor, then the next I would get like 40 coins from the entire floor, and that is without the Midas stage modifier - Get rid of the inverted stage modifier. It does not make it engaging, it is only annoying. I know it is very rare, but imagine if you have a great run and you suddenly get slapped with inverted, messing everything up. Would suck to lose that amazing run due to something completely out of your control.- No point to do challenges in this game other than to give yourself something to do after you unlocked everything. Would be cool if you can get guns from completing challenges, or giving a character an alternate starting gun, or maybe even just skins for guns. Hopefully something like this gets added down the line, as there is no reason to do the pixel challenge other than to flex.- Key drops are also inconsistent. See my coin drop point, this applies to keys as well.- Map UI is awful. It can get very cluttered and hard to see which room connects to which. Add icons in case I missed a coin, potion, shield, or interactable in the room.- Upgrade statues blend too easily in the environment. Change the color on them or make them easier to notice as I can easily walk by one in the earlier stages.- Item descriptions are extremely vague, for example the item with the description "Mind Flay". What does that do? Would be nice if descriptions were not so vague.- Codex for guns, spells, and passives that I pick up. Also list what each stat does specifically, like precision. I know what it does, but some people might not, it would be nice if more clarification was given.I think this game is AMAZING and has serious potential. I know it is only a couple of days old at this point, and I hope it improves in a great way. This game seriously deserves more attention. I look forward to the future of BPM. This game has a lot of promise, and I can easily see myself playing this for hundreds of hours once more content gets added.

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect example of a game that has a great idea but is executed poorly consistently through all of the mechanics presented by it.This game is a combination of an FPS, rhythm game, and a rogue like, yet this game manages to make it feel like the developers have never played any game in any of those genres.- Visuals - It looks horrible. everything is orange, including enemies and pickups. You can see how this is an issue when important items and enemies attacking you blend into the background.- Music - very bland and has no impact which is especially awful since it is a rhythm game that you need to listen to the music to play.- Shooting - No impact, awful range mechanic that should never be included in a shooter and honestly a very boring selection. In a pool of fantastic recent shooters that have the mechanics to back up the need for skillful playstyles like Doom Eternal and Ultrakill, this game comes across as incredibly basic and honestly subpar in the shooter genre.- Random/Rogue - Very repetitive and samey. Unlike games like Binding of Isaac, you don't get that feeling where each playthrough is shaken up just a little bit, it feels identical and boring each time. The items are boring, the guns are boring, the rooms are boring, the randomised aspects have minor effect, are repetitive and blend into the background to the point of not being able to see them, you always have so much money it becomes trivial. Essentially everything a rogue like shouldn't do.- General issues - This game has a huge problem explaining things to the player. Guns all feel just as pathetic and you don't know what they do without buying them. Bosses are often cases where you need to take damage first to learn what their attacks do, this is because some attacks are directly linked to rhythm, so you'll be shooting at them not realising that it wants you to press dodge in exactly one telegraph. I died against the first boss about 6 times before realising that him slightly raising his arm is him saying that he will instadamage you in one second if you don't dodge in a specific way in one second. After this I killed him consistently without issue but dying multiple times while actively trying to learn why and thinking "why am I dead" is almost always due to bad game design. Consistent stuttering issues. Apparently this has been an issue since a recent major update and honestly it is absolutely appalling for a rhythm game to have any performance issues considering it is directly reliant of timing and reactions. I know this isn't a hardware issues since almost every other shooter I own doesn't have this issue and considering this game is about a bare bones as it gets, I don't think it has an excuse for any performance issues.The starting settings are awful and a lot of players won't even know that they have been put on 'idiot baby' difficulty because that is the default settings. Auto Rhythm is just patronising and many players will think that they are doing great when the game is playing itself, maybe even completing the game before realising. Since most guns reload with multiple presses of reload this will stop the player from strafing correctly when reloading since their finger is hovering over the 'R' key, This should be on the right click as a default easily. The rhythm crosshair is very distracting and every player should turn it off asap. The sensitivity is bizarrely low, even on it's max setting it is still very slow.Also people were right for the most common complaint in the reviews for this.The Fly is bad.Not only that, the game has an issue with just spawning 20 enemies in a tiny room and only having 4 hits for you health makes this tedious, especially when the first level has awful music. Another game likes to do this but has the mechanics to back up the challenging enemy spawns. Ultrakill allows the player to dash, slide, heal on melee range, knockback, parry, jump off walls, piercing attacks and kill enemies with EXPLAINED weakpoints. This game you just shoot and dash, but not only that, these are handicapped by being forced to do them to the slow rhythm. The issue isn't that this is a rhythm game, the issue is that it is a rhythm game almost entirely based around being a shooter with minimal rhythm aspects that compliment it. For example, Curse of the Necrodancer is a rhythm game set up essentially like a chess board. This works because the rhythm is meant to give the player just enough time make their next move. This game is just a subpar shooter without any thought going into the rhythm part so the rhythm aspects only act as a hindrance AKA: not fun. This also stands out when you realise the entire game sits on a 4/4 rhythm and never changes to shake things up. Necrodancer changes tempo, time signatures, musical genres and even drops notes for the player to pause on. This game made zero effort on the rhythm part of it, and since the other genres are so poorly done it makes sense why overall it feels like a heartless mess of a game.I'm glad I only spent £2 on this, only buy it if you are so bad at shooters, roguelikes and rhythm games as this one waters down all 3 genres to a point that you might enjoy floating through the nothingness it has to offer.Otherwise:Doom Eternal / Ultrakill / Dusk / Any good boomer shooter since they've grown in popularity again.Binding of Isaac / Hades / Enter the Gungeon / Good Roguelikes/lites are everywhereNecrodancer / Thumper / Guitar Hero / Literally any timing heavy game like Bayonetta or Sekiro
