_childDocuments_.review: I can't see ♥♥♥♥.By design, every level uses one color palette. Everything in it - enemies, interactables, your guns, the walls, the floor, the scenery - is all done in that one palette. Everything blends together into an unintelligible mess. The options let you reduce the saturation (to turn everything grey, I guess) or shift the colors (to turn everything blue if you want) but there's no way to make things stand out better. The last two floors at least make enemies stand out by making them red - but the shrines, chests and other interactables were even worse than before and were completely camouflaged against the background, and I only found them by accidentally bumping into them and having the interact prompt come up.Yes, yes, we get it; you're an indie dev and you want to stand out, so you put your Aesthetic(TM) above all else. Including good visual design and clear contrast of elements on the screen. It's a pity because it's mechanically sound, has a great soundtrack, and a good gameplay loop, but it's just such a visually confusing mess. It's like a colorblind mode that simulates the player being -actually- colorblind.Also, it's got Binding Of Isaac Syndrome: It's a roguelike that absolutely refuses to tell you what its items do in anything more than a 3-4 word description. Guns can be bought in the shop but unless you've used them before (AND you can recognize them at a glance) you will have no idea what they are or how they work. Is that big bulky gun a shotgun? A burst-fire rifle? A bolt-action rifle? There's no way to know ahead of time. It's similarly opaque in other areas: What makes the difficulty levels different from each other? How much do those "speed up" boots actually increase your speed? How much does a "damage up" shrine buff your damage? The game won't tell you, so you'd better hope there's a wiki somewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fun of rhythm games, and of metal/heavy music, then you can enjoy this game.However at the moment the content it has is simply too small. The assets are also not original, most are gotten from a failed game of Epic (Paragon), which makes the game feel a bit fake. The artstyle, although coherent, is not as amazing as you'd think. You get bored of 100% orange and 100% gray-green really fast. It needs some more variety...In the later stages there are some rooms that really make this a "bullet hell". The problem is, there is no indication where bullets are coming from. In top down games like Binding of Isaac etc., you see all bullets and there it is justified that bullets come from all directions. In this one, there is absolutely no indication where the enemies are, or where bullets are coming from. This is just nonsense.EDIT: But credit where credit is due, the timing system works flawlessly.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 9/10This game feels amazing to play, when you first play it is hard to tell when you need to shoot and getting on beat but when you figure it out you find one hell of a game. At least at 100% it feels a little hard to see sometimes, I play at 50% in all area's and I think it looks pretty decent, thankfully that is an option so good on the development team.Optimization: 9/10No issues honestly, game runs well, good controls, only issue is when it says press any button to start that's a lie :(Enjoyably: 9/10When you really get into the rhythm and follow the music following each beat or half beat the game becomes amazing, I wouldn't call this a Doom clone at all but this game gives me the same euphoria of hearing epic music tied in with great gameplay, I won't mention much about the game because it's a good experience to have with some nice speakers, only issue I had was some upgrade stations can be hard to see and the game does not really have a tutorial but those are very minor issues in the grand scheme.Music/Sound: 10/10If the game was not based on actions on the beat I would have maybe put this section at an 8/10 but because you do all your actions on beat it makes me appreciate this soundtrack even more, even if you are not gonna buy the game at least take a listen to the soundtrack and give it a second chance. Overall: 8.8/10This is an amazing game, the visuals can be a turn off for some people but especially if you like music, fast paced shooters or rougelites then I 100% recommend buying this game and the soundtrack, if not just listen to the sound track it's really good, the first chamber music is stuck in my head HELP!

_childDocuments_.review: BPM: Bullets Per Minute is a rhythm First Person Shooter, yes I have never heard of such a thing before either.So what do you get if you cross a dungeon based FPS with a heavy rock sound track? You get BPM.The main gimmick of the game, and what sets it apart from other similar dungeon based FPS, of which there are a few, is that everything you do, whether that is firing your weapon, jumping, dodging an enemy, you try to do it to the beat of the music that is playing, if you shoot on a beat, then that shot is more powerful. Get the jist?Each dungeon is randomly generated, and are chock full of monsters, each more bizarre than the last, the end game is to kill everyone and take out the boss, and all to a wonderful rock soundtrack that literally will help or hinder your abilities. Of course there is a setting that allows you to enable auto beat matching, but that seems a bit pointless when that is the main gimmick of the game.There are 7 bosses and then a final boss to beat, there are lots of weapons to collect, abilities to gain, and so on. You play as one of 5 choosable characters, each with their own strengths and weaknesses.The GoodAn interesting gimmick for what is a tired genre, does make it interesting. The music is great.The BadAs seems to often by the case, the controls could be better, when designing any game, if you don't get the controls perfect, everything else suffers. I was also not a fan of the graphics. I understand that they are going for a certain style here, but I found the graphics to be bland and uninspiring.SummaryIf Dungeon based FPS are your thing, and you want a different challenges to what you are used to, then I am sure you will enjoy this game. Personally I come to any game as a newbie, I look at the game as if I have never played this type of game before, and I decide how much it grabs me, and unfortunately this game to me is lacking.I score BPM: Bullets Per Minute a 6/10I recommend this game to fans of Dungeon based FPS but perhaps not to those who are not fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: For 20 dollars, it needs a bit of work. It's a wonderful experience at first glance. The gunplay feels good most of the time, and the rhythm mechanic works perfectly in this space. However there are several key issues I have with the game that makes it kind of lacking. For example, some items appear to be far superior to others. ie. spacewalker vs angel boots. Also, the "blessings" which are a key component to how your character gets stronger seem heavily stacked to favor certain weapons and abilities over others. ie. clip upgrade on minigun. The Ability stat seems to have no effect on some abilities. The critical mechanic relies on being able to shoot each specific enemies "weak point." For some enemies, the weak point is a glowing part on their model, but for others it's either much harder to find, or non-existent.  This makes crit items, as well as the "Precision" stat utterly useless in some situations. Sometimes when entering a level, a random modifier can be applied to the level. This can mean changes to the gravity or slippery floors. However, the "Barren" modifier make it so that no loot seems to drop on the level at all. In a game where becoming more powerful is very necessary on hard mode, getting a "Barren" modifier on the first level can ruin your run right off the bat. There seems to be no reward for clearing the barren level either. I've played many hours of "Binding of Issac" so perhaps I am a bit biased towards perfection, but this game still features many typos on the item names.Overall a fun game for the first few hours, but not worth 20 dollars in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty much my favorite roguelike of all time, It is a completely unique and unexpected blend of so many elements: A roguelike rhythm based Nordic mythology themed first person shooter. The composers deserve a goddang medal for the incredibly catchy soundtrack that all but makes speedruns impossible as you can't resist dancing along to it. The combat is simple to pick up and fast paced but it also allows you to spend hours trying new combinations of weapons and items. The developers clearly have a passion for rhythm and sound as everything in the game seems to mesh perfectly with the soundtrack. Not even shopkeepers and bosses can resist moving along! One of the most striking things about this game is the stylized coloring. Its a bold move and definitely turns a lot of people off but i personally love it as it adds a very memorable tone to each area as you progress. I love the different characters and the unique challenges they bring to a run (I suck too much to beat Odr).Pretty much the only criticism i can think of for this game is that more often than not, boss fights are defeated in seconds sometimes even before their introduction banner ends! This is especially disappointing as the boss fights tend to have very fun attack patterns, songs and animations that we often don't get to see much of. I hope that they can find a way to balance boss fights to make them last at least a little longer in the future. Otherwise, I absolutely cannot wait to see what the devs do next! BPM 2? a different game? we can only wait and see!10/10 EXTREMELY worth the $20 price tag (practically highway robbery)

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw BPM, I wrote it off. It creates a VERY satisfying gameplay loop that ends up working quite well in-tandem with shooter mechanics.Keeping on the beat while having to dodge, aim, and reload tactfully is a very unique gameplay style, and I find it really entertaining. _childDocuments_.review: The music is great, and moving to the beat is an awesome idea that they make work. I don't like the graphics, it's not bad quality, it just looks washed out.  I know it's on purpose, but I think that was a mistake by the devs.  OK, on to the gameplay and why I enjoy this game:At first I hated it. Then I realized that's because I'm spoiled by other games.  It's tough and unforgiving for a few reasons.  There is progression, but not in the usual way. Stuff you pick up on a run disappears when you die and start a new run.  You have to do every action to the beat (except jump) or it doesn't work.  Enemies can shoot you from across the room, but you have to get close.  Enemies can hide behind pillars, but their shots go right through, so you can't.  There's a variety of flavors to the dungeons, and it usually just makes it harder for you, like flashlight mode, or ice mode where it's harder to control movement.You can eventually unlock new characters.  You can store some money in the bank. You can unlock more options from merchants.  That's about it for "progression".  It makes each game feel totally fresh, but also not completely rewardless.You start over and over each time you die, to a new random setup.  Sometimes banks and stores are available, sometimes they're not.  I wouldn't say this is for the hardcore gamer, because it's not overly super challenging for no reason.  It's also not for the super casual who wants easy -peasy games full of crutches where they don't have to aim and get all kinds of freebies (those get boring quick!).  I really like it because as you get better, you get better.  Not because you start with the same crutches you picked up earlier, but because you're actually getting better.  Each time is a totally fresh run, like you were playing at an old-school coin arcade.  It's fun and challenging, but not too hardcore.  You can sink 5 minutes, or hours into each playthrough.  Think of Doom but you've gotta keep the beat.  Want to learn to dance in Covid, and you like blasting monsters?  Try this!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr It's just okay.There's just not enough difficulty during the boss fights. Anyone who's played more than five hours of this game knows that rooms with 3 or 4 bats or flies as well as grounded melee enemies are infinitely more difficult than any of the bosses or the noids they spawn. This is mostly due to how boss fight HP scales linearly. You out-scale that DPS check really quickly. You will finish off most bosses in the latter half of the game within seconds of entering the boss chamber, simply because the amount of items you're able(and likely) to have isn't accounted for.As well as more frequent attacks, they should do them more correlating to their specific theme. If there are dynamic music cuts to play the right part of the song for their specific chamber and intro/mid-combat/outro sequences, I'm sure coding in the bosses attacking with the changes in instrumentation can't be that hard.Character design is heavy handed. Some characters feel overtuned and flying off the rails at all phases of the game, where as the design of others is just poorly done and unfun. There's a lot of pointless open space in the game that just doesn't need to be there, you just have to go for it Chekhov's Gun style. No more of this "big ass open space above the centre of a room with nothing there". The single most comparable game would be Crypt Of The Necrodancer, and yet the game takes no pages out of its book in terms of subversion of the game's original concept; It should try and do something other than just 'click to basically the exact same tempo for 15 - 30 minutes'.Solid game. Banging soundtrack, good sound design for most of the guns. Satisfying rogue-like elements and loop... But, BPM is just missing any sort of pizzazz to really reiterate on that foundation.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's been out for barely three days at the time of this review and I already have over 30 hours on it.Definitely recommend it, really fun to play and run! Gets to a point where the ability and shooting restrictions are just natural and don't even feel them. It may even feel too easy, until you get to the last unlock.Some items are OP combined with other guns, and there's some ways to cheese the bosses really easily but they're already working on a patch for that.The soundtrack is great, while running I'm sometimes sad that I don't get to listen to more of it.After you complete your first run you unlock more characters, each have different stats and playstyles so that adds replay value, and each are fun in their unique way. The last unlock will keep you busy for a long time, that's for sure!For a game made essentially by only two developers, this feels like a really polished experience with a few overlooks that are already in the way of being fixed. If it's not your type of game, I'd get it even if it was just for the soundtrack! _childDocuments_.review: BPM is an incredibly tough rhythm FPS roguelite and the first rhythm FPS I know of. Since its release the rhythm action genre has exploded with the likes of Hi-Fi Rush, Metal: Hellsinger and, recently, Robobeat. And while this game certainly is unique even within its genre, it has a general feel that invokes the feeling of an early access indie title, despite its finished state.This is a game I'm quite conflicted on but I'll still give an overall recommendation. The gunplay can be somewhat loose and the overall visuals are... Garish, to put it in a word, which can make it hard to identify enemies from the environment. What BPM does have is an incredibly diverse range of weapons to use, each of which having their own rhythms, even when reloading, alongside a killer soundtrack (despite every song having the same BPM).Overall, BPM laid the foundations for later titles to improve upon. It's still worth a play but I'd take Hellsinger or Robobeat over this myself.

name: Ship of Fools
detailed_description: Ship of Fools is a seafaring roguelite co-op game where you play the Fools, the only creatures fool enough to brave the sea. The Great Lighthouse that once protected the Archipelago is broken and a storm of malice and corruption is coming. Together, you and your ship mate will jump aboard The Stormstrider and make your voyage across the sea. Man the cannons, ready your sails and protect your ship from sea monsters over multiple runs. It’s up to you to defend your home from the almighty Aquapocalypse. In a clamshell, Ship of Fools is a game about blasting away your seaborne foes with mighty cannons as you defend your ship. Inspired by modern classic roguelites and built for co-op, you’ll want to bring your first mate on deck and enjoy oarsome combat as you unlock new trinkets and artifacts to help you save the world from catastrophe. Designed for co-op play, frantic combat encounters with the horrifying creatures of the storm will test your teamwork. Work together to defend and repair the ship, combine item effects in powerful combos and make sure you have your shipmate’s back if you don’t want to become fish food. Uncover lost treasures and remote shops on the islands of the Archipelago, but plan your moves carefully! As you chart your way through the sector, the Everlasting Storm shifts and changes, blocking your paths with its fury. You’ll need to adjust your course in reaction to storm movements and decide when you can brave a trip to discover what lurks inside the storm. Man your ship as a solo sailor and fight your way through dangerous waters and keep the glory for yourself, Ship of Fools offers solo play as well as multiplayer. As they sing in old sailor songs: it’s sometimes better to have no crew than a dysfunctional one! With many Fools to play with, unique items to find and unlock, combat encounters to fight in and many islands to visit, each run will bring something new to your voyage. Bolster your strength each time, ready to defeat the monsters of the deep sea. Key Features Frantic nautical combat with another shipmate in co-op or as a solo sailor Colossal leviathans to challenge the hardiest of sailors Chart your route through the maps of the Archipelago and brave the Everlasting Storm Embody one of the unique Fools with special abilities to help you on your journey 100+ trinkets and artifacts to collect and combo for winning strategies Swashbuckling hand-drawn artwork to put the wind in your sails Please note: A controller is required for local multiplayer

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game to play online with friends. It is really fun, but has a major issue that makes it unplayable online: if either player loses internet connection, the game abruptly ends without saving progress. So if you've been playing a run for 40 minutes, and your internet lags for a bit, the game ends and sends you back to the main screen without saving your progress.I hope the devs can find a better way to handle low connectivity (like "pausing" the game until the player with bad internet can get back on), but in it's current state you would be lucky to ever be able to play it without getting abruptly disconnected. I've never had any other games just end like this when someone's connection gets a little slow.

_childDocuments_.review: It makes me so sad how much this game could have felt better. But before that let me share my experience in this game.  Ship of Fools is a rogue-lite in which you play as a fool (or fools) who tries to bring light back to the Archipelago. This game has unique ideas and really good execution behind it. It is one of the best co-op games I have ever played. And playing it with a friend (my brother in my case) feels amazing. The game loop consists of 2 phases. First, you need to decide which way you want to go. The seamap consists of tiles and you can move one of the tiles next to your position. You can prioritize going toward cannons, trinkets, gold, artifacts, shops, curses, …etc or you can go directly toward the boss. After moving the chosen tile you need to kill hordes of enemies. Fights are tricky because you need to defend the ship, reload the cannons, and kill the enemies simultaneously. This causes so much panic and managing it is one of the funniest parts of the game. Also, you will find temporary trinkets, ammos, and artifacts throughout the game. Some of those items are cursed and you need to consider the cons and pros well. Also, it's really fun to shoot ammo that deals 35x damage but moves like a turtle. When your ship sinks, you return to the aisle and can upgrade your gear and open new items for further runs.It took 5 tries to kill the final boss and these first 5 runs made me fall in love with the game.Then we learned we need to finish it at least 15 times more to actually beat the game. My brother said who the ♥♥♥♥ is going to finish this game 15 times. Then we decided on 1 or 2 more runs and we were done here but we finished it more than 25 times and achieved 100%. How did this happen? Well, let me explain what happens when you finish the game first. It contains minor spoilers so don’t read the rest if you care.When you beat a run, the light level increases and this provides a buff to the enemies and opens new items for us. I won't spoil the buffs but the game becomes at least 10 times harder throughout the game. The biggest problem is over-repetition. There are 4 bosses in the game and you need to kill the same bosses at each run. As the light level increases, bosses do not gain new abilities, or new bosses are not added to the game. And that’s what I mean by the game wasting its potential. Even though the gameplay is so fun and carries the rest of the game, game content repeats itself so much. If it added new bosses or gave new skills to the existing bosses and added new enemies with the increased light levels, this game could have felt much much better and could have been 10/10All in all, although I think the game falls short of its potential, I really had fun playing it and I recommend it to those who look for a unique and remarkable co-op experience. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Animated trailer, custom song, amazing look...  at this point, I'm 100% expecting to be disappointed by such games. But oh, the concept was so enthralling. Made for 2 player coop. Sea-themed. Silliness mixed with badassery. It seemed perfect for myself and a certain friend of mine... So we decided to give it a go.It lives up to the trailer. Hell, it  it. But there are a few caveats. There is no online matchmaking. Come with a friend or not at all (even if you can, technically, play solo). We played online, and never had an issue - not once; it's possible to play locally, though. And you can play with exactly one person - you can't bring your crew, only one friend. As far as roguelikes go, the twist of having exactly two players allows for some interesting design choices. A lot of stuff is happening at the same time - and the game WILL punish you for getting in each other's way. You can't clip through each other, and of course your melee attacks will interrupt and even stun the other player... so a certain level of trust is absolutely necessary. Especially since there is usually no time to communicate about split-second things such as deflecting projectiles.I find the difficulty particularly interesting. The game's rather hard, but also... not really? If that makes any sense? There's a lot of stuff that can sink your ship incredibly fast, especially later on. Endgame bossfights have some hard to avoid stuns, and if both players get hit at the same time it's almost guaranteed game over; you WILL lose runs to these moments.And yet, once you understand the when and the what, once you get comfortable with deflecting and firefighting, once you develop some unspoken rules with your crewmate... the difficulty slowly melts away. The keyword here is 'slowly'; beating the game once is not enough to truly win, and you'll be presented with a nice ladder of ever-increasing challenges. And it's a very nicely paced ladder.As you go, you unlock new trinkets, artifacts, cannons, ammo types, characters. There's a quite nice selection, but this isn't Risk of Rain 2. These ruinous combos of ungodly power simply don't exist here. There are some items that break the game under certain circumstances, but the, uh, interaction chains are pretty short. So the POWER items do all the heavy lifting while the other ones are just... there. That sucks a little.You know what doesn't suck? The music. It's fantastic. I feel like this game is good in general, but it's the music that pushes it into amazing territory. Every boss has its own theme that progresses as you enter further and further phases. The soundscape is pretty great as well; some fights encourage listening for audio tells for better clarity during the fight. It's not necessary though - it just helps.Look. The game's good. It's probably better than you think. And it's still receiving some updates, plus some minor things in DLC. If you have someone that you'd see yourself playing this with, don't sleep on it. Great time all around.

_childDocuments_.review: You want to play something with your significant other? This is a game you might try.Our ship has sunk and the sea washes us back to our island. Again. Well, it is a roguelite action game, so every run is supposed to end where it started... at the Great Lighthouse. It is situated on a tiny island, sourrounded by sea monsters and inhabited by just a few people. Most things on this island are destroyed and abandoned. Your job, of course, is to rebuild it to its former glory, to bring back the missing population, rebuild the infrastructure while upgrading your warship.I came to play the game with my wife. And I kept playing with her. Playing it alone is difficult, maybe not impossible, but difficult. This is the game that I hoped the rather disappointing Trash Sailors: Co-Op Trash Raft Simulator would be. You are on a boat and have to defend it in melee and with cannons, bringing ammo to the cannons, carrying the cannons to the best shooting position, repairing the ship when it is damaged. Foes can come from port and starboard, so you always have to defend on two sides, which makes playing alone hard, even though you are granted an automatic cannon in single player. Using your harpoon to fetch ressources from the sea, using your oars to smash intruders on the ship, charging your melee attack to return enemy projectiles back to sender, using planks to repair damage to the ship, bringing ammo to the cannons... there are a few time critical things to do during combat, good cooperation with the second player helps a lot to survive. Steering the boat is not required - you just sail from one location to the next, always stopping on the new location until the enemies are defeated. Most of the time this is a fight where you have to kill all enemies, but there are also traders, islands with random items to snatch up or other surprises. Like in a typical roguelike, you sail from encounter to encounter until you are defeated and wash up at the starting island, losing most stuff you have collected. The maps are of course randomized, an icon showing what you expect at the next stop.Meta progression is rather slow. When your ship sinks you will wash up on the beach empty-handed (except a tendril or two), losing all the fancy equipment you found during the run. There are a few people to rescue on your runs, they might help you on the island in return. A few permanent upgrades can be bought back at home with the tendrils.  You can upgrade your weapons (after rescuing the smith) or go to old Halga for her magic soup improving some starting conditions for the next run (more money, harpoons, better ship armor). Cool roguelite designed for two players. Build a mighty ship and explore the sea to avert the Aquapocalypse.

_childDocuments_.review: Update June 22, 2024Decided to update my review after playing through the updates and getting all of the Steam achievements. New characters, ships, trinkets, artifacts, and game modes have been added since my previous review.Characters: Lotte and Krillstoph are all I need. Can only recommend the DLC characters if you want achievements.Ships: I enjoyed being able to swap between ships with their different play styles.1) Stormstrider: Base Ship. Decent cargo space; sad starting ammo. The artifact can repel the storm.2) Wavehulk: The best ship. The Foundry can transform a trinket into an artifact, basically duplicating it for the team in co-op. Combine it with the duplication pool after the second boss for extra fun. The starting ammo is serviceable.3) Siren's Call: A pretty ship. I found this ship to be the most difficult to use inn co-op as it has the least cargo space. The starting artifact can recycle items, but there's so many items in the pool that I didn't find the ability to recycle that amazing. Most of the time I recycled something sad into something sadder. The starting ammo has some fun random effects but not much damage.4) Red Scourge: Not as daunting as it seems. This ship isn't repaired with wooden planks. The starting artifact acts as a single shield and will make the ship immune to damage for a brief period once it's hit. If a tendril isn't inserted to activate the artifact after you get hit, the next hit will end your run. I actually didn't have a hard time clearing Brightness 15 difficulty with this ship. The starting ammo is pretty good.Trinkets/Artifacts:Some of these things shouldn't exist; they're just there to pad out the pool.Someone posted a trinket tier list on reddit that you can use for reference. I disagree with some of the rankings, though. The Light Purse, Drill, Spring, Powder and Fan trinkets are all great curse rewards. I've done the most damage by duplicating the purse and drill. I really enjoyed the addition of the Holy Artifacts that you get by exchanging items that the Sirens want.Game Modes:1) Brightness: Adds a little bit of difficulty to the game...just a little. Brightness 15 wasn't that hard on any of the four ships. What I did  like was the forced "replayability." You need to unlock the brightness levels one run at a time. Every run remains the same. Pick the same character(s), try to get the same items, fight the same fights.The co-op is very stable now. I didn't experience any issues during the additional 25 hours I put in. I would recommend this game for people looking for something cute, cozy, and casual in co-op. Maybe wait for the DLC to go on sale.------------------------I was holding off on writing a review for this game, because I thought this game had potential and wanted to wait for an update to see if there would be some quality of life updates and new content. Unfortunately after the most recent update, I can no longer recommend this game unless it has a significant markdown. What it is now is basically an early-early access game.With the release of 1.0.2, I no longer want to play this game. It didn’t have much content before, but I’d still play a game or two (either single-player or co-op) a day because it was fun. Not only have the devs not added new content or fixed major problems like multiplayer connectivity issues and lack of progression saves, they actually removed “exploits” and nerfed things that made the game less tedious to play. Seriously, you’re not adding anything that will get existing/old players to come back and you’re simultaneously removing the fun experiences new players could have had. Maybe these changes were an attempt to increase the difficulty to increase playtime but now I just dread the idea of playing this at all. It’s really sad since I was leaning towards recommending this game at one point.If you don’t mind a tedious grind and lack of content or if you’re just looking for a co-op roguelike with an interesting concept, then totally give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a quick heads up, as of time of writing this, there's not too much content and the game balancing is abysmal. HOWEVER, this game is an absolute ton of fun. Going in as co-op, it feels like Overcooked on a pirate ship. If that sounds like a blast to you, then you'll get some good enjoyment out of this. I'll specify what I meant in my first statement, but if you're looking for a general rating, a very solid 6/10 in its current state.Content Problems:There are currently 3 stages (technically 4, but the last one is just a boss). Each stage's boss is entirely predetermined, nor do the stages cycle between a roster of bosses. After you beat the game, there's a quick cutscene, and that's about it. There's no additional scaling, harder difficulties, endless mode, nothing to really add some spice once you've done it once or twice.Game Balancing:(AS OF JAN 18, THIS HAS BEEN PATCHED AND IS NO LONGER APPLICABLE) Charge shot is objectively the best cannon in all of co-op. Since there's no restriction on how much ammo can be loaded into the cannon by your co-op friend while you charge it, you can literally one shot entire bosses if you stuff enough ammo into the cannon. This is especially true for the final boss, which has tons of dead time in between damage phases for you to prep another volley of death. My friend and I literally don't know what the boss's attack patterns are because we've killed it immediately after it spawned. Also, many of the artifacts (the ones that are placed on the ship) are entirely useless in comparison to others. For example, why would I want an artifact that gives my ship +3 health, when I can save that same amount of health by getting +50% projectile damage and killing everything before I take that damage? Why would I build into eggs when it requires at least 2 artifacts to be good when I can, again, get +100% projectile damage, thereby getting the same output without the inconsistency of waiting for eggs. (AS OF JAN 18, SOME CHARACTERS WERE NERFED, SO THIS IS LESS APPLICABLE) Characters are also very off. While many of the characters have niche innate trinkets (which are occasionally useful), Krillstoph (1-2 melee combo) and Shelbie (loaded cannons bonus speed, damage, and fire rate) are so unbelievably universally good that there's no reason to take any of the other characters.Conclusions:While this game has some serious flaws as listed above, it's got so much potential, a vivid soundtrack, great artstyle, exciting gameplay, wonderful humor, and an excellent loop, I truly pray that the devs have more work planned for this game. To leave it in it's current state would be an absolute travesty, and I sincerely look forward to what the future might hold.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and unique, boasting an excitingly new system of gameplay.The introduction is abruptly paced and overall this experience doesn't have a particularly interesting story or lore. The game compensates for this with excellently polished visual and sound design, which makes up much of the lasting impression.The process of fighting enemies and defending the ship is very engaging and snugly crafted. It definitely has room for some more diversifying mechanics but the core system is quite compelling and distinctive. There's a significant amount of variety to the unlocks, characters and items; although the enemy, area and boss diversity is unfortunately lacking. The game maintains a relatively fair and consistent level of challenge, although the higher difficulties do occasionally throw out waves of enemies that are impossible to safely counter without a strong build. The general gameplay and expansive difficulty modifiers help to keep the experience enjoyable over an extended period of time. While a constant cycle of decision making and build development cultivates an engaging loop of gameplay.The game is relatively functional in both cooperative and solo play, although playing with another individual particularly highlights that the experience could use some additional basic mechanics to deepen the gameplay flow. In solo play combat is more frantic and thus can become much more engaging by comparison. Conversely it's very easy for players to get in each other's way during cooperation, which does place emphasis on coordination at least.A unique and fun experience, although it lacks content variety in some regards the game remains quite enjoyable and replayable after a variety of solid updates.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: Ship of Fools is a roguelite co-op game where you play as, you guessed it, fools! The Great Lighthouse that once protected the lands has broken and a storm of corruption is brewing. You must take your ship and voyage across the sea, defending against sea monsters and more. Chart your way across a procedurally-generated map and upgrade your ship to hopefully have a successful voyage. With trinkets, artifacts, and co-op play, you and a friend will get to figure out the best way to make it to the other side.Personally, I am having a field day with Ship of Fools. It is a ton of fun and I can see myself playing it more and more on Deck. I am a sucker for roguelikes and co-op games that I can bring a friend over and just have a good time with, this is one of those games. While the game is definitely playable, it isn't as playable as I would have expected it to be based on the artstyle and type of game, but it can be.Ship of Fools, without any changes or caps, tends to hover around 43-44 FPS in general with a 16-18W drain. I found that really odd since I established no caps, but the game automatically did it. But, I found that with a TDP of 10 and GPU Frequency of 1200, the drain stuck a bit lower and was stable most of the time. There are some areas where the game will slow down a bit, like in the hub area before going on the ship, but when fighting, the game stuck around 40 and felt good. There were also some little stutters here and there, but they were small and nothing that interfered with the action of the game.I felt that, while I did enjoy 40 FPS's smoothness, 30 FPS just felt better overall for the game. Not only was it more stable, but added an extra hour and a half to the battery. I was also able to bring TDP down to 7 comfortably and felt no drops or stuttering at all. That stability wins out in my eyes.The reason why Ship of Fools is rated a 4 instead of a 5 here is due to some of those oddities when uncapped, as well as the 30 FPS cap. The game stopping itself from going over, lack of graphical options, and some framerate drops went to that score. I would love to see an expansion of the options or at least the ability to change the window mode from fullscreen to windowed. This will allow me to lower the resolution and use FSR, which could help stability with 40 a bit more. I felt that this type of game should be able to play at a higher rate based on how it isn't as heavy a game as, lets say, Spider-Man, but it performs around the same framerate wise.I did also talk with the developer about this and they will be looking into support. I have also extended any way I can assist as I do believe this is a great game hindered by something that can be solved easily compared to deeper logical issues.Overall, I am having a lot of fun with Ship of Fools. Regardless of the performance issues, the game does hold 40 at the most important parts and is genuinely a fun game to play, but the 30 stability and battery makes this wonderful. With friends, this is definitely a wonderful game to play and have. If you are going to be fine with 40 with minor drops or a stable 30, and want a fantastic co-op experience, this will be the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: The beauty of Ship of Fools lies in its frantic co-op combat. It's a constant dance of firing cannons, dodging attacks, and maneuvering your ship in perfect sync with your partner. Think of it as ballet on the high seas, only instead of tutus, you've got blunderbusses. While the learning curve is fair, mastering this teamwork tango is key to surviving the ever-increasing waves of nightmarish sea creatures, from hulking krakens to mischievous gremlin swarms.But fear not, ye scurvy landlubbers! Ship of Fools throws you a diverse cast of playable characters, each with unique abilities that cater to different playstyles. From the nimble acrobat to the demolitionist flinging explosive surprises, there's a perfect "fool" for every pirate wannabe. Plus, the open seas are procedurally generated, meaning no two adventures are the same. You'll be charting new waters (and dodging krakens) with every playthrough.And the best part? Death, that ol' sea hag, doesn't have the last laugh. Sure, you'll get sent back to port after each run, but you'll unlock new trinkets, powerful artifacts, and permanent upgrades for your ship. Experimenting with these and customizing your vessel adds a fantastic layer of strategic depth, keeping the roguelike loop deliciously addictive.Now, all this swashbuckling wouldn't be complete without a feast for the senses. Ship of Fools boasts a hand-drawn art style that's as vibrant and charming as a mermaid's song. Even amidst the chaotic battles, the visuals are a delight. And let's not forget the soundtrack! Sea shanties and orchestral pieces perfectly complement the swashbuckling atmosphere, keeping your adrenaline pumping as you conquer the waves.So, mateys, if you're looking for a thrilling co-op adventure that blends action, strategy, and a healthy dose of humor, Ship of Fools is a treasure chest overflowing with fun. Just be prepared to get a little (or a lot) soaked, and maybe pack some Dramamine for your co-pilot – these seas can get mighty rough!

_childDocuments_.review: It's good! The price tag is a bit high, but I think this is one of the rare roguelikes that deserves it. Atmosphere:The artwork is excellent, animations are satisfying and really makes the goofy nature of the characters shine through. There's a bit of witty humor, and some one-liners that made me and my friend laugh out loud. Gameplay/Bugs:I loved the moment to moment gameplay, but I definitely had a few bugs. I recall having a run-ending bug on the final boss, which was really frustrating. I think that the gameplay was good enough that I could forgive most of the bugs I had, though. It's really satisfying working together with your partner, and there is never a shortage of things to do onboard. At first I was disappointed this was only 2 players, but I think any more chaos would be too much.  The bosses have cool, unique attack patterns that get you to learn and it's really satisfying getting good at playing around them. Upgrades feel satisfying, there are some special interactions at the end of each zone that really up the fun (and potential for nutty builds), and it feels like a really good pacing of power and difficulty.That being said, I think this game would benefit a lot from maybe 2 more stages, and some more breadth to the content you can experience. I could definitely see some updates on this game in the future that could make this game go from a 7/10 to a 10/10 (for any devs who might see this):More boss variety (I don't want to fight the exact same stage 1 boss each time)More item variety (really go nuts! make something where we can fly around with a paddle or something temporarily. Shoot for the moon, seriously I'd love some diversity)Ships are great! No notesMaybe even just 1 more stage. The ending felt a smidge rushedMore question mark tiles, similar to slay the spire. The worst feeling in a run-based roguelike is feeling like you have a lot of "plain" tiles you have to traverse. Even if they introduced some balance variations, I think the diversity of gameplay this would add is worth itShops could be a little more rewarding with the breadth of selection. Had more than a few times where it felt like a waste of time to include it in my routeTLDR: Give it a shot, a well polished game that could use a little more content. IT IS ONLY 2 PLAYER (I didn't know)

_childDocuments_.review: This game used to be much better than what is it after the first content update. You used to be able to play the game without it feeling like doing the same thing but made more impossible. Take this scenario for example: you have gone out of your way to get an item from the new siren's quests, but you seem to be stupid and tried to manage the new lighthouse tiers, and your on tier 6. The item is destroyed upon taking 3 damage, and you get to the first little area of the edge. Tier 6 does the following: 1. Raises the health of enemies by 50%2. Makes some enemies attack faster (no specific percent)3. Makes some enemies have DOUBLE health4. Makes some waves spawn higher health enemies in harder formations5. Makes an enemy projectile a "crit", making it deal damage instantly upon hitting the ship, along with the damage that comes afterwards from the base projectileYou are presented with the highest health non-boss enemy in the game at the bottom of the screen, which summons two other tanky enemies in front of it which will come to your ship and detonate after about 5 seconds. Along with that, the main enemy is SHIELDED, meaning that the enemy has a grand total of 900 health, giving it more than half the health of most bosses in the game. This isn't the only enemy though, as 5 enemies that shoot projectiles are spawned above you, which also instantly shoot a projectile upon being killed. The bottom enemy summons its goons, and one of them is lucky and gets what seems to be a 50% boost to the speed of its attack, meaning it is de-synced with the other one. It explodes, deals some damage to both the item and your ship, then the other one attacks nearly 2 seconds later. The item is basically on life support at this point, and the projectile enemies are attacking at the same time as this. They hit the ship, the item explodes and your damage halves while the enemy at the bottom is in pristine condition. You slog through this, losing half the health you had before, then move on. Later down the line in the area, a "boarder wave" appears, which just shovels about 20 boarder enemies onto your ship at once, which all go to a side of the ship and attack. The thing about the boarders in the third area is that they both put down a fire AND stun you, making it so you can't put out the rapidly spreading fire. You die to something out of your control. Doesn't that just sound fun? God you need to test EVERYTHING before sending an update out.Edit: I have a skill issue. Sorry for writing an essay about how your game sucks! The new update is fun and the crits are fixed. Play this game!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; It's cute and has a fun premise, but unfortunately in its current state, I don't recommend this game.- Gorgeous art design and animation- Fun core gameplay loop. It's fun to run around the ship with a friend, swapping cannons, grabbing ammo, harpooning supplies, etc.- Local and online co-op is beyond welcome. I'm starved for these kinds of games, really.- Limited options. No way to adjust difficulty. When paused during gameplay, there are NO option menus at all - just continue and quit. If you want to change the resolution or do any maintenance, you have to quit to the main menu to do it.- There is no option to "start over" with a fresh save. I booted it up for the first time and tried it for a bit before playing with my wife. Got partway through the tutorial, decided it was good, and quit out. I figured I'd just restart and do the tutorial from scratch with her. But the crazy thing is, not only was I stuck with the first playthrough - the game actually discretely marked the whole tutorial as finished, even though I stopped halfway through it. Since I couldn't restart the game, I couldn't replay the tutorial. So my wife got zero training, and I got half of what I needed. - It feels like half a game. It's not in early access, which makes this all the more frustrating. You have a hub island that you can wander around, and we enjoyed spending time there. We knew there'd be a lot of sailing, but we also assumed we'd get chances to disembark and explore islands between the sailing segments. Granted, we only played about an hour, but we got through a full map and tried to diversify the tiles we traversed. The only islands we saw were tiny with a single vendor or chest to open. Part of the reason we expected more is that the sailing itself is very simplistic. In fact, mechanically you don't actually have anything to do with the sailing aspect, apart from choosing where you'll go. The rest of the time, you're shooting or whacking monsters. To make a comparison, Lovers in a Dangerous Spacetime also confines co-op players to a single shared vessel, but someone is in charge of steering. You're actually exploring the regions you're in. Whether in the ship or on foot, we'd hoped there was more to the game than just the anchored gunplay, but that really is about it, more or less.Runs okay on Steam Deck, but with some major caveats. I know it's currently marked as "Unsupported" so I'm sure the devs are already aware of the problems it has on there, but if anyone else is like me and curious to see if it's one of those games that still works, just "unofficially," it DOES work... but it's glitchy. In handheld solo mode, it seems fine. But plugged into the Steam Deck Dock and my TV, I ran into the following issues:- The game freezes on its opening logos. Switch to handheld and it boots up just fine, then you can re-dock it and it continues working.- The frame rate is rough.- Audio drops out constantly.- Text is borderline unreadable- Screen is stuck with a thick black border, so the picture only takes up about 3/4 of the TV's screen.I'm sure with time it'll get fixed, but for now, Steam Deck buyers beware.In short, I really like the core of this game and expected a bit more than I got. In its current state, it feels like a fantastic recipe that's just undercooked. I requested a refund for now, but I will still be following the game just to see if it ever "gets its sea legs" and becomes a more stable, polished, and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun roguelite when played with a friend. The game revolves around managing your limited cargo space, moving and loading and shooting cannons, and using your paddle to knock melee enemies away and deflect projectiles. The gameplay loop is very fun, and I cannot recommend it enough.The game does have some issues in my opinion. Those being the varied difficulties of various enemy encounters, solo scaling, and the final boss. Some enemy encounters are easily dealt with in seconds, but others feel almost impossible to go through without taking damage. I don't expect each encounter to be the exact same difficulty-wise - that would be unfun - but the level of variance is a bit high in my taste. Playing the game solo is possible, but it does not feel balanced for solo play. The game gives you an automatic sentry cannon, but playing defense is impossible at points where you need to defend multiple spots across your entire ship with a single character. The final boss was a bit of a let down as it stands - each of the other bosses have unique attacks, but the final boss just moves around and summons enemies.Don't let what I said dissuade you, this game is amazing and feels like something Klei would make. I highly recommend playing this incredibly unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: First time changing a review, so I'm keeping the previous (negative) post below.  I always loved the core concept of the game.  And the most recent update added A LOT to the game; specifically the end game.  There are numerous modifiers that scale up the difficulty of each run (Think Hades and the Pact of Punishment). I have thoughts on the balance of the modifiers, but it has inserted a level of challenge to the game that has been lacking for a long time.   Moreover, there is very little ability to build up your next run. You can only pick your "Fool" based on their abilities.  This leads to only a few "Fools" ever being picked; I do hate that Lotte is basically required for solo runs. But this is a game built for Co-op.  And if you got a friend that loves hurting themselves, then this is the game for you!  Get this game!  There is no better Duo Roguelike.  (You could argue that it is a Roguelite, but the runs are always Tabula Rasa.  {COME AT ME BRO!})Get a friend and buy this game!  If you don't have a friend, join the discord and make one!  (I have an "Add Friend" button on my profile.)For the price, the game is FAR worth it.===============================================Previous Review:The game has a solid concept.  But I can't recommended it, yet.The game is seriously lacking in content; you can beat the final boss on your first run.  There are only three levels, or "boards," and the bosses at the end of each board are the same every run.  There is no randomness.  And the final boss is FAR easier than any of the previous bosses.  I genuinely struggle to find a reason to keep playing.  I have all these things to buy on the island, but what's the point.  I can already beat the game with no problems.  There is an achievement to "Destroy 10000 sea monsters" that I can bet NO ONE will get.  I've only killed 1,000 monsters and I'm already done playing.The biggest problem is that the connection to your co-op partner is VERY unstable.  Lag is the least of your worries.  If your connection drops, the run abruptly ends with no way to pick up where you left off.  Plus, all run rewards are lost.  The game needs a re-work: - More level variation - A higher difficulty - A save system - A reason, ANY REASON, to keep grinding money and upgrade the base.  As it stands now, it is not worth the listed price.  If they add more content, I may change my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty good! The core gameplay loop is solid, sort of a FTL meets This Means Warp with Don't Starve / Klei visuals.I'm ~8ish hours in and have beaten the final boss a decent amount of times but there's still a lot of things to unlock.The solo mode is actually surprisingly fun, and managing the automated sentry you get in parallel with other things you need to do during fights/bosses is pretty engaging.A few gripes that I do have about the game:- Coop play only progresses the host file rather than both files in parallel. Bit annoying when you have to sit through the tutorial multiple times when your friends are first getting off the ground. (It does seem that tendrils you earn on another host's session are still preserved?)- Lack of variety in the status effects that can be applied (fire, ice, oil, resonance). Not exactly a lot of combos to come up with here but the variety in ammo types (piercing, bombs, eggs, etc) helps mitigate that right now.- Trinkets and artifacts seem kind of tame and straightforward. I'd like to see more interesting decision-making for regular trinkets and artifacts that you can find during your runs. Like how certain items in Binding of Isaac penalize stats in favor of unique benefits. Right now it's mostly stuff like "Add 5% crit chance" or "Add [status effect] to your paddle/harpoon/shots". The cursed artifacts are a step in the right direction but they just turn into a regular drop which kind of misses the point in my opinion.And the biggest gripe I have about the game:- There is no true roguelite endgame grind outside of just unlocking stuff + upgrading your boat/cannons. No challenge mode runs, no alternate boss pathing, no Slay the Spire styled Ascension content. This means at some point, as much as I enjoy the gameplay, I will get to the point where I can continuously clear the end boss without really thinking too much about it.Devs have indicated that there will be upcoming content in the future (i.e. the Great Lighthouse will eventually get some purpose). I'd hope to see these future updates be free and add true endgame depth to the game because the core/backbone of the game is really solid! Would definitely recommend a buy because for its price I think it's absolutely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a Neopets game called Attack of the Revenge where you had to fend off a pirate attack. Your attention was split between swatting back swashbucklers on defense and loading cannons to earn points. Ship of Fools brings back fond memories of that simple design, elevating it to a rogulite co-op. There is a solid foundation for a frantic sea shooting gallery, but the game isn't great yet. This might be a touch easy for the roguelite enthusiast. My brother and i beat the game on our 4th run without getting hit. The runs have a nice amount of variety for building your ship and strategy and they aren't very long. But there are only 4 bosses in a fixed order, slim pickings for a game meant to replayed again and again. Enemy types that mess with your ship rather than deal damage would be welcome, like something that blocks you from placing a cannon down. Something that throws oil or glue on the deck to screw with your movement. In its current state Ship of Fools is surely fun but there are waters still to chart. (Played via a shared library, if you're wondering about my playtime for the review, lol)

_childDocuments_.review: ProsMusic is amazing. I love them so much I had them in my playlist for a while. If they added more it would almost be a reason to buy the game alone. I love the art style. The fools are really cute and animated in a very fun way. It really gives contrast  to the dark lovecraftian style of some of the creatures. The maps look really great as well. The map used for their roguelike is very fun and the concept of the storm removing opportunities on a timer makes sense and works really well.There are a good amount of items and characters that make the game feel fun. and allow for different builds.ConsThis game still feels new. I wouldn't say this is a terrible thing as the amount of content in the game is still expanding and there was a new update being annouced at the time of this review. However I did find it less fun after winning again and again. Speaking of beating the game again and again, There is no difficulty system in the game and so there is no way of customizing your experience to tailor towards a casual or hardcore audience. There just is "hard". But this one difficulty just ends up feeling way to easy after a while. Once I started getting endgame items it felt much less rewarding to win. Progression is permanent. There is no extra save files so once you progress you can't just start over for a challenge. I started maxing out everything and now I can't undo it. Edit: There is a datawipe option.No ability to remove certain items from the spawning pool. Now this one is understandable, it's not like dead cells with its massive library of items. But with the system of having a shopkeeper that forces you to purchase all of his items from one shop (which end up spawning in your runs later) before you can refresh and gain the new set of items there's no way of controlling what you release into the pool if you want the item at the way back.I know I give a harsh review, but I still definitely recommend this game. I personally am very optimistic for the future because this game is super early in its career. The base gameplay elements are there, and it's super fun. Just waiting on updates...

_childDocuments_.review: An entertaining, quick rogue-lite that works well for two player co-op; keeps you engaged with swift progress and ways to vary your setup. You play as two crew of a ship. Your job is to operate the cannons of the ship (load ammo, aim, and fire) as well as to whack things around with a paddle. In each run, you select your path through randomised encounters. Enemies come in multiple classes. Each class exhibits similar behaviour through stages, but varies slightly on each stage. End bosses are distinct and each has their own pattern and strategies. Apart from the randomised encounters, each run varies through the ammunition, equipable items, and ship wide buffs you can find.We played in shared screen co-op mode, using controllers. Controls work well, though there is some potential frustration in hectic moments (e.g., quickly abandoning a cannon to do repairs felt a bit finicky). Visuals are clear and indicators are well visible. Even if there is a lot going on on screen, enemy attacks and patterns are easy to track. The game progresses rather swiftly. Your power curve is a bit steeper than I am used to from other rogue-lites; there is a lot of tangible power increase after each run. This draws you in and keeps you engaged (“just one more run”). However, it also means that the game is over rather quickly. It took us just under 8h to beat the final boss in two consecutive runs.For me, this is the only downside to Ship of Fools. It’s over quickly, and there is no real “end game” that you can come back to. No modifiers to increase difficulty, no additional challenges. Beyond trying out new builds, and trying to unlock all characters and items, there is nothing to do.Still, the game is well worth the EUR 15 for what it offers. Absolutely recommended for some shared screen co-op entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: An Important Note: i do not reccomend it for full price, wait for a saleShip of fools be a game of Sailing, Shooting, but most important, Foolin.Had the game since launch, and after admitidly a very rough start, it took its first year to grow, from a game i would say maybe no, to a game id say maybe yes.But what do we got? well got 4 things i look for, so lets seeGameplay - DecentFoolin must be the key to immortality, since the fools themselves have no HP, only the ship. so must use ye cannons and paddles to shoot and deflect the enemies, which can make for a decent loop of attack and defend. the ammo types (while varied in designs) do lose a little bit since some may feel too similar to each other. the artifacts n trinkets and recently the new boats are where builds are made, with some making ammo better, others your trusty paddle. only noteable bad thing is most fools arent really strong enough to differentiate each other, save for lotte, who even with their nerf, still has an op perkNote: while the game is great as a duo, it can also work as a solo experience thanks to the sentry cannon, so even if ye got no friends, the game can still be enjoyedDifficulty - Variableso originally, the difficulty was... a bit of a mess. namely, without upgrades it can be challenging, but once you get all of them, it turns into a lazy river. thankfully the light house update added enough attributes to make it go from challenging, to a snore, to challenging again. Soundtrack - Amazingthe tunes of the Archipelago are truly great, from the battle themes of combat, to the calmer themes of simple shopping and treasure finding. Personal faves are Tyrant of the deep, Beakeneers and Unbeakeneers, and The Great Lighthouse.Worldbuilding/Lore - Greatthe world of the archapeligo has enough bits of lore sprinkled about to tell ye a story, but enough holes to perhaps fill in your own.  Anything else? - 1 Extreme Gripe, and the DLCif i had a chance to guarentee anything, it would be to make the final boss better.  as for the DLC, do find it overpriced, but for the deep sea duo, its worth. undecided on the garden duo, even with Mikoi's bonus songTL:DR A rough start, but the 2 big updates helped it get its sea legsNot perfect, but still enjoyable

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface by saying that I am a close friend to the developers of the game and I've had the pleasure of following, giving some input and testing out the game throughout development. It's been a journey for them and I am proud of the team and the IMO amazing and polished result. Congrats Fika!By now you might already know that Ship of Fools is a 2-player coop roguelite with a gameplay loop that is fun and engaging. It's a game where sailing on a new run with a friend is pure dumb hectic fun and often hilarious. The art is charming, the dialogues are funny and the sound and game design are great.It took me 7 hours to beat a solo run of Ship of Fools. Indeed, as other reviewers mentioned, the game is easier in coop (and meant to be played this way) but I've had a lot of fun in solo, improving my ship and finding out new builds to beat the final boss, Every run was a learning experience and it never felt unfair. Note that the sentry turret is very weak and I was forced to learn the encounters and bosses, making me better at the game. If you're looking for a challenge, try it out in solo. Oh and my god, few have mentioned it, but I must say that the OST is a banger. Kuddos to Philippe Grant, the composer for his work. I hope to see a hard mode added someday!To paraphrase Gandalf, I wish you a fun next "Run you fools!"

_childDocuments_.review: Ship of Fools is a 2 player co-op game that's well worth its $15 pricetag. Combat is made up of balancing keeping on the offensive with cannons and melee attacks with defending through melee combo knockback, melee to put out fires, and charged melee attacks to deflect projectiles while dodge-rolling through the occasional stun beam attack. There's a lot to juggle and it's a lot of fun. Between fights, you'll navigate a map for different loot and shops to beef up your characters and ship for upcoming fights.As far as cons, we hit a progress impeding bug about 10 minutes into a run where the camera got stuck not showing the fight currently happening and we found the cannon mount/dismount and the pick up/use controls to be unintuitive. I also have a strong preference to rogue-likes as opposed to rogue-lites and their gross permanent unlocks locking away boring but super practical unlocks like more health with the same currency as the fun but less practical unlocks like "a random swordfish trinket that I don't have a clue what it does".With all that said, it's still a very fun 6 hours or so playthrough to beat it once even if it doesn't hook you for extra hours of replay. Go grab a fellow fool and give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very easy recommendation. I personally think that people that find this game too short or want 4 player co-op are slightly missing the intention behind this game. Make no mistake, all of the design choices are very intentional, and in my opinion, combine to make one of the most special co-op roguelites I've ever played (and I've played quite a few). The game is relatively short but very replayable. 4 player co-op would be far too easy based on a game very finely balanced for 2 players. People have mentioned they want more cannons, but the point of 4 cannon pedestals is so you can move the two cannons around so you can have one each side or both to one side, depending on the encounter. I have nothing but praise for the devs who managed to keep a game this simple yet deep as well as a fun solo experience but even more fun with a friend! 100% recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a rouge-lite that's also co-op, this is for you. Otherwise, it's passable. 7/10.Note that I previously reviewed this game on the Steam Deck and performance was all around not great, especially at key moments where enemies boarded your ship. This has been fixed and it should now run well on most hardware.This game is designed for co-op. The difficulty is much higher with a single person. You can get a sense of this when according to Steam Achievements, 40% of players have completed a run ("beat the game") vs 9% of players that have completed a run solo. It took me ~15 hours to complete my first run solo, grinding and leveling up things. The game provides you an auto turret to make up for a lost friend. However, it's unhelpful in more situations that I'd like. Swarmed by pufferfish? Too bad, it probably won't do enough damage to kill anything. Ran out of ammo in a key moment? Well it just won't be shooting then.Overall, there isn't much diversity in runs early on. Most of the diversity comes from buying or finding Trinkets, Ammo, or Artifacts during the run. This relies on you getting to enough spaces on the map to push your luck, but your ship probably sucks too much to visit too many of them. It took me about 3 hours to beat the first boss, 8 to beat the second, and then 5 to beat the third and fourth bosses. It was a grind. The lack of diversity can be really painful early on and likely leads to lots of people dropping this game if it's not their cup of tea.Now that I've leveled up most of my stuff, I'll likely try co-op again but otherwise don't think I'll loop around and see the other mechanics they built in. They don't seem like it will honor my time with anything too new or unique.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a pretty cool concept, a bit like a co-op FTL with more of an emphasis on fighting with shooting cannons and smacking enemies with paddles. I was a bit surprised that it didn't run at 60fps on Steamdeck, but not a big deal. It's actually pretty fun for couch co-op... if you can get two controllers to be recognized. If you have two controllers recognized in Steam (I tried Xbox series X and 8bitdo SN30pro, both over bluetooth), the game for some reason will not recognize the 2nd controller. Looking around the internet it seems like this has been an ongoing issue with the game since Nov 2023 at least. I'm giving the game a "No recommended" because I bought it to play couch co-op and I couldn't get it to work.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is charming. But it's not fulfilling. There's lots of "fools", but it felt like there were very few options for trinkets, artifacts, and ships. After defeating the first boss and moving onto the next area, the grind quickly starts to feel tedious. With the game as it is now, I don't see myself playing it further.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun rogue-lite, great art style and gameplay, but there's almost nothing to it.It's an incredibly short game in terms of how much content there is as well as how long you actually play for between runs.I just cannot recommend it for what is available especially at this price considering it is a full release, and there isn't even a roadmap as far as I am aware.A few particularly annoying or bad things, mainly to do with solo play;Upgrading your cannons is 100% worth it, but you will almost certainly notice absolutely no change to the actual effectiveness of it. You also have no clue what the upgrade does without looking on the wiki, because there's no information at the upgrade shop.If you play solo, you can choose a cannon for yourself and then you also get a sentry cannon that is automatic, but extremely and disgustingly slow. If you want to move it to a different spot on the ship, you have to do that yourself while also keeping it and your own cannon loaded, and swatting away any enemies or projectiles that are on/approaching your ship. It also cannot be upgraded until you beat the very final boss, and even then I'm not entirely sure if it will actually affect the default solo sentry cannon or only if you pick it as your primary gun. It's ridiculously bad and only just worth even using.Pufferfish are stupidly deadly on a solo run. On levels where they are the main enemy, it is physically impossible to kill them all on both sides before they reach your ship, and it is impossible to swat them all away before they explode and damage you. The sentry gun is completely useless against them so you have to deal with them entirely alone.The final boss is a decent challenge, most of the enemies can be handled well enough in singleplayer (except the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pufferfish) by moving your cannon back and forth and just keeping the sentry loaded. But when you complete the wave and are fighting the actual boss again, it's almost not worth moving the cannon to the other side when it teleports there. By the time you acknowledge the boss has teleported to the opposite side, you pick up your cannon, and then place it on the other side, you are lucky to get even a few shots on it. If it happens to stay on the same side, great, you can shoot some more and if you have the precision or grapeshot cannon you can charge up and hit it hard. But chances are it will immediately teleport back to the other side and you will have to move the cannon . It's just a chore to try to fight it, and it doesn't get much better in the second part.19/01/23Latest update; sentry cannon can be upgraded from the start now, but they removed the ability to carry items in your hands to the next area - only things on pedestals stay, no matter what.29/12/23After playing a little bit more since I first did, I stand by what I said.It's just not a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool concept, art style very cutesy (a bit too cutesy for my liking, but I guess it is well done). It would be nice to be able to fit out the ship at the start of each run with different ammo and/or artefacts to vary the play style a bit more.  As it stands each run is very groundhog day, rinse and repeat.  There are upgrades to cannons/ship health / storage etc, but these don't really change the game play much.  You can change ships but the different ships offer little variation in play style or strategy.My main gripe with this game though is that it is really not for solo play.  As it stands it seems intended for coop play, being poorly optimised for solo play as soon as it starts to get a bit harder.  You simply can't be in two places at once to stop simultaneous attacks (particularly once you have unlocked critical hits which then happen quite often) and/or reload cannons at same time. On that note, there is far too much time spent in a battle simply reloading cannons which makes battles a dull, repetitive scramble.There are also too many different types of ammunition, many of which seem very similar, many of which are pretty useless.  A run's success entirely depends on finding good trinkets, ammunition type matters much less.  And overall there are too many items, particularly ammo but trinkets too, that are a waste of time.  None of the items (even the good ones) really result in much difference in strategy - back to the dull, repetitive point.

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now, I wouldn't recommend it if you're looking for a multiplayer roguelike. The game has very little depth. Enemies have very simple attack patterns, and there are not that many different types of enemies. This makes the game very easy. It's really more like a linear game with permadeath and metaprogression than a roguelike. It has the same areas every time, and there are not enough differences in the events and upgrades to make runs feel unique. It's fun for one or maybe 2 go-throughs of the game, but probably not more than that.Also, it's only 2 player. Fully expected to be able to play with my friend group, and then we ended up having to split up.I fully intend to alter my review and re-purchase the game if it is ever updated to the point where it has 4 player support, and more replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: Great roguelite if you like being TOTALLY BLIND about what goes on.the descriptions of all items are very limited and hardly explain anything at all. the game doesn't tell you a lot of things. One thing is "let's figure out what all these map icons mean by visiting them once" and another thing is feeling like a FOOL yourself because half the relics or weapons don't give you any helpful insight. I've spent half this game looking up info on the wiki or steam guides and there is no more info than what you can read in the game most of the time so you're just left wondering and guessing. it's good to not spoil too much of your game to players but this game feels like you either are a super veteran who knows already everything aftrer dumping many hours in it or you like to gamble your run. and on later runs it becomes frustrating, sacrificing an entire run just to find out if something is worth it because the game description prefers to be "fun" rather than informative :/Why the bad vote? despite the mechanic of the game being fun, I find out the lack of clarity frustrating, and at the end... you have to re-do it again? well duh! it's a roguelite, but like 20 times? and each time you increase the difficulty despite even maxing out all upgrades you don't get  that much help.. Maybe it's because I'm playing solo but I think the grind is real. so if you're the kind of player who will sink 80-130 hours on a game go crazy and have fun. otherwise just do a couple of run and put away the game for your own sanity.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent co-op game.Rescuing the village characters as you go and seeing how the Archipielago improves with every win is one of the things I liked the most. The gameplay although "repetitive", finds its way to be dynamic since the amos, trinkets and objects you get are different every round. Also, depending on the character and ship you choose at the beggining, you will need to adapt your plan in order to be prepared enough to fight the final boss. I see a lot of potencial in this game and hopefully Fika productions will surprise us with more lore next year. I saw other reviews talking about bugs ruinning the gameplay for them but even though I experienced some, it didn't bothered me much. It will usually happen when we were extremely powerful hahaha. So if anything, it made it more fun.I have finished all the Great Lighthouse levels, yet still have to unlock all the achievements with the different ships and to max out 3 cannons. Everytime I play this game it's lots of un and I couldn't recommend this game more. As an animator myself, I also really love the 2D animation and the artstyle as a whole (wish for them to sell an artbook). However it was the art what first caught my eyes, the overall game made me stay. Looking forward for more Ship of Fools! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Two fools, a boat, a couple canons, and that's it : Ship of fools is about fighting in these mysterious oceans, discovering new equipment, boats, characters (fools) and using your paddle & canons to take on the biggest monsters of the sea. The slowly increasing difficulty allows you to play both in a relaxed manner, or in a more serious and planned approach whille still having fun. The art style and sound design are incredibly well done, and the game can easily take over 20 hours to complete. It took me somewhere around 25-30 hours with a friend to reach the end of the in-game lore, but there are still achievments that we still have to obtain and some strategy we still want to try out. TL;DR : Ship of fools is a great rogue-like in an ocean-themed world, that really shines when played with a friend.
