_childDocuments_.review: As a player who loves achievement hunting in games until completion, I love Team 17, their games, roguelikes that are co op with a little be of competition (friendly fire). This is game is perfect for me... or it would have been except one thing that ruins the whole experience for me...You cannot complete the whole game without buying dlc as there are achievements that are character specific. Meaning if you want another shiny gold medal for your library, you'll have to pay up. While this isn't a problem for many people since forking over about five dollars isn't too bad, I'm not a person who has a lot of money and can really only get a new one maybe once every few months. So when I saw this game and how perfect of a match it was for me, I wanted to get it since it was on sale. I didn't realize this dlc achievement issue until I was already way past the 2 hour mark. I wish that either A. this update came with free characters in order to not force people to pay extra in order to get those achievements... OR a way better solution would be to lock those achievements away and keep them hidden until you buy the dlc. That way if you want to 100% the game, you can do it without getting hit with this snarky cash grab. As it stands, this game is two years old and the dlc came out in 2023. _childDocuments_.review: Ship of Fools is a fun, simple game with surprising depth and immense replayability. The element of randomness to the rewards you get means that once you unlock enough things, virtually all characters can be viable, even the ones with seemingly niche abilities. On top of this, the different ship types allow you to try different gameplay styles and pick the kind that you enjoy the most. And, crucially, you can play with a friend.The core gameplay loop is simple - keep your ship alive while fighting through "stages" of enemy waves and slowly upgrading your ammunition, hp, abilities etc. You can choose a path through each of the three main areas (which end in a boss fight) and the path determines what kinds of rewards you get, e.g. ammunition, but it doesn't determine exactly which one. Defeat the boss to move to the next area and repeat the process until you fight the "final boss" in a climactic showdown. As you progress, and as a reward for defeating the last boss, you earn "tendrils" which are basically the unlock currency for new stuff. As mentioned, there's a lot of replayability in the game. Aside from the random loot system, during a round you can unlock additional characters and ships to try on your next run. The game loop is short, usually taking about half an hour to win, which means you can try all sorts of combinations and upgrades quite quickly. It also means not having to commit too heavily to long gaming sessions to progress, which is always welcome. As you increase the difficulty you also unlock new features, keeping the game fresh and interesting as you go.All in all, a very fun, casual experience with more than enough playtime to justify the price. I have some minor gripes with the game's mechanics, but these are likely to get ironed-out before the early access period is over and it's already a lot of fun as-is, even if it were abandoned right now. Strongly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever dreamed of captaining a ship filled with eccentric characters, absurd situations, and more chaos than a seagull in a seafood market, then Ship of Fools is the game for you.In this comedic adventure on the high seas, you'll take command of a ragtag crew of misfits as they navigate through a series of bizarre encounters, questionable decisions, and the occasional sea monster or two.Visually, Ship of Fools is a delight, with colorful graphics that bring its quirky characters and zany situations to life. And the voice acting? It's so good, you'll swear you can smell the salty sea air and taste the stale grog.But don't let the laughs fool you – beneath the humor lies a challenging adventure game that will test your wits and resourcefulness. Whether you're navigating treacherous waters, fending off rivals, or trying to keep you from mutiny, you'll need to stay on your toes to survive.Despite its flaws, Ship of Fools is a hilarious and engaging experience that's perfect for anyone who enjoys a good laugh and a bit of swashbuckling adventure. So hoist the anchor, raise the sails, and prepare for a journey filled with laughter, danger, and more absurdity than you can shake a parrot at.Pros:-Hilarious humor and quirky characters make for a memorable adventure.-Challenging situations keep gameplay engaging.-Colorful graphics and top-notch voice acting bring the world of Ship of Fools to life.Cons:-Some may find the gameplay a bit repetitive, but the laughs make it worth it.-Occasional bugs and glitches may mar the experience, but they're as rare as a friendly kraken.Overall Rating: 8/10 – A comedic voyage that's as entertaining as it is absurd, perfect for anyone who's ever wanted to sail the seven seas with a crew of lovable lunatics. Just be sure to bring your sense of humor – and maybe a life jacket or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Ship of Fools

_childDocuments_.review: A Fantastic Way to Settle Who’s the Best CaptainShip of Fools is a great game for proving who’s the top dog when it comes to teamwork and strategy. It’s the perfect way to settle debates and show off who’s the real captain of the crew! The co-op mechanics are fun and chaotic, and it really tests how well you and your friends can work together (or throw each other under the bus). Sure, I didn’t exactly get to live out my One Piece fantasies, but that’s okay—the fast-paced action, hilarious moments, and constant pressure still make every match an exciting challenge. If you want to see who’s got the best sea legs and tactical mind, this is the game to do it!And the one piece is real!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this with my wife for quite some time and it is genuinely a blast to play together. The first runs of trying to get further and further are truly blissful. Progressing higher up in difficulty level at the lighthouse and then dropping down to the standard difficulty really shows how much better we had become at the game, but ultimately also shows this game's greatest weakness.Although the lighthouse update added crucially needed replay value and progression goals, latest update (adding new ships) really wasn't enough for us to get brought back in. Realizing that the gameplay loop really isn't anything more than the three zone bosses plus the last boss and the game abrubtly ending after that is really a bummer.Perhaps this game just lacks the depth of some roguelites, i.e. not having that kind of 100h plus replayability time, which honestly is totally OK.The studio has executed on its vision and delivered on their goals. Solid art style and compelling gameplay makes this a good pick up to play with a friend or SO, don't expect the game to last forever though.

_childDocuments_.review: Played many more hours locally with my best friend, but recently finished Lighthouse 15. (Highest Difficulty Level)The game is super fun, even though it is ungodly imbalanced and a lot of runs require extreme teamwork, precision, and a lot of RNGesus blessings. Some runs, especially at high lighthouses can be come an insane battle of attrition. The game also runs horribly no matter what your build is or what OS you are on. Its just terrible on everything it exists on for some unknown reason. There are no graphic options either in game. Changing the screen size barely functions.For example, in the Ice Area on 10-15  lighthouse, the enemies would absolutely swarm you and ruin your day. The bosses were the "Easy" part because they were consistently the same difficulty. This is still the same but they have balanced it an iota. Once you hit lighthouse 13, and get the reward, some guns become insanely OP and broken. Grapeshot my beloved. It does make for some very hectic runs, but you need some extremely OP amulets, trinkets, and ammo to win. I still recommend this game, even though the devs took holding items between tiles away, because its a blast to play with one other person. You can pick it up, play for a while and put it down, or play for hours. If you're here for story, forget about it, there is a barely functional one at best, but literally couldn't tell you a thing about it if you asked. It is very fun to play, but will aggravate the hell out of you in later difficulties if you're trying to go that far. Also the achievements are for the host... so there's that too. TL;DR: 6.5/10, would barely recommend, dont expect a masterpiece even though it could have been one. Absolutely need 2 people to play the game, solo is insane at high difficulty. Play if you want a fun pick up and play game with one other person.
_childDocuments_.name: Ship of Fools

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this locally with my friend whenever we get the chance, and we've been having a great time. This has the potential to be a top tier roguelite.Having a well rounded variety of meta-progression to work towards is what keeps these games feeling addictive and rewarding for me, and Ship of Fools does it pretty well with item unlocks and upgrades at your disposal between runs.The game does seems to have an issue with severe lag spikes, dropping you as low as 5fps at times. These don't last very long and overall happen pretty infrequently for me, but definitely need to be addressed.Adding new bosses that have a chance of showing up instead of the already existing bosses which we're currently guaranteed to face would be my top suggestion for adding more depth to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have gotten a lot of enjoyment out of this game, I can't entirely recommend it to others. Having more difficult runs with the lighthouse is nice, but my main thing against the game is how it adds difficulty. Most of my runs are either so easy they are boring since I got good luck with encounters or nearly impossible. I can win almost every time but when I lose it isn't because I made a mistake but because multiple crit projectiles came zooming at 100 miles an hour to the other side of the ship before I could reflect them. While this may be easier to deal with in coop play it feels like absolute crap for solo runs. I also feel that in most runs some encounters are almost certain death while the BOSS battles are so easy I feel relieved when I fight enough to get to them. Another thing that I think is kind of rough and have seen other people say is that the controls aren't super intuitive. There were times after coming back from a break from playing the game I couldn't even remember what button prompted dialogue. Often it is a toss-up whether the game wants you to click space, e, or enter because it isn't always the same between different interactions. A final thing that is more just a personal issue I have is there isn't any way to save any runs. Often after completing various difficulties and runs you will be gifted an item but now you have to do another run. If you don't then the next time you get on you won't have that item (it will be unlocked to find in the future) which makes it feel punishing to stop even after a long session.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game to play with friends (or like me with my brother). _childDocuments_.review: The art style is amazing but that's pretty much it.It takes an existing concept and makes it worst due to extremely poor game design decisions and poor balacing.Every run is too similar. The monsters are always the same, with the exact same attacks. There is a lack of boss and attack patterns.The items we found are lazy and uninspired. More often than not, you will retrieve new ammo that are worst than the starting ones. There is no info, no tooltip about their effect so be prepared to try new ammo and be extremely disappointed.The artifacts are simple and have too many restrictions. Some of them try to synergize but it's just not worth it.The trinkets are unfun, uninspired once again. They are the only items with cumulative effects that could have made a run unique but we don't get enough of them. They usually are a simple raw stat bonus.Accessing a merchant is frustrating since its position is just random. The game don't try to put it far enough on your path. It means you won't have enough money to buy things most of the time, and will just gain money for no reason.The worst part is the "game +" mechanic. It's like to "heat" in Hades but with *auto-censored* decisions from the game designers. For instance, at lighthouse level 3, slugs will appears every ~10 seconds. The issue is those slugs will spawn continually and can attack your ship, even when you are on a peacefull island (like a merchant) or even when you are locked in a map animation. This is one of the most baffling thing I have ever witnessed in a video game.There are currently some game breaking bugs. Some monsters will not spawn properly, locking your run. I also experimented audio issue where a sound never stops.The game is also too easy. You will finish it in just 3 to 5 hours before the lighthouse mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:If you enjoy rougelikes and are looking for a very unique take on combat encounters you should buy this game.Longer version:This game takes place on a ship and most combat is done through stationary turrets you aim,load, and fire, and through melee attacks for defending the ship. You take damage by enemies either approaching the ship slowly and melee attacking, or selecting a tile on this ship and launching a projectile. In general the combat is very fair, and you usually have a counter to anything an enemy can do. However with high enemy numbers it can feel a bit unfair.ITEMS: The items are highly variable in usefulness. some items do immensily useful effects and sometimes they do basically nothing.  If you get terrible rng the the bosses and random encounters can wreck you.However this game is very fun, and if you have a friend to play with it has a moderate amount of replayability. Once you unlock everything the game begins to get stale.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Ship of Fools! I'd rate it 8.5/10. As a game designer, I'm excited to share my thoughts.Pros: Amazing to play with friends for tens of hours and make memories (due to replayability, strategizing, improving synergized gameplay etc), hilarious text, discoverable synergies, great optional difficulty climb thanks to updates, tons of fun modifier items, lots of super individual experiences, etc. There are tons of characters that feel quite different when leaning into their unique perk (mixing and matching w ur duo is great!) and the ships feel unique too. There is consistently a workout-level challenge even after 40 hours if the difficulty is at least medium. The devs really care about getting making sure you can play as much of the content as possible--if your friend owns a dlc (theyre cheap!!) then you can use those characters too. You can push any one fantasy insanely in one direction and that's always funny and awesome.Cons: It's really difficulty to play alone, if not impossible at high difficulties. The bosses never change and enemies are consistent , the final boss , the replay grind is intense and LONG, the strats don't get super different and some are guaranteed to work if you wait long enough. It really feels like we need more different enemies--seeing ALL the SAME ones EVERY run is just doesn't feel special, even if it's a good marker against your power. There's a rare audiovisual bug that occurs only on one player's screen.I really highly recommend this game and it gets way better with every content drop!! IT'S PERFECT FOR NEW AND EXPERIENCED PLAYERS!!! It's silly and can be either generally relaxed or intense. And I'm so glad for this latest update with new ships and characters. But please, devs--decrease the downtime and increase the differentiation!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I like the game. I like that the developers seem to be pretty engaged. The game runs pretty smoothly and is really replayable.One issue I have is locking playable content (characters, items, etc.) behind paywalls. I know, devs have to eat, but I just don't like it and put my money where my mouth is when it comes to supporting the behaviors I like. I'm happy to pay multiple times for a game I like and to devs I want to support (I bought Stardew Valley 4-5 times, I bought 3 copies of Super Meat Boy, and I've bought every bit of DLC for Deep Rock Galactic even if I never planned on using any of it because they push out playable content for free and I really respect that).I completely endorse the game, but I have no clue on the extra characters/content released so far because I just can't usually bring myself to pay for it.EDIT: Yeah, upon further reflection, after two paid character DLCs and an increase in the base price... _childDocuments_.review: Game is good, very good. Can recommend it, very good for co-op, especially with someone that isn't well-versed to video-games.-Fun, fast and offers variety, lots of weapons/builds without being too complex since you have a limit of 5 slots. Major decisions that can either make the game or break it, but without feeling too unfair.-Animations/sounds/effects are all satisfying. Some enemies are meh and just flat out uninteresting, but visually speaking the game looks and sounds nice.-Gameplay feels somewhat fresh, a few good "new" ideas are presented in a nice manner, the melee/ranged hussle is tough at first but once you get the hang of it, it feels very natural.HOWEVER, has a few problems that can be frustrating at some points, which you do need to mind before buying this.-Ever since the lighthouse update, minor lags will happen, that might just make you lose. Didn't happen before the lighthouse update, so no idea what's on that end. Also, whenever you go into a new area, it loads A LOT.-The lighthouse becomes insanely difficult too quick. I mean alright, you're replaying the game to get more spice, but at around level 6-7 it becomes very difficult unless you get a very good combination. Which leads to point 3-You get new items, but the old ones DON'T ROTATE OUT. This is a MAJOR PROBLEM, because you might be at the second zone and get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥-ass piercing shell while you're in desperate need of something that is actually good. Not a "balancing" issue, but please, lower the chance of older/more useless stuff appearing later in the game.Can recommend, game's worth its money, at a discount even more so. Given that this seems to be the studio's first release, it's good that they keep updating it, that they are interacting here and on the forums (not a lot, but enough to at least feel ALIVE), so can definitely recommend supporting the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a roguelite co-op game with quirky cute graphics that I received as a birthday gift.The controls could benefit from better logic, making the game harder than it should be. For example trying to grab a seagull as ammo may end up make you pick a nearby object instead, or reloading a canon or putting down a plank for repair can fail because of other objects close by. I would have liked the reloading and repairing being automatically performed just by having the object in hands and being close to the canon or to the hole in the hull. In stressful situations it only adds to the chaos and the frustration of losing.The game is not really balanced, as some ammo and trinkets are completely overpowered and will trivialize a run while others are just garbage and incentivize to "run again" for that dopamine rush when the RNG gives you the right combination of trinkets, artefacts and ammunition... but I guess there is some fun to be had in stomping everything after hours of painstakingly learning the monsters pattern.Another dubious design choice is that for a co op game, the characters stun each other when hitting too close and I have not found any way to disable it, which makes the game even more frustrating whereas playing with a friend is supposed to be "more" fun. Not sure about recommending the game but I guess I've seen worse?

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Ship of Fools is a great coop experience for 2 players with many hours of content! I definitely recommend it.In short: you're on a tiny little ship with two cannons, sea creatures are attacking you from both sides, and you've got to sail all the way to the Eye of the Storm to find out how to repel it and save the island you're from.Ship of Fools is a tight gameplay loop with surprising amounts of fun hidden behind the simple options you have: shoot cannons, carry items, dodge/roll, and strike at close range with your paddle.Each of these basic actions is complemented by in-game items that empower them uniquely, meaning you'll often find yourself deviating from your go-to build to make use of your new trinkets and baubles.RNG, while present at all stages of the game, leaves a lot of room for strategizing and skill expression. This means you should be able to complete most of your expeditions without sinking once you've learned the basics as a young Fool! While it's possible to try and force the same build each game, it would be wiser to adapt, so getting an idea of what items work best together becomes a big part of your learning experience.Ship of Fools is charming all around, with beautifully drawn characters that will immediately clue you into the tone of the game. It's full of humor, colorful, and unapologetically cartoonish. You could draw a lot of similarities to Cult of the Lamb! Minus the blood sacrifices. At least, that means Ship of Fools is accessible to younger players! Parents, this is a great way to have fun with your little gremlins.Ship of Fools is definitely built as a duo experience. While solo is possible thanks to automatic cannons that fire without your input, the hectic nature of the game will quickly test your priorities. Hordes of enemies will swarm you from either side, projectiles will fly above your head threatening to damage your hull - something easily repelled by two coordinated Fools can prove difficult for the lone sailor. My advice: only play Ship of Fools solo if you are looking for a challenge.I am writing this after the Great Lighthouse update was introduced to the game in May 2023. The game was initially lacking an endgame, as I was happy to put it down after getting all Steam achievements. This has changed with the introduction of a new system that tests your might by throwing in extra difficulty modifiers (projectiles can directly damage your ship if they aren't caught, enemies are smarter, tougher...) and I've already sunken hours into the new content with a smile.More is planned by the developers, but in its current state, It feels like Overcooked met Cult of the Lamb, and the result is very graceful. Props to the developers behind such a charming title - but I must return to the High Seas now. The Storm is coming back, and it calls for a Fool to repel it. Ciao!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little rogue-like for you and a friend, would highly recommend controller over M and K but regardless you and a buddy can have a wild and enjoyable time. The game play loop is fun and due to the randomness somehow never feels repetitive, it's also definitely a memory maker in my opinion, especially if you use the local co-op option. The amount of struggling times we've had where we just barely make it through feels so rewarding and gives a real big hit of dopamine. Never once have I felt like a part of the game was an unfair difficulty and while some people complain about the lack of item descriptions on upgrades until you put them on the ship, I far prefer this as it's sort of the point of a rogue-like game. You get better at the game through experience rather than because it tells you something is good or bad. An item that seems like it's bad at first, might just be because you don't know how to use it yet. The only part that could improve is when you do get a description for an item, sometimes it is a bit confusing, as well as there isn't much clarity on what upgrading your cannons does. After playing fourteen hours I honestly don't know what it does, but it feels like they're stronger. Each Fool (Character) feels unique in their special abilities and design, not one feels like it would ever be useless and given the right combo's can be down right over powered. Betty being one of the most powerful offense and Todd, one of the first you have to use, being an insane defense machine.Without a doubt, you should buy this game, preferably at full price. But no matter how you pick it up, I'd just highly recommend you do.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun innovative rogue-like!Mechanics are engaging and fun to pull off like reflecting projectiles!Great Soundtrack!Responsive game play!Satisfying and easy to pick up learning curve!Cheap game!TLDR Fun, worth time, minor issues below first is quality of life change I think, second is Opinions:I highly recommend trying this game with a friend or solo either way is viable I've just beaten the final boss on a solo run and I only have 2 things I feel need a change. The first is a quick one, maybe an option to toggle this on or off, So many times I push down to get off a cannon then try to run left or right to quickly stop my ship from taking damage, but if you try to do it to quickly the game wont take you off the cannon like it has an input delay and you will be stuck thinking you've already told the game to get off the cannon and you are stuck in place which cannot happen in a solo game when you are responsible for everything, this happens to me multiple times a run and is very frustrating my solution is just make left and right take you off cannons as well, you don't aim with it so there should be no reason not to?This is more of a game design issue in my opinion, the final boss was the most disappointing thing when I realized it was just enemy spam and the boss doesn't even attack or pose a threat. Which I'm not really sure how video games have come this far and people still think enemy spam bosses are a good idea very rarely can they be pulled off and this is absolutely not one of those cases, this is not an interesting, new, or a fun experience. On top of it just being enemy spam its the longest fight in the game! 3rd Phase really?! For what?! in case you didn't see all the enemies that he spawned in the first 2 phases? It just doesn't make sense and feels like complete fluff which I hope isn't the case because the game doesn't have a huge amount of content to begin with only 4 bosses and one of them isn't really a boss has me worried but thats just my pessimism kicking in I really hope this game gets updates in the form of enemies and bosses the new ships sound interesting but this game desperately needs new adversaries.

_childDocuments_.review: After 36 hours of playing this game to full achievement and game completion I can say it's been fun, but missing a lot of features. It truly felt like an early-access game that got released too soon. Which felt like a huge disappointment when playing.This is written BEFORE the new spring release update 2023.The game starts of great, I love the rogue-like features and unlocking them at the shop and being able to bring them with is great.What's not great is that when you buy all three pearls from Briny; And they're artefacts or ammo, you have to walk back and forth 2 to 3 times to load them on the boat. Just have them loaded on immediately. It's less obnoxious. They also disappear if you close your game, which is quite sad.I wish there was a feature to randomly have already unlocked artefacts, ammo and trinkets be bought for slightly more expensive with tendrils at the start of a new run, this will make certain challenges like the no damage achievement a bit more do-able. There's enough market stalls, why put the only merchant on the far end? It will also solve the problem of not being interested in tendril tiles anymore. I got about 170-200 saved up after completion now, with no way to spend them.Trying for the no damage is so incredibly luck based rather than skill it cost me 4 days and a lot of frustration to get. Absolutely no fun in that. The common and 'bad' ammo is far too common for a fun run. It also feels like there is too much fire ammo compared to the other types. There's certain items I have only seen once, and others far too often. I have played most of the game solo, and gave up a lot after damage. If you play co-op you can't give up. You are forced to let the boat sink entirely or quit to menu. Can this feature please be implemented in co-op.An endless run would be a huge plus to this game, the three bosses and end boss does feel short after multiple completion.Another feature during the run which would be great is to be able to sell your items for a huge decreased sell rate. For example; Only 25% of the actual 100% price; Or to have the merchant re-roll it's products for a good penny. It makes the game a bit more fun, the amount of times I have seen the chicken statues without a chicken on my boat has cost me a lot of sighs.The sentry on solo play is great, but it'd be nice to have more sentry upgrades. Or be able to swap the sentry out for another gun and have that act like a sentry. I know this is hard to balance and motivates co-op, but it's not fast enough for the boss fights and makes them much harder than need be.Some of the damage you take feels very unfair. The Bully in area 1 sometimes are behind multiple enemies and hitting them is impossible. Being able to reflect their tongue would be a great last resort.The fire damage on area 3 is the most frustrating unbalanced experience I have had in this game. When the beakaneer appear or when multiple pecker die, its a lost cause. As experienced and skilled you may be. The beakaneer has been a run ender on many occasions because the fire damage just keeps coming and as a fool you can't keep up and get rid of a boat full of fire in time. Sometimes the fire doesn't immediately get extinguished when you finish the wave, resulting in losing HP anyway; And there is nothing you can do about it. Getting whacked around by your teammate might have a slight cooldown in my opinion. Sometimes it gets a bit too much when you have to focus on multiple things. But it's not too bothersome.Overall, the game has been fun to play co-op and solo. It can use some tweaks and extra features; Which I hope will appear in future updates. I have faith in this game's success and am looking forward to play future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Having now beat the game, I have a few notes. 1. The content is absolutely worth 15 dollars, however, once you've run through it there is little reason to return to runs. Things like run modifiers, "special events" across the sea board, and challenges would help give reason to continue playing.2. The gameplay loop is fun, I played with a buddy and co-op was very enjoyable. One small note, being able to be stunned by co-op partners seems like a nice addition of "difficulty" at first but after reaching further into the run, you'll find yourself in bad spots where it's very difficult to dodge your partner AND what is happening on the ship. It simply adds another layer of micromanaging, which for some may be fun, I just personally found it tedious.3. Stuns. some of the best runs we had were lost because we were stunned by an enemy attack and stuns are INCREDIBLY potent. Frankly, with how much you have to micromanage combat in this game, the stun feature just feels bad as even if you're playing well, there are simply scenarios where getting hit by a stun is inevitable unless you sacrifice ship health. Stuns last seconds and there is no way to fight a stun after you've been hit by it, leaving your crew immobilized and forced to watch the run end with no counterplay except simply not getting hit by them. With more content, this has the potential to be a longstanding roguelite. I look forward to it's future.
_childDocuments_.name: Ship of Fools

_childDocuments_.review: Ship of Fools is an extremely LITE coop roguelite with the unique gimmick that all encounters occur aboard your ship. All fights require cooperation and teamwork, there are around 100 combined upgrades for your characters, ships and ammo types, but most of them are flat upgrades or elemental types, there's room for build experimentation but not as much as I'd like to justify repeated runs after completing the game. Also, the game has only 4 zones with one boss each, therefore each subsequent run becomes incresingly similar to the previous ones. Pretty neat and clean coop experience, would totally recommend getting it on sale for a fun seafaring afternoon, but wouldn't buy if you are expecting infinite runs and/or replayability. Finished the game with most upgrades in 7 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Ship of Fools

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good roguelite, with a few caveats.It looks good, and sounds good, and writing is great, and co-op actually requires both players to do something (you can't just have a more experienced player "carry" your session to success), which is rare for roguelites. Some encounters and boss fights gain you "currency" that persists between sessions and is used to unlock more items or slightly upgrade your initial stats. More on this later.Online multiplayer mostly works. It could use a little polish, and you'll almost definitely won't be getting back in the game if you drop out mid-session, but overall was usable - at least for us. The game also features the strangest multiplayer pause menu implementation that I've seen - the game  like it's paused on your end (a still image of the game is blurred in the background), but the battle goes on for the other player.You can also play this game in single-player, though I would highly recommend playing it in co-op instead - with only one player on board, some encounters and boss fights boil down to you dashing around ship in panic (torn between putting out fires, slapping intruders off the ship, and repelling the larger enemies from taking a bite out of it) while the auto-turret sure takes its time with shooting the enemies on its side of the ship. newer versions of the game have added additional challenges and ship types, which spice things up... a little.The game can be won with multiple kinds of builds, but most of them boil down to either maximizing damage or stun-locking enemies. Anything else risks long fights where you might take damage simply because you can't be everywhere at once.Some things (like birds laying ammo-eggs) look fun at first, but ultimately never win over regular setups as they require multiple chance items and equipment slots to be  viable and in the end you're better off using those slots for items that offer extra damage/fire rate/ammo capacity.Not sure what you'd do with this either - perhaps this is the point where the main potential for improvement is in adding game modifiers and daily challenges.This game is pretty resource-intensive, possibly  most resource-intensive game I've seen to date that doesn't feature exponentially increasing numbers of entities. On my machine (i9900K, 1660Ti) the game runs at 90..120fps@1080p while maxing out one of the CPU cores at 4.6GHz (and usually  maxing out the GPU), so you might need some pretty beefy hardware if you're hoping to run it at high fps in 2K or 4K.I have completed this game with a friend in some 15 hours (some of which the game sat idle as you can't save&quit mid-session) and then completed a few sessions in single-player to see what's that like. Unlocking the Cooler Items and upgrades would probably take another dozen hours, but also make the game easier on average, so that's a tricky one.In its current state it might not be the game that you would usually play for hundreds of hours, but still it's pretty neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Ship of Fools

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give this game a Meh vote, other reviews are pretty accurate. It's SHORT. There's not a lot of content, three randomized floors where your path affects what loot you get, four bosses, and that's... apparently it. Buddy and I almost beat the game on our third run, and once we do I'm not sure we'll play much more. There's items that cost 50 meta-progression each to provide some pretty significant bonuses, but... when you get 8-10 per run, we might realistically beat the final boss before we've collected a sum total for those, much less saved up enough.That said, what is here is FUN. It's a goofy, lighthearted 2 player co-op adventure, the humor lands well, the gameplay is pretty great, but lacking any kind of newgame+ or ascension or difficulty modifiers... it just feels thin, for a 15$ price tag. The only real randomization is what loot drops for you, aside from that each run's pretty similar.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun. What is a bit annoying is that sometimes you have too much at once, fire on the ship, enemies that explode, enemies with lasers. We often died from that. But definitely recommend it. But what I find very unfortunate is that you can't read the text of the effects completely with the weapons you get, that should be fixed

_childDocuments_.review: I only played local co-op, but could not imagine playing any other way. The game's silly and fun presentation makes it very approachable for those less familiar with games, and the theme of "you crew a pirate ship" is immediately understandable and frames every mechanic in the game in a very intuitive way. Brilliant.The game itself could be summarized as a "putting out fires" type game. Sometimes literally. Difficulty in the game comes from having to react to and prioritize a response threats quickly. And the threats pile on quickly, the end of a run in particular demands full focus and attention.I don't think the game has quite the depth for hours and hours of constant play. But it's a great addition to a hang-out session with a friend on a weekend.This is a great game to play with a friend, or a fantastic way to make a new friend!

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, Ship of Fools doesn't quite hit the mark when it comes to game-play longevity. With only three bosses to defeat, players could potentially complete the game in just a couple of hours. I would have expected a bit more content, like additional boss fights or dungeons to explore. It would have been nice to see some variation in the existing boss fights, with new mechanics added to increase the challenge. Additionally, while there are various characters to collect, I found many of them to be lacking in depth, with the default characters being the most effective in most scenarios. Overall, while Ship of Fools has its strengths, its brevity and lack of character development may be disappointing to some players. That being said...Ship of Fools is an excellent top-down rogue-like adventure game that offers an exciting journey of battling sea monsters while keeping your ship intact and improving your combat tactics. The game excels in its progression system, making it a captivating experience for solo players and an even more thrilling one with friends. The wide range of items available in the game adds to the overall experience, making each run distinct due to the randomly generated maps, and the player's choice of path dictates the game-play experience. The game's visuals, music, and sound effects blend together seamlessly, elevating the overall experience and making it an enjoyable way to pass the time. Overall, Ship of Fools is a great game that delivers a well-crafted and engaging adventure that can be enjoyed alone or with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible Roguelike with a really fun gameplay loop and for $15 I think it's a great value.The devs recently added a huge content update that addresses the issue of low replayability. There's tons of stuff to do and the game gets pretty challenging with the new Lighthouse mechanic. I'm really happy to be able to report that the game has a lot of end-game content which was missing on launch. .. HOWEVER I still think that an Endless Survival mode and new bosses or variably changing bosses per storm area would be a much more productive way to get people to finish out multiple loops without getting bored. The way it stands there is 3 main area bosses and a final end game boss and they are all the same each run. I have mastered each of these bosses and there's nothing new to see in the core game in terms of areas or enemy variety within each boss zone. A looping mechanism similar to Risk of Rain would make it far easier to unlock tendrils (upgrade currency) for experienced players and give players a harder challenge for those seeking it. My only other wish is that the ship could accommodate more than 2 players but that might be an overly ambitious idea reserved for a sequel. It's not really a complaint but merely a suggestion. As the game is I think it's an extraordinary value and lots of fun with the new free update.

_childDocuments_.review: The debut game from Fika Productions, Ship of Fools is a 2D co-op roguelite naval combat game, where you have to move around cannons on your ship, the Stormstrider [cool name btw] in order to defeat enemies who're storming said ship. There's a lot of strategy involved, especially when it comes to the numerous different ammo types you can load your cannons with. Now, the game is intended to be played with another person, but I don't have friends so I've been playing it on my own for the most part. The game does actually compensate for the lack of a Player 2 by giving you an automatically-firing sentry cannon, but said cannon is significantly weaker than the cannons a hypothetical Player 2 would receive. Which brings me onto the difficulty of the game -I don't know if I'm playing on Easy or something, but Ship of Fools is disappointingly easy - even when playing solo. It was probably down to the ammo type I had during my victorious run [the stupidly overpowered Crystal Ball], but the final boss, who I expected to be very difficult, was quite honestly trivial. In future, I'll probably put self-imposed restrictions in place to manually pump up the game's difficulty.Final thing I wanted to talk about was post-game content, which Ship of Fools... lacks. I mean, obviously - considering the fact that it's a roguelite - you can just keep playing, and that's fine, but post-game content is something that really goes hand-in-hand with a lot of games in the roguelike/lite genres. Take Hades for example - once you've beaten the final boss once, you gain access to heaps of new content which you can use to change the difficulty of the game, giving you lots of incentive to keep playing. Or, Brutal Orchestra - beating the final bosses with different party members yield new rewards. In Ship of Fools, it's mainly just ''keep beating the final boss - oh, and you can try and get all the upgrades and stuff too if you want''. To be fair, though, it was released only recently, and I suspect the devs are working on more post-game content for future updates.I know this review has mainly been critical of Ship of Fools, but it really is a solid game - the amazing cartoonish graphics and incredible pirate-y soundtrack composed by Phillipe Grant are most definitely highlights - and despite the lack of post-game content, the game is fun enough that you'll be fine with going through and defeating the final boss a few more times. It's definitely a game that I'd recommend if you enjoy pirate games [like myself], roguelites and cool combat.EDIT:With all of the new updates that Fika has provided the game, Ship of Fools has been elevated high beyond its initial release form! "Lighthouse levels" introduce post-game challenges that get increasingly more difficult as time goes on, and "Endless mode" adds a fun new twist in your ability to create absolutely insane builds over time. There's a slew of new items, and the new ships add even more diversity! Overall, Fika has knocked it out of the park with all of the new post-game content!

name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands
detailed_description: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands: Chaotic Great Edition THE CHAOTIC GREAT EDITION INCLUDES: Full Game Season Pass (Includes the Butt Stallion Pack, Blightcaller class, and 4 dungeons with new bosses, loot, and environments) Dragon Lord Pack Bonus Content About the Game Party up with friends in cross-platform multiplayer! Embark on an epic adventure full of whimsy, wonder, and high-powered weaponry! Bullets, magic, and broadswords collide across this chaotic fantasy world brought to life by the unpredictable Tiny Tina. Roll your own multiclass hero and loot, shoot, slash, and cast your way through outlandish monsters and loot-filled dungeons on a quest to stop the tyrannical Dragon Lord. Everyone's welcome, so join the party, throw on your adventuring boots, and be Chaotic Great! AN UNPREDICTABLE FANTASY WORLD Tiny Tina is your disorderly guide through an extraordinary tabletop realm where rules rarely apply. Explore a vast overworld spanning majestic cities, dank mushroom forests, foreboding fortresses, and more! GUNS, SPELLS, AND MORE Blast baddies with powerful guns and devastating spells in frenetic first-person battles. Use your firepower to vanquish legions of enemies, including smack-talking skeletons, land-roaming sharks, and colossal bosses. Then delve deeper into dangerous dungeons for a shot at epic loot! PARTY UP TO DEFEAT EVIL Joining you at the table are headstrong captain Valentine and rule-obsessed robot Frette. During your quest to defeat the Dragon Lord, you'll meet a cast of lovable misfits like a lute-wielding Bardbarian and your very own Fairy Punchfather. PERSONALIZE YOUR HERO Create the perfect hero with deep customization, including a multiclass system that lets you mix and match six unique character skill trees, all with their own awesome abilities. Level up, refine your build, expand your arsenal, and become the ultimate adventurer. BAND TOGETHER IN CHAOTIC CO-OP Enjoy the story solo or start a party with up to three friends in seamless online multiplayer. Share the spoils or rush to get the shiniest loot—how you play is up to you!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving it a thumbs up because it's a good (not great) addition to the Borderlands universe.ProsTiny Tina is always entertaining. The Bunkers and Badasses format is fun. As with everything in the BL universe, the open world is immersive and fantastically detailed. It's just a lot of fun to walk around and look at the scenery. The game is exactly what you would expect when Tiny Tina is in charge.ConsThe game is just too easy. The boss fights are anemic. The side quests are only there for you to look at the scenery. They don't add anything to the game. The story line is too short. Without doing any side quests, you could sleep through the game in a couple of nights. The encounters are repetitive and after awhile, downright boring.It's probably not worth $60 US, to be honest, so you might want to wait until the price drops a little.

_childDocuments_.review: Shoot and Loot? More like Shoot and Grind.Story is meh, good enough. Antagonist is actually on point; his backstory is very good and character fits perfectly to VA (who also dubbed Bojack Horseman). Too bad he feels castrated from what he could have been, Spells are really fun to play with, nice chenge from grenades.As for upsides that's it. The gameplay is boring without Redux mod. Overworld is actually a nice alternative for travelling but they have this artificial filler called "random encounters" that (unless you're paying attention) are unskippable and take another couple of minutes to clear. They are also a part of every Overworld quest, so they quickly become tedious.Paladin Mike is just like Lorelei from BL3 - useless and annoying, but this time you see him way more often.Loot - utter s**te. In order to get something *actually* good, especially when progressing Chaos Levels, you have to grind Chaos Chambers. Just grind grind grind grind. I gave up after 3rd one. They aren't even a challenge like raid bosses from Borderlands 2/TPS, just a swarm of enemies with a couple of tanks.If you think "well, there sure are DLCs that add more to the story" - don't bother, they just add a couple of cosmetics and new... you guessed it. _childDocuments_.review: Out of all the Borderlands games, this is the only one that I've actually liked enough to finish.Even though I'm not a huge D&D fan, the premise works so well here that it's hard not to get excited about the tabletop roleplaying themes. The piles of randomized weapons with unique stats and modifiers that have been a core part of the series feel even more at home in a universe known for its numerical strategy and equipment management. The Borderlands formula fits the D&D setup exceptionally well and Wonderlands is quick to capitalize on those RPG parallels.The imaginative environments of Wonderlands are much more visually inspired and are, as a whole, more thematically varied than what each Borderlands game has to offer. Wonderlands' overworld once again fits the tabletop premise perfectly and is a delightfully compact alternative to the bland, flat, and useless horizontal planes of previous games. A new form of overworld also means the second-rate vehicles are graciously absent from this game.The overall humor is admittedly a six or seven out of ten, but it's easy to forgive the game for simply being itself. And to give credit where credit’s due, the jokes that do land can work pretty well. Whereas other games in the series try to tell a grand story in the same space as the Porta-Pooper 5000, Wonderlands is focused on making up weird sh1t and telling a story that adequately fits the tone and energy of the made-up, ‘anything goes’ setting. It's more of a journey > destination situation whose emphasis on situational intrigue facilitates a lawless, low-stakes, and ’fun’ adventure.There are plenty of other tidbits that make Wonderlands a suitably entertaining shooter/co-op experience. Stuff like getting a second class, slick reload animations, memorable characters, gay skeletons, punny skeletons, well-composed environments, or the fact that they’ve shoved Claptrap off into completely ignorable sidequests. Just, whatever you do, don't buy any of the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: The pricepoint is absolutely absurd for what it is. This game has no replayability nor endgame, it starts off slow and picks up the pace and gets really good towards the end only to faceplant into a wall and squash itself. Classes have been deeply oversimplified to a point that there are only TWO trees and most of what the skills are simply boil down to number changes like increased crit or reload speed. This game is great for one playthrough but after that it falls flat completely, it fails to deliver on any end game or replayability and as an avid player of borderlands since 1 on the 360 im sad to say this is the first time i didnt even bother with getting all my weapons to max level. Most bosses fall into a simple "fight fight fight, its immortal now, wait for dialogue/animation, fight fight fight" which makes farming feel like a chore. EVERY quest is the same just about. _childDocuments_.review: After reading all of the mixed reviews I decided to pick this one up on sale along with all of its DLC for the extra $10. It's been a minute since I played Borderlands and Borderlands 2 and I'm not tabletop DnD player so I came into this with a limited expectations and a vague idea of what it was all about, and I can not say that I'm disappointed!The play style is familiar and comfortable and its easy to get back into the Borderlands groove again. The artwork is nostalgic to my early days as a gamer though the color pallet is far more vibrant and spashy. The story narrative is absolutely hilarious! It's creative and well delivered and full of twists that will blind-side you and keep you on your toes. The professional comedic voice acting is a cherry on top. It's not any reason to purchase the game but it sure doesn't hurt it. There are choices (and consequences) to your actions and whether you take that short cut to an objective or put in the effort and see a part of the story that would otherwise be left untold.Is it another 2K Borderlands game? Yes, but lets look at the roots of this one. It was a BL2 DLC that 2K decided was worth its own game. And they delivered! They took the Borderlands model (that works and has been successful) and re-skinned it. Then they added magic and fantasy and kept the guns. They gave it a paint job. And then they gave it full serving of comedy. They put all of that into a tabletop game and threw it into a box and called it Tiny Tina's Wonderlands and I'm not sorry to spend the $50 on it and it's 4 DLC on sale. Even at only 4 hours in at the time of this review, this has already become my new favorite game, and based on my previous Borderlands experience, I'll be playing this one for a very long time.In short, is it worth the price tag? For me, yeah. I was happy to dish out the $50 CDN on this one for the full game and the 4 DLC.[EDIT:] Now 80 Hours in and going for 100% completion. Can't say I'm bored yet, and I haven't even begun looking at the replayability of it with all of the viable class combinations. I stand by my original review. I'm happy with the amount of content here for the price I paid and I'm looking forward to putting in my next 80 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is an excellent take on a new idea for a series that has felt dry and repetitive. + Amazing setting+ Great voice acting+ Immersive sound + High fidelity environments+ Fluid gameplay- Few fast travel points- Dungeons can get repetitive- Loot is a hit or miss- Only a handful of spells- No postFX options in menu. Need a mod to disable Chromatic Aberration, DOF and VignetteSteam Curator: Overall, this game is what I personally believe the borderlands series needed to feel fresh. The pre sequel was a boring disaster, and Borderlands 3 felt like the same game, just more fleshed out. This gives us a setting that I have not seen in an FPS like this before. When the "players" interject as your mission goes on and add actually funny commentary, it gives a creative freedom to the game that I do not see often. The way the game is set up gives it the unique opportunity to get crazy, imaginative, and unique, without needing to make a lot of sense. Suspension of disbelief is very easily achieved because of this.My favourite moments in the game is when the dungeon master, Tina, comes up with some elaborate scheme to trick you, or to change a circumstance to suit the progression in a convenient way. There are also moments where the setting she comes up with is dodgy at best, but in reality she was not trying to trick anyone. Things backfire, and it makes for a surprisingly decent character development for the dungeon master, as well as the other players in the game. The story so far is fairly decent, with a funny villain that I cannot wait to get my hands on. There are no vehicles for exploration as you just traverse the main world hub as if you were a pawn on a tabletop game. This does however mean that the exploring in the actual mission maps might come at a deficit since you have to walk everywhere, and fast travel points are far fewer than I would prefer.It is notable however that the main areas are A TAD smaller than in B3, so the lack of a vehicle is not as impactful. The class system is also present and you can dual class after a certain point. Do not worry too much about which class you choose as your second class as changing it is possible.I have been putting a lot of hours in B3 on my Steam Deck primarily, and I was starting to feel the fatigue of just going through the game mindlessly. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is such a favourable setting, to me, that it takes away the monotony of just progressing through a game by making it a lot more interesting. I would highly recommend this game, especially on a deep discount. Currently under 20$ on Steam and that is a steal.Stay away from the DLC of this game however. Especially the season pass. Borderlands games have already been laughable at making good DLC and this is no exception. For more, consider subscribing and leaving a like, it goes a long way for me.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a game with first-person shooting, dungeon quest crawling, and item looting—you can get your kick by playing  While I’ve enjoyed watching this  franchise grow, TTW has its flair by incorporating tabletop functions, heavily verbose characters, and a right mix of goth and sparkle themes in its gameplay.It is not best to purchase with its original pricing since other better FPS loot games could offer better gameplay at their original price. But it is best to get a 70% discount—and, at the very least, get the main storyline. If you aim to get a complete Steam Achievement, the four quests are “cash locked” via four separate DLCs.Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands caters to players with varying levels of FPS experience. Whether you prefer rifles, SMGs, grenade launchers, melee weapons, or ward shields, there's a playstyle to suit you. The game offers diverse gameplay options with seven unique classes, including the Brr-Zerker and Clawbringer for melee enthusiasts and the Spellshot for those who enjoy a balance of gun skill and spell barrage. The ultimate goal in TTW is to complete the challenging dungeon quests and acquire better loot. This can be achieved by revisiting previously finished dungeons or exploring the four purchasable DLCs, adding depth and longevity to the game.  You are assigned as the Fatemaker who will change Brighthoof’s fate, as played through the “Bunkers and Badasses” tabletop game. As the game progresses, the tabletop characters (primarily the Dragon Lord) decide to take matters into their own hands, shifting how Tina (the tabletop’s Dungeon Master) plays the game. Tangential side quests also provide leverage on the overall storyline—by unveiling how improper tabletop gaming (in real life) could somehow create a sense of disillusionment on the game’s “pawns” (in this case, the characters build within the imaginary sense of Tina). Tina’s infantile, over-the-top reaction could not be for everyone’s kind of gameplay. It’s one of the drawbacks of this game—you may want to mute the dialogue because Tina and the rest of the tabletop players could talk a lot—like The  franchise heavily inspires the graphics—the dark and sharp black strokes give the 3D animation a cartoon feel. The visuals of the different regions are a sight to behold—there are times that I couldn’t stop using the Photo Mode function because it is just too majestic. The music is fine—I couldn’t appreciate it a lot because of the heavily condensed narration—the music could no longer be heard. However, walking alone in Brighthoof and other Fast Travel areas is excellent. It's not an entirely  moment, but at least the music fits the scenery. The end-game progression, also known as the , is striking but needs to be more varied (especially if you already acquired the Ascended-tier items). You can finally test your character’s acquired gear by fighting higher-tier enemies. It is heavily inspired by Borderland’s looting system (procedurally generated loot), which means a higher-tier enemy can improve the odds of dropping an Ascended gear (the highest quality). TTW’s additional DLCs  are unnecessary. They cost 20 to 30 minutes of new gameplay, which is not worth its hefty price tag. But if you’re a Steam Achievement completionist and want to try out Vesper’s Mirror of Mystery, you can include this in your collection. It's also one of the reasons why I can’t give it a solid 9 out of 10 rating.The  DLC can give you a more comprehensive array of equipment options; it is the only DLC I could recommend. The  is the worst DLC offer, as it could only give you a gold tint to your armor—and TONS of better color options are available within the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's is an amazing addition to the Borderlands world! The game has amazing voice acting, with Ashly Burch bringing her over the top character to life (Tina). Valentine and Frette are voiced by Andy Samberg and Wanda Sykes respectively. With Will Arnett rounding out the cast as the main antagonist. They have some great deliveries, and I found that the interactions themselves, while exaggerated, are very much in line with the conversations that happen around a D&D table.This chapter in the borderlands anthology definitely changes some things:* No True Vault Hunter: While I have seen a good deal of complaints about the lack of this mode in the game, I have to say that I found it a very welcome change. I have played every single borderlands since the first one, and I have always thought that the TVHM system was terrible. I like to play different characters and try different builds, but if I wanted to try a new character I had to push them through two playthroughs before I could even start really working on a build. This is a welcome change in my opinion and means that I only repeat quests and stories that I want to.* Chaos Chambers: This is very similar to the rifts in Diablo. They are a series of rooms that require you to defeat enemies or bosses with secondary challenges that yield additional results. I really liked this as it meant that I could pop in, do a couple of runs and then go back to work. Some people have been lamenting the fact that this is the best way to get gear in the game, but I think it is much more fun than killing the same boss for hours on end for that one specific drop you are praying for. I feel like both of these options gives you more options to play the way that you want. If you want to go and boss, then you absolutely can. They have dedicated drops and work much like the bosses of old borderlands. if you want to just do a little mobbing and a little bossing, grab a chaos chamber and enjoy! While not as involved as some of the other Borderlands games, it is a welcome addition to the world. I would highly suggest this game for people looking for a more casual looter shooter who don't feel like copying build files or grinding 18 hours a day. Enjoy the fun and blow some ♥♥♥♥ up!

_childDocuments_.review: It's somewhat passable as a time-killer, but it's nowhere near as good as ANY of the other Borderlands games.* The game constantly reminds you of "the message" when I just want to play a game.  It's not just once or twice, or subtle, I can count about a dozen such in-your-face examples only half-way through the campaign.  Clearly, someone in charge was far more interested in "the message" than making a good story or good game.* The 4th-wall role-playing aspects are like ripping you out of a dream, destroying your immersion in a very sudden and grating way.* Much of the magical or fantasy aspects are basically reskins of standard borderlands mechanics, but instead made confusing and poorly described.* The environments aren't very interesting compared to other Borderlands games.  Even environments that are different, feel the same.* Setting aside story locations, you spend about 1/2 the game in these "instances" which have no reason to explore. There's no loot-chests in them or reason to explore, it feels like a randomly generated small area, with randomly selected enemies.* Oh, and did I mention "the message"?  Because if the game didn't drive that point home enough, it'll make sure you get it eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: My friends and I had high hopes for this game starting out. It had a fun (though quite standard) fantasy atmosphere with a heaping serving of Borderlands style combat, which is really quite nice throughout the whole game. Plenty of interesting loadouts to be had here, though with a distinct D&D themed twist compared to the usual Borderlands formula: spells replace grenades, wards replace shields, and so on. Melee weapons are also much more prominent in Wonderlands. At first they seemed like a nice addition the Borderlands style of play, but they ended up being a bit redundant for me personally (why use sword when have shotgun?)Unfortunately the bland side quests, average dialogue, and the utterly repetitive and uninspired "encounters" that the game likes to throw at you slowly whittled away the fun. There were a few good moments for sure, but in the end it all just continued to wear us down to the point where we just wanted to get the silly main quest over with and be done with it (and even that was a complete let down).I would also recommend avoiding this game if you aren't at least a somewhat avid fan of D&D. Most of the jokes and character banter depend on scenarios and tropes that frequent the D&D meta (honestly the whole story could be seen as one giant commentary on the peculiar relationship that builds between players and the dungeon master.) Seriously, if you don't have experience playing D&D at a table with friends, all of that stuff will be lost on you. You will forfeit the narrative's one saving grace—the thing that was actually able to give me a chuckle sometimes—and you will have nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I bought the Chaotic Great Edition at 80% off and would recommend the game at THAT price but not at this game's base price.  I also have over 500 hours across the Borderlands series on Steam alone so I'm well grounded on the franchise.I'll start off with my own personal opinions -- have never played D&D before, so the main theme and dialogue of the game doesn't interest me too much. I also consider Tina to be+ by far one of the worst/cringiest characters in the franchise, so basing a whole game around her was hard to push through at times.  It also didn't help the entire game is narrated by Will Arnet, Andy Sandberg, and Wanda Sikes, and while I don't really have anything against them, their attempt at 'trying-too-hard-to-sound-funny' dialogue made it feel like I was playing through an SNL skit.  As an avid Borderlands fan I think it's safe to say Wonderlands is probably the worst entry in the entire series.  The game replaces the open world/vehicle elements with an 'overworld' where you become a funko pop variant walking from place to place. The Myth(or 'BA') Rank isn't even unlocked until max level, which really makes you work for what used to be available at all times in previous games.  And for the full edition players, the DLC are the absolute worst in the franchise.  Some other notable, but not terrible changes are the removal of canon characters replaced with a 'character class' system, which isn't too bad, and makes room for more playstyles, but takes the fun out of playing some of the series now iconic characters.The removal of the Grenade slot now replaced with a Spell slot, which I have found to be quite fun and actually enjoyed.Overall, for $60, buy every other Borderlands game instead...they're much better and have much more content, but if you can find the game on sale for about $20 it's worth the money for avid fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I overall loved this game.  The story was great!  Tina is my favorite character since she made her appearance and it's awesome seeing this feral character grow.  And as you can expect her storytelling for a roleplaying game is fantastic!The multiclassing is great, the chaos chambers is actually refreshing.  I finally don't have to hate going back into previous zones.  The chaos chambers are arena runs that are altered by buffs, debuffs, and purchased buffs.  The less purchased buffs you buy, the more RNG you get for gear at the end of the runs.  And the gear chance goes up with chaos levels to spawn Chaotic, Volatile, Primordial, and Ascended ranks of gear.  I think you will be done with the game quicker than most in the series.  But it really does feel better for multiplayer than it used to.Finding all of the lucky dice, marbles, poetry pages, scrolls and whatnot to maximize your bonuses for the chaos chamber grind can be tough, but it is more fun than looking for those vault logos.Cons:I will say that end game is definitely more focused on the elements than previous borderlands games.  I feel like there are too many mixes and layers of resistances in these arenas.  So it can be pretty overwhelming with constantly switching weapons to mow through all of the layers the adds throw at you.  The characters definitely need some damage penetration because you can't focus a damage type like you used to.  Like if I stacked a ton of frost damage it will still lower shield damage, just not as fast.  Well in this game, it starts to feel more like cutting through a brick wall with a plastic spoon than it did in previous games.Conclusion:If you liked the borderlands games, but didn't like going through the entire game twice doing normal and then bad a** difficulty to get the better gear, than this one will be more appealing.    I think this one finally dethroned the first borderlands as my favorite in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will be a word vomit, and the first game I write a review for that makes me wish Steam had an in-between rating rather than strictly yes/no.Tiny Tina's Wonderlands was a game I was very hyped for upon its announcement after playing the hell out of Borderlands 2. I love Dungeons and Dragons and fantasy settings, so seeing a looter shooter from Gearbox set in a fantasy world with Tina herself as the dungeon master? I said count me the hell in! I love Tina as a character, she's whimsical and funny and the right amount of crazy. Her voice actress is phenomenal, I love how she's brought Tina to life over the years.Going into gameplay, it's your typical borderlands looter-shooter. You kill tons of enemies, get loot, sell it (a lot) and optionally spend time grinding bosses for the specific loot you want. Nothing about the gameplay loop has changed here in that regard, but the class system brings a refreshing take in Wonderlands. I like the idea of mixing and matching the equally great classes in this game. I started the game as a spellshot/graveborn, and finished it on a second character as a sporewarden/clawbringer (love my little buddies.) The abilities they have and the trees you spec into are great, it's fun and varied. Take note of that second playthrough, though.As for story, it's hit or miss for some. I enjoyed what I got out of it, for the most part, but the ending was very very rushed. There was a buildup and suddenly you are being ushered to the final fight. Despite my playtime, the game is WICKEDLY short if you avoid the side quests (more on that later, too.) Because of this, I hate to say it, but DO NOT BUY THIS GAME AT FULL PRICE. It's sad to scream that, but this game simply does not have the content to justify $60. At best, it's a $30 game, so pick it up on sale. It's worth a playthrough, yes, but definitely on sale.Okay, now to the nitty-gritty. Look, just...don't bother with most of the side quests. There's really only a few that I enjoyed, those specifically being: Walk The Stalk (Though it overstays its welcome), Little Boys Blue, Lyre and Brimstone, Inner Daemons, Goblins Tired of Forced Oppression, Trial of Crooked-Eye Phil, A Walk To Dismember, and A Wandering Aye. There are more quests in the later game areas but I honestly didn't bother touching them at all because of one thing: MOST QUESTS IN THIS GAME ARE FETCH QUESTS. I despise fetch quests, and Wonderlands is laden with them. 90% of the time you pick up a side quest, it's to go get something for someone and bring it back. That's it.I mentioned a second playthrough, and that's because I gave up on my first one simply because of the overabundance of these lame fetch quests that were never worth the reward. I was level 32, made it to the third area of the game and just realized, sitting there, I wasn't having much fun outside of the main story. When it comes to Borderlands games, I LOVE the sidequests. They're engaging and have fun objectives and dialogue. This game's sidequests are just the same thing over and over and over again and I got really tired of it quickly. It killed the fun I was having running around and killing things because you'd go into a marked dungeon, clear waves of enemies across several rooms, get the item you need in a chest, dip out, and go back to the quest giver.The primary reason I came back to Wonderlands and finished it at all, honestly, is because I'm clearing my backlog while waiting for Lies of P. In the end, I am glad I finished it because the main story is fun, but outside of it, very little else is.So...there you have it. My probably spicy take on Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. Do I recommend it in the end? Yes, with an asterisk. Get it on a BIG sale, look up the worthwhile sidequests ahead of time, and stick your guns to the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: I had more fun with this standalone expansion than with the base Borderlands 3. I wish it was more RPG themed, with weapons based on medieval weaponry, but what you get is classic Borderlands' firearms with more pronounced melee and a bunch of useful spells. It isn't nearly as annoying as Borderlands 3 with its brat-twin-duo, TIna as a gamemaster is a genius idea (if you know the character and her background) and takes chaos to another level but if you're looking for an epic story, just be aware that the plot's importance is marginal here.Also, dividing the game's world into smaller instances is a plus for me. You can achieve something and progress and get a sens of accomplishment even if you take shorter sessions.If you're wondering if the DLCs are worth your money - they are not. The laziness behind these DLCs is beyond me. All of them are divided into arenas, have time-filling quests and offer nothing but unique bossfights (and supposedly unlock some stuff in chaos levels).The formula of Tina's Wonderlands lasted for 50 hrs in my case, after that and a few runs of chaos levels, getting the same legendaries over and over again, I gave up. Nevertheless, I recommend to get it on sale, especially if you've got some friends to join you for 30-50 hour-long adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review, i have, for all intents and purposes, completely cleared the game. Every quest and side quest, every collectible, every piece of DLC. I have done so partly out of spite and partly out of a desire to make this review as thorough as possible.Unlike previous games in the franchise, where you choose a character with 3-4 skill trees to play around with, Wonderlands instead has you choose a Class: classes have two Action Skills to choose from and one single Skill Tree. After a certain point in the campaign, you're able to choose a secondary Class and choose from their skill tree and Action Skill. The maximum level is 40, and you have a total of 44 Skill Points to play around with.The first major issue with this system: not enough Skill Points to experiment with builds. 44 skill points are enough to reach the final skill in a single class' Skill Tree and reach the 4th tier of skills in another (barely). Builds, as such, are basically always the same: you can't afford to experiment with different playstyles or skill choices.Secondly: quite a few classes have zero synergy between them: often times you're forced to get skills you have no use for just so you can reach another tier. Worst of all, the skill trees themselves are boring and poorly designed, and there is no skill support for many playstyles. Here's an example:The Spore Warden is the closest thing to a sniper class the game has. Its passive grants it a Mushroom Companion which deals Poison (Corrosive) damage and its skills are centered around Critical Hits. I'll discuss a few skills which I believe exemplify its poor design.Quiver of Holding: Increases magazine size for all guns by 30% and grants them constant ammo regen (9% of the mag/second). Wrath of Nature: Enemies hit by Ability Damage take 30% increased damage from all sources. Play the Angles: Scoring a Gun Critical Hit has a 35% chance of making the bullet ricochet towards a nearby enemy, dealing Ability Damage. Sniper rifles as an archetype have small magazine sizes, fire slowly (barring a few exceptions) and deal a lot of damage: therefore they don't benefit from Ammo Regen and don't proc ricochets often enough to benefit from Wrath of Nature. Using a Sniper Rifle on the *only class* that has significant buffs to Critical Damage is a complete waste of time, because you're better off using something with a large magazine size and high fire rate, like an AR, pistol or SMG. Here's another example: the Clawbringer. It lacks damage bonuses to make it competitive with other classes, its action skills take too long to be usable, its action skill augments are worthless, some skills just do nothing (Indomitable), and what buffs it has to Companions are exclusive to its own companion and don't benefit others in any way. The lack of support for different playstyles is noticeable: non-elemental guns are almost universally outclassed when so many characters are based around specific damage types. The Blightcaller's entire skill tree revolves around status effects, the Clawbringer relies on fire and lightning, the Graveborn needs black magic to keep itself alive, the Brr-zerker benefits from stacking Cold damage: you're almost always better off using an element.Borderlands started off as an FPS, and while it's completely understandable and even commendable to have the franchise branch off in another direction, guns in Wonderlands feel like an afterthought. The addition of "proper" melee combat is certainly something. On one hand, being able to customize exactly how your character uses its melee attack is very fun and interesting, and opens up a lot of build variety (even for gun builds! you can use melee weapons as utility tools). On the other, it's another layer of grinding and even more items to dilute a boss' loot pool. In addition to melee weapons, Wonderlands also introduces Spells, which replace grenades. They're cooldown-based rather than ammo-based, so they feel a lot more spammable. Spells and melee combat are very clearly the main focus when it comes to skill tree support. As previously mentioned, the Spore Warden is the only class with significant gun buffs: though some other classes have skills that benefit gunplay (the Blightcaller's Geist in the Shell and part of the Spellshot's tree) the emphasis for almost every other character is either melee or spell combat. Even the Spellshot, whose final skill gives him a chance to instantly reset his spell cooldowns upon scoring a gun critical hit, is better off spamming Spells (usually Laserhands). Though playing with guns is viable (yes, even non-elemental ones), the gunplay generally feels bad: every attack (whether gun, melee, or spell) has a chance of critically hitting, so aiming for headshots isn't as rewarding because you can just spam bodyshots and be just as effective. Some enemies actively disencourage aiming for Crits: Cyclops have their critical spots disappear after taking a certain amount of damage and become Enraged, dealing increased damage and moving faster. Unlike Goliaths in BL2, where removing their helmets exposed a crit spot, Cyclopi are impossible to crit outside of random crit procs after their eye is destroyed. More than anything else, guns feel bad:
