_childDocuments_.review: The game honestly does not deserve the hate its getting, Yeah their are issues but it is a good game.The story is much MUCH better than 3, The Dragonlord is soo many league better than the twitch/Youtube meta characters that ruled Bdl3, Not wanting to burst your own eardrums with a pitchfork when the villains start talking is already a huge plus but even beyond that I just think its a good story, It starts like dragonkeep but then the story gets away from her and starts to do its own thing, Thats great.The gameplay is well fine, If you liked Bdl3 then you will like it here not much if anything has changed, Grenades are nameswapped to spells and they exchange ammunition for cooldowns, Its good twitchy fun, I personally prefer the slower more tactical combat in Bdl1 or 2 but it's not gearbox moreso than the times, Twitch shooters are the thing now and either you deal or look elsewhere, The class system is great, I think better than 3's, Things feel pretty good there, Survival can be frustrating, Health skills are throttled which is good for build variety but the number of times you go from full health to death save in what feels like a single hit even on normal is a bit much, Still it was like that is Bdl3 as well and its not throw fists level of frustrating, The chaos dungeons are interesting, I feel like overall they are a good pic for the setting but they really need higher exp and loot rewards, Finishing one especially early on feels very anemic and unrewarding, The endgame I haven't reached yet but i've seen enough youtube vids to know its those just cranked up which is a problem with all borderlands not just wonderlands, Gearbox has been struggling with endgame since 2 and I don't think an easy solution will be seen, Op/mayhem/chaos levels, Call em whatever you want it's the same thing we have seen in every Bdl game to date, Either you like it or you don't, You know what your getting into at this point.The dlc, I haven't got much exp with this so take it with a grain of salt but from what I can see they are all more contained chaos dungeons which in of itself isn't terrible but for the price I definately think they should have more story and better loot attached, Still it is what it is and you can absolutely ignore all of them and just enjoy the base game, You will lose nothing so its not worth dragging down the games score over.So yeah after all that I would give it around an 8 out of 10, It's good, Imo worse than 2 but better than the pre-sequel and 3, Probably about even with 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth it while it's on sale, but don't bother with DLCs, especially at full price. This entry into the series is by far the least polished, with multiple bugs found throughout a relatively short (for a borderlands game) campaign. There was surely more to the story at some point, but it must have been cut, because I beat the campaign in about 8 hours (don't let my playtime fool you, i left my pc on idle over three play sessions). When you think of completing all the quests (both main and side) in a Borderlands game, you envision an endeavor that may take weeks, if not a month or two, as each location is overflowing with side quests. In Tiny Tina's wonderland, each map has <6 side quests, meaning that my 2nd playthrough (100% quests on Intense mode) only took me about a day. A Borderlands pro can probably knock it out in an afternoon.The game had the potential to be a lot more than what it ended up being, but with the pandemic interrupting the development process and everyone having to work from home... well, let's just say it shows. Still, a pretty fun experience, wouldn't want to pay full price though. Unfortunately the devs released extremely buggy and lackluster DLCs and then abandoned this game, so don't hold out any hope for future updates. There is little to do post-game, as they replaced TVHM/UVHM with an endless "chaos" dungeon which borrows heavily from the roguelike genre. It's honestly not worth the effort though, as by this point you are earning incremental (like, 1%) buffs to your stats (as the level cap is a ridiculously low lvl40), and there isn't anything to DO with the guns you get from the chaos runs except do more chaos runs. It's fun for a few, but quickly feels shallow and repetitive.  Likely the team is working on the next installment in the Borderlands franchise, and honestly I didn't mind all the flashy spells and lack of gore, I actually prefer the spells to grenades as they are more powerful and easier to control, but the writing suffered from the ESRB restrictions. I hope they abandon the T for Tina rating and go back to their roots, a full-length M rated Tiny Tina's 2 would be at the top of my wishlist. 8/10 on sale6.9/10 if you're paying full price and buying the dlcsback up to 8.5/10 with the Redux mod

_childDocuments_.review: So far game is fun and enjoyable. From hearing other reviews of the game being "Too short" but I do so where there's more time into the game.Sidequests. Ya know, some people hate the term sidequests, but this game is D&D spinoff game. This game fleshes out sidequests more, whether you're helping an organization for their freedom with a funny acronym, helping an individual find love, or creating Forgery through... the other forgery... This game puts its emphasis more on exploring different things just as much as it does the main story, and with good rewards no less.As for the gameplay of the characters itself, without too much spoilers, Build flexibility is much more interesting in this game, and using spells instead of grenades feels much more diverse than previous borderland entries. The spells aren't just fun, they're good, and can have more than one purpose. They can do damage, plus heal, or give a damage bonus, or have a lingering effect. The same spell type can also be a variant, and not just because of element either, which is great. This isn't even regarding legendary types which also can be interesting.In the end, Game's great. People who complain about price tag probably forget what the other borderlands were like on immediate release, or don't understand that this game isn't meant to bolt through just the main story to actually enjoy the whole game. There is post content to do, replayability especially if you want to go around testing different classes/jobs/builds. I definitely will be putting more hours into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on sale for $30 and it was the perfect price. This game isn't worth $60 but has enough value in it to be bought at $30. This is fantasy mixed with Borderlands. I personally enjoyed the main story line and the side quests were entertaining and enjoyable. The fantasy setting is engaging, the monsters are awesome, and the Overworld setting mixes well with the actual game. I beat the game in a good 20 hours and it was a blast!There are a few shortcomings with Tiny Tina's Wonderlands. The main one being the lack of legendary loot. I play these games for the thrill of seeing a legendary item drop and having the icon pop up on the map. In my 20 hours of beating the game, only TWO legendary items dropped before the final fight. I received two more from quests but still, only TWO legendary items dropping in 20 hours of game play is unacceptable. You can argue that this makes greens/blues/purples more balanced but I don't like having to sift through hundreds of weapons to find the right one. When I saw the trailer for this game and the dice rolls I thought they had so much potential to drop good loot but they feel so underwhelming. The loot is easily the biggest problem with the game but everything else is amazing. Another shortcoming is the credits. Why are there 20+ minutes of FORCED credits? I'm all for appreciating the developers for the game but when I'm having to sit there for 20-30 minutes and I can't get out that feels real bad. Other reviews mentioned LBGQT being forced down their throats during the game but I didn't notice it (probably because I didn't play with sound for most of it). There's some characters here and there that are LBGQT but overall it doesn't feel pushy. In conclusion, this game was a lot of fun for what it is - a Borderlands game mixed in a fantasy world. The story and side quests are at their best but the loot feeling so underwhelming is a clear issue. Also, the credits... WHYFinal Score: 8/10-1.5 for lackluster loot-0.5 for 20+ minutes of forced credits

_childDocuments_.review: Review is based off of an almost 100% solo playthrough and coop playthrough, first 3 Mirrors of Mystery completed and Chaos Chamber up to 30 as of writing this, but I feel like I've experienced everything the game has to offer, so I'll just list the pros and cons like Borderlands 3Pros:Spells are fun to use, pretty refreshing compared to how montonous BL3's grenades wereGame is more technically stable than BL3, less bugs, crashes and frame dropsMelee ravamps have some nice touches like having bonus effects when hitting enemiesEnvironments are nice looking, Fear-amid and the Necropolis were my favourite sectionsClass customisation is interesting, especially since the secondary class can be changedSidequests are unique in their design that rely off the RPG and fantasy settingCons:Gameplay has regressed in almost every single way when compared to BL3. Guns don't feel nearly as satisfying to use, melee has improved and downgraded since lunge is now unreliable and ground pound is still bad, UI is worseEnemy damage and balancing is absolutely bonkers, even without Chaos levels my health was constantly reaching healthgate threshold, it only gets worse on Chaos levels where death is almost guaranteed. Enemy density is also very miniscule resulting in being forced to wait for enemies to spawn just to fight encounters.Endgame is really boring, Chaos Chamber is not fun to grind and repeats issues I have with BL3 Mayhem Mode and BL2 OP Lvls, Myth Ranks only want me to invest in one tree but I have to invest in all fourPersonally I did not find the story very engaging and wasn't invested in, when the story finished I only had the, "thank goodness it's finally over" feelingEquipment loadouts is pretty boring as well and generally only functions as stat checks for your characterThe Mirrors of Mystery are way too overpriced for DLC, functioning only as a singular level that can be repeated three times with minimal changes, the lost souls currency is also not motivatingOverall traversal is neutered with minimal fast travel and Overworld doesn't change enough IMOCollectibles is incredibly irritating and forced, Lucky Dice are the worst to search for and are bugged if playing with coopPersonally this game is easily the worst entry in the Borderlands franchise, each game has an element that makes it superior against the other entries, however Wonderlands offers nothing for me that the other Borderlands games have already given and on top of that downgrades everything that I like about the series. It was a chore from start to finish. I understand that the game was made in lockdown and compromises have to be made, but that doesn't forgive the design decisions that went into this game. I cannot recommend this game to anyone, casual players or hardcore Borderlands fans.

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of Borderlands storytelling, nothing has beat Borderlands 2. That being said, Wonderlands is second on my list of favourites, and most definitely the most accessible entry into the game. What I love about this game is that it has it's own unique charm without desperately trying to recapture the lighting in a bottle of BL2 (like BL3 and BL:TPS flopped at pretty hard). The character customisation is enormous, the DnD memes don't demand that you play DnD (unlike EVERY other DnD inspired game on Steam) and the gun-play is fresh without sacrificing the aesthetic styles or standardised controls of other games in the series. Guns are pretty unique and you're able to very well start a build around just about any gun without there being large balance gaps. Unless you go look on Youtube for a min-max build, but that's not much in the spirit of Wonderlands. The game itself has the classic Borderlands open-world regions that the series has done so well, but they've also implemented a very cool overworld feature as well as some fast travel options so you can walk on foot and solve puzzles with your bobble-head statuette before jumping into arenas to fight hordes for loot rewards. There's a good balance between exploration and accessibility without relying on fast-travel loading screens. Also if you hadn't heard, Andy Samberg (Lonely Island, Brooklyn 99) and Wanda Sykes (Ice Age, lots of comedy) are both companion voice actors that talk around the player, and Will Arnett (Arrested Development, Bojack Horseman) is the salty antagonist. In summary, is good. HumbleBundle gave me a nice half price when the Steam sales weren't on. It's worth the play, if you want a comprehensive Shooter-RPG or to be thrown into a DOOM arena and get shinies for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from someone who has 1000+ hours in BL2, nothing will re-live those glory days, but I got this game (Chaotic Great Edition) at a 83% discount, I'm safe to say that I'm very happy with my purchase. If you don't like Tiny Tina as a character though, this game will certainly drag. I adore the character I met in BL2 and this felt like a very natural extension of that original Bunker's and Badasses DLC.I don't know if i'd enjoy more play throughs, I think the gameplay is probably good enough to justify trying another class, but my current time is limited to actually try that (There was no obvious new game plus which makes me a little sad).I can't imagine paying full price for it, so take my review with a grain of salt! And finally, the DLC's were very meh, I only paid a tiny bit for them so I feel fine about that I would rather not have the FOMO - honestly I could've skipped them, they're very quick, tiny irrelevant stories with no meat to them and combat is just re-skins with one "interesting" boss encounter at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderland has a lot to offer and is in keeping in many ways to the Borderlands series. However the game still manages to fall short in many ways. The core game is really enjoyable and will have you engaged for many hours, the humour is on point for what you should expect from the franchise as a whole. The major pit falls with Tiny Tina's Wonderlands are the DLCs and the story as a whole. The DLCs are short, and I mean very short. They have attempted to pad the play time out with increasing difficulty options but if like me you turn to DLCs after the main gain then you will fly through these and they become annoying to have to do them each four times over. The story also seems lacking and at times like they padded it out to make the game a bit longer, very similar feeling to that of the DLCs.However, if you take in to consideration that this game is the successor of a small DLC from an earlier game then everything begins to make much more sense, and in turn feel less disappointing. I feel that it is unfair to hold Tiny Tina's Wonderlands up against the main series games as it simply cannot compete. However, as a successor to the Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep it has done an amazing job with one exception, the price.If you buy this game on sale, I am talking 50% or more off, then I would say it is a great game for the money. Otherwise give it a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: So, you want to read a review of Borderlands game huh? Coming right up like pizza in a restaurant you’ve eaten quite many times. This time a Borderlands entry was only three months EGS exclusive and Randy has apparently been too focused on upcoming Borderlands movie-adaptation that there wasn’t such a PR-cluster♥♥♥♥s like we witnessed with Borderlands 3 so great improvement on that area!It’s hard to come up big improvements over Borderlands 3. There’s still weapons with weakest recoil ever, making gunplay feel still quite boring. Mayhem mode is gone, replaced with random generated small roguelite expeditions. I’m a fan of said sub-genre but I still preferred Mayhem mode over these expeditions. And even when writing team had more freedom with this title due to DnD-session nature, I feel I laughed more on my seven hours Borderlands 2: Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep DLC than 18 hours with this game. As for change of spaceship to overworld traveling I’m not sure. While overworld is something new to quite stagnated Borderlands-franchise at this points, there’s no more vehicles to drive with, making moving with foot only option to move in this game.As for rest changes/ additions with sub-glasses, re-roll of gun/ equipment bonuses, hand grenades replaced with spells my opinion of those is most simply phrased “eh” with no huge benefit felt during my playthrough over previous entries.Tiny Tina Wonderlands is small bits of new to Borderlands-franchise, which those whom are fine with franchise’s gameplay have a good time with. As for those who wished that after Borderlands 3 Gearbox would have taken lessons back from Borderlands 2 writing/ tone will likely still feel disappointed as with third installment of main Borderlands franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't take this game seriously, its amazing, genuinely. Im a huge fan of the borderlands series, I put countless hours into every single game entry on my PS4 back when the handsome collection came out. Honestly this might be my favourite game since BL2. Let me explain. First I'll start with the setting, characters, story, etc. At first I wasn't really buying the whole D&D vibe of the game, but as I kept playing I found myself getting more and more sucked into the world; the RPG mechanics are surprisingly deep, and the developers are really in their element here with the "D&D parody" vibe of the game. To me the biggest draw of Borderlands was always how silly and fun it was, the characters that lost me with the bland story of Borderlands 3 have slowly showed me why I love this series to begin with over the course of the game. Seriously, I haven't laughed like this at a Borderlands game in forever. Borderlands 3 didn't make me crack a single smile (which was honestly my biggest complaint about BL3, it really lost the funny aspect for me). Also I gotta say the graphics are GORGEOUS. I haven't seen a Borderlands game look this good EVER. The environments are enchanting and beautiful, and the design of the enemies is believable yet creative (Again, another complaint about BL3, the enemies in that game were bland as hell). Also I gotta say, the sidequests in this game are the best. They are funny, creative, and challenging. Yet another big draw for me when it comes to Borderlands was the variety of sidequests that unlike other games; felt as if they actually impacted the world and absorbed you into the game more rather than just being random BS you have to do to get more experience or gold or whatever. You definitely will not get bored running around the world doing quests for the people of the Wonderlands and will run into a lot of things  that make you think "Did that really just happen?" while you're laughing your ass off.Now the gameplay. Like I said, the RPG mechanics in this game are pretty in depth, at the cost of less varieties in skill trees, you get the multiclass system and "hero points" (basically like badass rank but more inspired by D&D). The multiclass system adds a ton of variety to the game, I sat for 2 hours trying to decide what to make my second class lmao and I instantly knew I was gonna be coming right back for another playthrough to try more combinations. The hero points really help sell the whole "character sheet" idea to the progression system very well. Despite what many other people think, the biggest weakness this game has for me personally is the spell system. While yes, the spells are interesting in their own right and are very flashy and cool; a good amount of the spells feel very clunky to use and sometimes come with bugs and glitches. The gunplay is like any other Borderlands game really, you know what you're signing up for, Gearbox never really misses when it comes to this, you get some new stuff like crossbows which is cool but its pretty typical. The coolest addition is the new melee weapons; they are very flashy, have tons of cool abilities and stats and definitely add another layer of complexity to the game. I've always wanted to see something like this in the series and I hope it comes back in a future entry. Overall,  Id definitely recommend to anyone if its on sale, but thats just most games nowadays really. Pick this game up if you are willing to just turn your brain off and forget any expectations you have for a Borderlands game. If you've never played Borderlands before; great. Even better. This is a solid introduction to the series (though you will miss lots of funny references)

_childDocuments_.review: "Welcome to Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, where the Borderlands series decided to drop acid and crash a Renaissance Faire.Our story begins with Tiny Tina, a character who makes the Joker look like a model of mental stability, as your dungeon master. Buckle up, buttercup, because this ride is wilder than a hydra on a rollercoaster.The game throws you into a world that's part high fantasy, part fever dream. Imagine Lord of the Rings, but directed by Quentin Tarantino on a Skittles binge. You'll fight mushroom people, skeleton pirates, and creatures that look like they escaped from a nine-year-old's notebook doodles.The guns? Oh, the guns. They're as varied and ridiculous as the cast of a reality TV show.Character customization is deeper than a philosopher's midlife crisis. You can mix and match classes like a mad scientist, creating abominations of power that would make even the most min-maxing D&D player blush.The humor is relentless, hitting you faster than a caffeinated hummingbird. Puns fly like arrows, pop culture references explode like grenades, and fourth-wall breaks happen so often, you'll wonder if the wall ever existed in the first place.But beware: extended gameplay may result in an inability to take anything seriously ever again. Side quests will have you questioning your life choices.Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is a chaotic masterpiece that's more addictive than unicorn cheese (which is probably a thing in this game). Just be prepared for a fantasy romp that's more unhinged than a mimic's jaw. You'll blast your way through a world where unicorns fart rainbows, goblin hordes drop loot like piñatas, and the laws of physics are more flexible than a bard's morals.Warning: Side effects may include uncontrollable laughter, an inexplicable craving for cheese puffs, and the urge to shout 'EXPLOSION!' at inappropriate moments.4 out of 5 stars - Would've been 5, but my therapist says I need to stop encouraging chaos."

_childDocuments_.review: Roll 3d20+5 for firepower!After playing the standalone Assault on Dragon Keep DLC for Borderlands 2 I had caught the bug and Tiny Tina´s Wonderlands is everything I would wish for in a full blown game version of the DLC and more. After so many people were disappointed with Borderlands 3 this is a definite return to form in terms of humor, storytelling and just overall gameplay fun. They took the good innovations from 3 and packaged it in a very charming and character driven game with a lot of nerdy humor and jokes that every DnD player will instantly recognize. Throw to that a lot of funny references, great comedic voice acting and beautiful environments and you are sure to have a good time.Also you finally get to Blow up the Ocean!Gameplay and gunplay feel very smooth and rewarding with a lot of ways and options to design your character and what kind of build you want. With the weapons and spells, which replace grenades, being so ubiquitous and varied every new weapon box or beaten elite enemy can give you something that will influence your combat and raw power. You also feel very mobile and fast on your feet which adds to the rush of the game.Technically it is pretty solid and in around 50 gameplay hours I only had one hard crash and a handful of bugs and glitches, mostly connected to things on the screen not going away when they should but that is usually solved with a quick restart or similar.Reload your guns and upcast magic missile to lvl 20! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It work fine as a pure spin-off, if you have low expectationsabsolutely unworthy of BL4, but there is good fun in this self-contained gameMain Story: Short, and don't really tell much. Hero's Journey that tries to make it deep or with some twist, but kinda pointless in the end. Below average but not uncomfortable.Completed  in 15Hr, and the devs really try to make you do side quests by making giant gaps between story region to force you into do side regions, or being underleveled - a real shame since the side areas are actually well made and should be introduced more than a giant XP bundle.Side Story: Ranging from Good to straight up Grinds, but in some side quests you can feel Dev actually have TTRPG experience and there are many jokes can seem random to people not played it(players over investigating, DM forgetting to add hints to puzzle section, etc).Gameplay: Smooth as BL3, except most of the shotguns are so bloody ugly. The whole "cauldron as a gun" design would work better as a heavy weapon instead of shotgun, and the reload animation just doesn't really has the kick of reloading the good ol' double barrel.Change of Gameplay: Making Grenades as "spell" may be my favorite change for the game play, making those items much more than just a damage stick to throw out, every school of spells has their own modifers to further spice things up.The overworld section feel not really done properly, the dungeon and camp sections are just reused arena. I don't like them, but would give them a pass since those random encounter is kinda common in TTRPG too. (Good thing even random encounters can be skipped by punching the ambusher icon)Build Variety: Smaller, maybe worse? Making every class have a single tree greatly limited the amount of choices you have for playing an archetype, but allow you to take two class at the same time make some fun time trying to make them work together. Shame you can only have 1 active action skill though. Characters:For in-game character, it is beyond hopeless. Perhaps because it is so focused on the actual Players, there is 0 developed characters since all of them only exist in a single region with no further connection, even the final boss doesn't have anything interesting at all.Visual and Art style: I would say it is surprisingly good. _childDocuments_.review: According to Steam it's been almost exactly one year since I played Tina Tina's Wonderlands. In all that time I never even considered writing a review. You know why? Tina Tina's Wonderlands (TTW) is a looter shooter, like all of the Borderlands main series (a series that's now in its fifth iteration, and one that ran out of gas after the second). TTW, like most of its predecessors, features numerous fun guns; terrible, bland, skill-less, samey combat; "humorous" characters; and a story without meaning or impact. It is absolutely not worth your time.There is nothing to say about the gameplay. It is identical to all other Borderlands games. You kill mobs that spawn in areas, move on to new areas, and repeat forever. Occasionally you kill a boss. That boss might even have a weakspot you need to aim for, but you don't have to if you don't want to. There is nothing mechanically challenging or interesting in the moment-to-moment gameplay, although it  hilarious to note that sniper rifles have fallen into complete uselessness in Borderlands because actually aiming well and hitting a weakspot on an enemy is not just unnecessary but actively worthless.There is a new endgame gameplay mode that's just a Slay the Spire ripoff featuring an endless grind. I'm glad I played TTW after several patches, because it used to be even worse, apparently. You might find this mode fun if you aren't tired of games throwing random enemies into a room and then letting you pick a track with random boons and curses after you've cleared said room, but I've played that style of mechanic a dozen times now and I'm over it.Gearing, despite the plethora of interesting guns and an RPG-style multiclassing system, is the most simple and boring it's ever been in Borderlands. Rather than finding interesting synergies between guns and gear, like in previous games, TTW is mostly about just having the same enchantment on all of your weapons, which is only difficult becasue you need to grind the Slay the Spire mode to get the currency to reroll enchantments.Story is where TTW gets truly baffling. The conceit is that the player is sitting down to play a tabletop RPG session with Tina, an insane teenager. This should lead to quirky-fun storytelling, right? Wrong, it's mostly boring and nonsensical. The Big Bad literally makes no sense: he is Tina's former character who - as she's now Dungeon Master - she has turned into the antagonst of the tabletop game you, the player, is playing. But  the context of her game, the Big Bad has become self-aware that he's in a game and is talking to the player. Somehow. No one else at the table hears him, and Tina isn't directing him. The literal character in the tabletop game is talking to you. This isn't a 4th wall break or anything; it's just idiotic.But wait! This is a comedy game, right? Borderlands is famously irreverent. I'm sure there are plenty of great jokes about tabletop games and the way they're played and the people who play them that make up for all of this, aren't there? No, there are not. There is surprisingly little humor about TTRPGs at all, actually. Most of the jokes come in the form of banter between the people sitting at the table. I can only recall one quest, one single time, that was actually about the way players act when playing TTRPGs. And you know what? That quest was funny. That's why it's literally the only quest I can remember now, one year later.Also, special mention for a collection quest that runs through the entire game filling you in on the tragic backstory of an NPC that you .Well, I guess I lied at the start of this review. There was something to say, and it was the same thing I've said before: all told, this Borderlands game isn't worth your time. A bad story, uninteresting characters, boring combat, and braindead itemization make Tina Tina's Wonderlands just another Borderlands game for the garbage pile.P.S.: The DLC was once again horrible as well. Worst yet, actually. Four one-stage levels that you need to beat  to unlock the rewards from them you'd actually want. Just terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands – A Fun Fantasy Twist on the Borderlands FormulaTiny Tina’s Wonderlands is an absolute blast! If you love the Borderlands series, this spin-off takes everything great about it—guns, looting, chaotic combat—and adds a fresh layer of fantasy with spells, mythical creatures, and a hilarious D&D-inspired world.The blend of shooting and magic feels unique and super fun, with six different classes that let you experiment with your playstyle. The environments are gorgeous and full of detail, from enchanted forests to grand castles. Plus, Tiny Tina’s wild narration keeps things unpredictable and endlessly entertaining.Whether you’re playing solo or with friends in co-op, this game is full of action, laughs, and surprises. Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys fast-paced combat and a quirky, fantasy-filled adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: More fun with friends!    Borderlands games are always more fun when you have more people to play with, and this one is no exception. Instead of having the three trees for each character like Borderlands games before this one, there are eight character classes, a character creator, and cross classing! Instead of grenades you have spells because you are not playing a regular borderlands game, You are playing a character in a Tabletop Game inspired world with everyone's favorite demolition specialist at the wheel, Tiny Tina.     Expect weird things to happen throughout the story of the game because it is Tiny Tina's world. However, the amount endgame content is rather small. After the main story quests are complete, all there really is to do is try out other class combos, rack up chaos & mythic levels, fight raid bosses, or run through the DLC dungeons, which do not take long.    A good game to goof off and laugh with your friends as you approach the inevitable Borderlands experiences of making anything that dares enter your line of sight fly off into the distance. This time, with a character of your own creation, spells, and cross classing.

_childDocuments_.review: When the game is working as it is supposed to, it's some of the most fun I've had with a Borderlands game, when it functions the way it does the other 80-90% of the time, it is one of the worst gaming experiences I've ever had.*Bugs that make accessibility options not work or not work as intended*Regular crashing and freezing*1 out 10 of those crashes will give you an error that corrupts your character and deletes all of your progress*Connection issues that make it very difficult to play with others*The game does not allow you to cancel joining a game once it starts trying to connect you, even if it tells you in the top right corner of the screen that the connection failed, you will have to sit there for several minutes until the game releases you from its failed attempt, that you and it already know it has failed*It is very rare, but when enough effects are happening on screen, your frames will dip and you'll have a heart attack thinking that you're about to lose all of the hours you've put in to your character*Some side quest progression and overworld progression doesn't save properly when playing with others*Missing items or characters to quests, crashes causing you to have to restart quests*Some times the game will just decide to minimize itself, and when you bring it back up, it will go away after a second or two, and you repeat this multiple times until it randomly fixes itself*If you have other programs that like to update, or have any pop-up messengers, they will not just appear under the game like usual, they will pop up and the game will close entirely (This one probably won't effect most people)*Be very careful when adjusting things in your options, because some weird things can happen, and some times its hard to tell what issues are being caused by what.On top of that, there are also parts of the game that function as intended, but are downgrades from previous installments, or are straight up just missing quality of life features that existed before, making certain parts of the game that were fast and helpful, grind to a halt.*You will never use vending machines to purchase items because the equipment sold is worse then anything you'll find in the game, and the pricing is outrageous*Trying to compare equipment in the shop to your own equipment is tedious unlike other installments*Trying to go through your equipment to equip the best gear in your inventory is tedious, because the menus make sure you have to press several more buttons than needed (if using a controller)*The class abilities and skill trees are limited to 2, and the level maximum is unnecessarily low, especially when there are so many different combinations of two classes you could put togetherThis may not be everything me and my friends have experienced so far, but it is all I can remember at the moment of writing this. Some of you may have been lucky and not experienced any of this, or maybe you were having so much fun that you didn't notice some of the poor design choices, but all of the issues I've stated happened at least once to each of us, me and the two other players who purchased the game with me, and all of us have PCs that are able to run this game on its highest settings without issue, the problems are definitely coming from the game itself. We bought the game when it was on sale, which did include all the DLC.We have not yet interacted with all of the DLC yet, most of what we have played is really fun dungeons, but very short (a little under an hour to a little over, each)They are dungeons with about 5 to 6 rooms, per DLC (again, from what I've seen so far), you can play through them several times each, where the only difference seems to be the difficulty of the boss at the end of the dungeon. And again, these have been a lot of fun, but if you didn't get them in a deal like we did, they are not worth the $10 per. they are currently being sold for.This game has been a roller-coaster. If they were to fix all the issues, it could be my favorite of the franchise, but I believe the last time I checked the game came out 3 years ago, which means, if they aren't fixed yet, they never will be.I still plan to finish the game, and play through most of the optional content, as long as the game itself allows me.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands seemed to struggle to truly find its identity and is left feeling as though it desperately leans on the formula that made previous Borderlands titles majorly successful, whilst it does attempts to build on said formula none of it’s new features ever truly seem to shine through as phenomenal additions and even begun to feel jarring towards the games conclusion. With that said it isn’t all bad the games looter shooter design and gunplay mechanics make it undeniably fun to mow down waves of enemies but is never truly enough for Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands to identify as anything more than a carbon copy of all the other entries in the Borderland series.Right from the Opening Credits Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands oozes with the colourful charm and on the nose humour that its predecessors were beloved for, however I couldn't help but feel as though the writers had limited their sense of creativity by binding themselves to the theme of Dungeons and Dragons, this is felt exponentially through it’s main campaign that at times felt stale, uninspired, and as if the writers never truly knew where to go with the games overall story and theme. What started as a very tongue in cheek take on the self proclaimed “Worlds Greatest Roleplaying Game”, pretty quickly became a handful of jokes about the most common tropes and clichés that have been recited to death in other forms of media. On many occasions I found myself pulled from my enjoyment by one of these various clumsily delivered quips that left me wanting for something more that didn’t feel like a second hand joke that had been pulled from the mouth of someone much more charismatic. The main campaign felt rushed and as though the inclusion of side quests was only to extend the average time it takes to reach the story's climax. At the time of review I have spent just under 20 hours in Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands with roughly over half of that spent deviating from the main campaigns path in order to reach the level recommendations for each quest, which resulted in slogging through many forgettable quests that just never truly captured that Borderlands charm. The story is told through the form of an in-universe version of D&D known as Bunkers & Badasses and is rather excellently narrated by the prolific voice over talent in Ashley Burch who returns to reprise her role as Tiny Tina, throughout the main story Tina as the “Bunker Master” guides her players through a wild and haphazardly thrown together Bunkers & Badasses campaign which sees the Player referred to as “Newbie” and the other players at the Table, Frett & Valentine, take on the evil forces of The Dragon Lord. Whilst the voiceover work that is put on display is top notch and the cast boasts names such as Ashley Burch, Andy Samburg and Wanda Sykes their terrific performances are never quite enough to save the campaign from itself and fail to make up for the very apparent rushed and lazy writing. I found myself giving a resounding sigh of relief at the sight of the games end credits and was left with no real desire to continue on with what remained of Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands clearly lazily thrown together side content.For the most part Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands minute to minute gameplay loop is undeniably fun, however it seems to fall apart during the implementation of its new features that mostly feel ill-thought-out and at times tacked on to artificially increase the amount of time Gearbox could keep their players in game. The decision to completely remove vehicular travel and combat in favour for the new Overworld that seemed out of place and better implemented by games akin to Nino Kuni and Final Fantasies of old was a flawed design choice that not only had me feeling detached from the game world but has ensured that Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands has had more loading screens than most modern AAA titles. Unfortunately the cures of the new Overworld feature doesn’t end there, clearly added to the game in order to implement the new “Random Encounters'' that are a blatant design choice to reduce the amount of quality content needed to fill the game world. These random encounters see the player put into a small handful of encounter maps fighting a smaller diversity in enemy types making this new feature a very unwelcome one. My time in Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands was spent on their “balanced” or normal difficulty which was anything but balanced, leaving many of their bosses and minions feeling super easy to mow down and as though I was never in any real threat. My recommendation to anyone choosing to pick up Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands over any of the other entries into the Borderlands series is to play this game on its hardest difficulty in order to have the most enjoyable experience. Despite my harsh criticism the feature that I’d like to commend Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands for is their new class system that sees the player choosing from one of six classes that each are a take on typical character tropes from Dungeons & Dragons, this feature removes the character selection from previous Borderlands games and offers the player more choice in the character they want to play, this feature reaches greater depths once the player unlocks the capability to “Multiclass” giving them the chance to pick up a second one of the six classes. I spent my time playing a combination of the Clawbringer and Spellshot that gave me access to the wyvern companion and later multiclassing into the Spellshot heavily boosted the usefulness of my spells which take the place of grenades from the games of old. This combination of classes really allowed me to feel increasingly stronger the further along each skill tree I found myself going down. Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands gunplay is one of its best features, this however is overshadowed by the fact that it is still the basic combat and gameplay loop that other Borderlands games that in the past were renowned for  and resulted in it once again leaning on that Borderlands crutch in an attempt to fight for relevance.To summarise, Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands never truly manages to find its way out of the shadow of its predecessors and ultimately suffers from its lack of identity, whilst a fun but short experience it struggles under the weight of expectation that comes with the territory of being a spin off of a widely beloved series. After the curtain fell on its lacklustre campaign I couldn’t help but feel as though Gearbox Software never truly gave Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands the love and attention it needed to truly flourish into the game it tried to be. I cannot in good faith recommend this game at its full asking price but do believe it’s a valuable pick up on a hefty discount and believe that despite its glaring flaws there is still a fun experience underneath to be had. During my time with Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands I couldn’t help but feel as though this should have and would have been a great DLC inclusion to a main line Borderlands game instead of the half baked solo release that we received. My harsh criticisms come from a place of wanting Gearbox to recapture the love and attention older Borderlands games had in spades and not succumb in putting out soulless releases that rely heavily on the legacy of older games that other studios have become guilty of mass producing. Ultimately I had fun with Tiny Tina’s Wonderlands but couldn’t shake the unbearable feeling that it could have been so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give this game a thumbs down because of the experience i have seen everyone on the net getting from support. the game promises crossplay but we have been unable to join our friends using that supposed feature. When reporting this issue to support, we have met with either blame for our own equipment or straight up silence. no help seems to be forthcoming on this. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend it even though there's some things I don't like about this game. _childDocuments_.review: To say this is just Borderlands with a DnD theme is incorrect. While the base gameplay loop is pretty similar.. the class systems and more diverse equipment you can use allows you to truly play the game any way you want.. Unlike the actual Borderlands series, you aren't restricted to one of 3 possible setups for whichever class you choose. Which basically fixes the series' weakest point.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: Despite what people have said in other comments, I think the writing and jokes in Wonderlands are better than BL3, more like they were in BL2. People who say the story is trash when it is supposed to be D&D written by a like 13 year old are looking at it wrong IMO. The combat is probably the best in the series.  I am not a fan of how much of a grind it is to get to Chaos 100 (you gain 5 Chaos levels for each Chaos Trial run completion until 50, then only 1 until 100). I would recommend buying the game with the DLC when it is on sale (I think I got the Chaotic Great Edition for like $40, definitely worth it at that price).

_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: The problem is it's not good.I enjoyed Dragon Keep, but Dragon Keep worked because it was about something.Wonderlands feels like a gigantic meaningless blip of a game.The voice acting is fine, but the writing feels flat and bland. The script leans on references instead of humor, and it's peppered with "we're playing an arr pee gee, isn't that kind of lame?" remarks, which, like. I can't believe I'm writing this, but something like South Park Stick Of Truth pulls this formula off way better because it actually cares about and has an opinion on the rpg stuff it's making fun of.Wonderlands feels like it's made entirely of filler text. Half its content is airgapped from the main plot, stuffed into *large* optional areas, and none of the npcs really have any luster to them.Tina's VA does a fantastic job, but is fighting uphill against the phoned-in-ed-ness of the rest of the game.The gameplay is roughly the same as other Borderlands, with a neat change in that you select your class, not your character, and you can multiclass to mix power sets. However, Wonderlands is also buggier than any other Borderlands, and there's a persistent interact glitch that I keep getting stuck in. I've also bugged out the fight for your life state by jumping, and this turned enemy AI and damage vulnerability off. It's been ages since release, and I don't think these are getting fixed.If you're really desperate for a looter shooter, I guess Wonderlands fits the bill, but I'd get it on super duper sale and keep your expectations at floor level.Also the dlc feels even more phoned in than the main game. It's just arenas with a voiceover. It barely has waypoint markers.Edit: Rolled credits. It picks up slightly at the end, but *very* slightly. Not enough to justify having to get to it. And in a setting like Borderlands, where the bulk of the appeal is the characters, the villain being the only really likeable one is painful. The plot doesn't go anywhere. If it was shortened down to the length of Dragon's Keep, it would be better, but still not better than Dragon's Keep, which is a problem because it doesn't tread any new territory. There's zero reason to recommend this thing over a years old dlc, which sucks, because the premise is genuinely fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: It put almost 70 hours into this game playing it in 4 player co-op. This game is not perfect by any means but it improves in previous Borderlands games in a lot of tangible ways. My favourite improvement is the removal of vehicles. I HATED the vehicle sections in literally all the Borderlands games and I suspect I'm not the only one. This game knows the gunplay is the fun part of any BL game and just focuses on it and trims out the chaff. Changing grenades to spells and linking them a cooldown instead of a pickup is another good choice and helps eliminates the compulsion to never use your grenades. I've also found that this game is less annoying then other BL games. The story is kinda meh, but I've never cared about the story in BL games, but what I appreciate is thousands of lines of dialogue that get barked out while you do everything are at least fairly well written and voice acted. You will still get a lot of repeated vocal barks from npcs especially in the main hub city.The dlc seems like a cool idea at first, but I think I understand why everyone is downvoting them. They're too expensive for how short they are (they expect you to repeat them over and over to earn special reward currency but you start getting duplicate rewards after only three runs.)Like any BL game try to rope some friends into playing this with you. The core games lasts a good long time including maybe 10 or more hours after you hit max level. If you're on the fence (or you just need to buy 4 copies of the game so that your crew can play together) this game is an especially good value if you can nab it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: I got all of the achievements for this game and it was the worst experience I have been through playing a game. All of the quests are so drawn out. I get it's supposed to be like dungeons and dragons. However, the story is just so bad. The leveling system just doesn't make any sense. Why is their a difficulty you can change at any point in time on a single character and there is levels which don't correspond to the enemy level because they are always a level ahead. Do not buy this game if you are looking for a good experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is more or less an annoying experience with awkward/cringe humor and mediocre story telling.The game itself is not really all that engaging and gets boring really quick.Gameplay itself is as fine as it gets for a Borderlands title, content is lacking and it just doesn't even feel like it actually matters enough to sink time into.It more or less feels as if Gearbox just doesn't have that touch like they had back when they made Borderlands 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but after 14 hours of banging my head against it, I have to say that I don't.  Honestly, I don't think it's a bad game, but I don't think it's for me.  All of the enemies are entirely too tanky, soaking up bullets like sponges.  This stretches out combat encounters to the point where they become tedious, not fun.  And while I understand that the random rolled weapons are supposed to be part of the fun, they're so random that any kind of classification becomes useless. This means you have to equip (and use) almost every weapon you find in order to properly evaluate it.  Which again becomes tedious.There's a lot of things I do like, the art style, the writing, the acting (the main trio of Tina, Valentine and Frett are particularly enjoyable) and the shooting itself isn't bad (apart from the overly healthy enemies.)  I would just urge caution for folks heading into this game to evaluate it closely and be honest with the types of shooters they like.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, but you really have to install the Redux mod from Nexusmods. It fixed many of the problems the normal game has and make it fun and playable in the endgame. _childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game over BL3 but Jesus Christ its hard to play this game for long periods of time, it being the same issues that plague Borderlands 3 though not as bad as in BL3 or New Tales, the writing is still pretty cringey, the poor optimisation that for a more than competent PC which makes my fans go overdrive or the hit or miss voice acting (Ashly Burch and Will Arnett crush it pretty good though) or the same poor UI and Map that was in BL3 I can see why people don't like it.Get this if you like TTRPGs and Borderlands or want to play through a game with BL3s great gunplay and without BL3s ear-bleeding dialogue and story... Or if you're an insomniac and want something that'll put you to sleep.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this a fair and honest review. Would I recommend it to someone who wants a Borderlands experience? No, I wouldn't. I'd recommend this to someone who wants to run an actual Bunkers and Badasses experience without the hassle of determining who will GM and who'll pick what classes. It feels like DLC from 3, and the classes are limited to one skill tree and one playstyle. While the concept was good, the execution is what's at fault. If they made it like the older games, with one ability and three skill trees to differ playstyles and augment that ability, the game would be better. Tack the issues that the melee is finicky and the gunplay is meh at best, and the buffering that they did with "Dungeon Encounters" to help pad out the time, it really just feels half finished and haphazardly put together. I do suggest picking this up, so long as it is reasonably discounted by 50-75%, and picking it up if you have friends who would play with you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is repetitive, shallow, bland, and ultimately - .If you're one to believe that  is fun together with friends, you have an opportunity to torpedo that notion for whatever cost this piece of ♥♥♥♥ retails at.The genuinely infuriating thing to me is that this game does actually have elements of good-ness.The world is beautifully crafted.The voiceacting - great.Writing? It's engaging, funny, even.It does have the makings of fun gunplay under the hood.But then after about 5 hours of playtime they murder all the good bits with horrible scaling, the game becoming brain numbingly easy and unchallenging. And not in a casual, chill-gaming, easygoing way...There is nothing to adapt to, there is no threat. No thought process involved. It's not possible to die. It does not matter what build you build, what spells you use, what gun you choose - even on hardest difficulty all minions explode instantly, bosses are killed comically quickly. You just churn through a volume of mob HP, timegated by dialogue.The RPG elements are a facade. Nothing you choose or do matters, you just run and blow stuff up, and its not even fun to "blow stuff up", because in comes lazyness, where the arenas become reused, pasted, making for a very repetitive and constant gameplay loop.Whatever storyline there is, hard to appreciate it if you're yawning and zoning out due to the stale gameplay.If I could, I'd refund, but the shallowness and unplayability of this garbage does not become apparent until well beyond 2 hours of gametime.Stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: Take the review with a bit of caution before buying the game. The Art/Graphics is really great, and world design is done well. Combat with the spells and guns are decently fun as well, although it can get a bit boring if you have bad weapons. But having cool spells/weapons can make the process go smoother. However this is my biggest issue with the game, the story/writing isn't that fun. I was really excited when I saw the trailer a while back, and liked Tiny Tina's over the top humor. But overall, I struggled to make myself progress further in the game. But since I enjoyed the combat, I ignored everything story-related and just went further. I forced myself to continue since I bought the game. If you're looking for something lighthearted, and popcorn-style gaming, and the game is on sale, you can try out this game. I wish Borderlands franchise can improve its writing and storytelling. I know it's supposed to be whacky and goofy and over the top, but even with that, it can be done better. Some jokes are funny. Some are cringy. Some are boring. I feel like Borderlands can do better if they focus more on the writing. Because the looter-shooter parts/ combat can be really fun, and that's where Borderlands shines.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: I've really been enjoying this game. The worlds are pleasing to the eye, and if you've ever played a Borderlands game, you already know the gameplay is a blast. I really like how this iteration is DnD based with some Renaissance time period stuff thrown in as well. I like how they finally got the user interface right this time and it's flat and not off at a weird angle like in past games. The classes are interesting and you have more than one skill tree, which makes builds more complex and fun to experiment with.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: This game has entertaining game play with fun ttrpg elements adapted for the Boarderlands play style. While the Game itself is enjoyable enough i'd be remiss to mention the characters are Laughably poorly written and positively dripping with cringe dialogue. However if you can ignore the characters as you play its a perfectly enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a good game? No. But is it one of the better Borderlands games? Also no. The DLC is a clear money-grab with each one simply adding arena battles with a couple guns. Don't waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: the entire game is this cringey type comedy which you will have to hear constantly (don't play genshin, but similar to paimon annoyance levels) with a very weak story which is made up on the fly with a dim vision of beating a final antagonist.additionally, the theme is best described as a blend of sci fi, fantasy and a 7 year old girl's colouring book which i don't think works AT ALL. you will constantly be using fully automatic weapons since i believe it was less effort importing everything from borderlands than creating fantasy weapons.one good thing was the character creation, but all in all i think this game was really bad. however if the above appeals to you go for it
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: Such fun and addicting! Smooth game play, funny and entertaining story(the puns are an added bonus).I don't recommend getting the DLC, way too overpriced. The game is a nice Borderlands twist. Claptrap makes an appearance, which I love hahaI do have one bone to pick. For a game that has "Looting" in the tag, the QoL features for this are minimum. Why isn't there an option to automatically make common items trash? Most games with looting and gear mechanics have said options. 'Check a box if you want all gray items to be marked as trash, check a box if you want all green items to be marked as trash, etc.'This game has no such function. Instead you have to go down your inventory and one by one mark each item as trash, THEN you can mass sell the items. Which, in the long run becomes tedious and time consuming. Other than that, it is a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:* Funny writing.* Beyond-imaginative world.* By-the-book exploration.* Beautiful graphics and good sounds.Cons:* The whole frikking gunplay. I mean, what's even going on here. Normal difficulty: A 5th-level, absolutely lowly mob takes 2 headshots from a unique 5th-level sniper rifle with flat damage bigger than anything else. A 12th-level melee fighter with the biggest, rarest, two-handed weapon and all skill points invested in a melee tree still has to smash three times into a common mob to kill it. Submachine guns have generally 3-5x less flat damage than a pistol (!!). Okay, I get it. Supposedly, that should be balanced by the rate of fire. What a joke. What good is the rate of fire if I have to empty half a clip into one single mob.  Don't get me even started on tougher enemies. Weapons in general are either powerful but shoot in ways that are weird and cumbersome (whereas enemies move to and fro as if on cocaine) or are shooting straight but are "rightfully" much weaker. You might say this gets better later on, when you supplement the weapons with passives and abilities. No, it does not. Once in 5 hours you get a weapon that, by some miracle, operates on sane levels at least two more hours, before it becomes under-par, or an inventory mod that could technically make one more skill work wonders if only you had those other two mods that would complement it, and you would search for them another 5 hours, and once you get those, the mods are already outperformed, and... AAAAARRGGGH!This was most of my experience with Tiny Tina's. I am no stranger to FPSs; I've always done my successful builds in many ARPGs or FPS/RPG hybrids to satisfactory levels. I've played and mostly loved everything Borderlands with some exceptions of some weird choices in BIII. This... this is just no.I finished the game because of the scenery, humor, and imagination. But gameplay-wise it was a frikking chore to begin with and ended the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: Actually the BEST GAME they've made so far.Borderlands was a nice starter, but the WORLD, CHARACTERS, QUESTS, WEAPONS, SPELLS, GEAR, LOOT, CLASS( and multi-class) SYSTEM, CHAOS CHAMBER etc etc. The list goes on - it's just so good. Really.The game can both be EASY AND CHILL FOR CASUALS, or you can tune the game DIFFICULTY up to MAXIMUM and do Chaos Chamber runs that can keep increasing in difficulty, and thus allowing you to gain even BETTER STATS gear.For anyone into loot-grinding, story, cartoony/charming graphics and some serious fun in Coop aswell (but also equally good in solo), THIS IS THE GAME FOR YOU!
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has enjoyed all 3 Borderlands games, I cannot say the same about Tiny Tina's Wonderland. I can't pinpoint what exactly I didn't enjoy, cause I think it was many different things, but in general I felt the combat was not fun and not what I expected. Using spells felt much less tactical and satisfying than throwing a grenade, the weapons all seem to have some weird projectile, nothing just shoots a straight bullet, and the enemies felt repetitive at times (many of them will be a skeleton of some sort). The shops and chests never seem to have anything good, and after saving up 50 items just to get a slight upgrade from the shop I felt scammed. The story is fine but nothing exceptional, most of it Tina makes up as she goes, which is the point I guess, but it's just hard to take seriously.  It's not a bad game, just don't expect it to be like Borderlands.
_childDocuments_.name: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands

_childDocuments_.review: I have never tried any of the Borderlands before and this was my first one.   If you like simpler quests and more shooting then solving, I'd recommend it for solid entertainment value.   The toons become powerful quick so no reason to do less then intermediate play.   Still on my first toon (lvl 37ish) and I don't think I'll make a 2nd...they are too close to one another IMO and I'll get my $ out of 1 (possibly 2) toons.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is an okay game and the reason I say that is because that they do a lot of things great and wrong. As the game goes it took me over a year to drag myself back to play it. I am glad I did go back to it but it was a hard time trying to pull myself to play something that wasn't grasping me to. Overall I enjoyed my time playing this game and going as far to 100 percent it.The game play of Wonderlands is very similar to any of the games in the Borderlands franchise but with some minor differences. There are no grenades but spells and the addition of the melee weapons which was a cool addition and a change of play style and skills that you play around. All the sliding and mantling from Borderlands 3 still feels great in the engine that the game is made on. Still the same old format of main quest / side quest grind with collectables in between and loading screens galore but what do you expect from a Gearbox game. Gearbox fixed the loot system making legendries rare again and adding the loot luck system which gives the game a better flow of power. Spells give the game a different approach to the usual utility of a grenade with a wider aspect of buffs, damage types and play styles.   I am still not a fan of the enchantments which are just a re-skin of the anointments from Borderlands 3. Speaking of similar features the Chaos Level is a more tedious version of the mayhem levels where you have to spend hours upon hours to reach level 100. Guardian rank has been replaced with myth rank which works similar but has minor differences and all it serves as is an end game content dump for those who want to keep playing after they have done everything.Character skills and classes are very diverse and the ability to multiclass is a very good feature and in theme for the Dungeons and Dragons. This does give the game a creative class composition where you can pick and choose what you want. The class skills in the game or for the class that I played, the Stabbomancer, felt like that there wasn't much going. The class felt slightly boring to play and if it wasn't for the fact that you could multiclass then I would have just deleted the character and started again. Attribute points where a new addition to the character's statistics these are some additional stats to boost your characters ability and creates architypes that change the way that you think about playing your character in the first place.Opposed to the old map and fast travel the player has a map and can fast travel from there or they could wander around the map and travel to different places that way.  In the overworld there are different challenges to do and collectables to get that can make you stronger such as the shrines, which offer a variety of buffs to the player. Camps and encounters are a new and unique way to utilise combat in the game and provides a different experience to bite sized content.The Aesthetics of Wonderlands is pretty much the same as Borderlands 3 where it's this cartoon like drawing with thick comic book outlines. Some differences are that there is not as much neon in this game due to the environment setting, but the colour pallet is a lot brighter to give the game the fairy tale feel to it.The Animations are smooth, with the different types of creatures that are in the game, they all have their own physics and ragdoll pretty responsibly. The new melee weapons add a new aspect of animation for this game especially for the continuous swinging in a fluid motion. With the setting being medieval fantasy there is a lot of magic that has some really nice animations with lots of different colours and particles which makes casting spells really satisfying. The environment of Wonderlands is good and bad in all places sometimes it feels like the environment is bare and could use some little touches but at other points it seems to be flourishing with interactable and props that really immerse the play in this medieval world. The difference zone that you go to have their own themes and they are done really well with keeping the atmosphere correct, where you have a dark evil forest there is mushrooms that look deadly and the enemies that are there are also fitting too. I am so sorry Tina but your story sucks... I feel that the antagonist of the game really sucks and it doesn't want me to go an progress through the game to defeat him. I think that the 4th wall breaking villain was the incorrect move. It's dungeons and dragons for crying out loud there are plenty of examples where you can create a more interesting story line and give more plot hooks to keep the player interesting. As a DM in real life, I couldn't play this game for the story anymore and looked toward the progression and game mechanics which weren't half bad.Although the main story was terrible some of the side quests where good and made me chuckle at times but I am not paying the triple A price tag for garbage.Progression in Wonderlands is okay, I prefer the lower level cap and the changes to how the myth rank works. There was something missing which was a new game plus or a way to reset quests for that little bit or replay ability. I guess the incentive it to create a different character to try out their skills but that shouldn't stop me from playing the game more. Overall I think that this game in the franchise was an experiment at best to see what works and what doesn't as there was a lot that change, some better some worse,  but I found the game fun. I think that it is worth playing only if you haven't got anything else better to play or crave a casual FPS. I do not think that it is worth the price tag that it wears and you can pick it up on sale for pretty cheap or if you don't really care about the developers you can get a key on different sites for even cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: Am surprised by the lowish Steam reviews here because, as someone who has played all the Borderlands games, this is one of the better ones - certainly far better than the tedious and disappointing Borderlands 3. That said, I do feel that the first few hours of the game do not create a particularly good impression - mechanics seem confusing, the gunplay is bog standard Borderlands, the role-playing elements seem underwhelming and the amount of lame puns and jokes already start to grate on you so early on. But as more options are granted to the player, the game's customizability and the freedom at which you can mold your build gives the game a much-needed fresh spin, and the game becomes a lot more fun. And the locales you get to visit become one of the game's main attractions - a town uprooted by a beanstalk, a giant skeleton built onto a cliffside - the creativity in the places you visit keep things fresh. The fact that the whole game, even with DLCs, is only 50+ hours means that the game doesn't tediously stretch itself way, way too thin like in Borderlands 3, which was just too long for its own sake. The overworld can be tedious to navigate, as are those "encounters", but once you learn how to punch, they don't become much of an issue anymore. Oh, and this game features WAY less Claptrap - always a positive. And the game seems more stable too - not as many bugs as in 3 or Pre-sequel. And the story? Forgettable, but at least the villain isn't insufferable here, unlike in 3. Just wish the level cap was higher - 40 seems artificially low and hampers late-game build-up. And some of the warp points are just too few and far between.Overall, this one requires some patience as it doesn't give very good first impressions, but stick with it and it opens up in satisfying ways. It definitely deserves more thumbs up than 3's ridiculously high Steam reviews - that game is really the series' nadir.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. So I’ve put 80-odd hours into this and completed the campaign, so it must be good, right? Err well…yes and no. If you like Borderlands you’ll be OK with TTW. But the campaign is poor, there is little in the way of “Borderlands-style” humour and Tiny Tina is an acquired taste. As time went on, I found her voice increasingly grating. Best in small measures. Very small measures. The maps aren’t great. Some are really difficult to navigate. Not nearly enough fast travel points and/or vending machines – and the few that are there feel badly located. The loot drops are a bit rubbish too. I rarely found anything better than what I already had and - despite making real efforts to increase my “loot luck” score - I found that chests and enemies mostly dropped white, green and blue items – right up to and beyond the endgame. Purple drops were very rare. Orange drops were ridiculously rare. Saying that, the gear didn’t seem to matter that much, as I managed to complete the campaign with little trouble. I did make an awful lot of fast travel jumps back to the hub town of Brighthoof to sell useless loot. This got real tiresome. I also frequently encountered a bug whereby I couldn’t return to the area I had jumped from via the map because the fast travel point in that Zone was not selectable. This meant that I often had to return to an area via the Overworld – this got real tiresome. And on the World Map screen my cursor had a habit of flying way off the map for no apparent reason. Yeah…you guessed it…tiresome. The post-campaign “Chaos Chamber” stuff and the dlcs did nothing for me – tried them; didn’t see the point. They are both just extended inescapable “encounters” where you move through several areas killing bad guys who drop way-more mostly-useless loot than you could ever carry. Overall, I think TTW was a decent idea that was not terribly well implemented. Not enough TLC. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very sweet game, but buyer beware: there are some very key and glaring flaws in this game. Endgame feels awful and Don't bother with the PLC.Main Story: 7.5/10 - Worth it if you like Borderlands Characters and Style.Endgame: 3/10 - Boring, frustrating and repetitive.PLC: 1/10 - Just... dont.Story and Side Quests: 7/10Solid and engaging story, best enjoyed if you're a fan of TTRPG's and know the Borderlands universe & Characters, but not a necessity by any means.Gun play: 7/10Balance is very finely tuned and feels great, The weapons are amazing to use as always in borderlands games, new Melee weapons, Spells and gun types are fantastic additions.Overall aesthetic: 8/10The wonderlands are fantastic to explore with Beautiful visuals and areas ranging from Mountaintops, Forests, deserts, ruins and more*BUT*Areas, once played through, tend to get repetitive quickly, especially the endgameGameplay: 5/10The player classes feel great to play, and their skills really fit their themes, All have great features and all are fun to play.Good amount of enemy variety, each with their own characteristics.Some Quality of Life Additions: Melee Autoswing, Audio prompts for cooldowns*BUT*Lack of Endgame content, and what endgame there is, is deeply flawed. Mostly Spoilerless summary in 3 points:Repetitive Everything. Zero Variety. Game collectibles can become Monotonous to collect, 100%'ing the main game is not difficult for the most part, but it is tedious due to the sheer amount of collectibles in the world. Thankfully, Gearbox has taken steps to fix this issue, but I personally feel it needs further addressing.The Loot and Farming: 3/10While there are many great additions to the Wonderlands in regard to equipment, weapons and more. However, TT Wonderlands legendary weapons can feel lackluster, with some being outclassed by Purple and even some Blue items."Class mod"/Armor variety between the Character classes are lumped together, meaning you're dealing with RNG on Skill increases for specific skills you want on top of Secondary stats ON TOP OF it dropping for your specific class, meaning there's a lot of garbage farming.Many named enemies from quests and elsewhere are one-and-done fights that never re-spawn, leading to a Very empty feeling world after a first playthrough. There's little to no point in returning to previously completed areas except cleaning up side-quests or collectibles.----PLC ratings - Overpriced and less content than the small Headhunter pack DLC's from Borderlands 2, each require multiple Playthroughs to access the Legendary gear associated with them.PLC 1: 1/10Nothing of value beyond some specific legendaries that get added that are Borked with Cryo builds.Gameplay includes a MANDATORY 5 minute wait in an area with a insignificant trickle of enemies that killing is akin to wafting flies away from your face, just for them to loop round and pester you again half a minute later. The last boss is easy to farm for the aforementioned loot, thankfully.PLC 2: 1/10A small step up from DLC 1 going to bottom of the barrel from being buried 6 feet under the barrel, but still the same, garbage content but some good gear. Areas look interesting and the Boss is interesting but annoying to fight in a bad way.PLC 3: 3/10Actual Content!! (on par with a headhunter pack) Follows the same formula from previous PLC's but with actual effort to make it engaging and interesting. The boss fight is a challenge and interesting to fight for the first few times, *BUT*Fighting the boss becomes tedious when progressing in the Endgame, A tragic victim of TT Wonderlands awful endgame balancing with enemy damage and cheesing the healthgating mechanic is mandatory for victory.*BUT THAT'S NOT ALL*Completing fights VS PLC bosses adds them into the random boss rotation that act as a finale for the Endgame loop. PLC 1 and 2's bosses are manageable to frustrating. Running into PLC 3's boss means you might as well quit and start fresh, as it takes so long to fight and is incredibly punishing for the vast majority of viable builds.As good as PLC 3 is versus the others, which isn't that much, I can't recommend it as it makes an already bad endgame EVEN WORSE by adding a permanent random chance to ruin your progress for just playing the content.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that will make you laugh, cry, and shoot a lot of things, then look no further than Borderlands: Tiny Tina's Wonderland. This game is a blast from start to finish, with hilarious dialogue, crazy characters, and epic loot. You'll explore a fantasy world created by the lovable psychopath Tiny Tina, who narrates your adventures as you fight dragons, unicorns, and skeletons. The missions are varied and fun, ranging from rescuing a princess from a tower to infiltrating a cult of cheese worshippers. The gameplay is fast-paced and satisfying, with tons of weapons, skills, and spells to choose from. You can also customize your character with different outfits, heads, and skins. The game is best enjoyed with friends, as you can team up online or in split-screen mode to take on the challenges together. Borderlands: Tiny Tina's Wonderland is a game that will keep you entertained for hours, with its witty humor, awesome action, and endless replayability. I highly recommend it to anyone who loves a good laugh and a good shoot.
