_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of Borderlands series, although after BL2 it felt like the series was starting to get stuck in a rut, BL Pre-Squel was average, and BL3 didnt quite have that feeling of anything new, thankfully this new entry in the series has changed some of the format following the DLC from BL2 "Assault on Dragon Keep" which this game is a direct standalone sequel of. They changed up the mechanics so now grenades are replace with spells and seems a lot deeper in the loot system for interesting builds you can get. They have also greatly expanded the character editor as well, with most of the new parts being found as loot drops rather than all being available at the start. Aside from the standard campaign there is about 5 or 6 area battle areas (similar to the Moxi arenas except instead of wave rounds all being the same area, they move through to 5 or 6 locations as you progress) found in the camp near start of the game that can be used for grind souls (kills) for redeeming at a random wheel of loot... which sometimes gives out some amazingly good gear drops on par with a boss fight, and even when they arent there's a vendor to sell them off there too. So it feels like they put a lot of work into replayability of these side modes and they do scale and have optional difficulty settings for epic loot grinding.Graphics: 8.5/10 much improved textures and FX over the prior games (although still miss BL2's Physx ones) in DX12 at least, didnt try the Dx11 mode, but would expect more performance on DX11 if you have older hardware, as this is a tad spec hungry, and sadly lacks DLSS...but does have AMD FSR 2.0 which can pull a few more frames in.Sound: 8/10 Gun sounds and magic fx are pretty good, voice acting is a bit better than BL3 but doesnt expect huge differences as many are the same cast returning. Music is average, nothing really stuck out bit fits the content which is more dialogue led anyway with its typical cheesy dad jokes and puns.Gameplay: 8.5/10 Definately feels the best of the series in mechanics and controls, little refinements here and there that push it past BL2/Bl3 etc. Melee is very much a useful thing to use regularly in combat with mixing in freezing spells etc and once you hit around rank 12 things really swing upwards in the scale of fights and enemies running about.... and doesnt slow performance so well optimised.Overall 8.5/10 Probably my favourite after BL2, but theres a lot of new playstyles here that would suit people new to the series that prefer the fantasy style over the wasteland style aethetics. Version I have is the Chaotic Great Edition that came with all the season pass content and paid £34, so would say thats pretty great value, would thing its not reallt worth the standard £60+ for it though.... so buy it in sales.Gameplay from early levels below:

_childDocuments_.review: Since Steam forces us to either give a thumbs up or down I am going with the "no". Let me explain. The game looks gorgeous. The artistry on display reinforced by the Unreal engine makes this game the best looking in the Franchise. But (you knew this was coming) that is the best thing about the game. And when the visuals are the best thing in a Looter-Shooter you know something is not right. The "bazillion guns" that drop make it arbitrary if you really want to waste your time comparing stats when you will find one that is ever so slightly better just around the corner. I stopped caring altogether and just sold everything without ever looking at them. Ever so often I would take new one after leveling up a few levels but it was not really enganging wich brings me to my second problem. The enemies are just as arbitrary. The vast majority of enemies don't require you to tackle them differently. Basically all of them can be killed by spamming them with bullets and your special skills. Those could be interesting but they aren't because you just don't have any reason to refine them. And the skill tree is a smoke screen. They split them in multiple parts and sell them as extra classes which might feel like more but if you compare it with BL2 they just split them up and made them smaller and in direct comparison not remotely as interesting. Minor stats changes don't affect your playstyle and major new abilities are very rare and disappointing me more often than not.What made BL2 click for me just is not present here and it is really hard to pin down. Lots of quality of life stuff is missing, odd decisions like the names of your friends being just that bit too large on screen are annoying. The total overload of effects make strategic play absolutely impossible (not that you would need to) and the story is okay. The voice actors do a good job and the writing is okay but a far cry from being memorable like BL2. The tons ob side missions do almost nothing for the main story and you forget what it's all about constantly. The many cameos of characters from the other games are undercooked and feel like lame fan service.All in all, the sum of its parts leave me mostly indifferent. I stopped interacting with most of the systems like skill tree, weapon selection, listening to the story since none of it matters much since the core gameplay loop is just so plain. So, If I could, I would give it a neutral "meh" instead of the thumbs down. It is just not interesting enough for a recommendation and just not bad enough for a "stay away" warning. It is okay if you really do not have anything else which should be impossible these days.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is an action role-playing first-person shooter video game developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K. As a spin-off in the Borderlands series and a sequel to Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep, the game is set within the world of a fantasy-themed tabletop role-playing game. The game was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S in March 2022.Tiny Tina's Wonderlands was developed by Gearbox Software with support from Lost Boys Interactive.[11] According to Gearbox founder Randy Pitchford, the studio has been planning to release a fantasy spin-off of the series since the early 2010s, and it had unsuccessfully pitched several fantasy projects to publishers during the early days of the studio.[12] The game's overworld system was inspired by Japanese role-playing games such as the Final Fantasy series. Gearbox intentionally designed five maps that can only be accessed through the overworld. These maps feature their own narrative threads that are also connected to the main story.[13] Ashly Burch returned to provide her voice for Tiny Tina, while Andy Samberg, Will Arnett and Wanda Sykes portrayed other main characters in the game.[14]Despite Embracer Group's acquisition of Gearbox Software in 2020, the studio continued to partner with series publisher 2K Games.[15] The game was officially announced by 2K on June 10, 2021.[16] It was released on March 25, 2022 for Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X and Series S.[5] The PS5 and Xbox Series X/S versions will include the Dragon Lord Pack downloadable content. Players who pre-ordered the game would gain access to the Golden Hero Armor Pack.[17] Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is the first game in the Borderlands franchise to feature full crossplay between PlayStation, Xbox, and PC. Although Borderlands 3 did feature crossplay, the feature was limited in the platforms that could play together.Ahead of Wonderlands's release, Gearbox made the Borderlands 2 DLC Assault on Dragon Keep available as a standalone game Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep: A Wonderlands One-Shot Adventure, released on November 8, 2021 for Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One.Similar to its predecessors, the game is a first-person shooter with elements of an action role-playing game. The game can be played solo or with up to three other players in online or local split-screen multiplayer. The game is set within the world of a fantasy-themed tabletop role-playing game.[2] The game features an overworld, which is used by the playable characters to traverse the various locations in the game. There are random combat encounters and quests that can only be completed in the overworld.[3][4]Tiny Tina's Wonderlands builds upon the standards set by the Borderlands franchise that it originated from while also differing in several key aspects. In terms of the characters themselves rather than playing as a specific vault hunter, with their own personality and voice lines, players instead play as a custom made character using the games character creator system. The game features six different character classes, and for the first time in the series, players can mix and match these skills for their characters.[5] The playable avatars have stats that can be upgraded using "hero points".[6] Players have a large arsenal of weapons and firearms at their disposal, and for the first time in the series, players can wield melee weapons. The game features the same procedurally generated loot system from the Borderlands series that is capable of generating numerous combinations of weapons and other gear.[7] The game also features new types of gear for the players to use to improve their strength. Melee weapons have their own 5th weapon slot to encourage the player to fight up close. Grenades, which have been a franchise staple, have been replaced with a spell slot on a cooldown. Players can cast spells such as summoning meteors, or transforming enemies into sheep.[8] Lastly in terms of new equipment are two ring slots, and an amulet slot to further increase the power of the character.After completing the main campaign, players will unlock an infinite dungeon mode known as Chaos Chamber. Each Chaos Chamber consists of six levels and includes two boss characters. The combination of enemies and bosses is randomly selected by the game. After completing each level, they will gain access to a portal which would grant the player additional perks or combat advantages, or "curses" that hinder their combat abilities. Boss characters will drop legendary weapons, and players can also spend crystals to unlock extra loots.Set after Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep, the campaign is set within the world of a fantasy-themed tabletop role-playing game named "Bunkers & Badasses". Tiny Tina (Ashly Burch) is its dungeon master and can change the game's world on the fly.[10]The story starts with Valentine (Andy Samberg), Frette (Wanda Sykes), and the player, known as The Newbie, about to defeat the Dragon Lord (Will Arnett). The Dragon Lord uses his magic to raise the undead, but is stopped by Butt Stallion, wielding the Sword of Souls. The Dragon Lord is imprisoned for centuries, and the game begins anew, this time with the Newbie being "The Fatemaker". The Fatemaker goes through the starting area with the help of Butt Stallion as their guide. They are stopped by a gang of skeletons and their leader, who has plans to awaken the Dragon Lord, who was banished in a crypt hidden in a dungeon. Despite defeating the skeleton leader, the Dragon Lord is awakened, and disappears.The player goes to Brighthoof, which is under siege by skeletons brought by the Dragon Lord. After defeating the skeleton army, the Player is tasked by Queen Butt Stallion to retrieve the Sword of Souls from the nearby graveyard. After recovering the Sword and charging it up with the soul of The Dragon Lord’s poltergeist ally, the Player returns to Brighthoof and places the sword into the central fountain, repairing the town. For their efforts, the Queen decides to make the Player an official Knight of Brighthoof. Before she is able to, the Dragon Lord appears and steals the Sword of Souls, using it to decapitate Queen Butt Stallion. He disappears, taking the Sword and Queen Butt Stallion’s head back to his base, The Fear-amid. The Player is tasked to cross the ocean on a ship and stop the Dragon Lord, before he uses the Sword’s power to destroy the Wonderlands. Before they can cross, the Player is told to get their boat blessed by a bard or risk getting killed by an ocean monster. After finding a bard (Chris Rager), he dispels the bad vibes surrounding the player (Valentine and Frette’s arguing over how to play the game). Unfortunately, the spell works too well and instead destroys the ocean, forcing the Player to cross on foot instead.While crossing, the Dragon Lord secretly talks to the Player, revealing that he is fully aware that Wonderlands is just a game. He further reveals that he plans to harvest a massive amount of soul energy to use the Sword of Souls to sever Tina’s control over the Wonderlands, as he views her as insecure and quick to anger. Before entering the Fear-amid, the Dragon Lord shows the Player his backstory. He was originally Tina’s personal character when she was first introduced to Bunkers and Badasses by Roland (Markus Lloyd). However, after she improperly used the Sword of Souls to wipe out all evil, this caused her character to turn evil, which angered Tina. She swore to only play as Bunker Master from then on, creating a world where only heroes win and the Dragon Lord, as a reoccurring villain, always loses. When the Dragon Lord realized his actions weren’t his own, he swore vengeance on Tina.TL;DR: Definitely one of the games ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Something about Borderlands 3 felt hateful. Characters talking about the grizzly twists of their campaign stories is so much more enjoyable than the oppressive negativity of Borderlands 3. I don't think I chuckled once during BL3 and Wonderands had me laugh out loud every couple of hours.+ Sidequests were substantial and I got surprisingly invested in many of them.Endgame is admittedly pretty rough.- DLC 1-4 are pretty awful, essentially just new skins for Chaos Chambers.- Endgame just isn't compelling. The campaign is great and absolutely the most I've ever enjoyed Borderlands and it's shocking they cut you off from it once you finish it.I'll probably play it less hours than BL3 but I actually enjoyed myself this time. _childDocuments_.review: This game is tedious. That's the best way I can put it. The classic Borderlands humor is there in bits and pieces; the Skelly-mens dialogue in fights is hilarious. But the overarching story falls flat. Plus, the Tiny Tina bit gets old FAST. In BL2, it was great to meet this quirky character who did funny voices, or called you Mamasita, etc. But an entire game of that - it got old quick. Dungeons are a slog. Most of the game is "encounters." Where you collect a shrine piece, or a side quest item. You hop into a closed arena with a pre-set amount of mobs to kill and at the end get your item. This, over and over and over again, gets tedious.Adding stats to your character - Strength = Crit Damage Buff, Dexterity = Crit Chance Buff - that was a nice touch, and you can pick an Archetype at creation that innately buffed your class choice, i.e. +Wisdon if you wanted a caster, etc.There's a heavy emphasis on melee attacks in this game. In fact, your melee weapon is now equippable with its own stats and damage like any other weapon. However, you still only have the default melee attack button as with any other BL game. No combos, no rolling or dodging, you just stand in front of an enemy and mash 'V' (for PC players) over and over. Tedious.Everything else about the game is boilerplate for a BL game. Weapon types, damage types, art style, it's all the same. This feels more like an up-jumped DLC than a full game on its own. Like the main BL team handed over all of its art assets and game engine to another studio to make something BL-adjacent.Lastly, for lack of a better term, the game as "Woke" as hell. Quests, NPCs, even audio-only lore narration - someone is gay, or trans, or asexual. That by itself isn't a bad thing, but the game just clobbers you over the head with it at every turn. It reminds me of a 12 year old, green-haired tween at Thanksgiving who's decided they have new pronouns, are Bi and everyone else there needs to know it *constantly.* It's obnoxious."We get it, Tina. You're on the right side of history. Now eat your carrots."

_childDocuments_.review: This game is rather "Meh"tldr; recommended for die-hard borderland gamers who crave more content.  Not so much for anyone else. Get it on sale (at least 50% off) unless you are prepared to be disappointed that you paid too much for a mediocre game. Think of this as a very large DLC.Details:If you're already a borderlands fan, then this game will provide some light entertainment> But far from the best in the series, Storyline:Plot: it is set in a "game within a game" (i.e. you play as the imaginary role playing character of an imaginary character)  This is a cute idea, and opens up some nice storytelling and world building possibilities.  But ultimately it also has a fatal flaw, in that there is never any sense of tension in the game or a feeling that anything you do matters very much even to your imaginary character.  This lack of tension is compounded by how easy the game is and how un-threatening the main antagonist is.Dialogue:Dialogue between Tina and her friends (the players of the game within a game) mostly well written and well acted, if you can forgive the heavy reliance of poor puns.  Dialogue with npcs within the "game within a game" are mostly poorly written (stilted and rarely either funny, interesting, or moving) and very poorly acted (some of the worst fake accents I've heard in a very long time; e.g. if you want a Scottish or Irish accent then please hire an actor from there to do it right).Looting and shooting:I guess most people coming to borderlands are mainly interested in the looter-shooter aspect.  They want interesting combat and good loot.  But these areas are where the game disappoints the most. I played on very hard, and the whole game was ridiculously easy.  Just equip the strongest weapons you find and run into any situation spamming bullets, spells and actions, then you will beat everything with barely a sweat.  Most borderlands player, myself included, are not looking for extreme difficulty.  Nonetheless we need a certain amount of challenge to make it even worth engaging.  I never had to put any real thought into choosing smart combinations of equipment and builds.  Never had to respec.  Just choose anything and run around killing.  Compare to BL3 where creating a good build is a large part of the fun, then this game really fails to deliver.  So far as the loot is concerned. The legendary drop rate is good - i.e. they are rare until you increase you luck level which is a fun challenge in itself.  But the legendaries when you get them are underwhelming.  Not just because they aren't all that powerful (which they don't need to be considering how weak the enemies are) but they mostly don't do anything very interesting either.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is INCOMPREHENSIBLY bad. i mean first off - every single weapon in this game is so uninspired it is actually painful. unlike borderlands where you get a new weapon and you switch not necessarily because its better but because its got cool unique mechanics; this game will give you a weapon and you will immediately realise this is the exact same weapon you just had with different stats. my best example of this is that at the beginning of the game i was using a green pistol that was a 2 shot burst pistol - i thought this was quite boring but had hope that the epic and legendary weapons would be better. then the first epic i got was literally the same weapon i was just describing except it did more damage. now this scared me but i still genuinely believed they had just put all their effort into making every legendary weapon unique - and then i got my first legendary... and oh my god i was disappointed because there is no way in hell that they just gave me the EXACT same weapon i had just been using with an elemental effect and 20 more bullets.and this doesnt just apply to the weapons, however, it is worst in the weapons because i kid you not there is only one weapon per weapon type and they just change the stats and effects of the gun at different rarities. this also happens with the melee weapons as every melee weapon looks super unique when you pick them up but you will quickly learn that they havent really added a melee weapon system as all the weapons are just reskins of your melee that change your stats slightly - missed opportunity and kind of deceptive as they make out as if the weapons will all be different and even with the classes in the game they make out as if the melee will be a genuinely viable build but it is not - it is practically the same as every other melee in the borderlands series but you can adjust the stats slightly. same goes for the spell mechanic - i found out after the first hour and a half that i had already used every spell template and the rest are just stat adjustments. it is literally ripping the identity of the borderlands games away from the franchise.now that was only my first problem with this game. another is that all the characters in this game are very bland and boring - all characters in this game have very boring abilities and if they dont the ability is usually very impractical and bad. tbh i wouldnt even care if there were tons of characters in this game, however there is only 3 more than borderlands 3 and all the characters only have 2 abilities apposed to the 6 borderlands 3 had which if you do the maths is 10 less abilities and you could argue each character has 3 but even then its 3 less abilities and these abilities if were gonna be generous are just passive abilities which to me doesnt even make sense why they are even considered abilities, we arent even considering the directors cut abilities for borderlands 3 these are just the base game content. and despite this lack of abilities they make you pick between 2 abilities - like why? feels like theyre just trying to make the illusion that you can make tons of builds but you cant. theyve also reduced the amount of upgrade trees from 3 per character to 1 so you all sense of build making is kind of thrown out the window; this game is actually so dead and boring its unbelievable. ive seen peoples arguments for this be that their are 7 characters in this game not 4; however borderlands 2 and pre-sequel both had 6 characters and this is a massive downgrade from borderlands 3 which showed what type of cool engaging abilities they are capable of making.now that ive pointed out the game play is ass - i will now talk about why the story is also ass. first off the characters in this game are unbearably cringe except the dragon king. the 2 supporting cast that you will have to speak to through out the WHOLE game dont really add anything and also are completely random characters despite the fact that we know brick and mordecai play bunkers and badasses with tina who would of been a much much better supporting cast. secondly, they give you the impression that characters from the main series would be present with their own OCs as paladin mike is clearly lorelei. however this is not true at all, the only cross over characters we get from here is the fairy punch father as brick and torgue. this is another lost opportunity they almost try to replace characters who are iconic and weve come to identify with certain things like moxxi and the bar who they tried to replace with lizzy but she has no personality and marcus as the gun trader with a character who isnt even a character and is just a basic npc called the blacksmith. there is a time they mention a "handsome hack" but never shown.now over to the story writing - it is very very cringe. you see in my opinion tiny tinas explosive personality is very very tame in this game and due to this all her comments just comes off as really nerdy and awkward - one example of this is when she says "the sword clatters to the ground kind of like this *clatter clatter clatter*" this joke actually made me bury my face in my hands because why? what is the purpose of the joke... there is no way they thought anyone would actually think this is funny because there isnt really a joke its just cringe for no reason. on top of this all the jokes are very unfunny as they tried to go down a nerdy DnD route and i get this game is based off that but there is no reason they couldnt blend the themes with the usual borderlands humour.All the areas you go to in this game are also just super boring - the DnD board that you walk around with a huge head is so forced. its not fun at all and doesnt really add anything, i dont get why it was added other than for the gimmick. this board removes the only reason for borderlands to even be open world that being the engaging movement mechanics and secrets to find. this is because due to the board mechanic there are no vehicles and on top of this the movement in this form is very awkward to control. and as far as im aware - there are no secrets to unlock in this game; on top of this there are these annoying enemies that spawn in and attack you which forces you into a pokemon esque encounter where you have to kill some basic enemies then it kicks you out... this would of been very cool but considering the combat in this game is so bland its just annoying because now i have to go through more boring fighting just to get where i need to go.now on to the further removal of content for no reason; there is no explosive element anymroe and its been replaced with "dark magic" which is basically just vampiric effect that leechs health from enemies giving it to you - now this is kind of a boring effect and considering they added a new health type for skeletons which couldve been countered by some sort of "holy element" but nah why would they do that despite having a difficulty that states you will have to use weapon effects for the certain health type in order to get by. and while they still have shields in here they removed class mods and replaced them with armour pieces which are basically the same thing but you can have 4 - now this makes no sense to me, i believe this wouldve been great to have a system to choose between armour points or shield points. on top of this bosses are just reskinned badass enemies - i could go on and on but steam ahs a limit on how much i can trash this game.feels like they saw everyone loved assault on dragons breach from borderlands 2 and thought we wanted a whole game based off it but it doesnt really work as a whole game; it was great as its own little thing - the lack of content is really shown in the downgrade from 100GB for borderlands 3 to 40GB for tiny tinas wonderlands. i really wanted to try and finish this game to see if it ever gets better but i genuinely cant make myself because this game is just so boring. do not buy this even for £15 it aint worth it.

Oh yeah I sure love hearing Skeletor screaming the thing in my ear every 5 minutes. Or my character making the same fart joke at a mushroom. The chaotic playstyle feels gutted. All those special skills that would completely change your entire play style are just gone. Now it's just "if you hit a critical the bullet ricochets" (away from enemies I stg)And the villain GOD. The best thing about the first few games was Handsome Jack. The worst thing about the third games were the evil tiktok twins. But those were believable compared to Mr. Dragon Lord. What's your plan? oh to destroy the planet? ♥♥♥♥♥ YOU LIVE HERE. you dont have a space ship to leave. It's just "I don't like one little girl" spite to kill himself and everyone else around him. _childDocuments_.review: This is NOT a borderlands game. It has borderlands graphics and its set in the same setting but thats IT. Everything from the quests to how you complete those quests is completely different. This game is incredibly tedious. You will be fighting the same enemies, in the same room. It's incredibly dissapointing how tedious and boring the gameplay became late game because it feels like a mission you've completed a hundred times over. It's fun utilizing the spells feature, which replaces the grenades from borderlands. This added feature to the regular borderlands fighting gameplay is an incredibly fun change of pace. I played a spell focused character and was very happy with my character decision. In all, I recommend. It's boring, but also really cool. If you're looking for something to pass the time, this is a good game for that. If you're into grinding, this game is for you. I don't like grinding so this feature became very boring very quick. The replay value is awful. It's such a tedious and repetitive game that starting out with a new character will purely change how you'll fight down the same waves of enemies. Not worth it in my opinion. But worth one playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: If you look at this game as very expansive DLC for Borderlands 3, under the assumption you enjoy Borderlands 3, you'll likely enjoy this game — if you're not sold on the hack n' slash genre but with guns and the camera being first person instead of being isometric, stay very far away form this game.• Melee weapons are now loot, they have weapon manufacturers and are no longer tied to specific characters.• Grenades are replaced by spells and no longer act as a consumable but are rather recharged by a cooldown period.• There's a lot of customization up front for your hero, voice, appearance, class etc. • Guardian Rank is replaced by Mythic Rank.• Your character has an actual stat sheet; dexterity, strength, wisdom, all that good stuff. This is in addition to the traditional skill tree that Borderlands characters have.• There's an overworld map that has dungeons, random encounters that can be explored, as opposed to a HUB city. (Which is still present.)And that's pretty much it. The gun manufacturers, should you have developed a favorite by now, have slightly different names from the mainline Borderlands' games. Jakobs is now Blackpowder and Dahl is now Dahlia for example. All in some vaguely humorous attempt to create a more  setting.The entire game is based on the  popular Borderlands 2 DLC “Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep”. I was never that fond of that DLC: I'm still pondering if that is due to me not liking the  Tiny Tina character, not generally enjoying  fantasy settings or the fact that they tried to jam an ostensibly sci-fi theme into a fantasy setting, just for sake of it. These reviews are for sharing your opinion and whether or not you'd  that someone  purchase and play a specific title. And for that I would say, if you enjoy Borderlands, buy this on sale. There's really nothing worth full price here. Don't get me wrong, there are some  ideas in this game that are just poorly executed. If you're on the fence, just skip it.I do see it as a stepping stone for Borderlands 4 or whatever they call the next mainline Borderlands. More customization is always good, maybe one day they'll make a DLC package that suits everyone's desires but this one leaves a lot to be desired.My other Borderlands reviews:• Borderlands 3 review • Borderlands 1 GOTY Enhanced review • Borderlands: Pre-Sequel review

Speaking of the wave arena, they will throw these at you as much as they can and it feels like padding..... a lot of padding, and in some cases way to much padding. This gets particularly tedious as the games difficulties are a joke and they will just none stop keep throwing enemies at you. I spent a majority of the time just running around meleeing enemies just to have some difficulty. The linear story area just don't have the same feel as a borderlands game either as most of the time they are just longer wave arena areas with more dialogue and even more enemies for you to just breeze through. The over world where you will be spending a lot of time wondering around is cute and interesting but loses its appeal rather quickly, It would have been better to just link the areas together or something. _childDocuments_.review: Not a good game. Far too much unskippable dialogue. Many of the skills seem boring or far too conditional to be useful outside of niche situations. Performance is WAY worse and inconsistent than it should be for how it looks, and it also frequently crashes resulting in spending more time waiting for it to load up again than actually playing.Many of the guns feel bad to use. Some have a weird delay after pulling the trigger, way too many rely on burst fire which I've always hated. Some guns aren't actually guns and are crossbows, meaning that they shoot slow projectiles, mening you have to lead targets. This feels terrible. Hyper-accurate aiming feels more difficult to accomplish as a result of these things than in any other previous BL game.Overall, it's kind of a miserable, frustrating experience. Gearbox messed up quite a lot in BL3 as well and it looks like they took all the wrong lessons from that game and doubled down in Wonderlands. At the very minimum, we should not be forced to stand around and wait while a poorly written character monologues at us for minutes at a time. I come to these games for the gameplay, not the terrible characters and stories.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a wasted oppurtunity from the start. The campaign, unlike Borderlands 3, is good. Characters are fun, some jokes actually land and it doesn't stretch out in some places more than others. The length of the main story is actually good, along with the side missions which are so big they sometimes feel like DLC.If only there was a way to replay them with the same character after you finish them... You cannot, it's literally the biggest flaw for this game, there's no such thing as a "true" mode unlike each and every single other game from the same developers. I don't care that this is WONDERlands and not BORDERlands, the games are the exact same.And I can't grasp why would they force chaos levels and the chaos dungeon down people's throats like they did. It's fun the first 10 times you do it, now imagine doing it another 90 times just to get a different version of the same legendary that does more damage, kind of like annoints stuck behind a tedious grind.For me, the reason it feels so repetitive is not only because it is but the way they do it. In other games of the series any sort of raid or whatever you wanna call it have their own location and you can do all of them at your own will. Here, you're forced to do these random stupid tiny rooms until you kill a set number of enemies.Legendaries are also very meh in this game. I feel like there's an incredibly small amount of them, either that or the loot is very repetitive, either way farming also gets very tedious.I dumped 20 hours on this game in the epic version at release, with all PLC (NOT DLC!!!!!!!), and I couldn't even bother to play the last one when it launched because they were practically the biggest scam I've ever seen in gaming. They knew people thought this game would have some sort of PLC (NOT DLC!!!!!!!) similar in structure and LENGTH to other games, so they made MORE CHAOS DUNGEONS that last 10 minutes and have a mediocre boss at the end with mediocre loot. Though I'll admit the last 2 bosses are actually fun and different.I just can't play this game as much as the others and I think that says a lot about their quality. For example:Borderlands 1 - About 50 hours on PS3, Switch, PS4 and PCBorderlands 2 - 400 hours on PS4 and PCBorderlands 3 - 300 hours on PS4, 150 on PCThey knew what this game was, and they threw it out anyway just to get a quick buck. I even tried adding mods to improve the experience and it kind of did, saying a lot about the main game. Wonderlands redux not only adds several Quality-of-Life things to the game, it also adds new legendaries, ways to farm and PEARLS!!! (and also recently contraband, whatever that is). Even then, the game fell short, and I got bored within 20 hours.At this point if a Borderlands 4 is ever going to come out, I'll just buy it when it's 20$ with all DLC. This game is not worth it at all if you're a Borderlands fan. If you play games once and then never again, then this is 100% a fun game to try for 10$, which was the price I paid when it was in a bundle at humble bundle.Other than that, I hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderlands doesn't give a F#$% and you shouldn't either. Nitpickers and snobs begone!Anyone familiar with Gearbox' unique franchise knows what they've signed up for once past the intro. Wonderlands lends itself incredibly well to the heavy stat-based neo-RPG formula that defines the Borderlands franchise. It's quite a bizarre combination, but it works. The combination of procedural-generation with weapons and the sardonic lighthearted humor that Gearbox has engineered reaches higher levels of refinement than ever before. This is the kind of game that we may not have wanted, but we all definitely deserved. The timing of it is unfortunate, because if it had been released before the likes of the Pre-Sequel, its meta commentary on the gaming zeitgeist would have felt more of its time. Tina herself sports an attitude that TV's best writers have only accomplished once or twice: zany and charming but undoubtedly cool. There's a whole lotta numbers to stare at all day, but in the end, just go with what is most fun. This is the combat formula that makes Borderlands awesome and occasionally frustrating, like when the right combination of stats come along, but the projectiles move in eccentric fashion and render themselves useless, the opposite happens too. Compared to the franchise, there are many welcome QOL adjustments, such as an explorable overworld with encounters that you can take or leave, or conjure by walking through some grass, no long "get to the hub world" intro, and some things locked behind a bit of a grind are just available. It's a game to have fun and absorb the wacky story, voice acting, writing, and even copy such as UI elements and other small details.Jump in, have fun, some things may suck a just little but you'll be fine. Stop taking everything so seriously!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is done and dusted. This was definitely a step up from the Prequel, BL3, and Assault on Dragon Keep, which were all subpar for various reasons (although I actually did enjoy the Prequel alright).I would like to start by noting that this game doesn't want to let you go. When you finish the story, you immediately begin the epilogue, which features Chaos runs, which are effectively challenge runs with debuffs added to make them more challenging. The game really, really wants you to play these, lol.Anyway, the campaign is an epic run through Tina's tabletop session where she is Gamemaster. But, the antagonist goes rogue, defying Gamemaster Tina; and you, Newbie, run through the campaign helping people out on the way to defeating the antagonist and restoring order to the Wonderlands.This is represented by increasingly unhinged and insane scenarios, lol. Which are by and large a lot of fun. That said, by around hour twenty, I was ready to start skipping side quests and dungeons in favor of wrapping up the main story.If you've played any Borderlands games, you already know the deal. It's immature, with nonstop jokes and meta, has faced paced and incredibly tight battles and gameplay, interesting level design, fantastic graphics, and stellar voice acting.Where this game deviates from the standard BL format is by including an Overland map (think tabletop world map), quick dungeons, and a mix of quests that happen in the Overland map and in the individual areas.It was stellar on the Steam Deck, where the default settings provided a mostly consistent 60 FPS and required no tweaks to play. It was obviously a battery hog, and I found I'd get just a little more than an hour on full charge. I did play plugged in mostly, but be aware that your battery life will be limited.There was an occasional stuttering, but beyond that, there were no issues to report.I don't think I would've actually bought this game given how much I did not enjoy BL3 and AoDK, but since it was in a Humble Choice, I was able to give it a try, and all in all, I'm glad I did. This was a legitimately fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to review... The game is definitely fun -- if I weren't having a good time I wouldn't have sunk six hours into it so far.  And the game looks and feels great - I'm getting a consistent 120+ fps on NVidia RTX 3070. Nevertheless, this game feels like the developers stitched together a patchwork quilt of experimental concepts.  Each in and of themselves is cool and fun - but the game does not hang together as an organic whole in the way (parts of) BLI, II, and III did.  I have only played solo -- but it doesn't seem to be the kind of game I'd even want to play coop.  The overworld/underworld concept is maybe ok for single player but I feel it would be awkward for four players.  This is a shame being as 2K's other entries make such a strong, even genre defining, multiplayer showing.  (yeah, I know, this opinion means little being as I haven't tried it ) Tiny Tina was funny like fourteen hundred DLC releases ago but now I find myself straining to understand that shrill rapid fire voice -- it is *very* *very* annoying.  The guns are kind of disappointing and whereas sorting and selling the weapons cornucopia was fun in BL I - III, here it feels like a chore.  Combat is all run and gun and stupid easy... I would like to see more of a balance between the run right in and gun em down elements and some tactical stuff... allow for duck and cover.. peeking, etc.  I did say graphics are good -- but I do find the art kind of repetitive.  Same as with the weapons, Don't pay full price for this.  Pick it up on sale - at $29 you are, in my opinion, getting full value. Building upon the success of the Borderlands series, this spin-off offers a refreshing take on the looter-shooter genre, delivering an unforgettable experience that showcases Gearbox's signature style.Graphics and Art Design (5/5):The game immediately captivates with its vibrant and imaginative art design. From lush, enchanted forests to chaotic, explosive battlefields, Tiny Tina's Wonderland is a visual feast. The cartoonish aesthetic, combined with the attention to detail in character design and environments, creates a world that feels both fantastical and inviting.Story and Characters (4.5/5):Tiny Tina's Wonderland introduces players to a narrative spun by the titular character, Tiny Tina, as she takes on the role of Dungeon Master in a tabletop-inspired adventure. The story line weaves humour, whimsy, and unexpected twists, with a cast of characters that bring the game's fantasy world to life. While the plot may lean more towards comedy than drama, the writing is sharp and keeps players engaged throughout their journey.Game play and Combat (4.8/5):The core of Tiny Tina's Wonderland lies in its engaging and chaotic combat system. Players can choose from various character classes, each with its unique abilities and skill trees. The gun play is as satisfying as ever, with an added layer of magic-infused mayhem. The introduction of spell casting and fantastical weaponry brings an exciting twist to the traditional looter-shooter formula, keeping battles dynamic and unpredictable.Customisation and Progression (4.7/5):The game excels in offering diverse customisation options for character builds and equipment. Players can tailor their characters to suit their preferred play style, experimenting with a plethora of magical spells and outlandish weaponry. The progression system feels rewarding, with each level-up providing a sense of empowerment and unlocking new possibilities for character development.Multiplayer and Co-op (4.5/5):Tiny Tina's Wonderland encourages cooperative play, allowing friends to join the chaotic adventure together. The cooperative experience enhances the game's fun factor, as players can combine their unique abilities for even more explosive results. The seamless integration of multiplayer features and the drop-in, drop-out co-op option make it easy for players to team up and embark on a magical journey together.Conclusion:Tiny Tina's Wonderland is a delightful and refreshing addition to the looter-shooter genre, showcasing Gearbox's ability to blend humour, chaos, and fantasy seamlessly. The game's captivating art design, engaging combat, and entertaining story line make it a must-play for fans of the Borderlands series and newcomers alike. While a few minor technical issues may surface, the overall experience is a whimsical and thrilling adventure through Tiny Tina's fantastical imagination.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, long time Borderlands fan here. I've put over 200 hours into this game on PS5 and completed the main story three times, so I know the story and the end game pretty well. Let me start this review by saying the base game here is really good. The game play and the story are both great - aside from the odd story character I found to be weirdly handled...The story is several steps up from that mess in BL3. Is it on par with BL2? I wouldn't say so, but it's still great in its own right. Definitely a worthy continuation of the Dragon's Keep DLC. The main bad guy is surprisingly well set up. I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone that played BL2 and the Dragon's Keep DLC just for the story.The game play is very similar to BL3, in all the right ways in my opinion. The movement feels good, not like the awkward rigid movement in BL2, and the new spell system makes for a lot of fun. Spells replace grenades in this game, so while you technically have infinite ammo, you are restricted by the cool down (in most cases) so you can't spam all your grenades/spells to instantly clear a zone. The spells do make for much more varied play styles though, so I think they're a great addition.Playable characters now have voice lines and actually interact with the world in unique and interesting ways depending on your character's personality. The character customisation here is far better than any BL game previously, and offers a respectable level of customisation. My only wish would be the ability to transmog armour. Armour replaces Class Mods from previous BL games, Amulets replace Relics/Artifacts, and new Rings (you can equip up to two) also act like additional Relics/Artifacts. This is a decent change, and makes sense. Wards also replace shields, and function exactly the same as shields from BL3, for example. I like all of these changes.I also like the new hero point and myth rank systems. Hero points are like additional skill points you can use to increase crit damage, crit chance, spell cooldown, etc. Myth rank is basically like BAR from BL2. Both are great. The level cap is currently 40, so a little lower than the max level of 50 in BL2's base game. Although you do unlock your action skill at level two, so you don't lose out on as many points as you'd expect. I expect this to get increased in future though.The actual classes you can choose, however, leave something to be desired. Currently, the Spellshot is by far the most powerful class, and there's not really much point going with anything else. Spellshot + Stabbomancer seems to be the meta for most end game builds, and it's easy to see why. It would be nice if the other classes got some buffs to put them on par, or at least close to, the power of the Spellshot - in their own respective ways (I'm not saying Clawbringer should be able to deal as much spell damage as the Spellshot, for example).The new split class system is also a bit of a double edged sword too, I think. On one hand, it means players only have to level up half as many characters, which is great for more casual players that want to try every character. On the other hand, it makes which class you choose less impactful since their short comings can be offset by choosing an appropriate secondary class. Moreover, combining two classes which compliment each other in unique ways makes for an unbalanced end game - like Spellshot + Stabbomancer using Double Knot and From The Shadows. More character balance is definitely needed in my opinion.The guns also leave something to be desired. The vast majority of legendary weapons feel underwhelming, in terms of damage dealt, special effects, and cool factor. BL2 and 3 had some awesome legendaries... The Monarch/Dictator, Unkempt Harold, Slagga, Conference Call, etc. This game doesn't have anything that comes even close to any of those. In fact, a lot of regular (i.e. non-unique) blue/purple weapons outperform many legendaries. That should not be the case. This is made worse by the fact that legendaries are rarer in this game compared to BL3 (although more common than in BL2). So getting legendaries is harder than in BL3, and they also perform worse. That doesn't make for a fun game play experience.Melee weapons have also been added to this game, and they actually add a lot to the experience. Legendary melee weapons (unlike the majority of legendary guns) offer really cool benefits over their lesser rarity counterparts, and can change how you play the game. This is a really fun change. However, don't expect to be running any melee only builds because there are a lot of flying enemies you can't melee - plus a lot of bosses that also can't be melee'd (like... why?). That being said, I'm glad they're in the game, even if the developers seem to forget that sometimes when they're designing bosses.The end game consists of Chaos Chambers - dungeon style encounters which allow you to unlock Chaos Levels (mayhem levels from BL3). This is actually pretty fun at first, but due to lack of variety, tedious farming in the final loot chamber, and over reliance on farming Chaos Chambers for loot, they quickly become uninteresting. Spending 15 minutes doing a run and then another 15 minutes (or probably more) sorting through loot in the final loot room is not my idea of a fun time. They have made efforts to improve this experience by adding vending machines in the final room, but it still feels like a chore to slog through a Chaos Chamber. This is made worse by the fact that they keep raising the maximum Chaos level. I thought 20 was fine. It was pretty hard, but not punishing. Then they upped it to 35, and destroyed build diversity because it was so difficult. Now it's 50. I haven't taken the time to get to Chaos Level 50, but I don't imagine it's going to be fun. There are now more Chaos levels than actual levels... And you don't get skill points for increasing your Chaos level. You don't get anything. You get tougher enemies and a chance for slightly more powerful loot to drop in the form of Chaotic/Volatile/Primordial/Ascended loot. Great...Now for my biggest gripe with this game - aside from the current state of Chaos Chambers. The "first season pass." Firstly, I find the idea of a game having multiple season passes offensive already. Was my £55 initial payment not enough? You need another £50 in the form of two additional season passes? Really? Insulting... Not to mention the fact that the first DLC came out less than a month after the release of the actual game, so they were surely working on it before the game was released and decided not to include it in the base game... and it came out with bugs which they only just recently fixed by the way (shark enemies with missing names, for example). This whole things stinks of corporate greed, and I hate it. As for the DLCs themselves, well, they're trash. They're basically just additional Chaos Chambers you pay extra for. Yes, it's pretty nice that once you complete one of these DLCs their rooms and bosses get added to the Chaos Chamber rotation, but they're still ultimately more monotonous Chaos Chambers.Why no story DLCs? BL2 had some of the best story DLCs ever. This game is literally a spin off from one of BL2's DLCs. It seems like after BL2 you guys forgot how to make good DLC. BL3 had a similar problem with seemingly lazy DLC content churned out. The only reason to buy any BL3 or Wonderlands DLCs is for the powerful loot you guys put in them. Other than that, they hardly deserve to see the light of day, never mind the hard earned money from your player base. It's frankly insulting. And what makes it even worse in this case (compared to BL3) is there's no transparency. TALK TO YOUR PLAYERS. Leaving us in the dark is just disrespectful.In summary, I would recommend playing this game if you liked Dragon's Keep or BL3. Wait for a decent sale (<=£30) and buy the base game. Avoid the first season pass for now, it's nowhere near worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Big Borderlands player here, I just wanted to finally leave a positive review because I feel the game deserves it and maybe it can help someone new to try it out. I know many a Borderlands fan that have yet to or probably won't play Wonderlands. Now I was late to the game actually. Such an anticipated release for me, but it took me a year and a half after release to start it for real. Hence late to the game. But now I'm on my 4th 100% play-through, and I'm having a blast. I'm kind of a completionist when it comes to my Borderlands runs, or I give myself extra restrictions or challenges. But onto Wonderlands.I don't think I've written a review before, that's why I know I think the game deserves some good word. So all in all, I hear a lot that it's a short game with little content. And comparatively to an obvious BL2 with 10 DLC. However, I think Wonderlands has perfectly enough content. No more no less. The maps are huge and sometimes puzzle-esque. I loved the campaign map challenges in BL3, and Wonderlands nailed it with them too. And I'm having a hard time remembering where they all are each map, so that means they are well placed and take time to re-find or encounter. So the thing is, is that I've spent 2 hours plus in some maps to finish each mission and campaign challenge there. That's a lot of time. I don't think I've ever spent 2 hours in one map doing the story mission, couple sides, or couple challenges in the older games. (BL3 excluded since Wonderlands is essentially a reskin of BL3). Of course I farm for items, but just playing the game for what i'm supposed to accomplish, you can spend A LOT of time in this game. Not to mention for those that enjoy it, some parts of the game are pretty challenging compared to other Borderlands titles. The 4 DLC expansions are definitely challenging gauntlets, with good items too. It's no crazy story campaign DLC, but they are fun and unique I think. Not like the Headhunters, and not a campaign DLC.The writing is classic Borderlands style with plenty of throwbacks and "easter egg dialogue". A LOT of dialogue though. Plenty of unskipable paragraphs of dialogue, but again I personally enjoy the Borderlands writing. All but one or two cut-scenes are skipable. It is a fun story, twists and turns, and very exciting landscapes. The maps are beautiful and it's just such a flip change from mostly being on the dusty toxic wasteland Pandora. It's such a different vibe playing Borderlands but fantasy/medieval themed. Some parts of the game you spend much more time in that region, kind of like Eden-6 in BL3. But like I said, some maps are huge. And I enjoy that because that is the content right there. So many different ways around these landscapes. The End game Chaos Chamber is very rewarding for your progression. But it is definitely a grind and I think a huge step UP from Digistruct Peak and OP levels. I enjoy those too believe me, but The Chaos Chamber and the way you manage to get maximum level gear is actually fresh and not just a repeat of OP levels or Mayhem. All three are a bit different from each other. I don't think they should really be compared harshly. Each end game style is pretty unique to the respective game.But I'll wrap it up here I just wanted to throw down a few thoughts. I think this is a great Borderlands franchise title. And you know it's good when you have more fun with each play-through. My current 4th play-through is StabboShot on Intense mode. First Intense mode play-through. So the review is based on Normal balanced difficulty. Take care adventurers, if you haven't tried Wonderlands out yet, and I may be biased towards Borderlands as a whole, but I definitely recommend this very fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I am not a native English speaker, so please excuse my bad English.  Second, I am not a game developer, everything is based only on my OPINION. I am really disappointed with this game. I played all Borderlands titles up to this date and loved most of them except Borderlands 3.  These are some of my problems I have with this game:You don't have different playable characters, instead you have to make your own. This really took away from the replayability of this game.  I played through Borderlands 2 and 3 with all the characters, and every interaction was different. Now you have the same dialog over and over again. Yes, you can change the voice, but it doesn't feel that different. In Borderlands 2, playing Krieg and Axton was a whole other feeling. The personality of their voice lines were fitted to their skills and overall appearance. The skill and the skill tree got a really hard downgrade from previous Borderlands games. Every class has only one skill tree, and you can have two classes on one character. The skills are, most of the time, really boring. There are some many skills that say: “Damage Type: + X%” or “Reload/Swap Speed: +X%”. The cap stones and kill skills are some of the most interesting skills, but they shouldn't be the only interesting ones. Picking a backstory a besides the class is the second important choice you have to make at the start of the game. The backstory provides bonuses to your Hero Stats that are essentially your crit, health and cooldown stats.  The bad thing about this is that you can't change it. I understand why you can't spontaneously change your backstory, but it feels awful that some class combination have a disadvantage because of your backstory. You have to know what class combo you want to play to be able to pick the right backstory for your character.  Most enemies in this game are melees. They come running and charging at you, and you are surrounded by enemies. They are constantly dodging and with most of the new guns having projectiles with travel time it makes them really hard to hit. Like said in the point above, most enemies are melees, but we have melee weapons too, so why not fight melee enemies with melee weapons? Because melee in this game feels terrible. Every time you melee, the control of the camera is taken away from you, and you lock on to an enemy. That not only feels bad, but it doesn't do anything if you don't build around melee. The worst part about the new melee weapons is that they are clogging up the loot pools, but more about this later. The guns in this game are a mix between the new fantasy approach and ripped straight out of Borderlands 3. The problem with the new weapons is that most of them have projectiles with travel time. There are so many enemies that dodge your shots or run around or in the worst case fly around that hit something with the new weapons is a pain in the butt. The old weapons that got ripped aren't bad, but leave a bitter taste. I really don't want to call Gearbox uninspired or something like that, but it adds to the feeling that this game is more like a DLC for Borderlands 3 than a stand alone.  Bosses in this game are another thing that bugs me. In the base game, we have 8-story bosses and 4 from side quest. That is not a lot of bosses. Especially when you play chaos runs, you see the same bosses over and over again. The bosses we have aren't really special, most of them have mechanics where you have to dodge an incoming wave.  Loot is one of the most important things in all the Borderlands games. But this game has so few legendary items, and a big portion of them are melee weapons. That wouldn't be a big issue if they were all ok and useable, but with the introduction of chaos mode, most of them can't keep up.  Then there is the problem that a lot of the good rings and amulet don't have a dedicated loot source. That means if you want a specific ring that doesn't have a dedicated loot source, you have to get lucky and is just frustrating. Since Borderlands 3 it is impossible to farm for perfect guns and other gear, but it was still possible to farm a nearly perfect class mod. Now class mods or armor are a complete mess. A class mod now has an own effect, two classes, up to 3 skills and bonus stats. The order of the classes on the armor has an effect on the skill that come with it too. The naming scheme for items is just confusing. The name for an item contains, most of the time, a prefix, the name of the item and a suffix. That makes item names way too long and is a pain to keep track of.The last gear specific problem I have with this game are the enchantments. There are too many of them, a lot of them aren't good and the amount of Moon Orbs you need to roll another one is way too high, for the amount of possibilities. One roll starts at a cost of 9 and goes up to 4000 Moon Orbs. You can only have 16,000 Moon Orbs at a time. Farming a specific enchantment is not only time-consuming, but tedious. Farming 16 000 Moon Orbs to roll 4 times when I rolled an item 10 times.Chaos level are now the new form of end game difficulty like mayhem level in Borderlands 3. That wouldn't be bad if there weren't 3 issues. First, there are too many chaos levels, at the time of this review there are 50 level. After a specif milestone, gear of higher quality can be dropped, but the problem is that the enemies get stronger, and you only have a chance of better loot no guarantee. Second, the chaos level's maximum was raised to quick. I can't say if / when they will raise it again, but if it happens, you have to farm everything again. Third, the higher the chaos level is, the higher the chance of you getting killed in one shot. The scaling doesn't feel right, and enemies mutate to bullet sponges. It doesn't make it better that you are constantly getting swarmed by melee enemies. At the end, I want to say that I don't hate this game. I am going to continue playing this game, but I hope they will change some of the points I have talked about.For everyone who is thinking about buying this game, I want to give some advice.If you are looking for a fun looter shooter that you can play with friends or solo, and you don't care about longevity or overall balancing, I can recommend this game. But please buy it when it's on discount you maybe want gear from the DLCs, and they are not worth the $9.99 each. If you are a long time Borderlands fan like me, and you hope this game is a step forward from Borderlands 3 I think this game is not for you. There are too many flaws that hold this game back from being a good Borderlands title. But the game is still being work on, so perhaps it will get there.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR For a post DLC completed game experience, the amount of bugs and issues present is unacceptable. If I had paid full price for this game I'd want my money back. Buy it on sale and enjoy the gameplay.I'll keep this brief as yeah, I do intend to complete the game but not in the sense I did former Borderlands titles by finding the best gear doing all the quests etc. This game is held up by its gameplay for me. If that wasn't fun, honestly I would have refunded it and tried to find a different game for my buddy and I to play. To put it simply, this game is pretty buggy, even moreso than any Borderlands title I've played in the past. They range from complete game crashes, graphical issues minor and major, sound issues minor and major, desync issues, a few of them requiring complete restarts after booting up the game. The gameplay is fun enough to be willing to tolerate these to a degree. Some of the other issues come with the maps design and the existence of certain invisible walls in places they really shouldn't be and some not being in places they should. The worst bug I found is in the magical bean quest area. There's a completely random spot on the map that if you "superhero slide" into it, you just die. The other part, I'm not one for politics in games, left or right unless it's a proper fit to the overall story and really is setting a deep tone of some kind or whatever the case may be. I will say seeing pronouns on the character creation screen had me a little leery and it was rightfully so. Now it isn't that they push themes too harshly or anything but it's just the writing in this game isn't flavorful or really all that good. The lack of wordplay for innuendo and overly crude humor just for the sake of it gets old really really fast. They just don't land, the characters aren't going to be memorable from this game. It's carried solely by Tina so far. If you just want the combat from Borderlands, it's here 100% and it's good. The rest of the game is most likely going to be forgettable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start off that i recieved this as a gift when it was on a 50% sale, but i had this in my wishlist ever since the kickstarter.I would 100% recommend this game to borderlands fans. If you've just finished Borderlands 3, play this game, even if just for the campaign, which took me about 30 hours to complete, but i had fun, i like to rush the main story line, i still got almost all the sidequests untouched, bunch of challenges and what not. If you'd like an apology from the writing team after what happened in B3, go for this, especially if it's on sale. The cast is all different, there may be couple of recurring characters, like Tiny Tina (duh), cl4p-tr4p is there running around the world, but he won't be with you for the whole journey. There are few more, like MR. TORGUE, possibly couple others. However they do not take main stage, they are most of the time in sidequests and in the background. Otherwise it's a whole new cast of characters, giving the writers some freedom and ease of baggage from the past. They're lovely, colorful and i find to enjoy them.The plot is simple, with its own twists and turns, it's no Shyamalan, it all fits well. It's a D&D type of story, with lots of refferences and puns to go. But even still it has strong moments. There were times where i could relate cause these things happened at my tables as well. They know what they were doing in this department.The jokes are back, baby. The borderlands game have a distinct humour that can be a hit or miss for everyone. It's very in your face, sarcastic, no-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, punny, full of references like you love them. In B3 a lot of things felt forced, a huge vibe of "hello fellow kids". Not in this game, the jokes felt like the borderlands i know. Sure there were couple that had me eye rolling but otherwise i actually laughed out loud, or made me smile with a dumb grin. This of course is something that will differ from person to person, but in my perspective, it feels like the writers gave a ♥♥♥♥ this time around. The gameplay is awesome, it's basically the best thing from B3 ported over here, what else would you want. Of course this time it's more with a fantasy aesthetic, and it's design very well when it comes to glueing together space-cowboy guns and fantasy magic. Instead of grenades you got spells and there's but ton of them. It's like a secondary skill that you can pick and choose (of course, you can pick and choose your skill as well, especially later on when you unlock multiclassing and you will have a choice between 4 skills), with infinite use and cooldown on top. Plus there's the variations of each spell like damage type, some unique quirks like shooting it twice, the way you cast out the spell, charges, etc etc. With classes and fairly simple yet detailed character creation, you can truly make your own vault hunt- i mean fatemaker. There are issues of course, some people might not like the map is much smaller than previous titles and the "quirky" way you move between locations, but honestly, this (and it's just my oppinion) is one of the strengths of the game. It's smaller, but much more detailed and each location has its focus. The outworld, or gameboard you walk on gives it a unique charm and it sells you the feeling that you're sitting down with Tina to play some tabletop. But there are some actual issues like bugs, they are not gamebreaking, mostly annoying. For example, sometimes (and this happened like two times exactly in my 30 hours of gameplay) when i'd use my skill, after it ended, the camera would stay in this awkward first person wind up moment, where you had no access to guns, nor spells, or actions, as if i was stuck mid animation still, but just opening and closing the inventory, or the pause menu fixed this. Second bug i encountered was having a prompt still up on my screen, even though there was nothing to Use or Open, but again, quick pause/unpause fixed it just fine.Overall, wait for a nice sale and get the game if you love borderlands. I can't speak for the DLCs, i see a lot of negative reviews, but i might still get them, if i'll get to them. But either way, this is an enjoyable game, with a bonus rogue-like loop at the end, which might be the main focused what they intended, but to me it's just a nice bonus for after-campaign shenanigans.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5It's Borderlands with a fantasy twist.Not much else to say really. If you like the Borderlands style, this will appeal to you, if not, well I think you're missing out.As it's pretty much just a Borderlands game, I'll only point out what would be different:1. you start off with only one skill tree for your class. You will unlock the ability to choose a skill tree from another class later on. After you finish the main story, you can change your second skill tree to any other class in the game.2. There is no New game plus or "True Vault Hunter mode". I'm a bit disappointed by that. The game is pretty easy, and I was hoping for a meaningful challenge to work through.3. Melee weapons. On the other games, melee is an afterthought, except for maybe a couple characters, and even then it's practically useless.  In Wonderlands, you can actually build a character around melee AND melee weapons are a specific item class, complete with their own stats. Some bosses you still need to use guns on because you cannot reach them, but it's a big improvement that I hope they keep in future titles.4. The Overworld. As the whole thing is framed as a game of Bunker's and Badasses DM'd by Tina, there is a sort of map that you can traverse between areas. There are some sidequests and other things you can do on the overworld. Overall it's an alright concept that did it's job.That's all I have to say.If you like Borderlands, you probably already bought it. If you've never played Borderlands, but like shooters with RPG elements and a stupid amount of loot drops, then I recommend you have a go.

Get ready to embark on a wild and unpredictable adventure that blends the best of fantasy and first-person shooting. _childDocuments_.review: **I played through the game with the Redux mod installedMost fun I've had in a Borderlands game since the pre-sequel. The classes are interesting and fun, and multi-classing especially gives some really interesting options when it comes to character creation. If you enjoy the gameplay loop of Borderlands games, you'll probably enjoy this one. One nice thing is that the game isn't too long so I managed to finish all the sidequests before getting bored. No comment on the endgame loop since I haven't really done much of that. The writing isn't as bad as people make it out to be - at the very least it's better than the trainwreck that was Borderlands 3. This game really doubles down on the wacky and zany part of Borderlands writing.. and I think it works really well. I think at least they were able to give the supporting characters some fun personalities. There are also some neat ties to the lore of Borderlands 2.The one major complaint I have is that I ran into very frequent game stuttering when I played through the game. My game will freeze from anywhere between half a second to 5 whole seconds randomly. My hardware is quite good and I don't have this issue when playing any other game. I don't know if it's an issue with the mod or something else but it's certainly the biggest gripe I have with the game. The DLC areas are also super unfun.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably better with friends, I did the whole thing co-op myself and had a great time but, everything is better with friends I suppose. Regardless I like the customisation, the world design is absolutely incredible, the story is cheesy and silly and not all that serious, a bit less serious than even the mainline Borderlands story-lines, but it's enough to keep me engaged. I did enjoy the twist at the end.What little I did spend of the game solo I really just liked wandering around looking at everything. It seriously is a beautiful game. I don't like the overworld. It's clunky and annoying to navigate. It fits in with the narrative but doesn't have any business being here from a gameplay or design perspective in its current form. The story is relatively short but I like that there is a genuinely decent amount of side content - including entire new areas and worlds that are exclusively optional, like the giant beanstalk. The bosses were much too easy. In general I felt the difficulty scaling was naff, the entire game was a breeze, the Legendaries felt soulless and uninspired (a crime by Borderlands standards), the enemies were predictable and sometimes annoying, like the dragon things and the weird walking land-sharks.Brighthoof is an amazing hub world that takes me back to the original Sanctuary of Borderlands 2. It's easy to navigate, has recognisable districts, and has lots of fun platforming potential and hidden locations. It's certainly a vast improvement over Sanctuary III, the disastrously claustrophobic and maze-like spaceship from Borderlands 3.Overall: Gameplay is fun, feels smooth and responsive and satisfying much like Borderlands 3. The story is what it is, nothing special, but it pulls the game along well enough. The level and world design is absolutely incredible and by far the greatest-looking game in the series. The overworld sucks and a few enemies are annoying.I never bothered with the endgame content so I can't comment on that, it seems fun but I was satisfied with completing the story and leaving it at that personally.

_childDocuments_.review: TIny Tina's Wonderland is just another Borderlands game. I played this co-op and the combat was largely the same as prior entries just in a different setting. I think personally the Borderlands series is starting to lose its charm. The dialogue felt grating but in line with Borderlands 3. The side quests dragged on and had a ton of dialogue that served little purpose other than to waste time and tell bad jokes. You might expect combat to be different since this is a fantasy world but you still use guns - although there are a few new variants. The biggest deviation is using spells instead of grenades. The spells in the game do have some various new effects and visuals that were fun to use. I did have some good mindless fun playing this co-op but I think Gearbox needs to reevaluate it's formula - but maybe I'm just aging out of the target demographic. Overall there is some fun to be had here but I find it hard to recommend unless the game is at a steep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game, had the highest hopes for another fun filled borderlands experience, and all I got was sick bard jokes. That's basically all. There is literally no real soundtrack, except some generic dnd background music. to the game and no engaging gunplay, which in combination accomplishes some of the most boring boss fights I have ever seen. The open world got cut for stupid random encounters in the same few battle arenas, filled with junk and so sparsley populated enemy wise, that it's not even worth using any AOE weapons/skills. The few enemies that are there sponge bullets like they are straight from bikini bottom and are plain as grassland variation wise. If it weren't for some badass enemies that tend to onehit you on higher difficulty levels you could literally just shoot wooden dummies. For me Tiny Tina as a narrator is not cutting it either, as her voice and hyper energy got boring and even tiring in just the first hour of the game. To charge 60 Bucks for this dumpsterfire is a scam at best.Quest wise and storytelling wise it boils down to being bombarded with dialogue whilst shooting at your bullet sponges and watching your weapon reload animation like the most bland animation movie ever made. If it is not that it forces you to  wait for some unimportant dialogue to finish whilst you are standing around and pondering life.I really don't get it why people recommend this game for i quote "A laugh or two", if I want a laugh i could simply watch a cat video on youtube and that's even free.I would only recommend this game for diehard fans with a high frustration tolerance and ask yourself beforehand if the money isn't worth investing in a actual fun activity, like a boardgame, or catfood, or a tree sapling. Conclusion: Stating that the game isn't cutting it for me would be a bold understatement. I am actually disappointed and bored by the lack of engagement this piece of virtual "Art", that I would really recommend reconsidering your choice twice or even thrice if you consider buying this game.
