_childDocuments_.review: ✅I enjoy the nerdy D&D aspects✅Loot can be fun – Feels good to score legendaries➖Boring story/Writing is dull➖Humor is just name references➖Endgame content is repetitive and lacks incentive➖Despite multi-classing, not very creative build optionsTiny Tina’s Wonderlands (TTW) does not take place inside the normal Borderlands universe, instead you are playing a game of Bunkers & Badasses (Dungeons & Dragons). The game world consists of 3 parts: The overworld, arenas, and zones. The overworld is new to the Borderlands series. It’s a large walking area that you use to travel to arenas and zones. Arenas are smaller areas where you fight enemies if they collide with you on the overworld, or from smaller dungeon-like zones on the overworld. The final one, zones, is what most Borderlands veterans would be familiar with. These are the large zones that contain the bulk of story elements. None of the zones really felt as memorable as places like Sanctuary, much of it I felt is just forgettable and uninspired. Historically, the narrative and loot are what propelled Borderlands 1 and 2 into stardom. Unfortunately the narrative took a nosedive after BL3 with the writing being atrociously cringe. I felt the narrative overall was bad, but not the lowest I’ve seen in the BL series. Nearly every single case of humor comes from a dumb naming reference. As a huge  fan, I was eternally let down when I got to a quest staring  and the writers did the bare minimum with the material. As for the lore, there are a couple throwbacks to prior BL games, but largely the entire game does not involve BL history at all. The length of the game – I did all sidequests and completed the story within about 35hrs. I spent another ~6hrs doing the endgame content. I didn’t use mods, but I felt the use of a save file editor was very useful. The main thing I used it for was to swap my classes (more in gameplay below) as you can only change your dual class and not the class you started as. There is no way I’m replaying this game 5x for all the starting classes, but I did want to explore and test out some builds. BL has always been a series that has deep gameplay mechanics, making it almost like an FPS RPG. TTW continues the tradition with skill trees and adds in a fresh D&D element of dual classing. Traditionally you choose a character and get 3 separate trees, each oriented towards their own playstyle. In TTW, you get a single skill tree out of 5 (4 without DLC) and as you progress far enough into the story, you can choose any of the other skill trees as your secondary. You still lose out on a 3rd tree, but its nice being able to customize. I started as a Sporewarden and picked up Stabbomancer. I quickly found out that companion AI is mediocre at best, so I wanted to swap out the Sporewarden. Unfortunately, you cannot change the class you start with, only the one you choose. Enter save editor to save the day! Eventually, I ended up with Spellslinger and Stabbomancer as my endgame choice. This is after much difficulty of trying to settle on a build because unlike prior BL entries, the talent trees here feel boring and a bit too safe. There is no crazy dual wielding guns or siren elemental shots of previous games. It just all feels watered down. Ultimately, I didn’t find a build that made me want to stick around and play the endgame….Speaking of endgame, I found the loop repetitive and uninspired. It entirely consists of endless battles in the arena zone as you grind out chaos levels. Once you hit the cap of level 40, you start gaining alternate advancement levels (myth ranks) to compliment the chaos spam. You spam arenas over and over to increase difficulty, loot, and loot quality, essentially ending with volatile and ascended gear which is much more powerful than regular legendaries. But….why? You get all this crazy gear and the only thing you use it on is moooore chaos runs. There is no leaderboards or anything of purpose to give the player a reason to want to get higher. The loot itself seems typical BL-ish. I acquired multiple legendaries and most of them had the same effects as previous games. Again, TTW seems to not want to try anything new. I found the difficulty on par with other BL titles, it mostly felt just right. I did enjoy the power you felt when looting a legendary and how it would carry your gameplay through the next few levels. I experienced multiple UI bugs with my companion, often showing he was dead when he was not. A pretty package, probably the best looking BL game out there. It’s been a while since I played BL3, but I’d reckon it’s the same or better looking than BL3. The art style maintains the signature cartoon outlined look. The UI is serviceable. I didn’t like the inventory setup. Would be nice to mark multiple things as junk as you get a LOT of crap loot. I also did not like how in the endgame they do not tell you the effects of the levels you choose OR the portals you choose in chaos mode. Like…just why?? Super lazy and easy to implement, they tell you AFTER you make the choice, but not before. So I’d need to have the effects pulled up on my 2nd monitor to make sure I don’t screw myself over with an impossible affix. Game ran pretty flawless on ultra at 120fps on my desktop PC: i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDI noticed constant issues with audio, it has this weird directional depression effect where if you are not facing the NPC, their voice loudness is cut by like 70%. Super annoying and I didn’t notice this in any other games. Tested across speakers and headset, tested multiple audio options, and could never fix it. If I wasn’t staring directly at an NPC, I ended up bolting away from them so their speech would come through my character’s “head” as the talking heads do in past BL games. Other than that issue, the sound was pretty normal – just there, nothing exceptional or bad. Despite the boring endgame, you still at least have the option to play endlessly. There is also NG+ with the story mode if you enjoyed that. There are tons of side quests that is the bulk of the content in TTW. Interestingly enough, much of the side quests also have a player choice, but pretty sure it doesn’t matter at all outside of which voiced line you get. A beautiful but mid experience. Nowhere near the writing expertise, and masterful gameplay that BL2 had achieved. With BL3 and now this, I’m starting to get the impression that BL2 was like catching lightning in a bottle and can never be repeated by Gearbox. This is the same, if not worse, than BL3. If you are a BL fan, then pick this up. Otherwise, wait and see if the next title in the BL universe can redeem the series. I would recommend this below $15 though. I feel as if I got my money worth at that price point. You can find my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: I would LOVE this game and put hundreds of hours into it if I could just shoot enemies and sift through their loot. This game is not made for you to easily shoot people and sift through their loot. This game is made for you to be forced into watching and listening to unskippable custscenes/dialogue/animations. This was the major problem with Borderlands 3 and it has persisted here. Seriously, this sucks. I genuinely hate to see one of my favorite series do bad for NO OTHER REASON than the developers put as many unskippable narrative moments into their shooter as possible. This is a looter shooter, not Skyrim. But, EVEN IN SKYRIM YOU CAN SKIP ALMOST ALL OF THE DIALOGUE AND CUT-SCENES IF YOU WANT TO, SERIOUSLY GEARBOX TAKE A HINT! WHO THINKS ITS OKAY TO NEVER SKIP ANY DIALOGUE OR CUT-SCENES OR CHARACTER ANIMATIONS IN YOUR STUDIO??? Did you guys like actually sit through any of your dialogue more than once? Did you think it was worth listening to more than three times? Did you listen to it while pretending you would rather shoot stuff than listen to someone flap their gums? I won't be buying the next title you guys release as a shooter, even after playing all of the borderlands games throughout my life. I get the feeling you guys have forgotten about your customers that just want to shoot stuff, and I mean JUST WANT TO SHOOT STUFF, not EVER be forced into listening to things that I am physically required to stand directly next to. Even Borderlands 1 and 2 had the option to listen to people through some kind of long distance stuff if you walked away from them, you guys stopped doing that on purpose and it was one of the worst design decisions I have ever seen a developer make. This was so bad in Borderlands 3 that during my contract in The Navy I didn't have time between duty shifts to finish some of the unskippable narrative moments in that game with how long they were. _childDocuments_.review: The latest and greatest Borderlands game, with a lot of improvements.The good:Changes to weapons and spells/grenades are all excellentEnemies are more fun than earlier titlesClasses are interestingSome of the world design is the best in the seriesVariety of worldsBig name voice actorsThe most dull part of Borderlands (travelling) now has an overworld to speed it up and make it funThe bad:A lot of fights are put into small arenas that repeatI really didn't like the writing for the first half of the game - it took half the game to make a good jokeThe ugly:The OST is barely there, and completely forgettableThoughts:There is a lot to like here.The gameplay is borderlands - I am liking the new enemies, and after the first several hours the enemy variety picks up nicely.  I definitely prefer this enemy set over the enemies in the other titles.  Psychos and skags got old partway into the first game, but this new batch of fantasy themed enemies are really good and fun to kill.The map design is better than the older titles.  There is plenty of cover (including destroyable cover) and welcome changes in verticality.  I am already seeing frequently repeated maps, unfortunately.  Many of the fights in this game just warp you off the overworld map and into an arena, and I think there are only three arenas per environment - or I have been getting unlucky.  The arenas are the worst part of the overall very strong gameplay, as enemies just constantly spawn in random locations and you need to spend an uncomfortable amount of time watching your radar.  Unfortunately the arenas seem like a major focus, the game keeps sending you back to them.  There are still larger areas with full, complex, detailed maps - and I think these are the best in the series.Getting you to each of these areas is an overworld map.  This completely replaces vehicle sections or lengthy runs from the earlier Borderlands titles.  This saves so much time, is cute, and makes it easy to focus on the combat in the game.The new weapons/items are big improvements.  Replacing grenades with spells is awesome, and the increased variety and lack of a grenade limit are both very welcome.  Adding melee weapons is fantastic and overdue.  The slightly increased variety in weapons and arrow shooting weapons may be minor additions, but are still very positive ones.  I feel like I run into guns that I just love using constantly.The performance is a bit worse than 3, and though at first I did not think it looked any better, I have now seen plenty of areas that are clearly the most detailed and nicest looking areas in any Borderlands game.  Though it is not as smooth as 3, this game still runs better than the older titles do on Windows 10.  The Borderlands titles have always had stiff animations and this is not the title that changes that.The dialogue writing can really grate.  For the first half of the game it felt like every joke was "I AM LOUD AND OBNOXIOUS LOL."  It got so bad that it was a struggle to play more than an hour without turning the game off.  There is a key and noticeable moment where the writers took a drastic and welcome turn for better, starting with the first good joke in the game and making it a big one.  After that one last "I AM LOUD LOL" joke the game reins it in, and plays the rest of the game out in a bit of a different tone.  I ended up muting the game for part of the first half, but if you can stick it out to the big joke then you are good the rest of the way.The music is almost nonexistant and one of the worst and least memorable OSTs ever made.  Most of the time it does not sound like music much at all.  Disappointing, as I was surprised by how much I liked the Borderlands 3 OST.  The game got a lot better once I turned off the music, lowered dialogue, and just listened to music over it.I would recommend this game to most people.  If you like to play your games on mute while listening to music, this would be a great game for you - you can avoid the main negatives and everything else is pretty great.  If your biggest issue with Borderlands is that you are sick of killing psychos and skags, then this is the title you have been waiting for.  The default enemies are straight up more fun to fight than enemies were in the older titles (even when they are just reskins).  A lot of that is because the maps are the best they have ever been, particularly the detailed exploration areas.  A lot of that is because the combat is the best it has ever been, with spells, melee weapons, the new abilities, and the new weapon variety adding a really fantastic flow to combat.  The overworld keeps you in combat more often, and is a welcome replacement to the large empty areas in older Borderlands maps.I would not recommend this to anybody who has already found Borderlands writing to be difficult to sit through.  The first half of this game was the worst writing Borderlands has had yet, but it fortunately picks up to at least being better than 3 and TPS by the latter half.  I muted a part of it, but am glad I stuck through - the back half is the better half.Verdict:The best Borderlands game, this has some great improvements to the formula.  The writing in the first half can really stink it up, but if you stick through you will have a great time.

Was it fun?  yes, it is a typical fun borderlands game.  but the legendary drop really puts a damper on it.  Overworld is completely pointless and I wish they would have not included it.  Story was good, I am not really a fan of Tina, but the story was entertaining.  Combat encounters were also completely pointless and they should not have included them.  They could have gotten the same results in the regular levels.  Armor was also a disappointment....all you do is change the color....really lazy development. _childDocuments_.review: It's okay, I guess. It's more Borderlands, but the story just isn't really there. Same humor; same gameplay (with a few fun tweaks); same shtick overall. Just not a strong story, which has kinda been the trend across the whole series. The first couple games were chock-full-o-story. The Pre-Sequel still had an okay story, but it wasn't quite as good. BL3 had a great story, just the player had nothing to do with it. You're just watching the story happen and aren't really involved.Tiny Tina's Wonderlands has a very boring story, and it doesn't make any sense. You have two NPC's who are "in the party," but never actually show up in the game. Throughout the game, these two are talking in your ear as if they're right there next to you, doing things, but they're not. And it's a shame, because they actually seem like fun characters that we never get to meet.So Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is pretty much the epitome of what has made every Borderlands game a little worse than the one before. I can't say this enough: the humor is still there, and is still a hoot. The gameplay is roughly as-good as every previous game. But when I sit down and ask myself what I'm gonna play for the next hour, TTW is rarely the answer. It's not bad; it's just kinda bland. Again: like every Borderlands game after BL2.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a borderlands game in a long time, since borderlands 2 came out, and i have to say i really missed the borderlands charm.The game is set on the D&D universe, with a new overworld "area" where you travel from location to location unlocking new parts of the map, get some side quests and other stuff, like shrines that gives you buffs to your character stats.I enjoyed the story, it was  ok, there are some really funny side quests, and the overworld adds a new flavor to the game.The part where this game really shines is on the weapons department, there are tons of fun crazy weapons to try out and have fun with, they all feel great to shoot and just feel nice use.I didn't really like the amount of loot you get , it's just too much, usually just trash loot you are not going to use, you can still it sell it on the vending machines sure, but i still think it would have been nice to get less trash loot and more good loot.Overall i enjoyed my time with tiny tinas, a good story with some funny side quests, nice weapons and good character customization made for a really enjoyable game. If you played other borderlands games and enjoyed them, you really need to give this one a try, you're going to like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan of Borderlands and dungeons and dragons? Do you like weird games? Well you'll probably like this one. Overall if you've played other Borderlands games, you know basically what to expect. Run around, do missions, shoot baddies, get loot, upgrade your character, rinse and repeat. I'm not sure this is the "best" Borderlands game, but I think it's one of the best. The biggest jump off is the story is really not that serious at all compared to the other games. This is a much more off the walls, funny and weird game. I think however that's  the charm. It's fun, loose and a little weird but all in a good way.I guess the only real complaints I would have is it feels like some previous characters are missing. No Moxie, Zedd, Marcus, or Sir Hammerlock. Claptrap , Mr. Torgue, and Brick make a few appearances. But overall the cast feels a bit thin.I guess the whole overworld system works due to the game but much prefer the whole open world driving we have in other games.Overall, great game. If you've played any of the previous games I would highly recommend checking this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: Bad version of Borderlands. Slow, clunky, poorly balanced, full of bullet sponge enemies, and swarms so large you can't even figure out what's going on. Enemies will launch things at you from across the map, track you perfectly, so that you're just constantly taking damage. Made the mistake of playing the Brr-zerker, which is designed around frost. Problem is, you won't be able to do any damage unless you have some sort of frost weapon in play at all times, to the point a level 8 pistol still massively outdamaged non-frost weapons until level 18. It's a melee based class and going into melee range is just asking to be downed. Barrels EVERYWHERE mean the use of the Feral pounce ability WILL kill you. You'll set off a barrel near an enemy using the ability and you'll die. Three quarters of the game takes place in samey arenas. _childDocuments_.review: For a brief overview, if you have played any of the Borderlands series you will know what to expect game play wise, and to some extent theme wise if you know Tina.With that said, I wouldn't go much beyond that for an explanation if you have prior exposure. Beyond adding melee weapons, rings, and spell slots (grenades), everything else is consistent for better or worse. The theme is the major sell here, and with a brief understand of Dungeon and Dragons, it does suit it well. There are no vehicles this time around, but rather a over world to which the character moves across with the appearance of a board game. While this matches the theme, it doesn't change anything beyond aesthetic as the story progresses appropriately and with guidance.When it comes down to much of the game, because it is D&D themed, most is just designed to match. Instead of characters, you have slight customization with a blank slate character, and classes to choose from. With that said, while the plot works around the "insert character here" theme, the engagement and characters are not as built.Also to be noted, that classes have skill tree, and while you can "dual class" to unlock more build ideas and potentially more pets, it does feel a tad underwhelming. Further playing into this was items that almost felt unnecessary (rings)/melee weapons. These just played into the idea for more things to grind for, but no substance. And while this is a "fantasy" world, much of the enemies were re-skinned, and the same guns/mechanics existed. While understanding borderlands was themed around guns and the combinations therein, the new spell introduction which replaced grenades, seemed more appropriate and innovative. The environments had the sword and shield, bows, etc, but at most the character had a "crossbow" machine gun. The game would have benefited greater if the emphasis was greater with melee weapons, and removed guns, outside of musket esque items, and replaced them with bow variations, slingshots, etc. This is of course my opinion, but does shine on some greater things the game has.The environments are far more diverse and engaging than in the past, and the universe and theme aloud for it. As stated before, while the universe built was great, some slight alterations that could have been designed would have greatly made the game more engaging or unique.In simplicity, if you ever wanted to shoot guns at dragons, to then loot more guns this is your game. Outside the realm of that, I would recommend other titles in Borderlands if you haven't already played before this.With that in mind, this is a spin off and met the expectations to that extent.

_childDocuments_.review: First couple of hours was fun enough, but then!Gameplay: is surprisingly boring.. combat feels bad and there are no good weapons in the game.I played through the game 4 times, and there was always 20-30 levels between finding a small weapon upgrade, which is bad because all enemies are super-powered sponges even on the lowest difficulty (which gives you 15% increased damage).That, mixed with most weapons projectiles having travel time and all enemies constantly dodging(with DarkSouls damage immunity) makes for a bad game in itself in a ''shooter''.But then there's the story.. Which is also super boring and dragged out.. The main ''humour'' in the game is npc's talking for way too long while you just have to wait for them to finish so you can continue.. There are no jokes.Endgame content: Non-existent currently.There is the Chaos Chamber, which allows you to go through about 30 Chaos Trials, to unlock higher Chaos levels. (difficulty/Mayhem levels without modifiers)Said trials are several small levels, small arenas/dungeons filled with traps and enemies that spawn way to slowly and in too few numbers. (one reason combat is really boring)And then there are normal Chaos runs, which are the same but serve no purpose other than boring, unrewarding grinding.Chaos Boss runs which is self-explanatory, except for having to do a Obelisk fight in between ''all'' 2-3 bosses in a RunSo nothing interesting or rewarding after unlocking Difficulty levels which you have to do WITH EACH CHARACTER.. It's insanely boring, even the first time going through that.Farming for gear: Gigantic waste of time and you will not succeed.I spent a couple of days farming a boss at max Chaos level (currently 50) without seeing even one a of the item i was looking for with even one mod on it i was looking for.All items can roll with so many different random things on it, it is literally impossible to find any kind of ''perfect'' gear... So, i tried farming the same boss, but with cheats to increase drop rates a whole lot.. after a couple more days, i got 1 of said item with the right class bonuses and mostly correct bonus skill points, only to find out 30 minutes later the Legendary power was wrong, so even that can be random on some legendaries.This game is in desperate need of a Smart-Loot system, like in Borderlands 3Been farming for 15 more hours now, still haven't found anything close to a good roll on any needed gear.Always only 1 out of 5 things that are good, the rest is useless stuff for other classes, or just plain useless bonusses.So i guess in short, if you are looking for a good Borderlands game, this ain't it.This game is as clunky/bad as the original Borderlands 1, just without redeeming qualities.I hope the game gets a lot of changes and polishing, as i can see the game being good, but it's just not..

_childDocuments_.review: There's both a lot and, well, not a lot that can be said about this game. The introduction of a proper Character Creation a la DnD style unlike other Borderlands was refreshing, and a myriad of classes above one of Gearboxes favorite numbers (4), left me sitting there for a good moment making the right choice. I quickly learned however that this doesn't matter in the slightest when you challenge the World of Might and Magic with a Trench Gun and a Remington 700. though from the small amount of time I've played, I feel as though there isn't much to gleam out of this game aside from its likeness to the beloved brain-dead shooter series, and the fact that it has Tiny Tina in it. All in all, It isn't the best, but it isn't the worst either. If you do play it, you might as well set it to the highest difficulty by default if you want any semblance of fun, or a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Tiny Tina's Wonderlands is a spin-off of the Borderlands series. The last game i played from this franchise was actually Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep DLC. Wonderlands brings players back by offering an alternate version of D&D called Bunkers and Badasses. Right from the start, I noticed a lot of nice references to games like The Witcher 3, Path of Exile, Curse of Monkey Island, and of course the older Borderlands games.The story is really nice. Your main quest is to defeat the evil Dragon Lord and save the fantasy world rules by a unicorn called buttstalion, the game is a continuation of the 2013 DLC. I won't spoil much but it was interesting enough to keep me wondering how it's going to end. The game also has some really high quality side quests that blend seamlessly with the main storylines. The humor and dialogue were lighthearted and kept me engaged without any character wearing out their welcome. In fact, I actually wanted to see more of Tiny Tina. Gameplay-wise, the fantasy setting brings welcome new ideas like spellcasting instead of just throwing grenades. Every spell type gives you unique options to experiment with. The weapons felt great and had top notch animations, overall the combat was thrilling and stands out as some of the most fun I've had in recent FPS titles. The overworld was a welcome addition as it really provides a spice of variety when taking a break from chaotic dungeon runs. I can only imagine how much better the experience would be playing coop with a friend.Last but not least, on the visual and performance side, the game looks great. It has that timeless Borderlands art style that is sure to age gracefully. The game didn't have any FPS drops although I had to cap the fps at 50

If we ever find ourselves company across the vast cosmos and we have to explain ourselves to any potential alien entity, this is the perfect game to show them how we, as humans, work. Not because this game itself is perfect, oh no, but because it encapsulates one of the most unique traits of any human: Liking stupid ♥♥♥♥ that doesn´t make any sense.Imagine you´re an alien with several millenia of evolution ahead of us, only viewing the universe around you with cold, hard logic. Then a human comes along and draws a penis on one of your planets, thinks it´s the most hilarious ♥♥♥♥ ever and flips off, enjoying the time of his life. This is Tiny Tinas Wonderlands.What probably started out as a cancelled Borderlands 3 DLC has now been made into its own game. And since that was the only DLC people liked, Gearbox obviously had to double down on that. So yeah, this is basically Borderlands, but DnD. Depending on who you ask this is either the best thing ever or the most lethal cringe in the history of mankind. And if you want to know how i see this, i can safely say: Yes.Since this game was written by the same people who would play a Loxodon Gunslinger in Curse of Strahd, i´m not gonna take this story anymore serious than an interim disposal. I mean, what did you expect?The Kingdom of Buttstallion (a joke from BL2 that someone found WAY too hilarious...) is under attack by the fearsome Dragon Lord. Yeah. This is the name of the antagonist. Any german reading this is probably already forming the joke of the century in their head but since i watched HBO´s Chernobyl, i learned to avoid toxic hazards so i´m not gonna elaborate on that any further. Then again i gave this game a thumbs up... The mechanisms of my inner mind are enigma.Anyway, that´s the story. Evil Lord does stuff, you undo stuff. Violently. That´s right baby we got guns in a fantasy game so you know what´s coming now!While everyone tries desperately to roleplay the knights of the round millenials, you, the player, are busy multiclassing warcrimes. _childDocuments_.review: Upon starting a new game, you will have the option to choose the game’s difficulty. You have three options to choose from: Relaxed, Balanced and Intense. Relaxed allows you to play the game a little more chilled, where players deal 15% more damage and enemies deal 15% less damage. Balanced is the difficulty on which the game was intended to be played, and on the Intense difficulty, players deal 15% less damage, enemies deal 15% more damage and you’ll gain 15% bonus in Gold and Moon Orb drops.  After you’ve decided how brave you are, you then have to create a character. First you choose a Class. There are six classes in total: Stabbomancer, Clawbringer, Spellshot, Graveborn, Spore Warden and Brr-Zerker. Each class has its own combat style and focus: the Stabbomancer is a sneaky murderer and has a focus on Critical Hits, the Clawbringers is a Wyvern tamer with a focus on Fire and Lightning Damage, the Spellshot is a magic-user whose focus is on constantly Casting Spells, and the Graveborn is a soul-trapper with a focus on dealing damage in exchange for Health.  Spore Warden is a fungal friend with a focus on Ranged Damage and the Brr-Zerker is an angry smasher with a focus on Frost Damage. Each class also has its own Class Feat and two Action Skills, all of which will help you to decide which class to choose.  After choosing your Class you can customise the look of your character or choose one of the presets. Here you can customise your character’s Body and Personality, Facial Features, and Face and Armour Decoration. There are quite a few customise options for you to create your perfect character. Next you choose your character’s Twist of Fate (their background); this will have an effect on the stats of your character. There are five backgrounds to choose from: the Village Idiot, Raised by Elves, Failed Monk, Recovering Inventory Hoarder and Rogue Alchemist. Once you’ve chosen your background, your next job is to assign some Hero Points to your character’s stats. The points can be applied to either Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, Constitution and Attunement. Once you’ve created your character, there’s a small intro with Tina, Frette and Valentine who will help you play through the game of Bunkers & Badasses, after which you’ll head off to the Snoring Valley - Glade of Helpful Tutorials. Here you will go over some basics of the game with Tina playing as Bunker Master throughout the game. She has created the Wonderland and you play as the Fatemaker, it’s up to you to explore, loot and save Tina’s Wonderland from the Dragon Lord who will soon rise again. Defeating the Dragon Lord is the main objective of the game, and the story will unfold as you unlock new campaign quests. There are also plenty of side quests; with each campaign quest you will have a number of objectives to complete. The campaign is divided into chapters and at the end of each chapter you’ll find yourself up against the final boss. Defeating them will then allow you to move on to the next chapter and open up a new location, maybe in the Overworld. After leaving the Valley of Tutorials you find yourself in the Overworld, which is the world map. Here you can move through the Wonderland visiting new locations and their surroundings, find quests, activities and encounters, some of whom may be dangerous although a quick left right can deal with them with ease when they appear, so beware of the tall grass, you never know who’s hiding in it.  Not all locations will be available for you to visit right away, they may need unlocking through either the story or from the collection of certain items. There are shrines which have a number of missing pieces; you’ll have to collect all of the missing pieces to make the shrine whole again. After completing the shrine, you will then receive some sort of reward from the god of the shrine.  You will also find Camp Sites and Dungeons along with the Shrines, and upon entering them you’ll set off an Encounter. This will pit you against whatever creatures reside in the location you’ve just entered. Defeating them will end the encounter, however, you will have multiple rounds of encounters before you finally complete the location. After each round of encounters a chest will appear with some nice goodies for you. After the last round of encounters, you will gain the reward for completing that location, such as a missing piece of a shrine or some other item required elsewhere. When you encounter the enemy throughout the game combat will commence. This will consist of you using a variety of weapons, different types of bladed weapons, hammers, pistol, rifles, grenade launchers and snipers. All weapons will have different stats and some will have added abilities and may also have the added status effects, such as poison, fire, ice and lightning. The weapons come in different qualities: common, uncommon, rare and legendary, which can be easily identified by their different colours. You’ll also have any abilities your character has from their class to help you spank some botty.  Scattered all over the place are chests, safes, wooden boxes and barrels. When opened or smashed, in the case of the wooden boxes and barrels, you may find some gold, ammo, weapons, gear or health vials. Keep your mince pies open for D20 dice, as finding one of these and opening them will also give you some items. Unlike chests, however, they could be hidden or in a place which might be out of reach at first sight. There are other things to find, such as Marbles, Poem Pages, Rune Switches and Obelisks where you can gain some sort of reward. You can also equip your character with new gear: Armour, Ward, Rings, Amulets. Like the weapons, they all come in different rarities, abilities and effects. You may also come across some small satchels mixed in with some of the other items, which will unlock some customisation in the Quick-Change booths. This will allow you to customise your character’s look with more options than those available at the beginning of the game. If you come across any that you already have, then you can sell them for a nice bit of profit to top up your coffers. You can sell any of the gear, weapons or items you find on your journey at some vending machines scattered around in various locations. You’ll be able to buy new equipment and weapons from these vending machines; there’s always a special item on offer so you might want a to keep butchers on what’s regularly available. Although I do find that they can be expensive and they don’t really give me much of a boost over my favourite stuff that I collected from enemies, chests and anywhere else I’m find them. One thing I would say, though, is if you do buy something for, say 50,000 gold, then don’t walk away and come back later trying to recuperate anything like that back because it’s not going to happen.  Positives  + Fantastic graphics + Multiple character classes + Cross-play platforms + Online Co-op and Lan + Crazy characters and story + Has achievements Negatives  - Some stuttering - No cards currently It’s your job as the Fatemaker to go on an adventure, loot dungeons, travel through magical lands, and more importantly, deal with the evil Dragon Lord who’s just been released from his slumber. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - 8/10 - Keeps the gameplay improvements from Borderlands 3 and combines them with a lukewarm story that won't piss you off, but also won't wow you. Not bad. Enjoyable, but not a must play.And now, the longer review you will almost certainly not read...GAMEPLAYJust like Borderlands 3, the actual gameplay in Wonderlands is fantastic. It features all the QOL improvements of the previous title (like damage scaling so that you can play with anyone at any level, sliding, and not getting stuck on every single little piece of map geometry) and combines them with some new D&D-esque mechanics and the chaos chamber, which operates like a randomized dungeon arena.STORYTELLING, CHARACTERS, AND HUMORThe story is an improvement over Borderlands 3, but this is very much not a game to be recommended for its story. Most of the time it feels very lukewarm, not pissing me off, but not wowing me either. Exceptions are any quest involving Mr. Torgue or Claptrap , the Pirate Words scroll, seducing the door, and Peasant-Ass Peasant. Like almost every Borderlands game, the jokes are very much hit or miss. The characters are often referential jokes, and they are also very much hit or miss.GLITCHES AND BUGSHad a bug where the game would freeze for about 20 seconds once after launching and spawning in a map, but that may have been due to my graphics settings. I never did look into trying to fix it. Mildly annoying more than anything. Also had the game crash twice without error message and without warning. Once in the middle of a chaos chamber I had reached the final boss of. Kept my gold and everything I got up to that point, but I was still pissed because I wanted to finish the chamber. That seems to have been due to graphics settings because I lowered them and didn't have a crashing issue after that.SEASON PASSI'm not buying it at this time. It seems overpriced for what you get.OVERALLI did enjoy the game and I do recommend it, especially if there's a sale. I feel like I got my money's worth. Gameplay is great. Story is mostly eh, but it didn't piss me off.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, sad days have come. Borderlands finally left me damn BORED. Holy cow this game has no substance what so ever, about half way through I simply stopped aiming as I had lost all motivation to continue playing this game, and somehow ti worked amazingly. The only game I've ever played where I never died, even when I stopped caring about how I play so why not dive into the pros firstGuns: As always it's an even split down the middle of worthless garbage that I'll never use for more than a second and guns that kick so hard that they blow everything in front of them away. I found the casual "Space AK" half way through the game and never picked up a better weapon. I probably found thousands of better guns but the Space AK worked so well there was no need. I used to test out many different weapons in the older games but it felt like there was no point nearing the middle. Loot: Astronomically to high, unnecessary garbage flows form every enemies veins at such a rate Oil barons would cry. Far to much is provided and 90% won't even get a second glance as the amount of common and uncommon drops are so high you know it's just garbage after 2 hours. You will be bombarded by endless worthless garbage that you'll never shoot, never pick up, and probably never even look at. Through my whole play through I got 3 legendary items, 2 being shields and one being the Space AK so you know how that went. A.I.: Brain dead, it feels like no one has any level of self preservation. Most will stand out in the open like an idiot and spray rounds your way or just rush you without care. No one will ever out play you or put you on the back foot as they either don't do enough damage to matter or stand out in the open for easy pickings. Like shooting fish drying up in the sandGraphics: Graphically the game looks good holding the same aesthetics of older borderlands games. Not to different from the previous so I don't think much advancement has been invested but doesn't detract from the games style so overall OK if not washed out at worse segments. Story: Thankfully I never spoil games but there isn't really anything here to spoil. Why? Cause I was half asleep playing it past the half way mark. So soul suckling mediocre that there's nothing to talk about, no deep messages to talk about, no imprint left in my mind, leaving nothing to be thought about so the story was simply forgotten. I will say I remember playing repeat quests far to many times as most are fetch quests or grab 3-6 of this item. There's collectibles too but they feel pretty lazy and don't add much to the world so you can skip them if you really don't careSingle player: You'd be better off spending time learning about desert survival or Bigfoot than playing this alone. At least you may find something weird or interesting there instead than feel completely lost and empty roaming aroundMultiplayer: Still the best part, don't play this game alone. Playing alone feels like I'm being forced to farm gold in WOW at a Chinese super prison so try avoid that. If you don't have friends, don't buy this game you will not have a great time. Multiplayer however feels fine, not because of the game play but the fact your gaming with someone else. Kyle finally gave up on this one and never finished the game which is pretty harsh, but understandable as this game blooooooooooowsDND: As a lover of a little DND from time to time this game has some elements there. Table banter and dice rolling exist but obviously your playing a looter shooter so it doesn't play a massive part into the game. You may think that's weird as the whole story surrounds the fact that your playing DND but as stated before, what story? The forgotten slop they threw in my face that left no impression? Sure man, it exists but don't buy it based on that as you'll end up pretty dissapointed. Comparison: To compare it to the older games, I'd rather play all but the tell tale games over this which should say something. Borderlands 3 was already on the downside of enjoyment so cracking open a new can of Sulfuric acid to drink really dissapointed me. In comparison I remember multiple fun sections from the first and second game with some minor sections in the presequal and the third game, but there just wasn't one here. Maybe the final battle but it felt so meaningless, like you accomplished so little of consequence along your way. Possibly the most mid DND session I've ever been apart of So how do I feel? Empty, can't believe how little there is not only to talk about but the little I even remember. Kyle completely checked out 8 hours in and though I really tried to enjoy this as I loved older Borderlands games but even I lost steam about 17 hours in. The next 23 hours were filled with half conscious me doing my taxes on one browser while finishing this garbage in the other hand. I stopped aiming or even recording around hour 20 as the care and investment swapped to me finishing my tax write offs and scholarships to college. To benefit this game though, It was so boring I ended up saving $700 on college as I was putting more effort into that than playing this game. If you want a score 2/10, would not recommend. _childDocuments_.review: You should not buy this game, nor its DLCs, unless it is on a massive sale. I payed 16 dollars for ALL of it in a bundle. like 3, I cant say its a bad game, it just is not a grate game. I believe the term would be "cringe" content leeking into most of the aspects of the dialog and detracting from the story or braking immersion of the setting. In some cases this is intended as it is meant to be people playing a DnD battle board, and for the most part these are nice nods to that, however specific NPCs tend to talk in a trying -to-be-witty way that often interjects unneeded banter in a diffrent tone of voice. You do however have a lot of control over your charictor both stats and visually, makeing this feel like a standalone game rather then an offshoot of the main game. It also uses a brighter color pallet and re uses a bunch of the more whimsical assets from the other games to make the world. I also have a strange fondness for the style they took with the over world, both due to its toy like appearance and the random junk imagined as obsticals, such as a cheese curl that fell on to the board. random encounters are also done in little areas that lack loot sources in them, and have a guaranteed chest at the end. these do get a little repetitive, but you can skip some of them. the curated maps that the story takes place in are more akin to a borderlands map, but bosses wont re-spawn until you move the story to a new zone rather then just reloading the area. Guns are themed for the setting with new named manufacturers that mimic the ones from the main game. some are just strait up guns, but a lot of them incorporate magic aspects. grenades have been replaced with spells, and slag has been replaced with dark magic that heals you when it deals damage. otherwise the other elements are present and do the same things youd expect. loot rarity is tied both to level and loot dice- randomly hidden around the map, they give you some loot when activated and increases your luck with each one fond. some are hidden rather well, others are in the open, but they all produce a sparkle noise when you are close to them. I think this sort of mechanic is pretty cool, and helps you increase your loot rarity by exploration. A few of the borderlands NPCs are also missing, but many have been reused in some way. apparently due to being rated T rather then M, moxxie was cut entirely but is mentioned. Tina is also meant to be a kid at this point in the timeline so all references to drinking are soda based and the jokes they make for it are kinda annoying. Borderlands as a series has been slowly eroding in quality, usually due to poor business practice decisions. it tends to focus on injection culturally relevant memes for the time the game was made, but they are likely old by the time it comes out and causes the games to age faster then intended.  This game has some of that, but most of the references Iv noticed are much older, either from DnD or older fantasy.to wrap this up, this is a borderlands adjacent game. if you like DnD and borderlands, you might like it. It is better then the movie at lest!Edit: I am not sure how far in I am, but I assume its about half way if not more. I think my review above stands pretty well but I do have to say that there are moments in the game that are rather unexpected and not the twist I assumed was going to happen so I will give it points for that. I have however noticed that loot feels very simile to one another. lookng up a database of unique / named loot this game has about 93 guns/swords. borderlands 1 had 105, B2 had  141, BTPS had 103, and B3 had 331, so its about on par with the loot availability of the first game or the per sequel, at lest as far as red text guns go. This game is also much smaller, without expansive DLCs, and uses a different loot drop mechanic that may make it harder to find some of the guns until a fair bit later. there are a large number of gun parts and combinations, it just kinda all blends together at some point. The game itself is semi linear but you have the option to roam around the board and find side quest map areas allowing for some deviation. I have been trying to complete all quests that I come across and explore and much as I can, so I think my level is higher then intended for the part of the story im in. I find that unlike a lot of other games out there, im able to say "that is enough for now" after getting through a few quests, translating to probably an hour or so per map area.

_childDocuments_.review: NB: I've been increasingly disappointed with Borderlands games since the first one, so if you generally enjoy them, you might have a completely different perspective.I don't think anyone would be confused by the fact that this game isn't called "Borderlands", but just to be extra sure: yes, this is most definitely a Borderlands game. It has the same basic gameplay, the same structure, the same kind of story, the same brand of humor. The only real differences are that the player characters aren't *actual* characters anymore and are instead fully customizable, that there are no vehicles, the grenades are replaced with magic spells, and there are now different melee weapons and "armor". Otherwise it's pretty much the same game.It doesn't even look all that different visually: despite being fantasy, it still has the same not-quite-cel-shaded appearance, you mostly pick up guns that look almost exactly the same as in other entries to the series (except some of them now have bow parts), and you fight some very familiar-looking and behaving enemies (though in the interest of fairness there are some fresh-ish additions).Since I doubt that a lot of people would expect anything from the story of this game, I'll be brief: the story is a mess. The writers try to go for something meta with the villain, include banter between both the characters in the Borderlands setting and the in-universe Wonderlands setting, and have some fun in the process with the D&D-type setting, but stumbled on pretty much every step to the point that even stuff that you'd think would be basic is unclear. If the "Newbie", i.e., your character, is playing with two other people, where are their characters in-game? Why do they keep talking as if they have any impact on the events? And if they do, why would the villain never address them? What was the villain's plan, anyway? None of this would really be clear by the end.One more thing that is related to writing before I move on: the jokes in this entry make my soul shrivel and die every time. They're the most shallow, often hopelessly outdated kind of referential humor, only sometimes connected with the premise of the game. It often feels like a Friedberg and Seltzer type of movie, not helped by the fact that at least one of the "jokes" in this game actually did appear in the infamous Epic Movie (2007).In terms of gameplay, at least at the time of this review the game feels incredibly unpolished, even compared to the other games in the series. The maps can be hard to navigate (some are three-dimensional, and one has portals to complicate matters even further) and have a lot of invisible walls and odd level geometry, there are some pretty serious buggy interactions between items and skills, etc.Perhaps the biggest issue with the gameplay, however, is the wildly inconsistent difficulty. With the exception of one particular boss, every boss fight in this game was a complete joke, some not even managing to finish their introductory monologue before getting killed. Even the final boss barely lasted two minutes. Meanwhile, battles with normal enemies can be anything from a breeze to a chore to a complete nightmare depending solely on which types of enemies you're fighting and seemingly no other reason.Most of all, this game feels lazy. The credit sequence starts with an apology that the development was difficult due to COVID, but I don't think that can explain every problem this game ended up having and every choice that was made. About half the gameplay is done in the form of "Encounters", fights with enemies spawning out of thin air with no real explanation or reason in small combat arenas (that are repeated for each of the four main areas of the overworld map). The DLC follows the same structure, but even the main game isn't all that much better: one tiny, but illustrative example is that the levels are full of impassable black voids out of which the enemies arrive, when the previous games in the series usually at least had put enough care into this to put doors or something like that there. And this kind of laziness is felt throughout everything.All in all, I would only recommend this if you're really, REALLY jonesing for more Borderlands, no matter the quality.

Short campaign they try to make longer by increasing the level of of each subsequent mission by 4-5, making you want to level from the (mostly) poorly designed side quest, just to experience the story. The story missions feel like side quests, and the side quests feel like content that shoulda been scrapped. A large chunk of the game is just horde mode they're calling "random encounters". If you walk near tall grass you might spawn an enemy who will take you to 2 waves of horde mode if you don't melee them. Most of the side quest force you to do a horde too. I found myself rushing the story missions hoping the next mission/area would be something I liked... That never came XD Final bosses wasn't even fun. And the character creator replacing the vault hunters you normally would select. This allows you to chose a class (a single skill tree). An hour or 2 of gameplay will net you a second skill tree you can select from the remaining classes. This system was great until you realize max level is 40 and you only get 2 skill trees. Every vault hunter got at least 3. Even borderlands 1 started with a level cap of 50 and the pre-sequal was 60.How does end game look? It's literally just horde mode or side quest you missed... The ability to redo the story missions or even just fight older bosses is removed. Oh, and there's 3 DLC bosses you can pay 10 bucks each to fight. Making this a $90 unfinished short game. _childDocuments_.review: + My personal favorite iteration on the tried and true Borderlands gameplay loop, featuring a robust character creator, a more involved melee combat system, loads of spells instead of grenades that are easier to consistently use, vividly different environments that are actually interesting to explore, and a cute world board system. + While already mentioned, character creator is still the star of the show, with loads of different choices to unlock for people willing to pursue all of them. You can use asymmetrical face customization for certain features, as well as pitch shifting voices to really express who you are. There's even a slider overdrive option that allows you to get crazier with your choices -- but, some of them aren't as good as they could be. More on that later.+ Collectibles are interesting and have real practical use, with dice that increase your luck and story-laced poems, marbles, and puzzles that often reward new cosmetic choices.+ Some quest design is some of the best in Borderlands history in my opinion. I really enjoyed three quests that involved breaking a goblin's heart (I didn't do it), serving an imp to find a new host, and taking a sharkdog on a walk who sounds absolutely adorable.+ Chaos Chamber and random encounters are a neat system that feels very rogue-lite, and I've enjoyed playing around with them quite a bit, even if some of the boss fights are awful. The reward structure is much better, as well, allowing you to focus on a particular reward if you so choose -- a HUGE step up from older games.+ The weapon enhancement system is so good, it's vastly overlooked and underappreciated. I don't recall how closely it resembles the one in Borderlands 3, but being able to give an enhancement to your weapon if you got a good roll is fantastic.- From what I've seen, the DLC in Wonderlands is some of the worst the game has ever prepared (as of 7/25/2022). Very minimal content that can be completed quickly, with none of the fun story or new world design that the older games brought forward (especially BL3). I looked into it extensively because I really wanted more game to play, but there's no getting around it -- as much as I like the random encounter and chaos chamber systems, I'm not willing to spend $30 on minimal changes to its formula that can be completed very quickly.- Borderlands did it again - interesting melee builds, and yet there are several annoying boss designs who decimate melee builds with no solution. The worst offender is Dr'yl, who has a poison pit surrounding him -- but he's not the only one.- Another "did it again" -- gun damage turning into nothing at higher ranks. This was a huge problem in Borderlands 3, where upper difficulty's health expectations get so high that all purples are useless and only a handful of overpowered exotics are viable. It gets to the point that, almost always, no purple weapon will be a worthwhile or exciting drop. There are some cool ass exotic weapons, as well, that are completely useless.- [Customization Gripes 1/3] Slider Overdrive is disappointing in a lot of key areas -- particularly when it comes to size. I wanted to make an imp, because A. I knew Borderlands 2 had a shorter character, and B. I knew imps and goblins were in the game and I wanted to be one of those, like how some tabletop RPGs have them as playable races. Unfortunately, there are several sliders that have hard limits for some reason, which was a huge buzzkill.- [Customization Gripes 2/3] The amount of hats/hair is a bit disappointing, truth be told. No isolated horns, no head conversions into, say, skeletons, or goblins, or snakes or... any of the beast races. I'm hoping this is rectified with future DLC.- [Customization Gripes 3/3]  It absolutely sucks mega ass that your clothing aesthetic is tied to your armor slot. So often I'll get a great armor slot drop that has the ugly basic armor visual style and I cannot use it. - I wish there was MORE investment in Tiny Tina's world. Some of the guns and spells are super unique and incredible to use, with unique modifications that at least tried to make them look more fantasy. Others were lazy copy-and-paste recreations of BL3 guns, without any attempt to modify the design into something more fantasy. If they do a sequel, I'd love to see way more time put into making the entire game feel like the RPG it could very well be.- Writing is so... weird. It's not quite as bad as BL3 base game, but it often devolves into a lot of talking that is uninteresting, and the main villain isn't that compelling (although, Will Arnett was a great choice, love him as the voice).I may have a lot of gripes with the game, but Borderlands is Borderlands. Over 45 hours later and, sure, I have my issues, but I cannot deny that I enjoyed Tiny Tina a LOT. I wouldn't be at all sad if the next game was a sequel to Tiny Tina over another Borderlands.If you love Borderlands, you'll at least like Tiny Tina's Wonderlands, but more than likely you'll love it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time enjoyer of the Borderlands franchise, I found TTWL to be probably the MOST FUN of the Borderlands releases. Where Borderlands 1 was a bit too serious, 2 hit a great stride as far as comedy, the franchise really fell off with 3. The extremely heavy-handed "girl power" vibe of BL3 and the completely unrelateable humor of the Pre-Sequal seemed to leave the design room during this game. Instead, you get a semi-funny and all around fun Borderlands game. Without spoiling too much, you're playing a D&D-themed Borderlands game with extremely flexible classes, fun combinations of how you do damage, and a complete overhaul of the grenade-system in the game to be 'spells' which add a TON of variety to the gameplay. The only REAL disapointment to me in this game is its DLC, as the base game was a decent length with a fun roguelike addition. I was sort of hoping they would add some raid bosses, or large multiplayer, or something that's been in previous iterations, as I just enjoyed this game so much more due to it not ramming obnoxious heroes/villains down my throat. Still, if you can get this game on sale, it's a great game to play, either solo or with a group of (4 max) friends. Definitely the best Borderlands release since 2.

name: CONSCRIPT
detailed_description: Deluxe & Officer Editions Trench Raider Pack Battle through the trenches with 3 additional uniforms to choose from in the Trench Raider Pack, containing: • Elite Trench Raider • Pilot • English Tommy About the Game ADD TO YOUR WISHLIST! CONSCRIPT is a top-down survival horror game inspired by classics of the genre - set in 1916 during the Great War. CONSCRIPT will blend all the punishing mechanics of older horror games into a cohesive, tense, and unique experience. In CONSCRIPT, you play as a French soldier searching for his missing-in-action brother during the Battle of Verdun. Will you be able to search twisted trenches, navigate overrun forts, and cross no-mans-land to find him, and ensure a home goes unbroken? Experience classic and methodical survival horror gameplay in a unique historical setting: the Battle of Verdun. Highly re-playable with various difficulty settings, multiple endings, unlockable costumes and bonus weapons. Fend off enemy soldiers and combatants with a variety of WW1 melee weapons and firearms. Survive in an intense, harrowing atmosphere boosted by a unique pixel art aesthetic and oppressive sound design. Navigate intricate level design that promotes item management and route planning, whilst solving complex environmental puzzles. Explore distinct WW1 themed areas that intertwine and overlap.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first completed this game after about 12 hours, I discovered that the "true ending" required a second playthrough. I was disappointed because while I really enjoyed the game, I didn't think I wanted to play it all again, so I just watched the ending on youtube and went to bed.And I could not stop thinking about this damn game.Long story short, 50 hours later (I occasionally left it running while paused) I have played it through I think 7 times and gotten all of the achievements, which I very rarely do. In fact I so rarely get invested enough to dedicate the time to mastering games that I've only done it one other time, which was Amnesia the Bunker, amusingly a similar game in many ways (damn rats!). Mastering both of these games is something I'm quite proud of.I'm not going to pretend this game is perfect, and I recommend you read some other reviews if it's important to you to have plenty of details before you buy or not, just keep in mind that the dev put out a couple significant patches after release that helped with most of the significant complaints. Though I'd argue the 94% positive rating speaks for itself. I personally think the first chapter is a poor introduction to what the majority of the game actually is, so just stick with it until chapter 2 and see how you like it from there. The combat gameplay especially is much more fun in the middle and end of the playthrough.I've bought both the cosmetic pack and the soundtrack (and also wrote my first real review lol) because I would love to see the game be expanded and I want to support the dev (that's right, (mostly) just one developer!) because he's done something great, imho.PS: If you are also a huge WW1 buff the historical themeing of this game is obviously cool and the environment and story are very authentic in their own pixellated way lol.

_childDocuments_.review: I was highly anticipating Conscript and it didnt disappoint. This is a hardcore, harrowing and relentlessly bleak game set in the absolute meat grinder of Verdun, where classic survival horror game tropes get masterfully assimilated into a historical setting. By far the most unique aspect of the game is the total lack of supernatural elements, nearly everything you see in this game has this amazing air of plausibility and authenticity that really amps up the grim atmosphere that hangs around every minute of the game. While the game has some welcoming options assisting players who are not as valiant, the game absolutely shines when saves are limited, every injury hurts, and you're resource starved. This makes the stop and pop shooting, the very risky but punchy melee, and those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rats to be as undesirable as possible. Maybe I'm just a masochist, but I really enjoyed how brutal and clunky the combat was, even if I can understand someone being very turned off by how slow and difficult it is.That all said, I have two grievances - the rats can be a bit too punishing (there will be a small nerf soon) and I find the amazing visual style can at times hide essential paths needed to progress due to the murkiness, which got me lost a few times. However, if the idea of surviving the trench warfare sounds interesting to you, or you just want a great game to play, pick this one up right now. Few horror titles have been as unique and engrossing as this one in recent memory.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: This game was carried by its style, not its gameplay.Would've benefited from less time spent running around due to maze like levels, item running due to restricted inventory space and having enemies die from fewer hits but be otherwise more dangerous. Once you progress opening up new paths in the levels, gain more inventory space and upgrade your guns to require less kiting in battles, things improve, atmosphere shines through and the game is at its best. I don't get why "inventory management" is so romanticized in these games. I've never heard anyone say "Silent Hill would've been so much better with restricted inventory". You can withdraw from almost any situation, so any poor choices of what to carry it will only result in backtracking time, which there is already so much of. It doesn't create impactful choices, only chores. Being able to infinitely reset each encounter by running out of the room and back in nearly kills all of the tension. Gripping and atmospheric to the bitter end despite its shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Scratches both the WW1 and old school survival horror itches! Im actually stunned that a first time developer made this, whatever you were doing before Jordan, ignore that and focus on game development. This is your callingElements that make it stand out from other attempts in the SH genre are things such as its level design and balancing. Both are pretty much spot on, aside from one or two long moments, I felt like it had been meticulously thought out and therefore was worth my time (Which is the biggest commodity these days). Take some of the later SIlent Hill or Resi games and they lost their way on this so its very refreshing to be able to see it again.One other really niche point I liked was that you still interacted with other french soldiers throughout the game, rather than being all by yourself during the "aftermath" of the event like in Resi 2.Also being a fellow WW1 nerd I appreciated all the factual touches and locations. Fort Vaux gave me Battlefield 1 flashbacks so was nice to see!In a nutshell;Positives:Superb atmosphereFaithful WW1 settingGreat resource balancingArt design Creepy soundtrackGreat well thought out level designVery functional combatExcellent pacingSome excellent well used emotional hooks with the photographs on the soldiersGood difficulty management, doesnt do unnecessary spikes or leave you in the cold if you missed an item earlierNegatives;Slightly too long (Seems to want to end and then goes on for another level)Rats (Already discussed, too fast and dont die that easily so are more grief than the soliders)Some long winded backtracking in later chapters (Essentially having to go the LONG way around for something got a bit tedious at times, a few more shortcuts would of been appreciated)Outdoor level design. It wasn't particularly clear what elements of the countryside I could walk around and what I couldnt so spent a lot of time getting stuck or caught by the rats on a puddle that was similar to one I walked over earlierPerformance was largely excellent, aside from a hard crash when repairing an item when your inventory was full and some frame drops in the last few scenes, also this random issue where the game window didnt quite fill the screen properly when first loaded (Resolved when going to a new room or loading a save)Suggestions;No map indicator if there are items left inside a room (This was a later edition to the resi remakes but I always felt like it was an improvement to know whether you had cleared a room or not)Blocked routes not being largely shown on the map. Would of been nice for that blocked marker to appear on areas that were now or temporarily blocked, this appeared sometimes but not all so would of helped with route managementThanks very much Jordan, I look forward to Conscript 2!

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a game with very high highs and very low lows. I'll begin by mentioning how a majority of the work seen in Conscript is done by one Jordan Mochi, with help from various others such as in voice acting. This alone is incredibly impressive, especially for a game of such quality, but of such length too. You most definitely get your money's worth with Conscript as it boasts 6 lengthy chapters to fight your way through (with relatively good area variety for quite a limited setting).For the positives: 1. The game is gorgeous. The proficiency in pixel art is on full display the entire time with fluid animation and detailed environments. Actions from both enemy and player character are perfectly clear and readable no matter the circumstances. The game world oozes atmosphere, with the soundtrack and sound design emphasising it in every room of the game2. The level design is top notch. There's a very good flow in gathering key items, using them, and getting new ones. Most if not all areas cannot be completely cleared on first visit, heavily encouraging backtracking and re-exploration of old areas. On this note, general progression is excellent also. You can very clearly feel the power increases when discovering new weapons and the severity of the war itself getting more extreme as the game continues on.3. Speaking of the War, the intensity and horror of war is captured extremely well within Conscript. Soldiers, either French or German, seemingly losing their minds or writhing from pain is an all too common sight. The occasional Soldier dropping a photo of a family member, animal or place consistently reinforces to the player that you are fighting other innocent people - fighting for a cause they may not even understand.4. Finally, the Merchant is well implemented. He never directly sells anything of immediate (effective) use, meaning the player must make critical decisions regarding their purchases and resource management. For most (non-key) items there will be a trade-off to make. Do you craft a Molotov, or do you create a disinfectant with the alcohol?Now for the negatives: 1. Beginning with what may be the most major negative, the Rats. When you kill any German Soldier, Rats will soon spawn and begin to fester around the corpses unless they are burned. Simply put, they are not implemented well. Rats are much faster than the player - though not in running speed. Rats can easily optimise their movement around the (sometimes strange) geography of the map, allowing them to easily catch up to the player.Upon hit, there is a chance for the player to be poisoned by Rats. Poison reduces your maximum health until it is healed with a disinfectant bandage. The status effect on it's own is a good idea (especially since it is applied in different areas of the game under different circumstances) however the Rats do it poorly. Rats will, more often than not, poison the player on the first bite (which may be unavoidable depending on the circumstances they are encountered). Furthermore, sometimes Rats lack the windup to their attack, instantly poisoning the player without a chance to fight back.Lastly, the Rats will not fight the Germans and vice versa. They will ignore each other, instead choosing to gang up on the player. Unless both Rats and Germans have a mutual hatred of the French, this is a serious flaw in the design of the game.2. Combat is generally not very good. It attempts to capture the clunky and slow combat of classic Resident Evil (and other Survival Horror games of the time). There is a severe lack of enemy variety in Conscript, and all the enemies really do is charge straight at the player in an attempt to hit them. With melee combat, this can devolve into a back and forth of running away and getting a single hit in - being more silly than scary. Ranged combat is not much better. It can be extremely hard to tell what exactly you are aiming at because the environment does not communicate well enough if you have line of sight or not. I have had enemies shoot me despite clearly being behind a wall they could not possibly shoot me from, whereas I can't shoot them back from the same position.3. Combat is further hindered by how weak a majority of the weapons are - especially in the beginning. Your beginning weapons might as well be shooting BB Bullets with the exception of the Pump-Action Shotgun. The rifle, which you would expect to pack a punch, takes numerous bullets to take down even a single non-armoured enemy. This is largely solved by chapter 4 where you effectively have the best versions of each weapon, but it is still a problem nonetheless. 4.  The story is incredibly lacking. There isn't much beyond the premise of the game, which is a shame. But I can understand how it would be difficult to write a more intriguing story about a World War.5. Some puzzles are far too obtuse for their own good. The main example of this is in the final area of the game, which the solution is so poorly communicated to the player that most people will not solve it. Granted, it is optional, but this is only one example.6. The inventory is too tight. Conscript feels like how people complained about Signalis' inventory. There is simply too much stuff to carry at all times, meaning inventory fills up fast. This inevitably leads to a lot of backtracking, something that is initially a positive, becoming a chore. The needlessly limited stamina (and how slow sprinting actually is) adds to the ever growing tedium.At the end of the day, Conscript is obviously a passion project. While it has several flaws, some which could be considered deal-breakers to specific players, I could not imagine not recommending it. It blows several modern Survival Horror games out of the water with it's quality of level design and atmosphere. It is definitely an acquired taste, though I believe it is worth a try (especially with the very generous demo) to see if it could become one of your Survival Horror favourites like it has mine.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: For the emotional elements of the story, the theme, art and presentation I can recommend the title. I played on Soldier, which was the highest difficulty I could play by default I think? I can't remember at this point, but it's above easy and normal and there was one higher than it. I found myself compelled to finish the game, most likely because I really love the genre of survival horror. A nice treat that also ends up being a con, is I certainly expected monsters or zombies going into this game blind. The game's theme showing both the pointlessness of this battle AND that humans are monsters is a good one, and they portray this well.Some story beats and secrets don't really make sense at times but that is mostly okay besides an ending being locked behind some things you wouldn't think of and you will get locked out of that ending because of it.The gameplay is middling at best, not particularly impressive. You've got a dodge roll but sometimes your hitbox seems to extend and you'll get hit from a long swing. It doesn't happen that often but when it does you'll just think, "Oh." Enemies can be dodge rolled and kited pretty easily, the danger comes from managing your supplies and reloading.Incredibly low enemy varietyLack of shortcuts resulting in incredibly tedious backtrackingRats are a punishment to the tedious backtrackingInventory will be generally reserved at 50-60% capacity for key items and key equipmentDifficulty is lacking due to no boss fights and poor enemy varietyBizarre pacing throughout the game. You can suddenly find yourself in a loooong puzzle breakSome pretty obtuse puzzles, especially one that locks away the "best" endingI really like this genre a lot, and can appreciate the theme here greatly. A lot could have been improved but as an experience overall it was a net positive, JUST slightly. If you aren't a fan of the survival horror genre, then maybe skip.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game in a YouTube video about upcoming survival horror quite a while ago, so it's been on my radar. I have to say, indie devs like this one are absolutely killing it. Conscript, Skald Against The Black Priory, and Faith are probably my favorite games I've played this year.This game feels like a love letter to old-school Resident Evil fans, albeit no tank controls. The setting is perfect for a survival horror game and the mechanics of the game work together very well both in terms of scare factor and narrative. Limited ammo, overwhelming number of enemies, and scarce health items mean you have to pick and choose your battles. Typically in every game I play I end up as a murdering b@stard, but just like in REmake, there are consequences for killing enemies and not burning their bodies. So far I'm only on chapter 2 of 6, but I'm loving it. The art style is charming, the story has me intrigued, the combat is really satisfying once you get the hang of it, and there have been no cheap jump scares thus far, just the right amount of atmospheric tension. Looking forward to seeing what else the game has to offer and I would highly recommend for fans of survival horror
