_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is quite clearly a labour of love - both a love of history and a passion for the game itself. So much care has clearly gone into finding ways of balancing accurate historical detail with interesting gameplay. It's quite an achievement, especially when considering this is a solo dev's work, and manages to be respectful of the real lives lost and the emotional impact of the war while also offering a wealth of content and replayability. I have to praise the bold choice to create a survival horror game with absolutely zero supernatural elements in it, and the game succeeds admirably at evoking the real horrors of trench warfare without paranormal aid. It's also incredibly old school in many ways, with all the positives and negatives that come with that as I'll describe below.  The level design is frankly superb, reminding me of classic metroidvanias and early Resident Evil games, with perfectly-paced exploration, backtracking, and shortcut-unlocking making the trenches, forts, and towns a joy to explore. Despite each area being vast I never felt lost - they unfold logically and you're never presented with a blockage for which the solution cannot be easily found with proper exploration. Revisiting old areas is kept interesting by the new possibilities presented by your equipment, as well as ever-present flesh-eating rats chewing on the corpses that you've left behind and the possibility of a German raid sending new threats your way. The puzzle elements are incredibly old school and resistant to the modern tendency to look things up rather than work it out yourself - many of them are randomized and will require you to either keep a pen and paper handy or use the notebook in the steam overlay to work things out and retain codes for doors and lockers. Despite being very lo-fi, the backdrops look excellent too. The whole place is a wet and muddy hell with corpses and rats everywhere, shattered equipment and craters blocking your path. Blood mixes with water, fire flickers, and lethal yellow-green gas haze drifts. There are even moments of desolate beauty, like when you find poppies growing in a swamp or a stained glass window still standing in a bombed-out church. The combat element is much harsher and more skill-based than I expected. It sits somewhere between Resident Evil and Dark Souls (I know, I know, everybody's bored of Dark Souls comparisons. Shhh!); you have to be very active to stay alive and spacing is key to doing so. When aiming a firearm it takes a while to attain accuracy, so you have to time your shots and concentrate on positioning under pressure. This makes the shooting almost feel like drawing a bow - you hold aim for a while before you shoot. Many of the guns require you to pull the bolt, turn the cylinder, or pump the shell before you can fire again, racking up the tension as your foes charge after you with trench shovels and clubs. Your guns also have limited ammunition and you're always scrabbling around for more, which makes missing all the more galling. The majority of your enemies will be melee fighters, so you'll have to make good use of the Souls-style combat roll and manage your stamina carefully to avoid their licks while dishing out your own while staying wary of any ranged attackers. Your melee weapons have a durability bar that is ever-dwindling, and once they break the damage they put out drops off a cliff. I actually thought this was a rare bad design choice - it doesn't really add anything worthwhile and the melee combat is tense enough without your weapon breaking and you having to backtrack to fix it. There are also a few issues with hitboxes, both yours and the enemies, that I noticed - obvious hits going astray while wild swings somehow connect and the like. Some enemies are also bullet sponges, which in such an otherwise realistic game also felt a bit excessive. Despite these quibbles though, it's an engaging and unique setup, and you certainly have to stay focused if you want to live. Some of the background mechanical choices will be divisive. The game has a classic Resi-style inventory management system and although you can expand your bag as time goes on, at times it's very frustrating being unable to pick up an essential item without throwing out precious ammunition or healing items. You're often forced to backtrack extremely long distances to try and find a stashbox so you can swap your items around. The dev has acknowledged this complaint and added more stash boxes to mitigate it, but the unnecessary backtracking still impacted the pacing for me - shuffling stuff around in your bag just isn't much fun as far as I'm concerned. Many modern games have a "Quest Items" tab for just this reason. I can understand the idea behind it - after all lugging around a satchel full of ammunition and artillery shells is hardly realistic, especially in a muddy environment - but I felt it could've been a bit more forgiving given the scarcity of places to rotate items in and out. The default save system is also very traditional, calling back to Resident Evil again with its ink-ribbon-and-typewriter and no autosaves. It's a mixed blessing. On the one hand, it does suit the ambience - war is hell and Verdun is one of the deepest circles therein. Death can come quickly and fairness isn't really a factor. Safety is a rare luxury. There are swarms of trench raiders, gas attacks, shelling, and landmines just waiting to end your life in an instant, so having an unforgiving save system suits the theme perfectly. However, if you're struggling with a particular area and you find yourself repeatedly losing 10-20 minutes progress, you'll quickly tire of it. After a particularly bad loss of progress in which I'd pushed out too far and forgotten to save, I lost half an hour's progress and I had to put the game down for a couple of days before coming back to it. Skill issue, you might reasonably say, but I doubt I'm the only one that will experience this frustration. This system is clearly the way the dev intended you to play the game, and some of the achievements and top rankings are locked behind it. Be that as it may, I'd still recommend that you at least think about what kind of player you are rather than letting desire for hardcore gamer legitimacy and bragging rights impact your playthrough: the option is there at the start of the game to enable checkpointing and/or more frequent saving and you should consider using them if the standard system would annoy you. Tying the whole package together is the replay value, which is excellent. As in some of the classics of survival horror there are outfits to unlock, but there's also multiple endings based on your actions, achievements for challenge runs that will put your skill to the test, and even unlimited ammunition if you manage to upgrade every weapon in the game to its maximum potential. Overall, I was really impressed - this kind of passion project feels rare and special in this day and age. If you're a fan of truly old-school survival horror this is a great place to find it.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of flaws, some understandable, and others completely baffling, that make it difficult to recommend. The following is an itemized list of some of these flaws.First of all, the combat is clunky, clumsy, and frustrating. This is due to the following reasons:1. You cannot move and shoot/reload. On it's own, this is not bad.2. You cannot cancel out of a reload. If you push R, you are stuck in place doing the animation until either it finishes or someone hits you in the face with a club (I may be wrong about this let me know if there is a way to cancel the reload animation).3. The weapons are, effectively, pea shooters. At least the ones you start with. Expect regular unarmored humans to take 4 rifle shots, 8 machine gun shots, 6 pistol shots, etc.4. It is actually hard to tell if you are aiming at / have line of sight of what you are trying to shoot at or not. Sometimes you will miss what you are aiming at and have no idea why. Sometimes you will aim at an explosive barrel, only to hit an enemy way to the left of it, as if your bullet had a mind of its own. When you melee, sometimes you will put your cursor over an enemy only to swing in the opposite direction. I don't really understand what causes this but I think it has something to do with how it calculates what direction you are facing based on where your cursor is.All of these reasons result in combat that just looks and feels sort of goofy. You will run circles around the enemies, trying to avoid getting hit, and making distance, until you have made enough distance to either aim and shoot or reload. Some weapons take a long time to reload, so you will have to run and make a LOT of distance. Either you will do this or you will just enter an area, shoot an enemy, leave the area, and repeat until the enemies are dead (their health appears to persist when you enter and leave an area and they do not follow you when you leave an area so this is a valid strategy).Secondly, the overall game map / level design, combined with the limited inventory, combined with the pathetically slow sprint / limited spring bar, results in gameplay that has a lot of tedious backtracking. The very good thing about the level design in the Resident Evil games, especially those with limited inventory, is that the item boxes are never really that far away. Here, they really do feel more spread out, and there are far more items you need to carry in your inventory, it feels, than your typical RE game. Also, some areas are just kind of difficult to navigate, particularly the wooded areas of the 3rd chapter, which has some water puddles you can walk through, and some you can't, with geometry sort of blending into itself so you can't really always tell at a glance if the bush is something you can walk through or not, with your map not really being helpful at all (it shows the entrances and exits of the area but not any of the obstacles that obstruct you).Third, the rats. There is really no excuse for how the rats are implemented at this point. When you kill a German, and leave the area, eventually when you return to the area their body will be chewed upon by flesh eating rats who will chase you down mercilessly as soon as you get in range and aggro them. They will NEVER attack the German soldiers, for some reason Germans and rats are best good friends, either that or they just both hate the French enough to work together. So if you aggro them in an area with German soldiers they hilariously work as a team. Also if they bite you there is a chance they will poison you which requires a med kit to heal, a med kit being a very rare and valuable item that you have a limited supply of. So the only way to deal with rats is to constantly bring around a lighter and fuel to burn bodies, but this means you will have less inventory space and will have to do more tedious backtracking, which will make your game less fun. So this game is asking you to juggle the tedium of having to backtrack constantly with the extreme annoyance of flesh eating rats. You can kill them but the melee attacks against rats are for some reason the jankiest of them all, with you swinging at the air above them half the time, and they often come in groups of 3-4 meaning you WILL get bit and lose health dealing with them. Rats are especially annoying in dark areas or tight corridors as you may turn a corner and suddenly get attacked by rats that you couldn't see or that were obstructed by the level geometry. I think the rats could be fixed, make them easier to deal with or just less absurdly strong, but honestly if they were removed from the game entirely it would be better for it.Lastly, and these are just some nitpicks. 1. Enemies can attack you while obscured by the level geometry. This should never ever be able to happen, ever, period. I should never ever be shot by an enemy that my character would be able to see, but that I as the player cannot see because they are obscured by an overhang. That makes no sense. An easy fix would be to make their outline visible, or make the overhang/obstruction blocking them disappear as soon as they enter the character's field of view. 2. Enemies can walk through level geometry, such as fences and crates, that you as the player cannot. I don't know if this is a glitch or intended but it can be annoying because it makes it impossible to close in on the enemy for a stealth kill when they can phase through a solid object and you can't. 3. The story is EXTREMELY basic / bare bones. You are a solider in WW1 who is looking for your brother, who is also a soldier. That's it. You know the entirety of the plot.AS FOR THE POSITIVES- I do love the art even if sometimes the obstacles blend with the background and make it difficult to navigate.- The atmosphere is great. Sounds, music, the sounds of planes and distant gunfire, a lot of the war torn environments, etc. It feels like WW1 but a horror game at the same time.- I appreciate the resident evil influences. They are obvious but I don't care. The more games that are like resident evil the better IMO.- It does have solid progression, as in you get introduced to better weapons and equipment as well as stronger enemies at a solid pace.- Having a new game plus mode is a HUGE positive.The bottom line is I do like this game, and if you are here bothering to read reviews for it you will probably like it too, but it is hard for me to RECOMMEND it to someone who isn't almost immediately sold by "WW1 survival horror resident evil clone."
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the early Resident Evil games and am always hunting for new things that put me in that state of mind.Conscript delivered exactly what I wanted while always feeling fresh and new despite its many mechanical callbacks to older games.I am very interested in WWI history and felt that this game delivered a thorough, tasteful, and emotionally meaningful representation of the era: the horror, the futility, the small struggles that played out all throughout the battlefield and are long since lost to time.I recommend putting in the time to get the various endings.I don't have much in the way of negative or constructive criticism. I experienced two crashes in 40 hours of playtime and one minor music bug (safe room music kept looping after I left). The crashes made me nervous about attempting runs of the game with under 6 saves but did not get in the way of enjoying my multiple casual playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is the only survival horror game I've played that doesn't have monsters or the supernatural. What's more is that the human enemies you fight, and the scenarios you encounter, are more than enough to inspire dread. Conscript is a very grim, tense, enjoyable and respectful game. The story is fairly light, but the setting and the central thrust to save your brother are enough to get you invested. I was so pissed off that I missed the true ending that I played through on the hardest difficulty, and had an even better time. Definite recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: are what I would say if I had to summarize Conscript in one sentence. The game tells a horrific and heart-breaking war story depending on your ending, and it does a pretty good job, considering there is very limited dialogue and no voice acting.At first glance, Conscript looks like a WW1 version of Signalis, both thematically and in terms of gameplay. However, it sadly can't live up to that standard due to its lackluster puzzles and the most abysmal backtracking I've ever experienced in a video game. Some puzzles are so long and bloated that you forget what you were even trying to achieve in the first place. This only gets worse as the game progresses, and in the end, the puzzles don't feel as rewarding or interesting as those typically found in the survival-horror genre. The game also has the single weirdest inventory system I've seen in a survival-horror title. About three-quarters of your inventory is filled with key items and passive-ability granting items. This makes exploration extremely stressful and less satisfying than in many other games in the genre. It also lays the foundation for the game's problematic backtracking.As I mentioned at the beginning of the review, this game is about pain and suffering, and by the end, I almost felt like these shortcomings were intentional. The developer, in my opinion, really wanted the player to feel hopeless and helpless, much like someone alone in a WW1 trench. So, even though I have serious issues with the survival-horror gameplay loop, I must admit that it all comes together in the end, proving Conscript to be a modern survival-horror success, especially as someone who has a brother, making the story of André and Pierre resonate with me on a personal level.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a hard game to review, mainly because of the preconceptions I had going in significantly compromising the experience. I learned about this game a while back on ABG's channel and was super interested. I was expecting a survival horror game with some psychological elements set in WW1. The biggest comparison I kept hearing for the game was Signalis, which is one of the best games of all time in my opinion. What I got instead was a very atmospheric shooter with some of the worst pacing ive ever seen in a game.Things I liked:Combat: This felt pretty much how I thought it would. It is clunky, awkward and frantic. For a WW1 game with resource management that actually works out super well. Even into the endgame I still found the combat to be really fun and engaging. Atmosphere: The game really does nail a feeling of futility and dread that I am unsure if I've felt in a game before. Everything feels miserable, dirty, violent and hopeless. *Most* of the game manages to look visually interesting even with the limited color pallet. Story: It isn't fantastic, but I did end up enjoying it overall. Things that were alright: The rat mechanic: This felt incredibly underwhelming. I struggled maybe once with this mechanic in the whole campaign. Having the ability to just destroy the vast majority of rat spawns in the game was a really bad choice. Instead of creating a potential minefield early on by killing enemies in bad locations, you can basically bypass and ignore this entire system. End of chapter scenes: Between chapters there is a sort of intermission. I will not spoil it here, but I found it to be pretty badly done. This really should've been were some horror was put into the game, but it instead just plays out pretty blandly. Gun progression: Some of this was executed well, some of this wasn't. There were several weapons in the game that really didn't need to be included. With upgrades for weapons being relatively uncommon and finite, this felt like a noob trap. Most of this game is fine if not a bit average. There are 3 major failure points of this game that made me want to make this review. Failure 1: The Merchant. Throughout the game you find a currency to trade with a merchant character. He is in just about every saferoom in the game and very quickly becomes your most seen friendly character. My issue with this is how much of the game is locked behind this character. Most survival horror game shops exist for alternative weapons, upgrades, character upgrades and maybe some limited health items. Conscript puts almost unlimited health items, key items, bag upgrades, ammo and troll weapons in the merchant inventory. This leads to situations where you can be forced into massive backtracking routes because you didn't know XYZ was an important item, so instead bought a spare grenade or save item. Late game, I had about 600 currency items with literally nothing useful left to spend them on, severely hampering exploring efforts. I was still regularly finding more currency items at this point. This leads into failure point 2Failure 2: PacingThis game has some of the worst pacing I have ever seen in a videogame. It is genuinely incredible how badly executed segments of the game are. The worst example of this is Chapter 3. Chapter 3 has you leave the trenches of WW1 to go explore a nearby wooded area. You spend about 20ish minutes doing nothing but running to an area. No enemies spawn at this time, so you just run around this exceptionally bland forest. After an eternity of doing that, you eventually start activating nearby patrols, allowing combat to occur in super scripted locations. In the main areas of this chapter, 3/4 guys spawn once. That is the challenge. If I wasen't trying to finish this game out of stubberness I'd have dropped it here. Failure 3: The inventory systemI am a fan of a limited inventory system in most survival horror games. I didn't mind Signalis having a 6 inventory item limit, I didn't mind older resident evil games having a limited inventory, I loved the attache case system in RE4. This game has without a doubt the worst inventory I have seen in a game. You are usually expected to carry multiple situational key items with you for large segments of the game. You do not know when these items are needed, but will often have a long trek to an inventory box if you forget a random item. This significantly jams up your limited inventory space, making looting a complete chore. I found myself discarding most of the items I picked up in the late game just to avoid running 3 minutes to drop off items. Overall, I did stick with the game for the entire runtime, but I will likely never play it again. I would have given it up repeatedly if I didn't have a vague hope of the game going somewhere more interesting with its story. I would not say it was worth the 20$ price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is really, really good if you like survival Horror, with a more "Realistic" Aspect of horror.Now for the long version.... Here we go, I hope I can do my feelings for this game justice in the review I leave.So as of writing this review, I have not finished my first playthrough, but I felt it needed to get some praise. This game takes the setting of the most brutal conflict the world has known, and gives us a simple mission, keep our brother alive. Weather we are a good or bad soldier, our only goal is to get both ourselves, and our brother home alive. I am not a soldier, I worked as a security contractor for a time and I have been unfortunate enough to get in a gunfight, and lucky enough to make it through it physically unharmed. There was a section in the game where I was going through the trenches, looking for more supplies, dodging German Trench Raids and stray rounds over the parapets, and I encounter a German soldier, alive, on his feet, seemingly in hysterics. Not wanting to leave a section of trench unsecured from the enemy, I raise my trench shovel and bring it down on the boy's head. The telltale sparkle of loot shows up on the ground and I reflexively pick it up, only for it to show a photo of a beautiful German Shepherd. When I worked security I carried a photo of my dog, a long hair German Shepherd with me because that was my motivation to make it home. That hit me like a ton of bricks. This kid, in the game, was me in my early twenties real life, that just broke seeing the unbelievable horror that was the Great War. That is the only part for risk of further spoilers I am going to include. Give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: *EDIT*With the most recent update, the previous complaints have been addressed entirely, and more supply boxes have been added around making backtrack even better. The previously mentioned rats are now able to be kited much better: they no longer hit nearly as hard but they're still worth thinking about taking care of during your backtracks, but they don't impede the prepared player.Signalis, Conscript, and Crow Country truly have been gifts to the genre as a whole, so if you end up enjoying this game I highly recommend supporting these devs.*END EDIT*Overall a good experience from what I've played, the meat and bones of the game is absolutely solid from a presentation and sound stand point. Thematically and mechanically should be appropriate and I can appreciate what they represent; in practice however, entirely different. The game teases their appearance prior to their "spawn encounter" so the player is technically aware it can happen, however when you actually pick up the item which allows you to burn corpses, rats actually begin to spawn. In my current situation what that amounts to is that because of the amount of corpses in key hallways I cannot make progress without significant sacrifice to resources against an enemy that is extremely mechanically hard to actually combat.Shooting them, hitting them with melee, or even attempting to burn the corpses feels very bad in practice, and it becomes even stranger when you watch rats completely ignore enemy troops to home in on you specifically. _childDocuments_.review: This is the classic survival horror experience us 90's guys are craving for.While the setting is nothing supernatural, the theme plays with the very real horrors of war and fear of isolation and death around every corner in such a unique setting that you wouldn't expect the genre to excel in.Actual jumpscares are rare (though effective the handful of occurrences) and it's mostly psychological; the effective usage of Silent Hill-style still images which give an unsettling air about them, your character's aim and crosshair devolving into a jittery mess slightly over time as the game goes on, entire areas in a catacombs/dug-out mines that require limited visibility flashlight items, finding remnants of your fellow platoon losing themselves and in the throws of being shellshocked, witnessing amputated and land-mine victims crawling toward you..It has the hallmarks of the RE/Silent Hill style metroidvania design down to a T and you'll quickly be associating the trenches and familiar Mess Hall areas to the Spencer estate, and marking down locked doors, Gas-filled areas or other obstacles barring your ingress until the appropriate tool is discovered. Puzzles are clever, and I've made use of Steam's handy notepad overlay on more than one occasion. Surprisingly enough they sort of.. fit thematically and feel like they are atleast justified and make sense also instead of just being there for the sake of it.The homages to the classics are all here between an ink ribbon save system (togglable off for those who dislike) and item boxes, a familiar shady Merchant+weapon upgrades, even being hit with waves of RE1 nostalgia as I returned from the 'Outside' area back to the familiar homebase to be met with more aggressive  armoured blitzing enemy-types and a mustachioed friendly face restocking supply rooms (At this point the game throws a curveball at you also to ramp up the survival/horror aspect by destroying half the safe rooms!)If someone asked me what a Silent Hill/Resident Evil/Metal Gear/Parasite Eve mashup set in WW1 would look like I never thought the formula would work as well as we've seen here.Absolutely worth your time to atleast check out the demo if this is the type of thing that piques your interest.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for some screenshots  to view all the ones I took for this game.The main story will not only encompass Poilu’s struggle to find his brother, but also recap his past via flashbacks, portraying the pain many families suffered in seeing their sons sent to war, with little chance of them coming back at all, or unchanged by the horrors they witnessed. A good assortment of accessory lore and characters tells the tales of other characters who had their lives ruined by the tragedy of conflict. All of them are well-written, plausible, and seldom have a happy ending.CONSCRIPT’s setting is bleak, greyscale and desolate, as it should be. War crimes, mutilated soldiers gasping for their last breath, reckless carnage and piles of mangled bodies will be common sights, as will be people driven to madness by the unspeakable things they were forced to do in order to survive. From a historical standpoint, barring gameplay-related choices, it’s an accurate setting from uniforms to weapons to locations -  that, compounded with a solid sound design, ensures tension and immersion for the whole experience.You’ll explore all places on foot, with a handy map marking doors, points of interest and utility NPCs (such as the trader) automatically, as long as you interact with them once. Later on, fast-travel becomes available in the widest locations, however this is limited, and you’ll have to do most of the work yourself regardless. There are supplies such as ammo and medicine, other than valuables such as cigarettes and jewels, hidden everywhere - the keen explorer will be greatly rewarded for the extra time put into looting; mandatory to have enough supplies on the harder difficulties. Maps are convoluted, with many optional and hidden zones for you to discover; they may also change after specific events, new paths open and old ones become inaccessible. Certain areas require puzzles to be solved, requiring  you to collect multiple items and make sense on how to use them.The biggest issue is backtracking: you’ll be forced to run back and forth from your stash hundreds of times if you want to gather all the resources or items (and you’ll need them) due to the extremely limited inventory space, which can be expanded a bit, but not anytime soon. This becomes a chore, made even more crippling by the Rats, an enemy endlessly respawning from corpses, capable of poisoning and damaging you - they can be removed from some areas using finite resources, such as fuel or grenades, but there aren’t enough for all of them. I probably spent 50% of all playtime just backtracking to deposit items - that's’ not fun, and this isn’t Death Stranding.Combat plays out using either ranged or melee weapons, the latter having durability while the former uses ammunition. Until late-game, ammo is rather scarce and should only be used in the harder fights, while backstabbing enemies stealthily or avoiding them are more viable choices. However, with how unreliable stealth is, you’ll have to ‘reset’ an area many times by changing location, and spawn rats in the process (they ignore enemies and only attack you), before you can successfully kill all foes without using tons of ammo. It’s satisfying to hit them, as there’s good weight and feel behind each shot or blow; however, the inaccuracy of ranged weapons - compounded with the fact Poilu will become more shell shocked and shaky as the game progresses - makes landing precision shots a pain. You may choose to skip the biggest battles by hiding, but this will heavily impact the story’s finale. The main issue with combat resides in how flat it feels. Most enemies have the same archetypes, no special skills or unique quirks, just stronger versions of something seen before. Essentially, each fight is a kiting game where Poilu will have to find some place to run in a circle, and shoot enemies while backpedaling until they’re all dead, or use the dodge-roll to go through them if he gets cornered. No weak spots, no unique mechanics to defeat any enemy, and no bosses - it’s the same exact fight from the beginning to the end, just against stronger, more numerous foes.The mysterious Trader will be a pillar for your success, trading resources to craft ammo or medicine, weapons, special items and upgrades for cigarettes, the only currency. He’ll also accept valuables and pay you. In almost all safe rooms, he'll be there, along with your bottomless stash and a save point, offering different stock based on the Chapter you’re in, and also allow you to upgrade weapons to make them deadlier. Some items, such as Morphine, will grant Poilu permanent upgrades to his stats, however these are rare - there’s no other form of progression. Until much later, the Trader’s prices will be too high, so you should only resort to him when things are dire. The in-game economy is fine, but becomes far too forgiving in late-game, especially if you explore everything.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a no from me, bowing out on the last chapter because the backtracking has gotten to levels of anti-fun you cannot fathom. The game has some really good moments and is constantly and consistently overshadowed by the worst pieces of Resident Evil game design. Paths you've cleared repopulating? Check. A worse enemy as the repopulating force? Check. 10,000 single-use key items? Check. The expectation of the player is to keep notes... while having a note system in the game that does not take note of codes or anything but fluff dialogue and HINTS at codes. You find several codes written down, and the character never once thinks to jot them down. (I lost a very important code for an ending because I accidentally closed the window it was typed in; it's randomised, so I'd need to either have saves preemptively set in the location where you get the code pieces or play the whole game again. Actually why would you make it this way?)The idea of replaying the game would be a little less not enticing in the slightest if the backtracking and routing around the maps wasn't designed to force the player to move the furthest path possible through rooms they have previously been to. If you unlock a shortcut (Town Streets, for example), you can BET ten minutes later it's going to be blocked to make you do this.I'm pretty disappointed because everything else not mentioned (combat mechanics, art style, writing) all hit really well but they are littered with the annoyances listed above, and I cannot in good health continue to wonder which of the 50 random doors in the fort the other two pieces of medallion I'm required to collect are. (I'm betting it's about half the fort worth of rooms away from what I last did, that's the most solid guess I can give because it would track with how the rest of the key items have been placed thus far.)

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those cases where it would be really neat if Steam allowed a neutral review, rather than a straight up negative one. Conscript has a lot of good, commendable things going for it, but they never coalesce into something cohesive. Or truly enjoyable, for that matter.The thing that buries any potential that this game may have had is terrible tempo. Conscript absolutely loves to waste the player's time on backtracking, and not the clever sort of backtracking that was present in Resident Evil, where you often need to carefully consider your route and the dangers ahead. The locations are so big and objectives are so far apart that item based puzzles quickly suck the air out of the game. To dev's credit, each chapter of Conscript experiments with different ideas and level design, but due to how monotonous everything looks the locales blend with each other. And aside from visual variety there's nothing to keep the player's attention, nothing to keep up the pressure or suspense. Although the ambience, the sounds and themes of different chapters are quite good, nothing but praise here.Why is there no tension? Because the combat system is simultaneously too clunky and too forgiving. Any battle where you do not immediately kill the enemy devolves into a silly dance routine, where you take a shot, walk a couple of steps back, take another shot (or a melee hit) -- and repeat until everyone's dead. In fact, you can just dodge roll everything. Yes, a supposedly serious horror game about World War I has a dodge roll, and it has a hilariously generous i-frame window. German soldiers are supposedly human, but they behave very much like monsters from any other standard horror game. Their AI is really dumb, and it completely destroys any illusion of danger. The game has a stealth mechanic where you can one shot enemy soldiers if they do not notice you, but they are incapable of hearing any sounds other than gunfire, even if you run behind them full-sprint. At the same time, once they notice you, there's absolutely no hiding from them, even if you break line of sight and find a designated hiding spot.There's really no other way of fighting the enemies other than dodge rolling / abusing their animation locks, so you can kiss immersion goodbye. It really baffles me that Conscript chose the setting where, in my opinion, any exchange of fire should be highly lethal and risky, but did not adjust its own rules accordingly. Ideas that were taken straight from Resident Evil just do not work right without extra attention to detail. The game even has its own version of Crimson Heads in the form of rats; you can glance at many negative reviews here or posts at community hub to see how people reacted to them. Yes, the dev reacted fairly quickly and patched them to make infernal rodents a bit less annoying, but they still do not contribute anything worthwile to the experience. If you do not count slight inconvenience, of course.The final nail in the coffin is the fact that Conscript fails to evoke any emotion other than mild boredom. It's not tense enough to make you fear for your life thanks to poorly thought out combat mechanics, and it's not really human enough to make you care about the war. Sure, it constantly shows you gruesome moments of conflict, like mountains of dead bodies, blood, ♥♥♥♥, rot and destruction, but sooner rather than later it all just becomes white noise. Sure, that might be the whole point, the bloodshed makes you numb and all, but Conscript does not really explore such themes. You do not know anything about the protagonist other than the fact thah he has a family and really wants to save his brother... Who you also do not know anything about and, thus, have no emotional bond whatsoever. Germans make an impression of totally mindless zombies that sometimes carry photographs of their loved ones (oh, the humanity!), and the french are just slightly better thanks to one or two named characters. It's like... Conscript is trying too hard to be gritty when it comes to visuals (and, for the record, they are great), but does not try to do anything even remotely compelling when it comes to narrative. It's not even a question of bias or historical accuracy, there's just nothing interesting to talk about.Conscript does execute some things well enough. First hours of the game are pretty compelling, since exploration of the first trenches is enjoyable, and you do not realise how much of a slog laters locations will be. Ambient soundscape is stellar: sounds of gunfire, heavy rain, sirens and explosions blend together into something horrifying and beautiful. Item management and weapon progression is also handled well.Unfortunately, cons do outweigh the pros, at least for me. I deleted the game with clear conscience at the last chapter, when i realised that, after hours of scrounging for puzzles at a small deserted town, there were another couple hours of the same chores, even though the story seemingly geared up for the finale. Conscript is an okay, sometimes good game that could've been magnificent with enough attention to mechanical details and trimming some of the fat.I hope the dev will not stop working in games industry, because the talent and passion are there. The only thing left is refinement.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the game for years now and even played the earliest demo, and I can say for sure CONSCRIPT impressed me.You can see a lot of influences from the classic survival-horrors, especially Resident Evil 1 and sometimes RE4 too. _childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It masterfully blends old-school Resident Evil mechanics with a retro aesthetic, offering a relatively unique survival horror experience set in WWI—without resorting to zombies to fill the setting. WWI was horrifying enough as it is. The combat is janky as hell, but that’s almost a given in this genre to ramp up the challenge. Most enemies are fairly simple and can be easily kited, and you can reset their positions by leaving and re-entering a room or area, which is a handy trick.The rat mechanic isn’t too frustrating since the rats are easy to kill (unlike the Crimson Heads in RE1), so they’re quite manageable. Plus, you’re given a decent amount of fuel to burn corpses. However, the spawn rate of rats is inconsistent. Sometimes they spawn after you leave an area twice, and other times it takes four or more loads. Still, rats aren’t a major issue if you don’t kill every single enemy or if you manage to stack them and burn them efficiently with a single use of fuel.However, the one thing that prevents me from fully recommending this game is the excessive backtracking. My frustration began around Chapter 3, where it was just barely tolerable. But once you hit Chapters 4 and 5—oh boy, it becomes too much. I’ve played almost every survival horror game out there, but I’ve never encountered as much backtracking as I did in CONSCRIPT. Nearly 50% or more of the game time is spent backtracking, retrieving items, and then trekking all the way back to open a door, only to find yet another item that needs to be used on the opposite side of the map.To make matters worse, certain parts of the game have "world events" that change the map, making the backtracking even more tedious. Just when you think you've learned the layout, you’re forced to navigate it in a convoluted, snake-like manner. The Town section nearly broke me by the end.If the backtracking weren’t such a huge pain, I would definitely recommend this game. This issue seems entirely fixable—unless it’s just me and I’m not seeing something others aren’t.I’ve never had a problem with backtracking in any other game, but in CONSCRIPT...man, it’s a real ball-buster.

_childDocuments_.review: This kind of hurts me to leave a negative review bc the game is genuinely really cool and I love this type of game, but the gameplay/combat has so many flaws that trying to play it on the harder difficulty is more annoying than hard. If even just the basic problems got fixed this game would be incredible but there's just too many aggravating mechanics stacked up right now to actually want to play this game.The combat is interesting bc most of the guns are manually primed after each shot (revolver, pump shotgun, Mosin) and it basically has Resident Evil's resource/ammo management, traders, multiple guns of the same type that you can choose between and upgrade, etc. The big problem with the combat though is that most enemies are melee fighters and their attacks are extremely clunky that it's difficult to not get hit. You have to frequently rely on a dodge roll that feels like it only gives you 3 i-frames and on top of that the hit boxes are so terrible that I've been hit by a gun swinging a shovel that looked at least 3 feet away from my character. The enemies also have 3 different attacks, which is an interesting idea, but the problem is they have a heavy and medium swing that you have to be careful to differentiate or else you'll get hit (cool idea) but then they also have a light attack that has absolutely no warning at all so the enemy basically walks up to you and then you just take damage. It is actually just frustrating bc in a game like this on the high difficulty just a couple wasted healing items can heavily impact a play-throughSpeaking of unfair mechanics and wasted healing items, that rats are god awful. They're clearly this game's version of RE1's red zombies where after you kill a soldier if you don't burn the body down the road some rats will spawn on the body. Again, super cool idea, but the problem is they spawn in numbers between 2 to 6 on a single body from what I've seen and they are pumped full of what looks like the black plague. The rats are faster than you, they are hard to shoot, the only way to hit them with a melee is if it's fully charges which takes about 2 seconds of just standing there slowly pulling back your arm, and they also have no warning before they attack so they just walk up to you and you take damage. They don't do much damage but they will VERY quickly infect you which drops your max HP down to the point of pretty much being one-shot by any German and the only way to get rid of it is to use very precious healing/crafting items. One time a rat ran up to me and instantly bit me and the very first bite infected me. That was just aggravating.This game also has very questionable game mechanics that by themselves aren't game ruining but them on top of the above mentioned combat mechanics just make this game infuriating to play. The areas all look super cool and are all unique but the way the map is laid out makes it to where to go from one area to another you essentially have to walk across the entire map to get there. This game just isn't aware of what a shortcut is which makes any kind of back tracking or exploration turning into just 10 minutes of walking from point A to point B. Then there's the problem with the shooting. Idk exactly how the shooting is designed but I sometimes if you aim at an object to shoot your bullet just completely misses depending on your character's angle. To burn bodies you can pour gas on them and then shoot the gas to light it if you don't want to carry the lighter but sometimes when I try to shoot gas puddles it just doesn't light? Even though my reticle was right on it? I would have to readjust where I'm standing to shoot it and actually hit it. Just frustrating sitting there wasting ammo when the enemies take like, 5/6 shots to kill with the pistol.

_childDocuments_.review: made waves two years ago at Steam's Next Fest and rightfully so. To describe the game in as few words as possible it is pixel-art  mixed with  but in the Great War instead of World War II.Describing it in a couple more words it is a top-down surival horror. Unlike the brilliant  that also takes place in the first World War the horror comes not from a supernatural being hunting you but from war itself. You play as the French conscript André who is looking for his brother Pierre at the horrifying battle of Verdun. The game takes place in several locations, a French trench that regularly gets raided by German troops, the "no man's land", a destroyed town and lastly a French fort that got occupied by the Imperial German Army.The gameplay is a mixed bag at least on standard difficulties and above but I think that was the creator's intention. The combat is clunky. To shoot your gun you have to stand still, to cycle a new round you also have to stand still which gives the terrifying enemies time to gain ground on you. So running is often your best option. Because the more you kill the more rats are swarming the trenches to feast on the dead. Just like the later  you have a trader who'll sell things and also upgrade your weapons for cigarettes. These refuges are also your save points. You can choose whether you'll want to have the classic ink ribbon save system or infinite saves with checkpoints. I chose the latter because the game is insanely difficult. While you're navigating the trench you have to solve puzzles that are randomized each playthrough. Some are simple like finding a pair of wire cutters other require more effort like finding the birth date of a certain soldier in the military registry. Mostly you'll be traversing from one storage chest to another because of your limited inventory space. Because besides weapons, healing items and molotovs or fuel to fend off rats you'll need quest items and your trusty gas mask. And there is nothing more frustrating then standing beside a door and not having the key with you. This gets easier the further you expand your inventory though. I hope you have a good understanding of the gameplay now otherwise I suggest you try the demo.Now, the reason I write this review is because many aspects of the game took me by surprise. While faithful to the  formula the atmosphere is unmatched in my opinion. It's small things like the clinking of your boots as you walk over thousands upon thousands of spent artillery shells, to slowly wading through mud filled trenches. The most visceral visions are imposing German soldiers wearing steel Brustpanzer taking swipes at you with a hatchet yelling in German that they will kill you, the sound of a whistle announcing another German assault but the most gut-wrenching moments are witnessing soldiers crawling with blown-off limbs, shell shocked soldiers from the constant barrage of artillery, soldiers asphyxiating from mustard gas, shot and bleeding out or just plain disillusioned by the futility of it all. To be honest the game had a greater emotional impact on me than reading Remarque's . And that is why I wrote this review. From a gameplay perspective you can find all of this in other games like (the from what I heard also excellent)  for example. But the emotional toll is entirely different.So if you have an interest in the "The War That Will End War" and aren't afraid of the harsh difficulty I absolutely recommend Conscript. There's also multiple endings. While I don't feel the want of playing it back to back right now I will definitely come back to it.

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT isn't only a game, it's also a piece of art. The whole art style of this game, the sound and the depressed feeling.... I can't remember a game that captures the terror and horror of war so good than this one. Sure, it use a different kind of artstyle, but it really fits perfectly for this game.It also brings some fresh air to the genre of action adventures. The gameplay loop feels unique and it's fun to explore and get deeper into the horror of war. Honestly, I didn't expect that... a game that's fun to play on the one hand, and also makes you feel so uncomfortable and let you feel you're in the middle of war.Thanks to the developer and Team17 for bringing this piece of art to life ! Finally something new in my list what I really enjoy playing and I can't wait to beat the game.My rating so far: 9 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: A gritty survival/horror game set in my favorite dismal backdrop of the trenches of WWI... specifically during the Battle of Verdun. Combat German raiders & stragglers, rats, gas attacks, and many other perils of the frontline as you fight to survive. Supply management is critical, as you only have 8 (i think) slots in your inventory and must continually make trips back to a storage chest to save anything you find. If not, you must choose what to save and what to discard in order to acquire more important supplies/items in your mission. But be warned: you may not find the item you're discarding again....  for instance, I had reached the end of Chapter 2 and had used/discarded scraps of fabric I had found previously.. to the point that I now had only 1 left when I encountered a medic asking for a bandage to assist a wounded soldier.Absolutely loving this game and looking forward to playing many more hours, seeing how this story unfolds in the gruesome madness of the Great War.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT is a well-executed Survival Horror (SH) game, you won't be facing the living dead here... something far worse, the man-made horrors that shattered the illusions of a civilised era during the Great War. For context, my play-through was on Veteran.Pros - Gritty, raw, and unrelenting, SH at it's absolutely core especially during the early chapters of the game. You're left constantly anticipating which resources to take, which enemies to leave/fight, your sense of vulnerability never leaves you. Plenty of influences and nod's to the likes of Resident Evil/Silent Hill but doesn't feel like a cheap imitation.Excellent pixel-art and setting, the game absolutely leaves it's mark by displaying a gruesome milestone in the history of warfare and humanity.Great soundtrack, as well as ambient noises that heightens the tension and often leave's you on edge. Solid puzzles that requires careful exploration and problem-solving, but nothing that leaves you feeling as though you're having to reinvent the wheel. Cons - The scripted battle sequences particularly during the early chapters just felt inconsistent in terms of progressing through them, I couldn't determine if it was enemies killed or timed, but I just felt it could of been implemented better. The environments are sometimes difficult to traverse and navigate due to the pixel art at times, this was at its worse during Chapter 3 for me. The rats are currently OP (fortunately the dev has acknowledged this) they can quickly chip away at your health and poison you consistently, making you use up precious alcohol or chemical fluids. I also felt the game could of explained them a bit better, I initially read it that if you blew up the rat holes they would no longer be a problem in that area, when in fact they will still spawn even if there are no holes in an area and you constantly need to bring fuel and a lighter. It would of been beneficial as well if your map displays where a rat hole is discovered. Lack of enemy types, by the end of Chapter 4 you've seen every enemy type the game has to offer, I was pretty surprised there wasn't an end boss in all honesty and was a little disappointed. Also by the end of the game you've got so many resources they really don't present a threat anymore even on Veteran. The ending criteria doesn't make any sense to me, I slaughtered every conceivable German during my play-through, never abandoned my post but yet was awarded with Ending 2A (Coward) which just left a very anti-climatic feeling. BLUFAll in all this is a decent Survival Horror, veterans and newcomers of Survival Horror should absolutely check out CONSCRIPT which is both terrifying and memorable, offering players an intense and immersive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Indie devs making survival horror games seem to keep taking the utterly wrong takeaways from what made classic survival horror games great, mistaking forced clunky combat, minimal inventory space, and way too much backtracking as some kind of genre virtue when the classics weren’t really that. The classic Resident Evils were tightly designed games where backtracking was never a huge deal because the games gave you shortcuts to keep traversal interesting  and less of a hassle, or they were like Silent Hill where there were separate areas in the town done in a linear fashion that didn’t make you go back very far. Combat also could be avoided and there wasn’t that many actual combat encounters really but the indie survival horrors I’ve backed that have disappointed me such as this game and Alisa just love throwing constant combat encounters at you and their clunky combat systems aren’t built for them.I backed Conscript a while back because it had real promise, I liked the grounded WWI setting and the isometric view reminded me of that GBA Jurassic Park 3 game and I was interested in a potentially better game having that aesthetic. And the final game does utilize that aesthetic well as it looks great for what it’s trying to shoot for. Too bad that the actual gameplay and level design isn’t of similar quality…Ultimately this game ended up being disappointing and rather boring to me to the point where I’m just cutting my losses and peacing out at Chapter 3. I give credit to the dev for being receptive to critique and patching absolutely overturned enemies such as the rats, but I honestly think the problems with this game are too embedded into it, and it’s mainly how bloated and labyrinthine the game is. Maps are way too big and the game is utterly stingy with shortcuts and this is further exacerbated with how little inventory space you are given and how the game expects you to have a whole bunch of key items at all times. The REs and Silent Hills didn’t really have very many puzzles that required multiple inventory slots but Conscript does it constantly. What really doesn’t help is how crafting focused the game is and how many different kinds of items it gives you because of that, but the inventory space doesn’t seem balanced around that at all. The OG REs and Silent Hills didn’t have that many different items so the inventory management was more about preventing you from having a full arsenal at all times. Conscript though is trying to have mechanics that survival horror games with more generous inventory space have and it just does not gel well at all with the restrictive inventory. The game also gives you many different weapons variants and upgrade paths with the shopkeeper but this feels like something from RE4, a game that had much more generous inventory management than this game does. It just feels like a bunch of popular survival horror game mechanics slapped together with no thought given of how they work in tandem as a wholeCombat is also clunky as ♥♥♥♥ and the game forces you into a whole bunch. Aiming is super awkward and I’ve missed shots even though I had lined up my reticule to the enemies. You can instant kill enemies with stealth melee but this never feels good. If you do manage to whiff a stealth kill (Which is likely enough due to the poor aiming) combat just devolves into Yakkety Saxxing around to get out of range of enemies so you can shoot them or whack them with melee. It’s just a slog and there is just so much of it that can’t easily be avoided. It really feels like this game would have benefited from auto aim like the classic survival horror games had.As I said I think I’m nearing the end of Chapter 3 of apparently 6 but I just don’t feel like I would trudge through another three chapters of this when I’m already hitting the ten hour mark, where most Resident Evil and Silent Hills tended to end around. Crow Country absolutely nailed feeling like an actual classic RE/Silent Hill throwback and unlike this game is paced excellently, so I recommend playing that instead of this.

_childDocuments_.review: its a fun game to play but its story and context aren't explored or polished enough to give any impact to my actions.one minuet i'm on the front line and the next i wake up in the body pit and i'm running around shoveling people because i'm supposed to be looking for my brother. Thematically this is great but there's a lot of missed opportunity of psychological horror/ imagery or map changes- puzzles are relatively well done and the solutions not only make sense it fits the theme- enemy variety is a bit dismal but understandable- combat gets annoying very fast especially when the hitbox dosn't agree (but that's more of a personal gripe)- item descriptions don't give enough details and force trial and error (which is fine for replay value but it makes it very difficult to analyze if the design desicion was intentional or not)- most of my issues with this game is that i wanted to get a solid traumatizing WWI experience and i got a semi annoying tunnel and trench simulator (granted this is only personal opinion i think its overall a fun time killer but it missed alot of opportunities in terms of story telling and imagery resulting in something that feels bland the longer i play it)

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the more interesting/different Survival Horror games in a good while. The music soundtrack and atmosphere was done excellently. I did really appreciate the dev managed to make a game that highlights the horrors of war and is mostly straight faced with little humor but is still a very engaging game with a big focus on gameplay and not much cut-scenes/walking sim like parts.The homages to numerous Resident Evil games through the games mechanics structures and characters was really well done. The game feels like a pretty interesting mix of stuff from Resident Evil 1 to 4 kinda but not in a copy cat or excessive way. Will warn the hardest first play through difficulty Veteran which I played on is very hard. I found this game much more difficult then RE games,Signalis, Tormented Souls, Alisa, and the like. Combat and guns will be a acquired taste but I really liked it, you have to be very deliberate methodical and strategic with guns and your placement and use of them.  Nearly every gun has to be reloaded or have the bullets ♥♥♥♥♥♥ after every single shot and fire very slow and slow recovery animation after firing with any heavy stronger guns. Similarly to Signlais the limited inventory mixed with a massive number of key items that are only used for progress and key items might not be needed for a long while gets very annoying and adds lots of artificial backtracking. Doesn't ruin the game at all but does take away a bit from it. While the rats are a bit much and a bit annoying I think they have been kinda overstated for how actually hard or awkward they are to deal with.The backtrack heavy second half and lack of inventory space with a lot of key progress only items feels like a much bigger issue then the rats personally. Also overall very good level design and light but fun frequent puzzles and fun optional puzzles and a ton of optional exploration.Like much much more exploration and side content then nearly any RE or survival horror like indie games.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: A legitimate review for this game.It's tagged as survival horror but it's not really survival horror so much as it is...survival.I don't understand why it's got horror labeled on there. Is it scary? I guess kinda. so maybe that's why?But regardless this is still a pretty legit survival experience. You play as a lone soldier stuck behind enemy lines after they took the trench-line you were stationed at.With gameplay reminiscent of Resident Evil you have limited backpack space, can combine items in your inventory, you have safe rooms with saving journals, a stash, and a merchant/companion there who can sell you stuff, buy stuff from you, or upgrade your gear which can of course be hot keyed and customized to your liking. There's no sneaking mechanic, or other survival mechanics like base building or status meters. the only meters you got are for stamina and health.The game's combat is a bit awkward and could have been better designed but it's not the worst I've ever seen. And that sound design is amazing.All-in-all in the game was very well designed. It has a few issues here and there, sure, but for the most part this is a safe and sound investment. A game that's NOT broken and NOT badly designed giving you more-or-less exactly what you were looking for or expecting from this game. I'm not into horror games but I AM into survival games and overall I thought this game was very interesting and very well crafted.It's worth its asking price. But please do NOT buy it's digital delux editions. It's not worth it and that kind of practice needs to die out already.But if you'd like a more in-depth look at the game then feel free to check out the review on my YouTube Channel (link below).Otherwise, thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

_childDocuments_.review: Essential survival-horror with minor modern tweaks that should not be passed by any fan of the genre.It can rough at times even compared to SIGNALIS, but I enjoy the gameplay loop and exploratory options. A few odds and ends can be tweaked, stamina maybe, rats, auto-aim with controller( classics use it idk), but for the price it is a helluva great time and by far the most terrifying game I've played in a long time as a fan of WWI, and not particularly scared by games. _childDocuments_.review: As a huge WW1 fan and complete novice to survival horror, the biggest honor I can give to Conscript is that I actually finished it, despite being bad at it. The authenticity and atmosphere of the setting alone were enough to keep coming back for more. There´s plenty of game here - 10-15 hour story with multiple endings, unlockable items and costumes that each add to the replay value. But be aware that the opening hours of the game are the hardest, as you don´t have that many weapons and your stats are low, but it only gets easier from there. My only gripe is that there isn´t a mark for fully explored rooms, which would help a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It is thematically and aesthetically interesting, but kind of a boring slog to play.So far (100 minutes in) it's just, not particularly good. Great premise, and I appreciate that (from what I have seen and heard) it stays grounded, and there is no mechanical hound or armored velociraptors (if you know you know) lurking in the trenches. The setting is not just a backdrop. Looks good. Sound is fine. Combat sucks. It's tolerable most of the time, but really you just kite enemies which is just so dull because even regular enemies are pretty tanky... a generic melee guy takes like 6 pistol bullets. The stamina mechanic makes sense I guess in theory but in practice does nothing but stop you from sprinting forever out of combat. Backtracking doesn't seem problematic, but seems tacked on for merely being a survival horror game. Certainly considering a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game since its conception when I came across the devs on Twitter. I've been keeping an eye on the game ever since, and let me tell you, it was very much worth the wait. As the description of the game states, it is a new take on classic survival horror in that there is not much in terms of the paranormal. It is more on the side atmospheric, the literal horrors of war, and psychological horror because of PTSD from war. The music is nice and at times, relaxing but has this somber feel to it, and the uses of the cutscenes are nice too! They have this dizzying, dirty, and visceral feel to them. The combat for the most part is fine. Although by the end of the game, melee (at least for me, and I was playing on Soldier difficulty) becomes largely useless unless you are going for a certain achievement because of the abundance of ammo that you can get, and if you are a person like me who saves all of his supplies, I made a ton of ammo thanks to all the chemicals and gunpowder I saved up. The game has a lot of backtracking but it is normal for these kinds of games. The biggest gripe I have for this game is that enemies' attacks can go through walls. Here is me thinking I can take cover behind another part of the trench to avoid the flamethrower guy's flame but phase through the wall and lit on fire! Or when an enemy's melee somehow smacks me through the corner of the wall. The rats can get annoying as well if you don't destroy the rat holes and/or burn the bodies of the enemy you killed. Dodging can feel a bit inconsistent at times too. Overall, it is a great game! Pairs up nicely with another WW1 horror that I really like called Amnesia: The Bunker! It would be really cool if the sequel/prequel for this game explores another army of WW1. Heck, even the Germans! 8.8/10!
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one because I do recommend it but there are a few negatives that were very pronounced for me personally.  The game's atmosphere, art style, sound design and concept are all amazing across the board.  The game proudly displays its love for Resident Evil and Silent Hill and also highlights such a cool setting for a survival horror and I think the only other game that has even tried this setting is Amnesia The Bunker.  Any fan of survival horror should at least try this game to see if it is for them.  I do not regret my time playing this game but I do feel that it was too long, the stealth mechanic is inconsistent at best and the stipulations for specific endings are kind of ridiculous.  I also did not enjoy the combat entirely, although I can appreciate what the game was trying to do it felt very inconsistent and the player is forced into arenas with waves of enemies multiple times which tends to feel like a slog rather than an intense experience.  Overall I do recommend this game but by the end of it I found myself feeling burnt out and will likely not go back for a replay soon if at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game if you are itching for a portable Resident evil with WWI and are not expecting anything else.It comes with a few negative points which are:-heavy backtracking during the later half of the game. not just any backtracking but VERY LONG WAY backtracking with very rare opportunities to unlock a door for shorter trips and they usually don't make sense because these shortcuts leads to room you know will leads to nowhere interesting. The first half had backtracking, but it was more fun to explore and more understandable to explore around.-jank aiming. your best odds of hitting is aiming in this order, up and down, left and right, then diagonally anywhere. Overall just try to not shoot diagonally unless you use a shotgun, it also influence trying to lit up fuels on the floor to burn bodies as i struggled to lit them up by wasting bullets at my first attempts, i favoured shooting fuel by aiming either up and down when i had the chance.-enemies line of sight is similar to a horse with blinder as they only see what's in front of them, they are also very deaf and easy to sneak up to.-the game has stairs and mud puddles that slows you down, but somehow enemies pursuing you are not slowed down by such things, i can't tell if it's an oversight or a way to say rats and enemy soldiers are just that better at stair climbing and in mud puddles than you.Then these are my personal peeves:-supplies in large quantities in normal mode, you might favour going through hard more right away-dark souls dodging mechanic, if you played old resident evil, it's another mechanic that make it even easier to avoid soldiers in tight corridor, the horror of world war one dissapear right away as you are already a master of evasion with I frame.(enemy kicks ignore I frames)Overall it's definitively a game to play for its original ideas despite being weighted down by it's own gameplay decisions, which you can overcome and master in no time if you give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of this genre in particular, this game nailed it. My first playthrough took me around 14 hours, which is an insane undertaking for primarily a solo dev. I play a bit methodically but even those focusing on speed will find a decent length ahead of them.*Great choice in setting, excellent sound design, punchy combat and tense atmosphere.*Light on puzzles and they're mostly easy, but a couple head scratchers in there.*Complete experience with in-game unlockables over loads of MTX and compromised gameplay.-Backtracking can occasionally be a slog since you're not sure when you may or may not need an item- such as the light or gas mask. Not as egregious as something like RE0 and the grapple gun- but you might find yourself short on inventory often when you're juggling 1-2 guns, ammo for at least one, key item(s), a melee weapon, the aforementioned mask and light, then maybe a healing item... and that's assuming you're not *also* carrying a grenade/lighter/fluid for the pesky rats.Some of the upgrades and valuable treasures are a bit back-loaded towards the end, such as 2 inventory upgrades in the last area. I think if those were spread out more evenly, or if you had at least 1 dedicated "accessory" slot separate from the main inventory for something like the flashlight/gasmask/lighter, it could alleviate some of the inventory woes. Or give treasures their own separate inventory a la RE4. As it stands, it's pretty fine- there is something to be said about the decision making of not grabbing an item the moment you see it- but if you like to travel even mildly prepared, be ready for quite a few item box trips.        I hope this game gains even more traction, it's well deserved for such a passion project. Can't wait to see what's next!(Also beat it pre rat-patch without burning bodies until the very last area when they seemed to come out in *force*)

_childDocuments_.review: Only about halfway through (I'm guessing) but so far its a pretty fantastic survival horror game and definitely a must buy if you love the genre especially resident evil, which it has taken inspiration from the earlier titles but still feels unique its not just WW1 but resident evilArt style is fantastic and the overall mood and atmosphere of the game is great, only real issues are the fact that combat can feel a bit clunky but you get used to it but the character movement does feel a bit stiff and you'll reach points where it feels like Andre is running on ice for no reason. I'm sure that stuff can get dealt with and none of it is a deal break. Wouldn't even wait for a sale its worth it at the price it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry, but despite being a big survival-horror fan I Really don't like this game...This game is a chore to play. You are constantly running back and forth trying to get all the items first to the item box and then to wherever they need to be used. The inventory management is a massive chore here, and I say that as someone that didn't mind it in SIGNALIS before they expanded it.The backtracking is insane and tedious. The maps are complex and twisting and turning and basic navigation can be a chore. Combat exists, but the closest it gets to being entertaining is if you manage to hit two guys with a shotgun blast.I guess there is a story, complete with flashbacks, but I really couldn't care less. Sorry...Trying to use WW1 as the setting of survival-horror was a novel idea. But I judge it to be a failure. This game is never scary. And while it is difficult to play, that is not because the atmosphere is traumatic, but because the game is agonisingly boring. Worse than boring, really! Painful to play!I haven't quite finished the game yet. And at this point I really don't want to.

_childDocuments_.review: "The horror, the horror"Conscript is something special, I think if you are a fan of old school survival horror games this one is a must buy. Intricate levels, puzzles, inventory management and everything else you'd hope to find. Using the atmosphere and setting of WW1 is a stroke of genius and I wish more horror games opted for unconventional settings/ideas.Praise:-Rich atmosphere-Mostly great puzzles and level design-Fun engaging combat-Really like how the horrors of war can make the enemy seem inhumane or monstrous -Lots of weapons to try out which is a nice throwback to RE4Some gripes:-This may be patched as of writing but the rats are pretty brutal on launch, they would have been tolerable were it not for the poison damage-The game is rather stingy with ink ribbons, granted I know its optional but there were a few times I lost 20-30 minutes of progress because I was avoiding saving. I don't think the ink ribbons gel super well with how often the player is expected to fight enemies and backtrack. Theres far more combat in Conscript than a classic RE game imo. -Got one of the bad endings SPOILERS: Because I went back to restock my items after killing all the enemies? I guess for some reason it triggered the cowardice ending by going back regardless. Kinda sucks but its not a huge deal.-I swear the golden pistol didnt shoot at times, not sure why8/10 Great time
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic old school survival horror game that should be experienced by fans of the genre. I was sold knowing it a survival horror set during WWI which has noticeably becoming a popular setting in recent years. Conscript brilliantly accomplished depicting the horrors and near pointlessness of the war.The presentation with the top down 'playstation era' graphics fit very well. The superb sound design really stood out to me more than I thought it would. The whistling shells hitting nearby and the clatter of your feet against clay tiles really pulls you in and builds that atmosphere. The overall map design for the most part worked very well and maintained a very satisfying game loop for anyone familiar with survival horror. I love seeing that map update with the rooms explored and which ones remain locked.I enjoyed the game a lot, but do have some minor issues I had that mostly stem from the "old school" nature of the game. I appreciated the additions added in recent patches (e.g. the truck) and think that there could be some other areas of consideration. I tend to err on the side of QOL rather than tedium. For me personally, I think it'd be good to have the torch light/lighter not take up an inventory slot as juggling the item + their corresponding "ammo" just adds a bit of unneeded tedium with the inventory juggling (given the ammo is already a limiting factor). Similar feeling with "key/important" items as for me it just ended up being a let's just run back and forth to the item box which doesn't really add to the game.Overall, the game is great so my hats off to the developers. I hope we will continue seeing more indie games of this caliber in the future. I look forward to more projects from you all. We need more indie games to showcase the talent out there as indie games are increasingly where I'm finding the most fun at.

_childDocuments_.review: Jordan Mochi, solo dev of Conscript, really managed to capture what made the survival horror games of the 90's so captivating (intense exploration with satisfying backtracking, inventory management, limited ammunition, safe rooms, etc.).It's a nice touch that he allows the players to personalize the difficulty by allowing unlimited saves and checkpoints or, on the contrary, by offering only limited ink rubans (oups, I mean pellets!) for the pleasure of hardcore gamers (which is the best way to experience the game IMO).It's also nice to have artist Survival Spheres taking care of some of the soundtrack, which always fits the action perfectly.To sum things up, we have a very good game that was crafted with a lot of talent and passion and that definitely shows while playing. I also appreciated some references to old classics like the door with the rope to burn in Resident Evil: Nemesis.I hope the game will sell well so that we can see more from this talented developer.Thanks for this bleak journey, Jordan!
