_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is a retro stylized survival horror, in the vein of old school Resident Evil games, but played from the top-down camera perspective. Its also mostly one-man project, 7 years in the making. I am happy to say its a resounding triumph in the survival horror genre.Conscript is very dedicated to its retro roots, but thankfully it implements a wide variety of quality of life improvements for a smoother experience. You'll be upgrading your weapons, expanding your inventory space and extending health and stamina meters throughout the game. Best of all: it will discard keys that have no more uses, single greatest mechanic introduced in this genre.I recommend playing this game on controller since mouse and keyboard controls are a bit weird and stiff. Combat in Conscript is surprisingly good for a top-down perspective game. There is a wide variety of weapons at your disposal and many of them require manual control of the bolt action mechanism to load next bullet, I really liked it and it added to the pressure of combat. Using melee weapons is just as satisfying and you can even sneak up on the unaware enemies to hit them for increased damage. Combat feels brutal and intense, with agressive enemies that beeline for you while raspily shouting in German. Overall oppressive atmosphere is helped by strong sound design and grimy, pixelated visuals of the whole game.Its hard to describe why this game gets under your skin so much. Graphics are one thing, but the feeling of danger is ever present, the soundscape is never silent, you can always hear some screams or explosions in the background and it keeps you on your toes. Enemies can ambush you, filthy rats will fill the corridors if you leave the bodies of killed enemies without burning them or blowing up ratholes. You will explore pitch black corridors, filled with deadly gas, with only tiny lamp lighting the way and gas mask reducing your stamina.Conscript constantly hits you with the horrors of war. There is no real jumpscares or supernatural themes and still it manages to keep you tense. Sometimes when you kill enemies they drop photos of their loved ones, its bloody haunting. Your crosshair will get increasingly shaky the more people you kill and the more horror your character experiences.I managed to get a 'good' ending and to be honest, it struck a cord in me I didn't know I had. Theme of pointlessness of war is nothing new and has been done before, but the psychological grinder Conscript puts you through makes you so vulnerable by the end, that I got a 'bit' emotional when the credits rolled.Conscript is a must play game for any survival horror fan or just for anyone looking for a tightly designed experience that explores horrors of World War I. I can't begin to imagine the dedication this game's developer Jordan Mochi has and I truly hope it pays off for him. Congratulations and kudos to you sir.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best survival horror game I've played since signalis which is one of my favorite games period. And knowing that one guy did all of this is insane to me. _childDocuments_.review: excellently blends the tropes of classic survival horror with a gritty, gut-punching narrative. The way the game subverts your expectations in organic ways, such as  Or how I did find there were some pacing issues toward the middle-late game if you wanted to min-max and pick every item up and play cautiously, however, in the first major patch pretty much all my gripes were addressed. As with any game in the  style survival-horror genre, it is still down to the player with how slow/boring and cautious/tedious they play, but it is entirely beatable playing as reckless and/or pacifist as you want. Given the various endings and freedom of playstyle allowed by the structure of the game’s obstacles,  suits itself well to multiple playthroughs. There is a weird tonal balance with how much deference the game has towards its subject matter, with a narrative that, while simple, is one of the most effective video game stories I've seen, and the gamification of some elements. To at one point have an emphasis on the real nature of PTSD and the mental struggles veterans experience, and then to also have achievements like "War Criminal: Kill 2 enemy soldiers with one shotgun blast" or "Who Needs Artillery?: Kill 4 enemy soldiers at once with an explosive barrel", I wouldn't call it outright offensive but it definitely feels like an unearned dissonance. I can appreciate the need for levity, and there are humorous moments in the game directly, such as the propaganda or some of the dialogue, but it nonetheless feels too game-y. Such is also the case with the merchant and the borrowed exchange of treasure for upgrades and supplies. The  games got away with the suspension of disbelief surrounding so many of its more absurd mechanics because they were often ludicrous zombie games about evil mad scientists and cartoonishly corrupt mega-corporations, it's all so camp. Having the same framework applied to something which seems to want the player to take it more seriously, at least in a narrative context, begs for a consistent approach. Not to say the game isn't allowed to be fun, or take video game-y shortcuts, as an act of respect for its portrayal of the harshness of war (although you could make that argument if you want this to exist as more than a commercial product). I don't feel as though  is intending to make a political message in terms of the validity of the war itself, or at least the individual agency of any one soldier, let alone a conscript. People had to kill each other, for the most part you are expected to kill NPCs in the game. And the game goes to lengths to show the mental effects of such a scenario. However, letting the player revel in the slick game feel of some of the weapons, creating obstacles where enemies just happen to be having a chat right in front of a mounted gun, it’s a bit too indulgent. Creating longevity and replayability in the game with additional difficulty modes with extra challenge, with ranking at the end of the playthrough, where each subsequent playthrough would have less and less appreciation for the tender moments the game has to offer and is instead a problem to solve as fast and efficiently as possible. Its as though the game wants to have its cake and to eat it too. Which, to be fair, is par for the course for video games,  is one of the best examples of actually investigating this dissonance, but given it feels to only go halfway is what makes it particularly disappointing in that respect. Overall, I would definitely recommend  if you are looking for a fun twist on classic survival horror with a great narrative. If you liked this game and are looking for more new survival horror, I recommend , if you haven't played it already, for its intriguing sci-fi narrative and similar love of the genre.If you liked this game and are looking for more games that integrate the player-character's mental state with gameplay, I recommend  for its tender narrative surrounding depression and self-acceptance combined with an excellent 2D platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: (TRIGGER WARNINGS FOR VIOLENCE AND WARFARE HORRORS)It's been said before, and I'll quote it again- "War is hell."Unlike other war-themed video games, however, Conscript does not not give any glorification in the process of waging war. World War I's European battles were a bloody and horrific affair, and the game offers not one iota of sugarcoating the inhumanity and terror that came with it. Yes, there are gaming aspects and acceptable breaks from reality- Bandages will heal your wounds instantly, and your avatar can take far more punishment over the course of the campaign than is within the bounds of reality. Guns can be upgraded for better performance, incentivizing players to ration rare gun parts for the boosts they really need.Beyond that, Conscript pulls no punches about the subject matter it covers. It doesn't add fantastic or supernatural elements, because it doesn't NEED to. Who needs undead horrors or demonic entities when you have men with spiked clubs, rifles, and flamethrowers whose sole occupation is to kill you and as many of your countrymen as possible? Why bother with sci-fi mad science churning out fictional superweapons when the horrors of mustard gas and trench warfare offer a much more visceral- and realistic- terror of man's inhumanity to man?Perhaps one of the most sobering mechanics of the game is what happens to the enemies you kill. Their bodies remain, attracting flies and, if specific precautions aren't taken, rats. Rats in Conscript are not simply things you can kill for a sidequest or sadistic sport- they can easily overwhelm you with a debilitating attack that whittles away health and can inflict disease that requires special, rare healing items to remove. The primary way to prevent rats is to toss a grenade into their burrows. The other way involves burning their preferred food- the corpses of the enemies you've slain- beyond recognition.Every aspect of the game shows the horrific conditions soldiers endured- your allies WILL die in battle and there's nothing you can do to save them. Being pursued by enemies through narrow trenches is bad enough, and then you encounter obstacles like mud and barbed wire that hinder your progress. Your avatar is not some military champion waging a one-man war- he's a conscript- just like the title says- a youth pressed into a war he had no say in, with the consequence for not charging headlong into enemy fire being execution for cowardice.Dreams come to the player's avatar in cutscenes of a happier time, and the filter and colors show the stark difference between a happy past and a horrific present. The past is lush, green, and bright. The present is brown, bloody, and the music sets the tone with themes that range from mournful requiems for a wounded nation to suspenseful horror and descending shepard tones to make it feel like your humanity and sanity are circling the drain, as you're forced to backtrack through familiar areas that become not only increasingly ravaged by artillery and fire, but filled with the corpses of allies and enemies alike.There were times after pausing a session of gaming in Conscript that I couldn't help but think- "Wow. There is something really wrong with us." Normally, one can dismiss a horror game as a work of fiction, but not in this case- Conscript offers not even the refuge of 'it could never happen in real life' to its players.Conscript takes inspiration from old style survival-horror games without apology- you have limited inventory, and true to the games from which it pays homage to, somehow a single key or lockpick takes up as much space as an artillery shell. The game does give you a very necessary break in the form of storage boxes that allow you to access a stash from any storage box you come across- the use of which will be necessary as you try to gauge the proper balance of weapons, healing items, and key items to carry with you. The game grants a further mercy in taking away key items once they are no longer necessary, leaving you with a much needed item slot for either carrying essentials or hauling back valuables to the merchant, who will trade you supplies for truly staggering amounts of cigarettes.Even the currency of choice adds to the horror. Money on the front lines is essentially useless to these soldiers- cigarettes, for all their damaging effects, at least provide some brief tranquility before facing another salvo.Combat in Conscript makes you ask yourself a question both philosophical and practical- is killing someone really worth it? Melee weapons will break over time. Ammunition is scarce. Every enemy you encounter- from the plague-carrying rats to the flamethrowing soldiers- is determined to fight you to the death, and killing enemies requires aiming shots carefully while dodging blows and running to minimize the drain on both health and resources. There are numerous times that taxing battles can be avoided by simply evading, hiding, or running away. And, of course, there is always the issue of the rats who will happily dine on any enemy corpse, only to chase after you to deliver debilitating bites should you get too close.The reward for successfully felling an enemy more often than not is that the enemy can't pose a threat anymore, with the few items that are dropped being very small amounts of ammo, cigarettes, or very rarely, gun parts. If the corpses fall in a place the player will have to backtrack frequently, they will need to consider whether to use precious fuel and firebombs to burn the bodies, or to simply run past packs of ravenous rats. In short, killing can cause more problems than it solves- the kind of lesson we as a species should consider learning one of these days.In short, Conscript is what it claims to be- a hellish portrayal of one of the grisliest wars in human history cast under the mechanics of old school survival horror- and it does its job very well. Perhaps, in the context of showing the nightmarish effects of warfare, *too well*.I do recommend this game- but only in measured doses.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth your while if you like old-school survival horror games. The game oozes dread from every corner of the trenches, and it makes the war feel as horrific as the Battle of Verdun was. Also, a pretty long game, should give you plenty to play, and some replayability (though a randomizer mode would be cool).
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Give the dev some credit, this is an incredible game. The top-down angle were blended pretty neatly with survival horror mechanics and the atmosphere. If you are a fan of old school resident evils and want to experience something similar yet still refreshingly different give this a go. For the price an absolute banger! I've yet to start a challange run or NG+ but my first playtrough had me hooked pretty fast. The latest changes also improve the game in certain aspects immensely even though i absolutely enjoyed it already before.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: This and Amnesia the Bunker are clear signs that we need more WW1 horror. The fact that this game has made me jump while not having any kind of zombies, ghosts, monsters, etc in it should tell you what you need to know. WW1 is scary enough in its raw form to be an effective blueprint for any horror dev to work off of. Conscript in particular, despite the art style, still manages to capture and punctuate the brutality of it all. Beating someone over the head with a shovel and then finding a picture of a loved one in their pocket just to burn the corpse regardless is what truly makes this a horror game.I waited on this for a long time and it was well worth it and Im hoping the dev can continue working on Conscript and any other projects he may or may not have planned for the future. Regardless, I think this game deserves much more attention than its getting right now.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Impeccable atmosphere, engaging combat and survival/upgrade mechanics and even has a bit of a heart wrenching story. It kept getting more and more intense, disturbing and hellish toward the end, i was just waiting for some kind of zombie or monster to show up.There were some parts where I didn't know where to go or some part of the level looked a bit confusing, but I enjoyed the game immensely.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: ~Signalis for the boys~Loving my time with CONSCRIPT, as of Act 4. The backtracking in Act 3 was a pain-point but the devs have released an update to help remedy this. I really appreciate how this game manages to make war a genuinely tense and horrifying experience. If you like Signalis and Amnesia: The Bunker, this is the survival horror experience for you!
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with lots of secrets that aren't too terribly hard to find along with good puzzles. The combat is really well made except for small bugs with shooting people that are really close (mainly the bullet passing through the enemy). The patches recently added help make the game less boring and less frustrating over unbalanced rats.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, reminds me a lot of SIGNALIS. Setting feels very heavily inspired by Amnesia: The Bunker (which I love greatly), whilst the gameplay feels like a unique spin on the classic Resident Evil games, with backtracking rewarding the player, optional puzzles, clever interactions and the overall vibe of the items (like for example including treasures that can be combined for extra value).The story is really amazing, the atmosphere is immersive and terrifying, especially in Chapter 5 and Chapter 6, and the overall presentation is wonderful. Despite pixel graphics, the world of CONSCRIPT is insanely detailed (I personally really like how one can see which item is laying in the world, despite the pixelated graphics, and the game puts effort into depicting it in an immersive way).Absolutely worth your money, especially if you want to enjoy a great RE-like game filled with secrets, puzzles, multiple endings and tons of challenges to satisfy completionists like myself.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: A gritty survival horror experience which takes the premise of war and adds a slightly surreal layer of intrigue atop it.There are some elements I'm not too fond of (an unavoidable ambush "cutscene" removing most your weapons, for example), inventory feels a bit narrow for all the "quest" items you're intended to carry, and some areas feel a bit like they're obtuse just for the sake of it - but these are subjective and at least some of these have been acknowledged and are being addressed by the developer.If you're looking for an enjoyable survival horror experience set in the trenches of the first World War, CONSCRIPT is an easy thumbs-up.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospherics and survival horror play make this good game great. Those who enjoy the Resident Evil franchise or Darkwood will recognize the format and feel at home. The developer is actively improving the game through post-release updates, so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and moans are being heard and addressed. It's overall a solid indie title that takes inspiration from classic survival horror games, adds an underutilized backdrop (WW1), and gives a balanced play experience which possesses excellent replay value. A final note and insult to fellow gamers: people that are complaining about the combat might be dumb; I found the combat to be intuitive. Spacebar allows you to dodge attacks... You can roll dodge through/around everything and there are somehow complaints about the game/combat being hard. Shoot, roll dodge, run, recock weapon, shoot - cycle of the conscript.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I watched someone play this game; it caught my interest, so I tried the demo. After the first 10 or so minutes, I decided I wanted to play the full game, so I bought it. After about 10 hours, I'm near the end of chapter two. I'm enjoying it so far. Have I found some parts difficult? Yes, but I'm still enjoying it. One of the main downsides for me, which they have patched now, was the rats.But I highly recommend the game if you are a fan of the classic survival horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is hard lol. by the end I was very desperate for health and the final area pretty much does not have any for you. not sure why some things were in the game, like the elephant gun, there's not boss fights, seems like a waste on the miniboss enemies. decided not to harm any rats this run and that was a mistake, no achievement aside from knowing the little fellas are fine, but I was not fine, they ate me alive frequently lol.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I was a kickstarter backer for this game years ago and I don't regret it for a second. This is the kind of game which when you play it you're genuinely surprised that no one has ever tried making it before. All Quiet on the Western Front meets Silent Hill with a great art style and fun gameplay. Guns are clunky but in a way that is very authentic for the time period. The game, while somewhat simple in graphics, makes up with an excellent creepy atmosphere that manages to stay authentic in the spooks and the historical vibe. While overall a great game, at the time of writing there are still a few bugs kicking around, some effects (like fire) can look somewhat cheap, some animations could use another pass. Extra variety in enemy types or weapons would also be appreciated - especially into the 3rd act.  But as a indie game made by one guy these can be easily overlooked in favor of a great addition to the survival horror genre, and a great addition to any history buff's library.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Great old-school survival horror that really nails the horrors of the Great War in a grounded and interesting way.Fantastic aesthetics and design, with solid gameplay and puzzles, especially for fans of games like Resident Evil and Silent Hill.Kudos to the dev for sticking with his passions and giving us an excellent game, I waited a long time for it and it didn't disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. Will this usurp the best in the genre? No. Is this worth your time? Certainly. A very impressive showing that gets gameplay and atmosphere done better than most games in the genre.Music and story struggle a bit, but aren't much of a hindrance. A lot of attention to detail went into making this game. Thoroughly impressed with the world they've created here. One of the best and most accurate modern PS1 retro games I've seen. That comes with good and bad as it carries with it hallmark styles of the past that I don't think are to anyone's benefit.But by and large a remarkable game that fans of the genre must try. Also, if you really care about getting the good ending research how to get it as it requires attention through your playthrough. And bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but that is accurate to how games used to be.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I really like a lot in conscript but i feel another few months in the oven would have done much good.The first 2 chapters are easily the best. you're weak and the world is always suprising you.The problem is that start chapter 3, the game has used most of its tricks and fails to introduce meaningful new ones. that and the problem of mid puzzles and a ton of backtracking, additionally if you do even a bit of exploring, you'll be overpowered by chapter 3\4. I love the games set pieces but rarely felt challenged or that the setpieces reached a dramatic high. Much of this would likely be solved if I replay on veteran but I wish the game would have done more to suprise me.I also must add that only 1 of the 4 endings is great and feels accurate and even funny in a way.But i still really like the game. The gunplay is excellent as well as the sense of discovery, specifically in the first 2 chapters and in the final one. I liked the characters enough but the selling point of the setting really works. I'd very much love to see a Conscript 2 where everything is expanded on.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I waited forever for something like Conscript and I have a lot to write about it but I'll try to keep it short.Great War setting with classic RE+RE4 game-play and similar to Darkwood for how it uses the ethos of commitment and punishment which makes me feel respected as a player. The audiovisuals are incredible and drenched in atmosphere. While playing Conscript, quotes from the book 'All Quiet on The Western Front' were coming up in my head all the time.The developer showed integrity while handling the Great War theme with tact in an unbiased (the exception these days) and empathetic way but also made sure to make one of the best experiences as a survival horror title out there.  You won't find this line of combination anywhere else, where setting and genre are connected so seamlessly.  It's the only work in this medium that touches on the Great War in a meaningful way and not for the 'cool factor'.There might be a few minor drawbacks for more younger players that aren't used to 90s frustrations or due to the 2D engine limitations but personally neither affected my enjoyment, just the opposite. This being a debut title from the developer makes any 'drawbacks' next to invisible to the overall quality. You won't see a problem if you're after true survival horror.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: hard but nice game :)resident evil meets ww 1.fun is not the word to describe this game :) for reasons but it is a very well made game. story is, as far as i know now, very personal an describes a soldiers "life" in one of the most brutal frontlines. a demand from the past... gameplay is resident evil typically. its good made pixle art and a tensive experience. enjoy this game and keep in mind our history ;)
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: An uncompromising and chilling depiction of the great war. A love letter to Resident Evil 4 in many ways, Conscript manages to carve its own unique identity while building on old classics that just work.An lovingly made indie with brilliant art direction, atmosphere, core mechanics, and story. Conscript is satisfying, eerie, and though.Some constructive criticism; the back-tracking can be somewhat exhausting at times, notably in chapters 5 & 4. This is something that becomes more apparent after finishing chapter 6, the last chapter in the game, where the game & level design really shines. Smart item placement and shortcuts make back-tracking feel needed and interesting, rather than a chore. Tiring back-tracking is somewhat exaggerated by the extremely limited item slots in the earlier chapters; do NOT get me wrong, I love inventory management and it is a crucial aspect of the survival-horror genre, but I found it extra difficult to keep my inventory a little open as to avoid backtracking to storage in this game. This is in part due to the fact that every item takes up the same sized slot, making the inventory "management" aspect of the survival experience a little hollow. This is what primarily led me to skip burning bodies all throughout chapters 1-4, because having 2 slots taken up by the lighter and the fuel was too punishing; simply choosing to outrun the rats was not a difficult task and somewhat nullified that mechanic. There is apparently a big with the "cowardice" gauge throughout the game, which leads to players (including myself) getting the coward ending even when they went out of their way to face and eliminate every single encounter (I wonder if running away from the rats builds up that gauge..).All in all, what a fantastic indie experience. I'm a pretty thorough player, and my first playthrough landed at about 12 hours; I would personally pay far more than $19.Congratulations to the team behind Conscript.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game awhile back on KickStarter and played a majority of the demos (not including any exclusive demo builds that were for higher tier backers) prior to the full game's release. Of all the projects I have backed I am very happy with how this game turned out! At the time of writing this I have only gotten one of the several endings to the game. Even after writing this I'm really looking forward to going back into the game and doing more playthroughs to get the other endings especially when the upcoming patch releases i.e. the patch meant to nerf the rats. Now I did have a few minor issues with the game one of which is being already addressed, but still worth pointing out that there are instances where some rooms will just have six rats on one corpse. There were points in the game thst weren't really clear on exactly what you had to do pr where to go. This kinda impacted me specifically because my experience with past builds where I didn't know that the room where you initially get the gas mask isn't filled with gas just yet but the color of the room at least from those previous experiences gave me the impression that it was so I initially avoided it. That's more on me than anything. One other thing and I believe that this was more of an over sight is that one of the final locked doors required three pronged keys. The keys looked all the same so I started thinking why couldn't we have used the first key just three times?  I had very little bugs that occurred in my playthrough which were very far between my play sessions. The first major bug was that when I accidentally selected the combine option on the surgical kit in the menu I was unable to exit out of the inventory screen or even do anything within that screen itself. Sadly because of this I did lose a bit of progress because of that. But this was the only game breaking bug that I had. The other bugs I had was sometimes, although this only happened like three or four times to me, the game will think you are pressing the attack button if you used your mouse before going back to a controller. I initially thought you had to reset the game but thankfully all I had to do was just click on my mouse again and it fixed itself. Another issue and this is extremely minor is that after beating the game and selecting continue it claimed that I was on my third run of the game and not my second. Not a huge deal but it was something I noticed. Othat thst that this game ran perfectly for me at 1440p at a locked framerate! Despite the minor issues I had a blast playing the game and I do hope we can see JD work on not only improving the game itself but also the possibility of additional content such as new weapons, costumes, enemies, story, etc. and possibly develop a series of games. It's genuinely a game I feel as though gave me a new interest in horror games set during major wars and historical periods. Conscript is absolutely a game you need to play at least once to see how much potential this dev has at making unique experiences within this genre especially if you're a fan of either classic survival horror games or new indie games that like to play around with the status quo to deliver something new and different from what you'd typically expect.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and gotta give kudos to the devs of such an unique and creative touch. Something I have never experienced before. The combat is really intense but it also gives that soulborne game achievement feeling,  There are some bugs here and there, and itemization still need to be improved. But overall this is a very niche game for its price.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game so far, gotten jumpscared a few times which I enjoyed a lot. I don't know how to report a bug but I wanted to say I was in the supply trench, shot a guard with a shotgun (not sure if it killed or just knocked them down), ran out of the area and when I cam back in the guard went from dead on the ground with blood to standing and not reacting to me. I  thought this was funny but when I shot another guard it alerted the glitched one and it was able to shoot me but I couldn't shoot it. Seems like the guard got knocked onto another plane but somehow lost its hitbox. Reloading the area caused the guard to appear dead again but he almost killed me when he was invincible LOL. Definitely not something that would stop me from playing though, just wanted to report to the devs, thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic and tone are pitch perfect. The subject matter, too: WW1 French armed forces at Verdun, is novel. There are some wrinkles, here and there. The aiming on certain weapons can feel a bit iffy. It feels like certain objects and enemies have larger hit-boxes than you'd expect, so I occasionally found myself hitting a corpse or a box when I was aiming for an enemy. One thing I didn't have an issue with, which several people do, is the rat mechanic. I thought of the rats like the Crimson Heads in Resident Evil 1 Remake: a consequence for deciding not to use a resource to properly dispose of a corpse. Also, I felt it did a good job of keeping areas threatening even after all of the soldiers have been dispatched. My only complaint is that I wish they had the same 'visibility' indicators as soldiers, so I could tell when I was about to trigger one. I Kickstarted this game, and I can say for certain that I do not regret it, and would definitely do it again if the developer decides to have another one for another game. I hope they continue.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: What the game does well: Foreboding and ominous, but never "too" scaryIt's longIt's beautifulThere's lots of weapons and items. Its somewhat challengingThings that you may like, but I personally didn't:You will get lost, absolutely, and be forced to run around like a headless chicken checking every area of the map to find out how to progressYou get an abundance of ammo. At first I tried to conserve it. Ended up getting to the final chapter and having hundreds of rounds saved up.Melee is basically ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (don't bring a knife to a gunfight)The enemies have fast interrupts in melee to stagger you, the player character can't do that.The rats are an omnipresent threat.Things I thought the game did poorly:There's six chapters, I got stuck on 3 of them. Chapter 3, 5, and 6. You will run around like a headless chicken, backtracking to every area of the map to find a new item. Some of the puzzles are so cryptic, they expect you to keep a notepad with you. I mean I get what you're going for but the execution is poor.You won't get the hidden ending on your first playthrough without a guide, you may struggle to get it at all. Again, it's so nonsensical. Your one clue that there even is a "hidden" objective is a watch being mentioned to you at the start of the game. Given the games length. You won't remember. It gives incentives for future playthroughs but it's just not for me.The game really suffers from the map not changing colour when you've looted a room. You're wearing your influences on your sleeve and not using some of the most useful features in the games you're inspired by. There is too much loot, too much ammo, gunpowder. Too many items for you to pick up. It makes the game too easy and you will spend time backtracking to store it all. With my previous point, maybe that's why rooms aren't marked as looted, there's too much damn loot.95% of the guns are terrible. All of the melee weapons are terrible. The only weapons that actually seem to do anything are the elephant gun, both the shotguns, the handcannon and one pistol. You're almost certainly not going to get the handcannon either on your first playthrough. Unless again, you have an incredible memory or you're willing to run around like a headless chicken.There's almost no reason to fight anyone. Fighting and killing enemies just makes the game harder given the amount of back tracking. You're best off just rolling away and running from every engagement.There's little enemy variety, two variants of germans with rifles, and what, 5 melee variants and a couple of guys with flamers. You can run past all of them and they're not worth fighting.There isn't a single boss in the game. Which makes sense, you're in ww1. However, towards the end of the game, it gets almost a little supernatural. Verdun looks much like the pits of hell. The final battle is started by some bestial demonic roar bellowing up from some burning abyss. The implication was cool. Where's our one fight against occulist boche?8/10 game. The best survival horror since Re4 remake/Alisa. Hopefully there's further updates and future changes. Game was a surreal experience.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute yes!It's a really cool survival horror game.The first play through was a lot harder for me, I've started the game with checkpoints enabled, but regret that because there is no real need, you can easily buy ink to save, and only a few part of the story have distant saves...I think I'll replay it in the future to unlock the other endings, and there are other secrets I missed.Well done, a really well made game!Worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute amazing experience! Does the survivor horror formula extremely well. The plot isn't strong but the message it's trying to get across, along with the atmosphere of the game and the environment, is very powerful and emotional. My play-through was about 17 hours and I did 100% map completion, plus the NPC quest lines. Highly recommend playing!The only gripes I had were: - The amount of back-tracing done overstayed its welcome by the end of the game.- The path to obtaining the secret/best ending isn't obvious or hinted at at all and that's EXTREMELY irritating! If you're thorough AND will only do a single play-through, like me, you WILL come across all the information you need for it. However, I, like many others I'm sure, thought it was just lore like most of the memos & notes you'll come across. Then, at the end of the game, you're expected to recall a couple of things AND THE ORDER THEY WERE PRESENTED IN in order to get what you need for the ending! This approach is fine for people who will play through again but sucks for folks who will 100% the game on first play only to find out they needed to remember something from 5 hours ago.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not normally a fan of top down games, but this is a very well made game that I deeply enjoyed. The setting, the story, and the art are all fantastic. It feels like a game made with passion and purpose. For enjoyment and to provide a message about how terrible and horrifying war can be. World War I is an interesting time period for me as well. It made the game all that much more enjoyable.It doesn't reinvent the wheel game play wise, but game play like it is tried and true. It didn't need to change up a great system of survival horror to do what it wanted to do. I played on Soldier, the intended difficulty, and found it challenging but fair and do able. I didn't get stuck or lost much. If I explored properly I found where I needed to go. Even managed to get the secret ending my first go around. Though I admit that was solely because I saw a tip about how to do so near the start of my run. I encountered very few bugs in my play through. I played it on my Steam Deck and only had the occasional bug of repeated inputs. Such as A the interact key being continuously pressed or one time the attack button. If you were to play on a more hardcore setting, like limited saves and/or no checkpoints it could be a bit frustrating.For me 10/10. I got great enjoyment from it and it has some replay value in the form of challenges, different endings, and unlocks. Like costumes, infinite ammo, and some secret weapons. I'm interested in finding out it secrets and completing its challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT is a fantastic survival horror game that is really atmospheric. The gunplay is great, as is the melee combat. The puzzles are about on par with others in the genre for me. The sound design is great and helps give a weighty feel to your actions and what’s happening around you. The game is tense, especially when you’re on the front and you hear whistles signalling enemies to rush your side. There is a nice variety of locations in the game but I wouldn’t have minded more of the game being set in the trenches or the front. However what hurts the game for me is the amount of backtracking, even though it’s survival horror. And often when you do end up backtracking after completing a puzzle the map may have changed and you only know that once you get halfway across the area and see that the route you had in mind has been blocked off so you now need to go all the way back around to reach the place you need to go. Overall I’d give it an 8/10, defo worth picking up

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast and love-letter to classic survival horror (especially older Resident Evil games with some touches from the modern games). The game's a mix of several mechanics from the series while establishing its own identity and having the great design needed to support it. I only have a couple of small gripes with the game that aren't too big but notable. The game has a decent amount of backtracking and sometimes will give you shortcuts to help curb down on re-treading old territory but they aren't too frequent. Until you've done a playthrough and learned the game you'll be spending a couple of hours going back to search for how to progress. A couple of items help alleviate this and the game gets a bit more linear later on but you'll really feel it in the large Chapter 3 area.Sometimes the hit registration can be iffy and I've had a fully aimed gunshot/melee attack miss an enemy, miss the explosive trap I'm aiming at or hit the wall next to me which can be a bit annoying especially on Veteran difficulty. Another common complaint I've heard is the rat system, but after a while I picked up how to run & dodge past them or have enough healing supplies to compensate for their hits, and the developers said the first upcoming patch will address them. Despite my small annoyances this is one of the best survival horrors I've played with a good amount of replayability and a great atmosphere. I highly recommend this if you're into survival horrors or the setting.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to review this game as soon as I started playing it but I made sure I at least finished the second chapter.  This game is a delight.  If you enjoy old school Resident Evil gameplay with a WWI coat of paint, this is the kind of game for you.  You're often frantically searching for the next key to move forward and juggling inventory slots, all the while you wished you had more ammo, more medicine, more save slot tokens, just more money to buy stuff from the merchant, I know I certainly wish the merchant had more medicineThe atmosphere is perfect, that feeling of being stuck in a never ending quagmire of the Great War, where weapons are that agonizing middle point between modern killing machines but still primitive enough that having to chamber a fresh round on a rifle feels agonizingly slow while a trench raider is running at you with a club.  Add on how wonderfully desolate everything looks and how rats and flies will feast on fallen enemies, with rats becoming an enemy, you truly feel like you are in the most miserable front of the warRats could use a bit of a nerf, but the developer already said he's working on that, so kudos(PS:  I can truly roleplay as a Frenchman by having not one but two opportunities to abandon my post)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game, and decided to start it today on the 110th anniversary of the beginning of the First World War. I'm only 3 hours in so this isn't a review of the story (which is so far so good).If you enjoyed Valiant Hearts or 11-11: Memories Retold then you will love this game. WW1 puzzle games is a niche genre but this game fits in brilliantly with those other titles. The crafting, looting and inventory mechanics are great here. This game really makes think about what you are going to carry around with you as you only have about 6 or 7 item slots. Combat feels very rewarding and can be difficult when you run into heavily armoured enemies with a   trench shovel for example. This add to the need of maintaining an effective inventory.  The ambience of this game is a incredible. The visuals have a very polished but retro style, reminiscent of the original Fallout games. The sounds as you are walking through the trenches are unnerving and puts you on edge constantly.I look forward to finishing the story, and already know this is a brilliant game and worth getting if you are interested in WWI or this style of too down, puzzle game. Will most likely update this review when I've finished the story.

Played vanilla before any patch/update, etc. without walkthrough.Pros:1) Loved the pixelated art, some are eerie depictions to show the horrors of war.2) Loved the soundtrack.3) Loved the voice acting, even though it's kinda minimum.4) What are you buying? What are you selling?5) Satisfies my itch for Resident-Evil ish games, but in isometric pixel style.Cons:1) Assloads of backtracking. I knew puzzle sections are a must in these kind of games, but holy hell the terrains are too much to handle, so many winding roads, and dead pathways that block your road to the destination. With limited inventory, you have to backtrack and backtrack again if you get the key items.2) Rats are too annoying. I understand the setting for "bad hygiene" setting, but they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gang up on you worse than the human enemies themselves. I heard they are getting a nerf soon in the future.3) Double the backtracking if you have to look for fuels and lighter (again and again) to burn the enemy corpses so the rats won't bite your sorry conscripted ass. The fuel item SHOULD be available in merchants.4) My eyes kinda hurt using default gamma setting, even though I already use that flashlight item thingy. _childDocuments_.review: Conscript is not what I expected. A top down survival horror game, it really does a fantastic job with the gameplay loop of exploration and item conservation. Combat can be a bit tricky, but running away is a very viable option for most if not all the game. What surprised me was the length, my first playthrough comes in at about 10 hours. And there is still so much more to do; multiple endings including a secret ending and new game+ being the prime examples.My biggest gripe with the game is that I ran into multiple points where I had gone through the entire map and had no idea where to go next because I was missing something or had not run into a door/obstacle so it had not been added to my map. The worst time this had happened, a route that was available to me the entire time seemed inaccessible because of how the terrain looked. Another time comes when I was looking for a key, and I had gone to every room and done as many things as I possibly could, but I could not progress. Turns out the key  was looking for was hidden in a fountain after I had turned the water off previously, but I had no way of knowing that. All in all once you get past these little issues the game is awesome! I look forward to going through it again and trying for better rankings in my next playthrough!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game since it's first reveal in 2020 and been anticipating it ever since. Played all the demo releases and always enjoyed them. So how is the full game? So far, been one of the best games of the year, especially in horror. I'd say all the hard work paid off big time. Imagine my surprise when I gunned down a soldier, only for him to drop what I thought was ammo, but instead was a photograph of his DOG. Immediate regret, but that's the beauty of the game - you're just a soldier fighting other soldiers in a horrific war, and these people are and were in fact real people, not just monsters. Speaking of which, the OG version of this game back in 2020 had monsters in it, but I don't even miss the fact that the dev decided to axe the monsters. The game is still super unsettling and the music, puzzles, and environments are very reminiscent of classic horror games. Definitely scratches that itch that I had for another classic RE style game. My only real complaint are the rats, but the dev is nerfing them in an upcoming patch. This game is also fairly long and highly replayable! 7 hrs in an maybe just over halfway done from what I can see. Perfect 5/7 game, buy it now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far, one of the best depictions of WW1 that I've seen. The amount of dreary, miserable environments paint the war as what it should be; 2 sides fighting over piles of bodies. Gameplay wise, it's very fun, and leads to interesting decision making when it comes to dealing with enemies (rats will mess your day up). It's also deceptively long. After every chapter I kept saying "oh its gonna be over soon, this is the final battle", only to end up continuing, often into a whole new area, just as dense with story, items, puzzles and enemies. My only complaint is if you don't plan ahead with inventory, you run out of space often and end up having to backtrack a lot, which isn't too bad in the trenches, but when you get to the larger areas you end up spending significant time running around. Overall, I definitely recommend if you like survival horror in any capacity

_childDocuments_.review: Conscript is truly an impressive game. The game's setting is absolutely perfect for this genre and I must say is one of the more interesting explorations of World War 1 in a game. The "Horror" aspect of the game is far from the traditional sense of a horror game, and is much closer to an experience of the horrors of the First World War, yet I feel this has made the experience of this game that much more noteworthy. The atmosphere in this game is perfect and the creator of Conscript has done a really good job of making it a claustrophobic and tense experience for the player. I have to admit, the combat can be a bit clunky at times (sometimes its hard to tell whether a wall offers cover or not or what is in line of sight of your range weapons), but I am sure tweaks will be made to reduce this. If you are a fan of survival games, or WW1 games in general, Conscript is definitely worth a play

_childDocuments_.review: My first real experience with the survival horror genre, and it's been an excellent introduction. The tone and atmosphere here is grim and harrowing (in a good way), really reinforcing the horrors of experiencing WW1. Gameplay is pretty difficult if I'm being honest, and might be a turnoff for some. I've been really struggling to make solid progress, but I'm learning to be less aggro and take my time to save my health.Important things to note that the game doesn't really explain:-WW1 firearms often require you to manually cycle the action, meaning you have to press reload between each shot for things like the Rifle, Shotgun, and Revolver. Don't get caught out!-Burn bodies, especially in indoor areas. The rats will come out as you make progress and they're really difficult to fight, so it's better to get rid of their food so they don't show up in the first place.-The Killzone-looking guys can kick you while you're in your dodge roll, which causes damage.

_childDocuments_.review: CONSCRIPT is a survival horror game that takes heavy inspiration from the older Resident Evil and Silent Hill games. Instead of being trapped in a mansion with zombies or a foggy town filled with monsters, the player takes the role of Andre Hiver, a young French conscript during the Battle of Verdun. When a German assault traps Andre's brother Pierre behind enemy lines, Andre must navigate one of the bloodiest battles in history to save him.As this is a survival horror game at heart, supplies will be short for most of the game, until you've got a good stockpile going. Inventory space is limited, like the games which inspired this, so you'll have to get used to running back and forth from the item box, or make some hard decisions about what you can take with you.Combat feels good, generally, but can sometimes be annoying. It's designed to be tactical, forcing the player to choose when and where to engage enemies. Andre must ready his weapon before he can shoot/swing, which roots him in place, and some weapons (Revolver, Bolt Action Rifle, and my beloved Pump Shotgun) need their next round to be manually chambered by pressing the reload button. Reloading new rounds into a weapon also roots Andre in place, so if you're running low with multiple enemies coming at you things can get hectic. But overall I found the combat serviceable, and even enjoyable at times. Some situations can get annoying, like when an enemy or enemies force you to constantly aim, fire, relocate, and repeat while they take half a dozen bullets to the dome before going down. The weapon upgrade systems alleviates this, and being able to craft additional ammo can help offset supply issues, so playing smart can reduce your headaches.And like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, Andre will come across a lot of puzzles. Some of these feel vast, stretching over most of a chapter (Of which there are 6), and this is possibly my biggest gripe with the game. If you come to a point where you don't know what to do, the game grinds to a halt as you search every last corner of the map for the next puzzle piece. There is very little guidance on what your objectives are or how to achieve them sometimes, which clashes with the urgency of the story. Utilize your map, and exhaust every possible doorway and area transition. Eventually you'll find the one item you need and things will open up, but a little guidance would have gone a long way toward making these sections less tedious in my opinion. The game looks great for a pixel art game. In fact, this is probably the closest someone can get to recreating World War 1 in this style. There's mud, there's blood, there's fire and chaos... and at the end of each chapter you're treated to a flashback that is full of green, orange, blue, and so many vibrant colors that clash with the dreary trenches of the Western Front. It's a great contrast, and gives a lot of weight to the battle as you see how Andre and Pierre lived before the war and establishes a brief but effective history for their family.Overall, I really liked the game. If you're interested in survival horror or the First World War then give it a try! I'll definitely be playing this again to try for a different ending. Even when it would get frustrating it wasn't that long before I found the way forward (And sometimes it was just me being an idiot, as I usually don't play these kinds of games). It has some really great set pieces in it (The ending of Chapter 4 was my favorite part, kudos to Jordan Mochi for that sequence!), it maintains tension while trying to survive with limited supplies in the gas filled trenches and flooded shell craters of 1916 France, and despite the simple concept I was invested the story and Andre's quest to save his brother. Fair warning, this game is fairly bleak. It's a good game, but it's not a happy one. It's about The War To End All Wars, after all.Oh, and watch out for the rats! The little bastards are more of a menace than the Germans.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: (TL;DR at the bottom)If you like games like OG Resident Evil, Silent Hill, or any other classic survival horror, you'll likely love Conscript. It's an impressive project (especially for a solo dev) that's a love letter to the icons of the genre, while also being a great game on its own.The world building and atmosphere are immaculate, the music is haunting, the sound effects and voice acting are amazing and add a lot to the combat and ambiance of the world, and the art is gritty and dark. It's the perfect environment to convey the absolute nightmare that WWI and, more specifically, trench warfare was.The puzzles are more than just "run around area and find code". There are times where you simply have to find a code for a lock or something, but usually that's only a piece of another, bigger puzzle leading you to the next step. The player actually has to think about the task at hand to piece together the solution, and when you figure it out, it feels rewarding.Mechanics inspired by its influences as well as newer ideas I haven't seen in many other games are implemented in a way that make the game a rather engaging challenge. These mechanics change up the resource management of classic survival horror in a unique and interesting way. If you want to go in blind, skip to the next paragraph, but one great example of this resource management is how many enemies you kill. Each kill takes a small toll on your character's psyche, and if you simply slaughter everyone you see, your crosshair becomes more shaky. You can still use guns effectively with full shakiness, but it will definitely impact your accuracy at long range. To avoid this, you can either avoid killing where you can, or use certain items to help for a time. This balance of action and consequence really set the game apart from its contemporaries for me as you actually see the consequence occurring in real time, it's awesome.It's also a lot longer than I thought it would've been. Not to say that one is better than the other just based off length, but my first run of Signalis (also a great game btw) took me around 5 hours iirc, and my first run in Conscript took me around 14.There were two bugs I encountered, like problems with enemy AI, and one CTD, Others have encountered a few more, but the dev is already working on getting them fixed and the patch is going live one week after today according to patch notes.At times the level design can be a bit tedious. This is mainly in the second major area you get to in Chapter 3, but there are times where it can be difficult what you can and can't walk over, or otherwise couldn't traverse. It's not a big problem outside of this one specific area, but it does get a bit grating, especially when you take backtracking for supplies/new items into account. For me, not a deal breaker, but something that did feel a bit annoying to deal with.Lastly, I want to give a shoutout to JD, the dev of the game. He's very active in the game's discussions, both engaging with conversation, and taking feedback humbly and gratefully. He's has already shown that he's listening to the community with the first set of patch notes, which addresses some balancing issues the community agreed upon and fixing the bugs that have been reported. It just feels great having a dev that actually cares about the game they've made.TL;DR - Game good, 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: A great survival-horror game, that also isn't quite a survival-horror game. World War I is an underused setting overall, so this was a unique experience I loved. It handled the historical material well, making sure to never hold back on showing the horrors of the war, but also not making light of it or adding in cheesy mechanics. I would call it a very tense, suspenseful game rather than outright scary, but navigating dark tunnels while hearing the thick gasmask breathing of patrolling Germans can stand up to any other horror game monster. Mechanically, the game functions well enough but has some rough edges. Aiming can be touchy, rats can be hit hard, and the classic horror-survival tropes remain such as limited inventory (combo'd up with keys and ammo taking up their own space). I enjoyed the added challenge, but others might not appreciate these old school details, so worth a mention. TLDR: A big recommend to any survival-horror nut, and a soft recommend to anyone will to try a different type of war game. Especially at this price point.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: While I don't think this was worth the 4 year wait on my wishlist, it's still a fairly accomplished top down survival horror, with the neat twist of avoiding anything supernatural or zombie involved. There's a handful of different chapters that actually give the game a decent length, 3 of which tread the same ground of the trenches, essentially acting as the main "mansion" esque area of the game, and 3 other areas, 2 of which were well done. I only think chapter 3 was the misstep with it's really annoying layout and slow progression.The combat is pretty neat and mixes up old school "clunky" gunplay with some stamina management and evasion. The aiming is a little obnoxious in an intentional way, which is fine for most encounters, but absolutely infuriating when it comes to meleeing the rats and shooting exploding barrels.Level exploration is standard RE/SH stuff. Find a succession of locked doors, find keys, progress onwards. Fairly easy puzzle solving. Lot of backtracking and item management, but not to an obnoxious degree like Signalis was.Stealth is also a main component of combat here too, which is neat, but also very clumsy in practice, to the players benefit. Enemy sight is so limited and binary it's just way more efficient to clear 80% of the enemies with one hit from a shovel. As for my major gripe, rats are the worst mechanic in the game. A complete misunderstanding of what made the crimson heads in RE1 interesting. The game wants you to decide which dead bodies you will clear so as to keep rats from spawning in those places. And they are a menace. The thing is, the way they function makes you want to actively avoid interacting with them. So you basically just run past them instead of engaging with any of the mechanics, like burning bodies or grenadine rat holes. It's just too much busy work.But at the end of the day, there's not enough of these games anymore. And this is a welcome addition to the top down SH niche alongside the likes of Signalis, Heavendust ,Lamentum , and this year's Crow Country.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I experienced a game crash bug in the Isolation room of Fort Vaux. Pulled my sweeper out, shot once at the dastardly German, and bam, crash. Lost about an hour of progress and still a little miffed. But considering it was just the one crash, I'm still happy with the functionality of the game.We really have a golden age of survival horror on our hands, and it's mainly thanks to indie devs putting out stellar entries. From Alisa's whimsical charm to the sleek, sci-fi terror of SIGNALIS, and many others that I haven't gotten to yet, I have had the pleasure of enjoying hit after hit that belongs to stand alongside the greats, my favorites of REmake and the original Silent Hill.So, what does CONSCRIPT bring to the table? A marathon through muck and mire, a gritty journey through trenches, wastelands, and cavernous forts. It works both to its benefit and detriment, but I'll get into the details later. For now, just know that if you like survival horror, CONSCRIPT should be on your list to play. It handles the genre near masterfully, with only minor complaints that fade away near the end of the game. At $20, you're getting a 12-15 hour experience for your first playthrough (mine was 12 but I died several times, plus the crash) and a slew of costumes, endings and weapons to unlock/upgrade through later playthroughs. It's well worth your time.Now, lets get into the specifics. Some spoiler-adjacent things talking about conditions to get endings, but I never actually spoil what happens.First, I'd like to point out a little confusion with the ending. Despite never abandoning my post in any defense segment, I received the 'Coward' ending. I clipped out of bounds rolling away from a flamethrower in the core mantle defense. but I was able to exit and reenter the room. That's really the only thing I can see as doing wrong. Was I too slow? Did I use too many healing items? Did I not kill enough enemies, despite the casualty report marking over 200 dead? I even insisted that one soldier go to the front in chapter 4, and killed him when he refused! While I was always going to replay the game for all the endings, I was left a bit confused and disappointed when I received the ending.On the subject of endings, please, *please* add Pierre's journal to the memos. I understand why this might not be possible as it's randomized, and now that I'm going back through the game I know what I need to do, but players know to write the code down, and have no reason whatsoever to write down what pictures were in the journal. I understand, it's a secret ending, and it's certainly less obtuse than SIGNALIS's secret ending, but I still think it's strange that we can't just have Pierre's journal in our memos despite it being a 'dream'.My ending complaints aside, chapters 5 and 6 are phenomenal. Chef's kiss level of survival horror level design. We're talking Spencer Mansion, Midwich Elementary-level depth of exploration and opening up the areas. Okay maybe not Spencer Mansion but it's hard to beat that. I do believe Chapters 2 and 3 drag a little bit, with 'rooms' in the trenches and specifically The Road that just feel too long. Puddles that only exist to make you go around (of course, not counting the ones that block off paths you unlock later) just made me feel like the game was forcing me to take the long route around enemies when I could still just run right past them, just 10 seconds later.As for enemies and combat in general, CONSCRIPT's enemy AI is quite dim, which is a good thing. Survival horror enemies should not be hard to fight. This isn't Dark Souls; combat doesn't need to be important. However, it is quite satisfying to bludgeon a soldier to death with your trench shovel. Enemy variety is good, with a lot of melee based enemies and a few different rifleman types. Gunplay is... well, it functions well enough. Aiming feels awful but actually shooting is quite satisfying. Just like the melee combat, every hit has substance, and the sound design for the shell casings, reloading, etc. is all fantastic.If you're looking to shoot as little as possible, just run from most enemies. Melee units are usually too slow to react, and even if you get hit a couple times passing by, you have plenty of heals by the midgame if you're exploring and picking up treasure. I didn't even bother to use my fuel and lighter much until Chapter 5 and especially in chapter 6, when you'll be going back and forth through a lot of short corridors that you don't need rats annoying you in. The rats really aren't that bad; you get an abundance of heals and Andre runs fast enough, especially with some stimulants in his system and the fresh puttees equipped. Huge recommendation: buy them as soon as possible and equip them for the rest of the game. They didn't leave my inventory, alongside that first pronged key which was in my inventory for nearly the whole damn game.The story is solidly good. You've seen these story beats before; a WW1 story where a young soldier descends into gradually more chaotic environments while searching for his brother and delivering messages through his trench. That's 1917, not CONSCRIPT, but close enough. That's not to knock the story; finding a child's drawing of a soldier marked "Papa" in a destroyed school got me choked up. It's just that the game tells us more about Pierre, our protagonist's brother and guy we're looking for, through several dream-flashbacks that just show how talented and cool he is, with little characterization of Andre. Anybody with a brain knows what's gonna happen to Pierre unless you get the secret ending (probably, I haven't gotten it yet.)Secondary characters are fun and likable, but just like in any other survival horror game, you hardly see them. Marcel isn't much different than, say, that STAR unit you meet at the beginning of Sierpinski in SIGNALIS. Likable, intriguing, even, but I don't expect them to make much impact. Medic is best boy though frfr, and I would give Gaston 500 cigarettes.I guess that's about all I have to say. If you read through all of this rambling mess of a review, thanks. I hope you enjoy the game, or that you already enjoyed it. Is it just me who only reads reviews *after* I played the game to see who agrees with me?

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I've backed the Kickstarter campaign a few years ago and the game turned out even better than expected. Conscript doesn't do anything new but it delivers on every aspect and wraps a survival horror game in an unique setting for this genre. Positives: - Game is fun and engaging from start to finish- Good pacing with a few hiccups. Everytime it starts to get boring something new happens- Level design is interesting and it is fun to explore the world- Great atmosphere- Good variation of locations (more than expected)- Not too many puzzles and the ones that are there are quite good- A lot of content. My first playthrough took me about 12 hours (explored as much as possible)- High replay value (different endings and challenges and NG+)- Very polishedNegatives:- Pacing is good overall but especially in chapter 3 and 4 a lot of backtracking disrupts the flow- I don't mind a bit of backtracking but the level design in some chapters together with the limited inventory space lead to me walking between storage boxes and single locations that require a key or special item way too many times. I wouldnt be suprised if 1-2 hours of playtime was spent on backtracking alone- Leaving bodies in the open attracts rats that will attack you on sight. The solution is to burn the bodies. There are two problems with the system. 1) It is not always clear in which area the rats are active. Sometimes I can leave bodies and nothing happens. 2) To burn bodies it is required to carry two items at the same time. In a game with limited inventory space I don't see why someone would waste two spaces to maybe burn a body that may or may not attact rats.
_childDocuments_.name: CONSCRIPT

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this to release for the past 5 years and I can say without a doubt that It's not so often a survival horror game like this blesses the community. The overall amount of love and passion that has been poured into this project is insane and you can see it oozing everywhere ! If you are a fan of Resident Evil, Classic Survival Horror or War Horror then this is the game for you. It offers some pretty d**n tense and crazy scenarios, I can't even tell you how many times I died and had to do certain sections over again yet I could not resist the urge to grab my controller and try again. The classic and scarce items and inventory management systems make themselves at home in Conscript and it's done incredibly well imo. I've not even come close to beating it but It's one h**l of a thrill ride so far! 10/ 10 would recommend homies, be a soldier and survive these crazy as h**l trenches... IF YOU DAREEE ;) !!!

_childDocuments_.review:
CONSCRIPT is a survival horror game inspired by classics of the genre - set in 1916 during the Great War. CONSCRIPT will blend all the punishing mechanics of older horror games into a cohesive, tense, and unique experience.

In CONSCRIPT, you play as a French soldier searching for his missing-in-action brother during the Battle of Verdun. 

Will you be able to search twisted trenches, navigate overrun forts, and cross no-mans-land to find him, and ensure a home goes unbroken?

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this title since the very first game, I was extremely pleased to see it finally come to PC. Although not everyone's cup of tea, I'll provide some pointers to anyone less familiar than I;Graphics - 5/10 (Passable, not great, but fine for a lower-budget cycling sim, little to no change year on year)Gameplay - 8.5/10 (A few issues regarding difficulty I'll touch on after, but overall they have made significant improvements through the years to the point where it's very natural and very fun, with tutorials for those less experienced)Modes and in-game - 9/10 (There is genuinely so much to do, whether you want to create your own rider and get from a cycling noob to a Tourmalet king, or create a team from scratch, or use a real-life team, there are so many things to keep you wanting to play!)My main issue regarding this game in particular is the difficulty is either way too easy or way too hard at times. I struggle to get away from the peloton at the start of a stage to form a breakaway, as despite being over 20 minutes down on the General Classification, I am somehow a threat to them and they chase me down brutally. All this for them to run out of steam on the final climb and end up 3 minutes behind me. This hasn't been as noticeable in previous iterations on PS4 so I cannot say for 100% sure if this is a real issue or not, but for my hours of play it has persisted. (Will update review after I play more if this changes) I also believe that this game could do with some integration with Pro Cycling Manager, I can only dream of going from sitting back and managing the team, to hot-swapping into the saddle myself for the closing stages of the Tour!All in all, providing you get past the initial difficulty of learning the mechanics, and hitting the difficulty sweet-spot, this game provides an excellent strategic challenge, and can be one of the most tense and exciting sports games I have played as a result! The achievement of getting a rider from a 65 overall, to finally pulling away from the pack on Mont Ventoux 3 seasons later is a feeling that few games replicate as well as this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Few things to say:- No energy management by AI - They either go full out until blow up, or basically stop riding so they can regain energy. Simply stupid to see on some mountain stages where peloton goes hard for like 15 km only to basically stop for final 3 km before summit.- Predictible - after riding like 3 TdF you can easily tell where breakaway is going to be caught, where breakaway can actually go away, what time will breakaway have at specific moment of stage(!)... (amazing "blockade" on some stages on 5 minutes mark, like 50 km of racing when time difference neither goes higher or lower than 5 minutes). Heck, on almost every single stage there is a certain "scenario" going on. And it repeats every single TdF. Fun, for sure...- Stupidity of AI - Yes, AI in this game is simply stupid. F.e: Direct Energie "chasing" breakaway for first flat 60 km on Colombier stage... with all 8 riders... not letting breakaway having more than 30 seconds. No matter how many riders are in it or what riders...  Only to have one of TDE riders to attack after it and join breakaway. Yep. Every. Single. Time.- Create your own rider - Yep, that's negative. If you want to do so, buy PCM, not this game. Stat increase is basically impossible at higher difficulty. And I mean only Champion by that. You pick climber for example. When you reach an amazing 68 in mountain, the only way for this stat to increase is by either winning mountain stages(!), or winning at least 2nd category climbs(!!). I want to ask anyone who was creating this game. How you are supposed to do so with rider with 68 MO? You can't increase your stats unless you're winning. Can't win having that low stat. And no, decreasing difficulty isn't an option. Unless you want to play on amateur and win Tour with... I don't know... Ben Hermans for example.- No crashes of riders. At all. I completed like 50 different TdF so far. I saw only one rider having crash. One. And it was most random crash I have ever seen in my life.- Real time weather (rain / wind) is basically non existent. Oh, you say there are some sectors with potential wind? If only it was possible to actually do something in those sectors... like splits for example. I don't know. - Comments on breakaway runners are NEVER correct. Including riders not riding in race at all.Surely there are much more things to add... Is it worth it? If you are cycling fan... Maybe, yeah. If you want to buy this game for creating you own cyclist, buy Pro Cycling Manager.Leaving thumbs up, but if it was possible, I would leave like... "Meh".

_childDocuments_.review: At it's best, Tour de France 2020 is actually a good game.  But as much as I'd like to sing it's praises, in it's more or less 'finished' state this year I cannot.  This series still feels more like a tech demo than a finished game.The main game modes (Pro Team/Leader) set you up for failure, because at first you have access to so few events that you can't achieve the ranking you need, unless you achieve unrealistically good results for your relative team strength.  Even then, you're still at the mercy of the simulation in races you can't compete in.  And in pro leader specifically, getting your rider into breakaways is a nightmare, especially when the peloton adamantly refuses to let a larger group dangle.If you get through the early game hell, what you're left with is still a game with less depth than Cyanide's other cycling game, PCM.  TDF does have an advantage in gameplay, as well as how it handles race day condition (seriously, what were they thinking with PCM 20?), but PCM is simply better when it comes to everything that happens between races.Even then, TDF wouldn't be getting a negative score from me if not for the fact that the developers recently gave the console versions of the game a major update... and failed to provide that update to PC players.  I don't understand why we were denied this update.  We're paying customers just like the console players, and maybe multiplayer was too hard to implement on PC this year, but surely they could've at least given us the rest of the update?Unfortunately, that lack of support sapped my interest in trying to overcome the pro team/leader early game and have fun with it.  If you still want this game, try to get the console version.
