_childDocuments_.review: I don't often give "No" review.. And I really did TRIED to like this game (I like strategy game, and look at my hours played), I went through the entire thing, and my final thought is: I felt like I've wasted my time here, which I shouldn't have.. (Writing this so you don't have to)The game started ok, but get boring and tedius soon at about mid game.. The moment you are able to recruit Tier 3, you've probably already checked the rest of the units and seen all the game has to offer. And if you know what you're doing, your team is probably already pretty OP too and most battles are just chores (I'm playing at Brutal difficulty). There aren't even much strategy involved, you could just use 1 same team and do every battle (occasionally swapping 1 back row maybe), it's just a click-fest.. My Avy can insta-kill 2-3 enemies with crits (easily maxed) in the first turn at late game.. Oh and the DLC is just adding even more OP units that you definitely don't need.. Really nothing to lose (except your time) without it.Exploration and items are also unrewarding and boring, almost all treasures are just randomized useless equipment or resources that you don't need more...  The city building part & resources management too felt like brain-dead filler to waste the player time... You just go there to click every level like playing a mobile game :/Dialogues and story is decent but not very exciting, some of those choices feel very out of place to me especially those that allow Avy to tried romance random stranger / monster lol... Then the main story, the true ending is locked at New Game+... I have a bit of interest in that but ultimately can't justify spending more days & hours on it just to grind through the same tedious stuffs, the game length should've been much shorter for that.The art and music are probably the only few things that are pretty well done here, environment and units looks fine. Some of the characters though.. Are reused model with added effects (which really cracked me lol, I don't care how the game try to phrase it, it's obviously due to laziness).. Man, the moment I saw Avy's mother model.. Am I playing a custom Warcraft 3 map or what..?Conclusion (4/10): Do yourself a favor and skip this one if you like challenging and satisfying gameplay, there are definitely better similar games out there (I have fonder memories of playing old King's Bounty than this). Unless if you prefer an easy game + time waster, you can consider giving it a try on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A good-ish turn based combat RPG,  that has some similarities with HOMM and Kings Bounty but not quite as good as either of those two.  It’s a bit Eurojanky, and the UI could use some work (way too many menus to wade through to do simple tasks), but it's fun nonetheless.  The difficulty isn't too bad as long as you play it smart, most of the time.  I loved the dark theme of it, there’s orgies, lots of murder and torture…even spleen collecting!  The characters that can join your party are engaging and their voice acting is quite good.  I especially liked Ejamar the necromancer:  “Death is close!”   It takes a while to understand the city building aspect and the four factions you’ll be interacting with the entire game.  Overall, it's a good game with challenging combat and interesting quests...definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: + Fresh take on the series+ Ability to play with units from different factions and mix it up + More relaxing than previous entries with no pressure + I appreciate the change of colors+ The dialogue is terrible. This is a big con because you just do battles and dialogues in this game. I usually like fantasy stories but the dialogue here is terrible in trying to be excessively sadistic and bizarre in a desperate attempt at making the game seem very hardcore and very dark with no real reason behind it. It seems like it was written by children for teens. Absolutely terrible, unrealistic and very immersion breaking. Good story and characters make a fantasy game believable but here it detracts. + You are very limited in terms of unit choice. At the beginning of the game you can choose only one unit from each of the 4 factions instead of having access to all of them. And they are all melee. Say goodbye to making an army of archers like in Disciples 3 or other combinations. After 10 hours I barely unlocked (based on choices that you do) a higher tier for one of the factions and it was still just melee. It takes a really long time to unlock things and based on your story decisions, you might not unlock them at all. This means either a lot of saving and reloading to get faction alignment options in story decisions that you did not like or not unlocking the better units. + Shallow game and progression. Press a button to get all resources, shallow characters, not much real progress for your story, relations or gameplay. I really appreciated that they choose a newer art style and wanted to make the game more accessible and more relaxing. However, the main problems relate to repetition and lack of quality.You will quickly be doing the same grindy fights with the same units mopping through terrible dialogue. Speaking of the terrible dialogue (and I am huge fantasy fan), I don’t know how they ended up trying to write such excessively sadistic-horror stories that it completely destroys all sense of immersion, realism, fantasy and likeable characters. I will give an example. You take some quest from random people to do random vengeances. When coming back to turn in the quest, the guy died because of some vengeance. Get loot and that’s it. No continuation, no relationship building, not much going into details, no mature story, no meaning, nothing.Then there are these bizzare stories of sadism without any reason that do not add anything to the game but just randomly detract. Dark fantasy is ok when it has some purpose not just random exaggerated violence. Weird random sex encounters. Meet some undead or some animal in some random place and you have an option to have a ‘romance’. There is no point to this, no relationship building, no animations, videos, interesting writing, nothing, Just weird abrupt unbelievable romances in silly places that add no value to the game. I am actually a fan of romances in fantasy games. Take the Witcher, Dragon Age Origins. Even hentai games for 2 bucks have done it better. Here, the things are just odd. At the time of writing this review, it seems that a good number of people are enjoying it if the Steam algorithm can be trusted. However, I caution that this game is pretty low quality. It does not really have an identity and does not really excel at much since the gameplay quickly becomes too repetitive and the rest is pretty basic in it.I recommend carefully reading reviews and watching gameplays before you buy since the game is very mediocre at best and depending on your tastes, you might not stand it.

It was alright but alot of things were jarring or just plain out of place. For example, especially in the early game, there are alot of bizarre voice acting choices, Some of them amazing voice actors totally miscast, others just kinda bad all round [Luckily this problem doesnt extend to the main cast!] . The story and characters start out kinda flat, [Orion is quite litterally a nothing character and every companion up to this point is more anoyying then fun] that was untill Greyleaf. In Greyleaf we meet Ejamar and are introduced to the many undead that inhabit this world, and this is where the game begins to shine. Ejamar is a insane Necromancer whos died many times,  killed many times and brought back just as many undead, We also get sent to this soul dimensions/prison thing with him. Now its during this soul dimension part that i really began to enjoy this story, We meet a Werewolf character here and I choose to have some romantic times with him, I wont spoil it but the sweet moment that happens after really showed me the potential this writing had. From then on this game grew and grew on me, Having lots of moments just like that, characters like Ejamar showing a deeper side to themselves, characters like Orion showing that theres more underneath the surface, Humans lying while demons tell the truth.Eventually most of the games problems either sink into the background or disappear entirely, Orion for example does get  character growth and the voice acting gets less bizarre the further into the game you get. But the combat dosent, ill be real theres alot of good in the combat, its fun, BUT there is so much of it and it isnt that fun that i want fight after fight after fight, because its a boring system, there isnt any mastering it, what you get at the start of the game is what youll get 20 hours in ( btw the game isnt 80 hours long they just expect you to play the entire game twice for a slightly different ending, no thanks I downloaded a save file for that ending).Heres just some final thoughts,I dont know if it was just me, or because I liked Ejamar and Sharlea so much, But most of the main cast kinda felt boring to me aswell, The demon lady and Druid were cool tho. The choices dont have much of a lasting impact, they more so impact that moment in time and then are left aside every time jump. I enjoyed this world and the various characters within it, this was a overall fun game. I hope if any future installments get made they build apon the best parts of this game. Id say this game is a solid 7 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Disciples: Liberation has a lot of good features - it has a lot of content, high quality world-building, questing and storylines, very solid voice acting and some interesting base building, army composition and faction alignment mechanics. I also enjoyed the 'conquer' ability in battles which let you automatically resolve them as a victory if you strongly outmatched the enemy army. I really liked the personalities of the various companions and the in-game decision making and its impact on the units you could recruit was excellently designed.However, the majority of the gameplay in Disciples: Liberation is comprised of the tactical battles and these did not sufficiently hold my interest to justify recommending this game to others. The maps the battles are fought on change only very slightly each time. The enemy units and tactics are rarely sufficiently different to warrant changing your own tactics or overall strategy. I only found myself modifying my starting line-up or gameplan a handful of times during the 60 hours or so of playtime and these were often prompted by unlocking higher tier units rather than necessity to adapt to a new situation. I also found that the lethality wasn't that well balanced (at least on Hard difficulty) and this further reduced the scope for setting up tactical positions as the length of fights was typically very short if you wanted to win without losing units.I really liked some of the elements of Disciples Liberation and I did enjoy the game for the first half of my playthrough but the lacklustre tactical battles eventually just became monotonous and dampened the experience significantly. I would not recommend this game unless you really don't mind grinding through a sea of battles which play out the same way every time. I would rate Disciples Liberation at 4.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a bullet point style review to talk about the good things and bad things of Disciples: Liberation.DISCIPLES 2 -  This is NOT a follow up to Disciples 2. Yes, that's disappointing because many of us adored that game. HOWEVER, this is still a good entry into the Disciples catalog, even if it doesn't mimic the second game. If you can put that to the side, you might like what you find here.GRAPHICS - This game is gorgeous. Every environment was clearly crafted with care. Tons of beautiful little details in the environments. The models of each unit look great - you can really zoom in on them and appreciate how well done they are.  Likewise, zooming in and watching the animations of combat is really satisfying as well.SOUND/VOICE ACTING - The original theme is great. This game doesn't have a ton of tracks, but what's here is well done. I did wish there was some variation in combat music because it got pretty old after a while. Sound quality overall was excellent, lots of satisfying audio through combat, spells and environment ambience. The voice actors here were all clearly very talented. Some of the direction of that voice acting was occasionally strange (e.g. a well established and clever demon sounded like a little old lady which I thought was odd) but despite that, the voice acting is quality. Ejamar was a particular favorite, his random maniacal cackles were a delight every time and the way the voice actor delivered every line was just *chef's kiss*DIALOGUE - Dialogue was mostly great. However, one of my biggest issues with this game is the side dialogue among your party members.  You might enter a new area or pass by a notable landmark and your party will have something to say about it. These conversations are NOT voice acted, but shown through text. That text pops up in the lower left hand corner of the screen and is small enough to be easily missed. By the time I'd notice my character was having a conversation, I'd have missed part of it and there was no way to repeat it.  It's just flavor, but if they went to the trouble to put it in the game, I wish they'd make it harder to miss.DIFFICULTY - I've seen this particular complaint pop up a lot in negative reviews and a lot of people think the game is too easy. I am guessing that likely these reviews were made while in the first act of the game because frankly the first act is fairly easy. It does get more difficult. By the third act of the game, I lost a lot of units in battles.STORY/LORE - The lore is RICH. There's a lot here, it's interesting! The problem is that there's an awful lot of it and there's no lorebook. There needs to be something to reference, because it was easy to get lost in it a bit. A lorebook would have served this game well.The story of this game felt disjointed. Between the first 25% of the game and the last 10%, I was fairly confused about what my real purpose was from a story standpoint. I do think they tied it together in the end so that it was much more cohesive, I just feel something was missed here with the storytelling. And time is VERY vague. At some point in the game I realized that what I had been playing was meant to represent years passing. And I didn't get that sense AT ALL from the storytelling. I have read that subsequent playthroughs will offer more story.GAMEPLAY/REPETITION - Gameplay feels good. If you've ever played any of the Might and Magic games or other Disciples titles, you'll know what to expect. Combat flows well and I like that between battles you traverse the map and gather resources, etc. It's a solid gameplay loop.  The problem comes in with the main complaint I keep reading - the repetition of the battles. There are far too many trash mobs/battles in this game. My playthrough landed me at about 77 hrs of played time and that was using the conquer function whenever I could (when it worked, more on that later). Frankly, that's too long for a game of this nature in my opinion. Even moreso because this game was designed to be played more than once. Without spoilers, this game was 100% intended to be a multiple playthrough game. And though I mostly enjoyed my time with this game, after 77 hrs I don't really feel like playing it again. I've read that subsequent playthroughs are a lot faster though can't verify that myself. Looking at how many people beat the game on Steam (the end game achievement currently sitting at a mere 15% of players), it looks like a lot of people might agree that this is too long. I think eliminating more of the random battles might be a good way to cut down on some of the time on this.The other complaint I've seen is that there aren't many units in this game and on that I disagree. There are four factions, each of them with four tiers of units and each tier with multiple units. There are plenty of different units to battle or use. There are more than 50 units in this game though, so truly the variety is a non issue.ROMANCE/COMPANIONS - I love romance storylines in my games. So when I saw this would include romance, I was so excited. I absolutely love getting to know my companions in games. Uncovering who they are and what their history is. Romance aside, this has good character building. Every companion here was interesting and fun to learn about. I've said it before, Ejamar was fantastic. I see a lot of love for him in the community and for good reason. Also Illmeren really grew on me. I think at first she seemed quite stereotypical but I love where her character development took her.Specifically the romance? Very underwhelming. It really boils down to 1 scene. There's a little tribute at the end of the game for your romance but aside from 1 significant moment in the game the romance is barely present. In fact, after meeting the romance option I took and immediately expressing "interest" to this character, the next time I spoke with my companions it was hinted at quite strongly that he was interested in another companion. And then romance never came up again until later in the game when you have a nice scene alone with your companion of choice. And that scene was good, really well done, brings you some more insight into that character. And when it's over, it's like it never happened. Your companion never addresses you like you have a special relationship or anything. That was disappointing. In this way, the romance felt very tacked on. BUGS/CONQUER FUNCTION -  I encountered very few bugs in this game. I had a bug 1 time where I was stuck on the victory screen. I also had a bug a few times where the top unit turn order bar was out of sync with who was actually having a turn. It happened maybe 3 times and ultimately had no bearing on my gameplay. The one BIG problem I encountered I don't think was a bug, but rather a function of it's design and that's the conquer ability.In the game, there is a button to "conquer" a fight without doing the actual fight. The idea behind it is when you were well out of the level of that group of enemies, you could just defeat them instead of doing the fight. I love this idea, because as mentioned above, there are too many trash mobs in this game. The problem is that by the 3rd act, the conquer function only seemed to work effectively about 25% of the time. Plenty of times I should have been able to skip a non story related battle and it just wouldn't let me. I went back to an older map to look for something I missed and had to battle groups of enemies that were 25+ levels lower than me! Why?  I think this function should be more consistent. It's a great idea and I love it's inclusion in the game.TLDR - Disciples Liberation can be a fun, well done entry into the genre. It's not Disciples 2 Redux, but what's here is solid enough to stand on it's own. It runs too long and battles can be a bit tedious, especially towards the end of the game. Despite that, it's still one I'd recommend for gamers who like the turn based battle games and interesting companion characters.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  I'm having a blast playing.-Pros   - Fun Gameplay:  Similar pacing to the old school games (Disciples I, II, HoMM) but with a twist on the mechanics in a good way.   -Music is good.  -No real bugs to speak of yet, and runs smoothly.  -Graphics are stylistically different than it's predecessors (speaking of I and II) but I'd put them in the decent to good category.  -Overall I'm having a very enjoyable experience.Cons:  -Not a strong con but there's an auto resolve battle option to save time if you have stronger forces, that may at times, be slightly generous.  But, as I said, it's optional.  Some people may love it and at times it's undeniably handy.  -The voice acting is, at times, on the lower end of mid tier.    -Sometimes character models are reused.  Mostly it's because those characters that you're speaking with fall within the same archtype that can be recruited but it would've been nice if plot characters, or the companions' art, was more varied than the standard recruit.If you liked the older Disciples games or are a fan of the old Heroes of Might and Magic titles then I'd certainly encourage you to pick this one up!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a bad game, but not a good one either. Really mediocre.Many pointed out that the game is too easy and doesn`t feel good for that reason. In my opinion the difficulty is not the problem, but the fights are boring. Games can be easy but still engaging and interesting. These fights are both too easy and boring. A really bad combination. This really shows in the first boss battle which is just a slog to wittle down th bosses health while there is no real threat.To elaborate on this: Some game mechanics are not well thought out. I compare this game more to the Last King`s Bounty The Legend (I haven`t played any Disciples Games before). In KGTL fights were also easy and one could certainly guess if you could win a fight or not. But it was important to minimize casualties. Here in DL the game uses singular units instead of army stacks. That way it doesn`t matter if your unit is almost dead or at full health. At the end of a fight you just use one of the healing shrines. There is no preassure to play good in the fights. I was able to just brute force my way through, even not taking one of the overpowered mage classes. And if I manage to loose some troops it is really easy to recruit new ones and train them to your level.Then there is some lost potential with unit abilities and army composition. In theorie there is a good and solid mechanic. Your units have one attack ability with various effects, one special ability with a cool down, most often a passive ability and a back line ability. The back line is a 3 slot system where you can put units which do not activly fight but rovide buffs or debuffs and auto attacks. So there is the potential to mix and match your army for different strategies. But I wasn`t forced to do that. I played with the demon horde as my main army. But I guess it wouldn`t be so different with elves. Yes there are different abilities and preferences (range or melee). But every army has ranged, melee, tanks and so on. The game didn`t require me to think of a special killer combo setup. Also some abilities are clearly better than others even on the same unit Tiers.Then mst battles will be one with almost no casualties. So there is the option to skip easy fights and well also hard ones. The Coquor ability lets you do this. But if you implement a game mechanic which lets you auto win boring fights doesn`t that show you that there is something clearly wrong with the fundamental game mechanics? The fights are the meat and bone of the game. You work your way up in the Tiers to get new interesting units and you want to use them. Just to see that they are not that special and do not change your gameplay much. Most often higher Tier units are just better and more powerfull. Don`t get me wrong, there are some cool units. The Demon ugraded Succubus which fire arrows and heal your inits for damage dealt are cool.And if I am speaking of higher Tier units let me say ssomething to the pacing: I am a slow and methodical player. And I don`t skip dialogues. But it took me around 30 hours to finish the 5th map. And the Tier progression is hard locked to finsih this map with the first boss battle. So until this point I was stuck with Tier I and II units. Only after this battle could I use Tier III units. The highest Tier is IV. The Tier III units are cool and more interesting But it was a slog to get there. The pacing is not good. Also the usage of different faction units is tied to a faction standing system. I wasn`t able to manage to get two faction to the required standing to use the Tier III units. Only for one faction. So even mixing two different faction units ist out of the question for at least some more hours.And soon I realized that using Tier III units is not that much different than T I and T II. Most have more AoE attacks. But fights often gollow the flo of using your cooldown ability whenever ready and only considering using it for maximum AoE effect. The AI uses all abilities as soon as they are ready, not even considering if they double buff the same units, which don`t stack for example. So fights are still boring. You move up, pop your secondary ability and use the rest of the fight your standard attack (which is an ability in of it self, granted. So it has different properties like damage tye and secondary effects.). The fights are most often done before you can use your cooldown ability a second time. There is no real tactics involved: No need to wait for the best moment to pop your cooldown ability. Also the cooldown abilities are often either som esort of damage ability or a heal or buff. More could have been done here. Maybe tone back secondary abilities and only have normal attacks but make them more nuanced and like a signature attack. Incorporate some of the secondary abilities in the normal attacks. If most of the fights you are using the normal attacks anyway. Thst way units of different factions could be more nuanced and factions could be more refined.Some quick thoughts:Graphics are good, unit design is cool. Albeit a bit glossy.Sound and music is good. Voice acting decent to good.Story writing is mediocre. Some companions are just to eager to join you besides slaughtering their people. It is just ticking boxes, talking to them and triggering secondary quests all at the same time. Also it is a bit strange that you can kill faction armies while at their respective army camo and still talk to their leaders?!?The romance option though are sometime really hillarious and often cringe worthy. Just use them all the time for fun. I mean getting on with an undead werewolf in an afterlife prison is kind of cool?!?Also most of the spells are useless. Your main character is the only one who can use them. Many level 1 spells are only single target. Why should I buff one unit if I could use another spell which buffs all my units? Or damage a bunch of enemies? Here is a problem with action efficiency. If my spells uses my one atttack action, the spells should be equally important.In the end even with all the criticism I still had fun but I wont finish the game. I played till shortly after map 5. If you have a lot of spare time and don`t mind an easy game, this isn`t a bad buy. But if your gaming time is limited and you want a good experience I wouldn`t recommend this game.It feels as if it has this potential to be great, just around the corner, just some hours more. This feeling got my until 35 hours. But not further.

_childDocuments_.review: Disciples Liberation fails to deliver the Disciples gameplay we used to love back in the day. The game even shifted its genre and it is not a turn-based strategy any longer, now it is more of an ARPG with "tactical" combat. Overall I did not like the game, the gameplay, and its length. I love big games but this one overstayed its welcome very soon given what it has to offer. So let me say a few things about Disciples Liberation.On a positive note, the game has the Disciples vibe and atmosphere. The world is still very dark and depressing, a lot has happened after previous games. The game looks nice, nothing WOW about it, but it is fairly decent, especially maps and bosses. Music serves its purpose, it is OK. Story is bearable even though it has so many nonsense points, but on a grand scale I can see the idea and it could have been good with proper writing.Now let's address the bad things.- Gameplay is completely changed, no end of turn and enemy actions, basically the world is static and you just glide through. Resources are collected on an hourly basis. Much loved unit upgrading system has been replaced and all units are generic and look like reskins of each other. This alone is enough to disqualify the game from the Disciples genre.- The game starts poorly with a horrible tutorial, the UI is hideous, I never figured out how to know just how much damage my spells will do to the enemy.- Voice acting makes me feel ashamed to listen to those people who just read the lines. Dialogue is so poorly written that I have no words, and there are just some lines so stupid that you read them in disbelief. For instance, you are in demon infested lands and demons have some sort of festival, and they hire you to take care of some animals that might attack people coming to the festival. Are you for real? I mean who's attending this festival, kids? It is in the heart of demon lands, there's fire and lava all around you and there are visitors to the festival, they come for music, food and drinks. Come on...- In general the story has been ruined with modern writing, the fantasy elements are overshadowed with casual language that is used in daily communication IRL.- I am stunned by who was the creator of stealth ability in combat, I have never seen a more useless ability.- Game does not provide any sort of challenge from start to finish, I played on Hard difficulty and most of the fights ended in round 1 or 2. Combat is also very boring, generic, you do not need to think even for a second what to do, just click through it and you'll win. Animations are painfully slow so even at 300% speed, a single round of combat takes forever. AI is so scripted that it always chooses the same actions, there's nothing to surprise you or outsmart you in combat.- The idea that you do not choose a faction but rather have a favour system with them all and then depending on your relationship with them you will have different unit tiers available really doesn't work well in my opinion.- And so on and so forth...I have so many more negative things to write about this game but I'll stop at this. I did not like it, I do not recommend it, I spent a lot of time on it because I liked previous Disciples games, and I really can't consider this one a true representative of the Disciples franchise. It is a very boring, over the top long game that does not deliver on any front. Good thing I purchased it for the price of a cup of coffee, but even that is too much for this disaster. Just skip it.

You would always have a "main hero" in the other games as well, but most of the skills in the skill tree were passive and didn't impact that much the gameplay of the hero.It is also a first to be able to mix and match units of all the races. Lore wise, it doesn't quite makes sense for me. Especially since you just start with them, they are just "there" and you can recruit them. I would have prefered to have to meet the factions and that there was a good reason to be able to recruit units from all the races. Exemple, I don't understand why a holy soldier would fight next to a possessed or a zombie, but Nevandaar is in shambles, so who knows... But apart from that, it is super fun to mix everything and try combos. Lots of possibilities here.Story is also interesting, it got me curious and I want to see how it develop. There is clearly some morale choices and some "good" and "bad" decisions that will impact your character. I am not very far for the moment, so hard to tell.Overall, very happy to have bought this one and can't wait to continue my journey. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for October 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before November 1st, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A tactical battle game, which feels like Heroes of Might and Magic Disciples: Liberation is an RPG with a tactical battle system where players command their characters and units to take on enemies.  The game starts with an assassination mission but then changes quickly to an attempt to build a home for the characters requiring the characters to form alliances with different races.  The story here is pretty interesting as well. Disciples Liberation has a good system where players have to hire units from their base and use them to fight in the battles, and units who die will be permanently lost. However, I had more of a challenge keeping my main character alive, though that won’t end the game.  There’s also a controversial “auto win” when you overpower enemies, which I prefer, but I know people disagree with it. Pick this up if you like turn-based tactics games, especially those on a hexagon grid.  This gave me a hard nostalgia for Heroes of Might and Magic but this feels like it was done right.  Though where most RPGs are about the story, people will have to look more to the combat here to decide if it’s right for them, which is why I’m showing it.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Ok... so... I want to like the game. Loved the series so far and been playing it since first game. The thing is... this is unfinished. Like super, super rushed. And for some reason I can't see any reviews saying that (maybe they are and I just missed them).Played for like 10 minutes and some things were obvious to me:1. You can't use mouse to pan / rotate combat map left or right. I mean... really? You can do it by keys but... come on.2. You can't rotate any map using mouse (you can pan the world map outside dungeons, but still no rotate).3. Some quests are voice acted, some are not. Ironically not even the main quest is fully voice acted. Come on guys... I didn't mind in older games when nothing was voice acted. Is fine, I get that, I get what to expect. But the first 3 dialogs are voice acted... then a main one is not... then you start a map and the first quest on the map is not... then another one is. Is a mess. Just cut voices at all. At least I know what to expect. This "is but is not" is just terrible.Game has been out for a while now, please fix this. Or mention it somehow. I thought my files are messed up or something. Repaired the game like 2 times, switched to french, checked my drivers... does that seem like something I want to do when I finally want to relax with a game after a full day of work? Put a note somewhere. A warning.There are some good things that are mentioned in other reviews. But surely this doesn't worth full price. Game has great potential, is beautiful (although in a different way than the others in series). But... yeah. I'm super disappointed by lack of finishing touches.I'll try to see if the story is captivating enough to keep me going. The start is a bit cliche but is not bad. Haven't lost all hope but... come on. Slap an "early access" on it or something. Anybody who ever played a decent game can see that this is NOT finished.Update after ~20h of playing:The story and overall feeling are worth playing. Ironically the voice acting gets better later in the game (less non voice acted quests). Is rather sad since ppl may actually leave the game before getting to those parts (I was really close on doing that). So... yes... the game is worth playing imo (if bought at a discount and with an average amount of patience)... but... I still have a sad taste of "unfinished" in my mouth and lack of early access / unfinished label is unforgivable.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit that i am confused how this game can have such a good rating to far. The campain has no difficulty setting and the normal (and only) difficulty is way to low. As long you dont try to fight a level 20 enemyteam while you are level 2, you shouldnt have any problems finishing the encounters, what makes the fights a pure drag since you simply spam the attack button over and over until finally all enemys are down, with a little bit of heal in between if needet. If you are looking for any deep strategic value you will not find it.The Story and Presentation is horrible, you start as a mercenary, to then teleport out of nowhere to a different plane, to then suddely try to liberate the whole land etc...the pacing is totally off but what is even worse is the dialoges. One + Point is that most of the dialoges that you have with your companions are voiced...with the big drawback that at least the english voiceactors are doing a horrible job, but what makes the dialoges even worse is the text itself. I played quite a lot of games, where the dialoge and the characters dont take themselfs to serious, like the Dungen Keeper or Tropico series to name a few, but the dialoge isnt only not taking itself serious, but it does it in a way that is neither funny, nor interesting nor anything good. It really feels like the game was written by a 10 year old Kid who is exitingly writing his first "Badass Story its gonna be sooooo epic wow" and i cant remember if i have played any game where the dialoge puts you so much out of the experience, then the dialogue of this game. The menus in the city also look very half backed, with ressource gathering that happens in realtime and slowly fills a bar, that you have to collect before it is full otherwise your buildings are not producing anything...it looks and feels in many way like a mobile game, with big and slow menus you have to press to upgrade just a single unit, weird menu placement that clearly shows that it was developed for a console first and ported to PC and in general nothing really clicks. What is left is a graphicly quite nice looking game, that did ignite my hunger for a successor of the wonderful HoMM franchise - but this game is neither it, nor is it a game that i would recommend to anyone. Especially not for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I rate Disciples: Liberation among one of the best games i played in recent years. Best part of this game is certainly it branching story. It actually matters what choices you make, they affect your companions and state of the world after you finish the game. Even tho not all dialogues are voiced, there is a lot of them and they add depth to your journey and relationship with companions, so you feel little bit involved and attached to what happen to them, similarly to for example Mass Effect. Quests often have unexpected endings and clever twits, I often found myself to reloading game just to see what other choices in would affect.Overall gameplay and combat is mix of RPG and turn based combat with simple management of you home town. Combat mechanics are intuitive and simple to learn and satisfying when you manage to win. Also spells and abilities are very nice visually and you can fell their impact on battlefield, especially ultimate abilities that you unlock in later stages of the game. One downside of combat is that there is a lot of it and it gets tiring towards the end of the game. Units that you hire are split to 4 tiers, however you will reach tier 4 long before the end of the game and it would help to have at least two more tiers, since for almost whole last third of the game you fight with same party and against same enemies.One thing to consider is immense length of this game, if you have limited time to play. I have done main campaign, all companions quests and roughly half of side quests and i ended up at almost 65 hours, and you can basically double it since game contains also possibility to go to new game plus to replay it.Overall Disciples: Liberation is very solid game with strong storytelling and fun gameplay. Technically it runs smoothly even on older hardware (gtx1060) and i didn't encounter single bug during playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Though not a terrible game I think it's hard to recommend. It's nothing like previous Disciples games.It is too janky, too drawn out, too imbalanced. And the story and dialogues are just too terrible. The game would need an overhaul for me to recommend it. At least in the gameplay department, but let's go over it in more detail:Bugs and jank:Your character often doesn't really do what you tell them to, they either won't move or move to a false position. Mind you, this is only in the "exploration" area not in actual combat.It's a minor nuisance, but really irritating.Bugs also exist. From the inventory menu suddenly not being displayed any more to reputation rewards being the opposite of what they should be (get positive rep? You lose rep with that faction ... sometimes) to buffs not being applied, like the reputation buff to morale. My units were still "neutrally motivated".Gameplay & Combat:Fine-ish for the most part, though imho deeply imbalanced. In the overworld you will meet enemies way above your level ... and sometimes way below your level. At least you don't have to manually fight the latter, but still. It is irritating to constantly have to backtrack, especially since you can only choose ONE map to go forward. Yes, you can travel back to other maps and your HQ, but you might just be stuck on a particular quest or battle ... and then you're well stuck, soft-locked so to speak. Unless there's something I haven't noticed. I never did speak to Orion when the game didn't force me to. Maybe you can select different maps.But what is the point in random enemies just in front of the quest battle being 10 levels higher, while the quest battle, a battle you HAVE to fight, is 10 levels lower? I don't get it. And level is everything in this game. While there are 4 tiers of units, their level is what really matters. I also don't get why MY tier 4 units get like 2,000 HPs, while the enemy's same units get 9,000 HPs ... that seems ... excessive. The problem with combat is that you start out REALLY weak. Your main character can barely tank 1 hit. Whereas around level 40 to 50 she just becomes a massive menace. But the general combat focus never changes:You need lots of healing, and only a few units can heal. You need lots of taunt, but only a few units can taunt (and survive the onslaught). And preferably you have lots of AoE, because for some WEIRD reason most or all AoE attacks in the game deal a lot more damage than single target attacks. To the point where it's not even funny anymore. Take a vampire into a group of enemies and watch ...This is particularly vexing if you've decided on focusing on 1 (or 2 at most, more just isn't possible) factions to level reputation with. I had Undead and Demons both at revered. At revered you get access to higher tier units from that faction (permanently) and powerful talents you can choose for your main character (which will be deactivated if you lose reputation, which is quite easy and irritating, because sometimes you just don't understand what for ... or you have no other choice than to take the hit).Furthermore your companions and "named units" are also basically just more powerful versions of basic units, but you can only ever have two with you on the battlefield. So they suffer from the same issues. Why take Orion who dies in 1 to 2 hits (he can cloak himself and deals nice damage, but that's it) over Bagthal, who not only has massively more survivability, but also deals fire damage, has a large AoE taunt, AND counter-attacks EVERY TIME he is attacked in melee????!!! It's not even a contest.And if you've decided on the "wrong" faction, imho you just make the game a lot harder on yourself. In the end I only had demons and the game was a piece of cake, especially thanks to the Daughter of Sin, a new DLC unit.You can probably make the other factions work as well, they have powerful units as well, but what does it matter when the enemy kills them on turn 1?And the combat is sooo sluggish. Even at 300% speed you're just waiting and waiting and waiting. For buffs. For animations. Etc. etc.And after each fight you have to go back to a fountain to heal. I mean, why? Just heal the party, all you're doing is prolonging the game for no reason!Then there's the fact you can't open the menu when it's not your turn. Thanks. And then you can't simply restart the battle or reload an earlier save. No, you have to quit to the menu to do that. Why?!Your companions and you can't die by the way. So it's often not a terrible idea to send them on suicide missions in a battle. As long as you are sure to win the battle without losing anyone else ... as a distraction so to speak. Especially to protect your backline from angry dragons and the like -.-Finally, there's the bosses. Experiments in frustration. You don't know what the bosses' abilities are. Have fun figuring it out 20 minutes into the fight and losing all your units.They're not fun. Or interesting. For the most part. Heroes 5 did that better imho. And that game is old now. But it's just ... well, you are primarily melee-focused? Bad luck. Oh, you have primarily caster units with less HP? Well, they won't survive the AoE attack that fills the entire battlefield. Come on. For the penultimate boss I actually had to switch my line-up, since my guys simply died from moving ... so I got flying units that just avoided 90% of the damage ... lol. So stupid.Story & Dialogue:The story is actually not terrible. The ending isn't just coming out of the blue. There are a few twists and turns, but none of them are entirely outlandish.The big issue is that whoever has written the dialogues just doesn't know what he's doing.Avyanna, the main character, and Orion, your trusty sidekick, are insufferable. They constantly joke when there's nothing to joke about. There's not a single dialogue in the game that isn't marred by endless quips and jokes. In the same vein the game doesn't shy away from telling you about dismemberment, sexual assault, killing children, mass murder, etc.Tonally it just makes no sense. For Orion this almost makes sense (as is explained in game). but Avyanna feels like a nasty 15 year old teenager in a fan-fic novel. Romances are inconsequential, decisions basically don't matter, either.Your companions will just stick with you no matter what ... until the very end when a scripted companion betrays you ... for no discernible reason. But no biggy, you just resurrect him 5 minutes later and everything is fine. I just don't understand any of it.Disciples Liberation could tell you a mature story about power, leadership and war. You could be a benevolent leader or a ruthless killer. Instead you're a joker. Through and through. Avyanna might have just killed thousands of people, but she sure has a quip ready ... WTF?!Until the very end there are no consequences to your actions... and even those consequences are meaningless, because nothing really matters, everyone basically "goes on" with life ... and then you get reset to the beginning.For "New Game +" or "Liberation Mode" as the game likes to call it. New dialogue choices, a changed story ... and the same old ♥♥♥♥♥♥ problems. Oh, and now you can take all your campanions into battle with you. Yay. Something that might have been cool in the first playthrough, instead of letting them simmer on the side lines. Oh well, I sure as ♥♥♥♥ won't play through the game again ... yes, you could try out different unit combinations, but for that the game just drags on too much. Maybe if it were half as long, but it severely overstays its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: First, if someone can clear some of these issues up for me, please feel free to comment.I really like the concept of this game, and I like the characters so far. But I have some big issues with the game. 1) I'm a casual player (I think this is important to note) and I play on Story mode. I don't want to be overwhelmed, but I don't mind being a little challenged. I picked one of the "normal" difficulty starting regions with the game on Story mode. There was no guidance on the number of units I should have or what level I should be. I lost completely in my first random fight. I restarted in the same region and rushed towards the story area, and while I cleared it, I was losing the main character in the first round because every enemy targeted her. 2) There is no tutorial that I can find. How does hiring units work? Should I mix and match? Am I supposed to stick to one of the factions? The story made it seem like you had to find one ally and stick with them. Is there a place for me to try out units before I recruit them or do I just have to waste resources and find out if they're useful?3) There are dungeons that you enter and then are forced to clear before you leave them, with no warning. It feels like a "gotcha" moment. I entered a dungeon with two units (zombies) and three companions (counting the lead) and couldn't win a single fight. I also couldn't leave the dungeon after realizing I couldn't handle it upon seeing the large enemy armies with double my level. How about a recommended level in the journal or before entering the dungeon? At least a warning message that you won't be able to leave it once you enter it.4) I find it frustrating when games hide the details of gameplay elements from the player in order to make the game more difficult. There should be a tutorial mission were you're taught the basics of using an army and recruiting units.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an extremely mediocre product in absolutely every aspect of it. However, I can't call it bad because I enjoyed it. Trim them down to the point that you are OK to READ the fanfic about world from your beloved nostalgic times with smile and irony.Disciples 2 was a masterpiece. Disciples 3 was meh. Disciples Liberation is a kind of unstable mess where some cool things are sewed together with a complete nonsense. Game hooked me with combat system of supporting units and combat spells in demo . But became quite unballanced during company. At some point whole you army became nothing more than a crossfaction meatshield for one-girl-with-undercut-army oneshotting everyone with T3-T4 spells. Story is very good for ambitious eroge. I'm not sure if they wanted to turn the Nevendaar's grim story into an eroge, but they succeeded. Cut scenes: Nope. It is a text jRPG.Bosses: Very dissapointing. Some random gold mine fights are much harder.Music: Not sure there is any.Voice acting: DISGUSTING VILE TORTURE. I think that Kalypso tried to make something good, but maybe they bited off more than they could swallow. At least i can see self-irony through the game this say me a lot. Not sure what made it so difficult: low budget or low effort. I still positive they will make enough and Liberate their potential in next game about Nevendaar.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This game is a hidden gem, but I would highly recommend downloading a trainer to increase the game speed beyond the maximum allowed in the settings.  (Google FLiNG trainer)  Even at 300%, combat really starts to become a slog by midgame when you see the same animations play over and over again and are just trying to advance the story.  For a game that is predominantly about combat I found it to be rather simplistic and it verges on tediousness by the end of the game.  Sure, there is tremendous unit variety that seems cool initially but you’ll quickly realize that there are superior options at each tier that make that variety a bit of an illusion if you want to progress through the game on harder difficulties.  Additionally, there aren’t any tooltips that give a real sense of character stat impact on ability damage scaling etc, so you spend a lot of time finding out what does more damage through trial and error.  I was hoping for a bit more complexity in this regard.Despite the mediocre combat, I found myself enjoying the story immensely despite its initial juvenile first-impression.   There are multiple different ways to resolve seemingly unimportant side quests and these often lead to surprising results like special units joining your party or special dialogue/mentions later in the game.   The companions are incredibly diverse and seem to have their own agendas that can often be at odds with your own or other party members.  Based on the epilogue it is clear that they each have multiple endings as well which makes interacting with them much more meaningful. Based on brief glances on discussion boards regarding certain quests, there appears to be a lot of nuance to how certain quest resolutions unfold.The game is also *very* long which might be a drawback for some, but as I said I enjoyed the story enough that this was a net positive for me rather than a negative.  If you’re looking for a game with a lot of content (and not in the Assassin’s Creed busy-work sort of way) then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played through the entire series.... yes, the first one as well, so I know what I'm on about.This one I feel breathes some new life into Disciples, it keeps the tactical element but drifts towards an RPG more than it's TBS predecessors. The story whilst not remarkable, takes you to some interesting places and memorable choices. Instead of choosing what alliance you start with, it will happen based on the decisions you make and on how you decide to go about quests, which is a nice touch, in my opinion.Graphics are nothing exceptional, however, the game is easy on the eyes, it looks a decent 8/10.Sound-wise it does better than the 3rd instalment which felt repetitive as hell, it does a bit of a better job with variation and voice-over (could have had more of it) so that's a 7/10.The gameplay is a massive improvement, there's more elements on the battlefield that influence combat, upgrades feel more meaningful, you can choose between troops from all factions depending on what suits and depending on your standing with said faction, you can upgrade equipment.... there's enough content, enough quests and enough choices to keep you from getting bored.Overall it's a solid game that does right by its predecessors. Yes, I love Disciples 2, absolutely, but I am glad Disciples: Liberation didn't lean too much on previous entries.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game on both modes, definitely would recommend.The game does a great job at pacing; when I saw the screenshot of the multitude of units, I was worried I'd be overwhelmed before I have a chance to fall in love with the game and its mechanics.  That wasn't the case at all - just play the game normally, and soon you'd wish you have more units and mechanics to control.  It is also just nuanced and deep enough with enough multiple choices to warrant multiple play-throughs.One recommendation - many of the legendary items fall off in terms of utility and power.  Some sooner than others.  Especially the legendary boots, helmet, and pants.  For those slots, the game's obsessed with critical chance; a useful stat for sure, but not what I'm looking for in those slots.  Would also be nice if there was an option to bring up an item's base damage to your current level instead of having them fall to gradual irrelevance.Finally, if a button or toggle existed for telling you a spell or ability's damage formula and grid coverage, that would be nice.  I was definitely disappointed to experience the tier 4 twilight spell damage to be barely above that of the tier 2 twilight spell damage (plz don't fix by nerfing the tier 2 twilight spell, most spells are already bad enough cause they can't crit).Overall, it's a pretty good game because the gameplay and pacing is great.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review to negative one.This game has a huge flaw : game design. This game is incredibly monotonous. Most battles are almost identical. And developers know this : they try to add variety by introducing special environment effects in some battles. However the core of the game remains flawed : there is very little variety in game mechanics. For whatever reason, developers decided to make factions symmetrical and almost identical to each other. Do you remember how different each faction was in Disciples 2? In Disciples Liberation factions don't have anything special about them. Undead seem to be the only faction which had some effort put into, but even they still aren't unique enough. The flaws described above are not noticeable at first since you are going to level up regularly and get higher tier troops. This forces you to change tactics which is good. However, after a certain moment, you will find the optimal tactics and will perform it for every battle. At this point game becomes boring.Developers should have cut the number of battles by 75%. Most of the fights feel like filler. For example, at the end you will have to fight 6 battles which is already annoying. And developers decided to add random enemies in between these battles basically doubling the amount of total encounters.As for the plot, I was really looking forward to it. There was betrayal and intrigues. Player is given information from different sources some of which are lying etc. Overall, it had great potential.However, closer to the end, the story became about gods and saving the universe. It feels like half way into the game, a 10 year old kid took over the script. What is more, there are ONLY 4 factions. There are no neutral units unaffiliated with factions. Game really feels like it was rushed. A lot of units seem out of place and look like they were added just to make factions symmetrical.CONCLUSION : I can't recommend this game. I have wasted enough hours into it and know I regret it. Game seems good at first, but gets boring fast.

_childDocuments_.review: Disciples II was my favourite game when I was a kid, and I absolutely loved playing with numbers, trying different builds and "rasing" my initiates into vampires, liches and deaths. It was fun, satisfying, crunchy.Then there was Disciples III which was so bad and buggy that I don't even want to talk about it.Now this. This is waaaay better than Disciples III, but is still pretty bad. It's almost ok, but not almost good. Here is why:1) The feel of the game. For me the main feel of the game of Disciples was growing your units over the tree. Here you kind of have a similar system... But don't worry if someone dies - you can always just hire the next tier unit. Moreover, your veteran zombie who fought 100 battles isn't worth anything - you can't upgrade them to the next tier. Just buy the next tier unit and upgrade with gold and steel to the max level.This completely ruins the feel of unit development. D2 was the deepest unit-development game of that time, and DL is more shallow than pretty much anything that has any unit development. 2) Game mechanics. It was my favourite part in D2, but here in DL it is very weird. First of all, most of the shown numbers are boring and the same for most same-tier units. E.g. almost all tier-2 warriors have the same HP and power. But, they have all different skills, which is almost cool, except unless you try each of them and use pen and paper (or spreadsheet) to calculate them - you won't know the power of each strike. Different units with the same stats for power deal different damage, but nothing nowhere says how much damage they deal. Even just saying 75% of power, 115% of power etc. - would be super helpful. But alas. If you are not into spreadsheers and testing - sorry. If you are - choose another game, where number crunching is funnier and less confusing :)Yet, despite being somewhat chaotic, battles become quite repetitive and boring, because due to poor unit development - almost nothing changes from battle to battle.3) And yep, since it is an "RPG" now, I have to say about this part as well. First of all, it is as linear and banal as it gets. Narrative is awful. All the role-playing feels completely fake and more of a filler than a core. Even strategies nowadays usually make better stories and better roleplaying, yet this game calls itself RPG. Sad.The only somewhat good part is aesthetics and lore - although it also feels super outdated, it is still rahter appealing - as long as you skip all the childish dialogues which completely ruin the feel.Yet, compated to D3 it is at least playable. But I couldn't force myself to finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a game reviewer and I am not  good with words so I would normally just do a "pros and cons" list of what I liked and what I didn't but in this case I cant because the cons are so many it will seem like I didn't like the game.     Let's start on what the game does well. It is a unique game experience that I have not played before. I am not saying it is the first game to do this style, but it is the first I have played. Unfortunately apart from that the game is the definition of "above mediocrity". Nothing is mediocre or bad, but everything is just good enough. The music is nice, the combat is nice, the story is nice and yet nothing really excels at anything. You drop in the game with a decent tutorial mission and the suddenly the main plot gets forced worse than when my aunt margaret forced me to do cocaine off her belly button. You feel like you get dropped in ACT2 of something you didn't play. At the beggining I was like "this can't be it, there is no way". The main plot gets forced really bad and you always feel like there is another game you should have played before it to reach that point of the plot. After that the story gets better, because it flows more naturally, but still it is pretty forced. Before moving to gameplay I would like to say also that despite what the review ,that always gets forced to your screen worse than the plot of the game, says, your choices do not matter at all. The only thing that your choices affect is what units you get from what faction, and seeing as every faction is just a reskin of the other with the same abilities but different visuals, it doesnt matter what faction you have high standing with.   The game is repetitive in every possible way. There is one track of music that gets repeated at every battle, AND THERE ARE A LOT OF THEM. There are at total i think 4 kinds of spells and 2 kinds of marcial abilities, damage in a line, damage in a cone, damage in a circle, damage around, and single target damage. The only thing that changes no matter the faction, main character, or companions are the visuals and the effects. This circle is divine damage, while this circle is physical damage and does a 10% miss chanse, while this circle is primal damage and does burning. It is the same. The companions are all reskins of tier 2 and tier 3 units from each faction respectively and the battle "sites" are all open areas with little to no difference. You could have more that "oh this hexagon does fire damage to whoever stands on it, and this gives power to whoever goes there first" but no, there is nothing more. You could have height differences for range advantage, cover from ranged units etc, but everything is the same open grid and whenever you think there is cover, there really isn't.  The difficulty is irrelevant because it is litteraly just 0.25x at enemy stats in each level of difficulty, which is irrelevant because by mid game every enemy is a damage sponge. Despite this the game is really easy even on hard difficulty, I am currently playing. You always play first on a round cause enemies have low inniciative ,mostly, so you just use all your ranged units and kill everything important the enemies have. If you don't and  the enemies play the round, the strategy is to quit the game and load a save before the battle, because you can't surrender or give up in battle for some reason. Also the experience of discovering items is completely void of joy. Everything is "+2 to constitution and dexterity". It is joyless and honestly lazy game design. The last thing I will say on the difficulty section is about the economy, because I do not know where else to put it. Basically there is an economy and there are resources for sure and you take these resources and do certain things. And these resources matter because you buy stuff you surely need and there are mines and iron mines and gold mines the provide resources.I am writing this review in order to gather resources because of the real time thing for some reason. So yeah good system.   They say the game time is around 80 hours, if the animations could be sped up more it would be 30. I started playing from the start on 300% animations and it still feels slow. If you start like this the 300% seems like normal movement. It is amazing how slow everything in battle is.  As you can see, I didn't want to leave a "pros-cons" review, because I have been analyzing in 3 paragraphs why the game is bad. But I do not think it is a bad game. Everything I have said is true, don't get me wrong, but I am not saying it is a bad game because of these things. It is just a above average game. It rise above mediocrity by one meter, but still it is not a bad experience. Currently I have lowered the difficulty to story mode, because I got bored of the battles and maybe I will change opinion later about the game, but I really think it is a decent game. Not an undiscovered masterpiece, but a decent game. I would give it a generous 7/10 for how unique it is, but I would not blame anyone who would give it a 5 to 7/10, because if this was my second game that was in that style, I would be less generous about my score.  In conclusion I would like to summarise saying a 2 things. The game is a decent experience with a lot of problems and a lot of repitition. Secondly I bought the game for 16 euros, for the deluxe edition, and not for the price these mentally insane people charge for this. If i had given 40-50 euros for this I would have commited sepuku and I would have given it a 5/10 for sure.  EDIT: another thing that just came to my mind about the game is that the developers past really shows. There was always something that was bugging me. Something the felt wrong, uncanny. I finally figured it out. This looks a lot like a mobile game. Simplified models, portraits, combat, maps. Everything you need to do is click where to move and click your 2 abilities. It is like it was designed having a mobile game in mind. Everything is good but feels a little off.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kinda torn on that one. There were things I liked, but ultimately there are too many problems that accumulate for me to recommend the game.First thing first. If you're familiar with the previous Disciples entries, you might expect this game to be a turn based strategy game. It is NOT. It does use hex-based tactical combat and the map is reminiscent of other turn based strategy games, but the map traversed in real time with no AI to speak off (except for some groups of enemies occasionally having very basic behaviour such as patrolling or attacking if you come close) ; the end result is that this game is a RPG through and through.So, for the good :-The combat. Having hex-based fights with some minor army management in a RPG game is an interesting take on the genre, and it works well.-The music. It fits the game's atmosphere pretty well and there was enough variety throughout the game that it didn't get old.-Pretty decent voice acting all around.-Pretty good visuals overall.-The game has boss fights, which are visually very cool and memorable and shake things up from standard gameplay.Aaaand now for the bad. -Bugs. I encountered plenty ; nothing gamebreaking thankfully, but lots of annoyances like the inventory becoming completely transparent, music stopping and restarting randomly, loot summary no longer appearing, looping conversation trees, some quests end step being available too soon, and such things. The game is playable, but that doesn't look good.-The game, for some reason, has several mobile game elements which are baffling to see in a fully realised "proper" game. You have to hold the button to upgrade or disassemble stuff or to learn spells. You collect piles of randomly generated equipment which only slightly differs from each other and are ultimately completely pointless since you end up getting your hands on non-random legendary tier equipment that is infinitely better. You have to manually collect your ressources. The game begs you to review it every time you go to the main menu (which will be more often than it should, because bugs!) It's bad.-Even outside of mobile games influence, some of the decisions the game made are just plain annoying. Damage to your units persists after a battle. To heal, you need to use fountains of healing found throughout the maps. There are very few instances in which you can afford to do two battles back to back without healing. So you are constantly backtracking to go back to a healing fountain after each battle. Worse, the fountains have recharge timers, that increase with difficulty.You can also only build 4 different buildings to recruit units (out of 12) at a time. If you want to build a new one, you have to "phase out" a previous building to free the space ; then you can sort of juggle buildings in that spot, for a cost. However, that cost is negligible (more on that in a minute), so the end result is just pointless tedium.Also (probably because of the way buildings are handled) there is no general interface to recruit or train units. You have to click on each building to recruit the units that are available in it, and if you want to train a unit you have to go to the building that allows you to recruit units of that type.Oh and for some reason you can't load during a fight. If you accidentally got into a fight you can't possibly win, you have to quit to the main menu and load from there.-Ressources are pointless in this game. Aside from the very beginning of the game, where you have 4 maps available and unlock new stuff after completing 2 so you might get stuff you can't build yet (e.g a building needing mana to upgrade when you haven't yet gone to the map with the first mana generator), once you're past that point you can stop caring. Between buildings and caches found on the maps, you will always have enough ressources to buy everything you want the moment it becomes available.-Balance. There are 4 classes in the game. Two fighters, two mages. While the fighter classes are decent at first glance, the mages turn out to be so much better it's not even funny. What would you prefer : the ability to hit good with a sword and react to being critically hit, or an incredibly powerful and versatile arsenal on demand?Also, the enemies just have plain better stats than you. Towards the end of the game on normal difficulty, I noticed that enemies had over 50% more HP than  that were on my side, and also noticeably more power. Although that's probably to compensate for the fact that the AI is very basic. It will only take a few fights before you spot the patterns, which you can then abuse liberally.-The setting is... edgy. The kind you roll your eyes at. I understand this is dark fantasy, but this game takes it to a ridiculous extent. It never misses an occasion to remind you that life on Nevendaar suuuuucks, that people are constantly getting tortured/enslaved/killed/eaten/reanimated/[insert horrible thing here], that kindness will be abused, that most people in power are jerks of massive proportions, and so on, and so on. It's a bit like Warhammer in that regard, in that it's  over the top dark and grim that it just becomes funny. Within the first few hours or so of playing this game I had had an orgy with a succubus and a bunch of dead people, cut zombies into bits for a stew, collected spleens off of random passerbys, sacrificed someone for a sword, built a throne out of body parts, raided graves to collect bones to feed a golem, and massacred an entire rebellion. It's just silly at that point.-Units never shut up. Almost every unit has a voiceline for every action they perform in combat. Except they say those lines all the time, and there aren't very few actions in combat ultimately (move, use first ability, use second ability, kill an enemy, die). This is tolerable for units with quieter voices, but some are downright irritating.-Boss fights last too long. Every boss is a big sack of HP, so even if you've played your cards well enough that you are certain to win, you will still need to slowly chip away at a huge health bar over more than a dozen rounds (typical battles last 3 or 4 rounds usually).-The game has four factions and claims you can ally or antagonize any of them as you wish, but in practice the Empire is setup as the bad guy and it's noticeably more difficult to ally with them since several story events will make you lose reputation with them.-The story is meh. It's ultimately a pretty standard "heroine has mysterious powers and uses them to conquer everything and save everyone forever, despite the efforts of a MYSTERIOUS and VERY BAD antagonist, yayyyyy". They did try to allow some wiggle room by letting you choose your answers to various events, but it's rather limited and in the end doesn't change much.There is also a secret ending which I did not like at all.-Progression is off. At first it's actually pretty good, you gain new levels at a decent enough pace to feel like you're progressing and becoming stronger, but not fast enough to feel overwhelmed or like you're outpacing the challenges you're presented with. But it slows more and more throughout the game and eventually becomes just plain glacial. You always need 1000 XP to gain a level, but you gain less and less as the game goes on. There was a point where fighting an army of roughly equal strength, something that took a good 10-15 minutes because of the already mentionned inflated HP pools, would give me something like 40 XP. Out of, again, 1000. And levels are incremental, you gain very few stats and a single skill point each time. It felt bad.Soooo... yeah. I really liked the combat (at least at first), but there are a LOT of issues with this game so I just can't recommend it. I got it in the Humble Bundle and feel like I got my money worth, but I wouldn't buy it full price.TL;DR : Pass on that one, or get it for cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly decent game, but it's a far cry form the old Disciples. It feels more like a cousin of King's Bounty.The presentation is pretty cool, and the new AP system allows for some decent depth, the companions also fit well with the story. Although it starts out pretty well, the core gameplay becomes atrociously repetitive, especially since there are only around 15 units for each race, with 4 races total. That's 60 units you'll see over the course of the entire game, most of which are kinda similar to each other (every faction has their <<archer unit>>, <<healer unit>>, <<assassin unit>>, <<dragon unit>>, etc, I wish everyone did certain things unique to them). There are no neutral monsters (spiders, golems, orcs, etc) to spice things up like in the previous games. Your choices don't affect the story at all, but they do change some gameplay elements (skip a fight, get a certain upgraded unit, etc).And whoever came up with the bosses should be fired. _childDocuments_.review: This is what King's Bounty 2 should have been.  It's similar to Heroes of Might and Magic and King's Bounty games - you construct and upgrade buildings with resources to recruit troops and keep improving your leadership by winning battles so you can equip more troop units.  Run around the map fighting battles, taking on quests, and opening chests.  Battles play out on a grid in turn based fashion - it's simpler than most turn based games and I appreciate that - you don't have to figure out the half dozen buffs/penalties and qualifiers for a unit, yet it does have some complexity (just enough to be interesting).You have gear slots to improve stats.  You also have a skill tree and pending on your class (select later in game) and alliances points different skills become available.  Your units gain xp in battle too, and have 1 or 2 slots for some gear buffing.I've been having a blast and watching time fly by.  Game may not be as long as HOMM series, have to see, I've completed 2 of the 4 areas the map has shown me (and done nearly all sidequests on them), but am not certain if more opens up after that, I'm guessing i'm over halfway thru right now.  So don't expect a 60 hour marathon.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10I was going to give it a thumbs down, but I managed to get a save with Liberty Mode unlocked, so it was fun to play. Additionally, I had the x10 gameplay speed mod installed. Without it it would be a nightmare.The advantage of the game is the graphics and music. Turn-based battles are fun, but the problem is that all such battles are similar and ultimately one strategy, "rush", works.The biggest drawback of the game is the story. I don't know who wrote it, but they definitely had no idea what the game's lore looked like, which is obviously a huge disadvantage. We have four races and the whole idea of ​​the game is to unite these four races and live in peace. It looks correct on paper until we realize that in addition to humans and elves, we also have demons and the undead. Yes, the game's creators assumed that magical, bloodthirsty creatures from hell could be "good" and coexist peacefully with people. I won't mention the undead. Seriously? Are the undead and humans supposed to exist peacefully? The undead literally eat humans in all forms (both body and soul).This idea itself is evil at its very base and unfortunately the entire history is constructed in such a way that the "unification of all races" is possible. So we have a lot of cases of "civilized undead and demons", at the same time humans and elves are placed on an equal footing with demons and undead. Let me be clearer: Living races and Dead races are placed as equals. To justify the stupid idea of ​​uniting the races, the developer obviously had to "humanize" both the undead and demons, so we have a lot of stupid quests, such as "freeing the undead from captivity" (yes, zombies, ghosts and vampires decided to surrender at some point during the fight). In another quest, the MC calls the walking dead "people with feelings" and that mindlessly killing the undead is wrong. There are more such quests. When a game gets monotonous and boring, it's usually a good story that makes me want to finish it. Unfortunately, it's not available here, so I didn't finish the game.

Lastly I didn't care much for the RPG story but it seems that the developer was a bit half hearted there too as only half of the dialog gets vocalized.The game is OK really, just not all that great.
