_childDocuments_.review: First of all this is a lot different game then the old glorified Disciples 1 or 2 and also diff from kind of weird 3. I think in this age you can not produce commercially successful game similar to 1 or 2. And 3 was a hybrid that didn't really satisfy anybody. When I first read the reviews I was sad and thought it is not a good game. Then I stumbled upon it again a year later. I found a demo like in old days and just 3 hours later I met Ejamar and was hooked and bought it. I played it through the first time and then again in Liberation mode. Which is kind of a bonus mode, where you tie up all the loose ends. Commercially successful that is. What next Disciple game to create that would suit modern gamers? Static battlefield with carefully calculated numbers in HP, DMG, Initiative, Chance to hit, Armor, Wards, Immunities, Special attacks? No. It needs to move. You need to have richer animations. It must also attract new auditions. Should you create a story campaign for each faction and let them clash? Creators said no. We want something new. I told myself, lets try it. I was no big fan of our starting heroes, but they were neither against the fur. But they won me over. Little rebels. This era loves them, actually as any other, really.  You are running with your hero thru many  which works like King’s Bounty and not like old Disciples. The map is populated with things to explore or conquer, some encounters start or are part of quests. It is real time. No turns. There are no other factions with heroes running around, conquering your mines. Mines are present on a map, they have garrison that must be defeated. Once yours it will stay yours and will produce resources per hour. There are no cities. No territory, no rods to capture land. You are not buying heroes, you are running with only that one. You are not picking a  at start of the game. You are an outsider trying to befriend them, so they might help you in your struggle. You acquire an Angelic city that has kind of teleporting pads where you place buildings. There are 4 pads for main buildings, each faction has only 3 buildings to produce units (Warriors, Mages, Special). And 2 for Marketplace and Smithy. You can phase Buildings in/out as needed. It works well, some might not like the graphic design. There are . They do not get experience to lvl up. You are buying them. You get access to better units by increasing reputation with given faction and having progressed enough thru main quest line. You have a leadership attribute. It increases with your lvl and with upgrade of your main building. 1st tier units cost 10, 2nd cost 20, and so on up to 40. Units have basic attack and an ability with cooldown. 1st tier units don’t have a passive ability, higher do. You can have 10 units on battlefield. Your hero Avianna counts as 1 of them. Then you have companions. You can acquire up to 9 of them. They are quite good and powerful. In normal campaign you can have 2 of them in battle. In Liberation mode all 9. And you have also supporting back line - up to 3 units. Each unit has unique support skill. This way you can create a better suited force and react to different needs. Companions have interesting stories, quests, conversations. They have a deepness I was not expecting in this game. Some are so outstanding that I will remember them for all times - yes, you Ejamar. Like I was not fan of Necromency enough already. They are all so beautifully voiced acted.  are acquired thru quests. You buy them for different mana. You do not cast them on the map, but directly in combat. It costs only your personal mana. I liked the old system but can live with this too. Mainly because the spells are quite many and good, some even excellent. Support, heal, dmg, summon. When you decide to be warrior then you can get up to 8 abilities - to be used instead of spells.You can  yourself with Helm, Armor, Pants, Boots, Weapon, Crystal. Companions with Weapon and Crystal. Units only with Crystal. There are plenty of them to choose from, can be upgraded, crystals merged.  is executed on field roughly the size of 20x10 hexes. Battlefields are randomly created based on the surroundings. It was never off. Seldom there are corridors created, so you can employ different tactics. It was always nice. Never so off as in D3. Mainly because of the units and their abilities. It was always a joy. Units can have blue, red or gold AP. Each has 2 APs with different combinations. Top tiers have 2 gold AP - as companions. Blue Ap is for move only. Red is for action. Gold is for anything. Every unit occupies only one space. You can increase speed to 300%, can adjust if only for enemy or not, skip this or that animation. You can adjust it to your taste. I didn’t had the problem as people were writing that it takes ages to win a battle. I think they didn’t try all options or it was before update. It is different to old games in mechanic. Not in theme, units, lore, graphics, sounds those are still great. But voices are more mediocre. I miss Demons and their latin. It was so fitting. Design of some units is questionable but overall it fits. There are many units that are done so great. Simply, nothing is perfect. I also hated the baroque touch to some imperial units back in D2. Story revolves around a Nephelim. Yes again. I would say it is time to start abusing some other idea. At least the idea here is executed quite well. A bit cliche but very well done. I would hate to reveal story. I will say it evolves nicely. You will meet a lot of companions from different factions who will create a believing alliance with you thru their storyline. That is perhaps the thing that I liked the most. There are some weak points to this or that idea in story [h]like with her mother. Why not invite her to Illian[/h]. I loved every single companion that I met. They have nice quests, conversations you have are not long, but I like the script. Unique personality. Nice voice acting and graphic model. Able to wield a weapon and able to acquire special one through their story line. Those nice little things. I do not regret that they are just special model of certain unit with same abilities. I liked the mechanic in which they worked and didn’t have a craving for something special. I am a big fan of the 1 and 2. Last time I finished 1 was 8 years ago. I played several times 2. I found 3 to be kind of weird, too forced. With later update (Renaissance) it was playable but still unbalanced (Like for undead penultimate mission had enough ex to go to ultimate lvl, but not possible without required building. Then in last mission you could build last tier building but not enough exp to lvl units - WTF). Mainly I have plenty of fantastic experiences with 2. And this one nicely ends the saga. It was such a joy with these games.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome tactic RPG game. I didn't play the previous games as some reviewers have but I enjoyed it and understood the story and the world in general starting from this one. Graphics is STUNNING. Visual effects of attacks and spells are cool and clear. Story was interesting to follow with a couple of cool plot twists. I love how some of the choices story-wise were frustrating me into multiple ultimatums so you have to choose which was more compelling for your play style. To keep the gameplay from being too repetitive, the "conquer" mechanic automatically finishes the combat if your party is much stronger. Helped keep the game pace good. Game worked at 1440p 144 FPS smoothly with no drops except during loading screens (played on a RTX 3080). The ability to mix and match unit from different factions is cool. Your relationship with the factions will help boost ur units as well so it's a neat mechanic to optimize your party. PLUS your character get to choose one of four classes and can easily interchange them. DUSK WITCH FTW :DI played on launch day and there were a couple bugs that I solved by restarting the game only. All of them were fixed within a week with a hotfix update. Thank you developers!Dialogue and voice acting is good at best. Not a deal breaker for me though.Overall a neatly polished game imo. I still have to finish Liberation mode for the true ending but an overall 8.5/10 game. Highly recommended.Deserves best visuals steam awards!

_childDocuments_.review: Raves:It's a mix between divinity original sin 2 and might and magic, your team consists of your main character and 2 'unique' companions that are basically just buffed versions of normal troops, you get to choose between 4 different factions to supply your army which is determined by the leadership score of the main character. Each faction has 3 different buildings you can add to your base to recruit various troops from so there's a bit of diversity about how you want to form your army. I especially enjoyed the exploring part and unlocking various things, the insane number of choices you can make that actually effect the story and characters (you can lose companions permanently that have real consequences on the game). It's a great power fantasy game!Rants:Combat is atrociously boring at mid-high level, you will often fight wave after wave of enemies slightly higher level than you with a massive tier advantage. You can't get Tier 4 units until you get revered with a faction which takes -forever- to do, so you'll be stuck with tier 3 at best while you're fighting armies of Tier 4 units. Not to mention the AI is actually competent and will position their troops spread out so you cant even get good AOE on them, they'll also do hit-and-run tactics making you spend an extra 5-10 minutes at the 'end' of a fight just chasing down the stragglers. The level of some of these packs of enemies makes no sense either, when I was level 40 there was a pack of LEVEL 80 enemies guarding a chest...over 15 hours later my team is only 65 so there was absolutely no way i could've even touched that when I saw it, let alone even now at the end of the game.Choices matter, but some of them don't make any sense. Good luck trying to be friends with 2 factions at once cause it aint happening, I wanted elves and demons as my two factions and it was nearly impossible to keep elven alliance rep. There was even one quest where I was sure I selected everything to side with the elves, only for the quest to complete and I gained +20 to undead and -20 to elves, even though the undead weren't even in the scenario.**Spoilers** Why does every game have to have some evil religious cult? Not once did I even sympathize with the Empire, they made them as unlikable as possible and the only factions that were actually reasonable at all were the demons and undead. The elves were stubborn beyond belief and the Empire acted worse than all of them.Anyway. Get the game, it's fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆(Good game bogged down by length and questionable design choices)============Review:Disciples Liberation is sort of like King's Bounty - an RPG with turn-based combat.Audiovisually the game is alright. It looks good enough, it has good sounds and pretty good music too.So what's the problem then?Well it looks like King's Bounty and is named Disciples, but it's really nothing like either of them. It doesn't have evolving units like Disciples, and it lacks the sense of adventure of King's Bounty. Yeah, it has units with same NAMES as Disciples and a half-assed castle construction system, but it doesn't feel like Disciples at all. Well, I suppose they just wanted to try something new which is fine, but I'm personally not a fan of this lazy route where you have the same units which just have a level number behind. Yeah, you have your Typical Zombies at the beginning (level 1), but you still have the same Zombies in the late game, it just has bigger stats (level 60+) which just feels very lazy to me.============The main beef of the game is of course combat. The core mechanics of combat are good and they work just fine, I like the different colored action point system. However, the problem is combat is too SLOW, like way too slow.. even at maximum speed (300%) it's still TOO SLOW. Especially when you consider the game is really FILLED WITH COMBAT this is not a good thing.Yeah, there's ALOT of enemy Armies/Stacks around you have to kill, like WAY too many of them. And if the combat itself is SLOW, you know what it does. It's artificially extending the game in a very bad way.Luckily they did add a "Conquer" auto-resolve system when your army is notably stronger than the enemy army, which practically just wins the battle instantly. But honestly why not just have LESS COMBAT, but make it feel good and meaningful?Playing on higher difficulties makes this even worse. It simply slaps stat multipliers on enemies, so the battles will last EVEN LONGER.It even has an extra "Liberation Mode" which you're supposed to play for the true ending but.. no thank you.============Overall, I think Disciples Liberation is pretty good, but it's simply way too long and repetitive to be THAT enjoyable for me.I imagine some people really like the repetitive nature of the game and don't have a problem with the length, but I got seriously burned out and bored of the game once I had completed about 75% of it.If the game was notably shorter, I would probably play a run with each of the four races, but because of its excessive length I can't force myself to play it again.Despite all the ranting, I don't think Disciples Liberation is a bad game. It just could be a lot better if it was much shorter and battles were faster or it had less combat in general. I think it's alright, so I give it a careful recommendation - but you should get it from a hefty sale.============Summary:The Good 👍+ Audiovisually good+ Core mechanics are solid+ Good combat mechanics..The Bad 👎- ..but combat is too slow- Too many filler battles- Too long- Repetitive

_childDocuments_.review: *POTENTIAL SPOILER AT THE END OF THE REVIEW*Firstly, my actual playing hours are not quite as high as shown. I tended to leave the game on to fill my resources (using my initiative). I maybe have 90-100 hours actual playing time.I have to say though, I absolutely love this game! It ticks all the boxes for me, from role playing the main character, through deciding what to build in the city, to the tactical and strategic options for combat (which units to use, which items to use etc.)There is a lot of game content to plough through, just when you think you've about got it beat, another map becomes available, with more quests. On the subject of quests, there are lots of side quests during the game, which I highly recommend completing.I found the AI to be quite intuitive, ganging up on my troops to try and eliminate them quickly, which is a tactic I tend to use as well. Also, the movement AI is quite intelligent as well, walking around obvious hazards rather than straight through them like other games of this genre that I have played.I like the advancement scheme as well, and the way xp is earned. It is a set 1000xp per level, but the more levels you gain, the less xp you get per combat.I have nothing bad to say about the game, only a very short wishlist, which is:I would have liked to have been able to equip armour on the companions rather than just Avy. Even just equipping armour onto Ori.All in all, I am really impressed with this game. I have just completed the main game .. or thought I had! There is even more content once you complete the game. For the money it is well worth purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, this is the Smack Down.I would and am recommending this game to purchase and play. Now with that being said please keep this in mind.I have now played all of the Disciples games ever since I stumbled on the first one on a demo disc 20 years ago.As far as game play, I think that Disciples 2/Gold, Rise of the Elves, and Galiens Return were the Epitome of these games.I still play the 2 series sometimes.I have also played Final Fantasy all the way back to Game Boy, and Super Nintindo days, and about 12 years of World of Warcraft, along with Hero's of Might and Magic.This game is enjoyable, and definitely an improvement over Disciples 3.  I do however find it limited in scope as far as game play. It is linear in nature, and while I can deal with it, I don't like it. It feels more like watching a movie then what the original game with letting you choose your hero, and team was like.I also find it both interesting and at the same time having a bad taste in my mouth with the 4 faction deal with making your group, and I deal ok with the Hex combat system, but it is another aspect I would rather not have, and would prefer the old face off grid set up.Don't get me wrong the old system had limitations, and issues that could have made it better, but I think this turn based combat style runs to much over the top with the amount of characters on the field that some times end up i a Benny Hill chase around the board to finish the combat.The Graphics are way better for the environment, and stage props. The game characters are good for 3rd person overhead, but I think, and have seen better 3D characters. Hell I have and do model them myself.I guess what I am saying here is I think it could have a better direction, and playstyle, but it is worth playing it for the content.The characters seem, and feel a little flat though, but so far it has proven to be a game that I can actually play for a couple hours a day and put up.So if nothing else I would say its worth the money if you really like the series that it came from, but keep in mind that it is not Disciples 2. It is like playing a guided movie, and a little bit like playing Diablo which I am not fond of at all, but it is entertaining enough to give you something to do if you are board or need a distraction for an hour or two, and should be played that way, or you get burned out real fast.Anyway good questing.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give a neutral or slightly good rating rather than straight thumbs up. _childDocuments_.review: Wow, i got bored with that quickly.  There is nothing to truly distinguish one faction from another.  They are basically all just lazy re-skins of each other with a few abilities swapped out.The tactics portion of the game is weak.  Every battle plays the same on battlefields that don't change much.There is no customizing the main character or any of the units.The plot is basically just one big uninspired railroad switching station.  There is no real choice and any illusion of choice is shattered by the presence of powerful armies WAY above your level blocking your path just in case you wanted to go anywhere the devs didn't want you too.Claims that this game is "Story Rich" are bold faced lies.The exploration maps are ridiculously small with zero procedural generation or randomness, so there isn't really any exploration either.Basically this game is a lazy, half-hearted attempt to recapture the essence of the old "Might & magic" franchise, and it accomplishes NONE of the things it promises.  If you like RPG's, Exploration, or Tactics games, then give this one a pass or get it dirt cheap on sale, because this title does NONE of those things well.

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed this game, it has some quirks that developers will hopefully iron out but overall it's a nice experience. It reminds me of King's Bounty, where you have a hero with skill tree and spells and you gather a party with units from 4 races. You have units on the battlefield that take leadership to field and units in the backline that provide support skills. The battles are simple to understand and quite fun. The game pacing is pretty good too and exploring the areas is nice. Your choices shape the plot and add quite a lot of flavor to the game.Some of the things I think developers should look at:- 400% or even 800% battle speed. 200% is too slow- Balance - most of the time your army outlevels the enemy armies and the battles are somewhat trivialized by that. - Ability to skip animations. Upgrading, dismantling items, researching stuff requires to hold button and wait for animation to finish which is a bit annoying when you get a lot of stuff to do- Boss battles need to be way harder than they are right now- most resources are just an issue in the very beginning, closer to the midgame you don't have any meaningful resource sinks other than for gold/arcane flux. Iron, wood and essences are way too abundant.- Ability to see what tier bonuses buildings give before constructing them.All that said, I really enjoyed the game, it wasn't on my radar at all. Being a huge fan of Disciples 1 and 2 I didn't get the exact sequel of the original games but it's good to see the series is alive and well after the Disciples 3 disaster. I hope this game gets some expansions ironing out the issues, adding more units, classes, skills, items, upgrades, tiers etc. Also would be nice to see units upgrade with level more than just stat adjustments, it was a big thing in the previous games and I think it could make sense here.

_childDocuments_.review: The UI/UX designer of this thing needs to be fired.There is no way of loading the game while in combat. I see that I'm losing a combat and I'd like to re-load, for some reason the only way to do that is to "Quit" to main menu and load from there. Every action (upgrading, training, etc.) needs to go through layers and layers of menus. Escape menu in combat cannot be opened until all enemy animations finish, which is exacerbated by the slowness of those animations (i hate fighting succubi because each time they are attacked you get very slow retaliation). Some screens lack back button (like "Select the area on the map"), it's just beyond me.Overall game feels (at least 2 first areas that I was in) a bit bland and story is Mary Sue'ish. Some dialogue options (most "romance") are somewhat out-of-place. This game is even more "romance"-filled than Baldurs Gate 3 if one judges by the number of those options.It's a shame, because combat is nice, models and graphics is pretty good. But UX and story kill it.

_childDocuments_.review: Disciples Liberation is a huge surprise, definitely one of the better games to have come out in many years. I didn’t expect to like it much until I tried the demo for a couple of days and then I realized how polished and well done it is. You can immediately tell this game is a labor of love from the developers, everything from the audio, visuals and the overall gameplay are on point. I love the unit designs and the overall maps you use to traverse and fight on, exceptionally detailed, unique and just absolutely beautiful. These are some of the best textures I’ve seen in a game, I play with an AMD 6800XT connected to an LG C1 48-inch OLED at 4K, max settings and visually it’s phenomenal, the set pieces on the map and the overall designs are absolutely stellar. I actually prefer playing this with my Xbox One controller and the implementation is flawless, very fluid with a controller, surprisingly. The way you level up is also just so awesome, the way all of your earnings pop-up on left side of the screen and the audio effect that accompanies your progress never gets old, very well done. I’ve seen some complain about the GUI, I’ve had zero issues with it, NONE, it’s very well done, I don’t see where the complaints are founded in this area. Everything is clearly laid out, non-obtrusive, scales well etc., to me, they did a great job of implementing a very effective yet non overbearing GUI. Same for the difficulty, I just don’t get it, I have about 12 hours in the game between the demo and purchasing it and I’ve had an awesome time playing it, and I still run into pockets of enemies I have to avoid due to not be able to win a battle against them, quite often, maybe I just suck, LOL. You're able to seamlessly go from the mission map to your home city or for that matter other regions of the map within seconds. Your home city is beautifully done, looks great and this is where you can upgrade your armies, get new units and learn various magic spells and such. Game really takes off once you get to specialize in one of four classes, I chose Witch.  Unit designs and level ups are fantastic, some of the best I’ve seen. I thought in some of the promotionals they looked too cartoonish, though definitely not the case when actually playing the release. The first time I saw a werewolf, the textures and detail were phenomenal, I was really taken back at how well it was done, whoever worked the textures for this game are seriously talented, big time! I love the unit barks as well, they should be a lot more variety and such, though nevertheless, they’re a nice touch. The four factions are completely different and all bring a very unique approach to your strategy either with or against them. You have the Empire (really cool looking knights and medieval design, exceptionally well done), Elven Alliance, lots of advanced ranged units, multifaceted, the Undead Hordes featuring zombies and such and the Legions of the Damned, possibly my favorite, a great mix of very powerful demon types, all are equally well done and implemented. Between all four you have approximately 50+ recruitable units, love it! The character dialogue in game for your missions are great, you’re basically given free reign to liberate or destroy mostly anything you come into contact with, it’s a refreshing approach, the humor, satire and overall flexibility is great.Frima Studio came out of nowhere and lMO, produced the best TBS strategy game of the year! I can’t wait to see this game get further developed via more DLC factions, units, missions, maps etc. I love TBS games, my favorite genre, comparing this to some of the other games that are similar to it, there’s just no comparison, the overall quality, attention to detail and presentation are second to none. Like many, I wasn’t happy when I saw how this game was going to deviate from its predecessors, I immediately dismissed it, now I see the vision they had and why they chose this route. In the future, I would like to see something like a fun free mode, where you can take your armies and fight on the battlefields already in the game outside of the campaign, a skirmish mode. Think of Heroes of Might and Magic approach, this is something I believe would greatly add to the replay value. I would also like to customize my armies a bit more, with your main protagonist (Avyanna), you have dozens of earned accessories, weapons, armors and such, would be great if you could give some of this equipment to your armies. I would also like to see these accessories visually represented on your main character model more so. The Elven Blueprint issue needs to be addressed ASAP, huge disappointment, they're the first faction I tried to align with, currently there is a bug that prevents you from recruiting most of their units. I most strongly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a great TBS adventure set in an awesome universe with fantastic game design throughout!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this game absolutely plays and feels like Heroes of Might & Magic 4, except you have just one party.  Personally I like this game, but it is pretty much a grind.  I would strongly recommend trying the demo first, which is long enough to give you a pretty good feel for what the whole game is like.Some things that some people will consider good or bad depending on taste.-You can get several quests, but really those no random encounters and it all feels pretty scripted.  - There are 3 skill trees, similar to Titan Quest and Diablo 3.  You do have a lot of choices.  - Like the rest of the game, the battle field (which is most of the game) is basically Heroes style.- The dungeons you go in are about equal to Diablo 2, which isn't good.  Can't move the camera at all.  Can't tell where your going, etc.- There's only one repeating battle music/song and one line for each person on the battefield.  Hearing my people say the same thing over and over when they move gets old REAL fast.  How hard is it to have more than one comment based on class?  A lot of games do it.... grrr.- You will have 2 sub-heroes you can pick as well.  I'd prefer to be able to field more of them, but over half your troops will be basic generic troops.- Trying to figure out what choices will actually give you what rep is pretty hard.  There's no clear indicator of what answer gives what rep.  It's annoying as hell.So I'm not sure why it's labeled Disciples.  The overall theme and classes are Disciples based, but 95% of the game is pure Heroes feel.  I love Heroes of Might and Magic, so it's why I really like the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a large fan of the turn based combat genre, and this fits all my needs. the demo was also a lot of fun and was a huge deciding factor in my purchase of the game. BE WARNED IF YOU PLAY THE DEMO PROGRESS DOES NOT CARRY OVER. I put like 5 and a half hours into that demo and was having a ball. Bought the full game and no saves present. So if you're trying the demo and think you're gonna play the full game. Just bite the bullet. Trust me.Edit: Something else to keep in mind, won't effect my recommendation just a few cons to go with what I enjoyed.In the late game, post chapter 5, There is a laughably bad difficulty spike where enemies starting launching attacks on you with armies of tier 3 and 2 units that you literally cannot reproduce because you lack the leadership ability to make such an army. i'm talking armies of 5+ tier 3 with 4 supporting tier 2s, you cannot stop yourself from taking casualties because they focus fire your weakest unit every time and then you have to fork over resources to replace the guy you just lost. It's very frustrating. Speaking of resources, the in game timer for collecting resources is actually really annoying. Because if you're planning on using one faction's troops like i've been doing then you're only going to use one set of the node thingies and having to wait an in game hour before being able to collect your full cache of resources gets really dumb really quick. I think the game is probably trying to discourage you from using units all from one faction, but I really wanna use the units from that faction, and punishing me by making it stupid hard for me to buy tier 3 units from all 3 buildings is kinda lame.The above are my gripes. If you want a solidly designed turn based turn based strategy with characters interesting enough to get involved with. Then this is a pretty good choice. Keep in mind my above gripes, and to close:  Corisandre is my waifu

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that is being dragged through mud on Metacritic by the boomer cultists because it's not that "holy and immutable game from 20 years ago".It's practically Heroes without the daunting strategy management, but with a good RPG-like story and companion interactions. The strategy management simplified to the base minimum and the focus is put on a isometric tile-based tactical combat, which while being somewhat simple works well.The game is decently voiced and there is a lot of text and interactions between protagonist, companions and the world. The world itself looks appealing, split with areas each of which is a map of its own, like Heroes. You are led through these areas as game progresses to meet and interact with 4 main factions, where you can make various choices to either align or otherwise with either of these factions and gain access to their units and buildings as you go. You are not hard shoehorned into any faction and can mix and match units as you see fit, as long as your relationship with those factions is on a decent level.You gather your companions with respective side quests during Act 1 and 2, as well as gradually gain access to more powers and classes for your protagonist which you can switch at will in your home base. UI is sleek, but clearly console oriented - there are a few management quirks like spellbook, item selection and unit upgrades that feel pretty bad to me. (Why can't I upgrade all my units one click? Why I can't filter or sell useless items? Why radial menu is the only way to quick cast spells?).Overall I think this game is a solid 7/10, meaning GOOD. With a Steam Sale discount this game is a steal. It's that Heroes of Might and Magic without the bull you always secretly wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a big fan of strategy/tactic RPGs, and this game has it's issues, but the game doesn't take itself too serious really.  Combat and skill build flexibility seem to be the best draw here.  Story is ignorable, voice acting is bad, music is good, sound effects are good, traveling across the map is standard CRPG style, but in dungeons it's not good since you can't move the map.  The resource management and building add a different flair to the game even though they're brainless activities. Like the unit variety, wish you could have more than two companions in your party, but special units kind of make up for that. Romancing everything is kind of funny and stupid at the same time.  The game wants you to be morally gray always otherwise you can't really rank up with the factions.  So, early in the play through I just decided to do what each faction wants so I can get the best they offer. If I play again as a caster maybe I'll be neutral and try to win with basics.  Speaking of, game is pretty easy as you can over power the enemy early by stacking up units including back row for buffs and debuffs.  The conquer function is great but it needs to apply to every fight and not only unimportant fights.  Once you get to an area with mostly casters they all hide in the back and never come forward making fighting ranged units pretty silly, mundane, boring, and they 100% of the time prevent you from flanking.  Also, with the choke points usually just stand and wait for the units to come through then get rid of most of them and clean up the rest.  Pretty good but not great. My biggest issue is the viability of magic aoe versus physical units; versatility is really hampered by this but I guess it's worth being a caster to finish the story once.  The game is easy but not as easy for melee as it is for magic.  Certain magic spells and talents really deal a lot of damage.  I don't agree with anyone asking for nerfs to certain abilities but the devs should introduce higher difficulties for better scaling.Lastly, there is a soft lock bug in Nexus where if you leave the cave too soon (teleport back home) you cannot get back to finish the main quest.  I hope the devs fix this fast as it killed a few peoples' games. Using the map shouldn't cause a game breaking bug, and people shouldn't be expected to save a CVS receipt's worth of save files.

Not a big fan of equipement, but shards are a nice enhancer and some parts of armor have tertiary booster similar to full sets in HOMM V and IV. Backline units are a nice change were you can have auto buff/debuff whitout having to remember about it. You can get your butt kicked early on (I see this as a win). In few places you can find a very difficult enemies that you will have to leave for later. Bonus points for sharp graphics, quite easy on CPU/GPU but still looking good. Some negatives could be: A bit confusing menu at times. Some statistics can be read only when accessing correct page (it took me a good while to see what morale does). There are hints in the game, but in general doesn't hold hand to much so mindless playstyle isn't advised.

_childDocuments_.review: The game definitely has potential, but it feels like whoever had the idea for the game, needs to find a better UI and UX team to work with.  I'm only level 8, so there's still hope this may change, but so far character progression feels meaningless - none of what I can invest my skill points into seems significant, nor do my choices of equipment without a better explanation of the stats they boost.  Hard to say for sure this early on (see the next paragraph for why I'm reviewing so early...), but the resource system so far feels similarly meaningless - so far they seem far too easy to obtain for how slowly you go through them.  I'm hoping the story will get better from here, as that seems to have the most potential, though I'm not a fan so far of having to choose between dialogue options that seem like they're in the "choices have consequences" category, but there's no indication before or even after (as far as I can tell) of what those consequences might be, the majority of the time.But most significantly, I've already run into the same type of game-breaking bug twice:  dialogue trees that put me into a never-ending loop, with no way to end the conversation.  This happened with 2 different NPCs now, in 2 separate regions of the game.  This could be fixed so unbelievably easily, by simply adding a button/key to end whatever conversation you're in and return to the map (which I would argue should be part of any dialogue design regardless of such bugs), that running into this over a year after release with no way out but to alt+f4 and load a save, is frankly unforgivable.Barring the bug issue, I would probably recommend the game but with the caveat that I'd wait for a discount.  I got the game via Humble Choice myself, so I can't say I feel cheated exactly, but I would if I'd paid full price for it.  As it stands, having already paid for it, I'll probably continue playing to see how long it is before I run into another game-breaking bug.  Depending on how quickly that happens, I may end up uninstalling with most of the game left unplayed.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best turn based battle RPG type game I have ever played. An absolute gem that has gone top of my list of such games. You build a party and add combatants to it yourself, you may pick up companions along the way depending on your choices in the campaign, there are many branching possibilities.  Like in King Arthur you also have a home castle to restore and recruit from which is a nice touch. There are several distant lands to go and explore all with differing atmosphere ranging from the Undead through to Elves. You collect loot of various types and explore crypts and dungeons etc. There are mana sources you can tap into and also healing fountains where your party can can return to full health. Beware some of the treasure chests, they may be guarded when you attempt to pick them up. The graphics are first rate and the variety of enemies/allies wide ranging. You can upgrade your hero throughout and research new magic spells. There are main quests and side quests with rewards. A solid and very enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: 18 hours in and I get the known "no location on world map" bug. Every manual/quick/auto save from the past three days has the same bug, so I have lost 18 hours of progression. Validated data, uninstalled, reinstalled...nothing fixes it. I'm pretty sure it happened when I went to the next quest area in the main story line, but decided that I wanted to finish up in the undead lands first before continuing, so I went back...which was likely the last time the world map worked.The game is grindy fun/interesting/annoying/boring/buggy, all at once...so I am tempted to start another game and play as a different "class"...but I also fear losing all my progression again. I do like the freedom of doing just about anything you want to do within the story and with consequences, plus there are some surprising choices you can make, but it isn't interesting enough to really make me want to do it all a second time. If they fixed most of the bugs (most importantly this game breaking one), I would strongly consider going back, but I would not recommend this game to anyone after experiencing this particular bug.I will watch the game patches for a while to see if this bug is fixed, but I will probably never see a fix for my current run (especially if the bug is related to save files), so I'll likely just uninstall the game again and forget it ever existed in about a month.Update 12/21/2021: A new patch was just released today and it didn't fix my problem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more similar to Kings Bounty/HoMM than to previous Disciples games, but that's the part I actually like about it. You have a hero who travels with a small army around the map completing quests, gathering resources, and killing enemies. You also have a castle to build and upgrade structures and hire units. That part is rather basic, but it works, even though the writing and mission design is not great.What I don't like, is how shallow and repetitive the battles are. Even though you can automatically win some of them (when your army is significantly stronger and that's not a story related fight), you still have to play out the majority of the battles, and they quickly become very boring. Every unit has only a basic attack and another active ability (the attack has no cooldown, the ability usually has 3-4 turns cooldown), so every fight turns into attacking every turn and sometimes using an ability.The main hero has more abilities (actually, the whole book of spells, but first you need to find a scroll and learn it), but majority of them are really basic and not fun to play.And since the fights are usually 7v7 or have even more units, it takes ages to play them out even at 300% speed. I am writing this review after having 3 (three!) absolutely identical fights in a row with every one of them taking 15-20 minutes to finish. It's zero fun and feels more like work than a game.Bottom line, there are plenty of superior turn based games with more meaningful progression, better designed battles, and interesting characters/units. Play this one only if you are a die hard fun of Disciples franchise or have no better turn based tactics to choose from.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a mixed review here.The tactical turn-based combat is good. It's the best part of the game. It's solid, it's interesting, it's different. There's loot and upgrades and team synergies, all good things.The story is its weakest part. The game aspires to be the next Dragon Age with morally ambiguous characters, romance options, multiple endings and "grown up" themes.What we got instead is tonal whiplash. The writers didn't talk to each other. One quest is wholesome fun of gathering bones for a golem who acts like a puppy, the next one you're having an orgy on top of a throne made of living flesh and it's uh... questionable at best.There is no continuity between events. There isn't any character development, there are just people who throw random lines at each other and it's hard to relate to them because I don't know them. Who am I and what am I doing here? What is my motivation?There are a lot of things this game has going for it, but all those parts don't quite connect to each other. Zone transitions seem like a total memory wipe for all my companions. There isn't continuity. What is this city we just got teleported to? Why is it here? How did I go from mercenary thug to mayor? What is this land we're all fighting for? The religious Empire whom I've pissed off at every turn, still thinks I'm neutral with them, and the Rebels I've helped never quite united around me. Consequences, where are they?I've played for a while hoping to find answers but when I realized it's going to be more humorous lines punctuated by macabre randomness I lost interest, mostly because I can't relate to any of my companions or the protagonist. At 42 hours in, you'd think I know at least one person?Anyway, positive review for combat. The story is why I washed out. If you want to have some tactical turn-based encounters with magic, it's got it. Don't expect a story line you can follow to go with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Guys, I have played through the campaign in normal difficulty. This game is plainly unfinished mobile game somehow published on pc market. It is a spinoff that has nothing to do with its predecessors, apart from turn based combat and 2d perspective.Let me start from the good:The graphics. Pretty spell particle effects. Apart from questionable looks of some units (extra chromosome dracolich) very nice.Early game combat is quite fun.Game does not crash, works fast and stable.Music is okWell now the bad:Maps. They look big when you open the map, but at least 40% of map is unaccessible and there is random gate standing that prevents you going any further. Maybe it changes in unlocked liberation mode, but i really have no inclination to check after first playthrough.Economy. I hate the income system that requires you to remember to click "gather resources" button every hour or your "buffer" storage overflows and you stop gaining resources. When you click the button, resources magically go to your resoure pool and you start gathering resources to your "buffer" storage again. Why? I dont know. This is made purely to inconvenience player to go to the city and waste couple of seconds. Resources are sprinkled all over the map without any reason or logic, mostly wood, which is basically worthless. There is no map in dungeons. Pure laziness from the devs. Fortunately dungeons usually have very basic layout.Unit animations are terribly slow. 100% speed is unplayable, 200% was still too slow for me. 300% was acceptable. Units say phrases when moving, casting or attacking. Half or them make no sense, or are poorly recorded. Their voices are fun for first three battles, then quickly became annoying. Especially three of them - chihuahua growls of werelopards and their undead variants, high on acid sorceresses and stuffy nose elementalists. Horrible to listen to and you battle them very often.Backline buffs are imbalanced to the point of being dumb. Dryad warpriestess combo is simply absurd, combined with bone golem, whole enemy army can wipe itself from damage reflect. Buffs have lengthy animations that are shown before every battle. They are replayed every time new unit goes into play - summons. Playing at 300% animation speed you can waste up to a minute or more every battle watching your or enemy backline buffing trash throwaway units.Backline nukes make game really annoying sometimes, as game has way too many nukes in general.Battlefield map is for some reason long and narrow and for some unknown reason unbelieveably cluttered. Sometimes i have had the feeling of fighting in supermarket aisles. There is very little place for any strategy and planning, Just boring outhealing enemy aoe wave and grinding through enemy army hp.Combat is going to hell starting mid-late game. In very narrow narrow battlefields, full of obstacles you have to face armies full of aoe attacks and game devolves to surviving all the first turn nukes, if most of your units survived, the battle is already won. Just bait their aoe with some trash sacrifice unit and its easy. Terrible enemy ai helps a lot, nuking its own units half of the time. Melee units like to waste their aoe abilities on single bait units. Enemy AI is terrible in general, it likes to run archers into your frontline or sometimes gets stuck behind a rock when pathfinding fails. Or wipe half its army hp with frost giant blizzard. Unit abilities effects are inconsistent. Melee units do not damage allies with aoe skills. Why does holy avenger wipe allies with consecrated ground? Nobody knows. Why my archers have no line of sight and cant attack enemy casters, when they can cast spells on you perfectly fine? This makes half of elven units obsolete on cluttered battlefields. It is always better to take units that ignore los.Seriously, why almost every unit, starting t2, was given aoe, be it cleaving attack, aoe taunt, aoe nuke+debuff taunt, aoe heal or nuke? It made battles last very short (because ai has really no clue how to use healing abilities efficiently}, i never used ultimate skill apart from boss battles, because everything was dead in 3 rounds and ultimate ability has like 6 round spoolup. My tactic was to cast primal roar first round and bumrush enemy with my aoe taunt units, basically disabling 2/3 of enemy units. Battle won. In lategame i just ran into enemy army with my main character and cast ABSURDALLY  overpowered t2 spell solar eclipse. Bam, half of enemy army is basically harmless. Battle is already won in first move. And I was not even playing a mage.When it comes to your main character, gear system is hilariously bad. You are beind voimited on with trash gear througout the whole game and the only thing to do is to dismantle it for resources. The amount you get is clearly aimed at equipping your companions, but idea was scrapped and you are stuck with one hundred worthless helmets that have like three or four models. What is more, you cannot even scrap this trash easily. You have to rightclick item and wait for an animation to end. There is no point to this animation, it is purely to waste player time and prolong the gametime. Oh, and the rarer the item is the longer it takes to scrap. Click and hold is hilariously bad mechanic on pc, where you can precisely operate with mouse and keyboard.If i wanted to scrap all of my helmets before last boss, it would take me more than 10min to do so, and this only one type of gear. Scrapping trash from your whole inventory during course of your playthorugh will probably take more than an hour or more.Did I mentioned that story of the game is really really bad? Literally C tier isekai webnovel has better writting. Fallout 4 dialogues are masterpiece compared to conversations between your mc and companions. Sidequests are forgettable and do not reward you with anything too intresting in particular aside from spells.Boss battles are nothing special.So, in conclusion, i would give this game like 4, maybe 5/10. Game is clearly unfinished and in serious need of balance patch. Do not buy if it is not heavily discounted.Maybe game gets better in new unlocked liberation mode but after normal campaingn experience i have no inspiration to try it, as the game tries to waste hours of my time with annoying, obsolete playtime prolonging mechanics

What happens if my dex goes up by 10?  Game won't tell you.  And while I like a little mystery in magic, movies and novels, not in my games. _childDocuments_.review: Instead of listing bulletpoints, I will try to write my review in a more fluid manner.Let me start this review by saying I am a long time Disciples franchise fan, especially Disciples 2. I still remember the day I received Disciples 2 RotE disc for Christmas almost 20 years ago as a kid. I've played hundreds and hundreds of hours of it to this day. Even now I still play Disciples 2, custom sagas, try out different mods. So I am as much of a Disciples 2 fanboy as your next guy.When I heard D: Liberation is coming out, it was a big shock to me as I wasn't expecting for the franchise to be alive even knowing that Kalypso has bought the rights to the game. I promptly signed up to participate in beta, and am very thankful for having this opportunity. As of right now, I have around 30hr in closed beta, and 34hrs at the time of this review.The game is definitely flashy (especially the combat effects) and beautiful. It's actually magical to return to the land of Nevendaar and see its current, modern version of it. I loved seeing the environment and places in a way that I only imagined when looking at the old D2. The game claims to be dark fantasy, and that definitely holds somewhat true. Some of the story and dialogue definitely is dark, however the art style they chose wasn't the most successful one when it comes to creating "dark" feeling. There have been places with body parts and blood pits, with vicious gore on the walls, and the most it elicited from me was a "lol" because it looked like a meme. The beautiful places do look good, but the ones that were supposed to be morbid are lacking. Overall, it's a pleasant new trip to Nevendaar.The game plays smoothly, and the collecting of items and levelling up is very engaging. At some point, you can select one from 4 classes, each specialising in magic or melee. Later in the game, the class you selected gets an advancement to unlock more abilities making you more powerful. Combat is satisfying in a sense that it is flashy and over the top like you'd expect a Disciples game to be. The downside, however, is that combat is ridiculously easy. There is no challenge whatsoever. You'd be cutting through the enemies like hot knife through butter, never thinking twice whether your move is the right one. There is a loading tip saying "If one strategy doesn't work, then try something else". Gurl, what strategy? Just crush everything.But I can deal with any of those. The biggest downside of D: Liberation for me are the units. 4 factions exist in this game - Empire, Undead, Legions, Elves. You can build a building in your city where you can recruit units into your squad. As you progress the game and complete quests, you will gain/lose faction reputation. Once your reputation increases, you will be able to recruit higher tier units of corresponding factions. Now the variety of units is just... I don't want to swear so I won't, but it's horrendous for a £35 game with a franchise name "Disciples". The units between factions are a copy paste of each other with different "skins", something you'd mostly see in indie games or mobile games. They only created 5-10 skeletons and then spread them across 60+ units. Your companions are not unique either - they are just copies of T3/4 units with a skin and increased stats with ability to equip weapons, sharing the same battle actions (apart from Ultimates). If that's not all, then majority of NPCs in the game are just copy pasted units too. Imagine meeting a major plot related character only for it to look exactly like someone you've had in your squad roster since the beginning of the game. It's honestly appalling on so many levels and I would downvote this game just because of this. This is a major miss for me. I am not a dev but all I can think of is "where did Frima and Kalypso use all that money in... console certification checks and submission?"The best part that I loved about the game, though, is that it's a Disciples game. They massively expanded the story and lore, and wrote new things that can be used in the future as "canon" to develop more games. That is exciting. There are some lore points that make no sense in regards to D1/2 lore consistency, but there are not so many of those to be offputting. The way the story is told is also a bit confusing, but not so much that you're not able to follow it. There's definitely an element where you have to engage your own imagination to cover some blanks. There are even characters from the main Disciples line! Overall, this has been a plus for me and despite everything else I've said, it's been an enjoyable game that I am still going through.I also want to note, that it seems Frima and Kalypso are reading, engaging, and listening to the players. They implemented several things since closed beta that was a popular demand such as animation speed. And they are discussing about giving the players the ability to increase game difficulty!The last point I want to say is that this is not Disciples 4, it's not a successor for Disciples 2 or 3, and it's not trying to be (despite apparently happening in canon after events of D3). This is a spin off that expands Nevendaar's universe and should be treated as such. People shouldn't listen to those who fanatically hate everything that is not D2. This game, as I see it, is an attempt to bring new players into the franchise with an attempt to revive it. If the game is doing well, perhaps we will get an actual D2 successor! Any Disciples is good for the franchise at this point, even if just for the story, and I am super excited for this title despite several things the devs have missed the mark on. I wish Kalypso the very best success with this title and I hope that I will see more of this franchise in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game with only one major flaw: The vast majority of the hundreds of battles are very similar and become a sort of grind routine (if you do them all)- Description: You govern a castle in which you recruit troops, upgrade stuff, learn spells. From there you venture into one region at a time, which are semi free roam and contain between 10-30 encounters. Here you progress story, companion quests and side missions. After you finish the main questline in one region, you can then select another. The fights are turn based on some sort of arena ground with obstacles and bottlenecks. - Good:- Looks good- Lot of content (68 hours to finish for me doing almost all encounters)- Level cap of MC so high that you won't reach it, so you can keep levelling- Nice variety of gear, upgrades, spells, abilities and units- I am not into lore, and skipped most dialogue. There seem to be a profound story, with seeminly good lore. But it is not forced upon you and skipping is fast- Meaningful choices regarding keeping companions at your side and balancing faction rep (needed for advanced units)- Bad:- Only one thing: The fights get very very repetative, with only a handful of boss fights, and the rest feel very generic and uninspired. If you doubt about buying, watch some fight vids, because if you seen one, you seen all (though with different units). Of course you do not need to do all encounters, like me. And about 20% you can autoresolve.- Gameplay tips:- When I started I redid encounters if I lost troops. Do this only with rare, unique troops you get through your marketplace or encounters. Your heroes cannot die and all troops you can recruit from faction buildings are very very cheaply replaced and upgraded to your level.- I saw some people complaining about this being hard. I played on normal setting and the beginning was challenging, but I made a caster lord which took 3-6 units in first turn (from mid game on, when you get Area Of Effect Spells), and usually my battles lasted 2-4 turns throughout late game. Just concentrate Area Of Effect abilities on packs of enemies, and have some units/heroes that can paralize other enemies from far. I had two different healers in backrow and the Empire unit that beams enemies, and after killing one goes on (getting up to 6 kills in succession for me).- I found melee relatively weak compared to ranged or magic, mainly because you loose half your action points by getting into position, and having limited AoE abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeaaaahhhh... when a game does not fully grab your attention in the first 10 hours, something's off.The intro cutscene and the initial tutorial section feel unfinished and confusing. Suddenly portal wheeeeeeee! No time to explain! Mysterious castle! Magic powers! It's fate! You're the one! You'll know it when it happens.The voice actors for the main character and companion so far are not bad, but the heroine failed to make me care for her fate. There's character building for her companion but not her, pretty much. You know that she's the boss and inspires devotion and is powerful and then gets more powerful, all of which is unexplained. There's even a skill that makes enemies OMG so scared of you, but with the utter lack of context for what happens the notion is more comical than anything.When you look at the RPG and town-building aspect, it's not really better. The game throws four unit types and three spells at you from the start, you quickly capture a couple mines and sawmills and then over the course of ten hours there's no meaningful progression except some generic loot that quickly devolves into finding the same boring equivalent stuff to what you have. No new unit, no new spell, no new castle building, just a few level-ups for your units and three skill points spent with very little impact. There's not even any real thing to spend your money on.As others have mentioned, combat is really slow, as units have huge HP and pitiful damage for the most part. I ended up skipping fights where I could've easily won, something I rarely do in HOMM. Even if you know you're gonna win it just drags on. At least the arenas you fight on are somewhat varied with various types of obstacles and interactive objects. The notion of flanking helps speed things up a bit with tactics by boosting damage, but there's no zone of control which I feel would've improved this game. One of the starting unit also has an interesting attack which targets a whole line, adding more tactical feel. I'd like to see where this goes, but progress is insanely slow.On the positive side, the map looks nice and conveys a good feeling of exploration, and quests are more interesting than your average King's Bounty or Heroes of Might & Magic map exploration. The world lore is also pretty intriguing, although it seems to lean a bit too heavily into the "evil catholic church" trope, complete with torture and all, and then trying to make some of its members sympathetic. It's heavy-handed and doesn't quite work.Overall, this is an unfinished-feeling game where they didn't have time to tie up the story, lore and characters into a coherent whole. They also did the dumb "insta-saviour" thing while trying to pretend the story is serious - maybe because they picked a woman and were afraid to make fun of her, while they'd have no qualms ridiculizing a super-macho insta-hero dude? Feels like someone was trying to collect virtue points but did not pass go and didn't collect 200$.Needless to say, they didn't take the time to balance the content either, as the progression is utterly unsatisfying.I'm curious to see where the story goes and whether the quest choices significantly affect the world besides just score with the factions, but it'll take me some willpower to go back despite the boredom, and that's a very, very bad sign. Your call on whether you wanna bet on the game coming into its own after 10h.

_childDocuments_.review: Disciples: Liberation is easy to recommend for fans of Heroes of Might & Magic or King's Bounty style gameplay. It's a bit simplistic, but otherwise a solid take on both the real-time RPG questing and exploration, as well as the turn-based combat with small armies of units. As for the base building part: there's only one so it's kinda there for flavor only.The entire theme of the game is about living in the moment and worrying about consequences later, and by flipping my brain switch to a similar mode of "take the writing as it comes and don't think about it until later" it was indeed enjoyable! That mode is important, so make sure to RTFM - yes, the one for your brain - and find it so you can have some fun with the story too.Almost every encounter in the game follows a rhythm of providing little information prior to you making a decision, only to provide both consequences and context afterwards. It goes so far with this that it seems to lampoon this kind of writing in other works and it flips around and becomes kinda good as long as you're in the right headspace. It also works  well for the main narrative, which is constantly revealing new layers and a deeper rabbit hole to keep jumping into. Choices don't really matter for anything but companion (party member) stories / faction approval though...Still despite all the above, there is some Disciples in here and it's the setting. It's dark, especially towards the end. There's oceans of blood. Some existential horror. And quite a few nods to prior games towards the end. A Disciples fan may not like where this game takes it all as it gets rather extreme in ... resolving things, but it's certainly not fluffy bunny Dragon Age fantasy.And better yet: no stupid Total War blood DLC! The base game provides. Get a few vampires together and you can coat the entire map in blood explosions! They even do tons of damage! Hurrah!Sadly, there were some downsides to this 100+ hour game. The main one being that length actually, because it's heavily padded. If you pick this up, don't be like me and fight every battle. Just pick the Conquer option. Any battle you can Conquer (auto-win) is pure filler and a guaranteed win anyway. It'll probably save you like 50-60% of that play time and definitely make the game less of a slog towards the middle. Especially with the game's animations being so slow that 300% combat speed feels like it should be  the normal 100%, and there really needs to be a 600% option.Another downside is that the game uses Unity Engine. It's a relatively new version, so G-SYNC works and so do high core count CPUs, but it's still just not great when it comes to performance. This game seems simple to optimize, mostly just small combat arenas with a few 3D models doing animations, but the performance is quite bad. Granted, I do need a new GPU too, so YMMV. There also seems to be a small memory leak, so restarting sometimes will help performance if you play long sessions.The developers also clearly cut some corners with some of the implementation to get it out the door, like the game constantly checking backline units for actions (when they have none) before going to the next turn, wasting more time. As well as constant UI background noises... when the AI is doing moves! And the audio balance is horrific, with dialogue usually being about 60% the volume of everything else. And some of the ambient noise is just an annoying static noise effect.This is mostly just nitpicking on an otherwise enjoyable experience. Don't expect a GOTY experience. Don't expect best-in-class HoMM gameplay. Don't expect magnificent writing that will drag you into some mindblowing experience. Do expect a fun over-the-top grimdark fantasy romp with solid gameplay. And post-patches in 2022: "conquer" anything and everything you can to avoid massive easy battle padding.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent tactic RPG, though not one of the best. May not be the squeal many fans are looking for, but the series will live on.Pros:1. an excellent combat system based on the combat in Reincarnation, but more complex in a good way. The back-line supporting position is an especially innovative and refreshing add-on to the combat system of Disciples series. 2. Your choice usually matters3. plenty of call-backs about characters and events from previous gamesCons:1. Slot cap for a party is too high. This may not seem to be a problem at first, but battle between two full parties can be dragging. It is even worse when the game has stunning but dragging attack / skill animations, although you have the option to turn up animation speed.2. Lack of both growth potential and situational use for most low tier units, which limits the versatility of party set-ups way before the late game.3. Probably one of the worst intro quest in gaming history, plot-wise.4. The most Mary Sue story I have seen in recent years...Other thoughts1. There is no difficulty option right now. Hardcore RPG players may find the current game too easy and system too exploitable.2. Resource gathering is still STG-like in Liberation, but players don't need to defend their resources like they do in previous games. I personally don't mind the design choice here, but I've heard someone complain about this.3. Old fans may find some plots and setting in Liberation exciting, because they add more details to the existing lore; however, some fans may find a few of them confusing, or even down right annoying.Overall, Liberation is an RPG worth playing. Just don't expect it to be Disciples 4.Thanks the developer for a different Disciples. This time, a good game, and more importantly a complete one.Thanks again for the developers' effort, to make sure that the series will carry on, one way or another.Just, can we bring back our beloved dwarves? Pretty please?

Furthermore there's a lot of systems which are poorly implemented and serve no purpose but to waste your time. The story is decent though generic, but the world is empty and uninspired. You'll quickly see everything the game has to offer. It's wide as an ocean but shallow as a pond.The main issue with the game is the speed in which the combat progresses. It moves glacially slow - even at 300%. Too much of my current play time has been spend waiting for auto-buffs and slow transitions between the action phases of each unit. The combat only feels worse due to the lack of strategic options. It doesn't take long to figure out and optimal strategy and then repeat ad infinitum. That is untill you gain some levels and become so overpowered, the strategic element all but dissappers. The result? Refraining from using a complete unit-board, just so your main character and companion can get their actions off even faster. The loot system is a broken mess. There's a lot of items to collect, but they're just slabs of stats, and you'll end up collecting so many items that are so useless, you'll dismantle them. Which can be done one at the time.The story is bland, uninspired dark fantasy, which would be alright, had it not been for a boring and empty-feeling world, where each area quickly resembles the next. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I do recommend this game but there are some downsides and some radical changes in comparison to the previous Disciples entries.This game is somewhat independent from the other Disciples titles and reinvents the well established formula of these RPG strategies. This will make it or brake it for someone as this game introduces crucial changes:1) game is real time in the main map and only combat is turn based. This feels nice until player realizes that there are no classic enemy armies with the enemy hero chasing on the map and conquering cities and resources. All resources are there for the player to be claimed and are generated per minute.2) with the real time approach, player does not conquer cities as in previous games, instead, player controls only one city Yllian and this city is never in danger to be conquered. This also brings a limitation of how fast player can build the city and there are progression gates behind the story.3) Player always plays as Avyana (human) and can recruit other champions and they are always story related.  Player has a first companion champion Orion from the get go and they are powerful units, however in the initial campaign, player can have up to 2 such champions in the party for combat.The game is overall nice and fighting does feel as old titles of the same genre. However, the artstyle is changed - it is not so dark as before and also it doesn't change the map when player conquers certain areas (i.e. in previous title player could conquer a node and it would change it depending which faction player plays). For the map it is for the most part easy to distinct and spot various items. The story is pretty much woke where player is tasked to: . I don't know how that is possible but ok we will go with it.UI is the oddest thing in this game. For the most part it is quite good but some choices are weird. Sometimes player just need to click, sometimes to hold left mouse button, sometimes the right mouse button. In some areas keybindings don't work (i.e. 'U' key for units doesn't work in the city but works in the map mode). Gear require some better distinction regarding the tier types as slim coloured line is hard to notice. Coat of arms of the alliances are nice but are beneath the alliance name, status and relationship bar... Therew are just weird things including the Journal which doesn't tell you where certain quest needs to be completed but instead player needs to right click on the quest and go in some area and if white arrow shows then on that map player needs to do a quest - weird.Units are nice but questionable - some with their design, some with their abilities. Design wise, I am not happy with the elves at all since the style is quite inconsistent. Some are made of ice/mana, some are looking as occultists and shady rogues while others look like have clothing inspired by the natives from the southern America. When it comes to abilities, it is quite inconsistent in regards for the damage type ( as an example to have humans using primal magic and shadow damage while it should be using divine damage). Then the visuals of some abilities is also inconsistent (one of the late spells that Avy is casting is supposedly making divine and shadow damage but visually looks like a huge fiery ball). Also some abilities that have a persistent AoE are making it hard to resemble which unit is there or if there was another environmental effect underneath. Difficulty is quite nice depending on which difficulty setting is being played. Some encounters might give a lot of challenge to the player. Campaign is a lengthy one and I think it is a good thing. Upon finishing the campaign there is a liberator mode unlocked which plays a bit differently and . With that said, there is no custom mode where player could potentially play as some of the companions etc (disclaimer I haven't played multiplayer). What is also illogical is that Avy can NOT open portal to Yllian while inside to dungeons which is illogical to me, but dungeons are not too big so it is bearable.All in all it is a fun game, nice encounters and serviceable story and colourful companions. I just think that all the mentioned negatives are ruining the experience. That is why I recommend this game but barely.

_childDocuments_.review: Disciples: Liberation further deviates from the Disciples II formula, but does so in a way that feels fresh. Unlike previous installments, Liberation is an RPG with tactical combat, real-time strategy, and choice-matters story elements. Since it wears many hats, it sometimes lacks a clear identity, but overall it manages to balance its many aspects well.The Good- Solid graphics and performance (on a Nvidia 1060 Ti)- Excellent visual effects- Satisfying tactical combat with limitless possibilities- Good conveyance of attributes and game mechanics- Decent replayability through story and hero progressionThe Bad- Combat can be tedious when large armies, bosses, and/or healing is involved- There are still a few bugs that need to be resolved- Unit and skill progression gated by faction reputation, which is constantly changingThe Ugly- Outcomes of choices can be hard to predict- Voice acting is sometimes awkward (but generally passable)- A few harsh difficulty spikes
_childDocuments_.name: Disciples: Liberation

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a review before, but with Disciples I just have to do it. I've now played through the game in a few weeks after about 35 hours of gameplay, as it was incredibly fun. The characters are great, both in terms of design and character development. The characters really grow on you, so that you often have a hard time making decisions during dialogues. And that's what was great. It felt like I was actually deciding where the journey was going at most times. The story overall was exciting until the end and I didn't have a moment where I got bored with the game.However, I still have a few criticisms. As great as the characters and story as well as the world design are, many battles with the same enemies often felt a bit repetitive and I was happy when I didn't have to fight and got ahead with diplomacy. The best battles were when they were tricky and I had to think to come to a solution. From the middle of the game, however, Avyanna was so strong that I just had to use a few spells and the round was often decided before the opponent's first move.Overall, though, I can definitely recommend the game. Story is great, setting and sound design is awesome. The game and the units look great and during the whole time of playing I only had two minor bugs, which were fixed by reloading.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but it's not a good game. Otherwise, give a skip.The story is meh, and the farther I got in the worse it got. The romance system doesn't really feel like romance, it's more just sleeping with everyone. Companions don't really matter in general.The combat is solid. Lots of different units to choose from, and different ways to use them. You find a ton of weapons and armor, but only the main character can use it so most of it is just vendor trash. Never really felt like I was managing my resources, there was just a ton of it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is good but if you don't like 4x games you won't like it. The Xbox port of this game was apparently a buggy mess on launch from what I've read but I have come across no bugs after playing for 60 hours. I think that playing a game without bugs is a good first impression. The music isn't bad but there are only a few tracks that play and it gets old fast. The story while it does have some interesting lore isn't all that interesting but the game play is addictive and the art design is fantastic. There is another game that came out recently called King's Bounty 2 which I played not that long ago that is very similar. They both have a faction system that upgrades your army as you improve your relations with a particular group, they are both 4x games with army turn based combat, and they both have you play as the leader of an army who rides around everywhere on a horse. The difference is that King's bounty had lazy art direction when it came to it's characters and units. Every character and unit was copy pasted variants of one another. Disciples is like a better version of King's Bounty 2 with way better art direction and quality of life upgrades. What do I mean by a quality of life upgrade in Disciples from King's Bounty 2? King's Bounty 2 had an unskippable 2 second animation every time you got off your horse to pick something up off the ground and then another 2 second animation every time you had to remount and had infrequent fast travel points that had you riding all over the map on your incredibly slow mount. You don't have to worry about that in Disciples Liberation. Avy has magic and an army at her disposal. if she wants to pick something up off the ground she can order some of her soldiers to pick up piles of iron ore or gold. She doesn't have to dismount and haul loads of material and equipment around like some dirty peasant.
