_childDocuments_.review: A complete rework of the franchise. But still a functional game in its own right.Pro:+ Nice art+ Plenty of content on release+ Yay TBS strategy games+ Instant resolve against weak opponents+ Good keybinding for a pc game+ Shard system somewhat encourages diverse team units+ Army units still level, which is niceCon:- The game is now child-friendly, the dark side of the story has been caned- only 1 character can equip armour and the player is flooded with it creating busy work and meaningless rewards- The writing is inline with anime, everyone monologues for no good reason. The writer lacks the ability to set a mood so everything is either comedy or "I kill you"- Citadels have been scrapped, instead player gets 7 pillars to build on.- Less than a quarter of the game is voiced, small complaint- The original grim artwork has been canned in favour of comedic evil enemy- Combat is very clunky and slow- Very easy- Voice acting is inline with anime Dub, majority is passable but none of it is capable of showing anger/desperation/insanity that the Japanese voice actors can do in anime and this game is much the same.- Yay to play a forced female protag + dialogue option to hit on half the male characters. Because that's something as a man I find entertaining. Lets see how many people that play this game actually find that as a positive function. The game has done many things I wished it did not but for the sake of the genre I’m still giving it a thumbs up. Tho at this rate if it keeps going i will change this review to a negative.My issues that I find other will have are as follows:1.	Four factions one story. Though I understand this is much cheaper to develop and caters to the new age of “Free-roam” this also means a washed down story for the four factions.2.	Disciples has always been a grim series with dark and in its own way “Kool” artwork. This is no more, the undead and demons are now an emo curvy art stile while the tier one Elven unit LITERALLY ATTACK WITH FARTS.3.	The designer of this game made the amateur mistake of forcing every unit’s animation to be watched before the next unit activating, this causes every battle to feel insanely slow. Perhaps this will be a QoL change later where only the first 1 sec of their action or none will lock the game state into watching the animation and instantly allow the next unit to move. Otherwise for 10+ units on the board it is far too slow.4.	All game play balancing has been thrown out the window

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the story and the gameplay. I did feel a bit over leveled at one point, because I was doing every single quest in the map area before leaving it, as well as capturing all of the resource points. A bit of level scaling might have been nice. The difficulty did go up, and I feel this problem less acutely. That being said, the combat system is fantastic. As someone who plays these kinds of games often, it managed to feel intuitive as well as unique and challenging. The story is engaging, and actually forces you to make hard choices. Many other games will provide a magical option that makes everyone happy.  I love the main character, and how they managed to make her have a distinct personality, while also allowing you to make choices in how she acts. The companions are interesting and fun. Although....as a hetero lady playing...there is a difference in the romanceable companions that makes feel a bit like the creators were mostly thinking of male players....two gruff men who speak in incomplete sentences about honor and vengeance, a power hungry morally near-black necromancer who looks to be dying, and a holy man who has grandpa vibes. Orion is the only normal one. I may be a lesbian this playthrough. But that is a small gripe that does not do much to lessen the enjoyability of this game, and is an extremely small element. The characters as a whole, and viewed with a platonic eye, are engaging and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by no means perfect.  It has its flaws, some of them pretty chunky ones, but I've played this game for 68 hours, and most of that was enjoyable.Pros:- Story choices matter- Varied world and mobs- Plots short enough to keep you moving and interested- Good replay valueCons:- The combat is too slow.  300% speed is not fast enough- Bosses are terrible.  Uninteresting and tedious.  (but there aren't many of them)- Most gear is utterly useless (although you can dismantle them for gold etc)- Not enough combat encounters can be skipped when you are over-levelled for them- Ultimate skills seem very poorly tunedThe game I think can be improved greatly if you use a mod to speed up movement and combat.   Although that shouldn't be necessary to install mods to enjoy a game, the devs haven't added faster speeds than 300%, so we have to do what we can ourselves.  Combat won't feel so tedious at times with the faster speed.  The other Cons are small compared to this, so if you can work around it with a mod, I would advise you to.

_childDocuments_.review: I have spent some considerable time with the demo and about 9 hours with the retail game so far. This is by no means a full/complete review as I have yet to see how the story will ultimately play out. With that being said here are my initial impressions of Liberation.So lets address the elephant in the room. While it carries the Disciples name it is very much unlike previous games in the series. In essence this is a reboot or different take for the series. It very much feels far more like a Heroes of Might and Magic or a Kings Bounty. This is sure to disappoint some who were expecting a game in the vein of Disciples II and I will touch on this a bit later. Combat now takes place on a hex based grid (like Disciples 3 before it) as opposed to the more static battles of the past. It has it's pros and cons. Flanking and unit placement do open up some strategic options. There is also a "backline" Where up to three units can provide passive benefits to your allies. The problem is with the amount of battles a certain degree of tedium can set in. The devs have to their credit listened to feedback and tried to alleviate this by allowing you to speed up enemy unit turns. It does help a lot but bear in mind that you are going to be fighting a lot of the same units over and over. The problems can be compounded when you fight a lot of ranged units that tend to hang out at the other end of the map. You typically end up in a protracted battle against melee units before finally making your way to the back where the healers and other ranged units keep running about until you all but box them in. The game does offer quite a lot of quests to complete and the maps you traverse can feel quite sprawling with a lot to see. And to it's credit there are nods/references to Disciples 2 Dark Prophecy for eagle eyed series vets. For instance references to Hubert De Layle and Yata Halli are among those I found. The game has a companion system where characters that you recruit feel like decent characters in their own right with their own motivations. Unfortunately these companions often share models with bog standard unit types. Take Corisandre for instance who is one of my favorites for her healing abilities. She looks virtually identical to other priestesses you face in battle. Speaking of characters, lets talk about the main character of Avyanna...I appreciate the attempt to craft an original hero and give them their own story within the world of Disciples. Avyanna herself is a likable character. However the dialogue and options presented can at times feel at odds within the context of the world. Being more of an RPG you are able to choose dialogue options but many times these options can feel like your pidgeonholed. Take an early quest where your tasked with siding with either the elves or the human over a 10 year old boy who had trespassed and was killed by said elves. The choice boils down to whether you justify said child or not. Witcher 3 for instance is all about choice and the "Lesser evil". But the choice as presented in the scenario I outlined above had no "lesser evil". These choices play into a "reputation" system for the various factions. Empire, Elven Alliance, Undead Hordes, Legions of the Damned. No dwarves again I am afraid though there is a story/lore reason and they do address it in the game. The problem I have with this reputation/faction system is that I've never really got the impression that humans would willingly seek out alliances with the legion or undead hordes. They have also written the empire to be quite a bit darker. It's a different take on the Empire and one that kind of lines up with the state the Empire is in in previous entries. The problem is if you really want access to certain units be it the empire's knights or some of the elven units? You need good standing and good standing with one faction affects standing with another. Further still, negative reputation gives your units a passive debuff that gets worse the worse your reputation is. In this sense the game kind of pidgeonholes you again regarding what units you may get access too. And these units never feel as precious as they did in the previous games where you promote them and change class via upgrades to your capital. Here the units feel more like disposable canon fodder and can easily be replaced should they fall by spending some resources like Gold, etc.Resources themselves are handled differently. In previous Disciples games you changed the terrain via planting rods to capture gold mines, or rune stones. The terrain based resource mechanic is gone here. Instead you capture buildings for things like lumber, or gold which generates over time. You then collect it at the capital. This can be a double edged sword because sooner or later you end up with so much that it feels inconceivable that you would ever run out. The capital upgrades are kind of like previous games where you "Phase in" new structures which determine what units you can recruit.Finally it has to be said that Liberation falls short in terms of aesthetic. This may be the first major release Frima handled. But part of what makes Disciples what it is; is the aesthetic/atmosphere. While the main maps you explore are quite nice looking with lots of environmental detail? This game at times can feel incredibly generic. The UI in particular feels pretty underwhelming and lacks the flair people expect from Disciples. Even DIsciples 3 I think had designs that felt more in line with Disciples. It's really quite apparent when your in menus, etc. and it at times feels like this could be any other mobile game. The music too is a crucial part of Disciples atmosphere. The title track is decent enough. But when you played DIsciples 2 you had a a lot of ambient tracks as well. I realize my review probably sounds incredibly negative, but that doesn't mean I hate the game. It's because I love the series and while there are some good things in Liberation? I feel at times it doesn't really feel like a Disciples game aside from an occasional wink or a nod to what came before. It feels every bit like the formula was changed to give it broader appeal. While I understand the desire to do so; it risks losing the series identity in translation. Does Disciples have to be another Heroes or Kings Bounty? Is Liberation worth checking out? Sure. If your looking for another Disciples 2 you won't find it here. At the same time it is perhaps unfair to criticize this game for what it isn't rather than what it is. Play the demo if you can (if it's still available). My opinion may change once I finish the game, but I still think there are some things they could improve if they look to do another installment. Perhaps Liberation's greatest test will be whether it can liberate itself from being compared to Disciples 2. Time will tell.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen so many "This game sucks because it's not Disciples 2..." comments when looking through various reviews for this game and tbh, I'm glad I gave it a shot and bought it.The major complaints I see are:"It looks too cartoony, not like Disciples 2!!" - Have you seen Disciples 2 recently?  The game was made in a time where cartoony style graphics was the way these games looked.  To be completely honest here, this complaint makes literally no sense as it looks less cartoony than previous games in the series..."The story and voice acting suck/This is nothing like the original Disciples stories" - Voice acting is largely above par, with occasional slip ups.  Better than some, not exactly on par with the likes of PoE2. but certainly not awful either.  As for the story, I'm around 2/3 through act 2.  So far it's felt very much like a Disciples story.  The story itself is a pretty convoluted, lengthy tale with various (potentially seen as convenient) plot devices to justify war.  Not sure what makes this one worse than any of the others lol.  I've been enjoying it so far personally and I come from a background of having loved Disciples 1 & 2.  Reincarnation, less so.I also tend to see most of these complaints come from people who have less than an hour in the game...  For a game that's 80+ hours..."The combat is boring" - Enemies are less bullet-sponges than Disciples 3.  The games combat also feels less brutally unfair than previous games. D2, getting started was always a pain as your casters would die almost any fight with archers.  D3. the fights often felt brutally one-sided to the enemy until you levelled up.Here, it's still much the same and they WILL focus fire your casters down, so that's still the same.  But the enemy die just as easily as you do rather than seeming to take 2-3x the hits of your guys.Otherwise it feels just like other disciples games.  Units have always had 1-2 attacks depending on level and iteration, no idea why people are complaining about that fact unless this is the first game they've ever played in the series.So TL;DR - Don't let the negative reviews put you off.  It's a good story, looks decent, combat is alright, but I find the story was always better than the combat in the series, this is no different.  Slightly easier, but feels less unfair against the player for BS reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent grimdark RPG with hex-based battles.  The story is also pretty good, the combat is fun, there's lots of choice in how you navigate the world and quests, the voice acting is good, there's a lot to like.But it's firmly in the 7 out of 10 territory, which is a shame as it had a lot of the elements of greatness.  But there's just too many rough edges.For starters, the game is way too padded.  This game takes 80 hours when it could easily have been 50.There is a Conquest feature which lets you autoresolve trivial fights but the problem is it isn't very well balanced, especially for play on the hard difficulty.  It forces you to always fight in quest battles regardless of how weak the enemy is and that's fair enough, but I was always going about with maximum number of units with maximum leadership, finding the weakest enemies I could find on the world map and there were still times I was forced to fight units of 5 levels below me which I end up breezing through.  Speaking of leadership, this is the amount and quality of units you can have in your army at any one time, with higher class units taking more of your leadership allowance.  And this figure ramps up so slowly, sometimes only for a value of 5 every few levels of XP (there are NO units in the game that have anything less than a round figure of 10,20,30 or 40 leadership cost, so the 5 point increase is pointless as far as I could tell), and you find that not only the fighting is a slog, but the evolution of your army is as well as most battles only give you about 50xp.  And with a XP threshold of 1000xp per level, it means you would potentially have to fight 20 battles per level up(!).  My advice is, do every quest you can find as soon as you can to speed up your leveling, to maximise your chances of being able to skip a few combats.The excessive battles are further hampered by the slow speed.  Every battle startup you have to wait for all starting abilities to trigger, again and again.  And the max combat speed is only 300%.  So every battle takes a minimum of 10 minutes when it's a foregone conclusion you're going to win from the start.And there's lots of other time wastes everywhere - once you enter the compare forces screen prior to a battle, if this particular battle doesn't let you retreat, you can't quick load or exit to menu - you have to proceed to battle, wait for the starting abilities to trigger, then EXIT TO MAIN MENU, and THEN reload.  It's bonkers that anyone thought this was a good  user experience.  And when you level up, you always want the rest of your army to be leveled up as well, so you go back to base and click level up.  But there's no mass level-up button, you have to click on every single unit in your army and hit level up.  This is incredibly tedious, to the point where you end up keeping absolutely no reserves to speed up the process of leveling, as then you're only leveling up your companions.  But then you inevitably get hit with a multi-battle scenario, with multiple battles are strung one after another without chance to return to base to replenish your army, so if you lose some units in the first battle you've no reserves to replace them and you're absolutely screwed.  It's beyond infuriating.Also there doesn't seem to be a point to the DLC if you're not playing in New Game +, as the enemies always scale to your level and in the first go around you're never going to reach the level cap, so those quests were always marked as hard in the game with enemies in those areas several levels above me.  Basically any quest that is medium is generally too hard, you have to level up until the quest is rated as easy or very easy before it becomes beatable generally speaking, as levels make a huge difference in this game.And there's other annoyances like you can't portal to homebase in a dungeon.  And some of those dungeons are huge.  And you're on foot in them so if you lose any units in a battle you have to slowly leave the dungeon, portal back home, recruit replacements, portal back and then walk all the way back through the dungeon.Honestly I wanted to love this game but it fought me at every step.Just a little bit more playtesting and a little more polish and you'd be looking at one of the best games of it's year of release.Instead it's just a mildly forgettable, decent RPG.  So if you can look past some of the above, and really enjoy RPGs and hex-based battle, then I would still recommend you pick it up, but only on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this one a thumbs down, since it is my kind of game.Sadly, Liberations has many great ideas, but most are very poorly implemented, the game could have easily used another year of fine-tuning the gameplay mechanics / designs in development. It’s a looker, but has little to offer beyond that.In the end it made me appreciate the Kitauri made Kings Bounty games even more - they are a well-designed, smooth running gameplay machines in comparison.The most negative points for me are:- the deeper you are in the game the more of a repetitive drag it gets; progression gets slower and slower….- extreme poorly designed loot/item system; soon you learn to expect nothing when opening a treasure chest; it’s just trash you will disassemble- unit design lags hard in gameplay mechanics variations, there are about 60 different units, that share like <10 skills with different color variations (main reason the combat gets boring so quickly - the fancy tire 4 dragon does the same stuff as your tire 1 unit, just with bigger numbers and different animations)- UI/UX and especially mouse control on PC are horrible (as of V1.1); whoever approved this for release deserves to be fired (because he/she has obviously no idea how to do the job)

_childDocuments_.review: Just a few hours in, and about to uninstall. Some of my issues are nitpicky, but - to each their own.First - the main character is set - female. Call me what you want, but I wanna play a dude. Period. No customization (except for occasional clothing changes) doesn't help.Voice-acting; mediocre at best.Skill Trees - almost seem pointless. Battles - Long-winded, repetitive.Sound - repetitive. Sound effects in some places are plain over-the-top. i.e. the enemies that shoot that ice-arrow attack makes it sound like an entire mountain is crashing into the planet - way over the top.XP - I get the same amount of xp no matter what kind of battle I win: There could be two enemies or six - same EXP. Regardless of enemy level. Same XP. Super-lame here.The maps are borrrrrring. Almost nothing is interactable. And you can't 'spin' the map, which for me in an iso-game is simply a requirement in 2023.Gear - pointless. So many pieces give +1 this or +1 that - which is mathematically pointless. Also, limiting gear slots to the main character (yes, I know companions get two slots) is just silly. Theme - my elves and my undead, and my demons and my empire and.... nevermind. The 'theme' of being able to freely mix/build these is incredibly lame. Not to mention, so many of the units are either reskins or very close to reskins.Not sure where all these high-ratings come from. I just don't see it. I do see a game that could have been great, but really it's 2 out of 4 stars, at best.

name: Way of the Hunter
detailed_description: Way of the Hunter Elite Edition The Elite Edition includes the base game as well as the following extras items: Way of the Hunter: Hunter's Pack Way of the Hunter: Map Pack 1 About the Game This authentic hunting experience lets you explore and hunt in large open-world environments in the USA and Europe . Discover true to life animals in beautiful natural habitats and handle various detailed and highly realistic weapons. Way of the Hunter provides a highly immersive, completely integrated experience amongst stunning wildlife with true to live animal group behavior. Witness the changing of complex ecosystems that react and adapt to your input. Learn what it means to be a true hunter and put your skills to the test. Face the challenges of ethical hunting, supported by a compelling story, or simply enjoy hunting the rich environments freely. Dozens of strikingly detailed animal species with realistic behavior models for a truly immersive hunting experience Hunt like a pro with features that highlight animal signs, blood splatter analysis, and shot review with the rewindable bullet camera Hunt your way through two unique and rich locations by car or by foot. Both the Pacific Northwest and Transylvania cover a terrain of 144 square km/55 square miles each Use Hunter Sense to highlight important details and info, or disable it and customize your HUD for a hardcore experience Complex Trophy system generates unique antlers and horns based on multiple factors like fitness and age Sophisticated natural animal animations and reactions when sensing the players presence 24-hour day/night cycle with changing wind and weather Realistic ballistics and bullet physics simulation A broad selection of firearms and equipment, including licensed gear from Bushnell, Federal, Leupold, Primos, Remington and Steyr Arms An in-game economy that lets you hunt game and sell the meat to purchase new gear, hunting passes, and taxidermy for your trophy stands A compelling story about the struggles of a family hunting business, and the rivalry and friendships that surround it Enjoy your perfect hunting adventure among friends in co-op mode Intuitive photo mode for capturing and sharing your favorite moments

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying hunting game that runs without noticeable issues on my 3080/5900hx/32GB laptop at 2560x1600 with all settings set to high/very-high. I have a universal driver-level frame-rate cap of 60fps for all my games and so far, I've gotten a solid 60fps with the aforementioned settings (the two settings that go up to "ultra" were dialed down to "very-high" to lower my GPU temps but still delivered 60fps when turned on".The bugs I noticed so far pertained to seeing your knees while moving around crouching, the left arm stuttering when crawling around prone, some clouds didn't render properly, and water-sounds are a bit imbalanced on the high-side and overpower other ambient sounds and important animal calls. Also, sometimes the "X" prompt to analyze does not appear due to finicky placement of the subject in your field of view. This can be "fixed" by adjusting your position until the analyze-prompt appears. None of the bugs I've come across so far are game-breaking.Some players have noticed that FOV seems to be tied to the selected resolution and at 2560x1600, the default FOV seems ok. An FOV slider that the dev will be adding in upcoming patches will be helpful in tweaking the FOV to individual preferences. Key-binding customization will also be added in upcoming patches. Would it have been better to have these options on Day 1? Sure, but at least the dev is listening to the community and promised to add improvements soon.If you use a controller, then you can use Steam Input to customize your controls. I'm using a Steam Controller and added gyro controls as well as modified some default controls like soft-pull LT for aim/gyro-activation and adding hard-pull LT to input LB for focus-aim. Works great so far!Players who prefer a more arcade-like experience be forewarned - this is game that leans much more to the simulator end of the spectrum. I came from 250hrs of theHunter:CotW and while there are many similarities between these two games, WotH is intended to be more realistic. As a result, it is slower-paced than CotW and activities like stalking or tracking are not as easy as they are in CotW. Currently, there are no mobile tents but you also do not respawn at a faraway cabin when you exit/resume your game.At this time, I believe this game can achieve a high level of polish and refinement as long as the devs are listening to the community's feedback (but keep true to the simulator-style of gameplay) and are efficient/effective in making improvements. The current state of the game, despite the bugs, still gives me the feeling that the devs have put a lot of heart into this project, which gives me hope that they will make the necessary improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another one of those games where Steam reallllly needs a neutral recommendation option (summary at end)..Way of the Hunter does 'some' things right Call of the Wild did not/could not. But currently, it does a little too much wrong..Animals look great, the animations are on point. But their behaviors are still unrealistic and quite stupid.. Young and Adult animals have one thing in common : they looked like they're being baited high protein diets.. seriously, young animals look buff. It's weird. Now for animal tracking : its lack-luster. Tracks are hard to see due to graphics (see below) and they are basically copy-paste. No real variety nor do they provide any unique information. In fact, there's absolutely NO need to follow any tracks. It's far more efficient to walk, spam calls, wait to see an animal in the distance or hear a call response. Its an element that feels like an after-thought. The environment looks great, at a medium distance. They did a solid job with bump-mapping texture..but the environmental graphics are still dated for 2015+. Textures up close are blurry and textures in the distance are blurry. They rely on vignette and depth of field to make the distant graphics look appealing.. but those exact setting cause nausea, eye strain and headaches. And I'm pretty sure the reason why we can't turn those settings off is ultimately because this game isn't well optimized (it's not).Now for weapons.. there's not a lot to choose from. Seriously. This game currently lacks content. And much of the content there is-is gated behind the WORST part of the game (standby for that). Crossbow ballistics are abysmal. Just absolutely horrible. And getting stuck in the reload animation is very frustrating. All-around, caliber ballistics are unrealistic. And again, there's not much to choose from; especially no option to choose different types of ammo.. Their 'bullet cam' is well done. Not surprising considering some of the devs came from Cabela (known for the bullet cam). There's a few glitches regarding the bullet cam/bullet pathing, but I'm sure they'll polish it out (glitches aren't common).Now for the worst part : missions/story/quests. They are HORRIBLY annoying. And you are FORCED to do them since not only is a lot of the content gated behind them, they are also the best way to make money. Yup. Be prepared to spend the beginning of your experience with this game knocking out useless quests, rather than enjoying a sandbox hunting experience..In summary, Way of the Hunter has a good 'foundation' to build upon. But it's NOT a finished game. There's a lot of work to be done, especially optimization to be had.. Their road map isn't very promising as a lot of issues/content players have been asking for attention aren't present on it. And knowing the past work of some of these devs isn't promising.. But the devs are at least active. If you're a fan of Call of the Wild, you WILL enjoy this game. You will understand much of what I have said in this review.."Way of the Hunter does 'some' things right Call of the Wild did not/could not. But currently, it does a little too much wrong.." What Way of the Hunter does right, is enough to throw $40 at it, if you have the money to spare. Else give it a wait. Also, if you are like me and your eyes are sensitive to graphical settings like depth of field and vignette, I would suggest giving this game a wait until the option to turn it off is added. I currently get about an hour of gameplay in before I have to step OUTSIDE and stare at trees in the distance.. the game makes me THAT nauseated (this is a game-breaker for many players). Hope this review helps some folks.. I suggest visiting their Discord for inquiry, and NOT steam's forums.

Someone can do the math on how many literal days worth of crawling that is.- To hunt in areas outside of the starter area requires a "private pass", of which there are currently 8, and they cost 4,500 currency each. A good buck gets you around ~300 currency. Hunting small game is worthless as they only yield ~20 currency.- Downed animals disappearing as you walk up to them.- Birds just sink straight to the bottom in bodies of water.- Shooting an animal in the lungs at 100 yards and the animal nor the herd reacting at all; ghost bullets?- Getting stuck in rocks and environment requiring a restart of the game.- Crashing to desktop.- Massive desync in co-op. Player models and animations look really wacky.Missions are bland, bizarre and seem like they give no rewards whatsoever. The 4th or 5th mission is As everyone else has said, no FoV or ultrawide support. Feels like a really bad console port. _childDocuments_.review: I am not sure if I have ever written a review on steam before. This game disappointed me so much, that I feel I have to write a review for it. I had reservations for this game almost immediately, it is so poorly optimized that the opening cut scene was stuttering. I have a good PC (an AMD 5800X3D and a 5900XT) and the game runs awful, despite my frame-rate supposedly being good (more than 100 fps). Even on max graphics settings the games visuals are fuzzy and often times, especially with fast moving animals, a blurry mess. As I am sure many reviews here have pointed out, this game launched without a field of view slider or the option to manually set keybinds. The default field of view is rather narrow. It is puzzling why the game launched without them.There are a number of small bugs, which mostly just made the game more frustrating. Bugs like going into the storage menu to find the mouse cursor invisible. Looking through binoculars to find that you have to hit the button six times to stop looking through them. Blood splatters being invisible when you looked the first three times in an area and after 15 minutes of frustrated searching seeing them where you know you looked before. Nothing game breaking, so I tried to be patient.My patience ran out when I encountered what I consider a serious bug, that has apparently permanently affected my game. I was tracking roe deer and found a drinking zone. I activated the zone, saw the information pop up on screen, and excitedly went to the encyclopedia entry for animals, just to find no entry. I exited the menu saw the pop up tell me it was a drinking zone for a roe deer, but no following pop up telling me an entry had been added to my encyclopedia. So I found another zone for roe deer. Same thing. No entry in my encyclopedia. I am afraid that the game bugged, because I hit the menu button after discovering the zone too quickly. Now I can not get an entry for roe deer, no matter what I do. I was really looking forward to hunting roe deer, as it was one of my favorite things to hunt in Hunter: Call of the Wild.This game clearly was released far before it was ready and I do not have faith these issues will be fixed any time soon. I have asked for a refund, but I am not confident I will get one because I pre-ordered it about a month ago and have played a bit too long. I regret pre-ordering this game. Strongly recommend waiting, if you are considering purchasing it. Honestly, you should look into Hunter: Call of the Wild instead. _childDocuments_.review: After having logged a number of hours into the game, I can see a huge potential with the title and this will most likely be my go-to hunting game. The game play style is a whole lot different than Call of the Wild. This isn't a run and gun game. The game takes patience and a lot of failing before you understand some of the mechanics and what you need to do to be successful.I'm going to structure this into my biggest Pros and Cons. I'll start with the Cons so I can end the review on a high note as I think the developers deserve some recognition for creating a fun title.- I have had several cases of getting stuck in trees. This typically happens when trying to use trees for cover. I have no idea if trees actually provide cover but a number of them will cause you to get stuck with no way out. I think it may have to do with moving between standing, crouching, and going prone. Only solution I've found is to fast travel.- Related to above is that I had an instance where I shot a deer, was stuck to a tree, had to fast travel to get unstuck. Before I fast traveled, I marked the spot I shot the deer. When I returned to the spot there was no blood, and no sign of the deer. I had shot it from 50m and watched it drop on the ground. It seems fast travel makes the downed deer disappear- Some of the sounds are just too loud. Rivers that are slowly flowing shouldn't sound like white water rapids where you literally can't hear anything but rushing water. Lots of other sounds need adjustments too. I'd like to see the sounds adjusted to fit the environment better. - Tracking in early game. I was extremely frustrated in the early game with trying to track using blood from downed animals. You'd make an excellent shot from short distance on an animal, and then be unable to locate the animal because following the blood trail using the Hunter Sense was next to impossible. The color is too dim and blends into the surroundings, the highlight view distance is terrible, you can only see the highlights if you're standing still, etc. The thing is, now that I have unlocked several perks related to the hunter sense, tracking is no longer an issue the tracks appear much brighter and are visible much further away, and works while I am walking. I do think there needs to be some adjustments for new players though.- Hunter sense reminds me of "dead eye" in Red Dead Redemption 2. The problem is that when using hunter sense, there is a filter that gets applied, the edges of the screen are darkened, and there is a blur effect that is enabled whether motion blur is on or off in the settings. With as much as a lot of players are going to rely on hunter sense, I want to see a lot of these effects removed. I'd rather have an icon or something telling me it's active than have a headache inducing bunch of filters. I generally play with hunter sense off most of the time and just flip it on for very short periods. - I think there could be a little more guidance for new players without making them go through an encyclopedia in a menu to figure the game out. There are a lot of things in the early part of the game that are going to throw off new players. I think a little more hand-holding would be nice for players that need it.- The environment - I've only played the American map so far but I'm really impressed with the beauty of the environment and the diversity of the terrain. Everything from grasslands, to marshes, to forests. Each area of the map presents different challenges and I find myself having to adapt my own play style to what area of the map I'm in.- The difficulty - I'm a big fan of how difficult the game plays even of the default Adventurer difficulty. It's that challenge that keeps the game interesting for me. Knowing that there are additional difficulties that I can change to in the future to keep the game fresh is awesome.- The animal animations are great. The animal movement looks really good. Watching a group of moose walk across some grasslands to a drink zone looked extremely realistic. You can just sit there and admire how big and lumbering the moose strides are.- The economy. I'm so happy with the decision to make the weapons and gear affordable. No more grinding for weeks just to get enough money to buy your preferred weapons or gear. - The perk system is very well designed. I love the idea of perks unlocking in a way that mimics you improving your skills over time. - Herd management - this is something that is going to take a long time and a lot of effort to improve over time. It adds a completely new element to my PC hunting experience. Rather than just always looking to remove the largest buck from a herd, you need to consider what removing that buck does to the future genetics of the herd. Are you better off removing a 3 star mature buck or should you remove that 1 star adult with poor fitness and genetics? - Vehicles - Thank you for finally adding a vehicle to a hunting simulator that isn't complete crap. The vehicle is functional, can be driven relatively well on keyboard and mouse, and doesn't drive 250 mph. - The story is an element that has surprised me. It's actually pretty good and has a functional purpose to help you unlock areas of the map without having to pay for the expensive passes. I've enjoyed working my way through it. I know that missions and stories are everyone's thing but it's much more engaging that I was initially expecting.Overall for me this game is a winner. I'm confident the developers will help correct a lot of the Issues from my "Cons" list if we all give them a little bit of time.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: this game is better than call of the wild in almost every way it can be at the moment.immediate downsides are that it's pretty graphics intensive and feels sorta unoptimized, an occasional crash or two is expected. $40 is a little bit steep but not really by much. it could be worse. i'm buying it expecting more content soon.it still floods you with an enormous amount of information when tracking or observing game, but without holding your hand too much. you won't get a glowing outline on animals, tracks are tougher to spot. reliance on audio and gradual perk upgrades feels like a natural and intuitive progression. you can still always turn off all the help and 'hunter vision' and play in ego mode if that's your style too.this game cares way less about animal "class". most guns can do most things without hurting your score, however it also provides you with all the information you might need on "why did i get such a low score?" in case you decide to hit a bunny rabbit with .338 LM. you can play back the bullet impact and path through your animal in 3D, see the cavitation and energy dump, recommended energy and amount of meat% lost by shot. animal behavior in this game makes animal behavior in CoTW look like cabellas big game hunter for the gameboy color. guns and gear are licensed if you care about that. ballistics model is a lot nicer, shots feel punchier and more commanding than cotw. there's bullet drop, windage, the whole 9 yards. you can zero out to 1km. animals & bullet impacts render far out into that distance as well.other downsides i can think of are only as a result of how new the game is - expecting to see a lot more guns, maps, gear, animals, etc in the coming year. hopefully tree stands, suppressors and night vision. maybe.anyways buy the game it's good

But all of them together with the risk of fatal crash errors is too much, I'll be waiting to see how this is going down the line. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. You can tell there's a lot of love put into it by the developers. It receives frequent patches with new content and bug fixes. There's still a lot of technical hiccups that need ironing out (buggy textures, random screen flicking, unresponsive button and mouse presses), but the overall performance is good. It can be a bit slow and boring at times, because - as opposed to other hunting games - this game strives for realism. Here, animals are scarce. There are times when you'll be walking around for 30 minutes not finding a single animal. It's part of the experience, I guess. I'd probably prefer a little more action while sacrificing realism, but if you want a real life hunting simulation, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: These "outrage" reviews are way overblown. I just played 2.5 hours on a PC and the "controls issue" is NOT A PROBLEM. There is very little key control usage in a Hunting game in the first place. You are NOT tossing grenades, changing rate of fire, or even changing ammo type. This SIMULATION has TWO basic control keys, besides the WASD movement keys. They are "C" to crouch or go prone and "E" to open doors or enter a vehicle. The Scope ZOOMS with the Mouse Wheel, the Scope range can be zero'd in with the Arrow Keys and you use the basic Left Shift to toggle run (which you RARELY use anyway because it's not advised or useful to run very often).Stunning Graphics, Sound is "just fine", animal animations seem to be very well and realistically done and I HIGHLY RECOMMEND this because, in my view, it is the BEST HUNTING GAME/SIMULATION out and I've owned and played them ALL.Buy it and see for yourself. But take a minute to try the available controls while the DEV sets up keybinding if it's really important to you. There is NO VALID reason to refund this game for PC USERS...

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the review bombing fool you, this game is easily better than CoW in every way. The issues people are griping about relate mostly to the FOV, which is annoying, but top priority in the next hotfix, ya'll are a bunch of babies.Having played The Hunter Classic and CoW, this game does just about everything better:PROS:-No microtransactions(!)-Free ammo-More realistic animal behavior-Herd health system is really cool-Animals age and grow-Ballistics are *chef's kiss*-Proper weapon zeroing-Tracking is far more intuitive and realistic-Damage model is closer to Sniper Elite series-Better graphics, environment, and sound design-Actually takes time to locate, stalk, and track animals (Some may consider this a con)CONS:-Limited weapons and equipment compared to CoW. (Still has everything you need, 30-30, .243, .223, .338, .22, etc. but no handguns or bows yet.)-Less maps than CoW-Audio bugs are annoying, sound is poorly mixed within 100m of water, and occasionally it  sounds like an aircraft is doing patterns over your head etc. Not huge issues for me personally.-Perk and character system needs work.-Story is a little cringe.-Blood trails sometimes disappear, seems to happen more frequently with .308 on elk imo-Foliage and fallen logs have no collision or sound yet.-Stealth system seems to be WIP, sneaking up on animals in wooded ar.eas is very difficult, as they sense you very far awayI didn't put the FOV or Keybind issues as those are on the short list to be fixed. If you like hunting, and play CoW because there's no good competitor, but find it a little too arcadey, give WotH a try. I was hesitant, but the game won me over within 15 minutes. Personally, the lack of microtransactions alone makes this game better than CoW, but it goes even further and improves the digital hunting experience in just about every way. If you're a sucker for realism like me, try it out, I think you will like it.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is exactly what it looks like, a Hunter: Call of the Wild clone. Where Way of the Hunter doesn't do anything awful, it also doesn't do anything well. The game is the definition of a "meh" title. Overall, Way of the Hunter feels like a bland hunting game that did its best to imitate a more well rounded title.The gun play feels off and I don't know how the developer managed that. My rounds always land low, no matter how much time I spend ranging the target, adjusting zero, and steadying my shot. The firearm selection is very limited as well, and I'm guessing its so developers can flush it out later through DLC. The hunter sense needs some work as well. I feel like it could benefit from giving players the option to assign colors to different markers, i.e. droppings, blood, prints, sound cues, and deceased animals. The hunter sense gets confusing while tracking a blood trail and the exact same flashing effect is displayed for everything on screen. Not to mention the default color for the hunter sense is yellow, and blends in with the light greens and tans of the grass.The amount of money you need to purchase hunting certificates for different zones feels odd too. Not in the sense that they added something you need to work for, but because of the conservation aspect. If you kill too many animals, then the population on the map lowers. This feels counter productive for game play, since you need to kill animals to make money, but then that lowers the number of animals within certain zones on map. The last thing about the game that strikes me as odd is how few fast travel points are on the map. I don't want to skip all over the map, but I also don't want to spend 30 minutes walking to a feeding zone. All in all, I feel like the game has potential, but it lacks polish. If the developers continue to build upon what they currently have, I think it will end up being a great title.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually hate these type of games and am very impatient, but this one is a blast. Way better than Call of the Wild (not that CotW is a bad game, this just does the core gameplay loop better). CotW comparisons like crazy below:Environment: Not really sure how to explain this, but the environments and forests feel "real" and organic in this game. In CotW all the environments and forests felt static and fake. Very very pretty and cozy/dreamy looking, but fake. Kind of like how Far Cry Primal's forests felt? Just a collection of trees placed w/ a map tool and nothing in between. IDK. Anyway, the landscapes and forests in this game are amazing.Hunting/stalking. Instead of taking out your smart phone and following glowing digital cones, you actually have to track in this game. You have to look at the footprints to see which direction the prints themselves are going. You have to look at the blood splatter and see which direction the smaller blood dots are headed, etc. Feels a lot more bad ass tracking this way vs magic phone GPS tracking in CotW.The XRay system after you claim a kill is great too. Very detailed, and you can play a little animation of how the bullet entered/exited the animal.I like the story this game has. Also cool you get your own hunting lodge right off the bat in a story way that makes sense and doesn't feel like you didn't earn it.Wish there was a dog. They need to add a dog as a companion ASAP.Oh and they also need to add bows and scents. Treestands and blinds? ehh I dont really care about those as I like stalking / exploring vs just sitting in a tree making calls covered in elk piss or w.e.Excited to see what further updates come.

_childDocuments_.review: The heat of the afternoon is overwhelming, the humidity of a mid spring thunderstorm possible. I glance down at the somewhat scattered pebbles and dirt of a fresh track wondering if today will be the day. Slowly standing and making my way forward through the overgrown brush, I can barely hear the unmistakable snap of dry twigs and the rustle of disturbed leaves. My pulse quickens as I realise my prey is closer than I first realised, maybe my hunters sense is not with me today.I glance left slightly without making too much of a sudden movement, from this vantage I glimpse the magnificent beast just heading away from me over the rise. As I move towards the crest of the hill, making sure to keep my scent direction away from the hunt, I feel the hair on my arms and neck slowly rise, that telltale taste of ozone suddenly fills the air. CRACK! Suddenly the dusk is lit by a bright flash of lightning and followed by the rolling peal of thunder reverberating off the valley sides in all directions. That was a close one... I sigh to myself and utter into the silence that followed "we will dance another day"

_childDocuments_.review: The sounds. They're horrible. The woods don't constantly sound like high pitch shrills going off every two seconds, bugs don't sound like helicopters. Probably scent because the wind, no matter what direction you travel, is at your back. And we don't get a scent spray to help us through the tutorial. The hunter sense is awful. I can't even tell when it's on or off or what it's highlighting. I understand they were going for realism but totally missed the mark. I also hate that you have no real control over your equipment. _childDocuments_.review: I dont write reviews but had to be done for this. I love sims but games like this i dont have the patience for because of well another title was hollow. I picked this up because One a friend said i had to try it and 2nd had been following their response to the day one issues. One i was very impressed the devs released a very thought out response to the issues and laid it out rather than just the usual drum of "we know and we are fixing it" and then left to the wind for eternity like most titles now. _childDocuments_.review: Reviewing just before the 2 hour refund window.To summarise, its good, no bugs found in my (short) playtime and the world feels like something i want to explore and get into, it gives that special feel of being out in the wild and hunting / exploring.Looking into a new area and seeing animals and moving in towards them is fun / satisfying and it feels rewarding / worthwhile to keep exploring deeper into the map and new areas.I have played approximately 200 hours of Call Of The Wild, and am at the stage where i just farm zones & fast travel around the map, rushing to each spot before the drink zone / feed zone timer runs out.The main thing lacking from COTW is the animal draw distance, it feels pointless exploring through a map as you are never sure if you are actually walking in the right direction.The graphics are abit funky and take awhile to get used to but after some tweaking in the NVIDIA control panel its now at a point where im happy (however sharpening is not supported yet) As others have said the blood tracking is useless and you often cant find an animal you have shot (and seen drop) right under your nose, perhaps there is something i am missing here or its a feature they need to balance.Overall im happy and will play past the refund time, its a game where i want to explore the world and hunt

_childDocuments_.review: So right, let's get started on WotH...As of Version 1.22 this game is just lacking content. For a game with it's focus on hunting apparently, it's still missing the essentials like tree stands, blinds, bows, different types of ammo and so on. Let's face it, it shows as a good foundation, but  there's some basic stuff you gotta come up with from the very start, if you want your game to be a hunting simulation.And with the new DLC out and one of the new weapons being part of it, I think we can already tell in wich direction this is going. PthF - Pay to have Fun. Meh. Currently not worth the price in my opinion.Then there's the graphics and performance...Let me get to this with sharing my PC specs: I'm rocking an I7 6700k @ 4.4 GHz, 32 Gb RAM with a 2080 Super. 144hz monitor. I've locked fps at 72 and play with vsync on in 1440p.So yeah, Unreal Engine 4... Maybe not the best for an open world scenario to begin with, but heyho what you gonna do, here we are...First impression - terrible! But that's UE 4 for ya. Grainy, pixely, blurry, all but smooth, so prepare for some time tweaking to get it somewhat nice looking and enjoyable. Tweaks and tutorials are to find in the community tab for some of you not familiar with UE4, just an FYI.So at least I got it running more or less stable at 72 fps, besides dusk and dawn where you get fps drops with any unoptimised UE4 game, since the lighting is off and buggy.I know many of them players call this game 'beautiful', I just don't get it. Maybe from a distance and standing still one could consider it somewhat nice looking, just don't look too close!Furthermore the game obviously has an option to turn on mouse smoothing, yet it does literally nothing. Oh and your PC should at least be capable to run the game @ 2k! 1080p looks even more pixelated. Terrible! Don't ever take a closer look at boulders and cliffsides... *gag*Animal behavior is somewhat realistic, I mean, I guess?The models are well done and it's interesting to just hide somewhere and watch them do their animal stuff. Notice - interesting! Not necessarily fun! That's two pairs of shoes!Some of the game mechanics, just as the fact that there's no dynamic tracks, the skill system and missions are also questionable to say the least, but that's a design choice the Devs made. Fine. Movement - Just feels off.Just "walking" is going to spook everything in 250 yard radius, so you better don't "walk from a to b, but crouch! Nice. Walking feels like jogging, moving crouched appears to be what should have been walking in the first place and if you're switching to slow mode, it just feels like you're never getting nowhere. This definitely needs some tweaking as well. So finally, would I recommend buying it? Honestly, not at the current state and price.Maybe if it's ever gonna be on sale or got more gear to work with (for free!) and being optimized and polished a lot more, yeah maybe. It's still early in it's lifespan, so only time will tell.Thanks for reading. :)

_childDocuments_.review: New Review:Yeah... They haven't done a damn thing for this game since release. They are too focused on releasing new DLC to actually fix the game. The graphics are somehow worse than at launch, to the point that you can ONLY play with DLSS on as Anti Aliasing, but even then, it looks as if im playing an arcade game from the 80's, the game is so pixelated and jagged. Not only that, but this makes it damn near impossible to see blood or tracks, or really anything, as its SO pixelated and jagged, the game ends up appearing blurry. This also causes moving objects to have terrible ghosting trails. Even the graphics aside, the game is riddled with bugs and glitches that have been around since launch. Your'e lucky to get a patch from the devs, and when they do patch the game, its maybe 6 fixes in total?! Its damn near unplayable at the current state, and while I was excited for it when it came out, after 2 years of nothing being changed, that excitement has long faded. Dont buy it. The hunting mechanics are fine, but you aren't able to appreciate them in a game that looks and runs worse than a unity asset flip. Hell, the devs even hide all of its downfalls more than asset flip devs. You can see the graphical issues in screenshots and videos of the game, but they rarely use still shots, and when the issue is brought up, it is ignored. Its horrible management top to bottom.Original Review:Okay, let me get this straight. This is by far not a perfect game. The graphics, particularly the AA is terrible, there are the occasional bugs, and there is room for improvement gameplay wise. That however does not mean it is a terrible game. This is by far one of my favorite hunting games compared to COTW or hunter classic. The story I find much better than those found in COTW. Unlike how every map is just helping out some old dudes jpeg image to clear a certain forest area of insert species here, you have orders to fill for local buyers, if you want of course. On top of that, there is a full story and background as to why you are there, what you are doing there, and why the place you are at is the way it is. Its a touching story, without being cheesy or a sobfest, and still focuses on the core gameplay. There are very few missions where you run around doing pointless tasks like in COTW. There are a few issues here and there however that are good to know before buying, but many will be fixed or implemented soon, according to the devs roadmap at least. Currently, there is only a small selection of shotguns, and no bows, handguns, or muzzle-loaders for that matter. On top of that, what you do have, you cannot select or buy certain ammunition, it is all locked to the firearm when purchased, and refills... somewhere, I haven't figured that one out yet. That however, is all set to be implemented, from more firearms, to different types of them. Alongside this, the new firearms are to be licensed, like so many products in game already are. This is one of my favorite parts, that I actually have heard of and possibly have used some of the firearms in real life. On top of this, It is planned for different ammo types, and the ability to select those ammo types, to be introduced. Many of the aspects lacking from the game, have been acknowledged by the devs, and are set to be put into the game. All in all, the game, while rough both at launch and even now, has potential that the devs are living up to, and i'm excited to see where it goes from here.
_childDocuments_.name: Way of the Hunter

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game to anyone wanting a challenging hunting experience. Fantastic visuals and sounds, really quality animal models, animations and behaviour... I'm not an expert in weapon ballistics (and mostly hunt with bows, in-game), but they certainly seem to have taken the weapon mechanics seriously.I've not played this on the easy settings, so I cannot really say how suitable it is for people wanting a really arcady, fast-paced hunting experience, but it has certainly delivered on my need for a genuinely challenging (in a fun and satisfying way) hunting experience. It certainly drives home the idea that the actual shot makes up 5% of the hunt. Well worth the money!I will say, though, that there seems to be some difference between the various maps in terms of optimization. Dithering in general EVERYWHERE, 10m 20m in front, in reflections making them unidentifiable, in everything.Yo... _childDocuments_.review: As a veteran player of The Hunter cotw i'll make a small comparision between COTW and WOTH. WOTH pros:-Ballistics realism: way better and complex than cotw-Animal tracking: tracks are a bit more realistic, blood stains are really better.-New mechanics as the herd management: This new idea of improve the genetics of the herds via hunting the worst animals is fun and innovative.WOTH cons:-Graphics/weather/effects/Sound: for sure that textures are better than COTW (7 years older) but not so far, lighting is way better in COTW, and general weather effects like rain, snow or wind also. WOTH looks to me like another videogame from 2022, but COTW was something else in the scenario inmersion that i can feel even today.-Optimization: not good, in the other hand COTW runs in ultra in almost every 2017 wooden toaster.-Animal behaviour: Animals look more realistic and generally better than COTW, but after some hours you realize than everithing is way too fixed. Herds are tied to a place and do a circuit around there. You can just follow it to find them. If you want to find an animal just open your map and find the spot to hunt it, go there and 90% there it is.-Callers: they try to add some realistic use of the callers, instead of the COTW spam 342347 calls per minute, but in my opinion its not good. Just a minigame with a bar and a white area in the middle, you have to call when the indicator is there... nothing realistic about that. Also you can call males or females with differente calls, which is good, but you have different calls for better or worst score game which is totally unrealistic. Also these calls works always 100% like stated, if you call a good score deer and the good score deer is there, it'll come to you instantly like a zombie to a brain. No fail possibility, no room for some random behaviour.For me WOTH deserves a try, and has a lot to offer mainly when it come to shooting and tracking the animals and the herd managemente. In terms of inmersion, scenario, nature realism and general effects COTW still better to me these days.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is primarily to be another counterpoint to the people review-bombing it.Pros:+ Animal models are very good, with good animations and transitions between animations.+ Foliage looks very good at a distance and not that bad up close.+ Tracking animals by the blood trail is pretty interesting, the blood splatters are detailed and show the direction the animal was moving without being an arrow pointing right to them. Tree limbs will be spattered with blood if the animal brushes up against them, and tall grass will also be spattered.+ "Hunting Sense" gives you the toggle-able ability to see animal tracks, spoor, need zones, blood trails, etc with a light outline. The fact that it is not on or off all the time and in an easy at-will keybind makes the game much more immersive and visually stimulating.+ The Perks system gives you a type of progression without being tied to "levels".+ Small touches. There are lots of these, far too many to go into in a quick review like this. From the blood spatters, the focus on ethical hunting, the calls and sounds of animals moving, to an extra-long-range rendering distance for animals (about twice as far as Call of the Wild).+ Animals age! That young deer already has an impressive rack (don't giggle), but it has room to grow. So let it grow. It will become a trophy buck after a few more play sessions. Though if you don't find it again, it may die of old age. Seriously.+ This goes hand-in-hand with the previous pro, and that is that you can essentially make trophy herds by careful selection and culling. That's an incredible level of detail in a game like this.+ Varied calls allow you to call in the specific type of animal in a herd you're looking to hunt. Does, low-quality males, and higher-quality trophy males.Cons:- No FOV slider on launch - Devs have already said this is coming in the near future.- Some people have had the game crash on them. Is this unheard-of on launch day for games?- No way to change or alter keybinds at launch - Devs are already fixing this in the near future.- Some controls are a bit sluggish, specifically weapon swaps.- The visual transition to and from Hunter Sense is disorienting to some people.- Multiplayer is unstable at launch - again, not unheard-of at launch (the game's been out for like 3 hours now) and I'd give it a week or so for them to get things much more stable.- Weapon descriptions are pretty poor, as is information on which firearms are better for which animals at-a-glance on the shop page.- Shotguns only have bird shot. Seriously?

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, but (currently) very limited in too many ways.Pro's:Nice graphics, the animals seem plentiful. Good mechanics with travel and camp sites, very nice ballistic simulation.Runs smooth, haven't had a single crash, haven't found any real bugs, just a few quirks, but nothing gamebreaking.Nice that the singleplayer part saves where you stopped, so you can continue a hunt/stalk/track when you come back. Very singleplayer friendly.Con's:Keybinding cant be changed and there is no where to see what keys to use for what. Good luck putting down a waypoint with you binoculars if you dont google/youtube/etc.Both maps are very heavily focus on forest and mountains. Haven't found any really open terrains so far.Hunting sense works akwardly - the glowing effect is annoying and the color matches the grass, making it very hard at times to track. Weird, fish-eye effect that just makes the graphics look worse.Animals are very limited minded, herds are "on rails" both fleeing and traveling, especially waterfowl, which comes right back to you within 2 min of shooting and wont spook in the air. Most bigger animals only spook a few 100 meters before being perfectly calm again, making herd-wipes very easy. Water-fowl is implemented VERY basic. You more or less have to stomp on the birds to scare them off and the come right back. No blinds, lures, calling does'nt seem to do much to them. Just stomp around and shoot - but the value of each bird is so low that its just not worth it. You cant spot most of them due to the heavy amount of reeds, so your really just hoping a 5 star pops into your sight some day.VERY limited gun selection, shotguns are useless for anything else then birds, so you only really need 2-3 rifles and everything is covered - and you can only buy around 10, all but one are bolt action, making them identical besides ammo.Once you have tier 6 riffels, you wont really need anything else, although you take a money penalty, but your trophies are fine. The shooting seems a bit too simple, regaining breath after holding it is very quick, using hunters sense is just an advanced aim assist, wind doesn't do much at all and although the elevation feature is nice, its mostly pointless for shots within 200m for most riffels.Although ammo is free, you are limited to 2 guns at all times and there is only a single lodge per map where you can change this.Shooting animals with a higher tier riffel cost alot in meat (=money reward), but its almost rediciulus how much meat is wasted. I shot a goat with a tier 6 riffel, it weighed 22kg, i wasted 20kg on a chest hit.Trophy mounting is VERY simple, most mounts have 2-3 positions for the animals you can mount, no rotation or anything like that. No rare fur/feather types as far as im aware, limiting trophies further.There is something with the scale of the game that seems odd to me. At normal walking, im going at around 10-15m/s, which makes the map seem somewhat smaller to me. Sure, the scale of the map sounds fine on paper, but if i can travers it on foot so quick, it seems a bit fake. And the scale of walking-running seems off. Although running is somewhat faster, it really isn't much, compared to the noise you make. Sneaking and prone is also tedious slow! Also - the player character feels oddly short! I feel like my head is between my knees when i look down.Alot of the missions is very simple: Go to camp site, pick up trash 5x, done. Deliver something to lodge B from lodge A. Go back to lodge A to get next mission. Go back to lodge B to complete next mission... Way to weak and with 600-1600 credit rewards, you can fast forward to most guns with barely any hunting at all.In all - not a bad game, but if your looking for authenticity, realism and a challenge, go to COTW instead.If its improved or on sale and you want a simpler hunting game without too much complexity, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing improvement over The Hunter: Call of the Wild in almost every way. Avalanche's game has been fundamentally broken since launch and they just release DLC after DLC on top of it, this appears to completely dethrone that game and make some incredible improvements along the way.Passive animal behaviors are interesting and realisticWide range of animals to hunt on day 1Engaging and sensible progression system: get better at things the more you do themBallistics are accurately modeled and are a fundamental component of gameplayGenetics ecosystem which rewards you for culling less fit animals and thinning overpopulationsComplex needs system and animal travel routinesGraphics are brilliant, performance is very good.Detailed shot replay system displaying projectile path in a 3D model with a chart showing bullet velocity as it makes its way through various organsWide range of weapons and attachments available on day 1Access to a jeep that you can drive included in the game's purchase, unlike Call of the Wild which makes you buy access to an ATV with a microtransaction.Real brand names and products, not made up mumbo-jumbo weapons and attachments.Responsive and fair animal behavior in response to player movement and concealment unlike another game in which it's completely unpredictable at times.Multiple difficulty levels to get the kind of gameplay that you want.Probably several other big features that I'm forgetting to mention. All around this is a Call of the Wild killer for me.And something I wasn't expecting: An engaging and interesting backstory. They went out of their way to make the world realistic and human. Every little detail is like a teabag on the face of Call of the Wild's forced poorly written political nonsense. For example (spoiler alert) when reviewing emails at the start of the game you find out how your grandfather became sick. A friend warned him that Mule Deer meat was getting people incredibly sick and your grandfather calls him a conspiracy theorist and dismisses the warning. You also find that your family tried to dissuade your grandfather from getting you involved in his world suggesting that the player had a comfortable life in LA. Absolutely brilliant, all of it.Currently the day 1 issues are annoying but sound like they will be quickly patched: FOV slider and key rebinding.The game is entirely playable in its current state but these couple items will really round out the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to get into a hunting simulator so I'd thought I'd treat myself to a nextgen game and purchased this; it is a visually stunning game which runs flawlessly on my computer specs: i5 CPU ; GTX 1650 GPU ; 8GB RAM - it's a 'decent' prebuilt computer from 2019. All that was needed was to turn shadows detail to medium and I was g2g.Animals travel in families; colloquially known as herds, which you will familiarize yourself with their patterns, and by selective darwinism, trim them to become great trophies.--PROS--• Experience is earned, not taught.• The other hunting game seems to be at the end of its life cycle.--NEUTRAL--• I had a problem finding species of animals (on the pause menu map) that weren't discovered in my encyclopedia.• The vehicle gets stuck on low geometry.--CONS--• There is no technical "boot camp" with access to live animals.• River Knox, our protagonist, can't really defend himself against hostile wildlife.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys hunting. I played The Hunter COTW on the console for over 100 hours and had a lot of fun with it. BUT: The game is very repetitive in the long run and the animals don't behave realistically. These problems don't exist in Way of the Hunter. The animals behave more realistically than in the competition. The graphics and map design are more immersive and make it easy to put hours into this game. Long-term motivation is also a given in this game. While in The Hunter COTW you could only grind for (far too expensive) weapons, in Way of the Hunter you have the opportunity to maintain your territory by constantly trying to improve the genetics. You are then rewarded with bigger and better trophies. I understand the criticism in other players' reviews. I also have the problem that the edges of textures often look pixelated. I hope that this will be fixed in the future. Personally, I would also like to see more content, such as tents, dummies, etc. (as they already exist in the game). (some of which already exist in The Hunter COTW).Overall, I am very happy with the game and I will invest many more hours in this game in the future. I honestly don't understand why the competition, The Hunter COTW, still gets a lot more attention than Way of the Hunter.  Way of the Hunter simply offers more immersive gameplay, which is why I will never switch back to The Hunter COTW.Cheers

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game so far, and it has lots of room to grow. As a hunter, I really enjoy the aspect of finding animals, in my case specifically whitetails, and watching them grow. The missions can be tedious, but the story is interesting and many of the missions are enjoyable. It also allows the player to acquire new items, like guns and callers, without grinding too hard. Since buying this game, I haven't played much else.Overall a great hunting game with amazing potential. The variety of weapons at launch is satisfactory, but feels lacking for people like me that like to bow hunt. My hope is that they add said bows, and purchasable tree stands. _childDocuments_.review: Among the hunting enthusiast simulation games, this one stands out with the rather enjoyable stalking loop. I always enjoyed outdoor activities starting even before Scouting, but the "need" to hunt ebbed as opportunities increased as I grew up. But I never lost my love of picking carefully through the woods to discover who lives there, and peek at their lives, their homes, their schedules. Sometimes even walking right up on some poor creature that didn't expect me in his day.This game captures that part I love so much, getting to know the land and its inhabitants. No, it doesn't have a 100 combinations of rifles chambered with every caliber you can dream of.  It doesn't have a giant array of kit and tools for stalking, trapping, baiting, or ambushing. Hey, humans are cool, we make cool tools, and there are hunting games that let you power game endless trophy hunts. I get it. And those games exist.But I have hundreds of games about instruments of mass death. This is about the only one that lets me stalk through the woods. If that's the part that intrigues you, and not the tools, and you like it to look pretty good while doing it, you'll like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being released in August 2022, my brief experience with "Way of the Hunter" left me utterly disappointed and frustrated. Even in just under two hours of playtime, I encountered several issues that made it impossible to recommend this game.First and foremost, the game's portrayal of animals is shockingly unrealistic. For a hunting game released in 2022, one would expect a higher level of authenticity in animal behavior. However, "Way of the Hunter" completely misses the mark. Animals exhibit bizarre and unconvincing behavior, making the hunting experience feel more like a caricature than a genuine simulation.Despite having the graphics settings maxed out, I was sorely disappointed by the visuals. I had anticipated breathtaking landscapes and stunning environments but found poorly rendered unattractive scenes. In a gaming landscape where graphical fidelity has come a long way, it's disheartening to see a game released in 2022 fall so short in this department.Furthermore, within this short two-hour timeframe, the lack of depth and variety in gameplay became apparent. Repetition set in quickly, and the limited content left me bored and unenthusiastic about continuing. "Way of the Hunter" lacks meaningful challenges and engaging activities, making me question the value of my time spent on the game.In conclusion, although "Way of the Hunter" was released in August 2022, my initial experience left me unsatisfied and frustrated. The unrealistic animal behavior, subpar graphics, and lack of engaging gameplay elements make this game a poor choice for anyone seeking an enjoyable hunting experience. I advise potential buyers to explore other hunting games that offer a more rewarding and immersive gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It has issues, sure. The tracking is kinda garbage. You have to wait for the blood trails to "flash". Sometimes they don't trigger properly, and when they do, it's all the same color as tracks, beds, droppings, urine, drinking spots, etc., which makes it really easy to step in the wrong direction and lose your way. The deer sometimes turn erratically while running away, and there's no clear way to know which direction the next blood stain is in resulting in so much standing around looking in every direction feeling lost and killing the flow of the gameplay loop. No FOV slider, though not a big issue with me, is kinda inexcusable, but the big one for me is no key bindings. Not only can you not bind your keys but, if you're not using a controller, they don't even bother to tell you what the keys are. Literally the only key mapping they show is an xbox controller. If you're using a keyboard.. you know... like a PC player (the platform we're literally on).. then ♥♥♥♥ you. "We're adding those in the next couple of patches" is a piss poor response.  It just is. This wasn't released as early access. That being said, the actual game itself is fun. It looks great, sounds great, performs great, and is completely immersive. I do recommend it, if keybinds and FOV aren't that big of a deal for you (for now). The blood trail thing is super unclear but, hopfully they work on that. Ultimately it just pushes you to be a better, and more careful shot. It's just sad that poor decisions on the dev's side are the reason for it.
