_childDocuments_.review: Like most of us I loved the first game! And like the most of us I'd like to love this one too but there are too many game breaking systems in here. Just to mention a few things I stumbled upon:- There are not enough spots on your map to gather resources! Gathering resources is a real pain in the a$$ in Sheltered 2. At least in your own territory and as soon as you want to gather resources in another factions territory you get constantly attacked - Durability is ridiculously annoying in Sheltered 2! First of all the durability of your items and devices depend on the "Intelligence" stat of its builder. Which means everything you build in early game must be replaced later anyway (which costs again ridiculous amounts of resources!). And what comes on top of that is the rate with which durability declines in in this game. It's just insane! I mean, how often does an oxygen filter need to be maintained in real life?! Or a water filtering system?! Once or maybe twice a year?! In Sheltered 2 every 2 days as you can watch the numbers decline within seconds!- have you ever suffered from food poisoning just because you haven't taken a shower for 2 days? No? In Sheltered 2 you do get food poisoning INSTANTLY!- or have you ever had a heatstroke when you were outdoors at 27 degrees celcuis (80 degrees F)? Here you get a heatstroke within SECONDS, not hours exposed to the sun, I'm literally talking about SECONDS!- My crew can't take medicine, it just won't work (at least the antidote for poisoning)- in a post apocalyptic world the one thing you should be able to trade with is in my oppinion WATER! but here you just can't do that (in Sheltered 1 you could do that)- you can automate some of your crews needs like hunger or thirst and so on, but sometimes if you manualy order them to eat or drink in a queue of different other tasks, they get to do it twice and waste valuable resourcess because the automated needs get to interrupt that queue- diplomacy is horrible in this game! Even though you have a "neutral" relationship with another faction they'll still attack you on sight or raid your bunker! You have a bare minimum of interaction options and those are really not satisfying- you can make rations for your outdoor expedition by preparing food. But let's say you have no other food left in your bunker except those rations, eating those doesn't lower your hunger bar! It makes literally no sense at all having your crew eat those rations!- and now my biggest issue with this game: RAIN! When your weather bar tells you it's going to rain on a certain day, it just doesn't! And from day 30 or so, it stops raining at all! All my crew members are dying from dehydration from that moment on and that's pretty frustrating because reaching day 30 is really really hard in Sheltered 2!- and last but not least: a bear, a giant grown a$$ bear gives you less flesh and leather than a RABBIT! xDLike I said, I'd really like to love this game and give it a postitive review but I just can't do that at its current state. All I mentioned makes the game unplayable for me and I hope these issues get fixed soon, because the potential to be a great game is definitely there.

I have clocked in my fair share of hours in the original Sheltered and in my 10 hours of playthrough since release I have to say this game has a MASSIVE balancing issue. Yes, it’s a good take on the classic resource management / underground colony game - but unlike the original game finding resources is way too hard. The original game had multiple places that you could go to to gather the materials you need. I cannot stress this enough - there are not enough places to travel to outside of the forest. This game essentially forces you to trade with other factions and the trade value on each item is RIDICULOUSLY high. Unless you’re planning on giving up some of your medical supplies (which are an absolute pain to craft at a low level) or a heap of food … you’re stuffed! The Dev’s really need to step up the balancing issues, and I would really encourage them to take what their community is saying into careful consideration to make this game the best version of itself.

Resource farming is just a pain and boring (excludes via traders)... you get to a location, your guys will 'auto-search' and you take what you can. or you kill someone, but....2. when you kill someone (from an encounter), your dude will get a -1000000 mood. Yeah, I get that killing is bad, but most encounters you are given 2 choices... Flee or Attack, and Flee is based on chance %. 3. Progression in the game is soooooooooooo slow, and there are no mechanics to feed you the urgency. Of the few hours I had, I'm just stuck at a certain point... basically doing nothing but moving around the map and scavenging of parts to craft. You are going to get busy in the shelter, repairing stuff... like everything everyday.7. Crafting... erm, you craft what you can with what you scavenged and with almost with no reasons or objectives to do any of that. _childDocuments_.review: At first I was a little hesistant because so many people gave bad reviews, especially about the "new rat problem" but that changed pretty quickly.So first of all: This game is by no means perfect but after 33hours I have not encountered anything thats gamebreaking or making the game less fun. Yes, sometimes you have to save and reload your file, because you get a sound bug or a character is stuck after rearranging the shelter. But that can be fixed in like 10 seconds by just reloading! It happened about 4 times now? Which is absolutely okay with over 30 hours! There are better or more expensive games that give you these kinds of bugs more frequently hahaNext point on my list is: This game is sloooooow! Getting ressources takes time and I have yet to start real fights over territory with the 6 other factions! Maybe that is the reason it's so slow and I would get more if I had more territory for my own? I doubt it but I certainly don't know!The furniture tier one breaking nonstop: If you pay attention you know you have to change, not the game. Because citizens with higher intellect build furniture with more durability. Start with int 5 in your character creation. If one has 5 intellect let him/her build your shelter interior! As easy as that. You can always get a higher int stat and "rebuild" your stuff. Just build a new one and destroy the old.The rat problem: I can't see it. If you want to have it "easier" against the rats start with a cat when you create your first character. You can add a pet from the beginning but cats are really powerful at the start. They not only kill rats if they encounter them but they also go "hunting" at night and bring home whatever they find outside your shelter. This may be meat, but this may also be ressources and gold/silver things.If you maintain a clean shelter (above 75%) there won't be a huge rat problem. There just won't be any rats. Maybe one but if you have a rat trap or a cat the rat gets beaten up really quick.I did have a pretty bad rat situation once where my citizens got really sick of it, were vomitting pretty much half the time and set half of the shelter on fire.BUT! And here is the point where I absolutely DO NOT agree with other/bad reviews: You can get rid of it! Get all your citizens back to the shelter and have them cleaning nonstop, meanwhile you put rat traps down, in case you haven't before and a fireextinguisher is very helpful aswell against all the mad lads breaking stuff and the rats nibbling on all your furniture. My cat was my hero in that situation though! It killed like 4 rats a day before he went out hunting for prey and bringing me more stuff to build more rat traps. My hero I tell you. I think the cat was smarter than me at that point.It took me about 3 ingame days with nonstop cleaning and emptying rat traps to get rid of them completely. Of course my citizens had to take turns to take care of their needs but with 5 or 6 people this was absolutely doable. My shelter had 3 layers at this point with 6 sections (or whatever is the maximum per layer) and one and a half layer was just dirt at this point. I honestly don't know if it makes a difference, but if so it was probably not very beneficial for me, having 50% of the worst tier rooms. I don't know how it would be with more or maximum shelter size or citizen count! After 33 hours I am still far away from that.All in all I can say: The only downside of this game is beeing slow, but you can also say it is very relaxing and you can spend a lot of time with it! This game has more aspects than the introduction shows you! Pay attention! Read the provided ingame information. Sometimes you do lose a citizen or two in battle but I personally didn't reload at that point because it was nobody, that was super needed. I just got two new ones :xA tip for everyone: When you rearrange your shelter, zoom in as close as you can. You do get more "room" when you squish everything together and zooming in has helped me A LOT! Sometimes it's just a pixel or two needed to place some new furniture, so zoom all in!I would absolutely recommend this game ♥

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game. It's got everything I want from a resource managing survival sim (well, maybe it's missing a few automation options that would be nice but it's pretty solid overall). The problem is the game has significant bugs that have ruined my several attempts at a play-through. The problems are generally one of two categories - people or built items. For people, 3 times in 3 different games I've had a player freeze and refuse to follow commands. Once was after a prisoner was recruited and twice it happened while somebody was sitting down to eat. They are clickable, I can assign them a task, but they don't move, they just slowly die of thirst or dehydration. I was able to work around this by going back to a previous save point because it's noticeable pretty quickly.With the other bug, it's usually too late by the time I notice it. What happens is something becomes inaccessible, with the reason being that another person is using the device, even when that can't possibly be true. It has happened to a planter and a lab bench, and I solved the issue by deconstructing and remaking them (a waste, but not game-ending). However, twice (on different playings), one of my 4 survival utilities fell victim, and there was nothing for me to do about it. When your water collector is no longer able to be upgraded because the game thinks it is in use, there is no way to reconstruct it and you're just stuck for the whole game with an inferior water collector. This also happened to my oxygen filter, which capped my shelter at 6 people for the whole game. I've put a lot of hours into this game, hoping that next time I won't run into one of these bugs, but at this point I need to stop and play something that works. Until these issues are resolved, I would stay away from this title.

_childDocuments_.review: My extremely honest opinion of this game:I feel like people rated it so badly because they expected it to be like the first game, which in some ways it is but mostly its not. This game is interesting and fun and has a lot of neat aspects, such as the moods and ailments, Sheltered is a great game and I think a lot of the charm is from the pixel-y game look which this one doesn't have. I still think this game is worth the money(I got it on sale for $4.99) I have enjoyed playing thus far and will continue playing because in its own way this game is fun.Similarities to Sheltered-The idea of living after nuclear falloutThe idea of building and preparing your vaultMaking your vault peopleDifferences-You can customize your character's clothes and accessories differently than the first gameYou can train your pets to have skillsthe graphicsbeing able to switch from side view to top down above groundbeing able to use the land above your shelter for growing crops or having animalsbeing able to complete jobs for other factions and gaining trust with them or losing trustItems, tools, food, and pieces for building all have ratings of how good they are (1 star to 3 star)All in all I think this game got more hate than it deserves. _childDocuments_.review: Word at the beginning:-------------------------I dont understand why people write a review for a game they played less then 5 hrs. Its impossible to fair judge a game and saying that the content is less then in Part 1 just proves they didnt really play the game. That beeing said, i played this game over 70 hrs (i Played about 72 hrs nonstop and then fell asleep at the computer) you can be sure that i do a fair review.Sheltered 2 Review:------------------------Graphics: Compared to Sheltered 1, the graphics are alot better (even though its not the best graphics ive seen in other games) still it is nice looking at The Yard which u can build stuff on. The Objects you can place look nice, all in one i like the changes.Gameplay:Gameplay is straight forward, you build your Shelter go out and scavange the area. But in addition they added a Faction system, and this is where it gets interesting, u can either be allied with em or go full crazy and try to kill em all. Everything u do has consequences towards the faction you are dealing with.Another really great addition is that you can take Prisoners, If u threat them good you can maybe convince them to join your Faction, or you can decide to execute him and just use him as Food or Fuel for your incinerator. By building a Garage you can build up to 3 Vehicles (Bicycle, Motorcycle or the PickupTruck) The Parts you can find by scavanging Carparks, Parkinglots or Scrapyards to name a few. In Fights you have several new abilities you can choose if u want, and you can choose to attack certain bodyparts which gives you extra things to do. Overall i think the Gameplay is ALOT better than Part 1 and i really like the changes they made. The Devs allready stated that they will add Pets in a later Content Update.Bugs:As for nearly every game this game has Bugs too, i agree with alot people that it would have been better to do a early access or atleast do some more beta testing. Unfortunatly its too late for that. The Devs are working alot to fix the Bugs which are present. I know it can be frustrating but its not a reason to write a negative review after playing for less then 5 hrs)Difficulty:this game (at least i feel like it) is harder then the first part. If you dont Plan ahead of the Seasons you will end up losing your people. Water is just one of the problems u will have in Summer ;) Summary:-----------Pros:- Better Graphics- Faction system- Nice new Buildings/Objects- Surface Buildable- 3 VehiclesCons:- BugsSo you see the only negative i can say are some Bugs you will come across. The devs are working on fixing them pretty fast (4 Updates in the first 3 days) I hope you wont read all these negative reviews, because most of them didnt play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright first off, I played the first game and looked forward to this game, the many concerns of other players are usually about rats and bugs, i also agree with the bugs, but for rats you really only need a cat and to keep the shelter clean with a mop to avoid the infestation also rat traps help when they spawn at night when the cat isn't there.Disclaimer:I've played about 20 hours on record and basically figured out what to do for the scenarios some people have problems with, minus the bugs so i'm not some "ALL KNOWING BUDDHA" at the game, no i just basically tinkered around my first play through and am now on my second which is doing CONSIDERABLY well compared to the dehydrated idiots on my first run, so here are my thoughts, but firstSolutions i found for anyone looking for it:-If the place is dirty use the mop every day or so, just basically assign someone to clean before the end of the in game day if you want to keep efficiency up, i've only had a cat as a pet so far so a litterbox will help and cleaning it when its up to 70% should help out a ton since the pets usually poop in the shelter thus leading to more hours cleaning.-mood going down fast? try not to kill anyone you see, essentially just knock them out, you still get their crap that way.-the "In the dark" negative mood? no idea why it does that even though you have lights, but just basically have electric tier 2 lights on the floor the settlers all hang out in, more or less make sure the lights cover the whole floor. Note: the survivors hang out in rooms/levels that have temps between 12C-18C temperature, so should be easy to figure out where.-food going bad? use the partitioner to section off the pantry, have a fan in there if you want and set the temp to the lowest, food will stay fine for a LONG while.-durability so crap? Use only one settler for construction and crafting, preferably one with high int stat.-slow game? speed it up, find the keybind, or if thats not what you mean, speed it up yourself. You can start a fight with any faction out there, just make sure to leave some people at your base OR, put the storage and pantry next to the door, and just give them what they want, they will leave without a fuss, its what i did at first and it was effective.-Most common problem i found scrolling is rats, the damn rats? Clean the shelter using a mop, have a cat as a starter pet, i dont care if you're a "dog" person, you can find a dog later, to survive even a little bit longer with the attention span of a goldfish (like me) you need a cat, they will murder any rats that wander in, bring you food if you level "prey drive" enough and also boost survivor mood in the shelter, a dog can be found in the wooded areas of the map, right click on the tile and bam options should show up. thus giving you dog, just basically let your explorers run around an entire set of wooded tiles on the map and should give you an encounter with a dog at least once (Also have a dog whistle equipped to one of your settlers).Main problems i found: -how slow the game feels, the base is comparatively bigger than the last game, so why not allow running? Maybe at the cost of getting tired quicker? Because fires happen suddenly and how leisurely they go extinguish the fire, and by then the fire has spread to multiple furniture thus being barely controllable. -upgrades, i hate this new upgrade system, you basically have to gamble with resources you find and hope you get a tier 2+ crafting material-Absolutely crap percentages. A 70% chance to flee from 1 person is impossible you say? 2 times in a row? yeah hard to believe.-Stats, they only level up fast if you keep fighting, which is dumb since you really should avoid fighting ANYONE you wouldn't want to piss off (just yet) since if you get enough encounters they will turn into enemies and be hostile. if you make enemies of 2+ factions they will attack your base and they will attack your base at the SAME time, no breaks, which is HORSE CRAP.-THAT!, they attack you in tandem if you piss them off enough, it was pretty punishing, i almost lost 2 survivors to this lunacy, they also didnt like each other as well, so there was also that.-RnJesus either loves you or hates you, item spawn is essentially a gamble, since the map is generated, there is no way you could spawn next to a farm, a scrapyard,  etc. i once spawned next to basically nothing, just a caravan and the next lootable place was in unfriendly territory. so had to restart.-Hit chance is somewhat dumb, i have a high dex survivor in my current playthough miss a body shot, the one without a % chance to miss, make hit chance obvious please.-Game is super punishing very early on since you spawn in only DESERTS, what with the droughts and such, hopefully the devs will add in some different spawn locations even if they are random so you could at least stand a chance early on.-automation of bodily needs needs to have a tweak, if there are free beds and your settler is too far, sure why not just collapse on the floor, but there is an open bed RIGHT THERE on the same floor as them, they somehow still choose to sleep on the floor. The bugs i've encountered:-A sound bug occurs when you've played the game for too long, if you speed it up the sound starts breaking, then eventually it starts breaking even if you dont speed it up-Fixing things sometimes doesn't fix things, a reload fixes that issue but reloading is too tedious for that one specific thing that needs repair.- Also the game starts losing frames the longer you play.try the solutions i've found in your next playthrough, maybe you'll stand a chance, because i HAVEN'T encountered a single infestation yet. and fires dont start randomly, remove the pyromaniac from your base, easy as that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a finished game. It's tremendously buggy. Certain functionalities are non-functional and the balance is awful. I'm at the point where no matter what I do, I cannot fail. The original game had that issue as well, but I feel to a lesser extent. I have a lot of complaints about the functionality and the basic behaviors of the survivors in your shelter. For example, running three floors down to get water for a fire that is on the same floor as them, with a free water source just a few feet away. Standing in the freezer long after their health starts ticking down. Had a guy go to sleep in a bed right next to a fire, unperturbed. You have to micro-manage or they will get themselves deleted. There are too many things like this to list here, and more bugs than I can count.People throw a lot of accusations of dead games around, this one is legit dead. They have a roadmap completely left untouched for a long time. There are broken achievements that you need to download a third-party fix to trigger if you want to complete the game. They fully released an unfinished game and then bailed on it. That all being said, I bought it for like 2$ and I have enjoyed it immensely. It's not a good game, but it's an enjoyable game. If the grinding in the first Sheltered scratched an itch in your brain nicely, this will probably scratch it similarly. Perhaps not as much, but it's a difficult itch to scratch sometimes. I don't regret my purchase and I do find it entertaining. I wish steam had a middle hand-wiggle with an 'eeeeeeh' instead of just a thumbs up and a thumbs down.

If you don't want it to be compared, don't release it with the same name and a number at the back.The Good Stuff:"Improved" graphics (Some people loved the pixel art)FactionsCooking(!!)Traits and skillsNew Temperature / Weather systemStuff that used to exist:PetsI absolutely adored Pets in 1. _childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is a survival management simulator. Build, defend, survive, make friends or foes, kill or get killed. 20 years after the end of the world, six fractions dominate the wasteland. Your fraction is the seventh and pretty new. Your goal is to bring peace into the lands. How you do that, depends on your decisions. You can make runs easier or harder, depending on the options you choose (how often people gonna break into your home, how many resources spawn, etc.). Either way, you start with a leader and two side characters in your faction.The faction creation is as simple as choosing a name and a crest. Creating the leader goes way more into detail. Aside from changing his looks, you can change his attributes and give him character traits. You start with 5 points, "good" traits will lower your points but you can add a bad trait to get more points. This allows you to add more good traits in return. In total, this allows for a unique character overall because there are over 50 traits! The tutorial will explain the basics very well. It will guide you through your first expedition, building a new room, and shows you how to satisfy a few basic needs. After that, you're on your own. You already know the goal but how you will achieve that, or even if you will, depends on you. My run started with one bus on the map. I got a few resources there but not nearly enough to build enough, so I needed to go into the territory of other fractions. They will immediately notice and ask what you want. There is no chance to steal from that in the very beginning. Make friends first. You can build chairs, beds, toilets, new rooms, and much more. I don't want to say there are no limits but it's enough for an in-depth experience. For everything you build, you will need resources like wood. You can get these things on expeditions, by recycling trash or even other things you don't personally need (right now). A good way to survive would be to build everything helping you in satisfying basic needs (A way to get food (vegetables), a bed, toilet, shower, etc.). After that, you can see what else. Technically, this is still the beginning but let's call it the middle. The tutorial is over and you're on your own. You now can do whatever some people will feel lost now. If you don't know what to do, look for your fraction's goals. They can guide you a bit and you will have something to look forward to. This helped me a lot. Meeting other factions and people can be dangerous. This can result in fights (especially if you are friends with a faction and meet their foes or have foes yourself). Another reason to send your people prepared. Give them weapons. Fights aren't tactical deep when you compare it to turn-based strategy games but Sheltered 2 isn't mainly one so it would be an unfair comparison.Battles aren't the only way to die through. Hunger, cold, and infections can result in death too.   Sheltered 2 is a fun survival and management game. It's deep enough to be tactical demanding while still not being overly complicated. Most of the time, you will have an idea of what to do and keep an overview of everything. You can decide how you want the events to play out. This doesn't mean it's easy nor that you can as you like. It could be a bit more beginner-friendly and have more QoL features but aside from that, it's a good simulation. You should definitely check it out on sale if you want a survival management simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loved the first Sheltered, the sequel has definitively lost the charm of the original.  I loved the pixel style of the original and the new 3D style (while showing a lot more) feels quite bland and needlessly complicated, which more or less surmises how I feel about Sheltered 2. ---But I digress. I will still go into detail as to why I can't recommend this.  Firstly, the whole premise really annoys me.  I don't particularly care for the dev's reasoning why there wouldn't be children or pets 20 years later in a post-apocalyptic nuclear wasteland, but the whole draw for me with the original game was that you started off as a family in a bunker.  Now that they've gone the whole "build your squad/faction" route rather than build on the original's premise, the game feels fundamentally generic and doesn't really bring anything new to the table. Even the music sounds pretty dull.I don't demand a sequel (or a new game) has to reinvent the wheel every single time. But a game should at the very least execute its mechanics well, especially when measured against similar types of games.  To me at least, Sheltered 2, at its gameplay core is eerily similar to The Last Stand: Dead Zone (a free-to-play multiplayer game on  that's probably dead now because of the end of Flash). I feel Dead Zone (from memory) still fundamentally has stronger core gameplay than Sheltered 2.  If I have to elaborate through another example, Dust to the End (while a more merchant oriented game) is another post-apocalyptic base-building squad builder with an over-world map, turn-based combat encounters and a social interactions system.  In comparison to Sheltered 2, Dust to the End has a far more enjoyable experience to offer than this game.  Furthermore, Sheltered 1 may have lacked detailed social and faction interactions, but what it did offer felt satisfying to play through and compelled me to revisit the game every now and then.This is not to say that I haven't noticed the more positive aspects of the sequel. I can still attest to having some interest in the new game mechanics (expanded faction and social interactions, prisoner/hostage system, more building options, temperature system, body-targeting turn based combat etc).  Unfortunately, I don't think these mechanics are an enhancement of gameplay but rather an over-complication of gameplay.  The gameplay issues I have are more or less surmised by the whole interface.  It doesn't feel particularly intuitive; you are immediately overwhelmed with information and systems that feel like chores, rather than things which compel me to be comfortably immersed in.  I understand it's a fine line between deep, meaningful complex mechanics and overly-complex confusing mechanics but with Sheltered 2 its sadly a case of the latter rather than former.While contemplating writing this review, I saw some discourse complaining about some reviews being released only after an hour of gameplay and people should play more before they give their opinion.  I was initially going to play more before writing this review just to be above question.  But I fundamentally disagree with the whole "it gets better after 100 hours" mentality.  First impressions are everything, especially with games. What you do at the start should set up your audience to want to continue playing the game.  Unfortunately, all that Sheltered 2 does is just set up a lot of busy work that doesn't fundamentally feel enjoyable to slog through, at least for me.  And the biggest detractor of the enjoyment and immersion is (as I've said previously) the interface design.---Though I have thought about refunding it, I think I will still keep the game and play things through until I feel I've seen everything that the mechanics have to offer.  But just know that its curiosity more than enjoyment that is keeping me sticking with Sheltered 2.---Edit 1 (23/09/2021): ---Edit 2 (26/09/2021): ---Edit 3 (4/12/2023): I don't know if any of the bugs I've listed above have been solved but I do know this game has more or less been abandoned by the looks of it.  So I've struck all my edits because honestly, it doesn't matter anymore and I'm never going to touch this game again.  Stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: The release of this game was VERY disappointing BUT the latest version of the game is very playable.Sheltered 2 is just as good as the original Sheltered but it's a different game. It doesn't have simple pixel graphics, simple game mechanics and it doesn't have personality/humour. None of the options have any meaningful (or fun) dialogue.If you chose to fight factions they will storm your bunker eventually, sometimes two factions at once if you've been very naughty.With the right charisma skill the factions can be totally avoided. Build a bookcase and let the expedition team read to level 6 charisma and choose "Mission of Mercy". Bingo.The skills are mostly a load of BS so you pick the ones that help in a fight. The developers seems to have been really bad at coming up with useful skills and/or how to implement them in gameplay.Making food stuffs is a bit more nuanced and you can actually make different dishes with the food you grow. The temperature restrictions on what you can grow is overly constricting. It IS very possible to grow what you need but and it takes planning and a lot of shelves to get the later game dishes on the menue.The shelter environment consists of heat, water, air and goop (and sometimes fire). The heat managing  seems to be hard for some players to get a grip on. If you put a radiator and a cooling fan, both set on the same temperature, in the same area they keep the temperature at a comfortable level for the inhabitants all year round. They only use energy if they are working against temperature differences, so you will not use up more energy using them at the same time.The incinerator is very useful for conserving energy. If there's a breach you can burn the intruders' bodies for many hours and save fuel.The pets (only cats and dogs, I miss my trusty horse) are a bit more of a nuisance but they are helpful. Don't forget to clean the litter box. You can have chickens.The easiest way to get through the game is to kill off all the faction leaders but you miss out on the little bit of narrative there is in the game if you do.For some reason the game puts my graphics card (Gtx 1660 super duper ding dong) at 100% even at the lowest settings, and it really shouldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 has a lot in common with the original Sheltered, but with some fresh twists. I've started a handful of games, my current, longest, game is on day 21. Pros: - the crafting system is great, and allows for creative recycling - bugs I saw on launch day were fixed and released 24-48 hours later (nice.) - I'm really enjoying the factions now that I've looted a few of their POIs and done some jobs. - I don't miss the pets or kids from Sheltered 1, which I could never keep alive. Sheltered 2 is dark, but not Sheltered 1 dark. - the character point mechanics are very nicely balanced, and added a lot of excitement to leveling up- it's a challenge to keep my small (5 people) faction alive and with moderately full needs bars while trying to move my whole faction and my base forward. I think that's also nicely balanced, I have to plan ahead and think carefully to succeed. - I like that there's a lot to figure out on my own. The tutorial is a great introduction, but it doesn't hold your hand to cover all the game play. I had several "ooooh" moments when I figured out what I was supposed to do. Cons: - the early grind is a lot of grind, I've started updating all my equipment and it helps, but poor Anna is out there fixing the water collector every day, lol. - I've started seeing some performance lag in the past few (18-21ish) game days, and one of my characters appears to levitate where ever he goes. Which is a pretty fun bug, if I'm honest. Fly, Ronald, fly. - the faces are a bit mush, but you only see a close up of your characters in the start up screen, they look fine at game distance. And who has time to worry about how pretty their character is when the water collector is down to 48% again. - there's a lot to like about the factions, but I think they're fairly generic. The descriptions for each faction imply an interesting backstory, but there's not a lot of distinction I've seen so far in how the faction AIs behave. - I'm one aloe vera plant short of being able to make a base defense against raids and I can't find it anywhere. All in all, I'm having fun and I'm excited to start the game again.

_childDocuments_.review: is a survival colony simulation with a focus on management and offers 4 difficulty settings. I never played the first game so I am unable to compare the two.You will start out with 3 people in your colony and get more inhabitants later on. You have a 2D view in your colony where you can scroll up and down, and this goes really smoothly.Outside you will have a water collector, an oxygen filter, and a patch where you can plant seeds. Whereas inside you can recycle items or junk that you won't need in order to craft new items.In addition to building, your colonists will also need a bed to sleep in, a place to shower and keep clean, etc. You can also build other things to help them improve, such as a bookcase so they can study and improve their intelligence, a treadmill so they can exercise and improve dexterity. There are 4 tiers of unlocks so you will be going through quite a lot of iterations.As expected, things will also break down over time, and you will need to also take care of the repairs as things wear down, in addition to making sure that your folks are also kept clean as to not get ill.You can go on expeditions in order to get new items or to meet other groups. After getting new items you can bring them back to base. When you meet other people you can trade with them, take on some jobs for them, or fight them.Likewise you will also face raids to your own base. There are 4 different difficulty settings so this determines how often this happens.Some of the in-base tasks can be automated such as eating and sleeping, so you don't have to worry about feeding them on time or making sure that they get to bed.The game offers a nice in-game tutorial to get you started, so even though it might take a little bit of time to get used to what you need to do, you still have a good starting point here.The graphics are okay, there isn't much variety in the appearances, but that is okay.The music is a bit sad and gloomy, as it should be in these kind of games.The game can be fully played with a mouse.I think the price of €19.99 is a fair price. You will get plenty of playtime for this price.It took me quite a while to get used to what I needed to do. For example, it was not clear that I should be scavenging enemy locations for new items, so it was a  bit slow going at first. After finding out, things became a lot smoother. The colonists do not always do the most logical thing, so the AI actions could be improved.I like the game because it's fun and doesn't have a lot of action--which is good for me. Mostly I am just finding items and creating new things, repairing items as they wear down, and building. The game has a management focus and is suitable for me.Verdict: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE/UPDATE: Changed my review to thumbs down.  All the cons are still the same.  There hasn't been an update or any word of an update in months and it looks like game has been abandoned by the developers.  It's a shame, the first game was amazing.  This as is isn't worth any amount of money.  I loved the first sheltered.  As some of the other reviews mentioned, this is similar, but is a bit more frustrating.  I have put this back on the shelf until they fix the issues with balancing positive and negative modifiers and fixing the rat issues.  Starting out with a cat and even with a cat, this feels like a hunting rats simulator instead of a survive the apocalypse simulator.  I recommend the game for 10$, it has potential, but as is, it's not worth full price.  Go play the first one instead and pick it up on sale until they fix it.Pros: - It's hard and gives you a good feel for apocalyptic living.- I do like the new factions system.  - The various ways to get food keeps things interesting.  It's fun, at least at the start.- My favorite part of the game is the new locations and how you can work them, however, because of the cons listed below, I never enjoyed or could play the game long enough to make use of the factions and the new location types.- Vehicles also sound cool, but again never really had the chance to test any of them out.Cons: - The killing rat simulator needs to be balanced.  Rats spawn way to fast and even with the antibiotics, there doesn't seem to be a way to cure the plague that comes with the rats, or at least be able to cure it faster that it kills you.  - The factions are a great idea, I am just not sure it works as is - there were bugs when I tried to trade and get jobs.- While the pyromaniac affliction was funny at first, it's really got to go.  Two games ruined because of rats and 2 games ruined because of the Pyro.  If you 1 dude back at the ranch becomes a Pyro, your done.   - Now, if there was enough positive modifiers to counteract the bad ones, Pro could be dealt with, but there just aren't.  For example, my last playthrough, the main guy had -70 for rats, -20 for dark (even though all areas had lights on), -20 for an argument (even though my guy had 10 charisma with all the + charisma affects going), -80 for killing someone - 75% chance of running and failed 3 times on the same excursion, led to me killing all 3 times, you would think you would eventually get used to having to kill people.  There were at least 5 other negative modifiers totaling over 400 negative.    That was with a guy who was specced for all the positive mood stuff you could have.   Recommendations for the Devs: - Fix the rat spawn rate or include that in the difficulty settings.- add a way to pick what type of terrain you start in - desert, hills, arctic, etc.  I didn't see rain for the first 30 days, so I assume you always start in the desert.- Fix the mood modifier balance.  Add more positive, reduce some of the negative ones - for example, the more you have to kill people, reduce the amount of stress it causes and the longer you have rats, the more you get used to them.  - Allow more customization for difficulty levels.  This could be part of the terrain options.

_childDocuments_.review: The AI and quality of life aspects of the game needs to be majorly polished. You can set the inhabitants to fulfil their needs once it hits below 75% (default) or 50%. Sometimes, the inhabitant just stands in one dark corner, making it hard to find them. There is no easy way of viewing all the stats of your inhabitants. This game has a lot of promise to be good, but the poor AI and complex management UI make it hard to recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't in good conscious recommend this game. I've spent a hefty amount of time to give it a reasonable review, having a love for the original. The Bad. This game is not beginner friendly, a few of your first playthroughs will just be understanding the mechanics, how to work with the absurdly bad UI and how to manage things that should be simple like taking prisoners, doing quests and otherwise. Unfortunately all of these things can unceremoniously break at any time. Eliminate 4 out of the 6 factions? Suddenly 2 of them revive, having no base and no way to actually destroy them a second time. They can, and will, continuously attack your outposts with nothing you can do about it. Horrible quests lines. If you manage to not break a quest, your reward is an abrupt end, no explanation on how to continue or just a fond "Thanks" without reward. Bad, horribly bad, faction reputation management. Killing a single member of another faction, if one gets away, nets you a 50-60 reputation loss. Doing a supply quest to -help- your reputation? 30 rep gained, and costs you 20-40 resources and you can only do this once in a blue moon while you can, and will, have 10-30 different faction encounters on each decently long looting trip. The only option you have when you encounter another faction is fight or flee, and flee is a percentage chance.Constant game breaking bugs. This one is a CONSTANT and I have encountered a game bug that has, in some form or another, entirely broken every single one of my 5 playthroughs. If you save a file right before your people return home, one of them will continuously stand by the door, not be interactable and have absolutely no way to do anything about it. Sometimes if you call a trader and it says one will arrive shortly, one never comes. This not only stops the traders from coming to your base on their own, but suddenly every aspect of someone visiting your bunker vanishes. No more attacks on you, no more factions coming to collect items for you to boost your rep, nothing. It's all gone. To the devs credit, they are smashing out these bugs, but it's one at a time... but this is a full -release-, not early access. To not being able to fix your generator(Devs fixed this one, but I'm still including it), to my leader dying from heat exhaustion despite being in a 0C freezer.The Good.If you like the first Sheltered, the mechanics are more or less the same with a few additional tweaks and new additions to keep your interest.Not only can you customize your three starting characters, your faction leader gets additional trait points for you to tinker about with, allowing you to customize each playthrough to your liking. Some of these perks, such as never having to sleep, are absolutely game changing. You also can find datadisks while looting in the world, allowing you to pick more of these traits, but not all, later in game. The updated in graphics is quite nice, and the base management is a lot more enjoyable. You're, to my knowledge, not limited by how far down you can dig and how expansive you can have your base. The surface of your base also serves as a garden, a place to build power generating buildings and otherwise. It adds a lot of fluff that was missing in the first game. The combat is a lot more RPG, with each attribute tree giving you abilities that will aid you and potentially your allies. There's a vast amount of combat items, from knives to sledgehammers, pistols to rifles. You can customize each of your characters loudout and there's numerous items to help further tailor your combat experience such as armor, grenades, etc. Looting feels nice and there's new ways to traverse, such as bikes, cars and motorcycles. These have to be repaired, but feel rewarding when you can finally kit your explorers out on looting runs. Conclusion.The frustration from this game stems from the fact that there is an absolutely wondrous game here, but someone made the choice to release it in a state that is obviously not completed. Each joyous occasion you'll have in this game will be met by an equally frustrating one that you have no choice on how to handle it due to bugs, broken mechanics or uncompleted quests.Once all the bugs are cleared out, I'd give this game a solid 8/10 and my recommendation. How this game currently stands 3/10, and my recommendation to avoid it until it's actually patched.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't honestly recommend the game, even though it does offer a fair amount of short term entertainment. Late game is pretty much just terrible micro management.Things that need to be fixed:- UI inconsistencies. Buttons vary from screen to screen, often causing you to click the wrong thing. Things like the recycler don't have the ability to sort by junk. Its just a mess.- Complex bases just light on fire all the time because you can't keep things in running order. Even if your survivors have the perk to automatically repair, they simply don't do the task. Either you have to spend all your time manually sending people around to repair stuff (super boring) or things break and light on fire.- Fires happen so quickly, that you often don't have time to even respond, or it takes to long to get there in large bases.- Crafting higher level materials is just a gamble. Even in late game, its nearly impossible to get the required materials to craft top tier things. After 40 hours I still hadn't been able to construct any T4 base stuff.- There are mechanics in the game that seem to be impossible to trigger. Such as the top int tree skill that supposedly gives the ability to raise another survivors max stat, I never found a way to actually access it.- Certain points in the game you can't get to the menu. For instance, if you start a combat that you know you're going to loose, you cant open the menu. I resorted to force quitting the game and reloading so I didn't waste my time in the slow combat.- Tons of arbitrary waits and button clicks in the UI. Takes way to many clicks to do basic things like having an exploration party try and flee combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only scratched the surface, but so far I have been really enjoying the game. I LOVE the first game, so I'm glad I wasn't [completely] disappointed with this. There are some pros and only a couple of cons that I have so far gathered in my short time with the game. I'll start with the cons.CONS: 1. Food: In my entire time playing, I have not encountered a single trader/location with any food. Not one morsel. I have tons of non-edible resources that I can just trade for non-edible resources. I found some seeds after desperately raiding a new order outpost, but that's about it. I'd get it if the devs were trying to be canon and made it seem as if all the food had been gathered, but there's no hint of this. I just... scouted until my food supplies were depleted. I know it's a survival game about the wasteland, but so was the first title and I had tons of food available then. At first I was like "cool, they made food more scarce, i like" but after four hours of not finding anything, it was more annoying than immersive.2. Customization: I don't want to be rude, but... well, here we go.It freakin' sucks. Worst part of my experience so far. Most of the faces look like versions of Sloth from the Goonies. The hair choices are boring, generic, and lifeless. There's like two shirts and three pants, each with maybe four colors (if that even). Years of development, and that's all that's been made? No shirts with logos? Tank tops? No shorts? Dresses? Only boots or converse shoes? For everybody? It's just so... bare. Huge turn off. Made my nipples soft. Not much negative I have to say. Like I said, I enjoy the game, but those two things really need to be addressed. Okay, now onto the things I like.PROS: 1. Visuals: Although I really dug the charm of the first game's pixelated style, I love the new 3D perspectives and I think its an improvement, at least atmospherically. The introduction of the z-axis is really cool, and I like the lighting/weather effects (ex lightning, sandstorms, rain, sunlight and fading shadows, floodlights during night cycles and how lurkers are only faintly visible in the dark). I give the new look a thumbs up. 2. Traversal: I like the new map. I love how you can take over regions, and I think the addition of factions created not only opportunities, but a sort of tension that wasn't as prevalent in Sheltered 1. 3. Combat: Combat is waaaay better than the first game. A lot more options available, both offensively and defensively. it actually feels like an old school turn-based rpg now instead of just feeling like a super simple fight-or-flight sort of deal. You can target specific limbs, steal mid-combat, daze, blind, cripple, analyze, IMPRISON (which is a cool new addition). It's much better.Overall, I can see how some people feel that the game isn't as fun as the first, but I really think that's only because they haven't given it a fair chance. The game really picks up once your base becomes somewhat stable. Once you have enough amenities, automating players removes that initial stress that feels like such a killjoy early on. Once you get going, I feel like the game is way more enticing than the first. All-in-all, I'm glad I tried it instead of listening to some uber-early reviews band-wagon-bashing the game. IT IS NOT the same game. Also, thank you for the loyalty discount. Paired with the launch sale, I got the game for only $15. I'm looking forward to all the improvements I know you will be addressing soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing for over 80+ hours now and enjoying so far. Played the 1st game and Sheltered 2 had some decent updates. Always enjoyed sandbox/sim, survival-type games and this definitely fits that bill. You start off with (3) inhabitants and eventually build up to about 15? (I'm still at 11). Allying and wiping out factions, discovering places and scavenging and working site to gather resources, getting better weapons and vehicles for transportation, and now even having pets/pests. All good stuff!!Not sure what happened to most folks after the rats update. I had one person solely tasked to cleaning up the shelter and though had a short challenge at first figuring and working things out, didn't have much of an issue. Loving the new pets and the challenges finding/taming them and figuring out how they fit in our scheme of things. They keep bringing back lots of "desperate" meat which I end up feeding them anyway... lol hopefully they won't develop an "appetite" for it. Also got a lot of eggs now from the chickens, so cooking lots of breakfast meals... All and all it's a well developed game, considering there are only a few devs working on this game currently. There is a pretty active Discord server and also very informative wiki site. The game is a great deal at a very decent price. Hope you check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sequel of the 1st game that almost unrecognized from the prequel lol. The graphics now 3d, quality of nowadays game and finally we can distinguish our characters. Not only graphics, some new features also implemented into the game and make explorations and combat better. But there still some things that 1st game did better than this sequel.+ Ofc, the graphics enhanced 100%, fully 3d with lightning and shadow.+ The base buildings much more resembelance to Fallout Shelter than Sheltered 1 tbh,+ It fixes the problem choosing workbench/players/things if you get them stacked in one places.+ Now pacing of game is much slower than 1st game bcs its also much to do in shelter than 1st game.+ You can train peoples with many leveled training equipments including your pets.+ Explorations also enhanced, now it felt like myth & magic explorations.+ There is 6 factions that you can encounter in game, you can either side with everyone, side with few or one of them, or kill everyone. Affecting to your ending in this game.+ Crafting items a bit easier than 1st game, nothing too rare as long as you looting/killing and know what you recycle is+ There is a leveling in this game, either for combat, surviving, and mood. But mostly for combat.+ The number of survivors in this game is increased much more than 10 persons.+ The stacking and storages is much forgiving, you can level up to carry more and even wear 4 equipment for 1 person+ Rations for travelling also forgiving, you can create 2-10 rations depending of what food you based in, if you got meat from snare/cats in early game plus farming broccoli is good. You will never run out except if it get fire smh..- 1st game have this family format of 2 adults and 2 kids. While in this game your 1st start survivor is 3 of random strangers get together in one bunker- The relationship and talking in this game is questionable, I rarely see anyone praising or get to good talking. Mostly is insulting and idk why if you interrupt. It considered as rude an negative the relationship. It happen autonomously so idk how to raise relationship in this game.- There is no kids, they completely disappears. No more kids that can craft armors, guns and fixing things again. No more child labor lol- The gameplay felt slower inside the shelter. Even if you can fast forward there's nothing get faster. They can't run inside shelter- The 1st game have more surprise elemtn that if random survivor visiting you, you can either be murdered or when you reject them to join you they will tamper with oxygen or rain filter. This game only have random visit by survivor that need join or someone to pick up your side job missions items. Nothing else.- The extinguishing of flames is too long, they act so leisurely than panic. Resulting all of them goes to flame. This is why we should be able to run.- The hunting deer now need bullets, an expensive thing especially locked to tier 3. And so far no upgrade for weapon workbench to craft guns.- Finding good weapons also harder since you need requirement to used it and your stats is so much lower than many weapons you can find. Don't forget guns need bullets and if your char is low on Dex and never upgrade ranged skills, you basically wasting ammo.- Repairing equipped items need to use the equipment menu not automaticly registered by workbench. you need to unequip them but game never told you how until i start tinkering- After long play, I noticed audio started to laggy and downgraded in quality. Causing those 8 bit ear stabbing music.- The durability of items here is too weak. and crafting give chance of 3 tier of that items/weapons. But ofc you will mostly get it to 3 stars rarely.- The manual recycling vs recylcer is day and night in early game. Recycling in bench took much slower time even with fast forward it didnt help much. this is so punishing- The leveling system is too much favor in combat, while there's many things that can actually improve or diversify roles of each survivors. But if you upgrade it the same, they are identical.- The amount of clothing, hairs, hats, etc. of your customizing looks to your survivors is baffling me, even some of colors not shared somehow.- The base defense that actually work is landmines. While other's not so much. Buffing your survivor doing much better than using them.- Food now can be rot, but left no purpose at all than filling your pantry sadly.- No matter how you light the base, its still dark. And its hard to see if its dirty. Resulting you keep over and over cleaning the bunker.- the autonomy only cover sleep, water, eat, and bathroom things. No repairs, clean, harvest, watering plants, etc. If you manage 6+ survivors this will be becoming a chore.- I encounter one thing that infuriating. Some of the items in my base get burned bcs its durability destroyed. But I can never fix/repair them. They are wasting crafting spaces and there is no way how to get rid or repair them.- There is some crash in the game if you crafting items in workbench. dunno what cause it but its only happen when you crafting and in middle of crafting I chose other items to fill the empty queue task.If i can give mixed reaction, I will give it, but in the end its not a bad game. It could be more polished and have a bit better features such as running and more autonomy but the game seems to be getting better and better. So let's see it. So bcs I leaned to recommended, yeah why not.

_childDocuments_.review: Its unfortunate how buggy the game is. its entertaining but i feel the devs might have rushed it out the door and any attempt at fixing it made other areas worse. _childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is not an Upgrade to the 1st One, it is a downgrade.Mechanics still have Bugs, Dialogue stuck somewhere in School and the Combats are ridiculous.You train your Charakters to get +30% accuracy and have +20% demand on the weapon (a +50% chance) and miss 7 times in a row.You skill perks wich give u a 50% chance to use Medikit as a characters capability,... u wont see it coming, it missed 5 times in a row.While your characters can only Deal 1 or 2 attacks in a Round, Enemies can deal 4 to 6 times an attack in their round (every in their group)...It´s absolutely Unbalanced as hell, same with materials. u get tons of stuff that u dont need at this point of your technology status, but things that keeps u alive - like Gas for the Generator - it´s rare like diamonds.The Mind beyond this Game to grind is a nice idea, but just a disaster.Shelter 1 is definitive the better Choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good game for what it is.I have 100 hours in sheltered 1 and now 30 hours in this game so far. It's "This War of Mine" with a slight Rimworld feel in terms of NPC personality and needs. I have 1,000 hours in Rimworld. I will not have 1,000 hours in this game but I'm happy with it. 4 months after the official release there are still bugs being fixed but they have actually been being fixed (slowly). Once you learn what materials break down into what things make a bit more sense. There's not a ton to it but there is still a learning curve to be able to really enjoy it. For $20 it's worth it. If you played Sheltered 1 then everything will be familiar. There are some new things but it's a lot of the same with a big face lift. I have no complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game severely pales compared to the first. Survivors: The Ai of your party is just DUMB. They can't take directives hardly to save their own lives. Like when things burn ( and THAT is an issue I will bring up,) they will stop, from putting out the fire to EAT or sleep. When they get exhausted they will crash on the floor despite there being beds open. The Survivors will be afflicted with various issues at any given time which causes severe micro managing of your shelter.Fires- EVERYTHING catches fire TOO fast. Your whole place will burn to the ground and there is jack crap seemingly to be done about it. Your party sure as hell isn't going to put it out. Not to mention IF you are lucky enough to extinguish the fire, it is SECONDS before, you guessed it, its on fire AGAIN!Repairs- you will be repairing EVERYTHING! EVERYTHING breaks down entirely too fast, even when it is not in use. That makes absolutely NO SENSE. Half the things in there are not worth building because its just an added responsibility to tend to that offers little assistance to your shelters survival.I wanted to like this game, I liked what they did with the crafting and the building and design but its borderline unplayable to me. Please keep your money and just stick to the first game. Devs, please fix these issues. They are too numerous and constant. Until this game is polished and balanced better....I have NO intentions of further playing this game. Quite honestly I wished I could get my money back.Update: 5/1/23I re loaded the game because I heard there was some changes. Not good enough to matter.Same damn crap. everything burning down when it falls apart. How the hell does  a weight bench and medicine cabinet catch fire!? I want my money back so bad.....Screw this game. Save your money! This game is broken and faulty. Clearly a cash grab. I repeat: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. Even  using wemod cheats its unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has all the hallmarks of an incredible game, but there are 2 VERY SERIOUS issues with the game that make it both unnecessarily tedious and also quite frustrating at the same time.1. No Auto-Jobs - Every game like this NEEDS auto-job management!  You end up clicking everywhere on the screen to see which items need to be repaired.  When items degrade as quickly as they do in this game, having the ability to ascribe a dedicated cleaner and repairer IS A MUST!2. No Character list - You're going to keep searching all over the screen to find each of your peeps, a character list is a must in a game like this.Do those two things and this game has a very big chance of going from Mixed Reviews to Overwhelmingly Positive!

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game had it been released as a Early Access title. But it was not. I've had to restart my game several times as each time I've encountered game-breaking bugs.Thankfully many of the bugs I came across were squashed in the numerous patches that followed but the game should not be considered a release version. Even after all the patches to fix the various broken or unfinished elements or to balance the game, there are simple item descriptions that are missing and are similar to: (Item_desc_here) or (incenerator%efficiency#hrs) or (Tier3_item_desc) and on and on... Totally acceptable for an Early Access release but not a full release title.. Sorry. But I can't hold back on this.I'm glad the devs are responsive and open to suggestions but just slap an Early Access badge on it so others don't get this game thinking it's a full playable experience. It really feels like a test version and even though there's an experimental branch available they feel like the same experience.

_childDocuments_.review: More Buggy than Herbie, and not the lovable kindI liked the first one, so I gave a try to this, hoping for improvement. And there -are- many more things; but the problem is - there has not been any decent amount of testing and debugging. It's clear enough when bugs are just funny or strange (characters floating in mid air); it becomes quickly annoying (broken things that you cannot move, or dismantle); then you hit Bugger Prime, King of All Bugs, and you become stuck. You can reload, but when The Thing happens, you're stuck again. You shall not pass. And they're kind, and tell you "write us if you EVER have troubles", and they don't annoy you with answers or even set a pesky bot to tell you that they have received your complaint. All this for the price of a fully developed game; and they're churning out upgrades, pets and god knows what else.A waste of time, which is basically what a game is, but not a satisfying one.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty disappointed not gonna lie. My mood throughout this game was back and fourth. First off the character designs look poor and I was expecting much better with customization but somehow it's worse then the first one. I like how you can change the flag and stuff but that's it. Going into the game I liked how there was a lot more above the shelter to do. the big changes in graphics though didn't please or displease me that much maybe for new people playing they might enjoy it but I liked the older one a little more because this one seems more confusing. I absolute hated seeing that literally everywhere around me is occupied by other factions I feel closed in a little 20 pieces of land and like I can't go anywhere to do ANYTHING  on the map or my people will get jumped I don't know what possessed the devs to do this but it's a huge disappointment and not what I was expecting. _childDocuments_.review: Annoyance over difficulty.Nothing in this game posseses a challenge unless you want it to.Example: I met a military faction. I expected bulletproof vests and firearms, serious stuff.Except they are like anyone else. They have "zone difficulty" which means you control the difficulty of your encounters.I killed first two outposts of "military faction" with one knife.But this somewhat okay. I understand that faction system is super basic and just there to be.Example 2: You don't actually need materials to repair stuff. So no challenge in this. BUT this is where it becomes a mobile-click game. Cause every single thing except for toilet for some reason will be on the verge of a break once a day. ONCE A DAY, KARL! The amount of annoying senseless clicking you will need to make in this game is astonishing.I like difficult management in a survival game. But difficulty must come from planning and forced sacrifices. Here i just need to make another thousand clicks to fix things. And it takes time and effort from me that i wanted to put in actually interesting parts of this game.Summary: Game has a lot of upside compared to its first part for me. Weight system is better, new perks are nice (although auto lvl at the start of the game is also annoying). No hazmat suits or gas masks (which was again just for clicks in first game). This is a good change. Other stuff is there just to detract your attention from actually playing the good parts of the game. It's a "click/repair" game now.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, if you played the first Sheltered game you will be prepared for a majority of what this game offers. they introduced factions so instead of you and your family trying to survive (I personally really liked that aspect of the previous game) you are a faction trying to take over the area. You can have relationships with your faction members which is a welcome change of pace but its random. You cant engage with them. The pace of the game and all of the mechanics are the same. The game is now rendered in 3-D as apposed to pixels which actually made the previous game more charming. You would think this would add problems to the games operations but it actually runs 1:1 to the original as far as movement and how animations operate. It does look alright but I feel like if you going to go through the trouble of making everything more detailed at least make it look nicer. The art style (in my opinion) is gross. I simply dont like the way anyone looks. People are ugly. Combat is exactly the same as the previous game, just rendered in 3-D and at a top-down angle. The added skills and attacks add a bit of strategy to the game so you can overcome some pretty one-sided matches with status effects like blindness.Do I recommend? Yes. Its more Sheltered with more content. It enters the 3-D realm quite well and the price is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why anyone would bash a game for the fact that it is not its successor.It's a good sequel, don't let anyone stuck in the past tell you otherwise.Graphics are hella updated, the world map works way differently (and better) now, the gameplay fells a lot more polished, fighting has been turned up both in controlability and looks - i like it.I like the fact that some things you actually need to know aren't served on a silver platter and you yourself have to figure them out. That's how this game worked in the first episode as well, and now it's bad all of a sudden? Get your facts straight, reviewers.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this is a game I would like, it has all the things I like. Base building, resource gathering, upgrading etc. But it is sooooooo tedious, starting a mission and not realising you forgot to bring bullets or take a vehicle. Constantly having to water things, repair things etc If this had a better layout for missions with your group and a standard fitout or change it as required and name the groups party 1, 2 etc that would have been nice. Also little things like letting you know the name of the character when you are upskilling them. Also the ability to change your base rooms around, moving garages etc. And allowing upgrades to be done direct to the item rather than 'deconstruct' and build new. I like the nitty gritty of placing stuff in my bunker and upgrading things. I even got used to which plants to grow in the various seasons. But I think stuff like that should come with info like onions in spring etc. I dont like having to fiddle about second guessing. The same with mixing drugs with 1-5 options. As the toons get smarter they should just invent stuff rather than me having to guess from 100's of combinations. The little toons should be able to be fully automated. One set on maintenance or cleaning etc. There is an option to assign a room but I dont know what it. The toons just wondered off to dark corners for some reason. Also the heating / cooling, I think having it more automated so you dont have to constantly adjust it for the rooms. The toons also never will go to the closest item be it a toilet, fire extinguisher etc. They go in a weird way to put a fire out with the extinguisher in the room (set up in case there is a fire) they instead go up to a different level to get one. Some aspect I liked but others were a real tedium. These games need double and triple bunks as well and the ability to add decorations like pictures to raise morale. The exploring is fun to find things and work certain workable tiles. It gets repetitive in the battles over an over and meeting traders or encounters all the time. My advice if you like this war of mine of fallout shelter avoid Sheltered 2. Perhaps if they made a Sheltered 3 give that a go. I never played the first Sheltered. The little toons all look the same and it is annoying 'trying' to find them. The skill tree's are good. Overall it is just too tedious to be lots of fun, I wont be replaying it.

_childDocuments_.review: NEGATIVE REVIEW WITH A CAVEAT: I enjoyed the game for the most part, but it's pretty buggy and you can run into game-breaking problems still. Fortunately the devs and other players on the official Discord are super helpful in getting stuff fixed. However, if you don't want to deal with that, don't buy this game. I will also say, after dealing with all of the six factions I got a message essentially saying: "WARNING: You are entering the endgame, which is designed to increase in difficulty until you are destroyed" and I gotta say - that was such a tonal shift that I never lost interest in a game that I had previously been enjoying so quickly in my entire life.PROSFun crafting system. Feels like a weird little post apocalyptic ant farm. Some great IDEAS for management even if the execution is not always there.CONSThe execution is not always there. Lots of talents, and items are poorly designed or don't seem to do anything at all. Music is repetitive and generic, when it's there at all. Combat - though challenging at first - is ridiculously easy once you learn what you're doing. Seriously once I got a few basic pointers on how to play the game I never once felt like I was ever in danger. The game is buggy, and often downright unstable. I've had it just flat out lock up on me a few times, ending my game. I enjoyed it until the stupid "You lose no matter what actually lol" endgame, but lots of people have run into serious bugs and problems, myself being one of them. I was fortunate that the most serious one was ironed out on the discord. That being said, It's only twenty bucks, though. Maybe pick it up on sale, like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea, but terrible implementation. The outside world doesn't feel right and is clunky, the factions are just plain and insignificant, the trading system is useless in the late game and the resources needed for upgrades are way too much. The achievements are just designed to artificially extend the game time. The most annoying were the 50 bear kills.If the game mechanics and world gets some polish, this would be a relatively good game. Hopefully the developers will stick with the game and continue to improve it. The roadmap already lets some hope shine through.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is way too tough. When travelling around the map, interactions tend to have three options, Trade, Fight or Flee, and this can become a bit repetitive, and if you come across a rival faction, it is just fight or flee. A couple of lines of dialog and that's it.The whole crafting system is overly complicated, meaning a lot of back and forth, whether it is trying to see what ingredients you need to craft, then trying to figure out what you need to recycle, and so on, you will be left stuck pretty quick, forcing you to explore outside the shelter, which is fine, but this seems to happen way too quickly, not giving a new player chance to feel settled. There are way too many things to worry about in the Shelter, leaving a new player feeling overwhelmed.Bugs are being fixed pretty quick by Team 17, but this plays like an Alpha release and not the finished article.OverallThere is a good game in here, but it takes time to find it, and restarting once you figure certain things out will help you, but the game still struggles to really grab you. There needs to be a simplified mode, and a tutorial that really explains things.With all my complaints, I just feel that there is a great game here, but it is stuck in some kind of hole, that the developers don't have the time to get it out of.I will keep an eye out for updates, and maybe they can improve things moving forward.

_childDocuments_.review: There were some bugs in the beginning but I feel like many have been ironed out.  A lot of things that I thought were bugs later I figured out.  I finished the first game on Normal by taking over all the factions - alliances don't seem to be worth the trouble. I'm now playing my next game on Difficult.  Things I've learned:1) conserve water early; put all auto-actions on red; build out water tanks; upgrade water filter efficiency; upgrade toilet and shower2) fight encounters - you get experience and loot; or trade so you at least get some charisma experience3) I don't bother with any alliance jobs anymore; I'm taking over outposts4) though it seems like you can put a pantry over the bed, I've stopped doing that since in my last game, characters wouldn't eat5) I'm not sure the sink actually works to stop food poisoning; characters are supposed to wash their hands before going to the food but they often don't so I have to order them to do it6) temperature management is still wonky; now a medium sized fan works pretty well even for a large room7) I didn't even figure out how to hunt/forage in the first game; I'm not sure it's worth making the lab to craft your own medicines8) blade proficiency seems pretty good so I max out on that and then build electric blades in the armory9) in the first game, I was late to build the exercise equipment so now I've built them pretty early on and have my characters who stay in the shelter rotate through them10) I now have 6 characters on D47, and I rotate 3 out at a time on trips; I had 8 in the first game but I don't think it's necessary to have the extra 2 characters; 4 per trip is great for fights but if so far, I seem to be able to manage fights, often just using melee instead of skills; another benefit of a blade is that it only uses 3 stamina so I can sometimes get 2 attacks per turn11) there's some skill - I think close combat proficiency - that allows double attacks - that's awesome12) I don't think the emergency tourniquet skill work - it seems to always fail13) I didn't check on Faction Goals a lot but I realized it's helpful to check to see if you're close; I think crafting items = tier 1; crafting objects = tier 214) In game 2, I'm not bothering calling traders or new recruits; I took in recruits slowly, waited til the fresh recruit got leveled up and loyal before taking the next one15) In game 1, I finally got the truck and all its parts.  that was great just to drive around but by then, my team was overpowering all enemies so it was just a matter of mopping up16) indoor planter seems to more trouble than its worth; I just have a small greenhouse outside and plant spinach, peas, and broccoli; everything else doesn't seem to be worth it17)  I now have 3 windmills but their power is unstable / uneven - I don't know how to get the battery power bank; I think I got the blueprint for it but not sure when I can build itAnyway, that was just a random brain dump.  Hope it helps.  I love the game - 117 hours so far.
