_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is pretty addicting and has potential like the first installment. If you can avoid many of its game freezes and annoying bugs (which are slowly being patched) then it is enjoyable and fun although may not be too challenging depending on the type of gamer you are. - Music was meh. I thought the first game had better.- The map user interface is a bit clunky and tedious to move around in. Travel rations does not show up in inventory and sometimes just disappears leaving your party exhausted when in combat. Workable locations do not stand out and you have to remember where they were. If you leave items behind due to full inventory, you have no way to find out what you left behind in that location until you go there again.- Map is divided into regions controlled by a single outpost. Take over the outpost and take over the region. The only thing you get is traveling through the region you will not encounter faction members but only regular people, similar to the first game. - There are six factions and members usually use different gear from each other and are stronger than regular people. If you head straight to a faction HQ outpost and take it over, you get control of all that factions regions as well. Most leaders have a strong item they will drop after you beat them. After killing or allying with the factions, you will encounter androids which have more hit points but do very little damage. They take over your outposts/regions and then you take them back, over and over and over. - Some quests are useful, others just waste your time and give you no rewards for completing them. - The temperature system is new but is very inaccurate and frustrating keeping your shelter at a set temperature. It can be 16-20 degrees Celsius with your members are freezing or sweltering with heat exhaustion but your vegetables are growing perfectly fine. - Obtaining certain 3 star ingredients takes forever due to high item costs, randomness of loot drops/location searches, and no way to craft or recycle for them yourself.- Some skill abilities are useless and new members recruited get abilities assigned randomly based on their levels. Its best to recruit them early so you can level them up and pick your abilities you want. One of the best abilities is the auto repair one, huge quality of life ability. No more need to micromanage your shelter anymore. It runs by itself as long as you plant some seeds and traps. Just pray your members stat isn't capped too low it can't be unlocked. - Vehicles are hard to assemble due to parts required. I managed to put 2 bicycles and a motorcycle together. Only needed to farm for 1 more tire for the truck but decided to stop. Motorcycle takes 1 fuel can while truck takes 2 and I only had 10 fuel remaining and no way to get anymore without respawns. - Pretty much beat the game with 8 members but really it was 6 since last two had low stats and somehow leveled up stats so slow no matter how much they trained for that they were basically useless. These are some of the things I encountered and may be different for everyone. There were a lot more but I think those were already patched or fixed in the test version.Anyway if you liked the first game, you will like this one. Graphics are a huge improvement and a big selling point over the first for me. Gameplay is very similar so try the first one to see if you like it or not before deciding.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion this game has two major flaws: 1. lack of immersion 2. steep learning curve (not to mention minor flaws like bad ui and etc)1. lack of immersion is more like a subjective thing I guess, because some games are very immersive and some are not. But since sheltered 1 was very immersive, I think it's reasonable for me to expect it from sheltered 2.You don't start with your family, you have to start with two strangers. You can't customize two strangers enough to meet your imagination. In sheltered 1 it was way easier to imagine and relate to characters since there were no face details. Please either let me customize as I want or just give charming preset characters. Currently they are neither customizable nor charming. (technically you can customize but they all look same)2. steep learning curveEven from the start you already have 20~30 kinds of junks and should know the recipe to combine and upgrade facilities and what they decompose into. In sheltered 1, recycling was locked in the beginning and in the early game you only have to focus on the water, and then food etc. So there were also lots of kinds of stuff but you should only know what is needed to build water tank or upgrade water filter and things like that. There were few important stuff at the moment and you can't recycle at the beginning. There are also faction goals make things even more complicated.. Also ui and graphics doesn't really help the learning curve. Maybe the art is realistic but not really visible or distinguishable.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is at its core, a good game. The new graphics are appealing and freshen up the game more in comparison to the first Sheltered, whilst mechanics such as easier recycling, better trading and better salvaging give you more freedom as a player.Equally there are a few issues with it that I feel need addressing before it can be considered as a successor to Sheltered. Everything listed below was played on Normal difficulty:1. The stats of your characters degrade WAY too quickly, with food being a constant problem from the outset. EDIT: Still an issue.2. Tinned food degrades a little too fast, as the new temperature system (though a good idea) does not work properly. EDIT: ALL food degrades too fast and the temperature system is still an issue.3. Getting murdered by trigger happy psychopaths day 2, leaves the AI feeling too aggressive regardless of their ideology as a faction. EDIT: AI is still too aggressive.4. Some items could not be placed into my pantry/medicine cabinet after an expedition, even though I still had space. EDIT: This still happens, though can be ignored by pressing "Take all".Bugs:1. In my first run of the game I was unable to fix my generator at all, as the button would not appear after right clicking the generator. I had to wait for it to break down and burst into flames before being able to fix it, which causes heavy suffocation damage to my characters. Equally in my 2nd play through the button was there. EDIT: Fixed.2. On my 2nd play through, my weather vane and flood lights had a warning sign indicating a lack of power, even though I had more than enough fuel and had practically filled up my generator. I had to disable the flood lights and re-enable them to fix this issue, though that did not work for the weather vane, and upon reloading the issue remained along with the same warning sign on my shelter door. EDIT: Fixed.3. After a fight, I couldn't press the continue button to progress, thus having to shut the game down completely. EDIT: Fixed.TL;DR - Good game, but it still has some issues after all this time.EDIT (23/04/23): This game is significantly better now, though there are still issues that need to be addressed. Why are other factions super hostile and OP for no reason? Sheltered 1 had hostility, but a good chunk of the people you met were simply just trying to get by.Equally, though playable and somewhat enjoyable, it looks as if the game has been abandoned leaving it unpolished and unfinished. All in all this is quite tragic to see, and I for one feel scammed out of my money if this is the case.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Updated after playing 56 hours from day 1 release. (see header)With more serious artstyle comes more serious gameplay.Sheltered 2 builds upon and offers more refined progression compared to and in relation to its predecessor. In contrast to Sheltered when one can easily skip tiers of equipment and max upgrade everything very easily and very early, Sheltered 2 offers a bit of a challenge. This challenge comes with accomplishment of faction goals that tracks everything the faction members do and accomplish. Although this may sound like "a bit tedious" as some reviews may put it, these are hurdles and not outright roadblocks. The doing and accomplishment of these goals not only puts a clear path of progression but also allows the player to experience what most of the game has to offer and ties neatly with its core gameplay of collecting, managing and crafting. The game so far balances it out to provide enough tension and participation from the player so as not to make the experience "too repetitive and boring" like eventually late game Sheltered 1 becomes.If you are a fan of management-survival games and do not shy from a bit of a challenge, then this is for you. But if you like a much more simpler gameplay with the option to be able to easily finish the game in no time, coupled with its pixelated art-style then the 1st Sheltered should do the trick.---------------The Update-----------------Bugs, bugs and bugs.I must admit that I ignored the game running a bit slow when opening the world map (kinda stutters with the forced motion blur even when I had it turned off in the settings).. but that was actually just a tip of the iceberg. A couple of annoying (but not game-breaking bugs):>item tooltip that remains even after closing the inventory window.>no descriptions for higher tier food recipes (only placeholder text like item.descrip.)>cannot autopsy corpses on the medical bed despite having the perk for it.>people going directly to the pantry even when there is a sink with soap on the way there and getting food poisoned (i think it says that people automatically use it when their hygiene meter exceeds 50%)>people keep wandering to the edges of the shelter and into my cold storage (suffering the freezing moodlet debuff). They should not move to non-ideal temperature areas when idle.>cannot raise a stat already maxed out with "experimentation perk" despite having the medical bed.>(already patched-I think) planter thief spawning immediately to take your fully harvested crops when reloading a save.>faction "rescue mission" bugged and remains on faction screen even after completed>"trade request location" remains stubbornly on map with the wrong faction after said wrong faction wins the territory of the intended faction (basically can't trade with the intended faction cause the other faction conquered their area - such that the intended faction always says that his representatives haven't returned on the faction screen)>trading in excess of your weight capacity causes traded items to disappear forever>destroying an entire faction by simply trading at their HQ... (traded them a lot of meat)Overall these bugs accumulated, make the experience quite annoying and sometimes frustrating when everything else, especially the gameplay loop is very solid and shows promise. I'd still recommend the game as the developers are doing their best to iron things out with each latest patch at 2GBs. I just wished that they released this game a bit better and not make people play-test it when it did not release as an early-access game.P.S. the game does run a bit slow even when by system meets the requirements....

_childDocuments_.review: As someone with a lot of hours in the original Sheltered, this game is different. The mechanics are similar, but the playstyle is updated to include new features. Some of these reviews have a point; the UI is more complex, tasks take more effort and there are more things to worry about. However, this is a good thing simply because there is more to do. _childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2.I enjoy this game, and if you like base management games with a post apocalyptic setting I'd say give it a shot. HOWEVER there are some things in this game that have really aggravated me. ( Both bugs and game mechanics. ) And I could see them aggravating other people as well.Bug 1. Enemies getting stuck on each other at your shelter door during raids: One of the most frustrating bugs happens during raids on your shelter, and it happens ALL THE TIME after the first raid. The enemies trying to get into your base will get stuck on each other and cannot enter your base until they somehow get unstuck. Meaning that the raid will last much longer then it needs to, or if your really unlucky it’ll never end and you’ll be forced to reload a save. This happens every single time after the first raid. ( Because theres literally only one enemy on the first raid. ) And to my knowledge there’s no way to get them unstuck. It’s so annoying that I groan every time I get a notification that there’s a raid.Bug 2. Rations disappearing on expeditions: This only happened to me one time but it was very annoying. During one of my expeditions all of the rations that I gave my party just disappeared, and I didn’t notice until I got in a fight with a outpost attempting to capture it. Meaning that they had the weak status effect for the whole fight. ( I still managed to capture it for those wondering. ) I have no idea how that happened and I gave them up to 40 to 50 rations. It only happened to me one time but it was very annoying.Bug 3. Enemies fleeing combat makes the hud disappear: This one also only happened one time but it breaks the game when it happens. If an enemy leaves combat the hud disappears, meaning that you can’t do anything. You can’t even end your turn, meaning that your forced to reload a save. ( This has caused me to immediately target any enemy that attempts to flee out of fear that this bug will happen again. No one escapes my leaders wrath. ) Annoying game mechanic 1. The guns are very weak: Seriously, don’t bother with the handgun or shotgun. They are so weak that they will get your survivors killed in combat. You are better off focusing on melee, and getting the perk that allows your survivors to attack multiple times per attack. ( Although the rifle is actually ok. )Annoying game mechanic 2 Teleporting fire extinguisher?: If there are multiple fires in the shelter and if a survivor doesn’t get to the fire fast enough then the fire extinguisher will teleport back to where it was originally placed and the survivor will drop what they are doing, causing more of your stuff to catch fire and get destroyed. ( Also they are SO AGONIZINGLY SLOW when responding to a fire in the shelter and they get heat exhaustion when in the same room as a fire causing them to go EVEN SLOWER. ) Side notes: Combat is to easy once your survivors stats get high and they get lots of perks.During raids I’ve noticed that the enemies aren’t even armed, so there not really that much of a threat. ( If they can get each other unstuck outside of the door that is. )Speaking of raids it’s also annoying to have to go through the equipping phase each time a fight starts in your bunker because you can only fight four enemies at once.More guns then just “handgun, shotgun, rifle and crossbow” would be nice, but that’s just me. In conclusion I did enjoy my time with this game, and I’ll play it while talking to Friends so it makes a really good conversation game. But I’d say wait for a deep sale if you plan on purchasing this game. ( My shelter is still going strong as of this post. )Edit: A patch for the game was released shortly after I posted my review that made the guns more useful. They now deal more damage.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite downgrade from the first game. There's not much to say on this, it's largely the same gameplay and yet it's just worse in all regards except this time it's in 3D! I liked the choice of pet from the first game, that's gone, the "family versus the world" aspect is gone too, and then there's the annoying lack of certain structures from the first game that just don't appear in this one. (I want my freezer back) What you get here is some annoying hex-tile map with "factions" that I could not care less about and don't interact with me in any way besides getting in my way. A lot of the dark, frankly menacing, aspects of the pixel art are thoroughly absent in the sterile and uninspiring setting and everyone walks like they've had an accident in their pants. There's this dumb "leader" thing too, it's just more junk weighing this title down.What finally provoked me to make a comment was that there is absolutely no way to save anyone who falls unconscious after a fight in the shelter. Provoking a fight, or rather avoiding one, is seemingly at random since the game doesn't let you click a button and say, "Yes, I would like to engage in mortal combat with these intruders." I'm sure there's something resembling the rifle sentry gun of the first game, or at least I'd hope so, but this trainwreck won't let me upgrade the workshop to even see that so I suppose there's not much point in playing. There are greyed-out tiers, of course, but what they do and how to find that out is a mystery that I don't feel motivated to solve. I'm sure it has something to do with those idiotic factions.Oh, and for what you get, this game is extremely over-priced. Even the initial sale price was far too much and I really regret buying it, but that's my own fault.

_childDocuments_.review: Much as I'd like to recommend this game, I just can't. The general vibe is nice, looting feels reasonably rewarding, like it when a game lets you break things down and build things with the pieces. Well, once you figure out how vital to basic progress building a recycler is. Wish the upgraded version wasn't a random find.You need to endure a lot of grind in this game. Grind for reputation, go out again and again to find resources and hope for some good ones because even with the best crafter in the world you can't make excellent quality of raw resources. micromanage your people to excercise or read to grind up their skills, right click on every single machine in your base to have people go repair it, every couple of days. How I craved a, go repair stuff command, similar to the clean shelter command. But your people would be too dense for that.Your people won't stop what they're doing for their needs till its too late often times, but they will stop randomly. They'll stop wherever they are in the event of a raid, even  if that means they're slowly dying and you need to manually tell them to seek safe temperatures. They punctuate every task with an annoying random walk to, somewhere, so if they have multiple needs they'll make sure to delay attending to the others. And they'll gladly eat the depressing human meat on the shelf we keep for the animals before eating the non-human flesh alternatives as well as eating the non-perishable cans before perishable goods, just to be sure some rots. The animals are no better. I do tire of watching them starving to death, checking their bowls still have food and wondering if they'll die before they get there, or trying to train a dog, which only pauses once they start dying.Remember the hard to grind resources? Well the game doesn't give any warning if your people are going to use top quality goods for a low quality purpose, and I can't find a way to deny them. I assume they use lowest quality first, but I don't trust that.I only tried capturing an attacker once, decided to let them go, big mistake. They just stood there till they starved to death, not even deleting the holding cage got rid of their dead yet not dead body, they ended up eternally embedded in the wall, giving my people a -20 to their moods, or I presume the game thinking they were still here was behind the slavery debuff.Short version, the game has bugs, is laden with grind, allows minimal automation or control of which resources your people use and just generally keeps on going long after the novelty has worn off.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather than merely criticize the game, I'd like to point out my observations from the first several minutes. I will update this review as I spend more time playing. I wish Steam had more options that weren't "yes or no", because recommending a game is difficult and sometimes the answer is in-between.From the get-go, it's clear that the game has moved from the traditional pixel-art look to a more modern 3D look. Whether or not the game looks better (from an artistic standpoint) is debatable. The pixelated look gave it a unique appearance but offered less visual fidelity. The new look, while offering more fidelity, also looks rather generic if compared to other titles in the genre.In the previous game, the ultimate goal remained the same; survive. But with the addition of a family, I felt there was more emotional incentive and an obligation to protect them. While I like the faction system here and I appreciate the thought put into it, I simply do not feel an obligation to protect my faction when we can't even begin to develop these characters in a meaningful way. What is their backstory or connection to my leader? If this is an "RPG", why can't I roleplay as a lone survivor rather than deal with the baggage that comes with babysitting other survivors? Why are there no more than three types of bottoms by which we can customize each character- two of them being pants and one of them being shorts? If our characters cannot be defined by the backgrounds we set for them, we might try to define them by appearance.In life we are often led to believe that clothes & appearance can represent someone's personality, and if the means by which we can define them are limited- then our characters become no different from eachother. Each person seems generic, regardless of said backstory you have created for them. There is also the idea of wish fulfillment to consider. In games that offer various forms of customization, such as VRChat, the idea is that many people will enjoy making something based on what best represents their self-image. Much like some prefer to using face filters, because they feel  best represents their perceived image as a whole. There is a reason we see so many people creating these flawless, big-tiddied characters more than we see overweight characters. Because it doesn't represent what is closest to our reality and it sets us apart from others. Even if the truth is that we are all very depressed and fat on the inside. I'm not afraid to admit I just took a massive dukie after eating taco bell. Everytime I eat tacos I warn people to clear the room in 5 minutes. I want people to know how much I like tacos, but I don't want anyone to  just how much I like tacos. There is nothing wrong with this, it's just how we like to play our games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much suffering from a publisher-pushed early release, but the team behind it all is working so very hard to fix it.Some really big bugs for me are the ones that can suddenly and irreverisbly delete resources in a game where managing said resources is the main purpose. Easiest trap is that you can que up more than 10 tasks on your survivors quite easily - but only 10 tasks will actually be saved, 11+ will simply be taken from storage and never be seen again.It's the sort of thing I'd be more open to forgive if there were an 'Early Access' flag hanging under this game, but I really find it hard to accept 'Full releases' that struggle with beta-bug-issues. I believe it will be fixed over time as I think Unicube is a solid team, but pressured by Team17 into a rushed release that will hurt the game.In general, the game thus far feels "easier" and a LOT slower than it's predecessor. The content-exploration makes it feel like I'm barely getting started still. When I say easier, it may be because of bugs since factions do not seem to mind that I take their territory, they just defend the next place harder. Training your survivors to get their stats up feels a bit to easy right now, my crew barely 2 weeks in having increased from mostly 2-3's to around 10's. Not a serious issue outside of that the pacing of the game feels a LOT slower. Finding higher-quality materials and climbing into T3 is where I'm at right now and it is feeling like an RNG grind which bothers me a bit as well.I dare say that once bugs that can delete items from storage is dealt with, I'll trust the devs to provide a great game and give it a thumbs up. At the moment, the game just has to many things to keep in mind so it's exhausting to play knowing that certain clicks can unintentionally erase much needed items rather than block the player from such acts.These are on the to-do list so I've changed my case to a thumbs up and just hope the devs won't give up their health crunch-timing to much trying to deliver patches like a machine gun.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent successor to Sheltered. The updated graphics and change in focus from a family to a faction of wasteland survivors makes the game considerably less charming and unique but maybe ultimately a better "game." What I mean by that is that there are game-play ideas and features here I would have really liked to have in Sheltered -- faction relationships and perks,  RPG style character progression, a reworked overland map with better exploration and way better resource management (like you get a junk pile on the surface to keep things you can't store inside). But unfortunately there is a lot missing from the original. For one thing the UI and overall style was totally reworked and I think it's a net loss. While the move to 3D was a positive change in theory the implementation leaves a lot to be desired. The only utility you get out of the new 3D is an expanded surface area above your base, so you have more room to build crops and traps. That part is cool. What you lose is a lot of the flavor and art that the original game had. The 3D assets are fine but they don't really have much style or character. This is perhaps most noticeable in the UI, sheltered 1 had a more material and artistic UI that made use of actual books and clipboards. The Sheltered 2 UI is functional and generic, no personality, it's "fine." On top of all that there is also the problem that the game feels unfinished. I'm somewhat surprised that this game isn't "early access" and there are issues I've encountered that I expect the game to be improved and fixed by either patches or mods. for example I have burned out items in my bunker and I don't seem to be able to do anything about them, that has to be a bug, i'm sure it will get fixed. development continued on Sheltered for a long time after it was released so I expect at least a couple of patches going forward. All this is not to say it's not good. It is, I've played Sheltered 1 on PC and Android and like it and there is a lot in Sheltered 2 that makes it a better survival game. So far I've played it quite a bit and will likely continue to play it, it's fine and if you liked the Sheltered survival experience I think it's worth checking out.

Items disappearing from the recycler, and thanks for patching the seeds as last 7 harvests yielded zero seeds back. _childDocuments_.review: I have played nearly 20 hours (multiple tries) and I am still not enjoying this game as much as the first one.It's a difficult game and the many bugs make it harder (rain never comes, glitches, UI disappearing in combat e.tc). The weather balancing is really bad (8 sunny days, 1 sandstorm, 1 rain for 2 minutes).I think the Devs must keep improving the game since its the only (other then the first one) decent bunker/survival game out there. It has it's moments and many things are better than before but for me the biggest problem with most survival games is when developers make the mechanics so complex and so time consuming that everything becomes a grind and I loose interest. This game suffers from that and the progression feels really slow and boring after awhile.The first game became a classic mostly because of the gameplay. It had a "complex simplicity", unfortunately I don't see it happening with this one. All developers should know that they can never sacrifice gameplay for graphics. Graphics are good but the gameplay is what makes games great.Some bugs have been fixed, the price is good and it's not a bad game but It needs a lot of work to become something special. I recommend it but only because I like to support small developers and I think these guys are solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't you hate it when you're not strong enough to use a knife?This other day while I was in my bunker, I wanted to make a peanut butter sandwich but my strength was only a 3 and I needed a 4 to use the butter knife.Or I wanted to go play baseball with my nephew but my dexterity was only a 5 and I needed a 7 to hold a baseball bat! I just couldn't figure out how to pick up a bat!To break the character now, this game is nice but Sheltered 1 is better than Sheltered 2. This game feels like a completely different developer took the IP. First off my biggest problem is the random people who come to your base asking to join. 99/100 of them are men, I had only 1 woman ask to come join my base. I should've named my fraction the Sausage Bois! Or maybe all the women joined the Black Roses which is an all woman society. I wonder how well that group is gonna work out once the women become 40 and have no young people around. Please note how short life expectancies are when there's no modern medicine.The other problem that really bugged me was the high skill requirement for weapons. Imagine not being able to use an electric knife because your strength is a 3 and you need a 4. Most people who asked to come join my group had a lot of skills that were level 1. And although they do upgrade it is such a gamebreaking slog to see someone unwilling to pick up a baseball bat to fight with because their skills aren't high enough. This is like how you can't wear a certain T-shirt in Cyberpunk because it's level 22 and you're level 12. Don't you hate when you can't wear Forever 21 dresses because their level is higher than yours?What bothered me the most is the tier item system. To get tier 2, 3, 4 you have to complete certain quests. Quests such as "Become friends with the AFK Group" to get the reward of tier 4 items. In my playthrough I was actually able to build tier 3 items before tier 2 items because I had accidentally completed that quest requirement first. I don't even know what the quest was but it was upgrading one of the items on the surface. Just completely happenstance and I got the tier 3 before tier 2 items. I would rather they make the laboratory a research station so you can invent new items to use in game.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I get it. It doesn't have the cute "survival family" vibe of the original, not the graphical style that was one of the things that made it so unique. Going from a cosy little survival simulator to a full blow "let's take over the known world" is a big step that may be a little difficult to process for some of the fans of the original game. But it's really not that bad a game.I have encountered a few non-gamebreaking bugs, but other than that it's pretty stable and everything that needs to work, works well. Expanding and crafting and exploring is pretty fun most of the time and. Almost all of the mechanics of the original game have been preserved too.Is it a great game? No, it's not. The developers have made some serious shortcuts that keep the game firmly in 7-ish territory. The factions are kind of fun, but grabbing territory from them is utterly pointless - outposts don't seem to serve any purpose: other than to keep them out of the hands of others, it achieves nothing. The game would have been better off if every faction had one base, and attacking it would destroy the faction and leave the shelter in ruins. And the amount of clicking you need to do when crafting (whether it is food or anything else) is ridiculous. And if you don't, you are end up prematurely using those 3 star resources on something way too simple. It's tedious to the point of frustration at times.Combat is a bit more extensive than the original game, which is ok, but... the way that battles are presented, the scope of the battles feels much bigger than it is. It's simplistic and you can name one skill "confuse opponent" and the other "crush windpipe" but if the outcome is that the target is dazed, it's the same skill. And most of the rest of the skills are superfluous.But these things do not take away from the fun of building a thriving shelter. If this is your genre, you'll easily have a few full days of fun, and there's enough there for a replay or two.This game is being judged too harshly.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, so I have played the first one, and have suck a huge amount of hours into this one.  It is a pretty decent game and worthy of the roughly $30 AUD price tag.The game was very buggy at first I must admit.  That has changed and been polished somewhat since.There are still bugs and glitches though.  The first bug I encountered was someone sitting and eating but were unable to get up and as a result ended up dying a slow death causing everyone who went past for a meal to feel sad.  This was a horrible bug that sucked the fun out of my first play through, and this happened some 40 hours into the game!  So yeah it was a simple but bad one.The next bug I encountered was I recruited a prisoner but she was still stuck in the prison! I destroyed the prison and she was stuck behind the walls.  Thankfully this one somehow resolved itself when the character was hungry and thirsty enough.  In the same play through, I was performing an autopsy on a corpse when I saved and exited, came back and I was able to infinite harvest organs.  Talk about gruesome!  The result was I had to remove the medical bed then harvest the corpse to fix this bug which caused the shelter to have a negative buff again.So yes, the game is still buggy.  The new pests addition can see rats get out of hand really quickly if you don't have a cat.It is stressful, and to be honest, it is a great game at creating stressful situations due to its own inherent and quirky bugs.The rats go from 0 to 100 in next to no time. The dog never gets any stamina to do anything.But you know what? It is still a fun game.  So here is the good bad and the ugly of it.Good:It is actually a lot of fun, and can take a while to master or indeed not fail.It doesn't have too steep a learning curve but a steep mastering curve.Bad:Things break down so quickly all the time, constantly fixing stuff daily!So much micro management even with certain perks that help you not to need itDid I already mention bugs?  Graphics a big improvement on the last game, but whilst the last one was pixel graphics with a bit of charm to it, the people in this game all look, well really ugly.  There is not much of a clothing range and all the preset faces look like they have been beaten with the ugly stick, twice!Ugly:So many bugs and glitches.Thankfully since 1.0 I have not had a game crashing glitch or bug, but there used to be lots!I don't understand why, but for something that looks kinda basic, this game actually sucks up a lot of system resourcesI am running a MSI Titan Pro 2 with a 1080 and i7 16GB of ram and yet sometimes the game still manages to heat up my entire room because everything is getting hot from the demands on the system, and that is quite a feat considering it is only 6oC and the room is now 12oC since running the game for a few hours.All in all this is a good game.  Can be a hard one due to the randomness of some of the game.  Go and get it and play!

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is a post-apocalyptic survival game similar in genre to Fallout Shelter, or This War of Mine. The idea is, a small group of survivors and a pet find an abandoned underground cellar and use it to survive for as long as possible in a post apocalyptic world dominated by gangs. The fun and reward in this game comes in you micromanaging a group of people's daily needs while transforming their small prepper-basement into a multi-level underground base with modern amenities and great furnishing over time.So the game is about real time base building, turn-based combat and selective looting. It's pretty much a copy of Sheltered 1, except the 8-bit pixel style graphics have been replaced with 3D realism. The con side of this, is the game looks rather drab in its shades of red and brown compared to the more colorful & charming artstyle of Sheltered 1, and is also way more GPU demanding than its predecessor. Yet the graphics arent the focus of this game, but a TON of micromanagement (clicking around to repair things, set up expeditions, answer the radio and assign tasks to your survivors within the shelter), so you won’t be too focused on the graphics anyway. In fact I recommend to pause often.Each survivor has a set of meters that keep filling up and need to be reduced: thirst, hunger, sleepiness, dirtiness, and the need to poo, initially into buckets that need to be washed out with plenty of water. Run out of water to flush the buckets out, and your survivors will pinch one out on the floor in desperation, raising their dirtiness bar immediately to max level. If a survivor then proceeds to go and eat while filthy, they will contract food poisoning and will find themselves retching all over the floor. So even if you have enough food, if you run out of water, your survivors will be reduced to a poo and puke stained mess within days, which is hilarious and sad at the same time.This brings us to the most important resource in this game: water. Which is automatically collected every time it rains outside, into your water barrels via the water filter that sits on the surface of your shelter (and degrades over time and one of your survivors has to go outside and fix it every now and then, just like the oxygen filter - unlike Sheltered 1, without having to don hazmat suits every single time they are outside). However, if the rain is black rain, it first has to go through the water purifier you also start the game with, something that requires energy to run (so keep it off unless it starts filling up during black rain). What appliances use how much energy is checked at the fuse box, and if you have more power draw than power generation, things start malfunctioning. And the more power draw, the faster you'll run out of fuel. In Sheltered 2 there is also the weather vane, which tells you the forecast for the next day (or more, if you upgrade it).So water is needed to slake the thirst of your survivors, to grow crops, to take a shower and flush the toilet, the latter two consuming less and less water depending on the quality of the shower or toilet you have built. MRE rations instead of water are now needed for the 2nd most important aspect of this game: sending your survivors out on scavenging missions. People say devs abandoned the game, but only a few bugs in Sheltered 2 remain, like your dog not regenerating AP after its attack, or that radioing for traders to come to your shelter never works, but every so often one stops by anyway. So scavenging is the only way to accumulate resources & expand your shelter over time. Resources are stored either in boxes you need to build inside the shelter that take up room, or they get dumped on the junk pile outside from where items will occasionally be stolen by passers by.Each scavenging party can consist of up to 4 survivors, and the dog if you have one. You have to create an exploration route (a loop that starts and ends at your base and formed by waypoint markers) for them to travel on, and they will visit any location that is on this loop. The bigger (further) the loop, the longer it takes.Before leaving, you need to equip your party. Each has 1 weapon slot, 1 rucksack slot (to increase carry weight) and initially 2 equipment slots for body armor, camo, whistles to attract stray animals, or binoculars to increase the visible tiles when exploring the world map.The sheer number of items that you encounter in the game world can quickly overwhelm new players. As you run out of inventory space while exploring, you need to start prioritizing which loot you bring back to the base and which things you leave behind. Thankfully, the devs have provided a “you have x of these back in your base” reference whenever you hover your mouse over a piece of loot you find at a location, so you have an easier time bringing back the stuff you desperately need, and leave the rest, usually heavier stuff, behind. Back in your shelter, you break down the items you brought back for their useful individual components, initially by hand, later by recycler.The third most important aspect in this game is fuel. Which powers your generator, which in turn powers your base by not just keeping the lights on, but also the oxygen filter working. If you run out of fuel, O2 levels drop and it’s game over far sooner than if you run out of water. Thankfully, fuel isn’t too rare, because the fuel canisters you find in most locations (rather than just at gas stations like in Sheltered 1), last a lot longer than the water you find this way, and you can build an incinerator pretty early on as an alternate source of fuel where you can chuck anything you don’t need to keep the power going, but preferably coal and fertilizer. Unlike Sheltered 1, the generator cant be upgraded for better fuel efficiency.This brings us to the long term goals of this game – fully exploring the world map, assembling vehicles and meeting all other factions and interacting with them (as i explain further below) but unlike Sheltered 1, Sheltered 2 has an even steeper initial learning curve that may make people ragequit. For instance, summer dries up all rain and your entire ecosystem breaks down without water which can after this point only be traded in the form of singular bottles from other factions (who offer it - not all of them do). Good luck washing yourself and flushing your business with the few bottles you bring back from a grueling 2 day march. And if you dont and just use it for drinking, good luck dealing with food poisoning every time you eat. Since crops wont grow without water, hunting rabbits and later deer become your only food source during summer. As a result, deaths and cannibalism can haunt your base, and you only lose the game if your main character (the base leader you began the game with) dies.But since new recruits keep knocking at your shelter door every so often, any survivor you lose can be replaced without worrying too much about stat loss as the newcomers also level up over time. Loot at visited locations respawns (but slowly, so dont revisit the same place too soon), and while enemies get stronger over time, your survivors also earn exp from combat or trading & can even train in the base using punching bags or reading books to increase their stats (and unlock perks).What is frustrating though, is the absolute lack of a combat tutorial. You learn over time though.Sheltered 2 also tries to offer more story than Sheltered 1 by introducing faction mechanics (you can expand your control zone by storming outposts, OR - and this is more rewarding - do various quests for every faction for an eventual alliance with them, while in the 1st game you just encountered them as variously clothed enemies). And then there is the endgame, an extra bit of sci-fi thrown in. Nevertheless, the DLC of Sheltered 1 was more interesting.So overall, I recommend Sheltered 1 over 2, but Sheltered 2 is addictive in its own way and took me 80 hours to finish

_childDocuments_.review: Alright guys, calm down. I have ~16 hours on the original Sheltered. I ALREADY have ~13 for Sheltered 2. The graphics are SO. MUCH. BETTER. The Tutorial helped me learn SO MUCH for the beginning. The character customization, and details to mental health(SCHIZOPHRENIA?!!), as well as detail to physical ailments, is so fun!! I mean, obviously Schizophrenia isn't fun. You know what I mean.ANYWAY. Yeah, the game has glitches. I had a guy get stuck after digging a grave. It was kind of fun. I just pretended he was a scarecrow. Developers should probably look into this. It seems that there is a possibility for corpses that are placed above ground to remove the body bags and still be seen by the game as "unconscious". You are able to select the corpse in excavations. I was REALLY HOPING to see Christopher Williamson zombie walk with the crew, but alas, the game just went through an endless cycle of waiting for him to walk. Lastly, the bug that bugged me the most was the eating function. It worked sometimes, giving the command to the character, but if you were to have them eat again, it would show the command and it would then IMMEDIATELY disappear. I found a workaround where if you save the game and load it again, you can then resubmit the eat command. However, as much fun as that is to do, I think there can be an easier way. ;)But yes. I had to step in. The hate is not warranted! After the loading screen, the game felt smooth! The tutorial (WHICH I RECOMMEND) helped me TREMENDOUSLY, and was very in depth. Yes, there are things the developers need to fix, but it doesn't ruin the whole game. They will fix it.This game feels like an amalgamation of Fallout Shelter and This War of Mine. I love it. Please keep fixing the bugs! Otherwise, I am in love with this game so far!

_childDocuments_.review: So the game needs more work and balancing, but I'm giving a positive review because I do think a lot of the negative ones here are a bit unfair and so far the developer seems keen to develop the game a bit further and is reactive to feedback. The Pros: Many systems are improved upon the original. Graphics, mechanics, some things like surface radiation having reduced after 20 years so you don't need hazmat suits always are a nice lore friendly touch. Also so far its looks like they've dropped the racist elements from the original.What the game needs: -Easier resources near your base or cheaper travel, because its a real dice roll if you get what you need to advance early on, and finding you're immediately surrounded by faction territory and need to tangle with them is a bit daunting. -More options when meeting folk, at least factions. Only being able to Fight, Trade or Flee is a bit shallow. Given characters have a charm skill, this would be used for some convo options to increase faction rep a little perhaps. -A subdue option. At least if you've got blunt weapons like the baseball bat. Forcing me to murder my way across the wasteland, trashing the mental stability of my characters for no real reason is annoying. Let us beat up, rob and then bail on people who attack us like in the original.-Love the automation of characters meeting their needs. Perhaps other tasks like repairs and that could be automated as well as eventually they do become a chore to keep clicking. Maybe a higher tier item you could build would be a work roster of some kind, assigning people to certain jobs throughout the day?Once again, its got promise. I hope they continue to improve it because it should outstrip the original given a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is an upgraded version of the original indie game. There's some new ideas, especially the factions and overland exploration that's been fleshed out compared to the original. You now move your team around a better graphical map. The game is fun overall if you like clicking.Speaking on clicking, You will be clicking. A lot of clicking. Items decay in your Shelter rapidly and you'll find you're spending an inordinate amount of time clicking on everything to repair.Bugs - The game was buggy at launch but at least the developers are aware and are fixing it daily. There are some critical bugs like losing all your rations, items going missing which in essence, will wipe out your Shelter. If you're ok with this sort of launch problems, Reload and start again.UI Issues - The game has some strange UI decisions making parts of the game not intuitive for what seems like mundane tasks. In a game of what essentially is about tasking, finding out how to do simple tasks from the discussion board is rather counter-intuitive.Combat is simple - very simple. Once you hit a milestone in stats, equipment and skills, You're Arya Stark wiping out factions solo. (There's a hint of what the perfect setup is)Factions - At the moment, it needs a lot of balancing. Either it's buggy or outright not working as intended but it's far easier to fight every body then to foster a relationship. What that pay off is we still don't know but it seems that you get nice thing being nice to people ;) - Very nice things. Fallout things.Still can't find that Medical bed blueprint...I hope it didn't disappear from my inventory due to a bug.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this is worlds better than the first game.  Exploration got much better and is quite enjoyable.  The bunker management feels similar however, just some more features and items for your survivors to mess around, with a good variety too.  Very dissapointed that the placement system is the same.. it lacks depth. A table and chair should be able to fit under the small pantry.. and why can I not put the weights under the cot? It fits... and the punching bag has a massive placement box that makes no sense.  After awhile it does feel like a chore issuing orders when you have 5+ people at home.  The AI however is terrible to the point where i wanted to quit.  They linger too much and will constantly just stand there in my freezer after eating and start to die... and on top of that they will somehow eat raw food when i have none and a full pantry of cooked food...  I get youre supposed to manage it all with help from AI assigning themselves tasks but sometimes you just hope the AI will be efficient while you focus on other things... they arent.  TURN OFF AUTOMATION FOR YOUR SURVIVORS!!!!(This seems to fix their stupidity) The bunker raids feel poorly done.  Picture fallout shelters bunker raids.. its exactly like that but slightly worse.  It was dramatic at first but the moment the raiders break in they just casually walk by my survivors i tried to place at the door(they kept walking away..turn off automation) and started looting... my survivor finally started the combat mode after they almost escaped... the combat is pretty good, its turn based so its pretty straight forward.  Was very disappointed after the fight because it gave no loot screen or an option to loot the bodies...Theres definitely alot of replay value here as its a randomised map every new game.  It just gets hectic when your bunker gets bigger is all and with terrible AI, it can be frustrating.  Hopefully the AI gets updated/acts smarter but until then turning automation off creates a better experience... and hopfully a reworked new bunker raid system but overall a fun game and looking forward to the improvement and development of the game.  In its current state its recommended, especially for $20, l i know ill get my monies worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 1 fan here, along with anything survival postapo-type games. I got SH2 on discount, because just like everyone else, I was worried about the reviews and the general state of the game.However today I come to tell you, the game is just fine. The first 11h of the gameplay definitely made me question what are all those bad reviews about (though maybe I didn't stumble on any jarring issue quite yet).What I did stumble on, is this:People who play in this type of games understand more than others that some games are just JANK - buggy, overambitious, but fun. If you ever played in games like Stalker or Kenshi, then you know what I'm talking about.And just like in case of Kenshi, Sheltered 2 visibly accumulates errors over long hours of gameplay, which then turn into bugs. And , all you gotta do is just quit the game and boot it up again as a break from your 6h marathon of playing the game.If you can do that, then great! If you can't, then I don't know what to tell you, other than stick to triple-A studios, instead of expecting the same quality from an indie dev studio that just upgraded this series from 2D pixels to quite beautiful 3D systems.Final note: For the current -50% discount it's a bargain. Though in all fairness it doesn't live up to its full price quite yet. I heard that devs are working on the game still so I'm having high hopes for it, but I'm also bracing for any possible issues that I may encounter later in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard Sheltered 2 no longer receive update, so i decide to try Sheltered 2 and find out whether it's fun despite issue mentioned by many reviewers. After playing a bit, i agree some of those issue definitely exist and find Sheltered 2 isn't fun. For comparison, Sheltered 1 is fun for me where I've wasted ~140h on Steam and few hours on Android. Anyway, here's my  thought and comparison between 2 games.* Better tutorial, although i expect more for game with $20 base price.* Somewhat better UI, but worse UX experience.* Some condition to unlock next tier of crafting object is ridiculous.* You can recycle item from beginning of the game.* Expedition now require food/ration.* From few expeditions, NPC always talk about fiction.* I like the idea of leader who have unique trait and usage.* Skill tree is interesting, but after reading some skill i think only some of them are useful or worth to obtain.* You can let the game automate certain basic task (eat, sleep, etc.) for certain character when the bar reach 50% or 75%.* Item with higher stars only lead to higher price. For example, canned from from 1-3 stars have exactly same integrity and hunger reduction value.* Better combat mechanics. Although i don't like the camera change back-and-forth whenever a character perform action.* Graphic/visual-wise, i prefer Sheltered 1 over Sheltered 2 where i feel Sheltered 2 has generic 3D style.* Only OKish music/sound effect considering $20 base price.* I experience few bugs such as character stuck or my command to stop existing task occasionally got ignored by the game.* No problem running this game on Linux.Obviously i can't recommend this game and suggest you to check Sheltered 1 or This War of Mine instead. If only Unicube improve 2D style (rather than switch to 3D) and not adding too much new mechanics, Sheltered 2 could be better or more enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is set 20 years after an apocalyptic event happened on Earth, wiping out most of the human race, what remains are splintered factions, all vying for their own land and resources.At first look the game will remind you of Fallout Shelter, and although there are similarities, Sheltered 2 is quite different and much more of a hardcore survival game.Your job is to run your shelter, grow your faction, all the while managing your resources, crafting items, exploring outside of your shelter, and generally trying to keep everyone alive.Now do not be mistaken, this is not an easy game, even on the easiest setting, the game is tough, it is probably a bit too tough, and the tutorial is about as much help as a Donor Kebab in a Vegan festival. With that said, each time you play, you do learn, and there is a lot to be said for just starting the game again, using what you have learnt, to help you make better decisions.Most of the gameplay will take place in your shelter, you need to keep an eye on your group, make sure everyone is happy and healthy, you will need to craft things like a toilet, a shower, beds, as well as expand downwards to make room for more things.When you are not in your shelter, you will need to keep an eye above land, set traps to catch rabbits, keep things powered, clean and working, plant seeds to grow food and so on. And when you are ready you will need to leave the area altogether and explore. You already control a small region, which is safe to explore on its own, gather more resources as well as grow the levels of experience of your group. But eventually you will want to explore outside of your region, and that is when you will come across other factions.The faction's system, is the main pull of this game, you will need to trade with other groups, forge relationships, and sometimes fight them, everything is a balancing act, choose who to fight and who to trade with and who to run away from. You will even complete quests, which become a big part of the game if you want your shelter to grow.The fights are all turn based, you can choose where to hit an opponent, what weapon or skill to use, and if you choose correctly, you will kill them, and then you can take everything they have.As you play, your characters levels will grow, you will get new skills and so on.Further into the game you will even find vehicles which you can fix up, to help you explore faster and easier.The GoodThis is a challenging survival game that fans of the genre should enjoy, the graphics are decent, and once you get the general idea of how to play, everything is pretty straight forward.The BadThe game is way too tough. When travelling around the map, interactions tend to have three options, Trade, Fight or Flee, and this can become a bit repetitive, and if you come across a rival faction, it is just fight or flee. A couple of lines of dialog and that's it.The whole crafting system is overly complicated, meaning a lot of back and forth, whether it is trying to see what ingredients you need to craft, then trying to figure out what you need to recycle, and so on, you will be left stuck pretty quick, forcing you to explore outside the shelter, which is fine, but this seems to happen way too quickly, not giving a new player chance to feel settled. There are way too many things to worry about in the Shelter, leaving a new player feeling overwhelmed.Bugs are being fixed pretty quick by Team 17, but this plays like an Alpha release and not the finished article.OverallThere is a good game in here, but it takes time to find it, and restarting once you figure certain things out will help you, but the game still struggles to really grab you. There needs to be a simplified mode, and a tutorial that really explains things. With all my complaints, I just feel that there is a great game here, but it is stuck in some kind of hole, that the developers don't have the time to get it out of.I will keep an eye out for updates, and maybe they can improve things moving forward.As the game stands right now, I score it 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Being a long term fan of the original Sheltered game, I was shocked to seeing it was getting a sequal, considering the game was stopped updating and finished many years ago, so as soon as Sheltered 2 was announced, I had to buy it being a fan myself. When I first started the game, I was very excited, but alot of things were disappointing (Which will probably be improved in the future) which is why I give this a 7/10, which I explain belowGameplay for Sheltered 2 is very transferable from the original game, just right clicking everything and selecting what you want to do. The addition of crafting really enchances the game, no more just meat and canned food, which really helped expand in the game itself. You are able to craft more things, not just what you could in the old game; medicine, weapons, guns, and items that you may use to build other items in your shelter itself. Recycling has been added as default, which is great. Going outside of the shelter does not grant you radiation poisoning, except in specific conditions, such as dust storms or acid or black rain. Going out and scavaging for supplies is pretty much the same than the original Sheltered game, only this time you do not need water to go out. You get supplies, then go to the next building. Meeting survivors is the same, only that your skills pay a part and may give you better results if your skill is higher Combat in Sheltered 2 has been totally revamped, having a whole new skill tree, stamina, and more. No more melee, subdue, or such, you now can choose which body part you want to hit, which has different effects, depending on what you do. As you level up your skills, you can get different skills, which do different things, depending on the skill itself.The introduction of the skill tree totally makes each character different from each other, meaning you have to decide which skills they should have, all have their own perks and benefits. Characters sometimes don't have max to level 20, meaning that you have to be careful which perks you spend on.There are 6 factions, all which have their own backstory, style, and objectives. They fight each other through out the game (But in my experience, it feels as its 5 of the factions against the 1, as they all wanted me to capture a specific faction member.) They have their own territory, and which if you enter, you are firstly introduced to the faction, and then after that, you'll have the choice to flee or fight. Throughout the game, you can do tasks for each faction, supply runs, freeing prisoners and capturing prisoners are a few tasks that gain loyalty points and to gain trust for that faction. Killing faction members deals negative points, meaning that they will hate you more. Depending on your playstyle, you can form an alliance with a faction, or kill the faction entirely in order to take over their entire land. Raids are very similar to how they were in the original game, except there are more traps for you to learn as you play the game. When a raid is activated, you have time to prepare, whether you want to fight or hide. This time, when you get close to an attacker, the person they touch is the one who will be in the fight, then you can choose 3 other people to fight. There are alot of bugs within the game, some of which ruin some of the things in the game itself. There was this bug where you could trade with a faction leader, and it would instantly wipe out the faction itself, another where corpses could not be interacted with, and some combat screen bugs. As playing the game, the developers are fixing these bugs, which is good. I really enjoy Sheltered 2, playing for 110 hours and in day 300 in my shelter itself is very rewarding, however, these bugs need to be fixed so that I can play the game I wanted to play. I imagine soon they'll add more content in the game to make it more fun, just like that they did with the original Sheltered game.

_childDocuments_.review: While no longer a pixel art game like the first one, this game feels very much the same in the way of the game mechanics. I do miss the optional pets though. The family unit has been replaced by a faction unit. All the inhabitants of the bunker are not related to each other anymore, but you still care for each of them in the same way as before. No more children, only adults.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love Sheltered. I've played it within the last month. They've done a great job building out the world in Sheltered 2. It almost feels more like a remake than a sequel. It's not ready though. There are still some balancing issues. Intruders will come into your shelter and one shot you. You're now limited to just two levels, which isn't enough room to built everything you need. There's no character wheel, so to select a character, you have to click on them in the shelter. If they're moving, it's twice the fun. It costs the same amount of resources to repair and item as it does to create it whole cloth. I've somehow unlocked Tier 4 of my workbench without unlocking Tier 3. I owned several outposts and regions at the start of the game. Not sure how it happened, not complaining about it either, just worth mentioning. My leader character is suffering physical ailments that  lower some of his stats, but not the cap, so I just have him raising those stats again. I didn't write down these issues, this is just what I can think of off the top of my head. Despite this, I'm addicted. The first game I started (before later patches) was a punishing experience. It took an in-game week of no rain, for me to realize there was a problem. On the day the weather vane told me it was gonna rain, it didn't. I was like, "Oh, this is a bug." It's definitely not done, but it is worth every penny. It's a discount at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: Extremly hard game even on the lowest level .... No time can you kick back and have fun in the game and the longer you play the errors you have done, punish you 2 as hard. Very big chanse that you get pisst off the longer you play :(  restarted 3 times and did 10 h sesions and whasent even close fun the first 3 h after that pure evil .i Gess thay want you to play the game 50 times so you know the exacly moves to do and when .Just Hyper klick everyting and dont be able to like what you creating
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: Idk what the problems are of some players. Tutorial is small but explains all basics. HuD is good enough to help you without give you too much useless details. Stile and sound give you the fealing of post-apo scenario.There are just some small things that need improvement (besides bugs) but maybe I'm not far enough: maybe more wood out from recycling or lower weight + higher amount when looting. Wood should provide more heat when burnt.In general loot of equipment need much more quality. The amount of repairing is too much (in life time, ressources and man power). You will need more man in your bunker or its impossible to repair everything besides cleaing, cooking and building. More man means a higher need of food and water. I understand the loop you will need between looting, building and recruiting but thats no more relastic how often you have to repair things.Cooking needs a balance update. Why a lvl 2 meal with the ingredians: meat + broccoli + potato gives you less value then roasted meat + broccoli soup + baked potato? I understand that the sim get a better fealing effect but I expectet in addition more value from a lvl 2 meal.All in all its a great game and I hope updates will come soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT Sheltered 1!  While there are a lot of similarities, the gameplay, goals, and challenges are significantly different.Although the first one was charming in it's own way, this one feels more gritty and tense.  It's not as forgiving as the first one, and you really have to think ahead and make some tough decisions.There are some minor bugs (the biggest one is losing materials when queuing a lot of meals to cook followed by a lot of workbench items--the items are never made, but the materials are lost forever).Still, on balance, it's a fun game, but you gotta spend the time to become familiar with the mechanics and the logic--you will be very frustrated if you go into it thinking it's just a slick repackage of the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game will not work for me. It comes up super zoomed in and the pointer is huge and I cannot read any of the menus they are super blurry and letters run into each other so it looks like a big line of white with some lighter and darker spots through it. You cannot make out any individual letters. I tried to get to settings to see if I could change graphics settings to make it to where I could at least get to the game (which I can't cause I can't read anything cause its' so blurred) I found settings... but could not read any of the options. I tried clicking things randomly ... The first one I clicked turned it from full screen to a little tiny box where I might have been able to read the writing if it was a tiny bit bigger but it was so small... I tried clicking things and eventually got it back to full screen but with all my clicking I was not able to get it legible at any point. I had to give up and I really did not want to give up. I have sent an email to the company in hopes they can help me. I'm guessing this is a temporary glitch and that they will fix it and like I said I loved the original and really want to play this one.EDIT: I could not see what the words said but guessed my way to settings and guessed my way to graphics and somehow managed to select an option that does work on my computer. It was toward the bottom of the list of options. I literally could not read any of it and was just messing around trying to guess. Since then, I have been able to play just in the last couple days and I'm loving the game. Its' much more complicated but still fun. I like it! Note to any new players. Work on your water first. upgrade water stuff and add containers and also crates to store your goods. Sometimes I've found stuff in my junk pile up on the surface and I had not even realized that not everything had transferred to my storage. Now I check it randomly to make sure it's empty. Also if there is a woods area, near you, you can go hunt and get tons of meat that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 is a fun game (just like it's predecessor) but it is currently riddled with a lot of very annoying bugs. Some of these bugs are so dire that the actual progression is affected. I'm surprised that the game was released with such obvious problems.As an example: in a fight I wanted to switch my pretty badly wounded leader into the backrow but the game decided to move the only remaining enemy into that spot instead. The guy then decided to stab my leader and the game ended. Another example: I also had a guy who could not access the medicine cabinet due to a movement logic error and as expected he bled out. Reanimation only has a 50 % chance of working (without a specific trait) and he promptly died. Really weird bugs like that happen all the time. You will already stumble upon them in the character creation window with traits and stats points all mixed up when reloading your last selection.That is the reason why I suggest buying the game at a later time or at least playing it at a later time when all the really annoying things have been fixed. Because otherwise it's a pretty solid game. Not much to say here specifically. If you enjoyed the first part you will most likely enjoy Sheltered 2 too.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played Sheltered 2 without prior knowledge of S1. I'm quite hooked by the game. It's true if it has its rough edges, bugs, balance issues and probably still misses some features, the devs seem to be eager to fix this. Provided they don't drop it and continue improving it, it's already a good game and it could become a fantastic one.I don't understand why it's sitting in "Mixed". I suppose S1 fans had expectations that were not met. But it's not my case and I appreciate this game for what it is : I'm having a good time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: i honestly dont understand why this game is being down-voted by people who have not even played it past 1 hour. i find this to be a fine successor to the first game. it could use a bit more work on balancing some aspects but all in all its fine. it adds a good amount without completely changing what the game is. if you like the first one i believe you will like this one also.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of promise and fun in discovery and fine-tuning. But it feels unpolished. The character models are miserable compared to the beautiful new artwork, for example. Customizing your character is hardly worth the time with such limited (and ugly) options. The font only displays as capitals when entering on the first screen, but show both lower and uppercase in-game. Little things like this matter for immersion.Overall though the playability is nice. Eager to sink more hours into it and get toward the late game. Will update review more later.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough, but the apocalypse should be tough. Could it be balanced to be a little easier? Probably ... especially when it comes to water. Strategizing the early game to focus on gathering as much water as possible would likely alleviate a lot of the water shortages later, but it would likely add to the grind and alleviate some of the fun of playing other parts of the game early on. Some balance adjustments in this department would not upset me at all, but it's workable as is.The game is a lot of fun and very immersive as you become attached to the game characters as the game goes on. If you could edit the names of the random people who show up, once you take them in, it could add even more to the game. My first play through I wasn't even aware that you could level up the characters, which was a treat to discover in my 2nd run. This added a lot more to the game and I was already really enjoying it.There are a lot of little unexpected twist in the game, which adds a lot to it. Watching one of my guys go crazy and start lighting things on fire was hilarious and upsetting at the same time. Then when one of the ladies was tired and just squatted to take a leak on the floor I busted up and had to screenshot it for my friends who live in California (they're used to that kind of stuff, so I had to rub it in and tell them she must be from CA).I've played a little over 25 hours and feel like I've barely scratched the surface on Sheltered 2 and that's a good thing. I've yet to encounter a lot of what the game has to offer and it's obviously going to take me a lot longer to even reach some of the abilities I've become aware exist in the game, like driving trucks. I found one on a long journey, but didn't have the ability to bring it back with me at the time. So I have something to look forward to when I go back.If you enjoy survival games like Project Zomboid, then this is right up your alley but instead of zombies you have to deal with things like pissed off cartel members or crazy church groups. If you like games that are challenging, require planning and managing resources, get Sheltered 2, you will enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: How is it possible that in 18 hours playing this I managed to see SOOOO many bugs related to factions, I released a hostage, and never got a menu to call the faction to tell them that, there is no way to ally with a faction.Thanks for the game, but I will stop playing it until we get a major update on these bugs, I like this game, it is fun and addictive, but the last bug made me alt+f4 without saving, it is frustrating to level up to complete a quest that does not have the UI needed to complete the quest.I blame marketing and the stupid deadlines the devs must have had.Revised review on my other 17 hours. I completed the quest where I had to return the wife to a dude, no reward at all, just a pat in the shoulder and "good work" I feel at work, maybe it is me that I am expecting rewards on a game when I do a task and not doing it because "it feels good"Update 1.0.10 When you add a blueprint and then cancel it, it won't let you add blueprints anymore, another game disrupting bug.Update 1.0.10, Sometimes when you deconstruct a tier 2 bed, it won't allow you anymore to place items in that "ghost area"Update 1.2.11, To make things fair, finally you guys got it together! thanks, so, in conclusion, release after is finished is a good practice, I haven't found a bug in this gameplay, probably the memory leak you got on the audio while playing for long hours, but that gets fixed once you restart, so it is not game breaking. Switching the review to positive! thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: In my humble opinion,as a lad that loved the original,this game is an lovely sequel to the sheltered we know and love.You have new stuff,and plenty of old stuff makes an appearance-Some things like the gas masks and the rad suits are missing,but it makes sense,considering the time this game takes place (years after the original)...I may be wrong here,as I'm just still barely scratching the surface,but it appears the factions aren't procedurally generated which is kinda a shame imo,but that's just me.The world seems to be,however.it's fun,give it a go :)EDIT; game is absolutely abandoned

_childDocuments_.review: A very welcome pastime I didn't see coming. Since I'm not a fan of survival games I fully expected to refund the game but ended up playing 12 hours without even noticing the time pass. The UI could use some improvements and there are bugs present, but I'm enjoying the game thoroughly.Unfortunately, the game's update roadmap has since been deleted and the whole project abandoned. The game remains unfinished.

Its a great game and its graphics are stunning , gameplay is relaxing and really improved on the previous game . Buy now , you won’t regret this .
