_childDocuments_.review: I Have played this game for quite some time and I was happy about the immediate bug fixes. However, it seems that bugs with regards to traders/recruits not spawning/visiting, as well as the person sent by one faction to collect quest items are still recurring. I thought that they had already fixed this problem. Also, the rare item quest now cannot be finished because no rare item is found upon searching the caravan. Bugs after bug fixes? Not recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is micromanagement deluxe (and not the fun type). My colonists  seem to love their corner. They always, gather in the corner of the shelter and just stand there for no reason, everyone of them. Also everything break down almost every day in the shelter, beds, windturbins, showers, yes everything, so i need to repair everything constanly, in the begining that ok when i only have like 8 things that need reparing but later stages its just A LOT of unnecessarily micromanagement. If my colonist when they are idle (which they almost always is) could help repair the base, like maybe in rimworld without me clicking and telling them to do so. No they just stand there in their corner doing nothing. They do not help with the farms, i need to click that, they do not clean, they do nothing in the base whitout me clicking them to do so, no they love their holliday in the corner.Also, for example, if a colonist starving and loosing health because they have not eat (the food storage is full of food), they decide that its better to sleep or do something else less important, and not eat even if their need of sleep for example is not even red yet. Sometimes they follow their needs but most of the times not and if they do they tend to prioritize wrong needs, so be prepared on more micromanagment. Its ok when you have like 3 surivors. But when your population increase its very frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  Liked playing the first game a lot.  This one is a much more complicated beast and I am still finding my feet.Already had to post my first bug so there are still a few things that need ironing out but nothing game breaking for me yet. Edit: also got stuck on the end of combat bug which has supposedly been fixed now.Some annoying things that I think are missing are,- inventory sort by weight- inventory sort by value- inventory filter junk/craft itemsAbout to start my second game as now I know how to make metal shavings so I can finally give my peeps a shower!
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Sheltered 1 and have been waiting for the 2nd one for a while.  Glad it finally released!  Yes, on launch day there are a couple of issues (like not being able to fix the generator), but the devs are working on patches and actively engaging with the community.  Would I recommend Sheltered 2?  Yes!!!!  It is a fun game and while it is 'like' the first one, there are some differences that makes this a different game (and not just a graphics overhaul).  The factions is an interesting new addition and being able to have hunting and foraging as map options is great.  Overall, I am really enjoying this and I look forward to more content updates from the devs to enrich the gameplay options.Well done Unicube & Team17!
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: Huge upgrade from Sheltered. Really interesting changes and I like the RPG aspect to the characters and how they used the new 3d perspective in a good way with top level building. I wish you could queue up multiple type of orders but I understand why you cant. Also fill your caravan up with rations since it doesn't affect weight and you may want to travel a bit longer since you probably explored a bit more of the map anywaysAlso seems like they just released an update that fixed the generator bug not allowing you to repair it. I got down to like 20% and was wondering why I couldn't fix it!Seems like devs are on top of things too! Just add multi key keybinding option!
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: Sheltered 2 has a new look and a few new features. I am enjoying the game but know that there isn't a HUGE difference past looks. Some new things are #1 Factions that control the map (ally or kill em). Even if you play easy its a lot more killing involved and less dense loot areas on the map. #2 inventory is now weight based. #3 Later on in the game you can make cars/bikes. #4 You interact directly outside you base more. #5 You have to make MRE's to travel and its now made from you food stores. #6 you have faction multi level goals now that work like achievements but once you unlock the levels by doing things, it then allows you to do those things quicker with boosts.  The developers stated they will do regular updates... so I hope they add more NEW items to the game. It still fun. And I am excited about what updates they bring... I have not run into any bugs yet either which is nice!
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: i've just barely scratched the surface but i can already tell If you liked the first game then you will like the sequel. Its more of the same with a fresh coat of paint on it but not in a bad way. A sequel does not need to reinvent itself to be a good game. Even though the game has mixed reviews atm i would still give it a try if you enjoyed the first game. I myself was on the fence but went with my gut and i'm glad i did.Game was abandoned...I was hopeful

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:I have to start by saying they fixed a LOT of the things that made shelter 1 annoying, the constant use of the mask is gone, and now u can disasemble and re-asemble a LOT of the key components for items, making svanging for scraps a lot more useful, overall it's a completly new game, i did some combat as well and it's a LOT more strategic than before... didnt reach any shelter attacks yet but i figure it will be lots of fun making a laberinth with traps for invaders.... i think a lot of people were expecting more of the same because there's a lot of mixed reviews, when in fact it's something different but at the same time so much better presented and balanced!!!there are some bugs but nothing gamebreaking for me, not sure what are the other reviews complaining about....what i would improve is a pre-set for what the party will carry when they leave, we really need that...this game deserves a LOT more love than it's getting right now, keep up the good work devs!Original:I played the first game for hours on end and i can confidently say they fixed a lot of things that needed improving yet kept the good parts....i dont feel like ive seen enough of the game yet to say 'yeh' or 'nay' so i will give it a yes and pending more playtime for a definitive revised review! happy gaming! (and really, if u liked the first one, this looks to be more of that with improved mechanics)
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: yeah they may have copy and pasted alot of stuff but its alot more challenging than the first game, you really have to push out and get food because it ONLY SPAWNS YOU IN SOME GOD FORSAKEN DESERT THAT HAS NO FOOD EXCEPT RABBITS so you gotta get out there and get seeds to grow vegetable to be able to make recepies that will actually sustain
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review: is gud... nice update graphically to the OG. Like the smooth transition from underground 2D to above ground isometric. It's like Shelter and This War of Mine got busy and had a luv-child,  Great game at a great price.Edit: So I'm 20 hours into the game now and have run across a few bugs. weapons not showing up in inventory after a trade. Audio pops & clicks after several hours of continuous play. But still I am really into this.  I'm reading some of these reviews that say it's not like the original. I have to wonder what game they were playing?  This game is awesome if you're into survival/resource management games.  It can get difficult when the temps warm up and water runs out, yes.  But why would someone play a game like this that is too easy?  The Dev is working hard at addressing bugs as quickly as they can but Jeez folks, what do you expect for a 20 dollar game?  Some of these post just scream entitlement. I'm an older gamer and remember first playing video games in arcades when you would drop a quarter and maybe get 10 minutes of gameplay, if you were good.  These games today provide many times that in playtime/cost ratio. I just can't get over some of the snot-bubble reviewers that seem to think this game should be Hello Kitty: island Adventure.  Keep up the good work Devs. I love this game and am more than willing to play it while it gets polished.
_childDocuments_.name: Sheltered 2

_childDocuments_.review:
It's been twenty years since the world as we knew it ended. The last of humanity splintered into opposing factions. Will you unite or conquer?

Building upon the original 2015 fan-favourite, Sheltered 2 brings new challenges and deeper strategic gameplay. You are tasked with creating a leader and building up your faction whilst managing resources and tackling threats both natural and human. Everything from starvation and dehydration to radiation poisoning and enemy raids can prove fatal.

Sheltered 2's new Factions system is pivotal to a base's success. Send out expeditions to explore the vast wasteland and forge relationships, or bitter rivalries with other camps. Trade resources to grow and thrive together; or go head-to-head with rivals in an expanded combat system and grow your foothold in the wasteland. Will you ally with or dominate the other factions?

name: PowerWash Simulator
detailed_description: Halloween Seasonal 2024 Something filthy this way comes in PowerWash Simulator’s latest Seasonal Special. You’ll have to hose off more than a few cobwebs to take the Halloween House from mortifyingly mucky to party-ready perfection. PowerWash Simulator – Shrek Special Pack Playtime is ogre. Get to work cleaning up five fairy tale maps inspired by DreamWorks Animation’s Shrek. It’ll take more than pixie dust to restore these iconic locales to their former lustre, but thankfully, happily ever after is in your hands! PowerWash Simulator – Muckingham Files – Part 4 Part four of the Muckingham Files series brings you two new Bonus Jobs from friends in high places. Clean up local crypto enthusiast, Devon King’s vandalised modern mansion and pilot Floraine Perez’ fire plane following a flight over Mount Rushless. PowerWash Simulator – Cruise Ship Sun Deck – Summer 2024 Cool off with sudsy, high-pressured water this summer in PowerWash Simulator’s latest Seasonal Special. Take a vacation from Muckingham’s mainland to clean up the sun deck of Crab Bay’s cruise liner following a rather messy departure. Once you’re done, it should be smooth, sanitary sailing from there on out! Ticked off tourists, fried foods and greedy gulls do not make for most folks’ idea of a dream holiday - but you are not most folks. If the destination is dirty, you’re on board! With the sun on your back and cool mist on your visor, cleaning up feels like a breeze. Say “bon voyage” to dirt as you slough off the remnants of an avian air assault, revealing the vivid sun deck beneath. Ahhh, so satisfying. Whether you take on the task as a solo traveller or bring all hands on deck in co-op, you’ll be sure to feel the winter blues defrost in this summer muckbuster! You’ll also receive all-new summer threads to have you looking and feeling cool. Well, as cool as you physically can in a rubber suit. KEY FEATURES: • Wash and explore the Cruise Ship Sun Deck • New custom summer suit • New custom summer gloves • New custom power washer skin About PowerWash Simulator’s Seasonal Specials PowerWash Simulator’s Seasonal Specials is a series of free content updates containing a single map themed around a season or holiday – after all, cleaning isn’t just for Spring! PowerWash Simulator DLC: Muckingham Files - Part 3 The third instalment of the Muckingham Files is the ultimate clean-up for aquatic fanatics, expanding PowerWash Simulator’s in-game universe with two free new Bonus Jobs. PowerWash Simulator – Alice’s Adventures Special Pack Take a trip down the rabbit hole to uncover a topsy-turvy, swizzy, whirly world of psychedelic colours, maximalist décor and larger-than-life locales. Clean up Wonderland in five fantastical new levels for PowerWash Simulator. PowerWash Simulator – Warhammer 40,000 Special Pack Imperial technology has fallen afoul to a litany of dirt. It is your singular honour to perform the ultimate purification protocol. Command potent power washing technology to restore a range of Imperial machines, ready to serve the Emperor once more. PowerWash Simulator - Back to the Future Special Pack Great Scott! Crank that water pressure to 88 miles per hour and travel back in time to hose down iconic movie sets from the Back to the Future trilogy in five new maps for PowerWash Simulator! PowerWash Simulator SpongeBob SquarePants Special Pack Soak up the sights of Bikini Bottom and get totally absorbed in a mini-campaign spanning across six new jobs for PowerWash Simulator! Restore the Pacific province back to a pristine paradise following a series of mysteriously mucky mishaps. PowerWash Simulator - Midgar Special Pack Your PowerWashing Services are needed in Midgar! From the gritty yet gripping world of one of Final Fantasy’s most unforgettable installments comes five filthy new maps for PowerWash Simulator, featuring iconic locations, vehicles, and enemies. PowerWash Simulator Soundtrack From sparkling ensemble Green Gills, the iconic track Make It All Shine will have you reminiscing over time-well-spent in sunny Muckingham, whilst the bonus Carousel Theme will have you twirling and bobbing just like those ponies (no cleaning required!) PowerWash Simulator - Tomb Raider Content Pack Grapple with grime in your ultimate quest to defeat all dirt covering Croft Manor and its grounds, along with Lara’s trusty vehicles. In this adventurous collaboration with Tomb Raider, wash and explore five new levels for PowerWash Simulator. About the Game Wash away your worries with the soothing sounds of high-pressure water. Fire up your power washer and blast away every speck of dirt and grime you can find. Build your own power-washing business and unlock new tools, upgrades and more – all with the simple satisfaction of power-washing to a sparkling finish.  Relax, unwind in single player, or play with friends in Online Co-Op; either way, have good, clean fun. No dirt is too tough for your range of washers, nozzles, cleaners, and extensions. From casual, clean freaks to players looking to get into the nitty-gritty, everyone can pick up and play to feel immersed. Absorb the relaxing atmosphere and stress-free pace as you strip dirt from patios, pavements, vehicles, and public parks. Get creative and make art. Your nozzles are your brushes; the neighbourhood is your canvas. Sit back, relax, and wash your worries down the drain. TIME TO CLEAN UP THE NEIGHBOURHOOD Build up your business in Career Mode and complete a variety of dirty jobs across the dusty town of Muckingham.  There's no right or wrong; no time pressure or final score, just you and the tools you need to soak away your stress. Want a clean start? Chill out and replay your favourite jobs in Free Play.  POWERWASH AND CHILL Relax, unwind, and play with friends in Online Co-Op! Lend a helping hand to your closest pal in Career Mode, or up to 6 friends can splash around in Free Play, tackling any job the host has already completed. KEEP IT CLEAN For those looking for a little more pressure, beat your best scores in Challenge Mode! Fight grime in different scenarios; wash against the clock in Time Challenge or test your accuracy by using as little water as possible in Water Challenge. GOOD CLEAN FUN  Graffiti, grime, moss, and mould, no dirt is too tough for your range of washers, nozzles, cleaners, and extensions. Different dirt types have different levels of toughness, so make sure you're getting tactical with your equipment. Feeling fancy? Then customise your look with washer skins and gloves! RELAXATION, SATISFACTION GUARANTEED From casual, clean freaks to players looking to get into the nitty-gritty, everyone can pick up and play to feel immersed. Absorb the relaxing atmosphere and stress-free pace as you strip dirt from patios, pavements, vehicles, and public parks. Stress gets to us all, so sit back, relax, and wash your worries down the drain. THE WORLD IS YOUR CANVAS  Create art by cleaning the way you want. Your nozzles are your brushes; the neighbourhood is your canvas. Unleash your creative talents and transform ordinary dirt into exceptional artwork. Share your techniques and showcase your power-washing prowess and mud-caked masterpieces!

RELAXATION, SATISFACTION GUARANTEED From casual, clean freaks to players looking to get into the nitty-gritty, everyone can pick up and play to feel immersed. Absorb the relaxing atmosphere and stress-free pace as you strip dirt from patios, pavements, vehicles, and public parks. Stress gets to us all, so sit back, relax, and wash your worries down the drain. THE WORLD IS YOUR CANVAS  Create art by cleaning the way you want. Your nozzles are your brushes; the neighbourhood is your canvas. Unleash your creative talents and transform ordinary dirt into exceptional artwork. Share your techniques and showcase your power-washing prowess and mud-caked masterpieces!
short_description: Release the Pressure with PowerWash Simulator! Wash away your worries with the soothing sounds of high-pressure water. Fire up your power washer and blast away every speck of dirt and grime you can find, all with the simple satisfaction of power-washing to a sparkling finish.

name: Townscaper
detailed_description: Build quaint island towns with curvy streets, small hamlets, soaring cathedrals, canal networks, or sky cities on stilts. Build the town your dreams, block by block. No goal. No real gameplay. Just plenty of building and plenty of beauty. That's it. Townscaper is an experimental passion project. More of a toy than a game. Pick colors from the palette, plop down colored blocks of houses on the irregular grid, and watch Townscaper's underlying algorithm automatically turn those blocks into cute little houses, arches, stairways, bridges, and lush backyards, depending on their configuration.
about_the_game: Build quaint island towns with curvy streets, small hamlets, soaring cathedrals, canal networks, or sky cities on stilts. Build the town your dreams, block by block. No goal. No real gameplay. Just plenty of building and plenty of beauty. That's it. Townscaper is an experimental passion project. More of a toy than a game. Pick colors from the palette, plop down colored blocks of houses on the irregular grid, and watch Townscaper's underlying algorithm automatically turn those blocks into cute little houses, arches, stairways, bridges, and lush backyards, depending on their configuration.
short_description: Instant town building toy

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing town assembly toy. The build options are limited to colors, all other variation is determined by placement (grid shape and nearby buildings). Simple controls get out of the user's way, and the visual & aural effects are satisfying to experience. It is easy to spend more time in a play session than planned, so set a timer to let you know when to quit.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I want to begin this review by urging you to look up the painter Carl Larsson. The bright aquarelle colours of Townscaper must have been inspired by his paintings (especially since the creator is Swedish), and it works almost too well.I'm absolutely positive about this game - that, is if you can call it a game. Because it's more of a zen creative experience without any real end goal. It's more of an interactive art installation which allows you to create the sculpture. Just build whatever you fancy, play around, change colours, enjoy yourself while listening to music or a podcast, and then share the result with others if you feel like it. It's not for everyone, but if you don't enjoy it, then that should be quite clear even before you decide to pay for the product.It's bare boned, of course. It's Early Access after all, and it's cheap. I get the feeling that it's more of an interactive art experience, created to allow the player to not only be creative, but to experience imagination. It might sound vague, but I feel the game really does that for me.If you want to play something that allows you to create an imaginary town, coloured by Carl Larsson, and described by Charles Dickens, then this game is for you. It's given me a few hours of zen enjoyment already (and I'm not done yet), and given some time to be developed further, I'm sure it will be able to keep my interest also in the future whenever I have some time over in which I just want some kind of meditative experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I've owned this game for a few years now and it's always chill and relaxing. I use it for ideas when designing cities for TTRPG's or just looking to pass the time. While sometimes I do wish I could see little people populating my towns, it's a perfect companion for anyone working from home or just looking for a game that doesn't demand anyrhing from you yet allows you to be creative.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Way too overpriced for what it is. Now that the developer promised no additional content will be added and is focusing on ports to other consoles (abandoning it while not doing any actual "early access" updates beyond a customizable sun angle), hopefully the game will drop to lower discounts (I personally wouldn't get it under 50% off, had I the choice) and it'll then be a decent buy
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I like the whole concept of this game, but I wish the developer would add people and pets like cats sitting on the roof or dogs being walked by people. Another feature that is badly needed is hedges and benches and/ or fountains as you upgrade the environment. Also beach terrain to make a larger beach area. Boats would also look aesthetically pleasing, they don't need to do anything, it could just be stationary. There's ways around saving memory and engine lag from games. I hope the developer doesn't half-ass this game and leave it as is. This has a lot of potentials. Signs on buildings would help to distinguish stores from houses.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I've just played for 2 hours but omg. The precious time is worth it. I've already built a big city and now I miss my Lego kind of childhood. Would be nice to have some people around though (it feels a bit lonely), also fountains. Not sure how that would fit in here, but it would be a very nice addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I never imagined that it could be so relaxing designing a town somewhere in the ocean.The game is nice, I wish I could also design more than streets. That you just could expand the little patches of sand you have at the edge.In general it would be nice to have more options to build with but I still like the way how the game is now.Love it hope the game gets more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really calm, relaxing and has a great and cute art style. With each new update it feels better if only for a bit. It really is a passion project because you can see the love put into it and it´s hard to believe only one person made it. The only con would be if you are a person who can´t live without symmetry because this game embraces randomness and asymmetry. It´s better not to plan and just "let the brush flow". Also, there is no endgame. The only endgame is to make something you think looks nice and maybe share the screenshots with people.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Really chill building. The graphics are really pretty and you can make large coastal towns and structures. It'd be lovely to see the game expand and include things like docks and terrain. I would definitely buy a DLC pack of such features since I know it'd be a lot of work to program and animate. Either way so far love the game, thank you!side note: The "bloop" sound when you make things is really pleasing XD haha
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and quick game to pick up and put your creative thoughts down. It is a little tricky to pick up how to move the camera at first, and it does take a little getting used to, but it's really easy to get lots of different angles to view your creation.I do wish there were buttons you could select so you could add staircases where ever you want, rather then needing them to be between buildings, but it's super quick to learn how they work. The little popping noises also make me laugh and makes the game feel very light-hearted.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I can easily sink hours into this game! I only hope they add more features as it goes on, but I still have a lot of fun playing it. You can make cute little homely towns or massive cities. Sometimes the loading could be a bit smoother, especially if you want to do a really big town. I love it a lot over all though.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Nookrium made a video about it, otherwise I wouldn't have heard about this little gem.Was feeling rather sad and needed something simple. Something to ease my mind and relax a bit.Bought it because of the price and didn't regret at all!I love the artstyle and how the buldings generate. Camera controls are different than I'm used to but after a couple of minutes I already forgot about it and gotten used to.Works like a charm despite being Early Access.Thanks for making this dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: An addictive little tool that has a lot of potential use for setting design. Slightly limited in certain terrain options and the grid layout, but overall a delight to work/play with. Infinite possibility and new features to be discovered with each little tweak made to a building, and almost complete creative freedom (that still adheres to the laws of physics!) I also really appreciate that it autosaves as I am awful with remembering to save projects - the fact it has them saved as images rather than filenames is very helpful too, me being someone who tends to name all my files "AAAAA1" or "shsndjfkdj" or the like.Going onwards, I'd love to see a couple of things; ability to lock certain features in - if you want a stairway to remain in place once you place other blocks around it, you should be able to 'lock' that particular block - as well as the option for a more linear, square grid instead of the curved one, for people who want a more symmetrical build, or one that is predictable in how the blocks will fall. The ability to place sand and create beaches would also be great, and someone else mentioned the idea of villagers walking around the town, which would be adorable. I bought this yesterday at the time of writing and I already adore it, and I can't wait to see where the development goes!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and unique town builder! As an artist who draws backgrounds and as someone who plays DND, this simple game could open up a bunch of possible waves of creativity. From making maps to making a reference for buildings to doodle a picture inspired by it, i think something like this could be awesome once fully fleshed out. I also love how snappy things are too, like the auto fill of grassy areas and building extensions. It's definitely a fun and relaxing time.The controls were a little hard to get use to at first, but i definitely got use to them once i learned them. I would definitely recommend at least a tab that shows basic controls in the main menu, just in case for any really new players.Another thing that i would love is the ability to add more natural land. Like making the beach extend out a little further or the ability to add grass or natural trees in town. The possibilities are endless for additions to this neat little game! ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely, serene timewaster. It is utterly impossible to create anything ugly or disharmonic.Now, developers, not all of us use gamepad. So, if I have for example, a rudder control attached for my flightsim, it is calibrated completely different than a gamepad, resulting in no control over spinning etc with my mouse, forcing me to find and disconnect it if I want to have a few minutes of Townscaper. Could you please consider a enable/disable switch when configuring gamepad?
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those rare games i had to buy within literally seconds after finding out about it. It wasn't a hard decision since it's really cheap. And for the price you get most relaxing playing experience & beautiful visual style. By the words of its creator it's not even a game, just a tech demo, well i wish there were more demos like this. There are really no reasons this game shouldn't be in your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: great town builder with an amazing amount of free play and creativity to unlock. it feels like finding a secret within the game whenever i place a building in a certain spot and magical balconies or fences and hedges appear. you must allow the game to play WITH you and your island, as we can't fully control the wonder
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game Is great. It is a small game about building cities in an Infinite (at least I haven't yet found a limit) 3D space on an asymmetrical grid, at the time of writing this the only real options are where you wish to place a building tile and what color the tile is to be. There are no other options at the moment but that being said this game has tremendous potential to be even better!With in the first five minutes of playing this game I found myself super relaxed yet focused, Playing a game yet working to build something cool. It was then I realized something, I got up went and got a snack as well as a drink then put of some chill music and it got even better. You wont notice the time fly when playing this game and it brought a similar feeling of peace and contentment that playing minecraft or slime rancher brings and is a great game to wind down after a long day. Despite first thinking about how I could use this to build visual representations of towns for my DnD games with my friends I now have a fuller respect for this passion project created by the dev solely because he felt that it was something he wanted to do, Just for fun you know? I think we can all agree that games made with the sentiment tend to be a bit more fun and have a lot more heart.So do I recommend this not yet finished and cheap game? Absolutely! though do keep in mind in its current state it may not be for everyone and it is my hope that going forward we can watch this game grow into something truly awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is one of those rare games that is a new genre. It's not really a game it's a toy you play with to create "cute" little (or not so little if you have the time) towns. It reminds me of the old "Kai's Power Goo" and "Bryce" unique toys to let you play with photos and create fractal landscapes. (google them) Apparently based on a procedural process you simply click way on the base of water and fun little structures magically appear, each click rewarded by accompanying cute sounds. The power of Townscaper is that is has a set of internal rules (some type of shape grammar like system) that understands the context of neighboring structures and builds meaningful structures. A single little island turns into a house of a church or all types of interesting structures. You can share your creations by saving the process as a little (unreadable) text file that other can import via the clipboard. (Would be nice to import via files) This is clearly a labor of love by creator Oskar Stålberg @OskSta a freaking game wizard. Just go buy this thing it's crazy inexpensive also!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access game it is really good. I enjoy the flexibility to place where you want to place. I feel the colours really help give a little bit more life. I use the colours for separating different districts. I can't wait to see where this goes, and I would like to see more things added. Yes there are games where you can build your own cities, but they always come with managing and not failing. This is completely sandbox, there is no complicated systems to worry about. I think it is really good to just build and express your own creative freedom.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest i mostly play this game whilst doing something else to keep myself from fidgeting. It is really pretty and easy to play with but don’t go in to it expecting to build something symmetric.  Getting things to look good is quite easy and the game works well in that case. But getting something to look great is a whole lot harder I have found. But imo that is part of its charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: - Perfect when you need to relax,- aesthetically pleasing,- no matter what you do, it will look good.- For this price is a must.Changed my review to not recommended:- I think more mechanics should be added, like population walking through the streets, balconies maybe some other structures... It still has a lot of more potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! I have been playing for a while and I am happy about how I found this! I thought it would be bad with such a simple premis but it wasn't it was very very fun! Also if the creator sees this add your other project to the game (you know, World Scaper) as a mode/seperate game and if it is a seperate game you should give free access to people with this game already.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. It's low-stress, a little mindless and a lot of fun.I would like the devs to add the following content:Roads that don't gate or fence themselvesThe ability to create the beaches and stairs myselfMore colour palettes, the one it comes with is fun but it needs more optionsGarden and fountain features that I can add myselfMore roofing options that aren't created automatically; I'd like to add some different roofs myself.Otherwise, this is very fun and very relaxing. Building the world is a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem of a game. Sandbox? Zen garden?First enjoy effortlessly create aesthetic small villages.Then enjoy the process of understanding, little by little, how the different interactions programmatically generate some elements (e.g. stairs, small flags, gardens) and awe in wonder when you accidentally discover something new.Then start being ambitious and start building bigger, more complex cities. Colorful towns. Impossible, intricate, architectures.Or just use it as you zen garden, placing blocks one by one, enjoying the really polished experience of building your little world.There is no right way to "play" this game, as long as you have fun all of them are right and I greatly recommend trying it and find your own unique way of enjoying this little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Totally addicitve game, even when I'm away from the game I see these cute little houses in my minds eye and come up with new ideas for my buildings. I love how it is relaxing and therapeutic and how you can create both little islands and big towns as well as castles. There's even a Schwyzerdütsch translation for the UI!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Barely started this game but I feel a strong need to review it. Ever since I was young, I've been obsessed with old, precarious construction that is built in a way that appears so unstable yet has somehow lasted decades. I don't know why, I just love that kind of thing. It's weirdly comforting and and warm to see something that seems like such a mess,  like it would never be built today, and is still standing. Rusty and paint-chipped, maybe (which makes it even better in my opinion!) but still standing. Anyways, this game lets me make weird, archaic towns and I adore it. I already teared up playing it. It's just really really my thing.EDIT: There was originally a whole section of this review where I talked about having an issue with my colorblindness in this game and how it could be fixed by adding a color dropper feature to the game, but I was messing around in the game and just discovered that there actually is a color dropper that you just use by holding down left click on a building of the color you want! I officially have no complaints with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: First, I wouldn't call this a game as there is no goal aside from your own artistic expressions. Second, the zen-like, catharsis one gets from this type of experience is worth more than the admission price alone. In a perfect world, this would have swappable themes like Fantasy buildings, Sci-Fi, Punks, both Cyber and Steam. I mean the list is endless obviously. Id also allows for a little more refinement in the camera movement, it can get a bit cumbersome with larger cities. All in all, this was an easy recommendation because at this price you are basically guaranteed satisfaction.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper delivers exactly what the title promises.  This game is just a chill model town builder, nothing more nothing less. 15 minutes in and I already want more! Theres no instructions, just do. The controls are intuitive enough to figure out, at least with a mouse. I think what gives it personality is the little touches like environments popping in and leaving little bits of rubble that scatter around or fall in the water.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredible, it's so simple, yet, so good. It could have some other living creatures, like fish and other types of birds. If someday add little people walking freely around the city, maybe add boats that arrive on the city. They even don't need to interact with each other, but it would be fun to see they walking and entering and laving the building.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's like painting with small block houses. No ppl to feed, no economy to worry about.U don't have full control of how things join up but it adds to the simplicity. I believe its a fully released game and dev seems moved on to other things so not expecting huge updates but u never know, some active ppl creating cool mods tho.Very zen like, great if u have trouble sleeping v relaxing before bed.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Hey everybody! I wanted to play this game for some time and I finally did! ^^ The game is unique and amazing for me. building things..remove some. and transforms into something else... Day or night time to take screenshots. it was fun. Recommended for all ages for sure :DI will add Townscaper screenhots soon on my website - Roxanna Stefaniuc Fabiola AKA Pictures With Vulpoaica
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game with some interesting building mechanics. It's like playing with wooden blocks that are constantly adjusting shape to match their surroundings. Vast variety of possible combinations may keep your interest for a long time. Also, it's quite easy to play for children without a help of adults.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The dev recently posted a message abbout his game and how he will be take'n this time to spend more time with his daughter, this is both my reply too his message and my heart felt recamendation for this game.I did not buy this game, i had it wish listed but never got around too it, yesterday a good friend bought it for me, he saw it on my list and gave it a try, he then sent me it, i love this game so much, and have reposted about it on two diffrent discords suggesting it as a great buy both for people need'n a simple relax'n way to let trubbles slip away or a stress releaver, my friend now plays it everyday before he goes off to work, he is a county sherrif so you know his days are stressfull, we love your game and thank you so much for it, and i know all too well how important dad is too a lil girl, i my self am a papa's little girl, i love my father so much so please, while you can, hold her, hug her, kiss that little princess, she will allways remeber it and hold it in her heart dad, Thank you, i love you as well for this. :Speech_Love: :ManaRegenerationYing:
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The store is upfront about not really being a city builder... or even a game. However, my problem is the grid is awful. All the tiles are irregularly shaped and don't use consistent angles at any point. If you want to build anything with symmetry, you're screwed. That alone is a deal-breaker for me. If there was an option to use it's 'free-form grid' or squares or hexagons or octagons and triangles then this would be a good timekill, but the only option is my least favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: i think this is perfect to play when i'm starting to get slightly overwhelmed because i can have a mindful moment but it's still mildly stimulating in that i need to decide where to put things architecturally to suit the surroundings and appear interesting. i think this is a great game for some neurodiverse people to consider if they like the look of the graphics and find committing to meditation really difficult as the brain may need a little something to focus on.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little toy (not a game, per se) with a good amount of enjoyment to be had from it. Graphically, it is simple but nice. Audio is adequate. There are lots of nice little touches to it.The only problem is that apart from a few birds, the towns you build feel empty. That's because they are, but still. What would REALLY make this shine would be townsfolk wandering around your construction, and the ambient sounds that went with them.  The ability to build on a field instead of just water would also help add to the longevity, I think.Either way, for the price, it's a nice little toy as it stands.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing for when Im anxious at night and cant sleep. No real purpose no goals, no time limits. Just a bunch of fun colorful buildings. If you want an exciting game this isnt it, but it you just want to mess around and make some cute buildings this game is perfect. The only things I would even really want added is some boats and people going around, but even without that its perfectly fine and worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: In its current version, Townscaper is just beatiful.As the dev puts it, it's not a game. It's a toy. You have endless supply of house blocks and you can do whatever you want with them. That's it. Nothing more to it.Wanna put on some music? Sure. Wanna watch something on the side? Go ahead. Wanna play it with a friend or family on the side? Why not? Wanna set challenges for yourself? You can do that too.Again, it's a toy. You invent your own fun. I made one "world" with it and I already felt it was worth the purchase half-way. If it looks interesting, I'd say go ahead and get it. This is not a game that you calculate bang for buck, just enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Is it even a game?   - KindaIs it good?  - AbsolutelyIs it worth the money?  -100% yesWhat do you do?  Well you go around, making a town, thats it.  simple, relaxing, elegant, fun.I of course want to see more from this game, but even in its current state, its fantastic to just unwind, and see what you can make.  I keep making new things, and end up surprised by how it turns out.  Kids love it, I love it.  9/10 with one point taken off because I want more of it!  Then it will get my 10!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of this game is nice, very appealing. Unfortunately there is so little variation in the "underlying algorithm" that you'll figure most of what it can do within a few minutes. I have played more interesting games for the same price, or even cheaper. That's why I can't recommend this game, not for the (low) price that it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Slip away into a gentle fantasy world where tall towers rise above calm waters, birds perch on tile roofs above the twisty walkways and avenues below. It's a tool for the imagination, a device for storytelling, a place to dream in. Take a screenshot and picture the dragons flying there among the floating cities.Simple, yet subtle, it works its magic as you build; the balconies sport benches and telescopes; laundry lines cross gaps with washing flapping; potted trees and buses sway in gentle breezes.Wonderful, delightful toy. I only wish it had more to it: a tool to adjust the palette; a choice to build on un-level terrain; a choice of grid styles (oh, how I long for straight lines), a zoom that extends a little further back, and a way to import alternate building styles (imagine crafting a futuristic city). Perhaps the developer will consider enhancing it. Or offer an enhanced version for sale (I'd happily buy it). But you will enjoy what it is now: a virtual playground.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: When enjoyed as intended, Townscaper is an effortless stress-reliever and an easy buy at this price point. However, it could be so much more. Many players (including myself) see the immensely useful applications Townscaper has for map creation, worldbuilding, and even role-playing. Unfortunately, the game's intentionally minimal interface only allows you to build in the confines of a mid-20th century coastal town. What if there was an option for a grass base instead of water? Or medieval buildings? Or different types of blocks that created unique features like shop signs and display windows? What if the rooftops could be weathered and old? or covered with snow? The possibilities are infinite.This game's community is bursting with ideas on how to improve and expand the game, and I dearly hope the developers don't let these ideas go unheeded, because this game is truly a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I am new to architecture games, but found this game so easy to get into. It's so relaxing, and it really lets your creativity shine. You can randomly click until you have a masterpiece, or you can try recreating a map you found online. The only thing that bothers me, is I wish there were an option to be able to make things more symmetrical. If you can get passed that though, I highly suggest spending some leisure time creating your personal fortress. Also creator, if you see this..... the ability to add beaches, docks, and boats would be amazing to add.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Want to love the game (toy, really), but we NEED a way to place and remove more than one block at a time, and there just ISN'T. Imagine a paint program where you have to click. every. pixel. one. at. a. time. Literally any single other tool (a larger brush option? click and drag? line tool? area fill?) would make a world of difference, but none are available. Any time I think of doing a build, the sheer volume of individual one-block-one-click stifles creativity and frustrates the experience. It's maddening how close Townscaper is to greatness, but this one thing sinks it for me. If the dev ever adds even a single simple tool to help with this, I would change to a thumbs up in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Before you buy this, the game is EXTREMELY shallow, you'll get bored within minutes of playing due to the lack of content and very small amount of things to actually well, build with. I quite enjoy the game as its fun to load up every evening and add a few houses to my town and leave it at that. No need to worry about saving it which is a lovely quality of life feature but you will get bored very quickly playing this if you prefer less dull experiences
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most relaxing, but also creative games I've ever played. Everything--the controls, the HUD, camera movement--is so straightforward that it doesn't get in the way of creativity. Even a little kid could pick it up and have very little trouble with it.Also--and this really goes without saying--it is one of the most aesthetically pleasing games I've played. You can make some pretty complex, beautiful structures with just a dozen clicks here and there, instead of having to rummage through a huge library of assets to find the right wall-piece to use for a house. It's like the game works with you to make exactly what you're imagining. It does take a tiny bit of experimentation, but that's part of what's fun about it. I was trying to figure out how to make stairs up to a higher level of my city, and a few clicks later the game was like "here's some stairs."I'd recommend this to anyone who likes creative games and/or slow-paced relaxing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this game for about 4 hours total (had it running in the background) and I would absolutely recommend this game/simulator/sandbox to people who just love to build it is very good at letting my creativity flow. _childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is quite possibly the perfect game to relax. It is certainly more a toy than a game; there's no goal, no levels, just you building your ideal floating city in the middle of an ocean sunset. It feels more involving than other "toy" entries, likely because the level of customization is high enough to be engaging but not high enough to stress you out over little choices. Plus you can export the perfect photo of your island hamlet so it feels like you're working towards something. If I only had 2 minutes to play something but needed to chill, this is what I'd go to.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a chill indie sandbox game centered around building unique cities and towns by simply pointing and clicking. There are no goals or objectives for this game. While building stuff there are multiple special interactions that you figure out as you click and build, such as stacking and removing buildings to create different appearances and how to build grassy areas, paths, and stairs. You start off on a large open hexagon layout and just start building and connecting land together. There are not very many settings in the game, but you can change the colors of buildings with a color palette, save your creations, and change the lighting. I don't have a tablet, but this would be great on one. It's very easy to pick up and put down and has great replayability because you can create new townscapes endlessly. I bought this game in early access and wished there had been more content updates since I got it since the game had great potential. But if you enjoy creative, relaxing sandbox games like this, for $6 it's still worth checking out. Overall, recommended ★

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I wouldn't say this game is bad. It's a genuine fun simple little town building game. But, as many others have said, there's some big problems. I understand that it's in early access, but I think it's too early. There's not much to do besides choose which colors you want your architecture to be, then click around on a grid (which is also randomly generated, meaning you could end up with a shape you don't want in that place) and build towers. And this wouldn't be too bad, but for the amount it costs, at this early in development, I think it would be best to either lower the price quite a lot, or work on adding more features. This game might be for you if you like a simple architectural building simulator, but for me, I'd like something with more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I love this little art tool, even if I feel like most of the actual artistry comes from the developer and I am merely implementing his fantastic aesthetic vision :)Since it's early access, a suggestion: this game is obviously not ever going to be a city building sim, but I'd enjoy a "challenge" mode which would place some constraints on me as a player, or give me some goals. Like a requirement to use X blocks of each color, for instance, or a requirement as to how many blocks I can have at each level of the building (like 25  ground level, 20 one story up, 15 two stories up etc, or the reverse!) Or (not sure how possible this would be to implement) a requirement that all the ground level paths be connected... or a requirement that buildings be connected above ground. Just some prompts or pushes to make me solve problems and try designs that might not otherwise occur to me. I guess such things could come from the community, but it would be easier to track if the game either enforced the constraints or at least displayed some stats :)Kind of on the opposite end of feature ideas -- I also think it would be fun to add a random generator with some parameters the user could set, like maximum horizontal and vertical sizes and colors to use, so we could watch the game "play itself" :)

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up on a whim just to snag a 5 dollar discount during the Steam summer sale. Honestly, didn't expect that much out of it, developer said he wanted to see how people use it and I've always been a sucker for city planning and logistics. Now I need to clarify right now if you're looking for logistics in the same vein as City Skylines, that is not what you're getting out of this game. What you are getting is as much of a game as say wooden toy trains. It's not a game as of writing this review, it is a cute fun tool. You start with nothing but water. You click the left mouse button and boom. A little island on the grid you selected. Click on top of that island and a little structure pops up. As you continue building, you can delete certain blocks and stairways and arches will form. If you build high up and add more blocks on the side of a building, steel support beams will reach down to provide integrity. And that's really all there is to the toy. What's great about this is that it honestly allows you to plan our things like rpg cities and fully realize various structures like cathedrals, castles, lighthouses, and even canals. You don't see people moving around or anything, but you might see a bird perch on a roof. The architecture in of itself reminds me of something I'd see out of a Ghibli movie, and that alone makes it quite charming.For a few bucks, this tool is a great thing if you just want to unwind and create little towns with cute architecture. I can't wait to see what else is in store for this great little toy.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps the most helpful gimmick that this game has up it's sleeve is that the "grid" isn't fully square or rectangular; it's procedural. Some spots will truncate inwards creating a three sided building while others splay out with five or six points, making it  difficult to build a Manhattan-style grid-city. It subtly nudges the player to get more creative without them realizing it and that is revolutionary for this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is addicting. I've played for almost 3 and a half hours, and I'm in love with it. It lets you create without having to perform using very simple tools. Honestly, anyone could play it. It is what you make it. I'm sure you could build impressive fortresses or whatever, but you could also just click randomly until you get something you feel somewhat drawn to. I think the trailer shows the gameplay very well. Only that it's a bit sped up.I'm an architect student, and going in to this I think I expected more stylistic options. But honestly, I'm happy there isn't. The creator is Swedish, and so am I, and I feel really quite at home with this old European-esque architecture. And I'm happy the game stops me from choosing too much - I wouldn't get anything done. Now I just choose a colour and *click* - it's a house!Something I'd like to see added - since it's still in Early Access - is if there would be a bit more life and movement in the towns you create. Perhaps people moving in to the houses and walking around the streets. And that you could hold and drag left-click to create a row of buildings. But those are just small things I thought about, overall I'm very happy I bought this.In summary - a mesmerizing game, allowing you to easily and forgivingly create your own towns in a European character. I can't do anything else than recommend it. To the creator - riktigt bra jobbat!

_childDocuments_.review: A simple game, or toy, that is reminiscent of building legos, lincoln logs, or tinker toys in a way. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It was worth all the pennies it cost me ( 6.00$ CAN ) Simple, intuitive design. Minimalist UI that lets all the space to your creativity. I'm stuck in a positive spiral where I need to recreate all sorts of things, cities, buildings, landscape I saw or remember in Townscaper. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It has a lot of potential;Like many other reviewers, I too am a DM for a Dungeon & Dragons game. This program, in my opinion, has a lot of potential to be the settlement builder we're all after. Between the simplicity of usage, as well as the flexibility of the camera angles, this game could be, well, game-breaking, if it just had a few more options. Personally, I'd like to see:- Larger grid sizes, for large cities- Terrain options, such as grass vs water map, eventual build up of mountains (such as how houses build into towers) with grass to hills, to mountains- Themes! Typical fantasy, themes inspired by cultures around the world, etc. - More customizability; perhaps the option to choose what time of day you're viewing your settlement at? Options for what misc. items pop up?- Ability to export your map when you're done?Honestly, I feel as though this program has so much potential. A few updates and QOL changes, and this could be something truly amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: After an hour of mucking around, i can think of a few things that this game could make use of.-Ability to select whether you want to build the bottom level higher or if you want to place buildings. And maybe different styles of "walkway", like say, one without handrails so you can make a harbor or something-A tool to paint over whether you want something to be pathways or rooftops, and maybe the specific rooftop you want. Also, rooftop colors.-Option to recolor a placed building (unless I missed that, in which case maybe point out where to view the controls)-Different background options/maybe the ability to make a town that looks like its on land/coastal.-Move camera rotation off of left click so we can paint houses like in the trailer-Grid that is more symmetrical, maybe multiple grids for different patterns-Boats? If I can think of any other additions I will edit my review. I think this is a great product and I could see people using this to do all sorts of things once it receives more features,
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper is a very good game, with a lot of potential. First of all, it is meant for free building, for those with a lot of imagination, don't expect a lot of action, just let your mind be free. You can design almost everything. The graphics aren't very demanding but they look insane. The gameplay is also very good, the game isn't buggy or too crashy. Keep in mind that the game is in Beta and updates are expected. The price is also very good ( 5$ ).My suggestions for the future updates : Make the game moddable ( Very IMPORTANT )Make a day/night cycle.Add some people or animals on the street, make a population count. That'd be more fun.Add roads, cars and more...Add natural disastersMake the game multiplayerAdd more materials, texturesAdd seasons
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little relaxing building exerciseIf you want to walk around your town in first personYou can export the OBJ of what you build, put it into blender, scale it (around 4-or-so times the exported size), then enable walk with Shift+Tilde(~) and press G to enable gravity.play around with the lights in the scene to add some mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: Less a game and more of a proof of concept as of now, but the mechanics are incredibly fun, satisfying, and creatively stimulating! I personally would like to see this game's ideas expanded to incorporate other base-building elements. Maybe a terrain editing system to help you craft the land and see with-which you can then build your town? Also I would love to see more of an extrinsic motivation to keep playing. For example, implement actual villagers or some type of population system, where you can house and employ citizens to perform basic tasks, and really get your town feeling alive! All in all, its a great concept that is already very polished and satisfying right now. I look forward to seeing what the developer does with it next!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I'm no artist, I've dabbled in 3D and game-design, so don't be discouraged that this is a game meant for artists.This game is simple, and by far one of the easiest to understand games I've played in a very long while. It makes you feel good, *really* good, by just clicking. It's a game that lets you be creative and think, without having to stress over anything. Something doesn't end up looking right? Then delete it and try something else. It's so stimulating and satisfying for something so absurdly simple and charming and I absolutely adore it. I've been building towns, pixelart, and experimenting and pushing the procedural buildings to their limits in a game that has so much potential you can't help but be on the lookout for what's next in this gameIt may not look or seem like a $6 game, but considering that there are plans for so many new features in the future, and with the dev being so supportive of this project, it's worth every penny.Regardless, it's very relaxing nonetheless, this is one of the few games my boomer parents actually approve of and I legitimately enjoy messing around with it and seeing what I can create, seriously looking forward to what the developer has in store for the future!8/10 - A little shallow, but hoping for more depth later down the road
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool. I wasn't really expecting to be so sucked into a game where there's no actual "gameplay loop" as such, but the mere act of placing buildings and creating intricate multilayered megastructures was so satisfying I managed to play for about an hour without even noticing the time go by. I could imagine lots of little stories about grand adventures that the hypothetical citizens of my city could have, and the history of the place. I hope this game has more features added in future, such as the ability to make gardens and green spaces without having them walled off by buildings, and a sort of "challenge mode" where little AI townspeople roam around as you build outwards completing various tasks, and figuring out the most efficient routes to and from places that incentivize you to plan smart would be awesome. 10/10 as a proof of concept and I hope it gets more work done on it!
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those casual, minimalistic, "feel-good and relax" games, one which despite having rather simple gameplay mechanics manages to be quite enchanting and addictive, constantly tempting one's creativity to indulge into further experiments and creations. Despite being sand-box with no achievements or challenges per se, the satisfaction factor of one's own creation is nevertheless high, provided one is into such types of games of course. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: See this game as a meal at a restaurant or a nice treat you bought to reward yourself. _childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could think of a way to describe this that would sell it more than what you can already see. Remember the first time you discovered paint on windows as a child and became totally absorbed in making random patterns by messing with the functions just because you could? Then this is for you.If you are expecting any kind of game then look elsewhere this is purely self absorbed aesthetics. But it does it so well.And now it has positional sun locations :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell this game (if you want to call it that) is still a little rough around the edges, but it has massive potential and is already as addictive as it is soothing. I was having a pretty rough day, sank a couple hours into Townscaper, and it really helped to calm my mind and bring me a little bit of peace so I could get some rest.The visuals are simplistic but elegant, like a watercolor painting. The choice to not add music was surprising but I can respect the decision and see the merit behind it. Perhaps some other sound effects; seabirds and rolling waves on the shore, maybe some rain or thunder could add to that ambiance without upsetting the mood.The controls take a hot second to figure out because there's no keyboard guide, and there's no long click to fill or drag to make building any faster, just endless clicking. There's no black or grey buildings, and different colors are different buildings, so you can't really blend them together to make that nice iconic red and white lighthouse. I haven't figured out how the zoom or paths quite work yet either. I'd love to see some different roofing and path types, maybe a few more embellishments like a docked boat, expanded shorelines, simple things like that.Overall this is a very impressive and fun little building tool and I'm excited to see how it evolves.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing to just boot up and mess about in for a few hours at a time. Let that creativity flow free and make anything from small shanty towns to a large palace looming over the township. Or flying towns, for that matter. Certainly usable to design towns for pen & paper RPGs, although a bit limited when it comes to anything more than layout.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: It's the most literal example you can get of a sandbox. Just build your little towns on a randomly generated grid with a handful of colors to choose from. That's it. No resources, no people, nothing to keep track of. And I  that.I can only think of like, 3 things that I'd want changed/added.1: The option for non-random/standard grids. I personally like being able to utilize symmetry, and symmetrical islands are next to impossible to find.2. Custom building palettes. Apparently folks figured out how to change colors through file editing, but it's odd that it isn't a feature.3. Different environments/cultural designs. I love the look of the buildings, but other "skins" would be nice.But as of writing this, sounds like the dev is done with this project. He made what he wanted to make. Which, hey, good for him, I guess.My one warning is that this game  isn't worth 6 dollars, even if I was happy to dish out the couple bucks for it. If you're actually looking for a game, keep looking or wait for a sale. But if you're like me and enjoy chill little time wasters, I  think you'll like Townscaper.OH and you can 3D print your towns, apparently. I think that's really neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.name: Townscaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something special, there's no objective, there's no tutorial and there's no ending.Townscaper is strange, it is so relaxing and satisfying, you build a small town from the ground up and that's it. Nothing more, nothing less. The randomised grid makes building interesting looking towns easy and it works like a charm. This game is clearly unfinished though, the lack of music makes it slightly unnerving and without any objectives at all, the game has no real replayability. The randomised grid makes it hard to recreate something from an image or imagination, and the lack of customisability on each "block" makes it so your towns end up looking very similar.If you are looking for a game to create detailed towns from referances, as of now, I cannot recommend this game. However, this game is very relaxing and is very fun to watch your towns develop, it lets your imagination flow. I have had fun with this game and I look forward to seeing what it turns into in the future. As of now, I don't think you should buy this game for its price unless you really do want to chill, but in the future, I'd say this is a great game to pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend playing this game and I feel like I got my money worth for how inexpensive this game is, however, I do wish there was even more to this game that would get updates in the future.I haven't played a lot of this game, since I played it during troubles with my internet, but I do intend to come back to his game and chill out working on creativity practice. I still got a lot on what I want to do, even getting into modifications to the game as to make and have different textures for different looks/themes. For example, having a more winter season to the builds I make. This game is mainly just a tech demo proof of concept type work, which is pretty well implemented rather than explicitly saying "this is a tech demo" with only basic textures that has no character to it.Also, I know this game is described as a toy. But I call it a game due to what I consider, and what a lot others consider, a game is. Some people had complained to me about my choice of words when describing this game, but they don't seem to understand I consider a game as anything digital displayed on a monitor display where the user is interacting with the medium. Legit, some of you need to calm down because I decide to use a word to describe this product. Before I get into this section, I'm happy with the game and I want to see the best for what this game has to offer. This is why I have criticisms of this game, so that maybe updates can come out in the future for improving the game.What I would like to see out of this game is more updates to it. There is a lot of support for this game and I would love to see the base game get more features for it to be better fleshed out. Like I said before, this is basically a tech demo and it will still have a lot of work I personally view as unfinished for it to be considered as a fully finished game. The asking price of this game is $6, which I do think is a bit too high considering this is literally just a tech demo. I would say the better price should be $3 - $4 for what you are getting in this game. I know some may say "why would it matter if it is a couple dollars less, it's not all that expensive at $6 anyway", to which I say, you are wrong. I care about the value of the game, this being the quality and quantity of content in the game relative to the asking price. Despite the content being great quality, there truthfully isn't much for this game to ask $6 out of me. Which thankfully I got this on the Steam Summer sale for a cheaper price more close to what I would pay for this game.If there were more features to this game, of the same great quality, I can see myself paying $6 - $10 if you added some more quality content. In fact, if you fully developed this game to be larger than it is now, I can see myself paying up to $15 for this game. However, the tech demo that it is now just doesn't seem worth the asking price of $6.Let me start off saying this, if they want to live up to the $6 asking price, they should have better modification integration for this game. This game doesn't seem to get any updates, but this one is a must if you want to meet up to the asking price and then just do nothing after that. I really don't want to have to deal with 3rd parties modifying the game as to make this game have all or most of the features I'd like to have.In no particular order, here is a list of updates I'd like to seer:I think this game was worth the money I had paid for, especially since I got it on the Steam Summer Sale. It is a fun game and I see myself playing it for more hours to come. I like to use this game to use during some downtime and for when I want to relax at the end of the day. However, it isn't without criticisms and I would like to see the best for the future of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Who would have thought such a simple concept could prove so beautiful, and so fun? The simplicity of placing down foundation, of setting down the building blocks that form houses, to see the streets appear, gardens, birds, and all the tiny little details, all that appear as if my imagination had been unleashed with magic. I find myself making castles, arches, avenues, winding climbs in between buildings, towers and platforms. When I discovered how to make a crane appear under a building I gasped to myself; such inventive detail on the behalf of the maker of this little game. All the little things you can achieve by simple experimentation, and as you understand how the various details can be achieved, you begin to shape your little world, your village, town, or whatever else you construct. Townscaper gives you simple building blocks which allows you to create masterpieces; from the basic and realistic, to the absurdly fantastic and imaginary. If only I could populate the town with tiny people; that is my one yearning for this game. They need not be much more advanced than the birds, in appearance, but tiny people walking the streets, fading in and out through the doors, or stopping next to each other as if in conversation, if even only briefly. I wish there were tiny people.. That, however, is such a minor issue, when the product and execution of a concept has been so brilliantly executed. I can hardly believe this is something still in development and not something already a finished, little gem of a product. If dice had numbers greater than 6, this would have that score. 6+ on a die of 1d6.

_childDocuments_.review: "Townscaper" is a wonderfully relaxing game that I’d definitely recommend for anyone looking to unwind and unleash their creativity. The gameplay is incredibly straightforward: you simply click on building tiles, and the game’s AI takes care of the rest, constructing charming and unique townscapes with a few simple clicks.What sets "Townscaper" apart is its serene and intuitive design. There are no complex rules or objectives—just a calming, almost meditative experience where you can create beautiful, intricate towns at your own pace. The game's visual style is vibrant and appealing, with a lovely aesthetic that brings each building and town to life.It's a perfect game for those who enjoy creative expression without the pressure of deadlines or scores. Whether you’re designing a quaint village, a bustling city, or an abstract masterpiece, "Townscaper" provides a satisfying and enjoyable outlet for your imagination.Overall, "Townscaper" is a delightful and soothing game that's easy to get into and hard to put down. It’s a great choice for anyone in need of a relaxing and creatively fulfilling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I thought this game was just placing houses next to each other and enjoying the simplicity of that but there is a lot more to it than one might think at first sight.The randomized alignment grid of rectangles, pentagons and hexagons is an interesting feature that forces you to improvise and to embrace asymmetric building. The game offers a multitude of connectors that spawn in depending on the building blocks' relative positions to each other which are a lot of fun to experiment with. The graphics are - while comic-like - surprisingly beautiful featuring many small details around the houses aswell as little animations when placing or removing blocks.I wholeheartedly recommend Townscraper as a unique experience to any fan of citybuilder games whether you are going to spend two hours or two hundred in it.
