_childDocuments_.review: First, a video reviewStreaming the game Broken Pieces is the debut of the French studio, which, with the efforts of five people, released a game presented as a psychological thriller. The trailers of Broken Pieces have been compared to just about everything. And with Silent Hill, and Syberia, and even traces of Life is Strange were found. Elisa, a woman in her thirties, and her husband Pierre, who is a fan of music and instruments for performing it, heard about the town of Saint-Eggsil on television. Love at first sight, a spark in their hearts - and they decided to move closer to the sea. They bought a big and cozy house, but battered by time and sea salt. It is our fortress for the rest of the game. The prototype of St. Agesil was the French region of Brittany.Happiness and intoxicating freedom did not last long. Something lurked in the region's waters. A Lovecraftian ancient horror, a scientifically explainable anomaly, a UFO base, or something else - in general, a signal emanating from the bottom interested the competent persons and a group of sectarians. As the doctrine of the leader says, there is an ancient deity in the waters, and the time has come to pay the bill for their sins. Aggressive citizens began defacing city property, desecrating graves, and performing mystical rituals.And then, in the spring of 1993, the military conducts an operation after which everything changes. The plot begins with Eliza's dream and awakening. Walking around the house, we go outside - and there's no one there. The heroine finds herself in a kind of bubble, locked in time and space. It is always April 3, and only insignificant things change from day to day. For example, fluorescent mushrooms grow and shrimp appear in fishing nets.Before starting the game asks whether to pass as intended by the developers or choose a simplified combat mode. The essence of this proposal becomes clear later, but it's done, you can not change anything. Ghost battles are disgustingly implemented and annoying, at least when playing with a keyboard and mouse, although the developers again recommend using a gamepad. It is very interesting how this idea came to someone's mind, given the genre of Broken Pieces. A lot of ammunition is not going to scrap, and Eliza dodges like a cripple, although she seems to be a young and agile woman. Also trains in the yard. As a result, by the end of the game, when the fighting gets more fierce, poorly drawn spirits can seriously hurt. Eliza's skill at driving enemies away saves her a little. Weapons, hits and all that sort of thing called impaction certainly don't feel like it, it's out of the question. Totally unnecessary and annoying mechanics. Broken Pieces comes out just in time. Exploring coastal Brittany in the fall is like taking a little trip filled with secrets, beautiful architecture, and uncomplicated riddles.PLUSES +++. Charming coastal townCharming protagonist with a pleasant voiceExploring Saint-Egzil and solving riddles doesn't bore you to the end of the walkthroughThe ending is abrupt, despite the completion of the general task. The ending is so clumsy that it sweeps you off your feet with its directness and leaves you with an understatement. The effect of surprise is revealed through the excessive simplicity of the final episode. MINUSES --Horrible combat systemPerhaps a little too chambery.Questionable ending Score 7 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing gaming experience in all aspects. I wanted to share my thought even before finishing the game, but I finally finished it recently. This is a classic silent hill or resident evil like game, with some very interesting additions. The game has an amazing storyline and plot which makes you feel lonely some times but it enhances this way the whole experience. It's like living the life of the character you play totally. There's a lot of mystery and the story is very well thought out and meticulously made. The cameras used are really outstanding. They give you the old good vibes of silent hill aspects but with even more dynamic views where you can control the the cameras and even see from a first person perspective, something really useful with some puzzle solving and to get into the mood of the atmosphere. The sounds is phenomenal, maybe one of the best I have experienced with games and it is adapted perfectly to the different viewing angles! Some sound-based puzzles are unique too! Speaking of puzzles, I found them really interesting! I had so long to experience something so unique puzzle-wise. The mini games are very interesting too! I solved all of them and I really enjoyed them! I finished the game without any guide. I stuck several times, but I found solving those puzzles myself very satisfying and rewarding! To me this is a masterpiece, and taking into account the fact that is made by a new gaming studio, this is a very brave and pationet attempt! I was impressed with medium quite a long ago, but to be honest it felt too brief and the gameplay was very naive comparing to this one in al aspects. I believe Elseware Experience deserved to make the next Silent Hill games or remakes more than Bloober Team. Of course this is just a personal opinion, but that's what I believe. I'm looking forward to the next creation of Elseware Experience. If you are a fan of Resident Evil or Silent Hill series, I believe you have to give it a try! It won't disappoint you!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh wow, I did not expect that this game would be such a great experience. I mean seriously, how a team of 5 people create such a deep and interesting story, detailed worlds, fantastic soundtrack, and diversified gameplay that does not let you get bored. It has a healthy mix of world exploration, storytelling, puzzles and side games, and survival / combat. Survival and combat while being present in the game is not the core experience, so don't expect something like RE or Us and Them experience from this game. I'd draw parallels with Alone in the Dark games in some sense. Voice over is great, the heroine has a lot to say about everything around her and never repeats herself. Music is fantastic as I already said and the addition of audio cassettes that you can find in various places with more music tracks to listen adds even more depth. Once I started the game I was instantly "sucked" in and sunk another 12 hours into it just that night. Wow, just wow, one of the best puzzle/adventure/survival games I've played lately. I totally recommend it, so underrated.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. But it has a few "little" flaws that i would like to address here. (Spoilers)Fighting:This system is the thing that is most annoying (for me)While aiming you can not move at all. Running from the enemies makes no sense, since you are always fighting in a little arena. You are forced to fight. Fighting boils down to: Aim, shoot, dodge (too tricky) or push the enemies away, repeat. Hoping you will not die in the process.This system feels not finished at all. If you want more fun with this game, just go for the "lower" difficulty without fighting. Just enjoy the story. Navigation:You have no map. Well yes, i am not using am map in my city...but in this game, where every transition between "maps" costs you ingame time, i would wish to have an ingame map. Sometimes i forget the right way or where i have to go at all. This is rather painfull.Changing the season: You can change the season at some point in the game. At first i though of it as a nice new feature...but basically you can only decide if you want frozen water or low/high tides...thats all. Other than than you get a few new obstacles. Elise can not open several doors. bacause there is a liitle bit of snow behind the door ;)Ground hog day:You can expect to encounter fights AT THE SAME PLACES. Over and over again. It is okay at first...but it gets annoying after a while. I need to go home to sleep or to heal and i have to pass a certain area to go there - BOOM. Enemies are attacking!What i like about this game:The graphics: Everything looks nice. It feels like the developers really wanted to build a nice looking village and put a lot of effort into it. Having to watch the clock:It builds a little pressure if you change places and this takes time. If you do not look after the time you might encounter problems later. This is something if have not seen in other games like that.A female Character:Yes this is nice. And in this game it does not feel like the "This has to be a girl" type of thing. She is a believable character for this game. Just for the protocol: I am a man.Environmental puzzles:Besides the fact, that some features do not make sense to me, i like the idea that you have to "interact" with the environment to solve a few puzzles. May it be by using her powers of else. Her diary and hew cassette player:The only game i remember where you can collect cassettes to listen to on the go. Hearing Elises thought about her experiences is surely a nice idea.Overall a nice game with some cool ideas that need a little more work.Dont get me wrong, this is not silent hill and definately no resident evil. At first i expected something alike, but this game goes its own way and that is ok. If you want a cool looking village at the french coast, while exploring a lot of places, solving puzzles and try to find out what is happenig for a few evenings, then this might be for you.But it would wish that the devs would bring back the demo so you can get a first impressing of what is awaiting you.

PROS:1. the game has a list of constantly changing objectives which is very helpful staying focused. 2. there is some shooting involved, but this is the first game i played that has a fabulous setting to make combat easy. and it really did!  aiming and shooting was simple and successful 100% of the time, although there doesn't have to be much shooting involved at all, if you follow the rules for avoiding bad things.3. although it was not an easy game for me, i kept coming back to it and got a lot of satisfaction completing tasks, even when i had to use the walkthrough (which was almost always). 4. real nice graphics and appropriate music. 5. a lot of work was put in developing this game i think. so all that being said, i definitely recommend the game! most of you are better at solving and figuring stuff out, so i'm sure would finish much sooner than i did with less assistance needed. i don't think my experience would necessarily be yours in this game.i was happy to finish it, and i think i know what happens, but i'm not really sure. so i'll check the discussions or youtubes. i think you'll like it in spite of my cons. i give it 4 stars out of 5, but a little too hard figuring out what to do for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, atmospheric puzzle game ala Silent Hill. The biggest (and imo really the only) issue is the combat; very lackluster and fincky. However, there is an option to 'reduce combat' so that you can focus on puzzles and narrative; I recommend taking this option as you'll probably just be frustrated with the combat mechanics.Outside of that, this game has a fantastic original score and is quite pretty. The story is a bit ambiguous but it unravels very well, primarily through audio tapes you find around the levels. There are some very fun side-quest puzzles and plenty to explore. Not so much scary as it is surreal, but very dark vibes. Overall, I definitely recommend if you like classic Metroidvania-style puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but also far from being great.This is clearly a game in which the developers have put a lot of attention to detail and the fixed camera works perfectly. Graphics are really good and its fun to explore the coastal town. But again, it's not a great game by any means and really close to a thumbs down.The story is The game overwhelms you with 4 different plot lines that seem impossible to fit into a coherent story.It takes around 4 hours until you start to see the connections between all these different plot lines and even then it's still messy.The rushed ending does not help.While the developers spent lot's of time designing various side activities and items, the main quest is basically a loop of using the same three items, solving the same environment puzzles and lots of backtracking. Combat feels totally out of place, it's like once they had already finished the game someone had the idea to include a bit of shooting to appeal to the RE fanbase.I really hope the developers use the experience they gained with Broken Pieces to create another fixed camera survival horror / adventure game. But please, ditch the story, make the combat feel less out of place and include a bit more variety with the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: I am recommending this game to anyone who likes survival horror or adventure games especially from the PS1/PS2 generations but with some big caveats. If you go into this game with the proper expectations you will get much more out of it than I did...First and foremost I would recommend Reduced Combat difficulty, because the combat in this game is easily it's weakest feature. The enemies are not fun or engaging to fight on top of the fact that you get an ability that can one shot entire groups anyway AND the strangest feature is the infinite ammo. In survival horror games especially, combat is a strategic trading of resources. When the enemies are random, infinite to a certain degree, and you don't need to worry about resource management, the combat needs to just be fun, and here it is absolute butt cheeks. Then get ready for copious amounts of meaningless backtracking in the second half of the game, to solve some of the lamest puzzles I've ever seen in the genre. Because of the open ended nature of the level design, you can never tell what is needed for progression and what is optional and because so much is left out of the character's journal you will feel lost even when you have already come across all the information you need to progress. Compounding this issue is the fact that you can solve several puzzles needed for late game, even endgame progression near the beginning so you will be even more confused on how to solve the related puzzles later in the game. For more open ended, exploratory level design, it's important to provide context to the player for key items, i.e. flavor text/character dialogue that let's you know whether or not something is useful now. One example is a key you can get near the beginning, needed to obtain one of the final key items of the game. You can get it whenever you want to, and there are doors that remain locked the entirety of the game that you will actually never be able to open. But you may try when you come across keys like this one. What makes this worse is that there are doors you WILL find, even in the starting areas that you can't even interact with. So the developers were not consistent enough in this regard and it will add to the confusion. All of these thing made EVEN worse because you can solve puzzles and certain story elements out of order, as is intended, but when you throw in all these other issues it makes for an overall bad experience imo.The best things this game has going for it are it's incredible atmosphere, sound design, and OST. The music, especially the cassettes you can listen to whenever you want to, are wonderful and honestly the most fun parts of the game are when you're exploring the streets with one of these playing and just soaking up the atmosphere. It's truly wonderful, and almost makes the game worth it's price point on its own. The story also started as one of the most intriguing mysteries I'd seen in an indie game in quite some time, but as I started to suspect after the halfway point, the payoff is almost non-existent. Even with every document, and cassette available to you, there isn't enough to make the ending worth the journey. But to reference the atmosphere and music again, the journey alone may be enough.To conclude, get this on sale, play on the reduced combat difficulty, and focus on the tone, music, sound design, atmosphere, and exploration, and if you can become immersed in this world, you may find some magic in it. But no matter what kind of games you like, I cannot recommend this game at full price to anyone. Don't let my played time at the time of writing this fool you. At least a third of that was spent doing optional stuff (which will not help you in the reduced combat difficulty) and getting lost in a game with unintuitive level design that also doesn't have a map. Not all games should have a map. This game severely needs a map and these developers honestly should've known better.One last thing... for added immersion, play with French audio and English subtitles. I think this is probably the best way to experience the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting game with a good difficulty level, ultimately undone by a weak ending. I grew up playing point and click adventure games and puzzle games, and I enjoyed the nostalgic gameplay of "running around, finding secret codes and necessary items." The shortcuts between areas helped with this quite a lot.The story hinges on a mystery, though, and it's a bit of a slap when the storyline neither advances nor clarifies any of that mystery. I didn't feel any more enlightened at the end of the game than at the beginning. Edit: After a patch with a short clarifying scene at the end of the game, I've changed my review from negative to positive. I'm still confused about some aspects of the story, but I appreciate the devs listening to player feedback and adding context. Making a video game is a really, really hard thing to do, and Broken Pieces is likely to be a solid experience for people who enjoy adventure/puzzle games. (And maybe I'm just picky when it comes to narrative.)Pros:-beautiful scenes-finding tapes and playing the music you like was a neat angle-weird and interesting supernatural mystery-the combat and daytime limits add a feeling of tension to the gameCons:-some resolution at the end, but still a lot of mystery (some players may not consider this a con--I admit I'm the kind of person who likes to know "what really happened" at the end)-occasional frustrating bits of running back and forth-limited inventory space adds difficulty but not much fun

_childDocuments_.review: As more and more classic survival horror adjacent action adventure games arrive lately, I keep being occasionally pleasantly surprised by the inventiveness of some of the projects. Even if the title ultimately disappoints, the creativity behind it can show new ways this genre can be done, as if it’s finally trying to break the mould it has been stuck in for decades. Broken Pieces is not a disappointment, however, even if it is a bit of a mess.This is an action adventure with a sci-fi/eldritch horror story twist elements and very light, but impactful, survival concepts. It plays as a third person perspective game with fixed camera angles, although each angle is actually 2 angles you can switch between at will with a press of a button. The character controls are handled with camera-relative/directional controls, so those who have an allergy of tank controls need not worry. You get the typical for the genre item collection and usage, puzzles and mini-games, some of which are optional, and combat. Combat here is quite poor, but I have to credit the developers for seemingly basing it on Parasite Eve 2, which is a great example to follow. Sadly, this has none of the tightness and nuance of PE2 and controls very awkwardly and some of the later game (and optional) challenge fights are stupid. Also stupid is the fact that combat is basically partially random and pops up like a jRPG random encounter. There are fights that seem required and somewhat consistent, but a lot of the others can not happen or have a completely unpredictable amount of enemies.What makes these base mechanics interesting is the attempt to set it all on a concept of a daily schedule and light survival features. Essentially, you have a timer and once you wake up in the morning you have until 20:00 each day to do whatever you plan before it gets too dangerous and you need to go home and sleep. Traveling between major locations takes time (that is shown above the door that takes you there), so you have to be careful about where you are as the deadline gets closer. Crafting resources that you’ve found during the day can be put into the item box and will turn into resources you can use in the morning. It’s extremely basic and really is all about higher damage limited ammo type for combat apart from rare moments when you run out of space in your inventory and decide to backtrack home instead of dropping items. But it does set up a very cool pattern where you plan your day and follow certain simple rituals.It’s also neat that many of the things you get are optional, a lot of things can be done out of order (though there is an “optimal” way to play) and there’s a genuine sense of discovery as you learn more and more about the strange situation the main character has found herself in. The conclusion to this whole story is underwhelming, have to say, and the developers are seemingly busy with thinking of a follow up already, but there’s enough interesting stuff here already to be fun. Even if the English translation (the game is originally French) is problematic at times.Speaking of problematic – some of the poor design choices in the game stand out especially well in contrast to how many cool things are in the game. One optional mini-game is extremely unfun, some of the puzzles are more of a busywork thing than a fun challenge. One optional challenge puzzle, for example, is extremely poorly designed and on top of it you can do it incorrectly, but the game has no way of telling you that you’ve failed or providing you with a restart option. So you must realize what happened and load the last save to undo the situation. And the whole fixed camera gimmick hurts the game far more than it helps, as more often than not you won’t see stuff that you should be able to see, unless you enter the first person mode, which shouldn’t be a requirement since your “puzzle” here is “we designed the camera system really badly and you must suffer for it” and it feels.Still, I have to say that despite many frustrating elements, Broken Pieces has left me inspired. It’s full of cool ideas, some of which are implemented well, and it tries to do something fresh and new out of something old and familiar. Instead of just following trends or copying formulas that have worked for decades by the numbers. I recommend checking out the game, though if your patience with crappy combat is lower than mine, you can set the difficulty to disable lots of that. The game won’t become a smooth experience, but it’s an experience still worth having.

_childDocuments_.review: If the game looks interesting to you, I'd say grab it and give it a shot.As someone that grew up in the area of Resident Evil and Dino Crisis, I love the attention to atmopshere and the style of control. It captures much of the feel without the frustration of the old tank controls. Rather than survival-horror, I would describe it more as a mystery -- why is everyone gone, what's the deal with the lighthouse, the cult, and the attack, and so on.The story is mainly told through documents and tapes you encounter along the way, not pushed very heavily beyond progression. Puzzles are doable if you find the clues and search all over. Combat is relatively easy and most of the time you can explore safely unlike classic survival/horror. If you're not content to explorer and unearth the mystery, you'll be bored; if you like exploration or find yourself wanting to know what Elise's story is then you'll enjoy the game.For a small team, I think the game was excellently done in terms of quality work. Especially nice attention to details. I especially love how Elise wears headphones when listening to tapes :D. The developers seem to be making an effort to support the game (at time of release), and the game is pretty stable for me. The worst thing that I can say about the game is that it feels a little dull, like there should be more action as part of the game play or more to drive you forward than there is. Honestly, I hope they make more games in the future because I'm sure they would be worth playing.Personally, the only thing I can complain about is having to bait seagulls and crows with food when the character has a handgun. But at least no animals were harmed, or turned into emergency rations, in the course of this game. I like the more laid back approach and the adventure style of game more than the old survival horrors, so for me it was fun if not exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay was satisfying and the puzzles were not overly difficult but felt rewarding to complete. The combat was a little difficult to get a hang of, but 1) it wasn't specifically difficult just a little clunky at times 2) you could choose to play without combat as an option, and 3) once I thought of the combat as resource puzzles to be solved it felt like it made more sense. Overall, worth the time to play, and I hope there's more to come!

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked Broken Pieces.The game is really nice and the story is great to follow. It's a bit cryptic at first but you discover all the elements as you go along.- The sound design and the musical atmosphere are really cool. There is no music as such but you use a cassette player to listen to music whenever you want. But above all there are narrative tapes to listen to in order to understand what's going on, there were many details hidden in the tapes.- The graphics: the game is very pretty and the setting is a bit different from many other games as it takes place in France. It's impressive especially when you see that it's made by a small team.- Level Design: I liked the fact that the levels are connected to each other and that you can unlock a lot of different paths and accesses. You often discover little hidden things and there are lots of bonus levels to do too.- The puzzles: Lots of interesting puzzles and there are several optional ones. Some were really hard but that was a bonus.I recommend this game which reminds me of the old point and click games or silent hill but in a modernized version. I find that you quickly get used to the changing of the camera etc.

_childDocuments_.review:
When Elise and her fiance decided to leave urban life and settle near the French coast, she could not imagine that she would end up completely alone.

Now, surrounded by strange phenomena in a dark, post-Cold War climate, Elise will have to investigate and unravel the mysteries surrounding the region of Saint-Exil, its ritualistic cult, and its lighthouse overlooking the coast.

Broken Pieces is an action-packed investigative and adventure video game set in France. The game puts you in the shoes of Elise, a woman in her thirties who finds herself in the village of Saint-Exil in an imaginary region reminiscent of Brittany. Following an unexplained paranormal phenomenon, Elise is stuck, completely alone and out of time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks great, and I'm convinced that the open world is a great idea for a racing game. With that being said, there are too many small and big gripes that keep Forza from being a great game.There is next to no progression. You unlock cars and races, sure. But what's the difference between one race and another one in this game? But what's the point of unlocking yet another car, when you get all types of cars including supercars very early in the game anyway? It's not like you can collect them all anyway, since some are hidden behind paid DLC and others behind achievements that would require you to devote your life to the game.The game wants to shower you with content, with a clear emphasis on quantity over quality. Some of that content is just plain unenjoyable (hello drift points!). But what's even worse is the constant paid DLC wall. I don't necessarily mind DLCs, when I don't get the feeling that they're being forced on me. When you're looking for another car to get in the game, the ones locked by paid DLC are there with the others. On the map, you have events appearing that are locked behind paid DLC. Even worse, you sometimes get unskippable video ads for paid DLC. I'm also slightly irritated by how the game also tries to force multiplayer down my throat.Finally, I want to stress two immersion-breaking issues. The first one is that the steering wheels in the cockpit view in game only turn 90° on either side (180° arc total). If you're playing with a steering wheel controller, there's no visual indication of how you are turning the wheel beyond those 90°. And yet turning your steering wheel further than 90° actually has an effect on how sharp a turn you're making. The second one is the broken sense of speed. The speedometer tells you that you're doing 180km/h on a small country road, and yet it looks like you're driving maybe 80km/h max. The speeds displayed are absolutely ludicrous, but it feels nowhere that fast.The final issue that I want to point out, though it is rather minor, is how corny and cringeworthy the dialogue is in this game.I'm still looking forward to trying FH5 to see how many of these issues have gotten better (or worse) because there is great potential in that game.

_childDocuments_.review: FH4 is the best arcade racing game. It has a lot content, great selection of cars, fun gameplay, good controls and physics.I'm extremely happy that Forza Horizon 4 is finally on Steam, I wanted to play this game for years. But xbox app was testing my patience.It's an open world racing game. I guess by cranking up the difficulty and realism settings you could bring it closer to sim-cade level, but mostly it's arcade, a fun one, where laws of physics still exist and different cars handle differently.A while ago when there were mainly arcade games on the market I always wanted more simulators or something arcade but which makes sense when it comes to handling. But then the age of simulators started. Sure they're fun, but they're tiring while Forza is relaxing in a way. Well, you can make it relaxing or challenging. It's the most fun racing game on the market.Car handling is awesome. The weight transfer physics work which is especially useful in dirt racing, you can drift which requires some effort unlike in other games. It's just that awesome feeling, fun and slightly realistic.Car selection is amazing. Everyone will find a car they adore. There are hundreds of cars, something like 700 maybe? Cars have classes and the selection is very diverse. From vintage cars to modern supercars, from regular road cars to rally cars or even trucks or vans. There are even Lego and hot Wheels cars. Just insane.Maybe one downside is that you get a bunch of cars really quickly so there's no sense of progression because you're being given the fastest cars in the first hours of the game. I prefer starting with regular cars and make my way up to earn faster, more expensive cars. Fortunately you can choose whatever car in exhibition races but still it lack progression.So you race in England. At first it's slightly confusing to drive on the wrong lane, of course you can drive however you like but still coming from other games like ETS2 it's a bit confusing, especially the roundabouts. Not in a bad way though.The map is huge and very diverse. Highways, dirt roads, small roads, forests, mountains, lakes, city, everything you want is there for you to explore. And exploring is fun. There are hidden barns and other collectables. While barns are fun, they give you a new car but other collectables are just there for the sake of...collectables. But again – not a bad thing, some of them are fun to find. One of the fun collectable types are beauty spots. You see a beautiful cut-scene of the area/object.The game revolves around competing in a festival. There are various challenges which give you rewards when you complete them. Most of the time you'll need to win races but there are other challenges, like speed traps where you must drive as fast as possible or the ones where you need to jump off a ramp and be in the air for as long as possible.But of course racing is the most important here and you have few types of races. Circuit racing, point A to B racing. But that's not all. There A to B races where you need to follow the road and there are ones where you just need to get to finish line as quick as possible by driving wherever you like, no rules. Team racing where one team competes against drivatar team or other players. There are also races against trains or planes. On top of that there are taxi missions. Which bring us to story events. Those are events/races with some story to it. They're fun and challenging and will keep you occupied for a while.Now multiplayer activities. Racing is obviously one of them but there's also capture the flag where you must carry the flag to destination and other team needs to stop you. Matches where infected team need to touch other cars to infect them. Protect the king matches which is similar. And the most surprising one – battle royale.There's also ranked play. It has stricter rules like you can't hit the walls because you get penalized.But it's not all multiplayer only. Amount of single player content is insane. You can choose to race solo on your chosen difficulty level, a coop race against drivatars and story missions.The game basically gives you a choice how you want to play it.You can customize your character and own a house, multiple houses which serve as your garage and home where you can tune your cars and your appearance.You can also tune your cars accordingly to race you're going to participate. Don't want that? Just download the setup straight from the game. You can apply liveries to your cars by creating your own where the only limit is your imagination or just download a livery.To get new stuff you spin a fortune wheel and rewards are ranging from money and clothes to some cool cars. You earn wheelspins by playing the game.You can drive anywhere, hit bushes, smaller trees, rocks, fences – the environment is destructible. But the best part are seasons. There're four seasons which change over time. Each season has its challenges to compete for you. And season changes could even change your driving. On winter it could be harder to drive but lakes are frozen so you can have fun on the lake. Seasons along with dynamic weather change the map drastically.This is one of the best looking games. Seasons change the map so much that it feels fresh each time. All the seasons are absolutely beautiful.Cars look amazing and they're all are fully modelled. You can look closely at every part of the car.Environments look great. Distant objects are lower quality but overall the game looks stunning.There's also a photo mode where you can take beautiful pictures. But I find most filters pretty poor so it's better to tune the colors by yourself.When the game looks that good I don't expect it to run smoothly. But this is probably the best performing game currently in my library. Runs on max graphics, 80-100fps, smooth as butter. I'm playing on 5800x, 2070s, 32GB @3440x1440.There's native ultrawide support. Although cut-scenes are cropped for some reason.It has a lot of loading screens so I suggest to install this to m.2 ssd. They're usually short, 3 to 15 seconds, but there are so many of them that it gets annoying. It's especially annoying in mp because everyone must wait until the slowest PC will load the game which could take 15 minutes. How fun is it to wait 15 minutes for a 5min race?I noticed many people complaining about stuttering cut-scenes. But cut-scenes are actually loading screens.One more minor annoying thing is unskippable voice when you open the map and there's something new on it. It tells you about new activities but after 20th time I just don't want to hear it anymore it's the most annoying thing in the whole game besides clueless online players.Sound design is perfect. Cars sound great, the festival site feels alive.There're radio stations so most people will find something to listen to but t lack a metal station.Overall an extremely good racing game for anyone who at least slightly enjoys racing games. It's great for everyone's taste due to plenty of different activities and modes to play.I suggest buying the ultimate edition. It only lacks two dlc's. Not at full price obviously.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimate Edition review.Great graphics, lots of stuff to do, fun online events/connectivity...you know what everyone says.But there's two things I cannot STAND. The menus and ui are horrible. My God. There's loads of important things buried between tabs, menus, and different shape and size boxes selecting just simple stuff. Played the game for 76 hours and never got used to the ui. Plus, passive notifications after you do something don't tell you enough information a lot of the time, which means you gotta go back into the menus. It actually drove me nuts. Probably the worst aspect of the game. Notifications are also very obtrusive (FH5 is slightly better though about the notifications but still needs improvement). The seconds thing is progression. It's cool to earn cars, but when you get a fast car early on, there's no reason to want/buy slower cars. You can do any event in almost any class car anyway. There's also no real story. There's a narrator here and there but it's extremely bland. There's events called "story" that each have about 8-10 separate things to do, but again, it's bland. What's worse, every single camera angle and panning Is. Exactly. The. Same. Both characters are in the exact same spot with the character who is talking to you conveniently has their back to you, probably as a way for the dev to save time/money so they don't have to do lipsync. However there was one "story" that was really fun and exciting to me. It involved going through a history of racing video games which was awesome. So basically it's just do stuff, get car. They try to spice it up a bit by added wheelspins and super wheelspins where you can earn cash, emotes, clothing, horns and of course more cars. But a lot of those wheelspins have some really terrible low value "prizes" too. One game that did both of these things right was The Crew 2. I know, a Ubi game. But the menu navigation, progression and notifications are spot on. And the game is still supported as of this review too. It may sound like I'm being too hard on the game but no, I had a lot of fun. I did every event, found every collectible and did the same for Fortune Valley and The Lego expansion. I bought at a discount for $35 plus the $3 dollar treasure map because I'm lazy. Got a lot of playtime on this one, however also consider I got The Crew 2 for just $10 on sale with the better ui on top and I played that for almost 60 hours with more event variety and plenty left to do, I'd go for either the base game of FH4 or The Crew 2.  -------------------------------Fortune Valley:Basically it's a much smaller map with the exact same event types and stories. For some reason I though there were going to be natural disasters in this one, but nope. -------------------------------Lego DLCAn even smaller map with much less to do. There's an excessive grind if you want to complete the Master Builder though. And the challenges are again, laid out poorly in a grid of I think 16*17. Oh my God is horrible. You always earn toward them even if they're not pinned but you can only pin one at a time which was annoying.  Also, there's no passive notifications during gameplay telling you how far you are in something you just triggered and maybe didn't know it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a fair few racing/driving games before this, but mainly old ones like Daytona USA and Ridge Racer. Hell, the newest one I played was Gran Turismo 4, which was on PS2! So to come from games like that to THIS... It hits different.It's surprisingly really well optimised, my outdated little GTX 970 can run the game perfectly smoothly at ~60fps on medium settings. It's visually stunning and captures the atmosphere of Great Britain brilliantly, and all the cars' models and materials look perfect. The radio music selections are great, although I mainly just stick to Horizon XS. The balance between fun and realism in controlling the cars is completely on-point. And of course, being a Forza Horizon game, it's open-world, so you can take everything at your own pace, do loads of cool stunts and tricks, practice drifts around corners, whatever the hell you want. Apparently the online multiplayer isn't as good, with lobby load-times being comparable to GTA Online, but I can't be arsed to do any of that anyway.This game has also frozen so damn much for me, I have 8GB RAM which isn't much, but the game shouldn't be freezing because of it when I'm on medium settings and have nothing else open. It has screwed me over a LOT, and is the main reasons I don't have more hours on the game. For a £54.99 game from 2018 I expect far better optimisation.If you love racing games, get this whenever you can (probably the standard edition, it's already pretty damn expensive as it is). If you're not too sure, probably wait for a sale. Wouldn't recommend getting Deluxe or Ultimate editions unless they're on a good discount, like 50% off or over.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 transports players to a stunningly crafted version of Great Britain, offering an exhilarating blend of breathtaking visuals, diverse landscapes, and an expansive open world that invites exploration. This installment of the acclaimed Forza series continues to push the boundaries of racing games with its vibrant environments and engaging gameplay.One of the standout features of Forza Horizon 4 is its dynamic seasons. Each season—spring, summer, autumn, and winter—transforms the world in visually striking ways and affects driving conditions, adding layers of strategy to races and events. For instance, winter brings snow and ice, making familiar roads feel entirely new, while autumn showcases stunning foliage that enhances the already picturesque settings. This seasonal change keeps the gameplay fresh and encourages players to return throughout the year.The car roster is as impressive as ever, featuring a wide range of vehicles from classic muscle cars to modern supercars, along with quirky options like vintage vans and off-road beasts. Each car feels distinct, and the handling is refined, offering a satisfying driving experience whether you're racing on a track or tearing through the countryside.The game’s progression system is rewarding, with plenty of events, challenges, and collectibles that keep you engaged. Horizon Festivals act as hubs for a variety of activities, including street races, off-road challenges, and seasonal events. The introduction of a shared world experience also enhances multiplayer interactions, allowing players to join friends or other racers seamlessly, making the world feel alive and interconnected.Visually, Forza Horizon 4 is a triumph. The graphics are stunning, with meticulously detailed cars and environments that reflect a vibrant, living world. The sound design is equally impressive, from the roaring engines to the ambient sounds of nature, further immersing players in the experience.However, some players may find the sheer number of events and challenges a bit overwhelming at first. The game offers an abundance of content, which can lead to a sense of decision paralysis.Overall, Forza Horizon 4 is a masterpiece in the racing genre. With its breathtaking visuals, engaging gameplay, and innovative seasonal mechanics, it sets a high bar for future titles. Whether you’re a racing enthusiast or a casual gamer, it’s a journey worth taking. Highly recommended for anyone looking to experience the thrill of open-world racing at its finest.

The music has been well picked, Horizon Pulse, Horizon Bass Arena, Horizon Block Party, Horizon XS, Hospital Records, Timeless FM, and LEGO Valley exclusive Radio Awesome are all amazing and bound to have something for everyone to listen to, or there's always the option to turn the in-game radio off and just enjoy the sound of your engine roaring in a race. Internet isn't required to play as Horizon Solo is the offline/single player option, but I highly recommend playing while connected to the internet and signed into XBOX Live, as most the best content is user created and you'll need internet and an XBOX Live profile to access it. Huge selection of cars to choose from, so pick your favorites and burn that rubber. happy gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: An Ordinary gamer's review:(TL;DR, Great game. Must have for the fans of Racing games. Has issues that need fixing. Nothing game breaking. Has Ads for Paid DLCs. Not cool.)The game itself is a 9/10. A fun offshoot than it's more serious Motorsport Counterpart. As of now I've clocked like 24 hours. And played enough to put an opinion out. First let's talk about the core mechanics. Solid. Fun. Every car feels different from another. Has more than 400 cars I believe. Beautiful graphics. Absolutely stunning. The Radio feature has unique songs to listen to while roaming around UK. Upgrading your vehicle is quite a tricky thing. Not every car drives the same. And also every higher level parts doesn't guarantee that your vehicle will perform better. It mostly depends on the Class mechanics. You can upgrade your vehicle to a specific class. if you max out your entry level car of A Class to S2 class, there's a high chance that it'll be out-classed by the other higher performance cars of the S2 Class. So be mindful about spending money on the max parts. All and all a very good experience for people who enjoyed the Forza Horizon series. Lots of races. Lots of cars. Lots of beautiful places to discover. And the best part are the 4 seasons. The whole map changes with the seasons. Well that sums up the Good.The Bad: Micro-stuttering like crazy. Even on beast rigs that put my ROG G15 laptop to shame. But when the stuttering subsides there's lots of fun to be had.The UgLy: Ads in a $60 game. You get ads suddenly after you load up into the world. This needs to stop. I got NBA 2K21 during the last Epic Free game thingy. But didn't install it only because of in game ads. We can let 2K slide with the ads. But not microsoft. This has to stop.

This is by far the best one out there—its atmosphere and map are on a completely different level. It won't be available in stores after December 2024 (possibly January 2025), so buy it now—you won't regret it! Playing with a controller is a must, and I highly recommend the PS5 DualSense for the best experience. Trust me, go for the Ultimate Edition—Fortune Island is absolutely amazing.If you check on Steam Database, there are still over 10,000 players online daily, which is almost as many as Horizon 5. And believe me, apart from the new cars, Horizon 4 is far superior to Horizon 5. The map and atmosphere in Horizon 4 are unmatched—seasons feel much more present. In Horizon 5, every season feels the same, with only a bit of rain in autumn or winter. The Mexico setting, which is mostly a vast desert in the game, is a huge mistake in my opinion. There’s no real city, just a few one-story buildings scattered around the map, and the highway is hardly worth mentioning.In summary: buy it now while it's on discount—it promises hundreds of hours of content.10/10UPDATE: (14th September): Horizon 4 currently has 25,000 active players, whereas Horizon 5 only has 15,000. _childDocuments_.review: Awesome game.This is what I would imagine an ideal open world street racer to be like lots of fun. I enjoy being able to just cruise around and drive where ever I want, the game feels kinda like a sequel to Midnight club and Test Drive Unlimited the location is set in Edinburgh Scotland which is nice and great to explore, the map is huge and the car selection is massive, there is so many different types of cars to choose from its crazy.The game play is quality, the cars handle nicely and the difficulty can be adjusted, The single player experience is excellent I never really run out of things to do, I enjoy being able to play multiplayer mode with my friends, it can be really fun with the various different modes, capture the flag and Infected are really good. I like all the different race events, searching for collectables is fun, doing side missions against the clock or stunt challenges etc can be cool and rewarding. Some times I find the race tracks can be a bit recycled or unorganised but to be honest its not really something that bothers me that much, I do think it would have been great if they added cops to the game kinda sucks that there isnt any.Something I should mention is that I had two problems with the game. The first issue I had was stuttering, to be fair it was mostly during cut scenes, I did notice it during game play and between transitions like when ever I finished a race event or when I was about to start one however I was able to fix this issue. It was kinda my own fault for not keeping my graphics card drivers up to date, as soon as I opened a tool on my computer called "Geforce Experience" I updated my video card drivers and this prity much fixed the issue for me. The game only stutters a little bit now before starting events but a part from that the game is smooth and runs great.The second problem was a crashing issue, basically the game would randomly close and go straight to desktop for no reason. This took me a while to actually get fixed it really gave me a headache trying to solve it. There was a lot of things mentioned by different sources such as: updating Windows to the latest version available, disabling my firewall and running the game as Admin then moving the game from my Hard drive to my Solid State drive etc. None of these worked. In the end one of my friends was able to figure out what the issue was and fix it for me. I had to change the Windows Sound depth on my computer to "24 Bit 44100 Hz" the settings I was using was 48000 Hz after I did this the game was no longer crashing and I was able to play it at max settings just fine with no more issues.Another thing that bugs me about the game is every time I load the game up it always brings up the Steam overlay then displays a web page asking me to link my Steam account with my Windows account which is not something I feel comfortable doing and there is no option to select NO so I always have to click the X icon to close the web page down some times it can be annoying it would be nice if the game stopped asking me. I was rather gutted when I ran into these problems but I am glad I was finally able to get the game working properly. Right now I think its one of the best racing games currently available. I would still totally recommend it just beware you may encounter some issues and have to fix them before you can play the game.Overall a fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best arcade racing game up to this date, with a beautiful open world that changes by each season and a huge amount of content. It can be enjoyed alone or online with other players. Online can be unlocked only after completing a series of races that serve as tutorial. There are many customization options for both your car and your sim, including clothes and emotes. No microtransactions, you can unlock all the stuff simply by racing, exploring and levelling up. There are some cars DLCs and a VIP membership that double your rewards and give you some exclusive stuff but honestly there is so much content in the base game that you won't feel the need to buy those. The rewards are pretty generous, with the wheel of fortune you can get rare items and super cars from the very beginning.Now the Steam version is unpolished. There is still some random stuttering and no support for impulse triggers on Xbox controllers, but hopefully these will be fixed soon. The biggest problem is the lack of cross-save between Steam and Xbox/Game Pass, which is awkward considering the game requires an Xbox Live account. It's something that Microsoft should immediately fix for all their games available on Steam. In any case the game is massively overpriced. I would only recommend it at a 50% discount or more and only if you're planning to get some DLCs too. If you want to play just the base game then Xbox Game Pass is a much convenient option, at least until Forza Horizon 5 comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is credited with being one of the best racing games of the past decade, featuring over 700 licensed vehicles and a dynamic weather system that is not conclusive to one season. Every Thursday - weekly - at 2:30PM GMT the season changes, altering the environment. These changes present the player with unique seasonal events and the ability to reach previously inaccessible parts of the map when lakes freeze over in the winter season.Forza Horizon 4 also features two DLC expansions: Fortune Island and LEGO Speed Champions based off LEGO's Speed Champions toyline. Each introduces a new map with distinct campaigns and a range of additional vehicles or Lego variations of existing vehicles.As of right now the only thing I would like to see within the game is a wider variety of music available through the in-game radio. I did initially have a problem loading into the event Super7 where it would simply crash my game - a problem other players reported having - but this appears to have since been fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4, Pure Racing Bliss.Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)Graphics and World Design: The visuals in Forza Horizon 4 are nothing short of breathtaking. The dynamic seasons change how the game looks and feels, providing a fresh experience each time you play. The attention to detail in the environment, from the lush countryside to the bustling cities, creates an immersive atmosphere. Whether you’re racing through autumn leaves or a snowy winter landscape, the graphics are consistently impressive.Gameplay:The gameplay is incredibly enjoyable, with a vast selection of cars and customization options that cater to all types of players. The driving mechanics feel responsive and satisfying, striking a balance between arcade fun and simulation realism. The diverse range of events, including races, challenges, and stunts, keeps the gameplay fresh. The introduction of the new "Forzathon" events adds a layer of community engagement and regular content updates.Multiplayer and Community: Forza Horizon 4 excels in its multiplayer mode, allowing you to race against friends or join online events with players from around the world. The shared world concept enhances the experience, making the game feel alive with other players driving around, completing challenges, and participating in seasonal events.Content and Longevity: With an expansive map, a plethora of cars, and continuous seasonal updates, Forza Horizon 4 offers hundreds of hours of gameplay. The inclusion of the Horizon Festival and various themed events provides motivation to keep returning, ensuring that players always have something new to experience.Performance: On PC, the game runs smoothly with customizable graphics settings that can accommodate a wide range of hardware. Whether you’re on a high-end rig or a more modest setup, you can expect a smooth gameplay experience with high frame rates.Negatives: While Forza Horizon 4 is an outstanding game, there are a few minor issues. Some players have noted that the AI can be inconsistent, occasionally making races feel unbalanced. Additionally, the in-game microtransactions have received criticism, though they are not necessary to enjoy the game fully.Conclusion: Forza Horizon 4 is a must-play for any racing game enthusiast. Its stunning graphics, varied gameplay, and strong community support make it one of the best entries in the racing genre. Whether you’re a casual player or a hardcore racing fan, this game offers something for everyone. If you’re looking for a vibrant, immersive racing experience, Forza Horizon 4 will not disappoint.Overall:Highly recommended for its engaging gameplay and beautiful world, with minor flaws that don’t overshadow its many strengths.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this review is mostly focused on the skepticism and bad reports on the Steam version of this game. Regarding the game itself, to put it short, it's as good as everyone has been saying it is. As one of the world's most casual racing fans, this is the most fun I've had in a non-kart racer since Need For Speed Underground 2. For the asking price (RM95 in Malaysia), it scratches the itch of every kind of racing game just enough, when all that ran through my head was "I want game to go vroom". This game definitely lets you go vroom and has been for 2+ years, and now that it's on Steam I can finally get in on that.First off, a lot of people have been complaining about the asking price. Again, it's RM95 in my country so I personally can't complain, I paid about that much for Gears 5 which I also loved but didn't get nearly as much playtime out of as this game seems to offer. Yes, you can pay tuppence for Xbox Game Pass and get full access to this game and many others. Yes, depending on your country, the asking price to buy this game outright here can be absurd for a game that came out in 2018. Whether or not it is worth fully owning the game on Steam is entirely up to you, the game doesn't seem to be any thinner for content since its original release and I personally justified it with Game Pass not being available in my country, my personal affinity for owning games as opposed to subscribing for access, as well as my subjective value for RM95. It's a big game that I was honestly ready to pay RM200+ for on Xbox One and nearly bought the console for it. I can't tell you what your money is worth, that is entirely for you to decide.With technical issues, the thing is there were some really silly hurdles to even get in the game. It didn't work right out of the gate, with the game refusing to launch no matter how many times I verified it. Some people reported turning off Steam Overlay worked, some said turning off Discord Overlay, some updated their drivers, turned off MSI Afterburner or RivaTuner, or even the Xbox app in Windows 10. My fix came from first turning off BitDefender, then ultimately deciding to exclude the Forza folder so I can keep my computer protected. It's 2021 and I still don't understand games not working with protection software, but here we are. The game runs flawlessly otherwise, and the Xbox Live integration works about as well as it did for Halo MCC and Gears 5 (honestly, Xbox Live has been a non-issue for me on PC since GFWL stopped being a thing, and even then it was never gamebreaking for me in the days of Gears 1, Fallout 3 and Street Fighter 4 so YMMV).A few hours into the game and now I'm running into absolute random crashes, with no clue as to what causes them other than them mostly happening if I dawdle in menus (i.e. pausing to go to the bathroom). The game freezes for about 20 seconds then closes to no fanfare or error message. Upon light investigation, I'm not the only person with this issue (even on the Microsoft Store version), but it doesn't seem prevalent enough to be a common widespread complaint.Regarding performance, I'm running an RTX 2060 Super with a Ryzen 7 3700x, and the 110fps I'm getting on 1080p Ultra feels warranted. There are slight microstutters which I understand are also somewhat common amongst users, but it's not frequent enough to be remotely annoying, and it mostly happens in transitions like the victory screen once you cross the finish line or when you start a new race. Honestly, it feels far more than I can possibly bargain for for how it looks (this game is probably my only reason to upgrade from a 24" 1080p monitor hah).So I don't know, there are people that complain for just about every game. All I'm able to tell you that with my personal regional pricing, for RM95 and 10 minutes worth of hoops to jump through, I got one of the biggest, best racing games according to many, and the first game to make me care for the genre since 2004. Especially when there are other more recent racing games that cost 3 times as much that offer maybe 10% of this game's content, I'd like to think it was pretty worth it.

I was in a really fun drifting session, and then I got instantly reconnected to another server without warning. I could almost thumbs down this review for ruining my wholesome moment, but I still love the Forza franchise none-the-less.This entry is a massive improvement over FH3, haven't experienced any game breaking bugs. FH3 had the "invisible wall of death" when traveling over 200+ MPH. You'd hit this wall, all of the other AI cars would pile up, and explode. And this was with the same high end PC I'm using to play this game.This is also the first game I've EVER actually liked the idea of being Online-Only. It makes the game a boat load of fun. Pretty effin cool.Love the world and the detail it provides, the seasons are also a nice touch and a welcome addition to keep the sequels interesting. Catch this game with the Ultimate bundle when it's on sale, you can't go wrong. _childDocuments_.review: I'm waiting for the cutscene to end. Jesus Christ, this game throws an unimaginable amount of cutscenes and unskippable dialogue (ie. you're staring at a map while listening to one of the main characters throw some total knee slappers and sidesplitters over the radio) at you at the beginning of the game. There's so many little cutscenes everywhere (I assume partially to hide loading screens? But then again, the game also has loading screens). The game also has the most aggressive DLC advertising I've ever seen. You're straight up forced to watch a couple minutes of advertisements for the DLCs during the first couple hours. I'd understand if this was a f2p game but this isn't a super cheap game. I can't believe some people actually paid the full 70€ price only to be forced to watch ads. You also can't turn the music volume to 0, for some reason. Luckily you can turn the radio off.This all being said, it's a good game. I bought it just so I can cruise around the British countryside and this game does not disappoint. I had no interest in any other content, but turns out the races, challenges, off-road free-roaming etc. are all actually really fun too. Driving feels good and you have lots of options for which assists you want to have on (I personally have all off except for automatic shift). The game also has a photo mode which is really good. In fact, a bit too good. As a photographer I can't stop myself from pausing the game every 10 seconds to take a new picture. I wish every other game (regardless of genre) had something like this.So, if you don't mind the pure, unadulterated sports game cringe dialogue, tons of  cool cutscenes and a couple in-game ads for the DLC, this is a great game and worth the sale price. Also, I've seen some videos of the game freezing if you play with 8GB RAM but I've never had that problem. I'm also playing with GTX 1050 2gb and the game looks and runs great (obviously not running it on ultra details).

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Nice optimization.-Seamless (almost) gameplay.-Shared tunings and modifications.-Can create your own track and challenges.-Great reflection on the chassis.Neutral:-Could have a better design for 'Car Mastery' upgrades, considering the amount of vehicles in-game, upgrading perks one by one is terribly time consuming.-The game have many nice details on the vehicle including the interior, but they can't be bothered adding actual models as passengers in 'Isha's Taxis' story levels.-'Starting Grid' is kind of pointless as there is no way to improve your place, you always start in the lower back of the group.Cons:-Music cannot be turned off completely, you can get rid most of it by checking 'Streamer mode' but it will reset after restarting the game. You also cannot set music volume to 0.-Unskippable cutscenes.-Cheaters appear in Eliminator (Battle Royale) mode occasionally.-Cheaters in leaderboards.-Some issues with audio if your sample rate is below 48000 Hz.-Some unobtainable achievements due to server shut down.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of great things about this game, and it's beautiful enough to want to spend time in for a cinematic experience -- a lot of time, perhaps. I still intend to go into this world when I have some minutes, particularly to dress up my character.Just be aware that the input mechanism is awful. Though it is an otherwise beautiful experience, it feels like it was brought to PC without playtesting. There is no way to gradually change acceleration on keyboard, and no warning in the publisher's literature that you may need additional hardware. Maneuvering is not trivial and there is no driving tutorial. Expect to need a basic driving guide, to say nothing of the menu splurge.I like many things about it, but cannot recommend it.Received as a gift. Review as of 15 hours playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is remarkable game. It's a racer that's for everybody, instantly accessible for people who don't play racing games, but with enough depth and difficulty to satisfy gamers who prefer simulation. The very premise of Horizon 4 is fun. The quirky, bouncy voice-overs and the festival vibe keeps things free and light-hearted. Races are aimed at creating tight, balanced races that are fun no matter what vehicle you drive, and it does this well. It's fun to just jump in a random race you find.There is a lot of depth to the game, multiple race disciplines keep things interesting and all are genuinely fun. If you get bored of one discipline you can jump in another and get the hang of it really quickly. It doesn't force you through awkward drifting mini-games or shift orientated drag races.Graphically the game is stunning. There is no other word, the cars and environments are photo-realistic. Set any screenshot as my desktop background and I wouldn't even suspect it wasn't the Lake District. The cars themselves look fantastic, lighting is done very well.The seasons mechanics is one of the main attractions to Forza Horizon 4 and have to say it is an interesting one. Certain driving disciplines are more tailored to different seasons, so Winter is good for dirt for example, and Summer more for road racing, and that can get frustrating if you want to change seasons. Seasons are locked to the servers, meaning every week they change, you can't change them in game by moving ahead seasons for example. Each season though does look amazing in it's own way, and adds diversity to game campaign.The long game though is predictably more tailored towards casual gamers. It can be easy to get a big roster of cars without actually having bought one yourself. In this way the game can be easy if you're more of a simulation racer, but Forza Horizon 4 isn't trying to be.Pros-Beautiful graphics-Embodiment of fun-Accessible to all types of gamers-Reasonable roster of cars-Celebration of car culture-Good map-Fantastic amount of tuning abilityCons-Season mechanic can get old, with no way to change to a favourable season-Extensively long tutorial; which keeps you in single player until it's complete-Generally gameplay music is not my cup of tea. That's why I listen to my own radio stations in the background when I play this masterpiece:PForza Horizon 4 is a beautiful game, well polished and full of cars and stunning environments. One more for the casual crowd but fun nonetheless, a fantastic celebration of car culture.Note: All of these ideas are based on ~150 hours of playing experience on the Microsoft Store. You can be sure to see more here^^

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I did not have any fun with this title, but I can see why others would be. I've always only played arcade racers, from mario kart to more realistic titles, but this game's feel falls far outside anything that you'd be used to with arcade racers. The simulations of how each car drives is very interesting, but falls outside of what I'm used to, and it generally felt extremely hard to control anything, no matter what difficulty/assist or car settings I changed. In addition to that, the game seems to have a *lot* of baked-in music, which could be a serious issue if you stream, or even moreso if you really just want to listen to your own tunes. It's utterly impossible to turn off the music.The only thing I really liked about this at all was the customization. The editor is incredible, and you can tune your cars to do just about whatever you want, and you can make them look just about however you want too, with incredibly in-depth appearance customization.If you're a realistic simulation fan and you enjoy racing with such things, customizing your rides to hell and back, and listening to what the game throws at you, this is most certainly the title for you.If you come from a background of arcade racers like Mario Kart, even to things like Burnout, this title may possibly rub you the wrong way. Exercise caution when jumping in and see if it feels the way you want it to.If you have the same tastes as me, this game will be unsatisfying, frustrating, and will only provide some nice eye candy as you trick out your ride.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overpriced. $60 for a 3 years old game is too much but it's hella fun. It is the best racing game for casual players who just want to race in whatever cars they like and don't care much about realism. Forza Horizon 4 is a great successor to FH3 and a great game for people like me who loved good old Test Drive Unlimited games. While it still lacks in its freedom and activities compared to TDU2, FH4 is the closest you're gonna get to that type of racing game.I've been playing it every day since it came out on steam and I wholeheartedly recommend it if you like this type of casual driving games. There are a couple of issues with it though.First of all, like I said, it's overpriced. I suggest you wait for a discount before buying it. I would also suggest buying Ultimate Edition or at least getting the VIP DLC because the grinding in this game is hell. VIP DLC will make your life at least more bearable cause you get double the money rewards from races with it. It's a dreadful thing and a terrible practice but because there're no alternatives to this type of games and no competition, we have to play by Microsoft's rules. And one final minor thing is the radio, it sucks, the music is bad, they've removed 2 radio stations from FH3 and overall there's like an hour of songs on each radio that you will hear repeating constantly. The selection of music is just awful compared to FH3, especially for the classical radio, it's the most overplayed pieces like Vivaldi's Spring and Pachelbel'd Cannon in D. If you're not sick of them already, you will be after playing this game for 10 hours and hearing them on a loop over and over again. I suggest that you spend an hour and prepare a Spotify playlist for yourself with the music you like that you can switch to after you get sick of listening to the ingame music, or alternatively just download BBC app for iPhone or Android and listen to BBC Radio 3.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been reluctant to purchase Forza Horizon 4 because of its arcade nature. Unfortunately, eventually I have fallen for great reviews on this game. Here is my take on it:- The good: good graphics, lots of vehicles.- The bad: yep, this is definitely not a racing simulator. If that's what you are looking for, my advise - look elsewhere. This is an arcade all right. Nothing wrong with this, just different type of a game.However, here is the really bad part: racing wheel support. Yes, it is the worst I've ever seen, even going quite far back in time. I have a G27 racing wheel. In Forza Horizon 4,  all pedals are mixed up - break pedal accelerates, accelerator pedal brakes, clutch pedal does not work at all. The worst thing is the steering wheel force feedback is reversed. I.e. when you turn, the wheel is fighting you trying to increase the steering angle, which makes it completely undrivable. I've seen tons of complaints about this issue. It seems that it is PC related. The good news - it is fixable. It can't be fixed via menu but if you unpack some game zip file, edit XML configuration file for your wheel and repack it back to the zip file - you can get this to work...  But come on! Doing this sort of thing in a $60 game in 2023??? Seriously?Also, there is no way to switch off some highly annoying music (radio) from the game settings menu... Imagine this - you can change the radio volume from 10 down to...  1! Which means that it will still be annoying you, you can't shut it off completely at all! Apparently, you are supposed to go to your car, and then flip "radio channels" until it says "radio off"...  Who made this game? As you can expect after reading all this, none of the cut scenes (and there are a lot of them) are skippable. You have to sit and listen to some amazing plot (I'm very, very sarcastic) being slowly unraveled for you...So, on the scale of 1-10, I would give it a solid 4, slightly less than glamorous 9.5 reviews that prompted me to purchase it...Cheers!:)

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I was skeptical because Forza had always been more simulator than off-the-rails racing like Need For Speed was (which is what I usually stick to), or at least that was my impression since Forza Motorsport 2 was my first Forza series game, but after dedicating some time into this one I'm pleasantly enjoying it a lot. From a gameplay perspective, it's amazing; there's lots to do (dirt racing, road racing, street racing, off-road racing, etc.), exploration is fun, racing feels good and realistic yet satisfying, and enemy racer AI adapt to your car level so you can quite literally play how you want without the forceful pressure of having to upgrade any car to the max, in fact, you don't even have to get first place. This game is all about having fun your way.Good things aside, I'm not too crazy about the stupid slot machine RNG to get cosmetics or cars, but you at least get spins quite frequently and you don't get repeats. You can also buy cars manually through various methods, but even that's done oddly. Another thing that bugs me is the UI, it's very cumbersome to go through. Also, more than half the dialogue in this game downright cringe and/or annoying and you can't even skip any of it or the cutscenes. In the end though, I'm all about gameplay, so even though this game does have various downsides, I can ignore them and enjoy myself nonetheless.It's also sad to see that the car licenses are expiring and therefore Microsoft is having to delist their DLCs and eventually the game, but that's the fault of car brands (or brands in general really) not the game companies involved in making this.

_childDocuments_.review: I hope this isn't true, but this might be the last halfway decent Horizon game. In my opinion the best Horizon game was Forza Horizon 2, with 3 as a close second. Horizon 2 required a lot of time to be put into the game to earn more money and get faster and more expensive cars. The map was also fantastic, although small, and the plot, although similar to every horizon game, was really good. Horizon 3 struck a good balance between needing to put in the time to progress while also making it a little easier for those who simply want the best. The map was also amazing, a broad range of environments from dunes, to urban, suburban, meadows, forests, and straight up deserts. There were also some elevation changes and one of the expansions added a giant mountain.Horizon 4 is where the Horizon series kind of starts to fall downhill, but it still manages to be a pretty good Horizon game. This game is a little more geared towards the people that just went the best as fast as possible, which inevitably means that progress is way too quick for the way the game is setup. Within a few races and just messing about, you will probably earn some wheel spins. This could be a small prize, like how they mostly were in Horizon 3, or it could be a free supercar or 250k. That is something that should be close to endgame stuff, but it's achievable without doing any of the story modes and by completing maybe a 1/4 or less of the races in the game. There is no satisfaction of being able to buy your first supercar.Despite all of those problems (in my opinion), it is really great for those that just don't care and want the best really quickly. The map is pretty good with a lot of forests and fields, an excellent urban area, fun mountain roads, and a very long highway for those top speed runs. It's just a fun game in general which is why I gave it a recommendation.
