_childDocuments_.review: What you’ll likeThe ideal of the Horizon formulaThis series has been excellent since its debut in 2012. The Xbox 360’s Forza Horizon was a great way to take the physics, customization, and cars from Motorsport add in some lighthearted fun. Somehow, each game has improved on that.Forza Horizon 4 maintains the series’ reputation. Once again, I’m left wondering how you make Forza Horizon 5 better than this. Among the reasons this entry is so solid is because the world never gets in the way. The environment looks detailed and realistic, but Playground is not going to destroy your momentum to give a stone wall. You can tear through obstacles like tissue. This series has done that before, but it has never felt quite as friendly as it does here.Another example of how Horizon 4 squeezes more fun out of its traditions is the progressions system. You steadily level up everything in this game. You have separate progression for street races, cross-country, and rallying. Even each individual car has its own leveling system. That might sound exhausting, but it gives you both a reason to stick with a car and a reason to start working on the next one when you’re ready.Unmatched presentationPlayground presents its games better than any other developer working right now. Forza Horizon 4 is more evidence of that. Its clips before and after races are gorgeous. They feature your driver and their car standing in front of massive stylized menu or display. This tells you what race you’re in or how many experience points you just earned. It looks stunning, and it makes the game feel lively and expensive.Great Britain is beautiful over seasonsForza Horizon 4 is stunning. Racing games are always technical showpieces, but I don’t think you could get a better looking game for your Xbox One X right now. I’ve mostly played in performance mode on console, which is getting me 60 buttery smooth frames per second. And sure, you notice the dip in resolution, but it’s not distracting. And even in performance mode, it still looks beautiful.It takes place in Great Britain, and that means you get some pretty roads, green pastures, and plenty of cozy-looking hamlets. Playground then adds variety to this already mesmerizing space through the use of different times of year.The conceit of Forza Horizon 4 is that it’s the car festival that never ends. That means a green pasture might sometime feature some fall colors. Or it could end up covered in snow or flowers. It’s not all just cosmetic changes. Rain and ice will cause handling differences as well. But it really keeps the game feeling fresh.It also looks stunning in 1440p running at 144 frames per second on ultra settings on PC. I recommend experiencing that.Forza Horizon 4 is a good dumb online gameThis game has character customization. That’s because it has a living online world where you will naturally come across other real players at any time. When this happens, you don’t want to embarrass your friends by rocking some ugly default icon. Instead, you want to rock a chicken suit or James Bond’s tuxedo.More important, you’ll need a decent emote when you challenge that online rando and beat them. For example, make them watch you do the floss dance or maybe the Macarena.You can even do these dance emotes at special scenic locations, and it’s just … well, watch.What you won’t likeMore of the samePlayground has made a lot of smart improvements. The progression system does a better job of stitching together the space between races than previous games. And Forza Horizon 4 has seemingly added content without taking any of the other modes away from earlier entries.But you are still primarily doing the same things as always. You’re still racing fast cars around a detailed world. And sure, the setting has changed, but that doesn’t feel too drastically different in the end.That said, Forza Horizon 4 has so much going on, and it’s all so rewarding and satisfying. What you are really getting here is the ultimate refined Forza experience.Conclusion (so far)When a game series is this good for this long, you can sometimes find yourself taking it for granted. Forza Horizon 4 once again refines its formula in a number of notable ways. But those improvements are getting diminishing returns. This is the best Forza Horizon game, and that makes it one of the best racing games ever. And, at first, I didn’t think that would wow me like it once did. But I can’t put the game down. It’s so good. The progression keeps me coming back, and every car is so much fun to drive.If you haven’t checked in with the franchise for a while, you’re going to love it. If you just picked up an Xbox One X and a 4K TV, it is a wonderful showpiece. And even if you’ve played every Forza, you’re going to fall deeply in love with this one.Score: 95/100

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4, developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios, stands as a shining example of excellence in the world of racing games. Released in 2018, the game has captivated players with its stunning visuals, realistic driving mechanics, expansive open-world environment, and an array of vehicles that span the automotive spectrum. In this essay, we will delve into the various aspects that make Forza Horizon 4 a standout title and why it has earned its reputation as one of the finest racing games of its time.Visual Marvel:One of the first things that strike players when they launch Forza Horizon 4 is its breathtaking visuals. The game is a visual marvel, boasting a meticulously crafted open-world environment set in the picturesque landscapes of Great Britain. The attention to detail is unparalleled, with each season – spring, summer, autumn, and winter – bringing a distinct and immersive aesthetic to the game. Whether it's the vibrant colors of autumn leaves or the serene beauty of a snowy winter landscape, Forza Horizon 4's graphics are a testament to the capabilities of modern gaming technology.The realism extends beyond the environment to the cars themselves. Each vehicle is meticulously rendered, showcasing the intricate details of their design, from the gleaming curves of a luxury sports car to the rugged exterior of an off-road vehicle. The dynamic weather system further enhances the visual experience, as raindrops bead on windshields and snow accumulates on the road, affecting the handling of vehicles. The visual fidelity of Forza Horizon 4 is not just eye candy; it plays a crucial role in immersing players in the virtual racing experience.Realistic Driving Mechanics:Forza Horizon 4 strikes a delicate balance between realism and accessibility in its driving mechanics. The game offers a diverse range of cars, each with its own unique handling characteristics that reflect their real-world counterparts. Whether you're tearing through the countryside in a high-performance supercar or navigating tight city streets in a compact hatchback, the responsiveness of the controls and the physics engine make every vehicle feel distinct and authentic.The realism is enhanced by the game's attention to detail in terms of tire grip, suspension dynamics, and vehicle weight. Players can feel the difference between driving on wet and dry surfaces, and the changing weather conditions add an extra layer of challenge to the driving experience. Despite the authenticity, Forza Horizon 4 remains accessible to players of varying skill levels, thanks to adjustable difficulty settings and a range of driving assists that can be tailored to individual preferences.Open-World Exploration:Forza Horizon 4's open-world environment is a sprawling playground for automotive enthusiasts. The map, a condensed but faithful representation of Great Britain, offers a diverse range of terrains, from the bustling streets of Edinburgh to the winding roads of the Lake District. The seamless transition between seasons not only affects the visual landscape but also transforms the driving experience. Lakes freeze over in winter, opening up new routes, and spring brings vibrant foliage that enhances the overall aesthetics of the game.The open-world design encourages exploration, with hidden barn finds, stunt jumps, and races scattered across the map. The sense of freedom is amplified by the absence of traditional race tracks, allowing players to chart their own course through the picturesque landscapes. The ability to seamlessly transition between solo and online play further adds to the dynamic nature of Forza Horizon 4, as players can engage in cooperative races, competitive events, or simply cruise around the open world with friends.A Plethora of Vehicles:Forza Horizon 4 boasts an extensive and diverse roster of over 700 vehicles, ranging from classic cars to modern hypercars and everything in between. The meticulous attention to detail extends to each vehicle's sound design, ensuring that the roar of a V8 engine or the whine of an electric motor is faithfully reproduced. The cars are not merely cosmetic additions; they are integral to the gameplay experience, each offering a unique driving feel that caters to different preferences.The game's deep customization options allow players to personalize their vehicles, from performance upgrades to cosmetic modifications. Whether you're a gearhead fine-tuning every aspect of your car's performance or a casual player looking to express your creativity through unique paint jobs and decals, Forza Horizon 4 accommodates a wide spectrum of player preferences.Dynamic Multiplayer Experience:Forza Horizon 4 seamlessly integrates multiplayer elements into its open-world design. The game features a shared online world where players from around the globe can coexist, participate in events, and engage in spontaneous races. The dynamic nature of the open world ensures that each session feels alive, with real-time events and challenges that can be tackled solo or cooperatively with other players.The competitive aspect of Forza Horizon 4 is realized through its ranked multiplayer modes, where players can test their skills against others in a variety of race types. The ranking system ensures a fair matchmaking experience, pitting players of similar skill levels against each other for a competitive and satisfying multiplayer experience.Conclusion:Forza Horizon 4 is not merely a racing game; it is a symphony of sight, sound, and sensation that combines to create an unparalleled gaming experience. Its stunning visuals, realistic driving mechanics, expansive open-world environment, diverse vehicle roster, and dynamic multiplayer features collectively contribute to its status as a masterpiece in the racing game genre. As players immerse themselves in the virtual world of Forza Horizon 4, they are not just racing cars; they are experiencing the culmination of gaming technology, attention to detail, and a deep passion for the art of automotive excitement. _childDocuments_.review: This review is strictly for the Steam Deck.I'm updating this review to now recommend it. I've had many more hours with the game, and with the many updates it's received, it seems to be much more stable.-------------------------OLD REVIEW-----------------------------I've always been a huge fan of the Forza series and have a considerable amount of play time on Xbox. As soon as I received my Steam Deck, I knew Forza 4 would be one of the first games I'd want to play on it.Just to be up front, at this point, it's not a great experience. Yes, the game looks great and plays amazing with the Steam Deck's controls - the real issue stems from how often the game crashes. Various settings and different versions of Proton seem to make little to no difference, and what's worse, there's nothing in particular that seems to be the root cause. You'll find yourself playing 30min just fine, turning a corner and black screen. Menu load, crash. Won a race, crash. Load the auction house, etc... That would be bad enough as it is, especially since there is a fairly significant amount of load time to get things running again. No, the real (well, serious) problem is these game crashes seem to love to corrupt the game save. I've lost numerous hours because I essentially had to delete the save from my PC to clear the cloud save that was corrupted by my Steam Deck. And yes, that meant I had to restart from the beginning.So, currently at the posting of this review, Forza 4 is listed as playable. That is true, but just know that it comes with a certain level of risk. Unfortunately you are almost certainly going to run into these issues... I'm just hoping, in time, the devs put some effort into making the game fully compatible. Until that happens though, I can't recommend it.

Why does steam overlay take focus and require manual exit every time the game starts. Why do the scrollbars behave oddly in menus, becoming longer like there are more items being added, rather than moving, depending on the selected item and movement direction.Looks like it should have been a fun game, and likely on console these were non-issues. If the game was 20 bucks because it's 3 years old, and included etc cars/dlc, I probably would have kept going, maybe dig into files and find a way to edit the default TS-PC profile, but at full price... I'm just glad to have Steam, reviews, and refunds.Also, the built in benchmark, 4k 60FPS on a 1080TI, it was very smooth and nice, but the game surely doesn't run that way. _childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is an absolute masterpiece of a racing game that sets a new standard for the genre. From the moment you hit the roads of beautiful, historic Britain, you're immersed in an exhilarating world of automotive excitement.One of the most impressive aspects of Forza Horizon 4 is its stunning visuals. The attention to detail in the environments, from the rolling countryside to the bustling city streets, is nothing short of breathtaking. Each season brings its own unique charm, with dynamic weather effects that not only look incredible but also affect gameplay in exciting ways.The car lineup in Forza Horizon 4 is second to none. With hundreds of meticulously modeled vehicles spanning various eras and disciplines, there's something for every type of car enthusiast. Whether you're tearing through off-road trails in a rugged 4x4, dominating the track in a high-performance supercar, or cruising along the coastline in a classic muscle car, the selection is unparalleled.The driving mechanics are perfectly tuned, striking a balance between accessibility and depth. Whether you're a seasoned racing veteran or a casual player, you'll find the handling to be responsive and satisfying. The addition of the Horizon Life online mode adds a new layer of excitement, allowing you to connect with friends and compete in a variety of challenges and events.But perhaps the most impressive aspect of Forza Horizon 4 is its sheer amount of content. The world is filled with activities to discover, from exhilarating races and daring stunts to hidden treasures and photo opportunities. With each new season, the landscape transforms, keeping the experience fresh and exciting long after you've crossed the finish line.In conclusion, Forza Horizon 4 is a triumph of game design that delivers an unparalleled racing experience. With its breathtaking visuals, extensive car lineup, polished mechanics, and wealth of content, it's a must-have title for any racing fan. Whether you're tearing up the track solo or tearing through the countryside with friends, Forza Horizon 4 never fails to impress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has got to be one of my favourite games ever. Everything about it is well balanced. Hundreds of cars to choose from, and a beautiful, large and diverse map to explore. Not only that, but changing seasons and weather bring me nostalgia for the snowy Scotland and Lake District settings. I bought it at the end of 2022 for about £20 because it was on sale and to this day it is one of my most played games.As well as providing a banging music playlist, Forza Horizon 4 rejuvenated my love for cars. My only gripe is the poor UI and graphics driver optimisation (I had to roll back my graphics drivers to play it), but once that was sorted out I had endless hours of fun and even the opportunity to play with friends and interact with other players. Even Forza 5, which I recently moved on to, fails to match the atmosphere and character this game has. I still recommend FH4 thoroughly to those who want an excellent open world racing experience.Stunning, timeless game!

_childDocuments_.review: All video games should be illegal.                 Forza Horizon 4 is a turbo thrill ride of a game where you can finally live out your dreams of driving like a berserk lunatic. If you are as much of a psychopath as me, and enjoy ramming families of 5 off of a thousand foot tall bridge then YOU will love this game. 	The graphics of Forza 4 are like an opera for your eyes, coming from Prince of Persia (a distinctly similar game). The team at  From Soft Studios have really upped their game when it comes to Forza 4. The eye punching visuals of this game have truly blown me away, whether I’m cruising through a mountain range, or barreling down the race track, the visuals truly send mine eyes on a carnival ride of dazzling views.	The story of Forza 4 is as if a squirrel were to be strapped to a bottle rocket. By this I mean it’s all over the place (MAJOR SPOILERS AHEAD). The story of this game had me LITERALLY wetting the bed at night, just ask my wife, with the outrageously simple storyline during the wax buffing arc, and the dreadful experience that was the air pump arc. Just as an example the main character goes from fighting off an alligator with his tire pump, to being bested by butterflies in the VERY NEXT CHAPTER. Overall I think that the game’s story would be better off sent to the gulag, or at the very least deleted from the game.                   I prefer F4 over F5 because the latter game has THE MOST ANNOYING TIRE SQUEALS. Forza 4 has profoundly less tire squeal noise, which is much more calming to my 3 year old. She enjoys the sound of me slamming on my breaks in F4, but F5 tends to make her more upset. To understand the gameplay of this game imagine your hands controlling a symphony of button inputs. The intricate button inputs make you feel like you are genuinely in the seat of that Ferrari EVO you wish you could afford. If you think you won't enjoy the gameplay of this game you might as well go eat a spoonful of dirt, because that’s about how good your taste in things is. The level of depth and thought put into this game’s mechanics will knock you back in your seat. The devs polished down to the pixel of even the smallest blade of grass like it's the jewels of the queen’s crown. You really feel the speed in this game. Some factors are required to make you feel the speed you are going in a video game, and developers tend to struggle to take hold of that adrenaline rush. Camera shake, motion blur, and wind noise are huge factors in the feeling of speed, and the devs at From Soft captured that feeling like cowboys wrangling a bull. 	I would like to, in closing, clarify as to why I think all games should be illegal. Video games are the devil, In fact, I heard on Facebook about a kid who died from playing games. We all need to keep our kids from games. Stop games and stop school shootings #videogamesDOcauseviolence. Please repost this in all of your middle-aged conservative Facebook groups. Thus ends my review of Forza Horizon 4

_childDocuments_.review: Dope! I'm not a huge racing game fan, but Forza Horizon 4 is a lot of fun. From what I can tell it's a happy medium between an arcade styled racer and a simulation (Maybe just slightly leaning a bit more towards simulation).The game is extremely optimized, I'm running ultra settings at 1440p getting around 85-100fps depending on particle effects and shadows on screen. This game with everything turned up looks gorgeous, and is such a visual treat. (I have a 2070 Super paired with an R5 3600 for reference with 16gb of ram.) The actual gameplay is pretty tight and the cars feel nice to drive, though I'm not racing game expert this is just a layman's perspective. The customization is also pretty decent and for tuners you can really mess with stuff to get your cars handling the way you want for better or worse (If you go for meme builds). The only issues I have are some odd frame stutters here and there but never during actual gameplay. Also the voice acting and the characters kind of leave a lot to be desired. Plus the overall soundtrack is just passable. Although Horizon 4 is just beautiful to look at (I keep mentioning this but it's true), and there's just so much content here from all the cars to unlock, modes, and just the single player "campaign". You can also just drive around the large hub world while taking in the scenery of the fictional representation of the UK, it's super relaxing (Even though sometimes the map can feel a little same-y, although seasons really help with the aesthetic). Can't comment on the multiplayer, but I've heard generally good things about the experience there for those interested in that content. Overall tons of value especially if you can pick this up on sale, Horizon 5 is just around the corner in a couple of months as of the time I write this, but the community in 4 is still lively for those that want to engage with it. If you're just in for the single player content alone there's still a lot of fun, achievements, and cars to collect. All-in-all super content rich racing game that anyone can enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: A Thrilling Journey Through Stunning LandscapesRating: ★★★★★ (5/5)This is an exhilarating open-world racing game that completely blew away my expectations. From the moment I fired up the engine, I was captivated by the jaw-dropping graphics and seamless gameplay, creating an experience that made time disappear as I delved deeper into its virtual world.Visually, Forza Horizon 4 sets a new standard for racing games. The meticulously designed landscapes are an absolute feast for the eyes, and the attention to detail is simply astonishing. From the lush greenery of the British countryside to the bustling streets of Edinburgh, every corner of this world feels alive and immersive. I found myself stopping on the side of the road just to admire the picturesque scenery, forgetting for a moment that I was supposed to be racing!The range of cars available is equally impressive. With an extensive collection of vehicles to choose from, each with its own unique characteristics and handling, the game caters to every driving style. Whether I wanted to cruise through the city streets in a sleek supercar or take on off-road challenges with a rugged SUV, Forza Horizon 4 had me covered. The sense of progression and unlocking new cars as I advanced through the game was gratifying, keeping me motivated to explore further.One of the standout features is the dynamic weather system, which adds an extra layer of challenge and excitement to the races. Navigating through rain, snow, and even thunderstorms not only tests your driving skills but also introduces a level of unpredictability that keeps each race fresh and thrilling. The day-night cycle further enhances the realism, making the world feel alive and ever-changing.The gameplay in Forza Horizon 4 is smooth as silk. The controls are responsive, making even the most demanding maneuvers feel natural. The variety of events and activities available ensures there's never a dull moment. From traditional races to stunt challenges and everything in between, the game consistently delivers heart-pounding action and adrenaline-pumping excitement.The online integration is seamless, allowing you to share the open-world experience with other players in real-time. Whether you choose to team up for cooperative challenges or compete head-to-head in adrenaline-fueled races, the multiplayer aspect extends the game's longevity and guarantees endless hours of fun.While Forza Horizon 4 is not without its minor quirks, such as occasional AI oddities or minor glitches, they are easily overshadowed by the overwhelming positives that the game offers. Its vast and visually stunning world, combined with addictive gameplay, make it one of the best racing games I've ever played.In conclusion, Forza Horizon 4 is an absolute must-have for racing enthusiasts and casual gamers alike. It offers a breathtakingly beautiful and immersive experience that will keep you coming back for more. Turn the key, buckle up, and get ready for an unforgettable journey through the virtual roads of Great Britain.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 Review: The Only Traffic Jam You’ll EnjoyI bought Forza Horizon 4 thinking it was a nice, relaxing racing game. Next thing I know, I’m tearing through the English countryside at 200 mph in a vintage Mini Cooper, dodging sheep like I’m in a high-speed wooly slalom. I’ve drifted through more stone walls than I care to admit, but hey, they grow back, right?The game has seasons, and I don’t mean just spring or winter. One minute you're admiring autumn leaves while driving calmly on a scenic road, the next you're plowing through a snowstorm, trying not to crash into a frozen lake. Turns out, driving on ice is a lot harder than Mario Kart led me to believe.Oh, and the game lets you race a hovercraft. Yes, a hovercraft. I’m not sure why, but I’m not questioning it. If they told me my next opponent was Bigfoot driving a monster truck, I’d just hit the gas.In summary, Forza Horizon 4 is like a fever dream where you’re the world’s best (or worst) driver. If you’ve ever wanted to make friends by smashing into their cars and calling it “multiplayer,” this is the game for you. 10/10 would launch myself off a cliff in a Lamborghini again.

Well, the game is really addicting and fun when it works, but considering the price point (which is way too much), I don't know whether the anger and frustration you'll experience is worth it. :)Edit:If you upgrade your Nvidia drivers, the game will crash and freeze randomly. _childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is a must-have for any racing game enthusiast. The game features a vast open-world set in the beautiful and picturesque British countryside, complete with dynamic seasons that change every week. The world is filled with an array of diverse terrains, from lush forests to rocky mountains, providing an exhilarating driving experience.The game boasts an impressive car list, featuring over 450 licensed cars from over 100 manufacturers. The vehicles are beautifully rendered, and the attention to detail is second to none. The driving mechanics are spot-on, with each car feeling unique and responsive.The multiplayer aspect of the game is well-designed, allowing players to seamlessly race and explore the world with others. The game's social system is robust and easy to use, making it easy to connect with friends and other players.The graphics in Forza Horizon 4 are simply stunning. The world is vibrant and alive, with stunning lighting and weather effects. The cars are beautifully rendered, and the attention to detail is incredible. The game's performance is also top-notch, with very little in the way of frame rate drops or other technical issues.Overall, Forza Horizon 4 is an incredible racing game that offers a fun and engaging open-world experience. The game's diverse car list, beautiful world, and well-designed multiplayer system make it a must-have for any racing game enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite "simcade" racers ever. I played it to death via the Microsoft Store, and having the chance to replay it via the Steam version has been a dream come true for me.Honestly, I prefer this to the sequel in several ways. Forza Horizon 5 is beautiful in its own way, but it also ironically feels TOO big and empty. FH4's map is just right, and a lot more dynamic, especially with how dramatically the seasons change the map and the driving. There's a feeling this game captures that few racing/driving games have managed to capture, as you tear through the Scottish countryside and the streets of Edinburgh in your favourite car, music playing on the radio as autumn leaves whip around you. It's just an absolute pleasure to play.Problems? Yeah, a couple. Sometimes, the AI on anything above the Average difficulty will choose at least one racer to be a "Peter Perfect", pulling ahead to the point it becomes more difficult to catch up than it should be (though to nowhere near the same egregious level as FH5 or Forza Motorsport 2023). Also some of the Quality-of-Life changes made in FH5, such as the ability to sell or donate duplicate cars immediately upon receiving them, are sorely missed. Also sometimes the Wheelspin's rewards are beyond a joke, but massive credit goes to the developers for not shoving in microtransactions.EDIT 21/2/24: It turns out you CAN immediately sell duplicate cars if you win them via the Wheelspin. I honestly don't remember that feature being there before; maybe they added it in an update?Forza Horizon 4 is just brilliant, in ways both tangible and intangible. Beautiful graphically and a ton of fun to play, along with the feeling of simple joy it gives the player through just driving and exploring. To me, this is as good as these sorts of racing games can possibly be.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW UPDATE:The fix in April does seem to fix the issues mentioned below. I am having a blast once again and can go back to recommending Horizon 4. After the fix, I had some multi-hour sessions and they were all smooth.The only things that bother me now are the lack of support for a dedicated shifter (TH8A) and the annoying centre dead zone, which is still quite substantial even after lowering the dead zone settings to 0. But the driving feels good overall on a wheel, and the content is fun. Bring a friend and you'll be able to enjoy some great racing or cruising sessions together.The map is gorgeous and portrays the area really well from what I can tell.ORIGINAL REVIEW:I love Forza Horizon 4 and I played the Microsoft Store version a lot. But I have to recommend against buying it, because it is (or rather we, as players, are) suffering from very frequent crashes on NVidia GPUs. Looking through the forums, these issues seem to date back to autumn 2022, if not summer or even spring.Apparently, it affects the Steam version of FH4. After a long break, I decided to buy the game during spring sale, looking forward to playing it again. Alas, I was disappointed by it constantly crashing... I tried everything I could to make it work, but to no avail. This left me with having paid for a game I cannot run, nor refund (because I tried finding a solution, leaving me with a total of almost five hours in-game).I can do my best to save you from being disappointed, however. If you have an NVidia GPU, do not buy it. You will most likely end up being frustrated by back-to-back crashes to desktop.Edit: I reported this game to Steam using the flag icon on the right-hand side of the store page. Selling it without any fixes and a great portion of the player base affected is just shameless...

_childDocuments_.review: As seen by a casual gamer with a life long passion for rally and racing games that enjoys playing on keyboard and external camera view.Forza Horizon 4 is one of the best car racing games I have ever played!!Strong :✔ Insane variety and list of cars!!!!!✔ Physics and graphics are super well done, the environment is gorgeous and the most mind-blowing thing is that every week the map changes to each one of the 4 seasons including all sorts of weather conditions✔best rain I have ever experienced in a racing/rally game to date. Rain has actual sense of depth just like IRL when you can see it fall on the street or on lakes from distance. it's not just a simple animation layer on your screen any more. ✔ Also water drops are actually dynamically and individually rendered on your car - which is a detail that blew me away. ✔ Even wetness on the tarmac is interacting with your tires going through it (sound and splash effect depending the amount of water)✔ Car design is absolutely magnificent. The attention to the detail is insane, even the car lights are done with so much detail. The detail is so great that at some moments you will be able to even notice the speedometers and RPM-meters animate and display fully real time accurate measurements while driving with external cam view ( ! ).✔ Satisfying amount of car customization. Not too much or chaotic and not too little. Just about right. From engine upgrades to body paints.✔ Pretty cool voice acting and some times a nice drop of humor. also a good cameo for top gear in there. some of the special missions include some very enjoyable historical and factual story telling about some specific cars.✔ Some secret specials here and there like a Halo themed mission that lets you drive the Warthog (you can also obtain if for your self when you can afford it), and a head to head that can let you unlock the QUADRA TURBO-R V-TECH from Cyberpunnk2077!✔ Not much for dirt effects but splashing through water is extremely satisfying.✔ The music selections are so damn awesome and some tracks are so memorable I eventually found them on Spotify and added them to my favorites!✔ SH*TTONES of things to do. Like seriously from the standard race events to the weekly events to custom events created by other players!!!✔ The 2 map expansions are actually worth playing and super cool to experience!!Weak :❌Rewind button response will fail way too many times❌If you select retry at the end of an event the loading time is going to ridiculously slow (extra ❌ given here because some times the reload finished and the car falls through the map) in order to avoid this either restart an event before you reach the finish line. or simply collect the whatever reward you would get, go through the event scores and restart it once you are on free-roam again (that's seriously faster than selecting "retry")❌tiny detail but it's slightly off-putting: old design flaw where the shadow of the tires does not actually start from the point of contact to the floor allowing light to be seen under the tires. This "floating" tire effect is such a very very old design flaw, i was surprised to come across it a couple of time.❌Car damage is limited to some very very basic visual scratches. best thing you can see is loosing a mirror or a spoiler (in case you have any) or some mad-protectors depending the design but that's it.I am left without words to describe how much fun I had playing this game. My time tracker speaks for itself and I'm not into any repetitive gameplay. It's super rare for me to reach anything above 100h for a car racing game. This is a truly awesome game with an open world design that keeps things fresh with an easy UI/UX design and the diversity of the environment combined with the seasons made me not get bored to even drive from one corner of the map to the other without fast traveling. From super cars to rally cars, from hyper cars to drift cars and trucks. This was a real journey and I will look forward to the next title from this studio for sure!!This is hands down recommended!PS: note to self, it's amazing how great the graphical details are evolving in racing games. i'm keen to experience more!

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst sometimes frustrating, this game is one of the most defining arcade racers I've enjoyed in a long time. Easy pick up and play whenever I have some free time. And it is set in the wondrous green and pleasant lands of the United Kingdom. From the music, to the activities, to the thematics, to the feel in the race itself - I can say I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Forza Horizons 4. I have the others in the series ready and waiting for me to pick up and play, but in the interim, I'll give this a rest.My main critical feedback - reduce the busywork. Activities can be fun, and so can all the different challenges, but it feels at time like I'm completing chores, not having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so the thing with this game is that you have to learn to make your own fun. The 'story' submissions usually take away your ability to use your own cars, which can be frustrating, there aren't all that many of each kind of race, and the map isn't huge when you're encouraged to be zipping around at several hundred kilometres per hour. All that said, the number of cars you can collect is truly astounding and the driving, while arcadey, is fun! I'm a huge fan of rallying and the car modding engine lets me turn just about anything into an off-road monster. Pro-Tip: AWD is always the best option for pretty much every car. For whatever reason, I don't think that and AWD swap adds much if any weight, so there's pretty much no downsides to it. The mods aren't super realistic and the tuning leaves a little bit to be desired. For instance, you can't adjust boost pressure, engine timing, cam profile, or anti-lag. On the other hand, the sheer variety of things you can do combined with the variety of cars makes those missing options smart a bit less. Another pro-tip is to make use of the route designer if you get bored of the dev made races. I've found that the point to point races are bit short, so my map is now crisscrossed by sprawling dirt races that take you from the mountains of the Highlands to the beaches of the East Coast and from the Cotswalds up to Edinburgh (again, the map is pretty small :P). This is definitely a great game and it easily scratches my arcade driving itch!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, fine, I'll make an actual review for the game.Forza has been on my radar since I started playing PC games back in 2015, but I always had an alternative version of it, aka Gran Turismo 6 and Sport, but now not having a PS4 gives me a great reason to play these racing sims and racing games on Steam and other PC platforms, and by god is it fun. But where others stand out in realism, or drift arcade styles, Forza is what I wish Gran Turismo had, it's the love child of the classic arcade fun of Need For Speed with the systems of casual racing sims, hardcore but accessible tuning and a huge selection of cars, tracks and racing modes.Forza Horizon takes that concept of casual racing sim fun and cracks it over it's back, breaking the norm and introducing some of the most fun I have had in a racing game since Gran Turismo 4 on the PS2. This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, the visuals are excellent, the community is fantastic, the driving is "arcady" AND simulator-like, the game has so many tunes for the hundreds of cars available in the BASE GAME, the DLCs are not needed at all to get hundreds to thousands of hours of gameplay out of, the game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brilliant.I love this game, I suggest wholeheartedly to buy this game on sale and experience what Microsoft and Playground Games have to offer. I am excited to buy Forza Horizon 5 when it's price lowers to around 30 bucks or so.10/10 No stupid third party software nonsense, no in-game bloat, no dlc requirements (they push dlc a bit too hard though in game with ads for them playing from time to time) and no limits to what you can't do. I love tuning a supra to be able to rally, and a mini cooper to be as fast as a super car.

_childDocuments_.review: Singleplayer score: 5/10As a first time player of the Forza game, I could sum up it as a fun game. But not great, if you want to pursue only a singleplayer experience. Just too much stuff thrown in your face; - buying homes in the game make no sense... in TDU/TDU2 it was much better executed; - some events are repetitive, so it gets boring; - unskippable ads (some LEGO addon for example), a lot of advertisement in a game; - unskippable audio; It is a good racing game, especially if you want just relax after a working day. But not great if you want more singleplayer experience. I think it is more focused on a younger audience, which is fine. But I enjoyed TDU2 more, I wish they released newer version of it...

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is a slot machine simulator that enables a driving game.In it, you play a wealthy, youthful car enthusiast attending a year-round racing festival during which the residents of a massive swath of British countryside generously agree to replace about 80% of their walls, fences, and trees with breakaway prop versions that explode at any collision over 20 mph, and endure thumping party music for the rest of their natural lives.It is also an effective dopamine drip. In the early hours of the game, every accomplishment, no matter how tiny, prompts some colorful meter or progression counter to update. These achievement metrics fill regularly and unlock new content. They also rain tokens for the aforementioned slot machines on you; slot machines on which every spin is a win and most prizes are cars.And boy will you get cars. So many cars. Your garage will be rotten with cars of every make, model, and style you can imagine in under a dozen hours. You will never drive 90% of them unless you need to make more content for YouTube or Twitch, or want to expand your collection of player-created cute anime girl paint jobs. But it's still important that they're all here because each car is someone's favorite.Once you decide which of your cars to drive (much to the resentment of all your other cars that will forever sit collecting dust, you monster), you will look at your map and notice that there is literally too much to do. You will almost regret unlocking more races as you transform the map into a mess of badges, icons, and search radii. You will have to aggressively filter the map to find the next race in your current championship series.But (eventually), race you will. There are many kinds of races. Track races, dirt races, street races, point-to-point, rally, and other novelties. There's even Battle Royale (Auto Royale?) racing, called The Eliminator, complete with shrinking battlefield, hunts for car upgrades, and 1v1 duels where the winner is usually whoever hits fewer unyielding trees on the way to a randomly generated finish line.Whichever modes you favor, the racing feels very good provided you take time to find, upgrade, or tune a car out of the suck zone. Between tweaks to the AI difficulty and driving assists, both of which reward accepting challenge with multipliers to credit and influence earnings, you'll surely find a level of resistance that fits your skill. The game even pipes up every few races if you win or lose too much, encouraging you to adjust your settings back into the challenge sweet spot.And you really should take the advice it offers. The right level of challenge, where you find victory attainable but not assured, will push you to improve your driving and tuning skills. But another reason is that FH4 understands that forcing players to place on the podium to progress just results in them lowering the difficulty, or restarting the race each time they botch a turn that will guarantee a loss. To save you those frustrations, the game largely lets you progress just by trying and finishing events, and allows you to rewind the most recent few seconds of races whenever you like to fix any failure so dramatic that you'd restart rather than finish.The result is a game that, despite my good-natured roasting, is always, always fun. FH4 is a joyous driving party that can entertain the casual player who just wants a no-pressure racing fantasy, alongside the most driven creatives, tuners, and racers.

_childDocuments_.review: Just delete their media files!DISCLAIMER: by modifying your game files, you're risking  of it (easy to fix, see instructions further down) and maybe even . That last one is unlikely, but don't try this if you do care. .To access these files, you have to:1. Right click on the game, then go to "Manage" > "Browse Local Files". This will open a new file explorer window.2. Go into the "media" folder and wreak havok!You might want to just rename files or move them around instead of deleting them, that's your choice.Here's the ones I've found so far:* Videos: <game folder>\media\ui\videos => I just deleted everything, you might want to keep some of them.* Voice-overs: <game folder>\media\audio\fmodopus\x64\VO_<something else> => I deleted every file that starts with "VO_".Next time you boot the game, you might see black screens instead of the usual intro videos depending on what you deleted. Don't fret! The game menu will come up. You'll also notice some assets, like animated banners and such, are now black. I haven't tested this too much, so I'm unsure of its effect on online play.Note that future updates to the game will definitely restore these files, so be prepared to do it all over again.To undo this, you have to:1. Right click on the game, then click on "Properties...".2. Click on "Local Files".3. Click on "Verify integrity of game files...".4. Let Steam do its thing. It should automatically start re-downloading the missing files.I want to love this game. In fact, I might continue playing it regardless of my complaints.OK, so first things first: why do you spend so much time on a racing game... not racing cars? There's a bajillion little interruptions and distractions. Unskippable intro, random unskippable cutscenes when you open the map or get out of a menu, tremendously disorganized menus... it's almost like the game doesn't want you to play it.Speaking about the cutscenes... none of the NPCs enhance the game in any way. The game would be just as good if they were gone. You can't completely mute them using the voice-over volume settings either, so you're stuck hearing them babble on and on about nothing useful. It's downright miserable!All of that is a shame, because there's a pretty good driving game underneath all the distractions and interruptions. A plethora of cars, lots of different driving modes, tons of online content... good luck getting to them though.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever dreamed of taking your grandma's vintage sedan for a spin on a Scottish countryside, only to end up doing a triple backflip off a cliff, then Forza Horizon 4 is the game you never knew you needed in your life!I stumbled into Forza Horizon 4 expecting a relaxing Sunday drive through picturesque landscapes. Little did I know, I'd soon be soaring through the air like a caffeinated seagull on a Red Bull binge!The game starts with you, a normal human being with a questionable driver's license, being dropped into the British countryside with a car that has more horsepower than the entire cast of Fast & Furious combined. You're immediately given the keys to the kingdom (or rather, the ignition to your dream car) and told to go forth and conquer the open-world map. And conquer I did!But don't let the lush meadows and quaint villages fool you; this game is a certified adrenaline junkie's paradise. One minute, you're cruising down a narrow country lane, narrowly avoiding sheep, and the next, you're drifting through ancient stone circles like a modern-day Druid.And the cars! Oh, the cars! Forza Horizon 4 has more cars than a parking lot at a Justin Bieber concert. From vintage classics to hypercars that make your heart race faster than a cheetah with an energy drink addiction, there's a vehicle for every type of player. You can even customize them to your heart's content, as long as your heart's content includes neon pink paint and a spoiler that could double as an aircraft wing.The game's weather system is like Mother Nature on a rollercoaster binge. One moment, you're racing under sunny skies, and the next, you're hydroplaning through a monsoon that would put Noah's flood to shame. It's all part of the fun and keeps you on your toes, or rather, your tires.Forza Horizon 4 also has a knack for turning the most mundane objects into potential launch ramps. Stone walls, farmhouses, and innocent pedestrians all become part of your high-octane playground. Just remember to apologize to the sheep if you accidentally launch them into low Earth orbit.But it's not all chaos and mayhem. The game also has a fantastic music lineup that caters to every taste, from classical to hip-hop. You can choose your own soundtrack or just listen to the in-game radio. And honestly, nothing beats drifting through the Scottish Highlands while listening to Beethoven's 9th Symphony. It's a cultural experience like no other.In conclusion, Forza Horizon 4 is not just a game; it's a wild, hilarious, and occasionally heart-stopping adventure through the British countryside. It's the kind of game that turns your driving skills from "Sunday driver" to "X Games contender." So, if you've ever wanted to explore the UK with a turbocharged rocket strapped to your back, this game is for you. Just remember to fasten your seatbelt, because things are about to get bumpy in the best way possible!

_childDocuments_.review: A nice, full-featured and beautiful open world arcade racer with hundreds of great cars, plagued only by the typical issues of AAA games these days: tons of DLCs, useless cosmetics, always online, and a mainstream presentation for western pubers, slippery as an eel. If you can live with that, it's a good arcade racer.Pros:* great open world, a beautiful interpretation of a mini version of the UK* the scenery changes depending on the season (e.g., lakes freeze and you can drive over them in winter), which is awesome* lots of content: tons of races, cars, and things to explore* tons of settings, customization options* there are different types of events (rally, cross country, street racing, ...) and nothing forces you into doing something you do not want to do. Real freedom! It's an open world that deserves the name, not just a boring map which replaces the main menu!Cons:* Annoying UI and menus* The typical AAA game disadvantages these days: more DLCs and editions than you can count, and even if you buy the ultimate, there is still stuff for that they charge you extra.* Presentation (always happy rich kid car festival crowd, main characters considers himself the coolest dude on earth, the music the loading screen animation of people cheering at you on stage with your car) is clearly aimed at pubers and feels borderline cringeworthy to me* events (the races you start from the open world) are very short, typically about 3 minutes* It does (almost) not matter whether you drive on the road or not, you have similar grip and speed in the woods and you can just drive through almost everything, even medium sized trees will just disappear in a falling tree animation and a minor sound effect without even reducing your speed. This means people drive everywhere and its often faster to go in a straight line rather than follow the roads, which can kill a lot of the immersion. You can even go through major rivers.* bad mainstream pop music. In general, it feels like they wanted to please everyone a bit too much.Neutral:* It's clearly advertised as an arcade racer so I will not count this as a negative, but if you try to race with all assists off and manual shifting, you will find that this makes little sense: there are tons of races, each on different tracks, and you do not know the corners, so you need the racing line if you want to be fast. Also it's hard to turn off the rewind feature: because you can just drive next to the road (see above), races use checkpoints every 300 meters that you have to go through, and missing one means your position is reset and you lose a lot of time and have to restart. The solution if you missed one by accident is of course the rewind feature. And in the cross-country races, where you are sliding at high speed through the landscape with very little control, you will miss checkpoints sooner or later. This game is definitely a lot more about finishing hundreds of short races in hundreds of cars than about properly learning a few tracks and cars.* Does not work with my new Fanatec wheel and paddles, they are not detected at all even though they work in ACC and Dirt 2. But as this could be a problem with the latest Fanatec driver according to forums, I am for now listing it as neutral instead of negative.Overall 8/10 if you are looking for an arcade open world racing game to play with a controller. Just don't expect something too serious.It's a pity they can't produce a world like this for more serious racing games with a smaller audience. But I'm a software developer and I can tell that this was definitely  a low budget project. Forza 5 is a copy of this game where they replaced the UK map with Mexico, btw. I have both, and I slightly prefer 4, but it's just about the map.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game.This is what I would imagine an ideal open world street racer to be like lots of fun. I enjoy being able to just cruise around and drive where ever I want, the game feels kinda like a sequel to Midnight club and Test Drive Unlimited the location is set in Edinburgh Scotland which is nice and great to explore, the map is huge and the car selection is massive, there is so many different types of cars to choose from its crazy.The game play is quality, the cars handle nicely and the difficulty can be adjusted, The single player experience is excellent I never really run out of things to do, I enjoy being able to play multiplayer mode with my friends, it can be really fun with the various different modes, capture the flag and Infected are really good. I like all the different race events, searching for collectables is fun, doing side missions against the clock or stunt challenges etc can be cool and rewarding. Some times I find the race tracks can be a bit recycled or unorganised but to be honest its not really something that bothers me that much, I do think it would have been great if they added cops to the game kinda sucks that there isnt any.Something I should mention is that I had two problems with the game.The first issue I had was stuttering, to be fair it was mostly during cut scenes, I did notice it during game play and between transitions like when ever I finished a race event or when I was about to start one however I was able to fix this issue. It was kinda my own fault for not keeping my graphics card drivers up to date, as soon as I opened a tool on my computer called "Geforce Experience" I updated my video card drivers and this prity much fixed the issue for me. The game only stutters a little bit now before starting events but a part from that the game is smooth and runs great.The second problem was a crashing issue, basically the game would randomly close and go straight to desktop for no reason. This took me a while to actually get fixed it really gave me a headache trying to solve it. There was a lot of things mentioned by different sources such as: updating Windows to the latest version available, disabling my firewall and running the game as Admin then moving the game from my Hard drive to my Solid State drive etc. None of these worked. In the end one of my friends was able to figure out what the issue was and fix it for me. I had to change the Windows Sound depth on my computer to "24 Bit 44100 Hz" the settings I was using was 48000 Hz after I did this the game was no longer crashing and I was able to play it at max settings just fine with no more issues.Another thing that bugs me about the game is every time I load the game up it always brings up the Steam overlay then displays a web page asking me to link my Steam account with my Windows account which is not something I feel comfortable doing and there is no option to select NO so I always have to click the X icon to close the web page down some times it can be annoying it would be nice if the game stopped asking me.I was rather gutted when I ran into these problems but I am glad I was finally able to get the game working properly. Right now I think its one of the best racing games currently available. I would still totally recommend it just beware you may encounter some issues and have to fix them before you can play the game.Overall a fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Forza Horizon 4 is remarkable game. It's a racer that's for everybody, instantly accessible for people who don't play racing games, but with enough depth and difficulty to satisfy gamers who prefer simulation. The very premise of Horizon 4 is fun. The quirky, bouncy voice-overs and the festival vibe keeps things free and light-hearted. Races are aimed at creating tight, balanced races that are fun no matter what vehicle you drive, and it does this well. It's fun to just jump in a random race you find.There is a lot of depth to the game, multiple race disciplines keep things interesting and all are genuinely fun. If you get bored of one discipline you can jump in another and get the hang of it really quickly. It doesn't force you through awkward drifting mini-games or shift orientated drag races.Graphically the game is stunning. There is no other word, the cars and environments are photo-realistic. Set any screenshot as my desktop background and I wouldn't even suspect it wasn't the Lake District. The cars themselves look fantastic lighting is done very well.The seasons mechanics is one of the main attractions to Forza Horizon 4 and have to say it is an interesting one. Certain driving disciplines are more tailored to different seasons, so Winter is good for dirt for example, and Summer more for road racing, and that can get frustrating if you want to change seasons. Seasons are locked to the servers, meaning every week they change, you can't change them in game by moving ahead seasons for example. Each season though does look amazing in its own way, and adds diversity to game campaign.Forza Horizon 4 is a beautiful game, well-polished and full of cars and stunning environments. One more for the casual crowd but fun nonetheless, a fantastic celebration of car culture.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just go over all the things wrong with this godforsaken game.1. If youre running this on an nvidia GPU, it will absolutely refuse to run properly on any drivers after version 522.25. If you try and run it on recent drivers, it WILL crash every 10 to 15 minutes, losing your progress.2, I have been getting constant connectivity issues every time I play online. I've tried like 4 different networks and it continues to show me that poor connection message every single time. The slow-mo + rubberband effect disrupts your experience and is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying in races.3. The auto-save. The autosave feature is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ broken. There's a little loading sign which shows up beside the speedometer which shows up when the game is saving, Sometimes, that sign stays there forever, and at this point, you can just kiss all the progress you made in that session goodbye. Attempting to force a save by changing difficulty settings will just freeze and crash the game and you lose the progress you made after the last save.4. It's been said a million times already, but the engine sounds really do suck. I thought people were exaggerating but I was wrong. There's probably only like 5 actual different engine sounds pitch shifted here and there and slapped on cars randomly. A 4 cyl engine will sound the same as a VR6.5. Online/ranked adventure is totally dead gamemode. You legit have to wait about half an hour to get into a lobby with 3 other people. In co-op races, you'll most likely find players IN YOUR OWN TEAM who'll try to run you off the track because you're passing them.I havent got much praise to sing. It used to be a brilliant game but Microsoft have left it to die in favour of FH5, which by the way, has its own set of problems. Just dont buy this game, its not worth it in 2023. After the recent patch, the game seems to work perfectly fine on my PC (1050Ti) even with the latest drivers. No crashes, no infinite save icon (yet), very few connection issues. For the most part, it seems to be fixed for me, but it reportedly refuses to run on AMD systems now. It works fine for me but I can't say the same for everyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is obnoxiously flamboyant to the point it's annoying.  There's a "spin the wheel" game where you can win a bugatti veyron, but then the wheel will tick over to the next prize, a pink sweater you can dress your character in.  Whiskey Tango Foxtrot.  But at least it's not as bad as some stupid emoji dance you can make your character do when they win...oh wait, no, it is.The clutch isn't a real clutch, it's just a button you push while selecting the gear.  If you're stopped you don't need to push in the clutch to stop the engine from stalling.  For supposedly one of the best car enthusiast games I would have appreciated a fully working clutch.  The shifting mode is determined by your difficulty level, not by the actual car, so you tend to have go through the setting when you get done driving a fully manual four speed like a 71' Dodge Charger to a 14' Dodge Charger with an slap stick 8 speed automatic.  WHISKEY TANGO FOXTROT.  I ain't got time to shift through 8 gears.  It's an automatic for a reason!Just the whole game is obnoxious, but I've already paid for it so I guess I'll keep playing :(So to some it up, this game is great if you want to feel like you're driving a car but you don't actually want the work behind driving a car.  And again, it's obnoxiously flamboyant.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially got Forza Horizon 5; the benchmark race ran fine but the game did not load because of a memory access exception. So I decided to try the Previous Version. It didn't seem to look all that different from the new game.Forza Horizon 4 is the best racing game that I've ever played. I am familiar with racing-serious games like Need For Speed and Gran Turismo. Forza Horizon 4 feels good. The cars feel heavy as they should, and the physics is as real as it can be with 'fun' as a factor in gameplay. I'm playing Civilization 6 and Disco Elysium, and I thought this game would be a great break for my Left Hemisphere. I let my Left hand manage 5 keys and it's all Muscle Memory once you get the hang of it in a few hours. It isn't some guilty pleasure game either. The mechanics is very sophisticated and the handling of your machine is a matter of razor-sharp timing and instinct-driven road negotiation. There are several annoying things about this game though. To start with, the good awful music makes driving a cringe-cruise. You can turn down the Radio to [1] and fire up Winamp feat Prodigy to address that. The characters are of funny design as well. You get to pick among a small pickle of protagonists who are supposed to represent the 'typical' gamer: lean, boring, 'jeans and t-shirt' wearing youths with social inadequacies. Some of the NPCs in the game, who I think might be professional racers, have better body frames, presence, and less social awkwardness. Reminder: You are just a Gamer and not a Racer. But hey, Forza 4 is set in Britain, so it's not like we're looking for high standards or substance. There is a great deal of Cheesing that happens in the game. Sometimes your vehicle just smothers out of control as though it is possessed by some wannabe Phallic-God programmer. This happens during every race that matters. The [R]ewind feature, when it's available that is, addresses some of the cheese with 'let's navigate around the Game Master with Time Travel'. All in all, the game is worth every penny or so of the 20$ I invested in it. Get serious with Civilization 6 and Disco Elysium; let go with Forza! Enjoy the company of the Bristol-pack and stale beer.

They did not issued a fix neither assisted the players in the discussion topics. The devs simply pin a few possible solutions and don't care about the rest. So it's up to you to fix the game you paid for.Secondly, i just found out that this month's update is having issues with steering wheels (And many other players are experiencing the same as me). Notice that this is the update after the one the game wouldn't start. (So, two updates in a row broke the gameplay.)Everytime you get something new in this game, you'll also get a hard time to fix what the devs broke..So, steer clear from this game if you don't want to have headaches fixing this every time an update comes out... Because i'm gonna be honest here, half of the time that i spent playing FH4, i was having either issues with my steering wheel freezing in-game, my game not starting or some other dumb issue that could have been avoided if someone payed attention to what they're doing over at PGG.Is it worth it in a big sale and with a low price ? Probably... But is it worth it full price ?? Not in a million years.

_childDocuments_.review: No!No? Why do I say no you ask? Well, the answer to that question my friends is very simple, ask yourself this. _childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game to review. The overall gameplay is pretty good, but the progression is extremely wonky due to the randomized prize system. There's little reason to ever load into a race with slow cars (even though the AI cars will be given cars of similar "rank", you still want to be the fastest car in the field), and only a handful of car categories are mandatory to use (mostly offroad vehicles), so you can legitimately just take one car, tune it to the max, and use it to clear the overwhelming majority of the single-player game. The side missions all force you into specific cars, and some of those are fun challenges, while others are miserable - missions with "gotchas" and tight time limits. They don't all tell you what the 3-star time limit is, forcing you to load back in, sit through the cutscene again, and try again. Which brings me to the real reason I have to mark this game as not recommended.The loading times.The loading times are freaking abysmal. I'm playing with this game on an SSD and the loading times are sometimes upwards of a minute. If you do missions or races in story mode, they're typically two minutes long or so. Between the loading times and the unskippable cutscenes, you're often spending more time sitting there doing nothing than playing the game. That's unforgiveable in a game like this.And in multiplayer? Forget it. Multiplayer's even worse. There's a waiting period of a couple minutes to get things set up (which is understandable, people have to join the lobby/queue/whatever), then you have to wait for everyone to load in, then you have to wait for car selection, then you have to wait to load the track... there's multiple loading screens along the way and you legitimately sit there for about 5 minutes between races that last about 2 minutes. The developers really need to sit down with a pair of stopwatches, play the game, and time how much time they actually spend playing and how much time they spend sitting there staring at a screen that's doing nothing. It's astounding a game from a company as major as Microsoft is allowed to exist in this state. I'm not sure if this is exclusively a PC issue or if the Xbox version is the same way, but it's a travesty. This has all the makings of a good game, except you only spend about a third to a half of your time actually playing the game.Don't get me started on the unskippable 30-second long ads for the DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only had this game for three days and I can already say that this is one of the best games I've played, and that's coming from someone who doesn't usually play racing games. Starting with the graphics they are absolutely stunning for a game like this, the attention to detail on the crashed cars and the fact that your cars can actually interact with the space around you instead of just crashing instantly is great too. The soundtrack of the game is also some of the most well put together I've seen, from how the radio practically goes away when your going through tunnels to how it muffles when you go into the menu really gives you a feel of the effort the sound designers put into this. You also have radio hosts for each of the 5 (I think) radio stations who chat with the people listening and announce events that are going on in the world. The map, don't get me started on the map, it has so many different locations each with painstaking detail put into them, I feel like I'm traversing the map for the first time each and every time I drive across it. Now onto the gameplay because even if everything else is great a game can only be as good as the content in it. Your never gonna run out of things to do in this game. In the beginning before you become a horizon driver you already have access to most of what the game has to offer. You have Road, Dirt, Street, and Cross country racing, all ran by amazingly voice acted NPC's and many various campaigns you can do. Once you become a fully fledged horizon driver (About 6-7 hours of gameplay in) you get access to even more thing to do including but not limited to, multiplayer parties, #FORZATHON an event that lets you do various different minigames to earn rewards for the #FORZATHON shop, the battle royale gamemode; a race where you try to knock as many players into the "storm" as possible, and many other things that I don't have time to cover. If you do all of this and still aren't satisfied then you can settle on collecting, customizing, and optimizing cars for different, weather conditions, race formats, and styles of driving. Now onto the downsides of which I could only find two, those being the price and the fact that it occasionally crashes, I personally think that the price is the lesser of the two problems because you will totally be getting your moneys worth, now the crashing on the other hand really needs to be fixed, I'm not sure if its just my computer or what but I have lost about a half an hours worth of customizing my car to one of said crashes, causing me to totally restart I was able to recover though and I only lost 30 minutes so I'm fine with it. Needless to say I will 100% be coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off with an info that I love this game and so I recommend it to anyone who seeks some action and cool driving mechanics.I've been playing on game pad so far and I must admit that the further into the game (I play on pretty realistic settings with any helpers off) the more game punishes you for not having steering wheel or pedals.If you don't want to lose your freaking mind then I suggest not playing for 3 stars in every story event with same setup as mine.Of course I've been annoyed by random AI on the road during some of the events because to get 3 stars in some you need be pretty accurate and the worst feeling ever to be at the highest speed possible, getting into the curve just right, and meeting the front of the AI car.. xDI haven't played multiplayer because I'm old-style solo car games kind of guy. And I'm enjoying it a lot...but it seems to be pretty multiplayer oriented anyway so don't get your hopes up. There is no story line if you expected one.I feel this game also suffers from some kind of off-road mainstream as the normal racing is basically limited to one events chain whereas off-road is basically main thing for everything. There still are some cool streets to race though, so that's okay.Skills system is f-ing bad. I mean it's not satisfying, getting points and streaks means nothing to me. I feel almost insulted by how the system works. No, drifting is apparently not the way to go, just f-ing smash things around, jump couple of times, smash things, do a 180 and repeat. Also have I mentioned smashing things is important?Overall I believe the game is nice, there are a lot of cars and a lot of fun, but I see significant flaws in game systems and also - which because of the scale of the game is quite obvious - level design on a lot of races. There are community ones so that's sorting this issue out a bit.Buy on a special price. Not full. Especially now that there is Forza Horizon 5 on the way :)

_childDocuments_.review: My PC is more than capable of running the game, but due to reasons beyond my mortal comprehension, the game refuses to launch. It opens the splash screen, then proceeds to sit there for 2-3 minutes and does many of multiple things. From causing all my monitors to go black, seizing my PC, giving me "Program exception" errors that seem to never get fixed, and when one of them are, it gives me another one; I've tried everything under the sun and my ability to make this game run, from uninstalling other programs that supposedly cause issue, uninstalling or disabling Anti-Virus software and Windows Defender, Troubleshooting, everything.Nothing seems to ever get this game past the splash screen and when it does get past it, it blacks out my monitor and disables my mouse and keyboard. I don't know what else to do, how else to fix it, or if its even my fault that it doesn't work, but I can say with utmost certainty that as much fun as this game looks; It's far more problematic and a chore to even get working if you can even get to that point without it crashing. Maybe I should've bought the Microsoft Store version... Or maybe Microsoft should learn how to make a better product that doesn't require you to jump through hoops in hopes that you MIGHT get to play the game you paid $40, $60, or even $100 for. The plethora of problems this game has for some people and the time and energy it takes to fix them far outweighs the reason to buy it. Maybe a hotfix or update might fix this game, but seeing how this is a 3-year-old game... It's absolutely ludicrous that it has any of these problems to begin with. For Christ sake, I'd honestly just rather have them make it so the Steam version sends you straight to the Microsoft Store/Game Bar (Similarly to State of Decay 2) if it meant I'd be able to at least launch, and more importantly PLAY, the product I paid for.Update: So, the memory leak and other problems I had were solved not buy an update to the game, but a windows update. At least I have faith that CDPR will fix CP2077 (and have done a lot with patch 1.2) but I don't expect anything close to this will come from Playground Games.I thought it might be my system so I did the usual test when I find a buggy and poorly made game.1. Wipe entire system, reset bios to clear any overclocks, set GPU to stock clocks2. Clean install Windows 10 via internet3. Install latest drivers for graphics, motherboard, etc4. Install Steam and download only the affected game5. Shutdown and cold boot the PC6. Play for an hourResults? Crashed in the 4th race mid-corner about 20mins in. Reboot and it crashed about 30mins in.It's not my PC. Considering it's a Core i9 10900K, ASUS RTX 3080 Strix, 32GB RAM.Absolutely wonderful game let down by poor porting to the steam platform.Edit (06/04/21) - Currently awaiting Update 34 with apparent fixes for crashing. Will update review if there's any change to the CTD issue.Edit (07/04/21) - Update 34 releasedStill crashing to desktop, just more frequently now. _childDocuments_.review: This is obviously very subjective, but here’s my review.  Spoiler Alert: 9.5/10 from me.Overview:I was a PlayStation gamer for many years prior to branching out to PC gaming a few years ago, so I never got to experience the Forza games until recently.  Forza Horizon 5 was my introduction to the series.  I really enjoyed it and scored it an 8/10 in my Steam review.  I then decided to try out Forza Horizon 4, and I just love it, can’t get enough.  FH4 is a fantastic game and far superior to FH5 in my opinion.  Driving / Difficulty:I generally opt for more simulator-type driving games, i.e. realistic driving.   It’s safe to say that this game definitely does not fall in to that category, instead leaning more towards the arcade style... there’s nothing wrong with that at all!  There are 8 difficulty (Drivatar) levels to choose from, ranging from from new player to unbeatable.  This allows the game to cater to most skill levels… unless you’re either really bad, or play like Jarno Opmeer or SuperGT (lucky you!!).  There’s also a huge amount of assists which you can opt for, such as, auto transmission, TCR, STM, ABS, assisted steering, assisted braking, damage on/off, tyre wear on/off, and driving line.  Whatever way you choose to play is up to you, but there are options to suit almost everyone.  Gameplay:The FH4 world is outstandingly beautiful.  The landscape is stunning, and I love how it changes through the seasons.  The attention to detail in the world design is superb.  The story was… meh.  Not memorable, with some very tedious moments and a few non-skippable cutscences.  But it was more interesting that FH5’s story imo.  The game has heaps self-contained storylines and businesses too which are fun, a nice challenge, and encourage you to explore parts of the map you may not otherwise experience.  There's a vast range of cars to earn (~500) by completing various races, events, stories, accolades etc.  You can also win cars, money, cosmetic items etc. through Wheelspins.  The game is very generous with how easy Wheelspins are to earn, especially when compared with how stingy many other game series can be.  Cars can be customised via upgrades and tuning options.  These are great to experiment with to find the right set-up for your favourite cars and to fine tune to suit specific types of races.  I love this feature personally, but for those who don't, there's also a feature that allows tunes made by other members of the community be downloaded.  You can also create your own paintjobs and liveries with infinite possibilities.  There’s endless amounts of stuff to do, along with seasonal (weekly) championships, challenges, and events.  I haven’t even mentioned all the PvP and user-created challenges - people's creativity will never cease to amaze me.  You’ll never be bored!!  After a hard day at work / uni, it's just nice (therapeutic even!) to drive around like a complete lunatic destroying fences, trees, drifting, racing at stupidly high speed, doing massive jumps etc. all while earning points and combos to gain fast XP.  It's even more fun with friends!  The tracks are decent and offer lots of variety in racing styles from drifting to cross-country to circuit to rally.  Performance:I run everything on max settings, and FH4 genuinely looks phenomenal.  A number of the negative reviews I've read mention issues with performance.  The game runs fine for me, with just a couple of minor stuttering issues and one or two freezes in ~100 hours of gameplay.  I’ve had no connection issues to friends / other players either.TL;DR – FANTASTIC game if you're looking for a fun, open-world driving experience.  Lots of styles of racing and tonnes of cars to choose from.  Looks incredible.  Lots to do.  9.5/10 for the fun factor.
