_childDocuments_.review: Its an amazing game, hell probably one of the best racing games out there. It mixes sim like racing with arcade style racing in such a flawless manner that I often think to myself "Why can't all racing games be like this?". Its fun and a very chill game. However, if I'm to criticise this game, the very praise I give the game becomes its dark side. The game just gives out rewards, leaving the player unsatisfied with the achievements they receive. For example, in Horizon 1, each purchase of a car was calculated, as every race event in that game required the player to meet certain criteria when entering the event. This made the player competitive when it comes to races as they have to win in order to get money so that they can buy a great car. But in Horizon 4, the event changes according to the car wit which you enter. Yes, it becomes more player friendly, but i feel it removes the challenge aspect. A game can be in the form of a stress free capsule like ABZU, but Forza Horizon isn't such a title. You have the open world which is amazing and calm to drive in, but the races are to challenging. The game fails to balance challenge with the sense of relaxation. What I'm trying to say is that the sense of progression is not present in Horizon 4. You can complete 3/4th of the game with the cars they provide for free in the initial stages. There is no sense of achievement when one shows in a Chiron in Horizon 4's multiplayer as the obvious thought which goes into the opposition's mind is "Oh, they must've gotten it in a wheel spin!" Even though the player might've played and bought the car with the credits he earned. To complain that a game is giving out huge in-game rewards for free feels like a douchy thing to say. But it removes the challenge from the game. With that being said, Horizon 4 isn't a bad game. Its an amazing game. The graphics, the gameplay all checks out. But I'm not so happy with the reward system. Its too REWARDING. Balance it out, THEN you have the best racing game in the world

name: Read Only Memories: NEURODIVER
detailed_description: You Are A Psychic Agent Take on the role of ES88, a young esper employed by MINERVA, a powerful organization specializing in information science, neurotechnology, and extrasensory phenomena. She has been tasked with tracking down Golden Butterfly, a mysterious psychic entity hiding in and fragmenting the memories of Neo-San Francisco's citizens. Who are they? Why are they doing this? And how will you stop them? The Neurodiver The Neurodiver is a bioengineered psychic creature made to assist in boosting an esper's natural abilities. With its help, you'll be able to collect clues and thoughts in your subject's memories in an effort to piece together distorted fragments inside them, pushing Golden Butterfly out! New and Old Read Only Memories: NEURODIVER is a return to the vibrant sci-fi world of Neo-San Francisco from 2064: Read Only Memories with a whole new story, and a whole new cast of characters. It's an adventure that newcomers can easily dive into, but those familiar with the original game might notice a lot of familiar faces making a comeback! An Fm Sound Sensation! NEURODIVER's soundtrack is inspired by the OPNA/YM2608 sounds of the PC-8801 and PC-9801 series of computers, brought to you by Scarlet Moon composer and sound designer, Ken 'coda' Snyder ( Tree of Knowledge )! If you love the sharp and glossy tones generated by late 80s and early 90s FM chips found in a variety of old computers, sound cards, arcades and consoles, then you'll be right at home here. name: Rollerdrome
detailed_description: Rollerdrome is a BAFTA award-winning third person action shooter that seamlessly blends high octane combat with fluid motion to create an action experience like no other. Dominate with style in cinematic, visceral combat where kills net you health and pulling off tricks and grinds provide you ammunition, in this adrenaline-pumping action shooter. The year is 2030. In a world where corporations rule and the lines between reality and performance are blurred, the public are kept distracted by the violence and excess of a brutal new blood sport — Rollerdrome. Will you have what it takes to become the Rollerdrome champion and unravel the mysteries behind the Matterhorn corporation’s true intentions? From Roll7, the minds that brought you the award winning and critically acclaimed OlliOlli series comes Rollerdrome, an intense shooter-skater hybrid set in an evocative retrofuture. Key Features: A third person action shooter like no other – an original hybrid shooter-skater that blends high octane, visceral combat with fluid movement and tricking mechanics into one complementary and challenging whole. A test of skill – Take on a unique challenge throughout the Rollerdrome tournament. Establish your dominance in the field with online leaderboards and push yourself to the limit with the unlockable 'Out For Blood' mode for the most extreme test of skill and agility. An original identity – An all-new fully original soundtrack that merges iconic era sounds and tones with cutting edge production to provide a heart-thumping backdrop to the carnage, brought to life with a unique comic-book inspired art style. A dark conspiracy – Discover a mysterious, sinister plot in this distinct retrofuture universe.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater in that you have a checklist of things to do in each level but made even more complex with the addition of gun-based objectives.  It is hectic keeping your combo and ammo up, dodging sniper bullets, shooting rockets out of the sky while swapping guns to get specific kills off specific enemies. I can already tell this has a high skill ceiling and it will be fun to get better and better at it..
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: (For any reviews saying the game is "TOO HARD" If you went into the options you would have seen options to make it easy, examples, Invincibility/Unlimited ammo/unlimited slow motion/change the damage taken for your character, skip challenges to progress to the next stages) Below is my review, just wanted to mention to the dummies that never seem to make an effort in checking the accessibility options in games. I seen the Dev Paul on Twitter prototype this game years back and it looked amazing, happy to see all the positive and well earned good reviews for it, I highly recommend Rollerdrome, it's extremely fun! And just gets more and more hectic, I wish more game developers out there took the top tier fun and innovation of some of the great titles out there, combined them and gave it a little twist of its own, because this title certainly does that. It's taking the likes of Tony Hawks/Jet Set Radio, and mixing it with Max Payne slow motion shooting and the insanity of Doom almost, just enemies trying to murder you from all directions near the end of the game. I'm excited to see what's next for this dev/devs

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a few negative reviews on the game's difficulty, so I'm just going to say this: unless you care about leaderboards, or are a hardcore 'easy mode is for suckas' gamer, don't hesitate to use the assists. If it makes the game more fun for you, go for it!This game is super fun and addictive. I'm not typically into sports but this has been a blast to play. The perfect game when you just want to shoot things and challenge yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Tony Hawk meets Max Payne.This game hits the sweet spot for a fast-paced violent shooter that is tough but fair. Very arcadey in its mechanics and presentation, once you get the controls down you can really reach a flow state during the intense battles. Dodge a shot, grenade an area of enemies, head toward a vert ramp for a 540 grab to get your ammo back, line up a crit shot with your shotgun in bullet-time to finish an enemy and heal yourself, then pull out your pistols to take out incoming missiles. Just pure reaction -- high-adrenaline action.Highly recommended if you're into challenging shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's a skater / shooter / puzzle game. The skater and shooter aspects are self explanatory  so I guess I should go into how this is a puzzle game.   For each map, the game gives you a list of challenges to complete. Some of them you'll achieve just by beating the map, but the others require you to collect tokens or kill enemies in a particular fashion. This means that in order to complete challenges AND get a high score, you can't let the combo meter drop. You need to think about the enemy types, placement and ammunition at all times- plotting out how to best approach the collectibles while taking out enemies at a pace that allows for exploration as well as keeping the combo. Easier said than done, sometimes that means managing what order to take enemies out and which ones are faster to deal with when a combo is close to ending, all in order to give yourself a buffer to complete the challenges. In my opinion, playing it like a puzzle game is part of the fun.   Apart from that, the style is OFF THE CHARTS and the gameplay is fast paced. Exactly the kind of game I hoped it would be. If it holds up till the end, it'll be a favorite of mine for sure.Edit: It held up till the end!As far as the story goes, while there are interesting ideas and world building being hinted at, we don't really see any of it unfold. We hear announcers on the radio and get notes pinned to cork boards, but we never really interact with any people. It wasn't a deal breaker for me, and I understand it mainly serves as the set dressing for the gameplay, but if you're looking for a story focused game this may not be your cup of tea.   Having completed the main campaign, I have to say that it is MOST DEFINITELY a new favorite of mine. Where I feel lots of skater games get bogged down in the number of button presses needed to perform a combo, Rollerdrome keeps it simple to understand, but still has variety in its move set. All the weapons have their place in combat and it never felt like one was the obvious answer to everything. All in all, this game is such a breath of fresh air and I'm glad I found it. Highly recommended for anyone that enjoys some challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous art style and graphics which are kinda reminiscent of Moebius style.Rollerdrome gameplay is so damn satisfying it's an absolute blast to play while your in the groove and nail the tricks and combat.The controls are spot on, it certainly will take a while to get used to and master them but oh boy the possibilities this game offer you are awesome.The arenas are really well designed with many ramps and spots to wall grind or wall ride.Pretty much everything is here to have a good time, honestly it feels really good to play.Sadly the game is single player only and I imagine the game may be a bit short or might get repetitive after a while.Rollerdrome is still highly replayable if your the kind of person chasing the best scores.Man it would have been dope if there was some coop or pvp modes !

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a very important game for me. I’ve been following the development since it was just a clip of a concept posted by an indie dev. And said clip is actually the only reason I created a twitter account, specifically so I could follow the project. And now, four years later, Rollerdrome is out and unlike anything I ever could’ve imagined. It is hands down the most fun gaming experience I’ve ever had. Such a simple (and unique) concept expanded into a high paced and thrilling game. The controls and options of tricks may seem complex at first, but they are so tight and carefully constructed, that once you master them you are able to achieve some unbelievably cool moments. The gameplay would’ve been enough of a selling factor, I mean who wouldn’t want Tony Hawk Pro Skater mixed with Doom? But the biggest surprise was the story. It kept me completely engaged, and I was constantly rooting for Kara against the other side characters (who have so much personality even though they are never seen). The team created a beautiful world with complex and detailed lore that makes me even more enthralled with this game. Needless to say, I played through the entire campaign in one sitting, and will continue to replay this for the rest of my life. I love Rollerdrome, it’s the most fun game i’ve ever played, and i hope everyone can one day experience the excitement this game captures.  Thank you Roll 7 and thank you Paul.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: What if John Wick could skateboard?Or what would Tony Hawk Pro Skater look like if it had been a shooter?Rollderdrome gives us a gaming experience that is both action-packed and addictive in which you have to pull a lot of tricks & hits to defeat a whole army of soldiers and robots in each level!Watch gameplay from a later level in the game here: I think a lot of gamers who grew up around the millennium switch would like RollderDrome, this is undoubtedly a great game that is both immensely entertaining and nostalgic, also the appropriate soundtrack in the game ensures that your reflexes are on point!The plot of Rollerdrome revolves around a future dystopia in which players join the Rollerdrome to fight for a better life.It's run by an obviously corrupt supercorporation, which you'll slowly learn more about as you play through a backstory.Here you can watch videos of more levels:  In each level you will get a series of challenges that you must or can achieve, it is also very clearly described what you have to do,to unlock new levels you must have achieved a minimum of challenges, so you may get to a point where you will have to replay some levels to get some extra challenges, but that's no problem, playing the same one will never be different unless you train yourself to speedrun the levels, then you would dare to stick to a fixed route.For this title cel shaded graphics have been chosen with a rather abstract design.All this together creates a unique taste with its own and new identity.The fun of Rollerdrome is ultimately in getting a feel for the game. Feeling for the skates, feeling for the weapons, but especially feeling for the different arenas and opponents. Which targets pop up where and when, and most importantly, how do you best defeat which enemy?you will acquire all the weapons you can use during the first half of the game, it is then up to you to figure out which enemies take the most damage from which weapon, and which weapon works the best and fastest against certain to attack,you will therefore have to react quickly, decide quickly and, above all, anticipate a lot,the slow motion in the game is then a perfect tool that not only provides comfort but also great images that you can admire in the middle of the battle.The game is also fantastic on a steam deck!: Rollerdrome is unbelievably cool!Fast gameplay, cool action, an entertaining gameplay loop, high replay value and a delicious audiovisual sauce make Rollerdrome special.Rollerdrome also has perfect support for ultra-wide resolutions, you can see an example of this here:

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Max Payne meets Tony Hawk, but on rollerskates. There's a highly satisfying flow of doing tricks, shooting enemies, dodging attacks and playing around with reflex time (slowmotion). Increase your score by never stopping that flow and building up a combo. Get a high combo, complete objectives, kill your enemies as fast as possible within the allotted time and you win the match. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The way the game teaches you to get better and rewards you when you do should be an example to good game design. I wasn't able to do anything fancy at first and by completing challenges the game taught me tricks and mechanics and enabled me to perfect them. Best thing is I could complete those one by one without losing progression and honestly there was no frustration completing any part of the game.By the end of second campaign I was a god skating on the blood of my enemies and it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun.Honestly the game fxcks

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was stunned - the graphics, the music, the gameplay, the little story in the background. I enjoyed it, but after a few levels I hit a wall. I felt like the game was too difficult and I couldn't properly progress.But then it just clicked! And the gameplay became just so much more satisfying and fun, suddenly I found myself doing high combos and scores without noticing. Rollerdrome is a really good action game, with a pleasing style. There's even a new game plus mode!Although as much as I cherish and wanted to play this game badly, I didn't play for that long. And I worry that if I aimed to reach the high scores and finish the Out for Blood gamemode, the maps and enemies could become boring. The maps, even though some of them are different, don't stand out that much and the variety of enemies is not that high. But that's just a thought I had. Other than that, this game is wonderful!

_childDocuments_.review: imagine if Tony Hawk's Pro Skater had guns and bullet time. That's Rollerdrome in 11 words.In more words, Rollerdrome changes the difficult gameplay meta of Pro Skater 2 and 3 of having to just do grinds/manuals on a loop for 2 minutes in order to full combo so you can get a high score. Instead, you combo by killing enemies (aiming gives you bullet time), and you get a certain amount of time after each kill to do tricks before losing the combo. Doing tricks gives you more bullets. Getting hit makes you lose the combo faster. It's an conceptually simple loop but it is done perfectly here. The game starts strong, shooting basic enemies with pistols. You learn to perfectly dodge which plays like parrying. Then you get more guns and different enemies; the new guns countering the new enemies. The game keeps improving on itself and no mechanic feels like it's wasted, nor does any enemy feel like it's meaningless. This is a noticeable improvement over Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, where I almost never used grab tricks as grinding rails was strictly better. The bad part is that there isn't enough of a  built on this flawless foundation. I took 13 hours in this game to get 100% completion. It's short, even though it felt much longer. There's only one boss enemy in the main campaign, used twice (though it's a very fun boss). There's only 11 levels, and more than half are duplicated environments with different layouts. e.g. there's multiple "mall"-themed levels, but with distinct layouts of half pipes or rails for doing tricks on. The levels don't have much character even if they're very fun to play.Finally, there's the story. Rollerdrome takes place in a fascinating Demolition Man/Smash TV/Hunger Games style of dystopia where everyone loves a ultraviolent blood-sport of a game show. This is always an intriguing premise, and the game leaves you clues about the resistance, the totalitarian nature of society, the corruption behind the sport, etc. It wasn't much, but it got me emotionally invested.Except, you finish the game, and there's no ending! I can't even call this a spoiler as there's nothing to spoil. You beat the final level and you become the champion! All the backstage intrigue and the resistance build up to nothing.I love this game. I love the gameplay. I mildly enjoyed the story. But Rollerdrome's fatal flaw is that it didn't take many risks and didn't try to overstay its welcome. It's a phenomenal game as it is now, and I enjoyed every second I played it. There's not a lot of games that offer that level of consistency, most have grindy (in a bad way) or boring parts. But I can't get rid of the feeling that this could've been one of the greatest games of all time, on par with the original Tony Hawk Pro Skater games.I would recommend Rollerdrome to adults that own a Steam Deck and only get a few minutes at a time to play, but still want a game that's focused on pure . It's short, sweet, and fun. I got through it over a few weeks just playing it on-and-off the shuttle bus to work. It's a hardcore game for someone who doesn't have the time to be a hardcore gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: This is entirely on me, I'll admit this going in. I should have done more research and watched more gameplay videos.I read a review from a website stating "it's an easy game to play that makes you feel awesome while you're playing it". Nothing could be further from the truth. This game is very difficult. I'm sure the "git gud" gamers will disagree with me, but I was thinking this might be an indie gem along the lines of Neon White, where winning the rounds is effectively an afterthought, the true challenge is in doing it quickly and finding new and exciting ways to do it. Instead, I've reached the Semi-Finals in the campaign and don't see a way where I'll actually be good enough to progress any further in the game, more importantly I'm not motivated to do so because it's not an enjoyable experience to progress (again, unless you really enjoy the masochism of difficult games).After about the third level, there's a tremendous spike in difficulty. Levels are just overwhelmed with 5 different types of enemies all bombarding you at once, there's never actually time to pull off full tricks as you have to spend time dodging, every enemy takes about 6 hits with the shotgun (even when perfectly executing slug shots), and forget having a chance to charge the laser gun or whatever fully, again... you won't have time as every enemy is in the middle of shoving a missile or an acid bomb or several other projectiles up your character's... skates.Overall, I guess consider this a recommendation if that's the type of game you enjoy. Unfortunately, it's not for me. I may just take a break from it and try again in a day or two, but I feel by that point I'll have forgotten all of the controls and I'll just find myself even more frustrated. More casual gamers who were looking for "Tony Hawk but you shoot a few dudes while doing cool tricks", that's NOT what this game is. People who were looking for "Doom but on Roller Skates", welcome to Hell, enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It’s very hard not to recommend a game that can take two genre vehicles and put them on the same road, opposite of one another, to create an explosive crash. Unlike watching a real life crash in a video where your curiosity becomes flinching regret, this is the sort of accident that will make you cheer for more. is a game that wants you to be cool and puts you on a path to succeed, the moment you start it up. You struggle to get an A rank for your first few games, but somehow manage to piecemeal the challenges. The challenges feel displaced at first, but then you start learning that there’s a lot of depth to how you can move around through steadily increased momentum. At some point, you’ll start realizing little things like “Hey, these guns can combo into each other really well for taking down beefier enemies” and “Whoa, I can one-shot this enemy if I’m in super-reflex!” You reach a point where the challenge asks you to pull off the level all in one combo, and your brain is struggling to process how exactly you’ll accomplish this. And then you do it after several attempts. And then you do it effortlessly to the point that you’ve now S-ranked every level, both on regular and Out For Blood mode. When it’s over, you’ll marvel over how you once struggled to just get an A rank.It’s that type of experience.My only complaint is that I feel like the world, itself, could have used more fleshing-out, since the small bits of story we do get feel like disconnected filler. I like the Running Man aesthetic, but the Running Man made me want to explore its cynical dystopian world after watching it, whereas Rollerdrome’s world made me want to just chase S-ranks without too much care for the world at large. Doubling down on gameplay over story, ultimately though, was the right call for this first entry. I feel like Rollerdrome is a game that could have a lovely sequel with more levels, additional weapons, more enemies, and some mechanical-tech-pushing a la Ultrakill.Get this game if everything I’ve said sounds right up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: Grind: BFlip: YGrab: XDodge: RBOptionally, go into the steam overlay, and in the controller configuration, set the left stick to dpad buttons and the dpad to left stick move. You need to quickly double-tap directions and it's much more comfortable on a dpad, but the game doesn't let you bind weapon changing to the left stick natively.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Rollerdrome knows exactly what to focus on and what not to.It looks easy. Tricks are simple to execute and you can't bail. Weapons auto lock and the shooting is forgiving. In the training and early levels, I was worried it would feel on rails.Then, a few levels in, it becomes a bullet hell. All the assistance in the mechanics falls into place. You have to constantly shoot, dodge, jump, trick to reload, avoid falling off the map etc. You have to know which guns work for which enemies and switch in mid air. Breaking your combo even once can ruin your chance at a good score. If you could bail, or if aiming was totally free, it would be a frustrating mess.Much like with the OlliOlli games, Roll7 has focused on flow, style, and fun here. You're assisted just enough to feel like a Rollerdrome star without having your hand held. Achieving that perfect flow and hitting 20+ kill combos feels incredible and takes real concentration. There's a sublime comedy to bringing an enemy down to almost no health, realising you're out of ammo, and having to hit a backflip to reload.A wonderfully polished experience that takes risks on how it limits players and completely succeeds in its execution. I really hope they find success with Rollerdrome and can continue development with more arenas, more challenges etc. This game came out today and I already want DLC. Superb.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: A spectacular, fresh, exhilarating and laser focused shooter with so much style and a killer soundtrack. It’s firmly up there with my favourites.The Case of the Golden Idol was my game of 2022 but I think Rollerdrome would have given it a good run. Or skate. Speaking of which, my girlfriend said 'Do the mechs wear rollerskates?' A true visionary.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This is a big yes if you are confident in your ability. Rollerdome is a fast paced time trials tony-hawk style shooter that looks fantastic (love Kim Hu's art on this) and plays very well. It's a satisfying ride for sure, even if some levels take a few tries to perfect. It's a shorter game but for the quality and synergy between the jet set/tony hawk style gameplay meets combat the money is worth the experience. The challenges make for a bit more playability too.NOTE: The game may be challenging to those that have never played a game of this genre but you can slow down play-time or give yourself unlimited bullets and ADS focus time so it's more accessible. If you're still having trouble with the challenges within each level you can deactivate them.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Short story but extremely cool action. Lots of slow mo dodging through the air while shooting. It reminds me of Max Payne meets Tony Hawk. Worth buying and playing through for sure. If you're someone really good at doing tricks and running combos I imagine you could get really into the online leaderboards for the game.The game could really use more substance though. There are only 4 different graphical environments. Every match is a "kill everyone" match in a circular, open arena. I'd like if things were mixed up more. Different objectives beyond just eliminate everyone. Arenas with closed off areas like hallways. You fight two "bosses" but they're barely different. Every enemy is a faceless personality-less template. Imagine if there were several different bosses with a name, personality and gimmick? That could really mix things up. The story seemed to lack substance as well. It seems like it's just kind of there to give an excuse to show off more of the cool 70s/80s art style. Maybe I just made the wrong choices but it seems like nothing I did really mattered and nothing was explained.Don't let all my complaints stop you from buying the game though, it's absolutely really good.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: In Rollerdrome, you play as Kara Hassan, the rookie entering the Rollerdrome, a bloody roller skate competition with the only requirement to kill the House players to bring in points, and maybe test a few new weapons for the company...The year is 2030, in a beautiful 70s cel-shaded aesthetic alternative world, within a fascist state with two factions opposing each other politically. Rollerdrome, the popular sport, is the sure way to gather a crowd who wants to watch a macabre spectacle. The 2030 version of the Coliseum.In terms of gameplay, Rollerdrome hits the mark, which is the most important for games like this. Skating and doing tricks is fun, and so is aiming your shotgun at an enemy. Doing tricks will reload your weapons, which helps to kill your enemies, and you are doing so with the rhythm of catchy synth wave music.  Your enemies are also just as heavily armed and will quite literally fire rockets at you. Dodging is essential as it is fast-paced and reminds you that you risk your life at every turn. The bold will be granted slow motion as managing to dodge at the last second will enable you to slow time and attack much harder for a short time. It also adds some serious cool factors to your every move.The tricks are easy enough to pull off, but it did feel like the input wasn’t always accurate (or maybe I’m just bad); there are about 20 different moves you can do, each giving you a different number of points. Rollerdrome is also pretty tricky to master but easy to take on; the challenges will keep you busy if you are a completionist chasing top scores and offer you quite the replayability. Should you be competitive, your scores are translated into global leaderboards, and maybe you could become the real Rollerdrome champion. Still on replayability, once the primary campaign is over, another mode, much more challenging, opens up to you. The animations are fluid until they aren’t anymore. Indeed, Kara can’t fall, and as such, it can result in clunky movements and moves you didn’t intend to take. Sadly, the biggest letdown for me was the story. Because it was genuinely exciting, and very little was done with it. While I understand that it wasn’t the focus of the game, I can’t help but feel that so much more could have happened in detail even, or just more elements during the exploration phase as you remain hungry for more as the political situation is extremely tense with murders we could link to both factions and quite the political intrigue unfolding before your very eyes unless Rollerdrome is a statement about society’s being able to numb itself bad enough to accept to call sport a game like Rollerdrome that is only profiting to Matterhorn this huge, hungry capitalistic bloc. Food for thought. While the experience was great, Rollerdrome is better enjoyed for its gameplay, and it’s better not to stray away from that too much. The environment is all remarkably similar, and after 30 minutes, you’ve seen it all. There are two major boss fights throughout the game, and it turns out to be the same boss.Finally, Rollerdrome is quite the explosion of action with entertaining gameplay, widely compared to Max Payne doing Tony Hawk’s tricks on rollerblades and with reason because this is precisely how it feels, and it is just great.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I had a fantastic time playing Rollerdrome but I was able to 100% the base campaign in just under 5 hours. This is probably the greatest flaw of this game. It doesn't have enough length nor enough challenge to warrant its ludicrous price tag and I'm sure this is what led to this game ultimately not succeeding even though it's tremendous fun to play.I've read tons of complaints saying the game is far too difficult. I would encourage replaying the tutorial if you feel similarly. It's extremely easy to beat the game along with all its challenges if you can master the perfect dodge which has a very generous time to execute. Even if you do take damage, health is very easily recoverable.A large omission for this type of game is some sort of horde or endless mode. I've seen the bonus campaign, but it retains the same structure as the main story where the match just ends when you defeat all the enemies, killing all the momentum and flow you had. Some sort of endless mode with escalating combat encounters would add huge replayability as well as address my prior complaints about difficulty.EDIT: I have now completed the "Out For Blood" campaign as well as all of its challenges with 8 and a half hours of game time. It's certainly harder, but I still believe this game needs a couple other modes to truly excel and justify the price tag.I hope a sequel is in the works because with Rollerdrome and OlliOlli World, Roll7 has clearly demonstrated that they deeply understand what makes a video game actually fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: : If you’ve mostly only played on-foot shooters it can be tricky to play, but it’s a breath of fresh air if you’re willing to learn unfamiliar mechanics. The game itself is short, but quite replayable.If you’re reading this review, chances are you already know what the game is about, how it looks blablabla. I think it’s a worthwhile purchase if you’re looking for something different, but it’s a relatively short game unless you really like getting  at games. Not to discredit the experience, far from it, I think being resourceful with the maps and focusing the game on mastery is perfectly valid. But on this review I personally just want to focus on my experience learning the game.My relevant gaming background has been of a good amount of on-foot PvP and PvE shooters on mouse and keyboard, or in general games where you’re mostly handling weapons one way or the other, but I have played absolutely zero “trick games”, let alone on a controller.It’s fair to say that I got the “weapon” part of the game fairly quickly, while on the tricks side I was just flailing my body in unremarkable ways, and thus reloading pretty slowly. My brain just wasn’t wired to think about movement like that. I say this just to set expectations for people with a similar background, I personally understood that tricks were a part of the game and I was willing to learn.With that said, I think the tutorial and UI, as of writing, could do a better job explaining the tricks.My main gripe is with the grabs mechanic: essentially, while you’re in the air, you can move your left stick, potentially multiple times, and then by pressing X you perform a pose, depending on the left stick sequence executed. The tutorial isn’t making sure that the player understands how to do different grabs, though, and the UI is not telling you what grab you’re doing as you’re moving about the stick. By the end of the tutorial, what I understood was that the left stick input was just  input, not a sequence, and I was very confused when the game told me to do an up-down-X grab for a challenge. I did understand grabs by the end of the campaign, but it happened while , rather than through playing the game. What could have helped immensely is if the current left stick sequence was just shown to me on the screen. Considering how the game does have icon terminology for it already, it should be pretty easy for the player to draw the connection between what a certain challenge is telling you, and the arrows that appear on the screen while they’re flailing in the air.Another UI gripe while I was learning was that I found the weapons wheel to be too eager to disappear. With how time-critical some moments can be, I would have preferred if the game was showing me that dpad up is for the pistols all the time, rather than me having to guess which dpad button it was, probably get it wrong, and  being shown the weapon wheel. While my brain understands that pressing 1 on the keyboard brings up the primary weapons, 2 brings up secondary weapons et cetera, I had no idea what “dpad up” meant, and I had to learn it by getting it wrong. This could easily be made smoother with an option that shows a reduced size weapon wheel in those situations, just to remind the player of the mappings.When it comes to the controls, they definitely made sense after getting accustomed to them, but they definitely were a learning curve. It was exacerbated by the fact I was actively getting shot while figuring them out. Again, calmly thinking about the whole thing and replaying the tutorials did help, which are luckily easily accessible. On that note, tutorials can be annoying when you’re doing them the first time, but I quickly realized I would’ve been hopeless without them, so I think they’re worth doing and redoing, albeit not 100% perfect.As for actually playing the game and finishing the campaign, it was pretty alright. You are essentially forced to replay previous levels to do a certain number of challenges to move forward, but I think it helps with pacing yourself and making sure you actually are ready for the harder maps. You unlock a harder version of the campaign after finishing the last level, and as of right now I plan on taking a crack at it.Ultimately I am satisfied with my purchase. It was legitimately tiring, but it was an interesting game to learn. There is a lot of juggling of weapon choice, positioning and doing tricks, but boy do you feel the rush when you pull it off.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing! This game is meant to take place in the year 2030, but the retro / nostalgic vibes are there, and just hit so hard;Rollerdrome's artistic style is simply perfect; as for the graphics / animation, they're at the same time simple, well defined, in an old 80s' comics way, enhanced with today's tech possibilities. Concerning the music, it's equally flawless and marries the visual aspect of the game in a perfect way too, still much 80s' inspired apparently.As for the controls, they are simple while hard to master: the main tutorial takes place at the very beginning of the game, in one full go, while some additional ones are added as you'll progress through the game, with new weapons and techniques; they might seem tedious to all memorize, fortunately they are available in the start menu. The controls are very well responsive, although a tiny bit unusual, as you'll have to marry different combinations of buttons in order to create figures while pressing buttons a certain length of time, such as for jumping. Handling well the directions can be tricky at times, as L-padding "up" won't necessarily mean going forward for instance, it's a subtle technique to use well both directional pads.Well...I really love this type of games: it's original, quite unique, incredibly nostalgic while being innovative. Quite a bit hard, but largely worth at least a try.. . . and even if you end up killed, you'll sure die smiling :' )

_childDocuments_.review: A slick and satisfying high octane arena combat game. It's easy to pick up, tricky to master and hits a perfect stride of challenge and fun factor. It's Tony Hawk meets Max Payne, with all the quality that implies. Controls are tight, mechanics are very well thought out. Oh and it's all wrapped in a gorgeous vector art style which looks insanely beautiful in motion.My only caveat is that advancement through the game does require completing specific challenges to progress, so arenas are designed to be replayed and mastered. That might be a turn off to some who want a straight line to the finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is relentlessly overwhelming.It's the sort of challenge you'd get after meticulously placing the late-game skill checks of Tony Hawk, Bayonetta and Doom Eternal into a cohesive whole. It is merciless in its expectation that you'll be bringing your sharpest reflexes and absolute focus. Indeed - when you play Rollerdrome your brain must be dedicated to Rollerdrome - as breaking concentration guarantees a break in combo.But there's a mathematical perfection in that difficulty, earn a time slow down and you'll have to make a split-second decision on how to cause the most damage with whatever ammo you’ve got sitting in reserve. Do you chip away at a nearby tank to guarantee a safe landing or risk sniping a far-away polybeam to give your combo a longer buffer? Rollerdrome tests strategy and resourcefulness as frequently as it tests precision, but it still leaves ample room for player expression and creativity. You’re rewarded with bonus points for each unique trick you perform so there’s a lot to keep track of during the thick of combat, even my ADHD-riddled brain is thrown into a teeth-gritting heart-pounding flow state.This is all presented through brutally sharp stencil outlines and sound design that nails the rupture of large stadium sports. Rollerdrome is loaded in atmosphere, I'm particularly fond of the short "run up" to an arena - a much needed moment of calm and anticipation in contrast to the violence and chaos of the match itself.Seeing this game falling short of an "overwhelmingly positive" rating initially surprised me, but the more I think about it the more I realise Rollerdrome isn't for everyone. If you've not played the prerequisite inspirations that are being built upon here then that oppressive atmosphere could feel suffocating, especially with a rather monotonous tutorial. On the other hand, if you are within the audience that Rollerdrome is targeting, then you're looking at a game that's not going to leave your rotation until you've mastered it.Rollerdrome is relentlessly overwhelming, and I know that's exactly what some of you are after.

Dodge the attacks...And at some point, you jump over an enemy to dodge them, wallride to the upper floor, which gives you enough points to reload your guns, which you use to multikill a few mooks with a grenade, and now you have maintained and increased your combo, so you start front flipping while twisting around, and that gives you more ammo and...And you realize, they did this to absolute, 110% perfection. _childDocuments_.review: I think this game is really cool and I desperately wish I loved it, but there's something off about the controls...I love Skate 3 and how fluid the tricks are once you grasp them. Each input grants control over specific types of movement. This makes complex tricks (like the Miracle Whip) feel intuitive as you can attribute the inputs you made to the exact movements your character took to perform that trick. Since Rollerdome is an action shooter, a lot of granularity for character movement is removed simply because the devs need a place for the Aim & Shoot buttons. Less space for movement controls means less control over movement. Tricks are basic "flick the stick in these directions and press X" combos instead of granular inputs over character movement. Add that to the fact that you can't fall/wipeout; landing "crazy tricks" like the coffin are super easy after a couple minutes of practice. The simplicity and complete lack of risk makes them unsatisfying and more of something you need to do to refill ammo and get a high score in between killing enemies.I understand why these sacrifices were made and I think the devs did a damn fine job of melding these two genres, but it doesn't do it for me. Unlike others, this game doesn't make me feel like a badass, it just feels like a series of unsatisfying quick time events.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a positive review. Bullet-time, tony hawk, music, aesthetics, all great.But is the whole game good - it will depend entirely on your mileage. _childDocuments_.review: Combine arcadey arena romps with tricks and objectives of Tony Hawk with bullet time shenanigans of Max Payne and you get this wild combo.You accrue points through tricks, but increase your combo through dispatching goons. The enemy variety is decent and each requires different tactics to dispatch effectively before your combo runs out.This is aided by a slick visual style, with each enemy type having a distinct visual identity, allowing you to plan your attack from the moment you jump into the arena and take in the whole battlefield.New guns and enemy types are slowly introduced throughout the campaign giving it a nice difficulty curve, ending with a final exam where you will need to use everything you've learned throughout the previous events just to survive.Dodging just as the enemy's attack is about to hit allows you to enter reflex time, where time is slowed and your shots do extra damage. This skill is essential and by the end will allow you to become an unstoppable skate god of destruction, ducking and weaving between attacks before slugging fools right in their dumb faces.Every level also has 10 optional objectives (which also teach you additional mechanics) and the coveted S rank to achieve, so there's a decent amount of content if you go for completion.Definitely give it a shot, it slaps and there is nothing else like it out there

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is creative, smooth and fun. The biggest issue I have with skating games is falling a lot. I was very happy to see that you can not fall when you make a bad jump.The gameplay is fast. But the movements work so smooth that it works so great. So Rollerdrome is a combination of skating and shooting. There is only 1 way to get new ammo. With every trick you make, you earn ammo. Health could be earned by killing enemies.Watch out. _childDocuments_.review: A good game that has some major balancing issues that I have not seen others address. The initial thrill of skating around doing tricks and shooting guys in slow motion is awesome. You feel cool, you look cool, and you're having a good time. However, after the first few levels I started to notice the lack of depth this game actually has. This game combines two very different genres and makes notable concessions from both. Skating is simplistic. There are only 24 tricks, half of which are grinds. There is no penalty for a sloppy landing or bonus for a clean landing, in fact its impossible to wipe out at all. The penalty for repeat moves is too generous. You can get an S rank in all stages without thinking about tricks at all. The shooting is also simplistic. There is a VERY generous lock on for your pistol and shotgun. As long as the enemy is on your screen and close  you will auto lock immediately. The grenade launcher and sniper require manual aiming however the sniper rifle gives you enormous leeway when aiming at faraway targets. As long as you're close with the sniper it hits. These issues are notable, but the biggest issues in the game revolve around the dodge and slowdown mechanics. When you aim time slows down and you may remain in this state for an extended period of time. It works well, however when coupled with perfect dodges it ruins the game. If you dodge at the last moment (a very generous moment if you play action games) you perform a perfect dodge. If you aim right after you perfect dodge you gain double damage. This breaks the game. Gameplay after the 4th stage looks like this: Skate with no thought towards what tricks you're doing, wait for a sniper to shoot you, perfect dodge, enter slowdown, one shot whatever enemy is closest, repeat. It gets old quick. You might think I'm meta-gaming too hard but the game actually encourages you to play this way. Many challenges revolve around entering double damage mode and killing people. There is a hard mode. What a great opportunity to let skilled players push themselves! Removing auto aim? Reducing slowdown timer? Stricter stale trick penalties? Bonus tricks? No no no no. Hard mode has more numerous enemies that do more damage and that's it. In some games, the real game hides in the second playthrough, in this its an afterthought.This is a great game if you are looking for a casual evening of fun. I would wait until its on sale, blitz the campaign and put it away. If you are looking for a deep score attack game that will keep you hooked searching for that high score look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Very very very cool game.That comes with a big however though.Do not come into this expecting Tony Hawk with guns. This game gets very difficult after the first set of levels. Its not uncommon to be targeted by 4 different enemies at the same time, Be riding into a mine field and out of ammo so you cant do anything about them. Oh and have a volley of missiles homing in on you as well. The game is very fast and frenetic. You have to be thinking two steps ahead and be able to react to 4 different kinds of attacks at any minute. And when you get into that groove after grappling with the controls for the first 30 minutes to an hour and you're just flying around the arena flipping through the air shootin dudes. It feels amazing.There is a pretty big learning curve for sure, but i feel like the pay off is well worth getting there.

_childDocuments_.review: Most reviews on here say that Rollerdrome is a mix of Tony Hawk with Max Payne. And considering the game-play is all skate, jump and grind while rocking some insane bullet time shooting, they are not far off the mark.There isn't too much of a story here, just some light commentary about a dystopian future that can be explored in between levels. The visuals and sound however make up for what the game lacks in narrative. Each level feels unique and is a pleasure to look at due to the rich cell shaded pastel art style. The music in particular does a great job of complementing the 'Running Man' type setting while complementing the intense game-play. And the game-play is where this one shines. If you do love the old skating games, except with no risk of stacking it after trying to pull of a massive move set combo, you'll be happy here. That doesn't mean this is an easy experience though as the gun play will keep you on your toes from start to finish. The overall control scheme and shooting mechanics makes it a dream to plan each combo across the arena, making for a satisfying experience overall.I think the best way to describe this one is Jetset Radio with guns. And if that sounds appealing to you, then the price is right. Even though it isn't a lengthy game, there is enough challenge and incentive to keep you coming back for plenty of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool concept for a future sequel to flesh out. It's like you mix Tony Hawk Pro Skater with Max Payne and you get a high action third-person arena shooter with a cel-shaded art style that's all its own. Building combos can be pretty addicting, although it can be a handful with multiple enemies and hazards being thrown at you almost every second in the later levels. The game has a learning curve, although it is more about getting use to multitasking to pull off tricks, grabs, spins, and grinds, while shooting enemies to build combos. All which makes the core gameplay really fun.Story is inoffensive and ok, nice that they made an effort for some lore. Music is good, techno high beats with some tracks I like more than others. My only complaint is that the arena based stages are a little too repetitive and I wish for some more open-level/open-world level design to mix up gameplay and flesh out the world. And while the game can be hard, it is fairly short with most of the time spent re-trying levels for challenges to progress or hard difficulty (about 7 hours in main campaign). I would personally wait for a sale if you are curious, but I would love to see a sequel with these ideas more realized.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Creative hybrid between a skate game and a 3rd person arena shooter. Your goal is to kill all opponents, but the get ammo to do so you need to perform special tricks with your skateboard. This sound like an interesting concept, but the execution is rather mediocre. The arena's are rather small and to keep the game playable, only a few enemies are present at the same time. Once you kill a few enemies, new enemies are appearing out of thin air, which is something I really dislike in video games: clear a part of the arena, turn around and you get still shot in the back by an enemy that just spawned there. Another annoyance are the enemies with sniper rifles and AoE damage. their attacks are hard to dodge and to predict, since they can hit you from the other side of the arena. To solve this, the devs added limited "bullet time" that slows the time for everyone but you. This is very helpful, but also kills the pacing of the game. Last but not least, to unlock the next arena, you need to complete lots of secondary objectives, which can be very difficult and/or time-consuming. If there wasn't a built-in cheat to override this, I probable wouldn't have bothered to complete the game.Tldr: very interesting concept, but also many flaws. Recommended on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect way to bring back pro skater games! Wether you were a fan of these or you just enjoy fast paced action game you should be thrilled with ROLLERDROME!The art direction's on point but that's not what this game is about. The gameplay is what makes it stand out. It's fast, makes you feel like you're playing well straight from the beginning and has a perfectly balanced learning curve. You'll enjoy shooting at targets on your rollers, switching weapons and performing tricks and the go while being surprised it is so easy to read when it's such a mess everywhere!!Have a blast with this game, it looks expensive but if you got the money, spend it with no hesitation!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so Rollerdrome:- Finished Main Campaign- Finished Hard Mode CampaignGraphics and art get the job done. They aren't super flashy but apparently run on a potato, and I never had any issues even on my trash machine. Controls are something, and I'll get back to that. At the core, you kill stuff to bump your combo (and your max score), and better tricks get you more ammo back. You have a bullet time mechanic that is absolutely key to... everything on L2, and you'll basically be holding it down the whole time. L1 is brakes and I never used it. Circle is dodge and it's very generous with i-frames. Square is grab, and you have the same grabs OlliOlli does - directionals, double directionals, and opposite directionals. Each time you use a grab it's worth less, which means you get less ammo. As a result, you need to cycle through your whole bag of tricks to keep your ammo topped off.  You can add flips to tricks for more points, and you can also cycle through grinds but they seem to be a lot more dangerous. Arrow keys switch between your four weapons.Activating bullet time while dodging attacks that would have hit you activates super bullet time, which amps up your damage. Super bullet time damage is what you want to have going essentially all the time because it lets you one-bang all the most dangerous enemies in the game, and conserve ammo.Gameplay is just you Tony Hawking your way around the map, shooting stuff and trying not to get hit. Finishing the main campaign without worrying about objectives is probably a couple hour affair, and hard mode (Out For Blood) is maybe another two hours. The real challenge is hitting the high scores and hitting the time challenges, and to do either you need to know the hit counts for enemies in bullet time and out of it - and how to quickly activate bullet time. As of now I've finished both campaigns and a smattering of hard mode challenges.As a combo juggling game everything plays tight and fun. I never felt cheated when I dropped a combo or got killed, and when I did, I realized later I was wrong. There are audio and visual cues galore and the systems that could really ♥♥♥♥ you have enough slop built in that the game is more of a logistics/movement puzzler than a tricks or shooting game. There's a reasonable amount of auto-aim on weapons, and the tricks are smoothed out a bit so you don't need to worry about falling, just losing momentum. In order to hit high score challenges you need to keep easy bullet time activations around so you can snipe, and all of the high score challenges revolve around keeping one combo going the entire time while racking up base score. It all creates a tight, fun balancing act that really hits a nostalgia spot that hasn't been hit since Tony Hawk 4 for me. If you aren't into high scores, time trials or Tony Hawk style tricks and combos, there won't be much for you here. The enemy spawns are hard coded so as you work a level you can really dial in your route, but there is some room for flexibility and improv in each run. Overall I give it a subjective 9.5/10, but objectively it's probably a 7 or 8 given the back half of the game could be considered mundane or spammy when you stop getting new enemies/weapons, and the maps and music are forgettable. Full recommend at $12, or even full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! THPS meets Max Payne's Bullet-Time.Very simple concept executed so well! The gameplay is very fluid and satisfying, there is enough weapon/enemy variety and challenges are fun and not that hard and frustrating to do. Yes, the game gets more challenging as you progress and last few levels can be overwhelming but that's part of the fun. 10/10 game and absolutely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 2nd, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Tony Hawk with guns, it’s a common thing to call this, but you’ll see why.Rollerdrome has players competing in a new game format where they rollerblade around, shoot enemies, and do tricks to earn additional ammo.  The movement and trick system heavily reminds me of the Tony Hawk Pro Skater franchise, and the combat adds in a slow-down mechanic and a combo mechanic for the score.  Each level is well designed but focused on an arena-style landscape, and has 10 unique challenges for completionists as well as a ranking system for those who want to chase the leaderboards. I have heard this isn’t the longest game, with people putting in around four to twelve hours depending on how much players want to tackle.  The shooting will force purists who just want to do extreme sports to tackle something different, and the required tricks for reloading may frustrate shooter fans, but if you exist at that sweet spot between those two genres, this will feel like nothing else.  It’s a fresh and novel idea, and well executed. Pick this up if you want to play Tony Hawk with guns.  There’s a reason that’s what people say about this game, but that’s also what’s brilliant about it, it’s a simple concept that works so well and is obvious enough that it can be summed up in a single line.  I’ve played for about two to three hours on this already and I just want to come back and play more.   I’m hopeful we’ll also see a sequel to it with larger and more variety in their levels.  Also, this is made by the same team who did Olli Olli World, so kudos to those developers.  It’s another game that’s just brilliant. _childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game. The core gameplay and animations feel very smooth and intuitive most of the time. The challenges add a decent amount of replayability and helps lead the player to understanding some of the mechanics better without outright spelling it out (such as the usefulness of perfect dodging or more effective ways to kill certain enemy types). Even if you don't care for the art direction itself, the game does a good job of making every enemy look distinct and what you need to visually watch out for as a player (which is all you could really ask for with this kind of skill based game). Story is sparse but tells you enough that you get the general gist of things and doesn't feel interruptive to the game part. Oh yeah, OST is some lovely synth music too.I do have a few issues but they do all sort of blend into the conclusion of, "I want more of this to come out in the future," (the tricks themselves are pretty simple to pull off nor do you ever combo multiple moves like THPS, the levels while all having solid design with a decent difficulty curve, do blend together since the environments are limited to, "arena, canyon, mall, and snowy area", and somewhat related to that, some environment stuff feels really half baked like wall riding and floor boosters).Hopefully this either gets DLC or a full sequel because there's a lot of potential to expand on the systems they've made like new stages, weapons, enemy types, expanded movesets, etc. Hell, if Roll7 get more of a budget, I'd love to see them fully embrace stuff like character customization and more lively arenas.

_childDocuments_.review: Strongly presented, poorly executed.The aesthetics and visual/auditory design of Rollerdrome are excellent, but the gameplay suffers from trying to be two games at once, rather than a hybrid.To explain, it simultaneously asks that you move, shoot, dodge and execute tricks. The problem is that the two movesets are only tangentially connected. For instance, why are dodging and jumping two separate mechanics? It feels like I have to jump to an entirely separate set of keys to do a "trick" than I would use to play the rest of the game. "Ah," but you say, "Then simply do the shooting and moving, and ignore the tricking, if you feel the controls for it are clunky."Except that you can't, because A) progress to further levels requires completing challenges(disable this function, dear God disable it and save yourself the annoyance) which are heavily Trick reliant and B) the only way to recover ammo is by doing tricks. You need to do a trick in between every two or three kills at most, otherwise you're constantly running zero on ammo.The problem with this is that you end up just executing the same reliable kind of tricks over and over again, for the ammo. Like, I can either try to do a SUPER SICK ELITE 720-DEGREE NOSE GRAB TWIST SPIN WITH CHOCOLATE SYRUP or I can just do my 15th rail grind of the level because that refills my ammo just as effectively with way less effort.What the game lacks is *functional* tricks. I would say it would work much better with "classic" ammo drops, but then have some of them in hard-to-reach locations that would require tricks to reach. Like perhaps doing a spin in the air gets you more airtime, maybe it requires a wall or railgrind to reach, something of that sort. Or maybe you want to do a front-flip in mid-air to be able to get a good firing angle on an enemy's weakspot or something.Secondly the levels have some design issues. The most "boring" ones, the "this is just a roller skating rink with rocket launchers" levels, are the ones that are actually the most functional, because all of the ones that are "this is a real environment we put some ramps" in either suffer from a lot of out-of-bounds walls(which harm you and then warp you back inside the arena) or from having a lot of "sharp" corners that you can get "stuck" in temporarily because our roller-skating protagonist uses tank controls for movement(It makes sense, but her insanely poor turning radius makes controlling her in a lot of these arenas pretty unfun considering how cramped they are).Another complaint is that the shooting is auto-aim, rather than manually aimed. It feels like it's partially responsible for making the game less fun for a couple of reasons. Firstly, sometimes you want to aim at an explosive barrel next to someone, but the auto-aim does not, or two enemies are close enough together that the auto-aim has different ideas than you do. The other thing is that it kind of kills a potential source of skill and fun mechanics. If the game does the aiming and locking on for you, you can't really have weak points of any sort, all you can have is enemies which are HP pools and maybe have different armor from one facing.Lastly, rarely has such a short tutorial felt so long, especially when they felt it needed to re-occur another two times afterwards. I guess it's a consequence of the poor control scheme, but then I feel like it would have been obvious that if such a clunky tutorial is needed to explain the control scheme, perhaps the control scheme is at fault and needs revising.I would not consider this game a good buy, but would love to see the creators roll their ideas into an animated movie, because they have a much better idea of what looks and sounds good, than what feels good to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a 3rd person action shooter game that combines Tony Hawk's Pro Skater-esque movement, levels and challenges with a score grading system typical to some spectacle fighters.The game takes places in a retro future, where a violent roller derby has become a popular spectator sport ala The Running Man. There is an attempt at keeping some narrative going around that theme, but in its core the main campaign consists of a total of 11 arena fights with a couple of them having a boss fight in a secondary arena.There is a brief tutorial sequence to get to know the controls at start, but rather quickly you're thrown into the first batch of four levels. Basic game loop is to not only shoot the enemies that spawn at each arena, but also perform tricks or dodges as those give you ammo to do so. Rinse and repeat until all spawned enemies have been killed, while hopefully managing to do it fast enough to keep a combo going.Completing levels sometimes opens up new weapons and the game introduces some of the movement mechanics and harder enemies gradually at later stages to avoid overwhelming the player. Each arena is placed full of ramps, rails and other obstacles that support the momentum forward as best as possible and there is a decent, synthwave type soundtrack that overall fits the theme nicely.However, like in Tony Hawk, completing a level does not necessarily mean you get progress to the next level batch if you have not completed enough challenges on the previous batch. Luckily the challenges are rather straightforward to complete and doing all of them in the first set allows you to mostly skip them in the later stages. Still, the challenges are where my main issue with the game is: Completing them does not feel rewarding.Moment-to-moment gameplay feels mostly fluid and executing perfect dodges and aiming shots in slow motion can be a lot of fun at times, but there is constantly the feeling that you're not doing the correct things or using the right weapons, which most likely leads to you not getting any of the challenges done, your combo ending and a bad score and grade at the end.Once all 4 stages of the championship containing the 11 levels are unlocked and done, a new game plus -mode opens where you can play through the same levels again, but with more and tougher enemies and some new score and time challenges. I already gave up on completing the regular challenges during the main campaign once the required amount to proceed was done and I think I might've had enough of the game altogether at this point.I first saw Rollerdrome as an early concept work years ago in a tweet that showcased a roller skating figure doing a grab trick from a ramp, jumping and shooting someone with a shotgun in a slow-mo sequence. That short 10 second animation looked cool and promising and I still feel like there is a good game somewhere in that concept, which unfortunately was not discovered during the development, at least not fully. While the game generally feels fun to play, with the main focus being the challenges and rather small arena combat and the expected longevity being grind for high scores, I feel there is not enough here for a somewhat casual gamer to enjoy. I would still be interested in a sequel though.

_childDocuments_.review: My first two hours with the game.So. I'm an old-skool Tony Hawk player. I even bought the remake, much to my chagrin.This is not THPS. This is THPS's edgy, prepper cousin who likes big booms, Borderlands graphics, and abandoning all prior muscle memory.First. the mechanics are much different than THP... yanno what, I'll just make my point by calling it That Other Game, or TOG. The mechanics are much different than TOG. Sure, combos lend towards your score, but (and I can't emphasize this enough) PEOPLE ARE SHOOTING AT YOU WITH SNIPER RIFLES AND ROCKET LAUNCHERS. The flowstate you get with other games is out the window here. You're always under fire. There is always a threat. Failure is always an option. What I'm saying is that the chill and skate principle is right the f out the window. I've heard this game compared to Doom, or TOG2. In Doom or Bulletstorm or even freakin' Halo, you occasionally get to sit, breathe, and think through your next move. This game is not TOG2. BECAUSE YOU CAN'T STAND STILL. EVER (and no, that's not a rollerblade joke).This is its own beast. It deserves the respect of being its own thing, unrelated to similar looking games. The lines are clean. The gameplay is flawless. And if you die, it's your own damn fault.So in that case, it's almost like another Souls-like, in that you must always act, not just react. You must always be able to roll with the punches (yes, that was a dodge-button joke). You must always keep your cool. Or you're going to die. Or worse. Get a bad grade. Give it a run. I promise you I'm going to be racking HOURS of play on this game when I get a chance.THREE HOURS LATER...Okay. I've spent over double the amount of time with the game than I did when I wrote the above.A couple things for the wary to know: So. Progression at the beginning of the game is quick, it's punchy, and it succeeds at getting you hooked. Having gotten to the next chapter, I can point out that, in order to progress the story, you'll need to complete stages AND also complete challenges. If you don't care and don't complete these challenges, you might find your ability to "finish" the story mode stymied.Don't fret. You'll find yourself completing most of these challenges without trying. But some of them you're going to need to sweat a bit over. These aren't cheap "throw them in as buffer" sort of challenges, either. These are "the developers wanted these weapons to be used this way" sort of challenges. Well worth the effort, but frustrating enough to be worthy of the term "challenge".New weapons get unlocked as well. They play differently from one another, to be sure. But the fact that different enemy types are vulnerable to specific weapons just adds another layer of complexity with meaning to the game. It doesn't feel cheap, and the fact that there is room for a total of 4 weapons tells me that the latter part of this game is going to be a mix of "don't get shot" along with "don't use the wrong weapon on this bad guy".It's hour 5 and I don't feel I'm barely scratching the surface.Stay tuned!

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this game incredibly fun! If you're a fan of high octane combo driven skating games, a whole lotta bullet time, sick cel shaded art style and pleasant soundtrack, then this is for you.Doing tricks and dodging at the last second gets you ammunition. When you defeat enemies the combo multiplier goes up. Dodge at the last second to get slow-mo, then get your guns ready for even more slow-mo action. What fun mechanics, I haven't played a game like this before.Guns are simple, nothing we haven't seen before, which ain't a bad thing. I am a big fan of the Z-11, very satisfying to pull off shots with that one.Each level has multiple, varied Challenges to complete, all of which test your skill and knowledge of how to dispatch enemies and traverse the environment. The enemies are all pretty well telegraphed, making it easier to plan your moves and avoid getting hit.This game pulls no punches, so neither should you. I don't have a ton of time logged in it, but in a few short hours I have been beating levels with full combos, not getting hit, etc. Whole lot of stuff left to do, especially in the Out for Blood campaign.For the completionists out there, achievement hunting will be fun for some of them, but others will undoubtedly be insanely difficult. _childDocuments_.review: Combining an arena shooter with a skating game is a really cool concept. As one might expect, it's unwieldy in execution - even while using the recommended controller setup. Rollerdrome provides some leeway in the form of auto-aim and never wiping out after performing tricks, but that just removes the traditional challenges associated with both genres while STILL being too much to keep track of for your average gamer. The game thankfully provides assists for middle-of-the-road gamers to work with, but having to significantly alter gameplay in order to beat the game never feels great.Still, Rollerdrome is a stylish novelty and I'd recommend it to people who don't mind adapting to unusual control schemes or keeping track of several different things at once in a fast-paced action game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a fantastic 3rd-person shooter for those seeking a fast-paced experience. What makes it so unique is that the shooter and skating aspects are dependent on each other: shoot the enemies around the arena to make room for tricks, and skate fast to get air time for tricks which will reward you with ammo. There's also a bullet-time ability you can use to shoot enemies while buying time to figure out where you'll travel to next. Later into the game's main campaign it becomes an intense bullet hell.The setting takes place in 2030, "Rollerdrome" is established as a popular blood sport where roller-skating competitors face against house players. New advancements in technology allow judges to remotely award competitors with ammo based on the tricks they perform. That's pretty much the gist of the story in the game but you can explore in some levels to learn more about the lore. I liked how the story exists while also not impeding the gameplay.Some nitpicks:__________The overall challenge is along the lines of difficult rogue-lite shooters I've played before such as Risk of Rain 2 and Gunfire Reborn. I can't find myself replaying this game much after getting 100% achievements, but I had a blast during the time I spent on Rollerdrome. Hopefully the devs add more content in the future. My overall rating: 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome takes place in the year 2030 in which we play as the roller skater Kara Hassan in a deadly arcade tournament where she must entertain the public by doing various tricks while trying to survive waves of armed enemies. As you may understand, the objective of the game is to clean the arenas of all their enemies in order to move up to the finals and become the new champion. There is a bit of story after reaching a new stage, but it’s really flimsy and pointless. It doesn’t tell much about Kara and only gives some more info about the futuristic setting, the company organizing this bloody tournament and the messages left by some opponents (which we never see in person, unfortunately). Easy to say, these parts are completely forgettable and only there to give a narrative background that is not enough to get you immersed.Now the gameplay is what Rollerdrome is all about, and fortunately it’s good for the most part. You skate at full speed through these giant arenas shooting at enemies, aiming under the Reflex mode (aka Max Payne’s bullet time) and reloading your weapons by doing all sorts of skating tricks. This mix of skating and shooting is certainly original and refreshing, but at the same time it’s also a bit too simple and it isn’t developed with its full potential. The gameplay is fun for the first hour, but feels like it’s still in the testing phase. There are some common tricks and grinds, but it can’t be considered a fully-fledged skating game. At the same time, the gunplay doesn’t feel great; there are only four weapons and they don’t even require the most perfect precision. I once tried to shoot the unprotected legs of an enemy carrying his shield, but even if my aim was correct, the bullet bounced off his shield instead, so it doesn’t really matter which part of the body you aim at. Speaking about the enemies, unfortunately there isn’t much variety and the only boss fight present in the game is re-used one more time, which is really disappointing to see.The thing that I didn’t like the most though is the story progression. Completing each level is not enough for you to progress through the Campaign. To unlock new stages, you must complete a certain number of challenges, such as killing an enemy X times using one type of weapon, collecting all 5 coins in the arena, doing a certain trick etc. Without these kinds of forced challenges, the game would probably last two hours, which is really low for the asking price. In other words, even if you don’t like completing “optional” challenges in any game, you will be required to do it in Rollerdrome. There is a partial solution though; in the assists menu there is an option to turn off the progression based on completed challenges and it works pretty great, but for some reason it also disables the Leaderboards (so your score won’t be registered like when playing offline). In the assists menu there are also other options such as infinite ammo, infinite reflex time and invincibility that make the game very easy, so at least the developers understood that the grindy progression could have been a problem for some players. As a matter of fact, the difficulty increases quite a lot during the semi-finals and you will probably try the same stage multiple times, but again, this feels like another way to increase the game length rather than providing a thoughtful challenge and progression. Completing the game unlocks the “Out for Blood” mode, which is basically an even harder Campaign mode, with the same stages you previously played but every weapon unlocked and all enemies mixed. This is supposed to add some more “replayability”, but I doubt players will spend lot of time on it after the main campaign. Other than this, graphics look good enough, pretty close to Sable’s art style, but with some good ‘80s retrofuturistic vibes. Kara’s animations are a bit too stiff and probably needed more work, while most of the enemies stay still waiting for you to kill them.I must say that I really loved OlliOlli World, but for me Rollerdrome is only a decent game and I can’t shake the idea that this small indie title ruined its progression trying to increase its length. The game is certainly fun and refreshing for the first hour, but once you understand how the progression works the joy of seeing a Tony Hawk’s shooting game ends very quickly. In the end, Rollerdrome proves that a refreshing gameplay idea also needs a great vision behind to support it.
