_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is an exhilarating and fast-paced roller skating game that delivers a thrilling arcade experience. With its vibrant visuals, catchy soundtrack, and intuitive controls, the game captures the excitement and joy of roller skating. Players can customize their skaters, master various tricks and stunts, and compete in challenging levels and multiplayer modes. The game's responsive controls and smooth gameplay mechanics create a sense of flow and adrenaline as you navigate through the dynamic roller rink environments. If you're a fan of high-energy sports games and enjoy the thrill of roller skating, Rollerdrome is a must-play title that will keep you entertained and coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere between 'Olli Olli' and 'The Club with rollerskates', and one of the most fun things I've played in ages. You will probably suck at first, but after a while it'll click and you'll be stringing things together without problem. The soundtrack is exceptional too.Biggest criticisms- some of the trick inputs are a bit sketchy, and given that you're supposed to mix up tricks through the match to keep the score high and your ammo refilling fast it can be a real pain when one doesn't come off and you don't have enough bullets to kill the thing you're firing at. Also, some of the enemies have a bit too much health, particularly when you get to the 'Out for Blood' campaign, which is essentially new game plus. Finally, you have to wipe out all enemies to finish a stage, and sometimes it isn't super obvious where they are- very frustrating with the combo ticking down.Overall though it's a neat game that does what it does exceptionally well. Definitely give it a whirl, although be aware that it is quite hard once it gets properly going.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great skateboarding game. The combat is great but, its renders the whole ordeal very confusing. You have to have eyes on everything (including the things behind you) constantly keep track of your bullets and also get a high stunt score.If you're someone that can't keep track of many important things at once, then i don't recommend it. If you can however, go on ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has got SERIOUS style to it; shazzam! Hits that Tony Hawk skater itch, with GUNS! It's like Sonic, but with GUNZZZ [BUT BETTER]!!!! Honestly haven't played enough of this, but between the visuals, challenging gameplay, and boppin' soundtrack, this is a definite big THUMBS UP recommendation here. Check this snazzy game out, ya'll!

_childDocuments_.review: is a title that feels retro, hypermodern, and timeless at the same time; Roll7 triumphs in wearing their inspirations both artistic (the psychedelic hard-rock art style of Mœbius) and cinematic (the films  and , obviously) and mechanical (, the first two  titles, and a little bit of ) on their sleeves and letting all elements blend harmoniously in sleek, minimalist packaging.In a dystopian future -- the 1970s' envisioning of a dystopian future, that is -- a megacorp called Matterhorn has taken over the world, and placates the populace with Rollerdrome, a death-game where lethal gladiators on rollerskates must kill an entire skate park full of "House Players" (heavily implied to be indentured servants).  The contestants enter the arena with a pair of pistols (and later, a variety of other weapons), but only one magazine: to earn more bullets and fight for their survival, they must complete sick skate stunts  dodging incoming fire and slaughtering their enemies.This little handwave -- "the corporation warps more bullets into your gun every time you do a trick" -- balances  into something incredible.  Equal parts  and , you're encouraged to master the shooting gameplay because every bullet is precious and the enemy attack patterns threaten to overwhelm you if you don't finish them off quickly, but you  have to master the stunt gameplay because it's the only way to arm yourself to engage the next enemy.  If you repeat the same trick over and over, the score meter greys out and you receive only a pittance of a partial reload each time, so you have to diversify your repertoire, alternating from flips to ollies to grinds to wall-rides and more.  The breathlessly kinetic tricks weave right  into the combat gameplay; as you're doing stunts to reload your guns, you need to  be keeping up-to-speed to outrun enemy projectiles, moving your stunts in such a direction as to get in range for your next attack, and planning for where on the map you're going to pull your  trick.  The game's bullet-time aiming and your inability to wipe out -- you always land on your feet even from botched tricks, maintaining at least some momentum unless you dead-end directly into a wall -- help to keep it from all becoming too overwhelming, because if you slow down for even a few seconds all of those enemies will catch up to you and you'll be very dead.On  of the excellent core gameplay loop is the game's  inspiration: each of the six enemy types are vulnerable to different weapon choices and engagement strategies, and particularly resilient to others.  The rocket guy puts up a force field one moment after he  taking damage, so it's better to hit him with lots of little pistol shots in rapid succession than it is to hit him with one sniper shot.  The beam sniper will warp away after she takes her first tick of damage, so you want the big hits of the sniper rifle or grenade launcher.  The big robot doesn't even take damage from your pistols, only from grenades and your slug shotgun.  Each of these enemies also brings a distinct and highly readable attack pattern to the table, which is vital when you're trying to dodge upwards of a dozen of them shooting at you while also doing stunts while also doing your own shooting.Despite the game's many moving parts and ambitious hybrid gameplay, every part has a role to play and every element of a shooter or a skating game that wouldn't serve the precise gameplay loop that  wants is nixed.  What's left after so much cutting-away is a 4-hour-long firecracker; too short, perhaps, for the $30 pricetag, but with generous replayability and more 'gameplay' in those four hours than some AAA action titles manage in 12 or 24.  I got it off an $11 Humble Bundle, and at that price point this game was an absolute steal and by far the best product in the bundle, despite it getting second-billing next to the big prestige AAA games.If " meets " sounds irresistible to you, don't walk but skate to the storefront to buy  immediately.  If you're more just a general action or shooter game fan, get it on sale.  I promise you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: A shooting game with Tony Hawk style movement taking place in a 70s style movie.This game is unique, fun, challenging, and nothing makes you feel cooler then doing a misty flip in slomo while shooting a tank with a grenade launcher watching it explode and landing on a rail as you grind through its smoking remains.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: You will either love this game or hate it. I assure you, if you learn the different kind of tricks and accept the difficultly of the game it's a blast to play. At first the game wasn't clicking for me but as soon as I tried to incorporate some of the more advanced tricks and got a bit more experience with the game I felt like I was a complete badass. The game also comes packed with assists for those who can't keep up with the game.It's only cons are the controls being ok, not great just ok and the lack of content for a game priced at €30.While I really enjoy this game the price for the game is a little on the steep side (11 stages, each one having an alternative harder mode. Campaign can be easily completed in about 2 hours if you ignore challenges). While its base price isn't recommended I highly recommend getting it when its about 33% off.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I have completed the Main Campaign, the recorded playtime may be inaccurate due to playing partially on the Steam Deck.Rollerdrome is closer in style to Vanquish on the God Hard difficulty setting than it is to the Tony Hawk Pro Skater series. The game values memorization, optimization, and execution much more than it does creativity and improvisation. It's quite difficult, and the input for more advanced moves requires a precision that I couldn't achieve on controller after a few hours of playtime. This would likely fare better on Keyboard and Mouse.That being said, it's a clever, well put together game and the core gameplay is very fun for what it is, just don't go in expecting the next coming of Jet Set Radio or something.Works perfectly on the Steam Deck, aside from small text.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, after each map you gradually become more skillful until the very end, where you'll be able to master every move and optimize every second in the round. The challenges are very fun; they can be very challenging but are never too far out of reach. I left some challenges undone that felt too hard, and when I came back after completing the campaign my skills & weapon arsenal had gone up so much that it suddenly felt like a cake walk, and I felt like a God. Which is the best thing for a game to make you feel.

_childDocuments_.review: Tagline: "What if Tony Hawk was a third person shooter?" I'm sure you're going to hear this same description in many reviews in one form of another. Whether posed as a question or a math equation ("it's Tony Hawk + [insert your favorite TPS here]). I imagine the working title for this game was THPS:TPS.And at its core that's what Rollerdrome is. If you have played Tony Hawk or any of its ilk you are going to feel right at home with how this game controls and how your character's momentum carries you into every leap, launch, and grind. Yes, you're on skates, not a skateboard, but it still feels remarkably similar. That said Rollerdrome has a few tricks up its sleeve to keep your own your toes.First of all, you can't crash. There is no bailing or falling down or losing balance on a grind. You can't misalign a 900 and break your combo. So where is the challenge you might ask? This isn't Tony Hawk for babies, is it? Well, no, quite the opposite in fact, because you lose your combo in one of two ways: by being boring and by taking damage.Let's examine the latter half of that statement first. If you can't beef your tricks and skin a knee on the asphalt, how are you going to take damage? Well, by taking a sniper shot or two to the dome of course! Eat one too many rockets, get hit by a couple baseball bats, and you'll lose your multiplier right quick. Or, if you really take a beating, you'll lose all your health and need to restart the run entirely.So how about the second half: "being boring"? Well, here's the thing, this is the far flung future of 2030 and the X-Games just aren't doing it anymore. So while your verts, rotations, and grabs might look pretty dang neat, turns out they're not what's upping your score and your multiplier after-all. The only way to get the crowd into it, and to post a run worth admiring on the leaderboard, is to kill every last gun toting, baseball wielding, rocket launcher strapping mofo in the arena with style and panache. Elegant murder is what gets you the gold here. All tricks do is replenish your ammo so you can keep the slaughter going and going and going!So that's Rollerdrome in a nutshell. Kill every enemy in the arena as fast you can while pulling sick flips and sweet grinds to keep your guns locked and loaded. Dodge enemy fire and go into bullet time to nail tough shots. And if you're feeling feisty you can even shoot for a good old level challenge or two, like wall riding a ski lift or slug shotting a dude from above. Yup, that's right, I wasn't kidding when I said this was Tony Hawk's Pro Skater: Third Person Shooter. You could almost imagine a world where the challenges were "collect S-K-A-T-E and get ten headshots!".The game controls flawlessly and plays exceedingly well. I haven't tried it anywhere but on my Deck and it plays great on it. It looks amazing. Impeccable art direction and thumping retro-futuristic tunes nail the vibe to the screen and are complemented by a story that could almost convince you this game is taking place in Robocop's old Detroit. The narrative is not the centerpiece -- and I hesitate to even call it that, as it's more world-building or thematic trapping -- but the whole capitalistic dystopia vibe definitely comes through. Your a plucky upstart in this sport and you gotta work your way up to star status. Who cares if you had to take a predatory loan to afford the equipment, training, and entrance fees?At the end of the day Rollerdrome is a pick up and play, easy to learn but hard to master, arcade romp that brought me right back to my days of endlessly replaying Warehouse in THPS. You can't really ask for much more than that, but if you did anyway Rollerdrome is the kind of game that tosses you a gun and says, "Have at 'em, kid!".NOTE: I'm playing on my Deck outside of Wifi range so do note that my playtime isn't accurately reflected. As of this review I have going on two hours in the game and I've just completed the first four stages which are the beginner set. There's three more sets of four after that going by the menu.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and unique gameplay. In later levels however, it feels like the game tries to have too many mechanics going on at once. It can lead to frustration when trying to dodge attacks every second, while also doing tricks to gain ammo/points and kill enemies at the same time.The game is also very short unless you want to play every stage again in the "out for blood" (new game+) mode or go for all the challenges. I completed the campaign within 3 hours, and I felt no incentive to keep playing afterwards, as there is no upgrade system or real progression in the game, besides doing challenges to unlock stages. The 30€ price tag may be too steep for some, depending on how much they want to invest in the game after playing the campaign. I recommended trying the game out at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:I went back and 100% this game, which is a true rarity for me overall. It's that solid.I never thought shooting while on roller skates would be this fun, or this fluid. If you're down to learn it, this game's got a real dang satisfying loop behind it that is well worth the cost of entry.It's cheaper than real roller skates or time on a firing range anyways. Worlds safer (for you, the player anyways, can't say the same for the House Players) as well. Out For Blood (NG+) flips this completely though and turns the entire thing into a dangerous dance with guns on roller skates where you could be liquefied at any moment. Pretty close to Doom but it's the 70's and for some reason Roller Skates are required.Could use a smidge of reworking on the tutorials as I found them pretty tedious and achievement percentages reflect this, but there's a dang good game in there worth working towards.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "turn your brain off and play" kind of game, not saying it doesn't require skill or timing, because it does, but it doesn't require much intellectual thought. I heard someone say this is like Tony Hawk but with guns, and that is about right (except that you are using roller skates, not skate boards). You refill your ammo (which is limited) by performing tricks like grinding rails and wall rides and such. It's a very fun time, and I think more people should play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, Rollerdrome is a good game that falls just short of being a great game in my standard, because of its narrative. Herein lies the problem : it didn't need a narrative, as the gameplay is just THAT good. It's a simplified and permissive Tony Hawk Pro Skater (Technically, Aggressive Inline, if you're like me and grew up during the THPS & "let's-put-together-a-clone-with-anything-with-wheels-hoping-it-makes-money" craze...) mashed with a third person shooter reminiscent of the bullet-hell tension of Platinum Games' Vanquish. Don't let the "permissiviness" fool you however: Sure, you can't splatter yourself on the curb thanks to Kara Hassan's plot-onium enhanced reflexes and agility ... but the opposition, with all their bullets, homing missiles and flamethrowers (and that's the sanest part of their arsenal), more than makes up for it. Rollerdrome definitely IS challenging, but it leans closer to Platinum Games than to Neversoft (RIP).But then, on the other side, you have the art-style and the narration. The Cel-shading is gorgeous, and the clear inspiration from 1975's Rollerball is an intriguing but welcome breath of fresh air. It takes from it the intriguing premise of the Rollerdrome and the surrounding media craze, the megacorporation backing it and a burgeoning revolution...... And then, ironically, it rips a page from the 2002 McTiernan's remake by just foregoing everything in favor of spectacle and explosions. The game barely focuses on the competition and the protagonist through embarrasingly short interludes, and does not adress its setting at all save from two or three news frontpages.That's a borderline-criminal waste of a promising premise, and why Rollerdrome didn't completely click for me. To sum it up :- Go ahead if you're looking for a challenging and original Shooter/Tony Hawk-hybrid.- Skip if you wanted to check the game for its setting (and go watch the original Rollerball instead.)(Steam Deck-note : It runs great, and is battery-friendly)
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: An action game of skating and shooting. Each level is an arena that's a skate park of death with ramps and people trying to kill you. Your job is to kill them first. You gain more ammo by doing tricks. It's pretty fun, but progression is locked behind completing a number of challenges across the different parks you've unlocked, which became frustrating as even after the tutorial and following the prompts displayed I couldn't complete some of the tricks. Give it a shot, maybe you'll figure it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is the best combination of Rollerball, The Running Man and something like Jet Set Radio or Tony Hawk's Pro Skater. It's an beautiful looking, mechanically unwieldly and ugly beast of a game and I absolutely adored every moment of it. It's gorgeous to look at, fast and fun to play and as long as you have a controller its one of those games where you can enter a flow and build up momentum.I also caution any would-be purchasers to not buy this if they do not have a controller. The KB+M controls are awful and actively work against being intuitive. Additionally, I'm generally not a fan of challenge hunting in games like these as spending inane amounts of time smashing my head over and over into a wall as I try to accomplish something that the game's controls or map design makes improbable is just not pleasing to me. I don't really see myself interested in the NG+ because of that there's not a lot of content here. The largest complaint I have besides the controls is the map design, at least how the PC interacts with it. I found myself slamming into walls, getting hung up on geometry, and otherwise ripping myself out of a good flow just because I had a tendency to search for the weird areas that the game didn't know what to do with me being in/on. Instead of a wall jump I'd just sort've flop, or instead of a grind I'd end up dipping down a half-pipe. Not a deal-breaker but definitely noticeable and for the size of the team and the quality of the game besides I can forgive it that.My five hours was pushing it but I enjoyed every second of those five hours I spent with this game. I really wish there was more money put in here for more story because I love the universe that was made and how it was presented and knowing I'll probably never get more is a little saddening - but I'm glad for what I got in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as part of the humble choice, I avoided playing it because I thought it wasn't my cuppa tea. Holy Sh!t I was wrong. This is some PS2 Tony Hawk's Pro Skater with guns, I know it's been said before but this is awesome. I really want a sequel, no micro transactions, no bigger, no better, hell I'd be happy with no multiplayer. Just a game that's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 Worth trying out for the combat alone.Rollerdrome is a game set in the future, 2030, where coliseum style death matches are quite popular. This game thrives when the energy is at its peak but can leave lulls in time due to its mechanics.The strongest aspect of Rollerdrome is the combat. Combat is derived from four weapons, each share the same ammo, that the player will collect. Reloading is unique, the player has to perform tricks to reload; the greater the trick, the greater the ammo return. Gunplay is very smooth, aiming weapons feels like the crosshairs glide across the screen very easily. Tricks can be preformed from two pools: grinds and flips. The problem with this mechanic is that on larger and longer levels, the pool of tricks feels too small. You end up repeating the same few tricks just to get the reload rather than preforming tricks for points. The coincides with the biggest flaw in the game: on plenty of occasions, you will have lulls in combat, especially on the larger maps. In the base campaign, you will often find yourself alone, having to seek out enemies, or you have to exit firefights to do tricks to reload. With time and practice this gets to be less of an issue, but the dull moments in combat do stand out. The boss battles (in the main campaign there are only two) are the same, it is the same enemy for both, with regular enemies on the field with it. Slowing down time is a mechanic in the game that does not feel like a crutch, it is balanced pretty well.The art style is great, it compliments the gameplay fairly well. The effects of lasers, rockets, explosions, and shields are vibrant and crafted in a way that is pleasant to look at. Enemy design is great, their attire and look match the feel of the world. There is a lack of variety in terms of visuals, not enemy types. It would've been nice to see gear change through sections of the campaign.The sound design is great. The weapons match their sound: the firing of the pistol is extremely satisfying. The rocket send out a loud whoosh which does a great job at selling the power of the explosive before it makes contact. The laser rifle has a crisp sound and the shotgun has a chunky sound that sells the weight of the impact of the rounds. Grinding on the rails and ledges in the game sounds simply amazing. The soundtrack is great as well, it must be listened to while playing to add to the overall experience.The story is alright, not too important, slightly shallow, does not boost gameplay. The campaign length is on the shorter side, but not too short to make the price not match the content. There is also an alternative mode called Out For Blood. It is essentially a new game+ with increased difficulty, if you need more Rollerdrome this is the answer to that problem.Overall, Rollerdrome is worth playing through. Although flawed, Rollerdrome gives a stellar performance.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: A pair of rollerblades. Four weapons. Seven enemy types. Eleven arenas. Countless ways to succeed. Or die trying. A lot.Rollerdrome is essentially a mix of the popular extreme sports sub-genre of the early 2000s (Tony Hawk's Pro Skater in particular) and third-person shooters (Max Payne, I'm looking at you). Add tiny bits of Wipeout - minimalistic menu screens and icons, funky electronic music - sprinkled on top, wrap it in retrofuturistic, cel-shaded aesthetics and now you have a slight understanding of what this game is about: score points by doing tricks (also refills your shared ammo reserve - things are layered beautifully like this), extend your combo meter by eliminating foes and keep going until there's none left. What might come as a surprise to some is that such a unique concept does not simply work but turns out to be a rather enjoyable (albeit often teeth-grindingly difficult) experience. If you're looking for a fresh new challenge, look no further!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Answering the question, "What would happen if you filled Tony Hawk's Pro Skater with heavily armed NIMBYs?" But, once the question is answered, there's not much more to get -- UNLESS you're the sort of player that seeks to 100% everything. It's great for high score junkies. Otherwise, I don't /regret/ it, but I certainly won't /recommend/ it either.Constantly fighting the camera for combat is probably more difficult than most challenges presented for points.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cool and unique. It combines a lot of cool mechanics like (Tony hawk skating and third person shooting) that once you master them it just becomes so fun and addicting, because you always want to do better to get a better a score, and make cool moves, but if you want to love the game and enjoy it your gonna have to be patient, because at the beginning it was so difficult for me i was struggling with every level but eventually i got used to it and got better to the point that it became so easy. I completed everything in the game in like five days, but my problem with the game that there is no extra content because you only have the main campaign and the out for blood campaign which is the same maps from main campaign but just harder with more enemies and they hit harder, but overall this game is so fun and it makes you feel like a badass, not a lot games have that effect. 10/10Side Note: This is my first review ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Grabs ahold of you and forces you effortlessly "into the zone" with intense, relentless, non-stop, gun wielding combo based action.Ultra dynamic and super smooth skating gameplay dipped in speed and style combined with well designed gunplay allowing you to cut through enemies and air using a plethora of tricks and weapons. Bit on the shorter side but perfect for quick runs and rerunsWhat a rad game!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the best game I would play this year was OlliOlli World. Then this game came out and I didn't even know about it beforehand. Roll7 has managed to capture something that not many developers seem capable of. They have nailed the "vibe" of their games. I'm addicted to the THPS style of this game with guns as much as I am addicted to the side scrolling chains of OlliOlli World. The setting, art, music and gameplay are all 10's from me. This is another gem and now I can't wait to see what Roll7 does next.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Classic Tony Hawk's Pro Skater style levels and missions with the added complexity of battling it out for your life in an arena with guns. You get a list of objectives to complete and jump into each mission with the goal of ticking off a few more, complete so many objectives and you advance a rank to the next stage of the tournament.Real nice simple gameplay loop, performing tricks is quick and easy, tied well into the fast-paced combat of the game by making it a mechanic that refills your ammo, get hea;th back by killing enemies, so you're consistently encouraged to keep up the pace and pressure. All the controls, even on keyboard like how I play, are nicely responsive and easy to get the hang of and don't need much to learn how they go.Vibrant comic book art style is always one that captures my heart in games, this one does the style well and makes that gameplay pop just as much as the visuals do.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty sure  is on its way to becoming *THE* indie sleeper hit of 2022. The fast paced combat, beautiful cel-shaded graphics, and dark retro-futuristic synthwave soundtrack were all big magnets for me and I can see how other gamers will be drawn to these things as well. Personally, I don't think I've played a skating game since the NES's  (seriously, it's been a while), but I'm sure glad I picked this one up. There's something so satisfying about skating through each level to dispatch various opponents with the appropriate weapon all the while performing sick tricks to earn more ammunition and, ultimately, a higher score. I also appreciate the more relaxed, first-person exploration in between matches, which gives the player some often darkly humorous backstory about the dystopian world of 2030 and the International Rollerdrome Federation. On a side note, and like Amber Midthunder in this year's , it's refreshing to see a woman of color in an action hero role because we just don't see this kind of representation enough. Move over, Lara Croft. Kara Hassan is bad ***. Finally, as others have pointed out, this game is reminiscent of , , and  (in all the best ways), but I also couldn't help but think of Richard Bachman's  as I played. At its heart,  is a fantastic arcade game. To become the ultimate Rollerdrome champion, you will need to replay each level in order to master the game's mechanics and earn the highest score you can, and this is what makes it so fun to play. What a ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: A gem out of left field. This is good.The controls are tight and precise. The skill cap is high, but the game is still accessible and fun at any level. Pulling off a single-combo run is immensely satisfying, and the game subtly delivers an interesting world and story that you can piece together if you so desire. This is a genre-bending masterpiece and a shining example of what games can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Apparently "flip" means "forward flip" or "backflip". Flipping on your sides doesn't count, and apparently according to the comments on this review, that means I can't read.Anyway, to the edited review:Let me start by saying I really do think this game is special, and I do believe that it has the capacity to do GREAT things.Is it clunky? Absolutely.Is it buggy? Sure, it is.Are there some extremely questionable design choices? You bet'cha.Is it still really really fun? Yeah, it's pretty dang fun.That being said, I just can't recommend this game as it stands for a few reasons. Primarily, the length. If it weren't for the game forcing players to complete unfun and ball busting challenges in order just to move on to the next stages, you could probably beat this game in about 30 minutes. I don't know about you, but a dollar per-minute is not exactly worth it - but even that would be better than what we ended up getting. The challenges, like I said, are some of the least fun things I have ever had the displeasure of completing.Instead of bumbling around in a corner of the map trying to complete an unfun challenge so I could progress, I COULD be going over there and actually engaging in the gameplay and having a good time - but I literally can't, because if I do I won't be able to progress. What this ends up boiling down to is kiting one enemy around while you do flips in the background and collect tokens. The main gameplay is some of the most enjoyable gameplay that I think is possible in the genre, but you're literally not able to engage in it because progression is locked behind these stupid challenges.Great game, awful design and progression. I really really hope this is addressed.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Mayhem on wheels and a total blast. Like a lot of fast paced action/arcade shooters the most fun comes once you've gotten comfortable, have all of your tools, and you know how and when to use them. Plenty of enemy types of varying threat levels to stop you dead in your tracks, learning how to effectively kill each was its own little puzzle. Once I got the hang of the controls I really found how each arena is packed with ramps and half pipes to help any on the spot improvisation. They're a ton of fun to skate around and they all look gorgeous with the comic book art style. The music I didn't find particularly notable but it certainly keeps up the pace and tone, though my attention was often elsewhere when playing. Though there's only about 10 or so levels, the Out for Blood mode unlocked after the main campaign is a great challenge for anyone looking for more out of the game. I think there's plenty here to enjoy, and I'm very happy to know that this game is just as fun as it looked when I first saw it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It like the golden era of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 and 2, but with quad skates, bullet time, guns and missiles, and a retro 70's roller derby vibe. And all of it is executed so freakin' perfectly. Seriously, this game deserves a spot in the Indie Hall of Fame. I don't know what it costs at the time of you reading this review, but whatever it is, it's worth it. F*** you. F*** your family. Get rekt noob. Buy this game, now!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: While at times frustrating Rollerdrome is unique and a real challenge. Sometimes a little too challenging! You've been warned. I completely understand the negative reviews but don't feel the same. Sure, everything is simplified. I couldn't imagine trying to do a complicated trick while shooting, it sounds impossible. This game is difficult enough. I really struggled trying to remember to do new tricks (for bullets and score) and keep dodging everything the game threw at me.Still, the combination of skating and shooting is novel enough that is carries the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: this games worthy of all the hype. I'll admit the start I was a little unsure. After completing the tutorial and 1 match I took a little break, when I came back everything clicked. Utilising the dodge button is key. I strongly recommend sticking with it cause once u get the feel for it it's a great! a fresh original gaming experience. Hope they keep making these!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: The cell shaded aesthetic enables awesome performance eclipsing your maximum refresh rate with adequate hardware. You feel like you are in Death Race or Running Man, and are empowered to pull off some styling kills. It feels completely unique with a vague familiarity (Tony Hawk, Jet Set, Max Payne) hidden in its mechanics. The competition between players is driven by a leader boards integration. One of the better drop in and play for 15 minutes single player games!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Magnificent, just magnificent adrenaline chaos. This is a very dense game, at least it was for me, like I felt like I've played the game for longer than I actually have, and I mean that in a good way... it wasn't "felt like I played longer" in terms of boredom, it was "felt like I played longer" in terms of did so much in such a short amount of time. So much to keep track of, so much going on, just so cool in so many ways, it's a lot to take in and it is awesome.Wonderful soundtrack, wonderful art style. I wish there was more of it, but at the same time, it's also an appropriate length (I beat the game in just under 6 hours) for how intense it is. With that said, if how many hours you can squeeze out of a game is of concern to you, and you're not certain if you'll really enjoy the gameplay or try to speedrun/challenge run Rollerdome, this game will be too short for you even with NG+ and completing all the challenges (which I have not done yet as of writing this review)I have some quibbles with the auto-aim: most of the time the auto-aim does exactly what I want it to do, but every so often I find myself fighting with it to pick a different target, and I was also a little annoyed to find out I could shoot my own grenades (thus preventing the grenades from damaging enemies), but that particular grenade instance was only relevant when I was trying to complete a specific challenge for one of the levels.All things considered, I cannot recommend this game enough. Rollerdome shares a place with En Garde as far as short games I'm really glad I played because I absolutely ended up loving both of them above most every other game I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is one of the most thrilling and original games I have played in recent times.John Linneman from Digital Foundry said it the best: the game is a unique mix of Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, Max Payne and Schwarzenegger's Running Man. This mix doesn't only work but it is a lot of fun! When you are first jumping into the match arena with the pumping synth soundtrack and you start shooting your dual pistols in slow motion, it gets your heart going and this feeling doesn't stop until the end of the campaign. Seriously, it is a lot of fun and the feeling is priceless when you start pulling off tricks while evading the enemies' bullets but at the same time trying to land a precise railgun-shot.The narrative doesn't get in the way of the action at all and it keeps the suspense high. I just wish there was a bit more of it and the conclusion of the story could have been a bit more elaborate. (Especially after beating the game's hard mode - it would have been nice to get an extra narrative section.) Nevertheless, if you are familiar with the dark utopian future themes of Running Man, you are going to feel right at home!I felt that the game needed just a tad more polish with its difficulty. Rollerdrome isn't exactly easy - other reviewers have compared it to Doom Eternal, and I think that's a good comparison. You need to keep in mind the different enemy types and you have to react to new situations in a blink of an eye, and that is not easy at all while your adrenaline is spiking. It's just that there are some difficulty spikes in the game that are surprising and might put off new players reaching the conclusion of the story. The campaign starts out strong with a good flow but I felt that the game needed one or two extra tutorials or it should have introduced new enemies/strategies a tiny bit later in order to maintain this good flow until the end of the campaign.Of course, if you want to tip the scales towards the fun part, I do recommend using the built-in assists. You can customize your experience in a way that the game remains a lot of fun AND doable if the challenge proves to be insurmountable.Despite of all these though, Rollerdrome easily earns my wholehearted recommendation for its original and fun gameplay and I'm looking forward to Roll7's next title!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game is as fun as you'd expect it to be for Tony Hawks w/ guns - and it's relatively inexpensive too with a sale on release!I definitely wasn't good my first attempt on the first 4 stages, but have since cleaned up all the objectives with an 'A' rating for each. I can see myself getting better and enjoying this even more. 2:35 on Houston Mall was actually kind of a nightmare.Annnd after playing this some more, and raging periodically, I can say I have gotten better. And  will get better too. Objectives you thought impossible will be collected with ease.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a game that takes the word "schmoovement" and injects it with so much growth hormone it's unrecognizable. the entire game is a stylised cluster♥♥♥♥ that you WILL suck ass at to begin with, but will ease you into feeling like god's gift to gaming assuming you aren't mentally stunted.One of few games I've 100%'d, and if i were a high score chaser, I'd chase them. Incredible game.The enemies seem daunting at first if you're trying to brute force them, but there's strategies for each one that make them trivial to deal with. you just need to figure it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played anything quite like this before. I did an 8+ hour stream of Rollerdrome, and it was a blast to play! Imagine Max Payne meets Tony Hawk’s, and you’ve got the essence of this game. The soundtrack is fun, the weapons are fun to use and the comic book art style is something I really liked. The game demands a lot of multitasking since everything happens fast, but that was incredibly enjoyable for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Focused, stylish, and tense celebration of 80s era hyper-violence. Understand that you are entering the arena with the sole intention of emerging alive. The tricks and weapons are means to the end of scorching the rink upon which you skate. Embrace that and you'll be glued to your seat and only realize how invested you were when you hit exit game and you give your muscles a chance to relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played any skating games besides a little Jet Set Radio - but I'm enjoying this game a whole lot. Each arena has enough room to allow for a variety of movement and enemy placement, and each enemy poses a threat to the player in a unique way.Sure, they can take quite a beating, but that's what Super Reflex is for - making things quick and painful.I must admit the music doesn't quite do it for me - it's not as high-energy as I'd like for this kind of gameplay, and the system for inputting dual combos is a little awkward since I have to use the control stick. But beyond that, I'm really liking this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always on the lookout for a game with a good movement system, and the next great one has arrived. You can dodge, flip, wallride, grind, jump, you can even "rocket jump" off enemy explosives or be thrown by enemy moves.If you're coming from Tony Hawk or similar games, on first impression you may think the forgiving landings and self-balancing grinds have been "made too easy". Just wait. In reality, these things have been removed in order to make way for a dizzying array of dodges, slo-mo gun stunts, and total mayhem. You simply wouldn't have the bandwidth to do it all. The game builds a very fun flow state, getting a "no damage" or A or higher run makes you feel like a superhero. There seems to be a lot of hidden potential in the movesystem that will creates a very high skill ceiling, especially with dodges and using explosives to launch yourself.Variety of enemies and courses is good. Sadly no multiplayer except for leaderboards but that's one of the tradeoffs you make with slomo/bullet time usually, and that is a super fun feature.Wanna call out the camera especially because that could really make or break a game like this but it works pretty well and feels natural!Recommend this to anyone who likes extreme sports games or bullet hell shooters, even though this isn't strictly a bullet hell, it's got that same sense of onslaught by enemies.I'm not sure if replays are a planned feature but i'd love to see that so I don't have to record every run hoping it's a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Now to be clear, it is a refreshing new thing and does that well. Style is nice and all but to put it simply there is only one thing that makes me not like this game. It's tpart of the controls. You get ammo by performing tricks, there is a trick button, there is no downside to holding it, so basically there is no need for this button for gameplay, but you kinda need it pressed to have ammo. Which makes you basically always hold down a button just cause it's necessary/makes most sense.Maybe sounds a bit silly, but that really annoys the heck out of me.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This is Jet Set Radio for egotistical sadists. Music is impactful and memorable, art style doesn't get in the way of readability and looks clean and stylish. Movement really feels the way that a game about rollerblading should without stepping on the gunplay's toes too hard. Only complaint is that the bossfights feel a little forced. Even then, it has an entire extra campaign included to remix the enemy patterns in an interesting and meaningful way. Easy 10/10. Roll7 hasn't ever missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good I wish I bought it when it was new.Apart from the very satisfying slomo-killing-while-doing-Tony Hawk-tricks game loop there is also a really well done subtle narrative happening at the top of each section of the game. It's the kind of narrative experience that only a video game can really capture and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Never played a skateboard/rollerblade type game before, but it's a cool experience and well blended with combat. I enjoy the variety of enemies and the different strategies you need to counter each one. In this sense, it reminds me of the newer DOOM games. The movement feels somewhat restrictive at first, but if you work with it, it actually provides a nice flow and rhythm to the combat. The bullet time mechanic balances this out perfectly, and takes the pressure off difficult trickshots. Overall, the gameplay feels awesome. Also, the art and design of the game is sweet too! Fun all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It is insane to me that a game this good is known about by so few people. It may be rather short, especially if you choose not to do the NG+ mode, "Out For Blood", or go for high scores on every level, but the level of style is so badass. Art direction like this is timeless, it's in one of my favorite styles, too. Not to mention a banger soundtrack.You will undoubtedly be really bad at this game at first with how many mechanics there are to learn and how there's really nothing else like it out there, but if you like the reward of progressing based on purely mechanical skill, as well as replaying levels to master them and go for every achievement, this game makes that very rewarding. If you're a fan of high-octane action games like ULTRAKILL, you'll like this one.There are a lot of accessibility options if you want to see all of what the game has to offer, but frankly the story elements are pretty light. I like them, they're intriguing, but it's not even close to the main focus, and the game is aware of that, I feel.The game recommends using a controller at the start, which I followed and was okay with, although when encountering groups of enemies and/or destructible objects, it was hard forcing it to aim at the right target. I imagine this would not be much of a problem on mouse+keyboard, but I think the movement may be harder with that control scheme. It wasn't impossible to work with, I just had to rethink my priorities a little and it turned out fine 99% of the time. The aim assist on the sniper weapon is thankfully quite generous as well to make it usable on controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: John Woo meets Roller Derby. Very Fun mechanics and interesting gameplay. Cool art design and soundtrack. Story is subtle and environmental with the main focus on gameplay. Its not a terribly long game unless you are trying to complete all of the challenges. It has two campaigns that can be completed fairly quickly with the second being all the same maps just with every thing unlocked, a new game+ esque. I'd recommend if you are looking for a fun game where you can glide through the air pulling off tricks and flips to dodge snipers and rockets, while also shooting back in slo-mo. Maximum style points. Great pickup on sale... $30 might be pushing it for how short the game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to paint you a picture; you're rolling along at breakneck speeds and catch air off of a halfpipe, while in mid air you effortlessly slip into a Coffin 900 Backflip before time slows to a crawl. Your view curves around to allow you to take in the state of the arena and with precision you fire a grenade launcher twice, blowing the side mounted flamethrowers off of a tank before diving into a roll to avoid sniper fire.This game is one of the best things I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing and I believe my life is more complete for having played it. You should get it, your friends should get it, your family should get it, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hell your dog should get it.Buy this game. Immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: 'Tony Hawk Pro Skater' + 'Max Payne' = Rollerdrome.  The equation is true, but it shortsells the experience.  This is a unique indie title, and one of very few, that I know will keep me coming back.  The artstyle is simple and clean, the gameplay is fun and engaging, and the story/characterization is there but not in-your-face. One of my favorite moments in the game was clicking on a soda can and reading it's flavor text: "Half-empty."  You only get bits and pieces, but it's just enough to know Kara Hassan and the world she lives in.This is one of the best games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. The skating mechanics are solid, if occasionally fiddly (I got stuck on level geometry multiple times, and the trick controls on M+K kinda suck, especially when trying to do the challenges) and the action is satisfying. The weapons are all pretty good, even if the shotgun feels a bit like an unloved middle child (probably doesn't help it's inexplicably introduced with an enemy that counters it) and the game does a lot with its limited roster of enemies. .Arena design is solid barring the oddities I mentioned above and the art style is nice but the solid particles can sometimes obscure the action. There's a story here that is fun to investigate but you can just ignore it. Music's not half bad either. If you like a little disco in your synthwave, here ya go.All in all, a solid action game with a unique twist. If my biggest complaint is that I want more, I suppose that's a good sign.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: The year is 2030. The International Rollerdrome Federation has told you they're gonna pay you $10,000 to hit a schmuck off their rollerskates with a baseball bat. You agree and step into the arena. Seconds later the starting horn blares, and schmuck in question, Kara Hassan, does a Nose Grab 1080 double backflip and empties two full mags into your chest cavity
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: ROLLERDROME has caught me by surprise as a beautiful mixture of two styles I had never seen cavorting in such a way. The art style works wonderfully with the game mechanics and creates a smooth and easy-to-enjoy arcade shooter. I was not expecting the game to be so well put together. I generally play on keyboard and mouse and games like this are often not well made and do not mix with this control style. With ROLLERDROME I have had no issues and the gameplay does not feel disrupted by the control scheme. Controller is an option and is suggested as the controls that should be used. I really like the slow-motion system and the integration of the reload mechanic and trick combos. The game just seems like it was really well thought out and planned to a degree that seems to have fallen off in many new games. Often mechanics are abandoned or half-finished and I love that this game does not fail at this. Level design has really been good so far, I love the art style and the levels give off a feeling of synchronization with the minimalist story. I like the character as well. I love seeing characters that innovate on protagonist themes and create cool, badass, characters without overselling the coolness to a degree that makes them feel fake. I love this game and am excited to see where the devs take the further updates. I could definitely see myself coming back to this one when I need to let off some steam or when I feel like playing Tony-Hawk with guns. -KirbyFor further reading and analysis check out this PC Gamer Review!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I read that Rollerdrome was the perfect mix between Tony Hawk's Pro Skater and Max Payne, and it describe really well the feeling of the game. Roll, jump, do tricks and kill dudes in slow motion is a combination of mecanism I never thought to find in a game and here, it's really good and well executed.It took me around 5H to beat the last Arena (but definitly without all secondary objectives). It seems short BUT there's a lot of fun in this game, and still a lot of challenge after the end game (like the "blood bath" mode or even just completing all objectives of all arenas in the main campaign).You have to be clever and understand how some mecanics can work together to help you defeat the most difficult ennemies in the fastest way. So yeah, I found the main campaign a bit short, not because of the price, it's worth it, but mostly because I had fun and I wanted more !
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Tony Hawk meets May Payne gun play. At first felt like a fun little arcade game that admittedly has a little difficulty spike about half way through. Sure the trick roster is small, and the gun play ain't all that complicated but play enough and suddenly it'll click and you'll be performing areal bullet ballets, prioritizing enemies by how easily they can get you to that active dodge, chasing those high scores. In short, fun for a quick romp, but if it hooks you and you get over that difficulty hump it's becomes an addictive chase to the top of the leaderboard reminiscent of popping quarters in an arcade machine.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't realize how truly,  good this game was until I went back to 100% the campaign and beat NG+. I initially wrote off each level's bonus challenges as busywork, not realizing that they very cleverly ease the player into Rollerdrome's deep complexities. Barely scraping by level-by-level can be fun in its own right, but  the game has been one of the most exhilarating and rewarding experiences I've had this year. Hard to believe a game can be so much "better than the sum of its parts", considering its parts are Tony Hawk Pro Skater and DOOM.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Paul Verhoeven's Pro-Skater is one of those games that describing it just turns into a mess of "It's really cool" and "this feels great to play" and all that jazz... Honestly that's just because it is, it's a "simple" idea really well executed. It's super fun, going for high-scores and full combos feels amazing; doing a crazy flip, perfect dodging a sniper, and using the damage bonus to blow up a mech with a grenade launcher feels beyond incredible; and slowly developing an understanding and mastery of all the mechanics means you start of just trying to survive this game to by the end of it pulling off some of the most outrageous stunts just to murder someone in the most awesome way possible; it's honestly fantastic and I can't recommend trying it out enough :)
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: this is EXTREMELY Aggressive Inline lol. Picture a cell-shaded extreme sports game with Matrix-like bullet play.I even had a crash, and I would give this a solid 10/10. Music is top notch, gameplay is engaging and fun, challenge is ever present, AI makes you work for your score/kills, and it's stylin' the whole time.If you like Tony Hawk, Aggressive Inline, SSX, etc. you'll love this. If you like Max Payne, Enter The Matrix, Viewtiful Joe, Stranglehold, etc. you'll love this. If you dig synth vibes with funky beats, chances are you'll love this.Roll7, you've made a mega-hit. I wanna see multiplayer eventually :D
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's just so good!  Beside RIsk of Rain 2 the first game with shooting elements that I like.  It's rollerblades + really nice weapons + slow mo === lots of fun and style!  I am still only in the semi-finals (level 6 or 7 I think), but it is really cool and challenging and for once this is a game that is teaching me how to play it.You'll need to switch up your weapons to get through things, have different tactics for the different enemies and of course take care that you maybe don't have 2 laserguys, 3 snipers and a couple bomb throwing enemies around at once.  Or more, because that happens.It's really good.  Even as more of a casual player, this is really good.  And because things ramp up so much now the first few levels are a breeze.  And on top of all of this it has a similar art-style to Sable, which is my favourite game ever.  Everybody wins and you will look so cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, simple but challenging, short little indie game that is a lot of fun and doesn't over stay it's welcome. The mechanics are well realised and tuned creating a very rewarding gameplay loop that makes you feel skilled while playing. I would compare it to the game Ghostrunner where when you beat the game and go back to the first level you will notice how much you have improved as a player and that feels very satisfying. I like the art style, the animations are so fluid with all the tricks you can do and just the general movement feels really smooth. Only really negative i can think of is i feel no incentive to continue playing after beating the game to do all the challenges and bonus stages. I feel like i hit my peak with my enjoyment after beating the final stage. 7/10 (Good)
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game is both familiar and yet alien. Learn new mechanics and play a game that isn't quite like any other. It might prima facie remind you of other games and genres, but it really is its own thing. Pick it up and get good at rollershooting. There are some short passive story elements and they neatly break up the gameplay flow. The artstyle is clearly inspired by Jean Giraud and because of that minimal artistic direction it runs very well on the Steam Deck.As gross as it is to discuss money when indie devs deserve more, it's definitely worth £16.49 (current sale price), £24.99 is perhaps a bit steep.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like lengthy reviews but I do like this game.I love Jet Set Radio. I even beat it's tutorial! I love Hotline Miami. I placed pretty high in its leaderboards back in the day, even among all those people who magically got 999,999,999 points in every level. I love Rollerdrome. It's exactly what I want when I imagine those two games mashed together. It's one of those games where adding or subtracting ANYTHING would detract from the overall experience. It's frentic. It's fun. The gameplay is layered without being convoluted and the style is absolutely superb. Again, I'll be brief. If you enjoyed Hotline Miami even a little bit, you will also like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's not the Jet Set Radio alternative I wanted it to be, but it's something that scratches a similar itch while doing something way different and arguably cooler. The game doesn't seem too long at only 16 levels, but it gives you a reason to keep replaying these levels and topping yourself again and again. I've not played much, but I very much love what this game's doing. Can Roll7 ever make a bad game? I think this once again proves they can't.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like an indie game, the character's movements are stiff and a bit awkward. The game looks like a lot of fun, but when you get down to the nitty gritty, it's about pressing "shoot" while auto-aiming in slow motion until the level is over. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun!Fast and tight (stylish?) action game that gives you enough tools to deal with any situation.Does not waste your time, each new level steps up the difficulty enough to keep you interested and encourages you to improve your strategies, but it never once got frustrating even as I completed all the hardest optional challenges. _childDocuments_.review: Incredibly genius way of implementing your use of reflexes in a THPS styled game with the addition of beautiful cell shader art design. Brings huge Jet Set Radio vibes. Even if this game doesn't seem like your cup of tea at first glance from the steam store screenshots and videos, you may be surprised. It's worth giving a try to feel out its great gameplay.  Nailing perfect dodges, getting slow-mo bullet time frags, and topping it off hitting some gnarly bro-bro tricks  off of ramps, grinds, and wallrides all in quick succession feels so satisfying. Perfect execution of blending sports and action in one game. I received this game in Humble Choice April 2023. Recommended to anybody that likes interesting games.

_childDocuments_.review: Found the game teased on a random post, and knew I had to get it.While I rarely play any games that involves skating, this game is really lenient when it comes to doing tricks as there is no penalty for failing to land on your feet after doing tricks allowing you to be careless while looking fancy at the same time which is good since stunts are required in order to reload your weapons.Each enemy type is also noticeably different, affecting which weapons you'll need to equip at a given time while at the same time making sure you have enough ammo to perform varying takedown methods depending on who you're facing at the time. All attacks can be dodged, which highly benefits you as there is a "Perfect Dodge" mechanic which can activate "Super Reflex", more on that on the next statement.You get four weapons which consists of a pair of pistols, a shotgun capable of firing buckshot or piercing slugs, a grenade launcher, and a railgun. All of them minus the pistols are capable of dealing piercing damage, but you can include the pistols as well by doing Super Reflex. Super Reflex not only gives you infinite slow motion during the time it's active, it also allows your weapons to deal increased damage which noticeable enough to reach breakthrough points allowing you to save ammo for more fliud takedowns on subsequent enemies in short periods of time. You also gain ammo each time it triggers.It can be difficult at times at least for the first few moments since there's a good chance that you're new to performing tricks on top of shooting frequently, but once you get the hang of shuffling between those two actions you'll surely be satisfied as you pull off long strings of combos even if you make a mistake or two during the match. It's honestly really great. I highly recommend this game to anyone who prefers gunning at high speeds, all while avoiding attacks on their way to being a trickster.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: So before i go any further, this is a great game, intriguing graphics and fun mix of combat and "tony hawk" style tricks (and great music.)The reason i'm not recomending this game is that the level progression is locked behind challenges that seem far too difficult (and too large in number requirements) for your average/below average gamer, especially in this specific style of game. I consider myself a "decent" gamer, not good, not bad, but decent. I beat the 4th match, but because i didn't complete enough challenges (and they aren't easy for a casual gamer like me) i was not allowed to progress, despite the fact i did in fact beat the level. Now if this is intentionally a hard game and not for casual gamers, OK, but it would be nice if there was a disclaimer for that. Personally, i think the challenges should unlock new/better gear, new weapons, better armor, skates, perhaps abilities (passive or otherwise.) Things like that, the challenges should be a "secondary" objective to make the game easier as a reward for completing them, not a requirement to progress, beating the level should be the requirement to progress. This way if you are a completionist or you just want better gear, grind out those challenges, if you get stuck on a level and need better gear, grind out those challenges, if you are doing well enough as you are, then just keep beating the levels. I also think the challenges should be more generic, some point oriented ones (get X amount of points per challenge tier,) dodge enemy attacks X amount of times, don't take any damage for the level (this should be in all levels, etc.) Things of that nature, not weapon specific challenges, because what if you don't feel comfortable using that weapon type, or that gear type? Again, if the game is meant to be geared towards a specific crowd, OK, but otherwise, for the casual player, it's way too hard as it stands, at least as far as I'm concerned. I came here to spend a few hours and play a fun tony hawk style combat game, and it was fun while it lasted. But, for me at least, it got too hard too fast, i'm just not that talented at gaming and i don't have the patience to pour hours into a single level.

_childDocuments_.review: The amalgamation of Tony Hawk, Jet Set Radio, and Max Payne mechanics results in an engaging, addictive gaming experience. Players find themselves immersed in a dynamic environment where multitasking becomes imperative—executing tricks, racing against the clock, and achieving combos and multipliers in the pursuit of varied challenges.The sensation of embodying a character akin to Neo from the Matrix, effortlessly dispatching opponents with John Wick-like precision, contributes to the game's inherent satisfaction. The execution of seamless dodges and utilization of bullet time enhances the overall experience, providing a gratifying sense of accomplishment.For those who appreciate the outlined elements and resonate with the game's art style, I wholeheartedly recommend buying this meticulously balanced gaming endeavor. Rollerdrome, while skill-based, remains accessible to casual gamers, allowing for an enjoyable pick-up-and-play experience. With dedicated time investment, players will inevitably witness a gradual enhancement of their skills, progressing from novice to adept.My current progress stands at 33 percent completion, revealing a discernible narrative unfolding within the game. Notably absent, at this juncture, are features related to character or weapon customization. It is my hope that the developers may consider incorporating such aspects through a future, complimentary update.In essence, Rollerdrome encapsulates the essence of simple, yet remarkably enjoyable, gaming. It serves as an ideal, quick diversion to unwind after the rigors of school or work, offering a seamless hop-in, hop-out experience to alleviate stress.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Highly recommended, so buy it! (return it if you don't like it within 2 hours)It's fair to call this Tony Hawk's Pro Shooter, though it has more in common with SSX (imo). I bought this game because both the gameplay and the art style are unique, and I hope to see more games like this one. It scratched an itch I didn't realize I had.General observations:* It's nearly impossible not to "land" a trick (very forgiving in this regard)* The game ramps up the difficulty pretty quickly (surprisingly so)* Replayability comes in the form of challenges & leaderboards, so you replay levels to accomplish a set list of up to 10 separate challenges and/or maximize your score* Gunplay & movement controls feel crisp and responsive* Can be very satisfying when pulling off some of the more difficult challengesCon:* Limited longevity - limited number of maps/enemies/tricks/guns, so I won't have much reason to keep playing once I complete all the levels & challenges (however, the content currently available is great fun)I'm really enjoying this game so far. The skill ceiling is way higher than anything I'll ever reach, but I'm having a lot of fun replaying the levels and doing the challenges. Beating the game unlocks something akin to "Hard Mode", so you can repeat all the levels but with higher intensity. I have yet to find replaying any of the levels tedious, but this does seem like the kind of game that would benefit from randomly generated levels/challenges/enemy spawns (though I'm no dev). I don't know if more content will be available in the future, but I'm pretty happy with the game as-is.I heartily recommend buying this game. You will know within 2 hours whether or not you're going to enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but amazing game. Indie studios just keep delivering Ws in an era where triple A studios takes Ls up the ass like Yagami Light in a Death Note fanfic. Pros:+The premise is already pretty awesome. You have a pair of roller skates and some guns. You roll into an arena full of people hired specifically to kill contestants like you in as many ways as they can. You will dodge sniper bullets, mines, rockets, laser beams, pools of acid, and everything else under the sun as you try to kill everyone before they can kill you. Yes, it is just as frantic, chaotic and breakneck as it sounds. This game is the patron saint of the "think fast" school of game design, and you're gonna be mopping up buckets of sweat after each session with it. +Gameplay is extremely fluid and tight. This game is a textbook example of good game design. Not only is the movement fast and responsive, the shooting is also very snappy and satisfying. The shooting and roller skating are intrinsically linked together, as you need to perform tricks to get more bullets to keep shooting. Although this takes some getting used to at first, soon you'll be flying through the air doing flips and emptying entire clips into the enemies. The devs really polished the core gameplay loop to a mirror sheen, with no real flaws or complaints I can point out. +The story is somewhat barebones. This is a definitely a game where the gameplay was conceived first, and then the story was written around it to establish the bare minimum context for the gameplay. I think this is a good thing, because it allows Rollerdrome to focus mainly on its gameplay loop, which is the best thing it has going for it. The game sprinkles just enough story here and there so that you'll understand the setting, the backstory and personality of the main character, the stakes, and why she's participating in a blood sport. I like this approach to storytelling; it's not overbearing or intrusive upon the gameplay when it's not that necessary or not that good, which is a mistake I've seen many other indie games make. Rollerdrome knows exactly what it wants to be, and it doesn't try to overreach in the story department.Cons:-If I had to nitpick something, I'd say the way you unlock new levels kinda suck: you need to do challenges for previous levels that force you to play a certain way, which is kinda annoying in a game that encourages you to "think fast" and spontaneously do ♥♥♥♥ on the fly. The game grinds to a halt when you haven't completed enough of these challenges in the previous levels, so you have to go back and grind them for a bit to unlock new levels. However, there are some upsides to this: it's pretty fun to revisit the earlier levels of the game that gave you trouble before and absolutely style on them. It's an extremely satisfying feeling to see how much you've improved and mastered the game's mechanics, and these things no longer pose any challenge to you. Secondly, the challenges are pretty forgiving as to how you unlock them. After you've completed a challenge, you can simply exit the level and it will still remain completed. You can simply get into a level to complete that specific challenge then peace out, so at the end of the day, grinding for them is not too bad.-Maps get reused towards the end of the game. However, the game does change them up a bit and make them feel just "new" enough to be a new level, albeit being the same map. Rollerdrome is an indie game anyways so I'll let this pass. It's actually pretty cool to see how much mileage they got out of 4 or 5 maps total throughout the entire game. Verdict: 9.5/10Some small nitpicks aside, Rollerdrome might very well be a perfect indie game. It's fast, fun, and extremely well designed. It might take some getting used to at first, but by 2-3 hours in, you'll no longer be struggling with the game; you'll be styling on it and doing some of the coolest ♥♥♥♥ you've done in a video game in a long time. This is the kind of ♥♥♥♥ that you saw in action movies as a kid and thought "damn I wish I could do that too." Well, buy Rollerdrome then. It's probably one of the best indie games this year.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, the perfect marriage of Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater and Sunset Overdrive. Although Rollerdrome may initially feel basic and simple, the difficulty quickly ramps up as you unlock more stages. The introduction of extra enemy varieties can be overwhelming, but as you begin to understand the mechanics and techniques best suited for each enemy, the game becomes a symphony of focused movement where you start completing all the challenges you once thought were impossible. Rollerdrome consists of a campaign with eleven different locations, with new enemy varieties and weapons becoming available the further through the courses you progress. Each of these courses come with its own checklist of objectives to complete, which is briefly used to level gate courses, however you shouldn't need to replay too many courses to get through the main campaign.Instead, these objectives provide an incentive to replay past courses once you complete the main story, aiming for top scores, and doing specific tricks or challenges. This is appreciated, as upon completing the main campaign (finishing each of the courses a single time) my enjoyment was slightly dampened by my desire to play more. The developers however, took this into consideration by creating an entirely separate second campaign called Out For Blood. In Out For Blood, every enemy type and weapon is in play from the very first course, making each arena feel fresh. The enemy damage is also increased, causing a significant difficulty jump from the final course of the main campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a game that knows exactly what it wants to be. It’s pure, unrestrained fun, stripped of unnecessary elements. From the very first moments, it reminded me of what it means to enjoy gameplay – that raw, dynamic entertainment that is so often missing today.Tony Hawk's Pro Skater is an undeniable classic that shaped my career as a gamer. However, I never thought that what it might have been missing was... firearms. Now, after experiencing Rollerdrome, this combination seems so obvious.Rollerdrome makes the satisfaction of eliminating opponents accessible and intuitive, yet incredibly addictive. Sure, we can simply roll up to an enemy and shoot them with a shotgun, but once we discover that only a few buttons and a well-timed jump separate us from a spectacular Nose Grab elimination with a flip, it’s hard to stop doing it.The story and universe are solid – they don’t overshadow the flashy gameplay, but rather make shooting while roller-skating feel less strange and detached from reality. The soundtrack further drives the pace, and the list of tricks and weapons ensures that the excitement doesn’t fade quickly. Each new round is a fresh challenge that draws you in even more, encouraging you to experiment with different combinations of moves and eliminations.Rollerdrome is a title that combines dynamism and challenge, offering players a unique experience. The game not only captivates but also surprises with its freshness and well-thought-out fusion of two different worlds – sports acrobatics and intense combat. It’s a must-play for those who seek something more than the typical action game and want to remind themselves of how satisfying pure, uninterrupted gameplay can be.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves so much more attention. If you like any kind of action game where movement and timing is also a big part, you can't go wrong with this. (Returnal, Doom and Doom Eternal, Risk of Rain 2, Cruelty Squad, Roboquest are examples)It is extremely well polished (especially from a gameplay perspective), runs like a dream even on old hardware, looks beautiful while remaining visually coherent and allows you to feel like a true badass getting long combos while styling on your enemies. A replay mode would go a long way to really take in the amazing stunts you pull off since the game is so fast paced you don't notice half the crazy ♥♥♥♥ you do.Personally I love the worldbuilding and universe they have created, it's just enough to pique your curiosity, but don't expect much storytelling or narrative. This is very much a "gameplay first" type of game with a bit of lore to complement the action, but it's done very well. In terms of difficulty, I would say it is introduced in spikes, but once you have all 4 weapons you are set for the rest of the game. There are no further unlocks, you just have to practice and experiment with the challenge checklists as they also serve as a teaching tool for game mechanics. I didn't find it too hard once you set a priority in your mind of which enemies to get rid of quickly and which weapons to use for every type of opponent. When it comes to controls, I only used a controller and that is what is recommended. I have tried with kb/m and it's totally possible to play like this, although I feel it is less intuitive (the highest scores on PC are done with kb/m). If you insist on playing with kb/m, I would recommend disabling camera autocenter and rebind the grind, grab and flip keys to mouse buttons if possible.Roll7  have such a solid foundation with this game, I just hope they release more content either in the form of DLC or a sequel, but it would be criminal not to expand upon this rock-solid core they have built.The synthwave soundtrack is also great and I would buy it on steam in a heartbeat.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game, It blends the best parts of Tony Hawk movement with blasting people and it works amazing. _childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome's intense high flying action acid drops you into one hell of an experience. Mechanics were starting click and managing combat and style together was producing a very enjoyable experience.There's something inherently cool about doing a 540 backflip as you fire slugs from your shotgun. The slo-mo (reflex) makes all of this possible without much effort needed. While it is beneficial to land on your feet, if you don't your senses kick in and you roll to avoid a nasty slam. This keeps the danger side of things for the enemies to handle.I played through the main story once, going through each level at least twice to check off challenges and unlock the next stage. This pacing was near perfect for me, not too long, not too short, just right.
