_childDocuments_.review: For the first hour, I'll be honest, I wasn't super keen on Rollerdrome. The controls felt obtuse, the combo system was nowhere near what I was expecting, and I wasn't over the moon about the games reliance on slow motion to make things possible. But after having completed the game and gone back to S rank most of the missions I'm pretty damn happy with what I played even if it what I wasn't expecting. When I started to treat it more like a Rhythm game, in the sense that the first time around a level is fully a learning experience and refinement came later, I found there was an ebb and flow that is unconventional but deeply satisfying to get good at. Planning routes around the level, figuring out when I need to start tricking to reset my ammo for the next segment, and learning the map so I can use the combo tokens to keep the score up while getting more tricks in - that was where the game shined. I still think there's issues, especially the game being built around the slow motion never letting it reach the ferocious pace I was expecting, but if you're the kind of person who's looking for a shooter all about perfecting a level rather than just playing through it once and letting it go, I think there's a lot to like here.

_childDocuments_.review: My eyes hurt and I don't feel well, which are unrelated to this game, but I want to write this before I lose the will to do. Please pardon any mistakes or weird sentences.Rollerdrome is a fast-paced third-person shooter on rollerskates. It is a high-octane, non-stop action ride that keeps the adrenaline pumping every second of every level. It is fun, it is challenging, and it is very cool. The backdrop of the game seems to be a retro-future earth where the death sport known as Rollerdrome is the number one sensation. As Kara Hassan, the silent protagonist and rookie to the Rollerdrome, you fight and skate your way through the competition to be crowned the champion. The story, bare as it is, is shown through about four or so vignettes before key levels. These vignettes are brief; you walk around one of a few small rooms in first-person view, picking up items and reading notes. There are radio broadcasts to listen to, bits of dialogue to eavesdrop on through locked doors, and some small roleplay choices (I call it a "roleplay choice" because they don't impact the story in any way, they're small bits just for the fun of it, such as choosing to move a sticky note on a board, or how to pose an action figure). Other than these small windows into the fiction of Rollerdrome, there isn't any other story to be gleamed. This is slightly disappointing, as the world and technology seem interesting if the developers wanted to further explore this worldspace. I would welcome a game that explored this world further, but within the context of Rollerdrome I feel the story given is sufficient. The gameplay as it is doesn't seem like it could easily support a longer, more in-depth narrative, and honestly that's fine. The game certainly doesn't seem to want to have a richer story, and the "protagonist" Kara doesn't give the vibe of a freedom fighter; they're here to be made champion, and that is the main goal the game gives the player.The gameplay is Tony Hawk with guns. You skate around an arena, some indoors some outdoors, blasting enemies as they spawn in. Your goal is to complete the level as quickly as possible while racking up the highest score by doing tricks, dodging enemy shots, and killing enemies in quick succession. There is a score multiplier that goes up with every enemy killed, and the multiplier slowly ticks down as you skate around from enemy to enemy. If you get hit you take damage (health is recovered by killing enemies) and your multiplier reduces, sometimes almost entirely if you get hit multiple times quickly. You reload by performing tricks, which can lead to some cool scenarios where, for instance, you unload on an enemy while in the air, do a spin-grab to reload, and then finish them off on the way down. The game wants you to be fast in both your skating tricks and your shooting, and honestly once you get into the rhythm it just feels fun.Progressing through the game amounts to both clearing each level, as well as accomplishing a set number of challenges in order to unlock the next round of the competition. Each level has 10 challenges, ranging from skating based challenges (such as performing a specific trick at a marked location), to eliminating enemies with specific weapons or under specific circumstances. Other challenges involve getting above a certain score, completing the level within a set time limit, or gathering all five combo markers on the level.Completing the challenges at first seemed maybe a bit daunting. Some of them seemed downright impossible to me, and I spent a good deal of time trying to hit certain point thresholds on some of the later levels (and never meeting them at all on the last few, damn is it hard to hit a million points!). But after going back to the first few levels to knock out a few easy challenges, I began to realize that by following and completing the challenges, the game was indirectly teaching you how to play better. Especially going back to learn how to properly use the last gun, a charge-up sniper rifle, was invaluable to even completing the game. I struggled heavily with the gun at first, before realizing that the gun didn't have to be aimed entirely accurately: dot is red, shot is going to hit. By the time I got to the last stage I had completed over half of the challenges in the game. It was tough, sometimes frustrating, but all very doable with a bit of practice and perserverance. The game very much reminds me of something out of an arcade or something that would have fit on an older console. The game doesn't hold you hand at all, but all of the tools are there for you to succeed. You, the player, just have to get the hang of it. It very much had me recall my days playing SSX on the Playstation 2. But, y'know, with guns. Like SSX, the game gets downright hard on the later levels, but if you sit down, take a deep breathe, and focus on small challenges at a time, you will get better at the game. You will suddenly find yourself charging the laser on a rail to kick off onto a wall, fire one full charge at one sniper across the map and then fire a second shot at another enemy in the same moment, just for you to dodge another sniper, get your ammo back, and finish off the second enemy. I definitely do recommend Rollerdrome, to those who enjoy games like SSX or Pro Skater. The game is challenging and fun, it has an interesting and clean visual style, and while the music isn't what I would call memorable it always fits and blends well with the aesthetic of the game. I'd say to most people to give it a try. It certainly isn't for everyone, but I had a lot of fun with it and I'm sure many others will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is an amazing twist on Tony Hawk, if Tony Hawk was a groovy futuristic killing machine on skates. The game does an amazing job at being stylish and making you play stylishly. You're equipped with 4 guns each of which share from the same pool of ammo, meaning choice of gun is really all about picking the right tool for the right enemy, and not managing different ammo counts. Speaking of ammo, you have very little, which sounds like a bummer but it's not I promise.  In order to get more ammo you have to do tricks, this leads to the game having a really good balance between doing flips, grabs, grinds, and wall rides; and soaring through the air in bullet time shooting baddies. In fact, you should be doing all these tricks WHILE shooting the enemies, while you fly through the air in slow motion, or wallride past them like a vertical drive-by. The game has super fluid animations, and you can't actually bail and drop your combo.Rather than punish you for launching off a ramp at a bad angle, the games combo meter is built off chaining kills together. This means you can't waste time just flipping around through the air, you have to be chasing enemies down and killing them in a single clip. The enemy combatants are no pushovers either, they come in a good variety that reminds me a lot of the combat chess in arena shooters like Doom. You have weak dudes with bats who can be easily avoided and act as combo fodder, big tanks who scatter mines everywhere, and teleporting snipers who chase after you with lasers. The game slowly adds these enemies to the mix and each one teaches you something new, you learn how to avoid them and the timing of their attacks, and which guns work best on them. But the game is never unfair either, you have a quick dodge you can do at any time that will shake enemy attacks off of you or timed perfectly will allow you dodge them. All enemy attacks are telegraphed super clearly and are easy to react to, once you learn the timings, getting a perfect dodge allows you to go into this really cool Super Reflex mode that inverts the games colors and highlights the enemies bright red while you gain extra damage on all your guns. This super reflex mode becomes a really important and fun aspect of the game that gives avoiding enemy attacks perfectly a big reward that can often mean the difference of being able to kill an enemy in one clip opposed to two, you can even chain these bullet times and perfect dodges and each perfect dodge rewards you with additional ammo. This means you're always able to react to the game, you have so much going on, keeping your combo up, killing enemies fast, shooting and swapping weapons, being able to see and dodge attacks quickly and at any time and still have all the animations look so smooth it really does lead to some really cool moments as you master the stages. The games main story mode even has little explorable sections, with objects you can examine and messages from sponsors and some of your opponents you'll be facing. As well as news about the dystopian world who all watches this future bloodsport.  There's enough here to give window dressing and stakes to your gladitorial murder sprees, which paints you as an up and coming rookie, with the odds stacked against them, who becomes a rising star as you advance in the championship. Each stage has a bunch of side objectives and of course a high score with a letter grade. Progression in the main game requires you to get at least 3/4th or so of the challenges to beat the campaign which then unlocks a much much harder mode with even harder challenges involving high scores and beating levels in a single combo or in a certain amount of time. These side objectives are totally optional in the "Out for Blood" stages, just surviving these stages is a challenge enough really, but it's there for those who really want to master them. Mastering the stages is fun as you go back and pick up certain challenges you missed the first time or really just when you die over and over trying to get those single-combo challenges on Out for Blood.I love this games art, it's gameplay, it's stylish animations, and tron-like soundtrack. It is most definitely worth 20 bucks if you love ♥♥♥♥ like this. You probably like ♥♥♥♥ like this. Get.

_childDocuments_.review: Super cool. This really is a Tony Hawk game with guns.The way you need to use tricks and your guns just works really well and it feels great to pull off everything smoothly.Basically, just doing tricks and shooting poorly won't get you anywhere. Shooting a lot without pulling off tricks is not possible. You have to balance both. Pulling off tricks while killing enemies gives you more points.It's easy to complete a level, but if you want to get a higher ranking, things get a lot more difficult.I do have a few nitpicks though.You know how you can exit a half pipe in Tony Hawk games right? Well it's the same here, except here you also use the right stick for different grabs, control which way to flip and turn while aiming and shooting and getting shot at.So what ends up happening for me a lot is that I accidentally jump out of a half pipe into walls or off cliffs.I'm not sure how this could have been done better, but it is annoying.Another thing that irks me is that in the larger levels it gets hard to locate enemies and when you're down to the last one it is a bit frustrating. There is no arrow or mini map to guide you around to the enemies. I think that wouldn't hurt the game at all or compromise the difficulty.I do wish the game had some options to turn this more into a 70's grindhouse movie (some color grading and film grain).It's obviously not necessary, but I really love the style this game is going for and it would be cool to be able to go all out.Oh and multiplayer... That would kick ass.Anyways, this game is great. It feels high quality, it's well designed and polished. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to love Rollerdrome. It has a ton of great ideas. But some of the difficulty balancing on certain sections is just bonkers. Some levels are absurdly easy to learn, while others seemingly are built to grind you into dust until you masochistically perfect them. And the trick is, it's not always the ones you'd think. Combine that with some maps being poor at indicating where that LAST enemy is stuck, and the keyboard controls being less than ideal... as much as I loved the -start-, I just am having less and less fun with Rollerdrome.If I had to highlight one particular weakpoint - the alpine levels with the giant ring out gaps. It's just irritating to fall to your death not because of choice, but Kara refusing to respond to your controls. What the trailers also leave out is that your ammo is reliant on performing stunts, so you're trying to pull off fresh moves over and over (some of which are NOT easy to do under heavy fire) just to keep up a sustained rate of fire. I'd have massively preferred ammo pickups as an option or another means of gaining ammunition for if stunts are less than ideal. Which you wouldn't think would be necessary, until 20+ rockets and two different cryo beam girls are chasing you across a map so frantically that you can barely make sense of what's happening.This is such a damn shame because when you do get into the -right- flowstate, Roll7's efforts here gives you one of the most unique third-person action experiences in years. It makes infinitely better use of the late 70's, early 80's aesthetic to inspire its gameplay than, say, Deathloop, but there comes a point where the "fluid movement' advertised is smothered under a barrage of too many attacks and the protagonist struggling to keep up with your inputs.And before someone inevitably says it - a controller shouldn't be necessary. If Tony Hawk and countless other games could translate to KB&Mouse, then Rollerdrome should too. Not only because it's more convenient if you don't own a controller, but because it's better accessibility for those who are better off with a keyboard than a controller.I really wanted to love you, Rollerdrome. _childDocuments_.review: I have to echo the sentiment of other reviewers, this is a sometimes fun game marred by issues with the difficulty. The core gameplay here is fun, and trying to achieve the challenges on each level is engaging and satisfying but all of that fun goes out of the window in the face of the frustration I felt trying to clear some of the later levels. I'm not one to pass up a challenge, but here the difficulty doesn't seem fair, with damage coming from off-screen and leading to a surprise death. There are indicators that missiles etc. are incoming, but these are a little arrow on a busy effect-filled screen. This came to a head with the final boss, which was so frustrating it's really soured my overall experience.There is a good game here, but not one that's for everyone, or by the end of the game and after the increase in difficulty, for most people.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great indy and is exactly how they should be. Roguelite used as an excuse to not properly balance a game or put in any effort? Nope. Proceedurally generated to save devs time and marketed it as having hours upon hours of gameplay? Nope.This is a work of love, the 10 levels are handcrafted, there are 4 weapons. It does feel slightly odd to control, but the game is an absolute blast to play, and the mode unlocked after completing the main campaign is great too and requires you to really be on your feet. The game is challenging in the later levels and really requires you to learn the game and the patterns, this is not something you can turn your brain off to play.It is a well made, well thought out game that is a blast to play and really has a unique feel. The visuals are great but there is no AA options and a lot of specular aliasing which ruins the IQ quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: With only 32 recent negative reviews, versus 1063 positive ones at the time of writing, I was more inclinded to give it a negative rating myself, since my whole experience with the game was rather mixed.I had fun  with the game at the beginning, even completing all challanges in about 50% of the levels, however, towards the second half of the game, levels became a lot more chaotic, and I started to struggle with the controls and the fact that ammo only replenished by doing tricks (with most of the later ennemies requiring 2 full clips of ammo). It's not a suprise that only 10% of the players here on steam got the achievement for completing the last level.Sadly what I'll remember most of this game is the chaos and lack of refinement. For the enthousiast, there's a few tricks and late dodges to master in order to get a bit more grip on the chaos, but this is not something for me.Avoid at the current full price of €30. _childDocuments_.review: There's not a lot of content and I can't recommend it for the price unless it's heavily discounted.Besides a lack of content, the game design just makes it not very fun to play:- It is fairly difficult, especially if you're trying to do all of the challenges for each level, which you're probably going to want to do because that's all there is to do in the game.- The challenges to complete levels in a certain time limit or maintain a combo bonus/kill-streak mean that you spend most of your time in slow-mo to kill the enemies quickly, and you briefly exit slow-mo to perform a quick trick to reload your weapons and recharge the slow-mo meter for your next kill.- The enemy attacks can be very spammy and you're pressured to focus on counter-sniping the sniping enemies which will continually lock-on to you from anywhere within a level.- Essentially the gameplay just doesn't really 'flow',  the gunplay doesn't compliment the skating and the skating doesn't really compliment the gunplay. It works better on the earlier, easier, levels but quickly starts feeling like a chore to play when you're trying to do the challenges.It does look great though!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay fine, I've decided to learn through all the 15 tutorials of weird maneuvers around the skating block this game forces you to right at the beginning, excepting that maybe afterwards, there would be a storyline to follow, characters to sympathize with, a plight to be had... Maybe this girl had her life on the line, and it was either Rollerdrome or a life in a brothel... Maybe like that famous Netflix Show, Squidgame, her mom is suffering and she needed the money, I mean why else would you participate in a Skating Murder Bloodsport game? No... no, none of that... This girl you play as just loves to kill men (lol) and the only legal way to do so in this cryptic universe of this game is to join the Rollerdrome.While the graphics are nice to look at, this game is horrendous. You play as Kara Hassan, a rollerdromer (people who grind around shooting men in Rugby uniforms) who, for whatever reason, wants to make it to the finales of the World Rollerdromer Tounrament. Some glimpses of a bigger picture are thrown into the mix before the start of some stages, but by that point, you're too annoyed to actually care. Now if you don't care about having a narrative in your games, let's talk about the mechanics: Kara has to build up a score by shooting the Baseball players in armor, grinding around the arena, and doing stunts called "Leg Grabs". The game basically teaches you all of those in an extensive, two hours tutorial lol. Anyways, a few stages in and you'll figure out that you'll be ditching 85% of what the tutorials teach you to survive: Grinding sucks, Grabs contribute to the score but you're completely vulnerable while doing them, and not all weapons work against all enemies... Try going for the challenges at the same time as trying to stop these hundreads of missiles homing in on you and you're dead.The most frustrating thing about this is that the game could've been great with the right balance patch... in a, just-play-with-no-narrative kind of way (like how we used to go play Windows' Minesweeper to wait for your parents to cook you lunch lol)... But some of the Grabs don't even work, and Acid Dropping, which is actually mandatory in some stages, seems to take you off the arena rather than do what it's supposed to do.Overall, Rollerdrome remains a poor man's Sunset Overdrive... There, I freaking SAID it. ! Oh and did I mention that all stages look exactly the same? Yeah, even the DLC ones are exact copies of the main campaign... *Sigh* Thanks Humble Bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent concept, wonderful art and style, interesting world, but in practice the game is simply far too congested and clunkyI really, really appeciate what the developer was going for, and the game is fun in the opening stages, but it quickly becomes far too much to manage, with the controls feeling limiting and constricting when compared to the stylish, free-flow nature of the game.As many other reviews have stated, it's like Tony Hawk mixed with Max Payne, but the issue is that the skating and shooting both feel much clunkier than either of those titles, and with an extremely fast-pace, very small arenas, and a ton of enemies, it quickly devolves from stylish, slick fun to a mash of buttons struggling to remember how to do anything at all.I have played my fair share of games with complex controls, like DOOM Eternal on Hardcore and I'm sure there is a hardcore crowd out there that this game appeals to, but for me, the controls were simply far too clunky and slow to respond to what I wanted the game to do, and when combined with the frantic nature of the game it just became frustrating. I would love to try to improve my skills, I love games like this, but to me it feels less an issue of my understanding and moreso the timing/animations/targeting, etc that are all working as intended, just not smooth enough for me, personally, for this style of game and combat. A real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is an innovative and satisfying mash-up of action and extreme sports games, and the combo works!  It pulls off this odd mix of genres pretty well, though there are issues and compromises that come with such an odd mix.  However, I give a lot of credit for innovation, and there's tons of room for improvements in a sequel.Audiovisually, the game has a strong and cohesive aesthetic that makes the gameplay easy to read in the thick of the action.  The game aims for a mix of comic book cel shading with an '80s retro-future dystopia, and hits the target well enough, though none of the art has been particularly memorable or stand-out.While the two genres work well together, which is quite the accomplishment, neither half of the game would be strong enough to stand on their own.  As just an action game or just as an extreme sports game, neither would be that good.  As an extreme sports game, the level design is extremely lacking when compared to many of the greats in the genre.  The levels are pretty small and open, with few distinguishing features or interesting lines to take.  The genre is well over 20 years old at this point, yet the levels on display here are ridiculously simple, even by basic PS2 standards.  The trick system is really basic too, and you can't fail any tricks, which is a fair compromise to leave room for the action.  This is very much an action game first, with some trappings of extreme sports.As an action game, the enemies are well-designed and distinctive, with each type encouraging a different approach to take.  However, most (maybe all) of the enemies are stationary the whole time.  You get four weapons, and they all share the same shallow ammo pool, which is rather annoying.  You refill ammo by doing tricks or dodges, but many of the enemies will take your entire ammo pool to kill one of them.  While this does make for an interesting strategic twist, it really limits the whole "cool factor" the game is going for.  While going into slo-mo off a quarterpipe and dumping 12 rounds into a heavy enemy shows no sign of getting old anytime soon, it would be great to be able to push it further at times, but you can't because your ammo limits are so paltry.  Recovering your ammo doesn't take much effort, so I've found myself just doing a basic flip and grab off the ground (you can't fail tricks, remember) to get a few more shots way too often.  I would've preferred a system where you had more ammo at your disposal but it took more effort to get re-stocked.Despite my criticism of the game, I am enjoying it quite a lot, because it is a fresh idea executed reasonably well.  I hope it does well because a sequel to this could be truly excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: Mark this down as another "I wanted to like it, but..." review - the basic idea is so cool, and the art style is so unique, that I was ready to put this on my Game of the Year list by the time I finished the first level. Unfortunately, the designers decided to lean in *hard* on difficulty over pretty much anything else, and the result is that most levels beyond the first two or three are a tedious slog. Getting to the end of a level isn't impossible, by any means, but doing so requires that you play in a very specific, ultra-defensive style that actively undercuts everything that makes the game fun in the first place. A huge example of this is the way snipers work. You spend probably 75% of the game, no exaggeration, with a sniper trained on you, waiting for the laser sight to turn white so you can get a perfect dodge. As a result, there's no real way to line up jumps, because you can't commit to *anything* when you're always only a few seconds or two away from having to dodge sideways. Over and over again, I'd have a great jump in view and start heading towards it, only to have a sniper land on me and force me to roll away and lose the opportunity. It's extremely frustrating, and it trains you to never go for anything more than a second or two away. I see a lot of comparisons to Tony Hawk, but this game is the exact opposite when it comes to that feeling of setting up a cool little route across the map; instead, you just learn to head directly towards whatever ramp or half-pipe is closest and pray you can get a little air before another sniper lands on you.There are a lot of other enemies that throw a wrench into the traversal too - one chases you with a laser beam that leaves a trail of flames wherever it hits, which is *another* example of artificial difficulty that limits where you can and can't go rather than rewarding you for finding fun and novel routes across the map. This whole game is a classic example of a design philosophy that makes having fun and doing well mutually exclusive - over and over again in this game, I found myself thinking, "Well, I *could* do this really cool thing... but my score will be higher if I just turtle up and take potshots at everyone while zipping back and forth across the map in a straight line." I got about halfway, completing all the extra objectives for each map, before just getting tired of it. A huge disappointment, all in all.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a fun game held back by poor features. The actual core is quite good, and it often succeeds in making you feel like the badass that the trailer promises. There is a lot to juggle during combat and it makes things feel stressful and hectic. The problems come in with the add-ons. The big thing is the challenges. It is required to get a certain number of these to progress, but also my gamer achievement brain demands I collect all of them. This poses a problem when many of these challenges are just outlandishly hard. Many of them involve pulling off tricks that I swear aren't even possible, while others are just "collect the 5 orange tokens that we put around the map lol". It means that instead of actually trying to hone your skill and get better at the game, you have to waste most of your runs just doing random ♥♥♥♥. Another thing is the pitfalls. Half the maps have these, and in most games they do work well enough. However, Rollerdrome has a very fast movement system with **auto movement** that requires sometimes large turn radiuses, which leads to falling off the map constantly. This subtracts 10% of your health and also really kills the flow of the game. Overall, I wish I could like Rollerdrome, but it is too frustrating for me to continue playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is pure sensory overload. The dystopian 70's futuresport combat mixed with cell shading is such a vibe. You bet your ass I'm gonna pull some tricks.It took me about 3-5 hours to fully digest the game mechanics, enemy patterns, and start putting some real flow-state runs together.  After beating a level, I instantly wanted to beat it again and see how high I could get the combo meter. Beating the game took about 8 hours, but the New game+ will take me quite a bit longer. Yes, it's the same levels, and the same enemies, but it feels like a completely new experience. Enemies are everywhere and you have to build the perfect run to advance, and when you do, it's just the most satisfying feeling in the world.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not be a fan of skating/skateboarding games today. But, this game makes it very simple in its mechanics, but difficult in its challenge. Yet, each level contains either a new mechanic, new weapon or (most intimidatingly) a new enemy. By the time you complete a new level, you have been through the trenches of learning a new map and narrowly dodging a slew of bats, bullets, mines, missiles, mechs, ice beams, and sludge (in that order!). _childDocuments_.review: In the cell shaded, synthwave future; there is only murder. I grabbed this game on the basis it was a mashup of games I have enjoyed before with the strong Tony Hawk of yesteryear vibes in the midst of an arena shooter, and it delivered on that emphatically. Graphically this has a really nice style and is very readable while moving at speed. There is a story in here too, it's fine.The core loop of tricking, grinding and offing the house players (ideally mid-backflip or wallride) to get your score up and clear the park is immensely satisfying and It eases you into it's various tools gently but fast enough that you are firing on all cylinders before too long. There's a decent amount of enemy variety here as well.The 4 weapons felt like enough to me (the shotgun and Z-11 having some nice sub-mechanics) and by the end you will be using all 4 as the situation demands. It took me a while before I really started leveraging the super reflex mode; but this mechanic is pretty essential to completing the game so make sure you make the most of it as soon as it's introduced! It also amps up the cool factor of the kills quite a bit so it's definitely got that going for it.The soundtrack is fitting and the remixes you get with Out For Blood mode freshen it up but there were points where I was considering muting them and using my own tunes, this time will come eventually I'm sure.You could probably argue that the price is a bit steep and after completing the main story and making a dent in the unlockable hard mode (Out For Blood) there is maybe 1 or 2 too few maps to style on. Although I definitely feel I've got my monies worth out of a very unique and entertaining game.All in all this is well worth your time. If it looks like your cup of tea it most likely will be. Easy to fire up for a cheeky session here and there or to dig your teeth into for a while.STEAM DECK NOTES: I found putting the graphics to low actually made it look better and reduced the jaggies/aliasing that was present to start with, it also struggled with the last couple maps on high/60fps but not on low/60 at all. Text is easy to enlarge in the menu, this game should 100% be verified on deck and it seems silly to mark it down for the in game text when there are settings to increase the font size (and quite a few verified games with unreadable in-game text.) Low watt usage at 60fps.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves games that are easy to pickup, hard to master and allow you to enter a flow like state, such as: Tony Hawk Pro Skater, Doom, Super Hot, Hotline Miami, this game scratches that same itch.You control your chararcter similar to Tony Hawk (though the skating aspect isn't the focus, it's much more forgiving) the twist being you have roller blades and a small arsenal of guns and there is a whole arena of people trying to kill you! The goal being to kill them as effectively as possible and complete goals. Every time you do grab tricks, grinds or perfect dodge enemy attacks, you are awarded ammo and every enemy killed will drop health and add to your combo meter, all leading to your score at the end. These three things allow for a simple but addicting and fast paced gameplay loop that I can get lost in for hours, taking my time to master the nuances of the combat, finding out what guns work best on what enemies, most effective grab combos to get ammo and adapting when things go wrong. It's an action packed game that demands your focus and attention. Side tangent - it also have a focus (slomo) mechanic like Max Payne, it passively regenerates and can be used at any time and if you get a perfect dodge and then enter slomo, you will do extra damage to enemies for a brief duration and oh man, pulling these maneuvers off feels great! All of this tied together with a stunning cell shaded visual style and dystopian theme. Unfortunately it feels derivative of other dystopian narratives like squid game/Hunger Games (people in red jumpsuits competing in dangerous games for wealth with a militaristic force, lots of death and a creepy announcer voice) but It has potential to be great on it's own... unfortunately we don't see that in this game, the story is mostly told through environmental story telling in a locker room/train and is very bare bones. I see potential in the narrative I just think it needs either more prescience or to be cut entirely. The content is also another downside, completionist will have enough to do, such as goals (get collectibles, do tricks, kill enemies in a certain way, get a 25x combo)  as well as an extra hard remix of the main levels. Unfortunately casual players  will only get a 3-5 hours out of main game depending on skill level. No multiplayer, no character customisation, limited enemy types, only 4 guns, roughly 5 different maps (repeated often and kinda bland) and 1 recycled boss fight with a generic mech design. For this reason I do recommend you buy this on sale, the price is steep for the content, despite high quality gameplay. Overall, this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun game. It may not have in depth leveling system, a dynamic story or loads of content but what it does have is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gold gameplay loop, unique concept and neat visual style and is a game that I can pickup at any point and enjoy without having to be overly invested in it.The fact this was made by roughly 40 people blows my mind and only makes me more eager for their future projects, this game deserves a full fledged triple A sequel, with dynamics maps, new enemy types, an expanded arsenel, multiplayer, character custimatisation and an immersive story with cutscenes!!

The first couple hours; you're just learning the ropes. trying to navigate the combos and movement system. once you get the hang of it.... BRO it's so awesome. Grinding on a rails to capping some guys, then wall riding into a 360 backbreaker for more ammo. This feels like an PS2 game in a good way. It reminds of Tony Hawk pro skater 4 and SS Tricky mixed with max payne. I bought this on a whim and I'm so glad I did. _childDocuments_.review: there's honestly a lot to love about Rollerdrome. there are a few asterisks to it, but so far, I am ABSOLUTELY enjoying this FAR, FAR more than last year's OlliOlli World, Roll7's preceding game since their acquisition by Take Two's 2K's Private Division.+ the visuals, inspired by the likes of comics artist Moebius (who basically godfathered the cyberpunk aesthetic, genuinely one of the greatest artists of all time, and someone who makes perfect sense to be inspired by), are stellar. this is sure to be one of the best-looking games of 2022, regardless of price point.+ I kinda dig the music, but it's not something I'd listen to much outside of the game. its sound effects fare far better, selling the fury of gunfire and the shredding of your skates.+ most obvious as one of its strengths is its impossibly stylish melding of gunplay and rollerblading. you'll pop a frontflip, then pop some dork's brains out with your akimbo pistols, dodge a sniper shot at the last possible second, and retaliate with a grenade which sends the sniper into orbit. it's hard NOT to feel like a god/ess as you're tearing through fools before grinding on a rail, backflipping over some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with a shield, and pumping a perfectly timed shotgun blast through his dome.+ these power fantasy highs contrast starkly with the game's (by default) sharp deaths. if you aren't judicious with your shots, you can very quickly be overwhelmed and put down.- this lethal ballet can, depending on the level, be cut short in unsatisfying fashion due to poor level geometry. I kept dying on one of the first levels due to jumping into one of the windows, but landing slightly /outside/ of it. instead of jumping over this incline, my goofy ass avatar would instead decide to walljump off to their doom. you CAN jump over that, but the range between what will immediately kill you and what won't is too damn thin.- these moments of frustration (as well as some of the more difficult moments of the difficulty curve, which takes sharp peaks and valleys as you grow accustomed to the different enemy types) are part of why I dislike how the game locks you out of later levels until you go down each of the preceding levels' checklists and perform an arbitrary number of the tasks. I don't feel like trying to do this overly precise kind of grind when I'm focused on not dying cuz I landed outside a window.in spite of the more obnoxious areas, Rollerdrome remains one of the more exhilarating releases this year. the way it naturally merges these two things that on paper do not sound like they should work together (Max Payne + Demolition Man + Tony Hawk's Pro Skater) is undeniably impressive, refreshing, and kickass. probably gonna be one of the top of the pile action games this year.

_childDocuments_.review: What a mess. Rollerdrome had me really excited when it was released. The soundtrack is pleasant. I love the art style and the concept is really original and refreshing, but after playing through the extremely easy tutorial missions, the enjoyment plummets dramatically. This game has one of the steepest difficulty curves I've ever seen and that's simply because it's way too short. $30 for a campaign you can beat in 3-4 hours is insane. There's only one boss that's reused at the end. Levels are reused repeatedly. Not even the Finals has a unique map. The game presents Kara Hassan like she's a character, but she has no personality in gameplay. She never speaks. What a letdown. Her face is all over the marketing and she only exhibits any personality during those four locker room sections when the game shows a caption of a few of her thoughts. That's not enough and that's not a story. Telling your whole story through small descriptions isn't compelling when they're so few and far between. There's so little character in the game. You don't even get to meet and possibly fight the other competitors. They might as well not even exist. There are basically no announcers providing commentary during this so called live tournament watched by millions of people. Something similar to Ratchet Deadlocked or Jak X for example.The best way to look at Rollerdrome is not a sports game like Tony Hawk Pro Skater with guns. It's an arena shooter with skating. Performing tricks is largely irrelevant outside of reloading. It's there for those who want to complete all the challenges and get a high score. The controls are extremely cumbersome because aiming sucks. I thought lock on aiming had largely died out by now for the better. The lock on here is over aggressive snapping to enemies/projectiles not even centered to the reticle just because they're closer to me. It's very annoying and like I said, this game is hard. Most people haven't even finished the main campaign. It's something like a 10% completion rate for the trophy alone, so some of these positive reviews are suspect to me. I beat it just because I'm competitive for no good reason, but I was not having fun.Combat is a mess of aimbot enemies forcing you to spam dodge just to get away from the brutal attacks. Dodging isn't even always reliable since you risk dodging into attacks anyway. Mines, rockets, lasers, sniper rifle attacks all at the same time. There's a high skill ceiling with this one which isn't inherently a bad thing, but the lack of steady difficulty curve due to the short length just means you're expected to master the mechanics after about an hour of playing. I just don't think putting a bunch of markers everywhere is good communication about upcoming attacks. I'd rather have more options besides just dodging to avoid damage.There's a lot of depth to the gameplay. There are a lot of tricks you can use. Four unique weapons to swap between on the fly each with their own strengths and weaknesses with a great variety of enemy types. It feels like it's going for Doom Eternal on wheels. There's just not enough content built around the core foundation. I didn't see any unlockables even after completing every challenge on several levels. No costumes, alternate characters, weapon skins, etc. There's another game mode you unlock with the same enemy types and maps again, but that's not enough. It's a shame what happened to Roll7 and I would've loved to see them expand this game into a bigger better series, but here we are. On sale (50% off), with the right expectations going in would be a tepid recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of shooters and growing up with games like THPS 1-4 I thought "why not."Short and sweet, the game is fun for the first few maps. Once it's patched and updated a bit it'll be a lot of fun. Right now the controls are just too wonky. Besides immediately recommending to everyone to remap your "air out" control to something other than "forward" on the Left stick (I have no idea why they thought this as a default was a good thing as everyone instinctively presses forward to go forward, thus ruining your jumps), it has a few gripes. I can give it a recommendation as it is a fun game, just not for me as it currently is. ::GOOD::LOVE the art designLove the VibeThe Soundtrack is absolutely fantasticThe overall aesthetic is great.It's Guns and Roller Skates and Backflips. ::Gripes::1 : Camera controls are bad. I fought the camera over and over when doing a sick backflip grab spin trick above an enemy and went into bullet time, but the camera will not allow you to look around in a full 360* so you have to weirdly swivel your camera and and fight to get a track on your target. This is fine for standing shooters where you never really perform a 360* front/back flip and hardly ever aiming at your feet unless jumping - but this game is all about aerial aiming and flips. The camera should allow you to spin it 360* full globe. Not hard stop at your feet or above your head.2 : Dodging seems to nuke your combo points, at least in my experience. I feel like it's >not< supposed to, but streaming this game I encountered performing perfect dodges mid-combo and seeing my entire combo just fall off and I'd get the 50 or how many ever points it is for a dodge, and that was it. If this is, in fact, by design.....why would performing a "perfect dodge" punish you? If it's NOT by design, this was just a bug I encountered and really soured my experience extremely fast. 3 : Snipers in the first set of levels are fun >at first< but get really old, really quick. Absolutely annoying to be in the middle of a super sick combo flippy grind fest and then need to dodge 4 times in a row, causing you to drop your combo chain, because suddenly 5 snipers spawn back to back and fire at you in what feels like every 3 seconds. 4 : Performing Flips needs some help. Unlike any other skater game, in this game you hold a button and press your Left Stick back or forwards. This prompts the character to perform a single, painfully slow, flip, and then stop. In order to perform another flip, you have to once again perform the button combination to initiate another flip. This feels very tedious and unnatural. You should be able to perform a flip with it's speed based on how far you have the thumb stick pressed in either direction, and for as long as you're holding that direction. You should >not< need to hit bumper + Up = Flip = Wait + Up = Flip 2. This is painful.5 : Not really an issue, but I wish the music was reactive to your performance. I feel like this, alone, would make the game absolutely stellar in a sound design outlook. Like Doom when you get into combat, or DMC5 where the better you perform the better the soundtrack gets.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking for fast, fluid, hectic retro vibe arcade skating combat?  Then I am sorry this isn't quite good enough.  It's not a terrible game, but I wish it was so much better, and the positive reviews are probably painting an incorrect picture of the experience.  For starters it feels super slow and often clunky.  Super slow.Certainly the default game pad setup for buttons is far from the best, but regardless, given the way controls work they take away any feeling of continuous momentum, skill, and make it hard to get into any zen state of flow.  It often feels like the character is ignoring your input as you get locked into an animation state machine that simply does not feel responsive - a trap Western developers often fall into.  I want to play the game not your animations - Japanese developers understand this much better.  The decision to not implement bailing out, stumbling and crashing doesn't help the overall problem either despite making it more casual friendly.The character you play as is a piece of uninteresting dead wood.  Her animations are lame, and she simply doesn't react at times in a way that feels consistent with what is going on.  The sound design totally sucks any feeling of frantic fun out too.  The aesthetics are of course great, however they are wasted on a world that through a combination of design choices is super dull.  Acrobatic tricks are somehow made dull and tedious too.It's frustrating as what they were going for here was truly interesting, and it is not all bad despite what I have said.  But they didn't stick the landing well enough in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall:Rollerdrome is an addictive arcade-style game that mix Tony Hawk's Pro Skater gameplay with Ultrakill's shooter mechanics. Bassically, you're doing double time in compact arenas, trying to bust a move while simultaneously shooting anyone in your vicinity as effectively as possible to keep your combo going. The developers' greatest accomplishment is that it doesn’t feel hard to juggle such a complex concept. You'll quickly get into the swing of things if you've played Tony Hawk games or previous roll7 game olliolli, and if not, you'll have plenty of time to learn the basics, get basic understanding of the gameplay loop and decide whether or not you're into that kind of game without going over 2 hours. So I would certainly recommend anyone to try it.Gameplay loop: You skate around arenas, shoot everything, dodge everything that is shot at you, you get the combo going, that’s it.Positives:- Fast, addictive, and snappy gameplay.- Tailored challenge: Every level is designed with highest skill ceiling in mind. You can start at your own pace and get better, if you choose so.- Well balanced array of weapons that fulfill all possible scenarios.- Unique concept, unique setting, unique artstyle.Middle Ground:- The story is engaging to observe, exactly like some flick from the 80-90s, but the narrative devices developers used made it quite shallow, throughout the game you'll feel alienated from the story or the stakes since you don't see any plot point directly, only premise and an aftermath of any event that happened without your direct involvement, just observing the environments. But the silver lining here is that you can ignore all of it and go from level to level, and I guess that's fair for gameplay centric title.- Music is appropriate to the style of despotic, retrofuturistic, Britain-influenced world of the future, but it certainly limited the variety of genres and locked it in one place, music will help you get the feel for this world, but I'd recommend putting your own playlist in the background.Nitpicks:- Movement can feel a bit stiff when turning.- Stage variety is clearly lacking with just 4 distinguishable areas- Some trick challenges are hard to pull off, you did everything right and it just didn't count and it doesn't feel like players fault.Needless Nerd Contention (The review is over):The thing that gets to me the most is the fact that roll7 never outgrew their early arcade gameplay, like it's challenging in a good way, but it gets to an extreme degree, and of course it was fine for their early games, because they weren't aiming high or for all-round polish, so beating them was an achievement in itself, but rollerdrome didn't outgrew these games, the challenge is immense and demanding, and what you get for trying to achieve perfect score on every level, one combo it, collect all stuff, kill enemies in a certain way, beat level in time, well, you get a hard mode, with even harder challenges, and what happens when you beat it, true ending? No, you just beat the game a second time. So you'll get head on with such array of questions: "Why am I playing this game for a second time if I won't get anything but stupidly hard challenge out of it?""Why would I even go as far playing those levels?""Why did I even completed these tasks in the first place?" You get nothing in return, no skins, cosmetics, power ups, cool things, you just play the game like you would play donkey kong or pacman in arcade, there's nothing but the gameplay, and it just makes the whole idea flawed and shows how developers remained oblivious or ignorant in that regard.

_childDocuments_.review: First, a "spoiler free" review: i rly did enjoy the artstyle, the idea of the game and the story is servicable too, with some neat details if u pay close attention. However, i do think the game couldve improved upon a few minor things. Minor spoilers ahead. For one, i didnt rly enjoy the variety of weapons all that much, i feel like a sort of sniper rifle wouldve done a lot better then the railgun. In addition, some enemy types were just rly annoying. Constantly getting beamed while running around due to their teleportation was kinda annoying. Next up, i wouldve enjoyed some sort of combo list, which displays all the possible grabs etc., making it a bit easier for the player to discover new tricks. Lastly, i feel like the game wouldve benefitted a lot from a few more bossfights. The one that u do get to fight was very fun and it switched up the whole experience a bit, which was nice.Overall, i did still enjoy my overall playtime with Rollerdrome, and my gripes with it might as well just be a skill issue, so dont hesitate to give it a shot, especially if its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: "THPS with guns", from the team behind OlliOlli? Sign me up!This game was a fair bit harder than I expected it to be. I got the game around April 2023 and played the tutorial and a few levels, quickly realizing that progressing would actually require some skill. That was not at all discouraging, because I instantly enjoyed the mechanics, controls and style. It felt good not being an invincible god right away, and tackling one challenge after another was a good way of getting better. Shortly after I got distracted until the end of the year, and it took me a bit to get back into the groove before actually going through with it and finishing the main campaign. As I had anticipated, the way that unlocking further levels is tied to a certain number of the various challenges in each level/stage, you actually have to work for it. I finished the campaign without too much struggles, but didn't focus on completing more than just the challenges required to progress. They got increasingly hard, so I figured I would just clean those up later. The (extremely thin) story that is spun around the levels/tournament is a nice touch – small enough that it can be ignored, but adding to the overall atmosphere.After the main campaign, the "Out For Blood" campaign is unlocked – same levels, different challenges. Holy cow, did I say the game required some skills this? In the normal campaign, the further you progress the less likely you are to managing more than a couple of challenges per run. In the "Out For Blood" campaign, even surviving the first level wasn't easy. Wow. I'll admit, the jump in difficulty made me bounce off initially. It felt like a different game entirely. About half a year later I came back to the game. Again I needed to first get back into the groove, but I still retained a lot of muscle memory and had an easier time doing so. Gradually, I made progress through "Out For Blood", and the more punishing the game became the better I got at truly getting into the flow. Some of the leftover challenges from the normal campaign that seemed like a stretch a few months ago now were a breeze, and tremendously satisfying to complete.Beating every challenge in "Out For Blood" was seriously among the hardest gaming things I did in recent memory (significantly harder than Elden Ring, just for example). Even though I ultimately managed them all, I think it's the good that there's assist/accessibility options that allow tuning the difficulty a bit – some of these were just absolutely brutal. But the good kind, where it never felt like the game's fault when I failed.All that is paired with a pretty decent soundtrack and made for an overall experience that I can highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game was recommended to me by a friend of mine, and since I was a fond fan of Tony Hawk's games, I was instantly hooked. The OST's excellency shows by the BAFTA award, and the sound effects in general really sound good. Now, for the story; there isn't much that's told to you directly, you're just Kara Hassan and you ride the Rollerdrome championship, but in-between the rounds of the championship you can discover so much about the world and the current situation outside the arena. All in all, a definite 10/10, charmed me the second I started playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the kind of game that I needed as a fan of the original Rollerball and Motorball from Battle Angel Alita manga. It feels amazing to play, while being really approachable for deadbeats with poor motor skills because of how generous it is with telegraphing attacks and slowing down time while aiming. A bit too generous because of a certain weapon that unlocks later on in the game. Even if you suck in the beginning, the progression system makes sure that sooner or later you'll be clearing the levels in one continuous combo like a goddess of destruction.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game with gorgeous presentation and fantastic gameplay, absolutely dripping with style in every corner, the matches are just the right amount of challenging to remain interesting and the list of challenges makes it easily replayable just to try and improve, exactly the kind of game we should all be celebrating...
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: To people unfamiliar to Rollerdrome:This game is like Doom meets Tony Hawk. Your primary objective is to clear arenas of enemies without dying. The reason it's reminiscent of Doom is that there are a variety of enemies and a variety of weapons. As the game goes on, you learn the fastest/safest ways to deal with different enemies. The reason it's reminiscent of Tony hawk is that you're always moving (on rollerskates, obviously), and you can only reload your weapons by doing tricks such as rail grinds, wall grinds, air holds, and flips. It's a really fun and unique combination that is far from a gimmick, and there's even a decent story and some (semi-) optional challenges to keep things moving forward. Definitely give it a try, this is an incredibly polished and satisfying game.My only criticism is that NG+ does away with the more interesting kinds of optional challenges in favor of just one tight score + time goal in every level. Normally I would be okay with this, but I do not think this game lends itself to the goal of pushing for really high scores-- the very limited trick options make this feel less like a fun skill expression and more like a repetitive slog. I typically LOVE the road to getting good at a game's mechanics, especially when they're as fine-tuned as they are in Rollerdrome. I wish the score challenges were either greatly reduced or deleted, and time trials were made a bit tighter. Because as small as this problem might sound on paper, it completely killed my momentum and desire to continue improving. What would've otherwise been a challenging but rewarding 30 hours instead ended in me resorting to toggling some difficulty modifiers in order to just get those over with (I HATE doing this-- but good on the devs for adding accessibility features). That being said, getting good enough to go from barely surviving to cutting through enemies as quickly as possible felt amazing. Rollerdrome is one of those titles that's really good at inducing a flow state and making you forget to blink. The game is also gorgeous and exciting to look at, with great level design too. If you don't intend to go for full completion, and/or you're less nitpicky than I am, you'll like this game more than I did-- and I liked it a lot.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique game that I think everyone should try! It's quite challenging, but they allow you to adjust plenty of settings to make it easier to shoot everything without worrying about getting points. I would only suggest adding a few more accessibility options that help make objectives stand out more or controls easier to read during the tutorials. Other than that,  it's going to become a perfect choice for anyone who needs something different. It's an intense shooter with a very simplistic art style; how could you not give it a shot?
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: "Kara Hassan, Match Victory."A very fun little indie game with tight movement, strong shooting mechanics and a perfect cellshaded artstyle. The blend of a trick-based skating game with a frenetic shooter is ingenious, honestly.I was absolutely terrible at this game but I had a great time with it.Thus, I highly recommend it, basically to anyone who likes fast-paced arena shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play Tony Hawk and score some sweet tricks while shooting enemies you will probably like this game. Will you LOVE this game? That depends. It's hard, and the focus isn't on doing tricks. Sure, you need to do tricks to get more ammo and increase score, but it's more important to track where enemies are, how long you have on your combo timer (that only stays up if you kill things in time) and the best path to maintain your combo. If you are the type of player who plays Sonic levels over and over because getting an S rank and all the red stars feels amazing then you will like this game. But it can be HARD if you want to complete everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique and cool game. Has a gameplay loop that is incomparable to any other game. That being said this game is very challenging, and im sad to say without putting in an insane amount of practice I will never be good (or even decent) at it. There is so much going on from the tech to enemy variety that it feels like you need four hands to play this game well. The game is a legitimate bullet hell at the end. Not a bad thing at all, just very challenging if you are going for completion
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun, creative. and stylish game with simple mechanics that flawlessly connect together. The basic flow is as follows:Skate around and shoot enemies -> Do tricks to reload your weapon -> Get kills to regenerate healthThe weapons that get added throughout the campaign don't change that loop much, but open up interesting possibilities to use the multiple tools together in novel ways. Each of the four weapons play unique enough to warrant their additional slot, allowing for versatile and dynamic approaches to the stages and their various enemy types. The starting dual pistols may give you the impression combat is rather up-close, but later weapons greatly increase your kill range extensively (at the expense of guaranteed accuracy).The campaign is admittedly short- expect around four to six hours- but the sandbox is addictingly replayable (I have an additional 20+ hours logged on console). While I feel the challenges present are serviceable, I do wish there were more "tactical" challenges (one I really loved was "Complete this stage without using the Dual Pistols"- more like these!). I was pleasantly surprised that a fair amount of the middle stages don't hold back with difficulty, as to challenge the player to accommodate to their new weapons. The high point rankings are also a welcoming challenge- do not expect to S rank many, if any, of the stages on your first go around.Couldn't recommend this enough to anyone looking for a short-but-sweet, quality action experience that offers something truly different in the Arena and Skating genres its melds together.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I've never sucked this much at a game before and I love it! As someone who was never into Tony Hawk-like games I was hesitant to pick this title up but I am so glad I did. Its got a learning curve, especially if you never play sports games, but the mechanics aren't too complicated and are very fun to get to grips with. The gameplay feels great and I love the structure of returning to levels to complete different challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A challenging third person shooter that puts both your reflexes and sanity to the test. Very short if you only play it one time though, and is intended to have various stages played multiple times in different ways.*Played with controller, laptop, and on a speaker*-Difficulty: This game is definitively a souls-like game with how hard it can be. You use weapons that need bullets, you earn these bullets by doing tricks, You have to do these tricks while avoiding various bullets and enemies while also maintaining a good time. If you plan on just playing for the story alone, you might be okay. But if you enjoy difficult third-person shooter, area type game with dozens of varying challenges, this is your game.P.S: there are accessibility options that can aid people who need the help.-Graphics: The graphics are good and don't make any enemy too hard to see. Almost all are yellow, or gigantic and impossible to miss. Similar to a Borderlands style with it's cell shading.-Music & Audio: High BPM and good tempo to keep you pumped during the very intense missions. Not annoying or repetitive, and I would say a great job was done with maintain the theme the produces wanted to achieve. -Story: Unless you dig for it, you won't find it. The story is not in your face and you must listen to various dialogue pieces you find by walking around during the story moments. Also by reading the various notes and letters found around, and finally making educated assessments based off of the information you have. I think it's good, but if you need a bit more assistance when it comes to story, just enjoy the game.-Price: Decently priced, given what you have. If this is your cup of tea, I think that justifies the price tag, if not then just wait for a sale.-Length: Very Short. Took me about ~4hrs to complete the base game, and that's with me going back to trying to get most of the challenges done before the end. There is a secondary, harder mode that's unlocked but you don't have to play it if you don't want to.-Replay Ability: 10/10. I'm personally not sure if it's even possible to get ten out of ten challenges done when you play a stage the first time, forcing the player to keep trying till they get it. The game is also very nice by saving the challenge you beat if you end up dying. I had fun trying to get all the challenges done in the base game, but the "Out For Blood" mode is only there for true masochists. -Overview: This is a game made with multi-tasking, reflexes, and situational awareness in mind that will easily push you to the test every time you open it. Although I did get frustrated with this game frequently, I would always find myself playing it yet again. I can only recommend this game while it's on sale in good faith, but I understand the developers wanting to get their money's worth for the hard work put into this game.No score review this time. I simply recommend while it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Super neat! It didn't really click with me at first, and I thought I might drop it in the first few levels, but at some point everything started flowing together and I really got into the rhythm of it. I ended up liking the game enough to 100% all of its achievements. Once you get used to it there are some fun and unique ideas here.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome is a fabulous little game with a well defined scope, tightly designed gameplay, a banging soundtrack and an aura of coolness permeating every frame. Even on paper, the concept for this game is a slam dunk. Slow-motion trickshots on roller skates? Sign me up. Somehow, Roll7 have managed to infuse what is already an insanely cool idea with a soul that makes you feel cool just by knowing that you're playing it. It's fast-paced and frantic but at the same time so readable thanks to its art. Every moment is a heart-thumping high as you do 360 backflips while taking down multiple enemies mid-air. The moody synthwave soundtrack is a perfect match for the retro-dystopian future, which is weirdly well fleshed out considering how there is basically zero exposition in this game. There are little newspaper clippings and emails you can read through and get a broad grasp on the themes of the game, and those do more than enough before every level to get you pumped for the action ahead.The scope is limited, but in a way that makes perfect sense for a game like this. There are about a dozen levels in total and you'll have to complete a fair few of the challenges in a lot of them to unlock the later levels as you progress. If Roll7 ever revisit this idea, I'd maybe like for there to be more levels and less mandatory challenge requirements but I do appreciate what's been offered here as it forced me to get better at the game. The gameplay itself is actually quite forgiving on the dexterity front. A lot of my time was spent planning on the fly for how to take down enemies and how to look dope while doing it. The shooting is simple, with a solid lock-on system and the tricks are easy to pull off with no real failure state as such for poor timing. Your only punishment is that you won't look cool, and I think that's fair when combining so much at once. All of this isn't to say that there isn't any skill required, though. To complete the aforementioned challenges, you need to have a good grasp on the level layouts, which get more and more interesting as the game progresses, and trying to string together a killer combo really does require some quick thinking. It's the classic easy-to-learn, hard-to-master type scenario.I really think they're onto something with this game. I've recently played all the OlliOlli games, and with this in tow, Roll7 are now a studio for me to look out for. This is a phenomenal game and I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and addicting shooterThis game is really fun and something completely different, a well placed break to those every day triple A shooters like CoD and its likes, that copy each other. The art style is amazing and a very bold choice, as it may seem "primitive" to the untrained eye. I love the comic book/shadeless artstyle that makes this game truly pop out. It also uses very clever game mechanics to go about routine tasks like getting ammo or eliminating enemies. Doing tricks is engaging and you'll find yourself spending quite little time on flat ground.  If I have to come up with cons, the only one probably would be that progressing in this game can be a tedious task. To progress in the game and unlock new levels and eventually the second campaign, be ready for a healthy amount of good 'ol grinding, as you're going to have to replay some of the levels to get all the tasks done and thus progress. If you're fine with a little grind and an astonishing indie title with a memorable soundtrack and a compelling story, Rollerdrome is a solid pick.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: No  non-sense fun. If you were a fan of Tony Hawk's pro skater I would highly recommend that you try Rollerdrome. It combines the trick-mixing and high-speed grinding  of skate games with Max Payne-style slo-mo stunts and combat. There may be few levels, but the challenges and difficulty promote replaying with adrenaline focused action.A great deal at any price.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

You have first to understand how to move, how to use your weapons and how to keep your combo multiplier. It's only when you understand everything that you it will become a second nature and you can focus on doing complicated/long tricks to do very high score.I think the learning curve of this game is super long but the challenges will teach you how to do each step very nicely.Last thing, if you are only interested in doing tricks (like Tony Hawk), you can just put some assist mode that will make you invincible and have your fun :).
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: (RIP Roll7. Such a shame Take Two killed them off. This game is incredible and they did not deserve to be shutdown) So much fun! Very refreshing take on gameplay.
