_childDocuments_.review: Audience☐ Beginner☐ Casual Gamer☑ Normal Gamer☑ ExpertGraphics☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☑ Beautiful☐ FantasticMusic☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☐ Beautiful☑ FantasticDifficulty☐ Easy☐ Average☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Hard☐ UnfairBugs☐ Bugs destroy the game☐ Lots of bugs☐ Few Bugs☐ You can use them for speedrun☑ Nothing encounteredStory☐ There is none☐ Bad☑ Alright☐ Good☐ FantasticGameplay☐ Frustrating☐ Sleepy☐ Boring☑ Fun☑ ChallengingGame time / Length☐ Really short (0 - 3 hours)☑ Short (4 - 8 hours) [if you focus on the main story]☑ Few hours (10 - 30 hours) [if you complete everything]☐ Long (40-60 hours) ☐ Very Long (61-100 hours)☐ Extremely Long (101+ hours)Price / Quality☑ Full price☐ Wait for Sale☐ Don't buy☐ Refund it if you canRollerdrome is a truly excellent game. Don't let any naysayers discourage you. If you want to grind for challenges, you'll really have to push yourself (I just finished the out-for-blood difficulty as of writing this review, and it can be truly brutal at times), but regardless, this game is just pure arcade-style fun. When you perfectly time the dodge with an enemy's attack and get the bonus damage, it literally feels like bullet time from the Matrix. Even just experimenting with the gameplay sandbox by replaying levels is awesome. As far as I can tell, the skill ceiling is pretty much endless since you can continue to improve your combo awareness and mix up trick usage in a level playthrough, and optimize damage with weapon swaps.Even the story and world-building, while not amazing, is still intriguing enough to hold the campaign together and hold your interest between levels. Couple that with a beautiful artstyle that just pops off the screen, and you're easily looking at one of the top 3 best games I've played this year. Do yourself a favor and just try it, full price or otherwise.I've seen others complain about the controls in other reviews. I have no idea what they're talking about: this is an incredibly responsive and smooth gameplay experience. Sometimes doing special command input grabs/grinds can be harder with an analog stick, but that's probably the only control scheme-related problem I've encountered. I've also only seen one or two gameplay glitches in my entire playthrough; it's a well-constructed video game in almost every way. The control scheme is also somewhat difficult to master if you want to fully take advantage of your character's abilities, but the basics are still very approachable for casuals. While the game is very punishing when you reach the harder difficulties, in my opinion it's never unfair.I've also seen some people complain about how campy the game feels, and how you have to play defensively. Absolutely not. Certain weapons in the game actually reward you for using super reflex time effectively, and if you time your encounter with a close-quarters enemy, you can actually charge up the Z-11 to snipe full-health enemies all the way across the map. Similarly, you can time a sniper shot super reflex to make short work of enemies closer to you. There are so many ways to customize combat given a particular situation; you're never forced to play super defensively or super offensively. You can get punished for lingering in one position for too long, but that's pretty much it; it's very free-form and fun to experiment with overall.There are only two real complaints I have about this game: first, the . Second, while the replayability is there from a combat and combo perspective, I do wish there were more maps to play around in.Roll7, if you're reading this, PLEASE add DLC maps, or a level editor. I will happily pay full price for both of them.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to share my thoughts as an aggressive rollerskater in real life.  From the first level, this game is a work of art both in design and mechanics.  The skill, style, and range of options in the controls is immense, and everything feels fast and responsive.  However, the game does leave me wanting an experience closer connected to modern park skating.  The tricktionary borrows skateboard-specific terms like nose-tail instead of toe-heel (understandable from the developer's past titles), and while modern skaters accomplish grinds by customizing wide trucks and slide blocks beneath their plates, Kara accomplishes these on narrow trucks and plates (not impossible, just much more difficult).  It's a minor gripe, as it feels like a missed connection to an under-documented yet fast-growing sport with little rep in gaming, but doesn't really hinder the gameplay or setting itself.  Ultimately, Rollerdrome is a dream come to life and I hope it inspires more extreme quads in games.(also I'm landshark_errant on instagram if anyone wants to see my amateur reels, look for me in 2030 haha)

I will still recommend it though but not at the current price, definitely get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Pure fun. It's not like Tony Hawk's where you're trying to stick the landings, it's all about making it flow from one target to the next while maintaining a combo. This makes it endlessly replayable as you constantly devise new ways to tie it in smoother and more efficientSuch a brilliant idea and the art/music is an absolute vibe too
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It is not every day that you find a game that happens to challenge you in ways you never thought to expect, so when finding this game's premise absolutely "Dope as ♥♥♥♥", I just had to play it. However, this game has a difficult learning curve that one may find difficult to follow. I myself am only halfway through the game itself and it offers all sorts of challenges (personally, the timed challenges always seem to get me) from the insane tricks and point scores you can get to the practice of ammo efficiency when killing goons (and how to refill ammo). I'd say that this community, however small it can be, actually can be learned from in terms of methods and efficiencies that will take you from an A-rank player to an S-ranker, if you take the time and practice your hands with them. Overall, this game can break preconceptions of how a game can challenge and push you towards becoming an excellent gamer. All of this should be expected from a fully-fledged 60$ game, but this in itself is a testament to the glory of new blood in the gaming developer industries. I hope to see more of this franchise in the coming future!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Just hundred percented the game and I enjoyed every moment of it. Beautiful art style mixed with smooth gameplay. I really love the steady increase in difficulty as you get further in the campaign, and the challenges make for nice replayability. If you stick with it and continue to clear each task, you can really feel your own improvement as later levels become easier despite increased enemy count and variety.What little story there is proves interesting but I definitely wouldn't pick this up solely for the narrative as it's on the lighter side. It does what is necessary to service the gameplay but other than that, it's mainly set dressing, and it doesn't need to be anything more.If you ever liked the Tony Hawk games, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, or any Bullet Hells, you will eat this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: There is going to be a few good similarities that this game will have with certain other games, outside of that however the game overall is excellent if you enjoy doing the cool and crazy thing. If you are worried about the gun part, the game makes it easy to use and have a slowdown mode that allows you to breathe while taking the shot, in fact it is encouraged to use it as you are rewarded in game by utilizing it. The challenges for each stage are easy to understand and you don't have to worry about 100% them all in one go, once you complete one, it's off the list even when you lose which is a welcoming sign if you are having trouble with the stage.If you understand the concept of "flow" you will enjoy what the game has to offer as the difficulty ramps up in later stages, I'm only at the halfway mark in game and it's throwing a lot at me but they are not cheap shots at all.Highly recommend this game if you are familiar with character action games.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game is NOT a shooter with quirky movement; it is a better Tony Hawk game than any other modern iteration. Buy this if you're interested in a classic arcade-style game with great movement and a combo system.It's missing that little bit of extra polish and features for me to consider it GOTY material, but it's very close. I loved this game and I'm hoping for some DLC or a Rollerdrome 2. Don't let it meet the same fate the current Tony Hawk Pro Skater series has met.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I am yet to finish this game, so consider these early thoughts but i think its so good that i wanted to say something.Those describing this as THPS x Max Payne x Superhot are right on the money - if that particular combo attracts you just buy it now you will love it.For everyone else Rollerdrome is a single player, arena based, shooter/skating game. Those familiar with the tony hawks series or any of its copy cats will feel right at home with the controls and the skating itself feels good with a y large number of tricks you can perform. The overall gamer structure also mimics the orginal tony hawks games with each stage having a list of objectives designed to be completed after multiple runs. These can vary from the general (high scores, collect all the tokens) or the specific (do x trick here).What sets Rolledrome apart is the shooter elements and how they are weaved into the skating mechanics - the shooting itself is good enough, with most weapons having lock on mechanics that make shooting feel cool but actually manageable whilst skating and tricking. The real genius is that you need to do tricks in order to reload - but you only earn points and combo through kills. It means each side of this hybrid is entwined with the other and leads to a very addictive loop. Add into that a generous slow mo ability (further enhance by a dodging system) you can soon go from dying on a level to completing it in one un-ending combo.This is all wrapped in a beautiful Mobius-inspired cell shaded aesthetic and just enough of a dystopian gameshow narrative that doesnt overstay its welcome.A wonderful, wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: KARA HASSAN: ELIMINATEDSuch a good game. Tony Hawk Pro Skater but you build combos by killing enemies in slow-mo stylish combat. Interesting world, killer aesthetic, great combat and roller skating action, gameplay is easy to learn with so much replayability after you finish the campaign. Sure, the physics break now and then, but not enough to ruin the overall experience. Beat it in a weekend, then keep coming back to perfect your high scores.PS: The soundtrack is dope. Whoever composed the music for this game, give them lots of money please.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: So apparently I REALLY like sports games... under the strict condition that the player character be given a firearm to use during the competition. So because of this knowledge I elect that the next football series made by EA in order to replace Madden should include an underground market where I can buy my team AR 15's, so they can roll out onto the field with as to dominate anything and anyone standing between them and those over hyped superbowl rings... this game is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Rollerdrome has basic 3rd person shooting mechanics made much more fun by making you have to skate around, dodge enemies, and do tricks to refill your extremely small ammo reserves back up. Unlike most similar looking games, it's actually impossible to bail when doing tricks. This may sound like a knock against the game but it is balanced heavily towards requiring you juggle attacking and dodging to stay alive so just landing some basic tricks between the madness evens out the pace. It's a fun formula that works really well.My only knocks against the game are that the tone of the barebones story felt a bit off and the THPS 1-3 style challenges on each stage feel a bit like an afterthought since they only come into play when unlocking the very last level and for an achievement.I beat the main game in 3 hours and that felt like just the right amount of time for what it had to offer. For those looking for more, you can still 100% all challenges and play the Out For Blood mode after you beat the main game which in my opinion is better than the main campaign. Out For Blood trims down the challenges per level in exchange for doubling down on the number of enemies trying to kill you at any given time. I was able to beat that mode in about 2 hours before going back to 100% the challenges. I'd definitely recommend checking it out when it hits a price you feel is fitting for 3-5 hours of entertainment for just the main game and easily 10+ if you're challenge/achievement hunting.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I have played for 5 hours now and have beaten the regular campaign and all I want is more! The difficulty really ramps up towards the end to where I definitely felt less flowy and more frenetic which isn't a complaint. The game just came out so I know its silly to say this but I hope they make more maps and once you beat the campaign give me some customization options. But really a great game that mixes tony hawk and max payne in a brilliant way that feels so smooth most of the time. The cell shaded graphics are stunning and the soundtrack is reminiscient of a 80's sci fi flick or something. I really love this game, buy it and support the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: JET SET MADWORLD-----------------------I put my faith into Roll7 and they delivered... again.Don't be put off by the modest length of the main campaign (it took me around 5 hours to complete).  I'm having a blast replaying the stages to get all the objectives. The new game plus will also keep you busy far beyond the main campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant bit of mad fun! Takes a little while to get used to, and a LOOONG while to master, but it's never boring! The game could really use a practice mode, for getting the hang of the maps and learning the different tricks. There's not really time for any of that, as soon as the match is going. Having the option to explore each map without getting blasted to pieces would be a very welcome addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Controls felt awkward at first and it took some patience to feel comfortable with the mechanics, but after I did a coffin grab and shot a guy in the head from across the map after killing three dudes under me with a grenade launcher in the same flip- I understood.  There is a bit of aim assist and your slow mo meter is pretty generous,  so it's not too hard to pull some pretty cool stuff off once you have the locomotion down.I recommend replaying levels and not just progressing doing the bare minimum- they really throw quite a bit at you pretty quickly and I was getting frustrated before I learned to manage ammo and time my dodges.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I played Rollerdrome until my hands hurt. Then I played some more. This game serves up the same intensity I feel when I'm trying to get a sick score challenge done in Tony Hawk and I'm doing a bunch of flatground tricks after the clock runs out. I frantically look for a rail to grind on to keep my combo going, squeezing out a wallride or two. This game is like that. But instead of kickflips and caspers, you're shooting people in the noggin and flipping like you're training for the olympics. And I think that's just neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: TLWR;you scoot and schutdodge bullets, bats ,missiles ,grind rails and rain shells babyplenty of levels to go through, a fair bit of verticality and alot of things to keep track of.Tutorial could use a tweak though. The main one gets you started and a decent handle on how to jump ,shoot and grind. But halfway through the second category;  it teaches you how to go over the ramps/change momentum midair and wall riding.I'm definitely excited to have more of a challenge and have the stakes raised, but i feel a core mechanic like wall riding should come right after the "how to grind rails" segmentA prompt of "Press this button to grind rails. Press it while jumping into a wall and ride it! Try chaining the two for more mobility..." would do wonders. Otherwise a great start.music is nice but 2mello is def a recommended artist to listen to with this gameplayart is nice and the colors are easy to read. cant help but wish there was more style to it though, yk?but the gameplay is where alot of the passion and love went toBig fan of perfect timed mechanics in games. Add that to a reflex mode and im hooked. But they also add a reflex function to the weapon that changes the spread/damage and that's like three functions working together within 2 seconds!Love it.however,Id like if the dodge mechanic would add to the style/score combo outside of refreshes reflex/gives a bulletGetting a chain of wallrides, rail, and a grab mid air only for the score to go *poof* because i did a perfect dodge is kinda disappointing.I'd like if a perfect dodge could refresh the dodge timer so you could chain perfect dodges together and dance across the sea of missiles and mines on the floor. Or even Ultra instinct that blue laser from a sniper ;watch the bullet count go up as you challenge the flamethrower mechsOf course if you mess up the timing, then thats what you get. high risk high reward ykThe game is fun, it's got a nice hefty weight and momentum based ride that you'll definitely enjoy. 4 weapons to choose and earn as you progress ;again reflex time mechanics for the weapons on top of that. Varied enemy types and im sure there's more to see. It's definitely got a high skill ceiling , but it's not like you need to be a person with > 180ms reaction speed to enjoy it. There's accessibility options and plenty of options to make it more enjoyable for each type of playerdefinitely give this game a shot
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: FUN GAME, well for the campaign mode, the challenges is what kept me replaying the level. The out for blood mode, which essentially a game plus section is a bit too much, it takes out the element of fun to the point of annoying and pesky. For Out for blood mode, It should have been options for upgradable armor with downside of heavier suit that makes harder to do longer air time, roller skate that do damage but leave flames that will hurt player too if skated on it before it extinguished, upgradable suit for ammo for one of the weapons. Anything that makes it feels I won the championship from the campaign, that will fit the narrative for Out for Blood mode.The graphics is excellent, it runs well on my old laptop too, so I can play while I'm not home with my dear PC Dekstop.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Tony Hawk Pro Skater and the Matrix had a baby that was really into synthwave, and you'll get this game. This game will have you pulling sick roller skating tricks, slow motion dodging baddies and blazing your way to victory. There are no shortage of "wow" moments to be had playing Rollerdrome.If any of this sounds good to you, play this, you'll most likely have no regrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly addicting and fresh arcade shooter. While the main campaign might be short, it has TONS of replayability (S ranking and objectives). It's one of the most tightly, smartly designed games I've played in a while. Everything from the varied enemy types, to your weapon selection, to how the score system works is just sublime. The game is also very fair about dodging damage so it's allowed to really push the combat difficulty later on, especially in the Out for Blood campaign. The strong visual style also helps readability a ton. This is a STRONG recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the main story and nearly finishing BFB (With many failiures in the process), this game genuinely might be my personal GOTY.Something about 2022 and releasing so many style-focused flowing action shooters.  Gameplay is snappy and polished, artstyle is poppy and dynamic, and a pretty banging soundtrack to boot.There's no feeling better than flying through the air in a max payne esque slow-mo after a 720 heartbreaker flip in a retro-futurist arena with synths blaring.  This game  love and style, worth all your time and money.And to those saying the game is too hard, there are difficulty toggles in the options, but its definitely a game that demands a certain level of mechanical skill out of you, especially in Back For Blood.  BFB WILL kick your ass if you aren't familiar with the game's mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool concept that's well executed. The game starts off fairly easy and almost seems boring in the first 2 levels but as they introduce more weapons and enemy types it quickly becomes a flow-state bullet-hell where you lose often and relish victory.If you like the idea of a Tony Hawk-style game with guns, then this is worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: The Positive (+):- Visuals style is fantastic. Not only does it perfectly match the retro future aesthetic well, it also provide clear lines and visual separation. For a game that has so much action happening at once, the fact that my eyes never felt fatigued while looking for my next move is a testament to how well this art style and the decisions made here benefit the gameplay.- Gameplay is crisp and fluid. The loop is engaging and the interplay between pulling off tricks while optimizing how you are taking down foes is engaging and leaves nothing to be desired from a core standpoint. The Negative (-):- None off the top of my head. Game doesn't really do anything that I would consider a negative, beyond just want to see more of the game. Nothing that is outright negative, just areas that can be improve that don't detract from the games enjoyment.The Feedback (~):- Music is great, but could improve upon. I think the style they are going for fits the vibe, but I feel like more can be done with it. Would love to see a more dynamic music system implemented with harder riffs that really accentuate moments in the gameplay. That would take this game to the next level!- More content. This foundation of this game is absolutely bursting with potential! I can see this games fundamentals being expanded on and providing even more depth to the gameplay. Imaging powerups, loadouts, more maps and modes. It deserves DLC and a sequel.- Additional modes. Two ideas for modes come to mind. 1) A racing centric mode where same gameplay loop, but enemies have higher health / racing objective etc. Just imagining racing along, pulling off tricks, shooting people, it oozes potential.- Multiplayer. Look, the bones of this game give rocket league. If there is a way to integrate a multiplayer aspect that keeps the core gameplay loop, that sounds incredible.Worth a buy: Yes
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Three hours in, this is a lot of fun as a twitch shooter, but it's a bit too squishy to really be a fun skating game. Skipping the double-taps in favor of eight tricks and directional would have been a better design decision considering how much this game throws at you. Nonetheless, highly replayable levels and fun shooting make this worth buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. This is what indie games are all about, combining already great concepts into a unique experience! Love all the Tony Hawk influence, which really comes through, but at the same time it feels like it stands on its own as an addicting arcade-style shooter. But it still shakes up the same old shooting mechanics which keeps things fresh. The narrative is a cool dystopian plot with hints of cyberpunk thrown in, which adds to the game's character. The learning curve is definitely a little steep, and it takes some practice to get the hang of the controls and play style (would definitely recommend some button-mapping to cater to yourself and make things easier). But once you really get a feel for the game, it becomes a fun and really addicting series of challenges, and the replayability of challenges and score rankings keeps you wanting to play for hours.Only thing I can think of is I wish the narrative was longer! But I'm sure the Out for Blood mode will keep me busy for much longer. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, has some flaws but nothing that I don't believe can't change.-Progression system is  'FINE' but it starts to ruin the pacing of the game in the latter half, as it turns out that once the gameplay itself requires more focus it becomes a bit harder to memorize and keep track of a tony hawk-esc goal list.-stick inputs for specific tricks feel way too inconsistent to be anything but frustrating whenever required by a goal-The lack of dualsense support is disappointing on pc , i imagine haptic feedback would do a lot for helping with awareness during more hectic situations -most enemies don't move much and often feel more like targets or static turrets rather than an opposing force uhhh other than that nitpicking, game is pretty great and unique, big fan of this
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the graphics, I was afraid it would run as poorly as Sable. Luckily, it doesn't. Rollerdrome is a wild ride in a distopic retro future straight from the 70s (and a homage to 1975's Rollerball). The art style looks like something from a 70's cartoon.Performance with this minimalistic style is - as you should hope - perfect. Controls are responsive and fast to learn and while you can do acrobatics like Mr. Hawk himself, you don't have to focus on your landings. You can kick in generous slow motion whenever you need it to help you with shooting and dodging.It's incredibly fun, easy to learn if hard to master and should you reach your personal limits you can always activate aids like unlimited health or ammo. 19,79€ is a more than fair price for this great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.user: X F R I M \\レベッカ\\
_childDocuments_.review: If the devs are reading this, thank you, this game is a beautiful mix of stunningly memorable visuals and the most satisfying gameplay I've played in awhile, everything just comes together to create some of the coolest moments I've experienced in an action game. As an animator I have to give props to the animation team for somehow blending the sick tricks of a tony hawk game with the beautiful shoot dodge of Max Payne onto Kara, absolutely inspirational work.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, and IMO a genre resurrector!. Never thought I would be looking for good routes to perform tricks on a level and chasing challenges like I did in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater. Combat was also a great addition to the formula, it feels and looks awesome. But those would  only add to it, the fact that it doesn't have them doesn't subtract from its awesomeness.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Action is very cool, music is awesome, but there is a cap on difficulty. _childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: After 10 minutes into it, This game is amazing. I love the idea of Tony Hawk but with guns to it in which is a very simple and great idea ever made. great art style and tone to match it very well. Already one of my favorite games this year and I recommend this if you love skateboarding or third person shooter games in general. you'll definitelyget a kick out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: you will die but you will like it.base campaign is kinda hard but out for blood is insanely difficult.challenges are a great addition for people who want..... a challenge.all in all its a solid 6 hrs of gameplay if you're good and I highly recommend if you like tony hawk mixed with some max payne. your wallet will only forgive you until the end of August this month tho :)
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Tony Hawk with a bit of Jet Grind Radio, mixed in with some of "The Club" (Who remembers that literal run-and-gun game?)Throw in a healthy coat of very consistent, clean art direction and an ungodly good soundtrack and you have a great package.  Controls are very fluid and polished.  I only ever die because my fingers can't keep up with the bad ass moves my brain thinks it can pull off.Sometimes, I just want to pop in a video game, feel super cool and jam out to a soundtrack.  This game scratches that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a sandwich made with all my favorite ingredients. I've been playing for a few hours now and could see myself playing ALOT more. The flow of the game is so smooth. Plays like Tony Hawk without the focus on landing. The game will feel easy at first until you get into chasing the checklists and some of the later levels that have fall hazards combined with ground hazards and enemies that you can't kill in one go round. Easily my favorite game I've never heard of.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I have seen reviews say this game is easy and seen ones that say it is hard...both are correct. If you played the old Tony Hawk games, the controls will probably be easy for you to pick up but probably less so if you have not. The game ramps up it's difficulty FAST so if you are struggling I recommend turning on options to make the game easier. I don't use these but hey play the game how you want man. You bought it. Controls are smooth and responsive and the game's autoaim is really good. Guns all feel good and you really want to swap weapons based on situations. Music is pretty good as well. If you want a fast paced arcade style game with a Tony Hawk style twist, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I'm hitting every single button on the controller.dodge, hold a, let go to jump, hit x to do a trick and left bumper to flip, all while spinning with the thumb stick. While you're doing that switch to the grenade launcher to hit the foes out of range of your guns. switch back to the shotgun before you land to hit the Laser gunner who keeps aiming at you. He teleports away as you switch to you pistol to shoot the missiles that have been chasing you down for the past 15 AGONIZING seconds. do it. play this game if you think you're GAMER enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the concept for this game on one of the Dev's Twitter what feels like ages ago now, It looked great and was a day 1 buy for me.I enjoyed it, but it does has a bit for a difficulty ramp up after a couple of levels, however these were pretty easy once you understand how the enemies, weapons and dodging works.It took me longer than I'd like to admit to realise that Super Reflex Time cause your weapons to do a lot more damage. For example the flamethrower mechs take 4 grenades normally and only 2 in Super Reflex Time.Overall I had a lot of fun playing this, died many times and the challenges will probably have me going back for more, even though I can't hit the right tricks to save my life :P
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: This game got a lot of great reviews.  So i bought it.  First and foremost, and it's only a tiny pet peeve for me but that have like a minutes worth of text that plays like a slide show that you can't skip.  That is annoying af.  I get you want the text, but put it all on one page and let me read it and skip if I want to skip.  Don't put it on a very slow slide show that assumes you read at a 3rd grade level.  That annoying instance beside...I just left to get a drink and snack and it was done when I got back.  So far the game is actually a lot of fun. It slowly introduces you to the controls and slowly introduces you to the chaotic nature of the game.  It's a lot of fun and very hectic.  Even the first campaign got you on your feet with hectic stuff.  THe graphics are great and a fitting style and just barely hit your card.  I am playing on a 4k monitor with a 3060ti and i have the graphics maxed out and the game barely uses up 20% of the gpu.  This game is like a mix of tony hawk meets doom with a cell shade type of look.  So far it is a lot of fun.  The music is like that retro type music and very fitting. The rollerblading is very smooth with it's no fall system.  So you are continuously moving.  It has a slow-mo feature that works really well.  They recommend playing with a controller but I had zero issues playing with a k/m.  The story is also fascinating. I am usually not into the game story but the game has me oddly interested. I look forward to more gaming. My 10 year old daughter likes to play it as well.  I highly recommend it especially at $20.edit for fun: there are a lot of skating moves that I didn't even realize.  Like before I understood that if you press left and x you would do a specific grab and that works for all the directions and grabs/grinds/flips...but you can do left left x or up down x...there are tons of moves. It definitely gets harder as you go on.  More enemies of varied types that require use of different guns or else.  Like I just got done with one map that has dudes that shoot some blue ray at you.  You can shotgun them but they will teleport away after one shot.  You can use your pistol on them and take away 2/3 of their life.  The maps are a lot of fun and varied.  I let my daughter play and there are plenty of "cheats" that make the game easier.  So easy my daughter wants to play more than me.  I don't get why people think the difficulty is too high.  Just put on god mode and infinite ammo and have fun. You can literally play the whole game that way and unlock all the maps etc.  Your score won't go high because of the cheats but you can still unlock everything and enjoy the whole game.  So they literally made the game for those who want to perfect their play and those that just want casual play.  It's a win/win.  I saw a few comments saying it got too hard too fast.  Play with cheats.  They literally give you a dedicated option screen that is there from the start...you do nothing but go to this screen in options and turn them on.  No weird cheats codes or anything. Highly enjoying the game.  It's worth it.  Also, quick tip.  You can easily unlock things and those unlocks persist even if you die.  So don't worry too much about dying.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, I'm so 50/50 on it. I think the story is just kind of passable, It’s the evil capitalist overlord’s thing we've seen a billion times now. A part of me wants to like it, but another is more leaning towards "yeah ok...like...I just don't get it". Idk what I was expecting from the game, but what's there just doesn't really do it for me. The gameplay, for me, just ended up being about dodging constantly and it completely took me out of doing tricks. The assists do a lot in helping you ease into the games steep learning and difficulty curve. But, since the game has no level where you can freely roll around and learn the different tricks, learn enemy behaviour/pattern and so on, it just became a disorienting mess. I’m going to recommend it to people who really like the Tony Hawk franchise, and a specific style of arcade game. If that’s you, then Rollerdrome is maybe for you. Glad I tried it, glad to support the devs and I hope to see more Rollerdrome content in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Tricks are pretty easy to execute, and game is also pretty forgiving when you mess up a trick mid-air, keeping your movement fluid amidst all the chaos. Also has auto aim when you're close enough to a target while in bullet time.Regardless of the ease of gunning down your opposition, this will make you feel like a the main character of a roller derby death match directed by John Woo. Feels pretty hype when you get a kill in the middle of pulling a 1080 christ air. If you're a fan of Tony Hawk or Jet Set Radio, give this game a look into ASAP.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good, exactly what I expected it to be.Seems pretty polished, didn't encounter any bugs, controls feel good but the camera did take a bit of getting used to. Gameplay is fun and pulling off insane ♥♥♥♥ in a match feels really good.From what I can tell the game is fairly short, I think I got about half way through in a few hours doing every challenge along the way. If you don't do the challenges you can rush through very quickly. I think it's value is heavily dependent on the if the player wants to repeat levels to get good runs, if you aren't the type of player who wants to challenge themselves repeating levels and improving personal time/score then you may find the game lacking.There is another mode that is locked until after the campaign, so I don't know what that has but there could be a bit more afterwards.Overall great game, having a ton of fun, but it does appeal to specific niche of player I feel and if you don't fall into that niche you'll probably want more than it has to offer.Also ♥♥♥♥ the beam enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Prelim Review (1.5 hrs gameplay): This game is awesome. Imagine Max Payne as a Techno-Retro Roller-Disco of acrobatic, Tony Hawk-styled, Cirques Du Soleil nihilistic dystopian death-sport and there you have the glorious ritual we all know and revere as ROLLERDROME. To say that this game is "cinematic" is an understatement. Full review to, eventually, follow, but for now: play ROLLERDROME.
_childDocuments_.name: Rollerdrome

_childDocuments_.review: The movement is fantastic, it's fast and stylish, and everything about it feels great right from the start. I don't remember the last game I played that I was having fun before I even finished the tutorial. It plays like a Tony Hawk game, only instead of wiping out on a missed jump the only thing that's going to slow you down are the enemies liberally spaced throughout the maps packing everything from bats to shotguns to sniper rifles trying to ruin your day.      You get ammo back by performing tricks as you move around, and the aiming mode uses a bullet time-like slowdown that just feels cool as you flip upside down and blast some guy as you fly overhead. It's an extremely fun game that you can play and enjoy in short bursts, on maps that are extremely replayable since you're going to immediately want to retry them to see if you can pull off a better score.      I'm not sure I'd have taken the chance on it at full price, but for less than $20 it was worth a shot and I'm glad I did. It's a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: The year is 2030, and you are a competitor in a brutal new bloodsport – Rollerdrome. Combine stylish skate tricks with devastating slow-mo kills, picking your weapons with care to land the killing blow and make it to the end of the round… and maybe, with enough skill and hard work, to the end of the Championship. [Roll7]

name: Redfall
detailed_description: PC Hardware Specifications About the Game Redfall is an open-world, single player and co-op FPS from Arkane Austin, the award-winning team behind Prey and Dishonored. Continuing Arkane’s legacy of carefully crafted worlds and immersive sims, Redfall brings the studio’s signature gameplay to this story-driven action shooter. Features Uncover the Truth, Take Back Redfall The island town of Redfall, Massachusetts, is under siege by a legion of vampires who have blocked out the sun and cut the citizens off from the outside world. Explore the open world and immerse yourself in a deep story campaign as you unravel the mystery behind the vampires’ appearance. Ally with a handful of survivors against the creatures threatening to bleed the town dry. Slay Alone Or Squad Up Redfall blends single- and multiplayer options seamlessly, allowing the player to venture into the darkness alone or to squad-up for up to four player co-op. Teammates can try different hero loadouts and combine their strengths to find creative solutions to the vampire apocalypse. You will collect an arsenal of specialized weaponry and customize your character with unique upgrades and abilities to suit your playstyle for guns blazing, stealth combat, and everything in-between. Unconventional Heroes Vs. the Night Created by science experiments gone wrong and gifted with psychic abilities, Redfall’s vampires will challenge you and your squad to get creative. You will choose from a team of diverse heroes – each with their own character-specific abilities – to overcome the vampire legion and their brood of maniacal followers. DEVINDER CROUSLEY – The Verified Cryptid Hunter: A cryptozoologist and aspiring inventor. Armed with weapons of his own creation, he’s on a mission to prove himself. LAYLA ELLISON – The Telekinetic Threat: A biomedical engineering student who volunteered for a medical trial where something went very wrong, leaving her with intense telekinetic abilities. REMI DE LA ROSA – The Ingenious Ingeniera: A brilliant combat engineer who has spent her life on the frontlines. With the help of her robot cohort, Bribón, she’s determined to help rescue Redfall’s survivors. JACOB BOYER – The Deadeye with an Undead Eye: An ex-military sharpshooter turned private contractor. Strange happenings on Redfall have left Jacob with a mysterious vampiric eye and a spectral raven that’s never far from his side. The Open World Of Redfall Redfall is a true Arkane experience set in a rich world that blends the familiar with the extraordinary. Redfall’s open world is handcrafted by the master level designers behind Prey’s Talos I space station and Dishonored’s Dunwall. From the town’s once-bustling downtown and the haunted forest to the decimated seaside boardwalk and beyond, you will fight through cultist outposts and supernatural psychic spaces as you piece together Redfall’s many mysteries.

_childDocuments_.review: This game launched a mess. Like a dummy, I bought it day one. Won’t make that mistake again. Well, I set it aside and waited until they did some fixing. Now, after update 3, I’ve restarted the game and I’m loving it. Is it perfect? Absolutely not. Some times (not often) an enemy will sit while you shoot them. I’ve seen some funky glitches like people sliding rather than walking, but it’s not often enough to bother me in the least. I’ve got 22 hours in the game since revisiting it and only one crash. I’ll take that any day.I think some games just are fun to hate, and once they get on the hate list, it’s really hard to get off. Call of Duty and Madden Football come to mind.  Check out the reviews on MW3, mostly negative. But guess what, it sells like hot cakes and there are a ton of people out there (including myself) that buy it every year and get more than their moneys worth.  But, since it has become cool to hate COD, the reviews are always negative. I think that is what happened to this game. I’d say that it has come far enough that it is worth looking at again. Positives: Good (not great) graphics.  Good story. I’ve seen hate on the style of cut scenes (they are voiced stills) but I don’t mind as I’m the type that skips cut scenes anyway.Nice open world with great atmosphere. I’ve yet to see the 2nd map, but I like the first. Great audio. Neat idea. I’m tired of zombies and Nazis. Vampires is a nice change of pace.Lots of variety in enemies. There are quite a few different types of vampires.Nice skill tree.Co-op. From what I hear it works, but my friends won’t get the game because of all the bad reviews, maybe if it goes on a big sale one day..Cons:Game does not tell you how ammo works in the beginning. I thought it was a bug (and it may be), but until the mission where you steal a supply crate from the Bellweather guys and open up a safe house, I was unable to purchase ammo. This forced me to rely on picked up ammo, and you almost never (at least in the beginning) get ammo for the UV gun or the stake gun. This makes it really hard to take out vampires in the beginning. The ammo in your main base (the firehouse) still does not work for me. I almost quit the game because of this. But my work around now is to just buy the ammo from a safe house and it works.Heroes are unbalanced for solo play. Tip here, play as Remi. The rest just don’t do well solo. Until switching to Remi, I considered quitting as I could not beat massed vampires, which will happen. I do think the Hero mix would work well in Co-op.Ok now for some fun. I often see reviews on Steam that are obviously designed more to get likes and awards than actually provide a useful review. I’m going to toss in my favorites; maybe I’ll get some awards as well!1. Nobody reads reviews, so I’ll just say I’m gay.2. I’m paralyzed from the waist down (no disrespect to those who really are). This game allowed me to finally get to know my son. We play it together and have grown closer than we ever were before, because, you know, I’m not very good at outdoor sports.3. And my personal favorite: I pledge to swallow 1 tablespoon of mayonnaise for each like that I get for this review.Happy Vampire slaying, and do yourself a favor and select Remi.

_childDocuments_.review: Redfall, very clearly, has been received poorly, however I don't believe the game is as bad as most are describing.  You have the obligatory performance issues on random rigs, some AI Jank that can easily be patched, the normal kinds of bugs that you find in an open world like this which can also be patched, etc.  Nothing I would consider game breaking or detrimental to the game, its no Cyberpunk or Darktide release.The storyline seems meh so far and the world does seem empty..especially in this day and age where we're so used to open world games having literally 20 things to do around each corner.  Maybe this is a good thing, maybe it's not...that's yet to be seen by me. The graphics seem nice, though I think the flashligh is a bit flat and lack luster.  The combat unfortunately is mediocre at best, but perhaps that's just the character I'm currently playing I plan on trying others when I find the time (Grown up life, am I right?).  I have, unfortunately, not been able to play with anyone as no one wants to buy the game with the bad press it's getting so I don't have any idea how the multiplayer is.  I've experienced some bugs, the biggest and most annoying one for me is enemies will just suddenly stop registering damage and I'll have to stop firing and start again for it to start doing damage again.  It's not me missing or anything like that, they just simply stop taking damage and it appears to be random so it's not anything I can easily reproduce from what I've seen.  For the most part my game play has been unbugged and the game runs well on my Ryzen 3950x and 3090 Ti at  5120x1440.  I've not had any noticeable hitching or frame drops, I've not personally noticed any memory leaks or any strangeness when running the game.  Is this game great...no, by no means.  Is it bad...to some I'm sure it is but honestly it's not as bad as the hate seems to be making it.  It's a pretty bog standard open world looter shooter with what I would consider normal issues for a game of it's type.  Give it a try, if you really hate it then steam has a great refund policy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so let me explain the game so far and put into perspective some of the negativity. The game isnt that bad, its actually entertaining. That being said; it was sort of billed as this "Left 4 Dead" style game which it is sorely not. This game is basically more like Dead Island than Left for Dead. The single player is the main focus and the multiplayer is basically rendered to an after thought in some aspects because they do nothing to encourage it. This is very sad considering the trailers and demo game play make it look like the next big coop multiplayer game like Left 4 Dead. Additionally the AI is ridiculously dumb for a AAA game. I mean stupid dumb... I cant believe they let it pass like this. The AI basically is super predictable, runs at you just to be shot. The vampire AI is slightly better but I almost feel like they dumbed down the humans so much to make the Vampires seem more challenging. The Vampires are basically the same situation but a bit more tanky. They run at you, jump at you, and warp around you. They are very easy to predict. Overall I would recommend buying this game on a steam sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I don't understand the hate. I played it for free on gamepass just to see what was up and I actually enjoyed it so I bought it on steam. It may not be a game for everyone and thats fine but I don't see why it has so many negative reviews. Ive had a lot of fun just sneaking by or obliterating vampires and cultists. Its basically vampire dishonored. If you like the dishonored franchise give it a go. If you are unsure of spending the $70 try it on xbox gamepass. But dont let the reviews persuade you like I did at first.Update: So since I finished it I figured i'd post an update. I still stand by what I said. I enjoyed the game. Throughout the entire game I never had a crash or any major bug. Occasionally the menu would glitch but swapping tabs fixed it. Could it use some more to the game overall? Absolutely, it was pretty repetitive but still had its fun. Could have used more story and missions.  Beat it in a little over 20 hours. Doing most missions (probably missed one or two side missions). The Vampire nests didnt really seem to have a point other than some chances at good loot and money and just something else to do, overall pretty underwhelming. They made a bubble in that area that made vamps stronger but they didnt serve a purpose otherwise and didnt effect the completion of the game. The little red gas bodies on the map seemed to randomly respawn so clearing them was kind of a waste of time imo. Downsides: Make sure you finish everything you want to do in Redfall before going to Burial Point because there is no backtracking that I found once you go to the next area. So if you miss anything you have to wait until the next play through. Also once you beat the game theres no "cleanup" for anything you missed. Thats the game and when you click play again it starts you over but you keep your weapons and all the gravelocks and stuff you found in your previous play through. Im not sure theres Gold snipers, stake guns, or UV lights because my entire plathrough I kept getting the same variety of guns so it does seem like its very limited on gold tier weapons which cant have their skin changed or stake changed which was kind of a bummer. The only way it seems to get gold guns is to hit the randomizer in the "gun shop" and hope for luck or kill the Rook which is like a mini boss that spawns after you kill enough vamps and always guarantees a gold weapon. Other than that I never saw a gold weapon from looting.10May24 - Changing my review to negative since theres no hope on this game ever getting updates or fixed now that the studio was axed. There was a lot of potential here. just need more time and love to it imo. And chances that no offline mode coming means there wont be more playability once the servers get axed too. Its too bad. Was nice having a vampire fps game, something other than zombies for a change. So anyways dont waste your time since the company is gone now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not deserve all of the poor ratings it is getting. Pretty much open world where you can run and gun as you please. Silky movement and the weapons are great. Graphics are awesome and the maps are very good too. Admittedly there are issues that have come to light playing further into the game. Its far from perfect but there are a lot of good things in this game too. The main problem that I see is that the guns and skills do not adequately reward you to be able to deal with the tougher enemies that follow. Also the combat movements when under severe attacks are somewhat clunky and very slow, when enemies are numerous and some lightening fast.This game was never intended to be an easy walk in the park, but as I see it there are some serious balance issues here. However, I cannot fathom why people are not happy with this. Certainly at full price not so hot but definitely worth it on sale, absolute.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I would like to defend this game, being such a long time fan of Arkane Austin games and their style (having hundreds of hours in both Dishonored and Dishonored 2 combined (though most of that in the first game) and having enjoyed Prey well enough)....I can't.The game is redeemable, with future updates and content.  The gameplay itself isn't the worst thing in the world.  But frankly the game is a 6/10 at best, and the absolute silence from the dev team and lack of updates in over a month (and no, the backend update a week after launch doesn't count), the game is officially dead on arrival.  I'll probably continue playing and replaying it with a friend of mine, but ultimately I've fully lost hope in the game being salvaged to even an 8/10 state at this point.Communication was all that was needed, really.  Sure it wouldn't have saved this failure of a launch, but it would've helped soothe the worries and the poor launch for those of us who saw the potential of a stable game in there.Don't waste your money on this.  The guns are random AF, the drops are worse, the balance is crap, the AI is some of the stupidest I've ever seen in a post-PS2 era game, the world is depopulated to hell and back, Co-op makes the game easier not harder (as in literally less enemies spawn in co-op than in solo play), and the bulk of everything going on is frankly just not engaging with almost only one exception.

_childDocuments_.review: I resisted the urge to buy it on day one, later purchased it at a discount, and played it after update 3. The story is like Deadloop: fringe scientists become godlike beings that dispose of hordes of cultists. The main loop is straightforward: kill countless enemies, loot everything not anchored to the floor, gain experience, level up, repeat.The game isn't terrible at this point (I wouldn't recommend buying it at full price), but it lacks content and gameplay variety. I really liked the aesthetics and enjoyed the story. It's not the most original story out there, but it's still good enough to keep you playing.For me, the game is still in its early stages. If Arkane continues working on it, it will likely be polished within a year. I think (and hope) that the early release was a publisher's error.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Redfall with little expectations, aside from it seeming like Borderlands with vampires and I was not far off. My main confusion was with the campaign and how it would progress or keep me interested being isolated to a town map. It does a decent job at keeping you on task as you roam across the city and recapture safehouses that each have their own area questlines. You fight a boss for each area after doing enough quests and pick up side quests along the way. The gameplay itself feels surprisingly good, each character has branching skill trees and you're constantly changing out loot for better stats or rarities. The map is littered with loot and guarded treasure, while most houses or buildings require lockpicking or hacking to enter, along with tripmines, safes, and alarms to disarm or loot. I was worried about the difficulty being too easy, but there are four modes to choose from and it's giving me a run for my money on solo hard mode. There are also lots of cosmetics to unlock just by completing quests and challenges.My biggest gripe is that the co op was not thought out at all. Hosting a game is invite from friend's list only, which means you'll likely be playing solo unless you have friends to play with. It's annoyingly difficult to play co op at all otherwise. They need to get public servers and allow public hosting if they want co op to happen.Overall I wouldn't jump on the hate bandwagon just yet, Redfall has potential. If you aren't bothered by pretentious FPS gripes and you enjoy looter shooters then you should pick it up, it's actually a solid game with decent challenge and detail put into it. The more you look around the more you seem to find.(Since the developers have been unable to deliver on key features involved with the genre like multiplayer matchmaking, I can't leave a positive review so I'm changing this to negative. There WAS potential here if you focused in the right areas, but you've proven that you could not deliver. We haven't even seen the two additional characters promised at launch and I would get a refund if I could. Redfall is a crippled experience from what it could have been.)

_childDocuments_.review: I was very hyped to play this game. I love the concept and Arkane Studios, but I just can't recommend this in its current state at launch. Performance has consistently been poor while the movement and moment to moment gameplay have felt clunky. I am hopelessly optimistic that future patches will clean up the performance issue, general bugs, clunky gameplay, and disappointing enemy AI. Until then, probably buy it on sale and/or with friends to play with (assuming coop works fine). So far it did have some of that classic Arkane worldbuilding which I'm looking forward to getting immersed in, but I'm going to wait for a more polished product.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on sale for 20 bucks, and honestly, I absolutely love it. I don't know what it was like before the updates, but I genuinely don't understand the hatred over this. I went into this expecting it to be awful based on reviews and youtubers saying this was genuinely purely bad, and I just don't see it based on experience. I've only been focusing on the solo campaign. I'm playing on the highest difficulty, and I gotta say it's challenging. The gun play mechanics are super fun and great to play around with. The map is gorgeous, as someone who once lived in Massachusetts they captured the spirit and aesthetic of it perfectly. I enjoy how you can only focus on one mission at a time versus having endless missions you have to keep jumping back and forth with. The writing is quirky, not the best, but enjoyable. I really like the quiche of having a vampire ex-boyfriend you can summon occasionally to fight your battles. Very reminiscent of Lollipop Chainsaw Massacre. Art style is beautiful. I have zero complaints, and I've been playing a great deal.

_childDocuments_.review: The environments were nice, you get two maps and an interlude in between, I just wish the props were destructible.For combat, the vampires can get in your face, but the human ai is dumb as nails. They'll run backwards and spend more time staring at your feet than pumping lead into your chest. Also included are explosive cars and electrical boxes, great for collateral damage. Maybe it was just the difficulty but I really didn't feel any danger. I don't think I got any cool loot either, just the occasional upgrade that carried me to the end.It's made for co-op but idk why they'd lock achievements to just the host. I got to about the halfway point with a friend when we realized this and had to restart solo. Accessibility settings include infinite ammo and I really didn't feel bad putting that on. Also, there's no in-game save system and there are branching decisions. Feel free to manually scum your documents folder. You'll need to max trust all 4 characters, which takes about 4 hours total, just sprinting through main missions with 3 and then another go with 1 more. I didn't have any technical issues playing solo on high, but when I played with others my frames would drop to single digits, especially in combat, then return to normal.  The story was ok? The cutscenes were just slowly moving stills with your character narrating. Pretty underwhelming. You shouldn't feel bad avoiding this, though there's something about dumpster diving and playing things other people avoid. Meeting all the challenge conditions was pretty fun to be fair. Maybe it's meeting friends that also play your games that makes it worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait and finish the game before I made a complete judgment, and it's safe to say this game doesn't redeem itself if you power through any of the obvious issues (like performance) However, I'm going to ignore those to point out the more glaring sins it commits in the realm of open world/looter shooter/rpgs: - a quarter of your skill tree is inventory upgrades - previous areas (though there are only 2 total) can't be accessed after you leave them - there is no "point of no return" warning before the final boss - the final boss, unlike the previous bosses, isn't a boss fight.  - there isn't a post game, you are forced into ng+, which sees no experience boost/buff and no difficulty change - coop progress is kept by only the host - loot rarity is worthless and only seems to be influenced by the percentage buffs to specific interactions or stats - without a "silent" method to kill, stealth mechanics feel wasted - no cutscenes, just 3d rendered characters and scenes that struggle to render fully while they're playing - dialogue is stiff, sometimes cringe and overly serious, and npcs are static while they deliver it - half of the traversal abilities are rendered useless in areas due to invisible walls and barriers - weapon purchases are expensive while trade prices are abysmalThe list could go on as I nitpick further, but a lot of these things were improved, fixed or avoided by games released well before Redfall came out and they were successes that earned appeal for sequels. How can a company miss so hard on every tenet of a good open world game when it unabashedly takes notes from something like Far Cry that has such mass exposure to players? AND even if not one of the developers worked on Arkane's previous titles, how can you not draw inspiration from at least ONE thing from the better parts of those games? I managed to maintain the minimum level of enjoyment and pace to get to the finish line, and now that I'm there the only thing I can give them credit for are interesting concepts in the lore/writing. Everything else either feels unfinished, unpolished, or entirely broken. Best of luck to the developers assuming they get an opportunity to make up for it. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I refunded the product, I only played for around 120mins on launch. Take this review with a grain of salt.The game takes Fallout 76 and Borderlands gun play and mixes them together. At times, the sights are clunky and the gun doesn't seem to want to cooperate. Though, usually, the gun play is decent and when it works it does work well. However, the minor issues do tend to build up to a ruined experience such as a shotgun reload not happening if you sprint or climb on the last frame of the action. Small instances like this are frequent as stutters can affect gameplay, and the game stutters/slows frequently due to terrible optimizationThe melee, too, is a part of this experience as when it works it makes things enjoyable. When it doesn't, it's frustrating at most and annoying in the least. There is no lunge which is fine. However, what is not fine, is that a leaf from a branch or twig obscuring that cultist's face can absorb your entire elbow's blow that would normally 1-tap the guy. Repeated melee strikes with your stake weapon to trigger the finishing blow on a vampire is also a must 9/10 times. Melee just breaks for no reason because you're not at the right distance.Skills on characters are bland and limited in my opinion. Get ammo, get health, and follow the same upgrade path everyone else does. It's a game that wants to be borderlands with less character customization/build options. Nothing exciting in the skill tree section.The map is like a Far Cry map, but smaller. Enemies are everywhere, but they're cultists or vampires. Or there's red mist blocking certain areas. The night-day cycle exists, but nothing really changes. Nothing different or exciting, this is just a Far Cry map with Far cry objectives. It just has vampires in it.Overall, the game is a 5/10. Not worth $70, not exciting enough. So I uninstalled to get a refund. There's potential here, but ain't no one making use of it from my 2 hour's experience. And if a game isn't fun in the first hour, I won't be spending my time trying to get to the fun bits when there's indie games that are fun from the very start for half the price.

_childDocuments_.review: If you come into the game wanting non-stop combat as a key element, it won't really be what you're looking for. Approach the game the way it's presented—a town to explore that was torn apart from the inside so you need to fight to save its remaining community, with oodles of environmental storytelling bolstered by PC and enemy dialogue—and you should have a better time.Redfall is a town beset by vampires and their cultists, but the situation had built up over time—weeks of neighbors acting strange, people going missing. That's why it's desolate, houses boarded up, shops shuttered.This isn't a town dense with corpses turned undead. It's a town devastated by people turning on their community, sacrificing neighbors to a couple people in power. Yes, there's space between fights—because untold numbers of townies are gone, or left dead in the streets. If you take the time to look while you run around, there's a TON of crafted environmental elements underlining all that. So many notes, items, and corpses indicating clear, unique moments throughout the town.I personally find the space between enemy groups a boon, because even while playing solo, you can't pause. So it's nice to be able to find an empty area to hide when a brief break is needed, without having to go back to a safehouse. And yeah, the game's got bugs—but what big game doesn't on launch? There's too many moving parts at this scale, within the game and for folks' respective setups. I personally haven't had anything game-breaking, so while I look forward to patches, I'm having fun poking around Redfall and figuring out just what the hell these vampire gods did.Aesthetically, characters are stylized rather than hyper-realistic, which I personally prefer. It helps to avoid the uncanny valley 3d is prone to, and prevents looking “dated” as quickly because the exaggerations are deliberate. There's also a good bit of dialogue from key NPCs that is custom to the PC you play—using the PC's name in greetings and goodbyes, plus extra little chats that happen when you approach them. Stuff like Eva asking Dev if this is the weirdest ♥♥♥♥ he's seen, Anna asking whether he's got new inventions he's working on, etc., which make the connection to the world feel just that much more solid. I've also had the unique vampires call out my character by name, which caught me off guard the first time—can't say I was expecting the vampires to actually be sharing info with each other. I would like if there were some way to get a little voiced banter with the other PCs while playing solo, because I LOVE all the characters. But it's also fun reading the color-coded notes on the whiteboards, and Devinder's solo commentary is absolutely AMAZING on its own, so I am well entertained.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of flack for this game but while I have some gripes I've still really enjoyed it. I've so far really enjoyed the visual style of the game. The vampires look nosferatu levels of monstrous which is a nice change from modern depictions. The playable characters all seem really unique and despite playing single player I haven't found any situation I can't handle with any particular characters skill sets. The lack of pausing and saving in single player mode for example. The customisation options for guns are a little minimal so buying a particular type of weapon isn't a guarantee of a particular characteristic (silencer). _childDocuments_.review: So the game for me has run pretty well overall and I do not think it deserves the mostly negative rating. However, it probably had more potential than what was actually delivered. AI is pretty lackluster, specifically detection range and pathing. Frequent travel out of the game world to linear pyschic zones and half-empty nests was also pretty meh. An actual area infested or even an RNG basement would have been a bit cooler in my opinion. Also would have been nice to travel between the two play areas freely. I feel like you see about the same 2-3 guns for each weapon category, which is probably the biggest annoyance. The unrivaled weapons still go off those few base weapons, just with an extra perk at the cost of unchangeable skins and stakes. Unrivaled weapons seem to have a lot of the same perks for that named gun. They are pretty satisfying to use though, especially the stake launcher and flare pistol against vampires. Also the perk that allows your bullets to finish vamps changes the tracer color which is pretty cool.The abilities are fun though, at least Devinder's abilities. His shock javelin has a fairly low cooldown so you can use it multiple times in engagements, the blacklight staff was also super dope. Very satisfying to AOE 4-5 vamps at once. Teleport was meh, more coop focused but still nice. The worldbuilding and setting are also extremely well done. I love the environmental storytelling, seeing a blood trail go down into the basement, or some groups final stand with backs (bodies) against a wall. But there is a tonnn of notes scattered about to accompany that, a bit too much imo. I've done mostly solo so can't comment on the team synergy too much but there is definitely coop only skills in the skilltree. I could see coop being more fun than solo. Prey is still my top Arkane game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent about 70 hours in the game at the time of this review. Completed the story on all difficulty levels including New Game Plus. I also played every character and did all quests including side missions and collected all collectables.My review is therefore not a short half-hour impression, but the gaming experience in all its width and depth.To be fair, I initially gave the title a negative review because I was struggling with technical difficulties and couldn't even start the game. After two tedious hours of internet searching, I got all the errors under control and was finally able to get started.First impressions were mixed and I wasn't sure what to think of the game for a long time. But the deeper I dived into the world, the more loving details came to light. For example, the story about the fire department, the first hub of the game, is very detailed. There are newspaper articles hanging on the wall that you can actually read and if you look around carefully you will discover even more cool story bits. You can also follow the characters' storyies and find their jobs or homes. and that level of detail is found in almost every aspect of the game world.The environmental storytelling is also very well done, for example if you follow a trail of blood you can often find loot or other secrets. Also reading the notes (which I skipped completely at the beginning because it unnecessarily slowed down the game... I just wanted to explore and not read) gives an interesting insight into the happenings of the world.The biggest problem of the game is probably the AI ​​and the many big and small bugs. The heroes' skill trees aren't really well thought out either. For example, why doesn't the game's Sniper, who relies on good position more than any other class, have not any movement-ability? Or why does the Closerange shotgun character have a springboard skill that toss you out off the optimal distance for his weapons? I don't see any real synergy there. they should have thought more carefully about that.But still, the world has charm and is full of things to discover. The explorer in me just wants to find them all. I can only hope that after the launch fiasco, this game still has a chance. Maybe the team behind redfall can do the impossible and win back their fans with some good updates. I can only wish it for them, because the potential is definitely there.

_childDocuments_.review: How Does the Zero Trust Exchange Work?The Zero Trust Exchange eliminates the attack surface by making applications invisible to the internet. Plus, because the traffic never touches your network directly, lateral movement is impossible. Ultimately, this approach significantly reduces your organization's risk of falling victim to ransomware and other malware, accidental or malicious data loss, and more.In our hyperconnected, dynamic, and distributed world, the traditional security perimeter is vanishing. Applications are moving into the cloud, and users are connecting from everywhere, on all kinds of devices. IoT and OT traffic are exploding, and apps are communicating with each other across clouds. In effect, the network connecting employees, apps, workloads, and devices today is the internet itself. The cloud and data centers have become destinations, with the internet as the transport layer for traffic.So, how do you secure a network you don’t own and can’t control?The Zero Trust Exchange provides a platform of services for securing all enterprise traffic and routing it intelligently through the fastest channels. It's the foundation for secure digital transformation, delivering the agility, security, automation, and experiences your organization needs to move ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a mash up of Vampire the Masquerade and Fortnite (loot without the building).  Definitely looks like an Arkane game.  Feels like one too.  Gameplay-wise, It seems OK.  I went into this not know a thing about it.  And, quite honestly, I still am not sure what this is trying to be.  Basically, you roam around a city killing some fanatics during the day and then vampires during the night, all the while collecting loot (guns mostly) and completing quests and side missions.  Each character has a skill tree as well, though I haven't explored it yet. The game is pretty easy without upgrading with the enemy AI being pretty brain dead and the maps being somewhat barren.  I'd recommend you crank up the difficulty for a slight challenge.Seems like people are complaining about performance.I'm playing at 1440p; 7800x3d, 7900 xtx, 32GB DDR 6000 @ Ultra.  Runs decent with highs at 145 and lows around 100 FPS.  No upscaling.  There is some minor, but very infrequent stutter present.Always disable motion blur.The game loads ultra fast; Less than 15 seconds to get in game after launch.Redfall is an OK romp.  Though, ironically, it's kind of lifeless.  It's not bad, per se, it's just not great.  Is is worth picking up?  Sure.  For $70.  That's debatable.  I haven't tried co-op, so maybe that's where it's at.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get straight to the point, I bought this knowing It was too good to be true. So many advertisements and CGI trailers for marketing leading up to a pretty disappointing gameplay experience.AI Is pretty busted, a lot of the time the vampires can't even get down from house roofs. Close combat feels super clunky because there's no "dodge" button In the game, so you're stuck running In a circle around the enemies waiting for them to take a swing and miss to then continue attacking.Optimization Is just non-existent, like I cannot believe this got the green light atleast for the PC version.Textures pop In and out. Now this Is something that gets on my nerves really quick In games, If you got textures popping In and out because you tried limiting the stress on peoples computers by not rendering things a set distance away from the player that's all fine. Lots of big games stop rendering things that the player can't see anyways, but we got an Issue when you're not rendering things the player CAN see and STILL lag optimization. It's just a disaster honestly.Gunplay Is fine.The Eagle dude Is semi okay too, that's the only one I've played so far.Skill tree Is fine, no Issues there. Map Is terrible, I get the artstyle they went for that's fine and all. But the map could reaaally use some love on the Information side, It feels way too bland and just empty. Settings could use some looking too. Why does controls under settings not an an option to scale the ADS sensitivity?. Game has no fps limiter besides Vsync.Loot that you can find In the world has NO Indicator whether It can be picked up or not until you mouse over It, this means you have to mouse over everything to find out whether It can be picked up a not. Looking at the artstyle I think It'd have been perfect to have a small white'ish border around Items that's Interactable, this would save so much time and headache. Overall for the 70/90$ I gave for this game I would have guessed a lot of the above would have been the most basic things to have In check before release, I cannot recommend the game at all In Its current state. It has a LOT of fixing to do, I'll be finishing the whole game and side stuff and then most likely update this review with further things that could use some work etc If any but that's about It for now.an overall 2/10 score from me, gunplay Is the sole thing keeping me bare minimum Interested atleast until I've gotten my moneys worth In playtime. Take care everyone.
