_childDocuments_.review: I would be even more negative about this game if it had not come free with graphics card and I paid money.  Boy it's got issues.  Many I could overlook.  Like all good reviewers I'll share what I was looking for so you can decide for yourself if you'd feel the same.  I have a zombie slaying posse that plays Back 4 Blood regularly and for the most part really enjoy the "jump in and kill a bunch of things together" vibe of that.  Our collective hope was that we could go from "zombies to vampires" and keep it up.  Sadly that is not the case.  I'll mention first that if you watch the IGN review (gent with Aussie accent I believe) he sums up pretty much everything I didn't like about game.   But to summarize in my own words here's the negatives first: - Boring gameplay marred with horrible enemy AI - Multiplayer as of now only lets HOST progress.  This is where it diverges from B4B the most.  The nice thing about the B4B "act" structure was if you played through a level mid-act with friends hosting, it would be "cleared" for everyone (so even if you go back to solo play, etc, that level is now cleared at that difficulty).  In Redfall, potentially because of how they structured missions, etc. maybe that was just too difficult or they didn't think it through.  Not sure what to blame, I just know the game play is way too boring to keep going back to sections you've played through already with friends. - Repetitive Use of Game Assets: I get that after dozens of hours in any game you'll see repeating textures, models, etc. but just in the intro tutorial level on the starting location (boat) you find the same "dead girl in beige sweater", in exact same pose numerous times.  And worse, you MEET her alive later when you clear the first "home base" as part of that same introductory level.  - You have to repeat the intro level for every character you want to swap out.  I have mixed feelings about making people replay from level 0 just to switch characters.  If it was more fun to replay maybe I wouldn't care so much- Mobility - stiff.  I'll give you an example:  Jumping over objects, like a guard rail in the road.  Most games give you more flexibility to do that at canted angles vs having to face the object you are vaulting straight on.  So this means if you are running parallel down a road with enemies ahead and you want to vault something to your left but still see the enemies, you have to turn 90 degrees and face the guard rail.  I feel like this is just poorly implemented.  Noticeably annoying. - Sliding: you slide for days. Not horrible, just a bit longer than some other games I've playedSo in summary, there's a lot to fix.  Lots of bugs (I'm hearing from review, I got too bored to find them myself) and bad AI.  Sadness.

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed the game twice now after very casually playing through it solo and taking my time to do all the missions I could find. TLDR, I still recommend this game, flaws and all, though I think it should really only be a $40 game. I think the $70 price tag is really steep, especially for what's on offer. Regardless, if you want to know more, I'll get more in depth in the following paragraphs.I'm probably one of a few people who like the game. This is not a hard game in any way, its really more of a casual romp through a decent open world, sometimes you get "spooky" things to happen, but nothing truly scary will ever hit you. Its best to view the game from the perspective of a really low budget adventure-horror movie protagonist, where the enemies are just thrown into the meat grinder that is the hero.If I had to say anything that I truly disliked about the game, its actually the music, it jumps up at really random times, and not in an exciting or "spooky" way. You'll snipe a single guy and intense combat music jumps up for like 5 seconds before cutting away, kind of jarring. The game also has a rough time performance wise because as you move around the map, it has to load things in, and that typically can cause a good second or two of lag when entering a new neighborhood (zone) or if a large number of enemies spawn in due to story. If they could improve the performance of the game, that would help it drastically. I encountered a very small number of bugs, such as staking specific objectives while crouching causing me to get stuck under the environment, or occasionally being unable to crouch after leaving a Psychic Vampire Nest. Annoyances at best, nothing game ruining.It feels like a Dead Island game but maybe a bit bigger? Cultists are the most common threat on the island, but the fun part is the Vampires. Basically just always have a shotgun on hand so you can abuse the stake attachment and you're set. My ideal loadout would probably be an automatic rifle, a shotgun, and the UV lazer for all around good coverage. The UV lazer slowly petrifies vampires, letting you instantly kill them with melee. The lazer is also pretty much necessary to deal with environmental hazards the Vampires leave in areas, which is more of a very minor inconvenience, and at some points I've actually enjoyed the challenge of dissecting a large area of all its hazards with the lazer; just wish there was a cheaper alternative, like a flashlight upgrade or something.Staking vampires is very satisfying and I find myself occasionally picking fights with groups of vampires just because I like the staking, its very nice. You can also get equipment after a certain point in the game that grants you decent boons, one of which is "Regain x% of health when killing a Vampire." Its worth it to continuously bum rush Vampire Nests just to get equipment with this modifier on it, because the staking animation gives you invincibility frames, allowing you to quickly heal off the kill and then tanking hits from any other vampires in the vicinity.The AI is definitely a bit jank for cultists but most Vampires have no issue getting right up in your face and making sure you understand why its a problem. I have beaten the game, all bosses and enemies defeated, and honest to god the only enemies that I disliked were the "Anglers" and the final boss. Angler's straight up just suck ass, if you got caught with an empty clip, prepare to lose a chunk of health. The Final Boss was really more of a set piece, which is a shame because I really enjoyed shooting up all the other bosses; if the developers had simply split it into phases with a real tangible health bar it would've been much cooler.I'm almost certain that the devs fully expected people to play this with friends as opposed to alone because once or twice I got a dialogue line that was definitely meant to be played in a lobby instead of in solo mode. Wasn't a big issue honestly, more of an interesting quirk. A good number of perks in your perk tree also mention helping allies, or you might have things that mention buffing allies in a radius, so yeah definitely feels like they expected people to go in a group instead of solo. Editing this paragraph post game completion, there's literally achievements that can only be obtained by playing with others and raising "trust" with their characters, so yes, definitely expected people to be playing this multiplayer instead of alone.As a final note, I'm not sure all of the characters are built equally; I picked Jacob as my Hero instead of Devinder because I wanted a more stealthy approach to combat, and originally I regretted that but I don't mind it so much anymore. A lot of Jacob's abilities sound really good if you had them fully upgraded, but upgrading them is a chore because higher level upgrades demand multiple perk points to activate; its much better to just get all the base upgrades asap on all of the abilities instead. This frustrates me a bit more than it should because it feels like I'm purposely being gate kept from playing with the upgrades I want; I suppose that I could hold off on getting cheaper upgrades to get higher level upgrades, but then I'm weaker over all for a whole 'nother level, which is a bad plan in a Dead Island style game. This really might just be a me issue though, not sure how others feel on the subject.Back to Devinder, he has a number of abilities that just seem so much better than what most of the other characters have. The player doesn't exactly lack for firepower, so what it really comes down to is how easily you can manage a group of enemies, and I think that Devinder would probably be the best for it. The fact that one of his abilities literally just dunks a UV light ray probably makes him the best right off the bat because it absolutely destroys vampires and if I had to hazard a guess, it probably works against environmental vampire hazards which means you could carry a 3rd gun of your choice instead of having to  carry the UV lazer just in case you need it.I'd have maybe given Layla a shot if it weren't for the fact that her abilities annoy me, and the combat Engineer looks cool but as I mentioned before, you don't need extra firepower and the AI for cultists is so jank already that there's no need to distract them. The reason I give Jacob a passing grade is because his abilities ♥♥♥♥ even more with the enemy AI, even vampires, and his Hero ability to summon the ghost gun is really strong; it can outright kill vampires without having to stake them, even if they need a few shots to go down.Closing statement, I enjoy the game, its definitely a different kind of game than Arkane's other stuff, I think its rather reminiscent of Dead Island with the loot, healing, weapons, and world over all. I've enjoyed my time so far, but realistically I got my enjoyment out of it at the 30 hour mark. Nests ended up being my favorite thing to do, just running in and splaffing the heart as fast as possible. I still recommend this game as I've stated before, but they need to reduce the base price significantly; there's just not enough content here to justify the $70 price tag. Again, not a reduced price via sale, but a flat reduction of the base price. $40 dollars is the honorable thing to do, $50 is the economic thing to do.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: IT'S DEAD. Arkane Austin is now defunct and the promised DLC has been cancelled. If you bought the DLC with money, expect a refund or compensation of some kind. Servers are up for now but they will be shut down at some point. I think offline mode will be added, but you're better off playing any other singleplayer game.If you weren't sold on this game during the previews, your skepticism was well-placed. This game falls flat in a lot of areas. The promise of epic vampire slaying is, in reality, mostly dealing with human cultists and getting swarmed by vampires when you enter a house and trying to not run out of ammo.>CharactersYou get to pick from four (with two more on the way that will be available for a price) characters. They each have their own backstory, abilities, and unique lines when interacting with characters. This aspect isn't terrible, although I feel like these characters don't offer much introduction and found it difficult to find them likable.You get several skill trees but there are only so many points in the game. Want to re-spec? Not an option. Roll a new character and do it . This is not helped by the fact that XP is not awarded for killing enemies but rather completing quests, furthering the disconnect between what the game is trying to be.This is also a HUGE issue when you have skills that are worthless if you are playing solo, only providing benefits to interacting with other players.>WeaponsMeh. They shoot but they don't feel particularly meaningful. The vampire-slaying weapons are cool but you run out of ammo easily. I saw footage of the UV-blasting weapon and it seemed... boring. This isn't helped by the fact that the game seems to be stingy about not giving automatic weapons to low-leveled players, which are the most fun.>Open-WorldThis is the weakest link of the game. Enemies are scattered about in weird places standing around or coming out of the trees, almost like the game is actively planting them in your way to throw you off. This is not helped by the fact that the game's world is tiny by open-world standards.The experience is similar to Far Cry, where safehouses are the default location to pick up new missions that will progress an area and unlock more content. Unfortunately, it falls flat where Far Cry normally succeeds in gameplay.>User ExperienceThis game did not invest heavily into good player design. From the moment you pick up your first gun, the game will pause and force you to read a wall of text on how to shoot. This happens several times whenever you discover a new mechanic. At most, these should be brief text boxes that show up in the HUD for a short time. In short, a lot of telling and not much showing.Even before getting into the menu, being hit with a character select screen was not something I was expecting. I just got the game, why am I being asked to pick a character? I have options to set first!Outside of that nonsense, the main menu's design felt bland, which was actually my first red flag while I was setting the options. Boring font, boring menus, etc. Something felt off for sure.>StoryAside from the basic intro and a few missions, I did not get far into the story before calling it quits. I just wasn't into the game enough to care.That being said, the story feels watered down by how cheap the production feels. The intro cutscene is a slideshow and voiceover. The same happens later in the game but with still 3D models. That's right, no animated cutscenes in a $70 game.I knew something was wrong when the entire firehouse was being rebuilt instantly by characters that I had never met moments after clearing it. While this is a thing in Far Cry after clearing a major location, it feels cheap to do this for what is essentially your main base of operations.>MusicI don't like trap music, even if it's mixed with church bells. I don't think it works but that's just my opinion.>MultiplayerYou can do this game solo, if you wish. The game has a way of balancing difficulty with more players if you choose to bring friends. Just be warned that any progress you make in someone else's game will only progress the host's main story.This is not something I would like to see as it disincentivizes co-op gameplay and may potentially be used as a way of padding out game time, forcing players to complete the same content again.>BUGSI didn't get much time in before calling it quits but I saw a floating object in a cutscene and a vampire that was in a state of undeath, moreso than usual. Stuck vampires seem to be a problem a lot of other views are reporting as well.I did not have major framerate issues, but I am running on a 4090. Consoles have not been so lucky, being stuck to 30 fps.>Final WordsI wanted this game to be good, I really did. I like the idea of fighting vampires in the modern age with homemade implements of destruction, but something must have happened in development. If this is the product we got after a year's delay, I shudder to imagine what it looked like before.In short, this very much feels like something that would be given to play testers instead of a finished game. _childDocuments_.review: Redfall - Bite Back Edition ..... is a game.Oh.  Should maybe say some more huh?  Okay.The basics of an Open World Loot-n-Shoot with story elements RPGish game are present.  The world can seem empty, but more target rich or loot filled would unbalance the game play.  Leaning to maintain stealth, ADS toggle, and other QoL options would make this game better.  The skill tree may be okay, but have not leveled enough to see how it works.  I wish some crafting, and weapon modding, had been implemented.  Story is interesting, and I am hoping to learn more.  I am not sure if this is a graphic or game mechanic problem but enviromental damage (fire, explosions, etc) are not always easy to notice.  I walk into a burning area that looked more like fluttering dead leaves.  So for this far I remain middle ground of Redfall is a game, and some may like it.As for the graphics I will say that things did not work as I expected.  The optimized preset for my hardware did not work well.  My rig is okay: AMD Ryzen 5900X, 32 GB DDR4 3600Mhz, AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, NVME SSD, Win10 22H2.  Monitor is a 2560x1440 144Hz display.  It was 40 - 60 fps with grainy odd looking textures.  Eventually I got this to improve to 144 fps avg.  Turning off FSR/resolution scaling was the first big help.  Then I could tweak other setting to where I tend to run games.  Hitching is still a minor thing.  Also minor visual effects that do not look right (some flames, random item physics).  Not sure if Nvidia problems are for the same reasons.So I plan to wait and see how things improve.  I will thumbs up, but this is a very minor thumbs up.  Bethsoft and Arkane make good games.  Seems more time for quality will be needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after 55+ hours. So have got to the end and completed the game once over in 'Dusk' difficulty level and all the side missions + neighbourhoods. I'll admit to not reading all the little notes and I found about 60 of the 100 grave notes. I'll admit to really loving the game in the end and got addicted eventually, but only after the first 5 or 6 hours of play. I don't know what it is about the early experience of it that put me off, but once I was in control, I started to settle in and couldn't put it down.I loved the game mechanics, despite a handful of minor bugs here and there (I did pick the game up for the first time 12 months post release, so I guess most things people complained about were fixed).It's pretty immersive, the art direction is pretty incredible, loved the music - Story could have been a little better, but you do get into it more by "Burial Point" (which is the 2nd area map / set of neighbourhoods).Looking at my game achievement scores, I can see that only 12% of people who buy this game complete it and a lot of the achievements have very low player percentage of achievement, which is a shame really. Think more people should have given the game a chance and I'm pretty surprised by the 'mostly negative' reviews.If you're sitting on the fence about it, I would say the game doesn't disappoint. It's entertaining to play, especially with a friend and we both loved it. Most of the negativity is related to the first 12 months where the game was released at full price as a 'finished' game, but was largely buggy and incomplete. Those issues have since been resolved for the most part (although some minor bugs still remain end of May 2024).--Update after 18 hours:  So, I have to say, I am enjoying this game. The negative rep this game has attracted is not the sum of its parts in my opinion. I'm playing along with a friend and neither of us can understand why people find it awful. It's a fun shooter. I suppose they could have gone full horror with it, but to be honest I quite like the cheeky lightheartedness of it. That's just a matter of personal styling, I think it would work either way. There's plenty of variety to keep you immersed in the game. The loot you're picking up to gain cash which you can use to buy better weapons if available at the safe houses, restock on ammo, etc.I like the different missions, the music design is well thought out and I personally like the graphics.There are a few glitches here and there, opening some of the locked cases, the sliding instead of walking of team mates sometimes... But to be honest they are very small, not really noticeable and don't ruin the overall enjoyment of the game.If this is still available at a low price, I would say the game is a steal and definitely worth the money.----So I've played around three hours or so and I don't consider this game to be as bad as a lot are still saying. It seems people are hating on it just because the pitchforks are out, or maybe it got off to a bad start almost a year ago now. I know I'm late to the party, but I'm enjoying this version as it stands so far. I wouldn't say it's the best game I've ever played, but I certainly don't dislike it by any stretch. So what do I like and dislike?Well I got it on offer for £14.99 and in my opinion, it's definitely worth that. I like the story, I like the artwork and scenery. The missions are interesting and I'm enjoying the exchange of fire with vamps and hollowmen! So in terms of beauty and entertainment, I'd say it gets high marks.So where is it failing? I'm playing solo game coop with a friend and we're having a lot of fun... But, the reward/loot factor is too high - We're always fully stocked up and so the challenge diminishes. This game has a balance problem and I think they could do with addressing that. I've only played a few hours, so I'm early into third or fourth mission, so the challenge could get harder...(?)The music and sound design is excellent, love that. But the sound direction feels off. It's a bit disorientating hearing an enemy behind, but it's not there at all. Maybe that's just me, not sure.I'll be sure to come back and add to my review after a few more hours and missions in. But so far, if you're sitting on the fence, I'd say go for it. There's a lot worse games out there at higher prices. Redfall deserves another chance!

_childDocuments_.review: About 6 years ago i was in a bad car accident that left me paralysed from the neck down and mute. My only real, effective way of communicating is by blinking (once for yes, twice for no etc). I have always been a huge gamer and my brother has too. When i lost the ability to play for myself i fell into a spiralling depression. All those hours i spent with steam friends, all those amazing memories, never to be repeated. My brother, bless him, picked up on this and offered to play the games I wanted to FOR me while i sat behind him in my wheelchair and watched. With tears in my eyes i agreed and i have been playing vicariously through him ever since. When Redfall was announced we both became super hyped and i couldn't wait to watch him play it. After pre-ordering it and waiting about 3 weeks the wait was almost over. He pre-loaded the game and after 2 more excruciating days of waiting we finally got to play it. He wheeled me into my favourite spot just behind my old computer chair loaded it up and selected our character. After watching him play for 4 agonizing hours i couldn't take it anymore, with the holy will of God himself i screamed internally at my muscles to obey me, I just needed them this one last time, I had to make it stop. With every ounce of strength i had I slowly pushed myself out of that wheelchair and hobbled over to the computer. Not knowing how long this divine power would last i shoved my brother aside and desperately fumbled with the mouse and keyboard to write a refund request. As i watched and waited for my confirmation e-mail with tears in my eyes i knew that while my body had been healed, my mind would never be the same. God bless you Arkane Austin for giving me my autonomy back.

_childDocuments_.review: Redfall is, for all intents and purposes, a game without a purpose designed by committee. It is hard to believe anyone had any creative vision that was poured into this playable nothingness.Its threadbare story serves only to connect playable point A to point B. It has little dramatic arc, as its main characters are not personally invested in what's happening, even though voice acting might melodramatically try to convince one otherwise, as a character's voice cracks while describing events that could pretend to rattle a bleeding heart teenager. The truth is that playable characters have only the barest of connections to the game's plot: they stand to gain nothing, are there out of literal obligation, and do not change or explore any aspects of their personality through the course of the game. Secondary characters, though more involved in the town's tribulations, are too absent to develop anything but suggestions of a personality, and, compelling as some of these might be, they are given so little breathing room that they, more often than not, amount to nothing.When one is out in the world, they might run into enemy humans or vampires: humans pose little to no challenge, as most die with one or two shots to the head, and do not move around enough to make this task difficult. Vampires have more resilience, and have to be finished off either with a stake, fire, lightning, or UV lights. Most will try to rush the player, and can deal decent damage up-close, making encounters with them a little more engaging once they come in larger numbers. There are a few special types of vampires, but these rarely force the player to change their tactics around, safe for one who creates an area of limited visibility around the player, and tries to flee while throwing projectiles, forcing the player to switch roles and give chase, and one who has rotating shields, forcing the player to be more precise in aiming, lest they waste their (frankly abundant) resources.These encounters run out of steam rather fast, as the game fails to throw any further curveballs down the line, and encounters increasingly become annoyances that serve only to interrupt the pace. The other side of the game is exploration, but the game very much discourages it. The only thing of value to find in its world are safehouses and historical markers, both of which are already marked on the player's map, so they might make a  beeline for them immediately. Once a mission is started, it, too, is marked on your map and one is given very little reason to take any detours. The only thing one might find in active exploration is ammunition and healthpacks, both of which can be replenished at one of the safehouses that dot the map anyway for very little in exchange, dry notes left behind by the unseen inhabitants of Redfall that fail to either add texture or suggest a sense of loss, or guns than more often than not are worse than anything you might be carrying. Should one try to ignore markers and objectives, they will find themselves at a loss, since there is very little visually distinct about Redfall that might orient the player to anything interesting, and objectives sometimes give so little direction, that one is forced to rely on markers anyway.I can think of very few reasons to play Redfall. It adds nothing to anything, everything it does, others do better. It serves only to spend (or more accurately, waste) time, it has nothing to say for itself, nothing distinct about its story, gameplay, or visuals. One would be correct in thinking fixing the bugs or developing content for this playable bread sandwitch to be a waste of effort, money, and time.

_childDocuments_.review: In the short time that I have played, Redfall has been a legitimately boring experience. I have no desire to hop aboard a hate train for clout or to go wherever the wind is blowing, thoughts are my own.The AI is ridiculously stupid, the world feels empty and devoid of any substance, gun-play is mediocre at best and if anything, feels stiff compared to other FPS titles I've played over the years. I don't care about any of the characters because the game right now hasn't done a good enough job of getting me to give a damn about them. I'm not expecting deep characterisation in under two hours, but I expect to want to get invested into the world & characters and nothing about it so far has been even REMOTELY compelling.Most of my time has been spent running from bland location to bland location, looting cans of spaghetti hoops and cereal boxes that auto-convert to funds, of which I've used to buy lockpicks and re-wire tools to get mostly boring loot. The skill-tree is also uninteresting. I came across a locked door and looked around the property to see if there was a clever or interesting way to break in. Nope, turns out I can just smash the front window next to the door and climb in, then unlock the door from the inside. Maybe there are some interesting puzzle locations in the game that reward outside of the box thinking, but I hadn't found it yet. I came across a safe-house where the power generator was locked in a shed behind a locked door, I saw a small window, climbed up on something and thought maybe I could hit something to turn it on or do something to open the garage door to get in? Nah, nothing at all, unless I missed it and I'm just stupid.Performance is also not the best. Running an RX 6600 + Ryzen 5600, I kept it on medium settings and found that the game all over the place performance wise. Sometimes it'd run smooth, then it would stutter or hitch, there was noticeable texture pop-in as well. Bugs all over the place, I've walked into locations where the enemies have no health bars and didn't even notice I was there, no reaction, shoot them and nothing happens, I had no idea whether that was a bug or feature but I assume it's the former.AI is a comical joke, imagine being excited to finally get some in-game action, only to be met with what feels like some of the most primitive AI I've seen in modern day. They aren't particularly threatening, nor do they make me think about how to utilise the environment or skills.I'm sorry, this needed more time in the oven. Whether it was six months to a year, doesn't matter. I'm glad I won this via a competition and didn't fork out £60 for it. Why waste that kind of money on modern AAA games when they're like this, when I could spend a third of that on early access games and end up with better results? I'll continue to play as I have mates that wanna vibe on it, but I don't recommend paying £60 / $70 for it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated: Okay, well, given that they actually bothered to do an update and address a lot of issues with the game, I'm gonna go ahead and change this to a recommended stance. Is it worth full price? No. It can definitely be a fun game though. If the devs keep listening to criticism and updating, it can only get better.-----I'll start off by saying... If you have people to play with, or enjoy just solo stuff and shooting things, this is an "eh" kind of game. It's a game. It's fun to play a game. That's all this is. It's not terrible, it's not great. It's not like it hurts me to play it, I've actually been having an alright time with the game so far, but... I got the game for free, so... If you can get it for free too, go wild. I would recommend trying it out if you can get it without paying 70 bucks. If you just have 70 bucks that you want to blow on something though, sure, why not. If you don't have friends that want to play this with you, and don't want to just play solo. Well... Just forget this game exists. There's no matchmaking. That already is a complete interest killer for a ton of people.I haven't had any crazy bugs, crashes, or anything, and the AI is... I mean, the AI is about as threatening as any Far Cry game, it's not very smart. You can snipe a dude's friend's face off right in front of him and he'll just stand there like nothing happened. If you're looking for difficulty, yeah, not here. I've tried the game's settings on easy, medium, and hard, and I see very little differences. I have yet to see what the super hard option is like, but hey, considering what I've seen so far, and what I've heard other people say, I doubt it's going to be that much harder.This game... It's not worth 70 dollars. I will say that for sure. It's a alright game, but it's a 20 dollar purchase, easily. As it is, at this current price, without matchmaking... I'd give it a pass. If you can get it cheap, or on gamepass, cool. If not? Pass on it. Go play Vermintide or something.I like this game's concept. I'd like to see it work. It's just not working right now.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:I can't see that there was 70 bucks worth of development done on this game. I barely see 20 bucks worth of development at this point.   They need to go on a hardcore fixing spree and add something to make the game coherent in what it wants to be, because mediocre(when it works) is all it's managing right now.This game has all the bones of a game that could be awesome, but these bones just aren't connected in any logical way. you can sneak, but being sneaky doesn't benefit you--every weapon is a gun and every nearby enemy gets alerted the second you shoot. the enemy AI is bad, it feels several generations behind.  The idea of vampire strongholds is great, they just don't affect the environment or enemies around them enough to feel different from anything else.The classes don't distinguish themselves from each other enough to make the choice meaningful. The best tactic for everything is shoot enemies in the head as quickly as possible. There's no tangible benefit for any class being close or far away, there's no reason to apply any tactics as a group.Bugs!It seems enemies don't spawn properly. Scopes and reticles don't load properly, sliding gets you stuck in the ground. enemies get stuck in walls. This game needed a serious playtest before launch.Critical strikes are too strong, with head shots on a 150 damage weapon doing 1500 damage. This might be a great thing if there was enough enemy diversity that finding the critical spot was a core mechanic, but as it sits, it's shoot everything in the head or they're bullet sponges.Very poorly optimized, stutters, pop ins, framerate issues. It feels like they didn't playtest anything.

_childDocuments_.review: At present I would only give Redfall a 6/10 and recommend waiting for a sale.Here is my reasoning:I have been a fan of Arkane since the release of Dishonored, which I thought for the time was rather unique and innovative. Dishonored II then really fleshed out the specialness of that universe while building upon an already solid foundation. Every time I play either one, I am intrigued by the lore, architecture, and allover aesthetic, so much so that I am hoping for another game (but we shall see.) But then came PREY! My god was that game an underrated work of art. From the beginning I was absolutely drawn in and immersed! I remember forgoing sleep just so that I could progress a bit farther the first day of release. It is a beautiful, startingly distinctive game that I have played for more hours than I care to admit. The neo-deco architecture, alone, was enough to reel anyone in, never mind the actual gameplay, and the requisite and beloved Arkane “play your way.” Deathloop, initially, I thought was a bit of let down; however, once a year had passed and a major update was released, I revisited the game and played it for two weeks. This game, too, revealed Arkane’s ability to create fascinating worlds and addictive gameplay. I also count this as a triumph for the studio.Then we come to Redfall, which I already had reservations about considering I knew it was going to be coop (sorry, but imo a lot of us are introverted enough that this is not appealing, but certainly each to their own); yet, I was excited because Arkane had yet to fail me. I will not go so far as to say they have failed, rather I will say that they released an incomplete game that needed a lot more work despite having already been delayed. Somehow this game looks less realistic than Deathloop (which was released in 2021), and the world of Redfall, while being significantly more interesting than the world of Forspoken (wow was that a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game), pales in comparison to more recent open world releases like Horizon Forbidden West or Ghost of Tsushima, or even Ghostwire: Tokyo. The cut scenes are just drawings, the stealth kill is an absolute joke devoid of any significance, and the powers—though awesome—are somehow forgettable. While I do like the atmosphere that Refall is creating, I think it would have benefited from a fall release when we all are in the mood for Halloween and the general creepy atmosphere of that time of the year. The moodiness seems somehow too dichotomous to May, but I guess they had already delayed it enough (I’m being facetious—they obviously had not delayed it enough). On another note, I am irritated by the game’s character creation restrictiveness. Where it claims again to be “play your way,” only allowing certain powers to be accessed by playing certain characters is not “the way I would play.” Furthermore, though the vampires are intriguing, they quickly become boring and predictable, and rarely are frightening or too threatening. As always, the voice acting is superb, but the architecture and design aesthetic is mediocre and rarely innovative, and—at times—also forgettable.I do appreciate that Arkane Austin was attempting to do something new and that should always be applauded, but I believe despite having ample time to work on the project the game somehow still needs more time to cook. In fact, as it is now, it could have been released into Early Access and I think it would have been more liked. Do as you please, of course, but I recommend waiting for a discount if you are not in the mood to spend $70 on an incomplete game.

_childDocuments_.review: Things that are good:- Gameplay: Different classes and their abilities are fun! The variety at which I can go at enemies isn't a new formula for Arkane, but enjoyable in this game like their others.- Freedom of movement: Again, like in other Arkane games, the ability to sneak, climb, and move about freely allows me to decide when and where I want to engage enemies.- Variety of guns: My favorite so far has got to be the UV gun and crisping up the vamps for shattering! Hopefully they add more later, I think a modified brass knuckles with a stake would be hilarious fun at some point.Things that need work:- Loot: finding a gold weapon every few minutes make them seem less special, and I shouldn't find them in random bags that don't require a lockpick/wiring kit. Perhaps tweaking the %'s at which certain loot is dropped can help with this.- AI: definitely needs improving, enemies run into walls a lot!- Optimization: I have a 3070, i7 10700K (4.0Ghz), and 32 gigs of ram and on avg I get between 70-80 fps on Ultra settings, but it certainly dips to 30 fps on cluttered fights and looking at the big water wave in the distance (and that's with DLSS on). Definitely needs some work here to ensure a bit smoother gameplay across the board.- Enemy density: at times it feels TOO empty, but on certain fights feels overwhelming. There should be some tweaking here. I'm not saying there needs to be enemies on every street corner, but also I shouldn't feel like there suddenly an overwhelming tide of baddies because I want to check out a new POI.- Progression: Give players who join their friends the option to tie progression to the host or not (at least with new characters). - Back and forth banter between characters: feels repetitive at times is all, I will have to see if it improves with the "trust" building system Overall the game is a great time in co-op, haven't played it much solo though beyond the intro mission. A lot of the extra lore bits feel unnecessary, but I understand it is part of the world building. I would say pick it up, but maybe wait until some tweaks are made, or price drops. I personally don't feel like it is a waste of $70 because me and my spouse are having a lot of fun together in the game, but others who are solo playing or saving money, may want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a parody of a triple-A game made by a parody of a studio released by a parody of a publisher that is owned by Microsoft who feel like a parody in themselves when it comes to gaming.As many others mentioned before, Redfall plays like a 20€ - 30€ early access game created by an indie developer who hasn't really figured out yet what sort of generic game they want to make.It tries to be a shooter, but the mechanics are basically worse than those of many games from 10 - 15 years ago.It tries to be a story driven adventure, but lacks both an interesting story and any engaging storytelling outside constant voice-overs and a lot of dull flashbacks.It tries to be an open-world game, but the world itself feels surprisingly static, without much sense of wonder and barely any reason for exploration beyond the main story missions.It tries to be a stealth game during many missions, but once you bring a couple of friends with you pretty much everything can be and will be steamrolled.It tries to be a multi-player game, or it was at least marketed as one, but it even lacks basic features one would expect from an always online single-player game. It tries to be a game about Vampires, but neither re-invents their interactions or depiction nor conforms to the long established norms of the genre.If one looks a bit closer at some of the mechanics and past the bugs, glitches or quirks, one has to wonder if the studio could have made a decent game with another year or two of development time or if we finally have entered the era of gaming where people happily pay for perceived quantity of content over any resemblance of quality of that content in video games.Maybe MS goes for a "No Man's Sky"-style rework of this game, but personally I'd guess some game devs in Austin will be looking for a new studio soon.At least Redfail has also some funny moments... finding PlayStations placed in the game world fits this lackluster XBox exclusive very well.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the Dishonored games and Prey, but Redfall is not ready for release. It seems like an alpha at best. I bought the game because I liked Arkane Studios previous games, but now will be more careful about buying them on the release date in the future. The game should have either been released as a lower cost alpha, or should not have been released until finished.The story is boring, almost absent, and there is no real interaction with the other characters. The so-called story is just narration over bad still images. Characters in the game just stand there and look at you and there is no sense of interaction. Most of the town is just an empty place with houses and stores that you can't enter. No throwable explosives or any other such things. Lots of glitches where the game just stops working and you can't complete the mission, forcing a restart. I am fairly certain that many people at Arkane were very upset with management that this game was going to be released at this price range when it was in this horrible a condition. I just hope these many negative reviews from Arkane fans will get the out-of -touch management at these game studios to stop doing this to their fans. _childDocuments_.review: Updated after 55 hours of gameplaySolid 8/10 game. Recommending because it's been fun for me and i've really got a huge amount of enjoyment out of this game. Despite what people think this is very much an Arkane game with lots of their style and gameplay elements littered if you just give it some time and go looking for them.You can't play this game like its Division. Neither is it Left 4 Dead. Its an Arkane game with some looting RNG. But primarily this game is about the story. It is about finding different ways to aproach a situation and it is about exploring the game world for the huge amount of detail and care the developers have put into it. Only then will you uncover a trully wonderful game that falls a little flat of its ambitions. But a great game is still there for those that can look past the few bugs. Coop is way more of a mess. I play mostly single player and experience very few bugs. I tried coop and it was filled with all kinds of bugs.What i see here is Sea of Thieves at launch. A game that has potential and has been crafted with love and ambition but that has fallen a little flat. I believe if the developers are given more time and support from Microsoft they can turn this into something really wonderful. That said with many many hours of gameplay, the more time you give this game the more it will give you back. The more i play the more i love it and i'm still not bored. I look forward to playing this at the end of each day when i've finished work and the kids are in bed.Are there issues? YesDoes the game feel somewhat half baked in places? YesIs it as terrible as the discussions or steam reviews want you to believe? Not at all. The main issue is at the price point its horribly underwhelming and from a studio like Arkane people expected much more.Games like Dishonored, Prey or even Deathloop were unique worlds and instantly fun and different and while its great to see the Arkane style out in an open world and its nice to see them try something new it just lacks some of the stuff that really makes an Arkane game great.  The environment and atmosphere are all fantastic and the game feels creepy. The storytelling is also wonderful but you have to work for it. It's like a big book that is difficult to get into but once you allow yourself to be come immersed the more it gives you back in return. For example, one of the best legendary perk pickups in the game isn't signposted. You may or may not come across a house with some clues and locked doors. You then can choose to follow the clues and read notes to uncover a pretty chilling and grim tale of three sisters who murdered a sibling as an offering. In return you get a really powerful legendary. But none of this is handed to you or signposted.There are plenty of things like this throughout the game. Nothing is handed to you other than the main questline and even this has pieces you really have to slow down and pay attention to or notes to read or recordings to listen to if you want the full picture. For me that is great. I love it as it immerses you into the world and it all feels very Arkane.Graphically its fine. Its stylised. Its Arkane through and through. Some have performance issues. For me i get a smooth locked 60fps at 4k on max settings which is just fine. I get the occasional dip once in a while which i presume is the game loading some stuff and in a couple of very wide areas with alot going on my frames might drop but none of this has hampered gameplay in any way. As with all games this stuff will improve over patches and driver updates over time.At first the class system felt dull to me but as you unlock deeper skill variants and learn how to use them in different ways each character has its own very unique play style. I'm playing two characters and really enjoying both right now. I'm looking forward to seeing what the other two characters will bring to the table.I also hope that they add another map to the game but somehow i don't see that happening as it would be a pretty huge undertaking.Are there improvements needed?Yes. Of course. Lots of the broad complaints are valid. The way people are going about making them is not. Its childish and indicitive of a very problematic issue that plagues gaming communites. People have no clue how to interact or behave. This is an issue you see over every game launch and getting worse over time. Steam harbors this toxic behaviour and does nothing to stem it. I'd be surprised if the devs bothered to even read some of the stuff posted here just because of how its being presented. The irony is if these things were presented in a sensible fashion they might actually get listened to.Right now their behaviour is no different from a toddler who doesn't get exactly what they want so they have a tantrum and then get even more upset because they don't understand why no one takes them seriously.Regardless i'm happy that Arkane were given the space to try something new and i hope that they are given the space to turn it into something even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Bethesda lives down to its reputation.(1) We "pre-loaded" the game over the weekend so we'd be ready to play on Monday. Nope. We all had to re-download all 77 GB. So... what was the point of giving us the opportunity to pre-load?(2) My version crashed when I first ran it, then crashed again when I tried to use the Steam overlay to join my friends. All of us have had at least one crash in under 2 hours of play.(3) My version skipped the 5-minute intro scene, which is minor, but I *like* watching cut scenes so I was disappointed having to sit there in the ferry waiting for my friends to finish the scene.(4) We finally managed to get to the fire station, at which point the game completely bugged out. There were no enemies, we couldn't interact with anything, and the quest line started progressing as we walked through rooms. "Defeat the cultists?" Check, without firing a shot. "Rescue the captives?" Success! Even though we never saw them. We quit out for the night.(5) Today my friends tried to start up again with new characters. Nope. The game remembers everything you picked up as your old character, so they couldn't even get off the ferry because all the guns had already been looted.Long story short, between the four of us we've had six crashes, had to restart the campaign three times, haven't managed to even make it to the fire station with the game working, and haven't managed to go 5 minutes without some interactable object being bugged out.Dare I say this launch is WORSE than Fallout 76?==================UPDATE AFTER FINDING WORKAROUNDS FOR THE BUGS:(1) To play multiplayer at all, we learned that you need to use the fastest machine in the group. Otherwise if the fast machine loads before the host, the game bugs out and you can't play. Once you've worked that out, it's buggy but playable. It still crashes every time I launch it for the first time (so it's start it, quit it from Steam, start it again), and one of our other players had such a catastrophic crash he had to unplug his computer.  So we have it "mostly functional", but the machine speed bugs, saved game bugs (see below), and nightly crashes make the game painful and frustrating.(2) Unfortunately, even without the bugs, the saved game system is still hosed. I expect any modern game to allow me to have multiple saved characters and campaigns, and to be able to save wherever I happen to be with minor exceptions. In Redfall, if you quit in the middle of a mission you lose all your progress on that mission. That's unforgivably bad programming. Also, even though you're supposed to be able to play multiple characters, it seems to store all the campaign progress in a single file so you can't host two campaigns on a single machine.Which, combined with the, "This only works if the person with the fastest machine is the host," puts you in a situation where you simply can't have multiple campaigns going at once. Inexcusable.(3) Once you overcome all the bugs, you get to the actual gameplay, which is pretty meh. You have a handful of gun types to choose from, a Borderlands-style gun selection menu, and otherwise extremely basic movement, abilities, and skill-ups. Nothing surprising nor exciting. The fights are easy, the missions are routine, and it's a fairly boring paint-by-numbers first person shooter horror game. Even Back 4 Blood has a more interesting plot and more interesting NPCs.In short, the game has nothing I haven't seen before, even in single games, it does its stuff poorly, and it's WAAAAAAAY too easy for its target audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased on a "bundle" platform. Performance wise, the game ran just fine for me. Epic settings at 1440 with DLSS on stayed pegged at my 140 FPS limit. Even ran it upscaled to widescreen 4k the first couple hours and it hovered around 110 FPS. Micro-stutter was barely noticeable for me.The game-play and the world however are far from what I would expect from Arkane. The AI is very noticeably poor, making hard difficulties almost laughably easy. The gun-play just feels... off... somehow. The world is empty and dead, and at least in the first few hours all there is to do is either the target fetch quest objective, or collecting random junk that instantly turns into cash in your bag when you touch it and/or excess guns laying around, which you then scrap for cash in your bag. That actually felt fine initially, but it didn't take long to realize the only benefit of looking through anything in the world was, A.) to find another flavor text note someone left, or B.) to hope you might find a better gun laying somewhere. Which I already had two top tier shotguns two hours in and nearly every gun I found was just a pile of coin in the shape of a gun. If this were maybe a $20 game I probably wouldn't complain and would just take it for what it is. But this is coming from a triple A company, and is up there among probably the top five or ten most expensive games I've purchased in the last few years.I've refunded my purchase. Might buy this again someday down the road when it's on a very deep sale. And hopefully they've improved the game some by then. It's got the bones to potentially work with and make something good. But I certainly wouldn't recommend it in it's current state at it's current price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a $20.00 game originally sold in broken condition for $70.00. Sadly, none of that happened. Instead it gets judged as an AAA game because that is how they chose to price it, and if you pay full price for an AAA title you expect a level of polish that Redfall in NO WAY delivered on release, and doesn't really deliver even now. Releasing it when they did, and how they did, at the price they did, was a massive mistake on somebody's part somewhere up the corporate ladder, and I hope they at least realize how dumb they were.If you can get the game for less than 20 bucks, and you like open world looter shooters with mostly boring loot and average shooting (and a pretty small open world, considering) than sure, pick it up I guess. If it's more than $20.00, that's a hard pass. _childDocuments_.review: I haven't put much time into the game at the time of this review, but I feel I can leave fairly comprehensive take on it. I won't comment on the bugs and glitches, there are plenty of reviews on here covering that already. Yes I ran into some bugs, only one major one that prevented me from completing a quest. I don't think the game is as bad as most of the reviews are making it out to be. Don't get me wrong though, the game does needs a lot of work. The best way I can describe this game is its like Outbreak from Call of Duty Cold War. A semi open world where you gun down enemies and grab all the loot you can. The missions and side quests are pretty rinse and repeat - basically kill everything and grab everything you can. The map doesn't seem very large. There's quick travel points you unlock by opening safe houses. And, the main hub (so to speak) is a fire station that you rescue at the very beginning. Beyond that the world seems very empty and bland. There's a skill tree of upgrades for your character, which seems tailored to the character you select at the start of the game - pretty standard upgrade system, nothing new or special. Tons of weapons to find which have the typical damage progression based on rarity/class/special color. Those weapons however seem very bland as well. Shooting the weapons is boring, there's no character to any of the weapons. What I mean is it feels like you aren't shooting a "real" gun, as there is no kick or any simulated realness to the guns. They behave like a child's toy. All the enemies are pretty much rinse and repeat - as is the loot you find. This game isn't worth the $69.99 price tag in it's current state. I'm going to give the game a thumbs up only because I got the game for free and it isn't as bad as I was expecting. I'd suggest waiting for a sale or until they fix the bugs and hopefully add more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Was really hoping the marketing was just not doing this game justice, but Arkane has absolutely missed the mark here. The gunplay is... fine, but the abilities feels so uninspired that I forget I have them. The upgrades seem okay but don't seem like they'll make that much of an improvement. Movement feels stiff, nothing like how fluid their prior games feel.  And how does this game not have a stealth takedown option?Graphics are okay. They aren't doing much to emphasize the Arkane art direction besides the bigger vamps themselves. The way they move and look is very cool, but the other 90% is pretty flat. Performance is okay. For the most part on an i7-12700k and 4070ti, I can maintain 120fps at 1080p with maximum settings and DLSS, but there are sometimes where it chugs for multiple seconds. At this resolution, I should not be getting any of those moments.Audio is another big issue. Sound effects and voicelines just don't seem well mixed and often don't play at all. Some of the dialogue itself is cool, especially the radio transmissions from The Hollow Man, but character to character dialogue is bland bland bland.I'm not sure this game would be better with friends, but it may distract me from the lackluster exploration, which stings especially compared to how rewarding and interesting exploration has felt in past Arkane titles. _childDocuments_.review: Redfall is a game with many issues. Enemy AI is fairly bad, and the graphics look like a standard xbox 360 games. Guns have a weird iron sight realignment after shooting (Which is actually really cool once you notice it, but very frustrating if you don't realize that it's there.) Enemy difficulty is also non-existent in the start. Playing through on Midnight difficulty (Highest you can go for first playthrough), with a group of three including myself. I have never felt remotely threatened. Performance is also really bad, I'm dropping to 20 frames from 60 on a regular basis. In spite of these issues, the game is still fun. Definitely Check back in six months to a year to see if they have fixed the issues. If these issues are fixed, Redfall can very much be an amazing game you wouldn't want to skip. But until these Issues are fixed I cannot recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: - (3 hour review) Been having fun so far, and I will probably enjoy it more with co-op. But otherwise it's a decent game.- Update after approx. 6 hours (3 hours of co-op, 3 hours solo): Game is still decent. I would say that there are definitely some areas where the A.I. is often lacking and making dumb decisions, and there are bugs/issues in co-op such as letters becoming unreadable if someone else interacts with them first (though they still get added to your log). Overall me and the gf are enjoying it and taking our time to just explore and do missions as we come across them. Hopefully the performance issues and A.I. are addressed in patches sooner than later, and I would personally like some quality of life tweaks such as the little robot companion not being so obnoxiously loud (actually that's probably the #1 thing that has particularly bugged me since it's so annoying to hear stomping around all the time).

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game is okay but the execution is not there. I'm playing on a RTX 2060 Super / Ryzen 7 3700X / 32GB RAM and on medium settings I was getting around 60-70 FPS at best but as low as 15 FPS at worst. The FPS is all over the place with noticeable drops when approaching buildings in the city area as well as the red mist that's all over the map. There are also FPS drops when there are particle effects such as explosions and when staking a vampire.For a laugh I increased the settings to high and ultra to see how bad the performance would be. I was getting a max of 50 FPS on high and on ultra it was a slideshow with FPS in the single digits most of the time. The combat is also lackluster. The non vampire enemies will stand there and let you mow them down or run at you in a straight line or get stuck on objects. Vampires are not much better as they too can get stuck on objects.Right now there's no way I can recommend this game and certainly not for $70. I'd play it on GamePass if you must play it but honestly it's probably best to wait a few months to see if they can stabilize and increase the FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Original 2023 review:I have nothing clever to say.  I bought and tried this game, and immediately refunded it.  I then tried to overcome my hang ups with the games performance in order to experience the games mechanics by subscribing to Game Pass for one month.  I spent another 4 hours or so trying to push my way through the main story and quests and ultimately I just could not find any enjoyment or satisfaction in this game.If the performance issues were resolved, and the AI was tuned/balanced better, this game could become serviceable, but it will never be fun for me... and I will likely never play it again.  I don't see myself buying a copy... If anything, I'll just subscribe to Game Pass for another month if I really feel the need to test these waters again.I would advise against buying this game, and instead... play it via Game Pass or just give it a skip._______________________________New 2024 review:Update: Got it on a deep sale.  Yup.  Three patches later, the performance and AI was improved, and the game is now serviceable, but still unfun.  Still... for $18, it's hard to pass up, if for no other reason than morbid curiosity.  The game world is very pretty... but everything else is just as DOA now, as it was at launch.Update 2: Well, that's all folks.  Arkane Austin has been shut down as of 5/7/2024.  We all got scammed out of DLC and deluxe edition content, fed false promises, and probably will never see our money back.  I wonder how many people will casually forget this tragedy, and buy an Xbox, or whatever live service trash Xbox slings at them in the coming years.Update 3: They released the final update with offline mode and major game improvements.  I would argue the game is now fun.  It's clear that if the version of the game we have now was the version released at launch, the game would have likely seen more success.  More proof that management is/was to blame for 90% of Redfall's failures.  Hopefully Xbox/ZeniMax was able to see that there is talent to be retained from Arkane Austin, and simply fired management... but I doubt it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, looked amazing from the trailers, and good in theory. Had hoped for borderlands style co-op in another amazing Arkane world, but they didn't pull it off well or do justice to the concept and what the game could have been. Having been an avid fan of Dishonored, Prey, and Deathloop, Redfall does not live up to their legacy at all, and falls short in so many ways.AI is lacking and horrible compared to their other games and enemies don't feel alive, weapons and powers feel lacklustre, controller default feel is spongey and bad until adjusted a lot, graphics aren't up to scratch given how much performance it requires to run, and what could have been a great world and setting to explore feels empty and really lacks that spark their past games had.Really hoping that it's updated and patched to fix all the issues, make the world feel less empty and enemies feel more alive, please fix it Arkane, it really could be a great game. But at present I wouldn't recommend it, and if you are really keen on it please wait and see how it's patched first.I'm no newcomer to shakey launches or bug-ridden games that don't live up to their hype, I think my hours spent in FO76 can attest to that. If they'd taken their time and not rushed the release I'm sure it would have turned out so much better, but if I could refund this game, I would.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying Redfall's open-world design which allows for plenty of exploration. I appreciate that I can ignore the missions and instead wander the game's map, which is filled with bits of story that add depth to the game's lore.Visually, the game is stunning, with its beautiful graphics and impressive combat mechanics. The combat is engaging and enjoyable. However, I wish that there were more weapon varieties available for each weapon type, as this would add an extra layer of diversity to the gameplay.The mobs are a little too easy, especially in multiplayer mode. However, I am still in the first area of the game, and things may become more challenging later.One issue is that mission progress is not shared in multiplayer mode, which means I have repeat quests if I am not the host. This can be frustrating if you enjoy playing with friends or joining random groups.Graphically, the game has a lot of settings to tweak, I am usually able to get between 50-80 fps with settings between high and epic using DLSS at quality mode. This is on a RTX 3080 at 3440x1440 resolution.Overall, Redfall is a visually stunning and engaging game that offers a lot of opportunities for exploration and discovery. The combat is fun, but the mobs could be more challenging or offer higher play difficulties. The lack of shared mission progress in multiplayer mode is an issue for me. However, these shortcomings are outweighed by the game's strengths.

_childDocuments_.review: Last edit: I have finished the game. I loved when the main character said it's REDFALLIN time and then the Red fell. It was such a joy.For real, this game houses unmeasurable amount of glitches and bugs, some of them are the most extraordinary and insane ones you could have ever seen. Idk how deeper the rabbit hole goes. Beware at all costs or burn your money and lose your mind.I thought it'd grow in me even a little but it really didn't. It's just an unintuitive & lazy game.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I don't mind putting a negative w/o finishing it. I don't think there's much to see.This is the most generic game ever. 2 hours in and first thing you notice is (aside from horrible performance) how generic the game is. Generic open world, generic interior designs, some cluster of enemies and unnecessary loot dumped over here and there. Storytelling is very plain and boring (whatthe♥♥♥♥ever it tries to tell) it's almost a visual novel. Static images mostly and voice acting over it during the cutscenes. For real? It's good when it's used right but if that's everything you serve to us, if that's the core of your mission briefing, that's simply lazy. The soul of the game, the vampires, are just a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ geeks with some of the most simple animations they could ever had. AI is kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ even for a guns-blazing game. I have no clue what they have thought when they were making this just another looter shooter cuz if I must remind you last 3 or 4 looter shoters have absolutely sucked (and yes, even Borderlands 3). Speaking of BL3 or maybe Destiny 2 none of those games have a gracious campaign but they have a ♥♥♥♥ ton of fun gunplay. Redfall does not have it either. It is also quite obvious mission design won't save the game as they are go to x, do the y type of missions (well you can argue most of the games are like this though) without any substance. But given how trivial Destiny campaign felt compared to its actual universe or how cringe was the BL3 (both also have the most generic mission designs) they had enough core gameplay to have you go for it. I just don't see what'd you lose if you were to quit this game in 2 hours. But out of curiosity, I'll keep going. Well, it's just 2 hours in but I have that strong feeling I am playing a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And I swear I tried to be as unbiased as I could ever be. Even soft gaming journalists cannot justify this game's existence. Arkane Austin is not as acclaimed as Lyon however Prey was just a decent beginning, a sequel could have been great. Instead they wasted time and effort on this, asking shamelessly for 70 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bucks. I have no clue when the development began how much Microsoft intervened and whether Zenimax were involved in these decision making processes (we had another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Wolfenstein game very recently so... I wonder if these are all a coincidence). It was an obvious dead on arrival and guess what? It's dead on arrival. This is equivalent to the story where Square Enix was unhappy with Deus Ex and Tomb Raider but they still insist on publishing niche jrpgs (therefore making some of the most generic cheapass games ever). Nobody can earth can make me believe this game deserves 70$. It doesn't even look like a 50$ AA game. A Prey 2 project was most likely to create a better revenue despite the first game was heavily overlooked. I just don't understand what these mofos cooking. They think a soulless and baseless co-op/mp game insta sells? Do yourself a favor and nuke this game out of the earth. Even for 15$ (thank you Nvidia), it's laughable. When one of the most reliable studios on the earth (which published critically acclaimed back to back for years) dare to release something like these... It's simply over. Arkane supposed to be masters of well thought level design (as well as the overall world design). These guys have made an unique puzzle for Dishonored 2 that you couldn't cheat via internet. And now, they copy pasta some safehouses without any ♥♥♥♥ in it. From Clockwork Mansion to this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ town... They used to have some creativity which they have seemingly lost at this game due to having limited class abilities and of course they had to be unintuitive too. And, people are at fault because they were expecting a good game? I'll go as far as saying anyone who liked this game has no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stomach. I have been gaming for over a decade as well and this is one of the most harsh downgrades you could have ever seen. Now, they have a chip on their shoulder to restore our faith in the industry and whatever left of their studio.Edit: Given how hard I treated the game I'll give the credits where they are due. Unlike some, I did not find graphics ugly or outdated. It's very Arkane-esque which is always very welcome by me. I like the art design here too and it does not look any worse than Deathloop. The art design of the enemies are kinda cool as well. They are somewhat unique on their own. But these are all there's to it, unfortunately.Edit 2: I have tried co-op with a (moronic) friend and instantly regretted. Not that cuz my friend was fooling around but the game is incredibly frustrating when it's played co-op. And this supposed to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CO-OP ORIENTED GAME? You need to wait for a friend when you are down (classic) and as far as I am concerned there is no way to give up. When you guys die you obviously go back to the nearest safehouse and the most mission requires all players to be there to progress. That's complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I also dislike the gameplay loop where you keep losing money every death as well as your ammo. Just lame. It's better rushing this ♥♥♥♥ solo. Otherwise, you will feel like as if you were supposed to play Ready or Not and you are swatting ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ vampires. Not a chill co-op experience.Edit 3: So... Apparently some of the objectives are not marked on the map (Fall Like Lightning mission, connect the antenna objective as a specific instance). So if you happen to forget where was your objective you should just gtfo and youtube it right? Interesting indeed. And, I don't know how I forgot such a critical feature like this but... You can't pause the game. Even if you are playing solo. That was the exact moment I knew I was playing a bad game. Edit 4: There are 2 point of no returns in the game. I have not any sort of warning popping up for either of them. Chances that I missed it? Slightly but it's still possible. While the ending does make sense why it doesn't let you free roam after finishing the game it's the absolute worse choice for a game like this. You probably will leave the game half way through the level limit. I don't even know why the ♥♥♥♥ is the level cap is 40. That's way too much. On the other hand, not that because I care but regardless I'd have wished there was a free roam option in the open world after completing the story so people could have freely grinded achievements and 100% the game. Going through this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ campaign would be an absolute chore for the most of achievement hunters. I pretty much lost all my faith in this game. I lost it all completely. It barely deserves a 4 for the good old time's sake with Arkane. Though this time it serves no good will.

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off as a bit of fun but quickly becomes a boring slog that you can’t wait to end. But it just won’t end… You will be tasked with boring errands that mostly consist of running way too long to the waypoint and killing repeating enemies with idiotic AI. Enemy health scales way faster than your weapon damage, so expect each fight to become longer and more irritating the higher your level is. Also, for me, the game completely couldn’t get consistent framerate, making aiming at agile enemies as painful as chewing on nails.To add insult after killing the main boss of the map, the game announces that you have 2 more maps to explore but doesn’t introduce new enemies or new mechanics - just more boring errands. You really stop getting new content and variety from gameplay about 3 hours into the game. From there everything repeats and feeling of novelty disappears. Even new maps consist of reused assets and buildings.Stay away from this even if you get it for free.

I am very happy with my discounted purchase price of $17.99 and I am very interested in this IP surviving as the world, classes, and enemies are fun to me. I hope the devs add more Vampire Nest mini-dungeon types and even an "Elite" vampire nest with multiple hearts, bosses, or paths to add more variety. This game type isn't usually my cup of tea, but I really hope this game gets a chance, I find it fun as hell. Lastly, the game starts out slow but ramps up the higher the level you are, so grinding a little, doing all the side missions, spamming vampire nests, and SPENDING YOUR POINTS to "reset the armorer inventory" for a RNG roll for epic/legendary weapons makes things fun.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would like to state that I have a NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, Intel Core i9 12900K 16 Core and32GB (2x16GB) Kingston Fury Beast DDR5 before I continue writing this review and I have to say... REDFALL is a joke. The PC port is unstable as all hell. I have played for almost 2 hours as of writing this review and below I will state EVERYTHING wrong with the game. ⚫So to start it off, it stutters. Not BAD bad but... its is unmissable. You can be running around just looting and then SMACK, your frames drop and the stutter hits you hard. ⚫The AI in the game are the most stupidest enemies I have EVER seen in my life. I can hold in S and A and dodge EVERY single attack from a vampire.⚫The stealth... come on.... you have blood in your body... vampires can smell blood... stealth should not be a thing against vampires... right? or is this just me being petty...⚫The game looks like PLAYDOUGH. On max settings, medium settings and low settings. It all looks like UTTER GARBAGE.⚫The "cutscenes" are not actual "video-scenes". It is a picture with AUDIO coming through. Didn't REDFALL get delayed? So what is with the state of this????⚫The gunplay feels off. Its slow, clunky and just a mess. The weapons feel like they have way to much weight to them to actually be good in a fight. Most enemies just stand there and shout out at you and you see their glint of when they go to fire at you.... how pathetically lazy.⚫Online Co-op, Cross-platform Multiplayer but no matchmaking. WHY? SERIOUSLY, WHY.⚫The animations are terrible also. When you go to "stake" a vampire, you will completely miss it and stake mid air but still kill the vampire. ⚫ANOTHER thing with the AI is that they are terribly coded. They get stuck on EVERYTHING. I was doing the tutorial mission in the firehouse and my vampire was stuck in the bloody floor.... it was just standing there letting me kill it and when I went to stake it, it glitched into the floor so the "F" prompt did not show and It regenerated FULL HP. All in all, AVOID THIS CASH GRAB AT ALL COSTS. It clearly needs more time to be a better game. Atleast 2 more years. THERE IS NO WAY IN HELL that this game is worth £60. NEVERMIND THAT... NOT WORTH £83.99. I will be issuing a refund as this is yet another game that is a complete joke. Here is a fact: Arkane and Bethesda had an EMBARGO on EARLY ACCESS reviews so NO review was allowed to be released until the game was released. Funny, eh.

_childDocuments_.review: Arkane finally flopped like most AAA studios today, and released an awful game. This game is just sad.The open world is empty and boring. There's no secret lore and/or side-quests to discover. Exploring is pointless. Buildings might as well be cardboard cutouts you can see, but not enter. Combat is terrible: enemy AI is nonexistent, you never feel more powerful leveling up your skills, half your skills are for coop only (sorry solo players), switching weapons is a pain. The game suggests using stealth for missions, but there's ZERO REWARDS for stealth, so you might as well go in guns ablazing.Storyline is just plain bad. With minimal cutscenes and storyboards instead! Storyboards are apparently the cool thing to do.Overall the game feels unfinished and like the developers just gave up. This is Cyberpunk 2077 all over again. Save your money. If you want a good vampire game, buy Vampire Survivors or Evil West. Both games blow Redfall out of the water with content and enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: If only we could :BENDTIME: ~ Thank you, Arkane Austin for your tireless work in concluding this chapter despite the circumstances. We appreciate each and every one of you. We're all wishing the best for you and cannot wait to see what everyone's next projects are! :Redfall_Bite_Back:Regardless of the state of it's launch (and I played it PRE-day 1 patch as media), I saw a lot of good things in Redfall. Warts and all, it really still found a place in my favourite games of all time - the heartbreaking part is it could have been so much more.I really really hoped Arkane was making major moves in silence to bring this game back to life. And the loss of the entire team is a heavy one.I still recommend the game when it drops in price - no point splurging if we're no longer supporting the people who made it.
