_childDocuments_.review: I was going to save my review for after I played some more, but I woke up at 5 am literally angry about last night's experience with this game. Thanks to NVIDIA for footing the bill, I guess, because if I had of paid money for this I would be requesting a refund right now.First, the release: Like many others I preloaded the 77 gigs ahead of time to avoid a huge download at launch, which turned out to be pointless. I was forced to sit through a 76 GB "patch" the instant the game finally became available. I'm sure my ISP thanks you for that move, Bethesda.OK whatever, the game has now been double-installed and we can play. I crank up all the visuals and it looks OK. The giant walls of un-moving water are odd but kind of a neat effect, I find a gun, start running out towards shore and immediately headshot and take down 4 of 5 human enemies that are serving the vampires, I guess. This part was insanely easy, but I was utilizing good aim and using cover like I've been trained to over years of shooter experience. But it doesn't really matter. The next group I run into I take down just as easily without using cover, and finally I give up trying to be sneaky and just channel john Wick as I sprint into areas and instantly take down any enemy I see with instant headshots while barely stopping to aim. This game feels very easy. I'm playing on default difficulty, maybe I need to crank it up.Finally, I run into the first boss and he's instantly taken down with headshots from my handgun but UH-OH I need to finish him off with a stake of some sort... Hmmm how to do that? I go into my loadout mid-battle (no pause by the way). The vampire has now recovered and is talking about eating my guts while he gleefully slashes me up as I am stuck in my loadout menu trying to figure out how to equip a stake. Eventually I recall that I had picked up a shotgun just before the battle began. I equip the shotgun and come out of the menu to see the vampire fully recovered and myself at 10% health. No matter, I shotgun that unholy fellow in the face a few time and FINALLY, Oh OK, I can use my shotgun to stake him.This is TERRIBLE game play. You have me fumbling around for nearly a full minute in menus WHILE the boss is walloping on me, then I have to make the leap of logic, mid boss battle, to equip a ranged weapon so that I can use a melee weapon that is attached to it? After I have picked up several standalone stakes along the way? Why not just give me a button to stake the vampires, or make it possible to equip a stake in the loadout, or at least make it FAR more obvious when I picked up the shotgun that the one and only usable stake in the game is somehow attached to that.Whatever... bad vampire "boss" is now dead and I get to save our band of trapped civilians and.... Jesus lord. The God of Redfall must really love ugly, because he made a ton of it. The character models in this game are all hideous. The worst affront to our senses being the Reverend Eva Crescenta, who despite having a female voice, looks and acts like a guy who is about to fight you in a bar for spilling a beer on him (her?) by accident. I guess this is some kind of a hamfisted attempt to shoehorn a trans character in the game, but it comes across terrible. For a much better way to do it look (ironically) at Hogwart's Legacy and the Serona character for an example of how to do it right. Or Maybe Eva isn't trans at all and the character design team.... No, wtf else could they have been doing? The character is terrible. The worst. None of the others are much better. Also, why does the pregnant woman act like she's drunk?Anyway so now I have a base of operations and a rag tag team of support people. The doctor tells me I can come see him for medical supplies but to only take what I need, as others need it too. No problem doc, my backpack is already so full of medical supplies from what I picked up running through town that I couldn't possibly take any more. Got a donation box where I can put some extras? There's also an armory where I can't yet afford to upgrade my weapons and some other random areas. I head to mission overview and get briefed on my next mission, but it's too boring to follow and I get distracted by something on my phone and decide to quit the game and go to bed.I want to say that I'm extremely disappointed, but I'm not. It's 2023 and this is all exactly what I expect of gaming these days. I was already suspicious when I got the game free with my new GPU, and my suspicions have simply been confirmed. I will probably play this for a few more hours before uninstalling completely, but if I had paid for this, I would be demanding a refund. There's no way that I can recommend it at all at its current price point. Terrible, Bethesda, take a lap.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it bad in terms of coop? not really. is coop VERY buggy? absolutely.is it bad gameplay? .... eh? It's not bad per se, just pretty repetitive.Not the worst thing to be but since singleplayer works better than coop, it can get lonely and boring. I bought it, might as well keep going. Simply there wasn't the most love with this game it feels like. More like it was an experiment. I feel the next game will be very good but till then, wait for updates and you know ... don't expect too much.other problems I have with this? leveling feels ... lengthy. there are a lot of nice upgrades for your characters but it takes a while to get the exp. for it. if you did nothing but quests then maybe, but I am very explorative, and I feel I should get more exp. out of searching around and doing a good chunk of the side stuff.characters? great. I was iffy on devinder (i think that's how the name is spelled) but he actually has some very nice abilities. if you wanna mess with coop, he would be a good pick if you are against a horde of vampires. assuming you have the 3rd ability available. if you are going solo, be careful. Though the game is kind of easy on even harder difficulties, it doesn't mean anything if you get overwhelmed by over a dozen vampires. If you get a UV light weapon, keep it equiped if you feel something is wrong about an area.Loot? very easy to get once you understand how it works. [most of this was observed in singleplayer] The highest level weapon you can get will always be your level at the time of getting it. The grade (color) of the weapon can be anything, simply RNG. Gold weapons are always special but you will eventually have to salvage those too, as you level up more and more. There is all kinds of boxes and laid about gear to find what you need. But also check shelves and closets closely, there can be something small but useful like a gold gun on the back of a shelf above your head. There are also random items that is basically money, like in dishonored. ... I forget, was I writing a review or writing a guide ... well regardless these were my thoughts.I'm off to die another 20 times to a horde of vampires cause im impatient.

_childDocuments_.review: So, i didnt listen to the bad publicity this game received at launch. I thought it was just the masses hopping on the band wagon following the horrible gameplay footage that IGN released before launch on IGN first.Let me tell you how wrong I was.first all, my specs, i am running with a RTX 3080 with 8gb vram, a 12900K I9 processor on a Z690 Hero board with 32GB of ram. its a fairly beefy system and even still i was getting frame drops and stuttering, for the majority of my play time it did run... okay, but the stuttering was just to noticeable during gunfights and just seemed to take what little enjoyment there was out of it. i did run the game on epic, high and mid quality, which seemed to affect the framerate very little.during my hour of playing, there were many many graphical issues and bugs, the game itself is definitely last gen as far as graphics go, even deathloop looked better than this. the shadows were very.... wavy for some reason, very pixelated. lots of light/shadow flashing for anything further than 20ft. the shutters on the houses would sputter in and out of existence and would only fully render if you were 5ft from them. enemy and friendly ai was absolutely horrible. played the game on hard and not once did i ever feel challenged. hard on this feels like easy on any other fps or rpg. i would literally just walk up to enemies without taking damage and kill them, their pathing is abysmal to the point i had an enemy walking backwards to me. enemies barely shoot and when they do, their accuracy is laughable leaving no challenge whatsoever. i had enemies spawn inside bushes, or halfway through flooring, and not once did i actually take damage from an actual vampire.... ya know... the thing thats supposed to be a threat. actually, the only time i died in this game was due to a car exploding with no prior warning. no sound to give it away, no visual effects (although that may have been yet another visual bug), just... bam.gun sounds seem to all be the same within each class, as in all handguns sound the same, all shotguns sound the same, etc etc. player model seemed to also do some weird things, while holding shotguns i would have the left arm go up waaaay to high for some reason, and during recoil from shooting, it would almost seem like my head/view would be where my chest is and my arms were above my head. .overall, what did it for me though was the boredom. running through the world felt more like walking through a ghost town than anything else. most of the houses you cant go into, and the ones you can all seemed to require lockpicking or special items to enter. vehicles would be randomly about the place, but again, most of them were non searchable. but most notably... no enemies. enemies seemed to be very few and far in between, to the point that i was actively having to search for enemies. most of the time when you did find them, they would be in groups of 2-5 and sometimes have a vampire with them. when you did find them though, it would seem that the game is set to just keep spawning them in off screen. at one point i was doing laps around a house, and every time i got to the other side of the house, more enemies would spawn on the opposite end and it became an infinite loot spot. other times while searching around, i would hear enemies and see it pop up in the subtitles, but when you look around, there would be no enemies in sight, almost as if they were spawn or glitched in an unreachable area, like under the map or in an object.so. poorly optimised, poor ai, graphical bugs and issues, player and enemy model issues, and..... empty and boring.

_childDocuments_.review: It's depressing. I really see the potential for such a good co-op shooter in here, but it's bogged down with so many technical issues and unpolished elements. The characters are unique, the atmosphere is good, the controls are smooth (when not getting tagged with visual lag and screen shredding) and I love the city and map design, but the game itself feels like it was taken out of the oven before it had finished cooking. I put the blame on Bethesda for that one. This should have had another 6 months of fixing up and polishing before release, especially given the $70 price tag. This game could have been so much better than what we all got.May be worth it at a much cheaper price, and/or after the devs get the time to iron out all the technical issues and patch it up to be visually playable. A shame really. I was looking forward to this one for a while as I really want a good, new non-Borderlands co-op shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: I can 100% understand the criticisms of this game and why it is currently so unpopular and poorly reviewed. My thoughts on the game: The performance problems it is having give it fun retro vibe; the low-density bad-guys honestly keep me spooked and on edge - crouch-walking around the entire map and praying I don't run into any of them; the controls are a little weird compared to some of the other (similar) games I play, but that adds to both the retro feel and to the adrenaline feeling because I'm already terrible at the game, and it feels like I'm constantly in danger.Again - I get the criticisms and don't believe they're invalid. My experience playing the solo mission has been a blast! Enjoying the story and being spooked out of my mind everywhere I go. It isn't a 10/10 game, but I'd give it a solid 7 or so. I expect to keep playing this for quite a while!

_childDocuments_.review: Janky in many ways and definitely very buggy, especially in Co-op. However, there is a fun Arkane skeleton underneath the jank. The world is easily the best part with lots of attention to detail in hidden areas and environmental storytelling everywhere. That being said, the gameplay loop doesn't do much to reward exploration of that world in the way previous Arkane games have which is a shame. There is plenty of lore if you're interested in that type of thing and the main characters have fun personalities, even if they are a bit cliche. The game definitely suffers from being a looter shooter and even a co-op game in a few ways. There was the potential for a really cool, tense, vampire killing, stealthy game here but it definitely fell short of the fantastic bar Arkane have set for themselves.Overall I did have fun with the game and I do recommend it if you like vampires, open worlds and cool visuals. Not for full price though! PICK IT UP ON A DEEP SALE!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really a "mixed" bag of stuff.Arkane Studios that developed games like Prey, Deathloop and the Dishonored series, it creates a high expectations and standards which Redfall sadly does not meet based on those games.Having said that, I don't feel that Redfall deserves the hate it's given, but at the same time sadly it's understandable.There is no denying that Redfall has it's bugs, from player characters gliding along/through the floor, player characters that look like they want a hug once loaded into the main base/safe house (I really find that funny), to a random Vampire that's stuck in place and enemies that spawn inside the floor or walls.The difficulty seems to behave oddly. As 4-players we started on Daylight to find our footing and then changed it to Dusk because Daylight had very little encounters. After the difficulty change the first 2 nights of playing was interesting and felt balanced with the weapon drops and the enemy difficulty, but after that it's been one shot-one kill, even with a pistol. However loading into a single player game with the same difficulty and character used in multiplayer, one is killed by the first vampire encountered outside the safe house.It is essentially in the same style as games like Left 4 Dead, Back 4 Blood, Earthfall, Vermintide, Zombie Army and World War Z (minus the 3rd person) but not as chaotic as these.If you enjoy those type of games it might be worth a try, but get it on sale, I would suggest around 75% off or more, which is when we bought it.There's a decent amount to explore in Redfall and missions to complete along with side missions and each character has different abilities.We're enjoying it a lot, bugs and all.I'm recommending it because I'm enjoying it and hopefully there will be more patches out sometime this year that will fix the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving a tentatively positive review.I loaded up the game for a short while to test the performance claims of other reviewers, concerned that this game might have been unplayable and result in a refund. I was pleased that the game ran flawlessly on max settings with DLAA (not DLSS) and frame generation with a completely stable 120fps@4k. GPU usage was between 57-81% & temperatures not exceeding 56 degrees.The very minor issues I encountered were a handful of textures for the landscape took ~2 seconds to load in after rebooting the game instead of being instantaneous like the rest and there's a very brief, maybe half a second, stutter when loading areas as you move further through the map but that's not unheard of in games so I don't mind.I always keep my system perfectly optimised for gaming and every software component updated so if you're encountering issues I'd recommend doing the same as there's more to a computer than just your graphics driver. Additionally, I've noticed a lot of reviews that are disappointed with performance are running old hardware. Try to keep your expectations realistic for how old your system is and check the system requirements, you won't always be able to play a modern game at the same resolution and quality presets that you could for one 6 years ago with the same tech.I'll update my review as I play more with the wife in co-op later on and include any issues we might encounter but for now I've no real complaints.Update: Co-op worked perfectly fine, no issues or bugs that prevented progression or hindered what we were working on at that time. Smooth performance persisted, never dropped below 120fps. Though after experiencing more of what the world and story had to offer I'm changing my review to not recommended as the game is for the most part quite lifeless and you'll spend more than half of your time just running through empty streets, finding a handful of enemies here and there but they never seem to be doing anything which makes them feel alive past being targets to shoot for a few minutes before you mop up their loot then continue trekking down the barren streets. The difficulty is also ridiculously easy, I didn't once feel that I was in any danger despite playing on the highest difficulty which further takes away from the enjoyment in my opinion as I enjoy being challenged.

_childDocuments_.review: is a game developed by Arkane Austin, developers of Prey, but you would absolutely not be able to tell without the splash screen on boot up. Ignoring how this game is a massive downgrade from Prey, it is fundamentally different. However, the game itself admittedly isn't what drove me to write this review, hell if things went differently I might have been willing to give it a POSITIVE one. It's more so...recent events surrounding the developer and the games future. is a looter-hero-shooter, I'll say it right ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ here, this game plays nothing like an Arkane game. Through the open world of Redfall (which is split into two maps depending on story progression), you kill vampires and their cultists, get weapons of varying rarity and stats, level up and use skills....yeah there's no magic in the traditional Arkane sense; there are four characters (would have been six but MORE ON THAT LATER), known as Heroes, and each of them have their own skills, with two cooldowns and one ultimate that needs a recharge. Only two characters have skills that could fall under magic, and I didn't pick either of them. I need me my on-demand flashbang dammit. In terms of mission structure, at multiple points you can select one of multiple missions(though it's more of a "which one do you do first" rather than a proper choice), and at certain points you need to acquire skulls to progress, done by completing Safehouse Missions. This is like the most obvious padding in the history of video games, but at least you can get them done with early. Contrary to what people say, this game is NOT like Left 4 Dead; it's simply NOT a horde shooter. It's more like Dying Light in mission structure (as well as in enemy variants).Stealth is possible but is very bare bones (if it wasn't obvious for the fact an update had to add cultist stealth takedowns), so loud is very much the preferred approach. Then again, not like I played Prey stealthily either.The gameplay in general is a massive stepdown from Prey, but honestly I kinda liked it, I definitely had some fun with the game. Not one of the greatest games ever made, but I think you could find worse. I mean, for a studio which never did co-op, open world or live-service before and were forced to (including the inclusion of vampires, that was forced too), it's not exactly good but honestly it's not the worst.Scientists make vampires real, blocking off the titular island town of Redfall via sea tides and a permanent eclipse. We have the technology. We can science magic into reality.Meanwhile,  four ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ end up getting plot armoured and being the ones to kill the vampires; totally not Insomniac Spider-Man ex-military Jacob, magic wielding uni student in crippling debt Layla, idk Remi and her robot Bribon, and self proclaimed "cryptid hunter" Devinder. Redfall's story won't set the world on fire. It absolutely did not. But honestly I didn't hate it. There are some exposition missions but aside from that it's relatively well paced.I played on low, which resulted in ABSURD pop-in (especially with the shadows), and I had FSR on which resulted in less than stellar image quality. The UI itself has issues, with copious amounts of default Unreal Engine 4 UI font. Artisically, it's not really unique but it looks pretty nice.Warning: the following text is going to be dramatic as an edgy 2010's emo fanfic. You have been warned.Now what I said is very much my opinion. The following is also admittedly my opinion despite the subheading. But there's a difference between an opinion about a game's various components and what I'm about to write.You will walk through rocks. You will get semi-stuck between rocks(you can get out easily bur your viewmodel will spaz out). Your Heroes hands will get freaky when using a skill. Your character will t-pose in menus. You will ocassionally be told you can't connect to the Arknet despite being fine, and you will need to brute force your way into the game. The HUD will cut off at lower resolutions. You will fall through the ground(though that might be a HDD issue). Performance probably still isn't fully fixed. These are just some of the issues I experienced. Not saying it's launch-state Cyberpunk 2077, but compared to other games it is terifically below par.Redfall in it's current state is broken as ♥♥♥♥.And it will remain broken as ♥♥♥♥.Today as of writing this review, Arkane Austin is announcing to be shutting down. Of course this means no Prey 2, but this also cause a more pressing matter at hand; the future of Redfall. With their shutdown, they have announced the cessation of further development. Now this would be fine if it was basic updates right? But no.As part of the  edition, you would have been able to get access to two new Heroes. This will now not occur and you can get a refund for the value of the BB upgrade's price.I didn't buy the Bite Back edition (no way I would pay 85 quid for this game), but still.But what I'd say more importantly, is the lack of further patches, and the fact that offline mode is no longer coming.Admittedly this review has gotten a bit dramatic, but you have NEVER heard a game studio announce "we'll add offline mode" and then go "umm actually you're not getting offline mode". Even though this happening to Redfall isn't the biggest deal in the world, it surely doesn't set a good precedent. What if this happened to Sea of Thieves? Halo Infinite? People would be absolutely losing their bloody minds. And on top of that, they will keep the game as broken as it is. If they were also pulling the game from sale or something, sure that'd probably mean they'd shut it down but it's not that big of a deal. Redfall would just be a drop in video game history. A stain in the long road.But as of writing, Redfall is currently still for purchase; the Bite Back edition isn't anymore, no, but the game itself is, and it is very apparent to me this will be like this for the long run. Bethesda likely has the money to keep the game going for stupid long periods of time.In my personal opinion, the continued sale of Redfall in its current state amounts to a scam. You may argue it was always a scam sure, but this has made it definite. There is NO way in hell Microsoft does not know how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scuffed this game is on a technical level. To bail out on it and STILL take money for it is, to me, absurd.And as of writing, they were working on the DLC eight hours ago actually. They were working on the DLC and then they get shut down.Arkane Austin was really forced to make a game they were not prepared for, and then proceeded to get killed when the end result doesn't end up being peak, ESPECIALLY while they are actively working to improve said game post-launch.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hell Microsoft.And not to mention they also shut down other studios, including Tango Gameworks. What the ♥♥♥♥ did THEY do? They did nothing wrong. Certified bruh momentUPDATE 17/05/2024: So the tweets all said there will be no more updates but Hi-Fi Rush got one final update like a couple days ago so uhh hopium sesh time????????UPDATE 26/05/2024: Apparently a final update with offline mode is confirmed, video game preservation w??????I hereby declare  asIf you  must play this game, it goes on sale for 75% off pretty much every major sale. But know you are buying a broken game that will never be fixed,

_childDocuments_.review: This game was 12 years too late...and I'm here for it. The gameplay reminds me of older shooters like the original RAGE, Aliens: CM, Borderlands 2, etc. Let me be clear; this game is an AA title, and shame on Xbox for marketing it otherwise. Overall, I enjoy the atmosphere and the way combat feels. The moment to moment gameplay is simple and entertaining. Redfall's gunplay feels just like Deathloop and can get intense. Also, the sound design is decent, the weapons sound nice, and the music is very unique. I've played this on the Steam Deck (which is why my hours are so low) as well as the Legion Go (the Xbox PC version where I have 20+ hours clocked) and I have to say that the game performs very well. It's probably one of the best performing games in my library (both on the Steam Deck and Xbox PC).If you're into older FPS titles from the PS3/Xbox 360 era, then chances are you'll probably enjoy Redfall. The story is intriguing enough to pay attention to and the ""cutscenes"" are literal slideshows, but what really makes Redfall enjoyable for me is the actual gameplay (as simple as it is) and the feel of combat. Swapping weapons depending on the enemy type and dwindling a vampire's health to eventually stake them in the heart never gets old.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very skeptical about purchasing this game after reading all the negative reviews but I have been waiting to play this for several months so decided to risk it.  After playing through several hours and missions, I have to admit that I'm not sure where all the hate is coming from.  Here is my experience based on the current PC version:1.) Difficulty- I mostly play RPG and survival games with the occasional FPS.  I found this game to be plenty challenging and have died numerous times to various situations.  Weeping Tammy was a major pain and killed me so many times I lost count. Maybe as I reach higher levels it becomes easier due to better gear but right now it is plenty difficult.2.) Open world- A lot of people criticizes how empty the world feels.  I have two thoughts on this. First, the setting reminds me of the movie The Purge.  Whatever is plaguing Redfall has been going on for at least weeks if not months from what I can tell.  With cultist and vampires killing people indiscriminately during that time, I would expect the town to be largely vacant (what normal person would stick around and carry on their daily routine).  For me, this plays into the atmosphere of the story and I found it to add a creepy vibe. Second, that said, I still easily found enemies to fight when I wanted too.  I'm not sure how the developer could add a lot more without the town becoming over crowded.  I don't think it would make sense to flood the streets with enemies like, for example, Dying Light.  I personally enjoyed the opportunity to explore houses for notes and equipment without constantly being attacked.3.) Performance- I average between 50 and 60 fps for most of the game with the occasional unexplained dipped into the teens.  I have not been disconnected at all since I started playing.  I haven't really noticed any major bugs either yet.  I would agree that the aiming for weapons feels a little off but you get use to it after playing. Enemy AI isn't the most sophisticated but it isn't the worst either.  I would say its about average. Can you exploit some of the enemies if you really wanted too? Sure, but that's a choice your can make or not and I have found it to be largely situational anyway. Maybe the biggest mistake was marketing this as an action shooter in a vampire setting when it probably should have been presented more as a horror exploration game with FPS elements.  I do agree that $70 dollars is steep but I feel that way about any video game (unfortunately I think this is going to be the new norm for price).  Overall, I would encourage people to give it a try on PC.  I cant speak to console.

_childDocuments_.review: A generic game that doesn't justify $70 cost.Graphics are Arcane recognizable style, but while those were good in Dishonored and Deathloop here they don't fit: usual Arcane is using closed and tightly packed places and here it's and open world that feels weird with that style. Some of the assets are reused from previous games and there is no upgrade on the technical side of things.Same as many AAA releases these days the game does not have proper PC controls and has hardcoded keys you either can't reassign altogether or reassigning them does nothing. Was it a last minute addition that no one even bothered to test? But they did bother to increase the price by $10...Gameplay looks basic and following all the known patterns of an "open world save the city from a plague game": we've got survivors to rescue, camps for fast travel/ammo refill to establish, resources to grab and infinite colored loot to pick, compare and discard to pick more - it's World of Warcraft decades ago (OK, maybe traditions are not bad, but in this case better honor first the tradition of having properly assignable keys on PC). Skills are generic "be better at the skills you're given" type and character development seems like just going through levels and gradually acquiring all of them. There is nothing that makes the game stand out, no personality, it's more of a checklist of things to do than a classic Arcane style mystery to solve.This review is written after two hours of playing. _childDocuments_.review: What a disappointment. Gameplay is nothing spectacular, storyline is absolutely standard, NPC are not interesting, weapons are generic.I was awaiting this game because I'm easy to please when it comes to vampire games, and had planned to play it with a friend. While I had fun with my friend, this is not really difficult : having fun when playing coop is dumb easy, as long as there is a vague gameplay.Still, the fun I had killing enemies with terrible AI doesn't make the flaws of the game less apparent. But the real shame is that it could have been so much better. There are ideas beneath the pile of blandness. The bits in "memories" have interesting visuals, for instance, that hint at environments that could have been spectacular to play through. Some skills are somewhat amusing to use.But... this just doesn't come close to being enough. Also, the storytelling is terrible : why so much text, in my fast action-paced shooter ? Who's got time to read tons of diary entries or letters ? Why do the memories kill the pace so much too ?The enemies : not very varied. Four or five types of vampires, and cultists that all act the same (shoot you), and they take a crazy long time to react to having you in front of them.We played in highest difficulty and took less than 12 hours to finish, while doing all the side quests we found on our way and liberating all safehouses we found.All the time I found myself comparing this game with another, far superior "Coop FPS with set characters and quests" : Borderlands. And Borderlands is better in all regards :- Fun, varied weapons- Varied builds- Amusing quests- Entertaining dialogs- Broad type of enemiesThis is not worth 70€. I had much higher expectations of Arkane and it's a shame they delivered this.If you want to play a coop shooter, just buy Borderlands instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game (and I do) but as it is right now, I cannot recommend it. Love the vampire slaying, love the characters + their abilities. It's very much an Arkane take on Borderlands + Far Cry with the open world hero looty shooty concept. However, for an island that is supposedly overrun by vampires + cultists, it's empty. Enemies are dumb and don't detect you even after you shoot at them a couple times (tried to headshot a cultist and missed THREE times before they became aware). Vampires are better enemies but still too easy to defeat. Loot is very inconsistent in the sense that you find "epic" and "legendary" items VERY early and VERY often. In one instance I opened a bag that gave me three snipers, each a different tier. I'm not gonna complain about good loot (hehe) but if I'm always gonna find legendary items, there just doesn't seem to be a need for the tier system, if that makes sense.You would think that after Cyberpunk 2077's controversial release that all game devs would know what NOT to do (release an unfinished game) but some lessons don't stick even in 2023. This game is buggy, glitchy, runs poorly........... it's  U N F I N I S H E D. I'm not the type to let performance make or break a game for me too much, as long as everything else is really enjoyable, but that's not what's happening here. I would rather devs delay the game until it's great then release it half baked.Also, what's the point of co-op if mission progress isn't shared? To ME, that's zero incentive to even try it out. Might just be a "me" thing though, idk.I do think that after some updates, patches, bug fixes, AI balances and what not, the game could be pretty good. Great, almost. I want to like this game. I want to play this game all the way through...but not in it's current state. I'll be requesting a refund and keeping an eye out for updates to see if anything has improved. I would like to revisit this game after it's gotten what it deserves: help.

_childDocuments_.review: Every studio has to try something different at some point. Playing this with friends feels like playing a number of other looter-shooters. Four people stroll into a building an holy hell breaks loose because there's no plan and everyone reacts on their own. There's so damn many of you that you make it out ok. Nobody knows the plot, but you're there to hang with your mates and that's the real point.To that end, the game works. Movement and shooting is good, healing one another is fine. Baddies require some cooperation if there is a lot of them. It's great that there is no loot competition; you can't trade gear and everyone has their own instance of a bag or item to pick up.    The world is pretty, and the plot feels like... Dying Light meets Prey, but with The Strain painted over it?Edit: There have been updates, and some of the dumbness of the AI has been fixed. I really like the world, but to keep the tension up it really needs to be played alone.I'm enjoying it a lot in solo. Lots of things to put together just by reading the notes and looking at the scene. Stealth feels good, but honestly I'm so well equipped that it takes a mob to down me. That's the scaling difficulty, and I haven't decided if I like that yet or not. There is a LOT of Deathloop in this game. A lot. From predictable NPCs to gorgeous and evocative places to discover. AI like that is part of what allows you to hide and take them down. It would be nice if some of the more cunning enemies WERE more cunning, not just able to see you through walls or something...But consider those four people walking into the building again. If it wasn't a 90 degree cone of vision and an unwillingness to see bodies on the ground, how would you sneak up on them? Alerting one sends up a shout that alerts the pod. One of your friends is going to be half paying attention, blast someone in the head, and ruin your attempt to be a ninja. And you can't Hitman the bodies around, sooo. Right now people are frustrated. There are some improvements I'd like to see graphically, but I'm definitely enjoying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a day 1 player of this game because I got it for free with a graphics card. I'm a huge Arkane fan so I was actually really excited for it. It has its issues, and it's far from being Arkane at their best, but it has a great atmosphere and had a ton of potential. The vampire hunter aspect is pretty cool too, with UV lights and wooden stakes as weapons.Obviously there's a decent amount of issues. The game is buggy, lacks variety in a lot of ways, doesn't have the same tier of level design as other Arkane games, has a pretty annoying loot system, and the emergent gameplay is pretty bland. It kind of ends up being a pretty straightforward open zone shooter with some sandbox elements. I was excited for the new heroes and updates, and was holding off until some content before giving the game another shot, but lo and behold the news of Austin being shut down came out and crushed any hope of that.I never felt to burned by the game because I did get it for free, and on one of it's $17 sales it is really a lot of fun for a bit. There's a final offline update coming out with a bit more content, and I hope they open it up to modding after that so the community can attempt to continue the game. This game has one of my favorite original worlds that Arkane has come up with, and I'm pretty sad they never got the chance to really allow that to happen.So I pretty much am giving this game a good review because I think it gets a bad rep, and to let Arkane know that this game DID have its fans and those of us who wanted the game to improve. I enjoyed my time in the spooky town of Redfall.Thank you Arkane for doing your best with Zenimax's tonedef demand for a live service game. Redfall has a really unique world, and I hope some game in the future takes notes and tries to do a vampire/paranormal hunter immersive sim again someday.

NPCs are well designed and some (like the priest in the firestation) are rather memorable. _childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this game. And now ive used it as a learning experience to wait for reviews. This game is a dissapointing mess, and honestly, i don't think any amount of updates could save it. This isn't just an undercooked game with a blatant lack of polish, this feels like a concept more than an actual game. All the pieces are in the game that couldve made it good, but it doesnt do ANY of them well. STORY:The story is incoherent at best and non-existent at worst. The most part of a story you can actually get is through notes and collectibles. The main missions are literally "go here, grab thing because we told you too, maybe kill a thing, and report back." There are few exceptions, but those are found in boss fights. I haven't completed the game to see the rest, and honestly, i dont think I can push myself to complete it. I know the game itself is short. You can complete everything in 12 hours. And some things are brought into the game that just dont make sense. Theres a third type of enemy thats like a private security, and it is never TRULY explained what their purpose is. Like at all. They exist, JUST to exist. And they play the EXACT same way as the cultists. In the notes, there is a DECENT story. But it is never given proper showing. There arent even actual cutscenes in the game. Not one single, actual cutscene in this game. Just models frozen in settings while the characters monologue over them. GAMEPLAY:Couldve been good. As i said, all the pieces are there, the just do NOT work. Its a generic shooter that doesnt reinvent any wheels. The loot system is NOT rewarding. You can find the highest tier gear with a 30% damage buff and use that for most of the game straight from the jump. The abilities are laughably bland. I found myself not using them, ever. And the skill tree is beyond pointless. It doesnt change things to cater to a playstyle, or do anything interesting. None of them do. Granted, i only played one character, but you only need to play one to see how little thought went into it. The AI is some of the worst ive seen in a AAA title. You kill an enemy right next to another one and half the time theyre not even aware of it. Constantly running into walls or standing in front of whatever theyre shooting only to get obliterated. As for the vampires, the main focus of the game, once youve fought one, its the exact same fight. Over, and over, and over. There are a few "specials." and by specials, i mean they do one thing differently, or just have more health. They basically just rush you. In groups, its a little challenging. But more annoying than it is engaging. The CORE element of their game, feels like a chore to deal with rather than a rewarding aspect. And most times you can just avoid them. Just run through everything. Its insane. I finished one boss fight, and it isnt even that good. Nothing rewarding about it. I have nothing to say on this end. It was just BORING. I imagine all boss fights feel the exact same. There is weapon variety, but it doesnt matter. All weapons feel the same. OPEN WORLD:This is probably the worst out of all the things in this game. The open world is not only relatively small, it is EMPTY. Sure, enemies are fairly placed around, but when every fight feels the same, it doesnt matter. The loot system isnt rewarding enough to care after awhile. If you were expecting to try and search for specific chests that contain great loot, well i hate to tell you, that isnt the case. The "looter shooter" aspect of the game is as bare bones as it gets. There is nothing in this map. Aside from side missions, like "vampire nests." which are very short dungeons with maybe 5 enemies in it that are supposed to give you higher tier items, but again, when every weapon feels the exact same, it really doesnt mattter. No weapon has anything interesting going for it. Even the Highest tier weapons. They just look different. ATMOSPHERE:This is probably the only thing the game does well in. Its creepy. The music is actually pretty good. The setting and set pieces feel like a stephen king novel. And the core of Arkane with enviornmental storytelling is definitely there. If this game took a direction that Arkane was naturally good at, it could have been a decent game, and it shows. MULTIPLAYER:No matchmaking. Havent played with anyone but ive heard its constantly bugged. They advertised it as a 4 player co op and didnt even bother to cater to that. If you cant make it accessible and easy to play with others, then why do it?PERFORMANCE:AI, as I said, is atrocious. It doesnt make the game fun. You can steamroll through almost everything. Stuttering is not CONSTANT, but it is frequent. FPS drops in almost every area with multiple buildings or enemies. There is a significant lack of polish in this game. It actually makes me question if this product was actually rushed or they just gave up.Textures take awhile to load in, graphic bugs are frequent. It just does not feel polished.GRAPHICS:Not terrible, but for a AAA in 2023, could be better. This studio has other games that came out YEARS ago that look better. Prey, and Dishonored 2 GENUINELY look better than this game. Not to say its terrible, but for those of you that care. OVERALL:Again, i really wanted to like this game. and I pushed myself to try and complete it before making this, but honestly, it came to a point where I was pushing myself so hard I wasnt having any amount of fun. The first mission feels decent. They tell you to play your way when finishing the first mission, but there is no REAL way to play. The lack of choice at all is masked by the "open world" aspect of the game. Arkane has made absolute BANGERS in the past, and i genuinely cant see how they thought this game was anywhere near ready to come out. Even if they patch it over time and fix things like the framerate, the AI, maybe difficulty scaling, change the perk system, that doesnt fix the main problem with this game. The game has no identity. It has a bunch of elements thrown into it to cater to as wide of an audience as possible and does none of them well. I truly dont believe Arkane is to blame. I think Microsoft made them create the game in the safest way possible, at the risk of the studio itself to make as much money as possible before people realize how unfinished this game is. Ill say it again and again, this game isnt a finished product, it feels more like a CONCEPT of a game.Rating: 3/10 Bad game, bad time, sad time.

_childDocuments_.review: Spent a good amount of time doing all the missions, looking for collectibles etc. Here's my thoughts after completing the campaign.PROSGood atmosphereGood soundtrack Solid story, I liked the endingCombat is solidStaking vampires is incredibly satisfying, does not get old. CONSA number of strange and just plain dumb design choices. The world is open, but not really. You have to be on the specific missions for things like keys to spawn. There's no real point in exploring if you arent on the correct mission.There are two maps, but after you finish the first one, you can't go back. When you finish the final mission, the game ends and you are forced to do NG+. You cannot go back for side missions or collectibles.The collectibles are ridiculously tedious. They are very well hidden and you cannot track them.The talent tree has tiers, you have to save points for higher levels so you end up saving a lot of points. The AI gets stuck on things and is pretty dumb in general.Why are lock picks limited? Why is not just an unlocking mini game? Overall, fun if you like the core gameplay loop but very rough. _childDocuments_.review: I received a review copy without seeing any of the game's promotional materials, so I went in with no expectations at all.There's a good concept at the core, especially surrounding the day/night cycle...but then the vampires just stroll around in broad daylight after the second morning? I couldn't figure out if that was a glitch or not, but it certainly killed any sense of tension and pacing that could've been created there.Many things felt unfinished (the first wave of cultists attacked me by running backwards while i was standing in the open, yelling about how they'd find me - that bug was worth the download size on its own), the AI pathfinding needs serious work (the vampires can fly and teleport, so if im standing on a ledge they cant reach, maybe they could just throw something at the player while hovering there? currently they just kinda freak out, run in circles, then go full-on "it must have been the wind"), the gunplay is seriously lacking feedback and the enemies don't flinch from most hits short of a point blank shotgun, melee is an afterthought, and performance/optimization is abysmally uneven. the option to play with locked framerate (other than just vsync) would have been nice, too, since that tends to work a bit better with streaming clients like OBS.I'll be revisiting this game once it gets a patch or two, but I simply can't recommend it in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, I cannot recommend this game to anyone. While many negative reviews are just jumping on the outrage train and are without substance, game really is that bad. It's unbelievable that we are served this. I usually don't buy AAA games on launch, but Arkane always delivered good games so I decided to trust them this time. While it was obvious that this game will be different than other Arkane titles and would not follow the immersive sim design philosophy so that we would not get another Prey or Dishonored, it still seemed that this game had good and innovative concept behind it and it would have a quality of its own. I mean, Arkane making a game in a small abandoned town full of vampires? Sign me in! It was literally the opportunity for Arkane to realize their take on Ravenholm level from HL2 into a full blown game. So I was ready to consider this game without comparing it to previous Arkane titles. But this game breaks on practically every front. Optimization is the least of its problems. Yes, it is terrible, but you can play it on a reasonable computer on  40-60 fps. Enemy AI is very basic, and that problem is more obvious when you are in open areas. Gameplay mechanics are also very bland and underutilized. There's very little reason to use any abilities in combat when just shooting enemies in the head will do a better job 99% of the time. Also, your ability to use the environment to your advantage in combat, is very limited, almost non-existent.Enemy placement is also very bizarre and is probably my biggest gripe with the game. To illustrate. I would stroll an empty street during the sunny day and just find a vampire levitating in a park near the road. Just standing there until I get close enough. Why? Game often feels like some fanmade map or a mod for some other game with random placement of enemies. Vampires are such a cool idea, and the opening scene where they hide from the sunlight is so cool. But then you realize that sunlight plays no role. Apparently there is an eclipse, but that is a BS excuse. The best encounters with vampires are in closed areas and dark corners, and that is where this game shines. I expected there would be some system where vampires would only walk freely during the night, and during the day they would hide. Also, its very easy to kill those vampires, so they are not so scary and just become tedious to deal with.Despite all of this, I can see that there was a great game in here somewhere. In the closed areas where the game is more focused there is that sweet Arkane environmental storytelling. Case in point: the opening level in the boat. You navigate through tight corridors, find a note about a hidden pistol in the car, look for medical supplies find shortcuts to utilize that sweet looping level design.But then the game decides to throw all of that away for the most part. There are some segments here and there where the good game/level design resurfaces, but they are very rare. Also, the town of Redfall is actually very well made, and there's a lot of ways you can navigate around and explore. The problem is, you barely have any reason to do so. Once again, this looks like some (very well made) map for Garry's Mod.My biggest regret is that I gave this game a chance for longer than 2 hours, so my refund request will probably be rejected. Maybe after months and months of patching this might start to resemble a decent game, but I wouldn't hold my breath.

_childDocuments_.review: A rare Arkane LThere's a famous staple in immersive sims: even if it doesn't do anything, the toilets should be able to be flushed. It's part of showing the player that the gameworld is meant to be a real place; that it doesn't exist simply as a combat arena. Ironically, flushing toilets is just about the  ambient interaction you can do in Redfall. There's no clutter to pick up and use to distract enemies, no drawers to rifle through, no bodies to search. In my first hour, I tried to shoot out a streetlamp so I could move under cover of darkness, and my bullet ricocheted off the bulb. I tried to pick up an obviously-explosive bottle so I could throw it at a vampire, but picking up objects is apparently beyond my ability. Maybe the flushable toilet feature is a small act of defiance from the one person on the team who wished they were still working on an immersive sim. The Dishonored games and Prey are among my favorite games of all time. I was super excited for Redfall and didn't even bother checking out the near-launch media coverage before I dove in. Maybe that was a mistake, but with the excellent reputation they've built up -- up until now -- I had no reason to doubt that this game would be worth my money. Unfortunately I feel like my best option at the moment is to refund it. Without serious, fundamental changes, it's not a game I could see myself giving any more time to.

_childDocuments_.review: My review of  is in response to the latest and final update the game received (May 2024), as someone who has played it on launch. I will say upfront at launch it was a mess. I thankfully played it on Gamepass and finished it through till its end. Glitches, bugs, dumb AI and all. I liked the premise of the game and the world building despite its problems. I can certainly understand the backlash, especially from those who paid full price for this game or beyond the standard base game.  I paid $20 for this game and deem it worth that much for the hours I got out of it. Also I have not experienced co-op mode, my review is from playing single player only. The town of Redfall has been besieged by darkness and vampires. You explore the origins of the vampire threat as one of four main characters, all with unique traits and abilities. The story itself is a strength in this game, sadly hindered by the short-comings of the game mechanics. I am writing this review from the standpoint that you know what an open world fps game is and hopefully this is not your first experience with one…that would .The different characters with their own abilities are fun. The first time I played through with Devinder and this run I played as Layla. I like her ability of the lift. It gets you up to hard to reach high places fast. The weapons themselves feel okay. I like the addition of staking the vampires after weakening them. But overall the game still has a lot of dumb AI. The enemies are more responsive than before but not enough. I found I enjoyed more of my time looking for collectables and focusing on the story. I really like the addition of the Community Standing chart where you can spend points after opening up the safehouses by completing safehouse quests and  freeing captives. They added a lot of great stuff that can be eventually unlocked through this system. Being able to find the Grave Locks and cosmetics revealed on the map was a huge time saver in my second run. Also I never experienced any crashes or stutters in my full play time with the game on Steam so despite in-game issues with some dumb AI or pop-ins from time to time the game overall ran pretty smoothly. Also you can remap keys (I recommend a programmable mouse if you have one). Once you leave the first map (Redfall Commons) to travel to map 2 (Burial Point) you cannot go back to the first map so finish all objectives on the first map before heading into the second one! Once you finish off the main boss (the Black Sun) the game will restart you in Redfall Commons in a new game+. You keep your character progression but all collectables respawn and once again you're locked within only Redfall Commons.  The greatest strength this game has is world building. The game world is incredibly detailed. I enjoy looking in the houses and buildings, jumping around the rooftops and finding secret rooms and easter eggs. I love games where a lot of the time you can actually go into the buildings and explore. For starters I love the game's concept and key art you can find online. In game I am not a fan. The characters look lifeless and ridgid. A lot of the time just repeating the same actions or sayings over and over. The cut-scenes were well done and reflect what your character is wearing in game at the time. More scene captures as opposed to animated cutscenes. I love Arkane games with Dishonored being one of my all time favorites and really enjoying my time with Prey. This will never be the game it could have been but I am happy to see offline support make its way to the game before the servers are gone.I really enjoyed the narrative of this game and the world itself. The story of Redfall is complete for the most part at the end of the game with some parts of the story left open ended. Sadly anything going forward is pretty much limited to our imaginations.  ⚰️

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart but where Deathloop wasn't for me yet I could recommend it to others I just can't recommend Redfall. There's nothing it does that you can't find done better elsewhere.+Arkane stylised characters return, mostly work out. The animations are a little stiff, more noticeable on the vampires imo.+The setting's interesting, who doesn't love vampires? Open world town to explore, the vibrant Arkane style also applies to the environment. There are a lot of interesting scenes to be found in the world that make you want to find out what happened there. -The game commits the 2 cardinal sins of collectables: it doesn't track completed pickups on your map and the reward for collecting them is minuscule.-Safehouse missions: If you accept a safehouse mission then quit before completion it doesn't stay in your log, you need to go back to the safehouse you picked it up from and restart it.-Ammo counter bugs out and loses track of your ammo.-Playing on a 4090, 7800X3D with 64gb DDR5 while most gameplay is smooth there are noticeable hitches when reaching denser regions with lots of environmental details or effect heavy scenes.-While the game is open world the town is divided into 2 maps and once you enter the second you can't return to the first. I can't recall if there was a warning about this (in case you wanted to finish any side missions or collectables) but there is no reason you shouldn't be able to choose to go back to the first map.-Arkane games aren't exactly cutscene reliant to my knowledge, mostly delivering story through in game dialogue, audiologs or written pieces. Redfall has written pieces but most of the significant story beats will be through cutscenes of still models or in-game memory echoes of still models. It's not terrible, the voice work is good, but it's not great.-Lockpicks: There are a lot of locks to pick in this open world game but rather than being a skill, it just relies on consumable lockpicks which cap at 3 (for three out of four characters). Weapons can be found in every type of container so it seems you're never not going to want to open a container. You can buy more from safehouses/base but fast travel to and fro just to buy lockpicks breaks the flow of gameplay significantly. I guess this could be less of a thing when playing as a party, more lockpicks in total but for solo it's not good.-Skills: Having set characters with set skill...sets detracts from the appealing thing about Arkane games imo. Their best game Prey 2017 is a masterclass in giving you a world to explore with clever level design that allows the player to overcome obstacles both with basic exploration and with their choice of skills; climb across pipes and vents to reach a drop ceiling, shapeshift into a coffee mug to fit through a gap, hack the lock, use strength to pry open a door. In Redfall one character has a translocate that allows you to bypass some obstacles, another has a leap ability that gives you some extra height. Every character has lockpicks and electronic bypass kits but not enough to allow you to interact freely; you might use your last pick on a door only to find the next room full of locked chests you now can't open without cutting your trip short for a supply run.I don't see myself replaying Redfall but if I did, I don't think I'd play on a different character. Losing the translocate would render Redfall very mundane to me.-The different weapon types each have uses but you can only equip 3 at a time. In a better Arkane game, you had a weapon/ability spiral so you could scroll through everything in your inventory and each ability.-Characters with periodic background speech delivered through radios etc may continue to speak after killing them.-There's an overall lack of polish in the world noticeable when items overlap (multiple item boxes in exactly the same spot, other item boxes placed so close they're half inside each other), inconsistent climbing mechanics (some waist high walls you can't climb and some you can, ledges you can't climb that you should be able to, ledges you climb but then slide off), barriers blocking pathing (an open path where you'll need to jump over an invisible obstacle).-Enemies in general do not have great AI but some such as the Angler can do a lot of damage that seems excessive (casts a hook that grabs you, pulls you in, takes off something like 30-40% health and you are vulnerable to other enemies during all this). You'll also notice that normal vampire swipe attacks extend quite a bit further than their animation indicates.To sum up, it's not a completely broken game. I found the world just interesting enough to finish the story, there's a lot of environmental storytelling and atmosphere is appealing. The story itself isn't groundbreaking but it's not bad. There are some ways in which you can find alternate paths, use abilities to find different approaches but very few in comparison to previous Arkane games. It is not the worst game ever made but it is probably the worst Arkane game ever made.The story has a little room to be expanded and the Bite Back edition advertises there will be 2 extra characters coming but with how poorly Redfall has been received I'm not sure how much attention Arkane can afford to give it or if it would even help.

_childDocuments_.review: A cautionary tale of what happens when you force a studio to pivot to live service games. Redfall is Far Cry 5 meets Borderlands 2, except just a little bit worse and with a vampire-hunting coat of paint. Gone are the immersive sim elements that Arkane is known for; it's a generic looter shooter with a modest open world and slightly above average gunplay. The game itself is passable, hardly the disaster that it has a reputation for being, but if you're paying more than $20 for this game then you shouldn't be. Go buy Prey or Deathloop instead.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game despite the FPS and Minor Graphical issues. Though I don't think it's worth the $70. $70 would have been the optimal price for the Deluxe Edition, but not the base game.First off it isn't really how they made the marketing seem like it was. This is a Single Player game that happens to have Coop. This is not a Coop Vampire shooter like we were made to believe.As an open-world co-op shooter, Redfall is a refreshing entry into the genre that more or less hits all the right notes. Arkane’s remarkable knack for art direction is ever present throughout the vampire ranks, with out-of-proportion hands, shiny trench coats and gnarled expressions bringing the fear factor when they’re up close. Siphons drain your life force, Shrouds cover the arena in darkness, and Anglers can hook you towards them for a deadly uninterruptible blow. This all comes together to create a superb setting, where you get to explore the pithy backstories of each Vampire God before you face them, seeking out guilt-ridden remnants of their past to expose vulnerabilities.What really hurts Redfall the most is the dismal shape it’s in. Stuttering and sharp dips in the framerate are just the beginning here. Graphical anomalies are pretty much constant, with textures failing to load and shadows flickering. After some updates however, Redfall will become another Arkane gem. I just wish they would have made the price more reasonable because as is the $70 price tag is going to deter a lot of people from playing the game until one of Steams many discounts.Pros-------- Vampires are done gruesomely well- Engaging ability-based combat with room to specialise- An inspired setting with a thick, immersive, open-world atmosphere- A fun story with plenty to say- Plenty to do with your friends in co-opCons-------- The focus on action can get in the way of narrative nuance- Arkane’s strengths struggle to shine throughCheck out my Curator Page for more reviewsLink -->

_childDocuments_.review: A friend gifted me the game and I've been playing both SP and co-op.  Co-op is a buggy mess, but I haven't come across anything game breaking, and it's still a lot of fun. The interaction between the main chars is cute, and sometimes hilarious.The story is interesting - but it requires some leg-work and note-reading if you want to see the full picture. All notes you open are saved in your archive though, so you can pick up fast when your friends are in a hurry looting and read everything later. The world feels quite empty, there aren't enough enemies re-spawning in the streets or buildings (and definitely not enough car or burglary alarms). When you have roamed around and killed everything once there's just the small events (nests and rooks) left. You are forced to continue the main story to find more stuff to do, and I wish there were way more small encounters and more side quests. Pick your character with care, there's only one save... I play Remi on Daylight difficulty - I don't want a challenge, I just want to be entertained -  and random encounters are very easy while most bosses are too hard to be fun solo (in co-op it's just right). I do recommend the game, it's a lot of fun! But the game in it's current state is *not* worth the full price. It really feels like it's in early access. Get it on Game Pass or wait for it to either go on sale or (hopefully) get a massive update.

_childDocuments_.review: Without matchmaking the game is quiet, I played Devinder who has the best abilities for exploration, and taking down vamps.The main story lasts under 6 hours, it requires you to complete 8 side quests which are kill quests mostly to even progress, with all side-quests I was able to find I beat the game in under 10 hours, some other time was spent doing the meaningless "vampire nests" all of which had the "blood trance" modifier making them quick and boring. Most of my other time was just on the pause menu(forgot to close the game) which prevented me from returning the game in the first place.story is ok, it's your general vampire storyline with a bit of that void magic thrown in, I expected more cannon from the shared universe but the only things I noticed were the whale byproducts from dishonored.boss battles were boring, just that, weren't hard at all, all of them save the last one were just somewhat varied kill quests with extra steps. I encountered only 4 bugs in the game which are listed as follows:1. occasional T-posing npc (only encountered three times)2. unable to crouch or use abilities (happened three times, usually after a mission complete, could be fixed with a return to title)3. clipping issue with a few objects (various places where you could get stuck, solved via teleportation with Devinder ability)4. not so much a bug, but lazy implementation, because the game is meant to be played as a group, several times throughout the game you hear things about the other playable characters, and in two cases you are referred to as a group even while playing solo.Overall, game is a solid 6/10 for solo play, with friends its probably better.

_childDocuments_.review: An open world role playing shooter with vampires. Sounded fun to me, so despite all the negative reviews, I gave it a try. Didn't expect to face the worst shopping system in video game history tho. That's because:- you can refill your ammunition at the shop. The price for that is based on your character's level, not on the amount of missing ammo, so if you're level 1 and have exactly 0 ammo left, you'll pay 50 credits; but if you're level 20 and are missing only a single bullet, it'll cost you about 3000 credits. Even better: you can refill your ammo even you don't need to (because you're full), it will still cost you credits. Basically, you can get rid of all of your credits by simply refilling your ammo a couple of times without shooting a single bullet in between.- like in other RPGs and shooter games, you'll need a lot of lock picks. Here, you can also hack electronic devices with a special kit, but these you'll only need once in a while. Once you've progressed a bit in the story, every item you buy in the shop will be replaced by another item. So if you buy a lockpick (which you need plenty of), it will be replaced by something else, most likely buy one of the electronic hacksy-kits (which you need like 1 per hour). Long story short: you can carry up to 8 lock picks, but most of times only buy 1. That's connected to the next point:- shops/hideouts: You can unlock shops in hideouts, which will also sell more or less rare items/weapons and also lock picks. But: same rule as above applies, so once you buy a lock pick here, it will be replaced. Of course you can fast-travel to another shop to buy another single lock pick and do so over and over again, until you visited each and every single hideout.- shops/hideouts part 2: there is a chance that the shop in a hideout will sell you a rare weapon, but to check that you have to visit that particular shop/hideout. Meaning if you're in an area with 5 different hideouts, you'll have to check each and every one of them to see if they offer anything of value. (It would also mean that you can get only 5 lock picks + 1 from the main shop, so not enough to meet the needs since you can carry up to 8 of them).Now, I know that you don't have to pick every single lock you come across, but for me, that's part of a good RPG. I want to know if there's anything special hidden there, after all. But this lock pick / shops / hideout ♥♥♥♥♥♥ really ruined the game for me. If I had a penny for every time I already fast-traveled, I'd be a billionaire by now. Apart from that, there is an open, but mostly empty, world to explore. Sadly, you don't get any helpful tools to explore, so every time there is a high cliff you'll waste minutes of looking for the right way to climb it.The enemies you encounter range from ridiculous stupid humans to vampires which can either two-hit you or don't give a damn about line-of-sight or not. So far, you can choose between 4 different classes, each of which have sklills that range from "meh, that sounds boring" to "how in the wide blue yonder is this supposed to be helpful?". It's also mildly frustrating that at least one of the characters is never shy to mention the obvious, e.g. when you're standing in front of a (so far) unknown hideout he'll say "there's a hideout". Oh, really?I'll try to muster enough resilience to finish the story and will most likely never touch that game again afterwards.

_childDocuments_.review: FIRST IMPRESSIONS This is one of those games that needs a meh option. Before the review let me talk about performance:Spec - RTX3080ti, 32 Ram, i912900KWith these specs I had no real issues with the game. I understand that some people are having worse issues than that, but it is definitely NOT "one of the worst PC launches ever" that is becoming a mantra now. Last of Us and Jedi Survivor are CLEARLY much more broken launches, so let's not call everything the worst ever.The only real performance issue for me was that It seams that when you move into a new area, sometimes you get a slight pause, but I don't think that is graphics performance issue; I think it is an always on-line loading assets issue like the Diablo 4 beta had and it is a very uncommon occurrence.I played through one neighborhood so far taking it slow and wandering as much as trying to do a mission. So far here are the ups and downs.UPS+ Atmosphere is creepy, but not scary+ The game feels like a town and the aesthetic is overall good.+ Weapons are solid and feel punchy. Despite what I have seen some others say, there are definitely several styles of weapon to play with from your basic shotgun, sniper, and handgun (I have yet to see an assault rifle) to the more specific purpose stake shooters, uv guns and flare guns.+ Weapon levels and quality both are very impactful. Weapon damage seems more level dependent and special modifier quantities are defined by rarity.+ Exploration is rewarded with lots of different things from rare guns to cosmetics.+ There is mob diversity so some fights could be interesting, but see below.+ No inventory concerns. You are frequently picking up items that the civilians can use at hubs and safe houses, but they instantly get converted to cash. So, the only thing you store is guns and even they can be instantly turned into cash.DOWNS- The world is too empty. There are too few roaming mobs so far and I have gone through a few buildings now that had only 3-6 mobs in them and one that had NONE. Perhaps this is how they intended to curb the difficulty for single player. But more would definitely be better.- The AI on most mobs is terrible. I was jumped by a pack of 4 vampires at close range. I should have been dead as I was just starting with mostly crappy weapons, but I killed them because half of them just stood there and they were getting in each others way as they just rushed me.- Small but significant bugs. That may sound contradictory, but what I mean is that there are glaring bugs that don't break the game in any way. There was one house where a vampire seemed to have gotten stuck in the ceiling and just stood there unavailable but not doing anything. In another place, I opened a chest and it displayed nothing, but then I shut it and walked away. When I came back, it was full of stuff. Things like that.- Odd immersive element choices, there are things that are just... odd and disconnected feeling about the game. You are picking up everything from rope to toilet paper for your survivors, but not aspirin or many other obvious and small essentials laying around. You also don't pick up food for them. Food is for small heals. You would think that, if you are full on health and you pick up a food item it would just cash itself for the community but it doesn't. So, I guess you are supposed to just leave it there? There was another place where there was a big deal made about a furnace in the basement and when I got to the place that allowed me to unlock the furnace... nothing happened and nothing was in there.- The graphics, while not terrible are very average and enemy motions are stilted and awkward. Even with fast vampires they are not liquid and menacing. They are marionettes with invisible strings. The cultists move more naturally, but they are pretty brain dead so they seem more like zombies in very small quantities.I would say that this game is pretty half baked, but that would not be fair as it is playable and there was only a bug or two that I saw. The main problem seems to be more design oriented than being launched to early.

Some funny graphical issues here and there with shadows and some effect shaders, but I didn't encounter anything game breaking or actually buggy that would've stopped me from enjoying the game.Main issues:- Shadows look blocky, pixeley and atrociously silly even on Epic quality setting and it takes away from the otherwise gorgeous aesthetic. Maybe some shortcuts were taken to get the game running smoothly before launch day? :3- Sometimes vampires just, like blank out. They're there, floating, but they don't have a collision and they don't aggro so you can just walk up to them and admire them :D- Occasional disconnects in co-opAll in all, the game definitely needs a bit of patching and an extra 6 months of polish, but it's clearly lovingly crafted and a lot of fun both solo and co-op! If you're going in with just wanting to have some fun and not get too serious, and not with a mindset of trying to find absolutely everything that is wrong with this game, you're gonna enjoy it, especially if you like Arkane's worlds and "shooterlooter" games.People slamming the game in the reviews haven't actually tried playing it or giving it a chance. Sure, the 70 € price tag is pretty damn steep, but I feel like I could get my money's worth with this game. The negativity around this release is mostly unfounded and getting way out of hands.

_childDocuments_.review: "Well with each good thing a little rain must fall, in this case Red Fall" I got this for free and can't recommend it currently. Came with a video card purchase. Pale (a buddy) asked me if the video card worked well, and I said yes... He then produced the best explanation of the situation:"Well with each good thing a little rain must fall, in this case Red Fall" I about died laughing so thought I would share.Gun play is fun, animations for killing the vampires, ect are fun.. the running speed vs leg movement is entertainingly wonky... The mechanics are fun so far, and the world is interesting and well pathed. Well pathed out could be a good or bad thing. It's open world, but there are paths and roads leading everywhere so just wandering around still has you going down the same paths it seems. There are actual choices but they are limited. You can stealth in somewhere, but not stealth take out an enemy... odd.  Guns blazing in this one is usually the most fun option. Separate loot for everyone! That's a good thing!No story progress even if you all start the game together, except for the host... this sucks.Multi player is fun, but they have a huge flaw, and that's that a character is an un-moveable wall... you can not push past each other, if you stop, you stop. So if someone is afk in a door way, well... you can never complete that quest until they move. They log out just before you complete or you DC? then the host also gets booted and loses all progress on said mission... it's a very very bad way to have a multi player game coded. Dialog can be started by anyone, they just speak into the world... if you miss it you miss it.. to bad. Can't go back and restart it or anything like that. On a similarly annoying note, you can not skip any dialog what so ever, so if you are on a new character play through, you are stuck with it all over again. You can skip cutscenes. So +1 there.Hardly any graphics options at all. Thought this was supposed to be a ray tracing demo of sorts again but there is zero options for it. The graphics options are like console options. "Look good or look bad" and that's basically all they give you.all in all, the game is fun to play though, and it's fun with friends. For the price tag though (I got it for free...) being as high as it is on the store, hard pass. This feels like a churned out 30 dollar game right now. Maybe if they update it and make some changes it will feel better. Current Bugs:If you Disconnect from each other, you may lose all progress, or just some progress.... but most likely you will lose at least some progress. Have had all three things happen. Some items don't spawn for everyone due to individual loot and, idk why I'm not a dev... All I know is I had to run through enemies without a weapon while my friends were blasting away because the initial weapon drop didn't happen for me. Audio issues, floating through the air isssues, connection issues, graphical issues and able to glitch through locked doors, the list goes on...Will I still play it? Yes, it's interesting enough and fun enough with others to get my attention.So why thumbs down a game I'll play? The price, it's simply not worth paying their asking for something as broken as this or with the just horrible game play choices... Some are fantastic, others are terrible. The ones that are terrible are so bad that they over ride multiple up points for me.It's OK, not great, but OK. Hopefully they fix the progress loss because that is just not something I'm interested in dealing with in any game.
