_childDocuments_.review: The idea of the game is really good and I think it has great potential. But this interaction system is horrendous, and the gameplay is not a smooth experience. Also what is going on with the gurney rotation, its a disaster.The game doesn't offer the option to save which is understandable, but in my case the game closed and it said continue but it started the level all over again. I think the the clipboard check lists should be progress savepoints or something.Good concept i'd like to see if become more intuitive and definitely a much better interaction system. But in its current state I cannot enjoy it, it feels like a chore to play, it feels like work to finish the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I am so excited about the new update now giving just an embalming mode, plus new bodies to embalm. The story line is great and interestingly told. Spread out over time and random events. It's and intriguing and deep/emotional story line. The game mechanics work well and are easy to use. Tense and fun. Worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Very unsettling and tense. I love that the game uses jump scares but is not reliant on them for it's entire scare factor. The atmosphere they've created is amazing and is psychologically terrifying. The mechanics are easy to use and overall it is a very very fun game to play. Definitely would reccomend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I want so badly to be able to finish playing this game as it is, as was promised, the most frightening experience I've had in a horror game thus far, HOWEVER, I am running into one glitch after another, specifically in wheeling or turning the gurneys in the direction they need to go. I'm using an xbox controller. Am I missing something?
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful horror game to make me tense. I got the bad ending the first time, but I was still learning and didn't realize there is a timer. The game does a relatively good job explaining the goal and then letting you figure out how to find the demon. I like that its always random so the replay value is there. I definitely got creeped out and found the game a nice change of pace from the usual kinds of horror games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Super cool game with an awesome idea, but in need of SEVERE polishing. I have less than 3 hours on record and i have had to close the game and restart on multiple occasions. Once when the pause and tab button just stopped working, and twice when the game decided to stop letting me work on the bodies. Not the biggest deal but pretty off putting when its so consistently bugged and it brings you back to the last time it auto saved
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often I write reviews for games, but The Mortuary Assistant is an exception. First, I'd like to say that of course this game is not perfect, I experienced a few bugs and glitches however it's only been a week since release. Ignoring those, the game is amazing, visually and story-wise. The mechanics are simple to understand - although a bit scary at first - and the story isn't a cliche, crazy protagonist who's just hallucinating, the scares are real and genuine that come out of nowhere and a few even made me jump. My only gripes with the game is the mouse sensitivity when it comes to moving the gurney, it's not too annoying that it makes the game unplayable, but MAN is it slow when returning them back to storage. Still, the devs made an AMAZING game and I had been so excited for TMA since the demo, and the full game did not disappoint!!TL;DR game is spooky, graphics good, a few bugs but nothing too bad and a few scares made me jump. WORTH YOUR MONEY!!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Phasmophobia? Are you a fan of subtle, yet terrifying jumpscares? Done right? You need this game. They say they will continue improving the game through patches and exciting updates as well. Are you brave enough? Play the demo for a sweet taste of the mechanics, then dive in and banish the demons!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I don't generally scare easily. This game freaks me the hell out! I LOVE IT. At first, it may seem daunting, but in all reality the game at the first level is extremely approachable. I haven't gone to shift 2 (level 2) just yet, as I am streaming episodically on my twitch channel (Take my username and remove spaces). I haven't tried this game with my Xbox Series controller, but I may have to next session to get a feel for it. In closing, this is a fantastic release that has the perfect balance of "puzzles", problem solving, gore, and scares. 10 out of 10, I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun stuff. Short but very unsettling horror game with 5 different endings. After the first 2 runs I sort of got used to the atmosphere, but I dont think there's anything wrong with that. There are a lots of scares in the game, and most of them don't rely on loud noises to make it terrifying. Some of them are actually quite clever, I have to say. The first three things to make your heart skip a beat probably won't even be any of the demonic activities. For my first 4 runs I didn't get ANY repeating scares, and 13 runs in I'm still descovering new ones. Lot's of them still get me good. So far I embalmed 37 bodies, and it still isn't not disgusting, I'm absolutely recommending it.Now excuse me, but I have to get back to ẁ̷̙̝̠͌̂̓́ǫ̴̯̺̪̲͓̳̬̻͓̼͖̏̀̌͐̄́̓r̵̡̙̣͇̪̻̥̰̬͕̺͊̓̀̌̏̚̚͝͝k̵̢̧̫͎̲̜̘̘̙͎̈́͊̃́̇͆̾̊̈́͘.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very authentic when it comes to dealing with paranormal activity and demonic entities. Each different jump scare, entity, vision are all randomized so you can count on playing in fear the entire time. There's 12 different demons to identify and banish, all which each come with their own cut scenes. Depending on how you play and quickly you go to do each task will determine which of the 5 different endings you can get.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: overall i would recommend this game. kinda repetitive but i like that about it. also having more than one ending is fun even if some are very similar. i liked how much lore there is to find too. one thing i don't like is how difficult it is to find the correct body/demon. i had to look up some tips because i was struggling. i don't think it should be too easy but not as hard as it currently is. 8/10 overall.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game a genuine horror game immersing you in its gloomy world from the very beginning!Despite of its sometimes glitchy graphics and gameplay mechanisms it possesses an overwhelmingly frightening atmosphere which offers you shivers freely!I really love playing this game with friends being scared to death!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: So I found this game a bit later in the development cycle and played the steam demo a few times and fell for this game. It sucks you in from moment one and makes you start questioning what the heck is going on even in the quote on quote tutorial level. I have to say I love that the tutorial helps set up for that nights events over just being a way to teach you how to play the game. Makes suffering through it for people who know what to do in this game a bit more manageable.I also love how the game gets to know you and is ever changing what scares are happening when or what pieces of the Rebecca storyline you get from the demon who is trying to possess you. No two gameplays are the same at all. I mean there is the basic mechanics that don't change but the bodies change, the demon name changes and the events you deal with change. It's just a brand new experience each time.I will say the bad revies, which I think is just wrong to have considering age of the game, are a bit valid. There is a few annoying bugs here and there that are a bit game breaking. I have had issues with doing a new shift for endings and being forced to carry a mark with me that I cant set down. I have had issues getting a mark on a different body so I could burn the right body and survive. Yes, it has issues but keep in mind it is a day old and is a one man developed game. For something that ONE guy created by himself, I would say its a great game with decent graphics. Of course the graphics aren't AAA quality, but they are not the same quality as most indie games that use free assets.overall, it's a great game that just needs time to have some minor/major bug fixes. The dev is working as fast as he can to solve them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game..Ohhhhhhhhh this game. It made me call my mommy and tell her to let me crawl back into her stomach and wait 9 months to come out. It made me double wipe and look under the toilet for the demons. It made me never want to step foot near a grave site even if a Taco Bell was close by. Well, maybe if they got those grilled cheese burritos. Cause I know my fat *** would want some food before I get nono touched by a demon cosplaying as a fast food worker. This game is incredibly terrifying and its amazing too. It doesn't rely on the traditional "haha i startled you now gimmie your pocket change scrub." kind of mechanics. This games tactics for scaring you are on a different level. If you missed something in the corner of your eye, you missed it and you will have no idea wtf it is until it comes back to haunt you yet again. The autopsy's however you spell it are disgusting and the game gets relatively simple the more you play. This is the definition of a good horror game. Simple concept, Simple gameplay, poopy your pants scares. Incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

However, this is a mortuary in which the dead do not remain that way, and demonic forces may be involved. Things seem to go as normal for a while. _childDocuments_.review: A surprising game I missed on the initial hype.  If you watched The Autopsy of Jane Doe and thought, "Hey, I might want to be a mortician," this is the game for you. If you want a mortician simulator with a demonic theme, this game is for you.If somewhat repetitive game play and some replayed jump-scares (ohh grandma, you bore me) are going to bug you, watch a good Let's Play.  For me, it's a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: game could be good if it wouldnt have so heavy game breaking bugs. already couldnt finish the first shift because it got stuck by the using pump so i was not able to continue. also 20 € is much too overpriced for such a small indie game. i would suggest wait until its fixed and works properly and get it for a few bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Streamers kill this game! What I mean by that is when they are in an audience they become jaded and not scared and blast through the game like nothing happens. Its a game you need to be engrossed in. There is a heavy story-line that is being overthrown by them. Streamers try to speed run it while forgetting that it's a game of horror. You need to let some hauntings happen in order to pursue the story' and yes there is one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I did my first play through yesterday and streamed it to my friends. I had a lot of fun the way this builds up fear and stress is quite ingenious. The idea your on a constant timer while you carry out simple yet hard to remember tasks gives you a base line of tension. Followed by smaller anomalies and scares that can be hard to ignore, the tension builds. until when you least expect it a larger event will happen that just really messes me up. The style and aesthetic of everything is pretty cool too. This old styled office where things feel slow and unfamiliar, when your on a timer you just really want things to be sleek and fast, but its just not possible to rush the processes. I love the way this was structured so much that I will play again once I've caught my breath I would also love the opportunity to work along side the developer behind this game. Just such a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the free Demo, I knew there was something special about this game. I was thrilled to see the full version was close to release. I purchased the full version of the game, hoping that the full version would live up to the Demo. After playing my first shift as the Mortuary Assistant, all I can say is WOW!! I have never been so scared playing a game. The movement in game was for the most part smooth. No major bugs, No game breaking glitches. A few moments where the game seemed to "hitch" or drop frames but it was extremely minimal and never hindered your performance in game. Accessing in game inventory is quite simple and after your first few embalming's, you start to get the rhythm of what to do and where items are located. I HIGHLY recommend this game to those who love a good jump scare/puzzle solving game. I streamed my first play through on Facebook Gaming (Yes I know It's for old people) as That One Teacher Gaming. If you are looking to see game play before buying, feel free to check it out! My streams are 18+ because I couldn't help but swear while playing this game. I cannot wait to play my second shift of The Mortuary Assistant tomorrow evening. I wonder what surprises await me! Pleasant Embalmings to you all!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. It gets old very quickly with the same events happening repeatedly the game-play loop doesn't change at all. You can beat the game very quickly once you know what to do and you know exactly how to beat the game after the first run. There are three corpses each shift and the models are the same for all three each night. It would be a good game for like €10 but the €20 is way overpriced for the lack of content. Aside from that there are a few minor UI bugs and Crashes but that's a given since it just released. Hopefully they add more content/ modes to merit the price tag but I cannot recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I truly enjoy this game, there are unfortunately a few things that keep me from adding a positive review. The main concern I have is that I had done everything correctly as in locating which body was possessed, putting the mark on the body, embalming every body, looking out for every sign (including major physical wounds), and yet I still end up getting it wrong after triple checking everything. I seem to not be the only one with this issue, either. This has happened to me at least four times when playing the game. There are other issues where I seem to have to shift+tab to get out of a menu which I can't click. I also sometimes get the gourney stuck, and it won't go into the cremation chute. Which, in turn makes me unable to press the red button.The scares are pretty good, and it overall has an incredibly dark theme which I enjoy. For 25$, this game is absolutely not worth it due to the influx of bugs and lack of content within. It's fun, but watching a youtuber play it gives you the same experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Oddly enough I worked as an Undertaker for about 3 to 4 months.  It was a very interesting job to say the least.  I have to say, the attention to detail in this game is really well done.  I never embalmed any bodies before, as this was mostly the Morticians job.  My job was mostly just transport from hospitols and house calls.  I got to see a lot of the process though and just the fact that this game is done by 1 person blows my mind.  Bravo on the cutscenes, and great job on the gameplay.  Simple to learn, and the replay value is clearly there already. 10/10 Highly recommend....if you have a strong stomach
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If your horror game can't make the player feel like they're fighting for their life, then it failed as a horror game.I won't fault this game for being made by a small team of developers, since I'm sure that making a working game is no easy task. That being said: I was told that this game would scare the hell outta me. I came away from this game feeling nothing but disappointment. I'd put most of the blame on YouTube gamers' word of mouth, likely trying to boost their view counts by attracting the attention of kids who wouldn't know descent horror if it slapped them in the face. Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me.It delivered a few jump-scares and a halfway decent story, but that was about it. The embalming process starts off as disturbing and morbid, but it loses its novelty fast and you get desensitized to it (like an actual morgue tech would, I'd imagine). In order to identify the demon possessing a cadaver. you need to use an item with the correct runes. In order to accomplish this, I'd recommend drawing those runes on actual pieces of paper, in order to keep track. The game has 7 endings total, which does give it some replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Each play through is different than the last. The premise is the same but the scares and experiences are different. By having the player replete the  same task over and over (embalming) increases the impact of when events out of the ordinary happen. Also there is an actual story to the main character. Very well thought out and great job by the creator.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece of horror. Only problem is when trying to complete all the achievements the game can get a tad stale and predictable (Embalm 100 bodies/Burn 50). _childDocuments_.review: Horror Fans....Who are patient.  I honestly wish I could give this game the thumbs up, as the atmosphere of the game and the creepiness of some of the gameplay mechanics is pretty good in the horror genre. The game understands that keeping the player on tilt while not just blasting jump scares at the player. You're waiting for the next issue to come around the corner, and the sound/visual design does a great job of putting you on edge. The story behind it isn't anything special, but the different “stories” that you come across like the drug scenario does want me to push forward. The gameplay is simple but effective, although when it comes to some of the demon/spiritual elements, the game doesn't do the greatest job on the tutorial. The game in essence has all the hallmarks of a great game. So you're probably wondering why I'm giving it a negative review.Well, the game can't seemingly stop breaking on me, and sometimes it's even hard to tell when the game has broken. Like, the game messes with you, and yes, there are times where your inputs are not being taken in because the game is waiting for you to hit a scripted event. That's not what I'm talking about. I'm talking about scenarios where a rune on a wall literally disappears, so you have no idea what symbol you need to use. Or doesn't even appear in the first place. Or it starts a cutscene and then just leaves you in a black room......forever. On top of that, based on other footage that I've seen, I'm not sure why the symbols aren't always appearing on the corpses heads once everything is ready to go, sometimes the game just decides.....nah. It doesn't help when the ending in the stream clip below......well it's hilarious, I'll give it that, but it points to the game's biggest problem. It's bug prone: and bug prone in a way that doesn't allow me to complete it fairly. That's the only reason why this is getting a negative review, and quite frankly, I'm really hoping that it's a just me scenario. But until that can be proven, I have to tell players to avoid the game....for now.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant : By Triple F"The Mortuary Assistant" is a unique horror experience developed by DarkStone Digital that places players in the unsettling role of a mortuary apprentice dealing with more than just the deceased. Released in 2022, this indie title has quickly gained attention for its chilling atmosphere, immersive gameplay mechanics, and psychological scares that break from the typical horror game mold. The game combines realistic mortuary procedures with a dark narrative that delves into the supernatural, resulting in a tension-filled experience that keeps players on edge from start to finish.The gameplay centers around the player’s responsibilities as a mortuary assistant, requiring a methodical approach to embalming and preparing bodies for funeral services. What sets the game apart is its attention to detail; players are tasked with carrying out realistic mortuary procedures, including cleaning, incision, draining, and suturing, which makes the horror feel grounded and unsettlingly close to reality. The meticulousness of these tasks creates a slow-burn tension, as players must focus on detailed actions while anticipating what might lurk around them. This procedural aspect forces players to stay alert, as simple mistakes or oversights can lead to intense encounters.What truly elevates "The Mortuary Assistant" is its supernatural component. The mortuary where players work is haunted, and each night brings with it a new paranormal threat. These hauntings range from fleeting shadows to full-blown apparitions, each one randomized to create a unique experience with every playthrough. This randomness heightens the fear factor significantly; players never know when or how something terrifying will occur, resulting in a game that always feels fresh and unpredictable. By intertwining the mundane tasks of mortuary work with escalating supernatural disturbances, the game achieves a remarkable blend of horror and suspense that defies predictability.The narrative is gradually revealed through disturbing events and documents scattered around the mortuary. As players dive deeper into the story, they uncover dark secrets about the facility, the spirits bound within it, and their character's mysterious past. The story takes a psychological approach, dealing with themes of trauma, regret, and the afterlife, which adds a surprisingly emotional depth to the game. Rather than relying solely on jump scares, "The Mortuary Assistant" utilizes narrative horror that builds slowly and steadily, drawing players into a storyline that feels both personal and haunting.Visually speaking, the game delivers an atmosphere that feels raw and unnerving. The mortuary is dimly lit, with narrow corridors and shadowy corners that contribute to a claustrophobic and oppressive ambiance. The developers have taken great care to ensure that the visual design enhances the sense of dread; flickering lights, decaying surfaces, and realistic sound effects come together to create a convincingly haunted environment. Character and corpse models are also detailed, adding a layer of grotesque realism that makes the mortuary feel like an authentic yet terrifying workplace."The Mortuary Assistant" also incorporates clever audio design that amplifies the horror experience. Background sounds such as the hum of embalming machines, the creaks of old doors, and the subtle whispers of unseen entities keep players constantly uneasy. The use of silence is just as effective; at times, the absence of sound builds a profound sense of isolation that makes every noise feel like a threat. This thoughtful approach to audio design ensures that each moment spent in the game is steeped in suspense, enhancing the immersion and horror.To conclude, "The Mortuary Assistant" is a standout in the horror genre, blending realistic mortuary practices with an eerie supernatural narrative that keeps players engaged. Its randomized scares and detailed procedural tasks make for a unique gameplay experience that is as unsettling as it is memorable. Though it may not appeal to everyone due to its morbid themes, those who enjoy psychological horror and immersive storytelling will find "The Mortuary Assistant" to be a refreshingly original entry in the horror genre, one that lingers in the mind long after the final body is prepared.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an unusual style of horror game, The Mortuary Assistant is one I can recommend for its uniqueness, although I'm lukewarm on how scary it actually is.The game is actually pretty simple when you get down to it: grab your checklist, find where all the items you need have been randomly scattered in the embalming room, and then get to work finishing your tasks for each of the night's three bodies. Along the way, look for demon sigils and unusual activity to help you determine which of the bodies is possessed and needs to have a ritual performed on it prior to burning. If you succeeded in deducing everything, you win. If not, things end badly. Once you get the hang of it, an entire night should only take you like a half hour to complete.And that brings me to the game's first drawback, it exhausts its replayability quite quickly. The game does have a story, but it's not very deep and gets drip fed to you over each night without much progression. From night to night, very little actually changes and you will rapidly start to see the same jump scares or events repeating. As many others have stated, the horror elements eventually start feeling more tedious than scary.Another drawback and part of the reason for the tedious feeling is that none of the game's horror elements actually put you in any danger. Once you learn what you're doing, each night is a very simple pass/fail situation. You have no health bar, sanity meter, or anything else to worry about from encountering horror events. Once you realize you're perfectly safe, it takes away a lot of the tension.I still recommend it because the game is good at creating atmosphere. If you play this alone in the dark, you'll likely still feel uneasy any time you play. And while the story isn't super in depth, it's interesting enough to keep playing to experience every event. There are 6 endings total that each shed some light on the game's lore.The creator is still actively working on improving the game, such as adding seasonal events for Halloween and Christmas, and squashing glitches, so I'm hoping they continue to add more to flesh the game out further. If there were less repetition in the scares I think it would do a lot to boost this game.Currently, the game's regular price is a little much for what you get, but if you can grab this on sale, it's a fun time to give yourself some scares around Halloween. I'd give it a 6/10.

The game is made by a single dev afaik and so I'm sure it might take a while but I'm down to reassess the game when that happens.My biggest issue is the lack of content and the scariness factor. The game does absolutely have its horrifiyng moments, and some of the scares are pretty unique and well thought out, but it took only 2 or so games to start getting repetitive scares, and there also were just  enough scares in the game in general. Atmosphere is top notch at first, but it really starts to wane when you realize after a two playthroughs (which a single play-through you can finish in like 30 minutes, though my first took probably took an hour and a half) that there are very few time when something will actually happen. There were an infinite amount of times during my first games where I got in my head about the atmosphere and thought something scary could happen at any time or around any corner, but the scares quickly became easy to predict, and I feel there were SO MANY MISSED OPPORTUNITIES FOR TERRIFYING MOMENTS THAT JUST WERE NOT UTILIZED THE WAY THEY COULDVE BEEN. Makes me want to make a horror game (somehow lol) to implement the vision. Idk, the game was good there just isnt  to make it worth the price. Brilliant concept though, and fun enough if you get it on sale. Top notch atmosphere and the gameplay revolving around having to slowly and patiently embalm bodies (among other things I wont spoil) while hoping nothing will get you as you meticulously go about your business was great. there just needs to be a little more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun and genuinely scary and is pretty unique compared to usual horror fare.  The entire experience takes place in a small mortuary where most of your time will be spent between the embalming room and the cold storage room.  Each 'shift' is different and pretty much randomized - the haunts are not the same and there seems to be many different ones.  Some are small like creepy faces peeking in at you through windows all the way up to full blown entities (one of which is in the top scariest things I've ever seen in a horror game and legit will haunt your nightmares.)  The pacing is also really good, you are on an unseen timer to complete your tasks which you can 'check' with an item in your inventory - when you start the night it will just be small things like tapping at the window and lights flickering but as the night progresses the haunts get more intense and hard to ignore.  All in all I've really enjoyed this game and it has a high replay value.  I can't wait for updates with more haunts, cadavers etc.

_childDocuments_.review: In Mortuary Assistant you’re tasked with embalming and preparing a series of bodies before the night is over. The catch is, one of them is possessed by a demon that constantly harasses you. Your goal is to exercise the demon by identifying its name, finding which body it inhabits, and burning it in the incinerator.The brilliance behind it is how it forces you to concentrate and steep yourself in these menial, repetitive tasks. It sort of gets you into a mental state where you’re very susceptible to the demon’s mischief. Stitching the mouth of a dead body, or filling it with embalming fluids is just grotesque and disconcerting enough that once stuff starts to happen in your peripheral, you’re always caught off guard.It’s a little bit of a one-trick-pony though. After a couple of hours you’ve seen a lot. And even though there’s some narrative stuff taking place across the different nights, once you’ve seen the bulk of it, the monotony of the work you’re actually doing starts to shine through.Either way, I think it’s a brilliant and really effective horror game that manages to mix in just the right amount of big, bombastic horror and more minute details that’ll keep you up at night.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game to make you want to buy it?Well, The Mortuary Assistant has to be one of the best pieces of Horror I've played in recent years, because it achieves so much more than a cheap JPEG jumpscare here and there.The biggest praise for The Mortuary Assistant comes down to its generic atmosphere, it takes a relatively normal 'uncomfortable' topic, being death, and dials it up to 11. There is no point in The Mortuary Assistant where you as the player feel truly safe and comfortable, even outside of the game's haunts, the way it has built the environment is just unsettling, preventing you from feeling like you have a "safe space" at any point for what may come next.Following on from that we have the writing, whilst the Story may not be winning any literary awards of Genius, it's actually a great story. Especially within the genre. Without spoiling anything, the story actually serves to augment the horror, providing some very uneasy grounding for the player that further adds to the constant questioning you'll finding yourself doing. "Was this purely a haunt?" "was some of this true?" "who really am I?" "why am I seeing this?" are all questions you will ask yourself constantly as you play through which in my personal opinion only adds to the incredible atmosphere this game creates. It even takes the time to ground some of the 'things' you see in the haunts with lore, so you feel more uneasy when you see these things, because there is a subconscious link in your mind that then attaches some 'reality' to the thing you're seeing. (Today I learned it's hard to write about a horror story without spoiling it).If I had to pick one flaw, it's a flaw I often pick when I'm reviewing games, The Achievements. 100 Bodies and 50 Burns is a big ask. At the time of this writing I have done 5 shifts and have almost all of the endings and have seen most of the haunts 2/3 times at this point. So pushing for those two achievements will takes some time, however as you can blitz through a shift pretty quickly, it's not a huge real time sink. Just repetitive. HOWEVER to give this beautiful title the benefit of the doubt, it was made by one person, and perhaps we will see even more events and haunts added to the game to further increase the variety that you can experience, if that happens, not even this flaw will apply.To summarise:Pros:-- A story written with a degree of care to compliment the horror instead of ruin it- A great variety of experiences for the first few playthroughs- An absolute gem of atmospheric eerieness and a masterclass in horror elements.- Soundtrack, where it exists, also pretty spoopy.Cons:-- Does get a little repetitive- 100 body/50 burns achievement is a grindI can't recommend this game enough though. Get it. Seriously.

Game has good graphic for a indie game. Get this game for a friend that gets scared easily cause thats all it is probably worth.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to be fair and wait a few weeks before adding a review, so that this single dev could have a chance to squash some game-breaking bugs. So far, he's been very dedicated, diligent, and communicative about it so that's already a plus for the review as a whole. This might be the scariest game of 2022. It has a good balance of jump scares, creepy ambiance, and tension. The story is interesting, albeit simple. If you manage to find the right secret, the story will expand in a way that makes it even more disturbing. DO NOT RELY ON SPOILERS! Avoid the forum discussion as much as you can and find everything yourself. Some points to make:- No, the bodies are not naked. This takes away from the realism of being a mortician, but the dev wants his game to reach a wider audience. While unfortunate, it's a fair compromise. - This is not a mortician simulator. The actual embalming gameplay is simple and streamlined, and is just there to give you something to do to move the story and scares along. Do not judge the game for something it was never designed to be. - At present, this game has limited replay-ability. Once you've done about 6 or more shifts, and you've found everything that you can do, you've pretty much burned out any reason to go back to it. Some games are just like that, but it was still a hell of a ride. - The dev has future plans to add to the game to expand replay-ability, but I have to review it for what it is today, not tomorrow. Pros: Extremely frightening and interesting story to keep you going until the end. Cons: Finite replay-abilityWish I could go back and do it all over again for the first time. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn’t like this game. The ‘gameplay’ consists of you doing the same tasks over and over whilst cliché jumpscares and cheap shocks go on in the background. It scared me a few times, yes, but only from shock value. It was boring and annoying, not to mention how it forces you to trigger jumpscares before allowing you to continue embalming. Not to mention how the jumpscares didn’t even trigger half the time, forcing me to listen to looping voicelines whilst wondering what on earth i’m doing wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: When you deal with a lot of trauma, the last thing you need in life is an awful boss who won't tell you that the paycheck comes with a duty to fight off demons. But this is exactly what happened to our MC, and now we have to help her fulfill her nightly responsibilities while saving her soul.Pros:- the game is great in keeping you uneasy (people with vivid imagination, have fun playing it at night, in an old house where you can hear every step and crack, which is how I did it);- the story has its own lore, it's interesting to explore it;- more details as you progress through all endings;- haunting events are fun and creepy in a good, chilling way;- MC's story tackles important subjects. such as guilt, grief, and recovery;- winning against the demon is very satisfying.Cons:- even after the Definitive edition, the game is somewhat buggy. I got locked out of doing anything two or three times (which can be solved by reloading, but it is frustrating because the reload can take much of your progress in the shift);- really hate one of the endings (it paints MC as kinda stupid);- 2 very boring achievements that basically need you to play 50 shifts. And after the 10th one, you're like "Yeah, yeah, you are a scary demon, but I'm not doing anything before I have my coffee, so chill".

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is a game I followed way back when the original demo was released.  Even then I thought it had potential to be one of the most freightening games ever.  I can honestly say the full game delivered on that and more.A major part of the game is how it seems to time the scares at the perfect moment.  Sometimes it lets you think that everything has calmed down, just to hit you with something when you least expect it.  Now I will say that while the bulk of the scares are jump scares, there are also other ways the game messes with you.  I won't go into details as I don't want to spoil it for you should you decide to try it out.What I will say is the game is absolutely worth it if you want something that will throw a wide and varied amount of scares to you through all 5 ending playthroughs.  Just when you think you've seen every scare - the game reminds you that you have not.Play it in the dark for the best experience!

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant.When I play this game I can't help but remember a series of books I read years ago. "I Am Not a Serial Killer", by Dan Wells. I'll leave some quotes here:“Embalming was like... I don't know how to describe it. It was like playing with a giant doll, dressing it and bathing it and opening it up to see what was inside.”"Is a Demon your best friend?" - Mills said."Look who suddenly got judgmental." - John said.On the other hand, I've always thought that it'd be interesting to work in a mortuary or funeral home. And this game gives you that little experience in a simpler way of what it'd be like to have a job like that. Furthermore, you have to discover which body is possessed by the demon and get rid of it, but not before finding out its name. Sounds fun, right?At first it was a little difficult for me to play. I tried to use control but couldn't. When I wanted to change the button configuration, something happened and I simply couldn't. On the other hand, I didn't like the default keys on keyboard so I changed them to my liking and was able to play properly. When you know exactly what to do and how to proceed, that makes everything easier, although the game itself is quite simple.Although the dynamic is the same on each shift and THIS for many players would be repetitive, for me it's not like that. After 20 hours and having gotten all the endings multiple times, the game still surprises me with new scares and manifestations. You always discover something new. I like this very much. There really is a great variety of manifestations. You can see the dedication of the developer here. The game is so well designed that it makes you feel part of it. I wonder if it could be compared to those "Enigma Rooms". If there was one with a Morgue/Mortuary theme, I'm in!It's a different, fascinating and immersive experience. You'll feel watched all the time, and when you let your guard down, BOOM, there's "he" or "she" or.. Corpses walking strangely in the Hallway or corpses levitating while on the "analysis table" or arms pointing places.This game varies mainly in certain events related to the past of our protagonist Rebecca, and the visions that she sees, these being a way of the demon to scare you, break you and make you give up and forget your main purpose: find out its name, the body in the mortuary that is possessed and burn it.I love the fact that the bodies smile in a macabre way sometimes, these are almost always the possessed ones, however, it can also be a deception. Pay attention and use the  wisely.Most of the "scares" are demonic presences, and they're so subtle, that when you realize them it's normal to be a little surprised. Even when they're silent.This game teaches you that the devil is in the details. You turn around to take the Formaldehyde or Methanol, and suddenly the corpse in front of you quickly moves some limb or levitates in the air.The game in general is very good, however, sometimes there are small bugs. In any case, just go back to the Main Menu and continue.The voices are good, especially Raymond Delver and his.. Possessed mother.This game was a gift from a good friend. I appreciate it, it's one of my favorites now. I highly recommend it, and it's even better if you increase the frequency of "Hauntsystem Aggressiveness". I love it! (not recommended if you have heart problems). But be careful. After a few games (shifts) in a roll, the time seems to be reduced and not enough, so you lose faster before embalming the third corpse, or so it has happened to me. Somehow ignoring certain events like phone calls and dark shadows calling you prevent you from 'unfocusing' on your mission, so.. Avoid them.This game will definitely be in my "💙" collection.Conclusion 1: The game is great and the demons are trolls.Conclusion 2: I'm ready to work in a Mortuary. PS: I'll wait patiently for Halloween and Christmas.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like the game, but it just got stale really fast. It doesn't help that a lot of things are incredibly vague, especially when it comes to the achievements. "Obtain all endings", which there's a tally for 5 endings, but it doesn't unlock (there's a hidden 6th ending that I have yet to find I guess). Had a bug where you have to essentially lose to unlock an achievement, which that didn't pop. There's a hidden achievement that can only be obtained during the very beginning, and if it's missed the only way to achieve it is by resetting game data. At least it's in the beginning, but it's a bummer that you lose out on any endings/embalming/burning that were accumulated before realizing you were locked from the game. Achievements aside, the RNG components may or may not trigger, or specific clues may not appear. I've had symbols not appear after burning letting slips, or a box where they should appear just appear as empty. Specific events may trigger repeatedly between shifts, while there may be other events that you've yet to see that you've just not encountered the right RNG for. There's different variations of some of the major events, which was really awesome to encounter for the first time. After the 4th or 5th time I was just going through the motions to end them faster so I could progress through the achievement.There were multiple times I was soft-locked out of the game. Things like not positioning the gurney just right which makes it so you can't pass, an event where a figure appears that doesn't disappear even when looking at it (the ones that you don't engage with), or getting to a spot to use items but the right-click menu doesn't appear (the coins in the hands is where I was locked out).I may try the game again at a later time. I put 7 hours which came out to 6 shifts (which I did three times, it never progressed past 6). Eventually I was just rushing through the motions, and the game stopped being fun. I don't really want to give it a thumbs down, because you can tell there was some effort put into the game, but when the core gameplay loop just repeats the same motions over and over, and there's a good chance that you'll experience some type of bug which can ruin a run entirely, the game just stopped being fun.I'd say for someone not going after all the achievements, you'll get a solid 4 hours out of the game before it gets old.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm personally a huge fan of horror games. Ranging from jump scares to a consistent feeling of dread and tension, many good horror games tend to capitalize on these elements and Mortuary Assistant isn't any different. Even after so many playthroughs where I start automatically doing the tasks, there are audio cues, things out of the corner of my eye, and quick jumps that still get to me no matter how long I play the game. Early on there were a few bugs (like every game) but the developers have done such a good job at weeding them out and squashing them. Every once in a great while I'll be soft locked out of a task and, when exiting and entering, might have to redo some stuff, but honestly it's otherwise really well done.My biggest complaint, I guess, would be that the story-driven events/scares and exposition can happen too frequently. In the game you can be hit with audio and visual clues, jump scares, etc. but your character, Rebecca, has her own story and some events happen that progress that story. Unfortunately there are a lot of times in which the same "big" story-driven events happen several times in the course of a few nights in a row or repeat. When this happens, I normally just bide my time until it's over.

_childDocuments_.review: I've found the game to be a solid horror experience so far, and I'm enjoying it! There are some solid jumpscares which are made scarier by the overall unsettling atmosphere of the game. As far as gameplay is concerned, it's a very focused simulator/puzzle experience (embalm three corpses, but burn the right one before the timer ends). However, once you have it down, it works well to allow you to start exploring some of the other secrets in the game. I've completed the game twice (failed the first, and figured it out the second time), and both times had revealed different bits of lore and story. In terms of shortcomings, I will say that there isn't much sense of danger beyond the timer (at least none that I've found so far). You either run out of time or burn the wrong body. This might not be a problem for someone primarily looking for a puzzle-solving experience, but might be a bit dull for others. Overall, I'm looking forward to getting the other endings and finding out the rest of Rebecca's story!

_childDocuments_.review: Length: First Playthrough <2hrs then 15min - 1hr per run.A Horror game that in reality is somewhere between a simulation game and a puzzle game, while having a fairly interesting narrative behind it. Throughout the game the player will be playing as a Mortician preparing the deceased, this is fairly simple to do in game, though is well made. Collect the body from the back, place it on the mortician slab, inspect the body and then find the tools you need from in the room to perform each action on the check list. You have multiple different tasks needed for the body, and it feels realistic in the game. Honestly 10+ bodies in and I was still finding it fun, you just get into the rhythm of doing it, and the hauntings really break the monotony.Each night the player will have three bodies they need to work on, the problem is one of these bodies is possessed and if you take too long or burn the wrong body the demon will possess you. Identifying which body is the puzzle, you only have one attempt. While the game may seem confusing at first it really is not, it’s like starting a new board game, the rules overload you but the game is fairly simple. Beyond the tasks of the mortician working out which body is possessed is really simple. While in game it does not clearly tell you, I’ll give you a quick overview below.Spoiler StartFollow the rules of SIT for easy Possessed hunting.Search - Using the Letting Slips search around the mortuary till it catches on fire this will reveal a sigil somewhere around where it immolates. There are four that will appear each night, though they spawn gradually throughout the night, one will already be there when you arrive. Once you have enough use the night computer and match up the four found to the correct demon, this will also identify the demon's house.Identify - While dealing with the bodies you will notice haunting happen, while playing you need to identify which of the bodies are causing the most paranormal events. I always found that one body will basically have nothing happen, and will ignore it leaving two bodies to choose from. Keep an eye out for new injuries appearing on the bodies; this can be from big slices across the chest to small injuries across the wrists. These injuries can already be on the body when you bring it from cold storage, and can be identified as you can not select them when doing the initial body check.Test - Once you know the demon, then choose the body you think is most likely possessed, gather the match from the front, ash in a bag from the back furnace and place the body on the mortuary slab. Chuck the ash on the body, ignite with the match to reveal the demon house. If the house matches the demon you know. Chuck the sigils onto the tablet, slap it onto the chest and burn it. Got the wrong house come up, well you have a 50% chance that the other body is the correct one.Follow SIT and you should be good, once I worked out this method it became really easy to complete the night.Spoiler EndThe haunting moments happen throughout the game, and these are some of the best horror moments I have seen in games. The frigid movements, combined with the creepy appearance, it’s like the developer drowned in the best J-Horror movies, while taking some of the creepier moments of modern horror. This really has made for some of the best visual horror moments I have seen in any horror game I’ve played. You can’t fight me on this, this year alone I have played more than 500 horror games and recorded them,I know my spooky moments. The combination of the amazing horrors that haunt you throughout the nights, distracting you from your tasks really makes for a fun experience. While comparatively to the previous works on Darkstone Digital, the puzzles are ok, there is no comparison to Our Secret Below, just the perfect escape room game. Honestly even though I would say the Mortuary Assistant is a great game, the horror moments are amazing, and really the mortician job was engaging. It just really felt like the demo was still the better experience. While there are a lot more different hauntings in the base game, they are not as active. There are not creepy things happening whenever you turn your back and if anything it feels really spaced out. Honestly still it is worth playing both, just someone who has played the full game really check out the demo, the game just feels different.Now, is the game worth buying, that is a resounding yes. The Mortician job is designed well so that it neither drags or is unengaging. The haunting is amazing and makes the little horror child in me scream for freedom, while the puzzles are not as strong and really if you read the spoilers now nonexistent for you the game is still fun enough. I really recommend you play the other games by Darkstone Digital, while the Subject is not an impressive game, Our Secret Below is a phenomenal game that really deserved more attention.Below is my playthrough to those stuck, or simply want to be generous with your time: Those looking for the Spoopiest of horror can check out my curator page, it is growing and will be one of the largest horror pages on Steam:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING! I have been playing since DAY 1 and honestly I am NOT really a fan of Horror Games, but that doesn't stop me from trying them out at least and this is the first one that I have ever put over 100hrs into. Even if you are not a horror fan, this game is well worth having. The atmosphere is extremely eerie and its what a lot of us would imagine a Mortuary to be like at night mixed with all the thoughts we may have with working as a Mortician. There are jump scares, and plenty of them.....the Mimic on the other hand is just simply goofy....goofy looking, shows up in goofy places, and just an all around goof....now with that being said, there are still some times where he may scare the hell out of you. Since the game changes each time you plan, you can never really plan for whats to come, which makes the game even more interesting. With each playthrough, nearly everything changes, from chemicals and instruments being in different locations to strange events occurring in places they haven't occurred in before. Just when you got used to all of your things being in the same place, it will be placed in areas you wouldn't expect them to be in, which can sometimes cause you to overlook something that you may need. There may be times where you just want to pause and take a small break from the game, possibly to prep for an upcoming scare, or you paused because you heard a noise in the backroom. That could potentially be a decent safe haven for some horror games, but not with this one. Things can STILL occur....or worse, change all together....and STILL scare the hell out of you at a different time than when you thought it would. Mortuary Assistant is one of my top favorite games, which says a lot being the fact that no Horror game has ever been a favorite of mine. If your read my review up to this far, then take my word.....and DEFINITELY get this game. This is also my very first review, so there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is a fairly simple game on the surface, and draws from the typical horror walking simulator that we're all familiar with (think the Slender era of horror games). That said it meshes that with just enough tasks to keep the player busy and distracted to create the sort of lulls that make the scares really work! The randomness of events and scares does a lot to make each shift unique and enjoyable, I'd say it'll take at least 6 shifts before you see something twice, and even then that doesn't mean you've seen it all. The sound is at its best when going unnoticed. The smaller details like having to walk backwards with the gurney, or focus zoom on the computer compliments the random nature of the scares imo as well. As far as criticisms I have 3: Each ending is relatively the same, not a dealbreaker by any means I would've enjoyed more variety is all, the mouse sensitivity setting didn't seem to work for me and I had to lift up my mouse 2 or 3 times to turn around, and I experienced a few bugs that caused me to have to restart, that said I did play on release and at least the latter 2 issues I'm sure will be fixed in time.TL;DR Great spooky game, good for at least 7 times around if you're uncertain I say buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't particularly find this game scary. It's also short despite being able to replay and get different hauntings and endings but eventually you'll see them all if you keep playing. The fact that items you need to do an autopsy appear in random locations is more annoying than anything the real horror of the game is how they made this such a chore. Even one of the hauntings required you to find items to proceed and that was the most terrifying part. When you can turn a spooky haunting into a chore then you know you've gone wrong somewhere. Also the fact that the lights keep turning off and doors keep closing isn't scary just more of an annoyance and the haunting that causes the constant slamming noise is really annoying. Another issue I had was the lack of clues to which body was possessed sometimes it was more obvious but most of the time it was really a coin toss there really wasn't enough to go on and I had to end up guessing in hopes I get the right one. Though despite this the character is set up with an interesting backstory though I don't know why she'd keep working with the weird boss who hired her at a haunted mortuary and having previous assistants die to demonic possession. But I guess the story needs to keep going somehow. That being said I didn't hate the game I just felt it needed to be more fleshed out and that it had many bad ideas put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my new standard for what a great horror game can do. I've played Outlast, Amnesia, Resident Evil, and while they all have their appeal in different niches, this game is the real leader in the horror genre. Spoiler free review.So the story starts with Rebecca, as the title suggests, the new mortuary assistant. The game has a unique way of telling the story that honestly can't easily be described without spoilers so I'll simply say that I'm very impressed. It's something I'd easily point to as how horror games should introduce their backstories. It's dark, it's raw, and the game doesn't shy away from the disturbing parts of peoples lives. The game has multiple endings and it is definitely worth it to replay the game to get them all for the story.You spend each night doing accurate, if somewhat simplified, mortuary tasks as you embalm bodies. Although it's a rather simplified version of the real life job, it's definitely accurate in what it does. The horror aspect takes place at the same time you're trying to work and it flows together really well. The one negative aspect is that controller support is a bit awkward, but not game breaking.The graphics are entirely average. It's built in unity and it clearly isn't a big budget title. They aren't bad by any means, but it's not something that's going to stress any modern hardware. The game runs well and looks decent enough.I never really consider sound design outside of soundtracks when I talk about games, but this is something that deserves it. From the background noises to the demons, everything works really well to constantly give off a creepy vibe and I love it.Overall, this game is a 10/10 for fans of horror. As a complete video game for general players, I'd still give it an 8/10. Great story, good gameplay with some controller issues, and average graphics. I haven't run into any bugs yet, and I definitely plan on going back to play for all the endings.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a horror game buff, but I do enjoy solving puzzles/mysteries, and I also enjoy this developer's take on achievements in both this and another game of theirs called Kohate.So with the multiple endings and various bits of story to find and uncover, I have enjoyed quite a bit of replayability.Without spoiling the story, I would say I found the contents of those parts plus some of the backstory pieces of how the mortuary got into this state way more harrowing and gritty / adult than anything else, plus I'm not really phased by pure gore/horror/jumpscares anyway.The embalming process is a 'task', once you get over the gruesomeness of the activities and have done them a number of times, they do become fairly routine.I don't have a problem with that though.  I feel like this task could be viewed just like those you come across in games like Among Us - the tasks themselves aren't the core of the game's longevity, they're just a distraction to force you into multitasking, to put you under some time pressure, and so causing you to make the occasional mistake. _childDocuments_.review: A unique and genuinely interesting mixture of a disturbing job with great horror-game ambiance and mechanics comes together in Mortuary Assistant to create an experience that has the potential to haunt and disturb you, but these spooks and scares can be harshly undermined by a handful of bugs, potential oversights, and quirks of the chosen mechanics. The result is a recommendation from me, albeit with an asterisk and hopes for further bug-fixing and fine-tuning. I will get negatives out of the way first, because every issue I have with this game is fixable. I do want to reiterate that I still recommend this game, and the number of complaints I have is actually  of my enjoyment of the game and desire to see it become even better.First things first- this game has the right idea generally speaking. The job of a mortician is a fairly unsettling and somewhat disturbing one for most, if not all, of the general public. Creating the perfect mood-setter and environment is crucial for a horror game, and Mortuary Assistant has exactly zero problems here. Mechanically, the story is similar but not quite as perfect.The mechanics of Mortuary Assistant are two fold- process and embalm bodies and determine the demonic entity haunting you along with the information you need to banish them. If none of the bugs or more questionable elements of demon hunting crop up, this system pulls itself off extremely well. Processing a body entails multiple steps and requires enough downtime and moving around the mortuary to allow you to investigate while you embalm, and it is involved enough to require the player to focus and not lose sight of the demon. This system is golden when everything takes off without a hitch, but there are indeed hitches I've encountered in both attempts I failed and within my ongoing third attempt.The "Night Shift Database" is essentially this game's version of Phasmo's Journal, and it is  to beating a level. It's meant to teach you how to discern the demon's name/sigil and what body they are bound to, but either this info is misleading or it is incomplete. Twice now I've chosen the wrong body, and while I can accept a dumb oversight the first time, the second time had me dead-to-rights convinced based on what the Night Shift DB told me, and either way, I've found replaying a shift to be a little too long and frustrating for the game's mood and atmosphere to remain impactful.Choosing the correct body is too unclear regardless of why I missed those two. The first time I likely made a stupid mistake and maybe even chose the wrong sigil, but the second time, I was EXTREMELY convinced. Only one body had shown any level of activity (far far more than the others), and the other two had shown none of the evidence I was told to look for. I'm aware the ashes mechanic can, later on, help me further narrow it down, but if I am struggling a bit on the first level, it is still an issue. The culprit seems to be how strongly the Night Shift DB comes off. I chose the bodies I did because multiple examples of evidence it listed were on one body but not the others- something that SHOULD be a way to at least 90% conclusively decide on the right body. I won't pretend to know the right way to "fix" this, but I do think this process requires some love, fine tuning, and iteration from the developers to reduce frustration.Frustration is the  to a horror game. If the player is frustrated, they lose immersion and aren't scared. Horror games have an INCREDIBLY thin line to balance proper challenge and stakes with consistent forward progression, because the very moment the game becomes too hard is when it loses the magic and spooks. While the game is new and will get bugfixes, there are a few too many bugs that heighten frustration needlessly. I've had sigils just not show up anywhere after I reveal them, gotten stuck in the environment between a wall and the side of a gurney, had the symbols on sigils disappear on me, and a handful of minor bugs that took me out of the moment. By FAR the biggest issues to fix are the sigil ones, as you need these to have a fair chance to win.The last frustration element is not really a bug, but it is a design choice I strongly disagree with so far. I do not love how some of the haunts require me to "stop and be scared" for a moment before I can continue with embalming. Its clear already that SOME of these are going to play into the storyline, but I see no reason I have to stop and be disallowed from interacting with anything while demon-granny is trying to honeypot me from the window, especially if the mortician character AND the game itself encourage being quick.To sum up my "preventing frustration" argument, I have a handful of suggestions. The game only autosaves after putting a new body out from what I can tell, and with all the interruptions, necessary investigation steps, and spooks, embalming one body can take a while. Restarting from the beginning with a body is a drag if you had to reload because you got stuck on a gurney again. Any risk of exploiting manual saves is mitigated by disallowing saving at particular times, and including it is a bigger benefit than any possible downside from exploitation. Losing a level sucks because it kinda takes forever, relatively speaking, and the game does not let you restart from a previous checkpoint. Understandably they want you to have a new demon and go through the process again in case you made a mistake earlier on, but there is no need to make me go through all story elements a second time. If the game simply skipped flashbacks, dream sequences, and whatever else, then the player can cut to the chase. As of writing, if you pick the right demon and sigils but choose the wrong body, the first half of the cutscene is IDENTICAL to a victory cutscene. I really don't understand punching the player in the gut like this when your first shift can easily take 45 minutes to finish. It is not fun having only 2 or 3 sigils because one never appeared and the other vanished. Please make them a little easier to see and make sure those bugs are fixed as soon as humanly possible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Becoming an employee of a mortuary, where you can work as an exorcist as an unwanted "sidekick" is possible in the game The Mortuary Assistant. In terms of the story, the introduction smacks of a particular cliché. Apparently, the creators did not want to deal with the story so much as a different experience from the horror itself.In the introduction, you will get to know your job and the steps necessary to perform the given profession. Once you've nailed the initial training, it's time to tackle your first night shift. You already know here that the situation is a little different and that in addition to your work as a pathologist, you have to face the evil that lives in the morgue building. As a complete novice in the field of demonology and exorcism, you are provided with guidance from your superior, who has been involved in these fields for several years.Most of the instructions are straightforward and clear, others require you to wade through a sort of homemade wikipedia system available on the morgue computer. Here, I sometimes had trouble deciphering what the author wanted to say. Basically, there are a few types of demons and a few names. The goal is to find the right one and perform the exorcism. In the meantime, you can "calmly" go about your work.As I understand it, each kind of demon haunts in a different way. I had the feeling that the game tried everything possible on me. Not to mention that among the various ways of being scared, there was actually one that had a big effect on me. So horror enjoyment is great for me. I got what I expected.The game lasts about two hours. However, there are five different endings to how this night shift can turn out. Given the experience, I'm really looking forward to playing through the next playthrough and seeing what other conclusions might occur.My rating: 9.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool idea this game presents. Horror in a simulator is pretty innovative and the Mortuary Assistant excels in both departments. This game actually scared me which is an art lost in most modern horror games and I'm interested to keep playing and get all the endings. The simulator mechanics are super in depth but can get a bit monotonous when you just can't seem to stop getting ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ possessed.My only major gripes are finding which body contains the demon can be a little convoluted and the decoy scares when you're looking for tells can really throw you off track. I also wish there was a little more to the Mortuary itself, whether they add a chapel or some kind of catacombs. I think the demonic lore of the Mortuary can be better fleshed out and hope at some point that can come to fruition.Either way this is a refreshing horror full of plenty of scares and story beats that keep you invested. I'm excited to see more from these devs in the future.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: There is a cool game hidden in here but it's way to repetitive and the act of embalming needed to be retooled to be more fun with how much you have to repeat the process. The way the game is set up is it very quickly tells you how to embalm someone witch is a short list set of steps but that are just short little quick time events and pick up an item nearby and use it. while you do this you get interrupted by haunting effects that are really well done. after the first successful night you are set on a loop of doing the same thing over and over again waiting for the next haunting effect that furthers the story and lets you know more about what's going on. This is a really cool setup that could work a game like happy's humble burger farm shows how this type of loop can be exciting and effective for a horror game. where this game falls apart is none of the random events change the steps at all and more serve as interruptions to what becomes mundane tasks and most you recognize as harmless. a lot of the repeated ones will drag on for a while longer then you'd like them to and you are just forced to watch the same thing you've already seen so it becomes just frustrating and boring. I gave up before I was able to get all endings and that's rare for me for this type of game piratically only after 5 hours. I feel like a couple of tweaks could really help this game out. I'd like the events or some something to mix up the act of embalming. Also making more events stuff you need to react to could help a lot. I'd also say making the events that lead to special endings more or less happen without fail till you get the ending would be ideal.  I feel the reason why happy's burger farm and 5 nights (I didn't play that much) works better is that the fail conditions were more pressing so each loop was more exciting. This just feels like waiting for the story to show up which when it dose it's admittedly really cool but the process of getting there just is too much.also ignore people complaining about price sure it mostly takes place in 3 rooms but the voice acting animation and events are superb sure I didn't like it but a lot of work went into this.

_childDocuments_.review: Game of the Year 2022I'm late in the train, but this game is amazing! It is scary, dark and disgusting, but it also has a great story. Although it is a short story. Lip syncing looks really bad up close (the intro). Encountered few bugs, nothing game breaking though, mostly just made me laugh. _childDocuments_.review: This game isn't worth the price. I'll avoid spoilers as I explain why this game should only be purchased on a heavy sale.If you play the demo you have done literally everything that the gameplay has to offer. The game is divided into "shifts", each shift you are responsible for embalming 3 different bodies and then trying to figure out which body is possessed by the demon. While embalming these bodies, you have different "horror" encounters where the demon will do something creepy or pull you into some other horror scene for a short time. This is all the gameplay has to offer. Each shift you are doing the same exact things gameplay wise and the only difference between these shifts are the horror moments you encounter. However, it's very common for you to experience the same exact horror moments you experienced in a previous shift (I experienced the same horror moments in my second shift that I experienced in my first shift, which cheapens the whole experience). For as simple of mechanics and gameplay as this game has, it also does a terrible - TERRIBLE - job at explaining these mechanics. It goes through an obtuse approach of using a pc in game to explain how you are supposed to decipher which body is possessed and has multiple web pages that literally take time to load. Why the hell would they not make changing webpages instantaneous is beyond me, I'm assuming to probably to pad out the game time length. Half of these webpages are entirely irrelevant by the way, but when you start playing the game you don't actually know which ones are relevant so you end up reading all of them. This makes what should be a very simple explanation of the mechanics into an affair that takes anywhere between 10-30 minutes depending on how fast you read. The mechanics are so simple they couldve been explained in less than a minute. There's a mechanic in the game where you can use a match and a bag of ashes to eliminate one body as the potential possessed, but it doesn't explain this mechanic really at all. If you use the match and ashes on the wrong body - welp you're kinda out of luck now cause there's only one match in the game. Guessing between the other two bodies is pretty much 50/50 cause what the game states as examples of a possessed body (random markings on the body or the body moving) can appear on bodies that aren't possessed as well. One of my playthroughs none of my bodies moved except for one, and the one that moved had random markings appear on it so of course I ended up thinking this was the possessed one so I burned it and, low and behold, it was the wrong body and I ended up getting possessed. So deciding which body is the correct one becomes a 50/50 guessing game where its seemingly random.The description of the game says it has 10 hours worth of content - but this isn't even close to being true. I have less than 3.6 hrs on record and already have most of the endings. I also had a weird bug where the mark I left on my first body disappeared randomly and I spent like 40 minutes looking for it before giving up, so realistically I have more like 3 hours. The remaining endings I already know the solutions for so I could knock those out in less than an hour probably. Best case scenario this game has somewhere between 4-5 hours worth of content, and of those 4-5 hours you are doing the exact same thing the entire time, with the only difference being some different scripted moments that you get to see. Buy this game when it's like 10 dollars or less, besides that it's not worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite frankly, I don't understand all the hype behind the game... Don't get me wrong, it's not a bad game, it has some good jumpscares/ghost events, it's also kinda cool to get to know more about the mortician job, but as someone who plays/streams a lot of horror games, I've seen way scarier stuff (like Visage or even MADiSON that came out recently).I hadn't seen a lot about the game before I played it so I didn't really know what I was getting myself into, some of my friends suggested it to me. It was fun the first hour maybe, but I encountered so many infuriating bugs that it made me give up after the second night shift. I've seen people say the demo was actually more polished than the full release. I'm expecting to come across bugs when I play games, but not that many "gamebreaking" bugs that just ruin the player's experience. Maybe I wasn't lucky, but the bugs broke the rythm of the game and I just didn't feel as immersed as I should have been...I also think it gets repetitive quite fast, you do the same tasks over and over and there are many redudant ghost events/visions as well (when they're not bugged out). Also, at certain moments, you can't interact with anything before a certain event happens, but the delay can be quite long and the game doesn't really let you know what's happening until it happens... It's hard to explain, but it just feels messy.I might sound rough and I truly wish the game does good/improve, but at its current state, the game might be worth $15, not the $25 it's going for on Steam rn. I might give it another try when they fix most of the bugs, but as of now it is what it is imo, a somewhat scary, but underwhelming game. At the moment, I wouldn't recommend it.
