_childDocuments_.review: ⚠️Spoilers ahead. If you didn't watch YouTube, read the wiki, or explore other reviews, be warned.⚠️📝 TL;DRLet's play Sam Raimi's non-endorsed The Mortuary Assistant of the Evil Dead. This game has you helping a Mortuary owner but things take a turn in that you're actually being recruited to be exorcist of the dead. Can you properly identify the correct corpse that one of the many demons is hiding is, or are you going to be it's perfect living host? The game is is creepy, unsettling, and at times campy, but very soon becomes worn out and tedious. Voice action and atmospheric music, or droning, helps sets the scenes. and immersion. There really is no replay-ability past getting the endings. This is not to say it isn't fun, which it definitely it, but after getting most of the endings and getting all the events and encounters, the game or experience is done. Now for the serious take...🎨 AestheticWhen playing a few games, you'll notice that there are a limited number of corpse models, I think 7, so they can come off as just generic bodies after a while and give less immersion. The design of certain possessed corpses appears to be a homage to Sam Raimi's the Evil Dead. The general design of the game isn't too realistic but isn't plastic or generic either. 🔈 SoundsI feel the voice acting is very well done, nearly natural as if it was dialogue in a movie and not reading from scripts. The voice acting and dialogue of some corpses, I won't mention which, are partially reminiscent of Sam Raimi's the Evil Dead. This is definitely a game that is needed to be played with headphones as the atmospheric sounds are directional and sometimes can be really low to nearly miss-able to blatantly obvious. Sounds created by the player are nearly realistic, but repetitive with no variation, like all the windows or cabinets don't need to creek the exact same way. The music is atmospheric and at there's there is an ominous droning, adding the tension and unease.There wasn't much music other than from the radios found within the game that cheekily repeat, and repeat and repeat, but for gags. Throughout the game there is a slight underscore that plays, which turns into a tense droning when something is happening or about to happen, creating a feeling of tread and anxiety.⚙️ AssemblyThis is the tedious part. You're given a limited inventory to hold all that you need, so you'll find yourself going back and forth to grab items. You can only hold one of each item or can only hold one large item at a time along with your trusty clipboard. With some, you can't hold them at all until you need them. With time, things become easier with repetition, but even then trying to perform the actions of certain required steps are clunky and makes you want to bang your mouse to dislodge whatever might be stuck as you can't reach through the screen and do it yourself.Depending on certain actions of the previous play-through, there would be additional items to interact with. What is standard in the game is that, through a note found, it will be explained that tools and materials needed to perform your job are set up in randomized locations every play-though. This is never truly explained, as obviously this would take you longer to do your job and make it easier for time to run out and for you to get possessed. ❕ NOTE: This is my opinion and thoughts, not an overall view of the game for general audiences, as opinions and experiences vary. _childDocuments_.review: For me, The Mortuary Assistant came out of nowhere and scared the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. Then it did it again, and it hasn't stopped yet. (minimal spoilers ahead)I'm obsessed with horror games (especially survival-horror), and this game arrived when I felt like I was running out of old and new spooky games to play (even through emulators), reduced to digging through mysterious indie demos and Doom/Half-Life mods and such. I've become desensitized though playing so many of these games and I thought nothing could really terrify me anymore, much less surprise me. Terrifying moments aside, what I find most surprising is either the sheer replayability of this non-action horror game, or the fact that it was CREATED BY ONE (1) PERSON (not counting VAs, publishers, etc).You can have a successful "shift," as runs through this game are called, on the first try in theory. You can even get each one of the endings in as many shifts. But the pressure and unpredictability never lets up. I'm 15-20 shifts in and while I can see certain spooky events coming now based on subtle signs, I'm still made very uneasy when the paranormal elephant in the room takes its time to show itself. I find the Resident Evil games very replayable, but even the least action-y of them lose their scare factor after the first run or two and become action roguelikes going for trophies. I've also replayed Outlast a few times, but The Mortuary Assistant still makes me feel as scared and defenseless as I did my first time playing that game.The lack of action elements, even though the game isn't really a walking simulator, should make it boring on paper. On the contrary it's extremely engaging and makes you want to get better at the embalming procedure to spite the dark forces harrassing you. The actual terror you face as the protagonist can't be fought directly. All you can do is go through the motions of a mortician on the night shift, and hope you've correctly identified the source of the increasingly unpleasant hauntings that you'll have to try your best to ignore before it's too late. It hasn't gotten old for me yet.The only evidence suggesting that this was developed solo is the somewhat disappointing variety of corpse models that randomly populate the morgue in threes on each shift, but I can tell this is being addressed gradually through updates. It's truly my only complaint about the game, period. The models that are there look great (for dead people, anyway), but it would be nice to see a wider range of body types and some new faces for the immersion. It makes me wonder if mods will ever be a thing for this game. There were only 5 or 6 different corpses when I started playing the game last month, and the Halloween update gave us three more. If there were closer to 20 models, I think this game would be just about perfect.To the dev, thank you very much for this game. To anyone else reading it, buy it already!

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the unfortunate opportunity to play "The Mortuary Assistant," and it was an absolute disaster. This game is so infested with bugs and technical issues that it is virtually unplayable. From start to finish, my gaming experience was marred by constant glitches and frustrating problems that prevented me from enjoying the game in any meaningful way.First and foremost, the game suffers from severe performance issues. Even on a high-end gaming rig, the frame rate would frequently drop to unbearable levels, causing significant stuttering and lag. It was as if the game was struggling to keep up with even the most basic actions. This not only hampered the immersion but also made the gameplay frustratingly sluggish.Furthermore, the game was plagued with numerous game-breaking bugs. Quest objectives would often fail to trigger, leaving me stranded without any direction. NPC interactions were riddled with glitches, causing characters to freeze or disappear altogether. These issues made progressing through the game an exercise in frustration and wasted a considerable amount of my time.The controls in "The Mortuary Assistant" were also a nightmare. They were unresponsive and clunky, making it incredibly difficult to execute even the simplest actions.On top of all these technical issues, the game's visuals were subpar at best. Poorly rendered textures, bland environments, and lackluster character models made for an unappealing visual experience. It felt like I was playing a game from a decade ago, rather than a modern release.To make matters worse, the developer's support for "The Mortuary Assistant" was practically non-existent. Despite numerous bug reports and requests for assistance, there was no response or acknowledgment from the development team. This lack of support left players to fend for themselves, struggling to find workarounds or fixes for the game-breaking issues.In conclusion, "The Mortuary Assistant" is a prime example of a game that is simply not ready for release. The overwhelming number of bugs, technical issues, and poor performance make it an unplayable mess. The lackluster visuals and unresponsive controls only add to the frustration. Save yourself the headache and steer clear of this buggy nightmare of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a great atmosphere and gameplay, my only problem is that the game is extremely luck based when it comes to solving the main objective, things that you need to look out for will happen in different places and circumstances, making it very hard to tell when it actually matters. Some of these things are also near impossible to spot unless you just sit there staring at the body, which is not a good idea when your on a time limit. With that said, the game has only just been released and I think these issues can be fixed, the game as a whole is very scary and incredibly clever with the way you uncover your character's past, it blends lore seamlessly into the main game such that you don't realise until after the event has happened. One more thing, this game does not technically have a story mode or campaign, it only has "shifts" which act as a "run", this does not mean the game does not have a story however, it only gives it an ungodly level of replay potential. From what I can tell so far, there are many different easter eggs and endings to unlock, and each shift will be completely different every time. Overall, I would give this game a 9/10, the only real issue is the somewhat unfair luck aspect of it

I like trying for different endings. Downside: The game can get a little buggy if any of your interactions with objects accidentally happen when a cutscene or demon interaction triggers. Overall definitely would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, fantastic game.The Mortuary Assistant most likely has to be one of the scariest, let alone genuinely nerve-wracking, horror games I have played in quite a long while.  The general atmosphere, and environment the player is tossed into, leaves a constant sense of dread as you anticipate what may be just around the corner, or down the corridor... or right behind you.Besides for the horror elements, the story remains intriguing with its own aspects, allowing the player to piece it together through each shift.  Every night being unique from the one prior, and consisting of new haunts, random events, and bits of story to take in.Of course, a few flaws I'd point out would be a couple of bugs throughout my multiple runs in the game.  They were nothing too profound to inhibit any progression into the game, however.  Mostly just minor inconveniences and little surprises.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: If you like adventure/puzzle games, I highly suggest The Mortuary Assistant. I've been playing it nonstop for a good 2 weeks. It's a little gross (you are literally the mortuary assistant embalming bodies) and there are jumpscares, as well as drug abuse and some intense scenes, but it's a pretty straightforward game once you get the hang of it. It's massively replayable too. Everything is randomly generated every time you play. You don't have to worry about your aim, or running and hiding, it's all about figuring out the mystery. I particularly like it because of the slow burn each round has, and how perceptive you need to be to the point that you can start playing tricks on yourself and see clues that aren't there. It's extremely fun, I very much enjoy it. As someone who needs a lot to get scared by media, this one does the trick. Get it. You'll love it. It's exactly what you're looking for
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

(For an example: They changed one of the dead bodies into a creepy clown for Halloween. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little horror game, it does so much right that it is hard to not recommend to fans of horror games or someone wanting to try them out. The jump scares are so dynamic that it is impossible to predict what is going to happen each night, and you are unlikely to experience the same one twice. The general work of a simulator game mixed in also helps lull you out of your safety net when playing these types of games, so it is that much more effective. The only thing I wish would change is that you could somehow force the needed events to happen to get one of the endings, just as a time saver as I did two additional runs after getting all the other endings and this one requirement didn't appear.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get right into it.You take dead bodies, embalm them, prep them, then put them in storage. During this time, you're trying to figure out what type of demon is around and which of the 3 bodies it is "possessing."Are there jump scares? Of course, but they're nicely done. I haven't had a playthrough yet that got me thinking "Okay. Chill with the cheese scares."The story element is tastefully done and provides replay value. You play in "shifts" as in; the first time you play is your first shift at work. Each shift provides more story element, so you unfold the story at your pace. The story itself involves some sensitive subjects for some people, so if you stream this, be sure to have a warning. No spoilers, but I'll hide it just in case; the story involves .For a game created by one person, it well done and worth the purchase for any fan of horror games. I think it would be so much better with VR capabilities though. Hopefully that's something they'll do in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the macabre and someone who wants to go into the funeral industry at some point, this game is absolutely amazing! The embalming process, while simplified, is very accurate. It's a peek into how the deceased is prepared for a funeral, which I'm sure is upsetting to some, and I would not recommend the game to them.The story is compelling and well told(drug abuse is involved), the controls and mechanics are great once you get used to them(which doesn't take long at all), and the graphics are amazing. No two shifts are the same. As soon as I walk into the lobby to start a shift I'm immediately on edge as I never know what the demons are going to throw at me, or when. Just last night I barely got in the door when there was a knock from the hallway door, and the demon was REAL active. Very spooky and atmospheric game.I'll leave you with just one hint: the game lists 5 different endings but there's two more endings you can get if you do certain steps.

_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: FANTASTIC GAME!!!Listen, I've played a lot of horror games, some VR, some Steam, etc. I can thoroughly say, that this game is diverse, creative, and above all else  CARES FOR THEIR COMMUNITY!  The amount of effort, constant patches, and dedication the Developer has really brings me joy. Too many games now are on the same structure, and only care about the money, this game is truly designed for PLAYERS.  I see that people are upset that it gets repetitive but honestly, thats the job of someone working in this field, its supposed to feel repetitive, I mean first day in Raymond says, "Treat everything like its normal." So, its that normality and repetitive tasks that I feel not only amplify the horror aspect but makes you more key into details, like a demon under a shelf, in a corner,  a subtle smile, a new bruise, etc.  I RECOMMEND THIS GAME TO EVERYONE!  And honestly, if they made a VR version I would play it all over again! Fantastic job to the Developer! (Also, I went through about two packs of underwear, so I suggest wearing a diaper.)

_childDocuments_.review: So, after a few hours (and a 50% success rate lol), I feel I can recommend this game.  if you're a fan of Phasmophobia-type psychological suspense/horror, this game will make you happy in all your naughty places. Although the different demons don't seem to have a significantly different personality (or not that I've identified in my 4hr of play), identifying them and progressing through everything IS an intense experience. _childDocuments_.review: Decent staple horror game for fans of the genre.Pros:+ Jump scares aren't tacky and are paced quite nicely throughout the game + Not hard to 100% for achievement hunters+ Story "events" are nicely done, although it does require quite a few play throughs to collect them all+ Interesting/good backstory once you have experienced all the events and endings+ Runs smoothly, minus the janky turns with the embalming table  (may have just been me)+ Really fun in the dark (especially with wine)+ Some puzzle aspects to it with needing to match the correct mark with the correct body, as well as one particular event  series+ Puzzle aspects are very user-friendly (ie. not too hard or brain wrecking)+ Does not require high end setups to run wellCons:- The price is probably just *slightly* too much if you dont plan on running through every possible (5) ending, plus all story events and/or achievements.- Embalmed and burned bodies from previous saves dont count towards the 100/50 achievements if you erase and start a new game to go back for missed achievs.

The gameplay is also very enjoyable and the educational value on how morticians perform their duties is very intriguing.I love the demonic element and possession.I give it a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this review by saying that I am a huge horror media fanatic, though I am venturing into horror games more and more recently. My point is, I don't scare easy anymore. So I thought. This game scared the pants off me. It got to the point where my spouse had to lean over me and walk my character into the dark room because I was too scared to do it. I screamed twice, which also never happens. I am so impressed by this game. They bypass cheap jump scares and a lot of horror cliches. Also, it does not let up. Every break from the scares is so tense because you are sure something is about to happen when it's been too quiet for too long. So far, I have only played it through once and sadly failed my task, so I will have to play it again. I have to give it a nice long break in between playthroughs though, I'm still recovering! The hallway I pass through to go to the bathroom in my house has become terrifying. I haven't had this good of a scare in years. Kudos to the developers. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. I like the creepy atmosphere and the spooky jump-scares. The concept of basing a horror game around embalming dead/possessed bodies is also pretty cool. But it's a pretty short game. It's a game that's designed to be played through multiple times in order to get the full experience. Although the developers obviously made the game so that you would learn and see more as you play through multiple times, it still seems to get a bit repetitive, especially when scare sequences are reused. And the concept of having to replay a relatively short game multiple times *feels* like a lazy tactic for developers to stretch out their gameplay (although I'm sure they did work very hard on this project, and it's otherwise really quite good for what it is). All that said, I did enjoy the game and would certainly recommend it to other horror game enthusiasts. However, the $25 price point seems a little too ambitious, and I'm glad I bought it on sale. $20 seems about right to me for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 2023 NEW ENDING:The new (free) content is pretty cool, especially the new ending. It's setting up some possible continuation of the story. Also the "unnatural events"-sliders makes it a little less dull, since there's always something spooky happening.I did a Let's Play of this game, which includes all endings, and also did one more episode with the last ending, check it out here: ----------------------Unique take on the horror genre. You're working as an assistant in a mortuary, but it turns out you have to do most (if not ALL) of the work. Learning the ropes can take a while, and then there's some more stuff to learn about banishing demons. Find out what type of demon, which corpse it wants to inhabit and finally banish it (or fail miserably)!There is quite some work on corpses involved, draining them of liquids and all that stuff. Then there's the horror stuff and finding out more about the demon before you get completely possessed.The whole game presents its main screen with statistics about the "shifts" you did, how many corpses you banished and which endings you got (I believe there are five). It is MEANT to be replayed at least a few times, to see different abnormal events and come to different endings.My first run (including tutorial) took about two hours, but I believe you can do the later runs much faster (30 min to 1 hr).Check out my first experience with this game below (I've marked where the REAL game begins, if you don't want to see the tutorial):EDIT: The Game has quite a few bugs, fortunately I did not encounter any gamebreaking ones.

As someone like the main character [Potential Spoilers] I too suffer from anxiety and depression, and the experiences of the character and this game are wonderful and accurate, it was literally a revisit to some dark places at points in this game and my life so this review is very personal and emotional. _childDocuments_.review: Delve into the somber depths of The Mortuary Assistant, a game that dares to tread upon unsettling grounds with an unapologetic allure. The experience, while initially challenging, thrives on the elusive pursuit of confronting demons, a task that resonates with a gratifying sense of difficulty. What sets this game apart is its narrative complexity, where each ending unfurls layers of a profound and haunting tragedy, enticing players to revisit and unearth its melancholic depths.Visually arresting scenes, though disquieting, captivate the senses with their intricacy, drawing players into a realm where discomfort intertwines with fascination. The game's ability to evoke unease while immersing players in a narratively rich environment is both commendable and unnerving. It's a testament to its ability to engage on multiple levels, offering an experience that is as disturbing as it is compelling. I found myself captivated by the morbid elegance inherent in the game's style, as well as by the profound exploration of the inner workings of a mortuary.Yet, amidst its atmospheric prowess, there lies a slight repetitiveness that may diminish the overall impact for some. However, The Mortuary Assistant remains a commendable endeavor, offering not only a glimpse into the intricacies of its titular occupation but also a journey through distressing landscapes that leave a lasting impression on the psyche.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you someone who loved House Flipper or Gas Station Simulator? Then you'll love The Mortuary Assistant! No, wait, come back! Hear me out!A big part of The Mortuary Assistant is having a predictable gameplay loop. The game gives you a clipboard with your "tasks," just like any other simulator game. There's something very comforting and soothing about knowing exactly what you need to do and how to get there, though unlike House Flipper, you're embalming a body instead of renovating a house. The basic gameplay loop satisfies that "simulator" itch......and then immediately subverts it with hauntings and demon infestations. You'll be minding your own business, mixing embalming fluids together or moisturizing the corpse, when the overhead lights will flicker or you'll hear the distant chime of the front door open or some unseen entity will rudely trip you in the hallway. You can ignore these distractions and carry on with your good work, but things escalate over time. That escalation is how the game's story unfolds, ultimately revealing its full self over each subsequent "shift."The story is pretty decent, though I'm not sure if all the questions I had really ever got answered. Ostensibly speaking, there are five official "endings" to unlock, but I think there might technically be more. No spoilers, but I did find one ending that was outside the five standard endings and broke one shift loop, leading me to assume that there might be more hidden endings. It's this drive to find all the secrets, along with the very satisfying "simulator" loop, that kept me digging around and trying out different things each shift on the hunt for more secrets.If you like simulator style games and enjoy getting spooped, give this game a shot! It's well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: While some horror games have given me scares and unease, this is the rare game that actually gave me goosebumps and chills.The fear in this kind of game is driven by several subtle layers, rather than blatant gore and constant jumpscares.  Working on a cadaver is already an uncomfortable process, providing the unease of a medical setting with some mild body horror as you work your way through mundane, but kinda gross, tasks relating to your work.  This game's greatest strength is that it does an amazing job utilizing blink-and-you'll-miss-it spooks, where you might find yourself catching something out of the corner of your eye only for it to vanish when you turn to look at it.  Or perhaps you notice something horrifying has been perched in your workspace for God knows how long and you only just noticed it leering at you after all this time.  I really would like to see this dynamic explored more in horror games!This game follows has several different endings and some secrets to discover along the way.  The background lore is pleasantly deep and fleshed out, waiting for you to discover it by reading notes or browsing through an in-game database, or through flashbacks or hallucinations.  The storyline, such as it is, isn't entirely unique or unpredictable but it still remains satisfying to experience.

The scare factor does lose its crunch if you try to go for the multiple endings since there is no skip cutscene button at all for every haunt that you encounter but the 5th ending is worth it just for a cry  if you manage to do the correct steps. The story itself is simple and effective at accomplishing a believable story of a I could see this game getting a sequel or maybe its a one time thing but if there's one thing to improve if a sequel does happen is to improve the gameplay loop since it does get repetitive seeing the same scares over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do wish I had an option to give a mid range review. The game is not terrible by any means (I've played 5 hours already so.. ) but there are def places to improve.I think it's a good technique to get a player in a tedious mindset, where you're focused on these simple, but repetitive tasks; it sort of eases your mind a little and sets you up for some good scares. There are some too, but then there are places where things fall flat. The events do seem to be randomized, and there are 5 endings, so it lends itself to replayability, which I DO like. And for 5 hours of fun (I mostly just streamed it to friends), 25 or so bucks isn't that big of a deal. There is a story to it, and you do seem to uncover more of it as you play, which also bolsters that aspect. I don't mind the realism. I really enjoy it, but I can see how it might put someone off. If you're squeamish, this might not be the best game for you. I haven't tried it with lower graphics, so I'm not sure if that'd help. There were some bugs, and still are, though the devs were pretty quick to get a large bunch of them fixed. I appreciate that.My biggest gripe is that I can't skip the ending scenes, so there is a scene I've seen three times already, and oof.. that's annoying. I'd like that option so if I get the wrong ending, I can just move on. I think there is some way the events could be improved, but if you do some a few good hours of fun, and replayability, I think it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: After 2 playthroughs, I'm torn about this review. This game is obviously a labor of love, and for a short spook-fest with some engaging game play, it feels alright and accomplishes exactly what it sets out to do. It has some scary moments without being overly campy, the dialogue is alright and it's neat how some of the "cut scenes" and scare moments are not always the same, with different bodies and different animations that happen. In general, I liked it and I think it was worth the buy for a few good hours of entertainment. It sounds like it's a pretty small dev team, so congrats to them for putting out a neat little horror game that's overall pretty fun.That said, I do have some pretty big issues with the game that make me hesitate to fully recommend it, and I don't know if I'll go back to play through it again. My main issues are:- The inventory system is AWFUL. You can't do anything out of sequence, and if you happen to be holding something in both hands, "large" items can't be picked up. Proving to me that I only have 2 hands is NOT immersive in any way, especially since I never actually see my hands at any point during the game. The inventory restriction is unnecessary and horribly disruptive to the flow of play once you get the hang of what you have to do with the bodies. The sequence doesn't vary, so at a certain point, ESPECIALLY if the devs want me to do multiple playthroughs, I really don't want to be needlessly time- or item-stalled when I'm trying to speed things up a little. It's even more irritating in that a simple fix, like making the clipboard its own button instead of an inventory item, probably avoids most if not all of this issue. - The other frustrating part of this is that you MUST do everything in sequence. You can't multitask. Want to quickly do some things at the body before you go drop off the embalming report? You can't, so buckle up and connect the dots the only way the game knows how. Got the embalmer running and you want to go mix the tank cleaner? Nope, and by the way, if you pick up the tank cleaner, get ready to jockey around your inventory yet again. It starts to feel REALLY clunky, especially since you're doing this to several bodies in a row on a given run. - Checkpoints are laughably sparse, given how often this game seems to crash. In two playthroughs, I've had the game freeze on me 3 times, and two of those three times, it loaded me into the very beginning of the main game, which meant I had to listen to the SAME several-minute sequence of introductory exposition before I could get into the game play, which I'd already done multiple times and once in the tutorial. None of these moments are skipable, so you just have to sit there and wait, which again makes me not want to do it over again. TLDR; Good game, but pretty repetitive. UI/inventory issues get in the way of a smooth game play experience and there are some issues with crashes, all of which IMO make it a bit less replayable than it seems the devs intended.Edit: I'm changing my review to "Recommend" based on the fact that the dev is already very active in and addressing and adjusting some of the issues I have with the game. I also think that, while I might not play it for 20 hours, it's definitely been fun for the time I've put into it, and that deserves some recognition and acknowledgement. I also removed some of the more "spoiler-y" parts of the review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more like a neutral review rather than negative. The game feels amazing in the first hour, but I think it has serious "balance" problems.The idea of the multiple endings (which is very common in small indie games) could mean more replayability, but this is really kneecapped but the repetitivity of what re-playing everything means. The multiple endings are also not really alternative endings, but they add to the lore and give sense to the story (every different ending adds something to it). The lore / story events happening during the normal game are few and are not skippable, meaning that given how many times you are going to repeat the chores (cleaning bodies, which for the same reason becomes tedious instead of tense), you'll be stuck with the repetitive unskippable story events and haunt events, which are already not scary at all by the third shift (and I am really weak at horror games).There is even an achievement of embalming 100 bodies...I mean why is there even such an achievement? You don't nearly come to half of that number even when unlocking every ending, and it's not like the embalming is a challenging puzzle or anything...it's cool in the beginning but then everything is the same. There are maybe 4 or 5 body stamps...never seen a fat woman, nor a child or a black woman. The bodies wear underpants and bras - totally unrealistic and less scary but I understand it could be because of some legal reason. After the third body, it's everything on automatic pilot, trying to figure out that little hint pointing to the other different ending.I think it could be (is?) a nice game but really many flaws in this sense. Technically I only found that sometimes the voices were either much too quiet, or completely mute...so, given that sometimes you hear demon voices etc, make sure you have subtitles enabled so you know you are not missing any line (the subtitles are working).

_childDocuments_.review: -------------------------ADDITIONAL UPDATE-------------------------So I dug it back up and started over, again, to get a fresh, bug-free run. Also, I'm playing on Linux and the game honestly runs shockingly well, considering it's on Proton AND on my workhorse's limited architecture. ANYWAY:So I beat it and got the good ending, and I can officially say that all salt has drained from my blood and mood and I can be fully objective. I will say that what's here is quite good, and it's really impressive for the dev to have produced it. But we're not quite there yet; there are some gameplay conceits that I really don't like (please don't take control away during hauntings; maybe make 'backstory' hauntings optional for a more 'pure' run mode?), but there's also a good number of bug and instability problems holding this one back. I would say I WOULD recommend, but not before either a significant reduce in price (I'd say $15, max, but everybody's judgment is different) or a more stable and less railroaded experience is available. I look forward to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around a little more and also picking this one back up during the holidays to see how far it's come. Good idea, good execution, good work.-------------------------UPDATE-------------------------I've had one of those things where you pull a game out of Hidden because you're not COMPLETELY sure you didn't like it, and after starting over, I got stuck in two different haunts because the things I had to do were unclear and couldn't be done out of order. The first time, it was the apartment, and not knowing I couldn't pick up the Needle item that I COULD find up before finding the Tubing that I could NOT, I was stuck in there for quite some time. Ended up looking up a guide to get through it, and then when I finally did, game just flat-out crashed. It did so again in the blacked-out hallway to cold storage; the lights went completely out and then the game never came out of the black void. Even tried moving around to see if I could catch light off of something or see a light where I supposed to go and there just wasn't.. When I quit out of THAT, now I can't even get to the main menu anymore; it's just a black screen with the save symbol in the center of the screen while the main menu music plays and I can't change it or make any choices to get past it.It is because of these things that I am adding "buggy, railroady, and not ready for prime time yet" to the pile.That said, damn game gave me the itch; I've been having a hard time putting it down and forgetting about it. So maybe I'll pick it up around Halloween and/or Christmas to see if they fix it.-------------------------ORIGINAL REVIEW-------------------------One of the few games to actually manage to get under my skin, but there are mechanical irritations that keep me from really enjoying it. The visuals are super good, the atmosphere is great, it's very spooks, but the controls are obnoxious and inconsistent (why do I have to use a key from the inventory sometimes and other times I just use the door while having the key in my inventory?). Beyond which, there seems to be a scripted sequence of events, or at least scripted points where one of a series of events CAN happen, so repeat playthroughs, you'll get repeat visions and events or whatever. The annoying part comes in in that the game locks you out of working once you've "entered" a scene until you finish it. So for instance, you can be working and you'll notice the color change on the screen. Look up and there's a stringy-haired woman in the hall way. "♥♥♥♥ you", I says, I'll just keep doin' what I'm doin. "No," says the game, "you are locked out of interacting with any bodies or equipment until you have experienced the minimum number of spooks. Now go walk up to that ghost lady and get grabbed."That's already annoying, but it gets worse. Things are conveyed very briefly with tutorial screens, and you can't call them back up. Granted, you can look everything up on the net; you'll pick up your moves pretty quickly, but the fact that I was as confused as I was in my first game, right up until the end, seemed unfair. On which note, I thought I was supposed to be managing my fear because the game says the more scared you get, the worse the hallucinations get. Instead, there seems to be an invisible time meter that you just run throughout a... well a run.The final straw came in when on my third game, keeping in mind the game tells you to look for a reaction (which can be subtle or very unsubtle) when you place the binding tablet in order to know it's the right body. I burned the wrong body on game 2, and I remember nothing happening when I placed the tablet. This time when I did, a symbol burned into the forehead of the corpse and it started talking and the lights flickered like crazy. Seems like a reaction to me, so I burned him. Wrong body again. And I know, the game says that while you're working, the demon may try to mislead you, but I was under the impression that the mark-placing reaction was a unique one, because otherwise, if the demon could still be screwing with you, why would they tell you to look for a reaction specifically when placing the mark?It all seemed obnoxiously esoteric and inconsistent, and after three tries, I wasn't confident enough in my understanding of how it worked that I had anything I wanted to try anymore, so I think I'm done. And that's a shame; I really wanted to like this. Also not a super great use of 25 bucks, but whatever, I guess; that's the chance we take.Anyway, visuals are good, so just wait for the LP scene to get a hold of this game, find someone who does 'em that you don't hate, and enjoy the game that way. I don't think it's worth the expense. Not at least until it tunes its ♥♥♥♥ up pretty significantly.

_childDocuments_.review: I have obtained 3 of the 5 endings so far but I think I have played enough of the game to give a proper review for the game."The Mortuary Assistant" is really a solid horror game that blends suspenseful storytelling, effective jump scares, and psychological fear and confusion. This game manages to create a few chilling but quick moments that make you question what you may or may not have seen. This takes careful planning on the part of the devs because these scares must happen when the player least expects it, but is looking directly (or through peripheral vision) at a common area in the environment. Do it too often and the creepy feeling is lost. Do it at the wrong times and the player may miss these brief scares entirely.While Rebecca's story isn't anything groundbreaking, I did find myself morbidly curious as to what her backstory was. Each shift allowed me to find out pieces of her story until the full picture was revealed. Again, it's nothing incredibly original or mind-bending but it provides the angst needed to make the psychological aspects of the game have some impact.The whole process of embalming the bodies was actually quite satisfying for my OCD. Granted, I didn't have to embalm every single body but it would allow the scares to last a bit longer as Rebecca became more and more on the verge of possession. One aspect of the story is definitely messed up when you consider Raymond's motives. I mean, As for what I didn't like about the game, well, as interesting as the embalming process was, it does get tedious after several shifts. The routine is easy to learn and you can basically run through each shift without much thought. Granted, if you pay close attention at key moments, you may be able to unlock all 5 endings sooner rather than later. However, if you don't find all the clues early, then you have to keep going through the motions with each shift until you do locate them.The replay value is not very high, mostly because the more shifts you work, the more repeated flashbacks and scares you encounter. After so long, you end up seeing certain aspects of Rebecca's past more than once, and see the same scares more than once. I wish each shift could have been truly unique so we don't get the repetition. Perhaps having a set number of shifts would have been best, and each shift would have had its own scares and you would only see new and different flashbacks of Rebecca's past. Despite it's flaws, I still think "The Mortuary Assistant" is well-done horror game that provides the creepy, chilling, suspenseful moments you hope for, and also has a decent backstory for the protagonist to add some depth.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best horror games out there. I played it with the haunt meter maxed out in order to get the full experience. I definitely feel like if u go in this game without previous knowledge of the jump scares u will definitely enjoy it waaaay more than what I did. _childDocuments_.review: I've been following DSD for a while, so I know that they can be extremely brilliant at times, and very disappointing at others.First of all, The mortuary assistant is great. Wonderful. it gives you exactly everything it promises in a very tight package, it looks great, it sounds great, and with many moments that are truly blood-chilling. HOWEVER. The awe factor quickly runs out as soon as you figure out that there's no threat, there's no variety, and there's really no story either.In order. This game is made by (mostly) a single dev, which is fenomenal, because the animations are rough but smooth and believable, the characters look like people (which in the game of the psx-horror obsession, it means a lot), the maps are very well done in terms of size, detail and usage. Everything in the game has a purpose, there's even a purpose for the weird matches that are the only thing you can take in the entrance. As for the game, it's exactly like in the title: you're a mortuary assistant, and wheter or not the tasks you're doing are realistic or not, they FEEL authentic, which is very important.Now, the corpse routine is exactly the same for every single body, and there's always three bodies every night, with no variation and no increasing difficulty. And even though the bodies are randomly chosen, there's only like five possible ones, so you'll see the same faces a lot, considering there's five endings. That means at the very least, to see everything the game has to offer, you'll have to go through 15 bodies, out of the 5 available.The scares and events are also random, which is good, but for at least 5 runs, there's not nearly enough of them. I've actually gone through the same scripted sequence three times in three consecutive runs, and there's no skipping these. You're forced to stop and do them all. On that note, you're not allowed to change the corpse task order either, you have to do number 1 before number 2, even if nothing should be stopping you, and if you start a corpse you have to do the entire procedure, you're not allowed to stop and put it away no matter what.The key here is repetition. There's not enough variety for what the game wants to be, and there's not enough player freedom to be able to circumvent this problem. You're forced to do the same sequence and see the same things over and over for... not a whole lot. The story is basically all in the intro cutscene, and one or two endings. Even then, those two endings only give you a bit more context to stuff you can very well piece together from environmental clues, and the other endings are just slight variations. You even get the same burning cutscene wheter you chose the right body or not. That just makes no sense.End of the day, it's a great game, really fenomenal. But for the price it has, I just wish it offered more than 3/4 hours-ish of stuff, of which, really just about an hour is interesting, and the rest is repetition. Much like me writing repetition so many times in this review.It works great, but you could do better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: A spectacularly terrifying game. It kind of reminds me of Phasmophobia in that it has a lot of random events that will scare the ever loving crap out of you. What I like about this game the most, is that most of the scares are subtle. A shadowy figure ducking out of sight, a face barely seen through the window, a flash of pale cracked skin gone in an instant. These are most of the scares which are punctuated with larger hallucination scares. These scares are bigger and more obvious, some of which being downright terrifying. The entire time you are trying to do two things. Embalm the dead bodies and, more importantly, survive the night with your soul intact. You work through the night while solving a puzzle and guessing which body is the target. The game has a couple of minor issues, I ran across bugs that stopped or delayed my progress, and the voice acting is hit or miss. The animations for the other non-ghost characters is stiff, but those are forgivable. My only real big complaint, is the very high mouse sensitivity. Even on the lowest setting, my mouse swings wildly across the screen at the barest hint of movement. That problem is highlighted further when attempting to move bodies with the gurney which drops the sensitivity to nothing, and then brings it right up in an instant when the gurney is released. All in all this game is easily worth the money. Between multiple endings and a bunch of random events, you'll be entertained for a while.EDIT: They have fixed the sensitivity issue. The gurney now feels sluggish, but intentionally so. There is less disparity between the regular looking sensitivity, and gurney sensitivity. They also added more events since I last wrote this review. Even better now. Well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Mortuary Assistant to me is something special. It´s one of those games that come along every few years where right from the start I feel like I´ve got a little gem on my hands.This one-person-project captures a very specific kind of horror and dread that I can immensly appreaciate. The key is atmosphere. The location the main game takes place in is compact with easy to learn tasks that one has to accomplish as a, well, Mortuary Assistant, quickly becoming your place of work. The structure the game takes makes it easy for the player to build a routine all the while things happen around you that further the horror atmosphere. While there are heavy themes at play here which I will not disclose as to not spoil the fun, the horror-elements rarely if at all rely on cheap jump-scares, which is kind of rare these days and much appreaciated by someone who values dread and horror over disgust and frights in terms of genre-elements. The game builds a very solid and interesting foundation upon which it expands every playthrough (which take around 45mins give or take). There is quite a bit to find and discover. Mortuary Assistant is a compact, well crafted game, designed by someone that knows that the horror-genre can work very well with a more subtle approach. The Dev is also very active in tracking down remaining small bugs and very quick in releasing patches.Do the dev and yourself a favor and give this game a chance as it will probably become a comfort-horrorgame for me over the next months.There´s a Demo too if you want to try it out first.Glowing recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is definitely one of the best horror games I’ve played. Here is a list of things I like about this game and why:The scares/ atmosphere/ vibe – there are many distinctive, well-crafted horror scenes in the game, making each playthrough a unique experience. Furthermore, almost every haunting event has a deeper meaning or hidden message waiting for the player to discover. Despite making you jump out of your chair, the scares in the game are very aesthetically pleasing to me. The game excels at building a suspenseful and eerie atmosphere. You will find yourself constantly looking over your shoulder, wondering when the scares will happen. The story and characters – the story is dark and appealing, seamlessly progressing from ‘fear of the unknown’ to ‘fear of what you’ve known’. The protagonist and her mentor both have intriguing backstories, which are told through dialogue, cut scenes, and journals. The game presents a bleak and tragic story, with thought-provoking themes like necessary evil, grief, acceptance, mental illness, and drug abuse. The endings are satisfactory, and the dialogues are well-written, with exceptional voice acting.  You can hear the emotions in the protagonist’s voice and she doesn’t act like she has never seen a horror movie before. Gameplay – instructions are clear and concise; information is always accessible to the player. The combination of embalming and investigating demons makes the gameplay thrilling and rewarding. It’s always a ‘hell yeah’ moment when you successfully completed a shift. Since there are a bunch of different scares and endings in the game, the replayability is extremely high. The quality-price ratio is high, the game is bussin’, worth every second and dime.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played five hours so far so do expect me to only give my take on just fives hours of this game. so far I have failed miserably to actually finish the first night shift, however every time I die and restart with new scares I came to realize there was more to the story, some scares were giving me insight into the story and the past of the main character. This in itself is amazing, but also the scares themselves are well done. I like the way they play out and how each time you go through a shift it's actually a different demon and bodies (unfortunately sometimes the items move too which can be a horrible and humbling experience, aside from that though I find this to be a cool af feature). The game is pretty too, I love the way it looks. the music is lacking but I think that's for the best because you are left alone with your bodies, the rain, and your thoughts. With the silence the build up to the scares are way better. anyway what I'm saying is for what I've played so far this game is great and fulfilling my need for a cool horror game. Do comment if I got anything wrong as I want to get things right about this (and remember I did only play five hours so there are most likely things I forgot or missed) or to add to this.

_childDocuments_.review: I should love this game, but it feels like its too hard to get the correct ending on a playthrough before you've played it so much that you know all the tricks and its lost all atmosphere and horror.  I think there's something to be said about getting so invested on your first playthrough and then getting crushed by the bad ending. I will certainly remember this game forever, but I'll also be forever convinced I was "right" in my first playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: What this game does good, it does great. The scares are subtle or they match up with the mind of the character. When a jump scare is done, it usually is pretty effective but it's not over done. Also, it's easy to get immersed into the actual processing of the body.That being said, I dealt with so many bugs and had to completely restart at one point. From the jaw wiring shut not working to finding a glitch with mixing the chemicals, I kept having to reload my game. This broke the immersion for me, but luckily towards the end of shift 1, the glitches stopped. This game is really good, but it really needs to fix those bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I would very much recommend this game to others. I thoroughly have enjoyed this game and its emotional story line. The game is randomly generated enough to give an eerie and scary feel to it. This game keeps you on your feet through anticipation and tasks to complete. Each night is different in its own way. The story within the game is interesting and could be relatable to some, it was to me. The only downside I have noticed is a bug where you would fall through the floor and not be able to get back up to the building. (Happened once) (Had to restart) Overall I loved this game and enjoy playing it. I think everyone can learn a thing or two from this game that they can take into the real world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic little horror game with a very creepy premise. It has a great atmosphere with some cool art design. The initial setup is perfect for a horror game and really puts you on edge. Then things start to get more intense as the supernatural parts of the game play out. There is kind of a ‘work sim’ style to the gameplay at first that slowly creeps you out because of the setting. Then the game unfolds into something more interesting with some really cool ideas. I’d be curious to know if the examining bodies gameplay was inspired by LA Noire because the way it works is very similar. The Mortuary Assistant is very clever over all and I can see why it has gotten so much attention online. I’m curious to see what these devs come up with in future games because this game is awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This is so much fun! The scares are done so well, Based on how you are playing, you will experience different kinds of hauntings throughout your gameplay. The scares aren't cheap jump scares or loud bursts of scary music. Most of the scares that got me were noticing things happening just out of the corner of my eyes. One time I was on the in-game computer reading something, when I noticed there was a demon/ghoul watching me over the other side of the monitor. There are 5 different endings, so there's tons of reply value. This is a great game, especially since it was developed by one person. I highly recommend the purchase. I used a controller to play, which could be a little wonky, when completing tasks, but it didn't affect me playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really scary and has an intense atmosphere.However, after 3-5 hours you've seen everything and also unlocked all of the 5 endings.I have currently played about 10 night shifts and the game already lost a lot of the tension.Many scenes repeat and you can almost predict what will happen next.I would recommend it when it's on sale. You will have fun and be scared a lot, but only for about 4-5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of scary games. I'm not too iffy with graphics, but i can sometimes be annoyed with controls but when I get used to it, it's usually fine. I don't mind slow games, but this really wasn't exciting to play, even if i'm a huge fan of some horror and gore stuff. The jumpscares weren't scary either? It gets loud sure There was one startling part that got me and I liked it, but it was the quickest one, and you kinda do expect it happen (the one where you go back and forth in the hall because it's blocked by a wall. The gameplay gets too repetitive and, unlocking the different "scary" scenes just wasnt worth the going back and forth doing the same thing over and over again, mainly because I didnt find them scary or new. It's like a compilation of different horror scenes from different shows and movies compiled into one, and most people have probably seen these scenes ones or twice in movies before. Anyway, so by the time I got to any of the "scary" scenes" I was already too sleepy. BUT if you scare easily, and dont mind doing the slow tasks, then this might be for you. If you don't scare easily and get bored by slow controls and repetitive actions, might want to give this a pass and just watch gameplay of it instead. Or even if you're the latter, just play it to see what it's like for you. Either way, this was my experience on it, it was okay. i would give it a 5.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me think why am I playing this game and question if I had ♥♥♥♥ myself on the amount of unsuspecting situation that unfolded on me. Of all the horror games I have tried and always failed to give me the Immersion I always wanted. _childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: After several years of absence from horror games and after being pushed by friends to try this particular game I have to say that I am surprised by its content and the quality of horror it gives the player. The first time experience is unique and the random generated scare events are amazing!! All and all its an amazing game for a horror night with a very fair price I would say! Hopefully  there will be a sequel!!! I Recommend it 100% for all horror enthusiasts out there!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: If you get this game on sale for a few bucks, it may be worth your time. Other than that, my biggest critiques (without spoiling too much hopefully)- This game REALLY needs a mechanic to prevent repetition in haunts. On my first savefile, I got the same haunt 3 times in a row. A big turnoff as you get bored already.- Game mechanics are really hard to figure out first playthrough. I had to look up a guide. It's confusing.- Processing the bodies is really repetitive- Endings are boring and not worth it- The special endings require specific *random* haunts to trigger.The only positive aspect about this game is some of the haunts/scares, but they only work once of course and tend to repeat.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is an amazing game. It can be downright terrifying at times, and has a good story. The backstory is very well done as well. _childDocuments_.review: Was opening a drawer moved some paper found a key, looked over at my friend who was watching to say "its a hidden key".  Looked back and that white horrific nightmare was right besides me, in a place that I thought nothing could fit.I SCREAMED and scared my friend, his cat and myself to death, he said that he never knew my voice could become so high pitched.To stop myself having a cardiac arrest I have to stand with my back against a wall at all times and I slowly look round now because I do not think I could survive another "viewing" of that nightmare.Great game, I really cant wait to play more but my heart can only stand small doses at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: Changed my review after playing this again following a bunch of updates to the game. The game is fun. We played for a few hours and didn't run into any bugs. Still one of the most terrifying games I've ever played, and the aggression level slider is great. Only thing I will say is that some of the events seem really common (grandma) and not having to sit through them multiple runs in a row while not being able to do anything about it can be kind of annoying. Would love to see a bit more variety in what events show up, but that's just a nitpick. Thanks to the developers for continuing to develop the game and smooth out the bugs.Previous negative review below - replaced by positive one**Some spoilers for events below**This is fun, if terrifying. Not all jump scares, some build up to the scares, which is nice. You never know when or what is going to happen. HOWEVER, on the first shift, we ran in a bug that meant we couldn't continue (body contortion that blocked the face while trying to put the eyecaps in in). Started a new shift and embalmed two bodies, then had to stop for the day. Continued and to re-embalm the second body again (an issue with the autosave function?) and then towards the end of the third got the void glitch after the endless hallway event) and had to restart and re-do the third body. Having to redo bodies because of bugs stopped being fun, probably won't play again unless they're worked out. Would like to get the other 4 endings, but don't have the patience to work around glitches and bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! I've only done a few runs of the game but they were all interesting and terrifying. It takes many runs to get the full story and all the different cutscenes but that's what I love about it. There are so many things that could possibly happen during one shift that each one is very different from the last. I don't really have any problems with the game so my cons a simple things I nitpicked.Pros:+ Great graphics+ Absolutely terrifying & creepy events+ Really interesting story that is slowly given to you over each shift+ Animations are well made, especially from the dead bodies and demons+ Multiple endings+ The basic mechanics are very similar and repetitive but the horror elements break that up through out the shift+ Good price with a fantastic demo if you are still unsureCons:- If you don't walk into the darkness when a body points down the hall to it that hand will stay like that for the rest of the shift- In any animation the clipboard can be pulled up (If you get thrown to the floor the clipboard can be pulled out mid throw), this isn't really a bad thing but I feel it should be locked while in certain scenes/ animationsSteam Curator Page: Full Playthrough & Video Review:

_childDocuments_.review: I decided just to rewrite this review! The Mortuary Assistant has turned out to be my all time favorite horror game, and it makes it onto my top 3 list of favorite games from all genres. I'm a fan of horror movies, books, games, etc, and I don't scare easily. But even after playing this game for almost two years I still jump occasionally!The lore is very rich and well written. There is a lot to discover. I still enjoy resetting the intro and replaying each of the 6 possible endings every few months. The characters have excellent dimension. I am bummed that the developer is going to do one more update and then move on from this game. I could see myself being excited about updates or sequel games for years to come!Also make sure you follow updates from the developer. I have found some other great horror games through his recommendations and from his company! I am looking forward to his future work and cross my fingers that we haven't seen the end of River Fields Mortuary.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: Little over 90 minutes in and I've encountered 2 bugs that have required me to restart the shift I was working on. One where I completely fell out of the world during one of the "scary" events due to a hallway being positioned incorrectly and the game just allowing me to walk out of a door into the worldbox. The other due to one of the demons/entities getting stuck on a desk while trying to run at me. For 25 dollars, this game is pretty weak. I could look past the bugs but the gameplay itself is boring, especially when you realize that none of the "scary" events have any impact whatsoever on the completion of the shifts. You can only lose if you guess incorrectly. Would've liked to have seen item positions change, different bodies requiring different mortician techniques to gussy up, etc. But in the end it just becomes a speedrun of how fast can I grab these items and complete the process before I get interrupted by another forced cutscene, or worse, a game breaking bug.Maybe wait until they add more content or fix all the bugs, but in its current state I can't recommend.tl;dr: It's not very fun, becomes repetitious very quickly, the demon encounters are just tedious and have no real effect on gameplay, and there are bugs which will cause you to lose progress - having to restart the already tedious shifts. I will say that the voice acting is pretty good though, so there's that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This is a horrifying experience that left my heart pounding after multiple attempts. There are several endings and 3 types of monster's you can encounter while you progress your shift, while also several cutscenes that vary based on the run.The most memorable demon i've encountered while playing was the Mimic. He is the pale demon with a crooked smile that loves to show up in random locations. Like along a cabinet, or even in the ceiling tiles! The one I found the most terrifying was when I went outside, I saw the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ standing over the corpse! I was scared to go back inside, as it followed my gaze. Luckily he didn't jump me. Phew!
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a decent amount of potential. If you like jumpscares, this may be a decent game to pick up, but that's about all it offers. Once you see each jumpscare, the only thing left to do is speedrun all the endings. There's 5 endings and together they're all pretty repetitive to complete.My biggest problem with this game is that if you go too fast, the game can't seem to keep up with the jumpscares and you end up locking the game, unable to progress. This is fun for the first run or two but if you are a completionist like me and want to complete games at a decent pace, you're in for a bad, glitchy time.Super frustrating! Can't recommend in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about the plot, characters, story, game play and scares is spot on.I can't remember the last horror game I played with such a randomised yet well designed jump scares.Only issue are the bugs which keep causing me to have to restart part of the game in order to progress.Since this is a small development team and they appear to be listening to the community on this issue, I'm confident that this game will continue to be enjoyable for a while.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I had heard of this game back when Dazplays had showed the original demo on Youtube and had been looking forward to this game for a while. One of my partner's gifted it to me for my birthday during the Halloween sale and I absolutely love this game. I love the story line and the graphics went above and beyond from the demo. The game eerie and every time I thought I had seen all the scares, something new would appear. I bet despite having done over 50 runs there is still stuff I haven't seen. (I really hate the pale white mimic ghost, something about his eyes and mouth just makes my skin crawl.) I like how the items would rotate between at least for different layouts so you didn't get too comfortable with their placement so the grind for the achievements didn't get boring either.I like how the game adds Holiday content for Halloween and Christmas as well, such a neat little touch to add.My only "problem" I'd have with the game is the numbers needed for the "Light Em UP!" achievement vs "Well Preserved." For "Well Preserved" it takes 32-33 runs to preserve that many bodies (that's including the bodies you get to do in the intro.) but for "Light Em UP!" you need to burn 50 bodies. That is a ratio of 3 to 1 for that achievement which means you'll only have had 32-33 bodies burnt by the time you hit "Well Preserved" so that's 17 more additional runs you need to do to burn a body. While you can just enter a shift, leave your house, get out of the car and just beeline to open the doors, grab the gurney and pick a body to throw in the furnace, you can't skip the cut scenes. So, you're stuck  (which takes about five minutes each time) and then rinse and repeating for an hour or so. I feel like the number should be lowered to about 40 bodies preserved if you want to keep some of that grind but be more generous. That's just my opinion though.Despite that I really recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of horror and finds a lot of the games recently put out don't hit that mark. The game is fantastic and really unique in it's play style. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Worth it at full price.I find this to be an absolutely phenomenal horror game. The premise is straight forward, and I found the gameplay oddly satisfying.The embalming process is fairly repetitive, but throughout you have a puzzle to solve based on a multitude of clues and goals. The scares range from straight up jump scares to subtle, to feeling like there's something right over your shoulder and the hairs on your neck are standing up. The game gets an A+ for atmosphere and presentation. I also found the story very well done. It may be repetitive, but the journey through the seemingly monotonous job is where things tend to go off the rails. There is a demo that gives you the basics of what the game is.GAMEPLAY:As stated above the core gameplay is straight forward and repetitive. The goal of the game is to solve a puzzle based on surrounding clues. There is more to the game that you have to find on your own. I will say there's enough there to keep you going, and there's enough endings that fill the whole story and world up very well. The act of embalming the bodies is satisfying on its own, and once you get 2 or 3 done, you'll remember the steps to do it. Finding clues to further your goals also adds some variety to the presentation. Go in blind, and have fun! There is a mode where you just embalm bodies as well. A nice added feature.CONTROLS:The game controls fine. Some of the embalming actions can feel a little janky, but it's easy enough to get used to. Otherwise your typical controls.SOUND:Honestly they did an amazing job with this. It always feels eerie. They set the silence and most minute sounds in all the right places that really add to the eerieness. The silence is also quiet enough that when things happen, it will make you want to look over your shoulder in real life.GRAPHICS:Overall the graphics are fine. Not bad by any means, but they won't blow your mind. The design of things that happen throughout the game are unsettling...at worst.-Is that body smiling? Ohhh no it's just the angle that I'm pus......ohh.....ATMOSPHERE/ENVIRONMENTAs stated above, they nailed atmosphere almost perfectly for what they set out to do. Working in the mortuary already feels off, the visual aesthetic of the mortuary is already off-putting without having any scares done. Once you start your shift, you will start to notice a variety of things.-What was that by that cabinet?! Oh a shado-......ohhhh no no no no no noThere are occasional jump scares, but the way everything is placed is pretty much perfect. Eventually the events may become repetitive and you know what to expect, but I still felt the hairs on my neck standing up on end while playing the game.STORY:I really like how they handled the story here. You have to do some work to put everything together nicely, but when you do I feel it pays off majorly. This is one where everything is given to you once you find it. There are connections you have to make, but everything is there and very apparent once you get the information. I really like what they did, and adding the FREE definitive edition upgrade made it even better than it already was. The main character and anybody else involved in the story kept my interest the whole time.IN CLOSING:I think this game is very much worth your time, and very much worth it even at full price. The game may take about 5-6 hours to get everything, but I enjoyed every minute I spent in this game. I've even completed it twice now. If you're still unsure try the demo, it will give you basically what you're going to be doing, but with so much more involved. I could tell the developers definitely wanted to make something special here, and they did a fantastic job. I look forward to see what they do with this little universe they've created, and where the story goes from here.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my first indie horror games that I ever completed - honestly loved the concept and hauntings, and especially the random cutscenes that would just show up. It keeps the game fresh among the tedium of the job. I love how effective it is, especially story-wise. I felt like the gurney controls could get clunky, but otherwise, the writing is solid. Jumpscares were also fun, and if the job got a bit tedious, it's because well... it is a job. Being a mortuary assistant becomes LESS scary because you know there's real ♥♥♥♥ out there. One of the most original concepts ever executed! Would even champion it next to PT/FNAF franchise. Would have loved to have even more endings, so I'm hoping for that in the future. One of the first games I ever received a speedrunning achievement for!  I really do believe the team is capable of creating an even better sequel in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting just a fun little mortuary game with a small yet delightful amount of ghouls and goblins, change your expectations. This game is surprisingly story-oriented, and increases in intensity as you go along. About as many jumpscares as you can expect in a game like this, but to me, most of the horror is in the atmosphere. This game is INSANELY atmospheric. I had to pause several times and for several minutes at a time to collect myself. It's so easy to quit, but you won't be satisfied until you get at least one ending. You HAVE to venture on. And it is a venture... Spookiness level: REFRESHINGLY intense.Update: It's been a few days since I've played this game, and I've been having nightmares. It has actually affected my psyche. It's made me very on edge and I haven't been able to sleep in total darkness, silence, or alone. I've had my partner on call when I sleep, and panic when she's not there. This game turns real life silence into hell.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and fun to playDoes't rely on loud cheap jump scares, it actually has subtle jump scares like things appearing out of nowhere or at the corner of your eye with no load audio cues (unlike most horror games nowadays) but them just showing up is enough to scare you.It is fun to repeat tasks a lot in the game (some may not find it enjoyable) because each task is short, which makes going through each "Shift" more quick and fun.You can turn off story events to make it even more quick (which helps for the 100% achievements)The problems I have in this game are:. The opening video's background audio kept glitching out. Can't skip the ending scenes (which is annoying when you are going for 100% achievement). Some times controller support glitches out when examining bodies or on the computer and will not allow you to leave the body or computer by removing the "back out" button and to fix it you have to use a mouse to switch to keyboard controls (i think it happens when you pause)overall it is an enjoyable game and I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: is an entertaining cross between an embalming simulator, demonic horror, and detective game. During a lengthy apprenticeship, the protagonist is called in late one night to take care of three new bodies … except something isn’t quite right.The Mortuary Assistant is a fantastically fearful experience that blends its horror, detective, and simulator gameplay to great effect. It is reminiscent of games such as Phasmophobia with its methodical and paranormal undertakings and success is highly satisfying. The scares, though they do include some recognised tropes, are implemented in a tactical way that prevents them from feeling tired or overused meaning the game feels genuinely creepy, fueling the player’s adrenaline and creating an intense atmosphere.The systematic yet disturbing process of embalming is very grounding in comparison to the more full-on task of demon hunting and these two prominent gameplay aspects work in tandem with one another. Additionally, the realistic art style and imposing sound design really help immerse the player and emphasise the visceral and threatening nature of the experience.Overall, the game has a lot to offer and has few drawbacks or flaws. It is a brilliant horror game and would definitely appeal to fans of the genre. It is perhaps not one for the faint-hearted due to its’ gruesome and intense style but I’d happily recommend it to anyone looking to feel genuinely frightened and I’d suggest playing it at night!My full review of this game where I go into detail about gameplay, narrative, and styling is available on .
