_childDocuments_.review: Despite an EXCELLENT IDEA (narratively and gameplay wise), the game falls short of twists and staging skill.First off, the inventory management is terrible. You have "hands" and "pockets" as a restriction, god knows why. So you drop and pick up again and again items you already know what to do with ! Why not being able to stack them ?Also you can't  proceed some steps in the order you want, even though it wouldn't be a problem. So you can't prepare items early for a later use, no. You have to do as the game tought you, once step at a time, and it wont allow interactions outside of set routine. This is all probably made to maximize the player's mobility in the map and jump him with opportunist horror scripts...Thing is, the staging is totally out the window in this game, sadly.If you are used to first person horror immersive games, this wont impress you at all and feel boringly generic.The spook meta here is just the same you've seen everywhere more than often : jumpscare, character appearence, pitchblack, voices, self moving items. I mean you can't reinvent the wheel ok, but if you're meant to use the same old gimmicks, please be subtle to introduce them. Here, it's thrown at you like swinging keys at a cat, expecting you fall for it. The reality is that it's not interesting after a few minutes.It's not "badly" executed, it's just clumsy in my opinion and could be improved ! It needs work on the pacing, on the suspense building, on surprise effect and perfect timing. Even the atmosphere is non-existent, it almost felt like office job. In a morgue ??I was always busy doing something, yet I never got triggered by any noticed "paranormal" event. And I'm not asperger I swear, but having a head showing up slowly, seeing a silhouette or hearing a door bang never raised my blood pressure here. At most it made me "ok bruh, that's... that's super scary I guess", or awkwardly smile.In a way I'm sure this game could even be funny if it was intentionally humorous like Ghostbuster. You know, like prankster spirits randomly taking your corpse subject away with its cart, or swaping items from drawers, closing doors you need to pass by, playing hide&seek with a tool etc. It would be annoying as hell, but what a fun roguelike speedrun experience it'd be !To be fair the game is rather honest, but it's definetly a better experience if you are highly sensitive to spooky stuff.Again, if you are a horror veteran, it's gonna disappoint you.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic horror experience. Play it with the lights off, headphones on and let the atmosphere take over you. _childDocuments_.review: When I picked up this game, I thought this would either be a jumpscare-a-thon or another joke simulator. That's not quite what it is. While it has ton of jumpscares, those aren't the meat of the game. At its core it's essentially detective game, where you need to figure out, which body is possessed by demon.Every game starts with 3 bodies to embalm. The process is fairly straightforward, first examine the body, then embalm it using various tools, that are found in randomized locations. And as you go, things will start to happen. At first it might be as simple as flickering lights, or footsteps, maybe a distant voice. Later you'll start seeing things. And for every body there is guaranteed event, where something messed up happens. Basically the longer you go, the more the demon shows its presence.You might be asking, what do I need to do to banish the demon? You need to to several things- first you need the demon's name, you have to find, which body is possessed by it, build mark bearing its name and finally incinerate the possessed body. You can only burn one body per game, if you get it wrong, either by guessing a wrong body or mark or simply taking too long, it's game over and you'll have to start from scratch. And this is where things get interesting, because you'll need to pay close attention to find clues. Some are subtle, others blindingly obvious. And it's different every time. It also needs to be mentioned, that if you examined and embalmed a body, you're not neccessarily done with it. So, double check everything. This game is really effective at creating paranoia and making you question your own senses. At least initially, we'll get to that later. And there are multiple endings based on your success or lack there of and other things.This is a low budget game, so cutscenes are of questionable quality, lipsyncing and animations in general aren't very good. But the voice acting is impeccable, which more than makes up for it. The writing is excellent too, the characters are very well fleshed out, demons included. There are many things I enjoyed about it, but it's hard to describe without getting into heavy spoilers, so I'll have to leave it vague.And I have to say this- manipulating the gurney sucks, specifically trying to turn it, it feels like trying to move in thick syrup. It's also a little bit buggy, once a body got completely stuck and I couldn't embalm it. All because the game allowed me to pull out a body then close the cabinet door, while the body was out. Don't do that. Another rather disappointing thing is very small number of events, I've played 14 games so far and got quite a lot of repetition. That kind of cheapens the entire experience. What makes things worse, is having more variety would have negative effect on the game as it is. Because it would make chances of getting one of the endings much lower, because it's tied to very specific in-game event. Also, guessing the right body is surprisingly easy, once you know what to look for. I failed two games at the beginning and haven't lost since.So, this game is really unique. Part simulator, part adventure game and I guess you could also say it has some rogue-lite elements to it. And it does work much better than it has any right to.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant.When I play this game I can't help but remember a series of books I read years ago. "I Am Not a Serial Killer", by Dan Wells. I'll leave some quotes here:“Embalming was like... I don't know how to describe it. It was like playing with a giant doll, dressing it and bathing it and opening it up to see what was inside.”"Is a Demon your best friend?" - Mills said."Look who suddenly got judgmental." - John said.On the other hand, I've always thought that it'd be interesting to work in a mortuary or funeral home. And this game gives you that little experience in a simpler way of what it'd be like to have a job like that. Furthermore, you have to discover which body is possessed by the demon and get rid of it, but not before finding out its name. Sounds fun, right?At first it was a little difficult for me to play. I tried to use control but couldn't. When I wanted to change the button configuration, something happened and I simply couldn't. On the other hand, I didn't like the default keys on keyboard so I changed them to my liking and was able to play properly. When you know exactly what to do and how to proceed, that makes everything easier, although the game itself is quite simple.Although the dynamic is the same on each shift and THIS for many players would be repetitive, for me it's not like that. After 20 hours and having gotten all the endings multiple times, the game still surprises me with new scares and manifestations. You always discover something new. I like this very much. There really is a great variety of manifestations. You can see the dedication of the developer here. The game is so well designed that it makes you feel part of it. I wonder if it could be compared to those "Enigma Rooms". If there was one with a Morgue/Mortuary theme, I'm in!It's a different, fascinating and immersive experience. You'll feel watched all the time, and when you let your guard down, BOOM, there's "he" or "she" or.. Corpses walking strangely in the Hallway or corpses levitating while on the "analysis table" or arms pointing places.This game varies mainly in certain events related to the past of our protagonist Rebecca, and the visions that she sees, these being a way of the demon to scare you, break you and make you give up and forget your main purpose: find out its name, the body in the mortuary that is possessed and burn it.I love the fact that the bodies smile in a macabre way sometimes, these are almost always the possessed ones, however, it can also be a deception. Pay attention and use the  wisely.Most of the "scares" are demonic presences, and they're so subtle, that when you realize them it's normal to be a little surprised. Even when they're silent.This game teaches you that the devil is in the details. You turn around to take the Formaldehyde or Methanol, and suddenly the corpse in front of you quickly moves some limb or levitates in the air.The game in general is very good, however, sometimes there are small bugs. In any case, just go back to the Main Menu and continue.The voices are good, especially Raymond Delver and his.. Possessed mother.This game was a gift from a good friend. I appreciate it, it's one of my favorites now. I highly recommend it, and it's even better if you increase the frequency of "Hauntsystem Aggressiveness". I love it! (not recommended if you have heart problems). But be careful. After a few games (shifts) in a roll, the time seems to be reduced and not enough, so you lose faster before embalming the third corpse, or so it has happened to me. Somehow ignoring certain events like phone calls and dark shadows calling you prevent you from 'unfocusing' on your mission, so.. Avoid them.This game will definitely be in my "💙" collection.Conclusion 1: The game is great and the demons are trolls.Conclusion 2: I'm ready to work in a Mortuary. PS: I'll wait patiently for Halloween and Christmas.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique kind of job simulator with frequent, but generally unobtrusive, interjections of jumpy or helpless horror.I haven't played much so far, but overall I really quite like it. The atmosphere is quite good, not as slow and drawn out and suspenseful as some titles, but not a constant tidal wave of jumpscares, either. As a Mortuarial Ignorati, it's fun to get little bits of info about the chemicals being used and things. I would personally enjoy seeing more comprehensive flavour text in future!Overall, it's interesting, and it seems to have an attentive Developer and Supporting Community. There aren't many titles like this, and a number of them are geared towards a more lustful audience, so I think this is a good addition to the Steam Store.I definitely recommend this game more-so for people who like atmosphere more than action. Of course, if you like morprohilogy, then hooray!== BEFORE YOU BUY ==- The Demo is misleading, little problems like gurney control are not present in the full game!- Game Length complaints can be misleading! What may seem like 'Replaying' in other titles, is apparently 'Continuing' in this one, though that is debatable in some ways.== BEFORE YOU PLAY ==- Be Sure to Press the 'CLOSE' Button after changing your Settings, if you just hit [Esc] they can look changed, but remain unchanged in-game.- Turn on Subtitles, if you do so during a Cutscene they will not start showing until the game loads the next 'section', as it were.- Consider turning down the Volume more than you think is wise. The Dynamic Ranges in this game may be a little high for some soundsystems. Your Character, certain FX, and some Cutscene Dialogue can be very loud, but the Phones and Tape Recorder, for eg, tend to be very, very quiet. Categorised Volume Controls are planned, but right now it's a Global Volume setting.- Consider turning your brightness up a little. I know it makes games less scary, but in this game the 'main' room (as I choose to label it) has a central light, and useful objects against the walls, meaning that your own shadow is usually in the way of the things you need to populate your inventory with. As you grow used to the objects you may well be able to reverse this, but at first it can be a little obstructive.- If something is occurring, and you can't seem to interact with anything, try moving around the 'map' a bit. Some instances expect you to be in a certain spot.---If you genuinely have interest and wanna buy, just buy. Otherwise, here are the things that irk me...TIME WASTING!- Putting Form details into the Record System is fine, but entirely pointless, so it would seem thus far. If we had to choose specific things from the total data collected, that would be different. In a Detective game for eg, you may be tasked with deciding which traits are relevant to a suspect's involvement in a scenario. However, this is just clicking every clickable option on screen back and forth for 20 seconds, with no options that would cause you to fail or do any better. Ultimately, this could be handled automatically without having any impact on the process of the game.- You can no longer select a marking on the left-hand side of the torso, when interacting with the right-hand side. In the Demo and even in the Tutorial of the full game, this was possible, but on Shift 1 it is not? I really have to close menu and walk all the way around the table to open the same menu and click something I could already see clearly? Animals are kind of programmed to be annoyed by stuff like that...- You have to do everything on the Clipboard in EXACT order... You can't Mix Tank Cleaner and bring it into the room early, and please, please let us apply moisturiser while the Machine is washing itself. Standing there for no reason, waiting for the next interactable icon to pop up, really emphasizes the staggering of pace.Similarly, you cant open one eye, place an eye cap, then close that eye, you have to place both caps to close either... It's just odd- and again - staggers the player's pace. Thank the devil that you can fill an IV bag while the body drains!- You can't skip the ending Cutscene. I got the same one twice in a row and I had to listen to it all over again...Similarly, I have to pick up keys and click on my front door at the start of every shift? If nothing happens in the apartment, and I can't do anything in the apartment, why am I in the apartment?NO CONSISTENT QUICK-CLOSE!- Some [LC] interactions can be cancelled with [RC], that's good, that's intuitive. Quick Inventory opens  closes with [RC], also good.But there is no fully consistent Close/Back key! I'd personally lo-o-ove if [Esc] closed ANY menu or interaction, and ONLY opened the Pause Menu when other menus and interactions (such as looking at the Clipboard or inspecting a limb) were closed. Alternatively, it would be nice to have a Keybind specifically for backing out of things.It's a small thing, but it makes games feel so much more fluent that I tend to miss it.---PS It is a Criminal Offense, that I cannot mix Coffee and Toothpaste, and make a lovely minty drink... IN MY OWN APARTMENT! T.T

_childDocuments_.review: I've played other survival horror games similar to this before, but Mortuary Assistant has a different vibe. The atmosphere created by the developer, combined with the music and sounds effects and the unsettling nature of the game create quite the immersive experience.  It's part horror survival, part mortuary simulator (which would have been fun on its own).  The jump scares are actually scary, especially if you are wearing headphones or have audio turned on.As a former licensed funeral director and embalmer, I was surprised to see certain elements included in the game that were accurate (or close enough), and others of course that were not so much.  I would love to consult on games like these, so if anyone is considering a mortuary simulator type game, I would be happy to help!!IF YOU ARE SQUEAMISH, I DON'T RECOMMEND READING ON FROM HERE:What's accurate you ask?  1. Storage of the bodies in a cooler or refrigeration.2. The setup of the embalming room is fairly accurate, although the desk, computer and other "office" essentials would not be in the same room. The tank cleaner would have been kept in the embalming room for convenience. 3. You would not be embalming a body without wearing PPE to some degree--an water resistant apron or cover, shoe coverings, rubber gloves and a face mask or splash guard although I usually worked without shoe coverings (RIP dress shoes) or a face mask or shield. Old school embalmers did not wear any PPE or gloves even. Ew.4. The implements used in the body preparation sequence including eye caps, needle injector and the wires used to close the mouth; the embalming machine and chemicals used (although you would use formaldehyde OR gluteraldehyde, not both. Gluteraldehyde was supposed to be a more "user friendly" option and less likely to cause cancer from overexpsoure.)  5. The trocar is accurate enough, although most had a tip for piercing that would not require incision, there was a rubber hose and apparatus for connecting the trocar directly to the cavity fluid bottle, and you would also need to inject the organs in the lower quadrants of the abdomen. The game only does the upper quadrants. The sounds the fluid makes going into the cavity are eerily realistic!6. The incision in the neck is too high up in the game and would be visible at a viewing unless you were dressing the body in a turtle neck or using a scarf. The accepted method would be an incision just above the right clavicle that runs parallel to the bone and allows for easy access to the carotid and jugular.  There would only be one PVC tube connected to an arterial tube for injection, and we typically used a long angled forceps for drainage from the jugular. The game does a good job of depicting the process with the blood running down the table into a drain. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: The horror aspects, the game itself, the idea of working as a mortuary assistant, excellent. There's things to be enjoyed about this game, and I will continue to finish. But i'm downvoting this game, because as someone who needs visual guides, finding the demon related stuff on the night shift took me so long. I found the card that's meant to unlock the computer night shift right away. But I had no clue you could turn things around and proceeded to assume since it couldn't go in my inventory there was nothing special about it. I proceeded to spend all my time finishing bodies and couldn't for the life of me find the way you're supposed to look at demons names, no guides online helped, they purely showed the computer screen on the demon names already. Maybe the tape mentioned this but I do have memory loss and I listened to it 5 times and do not remember it mentioning HOW you look at the demon names, only simply that they were on the computer. Maybe a click icon near the Three Houses would be a nice indicator? Also the music, the god awful music after finalizing your last body, it's terrible. I was still confused about what to do at that point and I hadn't even figured out where all my sigils were. The music continues and doesn't stop until you burn the body and I hated it, quite frankly I was so immersed until that music came on, the repeated soundtrack, the same noises just made me mad. I didn't want to play it anymore, I wanted to get off. I know to avoid it next time but there should really be a way to turn off that music without turning off the whole volume because I enjoyed the ambience and floor creaks, and creatures coming at me, I liked to know when they were there. The audio ques were excellently done for those parts. Until that little 5 second looped, repetitive music track! With a bit of a more direct tutorial in accordance to the night shift, and the music either being able to be turned off, or turning off on its own after a certain length of time passing would be wonderful and would improve the game for folks who struggle to make sense of an environment. I had two friends watching me play through and even they were confused. It just needs improvements. It's just not worth the price right now  from my perspective unless you like the irritating sound of the same track of music and the frustration of pooping your pants from scares while trying to find what you're supposed to be doing

I cannot believe it was developed by one person, alone.Granted, there have been some bugs that I have run into which have been pretty annoying (though I number of them have already been patched out). But, the overall experience has been well worth the cost of admission.From the developers explanation, the game has something running in the background called the Haunt System.  This system is setup to provide Dynamic scares based on a number of different factors. Some of the factors mentioned: What stage are you at in the shift, how quickly are you running through it, what have you interacted with, what direction is the player facing. The Haunt System uses all of these factors to determine the best scare to serve up to you at any given time.It's pretty awesome, I highly recommend the purchase.If you are not inclined to purchase the game but still want to see what it offers. _childDocuments_.review: I went in mostly unspoiled and man, I was just handed stinker after stinker here.The gameplay loop is well enough, you figure out where your tools spawned and then go through the embalming checklist as hauntings progress and you find more clues as to which demon is riding which corpse so you can burn them back to hell. Cool idea! However, major caveats ensue. The scares are usually kinda banal, and at times outright comedic.This game contains a number of outright terrible depictions of addiction and mental illness. One of the big scary reveals is that your character takes antidepressants, and at one point you are made to go through the motions of doing heroin.There's an interesting concept here, and certainly some budget and effort went in, but the hackneyed faith-healer nonsense underpinning a lot of it makes it feel so much cheaper than it might have otherwise been and every time I found myself in a setpiece haunting I quickly found myself just hoping I'd find an exit sooner than later.I'm glad the devs succeeded, the effort IS on display, but I sincerely hope they've improved their scope of the world and life experience since then because man these themes are blowhole booty butt cheeks.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant (TMA) is a horror game with a unique premise and randomly generated scares. It is designed to be played multiple times to uncover the full story and experience the other endings. I have had this on my radar for a long time, but with its short play time and repetitive game design, it is not a title that I would look at going back to, but it does manage to still deliver a haunting experience that horror fans will enjoy.The protagonist, Rebecca, is a recent graduate in Mortuary Sciences and has begun a traineeship at River Fields Mortuary. Rebecca has worked hard in the role and is on the cusp of being signed off and given a permanent paid position, when the rumours begin to become a reality. The protagonist then suddenly finds herself thrown into the world of the supernatural and is trapped at her workplace, but she is not alone. There is a demonic presence connected to one of the bodies in the morgue, but which is it? Finding the answer to this question will determine Rebecca's own survival.The story is simple, and Rebecca's past is only referenced vaguely. This aloof description of her personal life is purposeful, as it is slowly revealed in the story sections scattered throughout the gameplay. This game design choice to only reveal crucial story elements during multiple replays of the game and to have them only randomly spawn, is not something that appeals to me. Replaying multiple times to try and grasp a better understanding can result in the same events repeating,  the same ones previously seen in the last playthrough. Not to mention the already repetitious embalming process going alongside this as well. To me, this was tiresome and a poor way of trying to keep people replaying.TMA immediately appealed to me with its uncommon setting . To work alongside cadavers, experience creepy, randomly generated spookiness AND complete the embalming process, I thought, count me in! This element of the game, its setting, did not let me down. It is such a small environment, yet the developer(s) use this to its maximum potential and deliver some decent scares.Being a mortuary assistant, players must embalm bodies, repeatedly. This process is made easy with a step-by-step checklist on what to do. drain the liquid within the body, inspect for physical markings, enter data into the computer, sew the mouth shut and so forth. Just a normal day of work. After the introduction, supernatural events begin to occur and  through a series of tapes left by your boss,  you learn your main objective is not the embalming, but to locate the demon that is trying to possess you. This is done by locating  sigils which are scattered around the building, only becoming visible after using the Letting Paper which burns when a symbol is nearby. Gather the four sigils to make The Mark, put this on the body (that the demon is bound to), burn it and voila, job complete. I found the process very straight forward and too easy to guess. After my first playthrough and learning the basics, the second and subsequent attempts are simple and brief. I did not need to even inspect all of the bodies to work out which the demon was bound to, nor did I need to try and find all of the sigils. Having found only two, there was only one combination it could be out of the nine patterns. I suppose I could have purposefully guessed wrong, or let myself be possessed by waiting down the timer and receive a different result, but this seems null to me. Yes, the title is creepy. It does not rely on jumpscares which was a big relief, as these become tiresome fast. Instead, the scary moments are mostly random and some you may not even notice, perfectly building up tension within the players. Some examples include, a figure popping up in the window when you are at the other side of the room, a figure crouched on top of the cabinet. Eyes looking at you from afar, the lights going out, subtle noises and the list goes on. I very much enjoyed my initial playthrough. I found the gameplay to be innovative and interesting and I did not know what to expect. Unfortunately, this did not carry through in subsequent playthroughs and I experienced most of what I had already seen and done previously. Embalming the bodies was once an exciting and new task, but after already doing it four times in my first playthrough, to continue to do it (in the exact same checklist style) for each and every "shift", multiple times... is boring. It is clear that the developer(s) have great ideas for the horror market, but a repeated formula in this instance did not appeal to me. I imagine it would appeal to streamers, people who are new to the Indie horror market or those who simply scare very easily. Perhaps these are the developer(s) target audience, but at least for me, an Indie horror enthusiast, this design choice was a bit of a disappointment.The introductory scene with the awful lip syncing and character models was shocking, but thankfully, this was not indicative of the game as a whole. Graphics are decent, nothing breathtaking, but detailed enough to make the cadavers appear haunted. Majority of the demons are seen in fleeting moments and have a simple design, such as the ceramic-looking crouched demon, always lurking around corners. Its all-white flaky appearance with bulbous, dark piercing eyes is sure to catch players off-guard.Voice acting is decent. There are the odd door closing/creak sounds, light switches and even some demonic voices. However, I think the audio could have been used more to keep players on edge, or at least to mislead the process of trying to find out the demons name, which I found painstakingly easy. Took me around 2.5 hours for one playthrough, subsequent playthroughs less than 30 minutes. Player choice, but I imagine entering data into the computer would be more difficult using a controller. Yes, to achieve the five endings, find the extras and see the full story events (but see Story section for a more detailed summary).This review may come across as quite mixed, which it is, but I still enjoyed my time in TMA. In summary, I loved my first playthrough, the setting is fantastic and unique, the scares and intense atmosphere is chilling, but the game design choice to rely on replays to learn the protagonist's story, which may or may not even trigger, combined with the already repetitive embalming process is not encouraging for subsequent playthroughs. Overall, The Mortuary Assistant is a short but enjoyable experience for horror fans,  but at least for the moment, I recommend it at a heavy sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game would be boring, but it's actually really fun. I like the atmosphere of the game as well as the designs of the characters and demons. The Halloween seasonal content was a lot of fun, especially the clown, which I'm sad was only there for a limited time. There is more variety to the gameplay than I expected, with finding demonic sigils and preparing the bodies. I enjoyed the different endings too. Overall, it's a spooky game with quite a few jump scares. Jump scares aren't scary to me, but they are done well in this game. There are also "quiet" scares that I enjoyed such as figures just silently slipping into view before disappearing. It's fun spotting them each shift.I like that each shift is different and you have to pay close attention to figure out where the demon is, so it would be fun to have more content added. I'd like to see different types of shifts and a couple new characters. Maybe you get a visitor wanting to see the body of their deceased loved one and you have to deal with that on top of everything else. Or you have to visit another mortuary to help a fellow mortician. I did not like playing as a specific character. It would be more fun to me if you could create a character (or choose from multiple ones) and select different backstories that influence how the demons scare you.Honestly, I find the gameplay to be a bit... "cozy" in a way lol. I get so involved in the work of embalming that I don't notice the haunts half the time and find them annoying, like let me do my job, demons!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best designed horror games. If you are looking for a game that will genuinely give you nightmares, then this is the right game. It's not like some horror games where it's all just gore and jump scares. There are a bunch of scares that you just notice out of your peripheral vision, some you might not even notice if you're not paying close enough attention. The scares are super well done, none of it feels tacky or anything like that. My biggest complaints about this game: 1) Once you do enough shifts, some haunts and gameplay become repetitive. The game is great because there are so many scares, but there are a few scares that you have to sit through that just take a long time. 2) Another complaint is that, the tutorial makes it seem like a bit of a detective game, but the bodies and demon become really obvious after playing the first 2 shifts and very little detective work is required after you discover the pattern. 3) If you want all the endings, a lot of it is rng and very specific things you need to look up. After being on shift 8 or 9, I was ready to be done with this game, but was just trying to trigger certain scenes to get the different endings.Overall though, I would give this game a positive review because the horror aspect of it is so well done. I have yet to see a game that compares to this in terms of raw horror (I think this is scarier than RE7, Outlast, Alien Isolation just to name a few). Definitely recommend if you are looking for a game to piss your pants.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant a.k.a. "The Autopsies of John & Jane Doe's".  Most horror games don't scare me anymore, and this one is no different.  With that being said, it is an incredibly creative mashups of the dad-core sim genre (Power Washer Simulator) and survival horror, with much emphasis and thought put into the latter.  Using a randomized haunting system that adds variety through each play-through, it makes what would otherwise be tedious on replay interesting.Wear your brown pants for this one and wait for Andre Ovredal's lawyers to issue a C&D to Dread XP.  Until then, enjoy this wild ride!

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of horror games struggle to find the perfect middle ground between holding the player’s hand too much and doing too little to offer the player any direction. Both can lead to the player being taken out of the horror experience. Mortuary Assistant finds that middle ground pretty well and for that reason alone it’s worth a play.Are the graphics the world’s greatest? Nah, but they don’t need to be (and during the process of embalming the bodies it’s actually maybe better that they aren’t because ew), it manages to be plenty creepy with what it offers. If you’re in the mood to be spooked, Mortuary Assistant is solid, and it’s interesting enough to where friends or family will find themselves watching you play and not getting bored. That’s a big plus on a movie night!

_childDocuments_.review: A horror game with:* A good story* Effective jumpscares* Difficult puzzles that you can still figure out without having your hand held* Good voice acting* Randomness done well* Lore that can be entirely uncovered in-game without a wiki or ARG nonsense* Grim sense of humor used sparingly* AND a perfect level of self-awareness for the inherently goofy parts of the macabre subject matter...It's like threading the eye of a needle while the needle is still buried in the haystack.  I watched Let's Plays of this game first before purchasing it and it *still* scares me.  The story is *still* heartbreaking.  This is the least "indie-horror game" I've seen an indie-horror game be in years.  There are still some visual bugs, control frustrations, and even the sadly random run-ending bug if you're unlucky, but the dev seems very proactive in patching bugs and making improvements, so I 100% recommend this game regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect little game for Halloween. You play as a young woman thinking that her job will be that of  a humble mortuary assistant, but it turns out to be much more than that. The story is very well-paced, there are multiple endings and it's easy to make a mistake unless you're very observant. The creator of this game knows what tension is and how to build it. The sounds and visuals enhance the mood of the story. If you'd like to get some chills but are a bit tired of shooting zombies, this is your go to game. I hope there is a dlc or a sequel as the lore for this one can certainly be expanded.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite horror games to come out this year! A one-man dev team, this guy REALLY knows how to creep under your skin with subtle scares rather than loud jump-scares. Make sure to play this game several times to get the full story! Highly replayable. Very much looking forward to enjoying the game even longer because he is updating the game with new features!

_childDocuments_.review: Going against the grain here and giving this a negative review. To be edited later, if things suddenly change and take a better turn... I will try again later too. Maybe it will change my mind and I can change my review, but this is first run view point and  I bought this on a sale. It was initially pretty spooky. Had some shock and awe factor... I was early on infuriated at the random items strewn about the room. It really broke immersion for me. Then later found the game setting to stop the randomizing items...which omg.. godsend. I enjoyed it a bit more but then.... the tedium kicked in... the first few times I ran through the scripted events they were genuinely interesting and spooky... but that quickly waned. By the end of the night I was yelling at grandma to just go away so I could get my work done and frustrated because I couldn't figure out which paranormal scripted event was preventing me from doing the embalming part of the job... I'd already got all the runes, figured out the demon and just wanted to burn it with the mark in the fire, but one of the many different incarnations of activity were preventing me from finishing the job.Then the bugs... the shadow, who I named Charlie... just kept popping in and getting stuck in the area for long periods of time. Sometimes I'd get stuck sitting down with no head...have to restart. The key binds and ui feel janky and irritating. The story has potential of being interesting but the way the game is designed to have random events along with the bugs and the randomness of the story scripted events, it doesn't really let me see the story in a linear fashion and that's just a bit off-putting for me. I wanted to know her story...and by the end of my session I wasn't scared by any of it and was more frustrated by the events preventing from seeing the story. I would love to see a linear mode, where each shift gives you a piece of the story until you have everything sorted out. I wanted to like this, but it's just not scary being stuck in a scripted event I've seen for the tenth time.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave the game one more shift to make sure I didn't get unlucky, and I've decided to change to a "not recommended". I had  repeated, unskippable story events and once again didn't get the event required for the good ending. No wonder there's a setting to turn them off. Always good to bring up, so you know if it's "worth it". The game is quite short at about 3 hours. That will get you through 3 playthroughs with most of the content if you don't lose (and it's really hard to outright lose). Once you find HER, that's pretty much the whole game. It says there are 5 endings, but that's a lie: There are 7. 3 of them are natural story progression, 1 of them is being bad, 1 of them is a meme, 1 of them is being  bad, and 1 of them relies on a specific story even that isn't guaranteed after the third shift - meaning if you're half-decent you  have duplicates before getting it. So, realistically, 3 hours. It's  I just think the reviews have been hyped by Youtube. It's a decently spooky game, but it does rely on jump scares. A couple times it had phenomenal sequences of just pure atmospheric/psychological horror, but that probably lasted 5 minutes of my 4 hours playing.  Just... implementation makes this less than what it  have been, which is a shame.For instance: they didn't implement a system to only give you unique scares/scenes until all of them had been exhausted. In my 4 shifts, I saw the same unskippable minute-long scene three times. I looked at my phone during a horror game - that's bad. On the third shift, the minor scares started to repeat as well. And while they're still scary if they catch you off guard, you become desensitized to it pretty quickly. On my fourth shift, the game was mostly just a repetitive embalming simulator while I waited for the 1 or 2 story events in the shift. I might do one more shift to give it a fair chance - in case there's more content and I got unlucky with RNG.Another example: the scares themselves. Subtle events are so easy to miss once you get in the groove of treating the dead. You'll go to enter data in the computer and will turn the corner so fast the spookster doesn't even register. Then you're in the computer menu by the time the "scare sound" happens. Or you'll run around a corner to fill the IV bag and clip right through the spookster. And some events can be outright ignored with no consequences: there was a ghost at the end of a hall and I just closed the door and kept working. I still heard spooky music, then the light in the hall clicked off. Not superbly spookstery.The game just doesn't set up the atmosphere needed to really have those subtle scares pay off continually. This works in the quiet parts of Outlast or Amnesia or Dead Space because there's a fear of being harmed or attacked, with the ambiance playing off of it. There's a constant tension at play. But this game is just too comfortable. I thought it would change once  but all but the first shift completion resets the timeline, I guess. It's pretty clunky. Once you've seen an item once, the descriptions that pop-up and require you to press "E" are just annoying. Gurney movement is atrocious, the mouse sensitivity plummets to near 0 and you have to throw your mouse across the table to make a 10* turn. The sliders are finicky. It's pretty buggy and it's easy to screw up the controls or a scene by, say, taking out the clipboard on accident. Turn off two settings: (1) holiday decorations, they're not well done and interfere with the events. You have to turn them off BEFORE a shift, the setting does not apply to a shift already active even if you reload the game. And (2) the item location randomization. Who thought that was a good idea as a default setting?

_childDocuments_.review: Sept 20, 2022Full game completion update (11 or so hours in)The difficulty in this game is basically, they move the items/tools around to makeyou take more time getting lost looking for them. Feels like a weird way to add "difficulty". This is actually where my original confusion came from during my5 hours of night/shift 1 (where as most people beat it around 2hours). During theday/tutorial the items are in a specific place, then in night one they're somewhereelse. I can't imagine what the "lore-friendly" reason is, the demon/s are walking aroundcarefully re-arranging your items on the shelves/counter/cabinets. If you want toblame it on the demons, it would make more sense to just toss all the interactablesall over the room (but allow the player to place things on surfaces, instead of justdropping them at our feet on the floor only).A nice QOL change would be to allow the player to place things on surfaces.Currently you can only drop items on the floor at your feet. Another QOL change,would be to put the clipboard (that uses an inventory slot, even though it's not ausable item) on the wall somewhere so we can still hold 2 large objects. Or just a whiteboard/chalkboard/markerboard with the checklist on it. No matter how I thinkof it, it shouldn't be a thing. From a game standpoint or realistically.I like the different endings and how's there's a little replay value. I wish more gamesdid stuff like this. An idea I had (maybe for a sequel?) would be if it was limited to a certain amount of nights, all with multiple endings to unlock (like how it is currently, but not infinite nights to play). Then depending on the endings collected for the nights you played, you get a unique ending as a whole.___________________________________________________________________Probably a bug, but the "high DPI" setting seems to turn itself either on, or off at random times. In the apartment, my sensitivity is always sluggish, no matter what it'sset to. So i'll either turn it off or on (which ever it isn't, because no matter what it's setto, I HAVE to toggle it to the opposite setting). Then when I leave the apartment and play the night the controls are sluggish again (even though the setting is still set as itwas in the apartment). This makes me toggle a few times between high DPI on/off. Sometimes it fixes it with it off, sometimes on. I tried to find a pattern, but couldn't.___________________________________________________________________On top of this, there are several different buttons that interact/return-from-interacting. I'd like it if there was a global interact/drop button. Some things you interact with E, or space, or left click, or right click...and you put them down with q, or right click, or Esc (sometimes not the same button you used to interact with them). ___________________________________________________________________(Original review posted after first play-through of 1 shift, lasting 5hours below)The Confusion Assistant This game is so confusing, most of it I don't understand. Huge info-dump at the beginning, with no tool-tips/verbal cues to keep you on trackof what to do. You have a clipboard but that's only partially helpful.I've spent 20-30 minutes trying to find chemicals before (on to that later), or what Ishould do next. I really feel like the "post tutorial/training" activities should bepracticable, especially with how much of an info dump it is. Hey, it's later. I played on the lowest graphic settings. When you do this, one of the chemicalssitting near the connecting-corridor doors becomes completely illegible. Oddlyenough, the back of your bosses card can still be read fine.Unfortunately, these problems persisted throughout my entire play-though makingit almost unbearable to enjoy. When I finally started having fun, I died. I bet you're wondering why I chose to "recommend" this game?Because of the scares. That's it. Most horror games don't have SUBTLE jumpscares.You're usually bleeding from the ears at horror games. Not this one. The scares arethere, but they're quiet. They lurk in the dark like batman. They just waiting for youto notice them like you noticed senpai. Horror games need more subtle scares,lurking scares like this game has.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: This game has it all: - An engaging, detailed story with character development for main and side characters.- "High quality" jump scares, the type that doesn't need to blow your ears off with loud music, because the visuals, the timing and the monster designs are more than enough.- Good voice acting and soundtrack.- If you play long enough and stop getting scared, the embalming mechanics still remain enjoyable and become almost relaxing (which is why I suppose we have an "embalming only" mode now).- High replay value, for either finding more about the characters and story, unlocking different endings, or just "enjoying" the embalming process, as I mentioned before.Amazing, very original and scary game. I regret spoiling myself too much from watching others play it before trying it myself.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Its got a really cool concept and cool secrets that reward you for looking into everything. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:This game is not worth the asking price. The systems are too shallow and the game is too unpolished to justify it. It feels like a gimmick after a few hours. Buy on sale if you really want to try it. Someone needs to just make a game dedicated to performing extensive autopsies and funeral prep. This ain't it. This was a hard one to vote on. There's a lot to like in it. There's also a lot to not like in it. For the price and what you get out of it I cannot recommend it as is.The hook of this game got me when I saw that you actually did the prep work on cadavers. I initially hoped for some kind of extensive autopsy and mortician simulator. I feel like the game was even kind of marketed as such, with the exception of all the scary stuff added into it. What a cool concept! Something that hasn't been tried in the world of simulation gaming and I was so excited to see what they had in store. I saw the pictures of a dead man's mouth getting sewn shut and was certain this game would have hours of cool and macabre duties to get into. But it doesn't. In fact, after you play it for a few hours you realize its a shallow gimmick. Let's break down the game-play loop.If its your first time you have to watch a few cut scenes and get acclimated to the story and characters therein. The story feels more like a scenario than a fleshed out story. Basically your a person who needs a job so you decide to work as an assistant for a mortician -like the name...There is a main character and a few supporting characters with a very tenuous plot that gives you just enough to get invested. Voice acting is not too bad, but the animations feel a little exaggerated and running it on ultra still leaves you deep in the uncanny valley. You go through a tutorial section where you learn the process you will perform throughout the rest of the game. After that, the mortician sends you home and you hang out in your apartment for a bit before heading back. That night, you go back and work on three bodies that need to be taken care of. Its rainy and spooky and you will certainly poop your pants. The game will make you jump and scream and feel uncomfortable -its great at that at first.  You'll be working on things or entering data and something will move in the corner of your eye and when you look up its some it will be gone. You'll walk up to a door to open it and something will be on the other side peeking in at you and its so subtle you don't notice it until you're getting the crap scared out of you by it. I loved that. It isn't all about big bang scares in this, its got a nuance to it that respects the art of the scare and makes you feel like it was an earned scare and not a cheap jump. They really nailed the atmosphere and horror, but the problems arise with the illusion that this game has enough content to justify its price with multiple play-throughs. After my first few shifts, I was noticing the same events happening over and over. The night is exactly the same, the weather is the same. Everything in the mortuary is the exact same as it was the first time. The second play-through is not as unique as everyone's been saying. In fact, the gameplay is so linear that you cannot do anything besides a series of specific things in a specific order until the next cut scene happens. I'm gonna spare you details but heres the loop:Your goal is to find out which body is possessed by a demon and burn it. To do that you have to uncover 4 sigils around the building, and figure out what the demon's name is, as well as the correct body its tethered to. Don't worry, you'll figure it out. Its purposely vague to both pad game play time and to make room for the spooky stuff. Arrive at mortuary.Loot the same items each time: Clipboard, notepad, letting strip.Grab one of three corpses out of cold storage.(spooky stuff happens in background)Wheel them to lab where you perform your tasks.Use your clipboard to document any moles, lesions, abrasions etc the corpse has.(spooky stuff happens in background)Put the info you copy to to clipboard into the computer database. (spooky stuff happens in background)Get a little spooked. Use the letting strip to find your first demonic sigil.(That part can be done whenever I think, just do it periodically)Print the document you just filed.(Yeah you gotta use an inkjet)Take the printout to the front room and put it in a file holder.(spooky stuff happens in background)Go back to the lab, grab a needle, mouth wire and some eye caps and sew the cadaver's mouth shut.(spooky stuff happens in background)Apply eye caps to eyes and close themCreate embalming mixture by mixing different ingredients in a specific order into a really loud machine.Grab scalpel, pvc tubing and artery forceps.Cut cadavers neck open and install tubing using the forceps.Run the loud machine and drain the blood.Remove the tubing and sew the neck shut. (two clicks)(spooky stuff happens in background, maybe even a jump-scare. Possibly a unique cut-scene providing lore into your character's background and history.)Get a bag and fill it with cavity jelly. Grab a trocar and mumble foul language under your breath as you wrestle with the most janky and cumbersome activity in the game and fill up the body's stomach with this stuff. (The trocar is by far the worst part of the game and you have to do it to every body. There's no rhyme or reason behind controlling the trocar. It just has to go in at the right angle and right depth before it discharges its contents, if you don't get it right your wrestling with your mouse to get the trocar to do what its supposed to do. Its terrible and if its supposed to be simulating the difficulty of using such a device, its simulating it wrong. Its egregiously frustrating to use.)After you fill the body with cavity goo you gotta go get some tank cleaner an clean-out the embalming tank.Go to the bathroom, get jump-scared in the mirror. Make the cleaning agent and bring it back to the lab. Run the agent through the loud machine again and wait for it to complete.Next, grab a wetnap from the counter and "moisturize" the cadaver's face. You can now wheel this body back to cold storage and start on the next one. You will do everything I just listed in that exact same order each time you play through. You cannot skip steps, you cannot multitask. You cannot do anything more than what I just listed. Once you start the process you cannot stop and change out bodies. You must finish what you started in the order that's required on that clipboard. Cool for the first play-through, literally to be avoided in subsequent play-throughs. While you're going through this tedium you'll be trying to figure out the demon's name through the letting strips and sigils you find. Once you figure out the demons name and put this mark together with the right configuration, you put the mark on the corpse and burn it, face moisturized and all. If you're right you get one cutscene, if you're wrong you get another. Both are very similar but not too bad the first time through. Second and third play-throughs feel like they told us that it was unique each time to justify charging 25 bucks to have it. The actual game is less than an hour long and it baited me into spending 10 hours trying to find out more about it. First time you play through all of this you'll start to feel like the game has tons in store. But it really doesn't. I like that it has little secrets and different cut-scenes in the play-throughs, but I found myself encountering the same ones over and over. I put ten hours into this game and I could beat the loop within 20 minutes, so I feel like I've explored it. Can't type anymore. Out of space. Game is a gimmick demo. Buy when its like 10 bucks. Moisturize your face before setting yourself on fire.

One of my favorite aspects of the game is the way it offers clues on how to unravel the mystery, even in fail states.There are a few "mean" jump scares but I think they're mostly all earned. Some of the subject matter might be a bit upsetting for anyone with trauma stemming from the themes of drug abuse and suicide, but imo none of the content is inappropriate or in poor taste. My only other issue was two achievements seemed to be delayed but I randomly got them after completing a few other shifts. Nbd but thought I should mention.The Mortuary Assistant is a no-brainer in any horror fan's collection. This will be an annual all 6 ending playthrough for me every October!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! What a game. This is absolutely one of the best horror games I've played - especially one that's not a big budget AAA game like F.E.A.R. or Dead Space. It goes extremely light on the jumpscares and extremely heavy on atmospheric horror, which is by far the best kind. The whole game is eerie and finds ways to put you on edge that I would never have thought of.The first playthrough is absolutely flawless in setting the stage. The nebulous "time limit" you're on creates a real sense of urgency, and while you're given copious amounts of direction and "tutorial"-type guidance in the form of notes and tapes, it is a lot of information to take in quickly, which immediately immerses you. It's very much a "learn or die" type scenario, which is incredible for creating tension.Further playthroughs lose out on that as you learn the ropes and become more efficient, but the randomness of the "haunts" and the way the game functions does lend it quite a bit of replayability. Additionally, there arl=e multiple endings (many of which can be mutually canon, with at least one non-canon bad end) which encourages exploration and continued play, as well as a sense of continuity between shifts. Furthermore, it appears the developer(s) are intent on adding more content and expanding the game, which is excellent given that it has a very strong base.My one complaint is that you're tasked with investigating and deciphering many small mysteries within a shift, one of which is identifying a certain body - however, many of the "tells" for identifying a body are also shared with major "haunts", aka semi story-based events that occur, which can lead you very much astray. It is frustrating to fail a shift because you were not able to determine which was the correct body. I will expand on this in a spoiler, should you like elaboration.Overall, this is a fantastic game that is absolutely worth the price tag, and I would say a mandatory purchase for any fans of horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer that I got this game at a very steep discount and if I had paid $25 for it this review would probably be a thumbs down.   If you wanted to see 100% of the content I think you'd have to do like between 5 and 7 runs but after even 1 or 2 runs you've seen most of the scares, because they're all fairly similar to each other with slight variations. Your character can't really get hurt or die from the scares up until the moment you actually fail a run (which is pretty telegraphed). So this takes the tension away a little bit but I still thought a lot of it was very creepy. The job-simulator aspects of it seemed immersive at first but trying to do subsequent runs I realized there is so little variation to the embalming process that doing it more than a couple times starts to feel like a real chore. There is a little bit of a story that plays out across successful runs but honestly the game couldn't really keep me entertained long enough for me to justify playing through it that many times and I ended up just watching it on youtube.  I would basically treat this as buying a ticket to an interactive horror movie because that's essentially what you're paying for: About 2-3 hours of decent scares and some creepy ambiance with a light sprinkling of story. It is absolutely not worth 25 dollars but if you can get it for 5-10 then I would say its good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most (if not, the most) unpredictable and uneasy horror games I've ever played...and I think it's pretty great.The fact that this game is randomly generated every time you do a new shift really adds a different take, even if some of the scares are similar from the last shift you've done, they can still get you off-guard and you don't know when they or what will hit you.The only downsides I can say about this game is that due to it's small, condensed nature, the process of embalming 3 bodies in each shift can get repetitive, so I'd recommend doing each shift at your own pace (as the scares can also get to the player a bit much at times) and due to the unpredictable nature of the game, there maybe some events that may not trigger that can allow you to get a different ending.Still, the concept and mechanics work very well (despite some bugs here and there and turning the gurney can feel rather stiff), the sound design is solid and the atmosphere is nicely done. All this crafted by a solo developer is astonishing.The full retail price may seem a bit much for many, so I do suggest waiting for a sale, even for the most curious. I got this during launch week at a 10% discount and I haven't regret it since I streamed this game online via Twitch and has been quite of an experience. Definitely worth a look (if you can handle it).UPDATE: They've added a new ending to the game which expands the lore of the story in a very intriguing way that I cannot spoil and it does leave the player wanting more. That's one positive I'll give is the developer's dedication to not only improving the game but adding more post launch. Wish them all the best!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give this one a soft recommend. The first three endings are easy to get, but the last two require that specific randomized story events occur during the shift (gameplay loop), so you can waste tons of time doing shift after shift waiting for the needed events to appear to get the ending you want. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely giving this game a 10/10. Its a short game (I got all 6 endings in 23 hours), but it's absolutely worth it if you like jump scares. Not a whole lot of cons, it's just an all-around solid game. I recommend headphones and playing in the dark, and if you can, keep a pen and some paper next to you. There's some symbols you need to remember, and drawing them helps.It CAN get kinda gross. If you're not a fan of seeing wounds or teeth, you probably won't enjoy the game. The ick factor is kind of low, but if you don't like those things, I recommend watching a playthrough of the embalming process before buying.For achievement completionists (Is that a word? It is now.), I will say here: If you want to not have to erase your data for two achievements, look up an achievement guide for The Phone's Dead and No Way Out. You need to do those on the first night.The game is short and repetitive, but after the third shift, you won't even need to look at your clipboard anymore (especially if you don't have the item randomization on). However, your redundant tasks are spiced up by the different kinds of hauntings you can see throughout the night. After the first night, you can adjust how aggressive the hauntings are - I recommend keeping the low default until you get your bearings, it's easier to see the hauntings if you know what you're doing. Once I got comfortable, I cranked it up all the way, lots of fun!The storyline is pretty interesting - leaving you enough to be curious for more without feeling disappointed. I'm hoping they add more stuff. Also I got this around Christmas, and the seasonal themes were hilarious, my friends and I decided there was a string of Mall Santa murders, to explain why Santa was always there.All in all, a short but excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mortuary Assistant is one of the most unique and compelling horror games I've ever experienced. I have to commend the solo developer responsible for this game, as it outshines the bulk of AAA studios and their comparably poor output in the horror market. I greatly appreciate how tastefully employed the jump-scares are in this game - I don't believe that jump-scares are strictly off-limits for horror games like a lot of people do as they're perceived to be fairly cheap ( they often are I'll grant you that ) but in this game they feel earned and are typically spaced out enough to let you recover, but never fully. _childDocuments_.review: I don't ever review games...but this one... this one got me. I love horror, I love games. This one, proves that you don't need a high end budget to make a heart thumping great game. It's controls can feel too simplistic even sometimes frustrating .... BUT this game has the best jump scares..nerve wracking elements I've seen in a long long time in a game. WORTH EVERY PENNY. Think the best of Phasmophobia and 5 Nights at Freddy's with a large side of the Exorcist / Evil Dead movies. My only fear is that this title doesn't do well, and doesn't get more content added.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: The demo has some altered changes to keep from spoiling the full release of the game. Got locked into the computer, couldn't exit, close or move but could still open inventory and clipboard.This was a great game and I have kept my original review below this one.Original Review:( I got this game as a gift from someone who I thought was a friend )Honestly, I don't know where to start but if you want to get scared, you came to the right place.I've played Outlast which is considered by some as the scariest horror game, I played Outlast 2 which in my opinion is scarier! _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game is a *touch* expensive but it is a good experience. There's a couple bugs to be wary of as of this writing, one of them potentially game blocking but most don't get the bug as far as I can tell.The pros:- Good atmosphere- Good build-up to the end of a "shift"- Fantastic story in general for what's thereThe cons:- The animations are off-putting. They're not "smooth" enough... I'm not sure how to explain it but it's very evident in a couple of the endings- The graphics could be better- The game isn't very optimizedOverall, the game is really fun for what's there. Depending on if you care about the story, you're going to get anywhere from 1.5 to ~4 hours out of the game probably. It's a bit pricy for the $25 but it's not too awful. I think $20 would have been far more reasonable. I can't really talk much about the story other than it's too short but interesting.The jump scares have a good balance with atmosphere but they *definitely* held back some punches in the scare factor. The game could be 2x scarier if they wanted it to be. But given that I see people who are too scared about the game as it is, perhaps that was a good thing. Personally, I like a horror game that has me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ my pants involuntarily but the game is just shy of that.I'm not a fan of the UI or controls in general. The gurney is difficult to move for some reason, sometimes the damage you have to input into the computer doesn't "register" for some reason, but it's serviceable and I ended up getting used to it fairly easily.There could also have been a bit more variation in cutscenes and bodies that you work on.Overall, a good game to play and also a good game to watch others play. 7.5/10 (an actual 7.5 meaning well above average)Bugs I've run into as of this writing:- Sometimes when a cutscene moves your character model, it gets "stuck" so you can be literally laying down and walking around at the same time. This isn't a big deal (and more funny than anything) but it makes viewing whatever you're holding impossible... including the clipboard and letting paper.- There's a fairly annoying bug where two demons can have the same mark sigils... meaning it's impossible to accurately choose the correct demon, it turns into a 50% chance of choosing the right one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Mortuary Assistant

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: Absolutely worth $24.99.  Do yourself the favor of playing with headphones in a dark room, and just go in blind without spoilers.  There is creepy atmosphere and unexpected scare tactics.  It's a perfect download this month for the Halloween spirit, and the dev has already posted notes to expect continuing updates.  My wife enjoyed seeing me jolt, hearing me yelp, and nearly shidding my pants.  Experiences vary, but this is one of the scariest gaming experiences I've had in years.CONS: I've put just shy of 8 hours in and neared full completion of the achievements, so know that this game is an environmental and psychological horror that delivers expert scares, moreso than a chronological horror with a full-fledged story.  However, this just makes me excited at the possibility that the developer will release more content in the future.  He has been consistent in providing fans feedback on the latest bug fixes, add-ons, and projected new content so this seems highly likely.

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very cool game.The atmosphere here is really well made, from the lack of music to the subtle creaks and noises; it made me feel wary whenever I so much as got close to the corpse being worked on.I failed on my first real shift . While I haven't continued past the first shift (have to work in the morning after all) it left me intrigued and wanting to continue as soon as possible.I don't know much about the protagonist's story yet so I don't have an opinion per se. When I played the demo I feared this would turn into the Nth "It was all in your head/it was all a dream/you were the killer!/you are not even a mortician, you are in a psychiatric hospital!/nobody ever suspects the butterfly!" psychological horror game.Thank God . There are, from what I've seen so far, some elements of the mind playing tricks on you, but the threat is real and it doesn't look like it's the main focus of the supernatural elements that occur.There are some bugs here and there, nothing major.For instance, since I like to click anywhere around me and try to open all the closets and cabinets, especially to weird out my boss who's in the same room as me, I managed to accidentally pick up a notebook that I wasn't supposed to get just yet. I couldn't interact with it nor did I trigger any strange events or cutscenes or anything, so all was well.There was one "event" that triggered from a different angle than was probably expected, which made me jump regardless.Also, there are some funny things that can happen if you activate the "high dpi mouse" option and change the dpi settings while moving the gurney.Other than that, so far so good, and even the bugs I encountered weren't even annoying. I was itching for a horror game already and this game is really providing.Would recommend! I'd like to add, since I read some complaints about longevity, there are several endings, each shift seems to play different, and the developer has pointed out that there's more lore, story, etc. to unveil with additional runs (shifts).

_childDocuments_.review: Don't feel like reading the whole thing? Down at the bottom is the conclusion and score given to the game! :)The Mortuary Assistant is one of the best horror games you can play if you are looking to get scared and experience a horrific experience that is never quite the same due to its random paranormal events. You play Rebecca, an assistant at a mortuary who works under her boss, Raymond; her job entails putting corpses into storage after treating them with specific processes. The game is proficient in distraction and surprise, as you must manage your work as an assistant and deal with the demonic entities. The more time you take to perform the duties, the more Rebecca will lose her mind, making her susceptible to the demon's influence. It creates a pace of juggling your responsibilities while avoiding getting spooked.The Mortuary Assistant starts slow as the game gives you a tutorial on how to play it, and there is a big respite to get used to the title's mechanics. As progress is made and time goes by, the game will ramp up the scares to the point that there is no respite between the attacks specters and ghosts perform on you. That is an excellent design, as a horror game that sets the stage and atmosphere before the scares make you tense and more vulnerable to becoming afraid.The task also plays a massive role in that atmosphere of dread and horror, as while they do not change between corpses, the interactions you will experience while working on them are entirely different. Focusing too much on the checklist leaves you open to attacks, while not performing it fast makes paranormal activity more likely. While the map is small, as it's only the Mortuary, it works in favor of the game as it gives a sensation of being trapped in a secluded space and, more importantly, a dreadful realization that you are completely isolated from other humans. Your only company is the demons that are out to get you.The game's strong point is that the player shapes the experience, so it has no specific linear path. How the player plays and what the game presents in a single run creates a variable that makes it so that there is no way to prepare for what will happen or when. Coupled with the atmosphere and tension, the game slowly introduces, and you have a formula for a title that, while short for a single run, can be pretty intense.The Mortuary Assistant visuals are excellent; the game features high visuals that make the graphics look crisp and realistic, reinforcing the immersion when you play through it that you are in the Mortuary. The corpses all have good detail, making looking at them a sight that can make you nervous as you wonder if they will move out of nowhere. The demons themselves come in various shapes resulting from figures that give comfort only to them crushed into despair, uneasy forms that can provide terrible frights and even shadows that chase after you when you least expect it. Not having a single design for the demon and using multiple forms makes the game feel jumpy, for you do not know what shape they will take the next time they go after you.When it comes to sound, the game does a solid job. Noise, phone calls, sound effects, and voice acting all add to the game's suspense. The demon can communicate with you, and choosing to let them speak can result in discomfort as you don't know how to answer the opportunity of speaking with another human as you let the phone ring. The voice actors do an excellent job of portraying characters and making the story believable.Replayability is something that The Mortuary Assistant keeps in mind, as five different endings can be unlocked, and the game always presents each run with some differences, holding the title fresh even after beating it. If you are a player that beats a game and then moves to another videogame, know that a run of the game takes around 2-4 hours, while getting all endings can result in about 10-15 hours total.Performance-wise, the game runs well, and the glitches are few; that being said, some game-breaking bugs could require a restart of the game, but very little progress is lost due to these errors, which are rare to witness. On an RTX 2060, the game ran at 70 fps with the graphics in ultra.The Mortuary Assistant hits all the notes of what a good horror game should aspire to be: a dreadful sensation that slowly crawls up to you and then bursts into a horrifying experience that lets you feel fear. It understands the pacing for crafting horror and uses all its elements beautifully as it combines them into a blend of fear and nerve-racking gameplay. This game is a must-buy if you like horror titles and want to be stressed and scared. If you are not into replaying titles, consider getting it on a sale, and if you are looking to get into the genre, consider other games before jumping into the abyss. 10/10  MASTERPIECEIf you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator!

name: What Happened
detailed_description: “ What Happened puts you in the shoes of high-school student Stiles, a teenage boy suffering from acute anxiety and depression. You must guide him through the dark and twisted corridors of his own sub-conscious, with his fate depending entirely on your empathy with his tortured state of mind.” Key Features: Psychological thriller in which you guide high school student Stiles on an uncompromising journey through his troubled teenage mind. Unique first person perspective on an individual’s journey through anxiety and depression. Densely atmospheric world of waking nightmares infused with distorted memories. Environmental puzzles and cues guide you through the twisted corridors of Stiles’ mind. The empathy you show for the character will subtly affect the outcome of his journey.
