_childDocuments_.review: A great twin-stick shooter roguelite experience, that feels overall great mechanically. The obvious standout is of course the manual reload system, which adds a layer of strategy for when to reload, how much to reload, and which gun to reload, as well as giving that immersion for frantically reloading in chaotic gunfights. It's also just visually stunning and distinctive, with a closeup of the gun appearing on the right side of the screen when reloading. Plus, being packed with great levels, bosses, guns, and music, it's a great overall package. It can be repetitive at some parts so perhaps not worth at full price for the content you're getting, but certainly a great pickup on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: If you wanted a game that is a cross of rogue lite, westerns, scifi, and rogue lite, then this is the game that you need.     Every several seconds, you'll have to manually reload as you blow up robots while finding cover and dodging. To add to the stress, you'll lose your legendary weapons if you make a mistake. Unless you have the $$$ to buy it back at a steep price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: I 1CC'd this game, trophies and all. The game kills you twice for plot reasons, but past that, I didn't die. I finished this whole thing with a total of 3 clones. When I first found this game via Netflix about a month ago, I thought it impossible, but this game is ADDICTIVE and I couldn't stop, and I guess I accidentally mastered it. The combat keeps roping you in with that "Ok, just ONE MORE GAME" loop. Ragdoll physics really give life to every kill, upgrades are fun, and though simple, this Twin Stick Roguelike Looter Shooter has enough to keep fans of the genre hooked. This is The Tetris of Twin Stick Shooters, with a Western Borderlands-esque coat of paint. I'll gladly keep playing this until the developers release a sequel or something similar. I don't Twitch, but shint I might.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: This game has tons of potential, but unfortunately, it isn't fun and, as a whole, frustrating.1. The cover mechanism doesn't work sometimes, which results in getting shredded.2. Using an elevator, then down and back up, will lead to enemies stacking at the elevator, resulting in getting shredded.3. The defuse bomb game is impossible at times. There isn't enough time to get to the bomb, and you do have to kill all enemies; otherwise, some doors don't open.4. Although fun at first, the reload mechanism gets tiring after a while.5. The gun variety is boring; there are different shapes, but the gunplay is identical.6. Looting stuff is slow, and destroying an item gives you only 10 bucks; it completely kills the game's rhythm.7. Every time you finish a mission, you must return to the mission starting place.8. It would be a great co-op game, but it's not.Ideas: Add grenades, shields, element weapons, melee weapons, bouncing bullets, somehow make a mod so guns auto-reload, auto-pickup stuff on the ground, add co-op, add events in-game, being able to chain missions at the end of a mission for additional rewards.On the plus side, the realization of the game is very, very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be an arcady roguelite isometric shooter with combat that is too repetitive and fast-paced for me personally to enjoy. There is no single player campaign. You just go on roguelite runs in levels where you accumulate XP until you face a boss. Difficulty is also forced in these levels with only a few that are easy and the remaining being medium to hard. Levels also look exactly the same, taking place in a desert western setting with fences that create a maze. And I found these mazes to be sort of frustrating sometimes figuring out where to go. Each area that contains levels is also locked until you defeat the boss in the previous area, something that I had a pretty tough time with. This is because boss attacks are relentless, they are always well protected and regenerate, player health is replenished very little during boss battles, and crouching behind something offers little to no protection. You must also constantly keep reloading and most weapons only have two to three slots for ammo. Adding to the frustration for me was that when you die, you must start the level or boss fight completely over from the very beginning facing the same enemies all over again. Overall, I found this game more frustrating than enjoyable so I determined that it's just not my type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: A more old west style, tactical, roguelite, extraction shooter. Has quite a few randomized missions that last anywhere between 5 minutes to 15 minutes. Most of which being closer to 5 minutes. Gotta think about your surroundings, hide behind cover, shoot when you have openings, dodge, run. Super fast gameplay for those with minimum time.This game has an actual progression to it. You do one mission and go back to base to get stronger for the next mission, meaning that unlike other roguelites, there is an endEnjoyable experience
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks great, shoots great and feels great, but costs too much for what it offers. It also lacks function to remap keys, which in a game that requires repeated pressing of reload would be appreciated.Edit:They've added remapping which is nice.If you have the cash to afford the game then I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, third person, shooter and looter, robots, wild west, great soundtrack on the game too. Not too hard for now in the beginning missions, love that it has controller support too. Of course it released on my birthday which makes me love it even more :D Having fun so far, will have to see if the harder missions will succeed, I'm not that good in aiming, but practice makes "perfect", in my case "better". :D ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: A charming shooter with great music, great artstyle, and some awesome weapon mechanics... that just kinda falls flat. The starting missions get repetitive and dull fairly swiftly, and you have to grind out a bunch of them to get to the first boss. And if you fail the boss, you have to grind out more missions to get another try. I think it's very close to a game I would love, which is why the disappointment stings so much more. It's a no from me, alas.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Dust & Neon does have some interesting concepts but also has some that can be not ideal. It is a twin stick shooter where you build up a hub with currency you collect to unlock new weapons, upgrades and buildings. The combat can be tedious but I enjoyed it for what it was. I did enjoy the boss fights and will have to get back into the game to see what else it has to offer. I did find a lot of the weapons I found to be worse than my current one so I am thinking the further you go in the game the better chance you have of finding a stronger weapon and I would assume that applies for upgrades as well as you go through a hub and you can level them up once unlocked. I will have to give it a thumbs down for now as I just am not convinced but maybe that will change in the future. If you like twin stick shooters it is worth giving a shot and you may end up liking it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: It'd be neat if it wasn't geared toward you taking inevitable damage. Most of the damage you'll take is going to be from something flanking you or the stupid rolling bots flushing you out of cover, forcing you to get shot by a gun-bot, and that's just at the beginning of the game. From the forced-death mission, there's also shield users, grenade users, and explode-on-death rollers later on, which... Might work if this was actually 3D and you had stronger weapons and a way to dodge out of damage <the roll doesn't give invulnerability> or position away from it to begin with (since cover is meaningless as you're going to be immediately flanked or flushed out most of the time).The guns exacerbate this. You can hold barely any ammo, and the only thing that 1-shots is a good rifle... Which of course has the least max ammo and takes the longest to reload due to the weird reload mechanic and the gun itself having 6 bullets.There's also randomized gun stats that just plain suck. Accuracy is a stat here, so you can be frustrated with having your reticle on something, then the bullet deviates and doesn't hit, making you take damage (VERY noticable during the tutorial when you're asked to shoot bottles off of a crate); Handling is there to make reloading slower, not faster, it's always below 75%, and the lower it goes, the harder to reload it is ; You'd think having more mag size would be good, but, nope. Takes WAY longer to reload in a game where you need to shoot and reload fast for maximum worth. Boo.There's also just some plain old issues, too: Bots can hear you from three houses away, and can spawn in the areas/sections behind you, and they themselves have horrible AI that just randomly does stuff, making crowd control an impossibility while the 14 bots that just got alerted from you shooting a single roller in a shed then swarm towards you from out of the nearby buildings two or even three houses over (not counting the ones that spawn from the unenterable areas). Also, where you point your mouse is NOT where you're going to aim. During the first boss, I had my cursor over him while behind cover, aimed, and suddenly it was in the direction the character was facing, not where my cursor was. TL:DR, I think this is trying to be a precision shooter, but, it doesn't have everything set up like it actually is one. Enemies do whatever they please, even crouching outside of cover, while you're going to get forced out of cover, you're going to not have enough bullets in the gun when you need them, and reloading is weird and slow. Pass this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I needed this game.Pricey, maybeRepetite/Grindy just a littlebutgame is super-polished and cute, you can enjoy all the content with no issues at allgunfights are a lot of funcan be quite challenging if you try to kill bosses more than once, especially if you leave the manual reloading onI wouldn't trust reviews from ppl who played just 1 hour.My suggestion is to have a couple of runs per day so you don't feel the grinding for money or cores (currencies)If you are an achievement collector you'll eventually make it at some stage, no rush.Good Job, would buy again
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Really had a great time. I skipped it for about a year since tactical/cover shooters aren't my jam so the game's manual reload didn't appeal to me, but glad I ended up giving it a try.Gunplay feels great. Graphics and style are really cool too. You can turn on automatic reload in settings - literal game changer for me. I was glad for easy mode; and laser weapons which have very fast reloads. More of those please. Or better yet, no reloading and infinite shooting lol. And maybe a roguelite mode with waves of increasing enemies. Yeah, that's my jam. Will pay for that dlc lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: I would say overall I can recommend Dust & Neon in its current state. Only 95 minutes in so far but I think I've gathered enough about it already. There are some things some players may find mildly irritating, though. All keybinds are on "standard" keys. Reload is on R, dodge on Space, etc...but you cannot rebind. While I don't have issues with the keys, I think omitting the ability to rebind is a slight mistake. The reload mechanic is interesting and I don't find it too much of a hindrance. It does require you to mentally multitask a bit but I think it adds a good bit of challenge. The other main complaint I can see is incoming damage, which seems to be pretty random. There is no telegraphing of enemy attacks, but most incoming damage can be mitigated by using cover.  The difficulty is probably accurate, if not slightly too easy. I've just stopped playing after killing the first boss on just my first run, but the difficulty doesn't seem to ramp up super quickly or unexpectedly. Overall I'd say it may be a little pricey, but with further updates I think it's a solid recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: TBH, Rogue-Lite/Like/Whatever is one of my least favorite genres.  Why did I buy this game then, you ask?  Because I love looter-shooters and pretty much anything that has a lot of weapons to pick up and modify.  Soooo, I took a gamble and it paid off.  FYI the Humble Bundle store has the game on sale right now for 2 bucks, so it's an absolute STEAL.This game is a ton of fun with of course many different weapons and ways to modify your character. Yes, the gameplay is very standard rogue-like/lite but the gameplay loop is fun and I've been enjoying the game for the 5-6 hours I've played so far (my Steam tally includes some downtime).  If you like twin stick shooters with focus on finding lots of weapons, I wager that you'll probably like this game.  The GFX and artwork are fantastic as well as the audio, which makes the game even more enjoyable to play.  Lastly, I have been playing on the highest GFX settings @4K60 and have had zero issues with stuttering, frame rate, etc.  I'm playing on a 7800x3D and a Geforce 4070, 32G RAM and WIN11, but I doubt you need this much horsepower for the game to run smoothly.Hope you enjoy the game as much as I have!Cheers!!H
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: I was teetering on the edge of giving this a positive review. It's not horrible, it's just mid. Reload mechanic is very fun and satisfying. Dodging feels OK. Ducking behind cover is extremely inconsistent (wish the game would just give you a crouch button). Started seeing repetitive missions before the first boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: There really needs to be a "MEH" option.Dust & Neon is a pretty good Roguelite.It's nothing special, it won't rewrite or re-imagine Roguelites but it's ok.the gunplay is pretty slick, movement is ok.The Reload mechanic is pretty weird, especially when you're playing M&K (because you have to press R for every round you want to reload) and you need to move.The weapons are nothing interesting.Pistol, Shotgun and Rifle and that's it, though they each have different RNG stats.The bosses are nothing too hard.Everything about Dust & Neon is just Meh.The only truly annoying thing about the game is the price tag.If you're looking for a mindless Roguelite then Dust & Neon is for you.If the price tag feels too steep, just wait for it to go on sale.Again, it's not a BAD game.It's just a not a Great game.But what it does it does well.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the game is way to easy, it could get harder after a while, but i was just bored during most of it.Legendaries drop way to often for how powerful they are making the allready easy game trivial.Allthough the game is easy the gunplay feels rewarding and fun the bosses (allthough easy) are fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: First thing for me is that I personally don't think its worth the price, for example most roguelites I have looked at around 25 dollars and they have WAY more content then this game does. On a different note there is little to no enemy variation as well as quest variation. However I will say the boss fights are quite good.I feel like this game should have started out as a early access game.With all that being said I still hope that they add a lot more to the game to make it better
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Dust Neon is pretty much a top-down take on borderlands. No real roguelite mechanics in terms of variety(upgrades and  weapons are very basic), randomization or permanent death.I bought it for 10$ and I can barely recommend at this price yet it's apparently 30$ in some regions. The game simply does not have enough content or interesting mechanics. The gameplay itself is ok, the boss fights are the only interesting part of the game. Honestly the dev's were better off making this a boss-rush type game as that's the part they did really well.Took me 7 hours to beat but I'd say the last 3 were me repeating the same missions with the same guns to reach the level requirement to unlock bosses. Way better options in the genre especially for the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game so far. It's on the expensive side but the game is well worth it. The bullet animations, the movement it's all smooth like butter.EDIT: The game runs out of content around hour 3-5 depending on your tempo. Everything is shallow - just farm money, get some legendaries and then just run around and click on the enemies and reload. Really boring once you have legendaries the chance of getting an upgrade falls down to 0.001%. Only 3 types of weapons with no modifiers, just around 10 skins for each of them that don't change much. Bosses are easy on normal difficulty you will mostly die to traps which omg why are there TRAPS it's like the laziest and unfun mechanic you could think of. Just unkillable unstoppable, same pattern that are there to make it more difficult for you to aim at the boss otherwise you would kill him in 30 seconds.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Unavoidable damage and a useless cover system.   Enemies just charge and you have no recourse.  You need to reload constantly so you take damage. Your roll needs to recharge so you take damage. The dodge doesn't avoid damage as much as it delays it.  Enemies are spongy and relentless.  Switching weapons to finish an enemy doesn't work with how much hp they have.  There are no dynamics to the combat.  The enemy is always charging and as soon as they get close you take damage.  It's boring and mindless. Maybe it gets better, but its bad in the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: First, i love this game!However, it seems to have some accessibility issues. Aiming is difficult/impossible if someone has fine motor control or other issues with their aiming hand especially. It might be nice if there was a key binding with the opposite hand of the aiming hand to lock the aim (further movement of aiming stick is ignored while locked) where aim is held at current position until that opposite hand key binding is released.I understand it's a rogue like, but aiming is a little too fluid for anyone with issues.Buy this game! If you liked Borderlands art style, you'll like this, too. The game is certainly challenging so be prepared!edit: the game seems to aim easier with ge-proton7-49.still hard but not completely uncontrollable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is going to sit in my library as a reminder to not buy indie stuff over $20, even at $10 this game is a hard sell. Visuals and the idea at first was cool, but gameplay quickly becomes mind numbingly boring, having to grind out the same levels when stuck at a boss. Upgrades take longer and longer to get and are less and less impactful, leading to more grinding snooze fest. Biggest pet peeve was the dev didnt even play the game enough to realize your exp gain freezing mid way through a level because you ranked up is a stupid and punishing design that further makes the game boring and grindy, for a indie single player shooter, just massive design flaws to further making you regret spending an entire $30 on this garbo.

_childDocuments_.review: While this is a small studio`s game, it certainly pushes into a "very well done" territory. I have picked it up for several reasons - really loved visuals, dynamics and theme, but also loved seeing how devs are actively addressing points of valid criticism. And currently it is safe to say, that some of those older negative reviews are no longer relevant.Still, there are some issues left, so if you are one of those people who hates having any sort of bugs\glitches, and you abhor the idea of playing anything that is not 200% polished and AAA+++ , then skip it.Now, what is this game? -  Essentially, a shooter, with 3 types of weapons, with aiming, sprinting, cover and rolling mechanics . There might be some high-level stuff I haven`t seen yet, but most of the time you are cycling between shotgun, sniper rifle and a pistol\revolver.- You have a base you can upgrade, by adding new stuff there, or making existing stuff better, shops cheaper, more accessible, upgrading your loot, reducing losses on death etc.- From that base you chose missions to accomplish (I have seen about 5 types of those so far, plus boss missions, plus Arena type mission) - you complete objectives, hopefully loot better and shinier guns with better stats, and teleport back to the base. - At some point you can challenge a boss, kill it and unlock new region.- Mission types themselves remain more or less the same , but their difficulty, enemy composition and abilities, and also maps  - do change.You also have some skills to unlock (like life-steal on kills, better dmg, chance to revive, chance to return dmg to attacker or more ammo in crates etc). These are not overly complicated, but they are pretty important - especially those that give you more sustain.Overall skills are there to help you in blasting enemies more efficiently.There is no some RPG style vast talent\ability tree or smth.==Now, as for difficulty:First of all - this game does demand certain "agility\reaction" from you. So if you hate it - move on. This being said, it is not THAT demanding on those normal missions. You just can`t tank dmg, you have to roll often, and you have to avoid mechanics (like grenade launchers, turrets etc), one boss in particular makes you roll and avoid things A LOT. Normally, I am not a big fan of this stuff, but still managed to have fun with this game. So I guess this game has a moderate demand for cyber "agility".The beginning is actually quite tough  - when you die, you lose all your guns. So you start from scratch with basic pistol.But not all is lost -  after you die, game gives you a bunch of easy missions to get back on your feet.And life becomes truly MUCH EASIER when you unlock "buyback" terminal for your base.It allows you to buy your favorite guns back after you lost them on death (don`t start new missions tho, buyback works only immediately after death!).So, don`t get discouraged by rough start.==---- Overall it is a fun little game, with engaging maps. A game with pretty cool style and "feeling".- Combat feels good, enemies die in a satisfying way :D- Controls are fine, just a matter of habit.- Story is all about you killing more enemies and more and more. - Game has certain grind-ness present, but it is really more about "hey, you can grind a bit, to make battles less dependent on your skill level" type of grind. Not a "must complete 10000 missions, or you lose". The only really noticeable grind happens if you die a lot, and have to buyback your guns constantly, and then you run low on money, so you have to run some missions to make money, to afford yourself dying more :DWorth mentioning, that this is not a game to "rush and beat in one go"!  It is a game you play for a fun, blasting things for let say 30-40 minutes, then you switch to other games. Tomorrow you will remember that it was fun to kill those robots, and you come back and play for another hour. It is just a shooter after all so don`t overdo it. -cons :- Some reviews argued that initial price was too high, and I can agree, that you will feel much better about this game, if you buy it on sale.Not because game is bad, but simply because at full price it enters a domain of a really fierce competition with other well established bigger games, developed by big companies etc.- mission variety is relatively limited.- got stuck several times. Was able to unstuck my char two times, had to restart once. (which sucks, since restart means loss)- had a bug where script apparently didn`t fire, so mission was failed.  While getting that bug and losing mission was annoying, it was not a huge loss for hours of fun gameplay, so overall it is a confident : "recommended on a sale"\ "certainly keeping this game and not refunding"
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: looter twin-stick shooter game, with Wild West theme, and neons (obviously from the game’s title). You’ll play as a mysterious gunslinger, probably a cyborg where you kill enemies, and do specific objectives like clearing the entire map, destroying objects, and maybe robbing a safe from a train. While it's a bit expensive game compared to other indie games, it does went into a quite decent direction starting at the release of the second update.First of all, let’s start with the things that the game does right. It’s quite cartoonish and it does the job well. Cel shading with colorful design does fit pretty well to the game. What I truly love the most is the reload animation for every weapon, even if it's a top down shooter game, you can see that there's some cool reload animation. I really wish every game did this.  The game does recommend you to play as if it’s a cover-shooter game, though I mostly play it run and gun since it’s more engaging for me that way. Up until this time I’m playing the game (3 hours), I don’t have any trouble except that one part where you’re supposed to die (at least that's what I've thought).The gameplay length for every level is around 5-10 minutes, depending on which level you took, it’s quite short so you can take a break every once in a while.Just like other roguelite games, you will upgrade your character every run, and you’ll also unlock new features, such as stat boost for one mission, a shop where you can buy weapons, a weapon retrieval system in case you die, and so on.Of course, a gameplay review of a game that  The aiming system feels alright, shooting feels good, and the reload system fits quite well.  Though, it can be hard to reload for weapons with big magazines, so using high-damage guns and low magazines are recommended. Though if you do hate the reload system, you can turn on Auto Reload on Settings.As of the weapons, there are three types of weapons, a Revolver, Shotgun and Sniper. Revolvers are jack-of-all-trades weapons, which can be used in any kind of situation, can’t go wrong with them at all. Shotguns deal lots of damage in close range, but thanks to the game’s damage falloff system, it deals low damage on further targets. Snipers are decent accuracy weapons that barely have damage falloff., where you have to fully utilize both cover and good timing to make sure you’ll survive the entire boss fight. Not to mention, the second boss fight OST is absolute banger.Speaking of the soundtrack… it does fit quite well. The wild west theme with some futuristic theme soundtrack for bosses does put me into a flow state. Personally, I love the second boss’ theme.So I can say that the game does the art right and the gameplay feels great (except for one case which is explained later).The problem never lies on the gunplay itself (except for few), but let’s start with few things: Now the post processing settings have an individual settings, that's great. The offensive tree is alright so far, but the defensive part has one major problem at start, which is the HP upgrade only gives you VERY FEW points. Your starting HP is 80, while the upgrade per point only gives +3, then +1, then +1, and then +3 at the final level. It does mislead the player since, it tells that the upgrade increases HP by +3, +4, +5, then +8, which at max level, I thought it will give you +20 HP in total. My suggestion is to buff the HP upgrades and other upgrades that don't give much. I mean… +8 HP only gives you one more shot protection. Fixed. Now it's actually worth buying in case you died or something.And here comes the main problem of mine: Fixed and now you can aim further with snipers! Now it feels better overall.Lastly…It is really expensive for this price tag, yes. But then again, in a way or another, it's better compared to the first version of the game, which I did reviewed back then. With this re-review of mine, it is already worth trying, if you'd like to.This game is a roguelite twin-stick shooter game, where it does the art quite well and does have engaging gameplay,  However, the game might be a little bit too expensive for some.I rate this B out of A, Now it feels like a decent game overall. While the game is a bit expensive for some, you should try it out solely for the gunplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really a game reviewer but I'm going to address some things. Positives: The game's visual aspects and whole anchor-point of having 2000 guns is great. The roguelite action of upgrading your character and unlocking new "shop" to be introduced. Negatives: Repetition. After playing the game for around 2 hours, I can say that I'm decently informed of the happenings and key-parts of the game however I just can't seem to be addicted to finding new guns. I mean yes, you get another gun with better aspects and WOW, it's Legendary but so what? What makes the Legendary gun, the predicted peak tier of weapon better than a gun of a lower tier (epic, rare, etc.)? Nothing. I feel that finding a Legendary doesn't truly reward me. I'm just picking up another gun with better stats...Recommendations: Make the gun tiers have their own "unique" trait. I'm not saying that you have to go bonkers with a gun shooting a dragon or homing missiles but at least give each tier a fun of its own. Similar to other games, you have a rare weapon that has something that even a legendary or higher doesn't have. Make a legendary have maybe a shoot two bullet at once or even have elemental aspects of guns. The game doesn't need to be a diablo-like or Borderlands-like game in terms of crazy weapons, but make finding new guns refreshing, fun, and engaging considering this is what I assume is the highlight of Dust and Neon. This game has so much potential but for a game that fully released, I was expecting more.Review: 5.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Dust & Neon manages to make its 'gunslinging' roguelite gameplay feel unique thanks it's cover based shooting and a level of deliberateness required to succeed in its challenges.It ultimately fails to keep those thrills up for its entire runtime, in no small part to late game progression that demands you replay levels over and over again without having enough run to run diversity to make replaying feel unique.The few hours of fun it does have might be worth it on a sale, but I wish I could recommend it more wholeheartedly because there really is something to its core gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Janky Dust & Neon Review!The Short: Do not buy…The game requires you to invest time AND will punish you for time invested. Using a Waffle House bathroom is a more enjoyable experience. The Long:I want to start off by stating I was super excited for this game. I have ADHD and sometimes I can only play for a short duration before the gerbils in my head start screaming. This game looked like it could allow me to play for the duration I wanted without falling into a time sink, being punished, and being miserable…They just punish you first, then comes the time sink, then more punishment, and misery to wrap it up.This game now shares the title of “Games I wish I never bought”, as it joins the ranks of other popular titles such as Batman Forever on SNES. I bring up Batman Forever because if you have ever played it on the SNES with a real SNES controller, you will understand right away the level of jank I speak of. The games main concept is a Metroid-esque twin stick loot and shoot with severe punishment for dying. I would say think of “Enter the Gungeon”, but that would be an insult to EtG.   What Davey (the Dev) created was a game that is half baked and not thought through. Already putting several “hot fixes” to dial down the insane punishing “features” the game has.The Time Sink:Death - When you die in the game, you lose your guns. Now there is a way to get one back, but that requires you to grind 30ish hours in the newbie zone, stockpile all your funds, and buy the perk where if you die, you can hold onto a very small portion of your funds. Holding onto funds will allow you to buy back a gun…IF…you have bought the perks to even allow you to buy them back… Which you guessed it, even more grinding in the newbie zone… Now you will ask “Won’t you just gain money through normal means of progression in the game?” Yes you will, but because the game will also make the enemies match your level, which means you will always be facing tough enemies no matter the location. So… if you’re the type who likes to grind a bit before moving on, because grinding allows you to have an advantage against enemies later on…Well…The game negates it and you’re boned. How are you boned? If you die, the enemies stay at the higher level, while you have nothing to fight them with… The game won’t scale back until you get weapons to hold your own. It just sends the BOHICA squad after you from the start, creating a death loop. This all means if you have spent hours and hours grinding to get damn good guns and stats,  then die because of a slip in judgment, the game will laugh and proceed to push your ♥♥♥♥ in if you try to play again after dying.Now by some miracle, you’re able to kill the high level baddies with your starter weapons. You’ll have to repeat the previous grind again, just to get weapons to match the baddies trying to murder you. Once you get those guns, you’ll be able to make short work of them…BUT…The bosses don’t play by the rules. They actually scale to your level AND your weapons. So even if you do get the legendary BFG 9000, the bosses will brush it off like it was a wet fart.All the grinding will allow you to bump your stats, but if you sink those stats into the guns you had and then you die… You are now stuck with a build you can’t use… That’s how the game punishes you for grinding. But you’ll need to grind to get the better weapons to beat the bad guys…which makes no difference in boss fights because they got Konami code armor! If you gain higher levels, the missions all turn into hard versions and they become the only choices…But you’ll need GUNS that can hurt the bad guys on those hard missions…Which if you have died, you won’t have…and the missions will stay at those hard levels with them being flooded with T-800’s, T-900’s, T-1000, and that new feminist super bot they had from the latest movie. You’ll need to grind up the rare health packs on the maps, but again, if you grind you’ll start the whole vicious cycle. BUT,  you’ll need those leveled up health packs for the boss fights…which again, the boss scales to your level and weapons…which negates the health packs… Gun Play:Your guns are heavily dependent on real world physics…to a point…like Line of Sight…BUT…The baddies don’t. They can shoot through walls, doors, cover, and bullets can bend around corners. They also don’t suffer from bullet damage drop off, but you do. They also have Hawkeye level of aim at any distances. When they can snipe you across map with a shotgun, you’ll have PS1 Syphon Filter PTSD flashbacks.Music:There is a reason you can download the soundtrack for free… and it’s not out of the kindness of the Devs heart…Economy:The game uses Bidenomics for its in-game pricing of weapons and power-ups.    Visuals:The only good point about the game, but it’s a shame it’s wasted on shotty game design. For instance, the train robbery levels. Some of the cactus or background visuals will randomly be generated on the tracks and you can watch them pass right through the train. Additionally, the train robbery levels, if you kill a baddie, his loot can roll off the train and you miss out on it. This defeats, killing everything from a distance, as you now have to either bum rush to capture the cores or you simply wave at it as it rolls off into the sunset. The camera of the train levels also tend to put you at a disadvantage sometimes. If it allows you to view it from left to right, the next time you will be viewing it from right to left. But by doing that, some of the clickables (Health packs) are now hidden behind walls. You’ll have to randomly mash buttons to see if anything opens up. This bleeds into the next issue. The rest of the level visuals are repeated over and over, allowing the same map to be used for multiple “missions”. You’ll fight on one map to get rid of the toxic barrels, only to see the same map be reused for “Clear all enemies” missions. This happens to all the missions, and is a reason why they just shift the camera perspective, making it look like a new map, but just really is an old one.       This game feels like it was never tested to the degree a game of its price tag warrants. It also feels like it was built to be on a mobile device, as a computer monitor would be able to see all the glaring defects. It’s a $7.99 game disguised as a more expensive game. Either buy it on sale or don’t buy it at all. I have a feeling this game will soon become abandonware within the year. Honestly, it feels like I spent more time on this review then the dev did thinking this game through.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for about an hour and a half, I came out thinking that the games core mechanics are solid with its methodical gun play and frantic reload system but ultimately the game is held back by its core game play loop. Enter mission, gain exp, buy new things (if any are worth the purchase), and repeat until you reach the minimum level required to face the boss. Noting crazy or exciting. Also, there's an exp issue. If you level up during a mission you cant continue to gain exp until you return to base. Meaning its possible to reach a new level right at the start of a mission and waste your time going through the whole level in hopes of finding something worth your while. Unfortunately the core mechanics are good but enough to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: [Edit] Removed placeholder and made an actual reviewSplattercat brought me here and I am damn grateful for it. The game really scratched the itch for a western rogue lite shooter. Dust & Neon actually reminds me of another game called west of dead, only much more rewarding and enjoyable.Dust & Neon really gives you feeling of being a badass robot single-handedly gunning down hordes of robots. You have a pistol, shotgun and rifle as your arsenal to gun down a variety of enemies, from basic grunts to snipers and shield-bearing robots. The aim can feel a bit off when hip-firing but is something that the developer is addressing in patches.While I had fun with the rinse and repeat formula of spawning and shooting enemies, the game does take a while to get going. It doesn't help that maps feel fairly repetitive and until you beat the bosses and opening the zones, the enemy variety is limited. This does compound the later levels grind of the game to reach the final boss.While I feel I got my money's worth, YMMV. Even with the repetition and grind, I found myself constantly coming back for more. It's a simple formula and it works.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool mechanics of reloading guns: your press R for each individual bullet and your barrel can be anything from 1 to 12 bullets total. Great execution - everything runs smoothly and doesn't seem like there's a lot of bugs. Nice art style, sounds and gunplay. You shoot evil cowboy robots and pick up money to upgrade shops and gamble on new guns. You repeat this until the game ends. No seriously. This becomes tedious so fast, that when getting to first boss you already feel exhausted. Boring, grindy and doesn't provide any great variety between levels. Just kill everything in the same manner, upgrade your shooting gear (rarely lootin a better gun from 1 of each 20 chests opened) and kill couple of bosses. For 20 euros. :/Well, hats off to devs for making it happen and allowing me to grab as one of the bundled games for around 3 bucks, yet this is a fair price for depth and variety of gameplay this has to offer. P.S. Thanks for the Steam points :)

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:There are three types of weapons (revolver, shotgun and rifle), sprint button, aim button, shooting button, reload button and a dodge roll. Taking cover behind objects happens automatically (aiming will have you pop out).Reloading can be tedious (you have to keep pressing the reload button to load individual bullets), so I recommend setting auto reload in the main menu of the game.You can to level up by using an RPG skill tree and deck out their gunslinger with the best gear they can find in randomly generated maps across four distinct biomes. I love visual aesthetic with a very colorful palette (neon-highlighted environment combines well with the sci-fi).+ Beautiful graphics and atmospheric music.+ Dynamic gameplay.+ 4 biomes with lots of levels.+ Bosses.+ Weapon Upgrades.+ Character power-leveling.+ 24 skills.+ Variety of loot/hundreds of loot boxes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nice niche of arcade that took the graphical essence from the "Bordelands" franchise but with a different gameplay. ProsGameplay: The core gameplay is well thought out in terms of easy to learn but hard to master.Music and feeling of the game is very nice. You really feel like a cyborg regicide.ConsNice setup between storyline and missions however a bit limited in terms of skilltree, levels etc.Replayability is not that good due to the same levels and enemies. No minibosses or custom skirmishesConclusionShortlisting is a go. 19.50EUR is too much for a game with this amount of content. _childDocuments_.review: Do not waste your time with this game. The game starts fine with its moment to moment gameplay and the gun play is solid, and things like weapon buyback are decent. Those are the only good things. This game is the most repetitive bare bones roguelike I've ever played. You have 3 total uninteresting guns that you unlock in the first 5% of the game, and thats it. Theres no new guns, no abilities, nothing. You unlock some temporary buffs early on you'll barely never use, and do get stronger versions of the same guns with small stat upgrades and thats about it. Theres no multiple classes or different builds or anything. So any of the interest and variety of most roguelikes that keeps you invested and offsets the grind isn't here. You fight the same 4-5 boring robots in the same repetitive uninteresting environments with the same 3 guns for the entire game. Theres like 4-5 mission types you will have played by the first 10% of the game and that's all there is to see. Theres some bosses, but even that is done poorly. You unlock them by grinding repetitive missions, but they have A LEVEL CAP. So rather than just fighting them after doing a few missions you have to grind the same missions repeatedly just to level up in order for them to be available to you. And its so stupid as the levels are arbitrary.,.....one boss requires you to be level 17 and 27 and 32......why not make it 15-25-30......I guess that doesn't require as much grinding. The money and other mats you get are relatively small for no reason, you can sell a legendary gun for 20 dollars and weapons cost 1100.....uh ok? And dear god the permanent character and base upgrades. Nothing sexier than spending 45 min to level up and get "+2% pistol damage" or "+5% damage behind cover" and all these very specific small percentages that you will never notice the effect of. And then base upgrades are "+5% cheaper weapons in shop" and "10% less buyback cost". They literally are so pointless on 95% of them by the time you'll unlock them the upgrade won't matter. So theres no permanent base or character upgrades that you get excited about or that change any of the gameplay in any way possible. The game is just bare bones and repetitive and I'm just blown away theres none of the good parts of roguelikes that makes you want to keep playing, especially for how extra grindy this game is for no reason.....I guess because theres not that much content but they want to pad the run time. I only finished it because I had gotten so far before I realized how grindy it would be to the end and I was already invested. Don't make the same mistakes. Run for cover 5.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Dust & Neon is an adequate rogue-lite twin-stick shooter with exceptional combat, but whose mechanics don’t go far enough to make it stand out. Dust & Neon is a fun twin-stick shooter where you play as a robot cowboy shooting his way through futuristic wild west towns and menacing robotic enemies. The game feels awesome to play, and I particularly like its clever cover mechanic, but it doesn’t push itself or the genre into any new ground, and some of its progression feels a little unbalanced.Let’s begin by getting the fluff out of the way. The robotic/western/sci-fi setting is fun to run around in and fits the silly attitude the game is going for. I love the cel-shaded art style; the bright colors really pop and help make everything readable on screen. It’s easy to locate enemies, loot, and interactable objects and I never felt lost or frustrated because the visuals got in the way. Story wise there’s not much here. There are only a couple dozen lines of dialogue and they mostly serve to get the player into the action as quickly as possible and, frankly, I think that’s all it really needed to do. The sound design is immersive and satisfying - the guns in particular sound distinct and recognizable from each other. I found the soundtrack to be enjoyable but it started to become boring and repetitive over my playtime. Overall I would say these aspects didn’t really sway my opinion of the game too heavily in one direction or the other. The game is structured much like any other rogue-lite. You’ll select a mission, go out and shoot baddies, accomplish the task, and return to your base where you can spend your accumulated currency on new weapons and upgrades. If you die, you lose your weapons and money and have to start from scratch. The map is divided up into four zones which unlock as you defeat the boss of each zone. As you successfully complete missions, your Rank will increase, giving you skill points to invest into perks like increased health, faster cooldowns, higher ammo reserves, etc. Once you achieve the required Rank, you’ll take on a boss. As you open up more zones, the types of available missions increase. I think this is one of the weak points of the game. While each zone looks distinct from the others and you’ll find yourself exploring western shanty-towns, ducking and moving between train cars, and delving into underground caverns, the procedurally generated areas within each zone ended up blurring together and feeling rather monotonous to me. The mission structures also feel a bit uninspired. Apart from one mission type that requires you to hold a position for a set time limit, the rest of the levels ultimately boil down to going to a specified area and shooting the extra tough bad guy, or shooting a large group of bad guys, or shooting the bad guys protecting the thing you’re also supposed to shoot. The good news is…the shooting is superb!The gameplay is where Dust & Neon really shines and elevates the experience.You’re provided with three weapons: a pistol, a shotgun, and a rifle. You can find better variations of these weapons while looting on missions, or purchase some at your base. All of the weapons are effective and fun to play with. Shooting feels punchy and the camera shakes to accentuate the impact when your bullets connect with their target. The movement is nice and smooth, dodging gives you sufficient i-frames (I particularly like the dodge-slide your cowboy does when trying to move into cover), and the game cleverly implements a fun contextual cover system to great effect. Your character automatically ducks down as you approach large crates, barrels, or counters to protect you from oncoming fire. Pulling the left trigger allows you to stand up and aim, but leaves you vulnerable to enemy fire. Aiming in this game simply means being able to see the line of fire and effective distance of your currently equipped weapon so you can be sure you are pointing in the right direction. You aren’t required to aim though, which means that a skilled player can blind fire a whole saloon of robots away without the risk of exposing themselves or taking any damage. This leads to some really fun old west style shootouts as the enemy AI swarms around you, moving to find its own cover, and attempts flanking maneuvers. The enemy AI is good and my most fun moments in the game were when I was frantically sliding in and out of cover while desperately reloading and dealing out as many shots as I could. As soon as shots are fired you’ll have a wave of enemies gunning for you from all angles, and if the enemies inside buildings hear the fighting outside they’ll begin to spill out into the battle. There were times when my whole screen was filled with evil robots trying to end me as I slid, ran, shot, and changed weapons on the fly to deal with new enemies pouring in from off-screen. This all helped to keep combat engaging through my 8.5 hours of playtime. I felt like such a badass as I waltzed into an old jail, shotgun in tow, to wreak havoc on the robot enemies inside.That all being said, I encountered some balance problems in my playthrough that put a damper on the otherwise rewarding loot system. I’ll give two examples. First, I came across a pistol, shotgun, and rifle at Rank 20 that were so powerful that I was able to beat two bosses with them and also discarded every other weapon I found for several hours of gameplay. It’s nice to feel overpowered for a little while, but it was disappointing to not find any new weapons that would be as effective as what I already had, especially after beating a boss and hoping for a shiny new gun. Second, there’s a gauntlet style mission where you go through three combat arenas and, if you successfully beat each arena, are rewarded with some nice new weapons. In order to unlock the gauntlet mission, you are required to complete a checklist of 4 or 5 regular missions beforehand. On 3 different attempts, after dying and losing my gear, I made it my goal to do a gauntlet to secure some good gear. Each time, while completing the checklist missions, I was able to acquire good enough weapons that when I finished the gauntlet, the rewards were weaker than guns I just obtained in the regular missions. This cheapened the purpose of doing the gauntlet for me and left me feeling discouraged. What is the point of going out of your way to do something challenging for the promise of a great reward when you can more reliably get better equipment at a lower risk?There are other things that don’t feel fully fleshed out. There are two separate shops that sell character buffs for a limited number of missions, which feels redundant. I had a few instances of my character getting stuck in some awkward geometry and dying because I couldn’t escape. I found it strange that boss fights were gated behind achieving a certain Rank, which left me doing more of the repetitive missions to level up and  just felt like filler. I would have liked to see some greater depth in the combat as well. There are exploding red barrels that are begging to be thrown or pushed into enemies but can do nothing else but sit still and get shot at. Instead of another limited buff it would have been cool to substitute it for a special move or power. I think that with just a little more oomph, the already excellent combat would have been pushed to the next level.Overall I enjoyed my time with Dust & Neon. If you like twin-stick shooters, or are an obsessive rogue-lite fan who likes playing as many as they can find, this game is definitely worth your consideration. If you’re new to either, this is an accessible and easy way to get into either genre, but there are better experiences out there that you should try. I would probably avoid purchasing it at its full price of $20 and wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game at PAX a few years ago and finally got around to buying it. The gameplay is fun, but a few things detract from the action.The hub world seems unnecessary, is large (so takes time to traverse), and is mandatory after every mission. This slows down the game since the loop between missions isn't that long. They should make you teleport back to the mission select machine and make it so upgrades and such can be done in the menu.On one mission I think I did the quest things out of order which is fine, but that ended up breaking my navigation so I had to wander around the map several times until I found what I missed. Death, especially early on, seems a bit harsh since you don't have the upgrades to keep more stuff. Still, for $10 it's a nice diversion.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's a fun rogue-lite game and worth giving it a play through! With my meager 10 hours of gameplay, I was able to complete probably about 85-90% of the game. I've cycled through all the weapons and I've gone through most (except the final) boss, and it really is fun. As part of the rogue feel, it's not super forgiving. It is a bit of a grind to get the money to re-buy guns and upgrade stuff, and that's not a problem, except for the fact that it's pretty dang repetitive. Repeating the same missions over again is fine, but when you need to do that 5-10 times in a row just to buy a single upgrade it gets slightly stale. Overall though, a really very fun game that could definitely get better as more updates keep coming.Also, the soundtrack is amazing. *chef's kiss*

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing playtime is about 6 hours. All of that was right after launch. And the whole reason I'm writing this is I just recently checked up on the game to see what updates came out and noticed it's a "MIXED" review (69% of all reviews, nice). I'm posting this because the game doesn't deserve that.I can get the gripes - it is a simple game, with a simple loop, but it's fast, smooth, and stylish as hell. It brings a fun robot-borderlands vibe to the weapons that I appreciate, has some fun boss battles, and and with its neat aesthetic it's a pleasure to watch.Most of the things I found slightly frustrating - the punishment of losing a god-tier gun on death, the lack of mission variety, and elevated prices of the hub shops have seen been addressed (at least I'm told) by recent patches - my experience was before these tweaks and I still found it entertaining.All that said, my play time here is 6 hours and other reviews mention completing the whole thing in ~10 or so.  So if you don't like button mashing for the sake of button mashing, maybe it's not for you. And that's fine, but don't get caught up on the negative reviews. Buy it, play it for 90 minutes, and see if you think it's worth it.Bring a gamepad because I have NO IDEA how one would do this on kb/m.

Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: it's alright. Mild recommend.The cover based shooting is a lot of fun. There are three weapons (revolver, shotgun and rifle) which each feel preferable in different situations, and a character upgrade system which isn't really complex enough to make "builds", but just choose some strength and weaknesses. Their is clearly some Borderlands inspiration, especially the weapon crates, but the guns don't really have unique or special effects, just rarity grades and randomness in their stats.My main complaint is the game is kind of repetitive, and when you die you lose money and all your weapons. Depending on the upgrades you gained, you may get some random starting weapons and possibly buy back your old weapons. But you will probably have to grind some missions to earn money to find or get money to buy back those weapons. Missions can sometimes have extremely difficult opening sections which are almost guaranteed death if you don't quit out quick enough. I can handle the repetitive gameplay (because it is fun), but combined with taking away progress on death is a bad combination in my opinion. But I did enjoy the game

That feeling can be amplified by presence of the Reload mechanic that kept me on alert during missions. When it comes to the game's missions, my favorite have to be the train heists. _childDocuments_.review: YEEEEEEEEEEEEEES!I'm blown away that this game was developed by one person.  Absolutely amazing job.  Great graphics, buttery controls, competent menus, good backstory and characters, and really addictive gameplay! _childDocuments_.review: A Diablo meets Westworld gunslinging roguelike arpg. I was hesitant to get it due to the mixed reception it was getting, but said "♥♥♥♥ it, it looks cool" and turns out that its one of the most fun games I've ever played. I absolutely love it. The game is short, there's not a ton of content, and the gameplay only really does one thing... but it does that one thing so well I can't get enough of it. To me it is the ultimate western gunslinger game. Diving through saloon doors to take out a room full of baddies then ducking behind a table to frantically reload your six-shooter as the reinforcements arrive; dodging bullets and sliding behind them guns blazing only to find your chambers empty with one foe still standing; whipping out a double barreled shotgun to finish the last one off right before they get you. Getting good at this game feels incredible as you grasp and begin to flow with its kinetic chaos, and you start to pull off fights and desperate escapes you didn't think were possible when first playing. I also just really love that cyberpunk-western setting and atmosphere.Is it worth the full price? Looking at its feature list and game length in a vacuum I would also be inclined to criticize it as many others have. However in playing it, and experiencing the sheer serotonin rush it gives me, I don't really care about what it lacks, I just really love what it is. I'm hoping the developers continue adding content to the base game because I feel like they have the foundation of something truly special here.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Shocked by some of these reviews. great game. if you like Borderlands this game gives you all the same feels. the great gun loots, the satisfying kills, the movement and reload is great, even the animation feels borderlands, which I love. You are given constant perks and upgrade choices. except this game is even harder because when you die you lose all the cool guns you spent all that time looting. although as you progress you have the ability to re-buy those lost weapons.Time and love was put into this game. The map is broken into 4 quads and you have to defeat the Boss in each one to proceed.   the replay value is excellent with the huge variety of weapons. the reload system is totally unique and cool once you get the hang. buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Right, I don't usually play rogue likes aside from Isaac but this game goes hard.The game feels very addicting to play, through the fun and punchy gunplay, and the gameplay loop of getting new equipment as your progress which feels very rewarding without feeling overpowered. And based off of that alone I could see myself sinking multiple hours into the game, and would put in even more if the game had some kind of endless wave mode. I'm also a fan of the somewhat open level design which seems quite foreign to me in a rogue like game but is definitely a welcome addition. On top of all that the aesthetic of the game is pretty cool and the soundtrack is cracked. Anyway, maybe it's just because I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at rogue likes, but I also like the way the dying mechanic works in this game, it doesn't feel like a ball ache of a set back. but instead just gives you the chance to go back and fight some more enemies your level preparing you for the next challenge. Overall, I'd say if you're a newcomer of the rouge like genre of even someone who has experience in it, this is a great game to try out.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off a little slow paced but you get upgrades to movement speed and dodge cooldown. It gets intense pretty quickly - I've only played 6 hours and I'm having a BLAST. There's a section near the start where you fight some insanely tough enemies but you're expected to die there to show the death mechanic. Well rounded upgrade system - health, lifesteal, damage from cover, lots of fun upgrades. All in all a well-rounded roguelite (well kinda, you play individual levels instead of starting over from the beginning every time you die). When you die you lose your guns but you can get an upgrade to buy your guns back after death. Loving this game and def worth the $24 I spent on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Roguelike with a fun game loop with an engaging and beautiful furturistic wild west fantasy!Difficulty feels really well balanced, easy missions help catch up from failed attempts and the harder ones feel challenging and rewarding upon completion but not too punishing or final when failing.Guns feel unique enough to cater to both run and gun and more planned playstyles and rarity is generous enough that you aren't farming for hours to get a legendary in your hands/Would love a mini map or something to better navigate and make sure I clear out every last filthy robot before finishing each stage :D
_childDocuments_.name: Dust & Neon

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's really fun. But there are a few things for potential players to note:The comparisons to Borderlands are not quite what you would expect. Sure, there are randomly generated guns that you obtain through missions or buy, but they are lost on death. Additionally, in contrast to Borderlands games, the gun mechanics are not at all similar. Dust & Neon is much more of a tactile shooter. You don't want to run and gun but rather take cover and wait for your enemies to reload or sneak up on them.As for guns, I haven't found any with special perks yet, but the overall mechanic of "lost-on-death" is actually refreshing compared to the Borderlands games where you must manage a huge collection of guns.Reloading is also a very interesting mechanic in this game. By default you are expected to spam the reload key to put each additional bullet in your gun. Luckily there is an auto-reload option in the settings, but guns will reload at a slower pace than you can probably spam the "R" key (it's a good tradeoff to just use auto-reload in my opinion)As for price, the game has a moderate amount of depth, but not enough in my opinion to justify the $30 price point. I was particularly excited to try this game and so I could justify the $24 price at release. The sweet spot to pick this game up on sale is definitely $15-20.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is easy to get into and a lot of fun. _childDocuments_.review: The first thing I said to myself the second I booted it up was, “Damn, this feels like Borderlands.” Building upon the works of both recent and not-so-recent entries in the roguelite, looter shooter, and twin-stick arcade-style shoot ‘em up genres (a balance it strikes surprisingly well, given — or perhaps because of — its simple mechanics), Dust & Neon is the latest entry in a series of unrelated video game releases that have taken the Wild West and unashamedly mashed it together with some other period-breaking elements to further solidify its legendary status in popular culture.The game is set in a “post-apocalyptic Wild West overrun with villainy,” and that’s about all the player needs lore-wise to get into the nitty-gritty of its equally undemanding mechanics: aim the right joystick at an enemy, shoot them with R2 (or RT for the sods using Steam Big Picture with an Xbox controller), and repeat the process until all the robot enemies are riddled with bullet holes. (I leave out mouse-and-keyboard controls from this note because as a twin-stick shooter, the game simply cannot be enjoyed without using twin-stick control.) The mission of the lab-cloned gunslinger that the player controls is simple: kill all robots.Dust & Neon is mechanically simple. The gunslinger has access to three types of guns: a pistol, a shotgun, and a rifle. RPG-esque character progression comes in the form of two skill trees: an offensive tree and a defensive tree, while homebase progression comes in the form of unlocking and improving various shops as well as in gradually purging gameplay of its roguelite elements (i.e. being able to earn back the guns and cash obtained when dying mid-mission, the only significant early-game effect of the game’s roguelite mechanic).Playing the game, it immediately becomes clear the extent of the Borderlands franchise’s influence on Dust & Neon. This game draws heavily from Borderlands’ iconic apocalyptic wasteland of Pandora — in particular, one will notice parallels with the post-Hyperion takeover Arid Nexus - Badlands of Borderlands 2, another frontier-style landscape overrun with similarly-murderous robots.  Another game that Dust & Neon likens to, and more in line with its own mechanics, is another isometric twin-stick shooter set in the American Frontier: Devolver Digital’s Weird West, a self-proclaimed immersive sim that takes the occult to the Wild West. All three shooters have comic book-style aesthetics, though admittedly Dust & Neon’s simple cel-shading graphically pales in comparison to its two precursors, and there is a painful lack of landscape variety in the game’s four regions.Speaking of lack of variety, is the gameplay loop — another aspect of the game that it unfortunately cheaps out on. To fulfill the gunslinger clone’s task of ridding the world (i.e. the four accessible regions of the game) of robots, they embark on various missions by way of a bounty board, where they can select from a few different missions: robbing a moving train filled to the brim with cold, hard cash (a common trope in Wild West-based media), genociding a town, shutting down some sort of miscellaneous not-fully-explained-or-characterized power plant facility, and some others.This is where the repetition of the gameplay becomes apparent: the player takes on a bounty and completes it, dropping one or two or twenty bodies along the way and possibly earning themselves a sweet new gun of the three possible types (pistol/shotgun/rifle); returns to the homebase with their hard-earned cash, and upgrades either themselves or their base just to go back to the bounty board for the next mission.From the storytelling perspective, Dust & Neon is really lacking. That’s something most reviews get right. But, here’s where a lot of them grossly misunderstand the game: it’s a twin-stick shooter. Many games like Weird West are as well, but where Dust & Neon and Weird West begin to diverge is in their intentions: this game’s claim to fame isn’t in building up its lore, but in its arcade-style frantic gameplay, something that is less like Weird West and more like a version of Borderlands served in a small bowl of watered-down broth.And this is where the fun of the gameplay becomes apparent: it isn’t an “immersive sim action RPG” masquerading as a twin-stick shooter, and it doesn’t claim to be — it’s openly a construction of what the twin-stick shooter used to be, a mindless shoot ‘em up that echoes back to the times of the arcade, albeit less of a proto-roguelike and more of a diluted roguelite. When enemies begin to swarm the player from every direction with shots and bombs coming from every which way, is when the game really begins to shine. The gameplay loop may be simple, but it sure as hell is brutal (the game even makes a point of this in its store page description: “Be warned: Dust & Neon isn’t easy”).Despite its three types of guns, simplistic mechanics, and its limited set of enemies, Dust & Neon somehow procures a surprisingly strategic form of frantic arcade gameplay, and one can almost forgive the game’s lack of depth as the gunslinger is forced to rapidly switch between pistol and rifle and shotgun and back to pistol without pause while surrounded by death-robots, all the while having to button-mash square (Xbox’s X button) to frantically reload one’s equipped gun. (This game feels like it was designed expressly to be a leading cause of carpal tunnel syndrome.)It can be overwhelming at times when the gunslinger’s health bar drops from full to nil in three seconds flat, but the game is very overtly designed to be overwhelming, and that’s where the core of its gameplay comes in. (One can note that there does exist a free Netflix port of Dust & Neon floating around in mobile game stores, but it’s quite an underwhelming experience and the strategically frantic gameplay becomes frustratingly frantic because of the port’s erraticness and unoptimized controls.)So, there it is, Dust & Neon in all its glory. It’s a fun arcade-style indie game to pass the time between the releases of larger and more expansive titles; it does an excellent job of being actually a twin-stick frantic arcade shooter, and doesn’t shy away from the brutality in gameplay that the genre it comes from is most famous for. It’s well worth the time, but not exactly the cost — its $29.99 list price ($23.99 with its 20% launch discount) feels just over the edge of being too steep for such a simple game.

_childDocuments_.review: ** For full disclosure, I received a free review copy of the game from Rogue Games, Inc **Dust & Neon is a weird and wonderful game in which you take on the role of a gunslinging hero who is out to free the West from an invasion of robots in this roguelite gem.The cell-shaded graphics look amazing, the music is fantastic for setting the atmosphere and pace of exploration and engagements, and it handles very smoothly on both controller and mouse and keyboard.One of the things I have loved most about the game so far (and I'm a few hours into it) is the Borderlands-type feel the game has with its art design and the ability to loot weapons with random stats in a variety of rarities. There is also a great selection of game mechanics, such that you can come back as a clone when you die - with the abilities you've already upgraded. You always have some free weapons to start you off. And if you're lucky enough to tough it out on some long runs - you can keep your gear between missions as long as no one sends your clone six feet under.So far, I've not found anything I dislike in the game, except for some human errors (mine), but I'll post an update once I have seen those credits roll!

Maybe things will get tougher.Oddly enough I kind of wish the theme for this game was different like just a straight up western game.People have also mentioned price point, I picked it up at 24$ during the release discount which feels about right but if 30$ is steep I'm sure this game will go on sale soon enough.

name: Peglin
detailed_description: The dragons have been popping peglins and stealing all of your gold for as long as you can remember. Enough is enough. It's time to venture through the woods, conquer the fortress, and delve into the heart of the dragon's lair to take back what's yours and teach those dragons a lesson. Peglin plays like a combination of Peggle and Slay the Spire. The enemies are tough, and if you're defeated your run is over, but you've got powerful orbs with special effects and incredible relics that influence both your enemies and the physics you'll use to defeat them. Features: Collect and upgrade powerful orbs and relics to defeat the monsters and bosses that stand in your way. Fight enemies with Pachinko-like gameplay - hit more pegs to do more damage. Use crit potions, refresh potions, and bombs wisely. Explore a new map every time , with different orbs, enemies, and surprises along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one for me. I like it, and I definitely recommend it, but there's definitely some drawbacks.Some of the good stuff first: As far as a Peggle-type game goes, this is probably the best you're getting on PC. There's a simplistic, but charming art style to it. The music is pretty good. Definitely has some catchy tunes, which is a good thing since you'll be hearing a select few CONSTANTLY for large chunks of each playthrough.The classes have tremendous variety, each allowing for a very different way to try and build your run. Certain orbs and items are limited to one or two classes, and some can just use them better than another class can due to their starting perks. You can also make custom runs out of any combination of orbs/items you've ever taken with any class.The difficulty curve, though, is where things get a little...off. The base game's difficulty is reasonable, and if you're decent at this type of game, you'll get the hang of and beat it pretty quick. When you start going up in Cruciball levels (This game's version of Slay the Spire's Ascensions), It's not so much a difficulty curve anymore as a difficulty CLIFF. There's 15 levels in the current version as of when I wrote this, intending for 20 in the full release. 5 is what I'd call the best balance of difficulty since the negatives it puts on you there actually make some new builds possible. 8 is a good challenge. Above 10, each level has a NASTY debuff, and winning on 14-15 requires an absurd amount of skill to get to where you even have a CHANCE of winning (if RNG lets you).Overall though, I'd still say a good game and worth buying if you're into this.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin, for me, solved the reluctance I had for Peggle type games. Instead of the challenge being based around individual levels, with limited shots, needing to hot specific pegs, Peglin acts more like a roungelike. Hitting pegs simply represents damage done to enemies, with that damage doubling if hitting a critical orb, or the pegs resetting of hitting a reset orb. As you succeed at clearing levels you are given new orbs that act differently to eachother when used, and different artifacts, each one fundamentally changing the way you play the game. Peglin is the marriage between the fundamentally fun game play of Peggle, and the run based advancement systems of games like Spelunky or FTL. And as such, it is one of my favorite games.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is a game with a charming main character [the Peglin] and a fun combination of strategy (what orbs, what upgrades, aiming the first shot) and chance (everything that happens after you let go the orb). I find it a good way to relax -- and if I find myself getting frustrated with missed shots, I know it's time to take a break, so it's also somewhat self-limiting, which is a good thing in a mildly addictive game!
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'd say this is the lamest Roguelike game I've ever played. There is no sense of progression. You can clear the main game as many times as you please and every time you do, nothing changes. You always gonna start with the same 3 boulders and a knife. It's always the same game over and over. In Roguelikes I like getting permanent upgrades, to make the early game somewhat faster. Vampire Survivors got it right, Dead Cells got it right. Is it that hard? I know it's still in early access, so I'll come back to this game once it's actually enjoyable for more than a few hours. The potential is there, but in this state, the game gets boring fast. Right now, it's incredibly overpriced for what it offers.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Not actually that bad RNG-wise, it gets incrementally harder every time you beat it, with an option to go back to less hard if you just want a chill experience.  You just have to play strategically on the overmap and during the levels.  Still one of my favourite games, still unlocking things, the devs are constantly adding new everything and deserve much better than these reviews.  Yes, it can be hard sometimes - but you just got to play smarter.  Seriously, look at this tiny game and look at my playtime.  I work 40 hour weeks and I wouldn't put my time into something I wasn't having fun with.  Try it.
