_childDocuments_.review: Peggle meets slay the spire?More like; Mobile game meets Pachinko.TLDR REVIEW: The crit system does not make sense and went completely unexplained, the runs are too long, the unique orbs and "?" events are very uninteresting, it lacks variety in every sense, there is no discernible narrative after 15hrs of gameplay I've invested and the game costs $25 CAD when it plays like a mobile game in beta (That may be an insult to some mobile games tbf) and It feels like it was made by someone who had a decent idea but no idea how to execute it.LONG REVIEW: As a lover of both Peggle and roguelikes You think the concept would be a slam dunk for me but it suffers from the game being "All luck no skill" in the worst way and scratches neither of the itches I had for the aforementioned game/genre. I began hour zero with tons of goodwill (In fact I had genuine fun for the first hour) and I ended hour 15 annoyed and confused about the purpose of this game. It does not feel like it was made for Peggle fans or Roguelike fans. The Peg fans will be salty that its worse mechanically and less visually engaging then its inspo, and the roguelike fans will be salty it doesnt give you enough agency to feel like its more than completely random (AKA not a roguelike AT ALL other than in visuals for map navigation).Where Peggle had interesting characters, was vibrant, entertaining and engaging with clear cut power-ups that you could optimise and somewhat plan for, this game is drab and grey/brown with inconsistent abilities (some being outright virtually useless I'm looking at you Blind orb). Where rogue-likes are fun for their perceived randomness this is just frustrating and far too inconsistent not to mention LONG. A run sacrificed to the RNG gods after 2+ hrs at 1.5x speed is just too much for me when I only have so much free time.Strategy does not extend beyond picking the one peg you think you need to hit that round to reset the board or get a crit and leaving the rest at the feet of RNGesus, and god forbid the peg you need is out of reach. cause then you're just throwing away a turn. But even just picking a path after a fight forces you to play another round (or rounds) where you can take dmg POST fight. Too many if not "most" mechanics go unexplained, there is no narrative that I've been able to discern in 15hrs of gameplay. It has potential when you gather a few relics that compliment each other but this has happened on average once every 7 hrs for me. I could go on and on but I think you get it.IMO It feels less like a video game and more like I'm just standing at a Pachinko machine but the only prize i win is playing the game again. OH and charging $25 CAD after tax for this game is just offensive! I wouldnt have paid more than $5 but in its current state it damn well should be free.It feels like it was made by someone who had a decent idea but no idea how to execute it.Please spend your money on something else.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a phrase I saw in another review that I feel sums up the biggest downside of this game:DEATHS DO NOT FEEL EARNED.You can get a nearly perfect combination of orbs and relics, yet a few unlucky throws during a battle can make that synergy evaporate in an instant. It doesn't help that the balance of the game is way off, some builds simply suck and others are unbelievably overpowered. The rewards for finding synergies are dubious. You can spend an entire game searching for a combo and never get it, or if you do, it just sucks, and even if it doesn't suck, the aforementioned unearned death could occur. This game design discourages trying new things.A few pegboards are simply awful, which funnel your thrown orbs into death traps where they do little damage. This is made worse when your refreshes are trapped in difficult-to-reach places where the best you can do is chip away at each individual peg in the way to get to it, all the while doing tiny amounts of damage to enemies who relentlessly chip away at your health. I'm looking at you, Slime boss, Dragon boss, slime+bat fight, etc.A few specific relics and orbs have hard counters which are impossible to predict. This issue is somewhat limited, but the worst example of this is the Gift That Keeps Giving, a BOSS RELIC, which makes it virtually impossible to defeat the dragon boss on the final stage (whose appearance is up to chance).ALL of these issues are exacerbated when you play on Cruciball, where the game takes away the little saving grace it has. Some of the time, gaining a Cruciball level will simply increase the overall game difficulty, such as increasing enemy health and damage, which is a good way to amp up the challenge. The rest of the time, however, it severely cripples you by taking away vital game mechanics, such as refreshes, crits, gold, etc. You either get lucky and find an orb or relic to compensate, which has an opportunity cost, or you die miserably. I like that the game has progression and a goal to reach, but Cruciball makes the experience far too unforgiving and unfair. And without progression, the game gets quite stale. The best description for Cruciball is a series of compounding roadblocks that you must spend money (and luck) to remove before you can focus in on building your deck. It's a giant middle finger to people who want to have fun with the game still being replayable.If you like heavily luck-based games, then Peglin is for you. However, if you've seen the popular YouTube videos of extremely fun or overpowered builds/synergies and want to replicate them on your own, prepare to have your patience tested. Of course, you can always relegate yourself to the custom run sandbox mode, but, in my opinion, where's the accomplishment in that?

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Everything is far too RNG dependent and some design choices feel really unfun to play with as you progress into the endgame (Cruciball):- You either steamroll the game or die - there are very rarely close fights and in the endgame you either win everything easily by the start of floor 2 or you die- The shop main function is to remove peballs, which can only be done once per shop and gets more expensive each time. _childDocuments_.review: I really, really, REALLY want to like this game. It's such a good concept, and it does some things really well! But this game has some glaring issues. I don't think the amount of items is one. There should definitely be a bit more control over what you get or some kind of mechanic to help you extend a run, as I've had several runs where I'm waiting for one relic, get to the final boss without finding it, and end the whole thing feeling very disappointed. The biggest issue for me with this comes from trying to set up a build.You'll definitely be able to set up builds in this game, and you'll get some that feel SO nice and are incredibly fun! It's a really enjoyable game at those times, and that's what it should be! I don't think this game should be difficult. It should be a fun, satisfying experience where you can get insane runs. Instead you're often stuck working with what you have, failing at the second stage because you weren't offered any items that let you attack groups, and no longer having fun. But say you do get a good build. What happens then?This game is set up so that each build only works . You're going to experience over and over again runs where you have a  good build, only for the boss of the stage to ♥♥♥♥ you over! Say you have a damage build. Wouldn't it be so cool to get the wall boss, where you have this massive pegboard that aids your build? Well, tough luck. You get the ballista boss instead! Better hope you have group attack or else you're screwed! And this is the fault of this game. No matter how good your run is. No matter how much fun you're having, this game is going to take that away from you. It's going to find some new way to screw you over, and give you everything but what you actually want. It's not a fun experience. But that's what the majority of this game's runs are.So, do I recommend it? It's definitely fun at first, but don't expect it to last you that long. It's still in early access so there will be some fixes to some of these things in the future, hopefully, but as it is now I wouldn't say it's worth the $20.Also, this is a personal gripe, but it's never fun when almost all the boss relics are build specific. Ending up getting offered 3 or 4 relics that would only make your run worse after beating a challenge is not a good way to make people happy. You should be rewarded for doing something well, not punished.

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from some serious lack of consistency. The Minesweeper style boss in the caves looked really cool at first but then I realized that the way the pegs are structured is impossible to get a good set of bounces off on to maximize damage to take out the whopping 6500 frigging health points it has when it is constantly spewing out more enemies and is dealing increasing amounts of damage to me over time. Even if I got 500 damage a turn, (without overflow or piercing), he feels like he'd still kill me from full HP, and 500 damage a turn is something I've only consistently averaged with god-builds from runs that didn't screw me over.I thought we were over this random luck nonsense with roguelites? _childDocuments_.review: Short version: Yes, this game is fun and worth playing if you are a fan of deckbuilders. It's unusual in the genre because of it's Peggle setting, but that adds some charm to the game, and frankly makes it less RNG and more execution-dependent than most deckbuilders, which in my eyes gives it more longevity. It's simple, polished, has a surprising amount of run variety, and will give you your money's worth.Long version: Peggle is a very simple and straightforward game in almost every sense. It's easy to pick up and understand, it has simple rules and mechanics that are quickly understood, the artstyle is simple and low-demand (good.) It offers little beyond what it says on the cover: a deckbuilder roguelike crossed with Peggle. Weird idea, but it honestly works surprisingly well. Your 'deck' is the orbs you use to pop pegs, and they come in a wide variety of effects and even shapes. This variety is what differentiates your runs, for the most part; there's only so many different stage layouts per level, so eventually you will have seen every enemy combination, elite, and boss, and figured out more or less how to play the board itself. But adapting it to the orbs you have in question? That's where the game's longevity lies, because depending on what orbs you are offered and which ones you choose, you can have radically different playstyles. It's not always about clearing as much of the board as possible, and some orbs interact directly with the board in strange and novel ways.So how is all of this executed? Frankly Peglin is very polished. For the most part, the mechanics are well-thought out, well-rounded, and clearly a lot of care has been put into making a large amount of playstyles both fun and viable. Bugs are very few and far between, and the devs have been good about quickly addressing them. Aesthetically, the game is really simple but that works out in it's favor; the visual style is consistent and fun, a lot of creativity has been put into the details of making almost every orb have wordplay of some sort, and the soundtrack is hardly amazing or memorable, but it's never annoying or disruptive, easily above average.The devs are very responsive; early in the development cycle, I sent a letter detailing some findings about the game, and was more than pleased to get an answer that was clearly not a canned HR letter about appreciating support; instead the developer addressed several points of the feedback and hinted at how they might be resolved in future patches (and they were indeed.) That's a rare gem. Since then, updates have not been frequent but they have been of consistently high quality and added quite a lot of content to the game.So are there any downsides? Yes, two major ones to my taste. Firstly, some encounters are in my opinion poorly thought out and cause unnecessary frustration. The most egregious example of this is the third level featuring some stages with portals on the board that cause your shots to gravitate towards them. Now, at times this allows for some clever play with curveballs, but most of the time, it takes away one of the core components of the game, which is controlling your shots and trying to make sure they hit what you want to hit, when you want it hit, and instead add a heavy dose of randomness to your shots (technically, portals are not random, and in theory you could perfectly calculate every impact of four portals on your shot at any point, but if you seriously try to claim that you could do just that, I'm calling you a liar.) Taking control away from the player when in all other cases it's heavily rewarded, does not feel good.The second, and much more damning in my eyes, is the difficulty scaling. Like any roguelike and especially deckbuilder, this game has NG+ levels, the equivalent of say Ascension levels in Slay the Spire. In this game they're called Cruciball levels. And I have to admit, they embody the worst of difficulty design in deckbuilders in my eyes, particularly egregious in this game. At first it is simply a challenge, but rather quickly the Cruciball levels start taking so much power away from the player that they make certain builds and playstyles simply mathematically unfeasible. It gets to the point where each playthrough feels less like a test of skill and decision-making and more an RNG grind fest of resetting chests and elite fights until you get the relics that would make up for how terrible your starting deck, health, and gold have become. Now, take this with at least some salt, I am hardly amazing at the game by any stretch of the imagination. But I did give all of this a fair shot, I got up to Cruciball 15 (the maximum currently available,) but frankly about 5 of those Cruciball levels were forced. I did not particularly enjoy getting through them because every game felt like I was fishing for very specific things, otherwise I was at the mercy of a single piece of RNG going wrong on any given stage for 30+ stages (the crit only spawned in places you can't reach? Too bad, it's mathematically impossible to kill this elite before he removes 80% of your health.) On early levels, it takes a serious streak of bad luck to end your run. With the limitations each new Cruciball level after around 7 or 8 imposes, it could just take a single instance of bad luck which makes the game so RNG-dependent that it is no longer fun. More importantly, the game starts removing a lot of the mechanics that so much thought went into. You just get to play around and enjoy the variety the game has to offer a lot less, because you get so much less resources and so much less leeway. This all to me adds up to tedium and frustration, not difficulty. It's a shame because this game format offers a lot of ways of creatively adding difficulty, such as making individual encounters more intricate with different enemy types, debuffs, etc, but instead the chosen path is letting the player do a lot less.I am probably being unfair to the game by dedicating so much text to the very few negative points. I truly think the game is a lot of fun despite the difficulties being flawed. Even if you only do a few playthroughs of each character's different builds, and go up the first few Cruciball levels, which feel challenging but not crippling, the game still offers a lot of hours. The core loop is really satisfying, the variety is fun and engaging, and player ability matters much more than RNG. Peglin is definitely worth the price IF you are already a fan of deckbuilders. Even if you aren't, it's quite a good place to start, and I would strongly recommend this game's base difficulty and the first few levels to anyone looking for a good, light game to pass the time with. My own playtime will very likely increase, especially with new updates, and I hope that the development team continues to be as creative and polished into the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Obligatory joke: I'VE BEEN PEGGING FOR OVER 250 HOURSNow for the real review, this is aimed at those who are interested but haven't played, as you can see from my hours, I've played quite a bit of this casual game, and got every achievement.It's a lot of fun, I quite like just playing this while watching youtube or listening to something, and I think most people would enjoy it, the fun for me comes from getting relics and orbs that work well together and just result in broken and powerful builds. (Kind of like Risk of Rain in a weird way.)It's undeniably kind of luck based though there is a skill that comes from learning strategies, builds, upcoming bosses, and orb trajectories. However even then, the game can absolutely screw you over.The game also does a fairly good job at encouraging you to diversify your loadout, if you've got an entirely projectile based build there's a stage 2 miniboss that is very strong against that, if you've got an entirely direct attack build there's an encounter in stage 3 that is basically immune to that, etc. Though some reviews have said that this is a negative.The truth is some encounters are strong against certain builds, which can be annoying to be honest.When you get each ball and relic you are able to then later use it in Custom Games, which is what I do recommend you play once you've unlocked a bunch of balls, it's what I primarily play.There's a game mode called "Cruciball", where each stage gets progressively harder, and quite honestly, that just becomes frustrating and luck based, relying on you getting good orbs and relics. I wouldn't recommend playing it unless you're trying to get every achievement, honestly.Here are some legitimate issues that I've had with the game.The navigation can be absolutely frustrating at times, the way it works is you shoot a ball, trying to go on the bottom left or right side of the board, at the end of some encounters or with some relics it can feel a bit too random and really screw over the path you planned for the level.Also, the game feels like it should be 3x speed by default, the regular speed just feels way too slow and floaty. Just use 3x speed at all times, please.That's it, enjoy pegging.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine that Peggle and Slay the Spire had a baby.This is a roguelike deck builder, with orbs (Pachinko balls) as your cards. There are dozens of different orbs with all kinds of combinations (hots, dots, crit, gold, extra bounce, extra chances, magnetism, chain lighting, etc. etc. etc.)The maps have a choose-your-own-adventure style path with random battles, encounters, shops, chests and mini bosses with a random boss (from a pool specifically for that floor) at the end of every floor, just like Slay the Spire. You can unlock different starting classes to begin with as well. At the time of this review, I only have two and still prefer the starter Peglin. :)The Peggle essence of the game is aiming and dropping your orbs to bounce through each level. Each level has vanilla pegs, as well as ones that will give you gold to spend on upgrades for your orbs/items/relics at the end of each stage and at random encounters and shops throughout the map. Additonally, there are critical hit pegs and refresh pegs that will instantly restore all of the pegs on the floor.Very addicting components, and the creators just released an update. I can tell they care about the game and the user experience.Totally worth the full price tag, but don't hesitate for a second to pick this one up, if it ever goes on sale!

_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: The core concept of this game is solid. Pachinko is one of those game mechanics that tickles the lizard part of your brain because even though there is a level of randomness you feel like you’re just one good shot away from being in control.However the rest of the game relies too much on RNG to really be enjoyable. I highly recommend the developers play Monster Train to get an idea for how you can provide players with a way to better customize and control their “deck” while still encouraging them to embrace the randomness of each run.After 10ish runs in Peglin I’m not really sure what I should try to do next. Due to how random all of the pegs and upgrades are I don’t have a good idea of a “build” I want to aim for. If you look at a Hades for example the weapon you choose and the first power you’re given really set a tone for the run which you can embrace and build towards. But with Peglin I’ve only unlocked one other character and both of their starting relics feel kinda samey / pointless.It appears that I need to start a run, get a couple rooms in, then abandon if I didn’t randomize good power-ups and that doesn’t make me want to play more Peglin.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and unique game marred by horrible balancing and lack of content. While they may add more content in the future (remember, early access games frequently vanish without any updates so do not buy it on this promise) the balance is so poor in some areas I wonder if the devs play their own game or just enjoy entirely unwinnable scenarios. Some of the modifiers have such awful drawbacks you should almost never take them under any circumstances. Healing is scarce for the player and frequently you have very little agency over what's happening due to the random nature of peggle gameplay, but man can it be a bit harsh. I really want to see this game get better and succeed but it's a hard pass in its current state for $20, even $10 is a reach for how little there is to do currently. The only reason I have as many hours as I do is because there's nothing else like it right now so for the time being and for that I'll give it credit.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun as long as you don't mind rouge elements and a lot of luck. You learn how everything works through multiple playthroughs so don't get mad if you don't win your first few rounds. The art is cute and the music is fun. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game. It's cute, fun, and short. I have only played one game and i'm sure there is much more to explore but i can also tell that this game is not for me. I guess a good comparison game would be slay the spire. I wouldn't recommend picking this up at full price though. I don't think its work the £16 it costs. I would pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, just not when it is trying to be a Roguelite. There isn't a lot of content, and that might be enough for you to not want to spend money on it, but the game is fun and addicting, and as there is no doubt more to come, it's worth the early investment. The game challenges you with a variety of enemy types that act in different ways and have different effects on the board. This is genuine challenge. Navigating around the web-pegs and slime pegs so as not to lose momentum, building out your deck to maximize damage output, and dealing with confusion (The only enemy status effect I have seen so far, but hopefully there is more in the future.) and the game is also witty, and quite fun. The best part is easily the music, which is catchy and every song gets stuck in your head. But then we get to the games hard mode - "Cruciball". This is where the game fails for me in the same way that all Roguelites fail -- Instead of leaning into genuine difficulty to challenge the player, the game cheats by changing how it functions. The ball is heavier, more likely to miss pegs, and all the critical pegs you need are far away and out of reach. On occasion, I have fired orbs just to have them hit all of the pegs *around* a bomb, critical, or refresh but not actually hit the bomb, the critical, or the refresh. Other times it will bounce once, and then fly between every peg on the board straight to the bottom. This doesn't make the game hard -- it makes it unfair. Hopefully they fix this, and include more clever difficulty solutions than cheating against the player. But if they did, I guess it wouldn't be a Roguelite.Maybe you, a Roguelite fan (possibly) don't mind it when a game is unfair. But other people, not you (possibly), don't mind eating poop. Doesn't mean it should be a thing.3/5 stars. One for the musicOne for the gameplayOne for the humorZero for the lack of contentZero for being a cheater instead of utilizing the obvious presence of creativity to manage difficulty. (I.E. Being a Roguelite.)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to echo what others are saying: The concept and execution is great, but the content is lacking. As soon as the Devs prove they're not going to take the money and run, I'd say this game will be an easy buy.

_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I do recommend the game, BUT.At first, it's a really cool game. The premise is fun, the primary gameplay loop is fun, the art and music and character designs are fun, the puns are fun. It's a fun game.At first.Quite frankly, the Cruciball system is the single worst progression system I have ever seen in any roguelike. You can unlock three characters, each with their own unique special effect and their own starting orb. Apart from that, the only thing you unlock with each victory are Cruciball levels, each making the game harder. by weakening your character and strengthening the enemies. And the first few levels are actually interesting, giving you less critical hits, higher chances of finding minibosses (which have relics as loot so it's not even a total downside) or giving you an additional weak orb at the beginning (again, not a total downside because you might otherwise take damage from having to reload).But soon, those downsides become frustrating. Less board renewal was a major source of annoyance.I quit at Cruciball level 7, where your starting gold is removed and you get less gold from battles. That sucks a lot. Gold is one of your primary means of progression during a run, and gimping it is making the game harder in the most frustrating way possible. It's not a fun challenge, it's annoying.I might play this game sometimes as a stress reliever but there's no way I'll try to 100% it.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: I think for the most part, after going through most of this game's content that it's really fun and I agree with a lot of people saying it needs a bit more content before justifying the price tag, which looking at the roadmap, looks like it is coming.The main gripe I have with the game is how RNG dependent it can be. At least to my knowledge, it is completely random if you get an upgrade or a new orb at the end of a battle and due to the massive scaling enemies get between acts, this can literally lead to a dead run if you are unable to upgrade your orbs. This is also extremely frustrating in crucible mode where if an R peg gets in a bad spot and you don't have very specific relics, say goodbye to your entire 30+ minute run. I feel like the reduction of R pegs in the challenge mode just feels awful as it just takes the game out of your hands.Apart from this, I would say the game is pretty good and I have put a lot of time into it, I would recommend as a casual game but not for someone expecting an experience akin to a game like STS due to the RNG dependence.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Peglin is an example of what an Early Access game should be. The game has a solid foundation but could use some more development, and getting data and feedback from players is helping the dev(s) a lot as they actively work on the game and release updates. Absolutely worth the money if you have nostalgia for games like Peggle and you enjoy things like deckbuilder roguelites. The game is still early access as I'm writing this so I can't speak to the finished product, and if it wasn't still actively being developed and updated my opinion would probably be different, but so far my current 30 hours in the game have been very enjoyable. It could use a bit more fluff with the progression system to make it more interesting to get further in, currently you have access to all items on your first run and when the first build of the game was released, there were maybe half as many items as there are now. Starting out with some of the simpler orbs and relics available and getting access to more as the game was updated felt very natural, and some kind of progression system that unlocks more items as you progress through the Cruciball would make new runs feel more interesting and give more incentive to actually continue to play the game to unlock harder difficulty options. The luck aspects of the game can sometimes be frustrating when they don't go your way, but can also be immensely satisfying when they do favor you.I'm not the type to give the game a number rating but if I worked at IGN it would definitely get a higher rating than Imagine: Party Babyz
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Fun at first but becomes stupid difficult to the point of no fun very quickly.Things that will happen :--monster score when you only need a few points-1 in 5 chance of throwing into fire between stages feels more like 4 out of 5.-hate that Peglin that steals my HP for that rubbish score multiplier (often hit zero)-Nice music.edited - Cruciball mode past level 5 is stupidly frustrating to almost pointless.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love it, super addictive and satisfying. The type of game you can jump into and finish a full run in maybe half an hour or so. Some might see the short run length and fairly low difficulty as a negative but it's perfect for a casual, relaxation game such as this.Only negative I have are the post-launch changes. There seem to have been some very sever nerfs to a lot of the relics, as well as providing the player with fewer overall and it definitely meant gutting a lot of the aspects I found most enjoying. Yes it was a little ridiculous to be dealing 800,000+ damage per attack in the late game (there's an achievement for over 9000) but the OP magnet power among others were what made it so satisfying to progress through. I really hope they bring back some of the more ridiculous relics, there's a hard mode option right there if you want to turn things into more of a slog.I see some people complaining about the $20 price tag, and I don't know what they're so mad about. For one, it's still early access, and $20 really isn't that much. Heck I've put over 13 hours in at time of writing, and I bought it 3 days ago - there are $100+ games that can't grab my attention or provide enjoyment like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on a whim because I loved Peggle when I was a child.Was not disappointed! It's basically a Peggle rogue-like, but definitely has it's own identity!Super fun to just pick-up and play for a couple hours at a time :)General gameplay loop is interesting and the peg layouts feel quite rewarding! Lots of cool peg-related mechanics and balls make for interesting choices, especially the addition of "crit" pegs that rearrange each shot!The designer(s) definitely know how to make this kind of game fun and understand the potential of a rogue-like pinball-esque game.Also, I always play the game on 2x speed - great feature. I recommend using it after 5 or so runs.As for reviews about bad updates: It's been fixed! Updates made the game a lot less fun at one point because there was so much content getting added that made the odds of finding what you wanted way lower, but now a shop and a money system has been added which fixes everything! You can just save your money for the things you actually want - and if you really want something specific, you can prioritise shops on the map too.

_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been so much fun, so I'm recommending it, but beware of its current purgatory-esque state. Too many underwhelming orbs and relics, and only three zones to fight through.Biggest problem is relic and orb bloat. Poor balancing of several of the pegboards, enemy load-outs, and events means you have to hope RNG gives you the right orbs and relics at the right time. Most Orb and relic perks aren't really strong enough to be worthwhile otherwise. You can't collect them in the wrong order either, because some are completely useless at keeping you alive long enough to find the next one. The Cruciball challenge levels make the issues even more severe.  I also don't think we should ever have to consider skipping a relic after defeating the Boss at the end of a zone. There's only two boss fights that give a reward afterwards, so is guaranteeing a useful relic reward really too much to ask for? Several relics are great to have in the Forest, but do nothing for you in the caves. The original versions of the gardening gloves and salt shaker had this issue, but you could still find them anywhere. Both relics have been changed, but I'd argue the gloves are actually worse now. The new salt shaker sounds nice, but it is actually useless until you have enough healing orbs or relics. An easy way to address the orb/relic bloat and scaling issue is to overhaul the economy. Better orbs/relics should cost more, weaker ones should be cheaper, instead of everything being the same price. The same should be the case for Orb upgrades. We should also be able to sell orbs instead of having to pay to get rid of orbs. Being able to sell Relics we don't want would be even better. Gift that keeps on giving is a great example of a very powerful relic: the dragon hoard was the Only pegboard in the game that counters the Gift, (but that pegboard was horrible no matter what your deck looked like, so I was very thankful when they flattened it out a bit!). Otherwise, the Gift can turn a losing run into a winning run. I would love to spend up to 200 G if I found it in a shop! If the shops stocked a larger fraction of the available orbs/relics, that would also significantly improve the bloat issue.All orbs also need more upgrade potential. The price of upgrades could also vary depending on level and strength of the orb being upgraded. On a lucky run, it is possible to fully upgrade all of the starting pebbles during the Forest Level; But if you don't pick up any relics that boost the pebbles, you won't stand much of a chance at surviving in the castle when there are OP shields standing between you and a line of archers and mages that hit harder than the Slime Boss!Slime Boss pegboard has needed overhauled for a very long time. The slime Mini-boss and Minotaur mini-boss used to have horrible pegboards, but both were significantly improved and now I enjoy them even during Cruciball!! It is very frustrating that I have to consider abandoning a run when I see the slime boss on the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is an adorable little rouge like that I absolutely adore. There are some cool synergies and fun bosses to keep you playing, but I think the $20 price tag is too steep for how much content is in the game right now. This game is in early release so that is to be expected. If you like the concept I recommend purchasing at a later time but if you just cant wait, supporting the devs isn't a bad investment, since all I see is good things to come from this love child of pegle and the rogue like genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever enjoyed any of the Peggle games and also enjoy roguelikes, then this is the game for you! Lots of item and weapon variety that keeps runs feeling fresh and fun! The game also is very good about having everything synergize with each other in interesting ways that are just a blast to discover!Game can be a little RNG heavy AT TIMES, as you never know what items you're going to get, and sometimes you can make the wrong choice on an item that would've been great later in the run in combination with something else you don't have yet, but you can't know what stuff you'll get ahead of time. That part is kinda built into the genre though honestly, roguelikes can feel that way sometimes. There's also the fact that it's a turn based game where you do damage by playing pachinko, which is a lot of fun, but no matter how many hours you sink into it you cant predict every bounce the ball will make, so sometimes you take damage because the ball didn't go where you thought it would. Usually not crazy impactful, but you may run into occasional frustrations. Personally, I'm not really bothered by this, and the unpredictability can enhance my enjoyment and make runs feel even more varied, but it's worth noting.The only big downside I have is not with the game actually, it's with the community. Some of the regulars seem to be very gatekeepy and push away newcomers, and unfortunately my experiences with them have put a slight damper on my enjoyment of the game. It has apparently happened a lot in the past, and it will probably continue to happen in the future, as nothing has been done to actually put a stop to this kind of behavior as far as I can tell. Every community CAN be toxic or CAN be friendly, so join the discord at your own discretion. But, as I said, this is not the game's fault, so please don't think less of the game or the developers because of the community.All in all, This game is a ton of fun! I've sunk 49 hours into it and I don't plan to stop yet! Buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let me preface this by saying that I really enjoyed the game. My issue is that it doesn't feel fleshed out enough. And while I do get that it's not even at 1.0 at the time I'm writing this review, and that the game is receiving content updates somewhat frequently, $20 is definitely too steep of a price right now for what you get. I will keep watch of this game, and maybe someday update this review to be more favorable. But for now, this is where I'm gonna have to leave it off.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: The game looked promising at first, but the devs did the bare minimum content-wise, A fourth stage would have been nice, Endgame content  (cruciball levels) is a very lackluster and unengaging way to increase challenge, balancing is all over the place for the most part and has been for the majority of the games existence. _childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun and scratches the Peggle itch a bit while also adding roguelike elements. Beat it way too quick for a $20 game. Took me 2 hours. Only reason it gets a thumbs up is it didn't glitch at all while I played it. It's also early access so I'm hoping in the future there's more content. As it stands there are only 3 boards to go through before the end of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game to death, but oh my GOD is it frustrating to play sometimes. some fights just feel so unbalanced, and some orbs are just way beyond useless and never worth taking. There's so much potential for this game but all of the new bosses are frustrating to fight and the RNG is downright annoying. Refresh in a bad spot first fight? You lose. Bad first relic? You lose. No orbs to carry first boss fight on higher cruciball? You lose.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of mixed reviews here and many of them are valid. I've got a ton of time into this game, and still enjoy it. One thing you need to be comfortable with is a lot of rng. Higher difficulty modes will require you to save and replay a lot of missions. I'm fine with this, but I can see why many people wouldn't be. I really dislike the change requiring you to unlock the relics for custom games. It's just not a very great mechanic. I love the gameplay and the relaxing feel. If you enjoy puzzle rogue-likes, this game is great. You will not have fun in this game if you do not like puzzle rogue-likes. Also the shield enemies make many builds bad.

_childDocuments_.review: The truth is that I was really enjoying the game, but there's no way I should have finished the entire adventure in less than 3 hours. It gives you the illusion that you need to upgrade your balls  a lot to progress, but in reality, the progress is so fast that before you know it, the game is already over.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin is an almost great Peggle/Roguelike combo that is hindered by a lack of content and variety. The visuals and soundtrack are cute and colourful. The gameplay is simple but satisfying. On the downside Peglin is quickly beaten and offers little more after finishing the cruciball mode (think Slay the Spire's ascension mode). The game has balancing issues - at higher levels there is little build variety and there are only a few viable ways to win.A few updates and additions have been made at the time of writing, all of which I feel have improved the game. If Peglin can continue with great updates and address the issues with content and variety then I would fully recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: The developer seems determined to nerf any fun strategy or synergy that emerges instead of buffing weaker ones which is a shame because very few synergistic strategies even exist in the first place. It seems like there's a lot of opportunity for chaotic RNG fun but there's just about 1 build that does that and you'll get it once every 5 runs before dying to bad RNG. The pegs that can do the big combo damage rarely penetrate to hit the enemy that needs it, and the ones that penetrate don't have the potential for massive combos. It just feels really bad. Add the fact that everything is RNG and you feel frustrated more than you get that big dopamine combo you probably bought this game for.Picked it up after the fix. Same issue, seems worse than before with some combos. Example: Magnet now attracts to broken blocks so you can end up rocketing directly towards the bottom with nothing in the way or to spend the entire duration hovering in one spot. Another fun combo dead.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games, because I'm not necessarily good at writing them. However, this game has provided hours of entertainment. I have specifically chosen to write a review because there have been a lot of recent negative reviews, saying that the game used to be good buy has been going in a bad direction. I disagree. I don't like all of the balls/relics that have been added, but they are cool and can be used in interesting combos, even if they don't match my play style. It seems like a lot of the recent reviews simply don't like rougelite. I think it's a fantastic game, and I would absolutely buy it again at full price (currently $20) The devs update regularly and it seems like they are adding cool things, and I'm excited to see where the game goes from here. Though, if this were the game, I'd still be content.)
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: It's great but maybe wait for more and better balanced content.Half of the powerups are nearly useless. Having a successful run feels like trying to avoid garbage items (even by savescumming). Also many combos build up a status effect called blindness, which makes ONE enemy have a (stacking) 1% chance to miss. I wish I could disable those items.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: I like peglin, I think the concept is very charming and you can make lots of fun interesting builds but if there is one thing this game loves is luck, It's a fun element to have some lucky or unlucky moments at base diffculty but not on cruciballs,Without too much variety in runs, the real replayability of the game is in the cruciballs which make the game harder by stacking more and more rules against you, demanding more skill and specially  Getting past the first boss at levels like cruciball 16 is less of an accomplishment and more of a relief. At high cruciballs, if you find one unlucky encounter that counters your current strategy, you can say goodbye to your run. If you're running defense, just restart your run the moment you see the demon wall as the boss of the castle,There's still some little annoyances of the game itself like the refresh peg being able to position itself in an extremely awkward spot of the map that is near impossible to hit. You could argue that's what refresh orbs and relics are for but finding them in the first place is yet another luck based element. Pretty much everything is luck based, you just have to roll with whatever punches and gifts the game offers you.I like the concept of peglin and think it's a good game at the beginning but if you are someone who enjoys having a fun time or who likes to master a game, I cannot recommend Peglin.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Very derivative game, so much that it lacks an identity, it is basically slay the spire peggle and nothing more.That graphics are passable,  the music is forgettable.It adds nothing new to the formula.The UI is bad, the tutorial is flawed.I would recommend the old peggle game over this game because it has a killer soundtrack plus better level designs.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: This is THE spiritual successor to Peggle Nights, the ultimate pachinko game in existence right now. Already in the early stages of Early Access this game has the same type of replayability and excitement when you line up the perfect shot with the perfect abilities, except in this game with the amount of different relics (passives) and orbs that you can throw out, almost every run feels unique and differentiated. My ONLY beef with this game is it doesn't have something like style shots or the visual pizzazz of getting a 100,000+ point shot that Peggle Nights did. So in that sense while getting a high point shot is nice because you can see the numbers going up, it would be really cool to have some type of visual for the damage number so that when you hit certain tiers it changes colors and you feel like a god for getting a golden shot or something. Anyways if you liked Peggle buy this no questions asked, if this is what the game looks like right now, in one or two years it's gonna be absolutely insane guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: I like the general game idea and I really wanted to like this game since it reminded me of the older puzzlecrawl game “10,000,000”. Peglin is tuned-based and has much more elaborate game mechanisms and strategy (whereas 10,000,000 was mostly about solvning puzzles in real time) but the myriad of game elements just makes it a messy and opaque game design. The game play is frustrating and slow, there is a number of really odd UI choices and the description of power-ups and upgrades are lacking (the game uses many terms from the start without really defining them or offering any kind of guidance).
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: Worth revisiting when there is a balance re-work... right now there's too much randomness in the chests and stores and navigation so that it can be quite impossible to execute a specific strategy or build.  I don't bind games that force you to adapt to what you are given, but currently this game teases you that you have some control and then just throws so much random stuff at you that your choices are drowned out.
_childDocuments_.name: Peglin

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could recommend this game but in it's current state I just can't.At its core this is a cool concept and I enjoyed my time with the game. The fact that this is Early Access is very evident in the balance issues the game currently has. The first area is doable but anything beyond that will be a struggle if not simply impossible unless you have a build that focuses around bombs with one or two orbs that are big heavy hitters for most bosses. Enemies will have too much health or be too numerous to deal with without the bombs and without the heavy hitters good luck defeating anything beyond the first area boss. Area 2 and on everything has way too much HP while being way too numerous. Most of the orbs are pretty useless. The bramble orb seems useful until you realize there are about 5 other enemies with hundreds of HP behind the one that's stuck for a turn or two that aren't stuck and the damage done to them by the bramble is insignificant. There's an orb that passes through everything except special pegs which could be useful if essentially wasting a turn on it wasn't a death sentence. The only reliable healing orb I've found was a one and done for the whole game unless I wasted three upgrades on it which means I wouldn't have any upgrades on the orbs I needed to upgrade to actually deal damage. The list goes on and on.In addition the relics make or break a run. Some are just plain overpowered such as one where your remaining damage after killing an enemy will pass through on to the next (if you get this early and build around it is the only viable strategy that isn't bomb centered that I've found). Other relics will make only the first reload of the fight a free reload which is essentially nothing.On top of all of this during the fight the order of your orbs is is random every fight and is pretty make or break sometimes. You'd think "okay well Slay the Spire you get a random hand of cards every turn, so what's the difference?" but the difference is in that game you still have a choice on which cards to play. In Peglin you can skip one orb and then you're just stuck with whatever order the game decided to give you. You also don't get to see that ball until the next reload where it will again be shuffled in a random order. For example one orb does damage based on all the pegs you have hit during the combat. If you get that the first shot it's almost useless so you bin it. Then you don't even see it the rest of the battle because it was shuffled to the end or you finish before you even reload. This could be solved by doing a sort of hand mechanic like a deck builder or even just letting you hold on to an orb instead of binning it completely, swapping it out whenever you want similar to holding a piece in Tetris.If balanced correctly and if the content gets expanded on this would be an easy recommendation but as is I would save your money and wait to see what happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Original rating of the game during early access: Great game, definitely recommend!Reminds me of old games like Peggle. Fun unique concept brought to "deck making" games. Looking forward to more content being added.Now that the Game is out and more "content" has been added, I do not recommend the game.I have 150 hours roughly and am on Cruciball level 17/20 hard stuck. Why? Because the game is so RNG dependant that your 'choices' are basically made for you. In higher Cruciball levels you can't even save gold for the shop, because you have to rush and add any orbs to your deck (and/or upgrade them) that deal more damage than what you have, but most of the choices of orbs to add are so bad, don't synergize, etc. On the off chance that you do get a decent build going in Act 1, you'll still probably die at the first boss. If you do beat the first boss, congrats on making it this far! Now select from a Boss relic that generally has a downside and oh guess what? You picked the wrong one and the Act 2 boss (if you even make it that far) hard counters what you picked. GG an hour wasted.In Early Access there were less orbs to choose from, so you could generally get access to what you needed and synergize your build. Now it's a total crap shoot with the difficulty scaling way too high.The only way to actually get through the high Cruciball levels is to save scum hardcore. Even then if you don't get the lucky RNG to make a good playthrough it doesn't matter what you do, you're still screwed.Don't buy this until you see some balancing patches to sort this out. It's just not fun at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT EDIT: The new currency system really solves a lot of the games issues - Now theres a nice balance of wanting to get through an encounter cleanly, and trying to focus on money for upgrading or trying to get a solid inventory. A real step in the right direction. Some more content would be nice, but I'm glad that a major issue has been addressed. Changing to recommended for now.EDIT: Speed up options are a good start , and some rubbish encounters have been cleaned up a bit. However, there is now a new wave of relics which hint at mechanics that the game just doesn't deliver on (or need). For example, Muscircle and Spinesse, which increase damage by +X to either crit or damage, already exist on other items - These new relics provide nothing unless you manage to fulfil requirements that the game still doesn't really let you meet. Upgrading and getting new orbs is still complete random, and you still get runs where you get nothing but one or the other. A lot of new orbs seem to the same thing existing orbs do. A step in the right direction, but still needs a lot of polish. Cruciball still sucks, stop filling my inventory with crap instead of trying to come up with a real challenge.A great idea trapped in a web of poor design and frustrating encounters. I love that the game lets you go for utterly daft builds. That's great, more rogue-likes need to let you have absolutely ridiculous runs. Nothing beats throwing a multi-orb with the multi-orb item and having 10 orbs flying around. Throwing hundreds of bombs in one turn is hilarious. Relics are nice and varied, with only a few being absolutely pointless. Good variety of orbs, but currently the game seems to be balanced around anything piercing - If you don't have any of them by act 2, or at least a consistent way of hitting bombs, you're probably out. I can see this game being great fun with a LOT of work. Onto the bad - Everything takes far too long, enemies have to move one at a time, attack one at a time, projectiles move one at a time. It's not like you can react to any damage coming your way, so why not have it all just happen at once? Certain encounters (anything involving spiders) are so miserably slow that i often just restart if i encounter them in the forest.The Forest is the weakest part of the game - Almost every encounter is designed in such a way that there's not really any clear or optimal way to deal damage, or simply takes far too long. You just have to throw and hope your orb goes the way you expect. Many of the Forest encounters seem like you're expected to hit bombs to deal any damage, which means you're going to be throwing a lot of turns randomly hoping that you go the right direction.There are two good bosses in the game - Playing the game in its current state is mostly a constant series of asking yourself the same frustrating questions.Why do the majority of boss reward items simply defeat the purpose of the game? Why line up a shot when the RNG magnet decides your fate? Why aim when Multi-ball will send orbs flying everywhere? Why would i ever take anything that isn't The Gift That Keeps Giving? Why is upgrading orbs random? Why does the game seem to love events that just give you stones? Why does the refresh orb sometimes just spawn somewhere where you have to waste turn upon turn reaching it? Why even have sloped surfaces if the pegs disappear before you have any chance to roll down?In conclusion, currently, No, I wouldn't recommend this game. It needs a lot of polish, and could be great, but as an early access title, it just isn't worth delving into the frustrating mess that the game currently is. Give it a few months, and see how it turns out.

_childDocuments_.review: ===================================Edit: After leaving this game for a few months and then playing some of the updates, I'm sad to say that my suspicions were correct. The game kinda sucks now...at least if you play Cruciball. Because there's little to no skill involved in the game as it is right now, in Cruciball you're essentially treated to an awful experience of an RNG game with ever worsening modifiers the further you get in the Cruciball. Even the quit game reroll trick doesn't help me all that much anymore and the day the devs "fix" that exploit is probably gonna be the day I will uninstall Peglin for good.As for the rest of the game, it's still more of the same, it's just that updates added even more orbs of which 1/3 are useless, 1/3 are actively detrimental and why would you pick them ever and 1/3 are actually decent and are occasionally gamebreakers.Also why in the name of all that is holy would you add self-damage to bramble ball?!===================================I don't like the direction in which this game's development is going. It genuinely feels like there are few amount of builds that are even remotely viable in this game and pretty much all of them involve bombs.I will say this though: this is only the case if you're not doing Cruciball. In the normal game, you can actually experiment and, you know, have fun? And there's also a small "exploit". If you quit back to the menu (or just Alt+F4) before you die/pick a chest relic/any other randomised relic, you get another chance/get another option. This is the only way I have beaten the first 9 Cruciballs.Does that mean that all is good and Peglin is great if you just play normal mode? Well, no. Cruciball is still an integral part of the game and an exploit is still an exploit. And without Cruciball, the game is very easy and tbh, very very short,

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game as you can see from my playtime, but I can't recommend it. The game has alot going for it on the surface but in reality that's just not the case.The game's severally suffers from being in early access. It's a rougelike with little replay-ability which in my opinion is its biggest sin, and the base game can be beat in less than an hour, and you can probably experience all the enemies and bosses in 2.Another gripe is the gameplay itself. They have a whole lot fancy effects with the orbs and the relics that seem to be unique and cool but they all end up doing very similar things and leads to no real build crafting and without that you're left with peggle with extra vfx. I will admit some of the orbs are pretty fun to use but they are a very small few in a sea of dull unoriginal power ups you would see in a similar game. In the end you'll probably end up going into every run looking for the same orbs and relics as only a few are fun to use.The game updates very slow as to be expected from a small team so there's no ill will there, but the amount of content added with each update tends to be able to be experienced all in a fresh run, so you are looking at a good 20 minutes of new content on every release. I thought this wouldn't be the case with the huge update that just happened, but sadly it didn't live up to the hype they were giving off. My last gripe is the price. As the game currently is I'd say it isn't worth it and I feel it'll never be worth the $20 dollar price, as the dev has said they won't be adding any new areas so the game will have a total of 3 areas and the content they add to the game is very minuscule compared to other games out there with similar price ranges. In conclusion the game has a solid core and some good ideas behind it, but sadly they don't live up to what they could be and end up being dull and frustrating due to the fact you know they could do better. Maybe one day the game will be fully released and I can come back and change my review, and I'll gladly do it if the game becomes the game I know it can be. Until that day I can't recommend this game as someone who's been playing since the beta.

_childDocuments_.review: The newest update has completely gutted this game. Before this update, you could reroll relics by saving and quitting to the menu and then resuming the game. That has been completely removed and now there is absolutely no determinism in this game whatsoever. It is COMPLETELY random what you'll get, with absolutely no weight placed to items that might benefit your build. 8 times out of 10 you open a relic chest to a completely useless relic. It used to be that you could tailor an exact build to your playstyle. Now, you're completely at the mercy of RNG that has no ability to be meaningfully influenced. If I wanna play a specific build, before I could roll for things that would benefit my build. Now, I'll get a relic for something completely worthless and the game doesn't have enough options for loot that you can afford to have dead relics. I haven't even bothered trying higher difficulties in the new update because it's just not fun to be cruising for a decent build and have 3 dead relics in a row completely squandering a run. Any more than 2 relics in a row not worthwhile to your build is 100% a restart because you'll never recover against the ramping difficulty. On top of completely ruining build potential, the newest update also added Leshy, easily one of the worst designed bosses in a game I've ever played. It's not even hard, it's just tedious. There are other elite enemies in this game that are the same way, completely tedious and not at all fun to fight. The Upside Down as I call it flips the board while gravity remains the same, so you're flinging balls and PRAYING they hit something. It also has half as much health as end of act bosses. There's a ghost enemy that starts you with one single peg on the board that ramps damage so quickly if you aren't perfect with your skill shots, you're dead. The entire shielded enemies mechanic is just tedious. That's the best way I can describe this game. Before the update, making a build was fun and engaging and you had determinism in your build that let you fight the tedium. Now, its just a big ol pain  in the kiester 8/10 runs and when you do finally get a good run after hours of trying, it doesn't feel rewarding. It just feels like a relief that you actually managed a good run. Overall, I don't recommend this game it its current state, but if they add some forms of determinism into the game, it'll be back to worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. As a fan of the Peggle series of games and Roguelikes, this is just what I've looked for. It's as addicting as Peggle, but with infine replayability. There's still some things I  think would make this game a lot better. I'm writing this review when this game is still in early access, so there's a chance these things will change, but that's exactly why I'm writing this: - The final boss is a little too easy. I had a harder time beating the bosses from the castle.- The navigation system using the pegboard is a really great idea, but I've had some really frustrating situations where I shot a ball towards the direction I want, but it somehow bounced into the other side.- MOST IMPORTANTLY: It would be great if the game had some meta progression. Something like unlocking relics or balls after beating a boss or unlocking an achievement. If this game is going for a pure roguelike, it's understandable to not have this, but for me it would make the game a whole lot more interesting to play if there was a meta goal- More levels, more bosses. As the game is in early access, it's a given that there will be more of this stuff though.All in all I love this game and can't wait to see what's to come next!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Played a little bit of the new content after having not touched the game for almost a year. There's still the same problems as before. The lack of consistency when it comes to dealing damage and creating builds makes playthroughs frustrating. I am surprised that no change was made to this system in the year since I last played.You can add however many orbs, relics, bosses, or classes that you want, but if you do not fix the underlying lack of consistency, then the game is still as frustrating as before. ---------------------I bought this after watching some streamers and youtubers play it. From those videos it seemed fun, but what isn't shown is how many runs it took to get the content for said videos. The highs are high but the lows are oh so low.There is no meta progression in this game. So there is no way to get even the slightest bit of consistency. Between all the random relics and all the random orbs you will most likely get a whole load of nothing. Sure, a few of them are strong - but when everything else is so weak it feels awful. It's too dependent on the loot you get. And this is just the base game - the additional "cruciball" difficulties exacerbate this RNG issue even further.I feel that the game does not respect your time because you have to constantly play until you get that one good run. This sort of gameplay loop does not feel meaningful or fulfilling at all. At best the base game is acceptable to kill some time but there is not enough meaningful content beyond that to justify the price tag. I would recommend to wait for more content and balance changes before buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Eh... This is an almost.  But I just don't think I can recommend it for its price and effort level.-It struggles with any sense of balance.-Character unlocks are incredibly hard to get due to the sheer RNG.  It took me dozens of runs to finally get enough spinfection to unlock one, for instance, and I literally haven't even seen a single Bulwark or Slime ball/relic for even possibly getting one of the other two characters ever since. _childDocuments_.review: Peglin is a game with promise, but no polish - or at least, the polish has been applied in the wrong places, leaving huge expanses of dull gameplay. While I understand that it is an early access game, as of June 2022, .Visually, it is an engaging game. The cute pixel graphics are lovingly-crafted, and they're definitely the main thing that will keep your attention for at least 2 hours of gameplay. It also has appealing audio design, which is great, because every good Peggle-style game needs to have satisfying "plinks". The graphical design of the different orbs you can obtain in your run is also interesting, even if they don't have as much of an effect on gameplay as you might expect.I found the best parts of this game to be the parts inspired by Slay the Spire. The relics system - although not quite as robust and varied as StS - did keep me engaged, at least until I realised that not only were there relatively few relics, they also had little to no synergy with each other. Even the ones that you might think pair well together don't seem to make a tangible difference in how the game plays from round to round, fight to fight, or act to act. Similarly, the random events with extreme parallels from "that other roguelike" (probably one of if not the best roguelikes of all time) were also enjoyable for the first few rounds, until you start to see repeats. And believe me, you will start to notice the repeats very quickly, likely long before you finish the game. Enemy design is interesting, until you realise that there is little to no variety in what they actually do. Normal enemies are minor annoyances that die quickly, elite enemies are annoyances with a dash of bullet-sponge. They overstay their welcome. There is little difference between the types of enemy you face. Occasionally, you'll find gimmick enemies with a special mechanic that actually impacts your strategy, like the mirrors. These were cool the first time I encountered them in Act 2. Finding out that they repeat into Act 3 was a bit of a bummer, and make me feel like .The finest example of the ideas running dry is the Act 2 Wall Boss. Literally a wall with a high health pool and no interesting mechanics. It does not attack for however many painstakingly slow turns it takes to reach you, at which point you are dead. You are playing Peggle with/against a brick wall that does nothing to you, and your only goal is to complete the damage-check. That's it. No strategizing whatsoever.There isn't much strategy behind the random events and what choice you pick. Often, either way, your build gets shafted, and you end up with a hodgepodge of special-effect pegs which don't feel very special or synergize with each other. Peglin is missing that element of control over your destiny. You have very little control over your build, very little control over the path you navigate down (if you're blocked by pegs after finishing a level), and ultimately, very little control over the outcome of the game. You will immediately begin to feel the drain as soon as you finish a run for the first time, if not before then. I cannot imagine this fundamental failure of the game becoming any better without significant changes throughout future development, which is a real shame, because I want to like it very badly.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game because it looked fun, and never played a game like it before. Game has a lot of potential, despite the flaws, but the game is still unbalanced. And at the current moment in time  the devs are simply nerfing any good item in the game (specifically ones you get as a reward for beating the game's *bosses*), thus making runs feel... just average at best. Keep in mind the game also has a hard mode that is, at the time of writing this, been said to be unbeatable by the devs. Why not balance the game around challenge mode, while leaving normal mode for anyone that wants a fun experience?And by balance, I don't mean further nerfing items as that seems to be the case, but to stop overwhelming players with 6-7 enemies, but give us two or three that has lots of health instead?Or nerfing a crit boosting item that needs another two-three items to actually work properly? Sure some players have gotten an attack to deal over thousands of damage, and I've managed it once. But without pierce damage, all of that damage only hits one enemy in a line of five. That's not even mentioning enemies that shields, that can absorb all of that damage.But as it is, like I mentioned before, if any relic even hints to being good deems it as needing a nerf so it's just... average. As much as I want to like the game, I do, but the devs are focusing on the wrong things to make the game 'balanced'.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Peglin boasts a good gameplay loop with a neat base and an active dev that has more coming down the pipeline, pick it up and give it a few runs and see if you are charmed by this game like I was.I have seen a few reviews saying that this game is too short to justify the price, and although I can understand that; I overall think that this game holds long term value because the gameplay loop is enjoyable. Considering this game is still in active development and I can see that the developer is receptive and ready to tackle any issues, the future of this game seems very bright. I must admit, after a few runs you will feel like you have seen most of the game, but I think this is just because of how this game is still being developed. In my opinion, this game is great for ending a tough or long day and want something to play while you watch a show or video and want to keep your mind on instead of turning it completely off for the day. _childDocuments_.review: As of this game's release, my assessment remains unchanged. Without going into detail, you are at the mercy of random chance when playing this. While skill and learning are crucial for success, no amount of skill gets you anywhere close to guaranteeing a victory. Even the best runs are liable to end virtually at random when a couple unfortunate events and combats line up to end you. If you enjoy the randomness and the chance at an unexpected overpowered run, then this game may be for you. I do enjoy those aspects myself sometimes. But, overall, it can be extremely frustrating when a decent run ends specifically because it never had the chance to be incredible.===Prior to the Game's Release:Many runs will fail based purely on unpredictable and uncontrollable factors. Again, at lower difficulties this problem is not a problem, but this is not because the difficulty modifiers introduce it, simply because the lack thereof grants a sizeable buffer to random punishment that makes it manageable. Most of the game's problems are built right into its core. It would benefit greatly from a minor reduction to the difficulty of the modifiers and a serious overhaul of many of its random attributes to be more reliable.I will amend, however, that the game is still in beta so my concerns may be addressed, and, for some, they may just be an aspect of the rogue like experience. My specific complaints may come from a dissonance of how much control I wish to have in a style of game that hinges inherently on random factors. I believe it could be much better, but perhaps that is just me. All in all, the game is probably worth checking out, but at the higher difficulties its randomness can make it exceptionally frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely delightful little game. Currently there are 3 stages with many individual rooms and paths each. A full run takes about an hour, but each one is almost guaranteed to vary wildly based on the orbs and relics you choose to accumulate throughout each run.The core mechanics are simple, but the real charm comes from how behaviors of orbs with the levels change based on the relics you have. One of my favorite combos involves a maxxed out Matryoshka Orb, coin modifying relics and the Molten (something, peabrain memory) Relic that prevents you from gaining gold for the rest of your run, but applies your current accumulated damage to the selected enemy for every few coin pegs you hit. Its fun to watch it spiral out of absolute control.I cannot recommend this game enough. It's a casual game with enough depth to keep runs interesting, but not too much to where you're forced to play with a wiki (does one even exist?) open on a second monitor.

_childDocuments_.review: Peglin has grown a lot since I last reviewed it, and I'm happy to say it is still an absolute delight of a game to vibe out and unwind to; with simple yet satisfying interactions and gameplay loop. Watching the various orbs / balls you can unlock bouncing along the various peg boards is fun in and of itself, but feels even better when you manage to pull off a well aimed shot.The best way I can describe this gem in one sentence is if Slay the Spire and "Plinko" from the TV game show, The Price Is Right, had a glorious baby.My only complaint is that the class unlock conditions are demanding enough that I feel they rely too heavily on luck instead of skill / strategy; and there will be a lot of runs where you just won't be presented with the orbs and deck thinning opportunities needed for the synergy and consistency required to pull it off. That said, I think it'd be nice if they had alternate mercy unlock conditions such as simply playing X amount of runs to the end (), or defeating X amount of Elites, or inflicting X of total damage between all runs.Overall, definitely recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: They brought back peggle, and this time it has a kind of RPG meets roguelite theme. It's very cute and fun but short.Gameplay is basically peggle but each orb has different mechanics for how it interacts with the pegs, and you accumulate new orbs as you play or level up existing orbs to become more powerful. At the same time enemies will constantly be approaching along the top of the screen, you deal damage with each peg hit based on the strength / features of the orb and you take damage if the enemies reach you.It's a clever and simple design that's very easy to pick up and addicting to play. The only downside is that there's so little content. More is slowly getting added but because of how the game is built it's easy to experience everything quickly. A good idea with slightly too little substance at the moment, but a great starting point.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst the game's current early access launch content doesn't quite live up to its price tag, if the final product is destined to include a few more levels and additional items to match, then it will very much be worth it.Honestly, Peglin's basic description basically sums up the game. It's a pixel style peggle-themed fantasy game where you play as a goblin with an inventory of orb weapons. Whilst part of the game involves aiming your ball toward specific pegs, there's also a strategic element in what orbs you choose to pick up and what you don't, as well as rogue-like luck. It's a fun way to pass the time for anyone who just wants to bounce balls around a screen and watch damage numbers go up.I think the only negative I have on the current build is that the way everything ramps up, from the second map onward, aiming actually becomes kind of a moot point, as you start to find the board absolutely filled with pegs to hit, and you'll have (hopefully) plenty of power-ups and upgraded orbs to the extent where you can just let them loose and watch the damage numbers tick higher and higher. Therein, strategy of your inventory becomes the most important thing, and maintaining synergy that won't turn round to bite you in the rear.

_childDocuments_.review: Too many elements of RNG layered on top of each other.Most post-battle rewards are kinda bad. This leads to a couple restarts until you get something good early on. That said, there is so little content in the game that there are only a handful of ball types, so you won't be restarting too often. Saved for the wrong reasons here.Navigating through the map is done in a rather obtuse way. While I'm sure it's a neat concept to actually have to launch the ball left/right through the board, some of these boards are intentionally designed with so many pegs on the board that navigation is basically random, and this can really screw you over and set you on a very bad path. What's the point of intentionally saving up money if the shop is just going to spawn on a side-path that you can't reach? Time to restart the run again because the game didn't let you go to a shop.Development on the game is really slow and content is drip-fed into the game over a way too long time. But when an update does happen you should be fearful, as it almost always ends up nerfing something that's fun or interesting. A good balance is achieved by nerfing OP items and buffing bad ones. But the only thing that happens is the latter, slowly neutering everything to be homogenous and ♥♥♥♥-tier.The game is dictated too much by RNG, most builds are very bad and some are brokenly good (like bombs). Player agency is removed by world path selection being very wonky and making some of those (forced!) paths a very bad deal (such as 6 basic encounters or 3 shops in a row) which screws you for the rest of the run because a ball went the wrong way once. Want a skill-based roguelike "deck"builder? This isn't it. If you want a slot machine then just go play a slot machine.I can't justify spending the money on this, so I'm going to refund it.
