_childDocuments_.review: is a first-person narrative adventure set in the mid '900s, inspired to the Cthulhu mythos' lore. Players impersonate the member of a sailor crew, that got stranded on a mysterious island where unexplained events happen regularly. Between distorted space-time and elusive dark beings, the protagonist will have to make his way through a madness-inducing land.The Shore features a definitely solid art direction level, when it comes down to world representation and environment design. Each location has a distinct color palette, chromaticity and dominant theme that sets it apart from the others. From the calm but eerie island shores to much more disturbing locations, every setting is well crafted and rich in details. Documents and examined items also have good levels of care in their making.The ambient sounds and music tracks dominate the atmosphere of this game, kicking in mostly at the perfect times to emphasize events - as it should be with any good cinematic-oriented production. Voice acting on the other hand is only of passable quality overall, with some ups and downs depending on the situation. The sound compartment's contribution in building the eerie feeling that dominates each location, is surely significant.For a narrative adventure, The Shore has an above-average diversity of gameplay situations. From exploration and rather classic item-based puzzles, to more unusual combat phases and chase sections, the game proposes a good variety, especially in relation to the total short duration. In addition, several achievement-related secondary areas are present, to also shed a bit more light on the lore... or the opposite.The proposed price of 21€ (25 USD) is really out of line considering the short duration of the game, and no replay value (as expected from the genre). While it proves to be a good quality adventure, that doesn't justify a price to content ratio of 7€ / Hour, which is actually pretty grim all things considered. I highly suggest waiting for a significant discount before buying, even to fans of Lovecraftian settings.Even on a reasonably high-end system, The Shore has proven to be quite an heavy task to run, and unoptimized at that too. Especially in open-air areas, slowdowns and framerate drops were not uncommon at all in 1440p. The fact there is no Exclusive Fullscreen and as consequence no in-game Vsync, further accentuate the already present issues. There surely is more work to be done in this field.While most of the puzzles, action sections and exploration segments are fairly well designed, a few of them stand out for being rather subpar. Certain combat situations prove frustrating due to infinite-respawn enemies and unreliability of the "weapon" at players' disposal. A few puzzles prove to be especially obscure in their logic, without even a small hint to guide players - that can definitely become frustrating.Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Puzzles and Action Sequences.Is performed on foot across the island, and later on also in caves and other depths. There is no map, however environmental clues lead the player, such as signposts or strategically placed lights. Location layouts are fairly linear, with but a few secondary areas where one an find collectibles, lore items and the occasional achievement-related goal. There is no point in exploring out of the main path, except for finding such things, that given the game's short duration, give some more longevity to it. Generally players can't die while exploring except a few select locations, and in that case checkpoints are rather abundant.Are generally based on finding the correct item for unlocking a passage or path, especially in the first part of the game. Later on, when more tools are at players' disposal, puzzles may become a bit more elaborate as they involve the operation of unknown machinery and other "arcane" structures. This includes rituals as well in some parts. Apart from a few quite obscure puzzles, they are never too difficult or tedious.Involve escaping from or fighting unimaginable horrors straight out of the Lovecraftian mythos. At some point, an artifact is acquired and used to defeat such monsters. However, in some situations escaping is the best solution. Combat proves to be rather unreliable at times, because the artifact isn't consistent in effectiveness or accuracy. There is even a proper boss fight at a later stage, which is something not often seen in this genre at all.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is complete nonsense and you can tell the game is budget by the animation and scripting quality. _childDocuments_.review: First, I must say that the developer is very amazing in taking action on fixing bugs and making balance adjustments quickly and passionately.  Not only that, but the dev even added (and plans to add) more content.  This is a good game that provides a world thick with Lovecraftian lore.  If you like Lovecraft stories, you should like this game.  I beseech people to support it.The atmosphere and world provide a sense of mystery and is beautiful and tantalizing to explore.The fighting/shooting encounters can feel a bit clunky (at first, because the shift in gameplay suddenly changes which require the player to adjust their playing), but improvements came leaps and bounds by way of the developers updates has helped mitigate that feeling.  Don't let that deter anyone from purchasing this title.  If I can get through those encounters (as someone that will just quit a game due to painstaking encounters) anyone can.  The encounters are not painstaking, they require a sense of finesse of figuring it out.  Getting past encounters will supply the player with more Lovecraft.I love the idea of being able to play more from this developer, Ares Dragonis.Thank you for making this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It physically hurts me to thumb this down, mostly because i've been a lovecraft buff for years. The character design is on point... and that's it. that's the good. The story is choppy and i REALLY wanted to understand it but with very little info given in the beginning except some pictures which you have no reason to link characters to until someone mid game mentions you had a daughter and suddenly you're like "OH, its not about his wife". You feel no emotion for this guy or whatever plight he's in.You're shown that you can jump and sprint and everything but the game just wont let you until late game. There is no exploration so dont even try. I get that you cant kill the monsters because they're lovecraftian beasts, they dont die. The boss fight and i guess purposeful dying just left me frustrated. Topping off the review, i paid 24.99 for a choppy game that even with taking breaks to chat with my viewers and running around in circles because i wasnt given direction, I was able to finish in 3 hours. No Replay Value. Dont buy it, just look at the screen shots and enjoy those.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a masterpiece, but it's not terrible either.I have to agree with another reviewer who called it a "Painful waking sim." _childDocuments_.review: This game takes the opposite approach to Lovecraft which is throw everything at you really fast.  It takes away the mystery.  Plus there are some running sections that can be infuriating.  There were times where I had to run.  I would run the right path and still get attacked from the back and killed.  It's like they tried to combine Lovecraft and badly made Doom.  Lovecraft games have become TERRIBLE because they all use the same elements and story and don't innovate or really create   something new.  Can someone please make cosmic horror games that don't just use Lovecraft to copy and paste a story?
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Quite remarkable indie make with amazing graphics design that some AAA titles would envy. Incredible attention to details, every rock on the shore looks so authentic and realistic. Ocean design is one of the best I've seen (perhaps a perk from the Greek background of the author). Great soundtrack too, although secondary character voice acting and editing is very lacking.Gameplay wise it's very easy, almost relaxing. Yet it wasn't boring as there's a good balance between exploration and findings. Yes, the levels are highly linear (so, not much of exploration really), but this actually works much better in the context of this game. I personally hate huge open exploration indie games where nothing could happen for hours. This one I finished in a couple of hours and it was absolutely worth it. The only downside is perhaps the end of story. I would expect some culmination sequence, even if it was pre-rendered. I think the author simply grew tired and fatigued, or maybe caught a creative slug. But hey, this is indie, it could be wrong so many times but it wasn't! Really great addition to my Lovecraftian collection. Well done, mate!

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointed by this experience. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Full review: TL;DR:Despite there being some cool moments and designs in The Shore that I really liked, I cannot recommend it to even the most enthusiastic H.P. Lovecraft fan. In many ways, The Shore is like a haunted house ride that is going through all of Lovecraft’s ‘greatest hits’ as you wander the area. Unfortunately, its also like a ride that falls off the tracks and dumps you into a hall of mirrors, forcing you to wander for hours as you bump into walls you didn’t realize were there. There are some really cool things about The Shore that it does right to make you feel like you’re in a Lovecraft story, but they are quickly overshadowed by the miserable experience of playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really impressive game. I admit that I didn't finish it but I was very impressed. The immersion into a strange unnatural world of Lovecraftian horror was amazing. The VR system allowed for some truly mind bending moments where you look at the horizon and see something... indescribable for a moment.It was really well done.If I like it so much why didn't I finish it? Well, the game does make a few missteps.Lovecraft based games always take a turn for the worse when they give you a weapon. Killing a few mooks is OK but when you start to run into bigger boys later in the game and can hurt them, much less kill them, is where the illusion starts to break down.Real Lovecraftian horror should have humans being depicted as insects, unworthy of attention. We shouldn't be able to get Dagon or Cthulhu's attention at all, much less speak to them. I think the game would have been improved with more of a focus on stealth and avoidance mechanics rather than brute force.All that being the case, the game really was impressive and I look forward to future offerings from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

I would compare the gameplay to a SFW Lust for Darkness; Cosmic Horror walking sim with a couple of chase scenes and some "puzzles" that are really just pushing buttons. I actually liked this one more if I were to compare the two games and definitely felt more creeped out and on edge in THE SHORE. The only thing that really annoyed me about the game was having to shimmy around the endless invisible walls in the first act.Overall I give itCthulhu's massive dump truck out of 10

Even with limited graphical capability, The shore looks really good actually. there were a couple moments that really made me feel that shock, horror, and awe that is always associated with H.P lovecraft horror.gameplay is not very fun though. puzzles are very simple.Really if you love story and lore in a lovecraftian setting, then you should 100% get this game. if you are looking for re-playability, You should look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Just as a HP Lovecraft story is supposed to be, dark and full of illusions.As a crowdfunder of this game I hoped this game would really bring forward, what reading an HP Lovecraft Story brings forward as well. And I think it does. Its dark, its confusing (in a good way) and it has its sharp edges. I think the fact that this game isnt polished to the max and everything doesnt feel super optimized like in an Triple A title makes this game better! Because just like the storys, this game itself is a little out of the ordinary...and so far, I like it excactly for that!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my! That was a great experience. The Shore is a rather short game (not necessarily a bad thing), took me about 5 hours or so to complete and to be honest in the end I wanted some more of it. Considering though that it's an indie game from a small developer with very few people working on it, those 5-6 hours of gameplay make it seem like Triple A for the effort.The visuals and the sound design are simply top notch and they are the main strengths of the game. The art direction on that regard, along with the color palettes used, make it a very atmospheric experience. Being a loveletter to H.P. Lovecraft and his Cthulhu Mythos will help scratch that itch for eldritch horror if you are a fan of the genre like me and the whole artistic direction really helps with that. The best part of the game is, of course, the "creatures" (to put it mildly). The graphics for all the abominations, protoplasmic forms, powers and so on are simply amazing, grandiose and highly detailed, really bringing the whole thing to life. The great ambient soundtrack and sound design really help to make it even better and more atmospheric. The game clearly oozes passion from the developers in that regard and the whole project seems to be made out of love and not as a "job".The exploration is ok, with much attention to detail. You need to take your time and look. I would prefer a more open world approach than hitting invisible walls that force you to go places, but the rather linear path is well made as it is. I managed to get stuck a couple of times on the textures while trying to explore the edges, but that's just me, nothing game braking.Story-wise was ok as well, it was rather simple, but the good voice acting and the visuals mentioned earlier pretty much make up for it.The gameplay is on the walking-simulator side, you can use and react to certain stuff, and there is some basic "combat" later on in the game. Some say in other reviews that it is clunky. Well... that's because this game is not an FPS or even a pure walking simulator in that regard, and shouldn't be treated as either. It is what it is, don't go expecting snappy COD style combat, it's a basic mechanic that it is part of it's story, so you are not getting into this game for that.All in all, I really enjoyed my time with it and I think it's a must play for all the Cthulhu Mythos fans, so go check it out!To the Developers: Greetings from Greece and keep up the good work guys! Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I MOSTLY like this game. Its pretty alright for a mostly walking sim with some running and puzzling. I had some weird problem with my mouse not responding, which got me killed a couple times. Also I felt really weird about the  . It just seemed weird and wrong with lovecraftian lore but idk. If you want a short, pretty simple game with some weird obtuse puzzles and enemies that chase you (though you do get a 'weapon' of sorts that can slow some enemies and kill others) then this is certainly a way to kill a couple hours. I did like the little parts where you would stumble onto something and see something you werent supposed to see, those were cool. Overall....mid, but worth if you like Cthulhu stuff and are down with slow burn games

_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: THE SHORE is an immersive walking simulator with puzzles and combat taking place in a mysterious island in what can be assumed to be the 1900s, where you play as a shipwrecked sailor looking for his daughter. Behind a cliched narrative hook lies a beautiful game with tons of enviromental detail and charming sights and setpieces, where you'll be taken on a wild ride through several of Lovecraft's mythical creatures and their schemes to forestall humanity. If you can overcome a couple of pesky puzzles, it's a well worthy experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Extremely good visualsDecent voice actingCons:"Combat"Poor puzzle designEasily missed pieces needed to progressInconsistent gameplay elementsErratic storytellingInvisible walls EVERYWHEREUnclear pathingThis was a game I wanted to like more than I did, but it just turned out to be a walking simulator with some light puzzle elements. More than anything, this was just a tour of the Cthulhu mythos. Dagon, Shoggoths, Deep Ones, Elder Things, even  make an appearance. However, none of them really make much of an appearance, or much of an impact on the story. They're all more just there as fan service, shunted in for completeness' sake than any real necessity. For example, Call of Cthulhu: Dark Corners of the Earth was ABOUT Dagon and the Deep Ones. It didn't need much more than that. Sure it had Mi'Go and Yith, but they were instrumental to the story. It didn't need to include EVERYTHING in the mythos, which is often the problem that indie devs run in to. They feel the need to shove in ALL of the things, and it leads to something that's unfocused and disjointed, such as with this game. Heck there's one point in this game where you [spoilers] wake up Dagon for no other reason than because Nyarlothotep told you to, and he rides off on a giant walking obelisk. One hell of a visual, but nothing more than that. [/spoilers]That being said, what little appearance the rest of the mythos makes is pretty impactful. The models are beautiful, and the animations are pretty solid. The gameplay itself is straightforward and shallow. It's more of an adventure game than anything else. Collect the things, solve the puzzles, move on to the next area. What little combat there is kinda sucks. There's no real feedback other than the odd stunning animation that happens every once in a while. You don't really know if you're actually damaging the creature or just stunning it so you can run away, which is frustrating at times. Thankfully, the game is short and doesn't make you endure much of what passes for combat. In my opinion, it would have been much better without it. The thing that really irritated me the most was the silly invisible walls everywhere. They were everywhere, and they were just so stupid. Nothing breaks immersion like running up against an invisible wall simply because the developer didn't want you to go that direction. Especially when it's something stupid or time saving, like jumping over a rock or a crevice, or off the side of a ramp. All in all, it's really not worth it. Buy it if you enjoy walking simulators with a side of scary monsters, but don't expect to be frightened by anything other than the odd jump scare.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I really wish I could say that The Shore was a good game. Lovecraft always works for me. And the graphics, I mean, look at them! They are gorgeous! The maker of this game has a GREAT talent for graphics. The game sparks and shines with atmosphere, perfectly catching the Lovecraft theme. Thumbs up for that! But - as you may have expected - here comes the big fat "but". The game around the awesome setting and graphics is bad. Really bad. It would have worked PERFECTLY as a walking simulator. Nothing wrong with walking simulators - there are many great examples out there! Take the fantastic setting, add some smart puzzles maybe, have the developer shine where he shines and focus on that. It's so sad that the decision was made to add combat to The Shore. And this for me ruins most of the game's magic. It's so poorly implemented, so annoying. So much trial and error. Big monster pops up, bam bam bam yer dead, way too long loading screen, try over until you figure out what the hell the game wants from you. Zero fun. Also, I hate invisible walls. Sometimes when I walk along the shore, not exactly knowing where to go next, I constantly kept bumping into invisible walls. Not fun either. And part three: lame teleports from scene to scene. You don't fluently move through the game, but you solve a situation, and then you get teleported to the next. I am sure there would have been smarter solutons for this.Real sorry to say, but in my opinion this was a missed chance. Die-hard-Cthulhu fans may still give it a try when on sale. It's a great design showcase, but sadly not a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the overall atmosphere with this game at first. The story-telling was ok and I liked the overall graphics. Mid to late in this short game it got repetitive with the uninspired combat and the same way to defeat most foes. Puzzles were  overly simplistic.This could have been some much more. unfortunately I bought into the hype and the initial awesome intro video made me think of game that was a cross between Myst and Dead Space and all I got was a dead game.Wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the game.  It was beautiful, and the soundtrack was super awesome!  I thoroughly enjoyed the  concepts, atmosphere and story.  Hats off, my friends!!  I did experience a bit of frustration and had to walk away for a time, at least twice. All in all, would love to see more that you, as developers can do. _childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the positives. This game boasts absolutely stunning visuals and design. The voice acting of the main character is top-notch, and the music adds an epic touch. I believe it's a must-have game for Lovecraft fans.However, there are a few drawbacks. Despite the impressive visuals, there are some questionable design decisions. Additionally, the abrupt shifts in music tone from calm to dark can feel jarring. The story itself feels somewhat rushed, with multiple elements packed into a short gameplay without sufficient explanation or attention, leaving it somewhat underwhelming. I know Lovecraftian cosmic horror thrives on ambiguity, but a stronger narrative thread would have improved my feeling. It's still a good story, but it falls short of reaching its full potential.Considering these aspects, I personally don't believe the game justifies its 10 euro price tag. I do wish the developers had expanded it into a longer game with 5-8 hours of gameplay, as it currently feels more like a tech demo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Plays more like a walking simulator which is fine but the direction of the game is confusing and at times easy to miss but my main gripe is the combat, which became very frustrating especially combined with the lack of direction. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who collects all lovecraftian horror things (books, movies, necklaces artwork, ect) i was skeptical at first. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly a walking simulator where you're kind of locked into literal walking until the 2 hour mark where sprinting is randomly unlocked. There is "running" before, but it's barely faster than walking and is more akin to a powerwalkYou start off confined to a very small area, but you're going back and forth trying to figure out what to do and it seems like there's more going on due to how long it takes you to walk back and forthThe atmosphere is hit or miss. Lovecraft stuff is cool, but sometimes it's just not landing well. Some parts are really well made visually, but then they give you absolutely no time to look around and take it in. This game seems like they wanted to have puzzles, but all you're really doing is picking up objects and then using them in specific locations and you don't even get to guess which items are used where. You just automatically use the thing you need so there's no real "puzzle" there. The closest I saw to an actual puzzle was rotating some blocks so the mural lined up and I wouldn't really call that a puzzle even by the most lenient of standards.There is "combat", but it's horrible. You can punch if grabbed(strangely not unlocked when first encountering enemies), but it's quickly swapped out for a kind of laserbeam that has a range of like 5 feet and it's very underwhelming. There's no real depth to the combat and it boils down to "hold attack button down until enemy dies" and it even stunlocks them so there's no real danger. At that point, you might as well just take the combat mechanic awayI put in about 2.5 hours in and I was taking my time and trying to absorb the scenery, but I get the feeling I'm more than half-way through alreadyAs others said, there are definite graphical issues. Numerous small floating rocks and even some missing textures here and there. Nothing too bad, but it is noticeable. I'm not a huge graphics guy who will nitpick tiny little things, but if you're gonna go all out and try to make it realistic looking, I feel you can't really skimp outThe script and writing are pretty bad. You'll find notes that are written like "he's.....he's gone" when nobody ever writes like that unless they are quoting someone who verbally spoke those lines, but that will literally be written on paper. Nobody writes like that. The MC will literally say things like "there's no way that was my daughter" when talking to himself, which seems odd as nobody would talk like that to themselves, even in inner monologue. There are also spelling and grammatical errors here and there, but not too much to the point I'd say it's a major problem, but still noteworthy. The voice actor is also not greatA noteworthy problem is the initial beach design. There are an assload of invisible walls and barriers preventing you from accessing certain areas, but logically, there's nothing really stopping you. There are rocks all over the beach, but most of them are rocks you'd casually step on and climb around on with ease. I'm not even talking like you'd even need your hands to get up them. I'm talking rocks you'd barely have to fully raise your leg to get on top of....and the game puts invisible walls all around them so you're stuck on winding paths. If you're going to try to make people stay on paths, make the rocks taller and not something you'd easily be able to climb on
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Esther, but with Cthulhu elements and awful chase sequences. Looks great and has a great creepy soundscape, but is ultimately a walking sim with a story that only lightly makes sense and the chase sequences and "combat" almost made me quit. I'm not against walking simulators in general, only ones that are so high on their own writing, they don't think it needs anything more compelling to back it up. This game seems to attempt to try to overcome that by bolting on failure state sequences that do nothing more than slow down the pacing and cause frustration.For the first third, I was really enjoying the creepy vibes and wanting to see where things would go. By the time the last third started, I just wanted it to be over. Great potential here and I think this dev is one to watch, but I don't care for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Too dang short in length! The sign of of a really good game. CONS: There were times that I just did not know what to do next. Still very cool but compared to what came before it...PROS: Maybe not state-of-the-art graphics but still very good. Animations wee well done.Probably the very best representations of the creatures and Gods of the Cthulhu Mythos ever portrayed in a game. Better than any movie! BRAVO on that Devs!For the price this is a must-have for H.P. Lovecraft fans!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a long time to complete this game over a series of play sessions picking it up and putting it down again. Ultimately, I do recommend it on sale; however, this is with some caveats which I'm sure I share with many of the other reviewers here. My feelings towards this game are complicated. On the one hand, the art, visuals--all of that--is quite well done. The general atmosphere is all there. The scale of things is great. Forgiving a few clunky elements, it is a good looking work of art. Beyond that the story is fine, and the first half of it I would actually say is pretty great. At around the halfway point in the game the gameplay and the tone take a major shift. There are some puzzles throughout that might feel a bit arbitrary or difficult due to some element of level design (hard to read surfaces, etc). There's probably something worth saying about how separated some of these "incomprehensible and otherworldly" eldritch entities should be from the player who is just a human person, but it is what it is. At the end of the day, I think the average player will find this less scary (fine by me, a coward), but might find some elements frustrating until they get the hang of it. Even so, if you find this on a really good discount, want to do some achievement hunting, and like games which operate mostly at your own pace without holding your hand, then this game could be of benefit to you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: On the positive side it was made with love, and the first half hour really gives a lovecraftian vibe. The moment when I turned back from a strange humming obelisk and seen tentacles drawing back to the mountainside, or looking into a telescope and cache a glimpse of a deep one was really exciting, and the background noises made me feel unease. The huge old ones are really huge and impose awe.On the negative side, it is around 3 hours long and wants to put every sea-themed lovecratian motif into the same short game, creating an experience like you've bought a ticket to Lovecraft Theme Park. The story is a mess. You can lose direction because every rock looks the same. You get stucked then try the exact same thing and it works because you've completed a scripted prerequisite. This is especially annoying if you do a second run because you've missed something. After the first promising half an hour the game looks linear and strongly relies on shooting abominations with a pyramid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is an intresting game, with alot of potential. you could call it a Lovecraftian explaination of the Flannan Isles mystery, witch i loved. But sadly the story got driven away.i absolutely loved the introduction, it was driving me to play the game. The letters wasnt boring, and the disorded notes made the player slowly assambel the story of the 3 missing fishermen, witch was intriguing and eerie. the island that was isolated from reality and civilitation was a nice mix up with the tales of lovecraft. my only critisism story wise is it felt very quick before the player got thrown into another mindset. some slower progression of the question your sanity part would be nice. but even though i really wanna like the game for its story only, there is some inevitable cons about this game that ruined the amazing story. the atmosphere was raw and colorless witch i liked, but i didnt have a good sense of scale. maybe a thicker fog, and refrencing would help on that aspect. Even though the design was raw (witch was well suited), it still felt unfinished. and the shadows just wasnt there, and the map was very limited. i was'nt driven many places in the story, because i just walked the presented way. i would love to explore the island of its mysteries, and forgotten stories. every path was blocked or dead ends, also the game didnt comunicate very well witch way that was the "right" way either. another important factor for the atmosphere is sound. the dialog was intresting.. the sound acting, not so mutch.i didnt have mutch of isue with the soundtrack, but neither do i feel an appreciation for it.the puzzels also felt bland, repetitive and was there just for the sake of it. to sum it up, it was just walking from a to b, with out making you think out of the box. witch is okay to a limit, but it felt more like an obstacle for the game than a feature.what is there else to say... i was stuck in the trap door besides the lighthouse and needed to restart. the fonds are nice but can be hard to read if you look at the corners of the scribbled notes, it could use a normal fond aswell on an overlay. you also could make interactive items pop out from decorations conclussion: so in conclussion i cannot recomend this game yet, and i really hope you take some of this feedback  to improve. im writing this because it has a lot potential good gameplay. and i love the core idea. its sad that these cons are ruining this fantastic story to be told, with alot of detail. like the sailors/fishermen that got insane by the color out of space,and all the other small hints that combine the universes, i see alot of research and passion from the develpors. So i would  love to come back and play this game in a year. but its not ready for realise, especially with the given price. i hope to see updates and improvements. overall: 5.4/10sound design: 3/10puzzle designs: 4/10grapichs: 6/10story: 8.5/10horror level: mehshocking plottwist at the end the sums up our questions about the main story nicly: Hell ya.my current valuation of game: 5 dollars - its playable for now
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I am such a sucker for all things related to lovecraft's stories, but there is so much disappointment in so many of those purchases. Seeing that author's name has become synonymous with half-hearted efforts and half-baked ideas. Maybe there is something about creators not having complete autonomy in the creative process of the story. For whatever reason, the shore has a rough story, no intuitive signposting for player movement, annoyingly vague puzzles (such as putting a figurine in a chess board, doors unlocked by seemingly random keys, and bad monster chase scenes), and a lack of interesting level design. I also had technical problems with the video cutscenes not displaying correctly. (The videos show okay when run from the local file directory.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Game doesn't know what it wants to be. Is it a walking siumulator with a story? Kind of, but I didn't find the story engaging. Is it a puzzle game? Sort of, but the puzzles are either too easy or too opaque. Is it an action game? It is, if you count weak & janky gameplay mechanics & design "challenging."Nice aesthetics & that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Well this was a surprise in many ways. The premise is quite simple. A man wakes up on a beach looking for his lost daughter. After a small stroll along the shoreline utterly weird stuff starts to happen.. This is a very serene and strange game at its start only to drastically ramp up half way through into a tale of cosmic horrors and macabre discoveries knee deep in madness.. If you are a fan of cosmic horror and a weird walking simulator hybrid with a peculiar emerging narrative this is quite a hidden gem. However I will be a bit critical and say that the first half of the game is a brilliant piece of suspenseful mystery and serene atmosphere. As the story progresses it becomes a bit on the nose in the Lovecraftian fanfiction. The ending was a bit anticlimactic but in the end I had a good time with the game. And it offers a lot of eldritch sightseeing! It is not a Call of the Sea, but honestly it is a fine game standing on its own merits, had it been another setting than the Cthulhu Mythos it might have felt even better! I encountered a few bugs but nothing game breaking. Get it at a discount and immerse yourself in a strange journey.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game really messed with my head which was something I didn't realise until quite a while after finishing it. It was weird, unsettling, left me riddled with anxiety and filled with existential dread... and I f***ing loved it. It's a very pretty game with an intriguing story line and the atmosphere and sounds are brilliant and perfectly executed. To really get the most out of this game I recommend playing with a good headset and allowing yourself to become fully immersed in the atmosphere with no distractions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: this game feels like a love letter to the works of Howard Phillips Lovecraft. playing the game as a big lover of his work i felt as if the devs understood the mythos better than any AAA devs have.  its a slow burn for the intro with LOTS of references to Lovecraft's work. it feels like being on a time capsule inhabited by only the beings, gods and abominations within the mind of the man himself. its a must play for true Lovecraft fans and a must play for those looking for a game rich with passioni got this for just over $3 but would of easily pay full price

When I started it up next my saves were gone and I had to restart.  I did that, and the game is in total an hour long.  Don't waste your money, just watch a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A must for Lovecraft fans. Prepare to play bingo! It was so much fun picking all the Lovecraft bits and pieces out of the game as you go through it. Watch out for some great little easter eggs. Don't pay too much attention to the reviews saying the fighting is bad - this is a Lovecraftian tale, if you're trying to fight things, you're doing it wrong. It's a light puzzle game full of mythos, gorgeous views and fantastic sound design and some great voice acting. Go have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The game's strongest points are it's amazing visuals and great musical score, and these things alone are the biggest reasons why I enjoyed the game. One impressive thing about this game is that it was made mostly by two people, and while it is very good considering this fact, it does mean the game is unpolished right now and it will take some time and feedback before the major issues can be fixed. The biggest strikes against the game right now are repetitive chase sequences and confusing gameplay, like how it isn't clear what you are supposed to do for a lot of puzzles and it takes a while to get through some of them. Right now, I feel that the game's price is a bit high considering how unpolished the gameplay is, as well as how short the game is. Fortunately, the devs are actively gathering feedback on the game and are working hard to release hotfixes and improve the quality of the gameplay. Even though there are problems with the game right now, I'm sure that given time the devs will significantly improve the game. If you are a fan of Lovecraftian games, you should definitely buy this product. Despite it's flaws right now, it is still a great game, though you may want to wait a bit before playing to give the devs some time to smooth things out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an big fan of the Lovecraft universe and mostly seek out games that is bringing homage to the lore.I'm also an big fan of these type of first person photo realistic horror story telling games and just immerse myself fully when playing them.In an age where AAA titles are 80% trash and overpriced incomplete garbage indie games/developers makes up for it.We need to support indie developers more and let AAA companies rot in hell with their unfinished and bug filled games.Enjoyed everything The Shore had to offer and leaves me wanting more.Game is visually stunning and beautiful and the story is gripping... is he awake?The animations of the larger set pieces was done perfectly and I could not keep myself from staring at what is happening right in front of my eyes.Cannot wait to see what this developer comes up with next!10/10Recommend to any Lovecraft fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains spoilers, read at your own discretion. It saddens me to downvote this game, but i have to.  The main reason being - this is not a lovecraftian game, this is a short fan-fiction where the dev goes like "i want to see lots of the Great Old Ones and interact with them, NAO!" The guy is clearly passionate about the Lovecraft's entities and beings, but he totally misses the whole point of the H.P.L. works: the slowly unfolding fear of unknown and unimaginable, the creeping madness that invades your mind after the realisation of humanity's insignificance. This kind of fear requires a proper build-up, a story being told.  Remember the best lovecraftian game up to this day "The dark corners of the earth" - it starts out slowly. You arrive in town, you start your investigation, you see suspicious folks and strange shadows, the eeriness creeps in slowly only to explode later on in the iconic chase scene. This is perfect! You want another example of things done right? Here is your direct competitor "No one lives under the lighthouse". Same setup - small island with a lighthouse, same game length - between 1-2 hours. The 90's graphic of this game will make many people's eyes bleed and still it manages to do the thing that The Shore fails. It nails the lovecraftian essence and the fear of unknown, while keeping the slow build-up and escalation progress. (also you can take revenge and explode the freaking seagull into a bloody mess there, unlike here, where even the ancient artifact of an untold power cant even make the fu****g bird to flap it's wings) While the developer of The Shore utterly fails in the scenario-writing department, he did some other things exceedingly well and i have to give the credit where it's due. The Elder Monolith - Excellent. Nyarlathotep interactions - Excellent. Azathot devouring chase - Superb. Dagon scene - Veery good. The great C'thulu summoning scene and ship throw - Amazing! The whole otherwordly plane - Excellent. The grand ending scene - Beyond Fantastic. As you can see i rate some parts of the game very-very high. But despite that i still can't recommend this game as a Lovecraft fan. I have to repeat - this is not a proper story, but a fanfic made only as an excuse to make and animate the Great Old Ones and Elder Gods. If only the developer had a competent writer on hand, if only he bothered enough to create a longer story with a proper build-up, culminating in the epic revelation... ahh how cool would that be. I honestly think that the bigger developers can outright learn from The Shore how to make encounters with the lovecraftian pantheon exciting. But this is all this game is - a series of cool scenes involving H.P.L. entities. I would like to strongly suggest to the developer to find a skilled scenarist/author and make a new game from the scratch. But this time - longer, with a proper setting and slow build up. Don't mimick an excited kid emptying the whole box of his toys in one second only to brag to the guests. You nailed the pantheon, now it's time to make a proper story.  And work on the optimisation by the way. This game is not so graphically demanding as to have sudden fps drops on a PC that run Cyberpunk2077 at steady 50fps. And fix you music, because the "broken mic" effect doesnt add to the atmoshpere - it simply annoys.PS: and one more thing - invisible walls on literally flat surfaces are not cool, bro. The age of facing an impenetrable air is long gone in a videogames. At least make a visual obstacle of some kind or other excuse if you want your players to follow your rails. Being stopped by the thin air really sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Screw all the negative reviews. Atmospherically this is the BEST Lovecraft game I have EVER played! Several very H.R. Giger-esque areas as well. People who dislike it misunderstood what this was supposed to be.Game Play:So yes, it is a walking sim with minor chase/combat sequences. That said people ragging on the combat fail to realize it isn't supposed to be great. Lovecraftian cosmic horror isn't supposed to be Halo, in all of his literature it's supposed to feel horrific and hopeless going against the strange and horrific beings from beyond. So it not being fair for you to fend for yourself in some areas & having to get out by the skin of your teeth is built into the formula of some sections. You get a tool later on that helps you "defend" against them while you escape, but it is hardly meant as an offensive weapon, more a path clearing / slow down tool while you gtfo of there. If you were trying to play for combat you played the game wrong.Atmosphere & Visuals: For one dev this is beyond uncanny. There were 1-2 spots where textures left a bit to be desired (boats on the shore in some areas).... but that hardly mattered with how many things were done right, from the occult talismans & coins specially crafted in true Lovecraft fashion to all the strange monoliths & altars.... later on like introducing Giger elements as you are in more cosmic areas. It is WONDERFUL. 10000/10Sound:The atmosphere & soundtrack fit amazingly & when facing the creatures the "squelch & wriggle" sounds had the perfect amount of disgusting and tense. Loved this games sound. The voiceover work was good. I'm not a sound engineer but I'd prefer some effects that were more in line with "Dear Esther" to have the voice sound more "in-game" but it wasnt far off & was an easy adjustment to get used to.Story:Many people here are pissed about the ???? ending for the dude looking for his daughter. Sorry bro, but that wasn't the story, that was a plot device to allow you to explore & gather the real story through the things left around the world unfold the lore & whats going on through the narrator. If you didnt explore & rushed through the game then it's no wonder you didnt enjoy yourself. Why are you playing atmospheric walking sims anyway? That is how they all work.Tone: Is it scary? .... no. Eerie, gross, awesome, yes. This game was never going for "scary" it's going for the melancholic feeling of curiosity, being lost, & impending hopelessness, and on that it nails it. The tone of trying to piece together what is going on while learning about the area youre in and what has happened there lead you to feel an ever growing sense of dread & futility. This game perfectly accomplished what it set out to do, other people just missed the message because they were too focused on looking for their preconceived expectations vs experiencing the game. I'm now going to follow this dev & buy anything Lovecraftian they put out. To the DEV: PLEASE KEEP GOING. THIS WAS AMAZING!!!! THANK YOU FOR A GAME TRUE LOVECRAFT FANS NEEDED!!!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 3/27/21:  I want to revisit my review and acknowledge that the developer has made a significant effort to improve and correct issues with the game.  First of all, they provided a save game file (and instructions to recover your existing save) that allowed me to restore my progress from the update on 2/22/21 that had deleted my game (though it wasn't actually deleted, just moved to a different location).  I give them due credit for that, though they could have avoided the problem entirely by not changing the save location or having the game copy your save automatically.  And, after a few additional patches, I was finally able to progress further beyond the sequence that was crashing out my game and make more progress.With the additional work being done on the game, and the future goals of adding VR and such to the title, I have to change my review to a positive one and recognize that the developer is very active in improving the experience and the overall game is much better for it.  It still isn't perfect but it is clear it's a labor of love and I think they deserve credit for that (since some games never fix the issues).Original review follows:I backed this game on Ulule (a crowdfunding platform) because I enjoyed the demo and thought it had promise.  I regretfully have to conclude that I can't recommend this game in its current state.I want to take a minute and praise the game from a voice-acting, music, and visual standpoint.  It's clear the game was lovingly crafted from that aspect.  While I can't speak for how the game appears after a certain point or even the story (more on that later), the island and the early game sequences are pretty gorgeous looking for an indie title, and the music fits the mood perfectly.  The voice acting is also well done, though sometimes the on-screen subtitles don't exactly match the voice script.  Minor gripe there, but a little sloppy.Where the game fails is from a technical standpoint.  It runs awfully,  FPS drops are a common theme, and I reached a sequence (the "protoplasmic abomination") after about 50ish minutes of play where I simply could no longer progress because the framerate dropped to nothing and the sound became stuttered and glitched, the screen jumped around and my character could barely move causing me to be killed by AI and unable to get to the next area.  Today (2/22/21) the dev team announced a patch that supposedly fixed the FPS issues, so when I logged in to try it out and hope I could finally progress, I was extremely frustrated to discover that the patch had erased my save game completely.  I wasn't about to re-do the entire first section of the game just to get back where I was, so barring a solution from the dev team I'm done with this title.Additionally, the menus are lacking basic setting options that any modern PC game should have for graphics (for example, only offering "borderless" and "windowed" but not standard fullscreen, and displaying resoultions in terms of "1080p" or "720p" instead of the actual WxH screen resolution.  Again, minor nitpick but it comes across as super-budget. So yeah, while I hate leaving a bad review for a game... I have to in this case.  I was extremely hyped for the Lovecraftian design of this game and what I thought it was going to offer me based on the demo I played, and the final product here is a total mess of frustration that I wouldn't wish on anyone.  If the dev team fixes the problems (and makes it possible for me to resume where I left off originally) I will be more than happy to revisit this review and update my recommendation.  But right now, steer clear, especially at this price.It's a $10 game at a $25 price point that runs like $1 shovelware.

_childDocuments_.review: I had to think alot if I whould recommend this game and here is why:Its a an interesting game, mostly made by 2 (?) people I think. For that its actually not bad. _childDocuments_.review: 🎨 I thoroughly enjoyed this game, but there are basically two parts to this game: The gentle and eerie psychological horror with mystery elements where you walk along the coast near a lighthouse picking items and clues while coming across ominous and foreboding ritualistic objects and constructs, and the second which thrusts you away from the investigative walk on the shoreline and deep into a cosmic horror realm where you face otherworldly horrors and jump from one area to another within a matter of moments. With the focus surrounding the eldritch beings, the designers should have went by the "Less is More" option, leaving things to the imagination to fill in. The Lovecraftian horrors are designed concept-wise, but feel detached from the rest of the game's more realistic qualities. They seem too fake or cold when seen with the surroundings, lacking texture and some feeling like plastic or smooth digital models. More texture and detail would have made these eldritch horrors feel more realistic, while also using caution to not reveal too much as that would take away their mysteriousness and ethereal nature.All in all, this was a very well done game, enjoyable and definitely has many nods and homages to lovecraft's works. Even though they have no direct influence on the plot or puzzles, it definitely made you feel this island, this Shore, definitely was cut off and remote from the rest of the world, allowing these locations to be unknown only to certain few and allow such a cult or such worshiping to take place.🔈 Atmospheric.⚙️  Walking and experiencing with simplistic controls. No fighting.📝 A Lovecraftian-inspired game that starts off beautiful and amazing, and then just goes head-long into the campy and extreme in-you-face creatures of the cosmos, taking away all mystery of them as though they were merely seals you encountered on the shoreline.❕ : This is my opinion and thoughts, not an overall view of the game for general audiences, as opinions and experiences vary. As with all reviews, take this as one of many viewpoints, and do your own research. _childDocuments_.review: Short and beautiful.It's a good step above being a walking simulator, there are puzzles and interactions with the game world, but otherwise a fairly simple game. Sometimes it can be annoyingly obtuse with what it expects you to do. Unfortunately it's a bit trial and error-heavy; chase scenes where you need to learn the map and puzzles that have no real clues.Environments are great looking as a whole, though the level design can be a bit wonky. Your most common obstacle are waist-high rocks you should be able to climb over and there's at least one early moment where you have to traverse something you won't think you're able to.It's a little fanservice-y for a fan of the Cthulhu Mythos, but at the same time there are some strange things even I can't recognize. You do something early on that's just haunting and unpleasant to look at while you continue to exploring the island. You do get to see some all-stars of the Mythos but the game doesn't treat them as bosses to beat, you're an ant they're prodding and poking for goals you don't understand.Get it if you're a Lovecraft fan, it's worth a play through.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a mixed bag to me. It's a walking sim throughout a Lovecraftian showcase set on an island which exists seemingly outside of time. It is interesting at first but does not feature much in the way of plot, quests or other characters to interact with. The game is quickly revealed to be marred by bad, poor and uninspired design at all times. The movement, "combat", puzzles and VO are all subpar, sometimes infuriatingly so. Even taking a "less is more" interpretation with regards to the island itself, doesn't do it any favors as there just isn't all that much to it at all.I don't really know who to recommend this to... I don't even think I can recommend the source material after playing this game. The collected works are far more detailed, intricate and focused than anything this game tries to do. The game just seems to lump in a bunch of stuff in the hopes that there's some semblance of a worthwhile experience. And in my opinion, there isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is made for fans of Cthulhu lore. That means that this isn't a run-n-gun FPS (although oddly, there is some first-person "shooting" in the game). It isn't survival horror (yet, there are quite a few cat-and-mouse chase scenes). And it isn't strictly a walking simulator (and then, you'll do a fair share of walking in the game). It's a combination of all three of those set to an interesting tale of a man who lost his little girl and his dark path to find her.It's a surreal journey which is equal parts horrifying as it is beautiful. The game is gorgeously detailed and dripping in atmosphere. The narration and voice acting overall is above par as well. And the musical score and sound effects are great.There are a few puzzles in the game, which aren't too hard. Only one gave me a headache and it turned out to be a trial and error combination that I just hadn't completed yet (it's the prism room; PM me if you need a hint). But largely fairly simple.There's a few areas of the game where its a little tricky to navigate the shore's craggy rocks. And the destructive ray you "shoot" from your artifact has like a half second delay which I found a little annoying, especially when its needed in the chase scenes.Other than that, this game is an excellent find. I beat it in just under 4 hours and 100%'ed the game from an achievement angle in about 5 hours. For an interactive Cthulhu mythos story, it's a nice little pick up.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're in the mood for a short but well made lovecraftian horror game I'd definitely give this a recommendation. There are certain parts of the Shore that are a little rough around the edges since the puzzles aren't all that challenging and there are a few occasions where the game goes a bit too fast but these were easy to overlook by the end of the game. Would definitely recommend to a lovecraft or horror fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Autumn is a season of upheaval, so the Old Gods grow ever restless. They will not fade into obscurity just like the controversial author of our current source material has found his own little patch of fame and infamy. I’m talking about Howard Phillips Lovecraft and it’s almost ironic how he died penniless and with a firm conviction that he amounted to a complete failure, only to emerge post-mortem as one of the most influential fiction writers of the 20th Century. Just like our buddy Franz Kafka from my previous review, Lovecraft would also inadvertently create his own literary and stylistic subgenre which has been “bleeding” quite profusely into gaming as well. The Shore marks Ares Dragonis’ Steam debut, case in point that you don’t need to have previous titles under your belt in order to leave a positive impression. Originality still shines within an abyss of reboots, remakes and remasters!Not going to dwell a lot on the narrative since its initial ambiguity holds few secrets: main character is a fisherman called Andrew and he’s searching for his missing daughter along the shorelines of what appears to be volcanic island, judging by the pitch black terrain. A deserted lighthouse and numerous shipwrecks confirm that the place is deserted, yet you’re not alone. Like a slow descent into madness, things and thoughts change their shapes the more you push on seeking answers and closure. What starts as a seemingly benign walking simulator, eventually shifts towards survival horror with a few puzzle sections thrown in for good measure. The pacing is on point, you feel compelled to explore since The Shore does an excellent job at offering the needed incentives in the form of Lovecraft references and collectibles scattered off the beaten paths. Linearity is less of an issue if you provided the necessary illusions of alternative choices. It helps that the developer made full use of the source material mythos. From Outer Gods, to Deep Ones and of course infamous Great Old Ones such as Cthulhu himself. Once you start questioning the perceived reality, you know you’ve gone too far to turn back. All roads will lead towards a rather ambiguous conclusion that leaves plenty of room for a sequel or interpretation at the very least. The Shore is powered by the Unreal Engine 4 in a very stable manner, leaving me no cause for complaint. I applaud the decision to remove any potential HUD elements, they would have only eroded the experience since I firmly believe adventure titles of any subgenre are best played without keyboard prompts or hand holding tips. You’re left to your own device from a clean first person perspective. Whether you choose to take screenshots along your journey or not, you’ve been provided with plenty of opportunities in the form of eye-catching scenery, events and creatures. It goes without saying that the environment gets increasingly surreal as the story progresses. Just as expected. The sound department also received the necessary attention in the form of skilled voice acting for the narrator in equal measure to certain side characters. Soundtrack was spot on as well, never becoming repetitive or feeling out of touch with the scenes playing out before you. Almost relaxing at key points through the story but that's the literal calm before the storm, so stay alert.While I wouldn’t consider it a lengthy experience (you can probably finish it in under 4 hours if you’re not keen on exploration like I was), The Shore is cleverly structured in a manner that won’t allow boredom to set it. Exploration and peaceful collectible hunting is briskly interrupted by a totally different hunt in the form of chase sequences. Running for your life can only get you so far however. You will eventually gain the ability to fight back, Andrew’s own resilience growns as strong as his capabilities in time and the autosave implementation ensures that failure in combat isn’t unforgiving.I will advise that you constantly check the inventory for new clues as well as gaining further insight into the intricacies of the Lovecraft mythos. There will be numerous objects to pick up and study in detail, from abstract sculptures to seemingly incoherent texts. Expect some puzzle sections which will require a modicum of effort, but they’re not going to strain you too much. It’s a well balanced challenge in the end, the game never felt frustratingly hard while I definitely didn’t expect a cake walk either. Come to think of it, walking sims certainly evolved a lot since the initial days of a little Half-Life 2 mod called “Dear Esther”.If you’re itching to get those lovecraftian desires finally sated, look no further than The Shore. It’s the closest you’ll get to a Cthulhu love letter in 2021 minus hitting the rock bottom of controversies like a certain sinking city on Steam. It’s more than decently priced for what it offers and I can say for a fact that the title has been nurtured by its dev team constantly with updates both fixing any bugs and enhacing the gameplay with a handful of previously inaccessible areas and more Steam Achievements than it had on its release date. + Steam Achievements.+ Beautiful visuals and game design.+ Diversified gameplay encouraging exploration.- Quite short and with little replay value.- No Steam Trading Cards.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I’d like to address the big Lovecraftian elephant with tentacles in the room. This game was developed by 2 people with 2 months-salary funding. At least according to the crowdfunding campaign that I participated in. That said, I would probably review this game differently if it was made by KONAMI.I thought that this will be a game focusing on the story aspect and didn’t expect rich game mechanics or deep systems and apparently, that was the case. The visual style was one of the main selling points as well and for me, that was the most consistent aspect from start to finish. When it comes to the story though, there is a bit of a paradox happening here. In most games of this category, I expect the story and the visuals to go hand in hand and enhance each other. Here I felt that the story was mostly an excuse to have cool stuff show on the screen but not much more than that. It felt like a competent 3D artist made those cool 3D models and was dying to place them on a game, so he created a story that can fit all of the things that he wants to fit. The visual part is great, but all the Gods feel more like references than meaningful parts of the story. So, the paradox I mentioned above is that the great visuals make the story feel like an afterthought instead of offering more depth. Even so, the love for Lovecraft’s work is quite clear and there is a lot of detail and passion put into this project. The game offers some unique visuals and it really gives the feeling that you are experiencing a horrible nightmare that won’t end.The gameplay aspect is quite basic but as I said, not far away from what I expected. I could do with fewer monster chase sequences though. Unfortunately, I think those parts don’t add to the experience but more of the opposite since the game’s controls are not optimized for satisfying fighting. If it happened only a couple of times it would come as a surprise and it would have worked a lot better for me. Oh, and I have to mention that I had a huge problem interacting with things. There were parts of the game where I got stuck for 5 minutes because I couldn’t get the prompt to interact with something even though I was straight up facing it. I mostly played on a controller, so I don’t know if that made things worse.The levels look really nice visually and the claustrophobic atmosphere works really well later in the game. The problem for me was the shore part. The level looks quite open but there are a million invisible walls that make movement very restricting and sometimes frustrating. To my understanding, this was done so players have to visit the lighthouse before they gain access to other parts of the map and then linearly move from place A to place B and so on. I think this could have been avoided very easily and allow the players to traverse the map more freely.Last but not least, the game is quite overpriced for something that lasts 2-4 hours. I think lowering the price will help the devs in the long run.In conclusion, don’t play this game expecting to get the same experience as Resident Evil or Silent Hill. Dear Ester or the Vanishing of Ethan Carter is a lot closer. If you liked those games there is a high chance you’ll like this one too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game manages to fail at being a walking simulator and at conveying any sense of fear despite basing itself on the Cthulhu mythos. Thought that was spooky ? No ? Then nothing in this game has any chance to scare you. Oh, sometimes you have to press "run" for a few seconds to run from a monster in a corridor until some script ends the chase. Thought that was tense ? No ? Too bad, that's all you get. The only challenge you'll encounter is figuring where to go or what to do next because the game even fails at making your objective clear at any point. Conclusion : run away if you have any real expectations from a game about Lovecraft's universe. This is just a tasteless cash grab made by scrubs who thought that showing tentacles after 10 minutes is what cosmic horror is all about.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is best described as a walking simulator with the occasional eldritch horror in the background, and weak FPS elements later on. It also boasts being the first walking simulator I've played, where dead ends are so frequent and do nothing but irritate you. Voice acting is clearly done with cheap microphones in bedrooms, and honestly the story is confusing with a "WHAT A TWIST" type ending.And yet... I really enjoyed this game despite its clear downsides, it came from people that had a clear passion for the source material and did the best they could with what they had. Although it could have been done ALOT better i respect the effort put in to make such a unique experience and i can honestly say, this game has some of the most unique visuals and scenes i have ever seen in a game. The contrasts of colors between sections, the clear handmade monster designs, and the music is actually beautiful during the more "epic" moments. The ending in particular is downright gorgeous and worth the whole effort of reaching that point.The Shore wont win any awards in writing or design, but does get my respect for trying their best with what they have. The Shore is a unique one off experience that could have been better, but the few epic moments it does have are truly worth dealing with all the shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this recommended has several big fat asterisks that need to be mentioned. However a TL;DR can be summed up with "If you are a fan of HP Lovecraft, get this now." So, firstly, lets go through the bad.THE BAD:* This game is rather janky in places, for literally everything.* The voice acting needs to be re-recorded and remixed for everyone except the main character. He's fine.* Some of the puzzles (two for me, but the forums seem to have other issues) are badly designed due to one major flaw that could be fixed with a light source or larger interaction area, such as not needing to point at a pixel to connect.* Every chase in the game will probably begin with you dying. I wouldn't be surprised that, in a month or two, many of them will be solved.THE GOOD:This is probably the biggest wet dream any fan of Lovecraft could ever want. I'm serious. For $7 bucks, I played through the whole thing in one go just to see where else it'd take me. My God, does it deliver. The developer put all his effort into the animations, world design, and sound effects. If you are a fan of HP Lovecraft, you need to play this one. _childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the Mythos. The universe our beloved Howard Phillips Lovecraft created is so complex, so immense in every level! From the lowest creatures, whose fate are to be enslaved to extinction, to amorphous chaotic masses of tentacles, eyes and mouths that created everything in his dreams. Quite a huge, amazing and interesting universe of unthinkable cosmic horror.This game, however... It makes it no justice at all. This game is quite a big disappointment to any fan of the Mythos. Spoilers ahead.1) The plot. It's nothing but a rought draft of a fleeting idea. Absurdly bad. You're a guy that wakes up in the shore of a foggy island, with nothing around but fog, water, broken ships, half the population of France rotted to skeletons scattered around, and dark sand. All you know and all you're ""told"" (narrated through the guy speaking to himself) is that you're looking for your daughter. Then you follow a voice in your head that forces you to free several Great Old Ones in order to give you your daughter back in exchange for following his intructions. Once you've done everything he's told you, he tells you your daughter was never real, she was just fake memories the voice (Nyarlathotep) created in your mind cuz why not, but then encourages you to make it so Azathoth believes your daughter is real, and hence creates her in his dreams, which is everything that exists. Simply nonsensical.2) It lacks the main theme of the entire Mythos: HORROR. INSANITY. Seeing your grandmother coming out of the shower, naked, after barging into the bathroom without knocking first is way scarier than this. What about insanity? Well if you think you're gonna find insanity in this game, you're partly right! It exists! But only as the backstory of a sailor crew that ended up in that island. They ended up insane and dying this or that way or just killing themselves. That's it. Your character, Andrew, goes around freeing Great Old Ones, even standing in front of Cthulhu and freaking talking to him as Cthulhu talks about how he's gonna destroy humankind before epicly launching a boat towards you, but nah, Andrew's sanity is still there, he probably saw worse stuff than a literal god-like creature that wipes out every drop of sanity from any living being foolish enough to look his way or even being near his presence. He can even see Azazoth, The Nuclear Chaos, The Blind Idiot God, and not give a crap. They justify it as "Andrew's lack of sympathy made him lose fear", which is stupid. He probably just saw something way worse than all of that. He probably saw his grandma naked after coming out of the shower because he barged into the bathroom without knocking first.3) Textures. Absolutely disgusting. Even in Ultra, the sand, the damn first thing you see when you start the game, looks like Minecraft. Not even joking, it's so pixely that it feels like a recolor of Minecraft's gravel texture. Then there are floating rocks here and there, and big rocks that don't connect to the ground and you can peek inside the texture if you crouch a bit... Oh, also, everything you interact with and inspect up-close looks like a blurry 144p texture before focusing after a second or two. Don't even want to talk about the animations where things just shabbily go into the ground without any kind of effect to hide the textures going into the ground... The only good point I can see, is that some of the monsters in the game are properly designed, and have pretty good designs. Although I didn't check their textures from up-close for obvious reasons, so I can't say if they were good or shabby. Although, I did walk into the Deep One that was doing push-ups behind the whale corpse cuz I didn't know it was an enemy, and it was just... disappointing.4) Gameplay. This game is some kind of amalgam of several mechanics. First, it starts as a sorta phylosophical narrative walking simulator where you walk around figuring stuff out by yourself (because the game won't tell you anything about what you have to do), find a few pages of lore, -if you can call it lore-, and do some dumb puzzles with even dumber "rewards" for completion. At least they give achievements. Those are cool. Oh, also, you can't run or jump at first, you *unlock* those "actions" as you "progress". Apparently Andrew forgot how to run and jump at first... Then, the game introduces some sort of a failure of action/combat mechanics, where at first you're chased by a Deep One that was doing push-ups begind a whale's corpse, then sees you and runs after you *as fast as you can run*, which means if you didn't notice him and he catches you, he will attack you until you're dead, and you can't outrun him at all because the shabby attack animations doesn't even make him stand still or reduce his speed. After you die and try to run away again, and succeed, you start getting teleported into horrific "worlds", which to be honest were better than the previous areas of the game, where you go around solving more stupid puzzles where you aren't told anything nor given any hint at all (which isn't that bad cuz the puzzles are made for Primary Schoolers), and sometimes you were hugged by some weird humanoid thing and you had to push it back with the brand new combat "mechanics", and some other times some weird flea thing or a Shoggoth would pursue you and you'd have to escape. That is, until you obtain The Eye of the Gatekeeper! An artifact which shoots a beam to activate things, solve puzzles and hurt your enemies! Although it doesn't work half the time and you have to click and hold several times for it to actually shoot. Oh, of course, when you kill your enemies they just disappear with a shabby "blood" texture of a fourth of the size of the creature. And then you face this spider-like enemy that runs super fast and attacks even faster, which you can only kill by kinda bugging it by attacking it with the beam, backing away, and kinda hiding so it stays still. There's also a boss, who I believe is Shub-Niggurath, who is the shabbiest boss fight I've fought in a long time. Shub-Niggurath made for a way tougher boss in South Park, and it isn't a Dark Souls-type of game, to be honest.5) Immersion. Absolutely none. I tried my best to feel any immersion, but everything was just so stupid that I just couldn't. Even the few seconds I took to admire some giant creature like Dagon, or the walking monolith, or the giant walking flea in the distance, it'd be ruined by seeing the creatures calmly walk off. All I could admire was Dagon climbing onto the walking monolith like King Kong climing the Empire State, and Cthulhu's thicc ass. Seriously, he had quite a booty.6) Sound. Two things, voice acting, and soundtrack. To be honest, the soundtrack was pretty good in my opinion. The voice acting, however... It was... Mediocre. If you're drunk enough.7) Duration. I don't even know if I should say it's good or bad... My gameplay only took 2 hours, which is quite underwhelming and short for a 10€ game. Terraria costs 10€ when it's not on sale, and you can get HUNDREDS of hours of fun with it. I, personally, believe it was good that this game was only 2 hours. It was too atrocious for me to want it to be longer.Conclusion: This is an awful game. I don't think the developers wanted to disrespect the Mythos with this game, but they accidentally did. And I don't blame them, making games is hard. But even so, if you decide to make a game... TRY it before you sell it. Ask your friends to try it, so they can tell you "This game's ♥♥♥♥" before you sell it and decide to do something better with it, like trying to fix it, even redoing it, or just deleting the files and erasing it from existence. This game just fails at 96% of the things it has. I regret paying for this, and wasting 2 hours on this game. I could've spent them reading the wonderful Metro 2033 book.
