_childDocuments_.review: Guys, don't let bad reviews deceive you!This is one of the most beautiful and immersive Lovecraftian games ever!It's one of the very few games that convey what it would be like to become a mere human facing the great old ones.This game is an artistic experience and if you expect it to be some cheap entertainment or a combat slasher, please just steer clear, you will end up posting your misguided expectations here and ruining the mood for people who appreciate the game for what it is.Its best qualities: - Amazing atmosphere- Great area design like the amazing natural looking terraforming which very few artists can pull off- Subtle storytelling- Breathtaking music- Some object models you can get just mesmerized by- The feeling of grandeur, amazement, being a part of a mysteryNow I'll sum up the bad reviews for you:- Nitpicking, like "where is the invert Y axis option. Unplayable" (It was not a big deal and was added in a day upon release)- Outright false information "this game doesn't let me jump" (while it clearly does)- "the UI is not pretty boo-hoo" (that's a meter of taste. I loved it and thought of it as very fitting the art style and the narration)- A couple grammatical mistakes in the subtitles. (You'll be better of pointing those mistakes out to the devs instead of bashing the game for it. This is something fixable in the matter of an hour)- People expecting this to be Overwatch or some battle royal game, or I don't know what. (Combat is clearly not the point of this game, and for a story driven walking simulator the combat is amazing)You people, are the reason, why we can't have nice things! Games like this one don't come out often and instead of bringing it down you could provide your constructive criticism and give the devs a chance to smoothen the couple rough edges.Now I will do exactly that. What would I change so people could fully appreciate the game:1. Place save points right before the chase scenes. Having to listen to the same cutscene before you die is widely considered bad game design2. Make it more apparent where you need to go during the Protoplasmic abomination chase scene3. Make the creature underwater inside the purple maw a bit slower. I was running as fast as I could and dying anyway. (one of the very few places where the intense immersion has actually been ruined)4. Change voice actors for the Cthulhu and the wife. Their voices seem way out of place 5. Flash out the character model for the daughter. Right now it looks exactly like that: a bad puppet stiff computer model6. Make the transition between the "stuff collecting" part of the game and the action part more noticeable and pronounced. Like for example a cutscene of the character dropping all of his belongings to the ground. Right now the transition is a little bit odd and feels like you're playing two different games. Or maybe add some lore collection elements to the action parts if possible, so the contrast is not so striking.8. Do something to make the ending more impactful. Right now it's kind of open ended, we don't know either to believe Azatoth or not which leaves everything hung up in he air. On top of that strong emotional connection to the daughter is never established during the game which leaves the player not really caring for her all that much7. And for god's sake, turn that photo camera model on the beach towards the dead sailors. The lens is the part that absorbs light, not the photo film holder.8. Maybe bring the price down a little so people stop ruining the score. Although I was perfectly fine with the price. For me it's the price of a ticket to an art exhibition, and I'll take this experience over almost any exhibition any day!While these issues have somewhat distracted points form my experience, they are not even nearly enough for me to fall out of LOVE with this amazing adventure and the breathtaking scenes! I'm leaving the comments open for the people who have left their negative opinion in reviews, but can't get over the fact that I too have my right to give my positive opinion. Yes, I'm gatekeeping this game, get over it. Otherwise welcome to the comments, but I'm nasty to argue with, when I'm pissed, you've been warned ;)
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully weird feeling to the location where the game begins.  I've played thru the first part severaltimes and the sense of isolation and dread gets stronger.  I've notised that a number of "events" occuron a schedule, whether I'm nearby or not - they add to the weirdness, but aren't needed for gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game and it had a lot of beauty to it. What I can't forgive is slapping invisible walls everywhere and tiny object hunting."Ah, that looks like a path to where I want to go. That telescope drew my attention along the shore""You can't go that way""Why not? It's less steep than the path I was just on""Nope""Seriously, if you could just let me walk forward half a pace, I could explore that open area""Nuh uh""How about here?""Hah""Here?""Pfff""Where am I SUPPOSED to go then?"*Shrugs* "Just wander about a bit and look for tiny items""Why do some items go to my inventory and some of them stay where they are?"*Shrug*"That coin I picked up, but the other ones I just leave? Why?"*Shrug*"Oh, I give up"*Shrug*
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed this game over on my Youtube channel (link below for anyone wanting to see a sample of gameplay before buying), so here are some thoughts.If you're a big fan of all things Lovecraft, then The Shore is worth giving a shot. By far the most impressive element of this game are the visuals, which are stunning. Most of the game involves solving puzzles, but there's a bit of basic combat later on and there are plenty of eldritch enemies to watch out for. The story does feel like a bit of a mash-up of Lovecraftian monsters and entities, as if the devs wanted to try and get as many elements of the Cthulhu mythos in there as they could. Again, if you're a big fan of Lovecraftian stories then this is basically fanservice for you - but players unfamiliar with Lovecraft may find it a little bit chaotic.Overall, whilst not the most amazing Lovecraft-themed game out there, I still recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So this game has issues. It's short, it's sometimes buggy, the story is.. not great, but... The atmosphere, dude! It's ll about the atmosphere! It feels like you're inside a dream that you can't escape. You're walking around the island, then.. something happens and you're alredy running from a huge shoggoth, then ... again on the shore, releasing Dagon, etc.You'll see Dagon holding the monolith, Cthulhu rising from the sea, Shub-Niggurath spawning the Dark Young, Nyarlathotep above the pyramid and even Azatoth in space!  One thing really bothered me. Cthulhu laughing and talking like your typical villain wanting to destroy the world and some kind of conflict between him and Nyarlathotep. This is too.. Derleth-y. But you can ignore that, that's just a short momet, and the atmosphere is still great.If you want an other Call of Cthulhu or Amnesia - move along, if you want soomething more dreamy, closer to Dagon and Silver Key and can look past some typical indie problems - get it!Also the developer is reading all the bug reports and fixing the game, so it;s gonna be more polished.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, the ending was kind of bad, it felt rushed and I guess that's where most of the thumbs down come from.That's the negative out of the way. I think the developer did a great job bringing to life some of the hardest source material out there. A lot of it really felt other-wordly and very imaginative. I enjoyed playing this game and can recommend it to anyone who likes HP Lovercraft's work.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The shore is a very troubled game. The gameplay for most of this is atrociously bad. If you are turned away from games for terrible gameplay alone, then do not buy this. If you love games with good atmosphere, setting, and visuals and you can overlook some bad gameplay, then you should consider getting this. Most of the gameplay in this game will be annoying chase sequences (that really aren't scary) followed by a short puzzle. I think the gameplay issues could have easily been solved by making this a walking simulator with a few puzzles sprinkled in. The audio here is really good in some areas, and not so good in others. Some of the visuals and locations throughout this game are really quite amazing and very lovecraftian.If you plan to get this game, wait for a sale. The game is about 2 - 3 hours long, so keep that in mind when choosing how much to buy it for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: If you have thalassophobia or megalophobia, this game might actually kill you. I had to stop to catch my breath several times so i didn't pass out while playing. That's not a negative criticism btw, the fact that a video game is able to trigger those phobias so effectively is a testament to the developers attention to detail. On top of that, this is probably the most accurate representation of what I call "the Lovecraft experience" that I've ever seen in a video game. It manages to satisfy curiosity while answering basically none of the questions it asks while simultaneously representing Lovecraft's work with layers of detail rich cosmic horror I've never really seen in a video game. It also does more with it's three hour runtime than something like Outlast does with it's 6-8 hour experience. Some might see that as a negative criticism as game length is usually a divisive subject and many people prefer quantity over quality, but I'm telling you that I will play this multiple times over before I ever revisit a pile of s*** like Outlast ever again. This is one of the best examples of what can be done within the confines of the highly stigmatized "first person indie horror" genre. This developer deserves a ton of credit for pulling this off. No AAA game, no television series, rarely any films have ever managed to create such a faithful adaptation of Lovecraft's work. If you're a fan of Lovecraftian horror, first person horror, or just horror in general, DO NOT skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: As a Lovecraft fan I went looking for a game that embodied the cosmic horror from the stories. In short the game did live up to my expectations.  I would have liked a little more show and dont tell, but than again a game has to have something to do. It looks great and has te right feel to it. It might be a game I go back to every once in a while just to step back into the world.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty strange little game, but I really enjoyed it as a short mind-number and wandering game.The graphics are a mixture of some really nicely smooth textures (the shark, lighthouse etc.) with some really block parts (pretty much everything else on the beach), but strangely... this works so well, in creating a unique, fun style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game was short and sweet. It was very cinematic and brought the cosmic elements of H. P. Lovecraft's to the game with an impressively-rendered grandeur. The gameplay wasn't phenomenal but this can be overlooked because of the atmospheric and memorable world. The music and voice acting were also commendable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not horrible, but it is not worth $25. It looks pretty great and has great atmosphere. The beginning is the best part. The last half is just walking a mostly linear path and constantly seeing monsters to the point they get kind of boring. I got it on sale for $11.74, which I think is a better price. This game will take you around 3 hours max to beat, maybe a little longer if you replay part of it to get 100% achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly an art project wrapped in a thin veneer of a game.Whilst its clear that a lot of effort has gone into creating a Cthulu environment, this game barely qualifies as a walking simulator. The 'puzzles' are not really even puzzles, you just have to do some actions in the right order which can be figured out by trial and error.There are some instances where you can die, and at least one of those has an unnecessarily long reset time due to the amount of walking needed after loading at the last save point.There are some chase events which are extremely frustrating as you have to figure out what to do through trial and error, whilst dying over and over.The main character has good voice acting but most of the other voices are terrible.The story... what there is of it isn't great.Overall I cannot recommend, even at a steep discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I am impressed with this game's level of quality, given that it is an indie game with a small number of developers. I bought the non-VR version on sale for about $2.99. While I enjoyed the game, I do have to say that I would not pay anymore than that for it due to length of the game (took me about 3 hours, I think, even with my starting over about 30 minutes in) and the Cons list. (The VR version may be worth picking up at a higher price, however.)PROS:*Voice acting is much better than I expected.*Music and ambiance are very well done.*Settings are immersive and lovely, with wonderful color schemes!*Creature designs are awesome.*Based on H.P. Lovecraft's works.*Has that lonely, otherworldly feel that you're hoping it does. (Which is why you started reading these reviews to begin with, right?)CONS:*Invisible walls! There are many places you simply cannot walk, even though it looks like you should be able to. I understand that this is to help keep the story on track, but it is annoying to keep getting stopped by nothing.*The combat system. In many places you have to run BACKWARDS through winding corridors while yielding a magical beam that often only stuns your enemies for about a second and half. To top it off, almost all of the enemies that you face are WAY faster than you. This leads to even minor mistakes (which are tough to avoid because you can't look where you're going) causing you to die repeatedly and have to start the encounter all over again. This seriously detracts from the immersion; I ended up repeating some portions 3+ times and spent far more energy being angry about it than enjoying the story and beautiful areas. I ultimately felt like I missed out on these maps, being forced to rush through them and be salty about dumb mechanics.*The character's speed. Even at a sprint, your character is as slow as molasses. During some monster encounters YOU CANNOT RUN AT ALL; the ability seems to have been disabled by the developer at these points, possibly to increase the stress of the encounter. It's quite maddening.*I understand that this was likely a foreign language game, but there are noticable misspellings in the notes scattered around the island, and the English voice actor for the main character mispronounces several words.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most ominous and intense representation of Lovecraftian cosmic horror I've ever experienced. The feeling of dread is real in this one. If you can get over some bad voice acting (the protagonist mostly) and some janky mechanics in the 2nd half, you'll get a very effective horror game. Short & Sweet.Impressive stuff from a game developed by mostly ONE guy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A decent walking sim with some light puzzling elements and some really annoying chase/combat sequences and a somewhat muddled story. I basically enjoyed everything except when I'm trying to figure out where to go while something is attacking me. You can defeat them, but it takes a while.A nice diversion for Cosmic Horror fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: what a rousing romp through the lovecraftian weird and wonderful. quite eerie, if i dare say so. especially the craft that was on display with the mixing of the auditory qualities of the game. human voices barely heard even if all other audible brimborium is turned down to the slightest. as if to say: humanity is not welcome here and you shan't hear anything even remotely reminding you of the anthropic flesh tied to your waning sanity. spectacular.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore did a very good job of portraying the Cthulhu myth, all the monsters and surroundings look very good, accompanied by a beautifully melancholy soundtrack. The rest is unfortunately not that good, the story was very difficult to understand and the fight sequences were very fiddly. Nevertheless a very atmospheric Cthulhu game.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the tag, this game is very light on horror.That being said, it's an amazing treat for Lovecraft fans! It manages to work in many aspects of Lovecraft's lore and it does so in a logical way. That being said, it doesn't really explain much of the Lovecraft mythos, so if you aren't already familiar with the lore you may feel a bit lost as it name drops god/creatures without explaining much about them.Also, this game has some great creature designs based on the Lovecraft mythos. Especially since the game is only about 3 hours, they could've gotten lazy and just reused the same few creatures over and over. Instead they regularly throw new ones at you. They all look great!On the negative side, this game is pretty buggy, though not in a game breaking way. I never encountered a freeze or something that stopped me from progressing, but expect to regularly clip through objects, see graphical bugs galore (seagulls perched on nothing, etc.), and encounter various weird controller issues. Still, I found these issues to be minor.Also, though I liked the environments overall, there are way, way too many invisible walls. I think the dev wanted to keep the vistas an open feel, so the player can revel in the cool views, but that means that you'll constantly encounter invisible walls preventing you from getting to places you clearly should be able to go. This becomes a much bigger issue during chase sequences, since I never knew if I could walk over a low pile of rocks or if I would hit a wall. I recommend the dev just use natural barriers (i.e. high rock walls, dense trees, etc.) in future games. It will hurt the views a bit, but invisible walls are way more annoying.Last, as many reviews mention, the style of gameplay changes quite a bit in the second half of the game. I enjoyed it, but there was clearly less polish on some of those gameplay aspects. Still, the great level art/creature design and lore will easily sustain Lovecraft fans though the few rough sections.Overall, the game is only 3 hours, but I say if you can find it for $4 or less, it's a great deal. Lovecraft fans won't be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I rate this an average game.  For the positives: Nice graphics, some cool set pieces, beautiful music (when they're designed to be calm and atmospheric), easy puzzles, interesting myth, and a touching tale.  For the negatives: invisible barriers in the world seemed weirdly placed (like tiny mounds of rock that our character could jump atop, but not walk across); battle segments felt like they clashed with the game's calm beginning & middle; knowing where to go was sometimes obtuse; and I wish there were more lore.  I'm glad that I played through & beat this experience, but I shan't be returning to replay it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game, although with a heavy caveat.The look, the theme, the lovecraft mythos itself is done well and treated with respect, that is the reason I give the thumbs up.HOWEVER: The combat situations are awful and easily the worst aspect of the game. I feel they should have just skipped all of that entirely.That said though even with the weakness of combat, its a very solid lovecraftian adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Why are these escape sequences in there? It has nothing to do with the initial style of the game. The atmosphere was fantastic before some random monster came after me, instantly killing me. There is no need of forced action sequences. You already have the atmosphere right there.I could have loved this game but instead it is now rotting unfinished on the crap stack.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Enjoyed some parts but simply too short, unpolished, and downright flawed to recommend. Maybe try it if it is on sale for under $8 and/or you don't care about gameplay or story and just want to look at cool monsters and environments.I don't usually write reviews but this game was just not what I expected. I don't think I will refund it as I still admired some aspects like the atmosphere and art direction, but because of its many flaws and short run time I cannot recommend it, at least at its current price of $12.The game does a few things right, and by right I mean it does them beautifully. The art direction of the creatures and environments was incredible and reminded me at some points of H.R. Giger and at others Z. Beksinski. I especially enjoyed the atmosphere of the misty island and some of the more open sections mid-late game. While some may brand this game as a walking simulator (a term thrown around way too much), this game has plenty of puzzle solving, chase sequences, and combat which is always at least somewhat engaging.Unfortunately, all of the things this game does well are far outnumbered by the things it does not so well. The graphical quality was inconsistent. For most of the game the graphics looked amazing but some things like water splashes, those weird points of red or purple light in the otherworldly sections, and even the texturing of the entire  were ugly and made the game seem unpolished. The level design also seemed in dire need of polishing. I saw many floating rocks and low poly edges that really took away from the otherwise wonderfully crafted landscape. Invisible walls blocked me whenever I tried to go somewhere I logically could which made finding the "correct" path very tedious. The text seemed badly translated at times and there were many spelling and grammatical errors in the notes and subtitles. The voice acting was just plain bad, at times laughable, but mostly cringy. The audio quality of the voice acting in particular was distracting as some lines sounded like they were professionally recorded, and others sounded like they were recorded with a cheap cell phone. However, all of these things are forgivable as this game was made by an indie dev and it did not seem like English was their first language.What I don't find forgivable from a technical aspect is the design of the gameplay. While the presence of puzzles, chase sequences, and combat was appreciated they were often not that good. The puzzles require no brain power once you get past their frustrating obscurity. I especially had problems with . The chase sequences were either too easy because all you have to do is run from a slow moving enemy down an alien tunnel or too hard because you are trying to navigate a maze while being chased by an invincible enemy that is faster than you. Plus, you can't take in any of the stunning scenery when you are running from Shoggoths. The combat is uninteresting after the novelty of the singular combat mechanic wears off and consists only of  until it simply pops out of existence with a little splatter of black ooze.The worst thing, and the reason I cannot recommend this game especially to sincere fans of Lovecraft is the quality of the story, or lack thereof. As the description says the main story is you are Andrew and you are looking for your daughter and spooky Lovecraftian stuff happens. Believe it or not, the description oversells the game. You do play as an old fisherman named Andrew who is looking for his daughter, but that is where the similarities end. I did not uncover any "secrets lurking within his own sanity", I did not feel like I faced "overwhelming odds", there were no "moments that make you question his sanity", I did not feel like the game was a "series of slow-burning scenes", and I did not think the story was "deep and multilayered". The pacing was terrible past the first third of the game and there was no build up or payoff for any of the story's big moments. The majority of the game is just awakening Lovecraftian beings because the voice told you to and that is the only way to progress. Speaking of awakening Lovecraftian beings, I felt that the game lacked subtlety in that aspect. You are shown eldritch horrors (all popular Lovecraft monsters) in their entirety and in full detail. One of them even has a cheesy monologue. Then you just move on to summoning the next one without stopping to think about anything. Because of this the themes of fear of the unknown, the insignificance of the narrow scope of human comprehension, and the fragility of the human psyche that define Lovecraftian horror are completely absent. The only thing that makes this a "Lovecraftian" game is spooky tentacle things and references to some of Lovecraft's specific works that have no place in the game other than fanservice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Just started playing this game, and I've got to say, I have read every single story in the Cthulhu Mythos, and other related works, and this game brings them all to life in such an amazing way. I have been dying for a game like this for so long, and to actually have it and be able to witness the sheer Lovecraftian terror is amazing. I'm in love with the artwork, music, and the story. I wish the game could be free roam, and I could just walk around messing with all of the weirdness for hours. I'm not huge into fighting games, and thankfully there isn't a high level of combat, I can just immerse myself in the story and feel like I'm living in a Lovecraft novel. It's a dream come true. If you are a big Lovecraft nerd, this is seriously the game for you! It has the whole package!Edit: Just finished the game! OMG for the real Lovecraft fan, you will love the ending! There is absolutely nothing more pleasantly surprising and poetic than the ending that was given! Such an amazing game. I will keep coming back to play it, and probably will never ever stop playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I usually really like Lovecraft inspired games, but this is not one of them.Besides the decent graphics, is a tedious, clunky mess.The game is extremely poorly optimized.Various functionality (running, jumping) gets taken away at random, seemingly with no real motivation, making this an extremely sluggish and tedious game.There's plenty of bugs, floating geometry, hanging game states (probably badly designed blueprints)The story is dull and uninspired. The Lovecraftian themes are too on the nose and uninspired, and leave nothing to the imagination.Then there's the endless invisible walls, dear lord, so many invisible walls.Oh, and the voice acting is something to behold, it's a Lovecraftian horror all on it's own seeing how bad it is.Give this a pass, as pretty as the pictures look like.It's a 2.5 hour shlog, and the only reason it takes 2.5 hours in stead of 1 is because the movement speed is like you're moving through treacle.Better spend your money on something like Call of the Sea.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: While a fairly primitive gaming experience full of invisible walls and bare bones mechanics, lovers of weird lovecraft visuals like me may find a lot to appreciate after the unpromising first quarter. A lot of the classic usual suspects make an appearance in awe inspiring ways. People who aren't genre-addicts might be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: While I think the game possesses some very interesting imagery, a solid soundtrack and good (sometime almost photo-realistic) graphics; and would make a decent ride for die hard Lovecraft fans I can't recommend it to anyone because of many reasons :-The plot is nonsensical and just used as a cheap device to guide you through a Lovecraftian slide show-The puzzles aren't even worth being called this way-The level design is atrocious and combines the worst flaws of open world design and corridor design, filled with dead ends and invisible walls.-Voice actors are some random dudes from Fiverr with varying microphone qualities-The script is broken English and even the voice actors refuse to read most of it.-The "combat" is laughably trash and shouldn't even be in the game to begin with-The gameplay and chase sequences are broken and not fun to say the least-The big encounters with the Cthulhu mythos monsters are ruined with garbage choppy animations.I really liked the design of the monsters, the overall vibe of the game is alright but I really think it should have been a walking sim with a solid plot, this would have really suited the game better. The product we have here feels like it is some portfolio of a guy that is really into Lovecraft and wants to show us that he can design stuff.Buy it on a sale if you are desperate for Lovecraft content and you played everything else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The entire game can be completed at a leisurely pace in 90 minutes. The first half leans toward scaring/frustrating the player with unwinnable fights as you alternate between incomprehensible puzzles and running from advancing walls of doom with no weapons to fight monsters.The second half is a little more wonder. Still a lot of obtuse puzzles that make no sense, not much of a story. There's some nice set pieces where the Old Ones are concerned. But for all that, it's definitely NOT worth the $25. Maybe wait until it's $5 or less. I wish I could get a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: When you row your boat merrily down the stream, you may be inclined to wonder: IS life just a dream?Then your boat hits The Shore and you find out that it's more of a Lovecraftian nightmare, and it's being dreamt not by you, but by Things Man Was Not Meant To Know.There's not much "game" here, since mostly it's about walking around creepy environments, with brief interruptions of fleeing in terror from squidgy Horrors From Beyond. Your mad gamer skillz will not save you. You will not stand triumphant atop a mountain of monster corpses, holding your plasma chainsaw aloft while a buxom damsel in distress clings to your leg and gazes up at you adoringly.It's not that kind of game. And that's appropriate, because it's not that kind of genre.But what The Shore does, it does incredibly well. The visuals, sounds, and atmosphere are brilliant. I felt genuine dread at several points in the game. I bought it on sale for about 6 bucks and at that price it was a bargain.Two tentacles way up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for some time for a price reduction offer to buy this game, mostly by curiosity and support to my Greek compatriot Ares Dragonis, although I am not fun of this adventure like game genre. Haven't finished it yet, though I must say I am astonished by the atmosphere of the game. Very nice work Ares! The graphics, the music, the dialogues all work fine to produce a mystery and horror atmosphere. What needs more work to be done and somewhat ruins the experience is the control interface. There, some programming work is needed.To conclude is a yes! for me. Well done Ares. Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short. AND YOU SHOULDNT SPOILER YOURSELF BEFORE PLAYING IT.It took me around 2,5 hours. But if you are into Lovecraft and Read some of the books and like the art of H.P Giger and other artists. This is an absolute must. Its a very low budget game but the art direction, visuals and music aswell as the overall atmosphere is great. The ending was satisfying for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: From an artistic standpoint, the game is great. The graphic artists really nailed the alien geometries of the void and the Lovecraftian creatures. There are visuals in this game that you'll simply never see anywhere else, and that's a shame.The sound was decent. The music was pretty good, but was ultimately just the same track looping over and over throughout the game. Occasionally you'll hear these really bassy sounds when approaching certain objects which really improve the atmosphere and alienness of the world.The problem is the gameplay, and story.The game starts out as a walking sim. While not great, this is something I can live with, and the game was pretty up-front about this. The problem is that about 1/3 of the way in it stop just being a walking sim. First you unlock the ability to jump purely for the sake of hopping onto a ship to grab two items. After that, the mechanic is basically never used again in any meaningful way. The game is littered with invisible walls, so anything you can jump on (e.g. rocks) will likely have a wall preventing you from actually progressing further.The second gameplay problem is that about halfway in, the game also decides to give you... let's call it "combat". You gain an alien artefact that can shoot out a beam that stuns and occasionally/arbitrarily kills certain creatures. You see, by this point the game frequently sprinkles in chase sequences. You either have to keep moving (as some monsters move at the same pace as your sprinting speed), or turn around and shoot them with the beam to stun them. Occasionally, some monsters will die, though some will then just respawn either right where they died, or in your path. You will die several times for no other reason than because you weren't standing far enough away from a monster when it popped out.The other problem is story. The game basically teases you with a few tidbits about your character's past. It never really comes out and tells you a meaningful story, but you can piece together the fact that you were a fisherman, your wife died, and eventually your daughter died too. Your father often spoke about the island, and cryptic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about making offerings to the sea/elder gods. There are some notes at the beginning of the game that hint at other people being stuck there, but it was disjointed, and most of the notes were "We've been stuck here for an indescribable amount of time | I'm starting to go mad | We may have found a way off the island".I could go on, but ultimately this game just completely fumbles after the first 30 minutes or so. And even the intro sequence wasn't great to begin with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very short, but the atmosphere is very true to the Mythos. Its an adventure/puzzle game with a very nice story (lovecraftian ending, i am not gonna spoil), epic music, and very nice graphics, where you get to see many of the Mythos creatures. A unique experience, especially if you are a Lovecraft fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet but I feel more than confident to leave a positive review. I think it's one of the best lovecraft around at the moment, so if you find it on sale, well get it, it's worth it. Setting and sountrack are perfect, presence of (easy) puzzles and monsters to escape from. The only downside, it's not intuitive and the story is a bit confusing. 7/10 my rating
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The length of the game does not justify the price of 25$.  I took my time and in general I complete games a tad slower than the average gamer. This game took me 2.2 hours to beat. My biggest gripe with this game was the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ invisible walls. What could have been a cool island to explore is simply an illusion and it quickly becomes apparent that the seemingly big open areas are actually small confined spaces, there are invisible walls EVERYWHERE. I'm not even kidding there is an invisible wall in the most ridiculous spots where they are not needed at all. Like I understand that ok, it's not an exploration game it is a linear walking sim and the player can't just go run off into the boonies so you gotta stop them with invis walls sometimes... but this is just next level. The visuals are ok. The audio is ok. The story is is ok. There are some really creepy moments and some disturbing visual moments that are pretty good but I wouldn't call great. The gameplay is bad. There is combat, kind of, and it is really clunky and not fun. You have an "artifact" that can disintegrate anything you shoot. But when try to use it on a bird (or anything living thing) out in the wild, nothing happens.  Only if the dev allows it. There is some kind of inventory system I think but I only opened it once because it doesn't actually do anything. The puzzles are pretty bad, and leave you with a "you gotta be kidding me" feeling.  There were maybe a couple that were cool but majority were really boring and time consuming. I'm writing after just finishing  the game and I'm really shocked at how short the game was for the price. I don't see myself replaying this one either.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a real shame writing this. During the first moments I was reminded of games like Zeno Clash, Amnesia or Myst even where you had this bleak, exploration type of feel with that indie feel. 2.1 hours later, it was over, and a lot of that time spent on frustrating mechanics. I'll do a break down of the different aspects of the game to help you better understand where it succeeds and fails.The Good:-The monsters, they look great-The music, it's different and has this mix between creepy ambiance and cosmic noise.-The main character's voice actor. I know this will probably be controversial but I enjoyed it.Unfortunately, that's where the pros stop.The bad:-Length, it will take you 1.5 hours to beat it, going through at a regular pace. This depends on your luck with some puzzles.-The puzzles. Your hand isn't held with puzzles. At all. Which isn't bad, provided they made sense. One of the puzzles has you picking up skulls on the ground, until you find the right one and "feeding" them to a object on the ceiling. I say feeding because you hold them up and they drop to the ground when they are incorrect. There are like 100 of these skulls on the ground and only one of them correct I think. So every incorrect one creates a pile on the ground covering the other skulls....This is just one example.-The voice acting. Aside from the main character, it's BAD. Some of them are REAL bad.-Paths and level design. The game lets you crouch and jump, but you're going to laugh when you realize how little that means. The paths are linear in this game but you are given a fairly open environment. Which leads you to trying to go over rocks and obstacles that would not even require you to jump in real life to overcome, and be met with invisible walls. Invisible walls everywhere.-Optimization. Using a I9-9990K with a GTX 1080 I had stuttering throughout the entire game. There is never more than a few enemies on the screen at one time, so not sure what the issue is.-Interface. You have an inventory but you can't do anything with it. You can crouch but I think I used it twice? There is a section that tells you to avoid a monster and so I assumed I should crouch to "stealth" but boy was that a joke. Same with jumping. I think I used jump once to get over poorly laid objects around a puzzle.-Combat. Sluggish and confusing. Combat was implemented to basically slow your character down. There was only one true boss fight in the game. A second if you can call it that and both feature puzzles that require you to active a circle of objects around the "arena" that you fight in.It sucks, because if the developer had treated this game as a Myst style exploration game and just stuck to the allure of puzzles and the spectacle of the monsters, he would have had a winner. Instead poor dialogue, story, combat and cheap puzzles in a 1.5 hour package....all for $25. I wanted this to be my new Zeno Clash, an underappreciated gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice, fairly short Lovecraft game.Overall the themes, graphics and atmosphere were fantastic. I particularly loved the designs and textures throughout this experience.Where the game falls a little short however is the build and some game mechanics. I'll expand on a few points below:-First, although the environments are beautiful there seems to be some overlooked areas where rocks are floating or geometry hasn't been placed close enough together it allows the player to possibly get stuck in areas that look passable but aren't. Overall not a bad issue.-Second, probably the most problematic are level collisions. In one level I accidently walked or pushed through the wall to the outside of the level. I walked along a bit and managed to jump back into the boss room. -Third, the camera sensitivity is a bit wild which was a little bothersome. The curser position for interacting with objects I found a little too small at times. -Fourth, although miner I found some of the dialogue was hard to hear at times but it wasn't a deal breaker.  Overall, I enjoyed it, I had fun. I'd say if you want to support the developer get this game at full price. If you're mildly interested but not sure, wait till it's on sale and pick it up. It's visuals and designs are well worth it in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is a decently well-made game that honors the eldritch horrors born from the wickedly genius mind of H. P. Lovecraft. The game may not appear great graphically in the shed but I grew to love the game more and more as I kept getting immersed in this Lovecraftian world. The game likes to put fast flashing eldritch symbols in your face sometimes, so if you have a thing against that then expect quite a few in The Shore.You play as an old fisherman named Andrew who wakes up shipwrecked on an island in the middle of a vast ocean. You notice your daughter is missing as well as other wrecked ships, skeletal remains, and alien artifacts on this strange place. You set out to find your daughter by checking out the large lighthouse stationed nearby the beach. Who knows what could possibly be slumbering underneath the island? What dangers could be hiding? What will you unleash?I won't spoil much else for you but I will say that the plot is purely based on , so if you know what goes on in the genre then you already have a basic understanding of The Shore's plot. I will say that I kind of liked the abrupt twist at the end of the story that left quite the cliffhanger. Still it left me satisfied with the game and who knows if there'll be a sequel?The game first begins as a  in which you walk around the island looking at possible collectibles and lore items. You could find some hidden events that show just how messed up the island can be to its inhabitants. The game does a great job of balancing what to show and tell you because you pretty much experience it firsthand. The only issue with exploration are the  that block areas that seem very walkable.The next gameplay mechanic are the  that require you to use your noggin. They are very, very simple which isn't necessarily bad if you're thirsting to see some old gods. You can get this puzzles over with quickly as most of them are pretty intuitive. There's a couple of puzzles that I felt were too monotonous to add any real gameplay value.The last one would be the interactions with the monsters that you'll encounter. You'll be either  or eventually . Once again this one is very simple like the others. For the chase scene you pretty much hold sprint and 'W' then move through a obvious path. For killing monsters, you literally hold left mouse button to user your laser beam on them until they die.First off, the font and design for the main menu selections could have been a lot better. It just looks very amateurish but doesn't devalue the game, I just wish the font didn't hurt my eyes.In all seriousness this time, the graphics aren't that bad as the island looks pretty decent. I can't say the same for the human models as even their animation is janky. The ELDRITCH models, on the other hand, are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ . I absolutely adore the art direction the developers made with respect to Lovecraft's work, they just look so otherworldly and awesome.Voice acting is decent, I mean some people may not like the Eldritch voice but I found them to be satisfactory even though it's just deepened voices. It still sounds cool and not cringey.Music was great in keeping up the suspense of exploring unknown territory as well as encountering the dangerous abominations.The Shore is incredible in showcasing a world of humanity being ruled over by fearsome Eldritch gods. The story does an amazing service in honoring the legendary genre created by H. P. Lovecraft. However you will disappointed if you're seeking for a challenge in gameplay. So .

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a pretty fun experience, as mentioned in a lot of other reviews the second half of the game is a bit underwhelming, but by that point I was intrigued enough and engrossed in the story to have the drive to finish the game. There are a few annoying moments in the game, some either confusing puzzles or really REALLY easy puzzles, and very clunky chase sequences that can be very tedious especially towards the end of the game. So why am I giving this a positive review? Well I think the atmosphere, exploration, and overall narrative are really well done and keep you really entertained the whole way through, the length of the game may seem short, but it's very appropriate and leaves you overall satisfied. The annoying and tedious bits are short enough where they don't ruin the game, but only muddle moments. I think the good outweighs the bad by far and it's a very fun experience that I would recommend to buy on sale and if you really love cosmic horror and have money to spend full price isn't a terrible investment either.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore has a lot more  than meets the eye. I went into this expecting something of a walking sim, like a prettier Dear Esther maybe. And while it certainly starts that way, I wasn't expecting the game to evolve into a run-for-your-life-a-thon.I screamed a lot playing the second half of this game. I  being chased in video games, and this game has plenty of sections where you're being chased; Having to stun an enemy and then turn your back to it and run through maze-like corridors. It almost drove me to the point of quitting. But I persevered. Because I had to. I played alongside someone who knows a lot about the lore. She says they did a good job with all of the creatures and really enjoyed the references from various Lovecraft works. I on the other hand have never read a book in my life. I had no idea what was happening at any point of this game. All I knew was that I had to keep running and I did so.I think the visuals and set pieces are enough in and of themselves to enjoy this game. I had a few minor bugs like the menu making it so you cannot move (have to hit escape twice to get in/out of it). The audio also seems to be bugged and resets to full volume between set pieces, so mind your ears. And... Just be warned of the chasing. If you're a fan of Lovecraft, there's apparently much more to enjoy here than I got out of it, but none the less, I'd recommend this to anyone who likes a "casual" experience turning suddenly terrifying. I should have known this would be the case, but, now you know. You've been warned.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a fan of walking sims and usually when I stumble into one, labeled as something with actual gameplay, I end up annoyed, disappointed and ready to write a negative review. Especially when most of them are very similar, relying on cheap jumpscares or closing and opening the doors until something happens. But this one? This one I like. It's by no means perfect, some of the more action like sequences were frustrating and I got stuck on a puzzle or two, but it was easy to forgive, when the game got something else perfectly. The lovecraftian atmosphere, the eeriness, the quiet, cold dread of something ancient and incomprehensible. You find objects and see creatures you don't understand. The more you look at the world, the little details, the less sense it makes, yet at the same time it's somehow believable. On this vast, nearly barren shore the main character meets with the eldritch and the further he goes, the more he is unable to turn back. Was it actually *scary*? I'm not sure, not really. But deeply unsettling, it left me with a quiet sense of dread as I watched something rise from the sea, or stood in front of imposing obelisk, purpose of which I was unable to understand. I feel like few games actually nail the cosmic horror. And despite its' lackluster gameplay and some frustrating action sequences, this one manages it.

_childDocuments_.review: To begin this review, let me say I was looking forward to playing this game since it came out and I saw a YouTube video showing the graphical quality/atmosphere - other than this one video I knew nothing else about the game - and I picked it up on sale for $5.I'm always down for some Lovecraftian horror - but when it's just Lovecraft for the sake of Lovecraft with no real cohesive story or purpose, it may as well be a fun-house ride. There was a lot of Elder God-Name dropping and not much else in terms of story beats. First off - I loved the graphics, and most of the visuals. There were a lot of inconsistent moments in the story telling, and I ended up getting sick of the loading screens breaking up the action. Writing was weak - nothing wrong with non-English speaking developers creating games in English but hire a native English speaker/writer or get someone to help you with spell-checking to make the writing flow better and make things more comprehensible for the language you're creating the game in. Immediately takes me out of a game when I have to guess what someone was trying to say - especially in a game where you have the player collecting several pieces of written word to form the backstory.Sound design was rough at best (voice lines would randomly get louder and quieter without reason) and most of the time it seemed like the audio sliders in the menu had no effect on volume.In terms of game objectives - I often found myself just sprinting through while being chased by various random tentacle beasties and straight up guessing what I was supposed to be doing - definitely not a good sign for a game as linear as this. I got where I needed to go but having to guess so much and having items around the place that you can pick up and look at but not use for anything was tantamount to having empty drawers in horror games like Layers of Fear, or Outlast. The feeling of exploring and finding what you were looking for is fantastic but not when mired deeply in the illusion of choice and discoveryOverall, a pretty average experience. More like a collection of "oooo look at this elder god, and here's this guy too!" moments than any kind of cohesive, story driven experience. Had a lot of potential but fell short. All I can say is, I'm glad I didn't pay more than $5 for it and even then, I almost wish I hadn't.Props to the dev(s) for pushing this out and attempting to create something awe-inspiring and terrifying but I hope they learnt a lot from this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The Skinny: if there was ever such a thing as flawed genius, The Shore is surely it!Pros: - The story is solid- The sound punches way above the weight for an indie game- The visuals are STUNNING- The atmosphere is incredible.- This game is absolute must have and must play for any Lovecraft enthusiastCons- The controls can be iffy, and that's being generous- Movement feels stiff; how the game reigns the player in the play area can feel jarring- Some of the bit and pieces (important bits and pieces at that!) feel very poorly put togetherThe bottom line: it's a buy, if only just. Be sure to pick it up if you're a Lovecraft fan, you will take to it even more. If you are into horror in general, this is still a solid pick up, although expect more story and atmosphere than true 'survival horror'.Know for the "TL;DR" rant ...The Good:Wow, where do I begin? How about with the story ... The Shore transports you to a "Lost" setting (and I do mean the TV show), an island ripped out of time where the supernatural reins supreme. You're looking for your daughter, lost in this surreal setting for unknown reasons (at least, I don't know them yet, but I haven't finished it). There is plot aplenty, as you explore abandoned ships, a light house, and other more exotic structures; you collect messages in bottles, letter, photographs, and bric-a-brac that gives you context for the setting.As you progress, you meet quite the assortment of H.P. Lovecraft myths, monsters, and gods. If you're a Lovecraft fan, this is for you (honestly, I like this more than Call of Cthulhu, see below). If you're into Kaiju, you'll get a kick out it too. If you like amazing, atmospheric horror, where you feel like you could just be squashed by anything, this is for you. If you're looking for real, hard-core survival horror ... well, that's here for sure, but don't expect Alien: Isolation. This isn't super great for someone who really wants a super technical challenge.Probably The Shore's greatest strength is it's atmosphere it creates. The visuals are absolutely amazing, absolutely lush. This thing is a work of absolute beauty, dark art on a computer canvas. Every fleshy tentacle, every alien sky, every horrible abomination is a dream come true for the devotee of Nyarlathotep. Even more incredible are the sound effects and music. This game punches way, way above it's weight in that department. Seriously, the programmer who wrote this knows how to make a menacing sound track that is eerie and beautiful, and sounds that make you cringe in the best possible way.I have played, and not completed, Call of Cthulhu, the 2018 game. It obviously had a much bigger budget, a much larger scope, and was produced by a large programming house. For all of its bells and whistles, for all of it's more sophisticated and modern physics engine, it just doesn't pack the punch that this does. I think that The Shore just kept it simpler, really. It concentrates more effort at delivering just a menacing, punch-in-the-face experience, not worrying about tracking how crazy you are (for example).The Bad: Of course, if you've made it this far, you know that I've called this game a work of flawed genius. The first thing you have to know is that you really are exploring a setting. There is combat, you can die, there is that survival component, but it's not Alien:Isolation or Dead Space. There's no deep resource management, no crafting anything (which for me is much more of a plus at this point ... everybody is doing crafting nowadays, can we please knock it the heck off already???). So if you're looking for that, look elsewhere. Also, though not too-huge a deal but, if you miss a clue, you may not be able to advance to the next bit until you find it. It hearkens back to the old days, where the game didn't tell you exactly where to go all the time. That's both a blessing (I'm tired of the hand-holding) and a curse (DAMN IT, I missed that clue and I was stuck for fifteen damn minutes!!!!).There are some bits and bobs that feel like they could've used more work. I don't want to ruin anything, but there is a device in particular that fires a beam of energy that, to me, feels like an old Win3.1 game special effect. It's a pretty central thing too. I don't get it ... a game that absolutely banks on it's atmosphere got cheap on one of the key features. But the worst part though is the game controls. They are wonky for sure ... holding down the shift key is suppose to make you run, but it doesn't always work. The way your character interacts with the world feels iffy. The rocks that make the zones that you can access at any given point don't feel very natural, and the way the game reigns you in the playable part of the world is just flat. The game engine is not a super up-to-date, top of the line affair, I promise you.Also, I lied: really, the worst part of the game for me requires explanation. There are parts where your character are in some truly terrible - and terribly beautiful - places. Usually, you're being chased by something equally terrible. Its great for creating tension but DAMN IT, I want to stop and look at the amazing, the GLORIOUSLY AMAZING scenery! And I can't!!!!! The Conclusion: I like this game. A lot. It's atmospheric and menacing, the two most important things for me in horror. I'm also a fan of horror in the style of Lovecraft. I realize that this game lacks a lot that the standard gamer is going to want - like a super, up-to-date, modern physics engine and hot, fast-paced action. While I get this is a deal breaker for some, I would encourage anyone to take a chance on this cool little, plot-driven indie horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Nice atmosphere and enticing visuals overrun by tedious design choices, simple mistakes and fanfiction writingExploration game with endless invisible walls. Story is no more complex than "I lost my daughter, I'm gonna go through a Lovecraft haunted house to get her back" and at no point did I care about the protagonist or his daughter. Lore conveyed through several message-in-a-bottles is a cool idea, but riddled with spelling errors. Notes also often have watermarks of the monsters you encounter and are assumedly drawings by the note's author, but are clearly just images of the actual models of the creatures.Once you leave the titular Shore the nice atmosphere and excusable errors are replaced with constant teleporting between rooms accompanied by the disembodied narration of a kid trying to deepen his voice on Xbox Live. Run away from a monster that is either faster than you or laughable, fade to black, next room. Complete a puzzle that consists of "put object on pedestal, hold left click on thing using the artifact", fade to black, next room. This seems to only serve to pad the run time.As previously mentioned, the Lovecraft mythos is reduced to a haunted house of characters from stories. This seems like a new developer that is clearly passionate about the mythos and wants to include every character possible, but they have lost the meaning of the work along the way. The infinitely large forces of nature that existed formlessly and incomprehensibly by men now screech and pose like Godzilla before riding away into the sunset on an obelisk.The positive aspects are really strong, but are dragged down so badly I couldn't come to finish it. Apologies for my harshness, I understand this is a new developer and their effort is commendable, but I believe this kind of harsh but fair (I hope) critique is important for artists and will only benefit you in the long run.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended only with heavy caveats.  I absolutely love a good horror walking simulator. It's like a haunted house: immersive atmosphere + light scares + few frustrations = pure thrills. I started out thoroughly enjoying the atmosphere, from the beautifully desolate shoreline to the lonely, mangled skeletons, to the creepy ritual sites. Then about halfway through they introduced some clunky combat mechanics (being able to beat the spawn of eldritch horrors, for me, defeats half the horror of eldritch horrors) and I started just wanting to be done with this BS so I didn't have to go through it again. Dying over and over because you're not sure where to go for the next warp, which monsters are killable and which aren't, or you're getting stuck on the scenery is not fun. A few of the load-points are really freaking far back too. Fortunately the game is short enough to push through.  Go in for the atmosphere, but don't be surprised to find yourself flipping to a walkthrough before the end.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a game, it's art.Fantastic visuals, fantastic audio, fantastic pace.It drives you in a world of great imagination, with non standard artwork representing a great, never seen presentation of the Chutullu universe. It may be short, the few action  moments, item search puzzels and texture popups may be annoying, but for person you are interested in the Chutullu mythos or/and are walking simulator fans it is a must play.  Full price may be expensive, but i absolut recommend playing the game if you can get on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Like most the other reviews the first hour was absolutely stunning giving the true feeling of being in the Cthulhu Mytho's. However, like other have said there is a dive in quality with the second half. They added enemies that chased you and you couldn't truly kill with some being faster making them more of a nuisance compared to an actual threat. This takes away from the mystery and exploration and overall didn't add to the fear and instead made it more of a monster horror game compared to a psychological horror game. While you might say "well aren't the beings in the Cthulhu Mytho's monsters" to that I say "yes" but remember the fear they create is due to them not needing to do anything physical to scare us. So by adding a monster that physically attacks you it takes away from that general aspect of the unknown of being that don't need physical involvement to scare and kill us. This doesn't break the deal for me however as even with those flaws being 50% was a must buy for me with how much I love the Cthulhu Mytho's.TDLR Amazing start with decline in the ending hour (story only takes 2 hours to complete) if your a lore junkie and hate incorrect representations of these characters (in personality, motive, and power) then I would steer clear of this however this doesn't take away from the fact that it was made by a team of 10 or so people and only cost $12 base and lower on sale. So if you aren't gonna be angry in the later half at the shift in gameplay and lore consistency. I think its worth the sale price not sure about full though. However, if your super into the Mytho's and just need more content then this will satisfy that itch for the most part. Now to the more boring story issues which include spoilers so you have been warnedWhile I understand he was looking for his daughter which was driving his exploration of the shore. Once you first enter the different dimension they start to lose pace and direction because even after completing it I'm still confused to who was talking to the protagonist. Throughout the story the watcher is mentioned multiple times and from what i assume they are referencing Yog which is all fine and good but once you finally meet Cthulhu he mentions the "Traitor" which he then clarifies by saying Nyarlathotep which really confused me because Nyarlathotep is way stronger than Cthulhu in almost every way so to say Cthulhu was stopping Nyarlathotep from doing something is lowering Nyarlathotep. Great Old Ones even Cthulhu don't even come close to power to the Outer Elder gods. It is often said Great Old Ones view humans as we see ants. The same can be said for how elder gods view great old ones. So trying to give the impression that Cthulhu is stopping Nyarlathotep from doing something is a pretty big plot-hole, and even if you were relying on new players being the main audience they wouldn't understand who any of them are so mentioning Nyarlathotep as a traitor would only further confuse them. At the end it bring the good old "it was never real" trope in which makes since in the universe but that means he never had a daughter which "fine" Ill accept it, but a human cant influence Azathoth which means he would have to have been a creating of Nyarlathotep to do so again leading to another plot-hole because as a i said above Cthulhu cant stop Nyarlathotep.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is an atmospheric story-driven walking simulator game. It does offer some solid Puzzle-solving missions and some combat as well which is pretty unique for a game of this genre. The game was developed and published by  which is a small studio.Release Date: 19th February 2021.Last known update: 5th March 2021.I mean I can easily understand that a lot of work got thrown into this game but looking at the price from a consumer standpoint I will have to say that this is a little high for a game with a 2-3 hour story. There isn’t much replay value either. The story is obviously pretty good as well as the overall feeling of the game but once again the asking price is a little high for my liking and I would honestly suggest waiting for a sale (at least 50%) in order to get this pretty solid game.Once again this game is mainly a walking sim where you explore the beautifully crafted island but there are some puzzles and combat sections in this short game that are pretty okay in my opinion.As mentioned The Shore takes place on a mysterious island and the map is basically built for exploration. It is a pretty linear map without you really realizing it really quickly. The map might look as if you can go wherever you want but this just isn’t true. Some rocks and areas have invisible walls or you cannot even climb these areas. This does make the map seem a lot smaller than it actually is simply because I cannot go and explore all of the areas. Luckily there are still a lot of things to explore and find as there are small items such as letters inside of bottles or small mementos of various creatures.Puzzles are a usual sight in this game, most of them are pretty straightforward and do not require much thought behind them. Usually, you will have to take the corresponding symbol or statue and match it up with the bigger version of it or something identical. The puzzles do actually do a decent job and they will not feel like a chore and a timewaster which is always a positive in my eyes. Now combat sure as hell isn’t something that I would consider amazing but I think we should keep in mind that this is a story-focused walking simulator. Adding combat section made this game feel a little more realistic if you think about the entire story of fighting or running away from these creatures.Spoiler Free story section.The storyline is obviously the main selling point of the game. The characters are pretty memorable as the main character constantly mentions his backstory. Even the random letters you find inside of bottles tell detailed stories about each character which is a pretty nice addition. The entire map as well as the atmosphere it gives off is truly matching to the entire story as it really achieves that mysterious island type of vibe. What I really liked about the story is the plot twists that do happen in this game. Obviously I will not spoil anything but the game and its storyline have a nice slimax that will surely surprise a lot of players. Other than that I can only say that the story is a nice experience.Now the length of the story is an entire different discussion as I finished the story in just 2 hours despite going slow and taking a lot of time to see each detail in the map. Another thing is that replay value is almost non-existent in this game which basically makes this a one and done type of game. The quality is obviously very good but still, the amount of content is very very little.The game makes use of the well-known Unreal Engine 4 which is the main reason this game has such magnificent visuals. The Shore is a unique gamewith an amazing atmosphere, beautiful visuals and great voice acting. Sadly due to its short story and high price I will have to say that this game only makes sense in a good sale as the normal asking price is just too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though it was short & there were a few confusing moments of not knowing exactly where to go/invisible walls, as an huge Lovecraft fan, I really enjoyed this game. The atmosphere & mystery feel behind it IS what a game based on Lovecraft's work is supposed to be like. I honestly thought it would just be Cthulhu who would be appearing, (which would have been fine) but was very pleasantly surprised about the other Lovecraftian deities that appeared throughout the game, especially at the end. The alien puzzles were wonderfully bizarre, not so difficult that it's frustrating, but not too easy (some people may find them a bit too easy if they're avid puzzle solvers). I'd love to see some actual stories adapted into games with this much quality atmosphere & head tripping visuals as this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Followin' this project for a long time!and now that it's here...I say that the Wait was worth it!Okay, i'll be honest and admit the game came with some bugs and glitches, but i do believe it is excusable, not only 'cause of the small team (one guy basically did all the in-game stuff by himself) but also because in the following day fixes were already bein' issued.I played the entire game without finding somethin' game-breakin' or immersion-breakin', so not much of a problem either way!Now the game itself... it is Short.And that's a shame 'cause... the game's really good!this is the Biggest Lovecraft-Loveletter i have ever seen!Full of references, nods, creatures and locations from the Mythos!some that i never seen together with another one in any movie, book or game before!It is a small Lovecraftian experience that manages to condence an amazin' Eldritch Adventure in a single game!It is replayable, even if only to walk 'bout with that amazin' soundtrack!And it seems more content is on the way!SO COUNT ME IN!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game and the graphic is awesome... _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's kind of okay. Sort of. Maybe. Not really.It's a nice looking game and it's impressive if it's really just one guy that made all of it, but that's all it has going for it.Gameplay wise, it's a frustrating mess. It's pretty much a walking sim with a couple parts you defend against monsters. Even those parts are sort of trial and error, and honestly, really boring.The opening of the game works well as you search for clues and items; slowly building up tension and atmosphere. The item hunt does become tedious and there's a few "where the hell do I go?" moments, which becomes fairly annoying due to your character running at the pace of a snail and some of the areas being pretty large. Despite this the first third of the game is somewhat enjoyable. The next thing you know half of Lovecraft's bestiary is just thrown in to make an appearance whether it make sense or not. It gets to the point where the game simply becomes checklist of monsters to go through. Eventually I lost the Lovecraft atmosphere entirely and started to see more Beksiński or maybe Giger influence than anything. That's not too much the fault of the creator, as Lovecraftian aesthetics can be vague. I suppose an art style needed to be pulled from somewhere. Some design choices are questionable as well. Cthulhu seems kind of small, and I find it strange that he speaks at all. I believe Dagon was made around the same size. It may be nit-picky, but these are just choices that don't make sense.What little story there is unfortunately feels like it was ripped from one of those poor Lovecraft-inspired compilation books. That's really all can I say about it.Not trying to be overly harsh on this; it's a nice time waster for $6 and I'm sure this took a lot of work to accomplish for one person. The soundtrack is great. The opening is cool and it's really nice looking, but it's really lacking in all other aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: yeah its pretty and all, even captures the essence of Lovecraft's work. but its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ drag attempting to get past any point in the game because of it's lack of direction. regarding the laser artifact, half the time the game doesn't recognize that i'm trying to shoot it, which makes basic puzzles take longer than needed. at this point, i'm just gonna watch a lets play of this thing and free up some space on my hard drive.

_childDocuments_.review: I started it up and the first text box of the game featured a spelling error...that did not bode well.I was hoping for a slow paced Myst-like game or a walking sim in the Mythos, and the first portion of The Shore is that.  It was a clunky mess with invisible walls where there shouldn't be, and no walls where there should be, but it was serviceable.  While the game does feature some genuinely impressive moments, those get undercut by them going overboard and featuring virtually every creature from the Mythos.  Thus far, I wasn't super impressed, but I wasn't hating my time.THEN, you get to the monster fighting portion of the game which is simply unplayable.  Some monsters don't die, are faster than you, have a 50 foot reach, and you encounter multiple at once.  After dying 15 times in the same corridor even after trying to cheese them, I gave up.Had this been a $10 itchio game, I'd give it a thumbs up.  As a $25 Steam game, I will give it a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: A good Lovecraftian walking simulator, but a bit rough around the edges.Good:The models & setting. The developer is clearly very well versed at modeling characters.The bad: The developer decided to voice a bunch of parts himself, and the obvious accent kind of seems out of place. The hired voice actors are good, and it probably would have been better to hire a whole cast. Also the "game" mechanics felt forced and unnecessary. Too many invisible walls, and tinkering with objects and switches with no logic or reason about what they were or how they work. The ugly:Animations were a pass. They conveyed the idea just fine, but at some times seemed twitchy or way to smooth. Also almost everything including the player clipped through walls.Overall the visuals of the game were decent, but a lot of small details brought me out of the immersion at times. The game certainly has an "indie" feel to it, so I suppose you get what you pay for. That said, I hope this game is successful enough to get another. The developer has a good mind of this and given a larger team, better resources and a little luck I could see him creating some very interesting games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interactive spectacle, not really a game. It has some great visual set pieces, but the game itself is poorly crafted. Lots of invisible walls in otherwise open spaces, lots of clipping into terrain, character walks painfully slow. Strictly linear paths with no exploration. Several 2-3 second cutscenes all unrelated to one another showing different creatures and not explained.  Feels like someone took all their student work and stuffed it into one thing. If you're a diehard Eldritch / Cthulhu fan, you'll probably like this. Otherwise, steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: An Enigmatic Journey Through the Uncharted - "The Shore"ReviewOverall Rating: 9/10"The Shore" is a first-person horror adventure game developed by Ares Dragonis and published by Dragonis Studio. This indie title offers players an immersive and atmospheric experience that delves into Lovecraftian horror and cosmic mysteries while exploring the enigmatic world of a deserted island.Storyline : 8/10The game follows the journey of Andrew, a man in search of his missing daughter, who stumbles upon a mysterious and foreboding island. As he explores the island's eerie landscapes and encounters otherworldly beings, he unravels a complex narrative that blends elements of cosmic horror and psychological torment. "The Shore" stands out for its captivating storytelling, and it keeps players engaged with its intriguing and enigmatic plot.Gameplay : 7/10"The Shore" emphasizes exploration, puzzle-solving, and a sense of dread rather than action-packed gameplay. The puzzles are well-crafted and contribute to the game's overall sense of mystery. However, some players may find the pacing slow, and a few mechanics might feel a bit clunky at times. Nevertheless, the game's eerie ambiance and intriguing world make up for these minor shortcomings.Graphics and Atmosphere : 9/10Visually, "The Shore" is a striking game. The island's environments are beautifully rendered, and the attention to detail in its eerie landscapes is impressive. The lighting and sound design work harmoniously to create a palpable atmosphere of dread and wonder, immersing players in the otherworldly island setting.Horror Elements : 8/10The game excels in delivering a slow-burning, psychological horror experience. It relies on unsettling visuals, eerie soundscapes, and a sense of impending doom to build tension. "The Shore" effectively captures the essence of Lovecraftian horror, making you question the nature of reality and your own sanity as you delve deeper into the island's secrets.Conclusion : 9/10"The Shore" is a captivating and atmospheric indie horror game that manages to create a compelling Lovecraftian narrative and a sense of unease. Its well-executed storytelling, stunning visuals, and psychological horror elements make it a must-play for fans of the genre. While the gameplay may not be action-packed and could use a bit more polish, the overall experience is hauntingly satisfying. If you enjoy thought-provoking horror games that immerse you in a world of cosmic mysteries and existential dread, "The Shore" is an island worth exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game, I'm changing my review to a negative one. That's because after the incredible opening hour, the game takes MASSIVE nosedive in quality. The titular shore is incredibly atmospheric and immersive, to the point my initial review called it "the most atmospheric game I've ever played" - and to about half point of the game that is true.But later on we trade the moody, misty seashore for a more otherworldly environments, and those are less than stellar. Confusing, murky, repetitive. And the game starts trowing chase sequences at you. Again, and again, and again. It's seriously the only gameplay trick in its book, and those are done horribly - they're confusing, repetitive, and so overturned that I had to restart each of them at least 10 times.The atmosphere also goes to ♥♥♥♥. Long gone are quiet moment and environmental storytelling. The game becomes an endless gallery of monsters shown of with little buildup and fanfare. I truly was done with the game when it introduced Cthulhu, in a scene that lacks any semblance of buildup of pathos, and he started monologing about "mere mortals" and "seeing my world destroyed" in an accent so thick that I believe it to be the developer himself. It seriously felt like a joke.I do not recommend The Shore. Not because its without merit - parts of it are truly great- but because of how disappointing it is. It will take me a couple of days to get that anger out of my system, this could have been something truly special.
