_childDocuments_.review: Voice acting was good, visuals are great (especially for an indie game), music was atmospheric as well. The gameplay could use some work though, movement was quite janky and some of the puzzles didn't require much thought which made them feel like filler. The premise of the plot is really good, but without spoiling anything I personally thought that the payoff was lacking, relying on a Shamalan style gotcha moment to conclude the story. I also didn't like how for much of the game I couldn't access or interact with the items I had collected, even when there would have been room in the plot to allow for it. _childDocuments_.review: Don't get irritated by the many 'not recommended' reviews. I was mostly worried about the length of the game, but to me length and scope of the game was sufficent. Yeah, it's a rather short game, but it's okay.You can play it through in under 2 hours for sure, if you want to, but I have taken a lot of time to explore the game. Unfortunately you are quite narrowed down to relatively small accessable areas with (too) many invisible walls, but all in all there was quite a bit of content.I liked the rough sea atmosphere and that the story was told via several documents and letters which are spreaded all over the shore etc. I hoped that all those information pieces would in the end puzzle together to a whole story picture, what they unfortunately did not. This is a story-driven game and the potential is great and it is well done in the beginning. But during the second half of the game the story gets lost a bit and the focus is more on horror elements and spectacular monsters. Those are very nice, but story should be most important!Otherwise I really liked to play it. Very good voice acting and graphics are overall pretty good (except of constant graphics glitches in the water or occasional blurry rock textures and not so dense vegetation). Battles were not very tricky or demanding, but those action scenes were a must for me to make more out of the game than only being a walking simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: As intersting as this game looked on paper, unfortunately after playing it cannot help but feeling underwhelmed.The overall concept behind this adventure is neat enough, and there are interesting design choices. The island itself has this ominous and timeless atmosphere, and the feeling of loneliness is heavy... however, we dont' really get to explore much of the island itself, despite it seeming it rather big! Now that would not be a problem if the landscape looked more... unfriendly? instead, if you stray from the intended path, you'll simply run into an invisible wall, preventing you from wandering too far. It breaks the immersion and feels like a waste. Why not put some physical barriers instead? Chasms, thick bushes, rocky spikes, and the likes.The second part of the game, once you acquire the artifact, feels... rushed? You solve a puzzle, hear some otherwordly sound, and then just fade-to-black to some other place. This happens several times and transition once again is very immersion breaking: instead of getting the wormhole-like sequence we get sometimes, we are instead treated with a transition with black spots filling up the screen. Why not choose a less artificial transition?The Lovecraft mythos also is implemented a bit superficially. Names get thrown here and there, but the things that do happen feel rather inconsequential. It's... not clear why you do the things you do, or how the puzzles relate to the things that happen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing Lovecraft experience, the eldritch settings and creatures are fantastic and the excellent soundtrack creates a perfect atmosphere. The movement feels stiff and a bit off but it's clear that the dev has put a lot of effort into the game. If I could change one thing it would be the chase sequences, they were frustrating at times and didn't fit the pacing of the rest of the game.In it's current state I'd say it's worth full price if you're a fan of cosmic horror and want to support the dev, otherwise wait for a sale but it's worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game.  It's not what I hoped, though.  I hoped for some adventure game with multiple endings and branching stories with hard choices to be made in dialogue, siding with this person or faction vs the other.Instead, I got a walking simulator with plenty of H.P. Lovecraft references in it.  A nice little game.  The devs really tried to keep the mystique and not overplay the grotesque too early.  Some puzzles were actually clever.However, I also join other in criticizing the running segments.  The 'obstacles' are too aggressive and fast.  Slow them down so there's no RNG deaths and this is a nice, humble little story to be told.2.7 hours to finish the base game.  Another 0.7 hours to start a second playthrough to collect the missing collectibles for 100% completion.  I got this on sale for $12 and I'm happy with it.  I do not recommend the full price of $25 as it's not polished enough and just a tiny bit light on content for that price.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game recently and as someone who enjoys the works of Lovecraft, I felt like this game had some ups and downs. The setting was good, reminded me of the story Dagon a bit which was nice. However being met with a ton of invisible walls and odd inability to walk over objects any person could raise their leg to step over was annoying. I really wanted to discover the island more as the protag that just crashed there looking for his daughter. The first half of this for me really dragged. While the monolith and seeing the sea monster from the lighthouse were cool, there were many things just thrown in there for no reason. The meteorite from the Color out of space felt so disconnected if you read the story of color out of space. In addition they threw in the pillar from Utah or something next to a giant black orb that as far as I know was pointless to the story and felt threw in for "OOOOO SPOOKY WHAT COULD IT BE" without capturing the fear of the unknown whatsoever. Tossing in Dagon, Deep ones, Cthulhu, Azathoth, Nyarlathotep, the and all this extra monsters made it feel like a show and tell. For the story, using a mortal to ♥♥♥♥ around with things was interesting but, the ending twist just felt like a pointless slap in the face. While the dimensions were interesting and its setting was nice, the lack of exploration that railroaded me into the strange story. I didn't hate it and the fact it was made by such a small team was impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently it's mostly developed by one guy, and it's also his first game.Very enjoyable music and art design all across the board. They did a fairly good job making an immersive Lovecraftian experience, but even for its price tag it left me underwhelmed.The gaming experience as a whole was weak and short, with annoying level design and combat mechanics that are so poorly executed that I was constantly questioning why this is even in the game. Puzzles didn't feel rewarding, the story didn't engage me, and the immersion broke because of the transition (and teleporting) between scenes. _childDocuments_.review: Good sides :- Great atmospheric game. Big spaces, impressive and awe-inspiring landscapes.- Puzzles in general are satisfying : you get into them with no explanation but you never really find yourself not knowing what you're supposed to do. They're not "easy" but not convoluted either.- Love all the references to Lovecraft's works.My personal criticisms :- Big spaces make for a lot of walking, and it can be frustrating to walk all the way back when you feel like you've forgotten or missed something somewhere.- I would love to see the game have more achievements and easter eggs. All these empty spaces and deadends are wonderful opportunities to plant a plot piece that tells me 1. I didn't walk all the way there for nothing, and 2. Yes, I found all there was to be found in that corner, I didn't oversee anything and I don't have to come back. As it is, a lot of open spaces are just rocks, bushes and waves, and sometimes you're not really sure if a pile of rocks is supposed to be climbed on or not. Again, not bad per se as it contributes to the space feeling aerated and the player feeling small in comparison. Just a bit of a missed opportunity.Other comments :- This is not a classic Lovecraftian game, in the sense that you get very close to the "monsters" and they feel like they have human emotions and goals. They're tangible, they speak English, in short, they're not really Great Old Ones, they're just very big harbingers of doom.- It's weird to not have a sanity bar going down when you stare at monstrosities.

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with the negative comments. Game was good for the first 20 minutes. After that it's trash. It's a shame, game had so much potential. At some point I actually had goose pimples. But once you have to run from monsters pointing the triangle at them - tedious, annoying and frustrating. All immersion is gone. Plus, if you die on your first chase sequence, before you own the triangle, you will be re spawned way too far away AND facing the opposite direction plus running is disabled - takes ages to get to the place you died in, just so you can die again. Why the hell is checkpoint so far away? I didn't bother completing the game. I was too annoyed with having to point triangle at 2 monsters simultaneously while navigating a labyrinth of corridors walking backwards, listening to monster sounds repeating on a short loop. Such a shame, it was SO GOOD the first 20 mins. Eerie, uneasy, immersive... But also, too short as apparently I have missed out on a couple of things as I learned from watching a play through online. _childDocuments_.review: So here's my honest review for The Shore.First of all, we need to give a big applause to Ares for actually making the game. As an indie dev myself, I've started countless of projects but it takes so long to finish them all by yourself that you will most likely quit at some point. Ares kept going and he actually finished it, you sir have my respect! But wait there's more! Ares and his small team are releasing constant updates. So any bugs and glitches mentioned before this review are either fixed or will get fixed soon enough.The Shore is a mystery / exploration type of game based on the Cthulhu Mythos of the one and only H. P. Lovecraft. If that theme is your cup of tea skip my review and buy it now, you'll be supporting an indie dev and not some triple-A cash grab company (I'm looking at you Bethesda)!But let's go to the actual review now:Graphics---------Wait, are you sure this is an indie game? The graphics are fantastic! Sure it can get a bit dark at some points and the UI needs some work but overall I'm stunned and I'm sure that they will improve the UI soon enough.Music / SFX-------------It's OK nothing fancy here but it works well with the game.Narration----------The narration is amazing! It gets you involved in the story as soon as you start the game.Gameplay-----------As I mentioned before, if you like mystery/exploring type of games and you're into the "Great Old Ones", I'm sure you'll love it! If you only like pew pew stuff then most probably the game is not for you.Bonus points for: subtitles (probably they will translate the game in many other languages soon), constant updates, the boat resting at the shore named "Argyro" which is exactly like the small fishing wooden boat that my grandfather used to have... named "Argyro" as well! (I'm not crying, you're crying).Overall: a solid 8/10Not part of the actual review, but I'd really love to

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this knowing nothing about the game aside from watching a trailer.+New to Lovecraft, top notch audio/visual creature design from my perspective.+Atmospheric, immersive setting is really well done.+Even things that I literally saw coming still scared the pants off of me --- outstanding for this alone.-Almost criminally short considering the price, so I cannot recommend at full price. Price aside, some elements that I thought would get stale did not, as the game was over with before that happened. Silver lining I suppose. -Unpolished or incomplete feeling at times, with regards to some gameplay elements, level design, audio glitches, voicing, and graphical settings & performance. Nothing too egregious, but enough to notice.-Story felt pretty vague and generic to me (I know nothing of whether it references or relies on Lovecraft's original works), and it seemed to be more a prop to make a fairly disconnected protagonist walk through it all rather than to add anything to experience.Verdict: Absolutely get it, but get it on sale and be thrilled and/or terrified for an evening.

_childDocuments_.review: A meagre 5 out of 10. To be honest, I deinstalled the game after 1.5 hours, I don't know how much longer it would have gone, but it had already started to annoy me about one hour in.Don't let yourself be fooled by the beginning and the visuals. Yes, both are great, but the rest of the game is not only very different but also ... just bad.While there is some semblance of a story in the beginning (shipwrecked on an island, searching for your daughter), it soon becomes clear that it is a mere varnish. It's really only two bucket loads of disconnected Cthulhu mythos icons, words and creatures all over the place, without any coherence or story telling about what happened here, what the point of it all is or what to do.After the mostly engaging beginning you are finding yourself fleeing from enemies, searching for exists, shooting a laser beam from some artifact weapon. And when they reach you, the screen flickers red and you die. There are some puzzles. Then more tunnels and fleeing from enemies. More laser beams. That’s when I deinstalled it. Nothing about this is scary or mysterious or engaging. I bought this on sale for 2.50, so it's fine, no reason to refund, but it still is nothing more than a pretty good starting scenario, like a proof of concept, for an unfinished game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a "horror" game with a lot of "jump scares"... or a "horror" game with a lot of "action" in it... then this isn't a game for you. However... I don't think you're here because that's what you're looking for. I think you came here for the same reason I did... you're a fan of H.P. Lovecraft. If that's the case... then you're in the right place. This is a nicely done lore based game... where you can read up on the Old Gods from Lovecrafts mythos... and actually see a few of them in all their glory. It took me about three and a half hours roughly to get through the game... and I wasn't disappointed at any point in the experience. There are a few puzzles you can complete... and there's some fighting... but this game is a heavily story driven walking simulator. I wouldn't recommend this for fans of the "action horror" or "survival horror" genres... but fans of Lovecraft and most of the psychological horror community might find something interesting here (especially if you get the VR version of this game instead of the standard version).

_childDocuments_.review: This game's strength lie in its artwork. The island is quite bland to begin with but as you delve deeper into the cosmic realm you get to see some amazing and repulsive sights. A great deal of attention has gone into many of the sculptures of Cthulu mythos gods that appear as items in this game. They are beautiful to look at and I actually would probably buy one of those sculptures if it existed in the real world. The game music and sounds, especially later on in the game really fit with the atmosphere of the game.However, the game is short. I played it in 3 hours. This isn't necessary a bad thing if you go into the game considering it a piece of art. It might also be better playing this in VR if that becomes possible. One thing that really rubbed me the wrong way with this game and caused me great frustration were the invisible walls. I understand that this type of game has to limit my movements in the game but they could have been handled with a bit less abruptness. There were also quite a few glitches. Floating stones, spelling mistakes and at one point I even had to restart the game from the save point because a bug stopped me progressing.Overall, if you want a game that assaults your visionary senses, a thin plot, has you run from enemies to get to the next puzzle, but will still show you some sights you've not seen in a game before, you might want to try this one. The fact that it was done by one person or a small group of people, at least, made me want to buy this game. I think this game could have been so much more though. It feels like a patchwork of scenes that don't quite fit together but it was an interesting ride.

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is gloomy. The sounds are eerie. The art is absolutely stunning. Mind that I called it art, not graphics. And that's why. Landscapes are amazing. Details in everything are incredible. Animations are, well, embarassing. You see the walking monolith in the trailer? Isn't it embarassing? Yes, it is. I also caught a glimpse of a tentacled thing behind a rock, I tried to see what it was despite being scared, but it was gone as I tried to get close, all I can say it was a ridicuolus shiny green color. I shudder at the thought of action sequences, but the setting got me hooked.Another thing I loathe: railroad movment. You know, being confined by rocks so amazingly tall and steep that a three legged turtle could easily climb them but you can't.Edit. My judgement was positive until now. But then I met a Deep one chewing a whale's tail. There's no way to evade it (the surrounding rocks are almost a foot tall, totally unsurmountable), no way to go back. The whale is a pin cushion of harpoons but sure as Hell nobody would think about taking one to defend against the nasty looking critter who is about to attack. There's a limit to my tolerance of not-being-able-to-do-anything. I'm sure there are a couple of pixels somewhere that I should notice to solve the puzzle, but I don't care anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't call this a game per se but more of an experience tailored around HP Lovecraft's work and legacy. I would definitely point to the graphics and soundtrack as a strong point since they do a great job of creating a sense of ominous dread, but the caveat is that the game is horribly optimized so you'll experience some unwanted technical issues (i.e frame rate dips/stuttering) which take away from the immersion. I was not a fan of the voice acting but it was serviceable and the puzzles were a bit too simple for my taste... but again, you're not buying this game for challenging game mechanics, but rather to experience the cosmic horror Lovecraft is famous for. I would only recommend this game if you're at all interested in the Cthulhu mythos.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-	Art design: Lovecraftian mythos is truly impressive. A lot of effort went into making the huge creatures very detailed.-	Length: 2-3 hours might sound short, but I think it’s just perfect to show everything the game has to offer. -	Achievements: encourages exploration because some items are optional and add some lore. All can be gained in a single playthrough. Cons:-	Item hunting: some items are very small and hard to find. There’s no glow or anything that would help them stand out.-	Shooting/running sequences: although the opportunity to defend yourself in walking sims doesn’t come often, it feels like it was shoved in in this game. Running sections surprise you; if you don’t start running in the right direction, you won’t be able to outrun the monster coming after you.-	Disjointed and linear gameplay: after the impressive start at the lighthouse, you go through a lot of scene switching with no context or story. You're on a beach one moment and then fleeing away from a monster in a maze the next.-	Invisible walls: when you can only walk in a specific area despite the obvious flat and open world, it leaves a sour taste in your mouth. You're forced to take longer paths and search for an object rather than simply walking around the rock.-	Unoptimized and some graphic bugs: most walking sims done with Unreal engine have this problem. They have a habit of consuming far more resources than are actually required. Also noticed some rocks and birds hovering in midair. Despite the shortcomings, The Shore has some fun moments. It's definitely not boring like other walking sims. I bet a better connection between disjointed sections would give it a few more bonus points.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a long video on Youtube looking at a number of games set in the genre and asking why it's so hard if not impossible to get Lovecraftian Horror right in computer games. Won't post the link, but it's easy to search for.The point is that this game does nothing to break the chain of "nope, this ain't it". While it covers eery, creepy, haunted with some great sound, music and beautiful graphics, it shoots itself in the foot with all the force of an FPS.Invisible walls everywhere: they actually gave me motion sickness because they are so jarring and then force your character into weird lateral motion that my inner ear couldn't cope with what my eyes were telling my brain. Talk about playing games and chewing gum at the same time! You don't get to enjoy some of the most fascinating scenes and graphics: you go from carefully and methodically studying your environs to running away from some monster that will kill your unarmed toon in 3 hits. It has zombies - the most overused trope in games and one that is pretty much non-existent in HPL.Mind you, I haven't even finished the game. I'm about an hour or so in and not even sure I'll finish it. Maybe if I discover a god mode cheat that let's me just continue to look at the surroundings while ignoring some annoying pest to try and stomp me into paste. Shockingly, going by some of the walk-through video time markers as reference I'm already halfway through! The hell? Anything I've done so far would barely count as tutorial or prologue in a proper game!

_childDocuments_.review: Really impressive visuals and set pieces, despite the small team. Some of the "puzzles" felt a bit incoherent (the room with the heads on the floor being the worst), but nothing I couldn't really brute force my way through. Combat sections felt a bit tacked on, and I wish the artifact had a bit more "umph" to it in terms of audio and enemy impact. I did like that it was basically a Quake lightning gun though in terms of its functionality. Other than that, I think the overall audio design and voice acting is pretty good for an indie title. There's some pretty deeply unsettling sounds in this game.I finished the game in about 2.3hrs, but also got it on sale for $3.59, so I felt I got my moneys worth. The story kind of takes a backseat to the actual gameplay experience, but I enjoyed the constant sense of mystery and dread. I love that it's a Lovecraftian game that gets straight to the point and doesn't let off the gas. There are some collectibles and achievements, some of which are missable, so there is a tiny bit of replayability if you want to 100% it. I'd recommend picking it up on sale.Minor gripes (bug report for the devs): -Fullscreen option isn't selectable (have to use borderless)-Voice volume setting doesn't really seem to change anything. Voiceover volume was still a bit all over the place.-Changing pretty much any setting, or Alt+tabbing while playing caused me to be locked in place when exiting the menu/returning to the game (couldn't move camera or character) - hitting ESC twice was a workaround.-Discord Server invite link on the main screen is invalid ("may be expired, or you might not have permission to join")

_childDocuments_.review: GRADE: C+. The Shore is really more of a First Person VR Visual Novel. Its a chill game where you explore a creepy island straight outta Lovecraft's wildest dreams. Even when played without the VR set its  still optimized for keyboard and mouse, but its does get a little extra Shiny when you play through a VR head set. The Best thing about his game is the atmosphere and the stunning visuals. The Puzzles and actual game play are both pretty easy and I beat the game and got all the achievements in about 4 hours. However that's probably the right portion size for this game and it kept it from getting old, and since i didnt pay too much im happy enough with it.   The Shore is a walking simulator/visual novel steeped in the unsettling lore of H.P. Lovecraft. The game uses characters and references from his expanded mythos, crafting an eerie atmosphere that sets a creepy tone that does right by the subject matter. The Story is interesting but vague and not everyone will be pleased with the way it is concluded. Still there are some very striking parts of this game (especially in VR) and Some of the visuals are mind-bendingly awesome Also be prepared for some genre whiplash. The first act unfolds like a classic first-person point-and-click adventure. As you explore the environment you collect items and bits of story while solving puzzles. Click this, grab that, piece together some eldritch backstory. But the second act just throws you into a series of static scenes and adds some rudimentary combat. While its not inherently bad its just basic and these elements feel a bit out of place compared to the slow-burn exploration of the first act. Still some of the most memorable parts of the game are presented in these scenes. Overall i felt it was worth the handful of hours it took to run through this game. But i cant see why i would ever play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Short and simple: I loved this game! If you like Lovecraft and his universe of unspeakable horros, this game will push all the right buttons for you. Atmosphere and graphics are great, it has voice acting (which can be a bit funny because of the russian accent, but that's just the way the person speaks, and it's only a handful of people who did this game, so cut them some slack!) and there is no part which feels like dragging on or which is unneccessary.I can understand the reviews that give a thumbs down because of the price, because 20$ for 3 hours of gameplay (1 or 2 more if you get all achievements) can feel pretty unbalanced. All I can say is: If you can spare the money and want to have great 4 hours, get this game! If not, wait for a Sale at some point and get it for cheaper.But it is a project from a handfull of people, and I can't imagine the effort and time they took to create this game. And I think there are worse ways out there to spend 20$.The FPS drops and technical issues that people complain about are mostly fixed as far as I can tell. I played the whole game yesterday (2nd of march 2021) and didn't run into any problems while playing it, and I saw in the forums that the devs work on patches and fixes constantly to improve the experience, which already helped a lot.So yeah, I had a ton of fun, the graphics are great and the enemy design is top notch. Puzzles are mostly pretty basic and easy, and battle mechanics are just "press button to shoot laser at enemy", but the fighting isn't the focus here and therefore the majority of battles are over quickly, so it doesn't bother too much.

_childDocuments_.review: The design and many details are a treat for Lovecraft fans. Unfortunately, the gameplay is awful.The "puzzles" consist of either menial chores or finding very tiny objects in the landscape. Some clickable items require you to be in a very specific position and angle. There is nothing thoughtful about these puzzles, nothing for you to figure out. And you'll be scrambling back and forth and back and forth a lot to "solve" them.The other kinds of challenges involve chases. Something is running after you and you have to not let it catch you. They are annoying rather than horrific.And the game's whole structure is very lopsided. The first third of the game is far more interesting, with notes to read and objects to examine, an actual story. But then it just plummets into a series of disjointed scenes that seem more like individual demos than components of a game.If this had been a linear "walking simulator" it would have been an easy thumbs up. Instead, the attempt to turn it into a puzzle game has produced a frustrating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I received THE SHORE as a gift from my partner. I am usually a fan of anything Lovecraftian, so I do not know, how it went undetected by me for so long. Probably because it is a “small” game, which by no means is a bad thing.Positive:+ The story of the game is short but great. It worked well with the tone the Lovecraftian works have and while fans of those do of course know what they deal with, I found it to be very captivating and entertaining. + The visual aesthetics are really good. Of course, there is some clipping here and there or a floating small rock, but altogether the textures, effects and placements are neatly done. The animation of the creatures and environment is beautiful, although the walking animation of the human (Andrew) is a bit clunky in comparison. + The Audio (music and effect sounds) is nice to listen at, not too loud and thematic. The voice-acting is really good. I enjoyed it a lot. Neutral:> The mechanics and controls are very simple. Some like it, some don’t. > The game is short (around 3-5h)). It’s nice to have a game that I simply can turn on and play without investing days of gaming in it, to somewhat get started. But of course, since I think it was a nice game, I am a bit sad that the journey is over already. > The game has two parts. The first being more of an explorative walking simulator with little lore snippets and puzzles to solve. Some are a bit challenging, while most stay very casual. As a fan of puzzles, it is a bit too casual for my liking, but I see the point of making it approachable to as many people as possible. That said, I still had a lot of fun exploring and solving. The second part however dives a little deeper into survival-horror-action stuff. The horror, for my taste, is mild, though there were one or two points, where I actually got a little scared (mainly because I hate failing though). Negative:- The keyboard controls are not changeable (at least it didn’t work for me). Not a big problem, though I like to place keys as I want to have them. - With the second part being a lot more action then the first, there were almost no real puzzles to solve and with hardly enough time for me to enjoy the environment while I ran from whatever the game threw at me. Some might like the change of pace, but I did not. I’d rather have played the whole game like the first part. It did an excellent job there while the second half just seemed to lack stuff. I went through with it, because the story was still worth it. - The fighting mechanic is very simplified and I wouldn’t have needed it at all. But that’s on me. With everything said, I really recommend this game. I had a lot of fun playing it and probably will do again. I am impressed with what was created here. The creator did an amazing job!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The game's premise, visuals and concept stand out a lot compliment the Lovecraft aspect of them, even with certain flaws and a probably not fitting type of gameplay aside from just walking simulator.You get an over the top, extremely detailed and well put scenery that encases the style of majority of the Lovecraft characters, filled with references, winks, or straight up introducing every major entity of the booksHowever, this game goes from 0 to a 100, by reaching certain point of the game you just wonder how did you even there, when it only shows it's a game about walking across a cryptic shore.Yet the extreme it goes is nothing but intense and majestic. Adding combat, chases, puzzles all in different strange and messed up scenarios.By the end the story to me became rather secondary compared to the amount of insane imagery, enemies and situations you found yourself in.And even if some of its things didn't fit or didn't make sense, it was a solid experience that you can absolutely enjoy
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: So before I bought and played the game I checked the comments and one of them said "Cthulhu throws you a ship". It made me not want to buy the game right away because I expect Cthulhu to have less action but more "existence". But the visuals and music were so charming, when it went to discount I bought it immediately. I had some small issues at first launch but i got over them quickly. Then I proceeded on playing the game and here's my scoring.10/10 atmosphere10/10 character design10/10 music7/10 story (I liked the direction, but I can't help but feel it could have been more detailed)6/10 gameplay but I didn't buy the game for the gameplay so it was good enough8/10 Cthulhu mythos (-2 because Cthulhu is definitely a bit out of character, throwing ship does happen, Dagon and Azatoth were good though)So basically I liked the game, but only because I knew what I was purchasing. If I hadn't known it was a short game with kind of hard gameplay (hard as in annoying). I listed a lot of issues there but if you are a fan of cosmic horror, not necessarily Lovecraft, you would like this game. I really appreciate developer for making this game, it truly does what it advertises in the trailer: shows you amazing visuals, has great music and does have some gameplay so you don't just sit and watch.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good story, great lovecraftian walking simulator.Kind of crap gameplay. The first chapter is bog-standard walking sim, collecting notes, poking things you shouldnt' poke, etc.Then it suddenly takes a left turn into low-tier puzzles, and then completely goes off the bend with some weird chase scenes > semi-combat sequences.I got it on sale for $3 and I think $3-$5 is a fair spot for the content. $12 is definitely too much though. The dev doesn't really seem to have had a clear vision in mind for what he wanted this game to be.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: While I know one of the biggest complaints about the game will be its price for its length however for fans of Lovecraft and Cosmic horror that is a small price to pay. It is clear that the developers and story writers had a passion for this game. So many elements from the Cthulhu mythos went into this game and the visuals and game play have little to no flaws. it is a beautiful game and the world you are plunged into is bizare and disturbing to say the least. Some sections can be quite challenging and demand some very fast thinking on the part of the player. You will die at certain points if you are like me and require a minute to get your bearings. Don't let those parts discourage you. The monsters in this game are no joke and it is best to run from them as much as possible. Many of them will be able to out run you but you will have the tools to fight back.  As a fan of cosmic horror I have no complaints about this game and I am happy to support the devs in their endeavors. I hope they consider making more games.

_childDocuments_.review: Good walking simulator. Beautiful environment and pretty effective lovecraftian atmosphere. But, highly underwhelming story resolution. In a nutshell, we're on some island and a disembodied voice walks us through freeing pretty much all of the Other Gods for an unspecified reason, presumably so they can stroll around the island in the distance providing eye candy as we continue playing. Feels a little more like a showcase than a full game. But, under the stipulation that I had a huge amount of free time and not much better to do, I had a good time with this game. I was in a Lovecraft mood and really only wanted the atmosphere, and that's about what it delivers. It's definitely the right price right now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: What starts as a wonderfully atmospheric walking simulator quickly devolves into a mind-numbing monster chase with obtuse puzzle solving thrown in between encounters. Gorgeous island visuals, painted with a grey-blue hue and an abundance of fog, coupled with the low crashing of waves and the gritty crunch of sand and rock as you walk, provide perfect ambiance for what could have been a pretty good game. Within the first 20 minutes or so, this all melts away into a hodgepodge of tentacles and H.R. Giger-inspired statues with constant wailing and warbling in the background as large tentacle monsters chase you around constantly. Instead of the slow-paced exploration you first grow accustomed to, the majority of the game actually involves holding down the Shift key so you can endlessly sprint and periodically doing 180's so you can shoot a purple beam to slow down your pursuers. Everything becomes a slimy, jumbled mess of pulsating fleshy things, and it becomes more and more difficult to make out not only what you're looking at, but also what the game is expecting you to do in order to progress.This is probably the first and only time I've ever been disappointed in the fact that a game ISN'T a walking sim. Instead of Dear Esther we're given an amateur attempt at something like Agony or Scorn. Very bizarre, and ultimately very disappointing. Such a massive letdown for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great exploration/action lovecraftian game. I loved it. It's very unnerving, which is something I almost never feel while playing games. It really kept me feeling tense, masterfully displaying what makes Lovecraft's stories so great: the atmosphere. You really feel the cosmic horror in this one. And the art... It's just amazing. It starts out pretty standard (for the first few minutes, I felt like I was back at Dear Esther, an exploration game I actually didn't like at all), but it doesn't take long for it to take you out of your comfort zone with some pretty bizarre happenings. From there, it spirals down into total madness; I'd rather not spoil it by describing anything, I'll just say, it pleasantly surprised me. I definitely wasn't expecting what I got from this. The sound design was also (mostly) fantastic. This is definitely a game to play with headphones (I realized it in the first few minutes and went to get mine). Now, for the not-so-great stuff: it's definitely quite unpolished. The indie feel is strong with this one, and you will definitely find a few visual glitches here and there; feel annoyed by the walking speed on some occasions; get weirded out by some bad voice-acting (not the main character though, he was great); or even die a couple of times when the action comes along and you keep clicking your mouse and nothing happens. But really, to focus on these gameplay problems instead of on everything so great and so different that this game presents, is totally nitpicking. I have played my fair-share of lovecraftian games, and have never found some of the stuff done here. For me, the good aspects definitely overcame the bad. As an example, just a couple days ago I left a review on another lovecraftian game (more like a demo) that tried to do the "color out of space" thing, and I thought "that's a bad idea, how can you truly show an 'indescribable color' in a game"?. Well, somehow, this game did it right (and it's quite a coincidence that I played this right after the other one xD). The imagery in this one is so awesome... It definitely turned me into a fan, and whenever I manage to get myself some VR goggles, I'm definitely checking out the VR version. Many times I found myself thinking "man, how great would this be if I was seeing it through goggles...". Anyway, great game, I totally recommend it, especially if you are a fan of H.P.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This was a bit of a sleeper! I play any Lovecraftian game by compulsion and I can firmly attest that while each is a labor of love, not all are created equal. Be it the need to empower players with guns and such, or the saturation of weirdness that just overwhelms the horror you would otherwise experience (I'm looking at you Agony and Scorn), some of these games just don't capture the feeling of creeping, inevitable horror that the stories in the genre evoke.I can tell you with absolute certainty that The Shore delivers a heaping helping of every spine-chilling, uncomfortable feeling you got from reading Lovecraft and his contemporaries' stories. Whether its the bizarre, austere weirdness of the forsaken beach or the frantic, manic scramble of the outer worlds this game immerses you in the aesthetic. Its also quite creepy and sometimes downright scary. Great design, interesting writing, decent voice acting and the absolutely STUNNING visuals will definitely make this one worth grabbing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is a mesmerizing journey that transports players to a world of mystery and intrigue, offering a captivating experience that kept me enthralled from start to finish.From the moment I set foot on the eerie shores of a mysterious island, I was immediately drawn into its atmospheric and immersive world. The game's visuals are stunning, with breathtaking landscapes and hauntingly beautiful environments that create a sense of wonder and awe. Every step I took felt like an exploration of the unknown, as I uncovered the island's secrets and unraveled its mysteries.But what truly sets The Shore apart is its storytelling. The game weaves a rich and engaging narrative, filled with twists and turns that kept me guessing until the very end. As I delved deeper into the island's dark past and encountered its enigmatic inhabitants, I found myself completely immersed in the game's lore and mythology, eager to uncover the truth behind the mysteries that lay hidden within.In addition to its compelling narrative, The Shore also boasts atmospheric sound design and a hauntingly beautiful score that adds to the overall sense of immersion. From the distant cries of seabirds to the eerie whispers of the island's secrets, every sound drew me further into the game's world, heightening the tension and excitement with each passing moment.Overall, The Shore is a masterful blend of storytelling, atmosphere, and gameplay that offers a truly unforgettable gaming experience. Whether you're a fan of atmospheric horror games or simply looking for a captivating adventure to embark on, The Shore is a journey you won't soon forget. So grab your flashlight, steel your nerves, and prepare to uncover the secrets that lie hidden within the depths of The Shore.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Its got its good points very immersive, but immersion won't survive the games mechanics, either be a survival horror, or a walking simulator, personally I'd rather do dishes then slog through this crap, whats probably an 8 hour game will take you 15 cause you'll have to smash your head against the death wall until you figure out what your next step is. Very disappointing I was looking forward to this since it was announced.3/10 at best, save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: let me start off by saying i feel like the shore has a lot of potential. but the game is just overwhelmingly average in its current state.a lot of the spoken lines are really difficult to understand. i relied heavily on subtitles for any of the non-human characters, as the effects and overlays on their voices make it incredibly difficult to understand them. that, and some of the effects just felt a bit cheesy and like the stereotypical "big bad guy".the game also lacks a sense of direction. theres a story there, sure, but its a bit barebones and a lot of stuff doesnt feel like it makes sense in the story, given the very little context behind anything. however, i feel like one of the major faults of the game is just how little things are explained. theres a lot of walking and running around, trying to find objectives. other than walls of rock or flesh(?) blocking your path, theres really no indicators of where your next objective is. to me, i got confused pretty quickly. in each of the areas, the textures and areas all look the same. by the lighthouse, the rocks and paths looks pretty similar. later in the game, there are literally no landmarks to guide you, so you kinda just run through a maze-like area while some monster chases you until you either die or find your objective.theres also quite a few puzzles/interactables. there is literally nothing indicating what youre supposed to do with these. youve just gotta look around until the little eye/interaction icon pops up, and use context clues (or button mashing) to figure out what you have to do. theres even a room full of heads, with only one head being the actual "key" to the puzzle. i frequently found myself referencing a guide because its really not explained how to do anything.overall, i think the game could go somewhere. but in its current state, its maybe a few hours of really confusing gameplay with a less than satisfactory experience and ending. a lot of other reviews call this a walking simulator, and i have to agree.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this as a must-play to anyone who is a fan of, and already pretty familiar with extended H.P. Lovecraft Lore.Anyone else, I will give a disclaimer that you may end up disappointed and confused by the end of the game if you are not really into Lovecraft.The gameplay, puzzles, exploration, collectibles, and combat are all very simple and not very deep, the point of this is the submersion into Lovecraft's extended lore, and that job it does with flying colors.I also noticed bad texture pop-in until I increased texture streaming capacity, which also dropped my frames sometimes while playing in 4k on a 3080. I think this would be best enjoyed on a beefy rig if you are at all concerned with graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to preface this by saying that if you enjoy the Lovecraftian, you should just play this game, no research needed. Otherwise, while I would love to say that this game was absolutely perfect, it definitely needs some polishing.      The atmosphere was always amazing, the graphics were  good, and in general the overall concept of the game is fantastic. That being said, it has a lot of minor issues that do very minorly detract from the experience. On the beach there is one shell that is untextured, and while it's not that obvious, there are probably >20 instances of that shell. The camera feels a bit floaty and the controlls seemed inconsistent at times. I spotted a few other oddities, like a creature that swam away, appeared in its original position t-posing, then disappeared again, but aside from just small things like this, there were never any major bugs. I'd recommend this to anyone who's a fan of this genre or even just enjoys good atmospheres and stories, but it would be nice to see some of those flaws patched out eventually, even though I doubt that will ever happen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: 1-3 hours of gameplay (deppends on if you will be like me exploring every single stone on beach, or just go for the end).There are 2 stories, one of the main protagonist and second on papers you may or may not collect, nothing special.What this game excels at are visuals, both sound and graphics are really great... except few things, like leaves and stuff at the beach which are all same and I don't really like the way Cthulhu himself looks, I'd say the game would be a little better without him.Atmosphere is actually one of best I found in games, at some points it actually felt pretty sureal and getting you feel like you are really getting insane... until it breaks with transition.On the oposite side, I discovered several bugs and combat was pretty awfull, mainly the part with hands which felt almost like playing meatboy by the necesity dogding everything.Overall if you want the real feeling you'd expect from Cthulhu world, this game will (most probably) give it to you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I notice a lot of the recent reviews are super picky and not willing to dig a bit deeper in this game or frankly just didn't use the tools provided in it if they think all you do is run away. The game was a SUPER neat find and fun playthrough and my chat on stream loved watching it. It really gives you a taste of lovecraft.Pros:-Solid Atmosphere-Fun Puzzles-Easy to pick up-Cool lore/StoryCons:-Clunky at times-There are glitches when interacting with some objects-Things are not always 100% clearA good game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The visual and sound design of this game is rock solid. Some very cool stuff. Unfortunately, the addition of late game combat and some janky restrictions on travel (Invisible walls) reduce the quality of the experience. Additionally, though this is a personal gripe, it also feels like the creators stuck every element of Lovecraft they could find into The Shore without considering the atmosphere or qualities of Cosmic/Weird Horror outside of "big monster" (Though as stated, such monsters are beautifully designed.)It has some really fun ideas and art, but ultimately falls apart due to some strange decisions. Buy on a sale and be ready to be patient.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This was a crowdfunded project that basically one dude did. I backed it as soon as I could as I saw the visuals and it looked promising. It delivered what I wanted. It had all the Old Ones I wanted to see, and the game play is not about action as much as it is figuring out a mystery and unlocking the Mythos. Some of the puzzles took me a bit to get, but overall I think this is a faithful representation of Lovcraftian horror. Considering this was a passion project from a fan, whom I supported on Facebook until it was live, I have to give this a positive review. All the negatives are from people who came in expecting a triple A experience from Ares Dragonis. That was never going to be the case. Buy this if you are a fan of the genre, because at it's core it is faithful to what we fans love. If you are a fan like me, "like" the positive comments like this one to make sure new people see them when they consider buying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: None of the Parts in this Game seem to be connected, while i would generally categorise it's elements as Cosmic Horror there is just no cohesion between any of them. A few easter eggs like the Meteor from Colour out of Space or summoning some tentacles are neat, but not if the entire Island is littered with them. At one Point i walked into a creepy green cave, realised it had no bearing on anything and just decided to walk back out. Got attacked by a fish guy, he died, didn't know there were any beforehand, only saw one more and he just left. Consequences are usually a major Part of Lovecraftian Horror, but here most of the things you can find are just nothing. No reason for them to exist, no relevance to the Story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: A forbidden island full of horrors is the setting for the video game THE SHORE, which is about the mystery of the unknown. The narrative incorporates numerous of H. P. Lovecraft's most well-known works as well as other elements.Gamers will experience the world through Andrew's eyes as he searches for his missing daughter.Players will confront the most terrifying Lovecraftian horrors and explore The Shore through immersive, atmospheric gameplay while completing challenging puzzles.Strive to remain alive as Andrew does so while attempting to preserve his daughter's life and, possibly, learning the secrets of his own sanity.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about the game. I really want to like the game, the idea behind it sounds really enjoyable and in the class of game that I love. But, there are three major issues with the game that i found.1. The sense of direction is awful. Its so hard to figure out where to go or what to do. Most of the time I spent playing the game was humping against every invisible wall i could till i found the right path, but even then its still confusing what I'm supposed to be doing.2. The audio and graphics. Both definitely need to be flushed out. The frames are awful and it has clipping issues with the audio.3. The price. This does not feel like a 25 dollar game and should be marketed for less.  I don't hate the game, it just doesn't feel complete. I wanted to wait to put up a review for it till i got farther into the game, but I'm still stuck on the same part because i have no idea where I'm supposed to go or what I'm supposed to do. I pray that the developers post an update soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: My SHORT time with The Shore was overall an enjoyable one.It has a nice little story, pretty straight forward.No "Wooow" feeling but enough for you to know why you're there and what you're doing.Also, in the beginning there are journals you can read from a previously stranded crew which contributes to the lore.Unfortunately there's basically no exploration value. The game is very linear and you are pretty much walking through the story clicking on things.According to Steam, I finished the game in 106 minutes... Not very long game but understandable since it's made by one person.One thing that's really good is the environment and model design, everything looks very good and original and the creature models really live up to its source material.(well, as close you can come to something that cannot be comprehended by the human mind)Pros:+ Graphics/models and design.+ Lore (in the beginning)+ You can fight back (which you usually cant in these kind of games)+ Really cool and awe-inspiring environmentsCons:- Short! (106 minutes)- Lore again (Non exists after the beginning)- Linear- No exploration value- Animations are.....ehh....Cons that doesn't really matter.- Quite a few grammatical errors in the written text.- Text and speech doesn't match in many places- Voice actingAs you can see it leaves somewhat to be desired, but the things I liked about it is good enough to give it a thumbs up.Bought it on a sale for 6€ and I don't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Visuall stunning, but has some flaws.You have to press "Shift" key to run and hold "Shift" key to run even faster. Why? There is no reason not to be running all the time, since movement is very slow, so you end up holding the "Shift" key all the time.Often where is no clear indication where you can go. In some places you jump on rather tall rocks, in other - an inch high obstacle is dead end. In one area I got killed off like 20 times, because it wasn't clear which path is passable. It gets really anoying in the second half of the game.The game is pretty short, but I guess it's ok, because I wouldn't stand it was longer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative recommendation. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this because we need more indie games but really is more of a mixed bag.This game really could have used more time in QA. I came across an issue with my character getting stuck when the window lost focus. The menu items were interactable when not visible. The 'combat' was really awful. It shouldn't exist in a game like this but it's even worse when it's implemented this poorly. There were a few moments when I was like, "This isn't Lovecraftian lore accurate and sort of make the characters feel cheap and not mysterious."Other than that, most of the puzzles were pretty great and not overly complicated (the head one was awful though). The atmosphere was pretty on theme, the music was fitting, and there were a good amount of creepy level designs. I liked getting story bits through the messages in a bottle but some of the other lore notes weren't voice acted which felt odd.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This was not a long game and there were certain aspects that were a tad frustrating. That being said I enjoyed the entire ride. The Lovecraftian influence is done extremely well and if you are an eldritch fan then you should consider picking this game up. The environments that you are thrown into go from serene beach to cosmic realm of madness and all are a feast for the eyes. Having played a few different lovecraft inspired games I feel that this was one of the better ones.

_childDocuments_.review: My only gripe with the game is that it is a bit short. If you are a fan of H.P. Lovecraft, then you will enjoy all the references and nods in this game. It shows that the creator made this game like a love letter with care and respect. Even if you are a surface level fan, you'll recognize some of Lovecraft's most famous works! The Achievements aren't hard to get which is a plus for you completionists. If you are a fan of Lovecraft in anyway, this is one to consider for your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what I was looking in a Lovecraftian game. The sense of helplessness and that there is something a lot bigger going on behind the veil.Wanted the game to be longer and maybe more creepy things to be present which happen at the beginning (the ominous ball or the pit, or secret ritual). After that, it progresses too fast to keep up with whats going on. Some parts made me scratch my head for a while, however, that was only at the beginning of the game. When you obtain the Relic it becomes fight or flight, most of the time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels unfinished. Uneven audio levels on the voieovers; lots of places where the level geometry didn't match the visual geometry; objects floating in midair or with textures only half drawn; often there is no back-side to papers, just the mirror image of the front texture; if you press "Tab" you activate some kind of developer overlay with invisible text boxes. Just... lots of stuff that I feel like should have been caught and addressed before the game was released.Subjective gripes: not a fan of the control scheme used when rotating objects. Would appreciate a "Cancel" button on the settings menus instead of "Accepting" the settings you already had. Would like better signposting on where to proceed. Some of the environments, the way to progress felt like I was skyrimming, not following the intended path.Silly things: Pretty sure some of the assets chosen are anachronistic. The game leaves it ambiguous when it is set but I'm fairly sure they didn't have plastic jugs or modern nutrition labels whenever this takes place.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a better rating system for its games because thumbs up or thumbs down doesn't really give me much options, but I guess I'm going to give this game a thumbs down, even though it doesn't really deserve it. The game is very pretty, some very strong visuals, a so-so story, basic puzzles, basic combat mechanics, some very good and disturbing environments. I didn't dislike the game, but at four hours (and honestly you could beat it in far less) it isn't worth getting unless it's on sale, and I think even the $4.99 I got it for is a bit much considering the content.  The game could have used better puzzles, and a number of the puzzles have very little strategy to them. The game sometimes likes to plop you into a room make you do a puzzle and then transport you out of the room for no real reason other than doing a puzzle.There's nothing to the combat, you have an artifact that can blast enemies and kill them with a little effort, but it is so simplistic that I would have preferred a stealth game more than combat. There seems like a number of elements in the game that an idea was had for but never got fleshed out, especially early in the game when you are collecting items, but some of them never get used, and then later you lose access to your inventory, which makes me ask what was the point of it?And unless there is a better, alternate ending, the ending of the game is simplistic and poorly thought out, like it was rushed to finish.I would say give it a try if it is on sale, but don't expect more than you moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game in 5hrs including a decent amount of AFK and exploring for secrets. Overall, it's an okay game. I'm sure people who love Lovecraftian lore will enjoy it a fair amount. The jump scares weren't scary, at least not to me, and once you enter the void area, the game runs like hot trash. The solution to the problem in the void is to go into the game settings and turn the  music volume all the way down. It still had some stutter, mostly when entering new areas, but that fixed the game for the most part. It's not that difficult, and the voices tend to be a bit uneven. There's a "memory scene" toward the end of the game where the main character's voice is basically the only audible one; definitely play with subtitles on. Plus the entities are sometimes hard to understand.That all being said, the visuals were fantastic! The puzzles were okay, fairly easy. And the lore is pretty good. If you're into this kind of game and/or are a huge lovecraft fan, then this may be worth a purchase when, and only when, it's ON SALE.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game because I am a huge fan of H.P. Lovecraft's works, and I got excited when I bought this game, but sadly, this game is not good, really not. The atmosphere is the only good part, but after one or two hours, the gameplay just kills it, and the narrative is really weak compared to other fanfic Lovecraft stories. My advice: don't buy this game; read instead.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. I understand that it's not for everyone and that some folks may be disappointed in the length (about 2.5 hours for me) but I enjoyed every minute of it. I have long been a fan of Lovecraftian/Cosmic Horror and this game really did that well. Seeing some of Lovecraft's more...strange monsters on screen was a delight. For a mostly one person team, this game was clearly full of passion for the mythos and I'm glad I got to experience it. I'd love to see what could be done with a bigger team/budget. I was happy to spend my $25 on this and if you're a fan of this universe then you should be too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Great atmosphere. A true lovecraftian style story. Unfortunately the game is poorly optimized, and littered with performance issues. Some of them are so severe, that they make the game unplayable. I cannot complete the game on my rig, and it's a decent medium-high end PC. I'm not the only one with these issues either, and the developers haven't seen a need to touch up their product so that everyone can play. It is for this reason that I cannot recommend, as you may be wasting your money on a game that becomes unplayable halfway through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, the shore puts you in a place that feels almost familiar and does such an incredible job at the lovecraftian horror. its incredible but just feels like it comforms to modern tropes for a minute mid game. i adored the game all the way up till right now in the game. all the fear you feel comes straight out of your own mind and the scale of everything is incredible. the game does an incredible job at truly making you feel tiny in the grand scheme while still needing to look over your shoulder. its the first game to have made me feel that in a long long time and for only being done by one single person is nothing short of incredible. However, the use of 'Weapon' feels pointless and almost gimmiky, not to mention how in chase sequences, the enemy goes the same speed as you if not faster, making it take like 20 minutes to get through a 2 minute section. it slows down the pace of the game almost makes me wanna stop playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. The atmosphere is blindingly beautiful and the score is really complimentary to the game. Those epic scores, when you uncover new creatures is amazing and sends goosebumps through the body. I get that the shooting part of the game is kinda mweh, but then again, would a fisherman really be able to hand an alien weapon. Further more this is not a FPS game, but a puzzlegame, so I can forgive the lackluster control of the small shooting parts. The normal pricing is a bit steep for a 3-5hour long experience, but I bought it on sale and was mindblown with the experience. If you find it on sale definately give this game a playthrough :) Grafix: 8/10 The water and in general the gfx of the outside world is as beatiful as can be (apart from stone looking abit odd). The other world is abit gritty, but it gives a good effect to the story.Sound: 9/10 Very good complimentary soundtrack with epic scores, when you encounter new creatures.Gameplay: 8/10 It's a walking game/puzzle game with some wonky shooting elements. For the most part it works great. Engaging story as well and you feel the need to find that next puzzle. And for achievementhunters this is a nice relaxing list :)Total: 8,5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Holy. Crab.I just finished this and if I wasn't already sitting I think I'd have to sit down for a bit.Even though I'm not a fan of throwing all sorts of creatures from various Lovecraft stories into one single medium like it's some sort of Lovecraft's Allstars basketball match, I gotta admit that this is, hands down, the most atmospheric Lovecraft-themed game I have ever played. The look and feel and the surreality of it all are absolutely on point. Stylistically, it takes kind of an unexpected turn towards the end for my taste, but the fantastic designs, bombastic atmosphere and carefully designed, beautiful environment more than make up for it.If you're looking for a Lovecraft-themed game that actually succeeds at feeling like one, this one is for you. Absolute recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: The Shore is a great cosmic horror experience with some absolutely terrifying moments. The visuals are amazing to look at and i cannot praise the environment design enough. My jaw was on the floor for almost all of my playthrough.Now i don't know much about the Lovecraft mythos but playing this with a friend who knows a fair amount about everything was an absolute joy. Hearing about all the little details in the world and the connections to the stories was a great deal of fun.Can highly recommend this game to anyone even mildly curious about cosmic horror or Lovecraft's works
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: So as always like every dear Lovecraftian first-person game before The Shore this one has alot of issues as well.I specifically had a hard time playing it.To put it midly it was horrible in regards to the quality as a "walking simulator" even though the latter portion of the game don't it into something else BUT, and there is always a a but, it certainly has its charms.Especially the space part and almost everything after that.I adored the deep-diving section too because I'm a sucker for underwater diving levels.It clearly needs more improving touches but I'd overall recommend the game if you just love seeing visually appealling stuff.Still C'thulhu acted kinda ooc in that basically a fanfic game.Last but not least: TENTACLES!
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish is could give this game a "meh" or "huh?" rating. Not great, not awful. 6/10 Buy it on sale.Much like others have said, this feels like 2 different games. It's starts out all story & chill with a creepy edge to it, & then BAM! It becomes an action game. And we get a little bit more story added at the end & a wrap up that feels a bit lacking & not entirely worth the time & effort you've put in. Although games aren't only about the ending as the story early on is pretty on par with Lovecraft.Some of the fights are pretty hard if you're not used to it, like me who's just getting back into gaming again. Many encounters are nuts, unless you use a guide to tell you The graphics & scenery are pretty amazing. Lots of eerie, beautiful, decently realistic imagery all around. I just wish they'd give you a little time to really look at a couple of the creatures & surroundings that disappear quickly, or are too tall to see easily.DON'T PAUSE THE GAME! If you hit Pause/Escape, when you un-pause you won't be able to move the character nor your view. You'll need to Quit & come back in, losing some progress if you haven't just hit an auto-save checkpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing treat for Lovecraft fans.It is definitely an indie production, so don't go in expecting perfect technical polish or extreme length. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: This game has fantastic music and graphics and it's nice that it does its own take on the Lovecraft theme, but it's also very short and the developers make some perplexingly stupid decisions that bog the thing down into mediocrity through much of it.Pros:- A couple clever puzzles- 2nd half of the game is totally different from the first- Great atmosphereCons:- Stupid invisible boundaries and the fact that you have to "unlock" the ability to jump makes it feel cheap- Very short- Some of the puzzles are totally nonsensicalOverall it's good, but there are better Cthulu-themed games out there. Needed an extra hour and a bit more depth to pad it out. It is cool that you actually get a weapon at one point and kill enemies to an extent. _childDocuments_.review: I really liked The Shore. Lovecraft with a soundtrack worthy of the movie Annihilation.It's weird, it's grotesque, it's obscure. _childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmospheric exploration, 3 hours long game, in the world of Lovecraft with 2 majors flaws. First the atmosphere and music are spot on, many small items to discover and some messages to read about the Cthulhu mythos. Discovering some strange monoliths and anomalies on this forsaken island are really well-made and super fun. The story could have been more defined rather then you wake up on a beach, now find some missing generic family member the player have no attachment to. The walking feel sluggish like stuck in jello and it's pretty hard to tell if you are running or not. There is a few kind of puzzles but they are not really satisfying nor intuitive, pick the right head from the ground was a bit boring and shoot the beams in the right order or die too.All of this could have been forgiven, but its a major component for fleeing and fighting the various denizens of the island. Fleeing is a terrible mechanic of the game, it seems like all the monster go at the same speed of you, took a wrong turn, or got stuck into a  wall corner ? too late your dead. You eventually get a strange item that allows you to stun some monsters, then the game become a repetition of : Run, stop, freeze the monster, run a short while ... rince and repeat for the whole level.I really hope for a deeper sequel in the same universe, but without combat or running. Actual working puzzles would be a lot more fitting to this kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great short game, first playthrough took a bit over 2 hours because I take my time with games like this. If you are a fan of Lovecraft this is 100% worth playing, I picked it up on sale but for the $11.99 price it would probably be worth it for Lovecraft fans.
_childDocuments_.name: The Shore

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale and while it may not be the most complex or challenging game, I must say I enjoyed it. I have loved Lovecraft's work for a long time and it is rare to find a game which captures the feel and look of Lovecraft's Mythos. This game wasn't particularly long (I clocked in at 2.2 Hours from start to finish), nor does it have the most riveting story, but I found myself captivated by the locations and Lovecraft's monsters. There were perhaps two moments in this game that I found very frustrating, one where the game glitched and wouldn't let me put down an item (I ended up having to hard quit the game and go back in and just not pick it up again) and another where I kept getting killed by this one particular monster before I realised how to get past it. This is an Indie Game so if you go in expecting something AAA you will not find it here. At times the game can be clunky and the controls aren't perfect BUT all things considered I had a good time with this game. I would be very keen to see this developer take on one of Lovecraft's stories and purely focus on it, such as the Mountains of Madness or Shadow Over Innsmouth, as I feel this game was a good introduction to all of the monsters but never really had the chance to explore any one fully.Overall, good game but wait for a sale.
